Oysters, hot crab legs, various noodle soups, variety sushi, poke, juices such as guava and mango and more, great dessert station with must try gelato flavors such as mango habanero, mint basil, flavors you wouldn't get anywhere. 

I usually don't eat a lot at buffets but the variety was of such excellent quality I felt like it was very much well worth the 50ish price tag. 

Go here instead of wicked spoon. Had wicked spoon the day after and it had nothing good.

Pretty bad buffet for almost  $60 per person. We stand in line for almost 40 mintues. And the food is a totally disappointment. It's basic a seafood section plus a grill food section plus a cheap Chinese food section and some desert in the middle. I want my money back if I can. Wicked spoon is the way to go
Be careful of the oysters,  I got a stomach flu (maybe Norovirus) after eating them 3 days ago, now still feeling sick.

So delicious!  We visited the buffet over Christmas,  it was not crowded, plenty of food. I would have been in a food coma if I didn't control myself. Lol. I highly recommend that you visit this buffet before leaving Vegas!

Check this place out right when it opens or you will wait a minute.

All types of dishes - from sushi, raw oyster bar, crab legs, and all types of options around the worlds. So good!

$55 for the buffet dinner. Make sure to check if there are any deals for this place to save yourself some money. There's a large selection of food to choose from, so you'll definitely find something to satisfy your tastebuds. Chinese, Italian, Spanish, meats, seafood, vegetables, pizza...the list goes on and on. I thoroughly enjoyed my high stacked plates of food, but my only critique would have to be that the most of the meats I had were overcooked. I'm a huge fan of lamb chops, but the lamb chops that night were dry and overcooked. Was a little disappointed, so I opted to fill up my stomach on other foods instead. 

After dinner, indulge yourself in the endless desserts this place has to offer. Their thai iced bubble tea was spot on. If I didn't care about my weight or didn't care about getting the itis afterwards, I would've eaten for hours. All in all, I recommend eating here if you don't mind the steep price. But hey, that's Vegas for you. 

Also I recommend going a bit earlier around the time dinner starts so you can avoid the wait time, which can get super long. My two friends and I waited for 5 minutes and then walked right in!

Without a doubt, the best buffet in Las Vegas (and maybe the world?). The variety is insane and everything is very high-quality. I don't think I've ever had a dish I didn't care for here which is a pretty wild success rate. It's also the only Vegas buffet where I feel that the dessert section really matches up with the rest of the offering. 

It's a pricey meal, especially on the weekend, but 1) you're in Vegas and 2) the Zorro slot by the line is pretty loose.

This all you can eat buffet is a great place to come eat a variety of foods under one roof. It's a little pricey but they do have Groupon deals make sure you use those! I loved the food options, they even have great foods for vegetarians and some options for vegans. our waitress Esmeralda made our experience one I will not forget! she was so friendly and funny the vibes were great. I would recommend this place to anyone who is visiting Las Vegas. Definitely will be returning!

King Of Buffet's!!!  This place is truly one of the BEST BUFFET's in Vegas.  The quality of food and variety is just ridiculous.  The decor is really upscale and very clean.  The service is excellent and the waiters are really attentive with refills and cleaning up used plates.  The price for the Buffet is on the expensive side but you get what you paid for in quality and variety.  The Buffet is situated inside Cesars Palace so parking should not be an issue.  My fiancee and I did not have to wait at all to get in because we had an early dinner around 5PM.  The usual wait from we have heard from others is between 1-2 hours depending on the day of the week.  

I for one am a big fan of crab legs and oysters and Bacchanal really has one of the freshest seafood selections around.  Located literally smack dab in the front of the Buffet line right when you walk in so its pretty difficult to miss.  The meat selection is filled with massive slabs of everything you can think of.  One of my favorite was the lamb chops that was just delicious.  There is even a Udon/Ramen section where the chef will make whatever you like right on the spot and you can add the toppings on your own.  In the back where they have all the chinese food you can also find chinese chicken herbal soup that explodes with flavor.  The dessert section is also just out of this world.  They have a whole variety of mochi ice cream, gelato, and the usual sea of dessert cakes and goodies.  My favorite was the sesame mochi and the thai tea gelato.  

I would suggest looking at the whole buffet selection before you start getting anything so you can get an idea of how massive the buffet actually is.  This way you can map out what you plan to get and not get stuck missing out on food because you are so damn full.  Make sure you wear loose clothes because you will probably need the extra space.

We did the buffet of buffets and almost passed this one over because of the upcharge, but boy are we glad we went! This place is definitely the best buffet in Vegas! Crab legs are the best we encountered, even things like pizza and ramen were both amazing! The dessert selection is incredible and their service was on point! Skip the other buffets and pay a bit more to head here! You won't regret it!

I've eaten at this buffet before, and my experience was mediocre. Someone I know had a really bad experience where her whole party got food poisoning. My friend made a bad review on yelp, and the manager (Stephanie) apologized for the incident and offered to make it up to her by offering complimentary passes.

After my friend and Stephanie emailed each other back and forth, they set a time where my friend would return to the buffet. When we get there, Stephanie asks us to pay first before we get inside. WHAT?? Am I in the twilight zone?? Stephanie then tells us that the offer was for four free express line passes, NOT buffet passes. At this point, I'm looking at a $250 bill that they are waiting for us to pay with people in line watching us. We walked out.

While eating at the Cosmopolitan buffet, I reread the messages closely, and it reads, "I would like to extend to you four complimentary express line passes on your next trip to Bacchanal along with a complimentary bottle of house wine or a round of cocktails for four. The express line will grant you VIP entry and seating at Bacchanal." That was the zinger, right there. For those of us who don't work in the industry, it sounds like she was offering us buffet passes. "VIP entry and seating" sounds like a buffet pass. Of course we realize that it was just a bait and switch, and they just wanted to make themselves look good on yelp, when in reality, they are condescending when they explain to you in person that "the VIP line is a $25 value and it allows you to cut in line." Whoop dee doo.

Really wish I could give Zero stars. Thank you, Cesar's staff, for embarrassing and making us feel uncomfortable. When I die, I would like for your staff to lower me into my grave, so that you can let me down one last time.
Love it so much! It's definitely worth the price of tix. Lots of different seafood, meats and desserts! Expect to gain weight when you go

Like with any expensive buffet in Vegas, it's usually 75% hype and 25% something special (Actual quality aside of course). I didn't personally feel this was much different than Wynn's or Wicked Spoon (you know, attractive, IG artistic, tapas-style everything)

They had a street taco setup which ironically, was one of the best parts of the meal. Hate to think I paid all the money to ultimately eat street tacos but remember, you're paying more for the greedy delight of having so many options- what you actually consume most likely doesn't match what you paid. Tried the brisket which was extremely dry, nobody at our table liked it. Tried the prime rib which was almost too rare and had no flavor to it. 

Desserts were definitely great. Macarons, creme brûlée, chocolate covered strawberries- but again, nothing the Wynn buffet doesn't also have (that I noticed).

Won't come back. Wynn is still my favorite.

My first time and last time eating at this buffet. In the middle of the night after having eaten at this buffet I became very sick. I'm a nurse so I know what food poisoning is. I ate the crab legs and my husband had not and he was fine the whole trip (beyond the crab, we basically had the same food and I didn't drink - our only other meal of the day was breakfast at Giada's that morning, so this wasn't a flu bug). I may not tempt fate eating crab at a buffet ever again. 

I did the responsible thing and called the hotel to report the incident between bouts of severe cramps, nausea, and trips to and from our hotel bathroom. Their security desk took a message and had their EMT call. She took the report over the phone. I called not just for myself, but because I didn't want some elderly person, or immune-comprised individual, or even a child getting sick because it might have hit them a lot harder. I also didn't go to the ER because I drank water and Gatorade so I wouldn't get dehydrated. 

Weeks later I finally heard from their claims department in order to repeat the story. I could tell she was disinterested when we spoke. I wasn't seeking some significant settlement or remuneration and didn't even mention anything to that effect during the call, but I'd have appreciated having the cost of our meals reimbursed, never mind what was to have been a nice weekend get-away which ended quite poorly. 

Today, nearly 7 weeks later comes the letter - saying "...we  deny any responsibility...."  Okay, then I will share my story on Yelp and I won't ever eat at a Caeser's establishment again. It's not worth the risk to my health. 

If I could leave them zero stars I would have done so...

This is the top of the line experience. I can't even label this a buffet just due to the quality of what they serve. You're not getting standard buffet fare, you're getting some culinary delights probably not to be found at any other buffet. They have fresh exotic fruit juices in glass bottles ready for your enjoyment.

I couldn't do this place any justice by merely listing the food options which is a large task ..they have many unique options.

This is just something you need to experience for yourself....the high price tag on the buffet is for a very good reason.....also i went on a Monday and it was still packed if that givces you any idea of how superb everything is.

Food is subpar. There's a line to get to pay, then a line to pay, and then a line to get in!! :( There's even a line for the good stuff like seafood, so if you have to eat lower price stuff if you don't want another line. Came at 7 and only had an hour before closing. That's not enough to really savor it over talk. Nice customer service, though.

Worth the wait for us. Went on a Sunday night and we got in around 45 minutes. Our first instinct when we saw the line was "Is this worth it?" Apparently, our faces showed it cause a lady coming out told us what she thought and that we should wait in line. So we went for it and we're glad. 

The line moves relatively quickly. It smells like seafood, which doesn't help, cause it makes you hungrier. But the seafood section is RIGHT where you enter so it made sense after we saw that. Be careful of cheap young douche bags who try to cut. I saw 2 guys try and sneak in in front of the people in front of us and they heard me saying something so they kicked them out. But then they tried to cut in front of us and I just waited 30 minutes so no way was I going to let them in. He tried to pay us and everything and eventually the left the line but we unfortunately saw them about 40 minutes into our dinner. Keep your eyes peeled. 

Not a single worker was on my bad list here. From the person we paid with, to the hostess, to the person who sat us, to our waiter, to the guy who kept clearing our table, this place has exceptional staff and service.

So my brothers and dad LOVED the snow crab. They got plates and plates of the warm ones. The pastas, Mexican food, and seafood were my favorites. As an Asian, I didn't care for the Asian food. 

Definitely get the snow crab legs and ceviche and the fried foods. It;s unhealthy but you paid 50 bucks and waited who knows how long so just do it. They had sweet potato tater tots, which I've never seen or heard of, and they were bomb.com. I could not stop eating them even though it meant eating less of something else. 

Okay my other favorite food, the dessert. I have an incredibly bad sweet tooth so dessert is always important to me. UNLIMITED MACAROONS. im from LA where macaroons are a thing and these were good. I could eat as much as I wanted. They had creme brulee which is my favorite, sorbets, candy, cookies, and your typical desserts, but on another level. It was heavenly. 

And last, I can't believe I almost forgot, but they have Aguas Frescas ON DECK. Horchata, tamarindo, limonada, and more. I'm sure it's some instant kind but I don't care. I'm asian and I can't tell too much so I had as much horchata as I wanted. They come in these cute mini milk jug type things and you could take as much as you wanted. 

This place changed my outlook on buffets. I think every time I go to Vegas now, I'm going to have to eat here. I love Wicked Spoon but my love for Bacchanal beats that.

I had heard wonderful things about this buffet and believing it couldn't be all hype, my husband and I ate here last weekend. 

I've eaten at almost all the buffets in anyone's top 10 list of Vegas buffets. I really didn't see this one as being in the top 5. 

The crab was previously frozen and tasted like it. The lamb chops were cooked correctly but lacked seasoning. The deserts I tasted were meh or just OK. Many of the items were constantly out of stock and waiting to be refilled. The setup of the buffet was poor. What I mean by that is that there are lots of angles and corners so it's pretty easy to get boxed in or out when a crowd forms, which was normal. 

The setup to get in to the buffet was the worst I've ever seen. Consistently, there was just one person taking peoples $$ causing a huge multiple hour long queue to form. Alternatively, you could pay an additional $15PP to cut through the line. On that side, there were 2 or 3 people checking people in at any given time. The check-in folks were clueless to the unrest of the crowd and offered no apologizes from the long and unnecessary wait (the dining was NOT full by any means). 

The waitstaff seemed to be overworked. I ordered a soda and was given 2 glasses of soda, presumably because we would never see our waiter again, which was the case. 

I still say Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan is the best buffet in vegas...I'll avoid Bacchanal in the future.

Im just so full thinking about this place!!! And how I'm such a sad weakling when it comes to buffets, but I've been to other casino buffets and others and I can honestly say this is one of the BEST! 

Hands down a huge selection of food and made really well! 
It's very pricey BUT very well worth it!! 
There are NO signs as which food came from ethnically, i.e. ITalian, American, seafood, Asian, Spanish!!! Which I think is great because those signs are just stupid! You go along the back wall with the seafood you can see from the registers when you first walk in!! But as turn the corner there's another and another till you finally stop until you realize there's a "dessert island" at the center of the room! Everything tastes pretty amazing which is why it's so popular!! 

I was with some pretty picky eaters!   And out of all that they ate and drank there was only 2 they did not like at all! 

Tips:

LAdies this is a buffet so find something nice and stretchy(I proudly rocked my temporary pregnancy look) 

It's a buffet and if your on a diet portion control thing, coming here will face kick it to curb! Like it did with me!

This was absolutely the best buffet experience I've ever had!! The food was fresh and the staff were on point! Not one empty tray, not one piece of trash on the floor, not one unclean table. Food was excellent and plentiful. I'd recommend this to anyone looking for a great time.

This was OK, but not phenominal.  The food was fine but there were only a few dishes that were above average.  This is the kind of place where older people go to load up on crab legs.

I was mostly disappointed because it didn't live up to the hype.

I'm not sure what all the hype is about here.  I was very disappointed. If all you want is crab legs and oysters this is your spot. Other than that, there's much to be desired. I highly doubt that there are 500 food items here. I pretty much stuck too the Chinese duck and chicken wings. For a strip buffet I will stick to wicked spoon at cosmopolitan.

We're typically very good at getting to buffets super early before the dinner rush, but our schedule went off track and we didn't arrive till 6:45--didn't get seated until 8:30. The line also looks misleadingly short. 

I could justify the line if the food was amazing (like the Wynn Buffet), but even though we were so hungry our stomachs were devouring themselves, we left feeling rather ho-hum about the experience.

Everything tasted great initially, but I'm pretty certain that was because my gfs and I all experienced a second-wind of hunger. Fifteen minutes into the meal and we were pretty much done.

Additionally, the buffet lines are poorly organized. Each section of the buffet bleeds into the other (seafood next to meat etc), so if you wanted one of the more popular foods, it was hard to tell where the end of the line was without accidentally cutting off someone else. And sometimes, you found one thing but not the other in obvious proximity--like a bunch of different hummus, yet no pita. cheese and charcuterie but no bread :(

This buffet is amazing. It must be the best buffet in Vegas because it has everything. This place is massive.

You need to go and try it to believe it. Their orange juice came in the cutest little jugs. Even the carrot juice was yummy. I don't even like carrot juice!

Go when it's not lunch or dinner to avoid lines. The bottomless mimosas are worth it!

Average. It's not as special as you expect it to be. Dumplings are pretty good, don't  miss them, also the cheese selection is good. Don't waste time on sushi, not worth it. Leave room for desserts, there's pleenty of them!

Easily could get five stars and best brunch in vegas title except that I don't like misleading, capitalize off of people type schemes. When you check in the computer says 22-30 minutes but that is the wait time to go WAIT in line lol. Smart! Once they trap you in the line you assume you are going to wait 30 minutes to eat. Actually you will wait one hour to pay then get trapped again to wait another 30-45 minutes in another line to eat. Quite genius trapping actually for a $60 brunch. Go around the corner to the noodle shop and save yourself the trouble of almost passing out from low blood sugar.

This  is the best buffet I have every attended. The food was great. The craving station had a large variety of meat choices, prime rib,brisket, roast beef and chicken sausage. The was a larger selection of seafood. There wasn't any fried seafood most of it was sautéed and broiled. You want to wait to eat until you get there. There is soooo much food to chose from. They had cold and hot crabs to choose from. I had the crabs. Shrimp lo mein , beef ribs and shrimp creole rice. You may not have room for desert. You need to go twice during your stay in Las Vegas. It worth the price but how much can you eat at one sitting. The seating ticket said you only have a two hour limit to be there.  My husband had the lamb chops ant they were tender.

I'm generally not a buffet fan, but if you are going to a buffet, it can't get much better than this. As a VIP at Caesars we get to skip the line, which is a HUGE plus because this place is busy. 

Food variety is broad and quality is very good for a buffet. Service is not amazing and they are a bit slow on drinks and any requests you might make. 

I've only tried two buffets in Vegas and this is the best.

I have only heard about the buffet at Caesars Palace so you can only imagine my expectation ... as I walked toward what it seemed to a line, I saw these machines that calculate waiting time so I can come back when the line is not as long. The machine that I used didn't give me a paper receipt, but it took my contact information so it can text me directly. The estimated time was 58 mins. which wasn't too bad, but I received a text message 25 mins earlier than the initial estimated time. So I walked over to the buffet and perhaps waited about 35 more mins to be seated. 
My first plate full of sushi and other asian food was better than expectation. Food tasted fresh and well seasoned. I was hoping to get a second plate with exact same food, but I was hoping to try literally every food that they had so I had to resist myself. lol Their seafood selection is simply amazing. Unlike some of other buffet where they serve tiny little shrimp, Bacchanal buffet serves larger shrimp. 
On to the dessert. Wow! They have so many selections including gelato to fresh fruit! 
Although the food was amazing, the server for my table rarely came by which made it difficult to get refills or extra napkins.

I'm not sure if they have seafood only on the weekends, but we went on a Thursday evening and they didn't crab. The food was super tasty and quite unique. Come with an appetite. It's a decent selection. I believe it was around $45-$50 not including tip.
My fave buffet in Vegas so far, and I've been in Vegas for a decade!  The staff are clean, professional, and respectful.  The food is amazing!

Went two times for weekday dinner for $55/person. First entered at 5pm no wait at all on Tuesday 6/13/17 and Thurs 6/15/17 at 6pm with wait of 30mins and sat at 6:30pm. 

Pros: 
Good selection of food.
Tacos are tasty.
Prime Rib.
King crab.
Dungenus crab.
Flan avail 1st time but not 2nd time (all I see was them making more creme bre le wtf?) !
Fried calamari.
Waiters were speedy.

Cons:
lighting is horrible! too dim to see and appreciate the food on both occasions.
pricey!
No lobster at this price!
No scallop!
No Italian food like ravioli or any pasta!
Shrimp dumpling is dry!
Clams were sandy!
No fried chicken!
Sliders are dry and forgettable! 
No flan (my favorite) the second time!


Overall I would like them to offer better quality food. Selection is abundant but its missing quality and consistency. Would I go a third time maybe not! Also I asked a person who worked there if there is lobster or caviar (since the container was displayed) but he said its $200/ person?

Best Buffet in Vegas! Sets itself apart from the others. We purchased the buffet of buffets pass and paid the additional to eat here for dinner one night. This was for sure the best meal in the 24 hours. We had dinner the night before and then breakfast, waiting until about 7:30pm to make sure we were our hungriest! It was a splurge.. and I would probably skip the 24 hour pass on my next visit and only visit Bacchanal. This food had much more flavor than the other buffets, better and more high end options. I think my boyfriend and I shared at least 3 plates of crab legs, snow, king and steamed. ALL delicious! There is sushi, pho and ramen. There are all the options of a steakhouse. The desserts are truly amazing, I got pretty much one of everything and had a bite of each. I was hoping to have room for the crepes.. but just didn't make it lol 

Service was good, drinks were brought and refilled quickly. Napkins and fresh silverware brought upon request. 

Protip: Visit one of the new dispensaries in town.. and then hit up the buffet ;)
So many good things.  Don't skip the Asian station.  Hot and sour soup is great.  The pho is hit or miss though.
Over rated food not too bad, service is horrible.  Not a seafood lovers so not too many other choices.

Had to come here to try the buffet because it's known to be one of the best buffets on the strip.

There are different areas for different cuisines but the seafood area is usually the most backed up because everyone is trying to get their fill on things such as seabass and snow crab legs. There's an area for Asian cuisine, which things such as dim sum & dumplings, an area for American/Italian food with stuff such as fried chicken and fries in cute little waffle ice cream cones! 

Their dessert area is huge and has cute little desserts on sticks. I think one of my most favorite stations here is the fresh juice station as they are bottled up in cute little jars. 

Pace yourself and try not to fill up with too many good stuff on your first round! Just take your time and try a bit of everything.
This buffet is awesome!  It's a bit expensive but well worth it!  The quality and flavor is second to none!

We don't "do" buffet very often, but while we were checking out the various casinos, we took the time to check out a few - and quickly determined this one is far and away the best of the bunch... but not twice as good as the half price competition next door behind the lake if you know what I mean.

Fresh oysters in the desert? Why not, it's Ceasars. 
Snow crab legs, hot or chilled, plenty of each and conveniently cut in half for you.
Smoked brisket, in house overnight, incredible and only one of 6 items in the carving station.
So many choices, so little stomach real estate. The trick is to get just a bite of many things, if you fill your plate with your favorite, you'll be missing out on a hundred other items. 

Don't forget to save room for dessert, because those choices are equally enticing, including a gellato bar with a half dozen flavor choices.

All said and done, we agreed it was the best of the genre, and I guess Ceasars knows it and charges for it. We actually were not going to go, but we won a couple hundred bucks in the casino, and decided it was "free", so what the heck. 

For a special night out, I highly recommend it. Everything was really good and nothing sits boiling on steam trays, which is what turns me off about buffet in general. Service is polite and professional.

Downside - because of what it is, you might spend time in line waiting for your favorite offering. People are in constant motion, so the traffic next to your table is brisk. Soft drinks included, you'll get another bill on your table if you order something else. (Sparking water was $5)

I am not a huge fan of buffets, but it was my bday weekend so I said 'why not.'  Omg best choice ever! The meat options were insane. They had a variety of sausages which were amazing. The spicy linguiça was my favorite. At first bite you can't taste the spice, but give it 5 seconds and bam! The prime rib and ribs were really good. 

The dim sum area was surprisingly good. Being from The SGV I hold Asian food to a high standard. What was a little disappoint, which is a trend with all buffets, was the sushi bar. The fish didn't taste as fresh as I wanted it to be. The Mexican area is really cute. I didn't try the street tacos, but they had Agua frescas in these cute jars. Sundays it's All you can drink mimosas and bloody Mary's! So cheers!

The service and the contemporary design was amazing. This has to be one of the better buffets on the strip.
Lunch Buffett...its ok but service is lacking..not enough coverage, so hard to get beverages..food is ok...meat are good though (spicy links sausage is good)

I'm so glad that my girlfriend and I went here for breakfast. It is very high end buffet but it's worth it. They have so many diverse cuisines from American to Asian. I totally loved their eggs benny and siomai. They also have other foods such as rib-eye steak, bacon, pizzas, different types of cheeses, soups, etc. The hostess that served us was very helpful; she went to our table every 20 minutes just to see if we needed anything. I suggest if you are planning to eat here, wear something loose and come here with an empty stomach. I would definitely come back here!

Went here for Dinner on a Friday at around 4:30. There was no line. I read a lot of reviews about how long the line is, so we came a little early to avoid that. The dinner food selection was really good, the prime rib was probably my favorite, but everything was pretty tasty. I would have liked to have seen some warm bread or rolls, all the bread they offered was cold and stale. I also was disappointed with their desserts. They had a good selection but they didn't taste all that great. Their service was also pretty slow when it came to bussing tables. Plates were piling up on our table for awhile before anyone came around. It's pretty good, but I would probably recommend The Wicked Spoon over this place.

Awesome weekday breakfast buffet! 

We were pleasantly surprised by the weekday breakfast buffet.  It was delicious and I thought the price was reasonable.  The servers were so attentive.  The atmosphere and decor were very nice.  I would definitely go back again.
Best buffett I've ever been too.   Seafood selection is awesome.  The only negative is the long line...

Best buffet on the strip! When I come to Vegas I always hit the buffets, this buffet is the best I've been to and I've been to them all. Excellent selection of food from seafood, American , Chinese,  and much much more. Everything tastes great and is fresh. The desert buffet has a huge selection with a freshly made crepe bar. I go at least 3 times, waits can be sometimes long so be prepared and come hungry!

Buffets! One of the things we look forward to when going on vacations! Foodies unite!

We headed here right after checking into Bellagio. Caesars Palace isn't far of a walk. We walked straight to the buffet area and was told to enter our name and contact info if you had a working phone and they will suggest a time in which you can start lining up to pay. We placed our name around 1:15pm, and was suggested to come back around 2:30pm. Holy we were hungry already at 1:15, then had to wait over an hour to get into line. When we got there we had to wait again to pay. They let a few people every 5-10min it seems pay and wait to be seated. We then had to wait for another 45min to pay! So the wait in total for non express was 2 hours!! Crazy!

To be honest, the wait if you're not eligible for the express/VIP lines, its not even worth it. The food was average at best. The people serving the food too had no emotion and my prime rib was tossed on my plate.

I highly recommend paying the extra $25 to bypass the first line if you decide to go.

For being the "number one buffet in Vegas", the service is horrendous. Karen, the front desk cashier, carried a pompous and judgmental demeanor. She not only raised her voice but acted as if we could not afford the meal. Having worked in customer service for a period of time, this is not a way to greet your customers.

As for food, the selection is great. The buffet claims they have the best seafood. The crab was dry and we ended up having to toss it away. The best was probably the prime rib here and the dim sum section. The food is probably why I gave two stars.

The line is long at night. Beware for terrible customer service!

This is my second time at the Bacchanal buffet and sadly I feel that nothing has changed and if anything the quality of food is only going down each passing day since my last visit in 2013.

My review is for the Lunch buffet during the Memorial day weekend. 

Check-in Kiosks
The only positive change that they seem to have introduced since my last visit. You can check in with your name , party size and cell# which will be used to contact you when you are ~30 mins away from being seated .  Alternatively for 15$ per person on top of the buffet price you can directly go the express lane.. my recommendation AVOID.. NOT WORTH IT.

Price:
Priced at 55$/person .. with taxes before gratuity the total I was looking at 260 bucks for a party of 4. so definitely $$$.

Food: 
You get quite a spread here with the following stations each with approx 4-5 dishes laid out.
- Asian
- Sushi 
- American
- Oaxacan
- Italian
- Meat Carving station
- Seafood section
- Dessert

For the spread on offer; there was nothing that quite stood out for me. Most disappointing stations being Asian and Italian .. absolutely no flavor whatsoever. Saving grace of the buffet: King Crab legs from the seafood station. The desserts were MEDIOCRE and AVERAGE.

Overall: If you are really want to see the extravagance of a Vegas buffet .. don't mind paying big bucks and an average wait time of  2 hrs ;then this buffet is for you.  I am definitely not coming back a third time.

One of the best buffets in Vegas. I'm not usually a fan of buffets as I don't eat the amount that's paid, but it's a great place to entertain guests during meal times. A great variety of choices from different cultures. I've only been here a couple times, but the service never disappoints.

I love going to the Bacchanal Buffet and suggest you do so too.  Yes it is the most expensive, except the Sterling Buffet at the MGM. They have so much to choose from and everything that i tasted was wonderful,  The carving station was my favorite, but all the other stations have great choice.  There are great desserts as well.  Make a point to go and  you will be glad you did

I NEVER GO ON A RNT BUT I APOLOGIZE

So... we're in Vegas.  We are having dinner and the Bacchanal caesars buffet.  I get that it's the holiday but we got here around 130 to get a wait time, we were told to come back a 802 to check in... we came to check in at 745, got in a like to wait until 830 to pay and then got into another line to be seated... they split us into three lines, parties of 2, parties of 3 to 5, and parties of 6 and above... the line for parties if two is al ml out empty, and they are seating the 6 or more before the 3 to 5.  This is the longest line and it's causing traffic.  When I asked why many tables of 6 were being seated before us, the reason was because it was a big table... I apologize but I don't care how good the food is, this is poor management.  I will not be coming back.  I did not pay 70 dollars per person to wait over 2 hours and being told that food stops at 1015. (It is currently 942... and yes I can walk away but I've already paid and I am f***ing hungry!)

Yes,  this is a 1 star because of service.

Overhyped! Seafood is good but meats are well done & full of fat/ grizzle. Dirty dipping cups stuck together. Serious lack of service - plate racks were left empty, drinks slow to be refilled & dirty plates stacking up at my table. Then they took our dirty plates & silverware! Took 5 mins to get us clean silverware. Won't go back.

If you're visiting Vegas, you have to try this place. HOLY DELICIOUSNESS. This was SEAFOOD HEAVEN for me. I'm not going to lie, I completely skipped everything and went straight for the seafood. I loaded my plate up with crab, oysters, sea bass, and shrimp for my first plate, then went back for more for my second plate. My dad must have had 3 plates of seafood. The lobster bisque and seafood paella were also amazing! Some of the seafood items I wasn't as thrilled about were the crawfish, sushi, ceviche, mussels, and clams, so my best advice would be to skip these and just grab more crab instead. 

I didn't try their prime rib because my brother said it wasn't worth it but their sausage was really juicy. I also really enjoyed their ramen. The broth was very rich and full of flavor. I barely remember anything but the seafood because I was in seafood bliss during the entire buffet. All I know is there was just SO MUCH FOOD. It was like sensory overload for me. I could barely contain my excitement. 

Luckily, I saved an itsy bitsy little pocket of room in my stomach for dessert which was perfect for ice cream, creme brulee, and red velvet whoopie pie. My only complaint about dessert is the creme brulee had a really weird texture to it. But there are so many different desserts to choose from, this didn't affect my experience at all. They have a big ice cream bar set up with a bunch of different flavors, mochi ice cream, pies and cakes for days, and a whole bunch of other stuff I can't remember because there was just too much food. 

Next time I'm back in Vegas, I will definitely stop by Bacchanal again. We were lucky enough to get in without having to wait at all. Try to go on a Sunday around 5 and you probably won't have to deal with the long lines I've heard about.

BEST. BUFFET. YET.

Wynn was always my favorite just because of their quality. M was delicious because of their quantity + price. But Bucchanal...I think tops both of these. We were the smart people who got in line around 1:45 pm and paid around 2:50...just in time to pay for lunch but get dinner food! We live such a dangerous life, don't we? 
We did have a party over 6 people, so they charged us 18% tip. (Total was $36. My friends went for dinner, and with the 18% gratuity, it was like $51.) I don't really see the need to tip at buffets more than a few bucks, but what can we do...

I think one reason I really loved this buffet was because of the ASIAN FOOD. Living away from home really makes me crave this! They had miso soup, hot and sour soup, and black chicken soup. They had sushi, PEKING DUCK, and other general asian dishes. The peking duck was sweet and delicious. I ate enough of that to pay for my meal.

They ran out of salmon at one point, and one of the chefs, after asking what I was waiting for, went to go get me some. How sweet!! Plus points for great service.

They also have a ton of seafood including crab legs and oysters. All of my friends got their money's worth eating that. 

They had rib eye steak, fresh-made tacos, fresh fruit, lamb chops, amazing desserts including innovative ice cream flavors, and an all-around great selection of food. 

DEFINITELY RECOMMEND.

One of the best buffets in LV. Thanks to my high roller friend, we did not have to wait just to come in. Since being here, I have been craving for their red velvet small pancakes. I loved their chandeliers made of glasses. I want one at home.

4.6 Stars

Located in Caesars Palace.

**Not my first time here**

The four of us decided to try our luck around 8:45pm on Sunday evening.  Usually there is and hour to 2 hour wait here, but to our surprise there was no line.  

I've had my fare share of buffets and I must say this is by far the best one i have ever been to.  It is on the expensive side for a buffet ($59.99), but they are offering top notch ingredients and quality. 

Not many buffets offer Alaskan king crab, but Bacchanal does, however they do mix the legs in along with snow crab legs.  The dry rub bbq ribs were some of the best ribs I've ever tasted.  The dessert section has everything and anything you want.

Service was very friendly, always checked on our drinks and cleared our dishes right away

Overall Experience:
Service - 9/10
Cleanliness - 9/10
Food - 9.5/10
Value - 7.5/10
Parking - N/A

I'm not sure how to rate this buffet.  I don't want to be unfair since my expectations were high but I also think that any buffet as expensive as this one needs to be spectacular.  I'll start with the good.  Service was excellent, atmosphere is lovely and everything is clean and pretty.  I only loved 2 things; the fresh squeezed OJ and the crepes.  I liked the caprese salad and the tacos but I can get all of those things anywhere.  I actually did the worst grossest thing and spit out a couple bites.  The truffle scallop potatoes and the buffalo wings were sooooo bad.  I know that's disgusting but that's how bad they tasted.  Don't worry I was discreet and sitting in a corner .
Pho was yuck and the noodles were strange.  Dim sum is better in China town.  Desserts were ok but nothing blew me away.  As far as overpriced buffets go I've been to the Wynn buffet and it was much better.

This was my second time here and the first time was amazing - the smoked brisket I had the first time changed my life! 

However, this time around, the brisket kind of sucked and the rest was just ok. It was good but not amazing like I remembered from the first time. The dessert were great - I had a crepe and cream brûlée. Overall it was worth it but it wasn't as mind blowing as the first time I went here.
Came back again to this buffet because it is the best! This time I took pictures for all to see the wonderful delicious food  they have here.

First buffet I've tried in Vegas, best food in a buffet I've ever had, but worse service I've ever had at a buffet. 


We had to flag down other waiters to bring us drinks/refills because ours went MIA. Not acceptable, service should be good all around, not just with some waiters.

Great variety of dishes and love how many of them are already proportioned in individual servings so that they're not picked over or more importantly handled by gross possibly sick people.  I also love that they have a new check in and wait system.  Having a toddler it's important that we don't have to stand in like for over an hour, the new kiosk system where they text you when your table is almost ready is such a great concept.  The reason I couldn't give 5 stars is just that buffet food is never gonna be super hot or fresh cause it's made in big batches.

OMG SO MUCH FOOD! The price is definitely worth what you get! Imagine unlimited crab legs, lobster, freshly cut meat, and macaroons! I couldn't stop going back for more food! I even had to unbutton my pants!

I am only writing this review based on the wait and I intend to update it when or if I can actually convince myself to wait that long for food and I have had a chance to actually eat inside to determine if it is actually worth the initial wait.

The wait for this restaurant is abysmal. And I could understand it if they were crowded or something, but we waited for over an hour while we could clearly see that all of the tables were not full inside. I knew about this place and that the wait was unusually long, but it's totally different hearing that the wait will be long and then actually having to stand there and wait.

We had a show to go to at 7 so we got there at 4:30 to check in for dinner. When we got there there was 10 people in line ahead of us. Not 10 people waiting to pay, 10 people who already paid and were waiting to be seated. And, as I said earlier, there were several tables inside that were clearly empty. 

At the end of the day, none of this would have really bothered me because I understand how things go: short staff, not everyone is at their table all the time, or they were more crowded than they appeared. I get it, things happen. 

The thing that upset me the most is that larger parties will be seated first no matter when they show up. It didn't matter that there were, now 8, people in line for 45 minutes; they sat a group of 10 once their whole party showed up. And it's not like this was random or whatever there were two separate large parties that showed up after us and were seated before we even got close to the entrance. So they obviously had the staff.

Now that I'm thinking about it I might not go back because I really don't want to have to experience that again.

In the end, we waited for an hour and a half when there were only 10 people in front of us when we got there, to having 6 people in front of us and the line behind us was way past the stanchions. 

I realized why the line was always so long whenever I passed by; it's because they just make you stand out front for no apparent reason.

After an hour and thirty we asked for a refund because we were not going to have enough time to eat and make our show over at T-Mobile Arena. We ended up grabbing McDonald's before the show which was way more satisfying after standing around for nothing for so long.

My boyfriend and I were excited to try this place and we thought, by the line, this place was going to be fantastic. Well, it wasn't. You have to go to a kiosk to put your name in, the wait time for almost 3 hours. But wait, if you pay $25 per person, you can be a VIP and not have to wait so we decided to do that. It costs $168 for a BUFFET! I get it, we are in Vegas, everything is pricey but come on!!!! Ok, so the food, there was a boat load of it but overall, it wasn't that great, wasn't horrible either. The deserts looked great but they didn't taste very well at all. A lot of wasted food. Would I recommend this place? Absolutely not!

I was excited to eat at this place seeing that it had better reviews than Mandalay Bay, but was very disappointed. My stomach did not settle well and ended up puking whatever I ate in the morning.. which I found very weird because I ate other food after the buffet but managed to only puke whatever I ate at Bacchanal. Food was okay.. it's just beautifully presented. I think this place is just hyped, honestly. With how much paid, this place was definitely not worth it.

--edit 6.11.17.

Dropped 2 stars to only 1. No apology was made and they have seemed to ignore my case. No follow-up or investigation was done whatsoever.
Best buffet I've been to. And such beautiful decorations. Delicious meals, great service!

Bacchanal is in the top 5 buffets in Vegas.  With over 500 items to choose from, I was in food heaven.  At this Buffet, you not only get the volume and variety but also the high standard and excellent cuisine.  The rule of trying a bit of everything has to go out the window because there is way too much food (for me).  That is not a complaint, by the way.  Walk through the whole Buffet before choosing.  It was a long walk!  The food is endless.  There are 9 different cuisines or show kitchens.
I started at the Chinese Cuisine, not because it's my favourite, it's because it was at the end of the buffet and I had originally thought I could start here so as not to miss anything.  As I was getting full, I had to bypass some sections.  The authenticity and quality was very evident in the appearance and taste.  I was going to take a little from each of the 9 show kitchens., but I soon decided to just go with my instincts.  Then for my second plate I went for the pizzas.  The one I loved the best was the one with the truffle.  My 3rd plate was the best which has a lot to say for the high quality since I was getting full.  I went for the melt in your mouth prime rib with horse radish, crab leg, the butteriest (is that a word?) richest mashed potatoes in the universe, prawns, oyster on the half shell and a little shot glass of melted butter.  It was to die for!  I decided to take pictures of the desserts because there was no way I could sample even half of what they had.  At least my husband shared bites of his selections.  THE BEST buffet creme brûlée is at the Bacchanal!  I ate every drop of the creamy goodness with the contrast of the crunch of the sugar topping.  I also loved the cheesecake pop, and mini carrot cake.   Worth every dollar we spent and probably the BEST Buffet that have had in Vegas or elsewhere for that matter.  It followed Cosmopolitan's lead to increase the quality and excellence, rather than mass production  cooking so it's not hard to believe that it has surpassed the Cosmopolitan, in my opinion.  The table service was wonderful as well.

At first I thought this was a super expensive buffet, but then realized that they had almost every type of food there. Pasta, seafood, chinese, japanese, mexican, you name it. 

We first got a number to even get on the line, after that we waited about an hour to actually be seated. We started with japanese, then had a little pasta and snow crab legs. Everything was what you would expect it to be, maybe just a LITTLE bland. Unlimited seafood (super fresh) as well as everything else of course. I think the best part would be between the seafood and the dessert. Dessert was like.... everything you expected it to be. All in all, I feel like it's something you have to try when in Vegas and it's worth the extra splurge!

Best buffet in Vegas as of August 2014. 

Asian section is kind of tucked away in the back but once you find it there's sushi,  noodle soups in different varieties,  dim sum and other yummy dishes.  
Meat section, as I called it but I think properly it was the American section,  served a carving station with all the meat you could ask for,  tons of potato dishes (my fave was the truffled potatoes), even a quinoa dish, although it didn't taste particularly healthy.

Bottomless Mimosas were great but dangerous. 

Tips
* Stay awhile and enjoy dessert too. Green tea creme brulee was awesome!
* Asian section is in the back (#minoritycorner)
* Truffled potatoes = must try
* Stop by the noodle station

Before eating here, I would have to say that Bellagio's buffet is the best on the Strip.  After eating here, I am not sure anymore.  

I was lucky and the line was short for dinner.  It's a lot bigger than I thought it would be.  There so many selections that I am not sure where to start.  In one corner there's an Asian buffet.  It's deep inside another room so you have to go and look for it.  On the outside, there's variety of Mexican, Italian, and American.  I pretty much tried a little bit of everything, especially the seafood. They are all great.

The service was great and all the staffs are extra friendly.  If you can go to one buffet during your Vegas visit, try this one or Bellagio's.  You can't go wrong with either one.

In all honesty, this was the best buffet I've ever been to in my life. The variety is endless especially because they have dishes from all types of cultures and different cuisines. The best part about it all was the fact that the foods they incorporated from different cultures such as my own (Chinese) tasted exactly the way it would've if you would have gotten it from an actual restaurant that dedicated it's food to that culture. 

Me and my friends went here on a Sunday afternoon thinking it would be extremely packed and busy, but luckily to our surprise, it wasn't at all. We were all prepared to wait over an hour to eat even though we were all extremely hungry but figured with all the buzz bout how good it is that it would be worth the wait. They have a pretty efficient system in which you enter your name, phone number, and the size of your party into an iPad that places you in the wait list. We confirmed with the attendant there and she told us it would be about a 30 minute wait, which isn't bad at all considering we were prepared to wait even longer. However, we only ended up waiting 10-15 minutes!!
**I do believe they have a separate package deal in which you can skip over the line if you pay an additional to the buffet meal price (around $50)**

My favorites were the great selection of meats, the dim sum, seafood, and the endless variety of desserts.

Overall, even though it's pricey, I think it's worth the try if you're ever in Vegas. The price definitely is worth it and cheaper than you think if you actually eat things like prime rib and snow crab legs because those alone at an actual restaurant as a meal would already equate to the price you pay if not over that.
The best buffet by far out in Vegas. I highly recommend this to anyone looking for a nice place to eat.

By far one of the best buffets in Vegas!! It is quite pricey but all the food selections make it worth it. Wait wise is okay depending on the time of day you go. They set up a kiosk that texts you when it's busy. Their selection of crabs legs steamed or iced is one of a kind. No other buffet offers steamed or iced. Dessert section is amazing with gelato, crepes made to order and their huge choices of cakes. Peach tea is a definite must. You'll definitely need to be wheeled out afterwards!

They had warm snow crab legs, which was different cuz it's usually cold. I prefer the cold crab legs because they're sweeter. They had macaroons for dessert which was a bonus. Their udon tastes like regular udon broth. They had a lot of oysters and different toppings for the oysters like horseradish. Most places don't give that. I liked their tamarin juice drink. It was a little sour.

Honestly, hands down, the best buffet I've ever been to. No, I am not getting paid for this, I promise ;)

I'm not a huge fan of any the buffets in Vegas. I've never really liked Studio B Buffet (M Hotel) or Wicked Spoon. I only think Studio B is worth it when it's cheap (ie Friday lunch). 

On a Sunday evening, we stood in line starting at around 5:15 and didn't get seated until close to 6:30. Cost is average to what you normally pay at buffets, about $45-60? I think we got a decent discount for using our Total Rewards card. 

Seafood - AMAZING! Oh so fresh & delicious - halibut (buttery & melts in your mouth) & sashimi (restaurant quality, fresh tasting). Everything else was just as great! Lots of stuff to choose from. Dessert section was probably my favorite, I wanted to eat EVERYTHING!! I loved the fresh souffle, made to order crepes and  large selection of gelato ice cream flavors. Another plus, food presentation! :P

Wait and price for Bacchanal was well worth it! I'd go again ;) My only concern is that Bacchanal is indeed new and hasn't been opened (or re-opened) for a long time, so I am worried that the quality might not stay for long. Hurry and go!
oyster is not fresh at all, too few choices of food, dim sums are awful. Very disappointed experience

This is a nice buffet inside Caeser's Palace and for the money and what you can get if you are someone who can eat a decent amount, it's a good deal. They have a lot of things - from sushi to prime rib to crawfish to crab to burgers to cheese to charcuterie and of course the desserts. Of course, it's on the pricier side for buffets in Vegas, but regardless it's good and worth it. They have a ton of good desserts too. I'd recommend it as far as buffets in Vegas go. There's far worse ways to spend something like $40.

Bacchanal Buffet, currently ranks number 1 buffet, or at least what they advertise on the strip of Vegas and all over the brick walls of Caesar's Palace.

My tip for you: If you plan to have dinner here, come early for dinner hour. We arrived at around 5pm and had to wait for 15 minutes, but the line past 7pm was miserably long. 

Dinner (Sunday-Thursday from 3pm-10pm) costs $44.99

I felt like Katniss in the Hunger Games trilogy walking into the feast at the Capitol in the second book, except that I was not forced to join the game and had to fight for my life. Well, that being said, every station presents a new temptation. Seafood, meat, Mexican, Italian (pizza, lasagna, pasta), charcuterie, salad bar, Japanese (sashimi and sushi), Chinese (charsiu pork, bbq ribs, peking duck, dim sum), and desserts. Wow! My eyes had a food coma before my stomach.

My favorite savory dishes: prime beef (juicy and tender), turkey meatball (huge, and flavors were spot on), peking duck (crispy skin, yummy), lasagna (served in small clay pot, pretty and yummy).

The desserts station is located in the center of the restaurant, showcasing a bonanza of decadent sweets. OMG! The boyfriend can't get enough of their chewy macarons, of which the texture that we find only at 'Lette. My eyes sparkle seeing my favorite frozen sweets, Japanese mochi ice cream, and of course Italian gelato. 

Overall, I could only sample maybe a little more than half of the selection at Bacchanal since I skipped a few stations such as salad, sushi, pizza, dimsum, but everything tasted delicious. We left feeling completely satisfied and satiated.

I don't get why this Buffet is only a 4 stars! It should be 5
Yeah there's big lines to come in. And yes it was $50 per person. But don't u think it was worth it!! I'm that type of girl that doesn't eat a lot however paying $50 u know i had to go big. I tried a lot; Steak, Tacos, sushi, pasta, and off course don't forget the dessert. Yeah i went big; and yeah i went back to get more. Of course u know i had to take a long as break yo go get more, but damn it was worth it. The food was excellent! I loved it! And YES i will be back!! Yumm!!

Been to many of the buffets at Las Vegas, but this was by far the largest I've ever been too! So many selections and all the food was top of the line. Being from Texas I'm a hard judge on BBQ and this place held it's own! The brisket was smoked and juicy and the short ribs were to die for! Word of advice get small portions so you can try a little bit of everything, they have fresh made to order street tacos that were incredible! Overall wonderful experience and upscale environment. It's a must do when coming to Vegas!

They offer large selection of all kind of food.
Food is good but it remains a buffet, it's not a 5 star restaurant.

You can choice from pizza, pasta, sushi, seafood, meat, fish, vegetables, pretty much everything..
For desert, they offer pastries, fruits, cakes.

You end up being very full after this buffet.

I am not definitely not a buffet person, but the food here did not meet my expectations. 

1. Not worth $80 per person, went on a holiday weekend, so it was probably a bit pricier than usual.

2. The food was a bit salty, especially the seafood in my opinion. 

3. I didn't find any dish that I particularly favored or even liked. The only "ok" dishes were the Japanese food.

4. Servers are friendly and nice, and sadly, I think that was the only pro.

5. Would I go again? I don't think so.

We went there on a Sunday brunch time which I assume is the most packed.y sister bought a Groupon coupon which gave us an add on of a VIP line and 1 mimosa but we missed it since we didnt read the fine print which is only until 10am. (Bad offer). So we had to pay extra - which is already the full price of the buffet and had to wait in line as all the rest so it was nearly an hour before we went in around noon time.

Choices: Set up: cold cuts, breakfast, mexican soft tacos, ceviche, pasta, pizza, salads, dimsum, asian hot dishes, tons of desserts and a huge line up of meats of sausages, ham, beef.  What was missing: no oysters, scallops, very limited dimsum, hot entrees were indian or chinese only.  Hard to reach the dimsum where there was this hanging roof over the food that prevented you to reach it.

Flavors: dimsum was overcooked and the hakaw skin was too thick. The soft tacos was just okay as the meat was tough. Hot entrees was bland. Even the fried rice was not tasty. Red velvet pancake was dry and overcooked.

Service: lacking in servers so simple thing like water could not be refilled.  

Overall, very disappointing. Buffets in Asia is way way better with better varieties and even better service.

My expectations were perhaps too high. The wait was approximately 1 hr, but we anticipated that. Service was average. We had to flag down our waitress for a cup refills. 
Food: The crab legs are pre split for ease in eating, unfortunately this made them water logged and bland. The Asian section was poor. Chewy noodles and minimally seasoned. The vegetable spring roll was mushy inside. The cooked bok choy was cold. I would pass on this section. 
I enjoyed the Mexican section. Chicken tamales were great. 
The only section really worthwhile was the carving station.
My husband's reaction: "For the money, I would rather go to a nice steakhouse."  I agree.

My favorite buffet in Las Vegas.  Whether for the seafood station, carvery, or Asian station.  Great variety of food and each hot and cold station all stood on its own.  Not like some buffets on the strip that is only good for one or two stations.

Friendly service and great layout for easy access.

You do realize this is buffet, right? There is something to be expected regarding the food quality at a buffet, period. On that scale, I see why this place has been named the #1 buffet by USA Today like 4 years in a row or something? 

The variety is phenomenal. The taste of the food is better than buffet expected, but only if you don't allow yourself to be blinded by how nicely designed and kept the interior is. I do have to note that how incredibly clean they keep this place is pretty spectacular, given the amount of volume going through. 

Some of the food tasted pretty amazing, some of it was meh. Regardless, they keep everything STOCKED to the max (the cold seafood line had me drooling before getting seated) except for the hot crab legs. 

If you have a sweet tooth, you'll be in heaven at the dessert section here. This spot is a Vegas must-try, once.

Well we visited the Bacchanal on June 5 while staying at Caesars Palace.We wanted a good seafood buffet and decided this would be our choice. Big Big disappointment! Found seafood to be lacking, they have very limited choices . Snow crab no King  Crab unless you pay more. no lobster any shape or size to be found . nothing but cold shrimp, no fried shrimp! cold snow crab unless you want it from a pot of boiling water in the Italian section!You can't let crab sit in boiling water like that NO FLAVOR LEFT IN CRAB!!       
little cold plates of salmon,little cold baskets of chicken beautiful taco bar nobody ordering tacos because all condiments were out and stayed empty whole time we were there. Two stars are for the awesome meat station, but overall no one seemed to be walking the buffet to keep things full or clean. Meat was laying in front of station as was shrimp.  If all you want are oysters, cold crab and cold shrimp this is the place for u otherwise keep looking.Also the ticket gives you a 2 hour time limit that's a new one for me.

I am not sure why everyone feels that this is a great place for dinning.  Personally, I feel that I can spent my money in a much better place.  After dinning in this place it just confirms my opinion that buffet does not offer quality food. The buffet does offer a very wide variety of food choices and if that's all you look for in food than this is the place for you.  If you seek quality...you will not find it here.  I know thAt one can have spend $50 at a much better place.

Even if you're hungover get there early so you don't have to wait in an extremely long line!!! This is without a doubt my favorite buffet in Vegas! I has every type of food and it is so freaking high class. I want to go there again right now! If you're in Vegas and want to know where the best buffet is it is definitely the Bacchanal Buffet at the Caesar's Palace.

Amazing service and food is always available. We came for brunch, which came out to around $100 for 3 people. We went in at 9:56 and ended up paying $10 less per person because at 10:00, they crank up the prices a bit! All servers and waiters were extremely friendly and cleaned up our plates accordingly. We were seated almost immediately and the lineup for tickets took less than five minutes. Brunch is a great, inexpensive (compared to dinner) option. Lots of good food still :)
Absolutely the best buffet in Vegas! The variety is amazing. I can eat my weight worth in fine cheeses and my favorite: pork belly!

This is a really good and unique buffet. I can probably forgive the ridiculous waiting procedure they have since the food  exceeded my expectations. Speaking of which: you have to make a reservation at a computer ticketing thing and then they'll text you when you're suppose to get in line to pay.... Then you might have to wait some more depending on how many more people need to be seated. Our estimated wait time was 2 hours.... Ouch!

We came when brunch was being phased into dinner. For once I had a non-chewy prime rib at a buffet! The selection is interesting ranging from few Indonesian dishes, mini medium rare burgers, and bottled juices and horchata, to smoked salmon and good sushi. I really like how delicious the desserts are (and they were pretty cute too). 

The cashiers and seating hostesses weren't rude but it was obvious they were overwhelmed with the amount of people. The people at the food stations were nice especially the guys at the meat carving area. 

So, in short, I definitely recommend this place as long as you don't mind the wait or price.

My first buffet in Las Vegas and I have to say I was pretty blown away for $30. The seafood selection was ok, but everything was of great quality and not over salted. I enjoyed the fresh juices (Tamarindo, Orchata, Mango, etc.) and the bbq selections. The prime rib was perfect and so was the hen and spicy sausage. I also had some shao mai (shumai?) and ha kao. I was also able to squeeze in some desserts and I enjoyed the chocolate creme brulee, flan, and carrot cake. The cheesecake was very mild in flavor and didnt feel right in terms of texture. It was too smooth. I wish I had a bigger appetite to try more since there was Mexican, Italian, and Asian cuisines that I missed out on.

I'd come here again if I people wanted to try it, but otherwise I'll hit up the next buffet to see what others have to offer.

There is a lot of variety at this buffet which is the best thing about it. We had a party of six and got seated fairly fast. Thy have Asian food, sushi, soup, Mexican food, American food and Seafood. The oysters were a disappointment, I just feel as if the quality of the food isn't that great. Probably wouldn't come here again but it's definitely a good nice buffet and I'm happy I tried it.
hands down best buffett in vegas. the wynn is probablt comes in second.
Crazy good! This buffet is the be-all, end-all! It has EVERYTHING (except lobster). Service was good and the variety was insane.

This place was chaotic during the holiday. We got cut while standing in line and the staff didn't want to address it. The plates were dirty, food was meh at best, overpriced, and the service was terrible.

What are you doing reading this review when you can be drinking unlimited amounts of horchata in glass bottles and eating foods from various parts of the world at bacchanal buffet? 

Worth the money. Always finish Vegas off here before heading back home. It's my favorite buffet!

We came to the Bacchanal Buffet on a Monday morning, around 10:30. There was no wait for us, a party of 4. They were still in breakfast service at that point -we didn't realize the menu would switch to lunch at 11- so we got to try a LOT of different things. This is a smart way to pay the breakfast price and experience twice the food. Also- around 10:45 there started to be more and more people showing up. By the time we left there was a huge line. 

Highlights:
-Red Velvet Pancakes
-Shrimp and grits
-Made to order ramen and udon 
-Fresh juices: cucumber, watermelon, guava, horchata
-Slab bacon
-Crab Benedict 
-Creme brûlée 
-gelatos 

Lowlights:
-Oysters: they didn't taste fresh at all :(
-Oyster shooters 
-Lobster bisque: not served hot enough and no lobster flavor 
-Sushi: limited selection and didn't look or taste very fresh
-Donuts with bananas and nuts: sickeningly sweet 
-Ceviche
-Dim Sum: the only one I liked was the pork bun. All of the others were dry and bland. Seemed like they were sitting out for a long time
-Shaved ice dessert 

Overall, I think that the Bacchanal buffet is a fun and enjoyable dining experience- the service was quick and efficient and the plethora of options is exciting to look at. The sheer number of food items and desserts is extremely pleasing to the eye and will keep you occupied for a long time. Now- is the food actually good?? Not really. There were only a handful of things I thought actually tasted good and were worth eating more than a bite of. But that's part of the Buffet experience right? I would recommend Bacchanal Buffet for it's sheer size and variety of food choices - you won't have the best tasting meal of your life, but it's a lot of fun nonetheless!

I really wanted to like this place. Came for brunch and thought it would be great judging by the long line. Was excited for crab legs but there was only crab claws.... Not even sure how to eat those. Other selections were not impressive either. Would not recommend.

Vegas buffets....this is it!!  The extreme array of choices and the freshness speak for themselves.  But....be prepared to go away pounds bigger and stuffed to the brim!  Sooo good but tooo much!  Make me leave now!
Worth it to go & just hope the waitress/waiter are not to uptight(busy or not) during shifts.

I think the price is pretty high. $50 a buffet! The food selection is good but not phenomenal to pay the price. 

The line can get pretty long sometimes so its a good idea to go early. 

The desserts are pretty but i didnt fimd one that taste great. I definitely tried to!

They have good pho. Sushi is good as it gets for a sashimi lover. The line for prime rib is the longest. 

They have mexican, asian, italian, and breakfast foods. 

The bathroom is outside the buffet - atleast thats the only one i saw so i used it. I was afraid i might not get back in the buffet when i went lol

So my two buddies came up with the bright idea of paying credit card roulette. At the Caesar's Buffet no less. Reluctantly I threw my AmEX into the pot. And guess what? My friggin card gets pulled. I was like whatever man. We put our names in the res system and it was a 90 min wait......at 3pm!! Wtf! So we go to the casino to gamble, which of course is what they want you to do.

Fast forward about 100 min and our names are finally paged. So I go and pay...$200! For 3 of us....oh man I say. I'm gonna milk this for what its worth. We sit down about 430pm. And this is after a night of clubbing and boozing so don't mind us as we lethargically make our way to the table. 

We all scope out the spread and we were awestruck. Never in my life have I seen a spread like this. Anything and everything. They have it. My strategy at buffets is to sample a little of everything. But really on this day, and with this size, I just couldn't do it. I couldn't. I grabbed some japanese food and soup for a "starter", then some crab and shrimp. Then on to the heavier stuff like ribs sausage and other bbq. By this time I was stuffed! But alas, I have a sweet tooth so I had to do dessert. This is where Bacchanal shines, IMO. They got everything here. Macroons, gelato, cakes, cookies, fruit....aww yeah! 

Good value? An unequivocal no! But it is a must try. And you are in Vegas. So just do it. You won't regret it. Until the next morning. Oh and we sat there like the fat a$$es that we were from 430 to almost 9pm! And our hostess, which I won't name because we don't want to get her in trouble, was so awesome. And cute! She let us stay and just engorge ourselves.

For the price, I expected more.  My boyfriend went to the carving station for prime rib, the chef refused to give him a rare piece.  He asked to see a manager, she apologized and said she would be right back with a rare piece.  We never saw her again.  I'm not sure what the hype is, I don't think the food is much better than other buffets, just a few more food choices.

SO. MUCH. FOOD. Do not visit if you are "sort of hungry" as you will quickly get the desire to have a stomach double the size of the one you've got! A true cornucopia that the god Bacchus would no doubt visit himself if he existed lol.

Every dish you could possibly ever be in the mood for ever. Here. Fresh. Hot. My last time in Vegas was my first time coming here and I will certainly make it a point to come here at least once every time I come back. They've certainly earned every 5 star review and the claim to the "Best Buffet In Vegas" throne.

Variety of cuisines to suit your eating preference. Space yourself slowly so that you can enjoy the food to soak in the atmosphere. Aaahhh!!! Don't forget to check out the planet dessert. It's better seen then I say it all...

Note: if you prefer to eat vegetarian or vegan ask the chef and they will customize or prepare a dish of your choice. Ask them to prepare a small portion else a lot of food gets wasted.

Large food selections but there weren't any dishes that wow'ed us but food was decent/good. The wait was also too long. Overall, tons of space n food was decent, but for the price of (50 dollars), n the long wait, the food doesn't make up for it.

The best breakfast on the strip a variety of food get the unlimited drinks well worth it the money the staff go above and beyond to make the experience great ask for Julie during our brunch experience as your server.

We came here twice of course different times, when it first open. And this buffet is part of buffet to buffet the 24 hr bracelet pay $10 extra, so well worth it. The seafood are so fresh and desserts are awesome, lots of selection. My bf have to eat here every time we are in vegas, this time he ate the salmon and steam bass thru the night. He raved and noted next time we are we will eat here first. 

Only thing that is disappoint is the line, never fails it takes a good hour and half other than its our second place where we have to have..

Serves needs to be a little more prompt, slow attending.

Not a huge buffet fan, but hands down the best buffet option in Vegas imo! Great assortment of food choices! Service is good in the two times I've been.  Asian, meat, seafood, and dessert stations are the best!

If you had to only choose one buffet to go to during your stay in Vegas, choose Bacchanal. Usually buffet food is mediocre, but all the food at this buffet was delicious!! You really get the most bang for your buck. There's also a very large variety and the buffet is split into different sections - American, Asian, Italian, seafood, and a whole section dedicated to just desserts! 

Do not plan on arriving hungry! My family and I had to wait ~2 hours to be seated. So we spent the time playing in the casino!

The lines are too long and they manage the lines horribly. There are 5 different lines. Two lines for VIP and seven star?!. 3 lines are divided into 1 or 2 people, 3-5 people and more than 5 people groups. We've been waiting for two hours since we were party of two. People who were behind us with other group of lines were even much faster. I guess they have fewer number of tables for 1 or two people. I think this is terrible management and unfair.. I do not recommend this restaurant.

This place has the worst service. We were put in a corner far from the main dining area. When we asked for a table closer to the main dining hall, we were asked to exit the restaurant and wait in line again. Then they pretty much ignored us while we stayed in line. They wouldn't come back to us until almost 15-20mins later. If this is a their way to punish customers for asking for another table, this place would be the model restaurant for it.

Ate there last night and was very disappointed and left sick. The service is terrible! Don't order the bottomless drinks because the server never comes back to get you another drink I paid $15 for one small glass of wine. The cold food was warm and the hot food was just luke warm. The food isn't very good quality. Then to top it off my boyfriend and I both got sick and threw up all $135 of what we ate. NEVER GOING BACK!

So I have never ever been a fan of buffets until I came to Vegas. If I could sum up this review I would just say if you're in Vegas, you must go here. This is the holy grail of  Vegas buffets. It is also the priciest but well worth the money. There's usually somewhat of a wait to dine here but it's that good. They have the most food selections in all of their stations. You have anything from crab legs, tomahawk, prime rib, oysters, tacos made in front of you, ceviches, lamb, Asian food, you have everything. There is something for everyone. Desserts are great, creme brulee, carrot cake, gelato, everything and anything. 
Honestly, the only negative thing I found with this buffet was service. It wasn't horrible, it was just bleh. Both times we've been here our server seemed uninterested in whatever and barely swung by our table. However, every time I'm in Vegas I do come to the buffet.

I was kind of disappoint may be because I had too much expectation for this place. Went there on a Friday night, wait for about 20 mins. 

Service was 4 stars

But Food worth no more than 3 stars.
King crabs were fine like any buffets in Vegas.
They do have seafood paella, but its lack of flavor and dry.
Chinese dim sum disappointed me.

The crepe with ice cream was good 
They had japanese ramen which is unique to other buffet.
oyster shooter was not bad.

Overall, I'll be still going back to Wicked spoon instead of bacchanal

Went here for brunch on a saturday. The food wsnt as good as it was the last time I was here. The quality just wasnt up to par for the price($52.99). Our server was great however do extra star for her. She even brought a little birthday dessert plate when she found out it was my bday. And my mimosa glass was never empty for long befire she refilled it. The bagel and Lox bar and the made to order omelets were defintely my favorite part of my meal though. I think I'll check out Wicked Spoon next time I'm in town.
Lots of selection which is great when you're hungry.  None of which are considered quality food.  One thing to note is to avoid the dim sum.  You were warned.

I used to like coming here but I feel like the food is okay now. There's nothing really special about it anymore.  I just like the dessert bar. And it's way overpriced. I'm not sure if I'll be coming back here.

Simply disgusting. We went there yesterday night at 6:30PM and the line wasn't too bad,30 mins.

We paid 170 (included tax, open bar and tip) for 2 people. The service wasn't bad but really fast and impersonal.

The food was the major disappointment: bad quality and all cold, the only decent thing were the dessert.

Just a place for turist with that money you can go eat everywhere else on the strips with a better quality.

Food was definitely decent and I don't mind spending good money on good food. However, the price was much more than the food was worth. Flavors were a bit lacking. Crab legs were flavorless. Singapore noodles were very good. Sushi was decent. Wagu beef was not flavorful at all. Thick cut bacon slab was very good fatty but that's where your flavor comes from. Guy running the Mexican food station was awesome and so were his tacos. Pizza not very flavorful. Seaweed salad was one of the best things there. Duck was not great but the pork next to it was pretty good. Poke was good. I was not unhappy that I went but I was a bit underwhelmed. Waitress was very attentive and they did a good job of refreshing all of the stations. Gelato very good but toffee chocolate chip bad. A fresh, warm, gooey chocolate chip would have been awesome. Would like to see a higher concentration on quality over quantity but that was not the case. Waited about 30 minutes to get in but that was what I expected. I have been to the Wynn and Bellagio buffets and thought this was about the same as the Bellagio (with a much larger selection) but not quite as good as the Wynn. Going to try Wicked Spoon. Hope I'm not disappointed there.

Plenty of food and friendly staff. The seafood  station is awesome . Large shrimp and deveined. The crab legs are split open and easy to devour. 

All in all a worthwhile buffet, recommend.

At $50 a pop a bit pricey, but what the hell ur in Vegas so go for it
