The best buffet so far!!!! Great quality!  I went on a Thursday afternoon around 130-330 and towards the end they brought out oysters and king crab legs. I think they change the food around 3-330. It is on the pricey side but it's so worth it!

Omg! My fav buffet in Vegas! Every time I come to Las Vegas I try to make it my pit stop. Food is great as always. Good quality food not like those cheaply buffets. It's pricey but it's so good. It's $60 ppl but hey it's Vegas. You have to be ready to spend money right?! The Chinese/ Asian foods is on point with flavors. BBQ is amazing! Also the seafoods! 

Cons: long ass lines! To get in and for the seafood section.

After hearing all the hype, I was very disappointed in Bacchanal. For $50 and a long line it was not worth it. The selection was huge but nothing memorable and the things I liked can be found at other buffets for a lower cost and shorter line. They were missing a lot of the stuff my friends ate. I guess once buffets get popular they stop cooking the good stuff. Dessert was good, probably because its hard to mess it up. I probably won't come back anytime soon. Maybe if it was cheaper or shorter line

Line is crazily long, but we got a bit of luck to have platinum card; yet, still had to wait for another 10 min to be seated. All I can say is either the place too popular or seating arrangement is quite awkward!

This was by far the best buffet I have ever had in my life. The options are endless I had amazing lamb chops and a darn good prime rib. The seafood was so fresh and there was nothing there to disappoint. Save room for dessert they have made to order crepes which are so good. This was so worth the price and so good to eat.

this place SUCKS so hard!

all the hot food was almost cold and all the desserts were strangely not cold enough. the food was flavorless and blah. the best thing here was probably the warm crab legs which you can get in the italian section. 

don't even bother with the "sushi", so gross. 

all the cold seafood was either sitting in water too long or was washed too much. 

the wait staff is super busy so they were not the friendliest.

WILL NEVER RETURN!

We went here with a big group of 18 people. We got in quite easy. We waited in a separate line after we paid. There is a line for i think 7 or more people. Anyways, we got seated. The service after that is  1 star. Nobody cleaned up our table. We have to put away our plates in a tray that was set on the side for i dont know what. We piled up our plates there. And then a server picked it up but never asked us what we need or came back to clean up our table. One hour later no drinks no server. I asked one guy there, i guess he is the supervisor, i asked him to get a server for us coz we need coffee and drink refills. Then a different server got our drinks. And then 20 mins later our server came and asked if we need anything??? So it took 1 hr and 20 mins for her to check on us and we already paid gratuity for that?? For the price of the buffet $77 a person and to get such poor service. The food is not even worth that much. All the food that i got was salty. I love dessert and i was happy with the macaroons and thats it. I want to take back the gratuity. She did almost nothing for us. Got us one drink each? Lets just say we are las vegas locals with a group of 18 or more people will never come back to Bacchanal.

The food was very good. My favorites were the meat carving station, the street tacos and the king crab. The pork belly and the sweet potato tots were also very good.  In my opinion it was worth the price. The only negative thing I can say about the buffet was the desert bar. It all looked really good but didn't taste as good as it looked.

All I can say is WOW! This buffet has EVERYTHING You can imagine food wise. We went for a bottomless mimosa buffet. The service was really good. The chefs were very attentive to dietary needs and other requests. The atmosphere is very nice. Weekdays are less crowded and excellent for brunch.

I treated my bridesmaids to brunch after they planned a fun and unforgettable bachelorette  weekend for me back in May 2014.  Price for the brunch buffet was a little pricey at $45 per person but wow, Bacchanal offered a pretty amazing spread!  I got my fill of the crab legs and the craving station and a little bit of everything else. Desserts were yummy: gelato and chocolate-dipped strawberries were my fave.  Quality of the food was great and brunch included free flowing champagne or mimosas to keep the party going...

At 55 dollars a plate and with an hour wait to then wait in line for 30 minutes, it's a little intimidating. But worth it. Buffett is full of gourmet foods that are all you can eat. Considering how overpriced the strip is with food, this place is actually somewhat economical when you take into account its quality. We ended up eating there both nights in Vegas, it's an experience.

Hide $50, DO NOT GAMBLE IT AWAY until you go to Bachannal Buffet. Everything was incredible. I went there on business and ate alone. I didn't care that everyone around me was silently judging the outrageous amount of food on my plate (and then the desserts that followed). They have a giant seafood buffet as well as carving station, potatoes, fried chicken, mac and cheese. Literally every bite I took was the best thing I ever ate. I was stuffed by the time I finished dinner. That didn't stop me from getting myself upwards of 6 desserts and enjoying every last bit! They have an amazing aray of desserts from cupcakes to mini tiramisu to gelato to creme brulee. The desserts were just as good as the dinner. This is well worth the price... hopefully you will win it back at the poker table later. But if you don't, at least your tummy will be happy.

I didn't really plan on coming here because I heard the lines get too long and we were waiting for another restaraunt to open at ceasars around 11am.  We jumped on the oppurtunity that there was no wait at all.  We were seated way far in the back and had to walk far to get any food.  The crab legs had no flavor at all.  The wagyu beef and the chicken and waffles were really good.  But other then that i wasnt really impressed with the quality of the food.  They have a lot of intresting choices and the buffet goes on forever, but I actually was a little dissapointed and would reccomend wicked spoon over bacchanal.

Line. After line. After line.

Wait in line to pay, wait in line to get seated, wait in line at every station throughout the expansive international selection of foods. I ended up eating a bunch of shrimp and crab legs because Vegas, but nothing I tried here really blew my mind. Nor was it horrible.  I think the whole idea of a buffet is so anti climactic, especially when you are paying $50+ and spending so much time in line. This is supposed to be one of the best buffets on the strip right now, but I'd rather have a nice steak cooked to order and served without the clusterfuck.

My husband and I came here because of the reviews we've read online. This place is popular so expect wait time to be around 1.5hrs. We went there for the first time on Friday, June 23, 2017. We didn't know we had to get a ticket before getting in line so we waited for about 20mins before realizing it. The person working there never acknowledged or greeted anyone if they don't have a ticket to enter the line to pay. Their food was ok even though they had somewhat good variety. However, for the amount you pay, the food was not worth it. Wicked Spoon buffet inside The Cosmopolitan have better food options and are delicious. This is my first and last time coming to Bacchanal Buffet.

I told myself I was gonna run & work out first BEFORE I eat here at Bacchanal Buffet. I lied... that did not happen at all lol.

Came here during 4th of July weekend and there was a holiday special going on, serving up different kinds of seasonal foods. However it was $70 for dinner (regular price is $60). It's pricey but you get what you pay for = good quality food and TONS of it! 

Different kinds of food such as... crab legs, suckling pig aka "LECHON" (for you Filipinos out there, but that's a seasonal item unfortunately), ramen, pho, sushi, dim sum, oysters, prime rib, tacos, bone marrow, lobster mac and cheese, gyro, gelato, crepe station, etc. The list goes on! 
Basically it's the food you see at fancy expensive restaurants, but all in one place at the buffet.

Overall my experience here was great. The wait time is LONG though. We waited almost 2 hours to get seated. But it was worth it, everything is good here! Even the drinks!!! I recommend getting the peach green iced tea!!!! UGH, so perfectly sweetened and addicting! 

Your tummy will be happy and you'll never see another buffet the same way ever again lol.

This is one of the better buffets around.  

The highlights:
- Carving Station
- Cucumber juice - my favorite
- Taco station
- Decent, but not great ramen
- Dessert bar 
- Crab legs, heated
- Oysters

The low-lights:
- The sushi
- The Italian food lack in selection
- The Asian food was limited, there was no xao lum bao on my visit

I would for sure come here, again, when in Vegas.  Especially if someone in my party loves dessert, as they probably have one of the better dessert bars around.

Haven't gone to a vegas buffet for over 10 years.... Boasted from other yelpers to be the "Best buffet in Vegas"... So me and my family decided to start with the best.... Bacchanal buffet got me caught up really fast! Sitting at the table and munching away for three hours felt like a little fat kid in a candy shop! It was such an amazing feeling!

Ticketing: Just get line, press on screen, input cell number to be texted when seating is available, and wait for the rsvp print out. First time seeing a self check-in kiosk for a buffet! Technology is one scary mother!

Wait time: We came early around 1030am on Friday for brunch and got in after 10 minutes of waiting.

Tip: Come early to avoid long lines to get in. You can also elect one person to stand in line for you.

Service: Buffet staffers were intentive, friendly, and totally awesome. Our empty plates were taken away every time we left to get more food. Our mimosa glasses were never empty! Kudos buffet staffers!

Food: Sooo much meat, soooo much crab legs, sooooo much OYSTERS, soooo much desserts to chooooose from! Pinch me.... is this a dream come true? Have I gone to meat and seafood heaven?? I think I had octuplet food babies that gave birth to other foood babies... Ughhhhhh.... the struggles are real!

$50+ Gets you in! Worth every single penny, nickel, dime, quarter, one dollar, 5 dollar, 10 dollar, 20 dollar, 50 dollar, and 100 dollar bill! Won't be disappointed!
food is not fresh and very very salty. definitely not recommended and disappointed. do not try unless u want spend 60 bucks eating salt and ice (crab is totally frozen in salty ice) (〝皿）

What a fantastic experience! We came here based on the yelp reviews and we were not disappointed. 

The food was fresh and well seasoned. The variety was plentiful with numerous cuisines offered and they replenish the food very quickly! 

The staff was friendly and service was great. 

We had at the seafood station - the shrimp cocktails, clams in saffron sauce, seafood paella, fried fish sandwich and the mussels. All great!

The asian section we had the pork dumplings, shrimp dumplings, shrimp/pork fried rice, bbq pork, and the shrimp cigar. Again, all awesome!

The carving station- we tried the lamb chops, beef ribs, and prime rib. Very good!

Definitely worth the price! Highly recommend it!

FYI- we were a party of 5! I didn't eat this all on my own (I promise!)! :)

It's all hype and not worth the 2hrs wait to stay in line and pay for the buffet then another 1-2 hrs wait to be seated. The food are not that great in taste. The prime rib that was given to me was very hard. We went as a party of 5 and will never go back.
My favourite buffet on the strip! It is absolutely delicious and worth the price. So much variety in food and amazing quality. Wouldn't come to Vegas without missing on a meal here.

When we went the first time 5 years ago, this place was memorable and I couldn't wait to go back.

This time my wife and I were really looking towards going here to have lunch while in Vegas for vacation.  Things have changed however.
The food was not great or worth the $60 a person price tag.

The food was mediocre and some was inedible since it was not even warm and cold as if not heated.

The only thing here that was appetizing was the deserts and most importantly the crepes, especially with nutella.

Really disappointed this time and most likely won't try again due to the spendy price tag.

There are buffets, there is the M buffet and there is Caesars palace new Bachanl. A complete different beast . This is the VOLTRON of the buffets. The Constropticon of AYCE . combining all different parts to make a mega incredible spot. I swear by this buffet and everytime I go it is a great food experience

BUT with great flavor on the strip comes the massive amounts of tourists. And when I say massive , I mean the wait feels like you are going to be getting an Iphone 6 at the front of the line.  Ive seen lots of peeps just giving up in their quest ..because they dont know that the Elysian fields were waiting for them right after paying your

Stations are well devided and food is outstanding. Crab legs are huge and if you dont want them cold they cook them right there for you. Want hand rolls,ramen and sushi? fear not.theres a whole station full it. Someone said Dim sum or mexican? yep that too. They have a great selection of almost every food you might want y

After you are done eating through prime ribs,oysters , lasagna etc..stop by the desert area. Specially the make your own crepe part.Flavor is intense

The whole place went thorugh a 17 million dollar renovation and it shows it. new deco, new uniforms, presentation is impecabble, food quailty is hands down best for a buffet .Im fat trust me.well played Harrahs

If you are a party beast and want to quench your alcohol thirst ;you can add an all you can drink for 15 dollars. Worth every penny..all until you are dancing naked on top of a table holding 5 alaskan crablegs as glowsticks ..ask me how I know..

Buffets can be overhyped for Vegas, but I have to say that this was pretty good for a buffet.  Decor was definitely nice with wood paneling and modern feel.  Asian food options were actually pretty decent along with the shellfish and carving stations.  It's pricey, but it's Vegas and the food wasn't too bad.  I would recommend if you're wanting to go to a buffet.

My friends and I came here because of all the reviews. We went for lunch at around 1:30pm, which ended up being perfect. We got in for the lunch price (about $40 including tax), but at 3pm they brought out dinner food. We were able to have a little of the crab legs before we left. 
They had a wide variety of food. My favorite was the Chinese dim sum and street tacos and best if all was the dessert. 
It was nice to come for the experience.

We had a blast here! It was beautifully done up inside. The chairs and tables are outrageously comfortable. Our server, Esteban, was masterful at keeping our cups full and table empty of cleaned off plates. The sushi bar was a dream. Definitely try the eel nigiri. My fiancé said the crab was the most tender he had ever had. The dessert bar has an excellent selection of sumptuous minis. We both loved the tiramisu cups and cheesecake. I recommend doing it on the Buffet of Buffets pass and paying the upgrade. It's definitely worth it!

Worth every penny and worth the line .    Selections were very tasty  seafood was on point!   Good place for a seafood lover.   MGM buffets was disappointing.   So this was a great find. Easy to get to and decor fits the price tag.   Not for cheapskates or those looking for an American Buffet... this isn't your kind of place.  Worth the price for sure !!!!!

Best buffet on strip! Hands down! As a huge fan of Wicked Spoon, I had doubts that Bacchanal would surpass Wicked spoon, but it far surpassed it in every way.  The variety of food is AMAZING. Everything from Asian to Mexican to Deli meats & cheeses, they seriously offer a WIDE variety of food. Try the big slabs of Bacon and Sweet Potato Tots! I recommend having a big appetite coming here. 

Biggest it's the newest (and best thing) you need to know something about going.  If you're a diamond/seven stars, you can bypass the line and get in quickly so you can really go anytime you want.  Or for $10/person extra you can get a "fast pass" and pass the line. The general public line can take up to an hour or 90 minutes during peak times so get here early if you don't want to do one of the two above options.
We stop here every time we going Vegas. I think this is the best buffet here in Vegas. Recently they add ube gelato so that a plus.

Buffet had a large variety, a little bit of everything for everyone. Most of the food was very tasty and flavorful. I Loved the Mac and Cheese! My only regret is not going earlier. We arrived around 8:30pm and after the hour wait, it left us with very little time to pig out. I think its worth the money though, we were allowed to stay and eat till 10:30pm. Even though it was later there was plenty of everything and it was packed with guests! Desserts were good and service was helpful and attentive. I would go back again in the future, with more time of course:)

First time trying lamb. It was cooked so well. All of the food was extremely flavorful. We went at 3pm on a Tuesday. It took an hr to get set down. The food was worth the wait. The macaroni and cheese was amazing! My favorite side dish was the hush puppies.

Hands down the best buffet I have ever encountered.  As stated by other reviewers, it is pricey, but the quality, variation and amount of food you get is well worth it.  I would recommend taking a "tour" before you commit to your favorites, there really are so many choices of different kinds of food.. SO GOOD

ALSO! The bacchanal is one of the 6 buffets you can choose from when you get the 24 hour pass, if you pay a little extra, and that is WELL worth it.. especially when it's $60 a person just for dinner.

Talk about great buffets and a pallet blaster.

I've gone to so many that none has stuck out like this one. WOW great lamb, awesome desserts, delicious and varied seafood selection, multiple cheeses and types of bread. I can keep going but my goodness. 

Though problems include: 
1)LONG LINE FOR MEAT. My goodness I was eating while I was waiting in line (I know so bad) but it was that dang long. 

2)Terrible sushi. Yeah no. Don't do it here.

It's awesome here and it's a must---take it from someone who lives here and is oh so tired of all the buffets that they all start tasting the same. 

It's my top buffet overall now (BUT I haven't tried the infamous wicked spoon yet....excited when I do)

We visited this place on Sunday for Brunch Buffet. I've heard how good this place was so perhaps my expectation was too high.
We've waited about an hour to get in. It was a nice place for sure, but for a $50 buffet, I was a little disappointed. Sushi selection was just so so, and the cold King crab legs were way too salty. Prime Rib was pretty good but I'd prefer a little more on the rare side. And I was unable to find Au Jus for my meat.
Don't get me wrong. There were pretty good dishes too. I liked hot Alaskan crab legs and a few others. Like I said, perhaps my expectation was too high.

Whoever rated this place 4-5 stars must never had any decent buffet before!
This place is overhyped and overpriced for being the "BEST buffet" in vegas!

I came here for dinner at 3pm

Raw oyster - tasteless
King crab legs - ok
Crab claws - tasteless
Prime ribs - dry 
BBQ ribs - too salty, too tough
Lamb chop - undercooked
Sushi - One small tray for a $50+ buffet are you kidding? And the fish is drying than a mf
Chinese - maybe good enough to fool non-chinese food lover...but none looked good.

What I did like :

clam risotto
ice cream
egg tart 

Funniest thing is they take a picture of you as you lined up with no interesting background and tried to sell you the printed picture for $20!?  Who the F in the marketing department thought of this deserved to get fired.  

The TV ad for this buffet looks stupid as well, having a much of jazz dancers dancing to at the buffet..........that totally makes me want to come again!

Quantity vs Quality. The presentation and number of options are impressive. But it all goes downhill after that. Most food is bland and a lot of mush. Very generic. A special mention for the Asian section, it's just terrible. The sushi is bad and I actually had to spit out the noodles. I don't understand how this place has such a good reputation... Maybe I caught them on a bad day.

An absolutely epic buffet. The meat station alone is worth the price of admission for me (the prime rib was awesome), and...and...I'm losing my train of thought thinking of the meat station again (droooooooooooooooool). The desserts were all top notch as well. If you like buffets you will LOVE this one, well worth the visit. They play some pretty great music too and the atmosphere is really nice.

Two things I noticed that they have to correct:

1. The bread is sliced to order and there wasn't anyone readily available to slice some bread for me. I tried to take some bread myself as I thought it was pre-sliced, but they were only there for decoration. They should slice the bread and put it out for everyone.

2. The top row of salad bar items is completely obscured and you have to really really really duck down to see what the items are. I gave up trying to take some of the items as it was awkward to try to grab them.

All in all, a solid 5-star rating and the next time I'm in Vegas I will definitely be back here.

This is one of the biggest buffets I have ever been too! They have everything you could think of, seafood, pizza, all different kinds of meats, tacos, ext! They also have the most options of deserts I've ever seen! As well as many ice cream options!

Thanksgiving Holiday Brunch Review
- nothing special about the menu except for a roasted turkey yet charges double price $59.99/person
- seafood selection is limited. King crab is not fresh 
- sushi is very mediocre like what you get from a grocery store
- no special drinks unless pay $15 more. Only serves coffee-tea and juices
- seating and food stations are very spread out and you have to walk around a lot 
- location: near casino. Noisy and crowded 

Overall: food is very mediocre, not worth the rating and price.

Been there twice.
I like the place :D
The meat are good especially the ribs. And of course, the crabs are good. It has a good selection of cheese and dessert too.
Beyond average in Vegas :D

$50 for the lunch (tax and bottomless champagne). All different types of cuisine but all mediocre. I got a crab claw that was rancid (tasted like ammonia). Nothing else really blew me away whatsoever. I kinda like the cheese and meat station.  The gelato bar was actually really good and a few desserts were good but overall  I felt disappointed.  Sergio the waiter was attentive and kept refilling the champagne.  

Update: It's now midnight and I have ozone destroying gas. I've been in pain all day. If you like home town buffet and it's your 65th high school reunion then I recommend this place to you.

My boyfriend and I came here yesterday morning for their weekend brunch around 10:00 AM and had a relatively short wait (45 minutes) compared to the 133 minute wait time we were quoted when we last attempted to dine here. The mimosas and soft drinks are included in the brunch package. 

We had heard a gentleman remark behind us to his friends that "For the price I'm paying, this better be good, their mimosas should have fresh orange juice from the tree. I don't want no f@!?ing Sunny Delight s*** in my drink." 

We agreed with this sentiment and found the mimosas to have more champagne than orange juice :) 

The five stars are strictly for the food and the wait staff. The hostesses are indifferent, they are impatient with questions, and lack common courtesy so try to limit your interaction with them as much as possible. 

The restaurant is the largest buffet we have been to. It is spacious, bright, and airy. The décor is modern and featured a lot of crystalline structures which seemed to enhance the lighting. 

Our server Carlos was fantastic! He was very kind, gracious, and adept at managing our table. He let us know that there were 504 items served at the buffet and encouraged us to try them all. But between the two of us, I think we managed to sample 30 options. 

They have an Asian (Chinese/Thai/Japanese), Italian, Mexican, All American, and Seafood stations. The food was repeatedly checked on and replenished to ensure freshness, which was much appreciated. Their dessert section is notable for carrying sugar free options and international items ( examples are Jasmine rice pudding, almond jelly, French tarts, Italian cookies, etc). We felt the gelato served here tasted better than Wicked Spoon and there was more variety.

Oh my Gaaaaaaaawsh this is the best buffet eeeeeeeveeeeerrrrrr.

$33 for breakfast? Kind of took me off guard, but whatever. I was mentally prepared for this day. I HAD PREPARED FOR WEEKS. Seriously. Reading reviews, menu's, looking at pictures, I was ready to go. Specifically for breakfast.

First of all, the place is beautiful. Very spacious, clean, well lit. The food is fresh and some of it's even made to order. There's seafood, Mexican, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, American, and god only knows what else. I had a lot of food and felt like I got what I paid for.

The made to order crepe station was my favorite part of the buffet. The made to order meat and eggs was a close second. The fact that you can have crab legs, shrimp, and other seafood for breakfast is pretty cool. I wish I took more pics, and I wish I ate more. But it's so good. This is an absolute must do if you're in Vegas.

First time in Vegas and it was first stop in Vegas. We heard good things about this buffet. We waited a while to get a table but that wasn't too bad. However, one of the work was very rude to my friend.
 
The food was either a hit or a miss. Some food became cold fast. Our waitress was not taking our plates and filling up our drinks. So we were thirsty and overfilled. The best was the options, especially the desert table. Over priced but expected in Vegas and with all the selections cannot imagine them being cheap. I probably would not go again.

We finally understand why Bacchanal is considered the best buffet in Vegas. Having dined at Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo and the Buffet at the Wynn, we feel that Bacchanal is in a league of its own. The variety and quality of food at Bacchanal are unparalleled even though it is mass produced. 

1. How does the waiting process work?
Walk up to the kiosk and take a ticket which will provide an estimated time to return. Upon your return, you wait in line to pay for the buffet, after which you wait in a final line to get seated. 

2. When is the best time to dine here? 
Arriving at the tail end of brunch/lunch (between 2-3 pm) allows you to sample both the brunch and dinner menus at the brunch price as the restaurant transitions during this period. 

3. What are the buffet highlights? 
Must Try: 
- Street tacos
- Lamb chops
- Spicy sausage
- Crab legs: head to the Italian station for warm ones
- Horchata
- Rice pudding
- Crepes

Mediocre: 
- Oysters
- Sushi
- Chinese food

Skip: 
- Ice cream: very icy
- Kobe sliders: dry and subpar
- Red velvet pancakes

Bacchanal, you were everything we wanted and more.
It was all that has been described. The crepe was outstanding!!! Definitely worth the wait. We will return.

We bought the 6 buffets in 24 hours deal. We paid the extra cost in order to try this buffet. It was worth it - probably double! A never ending array of everything you could crave. And not the seasonless, cheapest costing foods that they can make the most money on type of food.  Everything was so delicious - I can't wait to go back!

Very good selection of all types of food.  Nice atmosphere as long as you're not sitting next to a large  family that is obviously camped out for a few hours. Most of the food is fresh and well presented. Our server was very nice even though she was dealing with the campers next to us.
Pricey but, definitely some standouts for a buffet! Loved the scalloped potato, some good pastas and pasta salads too! the sushi was just ok.

I came here early on a Saturday evening and didn't need to wait to be seated. However, it was a different story for those who were in queue by the time I left. The service was decent, although it did annoy me when they completely cleared my table before we were done eating. 

My stomach ate itself while I stood in line for the meat station, but I filled up on the meat really fast (try the prime rib). I liked that the crab legs were already sliced in half so they were easy to eat. There really weren't any other main dishes to choose from, but there was a wide variety of desserts. 

Albeit the food is good, I still think Wicked Spoon wins when it comes to Vegas buffets.

One word...disappointed.  40 for lunch and although there was a wide assortment of food  about 7/8 were sub par. Some tips. DO NOT GET THE RAW SEAFOOD. Most of the raw seafood tastes gross except for the shrimp which was just okay. Stick to the desserts. The desserts will never fail you. Also, if you are vegetarian or have food allergies do not come here. There are no labels on the food that tell you what it contain. Even still, for vegetarians this place is a no go. Only salad, fruits and desserts.

I love the endless options. They have Italian,Asian,Mexican, American and delicious desserts. The champagne was exquisite. Table service was good. Of course the 45 minute wait was not fun but worth it. I would say that this buffet is the best I've ever had. I tried to get a piece of everything but they just have too many options, which for a buffet it's a great thing. You will not be disappointed.

All of the food selections are delicious, especially considering that this is a buffet. 

The reason I give this buffet 3 stars is that no particular item really stood out to me. Everything I had was well prepared, fresh, and tasty, but nothing  was that outstanding. Coming to this buffet is a good experience when you're in Vegas, but I believe that spending your money at a nicer sit-down restaurant would be better.

so excited to first time trying this place what USA Today rated the number buffet in Vegas, food was overflowing with great looking foods, though price was so above average stunning $53 per person, what the heck for a dinner celebrating a birthday of a special person (my self) with a party of 8 an 18% tips is a must, end up paying $545 for dinner. really unforgetable dinner experience, especially when we were back to CA finding out they charge me another extra 18% tip added to my card, lessson learn dont be tooo excited on this place, paying $186 for tip alone was so dissappointing so remember dont be so excited about this and the so callled rated number one buffet in Vegas, because what happpened to me in Vegas i cannot stay it in Vegas, and until now i feel im vomiting for the amount of food i eat? or perhaps the amount of tip they overcharged me. Good luck and if ever anyone dare to see my bill im always happy to show and share it! February 7, 2014 Friday at around 7pm when it was happen
I actually wanted to cry because I couldn't eat anymore. We got a Groupon deal for $65 for 2 for brunch, and it was AMAZING. Would definitely return, though idk if we'd do it at full price.

I gotta say. Bacchanal Buffet is one of the top buffet in Vegas. If you go Vegas without stopping by Bacchanal, then it is one of the big lost that you have.

The foods here are good and have more variety , especially the desserts. One of  my favorite dessert that you cannot find where else at the buffet is Macaroons. All you can eat Macaroons. 

Make your money worth while you are in Vegas

I don't know if it's just about bad timing or this place really sucks. We get in line about an hour and a half till they are suppose to close. It was Jul 4th and they said the 67+/person price is due to a holiday rate and the food selection is suppose to be special. Well, turned out the food was not special after all. The meat, (ribs, steak, etc) were as cold as the beer I was chugging. The Italian selection consists of cold torn pizza slices, meatballs that looked like they were sitting there for hours. The only hot item I ran into was the udon soup but not after getting in line for about 15-20 mins. Well, all I am saying is the price we paid for is not worth a dime of the overall food selection that day.

Omg best buffet ever!!!! So much food!!! Except there's like only 2 soups hot & sour soup & a clam chowder one. 

So we already planned on coming here cause we heard it's the best buffet in Las Vegas. We got in a line to pay then they moved us to another line to wait for a table. It was pretty quick on a Tuesday around 3:30. Later around 6 it got busy. 

So the buffet goes from the front of the restaurant to the back & the desserts are in the middle. 

The front is sea food,then American, Mexican, Italian, salads & cheese & salami, then sushi & Chinese food. 

I tried alittle bit of everything. The Chinese food tasted a bit cold. The caesar salad, mash potatoes, ribs, prime rib, & crepes are my favorite. 

The prime rib was a bit to red for me so they put it on the grill to cook it longer for me. Also they can make you a taco, & crepes. 

There's also drinks like horchata. 

It's $55 per person from 3pm-10pm Mon-Thurs. Kids are $24.99. Drinks are included even coffee!

Food was great! The dim sum was actually pretty good compared to other buffets. A bit pricey, but the service and quality of food is high, so you get what you pay for! The desserts are really good, too.

Best buffet in Vegas by far! The wait can be long but it's worth it. Great selection of food across a variety of cuisines. LOVE the dessert bar! Great seafood and everything is very fresh! Many cooked to order options too!

The last time I came to Vegas this place was still being remodeled and a few months from opening. So during our recent vacation trip to Utah over the 4th of July weekend, I made sure to add Vegas to our Itinerary and pay homage to Bacchanal.

As a frequent gambler, I always make sure to take advantage of the Casino comps, especially Caesar's total rewards program. Membership does have its advantage and rewards. I was able to avoid the general line and go to the diamond and seven stars member line without waiting, avoiding the 40-60 minute wait. Without it I suggest getting here 1 hour early before the lunch time or dinner rush hours.

Like most of the high end buffet places in Vegas, expect to pay around $40-$50. Sure you can go elsewhere, but I can assure your $50 buffet price of admission and food indulgence at Bacchanal will be memorable and delicious. For an even better deal upgrade to 24hr Buffet of Buffets for an additional $25 more and a great value.

Typical of most buffet style restaurants atmosphere is bustling. The decor inside is eclectic and modern including chic dessert section. The ceiling is actually surrounded and framed in unique glass pattern which is very inspiring and beautiful.

As for the food, there buffets has one of the largest and freshest selections of food in town. Make sure to pace yourself and take small bites or taste to truly enjoy all that Bacchanal has to offer. Everything is set up in stations that represent different styles of cuisine and offerings - Meat, seafood, desserts, Italian, fried foods, Mexican, Japanese and Asian.

Seafood -
* Snow king crab legs - cold and heated options. Meat was a bit skimpy, but at least they were served in half allowing easy access.
* Jumbo shrimps - huge size and more like prawns.
* Clam bake - comes in cute little baskets - filled with clams, sausages and corn.
* Ceviche - raw fish served in a small shot glass and marinated in lime juice, onions, cilantro and avocado - delicious and refreshing.
* Salmon with cherry tomato - so tender and flavorful.
* Bouchot mussels - white wine sauce, parsley, and served sourdough crostini was fabulous.

Asian Food - Vast choices and selections that will make you feel that you're in Chinatown and Little Tokyo. The Peking duck and kalbi beef were so succulent and delicious.

BBQ Meats - the best and extensive meat spread I've seen in all of Vegas. Lamb chops, prime rib, Tomahawk rib eye steaks, beef brisket, sausages - cooked perfectly, well seasoned and all delicious.

Desserts section - Outstanding desserts and a perfect ending to an exceptional meal.  
* Ice Cream and Gelato - Balsamic figs and baklava - OMG so incredibly delicious!
* Cream brûlée - preferred regular version over the chocolate (more like a chocolate pudding). Perfectly caramelized top layer crust and rich vanilla custard makes one awesome treat.
* Souffle - so downright decadent and amazing.
* Tiramisu - served in chocolate cup which you can devour and feel happy afterwords - "Yummilicious!"
* Macarons - lightly crisp exterior shell, soft and chewy inside. Tasted so heavenly. My favorites were the pistachio and mocha.
* Crepe station - fresh strawberry drizzled with chocolate and dusted with powder sugar always does it for me and scrumptious.

Mexican - 
* Street food taco section was a fabulous idea and reminded me of the succulent tacos in LA served from Food trucks. Accompanied with a vast selection of bottled salsa and hot sauces, the carne asada and al pastor tacos were solid.
* Posole - delicious Mexican pork soup includes all your fresh accoutrement's
* Whole grilled Mexican corn with butter and queso fresco was outstanding.

Salads - watermelon and feta served in small square glass dish was refreshing and delightful. Just the presentation alone had me salivating. The Caprese salad was excellent as well.

Fried Food - 
* Fried chicken with sweet potato fries in basket - excellent crispy exterior followed by flavorful tender chicken and well seasoned.
* Crab croquette - So yummy with actual crab meat inside. Great with a dash of hot sauce.
* Wagyu beef cheeseburger sliders - were cooked perfectly medium, well season and flavorful

Italian section - 
* Lasagna, pizzas, garlic knots and Rigatoni - Typical and standard, but still satisfying. There pasta dishes needs more dishes and limited.

Complaint - 
* Sushi - Simple and lacking creativity, definitely needs sashimi dishes.
* For the price of admission, they should include beer, champagne and wine as complimentary item.
*  No stone crab legs during my recent visit.
* Long lines at seafood and meat station due to its overwhelming popularity.

Overall - Prompt and attentive service. Our server came by regularly to refill our drinks and take our dirty dishes away. Enjoyed our meal and had a wonderful time stuffing our faces. It's definitely worth checking out, but make sure you come with a big appetite and hungry because the food is overwhelmingly good.

Had the service been even remotely acceptable, I would have comfortably rated Bacchanal 4 stars. 

My SO and I have made it a point to try all of the high-end strip buffets since moving to Las Vegas two years ago and Bacchanal was the final stop on our list. 

As far as the food quality is concerned, Bacchanal is right up there with the other top contenders like the Wicked Spoon. In fact, the seafood and Asian selections are probably the best I've had at any buffet. The carving station, Mexican, American, and Italian food were all solid as well, though not exceptional. The dessert offerings were also above average quality, the Gelato and French Macarons were particularly delicious.

That being said, I will most likely not be visiting Bacchanal again because the service was absolutely deplorable. After the host grabbed three separate parties from the secondary line to be seated, we were forced to run and weave between tables to keep up with her and find our seats after we made stops to have the other two parties seated first, of course. We were sat and told to begin eating when we were ready and that our server would be by shortly. Our server did not show up for a FULL half hour after we had been seated to finally ask what we would like to drink. He brought our drinks out soon after and that was the last we saw of him for an hour. Not only that, but we were forced to go take fresh napkin and utensil sets from another open table as we were never given any nor were we able to flag down anyone to help us. Our plates were removed from the table exactly one (1) time in the almost two hours that we were at the restaurant, so we had to take matters into our own hands and take our finished plates to other empty tables in order to clear our own. 

When you're paying $65 per person plus tip for dinner, service like this is absolutely unacceptable. We've gotten infinitely finer service at the Cannery buffet where breakfast for 2 runs about 12 dollars with the club card. While the food was fantastic, the quality of service was nowhere near where it should be for a restaurant of this caliber and the great food was not enough to overcome the horrendous service. We'll take our money to Wicked Spoon or even the Studio B Buffet at the M Resort next time we're in the mood to splurge on an upscale buffet
Best buffet I have ever been to!! Absolutely loved everything kinda expensive but worth it

Thank you to my Sister Jose for recommending this to me ! My fiancé and I finally had a chance to experience this over the weekend. Granted yes 57 for each person for weekend dining, but I mean when you see what they have to offer it's worth it! My man was in heaven with all the fish and sushi and omg the meat station wow ! I recommend this to anyone! Will def be coming back here :-)

It was probably the night we went but it wasn't as amazing as I expected it to be from the reviews.  

Thanks to the reviews, we listened to the tips about Monday night at 5pm with no wait.  We had a baby with us so lines don't go well.  By about 6pm, we saw a huge line formed already.  

There is a huge variety but more isn't always better.  The meat section is definitely the largest I've seen but everything I had there seemed over salted and dry.  They said it was because of a southern style of cooking, which really isn't an excuse in my opinion.  I've had better buffet prime rib at Paris and the World Carnival one in Rio.  Never had ribeye, ribs, or brisket at another buffet but they were dry and tough when we were there.  

Interesting variety that they have here are: pho (I only got it to try it, its okay), horchata (which i enjoyed), dim sum area.  Don't need to bother with the dim sum area.  Probably because we were early and the things were sitting out longer but the steam got all their items soggy.  

Deep fried things were good: calamari, yam tots, waffle fries, but a little salty.  

I mostly enjoyed their desserts.  Mochi ice cream is good but they do run out periodically and have to wait for more.  Their creme brulee I felt was good but too deep.  It was a wrong proportion of the top sugar crust to the rest, which I've had better at the Paris buffet.  Macaroons were good as well.  

Overall, it's good but not sure if it's worth the $46 we paid.  Good service, good variety, but not necessarily the best tasting in one place.

One of the better buffets in vegas!

I personally like this buffet more than the wynn, rio and its also on par with the bellagio buffet! The crab legs were amazing! The pho and ramen were also pretty  good! The pasta and the prime rib were also yummy! Even the tacos were pretty damn good! The desserts were okay in my opinion. We went for lunch so there were no macarons :( lame!

Can I just live here? All I need is a shower and a closet for my clothes/shoes and I would NEVER leave. Why would you? They have EVERYTHING. Dim Sum, Taco Bar, Carving Station, Make-Your-Own-Charcuterie-Board, Pasta & Pizza, and endless desserts! I went twice in one week... (Oh, gluttony.) And on the plus side, I like that during lunch they offer a good range of seafood, unlike other buffets. If you're like my parents, you could go in at the tail-end of lunch and stick it out until they roll out some of the dinner items. You also end up saving a few dollars!

Really wanted to like this place but can't say I will go back for sure.  From registration at the kiosk to the table took 3 hours on 4th of July night.  

Pro:
- Sign-in at the kiosk, which allowed us to wait while not being in line. 
- Lot of food options
- Good service, the servers cleaned my table quickly and frequently.
- The folks behind the serving stations are very nice and helpful. 
- Had roasted pork and roasted duck, which were delicious. 

Con:
- Some of the food are not as nicely put together when comparing to the buffet at Wynn and Bellogio. The presentation just not as good. 
- May be it was because of the holiday, but some of the food at the stations appear old (the Chinese dim sum, some of the sushi pieces, and some of the Asian cook food)
- After tax and before tips, $75 per person.  Not cheap. 

Note:
- Be mindful that after they text you to come to the line, there will be another wait. 
- The Italian, Asian, deli food are in the back of the counter, you will need to walk around the corner to make sure you don't miss it.

The 1 star is for the dessert. I do not know why all the food are so salty, it's for us to eat less in the buffet? All food we got only can have a bite, cannot eat more. Only the dessert is good. Will not go or recommend anybody to this buffet, worst buffet I ever had. Food from the pic is firstly we got when we enter, I don't give review, but this buffet totally disappointed, the top rated vegas buffet.
Best buffet in Vegas. Staff is very friendly. Our waitress Julie was phenomenal

Solid buffet but the price makes you cringe. Dinner price is about $60 bucks as of my review date. At this rate, you'd expect everything to taste pretty good or at least edible, but it's not the case.

Let's start with the bad.

The wait time can be atrocious. The cool part is you can check in at the kiosk and be texted when your table is ready. Beware, once you come back to check in with the host, your wait will be approximately another 30 mins until seated.

Ramen that has no place being served. In fact, I've had better instant ramen. I'm not exaggerating. The "chashu" pork was literally the Chinese style charsiu, the broth was just salt water.

Dim sum was a nice try but it is mushy from sitting on the steam table too long. 

Insane line for the King Crab legs.

BBQ is ambitious but the pork ribs are dry and the brisket was very dry. No bueno.

Men's restroom next to the buffet only has 2 stalls. Really? Better make a run for the casino restroom.

Chicken and waffle (cone) is a failure.

Sushi is almost inedible, but what do you expect.

The good:

Chicken Chili Verde was bomb.

Taco station is cool but I didn't pay $60 bucks to come load up on "street tacos."

Prime rib was cooked well.

Seafood station has a nice variety of clams, mussels, crab and oysters but can be inaccessible due to the long line for crab legs.

Chinese "house special" style crab is bomb.

Chinese roasted duck is delicious.

Dessert area is great and the desserts are very well made. Crepe station is a plus.

PRO TIP: Get hot king crab legs without a wait, just go to the station that has pasta.

Best buffet I have ever eaten in the USA, if not the world.  You cannot go to Vegas without stopping by here. Period. In fact, my last trip here my first agenda for my Vegas trip was to come back here for dinner.  Since I was here for brunch within the first 2 months it had opened, it has haunted my all you can eat dreams with thoughts on fresh juices, meats, and sweets.

I've pretty much been to every casino buffet on both coasts.  And nothing compares, this is solid #1 for me.  Let me first start off with that line? I suppose it's long, and I did humor the attendant asked what the wait was like (1 hour or 45 mins, or quite possibly 1 hour 45). But have a cool kids pass, and don't wait on casino food lines. So non-issue for me, I suppose waiting an hour is a long time.  The place is beautiful designed and very clean.

The food? I really don't want to go into details aside from you should check it out yourself.  The Horchata drink, I found particularly unique, and you can't skip the meat/grill section. The dessert section was the only thing that makes say, 'hey it was very good' compared to 'omg you have try two everything"  I did find the Portuguese tarts there amusing, but it's not the same as Macau. But I digress, and also I did eat 2.  And also get the mochi ice cream, rumor has it that it used to be delivered from Hawaii fresh.  If there is a take away, just go.

I can definitely see why they call this one of the best buffets in Vegas! Keep in mind that it is of a very high price point, but the quality of the ingredients and finished food product are well worth it!
We first tried coming on a Sunday night 8 pm, but didn't think the 2 hour wait time was worth it. At least they have machines for you to "check-in" and receive a time, so you don't have to wait in the lobby the whole time. Came back Tuesday for brunch with almost no wait time (just get through the line to pay, ~5 minutes?).
For hot dishes (literally, like if the plate is hot from sitting under the lamp), they provide silicone finger gloves(?) so you don't burn yourself when grabbing said hot plates. There is a juice bar, serving single-ingredient juices, for those of you wanting a healthy option. The Asian foods section is the most authentic I've seen of any buffet, Vegas or otherwise, serving various dim sum, congee, fish maw, and wood ear fungus, to name a few. The sushi, however, is very little and consists of futomaki (pickled veggies) and tamagoyaki rolls and poke (like seasoned mixed raw fish salad). The burger sliders may be the best burgers I've ever had; I think the mere simplicity of it (bun, meat, cheese) allowed for appreciation of the ingredients, rather than be overwhelmed by various toppings. I skipped out on the chilled seafood, since the line for those was long.
Overall, a very enjoyable experience on both the food and service front.
(My opinion) Foods to skip: red velvet pancakes and fried chicken and french fries; they were both very dry; sushi rolls are hard (since they are cold and left out)

Definitely above average place to go to if you're into the buffet scene.

1. Food is fresh some stuff is above average and some is below average. They definitely do not skimp on the food.

2. awesome attentive service! every time I come here I feel very special by the way the server treats me and my family. 
knows when to pick up the dishes, when to get refills on our drink, always around to make sure we are being helped whenever we need it.

3. ambience is relaxing, pretty clean overall

4. lines is ridiculous just make sure to not  come here on an empty stomach waiting time is 1-3hrs depending on time and day. 

5. definitely would come back again.

This place is crazy... So many options you want to try everything! And when you do the verdict usually ends up being just "meh."

This place features many, many options but where they give you quantity they lack in real quality. Crab legs were really fatty, Mexican food was bland, even the Asian food station left me not wanting to go back. 

I'd honestly recommend going to the Wynn buffet instead of this. Wynn's may have less variety but the tastes make up for it times a million.
One of the best buffet I've ever been to. This place had a dish from every food category there is. Looks like I found a place I'd visit every time I come back.

Went here on a Friday for dinner. We went early due to other reviews about long lines. Lines were fine when we arrived, decent length when we left.

Only gave 2 stars due to high price buffet and barely average food.  Best part of the meal were the great choices of gelato.  Sushi was decent - nothing interesting. Thought the seafood portion was gross - some of the shrimp I had were slimy and didn't bother to eat.

This buffet was chill, probably a 3.5. They have an expansive selection but nothing we had was really that good. I did like the chicken wing that came in the waffle cone, and also the mac n cheese. Carving station and raw bar selection are both massive but everything was just ok. $50 or whatever it is that includes all you can drink mimosas is a nice deal as long as your server keeps on refilling.

On Thursday of last week I decided to try out Caesar's Palace's dinner buffet. It was the most expensive meal that I've ever treated myself to, but I can honestly say that it was worth it. The experience went a little something like this:

My friend and I entered the line that wove in a maze of black ropes and carpet with intricate detailing. Already famished from a full day of walking, we waited in line for about an hour until we got to pay the $48 per person tab. Once we entered we were greeted with cream linen furniture, classy stained glass room separators, and sassy glass adorned light fixtures, brimming with people. Then came the stations. Mexican, Japanese, Southern, Chinese, American, Italian, Thai, Seafood... it was overwhelming. We started with 8 plates and then another round of 'real food' before we took a second break and headed for dessert. Tiramisu, cookies, mochi, gelato, red velvet cake, carrot cake, molten lava cake, pizookies, custard, fresh berries, brownies, chocolate-dipped strawberries, apple pie, bread pudding, and those are only the items we managed to take advantage of. All this 5-star food in one place- available for consumption? A recipe for a full heart and stomach. And the indigestion to follow was the only detraction from 5 star rating, even though it's partially my fault.

This buffet is overrated. You actually need to wait in a line to get to the final waiting line and keep lining up there for an hour. A lot of dishes that are supposed to be warm are not kept that way. Snow crab legs are too slim and tastes like it has just been brought out from the fridge.

First of all this is in a nice fancy location inside cesars palace. That being said, the price is very stiff at $60 per person. Couple that with the extra 18% charge for parties over 8 people and you're looking at close to $77 per person. For that price one would expect something pretty decent at the very least. I have to say that I was extremely disappointed at the quality of the food, the layout of the buffet, and the overall experience. There was an extremely long line to get to the semi-decent stuff (like the meats). The meats were not that great either; the steak and beef were extremely tough and hard to chew. The steamed king crabs were way too salty to enjoy. The selection of cold seafood looked very unappetizing. The italian section had some slices of pizza that didn't look that good. The asian sushi section had food that looked on par with the stuff you get at $20 asian buffets. The dessert section was something you can get at a $30 buffet. To top that off the biffet was extremely crowded and they ran out of plates. Overall I personally think that this one is a huge rip and not worth the wait and the money. Skip

I think I liked this one the best out of all the buffets we visited (MGM, Cravings, and Aria). I've still got my fair share to try but I'm getting there!!

Things that stood out: 

Ramen! Not only was it awesome to watch them cook it, but it was absolutely delicious. 

Indian curries- delicious!

Crab legs- They're everywhere but they were great. 

Baby sliders- Juicy and fresh! They were also small, which is a good thing!

Roasted Veggies- random right? But they were seasoned very well and weren't too soft. 

The little bowls that had an array of soups/ pasta dishes/gumbos- The presentation is so nice! 

The green chili chicken with rice- the chicken was juicy, not dry, and the rice was delicious as well. It was hard not to eat too much! I needed to save room for more options 

Mochi- so awesome!!! 

Desserts- There were a ton, and they were, for the most part, all amazing and delicious. 

I also like how you can almost get lost. The food kind of wraps around the wall and it just keeps going and going and going. In the middle close to the entrance is the dessert bar which is an entire circle filled with heavenly treats.

Wait time - at least 1 hour - 2/10
Salad - average 5/10
Meats - good 7.5/10 
Asian cuisine - disappointed. Felt like Panda Express 6/10
Seafood - good variety bland 7/10
Juice options - 5/10. No fresh squeezed juices. For a high end Uber expensive buffet I expect better
Desserts - very good 9/10. All their small cakes are just worth trying
Overall experience - 7/10
For me this is no longer the #1 buffet in Vegas. Wicked spoon at cosmopolitan takes that crown

hits:
+truffle potato gratin
+hamburger sliders
+maccaroons
+sweet potato tots
+sweet potato fries
+chocolate covered oreo
+prime rib
+green tea mochi
+coffee ice cream
+attentive friendly servers
+mimosas were refilled quickly
+plates always cleared
+accomodated a huge group fairly quick went on a Saturday

miss:
- huge line for crab legs and it wasn't that great. skinny crab legs with hardly, to no meat. skip it.

Otherwise, everything was so good. My entire group thoroughly enjoyed the buffet so much. I will happily come back!

I admit that I am not a big fan of buffets but this is probably the best buffet I have been to in Las Vegas. I think the specialty is steamed crab legs. They also have little tomatoes with balsamic vinegar and a standard stations for sushi, noodles, dimsum, meats, and desserts. We had a sunday lunch and the lines moved pretty fast. It good place to spend several hours gorging on delicious food.

Let me start by saying that I am typically not impressed or inclined to be present at any buffet in general. But Vegas has a reputation for having some pretty stellar establishments, so I figured I'd give it a try. Plus, my girlfriend really wanted to go! Hah


Anyway, I was surprised by the quality of food. They really had quite the selection and it did not have that heat lamp feel that buffet food tends to get after sitting. Seemed to be much fresher than most all establishments I've been to. 
For the first course, I began with the Eggs Benedict and the pork belly. The flavor was delicious so I ended up having a second round, this time a slice of bacon and some fruit. The rest of the food I ordered was scrambled eggs, hash browns, and sausage. It being 10 am I didn't venture into the rest of the contents of the buffet. But it did smell and look delicious, everything but the seafood.
The only downside to my experience here were my initial thoughts walking in. It had an overpowering smell of garlic/rubbery seafood. Did not quite prepare the palate. 

But, as far as buffets go, this is definitely one I would go back to.

Due to all the hype and videos I've watched about the Bacchanal, I had been wanting to go here for so long. I had such high expectations for this buffet coming in, but unfortunately left disappointed and very underwhelmed. The quality of the food did not positively equate the $60 I paid. 

When I had searched up the buffet online, I had read that there was opulent dishes consisting of wagyu, sushi and tons of seafood. There was no wagyu and the sushi selection was pitiful as there was barely any selection. I was really looking forward to having some salmon sashimi, but there wasn't any. The prime rib tasted okay. 
The seafood didn't taste as fresh to me. I also felt like they were being stingy with the seafood because it wasn't being refilled quickly enough. The bone marrow looked good, but tasted purely of onions with no beef marrow taste at all. 

The best things there were the pizza, dim sum and the dessert line. They're banana fosters crepes were super good. However, these are all cheap dishes in themselves and are hard to mess up. 

Overall the food wasn't bad, but the quality was more of a $30 buffet rather than a $60. I've had way better buffets in Vegas for a lot cheaper so I would save your money.

We were here for brunch a few weeks ago, and I'm... torn. We were here because of a Groupon, which got us brunch, cut-the-line passes (which did indeed cut us straight to the front of the line!), and mimosas, for ~$30 a seat. I'm torn on whether it was worth that much - some of the food was excellent, some was terrible, a lot was in between - but it absolutely would not have been worth remotely $30 without the mimosas and the cut-the-line passes, it definitely wouldn't have been worth a bunch extra to cut the line, and it also definitely wouldn't have been worth waiting in the absolutely freakishly enormous line (around 11 AM on a Friday) at normal price. So I guess I can't really recommend it that much. 

Their food is definitely *expansive*, I'll give them that much. Granted, we got to see both the breakfast and lunch food (though there's a lot of overlap), but still. It is definitely a large place, but not all of the food was really worth it: 
* Sliders: so good. 
* Rest of their meat selection: salty and clearly not the best quality. Tossed it. 
* Seafood: kinda mediocre. 
* Cheese at their charcuterie: pretty respectable, though not amazing. 
* Meat at their charcuterie: tasted cheap. 
* Dim sum: pretty respectable. 
* The rest of their Asian food: tasted like cheap buffet Asian food. Not worth it. Specifically calling out the supposedly-sushi for tasting like cheap sushi you'd get at a buffet. Which, granted, is where we were, but for this expensive, I'd expect a little better. 
* Tacos: mediocre, not terrible but I've had way better. 
* Desserts: very expansive, and sooo good. Well, so good except the ice cream. The ice cream was crap. Funny how that works. 
* I'm sure there were other things, too, but those are all the ones I can remember. 

I wouldn't be surprised if this *were* the best casino buffet in LV, but that'd be kinda sad, cause it wasn't really that great. Not for the price, anyway. 

Mimosas were quality, though, I'll give them that - didn't taste like they skimped on either the champagne or the OJ. And it was definitely free-flowing.

Excellent buffet.  Went during dinner, and tried pretty much all from the prime rib, to the Chinese dim sum, Mexican chile verde, and the snow crab legs.  I'm not a desert person, but all the deserts were great.  One star was taken away as our server was nowhere to be found most of the time.  Prices are up there for dinner, about $59 for adults, about half for kids.  Other than that, will most likely return to Bacchanal in the our next Vegas visit.

Great buffet. Inside Caesar's Palace

It is a little pricey but the food is great. 
I love the all you can eat crab, although I do wish I requested them to heat it up. 

I also tasted their prime rib. Very good. 

I never waited to get into a buffet before, and this one had about a 15-20 minuet wait during brunch. It was definitely worth the wait.
LOVE IT!!!! Best buffett in Las Vegas.... quality is amazing!!!!! Food is awesome, I cant wait to come back....

Excellent buffet. Nice, clean, up scale restaurant. Who can ask for more? Crab legs, big shrimp, endless mimosas, not to mention great desserts:. Creme brule,  carrot cake, tiramisu. And, a great salad bar area. Second time here. I think I will come back each time I am in Vegas.
Excellent buffet in Vegas, one of my favs. It closes a little too early but that doesn't change my love for it. Amazing selection of food all cooked to perfection

Fantastic.

Let's just say I threw up.....just a little bit.

My last plate...

http://instagram.com/p/YD-oXPKsvB/

This place was absolutely delicious. I made it a point to try more than 85% of what they had and I might say every single dish was made with love. They were all culinary masterpieces full of flavor. We asked for another type of Italian pasta and without hesitation they special made it for us! And not to mention, the dessert section was perfect. They had everything you could think of! Try the covered strawberries if you go. Expensive but worth every penny!

I would like to give 5 stars to the manager, Raz Peri, for taking care of us the other night. Came here to celebrate my grandfathers bday and we were very excited for the all you can eat KING crab legs. When we arrived and found out what they meant by that (a few king crab legs scattered in with decent snow crab legs) I was disappointed since I  remember the day when they would pile up mound after mound of pre-cut king crab on your plate.  Raz explained how much Bacchanal was losing when they were doing this so they had to scale back. He then took care of us with a big, fat plate of king crab for the miscommunication. Much appreciated!

Had not been to a Las Vegas buffet in years but we came to Vegas with our 22 year old son and some of his friends for his bday weekend.  He really wanted to have a LV buffet experience.... So we came here. 
It was 1pm, party of 9 on a Friday and there was a long line so that took about 30 min or so to get through. Once inside we were quite impressed... 
The food and service were just fantastic. We stayed for about 2.5 hours and tried just about everything! 

As with most buffet's there were lots of people so getting food was (in some areas) a little bit crowded but over all everything was organized and clean. Dishes had good presentation and the food was delicious. The biggest and best dessert station ever! 
Coffee was on point!

Everything you'd expect from a high end casino's buffet: Huge selection, decent quality foods, and overpriced admission.  I'm not saying that it was a bad experience; On the contrary, I enjoyed my visit.  But to me, in the end the food doesn't justify the price.  I'll elaborate.

As I mentioned, the food selection is quite extensive and diverse.  It seems every major nationality and ethnicity is represented somewhere in the buffet.  I'll use my gluttony as an example: My first plate consisted of asian-style stir fry and meats, with rice and an Asian soup.  My second plate was build-it-yourself tacos, with middle eastern style doughy stuff and meats.  My third plate was typical American, steak and trip-tip with potatoes and corn. The dessert section is fairly large too- lots of gelatos, cakes, and other sweet treats.  Overall, most of the food quality would range between very good to excellent.

Now, even though the buffet is tasty and diverse, I still have a few negatives I can't quite get over:
Price- The buffet is great, but it's quality isn't much different from other buffets on the strip.  For example, the quality equals that of Planet Hollywood's buffet, and PH comes in at around $10 cheaper per person, with a shorter wait time. Which leads me to my next point...
Service- If you come during meal times, you're going to wait.  Unless you're a VIP, you wait to pay and wait again to be seated.  From the time we got in line until we got seated took about 40 minutes, which is kind of crazy for a lunch.  And after you're seated, if you're thirsty you are at the mercy of a server and must wait for beverages and refills. Which in our experience, was very lacking and slow. I went through two plates of food with an empty drink, and only received a refill when I flagged down a different passing server. 

So in conclusion, the food was very good and the selection was great.  The price was steep and the service lackluster.  Next time I do a Vegas buffet, I'll probably try somewhere else where the cost is a bit more in line with the value.

Don't bother.  This place is disorganized, expensive, and expensive.  It takes hours to sit down (or an extra $40 - $120 to wait in a slightly shorter line).  It seems like all the good food is stalked viciously by other patrons.  The staff seem overworked and in no mood to assist you with anything. I would not return here... for the cost I expected much better all around.  Instead I got mediocre food and sub-par service, not to mention I spent more time wandering around looking for food I wanted to eat than I spent eating what I eventually settled on.

This is hands down my all time favorite and go to buffet in vegas right now. Every single time i am in vegas i HAVE to eat here. And every single time it NEVER disappoints. 

There have been a few times that the line was long (~1 1/2hr wait) and times where there was no line to wait. I would say there were specific times the wait time is low but this time i went at 2pm and we had to wait 1hr. So its all about luck! Just like the rest of vegas! Haha! 

The perks of this buffet goes on and on but the main reasons are the lamb chops, the oysters, the cocktail shrimp, the mac n cheese, and the desserts.... (Mochi ice creams, the crepes, oreo mousse cake, even the cookies are yumm) 

Prices are definitely high.... But its okay because the food is so good.... ALSO the have a new drink called iced peach green tea? Oh so good.

Let's just say I am not a super buffet fanatic.  But let me tell ya...Bacchanal is the truth!  It's worth the wait and the money.  We went with a group of 9, on January 1st, so needless to say it was insane.  We stood in line of 30 minutes of so before we were seated.  Service was great. Food was overwhelmingly amazing.  So much to try and nothing was bad...nothing.  We will certainly be back. 

If you come with a group of 6 or more, go to the group line and have a credit card ready to charge for the party...it moves much quicker than the individual line. 

Enjoy!

#1, NOT worth the money
#2, completely hyped up beyond all reason
#3, food looks good, lacks execution and seasoning

Rediculous!

This place has lots of good reviews and we celebrated my wife's birthday trying this buffet for the first time for my big family party.  Overall, there are lots of good selection of food.  We ate there around 4pm and paid the dinner price.  If you are looking for good seafood, this is NOT the place to eat.  The reasons are the oysters are not fresh. the sushi selections are not good and even the prime rib I had was not tender.   

PROS:
good fried food.
good asian food
crab legs are good if you like butter.

CONS
not a good value for price/quality

The ambiance, hip-fine dining. The service, helpful and friendly. Those are about the only pros of this "top rated" Las Vegas buffet. The first thing that caught my eye upon paying at the cashier was the vast amount of empty tables. Now this wouldn't have been a problem had it not been a literal hour wait. Sacrificing the customers needs in order to make it easier on service? Questionable. The most important part though, for a 60 dollar dinner would be the food. One would think they would focus on this factor a bit more but every single item available was either completely tasteless or overly spiced. How do you justify a 60 dollar meal with cardboard food of low quality. Is your food cost really worth sacrificing quality? I truly wish they would focus more on customer needs and food quality. 

Tldr; wanna feel fancy and eat low quality food for fine dining prices? Bachannal is the place for you.
I'm  not normally a fan of buffets but this was fantastic.  Hands down the best buffet I've ever been to. Everything was good and the selection was incredible.

Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas, neigh -the world. 

There are already a million reviews explaining why Bacchanal is the best buffet, so I won't reinvent the wheel. Instead I will address the FAQs people have repeatedly asked me about Bacchanal so if you have out of towners you can just direct them to this review. 

Is it worth waiting in line?
Yes, unlike your birth, this one is worth waiting for. I'm positive you have spent hours in line waiting for worse things- rides at Disney, movies that ended up sucking, visiting your mom- Bacchanal is one line that actually pays off in food. Also, if you are willing to throw down some bribes you will find yourself waiting in line a lot less time.

I hate gross trough buffets....
Not really a question Karen (its always a Karen asking this)- but don't you worry your little highlighted head about it. Bacchanal makes almost everything in small plate form so you aren't scooping out wods of 8 hour old scrambled eggs onto your plate to go with your mini triangle waffles. They have a lot of stations where food is prepared fresh for you, and if something sits too long they take it back. 

Seems a little pricey
If this is the biggest waste of money you have in Vegas than you have gotten off easy. Gambling, strippers, gambling with strippers- you don't even get to walk away with a feeling of full from these things, at Bacchanal not only do you get that but you get free bonus gifts: diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and weight gain- FREE! But seriously, its not that much more expensive than other similar buffets but it is preposterously better. 

I'm staying at a different casino that's far away...
Well then your travel agent sucks. Nevertheless, get your ass in a cab and head over to Caesars, I'm not eating crappy food cause your cheap ass decided to stay in the Luxor. 


Now, some random food recs

-Fried Chicken- this is always amazing, a must get
-street tacos- if they are making them, stick to pork
-Soups- I usually never get soup at a buffet but here it is A++++
-Sole roll ups- not what these are actually called but whatever the rolled sole dish is
-Dessert- just about everything


Things to avoid
-italian station- not the best and makes you feel full

I'm not the biggest fan of buffets but my mom raved about this place after she came back from her Christmas trip so when I headed down to Vegas in March, I had to see how good this place really was for $50/person and the three hour wait. 

My boyfriend and I got to Bacchanal around 5 and saw that the line was already wrapped around a couple times. A few people ahead of us said that they hadn't moved since they had got there an hour and a half ago so we decided to just pay the $15/person and skip to the express line. We still had to wait about 30 mins which was sort of ridiculous since we paid close to $200 for two people. 

The buffet is new so the decor and ambiance was nice. The way the stations for food were set up was also great. The seafood area had the longest line but you could see that the food was fresh. They chucked oysters in front of you and constantly replaced the crab legs. 

There is also an American section, Mexican section, Italian section and a Chinese section way in the back.

Their dessert area was the best! Lots of gelato flavors to choose from, wide selection of cakes, cookies, and even ice cream mochi. The secret though is to get their made-to-order souffles.
The food is always magnificent, although the old chef did have a better shrimp and grits recipe. The atmosphere is upscale. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are awesome.  The price is high but worth it.

As the expression that Phil Knight made so incredibly famous says,

Just Do It.

The Bacchanal is as advertised.  If you are not happy with the food here then you need a very lengthy look in the mirror my friend.  The options are astounding in both their quality and abundance.  There is essentially something for everyone and the only knock on this place is the level of self control that it is inevitably going to make you choose to implement.  If you want it to, if you allow to, yes, this buffet can be the complete demise of a day in Vegas.  However, if you issue some restraint on volume then you are looking at a fantastic food option for Las Vegas.

The worst buffet I have ever had. The worst thing is the seafood. They are not fresh at all. Want to throw up when eating the oyster and crawfish. The oyster smell very bad. The crab is not that great and very cold. Don't ever go here

Holy Moly on macaroni!!!. Batman This place has got to the king of buffets in Las Vegas, no joker. Absolutely Come early stay late. This is the best bang for your buck. Robin Don't forget to leave room for Mr Freeze and his shave Ice. Half the fun is to explore and see what treats you will find.

The BEST buffet in Vegas! Don't agree? Check it out for yourself and you can thank me later.

FOOD. 
I'm not a fan of buffets, except for the ones in Vegas. My favorite buffet before I went to Bacchanal was Wynn's "The Buffet." I thought that one was delicious (still is), but Bacchanal takes the cake on this feud. Where to begin... I guess I'll start from end to end.
Starting from the very right side of the buffet, there is a huge display of Asian food of all types. Chinese food includes a variety of stuff, like honey walnut shrimp, beef and broccoli, fried rice, you name it. Next, there's a ton of dim sum options to choose from like steamed pork bun, shrimp dumpling, pork shumai, and more. There's congee available (with all the fix ins!) and miso soup. There's also fresh sushi and rolls available. My favorite is the salmon and the California rolls with fresh tuna and salmon sashimi on top. There's a chef available to make yakisoba and mongolian style noodles, as well as ramen! YES, there's RAMEN! 
Then, there's a salad bar with a ton of stuff (I didn't go there, obviously since I don't know much about it) and a huge display of breads, cheeses and salami style meats. Also, there's a section just for olives... fancy. 
There's an Italian section with a variety of pizzas on one side and then pasta on the other side. I realllllly liked their Pasta Carbonara. Randomly, in the middle of the pizza and pasta, you can get HOT CRAB cooked and sliced down the middle (no cracking)!
There's a Mexican station with a bunch of stuff and a taco maker! You just tell the person what kind of meat you want and the toppings you want. They also have a fresh juice section where they have pineapple, guava, mango juice, and horchata bottled for you to enjoy.
The American food section has sliders, hot dogs, mac and cheese, fries, sweet potato tater tots, mashed potatoes, variety of veggies, prime rib, brisket, ribs, you name it. The selection is huge. Then there's the cold seafood section with crab, shrimp, oysters, everything.
My FAVORITE part of this buffet is their dessert section! They have a CREPE MAKER! One time, I downed three of these in one visit. 0 shame here. They also have mochi ice cream in just about every flavor, gelato, cheesecake pops, cake pops, brownies, cookies, cakes, and more. They offer gluten free and low fat options too, but don't get those... if you're dieting, don't come to a buffet.

SERVICE. 
I haven't always had the best service here, but on my most recent visit, I received excellent service by a Filipino man who was our waiter! He refilled our drinks constantly and took away our plates. He was kind and extremely quick to do things, which I really appreciated.

PRICE. 
About $50-$60 a person... typical for a Vegas buffet. Rest assured, this place is definitely worth the money as long as you come hungry!

It's not a Vegas trip unless I come here. Until I find a buffet better than this one (unlikely), I'll be coming here every time I'm in town.
