I'm a vegetarian and I had a lot to choose from. As much as I could expect anyway. Wish the soba noodles/udon could have vegetarian broth as an option. There wasn't much vegetarian option for the dimsum either. 

The last time I went for dinner the wait was 1 hour and ridiculous. I went to Wynn instead and loved the buffet. It was cheaper too and had pretty much everything Buchannal had. I thought the Wynn one had better dessert (although less selection and less visually appealing, it was more appetizing). My family thought all the meat was better at Wynn too. And there's no long lines and the price is a little cheaper. Anytime there's a line now at bucchanal, I'm going straight to the Wynn.
Great buffet with something for everyone. Not your typical Vegas buffet. Food is delicious and everything is prepared fresh. A must see!

A great variety to pick from. Was disappointed in the server who helped us. She never came to greet us. Saw her walking to other tables but not ours I had to walk up to a hostess to ask if we can have someone stop by our table to get us water. I would have given this place 5 stars but the lack to customer service made the experience less worthwhile.

Food was really good and the variety was pretty amazing for a Vegas buffet.  I never even made it to half the areas and needed a wheelchair by the time I gave up.  It's not cheap but it's worth it if you go hungry.

I tried its lunch buffet on Thursday, 1/31/13 around 11:40AM. The line was not long, the place was about 70% full.
Pro:
1. A vast selection of foods, their ingredients are quite fresh.
2. It is one of the best buffet I ever had. I would rather spend a few dollars more here that at Bellagio's buffet.
3. Its sweet counter with all kinds of ice-cream is really super.
Con:
1. The quality of preparing the food could be better, considering the freshness of its ingredients. I think some of the meat or fish are on oily or buttery side.
2. I would like to see more steamed fish or vegetables, lightly salted and less oily to be good for senior citizens and health conscientious people.
3. I detect a tint of detergent in my ice water glass.

I went there for experience. I enjoyed it. However, being a senior citizen, I would like to see more steamed fish before I go there for lunch buffet again.

We went here because of the fantastic reviews everywhere online about this place, and because it was rated #1 out of all LV buffets.
I can understand now why it was rated #1.  It was a phenomenal spread.  We went on Christmas day and they were packed.  Thank God we went early in the morning to get a ticket for the evening - everyone who had not gotten a ticket earlier were turned away.
We thought because of the ticket we would only have to wait a short bit to be seated, but quite the contrary.  We ended up waiting 2+ hours to be seated.  
But once we got in, it was amazing.  Seafood could have been better, but their asian dished were great.  And the dessert was the most amazing spread I've ever seen!  Go for the desserts and just fill up on those.
Extremely expensive!  we paid $130 for just 2 adults.  
we will probably never do it again, but glad we tried it just once.

I bought in to reviews that said this is the best buffet in Vegas, and I do not share that opinion.  It's not worth the price when you can eat at a better buffet at the Wynn for less.  I paid about $60 for a Saturday afternoon buffet at Caesars, but I paid about $35 for a Thursday afternoon buffet at the Wynn and thought it was much better.  The Caesar's buffet does have all you can eat snow crab legs, but I was not impressed.  We have much better crab meat on the east coast.

Favorite buffet in town. There is a large variety of food, service was great and food was fresh. It is well worth the entrance fee. The mini red velvet pancakes are most definitely a must during the brunch hours.

Although I waited in line to eat here longer than any nightclub, I loved this place! 

So, buffets are typically pretty amazing because you get to eat a little (or a lot) of everything. This buffet has more food stations than you'd typically see and their food is actually really good and fresh. 

I came for brunch which is a good time to go since they serve bottomless mimosas! Also, if you go during the tail end of brunch you get more selection since they start transitioning into the lunch menu. 

Their seafood, sushi, and dessert stations were my faves. Their dessert station includes several different flavors of gelato. Try the Thai iced tea and French toast gelato. Yumm!

Not worth the hassle.  Food was only okay.  Nothing special.  Hard to be impressed by so-so renditions of everything.  Nothing was outright terrible from a food perspective, just don't know why everyone is preening about how awesome it is.  Maybe part of it is the hunger effect where everything tastes better because you're starving because you've waited almost two hours to get in.  Or you've bought an expensive dud and don't want to admit it.  From the reviews, lots and lots of people love this buffet, just not me.  Maybe my memory is hazy but the last few Vegas buffets I went to I enjoyed the experience much more.  

There are $15 cheap buffets back home that have much tastier (though less pricey) food.  Anything Asian there is done better by thousands of local joints back at people's hometown, wherever it may be.  Ditto for the Italian, seafood, prime rib and meats, and deserts, and whatever else I ended up getting from their troughs.  If for food alone, maybe 2 stars.  Price and service adjusts downward to one star.  As I was eating I kept thinking about those generic places you see with A#1 Best American food, and Chinese food, and Italian, etc plastered all over their store frontage.  

Price is what it is.  Up to individual preference on whether you think it's reasonable.  To me the cost/benefit was way out of whack.  

Service is terrible.  First, I don't mind prices in this range generally, but then as seems typical with popular Vegas buffets , you get treated like cattle, low rent cattle at that.  My fault really, I should have just gone for a nice meal somewhere.  Travel channel and the like suckered me into wanting to experience the classic Vegas buffet.  

The check in time/text thing they do is a good tool, but executed poorly.  You still have to unnecessarily stand around for another 45 min/hour after they tell you to come back to hang out in a glacially slow line.  Shorten that time a bit and the experience would be much better.  Restaurants I've been to that give you pagers don't page you and then ask you to wait almost an hour afterward.  Vegas is bigger with more room to roam than a restaurant parking lot, but this process could be much more refined and optimized.

5 cashiers, great.  Except they spend most of their time standing around not ringing people up because the line moves too slow.  They probably only need 3 of them based on how the line worked-- 2 to handle the VIP gamblers and such (really only need 1, but they're VIP!!! and of course can't have any sort of line to wait in)  that went to the front of the line and only 1 to handle the hundreds of other regular cattle.  It felt like more than half their time was spent standing around doing no work and not looking at the massive line of people standing there waiting to pay.  Not their fault really as the massive line of people who had paid was backed up to the cashiers with little room for more. Refer back to the comment about handling the line better.  

Inside decor is fine, except don't know why they choose such cheap looking tables and chairs.  Read a bit about how much money they spent on the place and was surprised that it felt like the tables and chairs were from a 1980s Denny's or Sizzlers.  I normally don't care too much about furnishings and wouldn't have mentioned it except it seemed weirdly out of place in something trying to be the top buffet in town.  Maybe the word buffet is my answer and underneath all the hype is just that, a buffet.

Please explain to me how such an amazing Buffet exist?! Anybody who is going to go to a buffet in Vegas do NOT go anywhere else but here! This place has everything you want and need! Servers kept glasses full of drinks, there wasn't a single food I ate that I didn't like! 10/5!!! Lol amazing!

This place is excess central. Came here on st pattys day and waited in a 15 minute line. On St Pattys day they were also giving out free unlimited mimosas. Definitely a plus. Everything here is excessive, in a good way. They go the extra mile to give you top quality food. The seafood section is the most brilliant buffet section I have ever seen. Steamed Crabs, Gigantic Skrimps, Oyster Shots, Lobster Soup. What more can you ask for? The dessert section was probably equally amazing. The crepes were out of this world. The flan was the best I've ever had. Only negative was that the macarons sucked. How hard is it to mess up? Either way, Bacchanal now has the crown for best buffet in vegas.

My wife and I went there for our only buffet experience while in Vegas. A little pricey. The that was fresh was really good,  but a lot of the food was not fresh sitting for a while. Was not a horrible experience but I would try another place.

I would probably give this place more stars if it wasn't for the tacky and cheap inside decorations! It is very small inside for the price I was expecting it to be elegant but the station casinos have better decor than this place. Tiny plain tables and chairs are dirty. Don't believe all the hype about this place half the stuff that you see in these yelp pictures are no longer available. I'm sure they did when they first opened but then stopes caring about what they serve.  The desert where the best part. They did serve a few different items I haven't seen served at a buffet before but everything else is pretty typical to a standard buffet. Not worth the 50 dollars a person.

Best buffet I've ever experienced. The best variety of food from all over the world in one crack. Try the lobster chowder and the smoked salmon shooter. Those two dishes were so tasty that I had to go back for more. The food quality is also up there. I highly recommend. Pricey but totally worth the experience.

After having a bad experience here that was cut short due to food poisoning at Bacchannal, I wrote a review here on Yelp of my experience. Stephanie, one of the managers, contacted me and asked if I would like to further discuss what happened. So we did through several emails and Stephanie, very apologetic offered me what appeared to be comped passes back to the buffet, (that appeared to seem fair to say the least, since my experience was cut short the first time due to food poisoning).  I was hesitant at first but figured if I was in town, why not give it another try since she seemed genuine about making things right and fair and perhaps it could have been an isolated circumstance the first time.  It is a buffet after all, with thousands of people passing through on a daily basis, not everything can be right all the time at any given moment, can it?  So we arrange a reservation and I get there.  To my utter shock and surprise, Stephanie said my comped passes were for a line jumping pass and a round of free cocktails--NOT FOR THE BUFFET. So she wanted me to pay for the buffet--something she could have easily straightforwardly told me through her several emails, but did not until I arrived in line at the cashier. Classic bait and switch? I believe so.  But wow...I thought customer service was an important thing to a place that claims to give its customer's "AN EPIC EXPERIENCE" but this was quite far from it. Not only did they not care to make things right and FAIR to their customers, they tried to be sneaky using the good old baiting and switching/playing games to appear like they wanted to make things right.  Shame on you Bacchannal Buffet and your management for doing this and not caring to make things right or at least fair to your customers.  This experience was EPIC alright, a great EPIC DISAPPOINTMENT.

Okay, so I will say the food was quite glorious, but no amount of glorious food could warrant the holiday price ($69.99). Including tip (maybe I'm too generous?), it came out to $87 per person. Yikes! Tag on the wait at each station and you have a meal that just wasn't "worth it" in my eyes.

My family and I came here the Sunday after Thanksgiving. We arrived at 5:30pm and we were seated at 5:50pm. Good thing we got here when we did, because I saw the line reallllly building up by the time we walked in. Don't judge me, but I actually did try at least a bite of everything they had - they even had this back room of food that I didn't notice until maybe two rounds of food in. That back room had a pasta bar and noodle soup bar, as well as a salad bar, dim sum, and sushi.

A couple of comments on their food. I thought the prime rib was okay, and I actually waited in line to get a second piece. The first piece of prime rib I got was tough and a little dry, but the second piece was better. The only thing I didn't like was that the knife (like a butter knife) didn't cut through the prime rib, so I was eating it like an animal. Don't judge me. The oysters weren't super fresh, or maybe I just had the bad pieces left. And some crab legs weren't really fresh, even though they cook it for you right there - they stuck to the shell. The pork belly was very well presented on little plates, but it was dry like jerky because it had been sitting under heat lamps.

Dessert was by far my favorite, and much better than Paris in my opinion. The macarons were cute and delicious. Gelato was also good. But, my favorite part - they had rambutans (a fruit) in this jar that looked like it was on display. I happened to ask if those were for eating, and they told me it was. I love rambutans! I think when people saw me and my family grabbing them, they went in as well. Tip: try a rambutan! They're like the often-forgotten cousin of the lychee.

Service was a little slow. It took forever to get drinks and drink refills, and the plate clearing also took a while. Again, I'm not hating on the food. They might have had a busy night, which could explain the dryness and some of the dishes not being up to par. But still, it was good. The only thing I have to hate on them for is that ridiculously high price. It's simply not worth it on a holiday weekend night.

My favorite buffet that is on the strip, but one of the more expensive ones. I came here with a large group and we got seated pretty quickly. They charged us 18% gratuity since we were a group of more than 6. The food was pretty amazing. There was wide selection to choose from, including Italian, Mexican, and Chinese food. There was also a section for meat and seafood, which I loved the most. The food was great quality and also had really nice presentation. The dessert section also had a big selection, my favorite being the macaroons, gelato, and creme brulee! I would say that it was worth the money.

I visited Vegas recently, went to 3 different buffets in different hotels. Out of 3, Bacchanal gets my 5 stars. It is a nice looking place with huge variety. I am not a seafood person, but if you re into seafood, this is a denitely buffet you would want to visit. I enjoy everything I ate.

I googled "best restaurants in LV" and this place is always on the top 10, so I wanted to see what makes this place special....

I must say that they have Great food selection & the dessert bar is to DIE for!!!! Love the desserts!! So far the best buffet in Las Vegas...

im sorry---THE BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS HANDS DOWN....the prime rib at dinner, the seafood, the asian ribs and sui pork is to DIE FOR...the only bad thing i can say about it is ... the sushi selection was sad....maybe 5 different sushi selections and no sashimi ....was weird...but everything else was F**ING AMAZING...WELL WORTH THE 55.00 PRICETAG

If you love Buffets this place is for you. I suggest you get in line before 5:00 pm to avoid the long lines and the possibility of not being able to get in. Hopefully you bring an empty stomach to enjoy the mass variety of food they put out. The dessert bar is incredible. The bad news is you have approximately two hours to indulge and stuff yourself. Don't worry 2 hours is plenty of time. I would give yourself 2 hours eating your favorite main meal and another hour eating your favorite dessert. Enjoy its Vegas.

Best Las Vegas buffet by far! Was disappointed that they didn't have mochi ice-cream but was highly impressed by the pho and Asian food. I know you can get Asian food anywhere but when a buffet nails the Asian food, they have to be good! Crab legs, meatballs, green chicken chile, green tea creme brûlée and lamb shanks were on the top of our list!

One of the best buffets we can try in America. Wow!! 
This is the most amazing place you can ever try if you're a foodie. The staff was sweet and very kind. They had Italian, Mexican, Asian, American, Seafood and whole lots of desserts.
Well, the chefs were very kind very friendly and they had a live grill and live counters for desserts. It's not something to point out at the moment it's a really one such place we need to try. We cannot try every single item but we can try most of them according to our choice. All items are kept in small quantities according to our choice if we like it we could pick them more. A wide range of choice of slices of bread, soups. There wasn't any dish that we can point out that it was bad because everything is high quality and great in taste who wouldn't love to try everything.

To be honest I love buffet, it is my kryptonite reasoning being that I like to try everything on the menu but you can't always do that at restaurants. This place had lots of options as for the quality and taste it was not like amazing I'm in a food coma afterwards good but it was okay my buffet crazing is satisfied for now good. The quality of the food was simple, nothing really special at all chicken was dry, meat was plain, sushi... omg... sushi was horrible (don't try the sushi) and the dessert was not so good.

I wish everything tasted a little better bc we paid too much for lunch. I don't regret eating here but do regret paying so much for a place that wasn't amazingly great as expected. 

Not worth the hype at all, if you say it is I suggest you try the other buffet in the area first and compare them after.

Everything was delicious! Soooo much variety...asian (even Pho), mexican, american, super fresh seafood (crab legs for days) and of course the dessert bar. The price is very resonable since everything was goumet.

It's among the better buffets but still lacking in taste. The choices are varied but not vast. Crab legs and oyster and oyster shooters makes it better than others. Still nothing notable, would recommend Wicked Spoon instead if price is a factor (it's cheaper by $10).

If you're going to charge what Caesar's charges for most of its services and restaurants, you'd better be good. The Bacchanal Buffet certainly is.

For my money, it's easily the best buffet in Vegas over some pretty darned good ones (Bellagio, Paris, and Rio come to mind as honorable mentions). The food selection is as wide as it gets, and everything's pretty darned good. Yes, it's expensive, but I've been here a few times and it's blown me away.

Fair warning: Do not just show up thinking you'll waltz right in, especially on weekends. For dinner, waits can be up to an hour at the busiest times, so be sure to account for that. Trust me, though, it's worth the wait.

Great service.  Very crowded but very well organized buffet.  All the people working here is super nice, they look happy helping you. Food is very diverse and good depending on what you like. They have Asian food, Tacos, meat, ribs, sea food, pastries. 
Worth it the cost.

My wife heard so many raves about this damn place and dragged me here. You know what happens to your manhood if you don't obey.. So, we came.
We arrived around 2:30 on Friday nov 9th. There was no lines. That was a sign but we paid 68.00 for both and started our adventure. 
The buffet selection was bad. The only good thing came out of this was around 3pm they started bringing out crab legs for dinner. We got to try some but the crabs were crap (way too salty and not edible)  also frozen. 
Bottomline, overpriced over rated. I was very disturbed and will never come back.

Long review again: see the TLDR plus full rating in the updated version that I'll post tomorrow. This is mostly just about the food.

I came at 10ish on Christmas Eve and we were seated immediately. Food & drink options: They had a juice bar that they were cleaning up... they replaced it with a salsa bar but before they did I got some green juice and watermelon juice. They had a nice meat bar where they served cuts of various sausages, thick cut bacon, and brisket. Further down the line I picked up some hash browns, mac and cheese, eggs benedict, "lobster" benedict, crab cakes, fried chicken and waffles, fingerling potatoes, and some mini pancakes. They had a cheese bar with an impressive amount of accoutrements... but a disappointing amount of charcuterie and cheese. I also tried a deviled egg and a watermelon dish. They also had a seafood bar, I had a handful of shrimp, a few oysters, and crab legs. Lobsters came out towards the end of my meal. I saw it on a few diner's plates so I asked two staff members where I could find it. The first said lobster wasn't being served but the second person got it right. The line wrapped around the whole back room and it took a while for everyone to be served. Some people were taking 5-6 of them at once... Anyways, everything else seemed like typical stir fried buffet fare. I like the idea of small plates but some of those plates are f***ing hot. NASA's guidelines to tolerance to hot temperatures before skin damage occurs are set between 110°-112°F and I'm pretty sure most of those plates exceeded that. My brother said they provide little silicone handles that you can use but I didn't see a single one while I was there. So you're forced to pile them onto the plates... and you can only fit about 3-4 of them on one plate.

The food: The green was alright but not sweet enough for my tastes. So pretty much, not sweetened at all. It tasted of cucumbers and unidentified greens. The watermelon juice was alright. The sausages were good, the thick cut bacon... not so much. The brisket was decent, tender and slightly smoky in flavor but a bit of it was hard and tough to chew. The hash browns and mac and cheese were okay. The eggs benedict was pretty good and flavorful. The "lobster" benedict was essentially the same just with a slight sprinkle of lobster. It tasted no different from the regular eggs benedict. The crab cakes were one of my favorite dishes here but after a few of them, you get kind of tired of the taste. I especially liked the asparagus shoot garnish. It provided a nice crunchy texture. The fried chicken tasted like nothing special and felt like it could have been from Popeyes or KFC. People rave about the fingerling potatoes but they didn't taste like anything special and were actually a bit tough to chew. Some hurt my teeth when I bit into them. The mini pancakes were a waste of time. A lot of these items I could say tasted decent but I had to remind myself that I was at a $60 buffet and questioned myself why I was wasting precious stomach space on only average tasting food. The cheese bar had anchovies, guava jam, nuts, and honey. There were essentially two cheeses: one was crusted with some herb, the other the same thing without the herb, and a brie (I believe it was president, just a generic brand). The prosciutto was cut too thick and had been sitting out for too long and was dry and hard. The deviled egg I tried looked good but tasted disgusting. It was bitter for some reason and tasted off. The watermelon just tasted like a cube of watermelon sprinkled with Tajín. The shrimp was good but the oysters... not so much. The oysters were frozen and tasted like they had gone bad and were super briney. Disgusting. Props to them having real (and potent) horseradish. My parents said the crab legs were lacking. The lobster was alright, a bit tough and chewy but the flavor was alright. I wish this had come out a bit earlier and I would have eaten a lot more of it.

I've heard a lot of good things about their dessert but I wasn't feeling it. I tried their eggnogg crème brule, chocolate peppermint cheesecake, mini egg tarts, tiramisu, cheesecake, rice pudding with passion fruit foam, and gelato. The holiday desserts were disgusting. They had an overwhelmingly artificial flavor. The mini egg tarts were dry and not that great but hey at least they're cute and make for a good picture. The cheesecake was the same. nice presentation, not memorable in taste. rice pudding was also nothing special and the foam was overly tart. The gelato was overly flavored and tasted like soap / perfume. The tiramisu was the only thing I enjoyed. It was deliciously moist and heavy on the coffee / liqueur flavor. Pretty bitter but it was still enjoyable. Such a shame I wasn't able to try the crepes. I'm not paying $60 again just to try them.

Is it really a trip to Vegas if you don't overindulge at a buffet or two? We were really excited to try this place out on a recent trip to Vegas. We went as early as possible and we were still quoted an hour and a half. We put our name in and walked around the hotel but were called back within half an hour. Our service was excellent. We opted to do the all you can drink beer/wine package in addition to the buffet. They had something for everyone: meat, seafood, and veggie options as well. For the price, I did expect a little bit more but that's Vegas I suppose. If you do not eat seafood, I don't see that the price is worth it. I definitely felt like this place was a pig factory. Getting people in and out as quickly as possible and it felt forced. Our server was excellent though and kept my wine refilled at all times and kept our table super clean. What does this buffet have that buffets elsewhere don't have? Variety. I enjoyed the sushi and dim sum and my bf loved the crepe bar. I wasn't overly impressed with the dessert selection but they did have plenty of fresh fruit to choose from. As with most things in Vegas, expect to wait in line for just about everything.

Was good but not like amazeballs.  It was a high end buffet.  Not the best. But I'm not sure how you could do better.  It was a buffet so all the shitty things that come with that are present which make buffets a taxing experience.  Long lines to get in.  Long lines to get food.  Very expensive.  I wouldn't go again.

coming to vegas is basically all about eating the buffet. for the value eating at buffet is the cheapest. needless to say the food was decent but the price is too high. While we only came here to eat, nothing else, I do not like Caesars properties, but still satisfying for eating lunch before heading back home.

One of the best buffets in Vegas with endless selections, but not as good the second time around.  The Asian section is the best with just about every type of Asian cuisine represented.  The wait was long as usual, but being a Total Rewards Platinum member or higher will save you a lot of waiting time.

Overall our experience at Bacchanal Buffet was excellent. My favorite dish would have to be the Mac n cheese, it was so creamy and cheesy  and delicious. Also, the dessert was phenomenal! So many choices and each dessert was so delicious!! They had make your own crepes, make your own snow ice things with syrup and jello, Thai boba iced tea with ice cream, a bunch of gelato, chocolate mousse, cupcakes with a shot of syrup u had to squirt in the middle, cheescake, key lime tarts, mini apple pies, cookies, blueberry cake, cake pops, papaya, blueberries, pineapple, Asian puddings, custard tarts, and so much more! As good as there dessert is, some of their main dishes were not so good. Their nachos were soggy and had to many toppings. Their fish tacos were overly fried and hard. Their rice with pineapple chicken kabob was dry and flavorless. If you like seafood they have a lot of lobster, crab, and oysters. Overall I think this buffet is great especially if you want to try a. Lot of different foods.

We had an amazing time at Bacchanal Buffet. We had a Groupon for brunch with mimosas. Though the mimosas were a little weak, the food and fresh fruit made up for it. We will def be visiting again. Good food, great staff, and great selection. The seafood spread was awesome, as was the guacamole, and dessert spread. This is definitely a buffet we will check out again.

Yup, they weren't kidding when they say this is the best buffet on the Strip.  Expensive but pretty darn good.  We ate the lunch buffet.  Where else but in Vegas can you get

Ginseng & Chicken Soup steamed in a ceramic bowl
Ramen Station
Oyster Shooters
Fresh Shucked Oysters
Sushi
American BBQ meats of all kinds - beef brisket, sausages, beef
Fresh made soft tacos with Wagyu Beef
Pasta - all kinds
Fat prawns with just the tail on
Ceviche
Chinese Noodles
Roast Duck (Chinese style) with Plum Sauce
Dim Sum
Build your own salads
Hot Sauce Bar at the Mexican station
Freshly squeezed juice in your own jar - cucumber, watermelon, tropical, orange

all in one place?

The lineup wasn't bad on a Tuesday at 11 a.m.  The line started to build at about noon to 1 p.m.

Come to the Bacchanal Feast with an empty stomach!
Tons of selections! Their desserts are amazing. I was very sad that they don't have crab for lunch but I'll just have to come back.

Let me start off by saying I generally hate buffets. I would rather pay more to get higher quality food made to order instead of sitting under heat lamps for hours with people walking by and coughing in their general direction. That said, this is one of the least bad buffets I have ever been to, the other one that still exists being Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo. There's also the one that no longer exists, the Rio seafood buffet BEFORE it started to suck (back in the early 2000s; I got married and brought my husband years later but all the seafood smelled and tasted totally rancid) -- since it sucks now, I can't count that one anymore.

So which to choose? Depends on what you want. The Asian food was better at Bacchanal, while the Wicked Spoon's Asian food was terrible. Bacchanal has some small selection of okay dim sum and made-to-order noodles (udon, ramen, pho, and even laksa, which I haven't seen at a buffet before). The Wicked Spoon had better prime rib and other cutting station meats, and had ribeye steak, which Bacchanal does not have. Both have lots of tiny cute desserts, but Bacchanal has daan tat (Chinese egg tarts). They had a puff pastry shell instead of the usual crust which is like a cross between puff pastry and harder, shortbread-like pie crust.

The best things Bacchanal had to offer were

2.) Suckling pig with crispy skin - really fatty and delicious and not sweet at all.

and oddly enough the best thing there was

1.) Mashed potatoes with gravy - seriously, I know that is a weird thing to single out because you can get this anywhere but they must put crack in the gravy because I was sucking it off my fingers and debating licking it off my plate when no one was looking.

Finally, like I said about the Wicked Spoon, to me it's worth going just once to experience it. But like all the high-end buffets, it costs more money than it's worth, and is also not worth the 2+ hour wait. We only managed to get away with just a 5-minute wait to get in because it was on an off day (mid-week) in the off season (winter, between Thanksgiving and Christmas) at an off time of day, between 2-3pm.

Now we only have one more buffet to cross off our Vegas buffet list, the Sterling champagne brunch, and then I never have to eat at another buffet for as long as I live.

Outstanding! And I am not a fan of buffets, because I do not believe that anything good in quality can be produced using mess production! Bacchanal is different. Went there out of curiosity . I find Caesars dining options, with exception of Hyakumi, excellent, so decided to check out Bacchanal! 
Most of the dishes I tried can be easily compared to high end restaurants food on  quality & taste. Duck, lamb chops, roasted chicken.. The list can go on and on. Seafood unfortunately was no different the anywhere else. Frozen, tasteless and very poor quality.     
My biggest complain would be the layout of place. It is impossible to walk without bumping into somebody.. Bad idea when you carry hot plates.
Over all great place. I just wish it would stay this way. Unfortunately seeing what happen to Wynn, Bellagio, Cosmopolitan,etc. I give them 2-3 months until cost cuts will take place.

This was worth the price because of the variety and quality.  We weren't really sure what to expect, but this buffet had pretty much everything you would look for.  The desserts are especially good for a buffet and there's a full gelato bar.

Wanted to say thank you to Julie. She was our server and was amazing. She not only made us feel welcomed, but she also gave us insight to who some of the famous celebrities that have she has come across. Julie has been with Caesar's since 1973 and still going strong. Again, Julie thank you for making my trip a memorable one!!! You are the best. 

Regards,

Nando Garcia

I mean it's GOOD, but it's not life changing or anything.   The wait is obnoxious, someone taking your picture as you walk in is also obnoxious, the lines to get to the food are obnoxious, and the way the whole buffet is spread out is obnoxious.  

That said, the pork belly, crab legs, dim sum, and prime rib were all excellent.

I was really looking forward to coming here.  I am not a fan of buffets, but with the reviews this place had received I was really looking forward to eating.

My complaint is not about the food.  The food was good.  It was decent, not over the top because obviously it is z buffet.

My complaint lies in the manner my guests and me were seated.  We were given a table to the very back of the establishment.  When we asked if we could be up closer we were told that was not possible.  When we asked why we were told that it was due to casino rules. 

After paying a rather large sum for dinner it was really not acceptable to not be able to allow us to change to a nicer table, especially when there were many available.  This was not a case of discrimination but rather a case of over elitism.

I will not return and neither will my dinner guests.

I'm sure you've heard it before and it's true, this is the BEST buffet in Vegas hands down! We come here EVERY time we're in Vegas or even just driving though.

Yes its pricey but you get what you pay for
Yes the wait is sometimes long (I've actually never had to wait because our party is always over 8 and thats an automatic gratuity so they walk us right in) however, quality is worth the wait
Yes the service is top notch; one of my visits was on a Sunday for brunch which includes unlimited mimosas or champagne. Our server was so on point that she got me drunk and thats hard to do cuz i drink ALOT!!! 
Yes I will be back over and over again! 
No I don't have anything bad to say about Bacchanal :)

My friends and I went to the Bacchanal Buffet for lunch on a Sunday and we paid at 2:52 and 2:53 according to our receipts. After you pay you enter a second line and wait to be seated. We waited for 20-30 minutes (at least) for a table. This brings our time to 3:13-3:23. 

We were enjoying ourselves eating our meal. I did not think the food was the best I ever had but it was good. The food was not bad at all. I was happy but the price at $44.31 was a little steep compared to other buffets in Vegas. At 5:00 (assumption, I never looked) our server (nice lady helping us) says she is done with her shift and Miguel will be helping us. Miguel comes and it becomes very difficult to track Miguel down for refilling our water and our tea. Once we flag him down he states he is busy and will come back. I go and get dessert (some fruit) and come back. Another girl at my table is eating some macaroon cookies and the other two girls are not eating but drinking their tea. Two of us are eating dessert when Miguel (our new server) comes back at 5:24 and points to our receipt and states "Excuse me, excuse me. Can you read this? What does this say? You have been here for 4 hours."  We read what he is pointing to and look at each other. The receipt states "Please limit your dining experience to two hours." We proclaim, "We have been here for 4 hours!? Seriously??". We are in dismay and start thinking when we entered the buffet. We realize our receipt has the time we purchased the meal and look at our receipt and it says 2:53 (my friends receipt). We realize it took a good 20-30 minutes to be seated (if not longer). 3:13/3:23-5:24  was how long we were enjoying our dining experience. I am shocked and a little upset. 

When you pay nearly 50 dollars for a meal you expect a good meal. That includes decent customer service. Never have I ever been asked to leave a buffet before. I was not sure if I was more upset about being asked to leave in such a rude way or asking us to leave in general. I look around and see empty tables around us so I am surprised after 2 hours to the DOT, (plus/minus 5-10 minutes), we are asked to leave. I can understand why they have the comment on the receipt. They don't need people spending 4+ hours in there or people not eating taking up space when people are waiting in line and waiting for a table. However, there were open tables and we were only there for 2 hours finishing our dessert and about to leave. I cannot imagine them (the staff) asking any patron to leave for staying two hours while they are still eating. That is another thing that made me upset. I feel if an elderly couple were enjoying their tea and cookies (clearly dessert) nothing would have been said to them. If a family had been enjoying dessert nothing would have been said to them. Four young adults? Another story. These are just my opinions and stray from the facts, I am not sure what they were thinking but clearly they had facts wrong. We had not been dining for 4 hours!

My friend is very upset and asks to speak to the manager immediately. Miguel brings Jamie Radke. My friend starts yelling at Jamie about how rude that was. Clearly it could have been stated in a nicer way if we HAD been eating for 4 hours. She then states that we had not even been dining for 4 hours and being asked to leave was beyond rude and unprofessional. Jamie agrees and agrees and apologies. We are expecting something for our dinner being ruined in return. I think most of us would expect *something*. We expect our NEXT meal to have been free in order to have us come back again. Jamie says she cannot do anything but give us a few drinks. Jamie states Miguel was wrong and out of line. She offers to allow us to stay as long as we want and move us to a different section. She is unsure as to why he asked us to leave. Miguel had been on shift 24 minutes. Someone above him asked him to tell us to leave. Someone screwed up and I blame the assistant manager on duty (Jamie). I highly doubt Miguel knew how long we had been there because he recently started his shift... My friend asks for Jamie's card and a form to file a formal complaint. We are still waiting on the Hotel's response over the incident but I am upset about what happened. There are a ton of buffets in Vegas and I will not be eating at this place again. There are too many incompetent people in positions that should be fired. There are plenty of hard working people out there that could do a better job. Oddly enough, I searched Jamie Radke in the yelp reviews and found 2 more complaints against her.. I do not like when someone/anyone screws up and it gets put on the lowest person in the company (Miguel) to take the blow. It bothers me a lot and people should take responsibility for the people working beneath them. That is their job. Jamie should have taken full responsibility for the incident and not blamed Miguel.

Went for brunch in a Sunday. $49 a person, and this also includes bottomless bloody Mary's/mimosas/champagne. Went around 1130am and it was already pretty busy. paid the extra $25 to cut the line. When you do this you become a diamond person and they sit you in a different area which I thought was nicer and more well lit. This also helped us avoid a 70 minute wait for a party of 3. All the food was amazing, especially the crab legs. The only down side was the wait since of course that's what everyone goes for. The Italian food section after awhile also started doing steamed crab which helped with the line. I'm a huge seafood fan so that's mostly what I stuck to, but the rest of my party thoroughly enjoyed the omelet and crepe section, as well as the sushi and all of us enjoyed the deserts, especially the gelato!! so make sure you definitely save room for some at the end of the meal! The only bad things about here is how busy it is, and the wait for certain foods.

I was not impressed with food.The dim sum was good,and the dessert were ok.The meat selections weren't seasoned properly, I was disappointed with this place. I don't think this was worth the $90 we spent.

Better than Wicked Spoon in Cosmopolitan. The food choices and quality is exceptional.  My group and I got in right before lunch and was able to pay the breakfast price.  

We especially enjoyed the thick honey roasted bacon (next to the prime rib station). They also have a lot of seafood options: oyster bar, shrimp cocktail, crab legs. The oysters were not in season and was pretty puny, but beggars can't be choosers. Our other favorites were the super creamy mac&cheese, the mini-red velvet pancakes, and the mango pudding dessert. Definitely one of my best buffet experiences. 

BTW - There is a 2 hours limit for how long you can stay (found out the hard way and was asked to leave after 2.5 hours!). There is also a $10/person unlimited mimosa that we did not see on any menu, but was informed after we ordered the watered down sangria.

没有做好功课，千辛万苦找到才发现CES期间的晚餐要近60刀，都想打退堂鼓了。

其实拉斯维加斯的自助餐都并没有十分3惊艳的。这家算是拉斯里面最热门之一，6点多的时候进场不用排队，等吃完七点多已经大长队了。但是里面拿东西都要排小队。确实比其它的自助餐要稍好一点点，但是并不值。

不过知道对面同事午餐在星巴克吃了一个包喝了一杯咖啡也花了30多刀，也就平衡了。

Gross. I just visited Bacchanal for the second time and I really think it has gone downhill. We had brunch on Presidents Day weekend so OF COURSE it was more expensive. The service was TERRIBLE. I ate almost an entire plate of food before we were offered drinks. No servers ever came anywhere near our table for like 15 minutes. Also, while we found a few winners, there were several items I tried and couldn't finish because they were so gross. The eggs Benedict is a prime example. It was cold, the English muffin was mushy, and the hollandaise sauce was disgusting. On the other hand, the lobster Benedict was delicious. Go figure... I think was probably our last time trying this buffet.

Going to Buffets is always a highlight of my Vegas trips.  This is why I was excited to try out the Bacchanal last Saturday, 3/25/17.  Even though we paid $63.06 per person due to a large party of 10, to celebrate my sis-In-law's bday, we all figured that it will be worth it.  After all, Bacchanal was listed as the #1 Buffet in Vegas.  

The seating was ok.  We didn't have to wait long.  Considering it was a Saturday and the price is more expensive than regular weekday, I hurriedly went to the sushi bar since I've been craving for sushi.  To my dismay, there were only 4 varieties of sushi and no sashimi in the Japanese selection.   

Next to the sushi are 2 selections each of pork buns and dumplings.  Along with 3 selections of different kinds of Asian soups.

I went to the carving station and they only had brisket for beef, ribs, chicken & hot links.  You would think, for the price we paid, they would have prime rib.


One of my favorite buffet must-haves are the oysters.  And to my surprise, they did not have any.  They had one of those white shells that look like clams.  So my family just went with the crab legs, as those were the only ones that were good enough.  We were told that we had to pay extra for the lobsters, but we were there until 4:30p,, but no lobsters in sight.  We were also told that lobsters are market price??? I've never heard of a buffet where you pay market price for lobsters!

The rest of the food is nothing much more than what you will get at maybe, Harrah's buffet for $26.  There were no teppanyaki, Mongolian or anything where you can have them cook special noodles for you.  Everything was like a regular all you can eat Chinese restaurant.

The dessert was pretty good, but not a huge selection.  Unlike the other fancy buffets in Vegas, there were no macarons or cakes or fro yo.

The worst thing of all was, my brother paid $15 for all you can drink beer & wine.  They only took his order once, never came back for any refill or anything.  So pretty much a waste of money.  We never got refills for any of our regular drinks, either.  

Our go-to buffet in Vegas is the M Buffet.  I think for their price, they make it worth the line and money.  Their quality never is their priority.  I am extremely disappointed with the Bacchanal because to pay $600 for 1 meal for all of us, the selection was only worth half the price.  For a Saturday to have a menu of nothing different than a weekday menu, but costs more is unacceptable.

I sincerely wish I researched before paying as the experience was not worth the price.  I hope The Bacchanal work on their quality or lower the price. I know everything in Vegas is expensive, but this one was like playing the slot machine and losing all your money.

Came here for the lunch buffet as we wrapped up a conference.  The food variety was amazing, and I tried a little of everything.  Only thing that was a bit disappointing was the crab.  Way too much work for little return.  We had a table of 8 and everyone walked away stuffed.  A couple of things not to miss...the meat station, pho station, and the desserts.  The brisket was especially good, along with the spicy sausage.  

Usually, you can get in for lunch with no issues.

This is the best buffet I went to. It is pricey but definitely worth the cost. If you go here make sure you have plenty of time to eat, I was here for about 2 hours and wish I was there longer. They have a diverse amount of food divided mainly into ethnics, they have a separate meat and seafood section which has many options for people. Their dessert section is gigantic and i tried everything there I wanted. I went here about 4pm and I still had to wait for a bit which I didn't mind at all. Whenever I think about buffets or large amounts of food my mind always comes back to this place and I think about the next time I'll be able to visit. This place is delicious and I'm sure if you go here once especially at dinner time you'll be hooked.

This is supposed to be the #1 buffet in Las Vegas, NEGATIVE! This place is not worth $60 per person.  The food wasn't good and either undercooked it over cooked, YUCK!  I wasn't impressed at all, and the line to get in at 9:30pm was stupid long.  Never again, there are other places to eat that will meet your expectations and not spend $60!  Save your money & time!

Everyone raves about this place and had to try it but this place is all hype.

Food is like your ordinary buffet, salty and no flavor....nothing to be wowed at and for the price I could have gotten a surf and turf for cheaper and 10X better quality.  Since it's considered "Holiday Brunch" we paid $59 a person.

Crab legs suck cause it was boiled in salt so expect it to be super salty.......which is not good but from a business stand point I guess that is a way to detour you from eating too much.  

Stone crabs were the only part that was good but make sure you ask them to heat them up for you, it taste better warm compared to cold.  And if you can track down your waiter, ask for the cracker in advance.

Yes this is an all you can eat but if the food don't taste good what are you gonna eat?  I must say tho, the image and atmosphere is beautiful so at least the view is nice but our waiter was no where to be found when in need.

This is the first time for me and it will also be the last.  Had a better meal experience at Joe's last night.

I can't say I'm an expert at Las Vegas buffets, but Bacchanal Buffet definitely lived up to expectations. After a week long hiking trip in Utah, my group and I decided to end the trip in Las Vegas. From eating PB&J sandwiches and jerky all week, Bacchanal Buffet sounded like heaven on earth. Their food selection is huge and definitely overwhelming. Multiple rooms have American, Italian, Chinese, Spanish, seafood, dessert, and more! I spent a good 10 minutes walking around figuring out what to tackle first. Definitely hit up the seafood and dessert. 

By the time we made it over to the hotel, it was the end of breakfast. We ended up paying the less expensive breakfast price, but got to eat the more expensive lunch items. Definitely a plus! The restaurant was surprisingly empty. We were seated as soon as we arrived. Servers were friendly and attentive.

Go, seriously.  And go hungry! So many options and everything I tried was amazing.  Look for the bacon, it's life changing.  Pricey, yes but as something that is once in a while, superb. $152 for 2 on a Saturday night.

I came here Halloween night for my birthday dinner. There was a wait as expected, but not bad at all! It was also pricey, but you get what you pay for and there are sooo many options. I feel like some people really dislike this place because they think it's overhyped, but it's definitely better than the buffets I've been to. Not being "as good" as the high expectations set for it doesn't mean it isn't good (if you don't walk in ready to critique every little thing). Come hungry, drunk, and ready to feast. :P
Brought our friends while they visit us. We always brought friends here while they visit us. This price for this buffet is increasing but quality is getting worse and worse. It's not worth at all.

I've been to the Bachanal before and enjoyed the experience however this time was not like the last. We arrived around 1pm and sat at about 2:30pm. The wait time quote was right but I feel the older I get the less patient I am so I found it too long to wait. The brunch price was about $55.  When I've been here before, I was wowed by several items there and the quality and level of exotic choices was high. This time I was impressed with only a few items. My favorite items were the boiled crab legs, hand carved brisket, and they had a jasmine rice pudding shot that was to die amazing. Honorable mention goes to the shucked oysters, and peeled shrimp. Food was good just now "wow" enough to justify the price and wait. Seems like the quality has come down since its opening. Service on refills was slow as well. You can go to other buffets a tier lower in price with about the same quality and variety and not wait as long. Seems like the quality has come down since its opening.

we finally got to come back here again to eat.  it's been over 3 years and it's changed a little bit as far as the quality. no longer 5 stars but 4 stars. it's still a very good buffet with the nice variety and all.  however i felt the quality overall was not as high as when we were here 3 years ago. i understand that when we went it was a very new buffet. i just hope they don't continue to decline their quality like they did at the Studio B buffet at the M Resort.

Creative food presentation but the food itself is bland. For lunch, it is a little bit overrated. There is no freshly squeezed juice. Nor good seafood. 
Environment and service are nice.
Dessert bar is very cool.

I was not impressed, probably because I had high expectations. 
We were very lucky to not have to wait in line.
For 2 people for a dinner buffet cost about $110 
The staff was very courteous and welcoming. 
They offered to take photos of you upon entering the buffet and then later sell you the photo for $25.
They had seated us near the entrance and it was a bit uncomfortable when you had to navigate around the patrons waiting to be seated back to your table.
The food presentation was great. 
I was not impressed with the food selection. 
They had big cocktail shrimp and it was good.
The snow crab was bland.
To finish our meal, my husband and I decided to have some coffee and the server offered cappuccino $5 extra to which I believed should of been included, let me tell you Starbucks is better!

Seafood Section 3.5/5
Salad Section 3/5
Dessert Section 4/5
BBQ Section 3.5/5
Asian Section 3/5
American Section 2/5
Mexican Section 2/5
Service 4/5
Seating 1/5

Too confusing buffet, crab was all mixed together didn't like that I wanted just king crab but only got little bit of it. I had much better buffets and cheaper too. It didn't feel like 700+ items like they said. Rio was better than this. Bellagio is the best in LV that I have tried. I will NOT be back to this buffet.

If you are ever visiting the Las Vegas Strip and you only have time for 1 buffet, then this is one to go for.  You should definitely go here at least once in your life; it's totally unforgettable and well worth the money that you are spending.  By the way, you can save on the cost if you get the total rewards card.  Not to mention, for all the crab that you can eat, it's well worth the money!  Ages 3 and under are free.  There's also Asian cuisine here, which is actually pretty good.  There's a lot of good meat here.

As buffets go this is top dog in my book. I have been here about a half dozen times now and even though this experience was a little less than previous ones it is still the best around, period. We went on a Sunday evening right at dinner time and had no wait and were seated immediately. I immediately noticed a little difference in food presentation from previous trips. Though they kept the seafood well stocked, they only put out what was needed at the time and there was a few times we had to wait for replenishing of the seafood stocks. I also noticed that a smoked salmon was the only fish dish available. I know that the menu is changed up often but to not see any other type of fish anywhere took me back a bit. I must say I spent most my time with the Chinese side of the line with so many choices that I love from soup dumplings to Peking duck and all the assorted soups. For the first time I visited the dessert bar and was overwhelmed with choices. Overall I would say on a Sunday night they did not bring out their A game, service was very good at tables but buffet line service was slow at times and choices were not as abundant as before. Despite my issues this is still the world's greatest buffet and I will always go back for more, Aloha

This is literally the best buffet I've ever had.  Omg everything from.the crab legs, shrimp , prime rib and ribs. They were amazing. I'm so full typing this but that's ok. I'm gonna barf but it was well worth it.

I've wanted to Bacchanal for YEARS since my hubs went without me. I've held it against him for years and I was totally right to do so. Bacchanal is amazing. Definitely the best buffet I've been to in a while. 

They have kiosks like disneyland that gives you a time frame of when you can come back and get in line to buy tickets. They've also have alcohol that is also unlimited for an extra fee. Why waste room in your stomach though when there's ALL that food?! I'll just go over quick highlights.

I had a ton of king crab legs but so many were still frozen and after a few I gave up. They also had a ton of frozen stone crab claws (they've must've been because they're not in season right now) but it tasted pretty good. Melted butter constantly being stirred and lemon was a great accompaniment. 

Their lamb is unbelievable, the best I've ever had. PERFECTLY cooked, moist, tender and seasoned. The sliders were also unbelievably good. I've paid $18 for a tiny mini 3 slider dish at a "happening" restaurant at Santa Monica 3rd St Promenade but this was incomparably better. Prime rib was also above average but that's expected at a place like this. 

For desserts, definitely get the house-made gelato. I had cosmo's wicked spoon back to back to this place and this place's stracciatella and chocolate is phenomenal and much better. Their chocolate tastes much more authentic (if that makes any sense) than any other place. Would DEF come back.
Umm I think it's over priced .... Crab legs were ok... Nothing exiting or special just like any other place ... Guess if u eat a lot it's worth it... I was full on my 1st serving...

There is a need to strategize in order to avoid waiting 2-3 hours but this is the buffet of all buffets. I only wish that I can fit more food into my belly. Presentation of the food is impressive here. It is a wonderful experience for your eyes and your stomach. It's not a cheap buffet but after dining here, you can see why. 

The king crab legs are sliced in half so there's no need for tools to crack open the legs. I also enjoyed the ravioli, xiao long baos, meatballs, cheese and charcuterie, New York style pizza pies, sausages, prime rib...the list goes on. There is also a little section for street tacos. They had a lot of different types of soup -- ramen, udon, etc. It saddened me to not be able to eat it all but I knew I wanted to save some stomach space when I spotted the beautiful glass displays of desserts. 

Overall -- beautiful, delicious food. Try to come when it opens to avoid a lengthy wait. Wear comfortable shoes in case of a wait. Try to share plates of food with friends so you can sample more of what Bacchanal offers. Enjoy!

Well...kinda disappointing. There was nothing spectacular that stood out food wise...great selection and variety of dishes most were Luke warm - cold. The seafood seemed previously frozen and when you cracked open the shells the meat fell apart like Parmesan cheese. The prime rib didn't have much flavor...but nothing that was like "ooh yum" we paid for the "endless drinks" and then after 2 the staff took away our glasses and when I asked for more, he snarled you only get 2 with your meal..unless you pay $15 which I replied that we had paid the $15, it took him 15 minutes to come back with another drink and at one point I had to get up to get his attention... now mind you we are also still eating and not looking to drink down the house and get sloshed , but hey $30 between 2 people I would like to get my moneys worth...anyway the guy never came back to our table and the food was just meh...I'd rather pay for an uber and get a Korean bbq alll u can eat for $20 (which we did the next day)

Giving two stars for the food only. The food was good and hot and they had a nice variety. I hate the fact you have tip up front, you never know what kind of service you are going to get. My husband has a tendency to overtip and our waiter was horrible. I got the endless mimosas for an extra $22 on an already over $100 bill. In the two hours we were there, I got one refill for a total of two mimosas. When we were ready to leave, we had to flag down a bus boy to take our bill and credit card. When he brought back the receipt, they had the nerve to ask for another tip. We put a large zero on that line. With the endless mimosas they advertise that you get a souvenir glass. I had to flag down the bus boy yet again to ask for the souvenir glass. He told me the glass was the one I had been drinking from, which still had some mimosa left in it. Just what I want to do, carry around a dirty sticky glass (we were not staying at that hotel). I asked him if he would wash it out for me and he said they normally don't, but he would anyway. I wish the tip we left up front had gone to him and not our waiter as we had more interaction and service from the bus boy. The food was good, but don't expect good service, it wasn't even that busy, we had to wait about 10 minutes in line. I would hate to see the service on a busy night. We won't be returning.

So I came here based on all of the fantastic Yelp reviews, but both me and my husband were extremely disappointed. After waiting about 40 minutes to be seated (it was half empty inside!) we had a full appetite and were ready to eat! My husband ate the crabs legs, which are a mix of snow and king crab and he liked them. I tried the bone marrow which was downright disgusting and the American wagyu was extremely fatty and had zero flavor. The beef tri tip tasted pretty good but was very overdone. The best thing on the menu was the sushi and the crepes for dessert. 

Our waitress was fine but never refilled our drinks, despite us asking several times for more water. 

Overall, I would definitely not recommend this place at $55 a person plus tax and tip.

We came here for brunch on a Saturday.  We had a large party, about 12 total, so we had to sit in 2 different tables.  That was fine with us considering they were side by side.  This place is huge! You definitely have to do at least 1 walk through prior to you getting your food just to plan your attack.  
The seafood portion is what I spent my most time on.  I liked the crab legs that were in the hot water the most. Even though they were sliced open for us, they didn't give you enough meat per slice.  I would have preferred they just cracked it open but not slice it completely in half.  That was you get the full meat per leg section.  I also tried the bloody mary oyster shots.  I wouldn't recommend this at all.  Once you get past the bloody mary taste, it gets worse from there.  The crawfish had no flavor and the mussels were dry.
The sushi portion of this buffet is something you should skip.  It wasn't impressive at all and the flavors make you question the freshness of the fish.  
The Asian portion was also not impressive.  The dishes I tried were all bland and dry.  
For the amount of hype this buffet receives I expected better.

I gave this buffet a 4-Star due to the"B" Grade it got from the Southern Nevada Health District. I wish I could have seen the rating before I went to eat. The price was way too much for this buffet, $40-$45 would have been good. The food was very good and they had a lot of variety for brunch. Everything tastes really good, I didn't get sick or the other 4 in my party. Like I said, the "B" grade rating disappointed me. For a great buffet like this, it should always be an "A." Nothing less! The atmosphere and the service was top-notch. Everyone was nice and courteous. It wasn't a long wait as I was expecting. Overall it did the job!

I can't say that the food is worth the 2 hour wait or the hefty price tag of $50 on a Saturday night, but I will say that this buffet should be a definite try for a foodie out looking for the Vegas buffet experience.

Outside of the dessert selection, I can say that this particular buffet is nothing out of the ordinary. If you're looking for a deal, you're better off paying for a 24 hour pass (http://www.harrahs.com/casinos/planet-hollywood/casino-entertainment/buffet-of-buffets-24-hour-pass-new-detail.html) which does include the Bacchanal Buffet (available as an upgrade). 

The actual area was large (25,000+ sq ft dining room) with plenty of seating, and the variety was equally as large (300 items +115 pastries for dinner). I absolutely adore the cute bottles of horchata and tamarindo, and I was thoroughly impressed by the offerings of pho and ramen. If you're a seafood fan (which I am not), you will fall in love with the seafood section; I saw plenty of tables lined up with crab legs which is a disappearing rarity. Tacos, pasta, cheese, bread, cold cuts, carvery, pizzas, fried everything...and the best part for anyone with a sweet tooth could be found in the heart of the dining room -- feast your eyes on the dessert stand-alone island! It included its own crepe station, macaron plates (orange, pistachio, coffee, etc), cake pops (pls skip this unless you're into a mouthful of frosting), cakes/cheesecakes, gelato (thai tea, anyone?) and mochi station, crème brûlée, flan, etc etc.

It is built from its walls to its ceilings with sophistication and class in comparison to say Wicked Spoon and The Buffet (Wynn), but with the title of being the #1 buffet in Vegas, it disappointed since I enjoyed the quality of the food at The Buffet at Bellagio so much more (and I hear Studio B blows  Bacchanal out of the water). Bacchanal was good, but it wasn't overwhelmingly amazing to deserve its popularity.

Still, it is highly worth mentioning that our server did a fantastic job in refilling our drinks and clearing our table! And to get a feel of how much I appreciated his friendliness and promptness, I left him a 40% tip.

I usually take my out-of-town guests here once and that's it.  It is a rather large buffet and can be overwhelming with its 500+ items ready everyday.  I enjoy it when I go there simply because its a different food experience every time.  Yes, some complain that its $52.99 pp  but how many times do you come to Vegas or even attempt to even try to conquer this epic buffet.

Bountiful. Scrumptious. Overwhelming. Bacchanal lives up to their name: Bacchus! Just when you think you've seen all of the selections, just turn the corner in the dining room and...BAM! more food!! Today was the Memorial Day brunch that served up more seafood and more everything else on the buffet. Stand outs for me included: Pork in salsa verde w/ cilantro rice, Kahlua pork eggs benedict, the ceviche bar feat. 3 kinds of ceviche, seafood pearl pasta, and the seafood lo mein. I tried to only eat things that I couldn't regularly get at home but that proved difficult when I saw the shar chu roasted BBQ pork. The buffet was a tad in the high price range ($62/pp) but given the quality, the mimosa, and the wonderful and friendly service (Thanks to Jung, our warm and gracious server!), it really was worth every penny. Definitely plan to make this a regular visit every time I visit Vegas!

wicked spoon may have come up with the individual serving idea, but bacchanal executes far better - each dish tastes like it was prepared to order.  the tacos were great and the ramen tasted better than most ramen shops in SF.  great shrimps, carving area with huge selection - like brisket and ribs.  one let down was they ran out of sushi...well, make some more. the ticket line system is cool too. you hold your place in line through a machine and you get a text when you are in front of the line.  so you can gamble while you wait instead of standing in line.  mimosa was also cold which makes it delicious.

This is hand down the BEST buffet I've ever went to. We went here for the first time a couple years back, LOVED IT, and just revisit them last week!
The food is still excellent! The cheese, the meat, the asian food, the seafood, everything was excellent!!!! 
Highly recommend the champagne brunch!

This is the ultimate Vegas buffet experience. There was a giant wait, but we paid $15 each to scoot to the front of the line--totally worth it. I've been for both brunch (bonus: unlimited champagne) and for dinner. Both times, we found amazing, world class food.

Heard this was a must try buffet in Vegas especially if you enjoy Crab. We went for dinner on the weekday which was priced at $54.99 Mon - Thur. $5.00 more Fri - Sun. If you only have a few people in your party then use their kiosk to check your party in. You'll receive a printed ticket showing your expected wait time and their system will text you when they're ready. Once you get the notification then it's about another 20 minutes before you eat. Well worth the wait especially if you enjoy crab and all the different types of meats. They have everything from prime rib to rosemary marinated tri-tip. Must try their dry rubbed smoked spare ribs which was awesomely moist and flavorful. Try them all!

This is one of the best buffets I've ever had in Vegas. I've been to this one two times already and it just gets better and better. 

They have such a wide variety of foods and all of it taste so good. I also love their wide variety of desserts that they have.

It's about $50 a person but I honestly think it is worth it. It had the biggest variety I've seen and on the weekends they have a unlimited mimosa brunch which is good. 

Definitely a buffet I would come to whenever I'm in Vegas.

This is probably the best buffet place I've been to here in Las Vegas. It's cheaper here when you're entering in for Brunch during the weekdays but on weekends it's 10 dollars more. I usually am a person who typically dislikes buffets, but this place made me be more open to it and changed my mind. 

We had a group of 9 and it really helps if you have large groups, we didn't make any reservations or did we wait for very long, it only took us 5 minutes. When you have a smaller group you will def be waiting in line for at least 20 to 40 minutes so come before the rush. They offer bottomless mimosa's but the time limit is only 2 hours. Is it worth it? Well, if you're getting a fat tuesday after then save yo monies! If not, cheers my friends. This will be the only other time you will eat like a king/queen as you write in your autobiography "Death by Mimosas". 

The variety of Food they have is amazing and on top of that best quality of buffet food I've ever had. Enjoy yourselves with a large selection of different cuts of beef, and pig. They have Charcuterie here which is just another word for fancy slices of meat and cheeses. Steamed crab legs, jumbo shrimp, lobster eggs benedict, great italian selections, surprisingly good chinese food, and top quality desserts and ice cream. Stay away from the sushi. Everyone knows you don't eat sushi at a buffet....

This place is way better than wicked spoon, sorry not sorry. They'll add a 18% gratuity fee automatically to your bill so make sure you choose whether you want bottomless mimosa's, or a Fat tuesday. Hard choices man.

Best buffet in town!!! I have tried many buffet in town. This one is a must to go!!! Great presentation, a lot of variety. Because I like sea food, so I prefect dinner here. Crab leg, oyster, shrimp cocktail, lobster soup...etc. Scallops potato and Kobe burger are must to try. Desert station is a food paradise! After my first visit, I never want to go to any other buffet in town.

Ok well... I absolutely love this place and this will be my to-go place every time I go to Vegas because it was worth every penny for me. It costed me $55 on a weeknight and was a little heartbroken until I saw the place and food. 

The buffet area is very big. It made me so happy that when I turned every corner there were more foods available. The decor of the place was beautiful. It costed them $100 million to create 'the bucchanel' and I think that they did an amazing job. There were big round tables and booths available. 

I ate the crap out of the cold crab legs. That with butter was OMG. The shrimp was very juicy and FAT. I have never seen a shrimp so fat before. my friend made his own carnita truffle fries because the buffet had all the ingredients available (guac, truffle fries, carnitas, salsa, cheese). 

I ate 8 legs of lamb. So good!! The prime rib and brisket was a bit too salty for my liking but I loved the lamb. 

The desserts were beautifully displayed. Too bad I'm not a sweets kind of person but everything looked so pretty I just had to try everything (and I did...no kidding..) yummy creme Brule, chocolate covered strawberries, cake pop, pudding tart (my favorite because it wasn't too sweet), cookies, and macarons. Loved the lemon and strawberry sorbet.  

I suggest coming early dinner or 2 hrs before closing to avoid lines. I didn't have to wait because we came late but there were plenty of foods available.

Overrated. 

I swear pictures are so deceiving. I went on Friday for lunch/dinner. Paid the extra $15 to skip the line. Wish I would have skipped the buffet instead. I'm not sure what the big deal is. The presentations are nice, but the food is blah. As with every other buffet in Vegas, food was cold and subpar.  A girl at the table next to me keep saying this is the best food I ever had! These are the best tacos ever!  Boy people need to get out. This place made me lose faith in the reviews on  Yelp. Everything I got was just average. Most of the stuff I saw on the pictures weren't on the menu that day. Buffet is extremely small. The pictures make it look like there is a huge selection. There really isn't anything that sets this buffet apart from the rest. I will stick with the Wynn or Bellagio.

First let me preface this by saying that I do NOT enjoy buffets.  While they're generally quite affordable, I definitely appreciate quality of food over quantity.

However, I was more than pleasantly surprised by the presentation AND the taste of the different cuisines.  But I'll get to that - first let me get to the details:

- expect a wait.  I MEAN A LONG WAIT.  We were probably in line for about 30 minutes, and this was NOT during the dinner rush.
- it's about $50/ per person so it's not affordable, but definitely worth the cost
- the interior and sitting does NOT feel like a buffet.  This felt extremely high end and sophisticated, which was a nice change from other buffets
- there are about 5-6 different cuisines.  As much as I wanted to try all, I could only stuff myself with about 3.  Crazy!

The food was amazing, but not out of this world, after all - it is still just a buffet.  I would definitely go again just for the experience, because there's so much variety and nothing is mediocre.  I also absolutely fell in love with their hot and sour soup!!!

A great Vegas experience if you're looking to get lots of food in Vegas style.  But if you're looking for amazing food, I would deter from any buffet. :)

This critically acclaimed buffet seems like a great choice for a high end buffet. They told my family and I that they wait time would be around 1 hour. It took a little over an hour to get in line is what they meant was 1 hour to get in line. So we waited about 20 minutes to be put in another line for a part of four. If you come with a big party apparently they'll let you in before everyone else since most people have smaller parties.  Once you finish the 2nd you pay upfront. There were 4 of us and we payed over $220 for the meal which will seem bad by the time this review is over. Anyway after you pay they put you in another line. The line your put in depends on the amount of people in your party. So we wait in that line for 25 minutes and when we get in we get our food because we were very hungry. Everything was just mediocre and they were understaffed. I had an empty glass of soda for half the meal. The employees had to work very hard nonstop due to not being many of them. The food was not fresh at all and felt as if they were instant. They taste was very bland and they chiefs were not equipped with high quality food to distribute. For the ceviche they would bring plastic tubs out of a fridge and scoop it with a bowl into a display and looked filthy. The dessert area on the other hand was magnificent with all the flavorful desserts and nice ice cream. That itself earned it two stars or else it's not even worth one. Another thing i forgot to mention is that many corners in service were cut and an example for that is the moist towels were dry. I would not recommend to ever come here. It is not a good experience and is a mess. Thank you for reading my review.
Very delicious food be back here the service is the best waiters are really good definitely will be back here with all my friends thank you buffet

***Over Rated!****
3 hour wait with high expectations., but were disappointed.  We have tried many vegas buffets and were expecting Bacchanal to hold its own like Wynn's buffet, but was more like MGM's, or maybe Rio's buffet.  $56.99 per person.  crab was big, but same size as elsewhere.  The carving station looked awesome, lamb chops were good, but the prime rib was tough. Noodle bar was okay...  We basically had a $32.99 buffet dinner for $56.99.  We will not be returning here.

This is based on the Mother's Day dinner menu. Supposedly they should be serving more seafood for this special day. They did add stone crab. However, no lobster were served!

I've been here before and sadly I have to say the quality of the meat went down. My favorite were the lamp chops (from last visit) but this time it was not seared properly :( and burgers were cold. Desserts were the best part.

My favorites:
Stone crab
Mexican corn
Duck
All of the desserts

As you can tell it's not worth it...$65.99 per person. Sorry Bacchanal, we won't be coming back anytime soon.
Not worth the price. The price covers the quantity not the quality. Coming from South Bay, the buffet here is no different from a common Asian buffet that you get for $25 there. Will not come back.

For $90, not including the $40 extra charge to expedite our wait in line was questionable. Customer service lacked immensly. For the cost, one would assume faster service, however, our server hardly came to our table. The food was just average, but for the price I was expecting something greater. I feel used and abused :0).

Went for my birthday, I had always wanted to go. Both me and my girlfriend and 1 alcohol order. For the price and all the hype, it was very underwhelming. I tried a bunch of things and was never wowed by any of them. I ended up having 2-4 salmon plates. The alcohol selection was also very limited, like 2 wines limited. The dessert bar was pretty good. They let you create your own crepes which was pretty cool. Other than that, I could've used that 100 plus elsewhere and enjoyed some really good food. The price wasn't a big deal, but I do expect good food if I'm going to pay for it like that. Likely won't be back.

Probably one of the best places in Vegas to go and enjoy yourself a higher quality buffet.  I have a Total Rewards Card, so I was able to totally bypass the line, to the chagrin of some of the non-card holding folks lol.  But still, great selection of foods, and the the atypical design of "different rooms" for different regions of foods really just make it feel like you're finding more treasure as you go further down the hole. 

Come here early, as the lines get long quick.  I heard someone say that lines were almost 2 hours long...as I walked passed him in the Total Rewards Card line.

Seriously..get the TRC, you'll save yourself the trouble, and hey you might start earning comps that way.

Love love love this buffet! I love the variety and the staff. Everyone was eager to please. Dessert options are awesome. Great seafood/carving station. A bit on the pricey side but well worth it in my book. I have eaten at a few different buffets in Vegas and this is by far the best.
I've been to a many Buffet's but this one is huge! The food is great and the service is amazing. You also can add unlimited drink service of memosas!

One word...... AWESOME! I rarely do buffets since I am very strict with  counting my nutrients and caloric intake, but since it was Father's Day I decided to splurge! Can I just say it was the BEST decision I could have made?!! After seeing this buffet on the news, I was eager for a special occasion to have an excuse to try it.
