When we arrived we had a small wait which is to be expected. After being seated, both a server and the same manager on the news program greeted us immediately! Both seemed really passionate about the food and you could tell they had pride in the establishment as they answered my questions about some of the popular items. 
We enjoyed delicious fresh churros, pineapple empanadas, an abundance of fresh traditional breakfast favorites. 
My son loved the chicken and waffles and Dungeonas Crab!
The best part of this buffet was the emphasis on freshness!
Beautiful and clean room and very helpful staff. 
My only suggestion would be to add more relevant vegetarian and vegan items to that section of the buffet to keep competitive and current with the times. 
However we had an amazing day and brunch!!
We will be back!!

I have been here twice, once during brunch and then during a week night dinner. I think what really sets this buffet from the rest is the variety that they offer. They have man of the same items as others but offer items not available at other buffets. 

Brunch: I was so happy with dinner that I forgot what brunch has to offer but remember it was quite delicious. They had your usual fares that folks have for breakfast but they had spam musubi, waffles, pancakes, bacon. They also had a variety of fresh juices like watermelon and cucumber basil. 

Dinner: Wow! raw oysters, snow crab, shrimp cocktail, frog legs, soft shell crab. They had Mexican cuisine, Japanese, and Chinese cuisine. They also has Singaporean Laksa, Vietnamese  Pho, as well as other options. 

They were all very delicious. I think the price is worth it for the variety. I was super happy and so full. I didn't want to leave but I couldn't eat anymore. 

I heard the lines are normally long but we got lucky as we went early enough and did not get lost in the lines.

Everything looks good. They have food from different countries like China, Japan and Mexico. I was not expecting more options so I'm fine with the choice. And their Chinese food, even without much to choice from the stir fries section, (They have good dim sum!) really taste better than other Chinese restaurants I had before. They are American Chinese edition. 

But, I am from South part of China. The food here to me are too salty. My cousin and I were both upset about the amount of slag they put in the dish. Seems like salt is too cheap to consider among all the condiments. Hope the cool did not drop his Salt bag in the pot. Sigh.....

So after most of the dishes we tried, there is only a "if it is not..." left.

We do expect more from the price.

I'm still trying to figure out the Vegas buffet scene, so take this review with that appropriate grain of salt.

I came here last month on a trip to Vegas from LA, and my group of friends and I (some of us who were first timers at Bacchanal, others who had been here at least once) stopped here for dinner on Saturday evening.  Even starting at 5:30-6, there was quite the line.  We waited a good 1+ hr, which I've been told is actually average/not very long for a Vegas buffet.  They kind of trick you because even after you pay at the counter on your way in, you still have to wait in a separate line to be seated.

For $52 or so, you get everything under the sun.  I was impressed with not only the variety here but the little things they did to spruce up otherwise ordinary dishes.  For example, there was lobster corn chowder - not like big sized pieces of lobster, but I could still taste it.  The oysters were great and the line was manageable.  Prime rib, of course, was a must as well.  The lamb, in my opinion, was a bit dry, but the angus beef sliders were delicious and also came with a nice serving of sweet potato fries - how can you go wrong?  

There's simply too much food to name, but I'll try and run through anything notable.  Some people had said there was fresh juice, and while I didn't see that, they did have a few agua frescas to choose from.  The carnitas from the Mexican section were excellent - moist, delicious, and the best part:  you grab as much as you want.  There was also a braised veal dish around the corner from the Mexican section that was absolutely to-die-for.  The meat melted in my mouth.

I wasn't really a fan of the sushi section, and the dim sum seemed oversteamed and like it was sitting out too long, but I suppose these aren't reasons why most people go to buffets.  I was hoping the sushi section would have more raw fish in nigiri form, but the best it offered was a raw salmon-tuna salad, which was good, but not exactly what I was expecting.  I will say there is Chinese duck if that tickles your fancy as well as a black Chinese herbal soup, which was soothing. The ceviche was standard but nothing to write home about.  

Dessert was amazing, too.  They have a bunch of different cupcakes - I got a peanut butter one because pb and I are besties, but I thought the cupcake batter was a bit dry.  Otherwise, you have an extremely impressive selection of pies, mousses, etc.  Too bad I didn't save more room for dessert - the savory food was just too good.  I think the best part of my meal, though, was the mochi ice cream I ended my meal with.  It was just too good.  I got black sesame flavor and I prayed that I had a separate stomach just so I could have more. What a perfect way to end a meal.

In terms of beverages, make sure you know you can order teas and juices - I got grapefruit juice to help with my digestion during this multimillion caloric meal.  No one said anything about it being freshly juiced, but I was already impressed by the fact that they had it to begin with.

Service:  Great!  Everyone was super friendly, despite probably being extremely tired from being overworked on a Saturday evening at such a well-oiled operation.  I feel bad that these workers are putting up with probably an extreme amount of pressure, and they all handled themselves very well, with smiles and grins abound.  No complaints.

Bottom line:  I've only been to a few Vegas buffets, but this definitely tops the bunch.  Next on my list, however, is to compare my experience here with the Wynn, where I still haven't been.
This buffet is worth the price. The food is exceptional as well the service! Lily our waitress was amazing, as well as Samy who helped clear our plates. We will definitely be coming back!

Definitely one of the better buffets in Las Vegas. Came here around 7:30pm and the line was insane. We ended up paying $15 more for the express line and still ended up waiting 15-20 minutes. The selection was definitely impressive. The fresh seafood was awesome, definitely recommend the oysters, crab and crawfish. There was also great lamb chops and tomahawk steak; ask for medium rare. My favorite part of the buffet was the desert section. They had a large selection of different pastries, but I recommend ordering the chocolate or pistachio soufflé and getting a crepe with fresh berries and nutella.

Bacchanal was the greatest brunch buffet I've ever had despite one caveat. For $15 per person you can add unlimited mimosas however after about 6-7 glasses I can attest to the fact that the alcohol content is slim to none. There's also a two hour limit on the brunch buffet but I know we sat there for about 3 hours. The array of foods available is vast & varies from breakfast to savory items. Everything from seafood to elk sliders is available & it'll honestly take you about 10 trips to sample every single item. There wasn't a single item of food that wasn't delicious. They have carving stations for proteins, a custom pancake station as well as a humongous dessert station that's completely separate from the entrees. The line can be quite extensive so be prepared but all the rave reviews are true. There were so many highlights& honestly it'd take another full review to list them all but I'll post pictures to do it justice.

2nd time here but I think I won't be back unless I have to...the wait time is scary.. We had been waiting for 3 hours to get in even though we did get the number ticket.. We got the ticket at 5:50 pm and they texted me to come back around 7:10 pm and I thought the wait time is not bad but right after I came back I had been waiting for 1 & 1/2 hours to pay and another 30 minutes to be seated.. In the end I started eating my dinner at 9 pm.. After 3 hours wait I duet feel hungry anymore so I paid $65 (including tips) per person without eating a lot!! Not worth it!!!

I was super excited to try Bacchanal after hearing from multiple friends that it is the best buffet in Vegas! But after checking it out for myself, I was actually a little underwhelmed. Maybe it's because I went for breakfast and not lunch or dinner? 

The restaurant itself is very modern, chic, and sophisticated looking. Lots of glass and soothing taupe colors abound throughout. The dessert bar is magnificent. For breakfast, there's a make your own crêpe area that is fantastic. 

The coffee is worth noting as it is truly delicious. I love that you get your own carafe. Some food standouts:

1. Cold seafood salad (fruits de la mer)
2. Shrimp cocktail
3. Steak and eggs 
4. Aforementioned make your own crêpes
5. Amazing assortment of salads

Overall, I enjoyed my visit and would love to try it again for lunch or dinner. Pricier than other buffets in Vegas.

Bacchanal Buffet will forever be in my heart. I had never tried a Vegas buffet before and this place blew my mind. My friends that had been to other buffets said this was the best they ever had so I'll take their word on the quality. Words cannot begin to describe how much I enjoyed this place. Plus, my friends and I went around 11, 11:30 AM to avoid the rush and I felt like a genius after. Great foods, great variety, great time. Worth every single dollar (something that can't always be said in Vegas).

This is my absolute favorite buffet in Las Vegas at the moment. Tons of meat, seafood, Italian and Asian choices.

If you're Diamond or 7 Star member at Caesar's there are special perks at the buffet including shorter wait, complimentary drinks and king crab legs on request.

An underrated dish that I would recommend to everyone is the mushroom soup, which is actually truffle soup, making an ultimate dip for crab, steak or whatever your heart desires. 

The food offered is worth the price!

Wow! What a total let down!

So much for "best buffet in vegas"!

The price of this buffet is pretty expensive! $40-60 depending on what meal you go for.

So I would expect something good for that huge of a price tag.

However the only "good" thing about it is the size. It's pretty big; i will give them that.

The food itself is very mediocre in quality. What is the point of having "500 dishes" when most of them are taste awful.

Some of the "hot" dishes were served totally cold!

Just walking by a lot of the food didn't look appealing. 

Me and my friend left hungry and disappointed. I've never left a buffet hungry before. Total waste of money! 

Please use the same money and dine any restaurant in vegas; you will thank me later! 

If you must have an all-you-can eat meal than go to fogo de chao and get quality food and leave happy!

The variety is okay, the meats where dry and warm, there is no salad bar they put a cesar salad in a tiny bowl and there are two types of greenery being called salad. Not much else for a salad. Husband had beef ribs which were tough, he did liike the crab legs, but for what you pay the should be the larger crag legs.  Also the dessert portions are miniature dollhouse portions,which is ridiculous. If you want chicken, porkchops, hotdogs, turkey, sweet potatoes fries, you are out of luck.

I was really disappointed because I'd heard good things and read previous reviews.  

For 59.99 a person it is NOT WORTH IT!!! I've had much better for less.

Long due review where I had last time I came in April! 
This place has become my new favorite buffet at least for me as I wasn't a fan of Wicked spoon. The best part of it was that we literally walked up and got a spot right away so that was the BEST part of it all. I don't think it will ever happen again at Vegas being able to not have to wait and get a spot!

It was around 32 per person last time I came here as we came around 2. I have heard that the price has gone up? but I'm not for sure on that yet. Regardless I had an awesome experience here where they had A HUGE VARIETY of food and desserts. We didn't have to get drinks as we had fat tuesdays coming in.

They have from chinese to american to mexican food so you can't go wrong if you are only into one group of food. I personally loved the mexican type of food they had here where there was a station where I could get forever tacos and they actually make the meat fresh for you and it was VERY GOOD. If i wasn't defeated, I would have got 3-4 more tacos... :p 

They have a bunch of ice creams/sorbets, crepes, cakes, and even mochi. Just go all out people because I had a great time enjoying all the types of food they had here. 

I say...from my last time experience that this is my favorite buffet now.

Mind you the wait time could be loooong! So bring someone who is diamond or 7 star member with you if you can. So u can skip the line. All the sea food was very fresh and tasty. I love their cooked oyster! Desserts are very yummy, love their flan!! So many choices. Service was okay, our server didn't bother to check on us much but the table next to us.
Probably one of the best buffets I've been to. Come ready to EAT! They had soo many choices and the food was delicious. I can't wait to go back again.

It is not common that I get excited to eat at a buffet, but this one definitely lived up to the hype surrounding it. They have several different styles of food to accommodated everyone taste buds. I started with a plate of meat and potatoes ( Prime Rib, Brisket, and Sausage with Hash-brown and some form of fried potato cakes all were delicious. The next plate was all about seafood ( King crab, snow crab, mussels, crab cake Benedict which were all delicious. For the third plate I decided to go look at the salad bar, it looked amazing, but I wasn't in the mood for lettuce. So, I went in on some Crepes and other sweets. 


This place is a win, but make sure you bring your wallet.

Well where should I begin? Great service but a  long assss wait  2hrs. But over all the food was good. The thing i suggest before you start piling up your plate take a walk from the front seafood area to the way back Chinese food area.  My wife and I did not see the other stations until later. We still think the wicked spoon at the cosmopolitan was a little better but that's our opinion over all we had a great time

Total waste of time.  Checked in at the kiosk and told to return 2 hours laters.  No problem plenty to do in Vegas!  Returned at told time and told to wait in line and it would be another 2 hours of waiting in line.  With my bad back no way I was standing in line for 2 hours after checking in 2 hours prior!  Plenty of better restaurants to eat at then gorging your face at this buffet!

Best buffet by far. Priced a little on the high side, but well worth it.
- Presentation on point
- Flavor well rounded
- Many options
- Fresh food

Everyone said it was the best buffet, so we had to try it. We arrived late on. thurs night, around 9pm. The we're going to close at 10:30pm, so 1.5 hrs was enough time for us. 

Will post pics separately. The seafood was average: crab legs, crab claws, sushi. Crab legs are split for you, do you don't have to work on cracking; was a little dry and saltier than expected. Maybe because we dined late. The meat and Asian sections were nice, and the dessert section had high quality options. They had these unique sushi hand rolls served in a cardboard wrapping to prevent drying. The raw fish was fresh, but the nori seaweed wrapping was tough, not dry, a thicker nori; not the right nori for a hand roll. I had to just eat the inside component. The spicy sushi was SPICY; no need for wasabi. For the desserts, try the green tea cake, the melt in your mouth macaroons, the gelato, and the mango dessert. Service was great and attentive. 

Unless you drink, where some alcoholic drinks would be included in the price,  $55 a person is a steep price  compared to other buffets. Keep in mind that we go to a buffet this pricey to try their seafood and main dishes, and we do not eat too much meat. And we don't eat that much anyway (1 plate from each station; no seconds), so I would rather spend $110 for 2 at a chef's 4-5 star restaurant. You would pay more on a weekend buffet to access their extra seafood, which I think is confusing. 

If you not tried this buffet & want the experience, go for brunch, or try their famous Sunday Bunch. It would not be my top #1 recommendation, but maybe #3. Read my other review about the Wicked Spoon to compare

I'm local and I remember going to the original Bacchanal at Cesars over 20 years ago and it was an "experience in culinary", was very disappointed this time when I went, this "buffet" did not show me anything different from any other buffet in town as a matter of fact the selection was less and less than satisfactory, the sea food area was very skimpy, the staff was more attentive to the guest that paid the outrageously expensive full price than the guest that used their group on and it was very noticeable. I rather pay $40 + at the M where the beer/wine/champagne are included in the price and the variety of dishes is way more than the few the Bacchanal offers, as stated before was very disappointed and will not recommend this buffet to anyone.

This place really deserves 3.5 stars. They didn't have any lobsters to my dismay. This was really disappointing since they had lobsters on display in the front and since it cost $55/person to eat there. They did have crab legs though so I guess that made up for it. Unfortunately the rest of the seafood disappointed also and that's why this buffet is getting 3-stars. The sushi was okay...nothing to write home about. The oysters were meh. The filet mignon had sat out so long that the green sauce stuck to the plate like gooey glue. Then there was that moment when my husband had to run to the restroom right after dinner so that was a bit unsettling. Maybe it's because we went on a Sunday night? I don't know. Luckily, I did not have the same experience since we had a flight to catch.

The dessert bar was pretty excellent though. Try the creme brulee, the gelato, and the macaroons, or have a crepe made to your liking. The dessert bar deserves 4 stars at the least.

Bacchanal is a good example of how a place can be really good and still overrated.  I felt like there was a lot of hype for this place, and all the anticipation gave me ridiculously high expectations, it's heavily oversold and I bought in.  Ultimately, I am giving it 4 stars because I really did liked the food and they have tremendous variety, but the service wasn't very good.

Like all the great buffets, they have many different stations, but the crown jewel is the carving station.  They have A LOT of meats: prime rib, ham, different kinds of sausage, brisket, lamb chops, ribs... and I'm sure I'm forgetting some, I didn't try all of them, but I tried a lot of them and they range from very good to great, the lamb chops being my favorite.  Other standouts were the dumplings, cheese station, crab legs, cake pops, and little jars of agua fresca.  The dessert station is surprisingly hit or miss.

I recommend trying to get your money's worth because it certainly ain't cheap, especially if you pay the extra $20 to stand in the 30min VIP line to bypass the peons in the 2hr line.  Our waitress was friendly, but hard to get a hold of, so much so that after waiting quite a while to get a refill, I told her to please bring me 2 drinks when she finally came around.

Bacchanal is a great buffet, easily in my top 5 buffets, but Wicked Spoon and the Aria Buffet both rank higher in that list.

Expected more for the hype and price. Food quality was not the best. The flavors were bold, but not in a good way: salty items too salty, sweet items too sweet, etc. Similar to buffets out there for half the price. 

Glad I experienced it but wouldn't go again. Service was good.

This was a bit of a let down for me. I have been looking forward to trying this place and it just did not live up to my expectations. We came here on a Saturday and followed suggestions from other yelpers to arrive at 2pm in order to experience the dinner spread as well. We were seated at 1:50 pm and the server brought our drinks right away. I went hunting for the bone marrow and crabs right away. The bone marrow was the biggest disappointment. Not sure if they have been sitting out for a while and maybe I just had a bad batch but they were hard and the meat on top was also very dry! SMH. Crabs were also very salty even to my liking and I like salty food. They don't serve oysters until 3pm so I saved some space for that. They were fresh and good. The dessert area was also a let down, similar to what you will find in a regular chinese buffet except for the crepes station. What a disappointment especially for a $60 buffet. Service was really good though adding 1 star to the 2 star overall quality of food!

For $60pp, this buffet sorta fell short for me.  First, price doesn't include alcoholic drinks.  You'll have to pay +$15 for AYCD.  Buffet comes with unlimited fountain drinks tho.

The best thing at the buffet is the sheer novelty of the variety of food:  various shellfish, Mexican, sushi, dim sum, prime rib, noodle bar, gelato, various desserts, and the list goes on and on.  HOWEVER, if I try to remember the best thing I ate, I blank out.  Once is enough of an experience for me.     

As for desserts, just stick to the fruits, flan, or creme brulee.  Everything else is waaay too sweet for me.

Hands down, best buffet in Vegas. Haven't tried it? What are you waiting for!?

FOOD: Selection is overwhelming in a good way. Love how they separate the "hot" crab legs in a different section which helps with the lines. A few highlights, the Asian soups are surprisingly good, for example the Pho. We all know how long it takes to make the broth and Bacchanal is on point. The best prime rib still goes to the Wynn and Bellagio though, Bacchanal lacks marbles. Also, dessert bar is amazing. Mochi ice cream ftw. 

AMBIANCE: Nice decor, not over the top but effort was made. Casual dress with a casual atmosphere. 

SERVICE: I love their new ticket system. Prior to it, you had to wait in a fat gigantic line ranging from 1-3 hours. Now, it's like the Disneyland fastpass system. Walk up to the machine, grab a number, and come back when it's your turn. From that point, it's another 20 or so minutes (depending on time of course). 

PARKING: Never stayed at this hotel, but all Vegas hotels have free parking. 

Overall: If you had one buffet to go to in Vegas (or anywhere for that matter), make it Bacchanal.

This is not your typical buffet! I have never liked buffets and have so many horror stories and stereotypes about them, but this one is the opposite of most. There are so many different foods to try that you almost have to take only one bite of each. Almost everything I tried was awesome! This place is expensive but in my opinion, it is well worth it!

Had Brunch here today. I went around 10:00 am. If you pace yourself, they bring out different items after 11:00 am. Unfortunately I didn't. I can only tell you about the food I experienced. First I had the lobster eggs Benedict which I thought was very delicious. I tried the sushi,  however I am a sushi snob and wasn't thrilled with it. Best of all was the King Crab. It's served cold but they will neat it for you. I thought the only had snow crab, but looks can be deceiving as the mix both kinds together. But it's easy to spot the King Crab. 

Deserts were plentiful and there were many that I liked, including the round cheesecake and the carrot cake. I had the flan but it was a little dense. Would highly recommend experiencing this buffet at least once. Line moved very fast at 10:00 am.  Practically non-existent!

you get what you pay for.  might be one of the most pricey buffets on the strip, but definitely worth it.  wait wasn't as bad, but we did go kinda early for dinner.  the variety and quality were excellent and the staff was very pleasant.  Steam King crabs were the highlight for our party.  if you haven't tried out Bacchanal because you thought it was too expensive, I suggest you give it another thought.  For a nice dinner at nice restaurant your gonna spend about the same or more, but at least here you can keep getting more and more!

Not impressed with the food. We went there on a Saturday night and the place was so busy. We paid $54 per person. We thought there will king crab legs but guess what?  No king crab legs, only snow crab. It seems like the quality of the food has gone down compared to other Yelpers who posted pictures and reviews.  The lamb chops and the prime rib were tough and the sushi quality was the same as the supermarket. The oysters smelled fishy and the stone crab legs were hard to eat.  Some of the Asian hot dishes were good (roasted duck). Where were the individual fried chicken baskets? And the Mexican corn on the cob? This place was just like any other buffet now but more expensive. Yes, there were plenty of food but will not recommend anyone to go there unless you like spending money for lots of bad food.

I purchased the Bacchanal Buffet Groupon - $88 for two brunch buffets, two express line passes and two mimosas or beer. There has always been a huge hype so we thought we would give it a shot. I was pretty disappointed with the overall flavor and offerings. Bellagio buffet had a much better selection and flavor. The only thing that stood out to me was the fresh squeezed juice selection. They had orange, watermelon, lemonade, carrot, and something green. I used the orange juice to dilute my mimosa, but quickly learned that the champagne was just really bad. Take your money to Bellagio and you won't be let down!

For an expensive vegas buffet, this is about as good as it gets. Being the holiday menu, we came with the buffet of buffets pass for about 100 including the add-on for this buffet (35$). We came right before brunch ended but ended up having to wait so were treated to the dinner choices. This place is probably known for the extensive choice including my favourites which were the fresh cold seafood (crab and shrimp), a delectable taco bar where they make it right in front of your eyes providing unlimited guac! Also, their chinese section is surprisingly good with tender BBQ pork and some dang good dumplings! They also have many many dessert choices all of which are only average (none standing out) but they do have a crepe bar as well. One of my favourite dishes was their cooked salmon which was perfectly rare in the middle and melt in your mouth tender! The mussels were also very good and although they lack a DIY salad bar, they have some good premade salads.

Overall, if you're looking to indulge in Vegas, this is a place to go but be prepare to WAIT A LONG TIME and to spend some big money.

Pretty good! Came in at 11am on a Monday and beat the huge line that formed behind us :) Lunch was pretty pricy at $35/pp, so get your money's worth! 

No need to order orange juice from your server if you want the fresh stuff--grab the jars from the buffet for freshly-squeezed OJ.

Brisket was probably the best protein I had there. Fingerling potatoes were also pretty good. Avoid the hashbrowns/potato pancakes/tater tots if you're trying to watch your salt intake--these things were almost inedible but they looked so darn good. Mac & cheese was also good, but I prefer the jalapeno mac & cheese at Wicked Spoon.

Spicy tuna sushi was alright.. what you'd expect from a buffet. Gyoza was really crispy and pretty good. Pizza was good for a buffet, penne pasta was also pretty good. Avoid those twisty garlic knot looking things--they were whatevs.

Chocolate croissant was bomb, and so was the cornbread muffin. Tiramisu was alright, and chocolate decadence pop was also tasty (imagine the rich filling of a chocolate cake, covered in a coat of chocolate). 

Best dessert of the day goes to the crepe bar and bountiful tubs of gelato available for your choosing. Favorite flavors: pistachio, sticky toffee, blood orange. The chili lime mango was interesting, but not my cup of tea. As for the crepes, you get to top it with whatever nutella, chocolate, caramel, or strawberry syrup your heart desires, then add berries, caramelized almonds, and whipped cream (or was it marscapone?). Totally ended my meal on a very satisfying note.

Read about the long line, so we got here around 3pm to eat an early dinner on a Friday night. Was surprised to see there wasn't a line. The food was good with many varieties to choose from. Will I come back? Most likely not. It's one of those places you just have to try it for yourself at least once. Don't think it's worth 2 hour wait.
Came here for breakfast on 9/9/17. The best buffet I have had! The only thing they didn't have was lobster. Worth the $50.
This place was worth the wait, delicious food. $60 for dinner buffet on the weekends and an additional $15 for unlimited mimosas and select beer.

Best buffet I've ever had! Really pricey but the seafood is so fresh and the quality of everything was top notch. 

There were very very few things I had that I didn't like. The highlights were the duck, fried rice, spicy tuna sashimi, and gelato. My husbands only complaint was he wished they had lobster (we went on a Thursday so maybe they have it on the weekends). 

I feel it is well worth the money and line :)

My husband and I never never miss a chance to go to Baccanal when we are visiting Vegas. Although it is one of the most expensive buffets on the strip ($60pp/dinner, $40pp/brunch) it is worth every single penny. 

Beware: parking is $10 (less than 4hrs). No validation.

This is my favorite place to eat in Vegas. Brunch or dinner...you will NOT be disappointed!!

I'll never truly understand why such a vast amount of variety is ever necessary. After sampling approx 15 items then hitting the dessert station,  I can say it is after my 3rd visit to this buffet, a solid 3.5. The first time I was here it was a solid 5 star.  Nothing ever stays as good as it was , when the idea was new and the staff had smiles

Went to Bacchanal for the first time this year as I heard that it was the best in Vegas. 

There's a wide variety of food, but I found the food there underwhelming.  The food there is decent.  However a lot of the dishes were salty. 

For instance there was some sort of lobster chowder that had little to no lobster in it and was so salty and overwhelming that I couldn't finish it. 

There is a 2 hour time limit, and it seems like they enforce it as 20 minutes before my table was up, I overheard some staff members trying to figure out which tables were almost at their 2 hour mark. 

Overall,  the food is decent but for the price, I'm not sure I'd go back.

This place is amazeballz! We came on a Wednesday morning. There was pretty much no wait and we got the breakfast pricing and they switched to lunch so we got both breakfast and lunch options. 

My fiance is a seafood lover so he went to town on the mussels, fish, and sushi. He was in heaven. I loved their carving station, tacos are sooooo good, and their pastas were delicious. Also they had elote! Seriously everything was excellent. This place has quality dishes not just quantity. 

My recommendation is to pace yourself and stay for a while. Get your moneys worth and try a bunch of different dishes.
I believe bachannel buffet is one of the best buffets in Vegas! Excellent food and great drinks.
This is...by far...the most magical.. fresh..expensive.. tasty breakfast (only came for endless mimosas) buffet ever!!!!!

OH MY GOSH. Bacchanal is so delicious.

If you're going to go on a Vegas buffet binge, don't start here or else you'll just be disappointed by all the others. The buffet is massive. MASSIVE. And pretty much everything I ate was delicious. 

I wasn't a fan of the truffle scalloped potatoes since the truffle oil was a little overwhelming. The korean short ribs were delicious. You can make your own crepes. The vanilla fleur de sel gelato was yummy. 

I could keep going on and on and on about everything I ate, but the rule that we followed for Bacchanal was, "Eat until you can't eat any longer. Then take a breath, and do it again."

We didn't eat again for the rest of the night. #winning

What a lineup of food to choose from. Have fun tasting most of it. One thing you need to do after is have a long walk like shopping to finish it down. So much selection that there is not enough room for my tummy to handle.

My boyfriend scored a free room in Vegas so we were finally able to do our Vegas foodie trip. Of course, we had to go to Bacchanal! To avoid crazy long lines we tried to come early and ended up arriving around 4:45pm on a Friday. We checked into the machine which gave us a quoted wait time of 53 minutes, but we waited around 25 minutes before we were texted to return.

I thought that the selection was pretty good. The chilled seafood is right at the front. I had a lot of chilled crab legs and thought they were very good. They weren't too salty. We also had some oysters, but they were kind of fishy. I think that it was really cool that they had fresh tacos! The salsa bar also has guac, sour cream, and different kinds of cheese for your tacos. They also had elote, which was very good. They had a good selection of asian food, even dim sum! I tried the sticky rice, which I really liked. We both liked the eggrolls. They also had a small sushi selection. I tried the salmon nigiri, but I thought that was just okay. Surprisingly I really liked the sesame balls, I'm usually not too crazy about those. We both also liked the truffle mushroom pizza. It has a strong truffle flavor. The pastas were decent. They also had different types of ceviche, but I didn't try those. 

Overall, we really liked this buffet! It is pricy, but we would come back on the trips where we wanna splurge on food.

Food is okay. Everything in this buffet seems better than it actually is because of the decor and ambiance. Service was pretty fast. There is so much food that you can't eat everything. All the desert was sugar free and on the healthy side, which is good I guess, but doesn't taste as good. This buffet was expensive.

This is the best brunch buffet I ever had so far. It was pricey ($56 or so per person), but it was totally worth it. Where do i begin. I was impressed with the selection and the freshness of juices & drinks. All desserts were amazing, especially flan cake. 
I arrived earlier than usually meal time so I wouldn't have to wait in line (came 10 am for brunch).

Finally had the chance to try out this buffet.

WAIT TIME
Bacchanal Buffet had a ticketing system, so you don't have to spend hours waiting in line. Use the machine ticketing system to "reserve" your party size and it will show you an estimated time of when you should return and get back in line to pay. If you add your cell phone number, they'll text you when you need to check back in with the host to pay.

However, you still have to plan ahead if you are planning to dine at Bacchanal Buffet, especially on weekends or holidays. I tried visiting on Thanksgiving Day and arrived in line at 4pm at the ticketing machine. The estimated wait times was 6-7 hours !!! Clearly, I wasn't planning to starve myself until10-11pm that night, so I decided to come back another day.

I returned on Sunday and the line was much more reasonable. The wait time was approximately 1 hour, and we were seated within 40 minutes. 


THE FOOD
There are so many different types of food here -- Seafood Station (Crab legs, Shrimps, Ceviches, Oyster Shooters, Salmon Mousse, Crawfish, Mussels), Meat Station (Lamb, Prime Rib, BBQ Ribs), Japanese sushi, Soup (Tonkotsu Ramen, Udon, Pho, Miso Soup, Chinese Sweet and Sour soup), Chinese Food (stir fry, dim sum, you name it), Salad Station, Pizza station,  Cheese station, Mexican, Dessert, and many more! 

Their Asian section was just OK- the ramen soup was bland, and the sushi didn't taste as fresh. The fruit juices at the Mexican station tasted a bit artificial.

My favorites were the crab legs and oysters. You could ask the chef at the counter to heat up the crab legs for you! The oysters were big and delicious and I had to go back for multiple rounds of oysters. Desserts were also amazing!


SERVICE
Overall, the service was great. Everyone was courteous and helpful. While we were waiting in line, the host offered to take picture of our party (which you can purchase later from them). I thought that was odd...I've never been to a buffet where they took pictures of you.


PRICING
It's slightly more expensive compared to other buffets in Las Vegas, but the quality of food is definitely worth it. Also, if you are a Total Rewards members, you could save a few bucks off your meal.

I'd probably return to Bacchanal again in the future, just not during the holidays or busy weekends!

A top notch classy buffet with so many selections it sends your head spinning.  This is one of my top two buffets in Vegas.  It is pricier than others, and the line to get in might be longer, but the food makes up for it.

I've been there twice for dinner.  Each time the table service of drinks was timely and the servers gave the impression they appreciated our patronage.  The only downside (having nothing to do with the buffet) is the horrible parking at Caesars.  Last time we were there it took nearly 45 minutes to find a parking spot and one has to be patient in self-parking.  The hotel has so much to offer that the existing parking structure is really too small.  I doubt that will change anytime soon.

The buffet features desserts galore.  I'm not a big dessert eater but my mouth was watering and I had to really test my resistance.
The Bacchanal is absolutely the best buffet on the strip - creative presentation of well executed dishes served tapa-size.  Its higher price equals its higher quality and is well worth it.

I have to say I think this is the best buffet in Vegas. It's in Caesers & is $55 a person. The variety is mind boggling! I loved the eggs bene! There is so much- carving station, waffles, pancakes, Asian pho, noodles, sushi, sandwiches, the dessert bar was divine. Just go hungry!

Let me start by saying I'm not a buffet guy. However, with all the buffets in Vegas I decided to try the best rated one. I went for dinner and those 4K+ reviews I read don't accurately describe what you're going to experience. $60 and not one item was prepared or presented well. Crab legs are thin snow crab legs. Only the top tier reward card carriers get king crab and they're small too! The carving station looked good but everything was tough. I suspect they chose select or a lesser cut of meat. The desert bar looked good but once again there was nothing good to speak of. Live and learn

What's all the buzz ?! We simply thought this place was okay.The wow factor for us was simply the variety of food offered and nothing we ate knocked our socks off ..... I will say the dim sum was pretty good ..as good as the spots we have here in the bay area but that was it.

Pros: lots of desserts. Gelato, macarons, cakes, jello, pies, etc. yum. Try their hot chocolates too.

Cons: long wait. They line you up depending on the size of your group which is cool but the ones in groups of 2 are put in tables that are way too cramped, that the table next to you can hear all your talks even if you talk in low voice. Can't even be romantic for those having dates. Another is we had to ask our server 3 times to refill our soda. Very poor service.

Food overall is alright. My husband and I went straight to the carving station. They just cut the steak for you. You can't request the doneness or however you like your steak. I prefer those ones that they cook it for you on the spot. Little disappointed with their Japanese option. 

FINAL NOTE: Sure, it has a lot of option and it's pretty over whelming but if you're after good food and flavor, this is not the place for you. If you just wanna pig out, this maybe the place for you. In all fairness, All food presentation is nice. Everything looks appetizing. So, $150 dinner for 2? Not worth it. Take your money somewhere else.

Probably the best buffet in Lasvegas right now. The only setback is the long lines to get in. The ambiance is inviting and warm. Alcohol is a bit on the expensive side but the great food and presentation more then makes up for it.

Bringing your appetite isn't enough, appetite isn't the problem --- it's your stomach size that is.

Love this place to the moon and back, they've got so many selections and all of them delicious in their own right.

I had the BBQ pastrami, spicy sausage and crab legs with butter for days.

What I thought was rather strange was that there was the main seafood bar that had the long line for the crab legs, but if you walked towards the boiling counter where they served pastas and what not, they were also serving crab legs there too. Since the line was shorter over there, I went over to the boiling counter and got my crab legs there.

Sometimes I'll have random day dreams of myself back in Vegas, dunking crab legs in butter and playing 25-cent roulette tables.

We decided to splurge a little and pig out at the Bacchanal Buffet on our last night in Vegas.  Eating at the Bacchanal involves a bit of a wait, so if you're planning on eating here you may want to plan ahead.  We showed up early - right around 4 on a Sunday afternoon, and after waiting through the digital queue, another line to pay at the cashier, and a third line to be seated, finally got to our table just after 5.  So that was around an hour, at one of the least busy times of day.

The food selection here is ridiculous.  There are seafood, american, mexican, italian, japanese, and chinese stations, not to mention the dessert section.  My one issue with the Bacchanal is that the raw seafoods weren't very good - I wasn't impressed at all with the sushi, and the raw oysters were pretty bad.  With that said, everything else was great.  There were mountains of crab legs, a taco station, and tons of prepared foods conveniently plated on individually-sized dishes.  I particularly liked the brisket at the carving station, the roast duck, and all of the cooked dishes involving fish.  Desserts didn't disappoint either - the ice cream and cape pops were cool, but my favorite was probably the pecan tarts.

Bacchanal is pretty pricey, and go there expecting to have a long wait, but the food is definitely worth it - the selection and quality of food is the best I've seen at a buffet.

You can have an international feast here! The prime rib and crab legs alone are worth paying $58 for dinner (on a Sunday). But wait, there's more! :D

Other delicious items...

- Lasagna
- Mussels 
- Caesar salad 
- Caprese salad
- Cooked carrots (I ate these with my steak)
- Strawberry gelato

If you are debating on eating here because of the price- don't. You get what you pay for and have two hours to eat as much food as you want.

Excellent buffet however a little pricy for the average person. It is worth every penny, I just wish more people could enjoy the amazing food. Also they don't give local discounts so we don't go here as much as other buffets.

This place is definitely as good as it gets. Yes, it's pricey but it's Vegas and it's a buffet. Cost is to be expected, right? But the nice surprise here is how legit this place is. It's not your everyday casino buffet. The quality and presentation of the food here is top notch. You feel like a kid in a candy store here so trust me, take your time and get a little bit of everything. Seriously, one or two shrimps at a time...you need the room on your plate to try everything else. Their prime rib was tender, crab legs were meaty, oysters were fresh, filler foods (mac n cheese, scalloped potatoes, sweet potato fries, etc.) were all deliciously sinful as they should be. Don't forget that there's a whole other side tucked to the back left corner. It was a whole new world when our table discovered it. Desserts were gourmet quality and the ice cream flavors were fun like french toast, thai tea and watermelon mint. Bonus points for having mochi ice cream at their dessert bar. 

Service was super pleasant and very fast. We had a great time at this place and would definitely go back the next time we're in Vegas. Enjoy!

We were excited to go to this buffet even though we don't normally go to buffet restaurants. We read all the great reviews and decided to go for dinner.  It was $60 US per person so we expected it to be decent quality food. Everything looked good but it was all cold . We had meatballs and they were ice cold in the middle the hamburger sliders were dry and cold.Im sure when this buffet restaurant first opened it was great but the standards are now starting to slip maybe new management is needed . I cannot recommend this restaurant , there are far to many better restaurants to spend your money at in Vegas with nicer staff

I don't know if this is a fair review or not because 95% of the time I go to a buffet I feel like, "Meh. I've experienced better." And by better, I just mean better food in general not necessarily a better buffet. 

We went for brunch while in Vegas. As far as buffets go, this one is pretty good for a number of reasons:

1. It is probably a mile long. It seriously goes on and on and on. We were sitting in one part of the dining room and didn't even realize there was an entire other room with different options until halfway through the meal.
2. It is very diverse. There is a station for pretty much any interest. They have the basics: salad bar, dessert station, carvery, etc. But they also have a number of international stations. The stations that immediately come to mind are Mexican, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, and Southern/Creole.
3. They have a pretty abundant seafood section with cold and hot seafood selections.
4. They have an entire charcuterie station full of cured meats and cheeses.

The reasons the buffet is not good is because every item on it was significantly poorer quality than I've had elsewhere. Just something not quite right about the eggs benedict and hollandaise sauce. The sauce on the pesto gnocchi was a little too oily and the gnocchi was over cooked. The shrimp and grits had ONE shrimp and the grits were very runny. The list of misses for me is extensive. 

The biggest issue I have with this buffet is that it cost a cool $120 for two people which could have worked out to be one amazing meal at a quality restaurant. $7 unlimited mimosas kept us alive during our brunch but ultimately we left defeated. 

Do yourself a favor and spend the money on a high-end brunch or lunch instead. You will not regret it.

Hands down, my favorite buffet here in Vegas. We came in at around 530pm, and for two ppl, the total wait time was about 30 mins. Also, this is one of the more expensive buffets out here, but in my opinion, definitely worth it. It's about $59/person for dinner..and if you want unlimited alcoholic beverages, that would be an extra $15. The seafood bar is the highlight of this buffet. With a huge supply of crab legs, crab claws, oysters, shrimps, clams. This was where we spent the majority of our time! My other favorite part of this buffet is the dessert bar! Many different treats from gelato, cheesecake pops and chocolate mousse to freshly made crepes and soufflés, you're bound to find a dessert that you'll like. They also have a sugar free section.

The wait is not worth it. The phone check in isn't worth it, no one checks what time you made the reservation. You may as well just show up at any time in line. Food is ok nothing special (I've been here before). Would recommend to avoid it possible. 

Edit to 1 star: after the 2 hour wait and not getting in several customers were upset and asked how long it would take. The manager on site told them "about 20 minutes" however it was clear it would take at least an hour. After requesting and receiving my refund, I felt obligated to let them know the manager was not being truthful and from their spot in line to my spot (about 10 feet) it would take 45 to an hour on top of another hour from my spot (after paying) to the front before being seated. 

I'm not sure how bachannal is ran, however, it is pretty clear the online "pre-reservation" to save a time for you to come in to eat is pretty useless, the horrendous management, and average quality food is not worth your time.

My family and I went on a Monday afternoon to this much talked about buffet. Make sure you get in by 3pm, because after then, you will be paying a dinner price (paid about $230 for the 4 of us). The food was good...nothing too extravagant. Some foods were very salty but some were very good. Our initial waiter brought us our drinks and then notified us that some other gentleman was taking over for him as it was time for him to go home. That waiter that took over for him took forever to come clear plates off our table and refill our drinks. I had to make several trips to get the juice over by the Mexican foods since our waiter lagged on bringing refills. The service overall was not good. The price is very expensive for what is offered, in my opinion. Most likely will not be going back to it.

Overpriced low quality food.  For months I heard my friends tell me to go to The Bacchanel. I went there tonight and to be honest it didn't meet my expectations.  The Asian and Italian sections were simplistic. The Chinese food lacked flavor and it seemed I was eating food from any other China Express or food court restaurant.  The Japanese sushi rolls were not fresh and you could see it was low quality fish/crab. The Italian pizzas and pastas were nothing special. As far as the meats, the sausage was ok, but the lamb was so bad I spit it out (I wasn't the only one).  I did not try the American section as I was already dissapointed. I would definately not recommend you to stop by. I think you can eat much better food for the $126 I spend for two.

Best buffet in Vegas. This place had everything, the cleanliness of the place, modern decor & service was great. The pricing is a bit high but worth it, I recommend to anyone looking to eat delicious WARM food (a lot of buffets have cold food and not that many dishes). This place was worth the trip and every penny. I'm craving it again hehe.

We visited this buffet on our recent vacation. There were 8 adults and everyone thoroughly enjoyed the service, food and ambiance.
Everything was done to perfection and the variety was the best we've ever scene. We will visit again.

Everything is pretty mediocre here but thats exactly what I expected out of the buffets even in Vegas. They used to have caviar and freshly shucked oysters on the spot but they don't even have those anymore and the quality of the food seemed to have gone down hill from the last time we visited. I ended up just enjoying plates and plates full of steamed crabs. The line was not too long so that was good and if you check in, you get to go to the VIP line which is much shorter. Make sure everyone checks in to get everyone in your party in the VIP line. I think their dessert was pretty good compared to other buffets I have been to in Vegas though. 

The service was actually a surprise was the server was very attentive and brought out new drinks even when we didn't even ask and took our plates away every time we finished a plate so it wouldn't stack up on our table.

We came on a Thursday night in October and waited about 30mins in line. I like the cold shrimp, crab legs, chicken ginseng soup, and chocolate lava cake. The bf like the corn, the tacos, brisket, miso soup, and gelato. It was $50 something for dinner, which is pricey for a buffet. However, it is worth trying once.

Great buffet! We upgraded our Buffet of Buffet pass to get breakfast for an additional $15. We got the tail end of breakfast around 10:30am on a Monday. There was a small line, nothing too long. The selection was great, unique. The chicken and waffles was most memorable of breakfast. After that, at exactly 11am the breakfast dishes started to disappear. It sharply switched to lunch except for the guy making omelettes and stacks of bacon on the front end of the buffet. We did stay to try lunch for the full 2 hour max. 

The carver David is great. The bussers are really on it! They make sure my dishes and even my straw sleeves were removed from the table. 

Our waiter barely came around though. Jeff was enthusiastic but the times we needed a refill he wouldn't be there, only when we basically had everything we needed. 

Also, if you're reading 1 star reviews... the one about the "rotten egg creme brulee" is totally bull. There's a sign that says Green Tea Creme brulee and Creme brulee. He obviously got the wrong one. 

I definitely would have loved to try dinner and eat some crab legs. I'm surprised a place like this doesn't have lobster. Or steak knives. I wouldn't pay $60+ for it though.

Went here with my school staff and I was pleasantly (!!!!!) surprised. I'm a local but I rarely go to Caesar's anymore. It has everything you can think of and then some. It took care of a long awaited lunch and dinner. I was stuffed for the rest of the night.  Asian section was probably my favorite (sushi, Chinese food, noodles etc...), lobster tails, crab legs,appetizers ( avocado toast ),  soups, salads, breads, the dessert section was crazy ... crepes and endless tarts, cakes and gourmet fixings... some that I never see in a buffet. Every time someone came back to the table we would rave about what they tried and it was a unanimous thumbs up! Pricier than most buffets but def worthy of the price. Great place to celebrate! They maintain the sections and there is always coming around to see if you're satisfied or need anything .
Kudos to the staff and managers running this place
Other than 500 suckers waiting in a 2 hour line ( I had front of the line passes) this place is top notch, not your typical Vegas buffet!!! Worth every penny$$$$$

I will certainly say this is one of the better buffets that Vegas has to offer so it certainly is worth the price tag that comes along with it, but they do discount with the total rewards so that's always a plus! I only marked it 4 stars for the simple fact that the quality of the food was inconsistent.

It did take quite a bit from paying to the time we sat which had me a bit disgruntled, but I'm certainly not going to ding any points for that. The layout itself is quite massive. There are literally stations everywhere and just when you think it's done there are.....You guessed it.....MORE STATIONS!

I tried to sample anything and everything that looked appealing, but still found myself hovering around the seafood station and slider areas. I was a fan of the shrimp as it was both soft and did have some great flavor to it. The hit seemed to be the kobe slider, but for me it hit a sore spot. The first one I had showed me why I waited forever as it was moist and tasted like I hit a jackpot in my mouth, but the second time around all I could taste was char and couldn't eat another bite. 

As I said it certainly pays off well beyond the price tag if done the right way. There is great selection and I'm certain something for everyone. The etiquette of the people in line could use an improvement, but that certainly is not the fault of the staff nor Caesar himself.

The best if not one of the best! Really worth the money. Everything is excellent. Their sliced turkey is sliced thick if you request it...the best food, wow! Take 3 stomachs for this place, it's awesome!

This is a must if you're in Vegas. Your experience here will change your perception of buffets forever. (Does not feel like a buffet.) 

Great variety to choose from. Every section catered a different culture and service was timely and friendly. Food is restocked almost immediately once low.
Excellent food and service!  My favorite was the seafood and dessert bar.  Will definitely be back again the next time I am in Vegas.

Not a big fan of this place....The decor was good, the service was quick and few of the items on the buffet were really great...but it is ridiculously expensive. I don't think anyone can do real justice to the money they paid, the buffet selection is so damn huge. May be  it was just me...other ppl seemed to enjoy it.

=The Facts= 
-December 7-9, 2012: "the off season", per our server.
-Friday AND Saturday night 8pm: ~10 people in line, seated in 5 minutes.
-Sunday just before noon: ~75 people in line, seated in under 30 minutes.

-8pm offered dinner items. 
At least 95% repeat items between Fri-Sat-Sun.
-12pm offered 20% breakfast items / 80% dinner. 
I say dinner instead of lunch, because they were the same items that we saw at 8pm on our previous visits.

95% of the food we tried was, for the lack of a better term, "restaurant quality", opposed to "cafeteria quality". The quality you would expect from your favorite local (insert ethnicity here) eatery that's been in business for 20 years, and not a chain, precooked and packaged after thought.

There's a battle being waged in Las Vegas, The Battle of the Buffets, and 
The Bacchanal is currently winning. I love this trend. As long as the quality of food and price stay in line with each another, and I think they have for the most part, I will continue to look forward to the next contender. 
Meanwhile, The Bacchanal Buffet is the place to eat.

PRO TIP!: If you have the constitution to pull off more than 2 visits in a 24hr span, you will likely benefit from the Buffet of Buffets 24hr Pass. Assuming you go 3 times, the savings equal 'buy two get one free'.

The food here might be ok but the entire experience was a nightmare. Getting in, we had to wait in 2 very very long lines. One to get a ticket to come back at a later time and then when coming back at the specified time on your ticket, you won't get in right away...you have to wait in another line for 2 hours!!!! The staff "managing" the line are very rude and herd people like they are sheep!!! 
If you want to be disrespected, and pay good money for mediocre food, then this place fits you perfectly!!!

Not as good as all the hype!   Not bad, don't get me wrong,  just not worth $50/person and the number one rating for all buffets in Las Vegas (AKA: buffet town).   Attention to detail and customer service is lacking at this price point.  The high end food options are limited and not that well executed.  I did really like the meat cutting station and the big personality chef working it.

I only ate 3 things from the whole buffet...crab legs, fresh pineapple, and chocolate covered strawberries.  To me, heaven!  We went on Sunday around 4:30 p.m.  No wait at all!  Went for the crab legs, they are on ice, but give them an empty plate and they will load it with hot ones from the pot.  Melted butter is around the corner, had to look for it, but no worries.  Marched back to my table, up to my elbows in crab, and went back for another plate.  Saw someone had a chocolate covered strawberry on her plate, and went in search!  They make them right there in front of you, so they are fresh and divine!  Must have had, um, 8? The fresh pineapple was perfect as a final
nibble.
Although I didn't eat at the other stations, they looked amazing, there was tons of
wait staff to clear and fill drinks, place was clean, and we will never go anywhere else!  Ate at the Mirage too, and we were both sick to our stomachs the next day.  It as $30, so for another $20, well worth it.  Enjoy!
Not as good as the reviews, the majority of the food was cold. Definitely  not worth the cost, based on all the high reviews, would not make it a.priority to return

I heard a lot of hype about this place.  So had to check it out.  A bit disappointed though.  My short list here is all I really have to say.

Cons: 
- Pricing: What is their pricing?  We paid $54 each.  From previous reviews on here, the dinner menu varies from $34 to $60.  Seems like they flip a coin each week?
- Service: Our busboy outshined out waitress by far.  He was far more attentive and even got us refills when she was MIA.
- Layout: yes, you get the 30 second breakdown of where everything is from your hostess, but it just didn't flow the way it should have.
- Location.... We literally asked 5 different Caesars employees where this place was and got pointed in 3 different directions.  At six months old, Caesars needs to add this to the signage around the hotel.  Had someone simply said it was next to the pool, I would have found it quicker.
-We noticed the disclaimer to 'please limit visit to 2 hours'.  However, we felt "kicked out" at one hour as our waitress brought us the check for our drinks at exactly 1 hour without asking if we were done.

Pros:
- Seafood: Everything about it was excellent!  The Mussels, Cajun Crawfish, oysters and king crab legs... yum!
- Variety was excellent
- Desserts... WOW!
- Décor - It is beautiful in here.
Best Vegas buffet I have ever been to! Everything was delicious. There was plenty of variety. It has the price tag to match, but if you have the opportunity to go, I highly reccomend.
I came here with my boyfriend for an anniversary dinner and it is hands down the best buffet in Las Vegas!! My favorite was the crepe bar, obviously (;

I was here some time between Christmas and New Years 2012/2013. OH MY GOD, this was awesome! I usually don't eat a lot. I eat small meals probably 6 times a day. But I saved my tummy for dinner here. They have... EVERYTHING. Each island had it's own genre of food, for example a huge island of red meat only. the HUGEST island of deserts ever. & a whole lot of sea food. I told myself to take my time because eating too fast and filling up is just a waste of money. Drinks-- you're only allowed to have one type of drink, that & water. So, that was disappointing. I ordered diet coke, so I only got diet coke for the rest of the night!

King crab legs! It's very light, so that was one of the things I had first. I took an extra plate and mixed up some salt, pepper & lemon. The people were awesome regularly coming along to take away our plates and plates of crab shells.
Soup & salads: meh, just like any other place that has a self-service soup & salad cart.

The best thing of all: DESSERT! anything & everything you could think of was here. Dessert didn't just have a cart, it had a whole counter that took up half of one of the walls.

If there was alcohol, I didn't see it.

There was no chicken anywhere! I was okay with it, because I have chicken all the time, but it's weird that it would everything but chicken.

Aw man... it was awesome.

Soooooooo much foooooood.

I originally head about this place via frolic and I was intrigued.  Then, by the awesome grace of God, Groupon had a deal. 2 VIP Access with drink of choice for $88.  I was sold.

We got there and I was glad we got to jump into the VIP line.  The other line was mad long like a Disney Ride of Doom long.  From entering the VIP line to seating it only took about 10 minutes.

Then the buffet battle.
I systematically brought 2 plates to the table at a time, making sure I got a little of everything and I didn't load up on the starches.  In the end my favorites included:
- pretty much everything on the Mexican bar
-the noodle station
-the fat slabs of bacon
-crepe station

The not so impressive notes:
-overly dry eggs Benedict
-stale waffles and chicken 
-"not in a good way" fishy sushi

I left rolling myself out and doing a half marathon to counter the calorie intake.
I will be back again!
Muahahahahaha.

I've had bacchanal buffet twice, during lunch and dinner. Both are good but dinner offers more options. 

The buffet offers so many choices including Chinese food, Dim sum, Peking duck, suckling pig, shrimp stuffed chicken wings, sushi, poki, soba noodles, ramen, pho, Singapore noodles, steamed crab legs, salad, cheese plate, jicama salad, taco made to order (chicken, al pastor, carne asada), all kinds of meat, seafood stew, salmon, lamb t rack, mussels, escargot in garlic sauce, crab legs (two kinds), oysters, sea snails,  oyster shots, rice, and the highlight is the desserts for me: creme brûlée, egg tarts, whites chocolate mousse with passion fruit, apricot tapioca, chocolate mousse with peanut butter, chocolate lava cake (personal favorite), crepes with different sauces made to order, cheesecake, matcha cake, lemon megrine tart, chocolate tart, strawberry dipped in matcha chocolate, strawberry dipped in milk chocolate, chocolates, different ice cream and mocha (green tea and mango).

Lines are common and you may need to eat for an hour to get in. 

Do not eat too much and respect your body. That's the last I can say after witnessing someone threw up after the buffet and missed the O show.

I was VERY excited to check out my first big buffet coming to Las Vegas. Haven't had buffet food since I was in the dining commons at school! I had heard good things about Bacchanal from friends so I had high expectations coming in. After dining here, my general comments are: yes, there is a ton of food choices around varying from Chinese, Italian, Meats, Seafood, Cheeses, Japanese and even dim sum items, but the quality of the food tasted average. For instance, the wood fired meat was very dry and bland, the shrimp and crab legs had ice chunks still attached to it (making it obvious it was cooked and then frozen again), the shu mai and dumplings contained a bit too much water.. I really wanted to love this place, but it was tough for me because nothing seemed to really stand out to me in terms of food quality, everything just felt like an over abundance of every item. 

Shout out to our waitress, she wasn't very present with us, but she was definitely working hard balancing multiple tables at once. What was awesome was everytime I got up to grab another plate, when I'd come back my knife and fork would be neatly placed and my old plate was gone, but I still rarely saw the waitress. She was like a ninja lol! I can't imagine how fast paced it must be to work here, so I definitely have to give my respect to the employees here.

I would have to say my favorite (and probably many other people's favorite) section was the dessert section. They have a variety of macarons, gelati, crepes, cookies, brownies, aka tons of sugar product everywhere. I got really excited when I saw they had a Thai ice cream with boba, but was let down because the boba was brittle and the flavor was not very memorable. I'd have to say my favorite part of this entire place was the baked beans and mac n cheese next to the meat section along with the pistachio gelato. Otherwise, besides the ice chunks on the shrimp, I had a hard time swallowing why I paid over $60 for this place. This place was definitely an experience, but not one I will be returning to anytime soon.

No matter what time you come here you have to wait at least 3 hours...........but if you pay extra 25 dollars you only need to wait about a hour........ so weird , won't come back anymore........ by the way , the food are just so so too

Worth the splurge for the reigning buffet on the strip.  Yes, that's my vote, hands down the winner of best buffet.  Don't waste your time, money or limited stomach space on other buffets.   

All the extravagance you would expect from a Vegas buffet.  Crab legs, oysters on the half shell, decadent desserts, lamb chops, meat and more meat,...

We were a mixed group of experienced Vegas buffet goers and newbies.  Everyone was impressed with this buffet.  The thing that stands out here is that every dish was well done.  Definitely some highlights and some A-OK dishes but there were no lowlights.   We were also pleasantly surprised that the Asian section offered really good food.  Asian approved ;). 

Pleasant and hardworking staff too.

Well now I've been to Sofritos Rest.now 5 times, this time brought 3 people with me you would think after the first 4 times and 3 times no pastillas I would call ahead and ask do you have pastilles  today? But no I did not, drove there from Aliente Casino 18 miles, new waiters who I might add were prompt, courteous and went over the order with all of us. 
And again we all order yup you guessed it pastilles! Once again no pastilles. Madre De Dios!! 
What we did have was wonderful, now for those of you who are not of the Puerto Rican persuasion when your told be there in a minute, that means at the minimum 10 min and optimum 30 mi and that's just to ask if you want a drink if they ask.
So if you can over look that then it's worth the aggravation, long drives, very little interaction with your servers.
Yes I'll be back food is great and only PR restaurant in town.
One day I truly want to give them a 5 star rating we shall see.

The glory that was Rome,  the empire that the sun never set upon, WAS the bacchanal. NOT any more. As with all great civilizations they get complacent and fall from grace. Don't get me wrong, it's still the best buffet in Vegas, but it's a shadow of its self and the value is no longer there. Most buffets in town have gone backwards in quality, because too many (B)ig (U)gly (F)at (F)ucks (E)ating (T)ogether have gorged themselves like bears hibernating for winter. All in all it was good and I should be good till springtime

and still...
the best buffet in vegas.
experience was worth the wait.
take your time in this place and don't forget the gelato.

My wife and I arrived at 3:45 we used a Groupon to get past the already growing line. The seafood was great if you don't mind waiting in line for the oysters, pre-cut crab legs, sea snails, and shrimp.
Every dish we had was the highest quality. Service was on point.
 The desert section not only did it look appealing it actually had flavor which is something that most desert buffets tend to lack.
I guess we will have to go back because there was so many dishes that we didn't get to try.
Side note: the curry and Peruvian ceviche were the best I've had.

Definitely a tad overpriced. Most expensive casino buffet on the strip, which would be fine(I don't mind spending money on good food), but the wait was upwards of two hours!! Other buffets in Vegas might not be as large, but the quality is just as good and the lines are usually almost nonexistent.

Bacchanal lived up to the hype! I recommend it to everyone! 

I went for brunch. They had an amazing large selection of food. Their desserts were my favorite as well as their seafood. All delicious!

We came around 1 and had about a 30 minute wait. So it wasn't as bad as I thought.
Amazing variety of great tasting food! You are guaranteed to leave satisfied. Service is great too!

It was okay, but I wasn't blown away. Long lines and a fairly high price for lunch.

Didn't hate it but would not bother going back again.

Well - this buffet is the buffet to ruin me for all other buffets. I loved that most items were pre-plated in small individual portions that felt perfect, so as to allow trying as many items as possible. 
My highlights were the coconut ceviche shooters, the mini bottles of fresh juice and the myriad delights at the desert displays. 
Great service except for maybe one guy slicing meat - who was a little annoyed with too many questions, but maybe he was just having an off day. 
We left feeling sufficiently satisfied- but not overly so - success!!

As good as I expected.  The reviews are correct.  It's a fantastic buffet and it's expensive but it was totally worth it. I can't eat a big quantity of food but I don't think I overspent because it was that good!  Favorite items: gumbo, bone marrow, crab legs, the thin cuts of Iberico ham, and the Chinese food section!  Least favorite section: the Japanese food.  The desserts looked good but I could not eat more at that point so I skipped.

Bacchanal is okay! They got lots of stations but I can't say much was super memorable and something I must go back to have! Wait... Does dessert count? If so then they do have orange beer sorbet and mango habanero gelato which was a little different from the norm. It was spicy for sure!

Crab legs hot or cold was okay! They plate it for you which isn't bad and keeps from people hogging it so I do like that. Too bad no dungeoness crab tho! Prime rib wasn't bad, lamb chops were good but again... Nothing memorable. I did like the Chinese chicken wings with lots of flavor but a little salty. Oysters were not fresh at all and super obvious for those who eat them on a regular. 

Go on a off hour and you'll be seated in 30-45 minutes otherwise plan on waiting forever!

Very disappointed!

The food was OK, not really any better than  Bellagio, Wynn, or Cosmopolitans Wicked Spoon in my opinion.

The low rating is for the wait times and setup of the buffet.  There was a two hour wait in line to get in.  We choose to do the express line for an extra $15 each.  Once inside the lines continued.

To get to the seafood or the meat selections you had to wait in 20-30 minute lines.  You would walk to other parts of the buffet and it would be empty.

Many of the selections are on individual plates or in baskets, this makes it difficult to carry your food as the plates slide round.  It is also cumbersome when you have to wait in long lines for your food.  

I also noticed while making a salad that the counters were so low that I could not get around the sneeze guard to get to toppings in the back without having to contort myself.  I am 5'9 so not overly tall.

I noticed that people were filling multiple plates because the lines were so long that to go back for seconds you would have to wait in line all over again.

Cesar's really needs to rethink this $50 million dollar mess, until then, don't waste your time.

I absolutely loved this place! 
The food was very good, desserts were delicious. My favorite were the different veriaty of Hispanic drinks

My new favorite buffet in Vegas! Like every other buffet in Vegas each one has its pros and cons. For instance, I like that the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan serves nice gourmet dishes in small portions so that you can try a bit of everything without over indulging. Also, I like that they give you the choice of choosing the champagne mimosas once you're inside. Bucchanal didn't give us that choice. It was just included in our brunch costing us $45 each on a Saturday. Pros to this buffet is that they have a ticket system where instead of waiting in line for an +1 hour you can walk up to their machine and type in your number of party, cell phone (they text you when to check-in) and they give you a time to come back to pay and eat :) think of it as a fast pass at Disneyland but for delicious food! 

Things that I looove about this buffet: they give you the option of having your crab legs cold or steamed! YES. Finally someone had the fabulous idea to take into consideration that not everyone likes to eat their crab cold (me) thank you Bacchanal! Another thing, they have a personal chef making your tacos, another making ramen, pho, udon and some other Chinese soups. Yum! And instead of having your same ordinary 3 types of sushi servings they are always changing it up to different varieties of fish and rolls as soon as soon as it's gone. Amazing! Didn't get to try the prime rib or ribs but it smelled amazing and I passed the long line. Don't forget to try their macaroons and desserts on your way out! Hands down, bacchanal did a fabulous job into taking consideration about what their customer likes. I will be back soon!

The selection is not as many as I have expected. The plastic lobsters are for display only. The pasta is very salty and the Chinese BBQ dishes look scary. The desserts are top notched so there are extra points for that.

Our group of eight visited right after the lunch cutoff but before the dinner crowd came, which afforded us a fairly quick entry into the seating area (that, and I think someone had status, which got us in the shorter line).

The buffet is indeed expansive (and expensive, as others have noted), but the results were mixed in terms of food quality. Hot crab legs were OK from a flavor standpoint, but despite being precut, harvesting the meat was a little tricky. Hamburger sliders in several flavors fared a bit better, with good flavor and tender rolls for buns. Some of the presentations made it tricky to get the food to your table - are you supposed to dump the tots from the little basket onto your plate, or take the basket? 

Beef brisket was tough and dry, but prime rib was better, probably due to its as-needed carving. Of the meats that I tried, the bacon might have been the best - very crispy and crunchy, it had a nice smoky flavor and was great just by itself. 

Another surprise dish was corn on the cob in the elotes (Mexican street corn) style, something I hadn't seen before, but it tasted nice, with a creamy sauce and nice crumbles of hard cheese. 

Perhaps the biggest surprise of all was a small creme brulee that I sampled from the dessert bar; I'm ordinarily very skeptical, as many crimes are committed against this dish at even high end restaurants, but since I saw them being hand caramelized right behind the display, I had to try. It was really good, with the perfect creme texture, not too gelatinous, not too stiff, and nicely creamy. The sugar top had a nice crunch and complemented the custard well. 

Unfortunately, the price here, even considering that it's Vegas, compared to the overall quality of the food, is what brings this review down to three stars. Yes, there were some winners, but many of the dishes were simply average. This was the only buffet we tried on this visit, and my last Vegas buffet was eight years ago, so I don't really have much to compare it to. Your mileage may vary, though - read some other reviews and decide for yourself if you want to give it a try.

We have never been more impressed with a buffet.  The king crabs were amazing.  This is truly the best buffet in Vegas.  The choices were high end and the deserts were wonderful.  A must if you want a really high end buffet. Pricey but you won't be disappointed food wise.

BUFFET SUCKS!
We were doing the Buffet of Buffets and there was an upcharge for this Buffet of $30 a person. We heard good things about the Buffet so we decided to pay it. It was not at all worth it. 
First of all, I'm a vegetarian and there was hardly any vegetarian options available.
My non-vegetarian boyfriend was not impressed either. He did not like the selection and the things they did have was not worth the price.
The food wasn't bad but for the high dollar amount, I would go to any other buffet in Vegas.

My favorite buffet in Vegas.. it's just an abundance of everything..  make sure you don't eat all day bc you'll want to stuff your stomach with their food .. waiters/ waitresses are very nice and take care of you.. all around awesome. Is alittle pricey but it's worth it.

5 stars hands!!! If you don't eat here while enjoying Vegas then you missed out !

Service was great and had them refills on drinks coming every moment I was out. Great music playing in the background in perfect volume . I enjoyed all my plates and dessert was delicious with lots of variety .

Great place for food junkys!
