You cannot believe the number of dishes until you dine there, I still can't. How does one believe that a buffet can be so big until they actually sit inside? The space was immense. The dessert bar out of this world. I would hit the desserts first next time I take guests visiting Vegas

My wife and I went here for breakfast and were supposed at all the options. Their buffet has everything you can think of and tons of dessert options!! Bottomless mimosas were great and our server kept filling us up. A little pricey but everything in Vegas is.
This is the best buffet in Las Vegas. The quality the food, the taste, the variety are excellent. Everything is perfect.. I extremely recommend..

When you've been here every time you've visited Vegas, you know it's the real deal. This place is great with small parties and large parties. Though there is a HUGE quantity and variety of food, most of it tastes really good. Even when I had vegetarian friends with me, they had PLENTY of options to try from. Sometimes the chef would even make the dish fresh with tofu and bring it to our table! 

Moral of the story: when in Vegas, go to Bacchanal. The end.

This is one our favorite buffets here when we are talking solely about food.  Although it is on the pricier side, the food is prepared well and there are tons of options to choose from.

However, the service is lacking (cashiers, hostesses and waiting staff).  They all seem unhappy, make weird comments that are more on the rude side and are quick to try to get you out even though you paid an arm and a leg to sit at a table.  The people preparing and serving the food behind the counter are a lot nicer and friendlier.  I'm not the only one who has said that. My friends and co-workers who have been here have said the exact same thing about the employees here.  We also notice that if you include the tip when you pay (despite the tip being a very generous amount), the waiting staff treat you with less respect than if you didn't give pay the tip ahead of time. All friends and I have now been putting the tip on the table prior to leaving the buffet so that we get treated better than in the past.

I.just.can't.  SO DANG GOOD!!!!
This buffet blew me away!! In this town where most of the buffets are interchangeable the Bacchanal knocked it out of the park!!
Okay, the wait was annoying but gotta say, worth it.
You walk in past the seafood station filled with delicious sea creatures of all kinds...shrimp, crab legs, clams, mudbugs..and lots more! On the way to our table was just amazing! There is too many items to lust but what we will tell you what we did enjoy!! The steam crab legs in the back with clarified butter was so good I thought I was in heaven!! Already split and pile generously on the plate..I mean GENEROUSLY!! I cleaned em
Up too!! Was gonna get some more but realized I wanted to try other things. 
There was a fresh salad area that was fabulous! Pizza was wonderful!! Braised short ribs served in an individual little pot was so tender and yummy! Hubby had rice with crab, he said the roast beef was yummy. There was the most delicious mashed potatoes!! Great vegetables and  Prob 25 varieties of bread scattered throughout.. So many stations!! American, Chinese, sushi, Italian, Mexican!! The dessert station..well it was just amazing.. Macaroons, fudge, iced, fruits, cakes, I mean just the best..of everything!
The thing is not just the variety..(which I have been told is over 500 items) EVERYTHING is high quality. 
If you like the dining experience as part of Vegas this is worth the price! 
We will be back!!
Did I say the best snow crab legs EVER? Lol

As a Food caterer, and lover of great food in general, this Buffet is the absolute best I ever had in my life.  Price is not an issue, and should not be, for anyone looking for a  top quailty meal, and I understand why some may feel differently.  I have been to Vegas 40 times, and tried the Bellagio(5 stars) Wicked Spoon (4.5 stars), and The Wynn (4.5stars), and this one tops them all. WHY???   The sheer amount of variety is off the chart, BUT the quality in everything I tried was top notch.  Anyone can serve a ton of different foods ie.. Rio, Cravings, Harrahs, but to me , Quality wins every time.
Suer Fresh seafood, and the Shrimp is fresh not thawed, which is awesome.
The oysters looked great, and they'll warm up the crab legs for you(YES!!)
          The Lamb chops were incredible, and Bone-in Rib Eye Steak was perfect, and The  Prime rib was great.  The Cheese selection was high end, and the salads were super fresh.  Excellent side dishes, and veges, all very fresh, try the asparagus, and carrots.  The lobster corn chowder was awesome.
Bottom line...  Oustanding, and the desserts were amazing with real fresh fruit without the crappy sugary glaze for the fresh crepes, with real whipped cream OMG!!
The lines can be long, but there is a reason for that, the food is that good.  It would take me 10 trips to get a feel for all the food, but it was awesome.  
Had lunch the next day, and it was great as well. Go there and enjoy, plus our server was very friendly, and cleaned up our plates pretty quickly.
You'll pay twice as much in an upscale restaurant or more for the same quailty you get here.  Long live Ceasar!!!!!

Amazing buffet and definitely got my money's worth. Huge selection of meats, and the Asian section is terrific. The meat is a little hit or miss. I had a terrific tri tip, but a dry brisket. My friend however got a beautiful and juicy piece of brisket. The desserts are also to die for. If you only have to one buffet in Vegas, pick the Bacchanal. I visited some of the others and Bacchanal definitely takes the cake.

Came in at the perfect time.  You know - at the end of breakfast, but at the beginning of brunch.  There wasn't a wait to get in at that time and I was able to have a little bit of breakfast and lunch.  Worked out well.   I have to say that this is the best buffet in Vegas.   

Though the buffet is smaller than some of the other top buffets, they make up for it in quality.  Like Wicked Spoon, they offer a la carte portions.  I love that - it's clean, individually portioned, and you get buffet items you'd expect on full restaurant menus.

They won me over when I saw red velvet pancakes and monte cristo sandwiches for breakfast.  And they surprised me when I saw taiwanese breakfast offerings and pretty solid XLB and hargow dumplings.  My favorite breakfast item was their Croque Madame which had a perfectly over-medium egg in the middle of the sandwich.  My buddy, a tough critic, thought that the eggs benedict was perfect.

For lunch, loved their shrimp cocktail, their ceviche bar and gaspacho.  They also had a taco bar where they freshly cooked carne asada and al pastor.  And they had a full guac/salsa bar.  It was definitely good.  But the star of the show was their meat station.  They offered prime rib, st louis ribs, and beef brisket.  The ribs were tough and dry - didn't recommend it.  But I requested my brisket extra fatty and the guy behind the counter lit up like my Christmas tree.  He gave me some great burnt ends and it was just some great meat.  I really enjoyed my brisket here.

While I love entrees, my heart is always reserved for dessert. They definitely had a few solid offerings.  They have some fancy looking chocolate, they have creme brulee, I really liked their praline tarts, they had a crepe station, and a gelato bar.  My favorite gelato was their baklava gelato.  Pretty solid.  It didn't beat the Thai Tea gelato I had at Wicked Spoon the night before.  And I can't say that the dessert was better than the Bellagio buffet.  But overall..I thought that the quality entrees made this buffet stand out above its competitors.

I went to Bacchanal Buffet because I heard how good it was. The Saturday brunch was $41.99, lots of food, service was lacking. i ordered coffee, and had to ask for a teaspoon, it took a while for the waitress to come back.  Our dirty dishes piled up and have to get attention to the waitress to clear the dirty dishes. Wow, if you feel you can charge me that much, I better have excellent service.  Some of my foods were cold or not hot, so I will not be going back for a long, long time. No thanks, there are lots of places on the Vegas strip, less money for better services.

Yep. It was good. Hot crab legs. Fried rice. Pressed juice. Sushi. Tacos. Pasta. My only negative is that the tongs for the salad were ridiculously difficult and their balsamic is kinda whack --went with the Ranch. But who goes to a buffet for salad anyway so no deductions. Definitely coming back.

My family and I had very high expectations when we finally got into the buffet. We had to wait a whopping 4 hours. For $70 for dinner I did not think it was worth it. You spend all your time waiting to get in and you also spend a lot of time waiting to get food once you are inside. For the price of that dinner they did not even have lobster. It felt like any other buffet in Vegas and that is why I gave it 2 stars. Maybe the experience would have been different on a different day but I would not come back to dine here by choice. Expect to wait longer than what the paper from the machine says.

When my girlfriend told me that her family recommended that we go to a "buffet" I nearly died. I am a foodie...we don't do such things. I mean...it is against the foodie bible (if one existed). I cringed and figured that I was going to lose out on spending a chunk of money for a crappy lunch. They told us to check out this place. Whoa I was waaayyy off.

Every station was incredibly well thought out. I loved the Singapore noodles, Clam Bake Buckets, and everything in the dessert station (especially the chocolate soufflé, chocolate croissant, and the red velvet whoopie pie). 

We went during lunch. Totally worth the price. Hard to believe...but true. I guarantee there cannot be another buffet in the entire universe that has anything to beat this place. I will never go to another buffet in my life, except this place.

Arrive before 11 to avoid the crowd.
We walked right in when we got there around 10am on a Wednesday, but saw the huge line as we were leaving. Place was pretty good in terms of a buffet, wide selection, from salads, pizza, sushi, eggs. Other than my coffee mug being dirty and having to ask for a different one, we enjoyed our breakfast.

EPIC and Perfect (except I took a star off for the wait)

But we love it and we'll be back.

Its got the smashing dessert collection, expensive seafoods and meats, weird drinks.

Only place to get unlimited fresh raw oysters that you can trust on the strip.  

So MUCH VARIETY, you will not know what to do with yourself.  Come hungry, don't waste your tummy on cheap food (even though its good), like rice or whatever.

Take a look at all the pictures other people took.
Horrible customer service that talks down to you and even worse management.  Doesn't matter how good the food is, I'll never be back

Yea no f**k this garbage. Website at 6am says early bird 29.99 until 10am, got there at 9am, cashier says there's no promo for early bird anymore. I checked again 930am website still says 29.99 before 10. 

We went over to wicked spoon because fk them, we got literally bait and switched. After we got done with wicked spoon, I checked again at 12pm and they did update their pricing (no more early bird) on their website. 

Because of their shit system we got screwed and wasted 40 mins parking and walking etc. not about to pay extra if we were informed of different prices beforehand by their lagging website. bullshit. 

I shoulda talked to management but the cashier just looked at our party like we were dipshits so yea fk that  we just left.

The food is delicious and there are so many choices it is hard to decide.  The desserts are over the top and beautiful for a buffet.  The only reason I couldn't give it 5 stars is the WAIT.  Waiting in line for an hour and the confusion at the hostess stand is frustrating and annoying.  There has to be a more efficient way.  Mind the price also, it is VERY expensive.

I'm going to preface this with, if you want to go cheap in Vegas, don't go here! But I knew what I was getting into when I read the reviews of how pricey the buffet really was. Okay so first of all, the wait. Well my boyfriend and I decided to do an early dinner and sneak into the lunch price because it ends at 3pm. We were in line at 2.45pm since we didn't have breakfast and waited for a good 45 minutes. I can totally see how the dinner line could be double the wait, so I'm glad we opted for the early dinner. On the down side, your price depends on the time you get to pay before you are seated, so no cheaper buffet for us. :( $55 per person

But can I say it wasn't worth the price? HELL NO. This place is the Willy Wonka's of buffets!! Steamed king crab legs, (sliced in half so all you need to do is use a fork to grab the meat), FRESH oysters (could definitely be better shucked, but delicious nonetheless), dim sum (everything tasted freshly baked and steamed), amazing vegetables/salads, sushi (not a very huge selection), fresh pasta, incredible crawfish broil, WAGYU sliders!, rice/beans (because I wouldn't be hispanic if I didn't try these), chicken in waffle cones and of course the custom areas were the best! So in between all this glorious food (some of which looked adorable in mini plates as if at a 5 star restaurant, and even though they look cute, they are most definitely not easy to carry around..) were areas that you could ask for specific foods that they were cooking in the back. Fresh turkey, sausage, steak, pasta, mac and cheese, crab legs from the boiling pot!, tacos with chicken/beef/etc, and so much more. I know I've left out a TON but these are a few things I had to try. I was looking for lobster, and that was the only thing missing in the seafood section. And even though there was so much to taste, I had to save room for the dessert.

I've got to say, I was overwhelmed by how huge this place is (25,000 sq feet) that when I got up to go grab food I thought I would forget how to get back at my table. It wasn't until my second helping of dinner that I realized I hadn't seen any dessert. It's only in the MIDDLE of the entire restaurant with the best selection of desserts I have ever seen. The reason the Bacch receives 5 stars from me is the dessert. No, I don't normally order desserts at dinner, and yes the food had incredible flavor with an incredible selection, but that took a seat back to  the dessert. To keep it short, they have fruits, cakes, cheesecakes, flans, cake pops, ice cream, gelato, cookies, donuts, I mean the list is endless. There is also someone behind the counter that is pouring gelato scoops into the smallest waffle cone bowls that can have any kind of toppings you want. But the best dessert by far, was the green tea covered strawberry with chocolate covered crispies. I literally melted away into another planet as I was tasting the mix of green tea, chocolate, rice crispies and strawberry in one bite. Needless to say, I will be back!! And also the $20 endless drinks (you can choose from mimosas, wine or beer) are also wonderful if you can drink a few of them along with all the food you'll eat. We had the mimosas and after 2, you pretty much paid the $20, so if, let's say, I had 5 or 6, I totally made up for that!

I tried about 95% of all the food offered here and since there is limited typing space, I will just name a few dishes that stood out and a few that weren't the greatest.

GOOD

Lobster Corn Chowder - Wow... full of flavor without being too heavy.  The fresh chunks of corn really add a surprising bite and sweetness.

Muscles - Fresh, not over done and great with a squeeze of fresh lemon.

Roasted Duck - FULL of flavor.  Fatty and duck-y... just how it should be.  Goes great with rice, but rice fills you up quick

Japanese Seaweed Salad - Full of sesame flavor.  Texturally this salad is just simply fun to eat.

Crab Legs - Not too salty, which i adore.  Don't forget the clarified butter!! It's great because these legs already come split lengthwise making it much easier to eat.

Assortment of cured meats, cheese, and dried fruit.

Pecan Tart - Buttery and rich.  Crumbly and butter crust.  One of my favorites

Tiramisu - It's almost hard not to f***k this dessert up.  Love the espresso flavor.

NOT SO GOOD

Brisket - Over-smoked in my opinion.  I personally like a light smoke ring around my brisket, but this was just SATURATED in smoke.

Prime Rib - DON'T FORGET TO ASK THEM TO POUR SOME AU JUS OVER YOUR CUT.  The meat itself is tasteless without it.

BBQ Ribs - Again, heavy on the smoke flavor.  Would've been great if it wasn't for such a heavy smoke ring.

Chinese Selection - Ok, I'm just saying this because I'm not a fan of Chinese food (I'm asian if you're wondering).  I tried every Chinese dish they offered, but every dish tasted similar to each other.  I mean, the Chinese dishes were pretty straight forward in flavor.

Italian Selection - Stray away from this section because it is extremely HEAVY with CARBS.

Sushi - No matter what buffet I go to the raw sushi is never that good.  The rice was saturated in rice wine vinegar and the fish wasn't of the greatest quality.

OVERALL:  I could go on and one but these are just the few that stick out.  If you're looking for a buffet that has a HUGE selection of food, look elsewhere such as the Rio or the M Buffet.  

Like I always say, YOU WON'T KNOW UNLESS YOU TRY IT FOR YOURSELF!

Buffet was good and offered a good variety. Much better than The Buffet in Aria that we been to. Quality is much better than most other buffets you can find in Vegas. Though Memorial Day weekend pricing plus tip put the price for two at $175.00. The  reason I decided to remove one star was because I thought it was a little pricey even for what we got, we waited a total of almost two hours, and we never even got a menu for the caviar menu. Nonetheless, the service seemed to be good for the number of people there. The waiter got me a refill on my drink without me having to ask, within 1 minute of me finishing my drink.
Total waste of money! Maybe my taste buds /standards too high.but it was awful nothing tasted good ... 130$ for me and my husband and we left and went to walburgers.

For being an expensive buffet, they should and could easily have more vegetarian meat substitutes.  Or have a made to order section for vegans and vegetarians, like a tofu chilequiles! Thank god I went for breakfast and was able to get eggs. 

But my major complaint is how quickly my food become cold by the time I reached my table. My server Fendencio was great and made up for the food temperature and options. 

So many options. I give them that! It's like Disneyland for food. The shrimp and grits was good and the Chilequiles. I also appreciate their very healthy cucumber green juice. Not sweet at all.

This place is still the place to go for buffet. I am so glad nothing really has changed and everything is still up to par. I like how this place has a place for you to check in and they would text you when the table is ready.

Hands Down 5-Stars for the dinner. The first time I tried it was in 2015, but this time I think it has even gotten better. Bacchanal Buffet is for me the Best Buffet in Las Vegas along with Bally's Sterling Brunch！Unlike the Sterling Brunch that focuses primarily on Seafood and Champagnes with a very limited selection of different cuisines, Bacchanal buffet offers the quantity and variety of different cuisines you have never imagined before in a buffet setting!  If you want a taste of different food cuisines from different regions around the world, there is no place better than Bacchanal.

What is even more important is that despite of the quantity and variety of the food offered, the quality hasn't been compromised at all. From the Chinese Beijing Duck and roasted pig to the Mexican Made-To-Order Beef and Chicken Tacos, to the Jumbo Shrimp, Oysters and Cold and Boiled King Crab Legs in Seafood, everything I have tasted here is delicious and fresh.

Also, the service here is so good and attentive, the waiters would always come to ask what you want to drink and fill your cup.

During this holiday season, I waited for more than 5 hours to get my table and paid $60 for the dinner, which is quite steep for a buffet. But I would say after trying it, it was worth every minute I waited and every penny I spent and I look forward to be back again when I'm in Vegas the next time.

It's an okay place, nothing out of the ordinary. The problem is, our society has become a sheepish society. What ever one person says about a place, they all exaggerate. The price, for a Saturday brunch of $119 + my $10 tip was definitely not worth the price, way over priced. Just my humble opinion.

The first time I tried this buffet, I thought it was okay. But after my second trip, I thought it was delicious. The best thing was the dessert selection. They have gelato, a crepe station, and various bite-sized desserts like flan, cheesecake, abuelita chocolate mousse and fruit tarts. Each tasted great. 
The only downside is the price. It's about 60 bucks/person. But, it's worth it.

I love Bacchanal Buffet! The gourmet cuisines offered here are a must if you happen to be at Caesar's Palace. Please get the king crab legs and dip them in butter sauce. They are so so good. The carving station is fit for a king and queen. They include delicious prime rib and succulent beef brisket. The desserts are oh so appetizing! Get the creme brulee and savor the  gelato delicacies. To be honest I didn't get good pics of my feast because it was gone before you could say, "Bacchanal Buffet rules!" I cannot forget our server Maria. She was so sweet and attentive. If you need a professional server who goes above and beyond, she is it. She should be training all new employees to show an example of what excellent service is. The delectable fare and service from Maria really represent the high standards you would expect from a gorgeous property like Caesar's Palace. I highly recommend and remember to come hungry!

Definitely a fan of this place. Love all their gourmet options and huge selection of meet and seafood.

I give this place 4 stars because of the price. Dinner is like $60! I mean, it's a great buffet and every single thing I ate there was sooo delicious, but I'm probably not coming back unless it's included on the buffet of buffet pass. Glad I tried this place. I'm sure I can go to less pricey buffets and have the same options...maybe.

I wish I could think of more things to say about this place, but pretty much everyone has already said all the things that I wanted to say.

All in all - try it if you're feeling adventurous/generous and want to dip some crab in their butter made out of crack. (it's not really made out of crack, but you get what I mean)

When my bf asked me what I wanted for my birthday dinner I said "Vegas buffet." Definitely glad we came!! This is way better than most buffets I've had in Vegas. I spent two hours here eating!

Yay:
-Oysters: I love raw oysters and I love that it was offered here AND didn't make my stomach hurt after.  I think I ate two dozen on my own.
-Prime rib: this is one of my criteria for a good buffet and they definitely pass! A lot of places offer prime rib that isn't season well but theirs is really good.
-Crab: definitely get it steamed! So much easier to remove it from the shell and had a better taste.

Other:
-Desserts: I liked the variety of desserts they offer.  However, their creme brulee wasn't good.  It was more like a flan then a creme brulee.  I really enjoyed their chocolate lava cake and their mochi.

Nay:
-The rude guy at the station where you get the crab steamed.  My bf asked if that was the place to get steamed crab and he said "right in front of your face." WTF!! NO! right in front of his face was a DISPLAY of the crab legs in buckets behind a glass asshole! When my bf asked if he could get some he responded with "just leave your plate here and come back in a few minutes." GEEZ!! Get a new job since you hate yours so much!

Omg... I can't believe they served lobster and cavier for buffet.
I have to say, they also have the best server ever!!!!!
My friends and I came here in New year eve and had really good time.
They have so many different kinds of high quality seafood.
The dessert are not too sweet. They even served all u can drink champagne.
I'm really impresed!!!!
Definitely we are coming back soon.
Even tho the line is crazy, it is worth it.
Or you can find some friends have Diamond card or 7 star card.
You don't have to wait in line too long.
^_^
Amazing food and service ! I would definitely be back !i go every ear more then 4 times there's the best of the best

Just a slightly above average buffet. I came here expecting it to live up to its reputation as the best buffet in Vegas but I left disappointed.  The king crab was ok but barely larger than the snow crab most buffets offer. The stone crab was probably previously frozen and tasted pretty bad.  The oysters were good though so I had about two dozen of those. The street tacos were just ok and the sushi was horrible. Prime rib was good but for $59 per adult and a two hour wait it was definitely not worth it. I feel like there has to be better buffets out there. The Wynn buffet used to be my favorite but that place has fallen off too. Really disheartening to see all these formally great buffets turning mediocre.

Lines are insane, prices are high (for a vegas buffet), but its totally worth it. The food all looks so amazing that it's probably the only buffet where I've actually wanted to try EVERYTHING. The quality of the food is on par with a really good 4 star restaurant, the meat station is awesome, the desserts are incredible. There's a ton of fresh seafood and maybe best of all, they do fresh fruit/vegetable juices. 

I think Sunday brunch is bottomless mimosas too but as anyone who visits Vegas, I'd already had my fair share of booze for the weekend.

Four of us waited two hours in line on a Wed night, only to eat abysmal food. I can't begin to describe the disappointment we felt after trying most of the popular dishes here. Both the chilled and warm crab legs were so salty that we couldn't even finish a plate of them between 4 of us. The 'American wagyu' and prime rib were dry beyond belief. Even most of the dim sum items, like the dumplings and jellyfish were extremely sub-par for any restaurant that would care to serve these types of items. I tried a number of other items in hopes that I could at least find one item that was somewhat enjoyable, however I left defeated and discouraged from ever coming here again. We frequent Las Vegas, and the Aria buffet was by far better than the Bacchanal buffet, in terms of price, food selection, and above all else quality. We won't be returning here anytime soon.

Situation: In Vegas for an All-Guys Trip, Saturday Lunch

The line was out the door. It was least a 2 hour wait. If you're at least a Total Rewards Diamond Star Member, then you can skip the line and look at all the people as you walked by them. Hint: Also a good way to pick up girls. It works for the club, I don't see why it can't work for the buffet line too. **DISCLAIMER** Not tested, but I'll let you know next time I'm in Vegas.

Lunch comes out to about $45 dollars. There is an 18% gratuity with 8+ people. Lunch didn't have oysters, but I've been here before for dinner where they did have oysters. 

The meal comes with bottomless mimosa. So you can definitely go HAM there. I was full before I went halfway around the food stations. Some of my favorite items were the Cheese & Potato Gratin, the crab legs, the seafood, etc. Actually I lived everything about it. My suggest to the Asians out there, don't just go for the high price items, do what you're suppose to really do at a buffet which is sample and taste everything on the menu. Every item is superb in its own respect. When the typical Hot & Sour soup that you normally see in the Chinese Markets was superb. This is culinary buffet cooking at its finest. They have Orchota. They also have the cold version and the hot version of the crab legs, try both.

5-Star Scenario:

-Come here on a Sunday after clubbing, if you're like me and can eat a lot the next day after a long night of drinking amongst other things.
-Come here around 10ish if you want to avoid the lines for lunch. This is usually before people check out of the hotels. 
-If you don't want to worry about food for your entire Vegas trip, get the Buffets of the Buffets deal. If you time this right, you can actually get 4 meals out of it. Also if you book the hotel room for 2 nights, they'll include you 2 buffets passes for free (granted, the price is baked into the price of the Hotel Room from the normal Hotel rate. But, you'll basically get one buffet pass free from the analysis I've done on a couple rates)

5-Star Recommendation:


-Be a Diamond Club member or know someone that's a Diamond Club member. If we're in Vegas at the same time, I'd be happy to walk you in.
-Try a little bit of each item, you'll never know when you'll really like something.
-If the price was $10 dollars cheaper, I would eat here every time I go to Vegas. At this price, I can only go every other time ; (

Came here with my family a year ago and waited 5 hours to be seated. Thought it would be worth the wait since long lines usually means great food. While the food was not bad, I found the selection not as big as Bellagio's. The seafood was lacking and the dessert was pretty weird. The gelato were too fancy. None of the flavored were familiar. I tried some jalapeño berry gelato and almost gagged. There was no simple vanilla or chocolate or strawberry flavor. In short, while this buffet was not the worst, it is simply not as good as Bellagio. And definitely not worth the 5-hour wait.

This place is HUGE! And they have a giant selection of food. The crab here are already split in half so you don't have to break them! There are two rooms, at first I thought there were was only one room, but you just got to turn a corner at the end of the Mexican station and BOOM! Whole mother room with Italian, cold cuts, salads,  and Asian food. They even have dim sum ( for dinner!). Most off the food was good, there were a few selection from the meat station that was a bit too salty. The desert station was the best, it is centered right in the middle of the main room and had every imaginable desert you can think of even mochi! The waiter suggested to get the peach green tea here, and it was soo good, I had like 4 of them, because they are so good. The price is quite expensive here at $50 a person, as well as the line being very long at dinner time. My friends and I waited for about 2 hours until we were able to be seated. Overall this was a good place, with good food.

If you're looking for a Vegas buffet, look no farther. The Bacchanal buffet has an amazing selection of foods from all different ethnic groups as well as a fantastic selection of desserts. Just make sure you have a few hours to kill so that you can eat your money's worth. You won't be disappointed.

Our group arrived at 2pm on Saturday and waited about an hour before paying $48 to get in, which included bottomless mimosas. After we were seated, we had noticed that they were transitioning from brunch to dinner, so we quickly scrambled to grab some brunch foods. The Asian foods were all really tasty, especially the dim sum type foods, but the sushi was average and the different fried rices/stir frys were good but not great. Moving on to the proteins, the prime rib was cooked to perfection, the steak tacos were great, and the sliders... oh man those wagyu beef sliders are game changers. The seafood selection was pretty extensive and the oysters tasted fresh, however the cold king crab was subpar in both taste and texture. The crawfish were tasty and the andouille sausage mixed in added a great flavor.

Onto dessert, the fresh made crepes, the huge selection of baked goods, fresh gelato and assorted sweets were a nice way to finish out the meal.

The servers were very attentive, constantly bussing our plates and refilling our glasses without needing much prompting.

FAVORITE BUFFET IN VEGAS!! my vegas trip is never complete if i don't go here! the wait might be long (2 hours) if you're not a platinum or gold member but definitely worth the wait! brunch is good here cause there's always so much to choose from! and their bottomless mimosas are definitely worth getting!

dinner here has an even longer wait but the seafood part is always worth it!!! there might even be a wait... we came on 4th of july weekend so they were super busy and they did have a holiday price ($75) buuuut worth it if you get a lot of seafood!!

After waiting in line for an hour, we were famished for the buffet. However, even in my hungry state, I found the buffet to be good but not amazing. There are many selections from Asian dim sum to seafood galore. It's a good choice for those who enjoy fresh seafood. I liked the freshly shucked oysters and heated crab legs. There are also lots of meats though I found them to be salty. There are mochi ice cream with 2 per person limit each time; there's only a small wait though. Overall, it's a fun experience, but I will stick with Wynn buffet next time.

"The $17,000,000 Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace offers a feast that boasts more than 500 options and may well take the ongoing battle of Las Vegas buffets to a new level. Bacchanal Buffet premiered on September 11th after a complete wall-to-wall renovation from the previous Lago Buffet and will likely become a culinary mainstay like the Carnival World Buffet, which opened over two decades ago." - Chris Rauschnot, The Huffington Post

So good ol' rich Caesar decided he was bored of his crapLago Buffet [finally] and decided to do something with his endless stack of pure and unadulterated cash to fix the main culinary mess in his own backyard. Although having expected much less, pumping $17 million just means that from launch and to a certain extent of time...this buffet is going to be - for lack of better words - G.R.E.A.T. But this article also mentions the Carnival World Buffet (by the way, is no longer that great...) as a parallel, which serves one main point...this place will only be good for "so long". SO GET YOUR GLUTTON ARSE OVER HERE QUICK...while it is still this freaking G.R.E.A.T.

Service is great as the staff definitely display their enthusiasm to work at the "best buffet" in Vegas (loved how the cashier reiterated that to us SEVERAL times). Need refills? It comes automatically. Need your plates to disappear? No, you don't need to chuck it under the table...they efficiently disappear on their own - even if you're a speedy little punk like me (gone and back within a minute with another full plate).

So after coming here several times for both lunch and dinner, I would recommend lunch if you don't want to break your wallet since the difference between both meals is minimal. If you have the 24-hour-Buffet pass, please note that you'll need to pay an extra $16'ish bucks per entry.

Summary of my main LIKES (this is what I come here for):

- EVERYTHING AT THE CARVING STATION: really tender and juicy prime rib, fall off the bone baby back ribs, luscious lamb chops, sausages and more!
- Steamed crab legs
- Fresh raw oysters: one of few times I would recommend RAW oysters at a buffet (additional Japanese version at dinner)
- GIANT cocktail shrimps...holy crap, these are the 5-8/lb types!
- Ginseng chicken soup and Chinese BBQ (especially the char siew...gives Sam Woo a run for its money - now that's something)
- Cheese and prosciutto section (used these on my salads)
- Bottled fruit juices (lunch only)
- DESSERTS: non-sweetened desserts such as the cheesecake was a plus for me!

Caesar made the right decision with his "back-anal" (bacch-anal) investment and is definitely raking in the profits once again to Rome. 

I definitely RECOMMEND this Vegas buffet (for now - before it eventually ends up like Carnival World Buffet)!

This is the King of Buffets. Or should I say Emperor.  Caesar's Palace set out to create pure decadence and gluttony and succeeded on so many levels.  Of course the ancient romans had the vomitoriums ( a practice frowned upon in modern day Vegas) and could probably eat much more than we can.  I don't even mind the price or the long lines. Realistically, to get the same quality food for dinner you would pay as much if not more per person and have far less food. Here is the best tip ever.  If you want to pay only 27 dollars per person and have almost no line, do midweek lunch.  You will miss the fresh crab legs and a few carving choices but the rest of the food is amazing from the lobster bisque and clam chowder, shrimp and grits, fresh Italian meat choices, Wagyu Beef sliders that are the best sliders I have ever tasted.  The waitresses are pleasant but the best staff members are those behind the counter making the food and explaining it to the customers.  Don't be afraid to ask.

My favorites are:

Italian Meats - 7 varieties of salami, proscuitto, etc.  The cheese selection is a little thin and could use a soft cheese choice.

The oriental duck and pork - right next to the sushi. (BTW yesterday I had some amazing shrimp tempura sushi.)

Wagyu Beef Sliders and Sweet Potato Tots.

Chicken Wings

Lobster Bisque and Clam Chowder

Shrimp Gritz

Paella

Specialty sausage

Slab bacon. (don't ask, just try it. And don't worry about the calories).

The desert bar is a treat of its own with amazing gelato flavors and a seemingly endless variety of chocolate delights.  They have watermelon mint, sour cherry, spicy chocolate, etc.

For dinner they have king crab legs made right in front of you, more meat variety including Lamb and Veal, and well, more food.

This is the finest buffet in Vegas and in my top 10 of Vegas dining must goes.
Muy Muy Delicious. Best Mexican food I have had in Vegas WOW.  Loved the Gorditas, Carnitas and Salsa's. Desserts were great too.  Taking my Family from California back tomorrow.

I always laugh at people who obviously know zero about restaurants and food post reviews.
For people who say this buffet is to expensive, you're wrong, the ingredients the chef is using are very expensive. Try costing out the carving station alone. 
Have been a chef and general manager for over 35 years and these guys do an exceptional job. If you feel it's too much money you have 2 feet be a big boy or girl and don't eat there, old town has plenty of cheap buffets for you folks.
And guess what you can ask to see the food before you enter, If you are a vegan check it out before you go. I just get so tired of listening to people whine about how it wasent this and it was not that, people grow up its a buffet, I have dropped a thousand dollars for dinner before that's when I become upset when everything is not perfect, not for friggin 50 buck buffet. 
Have never had a bad meal here, and the staff.while not outstanding was quite good.

I have been here a few times and find it to be the best casino buffet on the strip. The soft shell crab and hot Alaskan king crab are by far  the best I have had in any buffet. Price is a bit on the high side for sure. But it is a must try at least once if you are in Vegas.

I am on the waiting list for the Sterling buffet and will update once I have tried that. But to be fair it is $95 compared to $65 at Ceasars.

Definitely worth the 1.5 hour wait! Almost EVERYTHING was delicious...well seasoned and flavorful. I highly recommend the lamb chops and the seafood station (crab legs YES PLEASE!). The desserts are also nice and one of the few buffets that actually offer mochi, as well as cute cake pops. Desserts are also not cloyingly sweet, and it cools off the palate comfortably, rather than a shock of sugar. Macarons (blueberry, pistachio, coffee, and orange) are flavored from the filling; the outside shell is all the same almond flavor, just colored differently so do note that. 

Things I don't recommend, since some things are not as awesome (understandably so, as there is a LOT of stuff to eat). I would not get the sushi, as it is mostly rice and not much else. The seaweed has an overly fishy taste to it, and some of the sides were not that great (guacamole is only meh). Of course, these are all rather minor, and rest assured that the main stars of the show are all as delicious as they look (meats and seafood). Dessert-wise, everything was pretty decent, but I did not like the custard cups (one is passionfruit and the other is some blue-purple cup-boysenberry or blackberry?) and some of the ice creams seemed a bit diluted (thai tea had barely any flavor). 

If I were to go again--rather, if I want to bust my pants again (6 plates, 4 dessert this time), I would attempt to binge less on desserts and load up on more seafood. Alas, I have a sweet tooth, so we shall see...

A foodies wet dream! Over 500 items. And none are 'throwaway' items. Each seemingly prepared with full attention. Any of the items can easily be featured at a four star restaurant. So much too choose from. Worth the $50 plus especially when a lot of the other dining establishments cost a pretty penny and you don't get what you pay for. Definitely must be checked out on your next visit.

Good quality food.   Go for dinner with better selection.  I had the brunch and when leaving noticed the dinner had beautiful fresh oysters.  Not the little ones.  Nice big and very fresh looking.  Crab is excellent.  Service was only reason not five stars. Short staffed. Have to wait for drink refills and clearing used plates.  Didn't remove used plates for over 15 minutes.

It's pretty good for a buffet - but for the price? Maybe not... It's actually quite small for a buffet in my opinion, but quality I do see is a bit higher than some of it's competitors. Lines can get a bit crazy so try to get there early, duh! However, both times I went I had a fairly large group, about 6-8 people and we waited maybe 20mins total which isn't bad considering that some of the ticket times come out with a 90min wait time!

STEAMED CRAB LEGS - IF you're the type to grab plates on plates of crab legs - this place is for you! I'm not one of those people, but I'll admit that the steamed crab legs are pretty good!

PRIME RIB and all the other meat section - pretty decent! They had prime rib, sausage, ribs, etc. and they were all tasty.

ASIAN section was ok - I don't really go to this section at a buffet just because I'm Asian and eat it on a weekly basis.. but the sushi/sashimi section ain't bad either. Pretty decent in quality for a buffet.

NOODLE SECTION - Ramen, udon, pho - all pretty good! It's a decent size bowl and they have all the condiments on the side for you.

BREAKFAST/BRUNCH - this area was ok. I've seen benedicts, waffles, pancakes, etc. and they were all decent. They even had chicken & waffles and they were presented really cute, but it seemed dry so I steered clear of it. I saw lox, and although I love lox & bagels, I don't waste my belly on this. 

DESSERT - MY FAVE SECTION of all time.. their selection is decent. I like how they have a whole gelato bar to choose from and all the flavors I've tried have been pretty good. They even now offer thai tea floats, not sure if it's that good though cuz I really only trust south-east asian people to make it right.

One thing I do like though is the bottomless mimosa's they offer during the day, woohoo!
It's alright.  A lot of the food is flavorless.  The dessert is better than most of the other offerings.  Wicked Spoon is way better.

This was by far the best buffet we have ever been to! Don't let the price scare you - it is worth every penny! There was nothing we tasted that was bad. The service was impeccable. The ayce crab legs are served steaming, as the chef pulls them out of the hot water for you. Don't miss the sweet potato tater tots - I'm still craving them. This is my new go to place whenever I find myself in Vegas. Delicious!!

This was a great buffet! Lots of options to choose from, with fresh food at all the stations, and helpful waitstaff. Top dishes we tried include: Mac & Cheese, Assorted cheeses, Bottomless Mimosas, Smoked Trout, Pork Belly, and the Shrimp Tart. I like going to a buffet to try different dishes and this had plenty of variety. My husband and I thoroughly enjoyed trying several new dishes, our tastebuds were pleased! The price is a little high but we are thrifty people so take that for what it's worth. :)

FINALLYYYYYYYYYY got to try this place Christmas 2014 after trying to come here for dinner last year Christmas 2013.  We expected to wait in line, but not for 6.5hrs!!!!  That is the only reason I deducted a star. 

I did like the fact that they had a kiosk where you can take a ticket so you didn't have to physically wait in line. What I didn't like is that the wait time was not accurate on the ticket.  I checked in at 3:30pm and the wait time said it would be 676 min wait which would be approx. 11hrs!!!  Because of this my mom and I had NO idea when we would be seated.  We ended up getting seated at 10pm and have 30 minutes to eat before they started taking away the food. 

However, those 30 minutes were pure heaven. Everything was so fresh and of such high quality.  Every minute was pure bliss.  Staff was very friendly as well.  My friends asked me if it was worth the wait, and I say "yes" only because I had been wanting to try this since last year, BUT if I wanted to try it for the 2nd time, I probably wouldn't come on Christmas. BEWARE!!  HOLIDAY WAITING PERIODS ARE APPROX 6HRS!!! 

I would come on a regular day and be willing to wait 2 hrs max or pay the additional fee for the express pass.

The Caesars buffet seats a total of about 3,500 people per night, you can expect some pretty crazy wait times for the buffet, I wanted nearly 90 minutes on a Saturday night. If the line is extremely long, instead of cuing up, they will send you a text message when it's time to get in line. From the time you get in line to the front, it's about an additional thirty minutes. Now onto the food, I had the opportunity to eat at the Bellagio as well as Caesars both rated as one of the best buffets in Vegas.  The Caesars buffet has a lot more variety than Bellagio but I did find the Bellagio quality better than Caesars. Caesars focuses more on fish items than meat items. Of course Caesars has lamb chops, steak, prime rib, crab and shrimp, all which are really good. The hamburger sliders, definitely need some work or should be taken off the menu, they are dry, overcooked and lacking flavor.  When it comes to the dessert bar, Caesars blows away the Bellagio, their dessert bar is massive with a lot of great selections. The Caesars buffet is about ten dollars more than the Bellagio.

Absolutely sensational!
Ate baby lamb chops and peking duck till i was pleasantly stuffed! Everything at this buffet is chef quality!

Been here about three times. Food is good because so many people eat here, that there's always a new serving of food. Being that this place is busy and crowded at almost all hours of the day, I see that the staff is so busy that refills for drinks are hard to come by. 

Overall a I've had a good experience here

3 stars for variety and dessert but not for the taste. Been here 2 years ago when it was just 2 months after opening. It was very good, it WAS. Took my parents here expecting king crab leg but they didn't have it, on a Sunday night, I paid $53+tax. Without the king crab leg, it just a regular buffet. When I was here before, the chef helped the customer heat up the king crab leg in the boiling water, now they just do it for snow crab leg and let the crab leg sit in the pot until you ask for it. Almost every food taste very salty, hot and sour soup is bitter after simmering all day. Steamed bun is crusty because no lid covering. So, if you really want, you can ask or walk in to see if they have king crab leg before you pay for nothing.

May be a bit pricey! Spent $250. For 4. But I will go out on a limb and say that this is one of the best place that I've he ever had a buffet at. The food is the best I've tasted & it is well taken care of. the food was actually hot instead of just warm. they also have 5 different sections of food to chose from not including dessert. if your looking for a great hostess, ask for Lupe G. She is outstanding and takes very good care of you. hope this helps with anyone's food decision.

We came on a Thursday Morning some time around 10:00 am. We didn't have to wait long in line or to be seated. Apparently it was on the slower side this particular morning and for that we were grateful, specifically due to the fact we were told most people wait up to an hour and a half. The service was impeccable, the chefs were so inviting and polite I would recommend 10/10 I really enjoyed my experience here.

Amazing selection of food and great atmosphere.  Largest buffet I've ver seen.  The dessert part was my favorite.  Huge selection of sweet goodies.  Gave it four stars instead of I've or 2 reasons.  #1 - Cost, $46 per person.  Seems a tad steep to me.  #2 - some of the food was crap.  Slider buns were hard and the boiled shrimp was dry and horrible.
Great food!  Fantastic ceviche, crab legs, prime rib!  Huge selection of desserts and they are awesome!  Worth the money as the food is excellent.

Food 5 out of 10.
Price is high.
Wait time is long.
Service was better then average.
Seating was comfortable.
Place was PACKED!
Overall... DISAPPOINTED!  
I felt duped by the other Yelp reviews. I seriously don't understand what others see so positive in this place?

$60 buffet ($140 for two w/tip) to wait 30-130min to eat within a 2hr allotted time limit as it states on the receipt! You have to use a touch screen kiosk to be summoned via text 60-90min later or pay $25 to skip ahead to the pay line. There you have to wait 20-30min just to pay! Then wait 10min to be seated!

I can't eat $60 worth of routine buffet food for it to be worth it. Like any buffet you can always find something you like but for $60, 80% of the food should be spectacular. I'd say maybe 5% of the food was good, 40% was fair & 55% bad. GOOD: was turkey, cheeses, deli meats desserts, FAIR: was the Dungeness cold crab, Asian, meats, Mexican foods. POOR: was the hot soggy crab, gelatinous chicken feet, tomato bisque, grilled cheese, breads & most of the cold salad dishes. 

THE FEAST buffet at GREEN VALLEY STATION is $8 breakfast or $17-$28 and is BETTER than this place with far less wait times and better, cleaner, more artistic décor!
.

STUDIO B buffet at the M Casino $17-$40 with free beer & wine and BETTER buffet food! The decor is very nice and the casino is more pristine. Wait times of 40-60min.
Carnival World Buffet at the RIO Casino is $22-$30 with the largest selection of all but the décor is not as nice. This place is busy with wait times of 40-60min.
It was good but was like herding cattle the place was packed. We ate at the Wicked Spoon the night before and the food quality was much better.

Truly a buffet worthy of the Gods! Everything was great except the price. At $55 a pop you really need to get after the king crab legs and stone crabs to get your money's worth. Great selection of sushi, Asian, Italian, and desert bar! Super clean and fresh...definitely best on Vegas strip...,
I went for the Sunday Champagne Brunch and enjoyed this brunch very much.  The food was very well prepared and the fresh juice bar set this buffet above the rest.  Definitely worth the price.

Electronic check in at 330, in line at 630, sitting at 830. Never even received a text and they do not check. This system is a complete joke. 

No food can make up for these shenanigans.

This is a great spot for brunch or dinner. It's huge, but it still gets busy. Wait time can range from 45 mins- 2 hours on the weekends when they are busy. It all depends on the group size. 

The design is very modern. What's great about this buffet is that there is so much variety. There's a section for all types of food around the world. American, Asian, Mexican,... you get the point. There is something for everyone, so at the end of the day everyone's tummy is happy. 

Service is okay. Sometimes I've had very attentive service, and other times I had the opposite having to keep looking for someone just to get a drink. 

I'm not gonna lie, I've been going here every time for brunch the last several times I've gone to vegas. It's that good!
Not to mention the awesome dessert bar at the end of the meal!

I'm eating as we speak! It's so good that I ha to write a review! Great selection of food! Seafood, soup, meats, and everything in between. I suggest you come with empty stomachs because you won't stop eating!

I've tried all the major buffets in Vegas except for the Wicked Spoon (next time?) and Bacchanal is by far way better than the rest.  Standouts include the Asian, breakfast and seafood.  This is the only Vegas buffet where I never get tired of trying something unusal.  Add smiling and happy to be there staff and wonderfully sunlit dining space, I could spend a day here and it feels so relaxing rather than rushed and hectic like the other buffets.  A truly worthwhile experience.

I only eat at buffets on vacation in Vegas (and only for breakfast/brunch). Ive been to vegas a few times, and as such, I've been to a few different buffets. In my 7 years of coming to Vegas, I can truly say this one is my favorite. We went at 10 am on a Friday and there was no wait to get inside. The food was being properly replenished and things were kept in a cleanly manner. Many of the items are in their own containers (chicken and waffles, pasta, etc). The price point for breakfast is on par with many of the other smaller buffets in Vegas. The variety of the food was vast (though I have to admit I did not try many of the Asian dishes as it was all at the far end of the buffet and I had already had enough on my plate(s) by the time I made it to that side.

Looked at the pictures and reviews thought it would be great. If you are hungry and can eat their food you may find it reasonable. The quality of the food was not that good, in fact i could only eat the fruit. Even the choice of the fruit was limited and not that great. Very busy and reminded me of a luxury style cafeteria.
The buffet selection is great! Fresh seafood, sushi, pizza and lots of different dishes to chose from. The desert and gelato bar is awesome. Definitely worth the money.

Vegas brunches are notoriously amazing, and Bacchanal does not disappoint! We came here on St Patrick's day, so it was understandably crowded. We had the Groupon deal for brunch before 10AM, which worked out well for us to get us out the door early and beat the massive crowds. They jacked up the bottomless drink special price to $24, but most of our party still thought that was reasonable. Of the 8 of us, 6 purchased the deal, but our servers were awesome and basically let us all partake in bottomless mimosas. 

The seafood selection is bomb! The pre-cracked crab- both Dungeness and Alaskan King- were cooked perfectly and served with a vat of warm delicious butter. That was a definite win. Lobster eggs Benedict was amazing. The dessert area had ready to order crepes, fresh gelato, cookies, and pastries. Nutella crepe with an assortment of toppings was amazing, also loves the churros with hot caramel sauce. There are so many sections of different types of food, I am confident there is something delicious for everyone!  

Will definitely be coming back to this brunch on a future Vegas trip!

We've eaten here twice with the Groupon deal and while the food is great the Groupon deal was not a deal at all. The regular price for brunch is $39.99 and the Groupon deal works out to be $44 plus you have to pay tax when you get there. We've complained and nobody seems to care they are doing this...

One of my favorite buffets in Vegas, I come here mostly for the seafood and the prime rib, but they have basically have an international selection of food. The prime rib is cooked to amazing perfection - the meat is tender, much like the steak you'd get at fancy steakhouses. Their crab legs are fresh too. There is also a wide variety of desserts - basically anything you can hope for. 

The wait is usually very, very long, so now they have a fastpass system so there's not a huge crowd of ppl in front of the restaurant.

I wasn't overly impressed by this place. I went in using the groupon for their breakfast and they ended up charging us tax on the full normal price, why??? Our groupon was $60 but they taxed us on $160, the full price?? Again idk what the hell was going on but this place was just not worth it to me. The only upside was the unlimited mimosas so I made sure I got my money's worth. A deal that supposed to cost 25 a person ended up as 45, so pretty much you're paying the full normal price just to get free cheap alcohol. Also it was breakfast only so the food was very mediocre. I don't blame groupon at all because this was simply the misleading doings of baccanal's buffet. If I'm gonna spend $30+ on a meal again, i'll do it at all you can eat sushi. Not for some salad, few claws, eggs, and toast.. Maybe i'll come back when they have a real deal that is not misleading during their dinner times? But until then, I don't think i'll ever return, it's just not worth the money at all.

An expensive buffet with sub par food and service.

We went to this buffet with an expectation of excellence, but only to encounter a rude greeter, a forgetful waitress, salty food, limited choice, and an environment equivalent to a $20 buffet.

For $42/person for lunch, we expected a lot more, especially when Wynn is charging under $30.

We are every disappointed and will not visit again.

Waaaaah.... *heavenly music plays*

THE HOLY GRAIL OF BUFFETS!

With so many buffets in Vegas, it's hard to pick just one to eat at. My stomach only has space for ONE buffet while I'm visiting Vegas. Forget that 24 hour buffet pass. You'll find me passed out in the middle of the buffet tray if I ever tried doing that. 

The Wicked Spoon used to be my #1 stop, but then I heard Ceasar's Palace had the next great thing. I had to check out it out!

And then there was the line........... O_O

Just when you thought the line was over, there was another line. The hubby and I waited an hour and a half until we were seated. According to the employees there, that wait time was SHORT. Over two hours is the norm.

The buffet is normally about $40/person with lunch being cheaper, but because we were there during Thanksgiving, they had a "holiday price" of $55/person. Bah humbug. 

Once we got inside, we were just OVERWHELMED. Sooooo much food. Soooo many people! There was every kind of Asian cuisine, Italian, Mexican, American... eeeeeeverything. 

The most popular (and longest!) line was the line for the king crab legs. You can have them cold or have them warmed up by the staff. They'll give you a good amount at a time, but you know one visit just isn't enough! I can feel my cholesterol rising... The crab is fresh and tender. Definitely get them warm instead of cold!

The freshly sliced prime rib is awesome! You can tell them what temperature you want and they'll try their best to find the slice closest to it. You can even ask for one of the prime rib bones if you dare to man handle it!

If you love foie gras, try the foie gras soup! Totally droooolworthy!

Don't forget to check out the made-to-order noodle soup station! You can get beef pho, wonton soup or ramen. The ramen was my fave! I thought it was going to taste like some fancy packaged ramen, but it tasted really close to authentic Japanese ramen. The pork was so tender.

When it came to dessert, I was suuuuuper stuffed. But I had to try a bite of everything they had to offer. The Jean Phillippe macrons they had were amazing. I kept going for more and more and more. I even slipped some in my bag to take home. SHHH!

But the most amazing, most fabulous, jaw-dropping dessert they had was their FLAN. Who doesn't love flan? It was so creamy, so flavorful, SO FREAKING GOOD! Even though I was beyoooond full, I ate more than two of them. Not too sweet. Just the right soft, yet slightly dense, texture. I could eat it all day long!

This is definitely a top contender for buffets. I didn't think they could surpass The Wicked Spoon, but they did and then some! Definitely worth checking out! Just bring a snack with you while you're waiting in the two hour line to get in. The price and wait time almost makes it not worth it, but if you only have money/time for one buffet, make it this one!!

This is by far the best buffet in Las Vegas. Everything you try is one of the best you have ever had. Even something trivial like the mashed potatoes are amazing.  Look forward to coming here each time I am in Vegas.  Place is a little expensive, but worth every bite.

Among the best buffets that I have had in Vegas. Very close to Wynn and Cosmo. The seafood of both snow and Alaskan crab was awesome, service was great, shrimp was huge. Yes it is expensive, pay the extra money! I went to sister property Rio or the seafood buffet the same weekend and it was similar in price and was absolute garbage.

We had 5:30 dinner tonight 12/21/16, the Service was poor, seats was not  comfortable they put too many seats in the dinning areas, the foods was average, oyster was not freshness( this is second times we had) i don't recommend this$75 dinner at all.

Food is good but it's a long wait on Saturday.  Also some people in our group were upset over 18% tip charge for large party at a buffet.  Again food is good but you also pay for good service and a wonderful time and having people upset over tip issues takes away from the experience.  If service merits 18% at buffet, no one would have cared.   But service not that great.  Probably will not return.  There are much better places for $40 a person with full service where 18% or more gratuity is well deserved.   If you are a small group the tip issue is of no concern.

I've gone here three times and it's still my favorite Vegas buffet. They have so many different types of food such as ramen, truffle mash potatoes, clam/mussel buckets.  They even have a station where you can bring your crab legs for them to boil for you.  I thought that was pretty cool.  The truffle mashed potatoes were also delicious.  There's a station where you can order noodle soup.  They even have Chinese chicken herbal soup which was alright.  At $50+/person, it's kinda steep but for the quality of food you get, it's worth it.

After reading the hype once Caesar's Palace decided to upgrade Cafe Lago, I made a point on my next trip to Vegas to visit Bacchanal Buffet, which happened to be for breakfast ($25 with a Total Rewards card).  Overall, I liked the modern feel of the space with plenty of tables for large groups (8+) and somewhat uncharacteristic lounge music playing in the background.  The food, though, was pretty standard (and bordering on outright disappointing) in terms of breakfast/brunch buffets.

To start with, Total Rewards Diamond and Seven Stars members get little signs as they are walked through the restaurant that are placed at their table.  While perhaps off-putting to an outsider, it is interesting to see how you are more likely to see the elderly, stingy video poker playing couple or upper-middle aged overweight blackjack/craps player eating by themselves than, for instance, Jay Gatsby in a tuxedo.  It goes to show that gambling in Las Vegas doesn't look quite like what the mailers picture it to be.

I digress.  As I mentioned before, the breakfast food was pretty standard with the highlight being the carving station featuring brisket, ham, and a variety of what they termed "artisanal sausages."  Mind you, the sausages themselves--which usually had some extra spices or other ingredients mixed in--were just okay.  

Other sections of the buffet try to put out individual servings of popular dishes but end up failing miserably.  Corned beef hash in a 2-inch bowl with a tiny egg (nice touch) but a scant few traces of corned beef among the potato shreds was a disgrace.  Chicken and waffles as a quarter Belgian waffle and a chicken wing is just wrong.  The mini-pancakes were dry, though they did a slightly better job with the French toast.  The Asian section had some steamed pork buns and basic Chinese food.  I would have loved to have seen some freshly cooked fish choices for those looking for more of a Japanese-style breakfast.

On the plus side, I did like the large selection of juices served in individual-sized glass milk bottles.  It's more visually appealing and keeps the crowds moving faster than a Minute Maid dispenser or a couple of large carafes for self-service.

While the overall environment (i.e., everything except the food) is top-notch, in my opinion, the breakfast offerings at Bellagio and Paris's buffets are superior.  In reality, though, if your level of play starts to get items taken off the hotel bill, your choice of breakfast buffet should be dictated by where you're staying or doing most of your gambling.  I don't think any buffet in Vegas is so much better than the others as to overcome the presumptive choice of free food.

Great service and food. Had their weekday brunch today and it was amazing. Staff has an A+ in customer service. Especially one of the servers Javier. He was great and made sure we were taken care of. Thank you for the great experience. Cheers!

I went here for the breakfast buffet. The ambiance was quite nice with quiet music in the background. The brunch itself was more like a 4.5 in my opinion. I had eaten at The Wicked Spoon the day before and it was quite good but I believe Bacchanal did the same thing a little nicer and with better food. It was a dollar more and there weren't quite as many seafood options but the ones they did have were better and they might have more if you catch them when they are transitioning to lunch. The fresh juice (8 varieties) was nice and I think you had to order at TWS. Try the steak and eggs first if you like that sort of thing because you will want to hit that a few times.
Great food I pigged out, it's a great new place to check out, must go!

Best buffet! So much good food of many different genres. I love they portion many in small dishes so it is easy to get just a taste and try many new things. The barbecue was delicious as was the seafood, especially the steam crab legs. The dessert bar was amazing and fresh rambutan fruit too! They had Chinese food, sushi, Italian and southern home cooking among other styles of food available. Juice bar was good too. Service was quick and friendly.

I don't know what else I can say, go look at the pictures. What I like the most is that they have a huge selection of ethnic food.  It's pricy but worth it. It's always something I look forward to whenever I come to Las Vegas, definitely the best buffet in town. Can't leave without trying it. I always ate until I can barely walk.

2 stars becauses the food is fantastic. We had the champagne brunch today, and it was great. The best desserts, great meats and awesome seafood. 

We were dissapointed, however, by our waitresses behavior. 

As we were getting up to leave, our server saw us and walked over. She picked up our check and loudly asked us if we needed change, which we did not. Keep in mind you pay for everything before you eat here. Then she said "I didn't see anything on the check." It became obvious she was asking for a tip. As we left and were not walking out, she sarcastically told us to havbe a great day. Extremely rude and not acceptable when you are paying close to $50 a person for a weekend lunch.

Buffets quite good here.  I was expecting more variety considering price but nonetheless it was good.  They had quite a bit of seafood variety and the Mexican section was good.  Sushi was sooo as it was not very fresh.. Typically what you would get at a buffet.  Service us quite fast here.  Wait times can take easily an hour if you don't reserve a spot at nights..

We know why this place is rated so high. Hands down the best buffet joint in LV. Wicked Spoon and Belagio you are going to have to step up the game. Cool check in process that you enter your name and phone number on the kiosk and then will text message you to come pay when eating time gets close. This way you can wander around or play a couple hands. Trust me when I say it's better than standing around in a line like cattle.
 Great selection of fresh seafood, meats and the dessert section is sweet! You'll have to see for yourselves all the food this place has to offer and the service we recieved was just over and beyond. Modern decor and a nice layout for you to move around. The only problem we had was trying to get our $50 worth. Going price for a top buffet joint on the strip but well worth the experience.

Is the best buffet??? I think it is overrated and overpriced for dinner. They had some decent vegetarian options, but even my meat eater companion wasn't too impressed. I liked the gelato for dessert.
Place was pretty empty before 5pm if you don't want to stand in line. Price is $52/pp for dinner. They take your photo and charge you $20 if you like it. They offer to you while your eating...There's a 2hr time limit on your meal.

Waited about 15 mins for dinner on Saturday evening around 7pm. The lines were hecka long but we opted to pay the extra $15/person for express.  Totally worth it for us.  

Typical buffet with meat, seafood, mexican, asian, italian and american.... the quality of the food is a lot better than most vegas buffets...The lambchops were superb!!! Crab legs were good... The Asian food was Bleh. The sushi Bleh. The Italian food was alright...  The fresh juices were good. The dessert bar was delicious with a good variety. 

Overall the quality of the food is good and worth the price you pay. Would go back.

I have been here twice and will definitely not be back. I should have listened to other reviews that were saying ot had went down hill. My first time was in 2014 and it was amazing the food was hot and fresh and was quite literally the best thing i had eaten. This time around not so much food was served luke warm i had to keep apologizing to my guests as I had assured them it would be money well spent, well not the case. This time around the best thing was desert. Oh and swevice was very good. Do not waste your time or money.

This buffet was highly recommended to me as the best buffet in Vegas. I did the Spice Market Buffet the night before so this was definitely a big step up.
The service was great and the line moved fast. They do a cheesy buffet photo that they try to sell you later for $25. I think this really downgrades the experience. 

The highlights for me were the hot and cold crab stations, custom made taco station and asian noodle soup station. The dessert station has chocolate covered strawberries and macaroons, which I thought was very unique. They also had delicious juices and drinks at the Mexican station. 

Overall, I think this is something everyone should experience once if you can. It's very expensive at $50 per person base + tax + tip, which makes it $65 per person (if you are Canadian the exchange makes it over $70 each, which could be a nice meal somewhere else). If you eat a lot, you can get your monies worth. However, I'm sure the majority of people don't so it's mostly for the experience.
OMG this is the best buffet in Las Vegas. The best quality of meat & the variety of food is just perfect. And the dessert bar holy-moly is heavenly!!!!!

Easily one of the best buffets in Vegas and one of the newest additions. I was waiting and waiting to go try this place and finally had the opportunity to do so, but of course it was done with a hangover.. so I want to try to give this place the best review I can under the circumstances that I was in. I tried a bit of everything even if it meant a few bites of one thing and a whole bowl of pho. Yes, pho.. and it was good too! Probably the best thing there that day, and it cured the hangover but I still didn't eat much of the other stuff. Everything was really high quality though and explains the price of the buffet. I would definitely like to go back and try it when I am "normal" again.

I went March 15, 2013 for dinner.

It wasn't worth $50+.

It wasn't worth spending all that time in line. (There was a general line, a line behind the cashier, then a line to wait in to be seated, then there was another line for meat at the carving station). and we went when it was "dead".

The highlights....waygu sliders, the giant shrimp, the pecan pie bite, carrot cake, vanilla mochi ice cream. The wait staff was attentive and nice.

Not sure why they were playing house music. Maybe to make you eat faster???

I'm glad I got to experience the Bacchanal Buffet. I'd go back only if somebody else really wanted to go, but I wouldn't go during dinner or pay another $50+.

Honestly one of the best buffets I've ever gone to!!

Although the price is a little on the steep side especially that of dinner, their food options more than make up for it. Be prepared to eat, so my suggestion is starve yourself so you can fill yourself up with the delicious food (I'm kidding! Kinda). 

You first have to pay to get into the food area, so be ready to dish out the mula before you get to feast your eyes on the banquet of food. They'll take a picture of your group after you pay, which you'll have the option of buying towards the end of your meal. Upon being seated by your server who'll ask you for your drink option (you can also order alcoholic drinks!), you're free to run wild and grab food to your hearts content. There's pretty much a section for all types of food, Asian with the pho, sushi, curry, and others; then there's seafood with the lobster legs, clams, shrimp, etc.; Italian, soup, and so much more. Not to mention their dessert bar, which is to die for. I'm a sucker for sweets, so seeing that they had a gelato bar, boba, mochi, cookie bar, and other delicacies made my heart palpitate. 

Awesome, awesome place to eat! If you're willing to pay for the goods, DEFINITELY recommend!!

First... This place is a little pricey, but the food is fantastic. Every dish we tried was tasty. The food was presented extremely elegantly. Each dish was seasoned to perfection. The ambiance is lively and the service was excellent. 

Each kitchen had delightful dishes. Each time we took a bite, we were amazed by the taste. 

The reason we rated it 4/5 was the price. $41 per person for lunch (including tax) was a bit much. 

Must do:
Crepe station
Gelato
Asian kitchen was the best!

I don't regret it, just wished it was a little cheaper.

Love it!! Food was great, service was good, I liked the prime rib, it was very tender and juicy! Also, the baked clams were delicious, I got the banana cream sorbet for dessert with a crepe and powder sugar on it! Loved it all!! The price was reasonable for visiting during the weekdays, it was 55 for adults and 25 for kids. The waiting did take an hour but it was worth it!

Decking time around, 6 pm on a Saturday. And man!!! What a mistake lol. We had to wait 2+ hours to get seated, and we didn't think we would be in jeopardy of missing our 9pm concert, but we were.

The system is kinda jacked up, I know they are trying their best but you got different VIPs going through on the left, big groups of 8+ on the right, groups of 2 maybe faster than 3-5...

Anyways we waited a long time, I guess that made the food even better, but we had to rush. The service is great though.

I tried a lot of things including, brisket, sausage, dim sum, Korean BBQ (galbi), mac n cheese, mashed potatoes, baked beans, pork ribs, beef ribs, fried rice, steamed crab legs, cold crab legs, stone crab, and shrimp, and crawfish, and some deserts.

My favorite was the Korean BBQ and beef rib, my least favorite might have been the cold stuff or the crawfish, seemed like dead crawfish. And the cold stuff felt like icicles on em.

But the rest of the food is really good imo, still probably the best buffet in town.
Always never disappoint. All my first timer friends love it. Excellent food and atmosphere.

My favorite buffet place in Las Vegas. Always crowded , I need to wait 1 or 2 hours to eat here. But trust me , its worth the wait. If you guys come to Vegas , come to this place for buffet. Limit 2 hours eating.

There are many voices saying that Bacchanal isn't what it used to be, but that's besides the point. For me, the Bacchanal seems to be doing a good job defending its crown as the best buffet in Las Vegas. First, the place looks tremendous. Clean and crisp, artfully and tastefully decorated. It's very spacious with perhaps the broadest variety of offerings of any buffet. The execution is formidable as well, as the dishes taste like they were done to a high level of quality regardless of the vast hordes of people that they need to serve. People were getting customizations made to their seafood dishes and made to order tacos and crepes. On the downside, it is a very expensive buffet, and there's usually going to be a long line. I was short on time so I decided to splurge for the $35 upgrade to bypass the line only to find out that this only let me bypass some of it, not all of it. But it did cut my wait to somewhere between five to ten minutes from what would have assuredly been at least 45 minutes. But once I sat down and started eating all was forgiven. Here's what I ate:

Green tomatillo oyster shooter
Tiger prawns with clarified butter
Lobster bisque
Frutti di mare
Mac and cheese
Avocado lime pasta salad
Applewood smoked bacon
American wagyu beef
Key lime tart
Rum raisin bread pudding
Green tea cake
Chinese egg custard tart
Creme brulee
Pineapple juice
Peach green tea
Watermelon juice

Bacchanal Buffet is the THE BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS! We ate here two days in a row for the Brunch because it was so good! The freshest seafood, fresh cut meats, amazing sliders, sushi, taco bar, pizza bar and desserts to die for!!! They constantly are putting out freshly cooked food and always making sure the areas are stocked. 

It was all sooo good but the best part was customer service! 

We had brought our 3 small daughters with us and they were so accommodating! Our two strollers are quite large so we needed a large seating area. They didn't fuss at all (like some other restaurants did in which we left) and were so nice and friendly! I have never felt so relaxed and able to take my time eating! We will definitely be back next time we come to Vegas!

I really think this place is overrated or the quality has gone down. It was my first and also last time coming here. We were here for brunch. Not a lot of variety if you compare to Bellagio the Buffet. Food quality was not that great. Ramen broth was salty and noodle was not undercooked. Many dishes were left out for a long time and looked grossed. 
They do have nice decor though, very modern and appealing. The juices were good though. They came in many flavors in small cute bottles. 
I didn't touch the seafoods cause they are not fresh at all. 
It was my first time coming to a buffet wandering around not sure what to eat. 
This was a big disappointment.
