By far the best buffet in Vegas! I was in love with this buffet! It had pretty much everything!!!! The price was worth it! 43 per person was worth it for lunch but we got lucky because at 3 dinner started so we got there at 2:30 and got to enjoy both!!! 

I took advantage of every single station!! The Chinese food was bomb!! The fried calamari was one of my favorite ones!!!! But what I really love was the Mexican section! They had everhrjjng birria, pozole, tamales, sopes, tacos de asada pollo y pork. It was awesome! A lot of variety!!! A lot of selection! 

Seafood was great too!!! And the American food as well! I can't complain about anything! 
The orange juice was pretty fresh! One of the best juices I had tried on my life! 

Deserts were eve better!' Crepes were fabolous! Alor of different tipping and Ice cream flavors! The macarrones were delicious! The flan the cookies and everything!!! It was so yummy!!!! Everything everything. 

The service was fenomenal!! Always refilling our drinks!! 

I'll definitely come back when I go back to Vegas!

Good food selection and quality of good is much better than most buffets around. The ribeye I had was very dry but I got the end of it. My buddy had a fresh one and it was juicy. Nice venue, good selection, and quality. Well worth with it. The reason for only three stars is because the service we had was very poor. Cashiers made an error on check regarding gratuity and we said we'd pay cash but the person seating us rudely disregarded us and wouldn't seat us until that was fixed. Their fault anyways. Very rude service on that end. I am big on customer service and this one failed horribly.

Needless to say Bacchanal is one of my favorite buffets in Vegas, the service is fast and the line went by pretty quick... well it was 4pm when I ate there. 

The food was good! very limited selection though; however, the crab legs are amazing and served both chilled and hot! Yummy

I really enjoyed their small selection of meats and desserts. Would be coming back here for sure in the future.

This is truly the Mecca of Buffets! After waiting nearly a half hour in line for a 5:30pm dinner and shelling out over $60, I had high expectations to say the least. Happily, I have good news to report, it was all worth it. Plate after plate after plate of nothing but high quality, well prepared food. Quite the variety to choose from, everything from Stone Crab claws to BBQ'd Lamb Chops! To top it all off, the choices for desert look like they're straight out of nothing less than the fanciest bakery! Highly recommended if you think you've eaten at good buffets before, test that theory.

I've been hearing lots of goods from this buffet and finally here I am.  
It's alright.  They do have varity of selections.  Dessert dept. was very nice.  
Services excellent.  Not as expected though w/all the commotion.

It's already happening...the quality is going down.   Came here on a Tuesday night for dinner around 8:45 pm.  A 15 minute wait to the point of being seated; not bad. My appetite was building as I waited in line looking at the raw bar and the crab legs. I didn't get that the last time, because I came for lunch. 

With a bigger crowd than my lunch visit, I got a better feel for the weaknesses of this buffet when it is "packed".  The waiter was far less attentive than last time, he was missing the first 15 minutes after we were seated.  I waited to order our drinks and let my fellow diners go get their food.  However, my husband had a meatball accident...and the waiter brought a rag and club soda.  That was nice although it took him about another 15 minutes to get it.

Now about the buffet...
Again I love that for the most part they pre-portion food, so it "grab and move along".  However, the seafood bar is really not set up correctly.  The condiments and sauces are first, then the plates and then seafood.  People waiting in line (and there is always a line at the seafood bar) get down right angry cause it looks like you are cutting in line, but all you want are your condiments.   So about that seafood; I got oysters this time, and they were good but not great.  I guess I like a different type.  The crab legs....holy SALT! And I like salty, but I guess that is how they stop you from taking more than one plate.  So disappointing.

Meats- Impressed they had lamb chops, but they were, unfortunately, well overdone.  The prime rib was also a medium-well done; i prefer it rarer and asked for a med-rare piece but that was the piece I got.  

Mexican- I pick here and there.  Taking they carnitas, hot sauces, salsas and guacamole.

Italian/Pizza/Mediterranean-  I don't eat any starch, but it looked decent.  Hubby said pizza crust was a bit soggy though.

Asian- yeah. I finally made it this far, but none of it was impressive, but it was decent, better than most take out Chinese. Sushi- generic, but like they still offer it. 

Honestly, I think my favorite thing was the salad bar and cheese selection.

I actually walked away this time, not stuffing myself. That is a first. Anyway, I STILL think this is the best buffet on the strip, but I think I won't be back unless any out-of-town guest ask to go to a buffet.

This is by far my favorite buffet in vegas. The wait is always pretty long but we were able to get in within a reasonable amount of time on a Friday. There's a lot of variety in there and the buffet itself stretches from one end to the other. This buffet is also one of the more expensive ones but I feel like the crab legs and oysters make it worth it. I like the noodle bar and raw bar the most. They also have a carving station with at least 5-6 types of meat to choose from. Aside from cold crab legs there are also steamed ones further down the line. 
The desserts are okay to me but there were still a lot of choose from. I liked the cheesecake and gelato but some of the coated things like cake pops and strawberries weren't as good due to the outside layer.
I took my parents to Vegas for the first time and all they talk about is the buffet. Our waiter was Jeff and was super friendly and made us feel at home. He made our experience so much better.

This place has gone downhill over the years tremendously!  My most recent visit will probably be my last!

When this place first opened few years ago, the food was amazing, the variety was outstanding, and even the presentation of the food was novel and wonderful and always brought a smile to my face.

Over the years , the food and the selection remained good enough to keep me coming back, but I definitely had noticed it slowly declining.  Now though, the experience itself has gotten so bad that I'm not sure I'll ever be back.

We went at 6pm on a Monday night.  The wait was 40 minutes to get in, but that was really ok; I pretty much expect that.  But this time, once we were inside there were more lines to wait on.  The seafood area, and carving board area both had huge lines.  In the past, there might be a slight wait before one could get through these areas, but on this night there was a loooong wait for both, which was very unpleasant.  Not only that, there were people that would get to the head of the line and then have friends and family members (that had NOT waited on line) come up with their empty plates, and would then fill those plates.  It was if mom was in her own kitchen serving her family members.  This of course added to the wait for the rest of us.

In addition, the service was awful.  In the past, the servers cleared plates quickly, were attentive, and refreshed drinks and water quickly, and would check as one started in on dessert and then offer coffee or whatever.  On this particular night, our plates piled up and were infrequently cleared.  Although, I did find a soda had been refreshed at one point while I was away from the table, I was never able to get my water refilled once, even though I had consumed the first glass upon arrival.  I also could never flag down someone to get coffee. And finally at one point, I realized that the table that was right next to us (very close), had been vacated by diners and then became the dumping ground where servers piled up dirty dishes.  Every inch was filled, and the pile was easily a foot high.  Not very pleasant.

I would say that the food is still fairly good, but the overall experience makes it NOT worth the price.  I'm wondering if it's just because they're letting in too many people at once.  I'm not sure this is the case, but my perception is that in the past, they controlled entry so that there were less people inside at once.  That would certainly make the individual food lines more reasonable, and give the poor overworked servers a chance to be able to keep up, and make for a MUCH better customer experience.

It is very expensive for a buffet, and I have come to the conclusion that my (same amount of) money would be better spent at one of the many, many Vegas restaurants where I would not waIt on line after line, enjoy a great meal, have attentive service and have a more civilized experience.

If you are a local or tourist, you have to at least try this one time! This is the mother of all buffets in Las Vegas! Although the experience is priced at $50 per person, you have a lot of varieties to stuff your face in to make your money's worth. Lol they have king crab and lobster there for all you seafood fanatics... What was really cool is that they provide a plate grip for you to keep because of the hot plates that are given to the guest. You would keep in mind that they perform sanitizing and disinfecting procedures to keep a safe and clean experience for the guest. I would definitely come back wit my family and friends who visit town or for special occasions.

Pretty good. Your average buffet. Long lines, avoid it if you can, not worth the wait. There are better buffets on the strip if you really want to eat in the area. It would be a 3 star restaurant if not for the insanely long wait

Waaay too overpriced. 60 bucks for a buffet with only one station offering meat that has a 30 min line, so what happens is that people end up filling up on noodles, rice, bread, salad and other stuff. I am sure that works out perfectly for the hotel. I pretty much paid $60 for some average chinese food.

My advice is don't waste your money on buffets at the strip, they are all crap and over priced, do what the locals do and go to the good spots outside the strip.

See my review of Inka Grill - Las Vegas. For a quarter of the price, far more superior food.

The selection here is amazing.   I tried to sample as much as possiblr, but the king crab captured my attention.  I had a baked spicy mussel that was over cooked, Johan crab that was good, but a tad over cooked, king crab and boiled shrimp that were excellent.   I had both chilled and boiled crab - both excellent.  I had the lamb chop - very good, brisquit - very good, baby back ribs - excellent and the prime rib- good.  I tried the sushi, it was ok.  The desert table finished off the meal with creme brulee was the perfect finish.  The drink service for those drinking alcohol was very good, I only wanted water and was nearly forgotten - so no tip for the waitress from me.  Overall a lot of fun.  I would go back.  Go early, the crowd builds after about 1845

The best buffet we have ever have. Too many options and we can't try all of them. I wish we could eat more. The only downside is that they don't have sashimi and the sushi is very limited. The craw fish is not that fresh.
Everything is top notch! Beautiful and elegant! Food is super fresh and tasty!  I will def be back whenever I visit vegas!

This is such a great buffet in Las Vegas. The food was so fresh and delicious. The seafood area and dessert was my favorite. I had the crab legs which was my favorite part. You can get hot ones at the Italian part. There is even dim sum choices in the asian section. They even make fresh tacos. The dessert bar......heaven. It's a bit pricy but it is worth it. My favorite place to eat!

Found something in my food it was gross it was Mushroom Truffle and had a big white piece of something in it!!! Food not very fresh sitting out a whole long time. Never coming here again! I definitely do not recommend try a different buffet. Dessert is the only thing pretty descent here.

the food were ok. There's not much selection. There are other buffets that offer more selections but  lesser price. We paid 35$ for lunch and honestly it's not worth it. 

The line to get the food is ridiculously long.. even in the dessert there was a line.. desserts not that great compared to M buffet. Again, not much choices. 

Our server is in a hurry to get our plate.. not because there's little left in the plate, it doesn't mean were done.. im trying to eat slowly so I wouldn't get full quick. If we're still holding the utensils we're probably not done yet.

Would I come back here? Maybe.. but its going to be a while
what can I say when you are looking for a Vegas Buffett (which I do not anymore) this is the place I would go . .food was eccletic wide variety and quite possibly the best buffet in vegas

Just visiting Las Vegas and my friend told me to try the buffet here. 
I must say I love this place so much. 
Here's what I like and recommend you to try
- steam crab
- taco
- sea snail
- ice cream moji

They serve a whole variation of food ranging from western to Italian to Asian. My most vivid memory were the shrimp dishes I had (dim sum, Thai,). If I didn't have self control i would have totally taken he whole wok back to my table. 
Price is high, but you're in Vegas.

Without a doubt, the best buffet in Vegas now.
No contest.
Puts other casino buffets to shame.

People reading this 3 months from now will think I'm a lying prick, but let this document serve as a testament that at this point in time and space, Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's is the most kick-ass buffet in town.

As we all know, things in Vegas have a way of changing, sometimes from minute to minute.  When the next mega-resort opens, the crown will certainly change, but it will definitely take a page from Bacchanal's playbook.

Caesar's has upped the bar for what Buffet's can and should provide.

It ain't cheap, over fifty bucks a head for dinner, but you get Kwality, with a capital "K"!
Rumor has it that Caesar's spent over $17million on the remodel and food upgrades.  The money was well-spent.  Selection is mind-boggling.  Most items are made in small batches to maintain quality and freshness.
I also like the fact that the kitchen seems to allow some discretion with the menu.  Not all the offerings are directed towards the Western palatte, and as many of the cooks are Mexican, Filipino, or Chinese, some offerings are more "ethnic" than what you'd expect.  I had a Mexican menudo soup that rivaled anything served at my local tacqueria!  When I told the timid midwesterner that it was tripe soup, she nearly fainted... 
I like that the kitchen takes chances like this.  All of their food may not appeal to the average joe, but there's interesting and tasty stuff on the menu if you keep your eyes and mind open.

During peak Vegas season, plan on eating at oddball times (e.g. 6am breakfast or 3pm dinner), if you don't like waiting in lines.  Otherwise, plan on at least a 2-3 hour wait.  Caesar's does have a neat computerized reservation kiosk that will text you when to return, but it only means that you return to a 30-40 minute line...

So either spend like a whale at Caesar's to get comped line passes, or plan accordingly.  You have been warned.

One warning, stay away from the peanut butter stuffed chocolate cookies at the dessert bar.  
Those little bastards are more addicting than heroin.

The food is good, the service is ok, the price is expensive, and the design all though pleasing to the eye, not good for accessibility. The sneeze guards and counters are so low unless your under 5 feet you have to really lean over to see what is under the counter. The salad and sushi area is the absolute worst for accessibility. I do love the little gourmet tapas they make in each area. They have a small chilled plate with a beat salad that is to die for!! I have to get like 2 or 3 of these and dump them on a bigger plate on some butter leaf lettuce every time I go. (this way i make it a large dinner salad.) They are always shucking fresh oysters, you usually need to wait but when you get them they are freshly shucked. They also make sure they keep them very cold which is a plus. If you like dim sum they have a variety, The spear ribs are very tasty, and the bun boa most of the time is very soft and steamed to perfection. They have so many deserts. So they do have small secret if you walk over to the desert area and ask for a soufflé they will make you  a personal one. I was not a fan of the soufflé and think they should work on the recipe a bit. But what an awesome idea. If they can perfect that soufflé and give it the right flavor, it would be perfect with some fresh vanilla ice cream. The reason I say the service is poor is because I have to ask for refills every time I go. I have a diamond status with this hotel which usually gets you better treatment. I love not having to wait in the line. That is a huge plus!! I'm a little spoiled with this. But once I'm inside the service is mediocre compared to the other establishments the property owns. I don't think it's the individuals working I just think it's not organized well. Oh and if you go to get your seafood, be careful because sometime the line curves right into a door that opens out from the kitchen. your food might get knocked out of your hand if you stand to close. I think a couple tweaks constructionally to the restaurant and it would be perfect. It totally beats the previous caesars buffet they had!!! You have to try it at least once.
short and sweet, great food that has a worldy culture for all your taste buds! try it out!

So far my favorite buffet here in Las Vegas! If not M buffet!
Great food and service!

We went this place on Friday lunch and Sunday night.
Friday lunch:  Our server and food were just great.   No complaints.  - 5 stars

Sunday dinner:  Our server was busy chatting with different people here and there.  It was so hard to ask even water.   Food was different quality from Friday lunch, though the price was much higher than Friday lunch.    Food was just average.  Meat was dry.   I assume good chefs and servers are off on Sundays.   - 2 stars

Bacchanal bacchanal...another new buffet in vegas, another chance to load up on tons of food and then waddle around vegas afterwards in overstuffed food happiness. Bacchanal buffet at Caesar's Palace definitely did not disappoint! It definitely lived up to its status as the newest best buffet of Vegas!

WHAT I LOVED
Clear viewing
The decor I thought was fantastic here. The tables and seating were the usual cushiness and niceties, but what really caught my eyes were the way they laid out the food. All the cooking areas were very easy to see through the clear glass and the setup of all the hot food was in a slightly diagonal pattern. I especially loved how they set up the dessert area with the glass jars filled with candy for the taking. 

Saving a few bucks
Join their rewards program and get a few dollars off the buffet price! Yeahh!!! It's a pricy buffet so every little bit counts. And the program really isn't that hard to join, they even ask you if you want to join it while you're waiting in line.

Carving Area
Ooof...all the meat that I got from here was pretty deliciouuusss! The lamb chops were great and the brisket was pretty amazing. I can't even remember all the other ones!!! They had a pretty wide selection and the man carving it was so nice too. 

Seafood Area
I kept coming back here again and again to grab small pots of seafood. Mussels, crabs, cocktail shrimp, seafood gazpacho etc etc. The best part about the buffet though is the fact that they actually heat up your crab legs for you!!!!! Yummy!!! It makes the line long and slow somewhat but its so worth it! The raw oysters they had were also pretty good quality too!

Charcuterie Area
Wide selection of cured meats, cheeses and breads. I loveee charcuterie so this was one station I kept coming back to get some nibbles.

Other Food Highlights
Basically everything I ate here was pretty good with the exception of a few deep fried items which I know I shouldn't get, but I did...and of course it wasn't as good as freshly ordered. There was a very memorable ginseng chicken soup that was actually made really quite well. Loads of ginseng. They had a little tamales too here which I sadly didn't get since I didn't want to get too full.

The desserts here were absolutely amazing!!!!! I honestly think this was the best dessert I've ever had at any buffet! Everything I tried was so good with the exception of these little waffle cones on sticks which were stale. They had chocolate chip cookies that they baked in little dishes...that you then could plop any type of gelato on top! Yummmyyy! A lovely assortment of gelato including normal flavors and ones that were unusual. Cheesecake on a stick, little tarts and pies, nostalgic candy you could grab from out of the huge glass jars, crepe station...I definitely saved a lot of my stomach for the desserts and I was so happy I did!

NOT SO LOVING
Sushi Area
Didn't look so great at all and was pretty pityful...I waited until someone else in my group had tried it...meh not so good. 

Lack of vegetables
If you're a vegetarian...it would suck for you since I barely saw any veggies here! And if you're the strict type who doesn't even eat seafood...well good luck finding stuff to eat! I only saw one or two dishes devoted to veggies and that's it!

Crazy hot burn your hand clay pots
The ginseng chicken soup came in these little clay pots with a sign next to it that warned you that the pots were hot. Nice to have a sign, but it was so hot that I couldn't touch it with my bare hands. I had to go grab some napkins to get it, some pot holders please?

Asian Area
Sadly lacking...other than the ginseng chicken soup. Food didn't look appetizing at all. 

Obviously there really weren't that many bad things about Bacchanal. If only they beefed up the Asian areas then it would be perfect. I hope they keep it up!

TRULY the best buffet in Vegas! I can't compare against the other buffets yet, but Bacchanal Buffet wins by a landslide against Bellagio's. Despite its expensive entry fee ($41.07 with tax for lunch), the food, service, and atmosphere is totally worth it. 

I actually thought that the buffet was only one room, but it turned out that there were even MORE selections at the back room! The sheer number of food choices here is jaw-dropping. And the quality? You definitely get what you pay for, meaning it's GREAT. The seafood is all fresh and again, so many choices to choose from. I think I tried all of the seafood and found them all beyond satisfactory. 

The line for the meats section was really long when I visited but it was worth it for the ribeye. You can always ask for extra helpings once you're up there and there were definitely more meats to choose from; I just didn't want them. 

What I love about this buffet is that it doesn't just have a standard "Mexican" section or "Asian" section. They actually provided food that are traditionally not offered at buffets such as horchata, Thai food, Korean food, Indian food, etc. 

Finally, the desserts section is a killer. SO SO SO good and great two-bites-sized. The desserts were so beautiful and elegant, you almost didn't want to eat them but once you get a bite out of them, you had to eat more! 

My friends and I stayed here for a good 3 hours and we were full to the max! I would definitely go here again!

Finally a decent and top choice-variety of tasting foods... Most of the buffets I tried in vegas at the other popular hotels were gross. One of the most pricey for a buffet in vegas but I think the food quality and variety make up for the price. I enjoyed the seafoods and beef brisket. Dessert section could have done better for taste, but they were alright. I went during lunch hours and they also served mimosas which was a big plus.

seafood is awesome (oysters and snowcrab legs). The fruit drinks in the glass bottles are all very refreshing. The mochi dessert is the best (melt in your mouth mochi). The chocolate souffles are really good too (made to order, so order 15 min ahead of time and they bake it). Overall very delicious food with alot of variety, but more worth it to go for lunch. If you go around 2 (lunch until 3), you can get most of the food, but some stuff like mochi is not there until dinner (after 4), but definitely way cheaper at lunch.

Just a quick update to my review from 2015.  We've continued to visit here every trip we make to Vegas and continue to be impressed.  

While some food remains consistent, there's been enough newness every trip to make it worth while.  I don't remember steamed crap legs during my last trip but what a nice touch!  

What was so great about our last visit was the service.  It was impeccable.  They were so attentive and did an excellent job anticipating our needs without being overbearing.  A huge compliment to the team.  

Yes it's expensive, but the next day we visited an off-strip buffet and the service while efficient, lacked any feelings of really caring for us.  It makes a huge difference with the dining experience and we found ourselves wishing we had gone back to the Bacchanal.

Definitely the cream of the crop for Vegas Buffets. 

Unparalleled selection, and I mean no other buffet comes close. They had everything here - an extensive dessert selection, all sorts of carved meats including your usual culprits, sports bar food like wings and sliders and tater tots, sushi that was surprisingly decent, a variety of soups including a Chinese chicken ginseng soup that was actually well made, a great raw bar with fresh oysters and not-salty king crab, and the list continues with other various bits of deliciousness.

You can get a few bucks off with your Total Rewards Card by the way. It's not cheap, but definitely worth going to at least once to try it for the sheer variety. I know I'll definitely be going back here in the future.

Note: I visited this buffet in August, 2013, so I don't know if anything has changed since then.

This was my first experience at a Las Vegas buffet, and I have to say, I'm a fan! I arrived with a group of 5 at around noon and had to wait for less than 10 minutes. The entire area is very classy and our waitress was super friendly. The food is laid out in a bunch of different sections - Mexican, Italian, seafood, meat, cheese, cold cut meats, Chinese, Thai food, and desserts. 

I really enjoyed the soup noodle section - the pho was surprisingly good for a buffet, and they also had ramen and udon, which I did not try. I also went to town on the desserts, the green tea creme brulee was AH-MAZING.

It was $35.99 per person, which came to about $39 with tax. For the large variety of food available, and in comparison to other restaurants on the Strip, I found it worth it.

Please don't waste your time or money on this place. I've been wanting to go to the Bacchanal for a while and I finally made it with my Girls night out party last Saturday at about 4pm . I was told to go to the kiosk and put my phone number in just so I can stand in line . So after 45 minutes I got a text and I went back to the host and was told to stand in line for two hours and 30 minute (with heels on mind you) they have a person that takes a picture of you before you walk into the restaurant . And I'm walking through the line looking at all the food and nothing is spectacular. The crab legs are the best thing on the menu but hey you're in Vegas and you can have crab legs anywhere . They had a seafood station with no fried shrimp no salmon just a lot of cold seafood. Who ever said this place was the best in Vegas  is mental , DONT WASTE YOUR $60

I really liked this, but we didn't wait in the hour+ long line. It's$50 on the weekend though.  The food is good with a nice presentation and the interior is quite different than most buffets - good and bad.  There aren't any real walk ways to get from the tables to the food.  The food is basically on a long wall that winds away from the dining area, with the Japanese and Chinese food way in the back, and starting from left to right with the raw bar (slowly shucked oysters-few on ice), american food...

It doesn't totally feel like a buffet because of the look of the place.  Nice $19M renovation!  A modern look but not stark like Aria's buffet.  The food, though, can be hard to reach.  It sits at waist level and some of the items are set back so far under the sneeze guard that you have to practically kneel down to reach, especially in the Asian section.

There's no fancy ingredients (like at the Bellagio on weekends) but the presentations can be fancy - little pots of chowder and fried chicken in cones with sweet potato fries on the bottom, individual servings of truffled potatoes au gratin, yum!  You can get your king crab legs on ice or hot out of the water.

The tacos were pretty good off the griddle.  Too bad they are cooking them 3-4 at a time instead of trying to stay ahead of the line.  I got mine late and had to stand there for 5 minutes waiting for the two people in front of me.  I had to translate the Spanish to the gringo before me so that he knew what he was getting.  (High school Spanish only.)

I did really like the carving station which was piled high in bbq pork ribs, lamb chops, prime rib, chicken, sausages, etc.  My prime rib was cut from the middle and was a nice medium, juicy, and well seasoned.

Wicked spoon is by far by favorite Vegas buffet, but after reading reviews about how it's "fallen off" we decided to try Cesar's. It's the only decent buffet I haven't been to. Standing in line eagerly, even after we heard it'd be a 45 minute wait. I was excited, and hungry! Buffets are my absolute favorite, I get bored easily, so I usually opt for sushi or tapas so I can try a few things at once. 

Finally when we were seated the excitement continued, oooh Asian station, ahh seafood! Ramen and pho?? I decided to head for the Asian station first, which had some " sushi " and dim sum. The sushi immediately made my stomach turn and all of a sudden my hunger had vanished. The salmon was a burnt orange color.. On the verge of turning brown and the tuna just looked rotten. I was quite shocked as I saw alot of people still opting for the sushi..but I looked again and realized everyone I saw was non asian. Hmph, I decided to steer clear - I've had food poisoning once and it's definitely no fun. 

Had some dim sum which was really authentic - ( up to par with elite) The fresh shrimp was good, The king crab legs were decent, but I had a few frozen pieces which were a huge turn off. I understand that happens at Asian buffets, but c'mon! Seriously Cesar's?! 

The prime rib line was ridiculous, stood in line for another 20 minutes. But I figured hey, this must be their best dish - but no :( my slice was far too overcooked, and I don't know who said it's better than Lawrys, but they're smoking crack. 

The ramen and pho were surprisingly not bad. Not the best I've ever had but actually decent. Btw they don't have hoison for the pho, only sirracha.

The sliders looked ridiculously good oozing with cheese, but yet again overcooked. If you like your patty well done - this dish is for you. All in all my favorites were the juice section & dessert. The juice selection had fresh cucumber, tomato, grapefruit and a few others. the cucumber tasted so fresh, lovely after a night of drinking vegas. The dessert section had an amazing  lava cake. Not overly sweet, just perfect. I was quite sad they had no macarons though :( they are only made for dinner. They had a variety of gelato flavors I've never heard of, so that was cool. Try thai tea :) 

Also - maybe this buffet was better once upon a time, because half of the dishes in the pictures were nonexsistent when I went. I probably won't be returning , for $110 after tax and tip for a party of two - the juice and dessert weren't THAT good. I'd rather go to wicked spoon or the buffet at m resort.

We went on a Sunday for brunch, which is $50 per person.  We got there around 11:30am, and you check in at a digital kiosk, which tells you what time to come back, in order to cut down on the lines.  Ours told us to come back at 12pm, but a text came to me a little sooner than that, and we were able to come back around 20 minutes later.  The buffet is definitely huge--it's got anything from dim sum, to sushi, to Mexican, American, Italian, seafood.  It also has a great dessert section with gelato and made to order crepes, and everything inbetween.  What turned me off in the buffet was the crab legs that were still frozen.  I was picking ice off my crab legs!  At $50 per person, I did not think I should have to be dealing with that. =/

The last time we were in vegas, we went on buffet-hopping and Bacchanal was on the list.

We tried Bacchanal, Wicked Spoon and the Buffet at Aria.

Well, after trying all three I would prefer Wicked Spoon over the much-hyped Bacchanal. The only reason it was a 4 stars instead of 3 stars is because of the great service we got from our server. Food selection, quality, presentation and taste is 3 stars though.

Bachannal does have a lot of different kinds of foods. On the day we were there, however, we saw danishes on multiple different places. We didn't find any macaroons that some other yelper posted on yelp.

For $51 per person, I came in with a higher expectation than what we had been given. I would prefer to go with Wicked Spoon for $35 and selection, taste, presentation.

First buffet I've tried in Vegas, best food in a buffet I've ever had, BUT worse service I've ever had at a buffet. 


We had to flag down waiters from other tables to bring us drinks/refills because ours went MIA. Not acceptable, especially when you paid for bottomless champaign.

Worth it? Worth it.

You're going to spend about $60+ for dinner, and will be waiting in line, so prepare yourself and get ready.

You'll definitely be standing in line for maybe a good 30 minutes to an hour...and thats AFTER you recieve a text to start standing in line.

You give the host your name and phone. number; and they'll text you in about and hour or two (on a busy night).

So what we did was check out the Caesar's casino and resort, and their variation of pools (a must to wander the pool area).

Time went by fairly easily while we checked out the property.

Okay so...once you pay after standing in line, you'll wait a little more again to be seated (it's kind of like a journey). 

Once they guide you to your seats, you'll pass by all the fresh seafood sitting on the ice behind the window...

If you want crab legs, DON'T jump the gun..


Keep walking and there will be a guy boiling the crab legs towards the back...which is tastier than cold crab legs (grab the melted butter while you're at it).

The rest, I'll let you figure out.

Oh btw, $15+ gets you bottomless beer or Mimosa's.

This place is a must on your every vegas trips, the food it amazing.

The place is not your average buffet with just good food. The lay out and decor is impressive as well.

One of the best buffets here in Vegas. You have variety which is important to us! We went here for lunch and we were glad we gave it a try regardless of the lines. 

We called ahead to see if seafood was offered at lunch they said no only at dinner. We almost were not going to give it a shot because of this but we are glad we did because the receptionist was thankfully wrong! There were crab claws, large shrimp, mussels, and ceviches. No snow crab at lunch but that's OK we enjoyed the others. 

We tried everything from every section. The highlights for us were the pork belly tapas style dish, the claws, the meat selections, the sushi (which we eat all the time at our favorite local spot) the salmon was especially yummy, the burger slider with the bacon jam, the remoulade sauce, and believe it or not the truffle mushroom soup is a MUST. I want more just thinking about it. They also had exotic fresh juices, and horchata.The desserts were good but our favorite is the creme brulee and molten chocolate cake very decadent.

The service was great our waitress was kind and pleasant and our dishes were kept on top of. Some dishes didn't have as much flavor so that is why the 4 instead of five stars. The shrimp and grits could have been more flavored and the grits cooked longer, and I was looking for some horseradish cream for my meat but could not find it. Some of the Italian dishes were not the greatest. But these are things I can overlook for a buffet with mostly great food and great service. We would come again and we have tried alot of Buffet's on the strip and usually leave unsatisfied until this one. Give it a try! Just be prepared to wait awhile and skip the dinner price go at lunch for a cheaper meal.

Great service today from Vince! They rotate new dishes into the buffet all the time, which allows for a lot of fun options every time you go back. A fun experience, even though I'm not a big eater. Watermelon salad, gelato, and dim sum were my faves.

The best buffet I had in Vegas ! Great experience !!!!! We came around 230 cost us $60 for food and unlimited drinks ! The crab legs were fabulous ! Worth all my money right there ! Then steak then pasta and all the cute little dishes are so cute ! Had a lot of diversity ! And the dessert was amazingggg. Also they had a gelato bar 


Highly recommend !

We've eaten here three times on this trip, and probably 15 times in total. Calling it a buffet is like calling a Porsche a regular car. Some of the best brisket I've ever had, and the selection is unbeatable. It's like 15 mini restaurants in a line. 

It's pricey but worth it.

the food here is awesome. its 30$ for lunch if you want to wait 2 hours, its 50$ if you go to the express line.  Its 50$ without additional 20$ express fee after 3pm.  THE SERVICE HERE SUCKS.  we had this lady who rung us up and she absolutely didnt know what the hell she was doing.  We wanted split tabs and we were a party of 6.  She charged us gratuity when she wasnt suppose to and we ended up all standing in front of her for a dam near 15 minutes while she and her manager discussed the problem eventually being moved to another lady to complete our process.  Our waiter or buser said there wasnt unlimited mimosa.... which was a lie.. and we basically stacked our own plates left it on the floor cause she obviously didnt give a dam.  


BESIDES THIS THE FOOD IS GOOD! taco sstation, seafood station, pizza, etc etc but the food was legitimately good! and the dessert section was great! my gf loved that part

Me and my fiancé went here last year in march. I was very excited cuz this was the #1 place I wanted to experience. It's extremely busy and the wait time is about 30 minutes to an hour but it was well worth that and the price. They offered so many varieties of food from desserts to meats. I would definitely recommend and hopefully will do it again this august.
Foods galore! I'm getting fat tonight! Love the ambiance, the architecture.... mmmm and the food.... mmmmmm

Don't forget dessert. We missed lunch by minutes because of the long line to get in. Dinner, Could be considered pricy but the food was unique and tasty enough to justify going. There is a lot of filler foods that you should avoid because they can fill you up without letting you enjoy the unique items that are scattered all the way to the back. Don't just go with what you recognize, there is a lot to try. My wife and I ate our money's worth in steamed crab, sashimi (without the rice so we weren't filling up), peach wood smoked brisket, exotic cheese, fresh bread, fire cooked pizza, oysters and more. We stayed till the end of our two hour limit. The dessert was awesome and expertly crafted. The little green dome things were so good, we would go back just for those.

To get the most bang for your buck here, load up on the meats and seafood since those seemed to be the highest quality. And make sure not to eat too much carbs because you'll want to eat dessert too (they have custom crepes *heart eyes) 

They have every food you could possibly think of: sushi, chinese, soup, breads, various salads, mexican, american, italian and the list goes on and on. There's things to eat for everyone definitely. 

I didn't love it because the wait was long (expected in Vegas but still not fun) and I'm not a huge seafood person, also a lot of the other foods didn't really blow me away. Plus my friend's crab legs were still partially frozen which irked us :/ And the weekend buffet for dinner is most expensive at $56

Came here for a 7am breakfast so I didn't have to worry about a long wait.  I think since I've came the price has gone up $10 per meal.  I can't blame Caesars, it's all about supply and demand, but now I'm not sure if I'd rather go to a signature restaurant instead.

This is the best buffet I've been to in Vegas, I like the small individual portions with high variety of items.  I found myself trying endless amounts of things all freshly prepared, not growing a film under a heat lamp.

For breakfast they had all sorts of sides (sweet potato bites), a HUGE selection of juice and still laid out all the meats and cheeses and a few lunch items.  Another cool thing was the way the food is presented, fries are in mini deep fryer baskets, juices in baby carafes, pancakes in mini skillet pans.   

Looking forward to another meal here, I know I won't be hungry enough for the following meal!

Food does not get any better than this.  50 min wait before we could enter the line.  Well worth it!  So many different fares so fresh and delicious.  New favorite food I tried was the Bloody Mary Oyster Shooter.  Only downer.....wish the creme brûlée was not instant.  Many other good deserts tho

This was close to 5 stars but unfortunately I was let down by the cleaning the staff. The food was the best I had in Vegas without a doubt and worth every penny! My personal favorite station was the dessert station... Tons of amazing and tasty treats that kept me coming back after I was stuffed! This buffet was so chic as well but towards the end I was terribly grossed out. My boyfriend and I went up to try more food and came back to find tons of dirty, slobbered on dishes on our table! My guess is the waiter thought we were done and decided to clean all around our table and place all of everyone's dirty dishes on our table! It was so gross to sit down and look at the mess placed where my purse and food was sitting! I mean i can understand confusion but that should never happen! It really put a stop to our appetite.. It's a shame because the taste of the food was spectacular

I am a total and utter pig when it comes to buffets and especially at Bacchanal. The wait time is super long the first time i came. 

I just went back recently and they have these little kiosks that you can put a reservation in and it tells you when to come back so you aren't waiting in line for an hour. 

I love the lamb and prime rib and the seafood is awesome. crabs, oysters, shrimp, more crab, oyster shooters, yum!  They have a lot of everything, seafood, meat, cheese bar, chinese, japanese, noodle bowls, and the desserts should come first because you are so stuffed from dinner, there is absolutely no space for dessert. So I learn to not eat until i'm about to pop from the regular courses so I can have room for dessert. They have crepes, massive chocolote covered strawberries, and little dishes and cakes of stuff. 

Great customer service with clearing the table and keeping drinks full.  I will always come back.

After reading so many great reviews we were excited to try this buffet for my birthday dinner. We went on a Thursday evening, although it was between Xmas and New Year's Eve so maybe that had influence.  The wait was 2.5 hours so that by the time we were actually seated it was about 9pm. Our server was initially slow to arrive to get our drink order but otherwise kept us in wine and water just fine! The food on the buffet was tasty but definitely the end of the night - things were not replaced and left to linger. I had a lamb chop and salmon that were both better than expected for a buffet. The desserts were amazing, though again, being the end of the night, the options were limited.
All told it was about $150 total and definitely not worth that much for a buffet.

Ok this is the highest rated buffet in Vegas - and with reason, but let me also debunk some myths.

The good:
-Different types of meat - even jalapeño chicken sausage!
-Made to order crepe bar (in addition to many dessert options)
-There is table service - good because they come and take your plates away as you finish with them
Biggggg seafood bar/decent sushi selection 
-No wait if you get there for brunch before 11 am
-Great Italian 
-Amazing churros 

The not that good:
-Mini red velvet pancakes - much talked about, but if that's one of your favorite brunch items and you've sampled some of the best red velvet pancakes, you'll be disappointed. 
-Coffee-wise, anything other than plain coffee is an extra charge in addition to the buffet charge 
-OK Asian food

Date & Time: Tuesday, 2/24/15 @ 2pm

The buffet was for two people at the price of $83 and some change. There is such variety when first stepping into the buffet. There are sections into seafood, american, mexican, italian, chinese/japanese, and dessert. They have charcuterie with a selection of cheeses as well as a salad section. They offer all you can drink beer and mimosas for $22 (each)

The buffet highlight for me was the fresh juices and dessert. The food was good, I rather settle for a buffet a boulder station for cheaper, than to go here again. The food here was a little bland and I didn't really enjoy most of it. They do have a tapas style going for some of the food selections so you can try most of the items they have to offer, but it was missing something -flavor. I decided to try this place out due to the numerous reviews on how great this place is, I would recommend it for you to try it at least once (the seafood was awesome). This place has amazing food presentation, but other than that, the lack of flavor in most of its items makes me steer away from here again.

Never disappoints! This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas. Yes it is pricey, but you get exactly what you pay for- the food is excellent & good quality. Huge variety, great desserts, large seating area. They have something similar to a "fast pass" at disneyland in the front of the buffet where you enter your name & amount of people in your party, then it will give you a return time. This is waaaay better than standing in line for 2 hours! Very efficient. Excellent experience. Had to roll myself out as usual.
A big variety of mediocre food during lunch.   Just head to MESA instead.  And enjoy a nice lunch instead.

I came on Easter weekend so there was a surcharge in price. Waited approx 1 hour which is on the super short end since we had a party of 12. For the price, the food selection and quality is mediocre at best. My friends barely ate but for $90 per person, I had to get my monies worth so I stuffed myself while they waited for me. The service was OK but they had a really good tea drink you can order from the waiter. The first time experience is worth it but I would not come back.

This buffet has the reputation for being the best on the strip! Although I cannot confirm that personally, I can say it is absolutely one of the best that I have been to, hands down!

There are SO MANY choices of hot fresh food! I have gone for both dinner and again for brunch. Was not disappointed either time. There is an entire stretch of fresh seafood, crab legs, shrimp, and even a very tasty ceviche.

The "carving board" had beautiful prime rib, ham, chicken and even tasty fresh sausages.

Then you start to go into the food by theme. Mexican, Italian, Asian. Great selections here as well!

BUT WAIT!!! - Do not fill up on all the savory, because the dessert "Island" may very well be the very best part!! REALLY!!! Homemade Crepe to order? No problem! Fresh Gelato, OK! Tons of tasty little gourmet sweet bites...Ummm Yes! 
OK, I confess, I could start here and go backwards!!!

When I have visitors, and they want to "hit a Buffet" this is my recommendation. It is not cheap people, $50 for dinner or brunch. Breakfast and lunch is a better price.

And a word to the wise, come early because on a weekend, a 90 minute wait is pretty standard. The best part of that, hanging around really builds an appetite, so you can do some damage to the line up of delicious options!

Pretty good buffet! we had lunch here for almost $90 for 2 people! They have everything - seafood, meats galore, sushi, noodles, rice, salad, fruit, a crazy dessert area and more! nice setting a pretty good food but probably wont go again. i dont do well at buffets...never feel like i get my moneys worth! def worth going once tho!

My husband and I decided to have a date night here on a Sunday for dinner. It took maybe an hour to go from checking in to being seated. Not too bad of a wait.

We were sat in a half booth row with all of the tables being very close together. You could easily hear someone else's conversation without trying or even get a face full of butt. Not fun.

The service was okay. Getting drinks refilled was a little slow but seemed better than what I've read in previous reviews.

The selection of food is nice. However, my husband is an avid sushi eater and found the sushi to be too fishy tasting. He went to the ramen station and was told they were out of all noodles for the night. After listening to my husband's complaint, I headed towards the ramen station. The noodle guy must have had no idea what he was talking about because I was able to order ramen and the people in front of me and behind me were able to order ramen as well, including their other choices of noodles.

The other food was nice too. The Mexican area had nice fruit juices in glass bottles, as well as made to order tacos. American had the best chicken wings I've ever had. There was a pasta order station but didn't get a chance to try it. The desserts were very good. There was something with an Oreo in a cake or something. Absolutely delicious.

Overall, though, I found this buffet to be overrated. I was excited but left wanting more, especially with what it costs. Not sure I'd come here again unless it were free or at least cheaper.

Ok, the early hype about greatest buffet ever was probably a bit more than deserved. Overall food was good, but I would expect that for over $50 per person for dinner. Asian food was OK. You'll find better at mid priced Asian buffets in California. Grilled meats and seafood bar were very good as was the dessert station. If I had to wait two hours, then it would have not been worth it. New system when l where you register and come back later worked well. No wait to register and we paid and were seated with 10 minutes of return.

Overall, for the price I'd say 3.5 stars but with the short wait for a Saturday, I will round up to 4 stars.

Best buffet on town. Period!! We arrived exactly at 12pm and waiting time less than 5mins. When we walked out around 2pm the waiting line had grown substantially. 

We tried Bellagio, Paris and Monte Carlo and agreed the Caesar Palace was best food we had during our entire week in LV. 

Buffet has several food stations: 1. Sushi, Oriental dishes; 2. italian with pasta and pizzas; 3. cheese table with european and US Cheese; 4. Mexican including table with sauces; 5. Barbecue and meats; 6. Seafood, including spanish paella; 7 desserts. 

Place has modern decoration and lounge music, spacious and attentive waiters. 

Awesome dishes tried: lobster bisque, lobster ravioli, quesadillas, spicy sausage, turkey, mini burgers, paella, and creme brûlée; everything was spectacular. 
Paid around US$50.00 P/P

By far the best buffet in Vegas. Expect the wait to be at least an hour each time to get seated. Not cheap but good value for money. Prime rib is amazing, as are the crab legs. Plenty of choices. Seafood (mussels, crab, oysters), meat (prime rib, beef rib, pork rib, ham, turkey) Chinese, Japanese, cheese, salads, fruit and lots of desserts! Service is good too. I've been 3 times now and it's a must each time my husband and i go to Vegas

This past weekend was my second time trying Bacchanal, and this time I felt that it was even better for lunch than it was for dinner my first time around.

First off, this buffet is not cheap. Be prepared to drop $40 (with Total Rewards card) just for lunch, and upwards of $50 for dinner.

My friends and I lined up around 11:35 AM and there was only a short wait of about 10 minutes. It was not long before we sat down and were approached by a server for drinks. During Brunch they also serve unlimited mimosas (kind of strong per my friends btw so you may need to dilute it with their tropical/orange juice offerings) If you don't want to pay the dinner price, get yourself in line well before 2:30 PM.

The choices at Bacchanal outdo any other buffet out in Vegas, which includes Wynn, Bellagio, Wicked Spoon, and M. Items do not sit around long before being replaced with freshly made food.

I can't eat seafood, but they offer mounds of shell-less large shrimp, mussels, and King Crab legs (steamed on request)

Their carving station includes slow roast prime rib, smoked brisket, various sausages, honey ham, bacon, and sometimes tomahawk ribeye (though this last option might only be for dinner). This is the most popular station in the Buffet so be prepared to wait some time as there is only one (albeit very friendly) staff member doing the carving.

Dessert was probably the most disappointing to me. M buffet had a better selection of gelato and sugary offerings, and the creme brulee here is nothing short of disappointing. Sad really. This buffet could easily be 5-stars if their dessert got some work.

That being said, they do have a tasty Strawberry Sorbet and my friends have mentioned the Pistachio was delicious as well.

I can't comment on the salad/Mexican/Italian/cheese stations as I don't care for those but the Asian section actually has roast Chinese duck!!! I probably ate a good 2 pounds of this on top of what I already ate. It tastes almost as good, if not the same as the stuff you get from Sam Woo BBQ so this is a major plus in my book.

Other things I really liked: sliders, corn on the cob, sweet-potato tater tots (it's like candy!), chicken-mango sausage, prime rib

I was very pleasantly surprised by my second visit here and so were my friends. I will definitely take my parents here the next time I am in Vegas (which shouldn't be too long).

Seriously the most impressive array of buffet offerings I have ever laid eyes on. We were trying to sneak in for a late lunch with hopes of the foodstuffs transitioning over to dinner whilst we pay the lunch price (cuz we cheap like dat), but given the intense wait, ended up paying the straight up dinner price...so line up before 3pm folks. Dinner price was not cheap, $112 for 2ppl to be exact, but worth it for the experience alone!

Can't say I ate my money's worth. But my bf had about 6 plates of stone crab and snow crab legs, so he may have. Other more jaw dropping item included seafood paella, fish tacos (freshly made), New Zealand sea bass, Chicken and waffles, surprisingly delicious roast duck, and one ridik dessert station.

This is the first time that I gave 1 star on Yelp and I would give it zero if I could. My husband and I were so disappointed and had a horrible experience at Bacchanal Buffet. We paid roughly $60/ person and it was not worth it. It couldn't even compare to a $30 buffet. The only good thing was the dessert bar. The Bacchanal Buffet is definitely overrated and overpriced. It is a shame that this is the best buffet in Las Vegas. We will never come back!

Come early! I came here around 9:30-9:45AM and was seated within 15 minutes. It's worth it to wake up a little earlier to beat the 2-5 hour wait time after 10:30AM-ish. They do have special pricing during the holiday season (~ $47) but have a similar selection of foods regardless. 

FOOD
The food was good, great variety, but nothing too special. They have seafood,  Asian, Mexican, Italian, and "American" food stations. 

- Dos: crab legs, salmon, butter mussels, sweet potato fries, chicken & waffles, creme brulee, sample each of their desserts (no shame, they have a great dessert bar!), crepes, gelato, cheese station

- Don'ts: the "fresh" juice section, Mexican and Asian food quality was meh -- you're better off saving your stomach space!

SERVICE
Great, very attentive service! They also offer you free mini plastic tongs to hold hot plates (also can usually be found at the dessert bar).

If you choose this buffet to eat king crab, then you should find another buffet. This place is a true scam artist. Their KING CRAB PORTION is mix with snow crab and in fact 5/6 of it were snow crab legs.  

The hot or boil king crab is nasty. Some of it was still frozen eventhough they have soak in hot water.

Customer service was great. The place is pricy and the wait was very long. Overall i would not recommend this place.

So much to choose from and so little time. This buffet is amazing. much is hot and fresh & so many choices it is worth it. My favorite is the sweet sesame red bean buns, the lobster tail, the Alaskan king crabs, the salad bar, the tacos.

This is where everyone is at. Invite your grammy, auntie, uncle,  your whole family. Bacchanal has plenty of space to accommodate and this place is poppin. I suggest coming early and if you have a large party of 6 or more, there's a separate line for that. The group line is toward the back end of the building behind the main line and will soon wrap around the corner as more parties arrive. Thankfully, it moves quick!

Have your player's card ready and one credit card available to charge for the party. I don't believe they do separate charges per card for the party line, so prep yourself for that. Once your party is ready to enter the buffet, they hand out these nifty little hot plate holders so you don't burn your fingers. 

It's about $50pp with unlimited mimosas, and we hella indulged in mimosas! By the end of our meal (about 2 hours in), they topped off each our glasses and said this is the last round. Apparently, we got a noise complaint. Wooops!

A couple favorites:
Hot Plates: mussels, prime rib, udon is better than ramen (according to the table consensus), pork belly
Dessert:  jasmine rice pudding with coffee jelly

Man am I bummed that I have to rate this place less than 4 stars, I was so stoked to eat here!

Originally I bought a groupon for $88 for 2, but didn't read the fine print that stated we couldn't use it on a holiday weekend, boo. 
We came in for brunch anyway and got the buffet/all you can drink mimosas which came out to about $65/person. 

I started at the dim sum area which left me rather underwhelmed. Pork/taro buns were flavorless. Dumplings, shu mai, and har gow were all ok, I can get better quality from my local dim sum fast food place. 

Meat station was also lacking. Bacon was suuuuuper undercooked like no color whatsoever on it. "Prime rib" was an overcooked brick of meat, so so sad. Nothing else on the butcher block even looked appetizing enough to try :(

Mashed potatoes were good, lots of butter. As was the macaroni and cheese, but $65 for these two dishes to be the memorable things is not ok in my book. 

Mimosas were filled a little slowly, but we definitely had our fill of champagne (8-10 mimosas each to be exact) 

Our waitress was a sweetheart so I added an extra half star for her, this place for brunch was a 2.5 and my least favorite of the trip.

My brother, his girlfriend, and I went here on Saturday afternoon and there was an hour wait, which was understandable. However, we were told that the price would go up for lunch after 3 PM and that our buffet would be $37. When we got to the front of the line before 2:30, the price went up to $54. Really felt like they were giving us the runaround and the staff didn't seem very concerned or apologetic for the misunderstanding. 

Very hit and miss on the food. Some stand outs were the spicy sausage, the pizza and the french fries, but the Asian food, seafood (especially Crawfish), and burgers were not very good. Desert was a little better on the hits like the flan, the cheesecake, and the creme brulée. Overall, not worth the price of admission at all.

SERVICE: 3/10
FOOD: 4/10 
AMBIENCE: 7/10

The selection is plentiful. The food was decent enough. For the price I would say it's a very good deal. For me the desert was the highlight of the whole buffet. The crepe is a must try. My favorite combination is nutella, cinnamon sugar and shredded coconut meat. (I know you didn't ask, but I'm sharing anyway lol) crab claws were pretty bland. King crab legs were pretty good. Juices are not freshely squeezed but they are still delicious and full of sugar (quote from gf) . Overall a very well worth meal!

We went to the Bacchanal at 4:30PM on a Tuesday thinking that it's too early for dinner and it'll probably be empty. However there was already a waiting line at this point. The Bacchanal has ticketing machines in front of the lines which print tickets with approximate waiting times, and when they think they may be able to accommodate you they give your phone a text. I like the idea if these machines since it gives us a pretty good window where we can just walk around in the vicinity and check out the shops near by without having to stand there and wait for a long time. We received a ticket from their machines telling us to come back at 5:52PM, around an hour and a half later.

After coming back to the buffet at the aforementioned time, we were put onto another line, where we waited until around 6:20 when we were finally seated. Overall it was a relatively short wait on the line given how crowded it seemed. One interesting note though is that we saw plenty of empty tables towards the back when we got into the cafe, so it's a bit puzzling as to why there are no one seated in those tables when there is a long line outside.

The buffet itself for dinner is $54.99 per person before tips on weekends. There were a lot of nice seafood options inside. The seafood on ice tend to taste not as fresh. For example the oysters don't have the sweet oyster after taste that I'm used to, and the crab claws on ice also was somewhat flavorless. The shrimps on ice were pretty decent though, and the oysters shooters were also pretty good.

My favorite dish was probably the steamed crab legs which tasted very good, and they were very generous with portions. There were some other great cooked seafood dishes such as crayfish, mussels, and clams. There were also other cooked dishes but they were not as memorable.

Overall, I liked the buffet (since I love seafood) and would come back again, though it was really a bit on the pricey side.

Like some other yelpers, The Buffet at the Wynn was my favorite. I wanted to try the Wicked Spoon too, but this was closer to where we were staying. I think this is a close tie between Wynn and Bacchanal. We came here on a Monday afternoon thinking there wouldn't be a longass line. Oh man, there was a longass line. We waited for about 40 minutes, but it was worth it! We were pretty hungry by the point we got to our table, and I got to say they have a good variety like the Wynn. All the seafood dishes were very good. The one I liked most was the grits. So good. Mac and Cheese, roasted potatoes, salmon, prime rib, brisket, tiramisu were just so awesome. They also have juices in cute bottles, but they didn't stand out too much. I was waiting for the crab legs to come out, but the wait was too long. I like this place a lot. Good Job, Caesars Palace!
Delicious food and great service. Mark was an excellent server and will definitely come back.

I have mixed feelings about this buffet. I wanted to check it out as it's supposed to be one of the best of Vegas, but had read mixed reviews lately. The line wasn't too bad at 5:45pm. We waited about 40 mins. They have a weird system with a lot of roped areas and the actual entrance to line up was roped off which confused us at first. The kiosk wasn't operational yet and finally we found a staff person who was directing traffic and letting people into the roped area manually. A little strange. 

Our meals were very pricey ($70 per person after tax and tip, and holiday pricing in effect). The space is quite beautiful and spacious with nice ambiance. Unfortunately we were shoved off to the side right near a bright walkway, so that was weird. 

As for the buffet: The sheer variety was impressive and there was some really great tasting things, but it was so hit and miss that I felt like I was playing food roulette to find the hits. 

The good: Soft Shell Crab, prime rib, Mac & Cheese, mashed potatoes, made to order tacos, horchata (not too sweet!), duck fried rice, lumpia, sushi.

The bad: the oysters (they tasted off and were poorly shucked), crab legs (salty!), brisket (dry), pasta and pizza were all mediocre. 

I also tried a few desserts and the standouts were the coconut gelato and chocolate dipped strawberry. I noticed a sign for a made to order chocolate soufflé but was too full at that point. 

All in all, a decent buffet but hard to give it more stars when there's so much hit and miss. I'd go back if it were cheaper and quality more stable.

amazing! very pricey, but worth it in my opinion. Very clean and lots of cool decorations. Food is amazing too. There is literally a little bit of everything. And the dessert bar is definitely something you don't want to miss with its gelato bar and crepe station. Cant wait to go back

My husband and I were very excited to try the Bacchanal buffet, and we were not disappointed

We came with friends for Saturday brunch and stood in line at 10:30 am, the brunch is $44.99 per person. if your party has 8 or more, than 18% gratuity is charged. The wait for us was approximately 15 minutes.

The hostess was very accommodating 

The decor of the buffet was eclectic and modern, the lighting was bright, and the background music was not obtrusive. great ambience, and one did not need to raise the voice in order to carry a conversation across the table...but who needs a conversation when there is so much good food to stuff ones mouth, right ;)

The far left counter is the seafood bar, and the place that my husband keeps on going back to...extremely high quality crab legs and cocktail shrimps (this is where you get your moneys worth)...also available are smoked salmon, mussels, clams, and halibut

then there is the southern kitchen station, followed by meat station complete with a meat carver that bellows "welcome to Bacchanal" in a very pirate like fashion and with a hearty chuckle. The prime rib is good for a buffet, also available are lamb chops, ribs, and artisan sausages

next up is the taco bar, followed by cheese and deli station, followed by salad and fruit bar. then comes the noodles station with choices like pho, udon and ramen. the ramen preparation is surprising good.

and last but not least, dim sum station and chinese food. If you like duck, then you must try the roast duck at this station. forget Sam Woo BBQ, this duck is legit...

make the rectangular dessert station your last ten stops...there is apple pie, mousse, cookies, cup cakes, gelato (try the mango chile lime, trust me, your mouth will thank you), cake pops...only one complaint, the heavy ceramic serving trays under the individual desserts, completely superfluous ;) 

take home message, come hungry, go home like your 10 months pregnant

Also, bottomless Mimosas and champagne to wash the food down...I know, some will argue this should have been in the beginning of the review:)

(This entry was written by my husband)

The line is crazy! You wait on two separate lines and that's when you get seated . I guess the only way to get in faster is to have a diamond member or the seven stars . The food was good and had a lot of different selections and cultural food . What was the most annoying part is paying more per person because it was their "holiday pricing" ummm we went on July 2nd .... what holiday is that .. it's all bs but didn't want to walk out of the hotel to find food and bake in the hot sun

First of all, please stop pronouncing it "back anal". 

Second, it's in Vegas. The metropolis of buffets and other sins. 

So you gotta stand out from the rest. 

I'm going to rate the food 4/5 and the service 5/5. Our server was prompt and our cups runneth over (figuratively). 

Now, we were famished by the time we got to Bacchanal. We survived a weekend of hikes at Angel's Landing and some of us (read: me) very nearly died. So we've been fantasizing and strategizing about this buffet. 

That might be one of the reasons I wasn't overly blown away. 

For $60 a person and a $20 tip for every two diners in our group, I was expecting something ...more. That's not to say that the food was not very good. But I am scaling my review based on the average rating of this buffet and my overall expectations. 

PRO TIP: get there 30-60 minutes before Dinner so you pay the "brunch" price. Even though it was the President's Holiday Weekend, they still tiered their buffet and prices. So the "good stuff" came after 3:00 pm. Namely the amazing steak (medium rare) and oysters. 

The crab legs, which I totally HYPED waaaaay too much in my mind, was the frozen kind. Even the "steamed" crab legs were noticeably frozen. Which I should have expected. They're nice to snack on but not exactly worth traveling to Vegas alone for. 

Overall, I would recommend going here if you're with a group of friends and want to celebrate something :)

OMG‼ Bacchanal is AMAZING.... The presentations, service and delivery are the best I have witnessed in a buffet, it's unbelievable how GREAT this place is. Even with the different countries/culture of food; the flavor explosion that hits your mouth and taste buds is like Mr Chow jumping out of the Mercedes in the dessert in Hangover One... DO IT FOR YOUR TASTE BUDS‼‼‼

If you are in Vegas it's a must see and eat, you will love it
This place so far the best buffet I had ever been in my life! Their food selection is amazing and everything was very delicious, It is very worth it for the price we pay ($60 for weekdays brunch).
Some of the best thin crust Pizza on the West Coast. Their only rival might be Apizza Scholes in Portland. Even my Italian friends can't seem to find as good of pizza in Italy.

Bacchanal Buffet is probably the best buffet in Vegas.  Actually it is the best buffet in Vegas.  Hence the near $50 price tag.  Lots of options on food here. They carried stone crab when they first opened, but not anymore.

Lines are long so come early. Decor is neat and the desserts were probably the least impressive out of all the food.

Beautiful buffet with a huge selection, but it's the same old story as with most buffets. They want to give people more options, but flavors are sacrificed. Some of the dishes have something wrong with them. Either too bland, salty, dry, etc. They had the blandest crab that I've ever had at a buffet. 

I would say though that the Asian food selection was delicious. Everything tasted accurate and the variety was unique and numerous. I've never seen roast duck, pho, wonton egg noodle soup, and udon all in one buffet, and they were all tasty. So yummy. Best pho at a buffet that I've ever tasted!

There are so many dishes that I had never seen at other buffets before like green tea cookies and chicken and waffles. 

The best part of the buffet is the dessert table! Make sure you make room for everything on the table. You'll regret it if you don't. 

Bottom line: Unique options, large layout, but flavors lacking for the most part.
Definitely my favorite buffet in town! Good quality food and the selections are endless.   If you want the best Vegas buffet experience go to this one.

Got extremely lucky that my group of friends and I were able to make it here within the last few minutes before the menu pricing changed over from lunch to dinner! For a group of 6, we arrived at the cash register and paid for the lunch price at exactly 2:59PM. Since the register changes over the meal pricing systematically, we paid the lunch price for the dinner meal. We were trying to get here at 2:30PM to take an advantage of this option, but it still worked out and we got here literally at the last minute!

This was my first Vegas buffet, ever. I couldn't decide between here or Wicked Spoon, after reading an article that compared the two buffets against every category (from meat to desserts), Bacchanal won me over. 

Unless you can eat every single item that the buffet serves, recommend walking around to see what the stomach is in the mood for before eating away. I normally would not eat dim sum anywhere else except for well known chinese restaurants, but their pork buns knocked it out of the park! It was fresh and did not taste as if it was re-heated from a frozen bag. Yes, I know.. I should not be commenting on pork buns at a buffet, but they were that good! Consider it a compliment since I'm Cantonese and constantly judging any dim sum item. 

My favorites by far was the crab leg and meat area. The crab legs were already prepared and cut for you, all you had to do was take your fork, lift out the meat, and serve yourself. I wasn't expecting to finish a huge plate of crab legs by myself, but they made the process simple and it was much easier to eat! Moving onto the meats, I was not expecting them to give me a huge slice of the prime rib, it was the same size that's offered at steak houses! I expected just a thin slice carved out for me, but it was literally steak size. This by itself made the buffet price worthwhile. 

After completely stuffing yourself and loosening the belt, make sure to have room for dessert! I grabbed a variety of desserts after walking around the station and tried a sample of each one. The most delectable and memorable to this day were the egg tarts. The egg tarts were fresh, warm, and had a buttery crust. I felt like I could eaten 20 more of those just because they were that good.

Bacchanal, I will have you again.

As someone who is definitely not a fan of buffets at all...I have to say this is one of the best restaurants I've ever eaten at! The food is very much worth the high price tag. The variety of food is just right. The atmosphere is very nice and pleasant. Do expect to wait at least 45 to get a table though. Another thing that I appreciated so much was that their crab legs are already cut open perfectly so you don't have to spend a lot of time trying to get the crab meat out. If I have one critique it would be that I think the service could be a little bit better. For example I noticed our waitress looked at our receipt on our table to see how much we tipped before she started serving us....other than that, I give this place a solid 5 stars and will definitely be coming back !

First off, Id like to say that I had the highest hopes for this buffet. Seeing fellow yelpers reviews/photos made me soo excited!! 

STAFF: very friendly and attentive. Our dirty plates never sat on our table for more than five minutes. I also think it's very helpful that they give Bacchanal first timers a tour of the buffet.

FOOD: mehhhh. Many of the "hot" dishes were not very hot. It was more like cool/room temperature. It is not fun to eat cold lobster corn chowder (I was VERY excited for this). 

TIPS: wear long pants or a maxi dress! While I was in line for the carving station, someone had dropped a plate and the glass had shattered and got caught between my sandal and foot. There was also a woman between me and the person who dropped the plate. Good thing she was wearing a maxi dress! Lol. 

SIDE NOTE: good thing I looked at yelp pictures before the buffet! There were absolutely NO signs for the food. Like uhhhh I think this is clam chowder? Could be cream of mushroom soup. Who knows!

After reading the amazing yelp reviews had to try this hot new Buffett. After trying wicked spoon on my last Vegas trip the bar was set pretty high.

Bacchanal made wicked spoon like a shack. The sheer size of this place is amazing. I would for sure check out the build your own taco station as well as the seafood section. Price is a little on the high side but the meal was well worth it. Will be back again soon!

Its a tuesday and its 3:49p. Not much people yet the wait is really long. MORE THAN 20 MINUTES! And some of the workers look draggy and lazy. No one is telling us how much more long is the wait. This is a beautiful buffet. Quality is great. But is Bachannal willing to risk their 10 out of 10 rating for slacking in customer service and urgency? More than 20minutes of waiting is ridiculous.

Went here for the brunch, $58 per person. The food was pretty good. Different stations~ seafood, Mexican, American, Italian and Chinese. Overall it was okay. Worth the money if you want to eat everything here. But if you're craving a specific type of food ten it's not worth it, the dessert bar was fantastic tho!! I would go again just for the desserts!!!! 
They also have some items that u can order and they make for you~ tacos, crepes (AWESOMEEE), soup and prime ribs~!! Overall it was a great experience. GET TR CREPES AND BANANA FOSTER CREME BRÛLÉE FLAN ICE CREAM!! YUMMM

What can I say that has not already been said!  This will be my buffet of choice from now on!  Good small portions but the food is by far the best buffet, hey small portions just means you can try different food!  Went for breakfast but I need to go back one day for dinner!  I might not leave!

The only reason i am giving one star is because the food was great. HOWEVER the customer service is non-existent and we were higly offended and had a horrible experience.
We both work in mortgage so customer service is a huge deal! PLEASE read on:

We were waiting in the general line, and since i am 6 months pregnant and was very hungry, my husband asked the cashiers on the VIP side if we can pay extra to skip the line, the lady proceeded to tell him sure come over here and wait. So he pulled me out of line and we stood in the express line. After waiting a while we asked her if we can pay already, since the other general line was already moving along. She said "i have to take the vips first" mind you there were hardly any people walking up on the VIP side, we asked again a few minutes later since the general line was moving and we could already have been closer, she responded ill get my manager. We said fine!

Manager comes over and we explained the situation, and that we could have just stayed in the general line and saved time and hassle. She apologized and asked us to go ahead and pay, SO another cashier takes us and although we didn't pay the extra charge (why should we when we could have been there already at general line) but she did not ask us our name for the party on the ticket.
And so she took it upon herself to type on the reciept that our party name was "ANGRY"!!!! SERIOUSLY WE WERE LIVID!
