Our entire interaction was calm and honest we just said it like it was, never were we angry, regardless of the fact what kind of person types the customer's name as ANGRY!??? 
Did i mention i am 6 months pregnant!? this discriminatory action and unprofessional customer service is totally unacceptable. This is ceasars palace?? Ha! didnt feel like it!

The manager came over and when we showed her the reciept she was embarrased turned red and appologized continuously. She reveresed the charge and gave me a complaint form to fill out. She said someone will contact us about the incident in a couple days, its been over two weeks now and no one has called us!!! so this is the review they get!!! and i will continue to spread this rediculous action we experienced at supposedly the nicest Buffet in vegas people spend hundreds on!!??? i think not!

I am a big buffet eater and I must say, I was so impress with the Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace. My family and I went there for their weekend brunch and it was amazing. By far this is the best buffet I've been to. It is an upscale buffet and you get your money's worth. Plenty of selections, servers are nice, its clean, awesome atmosphere, modern and most of all FOOD is so GOOD.
Overpriced, long lines. Noisy. Only one variety of fish--salmon--and even for that had to wait. Rude sitters and the cashier.  Paris and Wynn were much better.

Bacchanal is a pretty good buffet. I was able to find a selection of different foods that I wanted to try, and most of them I enjoyed. 
I am not a huge fan of buffets because sometimes they don't have anything I feel like eating, or the quality is not that great.
I've been to this buffet a few times, and I have not had a bad experience yet.
It is a bit more expensive than other buffets in different properties, but I did not feel like I overpaid. 
I just wish the desserts were a little better.
Always a great option for breakfast.  Shrimp, rock crab, Alaskan crab options out front.  Great carving station.  Constant refills on mimosas.  Only problem is they won't let you stay there all day.

MOCHI AND ICE CREAM SERVERS MISSING PERSONALITY CHIP.

The 2 ladies assigned on the evening of 5/11/13 were so unpleasant to customers.  They both acted like they didn't want to serve or do their job.    You would think that the own the dessert section.  I was in line and not only they can only give you 2 mochi at a time but they were passing the duty to each other.  They charge a lot of money for the dinner buffet and these two ladies acted like they were assigned there to erase the DUI from their records.  

The lady with bangs said, "I don't serve mochi" when I asked her if I can have mochi.  Then the other non smiling short lady told her and she handed me mochi, unwillingly as if it was coming from her pay check.  They are missing the meaning of "serve" in their title "server".

I asked to speak to the Manager about their attitude and rudeness and the young manager give me the memorized speech about  "how sorry she is about the attitude of the 2 ladies and thanked me for bringing it to her attention....." but did not do anything about it. 

These attitude of  workers ruined our dinner.  We expected from from Cesar's Pace staff and I hope someone counsels the dessert servers.

Deep in Caesar Palace's, it can be a little confusing to get to this buffet if it's your 1st time. Luckily my BF has gone several time so I just followed his weaving path through the casino.

To check-in they have these kiosks to put you on a virtual waitlist that will text you when your table is ready. $20 if you want express waitlist. I would never pay that but my BF was contemplating it. Though the 1st time I went with my BF, the kiosk said the wait was an hour. 10min later, he got a text saying our table was ready so not sure how accurate the waiting estimate is (and good thing we didn't spend the extra $20!). If you're with a group of 6+, go line up in the large group line in the back. So much shorter! They will not seat you though until the entire party is present.

Mimosas are included at brunch. There's usually hardly anY orange flavor to them for me so I usually order a glass of OJ to pour in.

Love the Aqua Fresca that they have. Some flavors I've seen were Watermelon, Tamarind, Horchata, Guava (can't remember the rest). My favorite are the Horchata and the Watermelon. So good!!

The taco station is good and pretty cool to watch the chef making the tacos on the rotating griddle.

The dim sum they had during Lunar New Year's surprisingly isn't half bad for a buffet. Tried the Shrimp Dumplings (har gow), Shrimp and Pork Dumplings (shu mai), and Soup Dumplings (XLB). I've had worse at actual restaurants!

Love the Stone Crab Claws and Chilled Shrimp. The Stone Crab Claws are partially cut for easier cracking but I usually still ask for a crab cracker to get all the meat from them. The Snow Crab Legs are pretty decent if you pick out the good meaty pieces. They're already split for you for easy eating. Tried the Lobster Benedict but couldn't taste or see any lobster, so if you just wanted an Eggs Benedict, it would be pretty good.

The nigiri and sushi rolls tasted alright. At least the nigiri didn't look questionable where you'd worry about getting food poisoning.

The Chicken & Waffles in a Basket was very cute but super dry and salty. Another time, they had Spicy Chicken & Fries in a Waffle Cone that was really tender but was too spicy for me. BF liked the spiciness but thought it was too salty.

Lots of cheese & dried fruits at the cheese station. I usually grab a few pieces of Brie and Dried Apricots to nibble on.

Nice salad bar with non-wilted looking greens and a good amount of salad topping options.

The Pork Belly on Lentils was very salty, dry, and mostly fat. The ramen was very mediocre and no body at the table finished theirs. The Chinese Poorridge (jook) faired a bit better.

Saw that they serve Boba next to the Gelato station but didn't look too appetizing. The cake desserts always looks so pretty but have been generally pretty dry. Love getting the gelato and adding the roasted hazelnut bits on top. Tried the Habanero Mango, Melon, Black Sesame, Green Tea Mint, and Pistachio. Liked all but the Green Tea Mint (was just too weird of a flavor combination even though I love both flavors individually).

Servers are pretty good aT refilling drinks and clearing the table even though the buffet's almost always packed, so tip them well!

I haven't tried all the Vegas buffets, but of the ones I've tried thus far.. this one is definitely the top one! Not sure how often I'd come though because my friends and I are no longer in our college days and can't eat as much as we used to.. -_-||

Kind of new no mans land for this review. the buffet cost $55. yes. FIFTY FIVE. I was not pleased. The food was good though, the waiting in line part was not cool. I mean hell, it's a buffet, wtf. 

Def not worth $55. Maybe $30sh. So it's 3 stars for ehhhhh.

This buffet did not stand out as I thought it would for the price. For 2 people it cost $124.00 plus tip (that you pay up front). I expected at the very least a nice table and food that exceeded your average/everyday buffet that I can get in my home town. I had to squeeze past other people's tables and move empty chairs out of the way to get to my table at every trip to and from the buffet. After leaving a $20 tip, my husband and I had to flag waiter down more than once to get water refill. As far as the food, I have been to Vegas many times and you can get better quality and selections at many other buffets in Vegas at a much lower price. I will not be returning.

This place is over rated.  The line to pay and get in is crazy long and when you get into the buffet there are more lines (especially the seafood section) to get your food. The food wasn't even all that,  bad presentation,  mediocre in taste and on this occasion,  it made most of the people in our party run to the restroom (food poisoning, ahhhh). All for $55, what a bargain? Not. Perhaps the only good thing about it was the dessert bar,  but never again would I go to this buffet.

$41.99 for brunch. $40.99 if you have a Total Rewards Card.

Overrated. Absolutely overrated and not worth the price. I would have been so much happier and $10 richer if I had just gone to Wicked Spoon instead. Seafood selection is slim. I did appreciate crab legs, shrimp, and mussels but I was super disappointed to see them shucking oysters but not having them during brunch.

I liked the dim sum bar. Prime rib was nothing noteworthy. Sushi was mediocre.

The hype keeps this place busy but I will pass on this in the future.

Worth every penny. Fresh seafood, diverse spread. I mean everything we tried was delicious! Make sure you try the fresh fruit juice. I mean, I am at a loss for words and I am never at loss for words. This was the best buffet I've had in my life...don't even consider any of he other buffet options in Vegas.

AYCE elote!  That's all I gots to say!  This buffet is your above average musings!  Except for the gnocchi, which was dry...ending was divine!  There is a line for the fresh seafood (snow crab legs - steamed and cold, peeled shrimp, oysters, scallops, gumbo, paella, bloody Mary oyster shooters, coconut milk fish shooters, miso salmon).  BBQ section was terrific - fries, beer battered onion rings, brisket, prime rib, chicken wings, sausage, beef ribs, Texas and KC BBQ sauces, corn, mac n cheese, mashed potatoes, au jus).  Soups - minestrone, clam chowder.  Street tacos - al pastor, carne adana, chicken asada.  Nacho bar, ceviche.  Cheese - blue, brie, cheddar, prosciutto, apricots, apricot jam.  Siopao - mung bean and pork; roast duck, pork, chicken.  Pizzas!  Pasta bar!  Osso buco, beef lasagna, chicken parm.  Lechon.  The desserts - Thai iced tea float with Boba, jasmine rice pudding, strawberry jelly stuff, mango jelly stuff, crepe bar, Gelato, fresh fruit.  Mimosas cost extra - St. Germain and guava - $12 each, but there is a $15 bottomless option for regular Mimosas and beer.  Worth every cent, worth the 70 minute wait, will come back!  There is a two hour limit...took us 2 hours and 45 minutes, still managed to walk upright!  The best in Vegas!

We had been waiting for a while to try out the revamped Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's. Wonderful selection of higher end food for a Vegas buffet. Oyster's, Lamb, Cold or Steamed Crab legs, Desserts Galore.

BUT...Here are the issues which made this place lose all its stars...

1) We all got some sort of food poisoning from eating there, and it wasn't the meat because there was a vegetarian in our group who had the same result.

2) The lamb was inedible. It was rubbery and tough.

3) Checking in, we waited in a line for 15 minutes and when we got to the front desk, they said we needed to get back in line in 20 minutes because the line to get in after that line was too long (it was really short so we scratched our heads). The next party was told the same thing, and then everyone behind us was let in, so we in effect were made to wait in 3 lines. We were dressed nicely and we're pretty average looking, so I don't think that was an issue - most folks in Vegas are in shorts and flip flops anyhow.

4) The price is more than most of the other Vegas buffets. There's too many good buffets to justify it. Go to the Wynn or Cosmopolitan instead for more expensive buffets or you can hit the 3 1/2 star buffets at the Rio (there's two) for a good buffet.

Note: Not very good for vegetarians. I saw a Yelp review of the Cosmopolitan Buffet that said there were quite a few vegetarian friendly dishes there.

I'm not sure if we'll keep coming here after our latest experience.  The service and presentation was still spectacular, but some of the most coveted entrees left something to be desired.  The Prime Rib was tough and literally inedible, and the crab legs were hard to slide out of the shells, and weren't served on the half shell any longer.  The cocktail shrimp was still jumbo and luscious, and that Mac and Cheese though!  Honestly, it might be worth paying the price just for that.  As a die hard crab leg fan though, we might have to make a switch next year.

This is the best buffet I have ever been to. They have all types of food. American, BBQ, Seafood, Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, Mexican and more.

THE TRICK TO THIS PLACE IS TO GO RIGHT BEFORE 3PM BECAUSE THATS WHEN THEY BRING OUT THE DINNER FOOD and you can get it for Lunch price.

Almost everything is here great, BUT, YOU MUST GET THE BRISKET. OMG.

B R I S K E T B O Y S

The brisket is so good juicy soft and tender. I kept getting more like a fiend. I actually went here twice and the 2nd time I went I got nothing but Brisket, Crab Legs and Shu Mai.

The dessert I had was also awesome. I got this Nutella Coffee Gelato which was off the hook. I told my friend to go get it for dessert and he comes back with a Piece of Chicken inside of a Waffle Cone. Hilarious. 

There is usually a line but its worth it!
I will definitely be back next time I'm in Vegas.
Absolutely delicious, gourmet food with so many options. A lot of interesting things you won't see at other buffets.

My husband and I ate here on our honeymoon last week.  There were definitely an endless amount of options to choose from.  We came for lunch and it was about $80.  This might not be mentioned much, but we love iced tea, and their iced tea was brewed perfectly and fresh.  The service was great.  My husband loves seafood, so he stuck mostly with the raw oysters and shrimp.  My favorite thing was the MUSHROOM TRUFFLE SOUP.  To die for.  The only thing that wasn't that impressive was the Asian food offerings.  The options were plenty, but they were dried up and without flavor.  The hot and sour soup was goopy and thick.  The Asian food offerings at the Bellagio buffet were better in my opinion.  The CREME BRULEE and FLAN desserts were DELICIOUS.  Crème brulee and flan are favorites of mine, so I've had plenty and all over, and I must say, their crème brulee and flan were the best I've had in a long time.  If you are looking for meat, there is plenty.  I would eat here again and just not try any of the Asian food offerings.

Vegas is really stepping up its buffet game.

This buffet is located in Caesars Palace. Our group of 4 arrived on a Monday evening in January around 7pm with no wait at all. The look and feel of this place surpasses Wicked Spoon already (I still love Wicked Spoon!). Dinner price was $50/head.

The food setup and display is very similar to WS as they get creative with their displays.  There's also a meat station (it was prime rib and lamb when we went), dim sum area, seafood (crab legs!), sushi, and much much more.  Desserts included a crepe station, gelato, creme brulee, macaroons, gummy bears, and other favorites.

By far one of the better buffets on the strip, along with Wicked Spoon.  Will likely be back!

Try to come before the lunch rush, as that could save you 30-40min waiting once the lines get packed! Typical lunch price is about $50 and dinner is $7-10 more. Watch out for holidays as the price will be bumped up.

Once you get in line to pay, you have to get into another line to be seated, depending on how big your party is. This is the longest part of the wait. Once through, there's a plethora of seafood, meat, Asian cuisine, pastas, desserts, etc.

As a person that doesn't eat seafood, it's a bit hard to make your money's worth. I usually start with a mini pho or miso soup and then slowly make my way to the heavier foods. There's only so much steak I can eat to make my money's worth though, and more often than not--I don't eat enough.

If you love seafood, this place is for you as you can make it worth your money, if not, get ready because you'll need to eat a ton!

I remember I used to be super impressed by this place, but I think the novelty has worn off.  It's still REALLY good, but some issues here and there.

Usually there's this ridiculous line just to sign in, then you have to wait HOURS to get a text letting you know you can now STAND IN LINE.  Dinner runs about $50/person.  I think lunch was about $40, don't remember.  My boyfriend and I came here a few weekends ago and got here around maybe 3 something pm?  There was NOBODY in line. We were confused.  Are they even open? We decided to see what other people were doing and saw them walk right up to the front and get in line to be seated.  Whaaaat!

So we get there, wait in line to be seated for a little bit, and then get seated.  I love the range of options they have.  Presentation is always nice as well.  They have a good meat section (boyfriend's fave) and I like the little noodle nook they have where they have ramen, pho, etc.

There were a few things that were ehhh. Some foods were empty for the longest time.  This time around it was the truffle gnocchi.  I finally snagged some and it was cold.  WTH.  And a few other food items were cold.

Love the crepe station! Those were def not cold.

Very professional and friendly staff.

Thursday May 19 2016 6PM checked in at kiosk
TL;DR
Wait: about 45 minutes keep in mind our time frame though.
Lines at food stations: seafood was longest at like 8 people others had 1 or 2.
Price: $60 without tip add unlimited beer wine champagne for $20
Service: they did there job well for a busy place
Seafood: mediocre
American: meats were great, sides were good but simple
Mexican: meh IMO
Italian: looked good but I wanted to save space for more adventurous food.
Asian: awesome selection, some OK, some amazing.
Desserts: good, just wish I wasn't so full by the time I tried it lol.

Let me start by saying my company paid for this meal so I will not be heavily weighing the value of the food for the price paid. Also we came for dinner and with $10 tip it came to $70 for anyone wondering. If you wanted to add unlimited drinks it was an extra $18 (which I don't consider bad at all but my friend and I were still a little hungover from the night before)

When you go to wait you first check-in at a kiosk. Ours said 60-71 minute wait but we weren't in a hurry so we walked around and checked the gambling tables and the shops at the forums. They texted us probably 15 minutes later to tell us to come back. You go back and then you really wait in line, for us it was about 30 minutes in line. So overall 45 minute wait, and this was started at 6pm on a Thursday in the middle of may.

The service was good for how busy they were, drinks were always filled and finished plates were taken. 

The food here is very diverse and there are A LOT of options so pace yourself if you want to try everything. The seafood was OK but pretty basic. The crab legs were not Alaskan king crab legs but just the regular ones. I will note that I saw a table that had king crab legs but they were "VIP" so I guess higher retired guests get a better experience, but hey they did pay for it. Other than that the seafood was mediocre for a "high end" buffet. Shrimp, clams, scallops, oysters, different fish prepared different ways, nothing amazing though.

Next I tried the meats/Americans section which was very good. The prime rib was very good and the au jus worked well with its. The lamb and sausage were also very good, along with the pulled pork. Fried chicken and fries were good but nothing special. There was also your plain old mashed potatoes and gravy,  Mac and cheese, and veggies but I was saving as much room for more interesting food as possible.

The Mexican section was nothing to rave about, the street tacos were OK and nothing else really looked good (to me that is).

Next was the Italian section where I ate nothing. This is just because I didn't want to waste space on bread and pasta, etc. Also there's only so much that can be done with Italian food and I've tried my fair share.

And then we have Asia, my favorite cuisine. The selection was amazing the only thing I was missing was some Korean BBQ. They had tonkotsu ramen which was OK, very salty and the flavors were OK. The pho was good for a buffet too. The did have crispy duck through and I splurged on that! Probably about half a duck cooked perfectly. The sushi was good for a buffet, better than the buffet sushi back home. There were some good octopus dishes too. Then there was dumplings and egg roles fried rice and noodles, udon soup as well. They tried to focus on real Asian food and not as much americanized Asian from what I could tell and I loved it.

Lastly deserts were very good but didn't have much room to fully enjoy them lol. They were doing crepes to order so I got a Nutella crepe with banana topping and whip creme, which was amazing. They had ice cream and gelato but was too full to try that after tarimisu, creme brule, flan, and coffee cake. There were also some cake pops and plain looking cookies.

Overall it was a great experience, I would probably go back if I had not eaten all day and was celebrating something special.

We knew this was going to be the pricier meal of our trip but it was worth it. I paid approximately $60 for all-you-can-eat weekend brunch, without booze. As much as I love a good mimosa, I didn't want to fill up on liquid. We were here for food and we meant business. 
Reasons why I felt I got the full value of that $60 meal:
1. I went for the seafood first. You know that stuff is expensive and it is much less common in my life than some white or red meat. This means King crab legs, Cajun shrimp and grits, green mussels, lobster bisque, lox bagel  and lobster eggs benedict. Yes, I did eat all that.
2. The dishes are constantly being replaced with other dishes. I walked around 3/4 of the buffet every time I got another plate because where there was oatmeal and grits, there is now biscuits and gravy. Keep your eyes open and make sure to grab the things you really want before they're gone (they'll probably come back again but will you have space in your stomach by then? Doubtful).
3. Fancy cheeses and charcuterie! I made myself a personal plate that would cost at least $20 as an appetizer anywhere. Just take a slice of each. Remember, this is a marathon, not a sprint. Oh and they had fresh honey and jams too! My cheese plate round was FANCY.
4. If you do have enough room to eat some more after you hit the best stuff, go for the classics. I got a slice of prime rib, huevos rancheros, Mac & cheese, and fried chicken. Again, take small pieces because you're going to want to try it all!

Two things I will say that go beyond how delicious the food was: I wish one alcoholic beverage was included. No I don't want bottomless mimosas for $15 but yes I would like one. Cheers. Second comment is the crepe line was hella long and only got longer. We were lucky and got in before the major crowds come (the difference between 10:50am and 11am, folks). Only one person makes crepes on two burners. Each takes a good minute or two. Do the math, it's going to be a wait. If you want a crepe, even for later, go if there isn't too much of a line. Or don't go at all. They looked really good but I wasn't willing to wait ~20 minutes.

Overall, delish. I'm very happy with my six rounds of food and wouldn't change a thing (except to get ONE mimosa if they ever decide to offer that).

BEST. BUFFET. IN. VEGAS.  I love the variety of food they have at this buffet.  They separate everything into different sections to make it easier for the guest to pick what they want so that not everyone is cramped into one section at once.  The buffet itself is definitely on the pricey side but for the amount and quality of food you get it is well worth it.  My only regret was that I also got the unlimited mimosas with it for brunch and it made me full faster so next time I'll skip the drinks and focus on the food.

It is one of the better buffets but I probably won't be back.

A. I don't think it's worth the 2 hour wait. You get a ticket or text and then you wait again. 
B. The crab legs were salty so I really couldn't eat much.
C. It was overpriced for what we got. $62.99 plus tax and tip. There are other buffets that are half the price but with a few less options of course.
D. There was no lobster.

Not very nonmeat eater friendly. Everything I thought that was suppose to be vegetarian had meat in it, lentil soup, congee soup, potatoes, the rice, . . .uh everything. I do fish too, but the fish at the sushi station was just ok. I think what was more sad was that when I left at 3:30 I noticed they had pulled out different dishes including more fish entrees. I was angry. Oh well. There were a lot of cute looking dishes. Little quail eggs on top of corned beef hash or pizza. red velvet pancakes. I didn't really enjoy my experience here, cause there was nothing for me to eat. Omelette station was gone by the time I went. I liked the truffle potatoes. I ate about 8 macaroons. The fig balsalmic gelato was good. Mimosas took forever to come. So did my water. Service sucks. Is what I am saying. For the price, I would go somewhere else. The place is nice though.

Very nice buffet. I am staying at Cesar's palace and wanted breakfast and selected this place because my other breakfast option(Cafe Americano) cost point was very close $25 vs $30).  I will come back again. Highly recommended.

The food selection was great and tasty. However, the bottomless champagne was cheap and destroyed the whole meal experience. Disappointing. For 4 dollars more I got much higher quality champagne at the Wynn Buffet.

The decor the presentation of food alone deserve 4 stars.  The food was a class up from standard buffet food.  The up market stations of seafood and carving, the quality and selection was impressive.  The Asian station also bountiful of appetizing selections.  You can taste yourself silly with a huge variety of foods- over eat- and roll out the door.  It was a request of a guest that we dine here- otherwise I'm not a fan of buffets, but had wanted to see what the fuss was about.  As far as buffet's go it is superior.

My wife and I went there for the first and last time today. Beautiful decor and the food presentation was terrific but ... There was one "hot" food item we tried that was more than luke warm. Hot food should be kept around 135 degrees or hotter. Really tasty chowder - luke warm; fried chicken with sweet potato fries - luke warm chicken and cold fries; brisket - luke warm. Having suffered from food poisoning a little over a month ago at my own hand I was reluctant to finish anything that isn't at the proper temperature. We told a "manager" who acted concerned and said she'd tell the chef. Tell the chef? How about serving food at a proper and safe temperature. The scary thing? They had an "A" rating from the LV Health Inspection. Maybe I need to start carrying around my own thermometer when I go out from now on. Disgusting. This place was cheap and I expected better.
The Caesars Buffet was very good the food qualitly and selection were good, i enjoyed the manny selections that they had to offer,, By far the best buffet in Las Veagas.

This buffet is absolutely delicious!!  I advise everyone to go try this buffet out at least a few times.  The thing that I don't agree with is the price.  Although, the buffet was delicious, I don't feel that it was worth he price.  If it was about 7 bucks less, I would have absolutely no complaints about this buffet!

I honestly think this buffet was a teeeeeeeeeeny bit over-hyped. Don't get me wrong, the food was pretty good -- but I wouldn't say that this was, hands down, the BEST BUFFET EVER.

Luckily, our group of 7 had moseyed in right before the lunch pricing ended, so we only had to pay $32.99/person as opposed to $50.99/person for the dinner pricing. I would've been much more upset if I had paid over $50. For that price, I honestly don't think it's worth it, but I'd be willing to spend $35 again.

The food just didn't seem very appealing to me! The arroz rojo at the Mexican station was a little bland to me. The ramen was the same. The salmon was pretty good, and so were the endless crab legs (though I only ate 2 before I got lazy of tearing the meat out with my hands). I enjoyed the brisket well enough as well as the sweet potato tater tots, but the gazpacho was gross. The lobster clam chowder was pretty good. The truffle potato gratin was TO DIE FOR and I think the best food item I had that day.

I just felt like there wasn't as varied of a selection as I was informed there would be. Where was lobster, and the crab croquettes? Where was the lamb?? Maybe those options are only for dinner, but I felt like what was offered for lunch was pretty typical of any buffet, so I didn't feel like pricing -- or the hype -- was deserved.

The saving grace of this buffet is its' dessert spread -- I think this is where Bacchanal really shines. The macarons and mochi were pretty good (though you're only allowed to get 2 mochi at a time, due to demand). The chocolate crème brûlée is MUCH better than the regular one, and there was an oreo chocolate-y creamy concoction thing that I couldn't stop eating.

Our server was very nice (though I honestly think we scared her by how fast our group stacked up plates and plates and PLAAATES of destroyed crab legs), and she brought us coffee, tea and water refills repeatedly and was even kind enough to inform us that espresso would be an additional price if we wanted it (some servers would've just brought it and tacked on the price without an explanation).

I would be hesitant to come back. Maybe for dinner, but the price genuinely scares me away a bit. What I saw of the lunch spread wasn't too impressive, but maybe their dinner options are a lot better?

Lots of options! Asian, seafood, barbecue and American, Mexican, Italian, roasted pig and dessert. Unfortunately, not all of the food was fresh and some was cold. The staff wasn't really friendly either, and at $65 dollars a person I really expected a better experience. 

What was good you ask? The steamed crab legs, dim sum, raw oysters, roasted pig and the hot chocolate. This might sound like a lot but I had to taste a lot of undesirable food too.
Bacchanal Buffet in Ceasars Palace is Hands Down the best buffet in Las Vegas! While I have had many previous favorite go-to buffets in the past, nothing comes close to Bacchanal!

I'm pretty impressed with Caesars Palace's buffet. I've heard all the stories about how amazing it is, and they lived up to it.

Bacchanal is probably the pricest buffet on the strip, but for a reason, it has been voted the best buffet in Vegas, and there are a lot of buffets in Vegas. Depending on the day, your wait could be anywhere from 30 minutes to 4 hours. I came for a Friday dinner and it was only a 30 minute wait. After we entered, the buffet, the amazingness started.

Their selection of food is vast. They have everything from Asian food, to BBQ, seafood, and Mexican food. There are so many things to get, that it is hard to decide what you might want to eat. Even though it is a buffet, the quality of the food doesn't suffer because it is a buffet, it's equivalent to eating at a really nice restaurant. My favorites were the seafood, BBQ, and Mexican section. Everything tasted great and I couldn't get enough of the scallops, that was by far my favorite! One of the best things I liked was that you could get your own juice that they preportioned in bottles. The horchata was amazing as well as the pina, which was made to the perfect sweetness for my taste. After dinner, came dessert, and their dessert selection is no joke either. All of their desserts look, and taste quality. I had almost one of everything it seemed. My favorite was their mocha macaron hands down. Everything was so delicious and I can't wait until I can make another visit!

I had high hopes for this place. I mean, really, a place named "Bacchanal"? I expected an amazing (I wanted to use a different word but you know, let's keep it clean, kids) eating experience and that's exactly what I got. But as with all first times, things can be learned. 

If you go for brunch, try to go a little bit later. My friends and I got there around 10 am on a Saturday hoping to beat the line (that wasn't there, btws) and although I think we were able to get a good idea of what Bacchanal had to offer, we missed out on the following: the Italian food and more importantly, the SOUFFLES. They aren't available until 3 pm on weekends. Had we known, different decisions would've been made.

Favorites: sweet potato tater tots, anything that had a quail egg on it (oh. so. good), the CRAB (don't forget the clarified butter!), and the gelato -- which we were able to get on the way out and enjoy whilst we walked around the casino! 

Oh yeah, did I mention the unlimited mimosas? I think I really only had 3-4 glasses but eh, who am I to turn down free booze? And you know, it's Vegas. A meal without booze is basically sinful. 

I think this is probably my favorite Vegas buffet thus far. The varied offerings and the more hits-than-misses (in fact, I'm trying pretty hard right now to think of any glaring misses and I'm coming up empty) make it a great bang for your buck!

Always a bit pricey, I have been here 4 times now and this time wasnt as good as normal. The food was good,but the service was not what it used to be. we came in with a party of 7. We were seated pretty quick since we had a big party. They took about 15 minutes after seating just to come take out drink orders and were slow clearing off our old plates. To me this used to be a 4 or 5 star place, but seems like the service is getting worse. They also ran out of plates at the dessert station and took them more than 20 minutes to refill them.

Absolutely amazing buffet, we visited las Vegas a few weeks ago and decided to try this buffet. Terrific, great staff, large selections of everything. Without a doubt I will be back in there summer when I visit Vegas again.

The guys were in town for golf week and the second night we went to Bacchanal.  Usually, we go to Wynn, or Bellagio.  Since this was new, we would give it a go.  

Right away, the set up is the best of all buffets.  The food stations surround the dining area so you don't get people winding through your tables for food.  There is a design flow.  There were enough food stations, so one area doesn't get overloaded.

The service was prompt, drinks and plates were taken right away.  Our server was a hardworking and polite guy.  We made sure the tip was generous.

Best of all is the food.  It is set up by cuisine - Asian, Italian, Meat, etc.  I didn't expect much from the Asian station.  Over the years, and relatives, we know Asian buffet.  Surprisingly, the duck, Char Siu, and some other Chinese dishes we quite good.  The sushi was mediocre. The Italian was very good.  Little plate of lasagna, little container of calamari, both outstanding.  

Sure, they had all sorts of cold meats, cheeses, salads, and the usual buffet things. Even a Mexican and Seafood station. Why waste the space on the common stuff? Fill on Mac n Cheese, fries, burritos and buffalo wings?  The seafood was King crab legs which is naturally excitingly bland. 

The meat station was the best of all.  They had prime rib, beef brisket, lamb chops, and Carolina Smoked Bacon. Ahh! Bacon.  This is a must have item of the buffet.  A big pork belly slice of smoked, glistening, mouth watering delight.  As my friend said,  " An orgasm in the mouth".  

There were a ton of desserts.  Mochi ice cream, assorted gelatos, small baked items - cakes and pies.

All in All, we sampled about 1/3 of all that was offered and that's a lot.  We are two good sized guys and three small guys that eat like horses and we were there almost two and a half hours.  Have fun.

Currently the best buffet in Vegas.  All the standards (peeled shrimp, Alaskan king crab legs, etc) with the addition of traditional Chinese, Italian, BBQ and so much more.  

The best items imho are the seafood specialty items (mini clam bakes, puff pastries filled with seafood, etc.)

The price is a bit high and it does get crowded.  As a New Yorker I use the trick to go at 3 or 4 when the lines aren't long.

***NOTE: A lot of the really "Cool" items pictured on Yelp are not currently available. (Whole Crab, lobster, Honey comb, Souffle) ***

We went to this place and paid over $100 for two people for dinner. First off it wasnt easy to find, The people who you pay, are not friendly. I know I am not VIP, but I sure as shit didnt just pay $100 for you to act like I have to wait in line longer after paying for 2 other groups to be sat before me. 

The table we sat at was within arms reach of the other 2 tables next to us. Our sever gave us the first round of drinks and then never came back the whole time we were there. We tried asking other wait staff, but didnt get a drink until someone saw us get the Jar Drinks from the buffet line as a last resort. 

They do offer a lot of food, however, a lot of it is flavorless. The prime rib (which i was so looking forward too) was so cold, flavorless and chewy that I gave up eating it after 2 bites. They also offer crab legs, but they are split down the middle and dont offer a lot of meat, the peel and eat shrimp was still frozen by the time I tried eating it. This was barely better then the buffet we had a the Excalibur hotel the night before. The main difference? Bacchanal had macaroons and Excalibur was half price. 

I did get sick after eating here. Not too surprised. I tried calling to let them know cause it was the only thing we had eaten since breakfast, but no one answered. 

My husband did say the street tacos were good, and I did like some of the "Asian" style food they had.  The ribs were ok, dessert was ok, but a lot of the cheese cake items and flan tasted over cooked or like they had been sitting out too long.  Id rather go to golden corral before going back to Bacchanal.   We did go to The Wicked Spoon, the day before, that was amazing, go there, not Bacchanal.

If you want to splurge and you have the chance, go. It's not all it's hyped up to be, but it's good and an experience. I don't think it's worth the money, but we've gone twice already. Our server was attentive, but midway she introduced another server to us, as her shift was ending. I mentioned we left her a tip when we paid and that was a mistake because the new guy heard that and we were thirsty after that. Unless we hunted him down, he did not come back to check on us or refill our drinks. 

There are a variety of choices of food and some were really good, but most were just ok. The brisket was AMAZING...and I'm from Texas, so I know good brisket. Our son really loved the sliders and our daughter ate 3 plates of the potato noodles.  My husband enjoyed the seafood.  The desserts were just ok, but there is a good variety.

Super long line....entire party must be there just to pay, i understand if they cant seat me if everyone in my party is not present, but just to pay???... our service lady was great, 5 stars for her. Food presentation was impressive, too bad the taste wasnt. Either bland or super salty. Make sure to check for little bugs flying around/landing on the food before you grab your food. Not sure if ill want to go back...

Caesar palace buffet

The food was great,  but the service was so BAD!!  I arrived at 9:30pm, waited in line and paid at 9:41pm,  seated after 10 minutes.  From the time we arrived till the   time we seated we were greeted by a girl at end of the line , a cashier , an employee who showed us to our table and our waiteress. None of them telling us the buffet was closing at 10pm.  They still had a lot of food when we started eating.  Food was great,  fresh. As soon as we were about to go get more food around 10:40pm,  we found out all the food was gone,  all disappeared,  all stations cleaned up,  the only food left were some desserts,  however only about half of selections left. I know we came in at late time, but NOBODY gave us any kitchen last call notice.  We would only need 5 min heads up time to get the food if they could kindly remind us. However it didn't happened. Our waitress didn't tell us, none of the employee did.  We ended up have to take whatever left in desserts to finish our $55 per person meal.  
I think it is ridiculous, so I talked to an employee at the cashier,  she asked if the girl at the entrace told me about the kitchen closing time,  I said no.  She asked how about the waitress,  I said no.  So she went find her manager.  A few minutes,  the manager came and asked me the same questions. He (and none of the employees) didn't apologize for the bad service,  he only said he would reflect the incident to the management. He did ask if he could get any food we wanted.At that moment we were eating the desserts and we were so upset,  we just finished up and left.  I wasn't expecting to get my $ back or any free meals,  but to be honest that is not the service I would expect at a luxury hotel casino buffet. Very disappointed and I would never go back to Caesar Palace buffet again.

Eating at Bacchanal was a spiritual experience for me, though it was preceded by five hours at a day club without eating anything the entire day and drinking minimal water. So perhaps, eating anywhere would have felt just as magical at that point. Nevertheless, this buffet is one of the reasons I keep trying to plan another Vegas trip.

For $59.99 for a weekend dinner (which comes close to $70 when you add tip), it is pricey, but definitely worth it. I went with a party of seven at 5PM on a Saturday, and though we did have to wait a bit, we were able to go to a separate line for bigger groups which was much quicker. The cashier who checked us out was super friendly as well and our server was super attentive, who tried her best to accommodate us when we were seated in an area that was particularly cold.

I especially love Bacchanal because of the variety. I'm a super picky eater but there were so many different choices for everyone. Dim sum, tacos, steaks, seafood, pasta - everything I could dream of, including the ability to create a custom crepe and pair it with ice cream! I wish I had more room in my stomach because by the end of it, I had to plan out and prioritize what to consume.

The ALMIGHTY buffet of all buffets in Las Vegas! 
If you are into AYCE and you came to Vegas looking to eat, then this place is definitely a must try.  The only reason its 4 stars vs. 5stars is because I had to during dinner time and having to pay $50 really hurt my wallet. 

However, would i do it again?  Probably would.  Why? Because this buffet is definitely aesthetically pleasing in their presentation and layout.  Not every item was a scoop and serve feel but some were plated and decorated so beautifully it was hard eating it because it was pretty (such like the watermelon feta salad in a chess square formation)  

Also, this is one of the few buffets in my list that do not skimp on the QUALITY vs quantity.  It might be a buffet but each dish definitely tasted fresh and flavorful with all quality meats and produce. 

I'll be visiting this buffet very soon as this buffet is one of the top on my list. 
Others include: Wicked Spoon, M Resort Studio buffet, and Bellagio (in no particular order)
Would give six stars if possible!  Quality selection...excellent flavors...comfortable atmosphere...wonderful service.  I support the report that it is the best buffet on the strip!

I regret that I made so many trips to Vegas and this is the first time I tried their buffet. All I can say is this is the best buffet that I had so far in Vegas a buffet lover:) even though it was a little pricey. There r so many choices and u could tell the food r really good quality. I tried the oyster because they super fresh and I just couldn't resist :) lol I tried almost all of their desserts, none of them disappoint me. I would definitely come back to this place for my next trip. First choice on my buffet list

Love and Hate relationship about this place. 

Love: 
I would say the food offerings is about 80% Asian. (Jook Station, Sushi, Dim Sum)
They have Stone Crab here, that's awesome!
They have a soup/noodle station
They have a variety of juices: Tamarindo, Mango, and the usual ones
They have Peking Duck that I think it's better than Mr. Chow's.
Service is quite good
Love plates are nearby serving stations

Hate: 
The lines are out the door, well not literally but it's at least an hour usually
Dent in the wallet book
The way the line works towards the dim sum area in the back, hard to navigate

More Love than Hate, that's usually my Motto anyways. Guess I'll be coming back afterall.

Overall not impressed for the price. We even got in for the lunch price as they were switching to dinner selections. Don't get me wrong it's a really nice buffet. But it's a buffet. Very disappointed at the very few "small plate" presentations found during our visit. Vast majority of the food is served in the more traditional communal  "trough of food" style from which you spoon out your portion. The hype I had read led me to believe the majority of the food was prepared nearly to order and that's simply not my experience. For the price I was much more impressed with Wicked Spoon. Had their brunch price of $27, granted no crab legs for brunch but still liked their presentation and their dessert selection better.

Bacchanal is rated the #1 buffet in Las Vegas. Having the chance to visit one other buffet that shall remain nameless, I do understand why. Bacchanal is well organized and the food is pretty good. Enjoyed the nice variety. Its nearly impossible to try everything because there is so much to choose from. Overall, I really enjoyed the experience, and while it is a little pricey, it was worth the money, and I would encourage you to visit if you were in Vegas.

Bacchanal is the buffets of all buffets. If it is your mission to try every item - you will most likely fail because there is just SO much food. If you want to do Vegas right, you MUST stop by Bacchanal. The wait is worth it. The $25 express fee to skip the lines may be worth it as well. They have kiosks before the long lines where you enter in your phone number and they will text you when to come back to wait in line. The kiosk told me 2 hours but they texted me within 1 hour to come back. On a Tuesday night, I started waiting in line around 8:25pm and got seated at 9:40pm (they stop serving at 10:45pm). 

There is a wide selection of quality food. Everything LOOKS good and is presented very well but when it comes to taste I probably enjoyed only about 85% of the things I ate...which in retrospect is a lot given I am a girl with a massive appetite. I loved that the crab legs were already cut in half for us so we wouldn't have to crack them ourselves. The crab legs were very sweet, juicy and meaty. I really enjoyed the meat/BBQ selection...the prime rib was DIVINE. It was cooked to perfection and had just the right about of rare-ness to it. I decided to skip the Mexican section since it didn't look that appealing to me. The Asian food section was impressive. I was very amused as a Vietnamese person that they had pho! The dumplings/dim sum were very decent, I had to refrain from eating more to save room in my tummy. The sushi rolls here were MEH...but the hand rolls were on point. The pasta from the Italian section was lacking a bit of flavor...but the ravioli was awesome. The desserts were great! Give me flan and creme brûlée and I'm a happy camper. 

Management here is really great and all about customer service. They ran out of creme brûlée early and the people working behind the dessert section were adamant that they were completely out so we were disappointed...but the manager heard and made sure we got our creme brûlées! 

There were so many other things I wanted to try but was too afraid because they looked very filling. And I left here super, super full...

BEST BUFFET EVER. LITERALLY. WORTH THAT $55! 
BETTER THAN WICKED SPOON. 

Gosh this place is amazing. I was dying to come here. This place is super spacious and the table spacing itself is huge! Big enough for my numerous plates of food! Bacchanal is like a fancy restaurant serving EVERYTHING and ANYTHING you could imagine. Even their Asian dishes are pretty bomb. I underestimated their pho/ramen/udon (geez tons of noodle bowl choices right?) but wow they were even better than a cheap Asian restaurant! 

I went straight to the crab legs! Theres stacks and stacks of crab and it is all FRESH! So happy they cut it open for you, so all you have to do is, EAT! 
We were there for breakfast continuing onto lunch and their eggs and sausage were so tasty! They keep the food vibrant in color and it honestly tastes as good as it looks. 

There was a cute little chili dog station with fries, and sweet potatoes. The meat station with ribs and prime rib was pretty popular, but I didn't feel like eating that. It was nice to see the Mexican, pizza and soup and salad stations, but I just ate the crabs and went straight to the desserts right after! 

Their gelato wasn't too impressive. But their cakes were! I am a sucker for Pan Cotta and they had amazing pan cotta trio with chocolate and mango! 

Honestly you need to experience this place for yourself! You would feel like you're in FOOD HEAVEN here!

This was the first buffet I ever had in Vegas, so my gf and I wanted to try it out for lunch. You stand in line to pay first ($44 person). That line took at least 10 minutes. Then you go in another line to be seated. There are 4 different lines. One is VIP, 1-2 people, 3-5 people and large group line. We waited in line (1-2 people line) 30-45 minutes! Finally was seated and put in our drink order. The buffet had a good variety and another room around the corner with food. The food was good, but not out of this world good. Do not come here starving because you might actually die from starvation while waiting in line!  I'll probably not come here again and just try another place. You also have a 2 hour time limit. Not sure if that's the norm here in Vegas.

I came here for the champagne brunch and I didn't think the champagne portion was worth it.  Never had such pulpy mimosas in my life!  Other than that, the food is really good.  The chefs that work behind the counter are so sweet and give great service.  The highlights of my 3 hour eating escapade here were the gelato station (they had really unique gelato flavors!), prime rib, raw oysters, king crab legs, creme brulee, and fresh carrot juice.

Super impressed when I walked in... I mean it's a buffet, you don't expect much for the name...but I really enjoyed my food...for the most part. 

The Alaskan sea bass was HORRIBLE. everyone that had it at my table actually had to spit it out. My friend had unpleasant fries and they weren't very on top of keeping the food as fresh as it should be for what you're paying. 

Overall though, the majority of my food was really good and the desert buffet was to die for! 

I'd recommend it...for a buffet, but not as a restaurant to go out to in Las Vegas.

I have never written a Yelp review, but after last night's experience here, I feel if I can save just one person from wasting his or her money and time at this buffet, I will be doing my good deed of the day. I consider myself a major foodie, I have been in the food and restaurant business for 18 years, I own two very successful food trucks and I used to write restaurant reviews for our local paper. Let me put a disclaimer here, I do not eat red meat, so I came here to indulge in its seafood offerings. 
   My boyfriend and I got to the buffet around 4:15 on Sunday afternoon and there was already a huge queued line. We we told to sign in at the kiosk and we would be given a time to come back. We had two hours to whet out appetite, so we walked around the Venetian. We returned as instructed at 6:21 and were escorted to the end of the huge line. We were told there was still ANOTHER 2-hour wait. My boyfriend wanted to leave and I urged him to wait it out. After 10 minutes in line, we were approached by 3 people who asked us if we wanted to join them to form a group of 6 because there is another line for large groups of 6 or more and the wait is just an hour. I went with them and boyfriend stayed in original line just in case his would be faster. My new family of 5 recruited 4 more people in the line and went to wait with another mass of people. After about an hour, my alliance was corralled to pay $68 a person, sales tax and a forced 18% gratuity for a group of 8 or more. 
   I excitingly went up to the huge smorgasbord ready to indulge in the fruits of the sea. My first plate was stone crab claws, chilled snow crabs, raw oysters on the half shell, cold steamed shrimp and grilled prawns. The stone crab claws were over cooked and very hard to open, a nut cracker and small seafood fork was never offered, but this would not have helped with the sub par quality. The crab legs were very skimpy and split in half, but there was just not enough meat to make eating them satisfying. The posted menu stated snow crabs and King crabs were on the buffet, but there were no king legs to be found. I know the difference in the species and appearance of crabs. The raw oysters were flavorless, the muscle was not detached from the shell and were room temperature. The chilled shrimp were limp and because I am in the seafood business, I am 98% sure, they were shipped in frozen from Asia already peeled and deveined. They did not taste or have the consistency of a fresh shrimp. The only thing I thought was good on the whole buffet was the jumbo grilled prawns. These were split in half, flavored with butter, garlic and herbs and were almost as large as a small split lobster tail.
   I tried some other seafood dishes on my second trip. Cooked mussels with a coconut curry sauce, steamed clams with a beurre blanc some some sort of small salmon filet. The mussels were cold and over cooked. The small clams had the same temperature and cooking issues, but the butter sauce was tasty. The salmon filet was also room temperature and way over cooked. 
   Next I went up for steamed crab legs. I waited in a 5-minute line and the cook started loading legs on my plate. I was hoping these would be served whole, but they were also split and way over cooked. I asked the attendant where the king crab legs were and he proceeded to pull one out of one of the three pots. My plate only had snow crabs. My guess is they pepper these more expensive crabs few and far between in the mix.
   I was so full of mediocre food, I had little room for dessert. I tried a Bananas Foster crepe. The cook made me a fresh crepe and instructed be to put the cold cooked bananas on top. I asked him to please heat up the bananas, but he insisted this is how it is served. So I had a hot crepe topped with cold fruit- not a good mix.
   My boyfriend and I became friendly with 4 members of our new, extended family and they too were also dissatisfied with the quality of the food. We agreed the buffet should cost $50 a person at tops, not the $85 we just paid. They came to this buffet because of how highly rated it was on Yelp. They said they were going to go back to their rooms and open Yelp accounts just to warn people about the buffet.

This is the best buffet I have been to hands down. I have probably been to buffets that have had a lil bit more of a selection. I can't recall ever being at one that was better quality.

Had the dinner buffet this time. We arrived at about 8 PM and waited about 20 minutes to be seated which was fine. To be honest, I thought the wait would be a lot longer considering how many people were waiting. I guess there were a bunch of larger parties and couples were being seated much quicker. Once inside...There was a pretty large line at the crab leg station, so I'm sure that would be annoying to some people but I don't eat crab so it didn't effect me. There was also a decent line at the meat carving station but it moved quickly and was worth the wait. Pretty much everything else you could walk right up and get. The highlights for me were the: prime rib, lamb shanks, Kung Pao chicken and some really good pasta that had what appeared to be sun dried tomato in it. Oh yeah, I forgot the lil hamburger sliders, those were awesome. I also can't leave out the desserts. The bread pudding was awesome and I had a lil piece of cheesecake with a passion fruit topping that was garnished with a Blackberry, so good.

The service was good, empty plates were always gone by the time I returned from another trip. Our waiter even refilled our soft drinks while we were away at the buffet, never experienced that before. 

I love this buffet and I will continue to visit every time I return to Vegas. Just thinking about it is making me hungry.
Gourmet buffet, amazing! They have Chinese, Italian, Mexican and Sea Food!! Excellent customer service! I highly recommend it, will definitely return!

This is the second time ive been here. 

First time (dec 2016) was worse and i swore id never come back again. It was the holiday menu and my family and i practically made a vegas trip just to try this popular place out. Everything was SO SALTY. Like inedibly salty. The prime rib was oddly tough and flavorless. Crab legs - salty. Even my beloved soups - salty. We got in at 7pm and they ran out of lamb!!! Excuse me! Its not like it was 9pm....7pm PRIME DINNER TIME and they ran out of lamb. Did i forget to mention there was a holiday surge price??? You'd expect they'd stock up their fridge. Desserts were WAY too sweet. It was one of the only meals in my life where as i sat on the table i was regretting coming to this place. 


Everyone kept saying it was THE BEST. And despite swearing i'd never come back, i gave it another chance last week (oct 2017) since one of my good frds has nwver tried it before. Guess what the verdict was - DISAPPOINTING. Even from the other frds who have been trying to get me to change my mind. Granted it wasnt as bad as last year as i could actually ingest the food. Still the food was a tad bit on the salty side. The prime rib was MUCH better but thats bc i scoped out the rarest slab and asked for the most middle cut. My frds had no such luck and got some tough/tasteless meat. Dessert was STILL too sweet. Who hates ice cream??? I dont except ice cream from Bacchanal apparently. Dont be too excited about the freshmade crepes..the bitter looking man making them rushes out the crepes and gives them to us undercooked. AGAIN! How can there be so many plates of leftover crepe and nutella....only this place!

Tldr; NEVER. AGAIN.

Price is too expensive for food that is inconsistent.  Most of the food we had tonight were so disappointing, They've been sitting there for some time.  Bellagio's food is consistently good and we were there last night, thinking to save Bacchanal for last, since it was supposed to be the best.  Only to be disappointed for the quality of food we had for the price we paid.  more than $500.00 for 10 people.  Won't return for sure.

The amount of food I get for 50 dollars is well worth the price. Excuse the sob story, but when you grow up in poverty and have had dreams of all different kinds of food all racked up and displayed for your pleasure. It's kind of a big deal and not to mention they taste amazing. I love love love the honey glazed sweet potato tots and fries. The brisket was tender, a bit salty on the edges but that's what mash potato is for. I took one of everything in the desert station. Food coma, HELLO !
Very nice decor. Friday night, we got there at 6:40 the wait was around 10 minutes and even got a casino comp of 10 dollars and 10% off our meal from one of the staff while waiting. I'm so glad we got there at that time because come 7 o' clock the line went from around the corner. Crazy. Overall it was one of the best buffets I've ever had.

I haven't been to this buffet since it opened but it was the best I ever tasted.  It was better than Bellagio and I've been there several times.  As a person that use to live in Vegas, I know my buffets and this one is the best.  I hope to go to this one on our next trip!

Multiple waiting and very very expensive! Brought my boyfriend here for his birthday and our total came out to $150. Pretty much paid $75 per person because it was the "holiday price". Felt sort of disappointed for my expectations were so high for it because of all the review I heard about it. And from friends and families experience. The only thing that was really good was the meat and steaks. M resort would have been better

Best buffet in Las Vegas! My wife and I come here every time we visit ! 
It's a little pricey though!

Yummy buffet. Lots of great options but the line is a mess - we waited an hour to return to the line and from there another 40 minutes to get seated.
Def. a buzzkill when you're starving.


Crab legs, paella, prime rib and the desserts are forsure the best choice. Staff is friendly and helpful.

This does not need any more reviews...but, just in case someone doesn't know about this and it shows up on their feed - you need to go to this buffet. 

I came here 4 years ago, before they renovated it. It was probably as bad as going to Golden Coral or Ruby's. It just wasn't good, very poor quality and very overpriced. 
I decided I would never go again.

One thing I will tell you - I am not big on buffets. I don't like that people can touch the same things you're touching and you don't know where people have placed their hands. I eat out a lot and I can handle it with the restaurant employees because I don't see them making my food. At buffets, I see everyone touching everything or even putting their hands in something. I can't handle it. 

The #1 thing about this buffet is, almost everything is separated or served to you. High. Five.
#2 - the food is VERY good. I would say that this is the best buffet on the strip. I've been to most of them on the strip because when families come to town, they love buffets. This one trumps all. 
The food is very well cooked, not over cooked and served very fresh. I love how they serve hot crab legs to you so they're not dried out or too cold. 
I had the pizza, lamb, blue cheese wedge salad, Asian BBQ Ribs, Prime Rib, mac & cheese, green beans, chicken florentine, crab legs, crab wontons, I ate a lot. 
But, my favorite was the crepes. I'm not big on sweets, but I looooooooove crepes. 
I had her drizzle nutela on it and topped it with whipped cream, strawberries and caramel bananas...god, it was delicious.

The buffet is pricey, but if you're going to indulge, it's worth it. It's very clean and the service is very good.
Such a great buffet.  They have many options and great prices.  Its located in the Ceasars Palace casino and very nice.
Simply wonderful. Excellent and friendly servers. Incredible crab legs. Get you some prime rib and save room for dessert.

We had a great time here! The meal was $64, but there was a great combination of everything from a variety of food, quality of food, and quality of service. There was so much food that we tried here that it's even too much to remember what we are. Desserts were great, my sweet tooth was very satisfied with the variety and taste. The mango soup was amazing, with tapioca and dragonfruit. I was sipping it like there was tomorrow. That was definitely the dessert of the morning. And the bottomless mimosas! The service was beyond amazing. Jules was our server and she made sure the glasses were always full and checked on us regularly enough to keep us content. The meal items were sometimes a hit and miss. I like my bacon on the crunchy side and I wished they had some well done ones. Lol. I was wondering what the tiny, blue slipper looking things and then found out its so you don't burn your fingers picking up the plates. Nice little touch. Flapjacks were ok, they also had a red velvet flavor one. I did my best to sample as much as possible. I don't think it's worth the $64, more like no more than $50. It was still a good experience though.

I don't get the hype. Horrible. And coming here tonight reminded us that we came here a few yesterday ago and said we'd never come back. Service was dismal at best. Only real good things were the Chinese red BBQ pork, mini tacos and dessert. EVERYTHING else was not good. Shrimp cocktail looked disgusting, the crab legs looked and tasted old. Ugh why didn't I remember it sucked. Oh and never add gratuity when you pay in advance. Had to start ordering to drinks at a time to keep from running out.

Pricey but well worth it! The wait to eat wasn't too long on a Wednesday night in July. The prime rib was good. The dessert was excellent. The staff was awesome! Very attentive. I would definitely recommend coming here!
Don't believe the hype! Good variety, but expensive and the food is average. Can get better food in Vegas eating somewhere else for $60+.

my favorite buffet in vegas!!  i didn't eat at all of them :( but of all the ones i did eat at this is the only one we ate at twice!  It's quite busy on the weekends but the weekdays there is no wait.  

The eating area is enormous and the buffet is long.  You walk and walk and think your are at the end only to see more food around the corner.  there is a large assortment of food, mexican, asian, indian, middle eastern, etc. so it will please all palates.

the street taco station is great and the noodle bar makes AWESOME pho and tonkatsu ramen!  i was quite impressed with the flavor of both broths as some who just serve noodles can't get it right.  

truffled scalloped potatoes were memorable so if you like truffles do try these out.  

also the servers and chefs are so friendly and make you feel so welcomed!

Pricey at $45 each (plus tip for someone bringing drinks)and alcohol costs extra, for dinner.  But that's average compared to every other place around. Excellent food & selection. Prime rib, crab legs & dry rub ribeye were worth the price alone. The desserts are wonderful - we tried 10 or more &they were all yummy!  Mac & cheese & truffle scalloped potatoes were amazing too.

I got the Buffet of Buffets ($50 per person, if you are a Total Reward Program member, $55 if not. Total Reward is free to sign up) and came to Bacchanal. Here is a brief of how it works. When you buy the Buffet of Buffets, you have 24 hours to use it. You have unlimited visits to all the buffets in the program, except the Rio Seafood Buffet and Bacchanal. For Bacchanal, you have to pay an extra $15 for breakfast, $20 for lunch, and $25 for dinner. They serve pretty much the same items for lunch and dinner. I haven't been to it for breakfast. Since the weekend (Bacchanal stand alone) rate is higher than the weekday's. Monetarily, it is worth a lot more doing it in the weekend. Because you still pay the same for the Buffet of Buffets and the extra for Bacchanal.

They have different sections: seafood, American, Mexican, Italian, salad, Asian, and dessert. My favorites are the lobster corn chowder at the seafood section. The corn chowder is bursting with flavor. Whenever I go there, I would have at least 4 or 5 of this. I tend to stay away from the American section because they serve very fatty and greasy food. Most of them are fried. For the Mexican, I like the horchata. They also have taco to order which they cook in front of you. In the Italian section, they have pizza, pasta, and a variety of cheese and salami (that's what I am guessing they are). In the Asian section, they have sushi, dim sum, fresh spring roll, and some Chinese food. I am a bit disappointed from the Chinese roasted duck because it tasted a bit bland. It is missing the taste of the traditional spices. However, the congee is quite good. You can taste that it is well prepared and executed.

Rate the Management of the Caesar's Palace Hotel and Casino, in particular, the Bacchanal Buffet a ZERO, if I could.  During my family's visit to the Bacchanal Buffet this past Labor Day weekend, we received poor customer service from the management of the Bacchanal Buffet.  They were misleading, dishonest, condescending, unsympathetic, and unapologetic for a situation which they initially caused.  I spoke to at least 2 buffet line phone operators, 2 General Managers (GMs) and 1 Assistant GM and basically got the run around and brush off.  The buffet line phone operators initially caused the situation, the working GM was dishonest and appeared to trick us, the Assistant GM could not help.  The second GM (Dirk Siem) that I spoke to was the worst.  He was briefed with the working GM and Assistant GM's side of the situation and did not want to find out the cause of the situation and already decided that my family was wrong and at fault, and did not want to hear my family's perspective of the situation.  I am writing this review and spreading the word to my family and friends.  I am boycotting the Bacchanal Buffet!

I was unimpressed for the hefty price. Standouts: deliciously-seasoned fried chicken, smoky BBQ ribs, cheese and charcuterie, mini salads. Things that were really so-so: fishy raw oysters, bland and tough prime rib, weirdly sweet lamb chops, dry sashimi.
If you want to experience the LV ultimate buffet- this is it. Pricey, but you get what you paid for!

This is the only buffet on the strip to challenge the Wicked Spoon. The food here is tasteful, however they are beyond stingy with their mimosas (and when you're paying for unlimited, they better taste up to my standards). The overall experience at the buffet was good, however there were a few issues. The host at the cashier stand was not very friendly and the server was asked by the hostess to take two groups to two different tables, he mixed up the tickets numbers and gave the party of 2 that was before us the table we were supposed to have. When he realized his mistake, we had to go back to the front of the wait line and wait another 10min for a table.

Place was awesome, prob best selection of seafood, they got oysters, clams, king crab, crawfish, but they don't have lobster. I must say their BBQ selection was one of the best, beef brisket particularly stood out, so was their lamb chops, rib eye was just ok, not the best or the greatest as I thought the meet was a bit dry! If you like cheese, they have a pretty dam good selection of the finest cheeses. I was realLu contemplating wicked spoon of this , if you like seafood and a ton of selections, this place hits the spot. Their desert selection isn't as great or extravagant as wicked spoon, but all in all soo glad we came here.
Paid a little more because it was Mother's Day weekend but great selection! Would definitely go back. Favorites were hot crab legs, homemade meatballs and barbecue chicken.

So I have been anticipating this visit.. my family is big on buffets and I decided to take my dad and son for breakfast. Let me start with they have a early bird special before 10 am it is $29.99. I got there at 9:45am, my dad was meeting me there. No one in line and they did not let me pay or get sat until everyone was present. I am aware of policy's and have been a hostess. Usually when it is a large party this policy makes sense to me. I was waiting on one other person to arrive... So this did not make sense. We wouldn't have been taking up anymore space since my son is a toddler. So right off the bat I was already not having the "best" experience. Then my dad gets lost because he is not familiar with the parking structure so by the time he got to me it was 10:02am. The tab went from $65 to $85 quickly. Good for them for getting another $20 out of me in a short amount of time. Very unappreciative that this happened but again "policy." We get sat, the decor is modern and beautiful. Surprised the chairs were very comfortable. They have an impressive selection of food and a lot to choose from. A lot of it is already plated. I tried the frittata, chicken and waffles, sausage, clams, mussels, parfaits, and pancakes. A few more items. I pretty much did a sample of everything. To be quite honest I was fairly disappointed... In my personal opinion this is not worth $85. It also is a buffet. When anything sits out for too long it gets dried out and as we say in the restaurant business "dies in the window." I have gone to the Bellagio buffet for brunch and that was well worth the money. I do not think I will be returning.. Maybe dinner is better? I definitely did not eat $40 worth of food but I am thankful my dad did!! He had 5 plates and wasn't crazy about the buffet but that man is an eater so game on.

I have a stomach that's the size of a gall bladder so I'm not fit to go to any buffet. The word "Buffet" calls out the good old college days. Came here with BF and a group of 10+ friends to bid farewell to a couple who is moving to Asia for work. 

I only wrote this review not for the service nor the great selections of what this buffet has to offer but for the "Chinese Roasted Duck." 

Ambiance: not much to speak of. 

Food: Great variety of food for all types of palette. I have to rave about the Chinese roasted duck and for me it's all about the duck. It's so juicy when you bite into the crunchy duck skin. All the roasted duck dishes served at Sam Woo or authentic Chinese places are very boney or too much fat. So make sure you try the duck. Honestly, that's all I ate during this meal and some desserts.
It's hard to impress me and I am impressed. Very good selection and good service! Fresh food!
Awesome buffet!!!! Caesar's buffet is by far the best in Vegas. Come early if you don't want to stand in line forever. A little on the pricier side but well worth the money.

for sunday brunch this is one of the better spots. big selection of eats and very good quality but being so pricey knocks it down a peg for me. It's hard to eat $40+ worth of food in 1 sitting, y'know?

From the friendly staff to the melt in your mouth prime rib, this lovely buffet offered both excellent food quality and a multitude of food options.  The lobster bisque was among the best I've ever had.  Their house-made gelato was wonderful.  Yes, this buffet is pricier.  But the old adage "you get what you pay for" certainly applies here.  Everything I tried (and I mean everything) was outstanding.  I consider myself to be somewhat picky, but I could find no fault with any aspect of this buffet.  If quality is important to you, this is the buffet to try.

The desserts were amazing. I loved the thai tea float, japanese pudding, chocolate covered strawberries, mochi, and macarons. They also had pandan ice cream and pandan cake. 

I was not impressed by the prime rib, bbq ribs, chinese crab- too salty for me. I didnt like the bbq sauces offered. 

Hubs thought sushi was good quality, oysters were okay

My 4 year old liked the mac n cheese and fried rice.

Clean, delicious, expensive. Great customer service. 
Come hungry. 
Crab legs and oysters are amazing. Not sure I'll eat them till my next visit.

Buffet of buffets - for a C note and some change you can enjoy it as well. Overall a good buffet, we would go again but not sure if it would be every time we go to Vegas. We tried a lot of the offerings. Some of the offerings were: fresh shrimp, crab legs (hot and cold), sea bass, oysters, craw fish and much more. Meat dishes were: prime rib, chicken, brisket, lamb chops, bone-in rib-eye, sausage and much more. The brisket and prime rib were dry ;-(.  this was a disappointment as I am more of a meat eater than other things. 

The Asian food had lots of options: noodle soup (but nobody was there to make any when I wanted some), broccoli and beef (this was cold) and lots of other items. 

Tons of vegetables: carrots, potatoes, corn, green beans and much more. 

Desserts: so many, many, many what did I not try not many but had to save some for next time. This time I tried: flan, pane cotta, ice cream, chocolate covered strawberries, cremebrule and much more. There were so many desserts could not try them all as I was stuff to the max like a turkey ready for thanksgiving baking.

The con would be for the wait time in the line that's why only four stars and cost.

We would go back.
食物真的很差。要排隊三個小時。以他的聲譽來說每位500元的價錢不算貴。不過進到去真是大吃一驚。食物真的很差。沒一款是合理。基本上連街邊小吃都及不上。高檔次的食物如凍海鮮之類。跟其他在vegas半他一半又不用等的buffet一樣。排隊的95%都是華人。懷著滿心歡喜終於等到入場然後迫著要拿白飯面包等令自己飽肚。

Our last buffet of the trip. It was great and not much wait when we went past noon time.

They have a lot of foods to try here. It was all actually quite good. But when it is nearing the end of your Vegas trip and your last buffet - I don't know about you, but I just was feeling so sick. I was barely even hungry.

I wished that I came here as my first buffet, but I ate everything anyway because I had to.

The asian food section is quite good. No tempura the day I went, if you are looking for it. But their dim sum tasted better than the Aria Buffet. AND they had a steam pork bun, which I was craving.

Their little burger and fries were so good. Carving station excellent. Gotta get some Waygu beef in there.

There was of course a lot of seafood - shells and crab legs - but I don't like that stuff so didn't eat any.

The dessert section is great too. Their Tiramisu was actually really really good. Not like a fake cake-tiramisu like in the grocery store, but somewhat legit with traces of coffee, rich cream, delicious flavor. The black forest mousse thing was also really really good, as was the cheesecake dome. The gelato and sorbet is good too. I couldn't fit room in my tummy for a crepe, but heard they were mediocre and not that thin-crispy type, but if you want a crepe, they'll make you a fresh one and you can heap a pile of yummy toppings on it. They brought out cake pops just as I was about to vomit from being full, so I just couldn't try it. My friend did and said it was good.

They had jars of lollipops, gummy bears and salt water taffy. I saw a kid stuffing dozens and dozens of lollipops into his pockets and heaping his plate with hundreds of gummy bears. When there is so much other stuff, I didn't gravitate toward those pre-packaged items, but I see how it is a draw for the younger crowd.

This buffet was my last stop in Vegas on my journey toward obesity. I would go again.
A wide variety of food. The dim sum is ehhh.. I'm a big fan of the desserts and crab legs though. I prefer Wicked spoon, but the desserts are better over here.
Not the best. Crab is FLAVORLESS. The price was too much for the quality of the food. The mortadella looked awful. The paella was too spicy. The caviar bar was cool though.

Certainly one of the better buffets in Vegas but the BEST buffet is still eluding me and yet to be found.  Like a well thought out strategic Disneyland park plan, I think the trick is to have a early, hearty breakfast, skip lunch and have your linner here to reap the best price and both worlds of lunch and dinner options! I think the dinner prices start at 3pm from what I recall so be sure you line up between 2:15-2:30pm to time this right!  You'll be so stuffed you wont eat for 24 hours after that anyways!  :)
Short story short...just go!  Trust me.  If you are here searching for the best buffet in Vegas right now, stop searching and hit the cab line and head to Caesars Palace.    Best buffet in town.

I'm a native to Las Vegas having lived here my entire life, over 40 years. I grew up in the hotel and gaming community and if there is a buffet in Vegas, I'm sure I've eaten at it. So when I heard all the hype about the Bacchanal Buffet (named after the old Bacchanal restaurant of Caesars Palace ages ago) I was dying to try it.
