I've already experienced several of the other major buffets in Las Vegas such as the one at the Bellagio and my personal favorite, Wicked Spoon over at Cosmo, so my hopes were high for this place. I must say, my high hopes were let down.

My first experience with the Bacchanal Buffet was about a month after it opened. My wife and I decided to go down and check it out. It was mid-week, about 7 PM when we arrived. Much to my amazement, the line to get in looked like the line for the Matterhorn at Disneyland on Labor Day weekend. My jaw hit the ground when I found out it would be a THREE HOUR WAIT to get in. That's right, a THREE HOUR WAIT! I'm sorry, there is no buffet in the history of the world worth that. Anyone willing to stand in such a line needs to get their head examined. Oh, but wait, for an extra few bucks you can pay to get into a shorter line...what an insult! We left, but not before I asked to speak to a restaurant manager about this insanity. 

A young woman, still in her 20's introduced herself as the head assistant manager. I questioned why they had a line this long and didn't use a pager system or numbers or something like that. Hello?! They came up with these ideas 30 years ago! This girl looked at me like I was speaking Martian. The mere concept of this went so far over her head she looked like a deer in headlights. Evidently, this is the new system that Caesars Palace has implemented...get rid of anyone with experience or knowledge of the industry because they cost too much and, instead, hire kids right out of college with a Hospitality degree to run a multi-million dollar restaurant as a General Manager for $50,000/year. This is what happens when your flag-ship property is run by amateurs after a buy out. It's like McDonalds trying to run a Ruth's Chris Steakhouse like a McDonalds. Insane. After this brief conversation that went nowhere, we left.

Fast forward a few months, it was my birthday. My wife knew I wanted to go to the Bacchanal so she took me there as we decided to give it a second try. We went on a Wednesday at 8PM. The hotel was empty but there was still an atrocious 45 minute wait. INSANE. Once inside, our first impression was that it was very nice inside but nothing special. We actually were shocked at how small the seating area was, which would probably explain why the turnover of tables was so slow.

the food was wonderful but in many cases it suffered the same problems that many buffets suffer from and that's batches of food left under heat lamps. Much of the food was hot but much of it was barely warm. The crab legs were a nice touch but by far nothing special. I've had better at Red Lobster or Joes Crab Shack. Seriously, no joke.  The desserts were certainly the high point of the buffet and we enjoyed several of the different offerings.

My overall experience of the Bacchanal Buffet was that it was a fair value for the price but the insanely long wait to get in dropped what would be a 4 star review down to a 2 star. It is not worth the wait...not even close. What baffles the mind though is how not one executive at Caesars Palace has not screamed at them over this process. You have people waiting in line for HOURS when they could be putting money in slot machines or playing the tables. Stupid! Stupid! Stupid! I'm amazed that people haven't been fired over this and I'm even more amazed that the wait process still exists. It's run by idiots with no common sense.

Sarah Jane, one of the top reviewers of this restaurant is even a good friend of mine and because of her relationship with Yelp, she got right in and never had to wait for the gruelingly long line to eat here. She has even told me that if she had to wait an hour or more to eat here she would have dropped her review down a lot too. 

My wife and I eat at nice restaurants all the time and the price tag to eat at the Bacchanal seems fair minus the long line. Until they expand with more tables to accommodate more people and change the line system we will not return. We much prefer Wicked Spoon.

No other words to describe this then best buffet ever. Everything is fresh and clearly made in house or baked in house, selection is amazing and service is Amazing. It's almost over whelming being there because you want to eat everything

Food and value for me is 1-2 stars. Not a huge fan of buffet anyway, used to nicely prepared food from restaurant.  Recently fell in love with boiling crab in Vegas. Its expensive plus taxi round and the effort to get the food.  So I thought try the buffet since its so close by ( I stay in flamingo for business ). If its good could save me taxi trips to pickup food from boiling crab off strip. $58 arrive 4:35pm with no line at all.  Service is nice and efficient. The food is very disappointing for what they charge. And I am not cheap. food is very cold. Seafood very old sitting there for a while start to dry up. Crab is very very very very VERY salty. I try to finish what I have no my plate so I don't look like a big waste eater but it was really gross. Maybe I am just not a big fan of raw seafood but just loving the sauce from the last restaurant. All others are very mediocre nothing special. There is not one dish left impression. So I won't be back, for me.  Will still recommend people who likes Buffet cause the selection. People sitting around me seem enjoy it. So we have to be fair.

The stars are mostly for the $7 bottomless champagne and our server. 

The buffet was only okay, especially for $100 for two. If you really want to eat a ton of food but don't care about the quality this is probably a good place. Wicked Spoon is a much better buffet, but I went against my better judgement and decided to try something different.

I had a few different benedicts and the egg was way overcooked and the hollandaise cold on each, the meatball dish was lukewarm, the egg frittata lukewarm, and you could tell the crab claws were previously frozen because they had no taste and a weird texture. 

I'm sure the standard breakfast staples were good, but I don't need to pay $50 per person for eggs and bacon.

I mainly ate king crab legs, shrimp, champagne, and 20 different desserts.

Gosh, it's places like this that make me wish I had more than one stomach....

Bacchanal Buffet, hands down is my absolute FAVORITE buffet in Vegas. At some point in my food trance, I crazily admitted that I wished I could live here! It's that fabulous, and everything comes together---great food, beautifully designed restaurant, and attentive and friendly service.

Notables:
+ Okay, I know that this is a buffet, but there is literally SO MUCH FOOD. I liked that you don't really just get the traditional american buffet food, but they also serve up different types of cuisine as well. Like helllooo, congee station fully equipped with thousand year old egg and chinese donut? Yah, I could probably get a heaping pot of this in Chinatown for $5 but just the presence of this was surprising and pretty well executed. They also have thai food, and even a taco station added to the mix! 
+ Omfg, crab legs! I hear the complaints that these aren't king crab legs, and yes... while I personally favor king crab over snow crab most days, did anyone mention that these are pretty much pre-shelled for you? Gosh, I guess I've never experienced this before so call me misinformed, but having the half the shell removed so that I could just dig in and eat up made the dining experience that much more pleasant. I'd hate to have the job of the crab de-sheller though.
+ Lunch vs. Dinner? I'd do lunch a million times over. No one wants to have a night out with a food baby! Lunch is much cheaper than dinner in all cases, and if you're skeptical about less offerings being available, do the weekend brunch! Bottomless mimosas/champagne/bloody marys make the experience more than worthwhile. 
+ Again, bottomless mimosas/champagne/bloody marys. YES!
+ Dessert is a MUST DO here. I'm not all very fond of sweets, but the desserts they have here are just too good to pass up. Cookies, gelato, all sorts of different sweets to tickle your fancy. I've heard that they do macarons too, but they weren't available the day we were there. I loved all the flavors of gelato though, both the tried and true along with the uniquely uncommon. I sampled and loved both the sour cherry and the mango lime chile. 
+ There's just something about how the restaurant was so thoughtfully laid out that really wowed me. I dunno about other people, but most times that I eat at buffets, I feel like I'm back in high school or college, herded into a cafeteria for lunch with a hundred other bodies. Overall, I liked how they weren't stingy when it came to space--the buffet was sprawling, and spaced out in such a way that it wasn't so much of a sensory overload going from different station to station. Moreover, the tables were spaced out in a way that I could really enjoy my time dining with great company, rather than overhearing the next table over. It's just the little things, but for me, these small details speak volumes to the experience.
+ Props to the man at the carving station who theatrically exclaimed "welcome to Bacchanal buffet!", as I gazed in awe at the sheer selection of meats to choose from. Details. Service here is friendly and pleasant, though it got a little spotty towards the end when the restaurant started getting busier. 

My best advice is to come early if you can. What's so bad about pulling an early bird special vs. waiting an hour plus in line? I anticipated a crazy wait, especially on a holiday weekend (Easter), but when we showed up at 11am for lunch, the time from the moment we arrived to the moment that we were seated was less than ten minutes! Not too shabby. As we left a few hours later though, the lines were excruciating. Positively excruciating. Prices were escalated due to the holiday. Around $60 pp and for only lunch nonetheless, which is a little crazy, but considering what you get it's not too bad. 

When in Vegas, few bills is a small price to go to buffet heaven. Trust me, this is the stuff that dreams are made of!

to be honest, im not a big buffet person. it just calls for gluttony and feeling like crap afterwards. (sorry but you know its true!) 

BUTTTT this buffet was pretty darn good. i love the spacious, airy open vibe of the place. the display of food was gorgeous. they have a variety of options, all the way from Asian food, Mexican, American brunch, and seafood (which was cold shrimp, mussels, and crab legs). And unlimited mimosas for brunch? um..yes. they also have a great variety of different cakes, ice cream (thai tea!!!!) and crepes! 

ok so did i eat enough to make it worth $50? probably not. and honestly, i havent really experienced the other vegas buffets and have had not that good of an experience with vegas meals, so to be in a comfortable, wide, spacious, relaxing environment with plenty of natural sunlight, unlimited mimosa, coffee, and crab legs was a pretty darn good meal to me!

Damn Gina!!!!  I don't do buffets that much, nor do I do Vegas that much, but I will do BOTH again, if just for this place.

Our early-ass flight landed at 7:30am, so we headed straight for Ceasar's to be there when this place opened at 8am.  There was already a line (at 7:45 in the morning on a saturday in vegas! and people didn't look as if they had just stumbled in from the club) so you know it's good.

We slow-walked in to get a good look at all the offerings and my mouth is watering now just thinking of them.... We finally got our larger group to sit all together (18% automatic gratuity for parties over 8) and proceeded to HOG OUT. 

Some highlights: mini stacks of red-velvet pancakes, soup dumplings and shiu mai, fresh squeezed juices (we were partial to watermelon which we added to our bottomless - and included!!! - mimosas. melo-mosas, if you will), tiny fryer baskets of sweet potato tots, mini fried chicken and waffles, lots of interesting sausage and bacon, individual cuts of croque madame and monsieur, corned beef hash with quail egg!!!, and unbelievable eggs benedict served like 80 ways - one on top of a crab cake!  Also they had your standard seafood, pizza, omelette station, lots of bread and pastries (waste of valuable stomach space), and unlimited drinks.

But then, oh, but then.... The dessert bar. So much scrumptiousness.  At least 15 kinds of gelato, cakes, pies, cupcakes, even sugar free cheesecake!  And barrels of jelly bellys!

We stayed for three glorious hours.
WORTH IT.

We travel to Vegas a few times a year and are frequent visitors to the buffets at various hotels. We were recommended Bachannal by a friend and had a chance to stop by last time we were in Vegas. 

A bit on the pricey side and the wait can be 2+ hours sometimes, but HANDS DOWN BEST BUFFET I've been to in Vegas. Great selection, quality foods and very clean/well put together inside. We can't wait to go back!
If you can get there early and avoid the lines - this place is AMAZING. Great selection, delicious food and good service.
Treat yoself. Should always end Vegas with a meal here. Carving station, dim sum, desserts, everything is good here. That's why there's always a long line here.

This buffet is OK but not great. Service leaves a lot to desire and the layout of seating and navigating the counters are poorly designed. The food is pretty good and definitely a unique selection for multiple ethnic foods. Also condiments and sauces should be more available or have some kind of delivery system so that you don't have to carry a liquid on a flat plate making a mess. Overall this buffet is average with a high price tag.

No thank you. Don't get me wrong some of the offerings on the buffet were great.  Especially the fresh squeezed juices. The lobster Benedict was excellent too. The problem with this place is the cost. Over priced and over rated. There are comparable buffets at less cost.

Give the buffet at the M Resort a try. Not fancy but good home style cooking. Wine and champagne and I believe the beer is included.

The best buffet in Las Vegas! It is $52.99 per person for the dinner buffet, which starts at 3 PM. 

I've searched around Las Vegas strip for the best rated buffet and this one had the highest and most reviews with at least 4 stars. The lamb chops, king crab legs and lobster claws are amazing. 

The desserts were wonderful too. If you're in Vegas, this buffet is a must. 

Everything is just chef-prepped quality.

See pics!

I felt robbed after dinner at this place. I don't understand what the raves are all about so I tried this place. I had a lousy seafood paella, the salad was ordinary and yes there is seafood but I still prefer the seafood from Rio and the buffet from Cosmo or Wynn. Now the dessert part is good because of the crepe station but I'm disappointed they do not have cotton candy,

I came here for the Christmas holiday dinner buffet with my husband and found it way too overpriced. The price for the holiday dinner buffet was much higher than the standard $50/person. 
First there was a 2-hour wait time for the dinner buffet, and because we didn't want to wait that long we paid an extra surcharge for the separate VIP-ish line that was much shorter. Our total came to about $200 with tax and tip. 
When we got into the buffet, we were overwhelmed with all the food, but to be honest much of the food tasted only average or mediocre. Maybe this was because the buffet was packed with so many people during the holiday season, but everything was just a waste of my money. Nothing really stood out, many of the dishes could be found elsewhere, the food stations were relatively dirty with scrap food lying around, and overall, it was too hectic in there. 
The fresh seafood station was always empty because people took way too many at one time and the chicken and waffles...everyone took the chicken but not the waffles so there were lonely waffles laying around with no chicken.
I'm not going back and I prefer Wicked Spoon!

Been here about 3 times and I loved it! The food is good, it definitely hits the spot. They even have horchata and I've seen mochi ice cream as well! The only downside is the price, which isn't really worth it because NO buffet is worth 40-50 bucks per person, sorry. Only go here if you're trying to splurge on a date and wanna feel like you're ballin lol.

Another downside used to be the long line which you could have been standing in for an hour or more but last time I was there the line wasn't long at all and they had these machines that let you put your info in to come back when its your turn instead of waiting in line doing nothing..I guess it really depends on the timing!

BEST VEGAS BUFFET!!

Loved it more than Wicked Spoon! Be warned that the line gets long, though. We came at 1PM and ended up paying more to just skip the line and cut to the front.

All the food was delicious......... there was too many things that I loved at the buffet for me to list. ** EVERYTHING ** was good!! Our waitress was SUPER funny and great to us. We refilled our mimosas countless times but she was always really nice and really friendly! (Free bottomless mimosas on Saturdays!)

They have a huugee selection of food. I wasn't able to try all of it because I got too full, but all my friends had raving reviews about the place.

Bacchanal is a CANNOT miss when you go to Las Vegas!

Nothing special...way too expensive for the price. Don't expect any good quality sushi - no sashimi or good rolls. Besides the great selection of deserts everything else was disappointed. Wynn, Rio and Planet Hollywood's buffet was so much better.

Was great the first time I had it.  It seems as if they raised prices and dropped quality.  They charged 18% for large party and then didn't really serve us.  I had to go find a server for more beverages.  Then they tried to convince me that rice balls are supposed to have raw dough in it like it's the style.  Fail.

I cannot write a fair review for the food because we did not try it but I can say that they need to reconsider their price structure.

When we arrived to the cashier she informed be that the bill for, 3 kids and 2 adults, was $298.00 including tip.

Now, considering that the kids were 9, 11, 13, I will consider the price outrageous even for Las Vegas standard.

For this price, nobody will ever be able to convince me about anything positive for this place.

ermahgerd. sooo gerd.  read about the $17mil rennovations to Bacchanal and i was very excited to try it out a month after it opened!

our wait on a saturday morning at 11:30 was literally 20 minutes, could not have been any happier.  our party of 7 was seated in a secluded private room that had a nice view of the pools.. which was fun for the guys, but hello? for us girls, we don't need to see skinny girls walking around in bikinis while we're on a feeding frenzy.

there was an abundance of food, the layout is interesting.  unlike Studio B at the M Resort, where it's a big open space, and you just walk along the snaking path, it seems at Bacchanal, there are pockets of rooms with food, and you may miss it if you don't walk down a certain path.

i definitely love the creativity in each dish (mmm, hello flatbread pizza with a quail egg on top!)  it's nice that they're served to you in smaller portions so you're still hungry enough to try different things after your first round.

the service was great.  we got our free-flowing mimosas on, and it was dee-lish!  didn't do it this time around, but definitely a bargain if you do the buffet-of-buffets!

Uh only the best buffet on the strip? Tons of fresh seafood including raw oysters and lots of things made to order, like streetside tacos and crepes. Hot crab legs, excellent roasts, and just so much selection, all excellent. But pricey, but this place is really the most bang for the buck buffet you can get.

It's actually painful to eat here. I think I'm still recovering. With options spanning Chinese, Japanese, Salad & oyster bar, Mexican (with made to order tacos), Italian, American comfort foods, a cutting station, fresh seafood and last but not least the grand dessert station, there's no other way to conquer Bacchanal other to stuff yourself past the point of comfort or even movement. 

You put your name in the computer and they text you to when it's time for you to get in line. We shopped for an hour in Caesar's attraction of a mall while we waited and went back and stood in line for about an hour.

Once I had entered the labyrinth of majestic foods called Bacchanal Buffet I knew what all the hype was about. Although individually most of the dishes are just subpar, the huge unlimited variety was astounding. My favorite was their assortment of seafood and the king crab legs which they already cut in half for easy demolition. They also had some really well prepared seabass. Also the carving station is good with plenty of options. I found the prime rib a little dry, but the lamb chops very tender and juicy. 

And the dessert table. Don't even get me started on the dessert table. Just go see it for yourself. I strongly advise not wearing a crop top or any sort of tight fitting dress when eating here. 

It was really busy so understandably you won't see your server often, but everyone's always really quick in collecting your plates.
Still the best buffet in Vegas. The place looks modern and the food is consistently good.

this buffet was pretty good. it cost my husband and i about 150$ for dinner here and with that price tag and the huge wait i had extremely high expectations. (plus everyone raves about it) they do fresh piping hot plates of crab legs! amazeballz! their mushroom pallenta is to die for. alot of the food was pretty good. it was a decent buffet but i dont think it shouldve costed that much. i can see maybe 100$ for two ppl but damn 150$...honestly the wicked spoon's brunch/ lunch buffet at 27.99 a person was waaaaaaay more impressive than dinner here.

When you're in Vegas, what tops the list is definitely the variety of buffets to choose from and this one is the best for a reason. Be warned that this place usually is pack and you would have to wait in line. But rightfully so since after you are seated, you will not want to try the other places. There are many stations to choose from and presentation is very good. All sorts of seafood like crab and raw oysters, cuts of meats like a Brazilian steakhouse, Italian, American, Sushi, a neat Asian noodle station in the corner where you can request for Ramen, pho, and Dim Sum! and of course their huge selection of desserts! Definitely have to try the crepes and ice cream with warm brownie. At first $55/person seems a bit too much but you can see why after you are done. You can also request to ask for any kinds of beverage even coffee! Service was outstanding and we definitely will be coming back! 

Tip: try to come in on weekday or weeknight if you could in a small group to avoid having to deal with the weekend rush.

Suite à sa rénovation, le buffet du Caesar Palace est devenu le meilleur buffet de la ville. La deco est tres class et design. Le choix est varié et la qualité au top. 
Prix en conséquence. 
En revanche la musique d'ambiance est un peu trop forte.

$55 on a buffet, can seem pricey, but the variety and quality of food is worth it. My date and I had great comfortable seats so that helped with the experience as well. My advice, get a booth or at least a table for two on the right side were there isn't much walking traffic. Definitely worth a visit.

Great buffet! I felt like I was a judge on chopped and cupcake wars! There was a wide variety of food to choose from and I criticized each piece! I had some miso sea bass and I did not like that there were rice crispies on them. Carrot cupcake was too tart, juice bar is pretty cool. There's way too much to review on here. I felt like there could have been more food in the buffet for the price and the rant on how this is such a big buffet.

Best buffet in Vegas. Better than the Bellagio. Everything is quality, great service and very friendly staff. For lunch They have the good crab legs here (not the skinny crab legs), good shrimp, prime rib, asian, Italian, great Mexican posole, yummy desserts. Be ready to wait in line at least 20 minutes. My only regret is not being able to eat enough. I felt sick I ate so much, literally made myself sick. But it was worth it. Pricey so you gotta get your money's worth. Oh yeah almost forgot, great fried chicken!

Amazing buffet in Vegas!

Visited in mid-July and they sadly do not include unlimited mimosas with the price. Instead, you can opt to have unlimited mimosas for $7 more. The price was $49.99 per person. 

The horchata juice is my favorite and always end up getting two bottles. 

The meat counter is by far the best items in the whole buffet. Don't waste room eating dim sum or soups. You must stop by the meat counter. I had the sausage, prime rib, and brisket. 

Save room for dessert! Bacchanal has one of the best dessert bars I've ever been to. They have made to order crepes, gelato, creme brulee, assorted cakes, and even a jar of dum dums. The best gelato they had was the mango habanero. It had a kick of spiciness a few seconds after you have the first bite. 

Tip: If you have a party of 6 or more, there's a line towards the front of the entrance on the right hand side that expedites these larger groups.

I just love this buffet! Delicious, clean, and great customer service. The price is high but it's worth it. Suggestion-it would be nice if the kids price was lower considering they don't eat 65 dollars worth of food/drinks. 
Other than that- delicious!

In general I'm not a fan of buffets because quantity is favored over quality, but this place was so good. My strategy was to only have about one bite's worth of everything I tried so I could try as many things as possible. Obviously I couldn't try each of the 500+ items, but every single thing I tried was delicious.

Absolutely delicious all the way around.  Normally when you go to a buffet there are maybe 2-3 items that are legitimately good.  The rest are just ok but you're happy because of the variety and unlimited volume.

This place?  Man....there were at least 5 spectacular items and the rest were legitimately good.  Basically, the average dishes here were as good as the best dishes at place like Wynn and Bellagio.  If you compare them to the cheaper buffets in towns then EVERYTHING at Caesars is better than anything you get at those buffets.

Lamb chops were ridiculously good.  That was probably the highlight.  The bread was the same stuff they serve at Caesar's best restaurant (Guy Savoy).  And a lot of the things were cooked fresh right in front of you.  

There was even Ramen and Pho.  Just an insane buffet and highly recommended.  I hope they keep the quality up!

Really? Is this really the 'best buffet in Vegas?' This place was a huge huge huge disappointment. The first time I came here, I waited an hour in line and then ended up leaving when I found out the line was another 2 hours...ugh. This past time, I was happy to see that you could get a slip of paper with a time to come back so you could go do other things for awhile and come back. Great idea! We came back 90 min later... only to find out that there were 2 more lines to wait in. Seriously?!?! Why even have the paper? Just call me when you are actually ready. We waited another 45 min or so to pay ( a ridic 65$ ish with a prepaid tip) and be seated. Why? They kept letting people ahead who paid to skip the line. That is ridiculous and infuriating. Anyway, when we finally got in, we were overwhelmed by the amount of food there. It was a ton. Unfortunately, pretty much none of it was good. There was one dumpling I got that was good, but upon returning, they didn't have anymore. Tried to ask of they had more and the man behind the counter claimed a different dumpling was it (not the case, clearly...one was shrimp one was pork). The pastas were all disappointing...flavorless..boring. The pho was ok, but the ramen was gross. The lamb chops were way underdone...super red...ew. Poor lambs. The seafood was overly fishy...not too fresh. The Mexican food was awful... my friend actually spit it out. The only good items were the mac and cheese, the cheese (duh), and the yellow curry. The desserts were a joke...flavorless again. The service was awful. We never got a refill on our drinks. Plates sat on our table ready to be cleared for a long time. I would never go back here and never recommend.

MOST HYPED BUFFET & ALL DISAPPOINTMENT

Wait times are 3 hours to get in the line.  Once you get in line it's another hour and half.  Disney rides are better than this overpriced buffet.  To top it off the hostess decides to allow more ppl to cut the line without paying extra or having platinum status.   Skip this buffet during holiday season.  It was overpriced at 65 after tax during Christmas.  Buffett is hyped, same items in bellagio for less price and less crowd.  Will never do this Buffett ever

Wasn't what I expected. Too expensive, long wait, food was old, and alcohol beverages should be included for the price they charge per Person. Service was good, the check in line seems pretty organized. Maybe the good was old because we had showed up at a later time but that  shouldn't matter. They should be on top of their buffet no matter what time they close. Since it was a holiday "WEEKEND", we paid $65 per person. I don't agree with them having a "holiday menu" a day after Thanksgiving because it's over with. Not fair for others that already celebrated the day of. The only thing I really loved was the salted caramel hot chocolate from the dessert station. I'm very disappointed. We sat in traffic for 7 hrs from LA to Vegas so we choose this buffet to welcome us with great, breath taking food but it didn't!!

My visit was on Saturday, February 24 during brunch hours. I went with a friend and both of us were in love with Bacchanal Buffet. The options are so many! I think my favorite was the Mexican food - especially seeing how the cooks were making the tacos!!!! Our waiter was Carlos, he offered an amazing customer service to us. He was quick to bring the requested drinks and was very attentive!!! He definitely played a role in loving this place! Will definitely be visiting again!!!!'

Love this place!!! This place never fails to me! Every time I come to Vegas , this will be my place for dinner. This buffet is $60 per person, pricy but well worth it. I can stay there for two hrs! I love their varieties of food and there food taste delicious here!

Nothing screams lack luster food than the classic American buffet.  This is not the case with Caesar's Buffet.

The choices are not only diverse, but tasted fantastic.

I went straight for the boiled crab legs.  They didn't skimp and only offer snow crab, but king crab as well.  It was so tasty, whatever crab boil they used you could really taste it.  Some of the best crab legs I've ever had.

I moved on to the Chinese.  They had all sorts of dumplings and steamed buns.  The BBQ pork buns were so great.  The sweetness offered a good balance.

I then ate some sushi, I stuck with the nigiri.  The salmon and tuna was good, but nothing fantastic.

They also have a noodle stand, which I loved they had all sorts, like pho, udon and ramen.  I went with ramen with tonkotsu broth.  It was excellent for ramen at a buffet.

They have all the buffet standbys, but I was too full.  They had a custom street taco stand I wanted to try, but I just couldn't do it. 

Easily the best buffet in Vegas.

Been here 4 times in 3 trips to Vegas since October 2012.  Bacchanal is a 4 on some nights but a 5 on its best nights.  The spread is amazing and the food presentation and atmosphere is sophisticated and modern.  Yes, the line can be horrendous just like every other top buffet.  Twice we waited an hour.  Another time we paid an extra $15 per person to skip the 90 minute line.  The last time, we arrived at 5:45pm on a Friday and there was absolutely no line at all, amazingly.   The food is quite good to excellent but has been inconsistent.  3 out of the 4 nights, the King Crab Legs, while meaty and plentiful were way too salty.   As King Crab is the main attraction for many people, I wish that it wasn't so salty, bordering on unpleasantly salty.   Another night, several items at the meat carving station were dry.  Love the shrimp cocktail, cheese station, sliders, and tonkatsu ramen with extra pork though.  And Bacchanal has the #1 dessert station hands down.

What an incredible buffet!  Although we thought it was higher priced before going in, we were so impressed by the food, selection and service.  They even had my favorite bread pudding you can customize with toppings.  What a wonderful experience...highly recommend and will definitely go back.
My second trip to the best buffet in town, all I can say is AMAZING!!!

Seems everyone goes to here for buffet so do we. First of all, long line up anytime... guess because it is too famous?! No, they intend to make a long line out there... when u got in, you can see bunch of empty tables staying there!! kinda angry about that, 1 maybe the hosts work too slow, 2 maybe they really wanna make u keep waiting....
So come to the food, yes they have many selection, I tried a bit of everything. nothing really impress me, they are just very so so, especially the meat, they are tasteless,  and big! grill fish are overcooked, dessert are just looking nice but don't taste gd. The only better thing is the crab legs, that's it. Also, it takes forever for the servers to clean your dishes.....

It is $56+tax per person, I don't think the quality plus the long wait worth this price tho.
mmmmm  Big Buffet.. great food.   I have already recommended to others.  Not much other to say... look at all the reviews.  there all good!

Can I declare Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon a tie in best buffets in Las Vegas? They definitely changed my idea of buffets. Bacchanal had a bit of wait to get in on a Saturday for brunch, but the wait was definitely worth it. The brunch also includes unlimited mimosas which is fun. The cost may seem steep at first, but it makes sense once you see and taste the variety. 

I won't be able to adequately describe the variety. In the front room they have seafood, BBQ meats, desserts and breakfast foods. I was almost full on all of that when I noticed a hall, a hall containing another room! This is where they almost hid the Italian, Asian and cheese plate selections. I couldn't believe how many different foods they offer. Most foods are served on small plates so that food is still hot and served fresh. My only complaint is that the seating can be awkward on a busy day if you are seated at the back of the room. It felt like a maze trying to get through all of the people and tables to get food.

It has the potential of being 5 stars, if the meat was cooked and seasoned better and the hot food was "hot".   Another reason I didn't give it 5 starts was because my server was sick, and she kept sneezing at our table.   I just hope we don't catch what she has......

We were not expecting to make it here because we have heard of the ridiculous wait. However, we came on a weekday for lunch and were seated right away. First impression was the place is huge. We were going to be seated at a corner somewhere but we asked for a closer table near the pools of the hotel. There are many options here. The Asian area has good dim sum and the best BBQ pork my husband has ever tried. The sushi was meh. The rice was too chewy but the fish was fresh. They have a nice area with different cheese and cold meats. The prosciutto and manchego cheese were my favorite. Next to this they also have baby mozzarella and cherry tomatoes with basil.  Look hard because you might miss them but you don't want to miss them. Their pasta area looked OK.  I only tried a seafood pasta dish served in a small dish pan and it was very tasty. As far as American food we tried the prime rib which was very well seasoned and melt in your mouth good, and the mac and cheese which had a Southern taste to it. The sliders were very good as well. I also had the paella and it was very scrumptious. They had a pork belly with lentils in a small bowl near the Mexican food area. It tasted like the Asian BBQ pork I mentioned before. The only Mexican dish I tried was the Chilaquiles. The sauce was bad. I can make better Chilaquiles from a can. True story. They have a juice section. The guava and hibiscus were my favorite. The dessert section, my favorite section, was generously stocked. If you don't like star anise don't try their 5-spice Chinese chocolate cake,  yuk! Everything else was divine. Their gelato a little on the watery sude but very tasty. The coconut flan was good and so was the creme brulee.

Our tummies were happy here. We spent 2 hrs trying different foods and slowly enjoying them. Food is coming constantly so nothing tastes old.

The line is terrible long. There is a wait line. Then another huge line just to be seated. But it's all well worth the wait. AMAZING food!!!! Best buffet I been to. Everything I tried was delicious. Well mostly everything.  My favorite has to be the paella, and Mac & cheese. Even the pho was soooo good. And I am a picky pho eater. I had my family try a little bit with me and they were just sold! They needed there own bowl lol wish they had buffets like this back in Anaheim CA. I literally would go back just because of this buffet .

The brisket here is simply HEAVEN!!
Best thing on the buffet. 
The oysters were my least favorite as they didn't taste good at all and had a lot of sand in them. 
Love the homemade chips and the many options from Italian to Chinese to America. 
Definitely recommend

"BACCHUS  The Roman God Of The Feast
BACCHANAL  A Feast Worthy Of The Gods"

- Some sign outside

This buffet is seriously a feast worth of the gods. 

I came here with my mom and I as our first stop on our Buffet of Buffets adventure. For this specific buffet, we had to pay an additional $25 each, for some reason (I' didn't pay, so I don't know what that was for). It was a Monday and we got in line around 8:30 for dinner. FYI, they close the line at 10. It took us an hour to get to the register and to get back in line to be seated.   

As we were being taken to our table, the hostess gave us a little tour of the different stations they had and I was already sold. Everything is so beautiful in there! Most importantly, the food looked so good. Presentation - A+

Since we got in pretty late, we had about an hour before they were going to take the food (10:45). 

What did they have?
Asian, Italian, Mexican, American, Seafood

I made a mistake of taking so much from the Asian section, that I didn't really get to the meaty stuff, literally. My mom got some and let me try some duck and lamb chop, YUM. I didn't even get to try the crab legs! I saw this one table covered in crab legs; it looked like they were having fun over there. I did try the oysters which didn't make me sick so I was happy! 

I can go on and on but I'll just stop now.

I came to this buffet for dinner on a Tuesday and the price was $55 per person. It was not worth the $55, in my opinion. There were some good food options but highly overrated. I was so excited because they serve soufflés, which are my favorite dessert but they were awful. Take your money and go to Wynn's buffet - much better!

We'll ladies and gentlemen, I can honestly say this is the best buffet restaurant I've eaten at. Costly at $56 per person, but we'll worth it. The restaurant ambiance was great with the right amount of location lighting and a mellow low volume music in the background. Food choices was amazing and the quality was second to none. The tomahawk chops were tender and flavor packed. The dimsum was always fresh as it was gone one tray after the other. They even had gourmet cook chicken feet. Even though I couldn't get myself to put it in my mouth, but it looked good. Not a whole lot of choices with their sushi, but what they had out was fresh and appealing.
Servers were very friendly and quick to clean up the the tables. The establishment was very clean, super comfortable seats, and a very classy atmosphere. I was thoroughly satisfied with my experience at Bachannal. Looking forward to doing it again.
I heard so much about this place.  The wait was 2 hours and the food is pretty much normal.  Not exceptional like people said.  They do have a wide range of variety of food to choose from.

Don't bother. It is really expensive, but the food is mediocre at best. The only thing that was really good was the smashed potatoes. Tried the prime rib - dry and tough. Tried the warn crab legs - they were OK, but really watery. Deserts were mediocre. Nothing to really Yelp about. I would eat somewhere else.
I would say it is the best food buffet in Vegas. But very expensive and crowded. Come early to avoid long lines.

Like everything at Caesars Palace, the buffet is huge. Be prepared to stand in line for about 30 minutes from 6:00 pm on, but the line moves.  You can electronically sign in at some free standing kiosks, but you will still wait.  Once in, the table spacing is nice and you are not shoulder to shoulder with other diners. Food covers just about every ethnic and geographic possibility. There is plenty of it. Salads are fresh as are the many seafood offerings. Though I won't eat raw oysters in a landlocked state, they, as well as the king crab legs and shrimp appear to be favorites.  Your sever will take your soft drink order and replenish your drink as many times as you wish. Domestic Beer and wine are an extra $15.00 for unlimited refills.  While there is a two hour limit on your grazing time, it is realistic that in that span you will have tried everything, treated yourself to the amazing dessert selection (including a few sugar free entries as well as fresh fruit) and be ready to waddle your way out of the dining room.  Quality...this is not gourmet cuisine but mass preparation of many different foods. A very nice experience, but unless you are a quantity feeder it is something worth experiencing once and then exploring all the other possibilities Vegas has to offer.

This buffet is not cheap but we wanted to try a vegas buffet since it's so popular. 
We started with the seafood section which was pretty good. They had nice crab legs, oysters, shrimps. There were many things to try which was good. In meat section we don't eat beef so we were hoping for some nice lamb chops or something but they only had lamb T-bone which was extremely tough and after struggling with it for few minutes we just gave up on it. 
The dessert section was really good with a lot fresh looking desserts. Everything tasted fresh and good quality. Overall a good experience. 
Did we eat worth the money we paid? Definitely not but I would still say its worth experiencing at least once.

Lines lines and more lines. This is the second time i have been to vegas and tried it based on the reviews and friends reference. We went and took the ticket and wait was approximately 55 minutes which is not bad compared to the 3+ hours the others stated on here. We came back in an hour and then realized we have to wait once again to get in. After that we got to another line which were seperated in 3 groups. The VIPs, the couples, and the big groups. 

Then we were seated promptly after another 30 minutes. We had complementary mimosas and drinks. We wandered around to find food and yet there are more lines. One line for seafood, one for tacos , one for crepes, one for ice cream. Lines everywhere and to be honest the food wasnt even that great. Its really the rave that got people here. I regret waiting 15 minutes for 4 tacos because I didnt know what the line was about. 

Sure the decor was nice, the staff dressed professional but the food was average at best. I feel very proud of myself for not spending a huge amount of money on the buffet of buffets pass and paying extra for this. Overall at least I can tell my friends ive been here.

I have never walked out of a buffet so happy! Every single thing you try is amazing, the service is phenomenal and the drinks are simply the best!

Our server was Alvaro (El Chileno).  He was very pleasant and attentive.  He even gave us tips on how to fit more food in our stomachs! No rush whatsoever.  

The highlights of the night were definitely:

Raw Oysters (extremely fresh!)
Udon Soup

Salad-- tomato with mozzarella
Hot crab legs
Truffled scallop potatoes
Lobster corn chowder
Creamed leeks and lobster 
Vanilla crème brûlée

Pecan pie
Apple pie
Donut -- a.k.a. macaroon (rose)
Mochi - green tea and coffee

Make sure to try everything on that list if you go there.  

I also ordered the sangria and I must say it's one of the best i've ever tried.  It comes in a 16oz glass.  The deserts are to die for and the coffee tastes wonderful.  We probably drank 3 cups each.

This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas.  You definitely get your money's worth.
4 stars for all the good food I had but the desserts were a little disappointing. I wish they had regular vanilla or chocolate macarons or pies or something. I'll still come back for the food tho.

The wait was forever, had to wait 1 hour to get text message, then line up again 1.5 hr to pay and line up again to get in!!!! 
service was bad... waiter dissappeared and changed to another one without telling us 
food was delicious though... lots of meat cuts, king crabs... etcs
only good dessert that MUST have is creme burlee!!!! and crepes!!!

Does not worth it at all. $70 dinner buffet is pretty much the same as a $35 buffet in other place, and cannot ever compete with any seafood buffet in San Francisco Bay Area. Hours wait line with this quality of foods, I definitely do not recommend anybody to come.

The bucchanal buffet at Caesar's palace is 9.5 stars out of 10 for me. Excellent variety of choices and high quality prepared food. My favorites choices were the different ceviche's, the sashimi, the freshly made ice cream (tai tea ice cream was awesome), and the mexican rice.

Unbelievable selection, high quality food and great service. Best buffet in town and is a must for anyone traveling to Vegas. A little expensive, but good deal for rewards club members. Must try the fresh cut bacon.

This is my favorite buffet in Vegas, basically if you there is anything you feel like eating, they probably have it! Everything from fresh seafood to dim sum. This place definitely will not disappoint. 
 
When you're ready for desserts you'll feel like a kid in a candy store. 

I ate myself into a food coma and had to take a nap after.

Wow! This place put me to sleep in a serious food coma because I could not stop eating. This is the buffet of all buffets in my book! Seriously there were so many selections it was so hard to just choose one! I really loved having an assortment of selection. They have so many types of foods to choose from. We loved it so much we went twice!  We got to experience brunch which they had chicken and waffles, pancakes, French toast, potatoes, and food that they had at both for dinner and brunch. They had Asaian cuisine like pho, sushi, sweet and sour chicken, beer and broccoli and more. They had pasta like lasagna,meatballs, pizza and more. There were crab legs, oysters,brisket, the BEST mac n cheese and mashed potatoes.... there is much more but I don't want to spoil it! Go try it for yourself! Brunch on the weekdays is $43... but definitely worth the splurge! Make sure you try the Nutella crepes and all the treats at the desert bar!
Incredible selection, wonderful service, and all the food is well prepared and tastes great. Love this place!

You can't escape Vegas without going to at least one buffet. The question? Which one? If you're like me and you come to Vegas once a decade it is all a wild guess though Yelp is of course a blessing. That being said let me take the guesswork out for you and just go to The Bachannal at Caesar's Palace. Had lunch there and my girls were beaming after they left. As you would expect a whole lot to choose from. Definitely eat the waygu bed sliders. Everything from the Asian section was awesome which to me says a lot about the quality. The had a to order taco bar. Shellfish bar. The BBQ section brought a tear to my eye. Sausages. Prime rib. Brisket that you would sell your soul for. The carver at the BBQ station was so nice too. He was smiling away chatting the entire two hours I was there. Wait. Did I just admit I was there for two hours? I swear I didn't eat the entire time. 90 minutes tops! Every dessert under the sky including made to order shaved ice but you have to ask. All there is a little sign in the dessert bar.y daughter saw it got some and loved it even comparing the quality to stuff found in Hawaii.

So much food, so little time!
Everything on the buffet was amazing! The staff was professional and attentive, the food was replenished as fast as it was eaten, the price was more than fair.
I have nothing bad to say about this place!

Great food I am always thought vegas has lost it's touch in buffet style food. However this place was great sure few meats had way to much salt but rest was great. If your sea food lover they have every type of sea food. It don't matter what u like they have everything.

I'd have to say, Wicked Spoon has better desserts, but this place is pretty awesome in every other aspect. We paid a little extra to do the express line, for 2 of us, it came out to be a little over $100. 

My only qualm with this place was that there seems to be a line for the foods, but it's primarily for the prime rib & seafood. 

They have a lot of great food- Asian, Mexican, pizza and mini burgers, with some breakfast stuff out still.

There's a lottttt of choices- a lot more than I've seen anywhere else. I seriously think this is the best buffet in all of Vegas (although like I said- Wicked Spoon has better desserts.) 

For desserts, they make crepes, and it's up to you to deck it all out. They have gelato too, people tell me there's Mochi, but I didn't see any :( they had gummy worms and a bunch of random candy too- so that was kinda cool. But aside from that it was kinda plain. I do have to say, my boyfriend told the server it was my birthday & they surprised me with a cute plate with happy birthday & my age written out in chocolate syrup. I'm easily amused, and they sang. It was sweet. I definitely loved the experience here. You have to check it out! So worth it.

Yes, I am a fan. Friends of my wife and I brought us here. They highly recommended this place being they had visited 2 times prior. There are 9 food stations from exotic seafood to Chinese food to desert bar to Italian food to varies steaks, lamb and chops. I am normally ok with just 1 plate I had 3 plates here the food was excellent. My wife is not typically a lover of buffet food but she really enjoyed the options here. 

My only reason for giving 4 stars and not 5 is the extremely long lines (obviously the best buffet on the strip). We were told the standard line was about a 2 hour wait therefore we paid $15 extra per person for the express line which still took about 45 minutes. 

FYI: If you come with 8 or more people they automatically charge an 18% gratuity to your bill before you even sit down.

LOVE. I've been to the Wynn and Wicked Spoon buffets (albeit the Wicked Spoon for brunch not dinner) and the Bacchanal is the BEST hands down, but especially in the dessert area. We were seated at the large table overlooking the Roman Pools and the decor in the buffet is absolutely fresh and stunning. I've never been to a buffet that was able to do Chinese dim sum dishes properly, but the Bacchanal pulls it off. My only regret is that my stomach was not large enough to sample everything. I cannot wait to return. I pray to god that the quality stays the same.

Visits: 1st
Rating: 4*

One of the best buffets in Vegas, if not the best, if not the U.S. For $65 a pop, it better be. She loves buffets, especially in Vegas. Me? Whatever. For that price I can eat at a very nice gastro pub. But got to admit, this place is good. The selection is good & the food is higher end than what you would expect for a buffet. They try to cover all the most popular cuisines in their selections & they do it well. Very impressed with the spread & how good each tastes.

Tonight We got in line at 430pm to get a ticket. I entered my number twice I was suppose to get a text at 8.02 pm then go back and I understood it would be another hour. It's 9:04pm I'm still waiting for dinner. I have now been on the phone with a supervisor who is talking to Jackie and her manager is Micheal Lee.

I've came here for breakfast and lunch before and both times were amazing! The breakfast had a wide variety of breakfast foods as well as a bit of lunch dishes. Wide selection of desserts and ice cream/sorbet flavors as we'll. Breakfast did not come with the crab legs and as much Seafood though. I don't remember the price for breakfast but lunch was around $40. For two people for lunch on a Monday, the wait was pretty short - about 20 minutes I would say. For lunch there was pizza, dimsum, oysters , crab legs, prime rib, noodle soups, fried rice, egg rolls , sushi , and much more! Everything was delicious, definitely ended our meal with a food coma! x__x
Huge variety of food..worth the price....there is everything you can imagine! You will leave satisfied.

This place is still the favorite buffet restaurant in Vegas for us. Incredible dinner choices and many options to feed your various taste buds. I think it's worth the high price and I'd choose to come back here again if I'm ever in the area.

Great service and friendly staff too. Beautiful and spacious restaurant layout. The wait staff was consistently nice and quick with our drink refill requests throughout our meals. Gotta love Bacchanal!

"Do you have your stretchy eating pants on??" Enjoy!

Well I never expected to give this buffet a bad review but my experience going to try it did not work out as I had hoped or expected.  It was a weeknight at 8:30pm when we got there with a party of three.  The line was long, just passed the first hostess stand.  I went to the kiosk to "put our name in" and it said to come back at 9pm.  We got in the line that wasn't moving and the host lady came through the line looking at everyone's ticket.  When she got to us she told us to get out of line and come back at 9pm.  That doesn't make sense because by the time we would pay it would have been at least 9pm.  AND the couple in front us had a ticket that said 8:55pm.  So she asked us to get out of line when the people in front of us has a ticket with a 5 minute difference but they were ok.  The lady was so rude, she was short, older, with short gray hair.  We were so disgusted by her rudeness that we left and didn't even eat there.  When you are asking people to pay almost $60 for a buffet you should at least treat them nicely.
Most everything was very good with a great selection. Definitely get some crepes. Maybe eat just the crepes. Also most of the select meats were very well done.

Quality wise, this is probably the best buffet in Vegas. The line system is basically, first you go to their kiosk to get a time ticket. They offer you to jump the line for $25 pp but be warned that it's to jump only the regular paying line. You'll still have to stand in line for a seat which could take 20-45 minutes. They text you when it's time to get in the first line to pay. Then there's a 2nd line to get seated. We went for the beginning of dinner on a Sunday, 3pm. Got a 1 hour wait but we were staying at the hotel so we waited in our room. Total time for the table was about an hour. 2 rooms of food. Back room has mostly Asian and Italian. Note for those wanting crab legs, there's a lady near the pizzas serving warmed up crab legs so skip that crazy seafood line if that's what you're lining up for.

Best buffet I've ever had. I'm a huge fan of seafood, fresh seafood, chilled seafood, and all you can eat seafood. There were 3 dudes behind the counter shuckin and guttin oysters and crab legs all day. The seafood had a big turn over because it was super busy. That's a good thing for buffets! They had basically everything you could think of. The varietals really stressed me out, so I kept to my go tos. 

Here's what I ate: 
2 huge plates of crab legs - super sweet and very fresh tasting. 

1 plate of crab claws - amazing shiz

2 plates of shrimp - these were huge and must have been 6/8 count. They were amazing. 

1 plate of oysters - these were fresh, but not as flavorful. Still worth it! 

1 giant slice of luscious prime rib - perfectly medium rare with creamy horseradish. Oh so goods.

A few pork ribs and beef ribs  

1 plate of a random assortment of sushi

Some other ransom amazing shit: Korean BBQ short ribs, Chinese style crab legs, bread, and poke salad. 

I can't even articulate the dessert station. It's overwhelmingly good.

Not bad for all you can eat fresh seafood, steaks, ribs, and a bunch of other shit for $65.

I'll be back!

The wait is just nuts. There are touchscreen stands outside where you input your name and phone number, and it gives you the wait time (60 minutes approximately). That's only to receive a text to let you know you can stand in line (many people didn't understand it, and I felt bad for the older lady trying to organize a hungry mob of people).

Once you get in line, it's pretty decent until you get to the actual queue. That took about forty minutes, and standing on marble ground makes it hard on one's back.

The food is pretty good, probably the best buffet on the strip. But for the cost of entry, one would hope for nothing mediocre. However, many of the options (slider, beef rib, crawfish) were less than par, but what saved the place for me was the hot crab legs. Plates upon plates, which I usually frown upon in the average buffet, but I understand now. I really do.

Desserts were solid, champagne shots (apple pie filling with some sort of cream and baked topping) were my top.

Will go again if I get my yearly bonus, but will take a solid sit-down dinner to save money to gamble.

I wish I didn't have to write this review but I am very disappointed about my experience at Bacchanal due to food poisoning. I took my boyfriend there for his birthday on July 9, 2017 (we ate between 4pm - 5:30pm), and within a few hours, he was violently throwing up (7 times total within the span of 8 hours). It was the only meal we had that day and my group and I only had pizza the night before (none of us were sick from that). 

It has been difficult to reach management regarding my experience. My only intention is to let them know, nothing else. Please be careful when eating at buffets, even at Bacchanal, which was my favorite until what happened yesterday.

GREAT SERVICE.  I can't commend them enough for the great service.

Food looks beautiful.  The desserts are gorgeous.

But the taste didn't live up to the hype.  I've had better or been wow-ed elsewhere.  I've eaten at Wicked Spoon, the Bellagio, and here (buffet-wise) and Bacchanal is in third place.

EXCELLENT!

We had lunch on Wednesday (9/9/2015).  It's $37.95 for lunch.  There was no wait and we had our fill of:

- Stone Crab Claws
- Shrimp Cocktail

and a little:

- dim sum
- sushi
- desserts

The spread is huge.  They have every type of food I could think of and the stuff that I tried was very good, but I have to admit I mainly ate stone crab and shrimp cocktail.  The sushi that they had didn't look that appetizing.  I think the sushi chef needs to take a little more time in cutting the fish and shaping the rice.  The pieces looked like someone was in a hurry to make them (kind of sloppy looking).

There are juices in small carafes that you can drink.  The carving station looked really good, but I had lots of steaks during my Vegas trip, so I didn't have any.  The Japanese ramen station looked good too, but I didn't try it.

There's also a huge dessert station with freshly made crepes.  I was too full for dessert, so I had bread pudding and a few snickerdoodle cookies.

If you like a huge variety, then definitely try Bacchanal.

Xie Xie!
Is it just me or was it not worth the money or wait? I mean it was good but maybe it was over sold to me...

Within the realm of buffets this place is hard to beat. which is why i am giving it a 4 star and not a 2.

While other buffets may have a variety of crappy food, here you will find eclectic selection of food that are of descent quality

However, in the end this is still a buffet, you will not find anything extraordinary.

As with any buffet, things are hit and miss, and consistency is always an issue. Bacchanal, with its pricey $60ish dinner price per person, is no exception. The wait was also around an hour long for 3 people, and we came around 5-6pm.

At first glance, I was really excited. Really deceptively huge space, lots of options, focus on more composed small plates. You even get cute rubber finger holders to hold the hot plates.

Pros:
- Crab legs. The snow crab legs were really sweet and the way it's cut up allows for really easy eating. You can eat them either cold or hot.
- Mexican. Really surprised. The pozole was delicious. They do tacos (carne asada, pollo, and carnitas) to order on the plancha, and were smaller but delicious. Toppings include onions, salsa, and guac.
- Dessert. I was really impressed. Lot of options. There was a thai iced tea ice cream, red velvet yuzu whoopie pie, a platter of French macarons (though textural consistency issues were all across the board from soft to hard)
- The brisket was pretty good.

Cons:
- Asian food. The Chinese section had dim sum and some rice, noodles, and meat dishes. The shrimp dumpling skins were too thick, the stir fry chicken dish I tried a little of was inedible. The chicken had just been sitting out there under the heat lamps and turned into hard bricks. The Japanese food didn't have much either. The only decent thing was the noodle soup section.
- The mussels and oysters seemed quite dry and not fresh. It had a fishy smell and taste so that put me off.

Well, this was an experience that I think everyone ought to have at least once in a life. Come on an empty stomach and give yourself three hours (two to eat--there is a max time limit), and up to one for the wait to get in. I ended up going after 4 and paying $65ish for dinner per person. I recommend lining up at the seafood station first, which seems to be the most popular area of the buffet. There is also a meat area, with lambchops, an area with tacos and different meats, dim sum, an Asian noodle station (with tonkotsu ramen and pho, etc)...dim sum......salads...congee even...and a huge area with dessert.  It's worth the wait, and the desserts are a bit better than at the bellagio I think.

I went to the 'use to be my favorite' Wicked Spoon buffet a few months ago in Vegas and I wasn't too thrilled. The food wasn't bad but no where near the quality in the earlier days before it got super popular. Sadly, the food does not justify the long wait anymore. 

This time around I went to the Bacchanal instead and I was pleasantly surprised. Looks like Caesar's Palace really beefed up their game in the buffet competition. It isn't hard to see that they 'borrowed ' a lot of ideas from the popular Wicked Spoon. Most of the food is individually portioned and even give you these cute little rubber grip to hold the hot plates. Their raw seafood bar is the most impressive of all (among Ballagio, Wynn and Wicked Spoon). They exceeded in both variety and quality. It is not often you can find some decent crawfish cooked in Cajun seasonings. Raw oysters were fresh and sweet.

Bacchanal buffet have a lot to offer. You can find simple American fare, the usual meat craving station, as well as Mediterranean, Asian, Italian and whole bunch of International cuisine. Of course, they have a sinfully beautiful dessert station as well.

I enjoyed my meal. I think the quality is better than the Wicked Spoon and Wynn. The variety is better than the all time favorite Ballagio. If they could keep up with the quality, I have little reason to visit other buffet spots.

Best buffet in Las Vegas! Well worth the price. I went around 4:30 on a Wednesday and there was no wait time at all. I enjoyed everything I ate, everything was delicious. So many items I doubt you will be able to try everything before you're completely stuffed. The desserts were amazing. Now I know why so many people rave about the Bacchanal Buffet.

The best (of course also the most expensive) buffet I've ever been too.  But don't forget that expensive food don't always mean good food.  So I totally don't feel bad for splurged on this one.  I'm not a fan of cold crab leg or dry sushi, although that's what you need to chow down most to justify the high cost of the buffet.  But there are so many other choices, I don't even care about them anymore,  The beef slider and the fresh squeeze OJ are my favorites.

Our final Buffet stop just had to be this iconic name which for some reason is pronounced differently by different people :)

The first thing that will hit you is just the vast expanse of this restaurant. It's easily the biggest buffet spread I've ever had the pleasure of drooling over!! I'm not kidding, if say you were to pick something hot from one end of the spread and move your way upto the other end and finally onto your seat (Which due to the size of the joint can be tricky to find!), you shouldn't be surprised to see your plate of food is now cold!! So better strategize your way through this one.

I'll get to the food in a bit, but one of the best things about this place and something every other large scale buffet joints should follow (Wicked Spoon and Aria do to some extent), is the concept of Petite/Individual Portions! The idea is not just great to look at, I'm sure in the end it prevents wastage as well! Well done Bacchanal!!

Onto the food now, the crux of it is everything tasted nice although not great. The overall experience simply on taste was a bit of a mixed bag as some options were seasoned beautifully well and some not so much. The options though are endless so there is something for everyone here literally! Some of the Warm foods were sadly cold, especially on the Butcher section and specifically their American Wagyu Beef. The lady weirdly kept slicing away from the cold top while its bottom kept getting warm. 

The dessert section as with some of the other places, was phenomenal! Vegas buffets do nail their Desserts big time! Their Flan, pies, tarts, brownie were all top notch!

To end, this place deserves all the attention and accolades its gotten and easily is one of the Top 3 Buffet's in Vegas in my book!

Buffets aren't usually my thing, and I initially balked at the $70 cost for two people, but it was WORTH IT. They aren't shooting for the lowest common denominator here, which means you can expect the chefs to take risks (and in our case, resulted in feelings of euphoria with every bite).

Highlights included the perfectly juicy prime rib (cut upon order), beautifully acidic ceviche (a nice palate cleanser in between bites), everything in the Chinese section (especially the beef with Chinese broccoli; it's hard to find great authentic Chinese food, and I certainly didn't expect it here), and the molten lava cake (with luxuriously rich dark chocolate that was not sweet per se, but unmistakably indulgent).

Oh, and Bacchanal's decor is clean and modern, but who cares, it's days later and I'm still in a reverie about the epic meal itself.

3.5 stars

Buffet was smaller than imagined.

Pros:
-No line around 5:30pm Sunday night.
-Mochi (ice-cream filled) in the ice cream case were good (they have four kinds: vanilla, chocolate coffee, green tea, red bean)
-Service was good, waiters will bring you crab crackers when asked.

Cons:
-Little juice bottles weren't cold enough though they were partially sitting in ice.
-Macarons were way too sweet. Could a clever way of getting people to eat less hah.
-Didn't see sweet potato tots nor the other fried baskets.
-Didn't see the watermelon and feta salad.
-No honeycomb.

A little disappointed that they don't have all the good stuff all the time.. especially for dinner, but I left satisfied and didn't have any bad reaction to stuffing myself soo great job Bacchanal!

Hundreds of years ago the Romans would throw the grandest parties filled with endless amounts of wine and food, in honor of Bacchus, the Roman god of agriculture and wine. They called them Bacchanals. 

The Bacchanal Buffet inside Caesar's Palace absolutely lives up to its heritage when it comes to the food and the drinks.

Imagine all of the food you could possibly want to eat, and as much of it as you might want -- that's the Bacchanal Buffet. From endless amounts of meats cooked in every way possible -- prime rib, steak, pork, pork belly, bacon, chicken -- to endless crab legs to the endless sushi and sashimi to dim sum to tacos to salad to American country food to desserts to drinks. Just about everything under the sun is here, even Thai tea boba desserts.

Of course, being an all-you-can-eat buffet, you should come here hungry. Maybe starving. Skip your previous meals and then come here for a late lunch or dinner. Stay for at least an hour -- possibly two or three. Share stories with your friends or dining group, tell jokes, bring a small game if you need to -- let yourself enjoy the food and digest, and then enjoy more food and digest. 

Everything here is fabulous. And if it's your first time visiting, definitely do yourself a favor and just take the grand tour by walking around the entire buffet bar until it stops. And don't forget to keep going around the corner, at least twice or thrice. Just when you thought you're coming to the end of the buffet bar, there's always that next corner. And all of the food along the bar is different from the next -- so don't think that just because you're sitting in one section, you should stay in that section's food area. Keep exploring!

The biggest downside here is the price and probably the wait. Dinner is about $80-$90 per person without any drink packages. Lunch is a little bit cheaper (around $65). But the wait...that... varies. I've heard people waiting for just 30 minutes to an hour, and then I've heard some people wait 2 to 3 hours to be seated. 

Personally, I think the way to dine in Vegas is to find yourself a friend with priority line privileges (i.e. a Total Rewards Diamond Card). That way you and your entire group can skip the entire queue. Two hour line? No problem. Just go straight to the Diamond Line with your Diamond Card and suddenly your wait is 1 minute. There really just isn't another way to do Vegas sometimes. (Hey all of my Yelp friends, just let me know if we're ever in Vegas at the same time and I'm happy to swipe you to the front of the line.)
I actually prefer this buffet over the much talked about Wicked Spoon. The selection and freshness of all the entrees were great.

"THE NUMBER ONE BUFFET IN THE LAS VEGAS BY USA TODAY". If you're a tourist I'm sure you saw that and decided to Yelp it to see if it was any good. Great job!

The Bacchanal buffet has steady declined for me, mostly due to the behemoth price (~ $50) which could be justified for its mammoth sized choices. When it first opened it was around (~$30) for dinner which made it IMPOSSIBLE to pass in terms of buffets in Las Vegas, then they increase the prices gradually. Bait and switch :(!

Should you go here? 

Yes if:
1. The line isn't atrociously long (a hour plus)
 - you could pay $15 per person to get in the "fast pass" line 
2. If there is not a major convention (i.e. EDC, CES, SEMA, etc)
 - this would make the line 2+ hours long
3. Money ain't a thang
4. Comped!
5. Relatives from out of town that want to experience a Vegas buffet. 

Is it good?

Usually! I won't tell you what to eat because half the things aren't the same. The carving station has been solid and the assortment of ice cream flavors are pretty cool. I like the brown ale caramel and the thai tea flavor. You can get souffles baked to order, just ask! You might even see Dyan Ng, the dessert boss, whose pretty cute :).

Skip the line!!!!

There is not a lot of variety for the food, but the quality is amazing. 

Be aware they will have the A/C pumping to getting you to leave!! Bring a sweater!!

I grew up in Las Vegas, and when I was a kid the Rio Carnival World Buffet was the best in town.  I am back visiting, and it seemed based on the reviews that this place has taken over that ranking.

When you first walk in, you are overwhelmed with all of the amazing looking choices, crab, shrimp, BBQ, pork belly, salad bar, dessert bar, creperie, Mexican, Italian, Chinese, Japanese....We took a walk around to get an idea of what was available before we starting diving in.

It all went downhill from there, starting with the crab.  Both of us broke open the crab, excited to dive in....but almost spit out the first bite, not only was it frozen and stringy, it tasted like...nothing.  We moved on, taking 1 bite out of everything hoping to find something worth eating.  We eventually ended up full, off our 1 bite disappointments, and left.  I would say the only thing worth eating was the lobster mac & cheese (not because it had and lobster flavor, but because it was good mac & cheese).

$88 dollars later (for 2 ppl without alcohol), we left full and completely unsatisfied.

I would go somewhere else..... (especially for the price)

A few of my favorite foodie YouTubers have raved about this place, and it's one of the most well-known and best-rated buffet in Las Vegas. I came with my family on Thursday night and it was $54.99 per person. 

We came at 9:35, and they stop seating people at 9:45, so we were definitely cutting it close. The people at the front desk, the host/hostesses, the servers... everybody were extremely accommodating and patient albeit the fact that we came in hella late and my group was pretty rowdy. 

ENVIRONMENT: This place is beautiful, surrounded by mirrors and glass. The color palette filled with hues of turquoise and beige. The different stations strategically placed throughout. Honestly, I was just in awe with how appealing everything was. 

FOOD: They stopped replacing the food at 10, and start removing the food at 10:30, while dessert is removed at 10:40. There were some exceptionally delicious foods such as the sushi: the tuna cubes in ponzu sauce and the salmon poke were my favorite of the entire buffet. 
-The different stations include: American, Seafood, Mexican, Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, and of course, dessert. 
-Their soup selection was mediocre. Only three choices, and none of them really appealed to me.
Like one of the previous reviews stated, some of their food was absolutely delicious and then some of the other food was just average. Their crab legs were extremely salty, almost to the point where they were inedible (which is the reason for the loss of one star.) They were soaking in saltwater bath which explains the saltiness and I feel as though they should have been rinsed off in order to remove the excess salt. On the upside though the crab legs were cut in half so that you wouldn't have to crack them open yourself which saves you from the mess and the smelly hands. 
-Their roasted duck had wonderful flavor, the skin outside was crispy and indulgent. It reminded me of this dish prepared by Curtis Stone's SHARE. 
-The made to order crepes were delicious. I had them made with chocolate and raspberry sauce on the inside and the topped with powdered sugar. wonderful! They were spongy and I wish I wasn't too full so I could get another one with different toppings. 
-The chocolate lava cake was very chocolately and too rich for my taste, but if you're are a true chocolate glutton, this may be the dessert for you. 
-The raspberry beignet was also disappointing as you could barely taste the raspberry and the inside was too doughy. 
Another downside is the fact that I couldn't try everything so there may have been even more impeccable foods that I sadly missed. 

SERVICE: Our server's name was Jeffrey and he was excellent! He had a wonderful energy, and cracked jokes. When he heard that one of us forgot to grab a sauce for the steak, or a dressing for a salad, or the butter for the crab, he was wonderful and went out of his way to grab it for us so we wouldn't have to stand back up. 

I think this place may be worth it if you come with an empty stomach. I also think that everybody should experience this place once, but I feel as though this place is a little too hyped up. Don't get me wrong, I really enjoyed my experience.

I'd come back but maybe for brunch instead and with an emptier stomach.

Great food and great selections. The reason for four stars and not five is because I couldn't move and wasted half a day in Vegas recovering after I eat a lot . Big money$$$ but worth every penny without any question the best. My entire stay in Vegas was awesome!

We gave this place two stars but they think they are a five star buffet apparently. First, it took us 20 minutes of standing in line on a Monday night. No biggie though as we were expecting the place to be amazing. 

When it came time to pay, before being seated, there was a hassle, which seemed to require an act of congress to resolve. They check photo id's along with debit cards for every transaction. I totally understand they want to be safe so it's all good, my wife presented her ID. 

Problem was, my wife's name on ID didn't match her debit card name due to us just getting married. The name was so close most would let it slide, but not here. Again, no problem as we are being understanding. My wife pulls marriage certificate out of her purse on the spot just to reassure them she is the same person on the debit card. The employee ringing us up wouldn't even look at it! She called over a manager for this? Wow! Ok! Manager comes over and asks for my ID also. I feel like we were being interrogated to give them about $125 worth of business! Finally, after about 10 minutes we were cleared of all suspicion and allowed to pay.

Again, we don't complain about the issue paying and let it go. We get to our table and notice it was a super small table cramped between many other tables at one of those combo table/booths. We knew that wouldn't work for us since not much would have fit on that table, and with my disabilities from the military. We ended up going to another table no big deal.

At the buffet line there are of course many foods to choose from which is expected of a buffet, but many dishes you don't really know what they are. There are signs above the dish (well that's their plan anyways), but some signs are missing while some are in the wrong spot which can get confusing. You naturally ask the person on the other side what the dish is... But most either don't speak English to tell you, or they can't hear you which requires you to yell. Who wants to deal with eating their dinner with family or friends and hearing people yelling to talk at the buffet line next to you? We still don't complain at this point and let it go.

At one point, my wife and I felt like we were bothering a lady working behind the hamburger slider counter just for asking a question about the type of cheese used.
