I started in the seafood area, we cocktail shrimp, oysters, clams, oyster shooters, then the fish- halibut and salmon grilled, chowder, crab cakes (YUM!). Asian area: dim sum, hot & sour soup, miso soup, duck, bbq pork, sesame ball, potstickers, stir fried veggies, fried rice, chow mein, orange chicken, korean bbq, grilled chicken, sushi and more...Italian area have many different types of pasta: lasagna, spaghetti,  variety of pizza, bread and cheese area, cold meat area, salads, and of course a Mexican area with tortillas, carnitas, homemade salsa, beans, and more. Carving station have lots of different types of meats: sausages, beef, ribs, turkey. I really like the hot link. Also the dessert station was awesome. They have a variety of cookies, cupcakes, cakes, pies, cheesecake, ice cream/gelato and fruit. 
After all the food we stuff into our stomach, we had cups of coffee. The coffee was flavorful, it wasn't like diluted water. Everything was great and so delicious. I totally would recommend this place to everyone and I will definitely be back the next time I'm in Vegas, especially for dinner to try the other seafood they will have.

Went to the buffet with a group of 4, and it was delicious like the last time I went (7 months ago)! They had the exact selection as last time, which I was perfectly okay with. However, my only complaint is the waiter was slow in refilling our drinks. Compared to last time, the waitress was quick and kept the drinks flowing. This time, we found ourselves waiting impatiently for the drinks to be filled.

"I am not a player I just crush a lot" - Big Pun

Are there any more crabs in the ocean?   Wifey and I crushed 2 plates of king crab legs, 2 plates of stone crab, 1 plate of shrimp cocktail.   Just plain awesomeness!   The fresh juice station was a nice touch.   They had a made to order asian noodle station (pho,ramen,etc), carved meat (brisket, prime rib, etc...) but i didnt try much except the crab and shrimp cause i didnt want to fill up on the cheap stuff.   

There was a long line but i would recommend coming for lunch cause you wont eat dinner later

My cousin and aunt came in from NYC last Saturday.  We had been planning the trip for six months and had prepaid for helicopter rides, show tickets, the whole nine yards.  I recommended Caesar's Buffet because I have heard so many good things about it.  It is been the worst experience of the week!  We were gravely disappointed!  I had been told there were lobster tails there, but upon arrival I saw a sign in the case that said $62 for a whole lobster - nothing about a lobster tail.  We had to wait AN HOUR AND A HALF for shrimp!!!!  We kept going up and the man said they were waiting for it to come from the warehouse!  Did they not know they were serving dinner that day????  Several of the dishes looked like they had been left over from lunch - and some were not very tasty.  There were a few items we liked, but were very dissatisfied over the lobster and shrimp.  By the time the shrimp arrived we were ready to leave.  That was ridiculous.  But what was even more ridiculous was the fact that we had such difficulty getting someone to give us a drink and refill ...that my cousin had to actually get up and get the pitcher to refill our own iced tea!!!!!!!  I have never been so embarrassed in my life to have recommended a pricey buffet and have all of this happen!

Number one rated Buffet in Vegas and for good reason. The food is excellent all around and the selection is amazing. The only downside is we had to wait 1 1/2 hours to get through the line to eat. Other than that, make sure to save room for desert because it is too easy to get full on all the delicious entres they have! Oh and make sure to go around the corner, there is sushi that I didn't find until too late.

They would have received 5 stars if the crab legs weren't lacking in flavor. They tasted bland and some tasted only like water. Disappointing considering you can see them the entire time you are in line.

I bought the VIP breakfast with unlimited mimosas option for two from Groupon.com for $65 to the Bacchanal Buffet. Actually, since 3+ people bought this Groupon with my link, I only paid $54! The breakfast fine print stipulated that you had to arrive before 10:30AM I believe, and we strolled in exactly around that time. The VIP pass to skip the GA line came in handy (it looked like an awfully long wait for them). 

Arriving just in the nick of time actually worked out fabulously. My husband and I got to try out Bacchanal's breakfast AND lunch options! We agreed beforehand I would be the DD, so he was free to pound down the mimosas. I was afraid staff would hold back on refilling mimosas, but they kept our glasses flowing. Mimosas for days, yo!

Service overall was awesome. Plates were cleared and refills were constantly given. Staff was friendly too!  

BUFFET HIGHLIGHTS: I really enjoyed the hash browns and eggs for breakfast. For lunch, I liked the wild mushroom pizza, wonderfully cheesy mac 'n cheese and broccoli, and the caprese salad. For dessert, I liked these fancy, rich, chocolate pieces decorated with slivers of nuts and pearlescent balls. 

I sampled just about every section in the Bacchanal Buffet but was disappointed that the buffet wasn't very vegetarian friendly. Especially in the Hispanic and Asian ethnic food sections, vegetarian choices were severely lacking. 

Worth a Return Visit?
Bacchanal is a nice buffet, but I still prefer the buffet at the Wynn because it's more vegetarian friendly. It's a 50/50 chance that I'll come back!

YELP 100 CHALLENGE 2015: #41

This is hands down the best buffet in Las Vegas right now and blows previous favourites at the Wynn, the Bellagio, and Paris out of the water.

Is the food any better than these other buffets? Nope, not really. Nor is it even bigger than any of the buffets offered anywhere else. However, what makes the Caesars buffet THE buffet to end all buffets (in my mind, at least) is the crazy amount of selection and variety of food that's available.  It is the only buffet in Vegas that has an Asian food section serving up ramen, pho, hot and sour soup, wonton soup, miso soup, BBQ pork, roast pork, roast duck, AND pork soup dumplings (xiao long baos), to accompany a wide selection of dim sum and sushi edibles. Its seafood section not only has the ubiquitous crab legs (which you can ask to have steamed) but also seafood soups, oysters, mussels, and ceviches. And instead of a simple carving station, this buffet has a full-on meat station full of BBQ meats and roasts.

Oh, and did I mention that the (gigantic) dessert station also has giant mochi ice cream balls in flavours like sesame, vanilla, green tea, chocolate and mango (limit of 2 per person)? And (not related to dessert), that they serve fried chicken and waffle fries in a cute little frying basket? Amazing.

Yes, there is a wait. I wish I could tell you a strategy to beat the line. Your best bet would be to come right when it opens, but even then, expect to wait a good 40 minutes at least. My only tip, if you're coming in a group larger than 4, would be to split your group up as the line for smaller tables seems to move faster. 

Also, the air conditioning in the buffet is unreasonably cold, to the point of distraction. My guess is that it's to encourage people not to linger and loll around in a beached whale comatose state after eating so that they can funnel more people in and out.

I saw all the reviews and the rating and I figured I'd give it a try. Came in sunday after the big fight night for the bunch buffet.  While there was a large section I really focus on a few things and if they are done well. #1 crab legs, these weren't king crab legs and they were pre-split, #2 primerib was overcooked and bland. I tried the beef brisket but it was so salty I could only eat but a couple bites. I tried a few of the Asian dishes and they were ok. I did like the fresh juices. That was new to see that they offered carrot and cucumber juice. The mimosas were flowing. But sad to say the best part was the desserts.

Maybe it was because of all the people in for the fight or if it was because it was the brunch buffet but I didn't think it was better than others I have been to on the strip.

So I read other reviews and I thought the food would be more amazing compared to the other buffets on the strip.... Maybe I am just picky today but everything was salty and Luke warm... 

My husband and I arrived at 1;30 pm for lunch and there was no line and no need to check in via kiosk. We payed about 80$ for the two of us and if you want unlimited alcohol it's an extra 15$ per person. 

We started from one end to the other and I seriously think the only thing I enjoyed was the Chinese broccoli and the crab claw. The cheese selection had some goat cheese, Brie and other hard cheese but I didn't see any crackers. If you want some cured meat it's on the other side. The salad area was also well done.

The meat though.... Way too dry and overall too salty. They had a cool thing where they had real orange, watermelon, cucumber and carrot juice but be warned there is no added sugar so it was the real deal.

Dessert was ok but the gelato was totally not... The only thing I thought was good was the tiramisu cups and the pineapple.

Will I come back if I'm here in the strip... Uhh no.
Over priced and over hyped. Inferior to most buffets of its class. I'm definitely not going again. The service was the only good thing about this place.

My family flew in from out of town and wanted to eat at a buffet since vegas IS all about buffets. I decided to take my family over to bacchanal. I heard the lines can get really long so we arrived around 5pm. I am so glad that we did. Not only did I have a great time, my family enjoyed dining here. They raved about how tasty the lamb chops were, especially the charred ones. (My brother tells me that's the best way to eat it.) They also enjoyed the enormous selection of asian foods and the ramen soup station. We also enjoyed the large shrimp cocktail and king crab legs. ( Note : you have to pick out the king crab legs that's mixed with snow crab legs.) The salad bar was good, the food on the italian station had lots of flavor, especially the gnocchi dish. I went back for thirds. The desserts were ok, seems like your typical buffet dessets until we found out that they were serving Bubbies Mochi Ice Cream! What a way to end the night.

Lots and lots of options! Very appealing to the eye on presentation as well. Went on a Wednesday at 11am and didn't wait in line at all. I only wish they had snow crab legs but they have dungeness instead (just a personal preference) side note if you sign up for the players card you will receive 10% off the buffet , every bit helps!

I had a 50th Birthday celebration for my mother in Las Vegas and planned a dinner for a total of 20 people, and this buffet was the one I chose. I had emailed the guest services and they had forwarded me to the City Wide Restaurant Group Sales. I was given a quote for my event, and even ordered a specialty cake through the baker. 
I was quoted for each adult attendee a price of $68.99, and per child $26.99. They gave me a maximum of two hours for my event of 20 people (children and elderly included), and anything over that time frame would be an additional $500 per half hour. I also ordered a specialty cake (pictures below) that cost me a total of $340.00. I also already knew that I would be charged gratuity for my large party which I was more than comfortable with as this is done anywhere you go with a large group. The actual price for an adult dinner is $53.99... RIPPED OFF and I didn't even know it until I saw the prices when I arrived.
When I arrived to the location I checked in as advised, waited about ten minutes, and we were brought to our table. There was no line outside for regular check in which I was surprised about being that it was a Saturday night in Vegas. We were taken to our tables in the back of the restaurant and separated into two round tables. Had I known I was going to have to separate my party into two round tables, I would have never came here. They had plenty of long tables that they could have put together to have the entire party I was with sit together. There were also 4 other large tables in this area that were seated in our section. We were all seated and greeted by our one server and drink requests were taken.
 The first round of food has been completed and the plates on the tables have stacked up at this point, no waiter around refilling drinks and no place for anyone to get any more food without making the tables completely cluttered. I couldn't believe that they would stick ONE waiter for a large party like mine, let alone ONE waiter for the entire back area of SIX tables. It was frustrating that it was a mess, that my guests were unable to get refills when they were empty and I felt bad for the waiter mostly. Sitting around waiting for the tables to be cleaned and refills takes time out of my two hour window.
Half way through dinner my brother decides to take my niece to the dessert section to check out all that they had and let me just begin by saying WOW. The cake I ordered was a SURPRISE, the staff knew this, the lady at the group sales knew this, all my guests knew this. My brother returns to ask me if I had seen the cake I ordered...my response was no. He told me that the cake is sitting out at the dessert section in plain view, and is GREEN!!!! I went over to check the cake out and indeed it was green and in plain view. Low and behold my mother walks up and sees the cake that was supposed to be a surprise. A complete disaster. I spoke with the Manager and told him I would not be paying for this cake as it is not what we agreed on. I spent 45 min dealing with this cake situation, as my guests are sitting and waiting for the cake to be brought out all in the 2 hour time frame we are allowed. The surprise was ruined, the cake was ruined, and the entire event at this point went to crap. When the cake finally came out, we were given a knife and the cake. We asked for plates and they gave us HOT plates. I then proceeded to the dessert section to gather cold plates myself, and the manager was upset that I had to do this myself. We cut our own cake and served our own cake as there was no assistance.
Long story short, I was over charged per person $15 for an hour prior to the event that I was not told about, yet I could not stay an extra 30 min without being charged to accommodate the small children and elderly people in my party. My guests and I wasted 45 min of our time waiting on a cake that was a complete disaster. They decided to reimburse me for the cake and throw in 2 buffet passes for my next visit. Do they really think that I will ever return to this buffet, that my guests who spent hundreds of dollars to fly out and spend the weekend in Vegas will return to their buffet? This is a large company that should pride themselves on the service they provide, on the bakery they have and on the way they handle a situation that is brought to their attention.
When I emailed regarding the overcharge, she simply stated that's what you pay when we have to hold your table prior to your arrival. When I asked her other questions she disregarded them and didn't answer. When I was finally able to get in touch with her manager, her response was "What do you feel is fair"? I decided to stop talking to this inconsiderate people, and write a review on Yelp to allow others to make an informed decision on their next party they decide to throw.

It is the best Vegas buffet I've tried. Alot of variety. Very clean and well organized. Our sever was very nice. For tourists this is perfect because you can try Chinese, Mexican, meat, Japanese, Italian, seafood, etc. Since I'm from a city that has excellent ethnic food and other food. I rather go somewhere that specialize on one type.  So much food!!! Not a great deal for me since I could not take full advantage and get my $53 worth.

Not only is this truly the best buffet in Las Vegas, but they continually improve and innovate to keep them at the top of the highly competitive buffet industry in Las Vegas. 

I've come often to this buffet, and this buffet is notorious for their long lines and ridiculous wait times...and people do it! Thankfully, I have a line pass that allows me to bypass the stressful, Disney-esque line for the general public.

On our most recent visit, I came with a friend who has a severe egg allergy. As soon as our waitress was informed, she got one of the managers to come over. The manager let us know he will get a chef to come over and assist immediately. In mere minutes, Chef Ryan appeared. Chef Ryan offered two options: 1) he can take my friend through the endless buffet options and steer her away from anything with eggs, or 2) make her something from scratch. My friend chose option 2, and Chef Ryan did not disappoint!

Chef Ryan made a gigantic bone-in rib eye steak fit for at least two people! Talk about generous! I realize this is an expensive buffet, but that rib eye was certainly worth more than the buffet!

Also, my biggest complaint with Bacchanal has always been their less than impressive desserts. Well, their new pastry chef, Emma (I think that's her name), is absolutely incredible! The desserts have transformed from an afterthought to highlight! The salted caramel cupcake is so good! I usually take several desserts and just take bites...this time, I ate all of it!

Lastly, I have to really recognize GM Steven Kuo and his team. The management team really works to keep the image of the buffet in top form at all times...even during peak time! Through all of that chaos, they still take the time to talk to the customers to make sure they are having a wonderful experience. Truly impressive operations, amazing and inventive food, and world-class service! Can't ask for anything more!

The alaskan king crab i got was literally frozen. It felt like i was eating crushed ice. The line to get in was disorganized and long. The lines within the buffet itself were also long. The prime rib was too rare. The lamb was cold. The whole restaurant was freezing. Took forever to get somebody to get me something to drink. The oysters had to be pried out with a fork instead of just slurped down. The tables and chairs look like ugly furniture from criagslist i would never buy. Ive been to rio, aria, wynn etc and this was my worst experience. Two stars because im in a good mood after 18oz of Fat Tuesdays.

They say it the best buffet for a reason (and they are right!!!!). They have everything from ramen to street tacos to your meats and sea food. It pricy and there a bit of a wait if yr not platinum member and up. but well worth the wait.  The selection was truly amazing will defiantly go again.

Every thing was great and probably the best buffet we ate at in vegas...Service was awesome, food was top notch and the atmosphere was nice as well....Price was as little steep but you get what you pay for i guess.

BOGO Printable coupon from LasVegasFoodReviews.con made this 65  dollar buffet affordable and probably the best value in the strip  king crab legs, lobster, tomahawk ribeye, lamb, so much great food I can not list it all  if youbare in Vegas with a wife or friend take them here  heck even a stranger with the BOGO is worth bringing

you will enjoy this

Best buffet we had ever been to. The buffet line is huge and split up by regional genre. There were excellent options all the way down and I found myself having to run the line 4-5 times to get everything I wanted to try. Food was all excellent. My only complaint about this restaurant was the selection can be somewhat overwhelming. It's a must if you are into buffets and eating way too much food in one sitting.

Went around 4pm and did not have to wait long to be seated which was a plus. It is such a beautiful place. When you first walk in you see the desserts and crab legs. While I am not a fan of seafood, it did look good. The I fixed my first two plates, I didn't even know that there was a whole other section that wraps around. It seemed to go forever. The variety was good and the tastes were satisfying. We paid 125 for two adults and a child but it was good. They say you don't leave when you are full or miserable, you leave when you hate yourself. While I didn't hate myself, It was close to being miserable.

Our experience was delightful. The food is fine. The service was provided by Aurelio Hilario our waiter who helped us with cocktails for an hour or more after dinner as we enjoyed ourselves chatting and drinking. Aurelio helped us create a cocktail I invented at the table. This kind of service makes for a great experience.

Got there 10:20am on Monday morning for breakfast, there is no line. $28.99/person, but you get $1 off if you have rewards card. Our party has 6 people, they don't allow you to sit until everyone is there. By the time we sit down, it's already 11:15 which is lunch time. They didn't charge us extra though. lunch is more expensive. The food was great, fresh, well prepared, we even saw oyster for about 20 minutes, not sure if they put there by mistake. I like ginseng chicken soup, grill duck, dim sum, Mexican food, cocktail shrimp, dessert. Most of them are very good. But you can only eat there for 2 and half hours. We didn't notice that, until our waiter remind us.
So worth the money.  We ate for 3 hours it was so good and so many option's it was absolutely delicious no matter what you had and the service was superior.

I paid $175 for 2 adults and 1 child during Thanksgiving, and it was just a mediocre meal for us. The seafood quality sucks: crab legs are too salty and not fresh, Dungeness crab has soft and low quality meat, sushi so mediocre. Worst rack of lamb I have ever had. Prime rib is tough and only comes in rare. Pho and desserts were the only good selections in this highly rated buffet. Will never eat a buffet again after this.

My husband and I used to go here every Vegas Trip we took. Years ago it wasn't as expensive and they had amazing food. We went back a few months ago and it was super expensive and the quality of the food went down dramatically. They stopped offering rack of lamb and instead lamb shanks that weren't cooked well. They stopped offering the fun Mexican drinks in the little bottles. Sure they have oysters and crab legs but I've been to other buffets that offer that and aren't as expensive. The desserts are not as impressive as they used to be. Bachannal Buffet has lost its appeal. Time to find a new Vegas buffet.
I love this place!! The food was amazing! The staff members were so nice and friendly. I'd go back to Las Vegas just to go eat at Bacchanal.
Simply the Best Buffet in Vegas! Pricey. It high quality food. It is an experience. It is a Must Do every time I am in Vegas!

This place is where I had the best meal of my life. What else is there to say?

It's quite pricy, but completely worth every single penny. I'm still having dreams of that wild mushroom and goat cheese pizza. They have food for those with the expensive tastes, and food for those of simpler kinds. They have food for the homesick Asians and the food for the trendy street food lovers. 

The seafood was great. The entrees were great. The desserts were beyond great. I cried every time I returned back to my table. They literally have EVERYTHING here, from Filipino Kare Kare to Chicken and Waffle to Macarons. 

Although my doctor would probably say otherwise, I would recommend going here for your one major meal for the day. I still felt full the night after. The price was damn expensive. Get your money's worth. 

This buffet is the best buffet in the buffet capital of the world. It doesn't get any better than this. This ruined every other eating experience for me, because now I would always subconsciously compare it to this beauty. I left my heart here and I for sure will come back, but next time, with my stretchy pants.
Best buffet I've been too. Definitely worth paying for. It's like visiting the world of food in one sitting. I wish I could've ate everything they served but it was too much to try.
This place was really nice!!..  the customer service was great!! The choices were amazing!! I will be back for sure

Overrated at best!!! We had better buffet places for half the price. Flavors are so-so and the place is so packed up you can't get to the foods in a timely manner. Very expensive and not worth the money. Oh by the way, the waiting time is 30-45 minutes in order to be seated.

Obviously, the food quality and variety is higher than the other A buffets in Las Vegas (Wynn for example), but really not by much. Not 40% better. The 3* is really value-wise.
I was advertised a buffet that would have out of the ordinary items, such as King Crabs, Rib Eye steak, ... you name it, we got it.

I got there... it was all snow crab and prime rib, which I can easily get at a 15$ buffet off the strip. And there was a little bit of king crab, mixed in at a ratio of 1:20 with snow crab. So much for the hype. The meat was good, but nothing I've never had before at Wynn, in fact last time I was at Wynn, we had Tomahawk steaks...
The oysters were ok, fresh enough to be edible and not get us sick. The sushi was extremely dissappointing, the slices of fish were paper thin, the rice was badly seasoned. The udon was a waste of stomach space.

The baby back ribs were barely cooked, not enough smoke, unacceptable tough texture.
The beef brisket was well seasoned, but huge layer of fat, rather than well marbled.
Best item was the lamb chops which were tasty and large. 

The blue cheese was good but it was all crumbled. The parmagiano was also good but crumbled. The Manchego was the only cheese that stood out as integral and good.

The desserts were good on the other hand. There was a lot of options, crepes, creme brulee, macarons (which didnt really taste like almond paste), chocolate-covered fruits.

I would seriously recommend not waiting in line for 3 hours and just get the 30% off and go to Wynn.

Huge variety of food. The dessert and seafood lines were probably my favorite. If I ate here for a week, I probably still wouldn't get to sample all of the food options available. The only downside is standing in the long lines for food because everyone is at the seafood line, but it's still worth it. The service was also very quick at picking up your plates--whenever I got up, my old empty plate would be gone. If you're ever in Vegas, definitely stop here at one point in your trip!

I got food poisoning the following day (~6 hours after the meal) and narrowed down the cause to the chicken satay and spicy peanut sauce. 

I appreciated the large selection of food, even though I tried most of the asian section only. I don't think I ate enough to warrant the $60 dinner charge though.

So it's Vegas and we need to check out a buffet. Read great reviews and gave it a shot. Really really good choice. 
It IS. long wait but not nearly as long as originally told when we checked in. Great text feature let's you know when to come back to the line. 
And yawza, the food!!!!!
So many very well prepared items to choose from. We did purchase the additional alcohol option and for sure drank more than $15 worth each. 
Try to save room for dessert because there are some amazing ones.

Do you love seafood? 
Large prawns, crab legs, lobster rolls, oysters, clams, mussels (need I go on?)

Do you love variety?
American, Japanese, Mexican, French, Italian, Mediterranean, Chinese (need I go on?)

Do you love fresh, authentic, original, gourmet (need I go on?)

Do you love dessert?
Creme brûlée, macaroons, flavored fudge, gelato a such as beer orange & mango habanero, need I go on?)

Ate like a roman goddess here and I believe I entered food heaven for all eternity.

Best buffet in Las Vegas. The Wicked Spoon is a very close runner up. 

Downside is $52 price for adults and $25 for kids, but when in roam, you must eat here. 

Trust me. I. Eat. A lot.

The only Buffet worthy of 5 stars is the "Seafood Buffet" at Deer Valley in  Park City.  Bacchanal makes a solid effort but falls just a bit short when it comes to the high end shellfish.  The real star of any so called high end buffet.  Staff is a tad arrogant ... Maybe it's the hoards of mid-westerners in the "New Balance" running shoes.... Lot a sweat pants in the house as well.... Apparently you need to come prepared.
As you enter the 25,000 square foot feed lot you see the crux of all the excitement... The Crab Leg station.... 9 deep and 6 wide it's truly a spectacle of gluttony!  I'm thinking of a new reality tv show..... CRAB LEG WARS! VEGAS!!!! It's a literal frenzy ... All for an average snow crab leg that yields a thin flavorless reward .... Oyster Shooter are in tomato juice... Tip grab some extra cocktail sauce and reconstitute your own version (ala Brophy's).
Without droning on about this and that I'd say just go and experience it once it may be Heaven or it may be Hell.... You decide!?!?!?

Secret super tip for normal people... Make it your first and only meal of the day at 2:30 pm.... Line will be shorter and price skyrockets at 3:00 pm.  They also won't rush you when you get inside.... We stayed for 3 hours!!!!!
And ask for Jo's station she's amazing and oh so pleasant!

The food is incredible, the atmosphere is upscale and there is something for everyone here. But this review is meant to recognize the remarkable Michael Putnam, the Executive Chef who made sure our Thanksgiving dinner was truly wonderful. We will be recommending it to friends for sure!
Fantastic service!! Mike Lee was very nice and ensured we had a good time and met all our needs. Food was superb!

Food was mostly good.
I was surprised Ramen was delicious!
I got here around 9:45am and they changed most of food in 30min. It was fun to see.
Desert section was variety and nice.
I recommend this place. Breakfast was about 28$ for 1 person.

This buffet is pretty damn good. Came here to hit the lunch into dinner time and got there just before the crab legs rolled out for the dinner menu. The selection of food is huge and I didn't even know there was a back part to the buffet until I saw many people carrying noddles and Asian food around.

I must say this place has very fresh crab legs all split already making life easy to eat them. The oysters a huge but did have a bit of sand in them but that's okay. The meat selection is huge as well as if you go and see the pork belly with lentils get it. It is so delicious and rich in flavor. 

If you live in a city which has Chinatown's don't go to the Asian section of their buffet though unless you are going for their chicken ginseng soup. Everything else is very oily and overly salted with a very strange taste to the mouth. I would say stick to the outside western dishes over going for the Chinese and Japanese dishes. 

The dessert: holy. I was so excited to stuff my stomach with dessert that I got seven different things to try. They have such a large array of desserts that I didn't even know where to stop and end. While most were too sweet for myself, they were still yummy and I would go for them again. They are all beautifully decorated and looks too nice to eat but there is a variety of different options of desserts to try.

4 stars is a little bit generous. It really deserves between 3 and 4 stars. Came at around 11 am. Even 2 hours later there are still too many breakfast items being served. There are many different choices which warrant 4-star rating, but the food quality is just slightly above average. Sushi options are limited and very average. Asian items are not anything outstanding. Crab legs are definitely not king crabs, no more special than other buffets in Vegas. It is worthwhile to try it once, but not something I would look forward to in the future.

I ate at Bacchanal a little over two years ago (~02/2013) and remember having a good experience. I was excited to dine there again last night, but the food left much to be desired. Nothing was truly exemplary. None of the dishes I had were memorable. The variety is impressive, but at what cost? I generally don't eat at buffets, but have made exceptions in Vegas. Not anymore. I'm done with buffets in Vegas or elsewhere. I rather forgo the variety for a meal that is properly executed and prepared to order.

Service has gone down hill here from the last time I came. When we arrived we were told we could wait in line for 25 mins or pay an extra $25 per person (total $80+). We also paid for the all you can drink option. When we got to the table we were told that someone would come get our drink order.  10 mins passed, someone came took our drink order. 15 mins more passed we got our first drinks for just our water and soda. Our beers still didn't make it to it to the table. 

After bugging a few more people we finally got our first batch of beers.  After complaining about it again we started getting a flow of  drinks. When they started bringing our drinks to us they set a tray filled with mixed drinks & beer behind us for 15 mins which means another table missed out on their drinks too. 

The food overall was meh. We had some items that tasted great, most however was over cooked or just meh for the amount of money. The deserts however were all good.  Honestly for the money there are a lot better restaurants in Vegas that have much better food for the money.

Probably my favorite buffet in Vegas so far. Sunday brunch (FREE MIMOSAS UNTIL 3PM) was about $42/person. There was a ridiculous amount of food EVERYWHERE. Drinks are included (sodas, tea, coffee, but cappuccinos are additional)

IMPORTANT: It is NOT possible to try everything. 
Types of cuisines they had:
- Chinese (stir fry dishes, dim sum)
- Japanese - (sushi, soups)
- Italian (pastas, artisan cheeses, pizza, make-your-own pasta station)
- American (salad bar, meat station with ribs, chicken sausage, prime rib, honey ham, etc, breakfast foods)
They also had a seafood station with tons of shrimp, mussels, and crab legs. The crab legs are on ice, but you can ask them to dunk them in hot water to make it hot. 

Dessert was also pretty insane. 

I know I'm probably missing a good chunk of more things they had, but you will not be limited on options when you come here. 

A bit pricey, and a bit of a wait to get seated, but if you have all the time in the world and wouldn't spend a little more money coming for a bit better quality and taste, this is the place to be! A few things were hit or miss, but for the most part, everything tasted really good and fresh. 

We even saw a bride and groom in her wedding dress and his suit in the line for sushi!

Hands down, best buffet in Las Vegas as of 5/14. The wait in line took us about 30min on a Wednesday, which wasn't bad. The total bill was around $130 including tip for 2 people, kinda steep but well worth it. When we were seated, the servers were on point with the drinks and plate clean up. 

The food was great, everything was well prepared and tasteful. The seafood selection was vast as well as the other meats. The cooking crew was very friendly and helpful. The deserts were very good and they had a lot to choose from.

The only things that bothered us was the amount of people blocking the buffet line, plus the occasional person not going with the flow. That's almost expected due to the amount of foreigners that were there. I also felt under dressed wearing jeans and a polo.

What isn't there to love about a classy buffet in Vegas with amazing food? We came here for dinner on a week day night during the summer, so we had to wait about 45 minutes to get in, but the food was 1000% worth it. Great selections in all of the different sections, but I have to say that the best was definitely the dessert section. As someone who has a pretty big sweet tooth, I was basically drooling all over the dessert area. Everything from macarons to mini cakes to gelato - everything you can hope for and dream of was there (definitely got way more than I should have). This has to be the best buffet in Vegas, and you should definitely go if you're in the area.

I don't know if it was because I expected a lot, but I was pretty disappointed with the buffet. They had a lot of variety of foods but each dish itself was average. I'm thinking maybe it was the time of day I went but I don't think I would pay for dinner price. They had all sorts of dishes but individually, they weren't good. 
I went for lunch and paid about 41$

We had dinner here on July 5th ("holiday dinner" i guess to justify the higher price of $75/person). We got in at 9.40pm and at 10pm they not only stopped serving but also started taking the food back to the kitchen and cleaning. Pretty disappointing considering the money you pay.
Other than that the seafood was great, i personally wished they had more fish choices (there was only salmon) but liked the oysters, crab legs and the mussels. I am not much into the Asian food but the Ramen looked great and they had a large variety of dumplings which looked great too.
Italian secton looked average (1 chooce of piza, 1 of pasta); the cheese and cured meat were gone and there were some interesting meats which infortunately by the team we hot seated and had the seafood appetizers were all gone (taken back to the kitchen).
I don't think there was much of variety of food but what they had was really tasty which to me is more important.

Let me start by saying we are not big buffet fans, but on several visits to Vegas we have gone to buffets. So...

Check-in- WFT would I check in early, go gamble for 30 mins and then get a call to come to the front of the line only to spend another 30 mins waiting for a seat???

Service- yep it is a buffet., so no service right?? But no plates ?? Seriously??

Food- actually the food was decent, good selection and good quality.

Cost- stupid, as a total rewards platinum member I still have to pay $30 upgrade? What??? This after $99 credit? Give me a break.

Huge fan of Caesars, but not this place.

Very disappointed with this buffet... How can u charge $55+tax, yet let the same pieces of food sit on the counter for the entire 2 hours??? Beyond unacceptable when ur "sushi" is crusted and hardened... That's straight disgusting and inedible... Oysters sat out for the whole 2 hours, crab legs were frozen to the point where ice was present in the crab legs... One of the most expensive buffets and not worth an 1/8 of what u charge... Even if I came at an off hour, that doesn't give u the right to serve me leftovers at the rate I paid... I waited patiently for them to change some of the food and that never happened... Never coming here again...

Our waiter seems to be refusing to serve us. Ive had to ask for water 3 times before he finally brought some over.. never gave us a straw.. had to wait 3 more trips before we got a straw. Worst service ever. Woukd have been better served at a cheap buffet. Save your 100 bucks!

Horrible horrible experience. For the amount they charge for the buffet they should have a better system to seat people. After having a 1:30 pm time slot assigned we were seated at 3:30.

Not recommended at all! Better off paying the money and going to multiple other high end restaurant options on the strip.

I wish I could give them zero stars for the management.
AMAZING!! So many options ! Worth the $$$ but go in with an all day empty stomach and ready for a nap Afterwards!
Everything else was delicious - enjoyed everything I ate and our server was solicitous. But I was disappointed that I had to go through 3 chocolate lava cakes and I did not find any lava.

My boyfriend, my parents and I went to the Bacchanal for Champagne Brunch this past Saturday and it was almost as good as when we went for Christmas two years ago. We arrived around 10:00 am and there was no wait and I'm actually glad we got there early because when we left around 11:30 there was a huge line and they were directing people to the kiosks where you sign up and come back at a later time (kind of like fast passes at Disney). The reason that I say "almost as good" is because the eggs benedict that I got was cold :(. However, I give them five stars for their  crab legs! I didn't know that you could ask them to steam them - so much better than ice cold, in my opinion. And they were delicious!! I like my crab legs with just lemon, none of that butter stuff - but if you want it, it's there. The prime rib was on point and the dim sum was good as well. I also really enjoyed their made to order crepes at the dessert station. I get mine with just nutella but they have all of the fruit toppings also. Our server Maria was awesome and constantly kept our mimosa glasses full. If you go, ask to be in her section - she will definitely take care of you. As total rewards members we paid $43.99 per person which is definitely pricey but we really enjoyed it.

We enjoyed this place.  Just be ready to stand in lines.  We went on a Monday at 2:45 and was seared at 3:30.   We stood in line for the seafood. Which had a good variety of items. ( No lobster). Snowcrab, shrimp, mussels, chopinno, and salmon other items. There is a great carving station, Japanese station. desserts station with fresh crepes, the key lime.e tart was wonderful yum. The food was very fresh and I would go again

Very good buffet. 
Pros: dim sum and Kobe burgers
Cons: limited selection and price (Paid holiday pricing $50)
Last straw...creme brûlée just wasn't what I expected from a place that supposedly is the best buffet. I will definitely go again. Oh and the sweet potatoes fries were really good too.

Be prepared to wait. I mean really WAIT to be seated unless you go after 8pm. Or you pay $25/person to cut through all of that.  For me, it took about nearly 2 hours.  I guess the wait times are pretty typical for a Vegas buffet. This place can be packed, but it's definitely worth it if you come hungry -- which you should considering the price and obviously a buffet.

They have a vast amount of offerings and are sectioned based on types of food such as seafood, Chinese, Mexican, Italian and all sorts of meats. What really stood this place out from the rest are their selection of meats. From ribeye, tri-tip steak, beef wagu, pork belly, etc...I enjoyed them. For the most part, their offerings are decent. I enjoyed their gelato, but was not a fan of the rest of their desserts. That's ok though. 

If you have the time and money, I say at least check this one out. I don't think you can go wrong with this buffet.

Cashier named MARTA was extremely rude with the interaction we had with her. Tried to explain to her that we were waiting in line for 45 mins, after being told to do so by the gentleman who also worked at the buffet, she ignored and cut me off. I attempted again and she says "you'll have to wait in line again." It would be understandable if she acknowledged that if was a mistake by another employee but ignored everything. Customer service doesn't work that way. If you are in a bad mood or has had a bad day you should be able to not allow it to show or should not work directly with customers. 

The food was great so this one star is strictly towards Marta's customer service and the the person(s) in charge of staffing that department.

I was disappointed. I'm a local and have been wanting to experience the Bacchanal since I first heard about it. I imagined a luxurious dining experience with the most amazing food choices and quality. What I found was a fairly standard buffet with some very questionable food items. The oysters tasted like they were from the muddiest bay and I was concerned for a bit they might have been bad. The sushi was far worse than I had had from local super markets. The sea bass had a rubbery texture and the sole barely tasted like fish. That all being said, offering stone crabs should have made up for the questionable quality but a handful of them tasted of ammonia. The balance of the food items (shrimp, calamari and sausages) were good but for $50+ per person, I expected more. I'm glad I went but I'm certain I would not choose another visit given the many other choices in town.

Great buffet. Incredible selection - seafood, sushi, smoked meats, Mexican, Chinese, gourmet pizza, comfort food. Everything is fresh and well prepared. Many of the items are put on small plates to avoid the typical buffet contamination problems. Oh, there's also an incredible dessert bar.

OM NOM NOM NOM NOM NOM! As all the Yelpers below have said, this place is pretty AMAZEBALLS.  While it is pricey, you definitely get your money's worth because every dish is YUM!  The ambiance here is pretty awesome as well.  We were in a group of 7 so we were able to sit at a large table that sort of looked like it was a gnarly tree stump (in a cool artsy way) and tall chairs that are comfortable and very contemporary looking.  It is a very modern look!  I loved it!

The buffet's food was really good and it is sectioned off in the following stations:

-Chinese (Dim Sum, Duck, etc.)
-Japanese (Small selection of sushi and soups)
-Italian (Pasta, etc.)
-Mexican (Made to order tacos, fresh salsas & Agua Frescas!)
-Meats (Prime Rib, HUGE BONE-IN RIBEYES, Lamb, etc.)
-American Style Side Dishes (Mac & Cheese, Fries, Potatoes, etc.)
-Seafood (Standard... Shrimp, Crab Legs, Oysters, Clams) 
-Dessert (Made to order crepes and other various goodies

I was really impressed by how fresh all the food was and how tasty things were!  The food services were very friendly and our waitress/busboy were very efficient in taking our plates... Even when we brought two plates of food to the table for each person... LOL. 

My only gripe is that I feel the organization of the buffet was really odd.  It was sort of difficult to grab Japanese then try to grab Italian (i.e. putting my pizza on top of my sushi???? Ughhh! 

Pros:
-AMAZING FOOD
-Great ambiance
-Good service

Cons:
-Food is not necessarily organized in the best manner

Tips:
-Alcohol is separate so be prepared to pay if you want a beer or Mimosa
-TRY THE HORCHATA! 
-Get one Ribeye for the table and share... THAT is how HUGE it is! 
-GET THE CREPE and get ice cream on top... You'll regret it if you don't!

I do love their ticket waiting system so we don't have to wait in line for hours. When we arrived at 4:30pm thinking the line will be shorter we later found out we have to take a ticket and return on the time it tells us to which was 6pm. Not thrilled about it but better than standing in line.
We dined at the Wynn and Bellagio buffet so we though this should be similar price and quality. $140 for 2 people!!! It almost made me want to walk away!
Food quality and selection is good but $70 a person is still a lot for a buffet. I will suggest you to come try it once but be prepared for the ticket shock. 
I know some people compare the price with a fine dinning restaurant and think it's a good price but I compare it with other Vegas buffet and think it's not worth the wait and the money.

Like most places in Vegas, this buffet is overrated. After reading the reviews here, my girlfriend and I were so excited to try what most people call the best buffet in Vegas. 

I recommend that you go to this buffet a little before 3 pm. This way the line is very short, you pay the lunch price rather than the dinner price, and you can eat dinner items because they will be serving it starting at 3 pm. 

The service sucked (see below). The food was just okay. Not crappy, but not great if you are paying $50 a person. I'll go in order:

The salad ingredients were fresh, but that's not hard. Their "cheese" menu was severely lacking -- there were only 3 kinds of cheese, and they were all extra sharp. The soups were cold because most people want to make their money by focusing on the expensive meats, so the soups just sit there and hardly anyone eats them -- I love clam chowder, but theirs was cold and lumpy. I asked them if they could warm it up and they said it was a fresh batch. (It wasn't a fresh batch.)

The Asian ramen stand is good, and although I don't usually like tofu, theirs was really good. However, you can get a lot of good ramen from asian restaurants for a lot less money (and you should probably avoid ramen at buffets because it is so filling). 

My favorite item was the creamy salmon, but none of the sides were good, so eating just salmon was boring. The crab was a little too salty. The prime rib only comes in medium rare -- disgusting. The "lobster" corn chowder barely had any lobster, and in any case was not very good.

I didn't try the taco station because I live in San Diego, home of the best tacos in the country. But people kept lining up for them, so maybe they are worth a try.

The dessert was lacking as well. The gelato section looks interesting, but there is a line for it, and they only give you one little scoop per visit. I had to wait in line three times to try 3 flavors. They all tasted like frozen yogurt, and not the good kind. The cheesecake only came in sugar-free form. (What?)

All we wanted for drinks were hot tea, but they don't have tea pots. Instead, they use their coffee pots and just add water to them. So the tea just tastes like old coffee. We kept asking the server if they could wash them out and she said all she can do is add water. The tea was just horrible because it just tasted like bad coffee.

They make sure the most filling items are well stocked, so people get full faster at a lower cost to them. We've definitely been to better buffets that cost much less.

Excellent food, a really good buffet. 
Cost wise very reasonable and selection is excellent.

Our first time to Bacchanal Buffet and we were overwhelmed with the selection and choices.  Fresh! Hot food hot, cold food cold! Excellent prime rib! Lamb chops were to die for! We also very much enjoyed had tasting all the desserts! The dining room and service areas were very clean and the servers were very cordial and helpful! This is THE buffet to have when in Vegas!

This buffet was pretty good! There was a long line before lunch time, but the line seemed more tamed after lunch (around 2PM). After tax, total came out to close to $70 with tax and tip. Very modern and pretty buffet in Caesars. There are so many selections here and the foods looked great. I was very sad that I was not able to try most of the items that I wanted to; I was too focused on getting my money's worth via seafood. My friend was a diamond member so we were able to get seated before most groups, but honestly the line was not long in the regular line and we still had to wait another 15 minutes to get seated. 

The buffet is beautiful and well decorated. There are so many selections. In terms of seafood, they have cold crab legs, warm crab legs, ciopinno with crab/shrimp/mussels, shrimps, etc. I ate my heart out with crab legs (probably ate 2 crab) and was stuffed. I regretted as soon as I saw the other dishes and felt too full to try them. Other items I wanted to try were the taco and noodles bars. Also, the Chinese foods looked pretty appetizing. I am so upset that I did not try their meats, such as the prime rib, wagyu, etc. 

Besides the seafood, another highlight was the dessert section. Probably the best dessert I've tasted in a buffet. Everything I tried was so good, especially the Vietnamese coffee dessert; it tastes just like Viet coffee! Their ice cream (gelato, sorbet, etc) was so good and well flavored. 

Service was optimal. Our server was quick and professional; did not hesitate when we kept asking for drinks (coffee, soda, etc). For $70, you must train yourself to eat $70 worth... which means eating a decent breakfast to expand your stomach and then walk around many times around the strip to get incredibly hungry. Then eat after 1pm and stay until some of the dinner items come out. One downside is that the restroom was located outside the buffet, although very close to our table, I was paranoid they would not let us back in.

After 90 minutes wait on Saturday afternoon for this restaurant, I have to say I was pretty disappointed. They do have a pretty good selection, the food was just so so and  not as delicate for 45$ per person.

"Lady in the streets, freak at the buffet."  That's me.

I went caveman status at Bacchanal... all table manners out the door with no shame.  I highly suggest you don't make the same mistake I made by wearing all white.  Also, line up before you're even hungry, because there is a line for a line for a line, and by the time you sit down, you will be starving.  They do offer caviar service for $150 and up that allows you to be seated immediately, which I find to be a decent price.

Bacchanal is definitely really, really hyped up.  I always see the name listed as the #1 buffet in all of Vegas, and hear about it often from those who have dined here.  For 50-some dollars per person that includes AYCD wine and beer, it's really not bad, especially if you will eat your weight in crab like me.  Sure, pretty much every high-end buffet in Vegas has crab legs, but this one had stone crab claws, and I appreciated that the crab legs where sliced in half for easy access.  Avoid grabbing the legs that are newly served because they're kind of frozen.  I think the oysters and mussels are only served at dinner, because I noticed them putting them out as we were leaving.

I wish I took the time to line up in the meat line.  I'm too much of a seafood junkie and didn't pace myself well enough to save room for steak and such, but it looked great.  I had some soup, which was just alright.  The congee had no seasoning, while the hot & sour soup and ramen were over-seasoned.

I'm a little disappointed to not find a caviar station.  Maybe it only comes out during dinner, but I could have sworn that I read Bacchanal had one.  Overall, the food was good, but being so hyped up, I do not think that it met up to expectations 100%.  The sushi station at a buffet in my hometown is more lavish than theirs.  I do feel that it was worth it for me as I loaded up on quality crab and drank multiple glasses of champagne, but if you're like my boyfriend, the price may be questionable as he eats really bland food (i.e. mac 'n cheese, turkey, mashed potatoes, etc.).

Service was phenomenal.  I wish I had left a higher gratuity when paying before being seated, because I did not expect such attentiveness.  He was always topping off my champagne and two steps ahead of me whenever I needed anything.  Also, the restaurant itself is more beautiful than another other buffet I have visited, just make sure you're ready to make the trek from one end of the buffet to the other - the place is huge!

After reading several reviews of Caesars' new Bacchanal Buffet, I was excited to give it a try, but was tremendously disappointed. 

First, the service. Our wait in the "regular" line at 11:30 this morning was around 30 minutes. Normally, I'd have no problem with that, but when we did pay and were shown to our table, I noticed that only about 1/3 of the tables were full. Other reviewers have pointed this same phenomenon out, so I can only conclude that CP is trying to make their high-rollers feel more "special", or that they'd like people to pony up the extra $15 to jump the line, or that, if all tables were full, the chefs at the food stations would be unable to keep up. 

About that table: it was either too high, or my chair was too low. I still can't decide which, but either way, it was uncomfortable. My chair also straddled a carpet/ marble divide, with the back legs on marble and the front on carpet  not a big deal at a normal restaurant, but at a buffet, this wasn't ideal. 

I would, in fact, like to meet the idiot that designed the room. First, it's a clear rip-off of the design at Aria's buffet. (I did enjoy the light fixtures on the pillars outside the buffet). Second, the layout was confusing and somewhat claustrophobic, with the Asian area tucked into an odd dead-end. The stations where food was being prepared to order forced the lines of people waiting to block other areas. And the sneeze-guards were way too low, making it nearly impossible to reach food towards the rear. 

On to the food: there isn't much special here that can't be found at Aria, Wicked Spoon, or Wynn (my favorite). The carved meats looked rather greasy, and the whole roasted chickens were shriveled and pathetic-looking. The sushi selection was decent, but if you're a shellfish lover, you're better off at the Aria or perhaps the Bellagio. The Mexican station was unstaffed--I'd been looking forward to a fresh-made tortilla, but oh well. The quality overall was good, but not great, and certainly not worthy of the price they're asking. 

We ended up leaving after one plate--it was that bad. I expressed my displeasure to manager type on my way out, but she could barely say "I'm sorry". If you're looking for a great buffet on the strip, and willing to pay these prices, head for the Wynn, Aria, or Wicked Spoon--but avoid the Bacchanal.

5 stars for service.  Our waiter was very attentive.
3 stars for the food.  For the amount of $ I paid, I expected better prime rib - not something that's hard and chewy.  Quite a lot of desserts there but I can't say anything deserves a 5 star.  
Seafood section they have the usual crab legs, shrimps and oyster.  I didn't see lobster tail this time.  Soft shell crab was nicely fried.
They have a section of Chinese food including some dim sum dishes and chicken soup.  There is a Japanese section with maybe 8 different sushi.  There is a make-to-order noodle station with Vietnamese pho, Japanese udon and other Asian soup noodles.
There is a salad section but who goes to Vegas buffet for salad.  :0
1 star for security - saw people came in from exit line without getting checked - who knows if they really paid or not.  In fact, we saw people sat down on someone else's open table and ate...

Bacchanal is a place I will continue to visit every time I come to Vegas. We went on a Saturday around 1pm for their brunch.  The $45 per person price included unlimited mimosas, which seemed to be better than average, and they did not skimp on the alcohol.  Wait time from when we first got in line until we were seated was a reasonable 20 mins.  Our waiter Carlos was polite and prompt with our drinks.  The selection was seemingly limitless with their buffet areas broken out in sections, ie a seafood section, breakfast, mexican, italian and asian. Sushi to sashimi to crab legs and claws, it was all there and never in short supply. I started with breakfast, some corn beef hash, bacon, chicken and waffles and red velvet pancakes. All delicious, however the red velvet pancakes were nothing special. The pizza was delicious, as well as some of the ribs they were serving.  If you like desert then you certainly want to save some room, boutique pastries to gummy bears, my favorite was the mango Italian Gelato, I added some to my mimosa and ended up having 3 more. Highly recommend Bacchanal if you are in Las Vegas.

Pretty good buffet, but it didn't completely knock my socks off. Don't get me wrong, the food is good,  especially for an all you can eat joint. I used to like buffets, but I'm not so hot on them anymore. Maybe I'm just a little spoiled and expect a higher grade of food these days. Individual items can be hit or miss, ranging excellent to mediocre. Either way, I give it 4 stars overall, so not bad!

There is an excellent selection of food here, but not everything is great. I'll run down the list of what I ate during a weekday brunch:

Oysters - very good, fresh and crisp tasting. I do t know where they came from, but they were delicious.

Bloody Mary Oyster shooters - tasty, but missing vodka

Shrimp cocktail - huge, tasty shrimp. Not over-cooked, with a nice texture.

Stone crab claws - utterly tasteless. A waste.

Mussels - not great, not terrible. 

Snow crab legs - not bad, but the ones I got were still a bit frozen.

Lobster bisque - very good. Not the best I've had, but really solid for a buffet!

Baked Sole - delicious! Tender and flaky with a lot of flavor. I could eat it all day.

Prime rib - a little tough for my taste. Underseasoned, and not terribly flavorful

Beef Ribs - great beefy flavor, but pretty tough. Not low or slow enough in the cooking.

Smoked Sausage - not bad, but unremarkable

Fried calamari - very nice. Crispy and flavorful

Dim Sum (turnip cake, shumai, har gao, xlb)- pretty good! I mean, it's not as good as what you'd get in a run of the mill dim sum restaurant, but for a buffet in Vegas? I'll take it!

Desserts are pretty good. There is a large selection of gelato, but I thought they all tasted a little funny. The creme brûlée was pretty good, but the flan was terrible. Cookies were on point for the most part.

I left this place very disappointed. I always wanted to try buffet in vegas, and based on the reviews on yelp, I decided to try this place. I went for dinner on a saturday night, and only waited for an hr to be seated. Maybe my expectation was too high, but food was not that good. Now with tip, my friend and i paid $70 each. With that and little more, i could've gone to a fancier restaurant and left full and satisfied. People didn't know where to form a line, since the meat section and seafood section were next to each other. People cut in front of me, someone even poured gravy on my plate. There were so many people working there, but nobody bothered to control the place. I ended up eating a piece of prime rib, 2 crab legs, and some noodle. The line for seafood section was so long i gave up and ate noodle, it was very expensive noodle for sure. Will i ever come back? Probably not. Will i recommend this place? No again. The only good thing was the lady walking around to refill drinks, it seemed like she was only one actually working there.

On our last Vegas trip, we wanted to try out Bacchanal before heading back to Cali because of the rave reviews. Luckily, the line to get in wasn't too long and the wait was bearable between 10:30 am - 11 am on a Thursday morning. We got luck because when we got there we were able to enjoy some breakfast items, as well as lunch items because they were in the mist of transitioning. I loved all the different food stations and cuisines. My favorite had to have been the mini pancakes, as well as the paella. I didn't want to stuff myself because I wanted to leave enough room for dessert. Even though at one point when we got up to get desserts, they cleared out our table even though we were not done, I told an employee right away and they right away got us situated again super fast and apologized for the inconvenience. Maybe they should come up with a system where customers turn a paper over or something to let them know they are done dining instead of playing the guessing game. Overall, definitely great food and would love to come back again!

This place is ridiculous!  I came here, although it was a few years ago with a buddy of mine and the food was spectacular.  I came during dinner time and it was pretty packed which was to be expected and we had to wait about 45 minutes.  We knew it would be packed.  We wouldn't have driven down if we didn't have foresight lol.  To be fair, since it was awhile ago, I don't remember too many details except that the food was a bit difficult to pile on all at once since they seemed to all be in their own individual containers which seems really novel and cute at first but turned into a hassle as I had to get up so many time.  That being said, the food was really good and I can honestly say that I thought I was going to die from overeating when I left.  I hated myself and even though I hurt, real, real bad, I knew this is what I wanted when I ventured out that night.  It is really expensive though but then again, it was probably worth it.

The food here was terrible. Biggest waste of $150 for two meals I can imagine. The shrimp was soggy and soft, the raw oysters had sand and grit in them and the chicken was so dry it was like cardboard. They gave you a little skinny slice of prime rib. If I pay $75 for a meal I at least want an inch thick piece of prime rib. I would not recommend this to my worst enemy

Great buffet but not worth the price for the amount of food I (and my family) eat. Breakfast was $30 a person and we probably ate about $10 of food each. The buffet is divided into sections of types of food - seafood,  Italian, American and Mexican, dessert.

Caesars has always had a good buffet but this is FAB-U-LOUS!   It is pricey but worth it.  Go hungry and make sure you have time to spend.  They have different types of crab, asian and small snow crab legs which are cold unless you ask the staff behind the counter to dip your legs in hot water.  They are very small but good.  The shrimp were very good and very large.  It is a lovely place and staff was great.  Went for Sunday brunch and you get  mimosas with the meal which were very good.  I will return again even though it's pretty expensive.  Loved it!

They have all types of cuisine and options - Seafood (king crab legs, lobster bisque, sole), Asian (bass, dumplings, rolls), Spanish (made to order tacos), Soups and breads, Charcuterie, Italian (custom pasta), Bbq and carving station (the brisket and prime rib were killer), and also an abundance of desserts (gelato, fresh fruit, mini pies, cookies, fudge, fruit compote). One of the best buffets I've been to. Don't forget it is a buffet though.

Came here for lunch, made it here at around 11:30 and there was a small line but nothing too bad. Two stars because the selection was not what I expected for a $54.99 buffet. No oysters, no sashimi, sushi selection was bad. Shrimp wasn't good quality, it was pretty mushy. Crab legs were fine and the meat section was fine too. Most of the food was subpar, and trust me, I expect any buffet to have subpar food. But some of the food was subpar to some of the other buffets I've had. If price wasn't a factor, I'd give this buffet 3.5 stars. 2 stars considering it was $55 a person and at this level of quality.

Overrated!

I'm not sure why hordes of people would be willing to line up for 2+ hours... I think it's kind of expensive for mediocre food/service. There is a wide variety of food, but it's really a typical Las Vegas spread. Seafood, American, Asian-American, Desserts, Pizza, etc. It was cool to see them put out Ice Cream mochi, but I was a bit disappointed when the dessert chef was unwrapping them from a Costco bulk size box at the dessert station. 

Overall, I think this place is okay. Food is decent, but waiting 2+ hours is ridiculous. They do have a paging system, but it's very inaccurate (probably because they want you to gamble).

This place is definitely worth a try whenever in Veags! In Caesars palace, love the ambiance. We had a Groupon for breakfast. Came with two mimosas before 10am. Got there around 9:30am. Was seated promptly because the Groupon included VIP (skip the wait). Mauricio was our server, awesome and very attentive! 

The food here was deeeelish! Breakfast phase had breakfast items but also had things I would consider for lunch too, which is always a plus. They had fries, eggs benedict, shellfish (crawfish, clams, crab pieces), dim sum, salad, pizza, meat & cheese, seaweed salad, an omelet station, a dessert kiosk. Need I say more?! I can't haha, there was too much! We got TOO full, we didn't even get to try the desserts, could not fit anymore!! Would definitely come back next time we're in Vegas!

Next time, dinner! Pace yourselves, good luck!

Quality really has gone down here. Things sit for a lot longer and become gross. Used to love it here but have been dissapointed 3 times in a row. I might as well stick to the station casinos for this type of quality.

We came because of all the reviews so I want to know what it is like.  We were there for dinner on 05/01/2017 and was not impressed at all.  The line was long so by the time we got to our table it was about 30-45 min later.  The foods were so ordinary and the layout is so spread out that going from one end to the other end would take sometime.  Even the desserts section was not anything different than places I've been to.  NOTHING would standout on my standard.  Disappointing!

This place is worth coming to! I tried coming here a few years ago but the wait was around 2-3 hours and my party got impatient. After that Vegas trip I kept on thinking about this buffet and wanting to try it someday. I finally had a free Saturday and planned a day trip from LA to Vegas just to eat at this buffet. I grabbed 3 other friends and we headed to Caesars Palace to eat here! 

As usual, there is a wait, however, this time we went around 2PM and there was an hour wait; not bad. They have a machine where you enter your party number and phone and they will text you when to come back. We walked around Caesars for a while until they texted. Then, there was another 20 minute wait in the line to get seated. 

The decor is pretty nice and fancy. The place is very roomy and lots of people were there. By the time we were seated it was dinner service. 

The service here is pretty good. They are attentive and come by to check up and refill our drinks. 

--FOOD-- 
These are some of the types of food I tried. There are more categories that I won't list since there is a lot of food at this buffet!

Chinese: You will find some typical Chinese dishes along with dim sum. The Chinese food here was a bit too salty and strong compared to some authentic Chinese food that I grew up with.

Sushi: Sushi was good. The types of sushi was limited. They had some simple maki rolls like California rolls. They also had some nigiri - salmon and tuna. They also brought out some poki which was addicting. The sauce was tangy and the fish was fresh and melts in your mouth. The poki comes in small bowls with some rice.

Italian: They had a few dishes but what was memorable to me was the gnocchi with truffle oil. The truffle oil was so fragrant and good. The gnocchi was cooked perfectly and had a nice texture. They also had mushroom and truffle oil pizza which was also fantastic! (they really like truffle oil). 

American/Meat: The steak here looks pretty bloody and medium rare. It is very salty and bold with flavor. Not my type of food but it seemed popular. They also have some sliders, fries, mashed potato, corn, and mac and cheese. I enjoyed the mashed potato!

Noodle bar: They have a noodle bar where you can get ramen, udon, pho, and laksa. I really enjoyed the laksa here!

Other: They have hummus, mozzarella cheese, pita, and some other dips that I enjoyed. They also have small plates like pork belly, escargot shooters, shrimp curry, and more! They have soups and salads which are good. 

Dessert: They have a variety of desserts. What stood out to me was their macarons which I enjoyed. They had a nice bite to them and full of sweet flavor. Also, the Thai Tea boba float!!!!! My girlfriend is a boba snob and she actually liked the boba texture and quality here (at a buffet!) The thai tea is good quality as well. The ice cream is yummy and not too sweet. 

STEAMED CRAB: This is what most people come for. You see tables that are covered up with mountains of steamed crab legs. I typically hate peeling crab legs but these were so easy to peel! And the meat was sooooooo delicious. I never had crab so good. Tastes even better with butter! Our party probably got 6 plates of steamed crab. 

Overall, I would say that they have a good mix of typical buffet fare that is cooked to perfection, along with some more 'fancy, hor d'oeuvres style' dishes that are presented nicely and taste great. Also, I never thought I would come here for the crab legs, but they were my favorite and I would come back just to get more crab!!!
They have the greatest variety, quality, and service out of every place that we tried in Vegas! Definitely worth the $50 for brunch

Great selection of sea foods and meats.   Roast beef is very good. And so are the steamed King crab with lemon juice.   Asian food are not very good from an Asian's stand point.  Desert are good.  Especially the fresh made crepes.
Large buffet , everything we had was good but they could have more options for those that don't eat meat , even their waffles had chicken on them

Bacchanal Buffet is definitely raising the bar high for all other competitors.  It is on another level.   I just hope they are able to sustain the service and quality as I've often seen buffets gradually decline with time.  I would easily rank it higher than Wicked Spoon which I feel is overrated....probably along the lines of Wynn. 

The food was ridiculously good.   The lamb chops were cooked perfectly - medium rare to medium.   All of the food stations had general favorites along with more authentic options.   At the asian line, they have a Pho and Ramen station where they serve Ramen from Monta.  It didn't taste on the same level as Monta, but with over 500 items, we're knit picking.

I enjoyed the Italian station where they had a pasta station where you can choose your pasta and sauce.  I went with the bolognese which was delish.  

The biggest star of the show has to be the seafood line or at least if you're basing by lines.   My advice is to grab a first plate of food to get the first excitement out of the way.  Then make your way to the seafood line for the wait.   You can bring a fork with you too so when you first make your way through the hot seafood items, you can snack on the halibut, salmon, crab croquette, lobster corn chowder.  People may give you weird looks and judge you, but it's only because they weren't genius enough to come up with the idea themselves.   When you make your way around the L-shape towards the STONE CRAB and KING CRAB LEGS, don't forget to ask the cooks to heat them up if that's how u roll.

Save room for desserts!  I enjoyed the tiramisu and the eclectic sorbet with flavors such as Watermelon Mint and Mango Chile Lime.

The newest buffet on the Strip and it was amazing! I have not heard one person didnt enjoy this buffet!!! sure the line is long but its all worth it plus every decent buffet line is long in Vegas. Food quality is absolutely at top, seafood is fresh with huge selections with variety of 500+ dishes!! This buffet top Bellagio, Wynn and M resort, your newest spot to experience Las Vegas style buffet!!

Outstanding. Amazing selection. Very fresh. Pretty fresh. Definitely the best Buffett I've encountered in Las Vegas. Fairly well organized and fast seating. Like they have electronic checkin options instead of having to wait in line excessively. A few of the hostess seaters were rude though while others were friendly. We were pulled out of line by one friendly hostess cause we were only a party of two when everyone in front of us were larger groups. Then a rude hostess questioned if we were 'players card' holders or not and pointed back to the line and said we had to wait. In all I'd definitely go back. Desserts were just ok. Chinese offerings didn't look great. Seafood options were the best. Prime rib could be a little more rare.

I was in Las Vegas for a convention and after reading so many rave reviews about the Bacchanal Buffet, decided to have lunch there. Expecting great food, I skipped breakfast.

I was there for a late lunch at around 2:00pm and there was no line.  I paid and got seated in about 5 minutes.  I was excited and looked forward for a culinary delight but instead got a nightmare.

After the first hour of the Buffet, I started to feel unwell and thought maybe I ate too much.  At the end of the Buffet, about two hours after being seated,  I felt really bad and I knew something was not right.  I asked for a cup of tea, hoping the warm tea would soothe away the discomfort.

However, the tea did not help and I started to throw up.  Since I was seated at the back of the restaurant, I knew I would not make it in time to the bathroom, and I did not want to throw up in the middle of the dining room and inconvenience other diners.  I stayed at my table and threw up into the bowl and all over my jeans, TWICE.  I called a waitress who was passing by, told her what happened and asked her for some napkins.  She went and found some cloth napkins, handed them to me but offered no other help. 

When I was able to gather my strength, I started to walk to the bathroom.  I must have looked sick since the hostess in front asked me if I was okay.
I threw up again in the bathroom and felt really miserable.

When I came out from the bathroom, I told the hostesses I wanted a refund.  I did not want to pay for the food that made me sick.  Since the hostesses could not make the decision, they had to go and get the Manager.

The Manager, Mr. Robert Quintero came. The first thing Mr. Quintero told me was Bacchanal does not have a refund policy, he then proceeded to conclude that I could not possibly have food poisoning.  He announced that he is a restaurant manager for many years and he knew that food poisoning took much longer than the 2+ hours I was there to show symptoms.
  
With all due respect, Mr. Quintero is a restaurant manager, not a medical professional.  Puzzled about his reply, I later checked the website of the Mayo Clinic.  According to Mayoclinic.org, it is possible for food poisoning symptoms to show up 1 to 6 hours after consuming contaminated food. 
The site says that bacteria can be present in meats, prepared salads, cream sauces and cream-filled pastries, the symptoms of such poisoning could show up in 1 to 6 hours. The above mentioned food choices are plentiful at the Buffet.  

The point is not to imply that a particular contaminant was present in the food, or that the restaurant is not properly caring for its product (contamination happens, and no system is 100% safe), but rather that Mr Quintero is simply incorrect in his statement. Given his years in the food industry, I am surprised he said that, and it made me feel more that it was said mostly to dismiss my reasoning rather than acknowledge a problem. 

He further suggested that maybe I ate some contaminated food in the morning.  I told him that was impossible since I was so looking forward to the "one epic feast" at the Bacchanal that I only had a cup of tea the whole day before the Buffet and I felt perfectly fine when I walked into his restaurant. He then implied maybe I was already sick without knowing it before I ate at his restaurant.  Again, all this made me feel like I was a problem that they just wanted to go away and that somehow I was trying to game the system. 

He said he can talk to his Manager but he believed his Manager would have the same answers.  I asked him to try and he came back and told me his Manager said the exact same thing that he told me.  The only thing he could do is get my name and phone number and the kind of food I ate at the Buffet.  He would relate the incident to the appropriate department and some one would get back to me.

Two days have passed since the incident, and no one has called. At this stage, I would be surprised if I heard from any department.   

The bottom line is, beyond showing little empathy towards a customer who clearly was not well, the staff was not particularly helpful or friendly as I struggled to deal with this unpleasantness.  When I asked management to address the problem, I got the feeling that the blame was on me, and that I was not well from before.
