All through the conversation, he did not inquire my well being nor offer a kind or comfort word.  The $43.29 refund I asked for weighed more to Bacchanal than good customer service. In the context of the reputation of the buffet ("the best in Las Vegas," "superb food choices," "ridiculous amount of variety", and so on), this is doubly disappointing.

Love the food at this buffet! Very large selection and my companion and I are smart so we usually try to go around 10:30-11:30AM to avoid long wait times. Hosts are friendly. Food is 5/5. Want to know why I gave it two stars? Guess what time we got asked what we wanted to drink? We were asked 45 minutes after devouring two plates! We tried to flag numerous servers down but of course they were too busy running like chickens. Not going to lie, I'd come again though!

A M A Z I N G !!!! 

I cannot stress how fantabuloso this buffet is.
Is it worth that long line? I believe so.
Lets start with dessert and go backwards...

DESSERT!!!!!!!!!!!!!! OMG they have the most amazing maccaroons available - also carrot cake and creme brulee - the w o r k s ................

Entree(s)
everything you could ever think of
they got sushi steak burgers waffle fries truffle fries 
BEST STEAK TACOS (i must say)
SUSHI- omg sushi they have TUNA POKE and that was super delish.

They give you this plate rubber holder and i was like psssh I don't need that.... and I was wrong... hhaha some of those plates are hot......... some 12 year old gave me their plate holder when he saw i was struggling thanks homie!

The food i described sounds so ordinary... but the QUALITY of it is superb!!!!!

Long line, but lots of choices, seafood were fresh, food were tasty, tons of desserts to choses , Icecream was smooth n cream. Best buffet in town. The only down side was long line up, but I think it worth the wait.

I give 2 stars because it is an over price buffet for dinner. Don't get me wrong! Food is slightly better but it is still way over price. This buffet has become too popular to care about their food quality. I gave it 2 try and less likely to go back again. All of the dessert are taste barely acceptable. 
*** way over price for the quality of food and bad services.
*** the host who were organizing the line were so rude too.

If you hate buffets the Bacchanal probably won't change your mind about them but it's a gorgeous place to eat with family and the service is great. Basically it's the best buffet money can buy but don't anticipate being able to try everything. Pace yourself. Seating is fantastic, decor is wonderful, food is high quality but not the highest quality so don't go in expecting lobster tails and filet mignon steaks. Good choices all around, so if you come with a group you're guaranteed that there'll be something for everybody. Expect a long wait but it's worth it!

One of the best buffets in Vegas!  I came during brunch.   The Beijing duck, dim sum and udon noodles are superb!  The desserts were excellent.  The food is fresh!  Totally worth the money.   I went twice here.  The food is not as stale as the other buffets in the city.

One of the top 20 things I've ever spend my $40 on. The food was amazing! The prime rib and brisket were especially off the chain and worth the price alone.. Throw some dim
Sum, creme brulee and king crab legs/claws in the mix.. Yesssuhhhh!!

I almost exploded walking out of here. One of the pricier dining experiences I've been to, but I mean, it's Vegas. In the lovely Caesar's Palace. Lots of different food; impressive Asian selection along with made to order noodle soups - got the ramen and well, ti was good. Fresh foods; good service, before our guy went on break. Extensive selection of dessert; among which included my favorite - creme brulee, tiramisu, and macaroons. Overall, a good experience.

Don't get the snow crab legs in the morning, they are all frozen. Looks like they were cooked overnight and not freshly cooked like I remembered. 

You may ask who eats snow crab in the morning. My take is why put it out for comsumption if it's not good.

This is one of the biggest buffets in Vegas and also most popular. They have a variety of foods ranging from American, Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Seafood, Italian.. the list is never-ending! The seafood bar is my favorite since they service king crab legs and fresh raw oysters. There is usually a long line (I waited 356 minutes before and we had to get a ticket hours in advance before we were called back.) Since I do not eat beef, there is not much of a meat selection for me other than sausages. But I like how they have different genres of food which makes up for the lack of non-beef meat. I am also a Platinum Member for Total Rewards and they let you skip the lines sometimes on non-peak days. Overall, this is a buffet I always recommend to people to try at least once. It is on the pricier side, setting you back about $70 but hey, you are in VEGAS!

I'm the usual here. We came to Vegas twice a year. We always eat here. But in the recent 2 years, the food is getting worse and worse. Specially on the meat station and sweets. Seafood quality is also get worse. I wonder who is in charge now. If I spent $57 a person without counting tax and tip. I expect a lot better food, like when they first started.

Not sure it was worth the wait but im glad i stuck it out! Used their kiosk and returned at the specified time. Even with that said, still had to wait 45 mins to get seated. Once seated, loved the atmosphere and how comfy the place felt. Really clean establishment. Nothing stuck out per say but EVERYTHING was good. I literally took small bites of almost everything they had from asian, mexican, steak, seafood and desert. Most def a place U need to visit when in Vegas.

Yes Yes Yes, I will have Bacchanal Buffet!  So Ceasars spent $25 million dollars trying to create the buffet of all buffets.  I would have to say "HAIL CAESAR" for they have succeeded!

There was about a 25-30 minute wait to get into the modern and beautifully decorated buffet. There was honestly too much food to even try and attempt to describe but the main stations consisted of the following:  Asian food including sushi, bbq ribs, dim sum and a mongolian style grill.  Italian food including expensive cuts of italian lunch meats, and some pretty darn delicious thin crust pizzas. Hot meat station, prime rib, lamb chops, flank steak, rib eye, sausages and more. Seafood including King Crab sliced in half, lobster chowder with huge chunks of lobster, shrimp, cerviches etc.  Mexican food including a street taco station. Fried chicken with sweet potato fries, Fish n Chips and many many more foods that I cant even remember.  There was also a huge dessert section with souffles and crepes made to order.

You really need several trips to this buffet in order to sample the vast amount of delicious items this place has to offer. Even my vast stomach couldnt make enough room to try everything.  Dinner cost $50 per person and was worth every penney, but for a mere $70 you can buy the 24 hour pass and come back to Bacchanal and other buffets as many times as you like in the 24 hour time period.  In sum, if your in Vegas you must try the new king of all buffets and visit Bacchanal.
Best Buffet in Vegas hands down and they even offer open bar , can't go wrong with that

One of the best breakfast buffet I have tried. If you want seafood like shrimp cocktail or green mussel for breakfast then this place is a must try.

Hand them your rewards card for discount on the buffet when paying.

It's hard to believe this is the best buffet in town. The decor is great and the atmosphere is nice. That being said most of the food was never up to temperature. Everything was cold. The crab legs were much too salty. The best dish I had was the rare prime rib with mashed potatoes. It certainly wasn't $69 dollars per person worth of food not including tip 
If this is the best then all buffets should be shut down.
It was a pretty good buffet, but the wait on a Tuesday evening was ridiculous and the price of $55 per person was a lot higher than the choice and quality deserved. But we got a story!!

All the hype lives up to expectations.

Came in for lunch before leaving Las Vegas. Caught a good day with no line. Staff was helpful, friendly and prompt. Total rewards members (casino card program) entry is discounted. This buffet priced a little more than others but worth the difference. The discount helps it too.

Pan holders are provided and we are seated. Drink orders are taken in a timely fashion as we get straight to the stations. Lots of variety. Definitely one of the biggest around. There are clearly defined areas. Seafood, meat, Italian, Latin, Asian, dessert are some. There are dishes that are oven hot and have the pan holders if you left yours at the table. Fresh plates are used each round up. 

For lunch there is not a limited selection of seafood. From salmon to halibut. Shrimp several ways. Ceviche, cocktail, et. Oysters, mussels, crab legs, crawfish are some offerings. Warm and cold are the variable plates. Properly maintained were the cold items such as the oysters. (I've gotten sick at other casino buffets)

Meats. So many selections just at the carving station. Brisket, turkey ham, prime rib, mango chicken sausage, hot links, kielbasa were just a few I tried. The meats were seasoned masterfully. Meats melted and tender. The hot links were spicy mouth was burning. Oh so good though. Other items found at this station include fried chicken, roasted chicken, chicken and waffles, fries, potatoes, any practically anything for classic buffet faire. Most of the options were good. Some a little dry but nothing where enjoyment was lost.

The next station had some Latin faire. Chili Colorado, fajitas, enchiladas, rice, tamales and likes. These were some of the better Spanish and Latin I have tried at a buffet. Most times dishes are dry and lacking seasoning. These were moist, fresh, and wanting more.

A salad bar, soups, rolls, and various small plates. Some good tried included the truffle soup, gratin potatoes, and truffle macaroni n cheese. Each of these were good enough to return for a second helping. Moist and seasoned to perfection both helpings. 

Italian and pasta station I didn't get much into. Classic fair of sauces, pizza et. They looked pretty good. 

Asian faire station has been by a mile the best for a buffet I have tried. Japanese, Korean, and Chinese faire. 

There was a choice of three sushi rolls. Each distinctive. I enjoyed the spicy tuna roll. Fresh was the rice roll and the tuna. A good spicy was found. A ramen, pho, and udon station was available. I tried the ramen. Freshly made noodles are boiled to order in a light stock with the noodles, barbecue pork, and vegetables added (can be with held on request). The ingredients are pulled once cooked and added to a simple miso soup brith. The broth was seasoned and demonstrated respect found in preparation at a Japanese ramen house. 

For Korean and Chinese dishes, I tried the golgibi beef, various dim sum (shu Mai, dumplings), and duck were some of the items enjoyed. Tender easy to eat beef was the golgibi. Dim sum items were flavored, sized and appropriate like found in many Chinese brunch times. Duck was fair amount of meat to fat. The Chinese and Korean offerings were better than most actual restaurant fair without the outrageous pricing. 

Dessert and snack bar. Fruit, cookies, pies, pastries, donuts, gelato, chocolate/caramel apple and pears. My eyes at this point are bigger than my belly. Everything is so scrumptious. There is more than something for everybody here.

Good: variety for everyone, flavors hit most marks, proteins were appropriate temperature and seasoned, organized, friendly. 
Bad: didn't find lobster during lunch but otherwise everything was good and so full (from eating- not bad). 

I'd be back to eat more. Definitely one of the best buffets to date.

Cannot believe how large the food choices was. The closest to the entrance are the seafood; we were here during the weekday dinner, so it was snow crab legs, mussel, and oysters. If you want warm snow crab legs, you can go to pasta station, I think, and they'll dunk them in boiling water for you. 

The wait can be a drag, so be ready for it, but I honestly think it's worth it, even if it's $50 for dinner. The choices are, basically, endless. A lot of things were decent in taste, and could be made better by combining different stuff. For example, the pad thai noodles were way better when you added on the curry that was right next to it, for more flavoring. My friend also got everything that had truffle oil, and those dishes were delicious. I know people usually want feedback of the crab legs and the meat station. Crab legs were great, especially since they had butter. The meat station, I got the prime rib and like the pulled pork? Pulled pork was kind of too fatty, but prime rib was decent. I didn't try the other choices: lamb, rib, sausage. But I was impressed by the prime rib. 

Dessert section was pretty stellar. I usually stay away from those little individual sweet treats, But the strawberry gelato was awesome...

Definitely would be back next time...even if it's $50 dinner...

This is a must if you like buffets.

Just prepare to wait up to 90 minutes.

Shrimp crab legs and claws lots of shellfish.

Good meats and cheeses as well as Gelato in many flavors and a lot of baked goods. 

Just be prepared for a food coma afterwards.
My family had a blast here! Hit the seafood and very little of everything else. You will be happier in the end!

Easily not worth the price that was paid. I will just say the crabs are amazing and that's about it.

Pros:
1. Delicious selection of both steamed and cold crab legs that make the entire buffet worth it if you eat a lot like I did.
2. Delicious garlic parm steak fries that were for sure a treat.
3. Interior looks beautiful as it should and there are a lot of food choices if you are someone that likes to have a lot of food options.

Cons:
1. Food choice may be plentiful but the actual amount of food that entertained me was very bad. This is coming from a person that loves meats and hates vegetables. 
2. The sliders are just terrible when I went. The burger was dry and it just did not taste good. McDonald's was better.
3. The $50 price tag cannot be justified if you aren't here for expensive food items such as oyster or crab legs.

You like seafood? It's worth it. You're rich? It's worth it. You're poor and just want a good experience because you can't afford michellen (I know I spelled it wrong) star restaurants? Not worth it.

Not worth the wait. The regular line takes about 5 hours after asking the people who were near the front of the line. There is an a express line which took 1 hour but at a cost of an additional $20 per person. So the total per person comes out to  $77 not including tax.  I took the express line to save time but after being seated there are more lines just to get food - ridiculous. 

Most of the food was just okay and are mostly available at other buffets like the Rio, ie snow crab legs, salmon, shrimp, sushi, etc. However, they did have a tomahawk ribeye steak that was excellent. Obviously they won't give you the whole steak.

Big disappointment.  I read plenty of reviews on Vegas buffets before choosing to dine here a few weeks ago. There was a huge selection of food but the taste of the food was mediocre at best. No king crab legs that I expected. Snow crab legs were served warm and cold and they had lots of them. However, they were super salty and had no sweetness to them at all. Rest of the seafood such as oysters, sea snails, stone crab claws, and cioppino were only decent. Lamb chops and bone marrow were good but not spectacular like many reviews said. The Asian food section had Peking duck, Korean BBQ ribs, Char Siu, and roast pork. Also tasted just ok. The stir fry dishes looked horrible, old and dried up so I didn't even bother to try them. Spanish fare station, same pots of food there for the duration of our meal. Looked old and unappetizing. Obviously, hardly anyone went for it. Italian station, food looked fresh but again tasted ok only including the Osso Bucco. Dessert station had made to order crepes, gelato, cream brûlée, raspberry mousse, tiramisu, etc.  No soufflé though. We tried 4 flavors of gelato and all tasted horrible. Even my 6 year old son didn't like his. Despite having mostly mediocre food, our whole family did agree they had the best chocolate dipped strawberries. We all went back for seconds. Last but not least, service.  It started poor as our first server didn't even come by to get our drink orders until 15 or 20 mins after we were seated and never picked up our empty plates. Everything changed though when a different server showed up a little later. He was very attentive, friendly and provided great service. Kudos to this older gentleman. So overall, I personally do not think this buffet is worth the price and did not live up to the hype. I was expecting way better for what is supposed to be the "No 1 buffet" in Vegas. I won't come back again unless the food quality has improved.

Buffets are tough! keeping food under a lamp and maintaining freshness is not easy. I don't often do buffets for this reason. But in Vegas supposedly you have too! I read an article in USA today saying that Caesar's had arguably the best buffet in Vegas. We actually signed up for the "Buffet of Buffets" deal where you pay $55-$70 depending on the buffets you choose. We paid the extra $25 to add Caesar's dinner. So worth it! This buffet was endless and phenomenal. I literally tried nothing that I didn't enjoy. If I had to give advise I would say pass on the Buffet of Buffets deal because buffets for 24 hours is tough especially in Vegas. But Caesars buffet I would visit again in a heart beat!

This place has gone wayyyyy down hill..paid 75 per person holidays prices over Xmas weekend 1. Check in process was a joke...went to kiosk at 430..no ticket print out but told to return at 915...came back and host was like where is your ticket ?? Uh duh your stupid kiosk machine has been out of paper all day ..and she told us wait is about another hour but food will be cooked till 1050pm...waited in another line to pay 
2. Paid finally and waited in another line ...
3. Finally seated about 1020..
Nothing looked appetizing at all...
Prime rib looked like home town buffet quality ...
And it tasted like it
Oysters looked very disgusting ..and smelled bad
Soup was disgusting ..
Salad bar looked like souplantation but Worse
With bowls of vegetables and salad dressing
Slider burger ..this was the highlight ..bun was rock hard and my friend tossed on table and it made a thumping sound ..a joke
I can go on and on but think you get the point
4 they started to clean up and pulling items at 1030
5 no lamb chops when i went to meat counter at 1030
6 no refill on drinks at 1045..was told no more ice tea
7 only edible things was salty crab legs , crepe and gelato ice cream ...
-there's probably another 10 things I can specifically mention that was a joke 
For 75 per head check in process , wait line and especially food needs to be a lot better

I know some will think hey it was close to closing time ..I been to other buffets at close time and it was 100 times better then his buffet from check in to food quality at a much lower price 

Sorry but this is not Even close to best buffet in Vegas any more from scale of 1-10 this is now a 2

Stay away !! You been warned !!!

The food was good, but definitely not worth the price. Went here for Christmas brunch. Walked right in at about 9:30 am.

No eggs with truffles were offered. I had one slice of pizza, salami, cheese, beef with asparagus, frisee salad. The sushi had no fish -- just tamago and such. My boyfriend had roast beef and some scrambled eggs. The rest of the food didn't look great, but just okay.

Cost -- $130 for two with iced tea. Won't do that again!
Wow, this was decadent. Everything was delicious. Great variety (pho! are you kidding me!?!?!). And although it may seem pricey, for Vegas (and for the quality) it's actually a great deal.

You really can't go wrong with this place.  They have a good variety for everyone.  You really get to try cuisines from around the world.  Sometimes the wait can get ridiculous inside and out so definitely remember to be patient.  Came here for breakfast and dinner before which was all a good experience but if you want more seafood, you should come at dinner.  The desserts here are also really good.
Buffet here is definately the best in town. We went to a couple of seafood buffet and asian buffet, and it was disgusting. This buffet was a lot cleaner than most.

The worlds #1 buffet? - very deserving title. There are many choices to choose from: Italian, Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, seafood, meats, and desserts. The sushi and poki are very good as well as the tonkotsu ramen. The crab legs and shrimp are also delicious. Finally, I would also try to get as much meat as possible - try the smoked brisket!
Try to eat as much seafood as possible and wash it down with your drink of choice. And after that is done, sample the assortment of desserts that they have from chocolate covered strawberries to Thai bubble tea to Mont Blanc. 
Would definitely come here again.

This place is expensive but was so worth it. Food is good service also very good. Clean n friendly staffs. If u don't have a player card u have a long wait so get there before 5:30 pm then u don't gave to wait. 
Food they have a lots of varieties n the desert was amazing.

Not what it was. I have been going to Bacchanal since it opened and last nights visit showed its losing ground to the best buffet in Las Vegas. Food was lackluster and a lot of it had been sitting out for a while. On a weds night dont put out so much food when its not that busy . Every hot dish that was under a heat lamp was lukewarm. And the crab legs were so small I thought i was at Red Lobster, sad.  We brought this to the attention of the manager and he was apologetic and asked could he have the kitchen make us something up. A nice gesture but i brought a visitor here to impress them. They were not impressed. As a local here there are many better options . Sorry to see it go .

Unquestionably the best buffet in Vegas. I've never been to a breakfast buffet with so many cut/made to order options.  I ate no fewer than 4 different types of sausage, and they were all fantastic.  Also, if you're at all on the fence, the unlimited drink package is 100% worth it.  Refills were prompt and plentiful, and the mimosas were tasty too.

I share the same sentiments with the other 3 star yelpers.  Its just okay.  Wayyyy too expensive.  After tax it is $60 per adult for dinner.  It is worth $40 at best.  I can get a much better meal for half the cost anywhere else.  
Wait time on a Tuesday (8/09) night at 6pm was an hr and 40 mins.  It reminds me of a Disneyland ride.  You get a fast pass that tells you when to come back so you can stand in line for at least 45 mins.  You pay as you get halfway through then they funnel you into different lines based on party size.  I actually think this is smart because it does lessen the line and it forces you to go gamble in the beginning while you wait.   Without this, I could see it taking 3 hrs.
Anyway, we get seated and you get to wait some more as you are passing through the buffet line.  Its a pretty big place so there TONS of people milling around.  My waitress was terrible.  We had 5 stacked empty plates and no drink refills throughout most of our meal.  When you pay $60 and rely on them for drinks, you better come more often.  VERY disappointed with that.
Luckily that have some juices pre-bottled in the buffet which was a perk you don't usually see along with guava and horchata.
Here is what you are paying for that you don't normally see at an average buffet:
Crab legs both hot/cold but sliced down the middle so there is no fuss or cracking.  This costs more for them to purchase this way.  The cheese selection and salami is upper class.  Muscles on the half shell.  Dim Sum (these were good).  Street tacos made to order (were bland).   Gelato and macaroons.  Beef burger Sliders (HORRIBLE hockey pucks) that they should not bother with.
Everything else is your normal fair.  Some were very dry, cold and bland.  For the price, I expect none of that and I also expect excellent service.  I say its good to try ONCE but would not go again unless someone else was footing the bill which was the case for me on Thursday night but it was the same exact food in the same exact condition.  However service was a little better but we were now a party of 14 instead of 2. Hard to ignore a giant table like that.

This was third time eating here for our annual Vegas trip.  I'm not sure if the quality has dropped a bit or we are just getting used to the same menu items, but our group all felt it has lost a bit of what made it the best buffet in the past whether it's the selection of food or quality.  My biggest disappoint like most is that they have a great kiosk check-in system already in place where they can text you when your party can physically check in the line.  You would think that will shorten your wait but the five of us still waited over 2 hours to get our table which is unacceptable for people who love to gamble or shop.  Why not just shorten the line half the distance (or more) and page ppl more accurately to avoid wasting time in line?!  I would have given 4 stars but the wait time dropped it another star for me.

Not really worth the $52.99!
Seafoods on hand are crab legs 2 ways (hot/cold), defrosted oyster, crawfish, clams, & mussels. None of them are any good!

Crabs are salty! Crawfishes are peppery! Clams are blend! Oysters are NOT fresh!

Sushi is hard.

I think the only good items were corns & congee.

Again not worth $52.99!

This has got to be the best quality buffet in Vegas! You get what you pay for! During lunch, it cost about $75 per person, which included bottomless mimosa! Good quality gourmet food! The flavors were great! There were so so many good food to choose from! The facility is clean and in good shape! Good service from the servers. 

This is not like any other buffet in Vegas! Too notch quality food here!

So expensive but so good!  The wait was very long especially for a Monday night.  I'm glad they have a kiosk so I can go around gamble, drink, or shop.  After they text us it was time to go, the line to get in was still too long though.

There was plenty of variety and options available.  Desserts weren't so bad.

The ambiance is beautiful and large so it doe fit a lot of people.

The last time we visited Bachannal was in 2014 so it was quite a treat to be able to visit again. Wait time was only about 20 minutes which I was very thankful for. We were seated by our hostess Irma who was delightful. (Remember that name because it's important later.) The 5 of us sampled everything the buffet had to offer. Towards the end of our meal I found something in one of the dishes I had gotten from the Mexican food station. I will not go into detail as to what it was but I did see Irma and showed it to her and she swiftly got the manager at our table to apologize. I told him I did not want to make a big deal about it but that I did want to bring it to the attention of management. He was very accommodating and I appreciated his efforts to make this dining experience right. Overall it was a good visit to Bachannal and even with that little mishap I still think this is the best buffet on the strip!

When I read that the Bacchanal Buffet was the best on the strip with many food options, I was really excited to try it.  However, I have to say that it is VERY OVERRATED.  We had to wait in line for half an hour (which I sort of expected).  They had lots of seafood (if you are into oysters and crab) and many slabs of meat.  If you aren't crazy about that type of seafood or meat, you will probably be disappointed.  Yes, they have many "worldly" dishes, but they are all generic food (pizza, pasta, generic sushi, dim sum and Chinese food).  They did have Pad Thai, which was a little more unique, but being from California, it's nothing really special.  They also didn't have very many vegetable dishes and their salad bar was disappointing.  On the bright side, they did have many desserts to choose from (including the fuzzy Chinese lychees).  However, they did not have my favorite tiramisu.

Don't get me wrong, the food was good.  The lamb was tender and juicy.  It's just not amazing.  I've tasted better food at the buffets at  other casinos in Reno and Sacramento for half the price.  If the price wasn't so expensive ($50+ for dinner), I probably would have given it 4 stars, but it's really not worth the price.  If you are going to spend that much money anyways (and don't eat a whole lot of food), I would spend a little more, and walk a little farther to the Top of the World at The Stratosphere for a much better dining experience.

This is the best buffet I've had in Vegas! They had such a large variety of seafood and meat.

Upon entering the buffet, they request a photo of you in which they would later ask if you would like to buy for a souvenir.

The flavors at the buffet were delicious, and they also had a noodle station in the Asian food section with the choice of tonkotsu ramen, Singaporean laksa, Pho, as well as other options. We had tried the ramen and laksa and were so tasty! I wanted another bowl. The variety of food stretched from one end to the other offering plenty of delicious dishes to choose from.

Overall, nice buffet if you're willing to splurge.
My Favorite Vegas Buffet!!! Always a great variety of food. Food is very flavorful. Kinda pricy but definitely worth every penny! Dinner lines can be quite long.. plan for an early dinner.

Terrible queuing system. Wait to get into another line to wait to sit down. 1 hour wait to get in line to pay, 20 minutes to then pay, and an additional hour after paying to get seated. A lot of people were cutting in line at the "6 or more persons" line and the workers not even stopping them. Very disorganized. Will not be coming back.

So, this is the crazy popular buffet in Caesar's Palace that everyone talks about. I'll start with the good stuff. There are tons of selections that includes seafood, meats, salads, Asian, Mexican and the best part: dessert. 

Favorites:
Asian - There's a noodle bar! Although I didn't get to try the pho, I really enjoyed the ramen and udon. Skip the Kung Pao and go for the Orange Chicken. The sushi and sashimi were actually pretty fresh for buffet style. 
Meats - The brisket was juicy, tender & perfectly burnt on the edges. It was delicious with their bbq sauce. The street corn in this section is an absolute must. They were cut into small pieces; I had 4!
Dessert - Thai Tea Float served in a small shot cup! The Matcha covered strawberries were so good! And of course, the gelato.

The service was great. Our old plates were constantly being taken away and our drinks were always refilled. Also, the people serving food in the buffet lines were very kind and patient. 

The worst part about the whole experience is the wait time. We went on a Sunday for lunch and waited 3 hours for our party of 4! We were starving! We ended up paying the dinner price of $60 per person. Yup, pretty steep. 

Overall, I had a decent experience. I don't think it's worth the price, but hey, it's Vegas. I do want to come back and try their brunch someday.

I've been here once for dinner (2013) and twice for breakfast (2015) and while I think $50+ for dinner is better spent elsewhere, I love breakfast at Bacchanal!

The best part about having breakfast here is that there is zero line prior to 10 AM. Waltz in and have your pick of the place.

So I'm not a huge breakfast person and I'm not big on breakfast pastries or seafood. If you like these things, you're in luck. If you don't like these things, then you're definitely in luck.

Bacchanal's breakfast is more like lunch with a bagel station, an omelet station and some small plates of tiny pancakes and waffles. Asian food is definitely hit or miss, only because there isn't the same kind of turnover for those items.

Crab, oysters, shrimp and lobster Benedict are all available for breakfast in a zillion combinations.

Other breakfast stations include:
-chicken wings, fries, various vegetable dishes and hash browns are near the carving station.
-tons of fresh juices are near the bread and Mexican food.
- Pozole, breakfast burritos and chilaquiles are about the extent of the Mexican section.
-croissant sandwiches, sweet potato gnocchi in cream sauce (crazy delicious), various fancy cold cuts and cheeses and savory pizzas in the (South of France??) Section.
-Made to order pho, ramen, udon & miso soups are available with a topping bar.
-Various curries, noodle dishes and sushi are near the bagel bar.
- a congee bar, roast duck, bao, dumplings and lots of various Asian dishes cover quite a bit of the stations for breakfast.
-the full dessert bar is open although the offerings always change. One of the two times they had AMAZING crepes (I had two and only slightly regretted it.)

If you want to try a fancy buffet without waiting in a gargantuan line and spending cash that can go toward a nicer dinner elsewhere, check out breakfast at Bacchanal. It's so worth it.

I would describe myself as someone who is very familiar with the various buffets in Vegas. Been here twice, and definitely still at the top of my list. The price can be a bit of a scare, but I do believe it's worth it. As you start to try the different dishes, you get a sense that each dish is very well thought out, something that might be at a fancy restaurant, where they give you a small portion on a plate because it's gourmet. Everything here feels better quality than just cooking a whole bunch of mac n cheese in a big pot or pan. It's a strange thing to judge on, but what impressed me is that they had a variety of bottles of fresh squeezed juices. Don't think I've ever seen that, but I think it goes to show the effort they put into each offering.

I can't just describe one or two things that I really like, but would say that they have one of the widest array of selections, and each one is very good.

Pay the price, and it's still better than Wynn, Wicked Spoon, etc.


One note: there's no need to wait in line now thanks to the interactive kiosks where you check in, and they give you a time to come back. Don't let them trick you. Instead of having you wait in line, they're happy to have you sit and play $20 of video poker, and now your buffet is $70 instead of $50. Don't let them trick you! haha

One of the best buffets on the strip. Well worth the $55.00 per person. I couldn't believe the food selections, about four different rooms with long counters filled with all types of cuisine. Crab legs, prime rib, salads, beef brisket, Asian, Italian, Mexican, American. Desserts where amazing. Gelato, Cheese cake, cookies, custards, crepes.. Nice fruits and vegetables galore!

You gotta go! Located in Cesar's Palace. If you have a Totals Rewards Card you avoid the long lines. If not You may have to wait 1 to 1 1/2 hours during dinner time. check in early!
So disappointed... Long wait for just above average food... Weighing food and waiting time and price , not worth it. Expensive for what it is drinks were extra.

I'm a buffet fan. A big one. When I came to Vegas and discovered there existed fine buffet I had to try it. Both this and the Wynn were pretty amazing. This one actually edged out the Wynn in terms of environment, variety, and overall quality. It would have been 5 stars but the service was just plain bad. When it comes to buffet the servers have 2 jobs: drink refills and plate removal. They did neither. Even for an off hour (3:00-4:30) our drinks took forever to arrive and after that I never saw a single refill. For an hour and a half! Plates sat at our table unmoved for 10-20 minutes at a time. When the price of  dinner is over 50$ you'd better include some sweet service. I'd talk about how amazing the food was but the service left such a bad taste in my mouth I can't really recall it.

Being the newest buffet, we just HAD to try this place out. 

We got here around 11:45am for the lunch buffet..only to realize the longest line I've seen since the opening of the M buffet.

You can buy the right to cut in front of the line for an additional $15. The lunch buffet menu was $39. Not bad.

The BBQ line was the best! The prime rib they had here was REALLY goooood; chicken apple hot links, pepper hot links, baby back ribs, five kinds of marinades you can smother all over..everything! 

Seafood was MEH; I've never tasted saltier king crab legs in my life. I had to stop eating the fourth leg because my tongue started to sting. The mussels were very dry, but I did enjoy the shrimp! I believe they have oysters available during dinner time as I saw one of the line chefs shucking a bucket of oysters...for a moment I thought those were for lunch, but they weren't...what a tease.

Anyhoo, come here and try it out. Overall it was a good experience, but the seafood line could definitely use a little sprucing up. I didn't try the Asian food they had here because...well..I'm from Rowland Heights.

Yummy but I wouldn't rate it as "the best" buffet in Vegas. They had excellent king crab legs, sausages, macarons, and cakes, but their prime rib/steak was a bit on the dry side. The lines are excessively long (about a 2 hour wait for dinner on weekends), but we paid $25 each to get in the VIP line (basically cut in front of everyone).

A little pricey, but definitely worth it. Food from all over the world. We came towards the end of the day, but the food was still delicious. 

The dessert bar was my favorite. :)

Probably the best buffet on the strip.

The buffets were the #1 thing I was excited about on my first trip to Vegas. I expected to feel overwhelmed, in the best way possible.  I had watched many Travel Channel specials regarding these buffets, the choices of seafood and meats, and the overall luxuriousness of the experience.  I came in with high expectations. 

This was everything I expected and more.  I had an awesome time.  We came in for breakfast (brunch?) on a Thursday.  The seafood and meat standard fare was there, which was excellent.  Also had a great variety of brunch options such as lobster benedict, ham/egg/cheese crossaints, red velvet french toast, and fresh waffles with all the fixings

Options I did not expect but was pleasantly surprised to see:
-Paella (!!)  
-A full authentic Chinese congee bar with all the traditional toppings.  They even offered chopped century eggs! Whattt.  that was pretty cool
-cold pressed juices

Ended up being about $65 per person but it's well worth it.  Definitely the highlight of my first Vegas trip and can't wait to return.

Absolutely delicious! Best buffet to date on the Strip! I came here for the Thanksgiving holiday special dinner. Price was steep at $70 per adult, but well worth it. 

I first tried everything in the seafood section. The shrimp were some of the sweetest I've ever eaten. Crab legs were very good too. I was also impressed to find raw oysters there. The oysters were ok...probably the only item I felt was below par. Mussels, crab cakes, craw fish....alll very delicious. 

What most impressed me was the Peking duck. So juicy with crispy skin! I ate so much duck, I didn't have room for turkey. Oh well, maybe next year. 

Desserts were absolutely mouth-watering as well. They even had rambutan fruit! It was so popular, people were grabbing it by the plate full as soon as more came out. 

There was so much more to the buffet, but impossible to eat in one sitting. Due to today being Thanksgiving, they had a 2 hour max sitting limit. 

If you're in Vegas and want to do buffet, I'd highly recommend this place. You won't be disappointed!

They have the paging system so that was a good start. We hit the tables to test our luck and we were paged 2 hrs later. We get in line and waited another hr. My friends have been here before and they said it was the best buffet around and we have been to...shamelessly, a lot of buffets. I'm damned excited. Paid the 80 dollars and sat down. Drink lady came and I politely declined because I've heard their in house juice was the business. Hell no! Watered down "fragrant" water. Gross. Alright. Seafood time. That's it? Crab legs and some damn clams? Ok, some fish but who goes to the buffet for white fish? The crab was mushy and salty. Alright they have a smoker so their bbq has to be top notch. How do you mess up bbq with a smoker!? Dried and over seasoned. Ok now I'm getting annoyed. I head to the sushi station and the salmon was good enough. So I'm trying to salvage my dinner and head to the sweets. Damn! Impressive! Looks good! Ow! Macaroons, love me some macs. I picked them up and immediately noticed the weight. Them suckers were heavy!!! I sit down and took a bite into one. Doughy and under cooked. Really? I'm pissed now. I look at my friends and they know it's gross. All that talking about the best buffet around, they know it was gross but tried to save face. Maybe it was a bad weekend they said. Hell no. Highly doubt it. Let me try one more item. Cheese cake. It's cheese cake, even store bought cheese cake is delicious. I cut a piece with my fork and taste... Wth?! It's straight cream cheese. Like Philadelphia cream cheese! I'm done. The only thing they did right was the paging system. I don't know how they heck they justify the 80 dollar tag otherwise. I went during Memorial Day. I'm headed back there next week... Some other friends want to try it out... What are the chances of it being a bad weekend? It's an 80 dollar gamble... Hmm

This was one of the worst experiences I've had during my weekend trip to Vegas. Besides the 3 hour wait, the food was mediocre. All the meats were dry, the bone marrow had no flavor and the selection was pretty disappointing considering the wait time and pricing at around $55. I would not recommend.

We made the mistake of going at right at 11am, when they were about to transition from breakfast to lunch. Food was nice but not fresh because it was slow at that time and the food sat too long! I ate too much to go back and try the fresh lunch offerings. Desserts were great but could only taste because just too much food to choose from!
Don't get excited about the seafood on display in the beginning of the buffet, it's only for display! Only limited seafood is served unless it's the weekend! Many people tried to get at the crab legs behind the glass only to be laughed at!

so called electronic check in system is a completely joke,.i wanna give them the negative if i could. you got your ticket for 8:30pm and then the front standing mean girl tell you this ticket is for you to come back at 8:30pm to line up from the beginning for anothe hour, its not a fast pass or anything meaningful. What a Freaking joke

The bf and I dined at bacchanal for Sunday brunch in August 2013. After reading other reviews, I was a little scared that we'd have to wait for a table. However, we arrived at about 10:15 am and walked right in. The Hostess at the front said weekend brunch starts to get crazy around 11, so if you want to avoid a massive line, plan accordingly. 
Tip: if you use your total rewards card, you'll save a couple bucks off the tab. 

As for food, there were sooo many choices here.  It was a little overwhelming, but not in a bad way.  As we arrived shortly after 10, most of the foods out were "breakfast" type items. However, right around 11, more "lunch" items like sushi, sliders, etc started coming out. 

Quality was great, and you get unlimited mimosas during sunday brunch.  Highly recommend!

The best buffet in Vegas. It's worth the wait. 
Chinese food was good. Poke was the bomb. Ceasar salad, seafood & desserts aaaah
Sooo good ! 
I just didn't like the elderly staff at the entrance bec I have a disabled friend who walks slow & she doesn't want to seat my group until she comes & we already told her that my friend's pace in walking is slow but I'm glad one nice staff said make an exception - so Thank you for your consideration & understanding

I'm not a big fan of buffet and such a small eater can't expand the stomach for buffet.  I found most of reviews were highly rated so still wanted to try this famous or the best buffet (so-called) during our trip!

We went for dinner buffet on Wed night, we got the "Wait" ticket from the machine!  OMG! We gonna wait for 56 mins!  However, I saw the people got the ticket and went into line up right the way.  We followed them to do so.... Eventually, we waited over  1/2 hour and got seated.  

When we walked in to dining room, we saw the tables were so closed like cafeteria style.  It was so noisy as well! Our server came to us and took the drink order shortly, my friend and I both took turn to check out the food.

Honestly, such buffet price over $50 per person, I would expect it to be restaurant quality food instead of buffet quality food.  When I checked out the Asian section food, it's so disappointing. It looked like instant frozen dim sim or dish for reheating on the steamer.

I started with some green and pasta salad, got 1 piece Alaska king crab leg. The prime rib was undercooked and kind of cold.  

I got few desserts and all of it were too sweet for me.  It tasted like icing sugar desserts.

I would say it's not worth the wait and money.

My wife got food poisoning from eating at the buffet.  July 1, my friend treated us to lunch at the Bacchanal Buffet, it was very crowded both waiting in line and in-side the eating area.  The lines waiting to get to the food items were long. The noise level in the eating area was very loud and the bussers were slow to pickup and clean vacated tables. 
I got a prime rib and other food items that I wanted to taste.  I was surprised by the poor quality of the prime rib, the meat was tough and hard to chew, I had better at other buffets in Las Vegas. My wife got food items she wanted to taste.  Her food choices were different from mine.  Besides the her regular choices she wanted to try the Asian food area and liked the steamed rice wrap and commented that it was tasty.
Later that night she had the runs and vomiting which continued for the next couple days.  We tried to figure out how and where she got sick.  We did not eat anywhere else except at the Bacchanal Buffet.  We narrowed it down to the Asian food area and possibly the steamed rice wrap. She went to her doctor who confirmed by blood test she had food poisoning.  
From my personal experience and my wife getting food poisoning we will not go back to that place because of the inadequate quality management of the food they serve, the poor service, and the over crowding of the eating area.
Way too much to say that's positive.  Lets just say everything is unbelievable!!!  I would travel from Chicago just to eat here again!

Love the food, great service
I miss the hash though.   Still one of the best brunch options and don't forget to have the dessert bar make you  a souffle.

I was at the buchannal for lunch this Monday and the wife and I have a horrible case of food poisoning. The one dish we both share was the Pozole. If anyone else experienced this please post. What a horrible way to mess up Father's Day.

We went here before getting on the 15-odd hour flight to Sydney - an excellent tactic as if you approach buffets as gluttonously as I do (which you definitely should) you can avoid having to eat hellish plane and airport food!

Seafood - excellent giant shrimp.  Crab was ok but a little flavourless (I like how they pre-crack it for you though).  
Mexican - awesome street tacos (made to order).  Lovely fresh juices/iced teas.  Very friendly chefs!
Carvery - decent brisket and lovely wagyu slides.
Italian - lovely cured meats and cheeses.  Pumpkin gnocchi was pretty good.
Japanese - excellent nigiri (especially the tuna, which was very fresh), but not replenished as often as might be hoped.
Dessert - amazing - so many options and all delish!

I am not a fan of buffets. The last time I had a buffet was at the Wynn 5 years ago and it is where I compare all buffets to. Since all my food friends have been raving about Bacchanal Buffet, I decided to kiss my diet goodbye, loosen my belt and dive in to the stations of food. 

The seafood is impressive. There's Alaskan King crab legs, which can be steamed, oysters, oyster shooters, mussels, clams, lobster corn bisque and more. The made-to-order tacos were good, although the Mexican corn was bland. The pasta was tasty and they even have pho, ramen and udon noodles. 

The dessert station offers a wide variety of sweets. From mochi to gelato to chocolate-dipped strawberries to made-to-order crepes, there's something for everyone whether you like sweets or not.

Let me just preface by saying...I had DREAMS about this place. It's that good!!

I felt like a little kid in a candy store when I first stepped in here and didn't even know where to begin with the crazy large selection of food from Asian to Mexican to Italian..you name it!

I loved their sweet potato tots, steamed crab, Japanese ramen, dim sum...well I basically loved it all...Oh, and I loved the drink selection they had right by the fried food with fresh HORCHATA, pineapple juice, and many more in these cute, individual glass jars (it's the little things!)

And don't even get me started on the desserts! Ahh, these are the times I wish my stomach was bigger so I could try everything, but unfortunately, by the time I was eating desserts, my stomach felt like it was going to explode.  Still, from what I managed to stuff in my mouth before feeling sick, my favorites were the Black sesame mochi, sticky toffee ice cream, macarons, and build your own CREPES...my mouth is watering at the thought! 

The wait is reallyyyy long here, especially on the weekends (I know someone who waited 5 hours!) so try coming for an early lunch/dinner or be prepared to wait! I think you can give them your phone number, and go do your own thing, then they'll call you back when it's time so you don't have to stand in line the whole time which is a plus!

Even if you're not a fan of buffets or aren't too keen in spending $55 for one meal, you owe it to yourself to try to this place out once in your life...it's definitely an experience eating here!
My favorite buffet ever! I love the variety of food, the presentation is a lot nicer than other buffets, and the food is delicious

Came here yesterday for the New Year's buffet! It was about $71 per person. Unlimited alcoholic beverages such as mimosas, sangria, beer, etc. were $24.99 per person. 

We tried many different types of food. The seafood was fresh. There were fresh oysters, crab legs, sea snails, and shrimp cocktails. There was also a cooked seafood section that included paella, and an American food section that had fried chicken and waffles, tri-tip, and turkey. The Asian section had a mix of Japanese, Korean, and Chinese fare. There were soba noodles, sushi, kimchi, lobster, and bbq pork buns. The roasted duck was really good! The dessert section was really good. I tried the creme brulee, flan, and a matcha cake.

They now have you check in on the tablets, give you an estimated wait time (ours was about an hour) and give you a call when it's time for you to wait in line. We waited in the actual line for about another hour. Then they have you wait in another line to be seated. This line was about 30 minutes or so. Be prepared to wait! But there is a variety of foods to try and the service is good. This is part of the traveling experience.

Overrated, over priced and over hyped.

After a three year hiatus from Vegas and studying a variety of reviews, articles, status updates, tweets, and listening to chatter from those who enjoyed this majestic buffet I left unimpressed. Sure it looks cool, but I'm not paying for an architectural tour. 

Price point wise it's the highest. It's not top shelf quality and execution. This distinction belongs to Wynn, Wicked Spoon and even Bellagio. It might be worth it if they bring their price down. Additionally, it cost me $26.95 for my four year old.

When I think of any buffet I'm always partial to the carving station. To me, this is fundamental component of every good buffet. It's like when I test a great ice cream place I'm not falling for the gimmicks, bells, and whistles. I want to know how your vanilla tastes like. If it's a wedding, I don't care about your photo booth, how was your wedding cake. Well, this carving station fell short. Real short. The prime rib was extremely dry. Lacked salt and any kind of savory flavor. I even asked for an edge piece and it still lacked any depth. The brisket was a little better, but also dry too. The ribs were the best, good smoke ring.

Maybe if they didn't bother with the meat and cheese spread they could have put more effort in their "American" station. The Mexican station was also disappointing. The carnitas were very dry. The agua frescas were the only redeeming parts of that station.

The Asian stations, the desserts and the seafood station were probably it's best features, but for a bay area native I was not lured by their Asian offerings. If I wanted seafood I would have somewhere else. If they had a dessert buffet option price I would reconsider returning.
 
Quality, not quantity is what's lacking. I won't be endorsing it unless you have money to throw away or want to spend most of your time at the dessert station.

CREAM OF MUSHROOM SOUP!

I know. I know. There's no way someone is raving about the soup when there's crab legs, oysters, prime rib, American wagyu, bone marrow, lamb, gelato, creme brulee, etc. Even when there could be better soups like clam chowder or cioppino. But this unassuming and overlooked soup was my favorite dish at the Bacchanal.

Just try it. No lines or competition. There is something so pleasant about this dish that I hope I can replicate it and make it at home... Otherwise I may find myself dropping $60 for a bowl of soup.

Is this place better than Wicked Spoon? Probably.  But would I come back, probably not.  We came on a Tuesday night at 8:30pm and yes it took an hour.. just to enter.  The only time you should wait that long for food, is if they are handing it out for free. People talk about great service, ours was craptastic to say the least.  

I always believed you shouldn't pay gratuity up front, so that your waiter would be more inclined to work for their tip.  Having no cash for a tip after, I decided to leave an up front 20% tip ($20) to our server.  And sure enough we ended up with one, whose only responsibility mind you is to clear plates and make sure your drinks are full, who loved to disappear for 15 minutes at a time.  On one instance, my gf made eye contact with her and waved to her to come, she completely ignored her and walked away.  ??????  This may have been an anomale since it was my first time, but the 5 times I've been to Wicked Spoon, i've experienced above average service.  

Other than that.  The only disappointment, was that there was no bone marrow which is the only reason I would go to Wicked Spoon over this place, well plus it usually takes less than 10 minutes to be seated.

The Oysters were good, crab legs were salty from preservatives. theres was this white saucy shooter with salmon that was awesome. Brisket was salty. dolmades good.  tabouli was meh, wicked spoon's waaay better.  asian section here WAY better than wicked.  salad bar not so  much. menudo had NO tripe, wth.  deserts were real good, I would say tied with wicked.

Again at $51 per person, a bad first experience with our server and an hour+ wait time, i'd just go to Wicked Spoon if I really want to eat a buffet.  The selection here is BETTER don't get me wrong, but seriously, that wait time just to eat... 

PS:  right before you enter, there are two lines that go left and right.  THERE WAS NO SIGN to direct large parties to the right and smaller parties to the left.  My gf and I went right, and about halfway in, some lady with a camera tells us we were in the long line, which extended our wait time by another 10 minutes.  At $51 per person, you would think they would have enough money to make a sign.

Maybe that is the problem with high expectations...

I've heard for a few months now how I had to try the Bacchanal Buffet and how it was the best in Vegas.  I understand the days fo the $9.99 buffet are over and I have no issue shelling out $40-$50 for a premium buffet...but when I do so, I expect premium food and service.

Honestly, I didn't find the food to be spectacular, or at least enough so to make me forget about the horrible service.  There were many items I enjoyed throughout my many samplings.  Overall, I was just perplexed at time by the set up and extremely frustrated by the service.  Maybe someone can help me with this one.  You have a long line building for crab legs (rightfully so) but why put the drawn butter at the beginning of the line...with no cups or other dishes to hold said butter.  Should i just lather it on an empty plate?  Upon further review, perhaps the crab legs should have been the START of the line and the butter the end...this would also explain why lemons, tartar sauce, horseradish and cocktail sauce were AFTER the chilled shrimp.  If this is the case, then why isn't there someone directing traffic?  I mean it wouldn't hurt to have people using the buffet the way it was designed instead of lining up the wrong way and getting in the way of the staff trying to go in and out of the kitchen and dodging swinging doors and carts.  The lines were going completely backwards.  You'd expect a place dubbed as the best to operate like a well oiled machine.

Another perplexing thing is how the line to get in is so incredibly long to get in but then inside the place is half empty and seemingly understaffed.  I'm looking around at waiters standing around, managers setting tables, dirty tables, and I can't get a drink order filled.  Our original waitress disappeared for awhile after serving us initially before I spotted her standing around doing nothing in another section.  I asked two different people and waited roughly 20 minutes for a drink towards the tail end of the meal before we decided to get up and leave.  This was all after we sat around for 10 minutes before a waitress even came by to take the first drink order.  Two beverages in 60+ minutes and nobody walking around filling up waters seems a bit unacceptable.  In addition, nobody came by to clear used dishes and glasses until we were almost forced to turn around and put them on an empty table just to make room.  I mean this seems like Buffet 101 type stuff to me...when people get up to get another plate, you clear the previous plate and/or bring a drink.  I don't know if we caught them at a bad day/time but $52 and a 30 minute wait is a bit too steep for me to run back and find out, especially with other good options down the street.  When comparing to Wicked Spoon in terms of price, food, and service, I would choose Wicked Spoon every time.

This buffet lacks alot of variety and the food is good and all but definitely not worth the price. The staff is very kind and courteous and the wait is not too long but in my opinion there are better options that are much cheaper

Friday Morning "Breakfast" 7:40am I waited 5 mins..The wait at 9:00am when exiting looked like a 10 min wait..Breakfast was 33.52..At 33.52 Do it once and realize you've spent to much on an Over-rated Buffet and move on with Life..With in the Last 10 month's I have tried The Wynn, Wicked Spoon and Bacchanal..I have tried 5 other Strip Buffets also in the past 3 years..And Wicked Spoon is the Best Breakfast Buffet..At Bacchanal, I liked the fried Chicken and the Beef Dish "Machaca"..Stone Crab was offered Chilled and I tried that for the first time and Liked that also..Everything else was just Ok..

This is the greatest buffet I have ever been to.  The only reason Bacchanal Buffet doesn't get 5 stars is because it's so expensive.
I probably wouldn't go again because of the price ($37 for lunch, $52 for dinner) but I am glad that I went once.  If you're REALLY hungry and you've saved up, splurge on Bacchanal Buffet.

2nd time here, this buffet is on the top! Shrimp and Grits, Oyster shooters, crab legs, and check this out, Sinigang too! Yup! Street tacos! Bam! Mochi ice cream too!
I usually come around 2 so I can pay for lunch, and get the dinner spread at 3 pm!

Worst buffet experience ever!

Came here on Christmas day with my family. We registered at 3 and got in at 6 pm. As you would think this is rated the best buffet in LV, it should worth the wait, right? Wrong! I've asked the lady at front desk and make sure they serve King Crab legs before we checked in. But later found out they do not serve King Crab at all. I asked the seafood section they told me to check with Italian section. I asked Italian section they sent me back to seafood section. If you don't have it, just tell me you guys are too cheap to serve King Crab, please don't lie to me.

I tried to find white fish and found they only have salmon. I was looking for sushi and found non of them were eatable. I thought I should at least find tons of fruit at this price point. Wrong again, fruit were very limited. We've tried all the food there and only found disappointment. I think my neighborhood's $11 buffet is better than this.

I concluded my experience on this trip. Any buffet place crowded with tourists (Wicked Spoon, Wynn...etc). Don't get in there. They will serve you second grade food. Shame on you, Vegas! I miss the old day soooooo much!!!

If you are looking for quality buffet in Vegas. Don't go for buffet places but go Sunday Brunch (Mozen, Sterling, Fountain...) and get your money worth.

The one star is for the decor.

So this place is the buffet in Caesars palace. I went for the weekend of Christmas. Now my main gripe with this place is it's terribly organized until you sit down. You "register" by putting a name and number in and it gives you a ticket saying come back (in 3 hours) at a certain time and check in. When you come back and check in you are simply put into yet another line and made to wait another 1.5 hours. What is the point of registering and giving your number? Would it be so difficult to send a text saying your table will be ready in 30 minutes(approx) please arrive no more than 15 minutes before said time. I didn't come to Vegas to wait in lines all day. The food was good, but king crab was on the menu, and I saw some "platinum and 7 stars" eating it, but we were relegated to the less expensive snow crab. This place could be amazing if they fix the wait issue. Even the staff thinks it's dumb. Get it together CAESARS!

Hands down one of the best buffets I've had in Vegas thus far! The lines for this place is ridiculous but now they seem to have a more organized system. You come check in and get a receipt with a return time on it. Come back by that time and wait in a slightly smaller line to pay for your meal and be seated.

They have a large variety of food selections. What particularly stood out for me is the quality in each of them. Every single thing I tasted was quite good or at least tasted what it should be like, unlike other buffets where they would be great in one thing and lack in another department. They have one of the best dim sums I've ever tried and their ramen was surprisingly tasty for a buffet-styled ramen. They have all sorts of different drinks including tamarind and horchata. I love horchata so I was so pleased! Their tacos were also amazing. I've tried almost everything they had there. It's amazing, you have to go experience for yourself!

I believe it's $30 for lunch and $60 for dinner. I can't remember the exact prices. Their dinner time starts at 3pm, so if you come around 2:30pm you can pay for the lunch price yet still be able to get dinner selections! :)

Was not impressed. Stopped here because I was too lazy to make it over to Wicked Spoon. Crazy expensive buffet, very little was decent-tasting. Sure, huge selection, but not well-done. Had breakfast at the Bellagio buffet the next day and it seemed quite a bit better.
Best buffet in Vegas no doubt! Friday lunch was 35$ a person so that's obviously pricey but all the food was delicious! The tacos and brisket are a must!!

An explosion of live cooking stations (including a fresh Ramen station, yes!), a huge variety of great food you don't see at other buffets, a relaxed atmosphere that almost feels like you're eating in your living room (if your living room happens to be enormous)... Caesars set out to redefine the game with their new, $10 million Bacchanal Buffet, and they pulled it off. This is the best buffet in Las Vegas.

My friend and I were seated near the Asian food, and we loaded up our first plates with Dim Sum style Chinese specialties, Ramen, and Sushi. I moved on next to the Mexican section, which featured absolutely excellent and perfectly moist Carnitas. The Pizza was great as well, with excellent and diverse toppings that you wouldn't normally expect. Even the cheese and meat board were a cut above the rest. Sliced Prime meats and Oysters were fresh and delicious as well. Fresh squeezed Orange and Carrot Juices served in individual carafes was yet another nice touch.

The dessert section kept the goodness going, with fresh Ice Creams served in Chocolate dipped cones and a Crepe station. The whole experience was incredibly impressive, and $21 for breakfast was completely reasonable.

I'd read a bunch of hype before I visited The Bacchanal Buffet, but Caesars delivered and then some. I will be back as soon as I can. Best buffet in Las Vegas!

The food is ok, not the best, but the wait is horrible, I waited for more than 3 hours even though I registered as I have been instructed to do, it is a wait following another wait to pay and then another wait to be seated, it is not the food you eat and die !!!!! Definitely I will never repeat it

Best buffet ever....I'm a local and I like to indulge in great food I am a chef myself but because of back issues I can no longer work in a kitchen...but eating here reminds me of all the luxury and beauty and effort Vegas has to offer...went there for brunch and got authentic street tacos...deviled eggs...but I wish they didnt put a piece of bacon on them all it's pretty but I dont eat pork...the seafood is amazing the coffee is great the dessert bar to die for the beef ribs I might've cried eating it was so good....I wish I could afford to go back

It does not get any better than this.  Pricy?  Of course. Worth it?  Oh yes. The gold standard of Vegas buffets. They say over 500 items, many cooked to order. The dessert area is sinfulll.  Hint: Show up about 10:15/10:30, get the breakfast price and enjoy lunch as they bring it out. Hint2: If you are drinking get the pre-pay. Hint3: Add a tip when you pay, you will get seated quicker. Ive heard they kick you out after 2 hours but I have never seen it happen. As if you could eat any more after 2 hours anyway.

Definitely the largest buffet I have every been to! The selection was AMAZING - they have everything you can think of (all kinds of meat, seafood, dim sum, tacos, fresh squeezed juices, and more). But unfortunately, the quality of the food did not live up to the number of options. There were some dishes that were well-made, and the number of choices made it easy to find things that each of us enjoyed eating, but for the most part, everything was just mediocre. 

The service was quite good though; we had our drink orders taken immediately after getting seated and our plates were continuously cleared throughout our meal. However, the long wait time to enter the buffet was paired with a long wait time for food items inside the buffet. Upon several occasions of reaching the front of the long lines, I was informed that they no longer had the item(s) that I was waiting for. Kind of a disappointment! However, it seemed as though other items were constantly being replenished so perhaps the popular items are put out more frequently.

The overall experience was nice though, as the interior decor was beautiful and ambiance was peaceful. Dishes were also extremely well-presented! Total for lunch on a weekday (including tax/gratuity) came out to approximately $50. Definitely not something I would spend on an average meal, but I guess it was worth the experience this one time. Probably would not come back with the dozens of other places to eat in Vegas for much cheaper!
Best buffet on the strip, and I have tried most of them. The food quality is exceptional and there are lots of options.

Meh, overrated. We went here because of all the hoopla surrounding it. I could take it or leave it. First of all, you check in at the kiosk and still wait on line. I think if you buy a buffet pass, your on an express line. Long line for the crab legs/seafood. It wasn't anything special about this buffet except it was pricier than most.

My wife and I arrived in town and thought we would try a buffet. I am a fan of buffets but she is not, however she is very loving and accommodates me. Needless to say she is a tough buffet selector.

We went to Yelp, always a great source of information, and looked for suggestions and good reviews on Las Vegas buffets. We discovered Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars. The reviews about the lines are true but we got there early around 5 PM on a Sunday. We were seated directly. By 5:30 the line to get in wound around the ropes and when we left an hour and a half later it had not gotten any better (surprise). 

I do have to say, and my wife would agree, the food was excellent.  The prime rib was cooked perfectly, very tender and the lamb to the best I have ever had. There was so much food selection to choose from I never made it to the seafood area.  But the clam chowder was also one of the best I have ever tasted. She had fried chicken and raved about the scalloped potatoes. She also gave a thumbs up on the prime rib and St. Louis ribs. However, the line at the carving station was insane. By 5:45 there must have been 40+ people waiting and it was NOT move very fast. Only one carver and she could not handle the flow. For $50 bucks/person and at Caesars this is not what I would have expected. We could see frustration on the faces of the people in line. I heard one guy who wanted St. Louis ribs say give him the whole rack, as he was not standing in this line again. My wife and I did a similar thing and asked for a very THICK (2in) cut of prime rib as we too did not what to run the gauntlet a second time. 

I do have to say the service was great. Jeff went out of his way to see we were taken care of and provided excellent helping serve up all of our requests. 

I asked my wife, the non-buffet goer would you go back and she said a resounding "yes". I will agree.

Viva Las Vegas! The city of glitz and glam, money, hot women, entertainment, partying, and endless indulgence of food. Bacchanal Buffet located in Caesars Palace offers the best spread of food in the desert. 

I'm talking about quality dishes from appetizers, entrees, to desserts and all for a reasonable entry fee of $37 for a weekday lunch. If you're down for some bubbly, you can order complimentary mimosas too!

In the past three years, I've never had a Vegas trip without dining at Bacchanal. It's the perfect Monday Lunch after a weekend full of partying! 

Quick Tips:
+Party of 6 or more? There is a separate line to get seated faster! We were seated within 45 min rather than the estimated time of wait 120 min for 2 groups of 5 people. 
+Save $1 by using your Rewards Card
+Skip the pizza and taco stations and go for the good stuff, Prime rib, dim sum, sushi, shrimp cocktail, seafood, and chef specials
+I can't stress this enough, save room for dessert. This has to be my favorite part of the buffet. From cookies, pastries, cakes, crepes, fruit, chocolate, cupcakes, ice cream to snowcones, Bacchanal has it all. 
+Finish off your meal with some hot jasmine tea to keep your tummy happy as can be.

Happy eating everyone!

Not ok! This Buffet has a lot of hype around it, but let me tell you , skip the whole thing.  There are a ton of variety, but the quality is very much lacking.  For 70 a person after tax, I expect the food to be just as amazing as a 4 star restaurant, well it was not!
 Seafood was flavorless and watery, oysters had tons of dirt and sediment. Asian food was oily and too sweet.  Waygu beef had no flavor.  The waiter came over once to give us drinks and that was it.

Do your stomach a favor and skip the buffet for a nice sit down restaurant.  But if you would rather eat 6 plates of crap vs 1 plate of amazingness, then this is your place. 

I would NEVER go back and would NEVER recommend this place, in fact I would actively discourage people to go.
Waited two hours to get in. Paid over $70 per person. Nothing tasted exceptionally good. Many of the food especially the crab was too salty. Dissatisfied. Not worth the money.

We have dined at this buffet several times but yesterday was the first time this trip to Las Vegas.  It is still our favorite but has slipped by one star since the last visit in Janurary.  First of all the place is beginning to look shabby and worn.  When I sat at the table my butt almost hit the floor because the springs in the chair were broken.  The carpet in the dining area is stained and pretty dirty, same with the chair upholstery.  Not what one would expect from an upscale eatery.  The food and service are still good but some items have disappeared since our last visit, especially on the dessert bar.  Just has the feel of being cheapened up a bit.   Price hasn't gone down though.

The mother of all buffets on the strip. For $42, we definitely got our money's worth!

The line was long so it helped that my friend is a  diamond member so we were able to by pass the line to get in. In just a few minutes we were seated and we got a table right in front of the buffet so we didn't have very far to walk!

The selection of food available is unbelievable. We got there to have some breakfast but they were switching over to lunch so that was a bonus for us. They definitely have something for everyone. My favorite was the seafood especially the salmon. I'm not big on crab legs unless it's King cab legs. 

Save some room in your tummy for the desserts here, it's to die for. They have everything from ice cream to dessert crepes.

This place is supposed to be one of the best buffets in Vegas. If that's the case, then buffets are failing in the "being tasty" department. Granted, they had more food selections than most buffets but everything was either dry, soggy, or bland. Nothing really stands out as being exceptionally tasty. This is only a review of the brunch buffet, but for $50pp, you'd think they'd throw in something that you can say, "this is worth it". Tragic.

WOW once again Yelp you didn't let us down. The food was Amazing. The staff friendly. The background music on point. No one should leave hungry or waiting more variety. The only reason I gave it 4 stars and not 5 is price. Wow expensive.

AMAZING!
May I start by saying I HATE BUFFETS! They are overpriced and mediocre at best! But so many people hyped this place up I just had to give the BUFFET scene one more try.
We were trying to get out of town and they said it was an hr wait...i wasn't sure, especially at 40 bucks a head for lunch...but we went ahead.
It only took about 40 minutes to get in.
The tables you're  sat at surprisingly have these very cushioned chairs, which just seemed different but so comfy and luxurious!
There are several stations:
Seafood (crab, shrimp, mussels, ceviche)

American (potatoes/gravy, mac n cheese, carving station, fried chicken and fries,  sweet potato fries)

Mexican (made to order street tacos,  refried beans, meats, tortilla soup)

Italian (scalloped potatoes, meatballs, pasta salads, caprese, 3 or 4 pizzas, salami and various cured meats, cheeses, about 4 different kinds, including brie)

Salads (tofu, Japanese, build your own)

Asian ( rice, dim sum, egg rolls, sushi, several soups including miso, and hot and sour)

Dessert bar (approx 15 kinds of Gelato,  plus a donut that you can fill with Gelato and the they toast it up some how, about 5 different cookies, cheesecake, cake pops, cupcakes, tiramisu cups, creme brulee, fruit of all kinds, made to order crepes with all sorts of toppings)
And of course there was so much more, this is just what I recall!
Your soft drinks and juices are included then they also have all you can drink mimosa, beer (miller light or newcastle), or wine (choose one for $22 and you get to keep the caesars engraved glass)

My favorite menu items: 

the shrimp was awesome, with cocktail sauce, lemon, and real horseradish.  

Their pizza was really good

Miso soup

Creme brulee

I think my favorite though: made to order crepe.  It was amazing I had chocolate sauce and real whipped cream on it and it was just right, (and not insanely sweet like we had the night before at rainforest cafe with fake cool whip ...gross)

We WILL go back...if vegas wasn't a 16 hr drive I'd be there for dinner tonight as well!

And if you are thinking it's really expensive...every other meal we had in Vegas for 2 adults and a toddler was the same cost and not all you can eat.   And our 1.5 yr old ate for free! Under 4 I believe was free! So bring the family!

Pricey and nothing special. I mean it is a buffet so I wasn't expecting a magical experience but warm food would be a plus. Some dishes were nearly room temperature. I will say the staff was very friendly and attentive.

The price is only worth it if you've never been here.
Otherwise the long long wait by no means justifies the price.
The food is alright not as amazing as you'd expect from the well regarded buffet.
The service is pretty good once seated but 
It's just basically an overpriced golden corral.
The Cosmo buffet is worth the wait/price over this.

This place was pretty good. It is the only place that will heat up your crab legs. I went here on a Monday night and the wait was 2 hours. It was worth it, but the buffet at the Wynn is pretty good as well. This place has many varieties of food. From authentic Chinese food to authentic Mexican food. This place did not disappoint.

Finally I had the chance to try one of Vegas' most infamous buffets. I was honestly hesitant to try this place out at first because I've been reading all about the long wait time and the long lines. However,  we arrived a little before 11:30am on a Friday (before 4th of July weekend btw) and we were only in line for less than 10 minutes. We were seated pretty quickly. The staff was very attentive, everything was very clean & the food was very fresh. I love their dessert bar (thanks to my huge sweet tooth). My one and only regret is that my stomach wasn't big enough to try everything at this buffet. (I had to skip the pizza area). All in all,  if you've never tried this place out,  you need to visit them at least once- you will not regret it.
