It appears to be a great selection, but for the price I'll go the Wicked Spoon every time from now on. Sand in all the seafood, the lamb chops and pistachio gelato saved the meal. Seriously don't for the seafood. My wife was nauseous after the clams. 

The atmosphere and gelato is remarkable.

One of the better buffets on the strip.

There were some boring/normal dishes, but there were also some unique dishes.  Delicately prepared, and presented in small bites.

The problem with this place is the MASSIVE wait to get in. it's unbelievable really how bad the wait is.

If you can get a pass or get past the line, it's a good place to eat.  Remember tho, it's still a buffet.

If I had to sum this buffet up in one word, it would be disappointing.  I definitely wouldn't say it was better than the Wicked Spoon...Hubby's  fav of smoked salmon capers and red onion was disappointing...the fish was gamey, and when capers and red onion can't cover it, that's saying something right there.  The meat station had a good variety of offerings, but most lacked flavor...sole exception was the Bacon, which was on point.  As for the seafood, the crab was too hard to eat without the appropriate fork (small seafood)., but again lacking flavor, it wasn't worth the effort.  On the bright side, the Shrimp were colossal and delish, nothing fishy here.  Overall, most items were bland or flavorless.  Bottomless mimosas for $7.00 was a winner!  Coffee was wonderful.  The Creme brûlée, is my pick for the tastiest item offered at brunch today, but by far and away, the BEST THING today was the service.  Our waitress Maricella was FABULOUS !!! Our glasses were rarely empty and if we asked for it, we had it in seconds!!!  Kudos to Ms. M.
Im way too full. Oysters didn't taste fresh. They were kind of dried. Everything is just okay. If you want good food, not the place.

After my boyfriend's and my canyon adventure trip we completed covering all 5 of Utah's famous canyon national parks and closing it up with the Grand Canyon and Hoover dam we were really looking forward to a nice dinner with impeccably made food.  

We went early around 5 or 6 and it was a good thing that we did because this buffet gets crowded fast!!  The line went by quickly and we were even offered to have our picture taken at the front of the buffet.  We sure weren't dressed for a nice picture to be taken but we did and then proceeded to order the picture later that evening, what better way to remember a great dinner at an amazing buffet than with a professional picture taken?  

We were seated in the wood themed seating area towards the back but it had a sense of peace in this area.  I liked that each part of the large restaurant had a theme going on which I can't really describe at this moment in detail but I assure you it certainly feels like a different experience in each part.  Our waitress was very attentive and sweet and though I was freezing where we sat my order of tea, which is not just any old tea by the way, helped bunches.  I love that this buffet goes the extra mile in taking care of guests.  My tea was certainly nothing I would find down the grocery aisle, in my opinion, and it came with my very own sealed itty bitty honey jar.  How sweet and cute is that?  I was amazed just by the tea.  

We started off from the Asian food section way in the back and worked our way up having a separate plate for the cut in half crab legs of course.  Everything was top notch and what I noticed on the other side of the counter was how well the employees worked together.  Coming from a food & beverage background it says a lot when the back end runs as smoothly as it does on the front end.  From what I saw  it seems that they've got a good team going on as far as who preps the food.   

The meat section was really crowded but that's where the bottled juices were, I loved these!! I grabbed the guava juice and it tasted just as good as I remember it does, guava juice is hard to come by in Nebraska!! The crab legs were probably my favorite next to the delicious desserts!  The next time I'm here I'd like to try the dessert first just so I have enough room in my stomach to try a piece of almost everything.  It's hard to try every type of food you want to at a buffet because everything looks good and at this buffet it certainly tastes good.  I highly recommend any of the asian dishes, the crab legs, and the Italian.  My boyfriend said his lamb was good and of course the desserts.  

This dinner, though pricey, was the perfect treat after a 5 day canyon adventure trip through Utah and Arizona!

Dinner is about $50 a person. The variety is endless. The Asian section is the best I have ever seen at a buffet, as well as the seafood section which had crab legs, oyters, clams, shrimp, and crawfish. Come hungry.

This is not your typical buffet. Most buffets I've ever been to consist of a lot of different choices that you grab and put on your plate, and because you need to make room for only the best tasting items, if you try something that is just okay or worse, you don't eat it. EVERY SINGLE food/dessert item is the best I had ever tried! Absolutely worth the money!

So this place is new, eh?  Sounds promising...

Sadly, I was disappointed in the food.  
The prime rib was just okay, it wasn't tender, but it wasn't rough either.
The Chinese food was not that great.  When you have the har gow dumpling skin overcooked, it falls apart easily and tastes soggy.
Sushi?  Standard buffet fare... skip it.
I was looking forward for their Mexican and Italian food, but they also disappointed me.  The Italian food was alright, but nothing stood out.  The Mexican food was a little too salty.  

So what did taste good here?
The sausages and dessert.  No, really, that was it.  :l

If you want atmosphere, sure, stop by.  Otherwise, I suggest you skip this.

This was our second time here and we had family visiting from Europe. We went for dinner and the line was very long, but the wait wasn't too bad. It was well worth it by the time we had the food. OMG!! Where to start! 

Let me start off my husband and brother in law were hysterical about the meats, they kept running back and forth for the brisket and sausages. Lol. The brisket literally was the moistest I've ever had and melted in your mouth, it was delicious.

Everything we tried was very good, and good quality, we just wanted more room in our tummies!

Den mest SINDSSYGE buffet jeg nogensinde har spist på!? Vi var seks mennesker, og fordi vi var så mange kom vi i en seperat kø, som ikke var særlig lang - vi ventede derfor ikke længe på at få et bord. Man betaler før man går ind (ca $40/person, som inkluderer alt mad og drikkevarer). Prisen er måske lidt dyr ift hvad ellers ville betale for at gå ud og spise et almindeligt sted (måske mere ala $10-15/person, men dette er virkelig pengene værd!!). Vi spiste kl 11-13 (man kan være der 2 timer), og spiste derfor nærmest for hele dagen i ét måltid. Buffeten bugner af alt hvad hjertet begærer; over 300 forskellige retter, 70 dessert-items (inkl en masse sukkerfrie muligheder), 9 forskellige spændende gelatos, friskpressede juicer, hummer og skaldyr, sushi, pizza, brød, osv osv osv. Det er ikke bare en ordinær buffet, hvor det er kvantitet over kvalitet - NEJ - her var der virkelig kvalitet over maden, som var serveret i små portioner på meget indbydende måder. Tjenerne var gode til at rydde af bordet, når man var færdig med sin tallerken, og serverede kaffe når man spurgte.
Det er en god ide at komme lige mellem morgenmad og frokost ligesom vi gjorde, da man på den måde først får prøvet deres morgenbuffet, og når det så bliver frokosttid, kan man gå i krig med frokostbuffeten.
Dette sted kan jeg virkelig anbefale - ligger i Cesar's Palace, hvilket også er et flot hotel.

Wow! It was a huge disappointing experience at this overrated & overpriced buffet!!!

We were there on 7/3/16 and it was special higher price on that day!!! Kids:$29.99 and adults $69.99 + tax & tips ..:

All the namely famous items were terrible!!!

The roast beef were dried.
The roasted ducks were bad
No caviar 
The slider beef were dried; In/out burgers were better
The macaroons are not better than the frozen ones from TJ
The selection is ordinary 
Hardly any fruits or vegetables 
The facility is old :(
Not sure what else to say but not
To go there...

The only decent item was the creme
Brûlée... But certainly not for $70 to eat that:(((

Some serious improvement needed!!!

Best buffet on the strip. The sheer variety is just phenomenal. Every dish is made fresh and hot. They already have the king crab legs sliced open for you. The sweet potato nuggets are placed in little wire containers that stay warm on the hot plate. Everything is presented so nicely, especially the desserts. You get what you pay for!! 

Only drawback is the wait. Make sure to get a ticket 3-4 hours in advance and be nearby in case they alert you early!
Early morning breakfast Buffett! Excellent food excellent service... great price... seafood... standard breakfast fare...you name it!

Buffets in Vegas, how cliché is it? You'll never know how buffets really are in Vegas unless you take the time to find reviews online. As of recently Caesar's Palace recently renovated and reopened their buffet with a whole new outlook.

What you need to know,
Dining plans, it is currently one of the busiest buffets in Vegas right now. If you plan on getting a good meal, this is it. Make sure you get there at least an hour to an hour and a half before you plan on dining. The line can be a ridiculous but well worth the wait. Diamond member? No waiting here just take the exclusive line and you're in! (open 7-10pm)

What's the cost?
Breakfast ~$19
Lunch ~$25
Dinner ~$35
Buffets of Buffets ~$50 (24 hour window of eating!)

How's the food?
Phenomenal, by far the best buffet I've had in my life...so far. There is everything from oysters to ramen. I dined for at least two hours to try to get a taste of each portion. Now you may be a little unease that the portions are small but don't be, it's a buffet!

Lets start with some meat. The lamb chop was great, I'm not a big fan but the flavor came together very well. The brisket was a melt in your mouth type of meat, it was so tender that you could sit there and eat it all day. Prime rib for some may be a little rare but the juices made the ribs so rich and tender it was hard to set aside.

Seafood? I didn't have a chance to try much (lines were exceptionally long) but it wasn't the best in my opinion. Crab legs were a little too salty but the good thing is, you don't have to worry about making a mess from cracking shells. The shrimp with cocktail sauce was by far the best shrimp I've had. Large pieces of shrimp with an excellent cocktail sauce beats it all. Now there was a shrimp and grits dish, it had a creamy texture right before you dive into the grits (not my favorite) but again, worth the taste. Lobster bacon cheddar soup, the title itself sounds awesome. Caesar does not hold back on their seafood, you will get a decent amount of lobster in the soup and the bacon just makes it awesome. Take a stab at their seafood! (Sushi is available too but it's too filling for me to have at a buffet)

Taste of Asia? Well, being Chinese/ Vietnamese myself, I'm not a big fan of the Asian cuisine within buffets. I only had the chance to try one thing. It was the ramen, it was good. Definitely not too ramen, folks. The noodles are cooked right before you and you're given a small but a filling bowl. Right after you get your bowl you're given directions to head to the condiments bar with onions, cilantro, jalepens, green onions, and various sauces to add. Raines was all I had but there was an open variety of Chinese Dim Sum dumplings, sushi, noodles, stir fry, and all the little things.

Dessert? Who has room for dessert when it comes to buffets? I certainly don't but I had to indulge. There was everything from macaroons to soufflé to gelato. It's every kids dream to walk around an island bar where there was desserts and pastries everywhere. I'll let you take that review on yourselves when you get there.

Biggest disappointment on our entire trip. Everything is so salty and/or has less than stellar taste. Some things were downright bad. The saddest thing was the quality of the seafood. I've had better at a Golden Corral ( and I don't like Golden Corral) . Service also took a long time to refill our empty drinks. Then the drink machine for my tea broke so I went most of the meal without a beverage. Only highlight: the desserts are pretty. At $56 per person, we definitely had buyer's remorse.

They have EVERYTHING. And more! The king crab legs are great especially when hot! Suckling pig crispy in the outside tender on the inside, prime rib melts in your mouth and the Asian section was very fresh and tasty, the assorted dim sum to the pho to the sushi everything was in point! Then! The dessert section came ! Crepes are fresh made and multiple selection of gelatos cakes and pastries, Creme bruleee was the best!

Wow, their selection is HUGE. There is so much to choose from, I don't know where to begin. There's even an entire taco bar and meat carving station. Pretty cool!

I was able to make it in just before dinner started on a Saturday. So I was able to pay brunch price ($8 cheaper than dinner) but get dinner items ;) Surprisingly, the wait wasn't long at all - maybe 10-15 mins? But my group did go at an odd hour (just before 3pm, which is when dinner begins).

Standouts were the truffle gnocchi (delicious truffle flavor!!) and the prime rib (tender and juicy). The eggplant tofu from the Chinese section was surprisingly good, too. As for desserts, the creme brûlée was my favorite!

Everything else I tried was decent, but not noteworthy. The pork belly was way too salty. The sushi was pretty average.

Next time I'd actually like to try their brunch/lunch items haha.

Been here on Friday dinner time and I knew we will have to pay the weekend price. I was hesitate to check in because of their high price and how the restaurant so crowded full of tours and walk-in, but we did check in and the staff ring my rewards and am so glad our meals were full cover by my rewards credit. I only been using the membership card for less than two years and I guess it paid off. 
Back to the restaurant: it made me enjoy my food more since it's free and with priority line and reserved table made us feel really special. I would be back again after I've got enough rewards. Lots of food option and very tasty. Downside: too crowded, certain line way too long to wait. Overall I like it.

We went here for the dinner buffet. Super expensive, $70 per person. The buffet just keeps going! An extravagant selection of fresh seafood, soups, bread, pasta, Chinese, adorbs and more! My favorite was the mini specialized items in the cups and the soup. Now, the dessert is what really impressed me! I wish I saw it first! It was like desert heaven and entire island in the middle for a variety of traditional, foreign, and health conscious desserts. Also they have made to order crepes which I missed the first round. The gelato and crepes are both things that are not seen, and need to be asked for. I really regret not eating dessert first! The main dishes were alright too. This place was actually recommend by our uber driver as one of the best buffets in Vegas. I would come here again just for the dessert!
Excellent customer service.  Food is fresh.  Restaurant is clean.  So many different choices.

Like another poster said. I'm feeling stupid for paying double their normal buffet price just because it is Christmas. This buffet is robbing people cause they know they can get away with it. 

Oh if that's not enough, try the 2 hour wait and the most popular items like crabs running out all the time.
Talking about a dinner, Caesar Palace is the best. BUT, the DESERT in Bellagio is the best!!!!!!

Last time I came here they ran out of silverware. Happened again. We paid $20 per person to cut in line. The wait is 90 minutes naturally. By paying to cut we wait 10 minutes. The lines are just way too long to get to the sea food. Everything is pretty solid. I think Wynn, Aria, Bellagio, this place, and wicked spoon are all the same. Also with any popular place, your hot food is guaranteed to be cold.

Bacchanal is better than Wicked Spoon

I came here twice within a 48 hour period, not because its the best tasting food in vegas, but because its the best buffet in Vegas!

When it comes to buffet i typically hate them blah blah blah, so for me to come here twice its says something about buffets. I came here during two different times, once during the transition time (2PM) and the second time was during dinner. The transition time is best value time because they are transitioning from lunch to dinner, but you pay the lunch price. Lunch is $35 while dinner is $50. I was hoping that the dinner menu was going to be completely different, but it wasn't. 

Im not going to list everything i tasted there, but i will say that they offer a vast selections of cuisines from east to west parts of the globe. I was surprise that their dim sum was enjoyable (not the best) but great to there. The desserts were also a treat! The apple cobbler and expresso gelato being my favorite. 

This has been my best buffet experience yet. If you pay $35 during the transition hours - its the best value in vegas. If you go during dinner, $50 will get you the best buffet.

Good golly, I love writing positive review updates. 

My first experience at Bacchanal last winter was pretty lackluster. The breakfast items were nearly cold, there was no spoon in the rice cooker, and I just didn't dig it.

I went back tonight for dinner and--Holy Macaroni!--it was a huge improvement. NOW I understand what the raves are about. Bacchanal may even bump Wynn's Buffet from my #1 spot. Maybe.

Some specifics:

The first thing I noticed was that the piles and piles of shelled shrimp were beautifully sized and looked freshly cooked. If there's one disgusting thing I see again and again at buffets, it's limp, flavorless, pasty, waterlogged shrimp sitting on half-melted ice. Not here. Not today. Bacchanal's shrimps were absolutely perfect. 

The carving station was literally STACKED with piles of various meats ready to be served. Piles of freshly-smoked chicken. House made sausages. A huge roast beef. Now, get this: As I eyed the prime rib, I asked the carver if he had an end cut available. Lawd have mercy, do I loves the end cuts! He looked at the piece he was working on and said, "not on this one. Somebody got to them already." Then, without missing a beat, he put his fork in one of the other 5 prime ribs at the station and cut off a beautiful end piece just for me. Now THAT'S five star service, my friends.

Delicious barbacoa at the Mexican station. Tasty Kung Pao chicken in the Asian area.

But.
There.
Is.
One.
Thing.

Once again tonight, there was no spoon in the rice cooker!  Just like on my initial visit. I couldn't believe it. So, again, I drafted a nearby soup spoon for serving purposes. Crazy.

Do yourself a favor. Hit up Bacchanal. And consider going during off-peak times. Maybe 3pm to 4:30pm for dinner. There's no line, the dining room is not cramped, and you can get around the serving areas with ease.  Oh, please remember, Bacchanal is BYORCS (Bring Your Own Rice Cooker Spoon).

Let's cut right to the chase, this is the buffet of buffets. save up yo lunch money, starve yourself for a day, and get in line early because its worth it.

at first i thought okay this is over rated, but then when i had another buffet in vegas and thought about the slew of buffets ive had in my day...nahh...this one is great.

none the less the choices upon choices you get, everything is pretty damn fresh. dont get me wrong, a few things tasted funky, but over all the flavors were on point, and things tasted great. $75 for the buffet dinner and the unlimited drink package.

sorry gotta be a debbie downer, but a 2 hour limit isnt fair!

Starting off with the good...huge selection of food. We came on a Saturday night. King crab, snow crab, sushi, ramen, prime rib, brisket, sausage, charcuterie, salad blah, dessert; the crepes were amazing. Bigger selection than what I can remember at the wicked spoon. 

I was disappointed with the crawfish, the seafood wasn't as good as I thought it would be, the raw oysters weren't great quality but I get it, we're in a desert. Rock crab was ok and the King crab surprisingly wasn't as good either... And it was cut in half overall though it was very good the best buffet I've been to here in Vegas!!!!. The price is steep though and the wait is long but definitely worth a visit.

Crab legs were good. Buffet was strong. 
Pricey, so make sure you are ready to eat. Wifey doesn't eat a lot, so she says it was overpriced. I ate mostly seafood so I got my money worth. 

Did to say we did...
This is one of the best buffets in Las Vegas ! The food is fresh and they have a variety of different foods .. the wait is long but totally worth it !

I can't complain about the price as a friend treated us so it was all good. 

There was a wait, but this was for dinner and I am guessing it is always packed like this. Once we got it, it was a breeze to get our food and there are a lot of options. If you love seafood, you will love this place as there is seafood galore. I am not much of a seafood fan, but I was satisfied with what I ate and the quality of the food.
Awesome food, beautiful venue , great staff must try when in town . Great sea food and king crab .
Words cannot describe how I feel about this delicious buffet so great huge variety and they never disappoint you. You may want to spend a few hours there breathing before your next meal

Amazing... The champagne brunch is to die for and is totally worth more then they charge... over 500 items... they even have Dim Sum there and everything is prepared fresh at the counter it's served at.... save room for dessert though because even that is amazing...

Despite the high price and long lines, bacchanal is definitely the best out of all of the other buffets located inside the vegas hotels. The selection here is huge, and I remember every single food item being pretty good from each section. They have a pretty good selection of seafood compared to other vegas buffets, and their asian selection even has japanese ramen, pho, and udon which is great for a hangover (considering pho at TI is like $15 & chinatown is just super far if you're hungover...)!

This place is a toss up with Wicked Spoon as my current go to buffet. Wicket spoon has much better desserts but this place seems more consistent and more variety. This is located in the Cesears Palace. We went on a weekday lunch for $30 each. I've heard on weekends when it is busy that they charge people $20 for express entrance, really? is this a club?!

Anyways, the food is pretty amazing, they have different ethnicities and the quality is really there. The desserts is decent too, they have mochi and ice cream, just not as much cakes and stuff compared to other buffets. Most people seem to go for the crabs but their sea food department isn't that great.

The best buffet on the strip!  If there is only buffet you wait in line for, make it Bacchanal.

Phenomenal service, quality and quantity.  The buffet was fully stocked and carefully watched.  The food was fresh and perfect.  I am coming back this weekend so I will update with my favorites.

Best buffet I've ever experienced! The food selections were incredible and delicious! They literally have so many options for each cuisine (Asian, Italian, Mexican, American), you name it! The desserts option were so yummy!

It does get very busy! We got there around 5:30 on a Tuesday and the line was already pretty long so definitely try to go as early as you can.  

It does seem a bit pricey (~$65 including tip) but I do think they try to give you your money's worth with all of the selections.

I highly recommend you check-in prior to waiting in line! My friends and I were able to get into the VIP line and there was a minimal wait. Weekday brunch after 11pm was $40. 

I loved the variety of choices that Bacchanal offered. 

Amongst my favorites were:
-pizza (surprisingly delicious and fresh!)
-ravioli
-golden beet salad
-quinoa & arugula salad
-clams
-mussels
-strawberry lychee gelato.

Some misses were:
-pho (broth was so sweet, yuck)
-lobster bisque (flavor was delicious but so so salty)
-matcha cake (not very soft or flavorful)
-eggs benedict (the hollandaise was so lemony it offset the taste of everything)

This place was good but way overpriced. It cost $62 and change for dinner for 1 adult. While they had a decent variety and the quality seemed pretty good for a buffet, it just wasn't worth it given the cost. They had a lot of seafood, from crabs legs to shrimp to oysters and so on. They also had a lot of different international cuisines, including Mexican, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, etc. The carving station also had a lot of options and I tried prime rib which was decent but not super tender or flavorful. The standout here was the sushi, which everyone agreed was really tasty. They also had a lot of options for dessert which I loved. We got here around 9 on a Friday night and it was really empty. If they lowered the price I would be back but otherwise I will just take my money and go have an excellent steak at a steakhouse instead.

Oh yeah!  This competes with Wynn for best buffet on the strip.  Came in for lunch.  Their asian selection is surprisingly very well done!  They have cool fruit juices, different seafoods, fresh meats, tacos, a great dessert bar (they even have gummy bears in a jar that you can take away).  An overall really really well done place.  Service here is also up there.  Even the guy cutting the roast beef had this big smile on his face and is so happy to give you a slice!  Bacchanal if you're reading this, you should give him a raise (he's a black dude - yeah that's pretty vague I know)!  I would definitely come back!  Oh, and this is better than the Wicked Spoon.

Bacchanal has been on my go-to list for two years, and I'm glad I finally got the chance. It is the best buffet I've been to, and I ate until I hated myself.

The dessert bar is great! I highly recommend the creme brulee. Carrot cake, pecan pie, and lava cake were also pretty good. 

The meat station is GREAT. My slice of prime rib was quite tough, but my friend got such a tender slice, with just the right amount of fat. The soft shell crab was so good. The salmon was perfectly cooked. I only got the chilled crab legs (not the steamed ones located in the Italian section) but that was delicious. Sushi is not worth. Pork cheek on mashed potatoes were above average, but make sure you get a fresh batch. Bone marrow was pretty good, but make sure you get the ones that are piping hot!

I wish I had 2 more stomachs to fit everything, and I wish I remembered everything I did eat! I AM COMING BACK WITH MORE SELF CONTROL.

As far as buffets on the Strip are concerned. I think this is the top one after they remodelled it and remade it. The old Ceasar's buffet was a 2 star experience at that. But this place is amazing. Shrimps, oysters are fresh and big. You can see them schuck the oysters. The cheeses are different and delicious. The desserts are just ridiculous. The asian flavors are pretty authentic. They even have the herbal soup in the little earthen stoneware. Yes, they actually serve the high end soups in this containers as it is supposed to keep in the vitamins better. So I've been told. I usually avoid the crab legs, not because they are not great. I am crabbed out living in Vegas. But these monsters are what Green Valley Ranch used to be like.
We go here everytime we go to Vegas and it never upsets. Always something new! Soft shell crab, macaroons, cut meat, asian, italian, mexican, american, endless mimosas, the list continues!

Been here twice over the past month due to friends and family. Buffet used to be a lot better (came here about 5 years ago). 

Seafood and meat here is what you'd expect (decent). The asian soups are kind of a miss for me. Dim sum is decent. 

The lack of ice cream is very disturbing. They only have gelato. And no, they are not the same thing. 

Will not be coming back at the price-point of +$50. Gratuity is also force charged for larger parties so be warned (I think it's 8+, but don't quote me).

The newest big budget buffet in Las Vegas and it is as good as buffet's get. Pretty much tried as much as my stomach can take. I would say 80% of the food that I tried was good to great, which is a big fat B in the yelp report card.

It was pricey, but it was worth it! Loved their dessert options (I seriously think I had all of them). They had a good variety of food and I definitely enjoyed trying all of their different options. We went there for dinner and my dinning companion really enjoyed the lamb. Whenever we are back home and he orders lamb he will always say it does not compare to the one he had at the Bacchanal. I personally do not like lamb, but would recommend it per my companion. Seeing as their dinner was so good I would love to go back and try their brunch buffet.

The hot crab legs are to die for! So delicious!!! 

Came here on a Wednesday night around 8pm. No line (thank goodness)! Last time we came, the line was wrapped around, and the wait was about 2 hours! The cost was about $50/ person. I thought that was pretty reasonable considering the amount of variety there was. In Hawaii, you'll easily pay $50 for a buffet that doesn't have half the choices of food. Our waiter was very friendly and always made sure our drinks were filled. My boyfriend and I really enjoyed our meal here.

freaking unbelieveable .... i had to wait 4 hours to get into this buffet . came here on jan. 2 because my hubby wanted to eat this buffet so badly . you can't just go there and stand in line .... no , you have to register your phone number to get a ticket . 
the ticket will tell you about what time you can expect to get in .
they charged us 59.99 $ per person for a holiday dinner , even though it was not a holiday anymore .
when we walked around to look at the buffet , we noticed , that most of the food was regular dinner food  and a lot of the special holiday  food wasn't even available .
we asked around for the lobster and filet mignon , which was listed as 1 of there holiday day food. everybody told  us it was only available on the jan 1. buffet .
????? why did they charge everybody the holiday price for a regular dinner ?
we felt chipped and pointed the holiday menu out which was placed in front of the buffet. the manager then magically brought my hubby and me a plate  with steak and lobster . that was nice , but we still felt cheated , since a lot of the special holiday food was nowhere to be found.
the food was very average on this day and very dissapointing.... sure not worth  122.25  $ plus tip  for 2

Big selection of dif cousines, asian european n american. Good service, seats are comfortable usually very busy on weekends but overpriced n dont beat that much othe good buffets on strip like wicked spoon, spice market few rest on aria n belagio buffets. Jus bigger n flashier place

So after waiting one hour (which didn't seem as long as I had a friend with me), we were able to get in and experience the hype.  Once inside, you'll find modern decor with trendy music softly playing in the background.  It's a nice fresh experience.  My issue is with the layout of the restaurant.  There aren't good lanes and walkways to get to the buffet stations.  Additionally, the stations are broken into different sections in even different rooms in some cases.  As a result, this design leads to confusion and adds to the long wait lines at each station. 

My favorites for the evening were the meatballs, prime rib, rib eye, lamb chop, and mochi ice cream.  The dishes that were less successful were the oysters and sushi.  In fact, my oysters were gritty and I had a hard piece of shell in one of my bites.  I don't think that they did a good job of cleaning the ones I ate.  The food was good and certainly the highlight of my experience.

Overall I wasn't impressed with all of the hype.  I personally had higher expectations for the buffet that is rated as the best that Las Vegas has to offer.  My perspective would be completely different had their not been a hour wait to get in, lines at nearly every station, and the highest priced buffet on the strip.  It amazes me that this buffet can command $50 a person and be this high in demand.  Nonetheless, it's working for them... at the moment.  I doubt I'll ever come back.  I'm a fan of Wicked Spoon instead.

Reason for the poor rating not telling the truth about the cost and not giving the correct discounts specially when you're a local you catch those kind of things and the person did not care at the cashier we were overcharged $20 the food was great the service was great but the cashier suck

We went on a Sunday night for dinner and the line outside was not too long but we still had to wait about ten minutes to get seated. We came here because of the reviews and left quite disappointed. I already noticed the long line at the meat and seafood section so we decided to go there first and see what the hoopla was all about. Cocktail shrimps and crabs were excellent. My husband loved the Chef's seafood special and salmon. The guy who serves the hot crabs was a bit rude though. I'm hoping it's just because of a long night since we got there around 8:30pm. 
We love sushi and sashimi but this one did not deliver. I've tasted better sushi, there was no sashimi and the sushi selection was limited. Tried the sweet potato tater tots and that was good. Fruits and veggies selection were also very limited. They do have a wide array of desserts in small plates/containers which works for me especially if you just want a taste of a little bit of everything. 
Overall ambience was upscale for a buffet and decor was creative. Price wise, I feel like we did not get the value for our money ($44.99/person) since we've been to better buffets for less. There are also a lot of other options for buffets here in Vegas. We just decided to try this one out to see what  it was all about. Still having second thoughts if we want to go back or not.

Overall: swanky buffet but it's not as tasty as it looks

Pros
-all kinds of food
- gelato is super tasty
- mushroom truffle soup
-charcuterie station
-crepe station

Cons
- the seafood was rather sad/ bad
- no crab legs
- lines for anything like prime rib or tacos take forever 


Sidenote: 
-come if you have no plans, lines are so long it's hard to say when you'd get out of here
- quality is lacking, especially when you are paying this much for a buffet

This buffet is pricey, but worth every penny. Everything is upscale and the quality of food is top notch. Some people hate buffets, but this one is fantastic!!!  Got a bit confused about checking in with the machine.  I got a time, from the machine when to come back, but I think you had to just hand the ticket to the lady at the line and wait. I asked, but she wasn't the nicest.  Don't even know if that was right. Really never received a clear answer.

Very large selection of a variety of foods including seafood, meat, sushi and Chinese. The crabs and shrimps are very fresh. American wagyu (beef) is very tender and delicious. The crepes for dessert is great to end the meal.
Dinner starts at 3. If you come later than 5 there would be a significant line up so do come early.

This is the newest buffet in Vegas. The food was all great and had everything you would expect at a buffet in Vegas. The service was just ehhh. When I sat down I noticed a spoon was missing. Then later on when I left the table to get more food, I noticed someone took my napkin cloth. 

Then at the end, my wife and I were walking around on our last round to get some dessert.. and when we walked back to the table, our table had been cleaned already. Luckily we didn't have any other food left to eat besides our gelato. I was going to tip, but since they cleaned off our table before we were done, I didn't tip. We just ate our gelato and walked out. Good buffet! Service could use some work.

We love this buffet. There is so much to choose from! The wait staff is very attentive and the food is never gone so they make sure that all the food is always refilled. It is definitely worth the money.

Can't imagine that a buffet could be any better. Top quality dishes that are also creative and top restaurant quality. Worth the price tag. Line is reasonable compared to Wynn,Bellagio. I left the Bellagio line after reading the Yelp reviews and came here. Very glad I did.

Delicious worth every penny of the price! 
The wait is a little long but it's fine works up your appetite! Took my family for the first time they loved everything! Definitely recommend!

not all that considering the hype. honestly the selection is lackluster when you consider the hotel and price. I give it a 2 overall because i was just disappointed in the offerings. The big bad Vegas buffet was just blah . i bumped it to 3 because it was clean. Food was hit and miss as with most buffets. The flavor of some items was on point whereas others were just basic, reheated overinflated buffet fare. It all just seemed random and I've been to many a buffet with lower prices but the food was delicious. There are plenty other options on the strip. Wouldn't return but glad I got to finally try it

The lines were crazy long. If you are a meat and seafood lover, this place is worth the money. Bottomless mimosa, crab legs, oysters, meats of all sorts, and on and on. All the food tasted great. Too bad they were out of macaroons. Overall, I highly recommend this place, especially during the weekend when they serve crab legs and oysters for lunch.

We had about a 3 hr wait time once we checked in to the kiosk. When we returned and paid, we had an additional 30 min. wait for seating. Finally, we got to eat about 45 min. before closing. I most enjoyed the prime rib, tri tip, creme brûlée and the flan. 

I knocked a star off because there were items I was expecting, based on the pictures, that weren't available; king crab legs (only had snow crab out), lobster bisque, and watermelon feta salad. I was really looking forward to trying them here. Maybe I'll have better luck on my next visit.

I was going to give a better review, after looking thru the past photos, I can only give it a 2 star. The crab leg we had was not snow crab leg like it used to be. My wife was telling me how good this buffet was, but it's not what I expected. We paid $46.99 per adult and $29.99 for kids under 10 years old last Sunday because it's holiday pricing. It's not worth it. Don't go there during holidays. Our server was arrogant, I was trying to decide to get champagne or mimosa, the server stopped me and said: "listen to me, mimosa is champagne add orange juice" Like I didn't know it!? 
They even criticized other customers who didn't left him a tip. And was checking their receipt on the table to make sure they didn't pay tips upfront. I don't think any server should talk about tips and guests in front of other guests, very wrong. Can't believe it.
The food was just ok, but the line to wait to get seafood was very long. It made me lost my appetite.

Excellent variety at this buffet.  My son and nephew who are in their 20's ate well!  Lots of seafood, Asian and Hispanic food. Great variety.  I also like the elegant decor.  I did not feel like I was in a cafeteria the way I do at most buffets.   It was worth the wait!!

Dinner buffet. The food look old. Crab legs and carving station look like some 9.99 buffets. Dinner is 50.99. But I would not eat here if the price was 20 bucks. I was smart enough to ask them to let me check out the food first. 5 stars for me.

My goodness this buffet was amazing! The checkin is weird. You have to check in at a kiosk and it gives you a time to come back to get to wait in line.  Be prepared to wait. There were so many options and they were all very tasty. The meat station was impressive with so many selections. The desserts were divine. Gelato, cheesecake, and my favorite Creme  brûlée. If you plan it just right you can get in during the brunch price and get to try some of the dinner options as well.

I don't really know what's the hype about this place.

Ate here today, and I am very disappointed. The food here is mediocre. It's just the presentation of the food that makes it look good. Overall, I would not recommend this place to anyone especially the price. Not worth it.

The Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars is incredible! When I saw there was a two hour wait, I didn't get discouraged, I thought to myself this place must be phenomenal to have a price that high and a line that long. Let me tell you... worth every penny! Bacchanal is what happens when you give world class and classically trained Chefs millions of dollars and tell them to go for it. Best buffet in Vegas!! 
I always do a walk through before plating up. At this price, I skip the easily ascertainable food (pasta, salads...etc) and go for the premium. The seafood was on point! Delicious crag legs, shrimp and the oysters were outstanding! Also, they had a BBQ station in the middle of this elegant and sophisticated restaurant. I've been smoking meats now for a few years back home and these smoked meats were tender, flavorful and succulent. The smoked brisket (ask for the point and not the flat) was mouth watering delicious. Everything there was top notch. This buffet could give fine dining a run for its money. And if you are a fine cheese person, you're in luck. The assortment of cheeses was quite impressive. The décor and the service were also excellent. I plan to visit Bacchanal many more times!

This buffet is worthy of Dionysus himself! As soon as the hostess shows you to your table, prepare to be amazed with the selection of the most exquisite dishes of all types of cuisine: American, Italian, Mexican, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, and more! And let's not forget the desserts. If you're planning on losing some weight, do not eat at this wonderful cornucopia of delectable delights.

My all-time favorite buffet in Vegas, hands down. I can't say enough how much I enjoyed this buffet. The choices are just superb! There's so much selection and they all taste amazing. I wish I had a second stomach just so I could eat even more. 

What's great about this buffet is that they have choices that people will eat. There's not many bizarre dishes that you'll wonder if you'll like or not. Their sliders are a must have. Their seafood selection is to die for. Oh the succulent Alaskan crab meat, oysters, clams...just absolutely amazing. 

Their dessert menu consists of a variety of gelato flavors, puddings, cakes, cookies, pastries and even a crepe station! I can't wait to be back in Vegas so I can have this buffet again!

As we were brought to our table we were told where everything was and I was excited about all the choices.

First, I went to the seafood area and chose the shrimp, roasted red pepper bisque, and the miso glazed cod. The plump shrimp was the best of the 3 but with the shrimp being straight on the ice it tasted soft and semi water logged. The roasted red pepper bisque was flavorless and tasted more like a tomato soup. The miso glazed cod was cooked well but was luke warm and the wasabi mashed potatoes accompanying it were also luke warm which made the outer layer hard. Next, I went to the italian station and got the meatballs which were nicely presented and the penne carbonara. The meatball tasted fine but the tomato sauce was overly sweet and made the entire dish taste artificial. The carbonara tasted nothing like a carbonara, pasta was overcooked and it reminded me of the quality of pasta I would have tasted from a Souplantation. A few more low points were the sashimi being warm; pretzel rolls being dry; corn chowder crusty on top from it being luke warm; brisket more fat than meat. The one positive thing I will say is that this buffet has solid and well done desserts. I had the carrot cake; beignet; churro; strawberry cheesecake ice cream; mint chip ice cream; cheesecake pop; chocolate ganache log; oreo chocolate mousse. Carrot cake was moist and cream cheese frosting on top was nicely done. Beignet was also nicely done with it being freshly fried and warm. Churro was tasty but was more soft than crispy. Chocolate ganache log was my favorite; you could tell the chocolate was of high quality. 

Overall, I was very disappointed in the quality and execution of the food especially the hot items. The only reason I am even giving Baccchanal 2 stars is for the thoughtful/tasty dessert items.

This place is absolutely incredible!

When you think of Las Vegas style buffet, this should be what comes to mind. I don't know the exact numbers but it is somewhere in the $15-$20 million that they spent creating this space and experience.

Located in the already beautiful Caesar's Palace, this buffet has everything you can imagine plus more. Everything that you taste here will be of the best you've ever had and I really feel confident in saying that. 

It's going to be the most costly buffet that you'll find but I absolutely promise you that it's worth it. I have been to 10 buffets or so in the valley and nothing even compares. I also have been on cruises that have had all you can eat buffets and been to buffets in other cities but absolutely nothing compares to this.

When you go, make sure you take your appetite so that you can take full advantage of it. You will see the photos of the crab legs, prime rib, amazing desserts, sushi... it is all AMAZING.

I have to be honest, I'm probably one of the cheapest people you'll ever meet but any chance I get to go here, I splurge! You should too!

I decided to come to this buffet because it is one of the newest buffets, and is supposedly chef-run so that the dishes are all made to perfection.  I had very high expectations when coming to this buffet, and needless to say, I was still blown away by the quality and variety of food.

Seafood:
- Crab legs were very fresh, and can be prepared warm (steamed for you on the spot). It was not as sweet and fresh as Bellagio buffet crab legs though.  I haven't been to Bellagio buffet in a while so this difference may just be a seasonal difference.
- Shrimp cocktail was also incredibly sweet and fresh.  The shrimp were large and crispy. They were all very well cleaned and deshelled.
- Oyster shooters were another highlight of the meal! The sweet and tangy tomato juice/sauce with the very sweet oyster in a shot glass was brilliant! I found that the oysters in the shooters were sweeter and less metallic tasting than the oysters that were served freshly shucked.
- Various fish

Asian:
- Blackened chicken ginseng soup was not actually prepared with blackened chicken but was still amazing. Ginseng is really expensive, and on top of that the soup had dried scallops in it.  It was very high quality soup, and I was impressed by how much they were willing to spend on food cost to make such good soup! 
- Sushi was not particularly good. I'm very picky about my sashimi fish.  They had a very limited range of fish, and nothing was served just as sashimi.  I recall Bellagio buffet as being superior in terms of raw fish.
- Xiao Long Bao (steamed little dragon buns) were seriously legit.  Very thin dumpling skin, and the filling was perfectly flavored.  Each bun was perfectly sealed so the juices were retained perfectly in each little dumpling pocket.

Carving area:
- Wicked spoon prime rib was better.
- I ate too much seafood to stuff down that much red meat.

Desserts:
- Who can forget about desserts? I was so impressed by the variety of desserts! People say that Wynn is known for their dessert bar, but I would say that this buffet's desserts surpass those of Wynn.
- Crepe bar. OMG. The crepe was so thin and the edges were made perfectly crispy. They provide fresh berries, various sauces, and whipped cream.
- Gelato bar. Very good flavors, but some of the fruity flavors were diluted down and lost the creaminess. Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan had better gelato.
- Souffle: the pistachio flavored soufflé was interesting but too moist
- Crème Brule: perfect  I wish it were served warm though.
- Macarons: It was my first time trying a macaron and it was really good! I still don't get why macarons are so expensive though... 

Other information:
- There were lots of other choices but I filled myself on the expensive stuff (seafood, etc). There was an American, Italian, and Mexican food bar.
- All items are served in individual portions, which help to maintain cleanliness and presentation of the food.
- The line was very long on Thanksgiving Day (2 hours around noon), but very much worth it.
- $44.99/person for "brunch" that holiday weekend.  We got in right before they switched to dinner menu (which would have been $50/person).  If you are too rich and can't think of other ways to spend your money, you can pay $20 to skip the line.
Average food. Pay $80 for Thanksgiving dinner. No king crab, no macaroon, sub par oysters. I am disappointed.

Just no.

Yelp led me here with its great rating, especially for a buffet, but I will never go back nor will I recommend it to anyone. The ambiance and the service was nice, but be real- you go to a buffet for the food and with the exception of the taco station and the sweet potato tater tots, the food was not good.

I've never paid so much for a buffet so I thought surely, this place must be legit. But no. My husband and I are the buffeters who do it right and go for the good stuff first then dink around with the filler foods. First of all, there was no Alaskan king crab legs, even at dinner. Just snow crab. We got a plate of steamed crab legs and they were tasteless! The cold legs were actually better, but those were bad too. Not a lot of meat and no flavor. We usually shamelessly go through at least two full plates of crab legs each, but we didn't even want to waste room on these. Fine, we'll go to the next best thing: prime rib. Their prime rib was the worst I've ever had in my life. They weren't even the slightest bit pink in the middle and I like mine rare, but not only was it over-cooked, it was tough and gritty and after I took a bite, my mood was ruined and I lost all hope. The two main things I go to a buffet for were crap! We spent the rest of our dinner picking at and pushing around filler foods on our plate and left unhappy and underwhelmed. Were they having an off-day? Perhaps, but at $118 for two people, I can't afford an off-day and neither can they. Shame.

My friends and I waited 2 hours for the buffet about 2-3 weeks after it first opened.  It was $39.  I heard it was $35 but I guess they maybe jacked up the price for the I Heart Radio weekend.

Tip: Each person in your group should get a player's card to save $3 on the buffet.  (the $39 was after the discount)

My thoughts on the buffet...

Food - AMAZING! They have so much variety from Asian, Italian, Mexican, American, etc. They have BBQ pork ribs, beef brisket, tomohawk steaks,truffled potato, sweet potato fries, seafood like crab legs, shrimp, and mussels. They have dim sum, ramen and pho!  If you like hot crab legs, ask the chefs to get it for you from the back.  They don't put the hot ones out in front for some reason, only the cold ones.

Only bad thing was no fruit for dinner except if you can find them as toppings from the desserts. Some desserts to name a few arecrepes, cupcakes, cakes, creme brulee, gelato, tiramisu, mousse, souffles, and cake pops.  Desserts looked great but wish they tasted better.

Presentation - Super cute! It's very similar to the presentation at Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo.  They have their fried chicken in mini frying baskets and mini ketchup bottles.  The amount of desserts were impressive but I wish they spent more time of the taste of it instead of how it looked.  
 
Service - POOR.  I understand they were crazy busy but our waitress would forget one drink and bring another.  She wouldn't take our plates away without being asked.  I expected better service for the price you pay.

If you're a vegetarian, you should probably stay away.  You would not get your money's worth at this buffet.

Best buffet in Las Vegas! I'm honestly not so crazy about buffets because the quality of food isn't usually the greatest, however at this buffer you get both good quality and quantity. The variety of foods are endless! The sushi is by far outstanding. I ate a dish today of mixed salmon, shrimp, octopus, it was the best plate I've had In a longggg time! The deserts are mouthwatering as well. If you're in Vegas and want to eat at a Buffet then you have to try this place.

Came again for dinner after first experiencing it at the yelp elite event. So a couple things have changed, such as you have to get here early if you want to try everything!  Example, Chocolate covered strawberries (the size of your fist) come out at about 7pm and are all gone by 8pm. They still make souffles (chocolate, pistachio, or banana) to order, but you have to ask as they don't have them sitting out there readily. They have added mochi ice cream, and they don't replenish the fresh oysters as quickly as before. Also, they don't keep restocking the beet salad. 

I got there around 5:30pm on a weekday, and the line was about a 45 minute wait to the end of the waiting line ropes. By the time I got to the front the line looked an hour and a half long, it snaked past the ropes and back to the pool area entrance, eek. 

Anyways, the food was still as delicious as ever. The oysters were cold and fresh, the crab legs were sweet (best eaten cold even though they will heat them up for you in a pot of hot water), the prime rib, ribeye, and lamb rack were cooked perfectly medium rare, great variety of charctuerie, delicious version of caprese salad and beet salad with goat cheese. For those asians out there, they have a very nicely done asian soup of black chicken with longon and stuff in the asian section. I saw asians grabbing 2 bowls at a time. They also have those soup dumplings that got famous in new york. Desserts were amazing with macarons, tiramisu, souffle, crepes, lollipop cakes, (didn't get to the chocolate covered strawberries because they ran out), mochi ice cream, gelato and sorbets (give the blood orange sorbet or the thai tea gelato a try). 

I kept wanting to eat more but my stomach just was not able to hold everything. As I told my boyfriend, I looked 5 months pregnant with my food baby belly after eating here. 

Word of advice if you want to save a couple bucks, get your Caesar's Total Rewards card (the casino gaming club card) before you get to the front of the line, it takes about $3 off the cost of the buffet.

Om nom nom! Usually I'm skeptical about places that are advertised all over the city as "Best in Town" but this was the BEST buffet I've ever been to. The food selection is varied and vast, and everything seems to be something you would order at a very nice restaurant. And the desserts....oh. my. GOD! It is expensive, but so worth it. You will be rolling yourself outta here. 

Tips: Go for Lunch when it's cheaper.

Only complaint is the wait staff wasn't very attentive and it took forever to get refills on drinks.

I'd like to start this out by saying I'm not a big fan of buffets in general.  The idea of standing in line like a pig going to his trough to be stuffed is pretty disheartening, especially when Vegas has so much to offer in the way of food.  But decided to give one another try on my last trip and I will say that Caesars has something solid going here.

You need to be prepared for two things going into this one.  First, this buffet is not cheap.  $55 ish per person + tip is pretty outrageous, but we had a $75 dining credit so that made the decision a little more manageable (thanks Travelocity!).  Secondly, there's a long Congo line to get in and a computer at the start of the line to check in on.  The line didn't move very fast and we were there at an off-peak dinner time during the week, so I can only imagine the insanity on the weekend.

The Good: 

The buffet offers easily the biggest variety I've seen at one of these and has everything you could possibly want.  If you have picky eaters on your trip, bring them here and they will be extremely grateful.  Fortunately I'm not too picky and went to town on just about everything they had but it's easy to hit the "drowning in gluttony" wall quickly here.  Moderation is key, one bite per item was my general rule of thumb.

King crab, a full seafood spread, sliders, chicken strips, Asian cuisine, an absolutely amazing BBQ section, pastas and meatballs, and a dessert section that even impressed this very seldom dessert eater.  I had never had Gelato before (and I'm Italian so not sure how that happened) but this was fantastic, I don't know if I could have any other ice cream other than it again.

The most important part of the buffet experience though was that everything was being routinely refilled and prepared fresh in front of you.  I've seen other buffets where it's heat lamp city and everything seemed luke warm or un-enticing.  The presentation here is on-point, and the chefs make sure that what's under the lamps just came out of their hands.

You do get servers at the table, but ours took 20+ minutes to get us a glass of water so I'm guessing it can be hit or miss.  Thankfully most of it is self serve, so lounge at your leisure.  Also enjoy the spectacle of watching some people who are only 100-150 pounds with 6 plates at their table because wow-wow-wee-wah I have no idea how they put all that down.

If you're a buffet fan, I think this should be the first stop on your tour.  Otherwise I'd never recommend it at full price, but not a bad option with a discount or the 24 hour pass.

Best buffet I've ever experienced! This will be my one stop every time I visit Vegas going forward! Crab legs and Sushi are a must try! The street tacos were super delicious and the dessert station was unbelievable!

1 word. Ammmaaaazinggg. This is not only the best buffets. But prob one of the best places I've ever eaten. Everything was absolutely incredible. And trust me! For the price of entry I made sure I tried just about everrytningg. We had seafood till we couldn't eat no more. Endless King crab legs. Just had a blast love love love Vegas and this is def a place to eat

The best buffet I've ever been to! The options are endless and even though we went right at noon there was not a long wait at all! The best was definitely the dessert buffet! Will definitely be coming back!

After THREE attempts of complaints, the buffet manager finally contacted me and offered to dine at the buffet again for free.  The second experience was much better. On the same trip, hubby and I also ate at Bellagio buffet.  And Bacchanal definitely offers better variety and food.

Not worth the $53.99 on a sat night. I mean if there's gonna be a price hike on the weekend then at least complement it with higher quality food. I really didn't see anything that would have justified the price. There was no lobster, rib eye, foie gras, or brontosaurus. It was said they had King crab, but what they actually had was a blend of snow crab and small king crab legs that were the same size as the snow crabs. They did have some miso glazed seabass which saved them from a 2 star rating. 

The best part of the buffet was their dessert bar. They had frozen mochi, macarons, cake pops, chocolate dipped strawberries, gelato, and great toppings for ice cream. Presentation of all these were very exquisite.

Although the dessert was awesome, it isn't what I would pay $54 for. You would think for the 2hr wait and another hr to get seated, it would be life changing but it's far from. You still see the Chinese food, corn on the cob, pizza, tacos, and other ordinary offerings you'd see at Hometown Buffet. If you want to experience this place, I'd suggest coming on a non-fri or sat night.
Great buffet but the line sucks.    The food is above average but our service was really great

So far this is the best buffet in Las Vegas. They have A good selection of different ethnic foods and high quality, but It's quite pricey $55.99/ person on Sunday night. Must try! If don't mind paying for what you get.
Overpriced, overhyped, the food is decent but definitely not worth it. The lines are atrocious as well. Hate this place lol.

This is the best buffet in Las Vegas.  The food is top notch quality and is always fresh!!!  While here the oysters were the plumpest I've had in a long time!  The oyster shooters were off the wall good.  Crab legs were great and cut in half making it easier to get too.... I like snapping my own in half but their way works OK.   Dessert island is awesome.  Everything I tried tasted wonderful!!! The atmosphere and seating makes you feel like you're in a high end place.  Worth the price of entry

I've been to many buffets in Las Vegas and by far this is one of my favorite. There were many choices to choose from so I don't know where to start. I will start with the Chinese section. They had dim sum at the Chinese section along with blue crabs and pepper steak. To perfection. No complaints there. Another great touch is that you can have the Alaskan King crab legs cold or hot. They also have scallops on the shell with crispy fried onions. The seafood selection there was humongous. They had large shrimp cocktails along with oysters, clams and mussels. The carving station had prime red and I was cooked to medium temperature. The dessert station had many choice to choose from from fruits along with ice cream ,gelato ,sorbet and crème brûlée. The price is not cheap which cost roughly $75 a person with gratuities but given the amount of food that was Offered I  don't think you can find a better deal somewhere else in Las Vegas.

This place is everything! I've been here twice in the past 2 days and I can't get enough. I am skeptical about buffets but OMG this place is amazing. They have everything from seafood to tacos and more! This place has everything and it all tastes so good!!! The place is pretty expensive so make sure you go in with a huge appetite.

After hearing really good news about this buffet, my friends and I decided to close out our Vegas trip with a visit to "the buffets of all buffets" Vegas had to offer. Lets just say waiting until our last night in Vegas was a great decision.

The wait time wasn't too bad, a total of 80mins.

There were a lot of uncommon buffet options (Bone Marrow, Pork stuffed chicken wings, etc). For some odd reason there wasn't fried chicken so that was a let down.

And for the most part it was enjoyable, but in no way did it live up to the hype or the price. 

The worst part of this experience was the food poisoning I got the next morning and continue to feel 2 days after. It's not fun traveling back to the east coast on a 5 hour flight when you need to use the restroom every few minutes. I think it was the really, really salty crab legs they serve. 

Anyways, eating at buffets are always risky, so if you're feeling Lucky go head and feast at The Bacchanal. 

T's and P's for my fiery butt hole. Hopefully I'll be able to sit properly at work tomorrow. Now excuse me while I go back to my throne ...

We stopped in during our vacation in Las Vegas, on the recommendation of several friends who had been there in the last 2 to 3 years. It was a disaster, being too expensive and the food was terrible. Plus, it seemed that there was some ingredient in the food that made us feel full. We usually eat 3 times what we did at this "international" buffet.

First, we had to get instructions, from a woman, who told us that we had to go to a kiosk and get a ticket. The ticket told us, that we had to wait 61 minutes, before we could get in the line to buy into the international buffet.. We were in that line for 30 minutes, before we got to the teller that wanted $58.00 per person to eat at the "international" buffet. Took us at least 20 minutes to pay her. So after 2 hours we finally got to our seats and started to get some food. I waited at the table while the other 2 went and got food, no one approached me during that 15 minute wait. They looked happy about their selection, so off I went to find something to eat. So 2 hours and 15 minutes later, I'm searching for food.

Second, walking down the food line, I searched through the crowd for items I might be interested in, not much caught my eye. After walking almost a block and half, I got to the beginning of the food line. Picked out some beef pepper steak, scalloped potatoes, some green beans, crab rangoons, fried asparagus and waffle wrapped chicken. Got back to my seat after 20 minutes of walking the food line. Now, 2 hours and 35 minutes have passed. The beef pepper steak, green beans and fried asparagus were all cold. Scalloped potatoes were tasty and hot. The crab rangoons had no crab in them, just cream cheese. The waffle wrapped chicken was hot, but the waffle part tasted awful,l so I peeled it off the partial chicken breast piece and ate the hot tasteless chicken. My friends had each gotten some sliders, which weren't there when I walked through, they said that the sliders were good. They also got some prime rib, of which, one got some almost raw meat and the other had to have it cooked a lot more. I couldn't get any prime rib on the first time through, as too many people were crowding the station. They each also got some cheese/sauce covered chicken breast filets, they said they were good. There weren't any either time I walked the food line. A waitress had brought drinks to the table while I was away. As I was eating my friends went back through the food line and came back to the table with some other food. Then I went a second time to get some food. There were some sliders, this time, and I was able to get some prime rib, which was now cooked a lot more. As I was leaving the "meat window", they brought out some HOT sweet potato tots which were great hot. Got some watermelon too. My friends didn't eat much of what they got the second time, complaining of being full. I ate my prime rib, which was tender, but tasteless, after salt and peppering it,  I managed to get it down before it went cold. By this time my sliders were cold and the meat was raw, so I didn't eat them. I was starting to feel full too. I ate my watermelon and my friends went and tried some desserts, which there were unable to finish because of being too full. While I was getting my second plate, a waitress came by and left some receipts for the sodas at $6.00 each. On the receipt was a note that we were requited to limit our "dining experience" to 2 hours. Each time they refilled our glasses we got more and more ice and less and less soda.

There were mashed potatoes and gravy, 4 kinds of pizza, crab legs, muscles and shrimp on ice and all sorts of breads. I think that there were baked potatoes, but not sure. They had oyster shooters and some salad makings. I could not find any hot shrimp dishes, either breaded fried or stir-fried with or without veggies. Maybe hot/warm shrimp is a supper item.

In conclusion, we got charged $192.00 (3 of us) for waiting in line for 2 hours and 35 minutes to eat terrible cold food and raw meat and be filled up on eating so much less food than either of us was used to eating. I would recommend that you skip this "international" buffet and go anywhere else. If you like cold crab legs and cold muscles, I recommend getting a "Caesar's player's card" or a "buffet of buffets pass". At least your culinary disaster will be cheaper than ours.

Came here on veterans day for lunch, and got seated in 30 minutes.  Food was delicious. Dim sum was actually fresh and tasty. They had har gow, bbq pork buns,  and shu mai.  Corn bread and chicken wings are a must. Their dessert selection of crepes, cookies, and gelato are to die for. The ambiance is nice, with all the rooms uniquely decorated.  Service needs to be worked on.

4.75 Stars rounded to 5.

Over the past couple years, I haven't really been big on buffets- I prefer quality over quantity and don't feel the need to get super full during meals with good, but not exceptional food.  But... i hadn't done the obligatory Vegas buffet thing in a while, and using high quality food to soak up the effects of alcohol-induced nausea sounded awesome at the moment, so I thought, ehh, what the hell.  Light internet research revealed Bacchanal to be the "top Las Vegas buffet, by USA Today", and I just had to insist on seeing what the hype was all about.

Overall, despite opting to pay $25 to skip the 125+ minute estimated wait time (because, fuqqqq that.), the experience was pretty great.  They had a ton of above average options and unique items that caught my eye.

The Stand-Out Winners-
+Shrimp-Succulent, perfect texture, and delicious.  I actually hate cocktail sauce, and nonetheless was able to enjoy them plain.
+Individual Pork Belly plates with accompanying sauces- the plate is so hot, I had to use mini rubber tongs to move it onto my plate.  And, it was hella good.  It's so perfectly seasoned that I perferred it without the sauces.   
+Linquica Sausages- Excellent quality meat, and a potent, spicy bite. Tasted very fresh.
+Creamed Corn and Elote (Mexican Corn Snack)-  Doesn't beat the Creamed Corn from Lawry's in Beverly Hills or the Corn Man (Lincoln Heights, LA) Elote, but both were really good anyway.

1/2 Winner- The crab legs.  Similar to my shrimp note above, the meat is delicious plain.  My only gripe is that some of them had ice-chips stuck to them..since it tasted fresh and not frozen, I can't say for sure that the ice is indicative of being low-quality, but it is something I noticed.

(Delicious) Misses-
+The Prime Rib-  Here's a tip- ask for Rare to get Medium Rare, and for Medium Rare to get Medium...at least thats what I got out of it.  I would have to say that even the "true" medium rare piece was good, but not the best I've had (i.e.  HOPR (SF), or Lawrys (Bev. Hills), but it was bad.  I guess I say this because Prime Rib and Crab Legs are *the* things you gotta try at a buffet, and their's was just ok.  It's the reason why they dont get a full 5 stars from me.
+Poke- It was good, but I didn't like it's preparation (spicy rub).
+Brisket- Great, but I'e pre-determined that Franklins (TX) is the best.

Things I Thought Were Cool, But Didn't Try:
Menudo
Cheese and Charcuterie Meat Spread (there was good stuff, like Brie).

Generally Good Stuff:
-Carne Asade "Street Tacos", which were prepared on a rotating grill-thingy.
-Shrimp Hai Gow
-Red Velvet Mini-Cakes + Creme Brulee
-Boil-style Crawfish
-Oysters
-The 3 glasses of Ginger Ale I had to supress the need to hurl/thoughts about how much I drank over the last 2 days, and get my money's worth.

So, in short, I'd definitely recommend this buffet and left happy.  I wouldn't say that every item is a revelation, but it's still great in my book.
Wow. The best dinner buffet in Vegas. Come hungry and you'll leave full and satisfied

Got here early on football Sunday 7:30am as I wanted to start the day off right. Heard this was the best buffet in town besides Bally's hotel . So upon entering the buffet there was no line or wait. Hostess was nice giving us the once around tour because it was our 1st time. The food looked incredible and my mouth was salivating to try it all. I'm the type of person that my first go round is to try it phase then the next time , and the next time I Attack !! Steak and eggs were bomb , omelet was on hit too. Red velvet pancakes yum . Had problems with the country fried potatoes but the onion rings made up for it.                                             Not a big fan of the champagne and orange juice so I instead opted to order the bottomless beer  Yeee !! Sea food was incredible and made sure I did damaged there also. Made a pit stop for the food truck type tacos . Brought it home with the desserts ! Well rounded buffet really , really enjoyed it . Some yelpers I see complained about $$ it's well wort it !! Will come back !!

Um, yes please! This is now mine and hubs' favorite buffet in Vegas. Really top notch stuff going on here. We made sure to get here early like around 5-6pm so that we could avoid the lines. They say there's a 2 hour limit, but they don't really check so if you get there early you can "stay as long as you want". 

Before I start to talk about their delicious food, I'd like to comment about the service. I saw that a few Yelpers complained about not getting enough attention - no one checked on them or refilled their water. Well, this was not the case for me. The busboy waited on us and was super attentive. It was great that he pitched in since we barely saw our actual waiter. I think our waiter was too busy with all the other tables he was in charge of. Water, tea, and drinks were a plenty for us and our plates were promptly cleared! 

The food. OH THE FOOD! 

Before I grabbed anything I walked around to see what kind of foods they offered. So much of everything. I was impressed with their Asian selection. It's not the best, but it's a few notches higher than what other buffets offer. Also, their cheese station!! DROOL~ So much seafood! 

To get my money's worth, I avoided the Asian, Italian, and Mexican stations! I only hit up the seafood, meat carving, and dessert. I did try some cheese though because I couldn't help it. I also got a scoop of veggies just to be healthy. 

Crab legs and oysters were fresh. They had some miso glazed seabass which I got several plates of. Really yummy! The lamb chops were really good too. Everything was high quality and well made like you could get at a fine restaurant. 

I would probably make a whole meal out of their desserts if I could. Everything I tried was tasty but not overdone. The pandan cake was my favorite. 

This is now a must when I come back to Vegas!

Weekend dinner was $58.
The food was as good as I remember... I think it was like $60 per person for the brunch... but the food is restaurant quality.. very huge selection of food.

I went for here for lunch. Lets say for $33 a person I was not happy.

I love the fact that they have at least a few hundred food options but it would be helpful if it tasted good.

I had a plate from every section which consisted of seafood (for lunch no crab legs), american BBQ, mexican, american Italian, chinese, sushi and then the dessert.

Mussel's, oysters and shrimp were average.

keilbasa, ham, n the american BBQ section was not as good as my family BBQ's, which was disappointing. The cute mini waygu beef burgers were ok. the cute tiny portions of onion rings was yummy

Mexican area was nice they heat your mini tortillas and meat right in from of you. 

the american italian station with pizza and pizza rolls was average. Pizza was bland. Pizza rolls were dry.

Sushi was just sushi

the chinese was ok. the orange chicken was yummy. beef and broc had a funky taste. The fried rice was dry & lacking veggies 

The desserts was what I lived for. Yet again i was disappointed. The tiramisu was not good. Pecan tart was ok. The sorbets were good unless you tried a weird flavor like mango with chile and lime.
the cupcakes were divine. The flavor combinations were yummy, the whipped frosting could have come on a spoon and I would have been happy.The cupcakes themselves were also very moist.

In the end if your thinking of going I would recommend dinner. Which will cost you about 45-50 a person but you will have that option of crab legs during dinner.

I plan on giving them a second chance during a dinner service, but lunch wasn't worth it.

WE ACTUALLY GOT ASKED TO LEAVE BECAUSE WE STAYED TOO LONG!!!! Hahahahahahha. I never knew buffets had time limits.... Although it was a bit embarrassing, I guess we stayed so long because we enjoyed it so much. 

So my friends and I decided to buffet it up after three nights of clubbing... so yes, we definitely needed to recover. Wait time was only 15 minutes, so we were seated in no time.

I'll admit - this is my first Vegas buffet, but damn, everything I put into my mouth was amazing. Here's some of my favorites!!! - 

Mini deep fryers containing fatty goodness - corn dogs, tatertots, onion rings...
Fresh juices in cute little bottles
Roasted duck + plum sauce
Oysters, mussels, shrimpies 
Oyster SHOOTERS!
Prime rib
Rib eye
Truffle soup - i still have dreams about this
Korean short ribs
Salmon
Corn on the cob
Sliders - soooo goood. 
Potato gratin - must try!!! I ate 3x of these. 
Lobster bisque
Gelato, gelato, gelato! Try pistachio and baklava! Or everything 
Calamari with this coconut rice(?)
DIY Crepes!!
Creme brulee
Broccoli & Cheese
Mac & Cheese
All the sushi
....

I'm probably missing a lot... but as you can see, we enjoyed everything! Every time we took a bite of something, we would sigh in pleasure or encourage each other to try it.  My vegan friend even broke her veganism that fine afternoon because the food was THAT good (sorry I'm not ratting you out!). 

Service was good as far as I remember. The man cutting the meat was extremely polite and patient, which I liked. The gelato lady was kind, friendly, and didn't mind giving me several samples. Our waitress seemed nice, except for the part when she said there was a two hour time limit. Well, I'm sorry!! What if we all just had really really big appetites?

Price is reasonable (~$35 for lunch)! That filled me up for the rest of the day, so I thought it was worthwhile. I would come back, but probably wont stay as long. 

So if you're DTB (down to buffet), I highly recommend this place!

4.5 stars!
This place was awesome.  We rocked the Groupon.  Ate an amazing brunch and were very happy.

Bacchanal- rated #1 buffet of Las Vegas. We decided to try it on the first day first meal of our weekend trip to LV. Found out no oyster for lunch. We waited 3 hrs to get in for dinner with oyster. Luckily. We went in at 2:30 ish and paid for lunch price but getting dinner dishes right by 3 o'clock. The selection wasn't that versatile. But mostly high quality stuff. So other than what you can get at every buffet, I mainly ate a bunch of cold crab legs, cooked crab legs and whole lot of oysters. The oysters are huge and fresh. After all the seafood and sweets, it is totally worth the money even for a girl like me who can't eat that much. 
Last but not least, we got there sat afternoon, no line no wait!!!!
P. S. The bf was surprised not only the standard prime rib but the smoked brisket. I Donno what's the big deal about the brisket but he was impressed. 
Another note. Be prepare for five hours of food coma!!!!!!!!

Maybe my expectations were set too high prior to coming to this buffet but my experience did not meet my expectations and I most-likely would not come back unless a big group of my friends come and I am forced to be with the group.

The food was good- don't get me wrong. It wasn't great but it was good for a buffet. However, the service was a-ok. What made my experience not so great was the fact that there were long lines at the seafood station and when I approached the seafood station, there were only about 5 different things. For a "seafood buffet" you would think there would be more seafood dishes.
