And again, I have to stress the high quality of this food. (Sure, if you only get a tiny plate or salad, then yes, you've wasted money, but only have yourself to blame.)

The people cooking/prepping at each food station work hard to maintain the quality, and it shows. Is every single item they put out perfect? No. But the majority of the items are great. There was even a chocolate cake pop at the dessert station that completely blew my mind.  A cake pop!!  And did I mention that the selection is so wide and varied that I think a normal person would need at least 4-5 visits at different times of day to experience a bit of it all? Other Yelp reviewers go over the different food stations so I won't repeat that here.  Suffice to say there was just so much good food!

As for service, it was generally good. Our first server was slow with drinks/refills, but on a different visit the server was spot on. Separate bussers go from table to table clearing old plates.  We never had a dirty plate stay too long at our table.

I will note that there was no long line the times we went mid-week so that added to my positive review. Also, we had our young grade school age kids with us, and they enjoyed it too.

Exceeded our expectations and was an unexpected highlight of our trip. 5 stars.
The food is good, but the wait time is ridiculous. We waited for two hours, so to make up for the wait, we ate for about two hours!
Tons of food, good quality.  The only thing was their prime rib wasn't that good but everything else was pretty good.

Once you digest the price of this buffet, you can enjoy one of the higher end buffets out there. The Bellagio is the best priced buffet in my opinion but this Bacchanal Buffet is the best tasting buffet I've been to. 

Price: $44.99 / $43.99 (TR Member). You pay a reduced rate of $25 if you have the buffet of buffet pass. (Separate Review of the BoB pass) 

Is $45 per person the best use of money? Probably not unless you're going to drink a lot of champagne / mimosas (only until 3pm). Which we did :)

We ended up going twice within a 24 hr period and my first mistake was going straight for the buffet food. On the 2nd visit, I sipped my coffee while eating dessert as my appetizer.  

WAIT: The buffet opens at 8am on the weekends. We had no wait on Saturday at 8:30am and about a 15 min wait on Sunday. I've read that some people have waiting over two hours for this thing and I just don't think that's good planning. Go early or avoid peak lunch / dinner times. 

SERVICE: The cashiers, host, waitress (Sat - Maria R), waiter (Sun - Hector) were all first class. Each person really provided great service on each visit and we rarely had to ask for refills. 

FOOD: The food there was 98% fresh and made that day. The seafood selection was top notch and I always say that you can spot a good seafood buffet when you see us minorities constantly up in the mix there. They have U12 shrimp that's very fresh and the crab legs are cracked so that it's easy to pick out the meat. The Asian selection at the far end of the buffet was great. 

What sets this food apart from the other buffets is that you feel like most dishes have a personal signature on them. While the line cooks are there making the food, it's obvious that a chef crafted many of the meals there and it's translated well. 

There were some dishes that looked like leftovers from the light before but even the batter on the chicken with the waffles was really flavorful. 

They do need to get rid of those plastic looking cheeseburger sliders. They're like hockey pucks. They just don't have a long shelf life and other people have commented about them here. 

Would I go again at $45 a pop. YEP but not at peak times and I'd go before 3pm on the weekend when they have unlimited mimosas / champagne.

First...thank you Yelpers with positive ratings.  Bacchanal Buffett It is everything and then some!  I started brunch at 12:30 for breakfast and stayed until 4pm for early dinner.  I wished I took pictures of my plate"s" but I enjoyed eating too much to stop!  For anyone that hasn't been make this your first buffet stop on your visit.  Make sure you wear your "stretchy "pants and loose shirts and block out some time because you are not going to want to leave after a couple of plates.  

I paid $60 for the buffet and all you can drink (Champagne, Mimosa & Beer).  Well worth it, my server Socorro was awesome and she was attentive. The vibe is very modern And contemporary not your cafeteria style dining area!

I don't know if I can ever give any buffet 5 stars because I always walk away from one hating myself a little bit. Bacchanal is pricy (~$33 for lunch on a weekday) so you will see people including myself overeat here to try to get their "money's worth". I will say though, when I first entered this restaurant, I felt a sense of wonderment with the amazing variety of the food. Everything here was tasty...just remember, all things are better in moderation!
It was okay, nothing special. I liked the oxtail soup and the poki salad. The boiled crab legs were good. Prime rib was dry. Desserts were awesome.

The food at this buffet is AMAZING! Pretty pricy but considering the foods that are provided, understandable. VERY CROWDED! Lines can be anywhere from 45 minutes to 3 hours (depending on what times you go at). Exquisite food that is always changing on a day to day basis and AMAZING desserts :). Very good :)
I give this place 4 stars because it takes so freaking long to wait in line, and the layout of the buffet could be better.  The food is great though!

A new king of the buffets has been crowned in Las Vegas for me. Everything top to bottom was outstanding (except the price) Actually didn't have to wait to get in, got seated right away on a Thursday at around 5 pm.  Started with king crab legs and shrimp cocktail. Excellent legs and perhaps the biggest shrimp I've seen at a casino buffet. 2nd plate was the smoked meats section. Really good BBQ style meats and I'm from an area that specializes in this, so I know good BBQ when I taste it. Italian and Asian sections I only dabbled in, for I was getting quite full. Desserts were fine, I'm not a huge sweet eater to judge. Service was great, never had an empty glass or dirty plate in front of me. 1 thing to improve; the prime rib. very dry and overcooked when I asked for medium rare.

Not impressed at all. I had high hopes and was really let down. Wicked spoon is way better. Nothing special at all here. Nothing was great and barely anything was good. Service wasn't even good. I will not be back.

We ate labor $129 for 2, before the food is good, now the food is salty, too expensive, quality not like before and long line you have to wait for the kiosk, line to pay and line to wait for the table. Please close the mexican food section no one cares about it and you can eat better mexican food outside, taco bell is better. For the price is not worth coming.

5 stars for a buffet, It better be out of this world!  It has to revolutionize buffets as we know it.  Short of serving Unicorn and Dragon meat, Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace delivers.  WOW and do they deliver.  I am going to give you an idea of what they were serving this Saturday night I went and do a little review on the food.

As you enter, you see the "modern", fresh clean look of the restaurant.  They have different stations and they actually cook your food, made to order at each station!  The line starts with the seafood.   They have someone that offers to steam your snow crab legs or you can get it off the rack cold.  They have 4 people in the back schucking Oysters and the had a Monster pile of large shrimp.  Curve around the corner you they have small plates of food ready to go (a la Wicked spoon).  Clam bake, Seafood Piaia, boiled shrimp w/head on, Lobster chowder..etc.

The next station is the bar b que station.  They were cutting brisket and cowboy bone in steaks.  Chicken and fries, Mac and cheese..etc.

We then have an Artisan bread station (which I did not try) and goes to the Mexican Food station.  Fresh made tortillas to order, with Al Pastor cut from the rack!  Amazing Salsa bar.

Then it curves around to the italian station with Pizza, pasta, Lasagna, meatballs etc...  Continues to a Cheese and meat station (yes they have a designated section entirely of meat and cheeses.)

Continuing down the line to the Salad Station and then the made to order Noodle bar!  They Noodle bar makes Ramen, Wonton noodles, and Pho.  

Now to the Asian Section.  they had Amazing Duck (large Large pieces), Char Sui, Moves to Sushi then to Japanese Curry station with Chinese Porridge.

If that was not enough, it moves to the Dim sum section (Har Gow, Shui Mai, Sho Long Bai, Lotus wrapped rice, Char Shui Bao etc..)  Then finally to the Asian noodle section (Pad Thai, Fried noodles..etc.)

I did not event mention the dessert section which features a Crepe (made to order) section, Candy bar (yes like at weddings), Banana's Foster, Gelato and Amazing Maccaroons (that rival Payard's across the way).

Phew, that was just from the amazing memory of seeing everything, but to give you a review of the food:

Noodle Bar:  Worth the trip alone!  I went back twice for the Ramen Noodles.  They serve it in their special Tonkotsu broth.  AMAZING. You would think you were at a Ramen house.  Not too salty, but savory with a hint of pork fat.  I added a piece of duck in it to give it a bit more emphasis.  I went back twice to get it !

Mexican Taco's:  Had the Al Pastor.  It was very flavorful and the tortilla really makes this taco great.  Like any great taco place, they made the tortilla fresh and put the Al Pastor on it.  I would suggest getting the taco and moving to the salsa bar and put your own toppings.  

Seafood Bar:  I had the cooked snow crab legs and they were sweet and on point.  I liked it better than the cold version.  The fresh Oysters were great also!  I am weary about raw items at a Buffet, but the quality was great and it had a great sweet, smooth taste with only hint of the ocean on the backside.  Perfect!  The Lobster chowder was smokey (from the bacon) and smooth.  Very good.

Meat Cutting station:  The lamb chops were the best ever.  I used to think the Wynn buffet Lamb Chops were great, but these were twice as big, medium rare and just a little gamey.  They are a must.  I did not try anything else, but the Brisket and the Cowboy steak looked perfectly cooked.

The Dim sum was good not great.  Har gow skin was thick and the Shui Mai was ok.  Sho long bai was a bit dry, but we are not going to get HK dim sum at any buffett.

I made a plate of Duck and Char Shui rice (like at Sam woo)  The Duck was as good as any Chinese Restaurant with large chunks, a lot of meat.  Sweet and great skin, I found this to be one of the best part of the meal, since i also put it in the noodles.

I had the Nutella/Banana Crepe and it was wonderful, but the Macaroons were the star of the buffet.  I had to ask if they were from Payards, and they told me were not, but the place that brings it in always gets mistaken for the Payards Macaroons.  They sweet, crispy with just a hint of the "jam" layer.  Not over powering, just right.

I used to think the Sterling Brunch was the best Buffet.  Although it still is one of the best I found the fresh food stations, made to order, put Bacchanal over the top.  Next to the lobster tails w/Caviar at Sterling Brunch, Bacchanal is the new sherriff in town and I highly recommend to everyone!

You need to go here. It's as good as you're going to get at a buffet. Out of probably 30 different dishes I tried (one bite each​ is my trick), I didn't like ONE. That is impressive in my book. I will be eating here when I'm around LV. Expensive, totally worth it. Great service.

Sure the experience was cool, but the food was a disappointment,service was terrible not worth it for the price. The only things good were prime rib, crab,tacos and the dessert bar.  The bus staff was very slow to clean our tables and others. The soups were good but not hot enough, barely warm soup. We were at the brunch buffet and the sushi selection was very minimal. There were NO SIGNATURE dish that make this place stand out versus other buffet.

We opted for the buffet. My husband likes to try a variety of food.. Which they def. had, I love that they serve Sushi- Dim sum Mexican food- American- seafood.. If was a great mix!! Only disappointment was when I went to get the nigiri tuna sushi- they were out!! It is a bit pricey and there is a wait.. But that's okay.. You get what you pay for!! Enjoyed!!!  We will come back on our next trip!!!

We went for dinner ,so went there and took waiting ticket from kiosk at 4:15 pm , got a text by 4:30 to join the line so we entered the line by 4:40(we were killing time around ceasers palace ) ,got a seat by 5:20 ! Started our savage !! You basically have all sections Spanish ,Italian ,Mexican , Asian ,etc .!! Loved the crabs and deserts !! So good !!! Too much to eat !

As Buffet's go this is the nicest, most elegant and the best quality food I have seen yet!
I don't think I had one bad thing here. Everything was super fresh and amazing thought and preparation put into each item. The only thing that could have been better was the Stone Crab Claws, they didn't have much flavors at all and you had to crack them open yourself. I had about 5 or 6 plates. I recommend getting small amounts of everything no matter how good it was so that was you can try everything. There is a lot to cover. I Highly recommend this place. Even if your not a buffet person you will still like this. I love high end buffets with high quality food and this was no exception.

There were a variety of foods from different cultures. For example for asian food they had: pho, ramen, roasted pork & duck and the infamous dim sum. Although there were a plethora of colors and choices to choose from, nothing much stood out. The only item which I found worthy of writing in detail about was the made-to-order tacos. The al pastor, carne asada and pollo were all very good. They also had the proper dips for you to craft on the side.

Vegetarians beware: this is an incredibly poor deal for non-carnivores/pescatarians. 

My boyfriend (a seafood lover) and I came here on a whim for our last meal in Vegas before heading to the airport. We figured a buffet of this size would surely have veggie-friendly options. Wrong.

First off, the service is terrible. Everyone working here seems so unhappy, which was sad to see and it definitely influenced the atmosphere. We didn't see our waitress for the first 30 minutes after being seated, but luckily fresh juices are available next to the Mexican food. She was pretty much M.I.A. the entire time we dined and dirty dishes weren't cleared. 

As for the food itself, labeling is very poor and it's difficult to get the attention of anyone behind the counter to inquire about whether items are veggie-friendly. When I asked for veggie tacos at the Mexican station, there was an incredible amount of cross-contamination since the area where meat had just been cooked was used for the rice/veggie combo. Nothing else was memorable (other than strawberry-balsamic gelato), so check out photos if you really want to see documentation of this depressing meals 

My boyfriend was so happy with the seafood, but was so sad to see my dishes because he was shocked by how few options there were for me. We had just gone to Wicked Spoon the day prior and had an incredible time, so neither of us decided this visit to an equally famous buffet to be such a waste.

I'm trying my hardest to not give this buffet a 2-star rating. Because honestly if you hover that tiny little mouse over the 2-star rating, it reads "Meh. I've experienced better." And frankly, I have. Hands down my favorite buffet in Vegas so far is Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo (see my review for more about it) and taking second billing would be the Wynn Buffet (also reviewed).

Reason why I'm not giving it a 2 is because it's not horrible; I didn't get food poisoning, food wasn't tasteless, I didn't leave hungry. BUT I did regret what I paid for and felt absolutely disappointed in choosing to eat here. I understand that they're known for their wide variety of items to choose from which there were, but the quality of those items were pretty run of the mill. Chips and salsa. Mac and cheese. Your token "Asian section" with chow mein and fried rice. The seafood section was lackluster. My cod was dry and bland. Probably the only food item I did like was their truffle scalloped potatoes. I went for seconds on that one - must have! But that's about it. Their dessert section didn't excite me. I think I ate all my custard cause it tasted like leche flan (shout out to all my Filipinos), sampled the rest of the desserts and pushed them to the side of my plate. Super wasteful but I pretty much saved other people's time from grabbing a sub-par dessert. You're welcome, Vegas patrons.

You expect grandeur at a place like this, well at least I did. Especially with this kind of price tag, you expect tiny ass rainbows to come shooting out of your eyes as you body roll in your seat making yummy noises. Sadly, none of these things happened. I was left rainbow less and my body refused to roll.

I would not come back. Sorry, Bacchanal. I'm probably better off taking my money elsewhere... slots anyone?

Had heard of this buffet and I finally tried it this past weekend!!!! This buffet is by far the best buffet I have tried so far. It is pricey but worth it once you try the food!! I have tried other buffets from the Mirage's, planet hollywood's, and Rio's.  My fave used to be the Rio's buffet because they have lobster but the last 2times i've gone it does not taste the same. The lobster does not even taste fresh, it made me feel sick/nauseous. But the Bacchanal buffet, OMMMMGGG!! Eveything i got was very tasteful/delicious! I will definitely come back!!! My favorite was the mexican pozole, pad thai noodles, lamb, and the desserts were ALL delicious!

From a food perspective....  the meats were awesome.  Prime rib?  boo yah dawgie dawg.

Asian food was pretty good for buffet style.   The sushi rice was packed in although I think their mixture for making sticky rice was a little tooooo sticky since the rolls would clump together.  Sushi in general fine although not as good in choice as sushi buffets but made up in the plating and a few choice things that you usually can't get in buffets like temaki rolls.

They actually made a go at soup dumplings which I was definitely interested in.  It's by no means Din Tai Fung, but they were pretty yummy considering.  I think they packed them in little tin foil platters just so they could hold the warmth that's needed and have a little of the soup in them.

Didn't have the crab legs, but I will say that pre-cut crab legs are a good idea in theory, but less great in reality.   It's still hard to crack without a nutcracker.

You can actually make things to order which is definitely a HUGE plus for this place.

Also, a huge miss for most buffet goers was the special salads (watermelon and feta cheese) and the prosciutto.   I think that in general it scares the general populace because it's different from what you expect in a buffet.

Damned good coffee.  That's all you can really say about that.

Desserts looked awesome.  I can't really say how they tasted since I'm not a big fan of desserts in general.

Service was excellent and the logistics of opening a place like that has got to be a nightmare.   So I was happy to see that drinks were taken care of and waiters were always on top of their game.   Curious to see if 6 months to a year from now, if that would still be the case.

Overall, it's a great buffet to check out.  Not sure if it's the best in the world, but for sure it's unique enough to contend.

Just great. I ate crab legs, mussels, and oysters for breakfast at this place. They will steam the crab legs for you. Everything was really fresh, they had a nice selection of foods-- but if you are a seafood lover, you can eat your $50 worth of seafood anytime of day at this place. I tried some of the breakfast items and they were very good, the service and presentation was great-- worth the money. Avoid the line for breakfast by going early.

Omg! Best place in town m, HANDS DOWN!!! 

Not only is the food delicious, wide spread and fresh but the service is on point! Every time I ask the cook/chief to make anything that's not on the display they do it with no questions asked. I'm a huge fan of Philadelphia rolls, so when it's not on display I ask & they make it right away. The cook Robert was friendly, attentive & hooked me up with some feda chinni Alfredo.

Keep up the great work.! 

And p.S 

To the servers need improvement on their attitude!
just ok.  would not go back for $50.  the yelpers giving 5 stars do not know any better and are the Obama voters.

We were in Vegas for the World Series of Beerpong; and because my husband wanted to take me out on a date before we flew back to the real world; i got to pick a brunch place!

I picked this..

And mind you.. It did not disappoint.

We got here a little after 10am and we got there at a very good time. There weren't any lines yet.... (no f*cking joke; there were like 30 people in line after a good 30mins since we got there. and it was a Monday)....

Incredible ambiance; Attentive servers and AMAZING Seafood bar.

Since this was brunch; i started off with the breakfast items...

If you know me; you would know that i work out for Bacon. I am Bacon Girl and I had a Bacon themed party and i am not ashamed.

Anyway; they have Turkey bacon (boring!) and Regular Bacon (perfectly cooked with all it's crispness and crunchiness but not overcooked) AND they actually have a Bacon Slab.
A freaking BACON SLAB. and you know what? YOLO with a capital YO.

I wasn't a fan of the sweet and sour chicken and waffle cone --because i like the southern version.. Fried chicken and waffles and syrup. PERIOD. no fancy schmancy sweet and sour yuck.

Then i moved on to Steak and Eggs. AMAZING.

Then i moved on to the Seafood bar and tasted the JUICIEST Crawfish EVER.
Yeah i've tasted crawfish from New Orleans.. and these were seriously at the same level. NO JOKE.

Chef's creations: were mussels and Raw Oysters. YUMMMMMM!!!!!
Also..Some Crab. Love!

With the breakfast and seafood bars; i thought i was already in heaven...

But come come... there was a LEFT TURN to another room with more FOOD!

There's a cheese station with crackers and bread... there's a mexican food station; there's a DIMSUM station. oh dear the Dimsum was exceptional for a buffet level.
and there were some chinese dishes that I didn't even get to try anymore.

and of course there was a dessert station (crepes and more) that I didn't even get to either because.

FULL.

A must try and you really get your money's worth. (especially with the expensive Seafood they have!!!)

Our group decided to eat here after reading that this was rated #1 in Vegas. I have to admit it was impressive, great variety and everything we tried was exceptional. The dessert  bar seemed to be the best feature to our group. Having said all of that, $60 dollars a plate for a buffet is just too much in my opinion. Kids loved it though, so all good.

Definitely the very BEST Buffet experience I have ever had.  So why not the 5 stars?  The price...for what the food is, I just can't in good conscience fork over that kind of cash for the grub each time.  This place is 100% worth trying, but I hope the "hype" dies down someday and the buffet pass is taken here without the additional monies PER MEAL that is currently required.

Love this area! Dessert is really good and for a variety! I prefer the steamed king crab leg, it is hot and fresh. You need a cracker for this. Stone Crab is also a recommendation. The most surprised is Chinese style veggie, that is my favorite part. Prime Rib is juice. Worth to try! Do not miss!

Came here with my boyfriend at 3:30pm on a Wednesday in January in hopes of avoiding a wait... but there was already a wait! Stood in line for about 60 minutes before getting seated... at a very shitty table next by the Asian food section. The table was propped against the wall, probably because IT WASN'T EVEN STABLE. It would see-saw whenever we put plates on it. Secondly, to get to my chair, I'd have to squeeze between a pillar and the table. What the hell? Thank goodness I'm 105lbs; otherwise, I don't know where I would sit. 

So... seating 0/5

Food: 3/5
It's a buffet! Don't come here expecting quality, come here expecting quantity. I loved the Blackened Chicken Soup in the Asian section... probably the only thing I "loved". Their macarons looked incredibly sad... the shells were all broken, smashed, or scraped off. It tasted good though, despite it's pitiful appearance. I don't even know how they made it into the bowl. Mac n' cheese tasted alright, mashed potatoes were good; actually, most of their potatoe dishes were tasteful. Had their "Watermelon Mint" ice cream, which was definitely unique. Tasted all their meats, I'd say it was good. Crab legs were alright.

Decor: 5/5
I love the decor here. It's very modern, clean, and bright. Classy, too.

Overall, I would have enjoyed it much better if we weren't seated at a poor excuse for a table.

More like BOTCHanal Buffet..

Let me start by saying that I don't usually take the time to review things on yelp, because I feel other people will usually do a good job of posting accurate reviews.  With that said, I usually write a review when something is really good, really bad, or I disagree with the majority of reviews.  Here's my review:

THIS PLACE IS OVERRATED!!!

I've been to buffets that are 50% cheaper and have the same quality, selection, and better service.  Granted, we had a very responsive busboy and server.  But man, the hosts and hostesses could not count or prioritize to save their lives.  We ended up waiting 265 minutes total.  Then when we got to the front of the line, the "joke-stess" called forward a party behind us.  She told us we would only have to wait 2 more minutes, which turned out to be 30 more minutes.  We had to complain to the manager in order to be seated.  And finally, when the rope line was opened for us to go sit down, the hostess miscounted the number of people in our group by a large amount.  Whether for lack of attention or inability to count, they obviously were not running the place competently.  

Similar to what another reviewer stated, we got to our table to find that there were plenty of open tables that would have accommodated our group.  We also saw that they seated a party with less people than ours at a table meant for 8.  

O_O

Ok enough of the introductions--let's get on to the food.

Many people seemed crazy about the crab legs.  I guess many people go to buffets only for the crab.  I go for everything.  

Typically, buffet food is a little stale because it kinda sits there for a while.  For the price this place charges, you would think their food would be a little different......  not the case.    this food is your usual crusty-edged garbage that results from being over exposed to warming lamps.  

The variety of options was also not impressive.  Even if there were items that are not normally at a traditional buffet, people didn't choose them.  They just remained in the heating lamps drying out.  My guess is that there is a reason some dishes are not typically served at buffets.   

Overall, this place felt on par with other buffets that charge around 20-25 dollars.  
Save your money, time, and the headache for something else!!

P.S.- BE PREPARED FOR ANNOYING PEOPLE TAKING CELLPHONE PICTURES OF ALL THE FOOD.

This is my first buffet experience in Vegas.  I only wish I had another stomach to fill my belly with all yummy goodness they had to offer.  Brunch on Saturday for two, total around $90.  I was impressed with the array of different cuisines they had.  I'm typically not a buffet lover, but I did enjoy the food here.  I would have to say my favorite item there was the prime rib.  It was so juicy and cooked perfectly.  

Presentation of food is on point and I wanted to eat everything.  The décor is very modern and clean.  I was a little disappointed with the flavors of the dessert they offered.  I was expecting to be blown away with the wide assortment of sweets, but found myself just missing that wow factor in flavor.

So after weeks of reviewing buffets before my long awaited trip to Las Vegas I decided to try this one out for the first time.  The buffet has a really good selection with all different types of food .  HOWEVER....the quality of food wasn't really any better than say, the Carnival Buffet at the Rio. The price tag was $109 just for my wife and I on a Monday.  Again, the food was good, but definitely not great.  I probably won't be coming back to this one for a while.

This is probably the best buffet in Vegas. There is a large variety of foods and they are all good quality. The service is exceptional, our waiter constantly checked up on us and took away all of our finished plates. Their dessert bar is phenomenal, they have a station with freshly made crepes and they have a plethora of different desserts. For 40$ per person, you are getting your moneys worth.

We arrived at 10:15am on 12/21, there is no wait at all!!!!! Lucky us! This is our second time here, everything was as expected. The only thing is this holiday season, it's $46.99 per person, $29.99 for kids. The thumb of rules are arrive early to avoid the long wait.

I've never been to a Vegas buffet so of course I have to try what everyone considers the best!

We came around lunch time so I guess it was technically still considered brunch...which meant we only paid $50! The wait wasn't too bad - they have electronic things you can fill out which will text you when it's your turn to wait in the actual line. It took around 40 min but we just spent that wandering around the casino. Once in the actual line, it was about another 20-30 minutes I'd say? All in all, not as bad as I anticipated. 

Now for the food...definitely more high end than I'm used to and I loved the variety. However nothing was so amazing I wanted seconds. The mushroom and truffle pizza was pretty bomb though. I was a bit disappointed in the prime rib and tri-tip because the pieces I got were WAYYY overcooked. The best thing I ate was probably the creme brulee. The other desserts are not worth getting - save yourself the pain. I tried the tiramisu and the tapioca, among many others, and those two were the stand out worst. I almost spit out the tapioca because it was simply inedible. But yeah yeah get the creme brulee. That one's worth it.

3.5/5 stars IMO. Good to experience at least once, but probably won't come back.
for the price.... poor quality food. rude hostesses. menu is only created for Asian clientele . worst experience in Las Vegas for us who only visit high end eateries.
Disappointment from last time no King crab legs and no large shrimp cocktail. The food was good. But they have scaled it down. Didn't think it was worth $50.

My favorite Vegas buffet! (replacing my previous favorite, Wicked Spoon).

The quality and variety of food they are able to achieve at Bacchanal is amazing.  It's the only buffet where I can honestly say I would be happy with many of their items if I had ordered them a la carte. 

The line and wait can be very long. The first time we tried to go here (many hours before our flight) we had to step out of line because the wait was so long that we were in danger of missing our flight.  I would highly recommend going early or maybe try on a weekday if you can. 

But once you get through the line...
The quality and flavors here are absolutely fantastic.

A must try!
Pretty good food, HUGE range of selection, comfortable ambiance, fabulous customer service, by far the best buffet we had in Vegas.

Dinner time Price: 49.99 + tax. 

Food: Top of the line raw oysters, crab legs, meat selection, cooked salmon, cooked chilean sea bass. Nothing salty or overcooked. The shrimp were big and seemed like they were gulf shrimp with quite a bit of flavor. I did notice that they had a cooked lobster in the display case by the entrance/line but there was no lobster to be found on the buffet. 

Dessert was great with fresh ice cream selections and huge chocolate-covered strawberries, etc. 

The atmosphere: The place is huge and they play club music which seems designed to get you out of there. That was a big negative, but the food was very good. I wouldn't go back at prime time dinner because of the huge crowds and lines. If they are still playing that music, it's really annoying.

Go early if you go because the line gets long.

BEST.... BUFFET....EVER....

I did not want to leave...seriously..
It's a must try, completely enjoyed every single bite that i had in this place
It's like if the Wicked Spoon Buffet and The Bellagio Buffet had a baby it would be this! and i went on friday so who knows how amazing it gets during the weekend!

First off, if you're going during the week and want to save some money, go in before 3PM, around 230issh so you can pay lunch price for dinner;)

The seafood station was amazingggg..One of the best parts of my meal was definitely the king crab, it was cut open for you and served warm if desired! The had oysters, mussels, oyster shooters and large cocktail shrimp for days.

Went here when it first opened and completely hated it other than the decor so years later when it's being touted as the best buffet in town I had to give it another try. I happy to say they are doing better but not by much. The food selection seemed like it went on forever and there was no way I was gonna be able to try everything. So I had to strategically go through the buffet.

First stop the Asian station...I had the lumpia which didn't have a single piece of meat inside, the sesame balls which were reminiscent of Sunday dim sum with family, exactly 1 bite of the hot and sour soup because it tasted nothing like its name sake, and some roasted duck which Sam woo definitely does better. Oh and the pork stuffed chicken wing which didn't have much flavor

Next was the American/carving station. The roast beef was cooked well but didn't have a lot of flavor. The everything corn was the highlight of this section...reminded me of elotes. The Mac n cheese has no flavor and the baked beans where no better than out of the can. The mashed potatoes at least look homemade cause the skin where mashed in but tasteless again.

On to the seafood bar...first had to try the hot crab and sadly too salty again. So I tried the cold crab to see it it had the same problem which it did. The oysters though were exactly what an oyster should be...fresh and tastes of the sea! The garlic soup in the escargot was delicious but the shrimp cocktail were small smooshy and water soaked...almost as if they had been thawed after being frozen for too long.

Last of the savory was the Mexican section...the redeeming quality of this buffett was the man making the special order tacos...he was cheery, did a little chit chatting while cooking gave me my al pastor taco and informed me that all the condiments where at the end of the bar...he genuinely seemed like he enjoyed his job. The taco was pretty good too!

Lastly was the dessert bar...while the last time I visited the gelato bar was the only section in the buffet that held up to its reputation of offering new and innovative flavors, it just wasn't the case anymore...all the flavors had been replaced with classics...strawberry, chocolate, vanilla...the most complex flavor I could find was ginger green tea and this bar must have been the yin to the Mexican bar yang cause the man serving the ice cream could have not been in a pissyer mood...he hated his job! The buffet no longer makes the fresh soufflé thank god cause they were awful but they do offer freshly baked lava cake which were equally as bad...barely warm chocolate cake with no lava in the middle. 

All in all I don't I will coming back to this buffet which is too highly priced, serves dreaded Pepsi products, and just doesn't match my taste buds when there are much better options in town.

I rarely go to buffets just because I know that it's impossible to have everything up to par. I kinda felt like that was the case at the buffet there. Certain things were spot on but many of the main dishes were weak. The brisket was great, ribs were cold and a bit gummy & the sausage was too greasy with not enough flavor & also cold. They had some of the best mashed potatoes I've ever had & when you added the gravy took it somewhere crazy for me lol! the Mac & cheese was bland. I wasn't a fan of the pasta, but they made great ramen & the pork broth was identical to the soup houses in japan. The tacos were money!! Boiled crab legs were on point & they cut them down the middle which made it a neat treat. I can go on & on but overall it's not worth the wait unless you're really patient and can't decide what you want for dinner lol. It's a step above golden coral if you ask me
One star knocked off for the cold air conditioning and 1 star knocked off for the loud music and the food was good so it will be only 3 stars.

Whenever i go to Vegas I love the buffets. We went at an off time -- Saturday at 3:30pm. The wait was about 45 minutes. We were starving but was too cheap to pay the extra $15 for the express line. 

My favorite part of the buffet: So easy to get crab. You just have to hand them an empty plate and they fill it up with warm crab leg goodness!

Ive tried most all the famous vegas buffets and i have to say that this is one of the top 3 if not, my favorite of them all. Once you walk in, the designing of the place is just great and beautiful. Same as most buffets, the food is separated by country specialties. I really enjoyed all the japanese, italian, and american items. My family and i had at least 5 plates of steamed crab legs alone. But my absolute favorite is the country of desserts! I had a taste of all the dessert items and it satisfied my extreme sweet tooth. The service is fantastic as well! Its definitely worth the price to take a visit. Come hungry!

This place is good. 120$ for dinner but so much food. The Asian food was the best in my opinion. Dumplings are delicious! Only down side is seafood is a little flavorless and some dish looked as if the were sitting for a long time. Dessert was the best! Try it! I don't think it's a disappointment.
Fresh, tasty, amazing food! Awesome variety! Fantastic service! Couldn't ask for more!

The buffet is expensive and not really worth it. The food is just okay. We even found an insect in our crab. We informed the manager and the only thing we got was another plate of crab meat which was boiled by the same pot. Will not recommend to our friend at all.

The food is great. In my opinion one of the 2 best buffets in Las Vegas but the management need to replace all these incompetent, attention deficit people managing the entrance of this place.  It was a very frustrating experience to see them go back and forth stack and restack receipts, piling and recounting. Check in parties of same number of people as us who came 20 minutes after us, through the regular line before us. 

I suggest to management to have a customer service expert observe the check in process to watch this lady interact with customers and get to their own conclusion.

We were here twice for dinner, but it's impossible to sample everything - there is so much!  Wonderful selections; something for everyone.

Service is superb and friendly; never had to wait for refills on beverages and always served in a clean glass each time. Perfectly clean everywhere. 

Comfy seating in a modernistic environment.

Entrees/Beverages: some of my favs were the shrimp, brisket, prime rib, truffled scalloped potatoes, salmon, delicately flavored peach tea, and believe it or not, the best mac & cheese I've ever had! 

Didn't waste my time on chicken, salads or petite hamburgers; I can have those anywhere at home.

Many options at the dessert area.

It's an attractive buffet and dining experience. You don't have to dress too fancy, but at least change out of your tee shirt and grubby jeans and be a bit more presentable. Go and enjoy!

No question food is best of any buffet in town, both on quality of raw ingredients, as well as preparation.  Great choice. Seafood and Asian are best buffet areas in town. But it's not a pleasant experience.  Wait takes forever.  You get a time. Then come back and stand in line to pay. Then wait to be seated.  Even with time slots you are in line forever.  Setting is very pretty but actual buffet layout is poorly planned. Feels like one long line.  Not broken up well so you are pretty shiny through people in one line to get to another.  The dessert area almost makes up for this.  Basically it's great if you can find a time when it doesn't feel like a bus station. But for my money Wynn is a much nicer dinner even if food is not quite as good.

I 







I was highly satisfied by the hostess. She was the sweetest lady and was helpful getting us seated. She was informative about the food and drinks(more later). Bought a special online for brunch -2 people. Now it didn't say unlimited mimosas but it also didn't say it. To our surprise by the second drink we're told it's an additional $15 per person for unlimited mimosas. No problem but maybe let us know when your reading off our ticket.

They have a wide variety of food, Italian,Mexican, Asian, seafood and so on. Desserts... I'm not much of a sweet fan l, so I only had fruits and a sample of their ice cream, which was delicious. My friend loved the Mussels and I liked the spring rolls, pizza, The chow mein was always cold, like I always missed the new batch. 

There was a omelette/egg maker by the pasta area. He was great too!

I truly think this is the best brunch in Vegas. Overall I enjoyed and will come back

VERY good they have so much selection of food
i mean the quality isnt the best but they do have a lot of differnet types of food in a nice 
 
iv been here twice and rememebr i had to be taken to my hotel room via forklift...its NUTS i ate the whole place it was delicious! 

only knock ont his place is the CCCCCCCCRAZY PRICE but could be worth it. watch out for the line! can be super long. they also have a cheasy fast pass line where you pay extra...oh vegas....so dirty

Jeez, I don't know where to begin with this review. 

First of all, the intricate details that go into the interior of this buffet blew my mind. You will marvel at not only the aesthetic presentation of the food but also the upscale design of the buffet itself. I was mind-blown during my entire three-hour pig-out session at Bacchanal this past Monday. Imagine any type of food you could possibly want. You name it. Bacchanal's got your back; it sure had mine. 

This buffet is like an eclectic haven of cultural dishes: sushi, tacos, dim sum, eggs benedict, ramen, udon, pasta, etc. The list goes on and on. I think it's amazing that a buffet could hit nearly every cultural taste, not to mention the aesthetics and enriching flavor that go into play for the dishes. Nearly each dish was of superb quality in terms of taste and presentation. I've tried most of the dishes there, and Bacchanal has not failed me. 

And, the dessert bar. Wow. I was overwhelmed by the wide selection of desserts they had: gelato, cheesecake, tiramisu, etc etc. And, let me tell you. I sampled a good amount of the desserts. They were bomb, especially the cheesecake. 

I could rave on and on about this buffet, but I'll stop here. I recommend every dish/dessert at this buffet. I think the price and wait is worth it. 

Regarding prices: 
7:30am - 10am: $29.99 + tax
10am - 3pm: $39.99 + tax 
after 3pm: $54.99 + tax

Gosh...where to start? Just kidding! I've been waiting in line for over an hour just to pay! They pick out larger parties in the pay line to cut in front of parties of two...then you have to wait in another long ass line just to be seated to eat.

1 1/2 hr later.....OMG, We made it to the front of the "eat" line!!!....more to come!

Biggest disappointment ever! Food was mediocre. The crab legs were thin and the meats were dry. The only thing that was worth eating were the fresh oysters. I had to stuff myself with shrimp cocktails just to make it worth my money. When exiting the Bacchanal, I was tempted to yell " IT'S NOT WORTH IT!" at everyone waiting in the long ass line!

Service was good though...

Came with high expectations after reading all the good reviews and it being rated as the number one buffet in Vegas.

Variety was not as impressive as expected since all the other buffets I've been to so far have far surpassed in terms in quantity, quality was by far and short also close to the worst that I've occurred and yet at the hefty price of 60usd inclusive of tax, I would have expected so much more.

The Japanese section had close to zero sashimi other than some little Maguro carpaccio sort. Sushi quality wasn't that bad, but it could have have more variety of different fishes. Ramen soup was filled with so much salt, it was not for drinking standards and probably more to dip the noodles. Pho was the best dish at the noodles section and better if you put those cut green chili from the side into the soup.

Seafood selections were few and yet quality was low. The oysters were of a dubious color, and cold crab legs might have been very fresh since it tasted like salt water.

Didn't try much hot food since nothing seemed appetizing enough to make it to my plate. The meat section's beef prime rib was the best dish of the night.

Dessert looked like a party, yet only the cheesecake was palatable. Other cakes were too hard and dry, even the molten lava cake which was warm, was no molten. Crepe was kinda like uncooked flour with no taste whatsoever, even the Nutella topping couldn't save it.

Overall not worth going to, and lucky for our group, we reached a lil before 5 and didn't have to queue for more than 10 mins. Definitely not advisable to wait for a seat anytime more than 30mins.

I wish Yelp would allow video reviews because a walkthrough of this buffet would be epic.  Just to walk from one side of the buffet all the way to the end while taking cursory glances at each item took me 3 whole minutes. Let's go through this:

Ambiance: Everything you expect of a Vegas buffet: upscale and decadent. Cloth tablecloths and napkins and chandeliers made of wine glasses.

Service: The waiters very quick with water and drinks though in a buffet setting I'm usually in a get-out-of-my way type of mentality (jk)

FOOOOODDD: The selection here is amazing. Especially the amount of Asian food that was provided (dim sum, sushi, ramen, zhongzi, stir fry, etc).  And for everyone who complained about food selection, they were obviously not there for the dinner spread. Once dinner hits, the selection of raw oysters, king crab, and mussels come out, with crab being offered both freshly steamed and on the ice.

One tip I have is to come around 2-2:30 as dinner spread comes out at 3:00pm.  A lot of people pile in around 2:45 and hold up the line so I suggest coming a little earlier than that.  Bacchanal doesn't close in the middle of the day like Wicked Spoon does ( on the weekdays) so this trick would only work here. And besides, who wakes up in time for early lunch in Vegas anyway??

Overall, best. buffet. ever. If I could somehow live here, I would.

After reading the reviews I knew I wanted to come here. I would've been seriously let down if the dessert bar didn't save the place. The food here is very creative but I would've been happier if it was executed all the way through. For example the crab cakes. No salt at all! Just a teeny squeeze of lime juice after it was played would've saved the dish. My kids love basic sushi not the uncooked stuff so it would've been nice if they would've had basic rolls out for them to enjoy. We liked the place but I must say we will most likely not go again. It was a good experience for our first Vegas buffet I might add.
Service was great came for brunch the carving station and taco station were our favorites would definitely come again

Very huge buffet with lots of choice!  Crab, oysters, fresh scallops (first time I've seen that here) and a variety of meats and foods.  Sushi, Chinese, Italian...  The buffet is a bit pricy tho, paid $125 for two on a sunday night.  By definitely a must try at least once!

This restaurant is located in Ceasar's Palace and was a little difficult to find but once I started got into the main building and read the signs, I found it immediately.  Look for the Sports bar area and you will see signs pointing you to the Buffet.
Today was my first visit and I walked over just to see what everyone was raving about.  Due to the early hour, I was able to avoid the crowd and was seated immediately.  The hostess asked if I had ever visited before, I let her know this was my first visit.  She proceeded to give me a walking tour showing me what was offered and where the different stations were located.  The fantastic service did not stop there, Jennifer my waitress was extremely friendly and very attentive.  She kept my water glass filled and checked in with me ofter to see if there was anything I needed and how I like my food.  She was FANTASTIC, asked to be seated in Jennifer's area, she will take care of you.  Meat carver was equally as friendly and offered advice on the cut of meat to ask for and offered me larger portions if I wanted it.  He was very patient and informative.
The food was to die for to use an old worn out saying.  There is an abundance of choices, kept fresh and served in a very appealing to the eye manner.  They even include selections for vegetarians and diabetics.
You will not go away hungry, if you do its your own fault.  I will definitely return to this buffet in Ceasar's Palace the next time I am in Las Vegas.

The food was decent. Large variety but can be improved. 

A lot of the Asian cuisine lack flavor or was overcooked. The sushi was great. 

The Italian was great. Meatballs were moist. Ravioli and seafood pasta was on point. 

The American or meat section was decent. The mushroom truffle soup was delicious. The lamb was moist but too games. Lamb by nature is gamely but when properly cooked it's more an aftertaste. 

Seafood was fresh. 

Cremé brûlée was good. Tiramisu was awful. Cheesecake and flan was satisfying.

Variety gives this holiday brunch buffet 4 stars.

Btw, holiday brunch buffet is $52.99 per person. Whether you pick the champagne brunch or the regular brunch both options cost the same. 

No lines at 8:30am - peaceful. 'Til about 10:30am. Then it got real. 

The freshest food during this time is the crepe since these are made upon request. 

And I know what you're thinking after seeing my foodporn...just 4 plates?? What the hockey sticks??

Welp I'm not a volume gorger at buffets - rather I'm an assortment grazer.

Also when there's watermelon juice, I go cray. Not too sweet and packed w/lycopene. You'll thank me later after your next porcelain journey -_0

My fave section has to be the desserts area. I'm partial to sweets w/a hot cup of tea. Oh, their tea brand is Harney & Sons and they give you 3 tea bags *thumbs up*

We left at about 11:30am since again I graze.

The staff were excellent and they left you alone. The empty plates disappeared and the table was always clean.

Finally did you see the packaged terry cloth wet naps thingy? My word. You're great, Bacchanal.

So its $46 for Mon to thurs. $55 for Fri to sun. Great new place. Everything tastes top notch. Cons: There are lines to get the good meat and for seafood. Pros: This is worth the largest selection of food in Vegas. Cons: But I would say, wynn is good enough at a lower price for the crab legs. The crab legs were falling apart at bacchanal. Pros: u can get a souffle made in ten min. It's really good if they don't over bake it. There's macaroons, gelato, mochi which are the 4 best desserts.  The gelatin tho is better tasting at the wynn.
The restaurant is really nice, but the food is not worth $50. The bottomless drinks were amazing. Worth trying out, but I wouldn't go back often.

Wow I'm stuffed to the brim! Love all the crab, shrimp, prime rib and etc. high quality food. We had the groupon for $69 but with the groupon sale only paid $56 with vip (diamond line) and unlimited mimosas. We did not wait long at all, max 15 mins for both lines. We went at 10:35 am and was seated before 11. We got to eat breakfast and lunch. Little plates do cute! Steak and eggs, shrimp and grits. Must try in Vegas

Came here for brunch with my mom and it was delicious. If you get there early, it's a lot less crowded. We weren't in a huge rush, so we tried a good variety of items.  There is literally something for everyone, but the Mexican breakfast dishes were a standout. We also really enjoyed the coffee!  I have to give a special shoutout to the manager who so kindly went above and beyond to let me know the exact type of coffee they brewed there so I could look for it to make at home. Will always return whenever I visit Vegas!

This has got to be the best buffet we have in town! Very worth the price although I feel like they should give the locals some love with the discounts. They have a huge selection of different foods. The seafood area is my favorite. I also love the desserts. The wait staff is very efficient and nice I'll definitely be coming back!!

Being a Vegas local, I truly was not impressed with this buffet. My husband and I had a staycation at the Caesar's and had been wanting to come here for some time. This buffet gave me a feel as if I were at The M Resort buffet or the Rio. My husband is a total foodie and really thought the food was okay. It wasn't bad by any means, but would we pay $69.99 for a weekend dinner again? Probably not. Service was good despite the wait being very long at 7pm on a Saturday night. I feel that any Vegas local will probably consider coming here at one point or another as there is a big hype about this place. Come see for yourself, but personally, I just wouldn't pay this much for this place.

Bacchanal Buffet was like an answer to all your prayers, a dream come true... Their options were endless! 

If you and your significant other don't know where to go, then bring them here. I mean especially if they mean everything to you, then you should give everything to them.

Let's see. They have plenty of seafood! The freshest/largest plump oysters I have ever seen. Snow and king crab, shrimp, and even lobsters ! The crabs were a little salty, but that's something sauce can fix. Besides they save you work cuz the legs are already cut open for you.

They have American food.. steak, Mac n cheese, pizza, hamburger sliders, some pretty darn good French fries, and so on...

They also have Chinese food from the basic lo mien, fried rice, orange chicken, etc...
In addition they have that and dim sum. (Haha get it)

They have Vietnamese pho, they have Japanese sushi, they have Spanish tacos...and they have a bar dedicated to dessert itself!

100 restaurants in one... only catch is it's pretty pricey but it's definitely worth the experience.

Ehh..tbh I don't think any buffet in Vegas is like HORRRIBLE. They're all okay, and tbh so is Bacchanal. I'll admit that I didn't try everything that was there so maybe I just got the stuff that was just ok? 

The one thing that I REALLY liked was there juices..I stole two..ok not stealing since I paid 70 bucks to get in. (YES 70!!) It's because we were a big party so they charge gratuity ): 

Honestly, the only thing that I really liked there was the elote..omg the corn was SO sweet it was amazing lol..yeah i know corn right?!?! But they're creamed corn was whatevzzz..

Clams and mussels are also good but I didn't get my fat butt up to get another serving, I'm also not a fan of king crab legs but I did have a little there. They have the option of getting it from the man out of the pot, or cold ones that are sitting out there already for ya!

Oh another thing..the sushi was fishy ): not cool..blech!

NOT WORTH YOUR TIME AND MONEY. 
Sure they have prime rib, crab legs and other meat and seafood BUT please save your time and money for something else. You are better off eating in a fancy restaurant and spending $30 per head than this. It is just a hype! 

For $60/head, you would expect exceptional service and a complete array of food in the buffet. You won't get it at this joint. Bowls and plates weren't refilled and food at the buffet felt like leftovers. The taste was meh for some dishes too. Also, don't get me startedon the wait. It's a good 3 hours of your life you will never get back. 

If you are looking for a buffet to eat at in vegas, you are better off going to the one at M.

Went for Sunday brunch 9/27/2015 for my friend's birthday.  $49.99 plus tax.  Approximately 30 minute wait at 11:30am.  Original estimate was about 45 minutes but they texted me about 15 minutes in (too bad I was too engrossed in explaining craps and slots to my friends to notice that my phone had beeped about 15 minutes earlier).

Mains:
Selection was pretty good.  King crab legs cold or hot was the thing to get at our table; we must've gotten at least 7 plates of those between four of us.  Guy serving the hot crab legs was very generous with how many he scooped onto your plate.  Jumbo shrimps were good albeit *slightly* overcooked/old.  Sushi was alright except the nigiri was cut into very rectangular prism shapes and had very little raw fish.  Pho and udon were surprisingly decent.  Dim sum was a no-no; har gow and soup dumplings had dry skin and meat.  Prime rib might have been ok if the guy had listened to me when I asked for medium rare instead of looking annoyed that he had to do his job and ignoring me and cutting me a medium-well slice.

Dessert:
Our friend's birthday plate was an assortment of desserts they had at the dessert bar just arranged nicely and a few "happy birthday" chocolates placed here and there.  Desserts were in general quite delicious, especially the chocolate dome truffle-like thing.  Ice cream was no good, unfortunately; it's arranged like gelato but tastes like some of the lowest quality ice cream possible - very icy and not dense or smooth at all.

Best part:
Mimosas were constantly refilled.  Our glasses were almost always full.

Verdict:
It was a good experience, but I wouldn't go back unless a friend really wanted to/I was really craving endless king crab legs and jumbo shrimp with butter and cocktail sauce.

OK, this buffet gets 5 stars right off the bat for me because of one thing: FRESH MOCHI ICE CREAM!

It's very rare to find home-made mochi ice cream anywhere, at least where I come from in Texas. When I order it at restaurants, it's usually pre-made or pre-packaged stuff - but I eat it anyways because I'm addicted to the stuff. So when I came across mochi ice cream in the dessert section at Bacchanal my eyes lit up. When I took my first bite, I was blown away! The mochi was fresh, and if I didn't know any better, I could almost swear they make them in-house.  When I was there, they had multiple flavors including kona coffee, matcha green tea, red bean, BLACK SESAME (!!), and chocolate. I had multiple of each one and they were all amazing! I was in heaaveennnn

So besides the mochi ice cream, other highlights included the raw oysters and the ramen station (whose broth was surprisingly good). Everything else was OK, but good for buffet standards. Looks like they have a fairly large Asian-themed section.

For me, the mochi ice cream alone was worth the price :)
Good varieties on their dinner buffet. Kinda pricey compared to the other buffets but definitely one of the better ones on the strip

Overrated!!!!! Waited in line for 2 hours, just to be seated in a dirty area, and to wait in lines again for the food, which wasn't even all that! $70 pp for Christmas. Crab was watered down, food was a little above average. NOT AT ALL WORTH IT!! Wicked Spoon has better quality, cleanliness, anactually cheaper.
Second time I had a buffet here. Excellent service and variety of foods. Love it. It's a little busy at night

Place is not worth the price of $63. False advertisement online. Lobster is not included with the buffet. Also, they mostly serve snow crab, hardly had any king crab legs. The majority of the food was lukewarm and didn't have much flavor. Rio hotel had a much better buffet for a cheaper price.

"Best buffet in Vegas," I heard. Maybe I set my expectations very high, but this place wasn't as good as everyone mentions and the 200+ people waiting outside for 2 or 3 hours would agree.

Their buffet includes: 
- Chinese food (chasiu, roasted pork ribs, dimsum, soup, sauteed vegetables, etc)
- Dessert: cookies, ice cream, pies, cakes. My favorite was the selection of ice cream!
- Seafood: shrimp, crab legs, oysters
- Italian food
- Mini Steak House
- Noodle Station: udon, ramen, pho, tonkatsu

For the wait and taste, I would probably make sure I am really really really hungry to go. Otherwise, you should save those $60!

Food was average buffet food nothing special for the $50 per person price. Food was good, seafood a bit wet and frozen, overall good. I would disagree that this is the best Vegas buffet. Service was terrific! Atmosphere was modern and clean.

Favorite buffet for this local! Wynn is okay, Bellagio good, Red Rock surprisingly good. But dollar for dollar they just can't touch the Bacchanal. Even just saying the name makes me happy. The Bacchanal. 

The food is AMAZING. The street tacos are still the best thing I've eaten in Las Vegas (sorry Nobu!). The crepe station will make you cry. 

Everything is fresh and hot. The service is awesome and it's a beautiful space. Whenever friends come to town I try to Jedi Mind trick them here! That's one of the coolest perks of living in Las Vegas - out of town guests buying great meals! 

I've read some of the bad reviews and think they must have come on a bad day. Because the 10+ times I've been here have all been outstanding. 

Now if they would only hook up a local discount...or a punch card. Lol.

gonna have to downgrade 2 stars, meat station was nasty. quality of foods went down, wait is super longer now, buuut, they were serving straight from the pot crab legs, waay better than the oversalted ones on ice. the grilled prawns was gooood too. so adding a star for that.
Amazing selections -- Good for a sea food lover
1st Time here the food was amazing and I got to interact with one of the chef Raymundo ,he gave me great service definitely caming back here for my birthday
This place is good only if you want to eat a lot of seafood. Not much choice for vegan folks. Head over to Wicked Spoon or the Aria Buffet - where you will get better quality for a lower price.

Best buffet I've ever been to. They do many different cuisines beautifully and the dessert / gelato bar is outstanding. Lamb / Steak is done beautifully although the carver told me that the steamship round of beef was wagyu and I really don't think it was. However, the wait is 1.5 hours (but worth it, you can check in and then walk around so go early). One other however: they're really bad about removing used plates and even though we were Diamond Club holders, I had to bus our own dishes to get some room!

Went for the dinner expecting the best of the best, a feast perfect for royalty. It was expensive $129 for two people we said hey it must be that good right!? Wrong, each station was complete disappointment as far as freshness it felt as though things had been sitting for hours, and it was 6:30pm so things should have been coming out fast for dinner right!? The one star goes to the dessert, my only enjoyable portion of the meal. Save your money and go to a nice fine dining establishment.

Did not like it.  The lines were long for seafood and meat items.  In between these items are place holders.  It was obvious some of the items were from lunch and were dried out.  

I have worked around seafood when in college and fish isn't supposed to have a strong fish odor nor taste fishy.  The snow crabs that were on the steamed table were both.  Didn't bother with the chilled crab.

The cheese table didn't have a nice variety of cheeses.   Only variations of bleu cheese.  No cheddar, no gouda, no swiss.  And the salad bar was pathetic.  

Meat was of poor quality.  Chewed it and had to spit it out. Lowest grade possible, select.

I shop at Costco and the scene was something like that, long lines for the same old stuff.  And I mean long lines!  I spend time in lines already so it is so this was a turn off.

We went to Wynns buffet the day before.  Much nicer and fresh.  The ambiance was bright and cheery and enjoyed the beautiful flowers.  I felt like I was in a cave at Ceasars.  Half the lights in our chandelier were out.  Eating old meat and seafood rations by embers.  

Will not go back.

Gave one extra star for our waitstaff.  Very nice and attentive.

Christmas Eve 2016 dinner with the family. My mom treated all of us dinner here at Bacchanal. Totally worth it. I wish I had a bigger stomach, but I, sadly, do not obtain a large stomach to consume all the goody goodness. We were in line from 6pm and didn't get seated until 7:45pm...and were were in the Platinum line. If you were in the regular line, the wait will be at least 4 hours. Since it was Christmas Eve, they hiked up the buffet price to $70 per person. FYI, we had five people eating. My brother decided not to join. Or else, it would have been six mouths. They served a wide variety of cuisine. From Asian fusion, to Mexican, to Italian, to Japanese, to Chinese. Then the dessert bar! My favorite...the thai tea boba float! Sadly, I only was able to consume two plates. Baby only got to see us eat as it is only his first trip to Vegas and out of the state. What a lucky soon-to-be 6 month birthday.

This is my all time favorite buffet, and it's definitely a must try.

I came here last Saturday w/ a group of 12, and it was very disappointing.
1) The host that helped us reserve a table was not clear about waiting time and such. We told her we had 12 people, but only 11 are here. She told us we had to wait for the entire party to be here to put our name down to go in because there was no wait. I've gone to Bacchanal Buffet over 10 times in my life, and I've never had that problem. We were willing to pay for the entire party all at once. So, are entire party arrived and she told us we have to wait to pay and wait in line to get in. She didn't even write down a ticket that we had 12 people, so I don't understand why my entire party couldn't stand in line to pay then all go in when everyone was there. I went back to her and asked her, and she was like "I never said that." Vegas is known for amazing service because we pay a shit ton of money, but she was horrible. I believe her name was Eileenfish or something along those lines. Overall, she has definitely ruined my experience at Bacchanal Buffet, and I am not sure if I want to ever come back.

This was  one of the better buffet places in Las Vegas.  And I really enjoyed their selection  I got there for the breakfast brunch and surprise no lines or queue.  We were seated right away and service wise Wicked spoon wins in terms of attentiveness and quality of customer service. Food selection Bacchanel wins handsdown. And I wished  I stayed for lunch because I was there between the times of 9.45am. And it was a Sunday as well. My weakness is the Desserts sections

A friend had a party here on Friday night, and because we adore her, we agreed to drop $123 for two of us to eat at the buffet. 

I'm really torn on the "star rating" here.  I didn't have a BAD time.  The food was alright.  Was it $56+tax a piece alright though?  No.  No, it wasn't.  I'd have been happier over at Gordon Ramsay pub.  
I've decided, however to rate the buffet at a 3 star rating, because while I have experienced better...as far as buffets go, this was one of the best.  

Lets talk about getting into the place:

They have several different lines, and seemed to be pretty organized about getting a huge number of people in as quick as possible.  We had a party of 6, and so we waited off to the side with the large parties.  Sadly, we did have to wait for an hour (one of our party's fault NOT Bacchanal's)...but once all of our party arrived and paid, they got us in within 10 minutes.  

Service was a little on the slow side, when it came to keeping up with removing the empty/used plates at the table, but it really is a HUGE place, so not horribly disappointed in that.  

The selection is amazing.  
Asian, stinky cheeses, slices of salami and other cured meats.  Lamb chops, ribs, sliders, mac n cheese, pizza, pasta, and seafood...not to mention the ISLAND of desserts.  

The food I tried, in as close to the order it was eaten as possible:
veggie spring rolls: standard spring rolls.  Decent.
Shrimp and port potstickers: Really tasty.
Salad:  Good, but where are the toppings?  I saw no croutons, veggies, etc: just lettuce and dressing.
Stinky cheeses: The bleu Stilton was my favorite, then the Camembert.  the others were good too.  
The Cured meats were nice, but I get the same things from my grocery store.
Ravioli Florentine:  nice.  One piece of pasta in a little personal "pan".  Good size, good seasoning, good flavor. 
Scallop with some kind of sauce:  Meh.  Scallop was over cooked.  Didn't like the sauce at all.
Crab legs: good, but I make them better at home, $7.99 a pound and steamed.  I really don't like when buffets split the legs.  I can get the meat out much faster and easier if you DON'T split it first.  
Shrimp: Perfectly cooked.  Good cocktail sauce too.
Mac n Cheese: Inconsistent.  First helping was amazing, and comparable to Gordon Ramsay's Truffle mac.  Second helping was mushy and NOT flavorful at all. 
Lamb Chop:  Good. I prefer my lamb more mid-rare, and this was more medium well, but I felt it was seasoned pretty well.  
Bloody Mary Oyster shooters: my favorite item of the night...kinda sad isn't it?  But the oyster was tender, and the bloody mary mix was spectacularly spicy and delicious.  I had 3 of these. 
Taro Bao Bun: Nice.  Sweet.  Not out of this world though.
chow mein: Meh.  My local Chinese take out place is better.

The desserts....I'll be honest, I don't remember everything I tried, because I took a good sampling of a good number of items.  
Tiramisu cup:  pretty good. 
Blood Orange Creme Puff: Meh.  Dry.  
Thai Tea Boba Float: this was good...for a buffet to have good boba...I was impressed.
Cherry Cheesecake pop: not good.
macaroons: The green one (pistachio?) and the chocolate were the best.  Good consistency.  Very light. 
My fella got some kind of chocolate creme filled chocolate cake amazingness, which was the BEST dessert.  I wish I remembered what it was...really good.
Creme Brulee:  decent.  
Red velvet brownie:  decent. 
Pana cotta: disgusting.  

So...all in all...not a mind blowing experience, but better than the other buffets in town (that I've tried.)

Would I go back? No.  Its not worth the money, not by any stretch of the imagination.  I'd rather take my $123 dollars, go to Gordon Ramsay, and have a nice pub meal and a beer or two.  

Would I recommend it?  It depends.  If you REALLY have your heart set on trying a Las Vegas Buffet, and have the $56 per person to spend...sure.  Go.  The food is good.  I just don't think its $56 good. 

**Oh, and also, apparently for $15 extra, you can add all you can drink wine or beer.  They did NOT tell us this when we paid.**  ( I wouldn't advise that though...filling up on liquid instead of food....)
Put it on your bucket list. You miss this, you miss an unforgettable experience

It was New Year's Day about 5 pm. I was worry about 4-6 hour wait but lucky me it turn out to only be an 48 min wait from start until I sat down at my table. I was very happy about that. This place has food selections for days. Not only there's a large food selection, everything I tried was so flavorful. The presation of the food was Beauiful.. For $50 a person. I think it's worth it. I will return. I hope they will add it back onto the buffet pass for the additional $15..  The only down part to this restaurant was the servers. They were slow at taking your drink orders and clearing plates off your table.
Food is soso. Service is not good. Very pricy $260 for 4. Not worth it.  I would not recommend.

I've had bacchanal buffet twice, during lunch and dinner. Both are good but dinner offers more options. 

The buffet offers so many choices including Chinese food, Dim sum, Peking duck, suckling pig, shrimp stuffed chicken wings, sushi, poki, soba noodles, ramen, pho, Singapore noodles, steamed crab legs, salad, cheese plate, jicama salad, taco made to order (chicken, al pastor, carne asada), all kinds of meat (Korean bbq, turkey breast, ribs, etc.), seafood stew, salmon, lamb t rack, mussels, escargot in garlic sauce, crab legs (two kinds), oysters, sea snails,  oyster shots, rice, and the highlight is the desserts for me: creme brûlée, egg tarts, whites chocolate mousse with passion fruit, apricot tapioca, chocolate mousse with peanut butter, chocolate lava cake (personal favorite), crepes with different sauces made to order, cheesecake, matcha cake, lemon megrine tart, chocolate tart, strawberry dipped in matcha chocolate, strawberry dipped in milk chocolate, chocolates, different ice cream and mocha (green tea and mango).

Lines are common and you may need to eat for an hour to get in. 

Do not eat too much and respect your body. That's the last I can say after witnessing someone threw up after the buffet and missed the O show.

We got here at 6pm on a Thursday night. We were at the end of the roped section of the line and it took about an hour and 20 minutes to get from the end of the line until we were finally seated. The food here is good, but the layout isn't so great. The seafood and meat section were kinda connected and created one long line, so even if you only wanted crab legs (which was at the very end of the buffet table), you had to get in the back of the line and pass the prime rib and all that other stuff before you could get to the crab legs. That was another 20 minute wait or so, so I just grabbed 2 plates and grabbed everything that I thought I wanted to try because I wasn't going to stand in this line again. The dessert selection was good and overall the food was tasty, but was it worth $45 and standing in line for over an hour and then having to stand in line again to get your food?? Not really, but it's definitely something you should experience at least once when you're in Vegas.

Lotsa people in line for this one...arriving around 1:40pm, the kiosk showed a 57 minute wait for brunch that would end at 3pm ($38 each) and then the dinner rates would kick in ($54 each). We were seated within about 35 minutes in a place so large that a roadmap woulda been appreciated! Such a large place..the food line stretched thru the three large rooms, snaking around corners as it changed food selections from Asian/Chinese, Japanese to Mexican, Italian, American BBQ and eventually into a breakfast bar following a bountiful seafood ice mountain...shrimp, crab legs. 
Lotsa good food, lotsa variety and a nice atmosphere, sitting at butcher-block style tables with cloth napkins!

Woulda given a fifth star but the only discomfort was the chill of the air conditioning...bring a sweater! 
 
A nice afternoon, but ya gotta finish your feasting within 2 hours!

The best Vegas buffet as all of my friends had claimed! Expectations were set way high. My family and I came for late Monday lunch and stayed/sampled the dinner menu. We budget for at least an hour wait but were surprised to be immediately led to a table. I guess weekday visit is the way to go! 

Highlights: 
Hot steamed crab legs
Lamb chops
Pork ribs 
Carne asada
Raw oysters/shooter
Spinach ravioli 
Roasted duck 
Xiao long bao 
Macarons
Egg tart 
Italian cookies and cream gelato 
Chocolate/coffee mochi 

We actually had a hard time deciding what was worth filling our stomach with during lunch service. Lots of overcooked/dry seafood, tex mex, and pasta. Thank goodness we stuck through and waited out for dinner menu. Desserts were better made than wicked spoon! Well at least the macarons were in the right texture/consistency. The gelato flavours were however disappointing - I was excited to see green tea mint, black sesame, salted vanilla, Nutella coffee - but all were overwhelming sweet and lacked the interesting profile they were supposed to carry. Their pistachio ice cream was alien green - ew. 

Just like wicked spoon and Wynn the buffet, bacch had some tasty, unique items but also some not so great pieces. If only I can combine all the perks/highlights of the buffets into one place! Overall - a step better than cruise buffet but nothing mind blowing. Definitely not worth waiting hours for or spend $70+ for a meal.

Super good buffet! From the crispy and moist duck to smoked brisket (has the red ring), oyster shooters with cucumber water (very tasty), dim sum of Har gow and of course the crab legs that are sliced opened for you. Man, this place has everything for just about any type of eater. The quality is high and worth the price of this fantastic buffet. 
Now I know why some friends come here every time they visit las vegas. 
The only draw back was the okay server we had. Not that friendly but some others at the other tables were. Could have been an off day. 
Oh and save the appetite because the desserts was fantastic! The dark chocolate lollipop has a cake with a ganache, many flavors of gelatos such as mango habanero, mint green tea, etc etc etc. And all tasty. 

I guess also the prime rib was okay compared to the smoked brisket. Hard when my prime rib at family dinners beats this easily. 
Enjoy!
I love this buffet but for the price, you can get almost the same quality but cheaper at the M or Rio. still would go here though! :)

GREAT Food selection even for 10 years olds. We went for lunch and clearly 11:00am is the best time to arrive on a Friday because we had just a little wait to pay and be seated. We did not have to use Kiosk system. Food was fresh no matter the cusine. Only down side our attendant did not come to clear plates regularly or refill water glasses etc. We stayed 2 hours, not sure if that is typical but it was our first time. Definitely want to check out breakfast and dinner here soon.

This is the best buffet in the US I've ever tried, they have variety of foods, Mexican, Seafood, Chinese, Vietnamese. I love their crabs the most and desserts. However, this place would be much better if the price goes down from 50$ to 40$ becuz no lobster, salmon Sashimi and perhaps better pizzas.
Best Vegas buffet! They have all sorts of food from Asian, Italian, Spanish, and more!!! They have seafood and different kinds of meat! It is pricey but worth it if you have an appetite!

The food was pretty good. I was very disappointed in the prime rib especially after paying 50 bucks for breakfast. But I am VERY particular about my prime rib...Make sure you go all the way to the back as there is asian choices and iitalian choices hiding back there.
