We would not have known it even existed had it not been for another customer. We were not the only ones that had to find out about this area from someone else.  Javier was very kind and had to take over our section. The hostess, cashier, and the gentleman that was slicing the prime rib (sorry I didn't catch his name) were very nice and accomodating!

Holy Buffet Batman! This buffet is pretty much the reason I come to Las Vegas. The buffet is located in the back of Caesars. We got there a little before 11 am on a Monday and got breakfast price at $31 a person.

 The best thing about this buffet is the sheer variety of dishes. I would say there are seven stations each with a different kind of cuisine. The seafood section had you run of the mill items such as peeled shrimp and seafood salads. It also had some crawfish which weren't the freshest and Stone crab claws. The meat section had meats cut to order. I had the prime rib which was tender and flavorful although a little dry. You can also find assorted fried items served in little fry trays.

 The other stations included Mexican, Italian, Chinese and Japanese. You can get made to order noodle soups such as Udon, Ramen or Pho. I had the Udon which had well cooked noodles but a very bland soup base. The sushi wasn't anything special in my opinion. Most of the ones they had had cream cheese in it. The final station was for desserts, which included miniature cakes, gelato, sorbet and other items. The Hibiscus Raspberry gelato was my favorite flavor. 

 Our server, Javier, was very friendly and quickly refilled our drinks and cleared our tables. All in all, the best thing about this buffet is the huge amount of food. When you think you hit the end of the buffet, take a left and you discover a whole other half. The quality of the food is definitely a step up from other buffets I been to, but won't good as a standalone restaurant for each item.

So this place opened since my last visit in 2011...and holy damn why wasn't it open earlier??? The Strip needed a place like this!

Bacchanal has easily the biggest seafood options out of all the buffet restaurants in The Strip, ranging from oysters to mussels, clams, crab legs, crab claws, lobster bisque, etc. They also have various cuisines ranging from Italian to Indian to Chinese in the far corner, and also have great dessert displays that are only rivaled by the one at Wynn.

Thing is, stuffing on seafood alone would already make your $50 charge worth, and quite honestly that was the true highlight of this buffet. Top scores also go to the prime rib, lamb racks, shrimp dumplings, siu mai, and most of the dessert options. What would make this place 5 stars, however, is an increased variety of fruits, and much less salt/oil in their soups as they were way too salty.

Bacchanal is one of the busiest buffets on The Strip, so do expect a bit of a wait. There is a way around though: Pay $15 more and you can bypass the line completely. The other option is to be a party of between 4 and 8, as parties of 2 generally have a 30-45 minute wait during peak times.

This is probably the best buffet i have ever been too!!! This place was recommended to me by fellow yelper Vuena L.

Came here for my cousins graduation party and this place definitely did not disappoint.  My buffet of choice in vegas used to be M buffet but now it has changed to this place.  The vast array of choices and the quality of their food is incredible.  I started my meal with crab legs, mussel, and shrimp.  All tasted great.  Then went to the area where they served pot roast (very tender, juicy, and flavorful) and beef sliders.  The beef sliders were really delicious.  Cooked with top choice beef and ingredients (i probably had 5 of these).  3rd and 4th round i ended up getting mexican food.  At this time i was pretty much almost full until someone told me that i completely missed the back area where all the asian foods are at.  This place really is phenomenal.  Just when i thought i couldnt eat anymore i had to hit the dessert section.  They have a wide variety of mochi balls. ice cream, cakes, pastries, and other delectables. I only ended up getting the mochi and ice cream.  

Dinner price i believe is $44.99 and its worth every penny.  I would not mind spending that type of money for the quality and selection of food this place has to offer.
An excellent buffet but it is overrated considering the wait time. If you do not have to wait, a perfect choice. If you have to wait for E for more than 20 min, forget about it.

Literally the most overpriced and overrated thing ever. The food wasn't that great and it was $125 for two people! Not to mention they make you register at a kiosk and tell you to come back in 70 minutes and then you come back only to wait another 45 minutes to get seated!

We stopped her twice for food while I was here in Vegas.  Hands down, the best buffet in my opinion.  First time we got really lucky.  We came in around 4 pm on a Friday and we walked right in to be seated.  On Saturday, we came back, but we had to wait about 1 hour to get seated.

I was really impressed when I went here back in 2012, so I came back while I was in Vegas this week. 

The food selection is great. It's even better if you like seafood (but I don't). The dessert selection is ridiculous! We ended up stopping for dessert mid- meal and then had a second dessert at the end. 

Meat selection is good. Brisket, prime rib, turkey, ribs, etc.

Tip: Come here at 2pm so you get the cheaper price but your 2 hour time limit extends into supper. 

It's amazing compared to other buffets in Vegas, but it's only okay compared to traditional upscale restaurants. 

Also, the service here is pretty terrible. Our server was trying to push us out a while before we reached 2 hours and she didn't clean up the mess she made next to our table (she dropped food and then kept walking over it).

OMG! Ok so I thought Bellagio had the Best Buffet. And they might still have that title, but Bacchanal is running a very VERY close second. I loved the modern decor and soothing sounds blaring. The food variety was amazing. I like to hit the buffet around 10am, just before 11 when they start to turn over to lunch service. This way you get the best of both worlds. Get your taste of breakfast, then taste test all of the great Italian, Asian and classic American dishes. And though you spend $25 (or more) to dine, it's kinda worth it. You get to taste all kinds of great food, and if you go at the right time (and pace yourself), you'll be full for til dinner! This place is a must!
Fool me once...... for $80 bucks a person there should be plenty of bells and whistles. Instead we got a 2 hour timer and long waits in line. Worst buffet experience ever.
If you only have time to go to one Buffett in Vegas.... make sure it's this one!! 5 stars. Better than Wicked Spoon. So glad i got to try it.

Eek! Me thinks not
Meh. I've experienced better.
A-OK
Yay! I'm a Fan
Woohoo! As good as it gets!

So there you have it folks. It's A-OK but I'm definitely not a fan.

What annoyed me this trip.

I've been to many buffets and they are usually good in Vegas, but this buffet was outstanding! The quality of the food was actually impressive. The Chinese food tasted authentic and not like Panda Express Chinese. Sushi was fresh, loved the carving station with all the different meats. The taco bar was awesome as well. This buffet was totally worth it and would certainly return.

This is an awesome buffet with delicious options.  The service was great. I was skeptical that it was going to be another boring buffet, but it was beyond what I expected.  I had to take my time otherwise I would have been full in  5 minutes.  I enjoyed the experience slowly and paced out each plate.  I would go again except that there are so many places to enjoy in Vegas that it's hard to for me to eat at the same place twice.

I enjoyed it 1st time around when I found it to be pricey. 2nd time $65 Easter Sunday. It was more expensive. Nothing different from the 1st time. Lobster bisque was so salty. Quality of the majority of food deteriorated as well. There's so many other new places to try. Won't be going back.

Second time eating here. Need I say more? This is the BEST buffet in Vegas! EVERYTHING IS SO GOOD LOL! we spend three hours just eating to try it all. I recommend the steam crab legs! All the dessert  the Mexican section! The meat is tender, but not too much flavor to make you want to keep going back. Don't miss out on the unlimited drinks the white sangria is the best one out of all the drinks.
Awful flavor & texture. Poor selection of Asian food. 50 bucks wasted. Will not return. Would recommend trying other restaurants.

Ate lunch at new buffet called Bacchanal at Caesars Palace. It was a big upgrade from what it was before. Therefore, it's worth a try to see why the wait at the lines were extremely long. (A worker said the usual wait time was 1 hour for lunch and 3 hours for dinner)

A lot of the food that I sample were comparable to many other buffets on the strip; you pick up a big dish and get a nice cut of meat and serve yourself a bunch of sides.  I recommend trying the cucumber juice and fresh squeeze orange juice in the bottle if you can find some.  Both drinks are refreshing especially after almost trying everything. 

One thing I particularly liked was in the Asian food section. Normally I do not go for soups but I did noticed something interesting which was the black skin chicken soup. One sip and I was like "mmmm...chicken soup" and then I finished it. Even ate whatever meat that was in there especially the skin.

For someone who thinks buffets are only ok, this buffet blew me away!! If you're in Vegas & want to choose a buffet, I suggest this one! There is a great supply of variety. I actually ran out of stomach room & didn't get to try everything I wanted to try.The food didn't taste bland, dry or overcooked like at most buffets. Everything was hot, fresh & tasted like what it was supposed to taste like. All in all, I give this buffet two thumbs up!!!

So, sad to say, I only got to try breakfast, but, that was amazing enough for me! Breakfast was about 25$ per person.

I had tried this buffet once before they remodeled it, and let me tell you, that thing was tiny, would hardly call it a buffet. But now, the new and improved buffet is much much better. 

Our waitress was super nice, and she kept thanking us by the name on the credit card that was paid. For example, thank you ms Tam and guests. Or how are Ms Tam and her friends doing. Our table got a kick out of this.

There were two types of fresh OJ in cute little bottles. Regular and tropical, sadly I didn't try to tropical, they had ran out but my friend said it was amazing, she had grabbed the last one. 

We had only got through half the buffet before our plates were filled, and there were so much more left to eat! There were different kinds of eggs, hash browns, sausages, bacon, typical breakfast foods.  There was an Asian area where they made noodles to order. Everything came in cute mini baskets, skillets, or dishes. The presentation was amazing. 

There was a crepe station, where they make the crepe for you, but than you put on the toppings yourself. Fresh fruits, dried fruits, sugar, fudge, Nutella, caramel, whip cream and so much more. I also saw them started to chocolate dip strawberries for lunch.

I had wish we hadn't waited till the last day to eat here. I would love to try their dinner. But if breakfast was this great, I can only imagine dinner.
Delicious! It is among the more expensive but definitely worth it. Great selection, knowledgeable, friendly staff. Food was fresh and hot even at an off-peak time. Worth it!

Where do I begin this was so amazing. Things I highly recommend:
-the hot crab legs 
-clam chowder with bacon
-scallops in the shell with spinach & Panko crumbs! Mmmm
-Alaskan cod served over some yummy mash something- so good

-mushroom ricotta pizza 
-polenta with beef cheek & mushroom-sooo good

-cream cheese wontons!
-good sushi-pretty basic rolls but high quality & fresh 

-mexican style corn with mayo,chile & butter

I had to stop to save room for dessert, but some things I wanted to try were stuffed baked potato & Mac n cheese

Dessert:
-creme brûlée- perfect!!!
-made-to-order crepe, I topped mine with bananas in caramel sauce, nutella & whip cream- so delicious!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
-flan

Oh & the atmosphere is beautiful!

First visit to the Bacchanal for lunch service. Expectations were high, perhaps too high, after hearing it was named the best buffet in Vegas. Honestly I'm not sure it was worth the $40+ price tag, but there were many good features.

Decor: lovely glass accents in modern art sculpture and chandeliers. The seats are modern arm chairs that were quite comfy. The restaurant feels large and airy, and the buffet area had a good flow, not like you are cattle being fenced in.

Service: I had expected a wait, but there was zero line at 12:30pm. All staff were friendly and attentive. The gentleman bussing the tables was very quick and polite without feeling like he was hovering waiting for you to finish. The only thing I thought was a bit strange was our waitress' opening line of "can I offer you a Pepsi product to start with?" A bit heavy on the brand marketing if you ask me.

Food: there is a lot and general quality is high. My favourites of the day were the tomato soup - creamy and rich, the cheese and meats, the crepes made to order. I sampled many items from sushi to street tacos and they were all good, but not "wow". But if you're looking for variety of good quality food in one spot, you're well served at Bacchanal.
Brunch is not worth the price. There's a variety of foods, however a lot are dry after sitting under heat lamps for too long. It is quantity over quality of taste.
We've been to a couple of buffets in Vegas. This was the best, by far. There was a great selection and the food was fantastic.

This was THE BEST buffet I have ever had in my entire life!  I cannot express enough how awesome this buffet was.  I was a little surprised by the price at first ($45), but once I entered the buffet room, I understood why this buffet was so expensive.  When you first walk in, you will immediately be amazed with the décor of the buffet room - it is very modern and hip.  You already feel like you're at an upscale restaurant.  Then you start looking around at the buffet stations and there is so much to choose from!  They had a seafood station, Asian station, pasta station, Mexican station, breakfast station, dessert station and the list goes on.  The first thing that struck me were the mini chicken and waffles in trendy little fry baskets.  They were the cutest things I have ever seen!  It's a good thing that these things are mini because there is SO much you want to eat at this buffet.  Everything was delicious!  For my main meal, I tried the chicken and waffles, prime rib, vodka pasta, fresh pastries, mini cheeseburger, potato au gratin, mac n cheese, tomato basil soup and mini caesar salad.  Now on to the best part: DESSERT!  They have a crepe station with home-made whip cream and fresh fruits AND a gelato station with lots of different flavors to choose from AND a mini cake station with several different cakes with the greatest presentation.  I had a little of everything and it was all so AMAZING!  I wanted to stay there all day, but of course all good things must come to an end :)

I'm begining to dislike buffets. Maybe because I find that I can't eat that much anymore, so I can't fully enjoy them.

We came here to see what the big fuss was about, and although it was good, I'm not sure it was worth the wait and the pricetag. 

We decided to come in before dinner time to beat the "rush". So got in at 4pm. So this place has 3 lines. A line to get your ticket, which tells you what time to come back to line up. Then you line up to pay. And then you line up to get seated. Overall, because we came at 4pm, it took us about an hour. The ticket told us to come back in 30 minutes, and then we lined up for another 20 minutes to pay, and then another 10 minutes to get seated. 

Then once we were seated, there were a lot of empty tables. I think they do this to make it seem like it's a really big deal from the outside and everyone wants in. But also, there were no lines for the buffet, so they maybe wanted to keep it less hectic inside too.

Our server was terrible. She took our drink orders and then never returned. 

Okay. Onto the food.

The food was pretty good. There was a lot of fresh seafood. Oysters on the half shell, crab legs cut in half length-wise (both hot and cold), shrimp cocktails, crawfish. That whole section was good.

Other notables was the taco station, which are a must try. 
Soup choices were good, but they were wayyyy too salty that day. Not sure if it is like that every day, but I like salty food but even for me it was too salty.
The carving section was good too, the brisket was melt in your mouth yummy!
The salad section was a bit pitiful. Not as much as I would have liked. 
The dessert section was good, the ice creams were really delicious!

Overall, the food was good, but not sure if it was worth $60.

This place is way over-rated. First you have to sign in at a kiosk. You receive a ticket that says come back in an hour with the exact time listed. When you come back in an hour you then have to wait in line for nearly 45 minutes before you are seated. Interestingly the place was never full. Is this just s gimmick to make you think it's crowded? The food is nothing more than a country buffet. The food is uninspired. The crab legs were the tiniest I have ever seen. This place costs $60! Go to The Wynn's buffet. It is less expensive and the good is in redouble.

This is the best buffet in Vegas hands down! The food was delicious, steamed crab legs scrumptious,  desserts were delightful!! You can tell the quality of food here is top notch and the presentation was excellent!! This is definitely a must try while in Vegas, definitely worth the money!!

Breakfast -  I wanted to do weekend brunch, but ended up doing weekday breakfast instead.  Tons of options, everything was very good.  I saw where the had chicken and waffles mentioned on their site.  A chicken wing in a waffle cone with some fries was not my indeed of this for sure.  Other than that, everything including service was top notch.

Very expensive and I think it's a lot of hype for nothing.
Lots of seafood options for seafood lovers.
Place does not smell good as well.

The wait at 6pm on Easter was around an hour. The hostess monitoring the line was very friendly.Note that you need to enter your information on the computers. You are placed on a wait list and are texted when you should return to hop on the actual line- the entire process took about an hour. They keep the dining room really brisk temperature wise so you better eat those hot foods quickly otherwise they'll cool down in no time. But, ambient temperature was not my main concern. I thought the food quality and items served were completely subpar for the price. They have some nerve to charge 68.99 for buffet and serve (or not serve) the following: 
-Prime rib that was oh so rare in the middle and cooked well on the outer edges. But, somehow the meat was uniformly tough and lacked flavor. One of the worst prime ribs I've ever had at a buffet. I only had one piece when I've been known to eat 4-5 at one buffet.
-the online Easter menu mentioned a hot and spicy crab dish which was nowhere to be found
-the raw oysters on half shell didn't taste fresh and were mushy. They don't like it when you use your hands to pick. Sorry! I couldn't wait since some people like to take their sweet old time picking through and selecting the best looking oysters
-over cooked shellfishThough, this is the norm at buffets
-I was going to pass on the sea bass with miso but one gentleman said,"This is so good that I'm going to take two." Each serving was on it's own little plate and the man proceeded to slide the fish off of 2 dishes and onto his plate (this is where I should have questioned his judgement). Common etiquette dictates that you to take the dishes back to your seat to avoid leaving a mess on the buffet line. I digress...as he is about to leave the man says, "And I know good fish." Ughhh, the pinnacle of delusion. This dish was so overcooked and salty that I had no desire to finish the remainder of the  small portion

The only worthwhile and also unique thing about this buffet is that they serve crab legs straight off the stove so you can enjoy warm legs. Problem is, the advertised king crab legs are actually part of a snow crab/king crab mix in the hot section and the ratio that you are served is 7:1 in favor of more snow crab. How dare they?!

None of this desserts are worth mentioning. Well, except the crepe simply because I think it was the better than the other desserts. I feel badly for diabetics because the sugar free cheesecake tasted like paper.  

The other acceptable dishes included the shrimp cocktail, seasoned whole crawfish, soft shelled crab, xiao long Bao, char siu Bao, and Mac n cheese. Oh man, aside from warm crab legs, this was one the worst buffets I've tried in Vegas but the most expensive by far. Will not visit again.

I wanted to love it but didn't... Just a buffet, a really big one though.  Here were the best things: the mushroom truffle pizza and the Pozole.  Everything was pretty lukewarm and ordinary to me.  Dessert area was impressive , until you bite into them and it reminded me of a basic cruise ship dessert.. Not worth the $120 I dropped for 2 ppl.....

Try everything they have about three sections I say start from the back and work your way up unless you specifically want seafood thats mainly in the front. The BF not too happy about the lamb as he is a lamb expeprt lol otherwise its beautiful in there and your choices are plenty. Enjoy......

OVERRATED/OVERPRICED
Funny, last time I looked at the reviews for this place they were all negative hmm. Unfortunately I had to eat here again because we were meeting friends.
I guess I again picked all the wrong items to eat since there are now so many good reviews for this place. I don't eat seafood so perhaps that makes it over the top?

Saturday Brunch for 4 cost $216.00 (LOL!)
Scrambled eggs - very watery but excellent flavor
Prime rib - okay but expected so much more 
Fritata  - overpowering spinach taste, hard/inedible/needed a knife to cut into it!
Sausage - didn't care for it at all/tough unique flavor.
Breakfast potatoes - good
Meatballs - tough didn't like the flavor
Salami and cheese - okay, like any other nothing special.
Watermelon juice - not chilled enough and in a very difficult glass to drink out of.
Mac n cheese - okay, like any other
Coffee - sucked and though we asked for more cream the server just kept bringing out one tiny creamer each time (for 4 people!) So he had to bring more cream out numerous times, so ridiculous! That cream must be sacred.

We always go for at least seconds which we didn't do and I always go up for  seconds on something i loved but that didn't happen either. No buffet is worth $50.00pp especially brunch unless you are a gavone! Service was good but WE HAD TO always catch him when zooming by otherwise we would have had no service but our server was really nice  but probably stressed from to many tables.

Round 2. Just as delicious as the first time we were here! Everything is so flavorful! Glad we were able to enjoy the very end of breakfast and lunch items. I love the chefs specials and a few I had this time included pork belly and lentils, pumpkin gnocchi and lobster eggs Benedict! It always looks too busy but the line goes quickly and the flow of everyone grabbing food items is a breeze.

NEW FAVORITE BUFFET IN VEGAS! :D

This one is apparently fairly new, but it has the most reviews for buffets on the strips. My friends got here before the rest of us did, and luckily was able to make a reservation. The wait until the reservation for a party of 7 was only a 1 hour gap. I like how they give you a time to actually come back rather than making you wait iN LINE like at some of the other buffets. We made it in time before their lunch ended, but I was so hungry I don't remember looking at how much the price was per person. I do remember we got bottomless mimosas included with our buffet though!!

I would say you can break this buffet down into 5 sections: Asian Cuisine, Taco Bar, Meat, Seafood, and Desserts. The selection of food is amazing, and not only is it a large selection, but the way the dishes are cooked makes it different from your average buffet. The only thing that sucks is that there is actually a long line at some of the Stations, especially the Taco Bar and the Seafood section. Most people don't see it, but the Asian Cuisine section is off to the left past the Taco Bar :P

Don't get me wrong, everything was good, but these are MUST GET Favorites:
-Taco Bar! Customize your own tacos and the chef cooks it on a stone grill in front of you
-Hot Steamed Crab legs (Asian Section)
-Cold Crab legs (Seafood Section)
-Oyster Shooters (Seafood Section)

I know I'm stopping here for a buffet next time in Vegas!

Best buffet everrrrrrrr! Worth the money. Foodgasm overload! Seafood/shellfish on point and easily accessible. Dessert table is amazing! Great service as well. Very expensive and can get very crowded very fast. Just don't eat all day and get there early like 5:30 lol. That's what ended up doing and we didn't wait at all and had the best buffet experience everrrrr!
The best buffet I've eaten, definitely worth the cost. We'll be making this a regular stop every time we visit Vegas.

This is strictly on food quality going down feedback for the head honcho at this buffet.

Please bring back the previous 2 years ago management.

Too many main food items lost its quality. 

Great staff great coffee.
The meats and asian section was great, but was lacking quality in the desserts section. 4/5 is about right with a Groupon deal.
Crab legs were too salty. Escargot and soft shell crab were delicious though. Great selection of desserts -- don't miss the chocolate soufflé.

Definitely a must for buffet on the strip!! As always a great experience at Bacchanal Buffet! Food selection is awesome and food tastes great! No complaints here and would definitely recommend it to anyone whose never been!!
This is by far the best buffet in Las Vegas in my opinion. There is a huge variety of food to choose from. Highly recommend coming to this buffet when in Vegas!!

Four of us went there on a Thursday for brunch. We got the VIP which included mimosas. This place is not cheap so I expected the to be wowwed. We weren't. There was a great selection. Loved that they served pho but all our food was room temp!  I'm not sure if they had their ac on but nothing we selected was hot. The steak and eggs was cold, the chilaquiles were cold! Couldn't eat most of it. Good thing they had a great dessert selection. This place was not worth the almost $150 we spent. Will not be coming back.

We went here for the Saturday brunch. It was very disappointing. The price was $108.00 for two plus we made the mistake of adding a $10.00 tip. We got one glass of water each for that ten dollars. I have no idea why they call it a brunch. I only saw three breakfast dishes. There was a lot of empty spaces so maybe there's more food at another time. The food that was out was pretty mediocre. The valet parking attendant was the best part of our visit. He was friendly and fast.

I had really high expectations of this buffet since everyone was raving about it.  I thought it was over-hyped.  I mean it was good, but not like amaaaaazingly better than the other buffets on the strip.  The wait wasn't too bad at 45 minutes on a Saturday night.  There was a lot of selection though!  The dessert area was AWESOME.  The crab legs were REALLY good - you can ask them to make it hot for you.  Sushi wasn't that fresh though.  The burger sliders were waaaaay too salty.  Other than that... you should try it at least once.

Expensive, and kind of overrated. There was a very large selection and some things were good but nothing stood out as being stellar. The oysters were freshly shucked, but not as sweet as those we get in the Bay Area. The other item that people lined up for were the snow crab legs...which is the same thing that is served at Red Lobster, so there's that. 

Please remember that this is still a buffet (even though it's expensive), which means things are kept under heat lamps or over ice on open trays i.e. dry looking sushi. 

Pro Tip: Go early and get a ticket at the kiosk right in front of the restaurant and come back at the designated time. The wait should be less and they will turn away walk up customers at 8:00 because the queue has been spoken for. 

TLDR: Go to an actual restaurant, buy a steak made to order....that being said I loved having a million dessert options and I ate them all.

Wow! This place is great. You can sample cuisine from almost every corner of the world. You can't truly say you've been to a Las Vegas buffet unless you stop here.
Very clean, staff is very friendly and helpful. 
Too bad you're limited to only two hours a visit. 
I suggest this is the place for you if you want to sample many different types and flavors of food without having to pay for a full meal and find out it wasn't exactly what you had hoped for.

Equip your spare stomachs, folks. You'll want to eat EVERYTHING here, so wear some loose-fitting clothes and arrive hungry. 

The three of us came at around 11am on a Monday, and we didn't encounter any wait really. A nice thing about the time was that we still got to try some of the pre-11am breakfast fits. If you're a real pro though, you'll make it BEFORE the next meal shifts over, so you'll get lunch foods for breakfast prices. 

Walk around the whole thing first, identify your priority areas, and try not to get drool on anything. 

Some of the lunch highlights for me were the gnocchi with pine nuts, the Peking roast duck, the bottles of fruit juices, and... the entire dessert section. I have a weakness. 

There's about a two hour limit, but I found myself reaching the breaking point at about 1 hour in. Thank god the dress I was wearing hid my food baby. If you are going with people that don't mind sharing food (aka catching your cooties), you can try splitting plates of food, so you get to try a lot without wasting much. 

EAT SMART. EAT HAPPY. ENJOY. :)
Came here for brunch.Foods okay.Loved the congee, better than The Buffet @ Wynn & loved their beef brisket.

Best buffet I've ever been to.  In the end, its still a buffet so don't expect a fine dining experience.  Its also pretty expensive, but if you come hungry and enjoy eating crab legs/shrimp/prime rib/all food, you'll have yourself a good time.

Not much else to say that hasn't already been said.

My first experience with crab legs was here. If it weren't for the crab legs and the seafood bar in general, this buffet would probably be at 2 or 3 stars. HOWEVER - the seafood was so good and fresh and delicious with drawn butter and other condiment selections, that I would absolutely return to this place for those items alone. Everything else was very generic in terms of buffet - some subpar asian selections, some decent breakfast items, and a tempting fried food section. But these did not stand up to the crab.

Dessert selection - did not stand out.

If you don't eat seafood, I wouldn't recommend this place. If you do eat seafood... go, and go hungry.

Not impressed, quality was definitely not there. Save yourself some money  crab legs were so tiny, sushi was fishy  would not recommend. Harrahs was better quality. Everything was drenched with oils so you couldn't notice the poor quality of the food.

Largest selection of world class desert. There is so much to eat that even two hours is not enough:) seafood lovers would consider it as heaven. I personally liked the Italian station and the dessert station the most. Its an experience and a must try for any foodie. However not many chicken options.
Its a great buffett but when we came we had to wait over 2 hours .  If you like crablegs this is the place.

An amazing buffet for what it is.  Caesars Palace really took it's time in renovation and making the decor and ambience a world class feel with contemporary looks and divisions of room sections. Place was clean in presentation as it should be with a newly open place.  Depending on the time of day...average wait times can range between 45 minutes to 1 hour and a half.  For now, being a newly open buffet with all the hype, expect off times to be at least a 45 minute wait.  During Lunch times 12:00pm and Dinner time around 6-7pm especially on a weekend,  you will most likely be there more than an hour.  The Lamb Chops and Rib Eye Steaks were excellently executed in cooking and portion size.  I would even go as to say the cuts of meat here rival and to some circumstances exceed quality of Texas de Brazil.  The New England clam chowder was creamy and filled to perfection with real clams. The dessert bar is exquisite, rather small looking in size it does have plenty of selection that one can appreciate to choose from.  The best part is the crepe station...and you can go around and add any toppings from fruits, to syrups, to nuts & chocolate, ice cream and even candy or more.  I could go on and on about the food...and pros...

...but with the good reviews one may ask why I gave it a mediocre 3 stars???

 WELL ..... The quantity and variety deserve two thumbs up...but on an average appeal, Bacchanal would almost be typical to your usual quality buffet in Las Vegas.  The self advertised "over 500 items" supposedly makes it the most selections of food in a single buffet.  Could it be an illusion though, that it doesn't seem that way? Maybe...maybe not.  And what is up with the smaller portions in individual mini plates?  They must have took this one out of the book at (COSMOPOLITAN's "Wicked Spoon" BUFFET)  "your welcome for the free plug and advertisement" hehe, but on a serious note, this is plain ridiculous.  Sure it helps cut down on wasting food, but you can barely carry a plate with food without it taking up so much space! and plus more unnecessary dishes to clean?  I guess the price hike will take care of that.  On the other hand...the chefs/cooks cater to your needs upon availability.  Sometimes they are so welcoming, other times they are no where to be found or walking past you without acknowledgement.  It really is a hit or miss.  That is respectable for a busy buffet though.  What annoyed me is the price went up as I was told by the cashier for a second time.  Opening month was approx mid $35 minus any rewards club membership or discounts for dinner rates.  Now, the price with rewards card came out to $46 plus per person.  That's fine and dandy once in a while...but with that price you would expect the food on the counter being on point...re-filled and not being left to a crumb.  Not this time around I guess...it was kind of disappointing.  This was also my second time at this buffet...and our server looked lost giving us wrong drinks and not even making an effort to check on us or refill our drinks.  Felt like we were being ignored.  Could have been a second strike and bad day for our server...but no excuse for customer service.  We had to call a different server who apologized and gave us our drinks promptly.  Caesars management need to emphasize this critical area for it could be a downfall in the long run.  For this price...I might rather go to the Wynn, Bellagio or Wicked Spoon buffet instead.  Don't get me wrong...Bacchanal is a wonderful buffet experience that I recommend one tries at least once in their lifetime or during a Las Vegas Vacation trip...but seriously raising the price...Common Caesars Palace...Step it up!!! Next time I might not be so willing to empty my pockets and bring my hungry taste buds here...or more so... I may recommend others elsewhere, where they can get better quality and service.   I don't disagree with all the 4 & 5 star ratings on here...but this was a personal experience I had to be honest about during 2 visits here.  If I do come back a third time...please prove me wrong.

Best way to describe this is place is "meh". The food was very bland. 

Meats were a chewy, dry mess. Seafood was all over cooked leading to chewy bites. Probably the worst oysters I've had by the way,Shell bits everywhere and tasted like they had been sitting out a while. Desserts were very bland, hard to tell what you're eating with a few exceptions.

Service was by far below average. None of the staff seemed like they wanted to be there, all very unfriendly. Got one drink the whole time I was there, that's how much the waiters don't care. Even after asking them for a refill and water they still never made an appearance.

We came for dinner on Friday night and it came out to about $60 per person, so $120 for my wife and I. For the price paid you can get a MUCH better meal in the same hotel or anywhere on the Strip. Waste of money! I've had better tasting buffets at half that price.

Overall, the whole experience is not even mediocre. It's just bad. The only reason why I gave this one more star than it deserved is due to the selection of food and presentation. They do have a vast selection of culinary experiences and the presentation all looks great. The restaurant itself also looks fantastic but I came here to eat good food not just look at it. With the great selections Vegas has to offer, save your money and go elsewhere.
It's great, but honestly...save your money & go elsewhere. The food is delicious, service is prompt, but totally not worth the price tag. Must do maybe once...

I frequently run to Vegas for a quick business retreat. I'm not part of the player club at Caesar cause I'm not the gambling type. But I just pay the $20 express fee. I usually eat as much steak and sausages I can. A long with the casual Asian food dishes. The servers are really prompt and always checking up on yiu. The cooks are busy cooking away. Not much to talk to, sometimes the chef cutting the steak or sausage would explain the meat choices other times it seem he is having a bad day and just want to leave already.

I come here all the time when I head to vegas.

I usually go to Bacchanal during every trip I take to Vegas. Overall, I do think this buffet is relatively comparable to the other buffets around, like Wicked Spoon. The lines can be really long, unless you are a Platinum/Diamond member, which you can use the "fast pass" line for. If you come in the middle of the day, not during lunch/dinner hour it is also a shorter wait.

I really like the variety of food they have here. They have all sorts of dishes, ranging from Italian to prime rib to Mexican and Asian cuisine. Pretty much a flavor for everyone! They also have a fantastic seafood bar from which you can get crab legs. I recommend not getting too much food at once, since it can turn cold at the table. Instead, get small portions of what you find interesting, and go back for more/other samples once you're done. I've gone enough times to know what I like getting there now, so I tend to stick to those things. They have a nice mix of carbs, meat, and veggies.

What's really fantastic- and I'm sure most people look forward to this part- is the dessert bar. They can make crepes for you there, and it's a huge station all on its own! I love the chocolate-covered strawberries here, and sometimes they have flan as well. If you are unsure about what's on the menu but really want something, just call and make sure that they have it before you go!

This is by far the best buffet in Las Vegas and I have tried a lot of them. I only wish I could eat more at one time so that I could try more of their dishes. I haven't yet started bringing a ziplock bag with me in my giant purse to take home food for later, which I have seen some older ladies do at some local buffets. 

I really liked the potato truffle dish, the selection of cheeses and cold meats (prosciutto, salamis, etc.), and the various cake pops they had for dessert. My husband focused on the large selection of seafood and Asian dishes. He especially liked the shrimp risotto. He even ate two bowls of it. He said the flavor and texture were spot on. 

The quality of the food was excellent. You get what you pay for, but the price is about the same as what you would pay for the buffet at M Resort, Studio B. You get a better bang for your buck at Bacchanal.

Bacchanal means a drunken or riotous celebration, and as a result this place is named perfectly. This buffet is pure gluttony.

It's not the biggest buffet, and it's probably the most expensive ($49 per person), but the quality of food is Iron Chef level stuff.

The carving board area alone is worth $50. The lamb chops are easily the best I have ever had in my life. The brisket was juicy and smoky. We had a co-worker from Texas with us and even he said the brisket was as good as he's ever had. They even had full slabs of smoked pork belly they carved into the thickest juiciest bacon you've ever seen.

The seafood section had king crab legs, oysters on the half shell, scallops, ceviche, lobster bisque, and so on.

The Chinese section had BBQ pork that was like candy, pork ribs with a crispy sweet glaze, dim sum, and authentic Peking duck.

The Hispanic section had rotisserie crane asada and fresh grilled tortillas and homemade guacamole. 

I could go on and on. The desserts were off the charts as well. Gigantic chocolate dipped strawberries, French macarons, creme brûlée, mochi ice cream balls, gelato, pana cotta, tiramisu, etc.

I still say the M resort buffet is the best value, but there is no question this is the best food I have ever had at a buffet, and might be some of the best food period. If you are a Caesars Rewards member, you can get $7 off, so that makes it even better.

Despite dropping $50 each, we will be back soon.

It's crowded, hard to get around, and a little overpriced, but it 100% delivers on its promise of being the most over the top buffet in Vegas. 

The food quality is moderately consistent, but a few of the dishes (like the chicken and waffle, surprisingly) are as good as buffet food gets.

Was here on the weekend and waited 2 hours in the line.  You go through a line to get to a line where they make you wait to get seated.  While waiting in the second line you see many empty tables where they would not seat any of the people waiting in line.  Not to mention the girl who is in front of me all alone who took as long as we did (party of 2) to get seated also.  Not to mention them seating big tables before you who were in line before them!  so one star for their attentiveness.  

Food was good, variety is a plenty.  Just didn't like the amount they had out so you had to wait for them to make a few things while you are waiting.  Not to mention, they were running out of things, especially you are suppose to be a buffet place.  They had snow crabs legs and at the VERY end brought out the king crab legs, talk about cheap.  SO two stars here.

Overall experience, it was ok.  Not work my two hours to wait here.  Rather take the time and go to the M buffet off the strip.

Waited more than 4 hours in total: a kiosks ticket asking coming back 2 hours later and then 2 more hours physically waiting in line. 

And Caesars charged $79.99 each, $19.99 extra for thanksgiving without any sign telling people first. I saw many folks left after waiting then found out price changed. What a waste of time.

The food self is not bad. But no bottled fresh made juice as promised. No lobster, no king crabs, no sashimi, no nigiri. For $60, it's already expensive. For $80, they make money on every one. Waiting this long, no more!

I won't recommend this place! You are warned.
The best buffet in Vegas in my opinion! Great food along with great service! Our hostess Dragica was very friendly and so was our server! 10/10 recommend!

Tried this place again and I think it was for the last time.
It was just full of cheap food that was slightly elevated.
How do you eat your money's worth on pizza or street tacos or ramen.
Aren't tacos like $2 each?
Chicken and waffles...Dry ass chicken and rock hard waffles. Seriously...I tapped it on the plate and startled the person sitting beside me.
They served swai fish....probably farmed...This stuff is like $2/lb for good reason.
Sushi? Gross
Chinese food? Meh. Cheap
Crabs were snow crab and not king.
Pork ribs with a cumin rub was good.
Dessert? At least this time they had chocolate covered strawberries....Decent.
No sign of macarons though.
So basically I paid for strawberries and pork ribs.
What a rip off.
Lower the price to $20 to reflect the quality of the food and I'll return!
But until then...No thanks

Came here due to word of mouth, billboards claiming they are #1 in Vegas, and also because it was one of the selections in our buffet of buffets deal. So we chose the wrong weekend to come to vegas since every single buffet we visited was SUPER JAM PACKED (it was the week of the jewelry convention). The line for this one was so long it wasn't even funny. We made it in 30 mins before they were closing and I beelined for the raw oysters and seafood section. I must admit, the presentation for every single food item was beautiful and you could tell they spent a lot of effort, but I really was not blown away. Maybe I came when it was busy in Vegas or maybe it was near closing time but I mainly picked at a couple food items I liked. 

I ate massive quantities of my favorite shrimp cocktails and raw oysters. Some other notable foods were the black chicken soup in the chinese section (tasted VERRRY authentic so I give them props), their cheese and salami section, and also their gelatos, and chocolate strawberries. I would suggest offering maybe milk chocolate on the strawberries as well since some people HATE dark chocolate...hint hint..also the japanese section had no sashimi...!?!!? what!?!?...just some simple cut rolls that looked not so appealing..

Some of the food items I didn't even get to try since it was closing time and they were wrapping things up which was another thing that annoyed me. If you are a buffet and you let people in near closing time then at least let them get all their food before you start shutting your bars down! 

Overall, I think this place is a one time deal...since I'd much rather pay much less and get literally the same foods (minus the oysters) at other top notch vegas buffets.

Must go. I wish I can rate it 10 stars. It's worth every dollar. The food and the ambience are just perfect. The only downside is you tend to measure other places with Caesar's Palace standard, which would be unfair.

OMG!! Vegas Buffets are crazy!!!  If you really need to go to a buffet then this isn's a bad choice!  they have a lot of food options but their price is very expensive and for the $40-$50 per person you can enjoy a good meal in vegas and not feel like you are dying or having stomach pain! 
The wait is also extreme, we waited around 1 hour!

I been in Vegas several times and never tried their famous world buffet. So this was the time! I was so disappointed! Over priced for what you get. Over rated as well 
I love food, I love good food and this is something which is very far from "good" 
Crab legs suppose to be KING CRAB LEGS but there is mixed one with snow crab legs and few pieces of king. Not tasty at all. 

The photographer took our picture, and never showed up only when we asked for it on the end of our dinner. Table next to us which came at the same time get their pics right the way. 

Our server was really sweet 

Anyway won't be back.

This place was OK. Came here because of all the good reviews, but ended up a bit disappointed. Waited an hour in line and paid around $80 per person plus tip. However, the food was way too salty! Also, their raw oysters tasted like they were dead for couple days! They did have a lot of varieties but everything was either too salty or too sweet.

Visited today for brunch with family, no question is one of the better buffets in the Vegas strip. 

First price... Is NOT a cheap buffet period! We got unlimited Mimosas with brunch for $5 extra per person, definitely a good value. Despite that, it was an expensive tab. 

 Once you get in one can appreciate the reason for the high price of entry. The buffet is plentiful, reasonable variety with high quality items all around and good service. The whole table was quite pleased with the experience here. 

If price is not your primary concern check this buffet out, I feel you won't be disappointed.

If you are a fan of buffets, well this is one you got to try. It's for those who really love to eat! There were so many selections to pick from that it's really overwhelming!

First off, I'd recommend to go as early as possible, especially if you are going with a group. The line gets really long. We went on a Saturday evening and it was jammed packed with patrons waiting to get in. Cost was $57.99 without tax and tip. So as you can see, very pricey. As soon as you get to the front of the line, someone asks for the amount of people in your party and then has a hostess take you to your table as soon as one opens up for your party. 
After getting your things down and settled, then it's off to check out the array of food. 

To me there was just too much to choose from. Anything from Japanese sushi, Chinese stir fry, Vietnamese pho, Italian pizzas and pastas, salamis cheese, Mexican choices, a large carnivore meat section with prime rib, ribs, chicken, lamb, and much, much more. Too much for me to remember and retain! It was all too overwhelming for me. You feel like you want to try everything but then there's not enough room on your plate. There were simple mac and cheese, onion rings, white rice side, brussell sprouts, and much more. On the seafood side which had the longest line with consideration of the meat line, there was shrimp for shrimp cocktail, longuinista, clams, snow crab legs, crab claws, oysters. 

After getting what I wanted which all ended up on 3 separate plates, it was just hard to figure out where to start! I mainly at the meats and the crab legs. My husband was kind enough to crack those shells for me so I could just eat and enjoy. You could say I had my fill of crab legs that evening. I didn't eat as much meat as I thought I would. In the end we were super stuffed. But wait a minute! There was still desserts! Yes desserts was pretty crazy too. An area set alone just for the desserts! All different types. If you have a sweet tooth then this was a fabulous treat! There were an assortment of gelatos, blueberry cheesecake, flan, creme brulee, raspberry cheescake, cake pops, assorted cupcakes, assorted fudge, chocolate mousse, chocolate or matcha covered strawberries, fresh fruit, and much more that I can't remember the names to. I have posted a lot of pics of the wide selection but yet just can't remember the names of most. Too many to remember and too many pics to be taking with so many people in the area trying to get their fill of the wonderful array of desserts. 

I would highly recommend this buffet if you love to sample different types of foods and if you are a foodie. I am a foodie and love to eat! I will definitely go back when back in Las Vegas.

We were so excited to try this buffet after reading all the reviews on Yelp.  I think when it opened the quality of it must have been better.

We arrived at 2 p.m. on a Saturday. Because the wait was 2 hours, we decided to spring for the additional $25 per person to go through the Express Lane.  We still had to wait about 20 minutes for our table.  Once we were seated, hubby and I went through the buffet line to see if anything caught our eye.  Nothing really stood out besides the juice bar so we started with the seafood.  The seafood starts with some hot entrees such as fish, lobster ravioli, paella, clams and then moves into cold items cerviche, oyster shooters, and thai noodle salad and finally the stone crab claws, shrimp, and king crab legs.  For how much we paid, you would think they would be constantly replenishing not only the food but also the condiments.  Not true.  There was no clarified butter or cocktail sauce when we got to these items.  Didn't like that the crab legs were cold, but if you go to the Italian food section, they have hot crab legs there, which is what I did.  Hubby enjoyed the street tacos but there weren't many other offerings in the Mexican food station.  Tried the old standards of prime rib, mashed potatoes.  Wanted some brisket but they had run out.  Honestly, don't know how you can mess up prime rib and mashed potatoes but the prime rib was tough and the mashed potatoes were pasty, almost as if they were boxed.  Very disappointing.  

Wanted to try something from the Italian food station, but all they had out were two types of pasta, meatballs, and one pizza.  Really, the pizza area had four empty platters, every time I came back, there was only one pizza out and the cold cuts area was always empty.  Tried the cold cuts twice and each time they hadn't replenished the food.  The worst food was the Chinese food station.  Tried the dim sum - they have the usual shiu mai, har gow, and soup dumplings.  The wrappers on all of these were so thick, not worth even eating.  The spicy stir fried eggplant was not cooked through and the black bean crab had been sitting around for a while.  The peking duck was very greasy.

Thought they could redeem themselves with the desserts so I decided to try a little of everything, unfortunately met the same problem, very little selection as they hadn't restocked.  I tried the oreo cookie mousse (pretty good), blood orange cream puff (don't try it), flan (nah), crème brulee (best out of everything), molten lava cake (very dry and not molten), cheesecake (skip it), and various gelatos (that was yummy).

Overall, the hype was not justified.  Based on the food we had and their inability to even keep the stations stocked, we won't be returning.  It was just a big, overpriced, disappointment.

Probably the best buffet I've ever been to in terms of selection and taste.  We came on a Sunday for brunch and there was a line.  I'm under the impression there's always a line.  It looked daunting but it went fast.  So don't leave your friend waiting there while you crash a blackjack table thinking you can win the price of the buffet.

The line for the "street tacos" was kind of long but probably the best item I had.  Worth the wait.  Also, the eggs benedict ---UH-MAZING.  I think they do a good job of not letting the food sit out too long.

I'm going back the next time I'm in town!

This place has good food, but could of paid less for same quality food at other buffets in vegas. Went their mainly for seafood. Got some oysters and crablegs, which was super cold because it was sitting on ice for a while. I expected better seafood from some place that claims to be #1 in vegas.
Avoid the crowd if you can, during holiday seasons. Their holiday menu is not that great and you waste your time and money coming here. The regular buffets at this location is actually bette

Overrated. Funny part is when you're at the front of the line, about to enter - they actually have a photographer there who will take your picture (like you're at Disneyland) if you want.  

There was nothing wrong with the buffet, but it was rather enlightening/disappointing when we had lunch at the Aria buffet the next day and they essentially had all the same things (and I'm talking about the good stuff - shrimp, cold and warm crab legs - in fact, their crab legs tasted even better than Baccahanal's).  And that was obviously way cheaper.  

Well, now we know.  At least we can say we tried it once.

Base on 4 stars here. We decided try on dinner buffet here.i put very high expectation for that. Cause this is the most expensive dinner buffet compare a lot other 5 stars hotels. Totally disappointment! Tiny skinny over salty king carb legs, overcooked mussels, only limited selection of sushi and no sashimi?! Wth?! Desserts are total let down! Tiny unfresh strawberry coated with chocolate is nothing compare the neighbor hotel. Seriously $114 for 2 I can have a really good 3 course dinner else where.
Best buffet I've ever had. Food was excellent! Tons of choices as well. We went around 10:30 am, which happened to be a perfect time. There was no lines or waiting. Service was excellent too!

Very underwhelming for the price and fanfare it receives. Many options but literally nothing stands out as exceptional.  If you absolutely have to get your buffet on this one is just OK. For the money you can get much better food elsewhere.
It's a fun buffet but not worth the price. I can't eat that much food for the cost of it. I do like the wash clothes they offer. That makes it different. I just didn't see what the big deal was.
Terrible! They have the worst line management I have ever seen. Very disappointing experience for such a high price. Booo!!!!
Long wait but excellent variety from a lot of cuisines! The food is fresh unlike other buffets around the strip. Must go when in Vegas.

Every word that came out of my mouth after approximately every bite was: OMG! Go here hungry, go here and celebrate, everything and everyone was great, the chefs even came out to thank us for coming by! A must go to place for Vegas.. All other buffets bow down! Yaga!

We were set to eat here on Christmas Day. I decided to go to Caesar's Palace, even if we were staying at the Venetian at 1 pm to secure a spot for dinner. 

When I got there, there was a winding line only for reservations. Basically, you put the number of people in your party on a computer screen and it will show you your estimated wait time AND a text message when your table is ready. I got to the screen around 1:30pm and the screen indicated that I will get a table by 7:00. It also instructed me to go back to the restaurant at the said time and that I would get a text message, too.

We stayed at Caesar's Palace even if we didn't really do anything there but go to Sephora. At 5pm, I decided to go back because this was our Christmas dinner and I didn't want to disappoint my mom and sisters. To my surprise, there was another long line, and this line was for those who got their call time. So I asked the hostess and she said that even if I checked in early, got a reservation, I still need to get in line. By now it's 6pm and she said that the line's wait time is around 4-5 hours. WHAT THE HECK!!! I told her then that I was there at 1pm and according to that stupid screen, I would get a table at 7pm. Another lady heard my complaint and she said she did the same thing. The hostess just told us that whether we got a ticket, a reservation, or a text message, we still need to wait in line, and the wait is 4-5 hours and that there is nothing she could do about it.

So my question: WHAT WAS THE POINT OF THAT RESERVATION SCREEN?!?! I could've just gotten in line at 1 pm, and by 5 hours, be able to sit my family down for dinner. 

We wasted our time and it was Christmas Day. It was such a huge disappointment. I was so upset. Vegas was great until I set foot here. We decided to go back to the Venetian and thank God for their great service, we got a great table at Canaletto.

Hmmm? This was such heart breaker. I vividly remember eating at this place and it was Glorious! A 5 star buffet!  Everything was just so amazing and all the stations seemed to be teeming with extraordinary food with fresh vibrant colors, intoxicating smells, the tastes....OMG. 

This time however, not so much. It was a Tuesday right before the dinner switch. We made it just in time for the lunch/brunch price but dinner menu.  I mean, the food was good, but it didn't do it for me this time.  There didn't seem to be the same, Pop of color, the stations didn't seem to be overflowing with food, the smells weren't what I remember either.  

Our waiter though, he was amazing!  I think, however, I need to drop by again on a weekend to  test a theory that the food choice and variety is undeniably superior vs. a weekday.

I came for lunch on a Thursday around 1PM, which was technically brunch (only brunch is served on weekdays before dinner). The price was $38 and the wait about 20-30 minutes. 

I've been to a handful of buffets in Las Vegas, and Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace is hands down my favorite so far. Yes, it's elaborate and fancy, but the quality of food is outstanding without being outrageously expensive. 

The restaurant itself is stunning and has many different food stations. My waitress was very friendly and took my drink order, refilled my drink, and cleared my plates very swiftly. 

I love how a lot of the food items are served in cute little containers. They definitely pay more attention to presentation of dishes here than some other buffets. 

I tried to sample a little bit of everything, but even someone with a considerable appetite/ability to put away food like me could not manage to eat everything. The dessert island alone is huge and the restaurant overall has an unbelievable amount of very tasty food.

See my pictures for a sampling of what I ate. I highly recommend checking out this buffet, just be prepared for a wait!

Everything was amazing and you can add on an all you can drink package for $15! We went with a party of 12 and they accommodated us very well we got a "separate room" separated by dividers which was perfect for my toddler to walk around in.

Excellent buffet. I wasn't sure what to expect, but it definitely exceeded what I would have guessed this buffet would be. Waitstaff was curteous, funny and helpful, as were the cooks.  The food was outstanding, delicious and warm. The atmosphere was excellent as well. We went for breakfast, my favorite meal of the day, and I walked away happy. Yes, it's somewhat pricey, around $30 for brunch, but well worth the cost. So glad we came.

2nd visit..& will be our last. It didn't take long for this buffet to experience the downfall of others, food & service have both gone way downhill!.
First the food: many items were cold & tasted like they'd been out for awhile. Also, you know food is being prepared half-a*#'ed/cheap when everything is bland & way oversalted. & the buffet itself is still totally unorganized.
Service: had to keep asking for refills & for our plates to be cleared. Our server must've been having a bad day, he hardly spoke.
It didn't take long for them to raise the prices either. They should've concentrated on the quality of food rather than overcharging for this buffet.
Not worth the price and the lines are a joke. I'll take Bellagio & Wicked Spoon over this place any day..

the best buffet at the strip!
I tried many buffet at the strip, but, nothing can top Bachannal Buffet. I ate a lot here. Almost all the food was excellent. EXCEPT the sushi!
But, because the other food was supersuper good, i give this restaurant a 5!
If you come here you should try all of them, and make sure save room for their deserts cause they're deserts are beyond compare!!!!

In terms of overall selection and quality, Bacchanal is probably the best buffet in Vegas.

The brunch buffet offers everything from seafood (king crab legs, stone crab), a large meat carving station, classic breakfast food, italian, mexican, and asian selections. The fresh juices are a lifesaver after a long night in Vegas. I highly recommend requesting the steamed king crab legs over the chilled ones, which tend to be too salty. 

While most of the western selections were tasty, I was pretty disappointed with the Asian selections. The sushi was very limited during brunch hours, which is understandable, but I saw that the lunch sushi was just sitting in premade racks at room temp more than an hour before lunch was due to begin. I don't expect bacchanal to serve Nobu level sushi, but this was off putting and probably a health hazard. In addition, the dimsum was poor quality. The shrimp dumpling fillings were mushy and the XLB wrappers were improperly wrapped, causing them to break open in the steamers. 

Disregarding the disappointing asian section, Bacchanal is still worth the hype. Look out for groupon deals for brunch to make the price tag a little easier on the wallet. We used a groupon for Sunday brunch and only paid $88 for two VIP passes, including mimosas.

This is the best buffet in Vegas. 

What makes is great is the attention to detail. Yes, the major ticket items are delicious (crab legs, prime rib), but what stands out is how delicious the everyday items are. 

The sliders, small, delicate, flavorful. The tacos, as an LA native they get my stamp of approval. 

The other thing that stands out about this buffet is the Asian foods section, from Thai, to Japanese (not just sushi but also ramen), to Chinese (both dim sum and regular dishes) everything is flavorful and to die for. 

Expensive? Yes. Worth it? If you like buffets, absolutely.

I can't say ENOUGH about this place. It was nothing short of spectacularly amazing! I have NEVER been to a buffet in my life that was so WELL kept, stocked, organized, and the choices, the choices were unlimited. I felt like I had died and gone to food heaven. Now there was a massive line to get in and it is a bit pricey....but none of that bothered me when I got inside...do me a favor and pay your fare, grab your chair and indulge in that culinary greatness!

Appearance 
Open buffet area with some hidden private tables. Clean,  med.lighting, dominated by glass and woody motifs    

Food 
The food her is amazing.  I rivals my other favoeite buffet which is Harrah's of Atlantic City Buffett.  I thoroughly enjoyed the many many flavor available.   They have 4 sections for you endulgence and develop a food coma: asian (peeing duck, sushi, noodles), Italian (pizza, pasta, cheese,  cured meats), American  (Bbq, mac n cheese,  fried edibles ), seafood ( raw bar, snowcrab, shrimp cocktail) AND ALOT MORE.  Not to mention the Dessert island.  All the meats were cooked well and the BBQ BRISKET was OUT OF THIS WORLD! -rich,  tender, savory.. One of best brisket I've ever ate, orgasmic at best! 

Staff
Friendly helpful. . Servers are prompt and courteous.  Ask for Fernando he is a funny host which will entertain you while you're in line.
                                            
Price
$36 for lunch.. just before dinner to save on the lunch price.

Treated my husband to the buffet for his birthday. We waited about an hour and a half to be called for our number. The ticket system is actually great  because they text you when your number is up. So we walked around the Forum Shops to kill time while we waited.
We got in the buffet about an hour before they closed. The food selections were good. The servers were very attentive and kind. 
We probably will come again for another special occasion.

Omg I absolutely LOVE this place. It's a little pricey, but the food here is awesome! My fiancé and I went for brunch last weekend, paid around $70 for the two of us, then pigged out. The chicken and waffles are my favorite. I probably had about 4 plates of food and all the mimosas I could drink! Oh yeah, there was also a GROUPON promotion going on that day which I was super excited about. All in all, easily my favorite buffet in Vegas!

An Absolutely Delicious Buffet!!! Worth Trying for sure!

Come earlier if you don't want to wait in line for over a hour. Excellent food selection and easily something there for everyone to eat!

We tried Wicked Spoon and Bacchanal in two consecutive nights.  Both were excellent buffet choices in Vegas.  You can't go wrong with either one.  These are the gourmet buffet when comparing to the older buffet choices.  Lots of choices.  Portion are set in individual plates.  The chef or server is there to help you or freshly cook your serving.

By the way, Bacchanal is definitely better than Wicked Spoon buffet.   We found that the Bacchanal has more variety and may taste a little better.  Service and settings were both excellent.

Went for lunch and had a very little wait , not crowded which was also very fortunate. Start with the great - Dessert station! great and varied selections and everything tasted great. Seafood fresh and plentiful and lots of crab, shrimp and oysters.  Meats and sausages very tasty and prepared perfectly.  The good - Chinese, Italian and breads just had tasters didn't want to fill up too much. The so-so - Service, Our server gave the tables around us attentive service while we had sporadic service, picked up plates occasionally, drink refills not offered and when announcing that her shift was almost over, lingered a bit to receive tip, while we watched her announce to other tables the same thing, but didn't hover over their tables like ours.  Yes,  great buffet, our server took a little shine off the full dining experience.

the food was AMAZING at this buffet!  It took us almost 2 hours to get in, but the food was definitely worth the wait. Everything we ate was of quality... Our favorite was the peking duck, char siu pork, and clam chowder.  OH, and the desserts were amazing!! They have my favorite french macarons!!! 

The reason I gave it a 4 star vs 5 is because some of the food did not have labels on them, so I didnt know what some things were.... and because it was soooo busy, people were making a mess around the food.... they should have someone go around from time to time to check the areas. Other than that, everything was awesome! We will definitely be back :)

I went for lunch.  38 per person. ...It was ok..Atmosphere and ambiance. Was spectacular!  Buffet variety. Was ok. Seafood selection was slim most dishes were prepared.   I loved the street car taco area.  I loved the salad area very fresh and nice selection.   My boyfriend  didn't like it he said it was just  pretty mass amount of food.

$55 for dinner on a Monday. 5:20pm no wait. Dim sum, a bit bland. Xiu Mai pork wasn't very flavorful. Mediocre sushi selection. The nagiri was laughable. Oyster was fresh. Cold crab legs were well stocked.  Hot crab legs tasted good. Prime rib was good. Very dry looking chow mien and chow fun was bland. So basically ignore their crappy Asian selections. Burger sliders dry and over cooked. Mexican corn on the cob on point. Liked their mushroom risotto. "Fresh" Fruit is sour. Dessert is good. Liked the mango pudding and Nutella coffee ice cream. Lava cake dry. Flan was ok. Horchata watery. Pineapple juice good. Reviewed while I was eating.  6:50pm departure and a good amount of people in line. It's good compared to other buffets on the strip but I'm not sure it's worth $55 or a long wait.

The food here is good, but the insane wait is extremely dumb and definitely not worth it.  We called a few weeks in advance to ask the best time to arrive for a short line.  We were told that around 2:30pm on a weekday would be fine - no line.  When we arrived at 2:15 we got in line to enter our names at a kiosk.  The kiosk said there was a 100 minute wait, but this isn't actually true.  The 100 minute wait is really just how long you have to wait to get in line.  From there, the line looked to be over an hour to get to your seat.  So really the wait was 160 minutes.  You would also need to wait in the food lines.  When we saw this we bailed.  We returned the next day at 7:30am for opening.  The food is the same, but there was no line.  The food was good, but there is no way it's worth a 160 minute wait, and there's no way its worth the price either.

This place made me want to sleep in here. Came to get a reservation ticket. The wait said an hour, lady at the front hooked it up and let us in 5 mins after we got the tickets. The food is pretty good, but the desserts were so damn bomb. Probably gained 20pounds, but was so worth the $50 each. A must buffet destination to go in vegas.

The very first buffet I went to in Las Vegas and it's still my favorite. Despite of the high price, I like everything at bacchanal. Wide selection of high quality food, especially for the Chinese food section. Desserts are must haves at bacchanal so definitely save a lot of space for them.
Weekday lunch was "meh". Nothing special... I like the buffet at Bellagio much better.

I truly don't see what the hype was all about. Tried this place out with the family. Waited forever in line for dinner and it truly wasn't an awesome experience like everyone makes it out to be. The food was mediocre and service truly sucked. I feel you get better service and quality food at many other fine establishments for your $$$. We decided to try this place based on reviews on here and it was a let down. We had to get the GM to get us king crab legs because there was a ton of snow crab legs and not a single king crab in the pile.

My friend and I went to the buffet for the very first time yesterday--- Monday dinner.  We had early dinner; we got there at 5 pm and were quickly seated.  It was pretty slow until 7-8pm when everyone came to eat dinner.

Anyways, I liked it because it was quite small compared to Wicked Spoon or some other buffets in town.  The food was pretty decent too.  Very good seafood selections.  However, the Chinese food was just so-so.  Probably because my friend and I eat really good Chinese food at home.. so we avoided eating Chinese.  They also have a lot of carved meat selection for meat lovers.  Personally, I prefer seafood.. so I only had a slice of roast beef.  It was very good.  Juicy and tender.  The sausages were pretty good too. All I can say about the food is that its good.  I just had a good experience with food there.  

The only reason for 3 star is for the service.  I understand that 7-Star and Diamond guests are priorities there.  However, the server in charge of my table did not come to clean dirty dishes until my 3rd round.  As you can imagine, my table was crowded with dirty dishes.  I also did not get refill on my water so I was so thirsty... Every time I try to get the server's attention, he would look away... It was frustrating. Ugh.

Anyways, overall I would suggest other people to definitely try the buffet.  The food is better than other buffets on the Strip:  Wicked Spoon, Wynn, Bellagio, etc based on my experience.  But do not expect a very attentive server unless you're a 7-Star or Diamond member. :P

After much researching about which buffet to try while in Vegas I had my heart set on the Bacchanal, and all my expectations were exceeded. 

As far as buffets go, the quote "The meals not over when you're full, the meals over when you're disgusted with yourself" comes into play (and as another fellow yelper says as well, too hilarious not to repeat). 

Went on a Saturday night around 8:30 and only had to wait 20 minutes - timing is everything in Vegas! I read in one review that if you tip when paying they get you seated quicker. I definitely think that helped because we went in before a couple parties. Price isn't even a deciding factor, you're in Vegas, splurge on the best! It's so worth it. 

There are so many different sections to visit so prioritize your favorite things! I live in Hawaii so I skipped on the sushi/Asian foods. The seafood section was my favorite and unforgettable! Crab legs were pre-cut, the seafood paella was savory and had the right amount of spice, the shrimp cocktail was fresh, and the scallops and salmon were served hot and were a perfect serving size. 

Their meat carving station is insane! They have about 5/6 different meats to choose from. The beef rib, spicy sausage (don't be fooled, this is insanely spicy!), and prime rib were amazing, juicy and served hot. 

Take your time and get small servings with the Italian/Mexican/American sections since they're all mostly carbs! The nachos, sweet potato tots, gourmet meat/cheese selection, and the TRUFFLE SOUP were amazing and worthy enough for seconds. Seriously guys try the truffle soup.. if heaven had a fountain of youth it would be filled with this soup. I miss it so much :( Next to this heavenly soup is an assortment of bottled juices and horchata!!! I was so tempted to take some home...

The huge island of desserts in the center is overwhelming, but everyone can find something to fulfill their sweet tooth. The creme brulee, tiramisu chocolate cup, chocolate molten lava cake, and oreo crepe were standouts for me. 

Service I've read is so so, but Su was amazing, friendly and so sweet. If you have the honor of sitting in your section I know your experience will be awesome. The couple sitting next to us was celebrating their anniversary but left before Su gave them a special dessert, so she went out into the casino to find them! Seriously, service like that is hard to find these days. 

The Bacchanal is definitely THE BUFFET to eat at if it's your first time in Vegas or returning again. Can't wait to come here again!

I had high hopes for the legendary Bacchanal Buffet in Caesar's Palace but I have to say - with a heavy heart - that this place was a  bit disappointing. It wasn't terrible, but for the entry price (and the fact that you have to wait unless you're in a large group, and that too for potentially well over an hour!) I didn't think it was worth it. I was expecting life-changing food, but everything tasted more or less normal. I didn't experience much of a "wow" factor with anything I had, whether it was the pasta (though Vermont cheddar is kind of neat - I didn't mind this), sushi, truffle-dazzled pizzas or anything else I tried off the buffet tables. Maybe I erred in underindexing on the seafood selection, which seems popular? Perhaps. What I can tell you though is that the dessert selection is amazing - pastries and cakes galore.

After reading reviews of all the buffets, it was clear that Ceasar's was the best reviewed. I was very excited about the Bacchanal, but unfortunately found it very underwhelming.

First off, I had no wait for dinner with a party of four on a Wednesday, so that was a great way to start. The server was very nice and explained how everything was laid out, which was important because the buffet is HUGE.

There are sections for seafood, american, mexican, italian, and asian food. So there is something for anyone, but that something is ultimately kind of bland. I started with the good ol' USA. The american section had some some sliders that were very dry. You could get a lot of carved meats (including ribs), but for the most part it was just flavorless. The chicken wings were good though, and the chicken and waffles concept (a wing in a waffle cone) was very cute. 

I thought maybe the international sections would be more exciting, but was let down. The street tacos were the highlight of the mexican section and the asian-style wings held down the asian section, but otherwise nothing was memorable. As a pasta lover, I was very disappointed the pastas were overcooked.

Overall I think you're better off going to the Wicked Spoon or the Bellagio.

The best buffet in Las Vegas! We ate here for dinner and again the next day for lunch. My wife and I both agree.. It is the best buffet food we have eaten on the Strip. It is expensive but well worth the price.
