It's hands down the best tasting quality buffet on the strip, it's also the most expensive. If your considering a 50 dinner I'd recommend this over a all carte dinner. After all, your in Vegas home of the best buffets in the world. You can have a regular dinner anywhere.

Best buffet in Vegas! Got a groupon and it was worth all of it. There is always a huge line, so get there early. The groupon for weekend brunch said to get there before 10am, there is a 5 min grace period, after that you wont be able to get in. The groupon provided a VIP line pass, so we only waited like 10 min. It was excellent!! The food was delicious, probably the best dimsum in town. The desserts were amazing, they had almost like a gelato store! The cashier looked at your ID when we paid and she automatically wrote down it was my bf's birthday. The waiter brought a very pretty dessert w a candle. Best experience ever. Make sure you tip the waiter! Dont be douches, im pretty sure if you can afford paying 50$/ person for the buffet, you can tip extra 5$/person.
Best buffet in Vegas! Loved, loved the  dim sum, congee, desserts (they have a variety of mochi ice cream!), lamb chops, crab legs, oysters, and more. Definitely worth the price.

they have an amazing presentation on their desert. It looks very pretty and delicious. I love the "Mountain Macaroon" Crisp and not too sweet 
Lamb for me a little bit sweet, love the concept of Alaska Crab leg cut in half, so much to eat.

Went for breakfast.  Good choice!!!!   Was about $40 pp but worth it.   Lots and lots of choices.   A friend said Wynn's breakfast buffet was better but don't feel like that was accurate. Go - you won't be disappointed.

I came here on a Sunday night around 6:20pm and waited about 45 minutes to pay and be seated. Once we finally got inside I noticed a plethora of available tables so it was annoying that they had people waiting. Regular food was okay. I didn't think anything was amazing. My boyfriend liked the crab legs and they give you huge portions when you get them warmed. I would have thought they would have a wider selection of steaks. I really enjoyed the desserts though. I had a tropical cake that was really great. The crepes were my favorite part of the meal. Chocolate covered strawberries were gross. They were made with dark chocolate. The gelato flavors were too weird. I love Thai tea so I tried that one but it had a strange flavor in it that I didn't like. Wait staff wad very under zealous. I had to ask her for refrills etc which came out in tiny cups even though people around us had larger cups. She didn't do anything will a smile on her face and seemed either annoyed or tired. I also didn't like that I could hear a manager reprimanding our waitress for allowing a guest to charge her cell phone. Overall, I wouldn't come back here. The food was not at all worth the price in regards to the flavor and types of food that I eat. If you eat a lot of seafood then this would probably be a good deal for you. I still think Wicked Spoon is by far the best buffet in Vegas AND its cheaper.
Overhyped and underwhelming. Food quality was sub par and it was expensive. A good place for $30 but not $55

Hands down this place is still the best buffet on the strip that I've been to so far. It seems that everytime I come here,  I tend to be unable to have enough self discipline to consume a normal amount of food and end up over eating. The food selection here is phenomenal and they have something for everyone.  The best station it's own. Pretty impressive and the dessert station is in a class of own.

The buffet is slightly a premium cost when compared to the others on the strip,  but its justifiable with the quality of food served.

The food was fine, nothing really extra ordinary except for the $60 per person entrance fee on a Tuesday night and waiting in three separate lines (the entrance line follow by the cashier line then finally the seating line).  After all that you'd be very hungry but not worth the time spent in line. I think you get way better value for $60 somewhere else.

Decided to go because I read many reviews rating Bacchanal in Caesar's Palace as number one buffet in Vegas. While you're going to pay a steep price, $50, every dollar spent was worth it. Had the salad, cheeses, sushi, crab legs, salmon, lamb chops, horchata, ribs, shrimp, mashed potatoes, green beans, oysters, and many, many desserts. I could go on and on but if you're in Vegas and want a big meal that actually feels worth it, just go.
Literally the worst line I've ever encountered. Seriously no place is worth a 6 hour wait. EVER. You seriously need a better system. Or a bigger place -_-

This buffet is the best. I have been here twice. It's a bit pricy - $55-60 per person for dinner BUT so worth it. You will eat $60 worth and more. B Buffet has whatever you want to eat. The quality of food is excellent and the waitstaff is always there to get you a drink. 
The first time I came here with some friends, we ate so much, that I thought my friend needed a wheelchair to exit.

I've only been here via the awesome Yelp event, so I haven't had the experience of the long line... which makes me think that I won't be coming back until the crowd dies down a little (within 6 months or so).  My first critique would be that the buffet is placed quite awkwardly, the lines are definitely causing traffic for people passing by.

Second would be the Asian food. The Chinese bbq pork, though the cuts were HUGE, was missing some authentic flavor. All I could taste was honey. Their dimsum was good, except that since they've been out for quite some time they dried up a little bit. The positive thing though is that their Pad Thai tasted great. I know some buffets have attempted featuring this dish and failed miserably. Bacchanal however, did good on this one; it had the right spice level and wasn't mushy in texture. Their sushi was okay. Definitely better than other strip buffets that offers them, yes, but not much variety either. Then again, Bacchanal is not strictly sushi so it's understandable. I've seen some curry somewhere and wanted to try them, but couldn't find a bigger bowl. Have to remind myself to try them next time. 

I enjoyed the "American" dishes like: scalloped potatoes, prime rib, calamari, sweet potato truffle fries (was the BEST sweet potato fries I've ever tasted), pasta, glazed veggies, etc. I would say that their mini burger sliders was uh-maaay-zing! It was perfectly medium rare, a little salty with melted cheese on top, and buttery buns to tie it all off. Their pasta was al-dente and rightfully sauced (I hate over-sauced pasta, but not dry either). They had flavor, not bland at all. Scalloped potatoes were a little too salty for me. I think it was the breadcrumbs, but I just brushed them aside and tasted the potatoes. I love me some potatoes. Their meat selection was all juicy, melty goodness; but I only had room for the prime rib. It was too rare for my taste, but the part that I did end up eating was delicious. 

I didn't get the chance to try their seafood, since I eat seafood almost on a daily basis so yeah... skipped those for now. I do plan on trying them on my next visit. 

Dessert... there are too many good words to say about dessert. Since they have a crepe station I definitely had to try it. I got one with strawberries, REAL whipped cream, and Nutella sauce yum! I wished they'd put the toppings inside instead of on top, but that's just a personal preference. They had so much dessert selection that I was going dizzy (or maybe that was the wine?). I ended up trying their Aztec chocolate gelato, chocolate praline cake, chocolate creme brulee, and various macarons. The gelato was quite interesting. I'm not a big cinnamon fan at all but I devoured that aztec choco like it was the end of the world. It wasn't overly sweet with a hint of spicy kick. Loves it! Chocolate praline cake was so heavenly, I almost cried. If I had an extra stomach, I would definitely grab some more. Choco creme brulee was so-so. Maybe I should have tried the vanilla one instead. To me, the highlight was the french macarons. I grabbed one for each flavor. My favorite was the rose flavored one and green tea flavored macarons. 

I've never been so impressed over a buffet before. I've been to quite a number already, and honestly it all seems redundant. I'm glad that Caesar's Palace decided to open one that has more to offer than "the usual."

Beware!!!! They don't serve  crab legs on the weekdays until 3pm. They don't disclose this anywhere on their site or anything. Went with my family and waited an hour to get in to find this out and we ended up walking out and asking for a refund. What a joke.

OMG!! This is the KING of the buffets. With over 500 items to choose from, you really need to psyche yourself up to eat here.

We checked out the YouTube site for this buffet before we attended and eagerly looked forward to experiencing it.

So we journeyed to the buffet for breakfast and after walking around to "check it out" decided there was MORE than enough items to choose from, haha!

However boring old me, who doesn't eat a lot of things, ended up being somewhat traditional and just a wee bit experimental.

I ventured to the Asian and Italian stations and enjoyed dim sum, rice, miso soup, an omelet and some pizza.

I ventured to the Tex Mex station and enjoyed an array of salsa with scrambled eggs.

I ventured to the griddle station and enjoyed mini red velvet pancakes.

I ventured to the dessert station and experienced several bite size sorbet flavored--chili mango, Thai tea, French toast, espresso, blood orange, etc.

I also enjoyed French fries and even snow crab...yummmmeeee!

To say the least I was full, stuffed and satisfied!

We are locals and ate dinner here this evening. We got in right away as we planned an early dinner. The food selection is great. American comfort food such as Mac and cheese and mashed potatoes plus fried chicken, prime rib, sausages and brisket.  There was also crab legs, mussels, shrimp cocktail, oysters, and other seafood offerings. Then they have Italian fare, Mexican, Chinese and sushi.  The center area is full of all kinds of desserts from sugar free to moshi balls and everything in between. So if you're hungry you have a large selection at this buffet. For the two of us for dinner it was $120.00 without tip. They also have a $15 all you can drink beer and wine.  Considering we weren't staying on the strip and were driving we opted to not get this and I have to say I'm really glad because the drink service was terrible. For two waters a Diet Coke and iced tea it took about 15 minutes and forget about getting refills. While the staff was nice when they (finally) got to us it was a bit disappointing.  I mean I get you're busy but really we were already done with our first round of food before we even got a drink. Maybe if we had the alcohol it would have been faster but I kind of doubt it. For the amount of money that this cost the food was good but I was really disappointed that this is how we were treated. If you want that whole Vegas Buffet you will enjoy it but be prepared for sub par service.

Let me start by saying I do not like buffets- vats of food sitting under a heat lamp that is picked at by 100's of guests inst my idea of good food. However, this place changed my mind on buffets, there is a reason its the best buffet in town. The options seem to be endless, from Mexican to sushi to made to order pasta to crab legs and oyster shooters this place is unreal. The decor is fabulous, very trendy and you don't feel like your in a dimly lit smoky casino. There is a lot of natural lighting and views of the pool from inside. There wasn't anything I tried that was sub-par, everything was fantastic. Highly recommend checking this place out- it will change your mind on buffets.

First off, let me say that if you do not eat shell fish I think this buffet is great, but not worth the $60.  I don't eat shell fish, and while I liked most of what I ate, you just can't eat enough omelettes and potatoes for brunch to be worth $60, even with bottomless mimosas.  The ambiance is beautiful and they have any and everything you could want to eat (asian, italian, mexican, american, meats and of course seafood).  There was a lot, but I'll tell you what I thought of the things I ate:

Pork belly - delicious, rich, have more than 1 if you love pork like I do

Noodle soup - choice of ramen, pho, udon, etc.  the pho was ok, but not amazing

Sushi - good, not great and not a huge amount of selection

Omelettes - made to order and delicious.  You can even get some shell fish and give it to the chef to put in your omelette

American fried food - waffle fries, onion rings, and such were a little too salty, and not cooked frequently enough to be fresh and hot out of the fryer

Breakfast potatoes - meh, not crispy, not seasoned well

Fruit - yummy and delicious and fresh

Crepes - a star of the breakfast buffet and also made to order with lots of toppings

My friend eats shellfish and she filled up on crab legs, oysters, clams and all the other shellfish she wanted, so it was worth the price for her.  However, she did say that it was all over-salted, which made it just ok and not great.

There are so many vegas buffets that cost less and still offer great food, I just can't recommend coming to this one.

I found this buffet a little overrated for the price that was charged.  Yes there were some excellent items but like many other reviewers have said, they have cut some corners.

In my opinion, the best items are the general tsao chicken, Peking duck, bone marrow, brisket, waygu beef, shrimp, crab, mussels, smoked salmon, egg tarts and many of the desserts.

Items that were disappointments included oysters, crawfish, watermelon salad, and sushi.

It was a pretty good buffet but it would be better if the prices weren't so high.

My hubby and I finally were able to try this buffet.
It was excellent! 
The only reason for just 4 stars was that a few items on the line were either dried out or just warm. Other then that it was really really good.
We had the Sunday brunch whice included all the mimosa's you want. Nice!
The seafood was excellent. I had some of the green lip mussels and they were fantastic. That's not so easy to do either.
They have some wonderful little dishes too! They serve them in little mini pots or dutch ovens. 
Don't even get me started on the desserts, lol. I don't even eat sweets but, couldn't help myself and ordered a crepe. They make it right there and have these wonderful fresh berries and homemade whipped cream.
OMG!!!

Had a Sunday brunch over there. Absolutely amazing and flavory. A perfect spot for every kind of taste from fatty to sugar free to protein packed or carbloaded thats the place to have a huge meal!
The seafood table was complete with fishs, shrimps, lobsters, crabs and all you can imagine.
Unbelievably good! The best buffet in vegas for sure (i've been to almost everyone)
Get smaller portions and share with friends so you can try everything. Cake pops are the best.

As far as Vegas Buffets go, this one is awesome!  Huge selection of food.  Great seafood and desserts!  At 49.99 it is pretty expensive, but everything is expensive in Vegas.  Wait can be extremely long so arrive early.  We got there at 4:30pm on a Saturday, and there was no line.  However, when we left at about 6 the line stretched past the zigzag line and went almost to the casino floor.  Bottom line: this buffet is expensive but definitely worth the price.  Get there EARLY to avoid a 2 hour plus wait!

This one star review is for the Bacchanal's terrible/undefined pricing policy. The food was decent, but I'm too irritated by what we were charged to comment. I came in on a Monday at 9:45am with my family and in-laws. 9:45am on a Monday. Clearly breakfast time. The person who rang us up charged us for weekday brunch (38.99). When I questioned why we were being charged for weekday brunch instead of breakfast, she said it was because we could potentially stay until lunch items were brought out. Huh?! What is the point of denoting very clear breakfast, lunch and dinner times on your website, only to ignore those entirely and charge based on potential length of stay. This was ridiculous. 

[Note: At time of our visit there was nothing indicating weekday brunch was even a thing. Caesar's website has since been updated to state that weekday brunch is from 7:30am to 11am, but at the same time breakfast is listed as 7:30am to 11am. Confusing much?] If we were there at 9:45 on a Monday and were charged for brunch, who gets charged breakfast prices? Only those arriving before 9am? Before 8am? Whomever the Bacchanal employees choose? Nobody? 

Also, we left our table at 11am, just as lunch was being brought out. So no, Bacchanal, your fear that we would enjoy breakfast and lunch (oh no!) wasn't even realized. 

Overall, very disappointed with this experience.
Worse buffet I ever had in Vegas. Got so hype up because the high review on Yelp. super disappointed!

After sampling the buffets many times at the Bellagio, Paris, and other places, we wanted to give Bacchanal a try after reading recommendations on Yelp and other magazines. For this price, we had heightened expectations. It was a Monday lunch and the wait was about 20 mins from getting in line to sitting down. It's true, this is the biggest buffet place you will ever see. Let's start with drinks: I ordered OJ and it was not fresh squeezed. The coffee was pretty good, on the other hand. Without giving out the long and boring details, you can skip the Chinese section, the Italian was not bad, and the seafood section was okay as long as plates weren't under the heat lamp too long. The carving station was good but nothing too special. We didn't try Mexican. The dessert selections were hit and miss. The gelato was disappointing. 

Overall, we think for the price you pay, it's not worth the deal. We will stick with the Bellagio and Paris buffets when in Las Vegas.

I have been to a lot of buffets in my lifetime, and I can say that most places that I hear being the "best" buffet are generally 3 star experiences.  Lot's of options with a couple of high quality options, but the majority of the options having flavor and texture problems.  Buffets are generally a whole lot of mediocre food.

This place is the best buffet I have ever been to, and the next best place is not even close.  For the record I am not considering Brazilian steakhouses to be buffets, I am talking about traditional American buffets.  Almost all of the food here is delicious.  I have only been once, but this place set the standard in my mind of what a buffet should be.  I will go again in April 2014, and hope that the food quality is the same as it was in 2013.  If so then this 5 star ranking will stay and I will tell everybody that this is the only buffet you should consider going to while in Vegas.

The line is mad long, we waited for 45min. But the food is disappointed for $50/person. The ice cream is melted, and the people who seat around us were like this place is not all that! So we are not the only one who said it. NEVER again, but there is a really good Chinese restaurant right next to it is call Beijing Noodle No. 9! I am Asian and I really think they have the best Chinese food.

I would put 0 star if I can.  Electronic checked in at 4:30, in line to pay at 7pm for $68+tax per person, actually sat down to eat at 9:40pm.
Food was awful, been sitting out for a long time, or ran out.  Oyster still not totally raw.   Totally lose appetite after eating the oyster.  My son puked not because of over eat but not very good food.    Soooooo disappointed.

The lines were long, the wait was long, but I guess it was worth it?
My friends loved this place, and so did I (kind of).  I wasn't feeling too hot, and so I didn't get to grub like a beast like I would usually do.
One of my friends signed up for a card w/ the hotel, and he got a free $10 play certificate for redemption and got $1 off per person who ate at the buffet with him.  Sweet!  (Dinner buffet is ~$45.)

For those who like home designs etc, in line if you look at the lights you'll notice that cups were used as the design around the lights.  Looks pretty nice.

The lines were super long for the seafood section.  Right behind that was the meat section.   My friends feasted in both sections, especially in the seafood section.  They were animals.  There were also Mexican food and Chinese and so on.  If you like dessert, it's in a different section separate from the buffet--right in the middle of the restaurant.  My stomach was hurting so I didn't really try any of it, but my friends did and loved it.  Some went back for seconds, and thirds.  Crazy...

Holy wow!  This place has definitely earned its place as the best buffet in Vegas. So very good. 

First things first - be prepared to wait in line. It's worth it, I swear! One of our group members complained because he never waits in line for food. He ended up saying it was totally worth the wait. We came on a Sunday night and waited about and hour. Just grab a drink to sip in line and you'll be good. 

There is a huge selection of food and just about everything is incredible. Here are a few if my standouts:
. Crab legs - a must have
. Ceviche - delicious 
. Tuna and salmon sashimi (like a high end sushi place!)
. Charcuterie bar - lots of cheese and meat selections 
. Tiny baskets of waffle fries, chicken strips, tater tots etc. 
. Dessert!

Anyone who knows me knows dessert is ultra important and this buffet did not disappoint. I highly recommend the fig and balsamic gelato and the macarons. But most of it is great!  

So for a amazing buffet experience go here!

We went here for lunch and the selection was ok, not worth the very expensive price it was. I spent $45 for 1 plate of food and some gelato. Food tasted average, crab legs were not that big. Overall, very unimpressed. 

But the decor was fabulous. Modern and simple interior designs, and the buffet was next to the beautiful pool. 

I would maybe come here again for dinner only because they would have the more special seafood I was looking for.

This place is AMAZING! I LOVE IT!

It's like eating a quality fine dining restaurant but all you can eat!  

The food is quality and you can taste it. Most other Buffets seem like they are serving dog food after eating here.

I love the fresh juices, the steamed crab, the shrimp, the fish is not over cooked. The lamb chops are Amazing! The salads are incredible! 

The deserts are good, but I stick to the Gellato which is really good and has unique flavors, like Thai Tea, Red Bean. Aztec Chocolate, Baklava.

But you should not go here at all on Wednesday because I don't want the line any going when I'm going there for lunch. :o)

THIS PLACE IS AWESOME!

The Bacchanal Buffet is by far the best buffet I've ever had. Dinner was $52 a person, which is pricier than several buffets in Vegas. Don't even get me started on the food selection, but okay I'll tell you. They have an incredible selection of meats, salads, cheeses, breads, soups, and desserts (which is obviously the most important part of the meal). They had individual sections for BBQ meats, seafood, Chinese dim sum, Italian pasta, salads, etc, so be sure to explore the whole buffet! 

The presentation of their dishes was also very aesthetically pleasing; all of their desserts are definitely picture perfect. However, several of the BBQ meats that I tried were incredibly salty. 

Give this place a try and be sure to get in line early!

First time I tried this buffet was about a year ago.  We were here for dinner and waited about an hour and a half to get seated which is not bad.  Food is above average.  You'll find diverse selection of food and the presentation on their desserts were quite good (like in Bellagio and Wynn).  That night I asked if they have any lamb and the gentleman told me they ran out. Food was good but nothing really stood out.

This year we came back again to give my in-laws (visiting from another county) a Vegas Buffet experience.  It turned out to be a real disaster... and here's how it all went down:
Thanksgiving weekend pricing... $60 for Total Rewards members & $64 for regular price.  If you want to be in front of the line, you can pay an extra $20 for each person.  We asked the lady at the podium and she told us to check-in through a computer kiosk in front to give us the time to come back.  Estimated wait time is 134 minutes and our check-in time was at 5:18 PM.  According to our ticket, we needed to return and check back in at 7:27 PM.  I even left my cell number to get notified on our return time.  More than 2 hours of waiting time... so instead of keeping your money in your pocket, this is their subtle way of luring you in to playing on the casino floor and spending more money.  Then we came back around 7:00 PM and there was a huge line (BTW I DID NOT even get a text message  reminder for our return time).  We were told that we have to stand in line and wait for another 1 hour and 30 mins.  That is just ridiculous!  Of course we ended up eating at a different place.  I just hope that the line is not like this everyday. On a lighter note, there's this one lady who I think is a Diamond or a 7 Stars member who was going around the line of people and telling everyone that she can take anyone to the front of the line as long as they pay her cash LOL.  Talk about making some dough in the casino to sustain their gambling addiction LMAO!

Ratings:
1 star for service (the way they handled the waiting time and lines)
3 stars for the food (last year)

Happy eating folks!

My family and I came in on a Saturday around 11am. I was expecting to wait a while, because it was the weekend, but we didn't wait at all. We walked right up to the front, paid and were quickly seated. For a party of 4, our bill came up to almost $200. Yeah, I got a little weak in the knees but we really wanted to try this place. 

As soon as you start making your rounds, you'll notice that Bacchanal offers food that would normally be served at a nice restaurant. It's hard to describe the experience, but it is definitely worth your money. You could taste the time and effort they put into their food. It's like eating at 10 different high-end restaurants at once. Of course, you should save room for dessert. They have everything from gelato, macarons, fruit cups, pastries, etc. 

In the beginning, you'll feel a little skeptical about how much money you just spent. But it will feel very worth it in the end.

Bacchanal is a MUST when in Vegas. Just be prepared for possible long waits!

I'm not really a buffet-type person, but this place definitely exceeded my expectations. The price for brunch was reasonable (about $32 per person) and you get a whole variety of different cuisines and desserts. You also have the option of paying an extra $7 for a bottomless boozy brunch--such a great deal! My friend and I ordered mimosas, but you have the option of ordering wine or other liquor instead. 

They have so many different types of food such as seafood, greasy fried food, japanese, dim sum, assorted meat & cheese, spanish, italian, and salads. Out of all the food I tried, I was surprised to say that the sushi was the most disappointing. There was not enough seafood or flavor- it was mostly filled with rice so I tried not to eat too much of that. My favorite was probably the mac&cheese as well as the duck. 

I was also very impressed by the dessert section. They had so many colorful desserts such as cupcakes, shortbreads, egg tarts, gelatos, cake pops, mousse, fudge....and the list goes on and on.

If you're ever planning a trip to vegas, make sure you stop here for breakfast. This place was so worth it!

One of the best buffets on the strip. Endless varieties. Had to walk minutes to scout out the menu. Came with wife, sister in law, and baby son. You can find boiled crab legs at the Italian section. They looked like snow crab legs. 

Had taco stand as well, which was my highlight. 
Waited 30 minutes in line on a Wednesday afternoon but was soo worth. 

Dessert section has gelatos. 

For a buffet, it does have a darker atmosphere

Truly top notch. Good quality and great selection. Freshly juiced cucumber and watermelon among others! Plus the huge variety of well done foods! Omelette station is hidden. I'm impressed and will definitely be back!

Very good buffet.  A lot of friends advised to try this buffet as it is currently the go to buffet in Las Vegas right now.  Around 2 pm on a weekday, the place had a little wait time.  So regardless of time, plan to wait.  The food selection is awesome.   My first time to a new buffet, I walk around to see what is available before I get any food.  The lay out is a little strange because initially I thought to my self what is the hype about, I do not see very much.  The buffet is laid out sort of in a Z fashion with it wrapping around the corner.  As first I did not notice it until I saw a number of people walking out from around a corner.  I thought it was more seating in the back but the buffet bends around into the back where the Asian dishes are. 

The buffet is pricey with the probably the biggest selection of items on the strip.  As a result, it probably has the worst wait times on the strip.  Is it worth it? It depends.  For lunch, I thought it was.  I would probably skip it for dinner because I can not imagine an hour or two waiting in line to eat.  Also, like any buffet in Vegas come hungry, especially to this one.

I have to say this is one of the buffet in Las Vegas that even though quite expensive compare to others still worth every dimes spent. Fresh crabs legs , shrimps and oysters a must haves , various meat dishes like prime ribs and my favorite lamb chops or lamb racks so good so perfectly cooked, can't never get enough of their Dim sum also their dessert choices ; fresh made crepes, mini tarts, soufflé, macaroons, gelato..

Sunday brunch line was ridiculously long. We got thru it and the food was good. A lot of selection--even for the picky eaters. I have shellfish allergies and don't eat red meat...therefore buffets are usually not worth it to me. The food looked appealing and fresh! My husband enjoyed the burger sliders and ribs the most. I enjoyed the breakfast food selection and loved the dessert station! They blast the air-conditioning in this place, maybe so you don't stay too long...bring a light jacket or cardigan.
Lots of food variety to chose from. One of the best buffets I have tried.

I was told by so many people that this was the one place I had to go to for brunch while I was in Las Vegas. So I listened to everyone and came by, but was slightly disappointed. This place is definitely too hyped.

I came for brunch Friday morning around 1000. There wasn't a massive waiting line yet so I was seated fairly quickly. My waiter was very friendly and made sure I was taken care of.

The buffet offered a range of cuisines. There are chefs who are available to make tacos, omelets, and Asian soups (ramen, udon, pho). The seafood section had Louisiana style crawfish, clams, shrimp cocktail, and some seafood brunch items (the lobster Benedict was okay..). I enjoyed the croquette madame, steak and eggs, mini pancakes, and the cheese and prosciutto very much. There was sushi that was terrible - as if it came frozen and they thawed it before serving it on the buffet. I would avoid the Asian section completely.

If you absolutely need to order a drink, then go for it, but they have a fresh juice section that was probably one of the highlights of my visit. They offered fresh orange, watermelon, hibiscus, and cucumber juices. 

I would say go visit another resort for a possibility of experiencing a better brunch place!

$50 for a unforgettable buffet? Crab legs aren't very good. The only thing I love about the buffet is the meat station and  the awesome lamb chops. Other than that I think I'm going to stick to studio B

I was so hyped to try this place out since I wasn't able to eat here last time. After eating dinner here on a Tuesday night I was left quite disappointed and don't get all the 5 star reviews.

For being the most expensive buffet in Vegas you would think that they would be considered the best. I wasn't impressed with the quality of the food here. If I'm paying $53 I better get some damn good seafood. No lobster? Cold and nasty tasting crab legs? (Pechanga has better crab legs) I don't eat oysters and the shrimp were ok.

The meat carving station has a decent selection but I didn't like the tri tip too much as well as their sausage. Lamb chops were very good though.

Asian section had an ok variety of things. Tried the bbq duck and it was completely overcooked. Sushi section could've been better. Serve some yellowtail nigiri and I'll love this place more.

I like the concept of mini sized plates with something small to sample it. I tried the beef slider, pork belly with carrot puree and grits with spicy sausage. Only one I enjoyed was the pork belly.

I like the Mexican station with their street tacos. Got to try the steak and al pastor and loaded it up after the lady finished making my tacos.

By the time I got to desserts I was too damn full to stock up on sweets so I only got to try 2 flavors of their gelato and a chocolate cake on a stick. Banana cream and Italian cookies and cream were the ones I sampled. Banana cream was good but the Italian cookies and cream was not good. The chocolate  cheesecake on a stick was ok.

But let's be real. I didn't pay $53 to fill up on tacos. I wanted some damn good food and all I got out of it was average food I could've gotten elsewhere for a lot less money. I spent almost $200 for a mediocre experience and while I'm glad I finally got to try the most expensive buffet in Vegas, I wouldn't return unless I was comped. I'll settle for the other buffets on the strip.

The fruit juices they have in the little glass bottles were pretty good.

One last thing. No restrooms inside the buffet so you're gonna have to let the workers know that you paid already if you have to go use it. Fortunately it's close by.

This is the buffet ever.  I normally don't like buffets, but this is the exception.  They have everything.  I love that the chefs are from the part of the world where the dishes are from that they cook.  They make sure you're happy.  The layout is nice, too.

So I came for the holiday brunch on the 28th of March around 915 am. 
We paid 108 for two. Yes it was pricey but I loveD this buffet (notice the D) so I didn't care. 
Anyway I finish my first plate and go for my second which was a make your own omlette and as I'm eating my food I notice a hair in the omlette. Biggest mood ruiner ever. I notify the waitress and she says shell call the manager. We literally wait 15-20 minutes for the manager to show up to our table. I've had hair in my food before at other restaurants, but when that happens the manager comes over in a heart beat to show their concern and make matters better. The fact that she came so late showed how insignificant it was. 
Anyway she came. I explained what happened. And she took my plate to find the hair and took a pic of it. Then she offered to make me another omlette . Really? Who wouldn't lose their appetite after seeing that? So I decline.  Then she offers me coffee. I decline also. 
Then finally she's like okay we'll see if we can give you a discount. She proceeds to take my receipt and after 10 minutes she comes back. She ends up taking 20 dollars off. 
Is that even a real thing? Why wasn't my meal comped? I didn't even get to eat as much as I paid for. It ruined my appetite. I honestly wouldn't have expected a place of this high quality to show such lack of consideration and honestly common sense to their customers. 
Finding hair in food happens unfortunately but it's how the restaurant and management decides to deal with the matter that counts. Had she shown more care and dealt with it in a better manner I wouldn't even be writing this review. I loved bacchanal man. It's the only restaurant I look forward to when I go to Vegas. Now it's tainted. I feel like I can't go back because I'm still so pissed.

A food wonderland of joy and happiness. This is the best buffet i've ever visited. So many selections and so much time, but such a small stomach. I would visit Vegas again just to go eat at a buffet. And it was only $50 for all of that food. Amazing!

This is suppose to be the best buffet in Vegas, however it was one of the worst experiences i have ever had. The food was good and decent (the soup was cold), however my main problem is with the staff. 

Our waitress was rude and snarky, When my friend was at the table she asked her what she would like to drink and my friend said water, when i got to the table i asked for coffee, the waitress decided to give me a lecture and tell me when she asked my friend what she wanted to drink why didn't she say coffee......How is my friend suppose to know what i would like to drink that day. She didn't clear our plates, however when we were in the middle of eating thats when she tried clearing our plates :s. Also from the waitress who served the people next to us, we learned that beer and wine was complimentary, which our waitress failed to inform us therefore we didn't even get any. Majority of the time our waitress was no where to be seen, she didn't come check up on us, we couldn't order any more drinks, didn't refill our water. 

The chef who works at the soup station has a horrible staring problem, when my friend and i were in his area looking at what was there, my friend noticed he was just standing there staring at us. So we quickly left his area and went back to our seats near the asian food area. Then my friend noticed that he had followed through the kitchen to that area and stood there and stared at us. Way to make your guest feel uncomfortable thats the best way to do, I don't know if it was a racial thing or what but it creeped us out and we quickly ate the rest of our meal and left. 

For the amount of money we spent on this buffet due to the customer service it was money down the drain for us.

The wait system here can be a little confusing but I guess it's their way of being organized. So first, you will need to line up at one of the machines to check in and get a ticket. Then you wander around the area for approximately 40 minutes until you receive a text message or the time on your ticket is up so you then return to the buffet line and hand the worker your ticket, to wait in line for about 30 minutes. Once you get to the front of the line, you pay before entering and waiting in another line. After that line, someone will finally walk you over to a table. The wait can be long but it is understandable considering how busy they are and it is worth the wait!

The food here is great and they have so much variety! They range from asian food to Italian to american and everything in between. Make sure you don't fill up on one section because you want to get around to trying everything. They also have a little dessert island in the middle of the restaurant with endless desserts and gelato, yum! One star off for service because the workers here really are so rude but other than that, will be back!

This place was quite a disappointment. For the amount paid ($52.00 each) we expected more in regards to food quality and service alike. They get credit for presentation! Everything LOOKS great. Some of the foods we encountered were definitely not being served at their peak freshness. The sushi station had scores of little individually plated bites. Unfortunately, none of the bites I sampled were actually fresh. They seemed like they had been plated and left uncovered hours previously. What a let down. This joint has tons of potential!  I  was expecting stellar customer service and attention to detail. Our server only managed to visit twice during our visit. If I am expected to leave a $20.00 tip , is it possible to at least get some drink refills?? We got offered no coffee with our dessert, seriously? There are plenty of other spots that offer a better quality for less money. SKIP IT.

Hometown Buffet ain't got nothing on Bacchanal.

Good quality food. 
This is gonna be my regular spot when I'm in Vegas.

I wasn't too sure what I was anticipating when I first got here. My sister heard a lot about this place and said we should go. I didn't yelp the buffet before we went in so, I really didn't know what to expect. It's pretty pricey, not going to lie, but what we did was go in about 30 minutes before the time allotted for breakfast was over, so we could have the lunch food for the price of breakfast, knowing that it was the cheapest then. 

There's a lot of food, but if you're not a big seafood fan, your options are cut down by about 1/4. A lot of the food they had out included seafood, so for me, I didn't have a lot of choices. I got a lot of breakfast foods like the eggs and bacon, which were all ok. The mac and cheese however was delicious. Also, they had something called the "Chef Special" that was like pork in a green and brown sauce, also super good. They also have juices: watermelon, tropical, carrot, and orange. All of them are delish.

The dessert however was disappointing. I have a sweet tooth and was looking forward to some expensive and tasty treats considering the price we paid. There wasn't anything exceptionally good, so I resorted to fruits.

Also, the servers take forever! We had to wait 10 minutes for water and the refills took even longer. 

Overall, I don't think I would come here again, they have both good and not so good things out, but I guess it depends on your taste.

I came here in February with family and to be honest it is a real disappointment. They didn't have the good stuff like lobster or  king crab. The food was decent but I wouldn't say it is worth the hefty price per person. I get just as good of a buffet at restaurants back home. There was a decent wait but it seems that is to be expected. I feel like there was just not much variety in general. They had sushi but not much variety. It was always long lines for the seafood but that's to be expected because people tend to go for the more expensive stuff. They also offer a drink package to go along with your meal and I just don't see paying an extra $$ with the hefty cost per person. There are other buffets are much cheaper and just as good on the strip.
Wish I had it for dinner.. amazing Buffett for breakfast. Great eats can't wait to return. You want it they had it!!
Good food but pricey! My favorite dish was ironically their pho noodles....which i can get for 1/5 the price. But the staffs are very friendly!

It's a great buffet, much much better than the Caesars buffet in Atlantic city. You can almost find everything you want to eat here. The most impressing point: they have very huge and very fresh blueberries!!!

I do not recommend this place! 
Just look at the floor!
It's so dirty!

I lost my apetite when I saw that much dust yikes!!!!

First time trying here, love their cocktail shrimp the most.  They have lamb rack but not the same way as how Wynn cook it and it's too well done for me.  Bufflo wings are pretty good, but kind of spicy.  The only bad thing is sashimi looks pretty dry tho.  They have oysters, but doesn't really taste good to me.  The oysters have no taste at all.  Love the dessert area with crepes and their ice cream mochi is the bomb.

One of the most incredible meals I've ever had. Everything was so fantastic and delicious. Each section of the buffet reviewed alone would be 5 stars. The desserts were so good (mochi, gelato bar, macaroons and marshmallows were personal favorite). Loved it so much I went twice in one weekend. Yes, it was worth the money!

Bacchanal takes buffets to the next level. It is raising the standard and quality of buffet food.  Just the mere fact that it has the option of hot or cold crab is awe-inspiring! (Seriously, hot crab!)

Each station is treated like it's own restaurant, which keeps the quality fantastic. The meat station has more meat than one could ever think to try! The brisket, prime rib, lamb, and sausages are all great. 

The asian station has soup dumplings that are about as good as some soup dumplings that I've had from actual Chinese restaurants. The siu mai and pot stickers are pretty on point as well.

One of the best dishes is the truffle scalloped potatoes. Yes, you had me at truffle. The sauce has an amazing truffle flavor that continues through the entire dish. You can actually see the truffle shavings in the sauce. 

The desserts are also better than regular buffets. This past time my favorite dessert was the passion fruit tart. There's even a station that makes freshly squeezed juices served in little glass containers. My favorite is the guava. I saw they also had mango and horchata.

Get there early - the first night we arrived at 8:30pm and were turned away because it was too full and they weren't even going to start seating again until a few minutes before closing. Even with the long lines and pricey bill, Bacchanal is totally worth it.
Excellent food selection and great quality food.  Weekend buffet is $54, but it's worth every penny.

So, my hubby and I have been to this buffet several times in the last few years, and the last two times we have gone(today and in May 2017) the quality of the food as well as the variety have gone down, while the prices have gone up.  We went on Mother's Day, were charged an arm and a leg, when they ran out of a lot of things, and found out they weren't serving lamb chops(which is one of the best things on the menu).  Today we decided to try it again and were very disappointed.  Again, no lamb chops, this time, they ran out of crème brulee, they didn't have the variety of veggies they normally have, no ravioli in lobster sauce, so basically there were only a few items that I found that were tasty.  We were also told multiple times that the lamp chops would be ready at 3p and an hour later, still no lamb chops and it turned out they weren't serving lamb chops, so basically waited for nothing.  It would be understandable if they raised prices and kept the food quality the same, but when you raise prices and the food goes down, that's a really bad combo.  There are many other options in Vegas where you get more for what you pay for.  I have other reviews for some other places we have eaten where you don't get price gouged.

Ever since I found out about this buffet I've been dying to come here. 

I came in on a Monday around 11 and surprisingly we got seated right away. There wasn't a wait time which was a plus. 

Anyway, we were seated and the food selection they had was really amazing. The chefs in the back are constantly cooking and refilling the food so everything tasted really fresh. 

Although I did love this buffet, the majority of the foods offered are meat and seafood which I'm not a fan of so I was sticking mainly to the non meat dishes. They didn't have a lot of veggie options when I went so that was a bummer. 

The dessert section was really amazing. They had made to order crepes, a good ice cream selection, various cupcakes and other individual sized desserts. 

It's definitely worth a try.

Wow, quite the buffet, everything you can imagine. Seafood, breakfast, beef, Oriental, sushi, Mexican. You can't possibly eat everything at this buffet, even had stone crab. A little pricey but worth it, bring an appetite.

Yummy! Before I do this review, let me give my dish recommendations to you curious cats: 

- King crab legs
- Lobster corn soup
- Cheddar broccoli
- Oyster shot
- Salmon poke
- Sweet potato fries
- Vanilla creme brulee
- Mexican chilli-mayo corn

This is the yummiest buffet in Vegas, in my opinion of course. It took 30 mins for me to finally make it to the front of the line, but it was worth it. The presentation is fancier than your typical casino buffet (gold coast, the M, orleans, rio). Although be careful, all the fancy/cute ala carte dishes can easily slide off your plate. The chefs are all really enthusiastic & friendly. They try to help you & greet you. The server I had was "eh." All buffet servers really do is get your drinks & take away your plates, so if I needed anything (refills, change), we had to wave him down. This is a huge buffet for seating & good selections. Half-way through their stations I was getting full. Their food is a big hit or miss! It's either yummy & delicious, or blah. I noticed some of my dishes tasted too salty. As for everything else, it's above average! I was intrigued seeing the decor & certain food choices. Desserts have a big selection too & not just "the usual." This buffet is $45 but better than getting a Las Vegas whole day buffet-hopping pass. & that says a lot!

You know how food usually tastes better when you're really hungry? Yeah well I was starving and the food was still meh. 

Below average food for a ridiculously long wait and and expensive for no reason. Even the fresh crab wasn't good. The only thing they did well was their desserts. Best flan ever but other than that everything was so unmemorable and bland. The Chinese/Asian food section was terrible. One of the best things from last night's dinner was a lemon salad... 

I had to search for reasons to justify the price but there was absolutely nothing. Albeit the service was good though. Everyone was really friendly and nice. 

You would only come here to cross this off a bucket list, not to enjoy good food.
Don't understand what all the hype is about.  It was just ok.  This buffet was not worth $60. I would say it's worth $40.

Tied for the best buffet in Las Vegas with The Buffet at Wynn. Show up early because there is always a line. The Asian selections are perfect. The wagyu sliders are amazing. Best dessert bar in Vegas.

Five stars to Carlos, he is the best waiter ive ever seen, i ho0e they promote him to manager and then give him the entire casino because he is the best. #thankscarlos



Also the sushi is awful, stay away.
The best buffet in Vegas in my opinion. The food is fresher compare to the wicked spoon and the selection is bigger and better than others in town. :) luv it!

I keep hearing the buffet is the best in Vegas! So I finally tried it when I was there Mother's day weekend! I was there on Monday, May 15th for dinner and I tell you this place is overrated, I was very disappointed....

The food looks better in these pictures than in person.

The food here is not all that for $50 for dinner is not worth it.  In fact when we all left this place we all had stomach aches, I'm not sure if they leave food out too long or it was bad.  I would never go back here again it is not worth the money.  Also when we first went up to pay the women at the register was rude and not very friendly at all.

The lines are not very organized.

Please tell the workers they need to be more friendly and need to organize the line better.

Best buffet in Vegas if you ask me!  Over 500 items with a noodle section with ramen, udon or pho...A+!!  Only downside is their ridiculous long lines.  They charge a $25 cut in line...totally worth it in my book to NOT wait 2 hours for food.  Their gelato selection is awesome and I ain't even a sweets type of guy.

The BEST buffet that I have ever been to. Amazing.

We probably waited about 30 minutes until we got seated and of course you know you have to go when lunch is almost done and dinner is about to start to get the best of both worlds.

There is so much high quality food at Bacchanal, it will not disappoint. Some of the notable mentions would be:

Lamp chops
Roast duck
Hot and sour soup
PRIME RIB
Ramen and pho station
Dim sum
KING CRAB LEGS (cold or steamed)
Mussels
Oysters
Seabass
Lobster bisque
Seafood paella
BLOOD ORANGE SORBET
Creme Brulee
Macarons

All caps means MUST TRY! Even the more simple, typical plates were high quality: pasta, fresh shrimp, salad bar, pizza, sliders, chicken nuggets, fries, etc.

Be aware that if you have more than 8 people in your party, they will automatically add on a 18% gratuity fee.

Bacchanal will now be my default buffet when I visit Vegas...that is...until another hotel decides to build or revamp an even better one.

First buffet we tried on our day 1 trip. 

Wait is very long. Estimate wait time for weekdays is 120mins. 

Advice: go there and get a ticket so u don't have to wait forever. It gives you a certain time so you can go out or play until the time giving is up. Then you show the attendee and they will let u get in line to pay, after that you will get in line for seating which took another 15-20min.

Food: they have from Asian to seafood. 

Best: fresh seafood(crab legs, sea snails, shrimp)
Asian section they have dim sum, fried rice, soup, sushi, and pork. They also have tacos, great selection of meat like brisket, steak and mini burgers. 

Deserts: is awesome. Can't get enough.

It's worth the wait. 

Went to on Wednesday night around 6:30pm waited 120min and price is $54.99. 

Great buffet and will likely to stop by again

This is literally the BEST buffet I have ever been to, hands down! It's even better than the buffets on cruise ships as well! I believe this buffet is also on the ultimate buffet list (which we didn't do.)

For ~45 dollars, you get a legitimately fine dining experience with unlimited mimosas, fresh squeeze orange juice, coffee, and champagne to your heart's content. There are even well dressed servers to come by and pour you your much needed alcohol or coffee after a night of drinking!

Food is amazing as well! Lots of selection including different area of ethnic food. We happen to go for brunch/ lunch on a Sunday and there was your usual breakfast food, Asian, French, Mexican, ect. I can't even begin to explain the awesomeness of their dessert selection, I managed to steal so many of their little mints! 

The best part is we went for brunch, and stayed for lunch... We could have stayed for dinner as well but we had already been there for about four hours eating our life away....

The only drawback is the wait to get into the buffet... I think we had to wait for about an hour and a half. But once you weasel your way in, the place is so big and well organized that you'll never notice the crowd.

Tried the Friday brunch and was satisfied. ~20-30 min wait. The dim sum was allright. The Shrimp & Grits were awesome, street tacos great, and the flan and creme brule' excellent. Not a bad value for lunch, but the price tag for dinner seems high.

12/26/2016 peak hour seating.
came in at 2:30pm, prepared to wait for one to two hours to get in, but nope, virtual que told us the current wait time is 500 minutes, please come back after 10:30pm... is this a joke? so we have to wait until 10:30pm and pay roughly around $75 per person for a buffet? no thanks.
by the way, we never got that phone call or text message at 10:30, imagine if we really waited...

Pretty effing epic buffet. Only one star off for the wait. And boy, is there a wait. Started the line around 2pm on a Saturday. Figured the lunch rush would be over. Wrong. 1.5 hours later, we were seated. But man, SO much choice. SO much quality. From dim sum, to shellfish, crab legs, prime rib, burgers, truffled polenta, cute beet and mozzarella/tomato salads galore, it's everything you could want and more. The dessert buffet itself is pretty epic. Mochi ice-creams, gelatos, cakes, macarons, pies, tarts, cake pops, and these epic peanut butter cookies that my friends kept raving about. My favorite of course was the seafood legs. I pretty much filled up on oyster shooters, king crab legs, clam bakes (SO CUTE and SO TASTY), lobsters and leeks, and mussels. The dim sum was also surprisingly quality. As a Californian, I'm pretty picky about dim sum, but this pasts muster. Very good. The truffled polenta was a surprising treat as well. As for dessert, the mint and watermelon sorbet was incredibly refreshing. Would definitely hit up again when I come back to Vegas. Maybe I'll pay a little extra to not wait 1.5 hours though.

Excellent Buffet!!!!!! I really enjoyed eating here.  I love the seperate sections for each cuisine.  BBQ/ American homestyle, Italian, Asian/Sushi, Latin/Taco Bar, My favorite the Seafood bar with Shrimp, Mussels, Escargot and unlimited Crab legs ( Snow, Dungeonus & KING ).   Last but not least the massive dessert bar (Gelato, Pana Cotta, Cream Brullee) and much more.  In addition Chef Steve Lee was actually going around checking tables making sure everyone was satisfied and enjoying themselves.  Great customer service makes the meal that much better!!!!!!!!!! I will definitely be returning here my next visit to Las Vegas.  Thanks Again!!!!!

Went here on a Friday me and my girls were trying to come for breakfast but due to checking out and waking up late only made lunch. It was 38.99+ $10 for unlimited mimosas.( My best friend had never had a mimosa before so we need to change that pronto.) They food was great I stuffed myself full of meatballs and tacos and shrimp cocktail. The Prime rib was on point!!!! I was just disappointed I couldn't make enough room to enjoy all the desserts I wanted too but I did have the gelato which was delicious. I was bummed because they only make macaroons Saturday and Sunday but everything else definitely made up for that. I will definitely come back when I go to Vegas in a few months!

3rd time visit:

going downhill!!  but the price is still the same or increased.

The price, is still the same.

The wait, has changed. You now have to pre-check in at the kiosk then it'll print out a little receipt where it tells you what time to go back to the podium to check in and then wait in line to pay. 

We got there at 4:45 expecting a long wait.. but instead we had to do the kiosk thing and ended up eating at 7pm instead and we were in a time crunch since we had a show at 9:30pm. If we had known this early, we wouldn't have been so rushed. Anyway, so i'm giving you a heads up now.

on to the food. same selection but less. looks like they cut down on the desserts. back in january i remember being able to select from 4 to 5 different mochi flavors, this time, just two. There were more ice cream / sorbets back in january, now there were only less than one row of ice cream selection... the other row was DISPLAY ONLY.

the crab legs were alright. still not as meaty, however, it is better than the first time i've visited. The stone crab claws were not good - no taste. If i'm paying over $50 for buffet, i expect better quality seafood. Those crab legs need to be upgraded to fatter ones. Those skinny legs are not acceptable. I can get those crab legs at a different buffet for a much lesser price.

their turn around time for plates were slow this time. There were times when there were no plates at all in almost all of the stations. 

i must say that this 3rd visit, was a let down. Most of the time i was just walking around thinking what I should get to eat. Nothing really stood out this time (except for their miso glazed sea bass).

i'm not sure if i'll be visiting bacchanal again if they continue with this quality of food. It just wasn't as good as when they first started. If that's the case, i rather spend less money at a different buffet and eat mediocre food. why pay so much and also get [slightly above] mediocre food?

Not worth it at all. I heard many good reviews before coming to Vegas but unfortunately we were very unimpressed. Not only is it $60 a person but half of the food was cold and the other half of my food was bad in taste.

Best buffet I've been to yet. This was my first Las Vegas buffet experience and none have come close to matching my experience. All of the food tasted high quality, every dish Was restaurant quality. The shrimp was sweet and fresh and the deep fried food is presented in an adorable way. Most memorable for me was the maple glazed sweet potato tater tots. I've dreamt of them and even tried recreating them at home. Servers were really nice and didnt mind continuing to refill out drinks while we digested and went back for round two... Then three... Then...

I have not had a Vegas buffet in ages but I was happy to see that Bacchanal had an electronic system to avoid unnecessarily long lines. You enter your phone number in the system and they text you when to come back instead of you standing there for hours starving to death. What a great idear!

The seafood options were plentiful and super fresh. The fruit selection was disappointing as they really only had cantaloupe, honeydew, and pineapple. They had an amazing meatball but some of the dishes we tried were salty or overcooked. The dessert bar has tons of options but the lady scooping gelato was quite disgruntled.

Highlight of the evening....
They take your picture before you enter the buffet them come around during your meal to see if you are interested in purchasing the picture. We had a group of four people at our table but when the guy came back he showed us a picture solo Asian guy. We did not want to purchase a picture but it was shocking as he had no clue or did not care.

The staff are not friendly. Especially the hostess (older lady with glasses). There are times that she put her head down and shook her head starring at the tickets. She look overwhelmed and stress? Its only 9am.

I bought the VIP $68 for the couple breakfast Groupon and the only thing that was a plus was a shorter line. We were seated all the way in the asian food section. We ask for our drinks 2 times with 2 different waiter. When we were about to be full I remember the Mimosa that was included. I ask for it and the waiter looked confused. I show him the receipt (VIP) and he said "Oh how come, you guys are siting here." He came back with our Mimosa. Btw it took awhile for them to collect our finish plates, I had to push all the dirty plates in the middle to get space to place the plate I am eating.

We are almost done with eating, just needed to finish feeding our 11month old son. Another table with a party of 3 came to sit next to our table. The hostess said "Your baby can't sit here, you see (pointing the path) its blocking (shook her head)". I was feeding my son and had to carry him and the high chair to the opposite side. 

From the start of getting seated to pile of plates sums up, BAD experience for us. We really wanted to like this buffet but no mater how successful the business is the employees (staff) is the important part that draws coustomer in aswell. I mean the food are fantastic but just dont feel welcomed and comfortable. It will be nice to have a better service.

Will not come back.

I come here about once a year and I have not noticed the decline in quality that people have been mentioning in the reviews. Maybe the quality of ingredients has gotten cheaper compared to ten years ago, but as of late, they have been very consistent. I do not know what to say that 5,000+ reviews have missed, so I will just share my experiences from a few dinners here.

Last time, I did the Buffet of Buffets and added Bacchanal for the low, low price of $30? or so (this was on a weekday). Yes, it's pricy but, if you've never done it before, you might as well go for it. Because it was a weekday, there was no line. We were able to pay and be seated very quickly. On a weekend? Forget about it! You can wait up to an hour to receive a text that tells you "get in line" and spend maybe another half hour or more in line. Gives you time to check out Caesar's Palace - gamble, drink, or walk through the mall and pretend to be rich. That's what we do. You have the freedom to choose how you spend your hours waiting.

Once you finally get seated, you're free! Unless you're a very picky eater or you're the gluten free, vegan, non-GMO, whatever type of person, you'll find something at Bacchanal. I always go for the dim sum and sushi. My first plate is always packed with dim sum. The quality is on par with real Asian restaurants that I've been to in the LA area. Their sushi is not particularly special, but at least it's not frozen. (Wait for my review on the Wynn's buffet. I'll tell you all about frozen sushi.)

You cannot go to this place without getting a plate of crab legs. (Oops, accidentally submitted it without finishing.) I always get crab legs - especially when they're serving them straight out of the pot. Crab legs are always good, but they are much better hot than cold.

Honestly, thinking back on my visits to Bacchanal, I wish I had tried more items. I tend to stay away from Italian and Mexican food at buffets because I eat that very frequently at home. I did make it a point to try their tacos, though. The spinning grill is a nice touch, but I prefer actual street tacos. Something about the grease makes them taste better.

I think they have all-you-can-drink beer for $22? Never tried it, since I go there for the vast amounts of food. 

Overall, I recommend trying Bacchanal if you have not yet. It is pricy and there is a line on weekends, no doubt about it.

This was going to be the highlight of my trip. I've been to Vegas a few times and for one reason or another, I never get to make it out to the Bacchanal Buffet. For my current trip, it was the only thing on my list that I had to hit up.

We arrived at about 7pm on a Thursday night. The line was fairly large but it was actually fast moving and we were seated within 15 minutes. I saw that they have a machine to add your name to the wait list, if the line is extremely long. So that's kind of nice that you don't have to wait around if it's a large wait. The cost for dinner on a non weekend night is $54.99.

We were initially very impressed with the huge selection of food. The choices are great, and there were all sorts of things to try. We saw pastas, tacos, pizza, chinese, sushi, an impressive carving station, large assortments of bread, charcuterie, a massive dessert area and the pièce de résistance, the seafood station. Oh yes. I was very impressed there were things I hadn't seen at a buffet before such as bone marrow, escargot, oyster shots.. pretty cool!

Being from Vancouver, I have access to an incredible variety of food. We have phenomenal pasta, pizza, sushi, a HUGE selection of great chinese, and we even have access to seafood buffets. My favorite being a seafood buffet under $25 about an hour from Vancouver, located in Washington state. Being a bit of a foodie, I was so excited to try out all my favorites at once place! 

I skipped the Chinese and Japanese. I can get that at home and am not a newb to buffets. I'm here for the good stuff. Meat and seafood. 

I was sorely disappointed. The oysters were pacific oysters. Cheap, fairly tasteless and nothing exciting. There were some king crab legs but to be honest, it was a lot of work as they were small and offered little meat. And if you weren't quick, the king crab legs were taken, and what was left on the plate was the other variety of crab legs (even more work to get meat). My spouse had the octopus, and was disappointed with how overdone it was. He had to spit it out.

The meat was alright I guess. I've had better at cheaper buffets. I was super excited to see American Wagyu beef offered along with prime rib roast and bacon at the carving station. The bacon was great, typical bacon. Nothing to screw up there. I asked for the Wagyu beef, while my spouse asked for the prime rib roast. We got the same thing. Alright. Well, whatever it was, it was overdone. It was tough, chewy and flavorless. I did not eat the whole piece offered. 

I didn't eat the pizza myself, though my spouse did. From just looking at it, I asked if he was sure he wanted one as it looked like it had been sitting out for some time. He said it tasted the same. 

I tried the bone marrow. It was overdone. 

We spent our entire time at the table, talking about how terrible the food was. We gave the dessert table a shot, hoping we could fill up on that before leaving. The ice cream was good, hard to screw that up. I tried the flan, tiramisu, creme brulee and macarons. The flan and creme brulee were good. Nothing special but acceptable. Tiramisu was not really tiramisu but it tasted pretty good. It had the flavors of tiramisu, was just assembled differently. I was particularly excited to see macarons offered. In addition to being a foodie and eating out, I also enjoy cooking at home and baking. I bake macarons and have had some moderate success. These things are not easy to make. On initial bite, I was impressed with how fluffy the cookies were. There could have been a little more filling but it rivaled the cookies I buy for $3 each at home. Not bad. Then I tried the next macaron, and it tasted like it was 3 days expired. It was incredibly chewy and I had to spit it out. I had 2 more flavors, and had one that was acceptable and one that was old as well. 

The macarons basically summed up our experience. This experience was hit and miss. The food is acceptable. You do get a choice of a wide variety of food, and I could see this being particularly great for someone who doesn't get a wide variety of choices at home. If you do have access to these kinds of food at home and have a quality to compare to, you will be disappointed. It will not live up to what you are expecting and used to. 

It was an experience to try, and I'm happy I did. But I will not being returning in the future.

One word amazing! Definitely worth 24.99... 9 food stations over 500+ dishes, super fresh sea food selection and the desert divine! OMG the fresh squeezed jucies wow best ever. Prime Rib melts in your mouth and the oyster tasted like they just shucked them straight from the ocean!

Decor very tasteful & modern

Service ~ Nancy was Awesome thank you!

Don't come to here during the holidays. The regular waiting time is 3 hours. For the express line that you have to pay extra $25 per person (which caused the line waiting longer) with a horrible casher lady services you. My friends and I waited 2 times for the express line. The first time we asked the casher question about the price and the food for the lunch and she had no patience with us. Then we stand away to made a decision whether eat here or not, then come back to the cashier again, but she told us to waited in the line again!

THE best buffet that Las Vegas has to offer. Yes I said it, b e s t.
I always have to make a trip to Bacchanal on all my Vegas getaways.
Be prepared to wait during peak hours, but it's definitely worth the wait.

The selection of food is amazing, great variety. One of my personal favorites (and please don't shame me for carbing up at a buffet) is the Mac N' Cheese... it's packed with flavor and it's nice and heavy. 

Meats are A-1, desserts are yummy, and service is pretty good.

Great buffet! Tons of choices. Everything we tried was excellent! We went for brunch on Sunday around 10:30; line was reasonable and moved quickly. It was pricey for brunch ($80+ for two), but the available options were worth it. I would definitely recommend. Just make sure to take as much time as possible (they say 2 hours max) & try as many things as you can!

Buffets aren't really my thing, but in Vegas - why not? For $60, I really expected something amazing, but was really just a fancy Golden Corral. There was a big selection of seafood, but I was disappointed in the lack of red meat. No steak, Caesar? Also, the line to get in on a Saturday night was insane. We waited nearly an hour to be seated, and then every line for main courses were at least 20 people deep. Unless you think you can eat your money's worth in quantity, I'd recommend you skip Bacchanal and spend $60 bucks on a meal where the chef has actually touched your food.
Vegas is known for their awesome buffets and Bacchanal is one of the newest and is definitely one of the best. So much choices, so much food....KING CRAB LEGS FOR DAYS!!!

This rating if not so much for the staff but the food.  The staff was pleasant - can't complain there.  However, for the price and with all the buffet options in Las Vegas, this place does not deserve to have the highest rating on Yelp. Bacchanal should be in the middle of the pack. 

The husband and I were visiting Vegas in September.  We did a buffet a day.  Mirage's Cravings was the best.

I am giving it 3 stars because of the price! Way over priced for what you get. The dining area has no ambiance and the dinner music is way to loud and obnoxious. The food is very good and the selection is large. As it should be for the price! The desert bar is lacking. I have had more selections at a 18.00 buffet. Not much fruit to choose from. My recommendation for what it's worth is to look around there are much better deals in this town as I lived hear in the past and still a Nevada resident.

Pretty good, I don't suggest going for brunch. I have gone for lunch/dinner and had a much more satisfying meal. I really wish the crab legs were warm as ice cold crab just isn't my thing. I would go back, just not for brunch.

I felt like this buffet was mediocre at best. The chinese section isnt even worth mentioning. I think I'd rather eat panda express. Seriously. The meat selections were so dry and reminiscentof other typical buffets. The Desert section is decent. The best part of this buffet is the King Crab Legs and the shrimp. But if you think about it, It is pretty hard to screw that up considering they just buy it in bulk and freeze em. For the same price and less wait time, you would have a better experience at the M buffet.

This review is more for the staff than the food. The food was fine, but I think Wicked Spoon is a much nicer place to eat, this place felt a little worn out and the service was lack luster. 

My main issue is that halfway through our meal, an elderly waitress came up to me (and a woman a few tables away from me) and told us individually that we weren't welcome to breastfeed our babies there. Neither her nor I were showing as much as an inch of skin and in fact I'm surprised she could even tell I was feeding my child as I was wearing an oversized black sweater.

Both the other woman and myself were so taken aback by it, it's never been an issue for either of us, myself in LA and her in Vancouver- neither of us had ever been reprimanded. We were just discreetly feeding our 8 month olds as mothers everywhere do.

I felt so unwelcomed and when the manager, whom I asked to see, came over she didn't really have much to say aside from "um, sorry?". Barely an apology for making me so uncomfortable after spending a ton of money at their restaurant. 

Super tacky and totally behind the times. And especially ironic in LAS VEGAS where there were scantily clad women all around us. 

Breastfeeding mothers are not welcome here and that's not a place I choose to support.
Wow. Only just opened - I managed to make the opening day. Friendly staff, fresh food, masses of choice and comfortable seats! Excellent - all for $20?!?!

We went here during the Thanksgiving holiday. Place was consistently packed. You need to pre register at a kiosk and you'll get a text when it's close to your party being seated. Average wait time for us was a couple of hours. Who cares, right? You're in Vegas, so there's plenty of distractions to widdle away the time. The wait was well worth it. High quality diverse food, plus we opted for the unlimited beer add on to wash it all down. You got your crab legs which is probably the most popular item, also my favorite they have pork rinds and cheeses which I focused more on since I'm a lover of cheese. It's expensive, but well worth it. If you go to Vegas, do yourself a favor and check out this place

I used to think Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan was the best buffet in Vegas until I came here. I came here for dinner on a Saturday night with a few friends and the line was so long that the wait was at 2 hours. Instead we opted to pay the express fee of $15 on top of the $50+ price tag for this buffet and we were seated immediately. The dining area is humongous and I believe seats well over 700. The decor is very upscale. I really felt we were dining in one of the fanciest places in town.

I thought Wicked Spoon had a giant selection, but this place has a lot more. Its broken up into sections depending on the type of cuisine. There's seafood, chinese, japanese, mexican, american, salad, dessert. I was able to get a plate from every section and sample almost all the food, but was limited by my stomach capacity unfortunately. 

The quality/taste of the food was a lot better than the average buffet but of course not as exceptional as a sit down and order type restaurant. In my opinion the must try's are definitely the macarons, made to order ramen noodle soup, prime rib, salmon, HORCHATA, the sushi rolls....actually just try everything. The presentation of the food also was impressive. There's only so much I can describe with words though so I must say go and try for yourself and be amazed!
Super yummy! Worth the wait and price! Would definitely recommend this buffet if you are in Vegas.

ADVICE: come with an empty stomach and an empty mind, no time to think & converse. 
Lawwddd the buffet Gods has blessed us with this delicious place. Bacchanal has such a variety, ranging from Japanese, Thai, Chinese, Italian, Spanish, Mexican, and good ol' US of A. Didn't waste much of my stomach space on the Chinese and Japanese food, because not much luxury food items are there... My 60$ needs to be spent on seafood & meat!! 
My favorite section must have been the Thai food. They had little spicey shooters, I must have eaten like 5 of those. 
Their clam chowda was good, but what made it extraordinary was me pulling out the crab meat fr the king crab legs and mixing it in my sopa- slap yo momma good. 
They had a taco station, where you choose the meat and a dude makes the taco as you order.
Their dessert section was insane. I wish I could have stayed another hour to force myself to eat more dessert dishes, but I just couldn't. I probably had crab meat leaking out of my nose & mouth by the time I got to dessert. 
Much of their desserts had an Asian influence, lots of sago & tapioca... Matcha green tea inspired macaroons and ice cream... red bean, mochi things. 
Anyways, point is... If you're a buffet fan, Bacchanal is a must "try once in your life" type of restaurant. 
And DUH of course there will be a wait...

Bacchanal offers the best buffet I have ever eaten at.  The design of the restaurant is modern, light and beautiful.  The food buffets seem to be everywhere and go on forever and the food is so beautifully presented.  

Get this - I dined here for both breakfast and dinner yesterday by my friends' request because she loves it so much.  Here are my thoughts:

Breakfast here on a Wednesday was great.  We arrived at about 8:30am and did not need to wait in line at all.  We were seated immediately.  I really enjoyed their dim sum.  The pan fried chive and shrimp dumpling was a bit different from an authentic perspective but it was very delicious.  The "lai wong bao" (a custard bun) was only okay - the steamed bun was great but the filling was a bit off.  The Congee with thousand year old egg, all the toppings, and you tiao (Chinese fried donut) was delicious.  I also grabbed an eggs benedict, and it was the best eggs benedict (excluding specialty versions) that I have ever had.  I also had their fresh orange juice, fresh watermelon juice, and coffee.  All of them were excellent.
