On the same night, we had dinner here at about 8pm.  There was a healthy line but it was fine.  The Asian food was all excellent - pan fried green beans, cooked-to-order ramen, ha gow (shrimp dumpling), a vegetarian bean curd wrap, and blackened chicken soup.  I thought the pile of meat looked very enticing, but my smoked brisket and lamb chops were just standard .  The seafood I had was all good - crab legs, oysters and shrimp cocktail.  I loved the fresh juices so much for breakfast that I grabbed another one and finished it quickly!  Lastly, the desserts were great.  The shining star of dessert was the black sesame mochi ice cream.  The black sesame ice cream had a great nutty flavor, and the mochi wrapped around it was a perfect thickness and so soft and fresh.  I'll look forward to returning one day and having their mochi again.

Overall, well done Bacchanal!

Excellent buffet great variety and flavor is good!
I would recommend this buffet when in Vegas!

An hour and 40 minute wait for a Sunday lunch.  They have a fancy system where you can check in and leave your phone number so they can text you when your table is ready. You can also pay $15 extra per person to skip the lines but even those were sold out when we went.

The place looks clean and modern, with light, white colors unlike most other colorful buffets in vegas.

We ended up paying about $43 (saved $1 by showing a Totally Rewards card) and champagne was no longer included :( They did include soft drinks and good tea, which "helped" digest everything we ate (at least it made think so)

AYCE oysters and crab legs (the cold ones were a bit icy but if you go to the italian station they boil them a bit and they are yummier)

In the asian noodle station, they had pho, ramen and chinese noodles.

The desserts, omg!!!! they come in small sizes so you can taste everything.... GREEN TEA brulee in addition to the traditional, cakes, and even SHAVED ICE!!!! They really stepped up a notch and quality was very good! 

Yes, its pricey but its vegas, its a buffet.  TOTALLY RECOMMEND,!!!

If you happen to stay in Caesars Palace in Vegas and are a sea food person, definitely try out Bacchanal Buffet. Tons of fresh sea food dishes and cuisine across the world. The price is not too expensive given the variety and the quality of the food. I like the dessert bar in specific :) ！

Wow, this buffet is crazy with so many food selections from around the world. My friends recommended this place as being one of the best buffets in Las Vegas and I'm very happy I went. 

     To start off with, I should give a few tips. This is a HUGE buffet! I would suggest taking your time and be very selective when choosing the items you want to eat. I would just grab a little of everything because let's be honest, you are probably not going to love every single item here. (I was disappointed by how the ramen broth tasted way too salty)

    Also, all the time you spend picking your food for like ten minutes will make your plate get cold by the time you sit down to enjoy it. I would just go to one section at a time and take all the food from that section and then go straight to your table to eat. 

      Some items worthy of noting are the opened crab legs. Omg, they were so easy to just eat and enjoy that I ended up gobbling 10 lbs of this. The braised beef was bomb! And the dimsum was pretty decent!

     The desserts station looked amazing, but a lot of them were way too sugary. I recommend the gelato (my personal favorite is the black sesame gelato and green tea!)

       Overall, take your time and savor all this damn food! It's quite an experience and a highlight of vegas!

The food is not fresh I got sick after eating at this place !!! Never again !!! 
Everytime I eat in cheap buffet and I never had problems...

The seafood selection is amazing!! Steaming crab legs, salmon, oysters, cold crab legs.  The Asian portion of the Buffett is great. Mexican food I didn't try because I'm Mexican lol. The desert wasn't the best just because it's not my favorite desert selection. The items I did get like macaroons and chocolate molten mini cake were amazing.  Hilda our server is phenomenal.  Very attentive and caring.  Brought our drinks even before we finished and was constantly checking on us.  Jesus is a miracle crab man absolutely delicious.  He is funny and so kind.  Hilda and Jesus are a huge asset to this buffet.  A negative is the seats need to be changed not comfy at all. Wait times aren't bad.  However once you get through the line you wait in 2 more lines. Don't upgrade to express seating as you can go gamble or do whatever you like and you are texted when your seat is ready. Not worth paying the $35 per person express rate.

Lunch was $42/person. But worth it. They have everything. Shrimp, crab legs, ramen, udon, pho, sushi, pats, pizza, taco.... tins of dessert and gelato. My favorite is the fresh juices. Carrot juices, cucumber, hibiscus, watermelon. I am stuffed.

I got to the buffet around 5:30 PM on a Saturday.  The line was ridiculously long and slow moving.  There is an express line that you can pay an extra 15 dollars for, which i decided to do.  Even in the express line, it still was an hour of waiting in line before I was seated.

On my way to my seat I walked passed a giant line of people with empty plates waiting for the meat station and the sea food station.   I had already been waiting for a while, and was pretty hungry so I decided to try other things first.

I started off with their salad bar, they didn't have black olives or mushrooms, and they had these tall bottles for the dressing, the blue cheese seemed to be clogged up though which was a pain to deal with.   The lettuce was not cut small enough or at all in some cases, overall it was a pretty poor salad bar.

I got some beef with broccolli from the asian station, and some lo mein, I also picked up a slice of pizza.  The beef with broccoli was the worst I've ever had(worse than when I used to make it in on a hotplate in college), the pizza was soggy and the lo main was mushy.   I found a section that was being blocked off by the enormous line, and got some clam chowder, which was watery and way to salty.

Giving up on the other foods there I decided to wait in line for the meats.  It took 30 minutes before I got to the front, I got ribeye and a piece of brisket and returned to find my table completely cleared, I don't blame the servers for this, I had been away from my table for half an hour.  Although once in a buffet, half an hour is a ridiculous amount of time to spend in line.

The ribeye was well cooked and seasoned, the brisket was dry.   I then spent another 20 minutes waiting for seafood, the crab was decent but I have had way better.   The deserts that I tried at the desert station were really good, though the selection was somewhat small.

Overall it was a pretty lousy experience, by the time I left the lines had significantly shortened, I might have just got unlucky with my timing, however the waits were totally unacceptable.  The whole buffet seemed poorly put together from the food, to the lines, to the general layout of the whole place.

For the price(45 dollars + 15 for the express pass), there are way better buffets in town.  Wicked spoon has been great every time I went, the buffet at the M was incredible.  The buffet at the bellagio and wynn are also good options.
Great selection of food definitely worth the price! It can get very busy so get there early!

I love buffets but  i think didnt have a big appetite that day! Came here for lunch and there was barely a line! $35 a person. The design of this place looks amazing! Food was literally everywhere! Only disappointment I had about this place when I asked for a plate of salmon sashimi with no rice the chef said something I couldnt understand. I had a ton of shrimp cocktails and a few oysters! I didnt eat any of the pasta but they looked delicious as well the salami and cheese station.

Loved the desserts! Crepes and different flavored ice cream were my favorite!

Best buffet I've been to but everything still was.... Like eating at a buffet. None of the food items had a prime restaurant quality feel so the price tag knocks off one star. Do yourself a favor and try their salmon and rack of lamb. Both were great

Bachhanal prides itself on being the largest buffet in Vegas with over 500 items.  However this is not another case of quantity over quality.  Located in Caesar's this place is an absolute must go for the die-hard buffet-ciando that's not afraid to spend a few bucks and a couple of hours pigging out.  

This buffet features items from places like American smokehouses, Italian pizzeria's, and New England crab shacks.   The must tries are the softshell crab tempura, the king crab claws, and the rock crab knuckles.  The seafood tastes remarkably fresh and sweet.  Also, for whatever reason, their pizza is amazing.  I almost felt guilty scarfing down pizza instead of  seafood...almost.

Then there's dessert.  Creme brulee, flan, cupcakes, gelatos, this place is heaven for those with a sweet tooth.

On the weekends this buffet serves brunch until 3 and then immediately switches over to the dinner menu.  I suggest getting there around 1:15 to be seated around 2.  That you you pay for a less expensive brunch price but have an hr to eat off of both menus.  Then you can sleep all afternoon to recover from your food coma

Having tried the M  , Rio , Paris and Wynn buffets just to name a few , Bacchanal Buffet is the best by a LARGE margin. We went here last September when it was still brand spanking new...so the lines were INSANE...But we were fortunate enough to know someone who not only let us go to the front of the line, but gave us all free buffet passes.

The wide selection alone makes it one of the best buffets ever, but the quality of the food really sets it apart.

From the carving stations, to the chinese food section, the italian food , dessert station and so on, the quality of the food will not leave you disappointed.

No wonder there was a 2 hour line outside

Will definitely comeback

Great place to catch Vegas style buffet. Fantastic fresh seafood from fresh oysters to crab legs and even Stone crab claws!  King crab legs are advertised but reality is they are the smallest king crab legs imaginable so it's like snow crab. But the snow crab are nice size so I'm not going to nitpick. Cold or warm snow crab you can't go wrong. There is a beer and wine drink package you can purchase for an additional 19.00. I didn't opt for that so my dinner was $60.00. Pricy yes but worth every dollar considering the quality of seafood. There was a huge dessert bar which had a crepe station. Good stuff

Big jump from before the renovation!  

AMBIENCE:

- Modern, new, chic, clean and elegant

FOOD:

- Selection comparable to Bellagio, M, and Wynn. 
- They baste your prime rib with oil and rosemary before serving preventing it from being dry.

PRICE:

- Comparable to big Las Vegas buffets.

Huge selection of fresh, tasty food. A decent meal of crab, sushi, shrimp, lamb, beef, etc. would easily cost this much per person anywhere in Vegas, and you wouldn't have the huge selection. The only down side was the desert bar. I find the desert bar at the Wicked Spoon to be more impressive.
Worst food I have experienced on my trip to Vegas. Our server never came to our table, the bus boy was nice about getting refills, for the price not worth it.
I have been here many times. Each day it's deferent. I like old Caesar's buffet the best.

Probably most popular ...     King crabs.  I don't eat that.  But everyone
 was.  Tomato mozzarella and nice salads and cole slaw.
Giant meatballs
Penne ala vodka
Sliders
Onion rings
Sushi and Mexican stations
Duck
Prime rib
Lamb chops
Corn
Shrimp cocktail
Loads of dessertsPizza.   Four diff kinds
Giant garlic knots

Sunday night was 48 an adult and 26 for my 8 yr old!!! Very good buffet but pricey

My favorite buffet in Vegas!! Hands down! Been to Wicked Spoon, and the Bellagio buffet, but this place tops it all. They had a little of everything I wanted! From all regions! They had tons of drinks and juices to choose from! Seafood, full taco bar, meat of every variety, so many kinds of fruit, pastas, Asian dishes, cheese plates, etc. The best part was dessert! They had a whole room dedicated to delicious desserts. Ice creams, boba, cakes, pies, cookies, fudge, chocolates, cotton candy, you name it, they had it. And they weren't only delicious, but beautifully decorated! 
*updated review: second time was on a weekend and less enjoyable. Obviously incredibly, and the food seemed to lack.

I went to lunch here and got a free pass from one of the guests.  Line was too long so he didn't make it.  We put our name down then got texted an hour or so later. Came back and thought we would get a table right away, but noooo..  Another line after we checked in. That line was almost an hour. We didn't pay attention at the beginning but it was halfway before we realized the line was a bit too long!  Food was just ok. Nothing interesting. Crab legs were small so I didn't bother. Other dishes were so so.

This buffet is epic! One of the top 10 in my list! You can find right about anything! I went for brunch and man it was the best! The staff is friendly and the vibe is wonderful! The dessert section is it a bit small but it's still great! Go here you won't regret it!

This was a solid buffet, but I was somewhat disappointed as I was expecting more based on the reviews. Frankly, I thought it was boring given the price range. Yes, there's variety, but the more boring kind of variety like fried rice, fries, porridge, etc that are simple and not particularly exciting. The prime rib was good. I did NOT like that the server dropped the prime rib on the counter in front of the glass when he was trying to place it on my plate and then tried to still give me the same piece!  Then he was annoyed when I said I didn't want that. They also had lamb chops (overcooked) and the standard Vegas buffet seafood options (crab legs, salmon etc). I did like that they had sushi.  I actually thought the dessert section was the most fun and interesting to pick from.  

All the pictures I saw on Yelp that made me want to try the buffet was usually from 4 years ago (things like pressed juices, lobster bisque, and others that would make this buffet more unique). My guess if this is what made it popular before but this time it definitely felt like effort was scaled down.  This was definitely good to try but I'm not sure I'd return unless they have more interesting food options!  Otherwise it feels like a fairly standard Vegas buffet.

Honestly worth every penny. King crab cracked open for you? Yes. Bottomless mimosa? Mm yes. Every type of cuisine was really well done. The attention to detail in the food was very apparent. Even the dessert was really good! (Really really good.)

By far the best buffet I've been to.  Better than M or Wynn.  It's going to cost you, as it's quite pricey at $44.99 if you are a total rewards member.  You would have to focus in on the good stuff, as there too many things to try.  Described are the best things:

Desserts - mochi ice cream, all kinds of flavors, green tea and mango are my favs.  vanilla bean creme brulee, sorbees - blood orange, watermelon mint, and mango chilli lime (that one is the best)

Seafood - hamachi sashimi, crab legs have no salt added, perfect, other sushi is pretty good quality.

Meats - beef brisket is da bomb intense smoke flavor and so tender, no sauce needed.  prime rib damn good, the best here is the roast duck, tastes like something out of a high end Chinese restaurant how did they do that, upon further inspection, saw real Chinese chefs cooking it... with ducks hanging and all!

Go early and weekday if possible, the lines do get long.  Highly recommended and way worth the money (or rewards points for all you gamblers out there)!

This buffet was AMAZING. I think I like it better than Wicked Spoon! We went there for lunch (3) and I was surprised they had a fresh seafood station. They had on ice, fresh oysters on a half shell, clams, mussels, and huge cocktail shrimp. That was the first place I went to! The cocktail sauce was amazing as well, I bet it had horse raddish in it or something because some of it was spicy, but it was really good. For their cooked seafood, they had a clam bake, baked halibut, rice with bell peppers, sausage, and clams... sooo good as well as others. I was very pleased with that station because the servers behind the station were ready and waiting to refill whatever as food got low! Not only did they have an awesome seafood station, they had lots of other foods: bbq, mexican, chinese, sushi, cheese, italian, and dessert! I sampled all the other food and it was pretty good, I was still just in love with the seafood station!

At the dessert station, they had different types of gelato that you don't normally see, I tasted each of them and they were all very good. They also had a crepe station with a few fresh fruit selections. The servers behind the dessert station were very nice and offering souffles (sp?) right out the over! I'm not a souffle person but that was pretty darn good. They also were caramelizing the crem brulees right there! They had milk chocolate and hazelnut - my brother got chocolate, he liked it and I got hazenut which was good. They had a chocolate cake that was awesome as well!

After eating we had coffee which had a great flavor. Our server was very kind and sweet to us. We asked for ketchup for waffle fries and when she couldn't find anyone, she got the manager to hunt it down for us.. wow! She was pretty good at taking our dishes and not leaving us with a table full of them!

All in all, it was a great experience, awesome to be one of first people to eat at the buffet! If you're going to Vegas, the Bacchanal Buffet is a definite must!!

HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE and MANAGEMENT SKILLS! I am an MBA and specialize in online marketing. They completely false advertise their prices on their website and on Yelp. When you confront them, they state that they are not the ones who post their menu and pricing info online- which is completely not true. They are rude to their customers and talk back to you when you confront them that they have the wrong pricing online. They false advertise and their manager Wolfe heisey is especially RUDE!!!!!!!!!!!! instead of being courteous and nicely responding to your concerns, he gives you a cocky attitude and treats you with disrespect. I am pregnant and should not be talked down to that way, very disgusting and not managerial behavior. Rather than being cocky, he should be courteous to any customer that approaches him. It was very disrespectful
And harassing. Completely deserves ZERO stars for their poor customer service and rude behavior.

tasty, but not awesome.
expensive, but not all that classy.
the waiter was excellent, but it's a buffet.
I'd suggest bringing a coupon and your appetite.

It does not suprise me that this is the number one buffet! The buffet goes on forever and the variety of cuisines is incredible. Where else can you get sushi, pizza, salad, sliders and amazing desserts all in one place? 
The kicker is: is all tastes incredible! Nothing is buffet quality or underwhelming! It tastes like they have mastered each dish as their specialty.
It is definitely pricey! Unless you are looking to spend some serious money in Vegas, this is not an every meal place! Nor is it included in the infamous  $50 24hrs buffet pass. It is worth trying once though! Come starving, leave so beyond satisfied!
Always fresh and amazing.  I come for the barbecue and can't resist the rest.  Great seafood with warm crab legs and fresh oysters.  I love the deserts.  The quality here can't be beat.

MEH I was disappointed after hearing about how great this place was, we got here around noon and there was a very short line but right after we got in line the line VERY quickly got extremely long so I guess we got lucky. $41 per person for lunch on a sunday for us.

a large variety of different types of food but each type had very basics, you get your Asian section with your typical stuff you would see at panda express and some special items like the pork bun and stuff, nothing amazing though.

Mexican section was good, they have a taco guy that makes u warm tacos, some beans, some salsa, some rice, and they have a small ice chest with special Mexican drinks so that was pretty cool

meat selection was pretty good, and the meat server guy was really nice, the prime rib was TOP NOTCH, definitely the best item at the buffet for sure, it was very soft and tender, melted in my mouth, done right! 

seafood section was mostly cold stuff, I didn't really get much from there at all

then there were some chicken and waffles, eggs, breakfast items, pizza and omlettes 

dessert section looked nice, mostly cakes, pies, ice cream, crepes but nothing was amazing to me, my favorite was probably the oreo moose cake which was pretty good!

glad I gave this place a shot after hearing all about it but I would probably try another buffet next time, don't get me wrong this is definitely one of the better buffets but just not as amazing as everyone makes it sound.
DELICIOUS! Totally worth it. Make sure you get everything!!! There's an area towards the back that everyone seems to miss. Probably the best food we had in Vegas!

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS!!! breakfast is amazing. i seriously try to come and eat here every vegas trip now. the bananas foster is outta this world! if you want your bacon extra crispy, you can ask the chef's behind the counter and they will do it for you! i will say that none of the desserts are all that but they do have a variety of food that is better. most buffets you only like very few things. at this buffet, it's more than just the occasional 2 things. the service here is great and they really do try to accomodate your seating arrangements. im really picky where i want to be seated and i had them running all over the place to find me a spot. make an effort to come here for breakfast!

Bacchanal has to be my favorite of all the so-called modern Vegas buffets. I prefer it over Wicked Spoon and the Wynn's Sunday champagne brunch. Everything from the eggs benny to their version of fried chicken & waffles served in a clever waffle cone with waffle fries was tasty. I really liked that. The roasted potatoes were tasty. So was the hand carved ham and kielbasa. The butcher cutting them had a great attitude. He livened up the brunch crowd with his humor and enthusiasm for sure. The bite sized churros I really dug and the slices of bacon were perfect... That was just my first plate. My 2nd plate all seafood everything. Yumm. I had snow crab, king crab legs, stone crab claws and shrimp. All that with lemon and cocktail sauce and I was golden. So good. So fresh and tasty... My next plate was all dessert. That's all I had room for. I couldnt fit any of their great looking sushi, any of the many soups, countless fruit and salad options. It was so much food. I never even made it to the pasta & pizza section. Unreal. So many great choices... My dessert plate was packed with macarons, almond cookies, double chocolate cookies, green tea cookies, pecan tarts and the classic chocolate chip cookie. They were all pretty good for the most part. I had a bite of someone's flan. It was good. The strawberry shortcake was also real good. 

Service was excellent. We opted for the champagne brunch for our party of 8. You have an option for peach bellinis too. And pretty much any fruit puree/nectar of your choosing. 

I highly recommend the Bacchanal buffet. I'm really not much for buffets unless it is for a special occasion and theyre spread is perfect for such events. So much to choose from that you wouldnt believe it. You have to experience it for yourself. 5 stars. easy.

Big disappointment. Arrived on Monday night. Estimated wait time was 92 minutes. Paid an extra $35 to avoid the wait. So $400 for a party of 4. Then we get into an endless line to get the meat (prime rib, lamb chops, chicken.). Then the sea food line. Twenty minutes to get ice cold shrimp, snow crab (no king crab or lobster on this buffet), and clams. I was so disappointed when we got back to the table, I decided to get some more of the tough prime rib again. However, the meat line was so long I gave up. This buffet is all about getting people in, but, not being able to handle the crowd. My advice is --Avoid this buffet at all costs.

We went there on Wednesday night at 6pm.  The line has already built up but couldn't believe waited 3 hours to get to the cashier.  After paid, still needed to wait another 20mins to be seated. 
Unbelievable.

Once inside the lines continued.  You had to wait in a 30 minute line for the meat section.  By the time we got back to the table and eat, the food was cold!  The seafood line was even worst.  The line was hold up because people were waiting for the staff to open the oysters from the shells.  Horrible experience!  End up eating salad and pizza for a $50 buffet!!!

 I would definitely NOT come back!!!

We tried this for the first time after having the Wynn buffet the previous night.  What a difference.  The quality and choices are far more superior.  Like many have said and recommended, this is the best buffet in Vegas right now.

They even have a ticket system that allows you to not have to wait in a Disneyland line for hours.  Genius.  

Tip: their "dinner" prices start at 3pm so if you get in around 2:30 you will only have to pay the lunch price and get extra dinner items after it starts, all while saving $10 per person.

Bacchanal Buffet is hands down a must visit place when you visit Vegas. After a drunken stupor night of clubbing and when you get told that you danced with a troll or troglodyte, this is your sanctuary. I am assuming the name Bacchanal is a tribute to Bacchus, the Roman name for Dionysus, the god of wine and intoxication. So by deduction, I think the place means you need to drunk off of food.

--WHAT SHOULD I ORDER--

1) With literally every type of patron, there is something for you. For example, the first part of the place hosts a seafood delicacy. It has crab legs, shrimp, salmon etc.

2) Its got a meat (beef, pork, chicken, turkey) carving station to satisfy that man meat you been missing out on if that's what you fancy.

3) Its got Sushi, Chinese food, hell its even got a taco making station.

4) The dessert bar is separate and it even has a whole island to itself.

5) Wear comfy clothes.

--HOW IS THE SERVICE--

Its Vegas, so you get top service at this buffet. There are endless mimosas before dinner is served. 

--WHAT IS THE PRICE--

Expect each person to pay about ~$60 at the end of the bill. 

Source: Came here after raging night in Vegas and I go back ever since.

$55 a person for an insane variety of food is pretty good. You go through a queue to pay for your admission to this paradise. The have lamb chops, different cuts of steak, pork, tacos, crab legs, oysters, truffle gnocchi, poke, etc. Their dessert selection was on fleek. Literally every kind of cake you can imagine, they have. They have macaroons, gelato, bark, etc. Service is quick and they almost always clear your plate before you come back with your next mountain of food. With that being said, two stars are missing because of the overall quality of the food. I have had amazing oysters, amazing steak, amazing crab legs, etc. I can confidently say that the food here does not come close to the quality of the food in those other institutions. I get it, one place can't be a master of every single dish. Was the food here bad? Not at all, I thoroughly enjoyed my meal. However at $55 a person, I hope that they can refine the little things to improve the food such as not overcooking the lamb chops.
Will be back, but definitely with a coupon.

We came here for Sunday brunch. We arrived at about 10 a.m. and the line was fairly short. It was my first Las Vegas strip buffet experience and I was impressed. Holy choices! I am a person who loves choices, and am also what the psychology text books call a "maximizer" so at first I was overwhelmed by such an urge to try all the foodz, I didn't even know where to start. I finally made a game plan and managed to check out a decent selection of different items without feeling like I missed something important. I do feel like I'd need to go back at least two more times to experience it all though. My husband, on the other hand, is a person who doesn't appreciate extra big a$* buffets, so he was overwhelmed by the options in a bad way. It's wise to evaluate your food personality when deciding whether to come here or a different buffet with less options but equally good food on the Strip (ex. Wicked Spoon). 

 I loved the dim sum, fresh juice selection, lobster Benedict, posole, and sweet breakfast items (bananas foster something or other, red velvet pancakes, etc). 

Things that didn't impress me so much are below:
1. The service - I almost considered a 3 star review because of our waiter. He treated us like an inconvenience and was clearly annoyed we had a young child with us, even though she was well behaved and there were many other kids there (and I'm not a parent who suffers from Special Snowflake Syndrome... I can acknowledge when my toddler acts like a monster and we tip accordingly).
2. Prior to my visit, I'd read in reviews that Bacchanal appears to be doing things to cut costs. I agree. More expensive food items were often slow to be replenished. Overall, the rate at which items were put out kind was kind of sluggish, but it was really obvious with things like the lobster benedict. 
3. The queue system was slightly annoying. They line you up in a big group and take you all to tables the same section. I understand why they do this, but it makes it feel sort of extra hog trough like. Despite having a small child with us, they sat us about 12" from a childless couple who was clearly trying to enjoy each other without distractions. I said my child behaved well, but I still understand and respect the desire of childless diners to dine more than a foot away from a table with a kid. 
4. The price felt a bit over-inflated, especially with the obvious efforts to cut costs. 
5. The desert station was very disappointing. The items looked delicious, but failed to deliver in taste and texture. 

One thing to note is that (as a maximizer) it was hard for me to decide whether to visit Bacchanal for Sunday brunch, or weekend dinner in order to get the best impression and selection of food. As far as I can tell from what I've seen in dinner reviews, and the items that were available at brunch when we went, most items that are available at dinner, were also present at brunch. I also enjoyed having the added option for breakfast food items. I was happy that we went for Sunday brunch. It also came with unlimited mimosas. One gripe was that even though I'm pregnant and can't drink, I didn't get a price reduction (I know, I'm cheap).

Overall, I'll be back, but only on a special occasion. It's a fun experience, but not one I need to do often. We've since tried the Wicked Spoon in the Cosmopolitan, and though I personally liked the food and choices a tad bit better at Bacchanal, the lower price and better service at the Wicked Spoon make us much more likely to return there first. For a more detailed comparison, see my review of the Wicked Spoon.
Not worth it. The flavor is bland and there was not too many choices. There was NO good Vegetarian options. It was just generic buffet food that is over-priced.

One of the best brunch buffets my husband and I have been to. We had a Groupon too!! #win 

We saw different types of individual foods/desserts, that no where else has. (See photos) Some were cute! Of course, I didn't have time to take photos of all, but I guarantee this is the place to go to for brunch next time you visit, not just because the food was cute, but of course it was delicious! It was nice that the waitress was helpful too. 

The buffet space is quite big, because when you turn a corner, there's some other type of food. I was getting lost. LOL

You just have to try this place for yourself. Enjoy :)

This place is like heaves!!!!! The line was long and too expensive but OMG every plate was amazing!!! One of the best meals I ever had in my life. The beef sections was my fav. Also unlimited drinks! I totally recommend this place!!

Mid high price.  Foods is ok. Oysters is not fresh. The only thing I enjoyed is the crepe. Because the person who serving the crepe is friendly.  Long wait and long line just for prime ribs. Peoples dont know where is the line start from. No one is guiding . The environment that we sat is terrible. I know is busy. But this is cesar palace. You should have the top team management.

Pricey but has some nice variety and a great way to try dishes you might otherwise not order.  Ate there twice during my stay at Ceasar's Palace, for lunch and dinner.  Dinner definitely had a better and more impressive menu.  Some highlights for me were some type of creamy escargot soup, a dish featuring bone marrow, and the various carved meats offered.  And the desserts are pretty good as well. Tried some interesting items such as lemon basil gelato. If you aren't a very adventurous eater there are lots of more traditional buffet items offered, but with nice twists.  You should at least try this buffet as it seems to get top reviews and is probably the best buffet I have eaten at. Realize though, most non buffet restaurants with a similar price point will offer better quality. However you get a lot of value in the variety offered.

On the downside...holy cow the line is long.  Lunch wait was about an hour. And even with kiosk checkin around 7pm, the wait was 80 minutes until they text you to jump in line. And then the wait was at least another hour!  All in all probably a 2.5hr wait from check in to seating.  And then the price.  Really expensive for a buffet but it's at least worth a try.

It's the second time I tried this place. Just saying: don't think it's the best buffet in Las Vegas!

The average wait for 3+ people group need to wait about one and half hour to be seated (for Sunday noon). However, when get enter it, we saw so many empty tables (except for those people go get food) and they are just not cleaned yet, which on the other hand shows how much they lack of nice operating management. 

The food quality, I gotta say, is quite unstable. the food I liked last time wasn't good this time. Tomato soup, smoked pork belly and tuna salad are recommended, but not sure whether they would be good next time. Many dishes are too salty, which makes us realize that we are still young with a sensitive tongue. Desserts are always the scoring point and they are doing fine. Recommend the Thai tea float, which is creative and tasty.

Great googly moogly do I love this buffet. As a Vegas local I like to treat myself to a meal here several times a year. It's super expensive (over $100 for 2) so make sure you are super hungry before you get here. 

I have noticed a decline in the offerings over the years: no more freshly carved ribeye, no more crab claws, no more delicate Italian pasta dishes, and green vegetables have been phased out with more cheap carby sides like corn and potatoes -- but it's still a great buffet with great quality food. The dessert station is a thing of beauty. You can try mochi, homemade ice cream, crepes, chocolate dipped strawberries, cheesecake pops and more. Oh nom nom nom. This is THE place I go when I want to blow my low carb eating plan. On my most recent visit I ate 3 baskets of the sweet potato tater tots all by myself.

Be prepared to wait in a long line. Try to go at "off" times if you don't want to stand around forever. And Pepsi fans rejoice: no Coke products served here!

I think this is the new favorite spot in Vegas. Service was amazing. The moment we were seated, the hostess tended to us immediately. Great atmosphere and fantastic selection. Definitely starting to favor this over the wicked spoon. 

Highlights:
The server went to grab fresh orange juice for me because mines was empty directly from the buffet line!

I think I am just a biased person about buffets, but I really didnt find this one any different then others. I do say they have good food, but nothing jumped out and said, "Hey! I am new. Eat me!". hahaha, just saying. 

I hate where the plates are and I also thing the glass is too low that it was hard to scoop the things out without spilling them. 

I waited in line for an hour and  I just didnt feel impressed. Not for that price and that wait. 

But I know a lot of people like it. I just dont think for me that it is worth the money.

This place has some of the best buffet food you can realistically ask for. This place has everything, sushi, nigiri, authentic chinese (roast duck etc) made by chinese chefs and they speak mandarin, authentic mexican, snow crab legs (no king crab), oysters, tons of meat (bbq veal, 4 types of sausages, prime rib, etc), salmon, to die for sliders, cheeses and breads, very good looking pasta but I didnt try it, and the best dessert bar you could possibly imagine; to name a few: mochi ice cream 5 different flavors, crepes, tiramisu, key lime, cheesecake, macaroons, creme brulee, and a ton of other things. It has the largest selection of desserts I have ever seen and I have been to a fair share of buffets.

Decor of this place is also stunning, and lots of room for giant parties.

My boyfriend took me here for my birthday breakfast and wow, there's a reason why this is one of the best buffets in Vegas! There was so much to choose from and everything was so good! My only wish was that I had a second stomach, so I could try everything. The big standouts for me were the steak & egg combos, the Asian line, the carved meats, and the dessert area.

I would probably give this place 3 1/2 stars if I could. We came on a Tuesday night for dinner. We arrived at 5:30 pm and there was already a long wait. We didn't get seated until about 7:30pm. So if you are hungry, just be ready to WAIT. According to the cashier, there are approximately 250 plus food choices. My favorite was the seafood - crab legs, oysters, shrimp! All yummy!!! I think I may prefer Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo though.....forgot to mention, be prepared to shell out some $$$$ for your meal!

If this had been the first buffet we had ever tried in Vegas I would've thought it was the best thing ever. However it was not the first buffet we had been to and compared to the others we had been to it was no different than them. Their was nothing on this buffet that was good enough for me to be able to justify spending 60 dollars/person. They have crab legs and so does every other buffet at dinner in Vegas. They make crepes for you at the desert station and so does the Paris buffet. They have sushi but other than the sashimi it was gross. Our waitress was not very attentive and while I don't expect much from them anyway at a buffet she was even less attentive than expected. The Mac and cheese tasted like it was from stoufers and not fresh. Compared to other buffets it IS good don't get me wrong, but it not what it's hyped up to be and not worth the price. I would've rather spent that money at a nicer restaurant.

The best buffet in town!  Though the price and the line may give you pause, I've found the food to be delicious, with such variety to justify the wait and cost.  Definitely a must-visit for the full Vegas experience.

My expectations were very high for this buffet! Especially for being $55 per person and a very long wait line. We were seated after about 20 mins and taken to the back of the buffet. I noticed my chair was dirty but the tablet was clean. The tone of the restaurant was very nice and relaxing. The buffet has MANY options that most don't have. This one even includes crab legs which was very happy about. As I started testing a lot of food I noticed more than half of it was cold :( or lacked flavor. That was  disappointing. For dessert we had gelato, macaroons, flan, chocolate covered strawberries.. all very good. I think they can definitely work on the temperature of the food and also the temperature of the restaurant was WAY too cold.

For lunch: Wicked Spoon is better Bacchanal. 

My gf and I came here for lunch. $33/person, about 1.5 hour wait and we got there at 11:30am. There is a line to get a ticket, which tells you when to come back to pay and get a seat. There was an option to enter if it was a special occasion. It was my gf's birthday, so I checked the box marked "birthday" and wondered what special thing would happen. Spoiler: nothing happened throughout our time there, and no one acknowledged it. Why put an option to mark if it's someone's birthday if absolutely nothing will happen when you check it? Anyway, when we got back at our designated time, we had to wait about 20 minutes in a line to pay. The group in front of us was supposed to come back 2 hours later (they had just gotten their ticket), but the hostess and cashier didn't care and let them pay and enter anyway, while the rest of us honest folk waited to return at our designated time. At the time of payment, I had to put a tip. This is weird to me, because I like to adjust my tip based on the service provided by the server. The cashier then pointed out to me that this tip would go to my server. Okay, how do they know who my server is when we don't even have our seat yet? 

It was then another 10 minutes after we paid before we were taken to our seat. I put the receipt - with the tip labeled on it - down on the table and after our server asks for what drinks we want she picks up the receipt and looks at it in detail. I don't know why she did this. Like any person would, I am sure she saw the tip I had left. And like any person would do, she probably decided in her mind to give us a certain level of service based on the tip that was preemptively given. Overall, the service by her, the cashier, and the host were poor, but the man bussing our table was significantly more friendly, and brought us ketchup and refilled our drinks for us, and we saw him more than we saw our server.  

Highlights and lowlights of some of the food:
Maple-syrup tater tots - very good!
Filet mignon - delicious, made me eat all of it even though I was stuffed
Fried chicken - it was very dry. KFC has better fried chicken
Made-on-the-spot carnitas tacos - bland, not exciting
Labels were inconsistent. Some foods had labels, others did not. The salsa bar had no labels.
Sausages - average
The Chinese food - my gf said they did this section well
Desserts - underwhelming. The best I had was the flan. The "thai" gelato tasted like vanilla. There was no honey display.
Overall the presentation of the food was sub-par. If you have been to Wicked Spoon, you will understand the difference in the food presentation.

I think this place is overrated. Wicked Spoon has a much better lunch buffet, better service, is cheaper, and has a similar ambiance. I would recommend you go to Wicked Spoon than Bacchanal.

Not worth the hype. Better value and excellent food quality can be found @ The Wynn buffet (our fave), The M (offstrip and a great value), Mandalay Bay buffet are better choices/value.  We are buffet goers - and  we love a good buffet.  At this price point - they need to improve.  This is not great and here's why;.  We had high hopes for this considering all the buzz- But they need a traffic cop on this buffet line.  Food quality is good (shrimp, crab legs) -- But the logistics are a mess!  Tables are too close - and the overall layout makes folks step on top of each other to get to the food offerings.  We gave up trying!   The carving section (meats/etc.) - is directly in line with folks entering and exiting. The carving station line is also in front of other selections which we couldn't get to either - Frustrating! (this was during the week approx 5 pm) - It wasn't even that crowded.  The Asian fare was tasty, Italian needed more varied pasta - the desserts were good. But all in all - the selections are weaker than other top properties here in LV.   Some  selections were just dumped in pots and not labeled.   In fact, some of the off strip buffets have more and varied side dishes, veggies and desserts.  Additionally, the service is not nearly as attentive as in other properties both on strip and the local casinos.  At this price point - they need to step it up and fine tune it; better service, better variety and better access to the food itself.  Too much of an obstacle course and hassle.   Wanted to really love it -- not running back.  Overpriced and underwhelmed.

Food poisoning at its best!!!  This was the only place i ate at on jan 7th as i flew in that day.. I woke up n the middle of the night in my hotel violently vomiting. Totally put a damper on my vacation. 24hrs later & i couldnt even keep soup down. Went to a phenomenal show & was on the edge of my seat for it to end due to sickness. I have chills, no appetite, & constant cramping. I called & spoke to management & was told they had to do an "investigation". I will be following up on this bc miserable doesnt even describe how i feel.

Went here last year during lunch time, spent about $70-80 for 2 adults. The food is good, my favorite was the polenta with Parmesan cheese and sautéed mushroom. I was sad when I got too full to taste anything else. Try this place out when you have the time, money and taste for adventure cause there is simply too much to taste. Don't waste stomach space with fillers like bread, go straight for the items you wouldn't normally have. That's my game plan for the next time at least.

In terms of quantity, Bacchanal Buffet is No. 1 in Vegas. In terms of price, 
service and maybe even quality, it's No.2. 

I'm gonna skip a lot of food details because there are tons of new reviews every 
day about this place. The Mexican section and the meats were my favorites but 
they have almost everything you can think of. I'll just say this: You cannot 
possibly eat it all. And what you do eat is of quality taste and preparation. 
But it's impossible to "get your money's worth" and any time spent waiting in a 
line for this is time wasted. I think the only way I'd go back is if it wasn't 
my choice, which is to say if friends of mine wanted to go, I would join them. 

Do not mistake this for a bad review -- the place is expensive but tasty. It's 
just not my favorite. Wanna know what is?

The food was excellent and worth the price and time you stand in line. Thankfully it was only a 10 minute wait in line to be seated. Our server was a really nice women and really made us feel welcomed and not like we are just at a buffet. 

I highly recommend the Clam Chowder - Ribs - mashed Potatoes - beans- Crab Legs - The Asian area everything was great!  - ALL desserts !

I promised long time ago to my little sister that I would take her to the best buffet in Vegas and give her an unforgettable birthday. We took her out for the circus at 2:30pm and got out at 3:45. None of us ate breakfast, because we wanted to eat in the buffet. After arrived at bacchanal，we waited in line for half an hour. Then, there was a staff suddenly showed up saying that we have to sign in before getting in the line. We didn't complain, thought she could have let everyone know that you have to get a little ticket before entering the waiting line. We did as what she told. The system shows that we have to wait till 8:50 to get into a table. Thought it was a five hour wait, we decided to go back to hotel and come back for it. After all, it was my little sister's birthday. And we want to make it special. We came back at 8:30, then informed by the manager that they were closed for the night. The waiting time was not a guarantee. Even if we could get a table at 9:30, all the food station will be shut down at 10. He especially mentioned that I should know better because tonight was suppose to be busy. What a professional thing to say! As a manger, you should know better than I do. If you expected so many people wouldn't be able to get a table, why giving out the waiting estimation first place. Or, you could at least try to inform the guest through the phone, before letting them starving for five hours! Don't blame it on the computer system. It was your problem to fix rather than the costumers'. Even worse, the male manager walked away arrogantly without even trying to apologize. This hotel should train their staffs how to treat the costumer with respect, before letting them become to the manager.  Thank u for giving my family the most memorable Las Vegas night! Never coming back!

I don't know that I've ever given any buffet 5 stars but this one is a solid 4. They all seem to be similar to me. We came for brunch during the week at $43.99 pp which also included unlimited Mimosas. Soooo I did fill up on those and our wait staff kept them coming and was ready with pitcher in hand each time our flutes ran low. Love That! I enjoyed the large plump shrimp as well as the dim sum and gelato. The lemon basil gelato was so light and refreshing !!! You must try it. 

They had a huge selection of items I never bothered to try and I mostly went for the seafood and Asian selection. However the rest of the family raved about the pork belly, Mac n cheese, crab claws and prime rib.

I could live the rest of my life without eating at another buffet but if I'm getting dragged to one you bet I'll vote for the one with the Bottomless Mimosas and rockin gelato!

My family and I ate at the new buffet last Friday, and I had to spread the word about the incredible expericne we had.  The four of us came got to the front by around 2 after waiting in line for about thirty minutes, watching the people working on what turned out to be the seafood station killed the time !   Once we got in, everything was great.

1.  The ambiance is great, all the people preparing the food really seem to love their jobs and the food their serving.
2.  The variety is amazing, we manages to catch lunch and dinner, everything we were able to try before becoming sickly full was ridiculously good.  Some highlights for us were the Mexican station, the "carving station" and all the delicious meats, and last but not least the seafood station which we waited for last was amazing,  They had a lobster corn chowder that was so good, cocktail shrimp cooked properly and very fresh, they even had ceviche!! 

Out of all the  buffets in vegas, BACCHANAL is by far the best , we all agreed, no one will come close !  After reading all the other reviews on here, and eating there, i really dont understand the complaints.. Caesars buffet stands high over Wicked spoon, the bellagio, planet hollywood, m, eveyone else..

My boyfriend and I both had high expectations for this buffet, but we left feeling disappointed. We came on a thursday and it was $54.99/person. While there was a very wide variety of food selections, the quality and taste of the food were mediocre. 

Cons:
Seafood section was not fresh at all. Crab legs tasted like they have been in the fridge for a very long time and the flavor was gone. Stone crab was COMPLETELY tasteless. Oysters were fishy and not sweet and creamy at all. Fish was completely overdone. Clams had sand and mussels were fishy. The entire seafood section which we were very looking forward to, was a complete fail. 

Hint: If you are looking for more flavorful crab legs, head on back to the Italian section, where they steam the crab legs and serve an abundance amount to your plate. These crab legs had so much more flavor than the cold ones at the seafood station. My bf and I both redeemed a little bit of happiness from these crab legs.

Pros:
Meat section and the soups. I really enjoyed their lamb chops and beef ribs here. The beef rib was one of the highlights of our meal. It was fresh off the grill, crunchy, and sooo flavorful. The lamb chops were a bit overcooked, but flavorful. The prime rib was good and the sausages were good as well. One of my favorites of the buffet was actually the truffle mushroom soup. The mushroom and truffle flavors were strong and the soup was creamy. Delicious. 

Overall, everything else was just mediocre and not memorable. The sushi section was almost non-existent. If you are looking to get sashimi, this ain't the place for you. Bacchanal is more focused on the large variety of food selection, but totally lacking in taste. We most likely won't come back to this buffet. For $54.99 which is more expensive than other Vegas buffets, we expected a lot better seafood quality!

Tried three buffets in Vegas. This was the best of three by far. The other two were at Wynn and balleys. 

Pros: 
Great variety of good food. 
Very nice ambiance.
Great staff. 
Quality preparation. 
All food is very accessible. 
Lots of meats. 

Cons. 
Price
Food was good decor very nice not your typical buffet!

A lot of selections but can be a hit or miss with the food. Good thing there's a lot of food to select from like seafood, italian, chinese, japanese, desserts, soup, steak, mexican, ramen, etc. I rather score them a 3.5 but there's no option for that. I guess i recommend it for first timers, tourists or for special occasion. The price is reasonable if you eat a lot. Don't bother if you're on a diet. Better take advantage of the money you spent and make this your 1st and last meal of the day because you'll be full. Enjoy the food non-stop for 2 hours! Hahaha

We are always in Vegas and decided to try the new buffet at Ceaser's. We were very disappointed. We were very happy upon arrival to see how large the buffet was, and yes they had a large selection of food. The biggest annoyance of this place was that only about 30% of the food was labeled. I have food issues so I need to know what I'm about to eat. I can't imagine I'm the only one that wants to know what kind of food they are about to consume. Of what I tried that was labeled, most of it was good. I had lobster benedict which was very tasty. My boyfriend had crab benedict and watermelon juice which he enjoyed. The pancakes however were crispy and the shrimp iny shrimp and grits was very mealy and tough. All in all I would not return simply because I like to know what I'm eating. I'll stick to Wicked Spoon down at Cosmo.

The best ever!!!!!! Honestly don't think I'll ever eat at another any other buffet ever again. I had the pizza, Chinese food, and OMG try the pozole and street tacos! Man, they're really really good! Oh and the deserts, they were so good! Creme Brûlée was so delicious!!! Definitely coming back to this place, not disappointed what so ever. It was a lil pricy but than again it is Vegas and u don't eat this everyday. Highly recommended...

This by far has been the best buffet I've been to! I've heard good things from friends about this place and they're absolutely right, this place is worth the price! It is pricey BUT if you take your time and utilize your two hour max to eat, then it's really worth it! They have a huge variety of food to choose from, American, Chinese, Seafood, Italian, Vietnamese, etc. So many different sections to choose from such as...

-A meat section
-A cheese section
-street taco station
-Ramen and Pho bowl station
-Crepe station 

This is just a few sections of the buffet, by you have to try almost everything because the choices are just endless! I especially like the fresh juice options (mango, guava, etc) they have near the street taco section. The service was just as great as the food as well. If you're hungry in Vegas and want to indulge in good food for two hours, this one is definitely recommended for your hungry needs!

This buffet is never ending!!! It's so big you could get lost! There's so many options and didn't things to eat. The tacos were my favorite thing to eat. They had a little but if everything. I'm going back next time I'm there.

A must go to buffet in Las Vegas! I would say the top two is Wicked Spoons and Bacchanal. Carnival World Buffet is not bad either and I would say it ranks #3. Unfortunately Bacchanal is not part of the 24hr all you can eat deal. 

Prepare to wait at least 1.5 hrs in line. The line may look intimating then it really is. Even though it looks endless it goes by fast. I guarantee it is worth the wait! Yelpers read on...

There is a lot of variety inside. From what I can remember there was Chinese, Mexican, Seafood (lots of seafood), Italian, American, Japanese, and something else I can't remember.

The dessert bar is awesome! They offer ice cream, gelato, and waffle cones!

The service was spectacular. Never had to wait long for a refill. There's even a juice bar at the buffet line. 

The dining area is huge! Plenty of space for everybody. Don't worry about being cramped. Way better designed compared to the other crappy buffet they have inside Caesar's. 

This buffet may be pricey but it's worth your money! A must try for every Vegas visitor.

I asked many people and most of them said Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas. 
I disagree after trying it.

PROS:
*Arrived on a Saturday before 5pm and we waited only 20 minutes. (Great)
*Server was nice and accommodating
*King Crab Legs & Oysters
*Variety of desserts

CONS:
*We paid about $58.00 each person and do I think that it was worth $58? (Nope)
I'd personally rather eat at the Rio Buffet. It was much more memorable and cheaper when I ate there 4 years ago. Bacchanal was not up to par with what I was expecting.

So for those who are wondering if Bacchanal tops Bellagio's, The Buffet at Wynn, or Wicked Spoon, the answer is a resounding YES.

It is pricey, sure, but for the quality of food you're getting I think it's very well worth it. 

The lamb chops here are phenomenal. Perfectly spiced. 
The prime rib is awesome. 
The seafood is top notch. Sweet king crab and great oysters. Fresh shrimps! 
The freshly-squeezed juices. Omgosh. Really memorable. Probably the best orange/melon juice I had. 
The runner ups: seafood paella, korean short ribs, veal, shu mai, artisan pizzas, shrimp & grits, meat & cheese stations ...

But for me their dessert  wins it all. Yummy crepes, cakes, & macarons. Truly unique ice cream flavors like watermelon & mint, chili lime & jalapeno, baklava, & aztec chocolate. 

We've been here twice (before 11 am & 5 pm respectively) and we never had to wait for more than 10 minutes. No lines! If you're planning to experience at least one buffet in LV, this is it!

Yum if you like buttery selections (eg. Broccoli , mac'n'cheese, mashed potatoes).  They do have a nice selection of Asian foods.  We went for lunch.  The dude cutting the meats have a positive attidude and makes the experience more enjoyable .  Though the price is a little high $41.99 for weekend brunch, but definitely worth a try.  You can save a whole buck if you are a current Caesar card holder, woot.

Probably the best buffet in Vegas! Huge shrimp, great prime rib, the street tacos are amazing! Not to mention the endless dessert options and made to order crepes. The service is excellent and always friendly. I would highly recommend paying the slightly higher price for this buffet and eating here if want an excellent meal. You will definitely get your money's worth and will not leave disappointed.
doesn't take military vouchers shame on caesars entertainment!!!!! i will never recommend any of your properties for anything!!!

The food is completely disgusting...everything we tried was inedible.  I would rather get food at a gas station. For $54 you can get a much better meal in Vegas and not have to stand in a line for an hour. One of the worst food experiences I've ever had.

I've been to this buffet several times. It was my favorite LV buffet until this last time I went (which was in January 2016). 

Everything tasted old and just bad..! All the seafood was not fresh (to the point that I didn't even try the oysters -- didn't think it'd be safe). The crab legs were dry and the meat was completely tasteless. 

After a highly highly disappointing dining experience, my friends and I just decided to load up on dessert to make up for the nasty food. To our disappointment, even the dessert was bad...! My husband tried the mini churro, and he couldn't even bite it off because it was so old and tough... 

Maybe it was just an "off" day, but I'm not going to risk wasting almost $150 (for two people).

as most of you may know, i go back home (to vegas) every month, sometimes 2x.  we mostly come here for sunday or saturday brunch/dinner. of the 7 times we've been here, we've only been disappointed once.

friends have told me the wait can be from 20 minutes to 2 hours. i'm not sure because i don't stand in that long line. there's a separate line for me, so i don't wait and i get seated right away!  those are the perks for gambling for total rewards. 

service is excellent. mimosas are always refilled and sometimes, the server will make it stronger for me. yay! plates are always taken away at a timely manner, water's constantly refilled, etc. no issues here.

i've found that the chinese, mexican and the italian sections are always consistent. carving station's a hit or miss.  their brisket and prime rib meats are yummy. seafood section - crab legs are just ok here (you can get them steamed). ceviche is good, though. 

their chicken and waffles were tasteless and dry, croque madame was nasty (i suggest you eat the real thing at Hatfield's), and sushi is no good.

favorites: chinese chow mein (i know, i know... but it's so good!!), miso soup, youtiao + rice congee, tacos, dimsum, mango juice, tater tots, and truffle potato gratin!

not a huge fan of their desserts... but i loooooooove their yummy donuts!!! OMG. I'm dreaming about that cinnamon donut right now. -_-

*books trip to vegas*.....
Every time we go to Vegas, we have to go to this buffet! It's the bomb! I like all the food here including the dessert area!! The workers are nice and professional also! It's highly recommended!! :)
Very delicious. A big selection. It is one of the best buffets I have been to. Everything was delicious. A little pricey but definitely worth it. Lunch buffet is significantly lower in price.

Hands down the best buffet I've ever been to. Food was terrific. Fresh and oh so good. Honestly, you'd have to go probably 3 times to truly sample all of the cuisines they have represented here. I've been once and didn't even try the Mexican or Italian (save for one meatball which was fantastic) and barely touched the deserts.

It's the seafood and meat station that were the crowd faves, as the lines would show.  
Vegetarians, you might want to turn away for a minute...Crab legs, oysters on the half, big succulent shrimp, lamb chops, prime rib, gourmet sausages, brisket, chicken. Gastropub orgasms each and every one.

The small plate idea is great, keeps it more intimate, unlike the food troughs of the old days. Speaking of plate, here's the one downside in my opinion: The dinner plates are tucked away in a cutout area below the serving stations....bad idea!! You have to reach between peoples legs to get a plate...or wait patiently while the line recedes enough to get one unobstructed, but you might be there for a while waiting. Just seems like a bad design.
It is new and yes it's busy. Expect to wait for entrance. 
Other than that, muy benito! That's very good for my gringo friends. Cheers

4.5 stars! Did you know that according to the dictionary, bacchanal means an occasion of wild and drunken revelry? And at the Bacchanal buffet at Caesars, I can see that happening with its bottomless mimosas during weekend brunch! The servers keep refilling your glass if it even looks a quarter empty! 

This is a super nice buffet - lots of food stations and a nice modern interior. There was an Asian food station (with dim sum and sushi and a made-to-order noodle area), salad station, Italian station (with pizza and pasta), a cheese station, a meat station (where they cut prime rib or sausages for you), a Mexican food station (where they make you tacos to order and have chilled horchata in bottles) a seafood station (with crab legs), and the dessert station (where they scoop ice cream for you, make ice cream sammies and shave ice bowls for you). 

For the half hour I waited and the $45 (before tax and tip) that I paid, I was going to get my time and money's worth and more from this buffet. I ate SO much that I had to unbutton my pants (ADVICE: wear stretchy yoga pants when going to buffet) and my stomach was protruding so much that walking afterwards was quite difficult due to the imbalance of my body's weight distribution. Gigantic food baby. But I think it's safe to say I got my money's worth. 

There were definitely some delicious goodies at this Bacchanalia, but a few misses as well. The dim sum was yummy - they had a taro paste bun, shu mai, bbq pork bun, and shrimp har gow in those steamer baskets. The har gows were so good, I went back for seconds. They also had oxtail in a soup and duck and fried rice and chow fun noodles. The made to order noodle bar was cool - you could choose from four different noodle soups - pho, ramen, udon, and a fourth that I don't remember. You tell the lady what you want and in less than five minutes, she hands you a piping hot bowl of noodle soup. The sushi and sashimi not bad either - not a huge selection, but they had tuna and salmon sashimi, as well as spicy tuna rolls, which are my favorites. 

I love crab, so I had to try the crab legs. They actually slice the crab legs in half the long way for you, so that the meat is exposed and you don't have to crack it - you just scoop the meat out with your utensil of choice. I've never seen that before and it's really convenient. But...the crab legs were really cold. I prefer mine to be warm. When I went back up for my fourth round of food, then I saw a sign that said warm crab legs were available at the Italian station. And then my friend said that they could warm them up for you too. Doh! Oh well. Next time.  One of my favorite dishes was this miso glazed cod that came with a side of wasabi mashed potatoes. Yum. 

Some of the things I ate weren't worth the tummy space - the pad thai was no good. The fried chicken was too salty. There was this mushroom polenta thing that was too salty too. So some things were too salty. 

Dessert was a mixed bag. The shave ice that they make for you was just meh. The ice cream bar was cool - they scoop it for you or you can have them make you a ice cream sandwich. I tried the mango lime chili ice cream and that was just okay. They also had macarons, so we tried one of each flavor - pistachio was yummy! They had flan that was just ok, and the creme brulee was good. There was a sign that said they had green tea creme brulee but they never refilled it so we didn't get to try. Some of the cakes were yummy. 

Overall, the buffet was very very very good! The service was great - they cleared away our empty plates speedily. And they provide these little rubber gripper things for when you have to grab hot plates! So smart! They even accommodated my friend's special request to have a grapefruit mimosa. Food was mostly yummy. I would come back - but I want to try other buffets first! :D Come hungry!

OMG. MOUTH IS WATERING JUST THINKING OF THIS PLACE. MMMMM. SO! I actually don't know where to begin my review! ... Just like the buffet! I didn't know where to begin!! ...so I went right in the middle buffet & attacked!

1. Got all the pasta- Lobster pasta... Mmmm. It was spicy but so yummy!!
2. Dim Sum- YES! Best I've had!! Must try!
3. Noodles needed more flavor! DUCK IS AMAZING. Sushi is bomb! 
4. American station- PRIME RIB!!!! You better get 5 slices of prime rib! Cooked just right! Omg. & the lamb chop, my first time & it was tasty! But definitely a different experience for me. There was also this simple pork belly dish & it's mind blowing!
5. The paella is 5 stars!!!
6. You need to eat the oysters & crab legs. It's a must!!

The dessert table is its own little island... BEST TASTING DESSERTS AT A BUFFET HANDS DOWN! I mean, Thai iced tea boba float... Where else would you get that?! And the butterscotch macaroons... OMG! Amazing!!!!

Honestly, you must try this buffet!
Some tips:
-Put horchata in your coffee!
-If you don't like coconut, ask for vanilla gelato instead for the Thai iced tea boba float.
-Sunday dinner starts at 3pm & it's $60/person
-pizza, tacos & potato salad you can do without. Get your monies worth!!! Prime ribs, dim sum, oysters, crab legs & sushi!! YES PLEASE!
-lessen your carb intake to make more room for the protein & SUGAR!

I have to come back for more prime rib & try the crepe bar. Mmmmmmm

The desserts... Deliciouuuusssss. And I am very particular about desserts. I don't like huge portions and sugar saturated foods.

All the desserts I had here were flavorful and not too sweet. They were perfect. I devoured everything I got (see pix). Went to "The Buffet" at Wynn the next day; they are supposed to be known for sweets. It did not compare to what I had here.  

I thought the crab here was not as good as Wynn's but my friend liked it better. They come out warm. My other friend said the oysters were better here. My friends liked the seafood. 

Other foods I liked: Lamb, corn, mashed potatoes. Friends liked their seafood and apparently they use really expensive meat in their sliders

Drink: tea drinks were really good. not too sweet

Servers- Excellent. Came around frequently taking away our plates and filling our drinks. Was there on a Friday around 530pm

The reason for minus 1 star- The price. 

They had a wide variety of food. I think it was worth it.

Food was delicious.  Had a little something for everyone.  Desserts were the best - love loved the banana bread pudding.  

Only negative was service.  We had two rounds at the buffet before we even saw a waitress to get a drink.  Ordered just soft drinks and water, so we were pretty low maintenance.  She was very nice, but seemed a little overwhelmed.  We did ask the hostess three times and then a manager before someone decided we were worth helping.  Very disappointing as we are Platinum Total Rewards members.

On my recent trip to Vegas, the family and I decided to head over to Bacchanal before going to Red Rock Canyon for breakfast. We went at 9:30AM on a Sunday and just as I had predicted, there were no lines. $50.00 per person and since it was my second time going to Bacchanal, I was over it. 

Bacchanal is a whole smorgasbord of dishes you can find anywhere in this world. It was breakfast but they were serving wings, crab legs and more! They have a lot of comfort food and Bacchanal just adds a little more spizazz to it. Your normal fries gets the extra parmesan and truffle on top. Your regular chicken wings have a buffalo with blue cheese and I-forgot-which-herb on it. I'm guessing you get the point now.

The extra touches that they add to completely "normal" food makes it worth your while though. I personally loved their fries (yes, I had fries at 9 in the morning. Don't judge me) and dimsum section. Along with that, I can't really complain about having to pay $50.00 either, their selection is vast and the majority are absolutely tasty.

We left at around 11 a.m and the line was starting to pile up. So if you're the type who doesn't like to wait, try waking up a wee bit early to avoid lines!

Personally I think #2 buffet in Vegas. They have everything you can think of and their version is great! Beautiful dessert spread. Seafood. Chinese food. American. Italian. Pretty typical buffet food but just great quality stuff and massive amounts of it.

Came here at around noon time on Saturday for Brunch-Lunch Buffet. The line was long but moving.. so it was not too bad. 

Bacchanal has A LOT of selections.

Asian food: sushi, dimsum, pho, ramen, udon, fried rice, chowfun, porridge with century eggs on the side, bbq pork ( must try.. delish!!!) and other Chinese dishes...

Italian food: pizza, pasta, etc.

Mexican food: yes they make tacos in front of you. And they are so good. You can choose from beef, chicken or pork..

Seafood: snow crab legs!!!! muscles, oysters, shrimps...

They also have burgers, fries, sausages, roast beef, etc. and more food. Everything is pretty much already placed in small portions (cute lil plates or cups)

Desserts: heavenly with cakes, crepes, gelato.. notes: the chocolate cakes are yummmmm!!!!!!

Lots of food to list out all here.. u gotta go check them out for yourself!

My husband and I have lived in Vegas for 12 years and had never been to this buffet. We decided to try it out as a celebratory dinner for our wedding anniversary. Can I just say it was absolutely amazing! The food was on point and delicious. The desserts were so delectable and delicious. Fred Stone, Chef Nicholas and their staff were outstanding! I can not say enough about how great our experience was. I would definitely reccomend this buffet a million times over to anyone who is looking for an awesome selection of entrees as well as wonderful service.
Best best buffet in Las Vegas. The food was great sooo good. There's a a lot of food stations also an ice cram station loved it. Haven't been to buffet like this .

Food was good not great, for the price alcohol should have definitely been included, oysters were kinda worn and shredded looking, king crab was mixed in with snow crab it was maybe 90% snow crab and 10% king crab, the shrimp was amazing though, and the Dessert was only average at best..... overall I would never wait more than 20 minutes to eat here, and never would I pay for the dinner again as I imagine the lunch would be identical, I guess for a buffet it wasn't bad but don't get your hopes too high also seafood was limited, definitely no lobster don't be fooled by the incredible seafood display :)

I like the ambiance.  Design is modern.  However some of the ergonomics are not optimal.  The food is buried under the hoods and very hard to reach at times.  

Some of the food was just ok and some was good.  The won ton soup was only average.  Egg roll was also dull.  

The ice cream cone and desserts were great.

General feeling of our party is that Bacchanal is definitely not the best Buffet in town.

Best Buffet in Vegas.  I've been here on two occasions, once for brunch and another time for dinner.  There is usually a long wait where you wait to get paged before you even wait in line.  The time we ate here for dinner, we paid extra to wait less.  Breakfast has bottomless mimosas, dinner, I'm not sure about bottomless alcohol.  Our server was very slow at bring drinks, but I guess that's just a hit or miss when you go.  I recommend trying everything, it's definitely an awesome food adventure.

A solid pick for a classier buffet.  Oysters were good but a few were sandy. Crab legs tasty and plentiful.  Meats a bit too salty, but the pork belly was nice.  Selection ridiculously large--two whole rooms, and I never made it to the end of the second room without filling my plate! Particularly loved the coconut ceviche and jasmine rice dessert!  Overall, very pleasant service and environment and absurdly huge selection, but as with all buffets, not everything was equally delicious.  If you like seafood and desserts and have a big appetite, you'll enjoy yourself :)

I am writing this review to inform everyone that if you are thinking about having your special event at the Bacchanal Buffet do not do it. After signing a contract and believing I had the best experience of my life I was slammed 10 days later with an unknown $3,000 charge. When I tried calling the Bacchanal it took them days to get back to me. They first claimed that I had a table outside of our groups private room that resulted in me having over 10 more people than I actually had and that's what the charge was for. When I asked who made the head count they admitted there was no head count taken but they counted the number of chairs that were in the room... last I checked chairs were inanimate objects that didn't eat food so I don't know why they would base my head count off of chairs and not actual people. They never sent me any kind of invoice when the charge occurred, then when I finally got a hold of someone over the phone that was actually part of Bacchanal management I was told that they were willing to give me a "discount" of 3 people for the mysterious 10 people that they wrongfully charged me for. I of course did not accept. The last I heard they would be having a meeting about it and get back to me within 1-4 days. That was over 2 months ago. Very disappointed with the unprofessional behavior I experienced from upper management. I even requested that video camera footage be pulled of my group walking back so a head count could be performed by their management... conveniently they delete all of their video footage every 7 days.

One champagne brunch coming up! ($45 w/bottomless champagne). We heard a lot of hype about this buffet and it did not disappoint and there wasn't a wait when we arrived, even better!  It was aesthetically lovely and the atmosphere was very nice and I loved the background music. The food was good, not great. Bottom line, it's always going to be mass produced buffet food...but I could tell that the Bacchanal took great pride in being unique and ensuring the quality of their food. They took the extra step to be different, but offering you a scoop of vanilla sea salt ice-cream on a warm chocolate chip cookie at the dessert station or offering you regular tater tots and sweet potato tots. lol

They offer alot of "bite sized" options in their own mini fryers or on mini plates....which allows you a taste without over indulging. I would recommend this buffet to anyone coming to Vegas. 

The Champagne was GOOD haha, you could tell it wasn't cheap! Our waitress was a doll..she was very attentive.
BEST BUFFET in Vegas!!! This is the only buffet I know that has the most variety food!!!!

For just under $60/person, it's worth it! Get here early though, or the waits gonna be at least an hour! I came here on Friday around 5 pm and my table of 4 was seated immediately. 

The juices in glass milk mugs are spot on and the seafood was the highlight. Had at least two plates of snow crab legs and there's another section where you get them hot too! Crab legs can already cracked open. Oysters and mussels were also fresh. 

Most other foods were hit or miss though. The sushi was sub par, pho was excellent, ramen was mediocre quality..so I recommend trying a little bit of everything. The variety was great and had wide selection.

Although my husband fell asleep at the table from being in the pool and drinking all day, I had a buffet delight at this place! I think I went back 17 times , ok ok ... maybe like 10 lol! Good is amazing and beautifully prepared! Dishes I've never had and flavors I've never tasted ! For sure a Las Vegas must go !

My goodness I have found seriously the BEST buffet in the world, EVER! When I heard about this new buffet, I was a little weary of holding it as high as it positioned itself to be. I have NOT been to the old buffet so I don't have it as a backdrop for comparison, but I have been to a few "best" Vegas buffets around. I sat down and ate my butt off the 4th day it opened so energy was high, lines were long, and food was as perfect as ever.
