I came around lunch time (12pm) and waited for about an hour until I reached the cash register. I can definitely say that it was worth the wait. The decor was very modern, simple, clean, and elegant. First, while our hostess was leading us to our table, she quickly introduced us to where the food stations were starting off with seafood, American, Mexican, Italian, Japanese, Chinese, and DESSERTS! 

There is seriously no SINGLE "best" dish... because ALL of them were DELICIOUS. High in quality and excellent in culinary skills. I tried to taste ALL that was out, but I failed... there's too much variety within my stomach space and time frame. Some highlights of mine were the lobster corn shower, salmon nigiri, PRIME RIB (wow, prime rib has never tasted so good in buffets - seriously a high class restaurant taste and quality), beef brisket, and their dim sum! (who would think that dim sum at a buffet ACTUALLY tastes authentic and delicious???) Also notable was a noodle station where you actually order upon request...

The REAL treat here was the desserts. The desserts have its own separate station away from the food and also have a gelato and crepe station. The desserts were immaculate. Every bite of the macarons, mousse cakes, creme brulee, cheesecake, tiramisu... everything was just delicious. I find it extremely difficult just picking out one favorite. It's impossible!

I don't know if it's because Bacchanal is a new buffet that it is absolutely perfect and delicious, or it just may have raised the standards for all the buffets out there. 

Words just can't describe the experience I had here with my taste buds. Forget the night life in Vegas, I'm coming back here just for this buffet!

I am giving it 3 stars because of the price! Way over priced for what you get. The dining area has no ambiance and the dinner music is way to loud and obnoxious. The food is very good and the selection is large. As it should be for the price! The desert bar is lacking. I have had more selections at a 18.00 buffet. Not much fruit to choose from. My recommendation for what it's worth is to look around there are much better deals in this town as I lived hear in the past and still a Nevada resident.

A 3.5 experience. I can generally appreciate a buffet, but all in all, it's not really my thing. Firstly, you have to check-in, and then come back at your allotted time, only to wait in line to pay, then wait in line to be seated. We visited on a Monday for a late lunch. We got our check-in receipt at 1:40 pm, checked in at 2:20, and were seated around 2:40. 

It was extremely busy, and there were long lines to get food, especially the seafood. While there was a lot to choose from, there were only a few items that stood out to me: the steamed BBQ buns, the meatballs, the beef burria, crab legs and cocktail shrimp, and the coconut macaroons.
Best buffet in Vegas! Variety of selections for everyone's liking. I'd definitely come back!

Easily one of THE best buffets in Vegas. 

The wait is almost always over an hour if not more so be prepared. BUT they just started a new system where you can put your name down and come back after your estimated wait time ends. (Genius!)

Everything, and I mean everything, here is good. 

The oysters, mexican station, creme brûlée, pizza, shrimp, sliced beef, french fries... It's all good!! 

You cannot go wrong at this buffet. 

It's expensive, $50+, but it's the BOMB.

If you're going to check out one buffet in Vegas, this is the one.

Our second visit and even better this time.  The snow crab is SO sweet and fresh and the Prime rib SO flavorful. Service is very attentive which is super important if you also get the all you can drink.   Best buffet in Vegas!

We went here for Mother's Day and it was awesome. They gave Mothers roses and they gave my two girls carnations. The variety in food was very impressive. Pho, sushi, many different types of seafood, truffle mushroom soup, burgers, pasta, tacos, and endless mimosas. The presentation of the food was really unique and sometimes too pretty to eat‍. It is a bit pricey, but we were not disappointed.

I watched a video on YouTube that made here the 3rd top breakfast buffet.  Honestly I wasn't impressed. It just seemed pretty average food. It's weird how they have the food set up with some brunch and breakfast stuff mixed around (like mashed potatoes next to bacon). All the servers and cooks I encountered were great with gracious to help with questions and directions. 
The mixed berry smoothly was really tasteful and I enjoyed the mini churros. Those were probably my top favorites in the whole buffet.

We are Los Angeles Residents that travel to Las Vegas a few times a month for work. On every trip we go to Bacchanal at least three or four times as we just LOVE it. Service and food is just beyond this world. 
However aside from everything that  Bacchanal offers the place would not be what it is if it were not for the people who work there. 

While we have had great experiences we have had "outstanding"experiences with one of the hostesses Vesna...even when she is not the one seating us she will stop by and say hello and ask us how everything is. She is amazing. 

Esmeralda Juarez one of the servers makes us feel so pampered and the service she delivers is amazing. She is totally on top of her game and what a great personality!!! Just love her. 

And then there is Giovanni ..an amazing young man who we have had the pleasure of having a couple of times as our server...great...fantastic and a total asset to Bacchanal. 

I can go on and on about these individuals and it would still be not sufficient enough to truly describe their fine qualities. We will continue to  go to Bacchanal and hope to continue enjoying the restaurant and be lucky enough to get these wonderful people helping us. We highly recommend d the place and endorse it as the best Buffet in Vegas.

Our group came at the right time. Monday at 2:45p. There was absolute no line! The trick is to come right before they start dinner. You pay the lunch price and wait a few minutes and they start rolling out the dinner menu items. Dinner prices start at 3pm so just make sure you are in before that time. 
As for the food, most of everything I tried was delicious. There were maybe one or two plates that I didn't care for. Also, try to grab the items more towards the center or back. The food items closest to the front were not as warm as those in the back. We also noticed they keep placing new menu items out throughout the night. By the time we left (we spent almost 2 hours there!) there were probably 3 or 4 items we did not see earlier. When you go to the dessert bar try to talk to the chefs, they were friendly and told us about the dessert menu and also offered us caramel apples which were not out on the bar. They will also give a few recommendations on what to try.
Long wait, go early at 10 for lunch. Good choice of food. Some highlights. Worth the wait

The food gets 5 Stars, the service 2 stars. We went last night to celebrate our friend's birthday. We got the VIP package which included us not having to wait on in line, a seafood tower, and bottomless drinks (red or white wine, champagne, blue moon, and red or white sangria). 

After being seated it took a little while for our server to arrive with our drinks, and the seafood tower followed shortly after that. Tower was excellent and had lobster, oysters, stone crab, shrimp, etc. 

Suddenly, at the table next to us, a man started throwing up. It took a few minutes for any employees to come to their table. Here were are, trying to enjoy this seafood tower, listening to a man throw up. After about 5 minutes a manager came over and told the table to leave, and then they left, but throw up was still on the table. One would think the manager might have come over and asked us if we wanted to move, or say I'm sorry you had to see and listen to that, but nothing. Eventually they brought over garbage bags and cleared that table - but man hearing and seeing that sure made it hard to enjoy the rest of our meal. 

The servers never took our dirty plates. We ended up piling them on a table on the other side that hadn't been cleared. We rarely saw our server. I think we had 3 drinks each total. So we really didn't plan to go all crazy on alcohol but it would have been nice to have the option for another drink.

All that said / the food was incredible. Wagyu beef, prime rib, cooked to perfection. A great selection of seafood including snow crab legs. They had pizza, sushi, many Asian dishes, meat and cheese boards, and really all the food we did try was good. My daughter loved the fried chicken. 

The dessert bar was incredible - so many choices - but really the crepes are where it's at. Freshly made with some Nutella and then a fruit topping. Yum!

What are you looking for? A beautiful glasshouse filled with gorgeous furniture and  lounge music? Well, that's exactly what you're going to find.

Setting: The setting, atmosphere and service definitely is one of the best I've ever encountered. 

Seafood: You can expect to see a glass cube of crab legs cut half open, or an ice mountain of raw oysters. Sounds exciting, right? That quite sums up what is to expect in terms of their seafood. 

Desserts: This restaurant offers much more in terms of desserts including but not limited to gelatos, crepes (and creeps) and deliciously, rich chocolate strawberries. 

Aside from service, Bacchanal buffet offers many, many good things to customers except for anything great. You want lobsters? You're not going to find it here. If you think you have an insatiable appetite, I think this might just turn your world upside down.

Ive tried most of the buffet  in town, but i could say this is the best buffet i ever been too. a lot of selections of food and most of all are live action stations. i brought my family here one time and they love it! looking forward to eat here again and i wont get tired going here. Pricey but all worth it.... I definitely suggest this buffet if your visiting Vegas or you live in town..

Long wait, so make sure you have a card to pass the line or don't go at 12. The food was delicious! Seafood was fresh and it's all cut and ready to eat. I loved the ramen that's made to order. 

They also have fresh carrot and orange juice. I would say skip the sushi but make sure the get the nice fat slab of bacon.

The quality of the food didn't go down so much as the beautiful display and presentation that they used to have. Whereas everything used to be individually plated, its all made in mass now and left in mass under heat lamps. The reason why this hasn't necessarily affected the quality is that there are now lines for the lines to get food. So there' s always people taking the food hot off the plate anyway. 

One good thing about the previous 2-3 hour wait time. Now you can gamble while you wait, and get a text when it's your turn to come back. OR being the starving impatient person that you might be as I am, you can pay an extra $20 to cut the line. Well, you can't say they aren't doing business, right?
Incredible amount of options and delicious foods, but the price? A little high for what your getting.

After seeing the line stretching into an endless maze that somehow folded upon itself eight times over, I figured the food here had to be really good, or there was a lot crazy people waiting. Either way, the group I was with heard all the buzz about this place and we walked helplessly to the end of the line.

We were only in line for about 3 minutes when someone from my group suggested we asked the people next to us (but further in line) how long they've been waiting--30 minutes. After waiting for another couple of minutes, we decide to take the express line instead. To be rational, we figured that it would've been the same, in terms of time and cost (15 dollars more + 18% tip per person in the express line) if we waited in the original line. And since there was 8 of us, we figured we would be paying gratuity anyway. 

In comparison, we managed to snag a table for 8, at the peak of lunch buffet on a Sunday, 30-40 minutes earlier than the group that was 30 minutes ahead of us line. 

The selection of food available at Bacchanal was beyond outstanding, and is something that seems to be a response to Cosmopolitan's Wicked Spoon Buffet and Wynn's Buffet. They do this really neat thing of steaming up crab legs by request, offer a wide array of juices, offer an extensive selection of meats, from brisket to prime rib and ham to sausages. They even have a full on gelato dessert station, next to a crepes station in the dessert area. I remember coming back several times for this green pesto based pasta, I don't remember the name of it but it was definitely one of the stand out dishes available. 

I decided to give up on my diet that day (only so I wouldn't have count for all the calories), but I hope to make another visit when I'm back in town.

I won't be able to summarize eaisly how great this buffet is. With the exception of price, this is by far the best buffet I've ever had the pleasure of dining in, in 50 years of life. Their wide variety of gourmet pleasures are vast to say the least. Their dessert are bar none the best I've ever seen offered at any buffet ever. I not only highly recommend, I suggest you forget wherever you where planning on going, and cone straight here, the best by far!
If you are vegetarian or vegan please don't bother... paid 40 bucks to eat veggie noodles .  But I gotta say that The service was great , our waiter was super nice

Really snazzy looking buffet but it's overhyped in my opinion. The food is just standard buffet food. Their Asian section is a little nicer than most other ones, which was nice, but the Italian section let much to be desired. The desserts are prettier and have more elaborate decorations than the other buffets, but the taste is bland. I do like the fresh squeezed juices that they offer and the staff are friendly. For the higher price point though I think my money could be better spent elsewhere.

First time at this buffet and last. Yes there is a variety of ethnic food, meat and seafood but quality wasn't there for the money. Crab was waterlogged, soups were cold, and deserts lacked flavor. Prime rib was good, pork belly was good but not enough to come back. Sorry Ceasars not fit for a king or queen.

Went here for brunch on a Sunday. Unlimited mimosas. Didn't think anything was great but it was good. I don't know if it's worth $50 (w/tax) but I guess it depends on how much you can eat. I'd come back again, on my bday. :-)

Came around lunchtime and the wait wasn't too bad. $36/person. I was quite disappointed, though. When I try a new buffet, I like to scope out the selection, and what I saw wasn't very appetizing. Maybe it was the presentation, but I wasn't excited to eat here. I went to the meat department, and got a taste of everything, but that was pretty much all I had to eat. 

The lighting was dim, and the music was ridiculously loud. It felt like they were trying to be a club rather than a buffet. 

I'm pretty sure I won't be eating here again.
The service is poor, the hotel is dated, the staff is going through the motions, the restaurants serve cafeteria food. AVOID this hotel at all costs. Stay downtown before this resurrected dump.

definitely experienced much better. 

we got here at the lunch to dinner transition ... didn't want to pay $50 for dinner (we paid ~35$ instead). the end of lunch is very ho hum... everything tasted very dry even the seafood. 

so we waited for dinner to transition ... 
seafood -- bad. overall dry, bland, over salted EVEN the alaskan king crab (didn't even look fresh). the clam bake was dry, the mussels were dry (and they were supposed to be fresh), shrimp was hard and dry ... i was wondering to myself, "SO GLAD WE DIDN'T PAY MORE!!!" 

the only redeeming items were their prime rib, rib eye lollipop and desserts. seriously. i walked through the whole buffet several times, trying to be enticed by something else, but no. the cutting board meats - pork ribs, brisket ... were so salty and smoked that i couldn't eat more than 2 bites. the prime rib, rib eye were very good ... but ONLY if you asked for the medium rare ones and ones they JUST cooked. *makes a big difference* 

tried other items... wagyu beef sliders ( too greasy, dry), fried chicken (DRY!!), sweet potato fries (pre-packaged), meatball slider (this was ok), pizza (this was ok), seaweed salad (ick, not fresh). salads had nice presentation though. dessert bar was good. .... liked their oatmeal cookie, cheesecake, and macarons. but otherwise.... TOTALLY NOT MEMORABLE. 

overall, not worth it. i feel bad for people who paid $50+ for that night's dinner. save yourself some money and go eat at a good restaurant. (order of buffet love ... m buffet, wicked spoon, wynn, bellagio,........., bacchanal (end of the line))...

[MY BACKGROUND]: I've been coming to Vegas since 1994, and tried pretty much every buffet on the Vegas strip. 

[DATE VISITED]: Saturday, March 16th, 2013, Dinner Buffet. Entered the line at 5:10PM, paid at 6:00PM, started eating at 6:40PM. 

[THE INTERIOR]: Before you enter the buffet, you will see a huge line, that will remind you of Disneyland. Once you enter the buffet, its major chaos..Chaos!! There are way too many people, and most of the tables seemed very close together. The noise level is really loud. I definitely will not bring my older relatives here, as they might find it too hectic. It seems like the people at Caesar's had a very obscure shaped room to fit in a buffet of this size. 

[THE FOOD]: Besides long lines, and chaotic atmosphere, the food here is really really good. The Asian section is probably one of the most authentic tasting Asian section at any Las Vegas buffet. This also goes for the rest of the buffet. The cocktail shrimps they serve are also one of the largest sized cocktail shrimp of any Vegas buffet I've tried.  My sister and I stood in line for the steamed crabs for at least 20 minutes. Determined that we were not going to wait in this line again, we practically filled mountain high 2 plates each (4 plates total), with a layer of cocktail shrimp, and a  huge pile of king crabs on top (we had 4 plates of these). Needless to say, we were a little carried away with how much we brought for my family of 4, but I think we pretty much were satisfied with how much shrimp and crab we ate, that it justified the $50 dinner cost. Also their dessert section is amazing. They also have different flavored mochi and gelato.

[THE SERVICE]: Our server was amazing, in terms of getting our drinks, and cleaning our finished plates. No complaints at all here.  

[THE GOOD]: 
- some of the best tasting buffet food hands down
- the selection and variety is amazing, 
- the presentation of the foods in the small plates is very nice

[THE BAD]
- long Lines to get into the buffet, 
- more lines in the buffet to get the food
- chaotic atmosphere
- noise level is high, definitely not a place for a romantic dinner
- One design flaw of the buffet is the line for the steamed crabs. The people that stood in line for the steamed crabs blocked off the whole seafood section. So for the people that did not want steamed crabs, but lets say want a piece of salmon in the seafood section, you couldn't because the people in line for the steamed crabs stood right in front of the food. I guess you could try to sneak in between people in the steamed crab line to get some food, but everybody in line for the steamed crabs had the "I'm waiting in line, you should too" face.  This design flaw also applies to the meat carving section. The line for the meat carving section blocked off another section of the buffet, hence other people couldn't get to those foods either. At one point the line for the steamed crabs and meat carving section blended together, to form one mega line, that caused a lot of confusion. The issue is, they steam the crabs a little at a time, so the line went really really sloowwww. The line wasn't moving at multiple points. We waited at least 20 minutes to get the steamed crabs. They really should place a line divider for the people in these lines so they don't block half of the buffet. 

[OVERALL EXPERIENCE]: I've always wanted to try the Bacchanal buffet ever since it opened. We asked the waiter if its always like this, but they said its less crowded on the weekdays, and at earlier times. If I go again next time, I'm going to go at 3:30 PM, and try to avoid the 6 PM dinner crowd.

A really good experience for a buffet visit. It took us about 35 minutes to get through the line and sit at our table, but once we were seated, we were able to get our food fast. Unique serving portions and upscale decor make this a place to visit in Las Vegas. Here is the breakdown of my review:

SERVICE:   The cashier and hostess were pleasant. We got a brief explanation of all the different stations and cuisines available, which was nice, but the place seemed shorthanded. Refills took a while and the clearing of dirty dishes around us was slow. Almost gave them 3 because of it. 

Food: Overall, there is tasty food all around. However, the carving station is OUT OF THIS WORLD. They serve up the biggest pieces of beef I have ever seen, including premium cuts like the tomahawk ribeye. If you are a steak lover, you will be pleased. The sushi and Japanese station was great (fresh) and the seafood station was ok.

Desserts: Simply AMAZING. Besides having the desserts you can expect at an upscale buffet,  the have a section just for their unique gelato flavors. Not sure if the ice cream is homemade, but you will find some delicious combinations, like the chocolate/hot pepper, which is sure to amaze your taste buds and blow your mind. 

Visit this place if you get a chance. Come hungry!

One of the better buffets I've been to. It's this or The Buffet at the Wynn. Price is not too bad. Good selection. You'll definitely find something you love. I've heard the wait can be hours. We went on Monday for brunch. We were quickly shown to a table.

Well, after all the rave reviews I just couldn't get past the over cooked prime rib, over cooked sea bass; how do you do that? Dry King fish. The food was decent but definitely not worth $59.70

I will say they do have a variety of food selections. Chinese, Italian, Sushi, BBQ and so forth. Some one posted that Bellagio needs to step it up but Bacchanal doesn't serve king crab legs. Anyhow try it at least once.

As far as buffets go - this is definitely the best one I've been to. I see a lot of comments about the lines being long - and maybe they are on the weekends - but we arrived right about noon on a Thursday and didn't wait at all. There was so much food - I thought I had seen the whole buffet, but then I turned the corner and realized there was a whole section I hadn't seen. And all the food is really, really good. I see someone wrote they ate so much they got sick - haha, but it would be so easy to do! Luckily, I had a spa appointment and had to get out of there, or I might have done the same. This is not your ordinary buffet food, it's really good and there is just about anything you can think of. Sushi, Dim Sum, seafood, Italian, Mexican, oyster shooters, chicken and waffles, pork belly, prime rib.... I could go on and on. Also, they have fresh squeezed juices. The watermelon juice was delicious - and perfect after a long night of boozing in Vegas. If you're going to do a buffet in Vegas, I highly recommend this one.

What a disappointment. COLD FOOD! Came here 2 years ago, and the buffet was Amazing. Everything lost quality. Will not be coming back here. Rather eat at a restaurant. This buffet killed my Vegas experience.

The interior decor was beautiful. Food display was awesome. Selection was large. Taste and flavor were bland. Service was terrible.

The food lacked any depth or spazaz in flavor. Selection and quality were on par with the Rio. Fine but not great. Some dude was angry that the olive oil was mixed with Canola oil and was calling the chef out. 

Not sure why the great reviews....I feel like I'm that odd hater.... but having been to many buffets in Vegas, I won't be coming back. I expected so much more from Caesar's Palace! Especially after paying $40.

I had to finally get a manager to get me help refilling my tea. I waited 40 min and asked twice for a refill. I felt like I was a starving man in a desert that had to fight for a taste of liquid. 

BLUF: Wicked Spoon is better. Haven't been to the Wynn to compare theirs yet.

Total garbage. Absolutely disgusting. Very expensive to eat old, flavorless junk food. Our party of 4 people cost $237 to get in, the garbage offered wasn't worth more than $6 per person. If you must eat at a buffet, go to the Wynn or Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan- their buffets are less pricy than the garbage buffet at Caesars.

This buffet used to be my #1 in Vegas, I come here every single time when I'm in town.  It just gone downhill so much to a point that it doesn't even worth $20 anymore. 

I went there again on Feb 23 based on my previous good experiences on their food selections (I have never had good experiences with their servers though), but this time it's the worst.

1. I don't know if they have a problem with Asian.  They love to group all the Asians in a single corner and give them a lousy server.  My server, once again, had NEVER cleaned up the plates on time, every time when I came back with my food, I needed to push the dirty plates away from the table.  ALso during my dining 1 hour I had to find someone else, to call for my server to refill drinks TWICE.

2. Food is horrible.  I mean, as you can see in the picture, this is what they called "prime rib".  I was so shocked and couldn't believe my eyes for a dinner costing $53 you're giving me such bad quality of food.  I then asked the butcher "may I have a piece that is more red?" he said "No!  Next!" and turned his head away.  I was really really shocked.

3. The crowd of the restaurant had gone downhill too, the gentleman next to me took off his shoes and put his feet on the chair.  When I first asked my server if I could change my seat she said "1 person 1 table, you already have 1 table".  I ended up speaking to the ladies at the front to solve the problem.

I'm so sorry, I will NEVER come back again.

Not worth the wait! Over 6 hour wait time. Lol. The food is really good, but it is taking longer to get seated. We checked in at 3:45pm on Friday and the estimated seating time was at 10:37pm. They close at 10pm!! The self check-in is useless. When they text you to come in, you still have to wait at least another hour just to pay and get seated. Dinner starts at 3pm. So check in 3-5 hours earlier in a Friday.
I laughed, I cried, I stood up and got seconds... and thirds. It is worth the price for the desserts and the marvelous Italian coffee alone!

Being the first grand opening weekend, I was surprised by how many people knew about this place even though they didn't advertise as much. I only found out because one of the girls in our group read it somewhere from USA Today (Food section)! As we got there, the line was already rows and rows filled so we decided to suck it up and wait the 1.5-2hr wait. When we finally got in, we paid the hefty fee of (45$ each) and got seated. We quickly ordered our drinks and ran to the buffet lines to see this "extensive" menu. I couldn't believe my EYES to see SOOO much food available. I made my way towards the seafood area which had snow crab legs to shrimp cocktails and even oysters. After that, I wanted to get some surf & turf so I went to the red meat area which I got my brisket, sausages, prime rib, etc. I thought that would be the end until I saw another room around the corner that had Italian, Asian and even a noodle bar where the chef made fresh Japanese ramen (which is to DIE for and surprisingly very good for a buffet), pho, and udon. This new buffet is literally the land of gluttony and our table was no exception. This buffet did remind me a bit of the Wicked Spoon for their aesthetic designs of their dishes such as their fried chicken and waffle came in vintage baskets and pots. 

Even after consuming all these savory dishes, we had to try their dessert menu; There's ALWAYS room for dessert! The dessert menu however wasn't as extensive as I thought it would be but they had some delicious gelato selection. The one that stood out the most was their strawberry. It literally tasted like the strawberry gelato that I had in Florence, Italy! It was that comparable. They also had macarons, crepes, assorted candies (swedish fish), and tiny cake pops.

My expectations for Vegas buffet are not that high for 1 main reason: Too much different food doesn't equate to good refined food because there's too many different options plus when you mass produce food, you skimp out on quality. But rest assured, this buffet offers QUALITY. I'm just hoping that the quality of the buffet wasn't at its best just because it was the opening weekend. I hope this quality is here to STAY!

Another nice plus was that the President of Caesar's sat right behind our table making sure that the buffet was operational at good standards and even greeted our table and introduced himself and bought a round of drinks for us. NOW THAT'S SERVICE!

OH MAN OH MAN BACCHANAL BUFFET.

I've been dreaming of this for awhile. We came for dinner at 1 pm but it was brunch and the wait would be two hours once you put it in the reservation machine. Perfect because dinner food starts at 3 anyway. 

Decided to go shopping got a call on our phone and literally ran to the buffet from Express. The only time I run.

It was crowded. Holiday pricing was $63 per person. It was pricey but that is okay because we ate our money's worth and more.

Everyone has a different idea of how to eat their money's worth in buffet food. Some ate a bite of everything. Some eat their worth in dessert. Me? 


King crab legs, oysters, shrimps every seafood imaginable. So that's the first thing we went for. Mussels good, clams not as good as mussels, salmon was delish, crab legs bomb.

Then we went for the MEAT. The line was kind of long but that's okay cause we delegated tasks. I got in line while my friend went to grab things to eat in line. We ate a whole plate of food in line. No shame. Oysters were yummy better than the ones I had at palace station the night before. Salami yummm and cheese. 

The meat was all right. Too salty and over seasoned on the outside. I'm not a big fan of lamb. Turkey was okay. BEEF RIBS were my FAV. 

I heard tacos were good. Desserts hit or miss depending on what you like but there's so many you are bound to eat something you like. 



Some tips: 
Eat fast so you don't feel how full you are.
Don't eat carby things like rice pasta bread you will get full too fast. 
Drink water to wash down everything.
Go for your favorite thing first before you get too full to eat it. 
Take breaks you are allowed to be there for two hours but they probably won't notice if you're there for like four five. 



Happy feasting!!
Oh no!! I'm not even reviewing the buffet because I've been in line for 40 minutes as they let god and the world in and forsake everyone else ..
Great food. A lot to choose from. Worth the price.  Highly recommend. Spacious, clean, and welcoming.  My husband and I recommend this buffet when ever you're in Vegas.

Worst buffet in Vegas, don't go there. 4 hr long waiting line, even waiting in lines inside. Just so so food for the expensive price, not worth at all! even service is worst among all Vegas buffets. Never go there again.

Decent wait but that's what makes the food taste better? Not really tho. Me and my family came here on a Friday night at 830 and were seated at 930. I anticipated this wait and kept hyping up myself for the "buffet of buffets". Nevertheless, I was a little underwhelmed. The selection was gr8 (seafood, meats, wide array of asian food but no sashimi??, italian etceteraaa). The prime rib was dank, roast duck was surprisingly good, oysters and crab were fresh and I was especially impressed with the desserts (crepes and chocolate covered strawberries mmmm). But for the price of 53.99?? it wasn't REALLY worth it. I guess all the buffets in Vegas are overpriced like this so it is what it is. We couldn't come to Vegas without having one buffet meal but this will probably be our only one.

Been here a few times and it's always delicious.  Price jumped for weekend dinner at $65.99 per person. No military discount even with Total Rewards. Pretty bummed about that. The hostess Samantha was a delight! Full of good energy and a great first impression. Stock up on crab legs first then enjoy the heavier foods like Waygu beef, roasted duck, sushi, and so much more. Definitely would recommend coming before 6pm.

When you think of Vegas, you think of clubs and buffets. It's not a Vegas weekend without stuffing your face at a buffet -- but I think this is one of those things that's always better in your head. We got to Bacchanal at 6 on a Saturday and it was already packed. We waited almost an hour before giving in and paying an extra $15 to go through the express line. That brought the grand total to $70, after tax. We like to think we ate $70 worth, but really, you're full after like 2 plates!

There's a seafood section (king crab legs and giant shrimp, oh yeah), potatoes section (basket after basket of different kinds of fries), meats, soup and fresh juices, Mexican (tacos made for you on the spot), Italian, cured meats and cheeses, and Asian (including a soup and jook bar). And then, of course, there's dessert! Cakes, cookies, tarts, macarons, gelato, mochi, and the list goes on. They even have a small sugar-free section.

I'd say most of the food was 3-4 stars (it is a buffet after all, and it has been sitting out), but definitely get some steamed crab legs and shrimp. And, if you don't want to wait, there's always the express line - or go at lunch! But I think the desserts aren't as extensive. Dinner starts at 3pm on the weekends though, so you can go for "lunner".

Sadly disappointed

Not sure if it was an "off" night for this 4 star yelped restaurant but I was quite surprised.  Someone needs to tackle quality control.

Nothing seemed fresh, the food looked as though it was presented well, but tasted like stale leftovers (I hate leftovers).  ALL the cut  meats were completely dried out and tough (yes.. Ribs, prime rib, turkey.. Dry and tough).  The Asian cuisine made me sick.. Seriously the only things worth eating 1) pizza was editable, and 2) the ice cream was yum.

I will not be returning!

This is the second time we've been here and it was way different than what we remembered. the first time we came, it was delicious. This time the food was not great at all. The sticky rice in the Asian section was hard and dry, dim sum was oily, bbq section was not good. The only good area was the fresh seafood and desserts.

Great buffet. Nice seafood. If you purchase the unlimited access for 24 hours, this buffet has an up charge plus it costs more on weekends. Has a great variety of food. Definitely something for everyone.

This place lives up to all the hype! The recent renovation was much needed and now Caesar's buffet is king once again. The place is amazing, with nine open kitchens, foods are freshly prepared and presented in a way only Caesar's could pull off. 500 items, that is a lot of choices people! I started with a bowl of very authentic tasting "hot & sour" soup, some very fresh sushi, edamami and a nice Mexican Caesar salad. All perfectly prepared and fresh. The most beautiful piece of prime rib came next, with a horseradish sauce that will open any clogged sinuses. Finally made it to the seafood kitchen, OMG! The Alaskan King crab legs were both tasty and fresh, cut in half for easy eating. Colossal already peeled shrimp (don't you just hate having to peel shrimp?). The Lobster corn chowder was almost as good as the little buckets of clam bake. Both are a must try, you will be going back for more, trust me. The oyster shooters were tasty and fresh. The only problem with this buffet is you will get full way before you get to all the kitchens! The Italian & the Mexican kitchens both had some wonderful wonderful dishes I never got to try. The american kitchen also had brisket sausages and several other meat choices, again, didn't get to try only because I was full! Plenty of choices for all taste pallets. I did manage to save room for dessert though and again was blown away by the array of sweets. The sorbets where awesome, as were the crepes. Creme brulle, tiramesu, tortes, etc, all so decadently delicious! My favorite was the white chocolate dipped cheesecake with rock candy sprinkles, the perfect blend of smooth and creamy mixed with a candy crunch, mmmmmhhh! A quick tip for all who go, dinner starts at three, so get there for lunch, relax a bit, and wait for the dinner items and save a ton of money (and leave plenty of time though, the line is long!). Again, hail Caesar!
Not cheap but the selection is amazing. Breakfast food...Mexican....Asian.... Everything.   Food is all great and the place is huge. We can see why it's rated as the best on the Strip.
Lots of variety! Good seafood selection. Wait service not the best but other than that, great Vegas buffet!

The buffet was good but not the best the sea food was alright but no lobster and the crab was nothing amazing. I give it a three because for the price I expected more, honestly for that much I would have rather spent it at a steak house on a good steak from a place that I know would make a nice cut of meats. The best part of the buffet was the dim sum and the Chinese food the American food was standard and the prime rib wasn't fantastic

I've been here about 20 times by now. If you want a really high-quality memorable buffet come here. So far superior to Paris, Bellagio and Wynn it's almost not funny.  Come early as even this buffet is not worth standing in line for hours for. No food is that good.  The only criticism I would lob at them is that the desserts are exceedingly mediocre.  Like an afterthought. No delicious cakes, only the flambeed bananas are great and the gelato is okay (not spectacular) A lot of bla cookies and sugar free stuff.

The only other buffet that I would say is on par with them would be Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo.

Descent for a buffet - but still buffet taste (mid-quality) there are a lot of choices from duck to crab legs and descent dessert choices, too. I think I paid 55 bucks for 2 hours worth of all you can eat. Not sure I would pay it again...buffets are good in a pinch but quality still suffers overall.

Best buffet I ever had. Very tasty many kinds of kitchen from all over the world. Will go there again. Would avoid 3-4pm. One star less is for the price. This buffet maybe worth $45 but definitely not $60. But honestly, after I tried hugely disappointed Wicked Spoon with $50, I realized in Las Vegas everything is pricier. Very good service. They cared about the kids' comfortable and safe, match a suitable table for us.

Yummy!!!! Came here on a Tuesday around 6. The line was slowly forming but only waited less than 30 mins. So worth it to come here during weekday dinner.. it's less than 60$ a person after tax. However I felt the items served on weekend is a bit different? This time around it doesn't seem as amazing as it used to be...but still good compare to other buffets. The cold seafood section will always have a line regardless. Even though weekdays the wait isn't crazy long but I suggest still try to get in before 7!

This place used to be awesome, but in the past year a new reservation system is in place that pre-queues the line for hours in advance.  Think Disney fast pass.  The problem is that while fast pass is a well executed system the Bacchinal at Caesars is a disaster.  100's of people with passes to stand in line after 8pm are turned away because he second wait is so long that the buffet will close before you get to the front.  There is no management system that says "hey, too many people have requested an 8pm time, let's close ticketing."  This results in hours of wasted time and probably lots of people throwing away money at the slots while they wait.  Avoid this place unless you want to devote an entire day to stand in line with the chance you will not be seated if the machine gives too many fast pass tickets.

One of my favorite buffets in Las Vegas! So many options, so delicious, creative and unique, and great decor. Long wait, but it's expected. Yummy crepe station! Both warm and cold crab legs! Choices go on and on! Great tasting food/desserts!

I really like this buffet! I'm not a buffet person but I think this is the one to go to when in Vegas. 

It is best to go on a weekday and early. I wanted to try their breakfast/lunch. We went on a Thursday around 9:30 and waited about 20 minutes.

I LOVED the Asian bar. It is situated in the far back. Don't miss it. 
My favorites are Shanghai dumplings, dim sum (Hai Gow, Shumai), thousand year old egg congee (yummy), ramen, pho, wonton noodles, udon, fried rice, lo mein, eggrolls, potstickers, and many more... I know it is legit because the cooks were all speaking Cantonese. However, the Shanghai dumplings could be better if the skin was a little thinner. It is fine for a Vegas buffet.

Some other dishes to try is the croque madame and the fried chicken and waffles. YUMMY! 

I am glad most of the dishes are portion control. That helps me not eat so much but I end up getting up often to grab more. So I don't know how that helps... I still ate a lot. 

We stayed until they transitioned to lunch. We had a few pasta dishes and pizza. Not impressed. I think I am sticking with the Asian bar with the all-you-can-eat dim sum. 

This buffet really impressed me!!!

Went for early lunch and were seated within 10 minutes.  Started with Kobe beef slider which was pink in the middle, cooked and seasoned to perfection.  Also had a crispy fried chicken leg with sweet potato fries with sea salt also very tasty.  The truffle scalloped potatoes were hands down my favorite.  Had the lobster corn chowder which was delicious but was cold.  Would have tasted way better served hot.  Next tried Mexican with the Red Chili Pozole which had lots of pork chunks, no skimping there.  The beans were so tasty I think they added a bit of longaniza to give it depth and it really worked.  The pork carnitas was seasoned well but a bit dry for my liking.  Cheeses and Charcuterie were yummy with cheddar, manchego, parm, salami, mortadella, you name it, all delish.  Didn't try any Asian this time but did save room for dessert.  Creme Brulee was not quite firm enough but the chocolate fondant cake was divine as was the dark chocolate and raspberry tart.  Our server was en pointe but I did hear others around me who couldn't get their servers to get them a glass of water and the lunch crowd hadn't even really arrived yet.  I will definitely be back and glad we arrived early.  When we left there was a 1 hour wait.

Five stars (amongst other buffets, this is got to be one of the best.) We had heard a lot about this buffet from friends who'd had experienced it. Everyone can agree that if you're going to divulge into the Vegas "buffet experience" you definitely need to try this one.

So let's start with the good:

Endless beer for $22 - we all know how expensive drinks can be (especially in Vegas) so this deal is on point, but plan to have several to make it worth your money. We didnt bother, we we're here for the food. And they only offer Newcastle and Miller Lite

The Food/small plates - if you're going to eat at a buffet, you got to try it all. This place boasts ten stations, from Chinese to Mexican and food is constantly being turned around. And not sitting under hot lights in huge portions,  instead, find individually plated portions so you can really let your palate explore. The food is DELICIOUS! And executed well and of high quality.  I loved the sweet and spicy sticky wings featured at the Chinese station. The prime rib was tender and full of flavor. 

The Seafood - fresh shrimp, oysters and crab legs! Crab legs are split in half (so helpful), delicious,  large shrimp,  and super fresh oysters.  I could have stayed in this section of the buffet all night.

The Service- excellent service from beginning to end.  Our cashier up front was gracious despite how busy
 they were, and our server was outstanding: Very personable and promptly brought all of drink requests and kept our table clear of dishes. He also recommended the hot crab legs which were in another area from the cold and went out of his way to bring us a plate full of steaming hot crab legs. And he was right, so much better than the cold! 

And the negatives (to be fair there were some negatives):

LONG LINES- for a Monday night, this place was packed. We waited in line for a little under an hour before we were seated. And the line just kept getting longer behind us. For the popular seafood and carving stations, prepare to wait. It's not terrible but it will slow your pace down...

Lack of ramekins- a lot of dishes that required sauces did not have ramekins nearby. I.e. dim sum, salad dressings, salsas. We had to take them from the seafood station. Again, not terrible just inconvenient...

The dessert station- maybe it was because I was forcing myself to eat dessert (I was so full by this point) but most everything I tried, was not that good. Except the macaroons, those were delicious! 

And lastly, the damn tongs! And the low glass awnings over the food. These were terrible. I couldn't pick anything up with the tongs.  And the low glass over the food (especially over the soup) made it difficult to ladle. I gave up after pouring half my soup on the counter... 

I definitely was nit picking over the negative stuff. They are minor when compared to the actual experience. To me, buffets are all about the gorge-yourself attitude and Baccahanal exceeded this and did it well. 

Lastly, for $55 per person, the value is exceptional.

I heard so many good things about this place and as an avid foodie, I did a lot of research before going. We got there at 245pm, paid lunch price for dinner menu which was about 40 dollars per person as opposed to 60. At first I think I was a bit disappointed with the amount of selection as I expected it to be more... grand? I think all the research backfired as my expectations were very high! As the dinner food rolled in, I got to try things I have never eaten before. I ate the best lamb steak ever, absolutely loved the meat and cheeses station, and had watermelon gazpacho. My husband had tons and tons of crab legs. Looking back, my mouth waters whenever I think about Bacchanal. I would go back in a heart beat but we are hundreds of miles away unfortunately. If you adjust your expectations, you get a lot more for what you pay. Cannot wait to go back the next time I am in Vegas!

This place was awesome and definitely worth the money and the wait. The omelette station was great and it you like pico de gallo on your eggs their's is one of the best! Spend the extra $7 for unlimited mimosas. They were great and the waitress wouldn't allow our glasses to get too low before she was offering another pour. Red velvet pancakes were on point! It's actually overwhelming because there is so much food to choose from. Best buffet I've ever had!

My friends and I came here for Saturday brunch since this was supposedly one of the better buffets. I had heard horror stories about the lines so we got here really early on Saturday morning and only had to wait about 10 minutes before we were let inside. The brunch buffet is a little over $50 (after tax) so we stayed here for over 2 hours to eat our monies' worth ;) I tried to methodically go through each station so I could try as much food as possible... but this buffet defeated me in the end. Not enough stomach space damnit! Someday I will win... someday...

*SEAFOOD STATION PLATE
-- Shrimp with Cocktail Sauce: meh
-- Ceviche: also meh
-- Lobster Benedict: ehhh it's okay
-- Shrimp and Grits: finally something I like! It was flavourful but also really salty

* FRIED CHICKEN PLATE
-- Fried Chicken: surprisingly spicy, overall meh
-- Curly Fries: okay
-- Parmesan French Fries: good as french fries but there is no parmesan flavour
-- Sweet Potato Tots: glazed and delicious!

* BREAKFAST PLATE
-- Steak & Eggs: eggs were fine but the steak was tough
-- French Toast with Maple Syrup: meh, not flavourful at all
-- Churro Tots: delicious!

* SOUP NOODLES
-- Ramen with Tonkatsu Broth: The noodles were not well cooked while the meat was really salty. Meh.

* MEAT AND CARBS PLATE (unfortunately I do not think I took a picture of this one)
-- Honey Glazed Slab Bacon: delicious but sooooo salty!
-- Smoked Brisket: apart from one super salty piece, this was good and tender
-- Pork Belly with Lentils: delicious
-- Southwest Slider: okay
-- Mac & Cheese: very creamy
-- Mashed Potatoes: fluffy and good

* DESSERTS PLATE
-- Strawberry Frangipane: refreshing
-- Vanilla Creme Brulee: good, of course
-- Banana Pudding with Bourbon Carmel Sauce: good
-- Egg Tart: pretty god
-- Meringue: good
-- Red Velvet Bread Pudding: okay
-- Blueberry Muffin: okay
-- Sugar-free cheesecake: this was gross
-- Regular cheesecake: better than sugar-free, but it was too soft

* YET ANOTHER CARB PLATE
-- Truffle Scalloped Potatoes: not as good as I was hoping
-- Al Pastor Taco with Extra Guacamole: okay

* GELATO (split flavours)
-- Dulce de Leche: One of my favourite flavours
-- Lemon Basil: the basil was too strong for me

* CREPE PLATE
-- Crepe with Bananas Foster with Rum Caramel Sauce topped with Caramel Sauce, Cinnamon Sugar, and Powdered Sugar: delicious because how could it not be?
-- Banana Foster Donut: did they mislabel this? It is just a plain doughnut.
-- Red Velvet Pancakes: cute but meh

I love the beverages offered here. While you mostly serve everything to yourself, there are servers who come around to take alcoholic drink orders. It's brunch, so we ordered mimosas for our group. They also have fruit juices in these adorable containers--I was very tempted to steal the glasses (but I didn't). I tried their Watermelon juice as well as their Sweet Mango juice--both were good but I prefer the watermelon one. RF said he really liked the coffee (for a buffet) but CW said she thought the coffee was just okay.

A lot of the food was meh, and I think there was more meh food than delicious food. But I did enjoy a lot of the items and I left very full and satisfied. This was a pretty good Vegas buffet! I would not wait in line for hours for this though...

Good quality.  Long lines.  Is it worth the wait and price - yes.  But as any other buffet, you get sick of it after 2 times.

Pros:
- Trip Tip, Ribs, Soft Tacos, Seafood, Steam crab legs (Snow Crabs, not king crab though)
- A good variety Desserts, Mochi ice cream (seasonal)
- Fresh oysters
- Good Chinese food selection (I like the thousand year old egg porridge)
- Delicious Coffee

Cons: 
- No King Crab Legs (Bellagio's Buffet has king crab legs)
- No Caviar (Bellagio has this)


Overall - I think the food quality is a notch better than Bellagio's Buffet and right on par with Wynn

What with all the hype up about this place, I have to honestly say, "it was mediocre" if any. The whole process checking in on the kiosk n being told you have an hour to wait. Then ten minutes later you get a text saying you're up, you show up n you have at least a minimum of an hour to wait in line.  The hostess that you check in with is rude n (not the right person to be at that position ) when you ask her why the hour wait? Her response is "that's how it is". You think Caesars would rather you played n gambled your $$ while waiting. Such a silly system. 
Food was okay, nothing great. Cold lobster legs rather than the hot that was expected. 
Would I go back? Nope!! I prefer M's buffet!!

Still my favorite buffet on the planet. My family usually go around 1pm so we can eat dinner for the price of lunch. Lol. This place is packed during holidays and busy seasons. Be prepared for a line if you come on their busy days.

Hands down the best buffet on the strip. They have a wide variety of foods and desserts. Different types of meats: there's crab legs,  pizzas with toppings you don't normally see at other places, an Asian section, Italian section, and mexican section amongst a few others. The hostess and waiters are friendly and helpful.  It is on the expensive side but, in my opinion,  it's worth it.  The only downside is you could be waiting to get in for a while due to the long lines. Come hungry and leave happy. ..or guilty for eating so damn much.
Best buffet in Las Vegas. Worth the wait and worth the price. Good quality meat, seafood and delicious desserts are my favourites

A big fat disappointment.

And I say this without having to wait in a ridiculous 3 hour line. We were seated right away, thanks to TR Diamond perks. The food? Gross. 2 stars for the crab legs and oysters ONLY...but come on, how do you screw that up?

I still prefer Wicked Spoon, although they lack the oysters, the selection is quality, not quantity!

We went around 1pm on a Wednesday and waited just 5 minutes to be seated. A wonderful variety of different cuisines were served with an upscale flair to their presentation. The food tasted fresh and my husband definitely enjoyed the prime rib. Wonderful service only added to the experience as our waiter was attentive and always checking on us making sure that our table was always clear of dishes and glasses full. The best part of course was dessert. The pistachio gelato with candied almonds I sprinkled on was so good! If you can avoid peak times you will have an amazing food experience. Enjoy!

The 1-star is for the wait and the way management dealt with the situation. I waited for basically 3 hours. Some people behind us in line waited over an hour and were turned away! Then they told us that essentially we would only have ~30 minutes to get food. Um, really? After waiting an hour, we discovered that we could have paid $15 extra to skip the line. We wished we knew that earlier, but at that point, didn't think it'd take another 90+ minutes to get seated. Once inside, the place was half empty and plenty of food. I went in feeling so frantic that it took half an hour just to relax and enjoy my dinner. 

The manager should have told us when we paid not to worry that the food will stopped being served in 30 minutes, but that it would plenty of time to enjoy. Because the way told us (with fear in her eyes) freaked me out. And honestly, there was more than enough time, I didn't have to run around piling plates on the table. I could have made 2 or 3 trips of smaller plates. Summary - overall, one star because of the horrible wait and customer service. Management should really work in this area.

For the food itself, it really is a 4.5 star buffet: 
Oysters - 5 stars, made sure to get at least half a dozen to get my moneys worth. They aren't as good as shucking your own up in Tomales Bay, but they do look like Sweetwaters. Most importantly, they are juicy and plump and tasty.
Crab legs - 4 stars
Shrimp - eh, 2 stars. seemed undercooked, not cripsy but plasticy, and were gross. I ended up wasting a lot of these because I got so many the first round, and they were gross.
Dim Sum - 5 stars, just as good as the best in the Bay. The hao gao and shu mai were good, but the Shangheinese dumpling was the best. Super juicy. 
Hot meats - 4 stars, co-worker really, really enjoyed the lamb
Nigiri - 4 stars, only 2 types, salmon and tuna, but both nice and fresh. The nigiri is kinda hidden away though. It's hidden in a corner and easy to miss if you're not looking for it.
Charcuterie - 5 stars, lots and lots of coppa and other good stuff
Cheese - 3 stars. tillamook, really? Tillamook is good, but they could definitely improve the cheese selection. There were no soft cheeses :( 
Beverage selection - 2 stars because there are only 2 wines by the glass. Seriously, meh. I would have loved a glass of Sauv Blanc for $7, but the bottles are $25 and  you know those are $10 at BevMo. Skip.
Environment - 4 stars. The place is brand new and designed, it's pretty and relaxing. Unfortunately due to the experience above, it took 30 minutes to relax after getting in there. Management has some BIG KINKS to work out. I won't be back for quite a while.

When we walked in, thankfully there was no line. The experience is lovely and the servers are professional. I was extremely excited even though I'm always excited when it comes to food. My favorites were the sticky buns and watermelon cubes. Everything was high quality and delicious. I love this place so much, I can't wait to come back. The price is reasonable, everything is so clean. I wish they had buffets like this back in New York.

A VERY SOLID 4 stars!

I came down to Bacchanal to scope things out and there was a huge line.  I asked the lady whats the best time to come for the shortest wait.  She indicated between 1:00PM to 1:30PM as the lunch crowd is already in and the cheap ass who come around 2:00PM to get the lunch rate for the dinner food will have not arrived yet.

We arrived at 1:05 walked straight to the cashier, paid and waited maybe 10 minutes to be seated.  This buffet is deceptively big.  There's a lot of seating and service was decent.

There's just way too much food to write about so Im going to list the highlights and the food you should try:

Asian/Chinese:  
Har Gow, Siu Mai were half way decent.  Think medium quality dim sum.
Chinese broccoli beef chow fun - Delicious
Chow Mein - very good quality
Roast Duck - very good

Carving Station:
Prime rib was good
Beef Rib was good
Smoked chicken wings were good
Smoked Pork Belly was ok 
Kobe Sliders - yum

Seafood:
Shrimp and Gritz was good
Shrimp Cocktail was good
Muscles were ok

Skip the sushi - meh

Fried chicken - just ok

Overall really good buffet and worth the high price.

Compared to other buffets in Vegas, Bacchanal ranks at the top. I haven't tried the Wynn or Wicked Spoon yet though so I can't compare it to those but I venture to say they are all pretty much on par with each other. What I will say is that Bacchanal is definitely worth a visit. 

The tough part about any buffet is keeping food fresh and hot - just naturally stuff will cool down if sitting out. Overall, there are some hits and some misses, but it's great to try a lil of everything. The modest portions allow for that. Desserts were great - wonderful selection. Plus, honestly, I just had fun eating here! You can't say that about all buffets. The interior is nicely decorated and there is a lot to see as you walk around the buffet.

If you get the Buffet of Buffet pass, this is an extra $15 per visit. It already went up from $10 when it first opened. But on it's own, prices are not crazy - ranges from about $17ish for breakfast to $37ish for dinner. Get the free Total Rewards card for a discount. 

I think Vegas and buffets are like Vegas and slot machines, Vegas and showgirls, Vegas and Cirque - it's a match made in heaven. So buffets are a must-do and if you're gonna do, then do Bacchanal!

Bacchanal, very much like the Wicked Spoon...is an amazing buffet that deserves to be called something else entirely.  When you think Buffet you think of a place with a ton of variety but mediocre (to sometimes bad) quality.  A trade off people quite often are OK with.  Bacchanal moves to change that dynamic.  The food here is excellent.  To put this in perspective, you can put the food here up against most 4 star restaurants and come out even or in some cases ahead.  This gives you variety of amazing food choices from all over the world, combines with quality you'd get at stand-alone restaurants.

There does come a sacrifice however as you are getting both quality and variety and this is price.  Be prepared to pay $58/person for this buffet (not including any alcohol you may want to partake in).  Is it worth it?  I believe so.  If you go to any great restaurant in Las Vegas, you are going to be paying between $50-$100 per person anyway.  At $60 here you also get the variety you lack at a stand alone which to me is worth it.

Now for the food:

They have several sections: (my memory is not 100% so not all options listed)

*Seafood - Crab legs, sea bass, salmon, dover sole, oysters, clams, mussels
*Carved Meats - Lamb, Prime Rib, Ribs, Steak, Sausage
*American - Hot dogs, Mashed Potatoes, Fried Chicken, Fries (sweet & regular)
*Italian - Antipasta bar(cheeses and meats), Meatballs, Ravioli, Pasta, Pizza
*Asia - Soup station (Pho, Ramen, Curry, Egg Drop, Noodle, Hot & Sour), Sushi, Chinese Favorites, Dumplings, Baos & other Dim Sum, Bahn Mi, Pork Belly
*Taco Station where they created street tacos for you
*Dessert - Pretty much everything you can want including a Gelato section and Sugar Free section


Do not expect to get through everything...it is too much...I tried!  I can recommend however my favorites so you make sure you get those on your plate.

The Meatballs were outstanding!  My #1 pick there.
The Ravioli
The Lo Mein noodles
The Pork Belly
The Bahn Mi
The Ribs from carving station (typically these meats at the carving stations are dried out and gross, but this was smoked beautifully)


Again, many of the items were amazing, but those were the stand outs.


I hope you enjoy!  I will definately be back here again.

The food here is very good, but the experience is marred by long wait (to get in ... wait for the food are fairly short or nonexistent), high prices, and poor service.

I went with friends for a late lunch/early dinner on a Saturday and waited almost an hour and a half and paid $48 to get in. As we were leaving (around 6), the line seemed twice as long as when we got there.

Anyway, the food. Just about everything is good. Highlights for me were the lamb chops, tomahawk ribeye steak, king crab legs (that they'll heat if you ask and are pre-cut), and dessert. Salad bar seemed good too but I'm a carnivore.

Not worth the money. The buffet set up was not good. We only thought the was two station. Surprise the sushi, asian, fruit and salad station was hidden. You have to walkaround the corner to see it. The dessert was the best. Seafood was not up to par on seafood. Crab leg was not good. Oyster was great. We were not in the mood to eat the hidden station after the disappointment of the lack on seafood selection.
Waitress should have told us since it was our first time here. 
Save ur money and eat at the Rio. Better buffet. Bigger and better seafood selection.

I used to love this buffet. My daughter and son-in-law had their wedding reception there when it first opened a couple years ago. But it is not the same place any more. I ate there the night before Thanksgiving. The food was either too salty or too sweet. Most of it, except for the salad veggies, was inedible. And the horrible duf duf music was too much. We asked the manager to please turn it down but he refused. He just simply didn't care.

What was particularly shocking was the oversalted Asian food. Asian food does not need to be oversalted. I tried three desserts and all were so sweet I simply couldn't eat them. 

If you want an elegant dining experience with excellent food and a staff who cares find another buffet.

Eh, it's okay. Okay, it's rather dissapointing.

I'll start by saying the good stuff: The food. For the most part, it's pretty good. They have a diverse selection to choose from. My husband REALLY liked and raved about the selection.

So that's it for the good stuff. So, here comes the bad stuff:

As much as the food choices were diverse, I am not sure if the preparation was up to par. First off, tell me why some of the food was bland? (Not the desserts, though) Secondly, why was there hair in my congee? Ugh. 

The time it takes for the staff to pick up plates. Okay, I probably came on an off day; I came in during Presidents Day, which I guess the workers were recovering from the Valentine's Day mayhem, but my table, as well as the ones surrounding, had dirty dishes for quite a while. For the amount we paid, I don't understand this. 

Finally, why would they ask for what occasion we are dining here for? We came here for our wedding anniversary, so we indicated this when we entered in our information on the reservation kiosks, but nothing else after that (with the exception of them taking your picture before they seat you, then they attempt to sell you those pictures). Doesn't make for a good dining experience. It felt misleading. 

I don't think I'll come back here. There are other buffets that has better service, shorter wait times, and better food.

Don't what all the hype about this place was. 
I would describe this place a pricey with a little bit more choices of food Chinese buffet. 

However, I would consider their dessert to be very colorful and tasted. Wish they had a separate bakery so you could have the option of just purchasing their desserts.

Impressed by the food, but even more impressed by the food poisoning afterwards. Vomiting on and off for 6 hours is certainly unforgettable. Thanks for the memories Bacchanal buffet!

PS Might also want to set up your voicemail just in case other patrons call expressing their concerns

We did wait for a while but it was totally worth it! No wonder why it's called the best buffet in Vegas. Everything fresh, lots of options for vegetarians (although could be even more) Everything we tried was quiet delicate and memorable.

I didn't really care for this buffet in Vegas after the experience. First we got our tickets and then we're called back because it was our time. Then there was another line to stand in and then when we were eating the waiter never came to refill our drinks. The food was ok different styles in sections! Presentation not so neat.

Waited a year for our annual buffet feasting in Vegas.  As always, it was worth the wait.  The warm crab legs were sweet and since they were already halved for us, it was very easy to eat and enjoy without damaging my nails.  The duck and chicken were very fresh and cooked to perfection unlike other buffets that I have been to where the meats were either over cooked or left under the heat lamp too long, thus causing the meat to be dry and tough.

Oysters were large and fresh, not the best I have had but for buffet, they were still excellent quality.  The shrimps were plump, large and fresh, fresh, fresh!  Overall the food was outstanding.  The gelato was too soft.  I think something was wrong with the freezer since the gelato seems mostly melted.

The service was great at check in.  Our server though was not so good, thus the 4 stars versus 5.  After taking our drink orders, he never came back.  Our table was bused by another lady who cleaned our dishes promptly.  We never got a refill even though our glasses were emptied the entire dinner.  Since we wanted to be filled with food rather than drinks, we did not mind so much.  Except it would have been nice to be able to wash down the food with something to drink.

Overall it was a great dinner.  Until next time....

This buffet is a MUST for anyone wanting to eat buffet in Vegas. Their selection is absolutely huge, there is definitely something for everyone here. Seafood, Asian, Mexican, American, Italian, Vegetarian, Charcuterie, Greek...etc. 
Make sure to set aside a few hours for this buffet. The lines can be up to an hour and a half (maybe more) during peak times and after you are seated, you will not want to leave. 
The dessert bar is always amazing and fun, every time I've gone, there is always something new. 
Note: other reviews complain about the pricing, however you get what you pay for here, it is by far one of the best buffets

4.5 Stars

Lunch review

Amazing selection of food
Well seasoned
Execution is done well 
Value is there

Fried chicken, ramen, and carving area are all standouts 

Overall Thoughts

Bacchanal is so far the best buffet I have tried in Las Vegas

This was definitely one of the best buffets on the strip.  There was a huge variety of food that there was no way you could try it all. 

The seafood selection was awesome, but if course the line was the longest so unless you really wanted it, it was a bit of a deterrent.  I was able to grab some oysters and an oyster shooter which I enjoyed.

The selection and quality of Asian food was above some of the other high end buffets on the strip.

One of my favorite items were the sweet potato tater tots.  Went back for seconds.

The desserts were good, but I was hoping for more or a larger variety and quality.  I am a dessert person, so I wasn't wow'ed.

I was here over the Thanksgiving holiday so the line was super long and I was a bit disappointed to find out there was no unlimited mimosas or bloody Mary's offered with the buffet price, which was higher than normal as well.

Went there last year and the experience was pleasant.  Returned there this year with some friends and my impression was completely opposite.  We had party of 8, so they charged us 18% gratuity upfront, which was fine.  But apparently the server knows gratuity is already paid, and never gave us any service.  Plates were piled up, and we could not even get a second glass of juice.  We repeatedly told her to get us more juice but that never came.  The food was not as good as before either.  Huge variety and selection but the taste was average for the most part.  As one of the most expensive buffet in Las Vegas, I expect better service and qualify.

Best buffet in Vegas! I've been here twice!

On my first visit I waited over an hour in line for dinner on a Saturday night and paid just a little over $100 dollars for two people and I still think it was completely worth it! They had such a wide selection of food and even the dessert bar had a chef station (for crepes)!!

But buyer beware: if you're in it for the meats and barbeque, you're in for a bit of a wait. The meats line overflows into the seafood line and it gets confusing where the appropriate joining point is. I chose to forgo the meats line in favor of the myriad of other cuisines that were available. I have no regrets; I'm not big on red meat anyway. 

My second visit was much less hectic as it was the tail end of brunch. I made it just in time for the brunch pricing with endless champagne but I also got to enjoy the dinner entrees too! I would highly recommend going this route as dinner pricing is $50.99 per person and brunch is $41.99 and includes champagne ( if your into that ). 

My favorite items included: the tuna & salmon sushi, pho soup station complete with pick your own toppings bar, crepes station also with a pick your own topping section,  beef broccoli, shrimp, taco station, creme brulee, tiramisu, aztec chocolate ice cream, salmon, clam chowder...I'm getting full just reminiscing. I ate so much.

This is my favorite Buffett in all of Vegas - and I've been to quite a few. No matter what you're craving there's something tasty waiting for you. Highly recommend the crab legs as well as the pasta station and you can't leave without taking a few trips around the desserts. And if you're looking to eat on the lighter side there are plenty of options including no sugar added deserts and fresh fish and sushi options. Writing this review made me hungry!

Ehhhhh I was super hyped to come dine at one of Vegas' newest buffets. However, after trying several items there, I don't think I'll be going back. I felt everything was just mediocre, especially in the Asian section. I may be a bit biased since I eat Asian food all the time but it just wasn't good or great like you expect one of the "best" buffets to be, although I enjoyed a couple items like the Chinese roasted duck and the Char Siu (Chinese BBQ Pork). But then again, you can't really mess up on those...The sushi and poke did not taste fresh as well.

I also made the wrong decision of starting from the right end, the Asian section. My advice when you get here is to go straight for the crab legs and prime rib and meats (those are the best items there) and don't waste your appetite on the other mediocre food unless you want a taste of everything. If anything, try them AFTER the crab legs and prime rib and sausages...because by the time my girl tried getting some crab legs, they ran out! They then had her stand there and wait for like a good while...over 5 minutes! You're a buffet...shouldn't you be aware of when food is running out and refill it before or immediately after? When they brought out more crab legs, those ones were literally half frozen. HALF FROZEN CRAB LEGS - WHO WANTS TO EAT THAT? Definitely ruined one of the best items there...

Sigh, another one of those overly hyped places that turned out to be a letdown. There are BETTER choices in Vegas, why pay $42 for a brunch at this mediocre one? My suggestion would be Wicked Spoon or the Buffet at Wynn and if you're willing to go a little of your way...definitely hit up Studio B buffet at the M Resort.
Check in on yelp to skip the line.  Lots of variety to choose from! Gelato is on poont

Last time we came they told us to wait 3 hrs and then closed the buffet right before we entered. Bad experience but decided to go for lunch instead. The wait was only 15 min. We gorged ourselves on crab legs and prime rib the entire 2 hours we were there. Champagne was included so we also drank up. My pants gonna pop. POP.

Going into this buffet, I'd heard that it was easily one of the best in Las Vegas, which is quite a recognition in this foodie city. I'd also heard that the line to get in was absolutely absurd and borderline not worth the wait. Luckily my date had a fast past, so we didn't have to wait in the almost 100 person line.

We came at dinner time where there were several categories of food with the most memorable being the seafood, American bbq, Mexican, Asian (sushi, Chinese, soups: udon, miso, pho, and ramen) and dessert. The bbq was my favorite with yummy meats and standard sides (mashed potatoes, vegetarian beans, and Mac n cheese). The chicken and waffles were good too. They have a taco person making fresh tacos, which were yummy. I tried their tamales and wasn't a big fan. Way too much masa and not enough filling. One of the small plates had very tender cuts of lamb that were probably my favorite meat. Desserts were beautifully presented and they had great homemade crepes (I had Nutella).

We also had all you can drink ($15 a person), but it was pretty whatever. No specialty cocktails and just your standard wines, beers, and sangria. 

Overall, I enjoyed the place, but I probably wouldn't go back due to the price and I would never wait in that line. Fast past or bust!

I waited in line for 3 hrs and all I thought was "really, that's the best you can do, caesar's?" Other than the fancy decor, the pretty plating, and the cute juice bottles, I was bored. The food was normal, the selection was bare, and the price is ridiculously expensive! Definitely a "one time, did that" kind of place. I really felt like I was paying for the atmosphere than the food, and for $50+, I'd rather not. I found myself get up only twice for more food. Meh.

This buffet is EXTREMELY expensive, BUT it's because they have seafood such as shrimp, oysters, crab legs, AND KING crab legs. Other than that, the buffet is pretty comparable to other buffets on the strip. In order to dine here, you have to check in these little kiosks. The hostess there is only for checking in and questions. The ticket it prints, gives you the estimated wait time and you can put in your number so it will notify you when to check in and actually wait in line. On the kiosk, it said it would text so that you had a confirmation and then again when your table was ready. I asked the hostess why I didn't get a confirmation text and she, a foreigner European lady, told me I have to wait for the text before I could talk to her. Okay, rude. However, when we finally sat down, my server was extremely nice and attentive. We obviously wanted to get our money worth so we went straight for the shrimp, oysters and king crab legs. King crab legs are served cold. REGULAR crab legs are served chilled or hot. I recommend hot because they salt the crab legs. With hot, they'll put it in a boiling pot of water to hear them up and then put them on your plate, this will rinse off more salt and you'll actually be able to taste the crab meat. After dining here, I only recommend coming here if you're going to eat the seafood. Everything else was average. But the four star rating is mainly for seafood and my server.

This is the worst dining experience I had during my California trip. I have no idea why so many people give more than 3 starts to this place. Are you guys crazy?  Start with the BBQ and grilling. The lamb is raw and the brisket are very dry. As to seafood, I have never had such stale oyster before even though I come from Boston. Did I see people say dim sum are yummy? Poor you, try some authentic Chinese dim sum please.  This place cost us 60 dollars per person and I won't be willing to have dinner unless the price is below 10.

I don't usually rave about the food in buffet, because it is hard to cook good food in bulk.  I was actually surprised how good the food
was for the price.  The seafood tasted fresh, they had a variety of dishes.  I thought the Chinese food & sushi was good.  The meat  dishes were ok but I think some were sitting for a while which made the dry.  The meats at the carving station was good.  The desserts was extremely good with a variation for all taste.  I would recommend this buffet.

The taxis are not lying when they are driving around the Las Vegas trip advertising Bacchanal Buffet as the #1 buffet in town. This is THE BEST buffet in Vegas, and probably on the West Coast. 

My boyfriend was skeptical about this buffet because prior to it becoming the Bacchanal Buffet, he claims there was a really bad buffet he had tried at Caesar's Palace. Honey, that was 3 years ago, lol. It reinvented itself, and Bacchanal was born in 2012. 

If you're worried about the price ($58/ person), I suggest you don't gamble, you don't drink, you don't go clubbing and save your $58, and eat here instead. It has an upscale environment like a club, minus the drunk people and having drinks spilled on top of you. Plus, you aren't losing money because this buffet claims to have over 500 food items and they are not exaggerating. 

And you don't have to doubt about the freshness of the food either; The seafood section of the buffet is filled with freshly caught fish, oysters, crab, etc. They are literally prying the oysters open while you're in line. It doesn't get any fresher than that. 

Just a little warning, because I didn't do this, but I ate way too much to my heart's content- MEANING, I wasn't able to enjoy the beautiful display of desserts in front of me. My boyfriend tried to feed me chocolate, but I just couldn't have anything anymore. 

We went on a Friday night, about 7pm, and the wait was 20 minutes... I was skeptical because the line was so long, but you tend to move pretty quickly because there are so many tables inside. 

*My margarita cost me $8 but it didn't taste like a margarita, lol *

4 hr wait?!?  Hell no. Purchased the $20 express line only to be disappointed by the food sooner than later.
