Yes, the selection is quite expansive, but the quality and taste were subpar for Vegas standards. Dry meats, sushi with higher-than-normal rice ratios, and a Reno-esque seafood station...no thank you. However, the cheese and charcuterie section--props to that. I will not be back. Will be at Wicked Spoon or the Buffet at the Wynn instead.

I finally got to stop at the famous Bacchanal Buffet. Yay! It was for Sunday brunch. I spent about $140 for my husband and I. $49 per person and $15 per person for unlimited mimosas. It's a beautiful, clean setup. The food was good but not amazing how I was expecting. I got to try a little of everything. I really liked the breakfast sausages, chilaquiles,and the wagyu beef roast and the creme brulee. Oh and our waiter was amazing! I wish I could remember his name but he kept those mimosas coming!! Lol also the mimosas where good quality no crazy headaches afterwards! I don't know if I'd come back here. I'd probably be at wicked spoon.

I would say it's one of the best buffets in town right now. If you want to eat on time be prepared to stand in line for about an hour. You will not be disappointed though. Just a tip, get a players card to get a discount.

Went during July 4th weekend so it was great crowd + great food and great drinks! Candice was the awesome manager that greeted us. She explained to me why we had to pay a little extra for the better food that they prepare for the 4th weekend. The food was outstanding and had dishes that you normally don't see in other buffets. Mimosas was outstanding! I would definitely go back again!

The fresh oysters on half shells & the sweet crab legs (cut in half so you don't need to crack them open) were what stood out to me the most. That and the all you can drink house wines & beer deal  for on only $22! (Please note the all you can drink is a separate charge from the cost of the buffet). I'm not normally a fan of crab legs at buffets but this place won me over! Everything else was between good/OK.

An extra star for their huge selection of food. The buffet spans out to another room which has all the Italian & Asian foods. 

One thing I wasn't too wowed over with was their dessert bar. I expected something grander with more yummy desserts. 

I'd definitely come back for oysters & crab legs! -and maybe the all you can drink!  

Tip: if you're not up for alcohol bingeing, order a pitcher of their perfectly made mojito.

This is by far my favorite buffet in Vegas. I've never been to a buffet that offers the eloquence and quality cuisine of a high end restaurant. Such high quality, it's unbelievable! The king crab legs made me feel vulnerable to its perfection, along with the beef ribs that made me feel as if I was dining with Lucille herself! The most profound buffet experience I have been to thus far.

I'd give this place 3.5 stars.  We had brunch today $59.99/person.  And if u want bottomless champagne u would have to pay additional of $24?It was a little higher than usual because of Memorial Day. The food was good the last time we came for dinner, but today wasn't so great.  The crab legs were kinda dry and overcook.  I saw a piece of black hair in the crab leg tray so I just stopped eating right there. Didn't  have a lot of selection at the sushi area maybe because it was brunch? I really liked the lobster bisque and kahula pork Benedict though. 

I would come back again but not on holidays and not for that price!

7 days in Vegas and I was here 4 times. 4 TIMES! With all the choices in Vegas, the frequency (and my newly expanded waistband) speak for itself.

After some major jet lag the bf and I woke up at the ungodly hour of 7 am on Sunday and headed to Caesars to check out the brunch spread. No wait and $100.00 later  we were in. 

Mimosas on the table immediately, mountains of crab legs, so many amazing choices I can't even remember them all. 2 hours of leisurely brunch and we didn't even make a dent in all of the options. Everything was delicious, hardly a dud in the bunch.

We ended up going to an additional breakfast and 2 lunches over the rest of the week, never with more than a 15 minute wait and always with friendly hellos from the cashiers and hostesses remembering us from the previous days. For me the brunch was the best with both breakfast and lunch options. However if you time it right on the weekdays you can definitely span both breakfast and lunch.

Another plus, every waiter/waitress encouraged us to stay as long as we wanted and to get our moneys worth. Usually I feel a bit rushed at buffets, but here it was the exact opposite. 

I was a Wicked Spoon freak before this trip. We went to the Wicked Spoon once and were so disappointed. It does not even compare to the Bacchanal on any level (food, service, setting, etc) But frankly many of the real, nice, sit down restaurants in don't even compare to this buffet!

Not saying you need to go 4 times but you must go to Bacchanal at least once when you are in Vegas!

I do not understand what's up with all these 4/5 star reviews.  Went in today for the holiday dinner menu.  I understand it's buffet, but given the price I was expecting something at least semi-decent.  Both waygu beef and prime rib were hard to chew.  Bone marrow wasn't impressive.  Gnocchi was just bland.  Dessert wasn't better than any other buffet and the selection was worse.  

Do yourself a favor and spend money on a nicer dinner.  We spent about the same at Bouchon and had a much better experience.

I went on my birthday. The wait was so long. When we paid the cashier wished me a happy birthday. That was nice that he realized. He called someone over and it felt like we were getting somewhat of special treatment. Our seater even went as far as to have someone make me an omelette even though breakfast was over. The food was amazing everything. There were so many options. Our waitress was kind and held a great conversation. She brought me a free mimosa for my birthday. The only thing I can complain about were the desserts. I felt that they were not good. They looked delicious but tasted weird. I did like that they offered sugar free options for people  who require that.  I didn't try them but I can't imagine them tasting any better. I left this place stuffed. You have to come here.

Of course I was expecting something grand after I read reviews about it online and asked around about it but It was a complete disappointment. It felt very unorganised and I am unsatisfied with the service. We put our name down on the kiosks provided at 8:30pm for dinner, it was roughly a 30min wait time through the online system, which was fine as the casino is a place worth exploring. When we first got the text we assumed we would get a table instantly or maybe within a couple of minutes of being there, however we had to queue up to pay first and mind you the queue was not a quick one. After paying the cashier at the counter told us the restaurant closes at 10:30pm which we thought would be fine, if we just came in and ate straight away BUT yet again there was a queue.... by the time we started queueing up it was already nearing 10. Absolutely terrible ! 
It was frustrating, staff were like machines. By the time 10pm rolled around there was still a line of people waiting to eat. When we finally got a seat, we asked one of the staff members about closing time and they said that they would push the close time to about 10:45pm as it was still busy. We haven't eaten since lunch and we couldn't wait to dig into the food. Imagine our disappointment when the food was just bland, tasteless and dry. The waitresses and chefs behind the bar were not happy to be there, and the mood in the restaurant seemed more like a fast food setting; get in and get out. Not worth the hype, very long wait times and way too expensive for the food they were serving. The food wasn't exceptionally great for the price, it just looks visually appealing. The only reason why I didn't give it a one star rating is because I've had worse food at a buffet, but it was dirt cheap. You get what you pay for and I certainly didn't get what I paid for.

Probably one of the most popular buffets in Vegas. Crazy amount of food options and the food is good...especially for buffet food. However they need to work out the logistics of the line and seating. As it currently stands you have to be placed on a waitlist to even begin waiting in line to pay, which was 50 minutes for us (at least this portion you don't need to be in line for, notification comes as a text). Then it took another 30-40 min in line to pay for the buffet. Probably another 20-30 minutes after payment to be seated. Probably wouldn't go back again until they work out the logistics. They need to just text when your table is ready, so you spend more time spending money at their casino and not getting pissed in line!

Bacchanal Buffet should actually get 5-stars for it's selection, quality, and insane amount of variety and food items, however service is still part of it so they lost a star for their cashiers. Bacchanal definitely has the largest amount of items to choose from out of any buffet that I've been to. It's definitely pricey for a buffet, but it's the best and top quality so it's worth it. Their food is always fresh and there are stations where you have items freshly prepared. Some buffets may have certain specialties or things they exclusively offer, but Bacchanal does everything well across the board.

The wait staff and chefs are friendly, efficient, and professional, however there was one cashier who was just not nice or welcoming so I couldn't give 5 stars. Other than that, it was a great experience!

Last Saturday, we waited about an hour and a half to get into Bacchanal. It's a bit pricy for a buffet but the food is pretty good. When we got in, it was already 2:30pm. There's food everywhere. There's a seafood station, a meat station, Asian food station, and pizza! There was also an area for just cheese!!! We caught the beginning of dinner and was able to eat a lot of their dinner items. There was sushi also but sushi was only ok. Here's a list of what I thought is good:
1.  lamb chops
2.  cocktail shrimp (these were jumbo sized shrimp!!)
3.  snow crab legs
4. clam bake
5. non-baked crème brulee 
6. mochi ice cream (sesame flavor was sooooo good!)

I cannot understand for the life of me why they would call this the Buffet of Buffets before you even get into the restaurant you have to place a reservation on a kiosk that they do not tell you or inform you on at all the wait time was high. The selection of food was plenty lots to choose from Meet station varies from lunch and dinner there is no chicken on brunch time service is very slow need to ask several times for additional service and drinks. The asian food was good. I liked that they had a taco station. A good majority of the food comes without season and needs to be extra seasoned your self.

renovation does a buffet good! caesar's palace went from being the worst buffet i've ever tried to being THE BEST!!!!!!! *round of applause everyone*

let's get straight to the point. the food is amazing! everything is super delish but here are my must haves! 
-BEEF BRISKET!! BEEF BRISKET!! BEEF BRISKET!! 
-prime rib
-crab legs (ASK FOR STEAMED CRAB LEGS) 
-wagu beef sliders
-tater tots 
-BREAD PUDDING!!!! 

i should note that this buffet is on the pricey side! lunch was $45 including tax! the wait can be long but my friends and i went at 12:00 and only waited an hour! not to shabby considering other buffet lines! 

Bon appétit!!! :)

This buffet definitely lives up to the hype. 

Line can get ridiculous (I'm talking 2+ hour wait) unless you want to pay extra money or just be lucky enough to be or have someone in your party be a platinum/diamond member and bypass it (Thanks June! :)) 

Although parties of 8 or more are automatically charged 18% gratuity, the service was beyond exceptional and unlike any other buffet we've been to.

Best part of the buffet is the dessert! I love the made-to-order crepes and the mochi ice cream. Unlimited. That's the way to go  

And if you find yourself not wanting to wait in line for that long you can walk to the buffet at the Bellagio, which nowadays has a shorter queue (and serves beef Wellington which bacchanal unfortunately lacks)

Where to begin.  So many items really not of value to mention any single one so focusing on the overall quality and experience.  Line is a more than bit long at peak times. Be prepared to wait.  Once in, the feast begins. Feast really doesn't even begin to describe it.  This is over the top to the nth degree. Great fun, great place.  Will return next time in Vegas.  This place lives up to the overall Caesar's big time atmosphere.

My boyfriend and I expected the wait to be extremely long but we went at 2:30 (after the lunch rush) this past Friday, and we were seated within 10 minutes! 

The selection was awesome, and we focused heavily on the fresh oysters and shrimp. The dessert area was amazing as well so save room! Crepes and shave ice made to order!

It was about $77 for two, plus we tipped the staff that were fairly attentive in cleaning up our used plates. You definitely pay for the variety in food ranging from American to Mexican, Japanese, Chinese and more.

i'm not sure how you can find out the prices without calling caesars palace. we paid $54.99 each for a non-holiday sunday dinner. lots of vegetarian options. crab legs were adequately defrosted. nigiri and roll sushi were passable--excellent by buffet standards. i think this has surpassed the wicked spoon in terms of the best vegas buffet, with bellagio and wynn close behind.

highlights:
mushroom polenta
beet salad...ok, hard to go wrong with this one
mochi ice cream...ditto
do it yourself congee, with all the toppings...dried pickled radish, 1000 year egg, fried garlic, wonton strips, green onions...the whole shebang! 

for those who care, the carving station included:
individual lamb chops in a sweet marinade
prime rib
brisket
chicken sausage
another type of sausage

bathroom was outside and fairly small--this was annoying.

Omg! Where do I start?! 
All of the food stations were kept clean and tastey. Coming in I didn't know what to expect, and well this buffet has so far raised the bar than of all of the other ones. All of there food stations were kept in tidy condition, and the food I ate was delicious. I couldn't think of one thing I didn't like. The highlight would be their seafood selection, which ranged from oysters to crab legs (warm & cold ones) to big delicious shrimp. All of the seafood was delicious. Now, the desserts were pretty great as well. Not only were there regular sweets but also sugar free ones, which was a great option. Sweets are always great and obviously delicious, but their macaroons were to die for. I've never been keen on macaroons, but they had me going back for some more. 
Highly recommend hitting this buffet up, it's a little on the pricey side, but sometimes you have to treat yo' self.

Wow!
I generally shy away from Las Vegas buffets, as they tend to be gluttonous feeding troughs. So I was reluctant when my friends wanted to go, but I am a team player, so I went anyway. I was glad I did.
First of all, the the line was VERY long, which scared me a little, as I imagined it was going to be an all-out free for all inside. 
Not so.
Inside, was a well though out, and well spread out seating arrangement. They could have sat twice as many people and just herded them through, but they exercised self control, and put together a comfortable seating arrangement that felt much more "restaurant" than buffet.
Next, the food was spread out in a vast expanse, that made getting your food comfortable and easy. I expected lines at the buffet, and people pushing each other, but only seating a certain number at a time kept the food lines short, comfortable, and relaxing.
Finally, the food was an overwhelming array of good quality ingredients and preparations, featuring a variety of cuisine cultures, and a spectacular selection of desserts.
All in all, they were going for a high-end experience, and they achieved it. I have always been a fan of brunch at the Verandah, and while it is still my favorite, Bacchanal was 5-Stars all the way.

This buffet was the best of the best.It was very pricey though.But I think it was worth it.The lamb rack was fantastic.I also liked the crab legs,they had oysters too.The service was great to.I liked the dessert it was very good.The stuff over at the carving table was awesome.The sausage was so good,the prime rib was so good.I would come back and recommend this for others.
Best Buffet in all of Las Vegas! You won't be disappointed! Best stations, best desserts! Period
Everything is so GOOD! Well worth every penny! Would have gave 5 stars but the waiters were spread a bit thin and had a little trouble keeping up.

The Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's is aptly named!!  For about $55 per person, this orgy of food is probably the best buffet in Vegas (although Rio's seafood buffet is a close second!).  Pace yourself - this place will challenge even the most sophisticated buffet strategies!  It is impossible to try even half of the offerings here.
     From the fried chicken served in a conical waffle to the dim sum station and the sushi counter - there truly is everything in the way of gastronomical excess.  Some highlights were the brisket - the Alaskan King Crab Legs, the raw oysters, and the sausage, salami, capicola, and cheese counter.  There were literally over 500 different dishes (I asked)!!
     The dessert counters were stocked with all of the usual suspects and included several sugar free options as well.  The best item on the dessert fare were the dipped strawberries.  These fresh, sweet, and huge (as big as your fist) strawberries were dipped in chocolate.  A stellar meal!!

Went on a Sunday night at 7pm and there was an 1hr wait to pay. Was with a big group of 13 and was told that big groups are rare and usually get seated pretty quickly. After paying, we only waited another 10 minutes before getting seated (albeit in 2 tables but we're not complaining).

I was treated to buffet so I didn't feel the sting of the $51 a head cost! Here are some my observations:

Best!:  
-  by far the best food in this buffet can be found at the meat station! The highlight was the beef brisket - so smokey in flavour and juicy! 
-  fried chicken was deliciously seasoned and not dry
- yelp tipped me about the souffle at the dessert station (thank you!) and the chocolate souffle was amaaaazzzinnggg. Done perfectly, not too sweet. I don't think many people knew to order it as it wasn't advertised anywhere. I also tried the banana one but it was too sweet for me.  

OK:
- I enjoyed the spicy salmon sashimi but they only served that for the first round and changed to just plain salmon sashimi afterwards
- boiled king crab leg. I always find it better warmed up than cold and this was warmed in a salt bath.

Skip:
- yes, there's unlimited oysters... BUT be warned that they taste pretty awful. It's watery and just lacks any kind of flavour
- dessert was pretty lack luster. It was bland and just has a sugar taste to it, not much else.  Just go ahead and stick to the gelato and the souffle. I also heard that the crepes were good, but I didn't have any

I was at Wicked the night before and I must say that Bacchanal has more selections, hands down. Food quality was a bit better at Bacchanal as well but compared to buffets I have had in Macao, it's still has a long way to go. I would come back to Bacchanal next time I'm in Vegas before other similar establishments around town.
So much high end food and delicious desserts. Its one of the best buffets I've had in Vegas, and i have had them all.
Best buffet on the planet. Very high priced so we only eat here on special occasions but we are never disappointed.  Great selection, amazingly large amount of different styles including seafood.

After visiting Vegas 4 times, I was finally dragged here by one of my girlfriends on my recent trip. I've heard really good things about this buffet, so naturally I'd be really inclined to go try. Needless to say, I was very disappointed in the food. The food is endless, and is split from all different parts of the world. From dimsum to Italian to Mexican to seafood. You name it, they probably have it. The presentation is beautiful! The most disappointing thing was that none of the food was hot. At first I thought, maybe it was me until one of the other girls at the table mentioned the same thing. On top of cold food, the flavor of most of the food was bland. You'd think for the amount of money spent on the buffet, the food would be better. I've had other buffets in Vegas, and sadly enough this wasn't the best, like what everyone makes it to be. So long story short, I waited for the hot pizza to come out the oven, and ate pizza... 

On the other hand, the staff was very nice and very attentive for it being so busy. It's unfortunate that I won't be returning back here... unless it's again my own free will!

We drove to Las Vegas from LA to catch a cirque de soleil show and wanted to check out the buffet as it is rated one of the best in Vegas.

We arrived at 4pm and the waiting time is 80 minutes. To catch the show at 7 we decided to purchase the fast pass (25/person). When we get the bill, we were charged 205.65 for two. Obviously their holiday dinner price go beyond the advertised 57.99/person on their website. 

They have multiple stations for Asian food, Latin food, cot and hot seafood. And with no doubt you will find the regular buffet food aka salad, fried chicken, grilled meat, and TONS of desserts. 

My personal favorite is the boiled crab leg, but very juicy and sweet, it's satisfying to crack it and take the whole leg out. Tacos are not bad. It's also nice to finish the meal with gelato and sugar free dessert.

In general, I think this is a good place for seafood and dessert. But try not to visit on a holiday or their peak time, and definitely no need to purchase the fast pass.

Omg I have been wanting to try this place for a year after I didn't get to the first time I was in Vegas. My eyes about rolled back and had a foodgasm when I bit into the truffled scalloped potatoes, it was seriously so damn delicious along with countless other items. Also one of the most beautiful restaurants. Buffets usually don't look as elegant as this place. Just beautiful. Like all buffets a few items were blah, some items are just beautifully plated. I was very upset and disappointed that I was way too full to try everything I wanted. That won't be the last time I go there. I will be back! Just so delicious. That's all I can really say. And omg the mini desserts were exquisite! I did not have a chance to try the wonderful gelatos:( and I grabbed a fresh juice but forgot it in the counter so that was another shame! Just amazing, I can't stop raving about it!

Best Buffet in Vegas. Crab legs that aren't salty, plump cocktail shrimp, amazing meat station, and all sorts of small plate dishes. The Asian section is awesome with dimsum, crispy duck and a noodle station. Their udon and ramen broth is seriously really good! 
Dessert station is good and the crepes are amazing! 

I took off 1 star because service is always on and off every time we go. Sometimes its really amazing and sometimes it isn't. We went this last weekend, and our server barely came to clear dishes and refill drinks. I had to wave and glare which I really hate doing to get their attention to refill our drinks and clear our plates. Other than that we always look forward coming to Bacchanal when we can.

Oh k.... so everyone that I know or met here at Vegas said to come and try Bacchanal. It's the buffet you must try. Well I totally regret spending my time and money there. Well a friend said to get in faster, to use Groupon, which was a really great deal. So my boyfriend and I go, feeling excited because we are passing the 2-3hr wait line. Right when we get to where you pay, they already have an attitude towards us showing our Groupon ticket. I was telling my boyfriend, it's oh k they are just having a super rush hour. So now we are in another line to get a table inside and we are up in front. The place looked amazing with all the seafood up from, the layout was great. Now they take us and the couple behind us to our tables. We are passing the tables up front where it's beautiful lit by the sunlight coming from the huge windows!! We come to a table there and the host sits the couple that was behind us!! I was so ecstatic to just be there that I didn't think must by it(my boyfriend did noticed). So the host continues to walk us to a side room in the back where it's darker and less servers. Once we sat down we started our lunch, which the food was cold or just bland. Nothing really impressive that we don't get at anywhere else. Really the only good thing was kinda worth it was the desserts. But other then that and them putting us to the back because I'm guessing we were not Caucasian. Which now, you can tell who they sit in the back of the restaurant. I would not recommend this place to any of my family or friends. Crappy part is, we were going to make this our anniversary place but Vegas has so much more to offer that we can find somewhere else. I wouldn't even give them any star rating, it was so disappointing!!!

Came back for the second time because the first time was too great of an eating experience! If you love variety and sweets, this is the perfect buffet to indulge into! There is a limit of 2 hours however to eat as much as you can! The quality of the food is amazing and service is spot on!

Went there this morning with zero wait time - make sure you go before 11 am to avoid the line! By far the best buffet I had in Vegas. It has the largest selections and the ambience is great. Highly recommend it!

Great food, but the wait destroyed the experience for me.  Just to get in, the line was 90 minutes, but then I had to wait another 20 minutes in the seafood line.  For $50 per person, i would have expected better.

This was our first time to visit the buffet.  My impression was a good one.  We did have to wait in line a bit, but it is worth the wait.
My first suggestion is to go through and look at all the food first.  Have a plan of attack.  You can't eat it all so be selective on what you select.  I wanted crab legs, and if u didn't scope it out, you wouldn't know that they are in two places.
King crabs (cold) on one end and hot snows on the other end.
Another suggestion is to get the $15 drink special.  It is all the champagne, wine you can drink. Might be other selections but I don't remember.
They even had sushi, which wasn't too bad, but not the worst.
Service was good.
Quality of meat was also good.
Steamship round of beef, prime rib, and roast beef, were just a few.  Lots of good selections if u are vegetarian too.
Desserts were impressive and presented nicely.  They also have a gelato bar and sorbet.
Desserts are small, but I assume they know you will want more than one.
We went on a Thursday night while CES was there, which I assume that was why the line was long.
Overall a good selection of seafood, tons of meat, tacos, Italian dishes, and homemade crepes for desserts.
I was happy when I left, and thought I would be back next year during CES.
Enjoy!

Round two! came here for my birthday and I thought the food this time around was much better during the Christmas weekend. Thinking that it would be crowded because of CES, but by surprised there was no line at all, so i think that made the experience a bit better. Then the price per person was much cheaper than holiday price. 

The crablegs again were just snow crabs -- it wasn't any better. The crablegs were all so skinny and NOT meaty at all. 

This time the cocktail shrimps tasted good, nice big plump shrimps. All other dishes were good as well as the dessert bar. The dessert bar is always amazing; my favorite part of the buffet. 

i would only visit Bacchanal during off peak season.

I have been to Vegas many times. This is hands down one of the best buffets I ever went to if not the best ever. Whoever gives this place anything other than 5 stars is out of their mind. Every time I go to Vegas I always make sure to go there. I went there with many friends, family, colleagues and every single person had nothing negative to say and will confirm it's one of the best dining experiences ever. Check this place out you will not be disappointed.

Absolutely the best Buffett I have ever been to! The food was all top notch and fresh! Absolutely worth the $45 per person price tag! The wait was a little long (we waited about a hour) but let me tell you it was totally worth it! I loved the fresh juices! I also loved how fresh everything was to the seafood to the pizzas and pasta dishes to everything in between! And yes all you yelpers the truffle potato dish was friggin awesome! I did however knock off a star because the crabs were very fishy and half of the items are not labeled! Is like to know what I'm eating, but that's not going to stop me from coming back! FYI you can pay $15 extra pp and skip the lines and be put in the express line which is a 15 min wait vs. 2 hour wait!
I was in HEAVEN! Loved everything I put on my plate! Wish they had more dessert selections
What is selection of good food. Fresh and perfectly cooked. This is definitely the best buffet in Vegas and the best buffet I have ever experienced. This is a must try

Wow I paid 110 on Easter morning for old food. The hollandaise sauce on the Benedict was horrible. The lobster pot pie would have been good if it was hot. The only good thing was the fresh cut ham. I have a major sweet tooth and the desserts were very mediocre. Should have gone to a sit down restaurant and gotten a fresh meal. Will not be back.

Came here with my mom and aunt for Sunday brunch.  We've already been to the The Buffet at Wynn for brunch and Cravings at The Mirage for dinner.


From a vegetarian standpoint the buffet was the best.  The cheese selection was the best, the fruit and desserts had more variety.  The Asian, Italian, and Mexican statins also beat the other buffets.

My aunt eats meat and seafood, and she said the seafood was really good as well as the carving station.  

I'll have to come back the next time we are are in Vegas

Pretty good buffet, but for the price, I expected better. Food in the asian section were all old and nasty. The Mexican section had some pretty tasty selections, same with American section.  I really liked the pork belly mini bites. Desserts were alright. Cold seafoods were okay...tasty with drawn butter. I'd probably go back if the group wants to eat here, otherwise, I'll pass.

Lots of choices, for the most part good food. Our service was horrible so it didn't make the experience as great. Had to wait 10 minutes for my second mimosa and after waiting 25 minutes for my third I gave up and we left. Great desserts, and meats, crappy pizza and OK seafood

Went for the holiday dinner for the first time at Bacchanal Buffet due to hearing all the hype.

The ticket system says they'll reserve you a time to come back, and they'll text you. Minimum wait time was 2-3 hours when we went, but expect to wait for another hour in line once you've been texted.

The advertised "King Crab" legs were simply snow crabs, which was much lower quality. Oysters ran out quick and a bunch of people were being sent back and forth between stations, a lot of guests were complaining to staff about this.

The Mexican station had ice cold tacos and other soggy  plates, which no one bringing out fresh dishes.

Sushi consisted of hard rice and stale tasting fish for the nigriri.

I would advise all to stay away from the "Vietnamese Pho" and Udon, as both smelled extremely foul and toxic, similar to industrial chemicals. I didn't think either soup bases can turn out so bad.

Not worth the $60 per person, very few items were edible, let alone "good".

I've tried the Wicked Spoon, but Caesar's buffet is now my preferred. The service was wonderful and there was no line when we went (1:30pm) on Monday for platinum member or above. The food was good and selection was huge including wagu beef. They have sections that vary from Italian and Asian to American and seafood. They have an island sector in the middle dedicated to desserts. One star off for charging my 7yrs daughter half price (she only ate two slices of pizza and some shaved ice). Overall, there is something everyone would like.

One of the best buffets in Vegas. Everything was pretty much up to par but the real treats are listed below: 

Guava juice (Mexican aisle) - chilled in little milk bottles
Oysters - fresh and sweet 
Boiled crab legs - hot on the spot ask for as much as you want
Grilled scallops 
Lamb chops - melt in your mouth (get two at least)
Boiled shrimp with cocktail sauce (the cocktail sauce has a good horseradish kick)
Lime basil icecream! Damnnnnnn bomb!
Cheese and meats (Spanish tapas) 

This place is a must. I think pretty much everything I've had was great but I had to lay low on carbs so that I wouldn't get full too fast. The selection was so huge I don't think I even tried half of the selection they offered. 

The sections are broken up into Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Italian, American, etc. just thinking about this place makes me hungry for more. 

The service is great and fast. 

Negative- you will be waiting at least 2 hours!!! The 1 hour on the ticket stub is just the first part. When they text you to return and line up you will be waiting another hour at least. So make sure you come early and not starving. Also we waited on a Sunday just imagine the chaos on a Friday and a Saturday. 

But when you are in... It's like the gates of heaven... Completely worth it lol

A month after the grand opening Elite event, I'm finally back at the scene of the crime for my official non-event review. Feel free to refer to my first review (https://www.yelp.com/biz/elite-grand-opening-feast-bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas#hrid:HtoQJRMMYxheSWyYYU_3XA) for the "before" comparison.

With my mom in town, I knew I had to take her to the latest Vegas hot spot. It was her first experience here and my first chance to see if the honeymoon period had worn off. The strategy was too obvious: go for lunch and stick around until the dinner menu transition. It actually worked too well since the wait only took 45 minutes starting from 1 pm. The weekday lunch price, which might or might not have included a slight players card discount, was $26.99. They've definitely raised the cost since opening week.

After a circumnavigation of the dessert island, we were seated at a somewhat awkward table next to one of the glass dividers. It actually felt like my chair was in the middle of an obvious walkway. It wasn't that distracting for me, but I did have people try to walk around me sometimes. Oh, and while I'm on the atmosphere, it was dark because the light above us had burned out, but I think that all the awesome light fixtures are above bigger tables anyway. And the music was... well, lounge-y and loud enough to be heard but not distracting.

I actually ended up trying a lot of different foods than in my last trip, and there were some real treats this time. The fish in the fish and chips basket was so fluffy and yummy. The lobster corn bisque was so good that I could eat it all day (but I only had two). The ramen was good enough that I found myself slurping up the broth, which clearly violates the general buffet principle of not consuming too much liquid. The poke salad was respectable for a buffet. The beef brisket didn't taste so strange this time, especially after cutting off the outer layer. The jumbo shrimp cocktail was solid, and the king crab legs (dinner menu) were great and came pre-steamed (no wait). Although the steaming was far from thorough, I enjoyed cold and warm crab meat alike.

Out of the desserts, the top-it-yourself crepe was so good that I'm not sure why I skipped it the first time. I can't recall any other buffets with so much fresh fruit (sliced strawberries, raspberries, blueberries, blackberries, and possibly a chance to do something which those bananas if you want) at the crepe station. With the cream and choice of syrups, you can probably just eat crepes all dessert long. The chocolate creme brulee was pretty thick and lived up to its billing as chocolate, although the brulee left a bit to be desired. I also tried new ice cream flavors this time: the aztec chocolate was strangest with its cinnamon and spiciness, the fig and basalmic was pleasantly sweet (although I'm not sure where the balsamic went), and the brown butter caramel was just so rich and creamy (my favorite so far).

Not everything worked though, and that's fine. That's why you read Yelp to see what to avoid, or else sample modestly so you can cut your losses. I thought that the prime rib had too much inedible stringiness, the ceviche and gazpacho were too strong in a bad way, the crab croquettes and the italian meatballs were just okay, and the blackberry panna cotta was not as good as last time. Also strangely lacking were some of the desserts that I remember from my first visit, including a green tea mousse - maybe it's only brought out later at night?

I haven't been to all the other popular buffets too recently, but Bacchanal is still probably the best buffet in Vegas. If you want to have a buffet some time this year, choose this one.

This is the first buffet I have ever visited in Las Vegas (on about my 8th trip).  So, maybe I should be more impressed, but it was just ok.

We got there just before 10am.  Go before checkout time.  We did not wait in a line.  When we left at about 11:20 there were about 150 people in line.

Our server didn't seem that busy but also didn't come around very often.  She always cleared my plate when I didn't want her to but wasn't there to give me more champagne.

The selections were good.  I am not a big eater really, but there was a ton of variety.  Fill up on meats, fruits, and eggs before you hit those filling carbs!  The desserts area was awesome.  Tons of mini pastries, cheesecakes, tortes, etc.

There were some lunch-type items already at 10am.

I would go here again if I was staying at Caesar's, but I think my breakfast at Central (in the lobby) was better.

I'll start by saying the food here was fine. However, I didn't enjoy my meal and felt that I didn't get a good value. The day before, I ate at Crave which is another buffet in Vegas. Nothing I had at Bacchanal was as good as Crave and that definitely includes the services of the staff. Indeed, service was the #1 issue here at Bacchanal. We purchased VIP tickets but we observed people in the general admission getting served first. After paying, they stuck us in the same line to be seated at general admission. I felt that I had been cheated on paying for VIP. We waited and waited in the line for parties of 2 while parties of 3 and more came and went. Still we waited. I was thinking "Wow. They must really be full. This line hasn't budged for 10 minutes." Finally we get seated and I see about 40 empty tables. Why did they keep us standing like cattle when there were so many tables available? Regardless, I'll take the less expensive Crave over Bacchanal any day.

This is one of the best buffets in Vegas!  Make sure you do a lap before you start to fill up your plate because it is bigger than you think it is.  My favorite part is the dessert island full of chocolate and crazy ice cream flavors!

This buffet is at an entirely different level from anything you could imagine. The buffet is set up by different types of cuisine and the options are endless. I spent most of my time in the seafood and Asian section where I dined on crab claws and dim sum. 

Everything is super fresh and the attention to detail is insane.
I was helped by Milka & Mahyar! Both of them were such a delight, loved every minute :)!

Honestly, I felt like this place decided to bring every single type of food and just dump it in one location. Seafood, American comfort food, Spanish food, European food, Asian food....and then desserts. I got full way too quickly, but like any buffet, I think the quality of the food was just okay. Some of the fish were over cooked, salty soups...just to name a couple problems. But it's a buffet. Of course the quality isn't going to be top-tiered. I have to say that I was definitely satisfied, but frankly won't be coming back again since it's overly priced for the food they serve. Good first time experience in a gourmet buffet though!

The Buffet is good but greatly overpriced. It is of course better then the standard buffets and features an enormous variety of foods from all over the world. But I still believe the price are not justified.
Not worth the fame. Seafood is not fresh. It only has several kinds of sushi. Very dissappointed. Although the desser is good.

Best buffet in Vegas hands down. Which is saying a lot since there's a lot of competition. It's pricy - so I figured that its more of  trying it at least once. 

The wife and I enjoyed the variety and quality of most of the food. Keep in mind it's a buffet so don't go in thinking your getting 5 star restaurant quality and you'll enjoy. 

Overall a solid 4.0

I found this buffet a little overrated for the price that was charged.  Yes there were some excellent items but like many other reviewers have said, they have cut some corners.

In my opinion, the best items are the general tsao chicken, Peking duck, bone marrow, brisket, waygu beef, shrimp, crab, mussels, smoked salmon, egg tarts and many of the desserts.

Items that were disappointments included oysters, crawfish, watermelon salad, and sushi.

It was a pretty good buffet but it would be better if the prices weren't so high.

Really THE best buffet in Vegas.  Expensive, to be sure, but worth doing at least once in your life.  The prime rib was excellent when we went - as good as any steakhouse.  Go to the italian section for hot king crab legs.  And the desert section.... wow.
Still my favorite buffet in Vegas. It's on the pricey side compared to the other Vegas buffets but the quality of the food and the atmosphere is worth the up charge.

The best buffet I've ever been to. There, I said it!!! 

Given the quality and the variety of food offered, I think the cost is at an affordable price point. 45$ for Sunday through Thursday and 50$ for Friday and Saturday. The only catch is that it's almost ALWAYS busy, so you'd need to coordinate making it so that you're not caught in the long lines of what looks like a wait for the hottest night club entrance. They DO have the option to cut lines with an additional fee of 45$pp, which to us was worth as the wait time was close to 90 minutes. Probably also need to note that we were H A N G R Y. 

When you walk in, the aisle of food is presented on your left and honestly, I thought there was no end :') I was in heaven. Before you make your Bacchanal visit, be sure to Youtube some "How To Be Successful at a Buffet" hacks and know how to strategize when you plate your meal! Definitely go straight for the seafood (i.e. monster oysters, cold and steamed snow crab legs, salmon poke, shrimp ceviche, etc.) and the meats!!! (i.e. prime rib steak). They have refreshments and many, many sauces. The coolest thing was seeing cuisines from different cultures and my Chinese boyfriend was highly impressed by the execution in their dumplings and crispy pork. 

My favorite part would have to be the dessert section because the feeling is similar to that of walking into a French patisserie and being able to collect ALL the aesthetically beautiful and delicious pastries and cakes - without being judged. They have unique options like matcha-chocolate covered strawberries and mochi ice-cream. Don't worry, you also have your traditional classics like gelato, cheesecake and brownies. 

I think we were there for a solid two hours and even then, I kept hearing myself say, "I'm never leaving". And now that I'm back home, all I'm thinking is, "When can I go back" *cries profusely*

Oh yes, and I recommend.

Pretty good buffet overall. Waiting system where you put your number in to get a text when there's a free table is nice , and on this Friday night we were able to get in right away even though the machines said 55 min. Very diverse selection of food and all of it is pretty well made and fresh. Seating is a little cramped, almost reminded me of a cafeteria or dining hall, which is not what you want when you're paying $54 bucks a person. Other the potential wait times and the seating arrangments, a-ok!

Cut to order Prime Rib all day! 

One of the better buffets in Vegas. 

Pros: good variety of choices of food genre: Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, middle eastern, etc. 
Excellent dessert station. Maybe the best in Vegas. 

Cons: lines for the taco station and the seafood station are way too long. The sushi could have been better too.

This is probably the best buffet. It has a large variety of food & the presentation of the food was beautiful. It is a long wait to get in but it just gives you time to look at the shops. The only thing I didn't like that I've never experienced before at a restaurant was this guy taking pictures of everyone that came in & asked if they'd buy the picture. Nothing I wasn't used to living in Vegas but it was the only bad thing about it.

I visited Bacchanal over Memorial weekend and found the lines to get food were quite long. This was a good buffet, among the best in Las Vegas, such as the Wynn and Wicked Spoon. The decor was cute. After reading such great reviews, I expected a lot more. It didn't blow my socks off, but I thought it wasn't bad. One thing I definitely crave from here are the glazed sweet potato tots.

Super disappointed! There was no line at 5pm the Friday before July 4th so we decided to have an early bird dinner. Maybe I psyched myself up too much before arriving in Vegas? There was no cute little bottled juices (they only serve them during breakfast now, I found out). Out of all the food in the buffet, my favorites were the braised short rib cooked in root beer or regular beer, and the korean short ribs! The cheese pizza was ok. The seafood was ok. The chinese food was bland. I enjoyed the desserts...notably the gelato and the crepes. It was so not worth the $70 tab per person! Should've listened to my coworker and went to the Bellagio buffet.

Oh, and because we gave a nice tip PRIOR to going in, the waitress was very attentive.

After Reading this was the Number one place for buffet in the whole of the usa, our expectations were maybe a bit too high. Yes it's big. Is it worth the 2.5 hour wait... That depends. The Mexican food lady is great. If you are Asian I guess the seafood is ok. The salad is not too bad. The rest could use a bit more refinement.

It really is the best buffet in Vegas. We got a special VIP treatment from the staff and especially Chef Niko which was truly a dream come true. Such a large variety of high quality food. Everything from amazing seafood to an excellent carving station to a huge array of dim sum, sushi, and Asian noodles. I loved that many of the dishes were plated as nice individual plates rather than a large tray. The attention to detail was spot on and everything was delicious. My favorites were the lamb t-bone and all of the desserts. If you're planning on coming make sure you have an empty stomach because you'll want to try everything. 

The service was phenomenal; everyone was very friendly and attentive. Literally every time I went to get food, when I came back to the table my dirty plates were taken away. This has probably been one of the best dining experiences I've ever had and I am not exaggerating. 

I came with a group of friends from school and I can speak for everyone that we all had the time of our lives and had a truly memorable experience and meal. I will definitely be coming back here in the future when I'm in Vegas again. 

I lastly want to just give a special thank you again to Mr. Cory Johnson, Chef Niko, and all of the amazing staff at Bacchanal and Caesar's Palace. You have all been extremely hospitable and made this a truly memorable experience for us all.

My favorite place to go to in Vegas! Has a huge variety of food and it's so classy inside. The wait time can be crazy so give yourself enough time if you have plans for after dinner. The dessert section is amazing it has anything you can think of! They have a street taco section. They have sushi, steak, crab, shrimp!

I give three stars, my friend I ate with gives four.  Its definitely not worth the wait, but the food is good average for Vegas buffets.  However, in my opinion, the Wynn buffet and the Wicked Spoon are better with less wait and better service.  I put this a little above the Aria buffet but only because of the boiled crab legs.

We waited the hour and a half after checking in like were were told.  After that we were told it would be 20-30 minutes to get a table.  It ended up being over an hour after that.  Definitely not worth it.  

We heard it was good but not worth the wait or money.  I'm glad we went so we don't have to go back but if I had to do it again, I would have gone back to Joel Robuchon or if I wanted a buffet, to go the Wynn.  

The pros are the crab legs which were boiled hot and there is no line for.  The lamb is good.  The ramen broth is good.  They have this soft pork dish that is also very good.  Nice gelato bar.

The cons are avoid the prime rib and sushi.  Also notable, unlike other Vegas buffets, they don't have small dishes for the soy sauce and wasabi for the sushi so it goes all over your heated plate.  Yes heated plates for sushi.  The sushi was the kind of warmed over sushi you get at places with no Asian customers.  The blue cheese was inedible.  

Also, the service was very poor.  They are so crowded that there is disorganization in the line where the VIP's merge with the common folk paying.  There was an incredible b@#$#! at the first cashier for the common people.  I get that her shift is over and wants to go home, but really the management should have made her bow out before her shift was over so she wouldn't have a pissy attitude.  I had to stand in front of one of the cashiers to pay because they try to ignore seeing you despite you standing in front of them.  They are so busy they don't care if you leave.  

When we got to our table, the server took our drink order.  Then 10 minutes later he asked again.  The drinks didn't arrive for 25 minutes.  In the meantime I flagged over the server from the other section who was busting his butt and I tipped him because he got our drinks right away.  I think his name was Michael and he was really good.  

You pay this much and wait so long at least you should get good service.

But essentially a two hour and a half wait is not worth tough prime rib and a taco bar.

Edit: I forgot to add that the rest of the night through the night my friend and I were really thirsty.  I think I had five cups of water that night.  I haven't had that problem at any other buffet although I'm sure all use MSG.

Edit 2: I mentioned that the first cashier was a b@#@!@! and the second I had to stand in front of to get his attention.  In many ways the workers are overwhelmed with mad people waiting too long.  I saw one VIP blow up for five minutes on how long he was waiting and made a scene and was expecting them to call security but you can't do that to the whales.  But you know I go to Vegas to relax and have fun and that kind of bad energy or karma or atmosphere is really a downer.  I would avoid this place until it gets less popular and the wait isn't as long.
Majorly blah! If quality was better maybe but, I just won't be coming here anymore! Shit was whack!

This is our favorite buffet on the strip. We've been coming back time and time again. The wait is TERRIBLE, but recently they've put up kiosks to "shorten" the wait time. It's a good idea but not well implemented since you can just sign in there and start to wait in the line. 

Once you're tired and hungry from standing for over an hour and almost ready to murder someone. The friendly staff shows you to your table and takes drink orders. As you spend your last bit of energy sprinting to the food line. You're welcome by an abundant assortment of options ranging from Chinese dishes, cold cuts, soups, Mexican food to seafood. 

Unfortunately for your shrunken stomach and overall health, everything taste great. You'd end up eating 3x the amount you should. Then towards your dismay, you'd discover the amazing desert section with all kinds of delicious, sweet confections that if you did a blood sugar test, your doctor would think you just got diabetes.

Overall great place to eat if you can manage the marathon wait.
Come hungry! It's amazing. Service can be slow due to large parties.

HOLIDAY/CHRISTMAS DINNER REVIEW

I can't believe we spent almost an entire day (Christmas Day!) at Caesar's Palace waiting for Bacchanal Buffet. 

Ok, to be fair- we got there early (~10:30AM) and got an early ticket of 12:00PM (!!) to come back. We had actually anticipated a worse wait (we didn't know that we'd be coming back at 12:00PM to line up...) so we decided to cancel (what a mistake that was) and try to go closer to 3-4PM. So we decided to try again- got a ticket at 10:50AM for my friend (return time: 1:04PM) and then again at 11:20AM for a return time of 3:25PM (crazy how much a 30 min difference can make). We came back at 3:25PM and entered the queue, and we ended up waiting an additional 2.5 hours before we got seated around 6PM. (Some people who mistakenly got in the queue without a ticket at 3:30PM got tickets that told them to come back at 10PM... Which is when the buffet closes. Just to give you an idea of how bad the line was).

My main criticism is that they don't put any effort in clarifying how the process works for this particular buffet. For most buffets, people show up, people enter the queue, and expect to wait a certain amount and eat when they make it through the queue. For Bacchanal, you line up for an electronic kiosk, then get an electronic ticket telling you to come back at a certain time, THEN you queue up, THEN you pay and get seated. Somewhere in that process, someone is supposed to check off on your ticket but I did not observe any consistent check-in process (my sister walked up to the lady to check-in separately). There are no banner of any sort explaining this process so you also end up having a number of people just entering the queue and facing the bouncer-type guy who asks to see their ticket. Or they're never confronted and actually make it through the line. 

(PS: If the electronic kiosk does not give you a physical ticket, try to go into another kiosk and get one. On the physical ticket, it states that you MUST present your ticket in order to enter the queue.)

By the way, apparently some people were asking if they could pay extra to get to the front of the line. They were told that this would not possible on that day. (Seriously, is this a common practice at buffets? SERIOUSLY?)

Now onto the service and the food. Our poor waitress was definitely tried and showing it. She was lugging stacks of plates- their plates are really heavy. We were stacking a few plates to make more room but two/three plates were quite heavy! She warmed up to us a lot after we complimented her strength and asked her how she was doing- basically showing patience and not being rude/impatient. 

Food-wise- pretty decent but nothing that justified the $70+tax/person price for the holiday buffet. Yes, they had unlimited crab legs (my parents said they were ok). Yes, they had unlimited raw oysters (not even properly shucked, btw- I had to use my fork to actual separate the oyster from shell). Yes they had bone marrow (it was ok) and a ton of other items. But most of the food was just ok, and after a long wait and high price, "ok" was not adequate. I will say my favorite item was probably the wild mushroom soup, but other than that I can't even think about what else stood out. The dessert section was extensive: I did like that they had a Thai tea boba drink. The boba was surprisingly soft and the taste was pretty faithful for a non-Asian restaurant. 

Overall, not worth the wait, not worth the price, and not worth the confusion that their system generates. 1/5.

I come here for the crab legs. They steam it right in front of you. Theyre so fat and juicy too. Just the crab legs alone is worth the price. They also offer ramen and pho cooked to order. Impressive.

Back again, and it was as good as I remembered!  Amazing hot and cold crab legs, as well as a host of additional seafood delicacies!  Try the Mushroom Truffle Soup, Sweet Potato Tots and Lobster Chowder before you fill up on anything else!  Desserts stand outs were the Crème Brulee, Caramel Cheesecake Cake Pop, Cheesecake Gelato, and Macaroons!

The service was even better than last time, with an exceptionally helpful waiter bringing the guys additional plates of crab legs, so they didn't even have to leave their seat!  We only waited about 30 minutes on a Friday night.  Bonus, there's a cute bar just behind the line that comps your drinks if you play the video poker games at the bar!

I'm not sure if it was because it was July 4th weekend, but the value was just not there at all. It cost us $88 a person after tax+tip and a 45 minute wait to get in. Waitress / Waiter service was good.

After you get in, more lines (plural) to get food! All stations except the cheap Chinese food station had long lines.

The good food:
-Bone marrow bones (hard to mess up)
-Rib roast (hard to mess up)
-Snow Crab legs and butter (hard to mess up)
-Dessert - crepes, gelato, macarons (super long lines for dessert)
-Pho (waited ~10 minutes for pho OR ramen, but the noodle soup guy was taking his sweet time with everything, so I just tried my friend's pho)

The okay food:
-Lobster rolls (the only lobster present in the buffet are the shreds in these buns)

The bad food:
-Sushi (may have been spoiled; REALLY BAD fish for an $88 buffet and kinda ruined my appetite)

I would have been satisfied if I paid $40-50 total for this buffet. At this price point (most I've ever paid pp for a meal), I was very disappointed with the quality and variety.

Fast check in service :)
Best all you can eat in Las Vegas.
Always awesome when I come here. The steamed crab legs are sooooo good. It's my favorite. I don't usually make room for dessert but I do when I come here. Yum!

Bonjour CP

I am SPEECHLESS! Superbe is the word that is in  orde..

I only have one Disappointment ! Your greeters the Hosr..I expected them to be a little bit more pleasant and charming and inviting..I found  the woman who seated me a middle aged woman .To be a little bit how do I say slightly rude.

But once you get past the host desk. You're in a wonderland brunch experience.

I shall be back next month to continue this journey of this:Culinary BRUNCH  Experience.

We had really high hopes for this Buffett based on all of the reviews. Unfortunately it was ok and not what was expected with the $59.99 per person dinner price tag.

We went on Saturday at 5pm hoping to skip some line as we've read. It took an hour from entering the line to being seated. And it's just that a line, no seats, no entertainment, nothing to drink.

We also paid the $15 pp unlimited drinks. Originally thinking this could be a good deal. No! The wine was horrible. 

Now to the food

Pros
Dessert station - gelato!
Crab legs
Dim sum station 
Prime rib station

Cons
A lot of the food was lukewarm to cold
Only snow crab was available even though they advertised king crab
Service was slow! Which because you tip on entering may be the problem.
SLOW BUSING! We were constantly surrounded by dirty tables of people that left. If they bused quicker the line might not be an hour ‍

Not planning on returning.
Lots of good choices; the chefs are friendly. If you arrive after four, there will be a line but the wait is worth it.

Bacchus, the Roman god of harvest, grapes, fertility, and theater.

Vegas translation: This buffet has abundant food, wine, sex (appeal), and drama -- welcome to VEGAS!

Vegas has definitely become the home of capitalism -- every new establishment is trying to outdo its predecessors.  What's the corporate motto?  Go BIG or go HOME! And with this buffet, they went big. $17 million to build this place? I had to try it out.

I went for Sunday lunch and the lines were pretty hideous.  I am glad that my friend is a diamond member and got us right up to the front, but I might have not had such great things to say about this place if I had waited for 2 hours.

Ambiance: Urban Chic -- I can totally see this place turn into a swanky lounge at night.  Wooden decor along side the walls of what looks like a part of "unblock" pieces from my iPhone game, combined with the elements of delicate glass casing throughout the buffet.  Very well decorated, good lighting, and a decent set up of seating arrangements to fit different types of groups.

Food: Variety.  Seafood, carvery, Asian, Mexican, Italian, deli, dessert... the staples of the Vegas buffet are all here.  However, biggest peeve of mine = cold crab legs.  Halfway through my meal, I realized that they will warm it up for you, but they do that by dunking the legs into hot water for a minute or two.  When it comes out of the vat of water, the crab has lost its bold flavor.  In addition, their sushi/ Japanese station was disappointing.  The freshness of the sushi was mediocre and the selections were few.  In terms of the food, they had many choices, including a wide selection of deli cuts and cheese and dessert station that included made to order crepes and notable gelato flavors, however, nothing stood out as "amazing" or worthy of the phrase "YOU HAVE TO TRY THIS."

Service:  Perhaps they were understaffed, but there were moments during our meal where the empty plates were stacked and just sat at our table.  We would go for another round of food and return to find the plates still there.  Aside from that, our waiter was very kind and attentive to our needs when he did come by.  

Overall, this is a good buffet and I see how they could have easily invested millions, however, it's not my favorite. I am sure I will be back, and it's worth a visit, but naming a buffet after a roman god definitely sets the bar at high expectations -- some tough shoes to fill.

I will say it was not my idea, and I was a little skeptical about going to a buffet, but this is a must have on your list if you decide on going to a buffet in Las Vegas. Bacchanal Buffet is located in Caesar's Palace, the hotel is beautiful inside and out. 

My favorites: 1) Fresh steamed crab (from the pot, no hands selecting the crab, no one handling the tongs, if you know what I mean, I hope they keep it this way). The best part about this is, the crab isn't so salty. Thank you! 2) The bok choi, I love the greens and they were done perfectly. 3) Crepes, they were freshly made by order. 4) Macaroons, the flavors were on spot!

Hope you get to indulge yourself here!

Being the hottest and newest buffet in town, we had to come and give it a try. Showed up around 5 and probably waited about an hour in line. Yeah - there's usually a wait and we thought 5 was early but maybe we should've came even earlier. Plunked down out $55 (ouch!) and got seated. Service was so-so. Our waiter was kinda scarce and spacey. It took a while to get our drinks, to get refills, to get our tables cleared. But then at the end, another guy/waiter showed up and asked multiple times about refills and clearing our tables even though we were ok and still working on our food. I don't think he was taking over for our original waiter because he was still around but it felt like this new guy was like the expediter, trying to hurry us along to finish and leave. Weird vibes throughout. 

On to the food. Like Wicked Spoon, I think I would be happy just having their dessert (but then I wouldn't get my money's worth). It's truly an impressive spread. Mutiple flavors of ice scream and we're talking about unique flavors too like mango chile or French toast. Mochi - though we looked behind the counter and it's just from the box that you can get at the grocery store so maybe save your stomach for something else. Fresh crepes which you can customize with fruits and sauces and whip cream. Bowls of macaroons, jars of candy, all different kinds of mini desserts, chocolate covered strawberries, cake pops, and it goes on and on. For the actual food, there's mainly 3 sections. An ethnic section with Italian, Mexican, and Asian foods as well as some salads/soup. A meat and hot food line with prime rib, a variety of hot meats, and sides like veggies and mashed potatoes. And finally the seafood section - crab legs (steamed or cold), shrimp, lobster bisque, oysters, clam bakes, etc. I would have to say my top three favorite things were the blackened chicken soup (Chinese herb-y style), the lamb (cooked and seasoned perfectly) and the macaroons (love these delicate desserts). Mmmm, I would come back if it wasn't such a pricey meal and long wait.

My wife and I got there on Saturday around 5Pm. We saw a waiting line so we get into it and wait for 30mins. Then we figure out we need to check in by Machine first to get time on when we could get into the waiting line. No body guide us before!! Totally mass on Management of arriving customer. All in all, not deserve it.

Okay, I can't really say this is the best buffet in Vegas because we went for NY's dinner.  So it was a special dinner.  But as far as best buffet dinner I've had so far?  By far.

Okay.  NY's was $70/person and it came with endless champagne.

The food was amazing though.  Lobster.  THey kind of ruined it with some spinich or mushroom cream sauce crap.  Come on, leave my lobster alone.  Steamed is perfect.  But I scrapped it off.  So it was cool.

The deli meats were tasty.  The carving station.  Oh god, they have everything.  RIb chop roasts (you get your own rib!), lamb chops, and everything else you would expect.

The seafood was wonderful.  THe crab legs here are much sweeter and tastier than other buffets.  The oysters were good too.  THey don't use those huge ones that get grainy, but the mid sized ones which are sweeter.

I would love to try this place again on a regular weekend.

Beware - gnats abound in this buffet. The presentation was unbelievable but when we settled in for desert the gnats attacked. Having spent over $100 for dinner for 2 I asked for a manager. This goon named Wolf came and said this has been a problem before but since we were onto desert there was nothing he would do for us. I contacted customer service after arriving home and while they were sympathetic all that was offered was a return visit. Since I was 2500 miles away I asked for something comparable in one of their locations closer to home and was ignored. No reply at all. Needless to say I will not be returning there or any of their other locations.  
Follow up -  It took contacting their corporate office several times but eventually they did the right thing and gave me a full refund.

Came here for dinenr. Lots to choose from - if you like seafood and desert. You'll probably like this place.

Weak fruit, red meat and veggie selection! I need my vitamin c.
I enjoyed the breakfast buffet at my hotel way more for $17 than this place for $57

Great selection of food. High quality food is definitely worth the price. Tacos, menudo, birria are just like what you would get at a Taqueria. Pho compares just as good, if not better, as pho restraraunts. Multiple selections of different smoked/bbq meats: American wagyu, brisket, pork belly, sausages. Solid seafood selections. Crab legs, sea snails, raw oysters, peeled shrimp, cioppino, clam chowder etc. Dim sum, roasted duck, the crispy skin asian pork are great options in the Asian section. Go wild with the desserts. Over 12 different flavors of gelato, mochi filled ice cream, freshly made crepes, cake pops, etc. Definitely worth the money. 

Only downside of this buffet is the wait time. We paid an extra $35 per person to jump the 2hr wait. This place needs more tables or figure out a different way to get customers in.

Quality of food and service has gone way down while prices remain high. No more kobe beef sliders. No fresh juices. Dry meats, even the wagyu was tough to eat. Truffle pizza was mushy and too salty. 

Place was only about two thirds full yet we came back to find that they had completely cleared and cleaned our table even though we had only been there for fifteen minutes. Beverage refill only came once after an hour. Never came back to check on if we needed more drinks. This place has gone from being my favorite buffet in Vegas to a huge disappointment. 

Double the price for half the quality.

This review is based on my third and last visit.

The food is definitely good. Not all "great" even though some of it is and there's enough variety that you're certain to find something you like. Why the one star? I'm ok with waiting to get IN to an establishment if the quality is good, but I am no longer willing to get jerked around once inside. This is supposedly what the wait is for. Getting a drink refill is nearly impossible, as is any kind of interaction with any wait staff. 

I made the mistake of taking a valentines date there and knew with 100% certainty based on previous visits that the experience was going to be a nightmare as soon as they took a photo with my date at the beginning to bring by later. I actually tried to discreetly decline the rose they were offering for the photo to avoid having happen what I knew was going to happen but was asked repeatedly until I selected a red or pink one to have the photo taken. Surprise. The entire meal was spent attempting to track down whoever had the photo. I was STILL unable to actually get it after speaking to three different people, each of which said they needed to "go to the back" only to take several minutes to disappear. At least 20 minutes AFTER the meal was wasted with still zero result. 

I don't care how high the quality of your food is. When you are charging a premium for a product such this, the experience becomes the product and there just isn't any room for ruining that experience with inattentiveness, especially for a prouct I'm not asking for in the first place. I'm sure there are more than enough people willing to wait to prevent any meaningful action on this statement so the rest of you who want to go will have one less person to wait behind. I'll patronize a business that is happy I am there rather than annoyed at the inconvenience of actually dealing with customers.

Update:  They implemented a new way to check into the buffet.  There's 4 touchscreen computers for you to enter your party size.  You'll receive a ticket which indicates what time you will need to come back to the hostess line (the one on the left with the pretty hostess).

EG: 4th of July Saturday, I grabbed my ticket at 410pm.  Ticket says come back at 5:55pm.  I was texted at 515pm to start lining up at the hostess line.  About 6pm is when I will make it to the front (I'm writing this as I wait in line).

Probably one of the best buffet I have ever gone to. Great experience. Expensive though. Therefore, probably a one time thing for me...or maybe every time I head to Vegas haha.

Food:
5/5, everything was on point. I enjoyed the food.

Service:
5/5 went on labor labor day weekend with friends. 8 of us got in super fast. We had a big party and they helped us skip the line. There was about 60-80 people in line and our group of 8 got put into a different line. Got in within 5-10 minutes. 

Con:

Bathroom is far and busy. 

Overall: 
Give it a try. One of the best buffet in Vegas.

This place is not worth waiting for a couple hours. Only the steak section was good but other food was less than average. Too pricey for their poor quality of foods. I wonder why people are so obsessed with this buffet.

It's a sad day to see what I considered to be the best buffet in Vegas go down. Way down. Their new seating system is setting everyone up for failure. It's a joke to wait for 2 hours just to fall in line to pay, then wait in line again to actually pay, then another line to be seated. If you still plan to go, make sure to have a back up plan!

If you are a buffet person, then this place will be your cup of tea. There is a little bit of everything for everyone here, from seafood, grill, Mexican, Italian, vegetarian, Vietnamese, dim sum, Indonesian, etc. At the same time, no one offering really stood out as being superb, everything was just status-quo. If you are craving one genre of food, I would opt elsewhere. But if you want to experience a true Vegas buffet, then you are in for a treat. And to end, the desert bar was really fun, be sure and save room and try the coconut and green tea gelato.

Compared to other buffets across the globe this is one of the best you will ever have.  Quality mimosas and the option to have cold or hot crab legs. The desserts were amazing and included a crepe and gelato station.  The service was very good as well.  You may have to take a ticket and wait 40 minutes but it is worth it.  We did Saturday champagne brunch.  I highly suggest the brunch!

Very clean and organized, their food selection was not bad. You have a mixed variety of food, from American, Italian, Latino, Asian, and Seafood food. Everything tasted above average, but I was not impressed with their seafood selections. Snow crabs looked so depressing, dirty and nearly any. It is served cold, so if you want them to steam it, take it to where they serve the pizza. I think we came on a bad day.

Dessert bar was awesome, they have a wide selection from gelato to cookies, crepes, candies, etc... I definitely will come back. $50ish a person for dinner, so come on an empty stomach.

Loved it. Went during a holiday so I had to pay $68 for the brunch, but it's Vegas and that's expected. If I can pump money into machines and throw down on tables...spending a little more for good food was a no brainer. 

Their seafood is so fresh! Sweet crab, large cocktail PRAWN, and fresh from the pot hot crabs. They had unlimited bone marrow (soooo goooooood). I ate so much of it, willing to risk a heart attack right there at the table. So many food options for seafood lovers, meat lovers, and dessert lovers alike. Grilled lamb chops, ribs, prime rib, roasted whole pig...the list goes on. 

Love their wait system of texting, this way rather than spending two hours in line...those two hours can be spent at the bar and gambling.
Average buffet. Had high hopes.  It's big though. There are better buffets...There's a 24 hour deal somewhere.

I occasionally travel to Vegas for work and leisure, and I always make time and save calories for this buffet. Do not expect this to be your average local fusion buffet, you're in it for a treat since it's quite pricey (I think I paid around $55-$65 for dinner) but they spoil you with options. I honestly felt overwhelmed every time I eat here, everything looks so good and 8/10 times they all tasted good! You also don't have to murder someone over crab legs in here, they have everything under the sun for you to grab and they're constantly being refilled by the kitchen staff so eat as much as you can. I'm a snob when it comes to Asian cuisine but out of other buffets I've tried in Vegas (Wynn, Wicked Spoon, Bellagio, Rio), Bacchanal really nailed it. I won't say the pho here is authentic but the flavor is there. Dim sum is actually better than some of the dim sum place I've had in Chinatown, which is a total shocker. I don't know about you but I "think" I have a separate stomach for desserts. The dessert options here is insane, ranging from the standard items like creme brulee, macarons, chocolate covered strawberries, gelato, all kinds of cakes, crepes make to order, I also saw some unique ones like Portuguese egg tarts, flan, custard steamed buns and other things that I can't remember. 

5/5 stars on ambiance, cleanliness & customer service too. 

Personal tips: come here starved and indulge.

Very beautiful place! Buffet selection is massive and the food ambrosial cannot compare to other place in Vegas. Been here multiple occasions and never been disappointed. Sometimes they are so busy they will lack the service a little, but it's understandable. Crab legs cold or hot are a must to try ok don't forget to dip them in butter!!

Food is very bland, no flavor. Nothing special about this place at all. For $65 per person I expect a lot more. The service sucked and the employees were rude, not professional. Waste of money and time! I can get better food for less in the same hotel.

Though the food is good, we got here at 830, they close at 10 but are no longer taking anymore people. An hour and a half earlier than the actual closing time is absolutely ridiculous. Definitely points removed for that. If they wanted to close at 8:30, they should say they close at 8:30 not 10, false advertisement!!!

I have been here right around when it first opened and just recently about a couple of weeks ago. I definitely noticed a downgrade of food offerings, diminshing food quality, and overall service was lacking. The food offerings were much better in the early days with actual steaks, but now they have the "typical" buffet meat items like prime rib and sausages. If they're trying to be #1, then please differentiate from all the other buffets in Vegas. It's quite typical now, but at higher prices. I usually try little portions of different foods like tacos, Asian noodles, cold dishes (e.g. shrimp, crab legs, and salads), and meats. Tacos were way too salty, literally tasted like it was prepared with ounces of salt. The Asian noodles, specifically the Pho, were not cooked properly (under cooked). The cold dishes like the shrimp just didn't have that element of freshness. The meats, although limited in terms of selection, were decent. I did like the sliced pork belly during my last trip as it was juicy, succulent, and had that melt in your mouth experience. 

The desserts were okay. All the usual selections like mini-sized cupcakes, tarts, and cakes. Just okay, some were not sweet at all (cakes) while some others were way too sweet (brule). Nothing was just right.

Service was somewhat lacking. Used plates were not taken away timely. 

Overall, still expect to wait in line unless you get there during off-peak hours. Would I return? Probably cause it's one of the A-OK buffets on the strip, and that's not saying much if you have ever tried others.

I was in Vegas celebrating my birthday early with my family, my mother really wanted to try the new $17 million dollar Caesars Buffet. We go for lunch and the line was worse than Space Mountain at Disney. We see a sign for a $15 line pass. This by the way is the only dollar amount being marketed in the buffet area. This entire area is a giant fail by the marketing department. There are no prices listed for the buffet. There are no prices listed for the special 24 hour buffet pass. People are getting to the cashier, which at 1pm on a Saturday, there is only one cashier, one cashier - and they are walking away at the ridiculous prices!
