Caesars, put up marketing materials, tell us how much the buffet costs. I was at wicked spoon and they tell you everything before you stand in line. Tell us the $15 line pass is per person. Tell us that if you come back the next morning, you'll have to pay another $15 to not wait in the line after you've already spent $65 a person plus tax and tip. Well after complaining to the manager, we finally sat down for the buffet. I liked the buffet, the food was tasty. I didn't overeat or go overboard because I was saving my appetite for my birthday dinner. Well, a few hours later, I'm gambling at the Wynn and it hit me. I got really sick to my stomach. I did make it to my bday dinner before I had to leave and spend the rest of my trip and a few min before my flight out in the bathroom. Thanks Caesars Buffet!

I don't frequent buffets but came here with some friends of mine who visited me from Seattle. Though the price is quite steep, you certainly get what you pay for. From presentation to freshness and quality, every item they served was delicious and the selection is incredible. I do not know if it is the best buffet in town but it certainly is the best of the major ones I have been to.

The wait is annoying.
You can pay $25 for no-wait pass, but you still wait a bit after paying to be seated. 

They give you 2 hours to eat, and that's plenty of time.

The food is good. Their meat selection is very salty. Thought I was going to grow chest hair. 

The line for food is ok, but theses people don't know how to stand in line so be patient. 

Overall the food is good. 
Desserts are so good!!! I recommend pecan pie, cheesecake, ice cream, and fresh fruits.


I don't know the reason for all the ravings though. It's like any other buffets that I have tried. 

Would I come back? Maybe. Such a gray answer I know...oh well.

I've been to many fancy buffets in my lifetime, but this one takes the cake. It's a little pricey, but it's worth it because it's all you can eat and the food is very fresh. Our service was great- our waitress, Su, was very sweet and friendly. As soon as we would finish one drink, it would be refilled immediately thereafter and our plates were cleared almost immediately after finishing each time. There are many options for many different taste buds here and I would highly recommend the seafood and the choices of meat, like prime rib, suckling pig and tri-tip. I only got a picture of the desserts because I was enjoying my dinner so much!

The amount of time waiting for to get in and the selections of food will really disappoint you. I think at best a three stars. Nothing much exciting to choose from.once pass the 3 hours wait and got in. Disappointment.... went to better buffets in Las Vegas.  Another one time deal for me.

Went there 4 times in one extended weekend (breakfast and dinner). Savage I know! Everything was great from the seafood to meat selection, Mexican food (they even have tamales and agua de jaimaca/horchata), Salad bar and Asian food! Tip: if you want to get your shrimp (or cold seafood) sautéed, take it over to the grill guys (next to salad bar) and they will sauté it for you! Last but not least the pastries are tasty and the crepes are made to order. Enjoy!

I was really looking forward to this but it was a slight let down.  Most of the food was good.  Asian food section and meat selection were great. Seafood area was very limited compared to what was advertised on yelp and their website.  For $50.99 per person on a Saturday night, I would rather be at The Buffet at The Wynn with beautiful flower arrangments surrounding me.

Breakfast was lovely almost everything I tried I loved.
I have to admit I came back for the meat gray quality flavour. I can't imagine anyone coming here and not finding one or two things to luv if not more.

I would suggest at least try thus place once, the staff are more than happy to recommend or assist with any request. I love my mimosa pineapple

Underwhelming. We managed to get in at the lunch price and I am still not sure how worth it this place is. My first and biggest problem was how poor the desert selection is. If you don't want them to make you a crepe, you've got pretty standard buffet desert fare. The bananas foster are an exception, apparently those were great. The cakes and treats were all meh. 

The food itself was pretty boring. There's a big selection but none of it was as good as a similar dish at Wynn or wicked spoon. I'd say just don't really bother with this place as the hype will die down as more people actually eat there.

After reading the reviews I wanted to come here and enjoy the food. The food was good until I got food poisoning from the buffet. This was the only thing I ate and that I can trace it back to. Will not ever go there again. Beware of Buffet's!!

This palace is amazing!! From their red velvet pancakes and orginial pancakes this place is amAzing!! The deserts are delicious but one down side was for their shaved ice they did not have any Mochi bites or fruit toppings but the person Serving the desert let me know when in asked for it and apologized for it. Our hostess was on in it since we had the all you can drink but some times it felt like we waited forever. Our busboy Vincent was the highlight our table was always clean, took everything and was very friendly and he was so sweet by pulling out my chair all the time. He made our visit great so shout out to him!!

The most horrible experience at the checkin. They have this dinky idiotic machines outside to sign in. I was in line and was asked to sign in and a ticket was handed over to me (I will attach the image) stating that they will text me in 67 minutes. Well I had an appointment with apple and I walked all the way to the other side of the casino. Got a text ( will attach image) that I have 15 minutes to get back and pay otherwise I have to be at the back of the line. Got back to be told that I take my place back in the line; right behind the last person that entered before me. Just amazingly stupid. 

They can have their food and shove it.

Went here in between lunch and dinner on a Friday afternoon, it was a buffet paradise! There's an endless amount of everything! They have seafood, BBQ, American, Japanese, Chinese and some pasta too! With a vast variety of desserts. The service was good, the place itself was roomy, great for groups. Definitely want to go back next time I'm in Vegas!

My husband took me to the buffet at Caesar's Palace for our anniversary because we heard it was really nice.  We paid $125 for two, so we thought we were in for a surprise.  We were and not in a good way!  The food was average at best!  The prime rib was bland, broccoli w cheese was nasty and the sea food buffet was all cold!  For someone like me who likes their seafood hot, it was a huge disappointment! Everything was on ice. Yuck!!  The pizzas were cold, salads limp and pasta old.  The only decent thing there were the desserts and the service.  I won't be going back!!!!

Food wise it's 5 stars but wait wise it's a 1. They tell you when to come back but that does not mean you will get the lunch price because they will stop you right before price change even when they tell you to come back by certain time. If the ticket you get says to return before 3 you should get the lunch price!!!!! Make the change

Several of my friends are Vegas "regulars" so I turned to them for advice on the best buffet. By far they all chose "Bacchanal" and I had already selected it based on Yelp reviews so it was a no brainer at that point.

What I'm most glad for is the advice to go right as lunch is ending. You pay the lunch price but see the food turn over to dinner and get to eat from the dinner foods.

Honestly, if I had gone during normal lunch ($40) and not had any dinner, I wouldn't have been very impressed and the rating would be lower. Nothing on the lunch line wowed me, maybe because it was almost over, food seemed cold or overheated under the lamps. One pork dish I got was so hard.

However at 3:00, that's when dinner starts rolling out and yay for crab legs! Although still skinnier type legs, they are split down the long way so it's SOOOO easy to get the meat out. Combined with their hot butter, so YUM! I had two plates full and that made it all worthwhile!

If you're a first timer, don't forget to look around the bend from the Mexican area. There's a whole other section with Italian and Asian foods that I missed until the end. 

Desserts were ample and they even had someone to make you a fresh crepe!

Food was amazing. I mean really really good with great variety. Waitress that attended us was fine. 
The staff where they sit you, on the hand, seemed unorganized and lost. We went on a weekday and it wasn't even one of those super busy days, but they were running around like chicken without heads.

The buffet of all buffets !!  Tons of options ! Food quality excellent. Clean, but it is Caesar's!! Totally indulged on the crab legs, so delicious, served hot or cold. Everything I ate was quite tasty. And the size of the spread ... HUGE!! Be prepared to stay 2 hours and pace yourself!!!
Definitely hit the cheese and cold meats - Humboldt fog...... slice yourself a huge piece and indulge!!

Best buffet in Vegas. Every single gourmet is delicious. Great variety of food to choose from and every single serving is well presented. So it doesn't only taste good but  also looks good! The ambiance is great, very classy and elegant, it is overlooking the famous Caesar's Pool.

Overall, this is definitely my favorite buffet in Vegas! 
Line can be long and it's a little pricey compared to other buffet places in Vegas but the quality of food and the service is what makes everything worth it!

Man so much good foods and drinks and stuffs. can't believe it but i did! too much two choose from all the way in the back and the fronts! always keep getting up for more and never stopping a lot until its like 7 times. Every planets food is there with different countries and stuffs. Helpy people always be nice with it and give me things. i told my family that i love the buff fay and wish i can live there everyday but only three times a week. Tank U for showing me the world in one place!

Normally I don't give 2 star's but I am going to give this over hyped buffet one for the first time being that I'm a buffet lover and have experience in tons of them to compare to.

First off this is as I seen one if not the most expensive buffet's in town right now with myself paying $48 to get in even with a player's card.

2nd off I have no clue how they got 500 dishes out of the mixture there is no way by far 500 dishes in this buffet there is the same amount of selection from stateion to station as any other typical big buffet in Vegas maybe there trying to hype up the fact you can CUSTOMIZE a dish up to 500 ways but either way I'm not buying it because I was expecting to see once again THE KING OF BUFFET'S here!

Let's say the quality was very poor, the rice in some dishes tasted like rice in a bag, the Italian food was very bland nothing interesting or unique especially the meat balls tasted like frozen freezer selection. They didn't even serve steak so I had to settle on pork chops also that were very cheap in quality.. just the list goes on and on of just miss after miss of trying to hit the spot on quality and selection.

The only positive thing I can say about this place is that my greeter was very nice and gave me a quick tour of the place and the server was a very nice gentleman which I tipped him accordingly but other then that I'll never return.

Line wasn't too long on a Saturday morning and they have a separate line for groups of 6 or more. Our group of 7 including a toddler still waited about 20 mins even though we were the 2nd group in the 6+ line. When we got in there were plenty of big tables so I don't know why there's a longer wait for the larger groups. Some of the stir fried Chinese veggies were a little too salty. Overall a pretty good selection of meats, seafood, and they even have a ramen/udon/pho bar which is nice. Great desserts to choose from and delicious fresh fruit juices too. Get your grub on!!!

Yes this buffet is more expensive than just about any Buffet in town- but it is so worth it! The crab legs were already cut for guests to devour! The grilled ham and cheese croquet sandwiches were one of my favorites. The sushi is delicious! Highly recommend this buffet!

This is unequivocally the best bloody buffet in Vegas, and now there's no way I'll ever visit Vegas without a pit stop here. They've really raised the bar on buffet food quality. I ate until my stomach (the organ) had shooting pain from all the food I managed to stuff down. Damn you, amateur stomach, I wish you could handle more of that good stuff!

Tips: 

- Oysters and oyster shooters are served beginning 3:00pm! 
- If you're staying at Caesar's Palace, it might be worth it to get a 24 hour pass to stop by for food any time within a 24 hour period.
- Most of the food stations have items there that are order-only and off menu. 
- Their ramen is freakin delicous. Okay, that's not a tip but I needed to include it somewhere.
- Your Player's club card gives you a $1 discount
- Our price was $41.99 but this number may be a moving target. I wouldn't be surprised to find it higher the next time I come due to the high demand.

This place is very popular.  I tried to avoid the long line so went around 4pm. Still had to wait 30minutes. 

The buffet is overpriced. It is good but same as all the other buffet places. Nothing special. Wish they had more food options.

I absolutely love brunch and the Bacchanal Buffet brunch was phenomenal ! Because I went during memorial day weekend the price was increased from the usual but with such a variety of choices which included Japanese, Chinese, Mexican, Italian, Thai (literally EVERYTHING) I would do it all over again!  I honestly can't even begin to tell you how many plates I had!

Those chilled Alaskan crab legs already sliced will call your name again and again. But so will the Mac and Cheese and the entire seafood station (of course if that's you're thing). I went to every station and picked something and there was nothing that made me say "oh that was okay," it all made me think I wanted to live in that obese moment forever.

One not so great thing was that our server was working her behind off to keep the glasses full with the unlimited mimosas. It was to the point that we started feeling bad for her. They should definitely have more than one person refilling glasses, especially during memorial rest weekend. Literally saw her going from one end to the other. Bacchanal, utilize more servers per section.

Outstanding but not cheap.  Lunch is when i eat big and i wish i could live at this buffet.  I like aria buffet for similarity at lower prices for lunch that is.  Great to feed a hungry date impress or celebrate.

The first time came here. It was really good!! There are so many kind of food like Chinese, Japanese, italian, dessert, and so on! I was surprised that there is oyster. It tasted good but that was not my type...:( I really liked there are sooooo many sweets! Like ice cream, crape(I choose Nutella source), shaved ice, chocolate, fruits, cupcakes, cookie, and others!! I really recommend this buffet:)) now I'm stuffed!!

Been wanting to go here for years. Finally had my chance by taking my daughter for a birthday brunch on Monday. It is a lovely restaurant and the service was very good.  The food presentation was very pretty and everything looked yummy.  Sadly, in many cases, the presentation didn't match the taste.  I would have thought that for the crazy amount of money I spent, I would have received hot food.  The lobster bisque, about 3 bites, was served in tiny silver pails that were already prepared.  The top had congealed and the soup was cold.  The gnocchi was sitting in a pool of olive oil and was cold and gooey. The dim sum had been sitting for awhile and was chewy. 

The highlight was the sushi.  Very fresh and cold, but only 2 varieties.  I could have paid $20 at my favorite sushi bar and had more choices.  And instead of a bottle of soy sauce, it came in packets which squirted all over the table when I tried to open one.

We did enjoy the desserts.  A very large variety all served in little 2 bite cups, which I thought was a terrific idea.  I was able to try a variety instead of filling up on one.  I recommend the tiramisu, chocolate mousse and crème brulee.  

It was good, but I wouldn't go back unless someone else is paying!

this was a perfect pit stop for our bachelorette party as us girls were super craving a huge dessert bar. we also had a good selection of their seafood, surprisingly good dim sum, and lamb. don't forget to try the corn on the cob... so much butter.. a definite must for splurging :) i love this buffet's dessert bar... unlimited creme brulee, macarons, and chocolate covered strawberries. heavenly!

Best buffet in vegas. Go at 2pm to get lunch price ($38) for dinner that starts at 3pm. Crab legs, ceviche, BBQ, sushi, chinese, anything you can imagine and more for a buffet. The dessert station is unbelievable.

We were here for Sunday late champagne brunch into dinner. It was not mind blowing...perhaps it's cuz I'm Asian. I noticed people loved the Asian offerings, which I usually skip in a buffet because I have a specific pallet for all things Asian.

Pros: Raw oysters were not gritty, fresh juices, truffle pizza, Asian-fusion desserts.

Cons: The American fare consisted of beef sliders and hot dogs...lol; the fried chicken was bone dry. We had a table for 8 who had to pay the mandatory 18% gratuity, which wasn't worth it because they didn't clear our tables and couldn't top up our drinks.

Everything else was ok and better elsewhere. Bottom line - not worth the money or the hype...unless you love Asian food.

My husband and I went to this buffet. We had read Yelp reviews and were on the fence as some of the reviews were raving and others just went ehhh.

The wait was not bad at all. We went around 1:00 p.m. and there was maybe a 15 minute wait. I want to say that with tip it was maybe $75, not too bad for Vegas and what was advertised.

They have many different dishes but really, almost nothing is the best you could ever have. The mac n cheese was lacking, the sushi tasted like any other low end buffet sushi and the pastas were meh. The assortment of meats were delicious however and we were especially impressed with the chicken jalapeno sausage.

The gelato selection, though limited, was delicious. It reminded me of gelato I had in Italy which was truly a treat. 

My husband was in love with the Rum Baba and the cookies. 

I'm glad we experienced this buffet but it was not the best food experience on our trip nor were most of the dishes we've had the absolute best ever.

So, I just paid $300 (family of 5) for the worst and most disgusting buffet in my life. We waited 45min in line and I was getting all excited because of the good review I read online. But the seafood was horrible, oysters, crab leg, crawfish were all smell really really bad and we end up couldn't eat any of those. Sushi was cold, and hard. I was very disappointed because it's not worth it. So, I end up paying $60 per person just to eat a few slides of pineapple, cantaloupe and a cream brûlée.
De las 3 veces que he estado en las vegas, he comido en muchos buffets de hoteles, pero sin duda, este es el mejor!

I think this might be the best overall buffet I've ever been to. Yes, that's a bold statement. They have a huge variety of all the food I love to eat. Seafood is plentiful and fresh(-ish). They had really interesting food stations compared to other buffets. Instead of a generic "Asian" section they had separate sushi vs dim sum section and a make your own ramen section. They had the typical meat station with rotisserie chicken and prime rib, and on top of that they had a really aggressive street taco guy. He tried really hard to get me to take 3 tacos, but I looked him in the eye and he finally gave me one. 

Here's a weird thing about the bread. The bread display looked suspiciously like the bread display at Guy Savoy. Could they have the same baker? I hope not. 

The only thing I was truly disappointed in was the dessert bar. Nothing was particularly good, and nothing set it apart from other dessert bars. Some of the pastries were mediocre. They have scoop serve gelato, which is a step above an ice cream machine I guess. 

The only thing(s) horrible about the buffet is the wait. I call BS on the pager system. Like other restaurants, it's a pager to tell you when to get in line. So you still end up waiting forever and a day for it.

Highly rated on yelp for a reason. It's an incredible variety of food which is very well done. One of the best buffets I've been to. Everything from pho to crème brûlée!  The price is worth it especially if you come to eat.

Ok. You might look at my review history and think I am crazy. HOWEVER, I am also factoring price into this. So here it goes.

It's expensive, which is fine. I am ok with that. There is seafood, unique dishes, lots of "higher end" ingredients, individually served items, and A TON of staff.  But I will break down where it failed. 
1- DO NOT TAKE MY PICTURE WHEN I COME TO EAT. Seriously? This is not a tourist attraction. I am not wanting to document my night out at a buffet and really? I know you are just going to try to sell me this picture for a zillion dollars later. Which sure enough, a gentleman came to our table with the picture and I politely shut him down. Fortunately, they aren't like the kiosk people in this regard, and he did not try to pitch me. That was the only redeeming aspect of it. But I don't want to be interrupted when I am eating to awkwardly reject the dumb picture. NOT CLASSY.
2- The buffet itself looks great. The lighting, atmosphere, buffet lines. very nice. 
3- Variety, - be careful, you could get lost. It's huge, and all over the place. Interesting
4- None of the dishes either of us grabbed from the buffet were hot, or even warm really. I thought maybe it was just me, but I overheard the lady at the table next to us mention it to her significant other too. 
5- There was a lot of creative ideas with terrible execution. Don't ask me why I thought the chicken and waffles (chicken wing in a waffle cone with some fries) seemed like a genius plan, but it was horrible. So the "cool" things just didn't work.
6- The truffle potatoes everyone raves about, not super impressed. Perhaps if the base recipe was good without the addition of truffle, it would have worked better, but it was pretty unexciting. I felt that this buffet really tried hard to be "upscale" utilizing "gourmet" ingredients. So people who maybe don't have the culinary experience are impressed by this, but I felt that everything was just flat. Desserts were the same. Cool, yeah macaroons. Uber trendy dessert of luxury, but they were sad. Creme brulee is literally my favorite thing on the planet and it was lacking. There was some attempts at gastronomy, which is great, and I appreciate it, but again if you can't do it well, don't even bother. I would have rather had half the buffet options and decent food. Unexciting. And again, I am factoring in price. Don't get me wrong, there were some dishes I did enjoy. The watermelon salad for example was fantastic. The butter dispensers all over for the seafood was a genius idea. I didn't eat any seafood because I knew I would be disappointed. (Grew up with crab off the dock) 

Overall: If we had not timed this perfectly (about 10 minutes after we arrived the wait became HUGE) and waited for any amount of time, I would have be pissed. Mediocre food passed off as gourmet and marketed as a high end buffet. Sorry, I won't be back. I'd rather spend that money on a good restaurant.

New favorite buffet in Vegas!  Sorry Mirage...  This place is amazing.  Every cuisine and plenty of it!  Champagne included.  Dessert even gets it's own area!  I went for lunch which has a mix of breakfast and lunch items but more weighted to lunch items.  $43 plus tip, but worth every penny.

Just be prepared to wait in line for atleast an hour during regular eating times.

Wow really.  For about $70 bucks including tip I really was expecting more.  Service was neutral but the food was so bad.  From sushi, to dimsum, and meats, everything was low quality, too greasy, too salty or just plain bad.  Long line of folks looking to get seafood, but judging by the smell of the whole area, I could tell it was not fresh, so skipped.  Those that give this place a good rating have either never been to  decent buffet or must just be country bumpkins.  I would honestly prefer golden corral.  When I see all the folks in line I feel like screaming "don't do it!!!".   Caesars..come on...fix this.

Brunch on a Sunday- the reviews were right... before 10:30 the line is manageable! The steak and eggs was a highlight- steak very flavorful! the fresh squeezed juices- sooo good! loved the presentation- individual small milk bottles... the red velvet pancakes weren't fresh for me- so, kind of hard and unimpressive.. THE SALSA BAR was worth what we paid alone! Why doesn't EVERY BUFFET have a salsa bar?! Only wish we could eat more at a sitting! lol.. I didn't "over-eat"... and I've regretted it all day!!!

The king crab leg and shrimp are fresh and juicy, and you have to try their cocktail sauce for these seafood. Other food are also ok. Go early so you don't need to wait or you can buy a fast pass for $25

Every time I come to sin city, I make it a point to eat here. It's not like THE best I've ever had (in Drake's voice) but I enjoy it. Fancy-ish buffet so it comes with a not so cheap price but they have an extensive plethora of food from different ethnicities so my palate is satisfied. My most recent visit here was back in June and I was actually pretty surprised how authentic their phô was when the hubby to be grabbed a bowl (since somebody was shit faceted the night before). It was tasty and my weird ass was eating my desserts whilst taking a spoonful of the broth each bite. I love the salty and sweet combo let's just say. I'll be back next time with my big appetite!

Their mini-fingertip tongs to pinch and move hot plates is a cute idea.

Bacchanal can be defined as:
1. an occasion of wild and drunken revelry.
2. a priest, worshiper, or follower of Bacchus, the Roman god of wine.
3. one of the top voted Las Vegas buffets

It all ties in nicely with the Caesar's Palace and Roman/Greek mythology theme. I haven't read much on ancient stories lately, other than watching reruns of the original Clash of the Titans movie. All I remember is that Zeus is a slut, Medusa is frightening, and that the magical, mechanical owl was the neatest sidekick before R2D2 was activated.

While engaging in the usual cabbie chit chat, our driver mentioned that the two most popular Vegas buffets were Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon. I would have been content at visiting either, but going with the flow we ended up here. I do like that they use a Fastpass system, so that you can check in, pick up a ticket, leave, and return during your scheduled time window. You might still be in a line, but at least you're not standing around getting hangrier the entire wait time.

Hours:
Breakfast M-F 7:30a-11a
Champagne Brunch Sat-Sun 8a-3p
Lunch Daily 11a-3p
Dinner Daily 3p-10p

Price range is $30-$50+ depending on the time of day and in consideration of holiday pricing.

The available offerings are quite impressive. While I'm not too critical of buffets in general (since the kitchen's goal is to mass produce quickly) the Bacchanal menu raises the bar on the Vegas standard and does a nice job of serving up some tasty dishes. Not everyone has an extensive buffet menu that includes an international variety of comfort food, street snacks, and fancy fare; or an amazing dessert bar, with gelatos, macarons, and gluten-free options (oh my!), that can satisfy any sweet tooth. I wish I had more room in my tummy because I wasn't able to sample a bite of everything. Being a popular AYCE hotspot, the visitor traffic is a usually good sign of dishes being made freshly to keep their various stations stocked up.

Service was efficient as expected. We didn't visit much with our waitress other than the initial drink order. Plates were cleared often and glasses refilled regularly.

You can try to gameplan your meal, but once you see what's going on at the Bacchanal Buffet, you might lose your mind or have a temporary lapse of restraint and start piling your plate in a frenzy like when you chugged and triple-fisted drinks when it was last call. That's ok, it's your occasion and you're here to indulge.

The buffet was a disappointment. 
We were led past the fish station to the table, it smelled terrible fishy, which is not a good sign that the fish is fresh.
The meat was ok, unfortunately every dish was cold. 
Buffet Selection is not very big. 
My husband ate some seafood, against my advised, he got stomach pain.
The dessert was ok.
All over it was expensive and not good.

Excellent! I guess my favorite person here is Maria! She has very good service! (Don't forget her tip!)  food presentations are wonderful and I keep on taking pictures cuz I can't resist it! Overall is more than very. Will comback!

5 star!! Hands down. Do not let this price tag intimidate you. You will get your money worth. I have been here twice, once for lunch, and once for dinner. I will ALWAYS eat here at least once in every Vegas trip.

Can you say fresh, innovative, gourmet  and authentic for a buffet? Yes you can at Bacchanal! 

Starting with the handmade corn cakes topped with posole, la crema and your choice of at least 10 different homemade salsas, some 20 bottles of specialty hot sauces, and a side of spicy cactus and jicama salad, for a minute I thought I was in a Mexican restaurant. That is until I hit the Asian section with delectable dim sum, stir-fries, poki and dragon roll sushi! Accept then I saw the fried chicken and sliders, carved rib eye, prime rib and sausages in the American section.To the point, each station was like a restaurant unto itself, spouting fresh and unique ingredients without sacrificing original flavor. The decor is modern and inviting, with glass canisters of veggies and spices lining the food stations and colorful glass dividers. I didn't even make it to the fresh seafood section with crab legs, oyster shooters, fresh mussels and shrimp, that I saw on the way out. Did I mention the dessert bar? Oh yes. A must visit experience updated and done right... don't miss it!

New waiting system, you first come in and get ticket they will tell you the wait time, you can come back when your table it's almost ready. They should do this for all the buffet at Vegas. :) (wait it's less than 20min. After you come back from the time they text you)

Over all food quality it's one of the best I would say, great quality for the price and many selection. Fresh sea food, king crab leg, oyster. Very good prime ribs, and they got the bomb chicken soup. 

Love the trendy decor, try to get the seat next to the window by the pool, it's really nice, great with groups of friend. 

Definitely the buffet of Vegas, I would come back every time cus their wait it's a lot shorter now.

This review is so long over due but I thought I'd post it anyway.  

We went to Bacchanal during Bacchanal's b-day which was a Tuesday (9/10) and the day before my b-day (9/11).  

After looking through food pics and reading reviews about this place on yelp before our Vegas trip and I was so stoked to finally try it.

My husband and I purchased the B.o.B 24-hr. pass. which cost $49.99/person + $25 upgrade for Bacchanal.  We went to Paris for breakfast, watched the Mac King Show (which was awesome!), gave our money to the craps machine, and then went to Bacchanal for late lunch/linner.  

There was two people ahead of us when we came around 4ish.  The place was massive and very fancy compare to all the other buffets I've been to in Vegas.

They have a great selection of food which consisted of a variety of Asian food (including BBQ pork, duck, short ribs, dim sum, soups, sushi, noodles, rice and more), Italian food (pastas, pizzas, meats, hot crab legs and cheeses), Latin food (tacos and other stuff I didn't get to try), American food (burgers, steaks, fried chicken strips, fries, tots, salads and BBQ sausages and meat), Seafood (shrimp, crabs, clams, oysters and more) and my favorite of all desserts! (see pics)

I enjoyed everything I ate and thought the food had nice presentation and quality.   (see pics).  I thought this buffet was the best over all (food quality, variety, bambiance and service) from the B.o.B list but somehow I thought the Rio Seafood buffet, though not as fancy had better tasting seafood and hot 
food.  Still, this buffet was pretty good and was worth trying.

The Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace was a big disappointment, especially with a 4-star Yelp review.  We got to the buffet at 6 pm to put our names in, which the hostess wouldn't allow.  We had to either wait in line for 30 minutes or come back and try our luck in an hour and boy what a difference that hour made.  We came back in an hour and were treated to a 2-hour wait in line.  No problem there.  We took the risk, but when we attempted to use the self-service machine to put our names in, the hostess promptly took the printout from us and ripped it up saying we had to wait in line.  This strategy is baffling for a casino, why would you want people to wait two hours in line when they could be on the floor gambling?

We finally got seated in the very back of the restaurant by the Asian food.  The seats that are against the wall are very cold as the AC is funneled along the back wall, so be sure you bring a sweater or wrap.  Our server was prompted and cleared out our plates as soon as we were done.  

The food was very disappointing.  The king crab legs and stone crab legs tasted like they were frozen and the texture was grainy with no flavor.  The mussles and oysters also had a mealy texture.  The only seafood that was decent had some kind of sauce to cover up the bland taste.  The dim sum was straight up inedible.  

The sushi, the meat and cheese section, and the dessert were the best sections in the buffet.  While these sections were the saving grace of the buffet, they did not make the price of admission worth the trip.  If you're looking for value, go to one of the fine dining restaurant than this disastrous buffet.
Worth it for the higher price vs other Vegas buffets. Best seafood and over all food variety. Quality is here! I left very satisfied.

GREAT buffet!  Seafood and Meat stations were the definite stars and make the price tag worth it.  The variety was amazing... loved the selection at the meat, seafood, and dessert stations.  The meatball from the Italian station was surprisingly delicious.  Skip the sushi and the sliders.  The crepe station at the dessert area was amazing, just wish they had apple as well as berries (not a big deal).  The gelato in the coconut cone was the perfect finish!!!  Definite go!
Well I didn't have much choice. I don't eat pork,  and their most of the dishes have pork.  I would suggest they keep more seafood items so that people who don't eat pork can enjoy! :)

Horrible management! my friend and I were there for New Year, we took a number and after 20 mins received a text message telling us its the time. But when we returned we figured out its not ready for us, the line is ready for us to be waiting in. So literary you have to take a number and wait to be arranged into the line! How insane this is? Cannot you simply ask the customer to be there when they can enter and dine? wasting hundreds of people's time everyday! Donot go to such an arrogant resturant

Set aside a lot of time if you want to eat here, but food was very good. On a Thursday in July, party of 2, here's the times: we arrived at the kiosks at about 7:30 pm. Stated the wait time was up to 81 minutes, which was ok by us, so we put in our cell number and got a ticket stating to come back at 8:54. We received texts starting at 8:40, telling us to report back to get in line. After finishing our drinks at another spot, we walked back over and reported to the kiosk podium, got there at 8:59. Took 10 more minutes to get through that line, to get to the register to pay. Another 30 minutes in the party-of-2 line, before we were seated. As we got to the front, it was now 9:45, and the staff was clearing out the display cases for seafood. The waitress said they stop seating at 10:00, and stop refreshing the food stations at 10:30. By 10:40, they were clearing out all stations except the desserts. 

Food was excellent, although we didn't get to the seafood. 

Cleanliness was horrible, it seemed there were no busboy staff at all. At least 5 tables around us filled with stacked used dishes that were never cleared. 

I would go for lunchtime instead.

The price might be a little bit high($110 for 2 ppl), but the food is worth it. Love the oyster, eat 3 dishes of it. The Chinese food is good. And the cake is tasty. Oh, and I also love the ice tea in there

Everyone was raving about this place and I've decided to check it out. It was extremely disappointing. The food was just so so, far from being good, definitely not worth the price of admission.

Some of the staff behind the counter were rude.

Someone had told me I had to try this place...
I came on my birthday with a party of 7, we had to wait over an hour before walking into heaven!!

This is by far the best buffet ever! They have everything you can imagine and for $7(I think) you can have bottomless mimosas with your food (before 4pm) they have everything!  from dim sum, to prime rib to Mexican to Asian and even a dessert bar filled with macarons, halo halo, and sooo very much more

Be prepared to eat like kings and feast ! 

Our waitress was super amazing, she always came around and was in top of refilling our drinks especially our bottomless mimosas!

Invest your time and money to try it once, it'll have you hooked.

No buffet will ever be the same.

Bacchanal buffet at Cesar's is billed as a once in a lifetime experience for anyone visiting the strip. This is my second time visiting the establishment. The first time I wasn't that impressed but I wanted to give it a second try. Well I still feel the same way as the first time. I will break this review into a few parts presentation, taste, price
Presentation
1. It is a labyrinth of food stations that stretch as far as the eye can see. The is no shortage of imagination that went into this buffet. The dining area is ornate and immaculate but what would you expect from Cesar. He is known to oversee only the best. The wait staff are attentive, there is a 5 extra charge for unlimited champagne(will discuss that later) the stations run the gamut for anyone's culinary needs. Seafood station, traditional breakfast station, southern comfort food (their version of soul food but without the soul) a carving station, a Mexican tapas station (tapas is Spanish but here it's a Mexican idea) fruits, bread station, pizza, pastas, did I mention an omelette area, and if you still haven't seen enough food they have an Asian section for sushi lovers, stir fry, dumplings and traditional Chinese foods.. The presentation along is worthy of 5 stars. After you've exhausted yourself with what's on the menu you can then try to figure out where to start. It's a long day of food.
The food
 Sadly this is where the mark was lost in my opinion. The warmers don't exactly keep the food warm so if you don't get whatever you plan on dining in within the first 5 minutes it's gonna be cold or lukewarm. Majority of the food tastes overlooked. It must be pretty difficult to make 10 gallons of Mac and cheese and keep the cheese warm. The shrimp and grits by far is the best thing on the menu and the seafood station lives up to a feast even Poseidon would be proud of. Cesar knows fish, seafood, & lobster. And since everything is served cold you don't really expect it to be warm. If you've had eggs before you can have them every way the chicken never thought about when she laid her eggs for consumption. Side note their cold so just go to the omelette station and ask them to do eggs for you however you like it. All in all the food was decent just cold.
The price..... Well it's Vegas so even a golden Corral buffet will be over priced so no complaints there. I mean if you're coming to the strip expecting to pay a low fat for a kings ransom in food you have visited the wrong establishment... Might as well splurge 5 bucks for unlimited mimosas cause nothing says brunch quite like bubbly and a buffet fit for a king. Will I visit this place again.. Probably so cause I try to support total rewards places but is this the best Vegas buffet not for me. That title remains with Wicked Spoon at the cosmopolitan but if you're in the area come down and say hello to Cesar and buy his food. 1/10/16

Save your money. No need to spend $53.00. Highly over rated buffet. 
I have had much better Vegas buffets for $30.

Buffet was good and offered a good variety. Much better than The Buffet in Aria that we been to. Quality is much better than most other buffets you can find in Vegas. Though Memorial Day weekend pricing plus tip put the price for two at $175.00. The  reason I decided to remove one star was because I thought it was a little pricey even for what we got, we waited a total of almost two hours, and we never even got a menu for the caviar menu. Nonetheless, the service seemed to be good for the number of people there. The waiter got me a refill on my drink without me having to ask, within 1 minute of me finishing my drink.
Overpriced for slightly above average food. Very nice, clean and the food was fresh. I had to over stuff myself to feel like I got my moneys worth. There wasn't anything that I really hated or loved.

It is indeed the best buffet in Las vagas.  I was on vacation here on November 2014.

It is about $55 per person before tax. The selection is huge.  It is much better than Bellagio. Considering bellagio is only $40, I still think ceasar palace is better. How often do you come to Vegas?  Don't mind the extra $15. 

The BBQ pit is the best, they have lambs,  ribs,  skillets,  and ribeye.  For seafood,  they have king crabs,  and fresh oysters.  The Chinese food section was impressive too. I was a little disappointed about the sushi though,  But It is alright. 

While you are in vagas,  you gotta try this place.

I am not really much of a buffet person, but my mother and I really did enjoy our dinner at the Bacchanal Buffet. I like how the food at all of the stations is made fresh and they cook it right in front of you. The desert station is also amazing! While the food is expensive, it is worth the money you pay!

Came here with high expectations after reading the reviews.  I've been to many buffets all over the world, and I must say that the buffet here is mediocre at best.  It is quite pricey (almost 140 dollars for 2 people including 15% tip).  There is a large selection, including a seafood section, western-style meats section, chinese food section, sushi section, and a taco station.  There is also a wide selection of desserts.  I ate quite a bit of seafood - crab legs, oysters, shrimp.  They were average and nothing to shout about - oysters were not very fresh.  I was impressed that they had a roasted suckling pig - however, it was a let down as the skin was soggy and not crispy at all.  The rest of the food was ok, but the worst was probably the sushi - rice was not cooked properly.  

All in all, a less than stellar experience with a large selection of food (though i've seen more selections in other buffets in other countries), with mediocre to average food quality.

Bombskiiiz!!! This buffet is by far the best buffet I have been to! They have every type of food you can imagine! Chinese, italian, mexican, american, indian! Ohh and dont get me started on the desserts!! Ayy diohh miooo!! That topped it!! All that fancy dessert  you see on tv, I got a taste of it here! Lol

I'm such a sucker for this buffet.  I don't know why.  It's not empirically better than the other buffets, but it always ends up being somewhat convenient.  

They have an incredible variety of foods.  Typically I go crazy on the crab legs (like most asians do).  The oysters look iffy to me at times, so I usually don't get them.   The prepared foods at the seafood counter are sometimes pretty good, so don't be shy about trying them.  The crawfish are obviously all frozen, but the dish is still worth trying.  

They have a pretty sparse sushi section if you're the type that likes to pig out at the sushi bar.  The selections they do have are kind of bleh.  The Chinese food section is actually pretty robust.  They have a couple traditional chinese soups as well as traditional porridge.  

There's a mexican section.  And a pizza bar.  But honestly these are all sections I don't often get food from.  The meat section is always nice.  They do have a medium prime rib available so for those of you sick of going to a vegas buffet and getting a well done prime rib, this place is better on that front.  They also have some delicious sausages here too :)

I would be remiss in not bringing up the dessert bar.  They have one of the larger dessert bars compared to most buffets.  They have an excellent ice cream selection but I do have to criticize them for discontinuing the mochi ice creams in early 2016 :(

Why 
Is
This 
Place
So
Good

As of 12/12/15 Brunch was $49.99

Is it worth it? Every last penny. 

All I can say is Stone Crab Claws. I ate maybe 22 of these and I feel like I got my money worth. 

Chinese station- fried rice (杭州炒飯), garlic eggplant (魚香茄子), fried cod (椒鹽魚片), egg rolls (炸春捲), Mongolian beef (蒙古牛肉), roasted duck (烤鴨), BBQ pork (叉燒肉), shumai (燒麥), hargow (蝦餃), BBQ pork buns (叉燒包), congee (皮蛋瘦肉粥) EVERYTHING WAS DELICIOUS 

You can order Pho, Udon, Ramen from them and they make it for you. I tried all three. Ramen broth was my favorite! The others were good too. The noodles were NOT soggy at all. 

Sushi variety is always sub par at buffets because it's the standard rolls so if you like intricate rolls you will be disappointed. Standard CA rolls etc. 

Pizza, salads, cheese.... TRUFFLE SCALLOPED POTATO is the BOMB dot com if you love truffles. Real truffle shavings. It was WAY bomb. HOT CRAB LEGS. 

You can order tacos from them. Small nacho portions. 

Fresh squeezed juice in cute glass jars. 

Soups and breads 

Roast beef sliders- ummmm yes please 

Fried chicken and sweet potato fries 

Prime rib, chicken, lamb rack (SOOOO GOOD), brisket, sausage links, ribs- ummmm all good 

Paella, crawfish, cold crab legs, STONE CRAB CLAWS!!!!!! This is where it's at! And then shrimp cocktail 

Desserts- currently it's Thai Boba Float (Thai tea with boba and coconut ice cream). Red bean mochi, mango mochi, gelato, make to order CREPES, cakes, pops, MACAROONS. Creme brûlée.... All delicious 

Took you through the buffet line. They have the typical pastas, mashed potatoes, but who really pays $49.99 for that stuff?

One of the best buffets in Vegas, they got everything you can think of to eat.

Lamb chops are amazing,

Food is fresh, service is good. 

If your hungry and want to pig out, with great food go here !!!

The food here is AMAZING. I was lucky enough to show up early and not wait in line. 
To begin, I started off in the seafood section and they had so many options, i almost had my plate full in the beginning. I got pretty much a plate full of Snow Crab legs and a small plate of Sea Bass. In the meat section, the Beef Brisket was a bit overcooked and under-seasoned. The only bad thing I have to say about this place is the fact that I went on a Monday, April 6, and paid about $69 per person because it was a "Holiday" . I don't believe it was a holiday but we were already there and didn't want to walk to the Belaggio to hear the same BS so we just dined here instead. Hopefully next time they don't try to rip people off and claim it a "Holiday" Price

Ok so this is really hard for me as I really really wanted to be in love with this buffet (especially since it's top rated, was recommended by a good friend, and costs ~$60/person), but while delicious neither boyfriend or I really found it memorable. 

The food was pretty good - but I honestly can't tell you anything about 80% of the meal.  What I do remember, given that this was Saturday morning(-ish) brunch was that the French Toast was fantastic, the fruit juices were waay too sweet, and that I didn't even realize that there was a whole other section around the conner.  The most memorable part of this buffet was the dessert selection - amazing donuts and ice cream.

Good food, but not totally worth the amount we spent.  In all likelihood we'll go to one of many other buffets that don't cost as much.

One of the better buffets on the Las Vegas strip!

We had lunch--it was pricey! $41 for a regular priced lunch meal on the weekday! I had the buffet pass--but it didn't make a difference. On top of paying $56 for the 24-hr pass, I had to pay an additional $25 just for this buffet alone! But I don't regret it--the food was great! Everything I tasted was at a much higher quality than other buffets. They had small portions that you can enjoy and then some that you would scoop onto your platters. I can't complain--I enjoyed the food. The extra--freshly squeezed juice--and a friendly waitress that kept telling us to eat, I had a good experience here. I would definitely come again!

There is soooooooo much to choose from, I was full just LOOKING at what they had to offer!

First things first, there's a huuuge line / wait! When I went, they gave us a ticket & told us to return in an hour ... so we had to kill time by gambling. I suggest to go earlier than when you plan on eating so that you don't have to wait for too long.

But wow, there was a great selection of desserts including ice cream, crepe station, cakes, cake pops, cupcakes, etc etc. the list can just go on forever! They also had taco station, soups, salads, and even guava juice!!! Oh! And the waiter even brought me over this peach green tea .... AMAZING! I kept ordering this over & over again.

I would have to say that they get really busy so you might not get as much attention from the servers as you want, but just be patient!

Aside from that, I was full within 2-3 plates but I kept forcing myself to eat more because they had soooo much selection! My favorite was the shrimp cocktail, king crab legs, and all the stations that they had. crepes were good but a little bit too sweet for my taste and also cause they don't use fresh strawberries. they used the can kind :(

We went for dinner on a Monday, which was $55 a person! Pretty pricey, so you better pace yourself before you get too full too fast!

For the money this buffet is over priced and over rated.. the food was dry and flavorless and after eating a bite of the lamb, it just ruined my appetite. The pho was good but definitely not worth $55 a person for dinner. Mostly everything we tried was dry and left out for too long. Even the desserts were displeasing. I would not recommend this buffet and would not go back.

Best buffet in Vegas!

I've been here a tons, mainly because of some work in vegas. After going about 5 times, I kind of know what to avoid and what not to avoid. I try not to eat anything I can get at home. My first stop is ALWAYS the seafood section. Grab an empty plate and ask the guy for some hot crab legs. SOOOOOO GOOOOOOD! And the crab legs aren't small or difficult to eat. Also their prime rib is always perfectly cooked (medium rare)

If you go during lunch, you get unlimited champagne and mimosas included as well!

Their juices are REALLY fresh and their desserts are pretty good. I always forget to leave room for desserts but the last time I went I made room for a crepe. You basically make your own crepe and you can throw on a couple scoops of gelato.

Every time I go to vegas, I ALWAYS go to Bacchanal. If the line reaches the very end of the rope, I'd say that's like a 20-30 minutes wait. Not too bad. The best time to go, if you go to vegas on the weekend, is probably late lunch on Saturday since a lot of people are out at day clubs. 

It's more expensive than the others but there's a reason.

Best buffet in Vegas??  Hmm.  I don't know about that but just don't have your hopes up too high.  This was the only buffet I went to during my most recent visit to Vegas so I can't compare it to any other buffet since they may have all gone down by now.  Anyhow, like most people who are into buffets, I have been wanting to come here for the longest time.  This was on the top of my list this time.  I'd have to say it wasn't bad, but I can't say it was amazing.  If you look at the photos on yelp from back in 2012, and you come to this buffet now, you would be kind of disappointed because there are a lot of foods that weren't available during my visit that you would probably have been looking forward to.  Also, you can tell from the pictures of the quality of the food.  For example, the fish on the nigiri sushi were sliced paper thin during my visit, if you look at some of the nigiri photos from back in 2012, the slices were not paper thin.  I avoided the asian food, pizza and italian meats and cheese portion because they really weren't anything special.  I did try the laksa and it was disappointing.  Seafood was ok.  The oysters were really dirty.  Asked for a thin slice of brisket at the guy carving it gave me a huge slice - it was VERY dry.  The slider was overcooked and dry.  Soups were cold.  Desserts were disappointing - nothing out of the ordinary and amazing.  I'm glad I only waited about 30 minutes to get in (saturday afternoon at 3:30pm).

Our 2nd visit here was a big disappointment for two reasons: 1. The wait was way too long and 2. the food was not as good as the first time.Between the kiosk, waiting to wait in line, and waiting in line  - 2 hours. Give me a break. The food was mediocre this time.
Delicious food every time I come. Best buffet Vegas has to offer. Worth the money. Huge selection!!

Best lunch buffet on the Vegas strip...totally worth the price ($39.99) and wait in line!  

The BEST lunch items: Shrimp and grits (AMAZING), Poki, Sushi, Bbq Pork bao dim sum (delicious).

Unpleasant lunch items: Ceviche (not ceviche-make it right or remove from shelf), Tatami salad (too fishy, maybe the one I grabbed wasn't fresh).

Desserts : White chocolate coconut cookies (yum!) and Jasmine rice pudding. 
Creme brûlée and cheesecake were good, but average.  

Best Gelato Flavors: pistachio and Italian cookies n cream.

Most interesting dessert:
Orange beer - surprisingly good!
Overrated! The meat selection was great until we realized everything was rare-medium. My party prefer our cows all the way cooked. Food was cold, selection as ok, just not worth the 65.00 we paid.

Definitely the best buffet in Las Vegas. I would highly recommend visiting for brunch if dinner is too expensive for you. It is so worth the money and wait! I recommend you take advantage of the seafood and desserts. We waited about 2.5 hours to stand in line to be seated. Sign in at the kiosk and you will be given a time to return. I wanted 2.5 hours and by the time dinner time rolled around, the wait time was up to 8 hours. Come early to get a time and plan to pass the time while you wait. 

In comparison to Wicked Spoon, this place offers more variety and quality. There's only about a 10 dollar difference between the two and trust me when I say you want to come here. I did both buffets in one weekend and wish I only spent my money at bacchanal.

Baller. 

All you can eat crab, prime rib, oysters, everything. This place had it all, and quality.  Awesome asian station with real sushi,  dumplings, lamb chops (cooked medium rare)

 SO many options, your buffet line is literally a half a block long.


Too much to even take in
 And for 50 bucks or whatever it was it was EXCELLENT. So impressed.

Good enough to go twice during one trip! In the number of buffets I've been to on The Strip, Bacchanal is definitely the best.

The price is more than some of the other buffets, but definitely worth it in the quality and selection of the food. There's a number of types of food available, including Italian, Asian, American, and seafood. The Asian food section was particularly impressive as they had a number of fresh steamed dumplings served in the bamboo steamers available.

Be sure to plan for a wait as we waited about an hour each time.

Not sure how this place rated a 4 stars...So disappointed. We were looking forward to try this place out to and didn't mind the long wait. They do have a variety of selections however the taste was a huge disappointment. Overall the meat was dry, the seafood was not fresh, the soup was bitter, the tonkatsu ramen was extremely salty, the dessert were too sweet, the Asian and Japanese selections were minimal. I will not go back there again! Should of spend my $$$ elsewhere.
Massively disappointing. Except for the seafood section. Everything else was bland, dry, under seasoned and overcooked. Not worth $65 under any circumstances.

My husband and I were hesitant about going here because of the line but wow! Thank god we stuck around!! This buffet is so amazing, everything is delicious! Waitress are awesome as well! I will definitely be back when I come to Vegas again!!
This place had the longest line ever to get into...but it went very quickly and efficiently.  The service was great and fast.  The food was AWESOME!  Definitely will come back!

Terrible service no drink refill service after the first drink is served. Plates are left there u till there is a huge pile. Food is exceptionally good but service is crap. Lines were a pain in the butt. First u get in line for a wait list. Then u wait again to pay and wait an extra 30 mins to get a table. Come early if u don't want to be waiting in line.

I really don't get the hype behind this place. Sure, they spent a ton of money on renovating it but does that equal good quality? It just means a good publicity machine.

If you are the type of person who "eats with your eyes" then this is a feast. There is no doubt about the vastness of this place or the sheer amount of food they put out. However, if you care about your taste buds or quality of ingredients then this is a lost cause.

Most of the food was average with some of the meats being downright inedible thanks to the extreme saltiness. Also, innovative and exotic foods are almost non-existent. Sure they have crab legs and oysters but that alone does not justify the price you pay.

In addition, we had an extremely unpleasant experience with the service. The hostess sat us down at a really nice table very close to the seafood and meat section. When we came back to the table with our plates of food a very angry looking waitress blocked us. She asked if we were diamond, platinum, out-of-this-galaxy superstars or something. On us saying no, she said we could not sit at the table, wouldn't even let us put down our plates of food. She was then joined by an equally aggressive busboy and they both accused of cutting the hostess line and seating ourselves without permission. We told her that we had stood in line and been escorted to our table by another waitress but they refused to believe us. They insisted we describe the waitress, tell them her name etc. this continued for a good, humiliating five minutes before the hostess walked by and confirmed that we had indeed been asked to sit there. The nasty waitress then huffed off without even a simple apology. Really ugly incident. I don't care to be treated this way when I've paid $100 plus for a meal.

Until this place sorts it's stuff out, I'll be taking my business to Wicked Spoon where the food and service is way, way, better!

Customer service is terrible. Group of 8 and they had a disaster of a time sitting us and the hostess was terrible and rude. Plus they kept coming back asking for more money. Food is okay but not worth the $70+... oh yeah, and that's the price without alcohol. Cesar's is great but your money can be much better spent elsewhere in terms of food.

Worst customer service Ever.

Not a great contender for food either they boat at being the biggest buffet in vegas but a lot of the food is the same thing done different ways which doesn't take any effort or creativity.. 8 different types of French fries.. French fries at a buffet if I wanted all you can eat French fries I would go to red robin and pay a fraction of the price... Give me potatoes in a way I can't get at a freaking drive thru you lazy idiots..

Everything in  Vegas is overrated, please keep this in mind while dining. 
I had a lot of expectations for this buffet while visiting Las Vegas, unfortunately, the 1.5 hour wait for a group of 9 was not worth it. Chef Ramsay's restaurant looked a lot better and slightly cheaper I suppose. For a $70 dollar buffer including gratuity, this was not what I expected. 
By the time we got a seat, most of us were pretty famished. I had high hopes for a lot of good seafood but other than the oyster shots and crab legs, nothing else was on par. If you do go, get the hot crab legs and ask for the small clams without the sauce. They claim to serve King crab legs, but these were the average snow crab legs in my eyes.

I like how there was a Mexican taco bar and also a small Chinese dim sum bar, but other than that, their lamb and steak were meh. 

Their dessert parlor was one of the best dessert buffets I have had in a while. From gelato to rice pudding, I rate this place a 3 simply because of their amazing desserts. Skip the artificial macaroons since those cannot compare to Pike Place's macaroons.

Excuse my language...But Damn..... This is the best Buffet my husband & I have been to in Las Vegas!!!! We absolutely loved it. This buffet had everything from crab legs, mussels, steak, tacos, shrimp, sushi, pizza, desserts, sliders...etc. I can go on. We had unlimited Mimosa & Beer for our entire meal and we were able to keep the glasses. We came here for lunch and I was very pleased at the service. Usually the wait is 2 hours or more but we got there at 1pm and was treated like royalty. Being a total rewards member we were actually able to get 2 complimentary meals to this lovely buffet. Our server was attentive to our needs and did a great job. The food was delicious and my hubby and I will definitely be returning to this buffet on our next trip to Las Vegas.

The food was good tasting in most cases (steaks did not have flavor). I liked very much the oysters, pizza, lamb, lobster corn chowder and crab legs. There was no lobster and for the price it should be included (two years ago I went to another LV buffet for about $40 and everyone was served lobster tails).

Service was not good but it wasn't the worst. I think that even though food was good it is not worth the money.

Im glad I ate here because of the experience and variety but not sure if I would go back.

I was  so excited about having dinner here on my trip to Vegas.  I had eaten their back in 2012, and it was a fabulous experience.  Sadly, I can't say the same for last night.  The food was cold and tasteless.  There were so many people it seemed the kitchen couldn't keep up so the choices were very limited.  I was so disappointed.  It was not worth the $60 plus a person we paid!

I don't know what all the hype is about, but we came here because it was rated best buffet in Vegas.  What a disappointment.  Food was terrible, tasteless and low in quality.  I asked for medium rare prime rib, and they offered well done.  Overall,  food was not worth the wait.  Don't waste your time and money people!

Certainly on my top 3 las vegas buffet, alongside with wicked spoon and wynn. Must not miss stations: Meat station, antipasto, seafood, dessert. Everything else was also good but I have to choose my battle of girl vs. food.  If you must have breakfast get there at breakfast time, don't complain if breakfast is not fresh at 2 pm. Servers were attentive although our particular server made errors twice, no biggie. If he tells you, "what would you like to drinks?" That's him! Price was not bad considering it's a buffet. $70 meal for two at noodle #9 or Gordon Ramsay's Burgr vs $88 lunch for 2 at this buffet. Not bad at all. Happy eating!

It's really not worth the wait. The food is ok. My family opt paying the additional $30 to get in front of the line which comes out to $85 per person. The wait was 2 hours. There was no way we were standing in line for 2 hours. The prime rib was really chewy, the crab legs had minimal meat, the carnasada tacos was also chewy, and most of the food had too much salt. The service was very slow. We had to put our old plates on another table because they were not clearing it. I can't believe people wait over two hours for this. The pros were the desserts. There were plenty to choose from. If u are looking for a good seafood buffet, avoid this place. The crab claws are not good quality. This place is only ok.

I've been wanting to eat at Bacchanal for quite some time. I found the perfect timing when it was my boyfriends birthday weekend in Vegas. I literally heard nothing but great things about this buffet from friends that had been here before, however started to have second thoughts about shelling out a pretty penny based on some of the bad reviews.

It was one of those places where I made it a point to make sure to include it in my itinerary to visit-and looked forward to it for over a year, and somewhat was the reason why I was excited to come to Vegas. I'm a little torn- I'm glad I did get to experience this buffet, and at the same time I'm not. 

Let me tell you the common and obvious- My love and I went here during lunch on a Monday afternoon, which is cheaper than the dinner rate. Bacchanal if you didn't know now is VERY popular. We waiting in line for about 45 to an hour. Since the line wasn't going to take more than an hour we weren't required to check in at the kiosk. My bf wasn't initially very happy at the fact that we had to wait so long. We had our luggage since we freshly checked out and just got out of the spa, and we were starving. We eventually made it, and paid. Tip is paid at the register. Register lady wasn't hella friendly but whatever she doesn't handle food. THENNN!!!! You have to wait in line to be seated after you finished waiting in line to pay. As we got closer to the entrance I could smell seafood. 

So I'll say this- I think the pricy fee is worth it if you're a seafood lover. I don't care at all for seafood and I'm also extremely allergic to Shellfish. I had failed to overlook the choices before dragging ourselves here. My boyfriend on the other hand was having a blast. Seafood is his favorite food and he also has a big appetite. It was his birthday weekend and I made it a point to enjoy it for him. He said the seafood was very fresh, and he said the crab legs were hella good. His favorite were the baked muscles. I liked the fact that they had some brunch options as that made it easy for me to eat. I do regret eating tomato bisque as a starter. It tasted very weird to me and I think it might've had some seafood in it. My stomach wasn't doing great once I had that. I tried to stay positive and optimistic about the other dishes. Unfortunately none of  the cooked, non seafood choices were rather enticing to me. Even pizza at the buffet didn't taste so great to me. Maybe it was the tomato bisque that had ruined my taste buds for the rest of my lunch or maybe it was the fact that I could smell the seafood that my boyfriend was eating in front of me. I loved the prime rib, but I just wished the piece that I got wasn't so bloody. Thankfully the dessert was something I could get down on. Again, my stomach wasn't going to have it with me. I had a bowl of Gelato which was amazing with some of the AMAZING hazelnut pudding. AMAZING! I didn't care too much for the other desserts like the smaller stuff and the cupcakes.  

In total I came back to get food at least 4 times. I felt fine until I after that bowl of Gelato. I'm nothing near lactose intolerant but damn I felt the dephs of hell trying to make way out of me. As we left the buffet, I had to use the bathroom.- No now #2 but I found myself throwing up everything that I had ate that day. I felt sad yet felt better because I was no longer feeling sick or nauseous. Sad because that was like $45 down the toilet. 

THE GOOD NEWS is that my boyfriend really liked the food, service was alright and that was very important to me. He said that it was good, but still considered it pricey. Nonetheless I don't think this buffet is for me, but if I needed to I would definitely give it another try.

This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas, and my favorite buffet in the world. Amazing selection of all kinds of food. The back room has sushi, dim sum, etc. It's easy to not notice it since the main room has so much already. The food is super high quality. Fresh-squeezed OJ that tastes like it just a came out of an orange. Watermelon juice from real watermelons. Horchata. Lobster Benedict. No steam trays here. Gorgeous dining area. 
The lines can get really long. They offer a "VIP pass" which basically means you pay like $25 extra to skip the line. Look on GroupOn and TravelZoo for discounts. 
Every time I come to Vegas I eat here. And I am a very experienced eater.

Patty was an excellent server. All good was fresh and not. Did the all you can drink package and they were quick with drinks. Ask your server to bring hot crab legs to the table, it will change your life!
Its worth your money only if they are serving lamb chops. However, their lamb chops are bomb. Definetely a place for anyone to try it out.

The buffet at Caesar Palace is kind of mediocre. I have heard raving reviews about the newly remodeled buffet and decided to try it out.

Came here on Monday for their lunch buffet. The cost was 35.99 plus tax, which is typical of Vegas buffets. The selection of food was okay, but most of the food was lukewarm or dried out which is strange when the place was packed.  

The layout of the buffet was also strange as it snakes around and people just stay near the front where the seafood and meats are. The lines for the meats and tacos were long and people blocked the food near there so the baked potatoes and other foods near the area were untouched.  
The prime rib and brisket were overly salty but compared to everything else, it was decent.
The seafood was also decent and but the selection wasn't that great.

Our server was also never around so there was always a lack of drinks. 

Overall. It was mediocre at best. Expectations were not met

There are a lot of people waiting at dinner time. Fortunately, there is a queuing machine. I  arrived at 4:30 pm on a work day and picked up a ticket to enter at 5. Not bad. The food was really good and was worth the time. I love the toasted beef bones and boiled crab legs.

FREAKING DELICIOUS! 
Awesome bite-size fine-dining. AND Great Mimosas!

Group of 10, $50ish for brunch on Saturday per person.
Totally worth it. Gelato flavors up to 20, bite size desserts.

Cant' even describe it.... but it's HANDS DOWN, the best buffet in town!

Going again next time! (Didn't eat again all day)

I'M IN LOVE!!!!!

Was contemplating writing a review for this buffet but decided to anyway. Yes, the food is good and fresh and offers a great variety of dishes. However, is it worth waiting 2 hr in line and paying over $100 bucks for 2 people. Absolutely not! The food sections were poorly organized and the line game is ridiculous. You wait about 1.5 h in the general line to finally get to the cashier. You think you're in right? No! You wait another 30-40 minutes or so just to finally get seated. Amazing. The seafood selection could have been better in my opinion. The crab legs lacked flavor and there was a lack of shrimp dishes. The desserts were not very good in my opinion but it may be just personal preference. The mini burger sliders were excellent I must say and veggies were great. Would I stop by again on a weekday while waiting 30 minutes, perhaps. But other than that, I would rather step into a nice restaurant on the strip with minimum wait time.

Been there 2 times for dinner and both times it didn't disappoint. Well worth price, I liked it better than Wicked Spoon. Be prepared to WAIT or pay extra if you are going during the holidays. Wait times were 4 hours + during Christmas. 
Loved the roasted root vegetables and carving station, brisket was awesome.

One word-AMAZING. Endless food and yummy treats you can't get enough of. Should have started with the Asian entrees then worked my way to the Italian. They had make your own ramen and pasta station which both were just simply delicious.
It's basically not worth the long waiting. It took me almost 90 min to get a table. The quality of food is less than average.

Although the wait was dreadful; great food. The selection was huge. Some of the reviews said that the food was just like any other buffet, but I disagree. Most of the food that they carried tasted very great in flavor and not bland. I wouldn't come again unless I'm ready to feast. The holiday prices are crazy but well worth it if you're with family.

Definitely an experience you shouldn't miss while in Vegas. I mean, come on ... it's the biggest buffet EVER! Not only that, but it's beautiful and for lunch it's not completely unreasonably priced. You also get a discount if you are a Total Rewards member, which you should definitely sign up for if you ever go to Vegas or Atlantic City. A lot of their food was normal buffet-style, but I liked that the chefs also went through the pains of making the food look beautiful. A lot of them were in pre-portioned containers, like the little seafood boil in a mini bucket. So cute! The only thing I REALLY didn't like was the cucumber juice. Yeah I know ... what did I expect? It was gross. Everything else was great though. And don't dismiss their Asian food, some of it is really authentic!

Yes, it is expensive.  Yes, it is the best buffet I've ever had.  Each station serves food that tastes good enough to be served on a menu.  The desserts are ridiculous (lava cake... Wow), so are the meats at the carving station (one of the best lamb chops I've ever had).  I am from San Diego, land of Mexican food and I can say that the made-to-order street tacos are almost on par with those at taco shops in my hometown.  If you can spare the $50, absolutely worth the price.

The wait is long, the line to the food is even longer, the food is bad to so-so, nothing impressed me. The lamp chop is okay if you are lucky to get the medium rare piece. the medium or well-done pieces are dry and chewy.
 
I don't know how it got rated as one of the best buffets in Vegas.

Every time I come to Vegas I always make sure I come here to eat especially since they are the best buffet in Vegas! They have everything from Asian, Italian, American, gelato, breakfast (during breakfast hours), fresh juices and pastries.  The service is good here and quite attentive. If you haven't been to this buffet while in Vegas then you are definitely missing out!

An amazing selection of foods that never feels like a big sprawling buffet (in a good way). 

Oddly, I thought the carving station was the weak link: the brisket was a little dry, the sausages were ordinary, the prime rib needed some black pepper, garlic... something (which is weird since some of the other dishes were overly salted for my taste)!!

Often the fried foods are throwaways at a buffet. Not here. Both the onion rings and the UNBELIEVABLE fried chicken were crisp and yummy. Some of the best friend chicken I've ever had.

Really appreciated the hot crab legs with melted butter. 

I had to take about a 15-minute break to make room for dessert. Glad I did. 

Unbelievable variety. Great quality. 

A lot of Yelpers talked about hourlong lines. Maybe Wednesday is the magic slow day. At 6 o'clock, I waited about 10 minutes altogether. By the time I left around 7:30...it didn't look that much worse.

Decided to use the computers but the lady host signaled for us to start waiting in line. We asked her how long the wait would be about and she replied within 20-25 minutes. This was an absolute lie. It was not even close to 20-25 minutes. By the time we paid at the front of the line, we had already waited for 1.5 hours. After paying, we waited another half hour in the exact same spot! We had tickets to a show so we decided to just leave the line because there was little to no hope for us to actually get seated. I understand generally buffets have long waits, but it was ridiculous for the host to tell us 25 minutes when we waited 2 hours without even being able to see the very front of the line. Overall HORRIBLE experience for everyone.

No words can describe how much i love this buffet. It is "The best buffet in Vegas". I came here on two different occasions and i am still in love with this buffet. 

Location is inside the Cesar's, the price for dinner is quite on the pricier side but for the quality of food they serve is definitely worth it!! I've tried many other buffets around Vegas and nothing can compare!!

What i loved most was their Mini Cheeseburgers served on a Hawaiian sweet bun. I do not like Cheeseburgers but this one got me sold! They were so small, sweet, and delicious, every bite was yummy. 

They also have Lamb chops which i LOVED. Cooked to perfection, nice and tender. 
They have tons of variety and their dessert was to die for! They even have different flavors of Mochi Ice cream. ^___^

This is def. my go to spot every time i am in Vegas!
This is by far the best Buffett in Vegas. The food is amazing. Service is excellent. This Buffett has it all. It is more on the pricey side. Check Groupon for an occasional deal. Its a must try.

I was a little disappointed in this buffet, maybe I went on the wrong day but many of the delicious looking items in the cute baskets weren't there the day I went. There were many good items to eat but the lunch price is closer to a dinner price. King crab legs were great though. The prime rib could've been more rare unfortunately. Still a very good quality buffet overall but hopefully the quality doesn't deteriorate.

This was the one remaining item on my Vegas culinary bucket list. I'd been to Wicked Spoon and a few other buffets, but everyone had been bragging about Bacchanal, so I wanted to jump into the "cool" bandwagon. My friend and I came here on a Thursday night shortly before closing, and we still had to wait 45 minutes. Insane! Good thing we planned ahead and got Fat Tuesdays for the wait.

Once we were at the front of the line, paying and getting seated were pretty quick. Pretty soon, we had worked up an appetite to feast. Immediately, I made a dash for the seafood station, since I felt that was the biggest bang for my buck. Unfortunately that meant I couldn't get over to the Asian stations, but oh well.

The seafood station had oysters, oyster shooters, mussels, crab legs, and so much more. It was delicious way to fill up my stomach. More worth it than tacos, in my opinion. There were also some tasty cuts of meat at the carving station.
