Service was friendly and attentive. I guess it's hard to tell the difference between "I'm still working on this plate" versus "I've admitted defeat." Personally I don't think there was anything that stood out at Bacchanal that made it better than, say, Wicked Spoon. Well at least nothing other than the seafood that made it worth the $60 price tag. Then again I'd be willing to splurge to give it another try if I was with a group of friends that suggested it. Until next time!

I think beachanel buffet is not that good. The food is ok!! The vegetable for salad is too dry and Asian food part is terrible.
Moreover, the outlook of the dessert seems good but it wasn't.

The biggest buffet I have ever been to, this place definitely delivers on quantity of food and options. Overall, it was an A-OK 3.5 star experience and I'm glad I tried it but I don't think I need to try it again.

Try: lobster ravioli, shrimp and grits, king crab legs, tropical juice, steak and eggs, mango and papaya salad

Avoid: Mac and cheese (probably obvious for anyone except me...)

I did not save room for dessert, especially because nothing at the giant dessert station stood out to me in particular.

The wait was only 10-15 min around 11:30am on a Saturday.

Of all the buffets I've tried in Vegas, I can say that this is by far one of the good ones. I know what all of you are thinking....Vegas buffets are all the same. You guys may be right, but with a good group of friends and not giving a crap about your calorie intake, this is a place for you. 

I am glad my experience here was with my group of friends. We had a blast here ! Don't expect gold and lobster and all that good stuff, cause you probably won't get it here. BUT the food here was pretty decent and surprisingly coming from SGV, I've had my fair share of chinese food and here at Bacchanal, it was GOOD! I was expecting some Panda Express but dude. The stuff they had was pretty good. 

Ramen??? PHO?!? PORRIDGE?! Who has porridge ?!? I was kinda shocked but hey, all the food in this buffet was bombay! Maybe cause we were starving waiting in that 40-1hour line but it was totally worth it. My girlfriends and I probably ate $200 worth of just dessert. Haha and some more. ;) But they had a meat station with 20 kinds of meat, a taco station where you get fresh tortillas and make your tacos. Seafood, aqua frescas, cheese and meats, salad bar...typical stuff you would find at the buffet. They also have fried items that they put in these little cute cart looking baskets and different kind of soups and pastas.

BUT THE DESSERT...IF YOU ARE A DESSERT PERSON, you better hope you have a copy of insanity workout after you inhale all of different kinds of sweets they have. I usually hate macaroons, but after I had it here, I fell in love! Especially with the caramel flavor one! I loved the chocolate desserts, talk about melt in your mouth! I will probably come back if I feel like inhaling another 10k calories! :)

I had high expectations for this buffet and didn't think it lived up to its hype. For $70, I appreciated the prime rib, brisket and crab legs. I hoped there would be more quality with the other foods. Most lacked flavor. The sushi wasn't fresh tasting. The other part of the experience wasn't great either: seating. I was near the end of a section and it was pretty poorly lit. Depending on where you're seated, you may have light above you. I had to keep requesting my water to be filled up as well. Probably won't be back.

Great quality and variety.  The lamb chops were terrific and a change from standard buffet food.  Too bad they only give you one at a time, not that I can't use the exercise.    The duck was delicious.  I have eaten a lot of Chinese roast duck in my day, this may have been the tastiest, juiciest I have had.  The beef rib resembled a tomahawk steak - prime rib style.  Really beefy, more like prime rib than bbq rib.  The shrimp was big and juicy.  I am not sure what type of shrimp, but it was much better than the others I have had at LV buffets.  These items I found to be the highlight and difference maker in the other buffets?   Why only 4 stars?  The price is the highest of the top-notch Vegas buffets and can be a deal breaker for some.  If you are not the lamb-duck kind of eater, the Wynn may be a better place for you.  If they had king crab instead of snow, this would make the 5 stars.

Truly the best buffet in Vegas. Most memorable? Shrimp and the best shrimp cocktail sauce with equal parts kick and ketchup. New England clam chowder was perfectly salty, fish and chips to an addicting crisp, chocolate molten lava cake, and those GMO'd humungous chocolate toffee covered strawberries. The best. Save room for those, they're amazing.

Great buffet!  Great service... Until you pay your drink bill... The server who was nice hovered over my husbands shoulder making tipping extra awkward.  Little did she know she would've been treated to a cash tip.. Instead of the amount my husband rounds the check up too :(. We all live and learn...

Best dinner buffet I've been to in Vegas. Choice of cold or steamed King & Snow crab legs cracked and prepared for diners to enjoy.  5 plates later, I definitely felt like I got my money's worth.  Dessert bar is unlike any other, including different regions across the globe.  Both times there, we've experienced outstanding service.

Please be sure to save your appetite before dinning here! They have it all.......I have never seen so many different cuisines being offered...... You can expect to try Italian, japanese, Mexican, American, foods from around the world. This 25,000 square foot buffet will astound you! Save room for dessert! They are hot and fresh out of the oven, scrumptious, lavish desserts. Wow!

Worst meal I had in Las Vegas. I've had better buffets from Indian casinos in Michigan. I'll name it, Firekeepers. There. No, they didn't have crab legs at Firekeeper's, but most of the food, from steak, to the Chinese dishes, Mexican, other meats were as fresh as what you'd get from a sit-down restaurant. I was a bit disappointed, seemed I just paid for the Caesar's name, more than anything else.

The chair and service were excellent. It was a bit uncomfortable sitting right next to people eating crab legs, especially considering how affluent some of them were. Some other places cut the legs in half, Bacchanal doesn't. The meat also had no flavor too.

I'll give an extra star for the desserts, top marks there. Everything else, Golden Corral would probably do better, lol.

Longest line for food I have ever seen. Took me 2 hours to get in. But thé food totally deserve the wait! Everything is excellent!! The beef, shrimp and desert are the best! You have to try it if you are in vegas!

I read a review below that you should go to the Wicked Spoon instead. GO TO THE WICKED SPOON INSTEAD.  Good, that should clear that up. 
  Look I don't mind dropping a $100 on a good meal, but when you start spending $50 a person, the food needs to be delicious and the dining needs to be an experience. So-so on the delicious and FAIL on the experience.  
    So of their menu items were actually NOT good at all. I tried some of their BBQ at the carving station and it was dry to the point of being toast like. Furthermore I don't know who is responsible for keeping everything clean here, but they fail EPICALLY. The place is disgustingly dirty. 
     On top of that I got my water refilled once, and I basically had to stalk the server down TWICE in order to get it taken care of. Seriously this place is not worth this kind of money. Go to the wicked spoon at the Cosmo instead.

When I first walked in, I absolutely loved it. First off, the service was absolutely fantastic. I came here on a Wednesday night and the line wasn't super long. The ambience here was super nice. They had a huge selection of food. I have to say, everything was absolutely delicious. I honestly thought this was the best buffet I've ever been too (even better than the Bellagio), until I had the dessert. This would've been 5 stars if it weren't for the dessert. I was extremely disappointed with it. Yeah there's a huge selection, which I guess is one of the fascinating parts of the Bacchanal, but unfortunately, I think they focused too much on quantity than quality. All the desserts were way too sweet, and there wasn't really anything special about their desserts. The desserts really kinda ruined my experience here, which really surprised me. Not sure if I would come back again.

I came here from brunch on a Saturday after hearing all the hype about this buffet.  I have to say that I was disappointed.  Yes, the decor was gorgeous, but there was really nothing about this buffet that made it stand out from other average buffets on the strip that I've been to. 

The coolest thing here was that you could get your tacos made fresh...but there was always a line for this and considering I'm from SoCal and can get bomb Mexican food anytime, I was not impressed.  Their meat spread was also pretty cool, with a variety of sausages, whole hens, smoked brisket (YUM), and pork ribs.  Unfortunately, when I went the pork ribs were WAY overcooked and had a rubbery consistency.  However, this may have been a fluke because my waiter (great service here btw!) took note and made an effort to ask what was wrong with the ribs when he cleared out my plate.  

Interesting enough, I found that the best food here was the Asian food.  They had xiao long bao, blackened chicken soup, noodle soup (pho, tonkatsu ramen!, udon), kalbi (but no kimchi anywhere?), a variety of stir fry dishes and Chinese BBQ (peking duck!!, charsiu pork, bbq pork ribs). The sushi was meh though.

They had a pretty interesting salami and cheese spread, but that's not what I really want to eat when I go to a buffet.  I LOVED their fresh squeezed juices and got two bottles of carrot juice :9 

They did not have their signature oysters when I went, and instead they had mussels. =/  The dessert was your typical Vegas buffet fare--I was ready to be wowed by the custom crepes and macarons, but they had neither when I went.   They had pretty interesting gelato flavors though--balsamic fig, chili mango, blood orange and baklava!!

This place still gets 3 stars because it is a good Vegas buffet. Just not the best, and not particularly unique from other decent Vegas buffets. For the price you pay, I had expected unique dishes like Wicked Spoon (which was priced $10 less than here that day!). I would rather go to the Carnival World Buffet at Rio for a wider variety of similar food.

Oh, and if you have a Total Rewards card you get a whole dollar off each buffet meal purchase.
Fantastic buffet!  Costly but well worth it.  Service is impeccable.  Food is outstanding with a wide selection, well prepared, and always plentiful.
This Buffet is like no other buffet. You will get treated as a VIP. I went in with a group of my colleagues and we could not have been more impressed!! Try the crepes, they are to die for!!!

Registered via their text message waiting system at 11:30am Friday - It's 6:45 am Saturday and I still haven't received a text saying that my table is ready.  This place is a disorganized, dysfunctional mess.

Very good buffet. Only thing is we waited over an hour and when they seated us, we can see that they had a lot of free tables having opened up another area. There's no reason to not have accommodated more guests sooner.

O my this buffet has everything and is hands down maybe the best buffet in the vegas strip... Yes I said it, best as in better than WS.

why you ask? K. here it goes.

quality of food. Ambiance.. almost the same amount of variety as WS, Bacchanal just had a nod more. Especially desserts. The sushi and Asian food selection much more home style cooked which I liked a lot. This time around the seafood much better and tasty. All the amenities and condiments made the food experience of taste and flavor much better. Also the Spanish/ Mexican cuisine was awesome!!! great Tacos, great condiment bar and especially the juices. 

yes, there are different selections. WS had bone marrow, and yes its delightful and hard to find places that serve it. But it wasn't amazing I thought it would be. However, Bacchanal has a great variety and it's selection compared to WS... what I liked most was after each cultured section there are condiments after condiments. For example, Chinese had there soy sauce, garlic chips, preserved eggs and onions. Thai/ Vietnamese had all the spices, limes and basil. That is what amazed me was giving the customer the opportunity to customize of enhance all the flavors and foods to there specs. So many extras and extra ingredients after each section I loved. As a chef this is a for sure hit and a great way to experiment with your food. Bow down!! and a round of applause and smiles from my side of party goers and restaurant loyalists you sure thought out every little spec to be the best buffet!. Thank you for a great experience... O also a side note i compared WS and bacchanal by eating trying each one in a 4 day stretch. 1st day bacchanal for dinner, 2nd day WS for brunch.. 3rd day took a break from eating.. 4th day bacchanal for brunch. boom! thank you chefs keep it up!

I've heard so much about the Bacchanal buffet, everyone says "it's the number 1 buffet", "it's the best buffet in Vegas". So me and my gf went there but before I begin I have to give everyone a heads up .. get the Groupon... TRUST ME! We got the 2 for $88 deal and even better yet you get a VIP line pass that will save you so much time. The service was overall great, had to remind them a few times about some paper napkins but not a big deal, right?  The food was great, I especially loved the mashed potatoes, crab legs and the tri tip. The dessert bar is great, such a huge selection (cake pops, chocolate pistachio cakes, cookies and oh yeah.. gelato). Next time I come back to Vegas I will definitely return, so yeah I definitely recommend this to anyone interested in a great buffet.

I would rate this place at 3.5. Great service, but I expected the prime rib, and sushi selection to be more on par. Call me picky, but paying for a $60 meal a person, I think the quality needs to step up a bit. Went to the boiled crab leg station, and the server gave us an immense amount of crab legs -- highly appreciated that. I know this place has a good selection though. The creme brulees are a must have!

I brought my family here on a Tuesday, which was yesterday. My mother, my daughter, and I came here around 11:20 am, and saw the automated  check-in stations (machines) right in front of the line, and several people were already using them. Without a doubt we went up to the the machine on the left, and started checking us in. The results showed we had to wait for 49 minutes, and we'd get a text message when we had to come back. Behind those check in machines there was already a line going. At the entrance to that line was the hostess. I thought my 49 minute wait is the estimation to how long I'd be waiting in line, so I went up to the hostess to ask. She (I think her name was Emma) said that I had to wait 49 minutes before I could get in line, so the three of us got in the corner there and waited to be called. Less than in a minute I saw two families come up to the check in machines. The hostess rushed to those families before they could even start checking in, and told them to get in line. I came up to her, and said that it was not fair and not nice of her to treat us differently, to what she got very aggressive, and started explaining to me about some yellow lines in her computer, that the people whom she texted did not show up, and that she had to make sure the line was filled with people up to a certain area. Things she said were irrelevant. She saw us standing there, and when we went up to her the line was not full. I left with a feeling that their check in system is not effective, or the staff doesn't follow it well, or she had something against me, or the hostess lets people, who tip her get further in line.
A little pricey but the food is very high quality for a buffet it has an array of noodle stations drink stations meat stations etc. the presentation is nice definitely a must try if you are in vegas

For the price and options available. 

4 stars. 

I've eaten at many buffets, I know exactly what I'm talking about. 



$52 a person. 



Nice place though. Shrimp cocktails are huge. Crab-legs were ok. Street Tacos were delicious, I must admit that.  Other food items were not anything I would rave about, but something for everyone.

Is a BUFFET.  Like always when you are done. You will be like grrr never eating this place again cause we eat too much. Food is not bad. Service is really nice. Nothing special just more choices. The prime rib and steam crab leg by the Italian food is the only thing that is good to eat. The Chinese food are so so not very authentic the sushi are not bad but the knife work on cutting a fish or very poorly cut. And for dessert the only thing good is a freshly made crepes.

Guess is an experience you have to go through at least once. But for the price you will not get your money worth! For two of us including tax is $120 I would rather spend it at another high-end restaurants.

I was at Bacchanal the 26th of March 2016, so last week or so ago. It was my birthday trip to Vegas with hubby and I have heard all the most wonderful things about this place both on Yelp and on YouTube by numerous people that reviewed this place. I didn't really care about the cost if it was really "that" outstanding. It was my first time in Vegas, my birthday and some much needed time shared with hubby away from family every day stress. I wanted to enjoy myself and Bacchanal was a place I planned on eating in while I was in Vegas. All the hype about it made me even more determined :)...... No matter the wait time or cost. 

So 26th was a Sunday. Actually, an Easter Sunday at that. There was no lunch but only brunch and dinner and on top of that  Easter holiday priced brunch and dinner. Dinner was $69 and brunch $59 per person. Which again, I knew it was gonna be pricey. We ended up paying over $140 that day for the two of us. We waited for 2 hours and than we where put in a line which made us wait another 45 mins of so before we where seated. I figured it is a holiday and this place is normally busy .....but it's worth it :).....so I'll wait. 

So we where finally seated. The server took our drink order, brought our drinks and disappeared .....never to return again. Out of two hours of allowed time in the buffet we where struggling to stay there more than an hour. Yes the choices where there but we where there mainly for seafood as we only eat seafood.......and there where 3-4 choices of it only and that includes the crab and prawn choices. There was no sushi, no hot and sour soup, no pad Thai......and not only that half of the stuff I saw on recent videos and review pictures was not there. Probably 1/2 desert options where not there, pizza was not there, dim sum was not there......a lot of the stuff I was looking forward to having was NOT THERE! 

The bread was stone hard and cold. Nobody picked our plates up from our table at all....not once during entire time we where there. Our drinks where not refilled either. We ended up having potatoes and macaroni and cheese with our seafood "choices" which we clearly would not end up eating if there actually where some decent seafood "choices" LOL. I never thought cheesy macaroni and potatoes would cost me that much. 

We had the crepes for desert and I was planing on pigging out on desert since I don't do that normally and well.....this was suppose to be a place for that :). I went to find some macaroon and there where only two left on a huge empty tray .....the desert options where underwhelming ......I felt like I was in a completely different buffet than the one I was really looking forward to visiting. We also where never offered coffee/tea with our desert.......we ended up just walking out after all that hassle, waiting time, poor customer service and lack of food choices that we expected where gonna be there according to what we actually saw in all these reviews online......and all that for $140+ :))). Don't get me wrong I don't care about spending money on things that are worth it........but I felt what happened to us that day was a complete rip off. Either I was in a wrong buffet or I was stuck in  Twilight Zone going bonkers. I'm not hard to please but this was unfortunately just beyond bad :( ....  

We ended up ordering pizza later that night after we came back to our room. How insulting is that for a higher end buffet Bacchanal  claims to be? We where suppose to be sick to our stomachs  and ready to explode from all the food we devoured ....instead we where hungry :). By the way I weigh 165 pounds ......so I doesn't take a huge amount to make me full.....

Bottom Line
- I WOULD NOT recommend this place to my friends and family nor do I have any desire to visit again.....next time I'm  in Vegas I'll go somewhere else. If you got money to spend I'm sure you will find plenty of quality places around Vegas. If you are on a budget do yourself a huge favor and go out to eat somewhere more cheaper where they are more attentive and caring about their customers and you will more than likely still have a lot of that money leftover from the $140+ I have spent here .....and ended up hungry anyway....go see a show, go shopping, do anything else ......trust me you will be happier with your choice that throwing it away at this place
- Too much hype 
- Not worth it one bit
- Just regular food
- Bad or non existent customer service

Outstanding food and SERVICE!!!!  I don't usually like buffets, but the Bacchanal is COMPLETELY different.  The seafood (shrimp, crab legs, oysters) are out of this world.  There is a great assortment of food.  It has the look and feel of a high-end NYC restaurant.

This is a great buffet with great service. The crab legs were cooked and served steaming right out of the pot. The presentation of the food was very modern. 
The dessert bar was scrumptious. We especially liked the creme brûlée and the lava cakes. The prime rib was sliced right off the bone. We also loved the paella and short ribs. The salad bar was just ok. That is probably the only station that was just ordinary but with everything else, it was not a true issue.

First things first, the food was amazing. Everything was well prepared, readily available, and the huge selection provided a great mix of delicious times. The price was higher than I expected but everything in Vegas is a little more than you'd expect, and with that said I definitely feel like I got my money's worth. I made sure if it, going back multiple times to get more prime rib, lamb chops, and pork ribs which were all to die for. The big downside was the wait. Start by waiting inline to enter your name and number to be added to the virtual cue. Which is nice cause you can leave and just come back when you get your text. When you do get the text about 45 mins later for us, that means you get to check in with a hostess and begin to wait in line. We waited online for another 25 minutes to get to the register to pay. Then we had to wait in line to be seated! In all we waited for about an hour and a half. That means if you get there any later than 8 you are seriously in danger of being cut short of your meal, since they stop serving at ten. It's a great dinner but get there early and be prepared to wait, then wait, then wait some more.

One of the better buffets available to blob out at. $50 per person. I can't really eat $50 worth of food in one sitting but I gave it a shot anyways. I didn't stop eating when I was full, I stopped eating until I HATED MYSELF.  There's a huge menu to choose from so there's something for all. I'd recommend off setting your show up time when it's not peak feeding time for all the cows grazing. We showed up at 11ish and we were sat by the entry way. I got a view of the extending line throughout my meal. It has one of those wrap around amusement park lines that just kept getting longer through lunch time. I was looking for a sign that said "1.5 hours from this point forward."  There was a previous post that stated that person waiting that long to eat dinner. I don't think I would have made it. Our wait time for the line was 13 mins. Good food. There's steam crab available, you have to look for it because it's not co-located with the cold crab legs.

Good tasting food, **It's not very vegetarian/vegan friendly. A lot of meat, seafoods, and yummy desserts. Pricing is a bit high at about $60 per person when we went on a Friday night with a 2 hour limit. After we paid we had to wait for seats which was a bother cause I wasn't sure if it was taking away from our limit. Not sure I'd come back but I'd like to try other buffets in Vegas.

Really, I'm not one for hyperbole, but believe the hype.  Caesars' Bacchanal Buffet is THE BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS (and perhaps the world based on the United Nations of diners eating or queued up in line waiting to get in)!  After our aborted attempt to have our Thanksgiving dinner at Bacchanal Buffet, my parents, the gf and I went there for brunch on a Friday late-morning/early afternoon.  The line to get in was very long, but moved reasonably fast and we were seated after a 40-minute wait.  Since it was a holiday weekend, diners were limited to two hour stay...not that I could eat for two hours without bursting a la Mr. Creosote in Monty Python's The Meaning of Life.

The dining room is modern, bright, but not as large as you'd expect.  The dominant, and most important, features are the long, multi-station buffet line that runs along the exterior and the dessert buffet station in the center of the dining room.  What makes Bacchanal Buffet stand out is that the quality and execution of food on the buffet line is amazingly high especially when you consider the sheer volume of food being prepared.  The ingredients are exceedingly fresh and incorporated into items that are made fresh daily, if not continually.  While you certainly pay a price ($44 for brunch, $50 for dinner), Bacchanal Buffet doesn't cut corners in terms of diversity of selection and gross quantity on the its buffet line. http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=XF8wOzssRcIpzTJkOIa5fQ#ewLgq_cCjrvvVHePLFtF8g http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=XF8wOzssRcIpzTJkOIa5fQ#O3vEnr2Kj_GXz0BlOpYOmg http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=XF8wOzssRcIpzTJkOIa5fQ#4c_IwHr_y8XjodmKWJ41HA http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=XF8wOzssRcIpzTJkOIa5fQ#RZ7vhOqOXm6qqhc9qiS2_A http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=XF8wOzssRcIpzTJkOIa5fQ#J91YSDvd5u6qEGdnwDbjZw Since we were there before 1 pm, the buffet offered breakfast items such as made-to-order omelets and crepes.  I passed on breakfast and sampled liberally from the Asian, Italian, Mexican, and seafood selections.  Dim sum?  Check!  Sushi?  Check!  Pho, ramen, or udon?  Check, check, and Check!  Charcuterie and cheeses?  Check!  Grilled and roasted meats?  Check!  Food highlights:  the Posole Rojo, which was nicely seasoned spicy; the Machaca con Salsa; the meaty Alaskan King Crab Legs warmed upon request; the chilled, peeled shrimp; Sticky Rice wrapped in a lotus leaf; and what appeared to be a very tasty interpretation of Xiao Long Bao, a broth-filled dumpling.  

The Bacchanal Buffet epitomizes American (and Vegas) excess...in a good way.  While I certainly won't confuse it with a fine dining experience, the food is better than the majority of restaurants on the Strip.  Is it too much of a good thing?  Probably, but what goes in your belly in Vegas, stays in Vegas.

Super overpriced and totally not worth the wait. Food was just ok with nothing standing out. Caesar would've been pissed off for serving that kind of food. Definitely a must pass and save your money for McDonald's instead.

Delicious! $80 for 2. When we got there at 1050 on monday, they were just finishing up breakfast so we sampled both breakfast and lunch. Less than 20 minute wait. One complaint was they cleared our table once and gave it to another group of diners before we were done. Same thing happened to a couple next to us. They had to reseat us.

Review is more like 3.5 stars.

Long lines that moves fairly quickly, but once you get to the register you have to wait in another line to be seated. They have separate lines for large parties w/ 4
or more ppl which they don't let you know until somebody checking the receipts says you're in the wrong line...Ughh...

Once seated the venue is really nice and spacious. The seats are quite roomy and really comfy. I hitted up the Asian section first since that had the shortest line. Peking duck, poke/sashimi, were my favorites.

The meat/ seafood line were ridiculous! I don't understand why they wrap around each other. If I wanted seafood I had to wait in the long meat line in order to grab seafood :/
That area really needs work with having a better setup for lines. 

I was really looking forward to trying the green-tea soufflé that I was stalking through yelp days prior, but it was nowhere to be found! Hmph..!!!  I had the watermelon mint sorbet and that was really refreshing which was probably at the top of my list. They also had mixed berries w/ some type of simple sauce, but it was so memorable even till today. 

For me I rate a buffet, by their dessert section. I have the sweetest tooth, and literally need a bib when desserts come by. But nothing really appealed to me and their macarons were so sad! One bite of the macarons and I regretted I even tried them. For a place so ridiculously expensive I had higher expectations. Unfortunately I was not blown away ;(.
Super long wait for average food.  Came here for the fuss but it's definitely not worth it.

As far as buffets go, Bacchanal wins. There are of course other fantastic Vegas buffets, but just know that Bacchanal is definitely up there on that list.

There are TONS and TONS of different types of food here, and the buffet spread is loooooooooong and probably goes on for a mile or two. Maybe. And I'm not gonna review everything I ate lol, but I do have some recommendations!

1. You must hit up the seafood section. Cocktail shrimps, oysters, king crab legs, etc. They also have stone crab claws but it was shit. Our group came in during the awkward lunch/dinner change, so we got to try some king crab legs after waiting for a bit. BOMB! Everything was bomb and fresh. OH and they have this SEAFOOD PAELLA! Omg it was so tasty and packed with delicious seafood. Must get.

They also have butter, cocktail sauce, tabasco, etc etc. for all of your seafood dipping needs.

2. MEATS. You also must hit the meat station. Seafood and meat station is how you win your money back from Vegas! I tried the spicy sausage and brisket..... DAMN! I shoulda gotten more of the meats but my dumbass wanted to "try everything" bla bla bla. Seriously tasty. That brisket has a bit of fat on it omg. So tender and juicyyyyyyy.

3. Fried stuff. Haha I don't recommend spending all your time eating fried stuff, but if you LOVE fries like I do, you just can't help but grab some.... They have some fried stuff in paper cones, like regular fries, regular fries + chicken tenders, sweet potato tots, curly fries, etc. NOT BAD, but I would probably just grab some regular or curly fries. The chicken tenders were dry. The sweet potato tots were not bad.

TRY THIS: get a little bit of clam chowder and dip your fries in it. CHOWDER FRIES! So yummy.

4. CARBS. Is it me or do all girls love carbs? lol. WELL I DO. I know I know you shouldn't spend your time eating all these carbs at a buffet, that's some noob shit. BUT, just a little bit is ok... right? lol. They had a couple pasta dishes that I thought were REALLY good actually, like some creamy alfredo pasta, or mac and cheese, creamy tomato pasta, etc. ALL DELICIOUS! I didn't get any fried rice or anything, but I did get some tonkotsu ramen! Uh... this was ok LOL but I was slightly hungover and in need of some soupy noods so I got some. Not bad lol. The chashu piece in there was fire, but the broth was a little on the sweet side? Noodles were good and chewy.

They also have pizza but they were all whatevs except for the mushroom one. I think that one had truffle oil? Yums.

5. Mexican food section? I mean sort of... haha. They have "street tacos" with several options like carne asada tacos, or al pastor, etc. I got an al pastor taco and it was pretty good! Comes with salsa, guac, and lime and etc. Whatever you want! Also..... ELOTE! Aka Mexican street corn. It's probably not very street food-y, they do it slightly different with like a creamy cheese sauce and whatnot. But it was delicious!!

6. Bottled drinks!!! They have a section of bottled juices like guava, pineapple, melon.. or cantaloupe? And even drinks like horchata and more. I pretty much tried all of them and recommend all of them haha. So delicious and refreshing! Not to mention... the bottles are cute lol.

7. Dessert was beautiful and plentiful lol. But I was too full by this time so I couldn't enjoy them too much. They have tons of stuff though, beautiful pastries, fudges, creme brulee, flan, egg tarts, and tons of different flavor ice creams/sorbets, etc. I tried like a bite of each thing, everything was good. I stuck to ice cream/gelato mostly. It was much easier to down ice cream than anything else I had to chew lol.

I also tried a bunch of other stuff, but if I didn't mention them in the above 7 points, then they probably weren't worth mentioning lol. Plus I already wrote a book. This is it guys. The buffet of buffets!

Was not a big fan of the Bacchanal Buffet.  For my  GF and I, we ended up spending 71.32 for lunch.  A majority of the food here was average and so was service.  Our server was polite but was barely around to refill our beverages.

They had a wide verity of deserts. But, besides the crepes and  macaroons nothing else really stood out.

Tip: Go for a late lunch! (2:15-2:30)  That  way you can experience dinner at lunch prices.

The food quality here is great. I just wish there were more choices. Also, the staff can be slow to respond to simple requests like refilling a drink or getting utensils. Otherwise, four stars for great quality food.

Maybe it was the too much hype but I was pretty disappointed.   Great variety but there is equal variety at buffets In Seattle.  The oysters were disgusting, snow crab decent, meats were mediocre.  Good prime rib, the baby back ribs were tough.  Decent Asian food like roasted duck.  Overall not impressed way overpriced in comparison to other buffets I've been to. The only thing they got going for them is the desserts.

this is a very well amazing place, the ONLY PROBLEM is the wait
be advise.. TRY TO BE THRE BEFORE 6pm, I showed up at 7pm and the wait time i have to wait is around 10pm...

Since alot of people mention the food, I might as well mention the wait time and how it works::
if you have a party of 5 or below, you have to go to a kiosk and type your name and phone number.. (MAKE SURE YOU GOT THE NUMBER CORRECT because this is the notification)..

Once you received a receipt from the machine, MAKE SURE you have your phone all at all times (and ringer on as well). 

YOU WILL RECIEVED A TEXT WITHIN 1 hour (MAYBE slightly more).. once you recieved the text, MAKE SURE YOUR ENTIRE PARTY IS WITH YOU because 
""you cannot have ONE PERSON stay in line while your entire party/family is out gambling.""

once your on the line, you will wait around 1-1 and a half hours because the line is incredibly long.

then you arrive at the cashier, and after you pay, there will be another line (MUCH SHORTER) for the table, AGAIN MAKE SURE YOU HAVE THE RECEIPT!


NOW IF YOu have a party of 6 or more.. you have to go meet the person Near the kiosk for a reservation table. Afterwards, you may have to wait ALOT longer than just 1 hour...

once your in the line, I am very certain its the same procedure, except after you are paid, you are transfered to a 6+ Line which is on the otherside!!!!!

Thats pretty it!..
IT IS EXPENSIVE but it is so much worth it than the paris one.

SPECIAL NOTE:: if your wondering what music they played during my visit here are some nice examples:::

Fort Knox Five - The Brazilian Hipster
One stone - Blauw Associates (Manila bay sketchbook)
Mellow Sunny Side (Feat. Leza Boyland)

Missed the lunch by 6 mins, at 3:00pm, so had to pay dinner prices. The buffet is just ok. In my opinion, wicked spoon in Cosmo is better. The stone crab claws are impossible to eat. Not cracked for you and too tough to do it by hand. I gave up. The king crab claws were good, sliced down the middle, and a little work for those too. Oysters were a little mushy. The stand out was the lamb chop. So tasty and cooked well. Good variety of food. Some items were on the line too long so dried out or mushy. Dessert was average but the creme brûlée was awesome. Our waitress was very attentive and nice servers throughout the line.

I have lived in Las Vegas for about 15 years, and have tried many casino buffets in that time. The Bacchanal Buffet is a higher priced buffet (it cost me about $40 per person for lunch). Therefore, I need to hold it to a higher standard than those buffets that may cost half as much. The food is overall tasty, and they do have a big selection. But I found most hot dishes to be only luke warm at best. I also found the quality, and selection, of deserts to be underwhelming. The decor is very nice (for a buffet), but they make a mistake that unfortunately many resturants make today, which is...normally, when people dine, they want to eat and chat with the other diners at their table...but the Bacchanal management thinks it's better to blast club music so loud you can barely hear yourself think. The bottom line is, there are many buffets in Vegas that are as good (or better), at much cheaper prices.

Awesome buffet, so much variety! There's a section for each cuisine, pretty organized! Prices vary according to the meal, the most expensive one being dinner at $57 (from about 3 pm to 10 pm). The service is good and non-alcoholic drinks are complimentary (aka included within the $57). 
There usually is a line to enter the buffet though, so even if you're not too hungry you'll start getting hungry, impatient, and hopefully will make the most of it!
The dessert is phenomenal, as are the "street tacos" and pizza. I really enjoyed the sushi as well. The fish section was crowded the entire time I was there (and I got too full to fast!), but everyone seemed to really enjoy it!
I suggest going with an empty stomach, eating slowly and attempting to try all (or most) of the food- good luck!

We went there on a Sunday during brunch and the food was delicious. It's definitely the best buffet on the strip. The wait time can be quite long so make sure you get there early or after the rush hours.

It's hard to make a trip to Las Vegas without dining at a buffet at least once.  Since we had decided to do at least one, it might as well be a good one.  One of my friends had told us that the bacchanal Buffet was very good.  He even suggested we try to get there at the very end of breakfast so that we could pay the breakfast price and stick around to where they change over to the lunch menu.  No luck. I guess the restaurant realized people were doing that and started charging a brunch price.  
No matter.  We were determined to go there and dine.  The price can appear over the top, but it is worth it if you consider what you get for it.  There are so many stations!  There was an Asian section with beef broccoli, orange chicken, chow mein and fried rice.  There was also ramen, miso soup and char sui bao (or manapua as we call it in Hawaii).
There was a made to order taco station where you have your choice of meats and the quantity of tacos.  Keep in mind these are the small, soft street tacos, which I love anyways.  They also have the condiments on the side.  
There was a seafood station and another station that had chicken and waffles! I've never seen that a buffet before.  Other friends had the chicken and waffles and they said the chicken was dry but I think it was because they had breasts and I had a drumstick which wasn't dry to me.  Make sure you save room for dessert!!! Sugar free and not sugar free!  
After all that food, it's a good thing we had planned to walk the Strip afterwards.  Or maybe that's why the seats there are so large that you can sleep in them!

The Bacchanal Buffet is one of the best buffets on the strip, but it is also pricey. They offer a TON of variety of different kinds of foods. They offer crab legs and wagyu, which were honestly OK compared to some of the other dishes.

They also have a different menu for breakfast and I believe it is also a little bit cheaper. If you are lucky, you might find a Groupon with the Bacchanal and definitely get your money's worth.

Dessert is pretty bomb here. They also offer gelato.

Great buffet!

Got there just in time for the brunch pricing but got dinner as well. Bottomless mimosas come with brunch!

The first thing I went to was their interpretation of chicken and waffles which is spectacular! The meat selection was amazing as well as the sides to go along with it.

A little disappointed with their sushi. Wasn't as good as other buffets and there wasn't a large selection either. No ice cream/gelato as well. That could've been because we were there around brunch changing into dinner time.

My boyfriend enjoyed the crab legs the most as well as the oysters. He was disappointed on our last visit when Wicked Spoon didn't have oysters so we was ecstatic when Bacchanal did. 

I loved the comfortable seating that this place had, it made my experience more enjoyable. Also, one last thing that disappointed me was the service. We went through about 3 waiters/waitresses and none really checked up on our beverage needs or how everything was going. Maybe thats petty of me but I hoped for better. 

Overall though it was a great experience and we will definitely return.

Lots of selection of high quality food.    Shared pietions with friend alliwing to sample more items.  Highlights were the Brisket, pork belly, and ceviche.  Only item I was disappointed in was the Waygu Beef which was chewy and lacking flavor.  
Staff was attentive and helpful.

This buffet place has gotten so much worse than a couple of years ago. 

Be prepared for a long line. If you want to go for brunch, the best time is around 10am. There was no line when we went. And there were like 50 people in line when we finished (around 11:30/12ish.) 

Food quality is ok. I was expecting way more varieties and better quality food.

Stayed at Augustus Tower (really nice btw) for 2 nights over Christmas week and went to Bacchanal for dinner with family on first night. I'm not going to review the food because you can find detailed youtube videos on all the amazing food they have to offer. Overall the food was good and even for me who doesn't eat meat, I was able to find lots of amazing stuff. 

What I want to review is the crappy wait system they have and the poor customer service at their wait line? table in the front.

First of all, their wait system sucks. Their automated kiosks are a joke. Although we ended up paying more to skip (more on that later) the line, I did originally put me number into the kiosks. Guess what - I never got a text. And with the amount of ppl they are getting, I'm not surprised that the system is not working.

While waiting, we were told by the staff at the front entrance that we can pay extra ($20 per person) to skip the line and not wait. We were short on time (had a show later that night) and paid the $80 - only to be told right after I handed their the money that the "skip wait line" is not really a skip. You can to wait inside. What they did is separate the wait area into 2 sections. All the ppl that you see on the outside by the automated kiosks, well that's just the first group of ppl waiting. Inside closer to the restaurant there is another line - for all the ppl who actually purchased the line pass. We ended up waiting another 30-40 mins to be seated, which I guess is better than the 70 mins wait time we were originally told if we hadn't pay extra.

But I still felt ripped off somewhat. They advertised the line pass as skip the wait line, only to not mention that you still have to wait even if you pay extra. To me, if I'm paying $20 extra per person, I shouldn't have to wait. Their price is kind of expansive (for buffets) to start with so adding that $20 per person really made it expansive.

While waiting, I saw a sign that says that the "line pass" wait line is for ppl who purchased the pass and also for certain reward members. Well I have that reward membership so I went asking a lady in the front if I can get my money back. From my understanding of reading that sign, the line was clearly for anyone who paid extra or for anyone with that membership, which I understood as not having to pay because otherwise if everyone needs to pay, then simply put a sign for that. The lady, in a very annoyed tone, told me no money refund and even if I have that reward membership, I need to pay anyways. I really didn't believe her (if anyone can confirm this plz let me know). I didn't want to argue to her and ruin our night. But either she was lying or the sign was just really misleading. 

I wouldn't mind going back again next time I'm in vegas but probably will just pick a day when I can just wait. Paying the extra doesn't really make the price worth it anymore. I was told the wait time can get up to 2 - 3 hrs so expect to wait if you go during a rush time.

Probably the Best buffet in town with just about everything you want at a buffet , without dragging down the rating I would like to see more options at the desert bar , some things seem simple and predictable

It is pricy, but worth it. They have everything in there! The meat section is impressive and somewhat overwhelming. They also have poke and a little taco station. Everything was great! Our waitress was also friendly and kept our drinks full. Our only complaint was the wait. The wait time is so long at times, we would just leave and look for somewhere else to eat. The two times we did get in, we enjoyed ourselves and the excellent food!

Very disappointed. 
All foods were way too salty, not so fresh, and the service was slow.

The food here is pretty decent...there's a lot of variety and items to choose from. My favorites were the beef brisket, macaroni & cheese and the strawberry spinach salad. My only complaint is that some of my food was cold...granted it is a buffet which means you're walking around with food on your plate and sometimes waiting in line but I would expect the food to stay warmer longer. Service was good.

This is a tough review because we had a mixed experience when we ate here. 

The upside is that there's a good variety of high-quality buffet food. It has the usual blend of mixed ethnic foods and a very good carving station (prime rib, chicken, ribs, hot links, etc.). In the crab line, a worker placed a very generous amount of legs in boiling water, let them sit briefly and then placed them on my plate, which was a great, convenient way of delivering this popular sea food. The dessert area had a large variety of tasty desserts, ranging from dark chocolate to ice cream to small cakes on lollipops.

The downside is that 1) it was very expensive ($62 a person after taxes) and 2) the wait and waiting line logistics were beyond ridiculous. We walked up to a kiosk around 2:30 pm and got a ticket, which had an 8:30 dining time. Very surprising since we were 6 hours early, but ok. We were instructed to come to the center line at 8:30, which was the shorter line for people who had reserved their spots at the kiosk. When we got there, we were told to go to the end of the LONG waiting line. We told the host we were told to come to the shorter center line, but he refused to let us in the shorter line.

Fortunately, a very aggressive guy named Vinny from New York and his group received the same treatment, and we joined forces to work around the dilemma. He called the host a derogatory name that was consistent with his rude demeanor, and we then escalated this issue to a manager on duty and were finally allowed to get into the shorter center line. I hope this logistics issue is fixed since it casts a dark cloud over a good buffet.

Superbly overrated
While the selection of foods may be intriguing it's not worth the price and the attitude of the staff. We had to wait 45 minutes just to get in although half the restaurant was empty. The choices of food go from eclectic (like elk sliders) and to standards. Seafood lovers and Asian enthusiasts enjoy this. Although most of it tasted bland even by buffet standards.

Great food. May be the best buffet I have been to but absolutely terrible inattentive service. What impressed me the most was the execution on the two different eggs Benedict I had.  The eggs were perfectly cooked with the yolks still fluid in the center. The hollandaise was pretty non de script but it didn't get in the way either. All the proteins were great. I had good quality ham, prime rib, sausage, bacon and cocktail shrimp. The Asian food items were good too with serviceable rolled sushi, shui Mai and shrimp har gow.  Although I did find a bone fragment in the shui Mai. 

The service was awful.  We constantly had to ask for refills and to clear plates. We had are server change mid meal too. 

Great quality buffet food with extremely bad service

Came for the dinner buffet. It normally closes at 10 and we arrived at 8. The line looked long and about an hours wait. Luckily with platinum status, we sat right away. The food was good as the seafood and meat lines, the most popular ones by the front, moved steadily. Would have been 5 stars if my waiter paid more attention to my orange juice drink orders. Had to remind him 2 times twice to get a glass. I could tell he said paid more attention to those who tipped him first before eating rather than at the end. I left him 10 as I was leaving under my glass even though others probably would have given less. Decent fruits & cakes for dessert although some of my strawberries weren't the freshest. Atmosphere is nice with mood lighting in some rooms and bright dining room lights in other sections.

Hands down to my best buffet experience EVER. My boyfriend and I waited about an hour to get in. But it was worth it. When you walk in, you will be surprised how big this place is and how well designed. We didn't get unlimited drink (wine, beer, and mimosas) because they already give you unlimited soda and any other drinks!

The food here is exceptional. I loved everything. They have dim sum, sushi (if you ask for sashimi, they give you sashimi), noodle soup bar, Italian section, fresh seafood, and steak bar (lamb, bone marrow, and prime ribs) were just amazing. Desserts were good too; macarons, creme brulee, fresh fruits, crepes, and gelato satisfied me.

The price was about $129 (including taxes, for two, weekend dinner) but I would say, when you're in Vegas and you want to have best unlimited food, it's definitely worth it!

P.s. beware of food coma

Tips: the line get ridiculously long after 3pm...I recommend to check with hostess/self check-in machine before you line up.

TRY EVERYTHING BECAUSE THEY ARE ALL GOOD!

Bacchanal Buffet is a $17 million project that boasts more than 500 dishes a night. If you want to satiate your Vegas buffet experience then Bacchanal is the way to go. A little on the pricey side ($54 for dinner), but I think it's definitely worth it -- but only if you have 1.5+ hours to truly make your moneys worth!

What's great about this buffet:

-When you first walk in, a photographer will take a picture of you and your party -- making you feel like royalty. I'm totally kidding..I felt so awkward and not prepared, but a nice souvenir, nevertheless!

-Different types of cuisines (e.g. Asian, Italian, Seafood, Mexican, etc) that have their own cooking stations. There are specialized chefs for each station continuously prepping the meal, keeping it fresh & hot. 

-Spacious & clean

-Free silicone heat finger protecting things so you can carry hot plates. A little extravagant, but cool. 

-Great selection of food to please all different types of taste buds

-An amazing dessert station that has an assortment for all types of sweet tooths:  macarons (although not the best), cupcakes, gelato (5+ flavors), shaved ice station, among others. Hands down the best dessert station I've seen at a buffet. So save room for dessert!

-Sliced up snow crab legs taking away the hard work of eating crabs! Makes eating a crab so much easier and worthwhile!

I thought the food quality was pretty good for a buffet. Do remember it is a buffet so don't expect every entree to be 5 star level. Bacchanal is a solid 4 and definitely worth it. Come here and prepare to feast like the gods, but reallly tho...be prepared!
Still the best place in Las Vegas for buffet. Awesome selection and high quality service makes this buffet still the champ along the strip

This is my 3rd time eating here in the last 2 years.  First time was excellent....2nd time was good but not as good as the 1 at time.  My 3rd time was on 6/13 for dinner.  It was very disappointing.  

Sushi-tasteless 
Ginseng chicken soup-was good before but now it tasted so water down.
Seabass-looked good by it was not fresh.
Raw oysters-tasteless
Snow crabs--good
Prime ribs-very good
Ramen----not good
Pho-good
Dessert- cream brûlée was good...the other items look good but does not taste good.
Service was good.  

Overall I don't think it is worth paying $55 a person for this buffet unless they bring back the good quality as they used to have.

I live here. I have visited every single BooFay you can imagine. Even the bad ones. This place is like sitting in a nightclub with bomb food. (no joke the music is great) And Endless great food. I don't think the bad reviewers have an experience of a proper range to determine what can be amazing food or not. The service was on target. They took the plates away immediately. No wait to get drinks filled up. ...So, the food..I can't say enough good things about all of it. ... All seafood was fresh. And amazing. If you don't know the difference. Don't bother. Especially the huge shrimp. Pizza, Salad, bread, sweet potato fries, au gratin potatos, pasta, asain food, all of it. A foodie would approve. And I swear it was Carlos Santana sitting next to us. Dude, if you like variety and good food and fun club music. Try this. You will have a super fun time. LOL !!

Tried it since most reviews were good, but should have listen to the unsatisfied honest reviews, it took 2 agonizing hrs. in line to reach the table which is well set and clean but wait you have to get in line again yes again for the food this time, service was good but after lining up again for food it was just okay not worth the long lines. Sashimi was not that fresh, Todai is better reasonable price & no lines. Oysters were sweet but the shuckers were slackers they were too SLOW on opening up the well liked oysters and they were shucking the tiny oysters not good, crab legs forget about it lacking in taste too low of a quality. I DO NOT recommend to spend 2 hrs in line for a so..so food.

Over hyped - Not worth it. 

Is it big? Yes, likely the biggest you'll see. If that's enough for you then go, you won't be disappointed in the number if choices. But if you think the food will be more carefully prepared than a typical decent buffet, you'll be very disappointed. Also, it's big but you know what, I've seen pretty much everything they had at other buffets, nothing new here. (I will admit, I hadn't previously seen French macaroons at a buffet - woo hoo)

To wit: over cooked beef and lamb, Kung Pao chicken so obviously thrown together and poorly prepared that had it been a Chinese restaurant I would have sent it back, really awful. Crab? Yup, but not fresh, all frozen and bland, etc,

As you make your final decision here's what it boils down to: for what you'll pay ($60/ea) you'll stand in line to get a large choice of pretty good buffet food self-served in a massive, fairly loud room. Same price buys you waiter-served entrees in a very nice, quiet upper level restaurant. 

$40? Maybe. At $60 it's just not worth it. I wish I hadn't gone.

The buffet for holiday the price is up, but the food is not worthy. Most of the food have to wait on the line to get it, not recommended, 2  hours limited time when your receipt printed out.  NOT RECOMMENDED

My first experience here was great. This was my second trip (first time I went for Sunday dinner and there was barely a line) and this time I went for Sunday brunch. 

The food, as always, was great. I'm knocking off one star because the oysters this time were weird and lower quality. Definitely not what I expected from a Vegas buffet, especially this one -- but the vast amounts of high quality other foods made up for it. We got the bottomless champagne upgrade for $10 and it was so worth it -- they stop by all the time and my glass was never empty.

The line was pretty long but they handle it decently well -- we did still wait an hour or so. Just make sure you grab some free cocktails before getting in line (from gambling) and make some friends in line, like we did. Everyone is friendly and chatty in Vegas.

It was a great time, delicious foods. They say there is a 2 hour time limit, but I don't think they enforce it very much. We stayed around 2 hours but after that much time you're pretty much ready to go.

And if you walk out the doors and there is a pool right there!

I've only tried 2 buffets on the strip. So, I can't vouch for if this is the best. What I can say is that this one was so good we went twice! The seafood section is what has the others beat, in my opinion. Small plates of Chilean sea bass, salmon and baked oysters were fantastic. Also, the dessert section has more than enough options. My wife and I loved the carrot cake.

So, after reading all the great reviews from all the local Yelpers that had a free meal here I had to come check it out. So , I came during a weekday at 11:30 and it was $45 errr ok . I am fine with that if it is good. 
The good:
good layout and clean look, great deserts (crepes were perfect and gelato was supreme) , Potato Latkes, fresh juices and sliders
The bad:
The food was not of great quality overall, the Chinese food was old, mexican food was  limited, and it was considered brunch up until I left at 1:00 and still had mostly breakfast out. They are trying really hard to be Wicked spook with Tapas style items like them and really not coming close. fairly angry people working here other than the desert people which were really nice. 

I think they were good but not as good as Wicked Spoon or Studio B and probably even with the Bellagio.

Haven't been here for a couple of years. Kind of disappointed in this last visit. Although we were seated right away, the food was a little off. Some things were way overcooked. I agree with what other people have said, the crab claws and legs were super salty. I don't know if it's worth the $$$$ anymore.

what can I say that thousands haven't already said?  if you are going to do a buffet in Vegas, go big or go home!  the food is high quality and the stone crab claws are excellent!  I could just sit and have those and nothing else.  oh wait, I did.    of course there are hundreds of other items from seafood, to BBQ, to Asian and Mexican. the dessert bar is also extensive with much to choose from between Gelato to cakes to pies.  just an excellent place to eat without feeling like you are at a greasy buffet.  the décor is elegant but relaxed.  the service is attentive.

Pricey for ok food. Presentation was awesome everything looked so delicious and just to pretty to eat. But for the price it wasn't worth it . Dessert was so pretty but out of everything the macaroons were the best and they had a lot of dessert to choose from.

I was very impressed with the buffet. They offered warm crab legs that are split in half so this I definitely a plus. Their sushi and dim sum was really good I had so many dumplings! The have a good variety of meat selections, ranging from prime rib, to chicken and sausage. The oysters were also very good and bigger than at other buffets. You get what you pay for and this is defiantly worth it. Dinner is about $60 a person but you will definitely be happy when you are done

Me and my friends went on a Friday evening. The dinner price per person was about $55. Overall, the buffet had a very large selection of dishes to choose from. We got there at around 5:30 so there wasn't a line.

Asian Section: Being of chinese american descent, I feel like I am entitled to say that the chinese selection was a decent effort. Not the best chinese food I ever had, but surprisingly decent. I tried the beef chow fun, a small selection of dim sum, and the fried rice. There was also rice porridge and chinese crueller style fried donuts. The sushi selection was small for a buffet, but the salmon sashimi was chunky and fresh tasting, compared to other buffets which just throw you low quality sashimi.

Salad Section: I didn't try much from this section. I don't go to a buffet to eat greens that I can make for much cheaper.

Cheese and Cured Meats Section: Has a selection of 5-6 cheeses, as well as 5-6 cured meats. My wife got some honey added to her parmesan cheese and it was pretty good.

Italian Section: Has a selection of 4-5 pizzas, including a chef's special. The pizza was so-so. The italian section also has hot king crab legs. Yummy! There was also this octopus puttanesca dish that I thought was really tasty.

Mexican Section: There are braised meats available, as well as fresh grilled tacos (the cooks grill them on the spot), as well as selection of salsas. I didn't try anything from this section.

American Section: Has your typical prime rib, slab bacon, and other carved meats. I tried the lamb chops which were pretty good.

Seafood Section: The oyster shooters were my favorite dish from this section. Perfect flavor. You can also get cold king crab legs as well as oysters on half the shell. I want to note that the shrimp cocktail was one of the best that I ever had at a buffet. The shrimp were large and chunky and cooked perfectly, not the small puny ones you typically get.

Dessert Section: The ice cream mochi here is really good. They are not the same as the ones you get in the grocery store freezer isle. The ones here has a perfectly soft mochi wrapping and perfectly creamy ice cream. I especially liked the mocha ice cream mochi. I also liked the macaroons that were served here. There is also a crepe station, your typical selection of cakes, gelato, and even some candy jars.

Overall, I enjoyed my experience and hope to come back some time in the future.

OH HELLO BUFFET!!!

I'd like to preface by saying that I typically hate buffets- and I'm talking the entire concept of them. My boyfriend convinced me that this place would go against my numerous buffet stereotypes. It's a rare occurrence, but he was right.

The place is bigger than it looks. Upon arrival, you see the luscious seafood section. Piles and piles of crab legs (which you can also get steamed) and pounds of cocktail shrimp. Heaven? If not... it's close. They had a meat section, which I refused to wait in the line for. I tried my boyfriend's ham, which was very juicy. Along with the meats they had American food- chicken wings, french fries, onion rings, every carb you could think of, corn, and other veggies that they somehow made into fatty goodness. The Asian section included not only the typical Chinese dishes, but they had dim sum, sushi, edamame, miso soup, and pretty sure I even spied a pho section. The asian food was very scrumptious (my boyfriend agreed which says something since he's Asian). The salad section was large and good. They had breakfast too. An Italian section with pastas and my personal favorite: salami, pepperoni, prosciutto and an assortment of cheeses. YUM!!!!!!!! Dessert was crazy... crepe selections, gelato, chocolate covered everything, and tons of fruits.. even good macaroons. 

The service was good- what you'd expect from a buffet, but they didn't let dirty plates rest on your table. I liked it... and my iced tea was never empty. 

I ate my heart out here... but I wasn't letting that $45 entry fee go to waste. I'll be back... next time I'm starving in Vegas after I get over my hangover.

Pros: Food was very nicely presented. The atmosphere was exceptionally beautiful for a buffet but expected when you pay this much for one. They had a good variety of meat including lamb, prime ribs, several sausages, and brisket. The main attraction to me personally was their desserts. They were all amazing but I definitely recommend the creme brulee and lava cake as the best. 

Cons: The Asian food was pooooooooooooooo. They looked all pretty and whatnot but seriously missing some serious flavor in them. They do have a nice variety but they all literally taste like water...=/
Ive had better food for a lot less.  The service was great...food....ok nothing spectacular.   For Buffett Food it was good but nothing special.

Wow! Huge selection of seafood, meat dishes, continental food stations: street tacos, sushi and Chinese food (just to name a few)! Desserts are excellent; great selection! Tends to get busy with long lines, so either plan ahead on wait time or pay a lil extra to jump the line! By far, the best buffet I've experienced in Las Vegas! Highly recommend!

The wait was atrocious and the ladies at the front where you pay your entrance fee before making yet another line to be seated were especially rude. The food wasn't anything special or spectacular and they did not have many vegetarian options as I originally thought. Wicked Spoon, which I had on a previous trip I took is by far a better choice.

Used to be great but now it's just an over priced average Vegas Buffet, the quality of food has gone way down. On my Aug 16th visit, had rubber prime rib, dry tri-tip and not to mention the jerky beef Chinese stir fry, seems like food was left under the heating lamp way too long. Experienced food poisoning at 3am, had to yack 3 times. Ate what everyone else ate except I tried the Cioppino. STAY away from the Cioppino.

Well worth the price of admission, staff is on point with their service. Food is a wide variety from different cultures and in large amounts.
If you come here pace yourself, otherwise you'll never get anywhere close to trying everything.

dont believe those 4,5 stars. this is a bad place to eat. the decor is dark and dirty. yes it's dirty, to the point that youll lose your appetite by seeing the walls and floor. foods are all low quality, lack of tastes, salty, nasty. just garbage foods all around. you are spending 56$ for food that are worse than fastfood. terrible.

Buffet is very nice...and huge. It is a bit pricey but the smorgasbord of food could be worth it if you have a big appetite. We went Friday night around 7pm and the wait wasn't too bad (20 mins). The best advice I can give is bring a sweater or jacket because it's freezing in there. I could barely enjoy the experience because the temperature was so uncomfortable. I suspect this is a planned tactic to get you in and out. Also don't forget to request to have your crab legs stemmed.

After coming here 5 separate times, it was about time I wrote about this buffet. We went on a Thursday evening and surprisingly at 8:45 pm, the line was jam packed! They even actually had a ticket system and our estimated wait time was until 9:45 pm. So we went to a nearby bar and just when we got our drinks, our number got called. We actually only had to wait 20 minutes, we were not amused. 

When we finally made it in, I went straight to the seafood as any good asian would. After inhaling more than just a few crab legs, I scoured the other kitchen exhibitions. The buffet offered lots of variety including: american, latin, italian, vietnamese and chinese. All the food was pretty good but I still felt the reigning star of the buffet was its seafood. Nothing beat its freshness, taste and extra customer service they provide (aka they cut the damn crab legs for you)! If I were to compare dinner to brunch here, I would still say brunch wins. But coming at either times will leave you more than satisfied.

Food was ok , service was horrible we waited 20min after being seated for the server to come get us our drink order. It did have good selection of food. DEFIANTLY NOT worth the $74 a person
. They have you do a keyosc check in thinking that you will have a speed pass but NO! That is so you can get in line. Manager said " It so you know that you will be feed" I know that when I pay usually. Not all what it's cracked up to be we will make the drive to the M Buffet,  Much,Much better and not a small car payment for 2 people.
Hope this helps

I do understand you have to ALWAYS wait for at least 2+ hours to get in which is alright. We were a party of 6 (2 couples, the friend's mother and a 1 year kid) so were to be in a different line so our men were in the line all the time. We 2 ladies, the kid and the mother were outside the line feeding the kid while the mother rested. When our turn came, the staff didn't let us in saying our entire party wasn't with him. She asked them to move to the back of the line so the next in line could be attended to. THIS IS WRONG. My husband came to call us while our friend was trying to explain to the lady. Once we came to the scene, we were right next to them but she still wouldn't let us go in because my friend was chasing behind the kid. After 2 hours of wait ANY KID would be antsy. Finally we had to raise our voice and be firm trying to explain that the mother can't be standing in line for 2 hours and the kid needs to be attended to. Finally, they let the mother go in the restaurant and offered her a chair. They let us in and gave us our seats. We hoped our experience inside would be better than the one we just had outside. Once we were inside, our world changed. The customer service was Fantastic. Our server was great and so was the food. We were there for over 3 hours and enjoyed every minute of it. Yes it is kinda expensive but all worth it and a wonderful experience. I would definitely go here again and hopefully it would be a better experience outside waiting as well. After eating, we were leaving around 3:30pm and there were still atleast a 100+ people still waiting in line to get in. It is a big place and amazing food.

Truly amazing. The food was exceptional, the service was great. There was a large selection of seafood, comfort foods, Mexican, Italian, and sushi. I had escargot and crab legs while my husband feasted on prime rib. Not to mention a dessert bar that included gelato. Would highly recommend!

Well, this was a fantastic surprise!  I've been coming to Vegas for the last 40 years and I can't believe I've never even experienced the Bacchanal!  Like you, when looking for a buffet, I do a quick internet search for 'Best Buffets in Vegas' and this one is often pretty high on the list. For some reason, however, I've always strayed away. Not this trip though!

We ventured over to Caesar's on Wednesday night at about 8:00PM, thinking we could miss the rush. They have a pretty fantastic electronic queue that gives you a time reservation and tells you when you should return to the host desk. We actually only had to wait about 15 minutes and then got in additional line that lasted another 15. Not bad at all. Then, when being seated the hostess explained all of the buffet stations on the way; nice touch!

And the food. The was incredibly varied and all delectable!  The stations included Seafood (King Crab, Oysters, soft shell crab...), carved Meat (try the Tri Tip and Prime Rib!) Italian, Spanish, Mexican, Bread/meat/cheese, Salads, Asian (a wide variety!) and much more!

Do NOT forget to save room for dessert!  Awesome!

Also, the furnishings and atmosphere is very nice and even classier than most. Certainly more so than any buffet you've been to. 

Great job Caesar's Palace!  I'll be back!

Skip & go to Wicked Spoon or Studio B Buffet. If you're into desserts then by all means, go to Bacchanal BUT if you want good, tasty & hot food - then don't go here. I was disappointed. Food was lukewarm & mind you, I got it from the tray that was just refilled. Crab legs were dumped in hot water but that didn't do it for me. Imagine cold crab legs dumped quickly in hot water... what do you get? Lukewarm crab outside with cold crabmeat.

Unfortunatly my experience in bacchanal wasnt what we expect at all for 50 dollars per person! the food wasnt good, especially the seafood the main reason we choose bacchanal. The oysters had rocks and in my opinion were unservable and the crab as really dry.even the meat on my strret tacos was burn like the staff didnt care about it, they spend more time talking to each other than taking care of us costumers. Was a bad experience for me and my husband our first time and maybe last one 

I think the locals deserve more attention from the buffets and managers

Read lots of the reviews on Yelp, got so intimidated by the looonggg wait time mentioned in so many of them... So, we decided to beat the crowd and came to this restaurant on a Tuesday night around 5 PM! This was way too early for dinner for me but I guess our tummies were operating on the EST time zone :) 

What I love: 
- Nice seating area, great ambiance for dinner
- Friendly service, our waitress checked on us multiple times during our meal
- Got seated immediately, but this was probably due to our early arrival for dinner
- Huge selection of cuisines to choose from 
- Seafood bar: king crab legs, shrimps, scallops, mussels, you name it! All fresh and delicious! 
- Delicious dim sum
- Amazing dessert options: strawberry dipped in chocolate, macaroons, lava cake, cupcakes, endless options! 

Not so crazy about the following:
- Sushi didn't taste fresh 
- No sashimi: for the price we paid, I expected a place that offers plenty of options for sashimi 
- More expensive than other buffets

The decor was beautiful.  We were seated in the back corner but I love how it doesn't feel like you're in a buffet room.  The decor was modern and everything was just beautiful.  I heard great things about this buffet. I was planning on going to wicked spoon from rave reviews from my friends.  But were wowed from this place.  What makes this place apart from other buffet is that quality and variety.  We went for Sat brunch at 43$ with unlimited champagne or mimosa.  We were greeted and the host gave us a tour of what was available on all stations.  This is a first for me at buffet. Usually they just seat you and that's it.  Over 500+ ...how can one person try everything. Of course, I have to plan to return.  We tried to get little bites of everything. All super fresh and most stations have ready to made order.   I expected a bit more variety for desserts though.  I love how they have unique gelato flavors.  I had the fig and balsamic and it was delicious!! Then my friends found macaroons. OMG..the flavors were amazing!  And they have ramen or pho! Wow...every station has amazed me.  I dont know how other hotel buffet can top this..Bravo Caesars!!
Amazing!!! Amazing variety and excellent food definitely worth the money not in even in the same bracket as other Vegas buffets!!

I'm pretty easily pleased but I have to think the people who rate this place so highly never went to the old buffet at Caesars? Basically it's 90% of the old food in a renovated room at a premium price. We went for the brunch in Good Friday, we arrived at 7am. $40.99 per person. I'd break my review down like this; Service: 9/10 staff were excellent. Display / Information: 2/10, signs on the wrong food, had no idea of what some dishes were & overheard a waiter ask if they were doing brunch or breakfast that day, so they weren't even sure, but they still charged $40. Food: 5/10, took 45 mins for the shrimp and crab legs to appear, be ready at opening times or don't open.  Honestly, catch a cab to The Palms and do their $5.99 breakfast buffet and besides the room and the kitschy skillets tell me the difference. Fail Caesars.
Big enough. I arrived there around 4pm and not that crowded. Chinese food are good. Desserts are wonderful!

I always hit up this buffet when in Vegas. We usually go around 2pm so we get lunch prices and dinner menu when it switches over at 3pm. 

The staff is totally generous with their portions. Sometimes I have to cut them off. In past years, the guy serving the fresh crab legs directly from the pot gave everyone about 5 stacks of crab legs. 

Other favorites include:
* Authentic Mexican style tacos
* Amazing juiciest briskest
* Tapioca with toffee jelly at bottom
* Chinese style jook with all the fillings including 1000 year old duck eggs

The best ever buffet in Vegas, 

Buy the Buffet of Buffet for 55, then upgrade  it to include Bachanal... 24 Hrs continues buffet .... Hahaha...loosen up your belt.

On Fri/Sat night recommend checking in around 330p with anticipated wait time of 2-2.5 hrs.  They have a kiosk where you check in, receive a ticket of return time, and they'll text you when it's time to return.  Personal faves: siu mai, buns, sesame balls, cucumber salad, sushi, truffle pizza, oysters, creme brulee, and coconut gelato. Highly recommend!

Being the new hot buffet in town creates some congestion. We went during the holidays but really Vegas is a holiday everyday. Line wait was just over an hour at dinner time . We could have ponied up the the extra 20 for line passes but glad we didn't. Noticed a couple that did and they still waited 20 plus minutes. OK, on to the food. I will start with seafood area. The crab legs are meh, cold or hot, yet they are cut in half and smaller than what I'm used to. I always like cracking mine open and releasing the juices. Oysters were fresh. Meat station was the highlight of the trip. I know meat is hit or miss with so many factors. The beef brisket was incredible. Rib eye not so much. Macaroni boo ya. Ribs were decent with a dry rub. Sausage ok. Sushi major disappointment. Peking duck well done. I did not look the way of the greens or veggies, sorry doc. I did take a gander at the desserts and lets just say mmmmm. Hot fresh made crepe with berries and whipped cream. Yes and Thank you!  I recommend going the first year it's open after that I predict a falling off of quality. Enjoy Yaw!
Over priced. Both lunch and dinner cost more than it can provide. It is just famous. The staff are not nice.

If I created a problem and then charged you to solve it, what would you call me? 

Answer: the government or bacchanal

Fight the man!

There are kiosks at the buffet entrance. Just key in how  many people of your party and your cell phone number. Then  it will give you an estimate wait time. You will receive text message as reminder. Come back the wait time on the print ticket, wait in line, pay and seated. It just that easy. Way better than just wait in line for hours.
