I wait  one hour to pay cashier and get seated. Not too bad for Columbus day weekend.

First, I arrived at the Bacchanal Buffet at around 11 fully expecting to wait 2 hours in line as mentioned by previous reviews. We did not even wait 20 minutes to get in. Price is decent for the Strip at around $40 per adult and $20 per child. Other reviews mentioned red velvet pancakes and macaroons. I was very much anticipating all the different flavors of macaroons to eat. However, the red velvet pancakes were very small(about the size of your fist) and there were no macaroons in sight. Considering I went during brunch, I expected some breakfasty foods, but no luck. They did not even have any bacon. They had egg tarts which were AWESOME and the crepes are to DIE for. Also, the crab was a huge letdown as it did not taste very good. Overall, the buffet was amazing and the ambiance exceeded my expectations.

The food quality isn't as good as it was when they first opened but still nonetheless one of the buffets in Vegas that you have to try or come back to. The crab legs that was once the Must Have is not meh, typical buffet crab legs. My wife loves the fresh oysters and I absolutely love....... Get ready for it...... Wait for it...... Wait....... Here it comes........ Anthony! (Think that's his name) the big brother that serves the meat. Dude is funnier than hell. Whoever is reading this please correct his name for me. You'll know who he is if you went. People like him makes you smile and enjoy the food that much more.
So yummy 50 or more Brunch and lunch options...Best buffet on the strip

If you haven't been to a Vegas buffet before, you may be thinking, "ew a buffet?" But Vegas buffets are on a completely different level and the Caesars buffet is at the top. They have so many options and almost everything tastes incredibly fresh and flavorful. The kitchen staff takes pride in their buffet offerings. By far the best things are their king crab legs and fried chicken. Oh and the prime rib and brisket. You can skip the pizza, but really, when there is crab and prime rib to be had, who needs pizza? And their dessert area is massive! With delicious gelato and made-to-order crepes available to you, it's a dessert-lovers dream. They also have the option for unlimited drinks for $15 per person which, in Vegas, is a killer deal! It doesn't not include hard alcohol, though, just wine, beer, champagne or sangria. The total bill for 5 people with unlimited drinks was $389.  So yes, spendy, but I've been to quite a few of the buffets in Vegas as I come here for work often and believe me, Caesars and the Wynn are by far the best. Don't waste your time at the others.

Best. Buffet. Ever.

I've been wanting to try this buffet for awhile now, but the price always kind of kept my party away. We came for Sunday brunch and it was about $63 per person. I was with 9 people, so we stood in a different line specifically for large parties. I think we waited no longer than an hour.

Usually since buffet food is made in abundance, it's made cheaper and loses tastes, but every single thing I put on my plate at Bacchanal was amazing. The churros tasted like the kinds you get from Disneyland. (Disneylanders, you naw'm sayin! So Cal represent) Bottomless mimosas! OMG the fresh squeezed juice in individual glass bottles! I got watermelon and tropical, and my friends got horchata and pineapple. Crab legs! You can get steamed or chilled. Soups are made to order and don't even get me started on the dessert island! I had a nuttella crepe made and had the gelato lady throw a lil somethin' somethin' on there. 

Just... eat there. Totally worth the money and time.

Researched top buffets in Vegas and this one seemed to have consistently strong reviews.  The price is on the higher end, but for dinner, I thought definitely worth it.

I enjoy buffets not so much to gorge myself with quantity, but for the sheer variety of options.  I literally like the EXPERIENCE of having so many options and having a BITE of one thing that looks tempting or novel is not out of the question.

Went for dinner around 8ish on a weeknight, so the wait was negligible. 

There were several stations organized by themes: Seafood, Mexican, American Comfort Food, Italian/Charcuterie, Asian (Sushi, Noodles, Dumplings) and Dessert.

Everything was well-presented and it didn't appear anything was sitting around too long even on a slow night.  

Favorites: Sweet potato tater tots, Seafood Paella (tons of mussels & clams), Dessert (Mochi, Macarons, Gelato -- some eclectic flavor options too!), Charcuterie meat selections, Supreme Pizza.  The seafood, dessert & american comfort food stations were probably the top 3.

As mentioned above, like to try a bite of nearly everything and I think I did with the exception of the Mexican station (there's no dearth of excellent options in Socal).  Also - I'm not a crab leg person as I'm allergic, but the giant snow crab (or alaskan king crab legs) were very popular - I even saw one tiny lady pack a plate high with at least 25. Given that - the favorites above were the standout for me.  Most notably - the dessert - I don't even have a sweet tooth, but I'd say the dessert offerings alone warranted the price alone. 

The disappointment was the asian food.  Lots of option - but all very mediocre to blech.  The dumplings were a shame (chewy and flavorless) and the sushi - well, I had one bite & never have high expectations for sushi en masse (and I thought it was meh), bbq pork chewy, noodles over-cooked & salty and so forth.

The ambience of the dining area is very upscale featuring modern decor - very open, well-lit and spacious.

IMHO - definitely worth it for the weekday dinner price!

Went on a monday around 6 waited an hour not bad Food was extreamly good looked just like their video...only thing was twoards the end of dinner around 830 9 the food quality started to go down so next time im getting there earlier so i can get in at five the $15 per person line pass if you have the money and dont want to wait is awesome! cant wait to go again and make this a five star review!
shrimp, oysters and crab legs! Don't get anything else! Oh and really liked their juices-- horchata, jamica and guava

Really upsetting we were inline for lunch and there was so manny people there they were not able to seat us for two hours and when we finally got up there they were going to charge us an overwhelming amount for dinner not lunch. We were there in plenty of time for lunch but they did not want to honor it. We walked so far to get there only to be turned away waiting in line for two hours. They did not care. They did not need our money. If you go enjoy the Waite because that may be all you get.

Extremely disappointed!

The waiting system was ridiculous. We went there on the Christmas Eve and the ticket we got asked us to come back in FIVE hours. Well, 5 hours, all right, we understood. It was a holiday night. We went back at 8:30pm. We didn't expect that we had to wait in the line for another one and half hour for the payment. It was already 10pm! We paid the holiday price. But No one at the cashier told us it was going to close or the food was going to be taken away soon. There were still around 100 people behind us. Well, it looks that they would have everyone in even after 10pm.     

Right after being seated at 10:15, we went for our first round. The food and the selection was very disappointing. I didn't see at least 70% of food people posted here on yelp. The food didn't look elegant or tasty. I had several pieces of sushi, some fish, some stone crabs for my first round. Well, stone crabs were not fresh, the sushi and fish was very dry. We went for our second round at about 10:30. HERE COMES THE MOST RIDICULOUS PART! One third of the stations were closed!!! Either the food was taken away or staff started to dump food. So they expected us to finish BUFFET in 15 min?!!! They should let customers know in the first place that the food will be taken away at 10:30!!! or They should provide same high quality service to customers once they have them paid!!! I felt even sorry for the 100 people behind us. They may pay the full price only for "sightseeing"! We complained this to the manager. He was very rude. What he said basically suggested that customers should be responsible for being seated late and having leftovers or no food. Then he just walked away! Apparently, they didn't respect their customers!

Taken together, we will never come back and we will not recommend this place to any of our friends. Based on the horrible experience we had, I don't think they deserve the "No.1 Buffet in Vegas".

Dined here on a Thursday around 3:00pm. We were seated promptly and had a server attend us shortly thereafter. The servers were amazing! One person in our group was vegan and the server went out of his way to grab her freshly made vegan entrees (she also had a wide selection at the buffet itself). 

The food is bomb! There was a wide variety to choose from. I stuck to the prime rib, seafood, and asian stations (sushi & dim sum). The crab legs were not my favorite, but everything else made up for it.

-1 star for one of the employees working behind the counter (a gentleman working behind the crab legs/oyster station with facial piercings/septum ring). He seemed to be in a foul mood and was extremely rude. No smile and when I asked a question he answered in the most condescending way. At another time I told my friend I would meet her at the table after I grabbed some tabasco. He rudely interjected without even looking at us and said "You can get it from your server." I didn't know he was talking to us and asked "Im sorry, what was that?" to which he replied "You can get tabasco from your server", still at no point looking up from what he was doing (BTW there's tabasco bottles on the buffet line)

Overall the food and servers are amazing. Without that one rude employee I would rate this buffet a 5/5.

To be honest this place was all hyped. When I went and tried the different food it was average tasting. The only thing I really liked was the bone marrow. It's was way to pricey for the quality of the food you get here. The wait wasn't worth it, I rather spent that money on a good steak, than come to this place.

We came for Sunday brunch and had an interesting experience. We were greeted begrudgingly... the hostess appeared as if we annoyed her! The food was not tasty at all. The mac and cheese was unexplainably gross! The dim sum, prime rib, Asian rices, and mimosas were are plain and bland. The sushi was mediocre. The lumpia was ok. The egg drop soup and hot and sour soup were disgusting, had a weird aftertaste. The Nutella crepes were good, but those are hard to mess up. Pass on the topping for the crepe it is overly sweet and runny. The chocolate mousse left a lot to be desired and definitely do not try the tapioca. The apricot topping and tapioca mix stirred a undesirable feeling in my stomach! The cheese cake was overpowered by cream cheese. Bright side, coffee was good! Overall, I was full, but definitely not satisfied. We used Groupon for this deal, so we saved a little. Would not recommend this buffet and don't understand the overall 4 out of 5!

Good food. Good variety. I paid $120 for me and my wife. I mainly went for the experience and just to say that I have eaten here before. Very good pizza and Asian food. I didn't care to much for the Bbq food that they had to offer. Except for the bbq smoked wings. They were pretty good. The mexican food was good especially the corn and the street tacos. They had a good variety of seafood. Only dissapoinment about that was no sautéed shrimp. I didn't care too much for the Sea Bass either. They also did not have any grilled steaks to offer. Im not big on desserts but from what i heard and seen they were pretty awesome. The customer service was great. Everyone was polite and helpful. Again, overall good food but I didn't think It was worth $60 a person. I probably will not come back to eat here again being that it's too pricey and would rather experience other food in Las Vegas for future trips.

The line here is ridiculous.
LIke crazy long and then once you pay, you get into another line to be seated.

Tis the life of a Vegas Buffet. You would have to come during super off hours to even remotely avoid an insane wait.

Bacchanal is littered higher quality than normal buffet fare. When I say littered, I mean like the back of a girls' 2-door car. There is such an insane large selection, you would be crazy to attempt to try even 1oz of each item.

With that said, I don't particularly think that all the food is ASTRONOMICALLY good, it's just for buffet food, everything is good. Tack that on to an absurd amount of offerings and I can definitely be a fan because of the selection.

Macarons are here! YUMMY, they're not the best macarons I've ever had but for an all you can eat macaron party, this is perfectly acceptable.

Though, this begs the question again, does any Las Vegas buffet have King Crab legs? Because this place was devoid of any.

Let's be blunt. This is Vegas. I've done the buffet at The Wynn, Paris and Bacchanal, and while the Wynn is a close runner-up -- and may even have a few superior dishes according to some reviewers -- there is no doubt which is the biggest, baddest, most opulent, outrageous buffet in these fine United States. If you want baguettes, go to Paris. If you want delectable herring salad, go to Wynn. But if you want sheer eye-popping decadence, go to Bacchanal. And if you don't want sheer eye-popping decadence, then get the hell out of Las Vegas.
Not good for parties. You don't get seated as fast with a party of 5 or more. If going with 5 or more, it's better to split up at check in.

I took my husband here for his birthday...we were lucky to beat the long line as this place is always packed. Though the American food was good, it was the Asian food and dessert that impressed me the most. Next time, I think that we will come back for lunch when it is not as pricey.

We did not have to wait and got right in which was good.Service was good and friendly even got me the drink I asked for that was not on their list.

FOOD
Awful not like it used to be at all
Crab legs still tasted frozen and no meat inside
Sushi don't even try
Mussels awful and dry

Duck and charcuterie was ok but not worth $40 each.

Hubby hated his lamb chops and could not eat them as smelled like burned rubber

Won't come back too much hype for nothing at a high price!!!
凯撒宫的自助餐，怎么可以这么棒！帝王蟹生蚝虾蟹鲜美无比，羊排叉烧披萨提拉米苏布丁每一样都想说：umm~好吃好吃 x100遍 ！ 连粥和油条都做的地地道道，萝卜干都是萧山的味道啊 吃出了泪花～ 肯定是请来了全球最地道的大厨吧！然而才300多一位，甩国内的自助100条街！！

Every visit to Vegas must include this buffet. Lunch or dinner, expect to surprise yourself with 2 hours of gourmet food and drink. Our lunch included bottomless mimosa's which was a nice touch. Went a second time for dinner and was also very satisfied. Line can get long (1hr wait or so), so go during off-peak hours.

Beware of requesting a small plate of crab legs though; they will ignore your request and pile on about 15-20 legs.

There isn't a better Buffett on the strip. This place has more variety than any other and the style/vibe of this place is nice. It's very modern hip and classy. 
You better come hungry and ready to wait 1+ hours just to be seated.  But it's worth it.

Hungry between lunch and dinner? Is that even an issue in Vegas?  I mean come on, people play all day and night here so how can I even think there's a dinner and lunch time?  Sorry, I digress.  We tried Bacchanal in the early afternoon and found that no matter what, you are going to find what you want to eat here.  Duh!  It was an accident that we came when they start transitioning from lunch service to dinner service, but hey, Vegas luck right?  The mini servings trick you into thinking you can try everything, which I tried and gave a good effort. I did enjoy the options, especially the meat station, but was overly excited when I saw they were starting to get the crab pots ready to heat up the crab legs.  Sorry, I have to eat my crab warm - iced legs don't do it for me.  Prepare yourself by having a small meal or snack a couple of hours earlier and you should be fine.  Pro tip - bread is nothing but a filler!  Enjoy!

I love this place.
Not even gonna sugarcoat it.

I want to live in this ocean of all you can eat goodness that is Bacchanal Buffet. If only living there didn't mean having to sign my soul to the devil just so I'd be able to afford rent every month.

When it comes to Las Vegas.. buffets are everywhere. They're like McDonald's or Starbucks, you can find them on every street corner. The thing is, less than half of them are worth your money. Bacchanal, however, is worth all $55 hard earned dollars.

I've been here a few times and there was a pretty decent wait each time. It took me anywhere between 30-45 minutes just to get seated. Once you're in though? It's go time!

I normally go to buffets for crab legs and prime rib because everything else that they have to offer isn't worth the trip the the bathroom later on but Bacchanal has decent quality dishes at each station. There's dim sum that isn't dry (GASP), sushi that doesn't taste like it came from the discount aisle at the supermarket (GASP), and bite sized american food that doesn't remind you of the good ol' high school cafeteria days (SUPER GASP).

When it comes to seafood, Bacchanal has the most offerings compared to any other major casino buffet I've been to on the strip except for (obvious reasons) the Seafood Buffet at the Rio. They have 2 different types of crab legs, raw oysters and oyster shooters, shrimp, and scallops. I probably missed a few but these are the ones that I've been able to try.

The carving station looks pretty good but the only thing I've ordered from there is the prime rib because well.. that's all I really need in life.

There are a lot of other cool things that you can get here as well. Some examples would be a full cheese and meat bar to go with that glass of wine you're definitely going to order, a variety of different salads so that you don't feel too bad about that one plate that only has meat on it, and plenty of tasty little sides such as hummus with pita, and bite sized pork belly over rice. What's really interesting is that they also have fresh juices bottled up! My favorite is the mango juice.

I should probably mention that they also have a mexican station and a dessert station but those aren't really options that I go to because I need the precious stomach space for all of the better things I could be eating.
My favorite buffet in Las Vegas.  This place is located in the Caesar's Palace casino and has a lot to offer with reasonable prices.

Went here for dinner on a Thursday night and the experience was... meh.

Food was nothing special, though I got to admit it's at least not terrible (looking at you, the Buffet at the Aria).  Their selection was good for the most part, other than not having any meaningful selection of sashimi/sushi rolls -- I think they had two types of nigiri, one plate with two below par rolls.  

On the other hand, their dessert selection is quite good and I enjoyed their hot crab legs (cold ones were way too salty). If the price was around $40 per person that would have been more reasonable but at $53, I  expected more. I wouldn't come back as there are other better choices for food at that price range in Vegas.
Best buffet I have ever had hands down. I can't wait to go back. There was great variety in the food. They had crab legs and sushi.

We landed at McCarran late in afternoon and she insisted we go to this place, It was my first time in Vegas and this was my first stop; let me tell you all that this is how you properly start a trip to vegas. I REGRET NOTHING.

First and foremost, the price may seem steep, however, the quality and variety of food is absolutely mind-boggling. Once you're seated, please run rampant and take a gander at what food there is, because as mentioned prior, there is a lot. Start with the crab legs near the entrance. They cut open already for you, all you need to do is eat the meat; yes you read correctly, EAT THE CRAB MEAT WITHOUT ANY WORK. After that, go to the mexican food area and get some horchata in the petite glasses, they are tasty. Thereafterwards, go to the pasta area and and get the meatballs, they are killer!! Go over to the asian side and check out the dim sum they have set up. Lastly, go over to the desserts and get a creme Brule amongst other tasty treats. I'm only skimming on what they have to offer here, but there is so much more to choose from! The service is also quite good. They were always there to give us refills and check up on us. 

Overall; in my opinion for the price, you definately get your bang for your buck. If you or someone else has a hankering for an epic buffet Vegas style, this is your place! You won't regret it!

Worth the $60. I have no regrets--even with the huge stomachache I incurred after the buffet. Most buffets' seafood section is weak in quality, but Bacchanal's is expansive and delicious. You could easily make your money's worth eating only the king crab legs and oysters. 

Some tips I have: 
- wait time is about 30min-1hr from the time we got our ticket
- expedite your wait time by going in a party of 3 or 5; for some reason, there's a separate line for parties of 3 and 5, and they get seated quicker. 
- the steamed crabs legs from the Italian section are WAAAY better than the cold crab legs in the seafood section, and you can skip the seafood line! 
- save room for dessert. The dessert section is so impressive, you could have a substantial meal just off of the desserts. (speculoo gelato was fantastic).

Long wait but worth it, tons of restaurant quality food from a buffet. Good selection of Asian dishes and the best carving station of any buffet we tried.

Also interesting selection of some good cheeses and fabulous dessert selection with lots of types of gelato. Only knock against it was the seafood selection, while good, was a little less than I would have expected.

I wish they would have had some sushi with unagi, but overall there was more than enough to choose from and it was all excellent.

For the price you pay, I expected my experience and the food to be better.  The reason why I say this is because the food that they have there, I could've have went to a buffet off the strip for half the price with same food.  Another issue that I had was that I did not know that the buffet continued on towards the back because no one told us that the Asian side was towards the back, and I also noticed multiple people only getting food from the front side due to the fact that they also didn't know that there were more food options towards the back.  There needs to be a sign or something to let people know.

I almost feel like my review can't be considered complete because I was only able to try about half of all that Bacchanal has to offer - this buffet is huge! 
Park in the Caesar's Palace parking garage, follow Gordon Ramsey's restaurant to your right (don't go into the forum shops) and walk through the walkway by the alcohol slushie shop. You'll pass the huge Caesar statue and the entrance to the pool and will end up right in front of Bacchanal! Yes a shortcut to get you in line sooner, because yes, there will be a line! We showed up at 3:45PM this last time around and there was no line (dinner starts at 3PM). If you're feeling lucky, show up a couple of hours before dinner start time so that you get the lunch price, but dinner options. Be warned, the line can get line so don't cut it too close! 
Their website boasts about their chicken and waffles, but I thought there were so many other better things. Crab legs and shrimp were good, oysters not so much. The cold legs were better than the hot ones. My meal consisted mostly of crab, shrimp, pork belly and sweet potato balls. The street tacos are made to order and are pretty good. 
The yuzu mousse, rum raisin bread pudding lemon gelato and chocolate covered strawberries were my favorite. 
Show up extremely hungry, but also not so hungry that you'll be hangry while waiting in line. Anyone that frequents Vegas buffets will tell you Bacchanal is the best, but there is always the conversation of it being worth the price that follows. If you're a big eater, splurge and eat some better quality buffet food at Bacchanal. If you're not a big eater, spend the same amount of money at a nice restaurant instead. It's fun to go to, but I would also hate to eat here and have plans to go clubbing after if I were a local. I had the biggest food baby of my life after eating Bacchanal!

This is our 2nd time to eat here. When we went two years ago the line was like 1 1/2 hours long on a Tuesday night. Now they have timed tickets so you don't have to wait as long. This time we went at 6pm on a Wednesday and we didn't even need the timed tickets because the line was only around 20 minutes. We went in and ordered drinks and then started getting our food.

The dessert bar is amazing!! Every kind of dessert you can think of. I especially liked the creme brulee and the mochi icecream. It was my husband's birthday and I asked at the dessert area and they made him a plate of desserts with a candle and a piece of white chocalate that said Happy Birthday. I told the server to go and get it from the dessert area and he brought it over and sang.

My daughter is 13, so we had to pay adult price for her. But at least my 2 year old was free.
One tip: Cooked crab legs are in the pot of hot water by the pasta area in the back with no line.

Also the last time we came they let us take the stroller in but this time they made us park it outside by the large party line.

A couple of friends and I went to Vegas for the weekend and Bacchanal was on our list of to-dos. I've been here one other time and it was a great experience. This time around was no different. 

We arrived close to 2pm on a Saturday & there was still about a 30-40 minute wait. Not surprising since this buffet is ultra popular. I'd suggest having a group of 3-5 people in your party, as the lines for groups of 2 and groups of 5+ was soooo long. The line for groups of 3-5 was fairly short (only 2 groups in front of us). 

Moving onto the most important part, the FOOD. Omg this is why I love buffets, especially Vegas buffets. So many great options that are delicious and top tier restaurant quality. 

My friends and I split up and took on a station each and shared everything. Some of the highlights were the prime rib, poke, cold crab legs (OMG SO GOOD), pizza (best pizza I've had in a while), and pasta. Was kind of sad they didn't have a great sushi selection (2-3 rolls max), but not a big factor. 

Let's talk about the desserts now. Oh my god I was in heaven. Lots of cookies, cakes, puddings, gelato, and build your own crepes! 

Overall, this buffet is a must if you haven't eaten here before. I'm always torn between Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon, but overall I'd give the edge to Bacchanal, as it's always been consistent.

Bacchanal, named presumably after the Greek God Bacchus, who was the God of drunken revery and festival.  How fitting.  Truly a feast fit for the Gods and a feast of excess.

My experience here was awesome.  Luckily, my friends and I came at a time where the line was non-existent, but within 30 minutes, the line grew to an hour wait.  If you come during peak dinner hours 6-8pm, prepare for a minimum of a 30 minute wait. 

Firstly, the cost is $55 per individual and if you have a party of 8 or more, than they will automatically add 18% gratuity.  Once you get past the line, they hand you little plastic rubber pincers that are meant to hold any hot items.  As soon as you pay, the hostess sits you down at a table.  While I walked there, I was very impressed with the environment and the decor of the place.  It was very clean, very modern, and colorful with some light music playing in the background.

After I was seated, the waiter took our drink orders and then my friends and I were off to pick our food.  The line of food is around 50 yards long, no exaggeration.  From what I remember, there are different ethnic foods including Chinese, Japanese, Italian, American, Mexican, and Seafood.

It would take too long for me to write all the foods offered but I will write about the ones I loved the most.  To keep it short and sweet, all the food was great quality!  

I tried the lamb chops, roast beef, spare ribs, sausage, sushi, sweet potato tots, ramen noodle, udon noodle, su mai, crackers, cheese, delicatessen, cherry tomato, won ton, pho, crepes, mochi ice cream, and apple pie.

Oh dear god.  What a lot of amazing food.  Its a must have if you are ever in vegas.  Apparently it was voted best buffet by USA Today.  I am not surprised.

Tips:
1.  Avoid peak hours or the wait will be at least 45 minutes
2.  The sweet  potato tater tots are surprisingly sweet and delicious
3.  You are only allowed 2 mochi ice cream pieces per visit
4. Bring loose clothing
Worth every dollar. This was some of the best food I've ever eaten. The brisket, sushi, pizza, and seafood were plentiful and delicious. The dessert was the cherry on top.

You get what you pay for, and then some when eating here!

Much needed escapade weekend to Vegas! Whoo hoo! And when I go, I always remember to put a lot of good fuel in my system to last the whole experience through. Gotta treat my body good, since I am going to punish it on the dance floor.

Ok, so the breakfast/brunch on the weekends is amazing. I've been coming to Vegas for years, and the Caesar's buffet continues to achieve high marks for variety, consistency in flavor, ethnic foods taste like they were made by people who know good ethnic (Mexican, Japanese, Chinese, real Italian pizza) food. 

Now, how does a girl like me eat three plates full and keep her figure? Watch what you eat and make sure it's healthy. And here is where the Caesar's bacchanal buffet excels, as there are so many choice options for healthy eating, as opposed to other places. Variety of fruits and veggies, good quality cuts in the meats with out excess fats, fresh delectable seafood, portions that are well prepared and not meant to bloat you. Solid combinations of fresh juices (cucumber! watermelon! jamaica tea!) .... I could go on and on.....

Spend the money and pamper yourself and your appetites! So worth it!

And the lines have not been that long this summer!
They have everything!  Our favorite was the desert bar, fresh crepes, creme brulee and a killer carrot cake!  Yummeeeeee!!!

Great buffet - went an hour before dinner service started so we had the best of brunch and dinner. 

Service was excellent and we tried all kinds of more adventurous items that we would not otherwise tried like Elk meat sliders and deviled eggs with salmon roe.

Gave them another try. This time for breakfast. We came 2 and a half years ago when they first opened for dinner and we didn't think it was worth the price at all. The food was decent but not extraordinary. This year, we tried them for their breakfast and we were blown away. Not only were there breakfast options but lunch/dinner as well. And they had an amazing selection of desserts. I thought the breakfast buffet was worth what we paid. I would recommend this buffet now.

Amazing amazing amazing! Couldnt tell you how pretty the decor is! I am ususally not a big fan of buffet, but this place is a must try! there are 12 live cook stations. from italian, to japanese, to live seafood. their desert station is probably the best in the entire buffet! BEST BUFFET in town!!!

I will have to say that I didn't try even half of the food available so they may deserve more than a three. I mostly pigged out at the seafood bar, crab legs mostly. For $60/70 bucks, better get your money's worth right? The oysters weren't anything amazing. They were actually still pretty gritty as they weren't cleaned enough. Their prime rib was no where melt in your mouth and their lamb, though flavorful, I couldn't get pass the tough meat. It will definitely give your jaw muscles a workout. 

I LOVE their little juice jars, watermelon is my favorite. They also serve a Peach Green Tea or something, ask your server. It's freaken awesome, so refreshing. The dessert bar was a let down. They didn't have the regular creme brulee that all you yelpers raved about; they had a green tea version which was a 3. Strawberries huge (chemicals!) and not sweet. I honestly forgot what else I ate. I guess you can say that really tells you how much I liked their desserts.

The service was really good though. Both our servers were super nice and checked up on us often.
Hot and cold crab legs, and an excellent seafood selection. Great cheeses and cured meats.

**DO NOT COME HERE IF YOU ARENT A SEAFOOD FAN**

Seafood and I do not get along. We came here for an end-of-year party for our Culinary Arts class, don't get me wrong, the place is great and they do have nonseafood items but its slim pickings and the place smells like seafood, which isn't settling for my stomach. I would come here again if I was seated FAR away from the seafood stations.

This buffet has good review and selection among other buffets, so we decided to give it a try. The overall experience should be 3 stars, but I am taking 1 star off because of the price we paid. With the price we paid, we expected a higher quality buffet. We visited this place for brunch during the July 4th week, so the price for lunch is $59.99 + tax + tips (close to $80 per person). During the holiday, the breakfast costs $39.99, brunch costs $59.99, and Dinner costs $69.99. First of all, one of the cashiers "Grace" is rude, and there is miscommunication between the cashiers, hosts and kitchen staffs. We arrived around 10am, and we were welcome to look at the food selections before we decided to eat there. One of hosts said there will be more items added to the buffets during lunch hours starting at 11 am. If we go in before 10:30 am, the price would be $39.99. So we decided to get in around 10:25 am to lock in the $39.99 price, the cashier Grace was saying the price should be $59.99 and the price $39.99 ends at 9:30 am, not 10:30 am. When we told her the host told us a different timeline earlier, then Grace responded us with an attitude like we tried to cheat to get in at a lower price. I totally understand if the host provided us the wrong information, but Grace didn't have to explain it in such a rude way. Anyway, we paid $59.99 per person to get in and the host apologized to us regarding the wrong information she provided earlier. Then it comes to advertisement issue... Many items from the brunch holiday menu are missing from the actual buffet selections. If you are going to charge more for the holiday buffet, please commit to what you advertised on the menu. When we complained the missing food items from the menu, they said the menu was wrong. So they removed the menu instead of adding the missing menu items to the buffet for their customer. Since we looked around during breakfast time (for price at $39.99), we know what they have for breakfast. At 11:00 am, nothing much was added to the lunch buffet (at $59.99). So basically, they are charging more with no additional items added to the buffet. Last but not least, the food is just average comparing to a regular buffet, but it is below average comparing to a hotel/ good restaurant. I am very disappointed with their desserts. I agree they have good selections of different cuisines, but nothing is performing at the best. I ordered a soufflé from the dessert counter, and it is totally taste nothing like soufflé. If you don't tell me it is a soufflé, I would not able to tell. It tastes like a chewy cake or bread? It is a failure for sure. I don't know what is going on with the food quality control at this buffet. If none of your chefs know how to cook a particular dish, please offer something else instead of adding a trash to the food selections.

AWFUL!  AVOID!  I've had it with the overpriced buffets in Vegas.  Saturday and Sunday brunch price is not advertised on the website and you can't just buy breakfast on Saturday or Sunday.  So, my girlfriend and I decided to give it a try because of all the great review, but no brunch buffet is $41.99 per person.  I'm not opposed to paying up for good food, but seriously, all I wanted was eggs, bacon and some toast.  Don't be a tourist.  

This place is designed by the same people who brought you the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan as evidenced by the posts that hold the ropes for the line.  Unfortunately, they don't have nearly the amount of space as the Wicked Spoon, so there's a ton of seating, but the buffet is crowded by the tables and people coming in.  In essence, you're cramped down to a single line along the buffet and with barely 25% of the seats in the place filled, there were long lines for the carved meat, seafood and omellete stations and there are only one of each.  

My girlfriend paid for brunch since I paid for dinner the night before, but from the moment my jaw dropped upon seeing the price - $90 and change for two people - things just kept getting worse.  We were first seated at a table which didn't have enough room to get into the second seat because it was crowded by a floor lamp.  They did move us, but I was extremely frustrated by this point.

Mimosas are included with the exorbitant price, so I ordered two and my girlfriend went to get food.  She had barely sat down when a child, obviously neglected by his parents, lobbed this little rubber handle they give you to pick up the metal dishes at the buffet at her, hitting her in the hair and then bouncing off her and landing right in the middle of the plate.  It was covered in BBQ sauce, so now she's go sauce in her hair and this thing right in the middle of the plate of food she'd just waited in three different lines to get.  Next, the 'owner' of the kid (I say that because he obviously had no parenting skills) starts mouthing off to us and which point I just started motioning for the wait staff or anybody else who attention I could get.  As much as I wanted to rip him limb from limb (he did quiet down a bit when I stood up and he realized I was 6'5"/300), it's better to let the hotel handle it and I figured this way my chance to get out of this awful experience and get our money back.  As the manager approached, he started mouthing off again, swearing, etc. and I just told the manager I wanted this awful experience to end.  She took us to the front which calling security on the guy with the kid and refunded our money.

Overall, and awful experience.  They did solve the problem and we did get our money back, but the bottom line is it's just another buffet and at $41.99/person, you can go to a decent restaurant for breakfast twice, get better food and not have to deal with the idiot tourists.

Upon leaving, we went to Crystal's at City Center and ended up having lunch at Wolfgang Puck's.  Yea, I know it's a chain and I've eaten at the one at O'Hare too many times, but the service was fantastic, the food was good as usual and the atmosphere was soooooo much better.

* Price: expensive buffet... but everything is expensive here. About $60 per person on a regular day; $70 for holiday. 3 star.
* Ambiance: nice dinning room and decor but very congested especially during holidays. The food counters along the wall, dinning room is sectioned. So one  way in and one way out... 3 star. 
* Location : Cesar Palace by the pool.  Convenient if you stay here. 3+ star. 
* Meals: huge menu, 9 stations. You name it, they have it! Food is high quality!  4+ star. 
* Service: friendly. 3+ star. 
This is averaged to 4 star.

We came here during our stay for 4th of July.  We want to see what all the hype about this place. The wait is ridiculous,  3 hours minimal unless you are diamond or High rollers or you can pay extra $25 per person to skip the line which we did. We still have to wait for another 1/2 hour.

The buffet is huge but the set up is very congested since all stations are right next to each other... so you are once again in line for food. 

The menu for 4th of July is huge. There are 9 stations (seafood, carved meat, cheese, Italian,  Mediterranean, noodles, Japanese,  chinese, deserts...) 
Seafood station has king and snow crab legs, saute clams, mussels,  shrimps.  Everything is tasty and fresh. Sushi and sashimi is pretty fresh. My favorite station is Chinese food. There is frog legs, saute greenbeans, peeking ducks,  saute snowpeas, etc. Everything is cooked perfectly.  For vegetarians,  there are plenty of choices here. 

The deserts are outrageous,  creme brulee,  flans, velvet cakes, and so on... everything is delicious!

The reasons that stopped us to rate it 5 star are the prices, the long wait and the set up of buffet line. It is so stressful to dine here since the line is long; people are on top of each other to try to get their food, reaching over each other. The label is very hard to read so if you try to figure what the dish is, you will get scolded for holding the line!

Is it worth the money and 3 hour wait? Probably not unless you have time to kill. It is worth to try once if there is less than 1 hour wait. It has a huge menu but not all items worth to try so don't fill up your stomach with noodles and salads!

Used to be a decent buffet. Not anymore. No selection at all. Meats are horrible. No taste at all. The best thing was the cheese, however it was not something they prepared. No selection of prepared dishes. Very disappointed. Never coming back .

Finally came to this place since my cousin Tiff recommended it months ago. So disappointed. Its over price for what they serve. Rio seafood was way better than this..the cold king crab legs are salty..if you dont have high blood pressure before co.ing here you definitely have ine now. I had to ask the server for hot water and literally soaked my crab legs and it was salty. Squeezed lemon and dipped in butter, still salty. The hot crab legs are less salty but still too salty for me.. the Jonahs crab claws. Either it is old or overcooked, didnt get to enjoy it l, you have to literally pick it out of the shell since its sticking to the shell, so ur eating crab claw crumbs. 
Now dont get me wrong i had the bone marrow, thats was ok, not the best but it was good enough. The steak well its just like any other, nothing special. I love the yellow tail collar, this is one of my fav when i go to sushi places, once again disappointed, undercooked and taste very fishy. 
The wagyu  steak, not worth it
The prime rib, very hard and chewy.
The dessert they look good but i havent tried it yet coz im writing this while taking a break and tryin gcb to get the aalty taste out of my mouth.  
The server is not attentive. Omg i ate something that irritated my throat so i was coughing, it took the server so long to come to our table then it took another 5 mins or so to get our drinks..
So far my experience  here is tnot bad but not worth the price. 
This place is not higjly recommended in my book.
This is jot a place i would go back to..
If you want seafood, go somewhere else..

Caesar's Palace? I would have done better to go to Little Caesar's.

I have to that, in a lifetime of eating in buffet restaurants, from cruise ship buffets to hometown smorgasbords, this is the single worst experience I've ever had.

We pulled into Vegas exhausted and hungry after an 8-hour drive, and decided to just do the buffet at Caesar's Palace, where we were staying. We'd heard it was good, and, as we both have dietary restrictions, we thought it would be a pretty good bet. Usually we have no trouble finding enough that we can eat on a good buffet, and we were too tired to plow through restaurant listings to try to find something better that could accommodate us.

Before I go on to the food, I do have to mention the price. Yes, I get that everything in Vegas is expensive, but $116 for a buffet meal for two people that doesn't even include a beer is pretty OTT. I don't like most soft drinks, so that meant water for me (or pay more on top of the already outrageous price for something drinkable). We probably should have backed out at that point, but we were starving and we were on vacation, so...

Still, it would have been OK if the food had been decent, but it was just horrible. In fact, It's difficult to describe just how terrible the food was. The salad greens were dried out and wilted. The salad dressings were completely mixed up, and dressings from one container dribbled into others. This was a serious problem, as my husband has a dangerous seafood allergy and one of the dressings was Caesar. None of the employees seemed to know which dressing was which, or what was in anything. We finally had to ask for  a separate bowl of ranch dressing to make sure he didn't get something that had been contaminated with seafood.

On the pizza bar, the only vegetarian choice was plain cheese, and it was bland and tasteless. I've had better pizza from the freezer compartment at Safeway. The rice and beans on the Mexican bar were also dried out and next to tasteless. Even the pita in the Mediterranean section was dry. I have, seriously, had better food in a high school cafeteria.

To make things worse, the steam table in the carvery section was badly in need of cleaning. I couldn't stand to walk past it, the smell was so bad. Really nasty!

Finally, to add insult to injury, the dish of pistachio ice cream I got  in the hopes of finding SOMETHING worth eating for that kind of money tasted more like vanilla than pistachio. 

Suffice it to say we won't be back. If we want another buffet meal in Vegas we'll walk over to Mirage...it's pricey too (though not this pricey!), but at least the food is edible!

Came here for lunch and magically, there was no line!

At lunch the pricing was around $36/person which is pretty standard for buffetts in Vegas. More recently, I've been to a brunch buffet at Navio (out in Half Moon Bay, CA) which to me was the gold standard of buffets. Bacchanal offers a plethora of food stations (9 total) with Italian, Chinese, salad, cheeses, meats, dessert, american, Latin american, and of course a seafood area. 

Having tried nearly all the stations here was my verdict:

American: Decent cuts of meat, great sweet potato fries, onion rings, and sliders.

Italian: Pasta I opted not to try, though the pizza options were plentiful, the pizza itself wasn't as great as I'd hoped.

Chinese section: Disgusting hot & sour soup. I didn't really enjoy this section.

Meat & cheese: Great selection of cheeses if you enjoy cheese. 

Seafood: No lobster claws at lunch. The mussels however, were delicious as was the ceviche and oysters. My favorite section, hands down.

Mexican: The taco stand is serviceable with your pollo, carne, and pork selections. The horchata here is DELICIOUS and I highly recommend getting it. 

Dessert: Great dessert section as with all buffets, however I think Wicked Spoon's dessert section is better. 

Service: Great service with attentive staff. 

Overall: Meh. I've had better and this doesn't really compare to Navio. In comparison to Wicked Spoon, they are about the same, it really depends on what you want. I feel Bacchanal has more variety but not the same quality. I prefer Wicked Spoon.

The plaque right outside the buffet say Bacchanal means "a feast worthy of gods"... I'd like to say it was a feast not so worthy of my tummy. I didn't feel my taste buds were in heaven nor did I feel like I had a god's meal. 

I came here for dinner recently with my boyfriend. And, we were both so eager to try out this much talked about buffet... only to find out it was over-hyped, over-rated, and over-priced. As my boyfriend puts it, the food tasted like a $30/person buffet priced at $50.99/person. I did enjoy the sushi and this macaron cookie they had- they were pretty much the most memorable things I ate there. 

We waited in line for about 1.5 hours before we were admitted around 8pm. There was a 4 part line: to get a ticket at the computers, to get called in, to pay, and then another line to wait to get seated. Those with a party of 4+ seemed to wait much longer to get seated. As orderly as Bacchanal tried to be, the wait just seemed to last an eternity. For dinner, you should definitely try getting there before 6pm.

This place is still worth checking out for those who never had it. But, try not coming with such high expectations.

If I could sum up my experience in a sentence- I basically saved my appetite and cleaned my wallet out for a few plates of disappointment. :\

My mom and I came her during a birthday trip to Vegas and although the food was excellent and the ambience/decor was beautiful, I really don't think this buffet is worth the cost. 

We would have had to wait almost two hours if we didn't decide to pay an extra $15 per person to skip the line (which we had to do because we were going to see Absinthe after dinner). The dinner rush was crazy, but our waiter was still attentive and I was able to try everything I wanted.

I have no complaints about the food and like I said, everything was nice to look at. But for being one of the highest-rated buffets in Vegas, it really wasn't THAT impressive. I feel like it just has a reputation and people are willing to pay so it will stay at the top of the lists but I'd rather eat at the Wynn or Mirage next time.
Very long wait. There letting other people go in front of us that have bigger parties. Very upset and hungry.

I finally had a chance to take my son to the Bacchanal, which we had both been really excited about.  We chose the Sunday Brunch, which I thought would have a good selection.  As it turns out, the buffet does not really have a great selection during the Sunday Brunch time.  Items would like to have seen, but were absent: king crab, oysters, poke or ceviche, some of the seafood dishes that you classically see in photos or in classic youtube videos.  They did have the stone crab claws out, which I was initially excited about.  However, it had a strange freezer burn taste.  Interestingly, the snow crab they had out had a better flavor and certainly tasted fresher.  The shrimp and grits is now one small shrimp on the bed of grits, which was ok. the dim sum selection was extremely mediocre.  My son tried the fried chicken, which he said was just ok, and the fries were not crispy (which you would not expect to be good at a buffet, but it Caesar's is going to put it out in a $45 buffet, it should be an exception). The meat selection was fine. Sausage, prime rib, skirt steak, etc.  I tried the skirt steak and the prime rib.  The skirt steak was a little overcooked and not very tender.  the prime rib was nicely med. rare, but had no flavor. 

Highlights: My son got the truffle pizza, which he was not fond of, but I thought was great!  The freshly made nutella crepe was really good, and perfectly cooked.  My son loved the coffee gelato. The personnel were all very nice. The interesting single-serve fresh juices were delicious.

Verdict:  Save yourself a frustrating experience and to go the M or Wynn.  They are both less expensive and the M had much better crab (if you go on seafood night).  Wynn had better thought-out and prepared dishes.  It was really not worth the price tag.  I purchased mine through groupon, so I got two buffets, 2 mimosa's (which were not offered and I did not get - which was not tragic since I was driving home afterward), 2 vip line passes (which I did not need, since there was no line) for $80.  With the $10 parking, about $7 in tax and a decent tip, it was still over $100 for two.  If I had paid full price, I would not just have been disappointed, I would have been pretty angry. As it is, I will just chalk it up to another adventure opportunity and move on.
For the price I rather go to a nice restaurant or steak house. way overpriced for a buffet $90 per person the food tasted old and stale, I guess that's what you from a buffet I guess

For a $160 buck's $52 a person 3 people I paid for horrible I rather put that money I paid to go to this joke of a 5 star buffet in a $50 a spin slot machine at least that way I have some chance of joy (if i win) my experience here was a nightmare food was cold the meat I tasted was extremely salty & cold crab legs were overcooked took ten minutes to fix my plate go back to my table forgot something so i left my plate for a quick sec and when i returned my plate was not there anymore worst part my uncle is diabetic so he ordered diet soda me and my husband ordered regular soda waiter mixed up are drinks and my uncle drank the regular instead of diet had to rush out of there so my uncle could take his medication terrible experience for me i wish i could have experience some of the good things I heard about it

Food was awesome as they had king crab, prime rib, fresh oysters, and those huge shimps. So the food had good quality and variety but the bill was $50+ per person. I can't quite justify that as most good buffets are around 25$. Service was good and the place looked nice. Go if you can afford it and like the seafood but don't go if you can't stand a large line up or like to eat cheaper food.

Honestly, I was hesitant to give a 5... But I have to admit, I'm pretty sure I had at least 5 plates... So obviously the food was amazing. To the point where I was so full that I was in actual pain. But I mean come on, its AYCE!

There is such a large and diverse variety of food here. And the quality actually isn't too bad being a buffet and all. But I mean, hence the $75 per person deal. But it's definitely worth trying. I wouldn't make a habit out of it, but I can see how it can be worth indulging in time to time. Maybe not to the point I did when I went last time haha. LITERALLY the biggest food baby I've probably ever had. 

But I mean come on... (relatively) FRESH OYSTERS ON TAP?? And of course the crab legs with large chunks of meat and melted butter sauce. Which by the way, were infinitely better than Wicked Spoon's. Having Wicked Spoon the day after Bacchanal may have depressed me a little and give more respect to Bacchanal.

This is making me really hungry. But they had some bomb prime rib there too... With the sauce and some mashed potatoes!? Oh and they have fresh crab legs, but also steamed ones at a different area. I personally liked the steamed ones there, but definitely try both. They have some fat shrimp at the fresh crab leg section. 

Definitely worth checking out, but get there early! Especially for dinner. Just know that you have to go get a ticket once you get there which is usually a 1.5 - 2 hour wait. But the waiting doesn't end there... You have to wait AGAIN once you get there. For about another good hour. This is kinda making me want to knock it down to a 4.5... I had a call back time of 5:40 on my ticket and we didn't start eating until 7!

Yeah, never mind. I guess my final verdict is a 4.5 haha. Just the wait and cost... I mean yeah they're all pretty fresh and theres a pretty large selection... But I don't know. Anyways, expect to wait and I'd suggest going there by at least 430 if it's a busy weekend and 5ish for a non-busy one to go pick up your ticket first.

I came here on Friday around 2p for the lunch pricing and stayed until 4p, allowing my taste buds to experience both the lunch AND dinner offerings (dinner starts at 3p... and you have a 2-hour limit, but it wasn't strictly enforced). There were only a few things that wow-ed me, but not enough to justify what I paid. 

The two stellar dishes were the salmon with aioli sauce and the bone marrow. The salmon was moist and paired great with the aioli. The bone marrow was amazing, and I think it had truffle salt on them; sooooo good! The cheese and cold cuts offerings were also great -- that chèvre, though!

The difference between lunch and dinner was so small that I really had to sift through all the buffet lines to figure out what's new. Most of the lunch items were there and the only notable additions were the raw oysters and new batch of nigiri. The oysters were tasteless unless you spritz a little lemon to heighten the flavor (sad). Overall, I felt bad for anyone that came after 3p, because it was almost the same food as lunch. 

The desserts were also sorely disappointing. I didn't think any of the various desserts made it past the first bite except for the delicious crème brûlée. The cakes were dry, the macarons were nothing to write home about, the cake pops were gross, the chocolate covered strawberries were falling apart, and the gelato was just OK. 

I'm left confused on why my experience is so different from everyone else that loved it. I really wanted to like Bacchanal, but it was very much so a fail based on this visit.

This place is not cheap by buffet standards but it's definitely worth every penny. Bacchanal boasts fresh, excellent and high quality dishes that range from Asian to Italian to South of the Border to American comfort food and everything in between. The dessert display will leave you in awe. The line is always very long and can take upwards of 45 min to get seated so I would suggest going as early as possible. The service can be a little slow in terms of drink refills but in the large scheme of things, that's a minor drawback.
Amazing, just amazing! When a Buffett has many dishes, not all of them are good. But Bacchanal Buffett's dishes are very delicious! I really enjoyed the lobster bisque

Overrated. The line (even when short) takes forever. The crab was still semi frozen. But the worst is the seating. The tiny tables are so close together you are practically sitting shoulder to shoulder with the people next to you. I gotta have a booth, thank you very much.

Ok...I'm comparison to Wicked Spoon, Bacchanal came in second.  The food was good but I felt like the offerings were more standard items that lacked that flair I was looking for.  An example is that I would have liked to seen a great pasta dish, but all I got was penne and Vodka and ordinary meatballs.  The highlights for me was the Chinese section which included a noodle soup station.  I really enjoyed the Ramen noodle soup!  

I thought the Italian section was lacking any type of flavor. 

There was a Mexican station that had nice make your own tacos and tortilla chips.  They also fresh bottled juices there such as guava which I enjoyed.

There was a huge seafood bar.  I tried to get crab legs which were halved for easy removal of the meat, but every time I tried to get them, they were not replenished.  The shrimp cocktail were huge and delicious.  

Atmosphere was very nice but a little crowded and hard to maneuver around the close tables.  

Desserts included a Gelato bar and cepe station as well as a nice selection of cakes and other treats.

I decided to go to this buffet because friends recommended this place. The good news is there's a lot of variety. The bad news is there's not much that are tasty. We touched each section and tried a little bit of everything. The only ones we went back for seconds were the cooked salmon, the steamed crab legs, and the sushi. We don't usually eat buffet because of the quantity vs quality problem. But you know, when in Vegas. 

So you pay in the front and they tell you have 2 hours to eat. Someone takes a picture of you and your family then a host seats you to your table. A server will come and ask for your drinks we ordered this peach green tea (it was good!!). Another lady comes by during the meal with our pictures printed and if we would like to buy it, we politely declined. (our most awkward pictures lol. I wish they didn't print it out because it is such a waste. Oh well)

Our server was polite and very attentive. She continuously checked on our table and cleared our dirty plates and religiously refilled our drinks. We sat there for two hours just catching up with our friend we haven't seen in a while. Their dessert selection is mouth watering. Everything looks so good and I wish had space for all of them haha! They even have a crepe station! So I got my crepe and had a nice little chat with the lady that I found out who used to live in San Jose. (We talked for a little bit after she found out we're from San Francisco. Next thing I know there's a line behind me.) The crepe didn't take long to make, it was just me being chatty. (sorry!) I went around and got myself an ice-cream and made my own crepe. 

Did I think it was worth it? For $65 per person, I would not go back. I probably would try other buffets next time and compare. Quality over quantity all the way. If I do come back maybe for their lunch price.

Everything and more. Went on a Saturday at about 3:30, waited for about 35-40 minutes. Party of 2. The food was divine. Seafood was cooked to perfection. Thoroughly enjoyed the seafood, specifically remember the ceviche being delicious. Ate my heart out... only to find out the oysters were on the other side that I didn't even know existed. So much food. The service was impressive, the chefs were really nice, and the other staff was very helpful was recommendations.

overrrrrrated
because of the 4 star rating, i had high hopes for this buffet but for the $50 (without tax or tip brunch price) per person price tag, it left much to be desired
first, regardless of whether you drink the unlimited mimosas or not, you have to pay the full $50, which is RIDICULOUS in my opinion
i don't know why everyone goes crazy about the crab legs at buffets because they are NEVER good. and it wasn't good here either. i couldn't even taste the stone crab looking things because they weren't fully cracked.
none of the roasted meats were tasty. 
dessert items were a hit or a miss. in general, they were aesthetically pleasing but wasn't great or anything. the chocolate molten cake and blueberry crumble were NOT good.
the asian food was like panda express. sushi was not good.
the pasta items were not bad.
service was bad. they were so slow to take our dirty plates!!!! 

i did like their churros and fudge filled cookies but not enough to pay $50+/person.
I don't normally Ever eat at a Buffett. This one is well put together. The service was great and the food was very good . I really enjoyed the sushi and the Asian foods .

This buffet is amazing!!! It has just about everything you can think of and it taste super good! Even my hubby who hates buffets love this place. It's pricey but well worth it. We pigged out so much at lunch we didn't eat anything else the rest of the day lol

Well well well....crab legs were my favorite, and they have cold or hot crab legs. We must have ate a ton of seafood at this buffet. Tried out lots of other food and i can say the service, food and atmosphere were just exeptional. Would go back again'

Sometimes the wait for a table can be a turn off, but whenever you do get the chance to get in, it's like you're walking into the gates of heaven. This is definitely my favorite buffet in Vegas. I visited twice my last trip, once for dinner, and once for lunch. Prices are about $55 before tax and tip for dinner and $35 before tax and tip for lunch. 

They have a bunch of different stations to pick your food from like, Asian, Italian, Mexican, American, Meats/Poultry, Seafood, and in the middle of the dining area is a huge dessert station. 

The foods that shined for me were the lamb chops, prime rib, and snow crab legs! All three of these items will make the money you're spending worth it since you'll probably go back for seconds or thirds of each! However, they only have prime rib out of the three during lunch. My boyfriend and friends really enjoyed their street style tacos as well! 

The dessert table has so many different options from creme brûlée, build your own crepes, cake pops, cupcakes, much more! Definitely give the creme brûlée a try! 

Service here is really good as well. They're always refilling drinks and cleaning off dirty plates fairly quickly. You usually don't even have to ask for a refill and that's a big plus in my eyes. 

This place is definitely worth trying if you're ever in Vegas! Wait out the line, and splurge a little! :)
Nice food here ,seafood are fresh and jumbo ,ribs are nice too ,chinese are pretty authentic,they deserve higher price.

This is the best Buffett in Las Vegas.  Take all of the amazing cooks at the best restaurants in Caesar's Palace and put them in one place and you have Bacchanal!  Yes it was about an hour wait, and that was on a Monday. So make friends in line while your party takes turns walking around. It was pretty pricey $97 for two people. But we pay twice that at great restaurants.   This place was amazing!  The decore beautiful, each station was super clean and polite . I took a trip around the world and ran out of steam before I got  to the seafood.  In Asia I had fresh sushi, dim sum fresh (watched 4little Asian man make everything in the station), duck was amazing.  Cheese grapes fresh honey right off the comb & dried meats capicola, salami, they were all amazing roll up all three take a bite of red grape the eat roll. Flavors that awaken the pallet . Pizza was great. Tacos freshly made by a man from mexi-cali w/freshly made tortillas(we were talking in Spanish and told me he made it himself.) The prime rib was juicy, tender and had great flavor.  Was to full for seafood so went straight to desert. Freshly made crapes delicious , chocolate covered strawberries with pop-rocks. Were my favorite but all the sweets were great!.  Well worth the wait but get there early so u can take your time and go for more!

I wavered between 2 and 3 stars and I'm opting to give them the benefit of the doubt. Would I return to dine here? Only if it was heavily comped and I was staying nearby. I would not go out of my way to return to this buffet. The service was atrocious. We purchased a travelzoo voucher to receive 2 buffets for $85 which includes unlimited mimosas, beer or wine. After 45 minutes we received our 2nd mimosa....so not worth the $15 charge for the drinks. Oh and that travelzoo voucher does not include tax...fyi. Just as I started to take pictures of all our plates piling up, the server suddenly appeared to clear our table. Absolutely unacceptable. It took forever to receive our water, coffee and that 1st mimosa.

Why am I being generous then with the 3rd star? Well, they did have hot steamed crablegs on a Sunday at 10am. They also had har gow and shiu mai that were pretty tasty. The only issue with the dimsum is that you had to practically get burned to bend under the window and reach the baskets and then try to lift the lid. It was a dangerous gamble but it paid off. Wonder how many people actually get steam burns though? Their chicken and waffles wasn't bad. But nothing else really stood out other than dim sum, crablegs and jumbo shrimp. The dessert was ok, but Wynn's and Wicked Spoons are better.
Definitely one of the better buffet in Las Vegas. Has a wide selection of food. Love their sorbet. So Yummy!

I remember eating here before but I don't remember it being this good.  We went with 7 ladies last week & we had a blast.  Of course we took our time.

This time I wasn't able to try most of the dishes because I just concentrated on my favorites.  Prawns, Crabs, Oysters, Snails, lobster soup, wagyu beef, & kobe beef.

I can't remember how much to get in because we paid as a group.  I just know it's pricey but hanging out with friends made up for it.  I know I didn't eat my monies worth, but every bite was worth every penny.

I took pictures for you to see.

Came here yesterday with high hopes. Came around 12:40 and the line was obviously long. However we went up to the very rude receptionist lady and she rudely answered it's a two hour wait. The lady working there was exceptionally rude. And if I am paying 75+ for a meal I expect great service. Two hours didn't seem bad so we just got a time ticket from the kiosk. To my surprise it said 4:30. It was in fact a four hour wait. So we then decided to just come for dinner. We got a text around five so we headed back to the buffet. Only to be disappointed by mediocre buffet food that was not even worth 50 dollars. For 75 dollars I expected at least better customer service. Never coming back here again.

This is a tough place to rate. Overall the food is 4 stars, but some of the items miss the mark. The steamed crab legs are awesome but the prime rib was average at best.  We purchased the unlimited drink option for another $15 but the red wine was bottom of the barrel quality and I would skip this and choose the beer or mimosa option.  However the big issue is getting a table. They have a terribly consulted system where you have to register electronically and you would think that by doing that it would eliminate the line wait but it doesn't. I signed up for the t Ct message and when it texted me to come back we still waited another 45 minutes before we got seated. It then took another 15 minutes to get our drinks. If you survive this part then you will enjoy your meal. There is a 2 hour limit to the buffet.

Prelims: a gorgeously decorated restaurant with a wonderful atmosphere filled with agonizing impatience, pure regret, gluttony, and the delicious aromas of fantastic food. My wife came here on our honeymoon and we were told by multiple people that this is the place of the gods - and our expectations were set accordingly. We saw the enormous line on a supposedly off-day and said that we were going to come back at 8 pm. We came back and while the long was smaller, it was still quite gargantuan. We waited for 30 minutes before we got in, it cost quite the pretty penny and our expectations were accordingly dashed. Service was at times good and horrendous. They served our drinks quickly and got us seated in a crowded table (but then again, everyone is crowded) right next to another couple, we constantly waited for non-refilled requests, like coffee and tea, but the sodas were premptively whizzing out onto our tables - to the tune that we had 6 half drunk cups of Diet Pepsi. 

The food was good - I had a bit of all the various dishes from around the world. Personally, I think it's fantastic that I get to experience delicious food from all over the world in one location and I get to eat as much of it as I want. But there were definitely certain dishes that were more popular than others - like the prime rib and the seafood. However, these were not as readily available as one would think - due to their popularity, there was a continuous long line for both stations, especially the seafood line. My wife said that she would go get seafood for us - and I ended up waiting 30 minutes! I noticed that there were a lot of people that were cutting in line. If you do that, I will totally judge you and then call you out in front of hundreds of people why you couldn't wait and expect me to wait instead of you for food. 

Desserts were great - I personally like almost all of them that were not chocolate. I'm a heretic. Bite me. 

All in all, while the food was good, I can only imagine just the sheer chaos and press of bodies during peak season. I can only assume that the individuals that were reviewing this place on the magazines and even on Yelp were given a private dining experience where they saw all the food in their perfect glory and didn't have to wait a single second to get whatever food their heart desired.  

TL;DR Reviews = high expectations. My expectations were not met. Good food - terrible lines and up and down service.

The Bacchanal was the best buffet ever! We were helped by Vanessa and she was the greatest! This made our stay at Ceasar's even better. The seafood selection was to die for and I would recommend this place to everyone when visiting Vegas!

Location: Insides Caesars. Look for the signs that say "Bacchanal". DUH!

Wait: I had an estimated 1 hr 1/2 wait at 12pm lunch time on a Saturday. I know.... WHAT THE FUCK? . The wait was actually pretty fast. 30 min wait tops. Pretty awesome! 

Price: 

* Breakfast/Lunch: $30-40

* Dinner:$40-50

Ambiance: Typical buffet. If you've been to Wynn and Bellagio you won't be surprised. Please tip accordingly for the drinks you do order. The service staff works really hard busing your barely touched plates of food. HAHA. So please tip! 

Patrons: Tourists, Filipino families who love Buffets, College kids, and everyone and their mother cause who doesn't like stuffing themselves like a fat-ass with expensive cuts of meat and seafood!?!?!

Food: Everything. When I mean EVERYTHING. Crab legs (Hot/Cold), Very in-depth carving station (Prime Rib, Sausages, Brisket, Honey Ham, roast Beef), Ramen, Pho, Udon station, Kalbi & BBQ pork ribs, Cronuts, and crazy ass desserts. 

Service: 

*A great experience and worth checking out if you're in the area. Comparing this to Wynn and Bellagio it's almost the same shit. I was most impressed with this one gentleman who went above the call of duty to make my experience truly memorable. I asked around a few chefs if they had any Eggs Benedict left since it was a breakfast item but since I had gotten there around lunch time it had already been switched out with sliders. Let me preface this by saying that one of the things I look forward to eating is Eggs Benedict. While a few chefs said "Sorry. We're out" He actually went to the back and brought two magically out for me. He didn't have to but I really applauded his service and his attitude to make my experience at this buffet awesome. Big ups man. 


All in all a fantastic buffet with great service! Next Stop Pan Roast at Palace Station........ BOO YEAH! 


J to the Y.

This buffet wins hands down for the best service. The woman who took us to our table explained everything as she was leading us there and our server was completely on top of things, taking our drink order right away, checking in on us frequently, and making sure our dirty plates were moved within minutes. Chefs all throughout the buffet would greet us at the station and ask if we had any questions.

The selection of foods was amazing. There were all kinds of seafood including crab legs, shrimp, shrimp in beer marinade, oysters, mussels, calamari... and the most amazing lobster corn chowder.

There was pizza, Italian food, and some pretty delicious Asian food. They had beef and broccoli, chow mein, hot and sour soup, spring rolls with peanut sauce, pot stickers.... it all tasted just as good as my local Chinese restaurant. 

There was a great charcuterie section with delicious spreads and cheese and an extensive Mexican food section. I'm not a fan of Mexican food so I didn't touch any of this but my husband liked it.

The desserts were also plentiful but by this time I was stuffed. Their gelato section was very unique - my husband had a mango chili sorbet and I had a caramel beer gelato. They even had a candy bar!

We were shocked at the price. A photo on here said $39.99 for a Friday night dinner - we paid $49.99 so the prices have gone up but it was worth it.

8/10/15..breakfast is 30.99, lunch 37.99 and dinner is 50.99.. Wkend is always higher!!
I usually don't give any buffet or restaurants 5 five unless they are worth it.. I've literally eaten all of vegas buffet, this one is by far the best even though it's a bit pricey. 
I feel like every once in a while I come, the price just keep increasing... Il still go but not as often as I would like 
The menu do change once in a while, but some food is always the same, meat, mexican, noodle bar, sushi,chinese and seafood. The only thing they change often is dessert.. Sometime it's good and other times are not..

Looong wait to even get to the cashier to pay over $100 for two for dinner buffet. Generally I thought the food was pretty good. Far from 5-star though and the high price. The crab was on the salty side and very thin so not much crab meat in the shells illustrating that management is buying lesser quality crab. Lots of interesting dishes and a number had good taste. One of my biggest complaints is a general one about most Vegas casinos and hotels now which is the parking fees. One of the benefits of visiting Vegas in the past was being able to go from casino to casino without paying for parking. Not only do you pay over $100 for dinner for two, but you also pay $12.00 to park your car. I would think that management could offer free parking with dinner purchase.

This was my first buffet experience in Vegas. We went for lunch around noon on a Wednesday. Luckily, there was very little wait. I'm not much of a buffet person, but the selection was extensive and food was good. $18 all you can drink add-on is a good deal considering Vegas drink prices. We paced ourselves and took the entire 2 hours. Line was huge when we left.

Sunday brunch at Caesar's is pricey. The food is quite good. My only regret is that we ate at the Wynn on Saturday and it was so much better, it was impossible to avoid comparisons. My only advice is this:  if you can only eat one buffet, eat at the Wynn.  If you are going to try both, go to Caesar's first.

Amazing- totally worth it.....if u love seafood that's ur spot!!!! Oysters and crab legs,  mussels.....and what not....the deserts...wow.....I can not stop loving this place.....I will be back everytime now...if they qould put a 24 hr Buffett pass for only this on on the market I would b their regular customer:))))!!!! Again...worth every penny........

Great food and Josephine Wade was great!!! My glad never went empty, and the shrimp and crab legs were to for for.  The chocolate covered strawberries melt in your mouth. I eat here everyone I come to Vegas!!!

I'm not a big fan of buffets, but this one was highly recommended, so my wife and I gave it a try. We were impressed. Not your typical buffet. The food tastes like it was prepared by a real chef. Everything is fresh, well presented, and tasty. Service is very good and the ambiance is rather nice for a large areas. So why only 4 stars? I had a slice of brisket from the carving station and it was tough. Good brisket is supposed to bed soft and succulent. This one wasn't. So it wasn't a perfect experience. But it's just a buffet, so who expected perfection anyway?

All of a sudden, your family is amazed at your ability to stack oysters, king crab legs, and mussels atop a giant mass of shrimp and carry three plates back to your table without dropping anything. Yeah - it's those hours of playing Tetris that you said would never come in handy in my life. 

For an extreme price, you're getting an extreme meal. Come hungry, and I mean don't eat for a day or so and think about eating the whole time you're not eating in preparation to come here. When you're here, the variety of options are just amazing. 

This is definitely a splurge for most people; and you're not going to be disappointed in the variety of options and plethora of food. When you're here, you're doing Vegas in a certain cut of excess and gluttony. Love it.

I have eaten here several times and have been very satisfied every time. This place is located inside beautiful Caesars Palace. This last time we came for brunch..we had a Groupon and I highly recommend using if you want to save a few bucks. I'm Diamond with Caesars entertainment, so I get ViIP entrance weather or not I have the Groupon. 

The pictures I have taken over the years speak a thousand words! There are too many incredible things to list and I wish I had a bigger stomach so I could eat more when I come here!
