But, I have to say, it really is my favorite of all the buffets in Las Vegas that I have tried. The service is excellent and the seating is more upscale than other buffets and comfortable. 

I recommend the seafood bar that has oysters and hot crab legs. The stone crab is amazing but can be challenging to crack! I Love the lobster Benedict that comes on a fluffy biscuit. I also went back for more shrimp and grits. Then there are the meats! Get a cut of the bacon slab, the prime rib, and the Waygu beef. Everything seasoned perfectly and tender and juicy. Pancakes, chicken and waffles, this brunch has it all and all you can eat! Move on to the desserts! Oh My! Fresh made crepes and chocolate soufflé while you wait. The choices of gelato are amazing. 

Check this place out when you are hungry! Be sure to give yourself plenty of time to savor the moment! I will be back!!

Step aside Bellagio, there's a new player in town. Baccanal at Caesers is where you want to be. 

The food selection is obviously extensive. I felt full just by looking at all the food. Want fresh hand made chinese noodles? No problem, Asian dude behind the counter is showing off his dough tossing skill. The seafood selection was amazing. I usually load up on alot of shrimp but I didnt realize how big they were until I sat down and looked at my loaded plate.

 I think gameplay play for this buffet is to hit the seafood first.  You'll get your money's worth in just one trip. Next, attack the meat section. Prime Rib, Tomahawk steak, ribs..need I go on? Japanese, Chinese, Italian, and many more. I wanted so badly to try every item but its just not possible. 

The wait is about 1-2 hours. You can pay the extra to get in quicker or hope you have a high roller friend with a diamond card. The service was very friendly, but one issue was that the waitresses seemed confused. They constantly forgot drink orders and where the orders went. It just seemed very unorganized. 

Bacchanal is definitely my new buffet spot now. Give it shot when you're in town.

Best buffet in Vegas? Probably. Worth $50/person? Not really.

The Good:
-Prime rib, beef brisket and sausages. Genuine restaurant quality, albeit still not near the best I've had.
-Small plates. Lots of items like salads, tofu, fish, etc as well as some creative dishes come in small individually presented plates/bowls and most were good.
-Boiled crab legs. Randomly located at the Italian food station. Look for 4 big pots and you gotta ask the chef to get them for you.
-Charcuterie. Not an expert but it all tasted fine to me.
-Sliders. Better than White Castle at least.
-Pizza. The only buffet pizza I've ever had that doesn't taste like it came from a hospital cafeteria
-Jucies. 6 varieties, all were good. 
-Most desserts, in general. Huge variety. Only tried maybe 1/3rd because I got too full but most were good.
-Electronic kiosk that will text you when it's time to line up.
-Overall restaurant decor.
-Food presentation and sheer variety.
-Service. Frequent water refills and nearly every time I got up to get more food by the time I got back the old plates were cleared out.

The Bad:
-Cold crab legs. Way too salty.
-Lamb chops. Overcooked.
-Macarons. Many different colors, all taste the same.
-Ethnic food section. Come on, it's a $50 buffet, you gonna fill yourself up with tacos and fried rice?
-Too many of the seafood items were shrimp.
-Sushi. Poor selection and worse than what you'd get at a $20 sushi buffet.

The Ugly:
-BBQ ribs. Worst I've ever had, by a long shot. 
-Buffalo wings. Tough and dry. Worse than grocery store wings.
-Waffle fries. Stale and flavorless. Going from Chick-fil-A to this is like going from Caesar's Palace to Circus Circus.
-Ramen. Broth is just awful, noodles too tough.
-Crawfish. Absurdly spicy.


Overall - 3.5. Rounded down because I can't honestly recommend Bacchanal unless you really love buffets.

We went there by 7 pm on a Friday and likely there were just a few people in line. We booked also all you can drink for an extra $35 per person "I think" and that includes " beer singaria, wine, memosa" they have( hot and cold crab legs, bone marrow, mussels, American wagyu, tri tip, and more stuff) our servant was nice lady and she always kept an eye on our wine. 
I think it is the most expensive buffet in vegas but it worth it.

This is the best buffet ever. I was so thrilled and happy the whole time I was there. There's just so much to choose from and everything was nicely displayed and freshly made. What surprised me most was the 'dim sum'- they had the sticky rice with minced chicken wrapped in lotus leaves, tofu skin wrap with veggies, century egg+ meat congee with the fried dough, and some buns and OMG the dessert station, WOW!- you've gotta see for yourself! ranging from freshly made crepe, mini cupcakes, variety of cakes, bread pudding and a wide selection of gelato!! Thai Tea flavor? yes, it's there- We got there for breakfast and decided to stay a tad bit to see what kinda lunch items they will bring out. Service was good, the waiter was very attentive and friendly. Sushi was ok- too much rice and not a whole lot of selection but probably more at dinner? Overall, it was a heavingly experience and the best $28 I've spent on food

As far as food goes, this is by far the best buffet that I've been to in a long time, hats off to the chef. However, the staff is just awful. One of the hostesses was such a wreck during the rush, I didn't catch her name but she was an older woman. And the manager, Steven, wouldn't even look at us in the eye when we asked him a simple question. The food is delicious but judging by the attitude of the staff and managers, they will not see a penny from me or my family again. I hear Bellagio has an outstanding buffet and I'm betting that their customer service skills are much more fine tuned.

One of the best buffet restaurant i have ever been. Food was excellent and staff are great! (There's one Black lady that was not nice, she stays at the cashier i believe. Stop being rude and don't point your finger to others) 

I will still give a 5 star, the chefs with their excellent food, the server with excellent service, and especially the server assistants who always come to our table to remove empty plates. They deserve a 5 star rating!

It is a large buffet so the star, but the food is not fresh, the price ridiculously expensive, the horrible service the waitress spoke all the time doing nothing with the ones at the next table and without filling the glasses. And the wait is ridiculous I approached because there was no line and let me in 30 min before. Although the variety is great when testing the food was not worth the waiting or paying $55 for less fresh food than a fast food

Long lines(waited in line for at least an hour) and expensive(over $50) but well worth it. Prime rib and rib-eye steaks are very tender and the quality is at least equivalent to, if not better than, most high-end steakhouse restaurants. Sushi is above average in quality and pastas are high quality. Dessert bar is a separate island with a huge selection of cookies, cupcakes, gelato and other treats. You can order crepes are freshly made and put what you want inside of them(Highly recommended). Creme bulee is outstanding and the gelato is amazing. Unlimited refills for drinks. I will definitely be coming back.

Crab legs and some good desserts, but nothing extraordinary. $60 for two hours. Seattle has better buffets. How is that possible? Well it is. All you can eat lobster at Feast in Seattle. No lobsters here, and average food. Unimpressive variety as well.

I use to love coming to bacchanal buffet and use my platinum statues to give us a shorter wait but now they have taken that away from me. The Food is great but I refuse to give higher then a 1 star til bacchanal reinstates the platinum line. Don't make me find a new place to go Caesars, make it RIGHT!

Definitely a must go when you visit Vegas. Don't forget to get a total rewards card because you get a discount. Amazing breakfast. They have seafood, your regular breakfast foods, Italian. Mexican, salad bar, fruit bar, dessert bar: build your own crepes. And fresh juice : watermelon, orange and tropical. 

Great for groups and kids.
Dress casual.
$29.99 for breakfast with total rewards card (get it in the casino) 

Carlos, our server was really nice and brought us the juice from the station while we were eating.

ATTN: Your server brings you drinks and coffee, don't forget to leave a tip. 
On parties of 8 or more: 18% gratuity is included.

I absolutely love this place I was there in late January and for the first time in Vegas and my first buffet there i was pleasantly surprised. We went for the morning brunch, line wasn't too bad and we had excellent service! A couple days later we went for dinner and luckily we had a diamond card and was promptly served. Our drink of choice for our 5 day stay was mimosas and hands down they had the best. I am so glad we stayed at Caesars we ended up going to Bacchanal 4 times in our stay and was completely satisfied by the delicious food and drinks. Will  definitely be going back again.

So close to getting a 5* recommendation from me.  Finally tried Vegas's newest gourmet dining buffet, and I definitely loved it.  The dishes were amazing, but for some reason I still like Wicked Spoon better.

That being said, I did have an amazing customer service experience.  I tried a piece of a square pizza that turned out to be amazing.  Went to get more at the end of my meal, and was told it was the chef's specialty.  I chatted with him and he said he'd make me a "personal pizza."  15 minutes later I came back to a HUGE pizza just for me.  It was blue cheese, prosciutto, and another meet I'm forgetting.  Go to the Italian station and ask for "Tony Gets" and have him make you this masterpiece!

This is a hard one to write.  The food was uneven in quality. Service was great, but it is ultimately  not worth the price.  Over $100.00 for dinner including tax and tip.  We went at 5:30 on a Monday and there was no line. 

The good: prime rib, dim sum, truffle potatoes, shrimp, which were huge, although you occasionally got a frozen-ish one and the watermelon and feta salad. 

The bad: ribs, hot and sour soup, some deserts, sushi. 

The OK, but I was expecting better: Alaskan crab legs, a bit watery and not very flavorful.

This is probably the best buffet in vegas. They have quality everything from the meats, juices, desserts side dishes etc. It's also the most expensive around $50-$65 per person. Crab legs cold and hot in the back area they can warm em up for you! TONS of meat from sausages, ribs, roast, pork ribs,steak and the list goes on...

From previous reviews I read I was afraid there would be a long wait. My wife and I had brunch around 11am on a Friday. We waited maybe 30 minutes. But it was worth it. The food was hot and a very large select. I enjoyed the shrimp and grits and grab legs. My wife really like the desserts. Her favorite dessert was the cream brulee. We also purchased the photos they took of us which were $20.

I was so excited to try this new buffet in Caesars Palace.  Usually the restaurants in Caesars is good but my experience at Bacchanal was just awful.  I came Sunday night at around 6pm.  I waited in line and was finally seated after an hour.  I checked the carving station and all they had was brisket, ribs, and some sausage.  No prime rib....how disappointing!  I thought that was a staple at all the good buffets on the strip.  The meat was DRY.  It was just not good at all.  I went on to try the nigiri and sushi.  The rice was mooshie and the fish was not fresh.  I also had a cute tiny bucket of mussels.  The mussels were all dried out.  I was thinking maybe it got dry from the heating lamp...but would the mussels on the bottom be dry from the lamp too?  I then tried the lobster corn chowder and that was way too salty.  I did enjoy the raw oysters and shrimp cocktail.  The dessert was good.  I liked the tarts, cheesecake pop, and macaroons.  The macaroons were a little chewy but what do you expect from a buffet?  The cupcake was dry.  I did not try the pho station (I'm from the bay area.  There is no place with better pho).  It was just a disappointing experience.  I will not be returning.  Step up your game Bacchanal.

I've been here twice now, once for brunch and once for dinner!

I enjoyed my brunch/lunch visit much more personally!  Perhaps the BOTTOMLESSCHAMPAGNE/MIMOSAS had something to do with it?  I'd say yes LOL.

Most everything seemed the same lunch vs dinner as far as selection is concerned.  I didn't notice anything tasting better/worse more fresh etc...seems very consistent here.

Some highlights :

The Lamb (dinner) was outstanding...almost perfect actually as far as taste and consistency goes in my book.  Very simply seasoned...it's just tender and not gamey at all.  Fork-pull-apart tender!

Andouille Sausage (dinner) also great!  Lots of flavor...yum :)

The Ribs here are good!  SUPER meaty, fatty, and yummy....wish they were more tender though....but alas, we are in Buffet world, not slow cooked wonderland.

Cajun Shrimp, Ceviche, and Oysters (dinner). Everything was good, even the oysters completely naked!  I'd rack up on Oysters next go around :P

They offer hot and cold snow crab...no other choices of crab.  I choose hot, but I get a bit tired of the super sweet crab...wish they had Dungeness or King, esp at this price point.

Truffle Scallop Potatoes (dinner)...just like it sounds, and yes, there is a good amount of truffle oil :)

There is some decent stuff in the Chinese/Asian area...the dim sum is just ok, duck was good though, but the Spicy Fish is great!  I'd recommend snaggin a piece or three while you are over there :)

Crab Benedict (brunch). This was perfect, with semi sweet crab and a delicious hollandaise sauce. Yummy!

Lobster Biscuits and Gravy (brunch). Pretty good as well! I enjoyed the Crab Benedict more though... 

As far as dessert goes :

Lava Cake is perfect!! I should have grabbed two more of em, but I was full by the time I remembered dessert LOL

Chocolate Mousse dessert...can you really go wrong with anything that has a mini Oreo on it??

Great buffet...expensive...but good way to do Vegas :)

Hands down the best Buffett in Vegas.  I was in love with the Wynn Buffett and that was my favorite, but Caesars definitely stepped it up a notch with this one.  I've been to Caesars old Buffett and it wasn't all the great and I didn't realize they had upgraded. 
The seafood selection is out even for brunch, which is something you don't usually get.  I started with crawfish, clams, shrimp, and crab claws.  The entire seafood selection was great and fresh. 
Next I tried the honey ham, brisket, pork belly , and beef rib.  All of these were super juicy and great.  
Too bad I got full quick, because in there was another room with Chinese, Japanese, Italians, and cheese that I didn't try.
The desserts were also fantastic.  I tried the flan, creme brûlée, a mini chocolate cake, then I had some cookies and creme gelato with a Nutella crepe topped with bananas and strawberries.
They have a selection of fresh fruit juice as well.

Pricey but worth it. There are a ton of seafood options. We enjoyed everything we tried. My husband is a vegetarian and there were many choices for him too.  If you are on a tight budget there are more economical buffets that have tasty selections. We enjoyed the buffets at the Mirage and Mandalay Bay too. Lasvegasadvisor has a list of all the buffets and prices. Yelp them before trying.

Food is great , I'm giving this a 3 stars because cashier precilla M. Was busy texting or on her phone she also didn't seem welcoming , she seem pretty piss about her job . Since this is a almost 5 star buffet I suggest you smile at the customers and not look like b****
Food looks fancy but tastes not that good. Crab is not that fresh. I prefer the buffet in Aria. At least its crab is awesome. In bacchanal everything is far from good. It's just fine.

What is there not to love about this buffet? Ok maybe the price is steep and the wait is ridiculously long but its well worth it. Wicked Spoon use to be my favorite buffet in Vegas but sadly its been going down hill over the past few years. Luckily Bacchanal came along. I miss how when it first came out it wasn't as crowded. Now the wait is like 4 hours. At least they have a kiosk where you can put your name on the wait list, what is cool is that if you have a US number they can text you when they're ready for you. The only downside is you have 15 minutes to check in and the estimate is not very accurate. One time we got a text 40 minutes before the estimated time and there was traffic. The last time we got a text about an hour and a half earlier than expected and we were across the strip. We made it both times though whew. I usually don't eat peeled shrimps at buffets they're just unappealing to me but it;s sooo good here and they're big. Love their juice in little jugs, the horchata one is good. There is a lot of variety of food and the quality is good. Not many buffets have good desserts but they have fairly good desserts here especially the ice cream! I think they replaced the mochi ice cream with ice cream sandwich, I prefer the mochi. They now have shaved ice!!!! Pretty tasty and the green tea flavor was on key. I wish they have more toppings though such as fresh fruits. The macarons aren't too shabby some aren't extremely sweet. Its hard to find macarons that aren't overly sweet.

Don't believe the hype! 

We came here for brunch after reading yelp reviews and seeing the long lines. The price for brunch is nearly $50 per person after tax and it's really not worth it. Rumors of macarons and delicious food were false. Maybe true for dinner or some other sitting times but definitely not for brunch. The food was underseasoned and tasteless. The sushi bar was disappointing. The dessert bar was either bland or bland, with the exception of the green tea creme brûlée which was excellent. But still not enough to carry the price of the meal. 

If you can eat your weights worth of Alaskan crab legs, then this is the place for you. They offer hot or cold legs that are split in half for easy consumption. It does have a large variety but a lot of tasteless food or salty food is worst than grabbing a quick bite at McDonald's.

People come to Vegas for the buffets as well as the shows and the gambling. Sadly, this place may have been a great buffet once upon a time. But with hype comes price increases but sadly the quality of food does not live up to its reputation.
Long line!! Topped up 25 bucks total for one person for so called express line but not so express at all still kept us waiting. Food was okay nothing special.

This was pretty good for dinner.  The desserts were awesome especially the french macrons and ice cream mochi!  Prime rib, short ribs, fish and sooo on...really was a lot to pick from.  They have a suggested 2 hr limit so couldnt try everything.
Thank u for the amazing service Alvaro! This guy is funny, hard working, and fun! He made our experience even better than usual. Thank u Alvaro!

Holy cannoli.... This place is great!

My family and friends decided to come here for dinner since we were all starving. We came in a group of 8 around 6:45pm. We got seated in about 20 minutes because I believe if you come in a bigger group, you pay gratuity which means quicker seating? Don't quote me on that though... lol.

The ambience is very soothing, beautiful guitar music playing in the background, and bright and bubbly. 

The wide variety of food is outrageous! High quality dishes spread out the entire place; from Japanese, Chinese, seafood, Mexican, Italian, and American cuisine. Don't skip out on the oysters! -- super fresh. I had to try out everything and it did not disappoint. They even have a great selection of desserts from ice cream to macarons to cookies.

For my first time eating here, I would most def come back for sure for the awesome meal and service! Shoutout to our waitress Su for being super friendly and accommodating. Perfect meal and setting for a buffet at Caesars Palace.

Great brunch buffet! So many choices, there's no way you'd leave hungry. Prime rib for breakfast - yes! The pastries were amazing, the mimosas were delicious, I'd highly recommend this place. We used a Groupon to go, but it's so good we would've paid full price anyway. The eloquent environment was a pleasure to the dining experience. The meat display was so unbelievable that even a vegetarian couldnt resist the appealing aroma. Two thumbs up

This is by far one of the best buffets in Vegas, if not.....the best!  I always say I'll take pictures next time, but never do. It is pricey, but the food is high quality and definitely worth the money.

Definitely not your typical buffet. The food and selection are fantastic and the service is equally as good. I will definitely be back.

The spread at breakfast has all bases covered- it should really be brunch because there are your standard breakfast items along with tons of seafood and pretty much anything else you could want.

This place was one of my highlights in Vegas. They had such a variety of foods. My favorite was the bone marrow and prime rib. The Bacchanal was worth the wait! The staff there constantly refilled our drinks and were super nice. If you're in Vegas and want to try out one of the buffets this is the place to be!

This is probably the worst experience that I have had at the Bacchanal buffet. I've been here few time and never have any complaint about customer service until now. Tonight we were seated next to a big pillar close to the dessert area which is nice cause dessert is my favorite. My son started to be very uncomfortable and scratching himself a lot. When I checked on him, his pants were totally wet. There was a water leak from the ceiling right above him, and I took a look at his chair and it was all wet. I had called one gentlemen in vest working there who was not our waiter, and explained the situation. He never said sorry to us, nothing. What he did was call another waiter. She just moved the table to the side. That's it. None of them said anything to us for this inconvenience. After that I had to take off his pant because they were all wet. After that we couldn't stay more than 30 mins in the restaurant because my son started to feel itchy and irritated. This whole experience for tonight ruined our love for this buffet. The food maybe 4 Stars but the service is 0 for a $55 buffet.

Bachhanal was really good--especially the seafood.  The first station when you walk in is just that.  There were raw oysters, crab legs, mussels, and the BEST cocktail shrimp.  My favorites from the buffet has got to be the cocktail shrimp and crab legs.  Both were really fresh and the shrimp was the most meaty that I have ever had.  

Some of their other stations do need some work, like that of their japanese, mexican and chinese cuisine.  Those sections were a bit small and were good but not what I had expected in terms of the quality and flavor.

In terms of the meat section, I thought the prime rib was really good, juicy and tender.  Some of the others were a hit or miss to me, like I didn't really enjoy the BBQ ribs very much...they were a bit dry and difficult to cut through. 

The dessert station is heaven.  Make sure you save enough room for dessert.  There's tons of choices and the standouts have got to be their crepe station and their gelato and mochi! 

Oh yeah, the service is FANTASTIC here.  I felt like everytime I set down my utensils when I was done with a plate, someone was already by my side ready to clear my plate for me.  Drink refills were quick and served with a smile.  Thumbs up on maintaining that great service! 

I still love the buffets at Wynn and Cosmo, hard to say which one I love the most, they each have their strengths...but I do have to say that Cosmo takes it for its regular dishes, Bacchanal has the best seafood and dessert and Wynn has the best meats and pretty decent seafood.  I'd definitely come back to Bacchanal again!

Food was good and selection was great.

Our original server was flummoxed and mostly absent. We waited ten minutes to place our drink order after being seated, but with no sign of a waiter, we went up and got food. We were done with our first plates by the time he came over. He came back to refill our drinks once and apologized saying he was "so confused". After that, a new server came over and said the first guy was on break. Everything flowed smoothly after that.

Pro tip: cold crab legs are available at the raw bar up front, but freshly cooked hot crab legs are in the back next to the Asian food.

Last night we tried the Bacchanal buffet at Caesars Palace because we've heard great things about it  It was not that great in my opinion. The seafood was overcooked and either lacked seasoning or was salty (we tried several types). Some of the other food tasted like it had been sitting a while. Other food had a metallic taste  The only food we liked was the dessert. Our server was great! We were not crazy about our table location near the entrance. It was really cold! Based on EXPENSIVE price and reviews, I expected a much better experience. Somehow they fell short  Therefore, I will not recommend this buffet to friends and clients.
Awesome.  Worth the $15 extra to get to the front of the line.  Everything was well prepared and the desserts were numerous and tasty.  I usually do not like buffets but this was great.

Servers are nice, and the atmosphere was beautiful. However this is RIDICULOUSLY expensive for what you get. Most of the food that should've been hot was ice cold, gross. I wouldn't be writing this bad review if it was a couple of things that had been sitting there but it was mostly everything. Major bummer we walked out feeling robbed.

I could keep this really short and it would get the point across: it's a buffet and it tastes like it.

To elaborate, there are no lack of options, but there is a lack of flavor. Many dishes are quite bland. You'll see people devouring tons of Steamed Crab Legs and Prime Rib to get their money's worth, but I would much rather spend $50-60/person elsewhere on a quality lunch. 

The best item I had, and I tried most, was the Steamed BBQ Pork Bun. However, you can get those at a traditional Dim Sum joint for a fraction of the cost of this place.

On top of that, it's a long wait and "cattle call" to get in this place. Make a reservation somewhere else unless you just want as many Crab Legs as you can get.

Overrated buffet with mediocre food. Yes, they had unlimited hot crab legs and oysters but our stomach can only take maybe $20 worth of food. Tonight's dinner costs $60 per person and it will be the last time for us. It's not worth the 2 hours wait. I even got food poisoning from eating here. 
However, the dessert and the staff were really wonderful.

My family and I have only been to this buffet during breakfast. This is a five star buffet. The food is excellent. The only flaw is that this buffet is extremely expensive. If you have a rewards card you are looking to pay $29.99 for breakfast.

Pro: Variety of offerings, good juices, some tasty salty breakfast meats

Con: Overpriced ($45+ for Sunday breakfast at 8a), slow service, many things were cold even though they just opened - why do I have to walk from middle of line to end of line to get cream cheese for my bagel - bagels and cream cheese need to be placed together

Nice place but overpriced - this was not a champagne breakfast - should not be $45 - also should not have cold food that should be hot at that price

Favorite buffet on the strip. Went for lunch on a Tuesday 39.99. Mom is a platinum member so we avoided the long lines yay! Lunch is just as good as dinner. Fresh seafood, pork belly, chicken and waffles, and pho! Desserts are excellent and they have fresh juices too!

I ate a dead fly salad today! Period 
When I was eating my salad , I saw something drop out of the salad from my mouth. when I looked at it, it was a fly! A dried fly!!! I asked for the manager and she just took away my dish!! What a nice restaurant. I can't imagine how do they prepare the food in the back!!!!

Edited. 
Another manager has contacted me earlier and applogize for the problem and she asked me to visit them again. I overrall i have good experience. I have change from one star to 4 stars.

It was an interesting experience. Very crowded arrangements of seatings w barely ne walk ways to table. Most foods r very salty n dry. N their long single line arrangement of food stations cutting off to bk area  was like bing in some sort of maze.  Best i can remembr is the zucchini side dish. Aqua fresca in individual bottles were cute but cant say flavors were as good. Condiments r hard to reach or see. Fortunately i paid lunch price bfr starting of dinner n had no line to wait in.  If it was othrwise i would've been very unhappy. Oh! But Shrimp lovers u'd like their jumbo cocktail but crab legs r waaaaaaaay bettr at wynn! Barely ne meat to eat.

I have to say that my first time at Bacchanal Buffet in Vegas was absolutely terrific! We experience first-class customer service and top quality gourmet style buffet food here. The experience here is one you will never forget. Julie, who was our waitress, truly enhanced our experience at this restaurant. She made it worthwhile and offered jewels to us that made her and our experience even more memorable!  The food is on point and will come back here again the next time I visit Vegas. Truly a great experience and is deserving of a 5-star rating!
I have had two good experiences here.  The bacon is awesome, these pecan tarts are to die for and the service is great!   It's clean and inviting.

I've been wanting to try this place for a long time. I'm not a fan of buffets but since this one is supposed to be one of the "best" ones, I thought I need it to give it a shot. We went during memorial day weekend on a Sunday and total wait time was like 2hrs to 2:30hrs. I was already mentally prepared to wait, the first hour we went shopping at the Forum Shops, so it wasn't that bad. I have say that they have more than other buffets I've been to, sushi, meats, soups (ramen, pho, etc), taco section, crepes, chicken and waffles, etc. We payed extra for brunch since it was a holiday. 
Just wanted to try it, nothing extremely special to come back.

Its a pretty pricey buffet but well worth the money!  The service is great!  theres a great selection ,   The crab legs are very worth it .... a great place for family.  Its one of the best place I have ate in Las Vegas buffet.   I can see why its pricey  seafood is not cheap nowadays and as much as some people waste food.  but great place to eat overall its delicious!

Delicious but expensive. Fresh squeezed juices if you go for brunch. They also have some of the freshest oysters and crab but many dishes are super salty. The prime rib has salt rubbed all over the outside.  You will not be able to eat the outer portion. Their leg of lambs or "lamb lollipops" as their butcher calls it are delicious and well-seasoned. Even my dog thought so. :)

What really sets Bacchanal apart though is the wide selection of asian cuisine. Pho was actually very good. Much better than some restaurants out there. Some of the sushi is fresh but if that's all you're looking for go to Goyemon which is off the strip.

Pistachio macaroons and mochi ice cream are the best deserts. Maybe because I get to eat them very rarely.

Amazing food and tons of varieties. It is also extremely expensive. My recommendation would be to get here at the end of lunch, so you pay much less for the same type of food. The only thing that changes at dinner time is the price. Their meats and barbecue line was very good

The most expensive buffet I've ever been to -- and also the best, by far!

There are so many options to choose from, whatever you like, you have a good chance of finding it here. The Asian foods were what I enjoyed the most, but there is clearly something for everyone . The Peking Duck is awesome and it's tied with the Wagyu sliders as my favs here. I would pay a lot just to get those two dishes!

The smoked salmon is first rate, as is the prime rib, brisket, char-shu pork, spare ribs, bao, pad thai, and chow fun. I was so full I didn't even get to try the sushi which looked good too.

Great dessert bar, I managed to put away some excellent gelato and finished with a pot of Italian roast coffee that was (surprisingly) savory.

I can not recommend this buffet strongly enough. If price is an issue, go at lunch when it's a bit less. Still pricey, but not a ton more than you'd pay at many other mid-range restaurants. You have to get your own food, but that's a small price to pay. And you get to choose what you want and how much you want. 

I can't wait to go back!
More expensive than comparable buffets but they carry more variety. I think the seafood is grossly overrated by other reviewers, but a solid buffet nonetheless.
Fucking stupid place! Very bad service. They charge your extra 25 per person so it will be 100per person.
Soooo yummy!!! I think that it was about 40 bucks a person on lunch before 3pm. I would avoid the seafood upon return but everything else was really good.

Definitely on the pricey side for an all you can eat buffet but then again it is pretty upscale. Was it worth it? I'll say yeah.

I spent 2 hours for dinner here because we couldnt catch the lunch hours. I had 6 plates! and I was so full that I could barely moved. 

Try everything there! the snow crab legs, raw oysters, lambchops, etc. Also remember the hidden italian and chinese sections in the back!

This will forever be my favorite buffet!
During this trip to Vegas I definitely lucked up!

We bought brunch tickets for 2 with mimosas for 88$ on Groupon 
Arrived at 2:30PM And by the time they sat us it was 3pm and we got to enjoy the dinner time menu!!! 
Oh yeaaa, that means unlimited steamed crab legs. 
Normally this would have ran us over $120 for two people 

My faves are the steamed crab legs and creme brûlée

Honestly food was good service was great! Raz the manager I believe helped us out! So many food options and it was really delicious. Be prepared to wait awhile unless you pay 25$ extra to skip the line. But definitely worth the money

Bacchanal is the priciest buffet on the strip, to my knowledge.  But is it worth it?  YES.  The quality and selection is there for sure.  My friends & I arrived before 6:30 on a Friday night & there was no line at all.  I showed my Total Rewards card and was surprised that even after discount dinner was $50 pp.  

After we paid we were escorted to our seats, and I admired how nice the decor was.  Unfortunately I wasn't that hungry so I didn't enjoy too much of this 500 item buffet, but we were all impressed with the meat carving station, the dessert station, and the seafood assortment to name a few.  Just like Wicked Spoon, they serve a lot of items in those cute little fryers and individual plates.  They also supply you with upon paying (and have them at the stations too) little rubber grabbers for hot plates.

My top picks were the: hot crab legs (the guy working the station gave me so many), the pizza special of the day, the poke, siu mai, prime rib & smoked ribs.

Wanted to love, but thought it was so so: Sweet potato tots, waygu slider (a little on the dry side), fried chicken (should have not gotten the breast) served with sweet potato fries), kalbi, sushi, broccoli & cheese.

Skip: Fried rice, shrimp and chive dumpling.

Dessert picks: chocolate covered strawberries, the different flavors of mochi ice creams. chocolate oreo peanut butter ganache cake thing, dessert cup with chocolate and passion fruit.

Dessert skips: My friends loved the macaroons but I didn't care for them.  Guess I'm just a total sucker for Bouchon's.  I'm sure the other gelato flavors are better but I got the toffee and french toast flavors..skip those.  The gelato seems like it melted a little on the quick side as well.  

My friends and I thought we came hungry, but I guess we weren't as hungry as we thought as we didn't get to sample as much as we thought we would.  Again, we enjoyed the different stations, next time I think I'll come for lunch or brunch to see the different spread and try some of the stations I didn't get to try, like more of the Asian stations and the Mexican stations.  Is it better than my favorite, Wicked Spoon?  I'd say quality wise, yes, tastewise, I did have more of an appetite at WS, so that could have played a factor as well.  The food is still delicious at both buffets.  But I've also eaten more items and twice at Wicked Spoon (solely for Mimosa brunch).  I think service at Bacchanal is a lot friendlier and a little more attentive.  Bacchanal is worth the splurge though.    4 stars for now.

I highly recommend visiting this buffet if you're in the Vegas area...and this is coming from someone who doesn't even like buffets. I went to brunch at 8am during a weekday so the food was still fresh and there were no lines to get in. Everything was well-prepared but the brisket, prime rib, and short ribs were my favorite. The orange beer and mango habanero sorbets on the dessert station were equally delightful. It was a nice surprise to see a crawfish boil on the buffet. As someone from the South, I'm not accustomed to seeing them in places outside of swamp territories so that was pretty cool. I still didn't eat it (lol) but I appreciated the variety. It was worth every penny. And our waitress, Judy H., was such a gem...sweet, attentive, and helpful!

The best damn buffet in Vegas. Hands down. Its pricey but worth every penny. 

I'm still thinking about those crab legs...Kobe beef sliders...and lamb chops!!!!! Let's not forget about the crepe station!

What a disappointment! After waiting in line for almost 2 hours after the time we got in the queue system I have had better food at $15 Chinese buffets. And this was far more than $15. I would say maybe the fact that it was Christmas week was an excuse but it certainly was not the crowd that caused so many dishes, including all the soups and and many of the items by the Mexican and Italian stations to be presented in crusted over condition. The Chinese station was acceptable but most of the items were low cost offerings. I did enjoy the duck. But still $15 Chinese buffets back home do it all better. People were flocking to the seafood station. The crab legs was ok but once again did not exceed the Chinese buffets at home. The fish items were dried out. The shrimp dishes were mostly smaller shrimp over sauced. The carving station was the best. The prime rib I got was very rare, but I like it that way. The lamp chops were the only item I went back to get more of.  There were a number of good desserts. I looked forward to a great Las Vegas buffet. I had to jump through hoops to get my buffet-adverse family to agree to one, especially at the high price of this one. After this major disappointment I am considering switching to their attitude.

The GF had never done a Vegas buffet, so we ended up here after a bit of googling and determining that this is apparently the leading contender for Best Buffet.

We came on a weekend night, meaning it was just over $50 each, and a 90 minute wait.  

The choices are almost overwhelming, and they had pretty much everything you could want.  

The real thing that sets it apart from other buffets I've been to (I live in Reno, so a fair amount of experience with them) was the lack of large chaffing dishes.  Most items were cooked in single services - e.g. individual baskets of chicken fingers for kids, small, single-serve cast iron pans of lasagna, etc.  The stuff that wasn't in single serves was in really small dishes, maybe a dozen items.  Many of the items were things that I felt could be served as a regular menu item at most other restaurants.

Other things that set this place apart were the fresh shucked oysters, a choice of hot or cold crab legs, and probably close to a dozen choices at the carving stations.

The one miss for me was the sushi - this was an exception to the individually prepared items - large trays of nigiri and rolls, and reminding me of a Todai or something.  Quality of the fish was just meh, the rice was not well seasoned, and the cuts of fish were sometimes not properly aligned with the grain of the flesh.

I don't think we'd go back, but that's because we've had the experience, and for me, once is enough.  

I think if you are looking for that big, grand, Vegas buffet, Bacchanal is probably the epitome of it.

Sad to say I was a tad bit disappointed.

In all fairness though, I was pretty hungover so it was hard for me to enjoy the food. Don't get me wrong - everything was decent but I think a lot of people hyped this place for me. I rarely go to buffets in Vegas but when I do, I go straight to the crab and shrimp. Typical asian, going for the expensive stuff. I started off at the very end which was the dim sum/asian side. Everything was good. I tried a bit of my friends things as well. Sushi looked weird. Prime Rib was bomb. The truffle cheese scalloped potatoes were BOMB. The crab was a bit salty but it was really good (and it was sliced in half for easy access *wink) The shrimp is always good and unfortunately I don't like the oysters but I hear they were good. 

I was pretty satisfied with the plain crepe with nutella for dessert but I wish I had gelato. My stomach just said NO MORE. 

I wouldn't mind coming back here. Endless mimosas.. how can I say no. For 60 bucks though, I think I would rather eat at the Wynn buffet for half the price
As a "Diamond" service very poor.  Removed Roast Duck, Char Sui. Jonah crab claws #1 size.  Prime rib more like roast beef. Hand towels not offered. Had to beg for crab crackers.  Won't return.

Service was horrible. Food was horrible. That's why I deleted my past review. What a horrible revisit to this place. Everything about it was bad. The food. The service. I mean come on. The waiter has one freakin job. Refill my drinks. She never came to our table. I asked for Tabasco. One hour later I'm still waiting. I asked for coffee and I think she went to Colombia to get it. $70 for a buffet. Almost a $400 bill with my family. My son who loves steak didn't eat their steak and he'll eat anything. He didn't even touch the dessert. The waitress walks by and doesn't acknowledge us. She's pathetic. I officially hate this place and will never come back.

Looooove this buffet. 

It's the only Vegas buffet I've been to, and despite the ridiculously long wait (seriously...I don't understand why they can't do proper reservations) I doubt I would go anywhere else. 

The seafood is on point - feel like we definitely got our moneys worth on just how much crab we ate. Lots of variety at all of the other stations as well - I tried everything that caught my eye and there literally wasn't anything I didn't love. 

Bonus - Mariah Carey walked through the crowded dining room with her entourage ...I suppose the restaurant is a shortcut to somewhere else within the hotel. She was an absolute stunning Goddess as she floated through the room ...though she did look like a deer in the headlights...I suppose she was afraid of being mobbed by fans with smelly crab fingers.

If you have never gone to big a Las Vegas buffet before, this might be worth a try. With its numerous food stations, this is a very fun place to dine at for those who enjoy variety. There are meat stations (lamb, beef, mini hot dogs, ham, fried chicken, etc), seafood stations (crab legs, mussels, etc), an Asian corner (a nice assortment of char siu, duck, ramen, and sushi), and a dessert bar, to name a few. In my opinion, the dessert area was the most impressive part of the buffet. It served all types of desserts that you can possibly imagine - from standard cakes to tarts to gelato in many interesting flavors. They even had a lot of international desserts, and thai boba floats as well! With the variety of foods offered at this buffet, there is something for everybody, so this is a nice place to go with a group of people who have different tastes in food. Although the line can get long, people are seated in a reasonable amount of time due to the extensive amount of seating areas within the buffet. 

Overall, it was an enjoyable experience. The reason why I hesitate to rate it more than 3 stars is because of the hefty price tag - although one of the most expensive meals that I have eaten, it is also not one of the more memorable ones. Aside from the extensive selection of food, I was expecting more dishes to have a "wow" factor that would leave me wanting seconds and thirds. I had been expecting to be able to rave about the quality of the food days after dining here. If the cost could be lowered, or the food quality becomes a little gourmet, then this buffet will definitely be worth it!
Yum yum. #1for a reason. Food was fresh plentifull and on top of it had special crafted taste.

Hands down the best buffet I have been to. Never a huge fan of buffets because quality always disappoints and I never think the price is worth it but wow I was AMAZED by the quality and presentation of food here; the only complain I had was that they had too much variety and I need to visit at least two more times to try everything. Even their desserts were on fleek e.g. Their creme brûlée and the chocolate molten lava cake, and get their green tea mochi. Everything I had, from their oyster shooters to their beautifully presented salmon, tapas sized meat, and even their salads and cured meat and cheese plate (yay for goat cheese and brie!!) did not fail my expectations. Also loved their potatoes gratin and paella (one of the best I've had, even better than the paella I had among several Spanish restaurants?!) and others. I tried to get a bite of their everything just to get a jist of this buffet and nothing seemed to disappoint. I was pretty amazed. Would I visit here again for the price? I would probably say no, but I suggest anyone to come here once to at least experience the best buffet he/she will probably ever have. The atmosphere also seems quite upscale for a buffet... You wouldn't really expect a buffet restaurant to look like this. Trust me you will be disappointed at other buffets after trying this one and will never want to go back to other buffets again.
My favorite buffet in Vegas. The lines are way too long if you're hungry. If you have time to waste this place is top notch and the dessert bar is HUGE!

Such a let down.

Went for lunch at about 10:15 no line, which was great. About 54 per person which is hefty so you'd think they must have some great stuff. 

They don't.

They have lots and lots of low quality stuff, the sushi tasted so bad and the seafood section was small and not fresh. 

Only thing that seemed alright was the dessert section and the Peking duck.

Not worth it, wicked spoon was way better

I have been here 4 times now and do have to say, I would have given this place a 5 but after I have watch the quality start to go down  and the prices go up as well, there is no way I would come back here again and my friends follow and trust me being known as (again) the buffet queen. Especially big casino's like this that pulls in so much revenue, they had started something great. Keep it up! But when prices go up and quality goes down, I see greed. I eat A LOT and I mean A LOT and I am very observant. So any changes, I would usually notice. The lines used to be much longer but not anymore, doesn't that tell you something? Obviously, I'm not the only one who notice it. Here are a few things in a flash:

-   Before they had choices of snow crabs and king crabs with pretty equal amounts of both. Now they mix it up where there is 80% snow and 20% king as some people would not notice the difference and just grab anything.

-   They still have the ginseng chicken soup which is delicious and used to come in individual small pots. Not there is a big pot for you to scoop in a big bowl yourself.

-   A lot of their soups are SO SALTY i can't even swallow it and had to spit it out.

-  They used to give you actual towel hand wipes which they now save and no longer give them out but this one isn't a big deal as I'm rating on food not napkins.

-  They used to have better sushi choices and even caviar which they no longer serve unless I went on a day they just didn't have it.

-  They used to serve fresh squeezed OJ in tiny jars which they don't anymore but they do however have aqua fresca's instead. 

All in all. I will give credit that they do use higher quality food and ingredients such as truffle in some of their cooking etc. and the only thing I DO have to still give them credit on is the desserts. For all you who love desserts, I LOVE the dessert selections here!!! I would eat a whole plate of dessert alone!! But is it worth spending almost $50/pp here, maybe not but in rare occasion its still ok.
Would give it a 5 stars if it wasn't for the king crabs being so salty!  The boba Thai tea is a must try!!!!

All items here are super gourmet. It's $48.99 per person for Total Rewards members so open that up to get a little discount when visiting any Caesar's owned casinos. They claim to have over 500 items but it didn't seem that much. Everything was so good though, especially if you like to try a little of everything and you won't be disappointed as there is something here for everyone in your group. For weekend brunch, they also include mimosas and bloody marys with your meal. It's always a plus at any Vegas buffets to have good crab legs and oysters, but here they have stone crab claws and oyster shooters. This place is a go-to as it is the highest ranked buffet on the strip.

Holy moly!  We waited in line for an hour and 45 minutes.  The only thing that was getting me through that wait was the thought of ayce king crab legs!  We finally made it in around 9pm and they only had snow crab and stone crab!  What happened to the king crab???  Fine, I had snow crab and it was just okay.  I wandered around to see what they offered and I must say that it was all about presentation.  The fried chicken, tater tots, fish & chips were offered in little wire fry baskets.  Each slider was placed on its own little ceramic dish.  Oh, and they have street vendor food -- corn on the cob slathered with mayo and crumbly cheese (where's the paletas??). They also have a charcuterie along with different types of cheeses.  I was excited about that.  I wanted to order wine with the meats and cheeses and found out it is not possible to order one glass of wine.  If you want wine, you have to order all-you-can-drink wine for $15.99 (on top of the $39.99 you just paid for dinner).  Anyway, we were a party of 6 and we tried everything.  A lot of the items were really salty so we needed a lot of water.  (Maybe they do this on purpose so you get full on water and don't each so much??  Guess they gotta recoup that $18MM somehow...).  For a buffet, the presentation is great, but the food is mediocre.  If you like to see your food sitting in something pretty, eat here.  If you want good food, go to the M.

Hands down.
Best buffet in Vegas of 2013 for me.

Better than Cosmo's Wicked Spoon, Bellagio and Wynn, which has been a favorites of mine for a few years.

Because it's a buffet, I stuffed myself, and I honestly cannot remember everything I ate that night so I will leave you with this...

My favorite stand out was the fresh raw oysters. And, as an Asian person, I'm usually disappointed (and annoyed) that these Vegas buffets always get the Asian food wrong. Here, the Chinese food is legit! They even have Japanese ramen. Crazy, right? (They still can't get sushi right.)

It's a must go!

A little bit overrated and priced for what they offer. 
Liked the risotto and fresh cut salami and some desserts the best.
A lot of choices tough and even have real Italian gelato.
Only a couple of bad things: bread was very hard as it had been there since morning and the cold cut Mortadella was defrosted before being sliced.

Vegas is known for their buffets and this is the one everyone is buzzing about. Been here a few times and my verdict? Hype. All hype. 

The food quality is great. Love that they have a huge variety of food from pastas, dumplings, tacos, carved meat, seafood, desserts, etc. nothing you can't get at another, less expensive buffet. I personally like the dumplings, the brisket, and the fresh juice they have next to the station you can get made to order tacos. Their dessert is definitely one of my favorites in Vegas.  Probably why I end up agreeing to come here. They can make a serious lava cake, green tea creme brûlée, and my ultimate fav is their jasmine rice pudding! 

The wait can be daunting to get in. Plus you have to have your entire party there before you can be seated. Also the lines to the food can be long since it's always so crowded! 

Service has only been... okay. The workers in the kitchen can be so rude! Slamming dishes and making it seem like they don't wanna be there. Mah bad but thanks for making the dumplings delish! Just hope they aren't spitting in the food! I feel like there's never enough waiters cause I'm always flagging someone down to refill my drinks. Meh. Definitely not impressed! 

I'll probably be back as it is the latest hype in Vegas but there are definitely other buffets to try that have the same quality food for a better price and much better service!

HUGE variety.  Food was pretty good quality too.  They have a huge array of seafood that can get you some good value.  The brisket and the short rib and pork belly were awesome.  Dessert cart was awesome.  

Some info on how to get a seat.  If you are a group or 5 or less, then you check in at a kiosk and they give you a wait time and give you a specific time of when to come back and wait in the line to pay and get in (I think its usually around 30-40 min).  If you have a group of more than 5, then you need the whole group there and they will send you to a separate line of large parties and you just have to wait.  We had a group of 8, got there at 1230 on a Sunday, and waited for about 30 min and the line wasn't super long.  But by sen just 1245, the line really grew around the corner of the hallway. 

It was good to go in the middle of the day because it was the only meal we ate all day.
Don't forget the cheese and meats in the back room. Ask for the watermelon juice.
Last year were much better, more king crabs, this year not so much, and it is $5 more now! However, i love the desserts bar, must try the pandan tiramisu cake with 24k gold leaf!

The service, it's like omg, I checked in at 4:24 and the ticket said we can come back at 8:20, then I asked the server if we can just leave and come back, she said of course we can, so me and my girlfriend left to shop and came back at 8:30, I asked the server where do we check in, she said we have get wait in line which we take another two hours she said, what the fuck is the point of letting customers getting the ticket? Even the Canadian old couple was forced to get back in line, and same as many other people, sincerely, Cesar needs to change the procedure.

I usually HATE buffets, but this is not your average buffet.  I knew that i had to try this buffet when the staff at the Cosmopolitan said that Bacchanal was better than Wicked Spoon. What could possibly go wrong when you can eat all of the fresh crab legs your heart desires? An added bonus was how they had them cut for you. I tend to shy away from crab legs because I hate cracking them open.

My fiancé and I came here twice during our most recent trip to Las Vegas. We fell in love after the first visit on a Sunday evening for dinner that we came back Tuesday for brunch. Everything we tried was amazing! We also loved the fact that we were able to by pass the stand by line, which had over an hour wait, and head straight to the front of the line with maybe a 5 minute wait. It pays to be Platinum with Total Rewards Casinos/Hotels! Will definitely be coming back here the next time we are in Vegas!

Damn! Hate to do this to one of my favorite buffet joint. 

Line was super long, not that it bothered us. It's Las Vegas and we don't mind the wait but wow that special feeling is gone. Bacchanal now feels like your everyday buffet joint and for the price they're charging us, it's becoming an over-rated buffet joint. Aside from their seafood, most of the other menu items are so-so. Their snow crabs were soo dry and it's unfortunate as I'm a seafood lover. 

Will I go back next time I'm in sin city? Probably, but I may hit up Rio first or visit the old M-resort for a quick change.

BUFFET at its Finest, top notch food, fresh seafood, spectacular deserts. I love this place, superb world class! If you have money to spare its worth to treat yourself or people (esp your out of town friends that were on vacation) and you'll make their experience a memorable one. Just make sure you have patience falling in line because it comes with the popularity that everyone wants to dine in, luckily my aunt is a diamond club member and we got in fast like just a walk in the park... Teehee!

Came yesterday for the thanksgiving dinner, it wasn't bad but wasn't worth the price either since the holiday price is 79.99 + tax per person.

There are not a great number of selections but the ones I tried are mostly pretty good. I would recommend bone marrow, but it might be too oily to someone who's not used to it. 
The king crab leg was good but too salty for me, and the smell of the oyster is a bit strong(as a person who loves oyster). I liked the shell next to king crab and the shrimp in the cold seafood area more.
I tried one slice of wagyu beef which was very hard to chew but maybe it's because it's cooked in such a big chunk. 

In the sweets area, I loved their Chinese egg tart, it was warm and crispy, I can eat it forever lol I also tried many other dessert which were all pretty average.

I wanted to give it a 3 because of the relative small range of selections in terms of a buffet, but the taste is not that bad. Maybe go for a non-holiday dinner

Hands down the best buffet in Vegas. It's pricey but worth it if you can eat a lot. I think it was around $55-$60 for the weekend. They have variety of foods that you can eat from seafood (crabs, shrimps, scallops etc) to the meat (prime rib, sausage etc), sushi, Asian foods, little sliders etc. They all taste amazing. All my favorite foods are in one buffet. They also have cute little baskets for some of the finger foods like curly fries and all so good and crispy! Mhmm...The line can be ridiculous when it's closer to dinner time so make sure you get their early. Luckily my mom and I went around 3pm ish so the line wasn't too bad and we only had to wait 30 minutes and it was a Saturday. The dessert was also delicious!! So many different desserts....the small cakes and ice cream were all very delicious. They also had little cake pops too and they were cheesecake flavor!!! AHHHHH my mouth is getting watery thinking about all the good food I got to eat this past weekend. This place is my go-to buffet place when I'm in Vegas! :)

A good buffet experience consists of high quality food and variety of choices.  Since it is Vegas, it would be expensive.  I paid $65 for weekend dinner -- pricy yes, but since you are getting fresh oysters, wagyu beef, and the freshest tasting salmon you can find anywhere, I'd like to think that it pays for itself.  

Dinner starts at 3pm and when I arrived at 4pm, I was told that the wait time is 45 minutes; luckily we were seated less than 20 minutes later.  The space is big, but lots of tables are left not cleaned.  Not sure whether the long line is a way for management to control flow, a reflection of short cleaning staff, a marketing tactic, or a bit of everything.

Also it's interesting that the price is not advertised outside as other places are. The website says $54.99 for weekend dinners, but I was quoted $65. I heard that the price can be different for different people.  Not sure if my fellow yelpers had similar experiences.

This is by far the most over-rated, over-hyped, over-priced buffet ever!  I'll save you the reader a long review and cut to the chase.  Caesar's new buffet is NOT worth the $50 entrance fee.  There is nothing special about this place, the only exception being fresh shucked oysters and mochi ice cream thats exactly the same as what you can buy from your local asian supermarket.  Yes they have a wide selection of offerings but not any more than other cheaper buffets.  Basically, if you're curious about the hype, waste your money and go check it out but if you're looking for a good buffet that won't break the bank, may I recommend the buffet at Mandalay Bay which in my opinion is the best value for money buffet in Vegas and at almost half the cost.

At first there were the loooong lines for dinner and then the $50 price of admission.  I must admit I was skeptical on how good a buffet could be.  That all changed once we were walked to our table and give a quick tour of the stations by our hostest.  My eyes lit up like I was in buffet heaven.  
Once I started to visit each station and loaded up on some food I was impressed on the selections of each station.  Peking duck and Chinese roast pork at the Chinese station, 6+ different type rolls at the sushi station, chilled snow crab legs on the seafood station and hot just boiled snow crab legs on another station!, a station just for cold cuts and sliced meats, a carver station, Mexican station, and a huge island station for sweets/desserts!   This place is buffet heaven and for $50 this is worth every penny!
I will be back one day Bacchanal Buffet.

Don't believe all the hype. Yes, it is good but no better than Wicked Spoon, M or Wynn.  Ate here on Saturday for "brunch".

The good:  NO LINE. Got right in with no wait at 10am. 

Food was all good quality and tasted tasted good. Memorable were the charcuterie selection of meats and cheeses (some fresh baked baguette would be good there).  Truffled scallop potatoes. Pizza and Asian selections were good. Eggs Benedict had no flavor at all. 

The less than good:  sorry guys, the dessert selection sucks. Lack of selection and all gelato was so weird nobody wanted to try - "beer shandy gelato", nah. 

NO PRIME RIB. Really? For brunch?  LAME. LAME. LAME
For $50 LAME!!!!!

They seated us right where the service staff stand and hawk over everyone. All we heard all meal were their Spanish conversations and them constantly glaring at us. Service was fast but uncomfortable.

It was awesome! I loved all the various stations and they variety was outstanding. I have gone for Dinner and Bruch and felt the brunch was more worth it than dinner just because it's a LOT of food. 

I'd go again...

I could write a essay on why this buffet truly is the best buffet in Vegas. First of all, let's preface this by understanding this still is just a buffet and you're going to run into a few things you may find inadequate. Overall, the food was amazing. The variety and quality of the food was well above your average buffet. We personally didn't have to wait in line because we are Diamond Rewards members with Total Rewards but I have heard the line can be hours long. Just a heads up. They have everything from sushi to prime rib, and even Vietnamese Phô! And it's good!!! The price tag may seem a little heavy but we planned our day around this meal and really felt we got our money's worth. I wouldn't recommend this experience to a family but for couples and friends it's awesome. Will definitely be back every trip.

Went to this place and was absolutely amazed, bar none best buffet out of several I tried during Las Vegas visit. From the second we walked in the smells and the sites tingled our senses even before we tasted the food.  
Very well though out presentation with great attention to detail. For example, to keep food hot plates are heated but to avoid burning fingers they provide little silicone grips. There are plenty of pictures already so I won't bother with more. Everything we ate was presented in best way possible, tiny buckets of lobster bisque, little fry baskets of onion rings and chicken and waffles, all looked like they came off of a textbook on how to market food.
Variety was great, I did not even taste everything I wanted and I made quite a few trips back to the line. 
Everything tasted fresh and delicious. Some unexpected items that I normally would not select like baby beets in citrus sauce or truffle mushrooms pizza were simply outstanding. Buffet Staples like cuts of meats and crab legs did not disappoint either. 
Dessert table was great with at least ten gelato flavors, fresh fruits and many many sweet delicious choices. 
Price was fairly high at 54 dollars for dinner but I feel it was totally worth the experience.

I'm usually not a big fan of buffets so to give 4 stars is saying a lot. 
Although the line seems long, it goes pretty fast. I want for lunch on a Sunday and waited about 30 mins. Although the price on the higher end, the food quality is worth it. Lunch includes unlimited mimosas and champagne, juices, coffee and soft drinks. 

The food selection is pretty good. Everything was really fresh. I really loved their seafood section with the warm king crab legs, clam bake, and shrimp cocktail. To my disappointment, they only had oyster shooters and not fresh oysters even though they had oysters on display. 

The taco stand was pretty awesome with a wide variety of home made salsas. Make sure you try the mango habanero salsa. 

They were very generous with the unlimited champagne and mimosas. 

I heard they now have check in kiosks to minimize the lines and fresh oysters during dinner.

Truly the buffet to compare all buffets to, at least in Vegas. A word of caution, this place gets packed really quickly, but if you're patient, wait in line and don't feed your rising hunger pains with tucked away snacks, then you will be rewarded with a feast fit for a king. The price of the admission is about $50-60, with an extra $15 to cover all alcoholic beverages. As soon as you enter the fantastic dining area, take a moment to pace yourself, walk around the 5-6 different main course stations to see which cuisine deserves a position in your stomach. They have great Asian food (take my word for it), petit salad concoctions, make-it-yourself taco stands, and an all-you-can-eat snowcrab leg stations with rock crab legs. Of course, there are the sushi station, the cheese and prosciutto station, the meat station (from ribs to lamb to chicken to sirloin), the soup (so much truffle love) and the Italian station. My favorite, however, is the dessert section, with so much amazing decorated, diabetes provoking deliciousness that made my sweet teeth tingle with excitement and my belly aching for belt-un-notching.

At the end of the day, if you are visiting Vegas, this is THE spot to visit for a day in gluttony. I'm not sure what the difference between lunch and dinner is, but def come to the dinner.

Food: 4 stars
Price: 4 stars
Service: 2 stars
Ambiance: 4 stars

This is my favorite buffet in town. I'm not a big fan a buffets but this one is pretty good. Besides the huge variety of items, the quality is great. Seafood is really good and in general all stations have delicious food. The wait is long and it is not cheap but considering the amount of seafood and freshness it is a pretty good deal. The place itself it's very nice, upscale, and cozy. The deserts are super yummy.

Meh. That's going to be the tone for the rest of this review if you're curious.

Ok so I've waited for 2 years to try this place, mainly due to the wait time. Most of the time I'm in Vegas I bring my entire village with me and that can be difficult getting a table unless  reservations are allowed. So for a while I passed by this buffet thinking what could've been.

Well, I finally got a chance to check this place out and I was disappointed to say the least. The selection is ok, not great but not terrible. I do see lots of shellfish which I'm sure is a great selling point, because hey, they aren't cheap! The oysters looked ok, not glistening like I would've liked. I passed on it. Everything else I tried was so under-seasoned that I actually had to use the salt shaker (for the first time since eating at Vegas buffets y'all!), and quite heavily at that! I wasn't feeling well (because: Vegas!) so I grabbed a bowl of congee and excitedly slurped it down. What I tasted was blandness. So yes, I added lots of salt but it's just not comparable to a well flavored bowl of congee you know? Same goes for a few other dishes. I don't remember what else I tried as they were all so lackluster. Now, if you asked what I had a W*cked Sp00n I'll be able to type out a list real fast!

Oh well, at least I can now check this place off my list instead of continuing to wonder about it next time I pass by. And next time I will just pass by...

Great meal, great food! One of the best buffets in Vegas when I stayed.

And we had such a great server. He talked with us, gave us tips, and was a pleasant addition to a great meal. We wanted to leave a comment card, but none were there, so hopefully the management will see this. Mark was one of the best servers we had in Vegas!

With care from Vancouver, Canada.

This location was a bit on the pricey side but also the only splurge-type place I ate on my most recent trip to Vegas.

I won't lie. I got my first plate filled and went back for plate #2 without batting an eye. I wanted to try everything! I somehow even saved room for a massive amount of desserts including baklava ice cream!

Our server, Michael, was wonderful.

Let me start off by saying the most of the food was great. Did I eat everything in line? No. So I can't judge for every single food item.

But the pork chops where my favorite. They honestly did not have a good selection of fine meats besides prom chop, ribs, and prime rib that was a bit overly fatty. The oysters where huge and plentiful which kept me going, my gosh I loved them. The crab legs were pretty good as well.. I just wished I added butter and garlic or something. Why didn't I?

The lines were quite ridiculous and not fair. They had multiple lines for each cuisine making it so unappetizing to go wait in line for 10 minutes to get something. That right there is what gave the 3-stars. Paying $80 (holiday weekend) just isn't fair to wait in line that long.

Ambiance was nice, waitress was nice, price was not nice. Probably wouldn't go again.

I'm staying at Caesar's Palace for 4th of July weekend and today was my very first time visiting the long anticipated Bacchanal Buffet. I have to admit, with all the hype and 5 star positive reviews I have heard of this buffet (from friends, peers and other reviews) there was a heck of a lot to live up to. The result? Two thumbs up of approval. Absolutely AMAZING.
Upon entrance, I was blown away by the decor. Stunning. The restaurant utilizes glassware for much of their decor, which made for contemporary, yet comfortable ambiance, garnished with an array of the most appetizing dishes I have ever seen at a buffet - and I have been to many around the USA, especially buffets in Las Vegas.
I sampled everything. Starting with the Chinese food to the Mexican Sope (stuffed with zucchini flower and cheese) these were incredible - I could have eaten THREE. Next was the Wagyu Beef, Brisket, and the Suckling Pig - not fatty, full of meat, skin was cripsy - perfectly done and the chef on the meat station was a hoot! Ended the meal with an awesome selection of desserts. The dessert station - my favorite - where do I even begin? (salivate salivate) Most of the buffets in Vegas I've eaten at are overly sweet and taste like they've come out of a box. The desserts here are spot on. Gelato and Ice Cream selection is excellent. Some of the best ice creams I have ever tasted - lemon basil sorbet- heart heart. Rice pudding was refreshing and tart. The coconut macroons, Good Lord. For the holiday weekend they even decorated some of the desserts with little flags - super patriotic and thoughtful.
Overall, I give this buffet 5 stars, A+++. Service was spot on as well, Super attentive. 
Great attention to detail. 
If you want a great meal, great dessert, and great service hit the Bacchanal. My only gripe was that the wait was long to get in, but 100% worth it.

Yes, it's expensive. Yes, if you want to shorten your line you'll need to cough up an additional $20 per person. Is it worth it? Yes, if you want the Vegas buffet experience. This is the Big Daddy of Vegas Buffets. It ain't romantic, but this is Vegas, baby. If you're here you're more into sleaze than romance.

So it's a buffet, let's talk buffet strategy. Ideally, you'll need a buddy that you don't mind sharing food with, and each of you tackles different sections and shares once you get back to the table. If you feel like being social, you can walk the lines together to food-gawk, but only one of you would put an item on your plate. Unless you spend hours going up to the buffet line and somehow only get a bite-worth or two with every spoonful of food, you'll never be able to try as many items as you can with this system.

The range of food available is huge, and it is always well prepared. Certain dishes in particular are far above what I would think possible for a buffet. They are among the best dishes I have had anywhere.

On our brunch and dinner visits, pretty much everything in the ASIAN section was a real standout. Their BEEF special with pepper sauce, CRISPY FISH, SHUMAI, DUMPLINGS and TARO BAO were particularly wonderful. The CONGEE station was great as well. I went back to the Asian section for another round right before I stopped eating my main meal, because I wanted my last bites to be of my favorite things.

I wish I had spent more time and stomach room at the CARVING SECTION...all I had room for once I got there was the SMOKED BRISKET, which my husband and I both agreed was probably the best we've had anywhere, and we seek out good brisket. On a second trip, we tried the RIBS, which were very good. They had excellent looking chicken and assorted sausages here, I don't think you could go wrong.

They serve both hot and cold crab, annoyingly but impressively split down the middle so you don't have to crack it open. It's great for those who don't know how to crack crab effectively, but for those that do it's a lot more work than you'd think. There is drawn butter in a easy-to-miss silver dispenser, too...just ask.

The pasta and soups were also excellent, and in the Asian section they had DUCK that was out of this world.

For brunch they had TATER TOT CASSEROLE, which I tried and yes, of course it is good, it's tater tots, man.  The CHICKEN AND WAFFLE is an interestingly battered piece of boneless chicken stuffed into a waffle cone and a hint of maple syrup, with some sweet potato tots at the bottom of the cone to round it out. Worth trying...it seemed like part donut part chicken.

Speaking of donuts, the ones near the Mexican section were good, but the CHURROS were a true guilty pleasure. They really hit that one out of the park. Don't forget to go back to that section when you're looking to end your  meal on sweet stuff.

The JUICE SECTION is a fun way to try different drinks and juices...my husband and I tried WATERMELON, TAMARIND, and HORCHATA...all interesting and worth trying, but the HORCHATA was worth going back for seconds.

SAVE ROOM FOR DESSERT!!!! This is probably the best dessert buffet experience in Vegas. You will want to make several trips up there, and there are some truly wonderful things. If you like chocolate, you'll love the warm brownie-like gooey-ness of the CHOCOLATE LAVA CAKE and the FIVE SPICE something something. The GREEN TEA AND WHITE CHOCOLATE CAKE was a true standout as well...it had a slightly crunchy exterior like the edges of a good brownie, and the taste was excellent.  The GELATO was good, and although we tried the RED BEAN and SESAME, our favorites were the NUTELLA and MANGO HABANERO. You haven't lived until you try spicy ice cream. There was also a PUMPKIN something in a white chocolate coating that was like a light pumpkin mousse...outstanding. I saw someone get a fresh made CREPE in this section, too...so if you're into that just ask someone behind the counter. Go ahead and pass on the CUPCAKES, though. My husband and I tried the red velvet and a chocolate one, and they didn't stand out nearly as much as the other items. Not worth your precious stomach space.

Just try lots of things...my husband and I didn't even pick up half of what was offered for dessert, and several items we just took a bite or two of and determined we wanted to spend our precious remaining stomach space on a different item. The Green Tea and White Chocolate Lava Cake I finished, and my husband did the same with the Chocolate Lava Cake and a chocolate tart.

By the way, if you eat here, don't expect to be hungry later in the day. We finished our meal at 1pm, and we were not hungry the next morning. So unless you have impressive self control, you can justify the expense (and truckloads of calories) because this meal will satisfy for 24 hours.

Go hungry early in the day, leave stuffed, and don't worry about trying to find a restaurant to eat at until later the next day!

In my opinion, the best buffet in Las Vegas!!
Already visited five times in two months(?), lunch and dinner combined. 
Awesome!!
Can't wait to go there again! 

Food: Good
Price: Good
Service: Good
Parking: Good

We came on sunday where you pay brunch pricing during the day which is about $50 a person plus tax. Overall the food wasn't bad but it wasnt amazing. Where they failed was with their sushi (cold/ hard rice) and they ran out of crab legs. It took about 45 minutes before they got more. What saved this from a 2 star review was their dessert which is sort of hidden. Its to the left of seafood but unless you are seated in that section then its an easy spot to miss. This worth a look. Maybe dinner is better?

Best Vegas buffet I have ever been to!      Everything was delicious. There was plenty of variety. It has the price tag to match, but if you have the opportunity to go, I highly reccomend. If you buy the 24hr Buffet of Buffets pass it is slightly less expensive. Seriously still dreaming about this place.

I love this place! Amazing food!
However I want to write and say, Really!?
Some customers are so rude and I have no idea how the staff puts up with it.
People push you over at the crepe station to get to the fresh fruit.
HELLO! It is there for the crepes!
On top of that I had to witness some mean woman assault the poor girl verbally because she couldn't build her own crepe. Yelling at her calling her a Bitch 
After the girl offered multiple times to build it for her. Is it rocket science to build your own crepe? You would have thought so the way the woman was throwing a temper tantrum like a 2 yr old child!

Then the seafood station people shoving each other out of the way for the team crab and grabbing the baskets to dump them on their plate. Take the basket with you if you want more walk your fat ass back up there and get more it is a buffet it is not like they are gonna run out!

Everyone should realize that these people serving us are not slaves and they are handling our food.
