On to the food! The build to order tacos amazing and a wonderful Chef George made the best tacos! 

An absolute must!

Had brunch here. If this is not 5 stars I don't know what is. Absolutely mind blowing selection of foods and all of them very well cooked. There's a buffet in Atlantic city that tries to mimic this but it doesn't come anywhere close. Stuffed.

The food was good, great variety but I"M PISSED.  I wanted to eat here on Xmas day, but it was a 5hr wait.  No thanks.  So, I think " I'll go on Dec 26th for breakfast".  Imagine my surprise, when we walk in( no wait at 8:30am), but am faced with a 50.00 brunch, not a 20.00 breakfast.  Yeah, I could have left, but we'd driven over from the Encore and were on our way back to Cali.  So, there went 110.00 down the drain.  I think its pretty shitty that they are still doing " brunch" even though its not a holiday.  The holiday was OVER.  Just a way to get more money from people. 

That being said, I wasn't in the mood for seafood at 8:30am so I didn't get my money's worth.  There are signs all over the place to talk to the chef, if you have dietary restrictions.  I cant eat runny yolks because they make me burp something awful.  I wanted eggs benedict so I asked for poached whites.  I was told that they couldn't do that, I would need to talk to the dude making omelets.  I talk to him and he says he cant poach me a white, even though he has a big pot of simmering water right next to him. 

That ticked me off.  If I am paying 50.00 for breakfast, I want a freaking poached egg white.  After awhile, I spoke to the manager who brought me to the chef.  I got my white and my toasted English muffin( they normally don't toast the muffins for bennies).  I didn't even want it at that point, but I got it. 

There was a very large variety of food, but the only fresh juice I saw was OJ.  The pizza crust was amazing, but they put way too much cheese on it.  I hope they remedy that.  

The desserts were a lot better than the buffet at the Wynn.  It was a good brunch, but not worth 50.00.  They didn't even have stone crab claws like I was expecting.

A little pricey, but holy crap all the good food we got. My wife and I were on a road trip through Vegas and decided to stop for a brunch buffet. $50/person and well, ya, it was awesome.

Totally worth the variety, the quality was good, and the 1 1/2 hours we were there were well spent! The portions are small which are perfect since I always tend to overload on stuff I don't end up really liking much. Got to check out almost everything and went back for the 2nds, even better 3rds, 4ths, food coma break, 5ths..

The fresh squeezed juices, the asian food, the omelets, the meat and cheeses, the egg benedicts, french toast, the gelato. My wife loved the desserts: the hazelnut rumcake, the smores gelato.. 

Anyways, the menu changes constantly so I say if you're willing to pay the ticket to get in, and quality of buffet is worth it to you, you should check this place out!

This was the very first buffet I tried when I visited Las Vegas, and I'm so glad I did. First off, the decor is gorgeous. Second, the food selections were AWESOME. Those lamb chops were some of the best I'd ever tasted, and the ceviche was out of this world! Definitely a top three favorite. My sister and I arrived before crowds even showed up, and we were amazed at what we saw. I recommend everyone go here, and the next time we visit, we'll be checking out their brunch.

Im not a regular buffet goer or anything but this was the best buffet ever.  Yes, its expensive. $50 for sunday brunch, but just do it.  When you consider a bloody Mary at the pool is $20+, this isn't that bad.

We went at 10:30AM on Sunday and there was no line.  By the time we left around 12:00 the line was Space Mountain on a summer day long.

Probably the best buffet out in Vegas. The quality of the food is good and the stations are all clean and organized. Everything was fresh, especially the seafood. The only complaint I have is the dessert section. As great as their food is, their dessert is so underwhelming. I was excited to see macarons, but they're the frozen kind because mine was still a bit frozen. Their other pastry options aren't that great either. If they step up their desserts I think this place could deserve 4/4.5 stars.

Another highly rated buffet, another letdown. 

The wait to get in this place is obnoxious. We tried to go last year and the wait was 2-3 hours long. This year, we called ahead of time and were quoted a 45 minute wait. Upon arrival, we put our name into the system and then had to wait 15 minutes for the "okay" to be added to the list. We then waited about 45 minutes to be "accepted" into the line to pay. Once we entered the pay line, it was another 45 minute wait. So, I'm not sure how we were quoted a 45 minute wait time... yeah, maybe 45 minutes for each "line". Overall, about 2 hours of waiting. Not worth it. 

For $54, I am expecting a grand buffet. This was nowhere near that. The prime rib was wayyy undercooked, to the point that there were pools of blood on my plate. The lamb chops were wayyyy overcooked. The butter station was constantly empty and they give you little ghetto plastic cups for your butter. I went on a wild goose chase to find horseradish for my prime rib. ONE person running the meat station, as opposed to Bellagio Buffet where they have a separate person for each cut of meat. The shrimp had a really stinky smell and I kept getting little slivers of shell in my crab meat. Just no. 

Honestly, the highlight of my meal was the gelato station. Strawberry Balsamic, Salted Vanilla, and Nutella Coffee gelato were pretty darn good. It's sad that this was the best part of my $54 meal. I'll be going back to Bellagio Buffet next time.

Crab leg is the reason why I am here.  Roast beef, beef short-rib, lamb chop are all very nice. Various dessert are also very alluring, especially Orange Beer sorbet! Suggest to arrive by 4pm as we arrived at around 4:20 already a long line of over 50 ahead of us.

Didn't even give this place a chance because the Disneyland reservation system is just asinine.
Background, its Friday... post-Thanksgiving and my family just arrived at 3pm. Fought the traffic and parking lot vultures... meandered through smoked filled maze. Arriving at an unintelligent kiosk: Wait time, 435 minutes....are you f'ing kinding me? Is there an option for $25 additional to "go VIP"? Nope. Went up to this hostess who's only intelligible instruction is to "Come back at 9:30".

Here's what's wrong with this....
1. There is no option on the website to inform possible patrons of the wait time or begin the "reservation" process...
2. So many international visitors were confused by this reservation system... POST multilingual instructions of the system.
3. Wait times are RIDICULOUS! 

The millions of dollars should have been spent on expansion of the facility or better information up front, i.e. website, translations, etc.

All these high ratings may just be psychological due to the higher cost to the patron... see http://foodpsychology.cornell.edu/OP/buffet_pricing

Just like anything in life you get what you pay for.
Avoid the line with the express pass
Service can be rather slow but don't worry just flag them down!
Good bloody mary!

Cheers.
By far the best buffet on the strip. The food is always fresh and delicious and all the staff is very hospitable and attentive... I always spring for the bottomless mimosas... they are so worth it!

"Too much of a good thing can be wonderful!" - Mae West

Loosen the belt buckle or better yet break out the sweatpants. Avoid eating any large meals all day, stick to a banana and arrive at the The Bacchannal ready to eat! The line to dinner can be pretty long we waited over half an hour to pay and then another 10-15 minutes to be seated. They took our picture before being seated, I think to compare how bloated and defeated we where at the end. The Bacchannal is really an orgy of tastes and flavors with over 500 dishes. They rotate so many different things that if you went two nights in a row they would mix it up. They have 6 different stations of food. The seafood section is amazing very fresh and amazing crab legs, lobster and corn chowder, a mini clambake basket, a mini crayfish boil basket. For warm crab legs go to the Italian section. 

The Chinese section is also a must. The dim sum was so good but seemed to lack the individual attention like most dim sum locations. 

The last location that is a must is the dessert station. Save room! So many choices, fresh crepes with so many different choices to add to it. Tiramisu shooters, small cheesecakes and carrot cakes. Chocolate dipped strawberry! 

The price for dinner during the week is 50 dollars. Slightly pricey (and what ultimately makes me deduct a star). During the weekend they jack up the price (which is standard in Vegas). 

Also tip your attendant, they are bringing you drinks and taking plates away for you. 

Enjoy rolling out of the Bacchannal!

The buffet had a lot of options from Japanese station, Italian station, seafood and burgers. Everything was good and the decor modern and nice. The waiters were a little slow at getting beverages and picking up used plates.

Went for dinner on Saturday night and on Sunday night. Both times the food and the variety was extremely satisfying an better than anything else in Vegas (been to Wynns, Wicked Spoon, Bellagio). However the waiting time before entering the buffet on a Saturday is ridiculous and even worse is that the buffet is very crowded and you have to wait a lot at the different cooking stations. 
Also the service could be better. Very friendly but it takes a while for all plates to e removed.

Woah. This buffet... is crazy... Food was really good and the service was phenomenal. My party and I were able to meet the executive chef as well as Chef Niko, who was so cool and friendly! The waitresses/bussers who took our plates were always attentive, which we were extremely appreciative of because we had a million plates. My favorite food item was the pho and the yummy wagyu!! I can eat it all day and night :)
Best dinner buffet in Las Vegas. Good selection and good quality food. That price tho. Expensive, but that's expected for Vegas buffets.

After 3 hours of wait, we finally get to eat and came back to the restaurant, it end up another half hour to an hours of wait . The buffet it self cost $75! Does anything really worth at least 3 to 4 hour of wait !!!!! Hell to the nooooooo. We drove all the way from LA to here and this is the service we got. So disappointed! Is this a joke ?!!!!

We have always stayed away from this buffet, because of the price.  However, we decided to give it a try on Saturday, August 18th at about 9:45AM.  

I believe the current price of brunch is about $55.00 per person, which does not include any alcohol.  This is what has kept us away from this buffet.   We believe one of the best buffets for your money is Studio B at the M.  We still believe that; however, we noticed a Travelzoo voucher online for the Bacchanal for $88.00 for two people for brunch with 1 mimosa each, IF you came before 10am on a weekend.

We arrived just before 10am and were seated promptly.  We had an excellent server, who was constantly checking up on us.

Well, this buffet does live up to the hype.  We thought it was excellent in every single way.  WOW!  The amount of food, the selection, the various types of cuisine and preparation methods.  Everything was fabulous!    I cannot even go into detail about all of the food, because I may have had 1 or 2 things I did not like out of the probably 25 things I tried.  For a buffet, that is absolutely phenomenal.

I will go out on a limb here and say that this buffet has the best desserts for a buffet, that I have ever tried.  Some of our favorites were the Pistachio and Ube Gelato, as well as the Pink Lemonade cupcake.  WOW!  

We were here for about 2 hours, and then decided to part ways, as we just couldn't eat any more.  

So, will we return?  We will return, if we find another offer online at approximately the price we paid today.  Although we loved it, we simply cannot justify paying $55.00 per person when we are not ridiculously crazy over eaters.  With that said, I would recommend that everyone at least try it once -- and make your own decision about value in the future.

We picked the right one! We have eaten at several buffets in Las Vegas and wanted to try something new. The  Bacchanal did not disappoint. The line is long but believe me it is well worth it. The food was fresh and fun with too many options for one visit. And the desserts!  We will definitely be back.

Okay, I hope I don't get shot for disagreeing with the masses. I ate here on Friday night for dinner, so my meal was $55 + gratuity. For $60+, I wish I hadn't pre-paid my tip at the register with my card. 

Seafood was not great at all. I tried everything except for one cooked fish dish that I can't remember. Bland AND salty. Way too salty. Yes, I know these are saltwater creatures, but that's just insane. Some were also overcooked so they were dry. 

Prime rib was okay, rib eye lollipop was so disappointing (tough and flavorless), but the lamb chops were so good! Sadly when I went back to end my savory part of the meal with another lamb chop or two, these were not as flavorful as the first round. The line for the meats was a mess--it combined with people trying to exit the seafood line, the staff going in and out of a kitchen door.

I didn't try much (or any) of some of the Mexican/Italian/Asian offerings, mostly because nothing looked particularly good or unique. Some of the deli meats in the Italian area were good, though some were a little.. strange. Maybe I was supposed to pair it with one of the cheeses? And the cheeses looked super cool on display, until I realized they were brands like President's brie, which I can find in any grocery store. I wanted sushi but they looked... off. Like they weren't as fresh as I would have preferred.

Dessert was much better, though! I had mochi ice cream, carrot cake, macarons, and a cookie (or was it a mini cupcake? or a cheesecake pop? clearly this was not memorable enough...) Crepe line was too long, and they had run out of bananas foster when I looked, so I didn't want to wait.

WORST PART:
I came with two friends who paid together while I paid for myself. The hostess accidentally gave our seating book (with our receipts and pre-paid tips) to a group of 4 and gave us theirs. We have no idea this happened. When our server came to ask for our drink order, he was confused when we said there was no fourth person at our table. He kept saying, "It says 4!" Us: "We're just 3..." And he made us repeat our drink orders. He snatched the seating book and walked away saying he needed to check on something. Minutes later, one of the hostesses is at our table demanding our receipts. We take them out, and we ask what's wrong. She couldn't answer us, but said that we had done nothing wrong. Yet, when we asked what we needed to do or what she needed from us, she wouldn't leave. She finally stomps away when we firmly said, "Well, if we did nothing wrong and we've shown you our receipts, like you've asked, then... what do you still need?" (Not so subtle hint.) She leaves. Then a SECOND hostess comes rushing to our table and asks to see our receipts. Again. This time, we finally get an answer on what's wrong, and she explains the mistake that I mentioned in the first part of this paragraph. She says she just needs our receipt numbers and names so she can track down the table and server that had our receipts so the right servers could get the right pre-paid tips. 

We never hear back from the hostesses again, so we never found out if they had straightened out the issue. Our server seemed to be backed up by too-attentive server from the table next to us, so he was actually the person to notice that our drinks were low. But, we were never introduced to this guy... 

So, yes, Yelp says it best: "Meh. I've experienced better." Go anywhere else and save yourself the money. Enjoy the pretty decor made of a billion cups from the outside.
They kick ppls out of the line becoz we don't have enough ppls at the middle of the line. The servants have very bad attitude too.

I'm only giving this 3 stars...because for how much you pay they shouldn't run out of certain things. I had a taste of everything,   and nothing really stood out.  It reminds me of any all you can eat buffets just higher class? Like they came in cute little containers.  The calamri was in a cute little fry basket, the lasagna roll was in a tiny casserole dish.  When it was time for desserts, they started running out.  So nope, wouldn't eat here again.  But was a fun experience.

This is definitely a place to try, but I think once is enough. Everything was decent and the selection is endless, probably one of the buffets where I couldn't try everything, and there were still things I wanted to try.

Good points: The servers were very attentive and nice. There was sea bass and salmon and they were both cooked to perfection. I thought the rack of lamb was decent too. We actually liked the porridge and the ginseng soup. The tacos were delish. I liked the fried calamari. The fresh oysters were very tasty and fresh. I liked how they offered steamed crab legs so you don't have to get the iced ones, just ask the guys working behind the counter for some hot crab legs. I liked the chocolate covered strawberries, too full to have a mochi =( 

Bad points: The prime rib was not very good, I've never had tomahawk steaks anywhere else, but I doubt it should be dry and chewy. The lines for the carving station was very annoying. The fried chicken was very dry and flavorless. 

Final note: it might be fun to try once to  experience it for yourself. I think for $50 per person it didn't wow me as much as I think it should, there is a huge selection of food but nothing stood out.

This is by far the best buffet I have ever been to in my life! Worth every penny! Everything they have is fresh and absolutely delicious!!! If you're in Vegas, you MUST go there! Their seafood, poke, OMG desserts etc...... I was in food heaven!!!! My new Las Vegas ritual will be coming to this place! I can't wait to go back and stuff my face!

Memosa's are harder to get when you get unlimited because one server is available per section. However, everything else is just marvelous-whether it's the food or selection- you are guaranteed to walk out full and happy. Their dessert section has the best crepes.

Yassssss!!! This is it. If you are a crab leg lover this is truly the place. And don't just stop at the ones "on ice"....The WARM / STEAMED crab legs are in a different area of the buffet!!! Go on empty and enjoy!!!!

THE BEST BUFFET. After eating here, we didn't even feel the need to eat at any other buffet. Even compared to regular restaurants, their food was awesome. There was sooooo much to choose from, and all different genres. The options are endless, I'm sad that I couldn't try everything I wanted to try because I was getting too full! 

Their dessert selection is huge and will satisfy any sweet tooth, and then some. 

Food presentation is great, with some items individually plated in small serving sizes.

the attendants were definitely attentive and checked up on us frequently.c

Do I need to mention the fresh squeezed juices?!

The dining area is also very clean and elegant. Tons of tables able to accommodate small and large parties.

2 hour limit. We were full in the first 20 minutes. Eeek! 

Seriously, a great buffet!

**BRUNCH & DINNER** 
So the plan was to arrive around 1:30pm on a Saturday afternoon for the end of Brunch. Then catch dinner items for the Brunch price. This worked out perfectly. Savings of over $20 for two people. The wait after signing in on the computer was about 30mins and then probably about another 20mins after we got into line, seemed like the bigger parties were having to wait longer.
We got a great table right at the end of the food line which happens to be the Asian Food. My husbands filipino so he was super excited for some Pork Belly. I didn't have any but he thought it was delicious, along with the Beijing Duck. He's all time favorite, which is a dinner item, was the Lamb T-Bone. I don't even like Lamb and I still enjoyed it as well. Another item that stood out to my husband was the Bone Marrow (I'm not a fan) which was way better prepared than the Wickedspoon, it wasn't just plan like Cosmo, it actually had meat on it as well as a delicious sauce.
My 1st plate consisted of some Brunch items and salads. I had the Avocado Toast with Lump Crab Meat on top, basically scrapped the Avocado & Crab off 4 pieces of toast. The Ahi Poke plate was fresh and delicious. Meats and cheeses were all really tasty. Now that I got some greens, time to really dig in!
2nd plate was my favorite! I loved the Lobster Benedict and it was extra tasty when I poured some Lobster Bisque on top of it, so RICH!!! I normally don't even like poached eggs but this one was cooked too perfectly not to enjoy. Really enjoyed the Caesar salad with sundried tomatoes and the dressing was so creamy, could really taste the anchovies too. The deviled egg was good as well with a avocado hummus on a bed of greens dressed with a vinaigrette. I got some ceviche and really wanted some fresh avocado to go with it. I found a chef walking around making sure all the dishes looked good, and asked him, "where can I find some avocado." He said one minute, while he yelled back to the guys behind the counter, "half of avocado, please!" I was so delighted to have this perfectly ripe avocado, I put it on everything! 
Plate 3.5 was full of Spanish/Italian dishes. I had to try out the Street Tacos, got one of each (carne asada(steak),chicken & al pastor(pork).They were okay, good but nothing too special (but I have lived in El Paso, TX for 6yrs, so I know good tacos). The pork chile verde was so tender and great flavor. For the Italian, I tried the meatballs (decent, not the best), gnocchi pesto (better when fresh, delicious & creamy), & same goes for the pizza...wait for the fresh slices. Again the Lamb T-Bone was delicious a must try even for those who don't like lamb (juicy & tender). 
Plate 4 was all Seafood (get your money's worth plate). One of everything they had! Oyster, Mussels, Soft shell Crab (served with this sweet polenta was deliciously devoured), Escargot, Jonah Crab Claw (so hard to get to the meat), King Crab Claw(see pic), Salmon (not that much flavor, was moist and flaky thou), Tiger Prawns(large & juicy) & Sea Snails(. My favorite thing off of this plate was the Sea Snail (first time trying this, reminded me of abalone) & Escargot, sauce made it so delicious!! If I wasn't so full I would have gone back for a few more! Always next time! 
So dinner starts at 3pm, but not all items are put out yet. I would say by 3:45-4pm you can see the buffet line change. They keep the good stuff and just add in more items. Like Suckling Roasted Pig, a few different Asian items that didn't even have signs yet, tamales, a new pasta dish (very creamy carbonara) and some new sides (instead of breakfast sausages/bacon). The Worst thing I tried was the Mac & Cheese, so gross, too al dente and the flavor was not good. Second Worst was the mini burgers, dry hockey pucks  Okay onto the good stuff, the SWEETS!! 
Plate 5/6 all the sweets I could stuff on two plates. I was so sad...I really wanted a tasty crepe made to order....but it was a fail. I asked for Nutella inside and caramel sauce on top, added whip cream and French vanilla ice cream...got back to my table and there was nothing inside my crepe. I did squeeze a sticky bun(hot) on my crepe plate to go with my ice cream, so that wasn't disappointing. Well my other plate of goodies were so delicious! All so flavorful!! They had really pretty looking desserts as well, even one with their name on it. I couldn't pick a favorite dessert...too many of them were so good. But on the other hand my husband managed to eat 2 Creme Brûlées...I got one bite and it was very rich and creamy! 
So overall...get your moneys worth and go for Brunch and stay for Dinner! Best of both worlds! Also I would personally go a little bit earlier to catch more fresher Brunch items! Hope my review helps you decide to try this unique buffet.

My mouth is watering just remembering this experience! Worth it! Mimosas are free refills! 

Cons: I thought the Chinese food was too salty and the Japanese/sushi was just okay. Crab legs were delicious but very WET. I think I would prefer that they don't serve it frozen like that. Boil for a few minutes and leave whole. Don't cut in half. Snow crab is easy to get into with just your hands.

Overall high quality food. Mostly refined plates.
Pro tip: Oysters come out later like 2 or 3
I'm not a big fan of buffets usually, but I do have to say that this buffet was good.  I thought it was a bit over priced. We went for breakfast, the buffet isn't that large but service was good.

When it comes to buffets, Caesar's is king.  It comes with a royal price tag, but that $50 per person is your golden ticket to an otherworldly buffet experience.  Not only are the sheer quantities staggering (they boast more than 500 offerings), but the quality and presentation were of a level that I've never experienced at a buffet before.  You will not find large troughs of food of indeterminate age and freshness here, oh no.  Most of their dishes are prepared in individual miniature-size servings.  You can serve yourself as many as you want, of course, but for those who are trying to sample as many different dishes as possible, the individual servings help with portion control.  Plus, the often adorable miniature presentation appealed to my girlish sensibilities.

I had six courses, and I'll attempt to recount as much as possible:

Course 1:  Salad and Asian
Watermelon and feta salad (great flavor combination), some sort of beet salad, selection of sushi, ahi poke.

Course 2:  Mexican
Tostada, pozole, Mexican street corn.  The tostada and corn were delicious, and I loved that the corn was about a sixth of an ear (back to that sampling size concept).  The pozole was pretty good, but my mother-in-law makes some pretty amazing pozole, and I don't know if anyone else's could ever stack up.

Course 3:  Meat
Have you ever been to an all-you-can-eat churrascaria where the waiters come around with platters upon platters of different kinds of meats?  This is what the carving block at Bacchanal is like, only you get it yourself and it's all in one location.  It was like a giant meat parade.  I loved the lamb chops (with a little mint jelly, natch). 

Course 4:  Seafood
Yet another adorable presentation:  the mini clam bake buckets.  Small buckets with a few clams, a few slices of Andouille sausage, and a tiny piece of corn on the cob.  Aside from that, I had mussles and some shrimp and grits.  If you've ever had really good shrimp and grits (such as those from Charleston) these might fall a little short of your expectations, but they were my no means bad.  

Course 5:  Fruit and Cheese
They had such an enticing selection, I just couldn't say no.

Course 6:  The big one.  The pièce de résistance.  The whole reason why I was there ... DESSERT!  I literally made three trips to the dessert bar to collect as many delectable dishes as I could.  (Does that mean I actually had eight courses and not six?)  So many desserts ... I had cheesecake and mousse and cookies and crème brûlée and chocolate lava cake and cupcakes and panna cotta and macarons and pecan pie and red velvet cake, and I know I'm forgetting so much more.  I'll just upload a pic; there's no way I could recount all this.  

Bacchanal was a feast unlike any I've had before ... and I didn't even have to make a trip to the vomitorium when I was done.  The next time I'm in Vegas, I would absolutely, without hesitation, fork over another $50 for another ticket to paradise.

Wholly schneikeis!   This was simply the best bang for your buck meal experience in Las Vegas.  It's the best buffet I have ever been to (and my fat ass has been to many of them through the years visiting Vegas and other establishments).  WOW!   Go and pay for it - you will not be disappointed because it has something amazing for everyone (except vegetarians).

Amazing variety and delicious food overall. The only section that wasn't incredible was the Asian food, which was really surprising given all the choices. The soups were also super salty and the brisket was hard as a rock. Nevertheless, I left stuffed and satisfied. This is my third time eating at the buffet. It's good but I probably don't need to come again.
Below average, most items not served hot. Too expensive for the quality of food. Carving station served in seasoned meats. Desert crape redeemed the appetite.

Considering my last Vegas buffet was anything but satisfying at the Mandalay Bay, Bacchanal was very good, The only problem is they have so much to choose from, you can't possibly try it all. I guess that's incentive to go back. The deserts were great, especially the pecan and key lime tarts. I concentrated on the Italian and Mexican food stations mostly. The Asian and seafood looked very appetizing as well. I'll be back.

The only city where I like buffets ... VEGAS!!  The food selection and quality is amazing: the CRAB LEGS, carving station, tacos, XLB, & secret souffles- ask for it at the dessert  bar.  It is pricey and a long wait, but so far my favorite buffet spot in Vegas.

The only down side is everyone in our party got the runs after...and if you're anything like us (you probably are) and you have 20 people sharing 2 bathrooms at your hotel, it's a bit of a challenge.  Almost every buffet I have ever eaten at has that aftermath or I go into unintentional bulimic mode, which is why I typically hate buffets.  

If you're in Vegas and trying to do it #YOLO style, go here!  At least you'll enjoy consuming it!

As a Los Angeles resident and a person who frequents Vegas quite often, this was easily the best buffet I've had.  The usual top choices for people were Bellagio and Wynn, and more recently, Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo. So you might be wondering what makes this so good? Everything. 

Let me start with the entrance. Instead of waiting for 1-2 hours in line, all you have to do is wait in one short line to put your name and number in a computer and it'll tell you when to come back. Our wait was 82 minutes. It told us to come back at a specific time and it even took our phone number to remind us. This is a win-win, you don't have to waste time in line and the casino will get you back in the casino to spend more money instead. 

Then you come back at your time slot where you pay the $41.99 for the champagne brunch. It automatically comes with the champagne fyi. 

Then you wait in another short line until your table is ready. After that you are overwhelmed with where to start. We were seated next to the dessert table and it was quickly drawn to the crepe station. Having gone to Europe in May, I was beyond excited. They crank out fresh crepes for the people and then you put on the fixins you like...fruits, caramel, chocolate, Nutella, whipped cream. The best part was the bananas that were already covered in caramel. I recommend taking the folded crepe they give you, unfold it, put in the bananas with caramel sauce and Nutella, close it, and some whipped cream and more Nutella. 

Then there is the real food. The Asian food was amazing - from the Thai Yellow Curry to the Pad Thai, to the Kung Pao. All perfect. Then they had this AMAZING taco station, carving station with bomb French fries. 

I will say that as someone who doesn't eat seafood really, this place had more than enough to satisfy me. Many of the other buffets make the salad bar, fruit area, and cheeses very prominent but the great thing about this buffet is that they had all of that stuff but it wasn't front and center. They gave more than allotted space to the real food. 

What really stood out to me was how authentic everything individually tasted. Usually when you go to a buffet, they have a couple really good things, but I could honestly say, everything here exceeded my expectations beyond measure. Each genre individually tasted so perfect. I can't tell you how on point the tacos were. 

From beginning to end, it was an experience I'll never forget. 

The one thing I will say is pace yourself, I did not feel good from stuffing myself. I got a little overzealous, but in the end, it was so worth it.

This buffet is by far the best in Las Vegas, but be weary it is pricy. You get what you pay for and there are many different types of food. I could spend hours at this place trying all the food. The desert is pretty fun too.

Ranked #1 Buffett in America by USA Today. A lot of hype surrounding this place before eating here. I would say by far it's the best Buffett I've ever had the pleasure. It's not just AYCE it's set itself at such a high caliber. Quality is superb. Must to dinner for the On the Bone Ribeye is a sight!

Very long lines and the food is subpar. I was a little disappointed after the fact that it's not really worth the 2.5 hours of wait. Still prefer the prime ribs at the buffet in Wynn. Probably will not come back and go through the wait again. Overall, it's just a buffet and nothing in particular that is worth the wait.

Best Buffet I have ever been to!!!  Been to Vegas a lot of times and been to a lot of buffets and never tried this one until now. It is so worth the wait and worth the money. We got the 24 hour buffet and had to pay $30 extra each time to go to this buffet but so worth it. Crab legs were so tasty. I don't know what they do to those but they are awesome!  Sushi was amazing too!  Everything I ate was amazing. The service was amazing too. Even though it was super busy, our server was visiting us and refilling our drinks constantly. Also we were still there eating after they closed and he went above and beyond to find myself and the table next to me some coffee. Amazing place!!!  If your in Vegas it's a must to go here!

Great food....but a bit overpriced. Just like most things at Caesars, I was in awe of the cleanliness and decor, and price. The food was really good. I ate there a few times but $70 a person......seriously?  Vegas come on now!  To the food. The meats were great. Lamb, ribs, roast beef, brisket, and I'm sure I'm forgetting more than one. All really good but I though the lamb was the best and the brisket was subpar. Sea food everywhere. Crab legs was what I invested my time in eating. Frozen out front or if you sneak around to over by the Italian it was boiled which I was happy about. Sushi was ok, and I eat sushi almost twice a week, so when I think it's just ok, really it's only edible because I paid $70 for a buffet and I was determined to get my money out of it. The had a pretty cool feature which was the mini, or as we call them in SoCal, street taco stand. Didn't try it but there always seemed to be a line and it was made to order.  The wait wasn't too bad unless you had a huge party then I'd think it would be. Would I go back.....only if I was bringing friend of mine that I know can eat our weight in crab.

What a great breakfast! This was probably my favourite breakfast buffet on this, my first, trip to Vegas. I really like the 'small plate' idea at many of the stations, which I think keeps fresher food coming and easier to sample many items. A definite buffet on my future visits.

When it came to the food, there were a lot of things they got right but fell short on just a few. Overall this is a Buffet lovers dream! You cannot beat the value for the selection and quality of food and flavors! Best value on the strip. 

This is not only a feast of feasts with the intense flavors from around the world but it has very attractive aesthetics and a rather unique design from one of the most sought after design firms in the world. It's unlike any other buffet. It's elegantly warm, modern and sophisticated. Designed to make you, the diner, interact with the Chefs who prepare your food in open show kitchens throughout each of the sections. Its incredibly thoughtful and you feel almost at home. 

Cuisines range from East to West and everything in between. It's got an incredible seafood selection. Freshly made to order just about everything! Street style tacos, Japanese Ramen, Dessert Soufflé, freshly Steamed Crab legs etc. It's no joke. 

There were a few things that missed the mark. The Paella was missing the lovely char at the bottom of the pan where the rice is crispy. It was more like rice and seafood cooked separately then placed in a cast iron skillet for presentation. If you're going to make fresh noodles for Ramen than at least do the Paella justice and cook it traditionally, all in one pan. 

The Pho was a little under seasoned. It was spot on for taste profile but lacking salt. Nothing more boring than bland soup. 

The Pork Ramen stole the show in my opinion. It was perfect. It was incredibly delicious. Perfectly seasoned with all the tender flavors of the pork. Freshly made noodles are cooked to order in front of you. 

I was a little disappointed that they did not have their long list of made to order Soufflés, instead only serving one tonight. Like a phantom pain, I will miss it. My dreams forever haunted by the Pistachio Soufflé!: (

If I could recommend anything to Chef Green, I would say that just about every item including my Ramen was luke warm or cold by the time I brought it to the table. In that respect, my noodles ended up a little too al dente. Not a big deal. Maybe it's personal preference but I just like my food pipping hot ;-) 

In the end, it was a lovely experience. One I'll be talking about for awhile.

Service is really slow. I guess the waiter is not working for tips. Food is OK for $60 per person. I don't think I want to come back since there are not that many customers and it took them more than 10 minutes to ask us the drinks.

I was seriously BLOWN away by this dinner buffet. I've tried almost every good buffet in Vegas (i.e., Wicked Spoon, Wynn, Bellagio, etc) and this ones wins hands down. The line is really intimidating, but it moves relatively quickly. I thought the wait was worth it, for sure. 

Usually at buffets, there are only a handful of dishes that I gravitate towards, but here I was overwhelmed with all of the delicious offerings (that's not to say that everything was fantastic, but close). Prime rib, tomohawk rib eye steak, ribs, oyster, sushi, gelato, crepe, and the list goes on. I REALLY LOVED the crepe, they make the crepe and you put your toppings on yourself. The ingredients are all really fresh and the texture of the crepe is so good; it tastes way better than the Paris buffet's crepes.

(WEEKDAY DINNER REVIEW ONLY) I am sorry but half of the photos on yelp are now false..they've brought the buffet way below the expectations that I had looking at all the photos, but be wary. I came on a weekday. Monday, WHICH MIGHT EXPLAIN THE BELOW QUALITY EXPECTATIONS.. 
1. Desserts- Only about 2-4 plates of each type of cake and their was no such cheesecake, which from the reviews was amazing but sadly their was none :( and tried a carrot cake..guess it was old or something it tasted so dry..I mean..wow. I'm sorry for being fussy Guys xD..but I was really looking forward for "A BUFFET WORTHY OF THE GODS (the motto)"
2. The way foods were served in mini baskets, mini pots, mini bowls. Nope. After review and review about the grand opening month with cute signature miniature bowls/pots/baskets, which I came to look forward to :3. But. Those fried chicken baskets? Those cute sweet potato tots in baskets? Nope. First of all their was not a single fried chicken ( I didn't mind anyway but just pointing out for those) and no such thing as tater tots in a cute basket..same with the ginseng chicken soup. No pots as pointed out in photos..
3. (Subjective) I'm not very fond of the taco station, dry meat
4. Fresh fruit juices, trust me guys this was really fresh before and now it's not..
Overall in was way below these expectations I had but it's my fault for reading all the good reviews xD..haha..sorry for being fussy again! But where their is cons their is pros :3
PROS- 
1. OMG. Divine sweet crab legs oh my dear lords as in most and nearly ever buffet in Vegas when you usually steam boil the crab legs they turn all..ugh and bland.. But these were deliciously sweet even after being boiled in hot water which I love them steamed and to those who don't know how, bring a plate to the Italian section and their is like these huge colorful pots, just put a plate on the counter and they'll give you bunch of cut up crab legs now people might think it's a con for it to be split, but at bacchanal I don't know how they do this but it doesn't taste dry up at all so don't worry..but I can speak for every day here..
OVERALL..Guys I totally think this place would of been better if I went on a weekend so..I'll see c:

I came here because of all the hype about this place. The dinner line was super long just to pay on the Tuesday night we went. The total bill for two was about $110. The line for the crab legs (which was the big draw) was ridiculous so I waited about 30 minutes and it got cut in half. The legs were very good and well worth the $50 per person rate, but if you don't dig it, then I would say go somewhere else. I also got some lamb, prime rib and sushi. This was the best and most expensive buffet that I have been to.

everyone says that this is the best buffet in vegas....it is not....the best buffet in vegas is the bellagio, by far....no comparison.....the food quality is 10times better at the bellagio....the wait staff at the bellagio was much more attentive to your needs...they were missing a lot of items that i had seen advertised...its not that it was a bad buffet....its just that it is not top notch like everyone says it is......and the bellagio is cheaper.....what your paying for at the bacchanal is the hype.....i don't eat hype....i eat good food....

I went there in Mother's day. This was my first time trying their buffet. For Mother's Day special, dinner is $69.99. They have a lot of food session including Asian food, Mexican food, European food and dessert session (my most favorite one). Their steak is very good. All of food sessions are full with my expectation. I gave them 4 out of 5 (actually I wanna give 3.5stars) because of the cashier girl. When I arrived the cashier counter, she even didn't smile and just asked how many people. She answered impatiently whenever I asked about the buffet. Just asked to continue the transaction. I don't have any idea why she was hurry. There didn't have many people the time I arrived. The woman who did serve my table is perfectly good. She is very kind lady that I've ever seen.

This was by far the best buffet in Las Vegas! Totally worth every penny!! they have a huge selection of different variety on foods and the taste was amazing! loved their Brisket it just melts in your mouth! and their dessert section was huge and the quality in their food tasted great!

I came here for lunch after hearing so many great things about the selection and taste.
imho every single type of cuisine is done very well here at Bacchanal. Carving station is highly recommended, great quality cuts and is never poorly executed. Usually includes lamb, which is different from most buffets in vegas. 

Seafood is also fresh, and safe to eat. I had a couple of plates of just the raw oysters and crab legs (steamed and cold). 

the kicker? the desserts are so effing great! a wide variety from homemade gelato to macaroons to crepes made fresh in front of you. this buffet is a must if you're trying to seek out the best of Vegas.

My favorite buffet in Vegas, hands down. Too bad the wait is super long. Came by recently on a Saturday around 2 PM expecting to make it for the weekend brunch, but when we got our ticket the estimated wait time was 1.5 hours. Bummer, but we ended up killing time on the slot machines and didn't get seated until around 3:30 PM. The price for weekend dinner is $57.99. The buffet is separated by different cuisines, seafood, carving/meat, Mexican/taco station, Italian, salads, and Asian and dessert. 

My first rounds are usually seafood, I prefer the steamed crab legs over the chilled ones. They have steamed ones over at the Italian section. I also like how big their shrimp cocktails are. My bf and I probably eat around 3 plates of crab legs before we move on to other sections. Some of my favorites are the prime rib, lamb chops, the street tacos, and truffle potato gratin (I haven't seen it in a while though). I also like their noodle station, they have udon, pho, ramen and laksa. The sushi station is just okay, they should add more variety. Their dessert selection is amazing, I usually go for the crepe, creme brûlée and gelato. They also have a lot of green tea flavored desserts.

Everybody raves about this place, and now I see why.  This is one of the best buffets in vegas.  I haven't tried every buffet, so I can't say it's the best yet.  The sterling brunch at Bally's is still pretty good though.  But, Bucchanal blows it away with more variety.  The food doesn't taste over salted.  Most buffets are so salty, they want you to drink more water.  Hours after eating you still thirsty.

Despite popular opinion & many raving about this being the best buffet in Vegas, the food overall was just alriiiight.

The prime rib was good, some of the Italian dishes were exquisite, but the Asian selection could really use some improvement. Also maybe because I don't like seafood so I didn't eat the famous crab legs. Yeah ok maybe it's just me.

The dessert though ..... Speechless. I've never seen such a variety of desserts in one place at the same time! Literally stacked. The gelato, Thai tea boba float, and creme brûlée were all so good, I highly recommend!! 
The tacos were good too but I can get good tacos anywhere (like El Gordo for instance) hmm oh yeah the unlimited champagne & mimosas were cool. It was a fun dining experience unlike any other but I probably won't be back, onto the next one. What else u got Vegas

Just because it's in an older casino doesn't mean it can't be the best! Best buffet and a great option to other pricey dining places at Vegas. We went to a few restaurants that cost more per entree than the bill here so we were wondering why we didn't come here more often. 

Be sure to arrive before 530 if you don't want to wait in a line. They have a large variety from different types of fruit drinks in milk jugs, sashimi, pasta, different cuts of meats, macaroons, and an endless amount of fresh seafood. Definitely come here at least one night of your vegas trip.
Come hungry cause the food is amazing and there is so much variety. My favorite part was desserts- I definitely splurged in. Coming back soon!

Looking to eat your heart out and stuff your guts beyond their capacity? Step right up. 

For a Sunday dinner we paid $63/person, and we certainly got our money's worth. 

The offerings are almost overhwelming. From prime rib, lamb chops, and crab legs/claws, to sushi, dim sum, crawfish, pasta and everything in between. The buffet really lives up to its name and you feel down right sinful after finishing your meal. 

I wasn't too blown away by their desserts which tasted okay, but if I was more of a sweet tooth I might be disappointed. 

After trying two of the main buffets in Vegas I don't know if I'd do either again because there are so many amazing culinary options, but it is definitely worth trying at least once in your life.

What a buffet! I've come here for both lunch and dinner after the revamping.

I'd say overall, dinner is probably more worth it than the lunch. With dinner you get the seafood, like oysters, oyster shooters, and ceviche. The lunch instead comes with melon juices and melons.

Good: Oysters and oyster shooters! So good and there are always tons of oysters. My only complaint is that one time, a waiter basically stole an entire full plate of untouched oysters from our table while I had my head turned. Also, there really should be small sauce cups or something for hot sauce to top the oysters.

Meats are also very good! The prime rib and brisket are pretty awesome. The bacon was decent.

Desserts are very good. There is gelato (flavors are hit and miss but mostly hit), a crepe station, and various small cakes/pies/candy.

Pineapple juice and free mimosas!

Hot crab legs are also amazing. They should put the butter closer though.

Asian duck is really good.

At some point I lost all dignity and was pigging out only with my hands.

Bad:
Watermelon juice was meh. Grapefruit juice was terrible.

The Asian besides the duck overall wasn't too impressive. The sushi is not very good as well.

Cold crab legs are terrible. Crab legs that were only partially heated up aren't very good either.

Came here for the dinner buffet. Make sure to come in early, you can also check in at the kiosk, it will print out what time you can come back and they will text you too if your group is ready to be seated. They have a good selection of food. My favorite part of the buffet is the boiled crab legs and the dessert station.

The word on the street is that Caesar's has the best buffet in town, so I decided to check it out with my party. We arrived around 10:30am and were seated immediately. Given our timing, we were able to enjoy some breakfast food before they crossed over to lunch at 11. They had a pretty extensive list of items and a very large section dedicated to desserts. Some of the highlights include:

Seafood - jonah crab claws, seafood salad (introduce shrimp cocktail at lunch)
Carving station - thick bacon, various sausages, ham
Breakfast - scrambled eggs, hash browns, potatoes, waffles, pancakes, french toast, bagel bar
Fried - chicken, steak and eggs
Fresh juice - watermelon, orange, other
Mexican - chilaquiles, bfast burritos
Italian - pastas, pizza
Japanese - rolls, sushi
Omelette station - made to order omelettes
Chinese - dim sum (ie. bbq pork buns, pork shumai), fried rice, various chinese dishes
Dessert - crepes made to order (ie. nutella bananna), cakes, gelato flavors, candy bar 

The food overall was pretty solid outside of a couple stations, mainly the Chinese and Japanese stations. You're paying for the wide selection. If there were more precise ratings, I would rate it 3.5 stars.

Great buffet? Yes. Great for the price? Not so sure. Worth the wait? Nope. The food is good, but I wouldn't say they're "outstanding." (Well still good for the Buffet food.) They boil the crab in front of you, I loved about it, but when I visited this time (2nd time) the crab wasn't fresh at all, couldn't eat them. The pasta didn't taste the same so my second visit was a bit disappointing especially after I paid $25 extra per person for not waiting for 4 hours. ( I instead waited "only" for 25 min.)

Next time in Vegas? I will just go to nice chef's restaurants, they're pretty same price.

Tip: If you want to eat this for dinner, get the waiting list ticket around lunch time, then you'll get in for the dinner time (weekends-when it's busy).
If you're a group of 8 or more, they have a separate waiting line (a lot shorter time) so tell the host/hostess.

We had absolutely the worst dinning experience tonight at the Bacchanal Buffet. This restaurant is totally over-rated. Their raw food section was not fresh at all. We complained to the manager on call because one of our family members was throwing up right after the dinner. Instead of showing any empathy for what happened or simply offer our family member to sit down or have some warm water, he yelled at us and screamed that it has nothing to do with his food! And he does not care about what happened!

It's a shame that the Bacchanal Buffet does not treat their food nor their guests with dignity and respect. I would wholeheartedly recommend yelpers to avoid going there. It's not a honest place and certainly not a fine dinning place as it's marketed.

Ok, so this was my second time in Vegas and I decided to actually stay and eat on the strip this time. 

I kept seeing ads talking about the Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's palace so I decided to go and check it out with my friends. When I got there and saw the price my inner frugality started to kick in but I was able to convince myself that it was worth it. So, let me be the first to say, don't let the price intimidate you. I mean, you're in Vegas, if you didn't want to spend money you wouldn't be here.

The food and service was amazing! Definitely way above normal buffet levels. I personally spent my time eating from the area with the brisket, prime rib and other meats. They also had an incredible selection of desserts which was a pleasant surprise considering I'm very picky about my sweets.

Also let me give a shout out to Michael Lee for being an awesome manager and going out of his way to ensure that we were completely satisfied and imparting wisdom about the buffet onto me and my friends.

I will definitely be back!

This is not your average buffet, it's a buffet on steroids. They literally have everything you could have the taste for to eat and then some. I would definitely suggest you bring your appetite to get your money's worth. It is expensive but worth it if you can eat as much as you paid for. Servers do stop by and keep your table cleared off and bring you beverages, other than that you're on your own to go build your plate to your liking. Enjoy!

After reading all the rave reviews and constant hype for the Bacchanal buffet, I was willing to endure the 90 minute wait and turn a blind eye to the $54 adult, $27 kid price tag for dinner, but I have to say that it was VERY disappointing. Tomi in San Jose is much better and for half the price. For how much I was paying, I expected some lobster, caviar or escargot, but there were none of those things. They had oysters which were passable, but the crab legs were frozen (one piece I got was literally frozen, like sucking on a Popsicle), and the sushi was grocery store sushi quality.  The cooked crab legs and the cooked Chinese style crab was bland. The meat was better, the prime rib, lamb chops and Chinese BBQ pork were comparable to what you would get at most restaurants. All in all I would say that the American style food was their forte, but the seafood and Asian food was generally below average. If this buffet was only $20, I would say that it is probably worth it, but for the price , and having to endure the wait and the crowds, no way!

I'm rating this place in comparison to other top-notch buffets in Vegas. My friends and I went here because of it's the new #1 buffet in Vegas and it was kind of disappointing to be quite honest. For $50 per person, I was expecting to be blown away, but I feel that the Bellagio buffet, Wynn buffet and Wicked Spoon are all better buffets and better values as well.

Overall, I was very underwhelmed. I think the expectation and the price set the bar for this buffet high and unfortunately they did not deliver for me.

Came here for brunch and it was worth it. Talk about never ending food! This place is by far the LARGEST buffet I have ever been to. Maybe I shouldn't eat for 48 hours before hitting this place up. 
Breakfast was good! The Benedict's were delicious and man, that lobster Benedict is a MUST EAT. They have fresh squeezed juices and a ton of pastries to choose from. 
Their "Asian section" wasn't too impressive... The Pad Thai was very dry and the noodles were crunchy as hell. I took one bite and didn't finish the rest. The dim sum wasn't great either, pork bun was yummy though!

Minus one star for the seafood and dessert station. The seafood was limited to shellfish and crab legs. There was a variety of desserts. They were nicely presented but I wish they taste as good as they look. My favorite station would have to be the America. The prime rib and pork belly are to die for!!

The second star was for the service. Let's just say we didn't see our waitress until the bill needed to be paid. Busers waited until the table was packed with dirty dishes before cleaning up the table. We had to hunt down our waitress to refill our drinks.

Golden Corral on steroids and $60+ to boot. You people who write five star reviews for this place should be ashamed of yourselves. I foolishly trusted you. Never been to a Vegas buffet and thought I'd like to see what the fuss is about. My friend and I couldn't decide on what to eat so I floated the buffet idea. There's nothing here you won't find on your local Homestyle or Chinese buffet back home, just butt loads more of it. Save your money and hit the mall food court when you get home. The quality will be the same and you'll have $40 left in your pocket.

We were very excited to splurge on a buffet for our last morning in town. We decided to go in the morning about 10 on a Thursday and I'm wondering if this was the issue? The place was sort of slow, no line, some empty tables so maybe the turn over for food wasn't so high. So many things such as the pancakes, French toast and cute waffle/fried chicken baskets etc were crispy and dried out from sitting under the warmer lights too long. The prime rib was the worst I've had! I don't get to eat it too often and it was SO dry and tasteless. Maybe just the end where mine was served? The sushi looked a little sad as well as the salads( fruit and veggie), both were lacking color and looked as if prepared the previous day. Positives: good service, juices, gelato, Creme brûlée was fantastic. We were pretty disappointed as we had saved up our appetites and spent good money to go. Will stick with the Wynn buffet or try wicked spoon next time.

I was very much looking forward to this buffet, but unfortunately it fell short. The variety is there, but the quality is not. I don't think the overall layout of the stations are positioned to their best advantage. It almost feels more like a cafeteria/canteen rather than what should be an upscale sumptuous decadent overflowing buffet.

I almost gave it a 5 because it is an amazing buffet, but if I'm going to pay $50 for a buffet it ought to be pretty awesome. I liked a lot of the smaller dishes like lentils with pork bell yams the oriental chicken wings. But I didn't care do much for the bigger things like the Prime Rib and the crab legs were snow crab not king crab. I liked the buffet at the Bellagio better.

I came here with 3 coworkers on a Saturday around 11am after a long night of drinking. There was no wait at all when we got there but the line was pretty long when we left around 1pm. Everything there was amazing and definitely worth $50/person. Everyone in our group enjoyed every bite of our food especially the desserts.

To get your money worth you should definitely get the king crab legs and stone crab claws. You can either have it cold or have them warm it back up in the boiling water. I loved the stone crab.

You must also get some prime ribs! There are also dim sum and sushi if you walk further down.

I suggest that you try a little of everything since they are all amazing! You must save some space for dessert. You will not regret it!

If I could give this buffet 0 I would. I don't understand why this place is getting good reviews. Other than the meat carving area everything was bland and tasteless. We had one night we decided to splurge on food and we decided to come here. We spent $120 on dinner for two. I just now left hungry and dissatisfied. If you like burgers that are cold and tasteless food and burnt pasta this is a good choice for you. The sweet station did look good but I never made it that far. I was too upset I lost $120 on a beefed up old country buffet.

I truly love this place there are so many options to get and the quality is amazing..BUT I actually found a piece of metal in my shrimp scampi. Luckily it wasn't in my mouth but I happened to notice it in my sauce and felt super disgusted after.
Best buffet in Vegas compared to wicked spoon and the one at wynn for me

The wait was like forever for most people on Christmas. I skipped the line for being a total rewards diamond member :)

The overall food quality is decent but the lobster was such a disappoinment.

There was a long line for lobster. My wife is a seafood lover so we waited for 15 mins to get the lobster. 

It was $80 for the Christmas Feast. Pretty pricey for buffet.

I think it's worth to try it at least once just for experiencing high end buffet. 

Will I go there for a 2nd time? Probably not especially if I lose my total rewards status.

This is the most amazing buffet I've ever been to. They have something for everyone from fish to meat to italian, mexican, sushi and dim sum ... My husband and I spent two hours here tasting everything! Our server was so wonderful and attentive he offered us coffee when we were eating our dessert. Everything tasted fresh and it was gourmet, there mashed potatoes weren't boxed they're dessert selection was phenomenal. You could eat all the cookies, cakes, and gelato your heart desired. I can't wait to come back to Vegas just so we can eat at the bacchanal buffet again!!!
This Buffett is expensive but totally worth the $$$. Great food and service. Would definitely come back to this restaurant.

Wonderful buffet with all different kind of foods.  A must do but you will be waiting for 2 hrs to eat and wait in line but it is worth it.  Love the pasta and seafood and the dessert is to die for.  Best buffet in vegas

WOW!  I've read some of the other reviews, and I fear my writing skills just can't compete with the other descriptions!  In short, this is the best buffet in Vegas.  Loved the food, ate as much as I could (and then more).  Many thanks to Dragica for sitting us at a great table with a great server, Alvaro Gomez.  Alvaro explained the buffet stations, gave us recommendations, and encouraged us to enjoy ourselves.  He went a long way in making an overwhelming selection seem more manageable.  The staff seem proud of their new buffet, and that, combined with great food, makes for a fun experience.  We'll be returning to the Bacchanal.

This buffet has saved me from never going to another buffet. I hate buffets but this one is awesome we went for lunch and it was 10 times better than any other hotel. Thank you Caesars. A 4 is like a 5 for buffets.

I had high expectations for this place since it was voted "Number 1 Buffet" by USA today and carried with it a pretty hefty price tag of 58 dollars per person for Weekend Brunch. We were staying at Caesar's and this made it the most convenient location.

Wait: when the queue is "beyond capacity", they have a check in system where you put in your name and mobile number and they'll give you a time for when you report back. Interestingly the time I was supposed to report back was different from the time I got my text, which was silly because there was plenty of room in the "queue" and the lady wouldn't let anyone in until you'd received the text. Wait time was around an hour at noon.

Food:
Overall pretty underwhelming so I'll just have to group it up. Worst of all was how there was little a long line blocking nearly 3/4 of all the food options at the buffet , sparing the pizza and italian food and asian food areas. It wasn't clear what everyone was waiting for but most people would assume that the line was the line you needed to get in to get ANY food, since it extended from the front of the restaurant where the crab legs and shrimp were, spanning the meat carving stations, the street taco stand, and everything else its way. You'd have to interrupt people in line and look like you're cutting just to grab some fried chicken.

Asian food - asian food offerings here were awful. Sushi was cold, tasted like supermarket sushi. Sweet and sour chicken was dry, stale. 
Meat - the prime rib here looks good visually but it is flavorless with no beefy flavor and juices that taste like nothing. Drench it in jus or bbq sauce as that's the only way to make it edible. Rotisserie chicken wasn't bad though! Bbq beef brisket was probably my favorite after drenching it with sauce.
Street tacos - didn't try this as I didn't feel like filling up $1 street tacos that are ubiquitous in LA
Seafood - salty snow crab legs, but at least they were thawed. Shrimp were large and tasted great dipped in cocktail sauce. Dungeness crab legs were cold and lost most of the briny juices, nothing special.

Price:
One of the priciest buffets at 58 dollars per person for weekend brunch. My tip would be to get the 2 person Groupon deal for 88 dollars which includes free mimosas and a VIP pass that lets you cut in line. Only drawback is that you have to be there before 9 AM I believe.

Service:
Nice waitress and they do a good job of clearing empty/used plates but it was hard to flag down someone to get water refills.

Overall: Food here looks better than it tastes, it is pricey, and you'll wait in long lines before eating, and wait in even longer lines waiting for food. There's a 2 hour limit, but expect to spend 30-45 minutes of that time waiting in line to grab anything to eat.

I'll preface our fave Vegas buffet is Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo. 

This was ok. The process to get in is unorganized. You go to a kiosk to get a ticket w a return time and to put your cell phone number in to be told to return sooner if possible - we followed the estimated time on the ticket of 2 hours not realizing we should've stayed at Caesars BC we missed a text 40 minutes after we left, oh well. Once you do return, you get into a new line to wait to pay to wait to sit down to eat - about another 45 min. This line had no one coordinating it w people cutting from different sides BC the registers are in a squared off area. We did not pay until 9:20, the buffet closes at 10:00. I asked a waiter if it was worth it to stay or if we should come back and he said they would continue to be putting out fresh food until 10:15 that night so we'd be fine. 
Once we got seated and go look around it felt like the food stations went on forever. And I don't mean that as a good thing. It didn't seem like there were more options than other buffets just the same amount spread 
out in a very long zigzagging line. 
The food was kind of disappointing. Everything at the carving station was dry even though it looked good (prime rib disintegrated in my mouth, lamb was gamier than I've ever had and I never turn down lamb). The oysters were dirty, crab legs v watery. There's a soup station w "clam chowder". Do not waste your time, it was water w some cream and clams dunked in- it should not be called a chowder! The Peking duck was v good but we can get a whole Peking duck delivered to our house and it won't cost $120. My husband thought the dim sum was done v well but we're not going to return just for that. The only thing we both really enjoyed was the dessert station. If you go I'd esp recommend the crepes, creme brûlée, mini apple pie, and chocolate cake pops. 
Oh, And tip your servers, they're stuck being there all night, ours was v nice considering how hectic it must be working there.

Best buffet in Vegas!!!! the only downside is the long wait, but it is definitely worth the wait! Every time I go to Vegas I have to eat here at least once. The best time to line up is around 1pm because you pay brunch price $49.99 (weekends) and you get brunch and dinner food since they change the food at around 2:45pm. So you get the benefit of paying the cheaper price but having  dinner food too, if you want! Regardless, even though bacchanal costs more than other buffets I believe it is way better!

I returned to the Baccanal Buffet with my daughter and son. The second time for my son and the first time for my daughter. She was blown away with the decir--the way it was set up -- and the choices of the food that was being offered, Both daughter and son remarked that from the time you enter, till the time you you are not pressured to hurry up-eat and leave. Both said that everything was very tasty and that upon returning for a future visit, that this would be the place, that they would most want to come back to eat.

Been a good lover all my life!  Been to countless buffets but by far this one is the best I've ever had.  The Pho was top notch-even way better than the authentic vietnamese restaurants with in Chinatown.  Menudo was on point, best clam chowder I've ever had.  The crab was succulent and sweet as oppose to other places where it was just salty.  Prime rib was moist and juicy.... I could go on and on.  Nothing was disappointing!

What a nice spread for Thanksgiving. We only waited 15 minutes for a party of 6 to be seated. This is the second buffet we've tried since we got to Vegas this trip and it hands down is equally as good as the buffet we had last night. We've done Carnival buffet, the hellacious. Aria and a few others but hands down this buffet is light years better in every way except for the long line to get crab legs. 

If you can afford it, this is a nice buffet for a special occasion.

I am honestly giving this Buffet a 1 star just because the customer service.It was amazing every staff member working there with a great attitude.Which I honestly give them props cause its soo crazy bussy! Non stop .As far as the food not impressed at all. I was expecting great quality food since the Dinner price was $54.99 per adult.They dont have a big selection at all. And to top it off the whole experience is just waiting from the time you sign in to the time you pay, to the time you wait to be seated.Great were Inside the buffet starving after all that waiting well suprise!!! There is still long wait time at the popular selections Seafood,meat section. Like a previous person wrote its honestly just something to cross off your bucket list. Food is not good at all,Honestly dont know how it is the "Best" buffet.My favorite is still the Rio Buffet.
Best buffet in Las Vegas- hands down! A bit pricey but the service and quality-quantity were top notch!!

SOOOOO OVER-RATED!!!! It's $50 per person but it is NOT worth 1/4 of the price charged!! Cold food, dry food, and even spoiled food. I had a shrimp dumpling, and the shrimp inside was sour (sour as in spoiled) when I bit into it!!! So very disappointed. Won't return here again!!!!

Given the wide selection, some dishes are hit or miss. Overall good selection of food and desserts. 

Go with dishes where ingredients are the key players: prime rib, steamed crabs, pork belly, salad. A lot of the cooked dishes like pizza, paella, etc. are subpar - probably the cost of batch preparation.

Save room for dessert. And go hungry.

Where do I begin? I was thoroughly impressed by the buffet at Caesars Palace. I liked the early check process to get into the buffet because it can easily be a 1-2 hr wait to get in. After checking in, it may have taken 35 minutes waiting in line which is totally do-able for a Vegas buffet of this magnitude. The restaurant is beautiful and we'll organized. The food was plentiful, fresh, and gourmet. They had something for every taste. Paella! I repeat PAELLA in a buffet? Not the poor man paella either. This was full of muscles, clams, calamari, shrimp, sausage,chicken and scallops. I am amazed. Better than MGM, Bellagio, and Aria buffets which some may consider top tier. $50 a person seemed like much until I seen the spread. I may have ate about $200 worth of food. Well worth the "investment"

If you don't eat something delicious at this place, you only have yourself to blame. There are so many options and, from what I can tell, they are all good choices. The buffet is sectioned off by type of food; from Asian cuisine to dessert bar (mmmmmm), there is always something to try and like. All of the food is portioned to be small so you can try a maximum amount of foods!!!!!!

Great food. 
An all around fun experience.
It is expensive. Although, my friends and I went to an different buffet and paid extra for the seafood upgrade. After all was eaten and done...I decided that I would rather pay extra for the Bacchanal Buffet, as I think it is worth the extra dough.

Hey there  fellow yelpers! If you wish to have a great chow for buffet don't settle for cheap ! Make it your all hands down experience on your chow down challenge and go all out! Nom nom. Def one of my favs!

This was my first Las Vegas buffet and I left only semi-impressed.  We went on a Saturday night an hour before closing, so expecting great quality that late was probably our fault.  My group of 4 went heavy on the crab legs and tacos and tried a bunch of other things.  The tacos were the standout in my opinion, especially the Pork Al Pastor ones.  I must have eaten at least 6.  It was cool they had all the different pepper sauces to accompany the tacos.  The crab legs were fine, although melted butter was nowhere to be found.  The rest of the food was mediocre.  It's nice to have 500 items but I'd rather they have 100 items and do them all well.

This buffet is the new IT buffet; sorry Wicked Spoon, your time is up.  For me, the way I judge a buffet is how far I've gotten along the counter before my plate is full, and let me tell you, my plate was full well before I made it out of the first room (yeah, that's how much of a selection there is---it spans a few large physical areas...)

VARIETY. 
-------If you've ever been to Rio Carnivale buffet, you know what a WIDE variety is like.  They have every major food type, along with a few "whoa, never thought I'd see this at a buffet"-things. (fancy a cheese plate and crackers, much?)

PRESENTATION. 
-------One of the things I appreciate most about people who create food is their ability to present it in a way that is just SO darn cute that I want to gobble it right up! And that is certainly an ability of the Bacchanal staff.  Everything from the sliders to the sushi hand rolls to the corn beef hash was picture perfect! 

CREPES. 
--------Is there anything better than nutella, fruit, and whipped cream atop a freshly made crepe? I can't think of any at the moment. I could have eaten these all day long. Now, if we had come for dinner and those macarons had been available... I can't say there wouldn't be some major competition!! Next time I will definitely have to come for dinner!

I had just come from 2.5hours of professional networking when we decided to come to Bacchanal and let me tell you, it was definitely a treat to end the day well.  Just be prepared for an extremely long line, as with all new and popular buffets, but hey, just think: the hungrier you are, the more of it you can fit inside your tummy! :) 

Bon apetit?

I thought this was an excellent buffet. I liked it way better than any other buffet I've gone to on the Strip. We went at 4pm on a Saturday to beat the crowd so we were seated pretty quickly. The variety is amazing! Their Chinese food is actually pretty decent, and their choice of cuts of meat (LAMB!!) was great. Their desserts were good as well; the only detracting thing is the price. $50 for a buffet is nuts.

My family and I (group of 8) tried the new buffet on a Saturday night.  It is good my uncle has platinum status as the regular line was really long.  We even waited about 20 minutes in the platinum line. Also, because we had a large group, we had to split the group into two tables so I did not see half my family during the whole dinner. I would say overall the food is really good here.  As with any typically buffet, they had food from all different countries, styles, etc.  Everyone I had was good.  My main issue with the place is all of their action stations.  They seem to not have enough staff to cover the amount of people that want food from the action stations.  There were really long lines and it blocked others from getting the food that was already prepared.  I missed many stations because the lines were blocking the way.  They have to either hirer more staff to move the lines along faster or they need to somehow arrange the lines so they are not blocking other people.  I would probably try the buffet again but definitely not for dinner on a Saturday night.

I've only tried a few of the Vegas buffet but this is by far my favorite.  They have such a great selection and a lot of seating to accommodate a huge crowd of hungry tourists. 

If your at the Caesars Palace then check this out.  Sooooo. Good
Be prepared to wait....the line was sooooooo long that after an extended amount of time we had to leave...I do want to come back when we are not in any schedule

You shouldn't trust stupid kiosk. I went to this buffet at 4pm and kiosk told me come back at 6:30. Then I came back to buffet at 6:30. There was a looooong line. I was forced to be on the end of line. I waited around 1 hour but it seems still need to wait more than 2 hours. Finally I gave up. They don't have a capability to manage the busy hour which small restaurant can do. My suggestion to you who is seeing this comment. Do not go this buffet during busy hours or season.

Bacchanal Buffet is located inside Caesar's Palace. Price is $52.99 per adult for dinner. They have more than 500 different dishes prepared on a daily basis from more than 800 recipes,  International dishes abound with American, Italian, Mexican, Chinese, and Japanese cuisine as well as expansive Seafood section including pizza, Deli, and an outstanding Dessert Station.  A unique feature is that each station has plated, made-to-order and mini-dishes. 

Combining nine distinct restaurants in one modern setting inspired by glass, wood and steel elements, the buffet is huge in size and flavors. The ambiance is an upscale setting, a massive 25,000 sq foot dining space.

We went for Brunch Buffet. Priced $49.99 per adult. I tried fresh juices, muffin, macaroon, gelato, cucumber, pizzas, and salmon, They also have omelette, sausages, croissant, and many more.

The service was good.
Best buffet ever, just super expensive. Love the variety especially the different cuts of meat.

Hands down my favorite restaurant ever! Yes I'm a Las Vegas local and yes I'm sick and tired of buffets by now BUT bacchanal is the greatest! Most times there's a long line but it's worth the wait. I know that when I come here I get top quality food. This review is more on the people that make this experience special. My husband and I came here one unassuming Tuesday because we wanted one last hurrah before he had neck surgery because he wouldn't be able to eat solid food for a few weeks. When we got in line we let the cashier Kumudu know that's he's a disabled veteran and he got a line pass saving us from an almost 2 hour wait which wouldn't be good for his back. When we got seated Lupe our server got our drinks in a very prompt and pleasant manner. Francisco our busser was also phenomenal like the two ladies mentioned before him. This type of service makes us enjoy coming to bacchanal. I highly recommend this place and come prepared with an empty tummy because the food will definitely fill you up and the staff is truly great from the back of the house to the front of the house. Fantastic food and service across the board!

Been to this buffet twice as well as many other Vegas buffets including Wynn Buffet, Spice Market, Wicked Spoon, etc... Let me tell you. Bacchanal is the BEST buffet in Vegas hands down.
