The first time I went literally changed my understanding of buffets. When I went a second time, it managed to change my understanding again. The food is amazing. The selection is amazing. You will have a dining experience that you will remember.

Is this worth the $50-$60 price tag? To me, yes. But what does it all matter? You are in Vegas. Unless Vegas is a monthly trip for you, it does not make sense to count pennies and dollars. Pay the extra $10 or so and enjoy a truly premium experience.

The 3 stars are due to the ridiculously long a.... Lines!! Omg seriously the wait is not worth it.   The food is comparable to the buffet at the Bellagio and the wait is not so long.   First you have to log on a computer and the computer tells you to come back at a specific time.  Then you wait in another line to pay.  Then you we wait in another line to Pay! 2 hours.   Yes. 2 hours.   

The process has got to be better.  Not to mention 4 bathroom stalls for the size of the Restaurant.  
We tried to get our $$ worth at the seafood area.... Lots of crab legs.  After 3 the raw oysters come out.  Didn't get a chance to try them and for a 2 hour wait.  I will go somewhere else!  

We did try the pastry counter across the way while we waited.  That was delicious    we will go there again!

Recently visited this buffet. I went late around 9 pm...no line so i know i lucked out wait wise. The food was endless and variety was pretty extensive. I personally enjoyed the pasta station and the asian section especially the sushi, although i wish the sushi variety was more expanded. . Amazing. The seafood was pretty good. The carving station looked amazing with many meats to choose from and the spanish station had a great variety. If you are a clam chowder fan be sure to grab a bowl. I will say the staff behind the bar was very laid back and standing around in groups talking more than being attentive and helpful. Im sure it was due to the fact it was towards the end of the night and they were just excited to almost be off work. Understandable...I've been there. The buffet bar itself is long. Very long how far it stretched with the turns and continued travels to find the end. All in all i was impressed but wish the price would drop from 50s to mid 30s to 40s. Next time im staying at Caesars i will definitely go again and try ecerything my stomach didn't have room for this time.

I think it deserves the designation of best buffet in Las Vegas ( although I haven't been to all them) it's large, food is good and for those who think it's expensive its VEGAS!  We had a salad and appetizer on the strip for the same price. 
Go during lunch if you want a better deal .

There was a 1 1/2 hour wait for the Sunday Champagne brunch which was a little ridiculous, but the check-in kiosk/ text notification made it a tad more bearable. There was someone taking professional pictures of guests in line which I'm guessing you could purchase later as a keychain or coffee mug to remember the experience... We probably waited another 20 minutes after our reservation was called before we actually sat down. The overall selection was decent and the crab Benedict was amazing! I had hoped there would be more breakfast options personally. The bottomless mimosas/ champagne was good but I wish it could have been an optional add on since my husband doesn't drink. It was ~$95 for the two of us which was pretty steep for brunch, but I wanted to check it out since they remodeled. The layout is great and the decor is very minimalist & modern. The food isn't any more special than before. I might go back for dinner if there's no wait and we did good at the tables :-)

Amazing! Must try. The food was fresh, and there were so many choices!!! It was fairly priced (considering how much I ate) and definitely better than any buffet in Vegas. From crab legs, sushi, prime rib, Mexican, crepes and dessert, you could have rolled me out! So delish!

Honestly you can save your money ($60.00) for the dinner buffet, and go to a buffet under $30 and get the same food choices, and the same food quality, with a better experience than coming here.   This buffet is definitely over priced, and over rated.

The good- variety. There is a lot to choose from. The bad (very bad) ALL the carved meats were dry. And bland... you don't pay $40-60 for a plate for pizza and tacos.... I'm very disappointed relative to the cost. I e had better $20 buffets...  Wicked Spoon is much better.
Besides the seafood selection, the others are aiiiiiiiiite. The oyster shooters were realllllyy good though! Macaroons weren't that great.

Whats the best part of vegas other than the perks of being a girl, free everything and pay for nothing? Vegas buffet of course! Lol


I had my experience of this buffet back in june when a group of us went to vegas for a friends birthday. It was a saturday and the line was pretty long, but i also remember it going by pretty fast. I forgot how much it was per person, but what i do remember is however much it was, it was worth every penny!


As you walk in youre greeted with so many sections of food you just dont know where to start. I actually walked around the whole thing just to see where i would like to start first. Since i was hungover i was so excited to see they have a section where they serve little mini bowls of pho and ramen. So cute too! I then made my way to the meat section where i got a couple of slices of their amazing thick cut bacon. I honestly forgot what else i got, but i do remember getting atleast 4 plates. The desserts are so cute and delicious! I was pretty sad at the end the fact i was going to head to a pool party and my belly was beyond big from all the yummy food. My fav vegas buffet so far!

This place has a wide selection of Asian, Italian, seafood, and comfort food. I ate everything from crispy Beijing duck to fall off bone pork ribs. Even with the large selection of food, the quality of each item was superb. They have all you can eat macarons for dessert.

Totally threw the diet out of the window to indulge here and it was worth it! Visited for lunch and got a booth near the windows. Having been to the old Caesars buffet a few times I have to say this buffet finally feels "Caesars". The decor is beautiful and I love the windows - so refreshing after being in the dark casino! There is a HUGE variety of food here. You could take ten trips to the food line and still not try one of every item. Trust me, I tried as many of the items as I could! I loved the Italian station, could have had a whole bowl of the basil pesto pasta and been satisfied. The desserts were phenomenal - flan, white chocolate passion dome, Nutella crepes, panna cotta, cheesecake, creme brulee, gelato.... So good! Definitely worth the trip. Plan on spending some time here to really indulge!

Been here twice, both good experiences. 

As a tourist, it's a definite must on your Vegas to-do list. But beware bc it's super popular. My family and I couldn't even get a ticket on our first attempt because the kiosks where you have to enter your name/info as a reservation wasn't even taking reservations bc they were at capacity for the next four or five hours! for our second attempt, we waited about 3 hours before being seated. 

If you're unfamiliar with how it works, you have to physically walk in and make a reservation on their kiosk. Then the ticket that pops out tells you when to arrive to physically wait in line (usually anywhere from 1-3 hours. So you're free to wander the casino until the scheduled time stated on your ticket). Once the designated time arrives, you have to wait in line for maybe another hour. Then you advance slowly like at a line at an amusement park, then there's the final line where you wait for a host to seat you. So there's like three tiers of waiting... 

Anyways, food is amazing. High quality ingredients, cooked well, and the service is friendly too (though somewhat frazzled. The waitstaff is sometimes hard to catch, but the servers serving the food are friendly & polite). Also, great desserts! I had the thai tea with boba & ice cream, sooooo good! 

One of my favorites is the cheese selection. :) the Chinese food is good too (recommend the non steamed dishes, like their oxtail is delicious. Don't get the steamed stuff, like soup dumplings, because steamed soup dumplings are meant to be eaten immediately, and these have been sitting out for ten min or more, and so they get dried out with a tough skin), but since I eat awesome Chinese food on a regular basis, I skip that. I love their meatballs, and their Mexican street tacos. The meat, sausage section is delicious, and my slab of bacon was indeed a slab of bacon. Feel free to ask for a half, or a third, of a sausage link as they are very filling. My second time I went for brunch and they had lobster eggs benedict. I'm an eggs benedict junkie, so that was awesome. 

Some downsides, in addition to the wait, is that people/patrons are so rushed. I don't like the weird frenetic pace or mindset people have when eating there. Also, the toilets are gross because people "unload" (ie puke) there to eat more.... Ugh. So if you don't want to lose your appetite, avoid the bathroom right outside the buffet. 

Anyways, if you're a local, you're probably not even reading yelp reviews on Bacchanal because once (or twice) is probably enough. If you're a tourist, it's worth the wait & expense.

Wow... This is really the best buffet on the strip. The top 3 buffets are: 
1. Caesars palace buffet 
2. Wicked Spoon buffet at Cosmopolitan
3. Bellagio buffet

Dessert options are amazing!!
Love the juice bar juices!!
The variety of food is great!! 
Beautiful, modern buffet!!

OVERRATED! Definitely not worth $60, would be willing to try brunch though. Nothing was bad, it just wasn't worth the amount of money to be honest. Meats were VERY tender and bomb !!! If you're a person of flavor like myself your going to have a problem. I just feel like I could've had this at another buffet (besides the tender meat lol) for more then half the price. Great service, GREAT selection of foods, just not what I expected after reading the hyped reviews

Spend the little extra money and have an epic Vegas buffet experience, its worth it. They have everything you can imagine and more. At the carving station we tried lamb, duck, turkey, sausage, they also have prime rib, etc.! Of course have the crab legs, they also have oysters,  calamari, fish and chips, Chilean Sea Bass, seaweed salad, sushi, chinese food, dumplings, noodles. There is also a cheese buffet and charcuterie station, all different breads, pastas, potatoes, there is a pizza station and phenomenal desserts! The wait staff is prompt and courteous and will bring you drinks, coffee and tea. They also provide warm towels and plate holders for hot plates.  We thought it was funny at first there is a 2 hour limit, but then we realized we were there for an hour and a half! Extra perks include wine, beer and there is also caviar for two! The deserts were so delish there is a crepe station and they have a gelato bar. You cannot go wrong.

Definitely the best buffet i've been to in Vegas.
Spent two hours in this buffet and didn't even realize we've been there for that long.
Definitely on the expensive side, but the wife and i both agree this buffet was worth it.
The best buffet I've ever had...it's $57 pp but you definitely get your monies worth.  They have a little bit of everything from seafood to Mexican to Asian to steaks!  Must try

This place is certainly not all that. But the bus boys and servers are very nice. Francisco was our server and he works very hard and is very polite and checks up on you all the time. His bus boy was an Asian guy....clearing the tables. This was on 2/16/18. They both work very hard and as a team.
But as for the food...the crab is what everyone comes for but the messed up part is the crab on display is the COLD CRAB. It was super salty!! Like gross salty! Like what the heck?!?
Now The crab was presliced. But being served cold was wack.
We didn't even know they served hot crab because they hide it! They literally hide it in the back near the Italian section, and you won't even know unless you ask, because you can't help yourself to it. You have to give your plate to the cook and he will pile the HOT crabs on your plate. BUT THESE CRABS ARE NOT PRE SLICED. Now tell me. Why would they slice the COLD CRAB, which no one likes, and not slice the HOT crabs? 
So finally after finding the hidden hot crabs...you go to the table and get messy cracking them, all to find out they are SALTY AS HECK!! It's as if they pour pounds of salt in the pot and boil the crabs. 
So yea. Even the fish in the Chinese section was over salted. Like ridiculously salty!
But yea...
There are some other foods that are Tastey indeed. But for $70...nah. I personally would not go back. 
Plus they limit you. You have 2 hours limit. So it's not a true all you can eat buffet. It's just all you can eat in 2 hours.

I LOVE the Bacchanal. I have been here three times total, twice for dinner (including opening day) and more recently for lunch.  First off I would say spend the extra money and go for dinner. It is well worth it. I was looking forward to the split king crab legs but alas they are not offered for lunch. Also, not offered for lunch is the made to order souffles in the dessert area or the hand rolls in the sushi area. Other than that relatively similar lunch and dinner items are served. 

The highlights to me are the meat carving station, the prime rib is exceptionally good for being at a buffet. The charcuterie area where there are house made salamis and other cured meats to tickle your fancy. The dim sum area - where they offer a decent variety of dim sum and Peking duck. The sea food area, where I indulge on oyster shooters, crab (at dinner), and more oysters. I also enjoyed the fresh squeezed juices, I do not think this was offered at dinner, the selection included Pineapple, Jicama, and Melon. And of course let's not forget the dessert section - where without my much awaited souffles I was forced to eat key lime tarts, Oreo mousse domes and sour cherry and balsamic gelato. 

So yes, I LOVE the Bacchanal. Despite my lunch let down. And this says a lot from me because in general I dislike buffets, in fact there are no other buffets I actually like in town (not including Indian lunch buffets). There are ones I will go to for the price and just have salad bar but for me to say that a buffet is great it takes a lot. I will be back and back again I am sure.

Came to this buffet highly recommended by multiple people. Man...was I disappointed. While the food was decent, 3 out of the 4 people in my group (including myself) came down with food poisoning within a day...all of us with nausea, vomiting and diarrhea for 24 hours.  I'm in the medical field, so I know the timing of food poisoning.  It ruined the rest of the trip for the entire group and we were all miserable.  Sadly, I cannot recommend this place to anybody. And yes, I do understand there are warning signs posted and we all eat there at our own risk. My group and I took this risk, but it did not turn out well for us.

Went to this place for dinner. Oh my god! This buffet is the best one I've been to in Vegas so far. Their lamb is definitely better than Bellagio's. Also got a HUGE plate of warm crab legs. Mmmm! Delicious, especially with their unique melted butter. Oysters were good too. Love their mac and cheese. Their Asian food section (dumplings) were good too! 

This place definitely deserves it's name. I'll definitely come back here! Definitely try it out if you've never been!

I was very disappointed. I was told that this was the number one buffet in Vegas. After waiting hours in line, which caused me to have a massive headache, I was greeted with food that was cold and over seasoned. For how much you pay you would expect the quality to be flawless no matter what.

Overall, the buffet was good. The price is a little steep for the quality of food there though. The service to refill drinks and remove plates was extremely slow. My boyfriend really got his money's worth but since I'm trying to transition to a full vegetarian diet, it wasn't as appetizing for me. Some plates were fantastic (Asian cuisine) and some were not so great (Mexican). My boyfriend really enjoyed the meat carving station and everyone seemed to like the seafood selection even though I'm not a fan. My favorite part was the dessert station which was fantastic. Everything was worth trying there.
Awesome buffet. Went for dinner time got some awesome lamb. There was a lot of different food and cultures. I really liked this place.

Expected so much, but slightly disappointed

They need a better system to seat people -- when we went in, there were so many empty tables, so why did we have to wait so long in line?

As a seafood aficionado, I went straight for the fish ---- overcooked and tasteless! So I settled for the scrawny crab legs. Enjoyed the oyster shooter and ceviche but not enough to want another round. Saw a display of lobster, but none were actually served unless they cooked them in the bisque. At least the shrimp were plump and succulent, otherwise their seafood station would have been a total let down.

Prime rib -- although I like medium rare, this was too rare for my taste so they had to sear a piece for me. 

Chicken in a basket of sweet potato fries was a special treat. Super crunchy chicken. Fries had a sweet glaze that made it taste like dessert. Loved it.

Ribs --- very dry. Definitely not the finger-licking kind. 

Vegetables and salads. Nothing spectacular. The Caesar salad was drowning in dressing which tasted like something you'd buy in a bottle from the local grocery store.

Tried several desserts --- not impressed.  At least the flan and tiramisu tasted good.  Glad they were not overly sweet.

Altogether, decent but hardly the best. I have a fondness for other buffets in Las Vegas. Maybe next time, we should just pick a fine dining place (like Michael Mina or Gordon Ramsey's). Buffets seem to be filling stations for gourmands, not gourmets

This is the most popular buffet in Vegas. The wait was about 45 minutes on Saturday when we arrived at 6. Once we were seated the atmosphere was great, beautiful decor. There are over 500+ dishes available so you have lots of choices. The first few plates of sea food were amazing! Had shrimp, oysters, crabs. They cut the crab shells in half or have slits in them so you won't need a cracker. It was pretty cool, first time I've seen that. I also had lamb and ribs which were good as well. There was also a taco station, dessert bar, and Asian selection. The only reason it is now 5 stars is the price. At 75$ a person it is very pricey but I feel like the value is not there. For that price I would want everything to be amazing. All the food was good but not great. I guess that happens when you have so many dishes and don't specialize in one type of cuisine. Anyways, it was a great experience! Would recommend to everyone!

AMAZINGGGG!!!! You have to go here if you are looking for a buffet in Vegas. My group went here for lunch (less than $45) and you can sit here and eat all you want for two hours, which is more than enough, believe me. I personally love seafood and really enjoyed the fresh shrimp and crab options they had there. There were also oysters, which came out at the end of our meal. Besides that, there are seafood dishes like lobster benedict and lobster bisque. 

And besides that... wow...  you can get all types of juices (if you like green juices, the cucumber one is great), Mexican cuisine, Chinese cuisine, Italian cuisine... you can get it all. The pork belly was great! The shrimp orzo was also one of my faves along with the truffle gnocchi. 

Then dessert... just go here!

Yes I agree with all other reviews in here cuz the food is amazing, fresh, hot and super yummy . You have to wait in line for minimum hour or more but it's with every penny that you spend. They have hundreds of different choices of food and sushi and almost all the food around the world. Love it
Amazing crab legs! That's what I came here for and that's only thing I ate until I felt almost sick LOL! Buffet is great, pricy yes.

I thought on this shit place is it was not worth the price and wait for a buffet that is so simple and doesn't even have king crab but only some nasty ass crab claws. Some of the food wasn't bad and the juices they had out where great and that's the only reason it's not a one star but it doesn't make up for how there wasn't any thing that makes it worth the price tag. I recommend people to go to a different place like the Bellagio buffet which has so much variety for all.

Come early! or wait in the ridiculous line. or pay the $15 extra bucks!

I came here 2 times...both times it was around 10 am and the line wasn't packed 30 minutes later people started to line up like a mad house...who knew 30 minutes would make a difference? it's like traffic on the 405 (except that it's 5 minutes instead of 30 lol)...the first time I went, I was amazed by all the food that they had!

They have the usual breakfast stuff, the Asian (Chinese & Japanese station), Mexican, American, Italian, Seafood, and you can't forget dessert!

I tend to go to the "freshly made" concoctions which are the noodles where you can get Ramen, Pho, or Chinese Noodle type that's clear broth. Tacos are the bomb! Omelettes and such and the Crepe for dessert!

As of today, I would say it is the best buffet in Vegas, but you know the second time I went it was a bit lacking but still the best compared to everywhere else..I went the weekend before Christmas. It was quiet but for some reason this place is always packed. For reason with all these people some foods you actually had to wait. The best thing about this place is that they actually have fresh squeez juices in that cute containers...i think they're like apple cranberry, mango, pineapple, and/or green melon (honeydew)...well, the colors at least i usually tend to get the honeydew one lol...but these go out so quick that some times it's not replaced quickly. plus, due to all these people its not as clean cuz people tnd to drop stuff etc on the counters.

But don't let that discourage you to try this place out. The food is pretty good compared to other buffets and have a lot of choices. but damn buffets this days espcially for vegas and especially for brunch (champaigne included) can run up your bill...say bye bye to your winnings! - if you won in Vegas ;) or say goodbye to your money and say hello to your big belly! lol
Terrible hostess and management! They don't know their own line groupings. Foods just okay, it's just like any other buffet!

I like that you can pay extra to get the express pass. It was very well worth especially for the Thanksgiving night. I think this is the best buffet in LV. (I haven't had a chance to try Sterling Brunch)
Well worth the wait. Go an hour before you want to eat, get a ticket slip, and hang out in the casino. I couldn't move after this meal and I will never regret that moment.

Best buffet in town. Selection is the largest and ALL of the food is fabulous. I had a piece of price rib that would have been $50 alone in any restaurant.  Service was great. We are planning on returning every time we are in Vegas.

Came on my birthday! In June...
I absolutely loved this place. I tried a bunch of weirdo things I don't normally eat...seafood related, and the dessert island was incredible. My favorite things there was sushi, meat and cheese plates, macarons, and big ass chocolate dipped strawberries.
My new fav buffet in Vegas great selection of sea food! Crab legs and sushi are fresh and delicious.

We came around 10 am, and there is a two hour limit to how long you can stay, so we came at a good time for both breakfast and lunch.

Although pricey, $40 on the weekdays, you are paying for the variety.  Their Asian cuisine is surprisingly good, we went back for seconds at their noodle bar, specifically the pho.

Their high prices items, seafood and meats were good.  Although the dugeonous crabs were not fresh at all, but the king crab was good.  Their large variety of meats is hot and have someone on staff to cut it for you.

The desserts and the freshly squeezed juice were definitely my favorite.  But they stop the juice at 11 am.

Desserts were delicious, and they have a fresh crepe station, with your choice of filling and drizzle.

I was disappointed that there was no omelette bar, and the eggs in most of the breakfast dishes were overcooked or had been sitting for a long time.

Glad I took the time to experience it!

My favorite buffet in Vegas. Amazing seafood selection, all you can eat macaroon, Gelato, mexican food, pasta . Yummy in my tummy ! However typical asian selection nothing extravagant ( when I pay almost 70$ for a person my expectation increased )

For the price it was mediocre. I did not get filled on the food, highlights? The Atlantic salmon, egg tart, and the clam chowder. The escargot was also amazing! The desserts were the main course meal for my sister and I. I would not eat here again but it was nice to try because the desserts were just too good to pass up.

I LOVE this place! It's by far my favorite buffet! My family and I went for dinner last night. The line to get in was long, but I suppose buffet lines are always long, and it's definitely pricey, but worth it once you're inside! The food selection is fantastic and everything was fresh and delicious.

At $45, this buffet will blow your mind. The expectations of a buffet are completely thrown out the door here. I had only ever been to the usual buffets like Home Town and Golden Corral. This place is heaven compared to any other buffet. Expect a long wait every single time. Usually you wait between 45 minutes to an hour since there are always large groups waiting to be seated. The experience is definitely worth it. Every section of food at the Bachannal is so diverse. You get more than a couple plates from each section. The seafood section is by far the most popular with so many different dishes from crawfish boils to oyster shots. Then the BBQ section is always a small wait because everyone is trying to get a piece of the roast, turkey, sausages, and prime rib. The next section is the mexican food section where they make the tacos right there in front of you. They also provide you with a plethora of traditional toppings from sour cream and guacamole to pico de gallo and red/green salsas. The Italian section follows with so many different pasta combinations that stay away from the usual spaghetti and meatballs. They of course have really good pizza which is also not the usual cheese and pepperoni but instead are topped with quality ingredients. My favorite sections are the last 2 which i would consider Japanese, Chinese, and Thai. From sushi to dumplings to pho, everything is high quality and delicious. Nothing is mediocre here. Physically he place is beautiful. It hardly feels like a typical buffet. For the price this place is worth a try if you're dining in Vegas.

This buffet is sooo good. The selections at the seafood and meat stations are alone worth the admission fee. I got the Caesars rewards with 24 hour buffet option, so I also got to hit up the Rio buffet, which is pretty darn good too. Not as good as here. I'd definitely recommend and will come here on my next visit

Bacchanal is now #1 favorite buffet, but keep in mind I don't go to a lot of buffets. Take advantage of the Groupon because you'll get unlimited mimosas - our server refilled our mimosas quite fast. Our group went during the transition between breakfast and lunch in order to try a variety. I had their breakfast, asian (dim sum!), seafood, soup, and desserts. The food was beyond expectation, and the ambience is even better! I was stuffed, but I kept eating more just to taste everything; it was totally worth it!

Went to Vegas for the first time this year, narrowed my buffet choices down to two, Wynn and Caesar's.  Both rated well, but Bacchanal Buffet was better, no contest.

Went for lunch, got a small ($1) discount from the Total Rewards card.  Huge food selection.  Clean presentation.  Modern, trendy eating area.  Tons of variety and you can see everyone preparing the food in their respective areas.  Desserts were incredible and unique.

I know I'm going back the next time I come to Vegas.

After how many failed attempts, I've finally crossed Bacchanal off my "to try" list in Vegas. This time around was sweeter. A self check-in kiosk met us as we tried getting in line which asked for a name and a cellphone number for them to reach us when it's time to pay and get seated. 30 minutes of trying our luck with the slot machines and my phone beeped saying it was time. 

Time to get our glutton on, that's what!

I always scope out the different stations categorized by cuisines before getting anything. I've finally learned to skip the bacon and other breakfast items I can eat at home so I started with some dim sum, roasted duck, and hot and sour soup. Can I say that was the best SIUMAI I've had just yet? It's remarkably tasty and perfect in texture from all aspects. Try it and thank me later! Meanwhile, the duck was great but the hot and sour soup could use less salt.

There's a long line for the seafood station so I went for the carving station for a nice slab of PRIME RIB (yuummmm!) and got me some of the best SCALLOPED POTATOES with MUSHROOMS from another part of the buffet. Wow! I got two pans of these buttery and flavorful carbs. Soooooo gooooood! I was told the LAMB CHOPS would be dished out around 3pm but by then I was already too full. Something to try next time, that's for sure. 

Offering a selection of soups, I had their tomato basil soup, very delish, and their mushroom with truffle soup, very salty! Next to it is their bread station and take heed when I say get their mini CORN BREAD muffins. Mmmhmmm!

I finally lined up for the seafood station to start burning what I ate. Mussels, clams, salmon, and seafood paella were the hot ones that I partook. I forgot to return for the shrimp and grits but those looked good. Cajun crawfish was also some of the offerings I decided to skip on due to the eating logistics of that crustacean. However, I certainly could not pass up on the oyster shooters, cocktail shrimps, KING CRAB LEGS, and their fresh succulent oysters. I recommend everything I tried in this station, however, I thought the paella was just alright and was on the salty side.

Ending this gluttonous meal on a sweet note, I will have to say that among all the beautiful looking pastries and sweets I've tried, what's really worth indulging in are their CREPES! They have a station where they make it fresh for you with your own choosing of toppings such as sugar, syrup, and fruits. The texture and flavor is spot on. It's so good I could easily eat it by itself! Or, you can pair with it any gelato of your liking with so many flavors to choose from, if it rocks your boat. 

If there's anything that didn't impress me other than a few over-seasoned items, it would sadly have to be the service rendered to us by our server. She was an older lady who was somehow kind and very accommodating to all the tables around us, but us. She seemed cold, always rushing without stopping to hear what we're requesting. When she was leaving, she said, "My shift is done, I want to go home now! You want anything else?" And it wasn't in a friendly way. She moved on to the next table and got all friendly to them endorsing the server who was to take care of them when she leaves. And this is why you should tip only after you've been served.   

Bottomline, we were all happy with what we consumed despite the price tag it came with ($50 for weekend champagne brunch). Because we got seated around 2pm, we were able to enjoy some dishes that were served only for dinner such as the fresh oysters. Either way, I guarantee you will leave this place satiated not just with the quantity of food you'll get but with a quality worth noting.

The food was great and the staff was amazing! We loved our cold crab legs and sushi. Our server Jo never let our drinks get empty and was really friendly. The managers Stephanie, Amber and Mike kept checking on us to see if we needed anything else. Great service!!!  Bacchanal is Vegas's best buffet, hands down.

This is THE best buffet in Vegas at the moment. I didn't even take any pictures because I was busy stuffing my face. Plus, pictures would not do it justice -- every dish would deserve one.

Crab legs, hot or cold? Up to you! They'll serve you a whole plate of fresh hot legs on request. Tonktasu ramen or pho? Why not... just eat everything here.

Seriously, eat. everything. here.

I tried Bacchanal during my trip to Las Vegas last weekend.  As this was rated the #1 Buffet in Vegas, I was excited to give it a try. 

There is a large selection of food to choose from. If they don't have it, you probably don't need it. :o)  There are Mexican, Italian, Asian, Southern cuisines and more.  I tried  everything from shrimp and grits, to sushi, to ratatouille, to charcuterie and more.  It was all good enough.  But as the old adage goes, they are a jack of all trades, but master of none. In my opinion, a smaller selection of food prepared impeccably is preferable to everything under the sun and it all being "meh".  I did manage to save a little room for dessert and really enjoyed that station, and I am not a big dessert person.  The chocolate covered strawberries were awesome! They were dipped in butterfingers, how can that be anything but awesome?!

Overall, the buffet is aesthetically pleasing.  The food selection is quite diverse. But I do not feel it is worth the $55+ per person.  I much preferred the more reasonably priced buffet at the Rio.

A buffet of truly epic proportions.  Since it was Chinese New Year weekend, they bumped prices to  $51/pp.  Overall, our party of seven had an excellent meal.  In terms of overall quality-to-value, I think Bacchanal is above Bellagio but slightly below Wicked Spoon.  Note also this restaurant is very large and loud - they play music and the background.

Lines for the meat section were longer than the line to get in at 5pm.  The meat section has ample selections, with the smoked brisket and lamb chops being the stars.  The lamb was seasoned well and soft and succulent.  Mint jelly was available but the lamb had more than enough flavor.  I enjoyed the lamb so much I didn't even get a chance to try the prime rib or artisinal sausages.

The other amazing dish was the corn tortilla steak tacos.  It had marinated grilled beef that was perfectly cooked and topped with a green sauce with a good dose of line.  The corn tortillas were warm and soft and definitely freshly made.  Probably one of the best tacos I've had anywhere.

The wagyu beef sliders were juicy when I picked them, however two of my dining companions found them dry and over seasoned. Guess I was lucky - I had two of these tasty mini burgers without issues.

Near the back of the restaurant you'll find the asian section along with sushi, followed by a salad bar.  Sushi was fresh and the rice was made perfectly.  Of the Asian dishes, probably the Chinese greens were the best.  They were stir fried with garlic to a point and cooked enough to where it still had crunch.  Strangely there weren't a whole lot of other cooked veggies at this buffet.  I tried some baby carrots and some corn cobs but that's about it.

Fried items were also good - calamari baskets, spicy fried fish, fried chicken, sweet potato fries and tater tots, etc.  You get a hint of spice as you savor the sweet taste of the sweet potato.  Surprisingly low on greasy but high on crunchy!

The seafood section was near the front of the restaurant, with fresh oysters, crab legs, etc.  Cooked items included halibut, which was cooked perfectly too.  Despite the cool decorations, I did not see any lobster or Alaska king crab :(

Lastly, the dessert section was truly massive, probably one-upping Wicked Spoon.  The have gelato, mochi, and crepe sections.  Also, four varieties of the mini dessert cones and other tempting goodies on a stick.  The chocolate-dipped strawberries was something else - probably the biggest, ripest, and reddish strawberries I've ever seen.    

This buffets selection is so massive you run the risk of getting too full early and missing out on some really unforgettable dishes.  My friend tasted one taco and then wound up getting three more before hitting the dessert section.  It's a bit pricier than other Vegas buffets, but their meat, dessert, and  Mexican, and fried selections are superior.  Everything else is similar to other buffets.

BEST BUFFET I EVER HAD!!!!

Some may think it's expensive, but in Hawaii, a buffet for $55 will not get you much at all! Therefore, for ME, this place was a steal!! 

I went during the spring and during the summer and the summer had better selections! There was more seafood so more bang for your buck!

A good time to go would be about 4 - 4:30, before anyone gets hungry for dinner obviously. But seriously, I went at that time twice on a Thursday and Friday, and there was NO wait!

If you're in Vegas, you can't miss out on Bacchanal!

Don't get me wrong Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace is the best buffet with the best food offered, but be warned the buffet is misleading.   You will read online that you can sign in at a kiosk so you won't have to wait in line, however, that is false and a marketing scheme.  You can register at a kiosk and will receive a time to come back and wait in line for an hour and a half.  One would think you would be automatically seated after registering at a kiosk for the buffet and having to wait 2 hours to return, but what you are registering for is a reservation to stand in line at a later time for a 2 hour wait to enter the buffet.  This false marketing is created so people do not leave for another buffet if they knew how ridiculously long their lines are.  In addition they make you pay half way in line so after a 1 hour wait you will pay the $50 something dollars for the buffet and be obligated to stand in line for an additional hour while waiting to be seated.  Furthermore, after being seated customer service is horrendous due to the amount of people in the buffet and lack of servers.  We stayed in there for an hour and never had our drinks refilled once.  We weren't the only ones as other tables had empty cups on their tables for hours also.  For the price, lack of service, and long line wait I would not recommend Bucchanal Buffet and would rather eat at the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan or any other buffet because price wise and food wise Bucchanal is not that superior to be demanding an addition $10 to $15 dollars more for their dinner buffet.  In addition, if I am paying that much more have your service people refill my drink at least once the whole time I am there.  Horrible service!

Hadn't been back to Bacchanal since I was a dependent! But goes to show that CP's buffet has stood the testament of time.

Get in before 10Am and your meal is $30 (which, incidentally, was less than my composite pastry buy at Payard across the way, and Savoy's Brioche-- all in CP too). No Total Rewards discount at the moment.

Standouts for sure! Steak and eggs, lobster bennie. Crab and shrimp, croissant breakfast sammies, chicken and waffles, crostata, congee and doughnut, dimsum, a la minute omelettes and fresh juice mini carafes!!!

Not good and don't waste your calories: pain perdu (dry, tasteless), biscuits (not good), leg of lamb ( wrong color, full of fat).

Other things like turkey and ham and sausages at carving station 

Lots of lox and Scandinavian cured & salted fish with bagels.

Skipped dessert bar altogether 

Please do not forget the Mx, Asian, and international room at an L-shaped 90 degrees from main dining.

My particular visit only 3 people ahead of me. Yay for me

Just go!
Best i have ever had
Should be illegal though. You leave only having had a fraction of what is available...and everything you had was some of the best...so you know you missed out on a whole lotta amazing food!
Kids loved it and i have never seen them eat so much food ...lol

It was just okay. We paid $45 each for lunch . I thought that the beef sliders were the best thing they had there followed by the crepes. They had a lot of food to choose from but it was nothing great.

I wasn't planning to do buffet at all but I guess it wouldn't feel right if you go to Vegas and not do buffet. 

Price:
Friday: $29 BEFORE 3PM, $40 something or $40 AFTER 3PM, which is dinner time then. We got in at 2:59 (= If you have Caesars card, it's $2-$3 cheaper. Free to apply btw! 

When you first walk in, all the food section will be on the left and I'll start out from the beginning.

(1) Seafood: It's near the main entrance. They offer a great different amount of seafood. Crab legs, oysters, mussels, shrimps, and several side dishes that has seafood in it. The crab legs were a little disappointing for me. Some were okie, some were SALTY was heck. Did I come on a bad day or what? LOVEEEEE the OYSTERS!! I ate a lil too much. My poor liver.
(2) MEAT: the station next to it is meat and nothing but meat. That's where you get the prime rib, steak or lamb....The prime rib was definitely a FAIL. I don't expect it to taste good but it was kinda sour! I didn't try much from this station.
(3): Mexican: Right after meat is Mexican food. I don't recall other buffets have Mexican's section eh? That was neat! They grill the meat for you on the spot if you want tacos. They have plenty variety of salsa for you to choose from. AND! They also do Mexican's corn if you personally ask them for it.
(4): Italian: I didn't want to get full off of bread so the only thing I got was a sliced of pepperoni pizza. Surprisingly it was hecka good!!! Crunchy and just perfect. 
(5): Salads: Nice selection of salads!!
(6): Asian: They have sushi, disum, and Korean I think. The only thing I grab was short ribs. Not bad! The sushi selection didn't look that appealing compared to the Bellagio's Buffet forsho.
(7): DESSERTS: This has to be my favorite selection. They have very similar desserts to other buffets but it was quite good because it was not too sweet! My favorite is the tiramisu in the little long cup, and red velvet cake. They make everything tiny so you get to try a lot!!

Over all, it was nice to try it but I think I can pass if I have to. If you're a crab legs person, you need to do HILTON BUFFET in LA....that's the right place to go to.

My experience at this buffet can be described in three letters.... WTF?... It's low quality food at fine dining prices. My buyer's regret over this place is worse than loosing all that money in one of the casinos would be. The only way they can count 500+ dishes is if they count all the condiments in as separate dishes. It's your friendly neighborhood Todai Buffett at overinflated price and a long line to get in. Skip it to avoid huge disappointment and spend your money someplace else.

Heard a lot of good things about this place and thought this should be the place to go in Vegas! Vegas is known for buffets so it's fitting to eat at a buffet when in Vegas. Came here on Sunday for the champagne brunch with my boyfriend around 10ish. There was a small line already but wasn't too bad of a wait. Each person cost $48.99 I believe, it was on the pricey side of course. There were a wide variety of breakfast foods to choose from. We got the bloody mary which tasted like straight up v8 juice.. But the mimosas tasted much better lol. Also, the fresh juice in the cute bottles were great too. I got to taste a little bit of everything. I think you get a different experience between brunch and dinner. I would want to come back for dinner to see the other options that they offer at night. Overall, the food was good but I think I prefer or would like more of the dinner option. But then again if you want to get your drink on feel free to drink yourself silly with the unlimited mimosas that they offer for the Sunday champagne brunch!

This was the BEST buffet I've ever been to in my life. It is more on the pricier side, but every penny is worth it! There's so much variety and options in the food choices that you can't go wrong. Definitely worth a visit when I'm Vegas.

4 ppl $155 kind of pricy but IMO better than wicked spoon
Chinese 4/5
Seafood 4/5 went for lunch but kingcrab is serving
BBQ 3/5
Italian 3/5
Paella 3/5

I came here last night and they had the holiday dinner which included King Crab Leg in the holiday menu. The main purpose I came here is to eat the King Crab Leg, I was very disappointed when I found there is NO such thing at the buffet. The people at Seafood section pointed us to Italian section for King Crab Leg, but the people at Italian section asked us to check with Seafood section. They were both handing out Snow Crab Legs, NOT KING CRAB LEGS. Sooo disappointed. If you don't have it, don't put it on your menu to trick people. LIE. If you want to try King Crab Legs, DO NOT come here. 

Moreover, if you like sushi, you will be disappointed as well. The rice was so dry. NOT GOOD.

Positive side: Snow crab legs and Oysters are good and fresh. Meat is good. Desert are great and the fresh juice is good. 

Overall, I will NOT pay over $60 (with tax) to come eat here again. Specially the wait is so long,  it's NOT worth it.

This place was amazing! I had been follow the construction and makeover and was so excited it was going to open right before I got to Vegas.

We waited about an hour and a half to get in for dinner right during prime time. There were lots of empty tables so I'm not quite sure what the hold up was there, but at this point I didn't really care. Once we were about half way through line it moved pretty fast. 

The individual stations are great and the chefs are super friendly! They all welcome you and will answer any questions you have about any of the food. I loved the chef at the pho/ramen station! The pho was pretty good although I would have liked some red chili sauce to put in it. I didn't see any, but I didn't look to hard. I figured it should have been right there. 

The seafood station was good, big hold up with getting your crab legs warmed up. Love that they offer it but need to ask people to move to the side and wait. The rest of  the seafood area was pretty good. The clam bake in a bucket was cute! The shrimp and grits was good as well...but...not like mama makes it. The sauce on top just sorta tasted like chili to me.

The Italian section was one of my favs! The sliced meats and cheese were fantastic. I read a comment somewhere that its nice they offer more high end meats and cheeses at a buffet but will anyone eat them?? yes this girl right here. It is all right by some of the fresh bread and it's just begging you to make a little sandwich with some olive oil drizzled on it. The honeycomb was right here as well, although I didn't try it, the presentation was amazing. Oh and don't forget to try the Caprese Salad that is in this area too!! I saw the individual portions of baked ziti and lasagna...I wasn't to impressed. It tasted good but was sorta hard and chewy in some places, I could tell it had sat some.

Lastly...desserts. Over all they were awesome. Warm chocolate chip cookie in a little bowl was super good. The chef made sure to give me one from her tray she took out of the oven, not the ones that had already been sitting there. The vanilla souffle was PERFECT. I really suggest the Aztec chocolate ice cream. Its got some red pepper in it, and give the perfect little zing to the ice cream. I wasn't to impressed by some of the things just sitting out, like cookies in a jar or bowl, and the Madeline I tried was hard, I didnt even eat it (and i love them).\

I was a little turned off by some of the items sitting out when all I had heard was everything was made fresh in individual portions. If you are going to do that, you have to throw the bad stuff sometimes. If not for that, 4 1/2 stars. Im taking off another half for the asian section. It was a little... dysfunctional. All the condiments seemed just sort of, thrown out and not by the main dish it needed to be served it. I LOVE me some asian food, and all I sprung for was the Pho. A little more organization is needed I guess.

Over all I would love to go back and try everything I didn't get to. Take your time looking and make a game plan. and pace yourself. There are lots of hidden little things here you can easily pass up, like the fresh breads and the Honey.

Food 4star 
Service 5star
Price  $$$.
Buffet overall experience 4.5star 
Seafood was okay. 
Beef and meat little dry but don't expect
100% from buffet. 
Most of the food was good.

RIP!  We went in at 10:30a on a Thursday before Christmas. I was told the buffet is in Holiday season so it's brunch pricing all day long for $40+ per head.  There was no posted sign, and I was not aware of any holiday season pricing until we got up to the cashier.  The meal is not worth the $40 per head price.

It was really good, but for $40 (brunch on week day), it needs to be really, _really_ good to get a five star rating, and it wasn't _that_ good. I liked how there were so many small portion slider-type things. It made it easy to try lots of different dishes.

Updated review: 
We came back for dinner and enjoyed the food a lot more. The steak wasn't as chewy as before. It was well seasoned and I actually had quite a bit to eat. They had delicious salmon too! I highly recommend the salmon if you are a fish lover. It was cooked perfectly. The shrimp and chips were very good too. Nice and light batter with crispy potato chips.  

Definitely try this place. It's worth a second chance if you were disappointed before. 
----------------------------------------------The quality of the food has gone down significantly since its opening. It is still one of my favorite buffets. However, a lot of the food is lacking in one way form or another. I used to love the crab legs and steak. The crab is so so now. They still cook it for you if you ask them to. Delicious In butter! 

Now the steak is something that I love for. And I love myself an all you can eat quality buffet. They offered three types: prime rib, waygu beef, and tri-tip. I always have my cuts rare or medium rare. The tri tip was extremely dry, prime rib was the best out of the three but extremely fatty, the waygu was a bit chewy but beyond tender. 

Bone marrow: I had 3-4 of these. It seriously tastes like butter. I would have taken them home for my dogs if I could have! 

Mexican food bar: best part of the whole meal. It is kind of a problem for the amount of money you pay. $60 a person. 

Bacchanal no longer has their large line/variety of soups. I was looking for the ginseng and chicken broth soups but found basic minestrone, clam chowder, and two more options I cannot recall. 

The dessert bar is loaded with AYCE desserts. Best part were gummy bears.

One of the best restaurants I have ever had the pleasure to dine at. Absolutely amazing and well worth the price. Every item was delicious, well cooked and baked, and my family and I had a great time stuffed and happy. We will definitely be back.
Best Service, clean & great food choices from American, soul food, Asian, etc. If you don't try the buffet while in Vegas you were not in Vegas. It's expensive but worth your money.

Just 1 star because of the big let down. First of all, service was poor, the employees seem to be tired and not happy to be there. The cashier clerk did not even bother to greet us, and maintained a grim face over the entire exchange. The price was super expensive (I would not have minded had it been worth it). The crabs (at both hot and cold sections) were super salted, this was probably a mean to discourage us from eating too much. You should not anyway because this is very unhealthy. The salmon smells ... fishy of course. The only saving grace was the tacos, they were surprisingly good. Deserts were also not worth eating. The flan was super sweet, again very unhealthy and every means seems to be deployed to discourage people from eating. Then you wonder why that much hype??? Stay away.
Would not recommend. You can get this food at any buffet for much cheaper. The only thing that was good was the steak. That's it.

I've tried a handful of the buffets on the strip and none were even close to being worth their prices. The Bacchanal always had the highest sticker price with the number 1 king of buffets on the strip title though according the consensus. I finally got a chance to try it through my bf's company event and I admit, it didn't disappoint.

There's always a wait here it seems. I tried to come one other time and the wait was 3 hours. Luckily, I went in with our big group and reserved tables so we just waltzed right in. 

There's so many food stations and the food is well up to par. Everything was delicious and seasoned just right. The only falter I found was the dessert section. I wasn't a fan of desserts. I think the only thing I liked was the ice cream. The french macarons were too brittle, cookies meh, and some mousse I think it was was also mediocre. But all of the savory foods were steps above your average buffets. 

I'd for sure try to get myself into this buffet again if I won big at the slots and had time for that 3 hour wait.

This was the second time I visited this buffet in Vegas. I had such s great experience the first time around, I had to bring my dad. 

First time wait: 2+hours then you get texted to go pay. Then I wanted an additional 30-40mins to be seated. Famished!

Second time wait: none. 30mins to get seated. 

Food: great variety of seafood (oysters, stone crabs, snow crabs legs, other hot seafood creations), meats (prime rib, trip tip and or sirloin, turkey, duck, lamb chops) and other ethnic foods (street tacos, sushi, Chinese, dim som, pho/udon noodle station) plus your regular salads, cheese, fruits, desserts and bread stations. 

Service: mediocre. It takes the servers a while to get your drink and refill. The dirty plates were left on our table until my leg crabs carcasses practically crawled on the table. Slower than my past experiences. 

Price first time: I came at dinner time so it was $50.99 a person. Dinner price. 

Price second time: I paid right before 3pm on a Friday. $34.99 (one dollar off with players card) lunch price. 

Quality of seafood: oysters were more fresh the first time around. The second time around, they looked a bit dry and dehydrated. Crab legs were smaller second time around in comparison to the first. Stone crabs were okay. Not much flavor to them but meaty. 

Even though they have a great variety of food. I feel the lunch price is more reasonable. I did not notice any difference with food selection from lunch to dinner. By then again, by the time I went in, it was already dinner time.

Located in side Caesar's Palace, $55 for a buffet sounded a bit steep for me, plus there are already so many great restaurants in Vegas so why would I engorge myself on a buffet? Well, after a more recent visit to this one, I am now very convinced that this is the best buffet on the Vegas strip. Yes, they do have bottomless mimosas on the weekend for +$15 I think until 2pm or so. All of that is really overkill though and you are guaranteed to knock out for the rest of the day. One of my biggest gripes about buffets, hence the reason why I'm still skeptical about the overall value of them. Either way, this one is pretty bomb!

At Bacchanal, I enjoyed their seafood, sushi, and desserts (uhm, more creme brulee please). I didn't much care for their American 'wagyu', roast beef and prime rib because by the time I would get back to the table it was all very very cold. The line does get rather large and they have three different ones based on how large your party is. We waited for ~1 hour with a party of 6. If you are thinking about buffeting it, this one is guaranteed to make you very full and happy. But yes, prepare for food coma afterward!

Not quite a five star, there are better, more elegant buffets (and most of those include champagne and/or wine), but only a few and even with all the Snow Crab legs you can eat it would be considered by many to be  a little pricey  at $50 until compared to inflated Strip prices (it looked like a gift compared to the $15 hotdog at many of the hotels; you don't eat on the strip or hotels if you are offended by high prices),  

That said, they will allow you to extend the buffet to a 24 hour deal for just $25 more and that is absolutely worth it on any scale or standard, plus the food quality, variety, quantity and flavor is good to very good (exception: sushi) and the service is very, very helpful and attentive.  The decor did not come close to matching the opulence of the rest of Caesar's Palace but it wasn't high school cafeteria either.  Treat yourself to it at least once (tip to avoiding long lines: go on off-hours!)

If you want a real vegas buffet this is the place. The variety is enormous. Seafood, bbq, Italian, Asian...ect. I typically don't get excited for sweets but the desserts were impressive.  My sole complaint is that the server was very slow and disorganized with beverages.

After hearing all the buzz about Bacchanal buffet, my friends and I decided to go here for Saturday brunch/lunch while we were in Vegas. We got up early (by Vegas standards, at least) and headed over to Caesar's Palace around 10:30-11:00AM. There was no line to pay, and only a few parties ahead of us to be seated. This is where the first problem came up - the servers seemed to be SUPER CONFUSED! There were 3 of them at the hostess stand staring at the iPad seating arrangement chart and it seemed like they could not figure out where to seat everyone when you could CLEARLY see a bunch of empty tables just waiting to be filled! (NOTE: this may have irritated me more due to hunger)

After we were seated, our server was very nice and friendly and brought us waters, juices, and a mimosa for one of my friends. Then we were off! Bacchanal's Asian station is BY FAR the most diverse and delicious Asian station at any Vegas buffet I've seen! They had dim sum (ha gao, shu mai, chicken sticky rice wrapped in a lotus leaf, leek dumplings, etc.), they had a noodle station that offered pho, ramen, and udon. They had Thai (spring rolls), Korean (bulgogi) and Japanese (sushi) offerings as well.

The pizza is delicious!! Thin crust, but able to support the weight of the toppings and nice and flavorful. There was a bunch of different pastas and the egg station that I didn't try. I really liked the croque madam sandwich (super cute portion), tater tots were nice and crispy and they had standard breakfasty foods like: eggs benedict, sausage, scrambled eggs, etc.

The seafood was a bit limited at brunch/lunch (more is offered after 3:00 PM). But they had mussels and crab legs. There was also fresh juices served in cute glass milk bottles - orange, cucumber, tropical, and melon.

DESSERT: lots of offerings! I tried the carrot cake (not carroty AT ALL), cheesecake (nice and dense, but a bit dry), and some of the sorbets. They do NOT have a gelato station but their sorbet offerings are SO GOOD! very unique such as balsamic fib, thai tea, watermelon mint, red bean, Aztec chocolate, chili mango and lots more! I'm glossing over the other 50 desserts they offer but it runs along the lines of pastries and baked goodies.

I liked the buffet, but I don't think I would come back because of the price $50+. Wicked Spoon is better (and cheaper!)

This buffet, located inside Ceaser's Palace is easy to find. We had heard this was the best of the best when it comes to buffets in Vegas. We had breakfast here on our last day in Vegas. The line was short and the staff were extremely friendly. The food selection was impressive and the crepe station was out of this world! The selection of toppings ranged from savory to sweet and the neighboring ice cream and gelato bar provided a nice cool topping. We loved the basil gelato as a palate cleanser between trips to the buffet. Although, this buffet was excellent, it was not our favorite. I would visit again, but it's not #1 on my list.

So I was at the bacchanal buffet and the food here is amazing.  The food I tried is the lava cake which was good and the best I had was the red velvet pancakes.  They are the best pancakes I have tried.I hope you have a good time at the bacchanal buffet.The eggs Benedict was ok not the best but still good.The bacon tastes like regular bacon.The yogurt was delicious.  This is an excellent place.  The music and atmosphere were amazing.  Highly recommend.

Food was really good for the price, however both ne and my collègue had some episodes of diarrhea, and it's our second week here in Us, shouldn't have any traveller syndrome. Maybe it's overdosage of protein from seafood

When I first got to this buffet I thought I died and went to heaven. That ended quickly when I decided to go to the meat station. The guy working there (Jake) was absolutely rude! I'm short (5'0) I get missed easily especially in big crowds. My husband and I were in line at the meat station, my husband got food and when it was my turned I got pushed back. I come around to the front and Jake actually refused to serve me saying I was cutting some imaginary line. What was worse, some random customers also got in on the fun by laughing at me with him about how I wasn't allowed to get food till I got in line when I was standing there for over 10 mins next to no one! He even went out of his way to ignore me and pretending like he couldn't see me even though I was directly in front of him. I was so embarrassed and felt so stupid that I started crying which made me feel like a fatty. I told a manager and all they could do was offer me food to fix the situation. Which was upsetting since I cared more about the treatment I received vs not getting food. I didn't take any food and left immediately after. I won't come here again.

Probably one of the highlights of my vegas trip. Came here for brunch with some friends (8 total). I would definitely recommend coming early, earlier the better, as this place can't get packed with long wait times. It's a little pricey but about average for vegas....definitely a MUST TRY though. I would label it as one of the better buffets in Vegas at this time. Prior to Bacchanal I was a fan of WIcked Spoon, but always great to have an alternative. For brunch it was $41/person plus 18% gratuity(additional $15/person) because of our large party. Bacchanal has a great space and lay out very spacious and airy. It overlooks the Cesar Palace swimming pool. They have a variety of stations which offer a selection of foods from: breakfast food, southern comfort, seafood bar, juice bar, mexican, italian, asian food, carving station. GREAT selection of food and each prepared in small portions served on individual plates/servings. During brunch they also offer bottemless mimosa (so drink up and make that $41 worth it) Aside from all the food they offer a great dessert bar with a wide variety to baked desserts, cakes, cookies, freshly made to order souffle's and a selection of gelato. Treat yourself and make sure to drop by Bacchanal you will not be disappointed. COME HUNGRY!!!!

I came all the way from Chula Vista To Vegas one day trip just to come enjoy the fabulous buffet they had told me about not my fav. The only thing I enjoy was prime rib and Mac and cheese e everything else was not out of this world and the $12.00dlls mimosas all u can drink was the favvvv really strong a r tasting. I was really disappointed because drove a long way for something I could of enjoy in my home town sorry. Will be coming back in April and will definitely try a different buffet
Really great food, good service. Not much more to say except this is probably my favorite buffet in Vegas. I've been to Rio, PH, Bellagio, Harrahs and this is the best by far.

The price is a little on the expensive side. Come really hungry! They have the buffet divided by types of food. The Chinese food was the best! And they have a dessert area separate. Pace yourself and you can try it all!!! The horchata was really good.

way over rated and way over priced. The long wait, definitely not worth it. They reserved lot of tables for people paying $25 more or their VIP guests, and the service...well, I regret paying $5 tip because no one came to clear my table and I had to remove dishes myself. Paid $62 for Sunday dinner and food isn't impressive at all.I had Ballagio, Rio, Wicked spoon and Wynn, all are way better than this.I see no point getting the ticket from kiosk, it makes you confused too. We waited almost 2 hours, never come back again.

I went there for brunch on a sunday and I didn't like this place it was over priced and the food was just ok I'm my opinion. 
But my mom and gr thought it was really good. 
Service was exceptional tho!!!
The only reason I gave it three stars is because my mom and gf liked it.

Beef is great here.  Wagyu, prime rib, tri tip, etc.  Also, slab bacon, bacon, polka kielbasa.  All were AWESOME.  I know everyone comes here for the awesome seafood station.  That station has a seriously ginormous line.  I could not waste my time in there.  Not into shellfish.  Went straight for the other meats and had an absolutely great meal.  Also hit up some decent sushi rolls.  My big COMPLAINT about this buffet is that the desserts are bad.  I did not enjoy them at all.  Found them all mediocre compared to the Paris buffet.  They were just too rich. Loaded with cocoa to the point of saturation of all flavor that sent me reeling after one bite. You need some options that are mellower.

We came here on Thurs. Jan 2 at 8pm and was told by the snobbish host that they are not letting anyone in without tickets. We told him that we are willing to wait and he said no.  We asked about paying extra for express line and was also told that it was not available. If you want to try this buffet, come and get a ticket like five hours in advance. We met a local couple and they told us they have been there twice. First time when it first opened and one more time recently. They said it is all for hype folks just like any new buffet in Vegas. I'm frustrated that they turned us and so many other people away.

Food at Bacchanal was pretty good, though some dishes fare better under heat lamps than others. My husband wasn't loving the seafood dishes as much as the other sections (I don't eat seafood so can't comment there). Variety was good in general and the desserts were my favorite.  This place isn't really a great 'value' at $90 for two for lunch, including tip. But if you're looking to check off the "buffet" box on your Vegas visit, as we were, this is a higher quality option than most. 
I'd probably give it 4 stars if a staff member in the dessert area hadn't given me attitude about taking a dessert off a mini plate (when I guess you're supposed to take the whole plate for certain items).  I stand corrected!  Otherwise, the service was friendly and efficient.

Easily the best buffet in Vegas. Yes it is expensive, yes it is usually crowded. The service here is really good though, and the food is definitely worth the price. Don't be afraid to spend the extra money for a better product, you definitely won't be disappointed

I never eat buffet, but in Vegas I make an exception. The food here has so much variety. If you want Mexican or Chinese or American this buffet has it. It works for everyone whatever there in the mood for.

My favorite buffet in all of Las Vegas. Worth the waiting in line!!! I came in to celebrate turning an accomplished 31,  with my squad of 3. Wish there was a local's price though. We always go for the seafood of course and the prime rib. Drink service was a tad slower this visit than last time and it was a regular Sunday. Our last visit was NYE and it was packed, but our table service was impressive. Not sure what happened this time around.

I'll be honest. This was my FAVORITE buffet up until this past weekend. We got ready EXTRA early and got there at 10AM to our early check-in receipt from the machine. Our ticket said: APPROXIMATE CHECK IN TIME WILL BE 11:05AM and that we'd get a text a few minutes before... We never got a text and when we went up to the line, they made us stand in line ANYWAY. WHAT IS THE POINT OF THEM HAVING THAT DUMB MACHINE THERE IF WE HAVE TO WAIT IN LINE?? THEY SHOULD HAVE SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS saying EVEN IF YOU HAVE THIS TICKET YOU STILL HAVE TO WAIT IN LINE.  Our group was trying to be understanding and saying well it IS Christmas and they're extremely busy. THAT wasn't the part that pissed us off. We waited over 2 hours IN LINE (NOT counting the 1 hour we spent near by waiting for our TEXT that we never GOT) and when we got to the front of the line, we stopped moving up for over 30 minutes because they started letting this OTHER line ahead of us. I guess these people were the 7-star guests, or guests that paid extra. WHY WOULDNT YOU JUST DO A SEPARATE ENTRANCE FOR THESE PEOPLE INSTEAD OF SHOVING THEM IN FRONT OF US WHILE WE STAND THERE WATCHING THIS HAPPEN?? IS THAT YOUR WAY OF ADVERTISING - IF YOU WANT TO GET IN, THEN PAY EXTRA PER PERSON? ALSO there were some guests that started complaining and screaming so THEY were ALSO shoved in front of us. SO LET ME GET THIS STRAIGHT... PATIENT guests like US get punished and stuck in line, while SCREAMING guests get put in front of the line... WHAT AN AWESOME management system  you got there. We got so fed up and left to eat at Spago - which turned out to be better.  EVEN THOUGH this WAS my favorite buffet EVER, I probably won't go back since they have the worst management/customer service ever. I just felt bad because I was the only one that has been to this buffet out of our group and the whole trip, I hyped this place up SO much til we got there. In the end, my family never got to try this place and everyone left angry.

We frequently travel to Vegas from Los Angeles and on our last day in Vegas we picked out at the buffet. This is the only buffet in Vegas I would recommend. Not cheap but worth it. The food is high-quality the staff is amazing. Can't wait till our next trip.
Hands down best buffet in Las Vegas and best on the buffet of buffets.  Worth the up charge.

I'd probably actually go 3.5 stars, but am choosing to round down simply because, to me, the value is just not there.

Don't get me wrong, the setup and ambiance is nicer than most buffets, the food selection is good, and quality seems to be pretty high - but it doesn't justify $57 per person. After tip, with just my wife and I, ~$130 is just way too steep. 

I did really enjoy their Asian selection, including the sushi. Their crablegs were pretty good, and if you want to get your money's worth, I guess you do what quite a few people were doing, which was to literally just eat plate after plate of them... but for me, a buffer is about the variety and newness of a bunch of different things!

The dessert bar was amazing though!
Holy baby Jesus this was amazing. Every bite was delicious. The pasta and Asian section were to die for and the dessert...I mean come on.

so this place was one of the MUST DOs on our list in vegas. my friend got us the hook up so we waltzed past the 90 minute dinner line. you can pay $15 to skip the line which i think is totally worth it if you're visiting, 100% healthy, and the line is over an hour.

decor is absolutely gorgeous. presentation is phenomenal everywhere. service is great from all the cooks and chefs.

some of the things this place has:
hand made tamales are too big
a full gelato bar
great mac n cheese
both hot AND cold half shelled crab
oysters
kobe sliders which my friend said was ok
chinese bbq pork which was phenom
hot and sour soup
soup dumplings
tons of salasa
macaroons
bananas foster
individually baked choco chip cookies where were too sweet but i think was just a bad batch otherwise great
ribeye
shrimp and grits
individual chicken parm which i forgot to try

its a GREAT GREAT buffet but there are some duds so you can't lose sight of the fact its a buffet. i dont know what second highest rated buffet in vegas is but i would only go to one buffet while in vegas and id make it this place. id love to see what they could do with breakfast. wear sweatpants FYI 

JEANS: OK by far
ORDER: you pay upfront after the line

shout out to the old european hostesses who were so so so so sweet
Hands down the best buffet ever! What more can I say? The service was excellent and the food was beyond amazing!

Okay, so I think I've found one of my top buffets ever.

We came here at around 10:30am so it was still breakfast pricing. It worked out well because in the middle of our meal, they switched out a bunch of the items for the lunch menu so we got to try dishes from both meal times. There was literally no wait since we came during an odd hour.

Some highlights:

-The mini fresh juices in a bottle were awesome! I wasn't a huge fan of the cucumber juice however.
-Everything was so fresh and looked appetizing; even the asian food section which is usually sub-par at most buffets was decent.
-The servers were nice and more attentive than Wicked Spoon
-Ambience was pretty awesome

I was pretty excited about the crepe station but it was definitely over-hyped. The crepe itself tasted way too eggy. Maybe it was just the day we went, but I've had way better crepes at a specialty crepe shop.

As with any buffet, I recommend scanning the selection before you start piling food onto your plate; gotta allocate that stomach capacity. And pace yourself!

I actually hate buffets, but it's been a long time since I've gone to one and hey, they're notorious in Vegas. I still wouldn't go into a dingy hotel that claims to have a great buffet.

We had a late dinner around 8:45, by that time there wasn't a long wait to get a table. There was a great selection of ... *almost* everything. The two things I was craving (pasta and steak) were N/A or had limited kind. Despite my cravings unsatisfied, I was still content w/ the other offerings!

I was kind of disappointed on my second visit here. Before we went, I was talking it up to my wife because of how good it was during my first experience. Needless to say, it didn't deliver on our collective expectations as to what a top-tier Vegas buffet should be. While there was a  large selection of food to choose from, the overall quality of the food was low. I eat at a lot of Chinese buffets and I can probably compare the food here to that level of quality, not great but not bad enough to scare everybody away. However, since it's a $60+ buffet you kind of expect more of everything. The buffet didn't serve king crab legs like I was anticipating but rather replaced it with dungeoness crabs. I wouldn't have minded so much but the crabs were mostly small lesser quality pieces which sometimes tasted like they were rotten. The snow crab legs were also lower quality, small and brittle like the purchasing department went to the bargain bin of suppliers to save on costs. The desserts were decent but that's not the reason we chose to eat there. The Asian food station which includes the stir-fry and sushi section was as mediocre as expected. It was a busy night so it took a long time to refill my drink but overall service was reasonable. Before this trip, I thought this buffet had topped Bellagio's and Wynn's buffets but now I'm not so sure.

Great remodel on the old Ceasars buffet! I was able to use my points from my players card and didn't know that my card works as a front of the line pass woohoo bonus!

We were able to sit close to the buffet where multiple trips would not be too far to trek. First of all I have to say, anything with free flowing champagne will be a good time. There were the usual stations of Asian, American, Mexican food with fresh juices and fruit and pastries and desserts. I can't say there was any one dish that jumped out at me, but I could say the selection was something to brag about. The carvers had a selection if prime rib, slabs of bacon and turkey. Asian food was so much to choose from it was like a Chinese buffet restaurant all on its own.

There was a mini juice bar serving horchata, pineapple, mango, agua fresca etc.  this was next to the street tacos maker guy. There were tater tots in these mini deep fryer baskets-super cute. I didn't have enough room to try the cheese station, but that section looked appetizing. I'd have to be here for hours to try everything! I kept it simple at the dessert area and just had a simple fruit crepe with whipped cream. Perfect ending. I don't think you'll be disappointed.

Again, definitely a repeat of how I feel about Buccahanal Buffet since my last visit.

Solid 4/5 stars, but if i had to wait in the long line (about 1.5-2 hours), I would've given Bacchanal Buffet 3/5 stars. 

Luckily, we were able to go in the VIP line and waited for about 20 minutes to be seated even though when there were 8 people in front of us at 2:15pm. 


Highlights:
1) Truffled Mushroom Pizza
2) Steam Crab Legs
3) Of all the cuts of meat, Prime Rib was the best cut and well seasoned
4) Dessert options were great--some good items and some not so great options. (Good: Mochi Ice Cream, Freshly made crepe; Bad: melted gelato, not so great cookies)

Lowlights:
1) Asian food: wow, these items (sushi, dim sum, made-to-order soups were very disappointing. 
2) Salad bar was just eh...

Overall, probably the only buffet in vegas I would go to.

A chef d'oeuvre that lives up to its reputation and will wow even those who don't frequent buffets. Arrive by 10:30am to avoid the line. I recommend a two-hour workout followed by 7 plates of food here, mostly crab.

This buffet is way over rated. Considering this is supposed to be the best buffet in town,  I found it a little average. 

The selections were plentiful but the wait times and the quality was subpar. Seriously there were so many people in line for the raw oysters,  shrimps,  and crab legs that my boyfriend ate 2 plates before I came back with just one. 

This place is a mad house on the weekends as well. One review said the chefs were friendly but they were so busy on Friday that no one bothered to look up from refilling their stations. The price also increases x2 on weekends and there are so many kids. 

The service was alright. The waitress cleared our tables in a timely manner and our refills kept coming. 

The dessert bar is also amazing. They have mini versions of everything. My favorite has to be the creme brulee and the flan.
Super expensive but the food here was better than other $36 dollar buffets I have been to, so in my opinion, worth the extra $25. Fun time! Friendly staff!

As you read reviews of Bacchanal you will see everything from a 1 rating to a 5 and you may wonder what that is about.  Let me try to explain.  Some people have an expectation that everything must be absolutely perfect and if it isn't, they will find things to bring their rating to a 1.  Others don't have much to compare it to and think it is the best and give it a 5.  Then you have a whole bunch of the rest of us right in the middle.  Those of us that may have been to lots of buffets and brunches, like we have, and really know what we are talking about.  The Bacchanal is one of the best in Las Vegas, for a high end buffet, but it is not perfect.
