I say for a high end buffet because you have to compare it to others that are in approximately the same price range.  Don't compare it to something like Circus Circus because they are in a different category.
We dined here on a Sunday at around 11:00 a.m. and the wait was only about 10 min. but it can be very long at prime times.  They do have terminals in front that will tell you approximately how long the wait will be and you can enter your cell number at that time for a reservation and you will be called when you are able to get in.  That way you can wander around or gamble in the casino instead of standing in a line.  Nice feature.
The room is very nice and spread out so you don't feel crowded together.  The food areas for the most part are also spread out.  With one exception and this is a complaint we have with many buffets.  The carving station is placed right in the middle of a line of food which means that lines of people form and block other items of food that are then hard to get at.  Especially if you don't want anything from the carving station.  Sometimes the same is true of an omelet station.  It seems like places would figure it out when they decide to put in a carving or omelet station.
There is a very wide selection of food here so that everyone should be able to find something they like.  Large shrimp and cracked crab legs are plentiful.  Many areas with different types of food.  The dessert area is set in the middle of the room by itself and has many many assorted cookies, cakes, pastries, ice cream, crepe and shave ice.
The overall quality of the food is excellent and not filler food.  BUT.....almost all of the hot food items were just warm to almost room temp. at best!  Maybe it was just at the time we were there.  Most of the items are served in smaller portions on plates or in bowls so there aren't many large inserts of foods.  Perhaps this is why the foods aren't hot?  You are given a finger protector for hot plates,when you pay, but you certainly don't need them.  If the food had been hot, I would probably have given this a 5 instead of a 4.
If you don't mind paying for a higher end buffet, other than the few things I mentioned in my review, you won't be disappointed.  All of the service we had was also very good.  Don't be unkind or demanding and you will always get the good service.  Don't forget to tip!  Even though the people that bring your drinks and take away all your dirty plates don't bring you your food, but they still work hard cleaning up your mess.  They deserve to be tipped.  
There is a sign when you first come in telling you not to pick up and eat food at the serving areas but there will always be slobs, and I use that term loosely, that don't care and will stand there while they eat.  Just can't wait to get back to their tables and they will often spill things on the floor and make a mess.  We all see that kind of thing!  Why not show a little class instead of acting like a pig?

The atmosphere is nice and the presentation is unique and refreshing. The food on the other hand is simply embarrassing. 

The Asian dishes:
Broccoli Beef was beef with broccoli stems
Unlabeled Eggplant thing - not good
Potstickers were beyond cold
Pork had no crust and was bland
Beef ribs were pretty good
Pork ribs were ridiculous 

Mexican:
Served in pots and neither attractive nor cohesive

American Comfort Food:
Inexcusable not to have white meat as an option for fried chicken
The sweet potato fries were soggy
The meat section while impressive to look at came up way short with bacon that lacked smoke, brisket that was dry and mediocre at best

Sushi:
Don't go to any buffet for sushi

Dessert:
Sorbet was good and earned a star on its own. Otherwise the taffy was rock hard and creme brûlée was simply not good. 

The seafood is the mainstay and was good. If you want to spend $45.00 for all you can eat crab legs and shrimp then mission accomplished. .
Very good service.  Oysters was fresh and a great variety of food.  Alvaro Gomez gave my table great service(I would consider it 5 star service).

Customer service is exceptional here. Josh from the kitchen is a master!   I requested octopus and Josh delivered with a plate of sashimi.  Everything seafood I enjoyed today was fresh & delicious.  This is in our top 3 Buffets in Vegas.

If this is the best buffet in Vegas, I don't know what others will be like. Let's start by saying the line is extremely long, but I thought it was a good sign so the food is as good as everyone says.  Once seated, we start to get in line again!!! what??? I waited 15 minutes just to get to the crab legs, and oyster. It is all you can eat, but the oysters are just don't come out as fast which cause the long line. I was there mainly for oyster, but the oyster is actually the very last item in that seafood line, and after going for the 2nd time, I was tired and couldn't waited anymore. All the other food doesn't taste good at all, and the deserts look pretty but taste average. I was so excited going there, but I think I rather go to a place where is not much people. I did not get my money worth. Oh and, the crab legs taste horrible!!!

I believe this is the best dinner buffet in Vegas. The presentation is top notch, the variety is diverse yet hits many staples, they have everything from fresh seafood, to meat smoked onsite, to deli, sushi, vegetarian options... And an entire cheese bar. A CHEESE BAR. 
Eat your way around the world, and make sure you save some room for the multiple sections of desserts! 
Bravo, Ceasars.

Hands down best buffet in Las Vegas!!! Prime rib, crab, oysters and the best Mac and cheese filled our plates. We left full and satisfied. Thanks to the Manager on duty who was very helpful when we had a question. My kids went crazy over the dessert section. They always request this buffet when we take a trip to Vegas.

After reading all the great reviews I was really hoping for this buffet to be wonderful. We went on a weeknight and only waited about 35 mins to be seated at about 7:40 pm. We were walked to the back of the dark not very appealing dining room. Lines were very long but moving rather fast, seafood lines we're by far the longest lines. Warm crab legs were nicely split open but not that good, same with the blue claw crabs ok. Most of the dishes looked great but lacked flavor, also many items were over cooked and dry. The carved meats were good as was some of the Mexican dishes. Sushi was terrible, hardly any fish in it and very mushy. Cheeses were dry on the ends and turning color, nothing really stood out. The only reason I'm giving this a 3, is the service was great the staff kept coming to the table to clear away plates and bring drinks. Desserts on the other hand was very good, lots of selections and the gelato was great. Would not come back.

After hearing all the buzz about this place, I decided to check out what the hype is all about.  It was Sunday Brunch and we arrived around 1pm.  The line was loooooong but that was expected.  Once seated at the table, my husband and daughter decided to tackle the ONCE AGAIN LONG LINE at the meat carving station while I decided to tackle the shorter line at the seafood station since I was already starving at this point.   While chowing down on the SUPER SALTY crab legs, I wondered where my husband and daughter were since they still haven't sat down to eat with me.   It nearly took them 30 minutes standing in line at the meat carving station!!  By the time they joined me at the table, I was ready to sample the rest of the food.  I then walked all the way towards the back to the Asian section (by the way the flow of the buffet just doesn't make sense!) to maybe try some sushi or sashimi.   There weren't that many good sushi selections either that's all they has or they just don't replenish fast enough.   I decided to skip the Asian section and walk my way towards the front.  I wanted some cured meats and cheese, but yet again the Parmesan cheese was a whole big block -no shavings or pieces one would have easy access to.  I was looking around for a knife maybe I thought one had to shave the cheese off himself, but no tool was around!  I was really getting frustrated at this point, but I still decided not to give up and try the meat carving station.  I had wishful thinking that the line was going to be shorter this time than when my husband and daughter were here.  Needless to say, the line was not any faster but at this point this was my last resort the last station i want to try since they have Prime Rib - my favorite, so I patiently wait for my turn.  Finally I get Prime Rib with Au Jus on my plate and  FINALLY join my family at the table, to only find out they are ALREADY DONE EATING!  I don't blame them since I was gone for almost 30 minutes!!!   To top it all off, the Au Jus that soaked my Prime Rib was sooo salty that I could only eat 3 bites out of that meat!  I was enraged at this point that I didn't even care to try their desserts!    Not being able to eat at the same time with my family because of the ridiculously long lines at the food stations and to be fed salty dishes is just absurd!   All in all, Bachannal Buffet DOES NOT live up to the hype!   The food is so much better elsewhere!  You're better off going to The Wicked Spoon at The Cosmo or The Studio B Buffet at The M Resort.

I am not a big buffet person, but I had so many good things and since we were staying at Caesar's Palace, what the heck. I am so glad we decided to try it. We went for lunch and the lines were not bad and the food was fantastic. Great selection and a great value.

First off I'm not a huge buffet type person, but this place had me going back 2x now on separate Vegas trips. Definitely a must try and the long lines move pretty quickly.
I like the fact that you don't get the typical cold, soggy and overly salty crab legs they actually have a station that serves them up hot here. Dribble some drawn butter and bomb diggity!. Also the carving station offer more selections, lamb chops, prime rib, assorted sausages , turkey, ham and BBQ ribs. The dessert area was phenomenal so many choices!

Came in for dinner couple of days ago and I was so disappointed. My friends have been here and they said it was great. Everything was cold or closed, they definitely didn't have the 300 items that they advertised.There was virtually no seafood available and the wine was undrinkable. I am so angry at my experience here. After hearing good things and seeing the advertisements, I won't be recommending this to anyone that's for sure. What a waste

Without a doubt, the Bacchanal Buffet is one of the top buffets in town.  They are located at the middle of the Strip inside Caesar Palace.  The only nuisance thing about them was probably just the wait to get inside, even worse than many popular buffets in town.  There were literally two lines, one to get to the cashier, then another one to be seated.  One can skip the wait by being a high tier gambler with Total Rewards.

The cold dishes started near the entrance and ended with Asian dishes at the end.  I do not recall having a bad dish here.   The steamed snow crab is better than the cold one.  Most of the seafood served here were on the fresh side.  Sushi and Chinese foods were ok.  They have a noodle station with pho and ramen, and both of them were just ok.  The curved meats were quite delicious.  Desserts were always the best part of a buffet, as it helped push your stomach beyond the limits with attractive looking sweets placed in tiny shot glasses.

Price is about the same as any other seafood buffets on the Strip.  For buffet, it was probably as good as it gets in Vegas.  They definitely deserve a revisit in the future.

This review is for the breakfast.  Because I have had such a great experience with the dinner previously, I thought I should try the breakfast buffet.  I was really disappointed.  First, some of the items appeared to be stale or leftovers.  Second, the selection wasn't spectacular.  Even what I heard was one of the must try options (red velvet pancakes) was meh, ok.  For this price, my expectations are higher.  While I will return for dinner again, I will never ever have the breakfast there.  It's simply not that great, and not worth it.

Came here with my Girlfriend for a winter get away. Normally I'm a little weary of buffets, but this far blew away our expectations. All the food was succulent and we'll prepared. My favorite item was the ozzo bucco. So rich and decadent!
I have been to many Vegas buffet - cheap to most expensive ones. This place serves quality food. Rich seafood seafood selection and tons of meat options. I wish they had salad selection like wynne

My wife and I got food poisoning at the Bacchanal Buffet.  It was the only meal we had shared in days, and we both got sick at the same time - there is no question that it came from the buffet.  We were sick for days, and it was terrible.

However, I had no intention of leaving a bad review for the Bacchanal until after my miserable experience  dealing with Caesar's after we became ill.  After working my way through the bureaucracy to report the food poisoning issue, I was finally able to file a report with their on-staff EMT (who confirmed that my wife and my symptoms were textbook food poisoning) and was then transferred to the "risk management" department.  Ultimately, after multiple calls spanning over a week, risk management and the hotel refused to take any responsibility or offer any compensation (including refusing to refund the cost of the meal).  It was a terrible experience with what I had thought was a great hotel - I was wrong.  

I would highly recommend against eating here.  If you do, hopefully you don't get sick, because you certainly won't get any help from Caesar's if you do.
Best Buffet on the strip. The food is so yummy and the desserts are spectacular. It is worth the wait and the price.

Place is big,and has so much food.

Can't complain,much except the waitlist is like forever and its pretty pricey but has to be the best buffet in the area.

The waiters were pretty attentive, considering,some just sit,you down and,forget you exist because you paid already.

Everything,was hot,still,too.
Good experience, also love the decor

I would have given 4 stars for the food. The reason why I'm giving 2 is due to the lack of enforcement on checking to make sure people aren't cutting. (Why bother with setting up machines and issuing tickets when you guys don't even care if people are cutting the lines??)

Went on Christmas Day, I don't have a problem with waiting as that's expected on a holiday as such. It was busy and waits were long, that's fine. What I do have a problem with are the mainland Chinese people cutting in line and telling other Chinese people that it's ok to cut. I'm watching these people get tickets and then going straight in line when our family got our ticket around 10am for a return early afternoon. 

BTW, I'm Chinese myself and I have no effin tolerance for this type of bs and I'll call your ass right out!! (Sick and tired of these Chinese people coming here from abroad thinking they can bring their bad habits and not follow rules). Which me and my husband did to these ladies right behind us that somehow crossed over to the other side and paid before our eyes. Are you serious? Earlier on, there was a lady that was checking tickets before people got in, she specifically told them that they cannot get in line yet because they just got their tickets and needed to come back at a later time. Well, they still continued to wait in line and didn't get kicked out which i don't understand. (the check point lady saw them still waiting). 

When we got to the paying area, we told the employees and they looked confused and had no idea how it happened and just tried to bs their way out of trouble. I should have called on a manager, but I decided to let it go, at this point, we were all tired and hungry and just wanted to get seated and have a nice meal. 

If the bacchanal management team is reading this, you guys should really try to employ people who are competent at doing their job and checking to make sure people aren't cutting. When one person does this, it ruins it for many of us. I'm sure you wouldn't appreciate it if you were in my shoes.
Went here for Valentine's Day it was amazing!!! Every cuisine in one place. I recommend going here the service is amazing

Wow.. was waited the whole day in total of Three rounds! First was getting the ticket at the kiosk(30mins). Been told the actual checkin is scheduled at 4pm which is 6hours latter. Came back at 4 for the actual checkin(the second wait). The last Third wait was after confirming with the front desk to be sited..

This place is amazing! Super long line but it definitely worth the wait, so bring your appetite.  There's a medley of food options, but I'd say stick with the seafood area and the lamb.  All the Japanese and Chinese food towards the back area isn't really worth your time and neither is the pizza.  Stick with the meat cuts and you will be set.  The dessert bar is to die for as well so make sure you save room!

Bacchanal is pretty good for what it is.. a buffet. Don't come in here expecting the best food on the strip. The variety of food is pretty good and you can definitely get your money's worth. However, many dishes do lack a sort of uniqueness. I don't typically eat at buffets so I can't compare to any others on the strip. Food is good so I wouldn't mind coming again.

I heard this was the best buffet in Vegas so I had to check it out. I took a ticket for my party and came back when they called us 15 minutes later. The wait was not long at all.

There's a lot of food here but not everything was quality.  Looks are deceiving. 

I tasted a lot of the Asian food items and they were either bland or way too salty.

All I ate was king crab legs & oysters and that was worth the brunch price. These babies are normally expensive.

After being a little hung over, the pho there was magical and soothed my body and soul. lol 

They have a ton of desserts. I liked the green tea creme brulee, red bean & thai ice tea gelato the best. 

I would come back for the same things again.

DO NOT BELIEVE THE GOOD REVIEWS OF THIS PLACE. 

Either the buffet has plunged in quality or its extremely overhyped. 

First off let me just ask you a question. Have you ever been to Miami Beach or some other place with a lot of cranky old ladies? This place is staffed with a lot of those cranky old ladies. Rude cranky 70 year olds with an attitude problem. 

We showed up here at 8 am. The restaurant was empty. No lines. Maybe there were 20 ppl in the whole place. The cranky old lady hostess still made us wait at least 15 minutes to get seated. 

Strike no 1. 

Cranky old lady no 2 was our server, who definitely had an attitude problem and ignored us and took forever with drinks. 

Strike no 2. 

The final strike was the food. Maybe you have never had a great buffet. This is not a great buffet. I would gladly pay 130 bucks (two people) for a great buffet. This is more like a 60 dollar buffet maybe 80. For two ppl. The hot food was nothing better than you would get at a much cheaper buffet. The pork, chicken, beef dishes were all cold.  I can't even think of one dish that was memorable. There was nothing spectacular. The shrimp was okay, crab claws were nothing great. The desserts were absolutely atrocious.  I can get better gelato and cookies and bread pudding at Safeway. 

Don't make the same mistake we did. If this is the best buffet in Vegas there is no great buffet in Vegas.

So. much. yum.

First, I thought this was very reasonably priced for the breakfast buffet.  I think it came out to $25 each.  And we ate SO MUCH.  #fatties

The place is so big that I actually got lost at first and couldn't find the way back to our table.  There's so many different sections.  I actually got a little annoyed with my friend for taking the first things she saw.  Does she not know how to work a buffet?  You have to scan the whole place first to make sure you can fit all the good stuff in your stomach.  And there's a lot of good stuff.  So skip the typical items.  Go for the Thai dishes, the impeccable sweets, the fro-yo/ice cream, etc.  I can't imagine what they have for the dinner buffet!

Every station was kept well stocked and the employees were hard at work.  Servers were friendly as well.

My partner & I aren't really fans of a buffet & have only been a handful of times in the last several years. We were only doing a short trip to Vegas & thought we would include one of the well reviewed buffets. 

After having a quick look online to decide on a buffet, we selected this one. We had noted that there would be a long wait but I wish I had looked at that a little more before going. 

We are not rewards members or entitled to any sort of VIP access so just went through the normal line. We arrived just after 6pm, saw that it was $60 per person & got a ticket which told us the time to return for our "booking slot". The ticket said 8.35pm so we had to really fill in some time. 

There is a VIP option to skip the line, but that is an extra $55 per person! No way. $60 each is more than enough for this. 

When we return at 8.30pm, we join the line to pay & then the next line which is getting ready to be seated. We finally get to a table about 9.10pm so in total, it's been a 3 hour wait since we collected our ticket. 

For anyone planning on doing this buffet & just paying the normal price to get through the line, definitely have something planned to fill in the lengthy wait time. 

After we were seated, our waitress was good. Attentive & quick with the drinks & clearing plates etc. 

There is a good selection of different foods, from a multitude of cuisines but a bit hit & miss. Some of the Asian dishes were quite good, such as the chow mein & BBQ pork. Pizza was OK. Salads were drab. Carvery meat was OK. I'm not a fan of seafood but many other people were packing their plates with crab. They also have a taco bar which I didn't try & a number of other things. Overall, quite a good range of food but average quality overall. 

The desert bar was nice. The crepes & gelato were yummy so try to keep room for a bit of desert at the end. 

If the wait time had been more reasonable, I might have given four stars, but it's pretty nuts. My partner & I also prefer a sit down restaurant to a buffet anytime so I'll tend to be maybe a bit more critical of a buffet. 

All in all, if you enjoy buffets & account for the wait, you will probably enjoy this one. I think it's a little overpriced for what it is & probably would have preferred to spend the money at a better restaurant.  For me, it will be a once only visit but it does offer a large range of options, especially if you have fussy eaters in your group & a restaurant selection is difficult.

The biggest buffet I've ever seen. And the quality of the food is commendable. We kept finding new stuff every time we went to get food. Even as we were stuffed, and leaving, we were like WOW, never saw that! Did you know that was there too? Its that kind of place. Its A MUST TRY place in Vegas. Just don't go for brunch. I prefer lunch or dinner. More food, less money.

I went here for dinner on Saturday and I wasn't impressed. I've been during brunch in the past and it was worth the cost and it had the same food as dinner. Dinner was $56 a person and there is a two hour time limit. If you are thinking of going. Save your money and head over for brunch you'll get the same thing. Make sure you get the shaved ice with strawberry and condensed milk. BOMB.com
Excellent buffet breakfast, with so many choices. Best breakfast buffet I have had in Vegas so far.
Service was good! Food was good! The hot crab legs you gotta ask for behind the glass or you will miss it. Loved the deserts there and the southern food!

There is a reason why the wait can be long on some days. This is as good as it gets for a buffet. We've been here three times and can't stay away. The seafood is fresh and they always have a lot to choose from. The carving station is out of this world and the Chinese food is amazing! My wife loves the crepes for dessert. Every time we come back they seem to be adding more and more. We normally spend close to 2 hours here then feel terrible afterwards :)
Add this place to your to do list!

Four stars, for a buffet. Choice is spectacular. Quality of the food is ok - it's a buffet so you can't expect too much. It'll never be as good as a decent regular  restaurant, but if it is variety you are looking for, this is one of the best in Vegas...

This place is over-rated.
I won't go into too much details but will pin point some areas that can be improved. 

1) King Crab legs - they looked like they are Mal-nutrition and they are kinda dirty. 

2) Small individual dishes - Yes they do look cute and all, but the problem is since the food are placed on individual dishes, it's hard to keep them warm. Most dished that I've tried are cold. 

3) A lot of the dishes are on the salty side.

4) Service is pretty slow, we waited about 15mins to order our drinks.

5) Salt and Pepper shakers (on the table). I've never seen a pepper shaker with holes smaller then the peppers inside. 

The only thing we're impressed of is the desserts bar. A lot of varieties and they all look and taste good. For $44.99 on a weekday dinner, there are better buffets out there. I rather go to the Seafood buffet at Rio.

Posting an updated review.  Initially had some issues however the manager contacted me and made it right.  I went back this week and wow.... fantastic food, great service, and it means a lot when a manager reaches out in response to feedback to make things right.  I will happily recommend and keep going back often!

Came straight here for lunch after driving for hours from Los Angeles, so my group arrived with an appetite.  We were in line at about 12:30 p.m. and the wait was 10 mins or so.  Not bad at all.  The food had its ups and downs.

Good:
- The shrimp dumplings were good, along with the other dim sum options
- Korean short-ribs.  Yes.
- The nachos plate was good, but had to be picked up during release as they go fast
- Dessert was great.  I had tiramisu, flan, and crème brulee.

Bad:
- Avoid the sushi, the rice is gross.  It tasted day-old.
- The sliders beef was borderline rare, which was a shame for people like me who prefer medium well
- The oysters were grainy.  I think they were being chucked with too little care.

This is an above average buffet at most.  I'm going to try another buffet during my next Vegas visit.

Buyer BEWARE: I decided to have dinner there on Sunday night and had the most horrible experience at a strip hotel yet. I noticed that my bill was quite a bit higher than I was expecting to be charged... $10 higher!! I asked the agent "Chona" why it was more expensive this time since the last time I was there wasn't that long ago. Thinking that they might have broadened there selections or something to warrant an almost 20% increase I was rudely told that I was mistaken and told this has always been the price. Really!! So I asked the manager "Ira Greene to please educate his staff as to what is true and false about the pricing and what warrants this rate hike. He rudely argued with me stating that I was correct in the increase of price but continued to say that I shouldn't expect to pay the same price at all times. He had no answer for what warranted the increase other than different time different price. Sad!!! I'm assuming that from the other reviews I've read lately that the other difference that I'm paying more for is a reduction in quality and freshness.. I'll never go back to this establishment... Actually I'll never go back to any Caesars entertainment run facility. Now I can better see why they are in the predicament they're in!

Service is good. Food is not great..king crab legs are too salty. meat portion is too big (should be smaller so people can try more different things with less food wasted) dessert is good. Overall it's a bit overpriced in terms of quality of food. and the interior design is like a food court..also..AC is too cold.
Quality of food was not as good as 2yrs ago. Tropical drinks, braised beef and seafood were great. Overall had a good time but for these prices this l won't be my go to next time I'm in town

We had brunch here for the first time and it was a great experience. Food was good quality and lots of variety. The best part was the fresh Gelato at the desert bar. Line was pretty long but very worth it! Overall it made me wanna come back and try there dinner!
MARTA was rude to my whole group of 7. She needs a new job because her customer service skills are horrible. I don't care how busy it is, customer service needs to be on point in any situation

Sadly I can't blame the experience based on wait, there wasn't one. From the start the cashiers looked as if we were bothering them. During my transaction I was left standing there wondering what I was waiting for only to be told upon the return of Karen P that I could go wait in the cue. Thank you for the info Karen. I then Learned that my addition of drinks was not added. Glad now since our attendant that was already tipped before we sat down was less than motivated to provide drinks, refills etc. I had to request several times that the dirty plates be removed and were now being stacked at the table. The food was ok, but there are much better options for a better price. $63/person is no problem for me, but for less than meh experience I could have received a better meal at the run down Denny's down the road. Oh the venue is nice and is what received the 1 star.

Got in line at 8:30, got a table at almost 10. $120 for two people. We paid $15 extra for the all you can drink beer, which is supposed to be for 2 hours but they close at 11 and our waiter definitely rushed us out. He brought the check at probably 10:30 when we both had full plates of food and were ready to order our second drinks. The food varied from basic, mediocre buffet food to excellent. My boyfriend said the seafood was amazing. The desserts were definitely awesome, except the cakes were very dry. There's a massively overwhelming selection of food, but for most of it I expected slightly better quality for the price. Would probably try a different buffet on the strip next time and hope for better service.

Not impressed. Plating wasn't what I had expected and the flavors of the food were not really a "I will have to come back flavors" the Italian selection was very poor to me since they had different types of cold cuts and pizza and one or two different pasta dishes. What I loved however was the Mexican salsas, they were great! As far as the "American food" I found it tasteless as well as the deserts. not to mention my colleague got sick from the sushi. Also, we had a waiter come bring drinks once and that was pretty much it, never saw him again in the whole time we were there. I would not call it the best buffet in the USA or even Las Vegas. I still think that The Wicket Spoon is on top of the list!

The only reason I'm giving them such a low rating is because of the wait time. It was horrible. We were in line for over 3 hours. First we had to sign up to actually stand in line. Once that time was over we had to stand in line to pay. Then we had to stand in line to be seated. The only reason we were seated before the people in front of us was because we agreed to share a table with strangers. After we got inside, we noticed we had to stand in line just to get food. Although, the food was delicious, the price was not worth the wait unless you're patient and have time to kill in Vegas. Admittedly, we went during a busy time of the year. But personally I believe there are better buffets in Vegas.

HONESTLY, do not go here if you are on a diet!!! Dieter's worst nightmare. They have such a huge selection and I can see why the lines are so long. It was $65 a person which is a costly but once you go in and see endless buffet, it's worth it. For a buffet that makes food in large quantity, the quality wasn't as bad as I thought. I'm really glad we came to try it! They have so many different types of food from different parts of the world.

It's a great buffet, don't get me wrong, but it's just overhyped. The Prime rib was great, and the seafood selection was great, but all the other food was just meh. It's a great buffet overall, but not worth the ridiculous price. For the money you could eat at a really good restaurant and order as much as you want, and the food quality would be better.

This is still the best buffet in town.  It has gone down a bit since it first opened but it is another level better than Bellagio or Wynn or Wicked Spoon.  If you only had one Vegas buffet, this would be the one you have to try.

One of the buffets I visited in Vegas. I had high hopes for this buffet, since it's been hyped up so much! I asked the cashier if they had plenty of vegan options. They asked me if I wanted to talk to one of the chefs while she shows me around the buffet, which I thought was pretty cool of them to offer. From what I saw, they did have some vegan options. So my friend and I decided to go for it and have lunch at Bacchanal. Just to try it out for the experience. 

In my opinion, it's not the best buffet for vegans. I felt pretty limited even though they did have some vegan options. The options weren't as great compared to The Buffet at Wynn. They had veggie sushi rolls, but the rolls were sloppy-looking. We're talking about simple veggie sushi rolls here. How can anyone mess this one up? Lol. I usually like edamame beans, but the ones at Bacchanal tasted weird. They had lots of desserts, but no vegan desserts. They had fruit (watermelon, pineapple, cantaloupe, honeydew, strawberries). I didn't find them to be 'fresh'. Some of the strawberries tasted off and were mushy. One food item was labeled vegan. They were the crudités with vegan ranch. Dear goodness, it was the most awful tasting vegan ranch that landed in my mouth. I couldn't stomach it. 

Overall, I thought Bacchanal was pretty average for what they charge. Wow, I don't even remember who our waitress was. Oh well. I don't plan on coming back to this buffet in the near future. It's not worth the hype or price. So overrated!

This was great! We went about 2or3 in afternoon- it was recommended to go at this time (smaller crowd). They had different ethnicities of food and a station dedicated to desserts. Bit pricey, true- but you truly get what you paid for- great service (for drinks) and awesome food... as much as you want!
Very mediocre for the price. Probably would not recommend going here when there's other restaurants that offer much better food at a similar price

This place rocks!  17 million dollars spent making this the best buffet on the strip.  I used to joke about Sleazars Palace and the sorry buffet they had called Lago.  

NO MORE!!!  OH my gosh, I am in heaven after eating here.  This is the gold standards of all buffets.  It's a bit pricier but you will know it's for better quality food.  Everything about this place has been redesigned.

Sometimes the line is a bit longer but well worth the wait.  There is only a couple of issues i had with the place.  The music a bit too loud.  Why do you dim the lights so dark for dinner?  Too much salt on your St Louis ribs.  Too much salt on some of the dishes.

The seafood station rocks.  Fresh king crab legs.  Delicious fried chicken.  Great chow mein noodles (a lot of buffets gets this dish wrong).  The Chinese spare ribs are the bomb.  Just like how my mom used to make them.  Noodle station could use some work.  I didn't like the Pho that much and the Udon was so-so.  Maybe you can fix that for me?

I wish I had more time to try this place for breakfast.  My love for buffets has been   rekindled.  Thank you so much Caesars!  Finally, you have a buffet worthy of your casino (the one that Celine built).  You heard our cries for good food and got rid of that Lago. 

We got great service from William.  The dessert bar was out of this world.  Great red velvet cakes, cookies, carrot cake, creps, ice cream, sorbet.  Everything here just looks so good.

Definitely my favorite buffet in Vegas! I HAVE to eat here every time I'm there. Seriously. You check in at the kiosk and they give you an estimated waiting time. It takes about 45 minutes to an hour, depending on what time you go. Last time I was here, not even 10 minutes and I already got to check in with the host. After you check in with the host, you have to wait in line to pay then wait in line again to get seated. The best time to come here is a little before 3pm on the weekend. You pay brunch price and after it hits 3pm, dinner food comes out. How perf is that!

There are soo many food and dessert options! The crab legs and street tacos are the best. Their dessert options include gelato, tarts, crepes, Thai tea boba sundae. What! Bomb. & more.
They have a good variety of Asian, American, and Latin food and you can even get pho or ramen for your hangover! They even had elote this time =') The meat and seafood section is good too. They also have horchata and other types of juice in these mini cute bottles. 

The price is worth it. I will never get tired of this buffet. Bacchanal, you the one!!

Wow, just wow! This was the only buffet on my list that I had to try while we were here. This place didn't exist the last time I came to Vegas, so Bellagio was all the rave back then, now it doesn't even compare. A bit pricey but well worth it. I read that the lines can get very long but we went on Thur night around 5:45 for dinner and no wait at all. 

The spread is huge and has got something for everyone. Whether it's Asian, meats, Italian, seafood, desserts etc...you're covered. Sometimes Asian cuisine takes a backseat at buffets but I have to say they did a decent job with it - they even have a small variety of dim sum options. They have a nice selection at the carving station and a big plus is the option to get your king crab legs warm or cold - it's usually one or the other only. And I love the personal serving sizes of some of the food options - my favorite was the calamari, sooo good!

If you've got a sweet tooth, oh man you're in for a treat. The dessert station is a dentist's nightmare. The service was very efficient and friendly. Plates cleared and glasses filled quickly. We ordered hot tea and it came with your very own personal jar of honey! I wish I had more room, so many things I wanted to try but just had no belly space for. Overall, the place is well worth the $60 (tax  included) and I'd def come back when I visit again.

I hardly want to put review as matter affect this probably the first 1. This was our favorite buffet place as been here many times but this time 3 of 4 of us got food poisoning. Only 1 of kid didn't as he only eat salami and rice. Really bad experience as spending over $150 and suffer for this.
Management, you have to focus more on your food quality.

I still think I prefer the Studio B buffet over at the M hotel, just cuz it's quite the hefty price to pay around $40-50 each time I've been here. The first time I went was during the weekend during brunch. The food was quite impressive then. The second time, however, not so much. Though that last time, I came on a Thursday night. Seems to me they're not entirely consistent. The wait for this buffet is pretty ridiculous!
Lots of choices for foods! Dim Sum tastes good . You can eat the crab legs cold or warm, that's very nice. Love the fresh juicy. Bad thing is that wait for a while to get in.

Good selection of items. They Have A Minimum of 300 Items at any given time. You might not get to try all the items haha...it's definitely worth the visit.
The CUCUMBER juice is must try but it is only available till 11 am
If you got sweet tooth, save space for dessert ;)

This place was one of those once in a lifetime got to spend and eat your heart out on a buffet type experiences. No line or reservation needed on a Saturday night which was awesome and totally not expected but this was not a busy time of year, price of entry steep but that comes with the territory. Started off with the seafood section, tons of clams, raw shrimp and oysters. Oysters were a bit tired looking but they soon refilled with some winners. The crab legs were abundant and some serious meat on them, not your generic buffet legs, very happy so far. The lull occurred while checking out the meats section, the whole pig was a bit dry and the prime rib a little over done but thats OK. The asian section was full of some interesting dishes, some dim sum, congee and fried rice all good stuff. Next highlight was the staff, our server was like a ninja, the second a plate was done it disappeared within seconds, truly high end, something other places should learn from. Last course of dessert, although not my fav but that my preference, if you have a sweet tooth the dessert section was massive and beautifully presented. The table next to us kept getting more of the small bites, taking pictures and devouring plate after plate. I enjoyed the egg custard and some flan but there are easily over 100 options on the dessert bar including a crepe station. Parents watch your kids here they will go into a sugar coma instantly. All in all a world class buffet, only wish is that there was lobster available, it was in the case upon arrival but nowhere to be found inside.

This is definitely the highest hyped Buffet in all of Las Vegas, and for good reason. At almost $65/head and long lines, you better be ready mentally and physically. There are hundreds of different options for food, all which resemble a fancy private university dining hall. My favorite was definitely the Angus steak along with the crab legs, although they were a bit small. The worst thing about this place was how consistently crowded it was, from the lines for food to the slow waiters. There is always a line out the door to limit the crowd in the actual restaurant.

Bacchanal Buffet is the epitome of jack-of-all-trades, master of none. It certainly is superior to Wicked Spoon, which I tried two years ago, but it isn't a major improvement over the other popular Vegas buffet.

Bacchanal Buffet is a value considering everything you get--snow crab legs and stone crab claws, Asian noodle soup station, raw oysters, charcuterie, beautiful pastries, bone marrow, pork belly, fancy takes on french fries, and so on. A meal for two, plus tip, will set you back around $140. Then again, you could spend about the same for much less, easily, on the Strip.

For me, I found that I was happiest when I stuck with creamy dishes, carbs, and desserts. For example, the truffle scalloped potatoes was divine. Also loved their gemelli pasta in a rich, white sauce. And all the mini cakes, tarts, and cakes were well executed. Sadly, these are the kinds of items that fill you up way too quickly.

I got all excited seeing their cooked seafood selection, like their coconut curry clams. They also had one or two cooked mussels dishes. Unfortunately, these shellfish dishes all consisted of overcooked, chewy molluscs. Nooooooooooo. Their raw oysters were okay, not that sweet, but hey, it's buffet.

My husband tried some of their meat offerings, including their pork belly, and he said it was way too lean for pork belly. Where's the decadence? Also, the mini burger was more fitting of something in the kids' section of family-style restaurant's menu than an upscale buffet.

Neither of us tried the stone or snow crab, but it seems like you can definitely get your money's worth eating just those two items.

Overall, a decent buffet place on the Strip, but hardly extraordinary.

3.5

Pros: A monster selection of different types of foods ranging from BBQ, Italian, American, Asian, and more. Every item I had was either good or great. They also had fresh squeezed juices from orange to cucumber. Knocks out the Wynn Buffet as the Undisputed King of Buffet in LV.
Cons: The wait, but you can expect wait at all buffets in LV these days.
Overall: New undisputed champion of buffets in LV.

My father and I came here right at the end of lunch service on a weekday and paid around $35/person to get in and stayed for dinner (saving money). The place is well decorated, but not gaudy. It has a more modern, restaurant feel to it rather than a buffet. There are 9 stations each with different styles/ethnic food (i.e. Mexican,Chinese, American, & Italian) and a big island of dessert. The staff were attentive and nice, and plates were cleared out very quickly. But on to the food.

I think the buffet tries to bring a more foodie sense of eating to diners through their variety and offers. Do not expect there to be king crab leg on a weekday as they only serve split snow crab legs. There are 3-4 selections of shooters (soups in shot glasses), all of which were pretty good. The raw oysters are decently fresh, but usually hacked up due to the speed at which they're prepared (they go fast, so once you see them putting the oysters out you should go for it).

(GOOD)
The prime rib was decent and the cuts were very large. The lamb lollipops were good, with every piece I got coming out to medium-rare/rare (you should tell them how you want it so they can find the piece that's closest to that temp). They brought out a thing called a "veal ship" later in the service which was good too, but at that point I was going to explode. The sweet potato fries and tater tots were very good (though greasy) and were probably one of the best things at the buffet. There's a thing called the "chef special" which was scallop that day, which was very good as well. The cheese and charcuterie are decent for a buffet, the salad line is pretty extensive, and there is a dedicated bread section too.

(BAD)
The Asian line should be completely avoided. Everything there was bad, including the hot and sour soup, which my father commented on as containing "nothing but corn starch". The sushi was "meh", as expected. The fish dishes were consistently overcooked and dried out so I didn't even try them. I avoided the Mexican and Italian stands as there were a lot of carbs there, pasta is almost 99.9% going to be mediocre-bad at a buffet, and I'm from Texas so I've had great Tex-Mex & authentic Mexican food already (no point in trying something I know will disappoint).

(GREAT)
Save. Room. For. Dessert. Between plates of other food I'd stop by the dessert station to grab a couple sweet treats and bring them back to the table and we still couldn't get through it all. There is a station that makes crepes to order (and you get to put on your own fillings/toppings), there're macarons, many tiny dessert plates, and a dedicated ice cream,sorbet, and mochi ice cream bar. Honestly the dessert bar is better than more than half the stations in the buffet.

This buffet was good, but very pricey. I'd probably come here after winning big at the tables or for a celebration, but that's about it. I hinted to it at the beginning of the review, but it's more worth it to come near the end of lunch and get in at lunch prices for dinner. You simply graze a bit while you wait for them to shift gears. And just a tip, the lamb lollipops, veal ship, and other dinner menu items came out later at around 5-6 so don't think that what they have at 3:30 is the only thing they have for dinner.

For some reason I expected a lot more from this buffet, may be all the hype set my expectations higher. There is a ton of choice and the food was great but lacks in service, we asked for water some 10 times and got one refill. Also, they try to make you add the tip to the bill when you check in, I really don't like the idea because I want to be able to tip based on the service. The service we got really did not deserve even a dollar in tip. The buffet is pricy, to really make up for the price and the hour wait to get in ...  you better be really hungry :).

Went here on a Thursday for lunch, had to wait 15 min to get seated.It was about $100 for 2 adults 1 child. They say this is the best Buffet in vegas so I had to try it. They have alot of dessert to choose from. They have all sorts of foods from Tacos,Sushi,Pizza,Fish,Ribs,Pasta. I would reccomend this place to Yelpers.This is the best review buffet in vegas.The sushi was great the service was great.Pizza tasted good and so did the fish. Give it a try you will love it.

By far my favorite buffet on the strip. I loved their Japanese section where they had really fresh sashimi and sushi. Their carving station and their seafood section was top notch. I'll have to say, I'm not much of a sweets fan but their dessert section was pretty impressive. We went on a weekday for dinner and it was still on the pricey side but it was sooooo worth it. I would love to go back if I ever have the chance.

Best buffet in Vegas.  It's what other buffets want to be when they grow up.

I went on a Saturday around 11 AM.  It was $44.31 with tax, so it's pricey.  But, well worth it.  I have been to all of the major buffets in town (save the M Resort), and this is the best.  There are the standard ethnic stations, but the carving area was massive.  Fantastic meats off the bone and artisan sausages.  The chicken jalapeno was the winner here.  Service was very attentive as well, which is an issue at a lot of buffets.  Our tea and water glasses never were close to empty, and plates were removed very promptly.  

If any area is lacking, it's the desserts.  This area was standard and not nearly as overwhelming as the main stations.  But, the bacon balsamic sorbet was a definite repeat.

The best dish I have eaten at ANY buffet was the truffled scalloped potatoes.  I would gladly pay $25 for this dish at a steakhouse.  It was very thinly sliced potatoes and an excellent sauce, combined with excellent truffle flavor.  Had a nice crunchy top.  And, you get your own small portion, something a few buffets here are doing now.  It's a good trend.

The line went very quickly too, and that's an issue with a lot of places in town.  It was well organized and the employees were smart and courteous.  Definite repeat.

WOW!!!  Expensive for a buffet, but well worth the price.  Crab legs looked good,but as I prefer mine hot, I passed.  Apparently there are Italian and Chinese options available, but I got sidetracked by the prime rib and a GIANT FREAKING MEAT AXE!!  I love ribeye, and with the bone-in, it is delightful.  This giant steak had a good foot long rib bone to use as a handle.  Wonderfully rare and tender, I want one now, just writing about it.  The best part was my then unmarried wife and a female friend of ours also partaking of the giant whole ribeye, and watching several men in line hang their heads in shame.  I was so proud.  This is a must-visit venue.

When a buffet at Vegas can maintain a 4 star rating. That's good enough for me to come back. As of 2015 this is my all time fave buffet. It's BETTER than "fill in the blank".

Wicked spoon
Wynn's Buffet
Bellagio's Buffet
M buffet (good value tho)
Mirages Cravings (great value)
Circus circus (for damn sure)
MGM Grand's Buffet

Take your chances but Caesars is the best if you can afford it. Please let me know if you find something better.

YEAH THIS IS GONNA BE A NO 
I have to say that I have had many of buffets in Vegas, but this is by far the worse of them all! We pay the 100+ dollars to eat and wait to be seated.  When it was time to be seated the waitress walked us around the whole seating area ( tables were empty as we passed) and seated us in the far back.  We get up to see what they have to offer to eat.   As we get our plates we pass by the carving station( the meats)  As soon I smelled the meat it turned my stomach to the point I lost my appetite.  I got a few crab legs and to my surprise they were still frozen solid.  My husband got a few lamb chops, and they were tender but really STOP with all the fancy seasoning. It killed the taste.  The prime rib wasn't anything special.  As for the ribs, well they looked good and for my husband to say I cook ribs better is a statement.  We are cooks ourselves and know food, and if you really want just ok food then by all means spend over 100 dollars for two people and have at it.  I won't be going back here.  You would be better off spending the 100+ on a rental ar and finding a better one off the strip.

The Express Text system is an absolute joke and the cattle call aspect of the experience isn't worth the wait. The kiosk stated 45-55 minute wait when we checked in. We received a text 15 minutes later to return and get in line. After another 30-40 minutes of waiting, we had moved half way through the line to pay. There was at least another 30-minute wait to pay with a larger line in front of it to get in the dining room. 

Seeing that this was a 2-hour plus line, we left and found another option. The Express Text is advertised as eliminating the inconvenience of waiting in line. It should work like the Fast Pass at Disneyland (to keep patrons shopping and gambling), but instead does little to alleviate the line and instead causes extreme frustration. I sent Caesar's an email with this feedback and received a generic response a week later stating they don't directly respond to this type of feedback but have passed it on to the appropriate people. What a disappointment and reason to avoid Caesar's. 

The popularity of the buffet is proving to be its Achilles heal. I will be avoiding until they do something to address the issues.

Ate here in October 2017. Waited for over 2 hours which I guess is the norm judging from previous reviews. Once we got in at around 9pm it was hard to figure out what I was going to eat as I was soo hungry.  The is definitely lots of variety to choose from you don't know where to start.  The dessert bar was great.  Best to come early.

This buffet was huge and expensive. Lunch for two was $108 and a hour and a half wait in line. Once you finally get in there's more food than you can shake a stick at.  Chinese, sushi, seafood, steak, Italian, Mexican, salad bar, and dessert station.

I've been to this buffet multiple times and have yet to be disappointed! Worth every penny. It is one of the more expensive buffets on the strip but as they say "you get what you pay for." I have experienced  both the breakfast and dinner menu. Both were unbelievable. I have never been to a breakfast buffet that served seafood and roasted meats! The deserts were divine. I absolutely loved the street tacos and the large array of cheeses. Oh, and let me not mention the pho! Everything I put in my mouth was delicious. I have to say that this is one of my favorite buffets on the strip. The one thing that does suck is that they don't have a locals' discount.
Umm YUM!!! We stop here for dinner every time we come to Vegas. The selection and quality of food is to die for!

High quality buffet and the price is worth it. You get what you pay for. A must when visiting Vegas. There are tons of options. Some basics like Mac and cheeses, mashed potatoes and gravy ( which are done well) to outstanding options like king crab legs, Chilean sea bass and my personal fav, the lamb chops. Great flavor and cooked to perfection. There was ceviche,  pallela, mussels, clams, Thai food, sushi, cheese, charcuterie, soups, salads, pastas, pork belly. Be sure to pace yourself and share so you can try more. We arrived at 2:30 so we paid the lunch price and stayed into dinner which starts at 3pm. We went on a slower weekday and it wasn't too busy so the turn around was a little slow. A few things were dried out on the buffet line such as the burgers. Although we were seated right away. I knocked a star off for some flaws in the service. My silverware was dirty so I had to ask for new ones and our server seemed a little overwhelmed. He messed up our drink orders a couple times. But the food was satisfying and delicious. Tons of options. Too many to try in just one visit. Make sure to leave room for dessert. They were amazing. Mini options of anything you can think of. Cheesecake, carrot cake, key lime...the list goes on and on. We will definitely make this a must go on every trip we make to Vegas.

The buffet offered a great variety of cuisines and dishes but most of them were grossly underseasoned.  The sliders had no taste whatsoever, nor did the brisket.  The cold shrimp on the buffet tasted old and were slightly slimy.  After trying 2 of them I was so turned off I couldn't eat anything else.  There were some great dishes like the beef lasagna, the pork dumplings, and the carne asada tacos.  I've heard great things about the buffet and am glad I tried it, but I won't go back on future visits.

One of the better buffets.  I wanted to eat a late lunch early dinner so was planning on going at 2 and maybe wait 1/2 an hour and get in.  Nope.  Even at 2pm on a Saturday, we were told to check in at the computer and come back in 90 min.  The check in process was pain less.  Entered my cell phone number and got a text on when to come back.  Came back and waited another 20 min to pay and get a table.  
The oysters were pretty fresh but everyone takes it so sometimes there isn't much to choose from.  The crab legs weren't as meaty but cut so it is easy to eat.  You can get it warm by the noodle section which was good, don't like cold crabs.  I was surprise the flavor of the dishes were good for a buffet.  Even like the roasted duck and cha sui flavors were almost there.  Some spice not there like authentic Chinese places but better than anything outside of San Gabriel Valley.  Prime rib was good and lamb chop was one of the best I've had, medium would have been nice though, a little over cooked.
Sushi was very thin and no just fish.
The little bottles of juice you can get was ok, nothing to rave about, but nice idea.  But I was happy with my pineapple juice at my table.
I was so full, I was not able to try everything, which says a lot because I always make room to try everything.
We sat next to the dessert station and it was great.  They were constantly refilling the plates.  I never saw the chef stop working at the dessert station.  Noteable was the flan, very creamy.  Macaroons were too chewy.  Gelato was a little too sweet.  They had a lot of green tea flavored items which was nice.  Tried maybe 4 rounds of dessert but that was not all.  Just could not get myself to fit any more.  
Lots of variety.  Good overall flavor to the food.  Prepare to wait a bit.  
I wanted the bottomless champagne but missed it due to the wait so had to take 1 star away.  On the weekends, they have bottomless for brunch/lunch.

Sunday night in mid December...wait time until we sat down was 55min. Price was at least $51 per adult for the weekend pricing dinner. 18% gratuity added for big groups so split up if you have a big group. They tend to sit people chronologically in line in the same section anyway. 
Entrees are lined up against the wall with desserts in the middle of the room. Felt like the ac was on (in Dec) and was too cold for me being under the vent so don't sit by the walls if you get cold easily.
Food was ok, better than most average buffets I've been to. Tri tip was perfect! Clam chowder too salty for me. Sliders were dry. Wasn't a fan of the cake pops-very mushy inside instead of cakey like I'm used to. LOVED the chocolate covered strawberries! I don't eat oysters, but everyone kept going back for more. More sushi options would've been nice. Horchata!!-Even some Mexican restaurants don't have this drink.

Amazing selection. I went twice for lunch once and for breakfast another time. Roughly $55 for lunch $30 for breakfast. The seafood was really good. The choices of meats were good. All in all everything about it was great. And don't forget to try their desserts!!!!! Loved it.

2.5 stars.
This is a make you feel sick kind of dining.  We're not big eaters but decided on our last evening to try this buffet because we had heard a lot about it.  It cost $108 for 2 of us.  There was so much food, and mind you, not great tasting food, just a lot of food.  The key is to arrive early. We checked in about 5:15PM for dinner. They told us it will be jammed by 6PM, it didn't get really crowded until 7PM.  

Our server, Felicity, was really nice and constantly checked back to see if we needed anything.  The only seafood think I liked was the crab legs which tasted pretty good. The oysters on a 1/2 shell, rock crab, shrimp, were all bland. 
The shooters were OK.

They gave me an end piece of rib roast and it was dry, even with the au jus, it didn't taste very good. The fried chicken was very cute in a metal basket with a quarter of a waffle but both were dried out tasting.  The fried pork skins were pretty crunchy.  
I skipped the pastas and pizza area. Had a slice of mortadella, cheese and headed to the Chinese food which was awful.  The oxtail broth was good but everything else - chow mein, shrimp har gow, egg roll, were not good.  Even worse were the sushi - sticky, starchy rice and flavorless.

The only salvation was dessert which were really good. They even have a sugarfree section. Hubby didn't know he picked up a slice of sugarfree apple pie and said it had an after taste.  The choc cake pop was excellent as well as a slice of the pandan cake.  

Hubby ate so much,  to get his money's worth and had to go back to the room to lie down.  He said Bacchanal saved us money because he was going to head off to gamble and ended up trying to sleep off the gluttonous meal.  I couldn't believe it when I saw this skinny young adult woman go back and forth to the buffet and ate about 6 plates or more of food. The entertainment of watching humans with bottomless pits is amazing.  The portly woman next to us went back to the dessert table twice, before finishing her 1st selections and came back giggling to her husband who was appalled that she brought back so much dessert.

OMG... this place is my new fave buffet... the line is ridiculous, but then again we didn't have to wait 2 hours to get IN... We went on Monday night around 6:30pm.  The line to pay was fast moving so we waited about 45 min.  There's also another line to be seated, so beware of the additional wait.  We paid $45.99 for the dinner buffet. If you have the total rewards players card, it's $44.99, yeah I know an EFFing dollar off... so LAME!! BUT, what we paid was worth it... here's what you get... 
crab legs, oysters on half shell, rib eye steak, lamb chops, prime rib, sausages, oyster shooters, lobster corn chowder, huge shrimps (the kind you get in a shrimp cocktail), craw fish, chinese food galore, 5 different kinds of soups, including asian style chicken soup, mexican food, weird little gourmet food, and much much MORE...  the dessert bar is CRAZY amazing too... MAKE SURE TO GET UR SOUFFLE ORDER IN... YES they even have soufflés ...  the service is excellent. EXCELLENT!! BTW, park towards the front of the casino. If you park near the mall,  you'll have to do some walking, the buffet is near the front lobby of the caesar's hotel, NOT nobu hotel.  If you love buffets like I do, you'll love this place.  I heard there was a front of the line pass for $25pp, but not sure cuz our total wait time was about an hour, still with an hour wait time for paying and being seated, it was worth it... if you're not a buffet fan, you should at least try it ONCE... There are some foods that are single plated, which I thought was cute, but it does fill ur plate up quick, so plan on having multiple plates at ur table... LOLz... NO JOKE!!

Overpriced. Poorly made food by poorly trained chefs. My wife and I both got sick after eating here. No regard for sanitation. Based on other reviews, which mentioned food poisoning, I should have known not to come here.

Just your average Las Vegas buffet. Nothing really stood out as being great. There were plenty of options to choose from. Staff was friendly. Buffet was maintained well and dining area was very clean.

I was really excited to try the buffet at Caesar's after hearing and reading so many rave reviews about it. 

I think the $35 price (if you have a casino rewards card) is right on point as it really is an amazing buffet offering a vast array of dishes.  However, I'm only giving it 3 stars cuz well alot of the dishes weren't really all that great tasting.  The presentation is beautiful and the service top notch but several of the dishes I tried were either overcooked or rather bland, especially the "American" dishes.

The best section was by far the Asian dishes -- these were all standouts IMHO including the dim sum and the noodle dishes. The dessert bar was also good but a few of the desserts I tried were just kinda meh. The gelato on the other hand was outta this world --- a definite MUST try. 

Just as a point of reference.. we went at 1:30 and there was NO line. When we came out the line was crazy long so it seems like this a good time to come if you want to avoid the crazy crowds.

I had high hopes for this Buffet. We attended for Sunday brunch. There was a good variety of food but the quality was only ok. I found much of it was cold, any pastry was hard or dry, and the desserts were down right disappointing. Maybe if it were dinner it would have been different. I would probably pass on this and go back to the Bellagio if I wanted a buffet.

I have tried most of the known buffets in Vegas and I would rate this one #1 (for brunch) as of yesterday. First of all, you don't have to wait in a long line like all other places. You just go up to a kiosk, sign in and they text you when your table is ready. So I decided to play some electronic black jack at the bar near by drinking my bloody mary. Our table was ready within 30 minutes at one of the craziest hours. 

I started off at the Asian section and worked by way through every dish, not wanting to miss out on any. Then I realized I did it all wrong! Make sure you start at the seafood section and try their hot crab legs! AMAZING. They also have another section where the guy cuts the meat. Unfortunately, I was way too full to stuff more meat down my throat so I passed on that. They also have a little juice section. Make sure to try the guava and horchata. They were great because it wasn't too sweet.

Finally, their desserts are mouthwatering good. I grabbed at least half of the selections they offered. All of them were so tasty, especially the mango pudding and chocolate chip cookie. I'm SO torn that I haven't tried this place before, but I'm definitely revisiting here on my next Vegas trip.

Great buffet delicious food we came for lunch around 1.30 on a Tuesday waited 10 mins and got seated   There is a 2 hour limit but I didn't see anyone push to get you out try a little of everything and pace yourself make sure you go into the back for the Chinese and Italian dishes it's a great deal for the money you will be stuffed !
慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢慢啊！啊，（ーー；） ing李敏1哦所以你你咋去搜个1XP啊！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！？！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！！？！

We waited until easter to try this buffet thinking it would be even bigger and better than on a normal day. We are frequent buffet people, eating at many of the buffets in vegas,  mostly the one at the wynn. Anyway, it was $75 per person without the liquor package. The liquor package was an additional $22. This buffet was very impressive to the eye. So many different types of food. Something for everyone. Not sure what happened but almost everything we ate was dry. The brisket, pork, lamb, even the oysters were so dry! Lamb was over seasoned and salty. Meatballs were dry. Fish and chips,  fish was dry,  the fries were soggy. Bbq chinese pork was great. The sushi I had was good. Large choice of side items. I didn't have many because i was focused on finding something as my main course. Pretty good assortment of desserts. All in all, we were very disappointed and felt pretty upset that we paid so much for this buffet. We won't be back and definitely won't recommend it to anyone.

As far as buffets go this was a great one.

The food was very good and had a large variety to choice from compared to other buffets on the strip. The presentation of the food was better than most and showed their efforts to make things a little nicer than your run of the mill buffet.

The hostess was very nice and walked us around the buffet to explain all the different stations. The waiter was very good and very response to our requests.

A great buffet option on the strip.

$447.57, that' was the price for our dinner, including tip. Kids only count up until 8 then it's full adult price. So my family of 7, two seniors, two adults, a teenager, an 11 year old, and an 8 year old forked out almost $500 dollars for dinner. We did pay for the express entry, good news here, they only charge the $15 for those 18 and older!

We asked about food safety for our 11 year old with allergies at the front desk when paying. They told us to ask the greeter, first greeter told us to ask the one that seats us, the one that seated us told us to ask the chefs, asked the "chef" who looked at me like I had three heads and he had no idea what gluten was. She ended up eating tamales and tortilla chips. Had I known the total lack of understanding and options for gluten free eating we would not have gone, reviews and information indicted it wouldn't be an issue, they were wrong.

Despite spending two hours there, much of it in line for food, I still don't feel like we got our money's worth.

Bacchanal buffet has been voted one of the best buffets from many of my coworkers who frequent the vegas scene. I came with high expectations but the buffet fell slightly short. Paid for lunch and stayed for dinner. The line was only around 30 minutes for 2:00 and we paid $37.00. I probably would not pay over $50 for dinner for this place. 

There isn't a huge amount of difference in food between lunch and dinner. Dinner does include crab legs, and oysters though. 

They have a pretty large buffet and they section off the VIP from the regular folks. If you notice the VIP, gold and silver members have way nicer chairs and carpet under their tables. The regular folks have wood floors. 

They have a huge selection of food. I really enjoyed their fresh juices. The mango, guava and horchata were delicious. I probably drank at least 2 of these juices. The shrimp cocktail was huge! None of those tiny little shrimp but pretty high quality ones. They had a guy service hot steam crab legs instead of people grabbing it themselves. It is much faster this way. The crab legs were meaty and sweet. They had cold ones too that I didn't try. Stone crab claws- some were really dry others were good. 

Some other highlights- the made to order street tacos. Your choice of carne asada, carnitas or adobada. The chinese station is good with shrimp haw gow, and good dumplings. The sushi station had some pretty decent rolls and even had tuna poke and unagi. They also have oysters during dinner but I preferred the oyster shooters. The duck was good but make sure you get it when the chef brings it out so you can pick a good piece. Carving station: I only tried the chicken apple sauce and kleibasa which were both very good. The sweet potato tots are mouth watering

Lots of desserts some which were good others the cakes were too dry. They have a huge selection of gelato with at least 20 different flavors. Let's not forget the macaroons. The green ones were my favorite, and freshly made crepes. You can even get thai tea here as well as shaved ice (not good at all). 

Come back again? Most likely yes but only if I can pay for lunch and stay for dinner.

Food was "meh" overall for the brunch buffet.  Maybe it's because we're culinarily spoiled living in California so we expected more. 

What's weird is that many websites, hotel admins, taxi drivers, and miscellaneous people recommended this. Not impressed. You're better off going to a place that focuses on brunch and where you order by the plate. I personally would choose ihop over this. Hopefully dinner is better for y'all.

Never done this in my life ever. You have to literally pay and wait in line for more than three hours to get seated. I mean why would anyone pay to suffer this long wait. Don't come here ever, it's just a normal buffet.

It's been almost two years since I was wowed by Bachannal.  Went back and wasn't as impressed this time.  (Go to Wicked Spoon if you have to pick one).
First of all, having to wait 90 minutes, including the time from when you use their lame automated text system, is a real hassle.  If you could go without waiting, the experience would be better.  But after standing in line, Disneyland style, the food needs to be better to justify the wait--and it isn't.
There are some wonderful things here, such as the king crab legs, the street tacos, and the Aguas frescas in their own little glass jars.  But many of the dishes, especially the Asian dishes were no better than any "normal" buffet in town.
The desserts are excellent.  A real standout was the dim sum-style custard cups.
Anything and everything you could ask for. It's pricy but you are getting what you pay for. I'll probably never go again--but it's a must if it's your first time in Vegas

Best in Vegas!!!!! I've been to all of them on the strip and this definitely beats the Wicked Spoon, Bellagio, Wynn and the rest. Went on a Tuesday at 12:30 and I waited for 40 minutes. Worth it, but TONS of open tables when I was seated. It has all of the usual but the quality is better than any other buffet in town- especially the fresh carving station. Prime Rib was the best ever, flavorful and not tough or chewy. Polish sausage was also incredible. Crab legs are by far the best thing but I always love their Asian section. Amazing sushi, fresh made to order noodles, but also great traditional Asian dishes and dumplings! Something simple like fried rice was even amazing. Dessert section was great, gelato, made to order crepes and every other dessert you can think of. My only criticism was the lines inside the buffet were annoyingly long for the carving station. I had to wait 24 minutes just to get meat. Not sure if there was a shift change or new product coming out, it was just SLOW. Staff was very attentive and I always had full beverages.

Just Ok. The service was fine, and the buffet is ok for a buffet. It's hard to prepare truly good food to hundreds of people. I will say that this buffet has the biggest selection of food of any buffet in Vegas.

Kinda pricey but by far one of the best buffets in Vegas.

One of the few buffets that have oysters (not my thing) but there's always a line for it.  Crab legs is probably one of the best I've tasted.

Overall just a great buffet.

Let's see where to start. I've been waiting 2 years to eat here and I finally had my chance a few days ago. For being considered the best buffet in town, there wasn't really anything special that stood out to me. It pretty much has the same type of foods from other buffets. They have a standard meat section which was probably the only thing that caught my attention. They offered lamb chops which looked juicy, prime rib, BBQ ribs and sausage. The prime rib tasted bland to me. Besides being cooked to perfection, there wasn't any flavor to make it seem like "the best" and I didn't notice any sauces to give it an extra kick. Don't get me wrong, it was decent but not mouth watering that it would make me want to come back and wait 40 minutes in line or pay a hefty price of $125 for two dinners.

They also have themed sections like everyone else such as Asian, Italian and Mexican which consists of typical sushi, pasta and tacos. None of these in particular caught my interest because it looked average, but I still tried a little of everything. I had 3 carne asana tacos that came out ok. The dim sum was average and I passed on the sushi because it wasn't appealing. They also have a salad section which I didn't care for lol. As for the seafood, they offered cold crab legs (split in half) or steamed crab legs (also split in half.) I've been hearing that this buffet had king crab legs which was the main reason I wanted to eat here in the first place, but they were just average crab legs.. I was extremely disappointed. I also noticed they had shrimp which looked a lot larger than others buffets, but I never got around to trying it.

For dessert, it was as typical and basic as it gets. You have a choice from cookies, ice cream, Rice Krispies treats, cheesecake, carrot cake and flan. They had other items, but this was all I can remember. They also have fruits such as watermelon, pineapple, honeydew and cantaloupe. I tried the flan which was honestly below average if you ever had a decent flan. There's no strong taste to it at all. Their Ice cream labels are completely wrong. They had a "green tea" flavor which was totally mint and a "s'mores" flavor that was chocolate chip..

Overall, this buffet had the best service that you can ask for. Drinks, napkins and utensils were constantly refilled without asking. They also did a good job on taking unwanted plates away and cleaning up the table when we would get up for more food. The servers were friendly and the cooks actually looked like they were happy to work there. Despite my disappointment in this buffet, I can't say that I'll never be back, but I'll definitely eat at cheaper buffets that offer the same items. 

P.s. You can cut the waiting line if you pay a premium price (varies depending on your party size) and they also take a picture of you after you pay for your meal that they bring to your table and try to sell you. 

Also, don't be an idiot like me and pay full price. I realized Groupon offers a dinner for two for $69 after I left.

Been wanting to come here for years now. First time trying to come here was 6 months ago but there's a big ass long lines and it was almost closing time. Will I finally got in without waiting in the long lines thanks to mom VIP card (yeah finally)  but sadly it was not what I expected from all the hype from fellows yelpers. I had the prime rib it was okay nothing special then I had both the cold and hot crab legs. Cold crab legs was sooo damn salty it's like they added loads of salt in the water. Hot crab legs was less salty but not that great.  
Had chicken waffles it's a so so kind of food
Had some of mom's oysters. Wow this was good (never had it before and it was fresh and not too fishy/briny at all
Had udon and it was good but then any udon is good to me (= ^v^=)
All in all not worth spending $59.

I wasn't impressed. Sorry. I will say that I was expecting a huge wait, but we ended up waiting about 45 min which was nice. 

Variety: they had everything from sushi, to dim sum, to southern food, to pizza. Tons of variety, but for whatever reason nothing really appealed to me! Some stand outs where the crab legs, taro buns, and Peking duck. Everything else was okay. Even the prime rib fell short. 

Quality: everything seemed freshly made. The sushi quality was a little generic tasting. The rice had a glossy vinegar taste to it, and the fish was warm. I had to spit it out. They had a charcuterie section which was pretty nice, but the cheeses all seemed intermixed. 

Dessert: this never fails! The Creme brûlée was bomb as was the mint matcha ice cream! Cake pops, gelato, macaroons, tiramisu! Everything under the sun! I'm telling you, the Taro buns were so good!
