I expected more. My boyfriend hyped it up, and I was really excited. Womp! I should have just made a pit stop at Shake Shack.

 Maybe on the day you go the selection will be better.

God no. Great concept, but poorly executed and managed.

We came for breakfast/lunch, looking forward to the variety of offerings. However, the food quality disappointed. The ribs at the carving station almost induced tears - dry, flavorless, tough. Sausages - cold. Smoked salmon (doesn't that just come out of a package anyway?) - oddly briny and just off.

At the hot stations, salty, lukewarm plates ruled the day. The dessert station was...deserted.

If you're going to come here, exercise strategic eating: eggs Benedict, wagyu burgers (eh, but good in comparison to everything else), rolled sole, and cocktail shrimp/seafood.

Though really, if the above categories are all you're interested in, just go to a specialty restaurant. Your wallet and taste buds will thank you.
The best most authentic buffet I have ever eaten at. Period.

One if the best buffet I've been to so far. Almost can't say anything bad about this place. They food is quality and has a nice fancy feel. The place is huge and can seat a lot of people so even if the line looks long it might not be a long wait.

I've been here for the Champagne Brunch ($36+) and for Dinner ($50+). This place is okay, both times. Somewhere, people have claimed that this is the best buffet in town, but I've had better. There are lines everywhere. Average 45 minute plus wait for the line to get into the buffet and then there's the crab legs line, about 10-15 minutes long. 

Brunch: 
I went to the Champagne Brunch this past Sunday. There were a few parts of the buffet that I liked, like that they had crab legs for lunch and the brisket and the service. I didn't get the crab legs though, because the line was too long. The red velvet pancakes are good only because they come in tiny portions, just enough for you to try, but they were hard and not at all tasty. Tried getting a lox bagel but the cream cheese was too hard for me to pull the knife out of so I ended up just getting the smoked salmon alone. The dim sum was okay and everything was mislabeled. New foodie adventurers would have been confused the whole time. 

Dinner:
FYI The last time I was at this buffet for dinner was a few months ago. It was a so-so dinner buffet. I had the crab legs which were good like any other crab leg buffet. Also had a cut of the prime rib and that was okay.

Overall, nothing too memorable but the lines. Service was good. Food, okay.

Timing is everything. I had party 2 and arrived between 5:00-6:00pm for dinner, no wait. This buffet is massive and I could almost get lost. It's so big that I would only get one of something only to get 1/3 of the way and realize my plate is full. The food is delicious, not a fan of the Chinese selection though. Bone marrow is good. Expect lines to get cuts of meat, crab legs, and oysters. Oysters are surprisingly fresh and large. You can get crab legs cold or steamed. Dessert section is it's own little island, Got a crepe and scoop of ice cream and I couldn't eat anything else. Definitely think about sharing some choices to see if you like it enough to get your own. Although you can order drinks from your waiter, I enjoyed drinking the horchata.

we went on a sunday morning around 9:30am so we had to pay for brunch which was a little pricey, but after we finished, we all decided it was worth the extra $$ for brunch. there was a wonderful variety of different foods and lots of flavor too! we had lunch at the bellagio two days before which we thought was well worth the money, but after eating at bacchanal, we will definitely go back to bacchanal! far better than the bellagio, imo.

everything we had tasted fresh. not like at some of the buffets that have something frozen and then thawed/warmed up. or the same thing at every buffet. 

mimosas were included, but we are not big drinkers so i would suggest to go during the week around 10:30am/11am and stay for breakfast and then they will change the buffet for lunch. this way you get a brunch for ~$20 less/per person.

the desserts were to die for! don't forget to stop at the made to order crepes too. lots of wonderful food to try. highly recommend this place. the wait staff was very attentive too.

I was super excited to eat at this buffet after reading all the positive reviews. Upon arrival, the buffet looked liked it held a lot of potential.  The new 17million dollar space was artsy and beautiful with loud music which made it feel trendy and hip.  The light fixtures made out ornate objects like water glass and vases made the space feel eclectic.  The staff was really attentive to my needs with refills on drinks and clearing plates off the table, even pausing for a little casual chit chat.  

I walked up down all the different stations to scope out which dishes I had to try and which to pass on. The food spread seemed to go on forever ranging from seafood, Italian, Mexican, and Asian.  It was like a kid in a candy store. Tons of choices but all unfortunately not to my liking.

I decided that the salad bar would have to be missed in order to try everything else. I started at the Asian station. They had a noodle soup station where you could even get pho. I had dumplings, egg rolls, and Korean short ribs, which were okay but nothing special.  The ribs had good flavor but where a bit chewy.

Moved to the Italian station next, where different pastas and pizzas were prepared.  The  best part of this station was the charcuterie station with all the different meats, cheeses, and mustards.

Next station up was the American BBQ.  This looked like the perfect all American BBQ spread...all the BBQ meats one could ever ask for from ribs to brisket, chicken, and lamb chops with all the best fixing available. Mac'n cheese, broccoli with cheese, mash potatoes, corn, and tator tots.  The ribs that I tasted were so chewy, I couldn't even cut them apart with my knife and the flavor tasted like gasoline...no smokiness or fall apart goodness.

The Mexican station had a woman making fresh tortillas and a bunch of different salsa choices to accompany the meal.

Last of the savory stations is the seafood station.  They had lobster, corn chowder, crab croquette, as well as, hot and cold crab legs, shrimp, and raw oyster...all too salty to eat.  

Then came dessert.  I had heard about the fresh out of the oven souffles that they offered and the wide variety of gelato and sorbets.  Tonight they had banana and pistachio flavored souffles.  The pistachio souffle came out of the oven piping and tall, but had no flavor...all that could be tasted was raw flour.  The gelato station was the only place actually lived up the buffet's claim of thinking "out of the box" and unique. I tried a fig & balsamic, watermelon & mint, blood orange, and mango chili lime, which was my favorite out the 4 flavors. 

Overall, the food was too pricey at $44.99 for dinner and too salty for my taste...will probably never go back.

This is one of the best buffets in Vegas. The food is great and there is such a wide selection. #ronmadmax and #thewebdoc are having a meal to end all meals and tomorrow we start our diets.  After a long extremely productive #nada2016 we are treating ourselves.  #testimonialbuilder was the talk of #nada2016 and everyone that saw it loved it.  

Looking forward to a relaxing day tomorrow so we can recharge and get ready for a big month.

So much great food

We had a wonderful seafood brunch.  All the food was fantastic,  including the mussels (2 types), shrimp, thick bacon, pastries, ceviche, omelettes, fruits & so much more.  One of the best brunch buffets ever!

This place was great. My wife and I went there for our wedding anniversary and thoroughly enjoyed the selection. One disappointment was that we were there for over 2.5 hours and some of the seafood was not restocked for the whole time meaning we missed out on oysters and crab legs which my wife loves. The food was very tasty and fresh but I was expecting more chefs cooking in front of me. Even though an upperclass Vegas buffet it still had that buffet feel. 

The place was fully wheelchair accessible and they made sure we had a place near the buffet so I didn't have to go past other tables.

Left feeling very satisfied

Good food, long wait. You have to give yourself at least 2 hours to stay in line. 

The crab legs were great but I thought the prime rib was so so. They have a great selection of food and desserts and everything I've tried was pretty good.

My sister and I have tried a new buffet during our annual trips to Vegas (Mandalay, Wynn, and Paris previously) and this is my favorite so far.  We actually went twice (brunch and lunch on two different days) because we stayed at Caesars, it was convenient, and satisfied all our cravings.  Highlights-salad bar, meats and cheeses, pizza, sushi, and all the American offerings.  May have been the best biscuits and gravy ever.  Yummy fired chicken.  The desserts at lunch and sweets at breakfast were outstanding too.  My only criticism is lack of offerings at the Mexican station, I love Mexican and couldn't find anything that appealed to me.

This was only the second time I've been to Bacchanal, so I'd forgotten how many OPTIONS they have! I brought some friends from out of town here so they could experience a "true Vegas buffet," but places like Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan are different - I like to describe them as "smaller portioned gourmet." By this I mean most of these dishes are already portioned off into a small bowl/plate, but as with any buffet, you can obviously choose how many portions you pick up and eat. This, in my mind, helps me float around and really sample more without getting overly full right off the bat.

They have multiple sections in their buffet; seafood, American (Elk Burgers were a unique sampling), Latin foods (they had a killer Posole), Asian, Italian, etc. Some of my personal favorites were the avocado toast with lump crab, the deviled egg with bacon, while I don't like horseradish, the bone marrow was surprisingly scrumptious (for my first time ever having bone marrow). The crab never fails, either. Within each entry there was a significant range of options, so I never felt limited to  chow mein, Mongolian beef, and fried rice, like you'd see at most buffets: there was an Asian Soup Bar, for crying out loud! 

Finally the desserts: aside from the gelato and crepe lines, there were miniature portions, absolutely beautifully presented, of everything from cheesecake, dulce de ledge flan, crème brûlée, and so on. Absolutely comprehensive across the broad, and most importantly, they did not sacrifice quality or taste in this endeavor. Highly recommend for anyone, and be sure to try the peach green tea!!

NOM!!! This buffet is sooo goood! They had a good variety of everything to eat. 

My family took a mini vacay trip to vegas and decided to eat at this buffet. We saw the long line which seemed it would take hours to go through, so we opted for the express which was an addition $20. It was soooo worth it. We ate until we all had food babies. I loved the dessert bar with so many ice cream options including mochi!! They also had a crepe station so I put ice cream in the crepes too!! SO GOOOD!!!

As for non-sweets, the had a great brisket that wasn't dry but really moist instead! It was really good. There was also the lobster with crab on top. It was one of the highlights of my meal. This is a must-go buffet for the next trip to vegas!

Best buffet we have eaten at in Las Vegas. The food was fresh and tastiest around. Nice hot crab legs, fresh sushi. Taco bar, wide choose of Asian food and American meets. Seafood bar with oysters. Dessert bar was amazing!! The only draw back was the price. It's pricey. But as a treat it was worth it

I've heard of this particular buffet being the best in town.  Does it live up to the hype?  In a word, no.  The selections on offer are varied and possibly overwhelming.  Is it truly any different from what's available in any other buffet such as over at Wynn or the Wicked Spoon?  Not really.  Yes, the buffet itself is truly massive (it spans the room itself) but once you get past that, you'll find it's not as special as the price tag may make it out to be.  It is indeed pricey to eat here ($53.99 for dinner on a weekend rate), and that's why it only gets a solid 3 stars from me.  Food is good, but not great.  Some have mentioned that some items were overly salty (particularly anything from the carving station) and I didn't experience that.  But at the same time, nothing compelled me enough to keep going until I was ready to burst unlike other buffets on The Strip.  You won't be blown away by anything other than your receipt.  Service is just ok at best.  Simple requests like a drink refill are quick enough, but go outside of that, and it falls apart pretty fast.  In short, if you're compelled to give it a shot, it's a solid choice.  But don't expect to be impressed.

This is officially my favorite buffet in town. We went for a second time and everything that I disliked the first time was improved.

 They took out the rubbery stone crab (and the need for crab crackers), the King Crab was not super salty anymore. In fact, it was so good and even better when it was steamed. 

I got to try other items this time such as the made to order taco station. Oh my... fresh hand made tortillas! They also had a ramen/pho station. I tried the pho and the broth was delicious! The dessert station is definitely the star of the show. Their made to order crepe station offers different fruit, toasted almonds, whipped cream, Nutella and more. The French macaroons were so good. They offer different flavors of gelato that I normally don't see in other buffets.

Service was much faster this time around. I can't wait to come back and try their breakfast offering!

Some people said this was the best buffet in Vegas, so I had high expectations. I went here on a Sunday night around 7:30, and the line was ridiculously long. I waited approximately 1.5 hours to get in. 

The food wasn't as good as I expected, and apart from bone marrow, all their food was just typical and ordinary food you would see at nice buffets elsewhere. This place is definitely not one of the best buffets I've been to. 

I definitely don't think it was worth my money and the time to come here. I would rather spend the money elsewhere on other restaurants in Vegas.

First time in Vegas and the first buffet I've tried there!! There were so many great selections, I couldn't get to everything!! They ranged from seafood, Chinese, American, Mexican, everything!!! Had my raw oysters which was BOMB, the crab legs were cut in half for your convenience which was SO HELPFUL, the dessert was so high quality and fresh! 

I loved the little Thai tea floats..but instead of the gelato, I asked my server for cream, so I basically had little Thai tea shots! Yum! There were juices in little glass jars which were so cute. There was so many variety of foods. It was great. So worth the money. So glad I was introduced to this place!! 

The seafood was high quality, the meats were so juicy! Just thinking about it all makes my mouth water...

Absolutely incredible buffet! We went here twice during our stay. Food is fresh, flavorful, and with such a great variety! We don't eat seafood and yet there were still endless choices. We did wait about 40 min for dinner and 15 for lunch. So, not bad at all an surely worth it. 

Lunch is a bit different than dinner, if you do get there at change over time the really fresh dinner options come out closer to around 4:00 I noticed. 

Major hits: Any of the BBQ, truffle mushroom soup, street tacos, little container of nachos, Thai spicy beef, juice bar, sweet potato tots, creamed corn, the entire dessert section! You have tip try the Thai ice tea ice cream cup with boboa!!! 

Misses: Servers can be very slow. And, noticed a bunch of clean, available tables ready that sat empty for a long time even while the mine was long.

All I can say is WOW. Vegas has a lot of great buffets, but this one is spectacular. There is more food than you could ever even begin to comprehend. Bacchanal has everything you could ever wish for in a high end Vegas buffet: HUGE selection of QUALITY, DELICIOUS food, beautiful restaurant, and great presentation to boot.

Literally. So. Much. Food. And it is all SO GOOD. Crab legs, raw oysters, shrimp, lamb chops, dim sum, pasta station, noodle station, taco station, sushi, prime rib, roast pork, beef brisket, truffle scalloped potatoes, mashed potatoes, every kind of carb you could ever want, desserts on desserts, the list goes on and on and on and on. 

If you're looking for an amazing Vegas buffet, Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace will not disappoint!!!!!!!
This is the best buffet in vegas what I hear and believe. About 40 bucks gets you two hours if non stop eating. Drinks may cost you 5-20$ depends on what you like.

I hated Cosmo's Wicked Spoon, so I was worried about risking so much money to be disappointed again ... but sweet watermelon minty jesus, Bacchanal Buffet was EXCELLENT!  I paid $48 for dinner on Tuesday night, and waited about half an hour to get in at 5:30, and ten minutes to get seated.

My gal pal and I take turns going up for food, so one stays with purses, and we each fill a plate with small bites of things to try.  For example, I make a plate and bring it back, she takes bites of anything she's interested in, then she goes up to fill a plate while I eat the rest.  It's a great way for us not to waste a bunch of food, and we get to share opinions bite by bite -- then make a second or third trip to get more of what we liked best.

For me, the best dinner item was the sweet potato tater tots.  The skin is crispy, the inside gooey, and they're glazed with a salty sweet syrup caramelized shell.  So simple, and yet ... amazeballs!  I also high five the staff for their excellent ceviche, chicken marsala, spicy fried fish, and charcuterie.  One slice of ribeye steak was great, but the next was fatty and awful (the flank steak too.)  I was so-so on the lamb, and the other veg choices.

Next time I'll remember to leave LOTS of room for dessert, and FILL UP on watermelon mint sorbet.  Maybe the best dessert ever?  Tho I'm usually gaga for french macaroons and mochi.  But I prefer mochi in mango, which they skipped ... and their macaroons had great shells, but the inner cookie was too moist, and too much filling, too thick.  The center should be like a sweet adhesive only, not a thick band of firm chocolate ganash.  Generally too much sugar in most of the desserts, and tho some say the dinner is overly salty as well, I like salt and thought everything had the right levels.

If I have guests in town who want the best buffet and can afford a real treat, I would def go back.  :-D

Get there early for dinner. You'd have to sign into the computer, get a ticket and wait until your party is called. Once called, check in with the hostess to get into the line to pay for it. After that, you stand in another line to get seated. So don't come super hungry and expect to be seated right away. 

The seating are nice and comfy. Seafood was tasty. Be careful though. There's a boiled seafood station near the Italian food and there's a cold seafood station. Overall, many food choices and they were good. My only complaint was the Asian food station. It was dirty. There was one man who had the worse attitude, and I'm guessing he was the head cook of that station. It was busy and things were getting low. Maybe he was overwhelmed? I avoided that station.

Now, onto the dessert. Made to order crepes, yes!! Everything in that station were great! Pricey buffet but worth it.
Heard so many things about this buffet. I tried it myself and it was amazing. The price was fair. $59 per person for dinner. The prime rib was so moist and juicy.

Best buffet in Vegas hands down. Is it pricey? Yes, but it's worth it.

We had tried this using the buffet of buffets pass and paying an extra $30 per person.

The buffet has several stations ranging from Asian, Italian, Seafood, etc.  The food was top notch and well worth the price.

Went back August 2017 and did the breakfast buffet. It's nice to see it's still worth the price. Can't beat the quality of food on this buffet.

Came here for the bubbly brunch! Great spot to eat and drink for a few hours! You definitely get your money's worth - great food and unlimited champagne or mimosas for the brunch special! Loved our sever Carlos - we never had to ask for anything he was super accommodating! Great spot to check out while in Vegas!

I've been to brunches at the Wynn, Luxor, Excalibur, MGM, & Palms & this was the Most expensive and least favorite. Food was just alright. Booze is extra. The real issue was how dirty the chairs are! $100 for two people and you can see every stain on the light grey chairs. If they are not going to clean them at least change them to a darker color. Not vegetarian/vegan friendly.

I am not a buffet type of person. Because I don't have big appetite, so I prefer good quality food over quantity. I gave Bacchanal a try because I heard it's the latest and greatest buffet in town. You can just tell by the decor. The buffet entrance looks like a fresh seafood market. It got my attention right away. I love the warm and fuzzy atmosphere which reminds me of the eat every possible delish dish til you enter food coma holiday family dinner celebration.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=yWgf1bzx39k05ffOYKUT4Q#tV6gVls4xOZ_g_JtJ8M_ww

I really enjoyed the colorful plating of small bite size portion (first seen in Wynn's Gerber size glass salad then full blown adapted by Cosmo on almost every dish there). I am not gonna go through the Bacchanal laundry list. I am just gonna hit all highlights of my meal. 

- Ginseng chicken soup: 
I was shock how authentic it was! Chef was very generous with Ginseng. It was great. I took a picture of it to show the bowlful of ingredients they cram into that little bowl of soup. To quote and agree 100% with the funny executive chef greeted us at the table, "authenticity is the name of the game (at Bacchanal), we do not have any Gwailo flavor here."

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=yWgf1bzx39k05ffOYKUT4Q#FEoVci-bHcanQrJojxiLEg

- Sugar glazed lamb chop with mint sauce:
It was perfectly cooked. Meat was juicy and tender bursting with flavors. This could match the lamb chop served at fine dining restaurant on strip (for a $38 dinner entree). 
=

- Clam Bucket:
Clams were prepared with sweet corn, sausage and orange (bursting with layers of  flavors; I wish I have other words to describe it... lol). Sweet corn was soaked with juice from sausage, clam and orange. It was very delish.

- Stone crab claws:
This is well worth it of this meal! You get to choose how you like to mix in your plate (mussels/snow crab legs/stone crab claws), and the chefs at the seafood station will boil it for you in flavorful broth with minced garlic and herbs (super personalized, attention to details, well worth the wait in the line ~5 to 10 min).

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=yWgf1bzx39k05ffOYKUT4Q#LleLz1tP_YUQ9Bqq58d8fg

- Crepe:
All crepes were made-to-order and whipped cream on top was killer for a girl trying to stay in shape.

http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/RESDUcs7fIiihp38-d6_6g?select=yWgf1bzx39k05ffOYKUT4Q#tP9B9-92At6gqz5KGwFojg

This place is truly the best buffet on food quality and deal-wise (under $40 per person). The savory dishes are just top notch and representing the best game in town. However, the showing at dessert section is lackluster, except the made-to-order crepes and possibly the gelato (saw some unique flavors there but ran out of room in my already bloated stomach). I have to deduct 0.5 stars from the weak dessert showing because I LOVE desserts. 

I really hope Bacchanal will keep up its great quality of food and service (up their desert game). It is hard to maintain the consistency (that's how restaurant business is). Because I can't wait to bring all friends and family with me next time and enjoy the food.

EPIC DISAPPOINTMENT & COLLOSAL WASTE OF TIME!  As a frequent user of Yelp to guide our restaurant choices, I am left baffled by the rave reviews on this place.  The process to get to the buffet was a MAJOR PROCESS  -  we arrived around 5:20pm put our name in the kiosk, it gives you a ticket which tells you to come back at 7:22pm.  We went and killed two hours and returned only so the greeter could lift the velvet rope and have us stand in line for 40 minutes to pay $125 for two ppl......and here's the "piece de resistance".....after paying you go and stand in yet ANOTHER line to be seated (another 20 minutes).  OFFENSIVE/ABSURD in my book when you are paying $58 per person.  We should have left at the onset when it was a 2 hr wait but we kept hearing how this was the best buffet in LV.   Bigger isn't always better folks and this was the case at Bacchanal.  Overall, the food was mediocre/generic and made me REGRET having wasted so much time (and $$$$) so i could be served fried chicken, dried sliders, corn, brick hard meatballs and standard asian fare and low quality desserts.  Yes, they had seafood but you can find this any many other places.  If you're looking for a high quality buffet with an elegant atmosphere and not having to stand in lines for hours and then more lines at the buffet - take yourselves to the Wynn Hotel where you will have a much better experience!

The expectation coming into this buffet was 1) good quality food and 2) endless quantities of it.

My results?
1) NOPE. Only the miso sea bass was worth having beyond a second serving of. 
2) SURE. I was able to indulge in more mediocre food after regurgitating it into the porcelain toilet conveniently located outside of the eating area. 

Now I'm off to figure out how to get the most out of my money while I'm still here...

This is the second time I have come here. I'm still impressed at the size of this buffet. The food is always good and the servers are friendly. Only had to wait about 10 mins this time in the line, so not bad.

This is the best buffet in Las Vegas! It has the greatest variety of delicious foods and I love their fresh juices and beautiful desserts. We always make it a point to come here whenever we go to Vegas!!

This buffet in the Caesars Palace hotel is supposed to be the "Best Buffet" in Vegas, so my expectations were up there. The setting is very elegant, and the displays are lovely, but this was definitely not worth the cost for me. There were oysters on the half shell from Washington state -- if you are a big Pacific oyster lover, then the price would be justified. There were also king crab legs, which I found a bit dry and stringy. The shrimp were very large, plump and tasty. Italian food was nothing special. The waitress said the pasta was homemade -- you could choose ingredients to have tossed with the pasta, but the pasta did NOT appear homemade. Lasagna was so-so. The Chinese offerings had nothing particularly special. We did enjoy the prime rib - nice and rare. The lamb chops were overdone. There was an "all you can drink" option for wine and beer extra charge. Service was very good! Drinks were filled, and plates were cleared promptly. This buffet was a little nicer than others, but for me the quality didn't warrant the very high price. I wouldn't go back. $291 for party of 5. 65 mins wait then additional 30 on another wait time for your table. So if you are patient enough then come on down and give it a try.
Over hyped. Really expensive for the taste of the food. The dessert chefs were kind of mean. But the place was nice, elegant and huge! Our waiter was nice and attentive.

Everything tasted absolutely amazing. Even down to the sauces (BBQ, cocktail, etc). The $15 all you can drink wine and beer was definitely worth it. My only complaint was the line. We got our ticket and were told to come back at a certain time (50 mins later). So we wait at a bar and get a text to come redeem our ticket. By this time we're starving. We then proceeded to wait in line for the buffet for another 1hr 15 mins!  We were caught off guard by this. We started waiting in line right by the kiosks, so we were at the very back of the full line. Everyone around us was miserable and complaining. If it weren't for the food being 6 stars, I'd take away a point or two. 

Had I known it would be 2 hours from the time we got our ticket til we were sitting down, I'd have paid the extra $45/person to skip the line.

What they say is true - this is the best buffet in Vegas. Not that I tried another one after hearing this was the best... and honestly, I will probably never go to another buffet in Vegas. I ate my weight in crab legs. Staff was ON IT with drinks and refills (which is good to know if you're ordering one of their bottomless wine/champagne/beer options). I went up to the buffet about 4 times for more food... yeah I can eat a lot. 
Pricey, but worth EVERY penny. I recommend going at an off time (i.e. not a popular eating time) to avoid the lines.

Horrible experience! Be prepared to wait 3 hours to be seated and pay $60 per person for lunch - subpar food and completely not worth your time. Check out a nice restaurant like Mesa grill at Caesars instead. A reminder why buffets in Vegas are usually a terrible choice.

My new favorite buffet! I'm so glad I got lazy to drive to the M Buffet and was willing to wait an hour for the Bacchanal Buffet. First off, it's $37.99 for Total Rewards members so make sure to show them your card! It's newly renovated and the place looks amazing, but the food is the more important thing. Their king crab legs were fresh and can be steamed if you prefer. The oysters were actually sweet and clean. The prime rib was tender but I felt the au jus lacked real flavor. There's a noodle soup station with pretty decent bowls of pho!  There was also ramen and wonton noodles, but I didn't have enough stomach space to try them all. Sushi was fresh but there wasn't a large selection to choose from. Chicken herbal soup loaded with actual chicken and herbs! The halibut was juicy. The seafood paella was moist. Oh, they even have the mexican corn with the mayo, parmesan, and chili powder! Also, the tamales were great. The best part was the dessert section and I don't usually leave room for desserts. They have crepes made-to-order and ice cream a la modes. There were a lot more that I tried and some I didn't get to try, but there was nothing I disliked. In my opinion, they have restaurant quality food and a great selection at that. This is like a dream buffet! Worth the $$ and the wait - DONT MISS OUT!

This buffet is everything you expect it to be! Highly recommend for you to make a stop here. We ate here for the Saturday brunch and arrived just before 11am.  What we saw were 3 lines to get in. We started in line 2 and the wait was about 30 minutes till we sat down at a table. 

1. There's a line at the very end where you can wait in person or leave your name at the kiosk. 
2. Then there's a line you move into where the wait is estimated 30 minutes to the front. This line lets you pay for the buffet. 
3. After paying for the buffet, you wait in a line for a table. 

So many food and dessert options here. Yes, there were crab legs, crab claws, shrimp, mussels at 11am for brunch. An Asian's paradise....MY paradise. Go for the hot crab legs near middle of the buffet, next to the cured meats. They're in a boiling pot and you have to ask for them. 

Other highlights were:
- dim sum at the end of the buffet
- meat carving station. The brisket... Yum...
- a coconut ceviche dish near the cold crab legs
- salads were surprisingly good! Lessened the guilt
- fresh squeezed juices
- so many dessert options

We did the lunch buffet with unlimited champagne. The food options here are staggering, and service considering how huge the place is was pretty decent.

With any buffet, some items are average but this was way better than others I've been to. 
My friend's top 5 foods:
1) lobster bisque
2) all the roasted veggies
3) shrimp and sausage creamy creole dish
4) made to order dessert crepes
5) BBQ wings

Mine:
1) shrimp shumai
2) made to order crepe
3) fried chicken and waffle
4) lobster bisque
5) roasted cauliflower

We had five glasses of champagne each. We stayed for two hours. Both of us could have been there all day. They change out the options. There are more options from more cuisines than either of us knew what to do with. The dessert bar is a thing of beauty.

I loved it here.

0 stars for service if possible... I get it... it's a buffet. However, we paid the extra $15 for all you can drink...but it was nearly Impossible to get a refill. We couldn't even get our waters refilled... disappointed that we paid for drinks that we couldn't get. Flagged down a couple bus boys before we finally got 1 refill... that in itself ruined the experience. Food was definitely extravagant but nothing so special to warrant $55 a person... then again, perhaps because it was a Thursday dinner and not the special weekend dinners. Disappointing dinner... especially since I was looking forwards to it during our short trip.

this place is sooooooo over rated. I don't see what is so great about this place, there is so much food but the flavor is missing, lamb chops obviously people probably never had the best lamb chops if they think bacchanal buffet has good lamb not at all couldn't even finish it. It's better to go and pay all that money in some nice restaurant than to be in this mass of food where there is no flavor.  I tried the  baby back ribs soooooo dry, I was scared that I would be losing me teeth, that is how hard it was to chew, and again no flavor. Forget it, never again. My only one star goes for the carrot cake and for the salad with feta cheese on it.

Service was amazing for the lunch. Our server was attentive and never had to ask for anything as she was very proactive in realizing what we needed.

Seafood selection was limited but alright. It was more mixed with carbohydrates which I wasn't fond of. I was expecting more than just crayfish and prawns and mussels in selection. It would be nice to see salmon, oysters, and some lobster too.

Dessert that were pastries was very limiting. Sure there were a lot of baked good but it was all cakes.

Variety in food was issue but it was all good.

This buffet is among the best in Las Vegas. Honestly if you're here to visit and want quality selection this place is your best bet. 

Where they go wrong is in the line maintenence to get in the place. I'm not faulting them for being busy, I'm faulting them for being disorganized. The kiosks are a cool touch for those who don't mind browsing around, I can see where it helps manage the line to a lower number. However, the poor girl you have working at the stand is overwhelmed and not managing the line accordingly. Not only is she bombarded with questions   my multiple guests, but she is also managing the kiosk lines and the main lines while answering everyone's questions. To maintain a level of luxury I do believe this is where you are going wrong. People are taking a look at the line and walking straight away, they don't even realize you have that awesome kiosk system. I also suggest that the hostess wait collecting the kiosk tickets until they hit the actual stand and not going down the line collecting. I feel bad for her. She can't even greet properly.

Update.....price is now $44 for dinner. OMG I don't get these reviews at all. I live in LV so I admit that I resist buffets but we had visitors in town so we had this at the top of our list. First of all, we get in line and a pleasant employee tells us the line is 90 minutes at our point but we can each buy a $15 fast pass so we can zip into the vip line. Well, we decided to decline that generous offer and lo and behold.....the 90 minute line was actually 40 minutes. Just a ploy to get you to part with more money. When we did get in, there were multiple empty tables that stayed empty the entire time we dined. Seems like they just want to build excitement and keep the buffet line long so they can sell some more of those "fast passes". 

The buffet stations were ill kept and congested. There were a few small plate standouts, but the bbq station had one guy trying to carve for too many folks. The server NEVER brought us refills and our plates stacked up around us. It appeared that they did not have enough bus help or servers on the floor. I hate it when I am surrounded by dirty dishes. It certainly did not live up to the reputation many have expressed here. Really LOUD too!

King crab was the worst quality I have EVER eaten. What a joke! Desserts were beautiful, but after a bite of several, I left them on my plate. UGH! Lousy quality for such lovely looking plates. The diabetic dessert consisted of three choices. I am only grateful that we tried this before we wasted a ton of money bringing our family members here during the holiday.

Like I said, I don't care for buffets, but if I were to consider any, I would go to the "M" resort with way better service, food & ambiance and even free wine and beer with the buffet. Please don't buy all the hype. We all thought it was one overpriced slop shop.

I heard from family friends that this buffet is the best in Vegas. The setting was nice with the seafood and dessert station in the front. The buffet is in a "zig zag" form starting from the seafood to mexican, italian, and lastly asian cuisines. The waitress was very kind and checked on us for refills. I love their peach iced tea! The best time to come here is for lunch (I think its 37 bucks). Was it worth it? Hell yeah. My top 3 items would be the bone-in ribeye, wagyu slider, shrimp dim sum. I wouldn't say I would come here often, but if you win 40 bucks in the casino then definitely congratulate yourself with the Bacchanal Buffet. 

Oh btw, I LOVE their desserts! Crepes made to order, cake pops, and PANDAN TIRAMISU....need i say more..

for the price, i'd rather go to a nice restaurant and have a really good meal. there are a lot of options, but everything tastes average. The oysters are really sandy, so I kept biting into the shells. The crab was decent, but i can get fresher crab at Costco. All in all, if you want to feel like you're in a Willy Wonka Food Factory, this is fun to try once, but the food is mediocre.

Great food and great service. Our waitress was excellent. We did not have to ask for refills because she was always checking on what we needed.  She definitely enjoys her job and because of that we gave her a generous tip. Other staff were friendly and nice too.  $57.28 per person plus tip for Monday night buffet was money well spent for great dining experience.

One of the best buffets in vegas. Great selection, clean, good presentation. Loved the mexican juices. Dessert station stands out the most when compared to other vegas buffets. Lines for each station were  incredibly long. Groups of tourists came in and were cutting in lines and was just CHAOS.

This review is only for the Christmas Feast. There are two price for the buffet on Christmas Day.  We went for the 79.99 one and are exciting to the items advertised on the pomo see attached.  We were there at 1230pm for lunch, however, not all the items on the list are available(eg the two kind of lobster, scallop etc are missing). We were told that dinner time will have all the item on the list available. The ads said $79.99 is from 11am to 1030pm. I expect there is no difference between lunch and dinner! This a false advertisement and I am upset with this overpriced Christmas lunch!

Awesome Buffett!! We walked in with a party of 15. It wasn't too long of a wait considering it was a busy saturday night. An extensive food selection. For the price we paid it was definetly worth the food. The staff was amazing especially our server Jie!! We will be back!

Typical vegas buffet. It's defiantly an upgrade from the old caesars buffet but its not the best out there. The poorly designed buffet leaves you waiting awhile to get to the seafood and carved meats area. While in the mean time trying to move so people can get side and other food while your waiting. All in all it's worth trying now while its new and before it goes down hill like other buffets in the past.

My husband is not a fan of buffets but the rest of the family loves this place....the Crab legs and desserts! Are our favorite. The guy working the taco station really made it the best experience. His name was Delmar and only because of his service my husband will return. He was very friendly and amazing. We never had such good service.

This was a great experience. Not as good as I was expecting but still very enjoyable. I was looking for a warm king crab legs. They did have king crab legs but they were chilled. Not bad just not what I was looking for. The desserts were amazing I would definitely be back

I knew I had to throw it at least one buffet while I was in Vegas.  Bacchanal was one that I missed out on the last time that I was in town.  I think I went to Wicked Spoons instead so I made it a point this time to get my grub on here.  Located inside Caesars Palace, this buffet is definitely a sight to see.  We walked in, paid and then around to scope the food options.  I thought it wasn't as big until we saw the back end and more options.  Whoa!!

We decided to split up our dishes into different types of food.  I went with the breakfast platter to start.  Bacon was on point, the benedicts were delicious, the eggs were solid, and the OJ's were freshly squeezed juice.  What an awesome starter.  Oh they had red velvet pancakes too, my goodness.  Next came the meaty portion.  It was all juicy and tender much to my enjoyment.  The seafood platter was after followed by the dessert plate before we both tapped out.  It was so much food.  I contemplated staying there the whole day but we had some more business to attend to so after dessert was finished it was go time.  I felt their desserts were lacking a bit though but the seafood was really delicious and fresh.  

Bacchanal has everything and I mean literally everything.  Vegas buffets always delivers for me.  The options are limited and theres just so much variety.  I likes me a ton of variety.  The food is 4 star quality too so you can't really knock that.  I think in total we paid about 100 bucks plus for 2 so it does get pretty pricey but overall very worth the money in my opinion.  Especially if you can get in about 5 to 10 plates lol.  Sadly after 5 it was tap out time.

I will definitely be returning here again.  Excellent food, great atmosphere and the service was nice and warm.  I wish more buffets were like Vegas style ones but oh wells.

I had heard rave reviews and love a good buffet. My first trip to Vegas. Got there early last Saturday morning at 9:45 so no wait.  A large selection of food but I have to say it was hit and miss on the cooking. The prime rib was literally not cooked all the way through and really tough. Some sides were very tasty like the mac cheese. Breakfast croissant sandwiches were delicious. Dessert bar and salad bar lacking. Dim sum good. And then unfortunately tried the sliders. The people in our group that ate the sliders got very very sick the rest of the day. Almost didn't get to go to our Cirque show at 9 pm later because all still getting sick. The people that passed on the sliders didn't get sick. They were lukewarm and tasted odd. So i won't be going back. Would rather have prime rib at a restaurant.

From: ChefDan the FlavorKing

WHY are these people rating this crappy buffet so high?!!!! Because it has snow crabs and shrimp on it?!! You are NOT going to get your moneys worth I promise!.....ain't gonna happen.

ONE STAR for the REALLY bad value, possibly two stars for the food.

1. Stood in line for 30 minutes watching the ridiculous OTHER line in front of the seafood buffet.

2. No King Crabs - They immediately run out at 7:00PM? and don't restock them.
Snow crabs - they slice them in half while chilled - HINT - go to the Italian side and they have them properly hot.

3. The rest of the seafood was a joke on each occasion...fake paella, fake ceviche, etc. Don't mind a fake version...just not a bad one.

4. Miniature hotdogs, hamburgers, and baked potatoes. REALLY?

5. Lastly a BBQ station, pizza station, and basically an uninspired dessert station. That's about it.

On the desserts, at least do people a reach-around and fake a bananas fosters or something tasty. We flame that on our own buffets and it blows peoples minds.

SUMMARY: $50 to stand in a bunch of lines and eat the above. Wow.

I ate here 2 years ago and fell in love.  I finally came back to Vegas this past week and the first thing that I thought about was - WHEN AM I GOING TO THE BACCHANAL?!?  Admittedly, I was a little nervous because my expectations were high.  I was a little worried that the quality of the buffet would have dropped over the two years - as restaurants commonly do after they aren't "new" anymore.  Thank goodness I was absolutely wrong and the Bacchanal did not fail to impress.  I was full of glee and delicious food.

Everything that I ate was pretty darn delicious - literally everything from the chicken feet from the dim sum station to the thick cut bacon at the carving station.  Pure heaven.  The desserts were delectable as well, especially the flan and the fudge.  I think Wicked Spoon beats Bacchanal out with dessert by an eensy bit, but  the Bacchanal beats it in every other way.  Possibly the best $40 I have ever spent!

Cool looking restaurant. Dishes were more misses than hits. Expectations were probably too high. I was really hoping to be impressed. Not worthy of the premium over the other top buffets.

I hear total rewards members get $1 off entrance.

Hooray for this buffet!!!

Finally I've found a buffet that isn't just another blah blando buffet.

I decided to try it out for breakfast. Cheapest option and no lines!!! $33

My God! Not only did they have breakfast items but there was also lunch items as well. A ton!- Asian, Italian, and seafood!

Dessert section had the most eye candy! Literally and figuratively.

I also loved that they included fresh juices- orange, cucumber, passion fruit, carrot, watermelon. 

So...Breakfast 9:30 am- 11:30 am
-pho, seaweed salad, charcuterie, bagel, salad, pistachio blondie, creme brûlée, fudge, almond croissant, shrimp & grits, steak & eggs, roasted tomatoes/mushrooms, bacon, chicken quesadilla, Chilaquiles, French toast, watermelon juice!

Everything was great and I completely took advantage of the 2hour max time limit they had.

plenty of options. Not enough space in my tummy.

As a Vegas local, I'm not a huge fan of buffets. To me, they're all about the same and I never feel like I eat enough to get my money's worth. And THEN a friend asked me to have dinner with her at Bacchanal. The atmosphere was classy and the staff was gracious and friendly. Although the restaurant was busy, our waitress never left dirty plates on our table and promptly refilled our drinks. Honestly, I've never seen so much food in my entire life! Every time I thought I got to the last station, I would turn a corner and there would be more food selections. Everything I got was delicious and although I'm not a seafood fan, my friend refilled her plate with crab legs so many times I lost count. The dessert bar is amazing! Had I known how delicious everything would be, I would have eaten less food and more cheesecake, cake pops, gelato and cookies. The almond cookies were the best I've ever had. I would gladly wait in line and pay $50 right now to have another one. I highly recommend Bacchanal whether you're a local or a tourist. Two thumbs way up!

Large selection, long line to get in. Have been for  Sunday brunch and Saturday dinner. Waited 2 hrs for brunch, time from check in to seating, for dinner waited about 30 minutes, so plan accordingly. The food selection was similar so honestly if I was going back I'd probably pick early dinner just so I don't wait as long. I would say the food is all good, nothing great, but also nothing bad, which is actually pretty impressive when you consider the selection. I find it similar to the buffet at Aria, if I had to compare. Can't say it blew my mind like the ads implied it would but worth trying at least once especially if family in town.

They claim that this buffet won top awards for the past 2 years. Go anywhere but here unless you're willing to ruin the rest of your vacation. Besides being one of the most expensive buffets on the strip, don't be surprised if you become seriously ill for 2 months following this meal.
The management takes no responsibility for their improper treatment of the food they serve.
We witnessed the handling of raw food next to cooked food.
We were forced to spend the last 3 days of our vacation in our room, sick as dogs.
We are still sick, 2 months later, and our doctor now has us on massive dosages of Flagyl along with Cipro. These drugs are not easily tolerated and it should not be necessary to have to go through this.
If you had a similar experience please call (800) 696-6699 or their insurance campany @ (866) 446-1424. They are wise guys!!!!!! We would avoid this buffet at any cost.
Don't waste your money. If you like good food you will not like this buffet. The food is the same as any other Vegas buffet. It's not worth the wait or the money.

Very disappointed! For the price of $55 per person. Crab legs were so salty and shrimps weren't fresh at all. I will not return to this over priced buffet!
Also the waiting time was ridiculous long, not worthy the time or the money.
Excelente comida únicamente una larga espera para entrar  pero sin duda una muy buena experiencia

Sat AM brunch/lunch.  very impressive.  500 items so it's a challenge to try everything,  but I recommend the fresh-squeeze juices in a bottle -- don't get OJ from the staff.  the fried chicken was impressive, crispy outside and juicy inside, can't usually get it like this.  also I was rather surprised by the pho and ramen, and other tiny stations that will make things for you.  while not all items are the best necessary, it's excellent for a buffet.  crepes freshly made, interesting sorbet flavors.  the tiny breakfast bite sizes are great, small little fryer baskets, plus ingenious little handles on the dishes to make them easy to pick up.

I haven't been to a lot of Vegas buffets (the only other one I tried being the Wynn buffet), but I would say Bacchanal is pretty good. Not only do they offer a wide variety of cuisines, but the items are of high quality. Seafood, BBQ meats, Mexican, Italian, Japanese, Dim sum, dessert bar... plenty of items to choose from!

Because I don't do buffets all that often, my buffet eating style is very minimal. The high price made me take advantage of the food I usually don't like to spend per plate... which is mostly CRAB LEGS. I must have had 4 or 5 plates of crab legs. There are cold crab legs as well as hot crab legs fresh off the boiling pot, which I preferred. I also really enjoyed the brisket (which was perfectly cooked!).

One cool tip - go have a late lunch and pay the lunch price. Why? Soon enough it will be dinner time, and they will be putting out dinner items, some of which are very special (bone marrow, anyone)?

Overall, I had a good time here. I would come here again when I don't mind spending and gaining a few extra pounds.
Very good.  All the chefs know what they are talking about.  This is a buffet where the chefs will gladly talk to you, and help you with anything you need.

I have been waiting to go to Bacchanal for over a year now. Just recently celebrating their first birthday I have heard such great stories. Some of my favorite buffets before entering this one were others regarded for being "upscale" or "fresh" like the Wicked Spoon (Cosmo) or Studio B (M).  Bacchanal did not disappoint. 

I was scared about the wait for the buffet. They close at 10, and I was arriving at 7:30. I expected a 90+ min stand in line. Instead I got to walk up to a computer stand, input my phone number, and print out a ticket to come back and pay / wait for my table. 9:02. The time frame was right, but I got to spend the time relaxing and not in line. Presumable this is so that they can let their customers gamble and make more money. I enjoyed the free bench at Starbucks and stayed entertained with conversation with friends. Going back to line around 8:50, they let us in early to pay and sit. I still had to wait a solid 15 more after paying to sit. 

Sitting down I was served a drink and bolted to the buffet. It is only one side of the floor, but it is huge. I read before over 500 items, which is probably somewhat accurate if you count each individual label for honey and bread. Starting with ramen and ending with hot crab, I went back to try almost everything. Unfortunately I did not get to eat a mass quantity of any one thing, but got to try most things. I was delighted to actually enjoy almost every dish. Every dish I tried I probably could have eaten as a full course.  

Many plates of prime rib later, the BBQ section was hands down the best, I made my way to the colorful array of desserts. By this point in the night a lot of the gelato was gone, but I ate a bunch of mochi balls, and a multitude of little plates. 

I loved the food. My only criticism has to be the price. Were this buffet 10-5 dollars cheaper it would be the best buffet, hands down, ever, period. I feel like you can get a similar level of quality at the M, but at the end of the day the price (and overall quality of food) is better here at Ceasars. I will have to be a repeat customer. It is just that 2013 was the year of the Bacchanal in vegas. My front desk man at the Riviera told me that they even closed their buffet because of people wanting this high quality expensive option like the Bacchanal. I hope that this trend continues and buffets in vegas all come to this quality.
All show and no go,  snow crab other then king crab,  Italian station and Mexico syations tasted very salty, waited 20 min to get in, counted 25 empty tables,  deserts tasted weak, would not go back

I came here twice in 2 days and LOVED both times!  They have TONS of FRESH options, and the dessert table is amazing!

The first time we came was for breakfast, but we stayed through lunch.  Then I came back for Sunday brunch.

Here's what I remember they served:
- Seafood (oysters, mussels).
- Mini red velvet (and regular) pancakes.
- Waffles.
- Made to order omelette's.
- Eggs Benedict.
- Salads.
- Pizzas.
- Bread & cheese station.
- Chinese station: sumai and other dim sum options included (YUM!).  and they had DUCK - MY FAVE!  
- Dessert table: macarons, cake, cookies, gelato, and MORE!  I wish I started here first, ugh.  Oh and they had made to order dessert crepes during Sunday brunch.

* This is all I can remember, but they have WAY more than this!

Some portions are small (like the red velvet pancakes), and others served just right (not too much and not too little - like pizza, duck, and other stuff).  I loved the cute plates that the smaller portions came in!

We got the best service from Aurelio. He always checked in on us to refill our drinks and clean our table.  

What I loved most about this place is the food is FRESH.  I kept refilling my plate with duck, and each time it was warm.  Avoid the wait by going early!  

Their $17 million renovation was SO WORTH it because the buffet here before was nothing compared to this.  They did a complete 180!

Favorite buffet in Las Vegas. All buffets are expensive, but this one is actually worth it. Huge selection of quality items, even at brunch. The Asian aspect is what does it for me, a whole section of delicious cuisine. Seafood station is stocked even during breakfast hours.

This place is espensive than other buffet I've ever been. I love their oysters it's really fresh, they have variety of food. Most of them are really good but some are kinda salty,the soups are okay,the sushis good and some of the dessert are very sweet but some are good too. So I guess it balance out. I would go again and try this place out when we get back.
$127 dinner for two people but worth it! Rack of lamb, all seafood, fresh sushi, truffle fries, prime rib, etc. Great food!

On my third trip to Vegas, I went with my Partner In Dining. He's the one who chose this spot to eat. 

Everyone always raves about Wicked Spoon. Well, move over because the Bacchanal just took the wicked out of your spoon.

The best time to go is 30 minutes before lunch ends. That way, you get the lunch price and still get the dinner food. That's what I learned on my trip following this one.

The first thing that caught my eye was all the fresh juices! Guava, watermelon, mango, tamarind, horchata, orange, and jamaica. WOW did that keep me hydrated. But, be careful because they you'll get full.

The Bacchanal has the following sections:
Seafood: Oysters, crabs, shrimps, clams, and some other hot food items
BBQ Meats with all the Southern side fixin's
Tacos, made to order with every kind of salsa you could imaging
Cold Meats & Cheeses + honey comb
Italian pasta/pizza
(if you want your crab legs boiled, they can do it here just ask!)
Salads
Asian/Noodles/Sushi/Dim Sum
Desserts/Ice Cream/Sorbet

Seriously, pace yourself so you can eat everything.

Lunch is around $35 a person, and dinner is closer to $55.

Definitely worth it to eat here after a night out on the strip and your alcohol soaked liver is crying for help.

It's well air conditioned so bring a light sweater/jacket so you can eat comfortably.

Until next time, don't forget your ID!

I would love to give zero stars if I could. This was by far no where near the best buffet in Vegas. The one hour wait was not worth the crappy food that we had to experience, and cheap, nearly impossible to drink wine. Half of the items that were advertised were not available such as cheese and meats, and the food quality was terrible.  I would prefer to dine at a Chinese buffet and it would cost me 4 times less than what we paid there which was $156 for two. Ribs were never available or burnt, the crab was soaked in water and had no flavor, and the oysters tasted so bitter I was worried that they were not fresh. The worst part is that my bf got food poisoning right after which prevented us from going out afterwards . Buttom line, never again.

Went here as the first restaurant with my buffet of buffet pass. The line was long but fortunately they have a nice queue system so we did not wait at all. Just checked in, got a text message a hour later when our table was ready. 

This buffet is far better than any of the other buffets included in the 24hr buffet. I loved the shrimp, crabs and oysters. The macaroons were also top notch. Everything I had was above average except for the Asian section. Below average ramen and sushi, but that is expected when eating at a buffet.

Update: went again in 2015 and the quality definitely went down. The oysters were not nearly as fresh and it was definitely a disappointment relative to our first experience at this restaurant.
Crab legs were smaller than expected. It was nice to go, but it's one and done for me. So many better options to eat in Vegas.

The wait can be very long but if it's more than an hour, go with the VIP Pass, it's $20 but worth it at times. The food is amazing, the selection is like no other and service is good. Certainly one of the better buffets in Las Vegas but will come at a price so hope you aren't easy to sticker shock!

The wait is long... so don't come here NOT expecting to wait. If you are impatient, ask your friends to line up for you... that's what I did =)

The selection of food was good. American, japanese, Chinese, italian, meat, seafood, desert... its a buffet, the more variety the better. The quality of the food is definitely better than your average vegas buffets. Many of my friends choose this over the other ones. I don't go buffets much but I can say I will for sure come back next time... and have my friends wait for me LOL jp

Best buffet on the strip!!

Didn't like paying Holiday prices on a Saturday-2 days AFTER the holiday. We paid $59.99 a person for brunch!!

I had a whole bunch of things! From Dimsum to Pizza! From Salad and to Mexican food! Beef lasagna, mac & cheese, biscuits and gravy! I was in carb heaven!! 

Loved this place! I would visit here every single time I'm in Vegas!!

Bottom line, I will never go here again. Even if they comp my meal, I would decline without giving it a second thought. If you have the notion to come here, do yourself a favor and find another buffet. Bellagio and Aria have really good ones and aren't as expensive and they have better tasting food.

I'm not sure who paid off the people claiming this is the best buffet in Las Vegas, but I've never been more disappointed in a restaurant with so much hype. I've been to Vegas several times over the years and tried a lot of the big buffets, but never made it here. I decided the most recent trip would finally be the time I go, although the main deciding factor was the 20% off you get at Mr. Chow with your buffet receipt. I can now say, I'd rather just pay full price than have to go here again.

We arrived around 5pm when the line was minimal and got seated fairly quickly. As we were being seated, the line had grown to at least 100 people. I've never seen so many people get in a line so quickly in a short amount of time. This had to be a good sign, right? Wrong.

The service was absolutely atrocious and one of the worst staff I've ever experienced. We got seated and our waiter took our non-alcoholic drink order quickly, but we also asked for a wine menu. The waiter returned with drinks, but no menu, and left. We didn't see him again for 10 minutes, still with no menu. We found a manager and asked for the menu, and he said the waiter would take care of it. Did he come back with one? Absolutely not. At this point, some of the party was starting to eat, but the ones waiting for wine had not gone yet (mainly out of principle). It took at least 25 minutes to get a wine menu, and another 5 minutes to actually get the wine. The water glasses went unfilled throughout the majority of the meal. It's not like they were understaffed, because the table next to and behind us were taken care of the entire time.

The food itself was very mediocre. The sweet potato tots were the best I've ever had in my life, so I had several of those. Outside of that, everything was your typical buffet quality food. The selection was large, but there was nothing that stood out that I wanted to go back and get more. Other than the tots, I didn't finish any of the items on my plate, including the disappointing dessert items. It's a buffet, so I tried a lot of different things, but I don't feel like I stuffed myself. However, the rest of the night I felt awful and a bit nauseous. I definitely think it was the food I had here.

Ate here last week. Always nice to jump the long buffet line with my diamond card. Service is fast and attentive. Everything we ate was at least good. Seafood is very fresh. Meats are excellent as well. Some of the cooked dishes are hit or miss but a few of them are so good you would think it was from a 5 star restaurant. Desserts have been better in the past. They seem to be lacking flavor and freshness. At almost 60$ for dinner I expect a little bit more quality all around.
Very good fare. Exceptional selection with fantastic variety. Be ready for a long wait. You may want to consider paying extra for the express line (extra $20)

One of the better buffets Vegas has to offer. Coming here on a Saturday, the price per person was $52 + tax. (-1 dollar if you have their players card). 

The wait time wasnt too bad. Since they changed it to the electronic "fast pass" system, our wait was about an hour. You can also input your cell number for text reminders. We decided to walk around the forum shops. 

We got through to pay fairly quick and were seated maybe, 5-10 minutes later. We were seated right next to the Dessert Station, right where the chocolate dipped strawberries were. *drools* 

First plate, meat station ! Both Doriee and I went for this first. Main reason we came here was because a friend came into town, and wanted lamb chops for dinner. Aside from our usual place to get lamb chops, we decided to try a new place. Since he hasnt been to the Bacchanal Buffet, here we went ! (despite my crying wallet Q_Q) Back to the story. When i arrived at the meat carving station, i asked for a slice of prime rib. then the lamb chops. here's how the conversation went between the carver and myself

Me: Can i get some lamb chops?
Chef: How many? 
Me: uhh 4?
Chef: 4? 5? 10?
Me: *joking* however many you want to give me ! ! !

dot dot dot . . .

*watches the chef use his tongs, and dig deep into the platter of lamb chops and grabbed all it can, and piled it on my plate.* For the record, he put SEVEN lamb chops on my plate. CHALLENGE ACCEPTED ! OM NOM NOM ! He did the same thing with Doriee but she stood firm on her request of 3, and would just pick off mine if she wanted more. 

To give an idea on the SIZE of these lamb chops. In comparison to like the the lamb chops from Koi (Australian? New Zealand?) or from Brio Tuscan Grille, these were at least 2-3x the size... EACH.. oh boy... what did i get myself into. They were heavy enough to make my arm tired from carrying it around to get more food ! x_x I could easily say, they were an easy 1-2lb of MEAT. yeah i ate it all. Meat temp wise, was a hit and miss. throughout everyone at the table, we got about a 50% chance of getting a perfect med rare cook. other 50% was medium or higher. Flavor was good. Overall great lamb chops !

Prime rib was a bit dry. Kind of sad. 

Crab was hot (station now at italian area). Butter still by the seafood station though. 
Cocktail shrimps were huge. Enough to make me take 2 bites instead of the usual 1 bite chomp-age. 
Oyster was fat and fresh. Not completely clean but not bad. I think i had a baby pearl in mine too XD 

Chicken Ginseng Soup is NOT in individual clay bowls anymore. I guess thats a good thing, so it prevents me from burning my fingers over and over trying to get it... Lol. Flavor was pretty good. I do believe they added salt to the soup though (we never do at home). No sight of ginseng anymore (sad ! i like eating ginseng too) 

DESSERTS !

yeah by the time i reached this stage, i was pretty stuffed over limit already. Previously noted chocolate strawberries were all gone for the night. Limited to 1 per person. 

Souffles ! my fav ! fresh made to order ! piping hot out of the oven !

pistachio - Light ! flavorful ! little sweet ! great with a cup of coffee ! 
chocolate - super rich x_x chocolate-y ! DEFINITELY needed the coffee otherwise i'd have trouble finishing this. 
churros - short pieces of churro, freshly made. nice and hot. filled in the middle with a pastry cream. 

Overall experience. Great ! Service was a bit slow on picking up used/empty plates. Friend was happy with his experience (he's quite picky).

I ate to the point where i didnt have much room in me to breathe ! doriee can attest to seeing my difficulty in breathing.. short quick breathes only x_x

Best Buffet I had! Me and my girlfriend were in Vegas and we made this buffet a 'Must go to' before our trip back to Chicago.
This buffet has increased the standards so high for the potential a buffet can have! Why can't Chicago have one of these with our high city tax rates!? Lol.
We went in early December. Virtually no line at 3pm (start for dinner)  I was very impressed by the pre cut crab legs, the plenty tasteful options to overload and diversify your palette, and just overall experience. We will be back!

Not impressed! Food wasn't bad but it isn't as good as people say it is & the service needs improvement, all in all it wasn't worth the money nor the wait.  

Waiting in the long line is so awful due in part to the lack of courtesy of those waiting in front or behind you. We had the worst people around us, really loud big group in front of us & group behind us constantly getting in our personal space either bumping us or breathing too closely. VERY uncomfortable!  Their msgText app seems like a good idea but be prepared to still wait a Looong time after you come back! 

The food: cold mac & cheese, dry fried chicken, cuts of meat weren't good (too fatty or not seasoned well). Sushi wasn't too bad, crab legs were decent and the dumplings were very good. Dessert was great taste wise, but the lady at the crepe station wasn't friendly & gave me an attitude because I ordered two crepes (one for hubby & one for me). Every worker at the dessert section (except gelato area) seemed extremely stressed & unhappy...they were also out of plates! 

Our server messed up our drink order, no big deal; it happens, but then he wouldn't come back to refill our drinks. He kept us dry :( NEVER COMING BACK. Left feeling full & dirty but not satisfied.

It has been long time before I stopped at this place, overall everything was great. Everything that you expect to have in a buffet will be there some of the food is nice and hot and some of the food is miss. But I do agree with other reviewers this is the best place for buffet.

I have wanted to try this buffet for the LONGEST TIME!  It opened about 2 years, and I did not have the opportunity to go yet. My best friend was visiting and she also wanted to try it.  She did the 24 hour buffet and paid an additional $30 to go to this buffet. 

We went for Sunday brunch. The holiday pricing was $52.99 for brunch and about $64 for dinner. Ouch. There was a total reward discount, so we went off to get a card. They do have a new check in system where you enter your information, and they will text you within the time. We were told we would be seated within 2 hours and 30 min. After an hour they texted us, and we were to wait in line for about another 40 min. So, I guess the text is the estimated total wait time. 

The Sunday Brunch came with unlimited mimisas, and we both never tried it. So, we were like why not. The lines for seafood and meat were super long! There was a lobster benedict that tasted amazing! There was a cheese pizza with mushrooms and I believe it was riccota chese that was amazing! I also tried the lamb chops that were pretty tasty. Their Asian station was awesome! The pork shumai and everything tasted amazing.

In order reviews, they had a souffle station, but when I went there, I only saw a crepe station and a shaved ice station at the dessert station. 

Now, why the three stars. The wait time for everything was horrendous. After waiting in that long line, we would still have to wait in long lines and wait. Plus, it was super expensive. It was good, but expensive!

I been waiting for years to finally try this place but in the end, I feel that this place is a little overhyped. Came here on a Friday night around 6pm, waited only about 10 minutes for a table of three. Lucky for us we beat the rush because around 6:30pm the line was looong. They have two separate lines, one regular line and another for parties of 8+. This place is definitely on the pricey side ($60 per person with tax included) and honestly, I had better buffets here in Vegas that are cheaper. They do however have the most food selection out of all the other buffets but the food quality isn't that great. 

Favorite/must try dishes:
-Prime rib: my first slice was overcooked and dry. Second slice was heavenly and just melts in your mouth. Guess it is a hit or miss. 
-Lamb chop: my favorite dish the whole night !! It was seasoned perfectly, juicy and delicious. Yumm! (I'm kinda drooling thinking about this right now..) 
-Fresh juice (from the juice bar, not the menu you order from the waiters): You can definitely tell they are made from real fruits ! Particles sink to the bottom of the bottle, just like how it should be! 
-Cheese: I love cheese *__* They have about 5 different cheese choices and they're all delicious! Main complaint is that they don't have much crackers you can smear this delicious goodness on. 
-Chocolate dipped cheesecake pop: omg these were delicious! moist on the inside, and dipped in chocolate. my favorite dessert the whole night. 


The "mehhh..could be better" dishes:
-Raw oysters: these were good but lazily prepared ! :( The oysters weren't cut off from their 'stem' to the shell and there was sand in them. Sigh...
-Macarons: yuck. They were soggy. Why are macarons soggy?! 
- Beef ribs: overcooked and dry. (come on guyssss.) you can tell behind the glass window (before even getting them) that they were.

Of course I tried way more than what I listed here, but overall I was not impressed. I expected high quality food for a $60 buffet but all I ended up with is a large variety/huge buffet with average to low quality food.

I don't care what anyone says but this is still the best hands down buffet ever ! Coming to Las Vegas bacchanal is always a must. I really don't mind paying the price nor waiting in line. Every time I come here it's always during dinner time so you can imagine how long the wait time is suppose to be. I always get told it'll be around 3 hours from where I stand but honestly I don't have to wait no longer than an hour and a half. Time goes by quick, it's better being more hungry so everything tastes 10xs better. I seriously love how clean this buffet is, I've been to a lot of buffets and it tends to get so dirty and messy with food spilled everywhere . 

If anyone has been to RIOs buffet just imagine bacchanal exactly like that with the food variety but better quality ! One down fall is I see people's reviews about the pho here and how great it is, honestly it's not that good .. it's whatever's in my opinion only because I'm from oc and we have a bunch of pho restaurants down here ours is so much better compared to bacchanal. I must say the udon though is on point as well as the ramen even though I'm not a ramen person. I can go on and on about this place but let me wrap it up really quick 

guys, this is a must try when in Vegas !

We arrived a bit past 3 on a Tuesday and there was no line at all. We were a bit surprised because we came prepared to buy express passes due to how long the wait was the last time we came back in 2013 (didn't get to eat, left line about 30 minutes into a 2.5 hour wait). Honestly, I have trouble understanding all of the hype of this buffet. It is decent buffet food but don't expect anything close to fine dining. Maybe it is because my husband and I are seafood sensitive and thus skipped that station (a lot of people were crowded around it). The American section was decent, with many options of meat including brisket, ribs, lamb chops, sausage, etc. I'm a huge fan of brisket and so I asked for some of that from the carver.  He gave me a very generous slice covering half of my plate but sadly I wasn't able to finish it because it was very fatty and didn't really have the taste or texture of the brisket I eat. Mac and cheese, however, was delicious. We had a bit from each section of the buffet except for seafood, and there was nothing particularly special but unfortunately quite a few items that we thought were bad. We're foodies and tend to love buffets... I'm just not sure what went wrong here, but we left disappointed.

It is pretty much as good as everyone says it is.  The food choices are incredible.  Like, literally my plate was full after I looked at just 1/4 of the food (not including the desserts).  Some of my favorites were the sweet potato tater tots, chips and guacamole, mashed potatoes and gravy and baked beans.  They had really cool stations that I had never seen at another buffet before, such as artisanal cheese.  I would definitely come back because the food was good and there were a TON of options so if you have a party that has picky eaters, they will likely find something up their alley.

The hostess who sat us was also very nice.  When she found out that my sister had been to the buffet before and recommended that I come, she thanked my sister for returning and suggesting I visit.  They have to know that word of mouth marketing is really strong and you can tell that everyone takes their jobs very seriously.  They had more staff on hand (cleaning tables, setting tables, serving, preparing food) than any other buffet.  They are obviously spending a lot of wages, but the quality of that really comes through.  I even asked someone at the dessert station about desserts without nuts and she didn't know she she checked with someone instead of just guessing (as happened to me at other buffets).  That follow up, even if simple, goes a long way with me.

With that being said, the price was ridiculous.  it was $75 for two of us for lunch.  I know they have to charge that much because of the seafood and sushi, but as a girl with simple tastes, my dinner probably only cost them a couple dollars to make, at most.  Considering how shitty all the other buffets were, though, I would gladly spend more to be able to eat here.

Waited for 30 mins before discovering that you can pay extra $15 and get in express line.  When I told person at the counter she did not even offer to expedite our entry.  We kept having to wait behind the VIP's.  Really amazing that after waiting in initial line we had to wait an ADDITIONAL 30 mins before we were seated.  I was really surprised that no one made mention of this until the other day stating it took 90mins to get seated.  Really irksome was that we called ahead and were told it would be around an hour wait, but when we talked to the manager he said it was really taking more like 2.5 hours.  

**What you really need to know is that a server told me that on Thanksgiving the wait is 4-6hours, and the price is $75.  What?!?  Who is waiting that long?**

Best buffet in Las Vegas. Crab legs...different kinds of seafood to choose. American, Mexican, Italian, Asian food and so on. During brunch time, there are four kinds of fresh pressed juice! Early bird brunch is so worth it! (Just come before 10am)

Pretty good. Food was fine- though there was some filler. The wait was long than estimated- so be prepared for that. The dining room was comfortable and nice. 

I enjoyed myself and may come back. Wouldn't say it was great though. The server was really good and prompt. There is a ton of variety so it is great for a big group because everyone will find something they'll like.

Just look at all the pictures online and you'll see what it gets 5 stars.  The food is pretty amazing for a buffet.

So many small single servings of items, and on individual plates!  There is almost someone at every station willing to help customize an item for you.  The food is top notch for a buffet.  

I've been there for breakfast and dinner now.  It's expensive, but so's a steak or good seafood restaurant.  

The key is the serving sizes are perfect for you to try a little of everything without feeling guilty for taking too much food.  This get pulled off brilliantly.  

If you're going to splurge for a buffet, this is my choice.  Keep it up Bacchanal!
For the price I felt the food could have been much better.  The desserts many were bland.  I thought the Wicked spoon was much better.
