$53 for Sunday dinner. I've been wanting to eat here and my family finally took me on my birthday. The only thing worth talking about was the lamb. It was amazing. Everything else was mediocre. No ones been posting recent photos of the food and I think after it was dubbed the #1 buffet in Vegas, it let go of itself. What happened to the French macaroons, crazy gelato flavors, fresh honey from the honeycomb and all the other goodies ppl have been boasting about? I feel hella cheated. As for the the chefs, I feel bad for them. Some ppl just don't have common sense. Idk how many times the chefs have told ppl to stop eating on the line and to take the plates with the food they literally transferred onto their personal plate via their hands. Smh* ppl!

My wife and I tried to dine at Bacchanal on Wed Nov 28 at 6pm. Upon arriving at the entrance which was in chaos, we were told the wait time would be at least 2 1/2 hours. I understand the buffet is wildly popular and why, but Caesar's needs to go back to the drawing board and devise a way to better meet customer demand. A wait time of 2 1/2 hours is simply not acceptable. We left immediately and won't be going back anytime soon.

Absolutely terrible, low class, and rude customer service! The staff/hostesses at the entrance were lost and confused and took forever to seat us, then as we exit they disrespected us regarding a minor misunderstanding. We are Vegas locals for 16 years and this has been the absolute worst experience we have had. My family and I are very offended by their unprofessional attitude. We paid $50 per person for terrible service and mediocre food. There are definitely much better buffets in town, especially for seafood lovers. We will never return to this one!

It was really good. I think the thing that is different between this and a regular buffet is that they serve food that is very gourmet. So I think you get your money worth if you like seafood or steak they have very good salmon if your a fish fan and you come here try it it has a kick of spice. Overall was a good experience only thing is the wait time is crazy and the price is pretty high but it's clean and offers a variety of food. Sister loved the chicken waffles and brother liked elk sliders and the gelato ice cream. So give it shot and bring yo wallet. V.i.p access like a hundred a pop and regular to stand in line is like 50.

This buffet was sooo good! I went around 5pm luckily the line wasn't so long. When I entered there was an array of delicious food, I stuck to mostly seafood: crab legs, oysters, salmon, ceviche...pretty good and fresh! I had a crepe for dessert I was in heaven. They also had fresh juices which were tasty. Perfect way to end my trip :) 
Great service also!

Our 1st visit a few years back (thanksgiving evening), the food and selection was amazing! This was our 2nd visit and we were excited for the experience again, but that did not happen. The 1st and 2nd time we did expect a long wait per usual what made this last experience unpleasant was the organization of the so called "line." There is a ticket check in where it gives you a stamped time to come back to check in, little did we know it would be another line to wait (after already waiting over 2 hours for our time stamp). The line was long which is some what understandable due to it being Christmas weekend. What was really making a lot of people upset in line was that we all have time stamped tickets and people were in line even though their time was not up to go in line. Our ticket said 6:25pm, which is the time we went to the line and then being surprised there was another wait of over an hour, the issue is that people ahead of us had times at 6:45 and even 7 and 8! The security did nothing after many people complained. There is no point to this ticket system, I would of waited the 3-4 hours in an actual line, where we can keep our appropriate spot and keep things in order. We ended up leaving and so did many others due to the frustration. The security is worthless they don't check tickets, they just stated "no one is getting any special treatment unless your a diamond or platinum card holder." This was truly a disappointment.

Many food options. Literally a huge variety. However I can't say that anything was exceptionally delicious. 
Still a very impressive experience. But not worth the high price tag.

Took my daughter for breakfast and was overwhelmed.  First plate was fried chicken n waffles, shrimp and grits, steak and eggs, and yogurt with granola.  All good.  Then I got an omelette, which was cooked very well, and then slathered on a bunch of fresh guacamole and salsa.  Finally got some ice cream and cookies.  I missed about 80 percent of the stuff there, too.  Worthwhile for us because it was early and not crowded at all.

Hands down! I am local and loved M, Rio, Greenvalley, wicked spoon all the way. Im frugal to spend 60.00/person but this one is worth it. One star more than wicked spoon and aria' buffet. Seafood and asian cuisine good. Line is definitely long in the weekend. I just wish more pasta options. 

Kudos to our server Felipe who has been great. and, Sergio from the American steak session who delighted with a wow customer service

Holy crap! There was food everywhere. And good food. I went in for the seafood first. After two heaping plates of crab legs, I was worried I overloaded myself on so much seafood that I wouldn't be able to enjoy the meats. Nope. I was good for another plate from the meat carving station where the prime rib and brisket were aaaawesome. Throughout, I dabbled around in the different areas (Asian, Latin, Italian) for bites of different sides. You know it's a good buffet when you skip the mac-n-cheese! We started at around 8:30pm and closed them down at 10:00pm. Admittedly, it was a little late to eat but actually ended up being perfect since we didn't have to wait in long lines and I could go straight to bed after eating myself into disrepair. 

If you're going to go to a buffet, you might as well make an event of it, and Bacchanal is the perfect place to do just that.

Five stars for food and negative four stars for the worst service. I used to work in customer service and offer lots of understanding, but the service here today was horrendous. I will not be coming back, which is a shame because the food selection and flavors were wonderful. None of the dishes were cleared off the table and everything was overflowing, and they didn't get us any refills or anything. The servers won't make eye contact so they don't have to serve you. I'm leaving $40 tip, but don't mistake that for good service. It was absolutely terrible. Do not come here if you want to be treated decently.

OMG. They have everything for everyone. The price tag is a bit steep but it is worth every penny. Mexican? Check. Chinese? Check. Continental? Check. Will you have a blowout while sitting and stuffing your face full of food? You betchya!

The wait is quite long; however the food is worth it.  They also hike up the prices during holiday weekends.  The select is remarkable, and the food is served fresh.  It is one of the best buffet around.  If the wait was not so long, it would give it more stars.  But as I stated before, the food is well worth it.

Please lower your expectations when you come here! The food was just ok. The selection was not what I expected for the price. Nothing much exciting to choose from. The meats are basically the same for lunch and dinner, but they add lamb and beef ribs.The Wagyu Steak and Prime Rib were both flavorless and not tender. The person who was serving at the carving station gave a very rude lecture about the difference between rib and prime rib when I accidentally said "rib" instead of "prime rib". 

Dessert bar looks fancy but it's pretty mediocre. Nothing made me want to take a second bite. Sushi selection and Chinese station are not good. Even shrimp wasn't good quality. 

The service is really bad. We had plates at our table for the entire meal. We got no drink refills until I wave down someone close to our departure. We wanted coffee at the end, but again no one came to get any drink order. 

It's supposed to be one of the best of Vegas, don't give it a high expectation!

This was kind of disappointing. The Chinese duck was always empty-I went back 3 times and just skin and bones were there. Also all of their roasted meat tasted smoked and that is not what I want. I loved the oyster shooters, the shiu mai and char siu was very good. $100 for 2. Then I splurged and bought Veuve Cliquot for $120 -only triple what I pay for at Costco. But after 1/2 a bottle, a bug was in my glass. I brought it to the manager who said it was still alive (but drunk) and brought me a whole new bottle. So I spent less for more champagne.

Last day in Las Vegas ready to drive home! Last thing on my list stop by at THE buffet Cesar palace !! Food amazing but what was more amazing the Staff from Sandra my server to the sweetest staff I have ever meet chef  Daniel carver Roy and my buffet experience ended with incredible experience to meet Dessert chef Carman and dessert chef Delmar the sweetest man I have ever meet ! I even saw him talk a special request to a nice coupe sitting next to me ! The restaurant is incredible decor food amazing . Can wait to return and see chef Delmar scoop me another mango ice cream ! Thank you Delmar God bless

My favorite buffet in Vegas! It is pricey but the quality and selection can't be beat for a buffet. I always look forward to the oysters and warm crab legs. The variety of desserts is the best. I had 3 plates of desserts on our last visit. The passion fruit tart is my favorite. We always leave feeling way too full.
Our buffet was really good, but our server Esmeralda Juarez went above and beyond tp serve us and make conversation with us, and we will definitely come back for both the food and service.
This is always a great place to pig out. Just remember to bring all of your diabetic supplies. Might as well take your cholesterol medications like... simvastatin.

Best buffet ever!! Words cannot explain, how wonderful this place is, from the food, service and ambience!!! 

I highly, highly recommend!! :)

*** PLEASE READ *** This place is highly overrated.  Place don't waste your time (2 hours total wait, probably more) and money. I'm a local and I could name more than 10 other restaurants that are better tasting and value than this place.  Food is pretty much mediocre and most of them are even dry. I love meat, and surprisingly the only thing that I honestly enjoyed was the watermelon and feta cheese salad.  I was really dissatisfied with this buffet/restaurant and I felt sorry for my Dad for he celebrated his birthday there. Again it's all hype!

PS 

No exaggeration, but if I could only put no star ...

My review is the only one you need to read. This is a good breakfast buffet. Wicked Spoon is better. The Bellagio buffet has really gone down-hill, don't even bother. If you have to do a buffet then either this one or Wicked Spoon is the way to go.  I can't believe I got suckered into going to the Paris buffet which I know is awful, and there's a long line like they're giving it away for free (they're not). Luckily I'm a diamond status Harrah's member so I don't wait.   

I digress.  My favorite 3 breakfast places in Vegas are Bouchon at the Venetian, Bacchanal at Caesar's, Wicked Spoon at Cosmo, and a little diner on Fremont with the best darn diner food ever. Can't remember it's name but it's on the end of Fremont and had the original phone number "1" you can figure it out. Best pancakes etc.....

Delicious and wide variety of food. Loved every bit of it. Everything tasted so good and I would love to come back. If you love seafood then you should definitely try the buffet here when in Vegas. A disclaimer too after having such amazing food you will not be hungry for the rest of the day

When I read other reviews, I wondered if I went to the same Bacchanal Buffet as the others did, because the experience I had was almost totally different. 

At least, we agreed on one thing, it cost $56 plus tax. With this price, I think we should lift the bar a little bit higher if we are honest. However, I soon determined that you actually don't need high standard to classify Bacchanal Buffet to be poor. My first question was "Where are the hundreds of selections as said by some reviews?" Their selection is actually quite limited, at least much less than the buffet at M Casino or Rio Casino in Las Vegas.

If seafood is considered to be superb at Bacchanal, then where is lobster? And where is sashimi? You see none of these, but they dare to display several lobsters right at the front of the restaurant in a glass container to fool people. If they don't serve lobsters, this kind of act is evidently unethical, sort of misleading, misrepresented, and even cheating. 

The night I went was on Saturday, March 12th, and I had tasteless prime rib, over salty beef rib, rock-hard lamb chop, warm-to-cold Asian watery rice (Congee), and clumsily chopped BBQ pork. Evidently, Bacchanal's food could  be claimed to be good only by those who seldom had quality or fine food and probably happened to be at Bacchanal to try an expensive food for the first time in their lives. If you're a bit more familiar with Las Vegas, you easily can find another buffet of much better quality with much less price at some other casinos of the same Caesars group in Las Vegas such as Planet Hollywood or Flamingo. 

If you went to the same Bacchanal as I did, can you show me where their wide range of selected fruit is? Why could I only see some dull-white watermelon, sour-no-sweet pineapple, grainy cantaloupe, and nothing else? 

By paying the pricy charge, I thought I should've been served with some finely prepared food there but honestly speaking, I didn't see any dishes that can be labeled as exquisite ones. Nevertheless, I did see arrays of pizza, taco,French fries, fried sweet potatoes, poorly layered mini-hamburger, simply stuffed mini-hotdog, heavily soy-sauced fried rice, over-oily fried noodles, and so on --- those common, cheap, mediocre and inauthentic items.      

Besides being deeply disappointed by their food quality and food selection, I was also deeply amazed by the poor service rendered by their cashiers, ushers, some waiters and waitresses, some bus boys, and most of food servers behind the counters. They all looked so grumpy and most were arrogant to customers.

By far the best Buffet in town.
When we go we always request our favorite server - his name is Vince, he is THE BEST server there.  Vince is very accommodating and very attentive to those in his area, be sure to ask for him!
Also, Elaine is the most gracious hostess in the buffet.  She too is extremely accommodating and very pleasant to talk with.  Elaine makes you feel at home and welcome.
A fantastic duo!

The unquestionable gold standard for Vegas buffets. The line is long, (we went on a Monday night and waited 45 minutes) but the buffet is worth every minute of the wait. Absolutely decadent. Everything you can imagine. I was completely stuffed and then I discovered an entire room of food I hadn't even touched! Next time I go to Vegas I'm not wasting any time with other buffets. I'm gonna park myself at Caesar's Palace and have somebody roll me to my room when I'm done. Great value, great fun. If you only can go to one buffet, go here!

This place sucks so fucking bad. We are waiting in line for almost one hour. They only let VIP members taking the available sits as soon as possible. My legs are fucking hurt right now and I just want to yell to somebody. I have to pay 60 fucking dollars to experience this shit. Don't do this guys!! Go anywhere else for dinner.

This buffet was amazing! It was a bit pricey, but worth every penny. Luckily, we were seated right at the end of brunch 2:30 & dinner starts at 3pm. We paid the brunch price and were able to enjoy the dinner options. I loved the crab legs!!!

Went for the brunch with mimosa option. It's over $50 per person so come hungry and be prepared to eat your weight in bacon.

Bacchanal has it all! I like to start with meat, have some meat in the middle and end with some meat. Potatoes, bread, rice, etc? No thanks.

The slab bacon was perfect. Melt in your mouth tender. The regular bacon was also good. After sampling more parts of the pig and cow, I moved on to the shrimp, crab and salmon. I consumed several animals when it was all said and done.

All great! Service is great! Say hello to your server and treat them well and your mimosa glass stays full. I also tipped well because the servers and cleaners work hard.

Here's my tip- it opens at 8am and people start to seriously make their way over there by 10am. Get there early and there is no line and more animals to eat than you can shake your now hardened arteries at.

Good quality, right price and the many features that allowed for a really good experience was involved. 

The folks at this Pricey but, quality buffet know their stuff. 

The only bad thing is, I can say, without a doubt. 

The crab legs are skinny and shouldn't be .

I picked this lunch buffet because of the decent rating from Yelp!  

The price is $35.99 per person

Overall, the choice of foods variety is somewhat limited with what other competitors offering.  Foods are so-so.  With this kind of price, I would go for Wicked Spoon at least they have good desserts.

At one point while at Bacchanal, sometime after eating a plate overflowing with at least a pound of crab legs and before taking on a final slice of cheesecake (one of the 5 desserts I ravaged), it dawned on me:

"Oh god. I'm like one of the citizens of the Capital in the Hunger Games. What have I become?!"

I quickly parried that thought however; as much as I want to imagine myself in the vein of a half-starved (and ruggedly handsome) hero of District 12, sometimes...it's nice to indulge. 

And at Bacchanal, indulge you will. 

From the get-go, you know you are going to try to cram as much food as humanly possible into your stomach to try and "claw back'" some of the steep entry price (~50$). As a long distance runner with seemingly hollow legs who burns thousands of calories a workout, I think I ended up okay at Bacchanal, maybe eating $30 or so dollars worth of food at its retail price. I can live with that. 

Beyond calculations of value (which are almost meaningless in Vegas, which seems to be fueled on the wispy fumes of luxury itself), the fare is par for the course. Everything I ate was of high quality and tasty. 

One thing I didn't like so much was the blaring Euro-hip music. I think they blast it so you'll eat and leave more quickly, but...it was annoying not to be able to have conversations with the people I went with. 

Some things had an extra fine-tuned and endearing touch though, like the fish and chips in little metal frying crates or the Chinese dumplings in individual bamboo baskets (or maybe I'm easily impressed). 

Either way, those small details made the experience more than just a ridiculous gut-stuffing smorgasbord.

Recently visited this buffet for the first time on trip through Vegas. 

It's true what they say, the best buffet in Vegas! 

A bit pricey, but the quality of the food makes up for it. If you go with a party less than 6 expect that wait time to be about 1.5 hours. Which isn't so bad since there are a bunch of shops you can wonder while waiting. 

Definitely would visit again.

This was my first Las Vegas buffet experience and it did not disappoint. The selection of food was superb and the service was awesome. There was a ton of variety and everything tasted fresh and delicious. 

TIP: Get there at 10:30 (weekday) - right as breakfast is ending and they are turning over for lunch. You'll get brunch for the breakfast price which saves you a bit of $$. 

I will absolutely be back!

It was ok. Had the breakfast buffet. Champagne was mediocre (but hey it's unlimited so you get what you pay for ). Also, couldn't find the omelette station but they have one somewhere. They make crepes on the spot for you! Galore of ice cream selections. Interesting, try it if you can't decide where to go.

Third visit and service has gotten worse. I have never had great service here by any of their servers but yesterday's visit was the worst I've had.

We got there early for breakfast and were in line for a while and the lady asked us to move aside to a different line which made wait longer than the other line that we were already in.

For the two hours we were there, not once did our server mind us or refill any of our drinks. Not once did I get a water refill and watched our server interact  and chat with other guests and refill their drinks.

I had enough of watching this and asked to speak with the manager of the horrible service experience yesterday. She offered to take a statement from me and review the camera feed of our experience which I told I was fine with to speak with him about it. It was interesting to hear that she said that he was one of her best.  

I opted to take a full refund of our tip (we paid in advance) as he didn't deserve any of it.

I'm not sure what was going through his mind as he completely ignored us and gave more attention to those he deemed would probably give him a better tip.  My only guess is that we looked really young and not worth his time to serve.

TIP: Do not pre-tip here and tip at the end if you feel they deserve it. Service is spotty and inconsistent.

Food quality is better than average (best in Vegas), but service is horrible.
Totally worth it. You don't need to read reviews. Just go and eat there. So much variety and food that actually tasted delicious.

Was just ok not worth the money. Don't be fooled by the good reviews on here. Went for breakfast on a weekday and there was hardly any breakfast food. The meat from the carver was dry. They had the nerve to have "assorted fruit" but it was all pineapple (which I do like) and like 5 blueberries. Don't call it assorted if its 98% one fruit. I didn't see any giant crab legs. It was hard to find the made to order omelet station. Even after asking someone I still didn't find it.

Stay away from the Asian section. It was not good at all. I don't eat Panda Express but if I had to pick between Panda Express & The Buffet Asian food I would pick PE hands down.

The bagels tasted like some old stale store bought Sarah Lee Bagels. Also there was no cream cheese! How are u going to serve bagels w/o cream cheese 

The oatmeal didn't have toppings. Just brown sugar and cranberries. For upscale buffet I expected lots of options to top my oatmeal.

Don't waste your money and again please don't be fooled by the good reviews.

The BEST buffet I have EVER had in Vegas!  Had I known, I would have eaten only Lamb Chops....total restaurant quality and the star of the show!  The Peking duck with plum sauce wasn't too shabby either!  The Salmon was also enjoyable, and there's more than enough crab legs, oysters, and shrimp to go around,  Went at 4pm Thursday and got right in!  Desserts were great, like the M used to make.  Totally worth it!

Yum yum yum! This buffet is the king of all buffets. It has everything: an Asian station with many sushi choices and the freshest seaweed salad, a seafood bar with the freshest oysters, giant shrimp, the tangiest cerviche, paella better than Spain, and unlimited (of course) supply of mussels, clams and crawfish! They have an amazing carvery with brisket as good as Texas, ribs, and big juicy prime rib! They literally have everything you could possibly want to eat. And I swear, they have the best Pho (Vietnamese soup) I have ever had.

This is the first time that I ever went to a place that had all of my favorite foods, minus kimchi. Even my husband found these tiny kobe burgers that melted in his mouth. Oh and the deserts!!! Everything you can possibly want, in every flavor. I was so wooed that I even took out one of the cupcakes and took it on a photo adventure!

Now pricing - yeah its heck expensive...but here is tip: If you go about 10:30 am, then you get to have breakfast and lunch and pay $10 less. Also if you are a Total Rewards member, you get a dollar off.

We payed $160.00 for 2 people to eat.  This included tip and an extra $30.00 to line jump the line to pay.  They have lamb chops, crab legs and beef brisket all of which melt in your mouth.  The desserts were the same blah stuff you get at any of the buffets.  The dinner was definitely not worth the money but it was good.  If I would have skipped breakfast lunch and desert and just ate the 3 items I mentioned it would have been well worth the money, but despite my size I can't eat what it would have taken to make it worth the money.  I give it 3 stars for the quality of the food.  That being said Las Vegas buffets have gotten outrageous in price since the first time I went there over 10 years ago.  Viva Las Vegas!!!!!

The place look nice, service was good ( when u pay extra $35/person to check in faster) 
It was ok, nothing great for its price. 
Seafood Was just so so.
Lamp was most terrible one I ever taste ( they don't know how to cook it for sure ) .
The pics on Yelp was from 5ys ago. I did not see anything like that now. No lobster, fresh fish ...

This is the best buffet I have ever been to in my life!

Food: The number of choices is overwhelming, but my personal favorite was the Asian station with the fresh ramen noodle soup. It was remarkably close to Ippudo NY in terms of taste and quality. The variety of dim sum there was a nice authentic touch, and I was very delighted to eat them. The dessert kitchen was my second favorite with the made to order crepes and bananas foster dessert.

Atmosphere: Trendy and upscale decor. I loved the furnishings. The tables are also spaced nicely apart so that you can carry on a conversation.

Service: The hostesses, kitchen chefs, and cashiers were very nice, but the servers who cleared the tables were terrible. I asked two different servers to refill our water, and they did not. After 10 minutes, I then resorted to getting out of my seat, walking up to a server, and directly asking for water. I also watched a server drop his dishes although he was only carrying three at most. Two servers in my area were also remarkably slow in cleaning up the tables and picking up the empty dishes from the tables. For a $34.99pp buffet (on weekdays), I expect them to pick up my empty dishes more quickly. I noticed the servers in my dining area (close to the cashiers) spent more time chatting up the patrons than actually serving.

Bottom line: If I ever visit Las Vegas again, dining at this buffet is a must! I love buffets, and there is nothing like this one. I dream of eating here again. :)

We had a $25 dining credit, so we decided to use the credit at the Bacchanal Buffet, based on the reviews we saw. I was excited about the seafood section, but it wasn't anything to write home about (we live in the PNW, and we've access to better seafood buffets for half the price). Overall, we were disappointed, especially for the value. For two people with a $25 credit and no upgrades, the bill was still $105 with a tip. The service was also pretty spotty.

This Buffett was pretty good , quite a selection but overall if your planning on coming here personally I would recommend the wicked spoon Buffett in the cosmopolitan! They've got similar entrees but better service and flavor. And I think it's slightly cheaper as well.

The food:  4.5 stars.  Huge variety, selection, freshness!  Probably the best buffet I've visited.  Favorites include Alaskan king crab legs, oysters, and bone marrow., oh and d-lush desserts.  Half a star taken away because even though they charge for dinner pricing beginning at 3pm, not all dinner food is available until 5pm.  Boo lame.

The service: 3.5/5 stars.  Service was so-so.  Plates were cleaned promptly. Slow to get drink orders, had to ask for crackers and towlettes, and just overall not too friendly or happy service. But it was sufficient. 

-1 star because I saw gunk on plates, inside the saucers for condiments, and one plate I grabbed had some sticky gooey junk that was pretty gross.  Had to wash my hands pronto!

Been coming to Vegas for 40 years plus. The Buffet  is so so. Too expensive and service is poor. Bought the "Package" and $15 Bottomless Mimosas. Problem is, they don't have enough servers on staff to service their clientele. Was at Ceasar's Americano Cafe, and realized how outrageously  expensive they were. Two (2) Bloody Mary's and two coffee's for $40.00. Give me a fucking break. Went over to Bacchanal Buffet. $65 for two people and an additional $30.00 for bottomless Mimosas.
All good but under staffed, so our Mimosas went bottomless most the time. Been at Ceasar's Palace many, many times. Time to move onto another Hotel next time. Now I remember why I moved onto the Bellagio Hotel. Don't know exactly what Hotel next time, maybe Palazzo.  Been at Wynn, Four Seasons, Venetian. Mov'ing on. I must say, Vic & Anthony's Steak House was worth the Uber ride. Fantastic !!!!!

I've been debating what to rate this buffet, but feel I really can't go any higher than 2 stars. The food was probably 3 to 3 1/2 stars, the service was 1 star, so really I'd probably say this deserves 2 1/2 stars...which I'm choosing to round down.

We were so excited to eat here, seeing the rave reviews and hearing it was the "best buffet in Vegas". We purchased an online deal where you got the buffet, a line pass, and unlimited drinks for $44 for weekend brunch. The normal price is $40 for the buffet, $25 for the line pass (I think) and $15 for the drinks. So pricey, but seemed like a deal.

First off, with our deal you have to be seated before 10am. At 9:45 Sunday morning, the line wasn't really that long, so not sure the line pass bought us much.

We were seated in a corner, kind of behind a post. Weird spot, but the entire restaurant had kind of a weird ambiance. It was dim, with food in various locations, and just didn't have a great feel.

We started with dim sum, which was tasty, but you risked 3rd degree burns to access the steamed items! Very poor design, and I have to wonder if it was intentional so they didn't have to provide as much food LOL. The dim sum items were tasty, and the chicken and waffles was tasty, but everything else was pretty much unremarkable.

Quite a few items were out when I made trips, which to me is unacceptable. I saw a sign for lobster eggs benedict but never saw the item! They had crab legs, but I had no desire to eat that at 10am. Steak and eggs was seriously oversalted. Chilequiles were soggy. I don't remember much else, if that says anything LOL. Although to be honest, the desserts were absolutely delicious, and bar none the best part of this meal. $44 for dessert is pricey even by Vegas standards though! Creme brulee and pecan tart were the standouts.

Service was absolutely atrocious, though, which really ruined the meal. We had finished our first plates before we ever got drinks. "bottomless" mimosas is a meaningless term when you have to practically kidnap your waiter to get refills after 45 minutes! And our table was a disgusting mess of dirty plates that never got picked up (well not until my sister took out her phone and took a picture of the mess...someone saw that and came right away LOL).

I might eat here again if it was free, but I sure wouldn't pay and wouldn't go out of my way. I ate at the Wynn buffet later in the week and for half the price it was more than twice as good. Go there instead!

Going to start off by saying that this is still my favorite buffet of the ones I have visited. 

With that said, do I think it is worth the hefty price tag? Yes, if you have a really big appetite (I'm talking an ENORMOUS appetite). No, if you don't have the biggest appetite (I would fall into this category). There is great variety at Bacchanal and I think the quality of foods here is better than at most other buffets but at a large cost of $55 (pre tax and tip) for a weekday dinner- so I honestly would only come here if you're actually able to eat $55 worth of plates...otherwise the dining experience and quality is, in my opinion, better at other non-buffet establishments both on and off the strip. 

Moving on to the food, Bacchanal has a great seafood section. This last time the oysters weren't very sweet (being very large oysters) but everything else was pretty good- particularly the snails. I've also quite enjoyed their escargot and oyster shooters. The crab legs can be hit or miss, sometimes they're very salty and sometimes they're just perfect! Reminder that you can get hot crab legs as well in the Italian section! The meat section is also pretty good; I normally get the wagyu and prime rib and both are nicely tender. There are good options in all the other sections as well, though I am less familiar with them. I will note that while I don't normally go for too many carbs at a buffet, the noodle section here is surprisingly good! I really enjoy the laksa, pho, and udon here. The dessert section is also quite good- they have single serving desserts as well as made to order crepes and soft serve alongside gelato. 

The space is beautiful and everything is spread out nicely. I think some of the tables are put a little close to each other but it's not too big of an issue. Restrooms are all the way out next to the entrance. 

I would recommend Bacchanal only if you're 100% set on a buffet experience and have the time (long lines) and money to drop!
My absolutely favorite buffet on the las Vegas strip!!  Such high quality foods from all over the world. This is one experience you shouldn't miss out on'!!  Well worth the price
I love this place very clean and friendly! All type of food and all types of drinks i love this buffet! Best buffet in las vegas!!! Highly recommend it!!

Wow... quite the food extravaganza.  I wanted to do at least one of these crazy buffets and Bacchanal is about on par price with the rest and had slightly higher reviews.  Huge selection to choose from and most things were delicious.  The biggest letdown was the deserts, despite the selection and how nice they looked they tasted rather average... of course I may have just been overstuffed by that point.  There is a double line, one to pay then another to sit, so you may end up in line for quite a while.  I decided to go about 1045 for brunch (it's $5 cheaper if you go before 11) and proceeded to hang out there with a friend for almost two hours.  Is it worth the $35-50... eh... I suppose.  For Vegas it's worth it, but you can do better brunches for less in other cities.

Loved, loved, loved, loved, loved this eatery! I like to think of myself as a fine connoisseur of buffets and I had always heard good things about this place. But "good" was an understatement. This place was the Garden of Eden of buffets. I'm not going into full detail, but I will tell you that I tried a sample from every station and did to complain once (with the sushi, burger, and dessert bar being my favorites). If it were physically and mentally possible, I would eat here for the rest of my life. With friendly staff, a super-clean environment, and more food (of superior quality, no less) than I've seen in a fortnight, there is no doubt in my mind I will go to any other buffet while in Vegas.

For $55/person, I'm not totally convinced it's worth it, but that's just a personal opinion. I can't usually eat too much in one sitting anyway so buffets in general are not appealing. However, I heard such good things about this one I had to splurge. 

We went on a Sunday for brunch so the selection was great. They had bottomless mimosas for $10 extra. 

Things that stood out:
Long line, long wait. We were there for an hour before being seated. A woman mentioned we could pay to hold our place in line? Not sure if that's even a thing, but we didn't do it. 
They had crab legs! They were sliced in half to avoid all the hard work of cracking into them, and you could literally slide out the big meat pieces. So yummy!
No other dishes that really hit the spot. Sure, the food was good and there was a VERY wide variety like asian, mexican, american, etc., but I would take ONE phenomenal dish for $55 over a buffet of regular food. 
The dessert was great, though. Crepe bar looked so tasty but there was such a long line. Bummer. 
Clean restaurant, and waiters were attentive. Our glasses were always filled and they were quick to clean up after our dishes. 

We probably stayed about 2 hours, just sitting back and relaxing. No one rushed us. I would come back again if my group of friends wanted to go. But probably wouldn't of my own decision since I'm not a big buffet person.

We went around 1:15 on a Monday and got right in, no wait. It was lunch, but I'm not (too) ashamed to say we managed to stay until 3:00 when they brought out more of the dinner items (e.g. hot and cold crab legs).

The lemon basil sorbet was sublime. Each bite was like the first bite. And the orange beer sorbet is not to be missed.

Other delights were the Chinese BBQ pork, the sea bass, the Thai beef, and the sangria cherry cake.

It's a Vegas institution, so you might as well go once.

It was voted the #1 buffet in Vegas by USA Today.  Intrigued by this honor and ready to overindulge Vegas style, we skipped breakfast and headed over for a late lunch.

There are many stations:  Fresh Seafood, American BBQ, Mexican, Italian, and Asian.

The oysters were fresh and the jumbo shrimp was not overly cooked.  The cocktail sauce had a nice kick from the horseradish.  Off to a good start!

The prime rib was overcooked; even the rarest piece was medium-well at best.  

The meatball was tasty and not filled with breadcrumbs.  The pizzas had a nice crust and were satisfying.

Step away from the Asian selection.  An interesting amalgamation of Chinese, Thai and  Japanese.  The chow fun was dry, the sushi was what you'd expect at a buffet but the selection (only 3 kinds) was disappointing.  The char sui bao filling was yummy but the bread was hard and the har gow was gummy.

All in all, just okay.  Buffet includes soft drinks, tea and juice.  Price is steep, but Vegas is not cheap.  And, if you make it your only meal you come out ahead.

I came here for the lunch and there was a long line, expect to wait. By far this buffet had the most food selection however, not everything tasted so great. 

Scramble egg (1/5)
Lobster bisque (1/5) 
Seafood cocktails (4/5)
Snow crabs (5/5) - I love that they crack it open for you! 
Cucumber juice (4/5) 
Bacon (4/5)
Sausage (4/5) 
Lobster Benedict (1/5) - yolk was over cooked  
Asian duck (4/5) 
Gelato (5/5) 
Thai tea (4/5) - just a little too sweet 
Calm (4/5) 

Overall, great selections of food but the taste is okay. However, it's good to try at least once.

After learning about the new opening of Bacchanal at Caesar's, of course the fatty in me had to go and try it.  It was only a couple weeks after it opened and my god, the line is ridiuclously long! I came around 6:00 hoping that the line wouldn't be too bad but upon my arrival, the line was snaking around like it was Disneyland or something.

Not only was the line super long but the it was moving ridiculously slowwwww. I swear I was standing in the same place for at least 10 minutes before moving an inch. -_- I'm normally a patient person but just the way the line was moving it was going to take at least 2+ hours just to get seated.  After about a good 45 minutes, I said F*CK it and I decided to shell out the extra $15 bucks per person for the express.  Thankfully, NO ONE was at there and I literally got seated within 5 minutes. 

So, besides paying $50+ per person for this meal, I actually had a GREAT time! I immediately saw all the different selections and my mood quickly turned from hangry (hungry + angry) to super happy! (sappy?) Anyways, when you first arrive inside, you'll notice the long selection of seafood in the front.  I was quite impressed with all the mussels, oysters, and crabs that you get to choose from.  There is a guy in the back who can steam them for you too if you're not a fan of raw seafood.  At first, I thought that was pretty much it but I quickly learned that the buffet stretched allllllll the way down the room.  It was a non-stop line of food! I was very impressed with their selection.

Everything tasted amazing! Well, everything except their pizza. I know, why would I get pizza at a fancy buffet like Bacchanal when they have steak and seafood?! I really enjoyed my meal.  I would say it was TOTALLY worth spending that extra $15.  Ceviche? Bomb. Lobster bisque? Bomb.  Crab fritters? ALL BOMB.  The bf also really liked many of their selections as well.  Definitely try a little bit of everything.  You'll find a mass amount of food here that you'll like. 

I think Caesar's did a great job of making sure that they offered a vast selection of food for their buffet.  They have everything from ramen to pho to typical American side dishes. I definitely think Bacchanal has topped Wicked Spoon. Food and service was way better than WS! The servers were super attentive when it came to refilling our waters and beverages and pretty much I had a really smooth good meal. Definitely a must try when you come! It will blow all the other buffets away!

I used to think the Bellagio buffet of 5-10 years ago was the end all of Vegas buffets, but in the past few years, the quality and impressiveness has seemed to go downhill a bit.  So, I'm back on the best Vegas buffet search again.  The Bacchanal Buffet was fairly impressive in terms of quantity, presentation, variety, and quality.  The wait to get in may drive you to get the hunger shakes though.  I went on a Saturday around 4:30pm, thinking that the lines would be a little more manageable.  Wrong.  Based on the overheard conversations in line, it sounded like it was at least an hour and a half wait to get in.  But, there is a "back door" way in, as there always is in Vegas.  The only thing is that it'll costs you a bit more money.  For an additional $15 per person, you can go to the platinum/players club line (which was empty when I was there) and and get "fast tracked" ahead of everyone in the regular cashier line.  After paying, you have to wait in another fairly long line to get seated.  I think that by paying the extra $15, we were also seated a bit more quickly.  In total, we probably waited a total of 5-10 minutes and that included the cashier switching out the register, and were out about $70+ per person.     

The buffet itself is bustling with a lot of people in line for food, but the line moves fairly quickly, and they do a pretty good job of crowd control.  The seafood section (on the far left) is always the most crowded section.  However, if you want a plate piled high with warm crab legs, go to the middle of the Italian section (make sure to bring a clean plate with no other food on it) and look for the guy dishing out mounds of crab legs.  The variety and quality of dim sum was decent as was the Peking duck (meaty and succulent).  I'm not a big meat eater so I wish they offered more vegetable options, but the truffled gratin potatoes were decadently rich and delicious.  My husband thought the prime rib was really flavorful and well cooked.  Other creative or interesting food/drink items were the agua frescas in the Mexican food section, lots of fresh fruit, custom made fresh soft tacos, and a jook (rice porridge) station.  The desserts were also an amazing display of decadence.  The buffet has the best gelato offerings I've see at any buffet.  The flavors are creative and abundant.  And they pretty much have all the desserts you can find at other buffets, plus more (including mochi with ice cream).  

The Bacchanal Buffet really is and opulent display of food and one of the best in Vegas.  It's expensive but worth it if you're looking for an extra special buffet experience.

(ridiculous manager ) yelling at the guest who is trying to ask a question from the rude host who is ignoring constantly and say you need to leave, GET OUT.are you kidding me now paying $70 and being treated like this, I have to say I'm taking this harassment and humiliation serious and who ever is owning this place needs to know the management is absolutely ridiculous and they need to have some manners. Again I will take this incident very serious.

Some of the best food from all different types of cuisine. The trays were always full and fresh. The ramen I had was one of the most unique culinary creations I've ever tasted. Everything looked like it was made with passion and care. The deserts on display were like little peices of art. A bit pricey but it's more than worth the experience.

My second dining experience at Bacchanal was just as impressive as my first, but I'm starting to think that the price is a little steep. Breakfast was $26.00 for non TR members ($1 off for TR members). We stayed long enough to chow down on some lunch options as well, but IMHO, $26 for breakfast is a bit steep. The food selection was still very good, but lunch is when the sushi, clams, oysters, prime rib, and all that other good stuff comes out. I'd recommend trying to catch the switch between lunch and breakfast (i think it happens around 11:30). Customizable cooking stations at the buffet included a noodle soup station (ramen, pho, etc), omelet (pasta for lunch), and a crepe dessert station. Other highlights include smoked salmon, sweet potato tater tots, steak and eggs in a skillet, and all the great freshly squeezed juices. Bacchanal is still the best hotel buffet experience on the strip,  and it is worth every penny, but it sure does cost a lot of pennies.

This buffet has tons of options and a lot of variety.  I wouldn't say every dish is totally delicious and some are just so-so, but the things I like to eat, they do well.  And I just love the idea of variety and I think the ambiance is nice.  I'm generally not a huge buffet fan, but with so many crab legs and dessert, and some pretty decent ramen, soups, potato, and noodle dishes I always leave really satisfied.  It's not cheap, so come hungry but be prepared to eat everything!

I am definitely a fan! Although we waited a while, it was worth the wait! So many different kinds of foods, and everything I had tasted good! Definitely tastier than your typical mass produced buffet food. It's very clean and pretty organized. We went for brunch, and the buffet came with bottomless mimosas! I'm excited to go back the next time I'm in vegas...it's definitely a must try!

Probably the best buffet in Vegas. The selection is huge and very good. They offer cold/boiled Alaskan King Crab legs that are already cut for you which is awesome, however I wish they would offer steamed King Crab legs instead because the water from boiling them makes them very salty/tasteless. Line can be very long so I would recommend getting there early before the dinner rush or super late before closing.

Best buffet during my trip here! :D So much variety and the quality of food surpasses all the other ones I've visited. 

The lines are pretty crazy.. We checked out the line when we were passing by and the wait was at least 2 hrs. Luckily lines weren't that long during the afternoon and thanks to our jetlag, it worked out well with our human clocks' "dinner" time. Haha.
Service was excellent - our waitress was so fast! 

Items that stood out to me were the raw oysters (including the spicy oyster shoots - so delicious.), ramen station, the marinated chicken wings (in the Chinese food section), sweet potato balls and the dessert section (they organized that section so well - very colourful and pretty :D).
Best crab legs in vegas! The food is great! Highly recommend coming here. It is pricy but delicious!

My friends and I were originally suppose to go to the Wicked Spoon but that place closed around 3ish to prepare for dinner so one of my friends called up Bacchanal and they were opened the whole day, so we went to check it out. The line wasn't extremely long, but still anticipate the theme park wait of 20 - 30 mins around 3pm, it was probably longer during lunch hours. They also have a fast track line, where you pay $15 to not wait in line, price of the buffet is about $56? That price included tax and tip for a part of 7. 

The decor of the place is nice, very modern, a lot of nice fixtures and glass walls, the stations for each food selection was clean and neat. The service is excellent, staff is attentive with drinks and clearing the table so you can stuff your face with their many options. 

The prime rib line was long, so I went over to the Asian side, they had the favorite dim sum selections, I grabbed some shui mai, har gow, pork dumplings and some fried potstickers, potstickers being the best of them all, the other four were decent for a buffet. They also had bbq pork which was pretty good and some fatty roast duck. Onto the other side of the restaurant, the crab legs, which are usually my favorite to get, so I grabbed two plates, and filled it up with crab legs for our table....to my dismay, they were salty, like really really salty, I think I ended up eating like 5 and gave up, it was too overbearing....like wtf. OK, forget the crab legs, I saw fried chicken which comes in its own little fryer with fries, pretty good..........but salty as well, fuck I seriously think buffets just pound a bunch of salt. And finally I reached the prime rib which was pretty good and wasn't as salty as the crab legs or fried chicken..they also have beef tamales which actually tasted decent.

tldr; about the same price as wynn buffet, very very salty food, great service, nice looking buffet
Best buffet on the strip. Hands down. Server was very friendly and attentive.  The food was great, definitely coming back here
Too expensive for nothing the food wasn't great never go back again . I would give it two stars only

WOW! I'm not going to lie, it is pretty pricey, $54.99. But the service, the atmosphere and the vibe and especially the food are amazing! I've never seen baby lamb rib at buffets and they had it! Absolutely amazing! Definitely worth the money and the visit!

Oh my god, so good!  A HUGE selection of food - the crab legs are my all time favorite and they did not disappoint.  Sushi, American, Chinese, deserts so much fooood!!!  The reason I only give 4 instead of 5 stars is because of how long the wait is.  Yes, I understand there are a lot of people who want to eat there, and that's great...but on Sunday at 11am (probably one of the busiest times) there was only one person checking in the "regular" folks that didn't want to pay an extra $15 to wait in line.  There were six computers and only four in use.  If you wanted to pay to skip the line, you could and three out of four of the people were taking those customers.  Pretty ridiculous.  I waited an hour and missed out on prime sun time at the pool, I'd wait again....but not happily!
This place is a food orgy.  Bring your wallet because the price is not cheap but if you want an all you can eat, high-end, pig-out, this is the place.

The trick is to start lining up around 4-5 because the waiting time is about 30 minutes and for those who have been here before know that it's at least an hour to get in. At least!  New thing they have is a kiosk where it tells you how long the wait is and if you pay an additional 25 per person, you get immediate seating. This only works if the waiting time is over an hour because from a glance at the "immediate" line, you might still be waiting at least 15-30 minutes. And btw, all party must be present in order for you to be seated. Otherwise, they'll pull you to the side until everyone arrives. 

The reason why people pick this buffet over any other ones is because they have everything and more, to King crab, oysters, prime rib, tacos, you name it and they got it. But Bacchanal is known for their desserts. I've been here a few times and their dessert dishes are constantly changing. Macaroons, crepes, mochi, gelatos, cake pops are just a few of what they have. Their plating style and flavor are on spot.

Service is amazing as well. I was asked numerous times where I was from and how I was doing. Our waiter was super funny and attentive to our requests.

$50 per person, and for $15 more, you get unlimited draft beer, house wine and mimosas.

By the way, two hour limit. And they WILL kick you out.

I'm just not a buffet person. I can't ever eat enough to justify the cost of one, and it'd take me a week of eating to justify the cost of this buffet. 

We came because my cousin is in love with the food here. She had it all planned out: show up an hour before lunch, eat slowly, and be there long enough to witness them swapping out breakfast food for lunch food. 

Unfortunately, it seemed every other person in Vegas had that exact same thought. When we arrived, a haughty employee at the back of the line told us that the wait was two hours, and that we'd have to consult the machines to our left to find out what time to return, just to be able to stand in line again. 

This, of course, totally screwed up the master plan, but what else could we do? We walked over to the machines (me mentally equating them to a Fast Pass machine at Disneyland), and hit the screen to start. The message that came up confirmed that we'd have to return to queue up in over two hours, but wait! A little box then popped up to tell us that we had a option. For the low-low price of $25 (per person), we could basically buy ourselves a place in the "ready to be seated" line. 

We stood there discussing the choice - I didn't mind waiting, hubby and cousin were interested in eating as soon as possible - so we decided to just go ahead and do it. 

I'll skip over the part where my behind clenched after hearing the final total and move on to the buffet itself. 

It is large. It is packed. It is varied. It is way too much for one such as me. It is a waste of money for one such as me. You may think you have a big appetite. You may be hungry. Hell, you may have even purposely starved yourself just to eat your way through this buffet. But you'll never get your money's worth. 

But maybe that's just me. 

Like I said, there's just a ton of food. Seafood stations, Asian stations, pasta stations, a dessert area that's bigger than my living room, but it was all lost on me. 

The food I did end up sampling was good. I spent most of my appetite at the Asian stations, while my husband and cousin were all over the place. 

We did a tour of the options before deciding, passing by lines of people who looked half-starved and mildly angry. I made mental note of the things I'd be interested in tasting, then went and grabbed a plate and some freshly-rolled sushi. To that I added some seaweed salad, poke and some dumplings. I then went back to the table to release my cousin, and found that our drinks hadn't yet arrived. 

In fact, it took quite some time for anything to arrive - water, soda, tea - which I wasn't okay with. Even the refills were a long time coming. Not cool. 

Anyway, my husband and cousin put their own versions of a hurtin' on the buffet, but I tapped after round two. 

To my mind, it certainly wasn't worth the cost, and definitely not worth the "fast pass" seating (quite a boon for their profits, I'm sure!)

This buffet puts out a lot of food of all sorts of cuisines. Japanese, Chinese, Italian, Seafood, American and carving stations with 4-6 different types of protein and a noodle station to select your own broth and types of noodles. I guess they are known for there selection of seafood, I've seen just shucked oysters of 60-80 go in 5 minutes and they will keep loading up the line with fresh shucked oysters. Oysters are not specified but they look like east coast and not the pacific nw or B. C. Vast amounts if Crab legs that are large enough for it to hang over plates, both chilled and steamed. And the Dessert station was probably the best menu for me. It has the largest space out of all the cuisines. So definitely leave room for dessert here. Price is a bit high but for the amount and selection of food that is out on the line its on par. Speaking of lines I've seen lines snake around the stanchions with 45 minute wait times. Being a casino guest speeds this process up since there is a separate shorter line. The staff and service are friendly but not speedy but since the seating capacity of this establishment is in the 100's I guess thats what happens.
I am very impressed with this new buffet ....modern ambiance with gourmet food. It's prolly $10-15 more than other Harrah's buffets but so worth it!!!!!!

The desserts are very good. I am disappointed by the choice of seafood. The salmon was very good. But the clams, mussels and oysters are okay. The crab legs are not king crab. And the taste is very average

The quality of this place has gone down so much it makes me cry. The dim sum items for brunch was dry and chewy. The snow crab legs where salty and the oysters were very briny. The seasoning was either to salty or bland. The udon and pho were definitely a joke. The dessert bar was great though. It could have been so bad because it was a weekday ‍. Either way, for the price, I wasn't expected something so bad.

Amazing variety of assortments (~600 dishes). Had breakfast twice here; once during the week ($40 pp) and once during the weekend ($60 pp). You can eat everything from traditional American to European, Mexican, Italian, and Japanese. Some dishes were much better than others. Some of the dishes that were supposed to be hot were warm at best. Service on the first visit was mediocre but great on the second visit. Very filling. Go hungry or you're not getting your money's worth.

Easily the best buffet I have ever been to. I stop by ever Vegas trip and it's worth every penny!

Grade: Oh Honey Yaaas

Food and service was Exceptional!  Best crab legs, sushi and desserts in Vegas. Street tacos were awesome. Servers were friendly and so helpful. Manager stopped by our table and genuinely took an interest in our comments. We will definitely be back. We'll worth the money.

It has the best food.  It has a wide selection of food.  Maybe I wasn't in the right frame of mind or I expected too much.  People go crazy over the unlimited crab legs.  I find them a lot of work and kind of messy to eat. Again, maybe it was my frame of mind.  The deserts were OK.  The real draw is the wide selection of food and the crab and shrimp.  I would give it another try.  It certainly is one of the best.
The best buffet on the strip! Love the seafood and Asian food here and also poke is amazing!!!

Bachannal. The quintessential. I love the ambiance here. The woods, the glass, the extensive extensive food counters. Oh, it's a high-end buffet, and a price to match.

GOOD
- lamb
- chicken sausage
- cioppino
- mussels in sauce
- tri-tip
- shrimp cocktail
- truffle pizza
- garlic bread
- gelato

OKAY
- bone marrow (need something to spread it on)
- grilled octopus (meh cooking)
- mussels (meh quality at best)
- american wagyu
- soft-shell crab
- macarons
- horchata (kinda milky, though it was fine)

BAD
- most of the asian food =D
- the sushi
- poke
- oyster shooter
- potato gnocchi

The guy sitting next to us was on his phone the entire time (he was lone, but chatting on calls). When he left, a lesbian couple was seated next to us....and the waiter called one of the girls 'sir'. Oh boy.

But otherwise, the service was pretty good.

After hearing all the hype about Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace 'dethroning' the legendary Bellagio Buffet in terms of food quality and quantity, I was very eager to dine here. I dined at Bacchanal during peak hours/days. I would highly recommend paying the extra $15.00 for the express lane pass rather than wait in line for 1.5 hours +. 

Attention seafood lovers: Line up here FIRST!!! The majority of people at the buffet line up in THIS LINE to get their hands on delicious king crab (just ask if you want it served warm and not chilled), yummy ceviche, and unfortunately, mediocre oysters. I started at the other stations and waited in the seafood line for a good 20 minutes before I received my crab, oysters, and ceviche. Much to my dismay, my food from the other stations was cold by the time I sat down. I forgot to grab a second plate and I basically formed an alliance with the other seafood philes to secure some extra plates for all of us so we did not lose our spot in line!

Bacchanal definitely has a lot of food options, but I would say the food is comparable to that of the Bellagio Buffet. Besides the fresh king crab, I enjoyed the dim sum/poke/carpaccio dishes the most. I liked the varieties of mochi, macarons, and Jelly Belly beans in the dessert area at Caesar's, but I would say Bellagio's desserts are more decadent and delicious. I have not been to the Bellagio Buffet since the addition of the caviar station, which may make it trump that of Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace. 

Bottom line: Bacchanal Buffet is an expensive buffet, but if you want to burn some of your winnings here, it's a great bet!

Hands down my fav buffet on the strip.  The seafood is excellent!! Two types of crabs precracked no salt added!  The Chinese section is a bit salty but not bad.  Make sure I get the truffle potatoes and tell the guy to give u extra truffle for ur crabs.  I cant seem to give this place a 5 because of their slow service.  Twice our waitresses have been slow to get us our drinks, clean the damn table, and provide friendly service.

Looked up the best buffets in Vegas, chose to try them out and it was a big disappointment.  We arrived early for breakfast at 8:30, the wait was ridiculous, even considering that there was no one inside.  Once inside the food looked dry and a day old and the selection was a big let down.  We asked for the manager and chose to get our money back and try the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan; which was a better choice.

I went here this morning (early bird special of $42 before 11am) because last night for Thanksgiving, there was a 5-6 hour wait!!

Maybe dinner is better but I thought it was just good... not exceptional.

There wasn't as much variety as I hoped. The fried chicken was dry, the lox was extremely salty, and the food wasn't hot.

The dessert is much better than the food. I loved my vanilla bean pudding and my fresh crepe where you put your own toppings on!

If I were to describe this place with five words, it would be, OH THIS IS THE BEST. 

Hands down, best buffet on the strip, in my opinion. Yes, I do remember the snake-like queue line to the cashier. But for those hungry monsters who can't wait anymore, there's an "Express Line". Remember the Express Lines in Universal Studio? Yes, with a little more fee, you can get into the Bacchanal Heaven in a second. But my girlfriend and I were broke then, so we stood in line. I think we waited around forty five minutes to an hour and it wasn't at peak season. Do your math. 

It was dinner when we were here and they have a magnificent array of food. High-quality buffet, and not just mere bunch of food thrown around in metal baskets. I would highly recommend it to anyone. Worth the price and the wait.

Seriously best buffet I've ever been to! Everything was in point and We only had to wait ten minutes on a Wednesday evening. Whoever decides to come here must try everything. The seafood section was amazing (crabs and fish) best rack of lambs ever, it was so tender and full of flavor...I can't even start talking about the dessert :o gelato and crepes were so good and the Mochi ice cream really hit my sweet tooth :P can't wait to go back to Vegas for this buffet haha

The reviews are true. this buffet is DEFINITELY a feast worthy of the gods. 
A couple of things, 

Yes, the lines can get long if you go on weekends, or dinner time. Lunch and weekdays are much better for it if you want to avoid waiting too long. 

Yes, it can get pricey, but you get what you pay for. You pay $20 for a mediocre buffet on the strip or off strip somewhere? you get $20 worth of food. might as well spend the extra couple bucks and give your taste buds an amazing time right? Party in your mouth! from Asian cusine, to fresh seafood, to italian and mexican and etc and etc and desserts? YUM. worth every dollar baby.

On another note, if you are a ceasars property gambler, there is a separate line for platinum / diamond/ seven stars to avoid or cut down the waiting time.
Also, you can pay $15 if you are not a players card holder to bypass the line. 

My experience differs a little bit i guess. because i didnt have to wait in a 3 hour line... but... i didnt come on a holiday weekend at 8pm for dinner either, so.. chose your timing wisely and enjoy!

There's a huge selection of food here. I like that their crab legs can be served warm or boiled. I don't like cold crab legs. Their red velvet pancake is good. I also like their crab burger. I also like the ease of checking in. Instead of waiting in line for 60-75 minutes, I get to walk around and do something and then receive a text when they are ready to take you in. The ambiance is also good. The servers pay attention to your needs. I will go back to this buffet. It's a must try.

I don't know where to start. The food is phenomenal. Steam crab legs is the top of my list, the ceviche, the oyster shooters, prime rib, the hot & spicy soup in the Chinese food section. Jeez I wish I can name all the food and tell it how it taste. BEST BUFFET IN LAS VEGAS, HANDS DOWN. I've been to a lot of buffets in Vegas and I thought The M Buffet was good, but after coming here.... "WOW!!! Now I know why they call this place Bacchanal named after Bacchus" That was my reaction when eating the food there. 

Note: Must try the Peach Tea.

Where do I even begin... When you first walk in you see the lobster and the Alaskan crab legs (NOT THE SNOW CRAB LEGS!!) but when you go in and ask the workers where the lobsters are they act like they don't know what a lobster is lol. Also they mix in the snow crab legs with 3 or 4 pieces of Alaskan crabs which is so cheap of the restaurant. The meats! I tried the bbq ribs and they were so saltyyyy! I looked at the prime rib that they gave me and it was so fatty that I could only handle one bite. They have maybe 4 juices available in the buffet and guess what they're not real juice! For the ppl on yelp saying that they loved the fresh squeezed juice haha you've never had fresh squeezed juice before because that is not even close. The desserts are the only reason why I would give this place a one star. This place Not worth the money and the hour wait in line.

Quite disappointed on the quality of the food. The lamb chop was dry and smelly. The ramen was oily and the pork tasted like armpit.. Everything was so salty that we didn't really eat much. I don't mind to pay more if the food quality qualifies for the price.. However, in this case.. I think I have wasted my $52*2. Really not sure why this place is so popular. Trust me.. Don't even waste your time to wait in line. Period.
For a couple of bucks more than the other buffets in Vegas you'll get a feast. Definitely worth the price and the quality of service is 4 stars.

I want to start this review off by saying that the food was so good here I got sick from eating here and I don't mean food poisoning sick but I ate so much that I was so full I wasn't feeling good on the way out. I mean that's how delicious the food here was, I basically overdosed on their food! 

My girlfriend had been talking about this buffet for a loooong time and when we basically planned a Vegas vacation with coming here as the main mission on our trip. There's a lot of other places that are for sure cheaper but every dollar you pay for the entrance here is well spent. All the food that I got here was basically upscale restaurant quality food at a buffet setting. I tried eating and tasting everything and that is where I got in trouble, I made it all the way to dessert and had a plate full of different sweets but halfway through I couldn't finish it and had to abruptly leave because I had to stand up to even breathe. Me getting sick because I couldn't stop eating should be enough to convince you the food is really good here. So far the best buffet I've eaten at in Las Vegas.

Yikes the price was $45 per person today on Saturday. So expectations were high. The selection is quite large and amazing. I was very impressed.

However, the prime rib was a bit over cooked and tasted more like roast beef than prime rib.

The truffle potatoes au gratin were pretty good.

Nothing really stood out and wowed me. But solid food. I did like it more than the Wynn Buffet.
We paid a $20 premium per person to skip the fucking line and are still waiting after an hour in line.  Don't give a fuck how good food is not coming back

Best buffet in Las Vegas! 

Saturday brunch. long line starts at 10-ish. $45 per person if you have rewards card. 

so many choices to choose from! so little time and not big enough tummy! 

I highly recommended to try their juice bar,  chef's specials section, and their ramen! everything else is expectedly delicious! 

definitely will go back every time I go to Vegas.

This buffet was great. We went at around 8:30 on a Sunday morning, so there were no lines (which probably had a lot to do with our positive review). I think it cost $40-something dollars for their Sunday brunch, which included bottomless mimosas. They give you a blue rubber thing which is used to grip hot plates. 

The food choices are insane. My faves were the seafood and dessert stations. I love how they halve the crab legs for you. Everything was presented beautifully on bold, colorful plates and cute individual baskets or cups. I'm embarrassed to say it, but I squealed with delight a few times. 

As with any buffet, we were a bit overwhelmed with the obscene amount of food and felt gross afterwards. But still, we felt like this was one of the best meals of our long weekend in Vegas. We spent over $300 for two people at a fancy steakhouse which had average food, so we felt like we got more for our money at Bacchanal. 

Next time I'm in Vegas I'd like to try Wicked Spoon to compare.

We went back again this weekend and this CERTAINLY is the BEST buffet in Las Vegas.  With workers such as hostess Elaine and server Vince you cannot go wrong by eating here.  Great food and fantastic employees.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

I don't know what happened but we went here the day before Thanksgiving and majority of the food that I had seemed to be salty.   Including the pasta dish that was cooked for me by the kind chef in the Italian section.  I love meat and the prime rib was good but not great.   I am willing to give it another try because for sure friends of ours would want to try this "new" buffet.  The desserts we had were very good though. The service was excellent but the food.....maybe next time it will be better for me.

We just finished buffet. We were a party of 8, seating wasn't a problem as they seat larger parties quickly. 
However, the quality of food was a big big let down. Based on the reviews we thought the place would offer great varieties. For more than $70 per person we paid, the food was really below par. 
The plates were smelly. My wife and my friends wife couldn't even eat as they have sensitive nose. 
Dessert was a big let down.  I was hoping dozens of great options, the options were really limited.  
I wouldn't advise anybody going to this buffet, if you have high expectations from it. 
I am really surprised to see so few below par ratings for such a let down.

This buffet is like the Kobe Bryant of all buffets minus injuries! 

I am beyond glad, BEYOND , that I get to cross this off my list! You have to go here when you are at Vegas! I think the price is worth it because the food is really high quality! 
I loved everything!!! 

And I ate about 3 fresh creme brûlée. That is all. Happy me.

Giving it four stars because it truly is the best buffet in Vegas.  However, as far as the food goes, you can definitely get better at a nice regular restaurant for the same price.  It's just better quality food than other buffets.  The selection is not more widely varied at all.  I would say that the amount of choices offered are pretty comparable to the buffet at Bellagio.  

We went early (4:30 p.m.) on a Thursday and there were only two tables ahead of us.  The service was so-so, and it took way too long to clear dirty plates which is not acceptable when they aren't even half full.  I noticed that it did get considerably busier as we were leaving.

I would have to think about going back next time we're in Vegas.  For $50 plus cost of alcohol, it's one of the pricier buffets in Vegas for sure.

Absolutely ridiculous, I understand that Christmas eve is busy and you may not have table available or need us to wait 3 hours to come back with a ticket. But changing the time on the ticket and telling us to go to the back of the line 2, 3 times is highly unprofessional and frankly not acceptable.

THEY CHARGE FULL ADULT  PRICE FOR KIDS 11 AND UP! I did not find this out until we had stood in line for almost 1 HOUR and had gotten to the cashier to pay. By then the kids were starving. And of course, my skinny 11 year old did NOT eat anything close to an adult or a teenager, hmmm, why? maybe because he's 11 years old and still in elementary school!!!!  I plan to write a letter to Caesars as well since SIGNS OF AGE LIMITS WERE NOT POSTED.

Came in on a Friday night and it was packed! I checked in online for the VIP pass so thank god because we were so hungry. This is prob one of the best buffet I have ever had. Seafood section was delicious. The section where they served prime ribs and all that goodness was amazing. Asian food was good as well! My favorite section has to be the desserts. Everything in that aisle was sooooo good. I will be coming back to this buffet whenever I'm in Vegas!

We went at about 4p and no line.  Luckily it was comped from my play at caesars, as a $50 is too much to pay for this buffet.

I was under the impression that they served king crab legs.  WRONG or maybe only on certain days.  Sorry but snow crab is a waste of my time.  Oysters were sandy and gritty.  Shrimp and the other seafood was ok.

The meat section was really good.  From the prime rib, to baby backs to pork belly to lamb.  All delicious.  Asian section was not bad.  Good selection of your normal buffet sushi; salmon, ahi, spicy tuna, cali roll.  Had ramen, sobs, udon section too.  

I also like the bread, cheese and italian meat section.  proscuitto, salami and other meats were all delicious.

Didn't visit the italian or mexican section as nothing looked appetizing.

The dessert section is the highlight of the buffet.  A full sections of any type of sweets, cakes, pies, macrons, pastries you can imagine.  Too bad you are too full to try everything at the end.
Definitely the best buffet in Las Vegas. Quality, taste and presentation all were amazing. The staff are also very friendly

This is by far worth every penny and then some. I never wait in lines for anything....especially food but here lies the exception. 
The food is simply perfect and perfectly prepared. 
Every employee from front of house to the back is always pleasant and friendly. 

I was so impressed with the consistent level of excellence my family experiences every time we come so I felt compelled to speak with a manager. 

I went to the front and had the pleasure of meeting MIKE...he was professional and a fine representative of such a great establishment. 
Very handsome too! Lol
What else can you ask for. 

Next time you are in Vegas take your friends and family and enjoy!

This buffet was an amazing experience as advertised.it is upscale and the seafood and deserts are amazing.the only problem is the price is 53 dolars and its no more upscale jere than at the wynn or bellagio.

The reputation is far exaggerated.  Food is good to fair, but not spectacular.  Lots of variety, so good if you're with people that can't agree on one type of cuisine.  Truly a bacchanal, feeling a little guilty about the gluttony.

I finally found the answer to "which buffet do you like the most in vegas?" BACCHANAL BUFFET is where it's at!

The price for dinner now is $45 so I think it went up a little bit but honestly, you get what you pay for, and the food is really delicious.  

They have steamed crab legs...yes steamed, not the legs on ice stuff going on, legit.  I also went insane on the peking duck they had...what?! how do they afford that?!  sorry ducks, you just had to get in my belly.

There's honestly sooooo much to choose from and it's crazy how huge the buffet area is, it feels like it just keeps going. But that's totally fine with me!

One downside is that they don't have the endless drinks option here so you do have to pay for alcoholic drinks, soft drinks are still free with purchase of buffet.  

I definitely ate about 10 lbs after this buffet, so needless to say, bombdotcom!

We decided to try this place last time we were in Vegas and we were so happy we did. Absolutely amazing food! We ended up paying about $54 per person, but well worth the wait, and the money. We highly recommend this place if you are in mood for a lot of great food.

For the money ($40+/ person), no oyster and terrible tasting mimosa? Not worth it.

Last time, $20+ with oyster and without mimosa? Totally worth it.

Pretty decent prime rib but if you like the thicker cut, you have to ask for it. Otherwise, you may end up with an English cut sliver!

I kind of wish I wouldn't have eaten here. I may never be able to go to another buffet because no other buffet could compare to this one. The amount of food here is indescribable. The quality is amazing. There are individual servings at the stations for convenience. There is an omelet bar, a carving station, and gelato! They have chefs at each buffet station so if the food happens to be cold or not exactly to your liking they will make something fresh for you. If you're tall, make sure to look under the counter for plates.

Worth the wait and the money...be sure you are hungry. Brunch worked best for me except I couldn't last long enough to get to the oysters. The service is awesome...people tip the cooks, waitstaff, and the bussers!

The food may be great but the service is the absolute worst. Don't know if it was because I went during the holiday season or not but I have never dealt with such an unprofessional business/management. 

The food is delicious but for the wait, price, and customer service combined is not worth the experience. The customer service itself is shit and do not expect to eat for at least 3+ hours with rude workers and irrational policies. 

Their 'policy' of the whole party having to be there in the entire duration of 3-4 hours of the line is bullshit.

I came here once with a party of 4 about a year ago during the summer and the food was great but the wait was.. insanely long and not worth it.

The second time I came with a party of 11, called twice to the front desk of Caesar's Palace AND got directed to the front desk of the Bacchanal Buffet to make sure that the whole party did not have to be there, and they both confirmed that it is completely fine.
After waiting in the line for 1+ hours, the so called manager named Melissa comes up to us and rudely says that we may not stand in the line unless our whole party is here.
