Even after arguing with her, and questioning the existence of the policy, she rudely interrupted us every time to say there was nothing she could do about it. She was extremely rude and did not know how to apologize. 
Asked if I could talk to the head manager, she rudely cuts me off and claims that she IS the manager in a derogatory tone.

Not only is this place not worth the wait, but it is also not worth losing your sanity.

Bacchanal Buffet is located at Ceasars Palace.

I'm a victim of expecting a grand feast from this mega buffet, only to have my expectations shattered like a huge mirror hitting a concrete floor. Fellow Yelpers raved about it. Family and friends that had gone, had also raved about it. So naturally I bookmarked it and anxiously awaited my time to feast like a king at the "buffet of all buffets."

Upon arriving at the entrance to the buffet it was already clear that we came during the dinner rush. The line was insanely long.  Fast forward 1.5 hours later and we were finally seated inside....oh yes, it took us 1.5 hours of waiting & $50+ per person to get in. 

The place is freaking huge. Food on food on food & tables on tables on tables. The decor was pretty and oozed of opulence for a buffet. We were seated relatively close to the dessert station. The entire meal was a blur, there was a lot to choose from (meats, pastas, ethnic foods, desserts, sides, salads, soups, etc) and yet nothing specific comes to mind about what was the best at that buffet. However, I did enjoy the crab legs and the choice of either cold crab legs or boiled crab legs; which were boiled fresh upon each order. 

The only thing I didn't like about Bacchanal was the buffet set up. The majority of the food stations and the dessert station were located in the same room; but the crab legs and the majority of the Asian dishes and pasta dishes were located in a separate room. I suppose this is my buffet pet peeve and the worst offender is the buffet at Mandalay Bay, where the majority of each food station is sectioned off in its own space@!&$# LOL I digress. 

I'm pretty sure the long wait left a bad taste in my mouth making my expectation of the Bacchanal that much more important. Would I come back to Bacchanal? Yes, to give it another shot, BUT will need to time my next visit so it doesn't coincide during the rush -_-

We got a Groupon for the buffet and it cost me $60 for two people with fast pass and mimosas! It was so worth it. 

The food was great (try the pork buns). They had everything from sushi to pasta and seafood. And, I had no complaints about the service. 

TIP: Get there early because the place gets packed around 10AM. No one like to wait in line for food.

The buffet has a very large assortment of different types of food such as Mexican and Asian food. Although there were a lot of foods, there was only a few good things I personally liked. The snow crab was very delicious and juicy. It's a bit pricey, but if you're into seafood I recommend going here

I have always dreamt about dining Bacchanal Buffet. On the last night of our staycation, that dream turned into a reality. 

 Outside the Buffet there is a plaque on the wall. It says, "Bacchus: The Roman God of the Feast. Bacchanal: A Feast worthy of Gods."  I don't think the Gods would appreciate the lengthy cue to get in the first line of the buffet. A negative of Bacchanal Buffet is the endless lengthy lines. In my opinion, the buffet arrangement exacerbates these lines. Caesar's Palace would be doing a good service to their guests by putting up a sign stating the approximate wait time from this point forward. The line did move relatively fast. And by the time I wrote my review on Bellagio Snack's we were paying for the dinner. At $44.99 per person with $1 off for Reward members (whoopee!), Bacchanal Buffet does not love locals. After waiting on this line for a few minutes, we were directed to wait on another line. A few minutes pass. Finally, a hostess walks us to our table. The first thing that struck my eyes was the dessert station in the center of the buffet.

  After we are seated, we got a quick course on the different stations and their locations. From that point on, I rate the service a 3 out of 5. Piles of empty dishes sat on the table far too long. The drink refills could have been better.

  I started from one end of the buffet to the other. This review mentions the stations and a sample of the food at some of them. I have posted comments where applicable:

Conclusion:

   It was a difficult decision whether to rate Bacchanal Buffet 3 or 4 stores. I was not happy that the miso soup was cold. I was not happy about the extended wait at the seafood station. I am under the impression that a poor layout is creating this long line that moves exceedingly slow. I was going to give it 3.75 stars. This is the reason that I am giving Bacchanal Buffet a soft 4 stars. One of the people in my party was in a rush. The result is that I passed over coffee and dessert.  My dream of dining in the Bacchanal Buffet is over. The constant lines and high pricing leave me with better dining options on the Strip in the near future. As it stands right now, Bacchanal may return to Rome by the time I pay $44.99 to return to Bacchanal Buffet.

The Yelp 100 Challenge. Review 57.

Not worth the price and wait for this buffet.  Initially excited to try this upon reading all the yelp reviews.  Paid $60 during the holiday weekend, must be a couple $$$ less on regular days.  Bottom line, I get what I had here for $20 in buffets in LA. Yes, it was that bad. Sushi rolls were not fresh, crab legs were cold (even though they were requested steamed), and overall just a lack of variety. Add into this an insanely long line for seafood that happens to spill over the adjacent food stations that trying to get food from these areas run the risk of other hungry customers go off on you as they think you are cutting into the seafood line.  There was a not dish that I tried that stood out to me as above average.  "Over 500+" items? I don't think so.  The desserts somehow made the experience a bit better but it was mediocre at most.  Wanted to try their asians soups (ramen, pho and udon) but guess what... The broth isn't ready for another 20 minutes.  Save your money and time and go to either the Buffet at Bellagio or the buffet at M resort (unlimited wine and beer included). Never has a vegas buffet disappointed me such as Bacchanal! :p
Best buffet on the Strip, it's a must! The flavor and authentic style with amazing presentations!

There is NO better buffet in Vegas!  Take it from a Las Vegas native!  I KNOW!  Better than The M, Better than Bellagio, Better than Wynn!  Hot and cold crab, Oysters, Salmon, and so many kinds of seafood.  The Lamb Chops are heaven!  The Veal Parm was good too!  So many kinds of meat, chinese, (oh the duck!)...with over 500 items, GOOD items, to choose from...you won't leave hungry, and yes it's worth the wait and the price,  The crepes, chocolate covered strawberries, and unique gelatos and other desserts make this buffet one of a kind!  NO ONE comes close!
Best Buffet in town! I had an incredible dinning experience with a variety of gourmet cuisine to try. Their sea food selection is excellent and their dessert selection is delicious!!!

This buffet is brand spankin' new in Vegas, so naturally everyone is curious and it's a bit hyped up right now. The long lines right now are no joke, but it's a little misleading, as they tend to slow things down as you get closer to the cashier -- they don't want a bunch of people clogging up the front area to get seated.

I consider myself a Vegas buffet veteran, as I've tried just about every one. The first thing one should know is that it's a bit difficult to compare each and every buffet out there. Each one has its pros and cons, it's own inconsistencies, and nuances. It all depends on what you like. Rating buffets is very subjective, to say the least.

That being said, I thought the new buffet at Caesar's was okay, nothing earth shattering in terms of Vegas buffets. I'm going to judge a buffet mostly by its seafood, meat, and dessert. Here's my breakdown:

Seafood -- they offer pre-cut, cold king crab legs. However, upon request, they will steam a plate of crab legs for a few minutes. This inevitably holds up the line longer than it should, because it seems like most people don't get out of the way while they're waiting. I got my fair share (and money's worth) of king crab, but it tasted rather bland even with the melted butter -- the snow crab legs had a lot more flavor. 

The stone claws may look appetizing at first, made famous by Joe's Stone Crab. But once you get into the meat (and that's a big if), the meat inside is dry, crumbly, and flavorless. The tin cans of clam bake, fish entrees, and mussels were all dry, shriveled up, and rather pathetic-looking. Sad face. 

Meat -- thankfully, I enjoyed all of their meat options over the seafood. The prime rib was excellent, and the brisket was actually good. Smoky and reasonably flavorful, with a nice bark. They don't slice against the grain, so it can get a bit chewy.

Dessert -- thumbs up for the dessert crepe station and the great gelato flavors. Everything else was just so-so. The cheesecake and dessert on a stick may look cute, but it just didn't have much flavor. Overall, I thought dessert options were rather limited.

As for the other food options, I thought everything was just okay. The thing with buffets is that a lot of food just sits out in the open -- getting its life slowly sucked out. As we all know, food is at its best when it's pipin' hot and freshly made. So food like dim sum, sushi, and other of these delicate dishes all suffer as a result.

None of the dishes are anything original, but where this buffet stands out are things like the cheeses and the charcuterie spread. The problem is, will people eat this at a buffet? Each time I walked by, nobody was even remotely slowing down to put some on their plate. Mostly everyone will be stuffing themselves with meat, seafood, and dessert. 

I was torn between 3 or 4 stars, but I'll go with 4 stars because this buffet does offer some unique options, king crab legs (which is crazy expensive, so we'll see how long that lasts) and a good meat station. So if you're a fan of Vegas buffets, it's worth a shot. Whether you return for a repeat visit remains to be seen.

This is probably the most overrated buffet in Vegas. I heard good things about this place when they first opened, but when I visited a week ago for dinner, it was overcrowded with very long lines on the meat and seafood stations. I had to wait more than 15 minutes on the seafood station line! And for what?! Crab legs that were overcooked and oysters that smelled like women's makeup! The meat station was little better but it did not make up for other shortcomings.

Getting straight to the point, today's meal at the prominent Bacchanal Buffet was absolutely terrible. 

1. As you may have heard from previous reviews, the ticket that you receive upon reaching the restaurant does absolutely nothing for the wait time. The "text" that they were supposed to send to notify us of when we were supposed to be at the restaurant did not arrive and was a complete waste of time. Even though we arrived at the restaurant earlier than others to receive this ticket, those who received the ticket after us were somehow able to be seated before us, thus making the ticket very much useless. After being presented the ticket, the woman in front, as well as the ticket, very clearly stated that we were to come back at that specific time after receiving the text message to be seated. Fair enough. After wandering the streets of Las Vegas for almost 4 hours, which was apparently the wait time for the restaurant, we returned to the buffet, only to find the huge line awaiting us, not to mention that we never received any form of message from the business. Convinced that we were able to get in sooner because of the ticket, we asked the same lady in front and she just quickly pointed us to the back of the line and left. Still utterly confused, we asked around only to understand that the ticket was not a pass to be seated earlier, but just a piece of paper to show that we were eligible to get in, meaning that we still needed to wait in line to be seated. We then waited in the never-moving line for about 1.5-2 hours before finally being able to see the inside of the restaurant. It was around 9:30 or so and with still so many people behind us and the restaurant closing in about half an hour, we were at our limits. What should have been a relaxing dinner with family was rushed and uncomfortable for everyone. Technically, the time we spent waiting for the text, a thorough explanation, and the line was actually around 6 hours, which is a huge amount of time for the quality of food that was served there. Not satisfied at all. 

2. After finally being seated half an hour before the advertised closing time, we immediately went to get food, filling our plates with as much as we could take, expecting the food to be absolutely delicious, but sadly we were once again very wrong. Throughout the meal, the food was at most mediocre and most likely able to be bought at any restaurant in our home town, making us instantly regret our decision to spend more than $200 on the place. A lot of the food tasted overcooked, burnt, and almost vomit-worthy. After barely eating anything and having spent a tremendous amount of money, we just left, with still many people left eating/unseated. I would have described the food there to be leftovers from a trashy restaurant if I did not know where it actually came from, though the argument still stands. 

It's overrated and the management for crowds sucks. Don't go here.

crazy line! Expensive! 
The food was amazing. Lots of seafood choices.

I came 3 yrs ago and I remembered the food being phenomenal. This time around the wait was about 3 hrs just to be seated. Apparently, the 3 hr wait is normal and it wouldn't have been that bad if the food were worth it. There are better buffets like the Wynn or the buffet at the M resort that are $20 less and No wait. Service was nice but honestly I was still disappointed at the end of it all.

If you're trying to decide what buffet is worth waiting, paying and going to in Vegas, consider your decision made, GO HERE!

This buffet has something (or a lot of things) for everyone regardless of whether you're an all you can eat seafood lover or enjoy a few bites of basic foods.

The buffet starts off with the section I don't even bother looking at, seafood. From what I can tell they have crab legs, mussels, shrimp, oysters, ceviche, etc. 

Then you get to the fried potato, bbq type sides and meat station. All sorts of meats from ribs to sausages to chicken. I choose the truffle tots, waffle fries and mac and cheese from this section. (I'm the enjoy a few bites of basic food type.)

Then you have at least 5 kinds of bread and 4 types of soup.

Then you get to the mexican station, one of my favorites. You can make your own tacos here, or any other sort of mexican creation between the rice, beans, different meats, sauces and toppings they offer. Nachos made with waffle fries anybody?

Then you go around the corner to the second part of the buffet. Here you have some pastas to choose from, made to order omelet bar or boiled crab legs (depending on the type of day), and pizza. 

Then you have the charcuterie section, followed by the cheese section.

To finish it off comes the asian food section which includes more foods than I could identify. You have your noodles, sushi, some sort of soup making station, pork buns, fried rice, meat dishes and then some. 

For the cherry on top, make your way to the dessert buffet island in the middle of the floor. There you can stuff your own made to order fresh crepe, order some gelato or pick your favorite small bites of dessert. 

I cannot wait to go back!!! Best part is the new waiting system. You check-in and can then go on your merry way around the casino. The computer system will text you letting you know when it is time to head back to the buffet to be seated. Sure you'll still wait around 15 minutes or so but that's better than an hour or two!

This is the best buffet in Vegas as of the date of this review.  It's better than Wicked Spoon and has more of a variety.  Also, it has a virtual wait machine so go pick up your ticket and enter the number of people in your party and your phone number.  You'll receive a return time and text when they are ready for you to pay and get in line.  This saves a lot of hassle.  Dinner was $54.  It is located towards the back of the hotel (away from the Forum Shops).

This place needs help on the labeling since it wastes time trying to figure out what is what - especially when there is a line and a wait.    The oysters were not good here (tasted fishy) and the ramen did not have katsu in it (like in the yelp photos), just a slice of pork.  The savory American food - fried chicken, truffle potato, artisan bread, sweet potato tater tots, sliders, etc. and the dimsum were pretty good.  The cheese , honey and jams were yummy too.  And they have black sesame mochi ice cream!

Incredible buffet. The buffet is out of this world.
I have tried at the Bellagio buffet and the RIO seafood buffet, but I think this buffet
is much better than the other two. The shrimp, the oyster, the crab legs and the
sea bash are all fresh & excellent. The deserts are excellent.
 Customer service is also very good.
The only thing that I did not like is the table is kind of small, and they are very close
to each other.  The price is $50 but it is not bad compared to other buffets in the strip. I would definitely come back again

I would have given the place 5 stars as the food was phenomenal and the service was on point however I am taking one star off because of the wait in line. We came at around 145pm and the line was like an anaconda for the "regular people". I'm no gambler or vip and so I'm one of the "regular people" who had to be in this line. Me and my fiance were hoping to get in lunch as that was our budget however the line movement was so loooong and sloooooww.... at 245pm they started opening up this kiosk to reserve your place and they will text you. By the time we get to the the cashier it was 3:02pm... guess what, it's dinner price now! What's sneaky about it was they started opening 2 more other registers to take people I.  There were only 2 to start with for the lunch time and now 4 are open for the dinner. I told them I was in line since lunch however the cashier said that she's sorry bit it's dinner price now and so ended up paying $59/person plus tax no gratuity yet. In any case, I made sure I get my money's worth. I ate 8pcs of stone crab, 15pcs crab legs, 10 pcs oyster, sea bass, lamb chops, truffle soup, wedge salad, Peking duck, corn, mac and cheese, crepe, 5 more other desserts and 4 Thai iced tea with Boba, 1 guava juice and 1 tamarindo juice. There! Everything was delish!!! There is no one dish that did not stand out, even the side dishes were delicious!!

I think I got my $60 worth haha! Hopefully my stomach will be able to find peace with the assortment of food I stuffed in there! 

Would come back here but hopefully be able to get on the lunch price.....

All I have to say is GET THERE EARLY so you don't have to wait that long in line. I've read other peoples review and yes you can wait a really really long time. I got there at 5:30 pm. I waited for about 45 minutes. As I was waiting, the line got really long. Anything later and you will be waiting for two hours. They have so many different selections to choose from. The only thing that I would have preferred is more selection of sushi. I could be here all night. I think I gained 10lbs walking out of there. They have one of the best dessert selection as well so save some room. The macaroons was amazing. It melted in your mouth. I ate about 8. Sunday dinner was $60.55 ($55.99 plus $4.56 tax). My other suggestion is take it slow, try and eat everything. I felt like a little fat kid. Have fun and enjoy!

First of all the, it is going to be a long wait. I went first night at 6:30pm, which was a terribly wrong decision. Gave up after 1.5 hours of wait without getting close to the gate. Next day I went at 2:30pm, still had to wait almost 3 hours and seated around 5:30pm. So if you are going, be prepared, and that's why it has one star off. If you are willing to skip the oyster and Macaron, then the brunch is cheaper and line was almost non-existent.

The place look fancy AND the food is good. Food selection is wide: Seafood, Mexican, Chinese, Japanese, Italian, etc. It is definitely not an average level buffet.

It's my first time here. I came here for brunch. There are so many selection for you to choose from. Everything is pretty fresh. I like the Ramon noddle station. I like the crepes station. The rib was very flavorful. Fresh squeeze juice. And sea food selection. Off course, great dessert and ice cream. $42 per person excluding tax and tip. Service was great too. I highly recommend even is a little on the pricey side. But it's totally worth it.

Best Buffet EVER! 

Seriously, Las Vegas has tons of buffets but this is the King! Yes it's a little pricey compared to others in town but the quality is much better and you defiantly get what you pay for!

Definitely worth the extra $ if you can!

I've been here probably 5 times since they very first opened and got all those rave reviews from the media. It's gone slowly down hill as they have taken off some of the best items like the tomahawk ribeyes and they are hit or miss on king crab legs, some times they have it sometimes they don't. The service is horrible for Caesars palace level. Still it's worth going only when you time it right and come when its slower. Would never wait for more than 20 minutes much less the hour or two during peak times.

I finallyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy got to try Bacchanal's dinner and it was amazing! But please consider that I got in Bacchanal at 2:50 pm (10 minutes before dinner time!) so I got in for the price of lunch and ate dinner menus. :D

Also, there was hardly any line to get in to Bacchanal because it was Tuesday afternoon after MDW (everyone left by Monday!) and there weren't many people left in Vegas. If there is no line outside, there's going to be hardly any line inside too when you're waiting to get your grub on those steamed king crab legs, oysters, prime rib, and moar. Literally there were only like 6 people in front of me everytime I wanted to grab some seafood so the wait time was extremely short! Short wait time = happy lisa!

Anyway let's get down to the nitty gritty details. Unlike brunch menu, dinner had a lot more to offer but I mainly focused on their seafood items. The steamed king crab legs were great--I can taste the sweetness of the crab and the crab meat was so meaty yet moist. I ate a whole plate full of crab legs to myself! Their oysters are probably one of the best I've eaten at a buffet. Totally beats M Hotel's Studio B buffet oysters that are greyish-black and.. questionable. I also tried their seafood paella which was just good--never had real paella so can't be the judge of it. The steamed shrimp thing was okay, would much rather eat the crabs and oysters.

I also tried pasta which was super good and had some creme brulee for dessert. I overly stuffed myself with seafood so couldn't venture to try out more of their menu but will save it for next time!

Warning: I wouldn't have enjoyed their buffet as much if I had to wait in line for 3 hrs to get in and also wait in line everytime I wanted to grab a plate of food. I think Bacchanal is only noteworthy when you can go during the weekday or slow days!

Absolutely beautiful and incredible. 

What's the most amazing part? The little things and all the individual dishes/parts in such a big buffet are still perfectly executed.

I don't normally like buffets - I never eat enough to get my money's worth, but everyone keeps talking about Bacchanal..sooo I had to try it! Loved it! Was it worth the $60? If you're gonna eat at a buffet and spend $40-50 then you might as well eat here! 

You must go there, get a ticket and then come back for the assigned time you have on your ticket. That way people aren't waiting in a massive line. We got there at 3pm on a Saturday and the earliest time available was 5:40pm.

I came here for dinner, mostly for the fresh oysters everyone kept raving about. It was definitely good and fresh, unlike other buffets.

Lamb chops were also very good. I don't usually like lamb because it's too gamey for my liking, but these were so good! 

They also had steamed mussels! Omgggg I couldn't stop eating them.

I had plates after plates of mussels, crab legs, and oysters!

Then I headed over to get some desserts. I liked this green tea cake they had and the macaroons were good too! Creme brûlée! A good selection of gelato! 

Oh and they had juices in these cute bottles! I grabbed the guava one and I really liked it!

We came here for a brunch. OMG!!!!! This place is amazing, the quality of the food is really good. THe selection is amazing. It looks like it recently has been renovated, everything is new. I am definitely going back.

I won 50 bucks playing some silly slot machine featuring a meerkat jumping into holes, so it was like my meal at Bacchanal was free. But even if I had been in the red, I would have gladly ponied up the money to spend a couple hours at this, the greatest buffet of all the buffets.

I'm not going to list everything I ate, but here are the highlights:

Impossibly good pho. Who'd have thought a buffet would have such delicious pho? I almost didn't get it because I assumed it would be a mediocre waste of space, but it ended up being the high point of my meal.

Meat. The brisket was my favorite. Perfectly seasoned and cooked, juicy and yummy.

Desserts. Usually I don't go too crazy with desserts at buffets, but I couldn't help myself here. The made-to-order bananas foster crepe was probably the best dessert I ate, but I loved just about everything.

Wait service was pretty on the ball with drinks. There were a couple of lulls here and there, but we were taking our sweet time in there, so I didn't mind it too much.

I've been to a lot of buffets in Vegas, including other high-priced spots like Bellagio, Wynn and Aria, but Bacchanal is the only one I will return to over and over again in the future. It's that good, and totally worth the money.

Came here thinking the lines would be long, but to our surprise, we waited 10 minutes the most at the pay line and 20 minutes to get seated. We just touched down in Vegas, driving for 5 hours, traffic on and off the whole way, we were HONGRY! 

I went straight to the oysters and got myself a plate full, some crab legs and ceviche. YUM!! I loved the oysters, definitely fresh. I ate about 30 that night. I wanted to go back the next day for more.

All the other foods were okay, but I'm glad the buffet was huge and had lots of diff selections. My son loved the spicy Mac n cheese (he's 15 months old). My fiancé loved the wagyu sliders.

Oh and the fresh juices!! Soooo good! Wicked spoon doesn't have anything like it. Before trying bacchanal, I loved wicked spoon, but I can now say I found my new fav!!

this place as far as quality and variety is as good as it gets for a las vegas buffet. be sure to get there super early for dinner to beat the crowds. their seafood and dessert selections are outstanding. my personal favorites there included the jumbo shrimp cocktail, pho noodles, and thai tea ice cream. since we went on a holiday weekend the price was increased by $10 per person. however we felt we got our money's worth. also had 4 different non alcoholic beverages which are included in the meal (mango and pineapple juice, ginger gale, and green tea).  i would go back for the sure. but as for overall value the M resort is still the one to beat!

First off, the price is RIDICULOUS! It is probably the most expensive buffet on the strip. Being an avid Wicked Spooner, I felt guilty for trying Bacchanal because I didn't want to fall in love with the place but, I FAILED. I did fall in love with it.

My boyfriend & I visited around late lunch time on a Tuesday. No crowd (yet) which was good. You walk in & it's seriously an array of food heaven. Fresh juice, oysters, all your favorite carved meats, Asian cuisine, etc. 

We personally loved eating the fresh oysters (they run out fast, so get em quick), duck, sweet potato tots, sushi cone rolls, fresh watermelon juice, peach green tea & definitely the desserts. Had some meringue, crepes with nutella, thai tea ice cream & french toast ice cream.

You have to come extremely hungry so you can get your money's worth! I've heard people also come in around 3PM-ish so you can get both lunch and dinner entrees, since they don't kick you out. Overall it was a great foodventure, expensive, but great nonetheless.

I was expecting to have KING Crab leg for the price of $70/person (holiday price, not included tax & tips ). It is a FALSE ADVERTISEMENT, the king crab leg is only for premium members, they only provide snow crab for everyone else. 
Good variety of foods but they taste just decent...
Won't come back again..

Went for brunch, simply amazing. 
Got here at 11 on a Sunday and got right in. Once 11:30 hit it turned into a circus and an hour wait!!!

Highlights:
Steak & eggs
Dim Sum (far in the back corner)
Variety of fruit juices
Street tacos 
Sweet potato tots
Shrimp & grits 
Flan 
Bread pudding 
Mussels 
Clams


So-so:
Chilaquilles 
Sticky bun
Pancakes

I mean, it was so so but still the buffet is amazing. More expensive on a Sunday, about $50pp but it was a phenomenal meal

Came here the day after Christmas for lunch with my family and holiday prices were in effect. It ended up being approx. $68/person.

Food: Good
- There are a few different types of food offered here like Asian cuisine, American, Italian, and etc.
- The best thing about this buffet is the types of Asian/American/Italian cuisine offered. For example, there was pho, egg drop soup, and curries. I was pretty impressed with this since most buffets won't offered this many selections.
- I really enjoyed the variety and quality of the food here. I especially liked the prime rib, el lote, and steamed crab (pro-tip: head over to the section to the left of the pizza, place your plate on the top of the counter and ask for steamed crab instead of boiled).

Location/Parking/Seating: Poor
- The buffet is located in Caesar's Palace and parking is about $10
- The directional signs make it easy to locate the buffet, but once you get there you'll definitely be in for a surprise
- The lines can be up to 2 hours (we came at 2pm and it was about 1 hr wait). Once you wait to pay, you'll have to wait even longer to be seated.
- Dining limit is 2.5 hours

Install, I enjoyed the food here and would recommend to at least try this once. It is a steep price but it may be good to a celebration instead of a casual meal.

This place is literally my favorite Buffet in Las Vegas everytime I'm in town at least one of the nights I have to have dinner here their variety and different types of food makes it greats even for the most pickiest people

It was a typical strip buffet in Vegas...couple of more dollars per person than other comparable buffets. Over-hyped for the offerings that you can get in other places...not the greatest service at the crepes station. Had to try it...probably wouldn't go back.

Use to be my favorite buffet in Vegas. Came on a Saturday around 7. Waited hour 45 mins. Anticipated a great meal, only to be disappointed. Went for the meat area 1st. Prime rib being my 1st choice but they said it'll be a 25 min wait. WHAT!! I paid $60 to wait 25 mins later for an item that's suppose to be on the menu!!! I'll be done w/ my meal in 25 mins!!! Okay, make the best of this situation. Next stop, seafood. Steamed crab was extremely SALTY. ugh!!! Stir fried crab, bland. Okay, it's been 15 mins, lets try the meat section again. Prime rib came out! YES!! Medium please. The cow was still beating. Blood covered my plate. It was so undercooked that I lost the taste for meat for awhile. Beef rib was cold and extremely SALTY!!! Pork rib was cold. Clam chowder was watered down and bland. Desserts was great though. Service was awesome!!! Oooh the disappointment! What a waste of $60.

Soooooo much to choose from! It's pricey but well worth it! I'd pay and go again. Make sure you're hungry because it has a wide variety of food! They had Mexican food, Chinese food, American food, salads, fruits appetizers, sea food. Too many to name. The crepes cooked right in front of you are so good! Loved this place!

Personally I find this buffet overhyped and overpriced.  They have a lot of options but nothing was good enough to make me want it again. We wanted to try something new as we usually go to the wicked spoon. But I found it over priced for the quality. We also paid for the mimosas and they barely ever come back to fill it up so we didn't get our moneys worth there. Wouldn't recommend

Well, maybe I'm just not a buffet person anymore, but the whole wait time and price for what I ate, wasn't impressive.  First, the crab legs were really skinny, and not meaty at all.  Second, the oysters were the worst I've ever tasted.  They were super flat, paper thin, hardly any oysters on the shell, and tasted grimy and sandy.  There were lots of sand or tiny stones on other shellfish as well.  Other dishes were ok, which is expected at buffets.  I think it's a fun dining experience to walk around to get as many variety of food as I want, but as far as quality of food and taste, it was just ok.  The best part of the meal were the desserts.  Desserts were really tasty...especially the cream brûlée, mini donuts, egg tarts, and gelato....those were worthy~yum!!  One other thing, they charged my 11yr old an adult price, but she ate even less than I did.  Well, we tried it once, and that was that.

I came here for my birthday and it just so happens to be a Mexican holiday so I guess the buffet price was a bit more than usual. I came at 2:30pm on a Saturday and paid $55. I had to wait in line for about an hour. 

When I finally got seated, my friends and I didn't know where to start! There was soo many selections and everything looked delicious! I went for the king crabs and oysters! They tasted so fresh and easy to eat.
I ate my money worth here and my favorite part was the dessert section! They had macarons and ice cream, and you can even make your own crepe! I was so full from eating all the food but always have room for dessert. 
This place did not disappoint. I would defiantly come here again and try some other foods that I didn't get to try.

As far as buffets goes, this is the best I have ever experienced. I am someone who cannot stand buffets because of the germs that often comes with the name. However, Bacchanal Buffet is the exception. The restaurant was extremely clean as they staff constantly wiping down counters and tables as well as changing out old pans including serving utensils. 

I dined here back in March of 2014 when I was in Vegas for vacation. Because my boyfriend is a platinum member on some Vegas deal he has, we were able to skip the long line ( GREAT bonus) and be seated right away. We had a server who came and took drink orders and we were on our way to feast on great food!

The buffet is gigantic. It's almost overwhelmingly large to where you don't know where to start. They have different "stations" offering a variety of food from salad bars, to BBQ, Italian, American, Asian, seafood, and so on. Because the buffet is so large, there were stations I missed completely because I never got around to visiting every station

 The best buffet to me was the dessert bar. Wow! Every dessert your heart desires they just about had. 

They are expensive $50. However, the meal ended up being free for us because my boyfriend had over $400 worth of pts to use at restaurants so the cost didn't "hurt" us. But even if we did had to pay out of pocket, it would have been worth every dollar. The food, the service, the atmosphere all were considered when dining here.

I cannot wait to get back to Vegas so I can go back. You will not find a better buffet than Bacchanal Buffet.

Just like they claim in all their ads around town - Best buffet in Vegas! Many buffets have a lot of different types & styles of food to offer just like this one, but if you compare each dish alone to the quality of a restaurant that specializes in that type, the buffet food doesn't hold it's own. But not here! 

Each dish ranked in the top 3 I've ever had, from the beef brisket and ribs, to their pizza, Thai food. I could have stayed on one style of food & would have been completely satisfied! The night before, we ate at another well known buffet and I was disappointed by the quality but with the quantity of different types made the dinner alright. There may have been only 2-3 dishes I'd even want to go back for seconds. Here I wished I could have, on pretty much every dish but the stomach wouldn't let me.

I did straddle the meal between lunch & dinner (which started at 3pm) to get the lower $ (35 instead of 50). Yes it's a bit pricey but SOOO worth it!

Personally, I think it's overrated. There are not more than 100 dishes like people said. The prices are too expensive. About the foods, some of them are salty, some of them are too much cheesy. The dessert is not as good as the Wicked Spoon. However, seafoods and the services are good and nice.

Awesome buffet. 3 years ago I saw a few signs that said Spices Buffet at planet hollywood was voted the best. So we tried it and it sucked. Then 2 years ago I saw signs that said Bacchanal buffet was voted the best. But was hesitant because I was lied to before with the Spices Buffet.  This year I see they're still ranked at #1 so decided to try it. IT WAS AWESOME!!!

I had about 8 glasses of different juices. Strawberry, Guava, Jamaican, and mango! The food is very good also. The buffet is well organized. you have to check in at the terminal and they let you know what time to come back.  We went on a thursday around 8:30pm and had to come back at 8:50.  It was pretty crowded. After that it only took about 5 mins to be seated.

My 2nd visit to Bacchanal Buffet was a disappointment. My DH and I ate here 2 1/2 yrs ago and were impressed with the quality of the food and its presentation. Yesterday we revisited Bacchanal and I had a major let down. What happened to the individual servings in their cute dish/bowls? There were still some individual servings but majority of the dishes were self-serve.  The seafood didn't look fresh; the prawns and crab  legs lack the vibrant orange/pink color, looked more pale in color. The prime rib was tough--texture more like roast beef. For $51.99pp, I expected better.

A pretty massive buffet. If you aren't sure what you're craving, I'm pretty sure you can find something here.

I went through a few plates and everything that I ate was pretty good. Countless rounds of crab legs and claws and scallops. My cholesterol levels are probably still pretty high after eating here. The chinese food is basically pei wei level sort of chinese food, nothing crazy. I didn't try the sushi because I get a little nervous around buffet and raw fish forces combining. It just shouldn't happen. The desserts are hit or miss. Then creme brulee is good, the flan was ok, some of the mini cakes were meh.  Everyone in our group seemed pretty happy after eating nonstop however.

Service- subpar. Drinks were dreadfully slow to come out. Some of the drinks that came out were wrong. 

Bacchanal isn't the cheapest buffet out there, but it's definitely one of the biggest and you can't deny the vast variety of food you can get.

I am not terribly well versed in Las Vegas buffets as I hail from Massachusetts, but I did not like this buffet.  The price was substantially higher than the other buffets that I saw in Vegas.  This would have been an excusable offense but I did not find the food to be very good. The beef was either over cooked and dry or fatty and under cooked.  The selection of sushi was so underwhelming it made me wonder why they even bothered to offer it.  They had the standard pasta selection and I did enjoy the pasta with seafood.  On the whole though the food just wasn't very good.
Price was actually 59$ per person when i was there around christmas time. but i thought it was worth it, only worse part of the meal was the mexican food. I also killed the desserts!

We know we had to do a buffet while we are out in Vegas.  While we been to the all you can eat off the strip at Fogo de Chao (see my reviews), this buffet at Caesar got favorable reviews amongst the rest.  Price wise, we went weekday afternoon for 39.95 per person (kids age 10 below) half off.  It comes with non alcoholic drink of your choice.  I opted to pay an additional $15 for unlimited choice of mimosa, champagne, sangria, or wine.  Believe you me, I got my money's worth.  That $15 fee is non transferable and only apply to that one person in the table.  Now onto the food selections, it is more than anyone can eat.  For lunch, they had shrimp cocktails, tacos, bone marrow, etc.  They also have snow crab legs which are chilled but if you ask, they will warm up no problem.  Sushi selection is so so.  They do have udon, ramen section which my son loves.  The dinner price goes into effect at 3pm at close to $60 I think.  Tip - go around 2 ish and you will have the layover when they bring out dinner items such as ribs, lambs, Peking duck etc.  All in all, great buffet place and a very exquisite seating ambiance.  Only bad thing is you have to show up early as the lines to actually get seated in the queue is lonnggggggg.

This buffet is the definition of gluttony and everything Vegas is about! If there's something you're craving, Bacchanal probably has it. I've been here twice and I can't deny that quality and taste of the food is really good. My only suggestion is to try everything you possibly can because this place is pretty pricey. First time I came here the Mimosa Brunch was ~$65 and more recently dinner was also around the same price. Definitely a must-try though!

OMG!!! Great selection, great food, great price for what you get!
The line can get long, but there are definitely times when there is almost no wait; but, the wait is worth it. Pastries, desserts (including sugar free), a meat carving station, seafood, pizza, omelettes, Asian, street tacos, breads, etc. I will definitely come back to this one again.

Meh - it wasn't that impressive. I would have rather paid $700 for 5 star service than being in a cattle line.  The food was nothing to write home about.
We had to stand in line for over 2 hours, only to have our party split into 2 groups and placed separately. I might go back, but not during dinner on a weekend. No, they don't take reservations.

Excellent food! Great service! Maricela our waiter,  kept our mimosa glass always full!! We got there close to 11am, so we were able to try the breakfast and lunch menu!! Not busy, didn't feel rushed.  All very fresh very tasty, definitely worth the price.

Before I like to start my review...Thank you my fellow Chiver that got me and friend in without waiting in line...Keep Calm and Chive On

Service: From the host to the server, I was welcomed with open arms with gentle gestures and a big smile.  The server was very kind to come to my table the moment we arrived, took our drink orders, and after that, me and my friend went to grab our food.  The moment we came back, our drinks were already there.  He was on top of our refills and clearing our table.  That's just amazing.

Food: The taste was simply amazing.  Easily, the best buffet I've been to in Las Vegas. I was told the buffet in Wynn or other places were the best, but no, this place IS the best.  The food have been properly seasoned, it's not bland, not overcooked, and doesn't taste like it was sitting under the lamp for hours.  If you're going to spend a good amount of money for a buffet, this is the place.  If you're broke, there's Rio. hahaha

Arrive early if you plan to dine here for brunch. Do not wait in line. There are many buffets that are comparable in terms of quality and options (Bellagio and Wicked Spoon are my other favorites).

They make several fresh squeezed juices. I opted for the OJ and was pleasantly surprised by the freshness.

Favorites: Waffles were good, flaky and could be topped with a variety of fresh fruit. Make sure to visit the crepe station for some hot, flavorful bites. The carving station offered a nice variety of meats.

Skip: Fried chicken was dry. I suggest passing on the biscuits too.

Don't forget to try the gelato or sorbets on your way out!

Heard this was the buffet in town so I went for Brunch. All breakfast food was under lights but was cold. No fun eating cold eggs Benedict, hashbrowns, bacon and pancakes. I decided to get the "French toast to order" because I thought it. might be hot. They pulled a cold slice out of a drawer. Crepes made fresh were good (and hot). I ended up eating the pastries and drank a lot of coffee. I should have gone to the Bellagio buffet. It's way better. 50$ down the drain.

WOW!!!! That's all i can say. Im a big guy 6ft 305lbs so obviously i love to eat, and this buffet is hands down the best in town for selection and quality. It is a little on the pricey end but for what you pay if you can eat that much its well worth it. Multiple kinds of meat from steak,chicken,pork,sausage and many many more all ready to cut and serve. When i went i did not eat the whole day before going and def got my money's worth. I would recommend this if you are really and hungry and want to enjoy an array of good quality foods.

My first visit to Bacchanal during NYE weekend I waited for almost 2 hours for a table for 8! Despite the wait- it easily became my favorite buffet. Why? TOMAHAWK RIBEYE STEAK ON THE BONE! I was speechless when the chef offered me the entire steak at the carving station. I recently went back again and had less than a 30 min wait for brunch, which was much nicer. Food was still excellent, enjoyed the variety, took advantage of the mimosas, and even though there weren't tomahawks this time around during brunch... Bacchanal is definitely still the fave!

Bacchanal is one of those "must try" places in Vegas, so we came for Sunday brunch and it was about $48 per person with tax. TIP: Don't pay the gratuity when you pay at the front before being seated because our server mentioned they aren't sure how it's split, so if you like your server tip at the end before you leave at the table! 

We were seated quickly as there was virtually no line around 10AM on a Sunday, and our server quickly took our drink orders and described the layout of the buffet to us. 

We quickly began planning out where we wanted to start and how to pace ourselves so we could enjoy as much as possible! I was impressed to see the made-to-order ramen and udon, as well as the seafood and carving station, and of course the made-to-order dessert crepes and gelato. 

Overall my favorite was the potato au gratin side which came out super hot and fresh, as well as red velvet pancakes, unlimited mimosas, and the dessert crepes. While the seafood and carving station was great, the lines were long and the food wasn't amazing, just average. In my opinion while the service and staff were amazing and the interior was gorgeous, for the food and price, this particular buffet was overrated. With so many other great options on the strip in Las Vegas, it might be a while before I visit Bacchanal again.

This is definitely the better buffet of the Harrah's/Caesar owned buffets. The decorations remind me of a modern 50s-60s feel with light colors and a lot of grey and brown mixed in. There is a wide variety of furniture and upholstery which gives the place a comfy look.

The food was amazing. Try the leek, shumai, and sushi bar in the asian section, lasagna in the italian section, and chicken and waffles in a basket. The congee is pretty good too. The dessert section has delicious gelato and sorbet with a large variety of other sweets for everything else.

My only gripe was that the clam chowder was over salted and some of the other American dishes had a lot of salt too. 

I would definitely come here again and not mind the 45-50 minute wait in line.

This place has been on my radar for years and I finally came here for Lunch.  

Disregard all the negative reviews.......If you want to eat at the best Buffet in Vegas (and possible the entire world) come to the Bacchanal.

5 STARS!
The best buffet in Vegas!! Every time I'm there we have to stop by for at least 1 meal.  The price is right with a large variety of food.

Imagine a $$$ restaurant - gourmet food. Think of another $$$ gourmet restaurant. Think of another. And another. and another. Now put those all together and you got yourself Bacchanal Buffet.

You can seriously take a tour of the world in this place. From Asia to Italy to US, you can enjoy the cuisines in one location. 

A few highlight dishes in my opinion:
- Fresh Cocktail Shrimp. They were HUGE! and juicy and fresh.
- Truffle sliced potatoes au gratin - it just melts in your mouth
- Tonkatsu Ramen - the noodle was aight but the broth was pretty decent
- Horchata (drink) - in the Mexican Food section
- Gelato Pistachio 
- Sweet Potato Tater Tots - light, sweet, crisp

I've been to several buffets on the strip is this one is definitely the top 2. The Wynn Buffet is the other top 2. Has better meat section (Veal, Lamb) but Bacchanal offers more variety and quantity since it has more real estate. 

Price has definitely gone up since it has opened. I ate at $35 dollars (TR price) in the 2nd week after it opened. This time around, i paid $50 (TR price) on Friday night.

This is food heaven. Seriously. Presentation, service, and cleanliness, this place lives up to its hype and cost. For all you buffet lovers, heavy eaters, this is THE buffet to go to in Vegas.

GO GO GO GO GO!

For my first visit to Bacchanal, I came here at 2:30 on a Wednesday. Just in time for the end of lunch (lunch price $37 pp + tax = $41 and change). Dinner price $52 starts at 3pm. They give you a two hour time limit but we stayed 2.5 hours without anyone coming to bother us. 

I mostly ate meats, fish, seafood, salad, juice, and dessert. Can't really go wrong with anything here. Tables and tables and tables of food. Left really stuffed but quite satisfied.

Well after reading all the great reviews on this buffet located in Caesar's Palace. We had to check it out for ourselfs.Lunch is served until 3pm then it changes over to dinner. We showed up around 2:20 and paid the lunchen price around $29. with tax. hey no line at that time for us.maybe just lucky? OK here's my grades for what I ate ..A being the best that I ever had on down.
Prime Rib B+
Chicken noodle soup A+
Ribs C
Coffee A
Baked Beans A-
Shrimp&sauce A
Blueberry cobbler& Ice cream  A
Service A
All in All this IS the best buffet in town .....would I pay $29 again? ...probably

My favorite buffet in Vegas. 

I always go straight for the stone crab claws. At least two plates. 

Then I move on to the truffle and mushroom pizza. 

Make sure you save room for the made to order crepes! My favorite is the Nutella with bananas. But my tip is to get a plate of whole strawberries and house made whip cream to go with your crepes.

Wow! The choices here are amazing! Prime rib, lobster, bbq, oysters, crab, sushi, etc etc etc. The place also looks beautiful! Servers are great, no real complaints. 

Expect 1-3 hour wait during peak times. We came at 930 and waited 2 minutes but by 1030 the line was insane! 

Cons: although superb in choices, no dishes were amazing. The lobster was over cooked, most items were salty, and drink options are limited. Also, they advertise king crab legs, but they "mix" it with snow crab legs, aka king crabs actually are like unicorns

You can choose to go here with the "Buffet of Buffets!" however they do ask you to pay a little extra on top.  

At Bacchanal, you can stuff your face with the finest cuisine!

I am not a buffet lover, but you can't go wrong with the buffet at Bacchanal.  There is a wide selection to tickle your taste buds.  The best part is that it doesn't taste like mass produced barf worthy buffet food.  Everything you want to eat is very fresh!

I highly recommend going to this buffet.  Ideally, go with then have oysters, crab legs, and macaroons! Oysters are on weekdays and dinner during the weekend.  On the weekend you have to pay for bottomless mimosas, which by the way are extremely strong!  

Drinker beware!

Food was amazing! The highlight of the day was our waiter. I forgot her name but she was amazing!!! Remember they have a groupon for this buffet. Use it. Save you some money. They only serve seafood all day only on the weekends.

After all the years running an All You Can Eat buffet, you'd think Caesar's Palace would figure out how to take a customer's money quickly and seat that customer promptly.  But they apparently haven't figured that out yet.  Hardly any people in line, yet it took 7 minutes for me to reach a cashier, then 5 more minutes in a second line waiting for a table.  For the outrageous price, you'd think a cash customer deserved better service.

The food is diverse, with some unusual items like Osso Buco, Bone Marrow, Har Gaw, Escargots, Menudo, Green Tea Gelato and others.  All of these are very expertly prepared, so that part is good.  It's that lengthy wait that  prompts me to rate them three stars instead of four.

If you prefer a traditional diet instead of the exotic fare mentioned above, you can find a better priced buffet in Vegas than the $55 that Caesar's charges.  It's your choice.

I came here for a wedding reception. The party was small (25-30 people).  They sat us way in the back which was fine until I saw the biggest cockroach I've ever seen. The manager barely offered an apology.

Stopped in on a Saturday for brunch with my bf. We bought the groupon, and on weekends you have to use it by 10am, so when we arrived, there was no line at all. We had a bit of an issue with my voucher, and the lady at the register was pretty rude about it, like she was in a rush to get us out of line... Even though we were the only ones there at the time. Didnt even ask us if we wanted drinks at all. Whatever, so we just paid full price since we didn't want to wait and we had a festival to get to later that day. 
The food was good, but we expected better. It was a lot of hype. The Asian food was lacking in flavor. The selection from the meat carving section was great, loved the pastas. There was so much to choose from. The portioned out items were cute , such as the mini baskets of chicken and waffles, and the mini stacks of pancakes. Adorable presentation. The dessert bar seemed pretty standard for Vegas buffets. 
 My bf said he actually preferred wicked spoon over at cosmopolitan though in overall quality. I feel it was on the good side of standard, minus the super rude cashier, but we probably wouldn't come back without the working groupon.

This place... WOW! The food here is absolutely delicious. The Steamed crab legs, the plump cocktail shrimp, the juicy lamb chops. I could go on and on of what my wife tried at the buffet.  The range of food is amazing and in my opinion the best on the strip. I would highly recommend eating at Bacchanal

This place is a palace within a palace. This place is a monstrosity.  There is so much at this place, it is impossible to see everything they offer.  It goes on for miles and miles.  This place requires the most planning.  Do not get sidetracked with sliders and hot dogs and pizza.  Go straight for the stuff you cannot get at any normal restaurant in your hometown.  Go straight for the ultimate amounts of meats and shellfish.

My wife received a recommendation about this Buffet. We waited in line (not very long, maybe 15-20 minutes).  But there were others who just walked right in though and that disturbed us a little feeling overlooked. We had been first in line, the dining area wasn't completely full. The food offered, Not too bad, Good meat selections. The crab legs selection was very poor and seemed like the crab legs were anemic. The asian food was typical from your run of the mill Chinese American restaurant. Deserts were okay. I've experienced better Buffets in Vegas. The hype for this one did not meet my expectations. May give it another chance to see if our visit was a fluke.

Aside from the longgg line up, this is definitely the best buffet in vegas. Their quality of food is top notch--if you're a meat eater, the prime rib is to die for!! They have a great selection of different ethnic foods. We came here for brunch and they served bottomless mimosas and even fresh squeezed juice!! Evrn though it's a tad more expensive than other buffets, I personally think it is worth every penny!

This is by far one of the best buffet I've had at Vegas on the strip. It is located in Cesar palace hotel and casino section. If you end up at the mall section of the resort just walk over and you'll be able to find it with the signs and everything.

Getting a seat here is easy, but the wait can be very long. Depending on the time, that's the food they are serving. I usually like to go for dinner because they do add more variety to the buffet, such as oysters and crab legs. 

I went during their "brunch" time and paid roughly around 50 something. This buffet has so much choices and it's all fresh. My favorite things on here would be the dessert and the seafood section. Their Mexican "street tacos" is super good! Totally love it! 

I can't emphasize on how great the dessert is. The best dessert I do love is the rice pudding. Another great thing is something called Thai bubble. It's ice cream with chocolate bark and I think some dessert pearls. 

I totally recommend coming here for dessert, esp during dinner.

The line was very long. We went for Thursday brunch.  Luckily as a Caesars diamond player, we were able to bypass the line.  But we sat and figured we would order our drinks then adventure off.  Probably for 10 minutes  we sat there-- normally I'm patient, but I was a little hungover and needed a Bloody Mary...and there was a whole buffet at our finger tips!  Finally after putting our drinks in, we ventured off.  

The other reviews are pretty accurate about the variety and quality, but as a non-seafood fan...this place was not for me.  I thought I was safe on one of the salads, it had fruit in it.  But when I returned to table, I noticed the shrimp.  I'm not going to rant much about it....its just not for me. And for that reason 3 stars as "OK".

I will skip this one and hit up the wicked spoon at the Cosmo.

Came here with my company for our company dinner in Las Vegas.

Reservations must be made through Caesar's restaurants about 2 weeks prior. However on the day of, everything was set up, the host was very accommodating.

(Food) I think this buffet is worth the price for it's CRAB. Literally, I divulged into 4 plates of CRAB and left very satisfied. I cannot comment on their other protein selection since I didn't try them, but will gladly go back to get more CRABS.

Absolutely the best buffet in Las Vegas! The selection is plentiful and the food is always fresh. My favorite section is the snow crab legs they don't hold back and give you tons of it precut already! The oyster shoots are another must have! They're just the right temp and fresh. Desert bar? Yes indeed! A whole section dedicated to sugar delights that are irresistible! The whole place is a must on your Vegas trip! You'll never get bored of this one! Keep your bellies ready, you'll never experience so much deliciousness under one roof like this place!
They were just ok They even charge for water. Where do they do that at? My salad was wilted lettuce. . I don't think i. Will return

As expected, there was a great variety of food to eat. The food was of great quality, and looked very presentable. However, in terms of taste, it was average. I actually thought everything looked better than it tasted. The sushi was decent, make sure to ask double or triple meat for the pho, crab legs were great, prime rib was cooked pink, exactly how I liked it, but didn't taste anything special. I tried so many different items that I can't list them all, but nothing really stood out to me to be honest. The ice cream was probably my favorite, lol.

Expensive but the quality of the food is totally worth it! Their seafood dishes are great and they have some dishes from Gordon Ramsay & other chef restaurants there to sample. They have a wide variety from seafood, Italian, Mexican, American, Chinese, Japanese, and Vietnamese. Their desserts are so rich. If you're gonna pay alot for a buffet, pay it here and make your money's worth!

I used to love the Wynn buffet and refused to try anywhere else.  Many of my friends told me about the Bacchanal buffet and finally i gave it a try last Thursday night.  It was $46.99 for dinner and I was so happy with the food choices and quality.

I was going to give a 5 star rating but i took out 1 star because of the service.  My server pretty much disappeared after the first drink, and no one came to pick up our plates and I had to brought the plates to other servers in order to get spaces for the table.  

My favorite dishes:
- Rib eye steak (Juicy and tender)
- Fresh made taco 
- Korean Ginseng chicken soup 
- King Crab Legs and Cocktail shrimp
- Onion rings & potato wedges (very fresh and tasty)
- Fried Pork Skin
- Tonkotsu Ramen
- Shrimp Scampi
- Strawberry Mochi 
- Creme Brulee

Awful. Basic buffet.Not only is it more expensive than Wicked Spoon but presentation is gross. The food was just ok. Nothing special.Not coming back. The Seafood station was the only thing that was nice.

$68 jacked up holiday price was not worth the food and the chaos and headache of getting inside and the pandemonium that ensues inside... the server was good... the food was great! But the wait time was so long in lines it was cold by the time you return to your seat. Very sad experience! PS the desert bar is also fantastic! But the wait kills how good it is as well!!! 

Update: I was contacted by the manager shortly after this post. Very professional and genuinely seemed to care about my experience! We will try again next time we are there because of that follow up service!

The best buffet I've been to, anywhere and everywhere. High-class super premium quality in both food and presentation. Love the oysters and peeled jumbo shrimp. The fresh Mexican juices/drinks was a nice surprise -- especially the Horchata and Tamarind. Cold and warm steamed crab legs, Chinese including Peking duck, and an authentic Italian offering (with cheeses and salami) round out an internationally eclectic menu that seems to have been designed for a top notch non-buffet restaurant.  Amazing dessert selection. Fast efficient service, including self-pay kiosks while waiting in line. I highly recommend this place -- pay the extra $10-$20 and enjoy a truly one-of-a-kind buffet! A+ 5 stars ******

Hands down the best buffet I have ever been to in Las Vegas.Sets the bar very high! There is plenty of variety to choose from and the quality of the food was excellent. Awesome experience! Will definitely go back.

Bacchanal Buffet...you have now entered the level of sin known as Gluttony. HAHA! I jokes but seriously, this place has A LOT of foooooooood!

First let's talk about the line and getting in. There are 4-5 computer stations where you enter your party number (if greater than 5 you must talk to the receptionist), enter your phone number, and then you'll receive a receipt. The receipt shows you what time you're supposed to come back to officially wait in that 130-170 minute line. Say whaaaaaaat?!! yup, I was surprised too. But hold the phone, there may be times where they'll text you to come and line up before the time it says on your receipt. That's what happened to us and it saved us an hour. 

The price is hefty and will very hefty for those large parties. Dinner was $67.99 on this holiday occasion. Go big or go home. Yes you can go to other cheaper places but this is Bacchanal. You've got to at least try it once. 

The food was exquisite; they had fresh crab legs, shrimp, prime rib, brisket, and so much more food. By plate number 4, I was already asking for tea to help settle that stomach because you know what's going to happen after all this. 

Dessert was good; gelato and other delectables. I will have to add in that the "cake pop" is not a cake pop. It's filled with crushed dreams! No it really does look like a cake pop but has like ganache inside.

The best place ever!!!! Super, super fresh and high quality oyster! And the Chinese food is not bad at all! There are many "American Chinese food" but Cesars definitely has "Chinese Chinese food", they remind me home!
Also, don't forget the fresh juice and desert! Definitely try the flan, it was AMAZING! I also had creme brûlée and it was ok.
I'm so easy to please and I've never disliked a place more. Thoroughly annoyed. No crab legs till 3pm. Such a waste! Never coming again. Should've went to the Bellagio.

Quantity buffet !

The hype was there but this venue sadly didn't live up to its billing.

The Sunday lunch spread looked promising and at a higher than ave price you are ready to enjoy the Bacchanalian (sorry can't help it) buffet.

Food taste were all average , nothing stood out for a second helping. This is true for seafood , Asian , Italian and carvery.

Saving grace? 7 upcharge for endless mimosa !

Crowded yes, over  the top delish ? No.
Better to go at Wynn and Wicked Spoon.

We almost left when we saw the price... almost 60 bucks a pop... the most expensive buffet we've been to. But..but..but... wow!! I don't think I've ever thought buffet food could actually taste good but I was wrong. And they had lamb chops!! Its kind of secretly tucked away but lamb chops make you get your moneys worth. My faves- clam bake, shrimp cocktail, mac n cheese, chocolate chip fudge cookie, and steak tacos. Highly recommend if you come on an empty stomach so you can get your moneys worth. Also our servers were awesome!

This place is amazing! Super long line but it definitely worth the wait, so bring your appetite.  There's a medley of food options, but I'd say stick with the seafood area and the lamb.  All the Japanese and Chinese food towards the back area isn't really worth your time and neither is the pizza.  Stick with the meat cuts and you will be set.  The dessert bar is to die for as well so make sure you save room!

This experience was thorougly underwhelming.  I am generally not a buffet fan but thought I should try this one, as it's such a Vegas experience and this is billed as the best buffet in Vegas.  

The crab legs were good, though kind of watery and cold.  The rest of the food was not that exciting!  We tried a bit from each area of the buffet and every cooked item was like a "not quite as good as the real thing" version of the real item.  The only things that were really good were the uncooked things - like cheese etc.  The desserts were pretty good.  Overall though, for the price, you could eat a pretty decent meal elsewhere.  I wouldn't go back.

I have been to many casino buffets and this one TOPS my list. This was my second buffet in Vegas and I thought I had died and gone to heaven! I immediately went to the very beginning and as I was walking, I felt like the bar was never going to end. It literally stretches and wraps around a back wall that feels like it goes into 4 or 5 rooms. Every item is made to perfection. I only ate three plates as a main entrée (I avoid salad and bread at buffets) , and I had tried over 30 Items. The desert bar though, WOW. Gelato, made to order waffles and crepes, dipped strawberries, cheesecakes, etc. I cannot wait to go back to Vegas and eat here AGAIN!

The food here and the selection was ridiculous. The Asian food tasted better than typical American Asian places knowing that buffet's are usually not as tasty. The other food was really good. Best buffet I've ever have and I haven't had many! Haha but I've had typical ones, but not ones in Vegas. Can't compare to wicked spoon considering that one is suppose to good as well. Would recommend the Bacchanal! 

The thing that sucked was we put our number in so we can receive a text when it was time to eat knowing it'll take 65-75 minutes. We go walk around the shops, 25 minutes we get a text. Holy crap we didn't have to wait as long ... Ha! We checked in, and then had to wait in a line. Waited for over 50 minutes just to go pay. Then had to wait in another line to be seated. Why couldn't I just get receive a text to pay and then wait in a line to be seated. Literally waited in one line when I could have been walking around doing other stuff. If I would have known that, then I probably should have just got in the line anyways. What's the point of giving out the number. 

However, once you get seated, it was glorious! I do think the service is slow. Saw many tables empty waiting for hungry Vegas vacationers that could have been sat. But will they fix that? No because people will wait just like my wife and me!

Wasn't very impressed. Average fare, if you're not a seafood person. The little salads in the cups were delightful. Different ethnic sections to find what you are craving easily. If you're a Seafood lover, they definitely have you covered. From shellfish, to sushi to fried fish, it's all there.
Absolutely HATED the seats at the tables, quite cramped space wise. Getting out of those chairs wasn't an easy task, not even before I stuffed my face. They're great for an office, or waiting room, but not conducive to a restaurant environment. Talk about a chair eating you!

Luckily the line wasn't long when we got there around 11 am. I was expecting around an hour wait from all the reviews but my total wait was around 7 mins. Whew~~  I'm not sure if it's seasonal thing but they were having brunch all through out the week. If I remember correctly, weekend brunch price was a little higher than weekday. Dinner was around $20 more than brunch. They do have different kid's price. I paid $19.99 for my 7 year old and free for my 4 year old. 

As for the food, i thought they were pretty fresh and clean. Loved their fresh carrot juice.

Over rated and over priced! Totally not worth any wait or the $$$$

When it come to buffets... I am not a rookie; just FYI

Sorry Bacchanal, I really want to LOVE you, and I am so sad that I did not fall for you.  

The buffet is really pricey, even during brunch.  I am am spending about $110 for two, I expect the crab legs not to have ice all over and NOT looking dirty (Wynn The Buffet offer the best crab legs). The Asian food were weak. The sushi wasn't appetizing AT ALL and did not have many fish options; I had some and didn't care for it after two piece. The ramen soup was a waste of calories (I didn't finish the small bowl-- thank goodness).

Their dessert bar absolutely did not impress me. In fact, I didn't even bother getting anything there--- and that NEVER happens for me. 

Their meat line was long and I am guessing this place is more for carnivores.  I didn't eat any meat because I hit buffets to eat seafood to get my money worth.  So I can't bash this place for their meat buffet.

Vegas buffets are like politics.  Everyone has their own favorite and you can't change their minds.

Bacchanal

A feast fit for the gods.

Not sure if Zeus would dine on sweet potato tater tots or Hades would need a pot of salted boiling water to warm up crab legs, but these are two of the things that made my experience of the heralded buffet better than your average buffet experience in Las Vegas.

It was by choice that we tried this place during the mid-to-tail-end of lunch to avoid the notorious crunch of a dinner rush that seems to be a trait for all Vegas buffets. This move proved to be the best in that we waited merely about 15-20 minutes to enter the buffet lines and modernistic décor.

The usage of design and ergonomics seemed to be what impressed me at first. The appeal is pleasing to the eyes of the millennial and the jaded buffet goer. There is a theme with Vegas buffets as they try and entice you to believe that by offering a smorgasbord of so-called international fare you'll feel a small part of a palate that has experienced the world over without being a world traveler.

Bacchanal attempts to do this and while the winding selection is immense and you can travel from Pan-Asian food choices to the Italian and Mexican atypical selections in mere steps is no different than the buffets at the Bellagio or Aria. In a way, Vegas sells you on the idea that each hotel offers a differing set of amenities but the reality is that there is so much you can do in the way of hotel themes and troths of food set forth for the masses. 

The displays of the food seemed a little cluttered but it is expected amongst the limited spaces and the stations are manned with friendly and courteous people. It is impossible to think intimacy with Vegas' overall meaning, but at least at this buffet and at least during this one visit, the chefs and carvers were decent and friendly.
That is not to say the wait staff was on the same plane of service. Our attendee was hard to track down and considerably slow on getting us new plates and clearing the old ones. I mean, the only thing keeping this review from a highest rating is her attitude and the comparison between her and the gentleman who took over her shift towards the twilight of our buffet experience.

Anyhow, I rarely care about a place solely based on its help staff since it is a very difficult job and I am sure she had to deal with a marathon of impatient eaters and rude tourists and that may have been a cause to her lousy service.

The food Ah, yes! The food is very good for a buffet. The crab legs were one of the main reasons we came and to be honest, they weren't the best legs I have had in my limited buffet experience and the fact that there are two areas in which they are served made things a little more difficult to enjoy. The Asian portion of the buffet had an excellent selection of dumplings and a wide array of dishes from China down to sauces that harken back to a childhood of experiencing what masterfully accompanying ingredients my father would put together to accentuate the dish we were enjoying. 

There were wagyu beef sliders and a great selection of Neapolitan pizza and a carving station that had enough animal to make PETA squirm. However, the favorite of mine (and it seems so quaint that it is an appetizer, but I find comfort in the simplest of things). 

The aforementioned sweet potato tater tots seemed to be my favorite. The light encompassing brown sugar glaze that is gently laying its sugary goodness accentuated the little nibbles of Americana to a point where they simplistically made the mundane seem exaggerated.  They were stuck in a tie with the dumplings and the crepes but since no one ever mentions tater tots as their most enjoyable thing at a buffet, I would hedge them against anything else I consumed.

For $35 apiece for lunch you're not going to find much more quality and selection as you will at Bacchanal. In a town that makes you overpay for indulgence and excess, this was worth it. I would come back (probably on the dinner ticket...) and dine at the Feast because it is certainly delicious.

the buffet was above the average vegas buffet but a few things could've been done better...

- the layout of the buffet was all on one side but did not understand the placement of food...seafood closest to the register, meats, appetizers, asian cuisine at the very back and desserts in the middle of the buffet... im no expert on where the placement of food should be but didnt understand the asian cuisine at the very back...would think appetizers would be the very back and work you way to the front or it only makes sense...also because of the way the buffet is laid out, lines that form for the crab legs or prime rib congest other areas for diners to grab food and makes things very unorganized

- fruit ....there was hardly any fruit...i spotted some pinapple but there should be more

- price  was your average new buffet price for dinner at $44.95...for an extra $15 dollars you are able to hop into the express line to skip the line...didn't think it was worth it too much since the line moved rather quickly

- food:  tried quite a few things but the items worth mentioning were the prime rib which was a 3.5 out of 5 stars, hot and cold crab legs was a 3 out of 5 stars because it didnt taste any different from crab legs at other buffets...lamb 4 out of 5 stars was juicy not dry at all   

- desserts : i give the creme brulee 4/5   very easy to eat not too sweet, red bean and coffee mochi 4/5, chocolate covered strawberries were delicious as well

overall the buffet was good but could've been better

Worth the regular cost although the premium price for Easter brunch was stretching it. Still, it's worth it. The red meat stuff was probably the weakest link (e.g. prime rib). But everything else was amazing. Favorites were the pork belly, pork bun, and sushi. Group of 5 or more seem to have a longer line (tougher to seat together).

I have been here 2 times. 

The first time was amazing. Prime rib, seafood, cooked foods, desserts, etc. 5 star. 

I went this last weekend, and it was not good. The prime rib was very low quality. The prime rib was more along the lines of Hometown Buffet level (not that Hometown is bad, but it costs 1/10 the price, so adjust your standards accordingly). 

The sushi section was very low quality. For $60 dollars you expect their sushi section to be much better. 

Also the line system is very long and annoying, with a number system that is just to get you in line. 

Considering the very high price ($60) and the long wait (1 to 2 hours) it deserves 1 star. 

If this place was $20 with a better line system I would rate this 5 stars.

Went the other day and cannot stop thinking about it! It was so good, fresh, quality and quick service. Any out of town family that visits will definitely be told to go here. Worth the money spent even though some may consider it pricey. 

Desert was delicious even though I don't have a sweet tooth.

I went there several times. But when I have been there last time which was christmas day, it was AWEFUL. I was luckily to get in after 3hours of waiting (even though I got a reservation ticket 500 minutes ago), but I saw how they treat customers who cannot get into the restaurant. 
This is well known for best buffet for LV, but I would not choose this over others because of customer service. I don't want to believe this is buffet of the hotel in the middle of Las Vegas.

Visited in January 2018 - Lunch buffet 

This is a foodie's paradise. It is a quality buffet has everything you want. You can find everything here from Wagyu steak and all you can eat seafood spread like oysters, crab claws and prawns which I truly enjoyed. The dessert bar looks like a work of art. 

This is one buffet I would recommend all to try in Vegas.
