I went to the buffet for dinner on Sunday, October 21st. I arrived at the line at around 4:30 and was seated about an hour later.  I was very excited to try this new buffet after reading all of the excellent reviews. My husband and I were very disappointed, first the cost is $42.99 plus tax with a Total Rewards card so I expected the food to be quality.  The decor is beautiful and selections of food great but the taste not so good. Also a big negative is that you wait in a long line to get in, then you wait in long lines for the seafood and meat stations, by the time you sit down the food is cold.   My husband loves crab legs and always goes to buffets that have them, they were extremely salty and not edible. He did say that the lobster bisque was delicious and had big chunks of lobster, he also liked the salmon and halibut.  The smoked meats looked delicous but were cold and salty, tried the lamb chop, turkey breast and ham. The people at the table next to us complained to the manager about this issue as well.  I tried the some pastas and lasagna which was just ok. The feta cheese and watermelon salad as delicious.  The desserts were excellent, especially the fresh fruit crepe and the banana souffle.  The service was horrible, I couldn't get a refill to save my life. They either need to  increase their level of service at every level or they need to lower the price because it is not worth it.  We are not picky and really wanted to love this buffet but it just was not all that.  We usually eat at the Spice Market Buffet at Planet Hollywood for dinner and Mandalay Bay for breakfast, the assortment might be less but the taste is great.

The title "Best buffet in Vegas"  and "Best buffet in America" are pretty much well deserved.  The quality of food is outstanding.  The service was exceptional.  The range of items was overwhelming.  Some items that you will not see at other buffets include:  oysters, street taco station (tacos made to order), brisket, etc.  It is pricey, so if you decide to check it out, come hungry!

Worst service ever, estevan, took forever to come to our table, we had to look for him everywhere, seriously our empty plates were sitting on our table for 45 minutes, we had to ask someone else to pick them up, we paid for the unlimited alcohol drinks which is $18 per person, and he only showed up once in two hours, so guess what? I only had 2 beers because our server only showed up one time after bringing the first beer. I am so dissapointed, food is good but service is super bad, and when you get a bad service, it is more likely that you never go back to a place. I am a server and I know this is not a fine dining place but honestly, I was expecting much more from this buffet at the Caesars Palace Hotel in Las Vegas.

Heard this was the #1 buffet in Vegas. The main draw of this place are its snow crab legs which were pretty good albeit skinny :P. The last time I was in vegas, The Bellagio had a similar buffet serving the same items for $35-$40 I believe(?) This place was $50.

3.5 stars, but rounded up.

I had high expectations for this buffet.  After reading so many reviews, I was determined to try this buffet, believing it would be the best buffet in Las Vegas.  We came in a party of 10 and the wait wasn't too bad.  So different from how I remember buffet lines to be - waiting in line an hour before it even opens just to get in at a reasonable time.  

The food itself was good for regular standards but to be called the best buffet in Las Vegas - nah.  I still prefer Wicked Spoon.  The lines to get food from each buffet line wasn't well managed as people were just coming in and out of lines, not knowing where the line starts and ends.  The food wasn't bad, don't get me wrong but it was underwhelming based on my expectations.  The meat selection was alright - the one thing that stood out to me was the lamb chops.  The international selection consisted of Italian, Mexican, Chinese dim sum, Japanese noodles, etc.  Those were alright.  I was so excited to try the Japanese noodles...I've never been to a buffet that had that many options for it, but the soup tasted watered down and bland.  The noodles were too soft in my opinion.  Towards the end, half of my group just got a ton of oysters to make their money's worth.  

Would I come back again?  If everyone else wanted to but I would happily choose Wicked Spoon instead.

"I ate like a pig" ( Pumba voice) 
This place was amaaaaazing. Especially the desserts :)

We were excited about visiting this Buffet as it had such great ratings. We've tried the buffets at the Aria, Luxor and Bellagio and they have been better than this. This buffet in comparison was a waste of money.

Thee absolute best buffet in Vegas right now.  Loved this place so much.  My group and I came here on a Saturday around 2:00 PM and the line was long so we opted out to skip the line and went to the express line for an extra $20 or so.  Plus taxes, we ended up spending like $80/person.  Was it worth that much money? I mean, YES of course it was but I will never pay that much again for a buffet (unless I win big at Casino Wars then why not?).  I'll either come early or wait in that damn line. 

Quality is great and they have an oyster/crab bar and macarons! Is this heaven or what?

Was it worth the 45 minute wait and $60 price tag? Ehhhhh. I'm still on the fence.... 

First, the wait can be ridiculous. We tried going at about 2 and there was a 45 minute wait. Most of the wait we spent standing in line. They have these little kiosks where you enter your info, including phone number, so you can walk around for a bit. Bacchanal is at the back of Caesar's Palace though, so you're kinda stuck sticking around the casino. In like 10 minutes, we were notified that it was our turn to stand in line. We waited in line to pay, then waiting in like a holding area before we were seated. When we did get seated, it was in the back where it was a little crowded and dark. The seating closer to the food/entrance looked better than where we were at.

We did get seated in time for weekend brunch, so we had some brunch items like crab eggs Benedict and lobster bisque. In hindsight, I didn't think coming early for the $8 price difference was really worth having the brunch items. There were better options for dinner. At 3, we got some oysters, prime rib, salmon, and escargot. 

Like some of the other reviewers, I thought the king/snow crab was super salty. Even the steamed crab was salty.  I liked the Dungeness crab the most of the crab options. I thought the shrimp and oysters did not taste fresh. 

The siu mai was the only dim sum I would recommend and the sushi/ poke were both kind of terrible. 

They had a crepe station, which was just ok, and the other desserts were ehhh. 

Overall, I think I'd rather spend my money on better quality food next time.

"The Bacchanalia were Roman festivals of Bacchus, the Greco-Roman god of wine, freedom, intoxication and ecstasy."  - Wikipedia.  Has there ever been a more appropriate name for a restaurant in Las Vegas than Bacchanal?  I don't think so.  Because when you go to Bacchanal, it is all about indulging and succumbing to all your carnal desires (for food anyway).  It's not an exaggeration when I say anything you want, you can have.  Let's take a trip through the halls of this food festival.

Seafood: Pre-cracked Alaskan king crab legs.  Shrimp cocktail.  Tartar sauce, cocktail sauce, and even butter for your dispensary.  
Americana: Sliders, crisscut fries, fried chicken and waffles, prime rib, sausages, roast beef, baby back ribs, beef ribs, mashed potatoes. 
Italiano: Pizza, pasta, assemble your own charcuterie plate.  
Asian: Dim sum, all Panda Express type items (elevated), pho, ramen, udon.
Mexican: Nachos, street tacos, chicharrones.
Dessert: Ice cream, crepes, creme brulee, macarons, cookies.

And it goes on and on and on.  There is something for everyone here.  The food is of high quality.  Every dish could stand on its own at a regular restaurant.  I have visited at least half a dozen times, and I always find it an enjoyable experience.  My recent trip had me demolishing nine (yes, 9) plates of food.  The wait time can be excruciating, but it serves a purpose to build up your appetite.  Worth the wait.

Bacchanal will intoxicate your senses and bring your stomach to pure, unadulterated ecstasy.  Enjoy it responsibly my friends.

I've come back here twice since my last review in 2015. Love their boiled crab legs because the crab meat is less salty when boiled. The prime rib is pretty good here. Love the roast duck, stone crab, and dessert bar.  Came here for Mother's Day dinner, and it was $67 per person.  Pretty pricey, but my mother-in-law really enjoyed the variety and got a pink carnation to boot.  My cholesterol must be through the roof from all the crab legs I ate, but so worth it!
Wow! Talk about amazing food and service! Every time someone says buffet, I'm sending them to Bacchanal Buffet.

If you haven't been to a Vegas buffet before, you may be thinking, "ew a buffet?" But Vegas buffets are on a completely different level and the Caesars buffet is at the top. They have so many options and almost everything tastes incredibly fresh and flavorful. The kitchen staff takes pride in their buffet offerings. By far the best things are their king crab legs and fried chicken. Oh and the prime rib and brisket. You can skip the pizza, but really, when there is crab and prime rib to be had, who needs pizza? And their dessert area is massive! With delicious gelato and made-to-order crepes available to you, it's a dessert-lovers dream. They also have the option for unlimited drinks for $15 per person which, in Vegas, is a killer deal! It does not include hard alcohol, though, just wine, beer, champagne or sangria. The total bill for 5 people with unlimited drinks was $389.  So yes spendy, but I've been to quite a few of the buffets in Vegas as I come here for work often and believe me, Caesars and the Wynn buffets are by far the best. Don't waste your time at the others.

This review is for the service, which is so poor that we didn't even get to the food part. 

Oh, boy!  Where should I start? 

So, our 8-month-old pooped and needed a diaper change,  while we were waiting to pay to enter the buffet for brunch.  This is what i experienced:

1) NO CHANGING STATION in the restroom at this place.  Had to improvise on the side of the sink

2) NO COLD RUNNING WATER to rinse off stained clothing in the restroom

3) NO HELP from their staff whatsoever, when asked to help locate husband inside the buffet (happened not to have his cell on him), just so that I could go back and clean up the mess inside the restroom

Me, hungry and with a screaming wiggling baby and poop stained clothing in hand, at the pay station: 

"Did you see a [insert description of husband] guy enter the buffet?"

"No idea... maybe he's in the men's room?  Why don't you wait?"

Few minutes later, baby still screaming, my blood sugar still low,  and no trace of husband, I walked up to the hostess at the buffet entrance, 

"Hi, can i go in to to find my husband, or can you call him over speaker or something and have him meet me here?  Here is his name..."

Hostess, "are you sure he's inside?"

Me, spotted hubby at a table from the entrance, out of desparation, I called out his name loud. 

Hostess let out a loud "GEEZ!", RIGHT IN MY FACE, as if I was a lunatic.  

Maybe I was, at that moment, given the fact that i had to get up twice the night before to feed a jet lagged baby, my Chanel had baby poop, and my head was ringing with ongoing baby screaming and low blood sugar.  All I knew was NONE OF THEIR DOZEN PLUS STAFF STANDING AT THE BUFFET ENTRANCE OFFERED TO HELP, OR EVEN JUST LEND ME A HAND.

Meanwhile, my husband got some unpleasant experience of his own, while waiting for me inside.  They threatened to call security on him, just because he dared to insist upon a hot chocolate made with milk, instead of water.

Naturally, we decided not to dine here anymore, and asked for a refund. 

On our way out, we told their manager that we are going to leave them an unfavorable review for the disappointing experience.  Their response?  

"... but this is a full refund."  

They were confused as to why we were still not happy after receiving a full refund.  Just shows how clueless the staff at this place is. 

I would suggest any family with small kids to STAY AWAY from this UNFRIENDLY place.
Great buffet we went for brunch. Great selection but pricey.  Not a bad wait for brunch, dinner usually about 40-45 min. One of top 3 buffets in vegas

This place was a food heaven. I can't remember not liking anything! With one exception.. The line. Be prepared to wait. Or call ahead and check out what the wait time is. The price is honestly worth it. For all the delicious gourmet food you're getting and unlimited amounts??? It's a great place to go for an unforgettable meal. The highlights were: the sliders, the lamb chops and in the beginning there was some kind of beef stir fry with tofu?? And believe it or not, even the tofu was delicious! And for dessert, the lemon sorbet was great, the crem brûlée was amazing and my favorite was the chocolate covered strawberry. I will be talking about that strawberry forever! Check this place out if you're ready for a great meal :)
Really good buffet.  Lots of made from scratch options.  A little expensive but it's reasonable for the options. Service was very good. My mimosa glass was never empty!

My favorite buffet ever!!! huge selection of great food from different cuisines, it i not just about the quantity, the food also tasted so so delicious. The presentation of desserts was beyond beautiful and the taste was so good. I Loved my whole experience at Bacchanal Buffet!!!
I would give it 5 stars because it was almost perfection.  Quality ingredients and excellent service.  The food was great.  I'll come again

Large buffet featuring an assortment of foods: American, Italian, Asian, Mexican, seafood, and so many dessert options. 3.5 stars

Food: 3.5, atmosphere: 4, service: 4
Cost to worth it rating: 3 ($35 for weekday lunch)
Return worthiness: maybe

Highlights:
- Asian area: the best station for me. Usually you get impostors, but the cha sui baos were legit: soft buns and sweet insides without fat. Also enjoyed the large cha sui pieces and duck.
- Italian: the spinach ravioli in vodka sauce and meatball were really good. I liked the single little dishes they put out for taste portions 
- Deep fried broccoli cheese casserole: surprising favorite 
- American plating: loved the little buckets for the tater tots and waffle fries and the mini fry basket with a piece of fried chicken and sweet potato fries
- Brisket: nice rub on the outside and liked the option of BBQ sauces
- Red velvet whoopie pie: soft and on point flavors for a authentic rendition 
- Dessert variety: from cupcakes and cookies to bread pudding to unique gelato flavors to made to order crepes to sugar free desserts and  more, there was tons to choose from

Midlights:
- Good amount of empty spots: those items looked good but guess they were so popular they ran out 


Lowlights:
- Shrimp: cold one tasted a bit fishy and the hot one with heads were overlooked 
- Spicy fried fish: was excited for this dish but wasn't that great--probably because it was sitting out
- Meat inconsistency: some was dry

Some items were great but as with most buffets others were mediocre. If you're a dessert person you might like it. I'd consider coming back, but won't be in a rush and wouldn't stand in a long line for it.

Wow!  This was my first trip to Vegas and my first meal in Vegas.  I had never eaten at a $50 buffet before and at first thought, "$50 FOR A BUFFET"!?  Once we were seated, I took some time to walk around the different stations before choosing my meal.  I couldn't believe the selection and everything looked so delicious.  I had a little taste of a lot of foods.  My favorite were the crab legs and shrimp.  I also tried meats from the carving station, sushi, a potato dish, tacos, spring rolls, fresh juices, and several desserts and gelato.  I'm sure I had more, but I just can't remember it all.  There are so many places to eat in Vegas, and hitting this place when we first got here was probably the best thing to do.  After a few days in Vegas and eating out everyday, I don't think I would have wanted to eat so much anymore.  I will definitely be back on my next trip to Vegas to have my first meal.

Im honestly super pissed. So my husband and I go yesterday for dinner. We paid $125.00 for the botu of us. He's a low raking Marine in the military so we're not made of money, but I thought we'd try the proclaimed "best" buffet in Vegas. We sat down, got our drinks and never got them refilled again, we were seated RIGHT INFRONT of the room where all the bussers and drink waitresses go in and out of. Second, they had a pretty decent selection of food which was cool. But everything was a hit or miss. More than half of what we ate was cold, and their mashed potatoes had this old rancid smell and taste. My husband is not a picky eater at all, considering he eats disgusting MRE's. And he was like thid food isn't good, and wasnt impressed. I think he ate a plate and a half of food, and like 2 desserts and didn't like the rest. Im honestly extremely disappointed because we just wasted 125$ that we couldve spent somewhere else like the Wicked Spoon or the Wynn. Please dont make my mistake, because I practically cried of how much of a waste going there was. This place is NOT #1, dont not be fooled like I was.

As far as buffets go, this one was good. That's really not my issue with Caesar's Palace Bacchanal Buffet. They had hot and cold crab legs, they had nice brisket, prime rib, and turkey. They had a variety of stir fry Asian food as well as a modest sushi bar. They had a variety of deserts. Basically, it was your standard buffet you would find just about anywhere you go. 

So what sets the Bacchanal Buffet apart from the rest? 

THE PRICE. 

Really. That's it. The price. Over $50 for what I typically get at a $20 buffet anywhere else in the country, and no, this isn't just "Well, that's Vegas" because there were plenty of other establishments that had $25 buffets, and some even cheaper that had just as good a quality of a spread. 

If I had paid $25 or even $30 for this buffet, this would be a 4 or 5 star review. Having paid nearly $60 for what was essentially a $20 buffet had me deeply disappointed. Upon leaving when I explained to the hostess that I was unhappy with the price vs what was offered, she merely shrugged her shoulders. It will be a cold day in Hades before I visit Caesar's Palace again. I don't like being ripped off.

Great selection of food! Sushi wasn't great at all tho.. I've had better sushi at different buffets. One thing that amazed me was the quality of the Pho! It was delicious!

My only complaint is the lay out of the main eating area..it is so confusing. The last thing I want to do when carrying plates of delicious food is walking through weirdly placed tables.

The food was ok, lots of variety, yummy dessert, and fine service. Problem for me was, nothing stood out. Going back for my 4th plate (yeah, I know but not I never ate everything on each plate), there wasn't a single dish that I wanted more of. I actually just moved on to dessert, which I normally can't physically do at Vegas buffets. Below average to average for a Vegas buffet, which I'd say is still much, much better than any buffet outside of LV.

The Las Vegas strip has always been like a second home to me and the buffets are always something to look forward to when coming here. I've tried many buffets over the years while on the strip but the buffet at Caesars is the one that just never seems to disappoint! In fact their buffet has gotten better over the years, providing such fresh and good quality food that tastes more like fine dining than buffet style. There's never an unpleasant ache in my stomach leaving this buffet just a happy tight belly! I would definitely recommend this buffet (especially for dinner) to anyone who's looking for a great buffet where you can get your money's worth in quantity and quality. Great job Caesars !!!

So many things to choose from. I like the layout of the buffet and the seating area. Feels much nicer than most buffets. Feels like you're sitting in an actual restaurant. The meats section had a great variety of meats to choose from. Of all the vegas buffets i've been too, this is for the sure the best one. The deserts area has a ton of great variety as well. 

The only thing that sucks is the wait. Which is understandable, but you get a spot in line, and then have to come back at the said time. Then you have to check in with the lady in the front, to then stand in another line that takes another 20-30 minutes. Feels like they could just short cut that but is what it is.

Great food for a buffet and great service! Almost everything is served a la carte!  Fresh squeezed juices in the am only so get here before 11am. The selection offered is overwhelming. I recommend scoping out the entire buffet before making any food selections.

The absolute pinnacle of Vegas Buffet's. Located in Ceasers Palace by the Pools. This buffet has it all. Great service and great food. The waits can be insane, up to 3 hours. Some come early if its a Saturday and grab your ticket for the line around 3-4 to have a normal dinner time.

cost was about $53 a person. Its absolutely worth it. The menu is always changing, but the food is always consistent.

The buffet itself is decorated magnificently and it puts any Vegas buffet to shame. I believe it really amplifies the experience. I stopped going anywhere else.

Make your own taco's, Fresh to slice BBQ, Amazing Shrimp cocktail, Asian foods, Italian treats. Not to mention an awesome selection of desserts. Your stomach will hate you at the end of the night.

Its a must try if you love buffets. Eat on!

Skipped day party w/ Kaskade headlining to eat here!!! That says a lot  and I have never been so happier with my decision making. So worth every penny! Food is phenomonal!! 

There was a huuuuge line  when we got there around 2:30ish... At that time we thought itt'd be bestt just to pay the $15 to skip the line because if we waited it would have prob turned into dinner hours and the price would have went up anyways. So worth it though. 

As close as it gets to heaven! If I was a Vegas buffet, I'd totally be jealous of Bacchanal every which way.

If I can give 0 star,  i would. Last year was terrible and this year is worst. We went on Aug 4 for dinner, party of 7. Prime rib was like rubber, lamb also like rubber. Green tea creme brulee was terrible and  no other dessert worth eating. Expensive as heck, over $50. I don't even know why i even try again. Spend your money at Bellagio Buffet. Cheaper and prime rib is very tender. I am a platinum member of Total Rewards. Anyway, not ever again I guess. I hope I remember next time.

Bacchanal Buffet is not a bad buffet. However, it is expensive. Good, but expensive. I have no problem paying for the good buffets in Las Vegas. But I found out both of the foods qualities and the services is not worth the price of admission. They are way over priced based on the foods qualities they are offer.
Best Buffet in Vegas.  Price is worth the selection.  Love the king crab and the BBQ pit.

I was there for my Dads bday brunch. Service and food was amazing.. well organized and the price was just right.  We had 15 people table and no one waited for a refill on they're drinks. Every one was happy

I hit the brunch buffet on a Wednesday at 8:00 A.M, nobody in line. The only buffet I go to in Vegas. Great variety, the sliced bacon is a must get. $35.95 for brunch, it's worth the price, I wasn't hungry until dinner.

This is not what the advertisements would make you think. I thought this buffet was going to be absolutely fantastic. There was a station for each food culture: seafood, Italian, Chinese, breakfast, Mexican and dessert. It was pretty good but nothing beyond that. It has a wide variety selection, but none of the food is 'impressive', some of the food was even dying at the buffet. It was similar to going to a 3 star restaurant to receive each dish. The food lacked quality in each item presented. Even though the mimosas are included this Buffett is Not worth the money. I feel that the majority of the budget went towards can advertisements as opposed to actual food quality. We thoroughly enjoyed the Aria buffet and rated that buffet 5 stars which was far better than this one.

We come to Vegas often, at least 4-5 times a year, and have had our eyes on this buffet for the last 2 months when we were booking our most recent trip. We read many of the reviews and watched a bunch on YouTube, so we were pretty excited about trying it out, even with the $60 price tag. So you can imagine how disappointing it is to leave this place a solid 3 star rating. The prices are ridiculously high for the quality of what you're getting. Everything LOOKS absolutely delicious. Taste wise, that's an issue. We were in line on a Sunday at around 2:15 and made it up to the cashier at 10 minutes to 3:00 - which saved us about $15 per person because they were still charging the breakfast/brunch pricing and not the dinner pricing yet, so that was a plus! We paid $108 with tax for the two of us, the Mister and me. Even after you pay, you still wait about a good 20 -30 minutes to get seated, so be prepared for a long wait. I'm on the fence about the staff. They seem friendly but stand offish, if that makes sense. Almost like they're being forced to be nice and is shows. Our waitress was a bit scattered, but wasn't rude. It did take her 3 trips to get the shell crackers that we requested for the crab claws and drinks sat awhile before being refilled.

TIP: There's NO lobster! They have a lobster display in front, so you think there's lobster, but you're sadly disappointed, especially after paying so much for the meal!

Here's a run down of the food we tried:
Crab Legs: Good, but I couldn't find the hot ones anywhere, so we could only eat the already halved cold ones. 
Cold Shrimp: DELCIOUS! This was the favorite of mine at this buffet. They were huge, clean, clean tasting, and fresh! No complaints about the cold shrimp at all!
Oysters, Mussels and Clams: These I stay clear from, especially at buffets, but the Mister had some of each. He enjoyed them a lot! Didn't get sick, so they were all pretty fresh. He even got seconds on each.
Prime Rib: Juicy and tender; not too much flavor, but was a decent chunk of meat.
Crawfish: Soaked in cajun seasonings and pretty good, but a little overcooked. 
Crab Claws: Huge and full of meat. Fresh tasting and pretty good!
Ceviche Verde: Nice flavor, but very small portions.
Meatballs: Decent flavor but they were not warm! Even under a heat lamp, they were almost cold.
Chopped Asparagus and Carrot Mix: The asparagus was very good, the carrot was not cooked long enough so it was very hard. Wish there were more asparagus than carrot.
Beef and Broccoli: Meh... very, very salty, tasted like it was soaked in soy sauce, not oyster sauce, and was not very warm.
Teriyaki Chicken: Tender and nice flavor, but again, not warm. 
Sushi: All of the rice was very dried out.
Chile Verde: Amazingly good! Tender and a great flavor!
Mini Burger: RAW!! I took one bite, tasted it, looked at the meat inside and it was RAW. Not pink, flat out raw! Spit it out and threw the rest away.
Blue Cheese and Bacon Wedge Salad: Was a decent flavor, but the dressing was very thin and watery.
Cheese: Good selection, terrible smelling, as good cheese should be, and very good tasting.
Pot Roast w/Mashed Potatoes and a Carrot Garnish: Very good meat and potatoes, the carrot was, again, not cooked and very hard to eat. The only problem with this dish was that it was SUCH a SMALL portion! It was a two bite serving. Would have had to pile on 4 of these mini trays on top of my plate to get a decent helping of this, but that would have looked terrible and it wouldn't have fit anyway!
Cupcakes: Every single one, with the exception of the carrot cake one, was dried out, like it was made 2 days ago. All were only half filled and were hard to get out of the odd holders they were in.
Orange Cheesecake Pop: This was okay.
Cheesecake with Fruit Topping: Decent piece of cheesecake and the fruit was fresh and really good. This was my favorite dessert.

Going through the photos others have provided, there were many items I see that were not available when we went. The seafood available was very limited, and most of the other food wasn't fresh or hot. The tacos looked amazing, but by the time I saw them on another person's plate, I was full of mediocre food so didn't get a chance to try them out. Overall, we will not be returning to this buffet. It was a huge disappointment. There are too many other buffets that are on par or even better than this one for far less pricing. The Orleans seafood night is about $23 per person and is as good as this one! Perhaps we came on an "off" day... but for the prices, there shouldn't be any "off" days!

But the line is so long!!! The line is RIDICULOUSLY WORTH THE WAIT! I mean, wait, $50 per person? Yes, but it's so very worth that price. The crab legs are endless, the selection of food is endless. Variety EVERYWHERE! If you're a picky eater - you have found the perfect place because literally there are a million options to choose from! Now the desserts....  the DESSERTS! Oh my lawd have mercy! So many-so good! I mean what more could you WANT?!

We had the groupon for breakfast, so we went.  Not a bad thing to say about this buffet, especially with unlimited mimosa's!!  I do wish they had an omelette station, or if they did I missed it.  
Its an expansive buffet with tons of options.  My first plate was like I was at a family BBQ.  I had mac and cheese, baked beans, and chicken mango habanero sausage!!  Not really breakfast, but who says you cant have BBQ for bfast, anyway!!
I eventually had eggs, potatoes, bacon, ya know, the normal bfast options.  Then followed by a crepe made to order with nutella from the pastry section.  Lot's of sweets at this particular section, more than I cared to try.  
They've a variety of fresh juices, some of which I've no idea what they were, but they were good.  There's a dim sum section, cheese section, fruits, breads, meats, seafood, just a whole lot of everything.  
Quality was above average, and I would def eat here again.  But drink less of the mimosa's the next time.......

This place is overrated for $50.99 pp. Sure it's a newly renovated buffet but they don't offer alot of food options and the food wasn't fresh. They have tacos and many choices for Chinese food- char siu pork, bao and dumplings. Then there's a section for chilli and mash potatoes, onion rings abc fried chicken. The warm crab legs were given only if you request it by a helper over the counter so it's all you can eat but not really. There wasn't much I wanted after the first run. The desserts could not compare to Studio B at M buffet.  Not interested in going back.

Definitely not worth an 1 1/2 wait, they rip you off with the express pass to bypass the big line and still make you wait a little while.  Food is ok for buffet food and definitely smaller than other buffets.  I would go to Wynn if you really want a great buffet!  They have an express pass there too!  I think it was only $15.

Pricey, but in terms of food quality, this buffet is great compared to the others.  When we went this 4th of July weekend, food didn't sit long under heat lamps like they do at some other buffets.  Even comfort food items, like mashed potatoes/macaroni and cheese I could tell were prepared with better ingredients.  

Crab legs were pre-cut in half.  I normally don't enjoy crab at buffets, but at Bacchanal it was actually yummy.

Selection is very plentiful and the desserts were great!  The gelato flavors were yummy too!  I recommend going during off peak hours so that waiting in line doesn't take away from the experience.  By the time we were finished eating and walked out of the buffet, the line was insane!

I was referred this buffet by  a dear friend. I am not a big eater but  
love great food.  This buffet was so good I liturally went back twice just to take friends. It was just as perfect as the first time the day before. 
I highly recommend this if you are a foody. 

Terry Rogers

The price that people pay for dinner at a buffet is not worth it for me.   But for brunch, OK, I'm game.   Went here for brunch, I love their wide selection.   Not offering what's in your typical buffet, like many items had lobster in it!   SCORE!!!   They have bottomless mimosas, I'm pretty sure you'll end up with a hangover because it's probably cheap champagne.

But like most buffets, many foods look appetizing but it's not mind blowing.   I did enjoy their meats, soups, and deserts selections.   Woohoo, gelato in the house!   When it's hot outside, you can take a cone of gelato and bring it out.   

I must say that out of all buffets, this is one that I enjoyed most because my friends and I were able to select different things we've never had before and share because in the end, it was something that didn't taste as good as it reads or looks and we don't want to waste food.   

They did have a lot of things that I did enjoy trying though.   This is a must try buffet for everyone who comes to Vegas.

Ok, so we were really looking forward to this buffet, there was 10 of us.  Since we had more than 8 people, we were forced to pay an 18% gratuity up front, and since this buffet is $55 for each person, that meant a $10 per person tip up front.  Keep in mind, this is a buffet, and a good one, but all the server needed to do was to fill our drinks and clear the table...not a server in sight!  We asked for a manager and suddenly the server is now free enough to help us.  
Look, I don't mind paying an up front gratuity, but I better get service in accordance to that mandatory tip!  This was NOT the case until I complained.  
My overall recommendation, save your money and go to a cheaper buffet where they appreciate your business.

Everytime I am in Vegas, I always end up eating at the Bacchanal Buffet. The wide variety is perfect when you go with a group... especially when everyone really can't decide on what to eat. It is about $60 - $70 per person. But with the bottomless alcohol beverage menu, it goes almost up to $90 - $100 per person including a tip.

The bottomless alcohol beverage menu includes beer to mimosas and champagne! They have a wide selection of foods from beef, pork, seafood, sushi and all the way to dessert (Mexican to Korean, to Japanese). 

The king crabs and the oysters were my personal favorite!

The main reason I did not give a five star rating is because the wait can be quite long. You first check in on a kiosk like machine, put in your number and you get a ticket. The ticket will ask you to come back in about 15 minutes to all the way up to an hour and a half. You can go and play some poker or black jack and time will past by! 

HOWEVER, the listed time on the ticket does not mean that you walk in and start feasting. It means that you get to stand in line and wait. The wait can be estimated to be about 15 minutes or so. 

I noticed that you get seated faster with a larger group - perhaps 4+ people.

I would visit again happily!

My hubby and I both agreed this was our favorite buffet on the strip! 

I made a reservation on Opentable for the "VIP" experience. It costs $98 per person which allows you to bypass the lines, unlimited drinks, and a seafood tower with oysters, snails, shrimp, snow crab legs, dunguness crab legs, and a lobster. We went during "brunch" at 1:30 PM where the seafood options were limited and they were still serving breakfast items. All the seafood items on our seafood tower could be found on the buffet besides the lobster. It was so disappointing that the lobster tasted frozen. Fortunately the rest of the seafood was indeed fresh. Honestly I could have done without the drinks and seafood tower but it was nice to pass 30 people in line though! 

Other than that the regular buffet items were plenty and delicious. 

We liked:
Seafood section (everything was fresh)
Prime rib (very tender!)
Truffle and mushroom pizza
Noodle soup station that includes pho, udon, ramen, and laksa. 
Made to order tacos
Bone marrow
Dim sum items
Dessert

The pastas from the Italian section were not very appetizing. Some noodles were undercooked or just tasted like it had been sitting for too long. Same thing with some of the asian items as well. 

I heard waiting can be brutal so best to come during off peak hours! We will be back next time we're in Vegas!

I want to start by saying you can eat anywhere in Vegas...lots of options...lots ...lots of options...but if you want style, class, amazing food and great customer service like Lupe...who spent so much time making sure we were happy with our food and drinks than this is your place. Buffet is second best in Vegas (have to leave room for improvement)....but again as for Lupe she went above and beyond...Erick the Cook also above and beyond....keep up the great work folks...

This was fantastic.  There was a 40 minute wait to get in at 2pm on a weekday; the timing worked out well since we still paid the lunch price $32.99/person (before prices increase at 3pm) but could then enjoy some of the dinner entrees as well.  All of the food was cooked and seasoned well.  Service varies depending on the server, but is typically standard Vegas-fare--they'll bring you a drink at the beginning, clear off plates in 5-10 minutes, and otherwise not refill or check on you unless you track them down.  Highlights of the various areas for me included:

-Asian: roast duck (tender meat and delicious!), spicy fish (breaded & fried fish fillet), soup dumplings
-Grill: lamb chops were well seasoned and tender; sliders used what tasted to be freshly ground beef; rib eye was a little dry
-Seafood: I didn't get any, but there sure was a long line for the oysters and crab legs
-Dessert: ice cream mochis (limit 2 per trip?!?), freshly made crepes (though the fruit had an overly sweet syrup)

The slight premium over some other buffets was well worth it to me, and I greatly preferred this over the Wynn buffet that I went to a few years ago, which had fancy ingredients, but hardly anything that actually tasted good.

Okay, you're going to try it once, like so many other things in life.

I was there on the evening of 1 January, which means I expected the crowds to have cleared out. My error. So here is the process: you go to the buffet area, and check in electronically on a machine that is in front of the TSA-like queue. You get a print out telling how long you're going to wait. Ours told us 70 minutes, but that's the wait to join the queue, not to go in. They have your phone number at that point, so go wander around or find a place to hang. Tip #1) The Cigar Lounge is quiet and excellent, with big screen TVs and nice bartenders. Then, you 'll come back to the queue and join it at your appointed time. Get ready to wait some more. It probably took us another hour to get to the pay station, pay for our meals, and then join yet another line (this one blessedly shorter) for a hostess to seat us.

When it comes time to be seated, follow your hostess. Warning: the place is huge. Bring flares so you can find your companion. Don't expect elegance. The two-tops have tables that are quite big, probably to accommodate the large number of plates that are going to show up. Tip #2) think carefully about how much you plan to drink Individual glasses of wine are $9, but there's an all-u-can-drink deal that is in the low $20s. Consider it. 

Then, go scope things out. There's a lot of different choices, to say the least. Here are some things that my dining companion and I decided were amongst the best of the offerings.

Tip #3) Try the following
* Peking duck
* Beef ribs
* bone marrow
* shrimp (her say-so)
* baby carrots
* shrimp and grits (her say-so)
* ribeye
* crepes for dessert (chocolate is good)

It's worth doing once, but I don't know that I'd come back.

This is not your ordinary buffet. Everything is so delicious. And the best part is that they switch up the food even in the two hours I was there. It went from lobster bisque to crab cakes. I went for brunch and also had the bottomless mimosa. Only thing is you gotta keep bugging for a refill. It's definitely money well spent. Next time I will try dinner.

I really wanted to like the Bacchanal Buffet and was excited to eat there especially since my wife and I were staying at Caesar's we were most excited about the seafood choices here.....you know where this is going unfortunately I got very sick from something at the buffet causing me to throw up the rest of the night 8ish times so basically it was a waste of $120 probably bad on me for eating seafood at a buffet but I really expected better from a high class place such as Caesar's palace oh well live and learn... despite that I enjoyed my stay at Caesar's and loved the food the next night at RAO's I mean really it's silly to go the buffet route with so many world class restaurants in Vegas off buffets for ever

Loved the fact that you didn't have to stand in line the whole time to get into the buffet. There's a machine that you can reserve a table and they will text you when to come back to the line. The food selection was amazing there was everything from Mexican, Asian, American, and seafood. The dessert selection was broad too with gelato, flans, cookies etc. This buffet is on the pricey end but you get what you pay for.

So happy we picked this buffet!  Wicked Spoon has always been our favorite but we decided to give this a try. Solid 5. Enormous selection  and the food is really prepared well. Favorites included clams, shrimp and grits, brisket, scrambled eggs, and several desserts - exotic fruit dessert, hazelnut cake, egg custard, and orange beer ice cream, plus fresh squeezed juices.  Very good for brunch price.  Good service too

Best buffet in Vegas by far...

Totally worth the wait. Plus you can just sign in and receive a ticket to when you're up to pay. So you can shop or gamble in the mean time.

Food selection is the best. Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Mexican, American, seafood and a big choice for desserts! 

Personally I like the dumplings or duck rom the Chinese area. Sushi quality is alright. Pizza is always good! The tacos are amazing and made fresh. A huge selection of juices next to it as well.

Lots of selections as far as meat and definitely more seafood choices than other buffets.

Worth it. Best buffet by far. Have a TR card and save a buck I believe.

Have a platinum or higher TR card and you can cut the 2ish hour wait and sit down immediately.

Honestly it's an okay buffet wanted despite the hype of it all. The reason being is that the snow crabs were super salty and if you wanted them steamed you would have to wait in line and they would still be partially frozen. The lamb chop had more fat than meat, the nachos were salty as well, and also the wait was to be expected. The deserts were pretty good tho. I would go to wicked spoon

Meh. I suppose the food is good. It's not the best buffet that you'll have. It's not the worst. I would put it on the list of high-end buffets, but if you're gonna spend the kind of money that you would spend going to the Bacchanal Buffet, you should probably just skip it and go to the Wynn buffet.

This is the best buffet in the U.S. Great food. Great service. I don't know what is up with it being four star. The meats are exceptionally good and the pizza is great. Same with the fried rice. Highly recommend this buffet.

Why wouldn't you want to stop by a buffet while in Vegas?! 

The check-in process is very efficient. Sign your name in on the computer, walk around and they text you saying your table is ready! Super easy. The wait time is typically quicker than what they initially tell you when you sign-in. Double yay. 

You'll find something that will satisfy whatever craving you have. I dove right into the crab legs (which they'll steam for you, just ask) and the dessert bar...because, why not? I love how some dishes are served in there own cute little plates or containers. I'm a sucker for cute presentation...

Around $55-$60/person...I don't remember...oy.

Me and my boyfriends favorite buffet in Vegas. Despite how long the line can be and how pricey it may be, its worth every minute and penny. We always come here for different occasions and it never disappoints us :)

My husband and I were very excited to be back in Vegas and get back to Bacchanal. Well, things sure have changed since 2013! We were VERY disappointed!! The seafood was sub par. Stone crabs from Mexico instead of the wonderful Florida kind. Tiny snow crab legs, tiny oysters filled with bits of shell. Little clams with gritty sand in them. The whole roasted pig sat there and was dry. Much of the food just sat there under the lamps. The charcuterie was dried out and inedible. The Asian food was just sitting there luke warm at best. The blue crab stir fry was cold and dry. The sushi was warm... (a very bad thing) and it's rice cold and hard.  The sushi rolls...not even a decent tuna or salmon roll...just that mixed fake crab salad roll. The poke also warm raw fish. Surprising people aren't getting food poisoning. The made to order soups... Singapore laksa was soooo greasy and smelled of fish in the wrong way. The ramen broth was ok but the noodles not cooked enough. The entire mexican food area just sat there with knowone taking any of it. They must see how certain areas are not moving; why on earth do they keep serving it!! Strange desserts. I'm sorry but this experience was liken to the disgusting Golden Corral buffet but with a huge price tag. They have some nerve charging what they do. Much of it left on everyones plate going into the garbage. There's nothing lux about this place! Frankly, I want my money back. Do yourself a favor and keep your money in your pocket. I'm serious. I travel all over the world and have tried many a cuisine... this is bottom of the barrel at best.

This place is huge...long line yes its Friday, but geez its buffet, really?! Ive never had to wait so long for a buffet, I am from the fourth largest city in the United States and so I am very familiar with big crowds.

15.00 extra if you wanted to be bumped up to the front of te line, but then you have to still wait to be seated. So I kept my 15.00 in my pocket and just willed my patience to hold on a little longer.

Once you pay your buffet fee of 49.00 (normally 51.00 + tax) then the "paid" people wait in another line.

After an hour and a half we were finally seated.

Our waitress was really slow getting to us once seated, we were so hungry we decided she could get our drinks later one we returned to our table.

The Buffet....I was not blown away but there are a few things there as dinner and dessert that were a stand out or different for sure.

Every magazine describes this buffet as a top notch experience on Vegas. We paid with my husband $120 and were expecting that experience would be unbeatable. Unfortunately we were disappointed because our expectations for that price were much higher. It's just ok, nothing special, the desserts are much better at Wynn and the seafood station wasn't great. I regretted for paying $120 for two and getting such a mediocre experience.

Anyone who rates this place with one or two stars is just way too snobby. Great presentation. Didn't have any problems with waiting. You're in Vegas. What do you expect!?

It's about 40 per person during midday lunch but its worth it. Everything is fresh and delicious. I got bite size samples of almost everything there and enjoyed everything. 
Service is top notch as well. All the cooks are very nice and gladly answer any questions you have as far as the food goes. 

An overall brilliant experience.
I have tried several buffets in Las Vegas. This one is my new favorite. Everything on the buffet was flavorful and tasted of high quality. I will definitely go back when im back in Vegas.

Maybe my expectations were overly high after two excellent trips to the Wicked Spoon, but I was thoroughly unimpressed. I tried nearly every dish during the dinner buffet. Everything was cold to Luke warm. The only dishes that were hot and tasted fresh were a bowl of soup, the meat from the carving station, and the pizza. 

The fried chicken was awful, a bucket of extra crispy from KFC is far superior. The French fries were stale. The corn and Mac n cheese were both cold and had no flavor. All of the food from the Asian stations were cold. Due to the fact that there was a line for the seafood, I didn't try it. I was already sick of waiting after an hour in line just to get in the buffet. 

I notified a manager about the cold food, and he did refund a meal for me. The reason provided to me was that the chef "forgot to defrost the meatballs." I was not provided an explanation for the rest of the cold food. The manager was apologetic, which was appreciated. However I would have been more appreciative of  a personal apology from the head chef.

The only saving grace, which is what earned both stars, was the dessert selection. I loved the unique options and crepe station. If you're deciding between Bacchanal or Wicked Spoon, I would stick with Wicked Spoon. I have eaten at $15 buffets that tasted much better than this $55 ripoff.

Food was good, some very good. The wait on Christmas morning before 10 am was only 20 mins.; however, I have a special needs child who doesn't chew food well and wasn't going to eat much anyway.  I kindly asked if they could charge a child's price instead.  The cashier went and asked her manager and was told NO.  I had to pay the full $50 plus for him to eat about $5 worth of food...merry Christmas from Caesar Scrooge.  He had some scrambled eggs and biscuits and gravy and about three ounces of OJ.  Thanks.  Try Bellagio buffet for those with special needs kids.  They treated him much better and if you wanted to be seated sooner, ask to speak with the manager, he'll get you in sooner.

Anyway, the good was the dim sum, the black chicken soup with ginsing, brisket, fried chicken and waffles, the Kobe sliders (great!), skirt steak with egg, sweet potato fries, sushi and spicy chorizo con papas.

The OK, was the shrimp cocktail and crab legs .  Had better at Bellagio and better sushi.

The really good was the watermelon mint sorbet and the cucumber juice if available.

Quality was very good, but the customer service with my son was a deal breaker.  I had called Caesars three times and could not get someone from the buffet or a manager to speak to earlier to ask questions before we went.  We could not even get a voice mail.   Got to speak with operators who did not give me any viable information.  Similar thing happened at Wynn a couple of years ago...will never go back to gamble or stay or eat ever again.  Sometimes an act of kindness on a day like today would have gone a long way.

To me this place is like heaven on earth! Amazing variety. My favorites are the pork belly with carrot purée, the seafood, gelato, creme brûlée...everything I had was really good quality. Our waitress was sweet...perfect evening!

This place IS DELICIOUS! This has to be my favorite buffet! Sucks that it's in Vegas but man is this place good. Definitely worth the wait & cost. 

Get seated.
Get acquainted.
Bring a appetite. 

I literally made sure I ate from each area. Tacos, sushi, Italian you name it! 

I was so hungry and impressed I forgot to take pictures of any of my plates smh. Next time for sure. 

I'll be back in a few weeks, 3/24 to be exact! Haha

My friends and I decided to try Bacchanal Buffet for brunch on a Saturday and came during peak lunch/brunch time. We almost gave up and turned around when we saw the super long lines and crowds of people. Luckily, the line for large parties was empty and we had a group of 7, so we were able to get a table within minutes.

This was easily my best buffet experience ever. Brunch was ~$50/person and we definitely ate more than $50 worth of food. There were so many different types of foods to choose from, I'm almost positive there were sections of the buffet I never even got to. I had to go for the crab legs and lobster eggs benedict first, and then I moved on to dim sum, more seafood, soups, cheeses, and traditional brunch items. Some seafood items tasted more fresh than others, but nothing tasted bad. 

If I'm ever in Vegas again, I am definitely coming back to Bacchanal Buffet.

We looked at the great reviews on this restaurant and took our business partners here for dinner. What an embarrassment it was. The food was beyond disappointment, and so was the service. Would definitely go on the list of worst Vegas buffets that we've been to.

This places KIOSK is not serving its purpose. I heard from the review here that it now has KIOSK so I had higher hopes that we don't have to wait in line as there are thousands of other things I can do at VEGAS than standing in a stupid line.

What they did to us is that we got a ticket around 2:30 pm. Ticket saids our turn was 8:30 pm. We thought its long wait but that's ok we'd come back for it for amazing meal.

Only to find out that when we come back on 8:20 WE GET TO WAIT IN ANOTHER LINE THAT GOES ON FOR ANOTHER 3 HOURS. What exactly is the point of the KIOSK if it doesn't serve its purpose?

Yup... This is the best buffet in Vegas! They cater to Asian ppl so there's tons of good options! It's super busy so get there in between meals like around 2-3pm lol you get the best of both worlds that way! They don't even rush you out when you're sitting there about to explode and holding your bellies! 

I will definitely come back here again next trip!

Mediocre to say the least. Always a line here and I thought this buffet would be one of the best however it was pretty dissapointing. There was only one staff working in carvery section and everyone was in line just for a piece of meat. Everything else was mere ehhhh its okay.

Not a fan of buffets and I was told this was one of best in vegas but unfortunately it wasnt.

This is my 3rd time in Vegas. The other two time I really want to try out this place. Finally this time I have a chance to try out. We get her around 7:30pm on Friday, wait around 30-45min to get a table. This place has many varieties of food. Many choice and selection, however some of the food is really good and some taste like"nah" my favorite is chowder, and cold snow crab. Steam snow crab is good but when I eat it, is very salty that why I didn't like it. I try pretty much everything. I saw the picture that they have Dungeness crab, however when I was there is Just have Pincers (Not fresh produce), not whole crabs .  Also, this place is expensive. Two people including tax and tip around $150. I don't eat a lot but I want to experience new stuff. At least now I can said that I actually try. For me to come back here again, probably not. Because I never fan eating buffet. ever single time I eat buffet I always want to try little bit of every thing.  And I have too much stuff mixing together In my tummy and get me sick. But if you never come here before. You should come and adventure your new experience!!

Truly Bacchanalian!! This buffet is really the best of the best. We got the 24 hour buffet pass (Join Total Rewards club for discounts,this is free) and paid extra $25 for the dinner. The look of the place was amazing, you are greeted with the seafood bar, they have fresh oysters, mussels, oyster shooters, huge cocktail shrimp, ceviche, lump crab pea soup, gazpacho, buckets with clams and sausage (clambake) and much much more. The key is to browse the selections first, then pace yourself. There's prime rib. Tomahawk style ribeye steak, sushi, Pho, crablegs heated to order,pecking duck, chinese bbq pork(divine), and then there was dessert...macarons!!and more..yummm. I felt this one was not too overwhelming, the taste of the food is good individually and made very very well. The experience was beautiful, it could be a Vegas attraction, so good we came back for brunch, paid extra $15, the honey ham carved to order, the fresh bacon and congee made the return worth it!!

I had very high expectations. Went on a Monday. Very upset. Never going back. Good ambience. Desserts were okay. Other dishes were cold and seemed stale(probably weekend leftovers) 
Very overrated place! A big NO.

Our favorite buffet in Vegas. All the food is fresh, displayed beautifully, and most important tastes amazing. Great variety. 

Tips: Try to go during off peak hours to minimize your wait time.

The BEST buffet I have ever been too! And this is coming from someone who isn't a fan of buffets. 

There were so many assortments of foods from different cultures... Mexican, Asian, American, Italian, etc.... Oh and you must check out the seafood bar! Personally, my favorite area was the desserts! Their desserts were high quality compared to typical buffets. There was no way I was able to taste a little bit of everything. 

The service was amazing! Make sure to show your appreciation to the chefs and servers. They really deserve it!

I need a bigger stomach. Bacchanal is overpriced and the wait is terrible, but I loved the food. It's not 5-star dining, but it is a fantastic buffet.

Food 5/5
This is the reason to got Bacchanal: the food. The variety of section is impressive. My favorite stations were theses
- Seafood with crab, shrimp, and oysters on the half shell
- Meat with lamb chops
- Chinese with dumplings, crab, and noodles
- Desserts with anything cause they were all great

Service 4/5
The people working at the food stations were extremely helpful and in a good mood. Our servers were ok. One host at the register was rude, but once we got past him everyone was generally kind.

Price 3/5
My husband and I went the day before Christmas for lunch. It was $54 per person and an additional $20 for express. It's hard to get $74 worth of food at a buffet.

Parking 3/5
Parking for Caesars Palace was free in the self parking lot. We had to drive around and wait for a spot, but eventually found one on the top floor. After parking, it is about a 10-15 minute walk to Bacchanal.

Atmosphere 5/5
For a buffet, Bacchanal is all class. Just don't forget it's a buffet. People were cleaning around the food stations all the time. 

Good food, service, and cleanliness will bring me back to Bacchanal Buffet. Until then, I need to check out getting a bigger stomach.

Ahhhhh, a good Vegas buffet.. Who doesn't look forward to absolute permission to eat their face off and the food coma that ensues? But since the prices of these buffets have increased so significantly in the last few years I've found it a little harder to justify multiple visits in one trip. For the same price of a buffet, I can go eat at a fun restaurant and maybe save a few calories by not having the option of eating pizza and chicken wings and French fries all in one go. My last trip to Sin City included a trip to Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace and this may have completely changed my mind about what a buffet should be and how often I'm willing to go.

In a word...incredible. Anything you can imagine was available at their weekend brunch. From an amazing assortment of Chinese, Korean, Japanese, even Vietnamese to Italian pizza and pastas. Sliders and hot dogs to chicken and waffles to pancakes to quiche, I mean the list goes on and on. There were so many different stations (I counted a carving station, an omelet station, a pho/noodle station, a pasta station) and I think there could've been more, but after a while I knew I wouldn't be able to walk back to the room if I kept eating. There was also a fantastic array of raw sea food and sushi available. And everything was good, some items were even great (any of their pizzas and the Korean bbq short ribs, for sure!). I loved that many of the dishes were served in individual hot dishes instead of the big bulk catering dishes that everyone picks out of. The downside to that was that it made carrying things a little difficult as you could really only carry two personal dishes at a time. I'm going to try to think of a system next time I go where I can try to grab as many as five different dishes in one trip. 

I never made it to the dessert section, although my friend did declare that they had some of the best bread pudding she had ever tasted. For $45 (that's the weekend brunch price - before 3:00 PM) Bacchanal is 100% worth the money, time and calories. Drinks are included (even mimosas!), and you will definitely eat enough so that you won't me hungry for a very long time. Considering that the night before I bought a bottle of water and a very small turkey sandwich in the hotel lobby for $18, this is an absolute steal. Can't wait to go back and try this one more time!

This is my favorite buffet to splurge on in Vegas.
Everything at the buffet is to die for, not to mention every day they have 15 brand new chef specialties on the menu! 
Not only do they have standard buffet fare like an array of hot freshly cut meats and seafood, but they have unique things like Fried frog legs, bone marrow, grilled octopus, lamb shank with chimichurri sauce on it. 
The QUALITY of the food is on another level.. consistently putting out more freshly prepared product, full of flavor, and of premium restaurant grade food.
I'd rather spend $60 for all of the options here, than one fancy burger and salad.

At a steep $54.99 per person for a weekday dinner, Bacchanal is definitely one of the most expensive buffets on the Strip. They offer a wide variety of cuisines and I enjoyed almost everything I tried. The oysters, bone marrow, octopus, and dimsum were my favorites. Even the made-to-order carne asada tacos were good. The dessert area was also extensive and I wish I saved more room to try everything. 

There were a few misses for me though. Our waiter gave each person 2 drinks at the beginning of our meal. With 10 people in our party, there were 20 drinks on our table! He probably did that so he wouldn't have to keep coming back. The lines for the food were kinda slow, especially for the seafood. Avoid the "wagyu" beef and egg tart, so disappointing.

If you're a Total Rewards platinum member, you get to skip the entire line!

There are certain stops and things one must do in the quintessential Las Vegas experience.  One of these is visiting a Buffet. Grand, new, well-advertised, we ventured into the Bacchanal Buffet. True to its name sake, this was a site to behold. Grandiose décor, hundreds of selections, and a massive seating area, this certainly fits the Las Vegas over the top bill. 

I never thought I'd find myself reviewing a Buffet, but yet, here I sit. Compared to say Aria, and at double the price, I expected a certain higher quality than Aria. I didn't find it. Seafood selections are nearly identical, and while Bacchanal does offer warmed snow crab at particular times, it is still the same snow crab, shrimp, and green lip mussels you find at most buffets. Salads, charcuterie, and pizza also stand out as common to all buffets. Now to the standout, to what makes this stand out as a step up. This, stands in the carving and dessert sections. Fine selections of well-prepared meats, such as prime rib, ham, artisanal sausage stand out from most nicely. The desserts well prepared, and well executed, (except the crème brulee) are quite pleasing, and complemented with an interesting selection of gelato (Blood Orange and Pistachio being my weapons of choice).  

Having said all that, for the price point, I'd rather visit Aria, or a proper restaurant, but if you're going to do only one Buffet in Las Vegas, and don't mind splurging a bit for the one, go ahead, and give it a whirl.

I have been to Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace a handful of times and it has always been an enjoyable time. I leave feeling sick-full from overeating but it's so worth the discomfort. 

I don't even know where to begin as far as what food they have to offer but you name it, they have. Any type of dessert you can imagine, endless pastas, salads, crepe bar, taco bar, fried foods, BBQ, steaks, seafood. EVERYTHING. Every time I have gone has been around brunch time and there was never a time I thought to myself "I wish they had...". They have it all. 

I have the biggest sweet tooth so their dessert section is my absolute fav but there has never been anything mediocre at Bachhanal. Anything I have ever put on my plate at this buffet is delicious. I have no desire to try another buffet in Vegas because I love Bacchanal that much. The wait is worth the meal you will have here. One of the best buffet's around.

I've been coming to this buffet once a every 3 month past 3yrs and this time it was very dispointing.  We went in around 4pm right after lunch and all the food was soooooooooo dried.  Sushi, Chinese foods, bbq section...most of the food was dried and it wasn't worth paying almost60 bucks for that food. Ill never go back again ever.

Came here on a Saturday morning after hearing that it was the nation's best buffet and was very impressed.  This buffet offered every item of food I could hope for and all items were of great quality... Excellent brisket, cute and tasty pouched egg creations and some of the best dim sum I've had.  The dessert selection was also extensive and fantastic... I particularly enjoyed the crepe station and bubble tea.

After going to the Bellagio Buffet, this one seemed pretty overrated.  If you love Asian cuisine, you'll love this place.  There was a huge variety of asian food, and even the desserts had many asian flavors.  But as far as italian, mexican etc, not that much.  
I mainly stuck with the crab and oysters to get my moneys worth.  The meats werent as flavorful or juicy either.  Spend your money elsewhere.

Service: The wait for this line varies anywhere from 10 mins to 3 hours. Yes, you read right 3 hours. I would recommend avoiding this buffet during busy holiday season and long weekends. Service is good, your plates are cleared regularly. Most of the time you are able to get your drinks refilled in a timely fashion. 

Atmosphere: Grand. It looks really pretty. They made good use of glassware (such as drinking cups) as their decor. Each station is decorated well making the food even more appetizing! 

Food: The food is ABOVE AVERAGE for a buffet on the strip. Food quality was much better when they first opened. There was more variety and fresh juice served in these cute bottles! They still have the juice now, but they are not the fresh squeeze juice it once was. If you are looking for seafood, it is only served after 3:30pm for dinner. They have different food stations that caters to different type of food - Asian, Salad, Cheese and Preserved Meats, Italian, Mexican, Soup, Bread, Meat, Seafood, DESSERT, and a few smaller stations.  

Price: It is definitely one of the priciest option on the strip. However, if you are only going to try one buffet on the strip, then you won't regret picking either this or the Wynn buffet :) 

Overall: Highly Recommend!

Fourth time here, and I must say, we chose this place over Joe's because they told us the wait would only be 20 minutes on a Sunday around 3 pm.  

I'm never gonna eat beyond a total of six plates, but when in vegas, do bacchanal cause the options will please you despite however many plates you can handle.  Crab legs and waygu beef were so-so and everything else was above average, but to me, it's the grandeur of it that made me content.  Lamb, bone marrow, oysters, escargot, and other meats.  

I wish they had rib eye  like they do over at the Wynn...hopefully management will see this and consider****


 The food didn't seem like it was sitting out there long like other buffets, so the food quality was pretty good since there seemed to be a good system of rotating the food.

The desserts and fruit were very satisfying.  Choose wisely and be kind to your server.  They're really patient and pleasant, and are part of your dining experience.

Fantastic place. All kinds of options. Long lines on the good stuff. So when your looking to see what looks the best I would recommend just follow the line of people.  

Great past and seafood options. Service is great the staff takes pride in what they do. 

Desert time is always my favorite. And here the little pies and stuff topped off the meal well

First time trying out this place and it's okay! 

The waiter was great, cleaning our plates and checking in if everything's okay. I feel it's a bit overrated and not a lot of options to choose from when you pay about $50 per person I expect to more variety of foods.

Been looking forward to Bacchanal for a while and tried it on my last Vegas trip.  Couldn't be more disappointed.  Nothing from this buffet was memorable.  Most of the food was either bland or cold.  Skip this one if you are on the fence.

Hands down, the best buffet I've ever been to.

Usually, when I visit a buffet, I run across a pretty vast range of quality. Some items are good, others not as much, and some downright bad. This was far from that formula. The majority of the items I sampled at both breakfast and dinner (and trust me, I sampled quite a few) were from good to great.

Several items surprised me with their quality. For example, the mini hot dog. I didn't expect to enjoy this, but they got the details astoundingly correct, down to the wax pepper and the bright green relish. 

As with many buffets, the food run the gambit from classic American fare like your mini burgers, fries and mac & cheese, to Mexican, to Chinese, and again, everything worked quite well. Very few weak spots at all, and if you don't like something, you'll find another half dozen to replace it on your plate.

Is it pricey? Probably the most expensive buffet I found on the strip. But is it worth it? Absolutely. You could spend half as much very close by, as long as you don't mind crappy food. But I, for one, will always spend more to enjoy good, quality food. And that'd exactly what you get here.

My husband and I were in town for the marathon last weekend. We heard that we should try out a buffet while staying in Vegas so our search for the buffets began. The reviews for the Bacchanal Buffet were so good that this was our first buffet destination stop. We went on a Saturday morning which we didn't know that weekends are their champagne brunch. The price shook us a little with being round $47/pp but we decided with so many great reviews and being in Vegas on vacation we might as well splurge. Needless to say the money was well worth the trip! The food was of good quality, so many selections from sushi to various meat stations to seafood to desserts. The serving line for each station was extremely clean, the chefs were friendly, the mimosas were endless! Our server was efficient (always bringing us refills and clearing the table) and super friendly! We definitely recommend this place at least once!
Hands down the best in Vegas, price kinda sucks but it's worth it. Hot and cold crab legs, claws and oyster bar

Food/Price
- Price varies. Lunch is around $40 and dinner is roughly $50 per person. They also mark up the prices on long weekends.
- This place has great variety. Entrees include seafood, prime rib, lamb, tater tots, tacos, dim sum, sushi, burgers, and many other dishes. Dessert menu is also extensive so I won't go into that.
- The quality of the buffet is probably one of the better buffets that I've been to in Vegas. I was satisfied with majority of the dishes with the exception of the seafood. The king crab tasted like the ocean and the oysters were not fresh. The meat (prime rib, lamb, etc) by the carving station is also a hit or miss. If you get there when they have a fresh batch, the meat is amazing! However, there are times when the meats been there for a period of time and becomes dry. (Wait until they bring out new stuff!) As odd as it sounds, the tacos are my favorite at Bacchanal! Everything is made on the spot! I always order the pork with guac, cilantro, green sauce, onions, and a squeeze of lime to top it off! 

Ambiance/Location
- Located at Caesar's Palace
- Place is upscale and modern. Casual environment with people of all ages.

Service
- Been here many times and never had any issues with their service. 
- Be sure to tip waiters/waitresses for their hard work!

Recommendation
- The wait can be dreadful so avoid coming at peak hours to avoid long lines.
- $10-15 cheaper during lunch time and weekdays.
- Great gelato selection!
- TACOS TACOS TACOS!!

My favorite buffet in Vegas at the moment. All I can say is LAMB CHOPS are a must! The food here is so exceptional, despite the fact that it's a buffet. They really hold up to their title of being a premium buffet. My go-to favorites when eating here besides the lamb chops are the sliders, and the crab and oyster shooters! Also another favorite is the miso glazed sea bass. The sea bass is so delicate and flavorful, it literally melts in your mouth. 

I would give 5 stars, however the wait is so long, and the one time we were supposed to be paged by the hostess, it never happened and we ended up waiting an additional 2 hours, when in fact we could have been seated in 30 minutes. She had told us to wait to get the text, and apparently they never did text us.

However, based on the food and service inside the buffet, this still is my favorite buffet!

Try and get here before 5pm. Dinner starts at 3pm, avoid the long lines and get here before 5!

This is definitely one of the best buffets in Las Vegas. Lots to choose from and very fresh prepared meats and high quality seafood. I've been to all the major hotel buffets and this is my favorite. The only reason I can't give it 4 stars is the price ($59.99 for Easter brunch is a little steep) and the long wait (~1 hour).

This place truly lives up to the hype. Me and my friends got here around the time they opened. We waited in a short line and got seated eventually. Just 15 minutes later, the line got extremely long. There were all sorts of stations. Most notable is all the seafood offered and prepared in various ways and they had a ramen and pho station. I would definitely go back on my next trip to Vegas!

One of the best buffets we've been to in Vegas. The price is high but so is the quality. Take your time and survey all the offerings before you dig in! So much to choose from and everything is high quality. Even at lunch they had crab legs when we were there. The desserts were fine, but the savory items are the real reason to go! Don't miss the chicken and waffles!

I went to this buffet to scope it out for a party in Dec.  Brought friend who is a local who has been to many other gourmet buffets. I wish I could be more upbeat because I liked the atmosphere but it's the FOOD ------! BB has been open 2 mo w many reviews saying it is the best buffet. My friend & I beg to differ. Since opening price of $30 for dinner it went to $40 & is now at $43 which doesn't bother me if quality was there. 
Specifically looking for quality in Asian section which was maybe better than ave but not outstanding. 
Dim sum was good, halibut & crab legs were too salty. 
Since they bragged about more variety than anyone else expected to find bananas foster or cherries jubilee but desserts same as other places. 
Maybe I caught them on an off day but it was Sat which is a busy day to not be at ur best. 
I've got 7Star status which allows me to skip the long pay line & be seated next to window looking over courtyard to Augustus & Octavian towers -- great view! Really liked it but disappointed in so many ways. Even tho we were seated at VIP table we had to ask for refills. 
Night before did a drive by to check BB out & talked to a manager, Markus, regarding party in Dec & I am used to people being more enthusiastic. 
The 3 stars is due mostly to atmosphere because I'd really like to hold a party here but will probably go to a restaurant across the street which charges 50% more with little atmosphere. It's too bad you can't eat atmosphere.

We went of a Sunday at around 5:30 pm and the line was not that long. The food was not bad. I love the seafood and dessert. The best thing to do is to buy the 24 hour all access pass. You pay $30 more for any buffet that has seafood but it's worth it. They have 5 buffet choices to choose from (flavors the buffet at Harrah's, paradise garden at Flamingo, Le village Buffet at Paris, spice market Buffet at Planet hollyhood, Carnival World buffet at Rio hotel are included and free). Bacchanal at caesar, carnival world &seafood buffet at Rio, high Roller at LinQ are extra $30 more each time you eat.

I have had several friends tell me I should not come to Vegas without trying this place as it should blow me away.  I arrived about 2:30 and had the pleasure of being seated next to a charming younger couple to my right.  As the meal went on we got to discussing food and life in general.  All three of us had at least 2 menu items we rated as sub par.  In my case: fried chicken that was very, very dry under the coating and creme brulee that was drinkably liquid under the torched crust..  Too have 6+ items amongst 3 people that were not up to par in a buffet rated this highly is a fail.  As a personal note I felt I sank down too low in the chair to be comfortable, it felt like a booth which is why I normally prefer sitting in a chair.  Now that I have complained, this place has a lot going for it with the total number of items, most of which are properly done.  The entire staff was very pleasant and knowledgeable.  Considering this place was full with about a 10 minute wait in line you would never know they were at capacity. 

I just come up a bit short being able to give it the 4 stars it probably, on many days, deserves.

I give it 3 stars cause they tried. Nothing was any better than most of the buffets in town. Yes its all nice and pretty. But come on. For $120 for 2 people you should get more. The cracked crab legs were very small. Only tiny slivers of meat. Not worth it. Seems like you get more doing it yourself. And for everyone to rave about the brisket. You must not be from texas. It tasted like a roast. Im not trying to talk any of you out of eating here. Somethings were real good. Like the scallopped potatoes. Not $60.00 good. But good. Just go in thinking its just going to be ok. That away you wont feel disappointed.

Worth every penny! $50 USD For each person is amazing for the variety of food and quality you are getting... we were lucky and beat the rush so the wait was less than 20 mins in line... last year I recall we waited for 1.5-2 hrs....They have an Asian section with dumplings and ramen and stirfry's, then there's the Italian section with the pasta, pizza and steamed shellfish and dried meat and cheese. Then you have a salad bar, attached to a long line of a selection of meat (prime rib, ribeye, lamb, chicken breast, chicken sausages etc.) then you have an array of shellfish at the cold bar as well. Pop and coffee is unlimited & included in the price. The dessert selection is huge! I loved their lemon basil ice cream. So many pastries to choose from!!!
