I love experimenting with new food at Bacchanal every time I visit because I trust that their chefs make delicious food.

I read the reviews of this place before I came. I had high hopes and great expectations. Came here during a weekday (Tuesday) and thought it was going to be a memorable dinning experience. I didn't mind waiting to get in. My problem lies with the damn salt content and the server being incognito. The ribs and asian chicken dish were the saltiest. I understand salt adds palatability but the amount added caused my tongue to burn. The server came around eventually, keep in mind the facility was not at maximum capacity. We had to ask other servers for assistance which amounted to them telling us that they'll relay the message. I've had other buffets in the area this one was alright.

Motto of this buffet: "You don't leave when you're full, you leave when you hate yourself."


This was probably my number one thing to check off my bucketlist when I found out I would be coming to Las Vegas. Being an avid travel channel watcher I think I've seen the same episode of greatest buffets about 10 times. Every time they showed Bacchanal buffet in all its glory I would tell myself eventually I'll go here. And now I have. 

Bacchanal is located in Caesar's Palace Casino & Hotel. It's not there when you first enter if I remember correctly. I believe we had to walk through the casino to finally arrive. 

The line is LONG. Be aware. This isn't the place to come to where you're hangry and desperate for food. But it is so damn worth it to stand in the line. Since we were a party of four we checked in at one of the computer stations and got a ticket. If your party is bigger than...5 or 6? (Not sure on the number) you'll be put in a different line to accommodate everyone. 

We stood in line for about 25-30 minutes with ease. We struck up conversation with the boys in front of us and they told us the food was so amazing and worth it. Basically hyping us up even more for what was to come. 

It is pricey for dinner, we wanted to come for lunch but SAT & SUN IS BRUNCH & DINNER. There is no lunch and therefore we paid dinner prices.  :( 

Once we got to the front and were led to the tables we all had game faces on. There was strategy in everyone's mind. I had two separate stomachs ready, one for sampling everything savory and one for sampling everything sweet. It was a delicate balance, but I think I succeeded. 

I started more on the asian cuisine side. I had the seafood pasta (YUM), pot sticker (yum), shumai (meh), macaroni (yum), lamb (YUUM), piece of beef (?YUM)--not exactly sure which one I had, mashed potatoes (yum), macaroni salad (yuum), bread (yum!), hummus (meh). 

I sampled as much as possible, which meant I didn't grab heaping portions unless it was out of my control (like going to the meat station). I obviously can't ask for a small slice. They just give you what they cut. But the meat station is definitely a must. Try to sample among your friends. 

The crabs are also a must, as my friend was quite satisfied with the crab legs they had to offer. 

The dessert station was my absolute favorite. I tried everything. I mean almost everything. Gelato, pecan tart, red velvet cupcake, cheesecake, tiramisu, cake. I dived in. I had the salted vanilla and the cookies and cream gelato. Everything was amazing. Good lord. 

You leave when you hate yourself. There is no such thing as being full. When you loathe your very presence that is when it's time to go, but not a cupcake sooner. Eat until your heart can't take it, stuff your face and remind yourself it's 60 dollars so you damn well better eat 60 dollars worth of food. 

If I ever visit Vegas again I will be most excited to be back in this line ready to devour everything in site.
Loads of food to choose from, of all styles. It's all fresh and great quality. Customer service is impeccable.

This is still the best buffet on the strip. Went to The Buffet at the Wynn the previous night and it didn't compare. The extra $7-8 makes a difference. Bacchanal has great variety. My favorite is the warm crab legs. The buffet has the cold version, but the ones from the boiling pots are the best! 
The Asian food variety was really good. The roasted duck was delicious! I remembered to save room for dessert and that didn't disappoint. There is a lot variety with gelato, pastries, cookies, and fruit. I would definitely go back!

This review is based mostly on the price vs other Vegas buffets.  Bacchanal charges a lot more than any of the other buffets in Vegas.  I went for a weekday lunch and the price was $33, ouch!!  This is compared to $25 at the Wynn.  I really like the Wynn a lot, so I was expecting a lot more at this place.  Unfortunately, nothing excited me at this buffet.  Maybe it was just a bad day for them, but pretty much everything was underwhelming that day.  A lot of the food did not get refilled in a timely manner and a lot of the signs were not in front of the food, so you did not know what some things were.

In terms of the food, I guess I got used to the Wynn, Wicked Spoon and the Bellagio.  Most of the food here was cheapie food, not that there is anything wrong with that, as I love cheapie food.  Its just when I go to one of these buffets, I expect to try high end dishes I do not usually eat on a regular basis.  They had street tacos, bbq meats, chinese food and noodles like pho, udon and ramen.  I would much rather get these types of foods in hole in the wall restaurants and they are much better at those places.  The food overall was ok, but if you are going to charge the highest price for a buffet on the strip, I think the food should be much better than just ok.

Small wait time but the line moved fast! The waitress was very attentive and knowledgeable. All of the food stations were organized and well stocked. The juices were fresh - standout was the watermelon. All of the seafood was phenomenal - go for the crab and shrimp. My favorite station is Italian and fresh cheeses. No other buffet in Vegas comes close to this one!

Ok, well I wanted to like this place being that my father in law footed the bill but im going to be honest about this place its just another buffet. The only thing that is worth trying is the crab legs and the rib eye steaks here. The wait wasn't that bad we waited a total of twenty five minutes included putting our names down. Some of the things I tried at the buffet were:

Sushi.....its alright kinda tastes and looks like packaged sushi from 7 eleven
Rib eye.... was good and tender
Lamb shanks....they were good but overcooked
Carne asada tacos.....never come to a $50 buffet for tacos you can go else where, but the tacos were ok.
crab leggs...where really good and they are unlimited too,so I guess thats good.
Brisket...overcooked and tasted terrible
fruit....some of it was overripe and was uneatable 
desserts...were eh ok

There was a line for the meat and the cook serving the meat was very rude to most of the customers, including myself. He asked me what choice of meat I wanted I told him and then he didn't repeat back what I wanted so I repeated it a second time to remind him and he then copped an attitude and said " I Heard you man you don't got to tell me twice" and I was like woah, this guy is pissed. He's probably policing the meat hoping that his attitude will only cause just a few people to return a second time. Screw him I came back about three times, after all this was a $53 dollar buffet wasn't going to let this go waste. 

The service was ok, the lady that served us brought our drinks and after that I pretty much had to flag her down ever now and then to get a new drink. Would I come back? nope, very disappointed the wicked spoon is much better and a lot cheaper than the buffet here, sorry guys its the price that makes you want to like this place and not the food.

Finally got to try this place that everyone raves about. We came on a Sunday morning so they had their brunch offerings. The food was extremely fresh and well seasoned. They offer a variety of dishes ranging from Chinese dim sum to cocktail shrimp and sliced prime rib or the wagyu. My favorite dish had to be their mashed potatoes, lobster Benedict, and pistachio Gelato. I also enjoyed the service. Our waitress continually filled our mimosa glasses without us asking.

The classic Vegas buffet. Very nice, almost worth the steep price but I mean, when in Vegas, might as well try it! The food is pretty awesome inside, they make even the most basic foods really fancy and nice. Specifically the Mac n cheese. Somehow, I found that to be the most surprisingly nice entree. Anyways, the rest is great, check it out!

Had this for a second time and enjoyed it as much as my first.  If you're looking for sushi or may, go to wynn or bellagio

Good:
Seafood quality
Huge assortment of food.
Dessert selection.
Decor
Service!

Bad:
Pricing
Sushi

Ok:
Meat
Asian food

december 8, 2012 saturday 6 pm dinner. truly, truly devastating to pay $214.00 for 4 people with high-expectation on the food quality of the famous ceasar's palace casino... the meats tasted like saw dust, the bbq pork & ribs, the cold crab legs, the wagyu sliders could nottt compete with white castle, the judean dried briskette, the architecturally goofed-up food line. i would give this place a lone 2-pointed star just because of the dessert presentations. the chinese section of the buffet seemed like an abandoned chinatown... how can this be!!!?! ceasar's palace?!?! i refused to believe a post i read before coming here that this place should be called back-anal! i was wronnnggg to ignore it!!! i hope others will have a better meal. otherwise gambling your money to win or regret is nottt just in the casino part of ceasar's palace?!?!?!...ceasar's palace?!?!

This is the best buffet in vegas! It's pretty awesome that quantity does not lower the quality! 

I usually go around dinner time because they have a better seafood selection :) I get the crab legs warmed and sprinkle lemon on it! Yum! Also, their oysters taste on the fresher side. 

Also, they have a good selection of mexican and asian. Don't forget to get their horchata! It's delicious. 

My favorite part of this buffet is their dessert selection.  They have macarons, crepes, pie...anything you can imagine. 

I spend a good 2 hours in the buffet and by the end of my meal, my pants get A LOT tighter. 

Tip: What I like to do is get the 24 hour band and when you get to the bacchanal you just pay an extra 15-25 dollars or so depending on whether it's lunch or dinner.

With everybody and their mamas talkin' about how good this place is I was expecting a really good experience. I have to say I was a little disappointed considering the price of $58 for dinner. At that price I was expecting good quality food which just wasn't there. My prime rib and brisket was dry and over cooked for example. The flavors of their food didn't excite me any more than that of other casinos at half the price. I won't name any casinos because you'll think that I just work for them. They do have a lot of variety and their presentation is better than most so I'll give them that. I prefer quality over quantity though. Their dessert section was disappointing as well. They didn't have much flavors to choose from in the gelato section except for the basic flavors. Same story with their pies and cakes. I personally wouldn't pay to go back there but that's just my opinion. I'd rather go elsewhere for half the price.

As my friend described it, if there was a buffet in heaven, this would be the place. This place is just so heavenly. The food was terrific and there isn't anything that I didn't really like. The only negative of this place was the wait. My group waited for about an hour and a half and it began to become really tiring and annoying. However, regardless of the long line to pay, long line to be seated and long line to get some food, everything else was glorious. It's a must try when you are at Vegas.

I can see why this buffet was rated the best in Vegas for 2012 and 2013. This place was amazing!!! When I first arrived on Sunday at 12:00 pm I liked the fact you signed in at a kiosk and a ticket voucher gave you the time your party could be seated (similar to the fast passes at Disneyland.) This means you don't have to stand in the maze line for hours and you actually have the freedom to wander around until your time slot. Additionally, you have the option of paying $15 more per person to get seated right away without having to wait for your time slot (well worth it since the wait time for 12 people at 12:00 pm on Sunday was 2 hours.) When I got inside I was happy to hear they had bottomless mimosas for brunch. In regards to the food, everything was surprisingly delicious and there was nothing I didn't like (crab legs, lobster dishes, oysters, dim sum, soups including pho, variety of meats, chef specials, desserts...) Usually at buffets there are always a few items that look good but don't taste very good but this is the only buffet ever where this was not the case. Oh man... this place was so amazing I'm still thinking about it even after my trip ended. I can't wait to go back here!!!

Me and my girlfriend have been coming to this buffet a countless number of times. Unfortunately, today we had a poor experience. Upon being seated, we waited 30 minutes until we had to ASK for someone to greet our table and at least bring us a round of waters. After asking one of the employees, she apologizes and went to go look for our server...still no one came. So then, I asked for the manager thinking talking to a voice of authority would help control the situation and mediate any conflict we may have. I spoke to Amber, and after trying to explain the whole situation to her and how long we had been waiting, she responds with a "there she is", as she points to a server. Not only did it seem that she was uncaring and unapologetic about the whole issue, but after hearing the concern in my voice she refuses to apologize or make me feel any more comfortable about the situation. It was very unprofessional, and rubbed me the wrong way. A simple, "I'm sorry" would have sufficed. 

On a more positive note, Maria was our server and was outstanding. She definitely compensated for the care that others were lacking.

I love this buffet, but poor management is definitely hard to look over.

Not everything is great, but it's the only buffet that is definitely worth the calories. Most of the people when I was there were focusing on the seafood, but you can get steamed crab legs and shrimp anywhere.  It was the charcuterie, the wonderful little deserts and the appetizers that makes it worthwhile.

Yesterday we have a dinner here with company and family. We are total 12 parties and they won't let us make reservation. After 2.5 hours waiting and 79.99 per person and $140 tips what we got is stinky oyster. I can't image how this #1 seafood buffet in Las Vegas serve not only unfresh oyster but stinky one with black color with it. 

We are so disappoint with this thanksgiving dinner especially they charge more but bad quality. 

We came in and sit down around 7pm and they remove oyster after half hour. Maybe too many people complain the bad quality.

We arrive at 10am for sunday brunch. No need to check in at kiosk. Wait only 10 minutes for seating. I have to say being here one hr early is a wise choice. 
This is our third time here. For every single time, We always found surprise dishes. All the foods here are above average. Besides crabs, craving meats n sushi, ramen soup comfort me in 40 degree weather. 
For the desert, boba tea is the bomb. They add coconut ice cream in it. Make it taste like thai tea. Not everyone like it though. But for me, it makes my day. And they give us a pot of coffee. If it get cold, u can just add more coffee to make it hot again. Thats really nice of them.

Pros: 
Huge selections. 
Dessert was my favorite of all. 
Servers were amazing.


Cons:
Long line.

One bad thing on that day was a group of teenagers next to us of about 10 of them were so loud, obnoxious and they thought they were being funny at all.  Yes, you can have a good time but at the right place. This buffet is for family, couple, or for everyone who wants to savor the food selection and not feeling being on a frat house. They were lucky my stomach was bothering me at that time and don't feel like to confront them. Fortunately, the manager came over to them and explained to them to lower down their voices but that was after 2.5 hours. Heck, it wasn't a victory for all of the diners at that time.

As of now, this is by far my favorite buffet. From their king crab legs and fresh shrimps to their selection of Asian food and roasted meats, everything about this buffet is perfect. I came here for Thanksgiving dinner and just a word of advice to anyone who plans to eat here on a holiday: come early or else you won't be able to eat until 10 PM, or possibly even later.

In terms of food and desserts and drinks, Bacchanal definitely has an exceptional selection, no doubt about that. I saw their macarons, cake pops, and doughnut gelato sandwiches and felt like I had died and gone to heaven. So why 3 stars and not the 5 stars that the chefs truly deserve? Well, while Bacchanal's food was amazing, their lines were inefficient and absolutely unfair. My family and I had obtained a ticket at ~2PM and were told to come back in 2.5 hours. At 4:30, we were asked to stand another 1.5 hours to pay and get seated. By 4:30, the wait time had gone from 2.5 hours to 5-6 hours, and it was then that people began to cheat the system and lined up in the VIP area to pay when they 1) were not a preferred member and 2) did not have the original tickets to begin with. The whole system was just ridiculous and no one from the management team seemed to notice, let alone do anything about it, so my family and I had to just stand and continue waiting as everyone cut their way inside the buffet.

On top of that, our server was inattentive the entire time we were inside and ended up having to snatch the iced tea jugs from the server stands myself to refill my family's drinks. I understand that Thanksgiving day is a very busy day, but those are the days that establishments like Bacchanal make the most money, and those are the days that Caesar's needs their staff to be on their A game, not just to the parties of 15+ people. My parents usually tip our servers generously, but there was no excuse for the lousy service we had received that day, especially when that same server was so attentive to the tables surrounding ours. So while the food was some of the best I've ever had at a buffet, I would not come back unless they improved their management and quality of service.

I love buffets and this one was a great new one. Decor is modern and beautiful... Lots of creative foods really eye catching.  It's a bit pricey and the lines can be super long at times.  We in Vegas it's like adult Disneyland.   As we get older we line up for the ride of our lives in our mouth.  Lol

Came here after reading all of the yummy reviews. Pretty disappointed!

Came here on a Saturday, waited almost 2 hours in line. Then had to wait in more lines just to GET the food, like meat and seafood. They ran out of oysters sadly, so you see 2 people behind the counter trying to crack open the shells as fast as they can. Long line of people waiting to get the oysters, which holds up the seafood line. Seems like they are understaffed. Not good. Then for the meat, had to wait in another long line. The meat is sitting under a heated lamp, so for prime rib, it was medium well to well done. I like it medium rare! Sucks.

Sushi was ok, not much variety. Desserts were yummy though. That's pretty much it. Pretty pricey, but I didn't have a good experience.
Terrible food, dry, flavorless, way over priced.  Oysters are nasty and seafood is sketchy.

I went because it's supposed to be the best buffet in Vegas. It was quite good, but I think I would've preferred higher quality normal dining.

I did eat 7 plates though haha.

Go early : I was there for the entirety of the 2 hour limit and watched lines start and balloon the longer I was there. For example, when I first got in, the prime rib section was serve yourself but turned into a chef slicing station with a 15-20 minute wait for only a couple of pieces.

My favorite items were crab and seafood. I was not impressed with the desserts at all... They seemed pretty dull and dry.

This place is bomb!!! Everything was amazing! So many options seafood, pasta, pizza, sushi, prime rib, ribs, Turkey, chicken and waffles list goes on and on. I was really impressed with the fresh squeezed watermelon juice, carrot juice and orange juice. Worth every penny!

We came here for dinner a little before 3:30pm so we were able to get in before the crowd appeared. The seating was comfortable and there were a lot of food selection! My favorite of the day was kobe beef slider, second goes to prime rib. The chef who handles the meat was very polite and would grill my prime rib to medium well for me. I ate a lot of prime rib and kobe slider that day. The roasted chicken was good. They got a lot of seafood and they look fresh and good, but I can't tell if they taste good due to my allergy. The salad and fruit were fresh and good. The asian food section looks just ok to me, but I wasn't there for asian food anyway so it was not a show stopper for me. The dessert selection was good and tasted good. 

They also got bottled juices next to the mexican station and I tried a juice (forgot the name) and horchata, both are great!

I hope they keep the quality and don't go down in the future. I am happy with this buffet. We actually got the Buffet of Buffets (BoB) pass and this is our first buffet of the pass. Need to pay $25 extra with the pass and I think it's okay. We hit 3 other buffets with the BoB pass so it's like I am paying only $25 to get in the dinner buffet at Bacchanal.

Will come back again!

Note: Our server was very nice and didn't ask us to leave after sitting there for 2 hours. I am a slow eater so I am glad I get to sit there for more than 2 hours so I get to try everything out without any discomfort.

the more i got excited in my vegas bound and tried out this buffet restaurant, the more i got disappointed. i came here on christmas eve, and it would be the worst thing ever i can tell! the line was hella long and i had to wait around 3 hrs to get inside. the food wasn't worth the price (i paid $80 for each) because there was nothing special or tasty. the most crowded queue was for the lobster, i waited 30 minutes to get A LOBSTER. it was ridiculous! however, it was not a problem if the lobster tasted good, in fact, it was too salty. it's not worth the hype, i wouldn't recommend this restaurant. CLOSED! saving your money or trying this buffet restaurant LOL. terrible!!!

I tried this last week, and I must say that I was severely disappointed. 


I've read so many good things about this buffet and when they first opened up, I definitely wanted to try it due to the reviews & price. However, the price started to go up and up and when I went, it was already $46 per. It's not the price issue -- it really isn't. I'm not afraid to pay for something that's worth my while. Heck, the wait wasn't even an issue either. I've wanted 4+ hours for other buffets. It's just I don't think the Bacchanal Buffet left an impression on me.


However, I do LOVE their rack of lambs. It was perfectly cooked and it was juicy/tender. It wasn't dry at all like how some places cook them. Another thing I loved was their personal soup bowl of "Black Chicken w/ Ginseng" at the Chinese corner. The ramen was good as well. The soup base for it was pretty decent and light rather than heavy. Other than those three, there wasn't much to celebrate about or brag about. 


I felt, in my opinion, that there wasn't enough variety. There wasn't really anything that screamed at me to try it. I didn't feel as though my $46+tax+tip was justified. It was a great experience, they had great service, and they were good .. but just not what I'd imagine it to be. 


The dessert section wasn't all that great either. 


I feel as though Wynn's buffet or the M Resort (Studio B) would be a better selection. Though their dessert section beats Wynn's dessert section. 


I would say try it for the experience but it's nothing "that" great.

I am not the biggest fan of buffets but this one was awesome!! First off, I didn't have to wait in line since we knew someone. Otherwise, I would not even bother going. Other than that, food was great. They had everything - all types of cuisine. I need to go back here again!!

Why this by far is the best buffet in Vegas; 1) 2 types of steamed to order crab legs, 2) authentic dim sum, 3) made to order noodles-ramen, wonton, pho, 3) freshly sliced charcuterie, 4) selection of hot foods, 5) but most of all the desserts-made to order crepes, hot from the oven soufflés, gelato bar, variety of macaroons, hot chocolate cookie a la mode,etc!  If you're going to wait in line for an hour for a buffet then this is the one worthy of the time.

The service wasn't great. The food was average. My son wanted spaghetti and was asked to choose between shell pasta and another one. There is a lot of variety of food to choose from but the taste was average.

This used to be my favorite but not anymore. I went on July 4th weekday dinner and I was disappointed in the lack of culinary selections. The dessert section is fabulous, atmosphere is great, staff is friendly and attentive. But the food (and price) aren't worth it anymore. Who knows maybe they were having a bad day but I'm not going to pay $50 to find out again.

Somewhat overhyped, but still good. 50% of the items are good, 25% are terrific, and the other 25% are awful. The surprising hit was the comfort food station. Delightful array of favorites with some unique additions. Steamed crab and pasta also excellent as was the taco grill. Asian station fell flat. No better than street corner Chinese. Greasy, salty. Worst item was the broccoli soup. Like a mouthful of saltwater. Don't recall last time I sent back a plate, but this one would have been returned. Horrible. Dessert station also disappointing, comprised mostly of cookies and brownies and not fine cakes pies and tortes as I had hoped.

It makes sense. Cut quality on the high dollar items to steer customers to the bargain items. This works if the bargain items are really good. They were for the most part. But, man, the few really bad items are hard to forget, especially while reflecting on the $50 per head price and the 2 hour wait. Might have gotten my money's worth. . . But just barely.

My first time in Vegas so my boyfriend and I went to brunch at the Bachchan all. We decided to have made to order omelets. Our cook's name was Curtis. It was great!one of the best omelets I've ever had and he was showy with the flip of the omelet. Friendly and professional. Kudos to Mr. Curtis for making my first Bacchanal experience great!!

This place had never disappointed me every time I have been here. There is a big selection of food and it  doesn't seem like the food had been sitting under heat lamps all day like other places. I recommend getting your placement ticket early in the day so you can actually make it inside the restaurant by the time you want dinner 6 to 7 pm, otherwise you will be waiting in line forever.

I went here during a Thursday night for dinner and was quite frustrated with the waiting time. But I was patient and boy do I not regret it. Food was absolutely delicious. It was the best buffet I have ever been. The variety was infinite and the food was cooked as if grandma was in the back making it from one of her secret recipes. This buffet clearly has its ducks in a row when it comes to chowing down. This isn't your standard prison food buffet. This is definitely a full force working kitchen with actual chefs. Food never is sparse and you can eat all you want. Oh and the best part? They have gourmet cheese for you to nibble on. Delicious!!!

$36.99 for weekend lunch.

EFFICIENT. A good way to describe this buffet. They have a waiting time ticket system. Go to the computers and enter in your party number. They spit out a receipt giving you a time range when to return for payment and seating (they will also send messages to your phone if you prefer that option) Walk around and gamble until your seating time.

I can't say much for the hot food, as most buffets I gorge myself on seafood. The crab legs and claws were a point. As were the OYSTERS! I've never had such fresh and sweet oysters at a buffet before! 

Dessert was a bit lack luster for me. The creme brulee was disappointing as the consistency wasn't right, but the FLAN was delicious and made up for the custard craving. I give them points for having macaroons at their dessert bar, granted they weren't very good and many of them were rock hard. A lot of the girls in our party loved the chocolate covered strawberries as well.

Was so excited to eat here but was very disappointed with their king crab legs because it was tooo salty... Couldnt eat as much as i thought due to the saltyness but their dessert, oysters, shrimps, tacos, and sliders were the only things that is worth going for. Chinese and japanese is just cheap quality stuff wouldnt really recommend.

That's a 3.5, rounded up.  Yeah, I'm feeling generous.

The first time I dined here, it was a weekend day in November 2012 that coincided with the Las Vegas Rock N' Roll marathon.  Yes, you read that correctly - I came here for dinner with a bunch of ravenous carbo-loading runners.  There was a 2-hour wait that had me wanting to kill my companions.  Once we got in, the lines for food were so long that my piping hot food would cool down before I got to the end of the line.  Despite this, I thought the food was very tasty and managed to enjoy myself despite the cluster$5Ck.

This time, Monday evening during the winter...zero minute wait, yay, right?  I was anticipating a glorious, glorious eating spree that would get my tastebuds tingling with pleasure.  Nope.  The food was lackluster, the flavors were nothing to get excited over.

The best dish of the night was a scallop rockefeller, a creamy, savory little thing.  I had four.  The crab was watery, almost tasteless.  As for the meats, lamb chop was overcooked (tough), the prime rib was ok.  The best meat dish was the brisket, but how can you get slow-cooking a fat piece of meat wrong?  Everything else was just plain meh.  I remember getting a slider last time that knocked my socks off -- this time, they barely tugged at my boots.

What redeemed them was the dessert - one full star goes to the dessert station.  So many items to choose from: miniature pastries, made-to-order crepes, macarons, fudge, chocolate-covered whatevers, gelato...and get this GELATO donut-wiches!  Oh yes, thank goodness for my sweet tooth overwriting the mediocrity etched on my tongue.

If you're looking for a place to make up for the calorie loss of staying up all night (or two nights) or to get sugar wasted, come here.
The foods are suck. We expect a good quality food but it did not happen in this buffet. TAKE YOUR MONEY AND GO SOMEWHERE ELSE. If u want to eat crab with ice, then enjoy.

I'm not a buffet person but my hubby loves them. So after reading the great reviews, decided to try our luck with 2 kids in tow. Luckily over the holiday season, there was hardly any wait time. We went on a weekday and for the Lunch buffet, there was a 5-10 min wait. Best thing about this Holiday season here, they have crab legs and other dinner specials even for breakfast/lunch buffet.

The food selection was enormous. Even though we went at prime lunch time, most stalls did not have crazy lines, except the seafood one. I guess everyone comes to this place for carb legs! To be honest, I prefer them at boiling crab in LA, but I saw many tables only eating crab legs (20-30 pieces all over their tables!).

I love the Mexican food here...tacos and huevo rancheros were delicious, as were the shrimps and seafood paella. Their dessert table cost me a couple of pounds in weight gain, I'm sure! The Tiramisu and creme brûlée were the best. I also enjoyed the salads here but I think I was the only one eating at  that station! Loved the water melon juice, cucumber made me gag, it was like sipping wheat grass! They keep changing the selection, so you can try a lot more types. Towards the end of our meal, they had replaced water melon with horchata.

Overall, it was great food but too much food for me. I didn't eat anything after that all day. If you are into Buffets and the line isn't too long, definitely try this...service was great and friendly and food was fresh and with lots of choices.

One of the best buffets I've been to! I wish I came for dinner though. I went to Bacchanal in August of 2015 for lunch. My favorite was their shrimp cocktail and desserts. I must have ate a lb of shrimp by myself. I also really enjoyed their comfort foods like brisket, Mac & cheese, pizza, pasta and Chinese food. 

They have so many different kinds of desserts but make sure to make your own crepe and have some gelato. 

All in all everything was very good quality and the service was very good for a buffet. One of the cleanest buffets I've been to.

Okay ... I'm a buffet maniac. For $54 you have to think you can get a custom steak and a lobster tail at a traditional restaurant. I was tired and hot... Still had to wait an hour off prime time on a Monday. When I finally got in, I did a walk around. Nothing spectacular visually to make me salivate. I went light and had marginal sushi. Salads were McDonald's style without the container. I did Love the two cheese choices and select cut dry salami. Went to the seafood cold section ... The smallest queen crab legs I ever saw. Pre split with almost zero meat... But great clarified butter. The oysters must have been on sale at the fish market... No meat. Clams the same cheap small Manila style .. Oyster shooters all tomato juice and micro oysters. The shrimp was standard on ice. The meat section looked good but.... Had a select quality prime beef.. Tough and forgotten..beef ribs 90% fat... Baby backs were dry as the bones. The worst Cole slaw I ever tasted .... Now for the triumph ... The deserts saved the day... I sampled as much as I could... And I have to give it one of the best ratings for every aspect of flavor enhancing deluxiousness. Thats what the three stars were for. I still would pass this place and get everything on a Burger King menu for less than $50 and you'll be happier. Go to the Oyster Bar @ the Palace and see sea food at its best...

YES. My favorite Vegas buffet!

How can I even begin this review...there are so many varieties of food and dessert that you will definitely feel overwhelmed walking in. My suggestion? Do what your family has probably taught you over the years and go for the expensive items that you yourself would (rarely if that) never cook! Juicy, tender brisket, gigantic slabs of house smoked bacon, stone crab claws...the list could go on forever.

I especially am a huge fan of their Asian selection towards the back. I've never had a bad broth there (whether it be pho, ramen, miso soup, etc) and I love that they can take that broth and add whatever noodle/meat/veggie to it. I especially loved their hand rolls - I am a sucker for any sort of temaki where the nori remains crispy and doesn't get soggy! (Side note - skip the other rolls - way too much rice...)

Their dessert station always changes and that's what I love about it. This time around, the gelato was especially delicious and I couldn't get enough of my espresso/nutella combo! 

TL;DR ALWAYS LEAVE ROOM FOR DESSERT. :)

I came to the bachannal buffet this week after reading all the rave reviews, and was highly disappointed. 
Not only was it not specified that you have to retrieve a wait time before checking in to wait in line, but the food was mediocre at best.
The sign advertised holiday buffet , but served the same things at every other buffet. 
For 63.99 you'd think there would be more gourmet, varieties. But you get the plain staples of each culture, Asian fried rice, dim sum, noodle soups. Hispanic tacos, American sliders and fried chicken. About the only thing that was somewhat worth it was the white fish ceviche and dessert portion. 
This buffet is only worth it if you are only going to eat crab legs because that's what you're paying, and waiting Hours for.
Not worth the money or time.
Take your business to the Wynn or wicked spoon.

S2

This buffet took my Vegas buffet top spot; sorry Bellagio.  

Great variety and freshness.  Decor is quite nice.  They keep sending mimosas at me! 

I would definitely look out for the long lines...btw you can get a $1 discount/person if you have a Total Rewards card (which is free, and you can get while you kill time waiting.)

This is where you go to get your "big gurl on" or to eat away that hangover...we used it as both last trip.

We arrived around  11:30a on a Saturday for their big n boozy brunch.  We checked in at the kiosk and were texted within 5mins.  We waiting in line around 10mins as we made our way up to pay and be taken to our table.  Total was around $50 for the buffet and bottomless mimosas.  This buffet line is long.  I mean LONG.  As you make your way down it, you expect it to end.....and it doesn't, and boy do they have it all!  From sea food station up front, meat cuttings, every home style side under the sun, potatoes served each and every way.  Asian, Italian, Sushi, and then and then and then.  Seriously folks.  And to top it all off, in the center of the dining room is a station dedicated entirely to desserts.  

The wait staff is wonderful.  Our server made sure our glasses (be it mimosas or water) were never empty and finished plates were always gone by the time we return from another round at the food walls.  Among our tables fav items were the carved turkey, macaroni cheese, their creamy veggie pasta, mushroom pizza, veggie spring rolls, I could keep going but I'll stop.  Let's just say it was YUM central.  

So next time you're at the strip and in the mood to eat like an emperor or just needing something super heavy and plentiful to soak up the booze from last night, look no further than the Bacchanal Buffet.  It'll absolutely serve either purpose...or both.  Don't judge.

Really great buffet for any out of town visiting. Never heard one local say ine bad thing about thia buffet. Its always talked about the top 3. Varieties of dishes. So tasteful & yummy$. Price is worth its fancy. Try it and you wont be disappointed

Oysters and shrimp were fresh and plentiful. Carving station had Wagyu beef. Rest of the spread was decent as well.  Dessert station includes a crepe section which was a pleasant surprise.  Probably the best buffet in Vegas.

You know in life they say you get what you pay for . I've read reviews about people bitching  about prices and food quality .. yes you do pay $40.00 + dollars a head but believe me you get your money's worth . I'm a food critic and THIS IS hands down the best buffet 8ve ever had in my life .
Ate here every week about 2 years ago, line was about 30-45 min wait, but it was all worthit. Good food!

DINNER ONLY REVIEW:
Expensive? Absolutely. Worth it? Depends on what you eat. I easily ate my price worth of hot crab legs, lamb and chocolate covered strawberries so I cannot complain about the price. However I think it is around 15 dollars overpriced (though in comparison to other buffets in the city it is fairly priced). It is hands down the best buffet in Vegas that I have eaten at. 

The service was really good as well, both my individual table server/bussers, and the buffet servers were all very friendly/helpful. 

The Asian food section was not good in my opinion at all. It was the main downside to this buffet experience. The section is MASSIVE which I was excited about, but most of the food was very flavorless and seemed like it had been sitting out way too long (which I somewhat expect for a buffet, but it was exceptionally bad here). 

P.S. Hot crab legs are way better than the cold ones they have piled up on the buffet line. If you ask the guys at the pasta station, they will gladly fill a plate up with some hot ones for you.

This was such a huge dissapointment. Maybe this place was good once but not amymore. I have tried the Buffet and Wynn and the Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan and this was by far the worst of the three. All the meats are super dry and tough. The seafood had so much salt on it that it was hard to swallow even drenched in sauce. The non meat and seafood options look like they have been sitting there for a while. The sliders, pasta, and small bites certainly taste like it. It is very strange given how long the line for this place was. Maybe they made too much the days before and reheated it? I got so desperate to eat food I actually ordered noodles. The ramen was weird and sweet. The pho was decent. I actually ate the whole bowl b/c I couldn't find anything else to eat. The dessert was okay and only just slightly worse than the other two buffets.

Came here on a Saturday for breakfast, the line was about an hour wait and you can pay $25 to cut the line which my friend and I did and it came out to be $80 per person and it was well worth it! Some of the foods were really good such as the street tacos, pho and snow crab legs. The dim sum was ok. They even had crawfish! Though the cf was frozen it was the best cf I've had AT a buffet. This is a buffet in Vegas you definitely want to try out.

Absolutely the best buffet I've ever been to. Expect to wait at least an hour to get in. The food here is so good. If it weren't a buffet, I'd say that the food is still pretty good quality and flavor but seeing as they make this stuff for thousands of people a day and they make it non stop, the quality is really great.

They have different sections: seafood, smoked/bbqed meat + southern american food, mexican, italian, asian and desserts. The highlight of the seafood section for me and our party of 16 were the scallops. I don't know what they put in them or how they made them but they were uhhhhhmazing. After sitting under the heat for a while, you'd expect the scallops to dry out but they were still juicy and tasted perfectly cooked. Their smoke/bbqed meat favorite for me were the Wagyu beef sliders. I'd say stay away from their prime rib, fried chicken, and mac and cheese. All three of those were mediocre. The tacos were really good too. Coming from SD we have a great variety and selection of quality Mexican food. The tacos here were on par with authentic Mexican food shops in SD. Their seafood paella was also really good. Its got a kick to it so watch out for that. Stay clear of their dim sum area. Its not that good in my opinion. Their sushi was always out :( but I had one piece and it was pretty fresh. Their desserts are on a whole different level. SOOO good. My favorite was the tiramisu but I also liked the panna cotta and their macarons. They have this peanut putter dessert that I'd recommend but I'm a big fan of peanut butter so I don't know if it'd be the same for the average person. It was pretty peanut buttery?

Good place but expensive.

Breakfast (Monday - Friday, 7 a.m. - 11 a.m.): $25.99
Brunch (Saturday - Sunday, 8 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $40.99
Lunch (Monday - Friday, 11 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $32.99
Dinner (Daily, 3 p.m. - 10 p.m.): $45.99 on weekdays, $50.99 on weekends

Really for a buffet.

Everyone said it, and I'll repeat it: This is THE BEST buffet in Vegas.

Eat here. Like seriously eat here.

Normally I don't like buffets because I never feel like "I get my money's worth" or whatever nonsense, but this is the exception. Forget Wicked Spoon, forget whatever else you've heard, BACCHANAL. The quality of food here is so good that I wouldn't mind eating here multiple times and just enjoy the different foods, because--yeah sure a specialty restaurant might be better with their specialty item--but this place comes pretty freaking darn close, in every cuisine too.

Very clean, awesome and attentive service, nice and spacious.

I believe it's around $50-55 dollars or so for dinner on Friday, but not completely sure. We were walked in to the front of the line and paid for (any Diamond+ members can do that I think) by my awesome friend's dad :) :) :) definitely made the meal better but I'll try to be unbiased. (LOLwhoamIkidding)

----Food
-Brisket, prime rib for meat. GREAT. They have others too but I could not fit anything else in my stomach no matter how hard I tried.
-They have ramen. And pho. I only had the ramen but it was pretty great terms of ramen. I compared to ones I've had in L.A. (L.A. is def better) but I mean c'mon what can you expect, it's good enough.

******** Truffled Potato Gratin *****************
^^^ NOTE THIS ITEm. TRUFFLED POTATO GRATIN. GET IT. THEN GET MORE.
TRUST ME. TRUFFLED POTATO GRATIN. nothing I can say will explain the truffled potato gratin.

If that wasn't clear enough, get the truffled potato gratin. It's by the meat section. You're welcome.
**************************************************
-Another key item is the *PEACH GREEN TEA* drink. Order it, it's soooooooooo good. Even if you just want a taste (it's a buffet!) I've never heard of it or had it til my friends all got it, and oh boy this drink just makes me hate any other buffet for not having anything close to it.

-They also have sushi, and more variety and better quality sushi than any other (general) buffet I've seen in Vegas, including Wicked Spoon. Tuna and salmon, sashimi and nigiri, and wasabi. The only downside is I couldn't find any tiny bowls for soy-sauce-and-wasabi :-/ step up yo gaammeee bacchanal!

-Xiaolongbao (Chinese pork buns) and other Asian section dishes. Man they have like everything here. Tasty, but I didn't eat too much because high carb-to-price-ratio and we Asians all know we can't be eating those at buffets ;)
-Crawfish was decently great.
-Standard (good quality) crab legs. Can ask for it hot or cold!
-Good desert bar.
-Oysters are good too, not the BEST but they're passable if you like oysters.

I know I've missed a ton of sections and foods but trust me, you can go multiple times and still love the darn place. Honestly the highest quality gourmet foods I've ever tasted in a buffet. HIGHLY RECOMMEND.

mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm.

bottomless brunch mimosas. all the food is really good. the quesadilla with the egg on top is to die for imo. if you don't see what you want, ask and they will make it for you. by no means an inexpensive buffet. gets sort of crowded so try to get there early.

yyyuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuummmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm.

also, make sure you try the mango habanero gelato. spicy ice cream. so friggin good.

I have always wanted to try this buffet because of all the good things I have heard and finally got the chance.  Just a warning to anyone wanting to try it be prepared to wait.  It was 2 of us and the wait was about 30-40 minutes.... food was about a 75% success rate.  Most of the food was good and better than average buffet, but some were not that appealing.  Some of the fish wasn't as good as we thought and some of the other dishes that aren't as popular probably say out too long before anyone picked it up.

Another thing to note is that there are 2 sections of the buffet.  The second part is around he corner from the main section and has a variety of ethnic food.  We didn't notice this until halfway through the meal but were able to enjoy the new findings.  Overall nice experience and can cross this of my bucket list.  I would recommend anyone to try this place at least once for the experience.

Long lines if you don't come early. People were paying money to "skip the line". We waited. WAITED. And waited a little longer. And, it's worth the wait. Everything is well presented and really delicious. I personally wish the dessert bar had more options, but it saved me from overindulgence. The only draw back is it's costly ($150 with good tip) and the wait can be a bit much. But, it won't stop me from coming back!

A very impressive buffet with everything you can want and more. The buffet options are not typical buffet quality... they are higher than average for sure. Each genre of food is good enough for you to just enjoy that one for the entire meal. Plan on being a while if you want to enjoy and sample the various options.

They did finally heat up the crab legs, but the guy I had originally asked said no, but he checked and said okay and also other customers were saying "What?" and I got my backup. They should have a warm up station for the crab because a lot of people were like wow they heat it up?  The buffet was okay, I went to have a late lunch that ran into dinner. Maybe the actual dinner buffet would've been better?  First time there and it was enough for me. The crab legs with melted butter was the best thing.  Unfortunately nothing made my eyes close and hum a yum. The yelp photos sure looked great, but taste wise, I don't know. Bellagio's buffet, years back near when they opened, made me literally close my eyes and sigh with happiness with their creme brûlée. But as far as buffets go, Bacchanal is of course one of the top ones.  April 1, 2013, my regular adult lunch buffet was $31.99 and kids was $19.99. I'm not sure if being a Total Rewards member makes a price difference, but they did ask for my rewards card.  We had the middle booths with our own chandelier and it was nice and relaxing. If doing Buffet of Buffets, the Bacchanal add on charge is Breakfast $15, Lunch $20, and Dinner $25.  We opted to not do Buffet of Buffets because there are so many restaurants we want to try, yet still look hot. ;P lol

There were 13 of us and almost $800 for the bill. 3 of the 13 are kids! You have to come here very hungry and patient to get your money's worth. The line for the seafood was sooooo long.

Honestly, I would not eat here again because nothing I had was worth having paid that ridiculous price. The best thing I ate was here were the lamb chops.

Yelpers you have let me down - So disappointed! The wait was 1 hr today after we arrived at 7:30 pm on a Sunday. We had high expectations after watching YouTube video of the mountains of food at this buffet. How disappointing. We tried a variety of food and we liked: oysters, fried chicken, taco. There was NO snow crab as seen in pictures, the regular crabs and king crab legs were bland, mussels were meh. Meat stations were dry and cold and dry: the fries & corn were good but the prime ribs and briskets were tough, no other types of steaks and lamb was just alright. Asian area was just okay regular dim sum items and pizza all worth $30 buffet NOT $58. the dessert had better selections and flavours then the main buffet foods: rum raisin ice cream, fresh crepes, macarons WHEN there are some. Regular drinks such as pop cranberry juice pineapple juice tea coffee included. our waitress was nowhere to be found the first 3/4 of our meal and bus boys did not clean up our table. In vegas we expect food to be a certain standard especially at the Caesars palace so don't spend your money here. With this said if this is the best buffet vegas has to offer then we will stay away from other buffets. Bummer. Won't visit here again.

After the 4 hour drive from OC, we hit up this buffet to refuel. We arrived on a Tue so it wasn't busy and we got in right before 3pm so we got the lunch price. Score! The restaurant itself is very open, modern, light and clean. Our first server seemed horrified we brought our toddler but then he was quickly replaced by Rosa, who was very friendly and attentive. They have seafood, BBQ, comfort foods, Mexican, Italian, Chinese, and Japanese - maybe a few others that I may have missed. They have this Asian soup bar with pho, ramen and something else, but that was pretty cool. They even have congee! I actually think the quantity of stations was a lot less than other high profile buffets like Wynn or Bellagio. However, I thought the food quality was pretty good. I especially like the Mexican dishes. My least favorite was the dessert section! It has the impressive display of less than stellar tasting desserts. They did have gelato, mochi, cookies, macarons, etc. They have custom crepes and soufflés. I enjoyed the warm chocolate chip cookie and warm chocolate lava cake ramekins the most. I think it's worth going for the lunch prices for sure, especially if you love seafood, they have yummy crab legs, oysters and shrimp!

First time here in all my trips to Vegas.  They have some great stations available.  Good quality food.  Some of the highlights are the raw bar and the taco stand.  One area I wish they improved was the flow.  It seems to get backed up at some points and they wait for food can be longer than expected.
Good selection and quality. Nice ambiance and friendly staff. It's just a little overpriced in my opinion.

中国游客别去。Chinese tourists you deserve better service. The staff named DIANA standing at the entrance with eyeglasses in her sixtieth is racist! She refused to answer our questions and looked at us then turn around to talk with another American couple for about five minutes and just ignored all the Chinese customers.
This Buffett was a great value when it was $45 including Mimosas. Now it's $60 plus $24 to add mimosas even though the website says $15 for Mimosas.

Had Bacchanal 3 times now on my last 3 Vegas trips...which kind of means, gosh I have to have this every Vegas trip! This buffet is simply awesome--they offer so many things that the other buffets don't have! All 3 times I had dinner and all 3 times were very, very satisfying. They have a system now that you can leave your name and number, and the hostess will call you when it's almost time to be seated. But if you're a diamond reward holder--go to the left and skip the line! Yea yeah! I had the privilege to do that once, and it was sweet! Otherwise...expect to wait, but it's well-worth it!

 I recommend the hot crab leg station. They take them out from the giant pot while it's still steaming hot. Bring it back to your table and eat it RIGHT AWAY! It's still good when it gets cold, but why go to a hot crab leg station to get cold ones? There's a cold one toward the beginning of the entrance if you prefer that. I also recommend the noodle bar! I know, it's like why waste your stomach on noodles right? But oh my gosh, the broth is amazing! They actually take their time to make it considered I had to go back few times with them telling me to wait while they are cooking the broth. 
I like this buffet very much not only because it offers different cultural cuisines but also because within each cultural cuisines there are so many different styles and options within each cuisine! For example, Asian one has dim sum, hot entrees, stir fry, noodle, soup, and even congee! Italian one has pizza, pasta, charcutteries. Mexican one has nachos, made to order fajitas or tacos, salsa bar, fresh juice that include horchata! American station has prime ribs, chicken and waffles, sliders, etc etc. Seafood station has fresh oysters, shrimps, crab legs, stone crab claws, cooked seabass, seafood boil and oh, even ceviche! 

Oh yes, save room for dessert! Fresh crepe made to order, gelato, cupcakes, macarons, cakes, fruits, etc etc. Don't skip it!!

First, I went with the highest of expectations. However, I was not totally moved by it. The presentation and spread was amazing. Service was bit slow but I have nothing really bad our server. She was nice but very busy. 

Note: If you check in around 6:30-7:00 prepare to wait about an half hour or more pending on you party size. 

Now, when you enter the buffet you will be amazed by the spread and endless options, the decor is modern, staff behind the counter are nice. This is where I stop being amazed by this buffet.

The food was either salty or bland, too cold or warm, lacked seasoning, or was overall blah. The seafood selection was good but the crab legs were slightly cold/ frozen or too salty. The carving station looked amazing but was tasteless. The American Wagyu was not seasoned and lacked flavor. Also, the server cut the pieces way too thick, even after we asked for thin slice. The Italian section was decent but limited. The Asian section was good but some items were lacking flavor. The peking duck and roast pig belly were not that crispy.  The Mexican section was good and the made to order tacos were good too.

The dessert bar had an amazing selection and were the best part of the meal for me. 

Again, I believe that my expectation were set so high that this buffet failed to meet them and I was disappointed. 

I might give it another try but maybe for Brunch. Maybe

I work in the food industry and am usually NOT a buffet fan, however 2 years ago we discovered The Wicked Spoon. I fell in LOVE with. So when returning to Las Vegas I saw that
Baccahanal was rated #1 buffet, I stepped out a limb and tried it. 

I was disappointed. The food was OK. I did not like the lay out, I did not like the flow.

One thing I LOVE about the Wicked Spoon was that EVERY plate IS individual. I DONT like when TONS of people are digging thru my food.

I will give a plus to the fact we sat for a while and actually enjoyed our dinner company.

I am sorry, I will go back to Wicked Spoon.

The food here is awesome. So many different variety. Seafood options is the same as all buffets on the strip. The atmosphere just feels so inviting. Cool decor. Love their small little condiments. Must take a small little tobacco sauce to go. I would save this for special dinners as it is pricey. I say it's worth the price because the quality of food. Crab is huge.

This buffet is a little spendy but if you want the best buffet in town this is where you should go.  There was not one item I did not like.  The service was excellent, the restaurant was clean, we didn't wait in line and the food is amazing.  My favorite thing was the Yellow Curry Chicken, it was the best I've ever had anywhere.  But really all of the food was cooked properly and tasted great.  Go hungry because you won't want to miss out.  They even had shaved ice at the dessert station.

I really don't understand the hype.  Maybe I came here on a bad day?  

The dinner buffet was rather blah, I had the crab legs (hot and cold) and thought it was decent.  I tried some of the other items ... sliders, hot dog, risotto ... can't even remember them since it was so blah.  Mac n cheese was good but since when can you ever screw that up?

I will give them an extra star for the desserts, love the ice cream.

Overall, not a fan of the whole set up and how it's broken up into "sections".  Keep it simple Caesars!

There are lots of hypes about this buffet so we checked this one out! The line was crazy! It is totally worth it to buy the VIP ticket to bypass the line. So, first, you need to get in line to get ticket. So it said it would take an hour to have your number called. We thought it should be OK because we could go shopping around. But after that, you had to stay in another line to pay for your tickets and another line to be called. It took us 3 hours and 30 mins to be seated! 

I think the food was OK or a little bit above average but nothing was too special or I had to have it. The fresh oysters were the best I had there. For king crabs, go to Italian section to get the hot and steamy ones. They do taste better. 

I went there once and it is one time deal for me. That is enough!

The food is very good but the service is bad. In order for 11 people sit together, we pay extra 18% gratuity. Because of the crowd at Christmas day, they split us into two small group (6 and 5) even they promised that we will all sit together.   So 6 people was brought in to sit together at one table. We talked to the cashier who is our first contact about our situation. But the manager only give us separate table for the rest of 5 people later.  They even do not think this is their bad management causing customer unhappy.

Francisco Herrera is an excellent waiter at Bacchanal Buffet! He was constantly available with fresh drinks and to clear our table. He clearly takes pride in his job. Best buffet in the city with 100's of different foods. You must try it. It's worth the wait and the money.
Overpriced as day after thanks giving at $60 per head. Way too long a line. Could not even get to the seafood. You need to be really hungry to go here. Food quality and variety was good.

Perfection!  We loved the crawfish, enchiladas, Thai seafood salad, molten chocolate cake, passion fruit tarts, and gelato. My ten year old said, "Compared to this, it's like I never had real food before."
Delicious! Love the variety of foods from around the world! Especially the crab legs that were cut in half for easy eating!! :)

Of all the hot food I ordered throughout the buffet, 90% of it was lukewarm at best when I immediately sat down to eat. That was pretty unappetizing. I was also disappointed by the minimal options for salads or vegetables. Overall I was unimpressed with the entire buffet experience. I wouldn't go back. I paid $69 for dinner and it was an extra $15 if I wanted alcohol.

One of the most expensive buffet in town with easily the longest line. BUT, the rumors are true. Best Vegas buffet by far. Can't believe I am actually writing these words but the two hour wait time and costs are actually justified. It's true. Buffet options include foods made from very high quality and top shelf culinary execution. It's actually worth the exhausting wait... At least, if you can survive the wait...

Simply the best buffet I've ever had. We had very high expectations and they were exceeded in every way. We must have timed it right, as we walked right in and were seated with no wait. All of the food was fresh, hot, superbly prepared - the high quality makes it hard to realize it's a buffet. This will be a "must-go" on our itinerary whenever we're in Vegas.

What a waste of money!! I came for dinner buffet on Christmas Eve, and it was a huge disappointment. Everything was extremely salty to the point of being inedible. 

I am a huge lover of brisket and lamb, and I'll enjoy even mediocre versions of either. However, there was so much salt in both that I could only stand a couple bites of each. The fried chicken wasn't seasoned with anything but salt, and even their crab legs were too salty. I know people are raving about this buffet, but they should've done much better at $70 per head.

Note that I rarely give 5 stars.

This buffet is more than amazing. The whole process from getting seated to the speed of table attention is impeccably efficient. More importantly, the food is extraordinary and the presentation (very important) is welcoming and appetizing. The cleanliness and flow of people is streamlined and it seems that management has thought of everything.

I like the hot plate holder devices--you'll see what I mean. They give you 2 of them when you walk in and you're not sure what they are initially.

The seafood area is amazing--stations always full and all the pieces look big/succulent. You can get your crab legs steamed by the employees behind the station and the butter dispenser at the end of the station looks dangerously good. The carved meats looked and tasted amazing. Every dish they presented on their counters made you want to try every little thing. Hopefully you have evolved to have more than 1 stomach. Moreover, service was fast/excellent--easy to drop that good tip at the end.

It's basically $50/person. Worth it? 100%. This is hands-down the best Las Vegas buffet in the world. Yes, the most best Las Vegas buffet in the entire world.

We went for lunch on a weekday.  It's about $40 per person including tax.  The food is delicious.  They had a variety of choices.  French cuisine was the best, including the fish and pork belly.  Paella was ok.  Sea food was fresh.  Desserts were a blast!  You could see everything sweet that you can imagine, including Tai tea with bubble, French crepe, even gummy bears...my two kids' favorite.  It's pricy but worth the money!

By far best buffet I've been to in Vegas. It was $90 for 2 people but it's worth it and it came with unlimited mimosas!! 

They have all types of food and the quality is amazing. They have this sampler plate at the meat carving station that I definitely suggest.  Foods range from seafood to dim sum to American food.  The ONLY thing I didn't like was I felt the pad Thai noodles were a bit dry that's all.

There is a wait depending on when you go.  We went around 1250 and it was an hour wait.  But the cool thing is you can leave your name and # and theyll text you it's your turn to sit! It's awesome! 

Oh and they take your picture before you sit too and you have the option to buy them. 3 pictures and a case for $35. 

Definitely a MUST GO buffet here!!

Once again I'm writing this review as I'm setting in the restaurant.

This restaurant easily would've gotten five stars, except, once again, the drink service is abysmal. The attached picture is how my first glass of iced tea looked after my appetizer plate and then dessert.

 I would give you the waiter's name, except I haven't seen him or he hasn't come close enough to me since he brought me that first glass of iced tea. A second glass of iced tea sure would've tasted good with dessert, and most likely with my meal. 

I must have a sign on my head that says ignore this guy. Oh well, it saved me several dollars in tips!

I'm not a buffet person but I'm also Asian which means that even though I don't like buffets, due to family obligations I have had to sit through my fair share of vegas and non-vegas buffets so I can honestly say that my opinions are pretty valid.

We were really worried about the buffet line because it was a holiday weekend but we had a party of 8 and were saved from waiting in line. For parties of 6 or more they charge you 18% gratuity but in exchange for that you get into the big group line and we were ushered in after a 20 minute wait at most.

If you are traveling in a smaller party though, the line did seem horrendous. At 2pm the kiosks were telling folks to come back at 9:45pm.

We sat down around 11:30 for the holiday brunch. There are various stations from around the world.

While there was a lot of variety nothing really stood out as top notch and I tried a lot of the different items. For example: prime rib-overcooked, crab legs-on the small side, lobster bisque-too salty, sushi-not much variety etc. 

The dessert options were probably my favorite as I tried at least 15 different desserts.

For close to $75 a person ($60 + gratuity) I can think of better ways to enjoy a meal. Try it for yourself if you must but consider yourself adequately warned!

This is the most overhyped restaurant I've ever been to. The line is way too long for how mediocre this food is. They try to be upscale with their selection and set up, but the quality of food does not live up to it. I was very disappointed with mostly everything. 

The American Wagyu was bland and it took too long to get a cut, so by the time I got to my table, my vegetables were cold. However, I wouldn't have eaten them anyway because they had a rancid fish taste to them. If you do want sides, pick them up after you get whatever meat you choose. The tomato bisque was pretty rancid tasting, too. It actually tasted how dirty gym bags smell. The only beef that was well seasoned was the tri tip beef, but my cut was way over done. 

Even the desserts were terrible. I got a little sample of some of them, and tried a bite of them. The cheesecake tasted like it was beyond it's expiration date, the cookie was bitter, and various other desserts tasted off. I have no idea what was going on with the desserts, but I would not want to eat any of them again. None of them were worth a second bite. No one in my group finished any of the dessert except the fresh apple. 

The best part of my meal was the coffee, the cooked Salmon, and the Creme brûlée. They weren't delicious, but they were the best of what I tasted. I did not eat all of anything I put on my plate. More than half the food I tried didn't get a second bite. I was expecting a delicious meal for how popular this place is, but I left feeling like my time, and my money was wasted. I could have eaten something quick on the strip and felt more satisfied. 

My husband never complains about food and he always finishes what's on his place, but even he couldn't eat their food. It has got to be extremely terrible for him to turn away food. I've never seen him so dissatisfied with a meal and I've burned his dinner more than once. 

If you are very hungry, you enjoy standing in line after line, and you want to eat a pile of mediocre food, this is for you. If you like to enjoy your food and want something of quality, not quantity, this is not the place for you. I read that this is the best buffet in Vegas. If that's the case, I'll skip any buffet next time.

Not good service. Wait in line to wait in line to wait in line. First you come and have to registrar on a computer. Then you have to wait in line for an hour. While in line they take all the smaller parties in front of you. Don't know why they do that. Just push a table together. Then after you finally get to pay then you wait in another line to be seated. Not a good system. The older woman at counter Valerie was rude. My 2 daughters were in the bathroom and she would not help me until they came to the counter. That is ridiculous. The when I asked why she kept talking back to me.  They after that she talks about me to another worker named  Rosa. Then when we said why are you talking she lied and said she was not talking about me.

My husband and I came here two weekends ago on a Saturday for dinner.  It was our first time.  My good friend Gustavo recommended this place.  It's kinda pricy but worth it!!!  They had an abundant variety of delicious food from Asian, Italian, Mexican  and American food.  My husband was very pleased and so was I.  Everything was tasty.    I just wish they had more variety of shrimp and was hoping they would serve lobster.  The decor was beautiful and the restaurant was very clean.  Our server Guadalupe was wonderful.  She definitely provided exceptional service with a smile.  Thank you Guadalupe! I did approach Michael the manager (who was pleasant also) about how wonderful Guadalupe was I hope she was recognized.  We will most definitely come to this fabulous buffet again on our next trip to Vegas.  Thanks for everything!

Best buffet on the strip! i came in january (off peak season) on a weds afternoon at 4:30pm and there was no wait. they start serving dinner at 3pm, so if you'd like to skip the lines, i would recommend dining at an earlier time. The dining room is spaciously laid out and very comfortable. service is attentive. If you HAVE to wait, go explore the shopping area of caesars palace, or take a nap poolside (that's what we did) :D

choose wisely what you eat..
there's a lot to choose from and it's easy to be swooned by the individual sized baskets of fried calamari, onion rings and fried chicken but beware! they're delicious, but best to share these.. 

the stars of the show are definitely the raw oysters, king crab legs, seafood salad, prime rib, oxtail, nigiri sushi platter, paella, and THE DESSERT BAR. 

do yourself a favor and take a walk around the dessert bar BEFORE you eat everything else. It'll help you gage how much room to save for dessert, and trust me, you'll want to. this is by far the most beautiful spread of sweets i've seen at a buffet. everything is made with meticulous care. My favorites are the black rice pudding, matcha cake, warm pecan pie (add a scoop of gelato on top!) and chocolate covered strawberries. 

even if you hate buffets (i'm not usually a fan), this one is worth a try!

+ THE FOOD
Definitely one of the best buffets I've ever had but the Memorial Day holiday pricing was just ridic. From what I had heard, their weekend buffets have a huge variety of foods to choose from- lobster, steak, etc etc. While there was still a lot of different foods when we went, it wasn't as spectacular as I had imagined. Some notable dishes that I liked included their crab legs (both chilled and freshly steamed), shrimp, crispy pig, and DESSERTS. I loved how their crab legs were sliced in half so you could easily get the meat without making a huge mess. I was hoping they would have more meat than usual but it seems like they just focused on their seafood dishes more. The desserts were definitely the highlight of the meal. There were so many different things that I liked- creme brulee (so vanilla-y and creamy), white chocolate matcha covered strawberries, tiramisu cup, pandan jelly/pudding, and much more. There was no wait when I went around 4:30-5 PM which was a huge plus. The place wasn't very crowded since I went a bit earlier than usual dinner time. I would definitely give this another try but definitely not on a holiday weekend and they have more of a typical menu.

I thought it was a bit overhyped. I kinda had high expectations. I was slightly disappointed by their variety and selections.  They did have a lot, but I don't think they had enough for the amount we had to pay. It was around 50-60 for lunch.  They had selections from Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Italian, Mexican, etc. I was amazed with the street style taco thing they had.  I just wished they had a bit more than the typical stuff you get from each type of cuisine. 

Overall, I did enjoy my meal. Service was efficient and friendly.
I've been to a lot of buffet places but this one is the best of the best, you will love their selection and they have so many delicious food here. YOU WILL LOVE IT great seafood selection

I have tried The Buffet in Wynn, and the buffet in Mandalay Bay, both of them are good. But the buffet in Caesars is definitely the best! But the price is a little higher than others. $45.39 per person, tax included.

I first tried the buffet at Rio and that was great. The next night we tried the this buffet, and this buffet is unbelievable. The food is so fresh and high quality. Also, this is the only buffet that has fresh oysters. The cocktail shrimp is huge tiger shrimp and the crab is pretty cut so it was so much easier to eat. There were so many food options that we couldn't taste it all without getting full first. The buffet is probably the busiest in Vegas so we had to wait about an hour and fifteen minutes to get seated ( an hour waiting in line then 15 minutes after paying to get to our seats) The area we were eating was really clean and well kept. The bus boys were always on the move cleaning the tables. Servers refilled our drinks fairly slowly but it was busy so it's reasonable. Try the ribs, steak, crab, desserts, in general: everything.

This buffet was worth every single penny. It was amazing. The choices they have were great, they had everything you can think of. Every single food I tasted was great and so fresh/good quality. I would tell everyone to go there. I don't think anyone will be disappointing. There is something for everyone here. There is a reason its the highest rated buffet.
Amazing amazing amazing!! The wagyu beef was so delicious it melted in my mouth, wished I could stay in here for hours

Don't get me wrong there were definitely several very appetizing dishes during lunch, namely the pesto pasta the selection of cheeses, and possibly some more that I forgot. The seafood options which I can't eat also seemed appealing, and the selection size was pretty good. However, there were also some that were mediocre and what you would expect from a buffet half the price, including the vegetarian Chinese dishes (can't comment on the meat ones), the pizza, and several of the desserts.

Went here for dinner on the Indepdence day weekend after watching a lot of YouTube videos about this buffet. Price got marked up for special holidays, but we didn't care that much. However, the food was nowhere near our expectation (at least for the price that we paid for). No comments on the Japanese station. You could get better sushi elsewhere. Same thing for The Chinese food station. The meat station was not great as well. But the seafood station is decent. There's a variety of seafood to choose from, e.g. lobsters, king crab legs, oysters, scallops, etc. The dessert bar has a lot to choose from as well. Truffle mushroom soup was a hit for me. I also liked the ice cream bar. They have both classic and unique ice cream flavors. Loved the lemon basil and rum ones. Give this buffet a try if you're a seafood and dessert lover. Other than that, I don't think it's worth paying $90 for just average steak and sushi.
This would have to be a top place on my list. I can't believe they got rid of comp champagne Sunday brush :/  I'm not sure if it's always worth the wait even with diamond member card

Absolutely awful.  After waiting for 2 hours after getting a ticket, we came back and waited almost another hour waiting to actually enter the buffet.  The receipt says that you have two hours to eat.  We got in around 10 and they started taking food away at 10:45.  And the food that was out there was not all that great.  They had crab legs that were still frozen out there.  This was the one thing my mom wanted to do on our visit and it was a humongous disappointment.  They weren't ready for the crowd and we felt cheated and misled because we should have been able to eat until midnight if you let us in at 10 even if you say your hours are until 11.  If you aren't going to allow that, then you need to convey that to the consumer.  I have to wonder what happened to the groups even behind us.  Will never return here again!  Awful!

This place has since went down hill with their quality and variety of food.. we see much less choices in sushi, soups, seafood are all cut down 20-30% what use to be. Crab legs quality is bad, tasteless soggy and much smaller. Sample of cut they made.. the clay pot chicken soup.; substitute with tasteless flower egg soup, crepe is no longer made when you order...Oyster not served during lunch only after 3pm. Chinese soups is plain and tire looking.. so disappointing how bad this has come down ..for nearly $50 a person plus the wait time.. there is better choices in VegAs... did I mention the $45 express fee to cut the line? Still expect 30 min to wait for your table ..ouch!

Probably the best buffet on the strip! Definitely worth the calories and price! I would splurge on this buffet because of the quality and variety. The seating area sits 600 but it doesn't really feel that crowded. There was a large selection of cuisines from Asian to Italian to Mexican (made to order tacos!) The staff are attentive and Pepsi products are included in the price! Please be sure to tip your waiters (at least something!), as there were many parties around us that did not. 
Valet parking is available in the front of Caesars Palace and self parking is available as well. 

Enjoy and do not skip dessert! Freshly made crepes with toppings are delightful!
