Party of 4, we paid $190 since my youngest daughter was only 4. For the price we paid I honestly thought it was just okay. Many varieties but the quality was mediocre. My daughter had the rib it was so dry and hard she couldn't even bite it. But the oyster... Omg it was so gross!!! It wasn't even fresh and fishy... I'm hoping I won't get food poisoning from the 1 oyster I ate. Sorry Bacchanal, was looking forward to eating there was it was a BIG disappointment. Booooo.

Went for our family Christmas dinner and regret it, a big chaos. Wait time is 2-3 hours, so if you want to have dinner at 6 or 7 need to start stand in line 3 or 3:30, I was told to register at kiosk for the preferred dining time, but it is meaning less, later on found out they let anyone come in to the line.
It cost around $70 with taxes, but the quality of the food is poor. Snow crab legs are very salty it could cause kindly failure, the so call sushi are 3rd class rolls, they only have small tray of nigiri did not look good either and once it is out people stand in line for it. Baked shrimp came out very slow sure enough there is a line. Prime rib and lamb chops are just ok. 

I've had buffet at other places, can't say here is better, I think it is over priced, for $70 per person there are better choices, it really worth $40 consider food quality, services, and dinning environment, and the rest of the money we are paying for their advertisement. If you just want to have  buffet food go to any one around Las Vegas changeing 30-40 and you will enjoy same type of food. 
DON'T BE FOOLED BY THEIR PRETTY PICTURES!

This buffet is crazy! Living in Vegas, it still is a treat to come to the strip and do some touristy things, and Bacchanal is definitely one of those things on the list! A must try for buffet lovers. The waiter told us that there were 540+ food options to choose from. The weekend brunch is $49.99 which goes from 8am-3pm. (Cheaper on weekdays) It is well worth it for the different foods & such. Prime rib, king crab legs, lots of truffle oil foods, desserts, Asian food, Italian, Mexican, anything you can think of, it's here. Atmosphere is nice, loud, and the restaurant itself is pretty. You may have to wait awhile to sit down. I really enjoyed it, but to me it was not a 5 star experience. It was good, not "Oh my God!" The selections were wow, but the quality was still somewhat buffet-like, which is expected. I will be back!

This buffet is probably the best buffet if you visit Vegas but beware it is EXTREMELY pricey especially on weekends. It is a lot better than Wicked Spoon (that place is overhyped for no good reason). Prices at bacchanal ranges from 45-55. 

It tends to get really crowded. Wait time is usually 1-2 hours during the weekends. 

Food selections are great. There are so many good selections you can choose from and they're actually all really good. I focused mainly on eating the crab legs because it was so good! It can be a little messy eating it but it's worth it. Also the juices in the little containers are good and they have many different varieties. Other food that I thought was good was the eggs Benedict. It was nicely made and just right. Sushi was good but not exceptional. Sliders were great! 

Service was attentive and great. Our waiter was on top of things and made sure our used plates and drink refills were taken care of. 

Definitely a must go to buffet in Vegas. It's a bit pricey but it's a lot better than other buffets in this area.
Love this buffet went for brunch soo many options even freshly squeezed orange juice my top buffet in vegas by far!!!

Better than last time and it was already pretty amazing! 
I loved everything but my absolute favorite was that mandarin yuzu desert!

Came for the fame, and it did not disappoint! (other than my wallet... oh god). 

$50+ and I think their price is going up every year!

This place is HUGE, I get lost at where I am sitting for the first few times getting food back to my table. Nice decoration, they design it into sections and each section gives you different atmosphere. Ambiance is a little darker than my liking. 

Service is great, attentive and courteous. They would swap your drink even before you finish your previous glass. Nothing to complain and meets my expectation of a buffet this price range. 

Food quality definitely superb! With varieties from various parts of Asia, Europe, and America. Their cookware are all super expensive Le Crueset or Staub. Fresh seafood, and GET THEIR WARM KING CRAB LEG near the pizza section. From many posted pictures in yelp you can already tell they give you TONS. Desert is good, their gelato is okay not the best I've had, but I am very picky when it comes to desert. 

My dilemma when eating here is that since I'm paying so much already, I feel like I intentionally skipping all of the food that seems cheaper to make and will fill you up (carbs), like fried rice, taco, bread, hotdog... etc. However, I know I'm also missing out quite a lot because they could taste wonderful. And seafood is... just seafood. They are fresh, and high quality, but other buffets for $10 or $20 cheaper will have the similar seafood as well. So its a struggle to decide what to pick up to eat if you only have one chance. Maybe they should raise the price a little more, but make it a one-day-pass sort-of deal. So you don't have to stuff yourself up so quickly and can have more time enjoying all of the dishes. 

Oh they change their dishes every other hour or so, so sit for a little longer, you might find something new.

We hotel hopped during our stay in Vegas. We stayed at the Palazzo which was perfect but they didn't have a buffet? Eating at a Vegas hotel buffet was one of things on my to do list. 

My brother in law wanted to check out this buffet because of the great reviews and 4 1/2 star rating. This buffet is located in Caesar's Palace.  

We were able to get in the line right after their usual peak time hours which is reportedly around 2-3pm (Google it). The host also confirmed that we arrived at a good time.

Upon first entering the restaurant you are directed to pay first and then you jump into another line and wait to be seated.  Even though there was a fairly long line, they moved us through it very quickly. 

They have bathrooms conveniently located right in front of the buffet line. We had a party of 4 and we were discussing how great it would have been if there was a waitress walking around to offer you adult drinks while you're waiting....just saying...I mean its Vegas.

After being seated our waitress came to promptly get our drink orders before round 1 of this amazing,  delicious buffet.

So, my first impression was wow. They had such a vast variety of dishes and I really didnt know where to start! 

Let's just say it was definitely worth it. Their desserts were just as impressive as their food. I usually don't have room for dessert but didn't want to not at least try it. Especially the cheesecake cake pop...omg that was heavenly. It had little espresso like sprinkles on top (see my pic). 

All of us were fully satisfied- literally.

I've been to many Sunday brunches but this takes the cake. The food is outstanding. There are about 8 stations including a BBQ station, Asian food, Mexican, pasta, seafood and more. Don't load up on the junk like pizza and burgers. Go for the high priced cuts of meat and seafood including stone crab claws and oysters!  And the desert table: OMG! It's about $42 a person, which is pretty reasonable considering all the food you're getting. You can add $18 for all you can drink but it's not worth it unless you like crap beer like Coors or Michelobe. You can also buy a-la-carte drinks.

I came here on the thanksgiving holiday with family. The line was crazy. The place was very clean and elegant. There're many seafood dishes but not place in a attractive way. The oyster don't seem fresh( maybe coz it's holiday season ) however, I was happy with their snail dish; It was very special and delicious; and fresh squeezed orange juice. I think the price is too high for what they offer. I don't might to come again...

I'm a Vegas local and I will admit I'm pretty reluctant to go to the strip just to have a buffet dinner, however I was urged to go. It's pricey, but if you are like me and my boyfriend and can ignore the fact your stomach is telling you "Stop, enough, please... no more" it's worth it. Like most buffets (in my option) this is set up so it's wrapped around the dinning area, I can never find my seat. The only thing that I wasn't too pleased with was I had to wait almost 10 minutes for drawn butter, for my crab legs, which ended up causing a line of people. Everything was wonderful in terms of the food, quality, and service. I will have to say I LOVED our little Italian waiter who delighted us with short stories about NY (where I'm from), even with story time he was quick and efficient as well as super friendly. I wish I remembered his name because he was delightful. Overall a very very good dinning experience especially for a buffet.

*First let me say that my 3 stars is only because of the quality of the food. 

I was looking forward to breakfast since I received the suggestion from the concierge. I double checked reviews prior to getting a reservation and it seemed to be inline with reviews I read. 

I had a group of 8 and our breakfast came out to about $300 + without tip. I don't mind paying that kind of money for a great dining experience, to bad this wasn't worth it.

The food hands down was fabulous and the selection was unparalleled but sadly SERVICE WAS OUT THE DOOR.

We arrived at 735am and they are suppose to open at 730am. When we got there they had about 15 others in front waiting to get it. 2 employees were at the checkin desk and the stantions were down so everyone proceeded to walk up to the desk, out of nowhere another employee said " Get back ,Get back...you are not to go this way." 

All of us confused , went back to the line and waited while the checkin employees chatted and even one was talking about watching the Hunger Games movie with a friend last night??? So rude. 



- Our actual server who took our drink order was friendly but not sure if I would have gave the additional $64 bucks that was added to our bill considering he just dropped off coffee and OJ then refilled once.
-At each food station some things were clearly marked as to what it was and others not. I went to where the Mexican food was served and asked about what was inside the burrito. The chef was again rude and shirt with me when explaining. 
-Then when I went to the crepe station there was a young girl there who was rude when I asked what the filling options were, she said there right here and still didn't tell me what they were. 
-Lastly, when I asked for the restroom they did not have one inside you had to leave the restaurant and go out to the casino area to use it. paper towels were everywhere, water all over the sink and no soap. 

Again great food awful service with every interaction. Would not go back or recommend this place. I will stick with the buffet at The Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan. That is place is worth it!

Visited December 2015

I went to Bacchanal Buffet with a group of nine for lunch, which was priced at $36/person!  They have a wide selection of food from seafood, pasta, Japanese, Chinese, and etc.... 

FOODS & BEVERAGES
----------------------------------------
- Watermelon Juice - YUMMY! Bacchanal had a wide variety of juices in "cute" little bottles! (We were told that their juices is only offered during lunch not dinner, so by 3:30 PM they were off the counter!)
- Shrimp cocktail - Fresh shrimps, but the cocktail sauce was just OKAY!
- Raw Oysters - YUMMY & really fresh!
- Ceviche - Served in a small shot glass, very yummy!
- Seafood Salad - Very good! Another must try! 
- Clams - Grab a small bucket of these bad boys! They're good!
- Mussels - A bit too dry.... I didn't enjoy it as much!
- Oyster Shooters - Spicy... it's just O-K!
- Caesar Salad - Fancy serving of Caesar Salad in a bowl! The bread was good too!
- Waffle fries - Good!
- Mac & Cheese - They had a new batch when I got mine! Warm and delicious!
- Prime Rib - Get this! You won't be disappointed! Don't forget to add some veggies. 
- Turkey Sausage - Good!
- Watermelon & Cheese Salad - Very good!
- Mini Burger - delish!

DESSERTS
----------------------------------------
- Vanilla Creme Brulee - WAYYYY TOO WATERY. Wasn't good at all!
- Chocolate Creme Brulee - Not the most appetizing looking thing on the dessert section, but it was very yummy if you like that chocolate mousse taste!
- Mini Oreo Chocolate Mousse - Very Sweet!
- Caramel Flan - I liked the texture and the caramel syrup!
- Watermelon and Mint Gelato - It's like a watermelon mojito in a gelato form :X 
- Macaroons - Great selection of different flavors! I was full by the time they brought out the macaroons, so I was only able to eat two! Not bad!

Overall, Bacchanal Buffet is worth the price! They have a huge selection of food & I enjoyed most of the food I got, but had to skip some of their dishes because they did not look appetizing AT ALL! Their sushi selection didn't look fresh and their poke bowl just looked bleh. One of my friends had to spit out the poke and warned me not to get it cause the fish didn't taste right (AND SHE LOVES SEAFOOD MORE THAN I DO). This buffet also ensures great service with their friendly staff! 

Make sure you save room for desserts! I'd definitely come back here in the future.

A bit spendy compared to other buffets in the area, but it's not comparable to any other buffets in the area!!  This one is absolutely phenomenal!  And really what 5 star steakhouse can you dine for less that $60 per person for dinner, including dessert?  Not to mention this is all you can eat!  And it's less than $40 for breakfast and brunch, and this is when they have fresh squeezed juices- even veggie juices, red velvet pancakes, crab avocado melts, and made to order omelettes!  Kobe beef sliders, crab legs, sushi and the most incredible display of desserts I've ever seen, is what's for dinner!  Of course there's way more than just seafood, this buffet is HUGE!  But I'm a seafood lover soooo, that's about all I notice! 

One of the chef's came out to deliver our seafood platter and agreed to have his picture taken with his masterpiece creation!

It was recommended by many friends to try out Bacchanal Buffet in the Caesars Place.  We arrived at about 3:30pm on a Thursday, just missing the lunch prices, but there was no line so we decided to have a very early dinner.

The prices were a bit steep but considering the extensive selections of food items you get, it's worth it. They have Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Mexican, Soups, Salads, Seafood, Meats, and Desserts... pretty wide selections. 

There was a lot of things I've never tried before... because I was at a buffet, I decided to try a lot of things that I don't usually eat.  Wow, what a great way to try new things.  Everything that I got was so good... My favorite was the escargot in the sauce. Mmm!!! The only disappointment on the buffet was the meat carving station... I tried several of the meats and they were all hard to chew or dry... they need to up their standards a little more if they are charging an arm and a leg for the buffet.  

The interior of the seating area was really nice.  We sat in a large booth for the 6 of us in our party.... they put us right next to the desserts! LOL. The selection of desserts were amazing too!!! 

Bacchanal is a must try if you're in Vegas... just to say you tried it. Hopefully by then, the restaurant will up their quality of meats.

Decided to try Giada's new restaurant at the Cromwell for Sunday brunch, heard such good things about it we had to give it a try. We get there and the wait is about 2 hours away! Well next time we will not go on a weekend and will call for a reservation first. So what is our next choice? Well, Ceasar's Palace is just across the street for the highly touted Baccanal buffet. We get to the entrance and what do we see? some kind of "fast pass" system like they have at Disneyland, the machine says to register for a line ticket and wait time it between 58 to 68 minutes. Really?! they have it at such an exact science that they know it will be 58 minutes? not 47 or 61 minutes? oh wait, if you don't want to wait with the masses they will let each person in for $20 more! What a deal huh?
What is the strategy here? we can't let you in right now or even let you try your luck and wait in line....hey! what shoulld you do with a hour to kill inside a casino? gamble maybe?
So at the Baccanal buffet you can't even wait in line to see if maybe by some kind of miracle you get in within 1/2 hour or ? Overall, diners beware you can't just walk in, you are put into a take a number system, unless you want to pay the toll to get in now.

I  gave it a 4 star because of our great service we received from our server named Jung. She gave excellent customer service! Otherwise it's a 3 star for food and atmosphere.  Service was not good with our servers from our last 10 previous dining. It seemed like they were understaffed. Specially the Hostess that takes you to your table.  One of them was not friendly.  She had seated us several times in the past.  A couple of times we had a simple request of a different table.  She was not accommodating.  Tables were too close to each other.  Difficult to maneuver through when bringing your food to your table. The best items were the awesome Bone Marrows halves,  fantastic Truffle Mushroom Pizza,  Crepe Station and Meat Carving station.  The rest of the food is good.  Food presentation was great. Please revisit the Mexican food station selection.   Also, please add more better selection to the Dessert bar and back the Mochi Ice cream!  We tried to come for Brunch and Dinner to see if it's available.

Not worth  $60pp...it haf decent selection but the high price goes to the fresh seafood.  An abundance of crab legs, shrimp and claws so thats a plus, but the line just to get some was outrageous. The chicken sausage was good as well as the crepes. But not much else other than crab legs

I don't like buffets.  There... I said it.  Long lines. Mediocre food.  IKEA tables.  So why review Bacchanal?  Because I can do what I want.  This is America, pal.  I also visited several buffets while on a recent trip, so... I'll give you my worthless feedback.

I tried the lunch buffet at Caesars, Cosmo, Aria, and M Resort.  Bacchanal is the only buffet I've ever enjoyed.  The line moved quickly.  The food was fantastic (the brisket was the highlight).  The decor was decent... for a buffet.  Would I go back?  Yes.

WOW! I'm not going to lie, it is pretty pricey, $54.99. But the service, the atmosphere and the vibe and especially the food are amazing! I've never seen baby lamb rib at buffets and they had it! Absolutely amazing! Definitely worth the money and the visit!

I really really wanted to like this place but unfortunately, it got overhyped for me. The line was insanely long but that was to be expected for 12:30pm on a Saturday. We paid the extra $25/person for express which allows you to skip the entire line. This also included the bottomless mimosas which was a nice touch. My bf really wanted King crab but unfortunately, they only has snow and stone crab. I called ahead of time but guess I should've specified. I was really looking forward to fresh oysters but they didn't have any. Guess it's a dinner only thing? Some items were better than others, but what stood out was the prime rib. It was painfully dry! I was so disappointed! The brisket had more juice to it. I did like the desserts and how they have a crepe station. We both agree that we like Wicked Spoon better because we feel like that have better quality but slightly less options. After all of this, the worst part of this experience is that I got FOOD POISONING! I've only had that once in my 26yrs of being alive! My bf was ok. We couldn't pin point what it was from but the only items that I had that he didn't was the mimosa and shrimp cocktail. After eating, my stomach felt weird but I thought it was just from me eating more than what I usually eat. I just felt weird the rest of the day but it was a terrible night for me. Waking up every 30min to throw up! My bf was really shocked and has never seen me that sick. What bums be out is that I wasn't able to to anything the next day (which is today) and put a damper on our trip. I was hoping to have a nice time in Vegas before I start my new job tomorrow but sadly, I'm spending it sick in bed (and the bathroom, yuck!) Sorry to say, but I will not be returning to Bacchanal :(
Amazing, high quality buffet! Definitely recommend you try the tacos which are prepared fresh to order. Service could have been a little better in terms of refills and condiments.

I sampled a lot of the items and nothing really stands out as good. But a few did stand out as BAD. 

It's not a bad buffet but it could've been better. They could've had some sashimi. 

Steamed crab was overcooked and some were on the tray with no crab meat in it. 

I think the cocktail shrimp was the only item that was "expensive " during brunch which I enjoyed.  

A few items were VERY salty and I love salty food! Fried chicken and pork belly were salty. The porkbelly was especially salty! I had to spit it out. That's how bad it was. The porkbelly was chewy not soft like how a sliced of braised porkbelly should be! 

Cheese selection was sad. Logs? Really? 

DON'Ts: fried chicken, porkbelly and meatballs (wayyyy too dense and no flavor in the meat. I can make a better one with my eyes closed). Flan  (too dense).

DOs: Get a bottomless drink. Hit the dessert island. Clam chowder (not to die for but good).

Overall an okay experience.  I went in at 1:30pm during the week. No lines. Service was fast and good. 

If you're EVER in Myanmar you must have Sunday brunch at The Market  (my last great buffet experience at a hotel). Only $25 usd and there's seared foie gras made to order!

Best all you can eat so far and I've been to a lot of buffets here. Like all buffets in Las Vegas be prepared to wait a long time (unless your a 7 star member) of course. Huge selection of food, they have a lot of different dishes other buffets don't offer. That's why it's my favorite. They even had pho' and their taro dumplings were heavenly! I want to go everyday lol.

Came here at 2:30 pm on a Friday.  No wait and the price was about $38/pp with soft drinks included. 

Unlike other buffets I've been to it seemed that the employees here make an effort and know what they're doing so things moved along pretty efficiently. 

This buffet exceeded my expectations.  We ate as lunch moved to dinner, so that was kind of an unplanned bonus.  Standout items:

+ Seafood of all sorts: crab legs, claws, cold shrimp, mussels meunière (BEST DISH), sea bass (2nd BEST), sole.  Their seafood offerings are vast and everything was fresh with the mussels tasting amazing. 

+ Soups: I'm big on soup and had lobster bisque, truffle soup, mushroom.  All were great. They also have pho, laksa, ramen, hot and sour, but I didn't try them. 

+ Chinese offerings: Maybe a waste of stomach space, but I always need some Chinese and it was surprisingly good.  Broccoli beef, sweet & sour chicken, egg rolls, cream cheese wontons, YUM! 

They have the obligatory Italian section which I skipped, tacos to order, carving station meats along with American sides like beans, potatoes, creamed corn, sliders, pork belly, charcuterie/cheese, sushi, oysters, the list goes on forever. 

Dessert blew my mind. I'm usually disappointed, but in this case overindulged.  The rum cake, tiramisu cup, chocolate cake lollipop were all good and I even pocketed a handful of taffy for my purse.  Score!

I highly recommend coming here. I used to prefer The Buffet @ The Wynn, but this one is my new favorite.

Came on a Thursday night around 8:00 pm.  Probably waited less than 20 minutes.  Compared to how much food costs in Vegas in general I think Bachannal is a excellent deal.  The crab legs and shrimp cocktail were really good.  The oysters on the other hand were pretty bland.  i really liked the wagyu beef slider but it does fill you up.  Also there was a polento thing with truffles which was crazy good.

After eating here,  I was really glad i didn't buy the Buffet of buffets.. i could not imagine eating anything else for at least 24 hours.

Located in Caesars, this is one of vegas' busiest and most popular buffets. 

The cost to dine is $55 per person and one should be prepared to wait around two hours to be seated.  In addition,  there is a two hour limit once seated at the table. 

We came here for brunch and had a great experience. The cost is less than a typical vegas meal especially when you factor in the complementary champagne and mimosas. 

The servers were incredibly nice and ensured we had all the beverages we needed and that our finished plates were cleared. 

Our favorite food items were...  The crab legs,  brisket,  chicken and waffles, pork belly,  flan, Apple pie and ice cream.
The best buffet I have so far. Great selection here. They have crab leg, oysters, clams, and my favorite- lamb chops! The best part is their desserts. Love their presentation, beautiful!
Overpriced given that you have to wait in line for a while to get food, which is cold by the time you get to your seat. The food is pretty good, but I wouldn't call it anything special.

This is the best buffet in Vegas. They got a large variety of food which is more than what you expect. They have international food here and they taste authentic. All food are warm and super fresh. Their desserts rock!!

We are not much of buffet fans, but if you are going to hit a buffet, it should be this one. A little pricey but for the quality it should be expected. Had the prime rib and lamb chops were on back order-sushi was good but the rolls I liked went quickly. The desert selection was excellent. The wait was kind of long, but it was very good. our waiter brought our drinks quickly.

Wow, wow !!!!  This buffet is unbelievable!! You can't leave without having the slider, so good.  You don't know when to start or end with this buffet. Very good pasta, meat, seafood & everything.  Go very hungry !!!!

Was very excited to make this meal the star of our vacation after reading so much about it being the best buffet in Las Vegas. Went for brunch on 12/23 and had holiday pricing.  There was a lot to chose from but everything was cold when tried it. The food was bland and had a smaller desert selection than our local hometown casino. Maybe they changed it for the holidays but it was a let down.

TLDR: Pretty good pricey buffet with a lot of options. Quality of food ranges from not-so-great to amazing depending on what you eat.

Came here for brunch with my friends while we were in Vegas. I am pescitarian so I didn't any of the meat based foods, but below are some of my impressions on the foods that I did try/remember by section. 

(Cold) Seafood Section: Don't waste your time here. They have an assortment of seafood on ice over here, and some seafood based dishes. I tried the rolled sole (literally sole... rolled... into a roll) and it wasn't great, neither was the crayfish. They also have crab, but if you keep walking and you'll find a different section later on with freshly boiled crab.

Breakfast Section: Lot's of fancy looking breakfast foods. They have baby pancakes, eggs Benedict, piles of french toast, bacon, etc. I'm pretty sure the taco station is over here too. I didn't really eat anything here because I don't like breakfast food and they didn't have veggie/fish tacos. I hear that the tacos are worth a try though.

Boiled Crab Station: Look for the guys wearing purple hats. They'll be standing over some big pots and you have to give them your plate and they'll ladle you some hot, freshly boiled crab. The crab legs are all split vertically in half for you to make it easier for you to eat as much as you can. Although the legs are pre-cut, the crab is still pretty flavorful.

Pizza section: .......I'm not wasting buffet space eating pizza unless it is literally flaked with gold.

Noodle Station (in Asian Section): They have four broths and four types of noodles here. I usually don't eat carby things like noodles (even though I love noodles) because they take up too much valuable space. But their Ramen was AMAZING. They actually use real Ramen, and the texture and flavor is perfect. My biggest regret is not getting more and trying it with the Miso broth. 

Sushi Section: Their sushi is not fresh at all, and there aren't really that many options. The nigiri looks really old and the plates of artistically arranged sashimi look like they're juicing. The taste is still OK, but the quality is obviously not there. If you absolutely have to eat some sushi (like I usually do) grab the hand-rolls because the fish in there was by far the freshest.

Dim Sum Section: Meh, not great, I wouldn't waste too much time here. They do have some Congee in this section which is good way to start.. You can use it to prep your stomach for all the food that's about to come it's way. The Congee is cooked mainland style, so there is no salt or meats in it. You can choose to add a variety of toppings to help flavor it though.

Dessert Section: Pretty amazing, they have a bunch of different desserts and they're pretty much all delicious. They also have one of the best ice cream/gelato sections I've ever seen at a buffet. Luckily, the desserts are all tiny and bite sized. So even if you barely have any room left, you can still try a few of them.

Clearly the best buffet in Vegas. While prices seem a little high, the quality of food is outstanding and everything else the same. Only issue you find here are the rush hour lines for the crab legs and seafood specialties. It's ridiculous how much food there is to choose from, all equally great. Caesars is a proven winner, and this food says it.

I'm often not a fan of buffets.

The idea of stuffing my body with as much food in ratio to the price I paid - the idea is appalling and quite disgusting. Chalk up to the mediocre if not downright abysmal quality of buffets in the Toronto area and that's the reason for my pessimistic appraisal of what a buffet is really all about.

However, having been to The Bacchanal twice in one week - I can safely say that all my life, I have been going to the wrong buffet!

Bacchanal blows every single buffet experience I have had out of the water!  The selection is gargantuan, ranging from fresh shellfish to Asian, to Mexican and the biggest dessert selection I have ever seen!

While pricy, it is 100% worth the value and the money you pay.  After all,  the strip is America's playground if not one of the world's - when on vacation, you can't doubt yourself when spending money.  You can save yourself $1 by signing up for Total Rewards however.

The first night for dinner, we arrived around 7:00pm and was promptly seated by 7:15pm.  Surprising as I've heard that it can be as long as a 2 hour wait!  For the next 3 hours, we stuffed ourselves with nothing but shucked oysters, crab claws and king crab legs.  We hardly tried the other items that were available.  Service was great, as our waters were continually refilled, as was the pop. We didn't have to ask for more!

Our second visit was two days later for lunch at around 12:30pm, again, hardly a wait. If anything, this time the line moved even faster.  No king crab legs, so we got to trying everything else we missed last time!   I was surprise they had Vietnamese pho, and even Japanese ramen!  While not the best pho or ramen I ever had, it was a decent try given the environment.  It won't leave you disgusted, but the soup base for both will leave you satisfied - at least until the real thing!

Notable items other than the aforementioned shellfishes to try are:

- the chocolate mousse
- crayfish, very spicy and sweet!
- the cheeseboard items
- the roasted duck in the Chinese food section
- the fresh cerviche
- the prime rib and lamb chops

Bacchanal is truly an EPIC feast!

Worst Buffet. Came here during Thanksgiving weekend brunch buffet hoping it was special since the prices they charged were the holiday prices. It was nothing special. I've had similar dishes at Red Hawk Indian Casino for little ($19.99).Whoever gave this place five stars must have gotten a free meal. Extremely disappointing experience .
Bacchanal is a go buffet when you are Vegas, but it just seems they don't have too many selection on foods for the $$$, but the desserts are really good!

Wow!
The best buffet I've ever had. 
Located inside the Caesars Palace and with good prices and a lot of variety of food. 

Try this out and you will not be disappointed.

First off you will wait 2 hours in line for very expensive food that is not even close worth the price.  I'm a food snob yes so I know good food from bad and all that think this place has great food must not eat out as much as most people.

1st they advertise ribeye steak.  None to be found.  The prime rib had so much fat it was not edible.  The ribs were so tough to cut even the guy cutting me a piece off had a hard time and eventually gave up and pulled off some old pieces that he had that were tough and not edible.

The sushi were about the only decent things that were on par with most local sushi places.

The deserts were dry and just weren't good at all.

The food is basically Golden Corral Quality at an over priced rate and a 2 hour wait!

Many people that I went with said they would never go back.

Save your money and pay $50 on a better place to eat.  This place was below par.

We went to two different buffets while here and this was definitely the better of the two. Worth the wait and the extra $20. The dessert spread was phenomenal, the Mexican was amazing and the meat section was to die for. I definitely recommend going here.
Really good food! A lot of excellent choices. There's something for everyone. It was definitely worth the price.

Went in at $58.19 per person,  heard a lot of great things about this place, so I had high expectations. With a group of 8, was pleasantly surprised at the variety they had which was expected with 9 kitchens and 500+ menu items. Whether it's a quick fix ox tail pho to waygu sliders and your usual grill meats... Must I add im not much of a brisket fan but rather prime rib,  it was the most tender perfectly cooked brisket I've ever eaten.  Definitely ate my money's worth with quantity and quality.

I think one of the best if not the best buffets in Las Vegas.  Talk about ginormous selection!  There's a seafood station with crab legs, shrimp, ceviche, oyster shooters, miso sea bass, lobster biscuits, a whole meat station with sausage, prime rib, brisket, ham and chicken, a mexican station, a whole other room that has asian food including dim sum, roast duck, chow mein and fried rice, sushi, and cold meats and cheeses, and an italian station with pizza.  Then you have dessert with a made to order crepe station, gelato, ice cream, and various desserts.  Definitely have to pace yourself so you can try a little bit of everything.  I really think this is one of the buffets in Las Vegas that has the most variety and everything was pretty tasty considering it was a buffet!  July 4th brunch was $53 a person so it's not cheap but definitely worth a visit.  Wait wasn't too long for 3...came at around 10:30.  You check in electronically and they will text you when it's ready.

casinos are confusing.  i get lost easy in them and i think that is the point.  there are many buffets in ceasar's palace (as there are in vegas in general) and it would be worth it to make it a point to ask for directions to this particular one.  it's one of the more expensive ones, but it was quite easy to eat through what I thought would be about $35 worth.

buffets are also a new way of life for me with the little one.  while a buffet would not be a first choice for me in general, this one was worth it and it would keep my son happy.  a win-win i will take since i get so few of them.

being that he is a toddler, he was also free.  everything there is done with care.  asian food is decent, though i would skip the sushi.  i don't know if it's my two year long mexican food dry spell, but the carne asada and guacamole is delicious. seafood is plentiful and i was impressed that the braised fish dish was not over-cooked- quite complex (like something i would order as a plated dish).

desserts are prettier than tasty.  that really didn't stop me from sampling extensively.  
we got here early for dinner to avoid a defcon 1 hunger tantrum.  at about 5:30 we waited about 20 minutes to get through the line.  when we left, the line was easily 5 times as long, in which case i would never wait that long for this place with or without the child.

My husband and I were so excited to try this place ,which is touted as one of the best buffets in Las Vegas. What a bunch of hype---well, on this day for sure! The food was mediocre! Boy, did they skimp on the cold crab legs! They were the thinnest ever. I first thought I just got the bottom of the barrel...leftovers, but NOPE, they were just wimpy! The other items were just okay. Remember, this dinner buffet is $60+/person and should be above average. 

The best item on the buffet was the escargot shooter. Now this was first class and exotic! 

Hubby and I agreed...the Buffet at the Bellagio is much better in quality and price.

Worst buffet on the strip.
Seafood was sitting forever even discolored.  The server was rude.  I've been every buffet on the strip and this place provides worst food and service ever.  I've been going to Caesars Palace since 1980 when I was in first grade and the restaurants in there are getting worse and worse although the appearance is getting better.
Don't even try to go there to waist your precious money. You better go to Wicked Spoon, Wynn, M resort or even Rio Seafood buffet.

Buffet Bliss!

I came here with the recommendation of fellow Yelper Rose V. and my experience was super content. Bacchanal Buffet boasts high quality meals from almost all cuisine backgrounds, and I wish I had a second stomach to try them all. Their Asian cuisine was so-so but I don't expect every single station to be a hit. Italian, Seafood, Chinese, Sushi, Carved Meats, Breakfast items... I gotta eat them all! Their dessert section also tasted as amazing as it looked. This place is a little more pricey than they other buffets but it's certainly well worth the cost.

Aside from the awesome food and ambiance, the service is decent. One thing that puzzled me was the wait to get a table. I came for lunch with a friend, and it was not packed at all. Though we were in front, they seated other 3 and 4 tops that were in line behind and to the sides of us. I was kind of confused, but the awesome meal made up for it. Perhaps they wanted to induce increased hunger in their patrons so they'd eat more? 

I have no qualms with that!

We finally did it! After several years we checked of Bacchanal on our bucket list! Please note we are locals and we have eating hundreds of Buffets over our 13 years enJOYing Vegas. Last Thursday, we experienced the BEST Buffet Ever. It was over the top. 

It is unfair to call this a buffet. Yes a Culinary Celebration would be more appropriate, yet still an understatement. Partaking in many of the 500 selections was orgasmic. Needless to say we will return!.

Move over Wynn, I have a new favorite buffet in Sin City. So glad they revamped it, the previous buffet was not good whatsoever. 

Came for Champagne Brunch (~$41) on Saturday. They already had crab legs & shrimp cocktail available. Unparalleled carving station (prime rib, ham, turkey, SLAB BACON, and an assortment of sausages/links - there's also TWO..the other one is around the corner next to the pasta/pizza). Bacchanal also has a mexican food station - making some fresh tacos - yum! 

The Chinese food was also on point. There's even a noodle bar with ramen, pho (yes, pho) and udon! But, they also had a good assortment of guilty pleasure food - tater tots, waffle fries, fried chicken w/ sweet potato fries. OM NOM NOM. 

I caught the transition into dinner and that's when the mussels, oysters (yes, oysters - poor dudes were shucking them right there!), lamb, macarons, MOCHI ICE CREAM!!!! came out. 

Definitely a must-try!

My favorite buffet by far! The rumors are true and yes it may be pricey but it's so worth! (it was a Friday dinner, I believe it was between $55-60) My boyfriend and I came here 2 hours before dinner was over. No line, just waited to be seated which only took 10 or so minutes. The decor, furniture, the ambiance everything was gorgeous. Sorry no picture was taken I was too excited about the food! They have such a huge variety of ethnic foods. And of course each one was good it's not your typical like "ehh they weren't good in this area and they main for this" kind of feel. They put a lot of heart and work into each food item. We were so full and satisfied! I know if I go to Vegas again I should explore other buffets but if this is #1 why would you not come back?!

Amazing dessert section - would give 6 stars for that. Food choice is amazing and there's so much to choose from. Something for everyone at the buffet. Took away a couple of stars as the lady who was showing people from the line to the seats (we went as a group of 5) was pretty rude to our group. Lousy service after paying top dollar leaves a bad taste in the mouth no matter how amazing the food is.

I've been to many buffets in Vegas and Bacchanal and the Wicked Spoon are definitely the top two. The only thing that needs to be improved at the Bacchanal are the GAWD-AWFUL serving utensils, especially the serving tongs near the asian dim sum area. For such a pricey place its astonishing they have such poorly working serving tongs. I get hand cramps just trying to use them and pick up food, many times, its a total struggle to grab food and sometimes they are way.too.hot. The little finger heat pads they pass out are dont work for tongs. The managers in charge of picking and ordering these serving utensils/tongs should try to eat there once and try to get food on their plates with these. This may change their mind and hopefully encourage them to change what they use.

Been a few years since they first opened and wow, how have things changed for the worse, service-wise. Based on the shockingly chaotic system now, you've been warned: avoid this buffet (at least during the holidays). PR disaster here with many visibly frustrated people in the crowds around the buffet, but what does the buffet care? They will ring in the money anyway, despite lots of unhappy people and negative word going around. That's an unfortunate vibe that came off to me.

It's man versus machine. When you walk up to the buffet, there are now rows of ticket machines. No notable sign explaining what these machines are (they're like the Fast Pass machines at Disneyland). You're expected to wade through the crowds and insert your information into the machine and the screen tells you when exactly to come back -- do not expect anything less than three hours! Many of these machines don't even work, so even though you're supposed to get a ticket, they end up telling you that you "don't need a ticket." The system is *supposed to* help spread out/manage the crowds, and it's *supposed to* be your "ticket" in at the allotted time.

But when we come back at the time we were scheduled for and found a worker, he told us that they're not letting any more people in to the buffet even with a "ticket" and that the wait will be another 3 hours (so, a total of 6 hours). There are just "too many people we didn't expect." Wait. So what was the point of scheduling and giving out tickets and waiting the three hours? And why not alert people of the extreme wait times BEFORE they wait the three hours only to be then turned away. After all, the machine took contact information. Why bother with a flawed system that ultimately is much more confusing and chaotic than simply lining up when you get there? Unlike Disneyland's FastPass, this ticket system is a disorganized mess.

Finally, if you try to clarify with any of the few workers here, they respond with curt, smug replies. Maybe it's the holiday stress on everyone, but their demeanor and really lack of service or care is unfortunate and not helping the situation. No answers for anyone.

Family and I were looking forward for another go here, but it looks like we won't ever be trying again.

had the lunch buffet although breakfast was also still available.  Lots of variety of good quality food.  The Chinese Dim Sum food was actually very fresh and good.   Vegetables were cooked just right.  Crab legs were already cracked for you so not too hard to get to the meat part.
Desert choices were fabulous.  The sorbet ice cream was so good.  Just be sure you do not eat so much main courses that there is no room left for dessert.  Only bad thing is that you have to finish in 2 hours.  I was there in mid-May and although crowded, we did not wait but 10 minutes for two people.

The things that are a must-try in no order is the ramen, lobster corn chowder, prime rib, crepe, souffle, lamb chops, peppered beef, and their fried dishes that come in a basket. The way they designed the buffet and their allocation of foods is perfect!

The rest of the dishes are relatively similar to the other buffets in the strip casinos.

This is easily the best buffet in Las Vegas.

The food choices are really vast and there is a lot of options from all different kinds of regions. We went early for their Brunch and loved everything we tried. I have never been to a buffet that has this high of a quality for each item. I tried everything and I would honestly say that 90% of the food was fantastic. Highly recommend this, any other buffet is not worth it in my opinion.

I don't know WHAT could top this buffet. I wish my stomach was detachable so that I could have eaten more and tried everything. This is THE buffet to go to when in Vegas. Hands down, without a doubt! 
For dinner it is about 55 per person. Steep yes, but well worth it my friend, so prep your wallets and stomach accordingly. 
The variety made my head spin, in a good way. There was a seafood station, a taco station with like 3208493908 condiments next door, a bread station with small ramekins of softened butter, a meat station, sushi, chinese food (mainly dim sum), cheese and way way more. 
I just want to write a novel on how great the selection of food is. I mean, not everything is going to amaze you of course, but it's one of those excited to be alive moments at Bacchanal. 
The meat station: So many damn choices. I cried inside. 3-4 kinds of sausage? Do you want prime rib or ribeye (tomahawk chop)? Brisket? Lamb chop? Turkey? Chicken? I'm sure there was more, but my eyes went towards the lamb chops and ribeye. All of the meats I tried were simply seasoned and had low percentage of having been effed up. 
The seafood station: Oyster, king and snow crab, salmon, sea bass and more. You didn't even know you wanted it until you saw it homie. Actual clarified butter, cocktail sauce, lemons, horseradish; THE WORKS. Oh and one of the cooks behind the hot plates asked if I wanted hot crab instead of the ones on the bar. It's the little things that add up :) 
Dessert station: The last point and reminder at which you decide you need it all. Every single damn dessert. Creme brulee, chocolate or vanilla? Gelato...all 20 something flavors yes? Which cake? There are too many kinds that I'm not sure I want, but I actual do want. And more. 
I'd love to elaborate on the other stations, but you get the gist of this place; it's going to shock you even with high expectations like I had. 
The wait was like 40 minutes when I went earlier tonight and the line was long but you wait for quality. Suck it up and complain after, unless all your anger is washed away by the different foods at Bacchanal. 
***ATTENTION YELPERS***
WHEN YOU ARE IN VEGAS, DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME AT ANY OTHER BUFFET. YOU WILL ALWAYS WIN AT THIS ONE. Somehow...just somehow...guaranteed!

While this buffet is quite pricey, if you have a big appetite it does provide a large variety of tasty food. The sushi alone for me was worth the price. They also have seafood, multiple cuts of meat, breakfast food and American cuisine. The service is also very attentive and fast.

One of the best buffet on the strip.  When asking around it seams like most people directed us to try this place out. 

We did wait in line for a bit which is pretty common for any type of buffet around here. (would be nervous if we were able to sit quickly and not many people dining..)  They have an incredible selection of food to try and the food has excellent taste.  They also have many made to order selections, seafood and one hell of a dessert selection. 

Ambiance of the place is impressive and the service staff was top notch. 

This is not your typical buffet, variety is better than others and quality is superior. Bit pricey but worth it.

Couldn't wait to try Bacchanal, last year for Thanksgiving we were also at Caesar's for the Lago which was probably overdue for a $17 million dollar makeover.

With the old Lago, the line took about an hour. This year I figured based upon the reviews, the line for the new, renovated gastronomical rollercoaster ride should take about 2 hrs max. NO.  Are you kidding  me?!?  At 3:26pm on Thanksgiving it snaked around the planter at least 3 times.  I asked the guy how long it would take, he said 3 hrs.  3 hours?!? This buffet better do backflips and somersaults.

For $20 (must be another holiday treat - non-holiday $15?) they said we could take the express line which looked a lot shorter and curved along part of the window and back.  Sure, why not?   Well, the express line took almost 2 hrs!   No complaints at all, the folks who toughed it out in the non-Express line were probably looking at around 4hrs instead of 3hrs.  Anyway, we finally got to our seats and couldn't wait to get started.

It's the special Thanksgiving edition of the Bacchanal, so they had perfectly roasted turkey and ham.  The server carved up the piece of turkey and it tasted incredible, the turkey wasn't dry or overdone, I was pleasantly surprised.  Ham was excellent as well.  I had forgotten I just paid almost $70 per person (express line) with just the first few servings.

Didn't get a chance to try all of the stations.  Guess what? More lines at some of made-to-order stations, lines galore.  So I only tried a few things that just stood out.  The dim sum items were decent.  They had pork dumplings in tiny little foil cups which sat on a steam basket.  They are the tasty small  swirl top dumplings similar to Ding Tai Fung but it's not a fair comparison.  Be careful when you bite into them, they actually retain the hot soup inside. They even had an herbal chicken soup served in a special bowl.  The Hot N Sour soup looked beat up so I left it alone.  Sushi items were sparse but were done decently, their sushi rolls were small but flavorful.  

At the seafood station, the crab legs server was in an especially good mood, he was very friendly to all of the guests.  He says he'll give you a plate of crab legs with a smile in his heart and a smile on his face.  Picked up the cooked shrimp and the salmon was cooked to what you'd expect from a serving from a well-known national chain restaurant.  The lobster chowder soup was a bit sweeter than expected but everything else at the seafood station was top notch.

After feasting on the seafood, the dessert island was a paradise.  For the holiday, they made these pumpkin filled cakes and topped with whipped cream, delicious.  The tiramisu, ice cream, chocolate chip cookie a la mode, and cheesecake really hit the spot.

Service was excellent, the guy was hovering around like a hawk and as soon as we got up  for more food, he swooped in and cleared the plates.

It was well worth the price of admission.  Next time, we won't bother with the other buffets, we all had an unforgettable ride at the Bacchanal and can't wait to be back.

AMAZING YUMMY FOOD !!!

I was there with 3 people and we made sure we did not eat a big breakfast prior to visiting this buffet.  We went late in the afternoon and we made sure to take our time to enjoy the variety of food.  The restaurant looked very beautiful and I was in shock at all the different stations with pretty little mini-plates filled with food.  This place was so huge that I couldn't find my table at first.   It lasted us 2.5 hours to try a little bit from each section. 

First, I did a complete walk through to see what each section offered and then I began to start selecting food from each section.  At first the service was a little bit slower than normal, but then again it was quite busy.  Drinks were not refilled often enough and plates did not get taken away as often as we would have liked.   Some of our plates had only three items because of the adorable mini-plates/bowls/dishes that the food comes in, hence the need to have the plates taken away.  (For example, one fried chicken leg came in a cute mini deep fryer looking container but it took up half the plate.)  I accidentally spilled a cup of ice and could not find anyone to help me clean it up for a little bit.  After awhile, I think more staff arrived and service started picking up.  

All the stations had something yummy, except the Mexican/Latin station.  I've definitely had better authentic food elsewhere.  My friends did like the taco station though.  Dessert station was yummy.  Asian station was delicious.  Fresh hot crab legs were amazing.  I asked for steaming hot king crabs legs and I was told to wait 5-7 minutes by the chef in charge of steaming them.  I decided to take a few steps back while I was waiting and after 5-7 minutes the fresh hot crab legs came out.  Tons of people saw and came.  They pushed by me to get in front of the line.  As I politely waited in the back, the chef told everyone to make space for me to come up first because I was the first one to ask and had been patiently waiting...he remembered.  =)  Great service especially since, the chef was very busy not only taking care of the steaming crabs, but bringing more crabs from the back, passing out cold crab legs, and passing out the other shellfish and seafood to the customers.    

I've been to most buffets in Vegas that are on the strip.  I think the price at bacchanal is crazy expensive in comparison to other buffets, but then again it is Vegas and all those famous chefs did get together to create certain dishes here.  The food is somewhat higher in quality and the variety is nice

Overall, excellent food and great service.  Will go again...just wish the price was a little lower.  Wicked Spoon was number 1 as far as being my favorite but now it's number 2 because Bacchanal is now my new number 1 buffet.

Never been a buffet fan but food was mostly  spot on. Not the biggest fan of their crab but oysters were huge and the crawfish were great. Best time to go is about 200 pm and you can get dinner food as well. Went on a week day and there was no wait at all. Would probably not go back but still enjoyed the experience
Wide selection of food.  The brisket and lamb was delicious.  Very good prepared foods.  King crab legs were good but oysters and stone crabs didn't taste fresh.

Is it worth the hype?  I think so.
I'm not typically a big fan of buffets, cuz I never could eat enough to justify the cost of Vegas buffets.  But if I can pick one to go to, it'd be Bacchanal!
First of all, if you are gonna whine about waiting in line at the one of the most popular buffets in Vegas Strip, then don't go at the peak hours.  I went at 5:00 and waited in line for about 15 minutes before we were seated with a big party.  Also kind of ridiculous, but I think you can pay extra $10 or $20 to get to front of the line like at a club. LOL
Food is excellent!  It feels like you ordered each of the dishes separately not like they were mass produced.  Even stupid thing like a sweet potato tator tots were sooooo good.  They also have fresh oysters in a shell! Yummmmm And no limits!!!  And don't forget to have them warm up your crab/snow crab legs!!!
And their international section- with pho, japanese ramyun! OMG Pho was actually really good and my vietnamese friend even endorsed with stamp of approval! hahaha
And their drink selection is much better than other buffets I've been to (Wynn, Aria, Bellagio, Paris, Planet Hollywood, Mandalay Bay, etc....)
I'm definitely going back!

Amazing amazing amazing!!!! Best meal so far in Vegas! We came for lunch. The American and Mexican station were my favorite with dessert close behind. The pork sliders were incredible!! Really blown away and totally worth the 77$ for both my husband and I! Yum yum yum

Tried this buffet today and mannn was it expensive! It was $53 per person because it was Fourth of July weekend. I highly recommend signing up for the total rewards card which will give you  discount on all the restaurants and shops inside the hotel and other sister hotels. It's completely free and you can accumulate points. It was $49 person after the discount. I was really disappointed because it was not that great, especially for the price! Food was mediocre and the selection was not that great. I like the wicked spoon at Cosmo a lot more. However I did love the virtual line system they have. They text you when your table is ready so you don't have to wait in a long line. You can lose more money in the casino in the mean time ;)
I also saw singer Miguel at the buffet! Made my day! Even famous people like eating at the Vegas buffets :)

This is the best buffet in the US I've ever tried, they have variety of foods, Mexican, Seafood, Chinese, Vietnamese. I love their crabs the most and choices of dessert. However, this place would be much better if the price from 50$ to 40$ becuz no lobster, salmon Sashimi and perhaps better pizzas.

I went to the new Buffett at Caesars tonight with my family and we all raved about it! Sure it's expensive but the quality of food and the multitudes of choices were amazing. The only minor annoyance was when I went back for seconds to the carving station for turkey the server gave me a tiny piece. I continued to hold my plate and said keep going. He did but obviously they have been told to ration second portions. After paying $200 for the four of us I expect to get as much meat as I want!! The new remodel looks great and I'd go back in a heart beat!
One of the best buffets in town..Expensive but definitely worth the $$. The ambiance and the service is top notch! Would recommend to all!
Great food! Will definitely come back when in Vegas. Money spent is worth it. The egg tarts are the besr!

My husband and I got really sick after eating here for  Christmas and reported it to them. It was the only thing we ate the entire day so we knew it was from Caesars. They were unhelpful and refused to give us a refund for the buffet. 
Really bad place to eat. Never going again. And telling our friends not to go either.

Best buffet I've been to. The food was really fresh and presented so cutely!  It wasn't your everyday buffet food. Most of the items were imaginative and all of it was tasty. And that DESSERT TABLE...omg. 

Dishes were cleared quickly, servers were friendly. Price was reasonable, lines moved at a pretty good pace. Decor was gorgeous, with different themes like wood and glass. 

I'm trying to think of a con...um...The lights were kind of dim sometimes...?

I ate here the first year it was open and it was awesome!  Totally worth the price of admission.  Lots of great options, fancy handmade desserts etc.  Went back March 2016 excited to go back and it lousy.  The food wasn't very good, most items were way over salted.  The fancy deserts had been replaced with boring cookie cutter deserts similar to what you would find in any Chinese buffet anywhere in America.  Where are the Mochi Balls?  Service was not very good.  I made the mistake of tipping at the register.  Server was pretty much non existent  after bringing out the drinks.  Never came by to get plates or check if we needed a refill.  I cannot recommend this place going forward.  I realize sometimes you will have a bad experience eating out.  That is understood but when you drop almost $200 for two people everything should be on point.  It was not.
Everything was very mediocre. I don't understand why any one would eat the seafood here because it was watery and not fresh.

This review is strictly for server named Maribel. 

All I wanted was an iced green tea to quench my thirst. 
After she got upset explaining that iced green tea is actually a peach flavored green tea, she only brought out 2 orange juices and 2 glasses of water for my friends. Failed to bring my order of glass water and iced peach green tea that she yelled out "they come in hot or cold! You have to make up your mind!". Umm... I have been asking you for an iced green tea. I went to go have a decent meal and not be an emotional punching bag. 


Had to flag down a different server after waiting 20-30mins. The new server guy was awesome.

I'd give it a 4/5 for a buffet. But 3/5 for food/quality. It was $70!!!18% gratuity for groups larger than 6 (naturally). First plate was Chinese food with half rack of ribs and a waygu beef slider. Second plate was chicken and waffles(did not live up to the hype, honestly reminded me of McDonalds chicken nuggets) with lamb chops. Third pre-cracked crab legs (figured I'd eat those to get my $ worth) dessert was creme brûlée  banana creme "gelato" (not what you find in Italy, but then again that is difficult to replicate) chocolate cake and some coffee/cake pastry. 

The wait was about 40 mins, for larger groups there is a separate line around the side. They take you to the cash register to have you pay and then put you back in line to wait to be seated (kinda tacky in my book). Once in our waiter Michael was the man anything we needed he was there to give us, frequently giving us tips on what is best and how to make the most of the buffet.

The hot crab legs were awesome, this coming from someone whom rarely eats seafood, but hey I had to get my $70 worth right? The ribs and BBQ sauce were pretty delicious, both far exceeded my expectations of what I expected to get from a buffet.

I'm sad to be writing this review but I have to update my 5 stars down to a 3. Since the opening  3 years ago, I've dined here a few times. Recently, my experience was not so great in terms of quality. I don't know if they changed chefs/management or what, but I was quite disappointed in the quality and it does not come close to my 1st experience.

Some of the let downs:
- Chicken and Waffle: Served in an ice cream waffle cone, it contained a chicken wing and 2 pieces of waffle fries. Chicken was super dry and was not savory at all.
- Tonkatsu: Broth was a complete miss. Tasted super fatty and lacked depth. The pieces of pork were mostly fat and thin.
- Paella: Dry rice, mussels super overcooked, and not much seasoning
- Congee/Porridge: Too watery

The highlights are the steamed crab legs where you can get them at the Italian station now. Also, the desserts are always awesome. Is the buffet great? Yes, lot of options but the "gourmet" food I raved about... not the same anymore. I would be hesitant to recommend this place now.

**Total Rewards Pricing for Weekend Dinner which starts at 3pm is $52. It use to be about $35 when they first opened up. Definitely now one of the highest costing buffet's in Caesars.

Expensive and not worth the money. I have concerns about holding temperatures of food on the buffet line. First off food had good flavor, but was offered warm not hot. Food that was supposed to be cold was cool. Example had Noel of egg drop soup that was offered from line at just above room temperature. Serve was good but for the price not worth it.

this is probably my favorite buffet in las vegas

there is so much variety and its all really well made

they fresh baked goods are really really good

the asian section doesn't have much vegetarian selection but the chefs can make something for you if you ask

there is a cheese section that was really good

the pizza was made really really well

there's a fried food section with sweet potato tater tots. these are really delicious. i don't even like sweet potato but these are made so well!

there's a juice section with juice in bottles that you can take to your table. everything from tropical fruit juice to cucumber juice!

i couldn't eat the mexican section because was too full

the dessert section is pretty unbelievable. there's a ton of variety. the gelato is really really good. this is one to remember. i'll be back

Buffets are never a good option for me since I never eat enough and also don't really appreciate the "expensive' items as much as others.

That said, I really enjoyed Bacchanal for a number of other reasons. They have a huge selection that varies from traditional Chinese Black Chicken Soup (with Ginseng) to little baskets of Fried Chicken and Fries.

I personally really enjoyed the Bolognese (but I tend to love anything with Marinara/Meat Sauce). The dessert selection was pretty extensive but I found it odd that there was a 2-Mochi limit, when there was a free-for-all for the crab legs.

The overall quality of the food seemed pretty good to me and I really enjoyed the Spicy Poke (it is surprisingly spicy).

One thing I really wished they had more of was fruit, I know the typical buffet goer might not feel the same, but the limited selection of fruit was kind of sad.

The decor is super cute and my girls and I were lucky enough to get a semi-private room. The service was great and the waiters were kind enough to assist me with my bachelorette party scavenger hunt by suggesting a male escort.

Make sure you get there early enough to avoid the lines! If you have a party of 10 or more they will charge you gratuity right off the bat. Overall, the buffet was pretty good but not necessarily worth the price for someone like me.

Bacchanal = A feast worthy of the gods

During my last visit to Vegas last weekend, I made a stop at Bacchanal. I called them at 3:15 PM to check the prices and see how long the wait was. The guy on the phone told me it was $50.99 and told me about their new Fast Pass-like system that they implemented for about a month now. It's just like being at Disneyland! Expensive and has Fast Pass! If you're not familiar with Disneyland's Fast Pass, let me explain. You get a ticket that tells you what time to come back so that you don't have to waste your time waiting in line. Whoa, awesome!

I don't know how and why, but we took a lifetime getting ready and didn't get to Bacchanal until about 6:00. I was happy to find the machines that issued our Fast Pass to return at 7:45 PM. You can even input your phone number so that they can text you 5 minutes before you have to return to the cashier. Very clever, Caesars. I see right through your ploy. Now people have time to gamble while waiting for your buffet! Lucky for me, I actually won three bills from the slot machine while I waited for the buffet. I was also able to squeeze in some shopping time during my wait.

I got a text at 7:40 telling us to return to Bacchanal. A cashier took my payment, which was actually $52.99 per person ($2 more than what was quoted over the phone!!), and told me that the line would take approximately 40 minutes. WTF. Another line??? By this point, my husband and I were starving. The poor guy looked like he was about to faint. Since there were only two of us, we got a seat after 30 minutes of waiting. So, total wait time: 2 hours and 15 minutes. 

As other reviews state, the food is quite good. They have a meat station, seafood station, Mexican station, Asian station, Italian station, salad station, and a dessert station. 

Some things to note about the buffet: 

-I have to make a statement that their prime rib is superb. It's probably the best prime rib I have had at a buffet, and I've eaten at a lot of buffets! 
-Their seafood station only has snow crab legs, which you can get chilled or steamed. Unfortunately, there are no King crab legs. 
-Their Asian station has porridge and three types of soup: udon, pho, and ramen. Their porridge is quite tasty. I enjoyed their pho, although the broth was a little on the bland side. Two limes fixed that problem. Their ramen was not good. 
-Their dessert station has a made to order crepe station with nutella! Yum! They have mochi at the dessert station as well, but my husband said it tasted like supermarket mochi. 
-Ambiance was very hip with dance music playing. 
-Very comfortable seating

Overall, Bacchanal still has a ridiculous wait time that is slightly improved with their new Fast Pass system. Their prices are ridiculously high for a buffet, but the quality/taste of most of their food lets them get away with it. For now, this is one of the best buffets in Vegas.

Has the quality of the food gone down? My husband and I ate here during Sunday brunch. The line was ok. From 12-2pm the food tends to be out longer than expected. My husband ate the deviled eggs in which he told them he cannot have cheese because then he would throw up and have an upset stomach they went in the back and guaranteed there was no cheese however we do not know if it was contaminated with other dairy or cheese near it. After we were done with food he had an upset stomach and vomited for 2 hours straight. I'm sure the number one thing is that if you have food allergy like dairy tell the workers and be absolutely stern about it. Because we might have looked young they probably did not take us seriously. So disappointed. We may need to go to ER after this.

Absolutely amazing buffet! There was an extra $15.00 upgrade fee to go here on the Buffet 24 hour passport, but it was worth it!  Sure there was a long wait because the place is new, but everyone was in a pretty good mood in line.  If you're a diamond player, you can practically walk right in.  But for us common folk, it was about an hour and a half wait. The hostesses that meet and seat you are the nicest ladies ever! So warm and friendly, they treated us like VIP's.

The entire dining room is very comfortable and swanky - nice ambiance and spacing between the tables. Service was very attentive with continuous refills and empty plates whisked away quickly. 

And the food! This is high class, restaurant quality fare, beautifully presented.  Portions are displayed in cute baskets, individual servings in little dishes. The sushi here is very fresh, tasty dim sum, great hot and sour soup. Sweet potato tater tots were awesome! And the meal came to the perfect end with a freshly made crepe with berries.

One of the best Vegas experience ever. Talk about indulgence. I've been here a total of a dozen times and I simply will keep coming back. The buffet is very pricey, but well worth the money. The amount of decadent foods is incredible.... indulge in crab legs and oysters- truly amazing seafood selection. Their dishes are over the top flavorful and absolutely delicious. Come hungry because you'll kick yourself for not trying everything!

Very expensive for a buffet but worth every penny. It is the best buffet around. The service was amazing. Alvaro my waiter was so interesting and was very cultured. The food was amazing, even on a Monday night. However it was 110$ for 2 ppl.

On my recent trip to Las Vegas in September, we stayed at Caesar's Palace.  It's a shame this buffet was only tried by me on the latter end of the trip.

Breakfast:
Skirt steak & sunnyside eggs with freshly made rye toast, spicy home potatoes and scrambled eggs all with the most delicious coffee!  There were also lots of other breakfast options available such as pancakes, waffles, fresh bacon, sausage, biscuits etc.  There is a large variety.  Warning: a bit pricey but CERTAINLY WORTH IT!

Dinner:
Too many delicious things to name.  Fresh shrimp & seafoods, pasta's, sushi, pizza's etc. No matter what you got, it was delicious!!!  WARNING: So expensive on Fri/Sat/Sun.  It was $54 per person.  Whew!  But worth it for sure.

The decor is great.  Comfortable big seats.  The space is very large.  The service is wonderful.

Overall, certainly worth it to eat here at least once!

Not the best buffet but the most popular buffet. It is decent, with a vairous selection of meats and seafood. I love the shrimps and the clams, they are in good quality. The service is okay but the cooks that are serving food are not that friendly.

BEST VEGAS BUFFET. 

I think I died and was sent to heaven after eating at this place. Like no, seriously. I ate so much of everything that I knocked out from a food coma right after. There were so many options to choose from! There is a station for every almost every cuisine.

What's my favorite? Their 5 star gourmet dessert bar!!! Imagine creme brulee, gelato, macarons, chocolate covered strawberries, crepes, and other beautifully created sweets you can think of.

One of the better ones on the strip. 

Would recommend, get the quick pass believe it costed extra $11 per person. 
I prefer dinner over breakfast/lunch.

The only good thing about this buffet is the crab claws and legs are already pre-cracked so no messy hammering. Other than that, save your $53 per person (dinner price) and time (40 min wait on a Sunday evening) for the several other Las Vegas restaurants.

My God! This may be the best buffet on earth. They need to change name. This more accurately a feast. I've never such an amazing and diverse selection of food. Everything tasted amazing. They even had crab legs that were cracked open for u...so no work.

I ate the best piece of lamb I've ever had. The place is beautiful and the waiters moved fast and were very nice.

I would advise to arrive early or call ahead. We tried to go there for dinner the 2nd night and the wait was an hour and a half. They literally serve over 7000 people a day.

Hands down, Bacchanal Buffet is the BEST buffet on the Vegas strip!

My recent trip to Vegas led me to staying at the Caesar's Palace hotel and instead of us traveling somewhere else on the strip to get our last meal in before heading back home, we decided to give the Bacchanal Buffet downstairs a try and I was not disappointed.

AMBIENCE:
The line to get in is long and for good reason - the food is GOOD!  

*Tip:  Make sure you bring your Player's Club Card.  If you don't have one, make sure you visit the Player's Card Booth to sign up!  You will get a few dollars off of your buffet.  I got the mimosa buffet and the total came out to be $40 on a weekend.

The seating inside is made to make you feel like it is spacious and open.  The beautiful blue glass decoratively placed throughout the restaurant makes the restaurant look very modern and clean.

FOOD QUALITY:
There is A LOT of variety here. For my very very particular parents, they could not stop raving about how wonderful the Asian section of the buffet was.  For myself, I could not resist the fried chicken (fried chicken, i love you!!) pho, and desserts. There seems to be something for everyone here - desserts, seafood, juices, red velvet pancakes, fries, tator tots, breakfast foods, sausages and other meats, italian food, mexican food, salads, noodles, sushi, and other Asian dishes.

Some of the more memorable dishes:
*There was actually meat on the crab legs and they tasted fresh!
*The skin of the fried chicken was absolutely delicious!  The chicken also was super tender.
* LOVED the noodle station.  *TIP:  Don't miss the noodle station! They serve pho!  The broth was delicious, the noodles were tender - one of the best pho I have had.
* Dim sum - Ha gow is my favorite dim sum dish and they really got it right!  The shrimp inside was tender, tasty, and fresh!
* Chow mein was amazing!  I had to go for seconds - packed with flavor!
* I kept getting the coffee - it was so good and paired perfectly with my dessert.

SERVICE:
What sets Bacchanal Buffet apart from the other buffets on the strip is the service.  From the moment we sat down, our waitress was SUPER accommodating and on top of it!  She kept our coffee and the tea coming and came back very frequently to take away our dishes.  You will notice that it is not just the waitresses/waiters but the entire staff of Bacchanal.  You guys have it together and what a breath of fresh air it is to see!  Even those that are serving you from behind the buffet line are smiley and ready to help.  It truly made our experience here that much better!

OVERALL:
I have found my new favorite buffet on the Vegas strip.  Because of my wonderful experience here, I definitely have Bacchanal as a required stop to visit on my list whenever I come back to Vegas.  If you haven't come here yet, what are you waiting for? You deserve to give your taste buds some TLC!! :)

Arrived early enough that we only waited about 10min to get in and beat the dinner rush getting in. Always love to come here because they make intriguing dishes that you wouldn't find at a normal restaurant. I was able to try a sea snail which was slightly sandy but was cooked very well. Another interesting dish was the truffle pizza which was very tasty. When I went they also had horchata which was delicious but not as good as a normal taco shop. I always get very full off of this buffet while getting to try different dishes.

Honestly, this buffet disappointed me. It definitely did not live up to the hype. The wait was ridiculous (you have to grab a ticket around 12 PM to get in for dinner, then wait another almost 2 hours to be seated), and it was pricey for the food it offered. 

They had some good food, but I was hoping for a little more in their selection of sushi. It left much to be desired, to say the least. The crab legs were alright, and the shrimp cocktail tasted a little odd to me. I really loved the desserts, pasta, potatoes, and juices in those cute little bottles, but those things were not worth the wait or the price. 

Our waiter was very nice and talkative, so I enjoyed that. 
I probably will never be back for this buffet.

This was amazing. So much food. Normally on a buffet, I try the things that look good, then get more of whatever was best. Here, there were so many options that I was stuffed before I finished trying everything. And so many of the things I tried were amazing - I wanted to have more. My main regret was that I did not save more room for dessert - what I tried was delish and I wished for more room to try more. There are really only 2 things that keep this from being 5 stars... first - there were a couple things I tried that were distinctly not good and second - I previously tried Wicked Spoon and thought it was slightly better. Overall - an amazing meal.

Came here once.l with my wife. We had to get a number to get in line to pay. Yes, get a number to get in line.  I'm not sure if things just changed but my wife was so excited to try the ginsing chicken but when we got in, all it looked like was a pot that looked like chicken noodle soup. The high light were the crab legs but they have these at every buffet. All in all not "the best" buffet out there by then again, I'm not a buffet fan.
