So far the one that I liked the most is studio 8 buffet which is way off the strip. They have an amazing seafood spread that includes baked lobster tails. Unfortunately they only do these on special days like Mother's Day or something like that. Save your money and pass on this buffet. It's a dud. Not worth the $60 per person for dinner.

Visited again for dinner 9/6/17. Once again, I will say this with absolute certainty: Caesars Bacchanal Buffet is the BEST buffet is Vegas, no exceptions. This delusional lady with an accent on YouTube that reviews buffets mentioned that she thought Studio B buffet rivals that of Ceasars. I submit she must have been given a kickback to give it that good of a review.  The Studio B buffet doesn't hold a candle to Caesars.  More expensive at Caesars, but if you are looking for quality and selection, there is no comparison.

Come for only the fresh seafood (crab legs) and dessert. The rest is just passable.

People form a huge line for those coveted crab legs, and the line spills over and blocks the carving station. So you have to stand in a giant, slow-moving line even if you only want roast beef.

The sushi and Asian food in general is unimpressive. You can get better at regular, less-expensive restaurants.

The dessert is amazing, though. Crepes and chocolate covered strawberries and gelato. Save room!

I have to start this review with a disclosure: I am not a fan of buffets. The options at your average buffet are overwhelming to me and I find no pleasure in the variety of food mixing on my plate. With that being said, Bacchanal was the most high end one I've been to and the scallops and deserts were delicious. Low point was the ceviche.  Overall an excellent choice for a buffet if that is your thing - my husband and I probably won't be back.

This is the second time I've been to this place and dude, this place is beyond amazing. I woke up around 9:30 on the day after Christmas and headed to this restaurant to check out the line. There was no line!!!! My family n I got charged ($43.99 for holiday brunch) and seated 15 mins later and hands down to the best buffet in Vegas. They have great selections from breakfast, brunch and to seafood! The desert booth captured my heart with fresh crepes and other kind of sweets. Can't wait to come back the next time I visit Vegas!

Unconscionably long line.  I don't think I've ever felt like a slave to food than my experience here, and I don't mean that in a good way.  2+ hour wait, and even though the end product was terrific, I had to rush (because of the long wait) in order to make the show.  The wait expectations aren't well set.

* Platinum and Seven Stars: step right up, pay, and avoid the long wait.  This is the way to go.  The $20 express option was not available.

For the normal folk (and this was me):
=============================
* For lunch: 120pm check-in at the self-service kiosk, and issued a 90 min wait ticket (plus the line-up to pay).  Skipped, did an alternative lunch.
* For dinner: 6pm check-in - 45 min printout from the kiosk...but you just get to get in line when you are texted.  We waited over an hour in line, and finally, at 750pm were seated.

The food is outstanding, high-quality.  But I was rushed to catch a show that I didn't enjoy my experience much.  After all, I allowed 2.5 for dinner!   For $61, you shouldn't have to wait 2 hours to eat.  It's a near 5.0 star buffet choices and decor, it gets a 3.0 star when mixed with experience.

Like a few other people, we attended Bacchanal when it first opened because EVERY local we came across simply raved about it from start to finish.  We waited in line for about an hour and a half - again, really thinking, okay, this is really going to be killer!   Unfortunately we were not blown away, and at a high price tag, we left feeling a little dismayed.  While the food we tried across the different palattes was good, it wasn't mind blowing.  Maybe that's just the local in me talking?  Oh well.  Better to try it and know, than to never try it and be uninformed.  No worries!

The Wynn used to be my favorite, but the Bacchanal up-ed the ante and pretty much put it to shame. 

The sheer volume of food is impressive, but it's the authenticity and nuanced flavors in each dish that made it an over-the-top experience. I felt like I was taste-testing dishes for a celebrity restaurant. They also had many quality items that the other buffets do not have. Savory examples include fresh steamed crab legs, Indonesian rendeng and goreng, Paella (so hard to do well, but they nailed it!), Oyster shooters. Dessert examples include hand-crafted mochi ice cream (including Black Sesame flavor!), chocolate dipped strawberries, etc. Another cool option was the agua fresca selection in the Latino section - they had tiny bottles of Horchata, Strawberry Juice, Mango Juice, Jamaica, etc. 

I went on New Year's Day, so perhaps it was even more abundant than normal, but it was well worth the price tag and the wait to get in. 

Pro Tip: Check in at the kiosks early in the day so you have an approximate wait time for the buffet (can be up to 4 hours!) and arrive an hour early.

We came here at least twice a year. Used to be good. But now, Food and Service is not as good as it used to be. Food empty for a long time but they do not refill them. Our waiter ignores us all the time. We tried to call him for 5 times by raising our hands...no response...waiting for the hot tea for 15min...

I heard so much about this buffet that I went the first day I arrived in vegas. We went in at 2pm on Tuesday and it was very quiet, a lot of the tables empty. We first went forthe crab legs which was good. But the king crabs started coming out a lot later (when we were already full) and those were AMAZING. But minus one point for delaying the king crabs. And also other types of food was just ehh. The noodles were all too salty (I tried miso, ramen, pho) that I only had the first sip. The cheese was ehh. But I understand that buffet can't have everything perfect. I don't know if I'll return but it was a pretty decent experience overall

Unbelieveable!!!

Okay this place honestly deserves a good review because the food was AWESOME. The waiters were on their tip toes clearing plates out of our way so that when we came back with more food in our hands from the buffet lines, we would have space on the table. My relatives (age 21+) had champagne because it was complimentary due to it being a weekend and before 4 p.m.

The amazing food selection: snow crab legs, jumbo shrimp, oysters, crawdads, lamb chops, prime rib, ribs, pizza, make your own taco/burrito station, orange chicken, walnut shrimp, cha siu bao, a large variety of cheese, and more

I'm definitely a fan of the grill station because the flavors jump out at you with every bite. 

A lot of the food here is served in individual cute little baskets. Like they have tiny baskets with fried chicken and sweet potato fries. 

Definitely worth the $41 for lunch on the weekends. Dinner is $50 and the switch from lunch/brunch to dinner is at 3 p.m.

Ok, so came in to Bacchanal with very high hopes which could be the cause of my overall opinion of it being ok to pretty good. Before I begin though, I did go here on a Thursday and while waiting in line, we were looking at some Yelp pictures to see king crab legs, which we did not find inside the actual buffet (bummer!). SO, with that being said... friends overhyping this place up along with seeing king crab legs with none being served inside... you can see where I'm coming from.

The rest of the food though, not bad at all, it is good for sure. My personal favorite was the Wagu beef sliders (I'm a sucker for burgers though). The lasagna is also very good. I also enjoyed the cream of mushroom soup. The oysters are also a winner in my eyes. The regular crab legs taste just like any other buffet. The dessert is ok... one of the cooks played it up to be really good, but it wasn't all that great, though this might be due to the fact that I was full by then. The tacos are pretty good though... they make it there on the spot like a taco truck, which is pretty cool... 

a quick tip that I saw my friend did and thought it was genius... get a big plate of chips and have the taco guy place carne asada, cheese, sour cream, and guacamole over it... BAM, carne asada nachos! 

Some of the dishes are placed in big containers, plates, bowls... and you can only fit one or 2 at the most on your plate... I understand that it looks better but just a bit inconvenient that you can't put too many on your plate at once. Just a minor complaint. 

Overall experience is pretty good, though it's not the best buffet in Vegas in my eyes, it's definitely good. I don't think the quality of the buffet justifies the $50 price point, but it is worth a try if you're in Vegas, plus it's the new "must go-to" buffet.

I would have to say out of all the buffets I've been to in Vegas.. This would top all of them. After a bad experience at Bellagio, this made the end of my trip. First I'd like to say that the decor and ambiance of the Caesars palace really gave the intro to eating here. We got there around 11:30am and people were already starting to line up and crowd for lunch. We waited for about 15 mins since it was only two of us so seating a couple was quick. There were so many selections compared to other buffets and because of the variety and delicious food options I really have nothing bad to say about this buffet. The staff was nice and pleasant and actually made conversation even though it was brief just to say hello and how we were. 

I was craving seafood before we got there for lunch and the selection was pretty good. From mussels to crab claws to lobster bisk. They also have Mexican, Asian, Japanese, Italian to choose from. My favorite was the choice of meat and I enjoyed the prime rib and brisket.. The meat has flavor!! Omg ! Everything was presented very well and expressed their passion for food and giving people the best dining experience. Dessert area also had many choices I had gelato and rice pudding with hazel nut flavor (that was all I could eat after being so full) lol. All in all my time here has met my expectations and it was worth it with the price we paid. :)

Great selection of food! I am usually not a fan of buffets but I figured I would try this out since everyone that goes to Vegas seems to have been here. I went here for brunch. Originally, I had thought they would only have a majority of breakfast foods so I was hesitant. However, that was not the case. They had a great selection of different types of food. Dim sum, Italian, Ramen/Pho/Udon, tacos and ceviche, meat, sushi, deli, salads, etc. I thought the sushi was mediocre, but everything else was pretty good. Oh and their baked goods and gelato was also great. I recommend the roast coffee flavor. Seriously had a hard time deciding between them all.  Definitely worth the $40 brunch price. Be prepared for a wait. It was only me and a friend and on a Monday, around noon, we waited around an hour.

This is one of the most impressive buffets I've ever had- the only other comparable one is in asia.. 

It is a lot for a buffet, sure, but you're paying for creativity, presentation, variety of food as well as excellent service. 

They do an amazing job surveying different cuisines; while other buffets may dabble into other cultures, Bacchanal really immerses itself in excellent presentation and quality in their Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Italian etc dishes. There is an impressively authentic array of Asian cuisine with dim sum, stir fried dishes, porridge!, and ramen. They also a great seafood, meat, and cheese selection. Every time I looked over at the bf he was eating a different type of meat and looked quite happy.  I loved the sweet potato tots, seafood paella, creamy polenta, pork buns, and fresh juices. 

I'd come again purely to eat dessert. Everything was beautiful, delicate, and delicious. 

Compared to Wicked Spoon, Bacchanal has much more seafood, does a much better job exploring different cuisines, and has a somewhat more impressive dessert selection.

The best buffet in Vegas in my opinion! 
We arrived on a Saturday afternoon around 3 PM when dinner started. I followed the advice on the website that said to use the kiosks beforehand to check in. It gave us an hour wait time and I put in my phone number to receive a text when it was ready. 
Since we had some time, we explored the Caesar's Forum Shops and got a big delicious drink at Fat Tuesday(it is Vegas after all!) We got the text about 40 minutes after we checked in, which was a nice surprise! We got in line when we got back for another 15 minutes to pay and be officially seated. 
We were finally seated and went up and started helping ourselves. I started in the seafood section to gorge on crab legs. They had those and so much more! I loved how fresh everything was. 
Next I made my way to the cheese plate section and grabbed a few different kinds of cheeses to try. They also had olives, various meats,and crackers. 
On my way through, I grabbed some other various things from other "countries" including Asian noodles, pizza, a little bit of the Mexican food they had, salad, and even some mac and cheese. They had a lot of light options which I took advantage of, but I also grabbed some of the "bad" stuff too.
The dessert beer is INSANE! There are SO many options. I grabbed a few things, but I feel that I should have saved more room for this part of it. 
This buffet was about $60/person on Saturday dinner pricing. It was great, and we definitely feel that we got our money's worth.

Best buffet ever! I went here for brunch. Seriously the endless seafood options and food selection is so delicious. They had huge crab legs. I got the hot one and cold ones. I thought the cold ones tasted better and were less salty than the heated ones. They had crab claws which were not good. I would recommend you save your stomach for something else. I thought the claws had a interesting texture and flavor.
After I stuffed myself with the seafood, I tried their food. I loved the beets and their oyster shooters were delightful. 
They have a whole breakfast section with red velvet pancakes, waffles and chicken, churros, and so much more.  You have to try the churros because they were the best churros I have ever tried. They were warm and melted in my mouth. 
The best part was their sweets! The dessert bar was hard to find. It was secluded on the right side of the buffet. When you got there, there were so many desserts to pick from. My favorite was the coconut tapioca pudding and the green tea ice cream. 
So happy that I got to try this place.

the weight is excruciating but the food is really good. The only real downside to this Buffet is the snow and king crab is mixed together in the chilled area and there is really like one piece of king crabto 20 pieces of snow crab. And our table person that is supposed to clear our dirty plates and bring us refills on our drinks was MIA

This is by far the best buffet I've been to so far.
Food was warm ...there was plenty for the whole village... Very clean and the server was great. 
It's pretty pricy and the line is ENDLESS.
Def. worth the $60...
Don't forget if u wanna go in the express line to cut ..u can also do so by only paying a small fee of $25 extra dinero

Over priced and over rated. Tried a little of several items. The dumpling I tried had a wrapper that was to thick and doughy. More than half of the shrimp I took were mushy/mealy. The mussels were good, but the curry lack the depth of flavor one expects. The two best items that I had were the prime rib and a selection of meat from the charcuterie board. For the cost I had hoped for better. 
However, our waitress was great.
I don't usually go to buffets but this place was recommended and it was definitely worth it the steak and pasta are amazing and you can't forget about the desserts amazing
The brunch selection was out of this world! I enjoyed every bite of my seafood feast. I will definitely be back

All I can say is it was heaven for a foodie like myself. They had everything from sushi to burgers to a cold fish bar. I recommend walking the entire buffet to see everything before making any commitments. The dessert area was amazing, the had everything from gellato to cheesecake to cake pops and more. If your looking for a beautiful setting, great food and comfortable seating then Bacchanal is your place. I will definitely be going back :)

Theres certainly a lot of options. However, it's like any other buffet. I tried almost everything and hardly came back for seconds. The crab legs and pizza were the best but everything else was not memorable. 
It's completely overrated. Line was super long. We waited for 2-3 hours. Not worth the wait.

This place is one of the better buffets in Las Vegas. I've found that if you plan to eat here, pace yourself and prepare to pay a grip.  I came here with my fiancé and for the two of us for lunch it came out to be about $95.  They have everything you can possibly eat here. It's probably pricey but they have a gelato stAtion and a variety of crabs to eat. I would say it's definitely worth trying and the for the price you pay its worth it. Just remember to pace yourself.

Best buffet I've ever had.

So as you probably know, thus buffet can be broken down into a few sections. I came for the dinner selection so idk if it is the same for lunch. 

Asian cuisine-they have a wide variety of dim sum and sushi dishes, as well as a ramen/noodle soup bar. I did not try too many items from this sections since I eat high quality Asian food very frequently, but I was very tempted.  The ahi hand roll was by far my favorite from this section; I was very impressed with the quality of their sashimi. Definitely would do it again.

Mexican cuisine-I am so mad because they did not have the horchata available when I went. However, the guava Agua Fresca was very perfect. It was very light and pleasant :) I also didn't get to try the famous made to order tacos-but they did look delicious- so I am just missing out on everything! 

Soup-OH MY GOODNESS the truffle mushroom soup was AMAZING. It was the first thing I tried and I melted. I would highly recommend it.

Seafood- Personally, I am not a big fan of seafood. But, I could not pass up the sea bass and ceviche. Bother were delicious, I especially appreciate the texture of the sea bass, very well done. If I were to come back, I would want to try the salmon and maybe the crab legs(depending on my mood). 

Carvery-meh. I expected better. However, it wasn't terrible. Still high quality.

Desserts- FINALLY, my favorite section. They had desserts galore with everything from artisan ice cream to some Asian pudding desserts. My favorites were the red velvet cake,jasmine rice pudding, mango sago, and FRENCH MACARONS. The Thai iced tea boba item was good;however, the boba was subpar. Not worth the calories.

Bacchanal is definitely worthy of the title: "Best Buffet On The Strip"
I've tried all the top buffets on the strip(Wynn, Bellagio, The M) but Bacchanal tops them all in every category.
I notice the majority of low ratings come from the dinner reviews.. this review is based on breakfast and lunch.

Food: I love the breakfast here.. they cover all the traditional breakfast food but with different flares. Things like Chicken&Waffles, Skirt Steak & Eggs, Corned Beef  Hash with a fried Quail Egg, & Lobster Egg Benedict. They also have a good amount of their lunch menu out during breakfast including the meat section, featuring about a dozen or so cuts/meat.. I especially enjoy the prime rib, habanero sausage, and bacon-wrapped lamb. The Asian food section in the back is also open in the morning.. foods like shumai, Pad Thai, sushi, and the Asian soup station(Pho, Ramen, Udon), which are actually pretty decent.

This buffet has so much to offer.. from the 7 or 8 times we've visited, they've continued to come out with new, impressive options.
Some of my other highlights: Chilean seabass, broccoli casserole, fried fish, any of the dishes that are topped with a fried egg, Baklava gelato, the salted caramel brownie thing, and the Horchata! 

Ambiance: A very clean, modern look with a comfortable setting that gives you a relaxing experience when enjoying your food. The main seating area could be a bit of a maze when going back and fourth but the overall layout is great. The one thing that does bother me is how wide the party-of-2 tables are and how close the tables are to one another. I was literally right next to the lady at the table next to me and further away from my girlfriend sitting across from me. I felt like I had to talk extra loud for my girlfriend to hear me, but soft enough so the next table isn't involuntarily listening to me.

Service: Yes, this is a very popular buffet but they've come up with the genius idea of having a kiosk system where they text you when your table is almost ready. It is a very attractive idea because you don't get that discouraging feeling of seeing that crazy long line. It also gives you the opportunity to go do other things while waiting(gamble) :). All the staff members are very welcoming and polite.. quick servers and helpful cooks. The price of this buffet is a little bit more than all the others, but you will definitely get your money's worth every time. 

Tips: If you're coming for breakfast, try to come at the end of the breakfast time(10-10:30ish) so you can get a taste of the lunch items that come out at 11am. Take your time, try to get in all the options they offer and enjoy. Don't forget your Total Rewards card for a small discount!

Buffet was not that great. 

About the lines:  You have to wait in line to put your name and number down on a machine to let you know when you come back which is usually an hour to 2 hours. Once your back you show your time receipt to a lady to wait in line to pay. After paying youd need to get into a line to be sat. Once sat you could get into line to get your food. 

Food:  oyesters had pieces of shell in them. Choices of fish were scarce, himachi and salmon thats it. The line for pho and udon was long amd the broths were over boiling to a point where each both tastes the same due to it spilling over. Snow crab was frozen still even after the man boiled it in front of our eyes. Meats were all very salty,  I tried them all. Overall for food. If your paying 60 and waiting for 2 hours to eat, the food better have presentation, have quality product and better taste great. Well bachannal failed all categories. 

Desserts: they were very good but there werent many choices. 

Service : always attentive and was great. 

Overall review: place was very hyped. I feel belagio or wicked spoon was better.

This place is amazing. Everything was fresh! The seafood was fresh.  The meats were seasoned and cooked to perfection.  The sides were great.  I live that you can check in then go walk around until it's ti.e for u to be seated, that just makes it so convenient.  Waitress was good she kept my champagne topped. Overall great experience

If I could only eat at one restaurant while in Las Vegas, it would definitely be Bacchanal Buffet.  

Is it pricey?  YES
Is there a long wait?  YES (sometimes no, but it's really hit or miss)
Is it busy?  YES
Is it worth it?  ABSOLUTELY

My friends kept insisting that it's the best buffet and there were so many advertisements on cabs, posters, magazines promoting Bacchanal as the #1 buffet in Las Vegas and I would have to say that Bacall lives up to the hype. They are located in Caesars Palace and the restaurant is nice and clean, it's decorated with glass containers filled with food displays.  Bacchanal offers such a wide variety of food and what I thought was really awesome was that behind each counter were chefs from the same ethnic background of that particular type of food.  For instance, there was an Asian chef behind the Asian food section and a Mexican chef behind the Mexican food section.  They provide these cute little finger grips to grab hot plates with and they really came in handy because a lot of the plates were really hot.  

My Favorites
+Wagyu Beef Sliders
+Mac and Cheese
+EVERYTHING at the dessert bar (macaroons, warm chocolate chip cookie, gelato, flan, etc)
+Crab Legs

They had all types of food and I totally failed my mission of trying everything they had to offer.  They had a huge assortment at the seafood section, so many different types of breads and muffins, an American section, Italian, Mexican, Asian, salad bar, meat carving station, you name it and they had it.  I will definitely have to go back and try the other food items I missed the next time I'm back in Las Vegas.  What made the Bacchanal Buffet that much better was that the customer service was on point!

One of  the he best buffetts I've tried in Vegas! I can't explain how long I've looked forward to trying this place once I brought a groupon. Absolutely amazing! Service was surperb and all the food stations had something I wanted to try. Clean and great seating area all kinds of different tables for a small or big groups. Lovely decor and endless mimosas I can not complain! Pretty pricey for sure but it's not like I come here all the time.

Overall this is a fun buffet but the wait is crazy (even on a Monday).  Let me tell you what to do.  Come 3 hours before you want to eat and sign in at the kiosk, go gamble or chill in your room, then come back and get in line at your scheduled time.  4 stars for good food but the desserts were lacking.

Was it worth $60? Nah. 

I came for the crab legs. And I cried because of the crab legs. They were limp...cold....soggy and oh, so salty. The beauty of fresh Alaskan crab legs are their fluffy sweetness and there was none of that here. And let's face it - if I'm not gorging myself on expensive seafood, this buffet is not worth the price.

Yes, I had a lot of food. And yes, I probably had three plates of decent dessert. But I would happily drop $30 elsewhere for PHENOMENAL desserts. Now that I've done the buffet once, I probably won't do it again.

The only Vegas Strip buffet that never fails to impress. Ceasers Buffet had everything I wanted. 

The only two disappointments were the lines and prices. I know eating there on a weekend during brunch is expected to have a long line but 35 minute wait was not fun. 

The restaurant was clean and we'll kept. Quick service. Didn't have to wait to ask for anything, the waiter offered suggestions and even what to start with.
The desserts were beautiful. The sections of food were properly separated. 
The meats were, unlike other buffets, were actually cut beautifully.


THE FOOD WAS SOOOO FRESH. NEVER HAD TO WAIT MORE THAN A MINUTE FOR THE NEXT BATCH. 

I was only upset about the 2 hr maximum for the price  I had to pay.

Pros:
Clean tables and dishes.
Abundance in food.
Great waiters and waitresses.

Cons:
The line
The prices (at first)

I received a groupon for this buffet. The food was overwhelming and they accommodate a variety for every taste. I came with my son for his birthday. The service was great, the place was clean and the dessert island was yummy. We were lucky that our groupon was accompanied by a VIP pass so we didn't have to wait in line. This place is a little pricey but if you are looking for a treat this is a place to indulge. The spa at Caesars is amazing as well.

Loved this buffet! We've been to buffets all over Vegas and this is the best in my opinion. We went for dinner and there was so much to choose from. There were different varieties of tapas in each genre of food, different entree choices, and several selections for dessert. I over ate but it was totally worth. They also had the best pork friend rice I've ever eaten! The only thing we probably would have done differently was eat at lunch time. There would have been a reduction in price and we probably would not have had to deal with the wait. All in all, I think this buffet is worth a try.

I was hearing good things about the Bacchanal Buffet and even though I make yearly trips to Las Vegas and I've been to Las Vegas over 9 times, I never tried Bacchanal until my recent trip to Las Vegas in April 2016.

I've read about the long line-ups and lining up to get a ticket/card to tell you what time to show up in order to line-up again in order to get seated but when I went there at ~2:40pm on Thursday April 21, 2016, there was absolutely no line-up. I just went to the cash register and paid. The cashier asked me for my name and I gave her my TotalRewards card and she mentioned something about dining credits (I wasn't paying attention to what she said).

I paid $42.17 ($38.99+$3.18 tax) and was seated immediately. This was the second most expensive buffet that I've experienced (most expensive would be Sterling Brunch at Bally's). I noticed immediately on the bill/receipt that there was a 2 hour dining limit. It wasn't an issue for me but this was the first time that I saw a time limit for a buffet so I thought I would mention it on my review of the place.

The waitress asked me what drink I wanted and I mentioned that I wanted either Diet Coke or Diet Pepsi. I forgot which they offered.

This buffet had a lot of variety. It had more variety than almost all the buffets that I've ever experienced. The buffet doesn't close between the different meals so they transition the different types of food when the time changes for the different meals.

I can't comment specifically on what is offered during lunch or dinner since even though I started eating during the lunch portion of the buffet, they were serving dinner items by the time I left.

I'm a big seafood fan so I concentrated mainly on the seafood items. I had large shrimps which were great. The shrimps were deveined and peeled already which made eating them less messy. I also had crab legs which I thought were also very good. They had shucked oysters which I was not overly impressed by. They tasted fine (no smell or weird taste) but they didn't seem to be cleaned well since all the ones that I had seemed to have sand in them. I also had crab claws which were good. My only issue with the crab claws were that they were cracked but some of them were not cracked enough to easily open and eat and there wasn't any cracking tool that I could see/find.

I tried some of their Chinese Dim Sum items (Siu Mai & Har Gow) which were very good for buffet Dim Sum items. I've had better Har Gow & Siu Mai at a regular Cantonese Dim Sum restaurant.

I also had their prime roast (or beef dish) which I liked.

Excluding the Diet Coke that I ordered from the waitress, I also had 3 bottles of their juice which I really liked (you get it yourself from the buffet).

For the dessert, I had creme brulee, a slice of watermelon, a slice of cantaloupe, some type of cheesecake in the form of a "lollipop", a piece of rum cake, and multiple flavours/scoops of gelato ice cream. They had a very large dessert section and the gelato ice cream is served to you (as opposed to you scooping it yourself).

I ate very slowly at this buffet and left after approximately 1 hour and 45 minutes. The waitress was very good at clearing my table of the plates and also asked me a few times whether I wanted another soft drink.

I will probably come back here the next time I am in Las Vegas.

When we checked out the line-up on the weekend, it was too long. It was quite a turn-off to see such a line-up so we decided to go on a Monday instead, which turned out to be a great choice. After seeing the tips/suggestions on here, we went at 2:40 pm and there was no line-up to the cash register. As dinner starts at 3:00 pm, we paid lunch prices and we had access to the dinner items. From what I saw, there were just more meats available for the dinner menu in comparison to the lunch menu. When I checked out the line-up at around 4 pm and 4:30 pm, there was still no line-up and the restaurant was half empty. So if you'd like your fill without the wait, weekdays are the best.

Within minutes of being seated, our waitress came to our table and asked us what we would like to drink. She was attentive and cleared our empty plates every single time one of us left to get more food. She also provided re-fills for drinks when we ran low.

As for the food, I'm sure there is a higher turn-over of the buffet items on weekends when the restaurant is seated at full capacity. We went when it was at around 40%-45% capacity so some items were a little dry. It was interesting to find Chinese, Korean, SE Asian, Japanese, and Mexican cuisine. The shrimp dumplings were tasty. The kimchi fried rice and sushi was bland and dry. The laksa was so-so. There was a salsa station with various ingredients. King crab was available for dinner. I liked the clams, various meats, mac & cheese, and desserts. Overall, there was a huge selection of various types of food. It was impressive. The selection of desserts was impressive too. 

Of course, if you're a buffet lover who places quantity over quality, then this is the place for you. On the other hand, I'm not a buffet person so I don't know if I'd want to go back. For the price, there are plenty of quality restaurants that you can dine your heart out at for less in Las Vegas. If it's your first time in Las Vegas, you definitely need to try this place at least once.

So I'm not usually a buffet person and especially for that price. But we won free passes and went with some friends. Had a blast.
From the woman at the register cracking jokes with us thinking we were employees and the friendly servers who kept us on the ball with our glasses full and table cleared, it was a good experience.
The food was good with large selection from sushi, to lamb chops to paella. The sushi was good, the lamb average but the brisket good and filling and the paella was good! The ribs were quite fatty however. The seafood selection was great and quite enjoyed it! I tried different stuff than last time and was quite happy. Some of the bread was average but we liked the pretzel bread. The desserts were a hit with everyone as we shared and they had soufflé this time. Tom got plates of cake pops and jelly bellys, I tried mochi for the first time (not quite sure about it), and loved the cobbler!!! 
The little drink bottles: piña wasn't so good but the horchatta was and love the little bottles 
We were so full none of us could get up so we sat and talked for awhile. The four stars is for price and some of the stuff stated above. Also be sure to go either at off hour (no line at 9 when leaving) or be prepared to wait!

Food selection is AMAZING. I wish I could eat here everyday, but I can't afford it lol it is too pricey, but well worth it to go once or twice a year if your are on a budget like me great place for any occasion. It's clean, food is fresh. Beverages and desserts are tasty. Check it out! Service is good too.

Huge variety including fresh seafood, and I didn't get sick. I ate crab, different kinds of mussels, escargot, crab soup, shrimp. They will guve you a huge cut of prime rib. It is excessive what some people got. They have American Wagyu beef, brisket, you name it. Self-serve au jus or gravy. They have a bunch of different stations. Dessert is its own island. I didn't get tired of the food here. It was great. It was a little hard to get our waitress to come back but they have so many people to wait on that it was understandable. Not a problem at all. We stayed for 2 hrs, which is the max, as stated on their sign. It was a bit pricey but memorable and we left happy. Thank you!!

I paid extra 25 for skipping the line.  I came around 7pm in Saturday and expected line was 60-70 mins.  The stone crab claws were dried and hard to take meat out.  Cold king crab legs were salty. You should get the boiled crabs leg at the Italian station for better taste.  Crawfish had a nice spice.  Clams were sandy.  Oysters were not fresh. They smelled fishy and very dirty with sand and shell.  Sucking pig was bland.  Long line for the prime rib station.  The bbq pork rib has not flavor.  Shame that for the price and didn't have sashimi but some cheap sushi. Crime Bruce was good.  There are way better Buffetts out there than this for less.

Prologue:
In preparation for our first trip to Las Vegas as a couple we contemplated where we would like to dine out and agreed that a visit to a good buffet on the Strip would be an essential component to our trip.

The Plot:
We arrived at the Bacchanal Buffet at around 5:30pm on a Tuesday evening. 

The Scene:
The Bacchanal Buffet is everything one could want from a quintessential Las Vegas Strip buffet.
I had already been to a few of the other fairly well known buffets on the Strip, including The Buffet at Wynn, the Carnival World Buffet at the Rio, the Spice Market at Planet Hollywood, and the Bayside Buffet at Mandalay Bay.
The Bacchanal is easily on par with any of them in terms of variety and a cut above in terms of quality.
My girlfriend, who is quite discriminating when it comes to dining out, commented that she thought it was a very worthwhile experience.
In fact, I was enjoying some dessert at about the 90-minute mark when my girlfriend got her second wind and headed back to the raw seafood bar.

The Rest of the Story:
The price per person is very likely more than most people would usually spend when dining out.
However, the price is reasonable for a really good Las Vegas buffet and what we got was well worth the price.

Epilogue:
This first buffet experience together spoiled us for sure.
Next time we're in the mood for a buffet in Las Vegas we'll likely return here rather than trying someplace else.

Photo design by Billie Z.
The wait was three hours long, granted it was a major holiday. Couldn't wait so had to go somewhere else. It was better when it first opened but still one of the better ones out there.

Yes it more expensive than any other buffet I've been to Las Vegas, and I was pleasantly surprised.

The prime rib and beef brisket was steakhouse quality. The seafood paella was pretty good. The crab legs were better than other buffets. Stone crab was above average. Service was very attentive. Food was above average and tasted like good restaurant food. Nothing like a regular buffet, where you kinda scared and apprehensive.
Desert was good too

Save your money and go somewhere else! The food was terrible. I had to spit my food out several times. It made both my husband and me feel sick. We were only given a 50% discount after telling the manager that all the food was awful. We basically paid $50 for some waters. Big thumbs down.
The variety was impressive. I tried to sample a bit of everything without getting fat. Will be coming back next time I'm in Vegas to try the rest.

We dined at the Bacchanal yesterday for the second time.  We dined  here previously on the grand opening weekend. During the grand opening weekend dining experience I thought that the service was not very organized.  It took almost half an hour to order our drinks because no server showed up at our table.  I attributed this to the fact that it was the grand opening weekend the servers were new and inexperienced. However after dining here yesterday I can tell you that things have not changed. First of all the food is way overpriced for the quality. A lot of the food choices were cold and the stations were not well-maintained. There were many stations that were unlabeled so you didn't know exactly what you were eating. Our waitress never returned to our table to refill our drinks. A patron sitting next to us actually tracked down our waitress to have her bring us coffee because we could not find her. When she did appear at her table she looked like she was having a bad day and unhappy to be at work. You can find better quality food across the street at the Flamingo where the buffet is around  $22. 
Another thing that is ludicrous is the fact that Bacchanal  charges children the same price as adults. If you wanted excellent quality of food for the same price do yourself a favor and go to the Wynn. If you want a great selection at a cheaper price go to the Rio or Flamingo, where the food quality is better and the service is above par much better than Bacchanal.

This buffet is top notch and everything I tried was delicious.  After Bally's Sterling Sunday Brunch ($95), this is definitely my favorite buffet in Las Vegas.  The items that really stuck out to me were the small plate dishes, the sushi, and the meat carving station, but everything I had was perfect.  I didn't even look at the huge dessert area.  It's a little overwhelming, but it's a great buffet.  Go slow and pace yourself or your experience will be over way too soon.  I went on Sunday for the champagne brunch ($43) and felt like I really got a really great deal.  The "champagne" actually says "champagne "on the side of the bottle, but it's an inexpensive sparkling wine from California.  I have nothing but good things to say about this buffet.  It seems to be very popular and the line looked crazy long when we left.  When we arrived, it was about 10:30 a.m. on Sunday and the line was not bad at all.  The service was outstanding and our champagne and water glasses were always full, despite out best efforts.  Caesar's has done a great job on the contemporary design of the restaurant and it does not have a cafeteria feel.  If you're in Vegas, don't miss this new awesome buffet.  Food-5 stars, Value-4 stars, service-5 stars, Ambiance-5 stars.

Okay ... I'm a buffet maniac. For $54 you have to think you can get a custom steak and a lobster tail at a traditional restaurant. I was tired and hot... Still had to wait an hour off prime time on a Monday. When I finally got in, I did a walk around. Nothing spectacular visually to make me salivate. I went light and had marginal sushi. Salads were McDonald's style without the container. I did Love the two cheese choices and select cut dry salami. Went to the seafood cold section ... The smallest queen crab legs I ever saw. Pre split with almost zero meat... But great clarified butter. The oysters must have been on sale at the fish market... No meat. Clams the same cheap small Manila style .. Oyster shooters all tomato juice and micro oysters. The shrimp was standard on ice. The meat section looked good but.... Had a select quality prime beef.. Tough and forgotten..beef ribs 90% fat... Baby backs were dry as the bones. The worst Cole slaw I ever tasted .... Now for the triumph ... The deserts saved the day... I sampled as much as I could... And I have to give it one of the best ratings for every aspect of flavor enhancing deluxiousness. Thats what the three stars were for. I still would pass this place and get everything on a Burger King menu for less than $50 and you'll be happier. Go to the Oyster Bar @ the Palace and see sea food at its best...

I went to this buffet on Saturday 10/20/2012 and started to wait in line at like 6pm. It was a 130 minute wait from the end of the line to the cashier and then another 30 minute wait after paying the cashier to be seated. 170 minutes total! It was good that I wasn't hungry until like 8pm and I had my Ipad there with me so I was able to watch a movie so that wait wasn't that bad for me. 

I highly suggest going when you are not hungry so that when you finally get seated, you will get hungry. Also I highly suggest bringing a laptop or an ipad so you can watch your movie while you are waiting to pass the time.

Unfortunately on the day I went, they ran out of the stone crab claws and watermelon juice. Their souffle were horrible and by far the worse souffle I've had, but the rest food were good and this place is probably the best buffet in Vegas. I will probably go again, but I will be in line at around 4pm so that I can only wait for 1 hr instead of 2 hrs or greater.

This is a really good buffet, with all of the different varieties, flavors, cuisines, and beautiful presentations. However, it is not a delectable sreak and lobster dinner. Buffets should be attractive to the value oriented diner. One could eat very well at a fine dinning restaurant for the price of this buffet. I was very dissapointed, not because of the food, but because of the price. This buffet does not equal fine dining and should not attempt to fool value oriented diners. Let's face it, buffets should be really good food at a fair price and not attempt to present itself as fine dining.

This is the pick of the strip buffets in my opinion at the moment. Yes, it could possibly be the most expensive, but the quality of food and environment of the place is fantastic. 

The seafood section consists of the usual crab legs but also freshly shucked oysters, jumbo shrimp, clams and cooked dishes like paella - yum! The bbq'd and roasted meats are exceptional, the ribs were full of smokey goodness but strangely enough, the highlight for me wasn't the prime rib but was the spicy pork sausages. These are not your typical sausages, try it and you'll know what I mean!

There was a great selection of mexican dishes as well as some decent looking pastas and pizzas. The Asian selection was pretty good and there was also some good bbq pork and duck. There is a made to order ramen and pho bar which is a good change and along with the soups on offer, they help wash down greasy or cold items very nicely.

The dessert bar at Bacchanal is exceptional, the choice is huge and one does not have a dessert stomach large enough to try everything unfortunately. They have about 8 flavors of frozen icecream/mochi's which were great ! These are a good change from your standard icecream / sorbet options at other buffets.

I arrived just before the dinner session, paid the lunch price and reaped the benefits of the dinner menu. The big advantage of doing this isn't the price, but the lack of the queue which does look quite nasty later on in the evening. So skip lunch and head for an early dinner would be my advice.

Came here for dinner one night and I really enjoyed how many different options there are. The food seemed to be of high quality, but in order to get your money's worth you need to come on an empty stomach
First off they charge you a service charge off the back with out notice. That's bs then you sit down and wait another freaken 20min for drinks and you call this service but the food made it up.

My colleague and I arrived at 6:45p on a Wednesday. We registered and were told to come back at 9:30p to stand in line. Seriously? Yes, seriously. Anyway, the line was super long. Forget all that waiting. We decided to pay the extra $25 per person to go through the VIP line.  My recommendation is to pay the extra fee to get in ASAP. Otherwise, you'll stand line for a long time looking like a hungry loser.

The food was awesome. I focused mostly on the seafood.  The cold crab legs, oysters, shrimp, ceviches, etc., were delicious and fantastic.  The server was okay, she could have been more attentive with the drinks and cleaning off plates faster.  All in all, this by far is the best Buffett I've been to in my entire life.

They've been open for a few years and we finally went to check it out. We're not huge Buffet people, but heard they were one of the best in town. I saw on their website that they offer all you can drink mimosas or champagne so that was enough to get me to go.

We went on a Saturday and went for brunch, they had been open for maybe and hour and a half when we made it to the line. Now I did my share of research on Yelp, saw what people had to say about wait times...but my goodness I didn't expect this.

I check in at the automated kiosk, punched in how many people and out spit a ticket telling me the wait time was 2 hours and when to come back. The kicker, you come back to wait in a line! So the time on the ticket isn't the time that you get escorted to your seat.

With a 1 month old child I didn't want to wait 2 hours, and I didn't want to find another place to eat so I paid $20 for the 3 of us to skip the line and go VIP. Honestly on a day like Saturday or Sunday it's worth it.

We were seated, everything is so pretty inside it doesn't look like your average buffet at all. Fancy! 

The lady kept the champagne flowing, on the sweeter side and not dry. We were seated in the front area near the seafood line, and much to my surprise the buffet wrapped all the way towards the right in the back. 

The only con for me was that the crab isn't steamed, I prefer steamed but it was still good.

Oyster Bloody Mary shooters were good
Bbq pork buns, fried noodles, roasted duck and char siu were good
The sea bass in miso was tasty and so was the salmon
Oysters were fresh and yummy
I tried some of the prime rib (they didn't ask what cut) so I got what they gave and it was dry and over done
Mashed potatoes and gravy were good, and the spicy sausage too
The fried chicken in the basket with waffle fries were dry

The dessert choices...not really impressed. It's great if you like crepes, and gelato. But the baked cakes and other goodies were not impressive. The only thing I loved loved were the almond cookies....best I've ever tasted.

Service was good, she kept the champagne filled, water filled and our plates cleared. 

Next time we go I'll probably give the Japanese/sushi a try, and perhaps the Italian food. I always feel that with a buffet you have to go for the most expensive eats which is he seafood.

The buffet totally makes up for the long wait.

My party and I went Friday night to kick off our Vegas weekend. Initially I was so pissed at how they made us wait in this small corner FOREVER after telling us our table would be ready in 15 minutes. But we got to the buffet and all was forgiven.

They have different cuisines so naturally, I had to try each one. :P My friends were all about that seafood life. Unlimited oysters and snow crab legs, cooked and cold! I actually fell in love with their duck. They had American, Italian, Asian (including some Dim Sum!!), Mexican, etc. They also had small plates of chef's specialty.

The dessert bar is HEAVEN. I slipped into a food coma and was sent to buffet dessert bar heaven! They had gelato, cakes, crepes, flan, macarons, cake balls, chocolate covered strawberries (different kinds too!), and anything you could think of.

If I could have afforded to eat their every night, I would have!

I've been to bacchanal buffet a couple times over the past 2 years. Each time has been about the same..average wait, above average buffet food, and tons of people. However, today is the first time I've had to sign in on the kiosk prior to seeing the hostess. Signing in your party at the kiosk and receiving a text notification when your wait is up, seems efficient. However, there is an option to pay additional $25 to skip the wait and be seated immediately! So there is a wait if you chose not to pay extra, crazy I know..but just a heads up...if you plan on going to the buffet RSVP your party online ahead of time for a short wait.

This is wayyy better than the Wicked Spoon. Though the wait can be a bit long and dinner pricing ($50+) per person can be a tad bit costly, the buffet selection is one of the best in Vegas. 

Tip: Try to get your moneys worth by filling your self with brisket + crab legs :)

Not sure if this place is worth the 3 hour wait.  The lines will probably die down once the buffet isn't as new any more.  But once you get in, you'll be overwhelmed by the amount of food options to choose from.  It's like the Buffet @ Wynn or Wicked Spoon @ Cosmo but 2-3x larger.  There's Asian, Mexican, Meats (American?),  and Seafood sections to cater to everyone's needs.  In addition, there's freshly squeezed oj, cucumber, and tropical (mango, pineapple) juice near the seafood section which is near the front.

This is probably the best buffet I've been to in Vegas. The had a variety of things from raw seafood to grilled meats to chinese food. I love eating raw oysters but the oysters here lacked any taste. The grilled meats were good but only if you got a piece that wasn't overcooked. I went back for the ribeye multiple times and it was a hit or miss. 

I arrived at around 5:30 and didn't have to wait at all. Left around 7ish and saw the huge line. If you do go to a Vegas buffet, wait for this one. If you've already been here once it's probably not worth it to wait again.

WOW. There are a million reasons why this buffet is the best on The Strip! Though the price point is a bit high, the brunch buffet is totally worth it. Dishes are served in individual portions with some truly creative and savory options. The eggs Benedict is the best we've had at a buffet, probably because it (like most of the hot dishes) is made in small batches so it stays fresh. The croque madame, sweet potato tots, chicken and waffles, and tiny blueberry pancakes were standout offerings. The dessert bar, while extensive, was mostly filled with underwhelming breakfast pastries during the brunch hours.  The real stars here are the entrees, along with the fresh juice bar - cucumber basil and watermelon juices were amazing. If you're going to eat at only one buffet on The Strip - make it this one.

What can I add to the 6800+ yelp reviews? My server was above average, but then all service in Vegas is amazing. I expected food quality to match this. Not so much. Sushi was unimpressive. Seafood was OK; Oyster Shooters were excellent. I ate a ton of pealed shrimp. No room for carved meats.

Stuffed and gliding toward the exit, I passed the dessert bar, invisible until that point: Certainly I HAD TO TRY Some!

I may not need to eat again during the month!
wait to get in a line to wait more, and the employee makes it sound like waiting 6 good isn't a big deal... great service, should have told me earlier dimwitted idiots.

I came here on a Monday night at 5:00 PM and there was NO LINE!!!! ZERO!!! WOOHOO!! Paid $45.99 (a little on the pricey end for a Vegas buffet) but it's worth at least one try. However, I definitely would NOT wait over an hour for this buffet. I can't believe some people wait 2 hours! It IS one of the better buffets in Vegas (possibly the best!) but I personally wouldn't want to wait that long for it. 

I definitely got my money's worth from all the oysters I ate! YUM! The oysters here are small and slightly sweet (similar to Kumamoto oysters... not sure if they were those exactly though). I loved how they weren't briney! Just add a little bit of lemon and tapatio and voila! perfecccction! I also really liked their cocktail shrimp. They also have crab legs, but if you want WARM crab legs, they're in a separate section towards the back near the Asian food! Just ask the guy for it and he'll grab them out of a hot pot and plate them for you! The crab legs that you see next to the oysters in the seafood section are cold. Those are the ones you just get yourself.  

I liked how this buffet had a lot of their foods already plated so it was easy to just grab and go (similar to Wicked Spoon Buffet at the Cosmo). They also have a very wide variety of foods! Seafood, lots of meats (prime rib, lamb chops, etc. which were pretty good), Asian food (sushi, Chinese, etc), Italian, Mexican, seriously all kinds! One of my fave things I had was the corn on the cob. It sounds so simple and random but the flavor and the juiciness... OMG SO GOOD!! I also had a lobster corn bisque/soup which was amazingggg. I really enjoyed everything I ate here. 

I also really liked their dessert bar. They have the usual assortment of cakes, pastries, and cute little desserts like the other buffets. They can also make crepes! And they also have sorbets/ice cream as well as different flavors of mochi ice cream. Super soft and yummy! They also have macarons here!! I tried several different flavors and they were just A-OK. Not very consistent in terms of texture. Not as good as the ones at Bouchon Bakery so don't expect too much for the macarons. 

Overall beautiful buffet, definitely one of the best in Vegas! Worth a visit for sure!

Timing is everything.  After reading some of the horror stories about the wait, we decided to go for early brunch on a monday.  We got there about 10:15, which is the perfect time.  Most of the breakfast items were still out, but they began switching over to lunch about 10:30 or so.  Basically no wait, but by the time we left around 11:30 it was full and a pretty good line.  Food was well done and the presentation was perfect. Many items were served in single portion dishes or cast iron pans(cuts down on the waste)  AAmazing choices and even a crepe bar.  There are other reviews  that go more in detail about the great food but I wanted to give a heads up on the timing.

Cold pressed juices by the glass. Stone crab legs. Dim sum. Tacos made to order. Carving station. Noodle soup and pasta stations.  The choices are seemingly endless.  Don't focus on just getting your money's worth but instead enjoy the creativity and variety of top quality foods from around the world all in once luxurious meal.  Make sure you get those seats with the armrests because you're gonna need a breather with all the flavors you'll be enjoying.  Leave a little room for a last push to top it all off with some gelato though!

Awesome food, delicious dessert,  nice staffs, biggggg waiting line, expensive entrance fee ($50 on weekends).
Definitely recommend it!

Ok. This review comes with much explanation.
We have, twice now, gotten what is called, "The Buffet of Buffets Pass." What it amounts to is bacchanalian (see what I did there?) levels of buffet food smashing through your slotmachine for 24 hrs straight. If you are not an absolute mutant of munching, a gastronomical giant, a competitive eater in-training... DO NOT GO THAT ROUTE.
Twice now, I've gotten so sick that, when we finally got to this
MECCA OF SELF-SERVICE, I couldn't really do the proper damage. Upcharge and all... ugggghhh!
That said, I've had a bunch of great bites here. So damn tasty. 
We plan to come back someday, without a timeline of buffets forcing my guts into panic. I'll update the review, and I'm sure they'll steal the extra star I've always assumed they'd earn.

This is probably one of the best buffets I have ever been to. It has a large variety of different dishes from different cuisines. It is quite pricey but the best time to come in is around 2:30pm and pay for the lunch price. I love how they display their dishes and plate each individual portions of food. If you are a seafood lover, make sure to stack your plate up with the steam crab legs! I wish I wasn't so full that I didn't get to try the prime rib but there will be next time! Definitely go on an empty stomach because you would want to try everything!
Food was cold and bland.  Customer service was awful, Raz is about the worst restaurant manager I've ever spoken with.  Went for Sunday brunch and was very disappointed.
Love this place! I paid the $35 for express pass per person . It's so worth it not having to wait around for 2-3 hours.
It's pretty good. Tons of food choices and there wasn't a line for us. Loved the sugar free cheesecake. Definitely worthy!!

it used to be our favorite buffet place in Vegas.  And it's Chinese food section(and king's crab leg) is where it stand out because it provide GINSENG soup which make my whole family happy.  

The price increases every time I visit (its around 60 per person for dinner) but they replaced the famous ginseng soup with the cheap ox tail soup which really upset me.  And center egg with pork congee (皮蛋瘦肉粥) is replaced with base congee only which really ruined the Chinese section of the buffet.  

Their crab leg still good (although I don't understand why they cut the leg in half which really ruined the joy of eating a big leg) but this buffer really not worth the $60 price tag.
空間明亮 ，prime rib很好吃 ，甜點種類很多 ，也都好吃。但是中式方面種類比較少，但是我不介意，因為我也沒拿。墨西哥料理也不錯。可以再去的餐廳。

Good pizza and warm food. I really enjoyed the pizza and some of the italian dishes. The steak was tough as a rubber boot and the price left something to be desired. I was not impressed by the dessert selection.

Went for dinner, and it was nothing exciting, nothing amazing. Pretty disappointed for a $60 meal. How did I get so many recommendations for this!? Went on a Saturday and they said they would call us back in 2 hours. They get your number to text you when they are ready which is nice so you can go explore. We went to the forum shops to kill time and they ended up texting us to come back in a little over an hour so it wasn't bad. 

The stations: seafood, meat, Mexican, Italian, bread, Asian, salads, desserts.

I couldn't find anything I wanted to get seconds of! So sad. Well I would actually have gotten seconds of the crepe if I wasn't so full. But that's it, nothing else stood out, and the crepe only stood out because you can't mess up Nutella. Bahh, I spent $60 on whatever food, should have stopped walking when I hit Nobu.

Crab legs were good, I liked cold better than the hot ones which they serve at the Italian station. There is NO line for the hot ones. I repeat NO LINE for HOT CRAB legs, so go there first if you only want them hot. The only line I had to wait in was for the seafood station and it takes a while because everyone is filling their plates with crab legs and oysters to get their $'s worth. 

Overall not as many choices as I thought. Not even good quality. Meat was dry, seafood was low quality, Italian station pizza was horrible, sushi did not look exciting, dumplings weren't bad, bread was hard, didn't even try the Mexican station because it was so regular. All in all, nothing exciting. I looked back at the pictures and they looked more fun and exciting before, maybe it went downhill?

Dessert station looked so pretty. Too bad I tried ALL of them and only liked the Oreo mousse and the crepe. Waited 8 minutes for the Chocolate Soufflé, which you ask them to make, and it tasted like powdered fake chocolate, like the ones used for hot chocolate, so gross!!! Cake pop look a likes were gross, the peanut butter cone things were so cute, but the cone was stale. Gelato wasn't so bad so definitely try that. So sad, I have such a big sweet tooth I thought I'd be in heaven. I was so disappointed with every bite.

My whole group was actually disappointed and they love buffets.  

If you like good quality food, don't do this. If you like tons of options and endless eating with mediocre food you'll probably be happy. I'm more of a person that would rather have an entree and dessert that blows my mind, than 10 entrees and desserts that are very forgetful. This is more of a bunch of unlimited 2-3 star food.

To give context: I consider myself veteran of premium buffet. In SE Asia where I come from buffet dining in 5 star restaurant is very common and popular. Prices range from most basic $52 to $100 per person. 

So with that said, Bacchanal was on my list of must-visit since so many good reviews and you gotta try buffet in Vegas right?!

Well, if I want to spend money I'm not sure I would spend it here. The number of food selection was good but taste kinda "meh" (exclude dessert)
1) service: excellent. We came early before 5pm, didn't have to wait. Got a table and waitstaff was efficient clearing and all great
2) recommend: street tacos, crabs & seafood, few of the dim sums, soups, cheese and meat selections, Thai dishes. 
3) for the choice of variety its great but it wasn't memorable. They do better with the western dishes than ethnic variety. You could get your money's worth just by having their fresh seafood. For me I like to taste a bit of everything so the tapas-size portions were great and prevents too much wastage. I didn't try any of the pasta/pizza carb-loaded selections. 
4) Dessert: this was excellent. The number of choices was amazing. Definitely save room for this. Great small portions.

Was not impressed this time around. The oysters were sandy and didn't even look like oysters, they resembled some sort of seafood that had been thrown in a blender, then placed back onto its shell. I did however enjoy the crab legs, then again how could you mess up on that? 

The service was great. I would give them 5/5. 

Probably will not be returning or recommending.

Omg! What can I say?!?!? Definitely an impressive spread & well worth the the price. I've been to many buffets & this is by far the best yet! There are 4 different stations (not including the desert station) with a large amount of choices at each one. Rack of lamb, various type ribs, prime rib, large assortment of seafood (hot & cold), sushi, noodles, Italian, & Mexican food. It was a HUGE spread. Loved the ice cream & macaroons more then Jean Philips Pastries. Thai tea bobba
Terrible service. Extremely slow and unorganized. Dairy Queen has more intelligent people working there. No recommendation from me.

I just came for my Summer vacation with my two other friends, and I recommended Bacchanal since its one of the hottest buffet among all other buffet. We have gotten 35 dollors of food credit, so we decided to spend it at Bacchanal. So we asked one of hostesses Maria about using the food credit and she told us that we have to go to the front desk and get the rewards card (but we were told that we needed to charge it to our room). She was kept saying that we have to get the card so we had to go all the way back to the front desk to ask. They told us the same thing and tried to call the buffet. As they confirmed it with the buffet we came all the way back but Maria was saying the same thing, not even making an effort to ask someone else, being rude, and rolling her eyes. So we had to go ask the cashier for ourselves and wasted 20 min. It is okay if she was confused and didnt have enough info, but shes a hostess and she should at least show some effort to make a clarification. This is my first day in Vegas and I think the start is little annoying. I think you guys should give better service education.

Once you go Bacchanal - you'll never go back.

I first came to Bacchanal three years ago and to this day, I still haven't found another Vegas buffet that I preferred more than this (and trust me - I've had my share of Vegas buffets). The selection is simply ENORMOUS and at times, overwhelming. I typically walk around first to devise some sort of strategy but just end up stuffing my face with as much food as I can possibly devour.

Some of my personal favorites include the sushi, the prime rib and the seafood (oysters, clams) and of course my absolute favorite - the crab legs! TIP: Get the crab legs hot! There's also a taco station and pretty much any sort of food you can imagine. Did I mention that the dessert bar is FREAKING AMAZING? The dessert section is HUGE. The variety ranges from macarons to cake pops to different cakes and pastries to gelato to mochi and so. much. more.

Dinner was around $70 and lunch is just a little less than that, but since you're already in Vegas,  DON'T SKIMP OUT ON THE BEST BUFFET EVER!

So many choices , not bad !
But the oyster r not so good.

食物的選擇蠻多的，也不錯，不過牡蠣倒是不怎麼樣... 很多人排隊，要有排隊的準備。

A stellar buffet experience from start to finish. Remember to sign up for Total Rewards to get a slight discount on your meal. Dined during the weekend brunch ($39.99 non TR members, $36.99 TR members). Brunch comes with unlimited mimosas and champagne. 

The buffet is very large, but well laid out. It is roughly divided into seafood, american/meats, mexican, italian, asian, and desserts. One of the many highlights of our gastronomic adventure was the fresh juice that they have available (I sampled the watermellon, orange juice, and peach juice). Also worth mentioning was the prime rib and brisket. Highly recommend getting the brisket with Jack Daniels BBQ sauce. The dessert station featured ice cream, made to order crepes, amongst other pastries. Overall, would highly recommend. Bacchanal has surpassed Wynn and Wicked Spoon over at Cosmo to be the best buffet on the strip IMHO.

Why why why? I've never been so disappointed in my life with a buffet and I don't even know why! Oh wait I do, it's because I waited 2 hours and spend 80 bucks per person on this inedible-ness. 
In Vegas during LDW and everyone in my group was most excited over this. Not the partying, not the gambling, jus bacchanal. 
We have heard such good reviews, I heard they serve caviar and some of my group been here 3 times, yet somehow it still failed us on every degree possible. 
The food was crappy, the dessert was disgusting, the price was jacked up because it was a holiday and the food was crappy. I mean for 80 bucks I could have had better food at any old buffet. The selection of food was not extensive and poorly seasoned but the dessert section was the worst part! The ice cream was melting, the macarons tasted and looked like melted plastic and all the cakes made me want to throw up.
Nothing was fresh and I had to keep stuffing myself because i couldn't jus let my 80 bucks go to waste. 
I really hope that it was bad luck and I went during busy holiday so the quality lacked over the quantity produced. I mean wicked spoon was better and I hate wicked spoon!

Experience was fair, having worked in hospitality and having knowledge of 100% from what FOH is suppose to give. 

Our server was great though.

We went during one of the down times so the wait wasn't long at all. I was excited to try this buffet out. 

The lamb and elote is what I recommend, well any of the meats you can't really go wrong. 

I tried the oysters and they were alright, the food is comparable to Paris Hotel. 

The cute little juice containers and was almost tempted to take one. 

Must try the truffle scalloped potatoes, that was delicious.

Overall I was satisfied and probably would come back again with my husband cause he wanted to try this place.

I have to say, good job Ceasers for FINALLY making a buffet that *should* be in a place like yours.  I've been wanting to go since it was announced that they were even making it and then the reviews came out.  But the last time I was in Vegas, they had just opened, and it was NYE weekend so we didn't even venture to the strip (I was staying with a friend who lives in Vegas).  But this time, we were staying across the street.  There was NO WAY I was going to miss out.

Dinner during the weekend is about $55, Sunday Brunch was $45.  I think.  You get like a dollar or two off with your Total Rewards membership card.

There is a virtual queue - you will see the computers set up.  Make sure to go up and pull a ticket.  This will tell you when to come back to get back in line to pay and then get seated.  There are NO SIGNS for this or anyone telling you to do it.  I'm sure it's not as crazy during the week but on the weekends, this is a must.

When my friend and I were there Friday night pretty late and we had NO problems getting in.  We didn't even know about the virtual queue.  But on Saturday when we returned with more friends, we were denied entry and it was only 730pm.  They had already filled up their virtual queue and were not letting anyone else get in line.  It was basically sold out.  We had talked to a lady in line and she said that they were there at 6, got a ticket and it said to come back at 8.  The buffet closes at 1030pm.  Since we were hungry, we left and went to another place for dinner.  

However, we did return Sunday for brunch before we left town. 

Now on to the food!

There are several stations:

Seafood - oysters on the half shell, crab legs (cold and warmed up with hot water at request), shrimp, and various other seafood dishes.  There is a warm drawn butter machine for you!

Italian - pizza, pasta, meatballs and a made to order pasta station

Asian - an assortment of dim sum items (buns, shumai, etc) plus the usual chinese fare - kung pao chicken, chow mein, fried rice etc. also had some pad thai and some other meat options that I don't remember. A small assortment of sushi (there was definitely more fish on the sushi during dinner than brunch) There is also a noodle station to order where you can get udon, pho or ramen.

Carving station - there is so much meat here, your head will spin.  Prime Rib, baby back ribs, smoked brisket, smoked turkey, a variety of sausage links, lamb chops.  During brunch, they had more sausage varieties, but I had to wait until it was closer to lunch time to get some brisket and ribs.  I asked the guy carving and he went in the back and got them.  I had turkey on Friday dinner but they had run out of the brisket (since we were close to closing time).  Both were really good.

Mexican - you can get tacos to order.  There was also beans, rice, carnitas, machaca, chicken, a salsa bar and a juice bar.

American -  I don't know what else to call this area - it's where they have the mashed potatoes, veggies, mac and cheese, etc.  They didn't have any fried chicken when we were there for dinner, but at brunch they had it to go with waffles.  There were sweet potato tots, roasted potatoes, french fries. I think i seriously had a plate of potatoes.  There were even baked potatoes available.  Mini sliders (which we were sure they had been sitting for a while) were a little dry.

Salad bar - I didn't venture too much here - but there was a variety of salads and dressings you could get.  There was also a lot of fruit, a variety of cheese and cured meats.  And a huge area with a variety of bread.

Dessert - There is a gelato bar with some interesting flavors, crepes to order with plenty of whipped cream, berries, bananas foster and nutella to your hearts content.   During dinner there were macaroons and chocolate covered strawberries but they didn't have it when we were there during brunch.  There is the usual variety of cakes, cookies, brownies, and creme brulee as well.

I'm sure I missed all sorts of things.  The food was pretty amazing.  There were a few things that we didn't like, but for the most part it was really good.  I mean - we went twice in  a weekend !  Definitely will be back.

Must try buffet. Expensive. Long wait time but worth it. Go before the dinner pricing. Get some plates of that delicious crab for the table and enjoy! The receipt says there is a 2 hour limit but my waitress said we could stay as long as we wanted. Love this place.

Want to eat like you just hit the jackpot?  Come here.

It's not cheap.  It's $55 for dinner but it was worth every cent.  Get there early because after 6PM the line gets pretty crazy.

Excellent quality of food and taste was on point.  King crab legs were in the Italian section and upon request.  You're welcome :)

My one and only con was their molten "lava" cake.  There was no lava...

Best buffet I've tried on the strip so far.  Wicked Spoon can't touch this.

I have sung the praises of Bacchanal in my previous reviews, but for dinner the price is just too steep and the quality, not quite up to where I had expected. I actually believe that the brunch buffet at Bacchanal is more worth it - for 40 ish you get unlimited mimosas, sangrias, etc and an expansive fresh juice selection. For dinner, $50 bucks gets you an impressive selection of meats and seafood, but no booze. The line can also be insanely long - luckily my buddy had his diamond card and we were immediately ushered in and seated - by the time we finished, the people we originally stood in line with were just finally making their way to pay. I also preferred brunch because they had smoked salmon, red velvet pancakes, among other options. For the price of dinner ($50 ish), you'd be better served trying out a nice restaurant than gorging at Bacchanal.

In terms of quality, price, and time, I consider this place a ripoff. Decent food, but unreasonably expensive. The food selection on a normal day isn't super special. For me, the highlights were the lamb, salmon, and salads. Aside from that though, the crab was salty, the crawfish quality was bad, and the dessert was bleh. I'm am overall disappointed and unimpressed by this buffet. You can get better quality and more reasonable prices at a Reno buffet.

Beware physically challenged people! The policy of Caesars Palace is that if you are physically challenged and using a cane, a Walker , or a wheelchair, you will be allowed in by yourself, however if you are with somebody else they will have to pay an additional $20 to go through the handicap line with you. This can be very problematic, especially if you are a diabetic and have to eat at a certain time with medications and insulin. I can see this for presenting a problem in light of the expense of the meal. The additional $20 is ridiculous when you consider the cost of a meal itself . I guess Caesars is going to go broke if they don't charge that extra $20 . I guess most people wouldn't have much sympathy, seeing as 
this means somebody would jump the line , but in most cases we would only have one additional person with us as a helper .
I consider this highway robbery, and will not be spending my dollars at Caesars again!
Sure the food is great there, but there is so many other buffets in town of close or equal value and quality that do assist the handicapped that it is not worth they extra money and time.

AMAZING! I've always gone to the Bellagio's buffet, but this beats it hands down. Huge selection of incredible foods. Cold cuts, crab legs, ceviche, prime rib. And dessert is delicious: so many varieties of gelato, a crepe station, wonderfully thick cookies and so much more. The atmosphere is buzzing and there's always a line to get in. Arrive early to avoid crowds and give yourself plenty of time to enjoy all the buffet has to offer. This is not something you'll want to rush through.

Had the groupon, which I thought was a good idea with the bottomless mimosas. I only had two. Hubby only tasted his and said no thanks, so actually I had three. In all, food was pretty tasty. They have different sections with cuisine from different parts of the world. I hit the cheese bar without mercy. Pretty good. Had eggs Benny, also delicious. Staff was pretty friendly and organized. They also offer an omlette bar and crepe bar, both made to order.  They also have a seafood section of which I didn't partake. It's too early for seafood but it looked very fresh. Desserts were plenty and very eye-fetching. They also offer gelato. Would probably go again even though it's kind of on the expensive side. $30 a person for breakfast,  I believe but hey you're going to spend more on penny slots so might as well.

For what you pay for, it should be safe to assume that they are holding themselves to the highest standards and you are getting the best quality of food. My friends and I (party of 5) visited Bacchanal buffet on April 14th. We were looking forward to  having our meal here and we enjoyed the food we ate and selections were good. After our meal however, we felt sick. We were vomiting and it was just the worst experience. We felt so sick for hours that we almost missed our concert. 

My friend contacted their customer service this week to inform them of what happened and to possibly get our money back (we spent $250)  due to our horrible experience. They replied but no mention of a refund or try to make our experience right. My friend is also a rewards member, you would think they would do something to try to keep her as a member. 

Will not be coming back. It's not worth getting sick over. Eat at your own risk.
