If you aren't going for the crab legs and filet mignon, there's no point in spending so much money. The rest of the food was just mediocre. Service was amazing though. Be prepared to wait forever unless you fork up an extra $25 to eat sooner than 3 hours, which I did.
worth every penny spent always recommending and i have eaten here plenty of times

This was my 3rd visit but is was my family's 1st visit and we were treated exceptionally well by Chef O'Mack and Chef Nico! The king crab legs that were brought out were so delicious as was the beautiful sushi platter made for us fresh by their Sushi Chef! The buffet was clean and presentable as always and the food was fresh and delicious!

My First ever Buffet in Vegas!

Went here 2 years ago and went again the following year

Highly recommended with all the different varieties of food and awesome yummy quality!!! especially the seafood and desserts! 
amazing!! 

Pricey...... but Amazingg!!!! 


*Tip! Try to go during Lunch and then it becomes dinner Price is cheaper at lunch and then when it becomes dinner they hand out the seafood! :)
so many options where it made difficult to experience all dishes in one visit not once did I have a bad experience food service and everything was excellent.

It's the best buffet ever!!! I've been here so many times, we try a lot buffet in different casino, this is the best one in LV.  Fresh crab leg, scallop , shrimp , ribs, clam , oyster, so many choice, very very good!!!

This review is only for the pricing of this buffet.. I came to this buffet at around 3:30 pm thinking that there will be no waiting since nobody really eats dinner at 3:30.  Little kiosk says there is wait time of two and half hours and we can pay extra $35/person to skip the wait time.. this really bothers me.  First of all, place wasn't busy at all.  It literally seems like they want to over charge ppl.  $55 and some change per person for buffet is already expensive compare to other places and yet you guys want to charge another $35??? Total of $90 per person?? Not worth the money.. caesar's palace is going little too crazy with this buffet pricing.  I seen many ppl complaint about this pricing and gentlemen who was standing in front with tablet on his hand had this attitude showing too bad if you can't afford it.   It's not the matter of if I can afford it or not.. I won't just give free $35 to already rich owners of this property!

This buffet is located in Ceasars Palace. Don't even bother trying others buffets in Las Vegas because you will be disappointed. The quality at the Bacchanal is much higher than any other buffets on the strip. 

It's a bit pricey compared to all the other buffets but i don't regret trying it. 

The desserts are really good. I liked their salads too. For the seafood lovers, you won't be disappointed. There's a variety of seafood that you can have. 

Overall, it was a good restaurant.

Pretty good. This place ranks a close second out of the top 3 buffets in Vegas. I think Wicked Spoon has the best food and a more hip "cosmopolitan" ambiance. However, Bacchanal has much better food than Wynn buffet (ambiance at Wynn is probably more elegant though). 

Overall, I enjoyed my meal. We had a good server who made sure to bring additional sodas and take away our plates. They had crab legs that were halved making the crab meat easy to access. The people behind the counter seemed rather lazy and reluctant to warm the crab legs, but at least they did. I can't remember any particular buffet dish that stands out.

The dining area is quite comfortable, the lighting is just right, and the seats are comfortable too. The buffet looks new, clean, and nice.

If Wicked Spoon wasn't open, this would be the next buffet choice for sure!

Worth the wait! I went for breakfast and dinner last weekend- be warned that the breakfast buffet is mostly a lunch buffet.  I didnt see a ton of egg options, and they most of the lunch stations open (asian noodles/soups, pizza, ect).  HIghly recommend the taco bar if you go for dinner.  The lamb chops where incredible!! I don't even eat seafood and thought it was a five star buffet.

We were really looking forward to this buffet and were SO DISAPPOINTED! Most of the food was bland or poorly cooked or it was way too salty! Crab legs were overcooked and the shells were soft. Wagyu beef was tough and flavorless. I could go on but it was absolutely not worth it. $59 for brunch plus tax and tip. We told the managers Samantha and Ross and they listened but didn't seem to care. Wicked spoon is MUCH better and costs less.

Pros: sushi bar will slice up yellowtail and salmon sashimi upon request and it is a great cut of sushi.
Fried chicken.
Cous cous (surprisingly).
Deli meats and cheeses.
All asian selections.
Oysters were really good.

Cons: Crab legs were a bit smaller and not as sweet as the Wynn's.
Starches in bbq/american fare were a bit underseasoned.
Fish had a lot of bones.
Overall, the dinner buffet was well worth the price as the buffet selections were never ending and the desserts were awesome. Will definitely come back for lunch/brunch.
I really don't know what the hype is been here 3xs and each time it's just reg buffet food nothing special. Maybe the glass cup decor but it's just a reg buffet with nothing that stands out

Oh so good!! The selections were awesome. From crab legs, braised beef, Chinese food, sushi, good ol American classics to a variety of delicious desserts! The presentation is delightful and service was good! Only qualm...the wait! First you have to check in at an automated kiosk..it tells you what time to come back to wait in line. Ok...we came at 7:30pm and it told us to come back an hr later. We came back an hour later to stand in line..only to find that you had to wait another hr plus in line before you can get seated!!! I guess this is to ensure REALLY TRULY hungry before entering! I sure was! I was HANGRY!! Lol!!!

I have only ONE complaint about this place keeping it from a 5 star rating.... It really sucks to pay $96, wait in line outside for over an hour THEN have to wait another 45 mins just to get some crab legs on your plate.... A: because of the huge line and B: because of all the rude tourists cutting in said huge line...... that aside.... the food "once I actually got some almost 2 hours into the experience" was really good.... I LOVE that they have individually portioned Wedge Salad.... I ate 3 of them.... and OMG they have coffee flavored Mochi Creams... that are JUST as good as the ones you pay $2.25 each for at Mitsuwa Market... I ate like 6 of those and had I known they were there before I was full... I'd have eaten more.... I think next time I will Start with the Mochi creams... and leave the 45 min crab line for the dumb tourists.... since you can get crab at EVERY buffet in vegas... and Carnival world is better crab anyway.... Oh.... also awesome street tacos too....

This buffet exceeded my hungry expectations. After waiting in the non-Express line, which took over an hour, I was very ready to start stuffing my face. I tried to start slow but once you walk in everything looks so delicious you can't help yourself. 

I started with the Asian stations. The sushi wasn't great. I really enjoyed the different salads and the  veggies were so fresh. Then I moved onto the carving and seafood stations. This blew me away!! 
My favs- 

Crab legs- we had 3 servings (this alone would cost more than we spent)  
Mussel and clams- they come in a small serving bowl. There's corn, sausage, and potatoes in the bowl. Loved it!
Halibut dish
Truffel Mac & Cheese 
Lollipop Rib Eye- my bf went back for seconds
Desert station- so much fun! 

Overall everything was fabulous. The server was attentive and the food was top grade.  
Tip: Dress very comfy and ladies wear flats. You're going to have to wait in line so wear shoes that won't kill your feet. I promise it's worth it!

I'm getting started on my Vegas reviews with Bacchanal.  I chose Bacchanal as my birthday dinner because I have been DYING to eat here since it opened.  Unfortunately, it didn't really give me all I expected.  Don't get me wrong, it's a good buffet and they have a huge selection and most of what I ate was good, but I can get that at any buffet.

First, for dinner Sunday  night, it was $50.  We were just getting started on the buffet of buffets (feeling like this was the best way to hit Harrah's Groups buffets) so it was actually a $25 upcharge to the BoB to have dinner at Bacchanal.  Fine.  The line was about 30 minutes to get rung up and then another 15-20 to wait for a table.  Fine.

We get seated and head for the food parade and that's where I fell flat.  I started with the sushi as I've been wanting cold fresh items on this trip for some reason.  And it was nice that they did have more than just California rolls, including nice tuna ngiri which is what I love.  And, it was good, but I would have liked some soy sauce but there were no containers anywhere to put soy sauce and wasabi in!  In fact, throughout this visit, I found it incredibly hard to use any of the condiments because containers were few and far between.  I found myself using soup bowls for my horseradish, etc.  Crazy.

They do have a lot of little baskets and containers of things, they just happened to be things that didn't jump out at me, but some were super interesting if you like buckets of mussels, etc. then this is pretty cool.  But, they do the same thing at the Cosmopolitan Wicked Spoon Buffet and I just liked that one better for this type of buffet.

I think that in trying to have SO many dishes, the dishes they have fall flat.  Example is the carving station.  It is seriously LOADED with meats and sausages... pretty much anything you want is there.  I wanted Prime Rib.  For me, that is my buffet staple because they always have it and I rarely order it.  But the Prime Rib was so dry and tough, I was shocked.  That was not acceptable for a buffet of this caliber.

I had the same problem at the dessert bar.  The creme brulee wasn't set and was runny.  It wasn't good.  I was excited about the made to order souffles that they have because that and the crepe station were exactly what I expected them to have, but they only had banana souffles which is the one flavor I do not like, so I had to pass.  But the freshly  made crepes were delish.  Honestly, my favorite part was the dessert and they have a huge selection of mochi!!!  LOVED that.

So the money to food ratio made this not such a great value to me.  It was a disappointment and I don't expect to eat there again unless I had a complimentary opportunity to try again.  I would be happy at The M and their Studio B Buffet where the food is fantastic AND they have beer and wine included for like $30pp!

If you are going, I noticed the line went WAY down about 15 minutes before closing.  Might save you some time.

They have a vast amount of offerings and are sectioned based on types of food such as seafood, Chinese, Mexican, Italian and all sorts of meats. What really stood this place out from the rest are their selection of meats. From rib eye, -tip steak, beef wage, pork belly, etc...I enjoyed them. For the most part, their offerings are decent. I enjoyed their legato, but was not a fan of the rest of their desserts. That's  though.

visited this place on our stay at Caesars back on 1/10/16.
I'd rate this place a 4 out of 5.    It's a "Good Buffet"
dropped by this buffet for late breadfast at the last moment, but pleasantly surprised the fresh cooked food which has a variety to choose from. the max for me is one buffet if any when visiting vegas, since most buffet are not good. my two favorites in the past (wynn & bellagio) has gone downhill over the past few years, so this place was a pleasant surpise.

Well worth the price and the wait! We went at 3pm for dinner to avoid the line. Yet there was a line! The wait wasn't too bad, we got a table within 20 minutes. Everything was fresh and delicious, nice food presentation and great customer service. 

Excellent seafood selection
Fresh oysters
Crab legs 
Lobster clam chowder 
Cocktail shrimps 
Oyster shooter 
Crawfish
Salmon

I especially liked the authetic Chinese selections! 
Roasted duck
BBQ pork
Congee
Ginseng chicken soup
Dim Sum
Lo Mein

Needless to say, there were over 50 kinds of desserts to choose from.

Two hours into the meal I was 110% full. I guess I will come back next time for the stations I missed:
Full carving station 
Italian 
Salad
Cheese
Honeycomb 
Mexican
Soups
Bottles fruit juice

It was such a great experience!! Food was phenomenal!! The most I love about this buffet is their dessert bar!!! It got so many varieties to choose from and they all feel like heaven!!! Yum!!!! Absolutely the best!!!

We were very impressed with the array of different food available at this Buffet.
Pro's
1) Prime Rib.
2) Lamb chops ( ask for mint Jelly)
3) Sushi.
4) Dessert bar.
5) Fried chicken in a basket w/ sweet potato fries.
6) Crab legs. They were cut open, easy to eat.
Con's
1) Pork ribs were so salty they affected my taste on other items.
2) Signage on how to get to Buffet. We had a hard time finding it. Most casinos have better signage.

Overall a very good buffet.

This is my go-to buffet while in Las Vegas. They have so many different options including some that are not super traditional for buffets. (As well as the traditional: Chinese, Mexican, Italian). They have an international noodle section with udon, ramen, and pho. They also have extensive choices of meats (prime rib, rack of lamb, ribs, chicken, sausage) and seafood (fish, scallops, shrimp, oysters, crab legs). There is no going wrong. Even the pickiest eaters will find something to eat. The price is not cheap, but you are paying for quality food! It is $50 for lunch. Also look out for deals we got two lunch buffets for $25 each when we signed up for a credit card. 

I do want to say that as much as I love Bacchanal, I did witness something really uncomfortable during my last visit. I had exited the buffet and was waiting for the rest of my party when I saw one of the hostess run after an elderly lady that was well out of the hostess' way. She then said something to her, and the woman handed her a juice she had in her hand. The woman looked embarrassed and walked away. The hostess smugly walked back to the register. Bacchanal serves aguas frescas in glass containers that have a plastic lid. (They are by the Mexican station). This is what the hostess took from the lady. I thought it was completely unnecessary for a hostess to put someone through this over a drink. The hostess ran after her like she was a criminal. I'm well aware that taking food or drinks out of the restaurant is not allowed, because of my knowledge of buffets. But if Bacchanal has signs saying this, I have never seen them. Even if it is a rule, it should never shame it's guests. The aguas frescas do come in containers that make them seem like you can take them home. If they don't want guests to take them, they should just offer them in regular glasses like sodas. I would like to add that I actually got a drink to go, so if the glass is so precious they should communicate this more clearly. Las Vegas attracts people from all over the world. They should know not everyone knows the rules. I just can't imagine they are losing that much money over people taking these glasses! They charge a high price to eat there, and they are in a profitable casino! I did talk to the manager, and he apologized, and claimed they would rethink their approach to the policy. Not sure if this will happen, but it did change the view I have of this restaurant.

THE best buffet I had the pleasure of going to during my trip. I planned ahead and purchased a breakfast Groupon for $69 and this included VIP entry for two people and two mimosas. Normally I don't go for buffets because I feel like I never get my money's worth, especially ones this expensive. HOWEVER this one was an exceptional experience. 

Wednesday morning the spread included:

- Fried Chicken and waffle fries
- Shrimp and grits
- Spam Masubi
- Congee
- Red velvet pancakes
- Gelatos
- Seafood
- Mac and cheese
- Egg tacos
- Churros
- Steak and Eggs
- Eggs Benedict
- Sweet potato tater tots
- Fresh squeezed juices
- Sausage and bacon carving station
- Crepe station
- Dessert station: molten chocolate cake, salt water toffee, cheesecakes

I'm sure I'm missing the other 80% of items offered but you get the point. I didn't like everything I tried but the the items I did were fantastic. Overall a great experience and highly recommended if you want that "Vegas Buffet" experience.

I have been here multiple times and have always been satisfied, feeling the price is fairly well met with the service, experience, and good quality. But tonight was a major let down...
Where are the plates?! The lines are worse than ever and every spot where there are usually plates are completely empty. As soon as more come, people grab 2-3 because they don't know if they'll find some next time they get in line. Normally a big fan, but this is unacceptable.

Besides that, the people working are hurrying and responsive to any requests asked by customers. They're polite when having to push carts through crowds and I appreciate how hard they work. But I am really let down about the longer than average lines and wait due to the plate fiasco. The food is still top quality, which makes it all that much more disappointing to wait.

My husband and I visited here on a Thursday morning at 8:30. We had to wait in a small line for about 20 minutes, but we got to meet some really nice people from England, so the wait was enjoyable.
The restaurant itself was dazzling and elegant.
The cost of the buffet was around $90 (with tip), with one ticket for unlimited mimosas.
The service was prompt and there is something for everyone at this high class, upscale buffet. There was seafood, chicken and waffles, enchiladas, eggs and bacon, quiche, lobster benedict, red velvet pancakes, hand made hazelnut or fresh berry crepes, pizza, gelato, muffins, sushi and the list goes on and on.
The one thing I did not see was an omelette station, which seemed a little odd, but with all the other choices it did not really matter.
All of the food was delicious, just make sure that you come here extremely hungry in order to justify the cost.
We visited the buffet at the Bellagio and Harrah's and this was the one that I would recommend of the three.

Best lunch buffet! Lots of varieties!! I will definitely come back here again!!

There are price and time difference for lunch and dinner time. I would recommend checking the website for the pricing and time on the day you are looking to dine in.

This place is overpriced and the food and service sucks beyond belief. $173 for 3 people and the seafood portion was all frozen and the oysters smelled like death. The meat at the American portion was dry and rubbery. The server was no where to be found after she brought us our 1st drink. And after paying $173 they still want to charge you $10 for a glass of wine that you can get for free out in the casino. I do not recommend you wasting your time or money on this place.

We had a great experience for thanksgiving dinner at Bacchanal buffet, 

The seafood station is awesome with great selection ( love the sea snail )

Pastry station is full of sweets, nice display

The staff is very attentive 



Pricey but worth it

We have tried many buffet's in Vegas and have come to conclusion that with buffet's you really do get what you pay for. I will say that their boast of over 500 items to choose from is a bit overwhelming. There was just soooo much to choose from. I can honestly say though, that I don't recall trying anything that I did not like. The carving station was one of the biggest that we've been to. The chef's were more than happy to prepare something special for you if you desired. I wanted one of the Kobe sliders without cheese and they had 2 whipped up for me in just a few moments. I can't really comment on the dessert section as neither of us are big dessert fans but as far as the rest of the buffet goes, I could not ask for more. We will definitely return here for our next visit to Vegas.
The wait to get in was quite long but they did have an option to add $15 to the $50 price and not wait in line but being a frugal person, we waited the 30 or so minutes in line. It really wasn't that bad considering the wait that is generally expected at a buffet on the strip.

Absolute best buffet I have EVER been to. Rated number 1 for a reason. I went here with my parents on Friday night around 7 pm and we only had to wait in line 15 minutes. Yes, it's a very pricey buffet, but everything in Vegas is expensive. A bottle of water can be $3 there! I've been to many buffets in Vegas and they don't come close to this one. Plus, I'm a very picky eater (unfortunately), but there was so much food that I loved. They have brisket, prime rib, sushi, fried rice, crab legs, shrimp, baked potatoes, lots of bread, deli meats and cheeses, made to order tacos, Mexican rice, salad bar, grilled veggies, and SO MUCH MORE! The dessert selection is just beyond amazing. I've never seen so much dessert in my life. I wish I could've tried it all. I did try the coconut macaroon, ice cream, cheesecake, and chocolate covered strawberries. All very delicious, but I must say, the strawberries were my favorite. 
GO TO THIS BUFFET! It's worth every penny!!!!

There has been so much hype surrounding this buffet, that when I finally tried it- I was disappointed. Perhaps it's the fact that I was one of the first patrons to enter or that I was severely sleep deprived. Either way, the frittata and pancakes were overcooked. Some of my items were bland and others were just no bueno. 

For brunch, we spend $85 for 2 people. Definitely not worth the money we spent. 

Perhaps I'll have to give you another shot, on another day and at a different time.
The best buffet in vegas hands down.... it helps if you are a diamond or 7 stars member as the wait line is usually over an hour.

This is one of the few buffets in Vegas that doesn't shut down between lunch and dinner, so if you eat at odd hours or you want to get lunch and dinner in one go, this is the place. The place is pretty classy, but as this is Vegas, you can dress however you like; it's not uncommon to see one table dressed up and another with tanks, shorts, and flip flops. But enough of that, the food is what matters here.

SUSHI: THEY HAVE IT AND IT'S THE GOOD STUFF. None of that cheap filler crap that low tier buffets try to fill you up with. SEAFOOD: Crab, oysters, mussels, etc. All the good stuff is there, or at least it is for dinner. RED MEAT: Ribs, brisket, sausage, etc. You can get as much as you want from the guy that carves the meat. Line for this is typically the longest, so have one person at your table get some for everyone. Immediately after the meat, you can get some fries, sweet potato tots, and ROASTED BRUSSEL SPROUTS WITH BACON AND PARMESAN. MY GOD THESE ARE AMAZING AND THE PERFECT COMPLIMENT TO THE LAMB!

When it comes to dessert (if you don't have room, make room), there are all sorts of ice creams, cakes, and cookies. I LOVED THE MACAROONS. They were all made perfectly. Scoop yo ice cream with that and IT IS AMAZING!

5/5 Would gorge again.
I have no idea why this is a 4 star buffet, it's small and the food sucks, especially the Japanese and Chinese sections. The service was okay. This is the one and only time I'll be here.

I have tried all the buffets in town and this is probably the best buffet in town but it is a bit pricey. If you are lucky the line wont be that long. This is probably the best lamb I have ever tried. The selections are numerous. The chinese section is of restaurant quality. Everything in there was excellent. My only complaint was that they mixed the snow crab with the king crab. Some people don't know the difference  but I do.

I'm not sure where Bacchanal stands in the ranking of all Las Vegas buffets (it's the only one I've been to). But in the grand scheme of buffets, Bacchanal has to be the best I've ever had. We went at an odd hour to stuff ourselves before our flight (they were serving lunch) so the line wasn't terrible, but nevertheless it moved quickly.

The only disappointment I had was probably my fault. I had watched several videos (haha) and browsed Yelp photos of people touring the buffet, displaying the things they served. But I suspect because it was a weekday and lunch, several items were missing (most notably crab and other seafood!) that I was really looking forward to. I still ate a disgusting amount and felt terrible, yet happy afterwards.

I would list everything I ate, but I think I actually tried EVERYTHING--plus, there's a bounty of photos available already of what they offer. What I would recommend is staying away from all the French fries and pizza; they're decent, but you can get great fries and pizza elsewhere. I DO, however, recommend the little cheeseburgers! The sushi isn't terrible and if you stick with nigiri, you do get a good value. The ramen is also a nice find--so many people bypass it because you have to wait a little bit/interact with a human to get your food, so I got it pretty much on the spot. It was decent :)

As for the desserts...just ask for a sample of EVERY gelato flavor. They'll give it to you! But I recommend the thai tea flavor.

I know buffets are usually quantity over quality, but my husband enjoys them every now and then so we went. Last year, I really enjoyed the food here! I was very pleasantly surprised. Everything, pretty much, was delicious. The kids were in heaven. This year (Thursday, August 13, 2015) the food was disappointing! Very mediocre. Not worth the price, at all. The pork belly was really chewy. The Chinese food seemed like it had been sitting there a while. Not fresh. The sliders were okay, but didn't compare to last year. The crab was standard. The seafood station was sloppy, with spills everywhere. Even the cheese selection wasn't great. The mini-cheesecake wasn't good, at all. It actually tasted bad. Not sweet or creamy. My favorite thing was the passion fruit tart. I hope they get back on track. Not sure if I will be willing to give them another try, considering all the other food options.
Best buffet in Vegas... just not worth the wait. The hours I wasted waiting could have been spent somewhere else.
Good place. Every time that  I'm in Vegas I'll came back. They have good food, good sushi and sashimi, good waiters. Congratulations Makino. Love it

Well worth the wait, and I'd do it again! We arrived around 11:30am a Sunday morning thinking we'd beat the early crowd for the brunch buffet...boy, were we wrong. We waited for an hour on line, which went by quickly with drinks we bought from the casino in Caesars.  All that time spent on line, we couldn't help but wonder what all the fuss was about

This brunch buffet lives up to its hype, and is inarguably worth the $40+ tax (apx $45pp...gratuity not included)

The spread is unlike any other brunch I've seen and surpasses the cleanliness and sophistication of other buffets I've dined at...including The View and the Marriott Marquee in NYC...which dulls in comparison

Full breakfast spread, Asian foods, Italian, desserts, fresh juices, unlimited Mimosa and champagne. This place is not to be missed, if you're visiting Vegas. So glad we took a chance on this restaurant...such an amazing dining experience.

Better than Wicked Spoon. First time here and wasn't expecting they would cook tacos, pasta, Asian noodle soups, and crepes in front of you. The quality of the food was high. 

At the end of the meal, I was overly satisfied for lunch. There wasn't a long line when I came on a Tuesday at 1:30ish. Overall, I would come here again.

I have been here i think 3 separate times, and since my first visit, I would always visit this place once when i come back to vegas.

The presentation of the food is probably just as good as the food itself. Haven't been to alot of the newer buffets around vegas but this place is something new from what you see at Rio, Planet Hollywood, and older hotels. 

The food quality is pretty much what you expect for what you pay. They have a large variety to choose from, an example would be fries, onion rings, sweet potato fries, potato tots, sweet potato tots. So when you come here you can probably expect to see something you never seen at other buffets.

The environment seems to be more relaxed. I feel like i'm eating at home more than outside at a restaurant. The furniture they use has something to do with it, but also the decorations they decide to use is much more home like.

I gave this 5 stars because it is money well spent for the food quality and service. Although the lines are long during lunch and dinner hours, it's worth the wait. However I think this is someplace that everyone should come to at least once.

Amazing Buffet!  The Wagyu Sliders were delicious, all of the Asian dishes were very good, the made to order street style tacos were great, and just the sheer number of selections was amazing.  Most people were really hitting the crab legs and seafood as well as everything else, but I'm just not a seafood person.

A note to save a little money:  We checked in and paid on Saturday at 2:50 PM, so we paid for brunch which was cheaper, but by the time we sat down at the table, they were serving dinner which is more expensive and starts at 3:00 PM.

The desserts were fantastic.  The Oreo Mousse Dome was my favorite and the gelato was excellent.  There is a ton to choose from on the dessert buffet should satisfy any sweet tooth.

Extreme long wait but you can pay extra $25 to cut in line. Else u need to get a number then come back at a given time and LINE UP for another 45 more minutes to pay and get in.  No kidding. 
Food was good but for some $50 was expensive.  I heard its the number 1 buffet in Vegas so at least i gave it a try.
A must stop for us each visit to Vegas! Offers such a Wonderful assortment of dishes and most of all desserts. My entire family enjoys eating here :)

Clap clap bravo. Wish I took some pictures but there are definitely so many on yelp already! Anyway, gorgeous buffet, maybe the most visually appealing one I've ever step foot in. The grandness of Bacchanal left me in awe and the food left my stumbling cause my stomach was too packed.

The food is plentiful and excellently presented. There are so many options that you are bound to find something you really enjoy. Unlike other buffets where I always find food either shitty to average, here I can't think of something that was less than average. Everything was either good or really good! Personally I enjoyed the seafood, the taco station and the desserts.


enjoy!
Bacchanal is best and high end buffet. Someone else told me Wynn was really good, Rio, Wicked Spoon....but to me Bacchanal is actually one of the best buffets I have found.

Was in LV for a bachelor party (11 guys). We decided to come here. Large groups have their own line (6+). We came on a Friday night and got in right away. For $75 a person , it better be good! 

We got seated in the back at a large table plenty of space for us. Place was clean and spacious . 

Decent food selection (Chinese , Japanese , seafood , meats , Italian , Mexican , etc). The food that I did try the quality was good. I wouldn't eat all day if you are coming here to assure you get your $75 worth of food. 

Waiters come to refill water and take dirty dishes away. 

At the dessert area, there's this old Asian guy who was hella grumpy serving the ice cream haha. It was funny watching him throw the ice cream in the cup when people would order and the disgruntle look on his face when someone would ask for a sample haha! It didn't effect me and at one point he slide the ice cream box open and the sliding door came off the slider hahaha. The girl working with him was like "I can take over if you want"  haha. I guess I'd be in that mood if I was 60 years old serving ice cream to tourist on a Friday night . 

Overall good experience but a bit pricey if you ask me.

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS!  My family loves the bacchanal buffet !  There are so many selections to choose from !  The food quality is excellent and everything is delicious!  The wait always seems to be endless but it 100% worth it ! Ive been here many times and I'm sure will come back
Many more!
This is the best buffet in Vegas! So amazing but there is a long wait so make sure you check in first.

The best time to come to Bacchanal is around 2pm, which is when lunch is dying down a bit, and if you're lucky, they'll start bringing some dinner selections, and you're only paying the lunch price. I think I paid around $35. They literally have everything in this buffet, anything your heart desires! I was trying to pace myself to try a little bit of everything. They even have fresh juices that come in a cute container! All the workers are very friendly as well. Overall, the atmosphere is beautiful, and the food is pretty good for a buffet!

CRAB!

I'm a crab lover. I love meat, and I love variety. Ceaser's has it all at their Bacchanal Buffet. 

The crab was easy to crack. They pre cut quite a bit. Beef ribs, wagyu beef, a little bit of everything for everyone. Foods from all over the world. 
 
Delicious - Yes
Cleanliness - Yes
Service - needs help
Overall go at least once. Ceasers in general is a beautiful place. 

Tip:
If you're a big eater and wasn't all you can eat for 24 hours at 5 buffets ask about it when you go.

Pretty pricey but honestly I was able to have a hearty enough brunch I wasn't even hungry the rest of the day- I only had a very light, later dinner. Brunch is spectacular- mini churros, noodles made to order, fresh juices, sushi, gelato, fresh fruit, etc etc etc. also plenty of healthy choices!
If you're like me and able to have this as your one main meal for the day- it's not a bad deal at all!

If you're going to splurge on a buffet in Vegas, this is the one! Fresh seafood bar including hot and cold options, lots of different eclectic offerings I've never seen on a buffet, like bone marrow. Standouts for me were shockingly the hush puppies (yes I know super basic, but really good) and the desserts! Soooooo many dessert options to choose from including fresh macaroons. The $60 price tag for lunch was steep, but oh so worth it!

It really is the best buffet I have ever been to. The quality of food is very good, and the selection is ginormous. We came for Sunday Brunch and were very happy. They have more than one giant room full of stations. Our favorites include: the crab legs, huevos rancheros, waffle bar, omelets, make your own crepes, and bottom-less mimosas. 

It is pricey, but hey, it's Vegas. It's too bad you don't get a to-go box to make up for the cost. Overall, it's a great option.

This place is great. This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas. Be here early because the wait is very very long during weekends. This is better than Wynn buffet in my opinion. Make sure you stop by The Bacchanal Buffet when visiting Vegas.
Worth every penny! Large asian mexican seafood and meat sections. Ih and deserts  island!
Wanted to charge me $200 for (2) 24hr passes. Food was ok but not at all worth $60/head.. I'll pass on the next visit.

This is a five star buffet.  Great selection of everything.  The prime rib and lamb chops were cooked perfectly.  The dim sum was excellent.  The sushi needs a little work.  The desserts were abundant and delicious.  The shrimp was not watery (like many of the subpar buffets in town).  The coconut macaroons were standouts.  Will definitely come back on my next trip.

Sorry just wasn't a fan of this buffet -and it didnt help that its SUPER expensive. Honestly I dont care how good the food is - its still a buffet, and if you are going to pay 60 dollars for a buffet, you might as well just go to a restaurant and get freshly cooked food.
If do you go here make sure its not during a busy period as it can get super busy.
Loved this buffet!  Everything I had was on point - rack of lamb, fresh oysters, Asian station, dim sum, ube dessert, azuki bean dessert, etc.

Best buffet in town, but $50. Lines arent usually bad the last 2 times I went, but on a weekend or holiday I would expect longer. Try the salami bar, clamboil buckets and the chocolate cone lollipops!

This buffet is by far hands down the best buffet on the planet.  Came here around 9:30am on a Tuesday and paid roughly $27 per person.  Everything tasted fresh, and there was just so much to choose from.  I normally don't do buffet eggs but these buffet eggs tasted liked they cracked every egg as opposed to using some commercial mix.  The best item was the ham and cheese croissant they had waiting for you.

Coffee and tea were served to us and left on the table in hot pots so we didn't have to wait for the server to come around again.

To top it off around 11 they were transitioning to lunch, so we go to experience that as well.  Also had a great dessert - a nutella crepe, fresh gelato and bread pudding.

If there is one buffet you go to in Vegas, this should be it.

One word: WOW!

My group, 14 of us went there around 2:30pm on a Tuesday, the line were long but quickly got escorted to the group line and was able to pay our buffet individually.  We were seated right before 3PM just before the changeover from lunch to dinner.  We paid around $48 pp including drinks and tips.

Here you can find all the best food across the globe.  Sushi selection was the best of all Vegas buffets. Carving station was a bomb with the delicious prime ribs and all cuts of meats. Excellent seafood from Chilean seabass(not sure if real tho) to clams, mussels, oysters, Jonas crabs, snow crab legs(both hot and cold).  

Oh yeah, the pork belly over mashed sweet potato was my absolute favorite.  Save room for desserts.  I was like a little kid in a huge candy store.  Hahaha.

Pros: Best buffet on the planet if you arrived before 3pm for dinner at lunch price.  Friendly service.

Cons: Long wait but well worth it!
Food was displayed so beautifully, but some of the dishes weren't that good. There are much better buffets in Vegas. The service was terrible. Had to beg for water.

Delicious! Not only did everything taste great, but the presentation was appealing as well. I love that they don't make you stand in line for hours. Instead you sign in at an electronic kiosk, and you are given a ticket with a time to return. You also leave your number and they text you when it is time to return. 
Yes, it's pricey but worth it. The items they serve are not the typical buffet items. They had bone marrow, oysters, prime rib among numerous other meats at the carving station. 

For dessert they had made to order crepes and various gelato flavors. My favorite of the desserts we these small brownie bites that were served hot. Hot they do it I don't know, but they are plated already for you to grab and when you get back to your table and take a bite the middle is still hot. They were heaven!

When in Vegas check it out!

Caesar's has raised the price of their Bacchanal Buffet $12 to $69.99 for adults and dropped the age for kids to below the age of 10 since my last visit 2 years ago.  Changes to the food available did not justify the price increases in my opinion.  It might account for the short lines on this visit.  Most of my family thought the food was still outstanding.  The Snow crab legs were a big hit with my 14 year old grandson, but he did not notice the large pot of King crab legs behind the counter that were dished up only when requested.  The Prime Rib was very good as well as the Wagyu Beef.  The large peeled shrimp was very good.  I was disappointed with their chicken tamales, not enough chicken.  I thought the Peking duck was nothing special.  I did not see the Rotisserie Chicken that my 21 year old grandson said was outstanding.    They do have a nice gelato bar with about 8 to 10 different flavors. The vanilla bean was very good.  My oldest grandson and I thought the crème brulee was very good. The freshly made crepes with your choice of mixed berry or bananas foster was pretty good.  They did let me bring two bottles of my own wine for a reasonable corkage fee of $25 each.  Very good service.

I went due to its great reputation.
Way over priced and over rated. 
But I understand that it's the seafood that makes it so expensive. But if you don't care for seafood skip this buffet and get just as good food elsewhere and save your money.  
The tritip, and brisket was dry.
The taco meat was over cooked.
The desserts were not impressive. Just too sugary.
The only thing that stood out was the clam chowder and bacon slab.

Buffet-Restaurants haben fast alle Hotels in Las Vegas. Im teuren Vegas eine Möglichkeit, gut und günstig zu essen. Als Frühstücks-, Lunch- oder Dinnerbuffet. Wir haben die Opulenz des Bacchanal im Caesars Palace (http://www.qype.com/place/155631-Caesars-Palace-Las-Vegas) genossen. Ein Traum in jeder Hinsicht!
 (Siehe Foto unten) (Siehe Foto unten) 
Im altehrwürdigen Caesars Palace mit seinen alten Römern hebt sich das Bacchanal Buffet-Restaurant völlig romfrei ab. Nichts erinnert hier an die Historie, dieses Restaurant ist topmodern, klar gegliedert, weitläufig, hell, gestylt.
Wer hier frühstückt, sollte sich einen Block mitbringen und dann in aller Ruhe die diversen Tresen ablaufen, Notizen machen, Reihenfolgen festlegen, seinen Hunger- und Appetitstatus sorgfältig analysieren und sich dann hineinstürzen in ein lukullisches Abenteuer.
Wer möchte, kann hier das große Fressen beginnen. Die Vielfalt ist unbegrenzt, alles, wirklich alles wird angeboten. Das geht weit, weit über das übliche eines Frühstückes hinaus. Ich erspare mir Einzelheiten, denn es gibt nichts, was es nicht gibt. Warm, kalt, süß, sauer, westlich, östlich, japanisch, thailändisch, französisch . Wer es sich hier zur Frühstückszeit  die erfreulicherweise bis fast zur Mittagszeit geht  gut gehen lässt, der braucht sich für den Rest des Tages keine Essensgedanken mehr machen. 
Der Kaffee oder Tee wird regelmäßig nachgeschenkt, die Säfte auf Wunsch ebenfalls. Vanessa unsere Bedienung gab sich alle Mühe, uns den Start in den Tag zu angenehm wie möglich zu machen. Natürlich war es für uns dann eine Freude, das hier üblich hohe Trinkgeld fließen zu lassen.
Die Tische stehen nicht zu nahe beieinander, so dass man durch den Nachbarn beim Gespräch nicht gestört wird. Für die japanischen Gäste stehen auch Rundtische zur Verfügung. Und man kann sich wirklich Zeit lassen, im Gegensatz zu à-la-carte Restaurants wird man hier nicht  wie so oft in den USA  mit dem letzten Bissen freundlich hinaus komplimentiert.
Das Restaurant ist selbstverständlich für jeden zugänglich, nicht nur für Hotelgäste. Und der Preis ist für alle gleich (und für alles, was man in sich hineinstopft): $ 21,99 + Tax = $ 23,77. Das sind bei heutigen Kursen ca. EUR 18 !! Hier passt der Begriff Schnäppchen. 
Fazit: Buffet-Essen in LV ist eine uneingeschränkte Empfehlung. Hier im Bacchanal stimmte einfach alles. Wenn alles stimmt und schmeckt sind fünf Sterne angebracht.

Got there at 5 pm on a Friday night and the line moved very quickly.  Only waited 15 minutes not bad at all.  The food was FANTASTIC!  Not your ordinary mass prepared bland buffet food.  Everything we tried was great.  Been to quite a few buffets in Vegas and this was worth the money and the wait.  Your only problem will be where to start.

A Las Vegas buffet would be the perfect place for one of my favorite fictional heroes, Harry James Potter-Evans-Verres, who "tried to sample at least a little of all the weird new foods he saw. His curiosity couldn't stand the thought of not knowing how something tasted. Thank goodness this wasn't a restaurant where you had to order only one thing and you never found out what all the other things on the menu tasted like. Harry hated that, it was like a torture chamber for anyone with a spark of curiosity: Find out about only one of the mysteries on this list, ha ha ha!"

On the other hand, for those of us with more modest limits and some self-control problems, these places are tricky -- just how do you even begin to think about tackling a meal like this?  I'll leave those questions to the buffet pros and just list a few things that were noticeably above or below my expectations.

Above expectations:
BBQ ribs (nice meaty texture, nice dry-rub)
Roasted vegetables (fresh, simple, seasonal)
Shrimp (I guess these were just what I expected, but they were really good!)
Fruit salad with 75% kumquats (self-explanatory!)

Below expectations:
Raw oysters (a little gritty)
Dumplings (bland)
Prime rib (also bland, and a little overdone)

Beyond that, you're on your own, my friend.

I went here with the wife after reading about the grand opening and the great reviews.  Overall, we just were not impressed.  After an hour plus wait in line, and $35 for dinner, I expected more.  There is a decent selection, and there are high end items like crab, shrimp, oysters etc.  However, we found the taste of the food to be largely lacking.  Most of the items I had were either decent to pretty good, or not good at all.  I had several items that I took a few bites of an pushed away.  The service was terrible as well.  It was slow and unresponsive, and I noticed the tables next to me having the same issue.  They would ask for something over and over and it would never be brought to them.  How hard is it to bring water or coffee when you are asked 3 times?  All in all, the buffet was not BAD, and most of the food was decent or pretty good, but for $35, I expect the food to be largely very good and worth the ridiculous wait.  I will say the dessert station was tasty and had a large variety of very good items like gelato, crepes, and bananas foster.  For $25 and no wait, I would be back, but otherwise, I just prefer buffets like the Cosmo or Wynn.

Every time I post something regarding Las Vegas or I look at something online regarding food... Bacchanal always comes up. Ive eaten at most of the buffets on the Strip and I have eaten at a few higher end places and they all had amazing food. So, I pondered to myself .... "how great can this place be when I live in Chicago and I am already impressed with almost all the places I have eaten here" Well, in the end, there was only one way to find out.

We arrived here a little before the dinner rush, at around 5pm. There was no line but we did see the mobile check in for when the physical line gets too long. Well, if there is there... then there must be a good reason. 

We paid a good amount for two, and were seated right away. The first station was the Seafood buffet. It all started with an area for lemons, cocktail sauce and melted button. Followed by Pacific Oysters. At first, it only had small pieces but while we were waiting, someone came by and refilled it with passive pieces. Next few areas were chilled crab legs which were cut in half length wise, cocktail shrimp, stone crab claws and dungress crab. There was a few more seafood related items like Paella. 

I recall a steamed crab station, pizza station, carving station with ~5 meats, salad, "different" things like a single plate of beet ravioli, bone marrow, pork belly with polenta, etc. They were all amazing. The stations just got longer and longer and it seemed like they would never end. If that wasnt enough, there was a massive dessert station. 

Overall, I can see why this buffet is always mentioned and why you will hear it from everyone. The food was amazing and my stomach was stretched beyond its capacity and then some more. Service was friendly and if/when I return to Las Vegas, I will be back there.

At a destination for tourists, there's sure to be a ton of hype to go around. Bacchanal's success is warranted much more by hype than actual quality... it definitely has its pros and cons. Be READY to wait. You could have a partial group go first to put down a party size and be placeholders in line. 

Let me start by saying everything about the restaurant is beautiful! Interior decor is modern, and dishes are plated creatively. The taste is where I'm disappointed here. Almost everything tastes like a dish of salt w a hint of food. Have a lil pep talk w yourself and try your best not to let your eyes be bigger than your stomach here, so you can try everything! There were very few dishes that I would go back for. 

The dessert island is truly the most impressive I've ever seen at any buffet. Be sure to save room! Still, very few that I would enjoy more than a single bite of. 

Then again, this is all just my opinion. If you've never been here, I'd say give it a try. Personally would rather spend the money elsewhere.

Definitely NOT worth the 1.5 hour wait or most pricey buffet in Vegas. Got there at 7:45pm Sat, got my waiting ticket for 2 for 9:30pm; nice lady let us in line at 8:40 line took 30 min to be seated. Food qualify only fair, variety only fair. Seating very crowded and not well kept.

A big disappointment really. Here is the score card:
1. Ambience, very good and clean
2. Food? Hit or miss.
-Good food:
 The prime rib , the scallop, deserts

-Way subpar food :
Most of the Asian entries, specifically dim sum is stale (one of the worst I ever had), hot and sour soup is un-edible (I am a big soup fanatic, will drink basically any soup, but this is not edible, way too much vinegar and lack other regular ingredients). For the price I really expect at least ok food, but this section isn't. They really need a new Asian chef very badly. 

-The Susie is really so so at best.

Drinks: plenty of decent drinks around.
- The crab leg is small to medium and SALTY. I have had much better elsewhere at much lower price (eg. Paris's buffet), besides you don't need to pay 53 dollars to eat subpar crab legs, they are available at much lower prices buffets of same quality crab legs.

All in all they need to improve the above as mentioned. Otherwise it is definitely not worth $53 let alone the line.

Nice selection of food (Dim sum, ramen, italian, cold cuts/cured meats, crawfish, Jonas crab claw legs, prime rib, chicken and waffles, tacos, etc). The food is well prepared, but I feel like you can't try everything since there's just SO much out there. It's kind of a first world problem since you want try everything, but your stomach is so full that it just won't let you. 

It's $29 from opening to 10am I believe. Brunch is $39 and dinner is ~$59. Brunch still has crab claw legs, shrimp, crawfish, and prime rib so it's still worth it if you're eyeing the seafood like many of us are. 

The dessert bar has some things made to order like these thai tea shots. The thai tea is in a little shot glass with boba on the bottom and a small scoop of ice cream on top. They also have a chocolate soufflé that takes about 8-10minutes to bake, and honestly, it's not the greatest. I would prefer the matcha green tea cakes or any of their other excellent desserts.

This is my favorite Buffett in Vegas. We showed up for the seafood one and rolled ourselves out. Between the sushi, numerous Chinese dishes, selection of southern dishes and fresh seafood, there is something for everyone. And the desserts... That is a meal in itself. Worth the $50 a head and will definitely go back.
Stand outs were: papaya jicama salad, sushi, shrimp cocktail, crab legs, bacon, the entire dessert counter!

I loveeeeeee Bacchanal Buffet! Even when I had to wait an hour in line it was totally worth it. I love how they have a great selection of food to choose from and they're constantly refilling their food. I highly recommend their prime rib and clam chowder. So amazing!

Lots of food and mediocre flavor. All the dishes are displayed beautifully but once you take a bite, it's anti-climatic.
Alot of the staff were frowning too, in particular, our waitress. The man at the rice porridge (congee) section was nice though.
The dessert section was disappointing. So much potential just by the looks but again, no flavor.

Beautiful place. I really have to say that this place is the buffet of all buffets. They have ramen, pho, various cheeses, deli meats, Mexican food grill with a rotisserie for their asada, sushi(which was OK), freely made crepes, ice cream bar, freshly made souffle... worth the hour long wait!

*In cranky old person voice* - Buffets nowadays are getting more and more high-falutin', charging more and more for food that we can only look at longingly when our guts are full to the point of poppin!!

Fact - The décor at Bacchanal is equal to that of Michelin-starred restaurants, a setting in which overpaying for your food seems to make sense.  There is no question this place is beautiful.
Fact - The bounty is plentiful.  This is the stuff that could trigger sensory overload...think Willy Wonka and the Chocolate factory but with more than just candy.  
Fact - Their dim sum is better than most regular Chinese dim sum places I've been to in Orange County.  Sad to say but it's true!

Unfortunately, the ultimate fact is...unless, you're some type of competitive eater (or secretly employ the use of a vomitorium like they used to do in the olden Bacchanal days), you're only eating 1/3 of what you're paying for the buffet.  Everything else is going to the cost of décor and excess food.  "Getting your money's worth" is a purely subjective mission here.

As beautiful as the rest of the place was, hubby and I got shoved into what appeared to be an overflow room where our chairs didn't match and our table was no better than a two top in a French café.

Food was plentiful as I mentioned and nothing really stood out. It was definitely a shock and awe type feeling.

My biggest issue with this place was the service.  Our server was ok, not super attentive so we didn't get refills unless we craned our necks to flag him down.  The biggest offender, however, was the surly possibly racist jerk at the carving station.  I witnessed him being openly rude to a meek lady with limited English skills and then suddenly offering the next few Caucasian people the biggest brightest smiles and an almost subservient tone of voice.  When it was my turn, I was once again shocked at his brusqueness and his rude tone of voice.  I smiled/chuckled and asked him if he actually gave away the entire ribeye to which his reply was an icy glare accompanied with "No, you can't have the whole steak." I ended up with the worst, fattiest cut he could scrounge up for me.  My next visit to his station was wordless even when I attempted some banter.  I'm typically a "live and let live" type of person but if I ever run into this guy again, I believe will call him out on his rudeness.  A subsequent courtesy email to Caesar's customer service received no response.

As other Yelpers have noted, it's more expensive than typical buffets out there.  It just depends on whether you think you're willing to pay for décor and maybe slightly better tasting food.  I'm still down with Wicked Spoon....

Giving both the Wicked  Spoon and Bacchanal on this trip to Vegas.  I'll say that if you had to on to one I'd pick Bacchanal.  It has greater selection and better quality.  

I give the food a solid 4 stars but our waitress was too busy replacing sugar to provide adequate service bringing the score down a star.  Plates were piling up on our table and glasses were allowed to go empty.  I had to ask the bus boy to get some help.  Maybe it was because we arrived at the start of lunch.  But that shouldn't be a reason to provide poor service.  

I will most likely be back as its well worth the price.  Just making sure to not include tip upfront.  Tip should reflect service provided and I wish I hadn't included it upfront.  I do believe that it's better than the Sterling Brunch since the remodel, but you can read my review about that.

About as good as it gets.  I've had better crab legs at captain George franchises  but the sheer quantity and quality of all the food is impressive.  There is something for everyone.  I was full and was dumbfounded when I found out there was another 2 sections in the back with asian style food!   

Quick tip.  If there is a long wait,grab some strangers and form a group.  There is a separate line for large parties and my group got in almost immediately.

I'm usually not a fan of buffets, but this one was pretty damn good. 

- The fresh shrimp was nicely sized, a little sweet, and the cocktail sauce had a nice horseradish kick
- The snow crab was ok.  It was snow crab, which isn't special.  Probably too much work for the amount of meat and not much flavor
- I asked for the lobster and they told me it was an extra cost.  What?  This is a buffet.  I just paid $77 and no lobster.  Tragic
- The crab claws were pretty good.  Decent size and flavor
- The brisket was off the hook.  Tender, smokey, salty.  Mmmm
- The roast beef was meh
- The sushi was bad
- The pozole was delicious.  Spicy, full of hominy and savory pork
- The chicken poblano was likewise delicious.  Definitely exceeded my expectations
- For dessert, I had the creme brulee (average), the jasmine yogurt (nice!), the cheesecake (bad!), and the pistachio and banana gelato, both of which were delicious

- The space was too loud.  No need for dance music when there are already 900 people talking
- The amount of people that they tried to fit into a large table was borderline criminal (15 people at a table built for 12!)

Yes, I ate a lot.  Yes, I'm still full.  Yes, it was good.

The best effin buffet ever!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Lamb shanks, need I say more? The meat literally falls off the bone. Geez I wish I had ten mouths on my face so I can eat everything all at one time. I just want to go back to Vegas for this buffet alone, ok maybe the shows as well. But if I can just eat and not gain weight, I will be here everyday of my life. The price is little less than the Wynn buffet, but the choice of food and dessert is far better. I was planning to try Wicked Spoon, but I'm glad we headed here instead. I will be back!

For the price we paid for, like $65 per person (went on July 4), I'd assume that we'd get fed gourmet dishes and free beer. Didn't realize that you'd still have to pay for the beer, I was kind of sad about that haha. 

Let's start with the pros. The dessert station was like a candy land. It was HUGE. My eyes lit up when I saw the gelato station (or ice cream, I have no idea), cake pops, cheesecakes, pies, oh my so much more. A lot of variety in dessert. My favorites were the ice cream/gelato, cheesecake and the cupcakes. The cupcakes were especially cute and decorated well :D I tried the macaron but it was a bit too sweet for me. I was excited with the cake pops, but.... It jut didn't have he right taste or feel..... To it. 

Next let's talk stations. They have a good variety of Asian, Mexican, seafood, Italian, american, salad and bread/cheese.

The "dim sum" was too dry for me. The noodles were bland to me too. The Italian pizza was too sweet (weird right?) and the meatball had a weird texture to it. 

The salad was fresh. However the meat was dry for me. 

Let's talk service now. The cashier that rang us up was sassy and didn't really know what was going on. She told us to go back to the woman at the line even though it was obvious that we already went through her and was sent over to the cash registers.... The waitresses were nice and attentive to us, which was good. 

Overall, if we paid $30 I would be satisfied with the experience, but knowing that this is a 4 star and $65, my expectations were higher.

First time here. It's pretty good so far.

This is a very classic looking buffet. It had a great variety of food, and most of it tasted really delicious.

There were jumbo shrimp and cocktail sauce, which were probably my favorite. They were SO GOOD. Very plump and juicy.

The downside was that the sushi was AWFUL. It was just very disappointing, because sushi is one of my favorite foods.

Overall, I think I would come here again, though.

Bacchanal Buffet is not a cheap buffet. In fact, it is one of the pricier buffets in Vegas, but it is also one of the better buffets. If you like buffets, this one is fun and beautiful to look at. The decor and ambiance makes the Bacchanal Buffet look modern and grand.

The Bacchanal Buffet is a massive buffet. It is the king of buffets. There is a wide variety of meat and seafood. There are various sections dedicated to salads, Italian dishes (pizza and pastas), Mexican dishes (tacos made to order were a delight), Chinese dishes, Japanese dishes and French dishes. Some dishes are better than others. Some dishes are decent. Other dishes are not great and you can tell some corners were cut.  You should not come to the Bacchanal Buffet thinking you will get gourmet, Michelin star worthy food. What you can expect is some decent dishes with some below average dishes mixed in for good measure. 

As with most buffets, there is no way you can sample all of the dishes. You will never be able to eat your money's worth. 

If you are planning to go to the buffet in Vegas, Bacchanal is not a bad choice. However, only go if you enjoy buffets.

Why am I rating this buffet 3 stars instead of 5 stars like many others? The answer is very simple: raw meats, and I don't mean rare, it was raw. The lamp chop was raw and the slider was raw, yuck!!!

Other than that, everything else was good, but not $45 good. The one thing that surprised me the most was that this place has the BEST PHO in the state of Nevada. It was sooooooooooooooooooooo good that I ate like 4 freaking bowls (small bowls but still...) So now whenever people asked where can they get good Pho in Vegas, I told them about Bachanal Buffet.

Their desert is excellent too, hopefully the quality doesn't go down hill (with time) like the Studio B at the M Resort. Anyway, I should need to cut down on buffet stuff anyway, reading Yelp reviews too much make me gain weights :-)

Did you know that there's a 2 hour limit for this buffet these days? It's written in fine print on the bottom of the receipt. My lovely waitress had the opportunity to inform me of their rule as my family of 8 enjoyed our 4th round of champagne. Then she trotted off smiling like a goon. 

Hm... What does one say to that?! 

Regardless, I really enjoyed Brunch@Bachannals. There's a huge Asian section, and it's actually not bad. Dim sum, chow fun, made to order soup noodles, which includes an assortment of rice noodles, udon, flat noodles and egg noodles. Made to order omelette bar. And a pretty good spread of sushi. 

I really enjoy their Mexican section because they have these juices, horchata, watermelon, tropical, mango... ALLL FRESH! 
The seafood section was meh, good Alaskan crab and cocktail shrimp but for $46 for brunch, guess I couldn't expect more. 
I wish they had some type of beef or just freshly cooked chunk of meat for lunch. 

Complimentary champagne and mimosas for brunch! Not sure if it's all the time though as I went the day after New Years.

Good food, beautiful setting, great service.  I would definitely go back.  We went at the end of the breakfast buffet (around 10:30) and they started changing it out for the lunch selections at about 11:00...we got the best of both worlds!  There is a 2 hour time limit for staying so that was perfect.  Because we had a party of 10 we were able to get into another line and were seated pretty quickly.  The atmosphere was wonderful and felt much more like a higher end restaurant than a busy buffet restaurant.  The service was excellent, the staff very well trained.  We were thinking of going to the Bellagio breakfast buffet but am glad we opted for this instead.

Went here this morning to use my groupon: breakfast Buffett with VIP admission and bottomless mimosas. Got there at 10:15a with the plan to transition to lunch. The VIP admission-literally 1 person working the register, everyone in line had a Groupon. Obviously, we all had the same idea. There was an Asian station set up in honor of the upcoming Chinese New Year. The Chinese style duck and bao were delicious. I thought the star of the show was the desserts. As far as the hype-meh.

What happened to this buffet? It's been a year since I last came and it just seems different. The bottled juice that they serve was being replenished by those machines you find in a mall food court that sells orange drink. Tried the street taco and the meat was way over done. Lamb was delicious and tender. I recommend that. Sushi was Meh.looks like they soaked cheap flying fish roe in different food coloring to make it look like expensive caviar.
Dessert....looks like they cut back on that too...
Where are those pastries with the syrup syringes? 
No huge chocolate covered strawberries. No Macarons? 
Nothing with a wow factor.
Meh
Left full but a little disappointed.

We went to breakfast time.
Adult was $25.99
Child $14.99
It was lot of serection.
Chinese food, Thai food, Sushi, American, Mexican ,oyster, shrimp, beef stake,pork,
fresh juice in the bin.
Oyster was very very fresh!
One thing I do not like was no rest room in the buffet.
I had to go outside of buffet..
Desert was very fine too!

A plate of fancy desserts, a plate of carved meats & BBQ, while slurping a bowl of beef pho and tonkotsu ramen. Don't. f*ck. up. this. rotation.

Excited to see that Ceasars Palace was finally opening the doors of its highly anticipated $7 million buffet, Vegas buffets are very similar to one another (all equipped with seafood, carving station, fancy dessert station, etc). Generally, new buffets start off very well, so we jumped to try this before it begins to spiral down in quality (all buffets eventually do this).

Bacchanal seems to have adapted a lot of Wicked Spoon ideas like the brilliantly idiotic concept of individually plating items in dishes/pots/pans/mini-deep fryers so that items do not fit on your existing buffet plate 
(Why does fancy plating mean that we have to further frequently pace back and forth for more food?)
But, all in all, the food at Bacchanal is a solid buffet competitor to Wynn, Cosmo, & Bellagio.

The perfect time to go to a Vegas buffet is right before lunch ends (2:30).  
(Props to Justin Y.)
That way:
1. You avoid peak rush hours and the death line wrapped around the corner. 
2. You pay for the lunch price, while dinner items are new and slowly filter in at stations. I.E Crab legs were were not offered for lunch, but appeared later during our meal
3. Going out at night? Luckily for you, you had a late lunch/early dinner so you will feel like less of a whale in that tight dress.


Bacchanal Back-anal jokes aside, this place is recommended

We stopped in for lunch. No waiting in line on a Tuesday. The price was a bit on the high side for us ($35 each), but we were not disappointed. Lots of interesting food items stuffed everywhere. The buffet zig-zags into another room, so make sure you check out all of it. The dessert section was mind blowing. Lots, maybe too much to choose from. 
If you're going to pay this much for a buffet, you better arrive absolutely starving.

Lets be honest, I don't often find myself raving about a place of its kind. Places often filled with people that really should, but never listen to the doctor's orders. Not the case here, this is legit. Cuisines across the world, prepared gourmet in front of you, never left out stale. Chinese, Japanese/sushi, Italian, Korean, Mexican, American, seafood, want me to elaborate? Pizzas, pastas, breads, salads, carving stations, crab legs, I can go on. But the big hit for me, someone that only decides to be this gluttonous given an atmosphere of this kind was the dessert station, what a find.

An immense, endless array of ice creams, pastries, candies galore.

Need I detail this more?

You'll be so full and overstuffed from the meal had before.

But won't care when you see this stuff that will physically put you over the edge, to the point you won't fit through the door!

Endless ice creams, candies, pastries and s'mores.

Crepes filled with berries, whipped cream go explore.

Cheesecake pops, though one more thing some really adore.

Mochi as incredible as can be
Vanilla, Chocolate, red bean and green tea

Don't hit the buffet before hitting the pool
You'll bloat up immensely and look like a fool

Just one thing I'll say is beware of the line
An hour wait, but there's a trick you can find
An extra $15 express will save lots of time
Maybe some truly just don't see the signs
Or people are just irrational, would rather blow that on slots then pay a few extra dimes

Hands down best buffet on the strip when it comes to food selections. You get a little bit of EVERYTHING! 

However, they seriously need to work on their customer service skills -- they need to learn how to prioritize and organize. I informed one staff members that there was 5 of us in our group. She told me that it wouldn't be a problem. Later, another staff member came by to bring us to our table and sat us at a table designed for 4. I asked if we could pull a chair up to the table since there's 5 of us and the lady was confused. She looked at my receipt and says that because it's 4 written on the back, she brought us to a table of 4. I flipped the receipt over and showed her that I paid for 5 people. She went over to talk to the other staff member about this and they both came up to me and apologized. Then, they told me that the tables for groups of 5 or more were occupied and I'd have to wait longer (we seriously shouldn't have to go back to wait). Still, they didn't provide us a larger table but moved my brother (who was part of the group of 5) to another table across the restaurant to dine alone. 

Also, as I was about to sit down, the darn chair was soaked -- it was probably orange juice because of the citrus/sweet scent. I pointed this out to the staff member who walked by and he simply removed the soaked chair, put it at the table next to us, and gave me one of the chairs from the table next to us. The sad part is that about 5 minutes later, a group came and sat next to us...in that wet chair. You can imagine what happened next.... Of course, I kept my mouth shut and just watched....

Now, I assume that all of this happened because the staff members were overwhelmingly busy. Most staff members were moving non-stop. They've just got to take their breaks!
Sooo delicious. One of the best meals I've ever had. They literally have everything you could ever want and more. Left happily and fell into a deep food coma after

For the price we paid for our family , I would expect a lot more than we got. $55 a pop. The management implemented a line strategy that was confusing and misleading. We checked in for a group of 6 on our mobile app , that the front desk didn't even existed. There were multiple lines for parties of less than 5 and 6.  We had to wait an additional 40 minutes on top of our 1 hour wait. The management should not place the burden of organizing the crowds and lines on the customer . The table was unacceptable. It was dirty. Nothing on our amazing waitress but they were completely understaffed. Food was okay but not extraordinary. This experienced should have cost half the price. I would not recommend to anyone.

I went to the Bacchanal this morning for breakfast. The food wasn't anything too special, but my waitress Lorri was absolutely fantastic. She made sure all my plates were cleared, my drinks were refilled & was such a sweetheart the whole time I was there! I will definitely be coming back next time I'm in town thanks to the wonderful service I got!

The food is high in quality with nice variety, and the ethnic food seemed pretty authentic. My favorites were the fresh oysters, crab, burgers, made-to-order tacos (especially the carne asada), made-to-order noodle soups (the pho is pretty good!), shrimp scampi, vanilla creme brulee, and crepe station. I didn't care for the sushi, ceviche, and fried chicken (dry).

Service was very friendly.

I actually really like it here. Rate it about 4.1 stars. One of two of my favorite buffets in Vegas in high class food and atmosphere but of course, pricy up the ying yang and that is why it's short of getting 5 stars to me but can't rate on Yelp that way...

Love the variety of ethnic foods...my fave is the baby oysters with horseradish and cocktails sauce. I love the taste of their lamb chops! It's tender, juicy and not gamey..so good. They offer crab legs half cut to make it easier to take out. They have unshelled medium sz cocktail shrimp and ceviche shrimp, too. They have soups, sushi, salads, prime rib, pizza, sandwich stuff, etc. They have so many desserts like crepes; with
add banana and strawberries with nutela and of course, add ice cream is my fave. They have french macaroons and much much more. Been here how many times now but can never eat all as I always come out with food COMA. Burpppp.......

I recommend coming here on an empty stomach to try and concur all of the food varieties. There is a line to wait to get in here as well to consider. It's strange to me they would try to photograph you after you pay? Best time to go here is during the weekday dinner for $3.00 off from weekend pricing. ;-)

Pricey and long lines - but worth it!  It made me realize that the other LV buffets have decent buffet food,  but this place has really good restaurant quality / fine dining level of food.  

The sushi was fresh,and actually tasted like restaurant sushi vs wedding reception sushi.  I don't usually get pasta at buffets since it tends to be overcooked, but I got a cute little container of rigatoni and ragu, and it was cooked perfectly al dente and shockingly good - worthy of a fancy italian restaurant.  The shrimp cocktail was noticeably larger than at the Wynn buffet (which we went to the next night) and didn't have that just-defrosted look and taste.

I tried a whole bunch of random things and over-ate to the point of feeling gross afterwards.  Everything was really good to amazing -  so wear stretchy clothing.

Not so much.. mixture of king crabs and snow crabs consisted of just snow crabs. Seems like false advertisement to me. Other selections were limited. Could of gotten the same quality for a $30 buffet.

At first I was a little upset when we came into our table..our chairs was dirty and full of crumbs..they cleaned it fast when i told some waiter about it..wait was not long..food is good.. lots of good varieties and specially desserts..it was satisfying..the reason it was 4 because of this nice lady miss sue..she gave us a good customer service..they even sang a birthday song to me..though it's only the 2 of them..thats very sweet..made my Vegas birthday memorable..thank you miss sue..your awesome!

Michele and I won 2  free passes at the Bacchanal Bingo Buffet Elite Event.  So we brought a couple of friends to enjoy the night with us.  The line wasn't long for us to wait, but part of that was because our guests came early to do the waiting.  We get to the front of the line and provided the tickets.  We were mistaken for employees, but we soon rectified that.  Damn, our morals.  Anyhow, we were taken to our seats and the feasting began.

I sat at the table to watch some purses and order some drinks.  When they got back, I got up as it was my turn to "GLUTTON IT UP"

I started out with my new found favorite... Sushi.  I don't know exactly what I got but it was good.  Also on my plate was Dim Sum, Miso Soup, Lo Mein, and a couple of egg rolls.

Plate 2, I decided to go a different route.  I had a Lamb Chop.  That was the first time that I have ever eaten lamb.  It was good and I didn't feel guilty because the lamb was probably a cute thing running around a couple of weeks prior.  On that plate was also, a slice of pizza, some more dim sum and some other things that I can't remember.

Plate 3, the reason that I couldn't wait to get back.  Dessert: Cake Pops and Jelly Belly's.  Nothing else mattered to me.  I knew that I could eat about $30 worth of Jelly Belly's.  One of my weaknesses.  They were so good.

The company was fun too.  We took a few pictures post grubbing.  And, it took us a while to get out of our seats to leave.

So much choices ! Food is fresh and yummy and the price is cheap went for lunch was like 60 bucks everything was terrific wish i saved room for the dessert it looked good. Terrific choices in cheese all which i purchase from my local market here in sf and arent cheap. Id come back again

Stunning buffet, and offers such a huge selection of high quality food that it rivals many restaurants in Vegas. Highly recommend for anyone who likes quality food, buffet style, with modern twists.

One of the things I really liked about this buffet was that many of the specialty foods are served on smaller plates. It really seems the emphasis here is not to overindulge on one specific food, but to try as many of these different offerings as possible. Pumpkin gnocchi, scalloped potatoes with truffles, and the oyster shooters were some of the most impressive of these smaller plated items I tried.

The seafood is out of this world, and probably why the buffet commands such a high price. You can fill up on snow crab legs, freshly shucked oysters, and even stone crabs - surprisingly short lines for all of these items. The seafood is all prepared fresh, cooked just right, and is regularly rotated to keep from serving diners dried out crab.

Finally, the desert menu is incredible. The deserts are extremely varied, and brings some modernist cooking techniques to classic desserts. Again, the portions are small, so you can try many different things without filling up. Too much to list everything, but my favorites were the macaroons, the tapioca pudding with the cherry boba-like bubbles, and the bread pudding. Delicious!

If I had to pick something that was underwhelming, it'd be the sushi. The selection just wasn't that great compared to buffets that specialize in sushi and Japanese. This is understandable though, as there is so much else going on. I think if you are craving just sushi, there are better places to go at better prices. Also, the wait times to get in are a little ridiculous - however, you can check in at the kiosks and they will call you when you can line up to get in. This allows you to do other things in the casino while you wait.

Overall, this is easily one of the best buffets I've been to. The seafood and desserts really stand out as being exceptional. I can't say it's the best buffet on the strip, as I haven't been to most of them, but it is extremely impressive!

FORGET EVERYTHING YOU KNOW ABOUT A TYPICAL BUFFET EXPERIENCE.

Like other reviews, If you're looking to save money do the following: Get in line around 2PM, hopefully you'll pay before 3PM. Why? 3PM is when the dinner entrees come out. Go before 3PM, pay the lunch price and eat all the glorious dinner offerings.

Me and my gf went on a Monday before Thanksgiving and only waited in line for about 20 mins and the line moved quickly. We actually got seated around 2.20PM. This place is beautiful, and not just for a buffet. If I didn't know any better, I would have thought we walked into an upscale restaurant at Caesars or the Venetian. The light accent lighting is gorgeous and is just minimally decorated but enough to make you feel like you're eating in luxury.

The service was also very top notch. Our drinks were refilled frequently and dishes were taken up fast as well.
