When we went, I personally had: Sushi (selection was actually slim.. just your typical rolls like philly, salmon, California, etc. and there was no sashimi), duck, sauteed crabs, cha siu (chinese style roast pork), Ramen, selection of fine cheeses, assorted deli meats, Mussels, oysters, crab legs (steamed and cold), crawfish, flank steak,  lamb chops, risotto, Dim Sum, Smoked Salmon, P/D cold shrimp, and some fresh fruit drinks: peach mango, horchata, iced teas, etc. All the food was delicious, cooked perfectly and was served at the correct temperature.

The only things I didn't really enjoy were the crawfish, mussels (my gf loved them), crab soup shooters and the crab legs, unfortunately. The crab was a hit or miss both when it was cold and steamed.

They also had Pho, Udon Noodles, Pasta, Mediterranean food, Pizza, American food (wings, sliders, fries, tots, etc), create your own taco station. The only things they didn't have that I was expecting: lobster, rib eye steak, grilling station, and Kobe beef. 

P.S.- they ask you only stay for about 2 hours but we we're there for almost 3... You gotta try this place!!!

I really wanted to love this place...alas, no.
I spent $50 for the 24 hour buffet pass knowing full well that I would have to pay $15 more at Bacchanal, according to what I read online and the cashier when we bought the ticket. When we arrived, we were told it was $15 more for breakfast, $20 more for lunch, and $25 more for dinner! I sure wish the cashier had told me this at the first buffet!
But I was excited by all the pictures online and reviews, expecting gourmet little small bite deliciousness with each spoonful, so I paid my money and waited for my table. The place is lovely, but it turns out its all just regular buffet food in smaller plates. Nothing outrageously delicious. And my husband was sincerely disappointed...having seen previews on the hotel info channel in the hotel, he was expecting made to order, well prepared tacos, along with 1/2 cup portions of shrimp and grits in sweet little cast iron skillets...instead, tacos were slung at him with no fixins' and he received a tablespoon of grits with one little shrimp on them in a small condiment cup. And my fried chicken and sweet potato fries were greasy and soggy. Maybe 5 of the 25 items we tried were noteworthy. Severe Disappointment. Meats were overcooked, sushi didn't appear fresh and the crab, while served by someone at a steam pot, left much to be desired. Our waitress was pleasant, but buffet staff spoke little to no English and were rude, disconnected somehow from the patrons.
One thing that was a plus was the dessert area. Better desserts than I've seen at the other buffets, but like everything else - it's the luck of the draw. Some items were either runny or flavorless, but the selection was great and the majority of items were good.

Save your money - or if you really must try it, do it on the cheap. Get the weekday buffet pass, and go for breakfast during the changeover from breakfast to lunch. Not worth dinner pricing. The lunch at Paris buffet was better than dinner here. Good luck and happy buffet hunting!

The food is good 
And
The service sucks!!!!

Management:
-Please work on the front of the house-

It's like pulling teeth to get to take your plates and refill your drinks.

So much potential.

This buffet is top of the line of all Vegas buffets and the price clearly shows it. No matter what your taste buds are in the mood for, they have your fix and will surely deliver on quality.

We were very impressed at their exotic selection of seafood, and the long line says we're not the only ones impressed.

They also have a healthy selection of dessert, some of which we could have done without though.

If you won a few bucks at the table, be sure to treat yourself with this buffet.

Don't let them win!!! Of course you always want to come to a buffet with an empty stomach, it onky makes sense. It was about $118.94 for 2 people after tax, at dinner time.

There is a ton of food to choose from here. They have all kinds of seafood (crab legs, sea bass, shelfish), Italian food, chinese food, different meats, etc. Like any buffet that you go to, some things are better when they're fresh instead of how they are when they've sat for awhile. I really enjoyed a little bit of everything here really! (especially the chili crab)

There was a large selection of desserts here, all sorts of mini cakes, gelato, custards, and a fresh crepe station. Most of the desserts were good, but all of the cheesecakes tasted like icing! (I would say avoid the cheesecake). Overall, the atmosphere here was good, the food was good, and I would definitely come here again!
The best buffet in town!!! They had the best service and the freshest all you can eat food! The desserts were amazing too!!!

The best buffet in Vegas.  They have a little bit of everything, including bone marrow, sushi, Mexican, burgers, and steak and lobster brought to the table.  There is also an insane dessert selection and a juice bar.  I think this is the best selection of all the buffets.  Come hungry and stay awhile to make sure you can try everything!

I came twice this week for dinner. Luckily the lines were short given it was during the weekday. Service from the waiters was excellent and attentive. The food was definitely excellent compared to other buffets. Of course the first night I went there was better than the second time. I would recommend it.

this place was horrible by far the worst buffet in Vegas. We generally go to many of the buffets and it's one of our favorite things in Vegas but I actually got food poisoning from this buffet and wound up being sick on my vacation! go to the Spice Market at Ph, save money and get great food.

the service was a 5, but i would give it 3 stars because of the food.
most of the cooked food was on the salty side & there aren't many vegetarian/vegan options.
also, the labels for the foods left out were incorrectly placed.

Food was GREAT! The asian food section was GREAT!!! the sushi was so-so.... ive had way better at sloppier joints... There was also a mexican, american, and italian section...  All of it was reallly good! Now, the desserts were not that great.... I was actually pretty disappointed in the desserts :( and thats what I was looking forward to the most :(

Lots and lots of food. Shocked that the child's price only went to age 10. Everything was awesome except for the crab. Which is ironic considering that's the intense smell of the buffet when you're waiting in the line.

I was extremely excited about going to this buffet. I read multiple good reviews online, and figured this is Vegas so why not. After waiting an hour in line to get in, we paid at the cashier before entering, 118 dollars to be exact for my wife and I without alcohol. The first thing i noticed was they ask for a tip at the cash register before you even go in. When i left that area blank on the receipt, the hostess seemed extremely annoyed. I figured i would tip the waiter or waitress who brought the drinks. After entering, the lines were long for just about everything. I realized there was nothing on the menu that was worth the pricetag, unless you really love lobster and crab and that sort. They had no steaks, or prime cuts of meat. The pizza was soggy, the burgers were rock hard, the asian food was comparable to panda express. When i got back to the table, while eating my chicken teryaki, i noticed a long 10 inch piece of hair inside my chicken! Disgusting. I called for the manager who came over and took multiple pictures of the plate before taking it. She then offered us 10 dollars off the vip buffet next time, which is 75 dollars per person. No thank you, we will not be returning. Save your money and go to Applebee's or outback steakhouse. Trust me, it will leave you much happier than when you leave here. Not the best experience in vegas. If you can catch mat franco, it is comparable in price, and a tremendous show. We loved every second.
Best buffet in Las Vegas. What more can I say. It's fantastic and reasonably priced considering all the nice chow. I don't like buffets typically but this one has some great items.
Amaaaazing! It was worth every single cent. Some of the best food I've eaten on this trip, with a huge selection from all sorts of different styles of cuisine. It was wonderful.

This buffet was pricey and there's no way I could ever eat my moneys worth, but they had a HUGE selection of food, and I especially liked the dessert bar.  So many amazing and interesting unique deserts, all very tasty.  There can be a several hour wait depending on the time of day, but we called ahead and checked so we got right in.  We mainly went for the seafood which sadly was pretty disappointing, but they made up for it with the very handsome chefs and servers lol.  The fried chicken was ABSOLUTELY THE BOMB and made me forget all about my still half frozen crab legs.  My stomach was hurting by the end and while I feel $50 is kind of a crazy price, the mass amounts of diverse foods are clearly where that money is going.

This is the best buffet I have ever been to so far because no New York buffet can stand a chance. The displays are fun to look at while you walk around picking out your food. They have a wide variety of food selections and their food is fresh, quality is high. Each station was clean and decorated nicely. Their seafood was stacked to the top, and their meat sauces are containers that flow out.  I love their dessert section, there's so much to choose from, and they have so many flavors of gelatos. I literally took one of each dessert to take a bite and try everything. I was like a kid at a candy shop.  

Last year when I came here with my girls and we waited on the line for 40 minutes just to eat dinner. A few weeks ago, I bought the $88 VIP groupon brunch deal for 2 , which included 2 mimosas and no wait in line. My husband and I got there around 245 and stayed till after they started serving dinner. Got some of the dinner meats before we left. This is also the only buffet where they take your picture on the line so they can try to sell photos of your memorable experience to you while you're eating. No thanks. 
 
I'm glad I finally brought my husband here because he was tired of me telling him how amazing it was that my girls and I had food comas on the table after dessert last year. This year he was almost passed out on the table.

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS! I've come here every time I come to Vegas since it opened. Can't top it!

PRICING: Lunch is around $52 (ends at 3pm). Dinner is around $62 (starts at 3pm). They encourage you to only dine for about 2 hours.

LINE: Totally varies depending on the month you're there and the day. Holiday season tend to get more crowded (~90 mins). Weekdays during non-peak seasons are the best time to go! Less than 30 mins in line.

Get to a kiosk and check-in. If there's a line, it will have you enter in a phone number which will text you when to come back and physically stand in line. When we came during a holiday season (party of 5), we checked in at the kiosk. Approx. wait time was 90 mins. We walked about The Forum shops and we got a text to stand in line after 30 mins. We stood in line for about another 45 mins before we got seated.

FOOD: Seafood, meat, sushi/Japanese food, noodle bar, Mexican food, charcuterie, cheeses, Chinese food, and an amazing dessert bar!! It's got a little bit of everything. Take advantage of it all and try everything!

TIP: I usually cash tip the server who helps us during our meal instead of writing a tip down when we pay for our meals before we get seated.

You know I'll be back!

This buffet is definitely an experience.  The food was really good and I liked having a true waiter.  Many things were good, but the desserts stole the show.  I'm not a seafood lover so I don't believe I got my money's worth, but I very much enjoyed the experience!

dessert and gelato (mango habanero was the bomb) were the best.  Liked the seafood (chef's special scallop on the shell), prime rib, sausage and oysters.  So disappointed in the sushi since the owners of the buffet were Japanese.  My stomach shrank from waiting in line so long so I didn't try the hand-made Mexican food.  Everyone in my critical group enjoyed and no one complained about the $55/person dinner price.

For the price meh. They do have a huge selection of things but seems like a buffet is a buffet. Nothing is great -just lots. Most people are into lots so if that were the case then this is wonderful. I don't eat tons of food in one sitting, so I guess I am looking for that one item that'd wow me. Which is hard to find at a buffet since the food is sitting there under a warmer. I like buffets since I can have a smidgen of everything but if it's this pricey then I want at least one wow.

We had a great experience and staff are great. The good was good except for the dim sum it was over cooked and the soup dumplings were very dry and chewy. Also the lamb was tough, didn't try any other roast meats. Not much sushi selections (5 or 6 different rolls only). Desserts were elegant and delicious. Too bad I was not able to taste the crepes but it looked good too. Overall it was good!

This place is AMAZING!!!! I feel a little overwhelmed just thinking about all the deliciousness I would love to write about., but here it goes...

This place is truly like a fantasy world-- if your fantasy is a never ending selection of crab cake eggs benedict, hand cut slabs of maple smoked bacon, delicious udon noodles, little stacks of red velvet pancakes and lemon basil gelato.  Mine is.  And topped off with mimosas that are never empty?  We could have stayed there alllllllll day.   There were so many more things that we wanted to try but all that eating and boozing had to come to an end at some point, plus I could not physically shove another bite of food in my mouth (trust me, I tried)  I think, randomly, my favorite item was the smoked salmon vichyssoise-- SO rich and delicious! And the thing that failed was the fried chicken and waffles (basically chicken nuggets in a waffle cone.)

The price is steep, but it is WELL worth it, especially with the amount of food and drink we shoved down our gullets.  I mean if you think about the amount of champagne we consumed, that might have been worth it in itself.

Bacchanal has definitely earned its name and I will be returning the next time we are in Vegas.
Excellent food and even better desserts.  The food line is a hassle but they keep everything fresh.  Pricey but nice.

This is the most amazing buffet I have ever been to! Chinese food, Japanese food, seafood, Italian, bbq, and don't even get me started on the dessert! Everything was made with so much more attention to detail than I am used to from regular buffets. They are plated beautifully and the perfect serving size. My very favorites were the peking duck and the crab legs. Wish I could have fit more crab into my wimpy stomach but I had to try everything and was extremely stuffed by 9:30pm. Rolled myself back to the hotel to call it a night!

5 stars for my favorite buffet on the Las Vegas strip! I've eaten here multiple times for brunch and dinner and they never disappoint. The buffet has many selections of food from Asian, Noodles, Seafood, Pizza, Meat section, etc. They also have crab legs! Without even asking, they'll gladly fill a whole plate for you! 

Every item I have tried has exceeded my expectations of buffet food except for the oysters. The oysters were not that great! That was one I had to spit out right away. 

The dessert selection was plentiful! They have an assortment of baked goods, fruits and other desserts. My favorites are the crepe station, ice cream, creek brûlée and dulce de Lethe flan! Yumm!!
I really don't like this buffet. Even if the category are abundant, the most of them are terrible!!! This buffet doesn't worth its price, so expensive.

The one buffet in Vegas that you really need to go to is Bacchanal!! 

By far the best buffet I have ever been to, ever! This place is amazing, it has such a variety of food and the quality is amazing. 

It has a very modern look to it and is massive. 

It is pricey at like $50 or $60 per person and the wait is long, but totally worth it =] To get your moneys worth, you need to eat at least 5 plates minimum, not including dessert or crab legs!!

Everything tastes amazing and fresh and just delicious. I just can't say anything bad about this place. I can't wait to come back again and stuff my face with all this yummy goodness!!

The best in my opinion was the NE clam chowder & the red velvet bread pudding. Crab claws were good too. Other seafood items not as good, such as the salmon & the clams with chorizo. Suggest to come at off-time to avoid very long lines for the meat & seafood. A little pricey at $57.00
Best food ever! Very understaffed. Paid for unlimited mimosas and only got to have 2 because they took so long.

Best buffet in Las Vegas. Come for breakfast, stay for lunch and maybe dinner too. Biggest variety and food is a little better than what you would expect from a buffet. 

Critics are comparing this food to what you would order at a restaurant and therefore were not impressed but that's because they are not very experienced diners. I rarely eat buffet food because I think it's disgusting but this food was actually great for buffet food and mediocre for restaurant quality. 

Get there early and beat the line!

We came here on a Friday night (12/14/12) with a party of 9 and expected a two hour wait from reviews/word of mouth. To our surprise, the line was really short to get in; we waited maybe 15 minutes. Bacchanal Buffet might be pricey but it is definitely worth every penny and it doesn't feel like a buffet but a real trendy restaurant vibe. The food lines are pretty long but there is a lot of different options, all of which are amazing. My buddies and I went straight for the  protein and seafood and was not disappointed. The dessert bar was also fantastic (try the Mint Watermelon Sorbet & Banana Fosters!). Def worth coming back next time I'm in Vegas.

Oh no, another Vegas Buffet.

Yes, this is another Vegas Buffet. It is big and with long lines, but you will soon realize this is The Bacchanal Buffet.

The Bacchanal Buffet is just a cut above the rest. Everything here seems a notch better than anyone else. The selections are vast and the details are a little better.

I stopped by for a Monday breakfast. Twenty-two dollars is a bit high for breakfast, but I walked out of there thinking it was worth the indulgence.

The Dim Sum was borderline bad, but I wouldn't blame them for trying. (Dim Sum is best served fresh)

Everything else seemed to be made and displayed in smaller quantities. I think this method works. The big trays and troughs of food that other buffet use really ruin great tastes.

They even had BBQ for breakfast! What more can you ask?

Again, their selection was wonderful and fresh. The orange juice was really freshly squeezed, the crepes made right in front of you. The many selections of egg dishes were a breakfast delight. 

Enjoy the indulgence! I'm going back to try dinner soon.
Went for lunch. We definitely should have been more hungry to indulge. Everything was incredible. Our favorite buffet in Vegas by far. The others don't even compare. Can't wait to go back for dinner!

The first stop on my list was Bacchanal Buffet. It was my first time in Vegas and my girlfriend told me we had to eat here. So here's my review. 

They're located in Caesars Palace and you can park anywhere in the garage. The parking is free. They're open for breakfast I believe around 7:30 but I went for dinner. We got there around 8pm and I was ready to eat! The line was crazy... I figured it would be seeing that who doesn't love a good Buffet. Well you have to sign in through this digital sign in and come back in about an hour and a half. The last seating is around 10p so you have to be in line by then. 

So we signed in and went to go gamble for an hour and half. When we came back, you check in and you wait in line. We waited for about another hour before we were seated. The price for this buffet was $64 per head. 

I thought that was crazy but I figure by this point I was starving. Once you get seated you can go grab food. A waiter will come to get your drinks. The place is very large. They have all different kinds of food from Asian, seafood, pastas, sushi, meats, deserts and the list goes on. Most of the food was average I would say. But it is a buffet. 

The staff is nice and they're on point to fill up your glass. Overall, it was good, but the price for me was too much for what I got. I felt I didn't really eat $64 worth of food. If you're a eater go check this place out.

I don't know why Bacchanal Buffet has 4 starts. They make most the seafood are really salty. We ate dinner last night. The food are not fresh enough and too much salt add on. Dear friends, read this comment before stand on the line to buy a ticket.
Some place you do not wanna miss when you are in Vegas! Long queue to wait! Indulge yourself in the ocean of crabs and steaks; don't get drowned!

HMMMM, changes being made here as Ceasars tries to figure out how to make money at this buffet.  First off prices have gone up!  Dinner is $46.95 mon-thur and $54.95 fri-sun.  You can still buy a 24 hour buffet pass but it is no longer worthwhile if you intend to use it on Bacchanal.  The pass is $55 plus $25 extra EVERY time you eat at Bacchanal whether it is breakfast, lunch or dinner.  In effect it is cheaper just to pay the regular price if you intend to eat at Bacchanal more than once.

Portion size has also been changed for a few items, the lobster corn chowder is in a smaller ramakin and no longer contains large pieces of lobster.

The made to order souffles are no longer in a ramakin and are being baked in foil cups, leading to the soufflies being over cooked.

The changes being made are sort of alarming as it makes you wonder if Caesar's will be able to continue this fabulous buffet or will quality suffer down the road.

Worth every penny! If you're doing buffet, this is the one to do! You get everything and the seafood area alone makes up for what you pay. They even had Phó & I was hesitant but it was just like Mommas! Flavorful- just wish there was bigger bowls! Desert area was KILLER! I went for lunch & no Macarons! They said for dinner it's out then. You're allowed 2 hrs and stayed entire time and got my money's worth if not more! Paid extra $5 for Champagne- DO IT! I think we had maybe 5-6 glasses each, worth the extra $5!!!

freaking fantastic! worth every penny. i mean i don't really need to say much after the 500 plus reviews lol. i gorged on both land and sea lol. the gelatos were great too and omg the one i loved so much was the sesame ice cream, coconut and their mini cheesecake!
ooh their lamb was dried out.....but the brisket and prime rib yum. 
sushi was awesome too. 
honestly everything was delicious and even though i was full, i was like STFU to my stomach, this shit's going down. lol

It was the best brunch we had in Vegas - I was expecting to have a regular lunch - didn't know about all weekend long brunch - but it was good. Kind of disappointed for not having lobster at brunch - crab was good thou...

Hands down the best buffet I've ever eaten at! I pretty much died & went to food heaven.

It's a bit pricey, $50 per person for dinner, but it's so worth it! (At least for the amount of food I ate, anyway).

You could taste the freshness of the seafood. I felt that they had a huge selection within each area of food that they had. Their selection of food ranged from American, Mexican, Italian, & Asian. I felt like the ethnic food they offered was pretty much authentic tasting. It didn't taste 'Americanized' if that makes sense. I don't know what else to say about the food except that I pretty much tried every dish that they offered & I loved each & every one of them!

The desserts were really good too! Loved that they had a gelato bar. & the best part was they had green tea cookies the night I went. Not only were they green tea cookies, but they were red bean-filled green tea cookies!!

I can't wait to come back!

My husband and I ate here earlier this month, and we were very disappointed to say the least.

To start off with, we were told the wait time would be 20-25 minutes, but it ended up being over an hour until we were sat.
When we finally got sat, we waited more than 10 minutes, but no server ever greeted us. We decided to go ahead and get our food, thinking by the time we returned to our table, a server would be over. We were wrong. After being sat for about 15 minutes, we eventually had to flag down someone to get drinks. 
We (finally) received our drinks (half way through our meal), and were told rudely "your server must be on a break" 
That was our only interaction with service staff the entire time! We had plates and trash stacked up on our table, and we were not offered any refills.

Overall our experience was terrible, I do NOT recommend this buffet.

After reading many great reviews about this place, I had to go.  The food was incredible (except for the prime rib, which I surprisingly did not get because my one companion, who is a prime rib aficionado, said it was rubbery and over done).  I focused on the Asian section and seafood section.  And let me tell you, the Asian section had all the goodies.  There's crispy pork belly, roast duck, Korean bbq ribs, duck fried rice, soup dumplings more dumplings, pork char sou, etc., and it was all delicious!  The seafood section?  The crab legs were already sliced opened lengthwise which meant no effort in getting the meat.  The shrimp was steam perfectly, the oysters fresh, the soft shell crab incredible and the mussels...YES!  

This is not to mention the wait staff.  Our waitress was incredible!  She was attentive, and made sure we had everything we needed and came to check on us regularly without being too intrusive.  You know how places can get annoying about that?  Well she was perfect!  She noticed our drinks were low, and she brought more out.  She noticed our plate was full of crab shells, she brought new plates and took the old ones.  

So, besides the prime rib debacle, which still surprises me, I would highly recommend this place.

Honestly, I expected less of a breakfast buffet, but I was presently surprised. I had the most wonderful, relaxing time that I bought a Groupon for my parents to go on a date here the next morning. 

At first glance, the decor is beautiful, the music is calming, and the smells were warm; which gave it such a relaxing ambiance. My wife and I arrived early around 8am on a Tuesday. We were seated in a private area away from other people dining. Our server was cheerful and made the experience even better. She gave us our mimosas and we went on our way. 

I was blow away by the freshness and all of the healthy yet flavorful choices. My favorites were the freshly juiced tropical juice, lobster benedict, sweet potato tots, sunny side up egg with steak, and shrimp. They had such a wide variety of foods like egg benedicts, shrimp and grits, mussels, pancakes, cheese and meats, and much more. We stayed for probably 2 1/2 hours and my parents stayed for almost 4. It just lets you relax and eat without the rush. 

I had an amazing time! I definitely recommend.
Best buffet!!! Amazing service and unique atmosphere I highly recommend it. A special thanks to those two kind servers Milka and Mahyar.

Huge buffet with lots of items and I tasted most of them. They are all good and service is nice.. But I knocked off one star as they don't have display names attached to each dish. In most cases we didn't know what we were eating. 

To avoid waiting time, be there before 11 AM for lunch and before 6 PM for dinner.

I never eat at buffets  but when I do....  I'm highly disappointed and disgusted . So much variety,  yet not one delicious dish.  I love quality,  I guess I will have to be content with quantity.  But I won't,  I refuse to conform to the masses.

The wait time here for dinner after 3pm ranges from hour and a half to three hours.  You get a ticket stamped with a time to come back at.  Once you're in,  you are seated and then you can join the frenzy of other dinners trying to grab the "best of the buffet".  The best probably being the crab legs and oysters. Or the California rolls (they call it sushi) or a mosh posh of pasta , Mexican ground beef hard shell tacos,  Chinese chop suey or overly mayo clams.  U pick your poison. 

When everything is said and done or half eaten you're left with a full belly of despair and dissatisfaction. 
 
Next time family or friends come in from out of town,  they're on their own if the suggest we eat at a buffet.

I haven't been here since about a year after they opened but it was as good this time as it was four years ago. The standouts were the shrimp and grits, the desserts (all of them were great), and the eggs Benedict. The only thing I wasn't found of was the crab, mostly because they only had crab claws and I prefer crab legs. My friends really liked the peach tea, I didn't have it, but they seemed to enjoy it. They had dim sum, which included my favorite shrimp ha gow, which was actually pretty ok considering we weren't in the San Gabriel Valley. I went with a group of 5 and we were all very please, and quite full, with our trip and would definitely be going back on our next Vegas visit.

As a side note, even a great buffet doesn't add up to a great restaurant, in terms of food quality, but the variety and quality here make this buffet far above the rest.

This place lives up to its reputation as the best buffet in las vegas. For the price the huge selection of food and the great quality was totally worth it. It seems like its always busy here but after my visit i get why. The options here are massive, a wide range from custom Mexican tacos, Chinese dim sum, Japanese ramen & sushi, bbq, steaks, Italian, seafood (fresh snow crab legs, shrimp,etc), there is something for everyone. One of my favorite things about the place was their dessert station with custom crepes, gelato, pastries and many more. It was easily one of the best meals I had in las vegas cause of the many different options that were all good. In terms of prices it was IMO a great value. Would totally recommend!

I was excited to eat at this buffet after reading many reviews on Yelp and on Google. I was highly disappointed by the service and food. I went here for dinner and we were seated right away. Our waitress was mumbling and we could barely hear her. We had to keep asking to repeat what she was saying. The buffet entree I was most excited was for the seafood, it did not live up to the hype. I wish the seafood was served warm and the crab legs were really small. Many of the other food was dry such as the ribeye, brisket, and the Asian food section. The fried rice seems like it has been sitting out all day, the sushi was old and the noodle dishes. I will not pay this price again for this buffet.

Bacchanal is THE buffet that you want to visit on your trip to Vegas. At ~$55/pp for dinner, you should expect a large selection of high quality food. This place does not disappoint. 

Bacchanal utilizes a queue system called FreshTXT which allows you to enter your name and phone number at a kiosk. You'll receive an *estimated* time to return to the host for entry. Just a tip, make sure you keep your phone on vibrate so that you know when the text comes in. Our estimated wait time was about an hour at 9pm on a Sunday, but the text came after only 15 minutes, which was awesome, but I didn't hear it or check my phone until about 30 min later. Once you return to the host the get checked in though, be prepared to wait in line to get to the cashier, then waiting in another line to be seated... It was still probably a 45 minute wait after returning to the host. Ok, that's it here - just bring a drink into the line with you and you're good. 

The food. Oh, the food. It's generally separated into sections based on region/style. You've got your Chinese, Italian, and Mexican sections, along with an epic seafood selection. Also, the snow crab legs - don't miss them as they were near the Italian area rather than the seafood, which I thought was strange. 

The quality of the food was top-notch. Really. It far surpassed my expectations. Everything was freshly prepared and each time I went back to get more food, a fresh platter had been set out recently. I think the high volume of people that flow through necessitates constant cooking, which is great. 

Finally, I know that it's probably going to be hard to do with all of the delicious food in front of you, but you need to save room for dessert. Apple pie, key lime pie, cheesecake, fresh and decadent fudge, tiramisu, chocolate "lava" cake, the list goes on. That's probably a quarter of what I put on my plate. 

Again, if you're looking for a Vegas buffet, try Bacchanal and you'll have a great experience. Make sure you have your free Total Rewards gaming card with you as it saves a bit on the cost (5-10%). Also, just so you're aware up front, all major buffets in Vegas seem to follow the pre-tipping concept where you have the option of leaving a tip when pay for the buffet before you enter and receive any service. I suppose you could always leave cash on the table that is commensurate with the service received, but if you're paying with a card and want to leave a tip, you'll do it up front. 

Enjoy!

Lots of selection; however it's not worth of money. Labor Day dinner price was $68.00 and waited about 45 mins. Food was way to salty and cold. Very few sushi selections, crab meat was way to dry, and meat was way too cold. Not with the money.
Hate your line system. Already paid but still a 40-50 min wait. Ridiculous. This is one of my favorite places to eat but the line is so hideous that I really hate you

The worst experience.. Ruined the first night of LV... Nothing but disappointment.... 2&1/2 hours wait, $130 for 2 including tip.. From the reviews from others, my expectation was very high... Dry sushi (rice was hard, dry tuna), salad- not fresh, too saggy, soup (tom yum soup-- TOO salty), corn chowder with lobster-- what am i having here? No taste of lobster, just corn and strong bacon taste,  clams & mussels-- too dry, I took them and lost my appetite... Seriously?? This place is supposed to be THE BEST buffet in LV?  My hubby and I could have gone somewhere else and could have enjoyed better quality meals than this.. We will never come here again...No star... But I guess I need to give one?

I feel like a trip to Vegas just isn't complete without dining at one of their delicious buffets. 

Pros: (My faves)
- They have Ramen & Pho!! And the broth is actually pretty good!
- Soup dumplings and other dim sum options - my faves were the steamed shrimp dumpling and pork buns
- Salmon nigiri was on point!
- CRAB LEGS!!!!!!! SHRIMP! OYSTERS!! - even though they are served cold, they are still delicious
- Waffle cone filled with Maple fried chicken and waffle fries
- Made to order gourmet street tacos!
- Ribs, Turkey, Steak, Pork chops...
- Mexican style corn on the cob
- Dessert station was truly impressive (aren't they all though?) - Snow cream station, crepes, gelato, fudge station, cake pops, macarons, and tons of small pastrys and mini-tarts - Definitely go for the Crepe and Gelato though!
- Service was attentive 

Cons:
- 75% of the items that we ate were COLD/DRY and seemed to have been sitting out too long
- Congee soup was bland
- Pineapple chicken paella was dry and had a stranger flavor
- Tuna nigiri and sushi rolls were dry or mostly made up of rice

Understandably, we came during the crossover from lunch to dinner, but the food is the same and I feel like they should have been better about replenishing. We have pulled this move at other buffets on previous trips and have never had an issue with everything being cold. Our soup dumplings didn't have any soup inside :(

This place is a solid 3.5***** with definite potential for 4 stars as long as things can stay fresh throughout the day.

*Tip* Try to get in before they cross over to dinner prices at 3pm
*Pto-tip* Starve yourself all day and arrive at around 2:15pm to wait in line so that you only pay $37 instead of dinner prices $53  (I have no shame)

What a buffet! I didn't want to go originslly, but my son said the reviews are great and we have to try it while here.
A little pricey at $55p/p but you could eat that in crab legs alone. There was an amazing variety and everything you vould want: Asian, Latin, Anerican. The Wagyu beef won raves from our party of five adults. I personally loved the dim sun offerings, the cioppino (fisherman's soup),  the ceviche was out of this world. The endless Jonah crab claws were sweet and succulent. Another favorite was the pulled pork tacos. The flavor was incredible.
I also loved the honeydew gazpacho. Light and refreshing.
Now the desserts!  Don't miss the pistachio and coffee gelato.  Dessert crepes are made to order. Creme Brulee,  lava cakes, maccarons,  and pecan tarts, oh my! All bite sized so you can indulge without getting stuffed, but able to sample some truly outrageous offetings.
Try the Bacchanal Buffet,  you won't be disappointed.

Excellent selection and price. They offer a kids menu price unlike many other high end buffets on the strip. I love the attention to details with their mini tasting plates. The warm dessert station with chocolate pecan pie was a nice touch. The lobster bisque, chilaquiles and fresh watermelon juice were unique and makes this buffet stans apart. The chef should be applauded!

I would not recommend going here for brunch.Its the same price as dinner with only a portion of the dinner menu biggest disappointment was the fact that for brunch they only have snow crab legs and not king crab legs.The buffet items they did have was descent far as taste just not worth the price.

The best buffet in Vegas, hands down. I have yet to eat at another Vegas buffet with the same variety and quality that Bacchanal offers. The wait can get crazy (so it's best to come at non-peak dinner times) but the wait is so, so, so worth it. Want meat? They've got plenty! More of a seafood fanatic? Well you can get both cold AND hot crab legs! Wish you were in Mexico instead of Vegas? Their tacos here are made fresh to order and are delicious to boot! Tired of "American" food? Loads of Asian/Italian/whatever else options! Ready for dessert after stuffing yourself? There's a make your own crepe station and gelato station! Seriously, if you haven't been to Bacchanal Buffet, you need to go the next time you stop in Vegas!

Ok, so another one of my other, "must not miss when in Vegas!! "

Been three different times. Everything was exceptional, especially for buffet dining style. Loved how everything is displayed and presented as opposed to the food sitting in a metal pan with a scoop. You eat with your eyes first, so they excelled in this area for sure. You want to know,"but what about the food ??! " 

It's the best buffet in Vegas Baby! Loved the seafood of course, but can't miss the pho, udon, ramen, laksa(?), hot noodle station.  Oh, my goodness the fresh juices too! 

Definitely get the bottomless champagne/mimosas and beer option too! You're welcome :0)

Mind blown. This place is absolutely amazing. Everything down to the details impressed my entire group. The price was reasonable especially when comparing to other buffets in Vegas, there was no wait and the staff super friendly. 

The food was fantastic. Everything we tried tasted delicious and the presentation can not be beat. (We especially loved the cute little milk bottle containers filled with fresh juice!) There was endless choices and things to please everyone. This place is truly unique and will be on our to do list every trip here on out. 

The only downside was the service we received. Although I think our waitress was the exception as every table we passed in other sections appeared to have full drinks and no dirty plates. Our waitress did not get around to bringing us refills of water or mimosas often at all and our plates kept stacking up without being taken away. She was nowhere to be found when we decided to add the endless drink option so we ended up not getting it. I do believe she was having a bad day and this isn't the norm here however.

The best buffet  ever !!!  They have sooooo much variety to pick and try ( seafood, Italian , American, Chinese, Mexican, ice cream bar, desserts , fresh fruits, sushi, alcohol bar, soups, salad bar,etc...)   But yeah the waiting line is long so you better be there early.   But I don't mind coming here everyday :D
Great Buffet with a huge selection and delicious food.

Bacchanal: a drunken and riotous celebration; a participant in such a celebration; reveller.

Caesar's Palace lived up to my expectations with this buffet.  Despite the 45 minute wait in line at 5pm for dinner and the $86 (w/ tax) bill to eat there ($100 with tip), it was worth the wait and the price.  The line wasn't bad at all considering how new and popular this place is right now.  Just standing in line was exciting because you can see the seafood section right at the entrance.  

As they walk you in, the hostess tells you about the buffet, pointing out the sections and letting you know as you pass the American counter that "it's not over yet".  Around the corner from the main entrance is even more food stations--Asia, Italy, and a hint of Europe thrown in.  

After being seated and greeted by Miguel, we headed to the back corner of the buffet--Asia.  I tried my very first soup dumpling, which was tender and explodes in your mouth.  I could eat fifty of those.  The sushi counter is great because it is the ONLY sushi bar in Vegas I know of that utilizes ebi furai in the roll instead of regular tempura--just the way I like it (that's how they did it up in Japan when we went and back on Guam as I was growing up, so I love ebi furai in sushi).  No cream cheese anything, THANK GOD.   I also grabbed snow crab legs and they flash boiled it for me.  Yummy.

There's a pho and ramen station, charcuterie, Italian, Mexican, American, soups, seafood...the list goes on and on.  What sets this place apart is definitely the quality.  The aged tomohawk ribeyes are delish, the fried chicken in a basket is fun and tasty, and their dessert station with four crepe outlets, cookies ala mode, and heavenly cheesecake pop bites with gelato is amazing.

This is now my #1 place to eat buffet in Vegas.  Screw the 2 for 1's at the station casinos.  I'll pay the high price for quality and quantity.  You think you can't do it all, but if you sit in there for 2 hours like I did with my hubby, you can.

My favorite buffet in all of Vegas for dinner. 
If your timing is just right, mainly between 4-5 for dinner, the line usually will be less than 15 minutes, which is hard to find in Las Vegas. Around 6-7 it gets insane.
I mainly love this buffet because of their desserts, they have quite literally everything. My favorite is the creme brûlée, as far as dinner food goes, the pizza, mashed potatoes (w/gravy), and macaroni & cheese are so good -- the crab legs are also very delicious with butter. You'll definitely leave stuffed.
My (very tiny) complaints would be that I wish that for tacos, they had the option of a flour tortilla vs only corn. Also, the bathroom are on the outside of the buffet, and it's small and so close to such a populated area, theres nearly always a line. But that little bit aside, I enjoy coming here for birthdays and other special events.

Come for lunch, stay for dinner! Bacchanal was really everything I've always wanted in a buffet and more: food that doesn't just look pretty but actually tastes good! 

Some of my favorites: 
-Their potato bar (sweet potato tots, breakfast potatoes, french fries, and more!)
-Their meat station (prime rib, ribs, lamb chops, rib eye...drool)
-Their seafood station (chilled crab legs, STEAMED crab legs--upon request!, OYSTERS!)
-Their dessert station (sorbet/gelato heaven!--so many unique and tasty flavors, chocolate covered strawberries, creme brulee) 
-Unlimited mimosa (during lunch)

Definitely beats M, Bellagio, Wynn, Wicked Spoon, and Spice Market buffet!

Came here on a Saturday around 1pm. To my surprise no line, but wait... They have a new system where you go to a screen touch computer and input your info (name, phone number, and # of ppl in your party); the computer then generates a time for you to come back to pay. Personally, I like this better than waiting in line for over an hour. Pretty smart for the hotel also because while you wait for your time chances are you are playing, so the hotel makes more money. 

We had a party of 9 people and we were given a time for 2:45pm, so over an hour wait. That's pretty typical for this buffet, at least we didn't have to stand waiting in line. They will text 10 mins prior to your  designated time and you just go straight to the hostess and she then directs you to the cashier to pay. We waited about 10 mins to get a table after paying. Not bad! 

For the food... Great selections; definitely better than other buffets on the strip. Make sure you come hungry because there will be plenty of food for you to choose from!

Awesome high end buffet. There are tons of options there so walk around first before grabbing your plate! 

We got here at 10:30 am. Breakfast ends at 11. What's nice about getting there in between breakfast and lunch is that you pay the breakfast price and have two hours to eat, so you can see the breakfast and lunch options. 

There are so many different types of food. Multiple types of eggs Benedict, bacon, sausage, Italian deli meats (salami, prosciutto), etc. There are different sections of the buffet, there's a seafood section (think crab, shrimp varieties, and mollusks), Asian section, dessert section, pancake/French toast section, as well as salads, soups, sliders in between. 

I loved the lobster eggs Benedict, apple tart, and creme brulee. 

My boyfriend absolutely gorged himself. Pretty sure he ate about 10 plates of food. 

Awesome experience overall!!!
The only reason it wasn't a five is because In the beginning felt like I was at an amusement park with the long line. After we got through that it was well worth the wait.

It was a very disappointing experience to eat at this buffet. We waited for 102 minutes and paid $52 per person. The steak was the worst I had ever eaten across all American restaurants; it was hard to chew and the meat was over cooked. The sea food was horrible with only crab leg being ok. I even didn't want to try it is sushi and Asian food based on the visual impression that they were not fresh at all.

Overall with the price tag of over $110 with taxes Caesars Palace buffet was not worthy either the length of wait time and seat environment. I am very surprised of the top rating it had at the website. It is absolutely misleading. Bad choice absolutely !

Thinking of going to buffet at Caesars Palace? Make sure you check in at least 4 hours ahead. I checked in around 7pm and waiting time was 270 minutes. (See my photo). I eventually checked in early with vip access pass. Regular buffet price is approximately $60 per person. My suggestion? Its not worth it. Food was good as any other restaurant with half the price. I give C- for service. Once was good enough. I have no plans for next visit.

Eating here was a much better experience than your standard all you can eat buffet. It is far more classy and elegant than the typical Vegas buffet.  They had a pretty large selection of foods. Mostly everything I had was good, but nothing in particular blew me away. The display of the food was magnificent. They made each item feel like you were taking something special.  The carving station had the largest selection of meet I have ever seen served in one place. Dessert items were cute and delicious. I would love to come back one day.

They do not serve Alaskan King Crab. Period. Used to I'm told. No more I saw. They have Jonah claws (small) and Snow Crab clusters (sawed in half for easy access). Snow is OK, but there is no compassion/substitute for Alaskan though. Small Jonah claws are sort of useless. Kind of pissed as they have AKC and Steamed Lobsters in the DISPLAY that is visible form the line, but not available to be consumed.

Shrimp is U25 - too small to impress anyone.

Sushi sucked. Sucked. Uninspired in variety and preparation... and yesterday's supermarket quality.

Service (non-holiday weekend Sunday dinner at 5:45 pm) - friendly but way too busy or understaffed to seem particularly valuable. Plates did get cleared each time the buffet was revisited, but drink refills were hard to come by.

So there are the failing grades.

Here's the passing...

BBQ area - sensational. Lamb chop, pork ribs, beef rib, and especially prime rib (as good as Lawrys) get an A.

Chinese, charcuterie, street tacos, and to a lesser extent, Italian section were all quite good. B+

Desserts - crepe station - that's all one needs to know. It's like the crepe unwrapped itself and enveloped me in the warm comfort of eggy goodness laced with Nutella, then rhythmically and lovingly rubbed my forehead and whispered to me until I drifted off to a French nap.  A+

For $62+ incl. tax, I'm glad I tried it once. Like visiting Graceland, or marriage.

Hands down the very best buffet ever.  We've been several times but this time i had the mussels which were so tender and perfectly cooked and sauced. The smoked salmon was great, the bacon crispy,  the steak tender, the veggies flavorful, the seafood and fruit actually fresh, the Chinese food really authentic!   So much food you can actually imagine you are at a Roman feast and you probably could stay and keep eating for 24 hours and not repeat a dish (if you got a new dish every 10 min). Wow, what decadence! My favorite was the little fried donuts (today they had it with bananas and syrup ) which i have never had so incredibly light crispy on the outside.  Unique dishes to please the jaded but with a healthy dose of your standard fare cooked well to please everyone else.  Those little silicone finger mitts they give you?  It is to reach for those hot small dishes.

My final day in Vegas on Monday we decided to come here for a brunch/lunch. We had a party of 6 and the wait was only about 30 minutes. 

We were seated and off for the food we went. I hit up the Asian/dim sum station first and had grabbed some rice wrapped in banana leaf, pot stickers, and shu Mai. All of the choices were great. 

Second round I went for their crab legs. Although small, they were good. I complimented the legs with a cup of lobster bisque. 

I had so much other food I know I was in a coma afterwards. This was the best buffet I had in Vegas and hands down I will be back again.

Known as the BEST buffet and almost 5 star buffet. I would give this buffet a 4.5, only because they weren't swift with replacing silverware and bringing something to drink. I needed new silverware and I had to wait to find someone to ask, then wait for them to bring it. Also it was hard getting refills because I couldn't find anyone to ask. They were swift with removing plates but not attentive to basic needs. That was my ONLY complaint. Everting else was perfect!

Over 500 food options and different ethnic food. I believe everyone should experience this place. Most of
The food was good. It was $60 per person for the dinner option. The lunch option doesn't serve crab legs. If you aren't a heavy eater I wouldn't recommend. I am not a heavy eater, at least if I ate $60 at a restaurant I would be able to take the food home. The food options definitely overvalue the price tho! Definitely try it when you're in Vegas!

Sort of disappointing.  Chose this place after reading the reviews and choosing this over the wicked spoon. figured I would try something new.
First, the wait to get in is insane. Between two people we spent $118 and some change. Then, there isn't as much food as I thought there would be. At the wicked spoon there is literally food everywhere...here? Not so much. That was disappointing because it's a buffet and buffets usually have many options for you to choose from.
A lot of the food that I tried tasted terribly... omg to the point where at some point I spit it out into my napkin because it tasted old? Or just not good. Food at the wicked spoon tastes REALLY good... like all of it. I will say however, that the presentation of the food was really nice so I will give them that.
 Service at the wicked spoon is also better because they altered more tentative to you! 
Overall, Between this buffet and the wicked spoon I prefer the wicked spoon WAY MORE than this one.

Friends who ate here told me I just had to eat here no matter what. I'm not a huge fan of buffets but after hearing there were over 500 items to chose from & it being the largest buffet in the world (according to the girl who worked there) & seeing all the delicious pics on Yelp, I just knew I had to eat here. 

We arrived around 730pm on a Tuesday. There's a kiosk machine where you check-in. You punch in how many people are in your party. Put in your cell number and you'll receive a text telling you to come back and get in line. On the ticket the wait said it was 45 mins but I got a text within 10 mins and we went to stand in line. I estimated we probably waited less than 30 mins. The host said the best time to go is between 4pm - 5pm, food for thought.

Now on to the food. I really was going to attempt to eat as much protein and seafood as possible. I wasn't going to waste any stomach space on carbs. First station - meat, they had brisket, lamb, spicy sausage and a couple of others I can't remember what they were. I decided to go for the lamb since I never had it before and also the spicy sausage and brisket. I was surprised the lamb was pretty good & not gamey as I thought it would be. Not a fan of it though. The brisket was tender and the spicy sausage was helluva good. Oh I also tried the hamburger sliders which have little sticks on it telling you how it's cooked. Just ate the meat and not the bread lol, it was pretty good.

Next on to seafood. Went for the crab legs and boy did I pig out on that. I didn't know where they steamed crab legs were until after I ate the cold ones but what the heck went and got them anyway. It's way in the back by the way, near the Japanese section. You give the cook your plate and they sure pile up the crab legs, they aren't stingy either. If I didn't have high cholesterol then I do now. Oh and btw, there's a video on a Yelp showing you how to open the claws. Thank you to the nice person who posted that. My friend kept telling me if I ate a whole plate of crab legs then I got my money's worth and yes I did - twice. 

I also tried the fried chicken and waffles, well just the chicken anyway & it was pretty darn good. The only veggie I tried was the corn on the cob. I decided to try the Tonkotsu Ramen and surprisingly it tasted like something I would get in Japan. It comes in a small bowl and the noodles were cooked perfect. 

So I know y'all are dying to know about the desserts. Well there's a lot. I tried almost everything that was chocolate except for ice cream. I think I was bouncing off the walls from all the sugar. I'm not a dessert person but all desserts looked so stinking good that I just had to try it. They had mini cakes, cup cakes, macaroons, ice cream and they even had mochi ice cream. You name it, they probably had it. 

I will definitely go back here the next time I'm in Vegas. Oh and wear lose clothing, you'll thank me later, lol.

I so regret purchasing the 24 hour buffet @ $308 for 2 adults and 1 child to include Bacchanal. All the other buffets do not compare. Smaller selection but excellent food and presentation. It is one of the best in Vegas. Next time, it's this place or the M buffet.

Came here for dinner coz we heard it's the best buffet in Vegas. There are a shockingly long line for wait. Well understood if it's the top 1, right? But after we finally got in, we found the inside is so crowded with little room between tables. Sure there are tons of things to choose from, but mostly are too pretty heavy for dinner. Oysters are the most popular things here, and crab legs - they ONLY HAVE SNOW CRAB LEGS can you believe that?!!!! Aidan food are below average level - you can get those sushi rolls from any cheap Japanese restaurants. Desserts are okay but not very impressed either. The best thing I love here are juices! All different kinds and cute bottles! Lamb and beef are good, but really how much can you eat at dinner? Not a bad buffet, but overrated and overpriced.

Delicious! So much variety on things to eat. From sushi, to oysters, to street tacos, to a selection of fancy cheeses even. A little pricey but boy do you get what you pay for. So good! I highly recommend it !

Man! This place is just expensive! 

The food is good but geesh!!! Dammit!!! They are too expensive. I guess what they say is true, you get what you pay for. But I need a doggie bag or suh'in. $128.08 for two people. I could feed a small country for a month with that, LOL! I made sure I squeezed down some King crab legs and they were sweet and delicious too. Only way I could stomach the cost. 

Yeah, I'm being cheap! So what, And???

It was still very good but I think I'm going to have to give them up for the rest of 2013. Might go purchase that Porsche I been eyeing instead...jk :-)

to tell you guys the truth, I am right at 3 - 4 and here is why...  I was really excited to eat here because of all the reviews I read and decided to eat here on Christmas .... I was driving in to Vegas from Sol Cal and was about to arrive around 5PM... I called around 4PM to see how things were and they said verbatim "We will not be accepting any more customers today, we are all sold out." I was confused and asked what it meant and they stated there was so many people waiting, the wait time was over 7 hours which puts them past 11PM (they close at 10:30). So I decided to try my luck the next day... I got there around 3PM to see if I can make a reservation or get a ticket, but when I got there, the wait time was at 422 minutes (I posted a picture lolol). But the workers were nice enough to tell me to come back around 9 and they will try to get me in. I got there at 9PM and there was a wait to pay for the ticket... then there was a wait to get inside the buffet.... at this time it was around 9:45PM... I asked them will I have time to eat and they said yes and that no one will rush me to finish early. Me and we arrived to our table at exactly 9:50 and was greeted by an amazing waiter... we got as many food as we can and we filled our entire table before they start pulling all food.... around 10:30 when the food was gone, we we were about half way done eating, when a stocky, bald, Caucasian male with tattoos came up to us and said please hurry and finish your meal we are closing... I was extremely furious at what happened... not only because I paid over $120 for 2 people, but the fact that the workers in the front stated they will not rush me and now this person is... the only reason why I am between a 3 and a 4 is because the food was not bad.. they oysters were actually pretty good and the steamed crab melts in your mouth.... will I ever go back? Only if I start eating before 9PM!!!

Best buffet in Vegas! Go for all you can drink champagne/mimosas and make it an afternoon
Prime rib and turkey dinner are my favs

What could possibly go wrong when you can eat all of the fresh crab legs your heart desires? An added bonus was how they had them cut for you. I tend to shy away from crab legs because I hate cracking them open.

This buffet is definitely above average in the Las Vegas buffet category, but not anything excellent. 

Here you have your typical buffet divided by origin, such as a "Mexican" corner, "Asian" corner, "Italian" corner, etc. You can get everything from crab legs to steak here as well.

Despite the cost of admission and the wide selection of food types, the food here is all just "good". I would say this buffet is better than the Cosmopolitan's, but I haven't tried enough buffets in Vegas to say much more than that.

I do like that this buffet offers dim sum, and a good variety of desserts, but aside from those and the interior architecture/decor, nothing really stands out as unique for this buffet.

If you can, try to find a deal/discount. Otherwise, you might agree that it's a once-and-done sort of place.

Can't wait to go back!!!  Bacchanal did not disappoint!  

My recommendations...
Steamed Crab Legs
Beef Brisket (the BEST I've ever had)
Sliders
Mac and Cheese
Truffled Potatoes
Baked Potato (had pulled pork in the middle!!)
Crab Ragoons
Har Gao
Custard Buns
Sushi
Guava Juice, Mango Juice
Mango Pudding
Shave Ice
Fresh Crepes
White Chocolate Covered Strawberries
Strawberry Cheesecake Pop
Calamansi Pastry (can't remember the exact name)

Dislikes...
Spicy Fried Fish
Creme Brûlée
Macarons
Passion Fruit Pudding
Lobster Bisque

Didn't get to try the taco station and we forgot about the chicken and waffles.  Next visit for sure!!

Heard lines were pretty long here and we were hoping we wouldn't be another victim as we came here for dinner on a Wed night.  They cashier said the wait would be 45 mins-1 hr but we ended up waiting for 30. We thought we could do the 24 hr Buffet Pass which included Caesars (at additional cost on top of set price) and other buffets along the strip but heard that we would be paying more since we came during dinner. We passed on that and just bought dinner at regular price (around $50) which is pretty pricey.

The restaurant itself is very intimate, fancy furnishings and dim lighting.  Like other buffets, Caesars had a variety of different cuisines: Asian, American, Mexican, Italian and of course dessert! Their seafood bar had Alaskan crabs, scallops, clams, crawfish, shrimp and oysters and more..

I really enjoyed the lasagne and the seafood bar mostly.  The desserts were pretty good, they even had a crepe bar! 

For the food and quality, I thought the price is pretty  steep!  Out of the buffets I've been to on the Strip, I still recommend the buffet at Wynn or Aria (for brunch)!!

The Bacchanal buffet is simply the best of the best!  As the saying goes " you get what you pay for".   Delicious food displayed like fine art!   This definitely a treat to share and sample for those foodies who enjoy variety with flair!

Let me start by saying we found a Groupon for this place and thought it would be a great addition to our ladies trip. Well I definitely underestimated how much of an "addition" we were getting. This spread was just sinful! We went for breakfast/brunch. Every type of egg you could think of, a section just for cheese, sushi, Asian cuisine, made to order omlets, seafood, fruit and a pastry section that will make you gain five pounds just by looking at it! Definitely recommend adding the endless mimosas! Great meal and experience with our without the Groupon!

The ambiance and layout of the place is great. Get there early on Sundays to avoid long lines. While it was a decent size buffet it certainly is not the biggest. The stations are well organized and a good amount of selections. One drawback is the omelette station at the dessert station. The small dishes looks good for presentation but not very practical. Many of the small plates are too hot to grab. The mini pancakes are great but not necessary to have it on small places. Grabbing just two small plates would fill your plate. Get rid of the mini-plate idea. The french toast was the was excellent next to the red velvet mini pancakes. I was disappointed on a dismal fruit bar. A mixed berry dish was about it. The meat selection was excellent. The dessert selection was very average. Overall this place is okay for a $39.00 breakfast buffet there are many places with more selections.

As far as the food-I found this to be the highest quality of a buffet one can get on the strip. It has the usual-crab legs (hot at dinner) and cold during lunch. Plenty of meat selections enough to give you a meat coma for sure. I loved the fried chicken. 

Yes it is really expensive! I believe all buffets are expensive on the strip that are good, but do not go on a holiday otherwise it becomes really expensive and kind of ridiculous. 

I would say the issue for me is the long lines. Nobody wants to wait in those kind of lines. We got lucky and went at a strange time 3 p.m. not lunch or dinner and only had a 30 minute wait. I don't think I would give it such a high review if I had to wait 2 hours. 

Something else I noticed was being really close to the person next to us, to the point where I heard their conversation then just started chatting with them because I kind of felt like I was a part of their conversation even though I wasn't, we were so close I felt like I was eavesdropping but it was not on purpose. 

Overall this is a buffet I would suggest to out of town visitors. I hope it stays good.

If you want to eat here, you're going to have to plan your day around it definitely.  

I love their inventive ticket kiosk system; its much better than your traditional line.  First, go to a kiosk and enter in how many is in your party.  A ticket will print out with a time; that time is when you can go stand in the waiting line to pay and then enter the buffet.  Be prepared, it may be a few hours before you can stand in the pay line.  But what's great about having a ticket is that you can gamble, shop, etc instead of just standing in line.

Once your time is up and you get to stand in the pay line, you might have to wait a bit more before you get in.  On a Friday afternoon, they told us that after a 3 hour wait, it would be an additional 40 minute wait in the pay line.  So we just returned on Saturday for brunch and the wait was only an hour and we got right in after we payed.

I believe the weekend brunch was $45 and totally worth the price.  This and Wicked Spoon are my favorite buffet places in Vegas.  There's a lot of great Asian dishes like sushi, dim sum, pho, pad thai, etc.  Crab legs are even on the brunch menu! They have the cold ones in the display but if can ask for the warm ones they keep in the back :)

And you better save room for dessert!  There's gelato, sweet crepes, mini cakes, tarts, pastries, etc.  One of my favorites was a fruit cocktail in a mint syrup.  A great palate cleanser.

A must try!

Bacchanal is slowly suffering from the usual buffet decline - it was absolutely in it's own league when it first opened but now they're slowly taking things off the menu or substituting things with cheaper versions/items/ingredients. On top of that, the price keeps going up sitting at about $70 (tax & tip included) per person for a weekend dinner. Don't get me wrong, the food and selection is still good and it is one of the best buffets on the strip but it's getting harder to justify coming here. 

Definitely get here as early as possible as the wait time can easily balloon to 3+ hours especially on weekends. They have waitlist kiosks (like Disney's FastPass) so make sure to sign-in about 3 hours prior to your desired eating time - For example if you want to eat around 6 pm, check-in around 3 pm...yea it's that crazy. But if you just can't stand to wait or you got money to wipe your butt with, you can pay an extra $35 per person to skip the line entirely.

My only other tip is to take your time and enjoy everything they have to offer. Maybe even consider dropping that extra $35 to skip the line and write it off as a gambling loss...at least you get something in return. It was fortuitous for me that I rolled with good company that help pass the wait time and frustration so maybe try that since it's cheaper and more interesting. Enjoy!

Horrible checking in system - the worst. 

Waited for almost an hour & the lady in front told us our name is not even on list. 

That's just the wait time to stay in another line to pay..

The lady at the front was rude & disrespectful.. As if she's doing us a favor to talk to us ..

Left hungry & totally upset 

Will never go back .. 

Not going to pay top $$$ to be treated with disrespect

This buffet was a big disappointment! I paid ~$40/person for lunch including 18% tips mandatory for having 6 people or more. There was no crabs! no lobsters! The clams were not satisfying since they make you eat it with corns, potatoes, veggies...What a rip-off!

What else can really be said? I'm a local and love going here with a Groupon for lunch. It's a stellar value for the money spent in my opinion. Likewise the service is also top notch, and friendly. My wife's champagne is always topped off, which indirectly benefits me as well. =)

Out of all of the attractions in Vegas, this one got me the most excited in line. The food is out of this world good. A Buffett with Brie and goat cheese? Eggs Benedict? Awesome! Food was always being refreshed. Great quality. Only downside is they seemed understaffed on the server side. Our server, a very kind older woman was running around frazzled. She said they opened up an extra section and had her take it. Almost everyone at this buffet had a groupon with bottomless mimosas. We got 2 mimosas in 1.5 hours. Not her fault, but it was $40 extra. She was embarrassed by her service and was apologizing to all of her tables. Every table was pilled high with old food plates. Just add a few more servers Caesars, you can afford it. Besides the issue with service I will be back. I mean there was sushi, jumbo prawns, prime rib....

Not as large and expansive as I expected, but a nice variety of food, nonetheless. Also, instead of standing in line for multiple hours, Bacchanal has several kiosks where you can input your cell phone number and receive an expected time for your seating. That way, you can wander the Caesars Forum shops or the casino until you're called back to the restaurant. Once you're called, there is still a 15-30 min. wait for your seat, but that's much better than multiple hours.

Anyways, they have the usual suspects - crab legs, shrimp, and 'world' cuisine (Italian, Chinese, Mexican, and Japanese). You can have your sushi with a taco or some crab legs with your porridge. Overall, I thought the place was well-appointed and the quality of food was good. The dessert bar was expansive - so much to choose from - from cheesecakes to shaved ice to gelato to cake pops. Remember to save room for dessert!

I'm conflicted on this buffet. Reading many reviews name it the number #1 buffet in the country, seems to have jaded my opinion. That why I delayed in writing the review for a few weeks. 
We headed over to the buffet around 4pm on a Monday and expecting a hour wait which is normal. It was actually 106 min in the ticket but we got in texted sooner. After paying around $130 we waited another 20 mins in a line to get seated.
First the decor seemed very dated for modern Vegas I told my wife it felt almost 70's like. The table was fine but the floor looks like it had seen better days.
We sat and ordered our drinks then went up to the buffet, and I will say it did have a ton of selections which honestly you should expect from a Vegas Buffet. 
The Asian food was excellent from the dumplings to the ramen noodle station and the Sushi was buffet sushi nothing special, but the stare was the two seafood stations one cold by the entrance and one hot where you can get fresh out of the water bath crab legs. 
The meat section was kind of disappointing most the meats were dried out like they had been sitting for a while and the lamb in particular was tasty but over cooked. The smoked brisket was terrible.
Nothing else in the main food station stood out for me, which really surprised me because of the reviews online.
The desert bar was excellent but I can think of a dozen other buffets that were equal in desert quality.
Personally I think the Aria Buffet was better and a lot better value.

My god... This Buffet is unreal. I used to live in Vegas for 4 years, and went back to visit with the girlfriend back in February, and hearing all the good press we decided to splurge and try this new buffet. Its unreal. Everything isn't just good but some of the best you will ever have. everything from Crab Legs, to more simple dishes like sweet potato fries, mashed potatos, sushi, bbq, tiny sliders that were unreal tender. Everything in there was amazing.

On our second trip, we thought we would try WICKED SPOON, and boy was that an epic disapointment. The selection was half as big and half as good, with an almost identical price point. we were very upset and ended up making an extra trip here because we wanted this good buffet so bad, and it did NOT disapoint on a second trip.

Go here, try as much as you can, share plates, and just count down the days till you can go again. its food bliss and the #1 buffet in Vegas, with the #2 not even close...
Awesome service the waitress Milka satisfied all our needs and she was very friendly. Awesome place will definitely come back.

After so many reviews I thought I would give this a try. The wait wasn't bad as they give you a time when to anticipate your table as I had no reservation. The food selection was indeed plentiful but I unfortunately found the quality underwhelming. A few items to recommend- poke sushi and tuna were both good. The prime rib wasn't bad. Everything else was really mediocre.

A really top-notch buffet. A wide variety of good options, all fresh and flavorful. You will stand in line to get in to this buffet, but once you're inside you won't be dissapointed. (We arrived at about 5 to check in, and got to our table about 7). The steamed crab was great, the Asian station had a Taro bun that was delicious, and the sushi was great. What really made our experience great was our server Jeff. His attitude and humour were fanatastic. He was fast to bring drinks and checked in frequently despite being very busy. This is a fantastic place to indulge a little while in Vegas.

This is the best buffet I've ever been to, and I know buffets when I see them. But first, some quick tips:

1. Parking is plentiful in the Caesar's structure. Try parking on the outside rooftop 5th floor. It has direct access to an elevator that takes you to the back area of Caesar's casino.

2. The buffet is located near the entrance to the pools. It is where the old Caesar's buffet used to be.

3. Arrive early to beat the line. We got in at 4:15 PM on a Wednesday and waited about 30 minutes to get in.

4. Lunch ends at 3 and dinner begins at 3. Technically this means you can do the old get in for lunch and dinner strat for cheaper prices. 

I wish I took pictures so my eyes could continue to feast on the offerings that the Bacchanal Buffet. Anyways, I could talk about how amazing the food was, but that wasn't just the best part.

I love the decor of this place. It reminds me of candy glass and it has a very vibrant and colorful look. The Asian/Italian station in the back seems to be a bit more intimate and dark though.

My favorites in terms of the food was the great dessert offerings that they have. There were different types of gelato with more exotic flavors along with the typical flavors for those less adventurous. There were all you can eat macarons and I gorged myself heavily on them.

In terms of the regular offerings I was surprised at how tender the prime rib was and the crab was so fresh. They also offered to steam crab for you on the spot so that it doesn't get all rubbery like other places where the crab has been sitting out for a long time. Another pleasant surprise was how authentic the Chinese offerings were. The Chinese style ribs were very good and the dim sum offerings were wonderful.

I enjoyed the sushi, but my girlfriend thought it was a bit dry. Their other American offerings were pretty decent, but nothing to rave about. I didn't like the chicken tenders. They were really weirdly breaded and seemed a little undercooked. Besides that though, the other offerings made me forget about that small oversight. I also really enjoyed the Mexican stuff that they had! Especially the made to order tacos and the large salsa bar.

I would definitely check out Bacchanal Buffet if you got the chance!

Waited 1h in express line that cost extra $15pp, price of buffet $50 on weekend, kids half price. For two adults, two kids, cost $201.00 in express line that took so long it could not be express! Then there is tip. At this point, too frustrated with wait to enjoy food.  For that price, you can get better food and service elsewhere for family of four, assured.  Go eat somewhere else no matter how good the buffet because it will never be better than what you get freshly made to your order in a nice restaurant.  The return on your time and dollar are over at this rate...unless you have nothing better to do but stand and wait for buffet food.

Worth every penny! I attended this buffet for brunch on a Wednesday, so I was lucky I didn't have to stand in a long line. They have delicious and fresh food. Several themed stations. Street tacos! Really..... And made to order! Pho made to order! Crepes were so good. I ate so much! And everything I had was mouth watering. My mom and daughter also enjoyed every single thing they ate. The staff was really nice too. I didn't have alcohol but I think that is included in the price, regular drinks for sure were included. I can't say enough good things about the food. Beware it's expensive and I've herd the wait can be ridiculous, but trust me you will not be disappointed! Join the rewards membership, sometimes you get a discount and if you become platinum you don't have to stand in the long lines, you get your own line

Thanks to my bestie ebony empress treated me to a fabulous time at this buffet
Jefferey was our waiter and he was amazing. He was sure to make sure that we were full and well mimosa and wined out, for sure
Thanks for the lovely time
Music was perfect
The staff here was amazing, keep up the great work

It's one of the most wonderful buffet I have ever had. There are a lot of choice of food, especially my favorite Chinese food. The Chashao is sooo good, even better than I had in China and I love the green tea ice cream so much. I am sure I will come back again.  Thanks for their chef and wonderful servings.

I come to Vegas very often especially to try out the new restaurants since I am a true foodie and I heard so much hype about this place of course I had to try it. 

When I got there the lines was ridiculously long.  They said the wait was over 3 hours long.  I don't know if it's just me but I would never wait in line for 3 hours to eat anywhere.  Luckily my husband is a VIP card holder so we didn't have to wait in the long line which was definitely a plus.  Otherwise I would have left without trying this place.

I have tried mostly all the buffets in Vegas so I had really high expectations for this place. For a buffet their decor is very impressive.  Maybe that's why their prices are a bit higher than most other buffets in Vegas.
