The food was pretty good and the dessert selection was great but I don't see anything that really stands out about this place except for the fact that you have to stand in line for hours for most people and that the price is more than most of the other buffets where you can get about the same quality of food for less in my opinion.  

If your a first timer in Vegas this place will most likely be impressive.  For all the regulars I don't think it's worth all the hype.
Best in Las Vegas... Food had great quality n flavor it might be pricy 4 some people but I rather pay extra than  get something  mediocre , bland food , the type of food u find on buffets in vegas

I had high hopes for this buffet after hearing friends say it's the best buffet in town and after reading Yelp reviews. The food was great; varying cuisines that were delicious. My favorites were the brisket, seafood pasta and dim sum. My criticism with regard to the food is that the seafood selection needs to be improved. Or if you're going to serve crab legs, don't cut them. That's my preference anyway. Service was just OK. The lady waiting on us seemed a bit frazzled, but maybe she had a bad day (?). Also, I asked for extra wet wipes and she said that they were instructed not to but she gave me an additional two anyway. The dining area cleanliness was a bit sketch- food, napkins and utensils on the floor. Overall, the food was great but the entire experience was NOT worth $125 excluding tip.

60 bucks! Well worth it. I was tired of spending $30 average on restaurants for just 1-2 entrees. So I said lets do a buffet! This buffet was great all around. Service was excellent as I didnt have to wait in line. I a vip guest. Cut right to the front. Haha. There was about 30 people in line. Service was great. Food was excellent. King crab. Huge shrimp. Raw oyster. They had a Hispanic selection. Asian selection. Sushi. The sushi was standard. The asian food was very good. Even the fried rice was delicious. They also had dim sum. The desserts was good. So much macaroons! Over for $60 I think its well worth it as so much variety with great quality not just quantity. Give it a shot. One of the the better buffets in vegas and I tried many. Come extra hungry.

Be ready to wait, you will first sign up and get ticket which will tell you when you can come back and get in the line infront if the restaurant....the upside to all the waiting is you will get very hungry.  We went to dinner buffet and got the all you can drink too.  Our waiter did suck at making sure we a drink.  We had to hunt him down to get a drink.  When we are another waiter they told us I'm not your waiter I'll get you're waiter.  

We were also celebrating a birthday, which they wrote on our ticket....don't know why it's not like our waiter acknowledged it all 

The food was all pretty good, it's good if you all want different things.  You get your money worth with the seafood.  Meat eaters will love this place!!!

Best buffet I had in Vegas. Hands down.

The GREAT
-Huge selection
-Food tasted great

The OK
-Pricey

Notice, there is no Bad.

Only good things come from this place.

Dessert, fresh squeezed juice, 18hr brisket, korean short rib, crab legs, oysters, need I say more?  

I made the mistake of going to Bacchanal early on my trip in Vegas. It made every other buffet seem inferior.

Service was good.  We had to pay the Memorial Day Weekend rate ($55pp), but it was well worth it.

In the wise words of a college friend - when you come to this place you need to do the following

1. Eat the good stuff
2. Keep Eating
3. Can you move? If yes, then keep getting food. If not, then stop and wait. Breathing exercises
4. Eat whatever it took to get you stuffed all over again.
5. Sleep.
6. You won't be hungry for the rest of the day.


This buffet is everything that is great about America and everything that's wrong with it too.

Purely amazing. I'll be hitting up Bacchanal again next time I'm in Sin City.

As platinum card holders, Bacchanal Buffet was our #1 spot to eat in Vegas every time we were in town. We usually have a great time at Bacchanal, but when we went there on July 16 we were disappointed. The service was terrible, the food staff in the seafood section was careless and unfriendly, the food quality was not up to par, the seafood was frozen, the meat in the sliders were dry, and you had to crack the heated crab yourself. I will not be returning to Bacchanals anytime soon.

Wow! I am genuinely impressed. I went for lunch last month and didn't have the best experience and I posted a review reflecting my disappointment. The manager Stephanie contacted me and asked me to give them another try. My work schedule is busy this time of year and I cancelled and changed times on her several times and would not have been surprised if she just said to forget it but she didn't. I had a last min change and phoned her on fri, St. Patricks day and said we'd be there in a couple hours. The entire staff from the first cashier you meet to our excellent waiter and everyone in-between was gracious and professional. Our drinks were always refilled and the table cleaned while we were getting more food. As for the food, it really is an amazing display  over several stations. One of the things that really impressed me was how they manage to keep everything looking good, clean, orderly and not picked over. They put out small portions - many in individual little pots and pans and they do this over and over through out the night. The result is even on a fairly busy night, everything looks good and crispy food is crispy, soft food is fresh etc. They really do a hell of a job with that. The food itself? Again I'm impressed. We had many trips to the food stations and took tiny portions of each and everything we tried was good. Standouts were the chicken and waffles, portugese sausage, corned beef, dolmas, crab legs, truffle gnocchi and spicy thai beef. We tried so many items and really only scratched the surface, the selection is insane. Then there's desert... save room because the selection is good and again, a huge  variety to satisfy anyone, even sugar free selections.  As for the room itself, very comfortable and well thought out. You don't feel like you're in a cafeteria. The way the food stations are laid out and the flow and bends of the room break it up and make good sense. Also, the way the food stations are laid out, there are no long lines. You can just graze around and grab what looks good to you. There was a bit of a line up at the meat carving area but with half a dozen dinosaur size roasts, hams, ribs, briskets etc it didn't seem unusual and it moved fast. If you enjoy a good buffet, I don't think you'll find anything better than the Bacchanal or anything even close.

Yes, a star knocked off for the wait before the wait, especially for a non-platinum member, unwilling to pay an extra $25 per head to skip the cashier line - commoner. 
You first have to check-in and get a ticket with your estimated time to come back and wait in line to pay the cashier, then wait to be seated after paying, then wait in line for your food (which I suppose, isn't as stressful but it's still a part of that dreadful WAITING process)!

The total wait was about 90 minutes for me and my friend, for dinner on a Monday night.

Stick to the seafood and meat. 
Seafood-wise: The clarified butter + crab legs / shrimp combo was on point. My friend really loved the oysters.
Meat-wise: Bone marrow, prime rib and beef brisket were pretty delish.
Desserts (if you have room): Creme brulee, freshly made crepes, chinese donuts were my faves 

Glad I was able to experience waiting, eating, but mostly waiting to get into this buffet. Would I do it again? Probably not, but I'd say go ahead and at least try the madness once.

Dinner at 5:30 on Saturday night, July 19. Only waited in line 10 minutes. We had a 24 hour buffet pass and knew that we would have to pay a surcharge to use the pass at the Bacchanal Buffet. Was surprised that the surcharge was $32. Without the pass, the dinner cost for the buffet was $52.

We were seated all the way in the very back of the restaurant which was a perfect spot. We had just a few other four tops around us and our dining room was relatively quiet and away from the clans of families seated at larger tables. Also one end of the buffet was just outside our dining area. It was from this end of the buffet that I began my assessment of just what exactly $52 gets one at this very popular buffet. My strategy before I pickup a plate is to walk the entire buffet line so I can see just what they have to offer and then plan my attack after I have gathered all my intel. 

I don't remember the order of the food stations that I passed on my recon of the smorgasbord but remember passing a sushi, Mexican cuisine, and Italian  food and thinking to myself that I have already seen all this type of food at other cheaper buffets. I was already halfway through my recon of the food line and did not see one item that I wanted to go back for and try nor had yet to see any item that justified the cost of the buffet. I finally passed a station and saw that there were steaming king crab legs being served from lobster pots. Made a note of that station and continued scouting the food line. After turning a corner I saw the lines queuing up at two food stations at the other end of the buffet closest to the entrance. One station was a carving station with at least 25 people backed up waiting online for some meat with one carver there handling at least seven or eight kinds of meat.  Why wouldn't Ceasers spread this meat amongst two carving stations and spread out the crowd? There was no one standing online in any of the other food stations I had already passed so they obviously have room to expand to less used areas of the buffet. I was beginning to get irritated that I had to wait online for food that cost so much money and had yet to impress me. Then I looked passed the carving station to the next food station to see an even longer line was queued up.  This I realized this was the money shot of the buffet; king crab legs, stone crab claws and cooked shrimp. So this was what I was paying so much for: the opportunity to stand in line to eat still frozen crab. 

While the dessert selection was good, it did not compensate for the lack of variety of food on the main buffet nor did it justify the cost. I wish I had read the Yelp reviews before we had eaten here. I feel sorry for some of the Yelp reviewers who stated they waited up to 4 hours in line to eat at this place. I would not come back here nor recommend this buffet. There are much better buffets at the Mandalay Bay, the Encore and Cosmopolitan for less money and less wait time.

First Vegas buffet! I was expecting something a little more bougie and flashier but the food was pretty good. They have a wide selection of meats, Asian food, seafood etc. I also loved how they had bone marrow! Everything was pretty rich so I wasn't able to eat as much as I wanted but overall decent presentation and quality. The seafood section was one of the most popular with plenty of fresh seafood including oysters, mussels, crab and crawfish. They had a large selection of desserts that were just ok but nothing too fancy.

THE LINE IS HORRIBLE...
1 pm in the afternoon and I waited 2 hours... 
I hate buffets in Vegas for this one reason.. 

Once you get by the frustrations of standing near coughing and sneezing sick tourists, and people standing so close to you it feels like they are talking in your ear then you should be fine. 

The food was really good. The servers were always quick to give you a refill on your drink. I went to every station to try one of everything. The sweet potato tots was my favorite out of everything! Greasy yes, but truly addicting! 

Only thing I didn't like was the lasagna. Bit on a onion and I almost gagged! Hate surprise onions in food lol.  

The dessert selection was so large! Every dessert you can think of was there! Brownies, CHECK! Ice cream, CHECK! Macaroons CHECK! 

Very good food but I honestly wouldn't go back though if the line was to long.. I am to impatient. I think there is way to much food in Vegas to have to wait 2 hours for it.

No oysters for the Sunday brunch!  Staff informed us that it was decided to only put the oysters out for dinner, "because no one eats them at brunch."  Really????  I think it is just to save $$$, and what a disappointment.  The sushi was also really lame.  And, the champagne is really "faux champagne" and not the real deal. This used to be one of my favorites, but, for the price, we will not return.  If you want a first-class champagne brunch, go to The Sterling, or just dine at one of the many fine restaurants in Las Vegas.  Save your money and skip the Bacchanal Buffet.

Buffets are the best example of indulgence and depravity in Las Vegas and Caesars' buffet is one of the most popular.

The entrance fee is high at $60 for a Brunch table, but is well worth it just to witness the spectacle of food on display; my only regret is my meager stomach size.

Many buffets sacrifice quality for quantity, but the Palace doesn't suffer mediocrity. 

Just a few of their features:
On-demand sliced roast beef
Crepe maker
20 gelato flavors
Too much fudge
Candy jars, not just for display
Make-your-own charcuterie 
Juice bar
King Crab legs!

My personal favorite was the endless pork belly ^.^

The food is mostly restaurant quality to justify the cost, with almost no exceptions. From soups to seafood to meats to veggies to Asian fare to their island of desserts, anyone of taste would be hard pressed to not fill their plate(s).

It's almost a shame to get a cut of prime rib, take one bite, then throw the rest away.

First time here and WOW it is AMAZING!!!! $7 extra for bottomless mimosas and it's worth it ! I came here at 10 so breakfast was still being served! Everything on my plate was amazing. Eggs Benedict, Chilaquiles, hash brown, and bacon was all delicious!!!!! Dessert was even better. They also had lunch items out but I was more hungry for breakfast!! It all looked amazing though. Dessert was also good. They have a crepe station and gelato!! Our server Jeff was soooo nice and friendly!!

The food I had here was the best food I have ever had in life. They had several different types of cuisine to fit every diet. The beef was so succulent, the sushi was so fresh and crisp and the dessert bar was to die for. Every single thing was delightful and the presentation of the food was just as great as the taste. The only cons were the long lines and it was a bit pricey but it was beyond worth it.

Coming here was #1 on the list for me because it was highly recommended. The Bacchanal Buffet is located in Caesar's Palace by two other restaurants. The wait line was probably about 15-20 minutes when my party and I got there for dinner. However, if you're a diamond/platinum member you can pay for the buffet pretty quickly & you can pay $35 for just 2 people. Regular price for dinner is $54.99. The food is really good and of course when in Vegas, go all out. The desserts were very delicious and quite unique to me. From Thai tea boba shots to cheesecake pops. You won't be disappointed.

Bacchanal is the biggest, newest buffet in Vegas. All inside Caesar's Palace. Naturally, being one of the newest and hyped as one of the best, lines for this place last almost 3 hours.

Luckily, someone had a VIP card which meant that 3hr wait turned into 15 minutes.

Everything is typical Vegas buffet once you get in, which is to say, nice. But you realize just how massive it is once you get your food. You could get lost just going from station to station.

It's got everything all the other buffets have and they even have freshly squeezed juice for lunch. The Texas squeezed orange juice being the best which explains why it runs out so quickly.

The crab legs weren't spectacular. Possibly because it's pre-cut and iced already. The oyster shooters were good though. Everything else was decent. I didn't get to try all the food here but what I did try, it was good enough. Not all it was hyped up to be but I'd still eat it and enjoy it.

Dinner lines do get long. Especially for the meats (prime rib, lamb, etc). Standing in that may be a 10 minute wait in and of itself.

All in all, it's a good experience but other buffets are comparable and the lines for those are going to be shorter. Go here if you want to hit up a new buffet.

Good buffet. Excellent presentation. Disappointed with the crab claws, meat was difficult to extract. Excellent variety consisting of Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Italian and seafood. I ate 4 of the soups and all were very good. Lobster bisque and truffle bisque were my favorite. Also immensely enjoyed the fresh juices. 

Didn't care for the pitcher of bloody Mary's. Tasted like well vodka used and mix was not fresh. Will skip this next time. 

Also waitress was grumpy- no smiles or anything. Didn't understand that we wanted coke, and finally gave up Pepsi after we told her 6 times we wanted soda. 

The overall price of the buffet is almost twice the cost of the other buffets. You get what you pay for.

Best Buffet in Vegas! I was born and raised here and have tried them all, and this is by far the best buffet. The seafood is delicious and fresh, the Italian food is amazing, the Mexican section taste authebtic, the Asian section is alway full of surprises, I always have a cheese and meat plate because it's so good! And the desserts oh my! They have crepes which are amazing! Plus like 15 flavors of ice cream and sirbet, chocolate strawberries, creme brulee, oies, cakes, cookies, and candy! The price is well worth the taste and amount of variety!
Incredible. Worth the price. Many different types of cuisines - all very tasty and authentic. Great service, and wonderful desserts!

A bit above average buffet.  Selection not that much among the different cuisine.  Dessert is probably their best tasting and quality.  Nice decor and host but that's all.   Service is almost non-existence and lots of messy tables with dishes... Not cleaned up,  very unsightly!  

The Carnival still the best buffet in LV... And I've been to all of the so-called best.

This place is so overrated.  Came in for weekdays brunch at 11am... juices were all out at around 1130. Fried chicken meat was old and bland. The rock crabs were ok being crabs as they are. However, I have to say that their Pho was surprisingly authentic compare to many specialty Pho restaurants. I'm Vietnamese and i know what the Pho I'm talking about,  so trust me on this. Save ur wallet and get off of the strip to eat better and cheaper.

Coming from Hawaii we decide to try this buffet because of recommendations we had back home. Now for the price of the buffet we expected more than what we got. Yes, it was fun with all the different food booth but my low rating is all about experience. Caesar' Palace. When that name comes up we're thinking classy and not trashy. What I mean by this is that I didn't expect raw chicken, which I experienced. Manager gave me a quick apology and never came back to tell me anything else. Sadly for the price I paid, we had better buffets which was cheaper than this place. And the lines, what do you expect in Vegas but some lines are worth the wait but not this one...the crab legs are cut for you but I still had better crab meat elsewhere... we tried to like this place but waiting an hour just to be seated and another 20 minutes through the seafood line just not my cup of tea... sub par food and service slacked after awhile. Water never refilled until almost to the end of our meal. Pay if you must to get the experience but watch your food...

Surprisingly unimpressive. Super crowded. Overpriced. Don't come here if you're not a pork eater. There's pork in everything. If you love pork, you're in heaven. 

The bathrooms are filthy as everyone jams food into their system then tries to dump it out. Refill. Repeat. Basically they smell like Caesar farts. 

Dessert and nice staff was the best part. They present the food in a stylish way. Chicken and waffles in a waffle cone. Sweet potato tots in a nice cardboard cone. But ultimately it tastes like elementary school cafeteria food. 

We've been doing the buffet tour and we're really excited about this one after reading reviews. Already been to Wynn, Aria, Cosmo, and Bellagio and Bacchanal comes in dead last for food and experience. My wife and I stared at each other after the meal and tried to figure what was the big deal and why we paid double to hang out amongst rude crowd and eat bland food. But it looked damn good.

This is indeed the buffet of all buffets in Vegas.  It's definitely pricey, but they have pricey food items to go along with it.  My main reason for wanting to try this place was to try their bone marrow.  Nice chunks of fat in it, but I wished it was more flavorful.  It had some nice subtle flavors to it, but the fat to flavor ratio was a bit unbalanced for me.  The real winner of the meal was the caviar.  It was in a cup full of buttery creamy soup.  I was never a huge fan of caviar, but I think anything soaking in that soup would've been just as delicious.  Their ox tail was also something worth taking a second trip for.  They seem to have a larger selection of seafood than meat options and absolutely delicious dessert.  Thai tea ice cream float, gelato, cakes - the list goes on.
As for the details of the visit, we had gone on a Tuesday at around 8pm with a party of 5.  The lines were considered short during this time with only a 30 minute wait.  I don't feel like we missed out on anything going during the weekday as opposed to the weekend because there was still so many good food options to choose from.  Because they're so busy, it takes awhile to get the table cleared so for a table of 5, it was uncomfortable at times eating off the table because it was already so full.

Best buffet in Vegas by a long shot. I like the build your own stations for noodles and tacos. Great quality of food that seems to consistently be fresh. Minus one star for slightly rude service, but I guess I shouldn't expect too much from a buffet.

Since my sisters and I only decided to try one buffet while we were in Vegas, I chose this one based on its dessert bar. Which did not disappoint! 

Our party of 3 ppl arrived during late brunch time and of course there was an extremely long line. The hostess walked us through their wait time process so we hung around the casino before returning less than an hour later. When we did, it didn't seem like they checked our ticket so I wondered if we could've returned a lot earlier so that we could eat sooner. 

The food and variety was good! I really enjoyed the hot king crab legs although I wish they had lobster. My group ended up staying through lunch and into dinner time where we got to see the menu change! This made it definitely worth as we were only charged for lunch time fees (~$40/person rather than supposed ~$55)! 

I probably spent the majority of my time eating ice cream and crab legs but my tummy couldn't be any more happier!

"For $51 dollars I was expecting so much more quality." 

Food: We came around brunch time so got the best of both worlds. 
(+) The breakfast portion of the buffet was great! I mean how can you mess up breakfast food?!?! Eggs, bacon, sausage, red velvet pancakes, and chicken and waffles were the best. 
(-) Eating seafood at a buffet has never been something that I really enjoyed so the sushi was dry and worth space in your stomach, crab legs had a variety which was ok and easy to eat so you might enjoy that, and the ceviche was something to forget. 
(+) The American BBQ section was good. I opted for the brisket which was fatty and delicious. Beans had bacon bits in them so I enjoyed that. Mac and cheese were oozing with so much cheese along with the mash potatoes that had way too much cheese in them. 
(-) The pho was no good, try it but it wasn't good at all. The noodles were overcooked and the broth was flavorless. 
(+) Tacos were good and they had 3 meats and I picked carne and pork. They have an assortment of different sauces and condiments. 
(+) If you make it to the dessert bar then you will have so many options. The dessert bar game here is strong and you will end up getting everything lol. 

Vibes: The dining area is kind of dim which made it difficult to take good pictures of all the food I ate. Check my pictures attached and you'll know what I'm talking about. 

Service: Our waitress was super accommodating and nice! She always made sure that our plates were taken away and our drinks were always refilled. 

Waited 2 hours for a $51 dollar buffet to realize that I don't like to eat at buffets and can't stuff my face like how I used to when I was younger.

Too high of a price and wait. We came here for Christmas dinner. $190 for two people with express passes and we still has to wait about half an hour. With no express passes? The wait would be 644 minutes. I'm not exaggerating. They have a machine that calculates the wait time. The good part is that once you're inside, it's not crazy in there. The selection looks decent in appearance but when you taste it, you'll feel like it's a bit subpar. 

Nothing stands out here. The only two things I really liked was the lamb and suprisingly, the egg tart dessert. All else was just meh and I tried everything.

People love this buffet but here's some hard advice that is just plain true. Unless you just want to stuff your fat face, just go somewhere else nice, you'll spend less or equal money for better quality food. If you must eat at a buffet, I actually liked the Village Seafood buffet in Rio much better.

Any kind of food you can imagine, at its finest, all in one place.  The employees are happy to have you there.  All-you-can drink 1% oj mimosas included?!  Sign me up!  This was a fabulous experience, and I can't wait to come back.  Maria and Fidencio were such kind and beautiful servers, making our experience that much better.  :)

The best ever. Crab legs, meat selection, cheeses, etc.... Whatever other buffets have just 20x better. It's just a little pricey but worth the money and wait time. Come early and get a fast pass ticket!

Food here is ridiculous. You couldn't ask for a better seafood selection. Love the street tacos station! The deserts were ridiculous - try the warm hazelnut cake with a scoop of Italian cookie gelato. You won't be disappointed!

We came in abut six minutes before lunch (11am) and were pleasantly surprised when they charged us the breakfast rate  --woot woot! They hadnt transitioned into lunch yet so we were able to sample a bit of breakfast and it was good. the donuts were hot and the selection was extensive...

But lunch, that's what we came for. buffets in vegas are a dime a dozen --obvs. and we're not very hard to impress. but when we saw a photo of the wagyu beef sliders we knew we had to make the musty trek to caesars and have at it. we had devoured the best of the best of EVERYTHING -- paella, "chicken and waffles" which was technically a chicken wing and waffle fries IN a sugar waffle cone. but each on its own was good! my favorite thing was the bbq pork bao. i know, random! but it was the perfect balance of savory and fluffy. 

the dessert selection was also great. don't sleep on the mango pudding --trust me. the fudges are each worth a nibble and go all in with the creme brulee. You can pass on the candied cheese cakes on a stick. they were just aight. 

anyway, bacchanal was indeed a feast fit for the Gods!

Food was good quality but not as good as Bellagio or Mandalay Bay. The line was the longest I have seen in Las Vegas in a few years. Selection was larger than the two buffets mentioned. Pretty happy with this buffet. The long wait was the worst aspect of my experience.

After hearing positive things about Caesar's new buffet, I decided to give it a try.  Admittedly, I am not usually a buffet fan because I am big on food quality, which buffets typically lack.  I went into Bacchanal with an open mind but low expectations.

I got there about 45 minutes before closing and had wait about 15 minutes to get seated.  Walking around, I was pretty impressed with the selection.  

I started with some of the Asian and Italian selections, which were not bad but not spectacular.  I had a rigatoni and sausage dish that had a little bit of a funky flavor to it.  On my next trip, I opted for American dishes, including bbq brisket, mac and cheese, a wagyu slider, and fish and chips.  The brisket was very tender and juicy and very smokey.  I did not expect the buffet to have actual smoked meats, but I was pleasantly surprised.  It does not compare to what you will find in Texas, but for a Vegas buffet, it was pretty good.  The wagyu slider was a mighty fine little burger.  It was, to my astonishment, cooked medium, so it was still juicy and flavorful.  If I was not already so full, I would have gone back for more.  The fish in the fish and chips was very fishy tasting, so I could not eat more than a bite of it.

In sum, Bacchanal is one of the top buffets in Vegas.  You could easily have a better meal for the money elsewhere at a non-buffet, but if you are intent on a buffet, this is a worthy choice.  Studio B at the M Resort is equal in quality at a fraction of the price, so that is still my favorite, but it is a 15 minute drive from the Strip.
Had lunch there with a friend.  Just another Vegas buffet.  It was over-priced and had to stand in line for quite some time to get in.  Wold not go back.

The biggest buzz...i get that there are many different buffets and i get that not everything that glitters is gold...This place does satisfy the appetite of the tourists. But i don't know if it stands out as much...

we saw crab legs, oysters, asian cuisines, italian, mexican, etc...
a whole island of desserts.

I feel like wicked spoon was more impressive.
The buffet of your dreams!!! Beautiful, bountiful food served in a warm, comfortable environment. LOTS of delicious options to please everyone. Mmmm take me back now!!!

Arrived at 2pm knowing the dinner would start an hour later. Saved $20 and everyone still got to feast on oysters and crab legs like there was no tomorrow. 

They've got a wide selection of foods for any taste from Mac and cheese to dim sum to street tacos made to order. Some favorites were the truffle onion soup, smoked bbq chicken wings (as good as some I've had in Louisiana), the cheese plates, and the brisket. Dessert-wise again there's a wide selection of ice creams, tarts, mousses, and cakes. You'll most likely find something to satisfy the sweet tooth. Plus their macarons are really quite flavorful. 

Only real issue I had here was the overuse of salt. I'm used to less salt in my diet overall, but even accounting for that, a lot of the foods just seemed to be overly salted to the point that I felt guilty eating it. Hopefully it was just a one time kinda deal...but other than that ambience is nice and service is decent. Would probably come back if my friends wanted to, but I probably wouldn't spark the idea. 

It was good for a one time kinda deal.

A total disappointment!  Literally ate one bite of each dish hoping it wouldn't be a fail...but it was.

The food is DEFINITELY not worth the price that was paid.  Seafood was lackluster and had few options.  Crab was waterlogged (even the "hot" version was waterlogged).  

The meat carving section was not good.  BBQ ribs and brisket were waaaay too smokey.  The prime rib seemed like it was rushed through cooking and the person at that station did not know how to cut the meat properly (cutting it into weird chunks, instead of the typical slices).  

The rest of the hot foods were forgettable.  As mentioned earlier, you'll only have one bite of each dish and be disappointed. 

The desserts were meh as well.  The only thing that WASN'T a total fail was the creme brulee.  Although if the only thing that was worth getting a second time (or taking a second bite of) was a small aluminum foil dish of creme brulee, that in itself is a fail.

Servers were nice, but inattentive.  Water glasses were empty for the majority of the meal and it took a long time to get ahold of anyone.



Wound up going to Wicked Spoon two nights later and was totally satisfied there.

Bacchanal is the most expensive buffet I've ever been to, but it's also the only buffet that I have felt was a good value.  The quality of the food is so high, and the service is so good, that it was unlike any buffet experience I've ever had in Las Vegas or elsewhere.

Usually the ambiance at a buffet just makes me sad, so I tend to avoid them.  People waddle to the service stations and ladle massive quantities of sub-par food onto their plates like they are plugging up for the winter.  Nobody ever looks like they are enjoying themselves or having a good time.  But everybody at Bacchanal had a smile and as I looked around the room all I saw were happy people laughing and enjoying themselves.

When I say "good food", I mean that the food is genuinely delicious--not just "good for a buffet."  Every dish I tried would have been appropriately served as a restaurant entree or appetizer by itself.  It's like the chefs at Bacchanal are just executing an excellent menu that happens to be served in buffet format.

The seafood and meat carving stations were the best I've seen.  Fresh, high quality proteins and a vast variety.  I also really enjoyed the southern/diner-style station.  Usually this area consists of sad looking meatloaf and a few fried items.  But at Bacchanal, there were some really creative dishes including sweet potato tots in a nice glaze, decadent mashed potatoes and carved meats like lamb and prime rib.

The dessert station was my favorite spot by far, though.  They had macaroons that rivaled the quality in some French bakeries I've visited--and six different kinds!  Plus a nice selection of creamy gelatos, fresh tarts and other baked goods.

You know those photographers who take your photo at the entrance to an amusement park so that you can buy it when you leave to commemorate the experience?  There is one of those at the entrance to the buffet.  I thought it was a little weird, but I guess I can understand why someone might want to document their Bacchanal experience.  One of my friends suggested that it might be better to photograph diners AFTER dinner as they exit.  I agree that would be way funnier.

Yes, this is an expensive buffet.  But it's also a fantastic dining experience that is worth the $50+ and the long wait in line.  I did not expect to be saying that.  But Bacchanal redefined my expectations for what a good buffet can be.

This is my second try at the bacchanal buffet at Caesars. Try to get here early if you can to avoid long lines. They have a computerized wait time system so you can get a ticket and come back later. We can around 4pm on a Tuesday for early dinner and the line up was still within the ropes only about a 10 minute wait. The food is excellent for a buffet style restaurant. Ample seafood variety cold and hot options. I like that they have portions of dishes in separate small plates so you get a nice portion for one with condiments and toppings. Excellent steaks and meats and hot dishes, Asian selection bbq meats dim sum rice and noodle dishes and sushi. Love the noodle station. So many options. They do change the menu. Desserts were amazing. I could eat only the dessert selection and be happy. Gelato bar with fresh ice creams and sorbets and they have Mochi ice cream. Cake pops were delicious. They don't have a large variety of fruit but they have the usual favourites. The drinks with the buffet include squeezed juices, soft drinks, teas and coffees. No pictures this time too busy eating. Overall expensive buffet but you get your money's worth here.

This is definitely one of the best buffets in Vegas hands down. However, for me, I think the price you pay isn't worth the food you get. Don't get me wrong, the food is good and the selections are plenty. I just believe that there are other buffets out there in Vegas that compare and are less expensive. With that said, if you have never been to this place, it's one that should be checked off of your list.
Really enjoyed. Perfect.  Normally I don't like buffet but my husband does..it was good to me.

BEST BUFFET EVER!

What else can we add?  The hands-down BEST BUFFET we've tried in Vegas!

Great selection of fresh seafood (oysters, clams, crab legs).

Great Kobe sliders!  Melt-in-your-mouth prime rib.  Bone-in ribeye.  

Everything was FRESH and excellent.  Desert was not the best we've had but who has room for desert anyway?

I've visited Bacchanal numerous times before the Yelp career.  It' s been 2 years since the last visit and yes, I'm still a fan.

Bacchanal service: Consistently good through all my visits, our servers were always good with clearing the table and checking up on our drinks.  The check in process is now automated via a kiosk that will text you when it's your turn to be seated.  I remember back in the day, the line was the only option.  I love technology!

Bacchanal Buffet:  The buffet section seems to snake around for eternity to get to the end and I'll always start with sushi/sashimi section.  The sushi is on par with your casual sushi restaurant.  Here are some of my favorite dishes that you normally wouldn't find at a buffet.  The truffle deviled eggs were an absolute delight. The boutique cheese section has an great selection if you're a cheese freak like me.  Carnivores will delight at the many high quality meats to take down.  The prawns are big in size and fresh.  The mac n cheese and the street corn are in the same section, so try them both.  The desserts are all sample size so you can so many without feeling too guilty.

Bacchanal ambiance:  There's a contemporary high end dining area appeal.  This could pass for a nice restaurant easily. The tables are large which makes sense as multiple plates can get to the table for serious buffeters.

Overall Bacchanal represents the Las Vegas strip in many ways.  Pricey, over the top fun, but in the end you get the quality Vegas experience that you expected when put down the money.  Fast before you visit, then let it rip when you sit down.  See you in the sushi section! =)

Please don't make me pronounce the name of this place. I am ESL and not too cultured. 

Back what? Oh. Oh hey now. Calm your tits. Not here at least. ;) 

NO! Anyway...

Every penny is well worth being here. Come with an empty stomach. Come with patience as the line is like a pilgrimage. Think of how Oliver Twist begs for another serving but i our case, it's just getting a table. It can be a ridiculously long wait. 

Like I said, it was worth it if you have patience and obviously the money queue in! 

The food is great in quality and presentation. It is better than most of the buffet that I've been. It is well rounded from almost every cuisine in the world. I tend to focus my attention to steaks, seafood and shellfish then sweets. 

The area is cleaned up almost promptly. The drinks they have are not too shabby. The staff is quite attentive of what their customers need. I don't demand much. Just top off my tea and change of napkins once I have used it.

Bacchus was the god of wine and hedonism, and a bacchanal  was an over-the-top hedonistic experience; almost an orgy. So I expected a lavish, high quality buffet at the Bacchanal at Caesars...not so...instead, I found it to be overpriced, with so so food offerings! Go to Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan! Less expensive and far superior to what the Bacchanal has to offer.

Loved the kiosk check-in and follow-up text to pay the cashier. A wise move on the part of Caesars and allows patrons to gamble or be otherwise occupied instead of waiting in line.

After paying the cashier, we were ushered to the photo line...not sure why anyone would want their photo taken while waiting for the buffet, but ok...

We tipped ahead of time, and our server commented on that, and thanked us. She was pleasant enough and very harried; looked like the restaurant was understaffed. We kept piling our dirty dishes on the side of the table, and it wasn't until we were on our dessert course that she started to pick up a few dishes. Again, really?

The restaurant looks old and tired....the carpet and chairs are stained...definitely not what I'd expect from an expensive restaurant.

We were seated near the seafood station, which made for great entertainment! There was a run on crab legs the entire time, with many patrons piling their plates high with crustacean limbs. I guess no one ever told them that they could go back as many times as they wanted...it was hilarious indeed to watch people juggling multiple plates of food...

Now to the actual food offerings...

The salad bar was ok, but nothing to write home about. I did enjoy the individually plated red and yellow beet salad. 

The overrated seafood station was exactly that...overrated. If you're not used to good food, then this will work for you. The ingredients were fine, but the overall experience was run of the mill; not what I'd expect from an expensive, highly rated establishment.

The Asian and Mexican stations were predictable and ok. The pad thai and thai curry chicken were good. The refried beans were very flavorful but the street tacos were meh...

The meat station was ok. I grabbed a bacchanal spud, expecting a loaded baked potato - sour cream and bacon. Well, it had shredded beef in it too...was not expecting that, and was not impressed.

Dessert was nothing exciting either...I tried the blood orange sorbet so I could compare it to the one at Wicked Spoon. The Bacchanal version was overly sweet...the chocolate oreo mousse was ok.

So don't waste your time here. For a richer dining experience, with quality food, an exquisite ambience, and top-notch service, go elsewhere...

This place is seriously in need of better management!  Waited in line for hours to pay; they could have hired more help to clean up the tables..... I have been here several times and will not return again.

Bacchanal is quite breathtaking... as far as décor and the amazing variety of fantastic food. Whatever you want- it is here. The bottomless mimosas are a great deal, and the champagne is top notch. If you want to impress out of town guests, you must take them here. The wait staff is very attentive and sweet.
Vote the best brunch in Vegas it true but I feel lately it's gone down a lot the service and the food but maybe it was just this one day.even at its worst they are the best

I was excited to try my first experience at this Buffet.  I had tried once before, but the line (and wait) was so insane that we never would have made it in prior to closing.  We went on a weeknight (off holiday time) and got in within 10 min.  

The buffet is very well designed.  The ambiance is comfortable, and everything is well laid out.   Service was pretty amazing and the part off all staff - very friendly, and helpful. We also had 3 young kids, and they didn't seem to mind, although we were seated in the back.

My biggest problem was the food.  Don't get me wrong - it was well made.  However it was incredibly rich - heavily spiced, sauced, and more (depending on the dish).  The main par tof the problem was there was little to nothing fresh to balance it. The fresh items, like salad, fresh fruit, and more were also poor, or sauced/spiced themselves.  The buffet has a shockingly limited salad bar section.  The desserts had 4 options for fruit (watermelon, cantaloupe, honeydew, and mixed berries). The buffet seriously needs more simple fresh dishes to balance the rich food.  This issue alone dropped it two stars.  

The dessert section though is the highlight of the buffet - a large and diverse variety, including some options you have to ask for (like shaved ice with homemade syrup).  Definitely worth a good chunk of the visit - if you still can handle it after eating the rich food.  

All in all, it was a worthy experience, but (especially as a local) I don't think all be back.

My best experience in this Buffet so far! You are lucky if you get Alvaro as a server  he's such a fun person to be around and Haas traveled all over the world so he will entertain you with many stories and give you best traveling tips to visit places and save money. For the food he went extra mile and was very patient with us! Brought us some VIP serving huge of king crab legs !!! Yummy ! Best ever

Line...wait...Line...wait...horrific experience. So bad that I created a Yelp account just to tell everyone. I've been to many buffets in my life and waited in many buffet lines. But Bacchanal, you take the cake on this one.

I can't complain about the 1 hour wait to get into a buffet. I've waited 2 hours at other buffets before. I'm used to it, but to wait the same amount of time once you get in just to get some crab legs? Ridiculous.

The 2 highest traffic foods, Seafood and Meat, are placed right next to each other. The Seafood line backed up into the Meat line so no matter which you wanted to eat, your wait doubled. By the time I got back to my seat, my meat was cold and I was completely discouraged from going back to try anything else and/or get seconds.

A party of 9 at $51/person before tax and gratuity, we feel robbed.

The food I did get to eat was good. Would have been great if they were at their intended temperature.

Recommendations:
1. Move the Meat section clear away from the Seafood section.
2. Can't move the Meat section for whatever reason? Rope off the Seafood and Meat lines so they don't blend together.

I hope this gets to an Executive that has the power to make some changes.

To future interested consumers, the Seafood line is located at the entrance so take a peak before you decide to fork out $51-before-tax-and-gratuity. Maybe by the time you go, my review made a difference.

The food was delicious and a great selection!  The service not so much.  Horrible service.  Several dirty plates remained on the table.  The server didn't remember our drink order and never came back to the table.  Service should be a top priority for a place like this.

The food was nasty, and the price too expensive. Definitely not worthy of the hype and wait. The clams were sandy, the crawfish were dry (like they were frozen) or the meat was black like they were dead!!, the orange juice was grocery store quality, the street tacos lacked salt, the pineapple was sour, the deserts were nasty and they only have Pepsi products for soda. Need I say more??? 

Try wicked spoon. Much better in my opinion.

I wanted to like this place. Heard so many good things, but for $58 for dinner definitely not worth it. Im writing this as im here eating. So far everything is cold. Prime rib, sauages, fish plates - sea bass and sole. Plates holding fish are hot, but fish itself is cold. Meatballs in pile of sauce - cold. Guacamole is in back - have to ask for it. Steamed crab leg - finally something warm. Street tacos were good and hot. Went for another chunk of sausage and prime rib - finally some warmth. Seafood pasta - tiny bit of warmth. Mac n cheese - chilly. Little serving of ravioli - cold. Sugar free chocolate brownie and gelato is real good. All the food tasted good, looked good, with a lot of selections it was just cold. Though no lobster or duck. For $58 there should be some lobster - at least some damn bisque.
Probably the best buffet in Las Vegas, especially if you're in the mood for seafood.  It really is well worth the price.  The sushi, crab, shrimp, fish.....just a wonderful experience!

4 star for service, 4 star for food, and 4 star for price. 
Service : attentive for buffet and very nice. Cleaned out the plates on point.

Food: four stars because the variety is amazing but the SALT level is over board, caution if you are on salt restriction. If they just added less salt and let the natural flavors kick in.

Price is very fair considering the variety 

I think it is most well rounded buffet in Vegas to date.

Things that Vegas doesn't need any more of: steakhouses, bros and buffets. Regardless, hearing about a new buffet opening up at Caesar's Palace had me intrigued (especially with the success that Wicked Spoon brought to the buffet game). There was a lot of hype: "over 500+ dishes!", "only 20 some odd dollars!", etc... We made sure to check out a little early on Sunday so that we weren't hit with waiting in a monstrous line. We get there and the line moves along fairly quickly. It takes about 20 minutes for us to get to the cashier. She then tells us that it's $50 per person.

She breaks it down:
- Food is ~$20 +/- some change
- Mandatory Champagne/Mimosa addition (Might be a Sunday thing. None of us want to drink after going out the night before.)
- 18% automatic gratuity (because we have a group of 10)
 
We're ready to be seated, but then our elderly hostess miscounts our group for 8 and tells us that we need to wait for a table that can seat 10. Another 15 minutes goes by, then they take us to our tables, plural...separate. What the hell did we pay 18% extra for then? Maybe it was for the service, but I fail to see how a waitress who came around maybe 3 times to fill waters, is deserving of it. The manager came out to what I assume was going to be an apology, but all we hear is that we can take it or leave it. No real, sincere apology. 

The food, in my opinion, was okay, at best. There were some hits: the mini carafes of fresh juice, the ramen, and maybe a few of the desserts. Everything else...it's been done before.

After this experience, I'm tempted to give up on Vegas buffets (with the exception of Wicked Spoon). 
Do yourself a favor AND save a little dough. 
Go to Estiatorio Milos instead, for their lunch special. Three courses, $20.11. You'll get better service and far better food. Plus, you won't feel disgusted by yourself.

The food in the pictures look way better than my experience. I am a huge sushi fan, half the reason why we chose this buffet, and their only choices were rolls that I can get at a grocery store. The prime rib was delicious but overall I wasn't impressed for the price. Be prepared to wait- the includes waiting to get in line to pay and waiting to get your seat. Arrived on a Tuesday night at 7:00 and only had about a 45 minute wait.  This was our second visit since it opened and was glad to see that they have strived to uphold the quality of execution.  All the flavors were amazing.  Some standouts were the lamb chops, prime rib, sushi, oysters and kobe sliders.  

Their dessert station was amazing as the wife and I indulged in endless amounts of creme brulé, macaroons, chocolate covered strawberries and much more.  

Plates were regularly being cleared and drinks constantly being refilled.  We will definitely be  again in the future.

Overhyped in my opinion.

Be sure to show up early if you don't want to wait too long - I came on a sunday, waited in line for ~70 minutes starting from 4 PM. 

The selection has great variety - you can have anything from Chinese, Japanese, Mediterranean, Italian, Mexican, and they have a nice carvery (including prime rib) and a seafood section. Despite the wide selection, I wasn't too impressed with the quality, and at that point, it becomes a matter of stacking as many steamed crab legs as you can to make the most of your money (good for the seafood lovers :P)

I did enjoy the prime rib, the pork ribs as well as the dessert section - they have a nice variety of macarons, creme brulee, gelato, fudges, mousses and more. 

Service was attentive and friendly.

Pretty decent buffet, probably best I've been to but a little pricy. Get the crab legs apparently. Nice decor and service though.

On our latest Vegas trip, we went to Bacchanal, Bellagio and Sterling brunch on consecutive days so I had a direct comparison of all 3 of what is generally considered the best buffets in Vegas. This one was by far our least favorite and almost double the price of Bellagio. 

Let's talk about the crab legs first because that's what people think about when they talk about Vegas buffets. They only have snow crab whereas Bellagio and sterling both have king crab and the size of the snow crab is tiny. 

They do have a huge selection of different cuisines and the diversity is more than the other 2, but I prefer quality over quantity. The best things here that stood out to me was their crispy duck, lamb which was beautifully seasoned and gigantic dessert selection. The prime rib was good but Bellagio was much better. Everything else I thought was better done at the other 2 buffets.

The service was also lacking as it took a long time for our plates to be cleared. We even had to move some dirty plates to the table next to us a few times.

P.S. The wait on Friday night at 8 pm was about 30 minutes.

The reviews were right. This place is GREAT! We arrived at 12pm on a Thursday and only waited 10 minutes from the time we walked into the line, paid, and were seated! I was surprised! We paid $37.99/per person for lunch! 

The ambiance is very nice and super upscale for a buffet but what else can you expect?? Vegas is known for it's buffets! The presentation of the food was lovely! I made sure to try a little bit of everything and boy oh boy, was it good! I literally loved everything I tried! I'm usually very picky when it comes to sushi but I loved the sushi here! The dessert station was very large and had wonderful options as well! The hubs and I were here for a couple hours! 

Our waitress was okay. She wasn't the most personable person and was slow at bringing our drinks and clearing our table. We also had an older gentleman take our picture before we paid to get in and then tried to sell us the pics after we were done eating. We decided not to buy the pictures. 

All in all, this is definitely the best buffet for the price and quality of food. We will definitely be back the next time we're in Vegas!

Totally overhyped!!!!!

Good Buffet so far but let me Tell you we went to few openings wynn, cosmopolitan & every Buffet was good when they opened but After few Weeks prices went up quality down very sad& Bad. :-(

Why only 2 *? Almost None of the Things were labeled. I Really like to know what i m Putting on my Plate, Waiting Time 1 hour is too Long when just 1 cashier is staying there, the others were not existing  ;-( restrooms Not existing inside or Maybe i missed it???!

All in all if they Improve& Hold the quality i will try it again.
Gone to crap. This is no longer worth even close to what they charge. Mediocre food at best. Not what it used to be.

I would give zero stars if I could. The customer service here SUCKS!  

During Thanksgiving weekend of last year, we waited 4.5 hours for the buffet and paid $50 to experience bad customer service, so so food and for our dream to be shattered when they said they ran out of Alaskan King crab... although the sign for the Alaskan King crab was still out but it was only snow crab legs out for grabs. My husband and I felt cheated.  A big name buffet trying to pass off snow crab for Alaskan King crab?  We waited for 4.5 hour for the Alaskan King crab legs and I had asked them repeatedly to make sure that they have it while we were waiting in the long line. After dinner, we tried to speak to a manager and the guy brushed us off and told us to speak with the hostess. And all the hostess did was handed us a complaint form.  Hubby took time to fill it out and explain our disappointment but months had passed and no word from them.

So, I was in Vegas last weekend again. We stopped by Bacchanal to follow-up to see what happened with our complaint. Apparently, it never got to the manager to review.  Steve the manager said he couldn't do anything about it now. After voicing my concerns and being super pissed off, he offered line passes. What good does a line pass do when the line was only 10 minutes long that day????  The idiot just kept saying "sorry there's no way we can track down the form and there's nothing I can do about it now." Geez, well, what good does it do when no one responds to the complaint forms? We love this buffet. This is my all time favorite buffet in vegas. All the food is so delicious and tons of premium options. The staff wasn't as friendly this time , maybe because we had a discount. I think the employee at the front may have cost them a star this trip , but overall lovely dining experience.

Came with wife on sunday night (1/14/18), while waiting to enter 1st of 2 lines for Bacchanal Buffet, we were watching the miracle in minnesota unfold at the bar that shares the entrance to buffet. Absolute pandemonium. 
We were given a ticket that read we would receive a text when ready to enter line for payment. After walking around casino for 5 minutes I received the text stating we can proceed to wait in line. First line took 20-25 minutes to reach registers. Now off to the 2nd line, here we waited for another 20-30 minutes before being allowed into buffet. 
Food was good and so was presentation. Waiter is constantly coming by to clear plates and refill drinks. Prime rib and t bone lamb was a bit too bloody but thats just me. Dessert was also beautifully presented and very tasty. 
I was planning on trying out a few more buffets during my trip, but ran out of time. I would def.recommend checking out Bacchanal Buffet.
One of the best buffet in Las Vegas NV, kinda pricey but well worth it! If you looking for a great experience in your mouth this is the buffet for you excellent customer service food is fresh!

Everytime Im in Vegas I stop by this buffet, but I noticed its always a hit or miss when it comes to the crab legs. There are times when the crab legs are humongous and tasty and once in a while its skinny messy. But when they are on point I would definitely rate this a 5 star. Oysters are always low quality and not shucked well most of the time that has shells in the oysters. Since buffet price is $60 wish they at least get some high quality oysters.

For a weekend dinner buffet for $57 without alcohol, the buffet at Caeser's is pricier than most buffets.  However, you get quantity and quality.  The lamb chops were fantastic.  I saw people inhaling the crab legs.  The vegetable side selection was huge.  I only had 3 issues that kept away the elusive 5 star review.

1)  The line for the carving station could be 10+ minutes.  They need to have 2 carvers splitting up the selections.
2)  You had to wait for your drink service.  I preferred the system at Bally's where you can get your own non-alcoholic drinks.
3)  The dessert bar needs to be improved.  No pie.  No ice cream.  Small selection of fresh fruit.

Great decor. That is all i can really say about this place. I would definitely prefer Wicked Spoon and Bellagio Buffet over Bacchanal. It was too expensive and the hostesses/staff move at sloth pace! To get crab you have to line up. To get to the carving station you have to line up. It makes no sense to line up to get into the buffet and line up again to get your food.

OMG, THIS PLACE IS WORTH THE $$$$ also a very long wait but, it was worth it too.  Unlimited Mimosas, they kept coming and coming and coming.  YAASSSSS, and the food is phenomenal. I tried to try everything but, it was impossible.  What I did eat was all great, let me tell you a must try the beef ribs were sooooooo tender and delicious myself and my honey loved them.  I will for sure be back every time I visit Vegas, and I'm not a big dessert person but, I had to try them.  Most buffets the desserts are a mess and gross, but not this buffet.  They were full of flavor, not to sweet you could tell they used high quality products.  So love this place!

This is my favorite buffet out of all the casino buffets in Vegas! You definitely get your money's worth when you come here! Expect to wait at least an hour before you can get in. They have now made is more easy with a number system. You sign in at a computer and it tells you what time you can come back for you table which makes it super convenient. You can make time pass by faster by walking around the casino floor or making your way to the forum shops and back! 

 Seafood is every night so you don't need to wait for the weekend to get those crab legs, oysters, mussels, or shrimp that you've been craving. They have an awesome asian section that serves a blk chicken medicinal soup which is very surprising to me since it is not something that an average person will drink. It has a lot of Chinese herbs in it including ginseng which has a very distinctive taste.

They have a station where they will make you pho, ramen, and udon. They offer a wide variety of different meats to choose from in the meat carving station. Lamb, sausages, prime rib, flank, and chicken to name a few. 

The hispanic station has fresh juices that you can pick up in glass containers. Horchata, Guava, Strawberry to name a few. Horchata was a big hit at my table. Just the right amount of cinnamon! 

If you are looking for gelato, mochi, or crepes this place has it all for you. Chocolate covered strawberries also available dipped in white chocolate, sugar free dietary selections, creme brûlée, and tirimisu on some nights.

All and All, definitely a place you want to check out at least once when you come to Vegas. Nothing will compare to this buffet afterwards!

The food was AMAZING and the variety was outstanding. I ate so many crab legs I almost died. The only downside was the wait. You check in at a kiosk and then wait (our wait was 1.5 hours) before you get into a line to wait another half an hour for a table. We did go for dinner on a Sunday night - there might be better times to go. Either way, it was worth the wait. The staff was so friendly and it was very clean even though they probably were serving a thousand or two diners.

As a local, I was excited to try "the best buffet in Vegas," it isn't. I've visited these buffets here, Studio B, Feast (GVR and Red Rock), Palms, and Bacchanal. If you're local or have access to a car, do yourself a favor and drive to The M for Studio B's, food is comparable to Bacchanal, and far cheaper. If you're a strip captive, Bacchanal is good, you'll be $50 poorer but satisfied. 

Got in line at 6:00p on Wed night and were seated at 6:30. We stayed longer than the 2 hours allowed (shame) and no one bothered us about it. Service is excellent, drinks refilled and plates removed in a timely manner. It's a buffet, I didn't expect too much. 

Honestly, unless you're going to eat your weight in crab legs, $50 (no longer includes beer and wine?!?! Come on Caesars!) is way too much to pay for sodium overload. Chinese: salty. 
Curry: salty and I still smell like coconut. 
Salad: prepareds were over dressed, not enough choices for build-your-own. 
Meats/cheese: good. 
Italian: didn't try anything but ratatouille but good. 
Mexican: greasy and sitting out too long, carnitas were there before we arrived and still sitting there as we left. 
American: sides were good, meats were just ok, fried stuff wasn't crispy. Disappointed. 
Seafood: good, I tried to eat $50 worth. 
Juice bar: good. 
Dessert: was expecting better, honestly, overall kinda tasteless and too sweet. I recommend the lava cakes. 
Sushi: I felt there should've been more choices for a $50 buffet. Disappointed. 
Things to try: seafood, chef's specials, small plates. 

It's nice to be able to walk the forum shops to help digest but I'll just head to The M for my buffet binges in the future.
Don't believe the Hype - tad better than other buffet and not worth the wait and $$$. Go somewhere else, food is NOT fresh and yuck, yuck, yuck

By far the best buffet I've been to in Vegas.  Pricey, but well worth it. Had gluten-free desserts as well, including ice cream filled mochi (my girls' favorite Japanese dessert)!

Sushi was high quality, and I like the fact that many of the dishes are pre-plated so you're not dishing out food from the community troughs!

Highly recommend!

Yummm!! I got indigestion after eating here but that's my own fault for wanting to eat everything in sight...
I'm not sure if it was the day and time we chose, my bf and I came here on a Friday at around 11 and our wait time was only like 30-45 min, which I totally didn't mind.
The food itself was delicious. The ramen was heavenly and their Asian station in general was oh-so-good. The raw oysters...*drolls*. The fresh horchata and tamarind water.. yum. Everything from the ceviche to the filet mignon were pretty damn good. The lobster chowder was creamy and perfect. The only thing I wasn't a huge fan of was the mini burgers. Other than that everything else was great!!
Oh! and the service was spot-on. Quick, attentive and friendly. For $35 a person and consuming what I'm sure would be twice that a regular restaurant, I would definitely come back!

Bacchanal, named after an unrestrained and gluttonous event associated with the wine/party god Bacchus, is a magical place touched by the divine. Upon entering the moodily lit halls and glass displays, one finds himself transformed into a wild pig, bent on eating himself to death. 

This is my second time at Bacchanal having visited a couple years prior. Although I remember this place being tastier than today, it's nonetheless still the best buffet to date. Maybe it's because last time my family paid for me, or it's because they didn't have that sweet glazed sea bass I've been fantasizing about. 

You'll find mountains of oysters and crab legs, cutting boards laiden with prime rib and brisket bursting with juices, and many other stations tempting your taste buds. However, I just found myself alternating between butter-drenched crab and that tender brisket. Also stop by the gelato station with a dozen different flavors to try. I found the orange beer gelato strange but enchanting. 

My only complaint about the place is the depressing, deformed, and diarrhea-inducing oysters I found every trip to the seafood station. Tasted awful and watery.
And where is my sweet glazed sea bass?!?!

Caesars Palace has free parking but try to avoid 10p when the massive crowd from the Colosseum is ejecting themselves from their concert.  
On busy days, there can be a two hour wait, but you can check in at the kiosk and come back later when they telephone you. 
Other days, the wait to pay can be 10 minutes, and the wait for non-communal seating is 20 minutes. 
Call Bacchanal/Caesar ahead of time to plan. 

Unless you're Mariah Carey and you have dancers to physically carry you around, bring a car. Or you'll be dragging your bulging stomach and piglet children all the way back home.

This is one of the best buffet I had in Vegas. (I've had a few buffet, and I am not a buffet kind of girl, I don't eat very much) There's a long wait but lucky us, we had someone that is a diamond or something to cut the lines.

There lots of verity of food and most of them are so good. They give great presentation and it is actually very GOOD! The one that you see everyone is grabbing is the crab legs because it's so delicious and fresh. 

I grab a lot of the dessert and I love the Cheesecake and Crème Brule the most. I wish I had a bigger tummy to eat more dessert! LOL

This buffet is awesome!

I thought the Wicked Spoon was good, but this one is WAY better!

No disrespect to Wicked Spoon, it's still good, but this place has a much WIDER selection of food.

Not much to say about this place. Probably best bang for the buck out in Vegas.

This place is a must try if you like buffet.  It has every thing from American, Italian, Mexican, Chinese, Japanese food.  Has burgers, fries, dimsum, taco, burrito, prime ribs, sushi, pasta, seafood, etc... I enjoyed the seafood the most.  The desserts selection were so extensive, I love it! I couldn't try every thing. Sooooo much to choose from.  Would definitely come back. 

-1 star for the longggggg wait. It was probably over an hour.

A very fitting name for a veritable orgy of food! This one in true Cæsar's Palace grandeur is like no other Las Vegas Hotel and Casino buffet. It is really more like if an array of top level restaurants were in one section. The major cuisines are well represented. There's a seafood section that features a wonderful ice bar with delectables like stone crab claws, oysters on the half shell and snow crab legs among other things. They also have hot seafood offerings as well. The carving station is more like a BBQ restaurant that features brisket and spare ribs along with the prime rib, turkey, chicken and pork roast. They even have slider hamburgers on little plates that are ready for the taking. The Mexican section has some authentic standbys like chicken chile verde. chile colorado, and pozole, but they also have street tacos done to order featuring carne asada, chicken, and al pastor. The Italian section has some lovely pastas and pizzas cooked in a woodfired oven, and an Asian section that had some lovely sushi, stir fried dishes, and hot sour soup that was actually both hot and sour. Plus they had a salad bar that I just looked at and an awesome dessert island that had gelato and crepes to order along with creme brulee and chocolate mousse.
One of the things that I really liked about Baccanal is that many of the items were served "tapas style" meaning in individually sized servings. It made it easier to try a multitude of things rather than just filling up on just a few things. The quality of the food is top notch. The brisket and ribs tasted as good as they would have in any Texas barbecue smoke shack, and I'm a native Texan so I know of what I speak. At any rate I ate entirely too much but it was worth it. So worth it that I will definitely do this again when I'm in Vegas again!

Unfortunately, I cannot get a refund (and, it would be huge)!!! The crab meat was soggy, like frozen carrots after they thaw. The shrimp had a strange texture and didn't taste like shrimp. The crepes were way too thick, but the only dessert I liked was a little concoction that came in a plastic bubble with the top cut off (I don't remember the name of the dessert). The Calif roll sushi had too much crab and not enough veggies. Our waiter was nice enough but took two plates I was wanting to keep. I have no idea how to let him know I wasn't done with them. Nothing was memorable. Would I do it again...NO!

Checked out the infamous Bacchanal Buffett on a busy Friday afternoon around 1 PM. We were seated after a 25 minute wait and our server promptly took our drink orders. Coffee, iced tea and OJ were all included, alcohol was not inclusive but were reasonably priced. (Assortment of bottomless drinks for $18). The variety of foods ranged from pizza, seafood, salad, assorted cheeses, pasta, sushi, and desserts. 

I sticked to the sushi (sashimi and rolls), salad and seafood. Don't forget about dessert! They even have sugar free options! The only thing I did not particularly care for was the hot and sour soup. It was cold and not traditional hot and sour soup. 

I will most certainly be back for dinner or breakfast next time I'm in Vegas!
Have to wait quite some time. The food is great，including lots of types. The steak is great，and love the crab legs，they already cut them so you don't have to peel it.
None better!!! You will be blown away at the selection and service. We would recommend this to everyone who wants to satisfy a wide appetite.

All I really remember about this buffet was standing in line. 

Standing in line for seating. We spent the extra $15 for the express line. Was it worth it? Yes...during peak times. It probably saved us an hour. 

Standing in line for the food. The way that the buffet is built requires everyone to stand in lines to get to any of the popular food stations. It was a nightmare, but probably also a strategy by the designers to get every one filled up on the cheap food. Because guess what is at the end of the line? The most expensive food...crab legs, clams, oysters and shrimp. By the time we actually got back to our seats with the food, most of it was cold. Eek. But the best way to get through the lines is to pair up and have one person hold a place in the line while the other person puts the plates full of food on the table. Repeat. 

The food: Prime rib and lamb chops were dry, clam chowder was super salty, sweet potato tater tots were delish, kobe sliders were ok, crab legs were ok, shrimp was huge and fresh and everything else wasn't too memorable. 

But...since I paid $65 for this buffet, I was going to get the most bang for my buck. The oysters! My friends and I originally grabbed a bunch of oysters in the shell, but then realized we would get the most out of the oysters shots, which are at the very end of the buffet line. We didn't even have to wait in line, we just kept grabbing the oysters shots from the counter. We poured the extra tomato juice out and just kept eating. Needless to say...a delicious overdose of raw oysters. =P

For dessert I really liked the macarons, the creme brulee, the watermelon mint sorbet (so refreshingly clean), and the fig gelato were delish. Also, they serve FRESH squeezed orange juice and watermelon juice here. Just ask the waiter. Loved. 

Overall, there are some high points, but I consider this place average when there are competing buffets in the vicinity with less lines, lower prices, and more unique dishes.

This is the best buffet.  I tried dinner at Wicked Spoon, and have been at Bellagio and Wynn previously.  I did the lunch buffet here. I think the difference was they brought out the cracked crab legs and salmon after 3 (had crab claws previously).  The little washcloth they give you is a nice plus (versus a wimpy wipey). It IS expensive and you need to do the whole sign in at the computer in the front, but I think it's worth it!!! :)

I hardly ever go to buffets because my primal instincts make me eat way too much food.  I normally eat smaller portions because I want to stay active and eat only what i really need.  That pretty much eliminates Casino Buffets.  Having said that, I have eaten at most of the casino buffets and my conclusion is that Bacchanal is the hands down winner as far as variety, presentation and quality are concerned. 

They have a food station for just about every food type you have ever craved. You would not be wrong in giving this place a chance.

more like 4.5 or 4.75 stars haha

the variety of food is hugeeeee but an extra bonus is that the quality is super gourmet. TBH if you just load your first plate with all the delicious meats (my favs were the ribs and the prime rib, omg droooool) and throw on whatever sides, you'll definitely get your moneys worth already. ususally i dont have enough room to fit in any desserts towards the end of my visit but during my most recent one i made it a mission to try what they got. To my surprise, i like the desserts just as much as all of the yummy savory foods they had. the mint green tea is a MUST-TRY! oh yea and beware, if you get the bottomless mimosa package (extra $7) they will continuously fill your glass and not let you ever go empty lol. Good if you wanna start your epic vegas day on a loosey goosey note but Bad if you get too full too fast or too faded to even eat anything haha.

I am still eating at buffet. I am very disappointed becoz hot meals were not hot at all. Either warm or cold. And Chinese rice was one of the worst here. They could spend more money to get decent rice.  Congee was good but again it was not hot enough. 

I and my husband are agreed that their cold dishes are really good except Japanese sushi. And desserts are okay. 

If you will spend this much money, I recommend Wynn's buffet. They are cheaper then here yet foods are excellent  and hot is hot and desserts are better.

If you like international foods, Wynn buffet is for you. If you like typical American style foods then here is for you.

Im not one to spend much time writing reviews on things like this, however I felt it was my civic duty on this one, to slightly warn those thinking of haunting this new and trendy Vegas buffet. Not that it was horrible, in fact, the food and atmosphere were FINE. 

FINE. Yep, that's the word I would use to describe this buffet. Just fine. It is in no way worth the wait or cost. Period. It is mostly buffet type and quality food. The selection is ok, the lines once inside the buffet are long but manageable; they do a fine job of replacing the food; the helpers are not always the most helpful. I  suppose its so busy because its the newest or getting the most buzz, but in reality I suppose, just like Vegas itself, the hype will die once something newer and shinier comes around. 

Please, do not be me. Do not give into your urges just because everyone else says its the best thing ever. Its fine, and if you want to impress your friends by dropping $200 for 3 of you to eat at the newest and shiniest buffet and wait in line for an hour or more for the privilege, then this is your best bet, otherwise, find something with far less people, save some money and go do something you will actually enjoy.
Man one of the best buffets I been to in Vegas .. Food is fresh and tastes so good .. The staff is super friendly and top of it .

I came here twice in three days (against my own volition). talk about fat and bloated.

The first time, I came for lunch on sunday 12/23 at 11:30am with my bf (price tag $48.99). We were afraid that the wait would be crazy, especially because it was the holiday weekend, but it wasn't bad. The line looked long, but from the time we started waiting until we got seated was about 50 minutes. Totally do-able.

We saw a sign that stated there was a 2 hour limit so we quickly got our grub on. steamed crab legs, tacos, corned beef hash, 5 types of meat, japanese ramen, charcuterie, fried chicken, sweet potato tater tots, desserts... it was A LOT of food. as we were progressing through our meal, one by one we saw the three couples who were in line in front of us leave. wayyy confusing because we weren't even halfway through the buffet yet! weak-sauces... anyway, we barely had a minute to spare before our 2 hours were up. service was GREAT. we had a super sweet waitress who was very attentive, and this other dude who cleared our plates consistently. the food was okay. not the best. wicked spoon is way better.

The second time I came was on Christmas at 11am with a party of 4. Again, the wait wasn't more than an hour and the price was $52. Exact same food. And same plate clearer man. I was finished with my meal within the hour this time because i was over it.

I always hit up buffets when I'm in vegas, but i don't think i'll be back at bacchanal for awhile. wicked spoon's food beats bacchanal's BY FAR.

I will readily admit that I'm not normally a "buffet" person.  I tend to feel it's a lot of sub-good food and I don't generally feel terribly awesome after eating at one. 

Went to Bacchanal for dinner with family who were down on vacation and really wanted to go, and everyone had a pretty darn good time.

Pros: 
- Almost everything was at least good, and a few items were downright great. Namely: The onion rings; crispy, hot, salty, and a little bit spicy, the fried chicken, which was damn near perfect, the peach brisket, the meat and cheese section, and several of the deserts.
