The hot and sour soup was event pipping hot and tasted weird! 

Seafood was okay as well.  The oysters were not succulent; they were dried up and just bleh! 

For the american side, it was okay too. The fried chicken was not even hot enough. It felt like it was sitting there for hours. 

Dessert section is pretty good a lot of variety so for peeps that have sweet tooth this maybe heaven.

I've been to Vegas more times than I care to remember. I've typically stayed away from the buffets because I don't think they represent very good value. I'm perfectly happy going to a nice place like Tao or similar. However, this trip, the wife and I decided to do something different. I did some Google work and this buffet consistently came up as the #1 buffet.

I was wrong. You'd be better off going and dropping the price of admission for two adults on 00 on roulette. Your odds of walking away happy would be better. Caesar's touts that it is the buffet of buffets. It would only beat a buffet that served warmed over cat turds as their feature dish. If you think I'm being harsh, I assure you that you are mistaken.

When we arrived at 7pm for dinner, the line was short. We walked right up and paid (lost money) in advance. It did take a while to actually be seated, which was a bit of a WTF moment. When we were seated, there was some unidentifiable meat under our table. Also, there were smears of some sort of sauce on the floor. When the price of admission is north of $100, I expect clean. Nay, I expect spotless. 

When we were seated, we were told to wait for our drink orders. Wait we did.  And waited...and waited some more. I eventually started staring a hole into one of the employees as he stood doing absolutely NOTHING. Finally he got the hint and came over to take our drink orders. He had barely spoken when our actual waiter came up.

In reading all the write ups for this buffet, they would lead you to believe that you've never seen such an epic selection as the one this buffet offers. It cost $17 million to build and features 25 stations...of the most boring food you've ever laid your eyes on. I walked up and down the stations twice before making any selections. Each station was a whole new disappointment. I saw NOTHING that made me think, "Oh, I want to try that!"  I searched and searched for a steak station or a grill area where they'd make whatever right in front of me. There wasn't one. I even asked someone that worked there where the steak was and they pointed me to the "American" station with the caveat that he didn't think they had steak.

At this point, I'm pretty disappointed in the dining experience. The Asian food looked like it came straight off of a cheap Chinese buffet. I tried some of the fish from this station and it was an overly salty mushy mess. I also resorted to having mac & cheese, which was decent, but how can you screw that up?  The one piece of bread I got was cold and hard.

The chilled shrimp was very mediocre...I ate two pieces and couldn't eat any more. I also resorted to having a couple of mini sliders. They were ok, but stuff like that has NO BUSINESS being on a $55/person buffet!  The best thing I had was the street tacos. Yay...street food. They did prepare it right in front of me...so there's that. The chicken was a bit dry, though. Then again, he's cooking chicken that's already been cooked and chopped who knows how long ago. And when you chop up chicken, how can you expect it to retain any juices at all?

I also had a spicy sausage. The first peice was decent enough (we're comparing foods from the same buffet here) but the second peice was a little odd texture wise. Like it had been sitting at the bottom of a bowl full of them in the prep area just soaking up 6lbs of grease.  The buffet also had sushi...and something just tells me that you should never get sushi at a buffet. But you know what? I tried it anyway. One piece later, I'd had enough. They had pizza on the buffet, too, but when I'm paying this price, the last thing I want is f#cking pizza!!  If you want pizza, do yourself a favor and go to 800 Degrees or even Pin Up Pizza in front of PH. 

If you're still reading this review, I commend you. If I had read this review, I'd have stopped halfway and decided the buffet wasn't for me. If you're still thinking it might be a good idea, do yourself a favor and just stop. You'd be better off going to McDonald's because the value you get there is better. That and it's not a disappointing dining experience because you'd know EXACTLY what you'd be getting. And it'd be under $10/person. 

In short, this was probably the WORST dining experience I've had in my entire life. I've had food poisoning, so that's saying something. I'm not a super picky eater. I'm generally easy to please. Both me and my wife thought this place was just massively underwhelming.

Vegas' biggest gamble and ripoff.

Food is great but service sucks 

We waited half hour before refills on drinks never saw our waitress.

She got drinks wrong also.  

Think her name was mercedes

I previously had purchased BOB before and the experience was great. So this time we purchased it again from Paris Le Village buffet and it was $74.99 per person due to holiday weekend (July 4th) which I think was reasonable. Upon purchasing it, I checked with the staff about the additional fee I needed to pay if I chose to go to Bacchanal buffet at Caesars Palace. The cashier lady at Paris buffet told us that it was $20. We found the price to be reasonable so we purchased three passes and decided to go to Bacchanal Buffet during these 24 hours. 
After many many experience with Vegas and misinformation from hotel staff, I went ahead to check with other hotel staff at concierge and its Caesars website about the additional fee to Bacchanal buffet. Some told us $20 additional fee, website said $30, so we prepared ourselves to be charged about $20-$35. 
It was a very hot sunny day at 104F outside, we walked from Planet Hollywood to Caesars with my mom, my hubby and my two years old baby. Since my mom was platinum member, we went to the fast VIP lane and ready to pay and stuff ourselves with food. We showed the cashier lady that we had BOB and we understand that there's extra fee. But we never expected the amount the lady said. It was $44.99 extra!!! Are you kidding me??? Even your website said $30 and there's no mention anywhere in your website that said there's going to be even higher price during holiday! (Which we have already paid $74.99 holiday price per BOB pass!)
We argued with the lady that everyone from total rewards told us it's either $20, $35, and website said $30. She called the manager on duty to come over and he told us that it's $44.99 and its either you pay or go elsewhere. He told us we can go to other buffet within the BOB. I was really pissed off as I even showed him the website from Caesars and he still didn't want to honor the price! Such a bad management and so many misinformation around. They should train their staff to provide correct information to customer because basically, they were lying to us when we first purchased the BOB from Paris, the $20 additional fee was one of the factors why we would buy the pass!! If they told us it was $44.99 per head, we probably wouldn't buy it.
Anyway, since there's no point standing in line occupying the line, so we stepped aside. I immediately called the customer service line that was provided by Caesars palace website especially indicating to call when we have any question about the holiday price. I told the CS that it was July 4th weekend and I have paid $74.99 for the pass, how much would I need to pay extra if I want to go to the Bacchanal buffet. The CS said it was $35 extra fee!! So I went back to talk to the lady cashier and I put the phone on speaker. I asked the CS the same question, she said $35! And the lady cashier immediately grabbed the phone and told the CS that it was $44.99. Haha
So after we put down the phone, the lady cashier immediately informed the manager and at the end, they honored the price of $35.
The point is not about the money. The point is about providing the correct information to the customer and train your staff!! And if the website didn't even say abt $44.99, why are you charging people extra! It's like they could just name their own price, whatever they want, which is wrong! 
Bacchanal buffet is not worth going anymore. They charge ridiculous amount during holiday to rip people off. The oysters had sands in it and customer service was just meh. They didn't even refill us our drinks the entire stay. The prime rib was just so so. I think the best in the buck buffet is planet Hollywood spice market. 
So the moral of the story- do not trust any of the staff said. Stand to your ground when things happen. Justice will serve!

We went there for breakfast last weekend and weren't impressed. We got seated right away but the food just didn't have any flavor. The only thing I enjoyed was the strawberry crepes but other than that nothing stood out. We had an amazing breakfast at a french restaurant the day prior for around $17pp so we were disappointed to pay $55pp for mediocre food.

Came here for brunch with my parents and son on a weekday and we were very pleased with the food options and the service. It wasn't too heavy sometimes I get food coma from over eating and it was just perfect. Even my picky son couldn't stop eating the rotisserie chicken it was very moist with a hint of smokiness and sweetness. Everyone agreed the clam chowder was unexpectedly delicious so many clams and celery! The prime rib and shrimp cocktail were my favorites but what really stood out were the desserts. They were beautifully made and I wish I saved more room to try them all. I had a tough time picking which buffet to try on our short trip to Vegas but I'm so glad we came here. The service was outstanding and we will definitely be back!

i feel like it's part of the vegas experience to go to a lavish buffet and be somewhat of a glutton - sin city, right?

we only had time to fit in one buffet during our trip and so the decision was made to eat at bacchanal. the wait to get into this joint was about 50 minutes for a party of 4, which from what i understand is expected during peak hours... and it was definitely worth it! maybe everything tasted better because we were starving by the time we got a table. i don't think our butts even touched our seats - we just made a mad dash for the nearest food station.

the food was great! we had a great time indulging in prime rib and brisket and all you can eat guacamole. remember to leave a little room for their desserts!

Food was made fresh. I ate a bunch of crab legs, oysters, and desserts! My favorite part was the dessert honestly. I love how they have different options and variety to chose from. I grab almost everything lol. But some of the food was on a salty side. On the seafood bar, they have this cute little tobacco sauce for you to take. It's like a sample side I never seen it before. I wish I get to try everything that they have there but my stomach was not big enough. Anyways, I loved it there!
The selection is much better here than Wicket spoon I take this one over WS any day. This the best one still.

If Caesar's palace is a real palace instead of a casino, then the Bacchanal buffet is the feast worthy of royalty. So far, I've only been here twice and I fell in love with it the second time since I was too tired to enjoy it during my first trip. At $75 a head for the Memorial Day weekend, this place ain't for the faint of heart or the cheapskates of the world. Ironically, I fall into the latter but my heart and stomach are always bigger than my financial considerations when it comes to splurging on good food. With that said, I couldn't help but cave in to my temptation to dine there like a queen for a day.

And let me tell you: It. Was. Worth. It.

The selection of food was utterly humongous. Although I've been here once before, my nomscope must've been broken since I had no idea how huge of a selection was offered at The Bacchanal. It was like walking into a giant hall of neverending good food. Maybe this is it, y'all. Maybe this is where I'll have my last meal on earth or my first in heaven. Let's face it: I'm a huge eater. But even for me, I couldn't help but to feel defeated by the sight of it all. Hell, I even had to strategize my portions so that I don't get full too quickly before I hit the crab station at the far end of the hall. I seriously only took a spoonful of everything I wanted to try, and good Lardy Lard....I still didn't manage to get a bite of everything else that didn't capture my eyes at the first glance. It was just so awesome. At the Bacchanal, quality is matched with quantity so it's somewhat unjustified to consider it as just another buffet. It's more like a walking into a feast for the monarchy where one wrong measurement of an ingredient leads to a head being chopped off somewhere. Ok. Maybe that's too dramatic, but the point is that I could tell the TLC that went into making each dish here is on the scale more comparable to that in the fancy schmancy restaurants than your run of the mill AYCE hub.


And just when I thought my mind was already blown from the amazing dishes, the teeny tiny piece of it that's left was further blown into smithereens by their dessert bar. How can anyone ever have a less than an uberly amazingly good time here when there's even gelato and MOCHI ICE CREAM to top the meal off?? Yes! Mochi ice cream!! I was full to the point of having my food baby come out from my mouth but I was still in love with the Sakura cherry blossom mochi ice cream. As a matter of fact, I loved it so much I had 2 of them after eating a bunch of other desserts. The Bacchanal is the real deal, y'all. If you're looking for THE buffet to go to when you're in the Vegas strip, this is it. Go there with your muumuu's or a loose pair of sweat pants and your stomach will love you for letting it expand to make for that one magical meal.

Absolutely LOVED this buffet! Came here for lunch with my husband earlier this year (Around April) when we visited Vegas... delicious food and great ambiance. :)

I went a few times to get food... The only thing I'd minus one star for is the service.. I think they could have been a little more attentive. But other than that, I loved the buffet...definitely will come back! Going to try Dinner there next time. :)

There's a lot of buffets in Vegas. Low end buffets, high end buffets, you name it. During my trip to Vegas, I decided on Bacchanal Buffet due to its reputation as one of the most famous and biggest buffets on the strip. I came here with my boyfriend earlier this year on a Monday morning for brunch and we waited around 30-35 minutes in line. The line moved quickly, although I did find it a bit frustrating that parties with 4+ people had their own special line that moved much quicker than the line for smaller parties. Pro tip - If you're a party of two and don't mind making friends with another couple, join forces so you can get access to the 4+ people line! You'll get into the buffet much, much quicker.

Once I got inside the buffet, I was pretty impressed with the diverse food options available. However, to be honest, I thought that there would be more options offered for a place that boasts about being the largest buffet in Vegas. Nonetheless, I was happy with the diverse variety and quality of food presented. There was seafood, classic breakfast food, Mexican food, Italian food, Japanese food, Chinese food, and a bunch of different desserts. At $40 or so a head, I tried to eat as much as I could. I ended up finishing most of my three plates of food and all of my salted caramel gelato (yum). Out of what I ate, I'd highly recommend trying their mac and cheese, eggs benedict, and shumai. All of these offerings were really tasty and well put together. Unfortunately, I did feel a bit meh overall about the Mexican food here. I loved how the tortillas were grilled to order, but I thought the meat was a little tough. I'd recommend getting the chicken tacos over the steak tacos if you're looking to save yourself some tummy room. I'd stay away from the gnocchi and gyoza here as well. I wasn't particularly impressed with the flavors or texture of either. I'm not a huge seafood fan but there was an extensive selection of offerings such as crab legs, clams, and shrimp. The prime rib here is also pretty tasty, though I didn't like how thick of a slice the guy cut for me. I only ate a few bites of it and felt kind of bad about wasting the rest of it. Overall, I'd give this place 4 stars due to the wide variety and overall quality of the food offered here. Besides, how can you go to Vegas and not eat at a fancy buffet?

This is one of the best buffets I have been to that has great variety of food, but the food had good quality. Here are my Pros and Cons:

Pros: Asian food, Steamed Crab, Truffle Mushroom Pizza, $15 unlimited alcohol add on, and array of desserts

Cons: Steamed Crab also was not cut open and no lobster as I was expecting

Just meh. Not amazing but not horrible. This buffet is definitely not worth the money. Everything was plain tasting. Especially the prime rib, it was okay i needed to add a lot of salt and pepper to it to make it have more flavor. The crab legs were wayyy too salty. Honestly my favorite thing was probably the mini Caesar salads. Save your money.

Variety, Variety, Variety  but the deserts weren't that great. 
If you like crab YOU MUST go to the HOT crab station. Oh My Goodness you will be eating crab for hours. One thing I didn't expect was the good music they were playing. One more thing, before you leave it is a must that you ask for their hand wipes, you won't be disappointed.
Enjoy

I couldn't agree more with the rest that this is "The Mother of All buffets"! 
I love their seafood selection especially the oyster, it is good quality oyster, ask the waiter for tobacco sauce ! 
For steam king crab legs, go to the italian station. The king crab, cold or steam, they are both good. 
Their Asian selection is great as well, I love pho and udon. 
My only complaint is their price. I came with a party of 6 on Sunday night and the total cost was almost $400, however it was a good experience.

We went for breakfast, and it was a great time. This was a Tuesday so there was no line and the atmosphere was pretty relaxed. Loved the food. Wish I had a bigger stomach. There was such a large variety of foods, from good old fashioned American to Asian. I actually really liked having rice soup (congee) for breakfast. Made my day. I liked being able to have prosciutto and fresh crepes.
One thing I didn't like was that our waitress kept looking at our receipt, which we had left of the table. It was weird and made me uncomfortable.

The food was waaayyyy above buffet grade food. The presentation was nice, but I really liked the music!!  Get registered early so you won't have to wait in the long line. It moves pretty quickly though. Don't eat all day before you go!!

Great selection, tasty food, and good service. The brisket, mussels, and crab legs were some of the best. Some disappointments were the paella (lacked seasoning) and pork belly. Also, overall table cleanliness could have been better.

My husband and I just recently visited this buffet, by recently...Saturday, December 12th for breakfast. Unfortunately I received SALMONELLA ... YES... SALMONELLA!!!!!!!!! Sadly, My husband and I were so excited to eat here as it has several wonderful reviews. I had the crab legs, shrimp with cocktail sauce, over easy egg with steak, crepe with sliced banana fosters, Nutella, and whip cream and lastly 2 mimosas. Immediately I was sick.. I just assumed I was coming down with something. I came home and I proceeded to get worse.. I visited my doctor and after some lab work, I was diagnosed.. So today which is Thursday, I contacted the restaurant to speak to a manager and they had the, "we don't give a fuck attitude" !!!!! I WILL NEVER STEP FOOT in this restaurant nor hotel.

It breaks my heart to only give 3 stars to Bacchanal given that I was very very excited to finally try it after the remodel and all. The automated line machine thing is definitely one of the bigger pluses here. It lets us know what time to get back on the ticket, and they even text us too. We were seated for the brunch menu, but really, by the time we arrived to our seats the dinner menu was starting to be served. The food had a good variety (especially in the asian section), but nothing worth raving about. They did have many juices and agua frescas which were served in these cute small milk glass bottle containers (I am assuming that's part of the brunch menu?). I particularly liked the lobster ravioli they were serving. The prime rib felt dry despite all the au jus I poured in it... and even though the food was good, I can't really justify the price tag on it. At a certain point, our server vanished. I believe her shift probably ended since later on someone else came to bring us the napkins we had ordered to our original server (we had to ask for it again). I think I would rather continue going to the Wicked Spoon buffet over the Bacchanal.

I have been to this place four times for both personal trips and business trips. It has remained the number one buffet on my list. The seafood is just phenomenal (cocktail shrimps, oyster, crab legs, etc.). The meat section is also tasty. They've had one of the best buffet trip tip roast I've ever had. Although I'm not a big dessert person, they do carry some decent stuff over on the sweet section. I'll definitely go back.

Man oh man I don't even know where to begin. 

My husband and I arrived at 7PM for dinner on a weekday, checked in to the touch screen computer, were told our table would not be ready until 9:45! Keep in mind, after they notify that your table is ready, you have to wait in ANOTHER line to actually pay and wait for an actual table to become available. 

Long story short, we finally made it inside with less than one hour before they start cleaning! The buffet does not allow any more guests in after 10PM but way before then, they were already removing all of the clean plates and some of the food! 

MOST IMPORTANTLY - AT EXACTLY 10PM ALL OF THE SERVERS STOP WORKING AND THEY LEAVE! So many people were still eating and our table was left with mountains of dirty plates with no one to take them away. 

Overall, yes, huge selection of food, but nothing stood out. It is a buffet after all, so I guess quantity will always precede over quality. To pay over $65 to eat for less than one hour, our used plates piling up, and being in long lines at EVERY food station, no thanks. 

Only bright side is that they seated us in a communal table with 4 other couples so we met some nice people. Other than that, this place can suck it.

3.5 Stars

Good selection of seafood and desserts, expensive.

Thought we'd try this place out for dinner with a group of 7, it was $65/person?  In order to be seated your entire party must be present.  
The decor is nice and trendy and the food selection is pretty good, but really, only 2 hours to stuff myself?!
I really liked the seafood and dessert sections, everything else was aright.  They even had ramen/pho but I'd rather go to a place that focuses just on those soups.  I was hooked on the horchata and aguas frescas though.

I prefer Caesars buffet still.
A very wide selection of food you can chunk into your stomach and your soul... if you don't have any space left! Worth the wait, and really great taste for a buffet!

Mediocre but totally overcooked meat. The only thing I liked were the pork ribs. It felt like a waste of money and time. We had to wait 2 hours, which was not a problem thanks to the automatic check-in. We wanted to do the "Buffet of Buffets," but found out just as we were about to pay that we actually had to purchase the pass for $59.99, instead of $54.99 for dinner plus $35 for the "Buffet of Buffets" upgrade, as advertised on their sign where the check-in kiosks were. The "Buffet of Buffets" pass actually does not include Bacchanal, so if you wanted to purchase the pass, you'd have to spend another $25 for brunch and $35 for dinner. This is totally dishonest pricing. We calculated it while we were in line and came to the conclusion that this "deal" doesn't make sense at all. We finally realized that it is only a deal if you plan on going to their sister buffets. We tried talking to a manager who didn't understand the issue and offered no real explanation why the sign in the front was misleading.

TL;DR: Two stars for the large variety of food, but it is not worth it if you like meat. "Buffet of Buffets" pass cannot be used here.

Edit, to respond to the reply. Yes, I agree that the pamphlet is clear about the pass being $59.99. The point is that their pricing signage board is very misleading and confusing. We were thinking we had to pay $54.99 + $35 to upgrade to the Buffet of Buffets pass, so to find out after waiting 2 hours that we actually had to purchase a pass for $59.99 and then spend more money on additional fees in order to even use it at Bacchanal is very disappointing and frustrating. These pamphlets are kept behind the cash register and not made readily available to customers. The point is not about the cost of the buffet, but that a business should make the pricing completely transparent so that it would not be a surprise to customers. And the manager on duty was completely useless after we voiced our complaint. Aside from this whole pricing debacle, the food just wasn't that good. Definitely quantity over quality here.
Best buffet in Vegas. Prime rib, lamb, lobster tail all veggie sides are amazing! Pistachio ice cream is to die for!
I love the buffet here. Wide selection of food and good service. Everyone needs to try the Italian cookie ice cream desert.

I waited in line for 2 long hours.  Was it worth it?  HELL YEAH!  The buffet is ridiculous.  It has the same concept and feel as the wicked spoon @ the cosmo but the food is way better.  I recommend trying this place soon before it goes to shit.  They are just trying to hype it up.  The amount of food they have is insane.  But I'd rather have less selections and more variety.  It will be hard to try everything in the buffet unless u are fatter than me.  The best thing I ate that night was the tomohawk rib eye chop!  What barffet carries a rib chop? This one fatties.  It was delicious.  I went to carnevino the next night and this steak was way better and 1/3 the price.  Fock i am hungry

I really do not like buffets. My parents live in Las Vegas and they love buffets and I read about this one in USA Today and decided to give it a try.
This is the best buffet I have ever had and would return. We went for lunch. I beleive it was about $30 per person. A good value for the quality.
The food is fresh, presented well and tasted good. I especially liked that there were healthy options such as carrot juice, raw oysters, delicious peeled shrimp and a fresh salad bar.  Also enjoyed the cooked salmon, which was still moist and well seasoned.
Choices were endless. From BBQ (which looked great with brisket, racks of ribs, pulled pork, etc), Chinese, Italian and Japanese, an extensive selection. They have something for everyone.
The desserts were excellent. I tried the mochi. Several flavors. It was incredibly fresh and creamy. Best I have ever had. Also had Jelly Bellies and fresh berries. Can't go wrong with these!

The buffet was enormous, and the food was pretty good, but we waited almost 30 minutes before we were seated. If it were a little less expensive, or if the food was extraordinary, it would've been a five star review, but I didn't try anything that would warrant a 60 dollar price tag. The unlimited mimosas, however, kept this from earning a lesser rating.

You have to take my review with a grain of salt as I did not have to wait a single minute to get in. 

The buffet is very pricey.  Three people, it was $200.00.  Yes, it's expensive but when you walk out, just don't slide in that $20.00 you were going to in the slot machine.  There, you've saved money so you can eat.

The food here is amazing.  Really, nothing tasted like buffet food.  Everything was fresh and excellently made.  I hate reading too much so here's the list of items to get.  

Chinese Line (on the far right)

Don't go there.  Are you stupid?  Why would you pay $60.00 for buffet Chinese food.  You are probably the type of person that eats at PF Changs (aka expensive Panda Express)  Move along to the left.

Mexican Line (next to the Chinese)

Read the above.  If you are paying $60.00 for buffet Mexican, take your ass back to Old Country Buffet.

Meats

Ok.  The Prime Rib was AMAZING.  I have to say it was better than Bellagio and that is really saying something.  Make sure to get at least two slices.  

Sushi - The best quality of sushi at any buffet.  Everyone talks about how good this is.  Every piece was very good, fresh and high quality.
Others

Wings - awesome and perfect amount of spiciness.  The chicken is high quality and there's plenty of meat.  Only get a couple pieces though because there's too much else to try.

Pho - yeah.  I said Pho.  This is definitely the best pho I have ever had made by a white guy in a chef's hat.  You are doing yourself a disservice if you don't try this.

Dessert - get the mochi icecream.  Don't forget it.  This item is crucial because mochi can be hard, stale or too melted.  This was just right and absolutely perfect.  They only give you two at a time so be ready for that.

Coffee - they give you your own little pot.  This is a small touch that I love because I hate having to track down someone for a warm up - especially in the chaos of a buffet.  

DO NOT MISS THIS PLACE IN YOUR TRIP.  IT IS VERY WORTH IT.  AND YES IT IS BETTER THAN BELLAGIO.

Instructions on how to get in to Bacchanal Buffet:
1.) line up at the kiosk machine and enter your name, your party size and specify if it's for a special occasion. & lastly, don't forget to put your phone number! Bacchanal will text you when your table is ready. Take your ticket and wait.

2.) don't be frightened by the wait time (65-70 minutes). This is just an estimate. I was told there will be an hour wait, so I walked to The Forum, bought a tie, and received a text shortly after. I only waited 15 minutes! 

3.) give your ticket to the employees by the podium and they will check you in. 

4.) walk a few steps forward and pay the cashier. I ended up paying $200 for 4 guests. I don't usually spend ~$50/person at a buffet, but it was our first time and everyone is raving about how good it is, so I took my family here. 

5.) the photographer takes your picture

6.) and last but not least, you are finally seated. 

The server asked what we wanted to drink. My brother got ginger ale (free with meal), my other brother got sprite (also free), and my mother ordered an unsweetened iced tea (also free). I ordered a mimosa. Our server informed us that a glass of mimosa is $7, while the endless/all you can drink mimosa is $10. Of course I went with the endless mimosa. For $3 more, I can drink till my heart's content. ^____^ must I add that I really love mimosa. So, best believe I drank $10, or.... rather $50 dollars worth of mimosa LOL.

-- Moving on to the food --
From my table, I can see that Bacchanal had a lot to offer. The buffet is broken down into different sections/cuisines. I didn't know where to begin, or how far the room stretched. I just knew that I had to walk every inch of the buffet before I took my pick. 

I found myself in the back of Bacchanal and saw a lady treading the room and thought to myself: "what's the hurry?" My eyes followed the lady and watched as she received a fat serving of hot, steamy king crab legs straight from the pot!! At that moment, I knew I was no longer Cindy. Oh no no no.. I was Ruby the Copycat. I took a plate and went straight for the King Crabs lol. 

I walked back to my table, dropped off my plate of hot and steamy crab legs and made my way to the seafood section. I got an assortment of seafood as well as raw oysters and shrimp cocktail! YUM!!! 

I went back for more servings of crab legs and shrimp cocktail. I couldn't look at seafood anymore after eating so much of it. So I went on an adventure and found myself in the Vietnamese cuisine section. In the far back, they served pho! Oh what the hellzzzzz. But I eat pho so frequently, that I decided against it. I walked further and found the Japanese section. I loaded up on the sushi, onigiri, miso soup, California rolls, and eel rolls. I grabbed another plate and loaded on the edamame. As I made my way back to my table, I couldn't help but double fist and dance my way back.

I ate and I ate.. And soon enough 3 hours had flew by. Where the time went? Idk, but I wasn't going to question or ponder why/where/how the time flew by so quickly. I was in my happy place. And I'm not going to stop stuffing my face just because of time. 

The food was delightful. Every bite reminded me that the gruesome three hour drive was worth it! As the plaque noted, Bacchanal Buffet is truly "a feast worthy of Gods."
The best buffet in Vegas. Nice layout, always a good selection, and the food is great.

We came the morning after our wedding for brunch. It was a Monday. I suggest going during the week as it is not crowded. The food was great. I liked how they serve small plates and tapas style. The deserts were better than your typical buffet. All in all, we will come back. Delicious

Quality selections describes Bacchanal. It should be, it cost our party $55 dollars per person!

Korean BBQ was the highlight of the buffet. Sweet, properly cooked and grilled short ribs. Yummy!

sushi was fresh and had some flavor

Pizzas were suprisingly good.

Tasty carved brisket meats. Juicy and hot off the oven.

Specialty beverages available on order. I had some green tea and was surprised to see them have that available.

worth $55? Maybe. the ice creams and pies makes it worth it.

 I'll be back when I have $55 to burn, you could get a decent dine in sit down meal for $55 on the strip too at other places.

This is hands down my new fav buffet place in Vegas. I never thought I'd find another buffet that impress me more than Bellagio's, but boy am I wrong.

Go early, or you'd have to wait in a crazy long line. They shuck oysters in front of you and these are the freshest oysters ever, and that my friend, says a lot. 

They have a wide selection of delicious food from all around the world. My fav were the oysters and Kobe sliders. Oh yum yum yum!!!

Absolutely worth every penny. One plate of food here is easily worth $60 by itself. Prime rib, shrimp, lamb, glazed hens, ribs, desserts, Chinese food, and Italian are all amazing. My friends were skeptical about spending that much for dinner, but we all left astonished and ridiculously full.

Wait time was expected.. Best time is right before 3pm because I guess at 3pm they start changing to dinner menu so we were able to enjoy both menus.. The sushi was great, oyster shots were yummy, amazing creme brûlée.. Lots of food really just wanted to take a nap after that next time we will have to go there not on the day that we a traveling back home

Buffet value to price at lunch is 5 stars. Wynn Buffett is closed until mid Nov otherwise I would have gone there instead. We had Bellagio buffet 2 days ago and it was generic, compared to Ceasars. $10 price difference but worth it. Crab claws, excellent, carving station had more choices than anywhere and the small plate concept for many of the more refined dishes kept the food fresh and more sophisticated. Seating area is better than most but not near as breathtaking as Wynn. Overall, value, taste, presentation and selection, this gets my vote for lunch buffet. Enjoy.

Is the food good? Yes.. is it great? Certainly not. I don't think a true New Yorker could eat at Bacchanal Buffet and be totally impressed since our buffets offer a great variety as well as flavorful and tasty options!
Granted, their presentation is classy, but I  do not think the price for dinner is worth it. 
Furthermore, for any families traveling with young children and infants... proceed with caution. This is not a family friendly restaurant nor do they have changing tables in their restrooms to change diapers. I asked where the closest bathroom was in which I could change my baby's diaper to which I was told by a Bacchanal employee that I'd have to go to the next tower for that.  With all the revenue and money coming in Caesar's, this should not be an issue..at all.

Go hungry! We went for the champagne brunch and loved it! Your eyes and stomach won't regret this place! The only disappointing thing I can say is that the dessert bar is not that fancy,only cookies mainly. I loved the steak and eggs,the the breads were very good.definitely a experience!

Rated #1 buffet in NV for six consecutive years and it definitely lives up to the hype. There's a station for just about every craving, but it's the attention to detail that has likely set them apart from the others for all these years. For example, it's easy to go unnoticed among the crowds of people throughout the day however when I complimented the master chef of the Italian station, Robert, he took the time to explain just how he makes his roasted tomatoes so perfect. For such a simple dish he has truly elevated every complimenting flavor profile within a tomato. Go check out Robert's roasted tomatoes, you will NOT regret it!

Been to multiple buffets both in Vegas and abroad.   This one here is all All hype from my friends.  Left unimpressed.  $59 and some change for and "alright" buffet?  Save your time and money, more importantly your time.  But hey, just like anything else in life, you got to try it in order to know if you'll like it.  

Best highlights were the coffee and Pepsi cola. 

Friendly staff though.  

Go elsewhere.

I'd say this is definitely one of the top buffets I have had in Vegas. It is definitely pricey, but for what is offered, it isn't so bad. Just be prepared to come hungry.

I am a Total Rewards member and had enough points to get 2 free buffets using my credit. I got so full from my 2nd plate, luckily my husband made up for it and ate for me lol. I just need to remember next time, to get a little bit of everything because there's so much to try! If you're a seafood lover, this buffet definitely has that. There are different stations, even one for street tacos and they make it in front of you! You can also get crab legs hot or cold, plus they even split them for you where it's cut and easy to eat.

There was a little wait in line, but not too bad, you just need to go when they first open. Just with the many selections they have, be prepared to be there for a while.

Bacchanal was a HUGE disappointment. I was so excited to finally try this buffet as it has superior reviews. However, I was very disappointed. I went here for dinner on a Saturday at around 5:30 PM. The wait was around 30-45 minutes, which wasn't too bad. I was extremely hungry, so I thought anything I ate would be delicious. Boy, was I wrong. There wasn't much of a variety or selection here. The prime rib was only OK. I ended up only eating crab, but I can always eat that at any other buffet. Plus, my last crab plate was extremely salty. It tasted like pure salt. The desserts were not all that great either.

Bacchanal is definitely overhyped and overpriced. I would not come here again.

As far as buffets are concerned, this is IT. They have EVERYTHING. I was actually a bit overwhelmed! I didn't even know where to begin. They have different ethnic cuisines, including tons of meats and seafood galore. Plus the desert table (or desert city is more like it). 

The only downside was the wait to get in (but understandably so). We were there on a Tuesday night at around 8:00 and it was about 90 minutes for two people. You can pay $45 a person to skip the wait (plus the cost of the buffet). That will run you about $100 a person, but at least it's an option if you really want to come and can't bear a long wait. And frankly for what they offer, it being unlimited vs what you would pay in a restaurant for the same food (um hello unlimited oysters and crab legs?) it's a bargain!

Came here with the boo on a Thursday night around 7pm and it took about 45 min for us to get seated. 

Being the newb, I started all the way at the end with the Asian food. I made my way towards the center and seafood eventually. 

Everything on my plate tasted flavorful and for the most part fresh? My favorites were the Kobe beef sliders, lamb chops, crab legs, and shrimp. I thought the prime rib was just ok, I expected more flavor.

I would have to say, this is my currently my favorite buffet in Vegas and would pay the $57.28 again.
Didn't realize the wife and I been here twice. When we're in vegas we always try something new. This must be good for us to try again.

Wicked Spoon vs Bacchanal? Read on...

Waited about 30 mins at 1:45pm on a Friday for 2 people. They switch over some items to the dinner menu at 2:45-3pm so you get both for the lunch price. In terms of variety, BB might be a tad better although at first glance the space is smaller than WS. Seafood (stone crab claws, stump cocktail, ceviche, oyster shooter, butter clams, shrimp scampi, miso cod...), lots of meat selections (prime rib, BBQ ribs, brisket, sausage, and least three more), American staples (Mac and cheese, BBQ beans, tater tots, fried chicken), taco bar, sushi, Chinese food (jook bar, dim sum, stir fry), soup bar (pho!), Italian, pizza, salad bar (a bit weak), and of course dessert bar. For dinner, they added raw oysters and crab legs. 

Although the selection is plentiful and I heard rave reviews about BB, I was disappointed in the taste of just about everything, even the desserts. The prime rib was weird and chewy, the au jus was tasteless. The brisket was good but the bbq ribs were so boring. The miso cod was cloyingly sweet. Butter clams were cooked well and cocktail shrimp never disappoints. The stone crab claws were not cracked but instead had a sliver sawed off in the middle. Unless I had a mallet, I wasn't getting into it. The Mac and cheese was SO disappointing - you could taste that the cheese was made from a powder as it was very grainy. Mexican section had horchata (overly sweet and watered down) and lots of fruit juices. Chinese and Japanese selections tasted ok, probably in par with WS. Dessert looked amazing but tasted just ok as well. A matcha green tea cake was green alright but had no matcha flavor. 

WS has a much better presentation as many items are pre-plated into individual portions. BB does this too but not for the majority of items. 

Decor and ambiance BB wins hands down. Feels like a nice upscale restaurant rather than a buffet. 

Overall - WS all the way. I'd take less selections for better taste any day.

When Vegas calls something Bacchanalian, you better hold onto your hats, and while you're at it, don't eat all day, you'll thank me later.  Superior service, incredible options and food that will truly inspire you.  Pace yourself and do not eat any bread...if you like seafood you will die for their king crab legs and drawn butter dispenser.  There is literally a food for everyone...seafood, latin cuisine, huge cuts of meat, pasta, asian cuisine...I am salivating just thinking about this wondrous buffet.  It is worth EVERY penny.  GO!

Be prepared to wait in a super long, tourist packed line.. Unless you want to jump in the express line and fork out an extra $15! We went around dinner time and waited a little over an hour in line. Not too bad when you're with good company but my stomach was growling like a beast by the time we got seated. The buffet was hidden so if you do not know where it is, be sure to ask someone. They don't even have marquees with directions anywhere! Bacchanal is also on the pricey side but you are definitely getting your money's worth. Most buffets in town don't have fresh oysters which is why I love this one! There were pretty lengthy lines once we got inside as well. I think I waited about 10 minutes to get to the carved meats. Not a big deal because I already knew the wait was going to be long.  The service is what bugged me the most. I understand that they're busy but that does not mean they get a free pass for service. Our server was not very attentive at all.  He never once came to ask us for refills on our drinks or to see how we were doing.  We had to constantly call him over to get drinks, which he did not even get right on 2 separate occasions.  Also, every time he brought us new drinks, he just left the old glasses there.  By the end of our meal, we had a table full of 14 cups, yes I counted. For such a small table, that does not leave very much room for our plates. It was super annoying.  We also witnessed him yelling at the busser for some unknown reason a few times.  It was very unprofessional and made us uncomfortable.  I think we were just unlucky with our server.  Other than the service, I think Bacchanal is pretty decent.  I probably wont be coming back though just because the wait is so long.
Great food!!  Been here for lunch and dinner. Service is much quicker then dinner. Food is outstanding.
Love this place. Great buffet. Warning, Very Expensive with pretty long lines at times.
Wow. This is the king buffet of all buffets! Awesome food, awesome service, and awesome ambiance! Any time I am in Vegas or anyone for that matter, this is a must stop!

This was like a dream come true for my stomach. Got a breakfast groupon with mimosas and a front of the line pass! My only complaint is there are 0 gluten friendly pastry/cookie/pancake/bread/pasta options. This is pretty behind the other buffets in Vegas who have been offering them for a while!

I don't like this place at all...waited for a long time, and paid for $60 for each person...but the food is no better than the $20/person buffet in Seattle...Don't understand why so many people want to go...will not come to this place again!

Great buffett restaurant. Remember to diet before you come here!

The buffett spread is amazing. 
The price/person is reasonable.

Be sure to arrive early, the line gets pretty long. Regardless of time.

The service is quite slow; so this is the only thing needs to be improved.

The restaurant is very clean and well-decorated.

I enjoyed my experience here.
I always liked this buffet but today it was way below par. Really dropped off in quality and choices. Big disappoint.

Bacchanal is the new king of buffet in vegas. The selection here is outstanding and authentic, and I can speak for the asian cuisines here. 

The Best Food: BBQ pork, roast duck, tonkatsu ramen, freshly made mexican tacos, XLB

Seafood: They have king crab on dinners and weekend brunch, and the price $45-50/pp does reflect that. The best way is to get in line at 1pm on a weekday and pay lunch price for the dinner at 3pm. The line is about an hour long so do time it correctly. 

Meats: Prime rib, brisket, bacon, chicken, sausage and lamb racks
 during dinner. I'm not a big meat fan so I thought most of the food was ok.

Other food worth mentioning: a big salad bar, sides, cook your own pasta bar and sushi

Stay away from: little wagyu sliders, they were super dry. Most of their chinese stir fry was overly salty. 

Icing on top: Love their freshly squeezed juices, especially the watermelon and orange. And the crepes were amazing as well, you can pick your own toppings, I could eat 4 in one setting if it wasn't so bad for me. Other desserts were ok, the souffle was kind of a let down and didn't have the right consistency at all.

Bacchanal is much better than Wicked Spoon and the Wynn, but you will pay for more. It's worth the trip if you don't mind lines too much, be prepared to be blown away!
Like the buffet here better than the Bellagio one. This is my third time brought my family to enjoy various food here. Especially recommend it's cute cute cute dessert.

If you have the money, spend it here.  Worth every penny.  In my opinion there is currently no better buffet in Las Vegas, and I've tried all the good ones (and some of the bad).

Looking at some of the other reviews, I guess it's possible that they have their off-days, but there was nothing off about it when I went last May.  Everything was perfect.

We go there ever time we visit Las Vegas to treat ourselves.   I noticed that food quality and selection went down.  Ice cream machine was down and made many people un-happy.  
They do not serve food on the little plate for the seafood section any longer. The fish was dry.  Yes most of the items are still very good.  But knowing and experienced very beginning of this place was much better.  Hope they bring back that again.
Upper end on price but food selection and quality were excellent as well as the service and overall presentation.

In all fairness, there's no way I could have tried all of the delicious food, there's simply too much.  I tried the following:

Dim Sum: Fantastic
Ramen: Below average
Fresh meat cuts: Great
Desserts: Great

I was really hankering for some sushi but the selection was abysmal

The service was pretty good and the restaurant was very clean and had plenty of whatever you needed.

I've done a few Las Vegas buffets before and on this trip to Vegas, my girlfriend and I decided we wanted to do one buffet as well, so we chose Bacchanal since neither of us had been there before. We chose to do brunch, as this was during the Christmas holidays and dinner was rather expensive ($65 I think). Brunch was not cheap either, at $53/person. 

We arrived around 11am and were seated quite promptly with no wait. This was during a weekday though, so your experience may vary. My favorite were the snow crab legs (I guess King Crab is only for dinner?), they were juicy and sweet, and cut apart so all you had to do was pry the meat out. The crab claws were done in a similar fashion, allowing for easy access to huge chunks of meat. 

The carving station was a sight to behold, with prime rib, beef ribs, turkey, lamb, and the best: smoked brisket. That brisket was fantastic. It was some of the best brisket I've had, and I've had BBQ in Kansas City and Austin before! Beyond that, the selections were varied and apart from a few misses, everything was good. Their sushi is absolutely mediocre though, and that was a disappointment. The dessert station is great, with lots of options and a crepe station as well, so make sure you leave room for dessert. They also have a juice bar available in the buffet section, with bottled fresh pressed juice (pineapple, watermelon, cucumber, orange, green). The green juice was fairly good (cucumber, kale, and ginger) and I figured it was a good way to "stay healthy" while consuming all the other rich foods (sarcasm). They offer a full complement of tea/coffee/pop as well, and have a fantastic peach ice tea available to order. 

This is one of the best buffets I've ever been to, and the service was great. Just don't forget to leave a tip for your server when you leave, I saw a lot of people leaving without placing a tip on the table.

Quite possibly the best buffet I've ever eaten at...and I'm not a fan of buffets in general. I went here on a family vacay (the one we take once every 5 years or so) and the kids coerced the parents to try out the new "it" buffet. My parents are damn fine cooks, so to take them out, it better be a good place, or we end up hearing lots of complaints about the food throughout the meal (and then some).  Their #1 saying: we can cook this at home, but BETTER!

Yes, we know you can cook well, and probably better too. But just this once, we want you to sit, eat and just enjoy w/o having to chop, dice, fry, steam or present a delectable dish. Although not amazed or in awe, my parents did managed to enjoy their meal and even threw in a few compliments here and there. VERY RARE!

We waited less than half an hour for Sunday brunch. $17 million dollars, 500+ dishes and 9 stations of finger-licking goodness. I wished I could stayed all day. Or have a bottomless tummy (like my bottomless mimosa!). I love their fresh squeeze juices, the steamed King crab legs, the juicy cut of prime rib, the soft mounds of cheese bread, the drool-worthy espresso coffee ice cream on a waffle cone, the lightly grilled asparagus, the smokiness of the smoked salmon, the moist carrot cake, the juicy roast duck...and their light fixtures that's made of glasses (as in what I'd find an Old Fashion in). Ah...someone take me back!

p.s. I'm the 100th review for Bacchanal Buffet...just thought you should know :p

Didn't even get to try this buffet because their "ticket system" is ridiculous. 

First, they give you a ticket that says come back in 2 hours. So upon return we find out that we have to wait another hour to pay for the food. 

We decide to wait and wait and wait. After the hour, we go up to the cashier and ask how long is the wait to get seated, "average wait time is 45 min." 

We look at the time and see by the time we actually get in the buffet will close in 45 min!!! At this point, we all leave and go to wicked spoon at the Cosmo where it was a 10 min wait and cheaper!

For Vegas standards, bachannol needs to get it together. Hungry patrons beware!!!

The best buffet I've been to (i've yet to try Bally's Sterling Brunch). I hate going to buffets and AYCE places. I always end up over eating to justify the cost. However, this buffet is something else. I wanted try this buffet since I had heard so many rave reviews about it. And it lived up to my expectations.

Just like any other buffets on the strip Bacchanal has Asian, American, French and Seafood. The must tries are American (burger sliders are delicious), Seafood (crab legs), French (pastries for dessert) and you have to try their lamb chops. I think managed to eat 10 of those at this buffet. The seasoning on the lab chops is perfect. 

The final stop is the dessert bar. They probably have over 75 different varieties of desserts and fruits. Just try anything from here. 

Overall, I'll definitely be back to break my current record of lamb chops. You should't skip this. Best time to get in is on Weekday nights. Use the automated kiosks to save waiting time.

So uh, what did I pay for again?  The nice pictures you see of the seafood station are an example of why you should never believe what you see.  What they serve and what they display are not one in the same.  Our server was actually great, and there is a wide variety of food, but...
Hostess was quite a bitch when seating us, I was gonna call her out for it but I had my child with me so I wasn't about to cause a scene.  On my way out we reported it to the manager whom just didn't seem interested.  There was a wide variety of food but most of it just didn't taste that fresh.  For example the seafood (snow crab was salty, mushy.  Oysters weren't really fresh, neither was the shrimp).  The beef was actually ok as was the dessert station but this place really left a lot to be desired.  I've had better quality food from a food truck.  The saving grace for this place is just the wide variety of food they have, but it's definitely not a place I'd go to again, just disappointed.  Save your money, go.. anywhere else.
Will never go back! Wait in line for an hour to get a ticket to return to wait in line yet again. $$$$$$ nasty, dried up, and cold food. Definitely not worth the wait or the money!
My absolute favorite buffet in Las Vegas. If you come during  the end of lunch and wait for dinner to start you not only get to eat more wonderful food you save about $15!

Came here on a Sunday morning around 10:30 and there was barely a line. You pay first and then wait in line to be seated by one of the hostess. It was about $55 for the lunch buffet.  As I was paying, there was a long line forming behind us! So we definitely came at a perfect time. Coming as early as you can is a definite must if you want to avoid waiting in line. The first thing I wanted to get and have heard about was the snow crab. The line for it was pretty long, so I had high hopes it was good. You get to pick if you want it cold or hot, so I went for the hot ones! The snow crab is great because they cut it in half for you = less work for you! Along with a side of butter, it's perfect. Other than that, I would recommend the fresh juices they have. I got the watermelon juice and it was very refreshing.

I think my favorite part about this buffet is their DESSERTS! I was in heaven walking around the dessert area. GET THE NUTELLA COFFEE GELATO. It's the best. You're welcome. My friend made her own crepe, which was delicious as well.

Other than that, I wasn't really interested or drawn to any of the other food that they had because I was so full. They had a variety from American, Asian, Mexican, even breakfast options. 

Long story short, I would definitely recommend coming here if you're looking for a place to eat in Vegas. But remember to get the Snow Crab and Nutella Coffee Gelato.

It's been a tradition for our family to dine at the Caesars buffet on every visit but this maybe the last time we go. Upon paying and checking in we were giving inaccurate pricing to add mimosas. Service was a 1 star at best....3 stars across the board because the food was good but if they're going to charge premium buffet prices there needs to be premium service. The service is the biggest gamble you'll run into in Vegas at this place...
My favorite buffet in Vegas!!! udon/ramen is delicious and so is the sushi. Surprisingly good quality! get some green tea to finish off the meal.

The service is terrible here. We were told that the holiday buffet starts at 11AM on Christmas Day. We went around 11:30 and were expecting a 1-1.5 hours wait. When we got there we were told that there's a 7 hour wait and we can take a token for our spot in the waitlist. We ended up getting a token for 2:30 pm. We showed up again promptly at 2:30. Lo and behold we were asked to join another line which would take an additional 2 hours! It just didn't make sense.. why can't they give a token which would calculate the entire wait time without having to stand in line again. The hostesses waiting outside were terribly rude with the exception of a young man who spared a min and answered our questions. Good food but absolutely bad management. What a waste of time!
Thousands of choice, great desserts, good atmosphere, comfortable chairs, average customer service. Overall, we were satisfied. So, equal to its price

THE bestest buffet I've ever been at!
The food is super fresh - seafood is being rotated every 15-30 minutes, I believe.  The choice is fantastic, and everything, literally everything, tastes absolutely yummy: make sure to try their crepes ( the best of the best) and chocolate covered strawberries with champagne salt. Champagne crackles in your mouth creating an explosion of taste - so groovy!!!
Oh, and Mimosas are bottomless :)

We showed our faces at the entrance around 10.30am, there was no line. Within an hour it grew into a massive gathering of hangover and hungry people. Dinner - forget it, the line gets even bigger, so it's really important to catch a moment when the restaurant is not too busy.

Best buffet that I've been to! We went for brunch so some of the dinner options weren't available due to having breakfast options. Everything we ate could have stood alone on a menu or as a side. Great food and great service.

After walking around Las Vegas for 5 hours, my family and I was starving. I heard from a friend that Caesar's Palace buffet is good, so I wanted to check it out for myself.

This place is so crowded! And I don't understand why anymore!

I waited 2 hours for my time to go in line then waited another hour to get seated.

$25 for each person even for children. NOT WORTH THE MONEY. I had 4 people with me, so the price was $125.

The employees were fine and that's one out of two reasons I gave this place at least a 2 star. The crab is horrible! There's barely any meat within the shell! The ramen and pho is decent, but didn't taste like I expected. There's only 2 sushi dishes that wasn't even appetizing! I only enjoyed the salmon skinned that's my last reason for giving this place a 2 star.

The porridge has no taste, the breads are too hard, and what made this place worse is that there's NO dessert.

The meat is alright, but unfortunately, not mouth watering. 

Now, oyster is my favorite dish I always get every buffet/restaurant I go to. The oyster (cooked and raw) disappointed me so badly that my appetite disappeared. It wasn't so terrible that I'd want to vomit, it was that the oyster didn't taste delicious. The texture was slippery and that's normal, but once I bit into the seafood, I pushed the dish away from me. Not my type of oyster for sure.

After the oyster I didn't try the rest of the varieties of food. There is a lot, though. It ranges from Asian, Italian, Mexican, and American.

I'm a picky eater who feels insulted when my culture's food isn't at my level of "good," so if you like Caesar, I'm not trying to insult your opinion. I'm stating what I experienced.

I tried it because I really like Wicked Spoon and a couple reviews said it was even better.  It wasn't. Crowded and noisy, with fast tempo music pounding (so you will eat faster?). The food was consistently too salty and not especially fresh.  Geh.  Skip it. Just another buffet.

I'm fairly impressed by this buffet the selection of food is by far one of the best and most diverse in Las Vegas, I had goat cheese smothered in quince, Singapore crab, truffle mushroom soup to name a few of the available foods. My only gripe is the service is awful, a server rarely came by our table to refill our drink and it took forever to get a high chair. For the price you pay the service should be up to par.

I was very disappointed with this buffet. Take this review with a grain of salt though, I came on Labor Day weekend and so the kitchen was likely understaffed and rushed.

We waited about two hours to get seated in the buffet and paid $55 since it was a holiday. The food was mediocre, nothing was spectacular. I sampled some of everything. 

The meats were a tad dry and a bit too fatty. The seafood was also dry and flavorless. The Asian food was subpar and uncreative. The desserts did not stand out either. Service was good, and the unlimited breakfast drinks was nice. 

I've eaten better buffets at my college dining halls. Wholly unimpressed with the Bacchanal considering how steep the price is.

(before I move on, explanation of the 4 stars instead of 5.... I went a few days after opening and it was $32 for weekday dinner.  My second time a month later and it was $42 for weekday dinner.  They admitted to having raised the price twice since the opening week)

The first time here, opening week, it was a 1.5 hr wait at 7PM.  Ridiculous.  Since that visit I've heard they have an option to pay $15 to bypass the line.  That first eveningI probably would have done it.

Onto the food:  AWESOME!!!  I'm a Wicked Spoon fan and (nearly) every Vegas trip visitor.  However, I'm scared to admit that Bacchanal might be better.  The most pressing point would be the carving station.  

Highlights of carving station:
- Ribs
- Ribeye (yes, RIB EYE!!!  And it's properly cooked a medium rare)
- hot links
- AND LAMB CHOPS!!!  LOVE THESE!!!  As much as you want

Other food highlights are the dim sum area, made-to-order ramen & pho, made-to-order suchi handrolls, DUCK, about 20 different salsas, oysters (big ones), and fresh made banana vanilla soufle.

Dessert highlight has got to be the watermelon mint sorbet.  Also, order the fresh squeezed OJ and watermelon juice.  They also have fresh squeezed cucumber juice, but I haven't tried it.

Got the Groupon for $80 for 2 people. We came at 930 and by the time we left there was a long line. Come early.  The food was all really good.  Shrimp and grits were my favorite.  Lots of choices. Mimosas were filled several times.

Excellent buffet!!! Only problem is after one plate of food and 1 plate of desserts I was so full couldn't eat anymore for $40 is a bit pricey unless you can really eat!!!! They offer a huge variety of Asian and seafood as well as pasta and Mexican food. Great selection. They even had very tasty tiny bite size cheeseburgers.  I highly recommend this buffet.

This was one of my favorite buffets I have ever been to. The crab was hot and fresh, the sushi was amazing, they had dishes from everywhere and a lovely dessert bar. My girlfriend said that even the pizza was really good.  I'd definitely make it a note to go back to this place and make sure I'm hungry too.

Worst experience and service ever in Vegas!!! We waited for four hours and got yelled and treated with really really bad attitude  by Soukina, who is the manager I think, when I requested to split table.  (I got confirmed that it is ok with other employee over there before I moved to a different line which would be 10 min shorter after 4hrs of wait)  We are not prisoner, we are guests OK？！！！Soukina made us so embarrassed and humiliated when she yelled at us out loud.  We were not trying to cut the line, OK?!!! Those who pay you gratuity to got in without waiting are who cut the line, OK?!!!  My family used to stay in Caesar every time we go to Vegas and will not anymore only because of their employee's attitude toward the guests.   Shame on Caesar Palace to have this kind of employee!!!!

LOVE the food there!  I especially loved the ramen.  Very good flavor.  Salami selection great too!  Meat carving station is huge!  If you like lamb chops, they have it!  Orange juice is fresh squeezed, and you can tell it was freshly squeezed within the hour!

Pricey, it was $32 (with Players card) on opening week.  Now (3 weeks later), it's $43 per person!

Food: Ok, I've just had it with buffets. I just feel like I pay a large price, and in the end, don't really eat my fill and everything just tastes meh, with only a few standouts. I seriously only liked one thing here - char su bao (bbq buns located in the dim sum area.) That was it! Sad.

Also, my husband only focuses on the crab legs anyway, so jeez, why don't you just go to a place and pay for crab legs! Well, now that is exactly what we do. 

So over buffets. Want to go to a buffet? No. My answer is no.

The Wonderful:
 Lamb chops were errmageerrrd fantastic! They were cooked to glorious medium-rare perfection and seasoned conservatively so that you really taste the flavor of the fresh meat and the crisped outer portion of fat. The lamb wasn't gamey in the least. 

Dim Sum: The shu mai and har gao were fresh, tender and moist. I can't say that I've had better dim sum anywhere it was that good! The pockets of steamed yumminess practically melted in my mouth they were that tender. 

The raw oysters were incredibly fresh! The meat had a slightly sweet flavor with pleasantly mild brininess. My only quasi-complaint would be that these are located directly next to the crab legs which meant I had to wait in line to get to them. The cold crab legs took some patience to get to since nearly everyone in line was asking for them to be heated up. (Kudos to the chefs and serving staff for complying with every request asked of them!)

The banana souffle was heavenly! It was served warm and had such simple unpretentious flavor. It wasn't overwhelming because the delicate foamy texture seemed to dissipate the sweetness so that it wasn't concentrated into one bite. 


The Good:
The sushi was fresh and nothing like any buffet sushi I've ever had. The hand rolls were a nice touch too! I would have liked to have a little more variety in the rolls since it seemed everything had spicy tuna on or in it. 

The ramen noodles weren't what I was expecting after reading some of the other reviews, but I think the other bolder flavored items might have skewed my judgment. I mean they weren't bad but not really a standout to me on this buffet of 500 items.

The sweet potato fries were tasty. They accompanied a piece of fried chicken that my hubby got, but he doesn't like sweet potatoes so I ended up with them. They were crispy and possibly doused in some sort of maple glaze that created a very nice savory sweet contrast.

The crab croquettes were surprisingly light. The crab concoction inside them was a delicate blend of fresh crab, bell pepper, onion and seasonings. It reminded me of the very delicate crab cake that I used to get from Commanders Palace. 

The prime rib was seasoned nicely and I really appreciate the fact that it wasn't overcooked. 


The Rest:
The blackberry pana cotta and the shrimp with grits fall under my "victims of a buffet" items. The shrimp with grits had decent flavor but I couldn't get past the hardened dry layer of grits on the top. The blackberry panna cotta had congealed to an undesirable firmness, maybe from the time it stood sitting on the dessert bar. 

The ceviche was too sour and acidic for my taste. It didn't help that I evidently picked up the only cup that lacked a slice of avocado on the top of it. 


Overall this buffet is well worth the money and I will definitely bring my next out of towners here. Finally, there's a buffet on the strip I can recommend to anyone!

Really delicious food with a focus on excellent presentation. So much food here that it can be overwhelming. Also, it's definitely on the pricier side, but it's a once in a lifetime experience. Will come back everytime I'm in Vegas
My family had a blast and enjoyed the food!  They were able to accommodate a big group!  Three tables to be exact!  Pricey, but great food!

As a Las Vegas local I had been eager to try this new and highly raved about buffet.  I met an out-of-town friend for lunch at the buffet yesterday.  We met at 12:15 and only waited about 15 minutes in line.  Once inside, we didn't have to wait longer than 3 people for anything, so we were very surprised how convenient the lunchtime buffet was.  Other reviews indicate that dinner is a different story - so I recommend going for lunch!  No, you won't get crab legs at lunch, but if that isn't important to you, then go for lunch!  I don't think anyone can eat everything here, so I will only speak to the things we ate.  The lunch buffet with tax was $32.  Honestly, most people will probably spend $20 to $30 on lunch anywhere on the Strip, so it's not an entirely bad deal.  The service was excellent and our drinks never went below half empty.  Here's my food comments.  Things I loved: the sushi was surprisingly good though the soy sauce had too much sodium.  The cooked meats were killer good - including the brisket and ribs, cut to order.  Excellent sweet cornbread.  The shrimp on ice and seafood paella was good.  The mac-n-cheese was not your standard mac-n-cheese and really awesome!  The tacos are made to order - you just tell them the meat and he grills it up and makes it for you.  NOW FOR THE DESSERT.  SAVE ROOM FOR DESSERT!  The bread pudding was excellent - espcially with a hot cup of coffee after lunch!  

It says there is a 2-hour maximum.  We stayed longer and nobody said anything.  But it also wasn't very busy and we were just chatting mostly - and not consuming ravenous amounts of food.  As we were leaving at 3:15pm, we noticed that the crab legs were being served.  Again, not my thing - but if they come out for "dinner" at 3:00pm, you might be wise to eat around 3-4pm to avoid long lines.  

I will definitely return for the lunch buffet.  Probably not for the dinner buffet - because I can't eat $50 worth of food.  It's a very good buffet experience that you should try at least once!

The biggest selection and variation you will ever see but pretty much everything I put on my plate was about 3 stars in taste. The pasta carbonara had zero flavor. The crab legs were dry and flaky. I will say the dessert bar is top notch.

I am writing this for their Sunday Brunch and not their dinner.....MAYYYYYBE I'll give dinner a try next time since other people pics on dinner seem like they have better choices. This is the 3rd time i've been here for lunch/brunch and this is by FAR the most DISSAPOINTING ONE!. Its like they charge you more for being SUNDAY BRUNCH, but they have less food than normal.

First of all the seafood was so so.....then the chinese section which is usually my favorite didn't have good dishes at all, they even got rid of the roast duck, bbq pork and chinese chicken. That's NOT EVEN AN EXPENSIVE ITEM!!!! Couldn't believe it. 

The carving station again was SAD, No lamb chops, NO PRIME RIB, or maybe that prime rib but grossley over cooked. The pork belly was dry. It was just worst than my previous two times and even those times it wasn't FANTASTIC but I would be decently satified, this time I was just FULLY dissapointed. If it wasn't that I'm Total Reward Platinum and didn't have to wait in line I would much rather go to the Bellagio Buffet, at least when I went a month ago their quality of food was ON POINT, less selection but much better quality! I hope they were just having a BAD day and I'll give it another chance because I do like the Bacchanal Buffet, but this past Sunday's exeperience left me LACKLUSTER. PLEASE STOP TAKING AWAY FOOD WHEN YOU MAKE PEOPLE PAY $55 for Sunday Brunch with NO SELECTION OF THE USUAL FOOD ITEMS!!!!

Food galore!! I've been here 4 times this year, I can't get enough of it.

I greatly advice the gourmet dinner, very amazing and succulent carving station; featuring lamb and an array of beef/pork cuts. As well as fresh seafood, and seafood incorporated meals.

Versatile selection of cultural goodies from Chinese to Mexican. Very well executed.

My favorite was the rotisserie style duck!!

If you ever want a good steak dinner, go here! Go to the carving station and ask for a whole ribeye tomahawk chop, they will give it to you! Then grab a salad, a starch, some ice tea and then hit the desert and you just had a 120.00 dinner elsewhere for 50 bucks.

If we could choose 0 star, I would choose for this one. We got there and was told that the wait would be 1-1.5 hours, but in fact we waited for more than 2.5 hours. The food was bad and low quality for that price $65 plus 18% service charge (which is inappropriate for buffet). I would not recommend this one - a complete disappointment!

The best buffet ever. I had dinner on a week night. Yes, the cost is $45, but it's worth it. Though I sampled most cuisines which were offered, I spent most of my time in the seafood line where I had my heart's desire of king crab, prawns, ceviche and lobster bisque. The crab and shrimp were steamed super hot just for me. Oh my and no words to explain the intensity of taste as I savored each morsel of seafood dipped in hot butter. Yummo! The experience is worth the wait and the cost.

It was very good. A lot of variety is what made it worth the price and wait for me. Everything was done very well also. I loved that they had fresh fruit. Went to 2 other buffets in Vegas and neither had fresh fruit, not even the breakfast buffet we went to. The waiting system didn't bother us, although ppl in front of us got upset when they realized they had put their name in a virtual line, and still had to wait in the physical line once they got the text. But it was only 20-25 mins in the physical line before we were seated and we were able to go do other things while in the "virtual" line.

Cuisine Type: Buffet

Main Foods: All you can eat.

Price: $$$

Date Visited: April 4th, 2015

Verdict: My second favorite buffet place in Paradise.
Is it worth the wait (if there's one)? Certainly yes. I prefer more gourmet food in Wicked Spoon but this comes as the second favorite place in Las Vegas. I would say there is a huge variety here, with seafood (the shrimps and the crab legs) are the best bets. They often change their menu up so each time you're going to see different stuff around here. The meat are a little overcooked, with the exception of the brisket. The oysters are not as good as they said they are going to be, while the desert is the best in terms of choices. They did not have green mochi this time (which was my favorite) though. The price is relatively high but this is Vegas, every where else is the same anyways. The oysters are not as good as they say though.

CLAMS. CHOCOLATE MOUSSE DESSERTS. GELATO. FRESH PASTA/LASAGNA. CHOCOLATE DIPPED STRAWBERRIES. Are you salivating yet?!

These are just a few delicious food options they have at this glorious buffet. The design is beautiful and so contemporary. The guys that work behind the counters are really friendly and funny. Almost everything here is decadent and amazing. Totally worth the price..you're in Vegas, baby!

Admittedly, if you are the type of person who can only eat one plate a food, this probably isn't the buffet for you. I think I ate like 6 plates that day...maybe even more. I couldn't get enough of the dessert bar. The gelato here is not that great though, Rio's is much better. They do have macaroons which I know people love but I'm just not a macaroon person. The things I couldn't stop eating where the chocolate desserts, clams, and fresh lasagna. MMM MMM MMM!

and it is included with the buffet of buffets pass but you have to pay a little extra to eat at this one.

Great buffet that is stocked with everything that you could ever want. 
Favorites include: crab legs (take them to the pasta area to be boiled if you want to eat them warm), lo mai gai in the Asian food area, and the fresh made crepes at the dessert station. My husband is a fan of the meat carving area and says he had some of the best lamb there. The dishes that are served in small bowls are the perfect amount to be able to try them all. The service is usually always on par as well. Considerably more than other buffets available in Vegas but worth the money in my opinion.
Awesome buffet. $59 with tax.  Colossal shrimp, stone crab and unlimited king crab legs.  Tons of great beef options, Asian, Italian.  Mini lasagna was awesome, meatballs were great.

I was excited to come here and try the buffet, but it turned out bad. First the environment is just not right. The temperature was so cold that makes all of the food cold too after you place the meal on the table. The cleaning cart wheels were so loud that made me Not wanna eat anymore.  Some times I also saw cleaning staff with the trash can going around the tables to clean upThe food doesn't taste right either, and it wasn't fresh at all. 

The only good thing about this place was our server Sandra, she did an excellent job and was so sweet. We personally give 5 stars for her service. The food and all other factors do not affect her service. 

Personally, Aria is a little cheaper than this place but it tastes so much better.

I guess it's either a hit or miss at the Bacchanal. I've come here twice. One experience wasn't stellar, but the last experience was pretty good, so I'll go with the latest experience.

The ambiance of the whole place feels good. The staff was constantly checking up on us to see if we needed any refills or wanted to order new drinks, which was really great because we went to eat in a party of nine. My favorite part of the whole buffet were the king crab legs. They were soooo amazing. The cold ones were served in the seafood section, and the hot ones were served in the Italian section.
