Tips:  If you think you pay more for the weekend dinner Fri-Sun for better food choices you are wrong they are the same. You are paying for the day.
Don't waste your money on the VIP experiene unless you plan on consuming alcohol or want a lobster.  Because all of the seafood on the seafood tower is on the buffet.
Next paying for line jumping.  The manager I spoke to told us it was 25 a person at that time due to the demand.  When we got off the phone and walked over 30 minutes later there was no line so we would have paid an extra 50 for no reason.  He also told me that the price goes up depending on the demand and wait time.
This was a horrible, over priced meal.  Only thing that saved a star was service.
I think they believe they have built a reputation that allows them to rip people off with promise of good food and they no longer need to try to live up to it.
Eating here is a gamble, but hey it is Vegas!
Let's see if Yelp keeps the review on this time or if Bacchanal Buffet pays to have mostly good reviews listed.  Check out the 1 star ones that aren't recommended by yelp

I just visited this buffet recently and I much appreciated all the yelpers that helped me so let me help you forward.  The prices are high and even more so for weekends, $45 dinner and $50 on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.  TR card holders save a whopping $1.  If you are a 24 hrs pass holder, you have to pay upgrade of $25, not $15 like before.  This applies for any day of the week.  Also, there are 2 VIP lines, one for 7 stars and one combo for Diamond and Platinum.  

Now for the food, it has not changed, meaning its good quality.  Seafood is top notch.  Crab, shrimp, etc.  If you get in by 3pm, you get dinner around 3:15pm for the lunch price.  My opinion, I suggest not to do the buffet of buffet, but rather pay for the meal and enjoy it just once.  It's really hard to eat 2 dinners, one breakfast and one lunch in 24 hrs.  But do start with dinner and end with dinner.  Also watch the time stamp from when you start and end.  Its 23 hrs and 59 mins.  And for the ending you must get pass the cashier to beat the clock.  If you are in line and don't make it by the ending time, it's too bad so sad even if you prepaid.  Hope this helps everyone.

Lastly, only Bachannal and Rio have surcharge prices for buffet pass users, otherwise you pay the listed price for whatever time you get in.

I decided to check this out since my friend raved about it so much the last time she was in Vegas and I found out why. Even though it's probably one of the most expensive, if not the most expensive buffet at a major Vegas hotel, it's definitely a worthy splurge, especially if you're hungry. There was also a line, but it went by pretty fast. You definitely ger your money's worth in terms of variety. All you can eat lobster and crab pretty makes it a great value if you're a shellfish fan. However, my favorite was the dessert bar, especially the crepes and gelato. Haven't had so much great food in a while. My usual buffet place in Vegas is at the Paris hotel. While that's also good, it doesn't compare to this one. Just make sure you are wearing stretchy fabric. You'll need it after coming here if you eat like I did.

For the price we paid for $75 per person. Food is salty and not fresh. Selection is great but none of the good taste good. For the $$$ you paid for. You might as well save your money and go somewhere. Not sure why people give good reviews

Dined here on Dec 27, you are asked to check in and come back after receiving a text two hours later (did not receive text till the next day). Than you have to wait in line again to wait in the 2 hour line to pay. 
Food was good the first time I went in May but this time around it was horrible,  food has been sitting out too long and they were already dumping the food into garbage bins while we were eating. Paid $75 per person including tax.

This is probably my favorite buffet in Vegas!

Price: ~$40 for lunch. The line wasn't too bad. Dinner would be ~$50-- but there's macarons + snow crab legs (I think).

A TON OF VARIETY! For lunch, the best stuff are the prime rib selection, oyster shooters, and sweet potato tater tots (trust me, they're amazing. I believe they're honey glazed too).

Oh, and fresh juice in these super cute jars!

Dim Sum!

Okay, that's all I have for now. Until then, hope you have fun catching this short review while getting ready for Vegas ya'lls!

not to much to say about buffets in sin city. this is probably one of the best i have had in a looooog time. dined on a friday night, buuuuussy!!! but, when ur with a group who make u laugh happy being with? noo problem. u can skip the long line n pay an extra 10-20 dollars to go to express line.

My Vegas trip consisted of buffet hopping and I can say with utmost confidence that Bacchanal Buffet was the best one we hit up! I would recommend searching Groupon or LivingSocial for a deal- it will be well worth your time!

There was SO much variety and the food was excellent. Everything I tried, I liked. Some highlights: look for the soup lady in the Asian and she'll make you a little bowl of pho! They also had steamed buns which were absolutely worth the try! Definitely hit up the meat section too! 

But the real reason I gave the buffet 5 stars is the dessert station. The desserts were small enough that you didn't feel bad about putting a multitude of them on your plate. Let me just tell you, they were worth every calorie! Scrumptious little bites of heaven- mini cupcakes, bread pudding, creme brûlée, crepes made to order. Need I say more? 

If you want to make the most out of your buffet trip, go towards the end of breakfast and stay for lunch! Don't worry, the crepe lady stays all day (I asked :P)!
Amazing decor, ambiance and huge selection of food. Meat was a bit tough though. Deserts was amazing. Would go back.
Yummy food! By far the best buffet in Vegas! Loved all the options!

Not as great as I thought it would be. There was a lot of hype to this place when it first opened up so I decided to give this place a try. To be honest I wasn't all that impressed especially for the price point . Not worth it. The food was mediocre at best. There are other buffets out there with better food and better prices.

This place is great. They have so much variety. I believe 200+?? I definitely overstuffed myself trying to eat as much as I can. We got the Open Table VIP deal that includes reservations, unlimited drinks, seafood tower and I'm guessing a better seated area. I had no idea that they have machines that you can enter your name in! If I had known that, that would have been a cheaper alternative since we were staying at the Linq Hotel. OH well, live and learn. :)

The food was good overall. I really liked their wagyu, prime rib and turkey LOL. It was all moist and juicy. The seafood is very fresh. I'm disappointed in the lack of sushi options but oh well.. compensate with other 199 dishes. I tried the ramen and forgot to try the pho. It wasn't bad. I also liked their tacos and dim sum and dessert bar.

This is the best buffet I've been to in Las Vegas.  I think it's impossible to eat $55 worth of food but it's fun to try.  The street tacos were one of my favorite items available.  Can't wait to go back.
Second time here.  Wait was non existent.  Food is great   only complaint is the price.  Groupon has a great deal.  Grab it.  You gotta try this place.  Don't leave Vegas without eatting here
Fancy place, lots of items to choose. Fresh stuffs and lovely dessert. The best buffet I have ever tried.

PRICY PRICY. but worth it. There is all kinds of food here. The desserts were the amazing part of the buffet. They had crepes, cookies, shaved ice, ice cream, muffins, chocolate, cakes and everything. The food was pretty good too. I said it was pricy because we came for the 3 day weekend so for the memorial holiday. I would come back again but not for a holiday, there is a 2 hour time limit.

While we aren't Las Vegas Buffett experts, we've experienced our fair share of buffets.  Elaborate ones in fancy international hotels, Mother's Day spreads, ordinary/average ones, etc.  Not once..ONCE, have we experienced food poisoning (even the "SEAFOOD" buffet at the Rio-and we were so skeptical that we would get food poisoning there because of the seafood scenario-nope..we were fine)  That all changed here

If you've read other reviews about Bacchanal Buffet, or read a newspaper/internet article-you know this place is brand new, a lot of $$$ was put into the project, everything is presented nice, the food options have massive variety, and the style and substance were expected to be on the same wave-length.  

The girl I went with was also supposed to post a review-ONE STAR.  So, in this sea of 4 and 5 star summaries, there should be another ONE STAR review in the mix when filtered by date.

Anyway, should we have avoided the Oysters? Probably.  Living in Seattle, Oysters can be consumed rather easily.  You always hear people say "beware of shellfish at the buffet", "don't eat oysters at buffets" "try everything but the oysters" "you might want to be careful about eating oysters".  However, this buffet had such a glowing reputation, the reviews we read before we went were all first class/5 star, we said "you know what? We're going to eat oysters...they look good, they don't smell off, and we're hungry..real hungry".  

BIG MISTAKE..both of us were throwing up about an hour after the meal.  We can discuss all the other stuff we ate, but that's not really relevant.  The point of the matter is that the oysters (and shrimp, but those were cooked)   were had by both of us.  Simple connecting of dots.

Now we can all say "that's your fault for eating oysters..you knew the risk..stick to cook foods at a buffet..use your noodle..that's an isolated experience..1 star is kind of harsh, dontcha think?" while those arguments can be made, it wasn't just the food poisoning scenario that factors into this rating, it was what happened after.

The next morning, she called Caesar's to complain, she talked to them for a little while, and it seemed as if the person on the other line was making notes of all that happened.  Why else would they tell her"we'll get back to you within 48 hours".  That makes too much sense...Oh..but what happened 48 hours later?  She called back, and was told there was no documentation of the original call..Can't make it up.  Not only that, but she was told that she needs to call their security department...they also thought we were making this story up, as if it was strictly about getting a refund..yeah, let's just make this elaborate scheme for $45..wake up

What did the security department do? Apparently they passed it on to Caesar's insurance department.  She was told that she needed to call them back to follow-up, not the other way around..Hospitality folks!  She did call back, and again the story about us getting sick was questioned..

Eventually she got a letter explaining that Caesar's wasn't at fault..no "we are sorry you had an unpleasant experience"..nothing..

I'm sure if you avoid the Oysters, you'll be fine..but gee whiz..atrocious customer service..we're not picky..we're not demanding..we just expect common courtesy/common sense/logic to be in the mix when something like this happens..and it didn't

#endrant

PS-Planet Hollywood's Buffet is pretty good, though..Paris' too!

There was a sign in front that boasted "Voted best Buffet in Vegas" I call B/S. At best I thought the food quality was okay. I don't see why people go nuts for this buffet but if I had to take a guess, I'd say its for the variety of options. Without a doubt the largest buffet I've ever been too. The buffet is separated into sections dedicated to different cuisines like Chinese, Italian, Thai, and they even a pho station. There's a seafood section & a meat carving station like other buffets. The dessert station was the largest & proly my favorite part. Nothing I ate was bad but nothing was really good either. I tried as much as I could but there wasn't one thing that I would tell someone else "oooh you gotta try this." I like having all these options but what I would have really liked would have been a good meal worth paying $50 a head for.

This is something I'd do once for the experience but I doubt I'd return. Not big on buffets and the food quality was blah. Plus the line was ridiculously long. The wait during peak lunch/dinner hours can be upwards of 3 hours. like whoa!

tip: look for the "chef's special" tags in the buffet counters

best buffets are cyclical.  as such, this one is the best so far. 

highlights:
-ramen, pho, udon bar (ramen's broth is amazing, pho sucks)
-bbq items (brisket and sausage is just okay, not as tender as i'd hoped, just for looks in the buffett)
-lamb chops (not as good as wynn's)
-fresh oysters (small ones too which is great)
-crepe station (could make sweet crepes with ice cream and fruits)

the newest joints will always draw the most crowds. after a few months to a year, they downgrade it drastically; offer less expensive items like fish, and all fresh berries.  good example is wicked spoon (downgraded but still very good).

This is my favorite buffet. It's a must for me when I go, I'm sure to make room for this and allow some walking time afterwards. You are in for the ultimate food coma, the meats and seafood are astoundingly crazy good. The asian side is pretty good, I like the dim sum and poke along with miso soup. Be sure to ask show your TR card, there's a shorter line and inside you get comp mimosas. (They take down your number for inventory I guess) So far they've all been great experiences. There was only one time the quality wasn't as good compared to other times.

The BEST buffet in town. It's pricey and take a while to be seated but totally worth it in my opinion. As you can imagine they have a variety amount of food. My favorite is the different kind of meats they have and the snow crab. 75 bucks because they included the 18 percent tip for our party but you won't be disappointed.
Obviously good for a buffet. Great selection of all types of food. Prepare for a long wait. They had hundreds and hundreds of options!

we were there at 2nd of Dec, After reception brought us to the table, we waited 8 minutes to have someone came to serve us.
The food are extremely Salty. no matter Prime Rib, or Baby back rib, lamb chop, or ribs. ALL of them are salty, it is extremely salty. And on Asian food section, I would say the food quality are bad.They ONLY has Long crab leg, but no King Crab.
good thing on here is they use larger Shrimps to be cocktail shrimp.

During the meal, the server seldom  came to us to take away the dirty dishes.

The conclusion is I will not come back, $50.99/person should not like that.
1 stars are  for $50.99 
another star for large cocktail shrimp.

This is absolutely the best buffet in Vegas right now. If you're a buffet person, i.e., can actually eat your money's worth, you can't miss this while you in Vegas. Yes, it's pricey. I came on Dec. 29 and paid around $51 and change for dinner. I think it had to do with holiday season too, but I also don't have the rewards card at Caesar's so there are ways to cut it down a couple dollars.

Foodwise, my favorite stations were Asian and Dessert. I'm surprised Asian was so good because usually at buffets the Asian station is the least cared for. They had good qaulity dim sum, and they even had this ginger chicken soup that tasted exactly like my mom makes it. It was pretty damn good. The sushi was OK, and when they DID refill the sashimi plate, it was really fresh. They even had legit porridge with all the scrumptious sides. 

The snow crabs and cocktail shrimp were average, you can't really saying special about them unless they were ridiculously fresh and plump, which they weren't. The meat station had the most choices I've ever seen in any buffet. Pork ribs, beef ribs, lamb legs, brisket, prime rib, chicken, sausage, and they even had this giant bone-in meat that I can't even say for sure what it was. The bone was literally the length of my arm, and my friend said got it said it's supposed to be beef, but no one could say for sure. I attached the picture comparing the size of it to my friend's head. Needless to say we couldn't finish it, but they did help me wrap it up for my dog. 

I would say I spent over half my time at the dessert bar. It was one of the best dessert stations I've seen in any buffet. The crepe station was to die for, and I tried every single ice cream/sorbet. One reason their ice cream station stands out to me is that their flavors are not ordinary and plain. There were baklava, strawberry basalmic, mint watermelon, sticky toffee, blood orange, etc. The flavors were not too drastically extreme where you couldn't understand it. The sorbets were refreshing and not too icey while the ice creams were creamy and rich. Everything at the dessert bar was made very well, and it was definitely the highlight for me. I didn't have room for this, but my friend said even their tacos were amazing. Overall, I didn't eat my money's worth, but the quality is definitely pretty high for a buffet. I'd say it's still worth it once in a while.

place is still very busy!! arrive early for dinner

unfortunately from my recent vist some of the food quality has declined MAINLY the MEAT section the lamb chops tasted like shit the ribs tasted like salt on a bone!!! WTF everything else was good as i remembered but whats going on at that section!?!?

they need to fire whoever is preparing/cooking that meat, im more angry that they are making meat that taste like crap and its being thrown out cause its not edible!!!!

and they need more people clearing tables still slow and nearly non existent!

still my go to buffet in LV doh.

AMAZING- it's unequivocally the BEST buffet in Las Vegas. The selection is vast and every bite is scrumptious. The chefs details are appreciated in every morsel of food. Pace yourself and try to spend at least an hour- the stations change frequently and each section is more delicious  than the last. I visit Vegas each year and Caesar's never disappoints. If you're on a budget- make the Bacchanal the one meal that you treat yourself too- it's worth the trip to Vegas!!!

Yes! More please! Thank you!

We were hesitant to hit yet another pricey possibly over-hyped buffet, but decided while in Vegas, let's hit what we've heard was the grand daddy of all buffets. SO glad we did!

We hit the buffet early lunch time during the week and had a minimal wait time. Some breakfast items were still out, which was a bummer since we paid for lunch - who wants scrambled eggs at these prices?!

The amount of choices are ridonkulous, and most food items were good to fabulous. I broke my usual "skip the sushi" rule and was quite pleasantly surprised. It wasn't top notch sushi, but definitely fresh and good. Dim sum options were mostly very good. Charcuterie included fancier cuts of meat and plentiful cheeses. Like Wicked Spoon, they had some items pre-prepped in cute little personalized serving dishes, but also lots of free flowing choices. 

The star of this show is definitely seafood, and you can crab-shrimp-clam-mussels-sush yourself to death, if you choose. Most was quite good. Often, cold shrimp on a buffet tastes like cheap, defrosted, mealy crap. These were big, plump, and delish. There was an spicy salmon sushi dish that kicked (ahem), a Greek shrimp and calamari salad that was ahhhhmazing, and I really wanted to marry and/or bathe in the lobster bisque. 

In addition to the plentiful seafood options, the bbq meat area was impressive. The beef ribs were juicy, meaty, albeit a bit too salty. The brisket was sensational - tender, not dry, well seasoned. There's also the aforementioned Asian section, a street taco section (carne asada and salsas were delish!), Italian food (meatballs were eh, but the seafood pasta was lovely), and salads. 

The dessert options didn't seem as plentiful as some of the other fancier buffets, but everything tasted was divine. The kids were in awe of the crepe station and the bins of candies. Special mention for the mango habanero and pistachio gelatos. 

Oh, and if you are one of *those* people, lots of fresh fruit. But who has time for peaches and apples at this sort of feast!? ;) 

And I must mention customer service. Wowzas. Our server kept our sodas refreshed, and as soon as one of us started on dessert, offered us coffee. Plates never piled up. And the servers along the buffet line were great. Got a question? They are ready to help. Looking for something they don't have? Apologies and may I offer you these items....? Lots of smiles. Lots of how can I help you. You don't expect such service at a buffet. 

Overall, I was impressed with the buffet and would definitely come back. Thanks, Caesars, for knocking it out of the park with a fun, delish, and tummy-packing experience!

By far the best buffet I've been to in all of Las Vegas, & I've been to more than a few.  Everything about Bachanal is 5 stars; the scrumptious food, the friendly & accommodating service, & the comfortable ambience.  My only regret is eating here on our first night in Vegas the last trip.  After that, no other Buffett could compare.

Many, many selections from all parts of the world await you, & the host takes you on a little tour so you can see what's available.  I thought this was a nice touch. 

A few of my favorites were the snow crab legs which were conveniently cut in half, eliminating the need to crack them; the many meats at the carving station, including a tender, succulent prime rib & a flavorful brisket; & of course the delectable desserts, all freshly made by a French pastry chef. 

Can't wait to return!
60 dollars for this?  Their briskets taste like rubber, and the crab? At some point I thought i was eating salt. Asian food looked like made by some cheap restaurant.

Buffet with rack of lamb?!?!!! Yessssss!!! I love the variety they have at the bacchanal. They have a raw section for your snow crab and then they were also making arepas too. In addition, there's the usual buffet food and also an Asian section.

Some of the items are served in its own small plate which is very cute and can help control the portion size. They have a small tiny basket with waffle fries and chicken, looks too cute to eat. 

There's also a section dedicated for desserts. There's a lot to choose from so save your stomach. They even have different flavored ice cream. There was a special small shot of Thai iced tea when I went. It was a small shot of Thai iced tea served over a tiny scoop of coconut ice cream.

The response from the assistant general manager was unacceptable!  She said she was "sorry" for the poor experience and that she would give me 20% off BREAKFAST or LUNCH in the future.  I did not go there for breakfast or lunch.  How could that possibly make up for a horrible dinner?  They can take their 20% and pay it to the servers who never refill your drinks!  I choose to go elsewhere! Oh ... and when you call and ask about the lobster tails...apparently they are only on the weekends and they raise the price even higher for that....they have MULTIPLE prices for times of day and days of the week so it seems you never know what you are going to get because the lady on the phone said "sometimes" we have lobster tails....hmm.  I was just laughing to myself as I was looking to see that most of the GREAT reviews for Bacchanal were from the year 2012.  There you have it.

Great buffet with a lot of options.  The Asian and dessert sections were probably my favourites.  The American section left a bit to be desired, but the Mac n' Cheese was actually really good...

We had a group of 6, but only had to wait about 15 minutes for a table.  Not bad.
Culinary dream come true! High quality, artistically crafted, delicious, beautiful food in an upscale setting.

Like the Patriots and Red Sox, this place is ov-er-ra-ted. My mother and I took my dad here for his birthday last week and the only reason why I'm giving two stars is because the line wasn't that long. Yes, there was a decent sized dessert bar, but other than that, there's not much to rave about. Cioppino? Big deal. The M has it too. Paella? I like the one at the Aria better. Prime rib, steak, and turkey? I could get those at Red Rock. Sorry, Caesar's, but you can do a lot better for the amount you charge...

We arrived at the buffet at 6 pm and we are told there was a 2 hour wait. They instruct us to get a ticket which will guarantee our place in line. The ticket says to come back at 8:05. We come back only to see that we have to wait in another line for another hour and a half. Unbelievable! I've eaten here before and the food is good, but not worth waiting 3-4 hours. So many people had to be turned away. The old fashioned system of waiting in line is still better than this tocket system. Not sure if I will come here again on a weekend.

Lies on waiting times.  If the lady tells you 30 minutes, it's about 1 he to be seated after they text you.  Be prepared to wait more time and it's ok food.  Wynn has much better buffet and they have their act together.
QUALITY is the word here, pretty much better quality on everything compared to the other high end buffets in Vegas. Worth it if you have never been and are ok with the price.

This is one of the most decadent buffets I have ever seen! GO!

While vacationing in Vegas Halloween week I decided to try the buffet at Caesars Palace. On the first day I went for breakfast which quickly eased my hangover from the previous nights activities. The staff was extremely professional and accommodating. The hostess took the time  to point out all of the stations. The room is massive yet comfortable. The food presentation is beautiful. Many items are presented on small plates or in individual fryer baskets. The "breakfast" options seem endless with three types of bacon. My favorite being the hand carved slab bacon. The breakfast buffet offered not only traditional breakfast items but also featured a Mexican station, sushi, cheeses, and full Asian dishes.

A couple of days later I decided to see what they could possible add for lunch. At one point I became overwhelmed, thanked God for his abundance and shed a tear. The massive dessert station was spectacular! Banana Foster, gelato, hand made crepes and on and on. The carver station was a meatasauras' dream! Artesian sausages, prime rib, slab bacon (again), chicken, ham, turkey, etc. there was pizza, pastas, sushi, paella, mussels, oysters, and again, on and on. All served with stunning presentation. More importantly, all delicious!!

This buffet is a bit more than most of the other strip but is well worth the cost. What differentiates this from other buffets is the food quality and service.

I was too frightened to try the dinner buffet knowing that I would hurt myself by filling up on crab legs. I can't wait to go back!!

This place is expensive especially for a Monday night 6/1/15. $52/person. The food wasn't even all that great. At least I know now and will not come here again. I will stick to bellagio's buffet. More choices and better desserts. Price is cheaper too.

I have heard so much about bacchanal buffet at Caesars so went there to check it out during my recent stay in Vegas, I have to say I was highly disappointed.   The food was very average and the service was far below average.  It was on a weekday and the place was not busy at all but our waiter hardly came by to take our plates, out table was a full of plates. We literally had ask another waiter to pick up our finished plates.   Also added the mimosa option for my meal and got one drink the whole night because like I said our waiter was hardly visible.  I am giving one star for the beautiful decor and that is it. 

P.S. you will be disappointed with the crab legs.   They were sliced up in half and steamed which completely destroyed the taste.   i am not sure why they do this,  it's a crime.
I mean, they crack open the crab legs for you. What more could you ask for? Those and the desserts are incredibly delicious.

Amazing buffet..will come back for more! Now to be fair I didn't go to other buffets so I can't attest that it is the best in all of the US but it has a pretty amazing spread. I am a big seafood person and the Alaskan king crabs stone crab mussels and every kind of shellfish makes my heart sing with pure joy!! I wish that the one here in Atlantic city would even have half this spread!!! So unfair!

Compared to the buffet at Mandarin Oriental, Wynn, M, Bellagio and Rio, I found the selection and quality of the seafood and dessert at Bacchanal to be mediocre and overpriced ($50.99/pp).

A few of my disappointments:

1) They did not have souffle that night and ran out of green tea mochi by 7pm???
2) They did not have stone crab...(Stone crab season: from October to May).
3) Some of the crab legs were still frozen (it was like biting into crab leg popsicle).
4) The oyster shooters smelled bad and I simply found them to be unappetizing
5) The line for the seafood station was at least 20 minutes.
6) Some of the meat in the meat station were either over salted or bland.

What was decent there?  As sad as this may sound...just their taco station and asian food station.

If you want to do an AYCE experience in Vegas, I highly recommend the Sunday brunch at Mozen (at Mandarin Oriental).  

And, the restaurant appeared short staffed because it was difficult to find our server to refill our drinks or have our plates taken away.  Also, they should provide wet naps when they see guests with crab legs (their most popular item and it wasn't even that good).

Would not recommend!

Self parking and complimentary valet services available (if valet is full, a sign would be posted) at Caesars Palace.

AH. I love Bacchanal so much, I seriously dream about it every day. I honestly can't wait until the day I go back to eat it again. I'm really skeptical about buffets and have tried quite a few in my lifetime, but I must say, Bacchanal is THE best and it seriously surpassed my expectations.

Gone here twice -- one time for lunch and the other time for dinner and both were amazing experiences. I know the wait can get super long (like an hour), but the two times I went, I only waited about 5-15 minutes max (came around 1 p.m. for lunch and 8 p.m. for dinner).

So what I love about Bacchanal is the effort they put into the plating (especially the dessert) and that the food is made and tastes FRESH. Most buffets just leave the food sitting for a few hours, but the food at Bacchanal is prepared and made right in front of you. The selections are endless! From seafood to meat to Mexican to Asian, they have it all so you'll definitely find a few thing that you'll love here (tacos, AHHH). Not only do they put in effort when it comes to making and preparing the food, but they also put in effort when it comes to the decor.

If you're gonna splurge in Vegas, definitely go to Bacchanal -- you will NOT be disappointed, I promise!

I just returned from spending Thanksgiving in Las Vegas.  We arrived at the Bacchanal Buffet on Wednesday, November 21st at approximately 6pm.
  
The line was about 1.5-2hrs long but it seemed to go by quickly probably because we knew this was THE buffet to go to and were prepared to wait for a while. 

There were about 9 of us in the party including 1 three year old who is a picky eater and can barely finish a hot dog by himself.. but still cost him $21.49.

The cashier also mentioned that due to the size of our party, there would be an automatic 18% gratuity to our bill.  The bill came out to $381.41 before tax and tip so you can do the math.  Okay it was $68.65 for the tip. 

After we paid, we were ushered to another line (more like an unorganized mob of hungry customers who just waited 2 hours in line and forked out tons of $$ and were ready to wreak havoc on the buffet) to get our table.  One thing we all noticed at this point while looking from the outside was the MASSIVE line for seafood.  People standing around holding their empty plates with blank looks on their faces..reminiscent of a russian food line.  My eyes followed as the line snaked around the seafood bar all the way past the prime rib/steak/lamb chop station...where another line started for those meats.  There was grumbling within the crowd of people who were waiting to get seated.  I overheard people in disbelief as more and more of them noticed the lines to get food.

As I looked at the seafood station itself...what did I see in the display case?  Well..there was lots of ice.  No crab legs, no mussels, no oysters, just crushed white ice.. the pellet kind.  All this while the line was backed up as far as I could see and the people in front of the line looked like they were ready to kill someone.

I mean I could understand if this is any other buffet.. but this is supposed to be the flagship buffet of las vegas and for $45 per person I would expect NO lines or at least nothing of this magnitude. 

This was just a foretelling of what was to come of our experience at Bacchanal Buffet.  

We finally got seated and in the beginning our host was very accommodating.  He provided us a high chair and our drink orders immediately.  So at this point I felt a little better about spending $68.65 for the gratuity.

Our party broke off to explore the buffet and grab our selections.  We were STARVING at this point.  It turned out, the 3 year old in our party only wanted to eat crab legs.  So his mom went with him to the seafood line to wait.. and wait they did.  I went and picked up some steak, fried chicken, mac&cheese, etc.  Because there were shorter waits for those, but planned on hitting the seafood station later.  Returned to the table, and finished my first round.  Went back and got a second round with the fish and chips, prime rib, and some other stuff.  Finished that one.  Looked around and said, "hey where's so and so?"

"they're still waiting in line for the crab legs.."

"WHAT???"

After what seemed like forever, they came back with crab legs, not much but some.  She stated that they just came out with fresh crab legs and if you want them to go now.  So I decided to brave the line and was prepared to wait again.  As I waited, I noticed there was utter chaos behind the seafood bar.  The cooks were just running around with no system in place whatsoever.  They would steam a bunch of legs, throw them on a plate, then approach people in line (not the first in line, just anybody in line..could be the middle of the line near the drawn butter and salmon) and just call out "who wants crab legs?" and basically the first person to say I do or get their attention would win the plate..  And no, people were not waiting for anything else besides crab legs so it wasn't like, "oh i'll pass I'm waiting for the 'good stuff'"..this WAS the 'good stuff' so why they decided to do it that way I have no idea.. Oh, and before this happened I'd also like to mention they were telling people in the line to go and sit down.  Because it would be a long while until they would be ready.  Or now that I think of it, the cooks there don't understand the concept of a line or don't even follow the rule first come first served. 

Top this off with our server (whom we tipped $68.65) who I thought was doing a great job given the circumstances..  decided hey it's getting late and I'm not going to work anymore, but I'm also not going to tell my table or communicate this to anybody.  Later on when we needed his services for refills, coffee, etc. I would notice him counting money at another table.  Hey, I don't work in the restaurant industry but isn't doing something like this in view of the patrons in really bad taste?  I called another server who happened to be walking by and after I asked for a watermelon juice, he kind of rolled his eyes and asked our table anything ELSE?  Irritated with the thought he would have to come back for another request.  And I'm out of characters....

I still believe this is the BEST buffet in LasVegas. A little expensive and sometimes a little busy, but the selection of food is amazing. I don't eat seafood but I know there is a wide selection. Favorites are the Pho location and you can't go past the lamb chops. All in all I always walk out 5kgs heavier . If there is any deals for locals I'd give it 5 stars and probably eat there every week

Overall a very nice buffet.  I think the price range is pretty good for the kind of food that you get. The line just to get into the buffet is always long but if you are looking for a good buffet in vegas, it is well worth it. Dinner is the most expensive but has the best food, take advantage of the seafood, although their might be a line by the seafood station it is definetely worth it if you paid for the dinner.  King Crab legs, halbut, raw oysters are just a few of the variety of seafood they have.  Make sure to check out all the stations because me and my friends almost missed the room in the back that had the italian and asian sections.  Also the dessert section is nice (although I'm not really a dessert kind of person), a lot of things you don't find at typical buffets.  Overall for the price point, the variety and quality of food is good.

Worth the price!!! Definitely a must when you come to Vegas. So many different dishes to try and the desserts are amazing! 

The all you can drink menu doesn't include much, but you really gotta get the AYCD mimosas. Even at dinner time! They put more champagne than OJ.... honestly I drank more than I ate. Don't be like me, EAT!
Definitely the BEST Buffet in Vegas!!! Tip: Try and get here at the Lunch (it's the same as Dinner only costs less)! Brunch/Lunch is from 12-3:00pm. It was ALL wonderful & Delicious!
Lots of food choices. Variety I haven't seen at other buffets. Try the ginseng chicken soup, spicy sausage, and smoked chicken.

By far the most amazing buffet I have ever been to! It is clearly the best in Las Vegas and in my opinion it is the best period. The place is very nicely decorated and the environment is that of a very nice restaurant. The service is great and they are on point. The food was amazing and I dont think there was a single thing I didnt like. The meat section is the largest selection ive ever seen and it is delicious. The lamb was perfect and the brisket and ribs are better then most bbq restaurants. The kobe beef sliders are also better than most burger restaurants. The seafood sections is amazing and there is endless real king crabs not kust snow crabs like a lot of the other buffets. There is also italian and asian and mexican and most things are cooked to order. The mac and cheese is the best ever. I will definatly make this place a regular place to visit. It is expensive at 50 dollars but worth every dollar.
Overrated and overpriced.  Not that special.  I can't see why people think it's great.  Selection was not good.

So this has been our "go to" buffet for the last several years.  It seems the buffet only gets more expensive, but the offerings have yet to catch up, to justify the increase in price.  We went on 4th of July weekend, which was (understandably) about $10 more expensive than usual, and grabbed the "fast pass" a couple of hours before we intended to dine.

With it being specially holiday priced, I really expected more.

They did not have king crabs at the cold station, those were only offered in the hot crab area, along with the regular mix of snow crab legs. The sushi was sad looking.  I mean, I suppose Bacchanal has never had impressive sushi offerings to speak of, but for me, a real sushi lover, I didn't even bother getting anything because it looked so unappetizing.  

I did enjoy their rack of lamb, which I am definitely NOT  a fan of lamb. I usually find it to be way too gamey, but this tasted like really tender beef.  It was delish, at least my first piece...next piece was gamey...so I guess the story there is you have to be adventurous as it is a bit of a russian roulette.  

No matter how stuffed I am, I always make room for dessert.  I don't think I will ever tire of their freshly made crepes, or the creme brulee.

They also did not have the little beverage bottles people can usually get when going through the buffet.  

For the fact that I paid more, on top of a price that already has gone up through time, I really think they should have had all of their usual offerings, if not more (and of course spruce up that sad looking sushi bar already!).  

All in all, I think if you can nab a groupon or get some kind of discount for it, then it is worth it, but if not, you might want to consider what foods are most important to you and decide if this is the buffet you want to splurge at.  After all, there are plenty of other buffets that offer many of the things that I value most in my Vegas Buffet experience.
Yup, hands down the best buffet in Vegas. A little pricier then most but still awesome buffet.

This buffet is amazing. I'm pretty big on Vegas buffets and because it's vegas, I really do only expect the best of the best. This buffet really does that, and I'm saying that based off of every buffet I've eaten in Vegas (Wicked Spoon, Wynn, Bellagio, etc) It has everything you could imagine from seafood to gourmet meat to asian food to pasta. Honestly, I feel like it's a little mixed inbetween of the Wynn buffet and Wicked Spoon. Their fusion stuff are actually not that bad and their seafood was worth the wait in line. 
The only problem I had with the buffet was that the meats I tried (prime rib and steak) were both kind of on the dry side. Also, I get that I was there on a 3-day weekend, but I still ate on a Sunday and had to pay $50.. not to mention that our waiter especially took a really really long time to clear our plates and fill our water. She actually didn't do any of it unless we flagged her down and asked her to and our table was only so big so it got kind of annoying trying to eat with piled up plates all around me.

We went for Sunday brunch and honestly the wait wasn't that bad - we got in line at the end of the waiting stanchions and it took about 45 minutes to get up to be seated.  The atmosphere was upscale and trendy.  The food was really good - best prime rib EVER!  The people working at each station were busy, friendly and fun.  The choices were mind boggling and we really did need to pace ourselves.  We never felt rushed.  The endless mimosas kept flowing and the food was appropriately hot /cold.  The different sections were interesting and well stocked.  I have been to many buffets over the years but this one really was the best.  Price wise I had no complaints at all.  We had a very basic burger that we split between the two of us and a calamari appetizer and one cocktail each by the pool at the Venetian for lunch the previous day and the bill was 80 bucks so having this much quality food for this price was AWESOME.  I think it was 90 for the two of us...can't remember the exact price.

Best in Las Vegas for a reason.

Bacchanal seems to never disappoint me. Each and every experience that I have there has been great, and I honestly don't mind any price increase that they have placed on this buffet.

As always, the area surrounding the buffet is spotless. Lines, as expected, are fairly long depending what time and day you go. My favorite time to go is brunch as the items that are being served at that time of the day is filling for the rest of the day.

I love the fact that the items that they serve here are already portioned out for you, so food is not wasted. Just like the Wicked Spoon buffet, the flavor profiles have been attended to, and it does come out when you take a single bite out of anything.

I especially love their dessert section, and I for one think its the best dessert I have ever eaten for a buffet. You have to take into consideration the amount of time it takes to mass produce these menu items, and to maintain that level of quality each and every time you go into a buffet is tremendous.

I enjoyed the promptness of the service that we had when we went. For a buffet in Las Vegas, on the strip, and for a hotel as famous as the city itself, this buffet can hold it down.

I would definitely recommend this buffet to family members, and anyone that is in town, and will definitely be back for more.

The food was fairly good but the service was terrible.  Our waitress barely came by to bring us any drinks.  I only saw her twice the whole time we were there.  I would say that the selections of food for brunch have went down hill.  There used to be fresh berries out by the crepe station but this time none.  Hardly any desserts out for brunch.  We paid a lot for brunch this morning and don't really feel it was over $100 worth.  The mimosas weren't great at all either.   I was unable to taste the orange juice in there.  The coffee wasn't good.  Just not a great dining experience compared to last time.  Disappointing!

Our experience at Bacchanal Buffet was OK.  It was frustrating waiting in line to be seated after paying the $65 per person entry fee - I estimate the time after we paid before we were seated was about 15 minutes.  

We ordered the all-you-care-to-drink alcohol option for an additional $15 each: My fiancée had mimosas and I had red wine.  Our server was extremely attentive in keeping our glasses topped up, even when we were away from the table perusing the buffet.  I made it through about 3 or 4 glasses, resulting in a very reasonable price per drink.  

The food was mostly mediocre.  The crab legs were just like any other regular old buffet.  The raw oysters, while good, had shell pieces in nearly every one.  We were excited by pictures that other Yelpers posted of uni nigiri in the sushi section, but when we arrived the only decent nigiri available were salmon and tuna.  I was additionally surprised how many dishes at the buffet were lukewarm when they should have been hot.  They have enough customers that this should be impossible, since people are constantly taking things away as soon as they are put out!  

The dessert, unlike the other food, was quite delightful.  There were fresh crepes made to order and a good selection of really tasty fruits and pastries.  

We won't return since there are so many other wonderful meals to be had in Vegas at much more reasonable prices.

This is my favorite buffet. Ever. And I've been to most. Bacchanal tops Sterling, Wynn and Wicked Spoon. 

The Sterling Buffet at Bally's has long been my favorite, never dreaming it could be topped... If for no other reason than the fact that it had broiled lobster and Veuve Cliquot champagne that never stopped. 

Well...Bacchanal killed it. Amazing king crab, sushi, BBQ and other awesome dishes were creative and delicious. I went to  Bacchanal twice on this trip. EVERYONE was blown away. I can't wait until my next visit.

I have been coming to Las Vegas for 25 years and have always enjoyed the buffet at Caesar's in its' different forms. The current one is no exception.  This gigantic buffet offers hundreds of choices: fresh salads, peeled boiled shrimp (my favorite), ham, turkey, prime rib, a very nice selection of Asian foods and delicious desserts. This one has it all.  We arrived just before the lunch hour began, so we paid the breakfast price, but ate lunch.  Each customer gets two hours to eat so plan your meal accordingly.  The line moves fast and the table service is excellent. Highly recommended!!

Not much of a buffet fan (stuffing your face until you get more food than you paid for...) but there certainly is a reason why Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas. A cut above the rest. Not so traditional cafeteria style, much more personal- guest service and clean interaction with the chefs. I am happy someone actually takes pride in a buffet here in town. Worth every penny spent and more. Dessert station is 5 stars on its own- more choices than you can imagine/ all with individual tasting sizes so you can try it all... err most of it anyway.

By far got too be the last Vegas yelper check out the Bacchanal Buffet. Save the best review for last. LOL! Right off not much of buffet person in general but the last two trips at buffet. Like to think hit current top two Wicked Spoon and Bacchanal. Not so entirely different besides the obvious both PRICEY although Wicked Spoon save little bit. Thankfully got here super early so no dealing with horror stories of long waits or find that fast pass get in and out. I guess some card program or whatever jump ahead in line. Still always hook. This one sure you go in separate line still have wait so really that much faster?? Best advice go early if want to avoid lines. Thankfully my friends visiting had good day gambling so never had pay the ridiculous price for dinner. 

The food I had nothing but praise for the diversity of food! Somethings that found never seen before at a buffet. The ramen station. On this night never got any cause the person working the station was non existence or even was at the station had back turned seem disinterested checking for customers. Needless too say never tried any. They had station of freshly squeezed juices in little kraft glasses all on ice and nice setup. Horchata as one of the choices found interesting. I went with the guava tasted really refreshing and good. The cold seafood section with the snow crab legs not often you see. I think snow crab legs are over rated besides lot of work get meat out. I rather stick with the crab legs. The craving station was mile high of meats from prime rib, sausage, brisket, and sure missing couple more. The sushi station though great was rolls not just your standard fare ones but spicy tuna and not just bland ones. The nigiri looked pretty good (tasted pretty solid for buffet) and again more then just your standard ones. The charcuterie station with meats and cheeses and breads. Something hardly see in buffets. Thumbs up! Ethic stations or trend in buffets got your italian station, asian station, and so on. Some hit or misses but its buffet with that many options it is what it is. The dessert station again like the diversity. They even make fresh crepes. I was way full get any. Overall the food here is really good and although paying for it like to think getting the quality in the price.

The things dislike. I think the tables are WAY too close to one another. I felt like eating in cafeteria at times. Three of us. The next round table literally tight fit turn the table around so  one of my friends could slide her chair in and out. Our server not the quickest came getting our drinks and keeping them filled. The location it tucked in the back. So if not sure Bacchanal can be hard to find.

Salmon poke... Omg!!!! Soooooo good... My friend and I had to promise ourselves that we wouldn't come back to get more salmon poke because we didn't pay money to JUST eat that delicious goodness. Everything else was really good but man... That salmon poke... *drooling*

We waited a little more than an hour to get in but it was totally worth it =)
That was THE best buffet experience ever!! Clean, great happy service and awesome fresh food

The best buffet I've had in my life, eaten here twice in my lifetime. I don't recall much 20 years back for the first time, but remember eating here 5 years ago. I plan to go back next year in hopes that their menu will have some new items.
Lamb was cooked medium rare, but you can ask them to heat it up more. Their dessert area was top notch! So many to choose from with a nice display...felt like a giant party for kids to attend to, lol
I can't give them five stars because I felt that they should have added more items, such as seafood that's rare to find in other restos. 
Too bad it was evening, because we waited for an hour to finally be seated. It's worth a try for anyone out there who wants the most bang for their buck. No wonder it's ranked the #1 buffet in the nation (at least around that time period)

Wow! I think that this is definitely one of the largest buffets that I have been to in my life.  They have literally everything you could possibly want from all sorts of ethnic groups of food such as european, mexican, asian, etc.  They have a large selection of seafood in the variety of ethnic groups and they have a large meat section with prime rib! They change up their desserts though, so you might have to go more than once.  Having a large group is always the way to go!  
*If you have a party of 6 or more, they will take you through to the group line, but note that you can only have a maximum of 3 credit cards charged for your entire group no matter how big it is

This was said to be the best buffet in Las Vegas on most sites I researched and it definitely held up to my expectations! The food was great but the one thing that stood out to me the most was the service! I don't usually write reviews but couldn't go without recognizing our waiters Francisco and Alvaro. They were outstanding from the time we sat down until the minute we left. The last thing I would have expected at a very busy buffet on the strip! Thanks to those guys for making our experience even better!

Totally stuffed myself silly...
Do come during off season, otherwise you might get 8 hour wait...

Lines were crazy, and we lucked out with just 2 hour wait after we got our reservation time.

First meal of the day, so I cleaned my plate on my first round and ate too fast that I had hard time after the meal so don't forget to pace yourself.

Everything on the Asian food area was on point. 
Minus the pho bar... need improvement on the noodle consistency and offering sauces to make it spicy.

Seafood was delicious with hot crab legs, shrimp cocktails, and stone crabs.
I didn't bother too much with the meats, but from my friend's reaction, it was a bit dry, which is usually the case at buffets.

Dessert bar was awesome, so make sure you leave room!  One more tip, make sure you use your total rewards card to get a discount per person on the buffet cost.

So many options to choose from! 

The only reason I would return here is for the seafood alone. Their crabs (hot and cold) were fresh and delicious. Their oysters and shrimp we're humongous and of course super fresh. 

The rest of the food options were just okay. I've had better at the Wynn, Bellagio and Cosmo. I love my dessert and I was so disappointed here. I read so many positive reviews that I filled up my plate on the first dessert round. That was a mistake. The dessert just tasted off. 

Seafood: 4-5
Other buffet items: 3
Dessert: 2 :(

The assortment and quality of the buffet food deserves 5 stars.

BEST
-Went straight to the steamed king crab legs definitely better than all other crab legs on ice at Bacchanal and at other hotel buffets. They'll scoop you an entire plates worth from big pots of salted water. I didn't use any butter, they were sweet on their own.
-The fresh juice in cute jars with caps. My favorites of the night were Pina and Horchata. For someone who normally only drinks water or coffee, i left 3 empty Pina jars and 2 empty Horchata jars on the table. Mixed the horchata with coffee!
-The carving station itself was absolutely impressive. Ribs, sausage links, lamb, prime rib and so much more. Prime rib was super rare though.
-Noodle soup station with ramen, wonton noodles, and pho
- Dessert! Made to order crepes, add your own toppings. Full gelato bar.

Knocked off 1 for their disorganized and confusing entrance set up. Hoping the madness was just the NYE holiday weekend throwing them off...

This is what you do:
1. Go a couple hours before you want to actually eat and request your table through the kiosk
2. Kiosk will ask for your phone number and print your a receipt to give you an estimated return time (it could be up to 300-400 minutes later and no that is not a mistake)
3. Drink, gamble, have a snack to kill endless amount of time
4. Bacchanal will text the phone number you provided via the kiosk when ready
5. Jump for joy and return to Caesar's to get in another line next to the kiosk where one employee is and hand them your ticket (when someone is not sneaking up front to ask them a question)
6. If all checks out, they will let you pass to the payment line
7. Pay $$ then get back in line for a table
8. Finally, someone will bring you into the buffet
9. Pile on the crab legs and prime rib

Total price: ~150 for 2 people after tax (holiday pricing)

If you have the patience, Bacchanal is worth it!

Well, this buffet is the most worst I have been tried. I highly recommend you not to go if you from the city near by ocean or the city cooks good foods. This is not the one for people who have high standards on foods.
Good variety of food choices, some very unique and all were delicious .  Very pricey at $70 a person so you better bring your appetite to get your money's worth

My favorite buffet in the whole world! It's a must every time I'm in Las Vegas. 

They literally have EVERYTHING! My favorite are obviously the fresh raw oysters. I love their ginseng chicken soup! And the ribs, the crab legs, the baked potatoes, just everything is so good! Did I mentioned their dessert station is full of good sweets. From cute little cupcakes to macaroons. And the ice creams have some unique flavors. (orange beer, mango habanero, etc) My mouth gets all watery every time I think about that buffet! Awww!!!

Now if you are buying the buffet pass for 24 hrs, you'll need to pay additional EACH time you dine here. ($15 for breakfast, $25 for lunch and $35 for dinner) 

After dining here, all other buffets are shit. My favorite used to be the buffet at the Wynn, not no more!

This is my first review. I've wanted to leave reviews in the past, but didn't really get around to it as I'm usually left satisfied or didn't want to make a big deal about food taking a little too long or service not being the greatest. I feel very compelled to write one about this buffet as it seems so highly praised by many. 

Appetizer:
First, the wait (to pay) was about two hours. I guess that's what's expected as it's the holidays, so Ok. But after paying it splits off into two separate lines; apparently one for groups 5+ and one for less than 5. We had a party of four and get into one line. After waiting for about 20 min I'm told [by the photographer] that we are in the wrong line and that we should have been told to get in the line for parties less than 5. A hostess came and took our ticket and said we could stay in that line since the cashier didn't inform us of the different lines; I thought that was nice of her. After another 20 min we notice that no parties are being pulled from our line and the people that were in back of us in the original line have caught up to us. I'm pretty irked at that point so I ask the hostess what's going on here.  Quite rudely, she said that since many people were not told of the different lines they took people's tickets and started going by the time that they paid. After a little back and forth I say 'fine'. And then somehow a family in back of us gets pulled?? How would they have paid before us but ended up in back of us in the same line? Also, they had 3-4 workers in the front trying to organize that fiasco, which seems like a huge waste of manpower. 

Entrée:
Once we finally got in, 3 hrs & 10 min later, we are pretty impressed of the size of the buffet, however much of it was very disorganized. For example, the condiments for the meats were at the beginning of the line, so once you get your selections you have to go back for the jous, mustard, etc. They had hot/boiled crab, but then had to go to 'the seafood' section for butter and lemons. 
Much of their food wasn't labeled, which wasn't the worst thing. Their Asian food was pretty good, besides their sushi section, which was very lacky. 

Dessert:
Between plates I did some observing since we had to wait a while for plates to be cleared. I started to see why the wait was so long. Two tables next to us had left and they had sat dirty for at least 20 min. By the time we left they were still dirty. 
And the cherry on top: as we were waiting for coffee for our desserts, a manager comes up to us and 'politely' tells us that there is a two hour limit and shows us our receipt and that we had been there for nearly two and a half hours. Of course, at the end he says that we can take our time. He was going by the time of when we paid and failed to realize that it had taken us 45 min after that to get seated! If we're spending $200+ and waiting that long, go away and let us be/take our sweet time, please. And, do not rush us when dirty tables have been sitting for nearly half an hour! 
And a side note on their disorganization: we had called in earlier in the day and asked the price and approximate wait time for dinner. We were told that it was $50.99 and the wait for dinner is usually about one hour. We get there and it's $53.99 and a 3 hour wait. Not a big deal on the price difference but just reiterates their lack of organization. I guess they won't go announcing how long the wait actually is since it would probably deter a lot of people, but just adds to the overall negative experience. 

Overall, the food was OK, but the service really killed it for me. I'm sure if service was better/decent and the wait wasn't as long as a theme park ride, we would've enjoyed it more. But, their dessert section was a little lack - luster for being 'the best buffet in Vegas'. I would much prefer the M Hotel or the Bellagio. 
Do not go unless this is how you want to spend most of your day and evening. We left to go there at 2PM, got in line at 3PM, and left the buffet around 8:15.

As there are many positive reviews on this buffet, I'm sure this one isn't worth two s#%@*, but those are at least my two cents.

I had a lot of great restaurant experiences during my recent trip to Las Vegas, but this is the only place to which I would return. It was super-pricey (we went for breakfast) but super-worth-it. I particularly enjoyed the shrimp and grits, the steak and eggs, and just about everything. No trip to Vegas is complete without one buffet meal... don't bother with any other buffet on the Strip. This one is fantastic.

This was a decent experience. I'm a vegan, and with the prices, I was hoping for a little more accommodation. Every station had chefs who were very helpful in letting me know if I could eat something or not, but not as willing to help me out and make something without butter or meat (except for one! Thank you kind stranger!) almost everything is made with animal byproduct, and the amount of food I COULD have was not worth the price.

DO NOT GO TO BACCHANAL.

I have tried nearly every buffet on The Strip and was excited to try this buffet, only to be disappointed at the end of it. Bottom line, you can get a much better value at the Wynn in terms of service and food. 

1) I brought my entire family of 9 and paid about $500 for a good dinner, a privilege my family rarely gets to enjoy, in order to celebrate my Dad's 60th birthday.

2) Started waiting in line at 7PM and did not get in the buffet until 10:30PM. The staff had assured us throughout the night that the food would NOT be taken away until at least 11:30PM, prompting us to continue waiting in line.

3) After we paid, management treated us like DIRT, informing us that the food would be taken away at 11 PM. They did not care that their customers had waited for more than 3 hours and would only have 30 minutes to eat. Keep in mind that there is another 15-minute line to actually get food, so there was really 15 minutes to make a $500 meal worth it.

4) Jamie Radke, the assistant manager, said they could only refund our money and gave us MAJOR ATTITUDE for inquiring about a pass to skip the line next time, a request I thought was fair after spending more than 3 hours in line with 9 family members and not having dinner at all. Jamie is a prime example of how poorly trained the employees at Bacchanal are. Bacchanal management, please give Jamie more training - she definitely needs it. 

MESSAGE TO MANAGEMENT: Please do not DISRESPECT your customers. Customers willing to pay good money and wait more than 3 hours for your buffet deserve more respect from you. 

You will not be the top buffet forever. When the hype dies down and you are desperate for more patrons, customers will remember how poorly you treated them when you were on top. 

Please trust that my family and I will be warning everyone we know NOT to eat at your establishment.

Use to go to the Wynn Buffet
Now I am going both
I woudn't be able to choose which one is the best
Food is excellent and various
LOVE IT

Buffets will always be buffets. But some of the items here were higher end.  The sliders here were really good, along with the individual mini sea bass plates. The meats were too salty. Desserts are more elaborate then other buffets. Overall, it was ok for me. The sushi offered wasn't that great. I ended up eating a lot of crab legs to make up for the $50/person cost. The free coffee/tea/juice touch is nice. Server was nice as well.  Get here early. We thought no one would be eating at 4:30pm, we were wrong. Still had to wait a good 15-20 mins.

The sheer opulence of the Bacchanal Buffet is everything I expected. The amount and variety of food can not be easily described, but it is mind-blowing. I started at one wall with Asian food and slowly (very slowly) made my way through salads, Italian (pizzas/pasta), comfort food, BBQ, Roasted foods and finally seafoods. It took me 4-5 trips to get everything I wanted to taste, and then I still had to try dessert. It was well worth the price as I was so full, I couldn't eat for 12 hours. The service was wonderful, although the servers seem to have a bit of a turf-war over tables and were fighting with each other in front of us. I highly recommend this buffet over any of the others that I tried on the strip.

I probably wouldn't go if we weren't Diamond Status.
Diamond and above gets giant steamed king crab legs (cut open) delivered to the table. The options are pretty extensive but unless you only focus on meat and seafood, I wouldn't think it would be worth the price.

I enjoy the fresh taco bar and the macaroons are the best I have ever had.

I also enjoy the cheesecake cake pops.

I have gone to a lot of the Buffets in Las Vegas and this one blew my mind. Excellent choices, great quality and above all, excellent flavor. I went during the Memorial Day Weekend with family and friends and although it is expensive, I can understand why. They had so many choices for everyone that at first I was overwhelmed. There are alternatives for the big eater, the vegan/vegetarian and the diet conscious. The food is cooked at each station in from of you so you know it is fresh. The seafood station was incredibly good. Also impressive was the Steak/BBQ station. They have also Mexican, Italian, Asian and Greek stations. There is also a soup station. The dessert area is also impressive with lots of high quality choices. Overall, it was an excellent experience. Highly recommended.

Came here Yesterday for brunch and I never ran out of mimosas! From the beginning to end I had a great experience. This is the BEST buffet in the Strip! I wont even say what I ate but from the crab legs to desert everything was GOOD! Pozole was amazing along with the nutella crepes and the everything else. I am glad my husband and I were starving so we were able to EAT. The fresh juices were so tasty and great for our "dehydrated" tummies after a great night of drinks. The mango habanero ice cream was to die for!!!!

One of the best buffets! Really expensive, so be sure to go on an empty stomach. The buffet is endless. The dessert buffet is also AMAZING. One of the best buffets in Las Vegas, and I have been to pretty much almost all of them. There is usually a long wait, so be prepated to wait awhile. A must try, at least once!

Despite having been to Las Vegas on several occasions I had never been to a buffet.It was definitely on my list of things to do on this trip.
 The Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace came highly recommended and did not disappoint.
 I have never seen such a selection of foods in my life.everything I tried was delicious.
I highly recommend a visit.

Best Breakfast / Lunch buffet in Las Vegas.  Hands down! One dish that got me the most was their lobster seafood chowder which was amazing! They always have different item each day. They had wide variety of desserts including Gelato, i'm in heaven.

An amazing selection of gourmet foods. I loved the lobster corn bisque and shrimp and cheesy grits, the selection of sushi and dim sum goes beyond the California rolls and bbq pork and the gelato is fantastic. Try the Aztec Chocolate. 
I've been twice now and the staff is very friendly. The quality of the food should get it five stars but the food that is meant to be hot, like the burgers or chicken, never is.

This is buffet us ginormous! All my friends kept raving about this place so after alot of convincing, my husband finally gave in.  He's very hesitant when it comes to buffets because he doesn't eat much, not from the main entrees anyway. He makes the monies worth it in the desserts. 
We got there at 2pm like my friends suggested and a line had already formed. We waited about an hour before we were sat.  
I was in awe when I seen how many selections there were! It seemed like it was never ending! The minus one star is for service, we waited about 10 minutes for our server and then another 10 minutes for our drink to be dropped.  Throughout our meal, we were only checked on at least twice. 
I mostly ate from the seafood area, mainly the steamed snow crab legs and oysters. I don't care too much for cold crab legs.  The main entrees that I tried were pretty good except for the spring roll that was mushy inside. 
As for dessert, I thought the it was really awesome that they had baklava! Who has baklava on the buffet line?! They do! 
Definitely recommend this place.

Food was decent and I only thought the seafood station was remarkable. Honestly, I spent most of my time thinking about how I had to eat $63 worth of food to break-even on the cost. 

The oysters and snow crab/king crab legs were gigantic and tasted very fresh. The desserts were pretty good too, I loved the key lime tart and Thai tea boba float. Also, my friends surprised me with their birthday platter! It was a cute plate of desserts, mostly chocolate-based.

No doubt the best buffet I've ever been to in terms of quality and variety. It happens to be the longest wait I've had to endure and one of the most expensive buffet's in Vegas so there's a reason why its a notch above the rest. 

The average person only has so much space in their belly's and because of the incredibly variety in things to try, you'll need to attack this buffet with a game plan in mind because you don't want to waste room in your belly. Take a walk around and look at the things you really want to try before you start diving in there and piling up your plate.

Now, something I observed quite often were people who came in here and targeted the more expensive items, particularly the crab claws, legs and shrimp cocktails. Tables of people would load up on crab legs, and crab claws. While It makes sense if you really wanted to maximize your dollar for dollar investment this buffet, however if you really wanted to do that I would suggest trying another seafood buffet as it would likely be about the same quality but less expensive and less of a hassle to get inside. 

Where this buffet shines is how so many things are done well here. In the Chinese food area, the chicken feet, and peking style duck are really solid. In the japanese food section, there is fresh tuna and salmon nigiri. In the italian food section, I felt the mushroom truffle pizza, and the pastas in white-wine cream sauce were really good. Try a taco or a tamale in the mexican food section. Try a slider (medium rare with a small slice of cheddar, mayo, on a brioche bun), or some paella. Taste a cut of prime rib. And yes, do grab some crab legs, and crab claws, but also try an oyster shooter, and other seafood there. 

I just imagine folks coming in from parts of the country that don't have assess to high quality ethnic food being quite blown away by this buffet, as each type of food that was here was well represented and high quality. 

About $50 per person for 2 hours of eating. Extra 15 for champagne. You can schedule coming in as they change from br

There's not much else I can add or say that hasn't been said.

I went to Vegas for 4 days, and paid $50 twice to go to this place - that's how good it is. It has gourmet food for EVERYONE - vegetarians and others alike.

Don't bother with soda pop - get their fruit juices that are on the buffet line near the meat station. 

You will marvel at how amazing this place is. Quite simply, the greatest food I have *EVER* eaten, and the greatest dining experience ever - bar none.

Save your money and go to the Wynn!!! The food is pretty much the same or better over there. We waited an hour to check in with the host only to be directed to to wait in another line for another 30 minutes to pay $120 for two people then move to another line and waited another 15 mins. I get they're busy, but they have this service if you pay extra they seat you right away which is fine but there is no special line for it and when you've been waiting over an hour it's annoying. Then the service wasn't great. Like their employees were over worked and exhausted. Just not a good experience. Will NOT be coming back.

Oysters. Crab. Prime rib. Dessert. I'm in heaven! This review is long over due and well deserved. I am the hugest fan of buffets and always try to get the biggest bang for my buck. You will never see noodles, bread, rice or any other nonsense on my plate. When I see people with half a plate of chow mein, a little piece of me dies inside and I lose hope for humanity. What a waste when there is such a huge selection of amazing food. There are different prices depending on the day and time. Dinner buffet is around $50+. Pricey but worth the money and the wait. 

This buffet has a large selection of all different types of cuisine. 

- Fresh raw oysters and shooters
- All different kinds of meat cuts
- hot and cold crab (cut in half for all the lazy people out there)
- mussels, shrimp, crawfish (yum), etc
- There is a person making tacos, ramen, pho, etc.
- Every dessert you can think of is there. Macarons, ice cream sandwiches, creme brulee, cakes, cookies, gelato, mochi, crepes, chocolate covered strawberries, etc. The list goes on and on.

Bacchanal  has dethroned Wicked Spoon and is currently my favorite buffet in Vegas.
Best buffet in Vegas. Worth the money. Love the Delmar who makes the street tacos, meat station, seafood, desert bar, and pasta bar...and really all of it. A must visit on your Vegas trips.

If buffets are your thing, then this is the place to go. Lot's of options, very fresh because of the massive volume of patrons. You will probably have to wait in line. A bit overpriced, but you can make up for it with crab legs alone

We got here yesterday around  2:45pm and since  there were only 2 of us, we paid right away and got seated promptly. We got to save on dinner since we paid the lunch hour price.  That was really cool.

I expected a huge place. I think the buffet at Wynn and Bellagio are bigger than the bacchanal.

This place is just like any other buffets in vegas. Food selections are typical buffet selection; Asian food ,Mexican food, American, Italian, etc. I tried almost everything but it didn't live up to my expectation. The snow crab were frozen I mean then there's the steamed crab section but it jist ok. It was too salty. Some of the crab didnt taste fresh as i imagined it to be. Desserts were average, my favorite was the crepe. The creme brulee was disappointing, it was not custard-like at all. I also liked the flan, that was very good. The bone marrow was also good but I've never had bone marrow so i don't have a comparison. 

I will not be coming back. I will go back to my favorite buffet at Bellagio.

I love this place. It's honestly amazing. Best buffet in Vegas hands down. The crab legs are the best out of any of the buffets and the dessert area is also better than other buffets. I'm driving into Vegas now and coming here tomorrow

If you're getting anything but the seafood, you're doing it wrong.  Needless to say, I couldn't help but stray from my seafood binge. The options here are vast and it's very hard to stick to just one section.

Crab legs are a definite must to get your money's worth. The Chilean sea bass was also very yummy. Mussels, clams, scallops are all good; Shrimp, crawfish, oysters, sushi, ceviche not so much.

The BBQ section lured me away from the seafood and I just had to try a little bit of everything there as well:
BBQ ribs - too dry
Briskets - delicious
Prime rib - tender and juicy
Lamb chops - Amazing, but only when juicy. 3/4 of the chops I grabbed were extremely dry.

Desserts were on point as well. I recommend trying the creme brulee and the cheesecake pops.

Definitely a good buffet experience if you make sure to eat your money's worth!

Been to Aria buffet, M buffet, Bellagio buffet, Rio buffet and was excited to try a new buffet. For All five of us It was the most disappointment. Steamed Crab legs were salty, fish and chips was over fried and dry. Sushi, tuna poke with seaweed salad was not fresh. Oysters looked and tasted horrible. It tasted look or it's been sitting out in the open for awhile. Cesar salad had no crunch and it was stale. This was around 5:30 pm so all the food for dinner should be fresh but it was not. Sadly to say the only thing that was good were brisket, sea snails, pickled ginger, sesame balls, and fried fish gills. Almost all the food was either too salty or bland. Our waitress was good. But nothing to rave about. The money and the time we waited was a waste. We will never go back. Such a big disappointment.
Great buffet.  I recommend this place to anyone wanting to try good buffet food.  Also don't forget about the juice at the juice bar.

When it first opened, this place was beyond amazing with quality, food, service, and gourmet items. Throughout the years has gone down considerably, but has remained extremely overpriced for a buffet. As a positive the service and ambience was excellent.

A bit pricey but a great buffet if you are in vegas. They have everything from seafood to Chinese food to a wide range of desserts to choose from. The lines can be a bit long but once you pay they are pretty quick to seat you. I would recommend going for lunch, dinner is a bit pricey and most of the items are not something you want for breakfast and I feel that you will not enjoy it fully. The desserts are my favorite part, don't fill up on all of the tacos !

Went here on a Monday at noon. The wait was about 45 minutes. The weekday price was $40 (as opposed to $60 on a weekend). The spread was quite nice - sections for the Chinese subcontinent, Japanese, and Italian, Spanish, Mexican, salads, meat and a wide variety of seafood. The desert section was huge with a variety of interesting desserts. Most of the food was usual fare and nothing innovative (spring rolls, sushi, pizza, pasta, etc). The highlights were the lamb shank and the avocado and lime pasta salad. I probably wouldn't go here again and would instead head to the Wicked Spoon where the food is far more experimental.
