Tea, coffee and juices/sodas are free but alcoholic beverages cost more.

This trip marked our 3rd visit to the Bacchanel buffet, and it was just as fabulous as I'd remembered!  We'd considered another buffet (as we only chose one while on our Vegas trips), but other high-end buffet reviews on Yelp cautioned, " it was okay, but we wish we'd eaten at Caesers!".  Why ruin a good thing, so we went again!  If you LOVE seafood, this is your place!  I continue to be impressed with their cold AND steamed crab leg options as well as the huge cocktail shrimp (I swear they were even bigger this time). I'm not much for dessert, but it's a no brainer here.  Don't miss the gelato!  This time we tried  Salted Mexican Vanilla Bean and Coffee with Nutella.  I can't help but be impressed by their imaginative concoctions.  I'll rave again about the impressive gourmet cheese assortment as well as homemade guacamole and delicious selection of authentic dumplings and buns in the Chinese section.  

We'll never choose another buffett Bacchanel!  Yours faithfully, Kelly.

This breakfast buffet is one of the best in Las Vegas, but bring money. For 3 adults and 1 child the bill was $190. Of course they do offer an incredible seafood selection, everything from crawfish to lobster Benedict. The dessert selection is fabulous, too, including made to order crepes and 10 flavors of gelato. They, of course, do have your usual breakfast staples, like eggs, bacon, hash browns, pancakes, French toast. 5 stars, except for price. Then again, you get what you pay for!

I decided to come to this buffet, against my good judgment, based on the hundreds of reviews raving about this place. We paid $150 for two people (it's $69/per person for dinner on a weekday). I had read online that it was $50 so this was the first shock. 

The biggest shock of all was the mediocre food. The seafood, which is the biggest draw, was all show and no substance. The king crab was more like mini crab - very little meat. The stone crabs are nothing like the meaty babies you get at Joe's Stone Crab in Florida. They are flaky and not very good. The rest of the buffet was filled with subpar slop you can get at a $20 buffet. Nothing we took warranted more than 2 bites. And to top it off, the dessert bar was just more of the same. The fudge tasted like wax; the molten chocolate cake wasn't molten; the chocolate dipped strawberries looked a total mess as they were all fused together; and the gelato wasn't creamy. The cream brûlée was the winner at the dessert bar. What I'm trying to say is that I think you should save your hard earned money and go some place else. Wynn and Cosmopolitan have much better buffets if that is your thing.

I would give this buffet zero stars if possible! The wait time is 2 hrs ( on a Tuesday at 7 pm), and it is very disorganized. People are confused about which line to wait in, they are unaware that you have to sign in and return at the posted time on your ticket. So many complaints from people in line and the food is less than mediocre at best. The staff did not seem happy to be there as well. Definitely not worth the price, I would return to the buffet at The Wynn and Bellagio.

I can't believe this buffet. The oysters weren't that great and the prime rib and brisket was SO TOUGH. Unedible. I really wanted those two things to be great but it wasn't. Those two items were a huge let down but everything else was OK. For the price of $60 each, I barely got my money's worth in crab legs, shrimp, salmon and dessert.

After eating here, I can see why this labeled the best buffet in Vegas. For $40 brunch, you definitely get your money's worth here with things like crab claws, prime rib, and American Wagyu beef. Some other standouts were lobster eggs benedict and lobster bisque and the brisket. The reason why I won't give this 5 stars is because the dessert section wasn't as expansive as I hoped, which I found quite a disappointment, after seeing some previous photos. However, I will definitely be coming back here the next time I come to Vegas.

We weren't too impressed with this buffet but glad we didn't have to wait in line at all since we came right at the start of dinnertime.  

I've noticed that you can definitely see the seafood area right in the front, but they served the same thing towards the back area of the buffet when they could've had more options.  

For the main course, I got the prime rib, tater tots, mac & cheese, wagyu burger (which was rather dry), southwest chicken wings (that only came with 2) and some crab legs.  While they were all pretty decent, none of them really wowed me enough to want to get seconds BUT nothing else they had was tempting enough so I pretty much got some of the same things the first time around.  

What's pretty cool about this buffet, though, has to be the areas where you can get pho or have someone make your tacos or even crepes.  They have a pretty good dessert section full of macarons, gelato and other pastries.  They seem to have a lot of those mousse desserts, if you're into that.  

Overall, we probably won't come back.

Not sure what the hype is over this place

We bought the express pass, which cuts on the lane, but once you pay it you still have to wait 45min to be seated on a table.

Food is nothing special has prime rib, sausage, sea food, pizza and Chinese. Definitely not worth the wait!

You gotta try out Bacchanal if you are in Vegas, hands down the best buffet right now. It is quite pricey for a buffet ($30 for breakfast and $55 for dinner). If you want a good value and most bang for buck, I would come in near the end of the lunch hour (230ish) and they'll start dinner service at 3pm.

If you end up buying a BUFFET OF BUFFETS 24 Hour band...be aware that you pay a surcharge of $15-$25 PER visit. Still worth it though, the food is amazing.  

There literally is EVERYTHING here and they use high quality ingredients (especially for a buffet!). I had dim sum, pho, eggs benedict, and the BEST bacon ever here for breakfast on one occasion. Can you say HANGOVER KILLER?!

Expect for 1+ hour waits if you go during peak times, so plan accordingly! :D

The best buffet in Vegas if you ask me. So expensive, but of you won a good amount of money while in Vegas... Or you are like me, and just want to treat yourself to a huge meal... Then this is the place for you. They have an amazing selection, and if you wish to walk thru it first to see what they offer they will let you!!! 
My favorite section was the Asian section, they had some amazing steamed buns and dumplings that were all great as well as a tuna poke that was also pretty amazing! 
They also had a salad/apps section that had an array of salads, fruits, and olives and cheeses as well as fancy deli meats. They had an awesome watermelon with black salt when I went....so good. There was also a pasta section, a Mexican tacos section as well as a meats and seafood area with all the fixings.  

The dessert section was amazing. My favorite was the flan, the creme brulee, and the lemon basil gelato... All so good... And so many options! 

You. Should. Check. It. OUT!!!! 

We also did the 15$ unlimited drinks (mimosas, beer, or wine).. Was way worth it... Think I had about 6 before we left she was bringing them out left and right!

I liked this place because it was very organized for the amount of people in line to eat... YES GET READY BECAUSE THEY DONT TAKE RESERVATIONS AND THERES NORMALLY A 40NINUTE WAIT!!! however there is also a bar in front, so nothing a glass of champagne can't help overcome..

If you are on for a very broad list of choices to eat this is your place. It has a seafood section, an Italian, a Chinese and a Mexican food buffet all in one restaurant.

And even though it was extremely varied, I didn't think the food was amazing. However I rate it with a 4 star because the all you can drink champagne for 7$ , the organization and all the type of food we were able to try makes it worth visiting at the Ceaser Palace hotel in las vegas

Huge disappointment. High dollar low quality food and service. Seafood had no flavor. Meats were dry. Nothing reflected the value and the quality except the wide range of selections. Save your money and find yourself a good restaurant instead of this low quality grand buffet.

What can I say... even with the long wait (an hour if you're lucky) and missing the brunch special cut-off, Bacchanal Buffet lives up to the hype. I've been here once before about 3 years ago, and I gotta say, the quality of the food has improved over the years. The dinner price for one was $58, so come hungry to get the bang for your buck!

Pros:
- Diverse selection of cuisines: Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Western, Seafood, Mexican, assortment of meats, and a fancy dessert bar 
- Awesome pizza (went back for seconds, even though we were super full)
- Presentation of food was impressive
- The dessert bar has a crepe station made-to-order 
- The gelato was very good. Would have had more if I wasn't stuffed!

Cons: 
- The inevitable wait. We came at 2pm and the wait was over an hour
- Dim sum and sushi was mediocre
- Desserts were only OK. Bring back the mochi ice cream!

If you're in Vegas, Bacchanal Buffet is worth checking out if you 1) don't mind standing in line for 1+ hour 2) are ravenous for a bottomless meal.

This is by far the BEST buffet you will EVER go to. I love that they are always cranking out individual dishes so that you know its fresh made. Not just sitting in a hotel pan wondering how long its been there, determined by the skin formed on the top. They even shuck oysters in front of you. My husband and I went there in November a few months after they opened on a tuesday night. We waited way OVER an hour and it was worth it, we paid $98 for both and at the time if you pay an extra $15 I think I saw its unlimited wine and beer.

Talk about food for the Gods! This new and remodeled buffet looks extravagant! The quality of food here definitely exceeded my expectations for a buffet. I mean think about it...they put $17 million dollars into this franchise for a buffet, so of course this has to be at top notch with Wynn (I think it's better...Ek...I think I have to update my Yelp profile for favorite places to eat)!

Where to begin! Of course Caesar's Palace is like a maze, but I found the buffet quickly. You will notice that there are glass cups on the top of the column lights. The line pouring out from left to right...God knows when you will be next, but guess what? The line wasn't too bad (about twenty to thirty minutes). Then, you wait to be seated and notice the clear plates, bowls, cups, pitchers...etc hanging from the ceiling in their own little box. As well as tanks of fresh display of fish and crustaceans.

Once seated in the Seven Diamond and Platinum area (front of the buffet), you are basically next to the delicious seafood station as well as the dessert station. Let's begin with the stations from left to right.

Seafood Station #1: Where all your money is going toward! Huge selection of fresh stone crab as well as king crabs (guess what you have an option of serving it cold or hot, some were salty and some were sweet), oysters (kind of tiny), mussels, cocktail shrimp (black prawn therefore enormous!), clams and where was the lobster? Located in a lobster bisque (very salty)...wish that they served it whole or at least the lobster tail. There was ceviche that had way too much lime...Whoa! Don't try this. The oyster shooter was very good! Much more selections (Just wanted to tease your taste senses)! Nom nom!
 
American Station #2: The top notch American favorite! Prime rib (melted in your mouth), lamb chops, hen (ask to cut which part you want or get the whole hen), BBQ ribs, veal, brisket, sausages, burger sliders (overcooked), sweet potato fries, criss cut fries, tator tots (not too greasy), macaroni and cheese (disappointed because some of the macaroni was uncooked), baked beans, chicken tenders, mashed potatoes (kind of looked unappetizing and the gravy was in a plastic bottle...hope it was BPA certified but it was good still), etc. Also, at the end, you get to choose condiments from these cute mini size jars! Love that all American feast!

Mexican Station #3: People people?! Omg! Unlimited ribeye steaks! That's right! Ask the personal chef to cook it how you like it! Yum! Of course I can't forget my nachos (this one is for you Frank S.) The chips were nicely seasoned as well as crispy. The different selection of toppings was excellent! There were over twenty selections...(Drool)! Homemade corn and flour tortillas, Spanish rice, tamales, refried beans, and so on. Bring out the Mariachi, time to celebrate!

Italian Station #4: My favortie selection of foods of all time...but was disappointed. The selection here was simple. Baked ziti pasta (macaroni was not cooked all the way and BE CAREFUL the clayware is EXTREMELY HOT....burned myself...) TALK ABOUT SAFETY ISSUE..., baked lasagna, spaghetti and meatballs (a bit dry and not well seasoned), pizza, Alfredo pasta, pesto pasta, and deli sliced meats right in front of you...I think that is it. Not worth eating at this station...

Salad Bar Station #5: Fresh and crisp! You can't even describe the beautiful colors as well as the selection...your stomach just grumbles...FEED ME! I have to say I recommend the feta cheese and watermelon! There was a wide selection of assortative cheeses...Mmm...Pepper jack. The vegetables are crispy and not like the limpy kinds that you get at a regular buffet. Yes! There is a huge selection of salad dressings as well! Cheers to you vegans! 

Japanese Station #6: Fresh sushi and sashimi! Seaweed salad, fatty yellowtail, poke stack, California roll, salmon roll, spicy tuna roll, unagi roll, and the list goes on and on! Can't go wrong with this station! 

CONTINUED BELOW (GUESS YELP HAD A CONTEXT LIMIT)...Sorry fellow Yelpers couldn't post this one on the same day.

I had such an amazing time at Bacchanal! We went in at 2:15pm when they still charge you their lunch price ($38/person). I am a Total Rewards member so they give you $1 less. They start serving dinner at 3pm so we hit the jackpot! Do keep in mind that they have a 2 hour limit, but I don't think they really check it unless they're packed and need you to leave. 

To be honest though, the only differences between lunch and dinner were: (1) they serve oysters and snow crabs, (2) more meat options at the carving station, (3) they have macarons. The oysters were amazing! They always keep the oyster bar well stocked & expect a line. Other things I enjoyed:

Fish tacos
Charcuterie 
Cheese selections
Baked mac & cheese
Gnocchi 
Mushroom and ricotta pizza
Chinese chicken wings
Oyster shooters
Cheesecake 

Service was on-point. They were always refilling drinks and taking away your used plates. Ask for new utensils and they'll be happy to bring some to you. I don't know if I'd pay their dinner price though ($50+/person). Thus the 4 stars.
Went for the brunch. Food were okay. Not that great. I bet dinner is more worth the money.

Wonderful buffet, lots of great variety of food. For Chinese New Year, it is tradition to start with a feast. This was truly a feast! The steamed crab legs were delicious, meats plentiful and desserts to fill one heart's content. Samantha, one of the managers, is truly keen to detail in making a guest's experience positive. Great buffet!

We waited here for 5 hours and was expecting really good seafood.  But it turned out that they only have crab leg and some oysters.  The long wait was definitely not worth it.  The price is ridiculous as well.

I have mixed feelings. Was it expensive? Yeah, but what can you expect from a Vegas buffet. Was there a line? Yeah, so what. Was the food amazing? YES. I still have dreams about those crab legs (get them steamed, and they're already cut in half for you). The first time i had the rib-eye steak i was in heaven, perfectly cooked and juicy. The second time however it seemed like it was hardly cooked at all, i get that most people like medium rare but I'm more of a medium guy, so to each their own. The sushi was rather disappointing, not enough selection and not tasty. Overall I thought everything I tried was good, if maybe a little over hyped.

Sand...sand in clams, sand in veggies 

hot dishes are served lukewarm or cold

not even one good soup

Very disappointed

My friend highly recommended this place and persuaded me to come when we were in Las Vegas. Came with a group of 8 people, so we were automatically charged for the tips, and the total was $75/person. Honestly, I expected more if I spent $75 (!!!) for a meal!!!
I got the crab legs, and honestly they were salty! Yummy and fresh, but not good for your blood pressure!
The sushi bar was errrr... not impressed! I expected to at least have some sashimi for this price, but nothing besides some regular rolls and nigiri...
Chinese station is so so... nothing special! Don't want to fill myself up with Chinese food when I had to pay that price!
Meat station was busy all the time, cooked nicely, prime rib kinda under seasoned imo!
The oysters were kinda disappointing! Fresh but there were pieces of dirt and shells in it :| Oyster shot was delicious on the other hand! 
The noodle soup station was kinda disappointing too, I don't expect it to be authentic, but it should have at least the signature flavor of the broth.
Other items were great: salad, other stuffs I can't remember the name, desserts (crepes, creme brulee), etc.
+++: service, decoration, atmosphere, quality
I don't know if I went on the wrong day but there were not many selections as I saw on yelp. 
So honestly, not really impressed :(

I think it's hands down the best buffet.  So many selections, crab legs were plentiful and cut open for you. The entire seafood side did not disappoint, lobster chowder =YUM!

The meat carving station was great! Tons of delicious goodness to be found.

Try the sweet potato tator tots. You will not regret it. 

Like others have said, the cutesy plating for the entrees made it difficult to fill up one plate, but it made it much more pleasing to see a handful of tots in a mini fryer basket. It made the experience a little better. It's not like a regular buffet with a boring tray and ladle for each entree and side. 

Dessert was a step above the rest. We filled our table with the shots of desserts they offer. Might want to avoid the panna cota, and the passion fruit chocolate, everything else was AMAZING! Perfect portion sizes to make sure you can have one of everything, which is exactly what we did. There's a fantastic crepe station, and gelato also. Seriously, nothing was missing from the dessert/candy bar.

Downsides: Terrible service. Literally, I had to flag a different person down to get a refill, or plates cleared or anything. It's a buffet, the whole tipping process is based on refills and clearing plates, if you can't get that down, you definitely aren't getting a 20% tip from me. 

The line is crazy ridiculous. Worth the wait, but allot time for 20-40 minutes of just standing in line.

Use to love this buffet but the last 3 times I came was just poor.  The quality of food has just gone down the drain.  I keep coming back for another try because it use to be the best.  They had the best prime rib and lobster.  The prime rib is tough now and no longer have lobster.  Just not worth the $60 anymore.  I think I won't be coming here anymore.  So tempted to give it one more try because it use to be that good.  But 3 bad times should be the end.  Just don't understand why they are still getting high ratings.  Do people think it tastes good because they paid a lot for a buffet?

This is my first time at Bacchanal Buffet and I had a decent first time experience and some of the food was great but I'm not sure if it's worth going to, waiting in line for, and paying 60-70$ for (I paid 70$ because I came on Memorial Day weekend)

Ambiance rating: The atmosphere was a bummer, we were seated waaaaay in the back of the restaraunt far away from the food in a very dimly lit table. I think it was just too dark where we were sitting, it was really hard to tell what all our sauces are and in my personal experience I couldn't see the bone in my lamb chop and bit straight into it. It's also TOO crowded. I won't blame the Memorial Day weekend because I'm sure the Bacchan buffet is always bringing in customers but it takes about 5-10 minutes to grab food at the Seafood section and the Dessert bar. Which sucks because you're limited a 2 hour time slot in this buffet.. When you visit food station and you try to scoop some food into your plate, I think the pots are too small and the glass that's held above it is too low. It's really difficult to reach in and grab your food to serve yourself, and this causes spillage. 

Food rating: I don't think the food was as delicious as everyone on Yelp makes it out to be. Yes, I agree at a buffet level, the food was great. But for the price? I don't think so. I paid 70$ for hard lamb chops, hard shrimp dumplings, bitter cheesecake, cold seafood dishes (pan fried salmon and mussels) that are supposed to be served hot, and very watered-down horchata. SOME of the food was delicious but MAJORITY of the food was unsatisfying.
I thought the huge prawns was delicious with the cocktail sauce. I really liked the poké that they served in the Asian section. I think the best part of the dessert section was the creme brulee, but their mochi was delicious and so were their crepes. In the meat section, I enjoyed the Waigu(?) Beef although its my first time having it so I couldn't really compare. My boyfriend said it was so chewy for him that he had to spit it out! The lamb chops were flavored nicely but I think its too tough to chew. 

Overall 3 stars, I think you can find better and cheaper buffets in Vegas because I don't think Bacchanal is as great as everyone makes it out to be. I preferrably liked the M Buffet a lot better! I would have actually preferred to eat at a restaraunt and have paid for a more satisfying meal than the foods I had here.
Had an omelette at the buffet this morning! Not only was it entertaining to watch Curtis prepare the omelette, but it has to be one of the best omelettes that I have ever tasted!

I went to Bacchanal with a group of friends, and enjoyed the majority of their selections. Out of all the buffets I've been to in Vegas(4 total), I would say Bacchanal is my favorite. They have steamed crabs, which isn't uncommon to have here in vegas, but it's nice that they provide it. A lot of the selection at this buffet is similar to other buffets, but I believe the taste of their selection is much better. I couldn't believe how good their ox tail pho was, and I typically don't have high expectations for asian foods at buffet. You should definitely try to come before dinner, as it gets pretty pack by 6 PM, and the line to meat and seafood gets long.  Expect at least a 10 minute wait when waiting for them.

As I am a dessert person, I absolutely loved this place!  I made sure to make room for all the variety of desserts offered here.  It's a bit pricey especially since we went during dinner time.  I could handle the wait time since people just love the Bachannal in Caesar's Palace so everyone just goes there whether it's only because of the hype or the food.  It's both for us and we loved it!  We could only eat so much until we hated ourselves but I can honestly say that it was good experience.  We recommend The Bachannal Buffet as it's a must try at least once when in Las Vegas.

Definitely a must try!. It is such an improvement over their previous buffet
Seating was slightly cramped, and crab legs were too salty, they might have done that intentionally so people dont eat so much, i dont know.
i am very impressed with their and not many establishments can make it properly.
Everything looked so delicious, if only my stomach could handle it, i would have tried everything.

Don't you love when Vegas buffets raise in price for the holiday but they're so delicious and gluttonous that you fall for the trap anyways?

It was first time here in over a decade and I was thoroughly impressed. Compared to the other four buffets I have been in Vegas, this is by far the best. Like all buffets, it has various cuisines- from assorted asian foods to hispanic inspired to seafood, etc. There's a lot to be eaten.

We were here for brunch. Line is actually not that bad if you're in the group sizes that are eight people and over. It's probably because if you're in that group size, you're also paying an extra gratuity that just sent this MDW brunch to probably being out of my price budget for the weekend. 

Definitely filled with meat (especially pork) options so certain sections are not the most vegetarian friendly. 

Highlights:

Crab legs! Steamed and cold available
Street tacos - not worth your money, imo, but fun
Juices! - lots of different flavors, more of a novelty 
Unlimited bread options
Crepes
Gelato - with an option of ice cream sandwiches

If you have some cash to blow on a buffet, you won't be dissappointed by this one.

Three stars is mostly because there was nothing "wrong" with the buffet, per se.  I don't have a lot of experience at Vegas buffets, but I was told the price had been bumped up the weekend we were there ($61 per person, ouch).  I have been to the buffet at the Rio hotel, which felt larger and I thought had better quality food.

I did enjoy the food here, though the selection did seem more limited.  There was a decent variety of types of food, but in each individual type there didn't seem to be an expansive number of options.  Also the food was really hit or meh, no big misses come to mind but a lot of stuff that didn't seem up to snuff for the price we paid.

By the way, do you like seafood?  You do?  Good, because after waiting 90 minutes to get inside and seated, there was another 20 minute wait to get through the seafood station.  I understand people like their All-You-Can-Eat crab legs, but that borders on ridiculous.

This is one of my shorter reviews because I really have little to say about it.  It was decent, but I won't be coming back.

The best of this place was the desserts. It's overrated and for 55 bucks a person, I expected more. It's your average buffet with crab legs, chinese food, and a place for delicious dessert with a little style. I will not be coming back to this place.
Eggs Benedict was bland.  No flavor what so ever.  Over priced for what we got. Eggs over cooked.  Not satisfied.

The best buffet and value I have ever gotten! I came for lunch and paid $49.99. They had such good selection and good quality food. I think what was great was the value of what you got. Just to name the top things, wagyu beef, crab, shrimp, nigiri, poke, steak, pho, tacos, etc etc. wait can get long but that's with any good buffet. This is easily my favorite buffet in Vegas!

Omg! This place was fabulous everything you can imagine and more. The food was fresh hot and delicious we went on a Tuesday so it wasn't crowded I ate until I couldn't eat any more . Ok so unfortunately I didn't take any pictures because I was I was too busy eating guys but there's plenty to see already . Yes it's great that's why I gave them a 5 and can't wait to go back !

Lunch is $30 I believe and dinner is $55 and all I can say is the food was delish! 
get their prime rib. So much flavor and cooked to perfection! 
They even had pho! Their pho was pretty good as well. 
OMFG and they even had a taco bar where they make it fresh for you...
Okay this place has everything. 
The MUST TRY:
Prime rib, scallops, steamed crab legs, oysters, pho, lamp, mac n cheese, tai tea coconut ice cream float, green tea cover strawberry, and flan. 
In my opinion their scallop was my favorite. YUMMMM 

I mean this is by far the best buffet in vegas so far. They literally had everything. This is one of the buffets I will always go to when I am here in vegas.

Even though this is a pricey Buffet it was worth the splurge. The crab legs are soo good and the Ramen was actually better than I had. The server we had wasn't very attentive, but she was replaced with someone who was. The desserts were really good especially the creme brulee. You will not be disappointed eating at this buffet.

Prior to this, we felt that the brunch at Paris was untouchable. We both agree that this place is amazing. By resisting the urge to just load a plate up with some of the best bacon I've tasted, and going with smaller portions, I had an extremely varied breakfast (although not like my wife's which included sushi...)

Not cheap, but nothing in Vegas is anymore.

So many options, so little time! I came here for the first time not knowing what to expect. I've only seen pictures of the buffet before but when all that food was right there in front of me, it truly was magnificent. Make sure to pace yourself so you get your money's worth! They have everything from Italian and Mexican to Asian. The crab legs are a favorite and people always line up for them. They have cooked ones as well as raw so be sure to get the type that you want. I enjoyed their pho, tacos, and skirt steak. The chicken biscuit sandwich was a bit dry and I'd probably avoid the sliders next time, but basically everything was good. You definitely have to come in here with a strategy. After eating all of the main dishes, don't forget that they have their own dessert station filled with a ton of other goodies such as creme brulee, gelato, and boba. One thing to note is that when you first pay, they ask for tip and if you tip they put you in a different line and mark your receipt. I haven't really noticed any difference service wise, but it is always good to leave some sort of tip!

I'm giving this place 5 stars because I was very impressed with the selection of offerings as well as the overall quality of the food. The crab legs, oysters on the half shell, wagyu beef, prime rib carving station, and sushi all make the price tag worth it in my opinion. On top of this, there are food options for picky eaters or those with dietary restrictions everywhere. My only regret was that I didn't save more room for desert, there were dozens to pick from. For as busy as they are, the lines didn't seem overwhelming.

The downside was how long we had to wait, but we were prepared for it, and fortunately you can kill some time in the casino while you wait for your text confirmation. If you are hungry and don't mind shelling out the money, it's very impressive.

Was in Vegas a few weeks ago, came here for brunch twice. This is the best brunch I've ever had in my life. Our waitress JULIE was amazing. She made us feel so special. She is truly one of a kind. Food was just so good. You must experience this brunch if you are in Vegas. And ask for Julie. You wont be disappointed.

In my opinion definitely not worth the wait and the price. But many people think it is worth it to see the hype, so it does not hurt to try it if you wanna waste a day out of your short Vegas trip in line. I won't be back. We were there for New Year's Eve, price was about $93 per person for dinner. Definitely not worth the price since I went there again just to see the difference at about $69 per person for dinner. Not much difference and the food is not worth the price point even at the lower $69. The wait was horrible. Las Vegas is a place you should feel luxury so don't punish yourself and your loved ones by waiting so long in line. 

Worst part about this experience is actually the service, not that I expect much from Caesar's Palace, since it is no match in quality to Wynn or MGM corporation hotels. We waited for our orange juice for 15 to 20 minutes asking two different servers. Finally I called over another server and asked politely:" how long does it take to get an orange juice usually?" He replied with disrespect and impatience and said "who did you ask" (like I would know your employees), "he should be on his way." First off, how would you know that he is on his way without checking. They definitely don't deserve tips. So don't pay the tips at the beginning with your credit card when you pay for the buffet. It is a sign that management is lacking here. Food is very mediocre and does not match the price point. Hope this review helps.
A lot of the food was really delicious. My favorite was the desserts. The servers were kind and would usually check to see if everything is okay.

I have been to Vegas plenty and experienced good and bad buffets.  Bellagio and Aria, great!  Monte Carlo and Luxor, not so much.   

The Bacchanal is one of the good ones.  Everything tasted extremely fresh and although there was a wide array of food, they weren't trying to do every type of dish of every single cuisine.  I was really surprised by their Asian selection.  The sushi tasted made to order and was super fresh as was their pad thai.  So, so good.  

As is to be expected, their seafood section was mobbed.  Although the crab legs were the most visited area, I thoroughly enjoyed their crawfish boil, mussels in lemon sauce, and clams in a garlic sauce.  Those were the standout seafood dishes for me.  

As expected, the lines can be quite long but service is great.  It seems they have a dedicated waitress and busboy for each section so there isn't a huge pileup on plates or empty drinks.  

If you are looking for an intimate meal, this is not the place to go.  It's always bustling and always full.  But impressive food for a buffet!

This place....lol our server was nice.  But for 50 something dollars for dinner was not worth it....Sorry but if I could choose another place to spend that much I know I would have been much happier. Not to mention they took a photo of us when we came in then brought us like 3-4 printouts of them, I mean nice ones...then they told us it was 15 dollars for one of the pictures...we honestly thought out of all the money we spent we'd at least get the pics for "free."  So they went through all the trouble to print them and then are going to throw them away because we didn't want to pay for them? Why not just give us the photos...Food was cold, poor quality of meats, etc..Also not near as big as this looks! Just bummed we spent so much. 
Sorry can't recommend this at all.

I visited here twice, once for lunch and once for dinner. For the price, this is the best buffet i ever had for 50 for lunch 60 for dinner.
Their seafood selection during dinner is phenomenal, although the crab legs were a bit too salty for me, i went mostly for clams and salmon which were cooked perfectly with amazing sauces. 
The ravioli in a stainless steel mini pan was the best. 
There is just way too much dessert selection, and i loved it. Creme brulee and hazelnut cake were to die for.
My friends loved that i took em there.

Amazing.  

5 stars except for the line to get and the lines inside to get food.  

Seafood was fresh.  

Soo much to choose from and it all tasted great.  It's the buffet standard.
Way over price over crowded and no pasta on the buffet. Carnival in Rio is better and cheaper I think.

Solid buffet but a little pricey for a Sunday night. 

Standouts were the (loaded) street tacos, Chinese spare ribs, and the Wagyu sliders. For dessert, my freshly made nutella-raspberry crepe topped with whipped cream was great. The plum pudding is worth a try. Next time I'll plan on grazing for a few hours.

$68 jacked up holiday price was not worth the food and the chaos and headache of getting inside and the pandemonium that ensues inside... the server was good... the food was great! But the wait time was so long in lines it was cold by the time you return to your seat. Very sad experience! PS the desert bar is also fantastic! But the wait kills how good it is as well!!!

2.45PM Mon. Nov. 26..Best day. .I got in rite away. Always go on a off time. Checked it out 2X before on busy nite and the wait was 2 1/2hr. It was $29.18 lunch price + tip.  I got a bench.

I had snow and alaskan crab. They were not salty like everyone complained, just not sweet. Maybe they get sweet in Jan.

Oysters were from East Coast. Not sweet. Clams were good.

Rib eye and prime rib was very disappointing. They were from a Nebraska ranch, dry, tuff. Sausage, ok. Tell the bbq chef to wipe the sweat off his head when he's cutting your piece of meat.

Best food I liked was the proscuitto, different salami from Italy and violet mustard...a balsamic flavored mustard.

Tried the pistachio and  banana soufflé. Not good. tasted like mushy cupcake. They don't make the choc. one anymore..Malted ball was shitty. Tiramisu, not good.

I liked the mint watermelon gelato and aztec chocolate. I ordered the coffee because another yelper said it was the best. Not! I drank the whole pot and didn't feel the caffeine at all.

The waitress I had was 90 years old with dementia. She forgot  my order.

I still like the M resort the best. The seating is better. The way M RESORT designed the layout of the  Buffet..And best of all you have access to the beer and wine..Free..

All I can say is try Bacchanal for a dif experience.

The food was good, not wow or anything, id say average strip buffet food; def on the pricy side. The price online does not match, so don't bother to check coz it's always different. Love the gelato and shave ice, lots to choose from. Overall, don't think I'll go back coz the price, u can def find a cheaper price for the same kind of food in Vegas.

Today we had a good friend come into town and she wanted to try a "good" buffet.  Hearing all the hype and doing research of the city, we decided to try the Bacchanal Buffet. From the start, we knew it was going to be pricey coming in a little over $50 bucks a person.$175 for 3 people with tax.. Ugh. Having never been,  we wanted try it. Initially entering the buffet it looked great, there was plenty of food, no real wait for anything you wanted. Unlike a traditional Buffets where the food is placed in metal pans and set on a steam table to keep it hot, this one was a bit different. Most of the food was placed in nice ceramic pots, sitting on a granite countertop for the guests to take from. The problem was I immediately seen is that the food was never that hot. By the time I dished something onto my plate and walked to my table it was almost cold.  The meat section had plenty of meat selections to choose from, being a baby back rib lover, I tried the pork ribs twice and both times they were pretty fatty. It was a bummer.. My wife said the crab legs were just ok, not great. The best part we all thought is the buffets dessert section, where we filled up on gorgeous looking sweets that did taste as good as they looked. Overall I can now say I have now tried the "Top Buffett" in town, however I don't think I would ever go back. For the price I expected better quality of the food. I have been much happier at a smaller off strip buffet for a fraction of the cost.  Conclusion, was is bad? No, Was it worth the $$? Definitely not, Was it an experience, Yes.

Excellent food, quality and variety. Staff really hussles,  loved our brunch. 
Mini crow monsuier, heaven.
Noodles and added broccoli beef over very tasty.
Waldorf spinach salad. Yum.
Added mini tomatoes, excellent.
Huevaos rancheros, eggs and extras on mini tortillas,very good.
Choc chip and toffee, and coconut macadamia cookies, heaven. 
Apple strudels, look like little pies puffy and yummy.
Hubs had an omelet, etc. Was very happy with all his selections also.
Thank you to all the great hardworking staff. Happy holidays.

Not worth it anymore.  No tomahawk ribeye.  Raised prices.
Got a rude host and meat carver one time.

And the meat was terrible one out of the 3 visits.  Really dry prime rib.

Tacos were really good one visit.  And just okay the second visit.

This place has a ridiculous wait. We kept thinking, well it will be worth the wait.... But it wasn't. 
After waiting for eternity to pay, we were told we had to pay an up charge to eat here. 
The up charge was $30 per person over our wristband purchase. 
The buffet was not even worth $30 much less $30 plus wristband charge!!!

Good was bland, Chinese food was horrible, as was the sushi.. 

Dessert was the only reason it even got two stars. 

Don't recommend!!!!

Best buffet after the Wynn of course!!! I have been twice and would come again.  My favorite station is the meat , I loved the lamb chops, the ribs, and the prime rib.  It was so juicy and well seasoned.  I loved the little plates with the different entrees.  The dessert station was decent the highlight is the ice cream station love it!!!
We've been back and it's still the best buffet around!  The lamb chops were absolutely divine, my favorite item!  Too bad it's so darn expensive!

When they say "what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas", I really hope they're referring to the pounds you gain from the buffets...

I'm not usually a buffet fan. Getting a ton of generic food that others have picked at isn't at the top if my to do list. But when in Rome (or at least Caesars' imitation)...

The food here was all delicious and elegantly presented. A great selection of traditional buffet fare like the carving station with prime rib as well as more exotic offerings like dim sum. A lot of dishes are served in individual plates; cute, but unfortunately leads to cold food as well. 

All in all, I'd try it again if I were here. Especially at lunch when you can save a few bucks over the dinner price.

Great experience here. My boyfriend and I came to this buffet on the last day of our little Vegas trip. A lady named Valerie was at the register, she was a pleasure. She was very sweet, talking to us and asking us questions - making us feel very welcomed. The host who seated us was also very welcoming. 

The food was great. There were an overwhelming amount of options but everything we tried was good. Don't skip out on the taco station, it was really good. The cooks will make you fresh tacos right there and then you add whichever salsas/toppings are preferred. We didn't save room for dessert, so I can't comment on that. But all the savory food was great. 

The buffet entrance is right next to the entrance for the pool so we stumbled out there after our meal and took a little food-coma nap by the pools. Totally recommended.

This place is considered the best buffet in Vegas but it's also the best buffet I've ever been to. I usually don't like buffets because the food quality always sucks. But even I gotta admit this place is great.

They have a great variety here. From sushi to tacos, the food quality is up to par. They even have stations where they make bowls of noodle soup, tacos, and crepes.

I usually get mass amounts of the crab legs to get my money's worth here. But make sure you ask the worker behind the counter to get the HOT crab legs. I don't usually like prime rib, but it's pretty good here. The sushi is not gonna be amazing but it's pretty good quality for a buffet. They don't have much variety in the sushi, but it tastes pretty fresh. I also like getting the crawfish, noodle soups, and shrimp cocktail.

The only downside to this place is that it doesn't have good desserts, which is why I didn't give it 5 stars. I grabbed so many desserts on my plate but none tasted good. The fruits that they had didn't even taste fresh or sweet.

Overall though, if you're looking for a good buffet to eat at in Vegas, this is the one to try. It's a little pricey, but it's worth it.

I see why this is rated the best buffet in Vegas currently.  Line was about 30-40 mins on a Saturday afternoon.  Many different food stations with tons of great choices.  Lots of deserts as well including gelato and macaroons.  Definitely hit up the seafood section with lobster chowder, ceviche, king crab legs, oysters, mussels, clams and of course cocktail shrimp.  All the other stations were very good as well.  Was a little disappointed with the carving station and the prime rib, but the lamb chops were BOMB!

My favorite buffet used to be spice market - this one kicked it out of the top spot. I tried the Bacchanal Buffet for the first time this past Christmas. We arrived around 9am and only waited about 15 minutes to get through the line and to be seated (this was not the case 30 minutes earlier - the line was wrapped around and around!). 

Oh my the selection at this buffet is amazing!!! For Christmas Brunch they had pancakes (including chocolate chip and red velvet!), chicken and waffles, french toast, croque madame and croque monsieur, crab legs, shrimp cocktail, fresh juices, kobe sliders, brisket, prime rib, pizza, pasta, asian dishes, sushi, menudo! (my boyfriend said it was AWESOME), street tacos, cheeses, fruits, salmon and lox and so much more. And the desserts!!!! Fresh crepes, gelato, so many cakes and cookies and pies. Everything was DELICIOUS. I wish that my stomach was larger so that I could have tried more. This buffet is expensive but it is well worth the money. Any future trip I take to vegas will definitely include this buffet!

This buffet was about $50/person and very worth it. There are at least 50 different dishes to choose from, including several varieties of crab legs(included with your $50). The food was delicious and they had a huge dessert​ bar! When I went, they also had horchata which made it even better! Any foodie would never want to leave this place. Only thing I didn't like was they ask you to limit your stay to two hours (eh, this is more than enough time anyway​) and that there are a lot​ of greedy customers who pile their plates but don't finish even half of what they took..

First thing off, I'm not a buffet person. The place is really pretty and service was excellent. But I did not enjoy the food at all. Granted, all the foods were ok but nothing outstanding or memorable. Oysters and crabs were very fresh and probably the best things in the buffet. Not going to any Vegas buffet ever again.

I admit I was a bit shocked when the cashier charged us $99 for 2 for dinner. A whole Benjamin pre-tip went into this buffet dinner! Cashier asked if we had a Cesar's Palace players card. We didn't, and I was almost gonna get one thinking I would save a considerable amount on our meal, but it's only a dollar discount.

Foodwise, I enjoyed the crab legs (you could get warm), and there were different kinds of roasted meats! There was actually a lot of selection, but it was all so beautifully presented, that it all looked tantalizing.

The dessert bar has to be one of the best I've ever been to. Moshi was offered, along with freshly made crepes, assorted gelato, 2 kinds of creme brulee, and a lot of other assorted sweets! I think I got my money's worth in macarons alone! 

Bottomline - pricey, yes, but shit, everything is in Vegas! If you've got a sweet tooth like me, this is definitely the buffet to go to!
Really sucks for the price. They are trying to pass off cheap roast beef as prime rib!

Decided to give Bacchanal another try and im glad i did . Food was all hot in temperature like it was suppose to. All stations were fully stocked and the service was great . Thanks to Samantha . We ll be back

Finally I get to write a positive review! I found the staff at Caesars to be very friendly and helpful. The buffet staff is included in this. Our server was on point! As for the food, it was just amazing. The beet salad....I don't even eat beets...was delicious, I can't stop raving about it. Smoked brisket, to die for. Be sure to try the green beans in the Asian section. Skip the gelato, it was the only item not up to snuff, but made up for by the other scrumptious desserts.

We went opening weekend and it was fabulous. However, I have noticed that the price has steadily increased since its opening. We had brunch for $19.99 - for what we had we underpaid. The raw bar was a great surprise - fresh shucked oysters, ceviche, shrimp cocktail. We love hitting the brunch hours for buffets, get the best of breakfast and lunch for a great price (usually). Everything from the red velvet pancakes to the fried chicken baskets was perfection. The dessert section was massive. They took a page out of the Cosmo's book and served everything individually - much more sanitary. All of the chefs behind the glass were talkative and helpful. The manager was checking in with all of the guests as well (granted it was opening weekend). The chairs are pretty hefty lounge-style armchairs which makes it a little difficult to maneuver with a hand full with a plate and your chair was tucked back in while you were gone.

Food here used to look like there was time and care spent on presentation as well as taste of the dishes. Now looks like everything was made half assed. Even the dessert section! It was a waste of $69 on Memorial Day. I would rather have gone to Rio buffet. Not coming back here again.

If you ask me what my favorite meal of all the time there is no doubt that my first experience at Bachannal is up there.  It's a Vegas buffet, what can you say?

It's hard to talk about the food since there is a lot of selection but my favorites were the lamb chops, the sliders, sea bass with miso glaze, braised octopus with creamy polenta (a chef's special sadly), the brisket, and their fried chicken.  I also really enjoyed their seafood selection (oysters!).

The first time I went my friends and I waited 3 hours in line as their was no good system to get in.  By my 2nd visit (about 2 weeks ago as of this posting) their was a computerized system where you put in your phone number and they tell you when to come back.  I thought this made the whole experience better and much more streamlined. Of course, depending on how crowded Vegas is that weekend, your wait time may still be 3 hours.  The 2nd time I visited we got in under 40 minutes (even arriving at the same time...of course the golden time near the end of lunch before dinner seating!).  Enjoy!

After seeing all the rave about this place, I really wanted try this place out. We came here during their brunch hours and it was 39.99+tax and since it was also a Thursday, we did not have to wait to be seated.  Right off the bat, the restaurant is beautiful!  All the food are presented nicely and there are glass walls separating seating areas.  I guess I came in expecting a little to much because I thought the seafood buffet was also included during lunch time but it wasn't.  They had some crab, mussels and some fishes.  Overall, I felt like it was overpriced when compared to the Carnival World Buffet at Rio. They had seafood, brunch food (eggs on everything), Italian, Mexican, and Asian.  If you want more variety like me, Carnival World Buffet would be a better choice.
Check out these pics! I still can't stop thinking about this damn buffet! Can't wait to get back to Vegas just to eat here again!

Came here for breakfast. Huge huge place with tons of options. Every kind of food you could think of plus a massive dessert station with made to order crepes, salt water taffy, donuts, churros, fudge, cookies, cakes and more. I loved the fresh press bottled juices they had. The only thing I would dock it for was not having a lot of vegan and vegetarian choices.
The selection here blew my mind! Come on the weekend for the brunch for the best selection. I've never been to a better, more expansive brunch. Coming back here every time I'm in Vegas.

One of the best buffets I ever visited! It's clean and the food is pretty fresh! I enjoy their selection and the seafood and dishes they offer! You will find something you like, trust me! I love their shrimp cocktail. It comes in a cup with some type of green sauce. Maybe cilantro sauce? I had four of these!  Go early so you won't have wait in line and they have great service! Btw, they charge a 20% gratuity for parties of 8 or more. Definitely going back when I visit Vegas next time!

Overrated buffet!!!!!!  Totally not happy about it!

First of all, the wait was long when there were still so many opening seats available.  Forget about this because it was labor day weekend.  

Let's talk about food.  A lot of varieties of food choice, but it tastes like inexpensive buffet that only cost less than $15.  Totally can't talk about quality here.  I wouldn't come back for this expensive but no quality buffet, unless you have no where else to spend your money.  Got that!?

I would rather spend $60 for some decent quality of appetizer!

I must mention I'm not a huge fan of buffets. I enjoy eating at them but I feel that a buffet is only good as its value. Bacchanal is probably the best buffet on the strip for the money - but it is still quite expensive and doesn't stand far ahead of the others anymore.

When Bacchanal first came out, only a few buffets had the "small plate" concept. You still had your carving stations and such, but prepared small plates showed more attention to detail than a huge pan that you scoop out of with a giant spoon. Over time, other buffets picked up on the concept at least partially (and I think Wicked Spoon might have done it first but I'm not going to nitpick on the timeline considering I didn't get to Wicked Spoon til years after it opened). The first time I went to Bacchanal, it was via a Yelp Event, but I've gone a couple times since. Unfortunately, I do feel the quality of the food has dipped, but not as bad as some people seem to believe.

Having experienced Sterling Brunch as well as local station buffets (which really are the opposite ends of the spectrum), I feel as if those are far superior options for either those that want to get value or those that want really special buffet experience. I just can't really say that I feel the mid-level buffet offers much better food for about triple the price.

Yes, this place has set a new standard for buffet.. Food wise.. but as for service and everything else.. had to take a star away.. sorry.

I had came here twice and was able to see if anything had changed.  The line, no.  It is estimated that if you start at the back where the sign is, that is about 1.5 to 2 hrs.  I waited once and paid an extra $15 the other time.  

On to the food.  Many items are a hit and some aren't.  Lets start with the good ones: Crab legs, HUGE! They do have cold and warm ones, chefs are prepared with them as you come by.  Oysters are a hit, but you have to grab them while you can.  Sorry, NO LOBSTER.. Deceiving since they have a lobster on display near the front.  I had the lamb and ribeye.. AMAZING! We had a debate about how lamb should taste with my group and it was interesting about the smell, taste, tenderness and it hit A+ on all three.  Smelled good because it was cooked correctly, tasted wonderful and leaves you mouth with a sweet taste afterwares (we suspect that it's honey).. and no knife needed which means tender!  The shrimp arent like other places (cocktail), this are man shrimps, big and firm.  I heard good things about ceveiche and it is true.. Very well made.  This is dinner.

During brunch: I like the fresh juices they have in the bottles in the front.  I had like 10. Sorry.. I would pass on the melon juice.. very light.  Red velvet pancakes.. OMG.. it's actually perfect the way it is, don't add syrup.  Their burger sliders are a miss.. Very dry.  Asian food: I enjoyed the lobster bistro soup they had, but the dim sum was okay.  I enjoyed the ham crossants they had in the Italian section and the different cheeses they had.  Remember, during brunch, you do get MIMOSAS! It's part of your meal, do take advantage of it..

Many of the misses was from the dessert bar.  Maccarons were not as good, not to mention that they just throw them into a pile and they crack.  They had this cake with a pipet sticking into it as a fushion cake and that was terrible (cake was hard and the fusion didn't go in all the way).  The fresh suflet they have in the oven are very well made.. I like how its very moist and soft (caution, extra hot).  The taramiso shooter glass, it was good (not too sweet).  They have a crepe station, they make it pretty darn good, different berries to choose from with toppings.  The gelato is excellent, they have unique flavors including such "spicy chocolate, baklava, watermelon mint, caramel delight, etc"  I thought they were pretty good except for the watermelon mint (weird combination).

Reason for me taking one star away, is the service:
Sadly, both times, it has been pretty bad.  First time, our server did not approach us until 20 mins into our meal (dying of thirst from your food!).  Not to mention that I had to wave her over everytime my drink was on empty.  Second time, they sat 5 of us at one of the round tables that was very tight and sadly, we ate very fast so the plates piled up all over the center.  
The place gets overwhelmed by the number of guests, but they have not gotten the idea of getting more help.  I know it's not the servers fault, but it's management.  Servers are nice and sweet, but lack since they are under staffed.
I think this place has the best breakfast buffet.  Food ranged from chicken and waffles to seafood and desserts.  Great quality food that perfectly matches the cost per person.

MY NEW FAVORITE VEGAS BUFFET!  I'm sorry Wynn, but you got some good competition here

Great variety and good quality, the most memorable being:
- King crab legs are juicy and not as salty as most other seafood buffets
- cocktail shrimp were big, fresh, and crispy
- orange juice was super sweet and tasty
- shrimp and grits - surprisingly flavorful, done cajun style with a little spice to the cheesyness of the grits
- korean short ribs - super tender and well marinated
- cold bean salad - very hearty and fresh tasting with cilantro
- potatoes gratin (?) creamy and flaky thin slices of potatoes YUM
- watermelon mint sorbet very unique
- caramel sugar butter gelato - SO GOOD!!
- fudge filled cookies

nothing was horrible that i could not eat.  i finished everything off my plate, my only regret is that i could not fit more into my stomach, or else i would have tried more items.  my recommendation would be to go get your food in groups of 2 so if you are going to pick a pre-portioned mini individual size plate, you and your friend could plan to share it, rather than getting full off of 4 items you want to try.

I ate at Bacchanal buffet twice in August 2013 and once in August 2015. I found that the quality of food has changed, however I still enjoyed this buffet. 
The Bacchanal buffet has an automated reservation system for waiting in line.  The system tells you when it is your turn to wait in line - it does not let you know when it is your turn to eat.  Using this system, you could still stand in line for two hours. Once you submit your reservation, you are handed a paper listing your return time.  However if you use the text message system, you could be called in quicker than the time listed on the paper reservation. When I visited the Bacchanal buffet, I received a text message twenty minutes before the time listed on my paper reservation (which caught me a little off-guard).  I went to this buffet on a Wednesday night in Aug 2015, and waited in line for about 25 minutes. 
Bacchanal's uses small plates for many dishes. The quality of these items is awesome, however the food cools quickly.  This is a big problem if you pick up a small plate at the beginning of a large line.  For example, the small plate items are first at the bacchanals seafood station; the shellfish is second.  So if you remain in line to get other items after you have made your small plate selections, your food will get cold by the time you are finished selecting your shellfish items. However, the seafood line can get long, so you have an incentive to remain in line even though your small plate items will cool before you make it to your table.
The Bacchanal buffet has some unique items, which you would expect given the price of this buffet.  However, I was surprised at the quantity of items available at this buffet that can be consumed at less pricey buffets. If cost is not a concern, then it may not matter to you that you can get these items at buffets that cost 40% less. My favorite station was the meat carving station at Bacchanals (the brisket was delicious). I enjoyed the thai tea.
Although I enjoyed eating at this buffet, the line, decline in quality, price and other options would likely keep me from eating here again.  Of course, if any of those factors would change in my favor, I would certainly reconsider.

POINTS: Dumb name with the word ANAL in it...All I saw was "Back Anal"...Of course standing there for this long. I couldn't help but think of bad things to say. This is a BIASED review due to our 5hr45min wait. Mediocre food at best. LONG wait not worth it. Great service staff despite their long hours for Thanksgiving. Possible #1 in amount of variety, not taste. 

For once we wanted to spend Thanksgiving in Las Vegas, no cooking, no cleaning, no left overs. We decided to head up to the advertised "#1 Buffet in Las Vegas". We knew there would be a long wait because of Thanksgiving, so we arrived early.....like EVERYONE else and started to wait. We were told that the wait would be 4 hours from where we were at 3:00pm, so 7:00pm dinner sounds fine to us. We switched off every hour or so to make the wait easier. Long story short, it took FIVE hours to get to the spot to pay, which gets us to another line where it took another 45 minutes to be seated.

There was also a priority line and a VIP line where you either pay $20 extra per person to get in quicker or you had some VIP status at Caesar's due to stays or lots of gambling. either way, it made the 99% of us really frustrated because they would seat 4-5 tables of them first, then seat the "normal" people, then 4-5, then ONE, etc. This not only makes it unfair in a way, but it made the line and wait even longer.

Only good thing was that Caesar's Palace had someone past out water as we waited in line. With all the money they have and make they should've done more for the people. Sure it was our decision on wait in line like idiots, but you were way off in your estimated time because you decided to cater to the 1% and screw the 99%. I wasn't going to wait four hours and just leave. So what;'s done is done.

This place is a "Jack of all trades, master of none". I'm going to assume that their "#1" status was gained by the variety of food, Not gonna lie but there was a LOT to choose from. Problem is EVERYTHING was dried up by the food lamps. And the flavor didn't really make me think "best buffet" dry or not. There was NOTHING that made me want to come back to this restaurant. In terms of authenticity in flavor, since I'm Chinese I'll tell you that the Chinese food is not up to par. It was close and edible. but definitely lacking the authentic flavor.....kinda like asking for a Coke and getting a Pepsi instead, there is a difference.

Will I revisit. YES, I always re-try the places I don't like for dumb reasons like this whole waiting issue. But until then I'll have to stick with a 2 star review. I REALLY wanted to eat here when when are on a more normal operation. The waiter even said they were short handed and that's why they were never 100% full inside since they didn't have the man power to handle it at full capacity.

We wanted to try something different since we've been to "Wicked Spoon" and this one did not disappoint. They had a wide variety of selections from their seafood, to sushi, street tacos and their meats. Their selection of desserts were also plenty.

There are so many "Vegas" buffets and we have tried so many. We would definitely return here because overall we had an awesome experience dining experience with their service and their food choices!!!

Everything here was amazing. The food and the service was fantastic. They have a wide variety of food selection. I've tried three different buffets in Vegas and this is by far the best one. I highly recommend this buffet.

They have a large selection of desserts and seafood. Most of foods were good during my visit last week. However, oysters were not fresh, AND they have no taste. Those oysters seem to be big, but they must did bad job on either transporting or cold holding. I grew up in a fishing village and used to eat a lot of raw oysters. I knew what would a fresh oyster tastes like. My girlfriend and I got sick badly after eating 2-3 pieces of them.
Staffs were very friendly, but they must be too busy to refill my drink. My cup was empty for more than 15 mins. It's normal in a $10 buffet, but not normal in a $55 buffet. Waiters should at least ask customers if they want more drink. If they were super busy, the management should hire more waiters since each table pays good tip ($15-20 for table of two).
They could have done better job for Chinese and Japanese food sections. I seen 30% of customers were Asian. I expected to see sea urchin in sushi bar and some traditional Chinese foods, but nothing special was showed during my visit.

Very disappointing. Figured Caesars was associated with Nobu Hotel which has a distinctive Asian influence and would thus have amazing sushi. Nope. Not even close. The rice was cold from the refrigerator with small fish again w a refrigerated appearance and flavor. The cold crab was watery. The seafood rice dish was gummy.  The mashed potatoes were bland. The sea bass was mealy.And the oyster was the most disgusted thing. I actually spat it out due to the fear I would get sick. On the plus side:1) I got a discount of $80. Dinner for four would have been about $240 but we got it for about $160. 2) The hot crab was great! 3) the beef ribs yummy. Sooo stay away from much of the seafood and rice dishes. Also get a discount so you only feel ripped off by $100 vs $180.

Delicious! Went for brunch. Had many options for vegetarians. Delicious freshly squeezed juice. The only reason I am giving 3 stars is for the dishonest pricing. They state on their website that if you get there before 10 am you can get $10 off each person. When I got there and showed them the offer they said they are no longer honoring that even though it was still on their website.
One of the better buffets in Vegas. Definitely enjoyed the food, but it was probably further enhanced by the company I had. The food definitely was carefully thought of and well prepared.

Super Auswahl, mega Groß, schönes Ambiete.
ABER: Der Preis geht gar nicht zu zweit 90 $!!!!
Deswegen 2 Sterne Abzug.

I was very disappointed maybe I was expecting a lot after I read the reviews the crabs legs are  very small , and at the Italian station they only have boiled " small crabs legs "and one Italian dish .yes, the do have a variety of pizza and good section of Asian food  but it not worth the high price of $51.00 I have been in much better ,cheaper and more variety place

Huge selection and great food! Love the layout--almost like it never ends! We each got an alcoholic beverage. For $15 each it left much to be desired. We didn't even finish them. Our waiter never asked if we liked them or not. She dropped the check off for the beverages immediately and continued to hound us to pay the check right away. Aside from that experience, the food was awesome and the variety was great. We went on a Friday night and the wait was less than 20 minutes. We will definitely return!

We went for brunch on a Sunday. This was a huge buffet with something for everyone. Italian, American, Latin, Asian (including sushi), salad station, yogurt/granola station, an assortment of seafood, as well as a sweets/desserts station. I ate my weekend's worth of calories. I suggest getting there early as it really starts to fill up around 10.

So we went for a late lunch in the thought to catch the dinner menu switch.  We arrived around 2:15PM and there was only a few folks in line.  We were seated within 10
Minutes.  For some reason we ended up in the way back area despite passing by empty tables.  
   I started out with a try of the brisket which was super moist and delicious.  I had some of the sashimi which I should have skipped.  I waited In line for the Crab Legs which were cut in half and very tasty.  Sweet and delicious and even better with the clarified butter they have.  
   At the switch to dinner I waited again for oysters.  I got 6 as I was excited to enjoy some oysters.  One small bite and my oyster craving was over.  The were gritty and disgusting.  Flipped the shells over and waited for the plate to disappear.  I also got a piece of prime rib.  Another regret as it was over cooked and basically leather.  What a terrible crime!  
   The desserts were all pretty good so that helped soothe the disappointing dinner adds.  The Wait staff was very good and keep our drinks full and cleared plates regularly.  
   So my verdict - lunch is the way to go if you come to the Bacchanal Buffett.  I don't foresee another trip anytime soon as I wasn't impressed.  The best thing was the crab legs but not worth the hassle and price.

one of the best buffets I've had! 

My friends and I come to have lunch before we hit up edc,  and the line was super long. They had a touch screen monitor in the middle of the line where you can reserve a spot for your party which was super convenient. It prints you out a receipt telling you how long your wait shall be and when to come check in at the front desk. Our wait time was an hour so we had time to gamble and walk around Caesars. 

An hour has passed and we come back and it's already dinner time and prices but luckily we got to pay lunch price and still eat the dinner food! So happy they were able to accommodate that for us, or we got lucky :) lunch price was 38 bucks and dinner I believe is near 60?

They had a HUGE selection of food. This is my second time here and I still get lost! Lol I'm a huge sushi fan so I went straight to the Asian food area and grabbed 10 pieces of salmon and tuna nigiri and half a roll. I think I made my money worth in that one plate already lol try their salmon! It's in the seafood area. So yummy. There are some dishes that aren't the best, but there are some where you keep coming back for more. You feel like you're in heaven when you're getting dessert. Chocolate covered strawberries, mochi, macarons, cheesecake etc etc. Ahh! I miss this place. 

Service isn't too bad either. Clearing up your empty or unwanted dishes and refilling your drinks. Come try this place out!
Expensive but good. No let down here. The meat and seafood selection is the best I have ever seen.

I would give 2 or 3 stars just for the taste, but at given price, it is 1 star to me.  

I am very used to AYCE from K-town in LA and expected Caesar's would be an infinitely better than the ones I am used to.  I visited Vegas in about 15 years... back then, things were not as crowded or expensive.   Now, everything in Vegas seems even more fantasy than before.

Sushi was exactly at Chinese AYCE quality.  I even noticed chef was a Chinese who doesn't speak English at all.  Servers were quite slow, but friendly enough.  All you can drink beer had only 2 choices, and on the second glass, it was down to only 1 choice.

Crab legs were all right, but not $70 something quality.
Great place for anything from the sea! So many options and choices. Sushi was fresh and delicious. Very busy, there was a waiting time at 3:00pm.

Awesome, awesome, awesome. That's all I can say. 

I mean the food is great, more than 500 items, clean buffet, and our server Michael was awesome.

You won't be disappointed even the line wasn't that long, maybe because we came at 4pm 

And better than some of the restaurants I visited 

If your in Vegas and going to buffet. Use this buffet help you gauge the other buffets and restaurants

This buffet is overwhelmingly big. I really liked the  ramen. It was some of the best I ever had. The pork stuffed wings were just so unique! The meats were all so good. I liked the chicken sausage! The crab legs were also good. My favorite desserts were the gelato and the chocolate lava cake! I'm so sad I missed a whole side of the dessert bar :(. Make sure you come hungry!

It's my first experience with a Vegas buffet and it was less than spectacular. While there was a diverse option with large quantity, the quality was average at best. Unless you're there just to eat alot, the flavor wasn't worth $60+.

Best Vegas buffet I have been to so far. (I have not been to wicket spoon but most of my party did and they agreed it was better) They do a check-in type reservation that requires you to walk up to a kiosk with all your details and tells you when to come back. I suggest come 1.5 hours before you want to eat - it's a way better system than forcing people to wait in a line for an hour.

Seafood is definitely a highlight here. My favorites were:
Oysters were super fresh, Crab legs for DAYS (be sure to walk to the back and get some steamed!), Scallops, Sea Bass and Clams served many different ways.

The meat was good, delicious, and juicy. I really enjoyed the lamb chops and prime rib. 

Taco station was actually pretty good but be careful and don't fill up on the cheaper stuff!

Don't waste your time with the sushi, it was okay but I have definitely had better at sushi joints (typical of almost any buffet)

There were a ton of desserts, most of them good, nothing life-changing.

Service was spectacular. Our waiter took care of our table of 11 with ease and barely left any plates after 2 minutes of completion.

The seafood selection and flavor is bomb.com. I tried almost everything else there, and it was mostly all good. I stuck away from their chinese/thai food since I was being asian and eating my $68 dollars worth - ouch. I will definitely be back!

EH....NEXTTTTTTTTTTT...is all I gotta say about this place.  I think it was a little overhyped for me.  I was expecting to be blown out of the waters with this buffet as everyone kept telling me how great it was.  But I wasn't really impressed with much.  I will say that I enjoyed their sushi bar, unlimited macarons, mushroom soup, pork tacos, sweet potato tots, fresh mango juice, and roasted duck.  Not sure if it's enough for me to justify paying $54 for.  Some big disappointments included the prime rib which was dry and very red, soup dumplings which were dry, the oysters which were very small, the crawfish which were somewhat dark and not fresh, and limited dessert bar.  I'm not sure if this was done on purpose, but they seated the four of us in a section right near the Asian foods, and as we looked around we noticed nothing but Asian customers in our section....just a funny observation I guess.  Overall, I think I would pick Wicked Spoon over this place even though I wasn't completely blown away by Wicked Spoon either.  The prime rib was a huge let down at Bacchanal compared to Wicked (which I feel has the best prime rib) and that to me makes a buffet worth the money...so I would probably pass on this buffet next time around and try the M buffet next.

HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT!! DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY ON THIS OVERRATED CRAPPY BUFFET. I WANT A REFUND!

I thought I'd treat myself and try it and see what all the hype was about. I feel CHEATED. I went elsewhere for desert afterwards because I was still hungry. I've never left a buffet still feeling hungry. Ever notice how every buffet in Vegas was voted #1 including the $7.99 ones & Bacchanal? They all can't be #1. Bacchanal isn't even in the top 100,000. 

The holiday price is $63. WHAT A RIPOFF. This was the first and last time I'll eat here. I've gone to most of the buffets in Vegas. A least one or two items stands out above the even at the worst buffets. Not at Bacchanal. There was nothing special Bacchanal Buffet to warrant a $63 price. The Prime Rib, if that's what it really was, was awful. Maybe it was horse meat!! lol. Don't laugh, I've known restaurants who serve horse and call it prime rib. Lucky's at Hard Rock, which I eat at regularly and the Crappy Silver Sevens buffet has better Prime Rib and it will cost you a 1/6 the price. Just the fact Silver Sevens has a better meat should tell you something!!! 

You can get same seafood at Asian Seafood Buffet for only $14 all you can eat. The crab is better there as well as the sushi. Asian Seafood Buffet also has a larger selection of sushi and better shrimp dishes and other assorted Asian dishes. Should've went there. Also the Orleans & Station Green Valley only charge $25 & $30 and have way better seafood and prime rib. They regularly send me 1/2 off coupons and if you play your rewards right, sometimes it comes out free. The mini deserts where amateur and not very tasteful. The Palms Buffet serves similar and better deserts for $7.99 at lunch time.

Pricey but worth it. Great variety.  They give you smaller sized portions per option but the quality is great. Don't worry, it's still all you can eat so you will fill up no problem. The dessert bar may be the best... Ever.
This is a bit pricey for a Vegas buffet but the food quality is worth it. The service was good and the variety of food was vast.

Las Vegas goers, locals, and people geographically distributed over the globe RANT and RAVE about Bacchanal Buffet, the numero uno (that's #1 for you non-speakers) buffet in all of Las Vegas! Price wise, be ready to drop the dough (~$53), but if you're only here once in a while, f it, drop that wad and go all in baby, WOO!

The line, oh the line, is a maze of warm bodies, huddled around the thin fabric separating groups of people like animals. If you're baller (or a frequent visiter), you can bypass the "commoners" line by having your fancy loyalty card and going into a "Disneyland Fast Pass"  line. After you enter the line, you can expect to stand and wait for anywhere between 30 minutes to an excruciating 3 hours, depending on the time and day you're crashing Bacchanal. Oh, and before you enter - make sure you come with the "winner" mentality, as in, power through and eat as much of each thing as you possibly can.

Fast forward to being seated, you're now faced with an endless variety of fresh and delicious foods of every (major) cuisine. Seafood near the entrance, American (BBQ), and Hispanic foods are at the front of the buffet. If you head to the back, you enter Italian, Asian cuisine. In the middle of the buffet, you can be enticed to wet that sweet tooth with a pool of desserts from everywhere. So where do you start? Wherever your little heart desires! For myself, I started from the front, and worked my way back! That's called strategy people. I eat so much Italian and Asian food, I have to get my money's worth of seafood and bbq! Oh, and street tacos up front? To KILL for!

After my horrendous experience (for other people who watched me devour 5 people's worth, not for me) of eating everything, let's call it ~14 plates, I headed over to the dessert bar and began the apocalypse portion of global desserts. I'm REALLY hoping I don't have diabetes. :/ But I'm sure the .. everything .. will balance out, right?

All in all, a DEFINITE must try buffet while in Vegas! Splurge your money, and enjoy the good life. Cheers!.. and to an excruciating amount of time at the gym afterwards. Whew!
my favorite buffet in vegas. i think i've been to all the major casino buffers and many of the other local ones.
There is a nice selection of food and it's always tasty!

If you are going to check out one buffet in Vegas, this is the one to check out! Food is amazing, excellent selection. Have been here many times, and brought many friends and family. Never had anyone that was disappointed.
