2: if I totaled the amount of time I got my ticket and waited in line, it was 3.5 hours. Do you know what could happen in 3.5 hours? I could've watched an entire football game or taken a plane to Dallas with some time to spare. Anyway, we were corralled in these never ending ropes like cattle. 
3: the line got out of hand so we all started arguing where everyone was and the people with platinum passes who only had to wait 30 min got in before me. If someone has platinum passes, they should have a separate line or if they are in a party of 6 or more they should've been put into the 6+ line on the other side of the restaurant. Everyone was in the same line! The fault all started at the beginning and it got worse. The greeter didn't know how to handle the crowd. The organization was garbage. 
4: the food was cold, the lines were long, and your food was sub par.

Guys though, I'll be nice. I'm not a mean person. I'll compliment you in some way so you won't be entirely depressed:
1: nice efficient service staff! Our waitress was very sweet.
2: good food variety. 

I'm sorry Bacchanal, but rot in your grave, because I hope no one goes. You're dead to me.

Enjoy the quality food here,one of my favorite for 2013
 Beef with asparus,Macarons,Snow crab,King crab,Steak,
Chinese food,Fresh pizza,Mussels,
Wish I can give them 6 stars

Bacchanal Buffet is awesome! ... The variety and quantity of food on the buffet is huge. You cannot try more than a handful of items because each dish was so tasty, you end up thinking, "Should I try another dish, or get some more of the this one?"

Most of the sections had chefs actively cooking more food. You can actually ask them to make the dish differently. For example, if you do not want the chicken rice, the chef will happily make veg rice just for you. All this comes at a price, but it is worth it.

Ok... So one of the things I was really looking forward to trying during my trip to Vegas was the bacchanal buffet. So many good reviews and hype on food network and other sources made me so excited to go to this place! I came here with my husband for brunch with a groupon I purchased. Maybe it was because it was brunch... But it wasn't all that the hype made it out to be. Don't get me wrong, there were a few notable dishes that blew my mind. Pork belly. Mac and cheese. Crab eggs Benedict. Shrimp and grits. And Nutella crepe. Everything else (and I do mean the many many everything else I tried) was subpar. Regular buffet food. The Mexican station sucked. I was disappointed there didn't have any sushi rolls out. I did enjoy their unlimited mimosas.

This was good... I liked the Jasmine sunday brunch at Bellagio better though. We came in between breakfast and lunch, so there was remnants of breakfast here and there. The crab legs were the stone crab legs which l dont like as well as the Dungeness. Husband loved the smoked oysters. .I liked everything else I put on my plate, with exception of some weird habanero sausage.  I would definitely come back..especially because this buffet pretty much costs the same as the others, except for that I wouldn't touch the others with a ten foot pole.

NOT WORTH IT! Save your time & money!!!! 4hr wait to be seated so you can wait in more lines for food. Quality of food was poor. Ended up feeling sick an hr later & throwing it all up!

Location/Accessibility: Located in Caesars Palace Hotel

Ambiance: Average noise. Seating arrangement is a bit off. There are too many walls in this place, its a bit of a maze to get back to your seat. Not a fan of the placement and look of the place.

Dress Code: casual

Menu options: seafood, meat station, american, mexican, asian. 
- Long lines for the seafood and meat station. Boyfriend and cousin stood in line and by the time they came back w food, we had already gone through two plates. Not worth it IMO. 
- Some of the dishes in the other areas (American, Asian) were a bit cold. Although the food was under the heat lamp, the temperature of the food was cold! I believe the lasagna gave me food poisoning! 
- Dessert station had many selections (macaroons, gelato, mini cakes, mini souffles). Variety was good, but quality of the desserts was so-so. Have had better!

Service: Came w a large party (18), had to be split bc after 4hrs of waiting, we were now determined to just eat, rather than sit together. Ended up having to split our party into 6, 6, 6 (my table in particular was split into two tables of four, so we couldve had to more at our table). Hostess was not very bright at the seating arrangements. It was a bit ridiculous IMO. Once seated, our server was amazing. He was very attentive and came w refills before we were done. That was the best part of our night.

Price: On avg $55/pp (NOT WORTH IT!!!!)

Overall experience: I would definitely NOT come back!!! It was such a horrible experience for all of us!!! The price was outrageous for the quality of food we received and the long wait to get it! 4hr wait to pay, 30min wait to be seated, 30-40min wait in the seafood and meat station line!!! Not worth the money. To put the cherry on top of this experience, an hr later, I threw up all my food! I didnt even gorge myself! I believe it may have been due to the cold temperature of the lasagna. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND!!

Food: 2/5 stars
Service: 3.5/5 stars
Venue: 2/5 stars

I liked it...

I actually was afraid of this place because all I had heard from friends was that it was just okay but I actually found a lot of different things I enjoyed here.

- roasted duck - my goodness, this was melt in your mouth good here! I actually was thinking there is no way this can be all you can eat.
- porridge - more Asian food that tasted good? I can't believe it, but the porridge here with the fried donut (which I could not believe they had here) was THE perfect way to end the meal (yes I skipped out on dessert)
- sushi - surprisingly, the sushi section of this buffet was decent- the rice seemed prepped properly and the fish looked fresh. There was a guy making hand rolls but I had no idea where he was setting them out
- cream of mushroom soup - this was simply ridiculous! I tried not eating too much of it because of the truffle essence and as you know, if you drink, and then you burp, and you had truffle... well yeah... don't be THAT guy
- steak here was decent, got a semi fatty piece; so was the crab legs; oysters were so tiny it felt like they shouldn't have even offered it
- the other buffet fillers - nothing really stood out to me

Would I come back? Absolutely- I'm curious how they are for their brunch/lunch hour...

This is our first buffet ever and we went big! My daughter was drooling from the pics so we decided we had to take the kids to a buffet before we leave Vegas. We chose Bacchanal and it did not disappoint. Although there was no crab of any kind so that was a bummer. We came for the weekday brunch on a Tuesday morning around 9am. Adults was $39.99 (ouch). Unsure about the kids. This was the biggest buffet I've ever seen. Seafood has shrimp cocktail, smoked mussels, etc. then there was the carving area with ham, sausages. There was chicken & waffle, steak n eggs, bagels, breads, Mexican, fresh juices, Italian with lasagna & bread, sushi (I didn't care for it at all), dim sum, Chinese food, dessert bar was on point. We were so stuffed!!! The selection was overwhelming but delicious. We walked right up, no wait at all. Awesome! This will be hard to beat. We were debating between this one and the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmo. This one was pretty darn good.

Waited 15 minutes in express line that cost extra $20per adult for thanksgiving brunch, price of brunch $59? on that day, but I liked not having to wait long this time, kids half price. For two adults, four kids, cost $280 plus tip, express. The buffet was amazing, fresh, and far better than the past now that I did not have to wait as long as the dinner and later crowds.  We stayed three hours and tipped extra, but really no one rushed us. Service amazing even though buffet.  The week prior I ate at wicked spoon and it had gone downhill in quality, so for thanks giving this was the only buffet I was willing eat at with the low wait.  Would I wait two hours for this buffet? no. It is not worth two hours, but when you see no line and come at the start of opening, it is the best buffet food, selection, freshness in town.

This place by far is the very best in terms of quality and selection amongst other buffett places on the strip.

No comparison and I have gone to many.

It's not cheap but we'll worth the price IMO.

Soooo many good things it hurt!!! 

I generally don't like buffets at all. They are always about "quantity"... Huge selection of below average tasteless cold greasy food. Bachannel has QUANTITY (as in variety) and QUALITY.  

Seriously - there are several dishes at this buffet which are so good that it's impossible to not have a second helping. A few of these items are: 

Udon - super flavorful broth. 
Crab legs - perfectly chilled w/ lemon & butter.
Raclette cheese - paired w/ multigrain bread.
Poke - fresh, citrusy, and spicy.
Pizza - crispy crust and a zesty sauce.
Kobe beef sliders - not overly cooked. 
Crepes - Made to order. Nutella goodness.

I've had this buffet 5 times now and I still haven't been able to taste everything. They have large sections containing a variety of dishes for whatever you maybe in the mood for:
Seafood section - cold and hot
Carved meat section
Italian 
Mexican 
Chinese 
Traditional American 
Cheeses and breads 
Salad bar 
Soups / noodles 
Sushi - only section I'm not impressed with 

Deserts - their selection is huge along with a made to order crepe station and a gelato station. If they had chocolate covered strawberries, it would be desert heaven!

Heard a lot of good thing about deserts here. Came here early on Easter Sunday expecting to have something unique especially they charge you $20 extra for Easter Brunch. Came to find out they won't serve any real desert until 11am because that is their lunch hour. Didn't we just paid For Brunch? They didn't give me an option to pay less for breakfast hour only. Bad business practice. Make sure you know what you will get before paying. Definitely won't come back again.
The best and my favorite buffet in Vegas. Lots of choices , great presentation , great atmosphere, crab legs are huge , and desserts are delicious. Definitely a five star experience.

ASK FOR CARLOS AS YOUR WAITER!!!!!!

As a first time Vegas goer, this was by far the best part of the trip. Not only was the food absolutely amazing (get the Mac & Cheese, mashed potatoes, seafood, spring roll and tiramisu) but the service was beyond anything I could possibly imagine.

After a TERRIBLE experience at the Wynn last night, we were blessed to have Carlos as our waiter. He is attentive, kind, hilarious and very generous - would recommend him 10/10 times. Seriously Carlos made the entire brunch worth the $70.

Let me say that we were in Vegas this Christmas and wanted to try the Bacchanal buffet for  Christmas day dinner.  I am glad I went super early and talked to one of the hostesses, who suggested I get a ticket at the Kiosk in front of the buffet for a time to come back for dinner.  I came back to the Kiosk at 11:30am, when it was operational, and got my time to return, which was 3:30pm.  However, they texted me at 2:30pm to come back for the dining experience.

Important suggestion:  If you are going at a busy time of the year, you need to get the ticket at the kiosk otherwise it was a 6-hour wait, yes, 6 hours.  That said, I returned to the buffet at 2:30 and had to wait 1 hour and 15 minutes to be seated.  Although there were tons of people waiting to eat, they only allowed so many people to dine as to not cause terrible lines at the food stations, which is a nice touch.   Once inside, we were promptly greeted by a pleasant server who continued to refill our drinks and cleaned the table of plates throughout our dining experience. 

I will limit my review of the food to this: Incredible.  By far the best buffet for variety and quality I have ever had.  I was truly impressed.  Although a bit pricey, especially for the holidays, I ate enough crab legs to offset the cost.  I would highly recommend.

I also don't understand why some people do not rate this buffet as good as you can.  I read many reviews about wait times, etc.  I say that is to be expected for this buffet.  You need to rate it on the quality of the food.

For $59 branch, I'd expect better food and service from it. It has the slimmest crab legs I have seen from any buffet, I do meant any. The table was rarely cleaned nor the glasses refilled even once. The rest of the food is ok, and was the exactly the same from two years ago. Oh, the newly installed system to check in to avoid the line? It was another line you have to stand behind to get your phone number entered. Once you entered your information, you get a text msg for you to come back.... So you could wait in line for 40 minutes. I have no idea what's the point of that except now they have my phone number. 

My next door table have to complain to the manager for lack of service and they get some comp. I didn't feel like to added more to it except here on Yelp. 

I think this will be my last time here. Bye bye Caesar!
not a big fan of buffet stuff but this place has pretty decent crab leg, large selection of different cuisines and 7 dollar champagne brunch.

Came here for New Year's Dinner ... for once in my life, I did not plan. I didn't plan to come to Vegas for NYE, I didn't know where I would eat any of my meals (although I did expect everything on the strip to be crowded), I barely even brought enough clothes. Everything worked out, but one of the hardest things I dealt with as a planner who didn't plan and an eater who couldn't eat was the wait in this buffet line.

Let me preface this by saying - I was told that this was the best buffet in Vegas, that it's expensive, and that it gets really crowded. But no one told me that I had to book a reservation using the electronic kiosk during the afternoon *if* I wanted to eat here 5 hours later for dinner. So at 6:30pm, when I woke up from a nap at the Mirage, responded to all of my friends about what it was like to see Fetty Wap and Bruno Mars the night before, put on my clothes, and took my ass over to Caeser's a little after 7pm... I had no idea what I was in for. We shouldn't have even been in that line, but one of the employees (to remain nameless and employed) told us that s/he could let us in (if we made it through the line in the next 3 hours). Man, that was a line full of grumps with time-stamped receipts and hungry stomachs!

Almost two hours later, we made it in! The selection was HUGE and I was starving. It was almost 10pm and they were shutting down the lines by 11pm. I grew anxious... I grabbed plate after plate of seafood and immediately inhaled an entire plate of steamed crab legs. I felt sick. I should have paced myself... Damn. Oh, I just remembered ... the oysters were TERRIBLY shucked. I was actually spitting out broken bits of shells! There is NO excuse for that at a place like this.

There are a lot of choices here, some of which are great, but I've realized that I would have rather gone to a nice restaurant with real reservations. I'm glad I tried the "best buffet in Vegas," but I wouldn't return unless the wait was less than an hour long. I would definitely advise against coming here during a holiday. Looking back at the reviews, no one thinks the wait is worthwhile.

Huge junkie (the buffet kind). Fresh sweet juices, around the world cuisines, and long lines to illustrate how popular this buffet has revamped itself.


There isn't any elbow to elbow fight over the last crab claw or xui mai cause not only do they replenish their food quickly, but this buffet is actually spacious! Thank goodness, another place in Vegas where I can have some breathing room apart from my hotel lodgings. 

The name baccchhhhhhanelllll hurts my throat to say but the food makes my tummy satisfied.

Okay so the line for the buffet is ridiculous. Then they give you the option to skip the long line and wait another 30 minutes for $25 per person....for 2 people dinner was $175.....the food was not that great. I've had better food....the crab legs were the best part.....I wouldn't bother going here again.

Just go. This place is what buffet dreams are made of.

Asian menu- 5/5
Mexican street taco- 5/5
Steamed crabs- 5/5
Dessert- 5/5

Italian, Meat Carving sections, and seafood are like 3/5

but overall, so worth the 50$ 
My favorite buffet on the strip so far!

During the last leg of my road trip from Dallas to Los Angeles, I decided to add a stop in Sin City so that I could commit the sin of gluttony at the best buffet in town. The last time I had eaten at a Vegas buffet was when I was a child and I remembered it being glorious, so I was excited to do it again. After looking some things up online, Bacchanal seemed to be the clear winner so I decided to give it a shot despite the hefty price tag. Unfortunately, midway through my first plate I quickly realized that my enjoyment of buffets is a thing of the past. Buffets are good for the variety and quantity, but it always comes at the expense of quality which was lacking at Bacchanal. The more I ate, the faster my initial excitement dissipated. Everything was merely average and no quantity of mediocre food could justify the price tag. If this is the best buffet in Vegas, then I think it's safe to say that dining at Vegas buffets is a thing of the past for me.

One of the more disappointing dining experiences I've had in a long time when thinking about anticipation given Yelp reviews and price of the buffet. Basically cost 60 bucks plus tip for dinner on a Tuesday night. 

There was a wide selection of food items at the buffet but it was all pretty mediocre. There really wasn't a single food item that stood out. Abundance without much quality. I'd say oysters were especially bad in that they were really gritty and meat wasn't separated from the shell indicating some poor shucking. Stone crab and king crab legs were probably best item but not much needs to be done with those in terms of cooking. Also, everyone at the buffet knows these are best selections and the lines for them build quickly.  By 545 wait times for them were around 10 mins.  Dessert section was pretty poor. Crepe station, gelato and a bunch of small cookies/cakes that were all ok. 

Service was also pretty bad even for a buffet. Slow to clear plates and refill drinks. There was some visible disappointment from a surrounding table of the service in terms of complaining. 

Maybe they had an off night. But it was honestly just ok and would probably be 3 stars if it was 30 dollars. But given price very disappointing. Better off opting for one of sit down restaurants in Vegas such as Mesa grill which is steps away but miles away in quality.

This buffet is very good, however, I don't think it warrants it as being #1 on so many Vegas Buffet lists.  It is just as good as the other top tier Vegas Buffets. It's a toss up.   After I've tried everything, the main things I gravitate back to are the ribs, oysters, salmon sashimi, and the creme brulee.

Bacchanal Buffet Review:

Started with General Tso and it was luke warm and ok. Same with beef and broccoli. Both 4 out of 10

Singapore noodles 6 out of 10.

Sushi was fair, a bit too cold. 5.5 out of 10

Meatballs were very good. 9 out of 10

Brisket very good outside in the tips with inside decent. 7.5 out of 10

Turkey was decent 6.5 out of 10. Not the best cut of turkey.

Pizza was good but not special 7.25 out of 10

Wagyu Beef was good 8.5 out of 10

Potato Gnocchi 7 out of 10

Smoked Mussels 9 out of 10

Shrimp 9 out of 10

Desert assortment and selection was excellent 10 out of 10. Dessert taste was 9 out of 10

French Vanilla Gelato  awesome  10 out of 10 

Lava Cake which was great but maybe a bit too rich. 9 out of 10

Peppermint bark, Hazelnut cake, crepe brûlée, lemon tart, matcha cake were good

Croissant, tiramisu, lemon sorbet were just fair.


Summary: My biggest issue at any buffet is selection, food quality and food temperature.

While this was brunch/lunch the selection was very good 8.5 out of 10. Dinner could be different.

Food Quality 8.5 out of 10 

Taste 7.5 out of 10

Food Temperature 4 out of 10 

Atmosphere and Set-Up 8 out of 10

Service 9 out of 10


Overall Grade 8.2

Loved the taco station w/ all the different juices!! The little burgers were specially good. Sushi was surprisingly good and the pat thai too!! All the different types of food was very good... I didn't try the sea food but my husband devoured it., I wouldn't mind coming here but a little over price I would say., $37 for lunch...

Compare to other well-known buffets (Wicked Spoon, Bellagio's buffet, Rio's) in Vegas, Bacchanal buffet is one that has fresh ingredients and executes on an above-average basis.  Which means if you're only there for the crab legs, you'll be disappointed.  But if you're looking to get some seafood, meat, Asian food, Mexican, French, etc - you can't beat Bacchanal. 

The first kudo goes to the juice section, where they offered multiple fresh juices for you to choose from.  I tried the cucumber juice and it was pleasantly refreshing.  

The second kudo goes to the seafood section, where shrimp, fish and countless other items being very fresh.

Lastly the meat section, the prime rib being cooked perfectly, and the jalapeno mango sausages were delicious.

I didn't have very good luck finding a coupon, but it's much more reasonable (price-wise) to go during the week, versus the weekend.  Not to mention the line is much shorter on the weekdays as well.

I'm quite torn between giving this place 3 or 4 stars, what it boils down to is ultimately the question of quality over quantity.

Granted this is a buffet and in Vegas, the sheer quantity of choices and variety dictates who's buffet reigns supreme. What Bacchanal lacks in variety, it makes up for in quality. I had some of the best tasting ramen, Kobe beef burgers, and pastor tacos. These were cooked to order and masterfully crafted to restaurant standards. Sadly though, given the competitions from places such as the Buffet and the Wicked Spoon, I'm not sure if I'll return for more.

For such a high priced buffett, we expected better quality and selection than what was had. The seafood selection and quality  was better at the Wynn.  The crab legs were skimpy and the oysters had too much sand and rocks in them.   Even the meat selections were nothing to brag about.  It wasn't bad, but I'd rather have saved a bunch of money and eaten at the Spice Buffett or at the Wynn. Maybe it was just an off night?

My first Vegas buffet experience--Meh. 

The wait was long and it was $60 freaking dollars. I could go to lunch sushi buffet 4 times with that kind of money where I'm from! 

Best part of the meal was the dessert selection: dessert mochi and tons of mini desserts so you can try a bunch!

There's a ton of food and most of it is good, but the cost wasn't worth it.
I love this Buffet. It's a little pricey, but can we complain? It delievers on damn good food. I hope the their standards stay the same and I'll keep coming.

I wouldnt believe this was real unless I experienced it myself!I stumbled on the best macaroni and cheese I've had so far. Yes, this is a buffet but the food is far from what comes to mind when you think buffet. Nothing but quality and you do pay for it. The price is about 60 per person but well worth it. Nice prime rib, sole, very nicely Cooked lamb chops the list goes on from American, Italian to Asian and every section taste authentic. Im not even going to get into the array of deserts even creme Brulee and some descent Gelato. The oonly  thing I wasn't feeling was that the crab legs were on ice only thats not cool at all but they are already split in half for quick hassle free eating. Overall very nice job caesars! Worth the almost hour wait.
One of the best buffet in vegas. Food is always fresh and good. Have not had anything bad.  Great for dinner and brunch.  Have been more than 20 times this year.  Im a foodie as well as a cook
Not worth for $60, no lobster. They look like have a lot of food, but most of them are cheap food.

Too full to fully enjoy
Overpriced for what u end up eating 
So cold in here to push people out
Idk we lost our waiter
Food was good but not worth the price

My wife and I have been talking about going to the Bacchanal Buffet for 5 years.  We where very excited to finally pull up to the trough on evening of Oct 17, 2018 and mehhh.   It was ok but not what we were lip smack anticipating.  Where not going back. For the premium money that you pay, we recommend that you get  a total rewards card and use the dinner discount that comes with the card to save yourself some money.  Or better yet don't go.  You have other buffet options. Your best value for your dollar is go to Studio B at the M resort.   That where I'm typing this review from right now after we have just finish our $16.99 lunch Buffett.   I might add that there were more dishes at Studio B lunch menu than the Ceasar palace dinner menu.

Loved it. We were there on a Friday afternoon around 2:30pm and there was no wait. The layout was pretty impressive and so was the food. The quality of the food and taste is what I really enjoyed. We wanted to focus on the food so decided not to go for the alcohol package. There was a pretty good layout of salads, Asian, Italian, Cheese, meats, Mexican etc. I loved the Taco bar, the guy made some amazing pork tacos. Last, but not the least the dessert bar. OMG, I really did over indulge and my husband took pictures while I was pigging out. I don't care but it was really good. I do recommend this place if you are in town, but try not to eat anything a couple of hours before you get here so you can have a good apetite. Enjoy!!

Really hyped up buffet - line to pay for entry, line to wait for seating, line to fill your plate... Still in the end, I would do it again.  So much food,  I was too full to have any dessert.  The kicker - Bottemless Mimosas!

SO. MUCH. TASTY. FOOD. 

The line to get in moves very fast. I went with a group, most of whom left because they didn't want to "wait forever".. those of us who remained were inside and seated in less than 10 minutes.

The staff is very friendly and helpful. 

Lots of food of all different cuisines. I was there for lunch and the selection was great.

What to make sure you try: The fruit "juices", especially guava. Delicious.  I also loved the brussel sprouts and scalloped potatoes. The grits were delicious.

What to skip: The baked potato had too much going on (I think it had mayo on it?! along with cheese. too goopy!). The sushi is not impressive or flavorful. The desserts did not impress me at all, sadly; they were dry and flavorless (although I didn't try to gelato! I was too full).

Bacchanal is a favorite. This last experience left little to be desired. 

After we sat, we waited and waited for our waiter to take our drink order. My bf has to take a diabetes medication 15 minutes before eating anything. After waiting for 10 minutes without knowing who our waiter was, I flagged a hostess over and she brought my bf water. She said she let our waiter (Mark) know and he would be coming. Didn't come until 5 minutes later...so it took him 15 minutes to introduce himself and get our drink orders. This buffet has a time 2 hour time limit??? But no time limit for customers to get water or drinks. So we waited another fifteen minutes for his medication to kick in. Mark checked on us once during our entire meal and we didn't get drink refills once during our meal. He walked by our table multiple times and never refilled our drinks. I was so mad, because when I looked around he seemed really helpful to everyone else around. Two couples that sat down after us were served by Mark immediately after they sat down. We complained to the manager (Robert Quintero) who shoo'ed us away with his business card. He told us to email him next time we were coming so he can give us drink coupons/ or front of the line access. Really?!? For $60 per person, I don't want front of the line access. I want them to retrain their staff on customer service. Everyone eating their can obviously afford to eat there, so stop being biased or discriminating. I really wanted to leave Mark a penny for a tip to get my point across. 

Food is still great but if you are expecting customer service to be the same, look elsewhere.

Lots and lots of food! Everyone else pretty much said it all. You really can't eat everything, so really you are over paying and it's better off visiting a nice restaurant in Las Vegas. I did love the fresh carrot and cucumber juice that were in separate glass containers. Everything else was pretty much typical for a buffet minus they did have a taco station which was a little different. Most buffets only have the noodle, meat, and pasta section which this buffet does have as well. It's a great place if you are looking for quantity over quality.

The buffets were the #1 thing I was excited about on my first trip to Vegas. I expected to feel overwhelmed, in the best way possible.  I had watched many Travel Channel specials regarding these buffets, the choices of seafood and meats, and the overall luxuriousness of the experience.  I came in with high expectations. 

This was everything I expected and more.  I had an awesome time.  We came in for breakfast (brunch?) on a Thursday.  The seafood and meat standard fare was there, which was excellent.  Also had a great variety of brunch options such as lobster benedict, ham/egg/cheese crossaints, red velvet french toast, and fresh waffles with all the fixings

Options I did not expect but was pleasantly surprised to see:
-Paella (!!)  
-A full authentic Chinese congee bar with all the traditional toppings.  They even offered chopped century eggs! Whattt.  that was pretty cool
-cold pressed juices

Ended up being about $65 per person but it's well worth it.  Definitely the highlight of my first Vegas trip and can't wait to return.

I heard rumors!   I witnessed the long lines!   I squealed at the prices!   BUT, on this vacation, we finally relented and made the jump to try this famous buffet.   

Since our room was not ready, we were starving, and there was NO line, we were ready to feast on our first meal at this talked about buffet.

The price of $49 was for Sunday brunch, and this price included all you can drink champagne, mimosas, AND bloody mary.   Our server was working extra hard and our glasses were never empty.   The lines for the various food groups did not exceed 2-3 people.  I think it was early in the day so it was certainly the best time to gorge.

Why the lines for the seafood group?    The half sliced crab legs were not worth the wait.  The stone crab claws were plentiful but honestly I've had better.   There was more than enough shrimp so people, no need to get up on my butt so you can scoop up your fare share of shrimp.   

My favorite food section was the Dim Sum and Asian favorites.   The duck and bbq pork were so authentic tasting, I couldn't ask for anything better.   The dim sum was constantly being replenished so the hao gao was always fresh, yes, I had many of those small mouthful of shrimp goodies.  The rice, noodles, and other asian stir-fry exceeded my hungry expectations.  

There was just too much to eat!   I saw an Italian section, a carving station with full on turkey drumsticks, sliders, dips, Charcuterie, pasta, salads, and breakfast items.   

The dessert station is not to be missed.  Despite the over-stuffed belly, I scooted myself over to that dessert world.  There was colorful fudge, candy jars, plenty of cupcakes, cake slices, panna cotta, ice cream sundaes, fruit, and so much more!   SAVE room for this mecca of sweets, it's so worth it!
Fantastic. Everything was amazing, staff was kind and friendly. I loathe buffets but I will go back. Definitely worth the money.
Tried this on my last trip to Vegas and I am looking to go during my current trip. The selection is great and the food is better. Pricey but as they say it's the best buffet on the strip.

SO. GOOD. But definitely a really long line, we waited about 40 minutes at around 1 pm for Sunday Brunch. But oh it was worth it. Even at 42 per person.

Good:
Shrimp & Grits
Dim sum
MELON JUICE (seriously amazing)
Shrimp cocktail: jumbo shrimps
Sausage (when they say spicy they mean SPICY)
Brisket
Waffle fries
FRESH FRUITS (omg the pineapples)
Breakfast pizza: the bf really liked though I thought it was ok
Quail egg with hash (sunny side up)
DESSERTS: There's a chocolate cake-y thing that was really good, there's was a crunch at the bottom that was like chocolate crisp or something and their blood orange gelato was really good too. They also had some sugar free options too though obviously they were a little more bland

Ok:
This sandwich with strawberries, hams, and a sunny side up egg on top (I'm just a sucker for sunny side up eggs)
Sushi was normal though the salmon poke was really good
Broccoli and cheese
Crab legs were a little tasteless and too cold, almost frozen

Unlimited Mimosas

This was my second time doing the Buffet of Buffets pass this year http://www.caesars.com/total/las-vegas/buffet-of-buffets/ and I was excited to learn that Bacchanal was added to the list.

We knew there would probably be a wait for dinner and that it would cost an additional $15 per person beyond the pass price, but figured it was worth a try.

We went on a Sunday night and started waiting in line around 7:30pm, and didn't get in until 9pm...by which point we were starving. [Since they close at 10pm, it was also unclear as to whether we would really get in or not, but it didn't seem like they actually cut anyone off. The cashiers and servers were pleasant, although it took us a long time to get our drinks.]

Despite the massive line and the 90-minute wait, there was a ton of empty tables, which makes me wonder if they're just understaffed/not able to handle the capacity of the restaurant.

The food was okay, nothing to write home about--the sushi looked gross and the selection was not as interesting as some of the other buffets. The most impressive part of it was probably the dessert spread (which we didn't try). I'm not sure what people think is so amazing about it besides the novelty factor.

But the first reason for the 1-star rating is that BOTH of us got sick right after eating there. The only two foods that we both had were the shrimp and the oysters, and we're guessing it's the latter that did it. The second reason for the rating is that we followed up with the restaurant the following morning to report our food poisoning. We started by calling Caesar's corporate customer service, and the lady I spoke with took a report and said she would get back to me in 24-48 hours. Not only did she not get back to me, when I called the same office to follow up after 48 hours, they said that no one there had any recollection of having spoken to me, and that food illnesses have to be reported to a different office anyway (their security department). So, I went through the process all over with them, and then THEY passed on my case to their insurance company (talk about making the customer jump through hoops). Then I had to follow up with insurance on the case--they would not call me. At no point in this process did any of the people I spoke with seem apologetic that we got food poisoning at their buffet, and instead seemed to question whether we really did get sick because of their food. (Which we absolutely did--we were both sick very soon after eating there and did not recover until the following day--totally ruining our plans to go out that night.) Finally, I get a sterile letter from the insurance company saying that Caesar's is in no way at fault for the situation, but that they still hope to see me back.

As if. 

I'm so disappointed with the complete lack of customer service that I don't want to patronize Caesar's again--for ANY of their buffets. It's not worth it spending money at a hotel that can't even apologize for getting their customers sick and ruining their vacation plans. The least they could have done was to refund our money for that meal, especially after all the time I had to spend on the phone with them.

Amazing buffet! Quite expensive so be prepared if you're not looking to drop $100+ for a party of two! There was a large variety to choose from but I'd have to say the asian themed selection was my favorite. Reminds me of how good Studio B at The M used to be. Hopefully they can maintain the high level quality. Will definitely return the next time I'm in town!

I paid $50 to stand in line for 2.5 hrs. for dinner on the day after Christmas.  I was thoroughly disappointed by the variety offered and the taste of the food.  They have different stations offering Chinese, Japanese, American, Mexican, Italian and Seafood.  The Seafood station offered crab legs, raw oysters and shrimp, but you have to stand in line for that.  There was variety, yes, but that doesn't mean they give you the good stuff.  All I remember was the impression I got was they gave me a wide variety of cheap stuff.  I ate mostly American.  I couldn't find mashed potatoes.  The roast beef was chewy even though it was medium rare, but the prime rib was o.k.  The variety of American food was very limited.  The fruits weren't even ripe.  The desserts tasted strange.  Many of the ice cream had peppermint mixed in, and you would never know it since they look like regular ice cream.  I got a chocolate ice cream and ended up not eating it because it had peppermint.  I got the tiramisu and it was very heavy.  The creme brulee had some other flavor in it; can't remember whether it was berry or peppermint; I didn't finish it.  The chocolate creme brulee was so sweet I COULDN'T finish it.  My family has never had so many unfinished items from a buffet (we don't normally waste food).  We are never going back again.  Definitely overpriced.

Can't really complain about the food.  It's one fo the best buffets I've been to.  Note for those wanting crab legs: there's a long line for the cold crab legs on the seafood bar, but go to the Italian section for hot crab legs.  No line there.
It's not bad. It's one of those "do it so you can say you did it" type spots. The food wasn't bad. The dessert bar is the star of the buffet.

I love buffets. I love varieties of food, how much you could eat and pretty much no waiting for food. The bad thing about it, it's gets kinda messy with people being dirty, food isn't fresh, waiting in line to get into the buffet and overeating. Bachanal isn't a bad buffet but i think it's overpriced. They do have other items that other buffets might not have but charging almost 70 dollars not including tip is outrageous. With those prices I rather go to a nicer restaurant. Wait here is also ridiculous. I heard people wait 2-3 hours to eat here. They don't even have a caeser palace hotel guest line. I tried this buffet once and might try it again but I wouldn't recommend it with other options on the Vegas strip

This is my favorite buffet in Vegas.  They have so many options, and nearly all of them are excellent.  I particularly enjoyed the Nutella crepes, the fired rice, and the hot and sour soup, but there are many options. Service was very good.  Curtis, who was handling the made-to-order egg station, was especially helpful, and found an additional ingredient I requested in my omelette, even though it wasn't typically offered and he had to find it in the back and prep it.

I hate buffets, or so I thought! Instead of waiting in line I paid for the line pass and only waited a fraction of the time others did in the general line. Which I think is a great idea; up to you if you'd rather be doing something else besides waiting in line...like getting down with some atypical food offerings!!! Freshly shucked oysters, authentic Latin, Chinese and Japanese cuisine. Carving station was awesome- BBQ chicken, ribs, brisket, prime rib, lamb chops. 
A definite home run!
I'm not coming back anymore. Foods suck!!!! Not going to recommend anyone to come here anymore. Shrimps have no taste, oysters are not fresh, dishes are dirty. SUCK!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This was the best buffett we have ever eaten at and that includes the ones we love at Disney World! There are so many choices of high end foods. We got to sample foods we only see on tv such as elk, lamb, duck, marrow..... and the dessert choices were amazing. It's expensive and the wait can be daunting,  but it's well worth it!!

Well, I came back to this buffet a few months ago. Though it wasn't as good as I remembered it from last year, it was still far superior to any other buffets that I have tried on the Strip. To my knowledge they are the most expensive buffet...nevertheless they are worth it. I think they may be the only ones to still serve Alaskan King Crab legs in addition to snow crab. They also have Jonah crab claws which can fool one into believing they are the much more expensive Florida stone crab claws...don't bother with these as the effort required to break through these shells is not worth the payoff. If you're lazy like me, you'll stick with the easier rewards of the crab legs, which are served chilled. If you prefer them hot, you can request these at the Italian station around the corner in the back (little known fact!)

This buffet has by far the most extensive choices. I thought their soups were particularly well done, as well as some of the Chinese dim sum and congee. I would pass on the Italian and Mexican stations, but partake of the carving station. The spread at the seafood station is great, especially the crab choices and chilled shrimp. Definitely don't miss the huge desert stations... it actually tastes as if they make them on location rather than buy frozen premade generic pastries. 

Now for the bad...unless you go at off times, it is crazy busy. They have a row of electronic kiosks at the entrance. You check in here and you are given a time to come back...to wait in line! But wait...it's apparently exponentially worse on holidays! I thought I was being clever on Xmas Eve...we would come early at 3:45pm so we wouldn't have to wait. What a shock to see the masses already in line...our printout instructed us to come back at 8:20pm. But I was assured by the girl supervising the line that we would only have about an hour wait when we actually got into the line...no problem...we got a snack at the food court, went back to our  hotel room at the Cosmo and showered and packed before returning.

Wow! The place was mobbed like a Justin Bieber concert! OMFG it was seriously crazy! It looked like half if Hong Kong was there! What made it worse was that it was so chaotic. We took our place in line which was no where near the roped section...we were near the doors to the pool...but there was nothing to keep people from just cutting in willy nilly...the girl taking the printouts was all the way up at the kiosks. What total BS! We moved about 10 feet in almost an hour. I checked in with the girl running things and was told that our line would probably be another 2 hours ( yeah right...more like 2 days). A quick bit of math told me that the buffet would be closed by the time we got in...she said they would not kick anyone out...but seriously, are we supposed to believe they would keep freshening food all the way past closing???

What really gets me is the way they price gouge people...first, they bumped the price up to $68 a head from $59 for the holidays...then they offered to let people skip the line for essentially doubling the admission fee, adding anoth $50 per person! Well, we finally gave up. I'm only an ABC...I don't have nearly the tenacity and perseverance of the hordes of foreign national Asians. We ended up eating at the Palm in the Forum Shoppes...a pretty good meal of itself.

The whole experience kind of pissed me off...they should have warned us earlier that it would get crazy like this instead of stringing us along. I intend to get my revenge the next time I'm here by fasting a week beforehand then eating my weight's worth in Alaskan King crab legs! That'll show'em!

Buffet is really not my thing but I have been to many of them and Bacchanal is definitely a quality buffet with a vast selection.  We went around 10:30 and during the course of our meal they were starting to transition to lunch items.  They have all of the usual buffet items for a Vegas "global" theme - carving station with various meats, seafood (shrimp cocktail, mussels, oysters), Asian food (sushi, variety of stir fry, so-so dim sum), desserts galore, Mexican (tacos), breads, charcuterie and so much more.  Beautiful restaurant, service not as good as expected, roughly $30 per adult, I believe.

Out of control buffet. Amazing. I'm from Chicago and we know good but how can you survive a place with crab legs and pizza? Mexican tacos and Kentucky fried chicken and biscuits. It's a food coma. You don't survive it you eat like a degenerate and never mind your self worth and diet that's how. I'll be back. Stay tuned.
Not what I have expected!!!  Their price doesn't justify their selections. They only have a few trays of sushi to say the least.

This is a serious Buffet. I feel you almost need to develop a plan before going. My group I went with could have maximized our experience if we had gone earlier in the day. It was so busy on a Saturday. The Chinese eggplant was good. I honestly could say I tried less than a third of the options then I was full. I wasn't a fan of the seafood it seemed like it had been sitting out for awhile, which is surprising because most people were picking around that area. The decor was very clean. I feel that the price might have been a bit high. I probably would try this again but on a weeknight and go very early. I wouldn't recommend drinking when eating all of this food. One would probably have a disastrous nap.

SO MANY OPTIONS. The wait for dinner was a pain (get their early!!) but food was worth it. Mostly, the desserts stole my heart. They offer so many options, and I wanted to try every single dish but my stomach was about to explode by the end! I have tried almost all their desserts though! Most of them were all super.

YUMMMM. good galore- everywhere! It was my first time experiencing a Las Vegas buffet. They have food from every region of the globe, well almost. They are separated into different sections for easy navigation.

I went for early lunch so the price was around $37 per person which was a good price but as we were leaving the line was super long so just plan accordingly cause it does get packed.

They have a carving station which is great and crab and good seafood! I really enjoyed the paella there as well! The trick is not to fill up on carbs so you won't get to enjoy the other foods too since you would be too full.

Would love to go back.

Price defnitely hits you over the head, but for the quality of food (and if you acknowledge the fact that EVERYTHING has gotten more expensive over the years, and that this is Vegas after all) it really isn't that bad. Currently, it might be the highest-end buffet in Vegas.

The decor is visually jarring (they need to fire their interior designer), and obscures half the buffet line.  But every time you turn a corner, there's more food!  They have a unique approach for some of their items: they give you little finger oven mitts, because some of the foods are already pre-plated (especially stuff like baked pastas or the Asian soups), which seems to be catching on at other buffets as well. Overall, I liked the selection, and ate too much, as usual.

Highlights:
-Dessert selection is hit-or-miss, but during dinner, usually a hit: awesome macarons (they get them from the café adjacent to the front of the buffet), good selection of mocha when they have it, Oreo mousse dome--nom, and on weekends, they have a Japanese Yam/Taro parfait-looking thing that's wonderfully different 
-The sliders--ughhhhh so tasty
-Pesto orecchiette and crab flatbread are definitely the stars of the Italian section

Not-so-great subjective stuff:
-Selection of juices at the start of the line--cucumber juice tastes exactly as it sounds. Which is to say, gross (or "healthy" as my mom puts it).
-Shrimps are huge but relatively flavorless
-Oddly placed decorations; navigating some areas is a mess
-Some foods are hard to get because the serving pot is high while the sneeze guard is too low

If you're a glutton whose standards aren't unreasonably high, you're going to like this place. Bring a wheelchair to roll yourself out post-gorging.

I'll admit that I built up huge anticipation for Bacchanal after reading all the early rave reviews and seeing all the pics from bloggers and yelpers.  I finally got to try it first hand with my recent trip to Vegas.  And I didn't waste any time as it was the first spot I went to after I got off the plane.

Because I wanted to maximize my time and money into trying most of their "500 menu items,"  I invested in a 24 hour Buffet of Buffets pass.  But since Bacchanal is considered to be one of the higher end buffets in the BoB group, you have to pay an upgrade fee of $15 per visit.  You can read about my misunderstanding of that fee from my Buffet of Buffets review here (http://bit.ly/VherAz).  

I visited Bacchanal twice for breakfast and dinner so I paid $15 for both visits in addition to the BoB pass.  Still a deal compared to paying $19.99 for Breakfast and $31.99 for Dinner.

Here are some things that I picked up for breakfast:

Mini Croque Madame, Shrimp & Grits, Bacchanal Benedict
http://bit.ly/11NCfOc
My first round.  Everything you see here was good!

Skirt Steak and Egg
http://bit.ly/UgKPjS
This was good!  But by this time I've already had enough eggs.

Mini Monte Cristo
http://bit.ly/141GjsL
Very rich considering it's size.

Shanghai Dumplings, Smoked Salmon, and Breakfast Pizza. 
http://bit.ly/UOmpgG
I really couldn't get enough of those Shanghai Dumplings.  Pass on the pizza, it was meh.

Chicken Fried Steak
http://bit.ly/UOm6CI
This was yummy!!!  

Red Velvet Pancake
http://bit.ly/V3tQip
Perfect serving size so you wouldn't feel so bloated after.  The pancake was very moist and was spot on with the red velvet

Sugar Free Creme Brulee, Fruit, Cheesecake Lolipop, and regular Creme Brulee
http://bit.ly/Xv8VoK

In addition, though i didn't get a pic of them where their wide selection of freshly squeezed juices.  My faves were the carrot and melon juices.

Here are a few things I picked up for dinner:

Shanghai Dumplings, Kobe Sliders, Kalbi Ribs
http://bit.ly/TedAjm
More dumplings.  The Kobe Sliders were good but a little dry.  And the Kalbi Ribs were awesome!

Al Pastor Tacos
http://bit.ly/UOlJI9
These came from their taco station.  It was like going to your favorite taco truck except you can order as many tacos as you wanted!

Ribeye Steak and Raw Oysters
http://bit.ly/10CehFj
Best finale entree for my time at Bacchanal.  Meat and oysters!!!

Macarons, Mochi, Panna Cotta, and I can't remember but it was good.  LOL
http://bit.ly/Wcxp9x
Best set of desserts to finish off my meal.  Mochi!!!  Seriously!!!

Despite the good selection of food that i picked up, I was a little disappointed because since I dined there on a Wednesday, they held back on a lot of their best stuff for the weekend, which is probably the best time to go if you wanted to try the majority of their "500 food items."

Final verdict:  It's a really good buffet.  Probably one of the better ones on the Strip.  It's on par with the Buffet at the Wynn, not sure if it's better though.  In comparison to Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan, while WS has an awesome Dessert selection, I'd say the edge goes to Bacchanal because they have so much more to offer even during midweek.  Because I'm not a buffet person, I'm not sure when I'd come back, but depending on the situation, if I'm nearby and in the mood for buffet, I would definitely consider dropping by.

The saving grace for this place is it's Kind Crab legs. If that goes away, I would not come here again.

The process to wait is absolutely horrific. They have a "pre-sign up" system and it tells you to come back at a certain time. The time it told my group to come back was in an hour and thirty minutes. I definitely did not expect to be seated immediately at the time the system told me to come back, but I also did not expect an additional 45 minutes to wait to be seated. What is the point of having this system when you're just going to have to wait AGAIN? It makes no sense. 

The rest of the food was not amazing and didn't blow me away to justify the almost 2.5 hour wait.

Completely impressed but the variety of brunch items available here! I mean salmon and lox...YUM! I enjoyed the fresh juices, traditional breakfast items, and the crepe station. I was unimpressed with the lunch items, luckily that wasn't what I came for.

This place was wonderful!!...a lil on the expensive side but worth every penny. I would like to give a special shoutout to the manager Stephanie you have great customer service and a wonderful staff!!!

We thoroughly enjoyed our early dinner at the Bacchanal buffet at Caesars Palace. It was not overly crowded at 3pm so we were able to take our time to taste a little bit of everything. Unfortunately, I felt the crab selection was meh but there were lots of other delicious foods. Surprisingly, I enjoyed the fresh made street tacos the most. The dessert bar was also pretty awesome. It was a good buffet even for the high price.

Everyone I've talked to, including Vegas locals, have told me the same thing. Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas - and for good reason. At about $60/person for dinner (or during holidays $70/person e.g. Father's Day), it's the priciest buffet I've paid for... but worth it.

Be prepared to wait. For some perspective, I came on both a holiday and a non-holiday. On a non-holiday Sunday, you can get a table right away if you come before 5pm. Even the workers will tell you that there's something magical about 5pm... once it hits, a wave of people start coming. On a holiday Saturday, we got a ticket around 4:45pm that put us on a waitlist. We were texted at 5:30pm telling us to come with the ticket. We still had to wait in line for about 1.5 hours before we actually paid and got in. Then, there's more waiting in line to get the popular foods like prime rib and seafood.

That being said, there's an incredible selection of food that seems never-ending. They've got seafood (oyster, crab legs, shrimp, etc), different types of meat (prime rib, wagyu, etc), basic foods (pizza, sliders, calamari), and even an asian section (sushi, pho, dim sum). Honestly, everything is good food here. Some of the dishes here can pass as better dishes than restaurants that actually specialize in those dishes. 

Recommendations:
- Get the boiled crab legs in the back and skip the cold ones up front. The boiled ones have so much more flavor.
- Prime rib - ask for a fatty, medium rare piece
- Save room for dessert. Their dessert crepes are delicious and their gelato was the perfect end to the meal

Bacchanal offers one of the most diverse selections for a buffet.  The new buffet replaces the old Lago buffet of years ago. I heard they spent $17,000,000 to fix up the place and they did well.  It is the strip's biggest buffet with over 500 items to choose from. 

Wagyu beef sliders: very good - soft warm grilled buttered bun, thick juicy flavorful beef, nice presentation. 

Grilled corn on the cob: fresh corn, sweet kernels, lightly seasoned - excellent. 

Shrimp cocktail - firm, fresh, large, deveined, delicious. - the best

Prime rib - good but not tender.  Skip it to save room for other dishes.  Brisket is better than the prime rib.

Tonkotsu ramen - props for just having it.  Broth is not rich - too close to Top Ramen for me.  Skip it.

Dim sum - shu mai is good. Xiaolin bao is good.

Crab legs: you can request the staff at the seafood station to heat them up for you.  They were small and not very sweet.  I would skip. 

Red Velvet pancakes - good but didn't have a different taste than the regular pancakes. They were just a different color and had a different topping.  Waffles are crisp outside and soft inside.  They were delicious. 

Tacos - carne asada was decent. They grill it up on a rotating round grill like at a Mongolian BBQ. 

Sushi- skip it all.  Not that impressed. 

Fresh squeezed juices were good especially the carrot juice. 

Crepes were delicious! 

Dining area has a weird layout.  It is not as easy to navigate as the Wynn Buffet because you are turning corners and avoiding opposing foot traffic.

Service. The staff tries very hard to give you good service.  They seem understaffed because our old plates began stacking up and not collected in a timely manner.  Also finished tables beside us were not bussed for at least 10 minutes. 

Iced tea - Brewed!  Ice is a little cloudy.  I like to see clear cubes served.

Okay yall this buffet is off the hook. I'm talking some good food. Fresh sushi, Fresh crab legs cold or hot! Street tacos of all kinds.. mac n cheese , pasta, and tons of desert!! Down fall Very pricey and a long wait!! But you can grab a ticket and come back ... worth it!!

I've always been very hesitant of all you can eats, because food is always salty, overcooked, or just old. Bacchanal is kn the higher end, but totally worth it! Went with a party of six and got to move to another line, which the wait was way less. For dinner I paid 70 bucks and some change, the most I've ever paid for a buffet. Makes complete sense because the food was amazing! From seafood, to barbecue, you'll find what ever your hearts desire. The dessert bar was my favorite part! Ube ice cream?!!! Ugh so yummy! 
 Service was amazing. Wait staff made sure our table was clean and our drinks always full. 
 Be sure to get some crab legs, prime rib (perfectly cooked), and some bone marrow!
Alvaro is the best waiter ever! This buffet is the best I've ever been to; so much selection of food and it's all tasty.  If you're here, ask for Alvaro to be your waiter!

This isn't your grandmother's smorgasbord......

WHOA - you will be amazed, so many choice and don't forget to see ALL of the buffet, like it goes around the corner!!!

We went early on a Sunday morning and didn't have a wait at all, but by the time we left it was a good 1.5 hour wait, so go early and come VERY hungry.

I love the way the food it set out, like tapas style - 'little plates'.   I'm a Wynn Buffet person and this one is on par.  

This is really a great way to try NEW things.
Place is bomb.com. The manager was great in making the night memorable and our server Michael was exceptional!

Best buffet I've ever been to hands down. I used to think Wicked Spoon was better but I've ate here every time immediately upon arriving to Vegas ever since I've first had it. Seriously, you can't have another buffet after BACHANNAL. You won't like anything else. You WILL be spoiled. Every section of the buffet you will love. Come on an empty stomach, maybe even fast lol. Don't even mind the price. You are absolutely getting what you are paying for.

We came here on a Thursday at 2pm.  I had read horror stories about the lines so I walked by around 1 pm and there was no line.  When we went back to eat at 2 pm, still no line.  When we left around 3pm, still no line.  So either the line stories are exaggerations or we got lucky.  Either way, I'll take it.

Price per person for lunch (with the casino rewards card) = $31.99.  Dinner was $44.99 per person.  We were seated at the same time as one other guy who was dining alone.  What I found interesting is his receipt had "TIP" stamped on it in bold black ink, so I assume he left a tip on his card when he paid.  We didn't.  The hostess sat both of us with one table in between us.  The server came over and looked at his receipt and hardly said a word to him.  She came and looked at our receipt and all of sudden started the spiel about where everything was located, things to look for, and reminded us to save room for dessert.  She was very prompt in refilling drinks and clearing plates.  At the end of course we left a tip, but I kinda wonder if she blew the other guy off because he'd already left a tip whereas she had to work for ours.  Who knows?  Just an interesting observation.

Anyway, on to the important stuff - the food!  We were there for lunch so there's a more limited selection of items but there were still an absolute ton of things to choose from.  We started at the far end at the asian section and worked our way back toward the seafood section (where we stopped because neither of us eat seafood).  My favorite thing in the asian section were the pot stickers.  Crunchy outer shell and very tasty.  In the salad section (yes, I know, who bothers with salad at a buffet?) I found the greek salad to be really good.  I would have eaten more but even I was a little concerned about the fact that I was eating salad at a buffet.  There was a whole section of sliced meats and cheeses that we did not try.  In the Italian section I was disappointed because they were out of the lasagna and I never made it back over there to see if they had made more, but the meatballs were SO good!!  At the Mexican station they will make tacos for you on a rotating grill.  You can have carne asada, pork or chicken.  I liked the chicken best, my husband prefered the pork.  We skipped the breads and soups.  My husband tried the prime rib and enjoyed it.  They had little baskets of fried food - fried chicken, french fries, tater tots, wings, onion rings, etc.  Everything we tried there was good.  On either side of the meat carving station you will find veggies and sides - broccoli, asparagus, mashed potatoes, fingerling potatoes, mac and cheese, etc.  There was honestly only one thing I tried that I did not like and that was the wagyu beef sliders.  The only reason I didn't like them is because they were pretty rare and I just can't handle meat that isn't well done.

Our server wasn't kidding when she said to save room for dessert... man oh man do they make some good crepes!  They make them to order and you can put your own toppings on!  They have a fresh berry mix, strawberries, caramelized bananas, chocolate sauce, caramel sauce, fresh whipped cream, etc.  I almost wish I had started with dessert - the crepe was so good!  They also had mini cupcakes, different types of cakes, cake pops, a chocolate lava cake (yum!), and a bunch of different types of ice cream.  I couldn't try it all and I was so upset with the limitations of my stomach.  

Next time I come to Vegas I will make sure I have a very empty stomach before coming to Bacchanal.  We tried one other buffet while in town, down on Fremont Street.  It was half the price but about 1/16th the quality of food.  My advice is suck it up and pay the money - the food is worth it!
Need I say more? By far the BEST buffet I've been to and as a local if Vegas I must say I've had my share of buffets. Definitely exceeded my expectations!

Dear Reviewers,
This place is crazy! It's phenomenal. The food is super amazing. It was first time here, second time in Vegas, I heard of this place all the time through a lot of friends. They always told me it's very filling has so many options. The only confusing thing is that when you're new, they don't really explain what to do, like do you wait for the waiter first? Or do you just start getting food? But once someone come over it becomes easy, also not to sure if you tip or is it considered rude since it's a buffet that you're spending a lot of money on. But we did tip anyways. Another thing that was a bit weird was the bathroom is outside the place, you have to leave and come back in which is weird because how do they know who is coming and going? But after all that food it doesn't matter about the confusion. This place is so good. I loved all the variety and not so busy. I got a very great deal on Groupon it was 88$ for 2 for brunch and 2 drinks per person alcoholic, and 2 VIP passes. We didn't get the VIP passes I think because it wasn't busy, I heard on a normal day the wait is about 2-3 hours and lines for inside are very long too. The time I went was about 10am to 11am on a Saturday. I heard they only give you 2 hour minimum but once you start eating you get full after 30 minutes. All in all it was an amazing experience and I look forward to maybe trying it again sometime.

We did the dinner buffet around 5pm and there was a short wait (15 minutes). The staff was very friendly and attentive. The food selection was excellent and the food all tasted great! Definitely worth the price.

Probably one of the top 3 buffets on the strip. Selection is amazing and flavorful. Staff are super friendly. Service is top notch, as you expect for the price you spend. Not cheap but it is a quality dining experience.

Meh.
Honestly, the meal was OK, but the price made it go down a star. Epic feast? More like epic bill! $50.98 per person plus tax and tip, more than $120 for two people. Not out of the ordinary for a meal in Vegas, but the food just wasn't that good. I guess it's the same for all great buffets, they can't stay that great forever.

What was good:
Shrimp cocktail--the shrimp was perfectly cooked and were huge.
Lamb chops--very tender, not much fat and also perfectly cooked.
The guy in charge of the carving station--I think his name is David. He's a very friendly tall black guy and he's always smiling. Seriously, he was the only employee that I saw smiling.
Leek dumplings--not the best but man was I craving Chinese food.
Buffalo wings--great, with a crunchy skin but where was the bleu cheese?
Creme brule and tiramisu--perfect.

And that's pretty much it.

What I didn't care for:
Oysters-- huge pile of oysters but the guys didn't know how to shuck them. Every single one I got had pieces of shell in them, and they didn't sever the lower abductor muscle.
Prime rib--pretty bland, overcooked.
Sushi--blah, poke was chewy
Oyster shooters--obv the dead ones went in here.
Maccarons--the best tasting one (salted caramel) was dry and chewy. The other flavors had nice texture, yet I didn't like the flavors.
Lava cake--had no lava

I noticed several times our plates were not cleared when we returned, and it was not busy. We actually had no line when we got there bc we missed lunch by 15 mins so we paid the dinner price at 3:15pm. The hostess made us wait for about 10 mins before we were seated and there were several empty table. The little rubber things they give you to hold the plates were unnecessary, seeing as hot the plates were not even hot enough to keep the food warm by the time we got back to our table.

The fruit section was pretty much non existent. Only watermelon, pineapple, and cantaloupe. I def missed the strawberries, not even any in the dessert section covered in chocolate.

I just can't help but compare this place with the buffet at M Resort. It's so much cheaper there, the food quality has been very consistent in the four or so years I've been going there, AND there's free beer and wine there too!

The food here was AMAZING! So many wonderful options to choose from. This was not your ordinary buffet. We paid $65 per person but it was totally worth every penny. The buffet area was never ending with so many tasteful options to choose from. The crablegs were my favorite. They were cooked to perfection and so delicious. I cannot wait for my next trip to Vegas to eat here again!

Hands down.. Best Buffet EVER!!!!  Everything was on point!!  From the seafood, steaks, asian; and not to mention.. DESSERTS!!!  Better than Wicked Spoon, Wynn's Buffet and Bellagio's Buffet... This is a MUST GO!

We went around 3pm and the wait was approximately 30 mins... Not too bad
Food was ok but the service was horrible! There are way better buffets in Las Vegas! We had to pay 18% gratuity even though we had no real service. The managers are rude and not a help!

Horrible and dishonest service! I ate here before
and decided to come back.The wait time to get 
seated was 2 hours. After giving my cell phone 
I was texted confirmation with the expected seating time, 
130 min later. When I finally showed up, I was told to 
wait in the line for another 1 hour. Seriously!

After speaking to the manager, it became apparent that 
this is just how it is, and they make it a policy. 
If you are not from the US and this is the first time 
you are going to all you can eat buffet, I suppose any 
wait is fine. For the rest if us, service is also important. 

Horrible-will not go back.

I am HUGE FAN!! Who cares if its pricey.. it totally worth it. First place and last place we hit up when in LV. The breakfast is awesome! Mexican flavors on point. The dinner is wonderful as well. This place is a buffet experience that wont disappoint. Try the salsas. Try the seafood (the mussels are amazing). The meat. The dim sum. The pasta. The sushi. Take your time and enjoy!!! Bacchanal is for lovers.. Food Lovers!
Not worth the money. Lamb rack too sweet, too much alcohol in obster chowder. This is what happens when there's over crowded people in the restaurant that quality suffers.

This place is the bomb! Apparently they spent major bucks to build this elaborate buffet inside Caesar's Palace, so believe me when I say...absolutely no expense was spared! I haven't been to many buffets in my lifetime, but this was by far the nicest one I've ever been to.

The wait is ridiculously long, so be prepared to wait! You first have to sign up on a computer, where you can input a cell phone number to receive a text. You then receive a ticket that tells you approximately how long your wait will be. Finally, once you receive a text, you then have to wait in another line before you can finally pay and get seated. When my husband and I came here around the holiday season, we had to wait an astonishing four hours!!! But man, it was totally worth it!

Believe me when I say they have an insane amount of variety here! They literally have every type of cuisine you can possibly imagine - and all of their dishes are well-prepared and thoughtfully presented. I especially enjoyed their boiled king crab legs (most places only serve them cold), lamb chop lollipops, fresh agua frescas in glass bottles, fancy nachos in mini roasting pans, noodle station (pho, ramen, udon, etc.), dim sum, crepes, mini desserts, sliders, curly fries, etc. 

I won't lie - I literally ate like 10 plates when I came here. I figure you might as well get your time and money's worth, considering the wait is so long and the pricing is so high! FYI, they do have a two hour limit, though...so unfortunately you can't hang out there all day, despite how tempting it would be to do so! Yeah, it's no wonder Bacchanal is rated the #1 buffet in Vegas!!!

Visited in January and April, 2013. Twice for dinner and once for breakfast. The only knock I would give it (once you consider you don't mind the price), is the ambiance. It's not the quietest of settings and tables a little close together.  As far as the food goes, it's very, very good. Shrimp are excellent. Lamb chops at the carving station fantastic. And essentially so is everything else including desserts. We chose to have early dinners, so never a line. I recommend this buffet above all others.

A bit pricey and very long waiting lines, an hour and a half. I noticed a line for casino players, who walked right in and made us wait longer. 
I was not impressed with the food, for the price. 
The floor was wet and I almost fell.
The Aria buffet is a better deal.

Eating at Bacchanal is like running a marathon with a free-for-all route: you have to not only pace yourself well, but also be meticulously selective about every cc of your stomach space. 

TL;DR most important tips:
*Scout the terrain before you start getting food. A lot of yummy-looking food is near the front, but you don't want to stuff yourself with red velvet pancakes and missing out on the truffle scalloped potatoes
*Think twice about what you get. The fried chicken and waffle fries in the mini fryer basket looks extremely photogenic, but lobster bisque is a far better use of your calorie allowance
*Go with a group so you can share food. Although items are already in small portions, you can try more stuff with bite-sized sampling (and get seconds accordingly!)

We came for brunch, which was a hefty $54 (sans drinks). It costs quite a bit more than the other big fancy buffets at the Strip, but Bacchanal does feature excellent quality and variety. A lifehack that some people use is to come in the middle of the afternoon so they can get the dinner food at lunch prices. 

(++) Favorites: 
- Lobsta bisque (you can really taste the lobster!)
- Paella (good flavor and juicy shrimp)
- Truffle scalloped potatoes (almost tastes like mac n cheese, except with more intriguing texture and aromatic truffle-ness)
- Anything pasta (creative pasta dishes, exceeded my expectations. I liked the giant ravioli and gemelli pastas)

(+) Recommended:
- Steak n eggs (really good steak and nice runny egg)
- Crab Benedict (a tasty way to enjoy crab if you don't like peeling the crab legs like me)
- Salads (given the scarcity of vegetables in Vegas)
- Siu mai (Chinese food isn't the first thing to cross my mind at Bacchanal, but this is conveniently bite-sized and appears made from scratch)
- Juice (usually not a fan, but it was fresh and there was a unique selection including watermelon)
- Lava cake (it's even kept heated)

(-) Pass:
- Fried chicken & waffle fries (nothing special; and yes, I did fall for the presentation)
- Red velvet pancakes (yes I fell for the presentation again)
- Desserts in general (too sweet in my opinion and nothing mind-blowing)

Service was great too; all the food is constantly refilled and the staff are very nice about helping you clear the plates. This is one of the few buffets where you can plow through endless plates, yet still feel classy.

The verdict? Worth it at least once for the experience. Despite its location in Caesar's Palace, I'm not even sure if Caesar himself typically ate this grandly.
Food is descent, but review is for service. The service is horrible. My first 1 star review out of 80 reviews. They do not know how to accommodate.

Absolutely one Devine place. So much food!! Be prepared to eat ALOT to get your money's worth. $70 dollars per person is not cheap! Great atmosphere, tons of food to choose from! Desserts were great, I ate so much macaroon this lady kept looking at me haha. Next time in Vegas I'll probably try somewhere else and use it as a comparison to this place.

Another buffet disappointment added to my list. Scallops on the shell and miso sea bass were overcooked. Clams and crawfish were previously frozen and not fresh. I'm not a fan and of snow crab legs but my 9 year old liked them. The dessert was definitely meh...didn't know flan could have a gummy texture. The gelato was icy and the green tea opera cake was mushy. The only decent desserts were the creme brûlée and mocha dome cake. I did enjoy the charcuterie which are a must and their rack of lamb chops were moist and flavorful (but make sure to get a thicker one). But the prime rib lacked good flavor and the au jus tasted just like watered down beef stock. The soup base for pho and udon were light and clean but not much to write her me about.  

All in all, a huge disappointment for being the best buffet in town, especially for $55/person not including tax and tip. Next time, I'll skip the dinner buffets and save my pocketbook for a nice meal at a real restaurant instead.

we decided to try the Bacchanal buffet since we had heard so much about it and we were going to see Absinthe (GREAT) later that night.

got there around 730, they told us it would be about 45mins-1hr wait....for a buffet???

in any case, they had an option for 25/each to go to the head of the line....went this route

it did look impressive, and we took a few minutes to take a look around

maybe from all the write ups, our expectations were a bit too high, this was bottom line, a buffet after all....

we tried quite a few things, with the lamb chops and crab legs being the better among the choices. some of the items seemed to have been sitting out a bit too long and were dry
the sea bass was among these, tasty but you could tell had been sitting for some time
the sushi was just ho-hum, nothing special and the pizzas just so-so
some of the Asian dishes surprised me, dim sum for dinner? chicken feet?....I do like these, but for dinner?

we probably should have started with the desserts, as they had quite a few choices and were among some of the better offerings.  do try the passion fruit tart, as we have not found many pastry chefs able to fully utilize this fruit properly in a dessert....they did a good job here though.

not a whole lot more to say about this place other than being a decent buffet
haven't tried wicked spoon yet, but I would say the buffet at the Wynn or Belagio better, and a bit cheaper
haven't been there in years, but I remember the Sterling brunch at Ballys still being amoung the best....a bit more costly, but I think with out head of line fee, close to same price

guess we should have kept our expectations realistic, this is still a buffet bottom line

......show more than made up for it later though!!!!

Been wanting to try Bachannal since it opened a couple of months ago.  Came here with my family over the Thanksgiving holiday.  We waited in line for 4 hours!!!!!  Personally, I don't think it's worth the wait.  If we had waited for 20 minutes, I would have given it 4 stars!  I think the only difference between this buffet and others (Wynn, Bellagio) is that they boil the crab legs so it's nice and piping hot!  Also, the crepe station is different.  You can also have your choice of caramel, nutella and chocolate topping. Other than the crab legs and crepes, everything else is pretty much in line with other buffets.

Oh the variety of gelato they offer is a nice touch too.  Try the fig + basil and blood orange flavor.  

One thing we noticed is the techno music that was consistently playing.  That's a sure way to get us to eat quickly and get out.  They need to change to better soothing music.  Also, interior is cold and contemporary decor.  Would I come back? Probably not - you'll find me at the Wynn buffet next time ;)

So I went to the Bacchanal Buffet to try some "high class" food that I don't usually have. I went to the dumpling section and picked out some dim sum. Usually, I'm a dim sum lover. I often go to dim sum places in SoCal with my sister so I know how dumplings are supposed to look and taste like. When I bit into this particular one, the pork filling was undercooked and still pink. BE AWARE! Next to it is the business card of the general manager, the shift manager tonight was Fred. If anything happens to us (my sister ate one too), how am I suppose to finish my trip?!?

Hands down the best buffet in vegas strip. It is expensive but there is so many options here its worth it to try it. There is seafood section, american section, asian section, mexican food, and a whole separate section for dessert. I like the presentation of the food and how some comes in cute plates.
