The only complaint is it takes up a good portion of your plate. the sushi here is actually decent and is a great cut. 

Ramen and PHO section: choose the ramen over the pho. 
Asian section: all good!!! they had dim sum, fried rice, noodles, and congee
(porridge). 
Dessert: they had limitless macrons, but not as good as it looks. The only thing i like at the dessert section is the gelato balsamic with fig, sounds weird but its good. 
Waiting in line here was definitely gonna be the most annoying part for people. I heard if you pay 10 bucks you can be in like a fast line. So come early and try the buffet. I think its worth trying if you are here in vegas.

An abundance of food.  About the only thing that they don't have (we went for dinner) was lobster and steak although they had all kinds of other seafood and lots of other kinds of meat. And a lot of different kinds of food.  We went around 4:45pm so there was a very short line.

The good: excellent red curry coconut mussels.  And the prime rib was tender and juicy.   Chinese steamed dumplings were really good, too.  Cheesecake pops were awesome.

The bad: fake/instant mashed potatoes?  Really?  That's why three stars instead of four.  Also, the lamb chops were disappointingly dry.  And the gelato was relatively melted/soft.

As for crab legs, look for the area where they steam 'em hot for you rather than getting the cold kind.

Editorial comment:  why in the world do people put so much food on their plate?  You walk around and see all of the wasted food.  What a shame.  People: you can always go back for more.  Your eyes are bigger than your stomach.

The meal is not over when your full. The meal is over when you hate yourself. 

Note: When you get the Tri-tip ask the cook to throw it on the grill for a minute. 

Pros:
Great selection, good service (if you are nice and friendly they are nice and friendly plain and simply).
I had a few special request and they took care of me.
The Boba Drink was good.

Cons:
Long line. If your a light eater then buffet may not be for you.

I went here yesterday for lunch with family
I loved their food/service/environment. Coffee tastes great after a meal here!

Even Caesar would have gone elsewhere. 

This spectacular sideshow of decorative excess is an overpriced ruse that will serve to disappoint your palate and only raise the cost threshold for all the other quality buffets in town. During my recent stay, I had a better quality buffet experiences at the Wynn, and even the Mirage (obviously less sparkly and new) than I did for my 70 dollar weekend dinner at this buffet. You're paying for the lavish settings, not an exceptional dining experience beyond comparison. But let's not be fooled. Lipstick can always be placed on a pig. But you're still in Vegas, standing in a line, shoveling food on your plate with the same folks who'll be back in line with you at Walmart on Monday morning. This isn't Cipriani and this isn't a good use of your money. Save your dollars, skip the mediocre customer service, the Disneyland-like lines, and fill your gullet elsewhere. 

Specific disappointments beyond price:
Dirty plates never collected
All red meat options were beyond dry
Very limited side options, nothing green
Poor soft drink selection

Highlights:
Dessert offerings, but not on par with Wynn
Vermont Mac n' Cheese

Edited review... 

Went two weeks ago.  Had some issues.  The manager reached out and offered to correct the issues.  I gave the buffet another shot and I'm happy to update to five star.  The food is above average.  The service is great.   The price is high but you get the quality that comes with a higher price tag.  

For the price it's worth it.  However it means a lot that a manager would take the time to reach out to me and resolve the issues I had.  That goes a long way.  

I now rave about this buffet and will happily return again soon.  Great food and nice atmosphere.

Since my family and I were in Vegas, we wanted to do at least one buffet while we were here, and found this place on Yelp with rave reviews.  We knew that there'd be a long wait, but of course, it's one of those things that you don't really get how long until you've actually waited.

We got here a little passed 5:00p on a Saturday because Caesar's Palace is so stinking huge.  How can people stay here and not get lost?  Anyways, someone said that we're lucky because the wait is only about 2~2-1/2 hours at the time.  Wait, what?  *cleans ears out*  ONLY?  But hey, it's 5:00ish, we can wait until 7:30ish, which isn't too bad.

The result: HOLY CRAP it took us THREE freaking hours just to get to the cashier, and another 30 minutes to get seated (we were a party of 8, so the 30-minute wait may vary if you have a smaller party)!  On top of that, dinner was $51.99 per person and kids 8 and under $26.99, PLUS parties of 8+ get charged a 15% gratuity fee!  "Money, money, money, must be funny, in the rich man's world."

The food, though, IS good.  Okay, it's more like it'd better be good for $51.99 a pop AND 3-1/2 hours of painstakingly herding like cows.  Let's see, there was a Chinese station, a Japanese station, a Mexican station, a salad station, a pasta/pizza station, a salami and cheese station, an American station, a seafood station (the line is longer here), a dessert station...that's all I remember.  The entire buffet area was so ginormous and the selection extensive that I don't think I visited every nook and cranny (besides, after the long wait, I didn't have the energy to explore).  I was actually impressed that none of the food I've tasted were dry/overcooked, and there were plenty of people working the stations to keep the food in check.

My favorites were the sliders (wagyu beef, people), crab legs (get the freshly boiled ones), salmon, sweet potato tater tots, acini di pepe pasta salad, pumpkin soup (in an actual pumpkin)...damn it, I wasn't even drinking, yet I can't remember everything.  The dessert station was the highlight IMO.  Crepes made on the spot - dollop with fresh whipped cream, drizzle with raspberry AND chocolate sauce, sprinkle with fresh blueberries and strawberries...ohhh yeahhh.  Loved the sorbets too (especially the blood orange and watermelon mint).

So, this was definitely an experience to brag about and recommend that everyone should eat here at least once, but I wouldn't say it's worth the wait and price (especially if you have kids) to come back for another round unless you live the high life.

Don't waste your money and time at this buffet. The bone marrow was dry, lamb was rough, the oysters were warm (how they washed it looked unsanitary). 
The restaurant is also very dark and you can barely see what you're eating or where your table is.

Also, the restaurant is too busy seating people and they don't even bother cleaning up the empty plates. Too many customers, lack of employees. 

They even charged 45 dollars extra for the Express pass which I am unfortunately regretting. 

I'd rather spend my money at the Wynn buffet. Much cleaner and variety of food unlike this place.

Fist I have eaten here about 5 times.  I am always pleased by the quality.  The selection is unreal.   So many different types of dishes.  Blows away other buffets.  Sushi was cut perfect with a delicate touch.  The blue claw and King crab legs were beautiful.  Even the simplistic slider was cooked medium and flavorful.  Cheese selection, Asian, meats all great.  And the finally, the pastries, dipped strawberries in chocolate and passionfruit caviar along withy the fresh crepes station.  So many selections.
Felt like I was in a dystopian sci if movie, filling me with fear and dread for the human race, which is precisely what I wanted out of a Las Vegas buffet.

Was pretty impressed with this buffet! We were really sold on doing this one because the wait wasn't too bad, especially for a Sunday morning! All the food was pretty good, they keep the buffet very well stocked and clean. The service was good as well. 

The inside can be a bit confusing to navigate because the individual sections are not labeled, I kept finding myself getting lost! The deserts were so good!! There's plenty of stuff for everyone here. I strongly recommend this one if you're looking for a Vegas buffet, especially if the line isn't too bad!

Shockingly mediocre. This was the only buffet I tried during my last trip to Vegas. We came here on a Saturday evening and were seated at about 8:30pm and it felt like nothing but leftovers. The line was long, the place was packed so I would have assumed the food would be fresh but almost none of it was. 

After so many rave reviews, I was really surprised at how dry and stale a majority of the food seemed to be, and how disorganized/flustered the staff was. The lamb at the carving station was quite good but I was unable to get another serving b/c they were perpetually "cooking another batch". The seafood station was a completely mess and the crab legs were partially steamed and partially cold, on the same serving tray. Eventually the staff stopped restocking it and just handed plates with a few crab legs and a lot of water to guests.

I had hoped for a better experience but all in all I just don't think I'll give this one another try. It absolutely could have been an off night but forking over $70+ per person for that experience (it was a holiday) was enough for me to skip this entirely during my next visit.
The quality of the food was average. For the service and price and wait that you get, I rather go to a lower priced buffet.

Lily and Delroy were amazing. Lili was our server, and she took great care of us. She never stopped smiling even when she got sat with 6 tables, and delroy was amazing and patient. He allowed me to try every flavor of gelato while also taking care of other guests. Overall it was a fantastic experience.
Perfect food with highest freshness. I'm sure that its the best buffets in Vegas, Bang for the bulk!

Yes this is a pricy buffet, but it's so worth it! So much variety. Sometimes I forgot I was at a buffet while interacting with the staff at the food bars, because everyone was so friendly, helpful, and courteous! There was ceviche, crab legs, a meat cutter asking how you'd like your meat, and a plethora of desserts!!! It's a high price, but I'll definitely be back.
This is a "must-see" buffet. Food was delicious. Service was also wonderful. Can't wait to visit it in the future

Food was good BUT beware of the random pricing they have. We went for dinner on Monday night, so to be sure I called on the day before AND emailed to get responses that the price for the Monday dinner was $44.99 and it WAS NOT going to be holiday pricing, only to be charged holiday pricing for Monday! I've since called and have been transferred around for the last hour to no avail. Do you seriously not know your pricing the day before and would quote incorrect pricing to bait and switch someone? We would've eaten dinner on Christmas eve if it was the same price, but we changed our schedule to save $10 a person X 8 people plus tax and gratuity that adds up. Horrible customer service in trying to resolve this!

You know when you get all amped up to go to one of the all you can eat lobster feasts in Orlando and when you are done wonder why I wasted $50 on a so-so buffet?  With my first (and probably last) visit to the Bacchanal, I am thinking the same.  While the food was actually quite good, it definitely wasn't worth the $50.  Not much selection, "hot" crab legs were lukewarm, two full stations with Asian offerings limiting variety of rest of buffet, dessert bar smaller than most other buffets I have experienced, and the traffic flow was confusing.  I have experienced better in other Midwest and southern casinos.  If this is the best Las Vegas has to offer, the reviewers must not travel extensively.  It was ok but I would not go out of my way to eat there again.  Noticed that not much of a line and no wait at 5:30.

Went here for dinner and the price was around $55 w tax per person.  It's pricey but I would pay the extra $16 compared to the buffet at MGM.  They have a great meat selection, brisket, ribs, prime rib, sausage and more. All of it was very tender, no tough chews.   They have oysters but they weren't tasty at all.  I say it's worth a try if you been to the Bellagio or Wynn already.  If you haven't I would just go pick the lowest price one out of the three for dinner.  Bellagio for sure for lunch.

The only buffet to go to in Vegas. Given the volume of people you'd expect below par service but it's the opposite.  Attendants are their to clear your table in a New York minute and v they can get food for you if the line towards what you want gets too long.  Be prepared to give an appropriate top for that though.  The food never fails to disappoint whenever we're there. Great selection.  The Chinese could do a bit better but it's sufficient given the numerous choices of entrees.  Be ready to gain lots of pounds.

If you want a lot of selection of below mediocre and overpriced food, this is the place for you. Came here for the brunch on a Tuesday. 10am, no line. Got some breakfast items and some items as they were transitioning to lunch. Pls, just walk 15 min to the Cosmo for the wicked spoon instead. Their food was more interesting and cheaper! Don't waste your time. Ceasar would have given baka a thumbs down. They need to close down and repent.

My first time! Came with my parents to foot the bill haha. I have had all the nice buffets: Bellagio, Wynn, Wicked Spoon, and other lesser ones like the Mirage and Rio. Bellagio used to be my favorite but I think Bacchanal has surpassed it. Each buffet has its signature qualities like the Wynn is known for desserts, Bellagio for seafood. Bacchanal had an amazing gourmet selection of all kinds of foods, everything was meticulously prepared and presented. 

Pros:
Seafood was fresh, esp the oysters and the king crab legs. Ceviche could use some work though.
The Mexican drinks at the Mexican bar!
The LAMB LEG was SO GOODD
Chocolate filled Beignets (I took the last one and it was like 9pm...) 
Gelato selection! Even mochi ice cream!
Lava cake was actually lava. But they don't serve it in ramekins anymore...
Brussels sprouts!
Veggie cup
Cold cut selection!

Cons:
Everything beef. The prime rib was dry and unjuicy. The wagyu beef burger was blech, with a terrible dried bun. The meatball was cold and blah. 

It is expensive, but the selection and quality of the food makes up for it compared to the other buffets.

Horrible!!! I'm now suffering from food poisoning ! 

To start off I actually liked some of the food, though some of it was way too salty! And the variety isn't all what it's cracked up to be... Well now thanks to this place I'm very ill... I promise this is the source of my sickness bc this is the only food I've eaten all day....

$48+ for brunch on a Saturday.  about an hour wait.  they text you a little before your table is ready, so you can gamble while you wait.  that's about the only plus about bacchanal.

the food was such a let down.  yes, there was a large variety, but nothing stood out about any of it.  i tried a little bit of everything hoping to something that blew my mind, but nadas.  

wicked spoon trumps this buffet any day.  the green tea creme brule was the only thing i ate all of. 

service was good, though we did have to track down our servers a few times for refills.  honestly, for 50 bucks i'd much rather go to a different buffet.

My husband and I have been wanting to try Bacchanal for quite some time now to see how it compares to some of the other top notch Vegas buffets such as Wynn and Aria. So we ate here for breakfast during are recent trip. It is pricey ($48 per person for breakfast), and for that amount, you expect high quality. That is exactly what we found.

The interior is beautifully decorated with modern glass fixtures and clean lines. Seating is spaced out in many different areas, as it is a very large buffet. You can find a variety of foods to choose from such as Asian, Mexican, American, Italian... all offering their finest breakfast staples. Everything was extremely fresh and tasty. My favorite station was the homemade desserts, which offered things like crepes made to order, gelato made on site, and lots of other tasty treats.

Overall, I enjoyed my visit. However, I still feel like Aria is numero uno, and just a bit less expensive, so I would rather spend my money on breakfast, lunch, or dinner there.
Very disappointed because a couple of our choices were extremely SALTY. Some were really good but I think having like 3 of our choices inedibly salty is not just a mistake for the day.

Okay, first things first - I'm not a big buffet person. I know, I know, that's practically sacrilegious here in Vegas but I just typically feel that buffets are more about quantity versus quality and I want GOOD food not just lots of stuff.

Then I discovered Bacchanal. The options are practically endless but everything is actually delicious, too, and that rocks my socks.

From the lamb to the carved-to-order BBQ to the crab legs (available cold and warm, dontcha know) and cocktail shrimp, everything is on point. There's sushi, tons of prepped salads, pasta, charcuterie, and a large Asian foods section that includes DIY pho and lots of steamed buns - the taro are SO GOOD. 

Is it pricey? Yeah, but you're getting surf and turf with all the trimmings plus dessert for less than a solo steak anywhere nearby. I like it. Just please leave me some taro buns.

Btw - yes, there can be a wait, but if you have a Diamond card or above you can skip the line and it moves pretty fast anyway. Or just get a ticket from the kiosk and go have a pre-dinner cocktail somewhere else. It'll all be okay once you have some crab in your mouth, promise!
For $53+T&T per head, this place is definitely not worth it! Buffet @ this price should have lobster!
My favorite buffet. Lots of variety! More on the expensive side but very well worth it!

Do not, by all means, pay $60 for the Dinner At All..! This place is completely overrated and not worth the price. I read mixed reviews and had this intuition that it will be mediocre and those are the people who know food and can taste the difference between quality and quantity. Needless to say, they are right, to begin with. The variety was good but the taste was not all that. It is 3-stars at best. I only enjoyed the Salmon and the small basic stuff you can get at any buffet place. If you are craving a buffet than I highly suggest you go to the Wicked Spoon that will have the same thing here and may be a lot more and less in price. Also, their Desert Station is the worst. If you have a good palate than you are able to identify that its done using short-cut methods and with cheap ingredients. I was a bit disappointed but I was able to come during the lunch period and not had to pay the $60 thank god!

Yes it's $50 a head which i thought was a bit high for a buffet but this was NOT a typical buffet, filled mostly with things you don't like and where just "ok."

EVERYTHING WAS PERFECT.

Pretty much every single thing I had, which was plenty but not even close to everything, was fantastic. I am very cheap with my $$ for food and not a big fan of buffets because i never feel like i get what i paid for. With this place i thought it was a bargain!

You can easily eat more than $50 worth of food at this place. It's Las Vegas, WE PAID $59 for four shots and two beers at the MGM bar.

So the price is actually low for what you get, i ate way more than $50 worth of food for las vegas prices.

This is now a must do. You will be very happy you made the choice to stuff yourself with great food.....you wont even feel bad or hate yourself later because the quality is high.

Loved it, cant wait to go again!

Long wait in line, otherwise excellent buffet

Came here for the Christmas Eve buffet. Very pleased with buffet spread. The festive menu came with all you can eat whole lobster which was decent. Tried a few buffets on the Strip but nothing came close to this. Then again this cost a lot more than the ones at Aria, Cosmopolitan ( Wicked Spoon), Bellagio and Wynn. My tip is to take a ticket and take a wander. My wait time was for 4hrs 45 mins so am glad I took a ticket first. Got ticket at 4, finally seated by 9.30pm as there's another line to be seated. Queue to pay was an hour from the entry point. It was a scene of disgrace. Ppl were sitting on the floor, children were crying and noted an altercation as ppl in line felt others were moving too slowly.  Staff could've handled this better by offering drinks to those who were exhausted and for the bigger and more long term solution, expand place to include more tables. 

Once inside, buffet includes all non-alcoholic drinks and all the stuff you can find on the spread. My favs are the prime rib, wagyu beef, shrimp and strangely the noodles which are made on the spot! Desserts are pretty decent too but leave enough room for it as I've seen madness on the Alaskan crab legs (some ppl think they can eat the value of their buffet or bankrupt Bacchanal by downing on the legs!). 

Go for variety not big on one thing and miss out on the other great things.

I came to this place for dinner buffet over labor day weekend wtih my family and everything was delicious!  I had been to other buffets in Vegas but it was my first time here.  The others I had been to were okay, nothing amazing, but I will definitely say that this one is now at the top of my list.  

Surprisingly, we arrived at 7pm on a Friday (of a holiday weekend) and only had to wait 25-30 minutes to get seated.  That was awesome because I was STARVING.  Upon walking inside, I was already overwhelmed by all the different food options.  I ended up trying as much as I could and honestly liked pretty much everything I tried.  They have a huge range of things to choose from- soups, sushi, tacos, oysters, crab legs, fish, meats, etc.  I personally tried a few of the chef special hot dishes and liked them a lot (although I don't know what they actually were).  The ox tail soup they had was also perfection, along with the mushroom truffle soup.  Aside from the main options, they also had a humongous assortment of dessert- macarons, cakes, pastries, crepes made to order, and gelato!  I ended up sharing with my brother and essentially trying a bite of everything.  I'd definitely recommend doing this if you have expand your stomach enough to do so ;).

In the end, I walked away feeling super full and regretting my life decisions (like eating that last mousse, or going to buffets in general)... but after recovering from that, I'd definitely go again because I just can't pass up all the deliciousness that is there :P.  This is most definitely my favorite buffet on the strip.

There are basically not enough stomaches in the world to prepare you for this meal. Let me just say, do not eat anything all day, or do the brunch and have this be the first thing that you eat because it will be the only thing you need to eat for the next 8 hours. Also be prepared to be eating for a good 3 hrs. There is so much here that you will tell yourself you won't be there long but guess what, they have different foods come out at certain times and BAM you won't be able to leave. You probably think that because of all the food and all the people that come here that the quality will be shit. This is not the case at all, the food quality was better than I imagined it. This buffet is one of the pricey one but well worth the money. I wouldn't go to any of the other buffets after this. I wish I could put into words how big this buffet is. It is like steping into 4 restaurants all at the same time. The meat here is so good and cooked at perfect temperatures and is never try. My favorite was the Prime Rib. It just melted in my mouth and so did the brisket. It was full of flavor and felt like I ordered it from a BBQ place. There was an asian area where they were serving dim sum and I was in heaven. They had a hot and sour soup there and it was to die for. The workers were busy like ants just constantly moving and replacing everything like a well oiled machine. The seafood area was the busiest. Here you could get all the crab legs you want and they are half shelled for you so there isn't any work trying to get the meat. They had a wonderful oyster shooter that was soaking in a cucumber watercress juice which i loved. At 3pm they brought out oysters on a half shell and I was so happy at this point. The desserts were crazy. So many cakes and gellatos. They had an gellato sandwich that used donuts as the bread. And get the asian 5 spiced cake so effing good. And the mimosas kept coming. I dont know if it was our server but she made sure my glass was never empty I ate so much I didn't need to eat the rest of the day. Never have I felt to gluttonous but if there was a place to do it it would be at ceasers palace in the Bacchanal Buffet.

you have to at least try this place once in your life.

The buffet was amazing! We came here for the weekend as it was my boyfriends birthday and he was andament about going to a buffet and with so many to choose from in Vegas it can be hard to pick the right one and not waste money. The buffet was awesome, the food we awesome, customer service was cool overall we had a great meal and was worth every dollar. I do recommend looking on living social and groupon for coupons

This place deserves a solid 4 stars.  I would give them 5, but they are super expensive!!! Pretty standard for Vegas on price though.  Their fries, and seafood were awesome and this would be a good place to take a big group of people too.  There is so etching for everyone, great decor and pretty good service too.
food was awesome.if you go at the right time no waiting in line. alot of selections!!! and their desserts....Mmmmmmm!!!
The await is horrible like around 3 hours. Good food but long long wait. So if you are hungry  please be prepared to wait .

Hands down one of the best buffets I've ever had! The high quality and endless choices will leave you very satisfied! It has everything you can imagine, from Chinese to sushi..Mexican, Italian, huge salad & cheese bar to the different varieties of meats & my personal favorite the seafood selection. I had to go back for seconds and thirds for the oysters & crab claws! I'm not a big dessert fan but wow, the choices they offer here made me into one! The unlimited macaroons to the crepes was probably my favorite to name a few! Def worth the $50 for dinner!

Omg... This buffet is amazing! When we got seated, we didn't even know where to start! So many choices of everything. The music in the background was great too! My husband enjoyed the tacos the most. As for me... There wasn't anything I didn't like. The desserts alone blew my mind!!!!

Hello everyone

Here at the Bacchanal Buffet in Ceasars palace and I gotta say it's my favorite buffet. And being my favorite sadly come with a price... literally. Easily one of the most expensive buffets on the strip if not The most expensive. But enough of that we are here to eat too! !
It's got a huge variety of food to eat from seafood to delicious meats to Italian and Mexican food then ending the buffet at an Asian section! Service here is great they are attentive for the most part. During weekends this buffet is packed so service could be slow at times but they will mostly always be there for you and you can actually see these workers quickly walking back and forth trying to get to everyone.
Now I will talk about the lines they are horrible!!! On a weekend or big holiday you have to check in first and get a time to return before you can start you wait in line so arrive early! Then your real wait will begin which could easily be an hour and a half to almost 2 hours during prime time dinner hours so be ready for that! But the food is worth it and it's unlimited of course!

Ps don't over stuff yourself and get partially sick... makes it hard to gamble...

Have fun everyone!!!
Overhyped, quality wasn't there for what you pay. Unless you are a big crab/lobster lover.

This place is expensive $60 ea for dinner, but it's good. Some of the food was great, while some of it was decent. Probably something you should do at least once. It's located in Caesars Palace and they've got great meats and seafood. I'm glad I went once, but I may not go back if I were to visit again, partly because I ate so much that I was uncomfortable. So depending o your budget this may or may not be for you. Lunch is a little cheaper.

Well I am sure I ate my $70 entry fee in oysters but the biggest disappointment were the stone crab. They were so hard to eat and once you got them opened the meat just would not come out of the shell. The sangria was overly bitter which left a strange taste in my mouth that rendered the flavor of the food nullified. The beef station was good but fatty pieces of meat really disappointed. Not sure I would eat or pay for this Buffett again but at least I tried. Save your money unless you really like buffets then this would be right up your alley.

This Buffet is a 1.5 , I refuse to give it a 2. The service is always great. They got the decent crab legs and ribs. Everything else goes down hill from there. Craw fish has no taste (anyone can cook better!), you can have better string beans in a carryout restaurant than the ones here which taste almost rotten, sushi bar sushi is simply salmon and tuna, an $8 all you can eat local buffet has more sushi selection, and makes much better sushi. Don't get me wrong, this buffet is extremely busy and popular, and just because of that, even when the quality is poor, they will always have the demend. I waited 5 minutes in the Vip line, I can't picture myself to  wait more than 15 minutes in the regular line for this. Its just not worth it. If you want buffet, Planet Hollywood buffet has better tasting food. Also try Todoi Seafood buffet, it's many times better.

4.5 (-.5 on price) Really great buffet.  Dessert AMAZING... didn't include alcoholic drinks. But we did order sangria..yes delic. Ok for the experience but a bit to pricey for me. def a one time thing bc it's over $50 per person  yikes! ..love the crab legs steamed and cold..yum with melted butter.  love the cake pops..mm good! Bit nice and classy. Great friendly staff n server.

So... not being the Las Vegas connoisseur, I had to consult my buddies on buffet choices while on a last second trip to the surface of the sun. I guess that didn't work seeing how they aren't any more "in the know" than myself. They heard it through the grape vine that Bacchanal has been generating buzz, and so we went.

I'll have to admit, it does have a bit better quality than other buffets, but at $45/pp I would like it would. I won't go into detail about anything specific, because nothing stood out. I tried probably one of EVERYTHING (except the dessert bar since it was closing) The selection is pretty good, but other than that... it just wasn't worth the $45 imo.

On a different note, the server/busser was excellent.

Next on deck to try is the M Buffet or Wicket Spoon at the Cosmopolitan...

Meh. This buffet is overrated. Food are actually mediocre to decent, though not worth waiting 2+ hours for. And with the high price, I'm sure we should expect something more. The bright side, the dessert are actually quite decent, so if you're into sweets, you would love the buffet more than I did.

I loved this place so much!! Very well worth the price, especially if you go around 2 and stay maybe an hour until the dinner food! You get to experience the luxury of king crab legs! Really great quality food, best pizza I've ever had (truffle mushroom), and a great variety of desserts. It's been over two months since, and I can still taste every food I tried--that's how memorable this experience was.

We met up with some friends who were also in Las Vegas on the Strip for Thanksgiving dinner.  Every place that we considered eating had lines of several hours, so we knew it was going to be a long wait wherever we went.  We decided on the new Bacchanal Buffet and did the "tag team" approach to the 4  1/2 hour wait in line.  This restaurant just recently opened and underwent a $17 million renovation.  Prices were $50 per adult, children over 8 years old are considered adults at Bacchanal.

The food was exceptional in most cuisine areas.  The turkey and Thanksgiving food was a little weak.  The seafood section, Asian section with full sushi area and meat carving stations were superb.  One of our favorite items believe it or not was the mini burgers.  They were about the side of a half dollar coin, and had a phenomenal taste.  No condiments needed.  The seafood was super fresh and with many different options available including Alaska crab legs.

Service was okay, but there had been hundreds of people through the restaurant by the time we ate around 7:30 pm.  They seem to not be very good at keeping the lines moving and had two "specialty" lines that took priority over the general line we were in.  To the left there was a line that for and additional $20 per person, you could pay and be seated in an hour.  To the right was the VIP line for guests and other people of self importance.  It was sad to see but also comical as well to watch how poorly and child-like grown adults behave when they don't get exactly what they want.  In this case, most were frustrated at the one hour wait time.  Poor people.....I mentioned our wait time was over 4 hours.  When we departed at 9:30 pm there were still people in line.  

I would like to visit again on a non-holiday time and give them another chance.  However, if the line is as long as it was and the treatment of the general dining people is as poor as it was over Thanksgiving, we'll pass.
Food is different and better than my expectations.  But I hate the wait that is always long.   A lot of different desert. King crab is a must here.

FIRST THING I MUST MENTION IS OUR AWESOME SERVER ENRIQUE! He is soooo awesome. He went out if his way to get my friend ramen when the chef said ramen wont be available for another 30 minutes. Enrique was very friendly and kind for the entire dining experience! THANKS ENRIQUE for being AWESOME!

We came on a Saturday night..wait time: almost 2 hours!!!

The food is ok. Clams had sand in it. Oyster had sand in it. Crabs were really on point. Asian section is always lacking in quality. Theres not ALOT of selection and theres always a line to get food. 

TIP: Get two plates..ur gonna b lining up so must as well use two plates at a  time!

Probably won't be my first, second, or third choice for buffet...but I want to give 4 stars to Enrique and the decorations of the restaurant. It is VERY PRETTY in there.
They are rude and unhelpful... Food tho good is very overpriced even for vegas def needs to be skipped

I hate to give a low rating but this is truly an honest review of my experience at Bacchanal. We went on a Saturday for dinner! 

The most horrendous thing from my experience was that the line to the carving station during our 2 hours there was all the way around to the Italian food section, wth!!!! My husband stood for 40 minutes in line trying to get his meat!!! (he is not a seafood person). Why would they only have 1 person carving variety of items (and the only meat stuff!!!).... I was appalled that the management didn't do anything about this.. Especially on a Saturday dinner service??!!! seriously, during the 2 hours that we were there, the line was horrendous, ridiculous! (we lined up outside, then we lined up inside too???!!!). They have a taco station, made to order (meat), but in my neck of the wood, tacos are $1 each, why would I want that at a buffet that cost me $60/perso+ tax+tip?!!!! The bone marrow and the lamb chops (not rack of lamb) were all extremely dry (overcooked because sitting under the heat lamb and lots of people couldn't have access to them because they were covered by people lining up!), and they also lacked of flavor. The meat from the carving station (when finally we got them after queue-ing forever!!!) was not worth the hassle! The prime rib was medium well (probably sitting too long), the brisket was bland, the sausage was good though a tad dry as well.

The only few savory food that worth being complimented: The mushroom and truffle pizza, Chicken wing stuffed with pork (chinese station), and Salmon. They only had Snow crab legs that were very very salty, and the stone crab claws (these tasted better than the snow crab, but harder to eat, because you had to crack them yourself!) There was no king crab leg when we were there, they had some cooked in the cioppino that tasted extremely salty and I couldn't even eat it.. yuck!

The singaporean laksa was flavorful but again, a tad too salty and the noodles were not right!!!! (they used udon noodles, wth!). 

Thankfully, the dessert was reasonably good, although, the much-raved-about made-to-order crepe was more like a pancake than crepe! (too thick, very thick!).

I've been to several other Buffet in Vegas, I would choose the Bellagio and the Wynn buffet over this one! Sorry!!!!

All the meats were VERY dry except for the brisket. I had to use bbq sauce for all my meats and that too wasn't even good!

The crab legs were really skinny, hardly worth the trek of balancing them on your plate. The butter is WAY too sweet. The service is awful, waiters don't move for you and always had a scowl on their faces. 

The only positive is that you can pay an extra $35 dollars to skip the line. Completely worth it. Makes it about $100 a person though (before tip).

A large selection of food from all over the world. Great atmosphere and ambiance.  Quality of food is on par with a 5 star hotel. But did not have lobster and king crab that I was expecting for this kind of price.

So much delicious food but I probably won't be getting the VIP package again. Didn't have to wait in line with my 6 person group but we didn't have enough people finish the premium seafood it comes with and it felt like we wasted a lot. I'd definitely come back and just do the regular dining.

Very EXTREMELY disorganized. The food is awesome as I've been here before but the wait and the disorganization does not make it worth it.  Better to make reservations at a delicious steak and seafood restaurant as Vegas has an abundance than stand in line for HOURS on a Thursday night!

OMG BEST BUFFET I HAVE EVER HAD IN MY LIFE IM IN LOVE. I wish I could eat here every day. There's so much food so many different options there's something for everyone! I love how unique all there sections of food are there's fresh tacos in Mexican food delicious pasta and pizza in the Italian section some pho for Vietnamese portion dimsum for Chinese sides sushi for Japanese seafood with crab legs and claws a bunch of hot meat and cold cuts they honestly had everything I got to try a bit of each and it's actually delicious that they could master so many flavors of food correctly, that's just the savory food portion. Don't get me started on desserts they were delicious and beautiful I'm at home craving the banana pudding bread. They also had everything at the dessert section too gelato, macaroons , fresh crepes, cakes, cookies, gummy bears the list goes on and on! Cannot forget to mention they had fresh juices in the cutest jars horchata, Jamaica , guava, mango and more they were all so cute and good!

Great upscale buffet.  One of the more nicer ones on the strip/vegas.  Amazing selection.   Would only come here with the Groupon.  paying full price is not really worth it, unless you have high tourist dollars to spend.  Getting the VIP with unlimited mimosas is a nice touch.

literally THE BEST BUFFET OF MY LIFE! (but I have yet to try other Vegas buffets) I came here with friends on Sunday for dinner, $57 per person but worth every penny! The wait wasn't too bad, 40 minutes total. The service was good, nothing worth mentioning. 

From seafood to prime rib to Chinese to soup to pasta to tacos to charcuterie to dessert, this buffet has the MOST variety, it has everything you could possibly want to eat and more. Everything is cooked and seasoned to perfection and will leave your taste buds happy and satisfied. The grilled scallops were delectable, and who doesn't love unlimited crab legs? I loaded up on my meat on my first plate which was a bad idea because it filled me up real quick. The cheese section made me happy because I had never seen a buffet have charcuterie items! LASTLY and my favorite: dessert. Macaroons, ice cream, crepes, cheesecake, cake pops, candy, fruit, ice cream mochi, cake, chocolate covered strawberries, cookies, flan..etc you name it they have it! 

Only complaint I have is that the Red bean ice cream mochi ball was gross because the actual mochi was hard, rubbery, and not edible whatsoever. (The green tea was yummy tho!) I would recommend coming with an empty stomach and staying for a couple hours to make good use of the $60.  MUST TRY AT LEAST ONCE! :)

When you think of buffets, you never think of it being elegant, classy, and fancy.  For me, buffets is a place were you stuff your face with mediocre food and unbutton the top button of your pants to fit more food in.  Bacchanal Buffet is far from it.  It is the fanciest buffet I ever been to.  I do not know how they are able to pull it off, but they sure did.

The place is massive.  There are many people that dine here yet when you're seated at your table it feels quite intimate.  I believe this is due to the place being sectioned off with dividers; I love that.  I also love that the table comes with table settings and an alcoholic drink menu; although I did not order from that menu.  However, I did have the peach infused green tea and oh my goodness, that is the best sweet green tea I have ever had.  Honestly, it was refreshing and memorable for a tea lover like myself.

Besides the drink, the place comes with a variety of food.  You have your seafood bar, your Italian cuisine, Asian cuisine, Mexican cuisine, all-American cuisine and the best dessert bar with a fresh crepe station.  You are definitely not limited on your choices.  This is the only Vegas buffet we know that serves hot boiled crab legs; king crab legs to be exact.  The food is definitely not your typical buffet food.

I keep wavering between giving this a four stars or five.  Though it is quite expensive for a buffet, it is one of the best buffet I have had.  Five star it is!!!

The Bacchanal Buffet is locates inside of Caesars Palace and since I've heard so much about it but didn't get to try it the first time I went to Las Vegas, I decided to give it a try for when I went for my birthday. 

The line to the buffet was long (I insist on getting there early to beat the lunch rush otherwise you'll find yourself really hungry and waiting 45 minutes just to get in) and I think the price was around $40 a person for brunch not including drinks, tax, and gratuity (I would say we spent about $120 for two people). The cashiers in the front were friendly but our waitress was not. I've noticed that they sectioned their customers based on race - don't know if it's by intention or by coincidence - but I was not impressed. The entire population of customers of the section where we were seated were Asian. Every. Single. One. You look to your left: Asians. You look to your right: Asians. You look in front of you and you see someone who people of other races would think looks exactly like you, which is Asian. I purposefully ate my food slowly to test my theory out and oh my god - lo and behold - four parties of customers sitting on either side of me came and gone and the waitstaff still continued to replace the last Asian couple with a new one. I think the most surprising part about all of this was the fact that my waitress was also a minority. 

The food was mostly European fare and tasted ok. I liked the eggs benedict and tacos the most (the taco guy was really friendly - he even gave me a little more carne asada than the other customers in line). On the section where I was seated had a small selection of pizza and flatbreads but mainly you see the Asian foods counter. (You see what I mean?) 

The environment was really nice and had a great ambiance. Nothing less than what you'd expect from a 4-Star hotel and casino. 

$120 would have been very reasonable for a a nice buffet at the casino if the food was amazing and service was great but it was a big let down and ultimately wasn't worth the price. I might try the buffet at Rio next time.

We had been wanting to try the Bacchanal Buffet for months so we were so excited to finally have the opportunity to try it yesterday. We arrived and the wait was 101 minutes which was a bit insane. We ended up getting seated in 45 minutes which we were thrilled about. Once we walked in I was already disappointed with the selection they offered for what is known as "the #1 buffet in Vegas." I think the biggest disappointment was having to wait in a 20-30 minute wait to get your food. Unlike other buffets where you walk up to a station to grab food, you had to wait in an extremely long line to get all of your items. It was a bit ridiculous. We ended up eating the food we grabbed as we waited. The best items they offered were the steak tacos, sliders, crab legs and pizza. Everything else was so/so. Also, the breakfast selection was highly disappointing. They did not offer omelets, pancakes; many of the popular breakfast items. The best thing about this buffet was that mimosas are included in the $45 price (for Sunday brunch.) I feel bad giving it two stars as the service was REALLY good, our waiter was on point and always ensured we had drinks which was awesome. I think because Bacchanal has always been marketed as the #1 buffet I had much higher expectations, especially since it is one of the most expensive buffets on the strip. I would much rather eat at Wicked Spoon at Cosmo or at Aria's buffet.

Overpriced, Mediocre Food,  So-so Service.
So Disappointed.
 
Too expensive ($60) for mediocre food and loud techno music. Maybe it was techno night when we dined. 10/18/15.

Some food are not fresh and have been kept under the lamp too long. The Stone Crab legs were so hard to open, it is not worth the laundry afterwards. Minimal Sushi selection. Salty Meats. Service was so so and the music was way too loud for a restaurant.

Good food... Terrible service.. 
Cashier was rude when we were paying for the buffet.. And when we got to the table, our server didn't bother to ask us if we want to have some drinks til we were done with our 2nd round of plates.. Terrible service...

stayed at Caesar Palace. My husband and I dined in at bacchanal buffet and used the 24hr buffet meal +30.00 each additional. It's Lots of food! But for us it's all over rated. Over priced! One dine-in is enough! We loved the boiled leg crabs though.

Lines can get LONG here, but trust me, it's worth the wait!! I recommend bringing a fully-charged smartphone or tablet to entertain yourself while waiting in the long line. Once you get a taste of their food, the wait will seem like seconds. The food that is served here will blow your mind, change your life, and leave you in absolute bliss! The wait staff, bus persons, and buffet servers are always friendly and courteous! Bacchanal Buffet is HANDS DOWN, the BEST buffet in Vegas!!

Latest favorite, almost replace the buffet of Wynn. Seafood portion is huge and fresh and generous. Waitress/waiters are super attentive, so is our tips. Black sesame mochi desert is awesome cuz it's from Japanese supermarket (seeing them unpacking) but its super expensive and delicious! Will be back in low peak period otherwise it's 2 hrs waiting time starting 7:15pm.
the buffet is as good as everone said.  definitely should try when you are in town.  sea food, steak and all kinds of dim sum. highly recommended!

Arrived early and didn't have to wait in line.

This place is big and does have the fresh cooked appearance.

They have an extensive, Asian section and beef.  Italian was small, seafood was excellent.

The fish had everything you wanted. Crab legs, muscles etc.
The meat section had prime rib with the rib if you wanted, lamb, brisket, ribs, sausage.

Most everything was good. Some was excellent, but overall a good dinner for 44pp

I was disappointed in the dessert section. Very small plates just not what I was expecting based on the huge selection in the main food area.

It was an experience, I would go back again for about half the price or free.  In other words, not going to happen.

Mixed drinks were about 14-15 dollars each.

Having read the raving reviews and having seen the consistent 4 stars i was really excited to try this place. Unfortunately I found the service to be sub par and the workers unfriendly. The food was mostly too salty. The only plus side is the oysters. Overall I felt like I paid way more than I got from this buffet. 

There's other buffets that are cheaper and in my opinion have better tasting food.

If I could give this place ZERO star that what I would of given.

We tried the buffet at the wynn on our last trip to Vegas and wanted to try a different place. We heard the Ceasar palace buffet was best in town. 

It DIDNT even come close to the hype. Half of the items that they advertise were not even on the buffet line when we got there.

The buffet cost $80 per person x 2= $160  for dinner. 
The crab legs were half cold and half warm. They must of not submerge the legs all the way in the pot. Also, they advertise king crab legs but when you ask for some. It mix in both snow crabs and king crab. My plate was mostly snow crabs and 2 tiny pieces king crab. You have to hand them your plate and the cook will give you what he wants to or feel like it. The other items were mediocre. Jonah crabs tasted bad. Trust me I ate a lot of Jonah crabs in my life. But the one they served had a funky smell to it. 

Servers were also not tentative. Our waiter was constantly arguing with two other waiters. They were fighting over who stole who tables. 

Overall, we will not be back. Save the your money!

Now this is what I call a buffet! I was in town with coworkers for a conference and we figured we couldn't leave Vegas without the true Vegas food experience - an all-you-can-eat buffet. We decided on Bacchanal which was just about a 10-15 min walk from our hotel down the strip. We waited a while with our party of 7 but once we were seated we walked by the entire buffet of food, which seemed like it went on forever. 

I was anxious to try a lot and I was pleased with everything I had. Favorites were the sushi, seafood paella, escargot, mashed potatoes, Parmesan fries, and crab legs. I kept going back for a little more of everything to try a variety of foods. 

I was getting stuffed but saved room for some dessert. Even the dessert was amazing! The macaroons were so good and I enjoyed the cakes as well. Definitely slept good that night. At around $55 a person, it's definitely worth it!

Long wait but decent selection. Weak desserts. 

Prime rib: Thick cut, a little too "chewy" and not tender enough. Disappointing. 3/5
Creamed corn: Nice milky flavor to complement the meat. I went back for thirds! 4/5
Brisket: Extremely thick cut. The first piece was melt-in-your-mouth delicious, but the second piece I tried was dry as the desert! Inconsistent. 3.5/5
Grilled lamb chops: Tender, flavorful without being a salt mine. Favorite! 4.5/5 

Creme brûlée: Disappointing. 2/5 
Orange beer gelato: 5/5
Pistachio gelato: 3/5
Green tea/sesame cake: 2.5/5 
Red velvet brownie: 2.5/5
Thai tea boba float: 1/5

3.5 stars, rounded up to 4. It was good, but not enough to definitely warrant a return visit.

Right, the Buffet. This was the second time we stayed at Caesar's Palace (love the Augustus tower!). Many-many times we wanted to visit the buffet. Finally did it on Thanksgiving 2016. The whole experience was an absolute mess and given how ridiculously overpriced it was I can't help, but feel that I've been robbed of $150 (a dinner for 2). 

The buffet has an electronic queue system: you register, take a ticket, it gives you a time to come back and...well, that's where things start to get interesting. You must remember all that footage of those horrific Soviet queues.  In the best tradition of Soviet queuing the electronic queue is essentially a queue to get into a queue. 

When we came 15 minutes before our assigned time, we were greeted by a tired looking bunch of people. Oh, there were tens and tens of them. And they all stood in a queue. We thought that it must have been a misunderstanding and that horde of people would somehow miraculously disappear. We had a ticket after all. They were they to stay, let me tell you. On a bright side, we all had something in common - we all had tickets we received after registering at the electronic queue system, which assigned us time to have an enjoyable experience at the most famous buffet in LV!

A nice supervisor told us that a big queue was because of Thanksgiving. Well, that's not entirely true, now is it? The queue there is pretty much always, but we used to assume the queue was for people who haven't registered in the electronic queue. [[[They do say that an assumption is a mother of all *&^&ups. Lesson learned.]]] Then a nice supervisor told us it was her first Thanksgiving at the buffet. Hm. Why is this relevant? The buffet was opened 4 years ago and a system must have been in place and should have been worked out regardless of a "human factor", this Thanksgiving was not more crowded than usual in LV (I've been in LV on several Thanksgivings in the recent years so I kind of have an idea).  

We've been standing in that queue to get to our table for an hour and a half!!

Now that we've reached our table (now I know how Columbus must have felt when he saw the land) we thought we would just get some food and finally enjoy the evening. Tough luck. For that we needed to get the food, you see. And for that we had to stay in another queue. Logically, right? For 30 minutes. Yep. Forget about going there for another round. The only stations with no queues were with Asian food and pizza. Thanks, but not when we paid over $150. Btw, $150 does not include alcohol. In what not Michelin star restaurant would you eat for $150 without a sip of wine?

Our plans for the evening went to hell (we left the buffet at around 11pm), my knee started aching (multiple sessions of physical therapy to cure my knee injury are no match to the Bacchanal buffet's queuing system), they didn't give any complimentary water while people were standing in a queue (at Wynn's buffet they do) and I had to go and buy a bottle of water for my pregnant wife ($7 for the water that off the Strip costs $1.50), no chairs/benches for pregnant, elderly and the hungry kids. So the kids were just running around (what else?), but eventually even their enthusiasm deflated. Yeah, hunger will do it to you, kids. Nothing better than a sound of a crying baby in your ear when you are tired, hungry, thirsty and generally pissed off.

The food was ok, no better or worse than in other buffets on the Strip and definitely not worth the hype. Personally, I thought desserts at Aria or Mandalay Bay buffets had a better selection.

I don't know how to describe my overall experience succinctly: profit at an expense of customer service? Complete carelessness about the customers' experience? C'mon guys, its a not casino when a drunken deluded dude is hoping to score a jackpot by betting 10c and you just expect him to give you all his money without having to give anything in return - you can't have that level of customer care at a "world renown buffet".

Never again.

P.S. When we shared our experience at a check out, a nice gentleman promised he would speak to the relevant people and we should expect a call to discuss this fabulous experience. Still waiting for a call, I'm sure any minute now.

P.P.S. Can't give one star since the food wasn't atrocious. The experience was.

Touted as the best buffet in Vegas / the States, Bacchanal Buffet had high expecations to meet, and I was excited. 

Yes, it was huge. Large spaces dedicated to particular food zones, such as a seafood zone featuring the longest crab legs I've seen at a buffet, a Mexican zone, an Asian zone (not so good), hot food, and desserts, you name it, it was there.

But as for the best buffet? I must admit, I was a little disappointed. Although the buffet spread was gigantic, the quality of the food was not the best. Highlights were the seafood station and the giant taco-making station, but everything else was average. 

Decor was okay, not world class. Patrons were the average pedestrian - jeans, sneakers, frazzled. It's not as classy as it markets itself as. No where comparable to the 5 star buffets in Asia or Middle East. On the scale of US restaurants, I give 4 stars.

Really good food.. rather pricey, but I have been 2x nonetheless. Everything from an antipasti style meat counter, to Asian style foods and BBQ.. the buffet also includes and bit of sushi and fresh seafood.  They have redesigned the previous buffet to include a more spacious floor plan and larger food stations. At something like $50 for dinner though, it's a hefty tag for a buffet. I know you get what you pay for, it is just a high price to pay when you consider how much gym time it will take to burn it all off! haha.. in actuality it's pretty good ~!

We started lining up at around 1 pm for dinner. It took us about 2.5 hours to get into the buffet with 6 people, but it was worth the wait. I can only imagine the wait time for someone who went during actual dinner hours.

We also got the buffet of buffets deal which gave us a 24 hour pass to the 6 different buffets in various hotels. We went to the buffets in Paris and Planet Hollywood as well. However, those buffets do not compare to Caesar's Palace in taste. We had to pay an extra $15 per visit to get into Caesar's Bacchanal Buffet, but it was worth the money.

Once you get in, it seemed fairly roomy and not so crowded. You would expect the restaurant to be packed inside, but the layout of the tables are fairly spread out for a comfortable dining experience. The ambiance consisted of modern decor with light colors.

Inside, you will find a line to reach the crab legs as well and a line next to it for the  steak, ham, pork chop. These are the seafood and American kitchens. No other kitchens had a major line.

The food was really authentic. I mean you had Japanese chefs working the sushi bar, Chinese chefs working the wok, Italians baking their lasagna, and Mexicans doing their thing... I think that's about as authentic as you can get. 

My recommendations include the crab legs, pork chops, scallop mashed potatoes, miso soup, and the quality selection of gelato.

Wynn, Bellagio, Wicked Spoon....move over aside. Bacchanal Buffet is the new GOLD STANDARD for buffets.
This place is so good that you wish you could die several times during your meal and come back each time hungrier than the last. IT'S THAT GREAT.
Friends & I waited 90 minutes on a Friday Night for this amazing experience. The cocktail waitresses come by every 5-10 minutes offering free bottles of water to any of the patrons waiting in line (GOOD JOB CAESARS)

After paying $37.99 plux tax ($2 discount with Total Rewards card), we waited another five minutes to be seated. It was then, when my food coma started.

There are SO MANY STATIONS in this buffet, just remember there's a back room too with Italian, Chinese, Japanese,  Mexican cuisine.

American Classics:
Cheeseburger sliders, Mac & Cheese, waffle fries, fried chicken, fried oysters, sweet potato fries, scalloped potatoes with cheese and other things. All of it is amazing, especially the scalloped potatoes and cheese burger sliders. 

Japanese:
omg, actual Japanese chefs making your sushi. I am not kidding, this is impressive. Most california chinese/japanese buffets don't even have japanese people making your sushi.
They make hand rolls, California rolls, tempura rolls, sashimi fish and other things.
They don't present all the sushi out at once. They rotate after each order. They will present an order of California rolls and tempura rolls afterwards and etc. Just keep your eye out if you don't see what you like, make sure you come back in 10 minutes.
 
Carving Station:
Prime Rib, Lamb, Roast duck, grilled chicken and the usual. wow, so good. Definitely try the Lamb as it's cooked perfectly. The Prime rib was a little too rare for my taste, hopefully it was just a mistake? They come with Au Jus sauce and some other southern BBQ sauce.

Chinese/Vietnamese:
seriously, Shanghai soup filled dumplings??? I LOVE IT. they taste amazing ( I wonder if they make it by hand...probably not). Theres your usual suspects in your dim sum lineup and fried rice, noodles and stuff. They also got Pho, which isn't very good. Caesars should just take that out of the rotation.

Italian:
Meatballs, pesto Ravioli, Spaghetti with marinara sauce, I don't know how it tasted, as I never got a chance to try it. I was too full :(

Seafood:
OMG, the life and soul of Bacchanal!!! They have crab legs on ice for you along with shrimp, oysters and these varying seafood mixes in shot glasses? My favorite part of this station is that they will steam your fresh crab legs for 30 seconds and give it to you on a clean white plate. They are cracked in half already and there's so much meat in them!!! They definite'y don't skimp on portion size too, as I got 5 crab legs. Be sure to grab the garnishing and butter for the legs.

Desert Station:
Words can't simply describe the layout of this desert station. fresh chocolate dipped fruit, delicious ice cream/gelato, fresh-made crepes, cake squares on sticks, gourmet cookies and whatever you can imagine. everything is presented elegantly and is delicious.

Service here is spot on. They clean your plates on a timely manner and refill your drinks quickly. I only hope Bacchanal can keep up it's gold standard for as long it can, as we all know how the restaurant industry can take a nose dive the moment it opens. 

Bacchanal, I shall see you soon :)

By far most consistent quality and quantity of dishes maintained among the big buffet restaurants at the strip. 

Definitely worth revisiting during next visit to Vegas.

The best buffet in town PERIOD!!! The staff was very courteous. Amazing selection from wide ranging cuisines. Tomahawk ribeye was perfectly cooked, superb lamb and tasteful brisket. Wish I had a bigger appetite, there so many selections there is no way you could try them all, guess I have to come back.  I have eaten at all the buffets in Vegas (local), you can't beat the price for the QUALITY!. They definitely have the best dessert bar!  Bacchanal is a step above Cosmo and Wynn which were my faves before I tried here.

This was amazing. We got the Groupon which saved a ton of money. We did the brunch and it came with mimosas. The food was phenomenal. Since a great assortment. I couldn't even try everything I wanted. So much food. I cannot wait to eat here again!!

Best buffet I've had so far since I moved to Vegas a few months ago, this is the first one I tried and the rest haven't compared so far. Bellagio was good but still did not come close to the variety here as well as the ambience/ service. Great for people who are vegetarians or love seafood as well! Dessert wasn't amazing but the food and drinks were top notch!

If it's your first time in Vegas you have to try Bacchanal, it's the best buffet in Vegas! Get your eyes ready for an amazing presentations of deco and food. Selections are unbelievable! from seafood, Mexican, high end cheeses, overwhelming meat selections, Asian food and yummy desserts. The best part of the buffet is you get to try some menu from the other restaurants at Caesars. It's worth every penny you spend!!!

This buffet was supposed to change my mind about how I don't really care for buffets. I was really hoping it would. But, alas, it did not.

Everything they had seemed like standard buffet fare. Quality was good, but it wasn't THAT much better than the other good buffets I've had in Vegas (Encore and Cosmo). I WAS impressed to see they had chinese bbq style roast duck. THAT was unique and different. So was their asian noodle bar (pho, udon, ramen). 

Of course I had my fill of their snow crab legs and oysters, both were good quality. I was just expecting Bacchanal to WOW me...damn you people who hyped it wayyyy too much for me. :P

I went there for my bday price are reasonable, foods good and the people that works there really helpfull. I would say my favorite there is deserts yumm... Ask for mark he works there he will help you.

I use to love bacchanal when they first opened and I went again and it was terrible! Everything was so salty. The crab legs, the meats, the soupy items, pork belly were all over salted. Even the dessert was salty. Jk. They definitely have good food options but for some reason taste didn't come through for me especially if I'm paying 50-60 bucks a head. Looking for good quality food if I'm paying that much.

4.5 Stars. This is best buffet in Vegas!  Had to see what 17 million dollars worth of renovations does to a buffet and all I can say is wow. We had lunch there on a weekday and it wasn't very crowded.  I suggest: ginseng chicken, oysters, menudo, and freshly made crepes.  Sushi selection could use some work, but I've yet to have really good sushi at any buffet.

Service was great.  Dirty plates promptly removed.  We found a live baby crab inside one of the oysters.  Was a little disturbing since it was moving around, but I guess that means it's very fresh.

We went at 6pm on a Wednesday - less of a line but might NOT be the best time to go.  The seafood bar was good except for the oysters. They were sitting out for too long.  By the time we left the lines were lengthy and wrapping around. Good to beat the rush, bad for quality. 


The meat station was disappointing - extremely salty and dry since it was also sitting out for too long. There was no medium rare meat. Everything was overcooked and dry...the prime rib was cooked medium and overcooked, both pork and beef ribs were dry and super salty, fried chicken was yummy but the chicken itself was dry too!  Boo!  :( the waffle part of it was amazing though. I had 2 servings!  Sushi was scary to eat - dry and particularly warm. Sitting out for too long. 

I'd give it another try when it's busier.

We are known here for our excess and opulence in everything- our dining is no exception, as you'll see if and when you go to Bacchanal.

It's the newest and largest buffet here at the strip, beating out even the highly praised Wicked Spoon over at the Cosmopolitan, also fairly new and was the first in town to incorporate the tapas-style buffet.

Great interior, great service, great everything.  The ONLY thing that separates the Bacchanal from the Wicked Spoon is that the Wicked Spoon has more 'chef-conceived' dishes, unique to itself and undefined by a cultural cuisine.  Bacchanal has your regular items respective to major world cuisines, just made very well with very good ingredients.

Soft, soft wagyu beef sliders, soft char siu bao, the biggest selection of prepared meat I have seen, tuna/salmon poke salad with the squishiest and freshest fish; everything is just amazing.

Only downside is that it IS expensive, but is much, MUCH worth the money versus the buffet at the Wynn or Bellagio.

If you have to eat only at one buffet in our city, it must be this one.

The seafood selection was pretty good, and overall selection of food was decent... disappointed in more of the fried foods and some cooked choices. They were either dried out or overly cooked and sitting under the hot lamp way to long. The wait was to long for the selection and hype... 35 min. Go over to the aria, about the same selection and less wait time with a little better price.

We visit Las Vegas several times a year and we always go to the Bacchanel Buffet once during each visit. I'm sad to say but I don't think we will be dining here again. We watched the left over breakfast items, pancakes and waffles sit for over an hour. The sushi rolls were not fresh and neither were the salads. We tried a couple of the meat choices and they all tasted the same, very smokey. The quality of the meat used in the street tacos (our usual favorite item) was low. They lacked flavor and were just not good. There are a lot of places to eat in Vegas, time for us to find a new favorite buffet

I am coeliac and eating out in the US has often been hit and miss. My friend, boyfriend and I went for the dinner buffet and we were all incredibly impressed. I told the lady who showed us to our table that I had dietary requirements and she promptly went and got one of the chefs to walk me around and explain what I could and couldn't eat. Oscar (the chef) was amazing and told me to just ask if I would like some of the dishes prepared gluten free.  

The selection and quality of amazing food has to be seen and tasted to be believed.  Whatever you do, make sure you are very hungry when you go. You will not be disappointed. To all of those coeliacs out there make sure you stop by and enjoy the most amazing selection of food that you have likely seen for a very long time!

So much good food! Such a big selection! Such cute displays! 

In all honesty though, this place was super hyped for me. To me, their food was like any other buffet....just way more expensive. I believe I paid $60 just to eat dinner here in February. I will give it to them though, they do have a bigger selection compared to other buffets. 

I really enjoyed their sushi the most here. I forgot what else I tried but I'm sure it was good as well. 

The customer service here was excellent. I believe we had two waitress for our table. The cleared out plates fairly quick. 

I'm having a hard time writing a long review for them because I don't remember what else was good here. Crab legs? Haha

Not sure what the hype is about here. I have definitely gotten sick off the oysters and cocktail shrimp on two separate occasions eating here. Also for the price its definitely not worth it. While the selection of desserts is very good, the rest of the food isn't that great. A lot of the food is over cooked to the point where it is soggy or not fresh. I would go with another buffet like Wicked Spoon or even the Bellagio buffet.

This is hands down the best buffet in Las Vegas. I've eaten at some of the best, including Bellagio buffeting Wynn buffet, and dabbled in some less expensive ones such as the Planet Hollywood and M buffets, and this is by far the BEST. The food selection is great, as the buffet offers you the range of different cuisines you would expect from a top notch world class buffet. What separates this place from the rest is the quality. The beef brisket was one of the best I've EVER had, including those at buffet joints in the south. The curries are fresh and taste straight out of Thailand. The Italian meatballs are very well made and authentic, rivaling even those of Rao's next door.  For those of you who only come to buffets to eat seafood...this might not be the place for you. The seafood is good but similar to Wynn and Bellagio. For those of you who come for a top notch culinary experience normally not offered in the mass produced mass consumed aisles of the buffet--this is definitely the place to go!

Went to bacchanal buffet for New Years night dinner.  Advertised lobster and king crab, both gone and we were seated at 6:20 pm.  WTF!!!  Crab legs were served cold but they offered them warm, they boiled them to warm them.  Some served were warm some were still cold.  The cold crab legs and shrimp were too cold, you could tell they had been frozen.  The prime rib was great, the lamb chops were perfect.  The suckling pig was very dry. Peking duck was very good, if you can grab the drumsticks they go fast and are excellent.  The pork belly or thick slices bacon over mashed potatoes were very good.  Green beans lacked flavor but were well steamed, not to soft with a bit of bite. 
Crab claws were previously frozen and the texture was off.  

The desert station was strong, gelato was excellent.  Fresh berries, macaroons, molten chocolate cake, and key lime tarts were very good.  

We went after a very heavy time, so some allowances should be made but when you are paying $69.00 per person for a buffet they should get it right every time without exception.  Thanks

This place is over rated and overpriced ! Wait time is about 2 hours and you pay 51$ plus tax and if you can't wait too long you can add 15 more dollars and your wait time is about 15 min and i think that's shady business from management calling it express lane !!!
Food is tasty but nothing special , I like their choices of meat and the way it's cooked but anything else is average and you can find it in any other hotel buffet (Wynn , Rio seafood and Bellagio ) . Our waiter was nice and helpful .  
We also heard a lot about their dessert choices but i wasn't really impressed  just normal buffet dessert .

I am a regular to Vegas, 2-3x times a year, and have been Diamond with Caesars for years.  Can't say I was very impressed, and most of that hinged on one thing.  Not the food, not the drink service, but the staffing in terms of keeping the tables clear of dirty dishes.

4 of us went on a busy Saturday night, naturally it was at capacity as would be expected. Got seated and every empty table we saw was stacked with dirty dishes.  At a $50+ price point for dinner, hire a few more bus staff.  We went up for a second round, came back to the table 10-15 minutes later (yes, buffet is that extensive) all the dirty dishes glasses, etc were right where we left them.  And no, they didn't have a good quantity of food or drink in them, they were clearly done with.  Again, at the price point of $50+  per head, in surroundings that reportedly made it the most expensive buffet to build in Vegas, is the expense to clear tables really that much?  Even the tables that had been vacant for 20 minutes were untouched.  That's a lot of lost revenue by not being able to seat new customers. (Did I mention it was $50+ apiece)?

To top it off, on the way out I saw a manager near the exit, and mentioned that while the food was good, they need more staff to keep the dining room clear.  His response, that there are plenty of staff, they're just union and lazy.  There's a sentiment for you. I wanted to reply back that perhaps it was more due to poor leadership, management, hiring practices, or just cutting corners on staffing...but restrained myself.  

Bottom line.  Go next door to Mirage.  Maybe the food isn't quite as high end (but still very good), but still very good, well staffed, clean, well organized, wine and beer included, and save yourself some money.

My 2nd time here. I have had both lunch and dinner at Bacchanal. A wide selection of food and the dessert section is very impressive. However, for the price, the food doesn't taste that much better than a regular buffet.

Rated as the top buffet in Vegas, I came in expecting so much from this restaurant. The selection was huge but the flavors and featured dishes were so-so. Most dishes are bland, and the hot crab claws salty. The crispy pork belly wasn't crispy, the Vietnamese pho broth tasted like water mixed with soy sauce, the paella negra doesn't have that flavorful seafood taste you normally taste in paella, the American beef wagyu was dry. For $60 Saturday brunch, the selection was plenty but I wish the flavors were better.

Probably one of the more expensive brunch buffets in Vegas at $45 a pop, but the quality was overall on point.  I would recommend to not come in a big group of ten like I did or you will have to endure a two hour wait..... They do have an option to skip the wait time if you pay $20. Yea we weren't willing to wait that long so F IT!!! :)  

The sushi selection is very lacking to only salmon and tuna so I was a bit disappointed in that since that's usually where I head to first when I hit any buffet.  I do give them points though on their dim sum selection which actually wasn't that bad.  It wasn't as bad as other buffets that serve packaged frozen crap.  Siu mai and ha gow were not that bad at all. Cha siu was bombskis tho.

I probably devoured two plates of snow crab legs, about half were on the salty side and the other half on the sweeter side.  Yea I know it's not great for cholesterol but I never really get a chance to eat it that often, so no bigs!  The shrimp were ok, they did have a slight smell to them but not totally offputting.  Our group stayed for a while past the brunch hour which was rolling into the dinner time so they were putting oysters out on the half shell as well!  I could only eat about 3 since I was so full by then but from what I could remember, they were decent as well.  Not the best but none of them made me sick.

I tend to stick with the proteins and stay away from all the starchy carbs so I can't comment on any of the pasta/rice dishes.  The prime rib was cooked well but the quality was no more than select.  The wait for the carne asada isn't really worth it either. It was good but not ten minutes in line good.  

I think the desserts were somewhat of the redeeming factor of the meal since as I said before, we stayed during the transition from brunch to dinner.  So macarons and chocolate dipped strawberries were on the menu as well as the breakfast type dessert pastries as well.

Our waitress Patty was outstanding and made the experience much more enjoyable.  She was constantly around refillling our mimosas and stayed around to chat with us from time to time and crack jokes.

I would put Bacchanal on level with Bellagio and the Wynn buffets so definitely worth a stop before leaving Vegas.

Great food! Last time I went 9 months ago was amazing! The brisket was dry this time and they didn't have as big of a selection. However, service was fast and friendly.

Food variety is CRAZY. Dim sum, sushi, sea food, Mexican, Italian. And don't even get me started on the desserts!!
A huge selections for you to choose from.  We were there for like 3 hours chilling out and enjoying the food. My family must have eaten away at least a week long worth of food there.

First time I ate here it was during the Grand Opening and the food was a bit cold.  I have since have eaten here several times and it looks as if they have got all of the kinks out.  The selection is amazing and the service is outstanding.  As a Diamond member in the TR program I get to skip the long line which is fantastic!!!  Love the buffet and I love Ceasars Palace.  The managers for the restaurant are always on the floor talking to the guest and I love this,  it really shows they care about the place.

This review is based on my experience of the current visit of the buffet; not the food, since I just did not get a chance to enjoy it.

Anyway, their waiting system is just pain in the a--.  For those of you who are first timer to the buffet, you need to get a ticket from their kiosk instead of waiting in line like other buffet.  Then you need to go back with your ticket with printed time and wait in line again.  Yes, you need to wait in line again.  Plus. for those people who paid for the EXPRESS LINE will seated sooner than who don't.

My wrap up conslusion to Bacchanal Buffet is: 
"Waiting, waiting, and more waiting."
