They were just a lot more attentive than they were the first time I was here. HOWEVER, during the last 30 minutes we were there, we were kind of neglected. NO ONE informed us that our server already left and was done with her shift. We had to ask ourselves. That's the only reason why I deducted a star.

I can't wait to come here again. Probably not anytime soon because I'm not a rich girl BUT I will be coming here more often!

I've been here twice and honestly it is my FAVORITE place to eat in Las Vegas. I was pregnant with my twins this year and craved this buffet SO bad but unfortunately my doctor didn't let me travel out of state, so I just got to Vegas today for my birthday getaway with my husband and I am super excited to go eat there tomorrow!!! Hopefully it isn't too busy! It's a little pricy BUT I don't care ALL the food is delicious and it's clean and staff is nice! Usually people come to Vegas to club and gamble but I come for this buffet...and gamble a little bit! Lol I come all the way from California!!!

My goodness what great selection of food!!! As soon as you enter you are greeted with an array of fresh seafood from crabs to shrimps, mussels, crawfish and a whole lot more! However being the asian that i'am i'd have to say i quite enjoyed their selection of asian goodies. I have tried their udon, sticky bun and pork bun, shrimp dumpling and their very flavorful pork siomai. Ooh how that siomai hit the spot. It was really good! Almost like eating at an authentic chinese restaurant.

Aside from the food, service there was great! Unfortunately i couldnt remember our server's name. Or i probably was unable to pay attention as i was enjoying the food so much. But anyway she was very pleasant and attentive of our needs. Also very patient and willing to take our picture lol she was also kind enough to tell us her shift is over and that another server will be attending to us once she leaves. 

But now back to the food...they have good selection of desserts too from cookies to chocolates, cakes, icecream, even candies. But my favorites were their thai tea boba float (try it! Try it! Try it!) and their made to order crepes! Thai tea was very addicting which is both a good and bad thing. I dont know how many shots we ordered since we were there. And the crepe was nicely done. Soft, tasty, somewhat chewy and flavorful just the way i like it. Stuffed with Nutella and topped with some fruit ugh! It was heaven i tell you!

Now all these good things come with a very hefty price. I think lunch was $60 something per head yikes! How much more for dinner right? But trust me, it is totally worth it. Definitely the best "casino buffet" in Vegas!
No buffet expert but I felt they offered a good amount if you can shell out $52 for dinner per person

Amazing Amazing Amazing!!! For $57.99, this is a buffet that is worth it, but make sure you go with a hungrrrrryyyy stomach. This buffet is located inside Caesars Palace. At first, it was annoying because the wait to get in was longer than expected. They make you sign up at a machine to get a time. We were slotted for a 5:55pm reservation, but got a text at 5:30pm saying they were ready. When we arrived at 5:55pm, they let us "enter", but you STILL have to wait in line. What the....??!! That wait took another 30-40mins. So I didnt understand why we had to sign up in the first place. What made it more disappointing is that when you go in, there are soooo many empty tables. The line is just for the hype!

Ok, now that I got that out of the way... the food - because we are here for the food! The food was amazing. They had sections catering to seafoods, american (mostly meat), tacos, Japanese, Chinese and a small Italian section. I tried the sushi and chinese first and was surprised that the Chinese food tasted good. Everything from the duck, salt and pepper shrimps, eggplant, to dimsum items were really good. It was flavorful.

The seafood section was great. The variety of fresh scallops, crab legs, oysters, clams and shrimps would satisfy all those seafood lovers. 

The kitchen staff was super attentive and filled up the food amazingly quick. I was surprised given that some buffets stop filling the dishes up. The waiters that walked around also was great and constantly filling up your glasses with drinks. 

Overall, great meal and the desserts were good too. the Panda Cana was amazing.. Just a bit disappointed on how they handle the lines. Oh did i mention that if you're a Total Rewards Platinum or Seven member, there is an expedited line.

update to previous review--the manager reached out to me to offer his sincere apologies and I really appreciate the gesture given that a place like Bacchanal doesn't actually need to care about one measly customer who may have had an off-day experience at an otherwise outstanding and unique buffet. Thanks guys, I will definitely be back in the future to give it another shot. :)

The food was good not great. It was also very expensive. I ordered a pomegranate martini and it was bad, it tasted like they used cherry instead. My husband and I waited to get in and then we were there less than an hour and they started to clean up. People were still eating, we were still eating. We were given the bill and asked to close our drink tab. It was my birthday dinner with my husband. We save up for these occasions.
We went in 2016 I think.

Maybe it is me? I just do not get it. I was not impressed with this buffet. Hey I forgot I hate buffets! What I strongly dislike is that it does not seem so sanitary for hundreds of people to touch the same serving tools, and serving dishes. I thought this would be a different experience so I put my hate aside and I was excited to experience this buffet. Fail! I was never too happy not to stand in the regular cattle lines but I had the VIP/7 Stars entry. No line. 

The first stop was the Chinese station. I think I may be Black-A-Nese because I love rice, and noodles. It was cold rice, and noodles. It was greasy duck, and fatty duck. Not good. Egg rolls were good. The savior of the station. Dim Sum was ok. Meh!

Round two was the seafood station. The herd had moved away from the crab legs so it was quick. I read about steamed crab legs so I asked where I could obtain them. I guess they do not want the masses to know but you can find them at the Italian station. The legs looked like the crabs were on a Jenny Craig diet. No meat. 2 thumbs down   The steamed were tastier than the cold legs. 

Round three on to the desserts.  The winner at the station were gelato. I got many choices that were colorful, and pretty but bland on the taste buds. 

The final decision of the Foodie Champ versus the buffet Foodie Champ wins! I delivered a knock out punch to an over rated, over priced Fatty buffet!

It's Vegas, how can you not try a buffet?!

Service was mediocre given how busy they were on a weekend, but it's kind of expected.

Food wasn't anything amazing but the variety you get for the price is amazing. Food was constantly filled as well so you never had to wait too long if it runs out.

This place is just OK.  Nothing special. I read the other comments before going there and expected food to taste super. I was disappointed. Macrons had too much fillings, way too sweet, and the crusts were too thick and not crunchy.  Prime rib was too dry.  Crab legs were good, but other buffet places have that also. Shrimp cocktails were too well done.  Just another Vegas buffet.

Huge variety of food! We went at the last minute on Saturday night and line was huge! Since we were very hungry after a day trip and we only stayed in Vegas for a night, we did not want to miss the opportunity for this buffet. We paid the express ticket which was like $25/person just to pass the line. When we went inside, there were lots of empty tables. I guess they were booked or they might create an illusion that they were in high demand. I think the express ticket was not worth it so don't pay for it if you can wait.
Whatever the price, we love the food! Seafood is very fresh and very different from lots of buffets we have been to. I love the fresh and delicious macaroons which you would not find in most of the buffets in SoCal.
I think it's ok if you would like to try once in your life. I would not pay that much money for a buffet on Saturday night. Go on normal days if you can. Otherwise, put your name on the list and go somewhere else and come back later.

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS!
Wicked Spoon ain't got nothing on Bacchanal. What I like is that B doesn't play. One of the first stations you see is the seafood. BAM! Piles-a-plenty of crab, shrimp, oysters, salmon, seabass 'n more. Work your way down from there and find all types of cuisines well-represented. I liked that they had a station of fresh juice, including horchata. Refreshing! Desserts had their own central "island" complete with varying fine patisserie-worthy delights and a gelato station. 

We had a late start to the day and caught a late lunch. Ended up paying lunch price for dinner stuffs. Life just doesn't get better than that.

Caesar have always been my favorite Las Vegas Hotel on the strip, therefore eating there was on my bucket list. Despite the $39 brunch it was worth trying once.

We arrive at 10:30 and there was absolutely no line. Thank God! It was the most relaxing brunch buffet  overlooking the water view outside. Majority of the food is good quality. Too bad they didn't have the chocolate cover strawberries.  I was looking forward to it.

Line was very long it felt like I am checking out at Walmart super store and have 5 full shopping carts of merchandise to checkout, after 40 mins of waiting in line and waiting to be seated, the food was NOT GOOD $54.99 per person is a hugeeee rip off in entire north america, the pizza was sucked, the humus was tasted old, the spanish rice was cold and it was a big disappointing, plz do not enter, this restaurant is wayyyyyyyy overrated. Do not go!!!! Stay away! It is a big rip off, the dine in is huge but food selection  is just bluh, stale, cold, undercooked and just garbage!
People take pictures of the food like it's a mountain landscape.  The best.  Period.  End of story.  Worth every single cent.

I have never been to another Vegas buffet so I have no real comparison.  I did think the $40 something price tag for lunch was a lot at first, but once I saw everything included I didn't think it was bad.  I wish they had some alcohol options included though.  I way over indulged here, but everything was amazing.  Some of my favorites were the Asian area and the carving station.  The carving station had everything you could think of prime rib, ham, sausages, brisket, etc.  There was also the best sides near there great potatoes and vegetables.  I was a little disappointed in the seafood.  I hoped to see king or snow crab legs, but they only had Jonah crab claws which I am not much a fan of and I prefer my crab warm.  The Asian section had dim sum, standard Chinese dishes and sushi.  All of it great.  

Mark sure you do not fill up before having desserts.  There is so much to choose from and everything I had was beautiful and delicious.

Truly the buffet to reign over other buffets

I'm always a big fan of value for the money and variety so I'm always drawn to buffets. I've had buffets all across the world (all you can eat BBQ in Japan remains one of my favorite meals as well as hot pot buffet in China). The Bacchanal buffet takes your standard buffet, and explodes it by 10 (or by 3 if you're a vegas buffet). 

I went on a Friday at 2:30 PM (Yes, tried to sneak in at the lunch price but get the dinner options when they switch over at 3:00PM). The line was nonexistent which was good, although there was a decent amount of people in there already eating. The waitress quickly got our drink orders, and refilled them once before disappearing for the remainder of the meal (big annoyance). However, they were fairly quick in clearing the used plates from the table (althought that's more the busboys). 

There was Asian, Italian, Mexican, Soup, Meat, American, Seafood, and dessert section (Just roughly categorized over 100 options into those buckets. Will try to list out a number of dishes I tried and my impression on each:

Asian: Ramen was decent and edible, but far cry from ramen shops. Seaweed salad was good. Duck was ok but oily. Didn't try the dim sum but they looked good. Penang curry was ok... nothing special. Roasted pork belly lacked flavor. Hot and Sour soup was... smoky? Very offputting

Italian: Charcuterie was decent, cheeses were decent as well. The rest of the italian was uninspired (unless you really just like italian food) meatballs could use more seasoning, while the pasta I got was ok. 

Mexican: Coming from Texas, the mexican was ok (I should have got the tacos as people were going crazy for them). Roasted pork lacked flavor, as well as the chile verde, mexican rice, and ranchero beans. There were 2 kinds of mexican soups / braised meats, the beef was better than the pork and very tender.

Soup: Got the clam chowder, was ok but a little undersalted for my taste.

Meats: Got the brisket, pork rib, slab bacon, American wagyu beef, and prime rib. Brisket was decent but been under the heater too long. Pork rib was amazingly tender, comporable to BBQ I had in Texas. Slab bacon is delicious if you like... fatty pork. Prime rib was chewy, you really have to get the right cut (more well done may be better). American Wagyu beef you need the right cut as well... so overall the meats are hit or miss.

American: Mashed potates were uninspired. Hushpuppies were delicious.

Seafood: Shrip, snow crabs, and king crabs were all delicious. Load up on the king crab, and beware the horseradish packs a punch

Dessert: great variety of dessert, creme brulee was good, as well as the egg tarts. Gelato was good... overall try as many options as you can.

from the staff i heard, to avoid the horrendous wait, you need to arrive between 9:30 - 10:00 for the lunch buffet... at 11:00 am. Meaning after a long night at Marquee or Crazy Horse 3, you need to bust your ass over to caesers to avoid waiting 2 hours in line... and wait 1.5hours in the line.

Needless to say, we arrived at 11:30 for a projected 3 hour wait, paid the express line feed of $20 / head and we were on our merry way. I figure, 2-3 hours is really $6-$10 and hour, and come on, i think if you're ready to shell out $40 for a buffet, you're likely not making just minimum wage, and your time is probably worth more than that. It should be noted that by the time we left, the line for the express lane was a good 40min - 1hr wait. 

food is exceptional as always. We went there for thanksgiving lunch and had the usually carved turkey, stuffing, mashed potatoes along with prime rib, seafood, noodles and everything else. I tried almost everything and decided that seafood and carvery are must haves. the asian food is definitely for the china people, who usually eat chinese food for breakfast / lunch / dinner, and it was pretty mediocre. The deserts were amazing, love the crepes. 

overall we spent close to $70 bucks a person for this and i could honestly say, it was probably worth it. we were stuffed to the gills with amazing food and it was an overall good times.

Highly recommended if you have the time, if you can't decide what to eat, or if you love the lines.

The food was amazing. Went here on a quick trip to vegas around 12pm. The food the so fresh and well maintained. The place was extremely clean. The workers changed out the food very quickly. The selection was amazing. From prime rib to crab claws to sushi to pasta. None of the food was bland. Everything was very flavorful. Only wish the dessert selection was as good as the rest of the main food selection.

My brothers and I are dinner around 630 pm after registering for a ticket to wait in line for the buffet. (Note: there's two steps to get into the buffet; (1) enter contact and party info into kiosk and wait for a buzz on your phone or whatever way of contact and (2) get your ticket marked by worker and then wait in line pay and then wait again until your table is open.) I believe this process took 2 hours on a holiday weekend.

The food overall was just about the same since last time although they didn't have black chicken soup that enjoyed last time. I recommend trying the various juices such as pineapple, strawberry, and hibiscus. There juices were natural light, refreshing, and not too sweet. One item I really enjoyed was the miso sea bass in the seafood section. It was hot, flaky, and deliciously full of flavor. I actually went back immediately for another portion. Another item I liked was in the dessert section; a light fluffy tropical cake was one my favorite dessert. I recommend drinking tea with this dessert.

As usual, the food tasted great but was pretty expensive. I wished I had the stomach of Joey Chestnut so that I can truly earn my money's worth but realistically we all know that is impossible.

Be prepared everyone...be very prepared so that you can sample everything on the menu.

Come here on a weekday/during downtime: easily 4-5 stars. Come here during the weekend/rush: dips below 3 stars. 

Bacchanal was AMAZING when we first tried it on a Thursday morning. There was no line at the entrance. No wait at any of the stations. Top notch service from the servers. And an endless supply of edible tid-bits from nearly every culture. I seriously thought I died and went to heaven. This place had it all...fresh nigiri, authentic pho, Chinese blacken chicken soup that tastes homemade, fried chicken that was just so nom, phenomenal sweet potato tots and fries, even better parmesan tots, vanilla infused honey, more salami than I knew existed, quality fresh oysters...shall I go on or are you convinced that this place is heaven? Okay one more...their xiao long bao tastes legit, with soup inside and everything! They even have red vinegar for you to dip in! 

I just wish this place wasn't so popular during the weekends because it gets irritatingly packed and there is a friggin line for EVERYTHING! In summary, the food runs out, what's left looks old, food selection diminishes, food quality deteriorates, lines get in the way, people get in the way, stress everywhere! 

So if you want to truly enjoy a top notch buffet, please come here during off hours. If you want to have one of the most stressful eating experiences of your life with mediocre food, by all means, come and see the madness during peak hours.
Expect a line, but also expect a great Buffett experience! Worth every bit of time and $$$

More like 3.5, but I'll just round up to a 4.
I really really REALLY wanted to love Bacchanal Buffet.. but it wasn't as amazing as I thought it would be.
I went for the Sunday brunch (49.99) with family around 9:30 AM and there was no line, so we were seated right away. Inside is HUUUUGE and decor is super nice and modern. Service was on point and unlimited mimosas and champagne were nice. There were lots and lots of food options. However, the food rotation sucked but it made sense, because it was still early and it wasn't packed yet. By the time it was around 11 AM, more FRESH food came out.... FINALLY.

+
crab legs
salmon/tuna poke
hash browns
bacon
pad thai
unlimited mimosas
tropical juice
macarons
creme brulee
black sesame gelato

-
lobster benedict
sashimi 
dim sum
mushroom pizza

Honestly, the dessert station is the main reason I still want to give this buffet another try. Maybe for dinner???

Just get a plate of crab legs and call it a day.

Ahh..Vegas, home of the buffet experience. It's easy to see why people frequent Bacchanal. There's no shortage of tourists who want to hit up a buffet during their stay here, because that's just what you do in Vegas... well, that and drinking and gambling.

We came here for brunch on a Saturday morning, around 11:30am. There was a line, but it only took a few minutes to get seated.
$60 for a weekend brunch is what I'd call a once-in-a-while treat.
Bacchanal has one of the better buffet selections in a very bright, inviting dining room. The service is not too shabby either.

To start off, we loaded our plates high with King crab legs and devoured them. They are quite sweet, yet also very salty. Sometimes the crab meat sticks to the shell, so some of them may be a little overcooked. To accompany the crab, we also had mussels, clams, and shrimp.

On the meat front, we had prime rib, brisket, sausages. There were also little baskets of fried chicken. To balance out all the meat, I went for the eggs Benedict.

Then we moved on to the noodle variety. There was laksa, pho, soba noodles. Where there are noodles, especially laksa, I just have to try it, but these definitely are not a must-try.
We concluded the savory portion with tuna poke, salmon poke, and edamame.

Finally, for dessert, I divulged in chocolate brownie, cheesecake, creme brulee, and matcha cake. I always enjoyed how the dessert section of the buffet is lined with bite-sized squares of treats.

If you are looking to eat for volume, I'd say any buffet on the strip will satisfy. However, the crab legs here are the featured item. Otherwise, it is a rather expensive meal. In short, just get a few plates of crab legs and some vegetables to balance things out. That's all you need... and a little dessert... and a drink. Unless you're set on trying out the bulk of the selection, I'd say this is the best way to get the most bang for your buck.
Overall, I give Bacchanal a 7.5/10

I had really high expectations for this buffet. From everything I'd read it was deemed to be one of the very best in Vegas. As we got in our Uber he even let us know we were headed to the best buffet in Vegas so I was excited and was prepared to experience some of the best food. First off the line was insane and didn't make much sense. You had to go to a kiosk and enter your party information and it tells you to return to the line when you receive a text message so we did just that. We had about a 25 minute wait and decided to walk around until we received the message. We got the message got on line and had to wait an additional 30 minutes to pay and then about 15-20 minutes on another line to be seated. By the time we were seated we were famished. To begin I tried a ceasar salad (yum but hard to mess up),  chicken tamales (pass) salmon poke (yum) on my next trip I headed to the carving station for some prime rib (excellent), mashed potatoes, mac and cheese, green beans and everything was good. Lastly I tried some salmon and crab legs. For dessert I grabbed some gelato, lava cake,  and mini doughnuts which were all ok but not amazing. My friend had the cheesecake and she said it tasted sour so she was extremely disappointed. Overall there are a ton of options so maybe we didn't experience the best of the best because of what we selected but I just didn't feel wowed by any of the dishes we tried. I probably wouldn't go back to this buffet if I was in Vegas again. For the same amount of $$ I could have a really good entree somewhere else.

My wife and I were visiting Las Vegas in early December 2014, and decided to try the "Buffet of Buffets" for $50 each. Unlimited access to five buffets for 24 hours. Bacchanal at Caesar's was, by far, the best buffet I've ever been to. As easy as it is to spend $50 for a meal in Vegas, this meal alone would have been well-worth the cost of the buffet pass.

The selection of food is tremendous, the food is all really good, there are tons of desserts, plenty of healthy food options, and many of them are prepared to order. As busy as it was, we never had to wait to get food. Our drinks (including mimosas on the Sunday we were there) were brought promptly and refilled often. The staff was very courteous, and the place was very clean.

We would have gone back again, but our flight was leaving at 4pm the next day, and we already had lunch reservations. We actually discussed canceling that reservation and going to Bacchanal again, but didn't want to waste our Groupon for the other restaurant. (It turns out we wish we had, we had a pretty terrible experience at Pampas Churrascaria, which I wrote a review about as well).

A couple tips:
- Get in line before you're starving. You'll probably wait at least 20-30 minutes for a table.
- Visit the crepe station!

Normal buffet....
Nothing special except the dessert.
I think i expected too much.
Great service but it didnt worth the price.

Came here last weekend with my husband and another couple and while we had a good experience, I didn't feel like it was a GREAT experience.  It was $50 per person and at 9:30 PM on a Sunday night, we waited about 20 minutes.

The Seafood station made the buffet worth it, but nothing else.  The fresh Crab Legs that they steamed right in front of you were delicious.  There was no Lobster which was a disappointment given that they have Lobster in a showcase before you enter (false advertisement).  The Asian station was pretty good -- but the Sushi was no good.  The presentation was awful and it didn't taste very fresh either.  The Steamed Dumplings, however, were good.  The Meat station was good but they didn't have Filet (which I heard they were supposed to have).  I found the Lamb Chops to have too sweet of a marinade.  And the slices of Ribeye they were giving were nothing but fat.  The Wagyu beef sliders were good but the patties were too dry.  Fried chicken was bland.  Pasta was sub par.  The dessert was a disappointment too.  I believe that they boast 147 desserts -- I think I saw like 10.  And the only one that was remotely good was the chocolate chip cookie in a ramekin and one of the ice creams I tried.

Not an experience that really sticks out to me so we probably wouldn't come back.  We kept hearing that this is the best buffet in Vegas, so I'm really bummed that everything else must be worse.

USE THE YELP CHECK-IN OFFER!!!!!! It's a free pass to skip the long winding line. Just walk up to the first line for VIP or something and show them the check-in offer!

Once we got seated, I immediately went for the crab legs that I saw on the way in. I slowly made my way through the seafood to the cajun to the Mexican...then, Boyfriend told me to go around the corner. WHAT THE HELL?!!?!??! The buffet basically circles around the whole back of the restaurant! There's dim sum at the end of the wall! Dessert is in the center.

The food is preeeeeetty fricking amazing. You have your fresh seafood, cajun, Mexican, Italian, Chinese, and probably more that I didn't get to because I tapped out SUPER early. But, of course, I got seconds for dessert. My favorite desserts were the Rice Pudding, Creme Brulee, and Matcha/Chocolate Cake. They also had Matcha White Chocolate-Covered Strawberries, which were amazing.

The service was great from the cashier to the hostesses to the waitresses. You can also tell the chefs actually LIKE working there. When I go to other less fancy buffets, you can tell the chefs are dying inside. But these chefs are laughing, smiling to their customers, and joking around with each other. It's nice to see. Eating at a restaurant with good service and happy employees makes a pretty big difference...
Waiting time is crazy long around 2:00 PM. After 1 hr, I left since they expect I need 1-2 hrs more just to enter.

Food-wise, this place is awesome and tops my fave buffet list, knocking Wicked Spoon out of the top spot.  I loved their Asian section and almost everything we had was delicious.  The peach lemonade also hit the spot, adding some more calories to the mix!

Quick tips:
- Sign up for a Total Rewards account and you get a $1 off the buffet price.
- Go about an hour before the food prices switch from lunch to dinner.  You'll pay about $10 less and after a while, they'll start switching things over to dinner time menu!
- Go in the Caesars Palace front lobby/check-in entrance to find this place.  If you try to find Bacchanal from the Forum Shops, you will walk for approximately a million miles and need to hire a sherpa to lead the way, since Caesars doesn't have any signage leading to it along the way!

Food list, from what we could remember:
Asian section: Young Chow fried rice, ma po tofu (no pork), lo mein with chicken, king pow chicken, soup dumplings, deep fried dumplings (gyoza), spring rolls, steamed BBQ pork buns, spicy fish, blackened chicken soup, miso soup, hot and sour soup, edamame, seaweed salad, marinated shrimp with cucumbers, spicy tuna roll, California roll, shrimp tempura roll, salmon and tuna sushi, made to order ramen, pho, or udon.

Small salad bar (SKIP, duh)

Italian section: Sliced salami and other meats and cheeses, variety of pizzas, garlic bread knots, meatballs, penne a la vodka, vegetable pasta, individual lasagna dishes.

Mexican station: At least 10 types of salsas and guacamole, refried beans and chips, pulled chicken in salsa verde, made to order mini steak or pork tacos (pork taco not tasty), Mexican rice.

4 kinds of soup including clam chowder, cream of mushroom.  Assorted breads and rolls.

BBQ/American section: Coleslaw and other cold salads, corn on the cob, Mac and cheese, baked beans, 4 kinds of sausage, ribs, ham, brisket, corn dogs, waffle fries, mini sliders (no good), normal tater tots, sweet potato tater tots, truffle potatoes Au gratin, fried chicken and sweet potato fries.

Seafood section: Shrimp and grits, mussels pot, clambake, shrimp cocktail, crab legs (split in half), ceviche (dinner only), oysters (dinner only).

Desserts - gelato and sorbet, lots of cakes, warm chocolate cookie, molten lava cake, at dinner they added chocolate covered strawberries, mochi balls, gelato, macaroons, crepes with fillings bar, chocolate mousse lollipops and strawberry cheesecake lollipops.

If you go at weekend brunch, the price includes unlimited mimosas.

Complaints:
- The price is like whoa, crazy.  I guess if this is your one meal for the day, it's reasonable.  I don't know if they can justify a $10+ premium on Wicked Spoon, although they have a wider selection.
- FOODS ARE NOT LABELED.  There are some sections with a half-assed attempt, but most of the things just flat-out aren't even labeled.  For example, 4 types of soup - not a single label.  This is just stupid.
- The layout/design of certain sections are also stupid.  The designer should be forced to go through the buffet and see what kind of contortionist positions are required for some of the serving areas, like the soup, which has a comically oversized ladle and a shelf right above the soup tureens, so there's no logical way to get soup easily without spilling half of it on the counter - fun!  All the sauces for the meats are at the front of the carving station, so you have to backtrack to put sauce on meats after you've gotten yours carved.  Same with a backwards setup on the seafood.  Hire someone with half a brain to re-arrange things!

disappointed。
3-hour waiting
oyster is sandy，and there is no sashimi。
dessert is ok，but there is only a few kinds of fruit .
The Chinese noodle with soup is very good, recommend it!
I love the crab leg the most, and the service is not that good . Service only come once to collect our plate
We picked the Bacchanal Buffet because of the reviews on Yelp. We enjoyed our meal very much. Definitely take a bite of everything!

After weeks and weeks of reading Yelp reviews and thumbing through the thousands of photos this place has, finally got to try it on my birthday!!

We came on Sunday 8/18/13 around 3:30pm. I was so freaked out by the horror stories I've read about the wait times. I made my husband power walk through the Caesar, as if that was going to get us there earlier. I certainly did not want to wait 2 hours, considering we had a plane to catch later that night. Thankfully, it took about 25 minutes to get to the cashier. $51.99 per person because dinner time starts at 3pm. Total with tax was $110 without gratuity. By 4pm, we were standing in line to go to our tables. There were 2 other groups of two people in front of us, and we were 2 people as well. The waitress took all 3 of our groups and guided us to our seats!! We must've been waiting in that line for only 5 minutes! Score!!! Otherwise, we would have probably waited another 30 minutes.

The Highlights:

**Jumbo Shrimp
**Medium Rare Prime Rib
**Steamed Crab Legs (don't get the cold ones in the front, go to the pizza area for the hot ones)
**Brisket (so juicy!!) 
**Lobster Corn Bisque (real chunks of lobster)
**Truffled Potatoes (creamy and cheesy, I could've eaten plates of these)
**Beef Pho (surprisingly delicious meat and broth, wish there were more noodles)
**Tacos and Guac (so fresh tasting!!! Tacos made to order, piping hot)

**The jumbo shrimp were the best I've ever tasted!! Seriously, they were so big, so succulent, so juicy!! I freaking ate a whole plate of them with cocktail sauce!! So delicious!! Prime rib was equally delicious too. Perfectly medium rare, juicy, and really soft. The guy at the meat section was super friendly too. Line went pretty quick in both meat and seafood areas. 

***Also forgot to mention unlimited drinks!! Free drinks!! Woohoo! I guess that's understandable considering how much we paid. They had all the sodas and I had some hot tea because the AC was blasting in there!! (swear it's to get people out).

The Lows:

**Sushi stations (sad, wish there was nigiri, which apparently was out)
**Dim Sum (it was okay) 
**Shrimp Alfredo (kinda goppy, sauce was a bit too garlicky)
**Mushroom Risotto (big fan of risotto but this was like mush)
**Cold Crab Legs (eating cold crab was not good, needs butter or there's just no flavor)
**Horchata (I'll give you the presentation, cute bottles. It was a bit watered down)
**The Whole Dessert Section (kind of a let down, but then again not too big on desserts in the first place. I did like the gummy bears, green tea mochi ice, and macarons).

Overall, a great experience. Though we both stuffed ourselves to death and felt literally like throwing up afterwards, we were glad we went. No one ever came around to tell us we had to leave (2 hour max) and the decor was lovely at the restaurant. A bit hard to find in the Caesar's, you kind of have to weave through the hotel to find the place. Definitely worth the money!

My advice is go REALLY hungry.  The food is incredible and there are MANY different varieties of it.  I've eaten all three meals there, and you definitely get more bang for your buck at lunch.  It is expensive.  It's about $35 for lunch.  You'll pay more than that at most good restaurants in town and for much smaller portions.

best buffet in vegas. Worth every single penny. They have wide variety of menu items to choose from. crab legs, chinese food, steak, sausage, noodle bar, soups, pho, dim sum.. and much more. it can get a little bit overwhelming at first, but take your time and try and eat a little of everything. We come here everytime we go to vegas. and sometimes just to eat here. Will def keep coming here.

In terms of a buffet, this is by far the best in quality and selection. It's located inside of Caesar's near their casino. We went on the Friday of a busy weekend at 11:30am and waited around 30 mins. We had an extremely large party (16 people) but they were quick to accommodate us.

Upon being escorted to our table, I quickly went to scour the variety of options they offered. Dim sum, Chinese, Mongolian bbq, salads, assorted fruit, fresh Mexican grill/tacos, American comfort (mini red velvet pancakes, wagyu beef sliders, mac n' cheese, scallop potatoes, sweet potato tots, cheesy broccoli, brussel sprouts), pasta, sushi (rolls, salmon and tuna nigiri), ramen bar, cheese platters, pizza, prime rib, brisket, assorted sausages, turkey and a seafood bar (crab legs, oysters, clams, grilled salmon, and cocktail shrimp).

Like with any buffet, I skipped the Chinese and salad section and headed straight towards the meat and carbs.

I was able to grab the last of their breakfast food, mini red velvet pancakes, to start off. Sadly, this looked better than it tasted :( It was a tad dry and lacked flavor. 

Their truffle mac n' cheese was really good at first but quickly got too heavy for me. 

The meats are worth salivating over but I preferred the brisket over the prime rib because of the fatty flavor. The sausages were also tasty!

My boyfriend tried the dimsum and was surprisingly impressed. The sushi was bland and not worth getting.

We thought the seafood bar was delicious! The stars were the huge pieces of shrimp with sauce and the oysters. 

Closing with their amazing dessert selection, we tried a little bit of everything: green tea crème brulee, green tea cookie with red bean filling, green tea tiramisu, flan, cookie pops, and ice creammm!! The desserts were pretty good, just wish we were able to try a few more items 

Overall, we loved everything and had a great experience. Lunch was around $33 but after gratuity, we paid $45. This buffet is worth it and would recommend if you're in Vegas.

Wow, not usually a Buffet fan (Gluttony!!) but this buffet is unreal! 
Prices are a bit on the higher side than other buffets in Vegas but the quality and variety of the food is excellent! 

They have fresh seafood (HUGE king prawns, crab, ceviche, oysters, mussels etc), roasted meats, smoked meats, chips, chicken wings (presented in little individual baskets), mexican (soo many condiments here, unreal!), sushi, Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese, Italian, French, amazing desserts etc..
I could go into detail, but I think everyone's covered all of the different cuisine's in these reviews. 

It's the highest quality buffet I've ever been to, top restaurant quality. 

I just wished I had about 10 stomachs so that I could get the most out of it & out of the price tag!

Food: 8/10
 The Bachannal  is definitely one of the best buffets in Vegas. It's a little on the pricier side, but the food is well worth it! Their seafood bar is well stocked, but there's ALWAYS a line so make sure you grab a friend and bring back as much as you can! But beware of dirty glances when if grab a few dozen king crab legs like we did! Their other selections are really good too and I don't know if they usually have this but their TACO STATION is LA quality! Real legit, real good! My favorite has got to be the dessert bar though! They always have such a huge selection and if you're not into the experimenting with different desserts, their Gelato is a good go to as well! The food here is simply amazing
Service: 8/10
 Definitely very good service here. The waiters are very patient with us, especially since we're a large group with 4~ tables or so and they were very accomodating. We started leaving a few people at a time and consolidating our tables and the servers were very understanding of that
Overall: 8/10
Additional Notes: You definitely need to come here! And being Diamond/Platinum/7stars definitely helps as these lines are YUUUUUGE.

Mark was our waiter last night.  He was very professional and welcoming.  He made sure we get our drinks as quickly as possible and cleaned our table frequently.   The food options were great.  Only problem is the lines for sea food.  I wish there was a better design for that.

I am a VIP at the ARIA specifically MGM GROUP. I exclusively eat at MGM restaurants and have never eaten outside of it in the past 20+ years. For this trip I decided to get out of my comfort zone and try a new place, the Bacchanal buffet, which I have heard good things about. I was totally and utterly disappointed. 

On August 6,2018, I brought my family of 5 to this buffet because it was ranked #1 on Google. I waited in line for around 30 minutes to pay. After paying, we had to wait another 25 minutes to get into the buffet. 

Not going to lie, the buffet looked extraordinary. There was a very large selection of food and a huge space for dining. 

During the meal, my plates were never taken away. I had to tell her to come take them and even trying to get her attention was difficult. There was not even once that she came to check up on us. We had to raise our hands like lunatics to even get her attention. 

At around the 2 hour mark, our server told me to leave the table because "time was up." I had not finished my food yet and the server told me to leave. I was incredibly unhappy that she asked me to leave because I did not know that there was a 2 hour limit. I cannot believe that this casino has this kind of service. I would have expected more from a nice casino like Caesars Palace. 

I will not returning to this buffet and I will stick with the buffets at MGM group.

Thoroughly enjoyed the large see room and well prepared choices to pick from. I purchased the Groupon for two and all went flawlessly. I recommend the eggs Benedict - well prepared and the hollandaise sauce was close to perfection. Breakfast sausages properly prepared - nova lox was in abundance. The coffee and mimosas were delicious. The atmospheres isn't like your typical buffet. Dim lights with comfortable seating. Waitresses are responsive and polite. With two hours to eat - get the bang for your buck and pace yourself.

Like everyone has said. Best buffet on the strip. Service top notch. Yes it's pricey but you do get what you pay for. 
Excellent meat selection hell excellent selection of everything really. Most every review mentioned the peach green tea. So I thought I'd try that. It was very thirst Quenching..... I had 4 of them. They have steamed and cold crab. I prefer the steamed. It takes a while to get but worth the wait. 
I would send anyone I knew here to the bacchanal it's worth every penny. Enjoy

Some quick tips, this place is solid.

The prime rib is bomb.  The brisket is good.  
All of the Asian food is highly mediocre.  Considering it's not their specialty they did good.

Crab legs cut in half reduce the mess, and the flavor; catch 22 there.

The dessert is mega bomb. Hit the lava cake a couple times, that one is a well made chocolate deliciousness. 

There's plenty to eat here so go easy on the meat, otherwise you will be a gassy mess a few hours later. It's delicious, but not the second time around. 

This place is worth the 90 minute wait on a Saturday night once.  Only once.  You can pay $15 to skip the line, but that makes your meal $66 for a buffet.  If you're a baller, fine, spend that money, but that's $15 you can use betting on black, or food for your hamster.  

Enjoy.

I rather starve myself than come back to this abomination of a buffet. 

Yes, i went in w/ high expectations because USA TODAY raved it as "best buffet in the nation"  & My friends were all singing its high praises, but still, the food they served ended up offending me. For the price it was, it had no value. 

The buffet came out to $52 because we had the discount card, but definitely not worth even a dime. 

Food looked pretty but tasted old, stale, either too flavorful or too bland. I think even drunk me wouldnt have stomached the food they served. 

They have made to order ramen, pho, and udon, I decided to be brave after wasting 2 full plates of random things to order the ramen. 

Wow, it was the only thing I was able to continue eating even though said thing was actually too salty. 

Maybe i went on a bad day, but my whole group was disappointed at this place. If i wanted to dine like that, i woulda gone to the local food court where they have panda express and a burger joint and paid a lil less.

I liked this place quite a bit.
Food was good, they have a HUGE variety of things, anything you can imagine food they have it there. From Asian to BBQ to sushi to crab legs(chilled) and hot and deserts to Chinese food to fruits to Italian. Everything tasting fresh and great 
It was a Friday night so it was super busy waiting wasn't that bad tho about 35 min from the time to got there to the time we sat down at our table.
It's pricey but I think it's priced well for what you have.
We had a party of 6 with the all you can drink alcohol and our tab came to a total of $483 plus we left $80 for tips!
Our waitress Milka she was very helpful and hands on!! Very Helprin and still super friendly 
We had a great time 
I will be back at this place.

I've been to my fair share of Las Vegas buffets and this has got to be the best one I've been to. I was more into the seafood selection they had on a weekday dinner. The meat selection was very good, especially the wagyu. They had cuisine from Asia, South America, Mexico, Europe, etc. I really appreciate when they take the time on their desserts. The gelato, shaved ice and crepes were a nice touch. I definitely will come back for weekend brunch.

Well deserving 4 stars for a buffet.  

We came here around 2pm ($45 per person which includes mimosas) for Sunday brunch and there was no line.  But the cashier mentioned that the lines were insane at around noon.

Bacchanal provides an endless array of goodness from authentic dim sum to fresh snow crab legs.  The 12 million dollar renovation is definitely noticeable and very pleasing to the eye.  

Favorites dishes:  Al Pastor tacos, beef nigiri, dim sum, shrimp cocktails (these bad boys were huge), brisket, prime rib, and the fried chicken wings.

Only downside was that our waiter was non-existent, took forever to get our drink order and rarely checked up on us for refills.

My Vegas Buffet ranking would go:  1st:  Bacchanal, 2nd:  Wynn Buffet, 3rd:  Wicked Spoon.

best of best...
    I like     Dim sum but I don't trust any local chinese restaurant or chinatown.- they all use bleach flour, and they mix it with the little amount of meat to let it look fluppy ..so not sure if it real meat.  Buchannal is the best in Dim sum..no bleach no blended flour/meat....real stuff.

it is the best.
   sushi -excellent
   dessert -excellent
   seafood-excellent
   italian -excellent
   
   worth the price...yeah $50 is expensive ..Cosmoplitan suck now so my top 3 is Bellagio, sometime M resort, Aria. Wynn is OK but nice atmosphere.

I've been to who knows how many buffets in Vegas and this is by far the best. It is the most expensive but you get what you pay for here. I can't even name everything I ate the last time but I am going back! Crab, prime rib, beef rib, dim sum, sushi, tacos, seafood... You name it they got it. The only thing that wasn't great was the sushi. Pretty poor showing for this but if you're going to do sushi do it right and go to a Japanese restaurant. Moral of the story... GO here if you have time if you want a great buffet.
This is great buffet...rule of thumb, eat slow and small portions of each item...the steak, and other meat was my favorite but i am a meat lover so i may be biased...enjoy all selection...

Was there today and overall it was a disappointment.  If you are going to try it based on hearing "it's the best buffet in Las Vegas" do lunch at around 2:30 pm.  (Lunch time pricing ends at 3:00pm) It is not worth more than $38.00.. I went for the seafood.  The quality is not up to standard. There was no king crab leg, and the large crab legs they put out on the seafood cold bar for dinner (Switchover is around 3:30 where they put out more items for the dinner bar) The crab legs were skimpy and FROZEN, not thawed out. (Maybe that was punishment for budget conscious people trying to get a dinner buffet, at a lunch time price, because they might be thawed out by 8pm for the mid dinner crowd. The crab legs that were a little thawed out were waterlogged.  The "shrimp cocktail" was yellowish, and waterlogged as well.  The mussels were not fresh, and the salmon was not fresh. The buffet (with the exception of the meat counter) had a hard time keeping the hot food from being cold thus the food is not maintaining the right temperature, which might be the reason people reported getting sick from the buffet in other reviews. From the time I got from the buffet, to my table, my pork ribs were cold.  They give you this rubber grabber for getting your dishes, as they warn you the dishes are hot, but I never used that thing. Dear Bacchanal Manager-- Save money, from buying those things and invest in the seafood part of the bar. As far as the desserts go, they are cute, but tasteless, with the exception of this dark chocolate mini cake with a raspberry on top, the fruit toppings and the creme brulee was good. My first experience of gelato was in Italy, so this gelato paled in comparison. The prime rib was the best thing on the bar, so I got my money worth on that and the sushi rolls were decent.  Save yourself some money, and do not pay extra for this buffet, it's not worth it.  (If you read the other reviews carefully they did state the quality went down, so be sure when you are looking at the photos look at the year the photos were uploaded).

It's a must every time I go to Vegas. Definitely get what you are paying for. The Buffett is endless. Seafood, meat craving, sushi, Mexican, Chinese.... Everything. I'm not a big dessert person, but even I get a plate full when I go. Expect a little wait, but it is well worth it!

Looks can be deceiving.  Food selection looks amazing but the food tastes blah.  Brunch for 2 adults cost over $100 USD and everything we sampled was disappointing.  Unless you're into cold eggs Benedict and an assortment of stale pastries, save your money and try your luck elsewhere.

Wow, the Bacchanal buffet is delicious, amazing, so worth the price. Get there early as the line grows quickly. Once inside they have stations. A seafood, American, Mexican, Asian and dessert. The sushi was yummy. But I recommend the brisket. I tried every station except the pizza and seafood. I'm not a big sea food fan but that was the busiest station. Me and my boyfriend easily had 5 plates lol. It is so good.

It is ok buffet in vegas
But not worth to spend that much money and waiting a long time.
I was expected to have more sushi in buffet
Only few kind of sushi rolls. Disappointed..
If you really care about new and nice decor in side of buffet rest, you can go and try.
I will go back to buffet in bellagio in the next time.

If I could give this a ten I would. One of the best buffets that I have ever been to! It was pretty pricy ($60 per person with tax), but I would say worth a try if you haven't yet. 

The favorite dishes that I would recommend include: 
- crab legs:  so extremely sweet, much higher quality than other buffets that I have.  To die for, especially with the butter sauce that they have.  Yum! 
- The grilled meat section:  they have everything from lamb, prime rib, spicy (and non-spicy) sausages, applewood smoked brisket
- Being Asian, typically try to avoid the Asian section of the buffet, but I decided to try it anyway.  Was so pleasantly surprised at the authenticity of the food!   I especially really liked the tom yum soup. 
-  The dessert section.  Ooooh man!  They had everything , from chocolate covered strawberries, boba, mochi ice cream- all the desirables.  

The only thing is for this place, just be prepared to wait for a while.  We got there at 2pm, still had to wait another 2 hours.

Hands down our favorite buffet! We went here at 2pm and was seated by 2:30pm. The only reason there was a 30 minute wait was because there are not a lot of seats for parties of 2. Larger parties are seated first. We were there for almost 3 hours because we had to try all their foods! All their foods are delicious, most are cold but still tastes good. There was a lot of us waiting for the dinner transition but nothing really changed. There were more meats near the carving station and that's about it. They did take out the crab legs during dinner and boy, the lines were long so I did not even bother. As for service, it was impeccable! Our servers made sure that our drinks were never empty!

Mm, I'd like to give it 3.5 stars.  

Bacchanal Buffet is in Ceasar's Palace, beyond the casino and near the desserts cafe. You can't miss it, it's where the HUGE line is.  We must have gotten there by 12pm and didn't get seated for another 1hour and 40 minutes.  line was crazy.  We got there and ordered the bottomless mimosas, which end at 3pm. We paid about $41.99 for Sunday's lunch.  

There was a good variety of food there. There's asian foods in the back (sushi, peking duck, ramen, udon noodle soup, etc), then cheese and charcuterie, pizza and pasta (the meatballs were really good), then there's your mexican/latino station (it's more like a taco station), BBQ station (some were really dry. I got the ribeye and that was juicy but really fatty), french fries and tator tots (sweet potatoe tots were really good), then lastly, your seafood station. The seafood station had snow crabs, oysters, and shrimp. I wanted to see some more stuff like lobster tails, maybe steamed mussels, but none of those were available.  

Salad station was limited but I liked the garbanzo salad and the japanese seaweed salad.  

Dessert station was AWESOME. get the lava chocolate chip cookie, mochi ice creams, and coconut macaroons. So good. We also got a ice cream cone on the way out of the buffet.  I highly recommend it, it was a good experience and worth the wait.

Hands down the BEST buffet ever! They have a wide variety of foods. From steamed crab legs (that are cut in half so it's easy to eat) to pork chops to dim sum to calamari....list goes on and on! Waiters are very friendly and are attentive. They tell you to put your finished plates in the center of the table and they will take them out. Their desserts were AMAZING! I had to try the crepes, cupcakes, and their macarons are so yummy!

Reason why I'm giving 4 stars:

There is an extremely long wait during dinner time.
Pretty pricey! But trust me, if you're HUNGRY, this buffet is the way to go!
Last, but not least, no one told me that there were plate grips (there should be signs or the waiters should warn us about the HOT plates). My hands were burning until I had to ask the guy in the kitchen what the purple rubber things were!

Recently went there for the Holiday buffet (Christmas eve) and it wasn't the best Vegas dining experience, and really, far from it. Also suspecting food poisoning from their oysters.

First off: The line was ridiculous. I understand it was busy because of the Holiday, but the wait time system was ridiculous. We got our time ticket at 4:30pm, and it told us to come back at 8:30. We come back right on time (They don't let you get in line earlier than the ticket time), and aren't seated until 10:15pm. So that was nearly 6 hours wait time! Not worth it for the price!

Secondly: Food was passable at best...until I woke up with extreme nausea and puking which my doctor confirmed was food poisoning. Being the only person sick in my family and the only one that ate the oysters, I think I have my suspect.

Service was alright, our server was a little forgetful, but it was Christmas eve, so I didn't want to blame them. 

Summary: Seafood got me in terrible pain, line is more like a line at Disneyland, price is not worth it.
Like any other buffet. Lots of variety to choose from, but food quality was not five stars worthy!

compare to cosmopolitan, I were more prefer to go cosmopolitan because their food is more impressed to me. and avoid to wait for 3hours in line, we go at eary morning for brunch in xmas holiday. $51/person for xmas brunch, I didn't feel its worth.

Anticipated this buffet to be the best I have ever had and it exceeded me expectations. They had complimentary bloody Mary's for brunch. Couldn't decide between that or the fresh squeezed juices which come in their own bottle. I went for the passion juice which is a combination of mango,
Lemon and orange juice. As far as food was concerned, I loved the sweet potato tater tots. They had a maple flavor that made it hard to finish! I also fell in love with the chicken and waffles. It consisted of a nice waffle cone which was filled with criss cross fries and a mild hot wing. The combination of all three items was like music in my mouth. The pre-slit crab legs and shrimp were a definite plus!! Was pleasantly surprised to see ethnic food items  like pho  bo or chilaquiles. The Mexican food section should of had more variety though. It seemed they seated patrons according to their ethnic background. I got seated next to the Mexican section and the Asian patrons got seated in the back where the Asian food was. The Asian section was very well varied.The congee lacked flavor. It was overall a great buffet and will return !!

Started off my birthday weekend in Vegas! We decided to try a buffet for dinner because why not...Vegas is known for their crazy buffets. My boyfriend and I were deciding on which place to try and bacchanal had the best reviews out of most at a decent price. We called cesears palace around 4:40 pm on Thursday and they said it would be around a 20 min wait. It's super easy to walk there or catch a free shuttle from some of the hotels. We caught the shuttle from the Aria to Bellagio and walked inside from there straight to cesears palace. 

The wait was only about 10 min when we got there at 5:30! It's $54.99 per person ok weekdays (M-T) not bad... The menu there is extensive! A seafood station, carving station, pasta station, salads, appetizers, Asian food, and dessert! 

Our server came to us when we sat down to take our drink order. She also constantly came to clear plates and ask us if we were doing okay which was nice! They also have hot tea if you want on top of cold drinks. If you're in the boozy mood you could pay $15 for unlimited beer, wine, and champagne! 

I really enjoyed the shrimp cocktail, the wagyu beef,  paella, Caesar salad, and crab legs! Some of the crab legs were frozen from being on the ice so log though. The oysters were okay...super fishy to me. And the prime rib, usually one of my favorite buffet items, was dry. The wagyu was so much better. I wanted to get the udon from the noodle station but when we got there, the worker told us it would be a 10 min wait and only the seafood laska was ready. I was confused because they are essentially the same...only different broths. He was also kind of rude to us the way he said it...ended up trying the laska which is noodles in a spicy curry broth. 

Finally, dessert! They have a crepe station, gelato bar, and a bunch of other desserts. I tried the chocolate lava cake (OMG!), matcha cake, creme brule, and chocolate covered strawberry. Definitely go for the lava cake. Creme brule was good too. I would've tried everything if I wasn't so full. 

All in all, it was a pretty good buffet! Go early to beat the lines. And there is a 2 hr time limit.

Needless to say, you should try to arrive as hungry as possible. This buffet is deservedly very expensive and usually has a pretty long wait. I passed the time at the poker tables on the other side of the casino. The food is soooooooo good.

Though, sometimes they advertise something and don't actually have it. In our case, it was the lobster bisque. However, you'll definitely dine like a king and this is probably as close as I'll ever get to being royalty.

Pricey- yes; worth it- yes. This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas currently. The food selection is huge, the quality is great, the Desert section pretty amazing as well. Crab legs are already cut in half for you, all buffets should do that. I still enjoy eating at the rio buffet, wicked spoon in Cosmo, and other buffets; but this buffet is definitely on top of my list currently

Disappointing experience. Started with Rude service at the cashier. Even with the long line the one cashier would continually close and come back after every customer. Lots of standing around doing nothing. Thanks for wasting my vacation time. This is what I get $108?!?!

The downhill continued with a the guy at carving station loding our plates with fat and gristle. He knows what he did was unacceptable but obviously didn't care. 

At this point we complained . The manager listened to our complaints and apologized. Furthermore the head chef came over and apologized as well. He returned with a giant plate of crab legs which we enjoyed. These two people understand hospitality but unfortunately I don't think the people working the various stations at this place get it. 


The manager gave us a pass to skip the line on our next trip but frankly this was not sufficient to make me go back or recommend this place. For this price I expect better food and less attitude. Too many other, better dining options in Las Vegas to tolerate this nonsense.

I just don't u understand why people are so crazy about Bucchanal Buffet in Las Vegas.  Always full of customers in line to get in..  Good thing I had my players card..  I was able to skip the long line and get in within 5 minutes.  

I like the interior design and variety of food they serve.  But it doesn't mean it taste good..  Most of the foods were salty..  I tried Calvin (Korean BBQ), clam chowder, crab legs, crab craws, beef brisket, etc..  I don't understand why they would make all food so salty.  

Compare to the amount I paid..  it is just not worth it..  It is good to know but I wouldn't come back..  one time experience is good enough.   I rather eat at other buffet such as Buffet in Aria or Wicked Spoons in Cosmopolitan.    

However, I do recommend the coffee..  This is the only thing I like about this place but not worth paying $50.00

What an amazing dining experience!  Definitely the best buffet I've ever been to.  I was there as breakfast slowly transitioned into lunch.  I begin the meal at the breakfast bar. Fantastic omelette, perfectly cooked. While there, I got some of the best smoked salmon I've had in the United States. Not too salty, just right.  Then I wandered over to the seafood section, where I grabbed an amazing shrimp and grits bowl.  Then a delicious dessert crêpe, which I enjoyed with little samplings from the Asian, European and American snacks sections.  When the lunch food came out at 11, it was time for the showstoppers. A nice collection of crab claws to accent the incredible prime rib!  I am a finicky eater and this was probably the most food I've stuffed myself with in the last year.  A delight!  I wasn't hungry again until late that night.

I really wasn't planning on coming back to Bacchanal Buffet for my recent trip to Vegas.  It was all situational because I literally spent a good 30 mins walking back and forth across the middle of The Strip trying to decide where to eat breakfast.  That when I just said the hell with it and go to Bacchanal!

It's been literally a year since the last time I've been to Bacchanal Buffet and at that time they had just opened.  The food has actually gotten better but the price has gone up.  Here now are all the plates I had from this visit:  

First plate went with comfort foods.
Fried Chicken & Waffle, Mini Chicago Dog, Huevo Ranchero -- http://bit.ly/IIdyfe
All good stuff.  The Mini Chicago Dog was the best part! 

Second plate went for all seafood.
Mussels Meuniere, Shrimp & Grits, Pan Roasted Salmon, Seafood Paella --  http://bit.ly/1h4c5vx
This was probably my favorite plate I put together.  The mussels were really good with nice garlicky taste, the salmon was cooked nicely, and the Paella and Shrimp Grits provided good filler.

Third plate covered the meat station.
Truffle Polenta, Roasted Prime Rib, Roasted Mushrooms, Kielbasa, and Shrimp Cocktail --  http://bit.ly/1fanybJ
I was starting to get full at this point but once again, no complaints with this plate.

Then I noticed they actually had a ramen station so I went ahead and tried it.
Ramen with bamboo shoots and chasiu pork -- http://bit.ly/IIe2SF
It was meh.  LOL  Broth wasn't too bad though

Finally, desserts.
Strawberry Peppermint Creme Puff -- http://bit.ly/IIefFw
Key Lime Tart -- http://bit.ly/1h4cmyF
Mango Tart -- http://bit.ly/IIedgC
Their desserts are very comparable to Wicked Spoon and Wynn.  So no matter what you pick up, you'll be in for a pretty and decadent treat.

Overall, I was pretty satisfied with my return visit to Bacchanal.  I'm a little on the fence with the $27 price tag for lunch (I meant to come for breakfast, but just missed the deadline and ended up paying a little more for lunch price), but for what I picked up, it paid itself off.  It's still one of the best buffets on the strip!

Skeptics no more. Very doubtful when we were in the line up parting with our $50 a piece; and became total believers on the way out two hours later.

Definitely the best buffet value currently in Vegas (perhaps anywhere).  If you are a foodie and you're in Vegas, not visiting this at least once will bring regrets.

Unusual service for a buffet.  They are actually friendly- up and down the line. Even the "chefs at the stations" will talk to you and answer questions.  Quite obvious that the training must have stressed customer service ... and it is working.

Most patrons are so happy that it is a joy to see.  Lots of complaints in the line for $$$ cost.  But inside the dining room - I've not heard one single complaint. 

Oysters tonight were sweet East Coast ... clear juice ... petite ... crisp. Wonderful.  Mignonette sauce, raw powerful horseradish, and lemon are all available.  King Crab legs - your choice hot or cold.  Oyster shooters, seafood Gazpacho, ceviche, jumbo shrimps, new zealand mussels, paella, lobster corn chowder, shirmp grits, crawfish cocktail ... just the seafood list goes on and on.

Ethnic and specialty stations were equally impressive.  Surprised to find EXCELLENT dim sum; highly authentic fried items, and even ginseng darkened chicken soup that is very very well prepared.

Desert station is another amazing place. I can go on and on.  But other reviewers have them well covered.

The quality of food, service, and preparation makes it hard not to get your money's worth.

And yes... agreed that it is at least 10x better than Bellagio's.  Easily justifies the marginally higher cost.

We have already decided to visit again tomorrow.  Before leaving Vegas.  

Vibes, operation, and value like this don't happen too often - and sometimes they don't last ... so we're going to enjoy it one more time while it is still great.

When we decided to have breakfast at the hotel in which we stayed I was not expected something extraordinarily but this place pleasant surprised me.  We ordered two meals: eggs Benedict with salmon and classic eggs Benedict which both looked spectacular in presentation. I used to eat lots of eggs Benedict but this meals were prepared excellent. It is difficult to explain the taste but every component of these meals and detail in the plate create usual dish something amazing. It seems like the meals came from chef who understands the meaning of good breakfast in the morning. The price was expensive but I didn't feel sorry.

The food was fresh and so much variety! Loved the dessert bar a lot! 
It was packed but still the service was great! 
Definitely will recommend ppl to go here.. It's the best buffet in town for sure! The best part they have a lot of variety for vegetarians and also some dessert options for the diabetic ppl! :)
Loved it. Prime rib and brisket was delicious. Good Quality food.  Sashimi looked fresh. Worth the money.

meh. not worth the hype. we went during brunch and had no waiting with the vip purchase. the regular line was somewhat long though. i was expecting to be wowed and each dish to taste exceptional. some were good, most were ok. even the desserts weren't that memorable. the hot and sour soup was delicious. the mimosa was excellent too. the mixed veggies next to the meat station was good but not great. the brisket was a bit dry and over seasoned. the sausages were ok. huevos rancheros lacked a crispy tostada under the topping. fried chicken was just ok. the breads were cold the more u got to the middle. they ran out of hot plate holders so you had to take your chances or use a napkin to grab the food. i would have loved the cookies on the buffet to be fresh baked. they seemed prepackaged. the red velvet pancakes were just ok. we tried several options and most were ok. it is a pretty and clean restaurant so i can't hate that, but i'll skip this buffet next time and go to a nice, made to order, sit down restaurant. i tried the bellagio buffet in 2009 and i still think about it quite fondly. bacchanal will soon be forgotten.

I've been here a few times and its one of my favorite buffets in Vegas. Its probably one of the most expensive but I think its worth it. My favorite thing to get here is probably the crab legs! Make sure you get them steamed so that they're even better! Their oysters are not that great but other than that, they have a variety of different foods from all cultures. My plates are always so random but I try to make my money worth it by eating a lot. And OH! I love their dessert bar. I love their gelato. I'd def recommend this buffet! Its inside Caesar's Palace!

Food was Good should've been a 4. However as ADA Compliant they Fail Fail Fail. due to issues from my 2 Hip Replacements and 8 Total Operations Traveling Long Distances I Still need to use My Travel Scooter. At the counter the "Gentlemen" Curtly explained to my Dad I and 1 Guest could Enter bypassing the Line. I was with my Dad and Mom who were Belatedly celebrating Their 50th Wedding Anniversary. The Bellagio Were Top Notch They Without even asking we Were Provided VIP Service Twice. However at the Baccahanal I had to work my way through the Snake of a line trying to maneuver my scooter through Lines of people with Children and try not to hit and run  people over. Upon reaching the Cashier and Paying for the "Las Vegas #1 Buffet. I was placed in a seperate line from my parents where I waited and waited and finally told I would get a table to Follow the Server and they would get my parents to meet me at the Table. Seriously? all that BS? I know it Hot and people are Hungry but for the Amount I Paid I should've been Treated Better. As far as ADA compliance This Experience was about the Fail I encountered at Knox Berry Farm Compaired to Disneyland. where Obvious High School Students without proper ADA training made Comments Completely Inappropriate. and didn't treat me Correctly. I Never expected to Recieve the same Treatment at Caesars Palace. After This Experience I Will never set Foot Um Wheel on this Property Again. I paid $$$ for What??!!

Oh my God holy amaze balls this buffet makes other buffets ashamed of themselves, especially the Luxor buffet. Feel free to read the review I wrote of that one yesterday. Everything here is sooooo good, there is a huge variety, and the decor is super nice too. My favorite item was the "pandan tiramisu." We got here when the breakfast buffet was ending and the lunch one was beginning, so we were only charged the breakfast price. It was about $50 for me and my husband. I will never go to a crappy buffet in Vegas again now that I know about this one.

I am giving this place a 3 because I'm very dissapointed considering the dinner price and food. The service was great, the ambiance was beautiful and warm food like pizza and sliders was awesome. However, I did not like the Asia  buffet area, omgod that was just gross! I did not like the Lamb considering how hard it was and the seafood choices just sucked. The desert, it was good EXCEPT....HOW DO YOU MESS UP ON FLAN!?!?! I MEAN COME ON! It did not taste good and the macaroons, was too sweet. I can go on and on but let's just say, you can go to any buffet but here....
Great food!! Mark, our server, did a great job!! He made sure drinks were flowing and that we had all that we needed!
Awesome food selection and service! We went for breakfast only, but enjoyed every small plate! Very good desserts, and price wise it is a very good deal! Try it!

I am sure others would give this buffet a 5 star review as it is an impressive buffet.  The layout and design is amazing, this is certainly where I bring all my guests when I take them to Vegas.  The selection of food is amazing, just when you think you are at the end of the food, you see more and more, there are plenty of choices.  The price is a bit high compared to other buffets, though you get what you pay for.  The two reasons I did not give it a 5 star review is the beverage service was slow and there are no self service beverage stations like most of the other buffets have and while the selection of food was vast, I was disappointed that there were very few items I really enjoyed enough to go back for seconds.  Sure, I filled a few plates with unique food, though I let a lot of it go as it did nothing for me.  Now when it came time for Desert, they had a lot of options though I had to go back up at least five times because each time I went up there were so many empty places which more visits to the desert bar is not in itself a bad thing.  While I had no problem paying the price, I think they forgot to focus on staff as the two biggest issues I had were staff.

Brisket was cooked to perfection. It was so moist it melted in your mouth. The seafood paella was phenomenal as well. The clams and shrimp all filled with flavor. My taste buds were dancing for joy from the deliciousness.
Food is good but expensive. $60/ person. The waiting line is bad. Recommend to come 1-2 hrs ahead to get in the line

So I was in vegas last weekend and I asked my friends what was the best buffet in vegas since I haven't been in vegas for over 6 years now.  Bacchanal came up a number of times so I decided to check it out.  We went at 6:30pm on a sunday and it wasn't that busy, we got seated within 10 minutes.  One of the things that I like about this buffet is that they serve hot crab legs.  You just have to go over to the Italian food station instead of the seafood station.  My suggestion for anyone coming here is to first go around and look at all the different options, and then decide what you want to try, don't try to over do it in the first pass, its not a race but a marathon.  Overall I felt that the quality of the different food was good but not sure if you really get your moneys worth at the $55 price tag.  You may be better off just eating in a nice restaurant but if you want variety then this is the place to go.

It's too bad that it's impossible to try every single item in this buffet because there's that much! They have everything you could possibly imagine!

Seafood: King Crab Legs.  Half peeled and easy to eat.  There are hot butter stations on pretty much each area.  They also have oysters, shrimp, crab claws.  On the side of the raw seafood bar are seafood dishes.  

What's cool about this place is you get to sample small plates from other restaurants at Caesar's.  Had fried chicken in a basket with fries.  Also had quail, which wasn't my favorite because they're typically hard to eat, but worth a try.  

Not many buffets carry lamb, but Bacchanal does.  Had that with prime rib.  They have rack of lamb and lamb chops.  

Don't forget the back area where they have artisan breads, meats, and cheeses.  Goat cheese and blue cheese were my fave.  If you go back further, you'll eventually hit the sushi and asian section.  

There's a whole station of good quality desserts.  Chocolate covered strawberries, macarons, custards, and a crepe station just to name a few.  

I'll have to go back again to try everything!

Bacchanal has definitely barged its way into my top three buffets in Vegas, and not quitely!  This new location will definitely become my go to buffet and has finally trumped The Buffet at the Wynn since the grand opening.  The only other comprable buffet is the Wicked Spoon, which opened not too long ago at the Cosmo.  Service is always great, but the line can be long, so line up early.  The dining area itself is beautiful, and the food just tastes of a higher quality.

Some memorable items: 
King crab legs that are pre-cracked, served hot or cold
Jumbo shrimp that is pre-peeled
Prime rib that is cooked just how you want it
All varities of cuisine (Asian, italian, you name it)
A wide variety of deserts

PROTIP:  The prices for lunch and dinner may be a little steeper than other lower tier buffets, but definitely worth it to at least try.  By far the most extensive menu and variety in cuisine.

The buffet was strictly OK. Especially for a vegetarian like myself I would give it only 2 stars.

Pros:
- Excellent meat and sea-food selection (from my non-veg friend's perspective)
- Not excessively crowded
- Great desserts

Cons
- Very few vegetarian options
- Dishes were not well marked with ingredients. Infact some of the dishes didn't have a name at all
- Veg food didn't even taste that good

I have been to the buffet at Bellagio and I think it is much better than this one. Had more food options also.
They advertise to have 500 items for lunch buffets but I am sure they were much less.

Amazingggggggg. Pricey, it was $59.99 for dinner but if you have your M Life card it's $49.99. The food was great, the meats were amazing, prime rib, brisket and even the lamb chops, YUM!

The seafood was decent, some of the oysters were a bit sandy.

A lot of selections...I love the desserts and fresh juice...Overall, I have a great experience there. The line wasn't too long when I was there. Only downside was that they limited 2 hours for holiday season, but it wasn't too big of a deal. I was full by the time.

Holy shit, now this is a buffet.

I've never been much of a buffet person -- heat lamps over food of middling quality. But the Caesar's buffet blew me away with the quantity, variety, and quality of food. The decor is pretty pimp, too.

The coup de gras was that they had sushi! Some of the best maguro nigiri I've ever had, and I've eaten sushi in Japan.

We have a lot of buffets to choose from in Vegas. Lots of them start off great and slowly as time goes by, the quality goes down. Not at bacchanal. The food is even better now than it was when I first went there. And believe me, it was already delicious to begin with. They've even improved the fact that you don't have to wait in line and can just check into the kiosk and be notified when to come back. 

Each station has the best food from each ethnicity whether it's Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, or American food. Their carving station is also top notch with lamb chops, prime rib bone, sausage links, brisket. The list goes on and on especially their seafood section. I'm also not a desserts person but I find it mere impossible to go there and not grab a plate full of desserts like chocolate covered strawberries, macaroons, black sesame mochi ice cream, etc. 

No other buffet in Vegas comes close to this one. For those people that don't want to wait, you can pay $20 more to cut the line and start eating even sooner!

Having dined here a couple of times, I think the long lines and the high pricing doesn't deserve The long Walt or cost. The cheaper snow crab legs are what is served here rather than Alaskan crab legs. Variety and dessert selections are OK, but I can go to Bellagio or the Wynn for similar buffet selections and avoid the longer lines.

I wish they had buffers like this locally. Apparently Vegas hotels are known for their extravagant buffets. I was recommended this one and it did not disappoint. As far as buffets go, you get to try so many options , a little bit of this a little bit of that, the food may not be cooked to five star quality but you get to experiment with everything and if you don't like something, it's not a big deal since you paid a flat rate to get in.
