This is definitely a great buffet. Large selection of everything. Their desserts are adorable! If you're in Vegas and feeling really hungry, I'd recommend this buffet over the others!

The food was good, but this rating is more so because of the service. I was standing next to my boyfriend when he was trying to purchase two lunch spots for us. For whatever reason, the lady charged him for only one person instead of two. My boyfriend went back to another cashier who explained what had happened and why he had to come back into line and purchase another lunch. This cashier was very snappy to him for no reason. I'm sure you guys have to deal with big personalities in Vegas, but the receipt thing was probably an accident, so the lady could have been more kind about it.

Not worth it, sat in the table for about 15 minutes before somebody came and got our drink orders. After that , had to wait on a very long line to get food from the seafood counter. At the end was only able to get salad and dessert.  They charge us $250. 00 for four people. The most expensive salad and dessert I ever had.

It's been a while but having just eaten at the Wicked Spoon reminded me of how good Bacchanal is.  They have a great selection and the food is very tasty.  I especially liked the street tacos and carved meats.  I would return again although a bit on the pricey side, but you're on vacation and don't eat there often.

Way overrated. I have been waiting to try this buffet out because of all the rave reviews. I knew that there were going to be major line-ups so I went around 3:30pm to put my name in queue for dinner. The wait time was 364 minutes and it told me to come back at 10:12pm. The buffet closes at 10pm. I asked the attendant and she told me to come back at 9pm to wait and see if there are seats available but there is no guarantee. Charging $56.99 a person for the holiday dinner and not guaranteeing a seat I decided to return the next day for holiday brunch instead.

My party and I went early (8am) so there was no wait times. There are a lot of variety of foods but the taste is nothing to rave about. The brisket was over-seasoned, and the pork ribs were dry and just tasted like salt. 

The Asian Station had - Mandarin/Manchu Wok/Panda Express type Chinese Food
Italian Station consisted of Pizza and one Pasta. 
Seafood station had overly salty crab legs and stone crab

The best items include: Oysters, Pho Station, and the gelato bar and desserts. 

Overall, the food quality just wasn't there for a Buffet that was charging $50+ a person. Caesars Palace needs to do a better job at ensuring the lines are controlled and moving at an efficient manner 

Some people I talked to waited 5-6 hours in order to try this buffet. But let me tell you, this buffet isn't worth the way. Better to save your money and go to another restaurant  that has quality food and service.

I've attempted multiple times to get into this place but the waits have always been two hours or more. If you need to wait that long to try this place, just go else where bc its good but not worth that much time standing around. This time it didn't have a wait and really easy to get inside. Plenty of food choices and you will find something you like. The food was very good overall.

Definitely try at least once. Would I repeat it? No. Quality of food on point on 95%. The wagyu I had was dry, the prime rib was over cooked too. So I went for the steamed crab legs which was by the Italian station. I thought it was odd but made sense, someone would serve the legs so it was piping hot on my plate, I liked that but the butter was 10 ft away. Seafood was great and deserts were amazing!  Where they lost the stars for me was the meat, atmosphere, seating and service. The lightning was almost too dark, there is a level of appropriate dimness but I don't like eating in the dark. It was only two of us at the table a chair on one side and booth on the other.  I hated the table! 4 legged table pushes against the booth bench seat, constantly moving table to get in and out. My husband couldn't really back up because all the tables are too close to each other. Most restaurants the table height there is an average and this was high my arms actually hurt after a while. Service terrible! Being shown to our table and the lady states oops someone took the table as she scrambled to find another one...then the server took forever to refill my drink and clear the table. For the amount you pay service is lacking, it's really almost not worth it when another top rated buffet is similar, not much difference. 
FYI: there is a long wait after you pay, but that is to be expected and I did not take that in to consideration for the stars given.

We came New Year's Eve and it was super busy. They gave us a round of champagne on the house because of the holiday. Every person got a lobster and prime rib. The food was amazing, oysters, crab legs, sushi, and many more foods. The dessert station was so pretty and delicious.

After having tried almost all the buffets in Vegas at one time or another I waited to try this one last because of the bar that was set in my mind.

We went Monday night and well...  It just fell flat.

After standing in line for a half hour just to be seated and paying $50 per head I just wasn't that all impressed.  Perhaps it didn't meet the standards I'd set in my head after reading all the rave reviews.

The oysters were not good.  If anyone has ever been to the Gulf of Mexico and had fresh oysters from Apalachichola then you'll know what good oysters are supposed to taste like.  They should be cold, fresh and briny (salt) just like the ocean.  These tasted like warm tap water...blah!  The crab legs were just like every other buffet in Vegas.  No better, no worse.

The meat selection was really good!  The brisket and lamb chops were just incredible and I've eaten a lot of BBQ here in the south so it's safe to say I know BBQ.

I didn't try the Mexican as I simply didn't have room, but the line was constantly full.

I loved the truffled potatoes and mushroom risotto. I also really enjoyed the fresh made udon noodle bowl next to the Asian section.

The sushi was not very good at all!  Don't waste your time.  It looked like it was prepared by my 11 yr old.  Just a ball of rice with a piece of fish that looked like it was hacked with a meat cleaver.  The fish had started to dry out and had a little funk to it.

Now the dessert section was a homerun.  I tried the multiple flavors of mochi and sorbet.  I could not get enough of the thai tea sorbet and the mango chili lime sorbet.  They were top notch!

All in all I had a nice meal but it was nowhere near the hype.

Arguably best buffet in vegas.  Large selection of seafood, sushi and salads.  A bit overpriced but I will return.  Make sure you see all the foods as paet of the buffet is a bit hidden.  If you are not a big seafood fan then you are probably overpaying.

This year, we wanted to try something different for Thanksgiving week, so we went on a road trip to Arizona to visit our friends. Arizona was amazing, but that's another review. We had toyed with the idea of doing Thanksgiving in Vegas, but ended up leaving on Saturday. At the last minute, we took a detour and headed to Caesar's on a friend's recommendation.

I'm not a Vegas person, this was only my second visit, unlike my husband who used to be a high roller (before marriage and kids). I'd heard from a few people about Thanksgiving in Vegas being a great time to go with great food, but he kept insisting that it was going to be quiet, that it's one of the slowest times of the year. So we were both curious.

We weren't disappointed. He was amazed by how Vegas had changed and when we got to Caesar's, we got our ticket to get in line. While we waited for the text, we had fun walking around with the kids. There's plenty to see and the kids loved it. By the time we got our table, we were hungry and ready. 

We were blown away by the variety. I'm a pescatarian and the seafood selection was off the hook, including escargot and of course, crab! My husband went to town on the meats and the kids were in heaven. I also really liked that there was a nice variety of veggies, not just the usual salad mixes, but there were roasted root veggies, and arugula and waldorf salads. I try to eat healthy and that was a big plus. There was a nice pizza for my picky youngest one. There was a good selection of drinks that were included which we took advantage of. Of course the kids went crazy with the desserts. I loved the different gelato selections and the freshly made crepe which we also ordered. Since we were driving we didn't order any alcohol, instead got coffee for the long drive ahead. On the way out we started planning for when we could go back. It was a great treat that was totally worth it.

Among my favorite in Las Vegas.  We used to like Bellagio and Wynn, but Bellagio seemed to have changed in quality (dramatic decrease).  Cosmo (Wicked spoon) was promising when I laid eyes on the salads, but the dessert seemed pre-ordered and not made in house.

Overall, Bacchanal was the one we keep on going back to!  Their Achilles heel, however, is the sushi and the pizza.   Everything else is excellent!  Don't laugh, but the carne asada tacos are something I get every time even though it is probably not the biggest bang for the buck...LOL

TIP: walk behind the casino through the mall to cut down on walking time by half!  Just enter the mall from the casino through the margarita bars with the low-cut hooter lookalike servers, and the next entrance point to the buffet will be just a few stores away.  Secret shortcut!
Food was excellent, good variety.  Sevice good be better,  took too long to clear used plates.

This by far is the best buffet I've been to. Yes, it's very pricey ($50 for brunch) but so worth it when you see the spread. There's the usual crab legs, Chinese food, sushi, meat station but then there's the taco bar, noodle bar, dim sum, Spanish food and so much more. It was a bit overwhelming but I managed to eat a little bit of everything.

My most favorite was the congee. I was so happy to see Chinese donuts which was so crispy, fried scallion, and dried shredded pork - the good brand! 

I also loved the dessert section. This buffet served such interesting gelato flavors such as mango banana and lemon basil. So good! 

Tip: there's always a long line but there's a separate line for parties of six or more.

We came around 4pm and there was no line at all. We got seated immediately and went to their asian part. This is one of the few if not the only buffet that serves shumai and har gow and to my surprise it was really well made. They have a few veriety of sushi, pizza and a cool small cheese and different type of salami section. Moving on to their meat section that were things get good. Big selection of different types of beef and ham and sausages. You can also get chicken and biscuit in a cup. Their dessert section is so big and good. One of the best dessert sections out of any buffet and you can make your own crepe.

I gave them 4 stars for the price since it was $60 a person which is a bit over priced. Otherwise for food selection they get 5 stars.

This is my new favorite buffet on the Strip! We came on a Friday afternoon, and somehow miraculously avoided waiting. Literally paid and walked right in. It was $32/ person. I loved that there were various cuisines and it was grouped accordingly. My favorites were the tacos. I thought it was comparable to taco places and there was even a full salsa bar to match. I also surprisingly loved the hot and sour soup and found it just as good as ones in Chinese restaurants, ha! Towards the end of our meal (or the beginning of dinner service), crab legs arrived. Yum. Some negatives would be the overdressed (thus salty) Caesar salad and the overcooked (thus dry) prime rib. The desserts looked really good too but I was so full I just had a scoop of blood orange sorbet. Restroom is in very close walking distance (right by the entrance) and service was average. I will be back!

Lots of delicious food! Great VARIETY of food!!!!

def suggest to go for dinner on a "empty" stomach so you can eat! 

It was pricey $50.99 per adult.

But definitely worth it!

I fell in love with the nutella crepés! BEST I've ever had!!!!

We went on a Wed evening and there was a 2 hour wait !

DEF suggest to Go 2 HRS prior to eating to make reservation!

Try the brunch buffet today and it's average at best. However factored in the high price ($39.99 + tax + tips) then this is not a very good proposition. There are four stations for foods and one for desserts. The American station with the meat carving is the best as the taste is somewhat expected. Seafood station is below average. Same for Asian station. You taste something that's not authentic and lack of clear flavor. Did not try the Italian station but it's probably the same. Desserts are good. Definitely won't be back

Came here with BF on Friday for lunch. The price is $31+ per person that's with discount for having a Total Rewards card. Food was good, for shrimp lovers, the shrimps is like 40/50 count size or even larger, its like as large as my thumb. It was fresh. I asked if they could heat up my shrimp and they not only heat it up but saute it with butter. That was very nice of them. I liked that they have different type of juice, crepe making. The chinese food were near authentic per BF since he's chinese. But it is good, as good as any nice respectable chinese restaurant. Is it worth the $31? Yes it is.

After the 3 hour wait which was for the payment line of $60 pp, then another wait of 20 min for a table we had less than a full hour before closing. Keep in mind we arrived around 5:30 on a Tues. The wait and $ was so not worth it, a huge disappointment.  The line for seafood was long, the meat looked like it had been sitting around,  lots of labels missing so you just don't know what stuff is, very sad.

The BACCHANAL BUFFET at Caesar's is billed as the best buffet in Vegas.

Pro's - the buffet provides a wide variety of dishes: seafood, Mexican, Asian, Italian pasta's, large selection of meats, and a large variety of desserts. Everything that we tried was well prepared, hot and appetizing. 

Con's - the noise level was horrible. Music was too loud.  Finally, the cost. Price was $45.99/person. 

Conclusion: BACCHANAL BUFFET is good food even if the environment is annoying. The best buffet in Vegas? No, we still prefer the buffet at Bellagio.

Ths buffet was great about two years ago.  But, recently, I went to Bacchanal, and it had gone downhill. First, the food lines are not arranged well- for example, the crab line extends into a lot of food that people can't get to without waiting in the crab line. My guess is that this is not a mistake. Second, the brisket used to be the best I'd ever had outside of Texas, but something changed, and I choked down a couple of bites. They also used to have a small portion of chicken and waffles that was amazing, but now it is honey/teriyaki chicken and waffles, which was not very good. Finally, the biggest food area here is the Asian food part. While I like Asian food, it is not what I pay $$$ to eat at the Bacchanal Buffet. So, in a nutshell, FYI, I think US customers are no longer the main target audience here. Desserts are still very good.

This is our first time coming for caesar's lunch buffet.  We had a great experience!  We especially love our waiter Mark.  He is such a friendly guy.  He is very attentive and always has a happy smile.  The restaurant has a great variety of food choices and most of them taste really good.  The only con is the seafood is so so, the stone crab is not up to my expectations.  But overall, we love it, we will recommend it to our friends.

Hadn't been to a top Vegas buffet in a while so decided to try the "new" one - Bacchanal, which had a lot of great reviews.
I ended up very satisfied with my choice.
A friend and I went there during early Friday evening expecting to wait for a while but I guess we hit the sweet spot and walked right in (just before 6 pm).
Somebody had recommended the tomahawk steak but apparently it was not available on this night.  Perhaps a weekend only item?
However, there was plenty of other good food including:
- Pork ribs - excellent dry rubbed ribs
- Fine cold cuts  (salami, etc)
- Warm crab legs
- Sashimi
- Sliders
- Truffled Potato Gratin - these really are great
There was plenty more to be had if only I had room for everything.
The dessert selection and apparent quality is amazing but I only had enough room left for a little sherbet, which was delicious.
To be fair, let me mention the couple of small negatives: 
1- the sashimi was gone when I went back a second time 
2- there was a bottled juice section but the juices were warm
3- maybe I could have asked for ice for the juices but the server was not around as often as we would have liked
It was a great experience and I would not hesitate to eat there again, provided I wanted to spend around $60 (including tip).  For me, it's a close race between this and Bellagio.

Best buffet ever! So much to choose from. I skipped the soup and salads so I'd have room for desserts. The cherry stone clams were my favorite but a close second was the roasted duck. Then I realized I had missed the lamb. Oh my. The snow crab legs and stone crab claws rounded out the meal. 
On to the desserts. Cheesecake pops, gelato and creme brûlée were a fine finish. It was a relaxed, no hurry atmosphere and worth almost what we paid. It's just a little bit higher than I'd like to pay but I had to do it once.

This is my Haiku review for the "Bacchanal Buffet" in Caesar's Palace.

Extravagant food
Really bad Asian section
Overall p good

Fantastic buffet! So many different stations to go to and food to choose from. Very personal experience, the chefs and waitress always asked if there was something else I wanted. Great selection of breakfast and lunch items. Desserts and juice bar were fantastic as well.

OMG! I can't say enough about this restaurant! They have everything from frog legs to bone marrow. This isn't your typical casino buffet and was well worth the $65 price tag. It wasn't crowded so I was kinda leary, but we we're allowed to view the choices beforehand and it was agreed that we must eat here. The crab legs were good, not a fan of bone marrow, but I can say I've finally had it. The lamb tbone was my favorite and my first time eating lamb and I've been missing out! I ate and tried as much as I could. Why eat the same ol stuff when you can venture out and try new things, and if I didn't like it I could go back to my usual. Give it a try!!!

My first buffet in Vegas (well apart from going to the one at Planet Hollywood last year on a Groupon, but it hardly gets mentioned on any of the 'top buffets' lists), so I wanted something big... fancy... yummy... full of choices........... you get the point.

The Bacchanal Buffet definitely has all of that. Consulted the Internet for the best buffet, and this one kept popping up. Apparently the place costed $17 million to open! And they have something like 9 kitchens (all of which are open).

So what's on the buffet? Not sure how often it changes, but pretty much everything. Seafood included hot AND cold crab legs, ceviche, clams, oysters, shrimp, salmon, and so on. There was a carving station with about 6 different meat choices - brisket, prime rib, ribs, sausage, lamb chop, and a couple of other things I can't remember. There was sushi, a cheese and meat station, a huge dessert bar, ...

So the only reason I didn't go with a 5-star rating is due to the lack of service. It wasn't horrible, and in fact got a lot better when our server changed about halfway through the meal, but for the first half, we had to practically beg for refills, and were given no information about the buffet when we sat down. We didn't find out about the sushi and oyster section until our 2nd or 3rd time up. For over $50/person, I expect slightly more info.

Unfortunately I don't really have much to compare it to in terms of Vegas buffets, but there was definitely a lot of selection, and a lot of food. Most of the food was good - the meat from the carving station was a bit dry, but maybe they were just having an off night.
This is a good buffet but not worth $50 early in the morning. The cashiers were also pretty rude.

CRAB LEGS, LAMB CHOPS, AND MACARONS. 

Straight up, these lamb chops are some of the best lamb chops I've had ANYWHERE and I've had a lot of lamb chops. Well seasoned, crisp in all the right parts, and cooked to a perfect medium rare, these lamb chops really set the standard for all future lamb chops to be had. Love them. 

PRO TIP: Buffet switches over from lunch to dinner at 3pm. So, show up at 2:30pm, pay your $38 lunch fee, enjoy a few light appetizers, then wait for the magic to happen at 3pm. That's when all the best things come out. 

Cheers to gluttony!

Don't waste your money. Overpriced and don't get your hopes up for king crab, 99% was snow crab. Other food was ok typically buffet food. Don't come here assuming you will eat $70+ of food per person the lack of flavor in the food will make it less appetizing.

Sun, Dec 7, 8:50pm

texts w/ my boyfriend:

I've decided that I'm never coming home. I'm going to live here in the seafood section of the buffet, next to the drawn butter dispenser.
-----------------------------------------------
Where at?
-----------------------------------------------
Bacchanal inside of Cesar's Palace. I've had 4 plates of crab legs babe. I'm so happy

We went to vegas over the weekend and wanted to hit up only one buffet. We went to bacchanal for its seafood selection. Unfortunately...their seafood has NO FLAVOR, I guess that's what all the sauces are for!

I had never ever in my life ate seafood that had absolutely no flavor, NONE at all. I had hoped for the crab claws since they were enclosed in the shell but it tasted as if they were soaked in cold water and watered down.

The oyster were very questionable as well. They didn't look fresh and were also super washed down with water and almost tasteless.

This was dinner #2 in vegas and another disappointment, vegas food needs to redeem itself the next time I return.

Excellent service and food. What a vast array of choices and cuisines. From chicken and waffles to street tacos and dim sum. The seafood area was wonderful with fresh shucked oysters, crab legs either hot or cold, broiled scallops in the shell, you name it they have it. The dessert area was sweet overload and everything was beautiful and full of flavor. The entire area was gorgeous. I'm sure we didn't eat $50/person worth of food but we did have a wonderful meal and experience.

Downgraded to a solid 4. Wynn and Cosmo outdo here now. They ran out of King crab, so they served whatever was left from day before an blended in a very few pieces with the snow crab to fool the customer (doesnt work) and then they ran out completely. This was for Sunday brunch early morning.
Whoa. This place is too expensive for what you get. $55= a rip off. There is only so much a person can eat for that much. The food is also mediocre.

Truly unremarkable buffet food at its best, absolutely disgusting pig slop at its worst. The sushi was good and fresh. The rest of the seafood was nearly inedible. I kept going to the different stations trying to find something that could save the entire experience and came up with nothing. But by far the worst was the chocolate gelato. It tasted like someone dumped dark plain cocoa powder in water and froze it. There was no sugar, dairy, or egg yolk to speak of.

This place is GREAT, but I cannot give it that last star. Mainly because I have a grudge against the price. It may be a personal issue though. I paid for 4 adult dinners and 2 of the adults had 1/2 a plate of food. Period. I'm still hurting from the price. 

But first! I LOVED the little finger grips that they give out right at the cashier. Plates are hot! It was quite handy at times! It was so cute.

Things worth trying:
ALL the bottled juices on the food bar
Tacos!!!
Crab legs
Oysters
Prime Rib

I was doubly impressed that they offer chilled crab legs AND boiled crab legs.

The dessert bar was so pretty. I didn't want to eat anything.
Here is the key lime pie , creme Brule , red velvet cupcake , and flan. Sooo good, not too sweet just right.

The food is really good but your stomach is only so big. It's hard to eat your money's worth. It's also hard to have the patience to wait so long. It probably isn't the best idea to come for their holiday specials which was $79.99. We got a ticket for seats around 3PM, got in line at 6:30PM, and didn't get seated till 8:30PM. By this time, they ran out of a lot of advertised items such as the bone marrow and loaded corn ): super disappointing after waiting so long! Closing was at 10:30pm so they really shouldn't advertise their menu if they weren't going to be able to supply enough portions. My favorites included the lobster, prime rib, BBQ ribs, Nashville hot chicken, scallops with truffle, creme brûlée, Thai tea float, warm crab legs, and their Mac n cheese. I'd avoid the Asian food and the rest of the desserts. The service inside the restaurant is pretty good.

March 16th I ventured over to this "best buffet in the world" at about 10am. I figured I could catch some breakfast and some lunch. They have a fast line for the higher level player card levels, but any player card will get you $1 off. It was still about $30 for the buffet though. So it's not one that you would go to everyday. A short wait after I paid and I was taken to a table and asked what I would like to drink. Since it includes coffee and I need coffee to survive I ordered that. I was brought out a nice mini pot of coffee, a cup of cream (like actual cream not half and half) and some ice water. I then proceed to... breakfast. Honestly the breakfast was meh... they had fancy dishes yes, but the quality was that of the average diner you'd go to that advertises breakfast all day... (Denny's) They have a very large meat and seafood stations, as well as an Italian station (mostly pizza) and a Chinese station... featuring several dishes that you don't find on your average Chinese buffet trip. They had several different types of sushi, which was pretty good. After I stuffed myself with their many different options, I proceeded to the desert table. The desert table was filled with several different treats. Wasn't a big fan of the almost marshmallow type things they had but other than that they were delicious. A couple things that really stood out to me were fantastic mashed potatoes and they had sweet potato tots. I may be back, but I think I am going to try and tackle the other buffets first before returning.
Good food here but service is terrible! Went off peak times and still waiting for nearly two hours.
Best in town. Steve O served with a smile on Easter!  Even with a 1 year old at home!    What a great guy. Great food, good service all around!

Came here Sunday the 11th for my mom's birthday and the food was amazing! I seriously cannot believe the quality of this restaurant. I was worried about the wait time since we came Sunday for lunch, but we were sat in about 45 mins, not too shabby! Our busser Ana was very sweet and helpful to our waiter. I forgot our waiters name but he was nice and goofy... he kept telling Ana that her shoes were tied... kinda childish... but I didn't mind when my mouth was full of delicious UNLIMITED prime rib! Can't wait to come back. Bacchanal, you have my heart.

If you are in Vegas and you are hungry, these is the go to place for AYCE buffet.  Can't beat there food selections, fresh seafood to meat selections.  It is not cheap but if you can eat it's all worth it.  They have oyster, crab, different types of fish, sushi, prime rib, bbq ribs, Asian food, Mexican. Food, Italian food, etc and the dessert selection is out of the world.

We only had an hour during our lunch here, and you definitely need more time than that. Just checking out all the different stations is an event. We went on a Monday at lunch time, and so many buffets have less options during the week. I wasn't expecting what all they had.

Two types of crab legs, 7 different meats at the carving station, sushi, and hand made to order tacos, a super delicious ceviche, and the best fried chicken I've ever had. The prime rib was to die for. The only thing I disliked was the brisket, Idk something about the flavor, but who cares when everything else was so great.

On top of the food, the service was outstanding. I don't expect anything great at a buffet, just refilling my drink. But when I was coming back from the buffet and passed our server, she apparently noticed I had gotten the crab, and as I sat down she had run and got me a cracker thing without me even thinking about it. 

It was really a great experience. And beautiful ly designed. When my mom comes to town we'll be going again, and I'll make sure we give ourselves plenty of time. That's right I'm a local and will happily pay the high cost of coming here again. Worth every penny.
One of the best buffet in Las Vegas! This is amust try place to eat. There are so many selections from main dishes to desserts. Servers are very attentive.

Literally the best buffet I have ever been to in my 30 years of life!! The waiting process, and it is a process, to get in could be a little more organized but other then that this buffet is superb!! The decor and ambiance alone is beautiful and tasteful! It may sound silly but the light fixtures were awesome and were made of all types of drinking glasses (pic). Anyway moving onto the food, well what didn't they have? Every type of ethnic food you could think of! Italian, korean, japanese, chinese, mexican, spanish, some french,Mediterranean, the list was endless! They did however leave out Indian (my friend pointed that out to me). The seafood selection was amazing as well! And don't get me started on the desserts.. Well anyways my favorites included the Italian antipasto sections, all the soups were amazing, and the meats!! My party and I indulged to the fullest and we paid for it later! All in all the food was to the highest quality and every thing we tried was beyond delicious! I literally just tried a small portion of almost everything, and I was beyond stuffed!!! If you are looking for options, this is your place. Even though it was exspensive, I would not hesitate to go again next time I'm in vegas!

Holy crap on a cracker!  The line to get into this posh buffet during dinner hours is major.

1 hour to pay...
1 hour to get seated...
10-15 minutes to get seafood...

But the upside is, the food was pretty darn good.  When I hit a buffet, I always try to squish in 'AT LEAST' 3 rounds of servings.

Round 1 - zero waiting:
Pork fried rice, chow mein, veggie spring roll, pork sui mai, Shanghai dumpling (YES, juice inside too), cali roll, salmon nigiri, beef with broccoli, kung pao chicken.

I drank diet Coke for burp-age power, its to make more room for food after burping out the air in my stomach.

Round 2 - 10 to15 minutes wait:
Baked salmon, lobster bisque, seafood ceviche, lots of Alaskan king crab legs, lots and lots of shrimp cocktails, 4 freshly cracked opened oysters (this took the additional 5 minute wait)

Break time!  Drank diet coke for burp-age.

Round 3 - 5 minutes wait:
Wagu beef slider, prime rib, bbq ribs, garlic mash potatoes, french fries in it's own fryer basket

At this point, I'm full up to my neck.  And almost can't walk anymore... but dessert must be eaten too.  At this point, I ordered a cup of hot tea to go with my dessert.

Round 4 - zero waiting:
Dark chocolate layered mousse cake, lemon strawberry cupcake, creme brulee, chocolate dipped strawberries

When I got back, my tea was waiting for me.  It was a nice touch for them to provide the hot water in it's own decanter but the tea was basic Lipton.  Yuck.  For $49.99, they should at least have better tea available!  

I got my money's worth...definitely did.  I seen others shove more food into their mouths than I did but to each it's own :)

Tip:  Make sure to tip your waiter/waitress directly, they provide better service when you do this.  I took 1 star off due to all the waiting.  Otherwise, the food is 5 stars to me.

Worse service ever! 

Never got out drinks and food was horrible ! skip this place nothing to talk about only bad after bad.

My loving companion and I decided to dine here after seeing Sir Elton John in concert at Caesar's. BTW, fantastic concert! We got to the buffet and we're seated immediately. So far so good but from there it was downhill. Our drink order was taken and it took 15 mins them to arrive. We went to the buffet and upon return to the table still had no utensils or napkins. We told a server who passed by our table for the silverware and he returned with them quickly.

We began to try our choices with mixed results. The best item was the chilled tiger prawns; large and succulent. The crab legs were a bit stringy, the raw oysters gritty, the Thai rice dish cold and little flavor. We were told that the buffet started to close in 15 minutes so we went back for another round. An almost raw short rib was tough, I tried the lamb t-bone but it had little taste and was so tough the steak knife wouldn't cut through it. At least the seconds on the tiger prawns was still good.

Except for the gelato dessert was a bust. Burnt coconut macaroons, scorched mini-lava cakes and disappointing lemon meringue tartlet that was not lemony and did not have a smooth texture.

Overall a waste of money in our opinion. Will not eat in any of Caesar's restaurants again.

Went to the Saturday morning bruch buffet.  It was around $44, but I thought it was worth it.  I was the first person in line, and by about 5-10 minutes before opening there was about 10-20 people in line with me.  

Great food assortment.

I didn't get to try the other buffets in town but this one is pretty good. I was especially impressed by the quality of the seafood. We were seated promptly when we got there at around noon. There is a 2 hour dining limit.

The sushi was not good but it's unreasonable to expect good sushi in a buffet. The brisket was a bit tough too. Everything else was great. If you like crab, you will love those giant king crab legs. My favourite were the mussels though! Absolutely delicious!

Omg!  This is the best buffet I have been to ever!  Best selection: Asian, America, Mexican, sea food, meat bar, desert island, drinks (bottomless mimosas is the drink of  choice!)  everything tastes as good as my favorite restaurant at home.  That is why there is a plus 90 min wait to get in this joint for lunch.  I did not have the stomach capacity to enjoy every continent represented. I'm done, wheel me out.  Oweeee! 
Mi pow
Mahalo

I feel like a pig eating at the trough - that's the kind of food u get from this buffet after 2.5 hours wait. Don't waste your time and belly. Go somewhere else unless you like to be a pig - oink, oink, oink.

Hands down, BEST BUFFET EVER!!!! I can't really compare it to other buffets on the strip other than "Wicked Spoon," but this one, can't compare to any of the buffets I've ever had in my entire life (BTW, Wicked Spoon isn't all that great). 

I stopped by Bacchanal on Sunday right before I left for LA around 4pm. Surprisingly, there was no line and my party was seated quickly. Right when we were seated, a waiter came by to take our orders for drinks, afterwards, I rushed for the buffet lines. The selection is large here and the food is AMAZING. Unlike most buffets that lack quality but excel in quantity, Bacchanal excels in everything. Not only is the presentation of the food elegantly placed, the flavors and richness of everything is delicious. 

Foods range from seafood (raw oysters, clams, king crab legs, shrimp, salmon, sushi) to red meats (prime rib, bbq ribs) to desserts (macaroons, creme brule, cheesecake, gelato, mochi, gummy bears, lemon tarts, chocolate covered strawberries). The selection is endless and it caters to all tastebuds. 

My favorite part of the buffet was definitely the seafood and the dessert. When I approached the seafood line for oysters, the chef behind the counter offered to hand pick fresh and large oysters for me from the back that were just shucked. He gave me a generous amount for me to bring back to my table. The oysters were large and my favorite part about them was that they didn't smell like the ocean. 

Just thinking about the dessert makes me drool. The selection is endless!! I wanted to try everything but my poor belly refused to let me stuff more. I'd recommend everything at the dessert bar. EVERYTHING... well, maybe not the macaroons. I've definitely had better but I guess if you've never had them before and have no expectations for macaroons, you'd enjoy it.

Price: The price is pretty reasonable for a buffet in Vegas. On weekdays lunch is around $37 between 11am-3pm. Dinner starts at 3pm and is about $52. Weekends for brunch is $42 and for dinner is $52. 

Parking: Parking is basically free everywhere in Vegas if you park in self-parking for the hotels. So parking at the Caesars was not an issue for me. However, taxi's are also convenient if you don't want to drive.
I have paid 81$ for a brunch(25$ to skip waiting) food is not good, not the quality for 50$! Worse than most buffet I have ever had. Disappointing at all!!

Wanted to do a fancy Vegas buffet and settled on Caesar's.  The buffet was everything I expected! Crab legs, prime rib, and hundreds of other choices.  The street-style tacos and mac & cheese were among my favorites.

Food was awesome, service was not.

Easter weekend dinner was 60 bucks per person. Having the Total Rewards card provided a $1 discount. Beware that there are different lines depending on the size of our party--the cashier did not tell us and we had to wait an extra 15 min. The hostess seating us told us champagne was served all day but the server said no. Checked with another server and he didn't get back to us for the rest of the evening and avoided our table. Not very professional. Could've just come by and say that the champagne wasn't available at all. Our server disappeared for the first part of our meal and we had no drink refills for a while until we flagged down another server. 

The seafood section was great. Mussels, clams, lobster chowder, shrimp cocktail, crab labs, and oysters. The meats were cut against the grain and not very tender. Edamame was dry and not fresh, but the juicy pork dumplings were good, albeit a bit dry sitting under the heat lamps. They also have the Chinese herbal soup with ginseng and chicken, which is a good way to help cleanse your palate after all the seafood! Dessert was unbelievable with the macarons, mochi ice cream, various ice cream flavors, crepes, and cheesecake on a stick. However, no chocolate covered strawberries and the chocolate chip cookies were in fact raisin even though it was labeled as chocolate chip. I can see how it was amazing when they first opened, but they are starting to go downhill.

The plus side was that my bf saw Cee Lo Green while waiting in line for more prime rib.

Best buffet in Vegas so far. Everything from fresh seafood, Vietnamese sandwiches, a massive dessert bar (complete with gelato), horchata, Asian food, Mexican, Italian,.....just endless!! Everything was sooo delicious. Pay an additional  $7 for AYCE drink mimosas/champagne. Nom nom nom.
The best buffet in town! A little pricey but worth it. The brunch was super good with the food choices.

This is my favorite buffet in LV. There is so much variety and the service is great! I tend to go for the desserts, but I think small plates and meats are worth checking out too. 

BEFORE YOU GO: make sure you know the wait time and the hours of lunch/dinner. Even if you're in line for lunch, and the time passes to dinner time, they will still charge you the dinner rate!!! Be prepared to stand in the line to pay, and then the line to get seated.

This place is beyond phenomenal. 

Greatest buffet I have ever been too . I've been going here to eat for two years almost and they never fail me. I love going for breakfast and dinner . I go twice a day. There crab legs are to die for, their exquisite servings in all kinds of different culture foods. Starting from all the delicious food to even the service I had a great pleasure to have Alex as my server and he was great and knowledgeable on the menu . Definitely the number 1 buffet in Las Vegas . 

Oh and don't forget to also add a mimosa doesn't matter the time of day it you can't ever go wrong with their mimosas.

Although this happened awhile ago. I feel like I should still mention this so maybe management will see.
Before I lived in Vegas my friend and I vacationed here. We bought a Groupon for the buffet VIP line pass and all you can drink mimosas for breakfast.
Well we go through and everything is great. Except the waitress. 
When we go it's dead only a dozen tables maybe which isn't alot considering this place probably seats 500 comfortably. 
Waitress takes forever to get waters and fill mimosas. Here is the issue we had. I was hungover. Both me and my friend each bought the deal that included the endless drinks. 
I let my friend drink my mimosa because the waitress took forever to fill it up. When she came over we ordered more waters(2)and mimosas(2) . she looked at me and said "are you gonna drink it this time?" I said "um exscuse me" she continued " they said if your not going to drink it and give it to your friend ( the same girl that bought all you can drink mimosas) I have to take your glass away. 

Idt I've ever been that irritated before. I have worked in restaurants for years. If I had bought the drink deal and my friend had not I would have understood. But we both had unlimited drinks which took a good ten minutes to drink. We weren't throwing them back and being rude asking for quick service. So I said' yes  going to drink it "
She brought over the drinks. She knew she effed it up too. Because she wouldn't look us in the eye. Listen I have a tam card I know when you take booze away. No one was drunk. No one was loud. No one was belligerent. Literally just eating breakfast.
On the way out we didn't tip. She tried to salvage it by saying bye to us. Listen. Hire better staff.. The food is excellent and that's why I come here now.she has been the only issue I've ever had. 
And just to clarify this on our receipt which was on the table it said two buffets and it said 2 of the Groupon deal or drink deals idr what they were called.

arrived Sunday night 820, wait time 35 minutes to table

$60 per person

line to get meat and seafood

prime rib- nothing special, the usual
beef rib - nothing special, don't like the rub seasoning
lamb -overcooked

crab claws - not fresh
sushi- pass, not tasty, looks dried up
clam chowder - salty
corn- undercooked
mash potato - blah

desert - ice cream was good
purple cupcake was interesting - not bad
cheesecake - too sweet and where is the cheese taste?

Overall, not worth it at all

Went for the Friday night $55.00 dinner...here ya go folks...Bellagio and Rio are WAAAY better

Totally bummed on this. Not what I expected, not what everyone else experienced either I guess :(

I was super stoked on this place as its rated the "Best" I Yelped it and I was excited...super sad faced now...

Food Coma? For sure, of course, satisfied though? Nope.

The Lobster Corn Chowda had no Lobster, the Miso Glazed Sea Bass was so fishy and cold it was inedible. The crab did not come off the legs even though they were split and the ribs tasted funny...like crappy funny :(

I was really looking forward to the Souffle they make to order...didn't have it, FAIL. 

I was excited for the chicken basket everyone was bragging about on here, didn't  have it, FAIL :(

I went to get Pho, no one was there to help me and I wanted the soup dangit!!

Beers were cheap, service was good but I really cant say much more...Oh wait, yes I can...I got DIRTY SHRIMPS...nuff said :/

Long lines so upgrade your rewards to bypass the line. HUGE selection of food and most things are pre portioned! Loooove their desserts... It even has a gelato station! Best buffet in vegas. Solid good food and decent service. So why not 5 stars? The truth is it is a buffet therefore food are cooked in mass quantity and left out in the heat plate so the quality is compromised. For example, their sweet fries and regular fries were soggy...

I haven't been to Vegas in 4 years, and this was the first place I wanted eat. They have different prices depending on the days and times. We were here this past Sunday for brunch, so it was $49 per person. I didn't get asked if I wanted unlimited champagne, but it's an additional cost. Before you get seated at the table, someone will take a photo of you and ask if you want to buy them later on.

Luckily we only waited for about 5 minutes before being seated. I was overwhelmed with all the food options they had and didn't know where to begin! I decided to start with the chilled crab legs, which were already open, so it was easier to eat. I also tried some dim sum, sashimi, a slider, and various things. Later, I saw some people getting freshly boiled crab legs in front of our table, so I got some more legs. These were way better than the chilled ones since they were warm. 

We were celebrating my birthday a little early, so when I got back to my table, there was a nicely decorated plate of desserts for me. They were the same ones from the buffet, but with a candle on it. We tried everything and it was all very yummy! I also liked the mini Thai tea bobas with coconut ice cream they had in the dessert area. I still had room for one more dessert, so we each got a scoop of gelato to go. 

There was a two hour limit to dine here, which was plenty of time to eat for us. Overall, I thought the food was okay...nothing really stood out to me and we definitely did not eat $50 worth. On our way out, the line was getting pretty long, so I'm glad we got here before everyone else did.
One of the worst buffets I've had in Vegas. Nothing was flavorful or prepared with care. Would not recommend at anytime to anyone. I'm so disappointed and it really felt like a waste of money.
Disappointed!!!!!Service is very good but quality of food is mediocre. Food too dry and salty. Would not come back

Absolutely amazing! I have gone here multiple times but ONLY WITH THE GROUPON! Idk about you but I can't afford this place without it.. so thankful a deal is available because this place is on my mind all the time. The service is great also, always friendly and happy.

*Groupon Deal Review- Since this is now our 4th annual trip to Bacchanel, I'll review this time soley based on the Groupon deal we did.  We did the 69.00 Breakfast for two with bottomless mimosas deal.  We thought we'd try something new this time, and get in on some breakfast entrees.  Now, if you thought (and I *might*  have) that you could slide into the buffet around 10:30am and enjoy crab legs around 11am, you'd be wrong.  This isn't their fault, so I don't hold them responsible, but  I was bummed- that would have been the ultimate deal!  They DO have the crab claws, but these are a bit of a joke.  This place is still awesome, and if you're there when they switch from breakfast to lunch, you can still try some new entrees at 11am.  We loved the  Pumpkin Gnocchi, Lobster Ravioli,  Lobster Eggs Benedict, and especially the desserts!  The Crème Brulee game here is always on point!  They still have big beautiful shrimp this early in the day, as well as many other seafood included entrees.  The best part though?  Those mimosas!  They don't mess around with the bottomless concept here, WOW!  They carry around pitchers and top your glass off every time they walk  by.  I lost track, because honestly my glass was never empty.  If you LOVE champagne like I do, this is a really reasonable buffet deal.  We walked away stuffed and a bit tipsy, HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Presidents Day weekend FAIL on the "come for lunch, stay for dinner" tactic. If we had gotten there 15-20 minutes earlier (1:30-2pm instead of after 2pm), we probably would have just made it. It's just that we waited over 1.5 hours in that ridiculous line, and it seemed to get worse (but great for King Caesar!) from there on out through the rest of the afternoon and evening. It sounds like these lines (for most buffets) are only this bad during peak times and especially over holidays/holiday weekends, so plan accordingly. It's expensive (dinner is $52 and I think I heard lunch is $42 or around there). You can pay an extra $15 for the express line if you don't want to wait like the rest of the lemmings. I noticed, for a good 5-10 minutes, it seemed like the cashiers were standing around and not ringing people up (probably a "counter-tactic" to push it to 3pm and try to get the rest of these people in at the dinner price). Even after paying, we still had to wait 15-20 minutes to get a table. In the end, we probably waited close to 2 hours. Fortunately, we had no plans until at 7:30pm for the Beatles LOVE show...

So once we finally got into the buffet, I went straight to the seafood line and loaded up on king crab (they had snow crab too I think). There were oysters as well, but they kept on disappearing too fast - apparently the ratio of shuckers to consumers was severely lacking. One of the shucker guys dumped four oysters directly onto my plate after I stood there waiting for a few minutes though. The oysters were super fresh! So much so that my wife, not an oyster-eater, thoroughly enjoyed hers. The king crab legs were OK - some that we got weren't completely defrosted in some parts, so I found myself eating small bits of king crab ice at times. That said, Dungeness is still my favorite.... it's too bad they didn't have any of that cause I would have gone buck wild on it. 

Man, I felt like a kid in a candy store... now, the last time we made a quick "pit stop" in Vegas, we checked out Wicked Spoon. I was thoroughly impressed with that. But this is like Wicked Spoon x2, as another reviewer alluded to. It's literally almost twice as big. Amazing.

So I made it over to the meat station and picked up a nice chunk of brisket and a lamb chop. The lamb chop was pretty bomb. The brisket was okay. My wife got some prime rib, which looked good but by the time I stuffed myself with everything else I didn't get a good look or taste of it. She also got the spicy sausage and boy was it spicy. IMHO, the meat station at Wicked Spoon has the slight edge here. 

Other interesting stuff I picked up: 

Fried chicken & sweet potato fries - I didn't enjoy this as much because I was stuffed from the plates of king crab we destroyed. It was good though, and I thought the fries were pretty awesome (I think they were drizzled or coated in honey!)

Sushi - I only had one piece but it was pretty fresh. 

Shiao long bao - yes, they did have these. And surprisingly they weren't bad - soupy and flavorful as expected.

Pho and tonkatsu ramen - the broth was slightly lacking but the option to even offer these was pretty impressive.

I was looking forward to "chunks of honeycomb" that someone spoke of in another review. Disappointingly, I only saw a display of it (not sure if it was a fake display or real too) behind glass. I did get some "honeycomb honey" which was pretty good though.

As far as dessert, we were pretty impressed but so stuffed full that we could hardly enjoy anything. Creme brulee, flan, mochi, gelato, chocolate covered strawberries...... EXPLODE! We seriously couldn't eat anymore... but then I just had to get a slice of pizza to cap it all off.

It all became somewhat overwhelming after a while, but I'd say the top things to consider: OYSTERS, crab (of course), lamb chops, spicy sausage, sushi, fried chicken.

One thing I almost fainted over when I saw it was a large hot table (ala Mongolian BBQ). They were utilizing it to grill in the Mexican section, but I thought to myself "wouldn't it be crazy if they had Mongolian BBQ?" That would take things to another level, IMHO.

Too much to write about... too much thinking. Still digesting. Until next time, maybe. But only on a non-holiday, off-peak hour, and for lunch going on dinner.

Pros: 

- Good food
- good selection
- comfortable chairs

Cons:

- inefficient staff causes long line to get in
- spotty table service
- carpet not well cleaned/maintained
- "Express pass" is a joke and waste of money

Bottom line: good food, but not worth the long wait in line.

My girlfriend and I make it a habit to try one high-end buffet every time we come to Vegas. We had heard and read good things about Bachhanal, so decided to try it. We went on a Sunday night about 7:30, figuring the line wouldn't be so bad. Wrong!!!! We got there only to see a long-ass line that reminded us of a popular nightclub. There is a little machine where you check in and it gave us a ticket that told us to return in 77 minutes to be seated. Or, you could pay $20 apiece to skip the line. We decided to do this, but I was pissed with the result as we did NOT get to skip the line- instead they just place you in another line with people who came back after waiting their 77 minutes. What a ripoff. The dinner price was $53 apiece (before the $20 express charge).

Anyway, after 30 minutes of waiting in the express line, we were finally seated. I was appalled at what we saw- open table after open table. Several were not cleaned yet which told me their bussing service is lacking. It also was very clear that they either don't care about people in line or are purposely making them wait there as nightclubs do very often- to make it look like a "hot" place that everyone has to eat at. Either way, it's disgusting.

There was a great selection of food- seafood, Chinese, sushi, American, Italian, and a small salad bar. They also had a huge dessert bar with an excellent selection. We especially liked their sea bass (with wasabi mashed potatoes and Bok choi), the sweet potato tater tots, Asian green beans, king crab legs, shrimp dumplings, and custard dumplings. 

Our server was ok, but would sometimes disappear for lengths of time. Plates were cleared quickly, however. My girlfriend noticed food on the carpet in several areas. Disappointing given the stature of the place and the fact it wasn't even full ( don't get me going on THAT again). 

Overall, we liked the food, but were disappointed with other aspects of our experience. We think the buffets at the Wynn and Cosmopolitan were better and were about the same price. We would come back to Bacchanal, but only if there were no line (or a very small one).
I think this is my favorite place in Vegas. Incredible presentation and creativity, you will need a few hours here for sure!

Leading up to my trip to Las Vegas, visiting the Bacchanal Buffet was top five on my list of things I absolutely wanted to do and I am so glad that I did. This buffet is rated one of the best in all of Las Vegas and after my visit I can totally understand how. 

We went on a Monday afternoon for a early dinner on one of our last days in town. This was the perfect time to go, there was no crazy lines or waits as we had seen over the weekend. We also went early enough for dinner that we completely avoided the "dinner rush". We opted out of room service and received a $50 credit to use toward our meal! 

We walked right in and were shown to our table. We were also informed of the various sections of foods that were available to us. Our waitress came over and brought our drinks. We dove right in.

We started at the seafood section, yum! So much to choose from. I was very pleased with the crab legs. At other buffets I have been to sometimes the crab legs are so salty you can't even eat them. These were perfect. I tried just about a little bit of everything and didn't have many complaints. There was a carving station, taco/Mexican station, sushi/Chinese section, Italian section and much much more! The desert section was gorgeous with so many choices. 

Overall I would highly recommend this to anyone staying at Caesars or simply visiting Las Vegas. Its a must for food lovers!

Be prepared to wait. We were a group of 10 and we waited a good hour and fifteen minutes to get a seat.

If you have a big group, you can't use their electronic ticketing system. Instead, your whole group has to wait together. Make sure you pay before you stand in line. If you don't, they'll kick you back out to restart again. The system was super confusing with lines forming every which way. I think they could've done a better job directing people and also a better job with signage. 

Other than that, we had an amazing time. The variety here is insane and the quality is pretty top notch. It took me 3 minutes to walk around the whole buffet. There's Japanese, Chinese, Italian, Spanish, French, American, seafood, desserts and much more. 

Would definitely come back for another try but hope they have a better queuing system next time around

I went here for my birthday back in February for brunch there wasn't a line like I thought it would be because of the holiday weekend...All I have to say is that this is a really good buffet and HUGE! Really huge. They have pretty much anything you can imagine including street tacos! The price was high but I thought it was worth it.I didn't/ couldn't try everything that was offered.  The lobster bisque was fantastic everything had flavor, unlike the other buffets in town.  Service was great. Oh! The limoncello and toasted marshmallow gelato is to die for!  I will definitely return for another special occasion

i'm a marathon eater and vegas buffets are my playground. my current favorite has to be bacchanal. 

i can't tell you every single thing ive eaten at this buffet, but here are a few notables:
- chinese food/dimsum
- tacos
- kobe sliders
- prime rib
- baby lamb chops
- oyster shooters
- made to order ramen, pho, udon
- mochi ice cream

pros:
- delicious food! oh the delicious delicious food. the endless supply of delicious food
- the new paging system! i was lucky to not have to use it, but apparently the paging system lets you go and gamble and drink without having to wait in line
- the put a bar in! there used to be a fountain next to the line at the front, but the intelligently put a bar in for all the people who are waiting and don't gamble. at least let us drink the time away
- wine list was pretty reasonable. while the wine itself was just okay, the prices were very doable. 

cons:
- price. gone are the days when buffet was a nice $27. yea, dinner is pricey, but it's worth it. for the glutton in all of us. what happens in vegas stays in vegas, even if it's your weight in crab legs, right?

*tip* if you want to try to avoid the lines, opt for going on sunday, there should be less of a line, and try to go on the early side 

would i go again? yes!

Slightly disappointing. It was well worth the money for the seafood (cocktail shrimp!!), variety of cuisine and desserts available. However, I don't think the food was of very good quality and worth the money we paid (we went for lunch on a Tuesday). I think it's been overhyped. 

- The sushi was terrible, one of the worst sushis I've ever had. The rice was too sticky and dry, I couldn't even see the individual grains of rice!!
- The dim sum items were pretty dry, like they were steamed for too long. 
- The juices (cucumber, watermelon, carrot) were watered down and didn't taste pure
- The crab claws tasted like they were frozen and thawed
- Desserts were good though! The variety and quality of the desserts were the best I've ever had.

Simply put "A gastrointestinal happy dance in my stomach"   

Quantity and quality through and through

They get 2 stars because our dining service was good.  Went here for a friend's birthday because she was excited about a full blown extravaganza for her birthday dinner.  The only thing full blown about the place is the price. 

It was less busy than most people have experienced but because there were 5 of us, after we paid, we had to wait for about 15 minutes before we were seated.  We get seated and I looked around and realized how small this buffet is compared to others.  And every section seems to have a line and those that don't for their particular foods, have a line in front of them for another section.  Some of the lines just to get the more popular food took more than 15 minutes to navigate.  

The sad part: It isn't all that good.  The desserts were tasty but the actual FOOD... not so much.  I had cold food that was warm and warm food that was cold.  Bread that had been left out for too long and was stale.  One of my friends had a couple of the sliders and pushed the rest of her plate away.  

Honestly, it is a 1.5 star place.  One star for the service, .5 for the desserts.  Had I paid for just a dessert buffet, this would be a different story.  But since most of us went away hungry because the food was not good, I cannot recommend this buffet to anyone.  I honestly feel like people like it because it is expensive.  They feel like they must be eating some really upscale food.  But here is a note:  the food still has to taste good.  One does not need to eat it just because it is expensive.

My first time to try this buffet at Caesers and it is delish!  We are lucky we know a high roller & got into the shortcut line because the regular line was hundreds deep!

This is one beautiful buffet!   I love how they decorated the whole area.   Lots of action stations & a huge dessert island.  I barely got a sample of all the items they had to offer.   It was a big assortment. 

Here are some Highlights:

Warm boiled Crab legs.  The cook it in front of you!
Creme brulee with the perfect crispy layer on top.  The creme part was a little dense but very good flavors. 
Pepper dungeness crab, good flavor but not as fresh
Carne asada tacos were really delicious! 
Lobster corn chowder, great flavor! 
Sliced salamis/panchetta were very good
Steak was amazing!  Though the line was insane....  
Sweet potato tots with sweet glaze in a mini fry basket were yum
Poached salmon with arugula was flaky & flavorful
Mussels were ok
Spiced pumpkin pie was good for the season
Choc creme brulee was like choc pudding with a yummy chocolate layer

This is one delicious buffet with so many choices,  it's sure to make everyone happy!

Wow no matter what time you go the line still sucks. We ate at none peek time paid $39/ person. We'll have to try it again cause it was nothing special. No lobster as mentioned in some of the food blogs we saw on YouTube . Good variety of food & the quality was definitely better as long as they are busy the food gets rotated otherwise it's like any other buffet. Food gets dry & hard.
2+ hr wait.  Got here at 5:45.  I think Bellagio and Paris buffets were better.

What can I NOT say about Bacchanal? This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas. 

Every single thing I got to try was scrumptious, fresh, and did not disappoint! 

Oysters, king crab legs, crab claws, clams, shrimp and other seafood dishes! The Asian cuisine, the pastas, the breads, the premium meats, the made to order tacos or Mexican dishes and we cant forget the crazy desserts!! 

I've been here so many times, I can't list everything I've tried. 

My Go-To's:
Large Oysters.
Easy peel king crab legs 
Large shrimp with cocktail sauce
Prime Rib
Lamb Chops
Brisket
Pork Dumpling
Shumai
All the sushi
All the made to order tacos!
Chicken in a basket.
Salmon. 
Flan
Crème brulee
Thai tea boba with coconut ice cream is my absolute favorite! 

Side notes. 
For $18 ( I believe) more, its an all you can drink beer and wine. 
You have to ask for the Thai Tea coconut ice cream boba.
There are crepes, macaroons and gelato with other desserts. 
Don't forget the very back has all the Asian cuisines from Japanese to Chinese to Filipino dishes. 
Taco's are made in front of you. 
There's always a line for the meats, so don't look pass the side dishes around it. 
Wagyu sliders! 



You will feast like a Viking! 

....Man, now I'm all hungry as I type all this.

Well honestly we were highly disappointed. First we came on a Saturday (September 23rd) so we figured it would be busy but thought it would be worth the wait. Well first you go in and check in at a kiosk. Nobody was there to tell you how to do this check in process and it was swamped so we figured out how to check in and it said it would be a 90 minute wait at 7:30pm so  again we thought well a lot of good reviews even though its a bit spendy, lets wait. My husband ended up telling about 10 people behind us how to sign in at the kiosk (he should have been paid to be their greeter since they didn't have anyone else there) and then they call you to come back only to stand in line again. Then you finally get to your table. Well they do have a lot of food to select from HOWEVER their Dungeness crab was really disappointing...it looked like something they swept up from the floor. Then they didn't have enough people to carve the meat so the lines were so long all the time so by the time you got all of the food you want the other food on your plate is cold because you have to wait so long and its not like other buffets where you can go in and out of the different areas to get food and this you wait in line for the carved meat and you cant cut in to get other things along the way to get to the carved meat... Its really not set up or done well. Poorly managed. If I were a manager and saw this long line like that with 1 meat carver I would be getting additional carvers over there. The deserts are ok. Too gourmet for us. Bring in chocolate cake and pie and real ice cream . So we were pretty disappointed in this buffet.

This is seriously the best buffet I've ever been to in life!!!

The wait is super long! But we were platinum so we got seated real quick! The dirty looks of the people waiting in line were a little scary!

The food selection is EXCELLENT. Seriously the best selection I've ever seen! Corn dogs, Waffle fries, sweet potato fries, raw oysters, clam bakes, mochi ice cream, macaroons, SO MUCH STUFFFFFF. The items also come really classy! They have cute little tin buckets, and little steamers for their xiao long bao's. The only problem is that there are so many people, there are LINES to get certain food items. 

Our server was mediocre....but all the other workers were really nice and helpful!

Ok. The food is good but not significantly better than other buffets in town. The wait is RIDICULOUS. There are three waiting periods. The first is dictated by the sign-in kiosk. 230 min (yes, that's almost 4 hours). The second wait is at the registration line. 1:40h. The third wait is on the "wait to be seated line". 45 min. Did you do the math? 6 hours and 15 min. Staff is unpleasant about it all and the thousands of fellow attendees are mainly very large groups of entitled gamblers and their spoiled children. Stay away!

Was there for Sunday champagne brunch.     I'm not going to go into a bunch of details and just give you the facts.  

1. Food (including desserts) was pretty darn amazing and fresh.   
2. Lack of bigger ticket food items for the price.
3. Great service. 

I only give it 3 stars because for 55+ dollars you should have more higher end beef and seafood fare.  Great atmosphere and service for a buffet but I can't justify more than 3 stars.  I don't think I would spend the money to come here again.

Easily the best buffet I've ever been to.  A slew of stations offering everything from Alaskan king crab legs, mussels, oysters, pan-seared halibut and salmon to comfort food like shrimp & grits to ethnic fare including made-to-order tacos, sushi, Italian and dim sum.

The interior's absolutely gorgeous too and, honestly, even nicer than some upscale restaurants I've come across.  Service was friendly and attentive too as plates were cleared without fail after every trip to the stations.  On that note , I made my way through 5 plates of awesome with highlights including:

Lamb chops (awesome char and savoriness)
Beef brisket (beautiful smoke ring and perfect amount of resilience)
Spicy sausage
Prime rib
Green-lipped mussels
Italian meatballs (so juicy!)
Baked rigatoni
Xiao long bao (unexpectedly good!)
Char siu
Chinese roast duck (as good as the best Chinese BBQ joints in SF)
Macarons
Gelato

Yeah...just tons to choose from and great cooking across the board.  One thing I wouldn't recommend though is the sushi - the sashimi's not very fresh and the rolls are some of the ugliest I've laid my eyes on.

Next time I'm in town, gotta try the tacos and made-to-order chocolate souffles!

Holy moly!!! I was here in July visiting family and we decided to check out the buffet to see if it was over rated. Uhhhhh. Not 1 moment did I feel that this buffet was over rated. Everything was great. If you get there during the rush hour you can be a little intimidated by the line, but if you are looking for a buffet this is the place to go. The line can get a bit long at the crab leg station. You have your choice of snow (hot or cold), king, dungeness, sea snails, oysters. You name it. I couldn't stop thinking what bottomless ocean did they find all this crab to feed people every day. There is an Asian station with sushi, fried rice, vegetables, fried rice, Peking duck etc. A salad bar. A southern bar with mash potatoes, mac and cheese, ribs, steaks. A huge dessert bar. I can keep going on about the amount of food choices and different cuisines.The staff was extremely friendly and met our every need. Our table was continuously cleared so we could keep stuffing our faces. This place definitely makes you over eat. The drinks were flowing at an additional cost. The buffet was extremely clean compared to other  buffets I've visited. Please do not let the price deter you from coming here. I've tried the other buffets and I had to return here before I departed back to New York. I promise you will not regret it.
Best buffet. Lots of good and all great quality! Keep some space for desert or your regret it!

My husband and i enjoyed a nice week long vacay to Las Vegas and stayed at the Aria Vdara hotel. We made it our mission to try the top buffets and see which one was best. We bought the 24hr buffet pass for $49 I think per person and got to eat at Flavors inside Harrah's, the buffet in Paris and also the one in Rio. When we ate at this one inside Caesar's, we knew there was an up charge, I think it was like $25 or $30 more per person, but we didn't care. We visited Vegas on an off peak time so the whole entire vacation was just wonderful and not overly packed anywhere. Anyways , we went in for lunch and walked right up to the cashier, no wait! We sat down and the waitress was friendly, even told us don't worry about the 2 hour limit , enjoy your food. Omg the buffet is huuuuuuge. And the quality was great. It wasn't cheap foods cheaply made. It was fresh seafood, prime ribs, smoked bacon, fresh sushi, you name it. I managed to squeeze in 3 plates before a dessert round. Make sure you don't eat at least 5 hours before coming here! You want to come on an empty stomach. Everything was delicious and worth the price!

This buffet is worth it! Chinese food with real steak/beef, mochi ice cream, beef teriyaki short ribs, print rib, brisket, fresh salsa and chips of many types, and lots of meat. Very clean, fancy, and expansive. Nice renovation.

In my opinion the best buffet in Las Vegas. I think majority of the dishes here are really really good. I think it's priced rather heavily but then again what isn't in Vegas. I think for bang for your buck you might as will go to wicked spoon because I believe it is cheaper and still has a decent quality or range of food. What I like about Bacchanal Is definitely the quality and the signs and all the food items even though this is buffet style. It is definitely more festive than wicked spoon in my opinion which is weird because you would think there would be more of a fun vibe at the cosmopolitan but here hits home with a social scene.  Never been disappointed the many times I've been here. You won't go wrong !

The fresh oysters on half shells & the sweet crab legs (cut in half so you don't need to crack them open) were what stood out to me the most. That and the all you can drink house wines & beer for on only $22! I'm not normally a fan of crab legs at buffets but this place won me over! Everything else was between good/OK.

An extra star for their huge selection of food. The buffet spans out into another room which has all the Italian & Asian foods. 

One thing I wasn't too wowed over with was their dessert bar. I expected something grander with more yummy desserts. 

I'd definitely come back for oysters & crab legs! -and maybe the all you can drink!

Went Friday at 10a--double prices because this weekend was a Holiday weekend.  Abusive, but whatever, we were there and we were hungry.  What I can't abide, though, is that for $56 a head, the food had been sitting out since opening, and was cold and dry.  Preposterous.  Negates the overwhelming variety completely.  There was a food refresh at shift change, ~11:30, but a lot of the old food stayed out.  What can I say?  I certainly won't be going back, and I recommend that if you go, make sure it's not a price-hike time (anywhere near a holiday), and make sure you go at the beginning of a meal period.

The 2 problems with this buffet are the lack of transparency about their prices & dining hours & the over hype about their food. Do they post their prices & hours for lunch, dinner? NO. Can you believe the yelp reviews here? NO
My partner & I read the reviews & had dinner here Thursday Sept 28. We used our Total Rewards card & the bill for the 2 of us with tax was over $82. Reviews mostly don't know what they talking about. 1 review here said beer & wine complimentary with dinner. No, not true. Other review said they have 3 types of crab with even separate section for claws. No, not true. The crab legs are OK but were kind of salty. The salad selection is lacking in variety. Most small portions are OK. The staff is friendly. Bottom line: would we come back? NO

best buffet ever. 5/5

You should to go early or not during peak times or else you will be waiting in lines of +2hrs. Part of the buffet of the buffet promotion, I think its worth it to pay the $25 surcharge as its still beats paying regular price. They have a huge variety of foods from pho, udon, pad thai, ramen, fresher seafood, a vast dessert selection, unlimited mimosas, prime rib, a deep fryer section, creme brulee etc. All the foods were above average and the service was top notch. 

Basically its a must try if you are in vegas. Just try and come early to avoid the frustrating wait times because everyone wants to go here.

THIS IS MY ALL TIME FAV BUFFET! 

PRICE: $$$$
-breakfast $20+
-lunch $30+
dinner $50+
You are paying for an awesome buffet with so many different stations with unlimited, quality food. It is definitely worth it!

WHAT TO TRY:
-red velvet pancakes
-hand made dim sum
-pho
-baked to order soufflés
-oxtail soup
-fresh oysters

and can't forget: DESSERT:
-hand made crepes topped with fruit and other toppings
-sorbet and gelato
-macarons
-crème brulee

Only downfall is the wait! Expect an hour or two wait in line . . . but hey, you're in Vegas . . . its expected!!!

For the first time, I ate dinner at the Bacchanal Buffet last week and the line was long but in my opinion, the wait was worth it. When I compare restaurants, I try to compare ones which are similar to each other. My comment compares the typical good buffets in Las Vegas to the Bacchanal Buffet. Also, I read very little about this restaurant before I went. If you want quality buffet food and don't mind paying extra, you really don't need to read the rest of this comment. I would recommend to go here and enjoy the experience. 

The atmosphere is very modern and fresh, tables and seats are very comfortable. The food quality was excellent. I first learned from the server that they have 500 dishes each night and all the dishes are gourmet. 

Remember to get their early, plan on staying for about two hours and enjoy the food. The chefs are very open to questions and comments, I found this very refreshing. Then from what I've read online, the chiefs are open to requests. If you like a variety of food, enjoy a nice atmosphere and like to take your time while eating, I hope you have as good of an experience as I did.

I had decided to try the buffet after my friend had said this place was the best buffet and worth the wait and the price.  We registered at the kiosk around 5pm and it said the wait would be around 85 mins and we should return around 6:19.  They ended up texting us at 5:45, so we beelined over.  Turns out, that was just the line to pay.  We finally paid around 7 ish, and then had to get into another line to actually get a table.  We didn't get in until 7:30.  Once we got sat, we ordered our bottomless drinks from our server.  Who, maybe 20 mins in, was off his shift.  So we cashed out with him and got another server.  We had to wait a long time before she would refill our drinks and clear our table, I'm assuming because we didn't pay her, so she didn't bother to service us.  

All the negatives aside, the food was REAAAALLY good.  There was a giant selection, and everything we tried was delicious.

Had I known the time they quoted us was inaccurate, I maybe would have paid the 25 dollars to skip the line.  But paying around $80 for a buffet seems pretty ridiculous.  I think next time I will go much earlier to put our name in and just do an earlier dinner.

We decided to try this buffet based on recommendations from family and the selection was huge. There was a long wait but with so many in our party it was expected (7 people). There was so much variety of food I definitely recommend making a round to check out the selections. The food was pretty good with the exception of an incident with my son's food which is the reason for the one star. My son picked chicken, a cheeseburger, and Mac and cheese. He noticed blood on the bottom of his cheeseburger bun and looking further there was blood all over his mac and cheese as well. The culprit was the chicken he had already bitten into. The chicken was still raw! I had notified our waitress who had told me to show the dish to the chefs at the carving station. I took the plate to them and they inspected his food saying they would take care of it. I then told a manager about the issue and all he did was give me his business card and to call if my son had any problems. This was a disappointing experience from a highly rated and expensive buffet. Nothing was done to compensate for the issues with the raw chicken my son consumed and it seemed like there wasn't even a concern about the quality of the food.

3.5 stars

We waited about an hour for lunch! I hate waiting for food.

The food was okay, the layout was a little weird and the giant mirrors made the place seems huge but it was also misguiding.

I tried the prime rib, clam chowder, tator tots, fried chicken, pasta, risotto, and a bunch of other stuff. My favorite was the fried chicken, it had a flakey, buttery skin and fried perfectly. 

The dessert was okay, I had higher expectations since it looked so beautiful.
