Best buffet on the strip, don't waste your time anywhere else. Maybe only the Wynn for it's ambiance and opulent decor, but no other is superior that the Bacchanal as of today.
Best food this chain has to offer in Las Vegas. If you are a total rewards member the price is low for what they serve. Slight upcharge for the buffet pass but is worth it.

Let's face it, there are a lot of buffets in Las Vegas.  I've been to several of them and by far this is the best buffet I've ever been to.  I used to frequent the Bellagio buffet when I would visit Vegas.  Now that I've been here, I'm sure this will be my new go-to Vegas buffet.  

Similar to other buffets, they separate everything by cuisine/type: Asian (mostly Japanese, Chinese, and Korean), Italian (charcuterie, pasta, pizza), American (ribs, burgers, fries, etc.), seafood, salad bar, brunch food, and dessert.  The portions are smaller than most buffets, which I really enjoy because it gives you the opportunity to try more food without feeling guilty about wasting anything.  Most of the small plates also come in mini containers.  The sweet potato tater tots come in miniature fryer baskets, the yogurt parfaits come in small Mason jars, and the Shanghai dumplings come in miniature bamboo steamers.  They were so cute I was tempted to steal them, but didn't of course.  Dessert is my kryptonite and their dessert section is awesome.  They have crepes made to order, gelato, cookies, pastries, and pies.

Lunch is about $45 with tax.  We ended up going on Saturday around 11:30 am, which seemed like a good time.  The line was surprisingly short.  They start serving dinner at 3 pm, so if you're really hungry and/or feeling really glutinous, you can try coming a bit later and eating both lunch and dinner, but the line will probably be longer at that time.  

Just a tip: they won't seat you until your entire party is available.  We were waiting for my friend and her family who were running late and we had to wait on the side until they arrived.  The hostess mentioned they do this because some people will say that someone is coming, but they won't show up for another 1-2 hours which holds up the entire table.  This makes sense if they profit from table turnover.  After waiting a good 15-20 minutes for my friend and her family to arrive, the hostess decided to go ahead and seat us.  I'm assuming this was an act of kindness and definitely an exception to the rule.  Their waiting service was also really great.  My friend's daughter was not feeling well, and sadly enough ended up throwing up on herself and the chair she was sitting on (not because of the food, but from a previous sickness).  I thought the waitress would be upset, but instead she was very comforting and gave us wet towels to clean up the mess and a new clean chair for her to sit on.   

Out of restaurants in general, I give Bacchanal a 4 out of 5.  Out of buffets I definitely would give it a 5 out of 5 because the quality was great for food that is made in mass production.  I definitely would visit again, but maybe wear Spandex so I can eat more.

Yes - It is extensive.
Yes - The food is well made (only a few bland options, but hey, you've got to have something for those with more sensitive palates). 
Yes - You will need to block at least four hours out of your day.

I headed over on Sunday at about 2:30 in the afternoon. Long wait (about an hour) and finally seated in the main room area near the dessert section (thank you!). 

The options were plentiful and the Asian selection was so well flavored I actually headed back for seconds.

The sweets options were amazing too. Next time I will start with gelato and end with salad as I missed out on trying a few of the tarts. 

So why one less star? It's waaaaay understaffed. Our server saw my table (of 4 and 1 baby) maybe 4 times in the 2.5-3 hours we were there. Drinks were refilled once, plates cleared twice. It wasn't her fault though. The place was just too packed for the amount of staff. Our group even heard the chefs asking if their break time was coming up. 

From my experience with Vegas buffets, this is going to be a major issue in the future. Food quality will decrease and you will be stacking your plates high.

Go now when it is at it's premium high, in 6 months there will be some major reductions of quality.

I was sort of disappointed with the quality of food at Bacchanal Buffet. There was a variety of food from different regions of the world; however, they were just mediocre. Overall, it was an experience, but I would not come back

This place was amazing. We came here for a champagne brunch while celebrating a friend's birthday in Vegas, and she recommended this as one of the better buffets. There was a short line when we arrived around 11:30, but we only waited about 5 minutes to be seated, and our waitress was really nice! She was very on top of drink refills and was happy to bring as many mimosas as we wanted. Since we were celebrating, that was a lot!

There is so much variety here that everyone will be able to find things they like. There's a really extensive selection of Asian foods, a number of Italian dishes (including some delicious charcuterie and breads!), a Mexican section, a homestyle section, a big salad bar, and a seafood section. Then a huge, free-standing dessert display in the middle of the restaurant, including made-to-order crepes and about 10 kinds of gelato.

Everyone had different favorites and techniques. One girl ate two plates of crab before consuming anything else. Others went straight to the little-bit-of-everything, let's do this in order so we don't miss anything. Personally, I went straight for the meat. If I'm going to eat at a buffet, I'm not going to waste stomach space on side dishes! I really enjoyed both the brisket (smoked over peach wood) and the prime rib. The man who was carving the meats was particularly amusing. He greeted a number of groups as they entered/left and was very jovial and friendly!

The desserts were a highlight, particularly the made-to-order crepes. We left the waitress know it was our friend's birthday, and she brought out a really lovely plate of mini desserts.

I will add that I felt pretty terrible after eating here, but I don't think that was the restaurants fault. Anyone who starts the day with plates full of meat and 5 mimosas brings that stomachache on themselves!

We were on a return trip to LV and becuase we had some friends who loved this buffet we decided to give it another try, maybe it was "grand opening" issues that they worked out.

I will say the lines were not near as long, we went this time on a Sunday night.  The meat station still had a line that you had to wait in, in my opinion this is becuase all the meat is centered around a 6 foot carving station unlike other buffets where they may have multiple carving stations.

The food quality was as good as Wynn or Bellagio but I wouldnt say heads an shoulders better for the price.

Just OK in my book.  I wouldnt say no to going back but I think I would be just as happy at the others.
I was so disappointed.. Don't believe all the hype. Chinese food is like panda, pizza is pizza, sushi is basic and the meat section is the same as any other cheaper buffets. Better avoid.

David Jones,
Had dinner with the family,the buffet is such a beautiful place to din. The food was amazing! The dessert station is one of the best that you can find in a buffet. I would defenitely go back there again! I really enjoyed!

WOW!! This has to be my FAVORITE Buffet in Vegas hands down... We were there celebrating a Birthday, the Service provided by the Manager Samantha , the Server Maricela & Brian the GM  truly amazed my entire Party...This day will be forever etched in our hearts  As for the Food,  it was Absolutely Wonderful from Preparation to Presentation. Thank you for an amazing experience ..

This is the only buffet i've ever been to that requires the simultaneous use of focus, attention, planning, and execution. I would be doing you no favors by listing the food I ate; unless you also ate dinner there on July 29th, i'm sure there will be something different. And if you did eat dinner there on that night, hey, nice to see you again, want me to remind you what you probably ate?

How to plan, manage, and ultimately win at Bacchanal Buffet:

1. Get there early, knowing you will probably wait. A lot. Especially for dinner. The phrase "hey let's grab a quick dinner Bacchanal Buffet" isn't a thing.

2. Enjoy your wait. Take your ticket, walk around. Or, ask the hostess if there is "anything that can be done" to get in the line earlier because of "an amazing reason that is totally true." Our reason was ehh but it still worked. It was true, at the very least; we had a show to attend to.

3. Take a seat. You are officially on the clock, but, thankfully, this isn't the NFL draft and you have more than 10 minutes to do something.

4. Get some water, then go exploring. Visit the stations before you start piling food on a plate. Smell the smells.

5. Prioritize food you wouldn't normally get at home. Example: I can only assume Las Vegas pizza would be generally not as good as any slice I could routinely get in NYC, so I stayed away. However, the variety of dishes from the far east and a great deal of interesting seafood and carved meats peaked my interest, so that's where I gravitated.

6. Get a plate, and fill it with appetizer sized portions of a lot of different things. One or two dumplings, not 6. Easy there buddy.

7. STAY AWAY from the bread. You have bread everywhere. Don't fill yourself up on it.

8. Hit the meat and the seafood early. Depending on where you are sitting, that may be the farthest station from you. This is where the ROI is strongest, so enjoy a non-appetizer sized portion of crab legs. You've earned it.

9. Hey! Stay away from the bread!

10. Once you've finished round 1, grab your next plate. Get larger portions of things you really liked, maybe a few more small things to try. Don't forget to really go to town on the carving station and the seafood.

11. Eat at a normal pace, relax, have some water.

12. Full? Too bad. Go to the dessert area and go nuts. Big plate, small plate, bowl. Want some crepes? Done. Ice cream? Yup. Four varieties of chocolate covered strawberries? Indeed. Cake? Absolutely.

13. NOW you are full. You just won. Leave a tip, move on to the next activity of the evening.

For me, the highlights were definitely the carved meats, dumplings/asian food, and seafood. Pizza was pizza, sushi was sushi, pasta was pasta. There were more choices than I could really attend to, but I made an attempt to at least try as much as I could.

Come hungry, eat, and enjoy.
Great food at a reasonable price. Only downfall was the oysters were a bit funky. Maybe I'm spoiled being from the east coast

Ok - by far the best buffet I had in Vegas - way better than the Wicked Spoon at Cosmo.  The food was very very tasty and worth the 45 minute wait.  It is pricey ($55) and there are no discounts, but literally everything we ate here was better than its counterpart at Wicked Spoon which was also reputed to be a top 5 buffet spot in Vegas.  Will definitely be back!

I waited months in anticipation to eat here.   Seeing all the videos, pics and reviews I had high hopes the Bacchanal would leave me with a huge smile on my face and a happy satisfied tummy.   It turned out to be a huge let down.   After waiting an hr, then another 30 mins after paying I  was finally seated.   There wasn't a single item I ate that left me wanting more.   Everything I tried was mediocre at best.  Sadly most all of the seafood/sushi I tried got thrown away due to tasting rotten/old aside from the crab legs.  

The prime rib was raw (not rare) in the middle due to them cutting corners to keep up with traffic.  I don't mind a little rare but it was raw!  Crab legs should be steamed not sitting in a pool of hot water.  Having to walk back to your table slowly so all the excess water doesn't spill over, crab water squirting everywhere when cracking, along with destroying the beautiful texture crab legs should have.  As a result my table had to be constantly cleaned by my waitress.   The couple of different fish dishes I tried were bland, boring and had dried up edges from sitting out which ended up getting thrown away.   A couple of the dim sim items I tried were ok but the edges were also dried up from sitting.  The mac n cheese noodles were under cooked, still hard in texture (inedible).

Half way through dinner my stomach started turning I'm guessing from the oysters or sushi.  At that point I was so disappointed with the food I decided to throw in the towel and go for the dessert even though I was barely full.   Unfortunately they were closing down the dessert section by the time I got to it, so a lot of the items I eyed on my way in were gone or being packed up.  Pretty sad the highlight of the meal was the desserts.   I did enjoy everything I sampled aside from the Gelato.  The texture and creaminess wasn't proper along with an icy crusty film.  

All and all the biggest food let down on my trip to Vegas.  Such a bad feeling when you pay a lot of $$ for a meal only to walk away unsatisfied/unhappy.   The Bacchanal sure did manipulate me.  The design, layout and presentation of the buffet is top notch. But the food, flavor, freshness was the complete opposite.  This experience has made me never want to eat at another buffet again.   I personally would have rather spent the money at a nice restaurant and saved me almost 2hrs of my time waiting in line.  It was such a bad experience I regret not speaking with the manager to get my $$ back which is something I have never done but wish I did.
  

Jonah crab-so cold n overcooked the meat stuck to the shell which in turn made the time it took to get the little amount of meat not worth the trouble.  Even the little amount of meat I was able to get was little fibers rather than chunks. Huge let down.

Snails- surprisingly good

Shrimp- did not enjoy. Mushy in texture

Oysters-some of the worst I've ever had the displeasure of eating on top of lots of broken shell.  I tried force feeding myself after one due to not wanting to throw them out.   Almost threw up my meal after the 3rd one.  They tasted so old/rotten.   Nothing more unpleasant then old rotten tasting seafood.

Sushi- all the fish on the nigiri had a spoiled/rancid taste.  It was inedible.

Prime rib- the entire center of the roast was cold/raw.

Lamb chop- very tough, difficult to cut

We came this past April wanting to see what all the fuss was about. The line was reasonable (probably because we came at an off time) and we got seated within about 20 minutes. Once we were seated they took our drink orders (not a big fan of waiter service at a buffet, but I guess they figure it makes sense for the price). 

ATMOSPHERE:

The dining area is beautiful. I don't know why I was surprised but it was much cleaner and nicer than I thought it would be. They clear tables, clean messes, etc all in record time and it shows. On top of that, the buffet itself is well taken care of; the floors were free of spills and loose food and the counters were amazingly clean considering how many people were here. The space is HUGE! It was deceiving at first because we had seen one section, then turned the corner and there were at least 3 more! Crazy amount of food.

SERVICE:

We didn't have a lot of interaction with the staff (what I expect from a buffet, not a complaint). However, when we did talk with them they were nice and prompt in helping us with whatever we needed. The staff at the front were also very patient with large groups and families, so props to them!

FOOD:

Here is where it all really matters. A buffet isn't worth anything if the food can't match up to the surroundings and staff. Well, like a lot of others have said, I really expected much better quality for the 120$ total for both my boyfriend and I. Not to say the food was bad, because it was by no means bad! What I mean is that the amount of dishes that were amazing did not outweigh the amount that were mediocre or bad. I remember the tacos, pizza, and BBQ having a good flavor, and the fried chicken had a good batter that just needed a bit more spice. I really do recommend trying everything you can, because my taste may be different than yours. Plus, you're paying for it so you might as well get everything at least once! The only thing I STRONGLY recommend AGAINST getting was the ramen. I didn't expect buffet ramen to be anywhere near authentic tasting but man was this terrible. The broth was like taking a sip of salt with a hint of water. The noodles were still hard, too! Absolutely awful. Try it if you want but I did warn you about this one.

OVERALL, I'm glad I went to Bacchanal. It really is an experience that I think everyone should try at least once on their Vegas journeys. However, there are just too many other options for food (and buffet) for me and I'm not in a hurry to go back. I probably will return some time, but it is definitely not my #1 preference.

Super underwhelming.  Lots of choices, little that I would recommend.  Not sure why this place has such a high rating from others.  Even the pastries were mediocre.  I am second guessing whether two stars is being overly generous.

I tried it out since everyone was raving about the quality of the food. I was not impressed. It was "pretty good for buffet food" but that's not really saying very much...

My favorite thing was the street tacos, but for the price I paid to get in; I could have gotten that else where. 


I doubt I would go back.
Great food love those mini doughnuts need a place in oc please and one know of the place

Food was very fresh. Nothing showed signs of sitting around a while. I know what to search for in a buffet that has been replated. Nothing found with dried out crusts.. Fresh and if it's been out I see it being tossed into the trash. King Crab legs fresh. Sushi was fresh, everything was tasty. If you like buffets then this is a splurge.. We ended up sitting for 3 hours.. My legs went numb.. I'm not sure if I have enough insulin to carry me through. But it is worth the splurge.. I ate a little bit of everything and my stomach is paying the price for gluttony..OMG!!
Best Mac and cheese ever. And the mashed potatoes were so buttery, they slid around on the plate. AWESOME.

This buffet is considered one of the best buffets in Las Vegas, but in my opinion, it's not worth the price nor the wait. First of all, the waiting period is SUPER LONG, unless you are willing to pay an extra fee per person to cut in line. Overall, I think we waited almost 3 hours (including the waiting time in the ticket). We paid about $65/person, excluding alcohol. Once we were inside, there wasn't a huge selection of food as we expected. Maybe our expectations were too high for the price that we were paying.

For the price it's not all that and I'm talking about the food and the staff, most of them including the cooks are rude not all of them but the majority are. Lots of pork on their food like bacon and the signing isn't to clear on it, seafood is the big reason why it's expensive (of course).
 
But here's the kicker they give you a 2 hour dining limit! Wtf I mean I didn't plan on it but fuck at $50 a pop don't put a limit on me. 

It's Vegas guys amazing food at every Corner don't break your wallet for shit you can get back home for half price.

Officially my favorite buffet on the strip, hands down! 
Sorry Wicked Spoon.... After the hype and all the news about the greatness of Wicked Spoon, I was really disappointed in the quality of the food and the lack of variety and presentation.

Bacchanal... Wow talk about getting what we paid for. My hubby and I absolutely loved it. We waited about an hour but man, it was worth it! Very creative in display and presentation, awesome variety of unique dishes, very scrumptious desserts, and great service! 

We will definitely be back! Thanks for the great food!
The fresh oysters during dinner was my favorite. This buffet has so many different kinds of food, and so fresh and delicious. I just wish the staff could be more helpful and friendly.

We waited about 35 minutes.  I saw people had the option to pay $25 to skip ahead, but I think if you plan ahead and come earlier/check out the wait time, you shouldn't have to risk wasting that money and still have to wait, especially if the restaurant is already full of customers.

It was $37.99 a person but we got a partial discount due to the fact that our family members gamble a lot haha.  I would say this was an amazing first try, but for the money I would probably come here once a year.  When I'm in Vegas, I either eat at the unique eats or cheap buffets but I did enjoy my experience here.  The staff is very attentive and the food is ample/diverse.  It seemed that every time I went up, there was something different or new to try.  We enjoyed the option to get fresh fruit juices as well!

Main highlights for food: poke salad, pork belly (with mashed potatoes), dim sum, cheese selections, fish and chip basket, fried chicken and sweet potato fries basket, shitake mushroom, cocktail shrimp, and a lot of the other seafood options (although the shrimp scampi and lobster bisque were very salty..)

Main highlights for dessert: Mango Soup (with tapioca), lemon meringue tart, and the Blood Orange Cream Puffs.  (macarons were amazing but too sweet, and for gelato, there were lots of flavors but I felt it was too milky/melted too fast)

What people say about Wicked Spoon is that the desserts are pretty but aren't great in quality.  I could say the same about the cupcakes.  The cupcakes were decorated very nicely but the cake itself was dry; I could have made better quality ones.  I enjoyed taking the pictures of the cute cupcakes and trying the edible decorations though :P

Minus 1 star though because of this though: I didn't like that they took your picture for you and promised to pass them out to you at your table (no mention of price).  That never happened.  After we ate, we went to the front desk to ask a photographer on the status, and she was kind enough to go to the back and reprint them.  But when she brought it out, she wanted to charge us for the photo and the display they were in (over $20 I believe).  I wish they had told us it wasn't free from the beginning instead of wasting everyone's time and their ink!
This is hands down the best of the best..... The food is amazing and the service is great  . Been to all the places on the strip and no other Buffet comes close to the bacchanal Buffet, a must try

Best buffet I had in years! This is one of the best buffets I had in a long time. It's right next to Bellagio and Wynn standards. Great job in transforming into a high end buffet. Btw a lil tip if you wanna get seated quick and avoid the extremely long line then I suggest you pay the extra $15 and get the 24hour pass. So worth it.

This is not a place for those with small stomachs or picky palates. You want to make sure you get your $50 worth here and I sure did. The spread is AMAZING. I made sure to try everything that interested me. The Chinese was a little disappointing, sushi was good, and the prime rib was superb. Sides were delish (mac&cheese and sweet potato tater tots!), seafood galore and all the dessert your heart desires (gelato, an assortment of macarons, cookies, pie, EVERYTHING). Compliments to the pastry chef whom our waitress brought out for us to meet. 

I wish I had more space to try a half rack of ribs, lamb, BBQ and all that jazz at the meat station, as well as all of the other food (Italian, Mexican, American). I had to tap out and pretty much had to be rolled out of there. Then I slowly waddled my way back to my hotel. Gluttony's finest.

So disappointed!!! With all the great pictures and reviews we thought this was going to be fantastic!  We paid $70 per person (included a generous tip) and were so disappointed. 

Quality of sushi sucked.  Paper thin pieces of fish on nigiri and just California rolls as the other options.  Pictures we saw were of king crab legs, we got skinny snow crab legs. Other stations we just ok. Nothing spectacular to justify why we pay so much!!!  

Staff at the serving stations were so rude. I don't know if they were so busy, but they definitely didn't want to be there.  

Only thing I could say was the ramen was good. Fresh cooked noodles in great broth. Thanks for the $70 ramen!

Caesars Palace must have paid the newspapers to vote them as the best buffet in LV.  I went to Atlantis in Reno last year.   It's way better and cheaper.  They said they have king crab legs, but ends up with snow crab legs only.  The food is just average, and they charged us 50.99 per person on Christmas eve, that's ridiculous.  I gave them 2 stars because we could get a ticket which told us how long and what time to come back - 5 hours, so we don't have to wait in line for 5 hours.  But when we went back at the time showed on the ticket, we still needed to wait for 1/2 hours, that's fine.   But after we got in, we saw many empty tables with lots of empty plates.  No one cleaned those tables and they just made people wait outside.  If I'm the owner, I would be very mad.  The service is average.   No one refilled our drink until we asked the waitress.   I will definitely never go back again..

While I liked this experience and it served its purpose as a buffet, I would have been very disappointed if I paid full price to go into it. Despite the options it provided, it still racked up to over $170 for three of us, and if we didn't have a $150 voucher, there would have been no way we could have afforded it. After eating we came to the consensus that we probably wouldn't have tried to save to eat here again. 

The variety was rich, with a standout Asian section and an extensive seafood section (not here to diss crab legs, because they were amazing here). However, there were some features that weren't particularly amazing. For example, the dessert table. It might have been the night we went, but most of the desserts I got seemed off. The crème brulee, egg tart and gelato seemed like the stars, but they also were significantly better than anything else I got. 

If you have the money to spend to dine here, I suggest you do it since it is quite the experience, but don't bend over backwards to eat here. 

A side note: I went here for dinner, and realize that the brunch buffet is the one that people praise, so I would give this another shot for brunch, but probably not again for dinner service.

Bacchanal is one of the top buffets in Vegas for a reason. There's enough food to feed a whole country. 
I'm usually the type of person to try a little bit of everything at a buffet, but here, I had to pick wisely.
While the variety is pretty amazing, I had a bit higher of expectations for the quality. Being as pricey as it is, I was hoping dishes would taste restaurant level. While there was nothing that tasted necessarily bad to me, I don't recall being really wowed by anything either.

I won't list every single thing I ate, so here's what I'd rank the top 3 items:
1. Steamed crab legs - Bless the lady for giving me like three pounds of this stuff. Although time consuming, this made the meal worth it more than anything.
2. Wagyu from the carving station - not overly seasoned and fairly tender (even though I doubt it's authentic Wagyu)
3. Grilled Salmon - Yum, soft and saucy. Great execution.
* Also, side note: the salad bar here stood out to me more than they usually would at other buffets.

And the 3 things I was most disappointed with:
1. Fresh oysters/Bloody Mary oyster shooter - Just no. Don't do it.
2. Wagyu slider - These looked sooo good, but tasted so plain -__-
3. Desserts - Yeah, custom crepes are cool and all, but other than that, I feel like there was not too much to choose from that you couldn't find at every other buffet.


I do think I'll come again since I only tried maybe half of their items. But not anytime soon. Cuz I'm not trying to go fat and broke that quick.

Nothing special.

Service: Average.
Price: Relatively expensive, not worth it in my opinion.
Food: Nothing special. 
- Fried Chicken was dry
- Burger sliders tasted like cafeteria food from middle school
- Sushi was terrible
- It goes on and on..



But the worst part was finding an eyelash in my girlfriend's creme brulee. Told one of the server and she supposedly told the manager, but never got back to me (So I'm not even sure she did). I decided to go tell management myself and their reply was "Sorry, would you like another one?"..........It's a buffet, I can get it myself. At least offer a partial refund to rectify the situation.

This place is good but I dont think it's that great that you have to pay alot of money for a good buffet in Vegas.  My husband and I did not have a good experience at this buffet. They took so long to sit us and then the waitress that was picking up our dirty dishes disappeared.  All I wanted was a cracker for the crab legs!  I had to get up and find a different waitress.  Overall,  not going back.  It's Not worth it!!

They have a oyster bar!!!  That gets 1 star on its own.  Everything at Bacchanal was fresh and good, although very salty to my taste.  (But I have yet to find a buffet in Vegas that does not have salty food so I will make this a uniform factor for all Vegas buffets and ignore it.  I heard they purposefully make their food more salty to get you full faster?  Is there any truth to this?)  I especially loved the little drink corner in the Mexican section with horchata, tamarindo, jamaica, etc.  They were so cute in their little jars!  The Asian section does need some major fixing up to do, however.  Especially in the sushi corner.  Nothing looked appetizing.  But the japanese ramen was really good (and much needed for my hangover).  I was soo stuffed I couldn't even make it to the dessert section!!  I am very disappointed in myself for this.  Next time I must leave enough space for dessert.

Thanksgiving weekend = three hour wait & $50 per person all day (i think usually its $40 per person for lunch)
& it was actually worth it! Everything especially the seafood was super fresh! There were mexican, american, italian, asian, salad, and dessert sections. 
Lots of meat- steak, ribs, sausages, chicken. fries, mashed potatoes, burgers, anything you can think of thats american
Served the crab both hot and cold, shrimp, ceviche.
tuna and salmon sashimi, mostly tuna sushi.
Lots of different kinds of chinese food
oysters came out after three so thank goodness we stayed for a good three hours
lots of variety for dessert, lots of ice cream flavors, cakes etc.
theres also on chocolate covered strawberries for dinner

service was great, everyone was super friendly and attentive.
the only thing was that I kept comparing everything to Wicked Spoon, Bacchanal has better quality seafood and more variety of meat but Wicked spoon has more small unique dishes and a better dessert section. Overall they're both about the same to me, just this place usually has a longer wait.

Would def. come back for more!

3.5 stars

Many choices
Great variety
Love the udon 
Love the Chinese food
Prime rib - eh..
Ribs - ok too
Price - expensive


Service - depends on the day. Sometimes it's awesome and other times are not because of the crowds and how busy it is.

Maybe it's just me but I like to sit and relax and eat rather than feeling rush or annoyed of the people and the wait for food? Also, isnt it annoying when you come back to your table and still find your old plate still sitting there? Or you have to flag your server for refills? No thank you. 

If I'm paying that much for a buffet I expect good service. Wicked Spoon and the Buffet has the best service but even know though the variety isn't as great compare to Ceasars I rather stick with them.

Sometimes having too much choices can be a bad thing and the quality isn't that great since there isn't a main focus.

Hands down, HANDS DOWN, the BEST buffet in Las Vegas. My wife and I went to most of the major buffets throughout the city during the past year (M, Red Rock, Wicked Spoon, various Stations, Luxor, Bellagio), and this one wins. The drawback is it is highly expensive, but it is worth every cent. The way I judge a buffet is as follows: Would I purchase an item found at the buffet individually in a sit down restaurant? If I can answer yes to the majority of what I eat, then I know I'm at someplace special. Everything I tried was of the highest quality and flavor. In addition, the buffet is HUGE. I had my plate full when I went around another corner and found another ROOM of buffet. I panicked, but I made it work. This place is truly incredible.

Features:
-This buffet is located in Ceasar's Palace.  When we came, the line was streaming long.  Luckily, we had a card that allowed us to walk straight in.
-The inside is huge!  Lots of tables and extremely spacious.  
-Depending on what you try, I would recommend to consume the seafood (especially crab legs), sushi, Chinese dishes, udon, and ramen.  Those were especially delicious for me.  
-The dessert bar had a lot of sweets from shave ice to cookies and cakes.  
-Champagne and mimosas are free! Drink up!

Improvements:
-They could definitely improve on the pho (taste), dim sum (har gou was cold and hard to chew), and fruits (did not seem as fresh).
-Service was a little slow.  I asked for ice twice and finally got it almost ten minutes later.

Tips:
-To avoid long lines, come early or go with someone who has the Diamond Card.
-They had carrot, orange, apple juice, and almond milk in cute little jars.

I am sooo sad.  I waited and planned and brought a group of 15 with me for what I thought was going to be an epic meal only to be sooo dissapointed.  
the food choices were minimal
the ambiance was loud and hard to navigate
the food quality was not worth the price 
this buffett is really small for the price and the wait
I have had so many better buffets, I am not sure what the hype is all about.  I have seen so many youtube videos saying how awesome this buffett was only to be sooo disappointed.

Very hesitant to rate this as 3 stars given all the praise Bacchanal has received. I would say it's 3.5 given the high expectations and price we had to pay (holiday dinner $70 per person). If it weren't for the holiday pricing, I would rate this place as 4 stars. Anyhow, I've been waiting to visit this place since 3 years ago when I first heard about it. Was expecting an explosion of flavor in each dish (or at least most of them), but sadly that didn't happen. Not sure if it's because the place was too busy or quality has went down since my friends first raved about it. 

Waiting: An employee said "It's like Disneyland". Honestly, it was. Thanks to previous yelp reviews, I planned my schedule successfully to eat on time. So, went to the kiosks at ~2:30pm to pick up a ticket and waitlist times were 100 minutes. Then, I came back at ~4:07pm after strolling around The Forum Shops. Once I arrived, I was expecting to wait an hour and I actually did since I got table at 5:10pm. FYI, if you came in at 4pm to get a ticket, the wait times went up to 200 minutes (3 hrs!). This means, even if you pick up a ticket at 4, you'll have to come back at 7 to wait in line and most realistically eat at 8-8:30pm. Also, this was the day before Christmas Eve (12/23) so wait times could be even worse in the days leading up to New Years. Or, you might wait less when it's not during holiday season. MOST IMPORTANT FYI, if you have a party of 5 or more, unfortunately you would have to wait the entire time in the buffet. There are no kiosks for large parties.....feel bad for those big parties to be honest because who knows how long the wait was for them. 

This will be a long review given the amount of food they provided...

~DRINKS~
Peach green tea was amazing (and free)! I didn't get that uncomfortable artificial sweet taste afterwards, but I definitely did feel the sweetness in the tea. Ironic really. However, the tea did bother my mom because she thought it was unnecessarily sweet. Just try it, it's complimentary. 

Grapefruit juice does seem fresh, but it was too bitter for me so I can't enjoy it, especially when I don't like grapefruit to begin with.

Pineapple juice was sold out, so I'd imagine that was popular. 

Orange juice was a bit sour. 

~FOOD~ 
There is really A LOT of food. I love buffets, and for the first time, I actually could not get a taste of everything they had to offer! 

Didn't try the Asian section because I come from a city known for good Asian food so I didn't bother. I did try the seafood winter melon soup, which was nice. It was too thick so I'm assuming this was because the winter melon was in the soup for too long. 

I waited 5-10 minutes in line for the steamed crab legs and they were fresh but also salty. The chef kindly gave everybody a full plate of legs!! 

Salad section was alright and so were the deviled eggs with truffle oil. 

Rigatoni, risotto, and meatballs were also good. Not plain-tasting, but no wow factor. Though, I appreciated how the meatballs were moist. 

Grilled vegetables was too salty for me. The fried green tomato dish that looked like a burger was strange for me. 

American wagyu beef was just....beef? I'm not a meat-lover, so I can't really tell the difference between fantastic quality beef and regular tasting beef. I just know I wasn't blown away. The ribs at the time looked dry, so I didn't get those. 

Fries were soft and chewy. 

In the seafood section, they had soft-shell crab so I took a bunch of those. Again, I wasn't amazed and I think it's because the white corn cream with the crab wasn't a good combo for me. The pan-seared salmon was fresh, but the sauce again didn't work well personally speaking (forgot the sauce sadly). Oyster was not that great and had a fishy smell. Wish they had more fresh fish dishes.

~DESSERT~
It's actually good! Sadly, my stomach couldn't take in all the desserts so I tried the gelato, macarons, chocolate-dipped strawberry, and chocolate cupcake. The cookies and cream gelato was fantastic and the macarons actually had flavor in them. Though, the lemon basil gelato (tasted like sorbetto) was too sweet for me. I noticed they had "Chinese egg tart" which is actually Portuguese style egg tart. Didn't get to try but it does seem legit!

~AMBIANCE/SERVICE~
Classy. It's what you would expect from such a world-famous buffet. Didn't get to sit near the pools, but it was nighttime so you can't see the outside area anyway. The place is HUGE and there were a variety of comfortable seating. Plates were constantly getting picked up and our server was attentive. Didn't wait long to get drinks or ask for something. Also, I had no problems with service from other employees. 

It has been a long time since I've been to Las Vegas, but I think it's safe to say that it is definitely one of the best buffets on the strip given the quality and variety of food. Nothing tastes awful which is an amazing feat.  However, I think the buffets in Macau taste better...

It's 60 some dollars for dinner and there is always a line I guess people want to say they ate  there. Lots of quality food selections but for the price it's just not worth it. The best deal is to get a Groupon or if you lose enough money the casino will comp you. They do have the biggest selection of seafood on a buffet in LV.

Decent buffet. I like how they crowd control this buffet way better than the other buffet on the strip. I hate when they over pack people and there are continuous lines for food or bring you to a table that is still being cleaned. They do not do that here! They also offer a great seafood amount making it well worth the price afterwords. the ribs here are moist. great dessert selection.
Their food is nice compared to other buffets. But sometimes the line is too long and some people give up to eat there.

WOW. Just wow. I can't believe I even get to review this place. And it's all thanks to babe! (Sayem R. -- go add him on yelp so that maybe he can be motivated and start reviewing for you people).

It was a random day. Like I don't even know (can't remember) what we were doing. I'd like to say we were just laying in bed. BUT, babe and I love to go adventure off to different places and try new things. While this wouldn't be his first time eating here (he says he's been there about 3 or 4 times... must be nice to be him right), it definitely was mine. I was super super super excited because I've always wanted to go here!!!! Now the reason why I say it was a random day, because I always thought I'd go there for some sort of big occasion. Like a graduation. Or an anniversary. Or a birthday. But nope. It was just a random day. Like, what do you want for lunch honey?

So we ended up going there for their brunch. And I was in awe that the line wasn't long. I was anxiously waiting like a kid in a candy store to get to the front. Turns out brunch was $50 and unlimited mimosas was an extra $15. I've never done that in my life so I said why not. 

Babe made me start allllll the way at the end (towards the back w/the asian food) and we worked our way down the buffet as we filled our plates. He wouldn't let me go venture off and see anything because it all was going to be a surprise for when we got to each station. 

Long story short, this place is nothing short of amazing. (Especially when you're with someone amazing). I think I had about 6 glasses of mimosas and 7-8 plates of food... OKAY sounds like a lot of food but it probably wasn't. Their portions are smaller but I like that because it gives you a chance to try out a bunch of different things. Their little pancake plates were so yummy. The texture was perfect for mini things. The steak and eggs was sooo good! Fried chicken and waffles was.... idk I didn't try it but babe took a picture of me with it (cause they are very picture worthy). The ramen broth was DELICIOUS. And their meat section was very impressive. I was trying to contain myself because I could tell I was getting pretty smiley towards the middle of the meal.

Babe was a trooper and ate a lot. Watched me eat a lot (so I think). And then made fun of me for how smiley/happy I was from the mimosa craze. 

I also want to mention that the dessert section was amazing! Tons of different baked goods, sweet stuff, ice cream, candies, but don't forget the little crepe station. The guy making my crepe made the experience so much fun. He was super sweet, very friendly, and was able to hold conversations with everyone.

I enjoyed this experience so much and I'm glad that I got to spend it with someone so special to me. If you have to choose a fancy buffet, choose Bacchanal!

This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas. Every dish is cooked and presented to perfection. I appreciate all the little details and hard work they've put into each one. 

I'm also very satisfied with the food options for each cuisine which makes me like it even more.

You've likely heard that Bacchanal is one of the best buffet's in Vegas. It probably is one of the best. But, having a men's room with only two stalls for a buffet of this size is a g-d war crime. Come prepared.

Disappointed to say the least...
We have been looking all day to go to a buffet in Vegas.. searched through yelp and google.. ended up here.. payed over $100 for my husband and I .. food was very mediocre .. we had better food at Chinese buffet.. even tho food looks really good, it tastes disgusting.. even pretty desert tastes really bad.. overall my husband got full on crab legs.. I had some sushi and salad..everything else we tried was dry and tasteless .. will never be back

Normally, I'm not a big fan of buffets because I feel like I have to gorge myself on food in order to get my moneys worth, but all the girls in the bachelorette party wanted to enjoy one buffet on our last day in Vegas. Since our party was so large, we got to skip to a special line. We were probably served faster than if we had gone to the normal line, but it wasn't especially quick either. Since it was the weekend after NYE, we had to pay the holiday price, though.

They definitely have a lot of selection and their seafood is strategically hidden in the back on the far right (I missed it my first time around). Nothing stood out, but I stocked up on an entire plate of oysters to make sure I got my moneys worth. They also have a lot of desserts and a large selection of gelato/sorbets. 

There's also bottomless mimosas, but we had our fill of alcohol after our weekend and went straight for the coffee.

Not quite sure if it's worth the price unless you're starving and stock up on seafood, but I guess buffets has almost become synonymous with Vegas now.

Not sure how to rate a nice place and balance it with the fact that 4 out of 6 of our party got food poisoning. If they can eliminate the food poisoning part of the equation I would give it 4.5-5 starts.

Anyways we had a party of 6 do a late lunch/early dinner on Sunday 2/1 at Bacchanal. It's by far the nicest buffet place in Vegas...except for the food borne illness potential. It wasn't the crab or seafood counters...so had to be either the meats, sushi, or desserts counters. The doctor in our group noticed symptoms for himself by 10pm Sunday and warned the rest of the group. By midnight I had symptoms. By next morning two others in our group were also sick with the same gastrointestinal issues.

Would I go back if they eliminated the food borne pathogens? Yes. Could they though based upon volume and quantity? Probably not.

I love this place. Great food and great staff. The only thing I would say. Is to figure out your fly issues. Because i see flies all the time. Also the captains seating people they need to be a lot quicker. I've seen plenty of seats open and they are trying to figure out where to seat people. I've gone here a number of times. I can see a few ways to improve it. The servers are great the cooks are great. Very clean and very nice.

Best buffet in Vegas!

This is just gonna be a short review since around 1500 ppl have reviewed this place already. 
Definitely a MUST when you're in vegas!
TIPS:
The wait could be very hideous; HOWEVER, if you happen to have some good luck and win some gambling moneyyy, LOL there's a express lane for 20$/person! you can SKIP and lined up in front of everyone!
I used express lane this time; so instead of waiting in like for 2.5 hrs, i waited 20minutes. :DAWESOME!

There're SO many choice! and PLUS, they all tasted REALLY authentic and delicious! i hated when I go to some buffets, though they have variety of choices, but they cannot make ONE DISH right. that's not gonna happen in Bacchanal! :) they have american, italian, middle eastern, japanese and chinese food.

Waiters are also very friendly and attentive; even though it's very busy but they will still try to get to you as soon as they can.

We came with a high expectation that this is the best buffet on planet. $52.99 for weekday dinner? You had better prove it to me. A total disappointment after all. I must say there are a whole lot more better buffets in the Bay Area where you can pay half the price including tips and taxes for many more selections such as Tomi's in Concord on a regular weekday. I agree it has nice atmosphere but I was here for the food not something else. No lobster, sashimi, giant clams or other kinds of seafood I regular had at a Bay Area buffet. $60 for snow crab legs, sea bass, Americanized Chinese/Japanese/Italian food... I believe $60 should not only count for freshness but also selection and tastiness. If this is the best buffet in Las Vegas, you will never see me in any buffet at Vegas. Sorry, this is an overrated and over priced place. Try seafood buffets in Bay Area if you are looking for high quality and better selection and don't care about atmosphere or service like I do.

This place is awesome I have been three times and it's always fab. The largest selection of food I have ever seen on a buffet!

Lines can be long but there is a way to reserve your place in line, see your seating time and come back when they are ready for you.

Remember on weekends they do brunch all day so it's approx $50 a person no matter what time. On a non-weekend and non holiday though you can go right at the end of breakfast or lunch and just stay for the transition if you want to taste both and save $ .

It's good but nothing special. It's def. not worth waiting in line for 2 hours and $50.00. They have the express line which is faster but it's $20.00 in addition to the 50.00. Glad I experienced it but wish I spent my time and money at a better buffet spot.
Best buffet in Vegas! Everything was very good and high quality.

Went here for lunch during SEMA week, paid 42 bucks a person which is not bad at all for Vegas.  The selection of food and drinks here is insane!! The food quality is top notch, everything tasted decent to amazing, nothing was bad, except for the buns on the mini burger, it was hard as a rock, but literally everything else was good! Definitely one of the best buffet in Vegas!

If I had to compare between Wicked Spoon and here... Definitely goin with here :) The hubby agrees. Great selection of sweet and savory. The service was top notch, thanks to the wonderful Su (older Asian woman)! She kept checking on us to make sure everything was to our liking. I don't expect much of anything in regards to service at a buffet, buuuuut when you pay $201 for 3 people ($20 tip included)... You'd hope for something pretty darn good. Su was just that. Thank you, Su! This review was for the dinner we just walked out of. And oh yes, when we checked in at the kiosk, we received an approximate wait time of "137 minutes". We waited about an hour. Not too bad. We walked around and received a text alert when it was time for us to be seated.

I wish the staff would have been upfront about the wait. We checked in with 150 minute wait. Then after to be told to wait in 2-hour wait line??? Why not be upfront about it so people can decide whether to pay extra to get to the front of the line or go somewhere else??!!!!

Sooo we were totally discussing over dinner at exactly which point enjoyment of food crosses the line into gluttony, and what exactly about gluttony actually makes it a sin. A very appropriate discussion for a place like Bacchanal.

We arrived around 3:30pm on a Sunday and only had to wait 30 minutes. We tried to get our tired bodies over before lunch ended, but unfortunately were not able (friends told me line up at 2pm to get in for the lunch price, but be able to eat the dinner food-- not sure what the changes is are but that's what I've heard).

What can I say? Basically everything I tried (except for the disappointing macarons and weird strawberry cake pop) was AMAZING. Every single entree plate was delish and I was shocked that even the Asian food was up to par (they even had XLB's! Though the sushi choices were a bit lacking, but standard Americanized sushi was offered).

Atmosphere-wise, the interior is modern and the heavy EDM music really makes eating quite an epic experience. There's nothing like slurping down oysters to every untz untz untz.

My highlights:

Crab legs (naturally)- get them hot from the Italian counter!
Hidden clam treasures in the miso soup
Tacos- okay this isn't really my highlight, but my boyfriend who LIVES in LA ate 6 freakin' street tacos. I was a bit upset, but he claimed they were the best tacos he's ever had in his 28 years of LA life.
Crepes- crepe making station with bottles of Nutella for the win
Sorbet- crisp, delicious, and perfect contrast to the meal

So this is definitely the BEST buffet I've ever been to in Vegas experience-wise and food-wise.

Bacchanal, you have lived up to the hype! 5 stars for you.

I cannot tell you how overrated this place is. You wait forever to pay sky-high prices for so-so food. If you came to Vegas to feast, this is not the place.

We hadn't ate all day in anticipation for this meal. First, we joined the online line using the app. When that line was done, we had to wait in an actual line for 30 minutes at the entrance of the restaurant. You pay upfront, $60 per person for dinner. I thought I was insane to pay that kind of price, but I read about this being a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

The place was huge and very crowded, but we had a nice table. We waited in long lines for food and everything was laid out in a messy way (food remains on the counter). They had so many cuisines; I can't even try to name them all. However, nothing was great. The sushi was not fresh, the crab claws had a strange taste, and the oysters were just inedible. Quite liked the lamb chops and salmon though.

I had five plates of food and don't remember most of what I had. Afterwards, two plates of dessert. I was disappointed though. I saw a "chef" literally unloading macarons from a plastic container, like the kind you get at Costco. Cheap and not made in-house! Many were broken too. I really wanted a souffle, but none were out that night. However, I did see some failed ones behind the counter. Chefs can't even cook a souffle!

Service wasn't great. No one ever came to refill our drinks until we chased a waiter down. All-in-all, incredibly overpriced. Walked out so full and threw up later that night. Probably my own fault, but I really wanted to get my money's worth. Now I know: no matter how much you shove in your stomach, you will never get what you paid for.

Overall, I think I prefer Wicked Spoon.

Their crab quality is just decent. As their crab wasn't that meaty when I ate here.

The buffet is much smaller than I thought it would be. I think it is bigger than Wicked Spoon however.

Around the same price as Wicked Spoon

The major selling point for me that would cause me to come back are the soups. The ramen and pho are so good. You'll likely need these soups after a night of partying in Vegas...

Overall, go here for the soups. Other than that you likely won't be able to eat enough to make the high prices of Vegas buffets worth it
Buffet is always one of the best! Was a little disappointed that the steamed crab is no longer cut in half. However, always wonderful food!

I've had many buffets in Las Vegas and have heard so much about this place from all the news articles raving about the new 17 million dollar buffet, to friends who have come and thoroughly enjoyed it. The expectations and the bar was set pretty high to say the least.

This buffet is absolutely gorgeous with its decorations and decor. You can definitely tell they put a lot of work in making everything look nice to complement the food here. To those who aren't familiar with this place, there are 9 different stations featuring food from 9 different parts of the world. There's lots of variety here and supposedly over 500 choices of different things to eat.

The things that really stood out from this place were the crab legs/seafood section, meat section and dessert station. The crab legs came out cold and fresh, UNLIKE those frozen legs that you would get at the bellagio buffet. There wasn't also a long line for them and I was able to get lots of helpings real quickly. The oysters, lobster clam chowder and paella were all excellent. 

The meat section featured many different kinds of meats and sausages, enough to make you VERY happy. The ribs over here were not tender though but I loved the various kinds of sausages that they have over here to try. 

The dessert section had a lot of desserts I've never seen at other buffets before. Mochis, cake pops and the macaroons were absolutely delicious and they had specialty desserts that were featured in different parts of the world. THEY even had some baklava gelato!

Other things that stood out were the asian noodles station, where you could order various types of noodles throughout all of asia (examples: pho, ramen) and the cheese station where they had various aged cheeses to try. They ALSO had dim sum for those who love it!

Solid buffet to come here, and it met my expectations.

I am not really impressed with their buffet. Overrated. Really good lamb though. But the prime rib was tasteless and dry. Overall, Food was OK but I wouldn't think it's worth the Wait time and the price.
Best buffet I've ever had. Granted, I have only tried Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon (which is still good) in Vegas. Is the wait miserable? Yes. Is it worth it? Yes.

Went here for dinner the other day. Have to say I was very impressed. The food was incredible. They had every option you could imagine and then some. My favorite were the crab legs and the prime rib. All other selections were amazing as well.

There's no arguing that this place has variety over just about every other buffet in Vegas. The risk in trying to serve every kind of food gluttony - everything becomes mediocre. Thankfully they avoid most of that. The Asian section is impressive, real hanging Chinese roast duck. but the sushi section is limited. The meat and seafood stations are the real stand-outs. Although the the snow crab legs (they are not King) are split down the middle for you, they are cold. When you want them hot, they boil it for you. Nice, cuts down on the salty brine, but it also means they are not as fresh as can be. Due to its size, service can vary. I think the waiters are overwhelmed because they first seated us at a table that was occupied, then they refilled our waters twice in two hours. As it's no doubt mentioned here, go in around 2PM, but before 3PM, get the lunch price and stick around for the dinner menu. Though they change it out slowly. I didn't see any stone crab legs out yet by the time I left (8.5 plates later!).

My wife and I were at this buffet about 2 weeks ago (May 20 2018) and were extremely disappointed. It was for the dinner buffet and the food was merely average at best . For the amount charged ( $140 for two ) I would have expected a much higher quality of both seafood and entree items. No lobster dishes and the crab legs were similar to what you find on a  much lower priced buffet elsewhere. The rest of the entrees were ok, but for what you paid seemed lackluster in both presentation and flavor. Desserts have been downgraded in quality and did nothing to enhance the buffet. Alcohol was available for a $15 per person add on but should have been included at the initial price of $70 per diner.   Service was poor too, as our server was much more concerned about the table of " high rollers"  near us and didn't even stop by more than once to clear our table or refill beverages. This was our second visit to the Bacchanal in the last year and we were disappointed in how the quality has dropped so much since our first visit. For a much better buffet I would recommend either the "William B." at the M Resort or the newly renovated Palms buffet which is excellent and costs less than half than the Bacchanal. We travel twice a year to Las Vegas for extended visits and have been to just about every buffet so I believe we have some experience in our rating.

The last time I was here was May 2016. Just about everything was delicious. The service was good too. Side note: We tried going to The Bellagio and unfortunately the food was terrible. We also tried the Cosmopolitan but for some reason the line was literally not moving and the staff didn't acknowledge us to keep us informed as to why there was a delay; they just kept chatting, so we left. With those things in mind, I would say stick to Bacchanal to avoid disappointment.

It has been a while since I've posted a review and perhaps it's because I fell into a rut of going to the same places all the time.  Tonight we decided to try something different and went to the Bacchanal Buffet at  Caesars Palace.

*** With all these five star ratings I really need to explain my two star rating ***

The food at this buffet is definitely above average and there are a lot of things to choose from.  

The staff that handled our beverages and dishes were prompt and friendly.

The meat selections are pretty tasty and there are a lot of seafood dishes.

The items that stood out for me personally were the freshly shucked oysters as well as the very tasty lamb chops.  Also, the crepes to order in the dessert area were awesome with a selection of fresh berries.

*** Here are the challenges they need to overcome that may affect your visit...

1.  After spending about 40 minutes in line to pay for the buffet, you spend a little more time in a "continuation line" waiting to be seated by hostess.  The problem is that tonight the hostesses were seating diamond and VIP players card members first before seating ANY of the regular paying customers.  I spoke with a manager named Stefani (sp?) and she told me that the hostesses were to seat people at a 3 VIP to 1 regular customer ratio when there were two lines.  This definitely didn't happen tonight as we waited for the entire VIP line of perhaps 50 or so people (about 12 - 15 different groups) to be seated before us which took about 25 minutes.  After paying a little over $160 for a group of 4, it's a little upsetting to see that you're treated like a nobody while others in the "Diamond / VIP line" get to skip ahead of us "regular" folks.  The manager I spoke to said she'd speak to the hostesses about it but the proof will be when we come back.  I drive a cab here in town so I'll ask my customers about their experiences at the buffet before I start recommending the place.

2.  The meat / carving station had a very friendly and very talkative chef / attendant serving to customers.  The problem was as he was talking to each and every one of the people coming thru, the line grew longer and longer for people waiting for prime rib, ribs, lamb chops, brisket, etc..  If the comments would have been short and sweet that would have been one thing but he was flirting with some women in the line as he served them so now what should take a matter of seconds turned into the guy talking with a random patron for 5 minutes while giving her a little of everything.  If there were two people working the station it would have gone so much faster.

*****

All said, the food at the buffet is above average for now.  It's a good buffet that could use a little tweaking in the way they handle customers.  This is Vegas after all and customer service is the only thing that will keep people coming back.

I guess all I really wanted tonight was a sincere apology and an effort to be made to fix the seating fiasco.  I feel I didn't get that and instead was brushed off.  The three other people in my party felt the same.  

Until they figure out what works and what doesn't I'm not gonna be the one recommending this buffet in my cab.  

**I'll update this review in the next week or so as I have friends who are coming in to town who want to go here.

My favorite buffet in Vegas.  Food was great, as was the service.  Some of the highlights:  large shrimp that didn't look like they were just thawed out as at other buffets; sweet potato tater tots; made to order street tacos...and the list goes on.  Friendly service as well from start to finish...  I like to go during the week for late breakfast (after 1030) when lines aren't so long.

Best buffet in Vegas!  By far this buffet in its own league.  It is krem de la krem!  Seriously, this place rocks!  We ate there for their weekend brunch.  It will take you some time just to see what you can eat.  This buffet seems like it never ends.  The best section from seafood, barbecue and Chinese, Plus of course endless champagne for their brunch.  Guaranteed, you will leave full and your taste buds in a happy place!

Bacchanal is hands down the best buffet experience in Vegas. Vegas eats on the strip can't be described as cheap, but here you get the bang for your buck with tons more cuisine choices, pleasing presentation and thoughtful prep compared to other buffets. While some $40+ buffets in the vicinity seem to reuse the same ingredient components over and over in their offerings, the Bacchanal menu gives lots of variety and flavors in each section that work together. A visit here is always a highlight of our Vegas trips!

Dinner: There was a line but I read previous reviews and was prepared for that.  To me it's a good sign if this many people want to eat here.  

Price:  It it fair for what you are getting.  I have been to cheaper and way more expensive buffets.  For the variety of food it is spot on.

Food:  I love buffets because of selection and not because of quality or the ability to stuff your face. With that said, it was way above my expectations. I hate a plate too many.  I mean KALBI is there!!!  Whoever put that on the menu, I want to give a high five!  

Service:  Everyone that worked there was super courteous.  So nice that I felt like I was in a commercial.  I felt very welcome.

There's no their defined "ticket rules" in any forms of instruction. So by the time we have waited for 30 minutes to get into the buffet. The lady in the front desk just said "oh , u need to press the machine for ticket and get into the line AGAIN" 
Maybe it's just the "Excellent service" they can provide.........

Buffets have to try very hard to get a 5 because there's so many opportunities to screw up the less popular items. Though I'd be leaning close to a 4.5 by the quality of food, this place gets deducted a star because their wait system is weird even if it doesn't actually take all that long.

When a wait starts forming, you walk up to their kiosk-thing and they tell you to come back at a certain time. Insultingly, this stupid machine also tells you that once you get back to the line a hostess will allow you to pay and will seat you in minutes. 

No dice.

The wait according to the kiosk was 20 minutes. Once your 20 minutes were up, you greet the hostess who will take your reservation and tell you to wait in another line. This line took 40 minutes.

So what's the point of the kiosk? In short, the kiosk wait-time is a wait to the back of the line. You can't just enter the back of the line without the kiosk slip; it's a queue for another queue. So why don't they just consolidate the queue into a single one and have the cashier greet you instead of some lady on a Dell laptop? IDK.

As for the actual food, there's not much to be said. The meats are all steakhouse quality, there are piles and piles of crab legs, there's raw oysters, and weird alien crustaceans,.

You can tell the aim isn't to please you with carbs because I saw zero pastas (but there is fried rice). There are some polentas and some risottos but this isn't a souplantation.

As is traditional with most buffets, go for the most expensive items, share or split the meals with carbs, and go to Los Angeles if you want Chinese food. Once you're 85% full, go wild with desert - crepe stations, gelatos, orange beer ice cream, a large pastry selection - you name it, they probably have it.

Once you've had enough meats and crab legs don't over stuff yourself; it's not hard to actually eat $55 worth of food. I ate probably $100 because I couldn't walk back.

TO MANAGEMENT:
It's tonkotsu ramen, not tonkatsu ramen. Tonkatsu is fried pork cutlet; tonkotsu is pork bone. Also it's a buffet so I guess re-using ingredients is fine, but Chinese char siu in ramen is weird :P

Can I get free comps for submitting this error? Thank you.

And here are some ideas I haven't seen executed in a buffet - Korean food options?

Worst buffet ever! Because of the service. Being that I am a vegas local I can pick any buffet at anytime and I would never come here again. We bought a Groupon for weekend brunch which had no specification on time on it said brunch available to 3pm and then we show up and the people working there are unable to honor it due to the time. Never coming here again, Cosmo buffet is way better. If you like getting ripped off and waisting two hours in line, then sure come here.
Overrated. Severely overpriced for the poor selection they offer. The M has $27.99 all you can eat and drink with the same quality food. It's a trap. Stay woke folks.

11:00am arrival 
11:15am sit down 

Holiday pricing for weekday brunch is $55 pp, though this price isn't actually advertised anywhere in the queue.

After this 1.5 hour affair, not gonna lie - I wasn't as impressed with this buffet as I've been during the previous years. Though it remains the go-to buffet with the widest selection, Baccanal seemed to have gotten complacent. I can honestly say that I ate my way thru the buffet and nothing stands out as "unforgettable" to me. Much less worth the $50 premium. But again, this may just be the nature of buffet-going. 

Nonetheless... 

Why you would come here: 
- You're really, really, really, really hungry. 
- You love a good selection of seafood, ethnic dishes, and desserts. 

Why you wouldn't come here: 
- you love snow crab legs. The line must've been 15 min alone, but the meat is Way. Too. Salty. 
- you love a good sushi selection at buffets.. they have about 4 types, none of which were particularly fresh. 
- You enjoy decent dim sum. The xiao long bao was soggy/ broken and the hargow very much subpar. 

Cheers?
Quality does not suffer based on quantity at Bacchanal.  If you're looking for a buffet in Las Vegas, this one deserves to be at the top of your list of considerations.

Two stars purely because the food was not good. I went on a Monday night around 8pm. Paid $60 for the buffet and was so, so disappointed. The meat at the American station was incredibly bland and dry. The lobster Mac and cheese had zero lobster in it and had a soupy texture. There were only three salad options--no salad bar. The charcuterie board had good cured meats but only two types of average tasting cheese. The Italian station had ONE pasta option and a bunch of sad, flat looking pizzas. Dessert wasn't much better--all the desserts I sampled looked better than they actually tasted. Honestly, the food was beyond mediocre. I know it's Las Vegas but for $60 a person there should have been something worthwhile to eat here. My suggestion is to save your hard earned money for something else because this place is just not worth it.

The choices for Brunch on this Holiday Weekend were enormous. The price was also enormous. $38.Per person for brunch is pushing it. I just don't get it.
Most of the food was good with the exception of the cold shrimp which were not edible. Several rooms offered different ethnic choices.
The staff needs to be more aware of the guests who stick there hands in the food without using serving utensils. They need to watch more carefully and remove items touched with dirty fingers by teenagers. That in itself is a real turn off.
All in all, this was an experience not worth repeating for the price.

Not impressed at all, the food was Meh and the price was way over stated. We ordered a pitcher of mojitos and had to ask 2x before we got it. We came here because so many people raved about. It was barely better than a Golden Coral. Save your money and go somewhere else.

Pros: lot's of choices
Cons: price

I have to agree with a lot of other reviewers here on the quality/price vs other Vegas buffets. It's way overpriced. The food selection was pretty awesome and the quality was good, but not enough to make it worth the $. Out of the 3 I've been to so far, The Wynn is the top on my list so far. Went at 4 in the afternoon, and walked right in.

(4.5 stars) The buffet at Caesars Palace is pretty much a Vegas institution. I'd say it's easily the best on the strip although the $60 price tag we each paid, which didn't include alcohol, during the holidays was a bit excessive. Yet the place was packed and we waited 3 hours to get a table. 

The buffet had so many memorable highlights, especially from the grill. To name a few, the lamb chops, prime rib, brisket, shrimp and grits, made-to-order steak tacos, meatballs, lobster ravioli, sushi, steamed crab legs, and most of all, venison with a port wine jam, were awesome. The only part that was underwhelming was the cold seafood which was icy, salty, and somewhat hard to eat. 

Then, there was the dessert bar, which was beautifully decorated with a few dozen unique and tasty sweets. Make sure to save (plenty of) room for dessert because it's a treat. From the rice pudding and cheesecake to the flan and chocolate lave cake, they were superb. 

I definitely overate but it was well worth it.

The Bacchanal is the buffet at Caesars Palace. It is one of the higher end buffets on the strip and I put it in the same category as the buffets at the Wynn, Bellagio, and Aria.  It is not cheap and runs in the $50 something range per person but it is pretty good.

When you first walk in you will notice the seafood section.  This is the highlight of this buffet.  We came at the end of brunch so we were able to see both brunch and dinner.  For the brunch seafood selection, they had a few varieties of crab legs and claws.  They had smoked oysters which were full of flavor.  They had a creamy mussels dish that was also great.  They had a variety of other lesser options that I didn't mess with.  For the dinner seafood selection, they brought out the pacific oysters.  These oysters were huge but not my favorite flavor wise.  They also brought out a mixed selection of snow and Alaskan king crab on a shared bed of ice.  These were alright but kind of bland.  They had oyster shooters, which were of the non-alcohol variety and consisted of a raw oyster in a shot of thick bloody mary mix.  I tried one but it was not my favorite.  The oyster shooter should be done with vodka and splash of Tabasco only.  They also had sea snails.  I was in the adventurous mood, so I had a few.  Not bad, similar to a big chewy bite of clam meat.  Seafood station gets a 5 out of 5.

The next highlighted area of this buffet would be their meat/carving station setup.  A various selection of large chunks of meats and sausages where you ask for said meat and they slice you off a piece.  This selection did not change between brunch and dinner.  I was not too impressed.  They had tri-tip, prime rib, "American waygu beef".  I asked for the rarest cut of the selection and the carver recommended the tri-tip.  It was alright, a little tough but OK.  Not too far from the carving station they had a bone marrow dish, which consisted of a half section of bone, filled with marrow and topped with some shredded beef.  Never tried the whole marrow slurping thing but gave it a try and it was alright.  The marrow was like a tender piece of fat with a very delicate consistency.  They also had a lamb dish I tried but the meat was tough. Overall, I would give the carving station/meat area a 3 out of 5.

The third area, hidden in the back corner of the buffet, is the sushi/dim sum area.  The sushi was very average.  The dim sum also likewise.  For dim sum, I went with the shiu mai (the shrimp dumplings in the translucent wrapper).  Typically, this is one of my favorites, but these were very bland and blanched.  Seafood/dim sum sections gets a 3 out of 5.

There were many other sections; Mexican, salad bar, and most of the other sections you'd expect to find a buffet.  I didn't partake into these areas so I couldn't tell you too much.  Nothing really caught my eye there.

To wrap up the meal, we went for dessert and the Bacchanal dessert section was impressive.  A large variety of self serving sized portions of most of anything I could think of.  They had carrot cake, flan, creme brulee, a gelato station and countless other options.  High quality stuff. 
 This section was done very well.  Dessert section gets a 5 for 5.

If you want to spend a little bit of change, the Bacchanal makes for a fulfilling lunch or dinner.

My wife & I recently visited Las Vegas for the first time. Bacchanal Buffet was one of the restaurants we had on our list. The great reviews of this place did not disappoint, the food was amazing. What you pay to get in is well worth it if you are really hungry & ready to feast I def recommend you pay them a visit. They have a large variety of seafood. ( Shrimp, Crab, Oysters, clams+) You will love their prime rib & wagyu steak. The pictures others have posted are spot on. When I visit Vegas again I will def stop byBacchanal Buffet. If you are reading this review & debating if to go or not open up your Uber or Lyft app & head on over. Enjoy!

FALSE Advertisement. SoO Disappointed. NO Stone Crabs. My friends came all the way from New York & we came here to eat because of the Stone Crabs. When we called to make sure they're serving it they said YES. When we got there after an 1 or so of waiting on line. The host seating us said to ask for the Stone Crabs it's in the back. She also said we can customize what we wanted to eat if they have the ingredients to make it. 

Got in, didn't see the Stone Crabs on display & asked the chefs from behind they said NO they don't have. Asked do you not have it for today only? He said they don't serve it. ?? Confused and upset now. When I called & asked, everyone said they have it & serve it. Asked the chef he said NO & there was none on the buffet line. SIGH

Went to the sushi area asked the sushi chef if he can make me a salmon, tuna, avocado with crab meat roll. He said NO. whatever is on the buffet line display. I told him thought you guys can customize stuff if you have the ingredients. He just said NO again and went back making whatever he was making. Annoyed & upset again.

While waiting on line saw these dessert on the screen display and when I got to the dessert area most the stuff on the screen display outside was not there. FALSE Advertisement. HUGE LET DOWN. Also they say there is over 500+ items there was not that many unless your counting all the damn hot sauces & toppings. sigh.

Also they ran out of crème brûlée, waited a very long time, walked in circles too see when there going to get more & finally saw they had a cart there just sitting there. I told the dessert chef that it's behind her & can she just make it now cuz I only wanted one. I was waiting for about 10 mins for it. She said NO it not there yet, they're bring up from the restaurant. I pointed to the cart & she said it's the other side's cart & not her area. BULL Sh%t. Cause 5 mins later she walked over to get the crème brûlée tray at the same cart I was telling her. Made me even more annoyed.

The line to get in was long like always & inside was only about half full. Our waiter was on top of his game but when he went on break. The waitress was kind of slow. It took us about 15 mins to find her & asked to refill our drinks. But she apologized because 1 of the kitchen was a hot mess & she needed to go to a much further one. When our regular waiter came back our glasses was always full. Then bus boys came out & started to get the dishes off our table.

The Food Overall was OK nothing that I will remember & crave for it.  But the oysters are small which I like but I didn't like the fact that they didn't clean it so good. A lot of them had sand/ dirt in them. I was scared that I can chip a tooth or something.

Desserts should always be the best part but it wasn't.

This buffet at Caesar's Palace is a long wait, but if you have the appetite, it is well worth it.
Brunch is $50 and goes until 3pm. When you sit down you have two hours to eat as much as you want. There is a variety of food stations, seafood, meat, Italian/charcuterie, Mexican, Asian, and dessert.
