There is a lot of food to eat, so take your time and get small amounts. Most food is pretty good, with a few stars hidden throughout.
Some of my favorites were the white fish ceviche in coconut, truffle gnocchi, steak (prime rib), and the creme brûlée.
The red bean buns were also a delight, but more filling than desired to optimize buffet cost to food ratio.
I would absolutely go again! It serve as most of what I ate for a day, with a couple of small snacks otherwise.

Came here for lunch on a Monday and WOW. The selections they have are a lot better than dinner at other buffets. It's a little overpriced, $35, but the food they have makes up for it. If you've ever been to Wicked Spoon, it's a lot like that. I'd definitely come back again for lunch or try the dinner. Definitely one of my new favorite Vegas buffets!

Not what I expected. Food area needed a wipe down . The oysters were frozen. Three selections for sushi and a few skimpy rolls. The cheesecake was good. The crap legs cut take to long to dig out. The Escargot was good. Overall If I had a choice I would choose Bellagio.

Definitely the best on the strip. A hefty price but for quality food that is well presented and with very good service. The selection of food was amazing and the non-standards were surprising highlights. We expected (and got) a great selection of seafood with a raw bar loaded with crab, oysters, jumbo shrimp (already peeled) and mussels but the ceviche, spicy crawfish and seafood gaspachio topped it off nicely. We expected lamb chops and prime rib but not the Mexican pozole, taco station and the chile verde which were all excellent. Pastas looked great but I really enjoyed the Peking duck, kalbi and  spicy fish and real chinese broccoli in the beef and broccoli was a treat. The kids enjoyed the dim sum, fried rice and the pizza. Don't forget to leave room for  the deserts: from creme brulee to mochi and a crepe station plus sorbets and cookies. Wow! Remember to pace yourself and try a little of everything as it is easy to overeat one thing and not be able to try it all.

They say variety is the spice of life and this place delivers.   Wonderful atmosphere however the music is a little loud for cross table conversation.  

The hot or cold crab legs are already split so you do not have to crack it yourself.  They also have a wonderful little drawn butter dispenser. Shrimp were large and wonderfully delicious.  Oysters on the half shell, mussels, all presented well.  Lamb chops that were cooked to perfection and wonderfully prepared.  Prime rib you can cut with a fork.  Excellently seasoned clam chowder.  Meatballs, pasta, cheeses, breads, pizzas, oriental, Japanese, sushi, there is literally something for everyone...   And I haven't even mentioned the dessert yet. Carrot Cake, flan, cheese cake, custom made crepes, Apple pie, ice creams, red velvet, tapioca, key lime pie, and more.   But this is not your typical buffet, some of these items are better then high end restaurants.   Everything was fresh, well stocked, and frequently tended to when little messes were made on the bar. 

It was a huge buffet and if you don't go around the corner you may miss a lot of stuff.   I think for lunch we spent $32.95 and the dinner is $15 more they told us.    We got in right before dinner time. 

I would highly recommend this place to anyone.

Love all the savory foods and all you can eat meats! Brought my parents here for the first time and they loved it! We will definitely return to this buffet. The ambiance made you feel comfortable and relaxed. Staff was friendly and always around to assist. Thank you for the amazing experience!

"Bacchanal" means "a feast worthy of the Gods" according to a plaque outside of the buffet!

Bacchanal Buffet is definitely the best buffet EVER!! This place was so huge that we didn't even realize that were was MORE food around the corner until we got up for our second round!

The line looked long, but surprisingly moved quick. We were seated in 23 minutes. We didn't bother with the kiosk thing. Once inside, I noticed there were actually plenty of empty tables. I found out that they can seat up to 600 guests!

Prior to arriving, my uncle wanted to make a reservation for our extremely large party. In order for us to reserve, they wanted to charge $89.99 per adult and $39.99 per child because they figured they'd have to reserve seats for at least 3 hours (1 hour before and 2 hours actually at our table). We ended up splitting up our group and it was $40 per adult and $20 per child for Friday lunch.

Seafood, carved meat, salad, sliders, mac and cheese, fries, sweet potato tots, various juices including horchata in cute little carafes, sushi, Chinese food, pastas, pizzas, tacos, and an amazing dessert station just to name a FEW! 

The dessert station was too good to be true. At other buffets, you get the choice of vanilla or chocolate frozen yogurt. At Bacchanal, you get the choice of various gelato flavors! AND they served mini cups of Thai tea with boba! Oh yea, there were made-to-order crepes! 

The sliders were served plain, but there are so many different cheeses you can add, plus onions, lettuce, etc at the salad station to customize it.

My aunt made a charcuterie plate with the cheeses, meats, figs and whatnot. 

My 10-year-old cousin loved it so much that he asked for my phone to take a picture of his food. He has never asked to do that!

I have absolutely no complaints of anything I ate. Everything had perfect flavor and the presentation was impressive, too. 

Drinks (non alcoholic) are included in the price, including coffee and tea.

The whole restaurant has a relaxing ambiance, with elegant decor and soft music playing. Towards the right of the restaurant by the windows is a table with red chairs and an awesome wine glass chandelier! 

The ONLY thing that was negative was when my aunt asked our server, a female named JD, for green tea. After my aunt received it, I decided that I wanted green tea as well. The next time we saw JD, my uncle asked if we can order a green tea and JD *RUDELY* snapped, "I already gave it to her!!!" My uncle told her it was for me.. duh. Other than JD's quick outburst, we received exceptionally kind service from the gentleman clearing our table and EVERYONE serving food/dessert. 

In my opinion, the price is entirely worth it.
RIDICULOUSLY GOOD!! Everything there is off the charts good. Even foods that I normally don't like I tried and enjoyed. Definitely a place to stop by and try. The wait is a little long, but Worth it.

Awesome buffet! Only reason for 4 stars instead of 5 is they try to up sell you into a faster line for $20/person. They said regular line to get in was 90 minutes, VIP/whatever was an extra $20 each. We said no thanks and they texted us about 6 minutes later to say it was our turn. Food and service are great and there is lots of selection, definitely worth the money.

4-4.5 stars. 

I'm writing this revew on behalf of my family. Haha. We go to Vegas pretty much every  Christmas break (excluding last year). This year, we had three straight buffet meals: dinner at Bacchanal Buffet, breakfast/brunch at MGM buffet (we were staying at MGM so we got meal credit), and dinner at The Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan (amazing!!!) 

This buffet, which re-opened in September, copies the original concept from The Wicked Spoon in which there are individual, warmed plates of food that you grab. The location is vast, fitting 600 seats and the decor modern and sleek. 

The seafood here was really good. The oysters were so fresh (from Virginia). My mom and I rarely eat oysters at buffets because of being wary of food-born illness, etc. (or oysters, period, considering how expensive they are) but we thoroughly enjoyed slurping on them here. Yum. There were also snow crabs and king crabs. You could also get them hot or cold, which were nice options, although the line system and organization for them was a bit awkward.

The other food was forgettable to me, but solid. I had to look back at my photos just now to remember what I had that was notably good. There was nothing in particular, which might be expected at a buffet. But, I do remember more of my Wicked Spoon meal even if it was later.

The desserts were a feast for the eyes, but by the time I got to them, my stomach felt so heavy -- I had been deprived for too long as a NYC grad student. Hah. I did still try some small bites from several desserts though, and I think I did end up being underwhelmed with the tastes. The mochi ice cream is from Mikawaya, which is good, but I somehow didn't imagine their green tea to be so floral and "western tea" tasting...unless the green tea flavor in particular wasn't from Mikawaya? There were two creme brulee options -- the standard vanilla creme and a chocolate one! Both were delicious with good texture and consistency in creme and glazed sugar -- not soggy or mushy, etc.

The price at ~$45 for a weekday dinner (versus $50 for Friday - Sunday) is expensive, but seems to be a common price for Vegas buffets these days. I'm not sure if it deserves its "#1 Vegas buffet" from USA Today, but I'm open to going back to the buffet for its setting and various, solid options.

This is the fanciest buffet I have been to. 
LOVE every single food they serve.
Every time I go here there is always wait, atleast an a hour wait. Yup!! 1hr wait, that is how good there food in here. A lot of people always go here and willing to waiting, just to have good and worth it buffet.  
I have tried there brunch and dinner there is not much difference. As always for dinner they have more options. 
For brunch they serve juice in a glass bottle and i think that is very cute. Variety  flavor: mango, orange, and strawberry. Not sure if you can take home the bottle but i took home mine. 
I am surprise out of all buffet I have been this is the only place they serve tacos and rice porridge. They serve your tacos warm, just tell them what kind of meat you want. 
Definitely i would come here when I visit Vegas and made sure I have empty stomach before going here. 
Service is good they always check up on you, very alert. 
FYI its inside the Caesars Palace parking is not free.

This Buffet on a Saturday night is $60 per person and need to wait for over an hour That makes the expectation high.  The food quality is good and for some reasons I feel its lag of exciting dishes.  (Although they clam it has over 300 dinner items.) 

I like the beef  wellington most. 
They also have bone-in rib eye steak, however, because they are so busy, the steak is over cooked and not paying attention to details.  The same go to most of the dishes, they just lack of attention.

The desert is very good but you don't pay $60 for just desert.  
Will go back to The Buffet at Bellagio instead.

We heard that this as the best buffet to visit in Vegas but honestly it was ok. There were a ton of people there and so many options on the buffet but it wasn't great. The noodles for pasta were dried out, salads were not great and you just felt rushed. The wait staff was ok but not happy at all. The meat and seafood section was huge but not tasty.
Everything is delicious! I have a serious sweet tooth and I love their desserts! Also be sure to eat the corn on the cob- it's da bomb.

I stayed at Caesars Palace and decided to try their buffet dinner based on the Yelp Review. Unfortunately, I do not agree with the majority. First, it is over-priced. For what I believe is a price on the higher end of the average cost of a Vegas buffet, I would expect more quality. I prefer quality over quantity.

Crab legs - the shells were cut in half making it easier to eat, but the exposed crab became dried out and lost it's flavor.

Sushi - also dried out from being out too long. 

Shrimp - I've had better for $3.

Oysters - flavorless.

And to top it off, I got diarrhea that night after dinner. I can't blame that on lunch since I didn't eat lunch, and breakfast was too long ago to cause it.

Up to this point, i've visited almost every major Vegas buffet, and if I had to choose my top 2 Bacchanal would be up in there. This is what I call a TRUELY AMAZING buffet for a variety of reasons:

The Food - The flavors are fantastic for every dish that is presented. They are given an unusual amount of care for even a vegas buffet, giving focus on depth of flavor and presentation. The variety is what you would expect from a super buffet, with one very surprising and very appreciated exception: It is a rotating/evolving buffet. 

What does that mean?

Traditionally, dishes for breakfast/lunch/dinner are set during the time period. At Bacchanal, they bring in new dishes every 30 or 45 minutes in certain areas of the buffet to mix it up a bit. It's a very refreshing take and makes for a fun experience.

The knock: Service. It's a bit lacking and it took me a long time to get my drinks, as well as refill them. I would have liked them to be more attentive.

Overall, really good buffet and worth the price of admission.
Best buffet in the strip. They aren't your standard grab a plate and slop type of facility. They plate individual items for you.

Somewhere between 3-4 stars. Food, yep, great selection. The oyster bar alone is worth is. It is super expensive and yes, you have to wait 2 hours. Just go put your name in and get the ticket, which tells you what time to come back. Once you go back, you could end up waiting to be seated. We went early--pulled a ticket on Sat night at 4. Came back at 5:45 and got seated at 6. Service is not great, but I have never been to a buffet with good service. It's worth trying it once. $55ish for dinner.

Very good. It was my first and only buffet experience in Vegas and it was worth the wait. Great for the seafood eaters in my party, the desert bar was amazing. Just wish they would have had more breakfast items for brunch. 
The staff was quick with taking plates away but took awhile for our beverages.

Was so excited to try this place, only to be met by mild disappointment and a lingering after thought of "is that all I'm getting for the steep price tag?"

Out of all the things I've tried, I'd have to say the chicken and waffles, boiled crab legs, and desserts station were most memorable. Every other dish I had made me question the decision to try this place out. Carved meats were all seriously over temp and super dry. I could have cooked any one of those proteins way better. 

The Chinese station had respectable dishes that were worthy of a buffett. The Italian station was good as well, but my mind was already made up after trying their meats. At this point I was just eating for value. 

I gotta say though, the desserts were good and the gelato and crepes are definitely worth trying. 

I don't think I will be back, unless somehow they figure out how to properly cook meat.

There is really no reason to go to any other buffet in your lifetime. 

It was about 35 bucks during the week for lunch I believe. 

The selection is just unbelievable. And everything is top notch. 

Sashimi was amazingly seasoned, I think I ate about $35 worth of sashimi alone so I was totally satisfied. The other seafood was fresh. 

Desserts! Went with 3 other girls we got probably 1 of each dessert and split them all so we wouldn't be wasteful. It was a giddy 30 mins just eating desserts. 

I would go there alone for the sushi or the dessert, or the amazing grill selection. But I got all 3 for an amazing price. 

It's sin city so you might as well be gluttonous :)
The best buffet I have ever had in my life. I feel I could come to LV just for this buffet (but this is the only buffet I tried in LV). The Bacchanal buffet makes the trip to LV memorable for me.

不用来吃了 一点也不好吃 食材不新鲜 还要至少拍一个小时队

not good enough to have you wait for 1+ hour. Not worth it at all. Save ur money for a nicer dinner somewhere else. Everything is so overcooked, the lobster, shrimp, beef, frog legs.

I've been here twice. Wait time's over an hour, the price is steep, the selection is good. I do feel that it's a bit hyped. People like to have something to be crazy about. Both times, I mostly just ate the har gao. I tried all the other stuff, can't say I was blown away. For the price point, selection, long wait time, service & food quality, Bacchanal was good. Wicked Spoon's better value.

I came here about two weeks after their September 12 2012 grand opening . In my opinion it is the best buffet in Las Vegas hands down !! They spent 17 million dollars on it . My advice is go on a Monday when it isn't so crazy busy. This makes the Rio Buffet look like a school cafeteria.  If you can do without king crabs legs, go for lunch instead of the $39 dinner. Can they keep up the quality ? Time will tell.
This is our champagne brunch standby.  Great food. Sometimes the wait is off-putting.

My friends and I (party of 5) came here for lunch around 4:00 pm. The restaurant wasn't busy at the time, yet their service was so slow. 

Our table ordered two lobsters and we had to continuously ask when the lobster would be done. About an hour later the lobsters arrived. We were so full by that time that we couldn't even finish one lobster. Let me remind you that the lobster was not part of the buffet, each lobster cost ~$60 on top of the ~$60 just to eat at the buffet. 

Our waiter took forever to come by our table to clean the table for us to have room for new plates. It took us 20 mins to hunt down a waiter, who wasn't even working on our table, to bring us drinks. If it wasn't for the juice bar we would probably be more irritated just trying to get our drinks refilled. 

Over all the selections in the buffet was nice but the slow service was a huge turn off. I was expecting better since this buffet is more pricey than the other ones in the area serving an identical selection of food.

I was a bit hesitant about eating at a buffet that refers to itself as "back-anal" until someone politely corrected my pronunciation.  I think that the name refers to the feasts honoring Bacchus (Roman, Dionysus - Greek) the God of the wine harvests.  These celebrations involved gorging, then purging, followed by another round of gorging, and finally a massive group orgy at the end.  Unfortunately, the group orgy is not available as an option at this buffet.

The Bacchanal does truly live up to its name, and is only what I could describe as an orgy of food.  If you want a variety of foods, this is the place to go to.  The meat station is probably the best in terms of different offerings - ribs, slab bacon, brisket, multitudes of sausages (ask for it by the inch). There is also a juice bar, that has fresh juices all individually set out in mini carafes. Don't get the green stuff, and watermelon juice is not as good as it sounds.

The buffet style is somewhere in between Wynn/Bellagio and the Wicked Spoon.  The quality of the food is pretty good for so many offerings.  

Is it worth the price?  Probably not, unless you are a massive glutton like me.  For around $50 per person you could probably get a better meal at any of the other Caesars establishments and get just as full.  But that is not the reason why we go to these buffets. I think of it as a form of entertainment for the eyes...like a strip club for my appetite, but here I can touch.  The dessert station is a bit weak compared to the level of the buffet, but I rarely make it to that point anyway.

Expect a massive line like you would see at Disneyland.  If you have Platinum, Diamond, or 7 Stars membership in Caesar's Total Rewards Club, then your wait is nil.

Oh Bacchanal - how do I love thee? Let me count the ways:

1) the sheer breadth of options always astounds me no matter how many times I go. From congee to bananas foster to made-to-order tacos to elk sliders, the diversity of options always pleases.

2) The friendly wait staff who are always on the ready to refill your bottomless mimosas, sangria and wine.

3) the quickness of the line no matter how close to lunch you go.

4) the quality of food relative to the huge amount you have to produce is an amazing feat.

5) yes there's a 2-hour limit but no one is pushing you out the door.

6) the many dessert options - from shaved ice to gelato to petit fours.

It's always an incredible experience and still my favorite buffet place on the strip.

The 2 1/2 hour wait was def not worth it. The only thing I thought that was cool was the fresh juices. I always love all u can eat seafood but I thought it was pretty standard compared to all the other high end buffets. I was looking forward to eating the macarons but that was just ok too.

Oct 2012
This is the hottest buffet in town for the moment.  They have up the buffet qualify bar.
Come early to avoid the crazy long line and come very hungry....
For me, it is impossible to try even a little bit of everything.
I will recommend to concentrate on the Crab Legs; excellent and protein.  All beef, lamb racks and sausages are all good.

Service:  The service level here is not your day to day server.  I can see that this group is the cream of the crop.  They are more like the manager level at other restaurant.  Very detail and attentive service.

Not sure where other reviewers have eaten, but this was VERY disappointing.  It cost my husband and me over $114 and was so not worth it!  

First, we entered our names into the portals to get a time assigned to us.  The time was 5:46, about 45 minutes from the time we checked in.  Three minutes later they texted us to say they were ready for us.  We were excited for the short wait, but once we checked in, we stood in line for over an hour waiting to pay.  If you are going to use a portal and give people times, don't then make them stand in long lines waiting to get in!!

We were seated in the back of the dining room, so we passed through most of the seating area.  There were MANY empty tables, so not sure why it took so long to get us in.  

The food was so-so at best.  While there is a large selection, very few things were that appealing.  My husband ate way more than I did, but even he said there was nothing that he would especially recommend.  I didn't have anything that was better than average.

Even the desserts were just alright.  I did have a custom made crepe and it was probably the best thing I had all night.  

The dining room was freezing cold (maybe they are trying to get people out quickly!), and the decor is very lackluster.  The area we were in had small square tables with a booth bench on one side and a chair on the other.  The table had four legs, one at each corner, so it was impossible to get in and out from the booth bench without moving the table out of the way.  This was not very well thought out.  Also, the people on either side of us were very close, so this is not a place to have private conversations.

Overall, this was a very typical buffet and nowhere near worth the ridiculous price that they charge especially for over an hour wait at 5 pm on a Thursday night!

Splurge for us as we brunched here for my wifes birthday. We also wanted to support the Strip and its businesses after the shooting.

Is it really worth $40 per person? If you have read my reviews you know I am price aware and hate being gouged.  My short answer YES it is.   Go very very hungry, this is no place to calorie count.  It is so big and the choices so much you could never try more than 10% of it.  Service was great.  My favorites:

1) The boiled shrimp
2) The bacon - oh my god good
3) Hash browns
4) Summer Corn
5) Jalapeno Mac and Cheese
6) The Creme Bulee

I could go on and on and on. Not really sure if I had breakfast , lunch and/or dinner   I think I am still full and we went yesterday

We went for brunch and there were lots of options for everyone: Asian, Italian, seafood, cuts of meat, lots of different sides and tons of desserts. They were even making pancakes and crepes to order. I had a Nutella crepe with banana topping...so yummy. They also have a bottomless mimosa option if you would drink more than 2.

This ain't no Golden Corral. This buffet is super fancy schmancy with over 500 menu items and not for the faint of heart.

Have a well thought out game plan before you try to attack this gianormous buffet. I'm not even talking in terms of maximizing your dollar, but enjoying the smorgasbord of cuisines. I personally liked the cured meats & cheese, kobe beef sliders, prime rib, some kind of tuna sashimi salad, and all the dessert offerings.

The Bacchanal receives my buffet stamp of approval and 3.5 stars based on its' high quality food and massive grandness.

This was the worst buffet I have ever been to. For an ungodly amount of money, I was woefully underwhelmed. The food was bland and tasteless, to say the least. Half the food I tried was luge warm at best. The staff was very nice and helpful, but that was about the only enjoyable part of the meal. Maybe if they put as much time into making their food have any sort of flavor as they do preparing how it looks on the line, it'd be more appetizing. Regardless, don't waste $60. Literally get a slice of cheap pizza or anything else. It'd taste just as good, and you'd save $55.

Great variety inside this place. They only reason I'm not giving a 5 is because the meat is almost rare, i like it well done. I had to avoid the whole meat section which sucked. There was so much other stuff to try though. Wish they would ask how you want your meat cooked that is all.

We arrived at about 6pm tonight.  I had a $50 food voucher for locals so I thought I would give this a try.  I was tempted to demand a refund but I kept thinking it had to get better.  

First course was crab legs and several seafood items.  I asked for steamed crab legs and I got to the table and they were still refrigerator cold.  Every item I got off the hot seafood bar was still slightly refrigerated as well.  

Next stop was the carving line.  I tried the sausage, brisket, prime rib and lamb chop.  Sausage was gross, brisket average, prime rib rubbery and bland and the lamb chop was average.

I tried Italian next.  Pizza was room temp but burnt on the bottom.  Pasta was room temp.  

Crepes were good and the man that did the carving was A+, as polite and helpful as could be.

My son ate mostly kid stuff.  He complained that fruit was warmish and everything else he had was room temp.  

I would have rather had Golden Corral.  I guess maybe we went on an off night but it was disgraceful.

There was a great selection and most of all the taste and quality was very good. I have been to almost all the buffets in Vegas and this one I highly recommend to try. I prefer it over the sterling brunch which I did not think was worth the money.
We went to dinner and we were expecting lots of seafood and a variety of sushi. Very disappointed and over priced. The salmon was over salted. We tried it and are never going back.

Don't waste your time waiting in line! Was sadly disappointed with this vegas buffet. Best dishes were the Asian section and desserts. No variety in the Mexican food section, bland crawfish, and where was the Indian food? Go to the Wynn buffet instead.
Average food. Lackluster in taste. Just like most buffet everything over salted. Dessert was below average. Nice decor though. By the way, got cold coffee.

This buffet has made my top five. Price wasn't as scary as some other venues in town, the wait time is painful, but worth it...food options are of plenty. I recommend visiting at 330 pm on a Monday; we nearly breezed right in. There were many desserts to choose from, Vietnamese coffee dessert was our favorite.

Our friend RAVED about this place, so my husband was determined to go. First, the wait... almost 2 hours to get sat. Once we were in, the lines for the food were not long at all which was very nice. They seem to have seating procedure and timing down very well so that they're only bringing in so many new seatings at a time.

The food: It was decent, but it was still a buffet. My favorite things were the seafood pasta and macaroni and cheese (which for me is even embarrassing because I'm a foodie...). I'm not a picky eater, but I want to enjoy everything I eat. Clams and mussels were in sauces that I wasn't a huge fan of, sushi wasnt worth finishing. The street tacos were very good and the carving station. Not a huge crab fan, so I can't speak to them (because I didn't try) but it was very popular.

Desserts: everything I tried from the dessert table was very good.

All you can drink: Beers are $7.50 each... we didn't know that getting in. Also there are only 2 choices Coors Light and some type of Ale). At first our server was amazing and super on top of getting us whatever we needed and then at about 45 minutes, there was a shift and we got a new server or the server transferred tables and getting a third beer (to at least break even) took over a half hour... we were ready to leave but being a server I wanted to see how long it took. I have never not tipped a server before... EVER. I couldn't find our original server to tip her, but the second one I think was switched over to push people out. A bit frustrating especially since I wasn't all that impressed with the food.

Annoyed because of long wait and "meh" food. For only 2 nights in Vegas would have much rather ate elsewhere.

I love buffets, you get to sample a little bit of everything instead of just getting one big meal.  Waited only 30 mins to get in, got in just before the dinner rush.  I really like the decor of the place and how everything is set up, real fancy.  On the pricey side but it the newest buffet and you pay for the quality.  I know for what you pay you could get a really nice meal, but what can I say I like buffets.  The Asian station was whatever but the meat and seafood is delicious.  Ate too much and didn't have too much room for desserts.  Will definetly be coming back for more because I like to go to buffets

Dude, anyone who says that the quality of the food at Bacchanal does not match the steep price of entrance is a VERY confused and disturbed child. The quality and creativity of the foods available at this buffet completely puts other casino buffets to shame. Because every dish is made in small batches and constantly replaced, the quality and freshness is never compromised for any guest. 

Their seafood station is an absolute dream for any true seafood lover. They have huge fresh oysters, incredible smoked trout, and a gazpacho with crab that's toe-curling good.

The gourmet and impressively fresh salad and vegetable selections won both my dining partner and I over. I highly suggest that you grab the chicken and waffles as well. I didn't eat the waffles as I only grabbed the dish because I was in the mood for fried chicken. The Bacchanal makes good fried chicken that didn't leave an oily residue on my finger tips at all! It was crisp, juicy, and everything I wanted out of fried chicken.

And as other reviewers have raved, the dessert station is something you just need to see and experience for yourself. Stupendous, top notch selection! They have green tea cookies, chocolate cookies, espresso tarts, mousses, cheese cakes, cupcakes, cake pops, everything! Usually when I go to buffets I'm not one to gorge myself and I usually just stop eating when I'm comfortably full (I know, I'm unusual..) but the Caesar's Palace made me want to leave a little bit overstuffed and I feel great about it.
Best buffet I had in Vegas so far. Amazing food! Pretty pricey as expected but its worth it!

I don't think this place is worth the $60 price tag.  Yes, there's a ton of food from various regions but it's just not that good!  I've had better food at $30 buffets.  I tried this place based off recommendations from friends and I'm a little disappointed.  Same yourself some time and money and skip the buffet.  There are better dining options in Vegas

Excellent food But very pricy. We went on a saturday which is supposed to be $57.99 and because Monday was Labor Day they charged us $70 and there was no sign to notify customers of the uncharge. Food was excellent quality. Waitress never came back to refill drinks, we had to find someone to refill our drinks over an hour later. If you are into quality buffet then this is your place. Expect a long wait in line.

The food was fresh, the selection was a bit narrow as far as buffets go. The flavors in my opinion were a bit muted. The seating was not great and a bit crowded. The dining area was immaculate and the service was great. Worth the price but not a wow for this diner.

Ate here three times on three different years. This place used to be pretty good. For some reason, this year the food quality is just average. There is no difference between this buffet than any other average buffet. Yes there are many variety of cuisine and dishes to choose from; however wow factor is no longer there . The line is quite long, about an hour wait. Just average.

Went here with my girlfriend and spent $114 for 2 of us to eat. When we went to be seated we were seated at a normal table about 6 inches away from another couple and we were probably in the worst seats in the whole place. The seats looked very nice but we were in a bad spot. Not to mention our waiter was very bad...he never came until the end as we had to stack the plates up ourselves and he came to fill our drinks twice out of about an hour and a half... only when we barely saw him and asked. The food was great and tasted great! Some food was cold though but I didn't mind too much. The cleaning lady wiping down the counters there was extremely rude to my girlfriend and I. She was wiping down the counters when my girlfriend and I were getting some food. She literally stood there staring at my girlfriend in here face with this very rude look until she made my girlfriend move and she wiped it down and she then stopped and stared at me until I had to move around her... that's just ridiculous! The people were eager and the only thing that was great was the food. Everything else wasn't so great lol...

Hand's down probably the best buffet we had while in vegas.  Can't give it 5 stars because of the price at 63 dollars for dinner.  (during the holidays) But you do get what you pay for.  

In terms of the holidays, as mentioned before it was 63 dollars a person.  Wait time was interested, the good part is you can get a ticket to check in, and come back during the time the ticket tells you to come.  The only interesting part was the wait was about 3 hours.  But for us, i believe we checked in around 6 to 630 and got a call to come back at around 830 to 9.  So overall for holidays our wait was 2 to 2.5 hours.  So your miles will vary on the wait times.  

Was the food worth 63 dollars?  I'd say yes, you get what you pay for.  I especially enjoyed the made to order tacos, prawns, and the baby back ribs.  There's too much food options to mention here, but i'll say there's a good chance you'll like something there.  

Overall, price was a bit high, but you do get what you pay for as the quality of the food was very good.  Would definitely come back next time we're in vegas.

Came here because we heard that they redid the whole buffet. We are HUGE vegas buffet fans and have almost tried them all. We wanted to do dinner here but it a little more than 50 bucks a person so we decided to do the brunch on Sunday. Which was still about 40 but included mimosas. We kinda were hesitant on the price but figured we had to try. And how happy were we that we did! They had full sides of beef cut to order. All kinds of meat. Everything from sliders to hummus. They had a lot of selections and all very good. The had crab legs and a seafood area. Only thing that was kind of a miss was the potato salad area. It was not as spectacular like everything else. 
Dessert area was also pretty good.  I'm a HUGE sweet fan so I went straight for the made to order creeps. They were good but felt they could have had more options on filling. Like bananas...hint hint. The cupcakes I have to admit we're kind of dry. But they did have a gelato bar with very interesting flavors. I got the watermelon mint and vanilla (I do love my vanilla). Overall we had a great experience and can't wait to return and try there full on dinner. :). We spent a total of a little over 2 hours here and wanted more but our stomachs said no more. We were happy we got our money's worth not just by the quantity of food but by the quality of the food.

Definitely best buffet in vegas ! So much variety of food and drink 
I recommend to go for dinner. You pay around $60 but when you go inside huge selection of different kind of food. 
Customer service was wonderful!! 
If you are in Vegas. You can not miss out on Bacchanal buffet 
It's inside Vaesars Oalace hotel. You won't miss the place.

If I had to wait 2 hours to get in, this would have been a 3 star review. We paid $15 per person for the express line to skip the line. However, the line to get seated took 30 minutes. But that is still better than waiting in that long line. I could imagine how annoying that would be for people who have already waited almost 2 hours to wait in another line to get seated. But I think the waiting in line helps build the hunger and anticipation. 

I didn't try a lot of the food because there were people in line everywhere. I started off with some seafood. I am usually not a big fan of king crab because it can get messy trying to eat it, but they split the legs in half to expose the meat. So all you have to do is expose the meat. The buffet is so big that I almost got lost getting food! There are many different stations including Japanese, Chinese, Mexican, Dessert, etc.

By the time I started on desserts, I was already too full. I didn't think any of the desserts were memorable and something that I would recommend. I tried the creme brûlée, molten chocolate, and crepe. They were all pretty good.

It was an good experience. This buffet is better than most buffets in Las Vegas. I just wish there weren't that many people and I had the appetite to sample more food.

This is by far the GREATEST buffet I have ever been too!!! I could sit here all night and talk about how great this place is...The quality of the food is on point, they have a deal of $15 for all you can drink--beer, wine, champagne! The service is outstanding, the buffet is well organized and stocked and best of all it's super clean!

This is one of my favorite buffets in Vegas. There is an impressive selection/variety of cuisines, way more than you can have enough stomach room for, unless you're Takeru Kobayashi ("The Tsunami.")

What to prepare beforehand? Starve yourself (JK). Make a reservation because the lines/wait time can be long. We went on a weekday dinner around 4PM, and it was about $55. Worth it.

There are many types of dishes to satisfy any permutation/combination of taste buds you and your friends might have. As Asians, we went for the "high-yield" items, such as:
-- snow and king crab legs
-- dungeness crabs
-- fresh oysters (shucked with the sauce still intact)
-- bone marrow
-- prime rib bone
-- lamb t-bone with chimichurri
-- mussels in fennel sauce
-- asian dishes (because, you know, asians..), like pork cheek, suckling pig, BBQ beef ribs, escargot in gilroy garlic soup, etc.
-- and many more.

After all that, it was time for desserts; and oh boy, they don't kid around when it comes to desserts. They have everything from dulce de leche flan, banana cream cake, key lime tart to creme brûlée and coconut mousse. Like I said, starve yourself before (disclaimer: I certainly don't condone bulimia nor anorexia nervosa behaviors.)

After you have gained ~15lb and lost ~50% of your self-esteem like I did, it might be time to leave. But I will definitely come back, in a week or so from the time of this writing actually.

Come hungry. Come ready. Have a plan! There's sooo much food to be had. I suggest you have an idea of which cuisine you're going to focus on, otherwise you'll be overwhelmed. The have everything you can dream of, taco station (made to order), Asian station, pasta, brunch staples (chicken+waffles...), and seafood. It's a perfect way to start your day and all items are fresh. The waitresses are not very present, which is perfectly fine, as you don't need much from them anyways. 

The dessert station, make sure you do not forget to pass by it! From crepes and ice cream to flan and sugar free items, this place is sure to please everyone!

The food is fantastic and everything one would expect it to be for this price-point (thus the second star in our rating). The process, however, is like gourmet dining at a McDonalds. This buffet is larger than Caesar's can manage. While the manager did quickly fix our many service complaints, it was clear that the system is so broken, the employees are not the problem here. Write this one off your list and blame the Vecorporate system that brought you 6-5 blackjack and triple zero roulette for its irrevocable downfall. We won't be returning again.

Update: After being kindly contacted by management to try the buffet again, we returned to see if our experience would be a better one. We are happy to report that it was. The service was far better than our first visit and the food was excellent as before. We are, therefore, upgrading our review from two stars to three. We still cannot give this experience four or five stars because we simply do not feel the buffet is worth the 2-3 hour wait or the excessive price required to cut the line. The buffet is already expensive enough as it is.  Ultimately, if you have a comp to skip the line; use it. We would rate this buffet four stars if the experience was walk-in. Otherwise, with so many excellent place to eat for this price point in Las Vegas, it's simply not worth the wait.
Food was overcooked, dry and salty. I was not impressed with the variety of food. I would not recommend this place because of the cost and quality of food

I wish I could give this place a higher review, but the truth is this buffet is only so-so. Sure, there is a large variety of things to try including sushi, crabs, assortment of egg dishes, different meat cuts, and even lots of flavors gelato and other desserts. However, given the price of this buffet, I expected much higher quality food. Given the timing of the buffet, which starts around 9 AM, I would not even try most of the heavy dishes such as pasta and pizza or much of the desserts. This buffet limits your dining duration to 2 hours or less, which is more than reasonable. Most of the items are tasty but really not outstanding. In fact, I think the only impressionable dish is the soft crab egg benedict. Again, for the price taste ratio, it comes lackluster. However, this buffet is extremely popular, so come early if you want to try it.

Amazing selection but expect a wait cause everyone wants to come here. 

If you're not familiar with how the line works, be amazed to be confused!  Line looks deceivingly short, but it's because you think you're getting in line just to find out those people in line already got called to stand in line.  You first have to go through the computers to get a return time to get in line... lol.  After the confusion of getting line you still can wait up to an hour, but hey, if you go here, you should know what you have to invest in time and $$$ to come here.  

They do not close between lunch and dinner, but they don't bring the dinner food out right away.  

All in all, a great selection of American, Seafood, Asian, Italian and great bite size deserts.  Not sure how to give a food review any justice cause there's just too much food to try and talk about, let's just say there has to be at least a couple things every should be able to enjoy here!

My husband and I ate here the day after our wedding. We couldn't decide together on where we wanted to go, but I really wanted to try this buffet after hearing a lot of great things about it. We came for lunch on Memorial Day Weekend nonetheless. The line was not that bad. I would say we waited about five to seven minutes to be seated. The decor in this place was typical to a Strip buffet: very sleek and modern. The price was a little up there. I even used my Total Rewards card, but I only got a discount of a couple of dollars. For a lunch buffet, I think we received a great value. There was a wide variety of food: wider than I expected. I liked that the food was served in small portions because then you can get a small taste of everything and get your money's worth. The presentation of the food was upscale. Everything I ate was delicious. The fresh-squeezed juice was my favorite. I've never seen a "juice bar" of sorts in any buffet that I have eaten at in Las Vegas. The only complaint I have is that the staff wasn't as attentive as I would have liked them to be, especially considering it wasn't very busy while we were there. I go through drinks fast and it seemed like forever for one of the staff to refill my drink. My husband was impressed though. I think we will come here again, but only on a special occasion.

Meh is how I'd describe the food. There wasn't one dish I tried that I thought "this is so good!"  That's pretty sad considering the price. Yes, it's set up beautifully, but is that what I'm paying for?  $120 for lunch is ridiculous for mediocre food. Out of everything I tried, the only things I enjoyed were the prawns, corn on the cob and a couple of things in the Asian section. That's literally it. I do have to say I have a big sweet tooth and even the dessert bar was disappointing.  I tried about 6 or 7 different things and literally took one bite of each one. There was nothing that made me want to finish it.  I definitely won't be dropping that kind of money there again when there are so many other better places to eat in Vegas!

This was my first meal of the day and everything tasted pretty great up until I got sick. I started with the cold sea food, worked my way to the hot foods, then barely made it to dessert because I guess the oysters weren't fresh enough and I swear I thought I would spend my entire EDC night in the porto potty. 

Cold sea food: 
-Crab claws were still a struggle to open even if there was a premade crack, so I only attempted to eat 1 and the effort was not worth the tiny morsel of meat in there
-oysters tasted ok but made me sick
-ceviche was kinda skimpy with the seafood
-the salmon and tuna nigiri tasted like it's been sitting out for too long
-miso seabass was really good 

Hot food:
-lamb was over seasoned and super salty at least when I had it
-the sausages weren't  spectacular because it tasted like any other sausage I can get from costco
-the pork was dry 
-king crab legs were pretty good and meaty
-pho broth was surprisingly delightful compared to all the weird pho at the other buffets
-the truffle in the tiny cute pot was very delicious I highly reccomended 

Desserts
-flan was super milky and creamy which was great
-best macarons out of all the other buffet macarons because it didn't taste overly artificial and still maintained the chewy texture
-I wanted to try the gelato but the oysters I ate earlier didn't settle too well with me

Since my cousin was coming to Vegas for the first time, we decided to go to a buffet. We heard that the Caesar's Palace buffet recently opened (in 2012) so we decided to go. It's been a while since I've been to Vegas, but it's pretty cool that they have the queue machines now so you don't have to wait in line for hours! The price was $51/person.

The thing I liked about this place was that there was a huge variety of cuisines/foods, and they're actually pretty good. However, the service killed it for me. Our waitress was horrible. However, I saw the other tables around us get a different waitress and she was super attentive. Because of this, I was a little annoyed. It took a while to get her attention to get utensils or drinks. We also ordered a pitcher of sangria, and it wasn't that good. It wasn't fruity enough or alcoholic enough. 

Afterwards, I went to the dessert section and it looked amazing, but didn't taste that amazing. It was good that it wasn't too sweet though. However, when they were boasting about how they have "souffle made to order" I was disappointed that they said they "ran out". When it was like 7PM. I don't think that they really ran out, rather that they didn't have it at all.

Overall, I thought the food was good, but I really don't think it's worth $51/person.

This has to be my favorite Vegas buffet! There was so much variety that you don't expect everything to taste as good as it does! And it was so hard to try everything that we actually ate there twice in one trip!

There are lots of seafood options, Italian, Asian, Mexican, etc. Freshly carved prime rib, brisket, gourmet sausages...Everything here is just upped a notch. For instance, fried chicken and fries? NO. Fried chicken and SWEET POTATO fries! Made to order udon, pho, and ramen...crab legs galore - chilled or freshly steamed in the Italian station.

And get this....CONGEE! WITH FRIED DONUTS! My hungover self has never been so happy. Bachannal, you've really thought of everything.

Their desserts are also to die for...macaroons, gelato, mochi, creme brulee, chocolate covered strawberries...anything and everything sweet your heart has ever desired.

$50/person and a crazy wait if you come after 5pm. Price is steep, but you get what you pay for!

This place is shockingly good. Wicked Spoon is awesome and this is better, hands down. All the ingredients taste fresh and premium, better than most of the restaurants  on the strip I presume. Expensive ($60) and can be a long wait (20min at off peak 4pm hour), but totally worth it. For sure the best buffet here, and I've tried them all.

Not such a great experience when I was here. Wait staff cleared plates while we were still eating and ignored us while bringing drinks to other guests. I found a black hair in my eggs benedict, an eggshell in another egg dish, AND a ton of grounds in my coffee. Disgusting!! I told management about these things and I was told sorry.... completely wasted over $125 going here for two people... If I ever go back the review may be altered to reflect a better or worse experience depending. So far I don't see a reason to go back.

Five stars for the environment. It makes me just want to sit there and chat with friend even if I am not eating anymore. 

Three stars for the food. Most of the food looked very appetizing, until you eat it.
I got five cold crab legs, three of them are way too salty that I couldn't eat them. 
BBQ rib needs a little bit more time
Fresh oyster did not taste too fresh and was a little sandy

Must try - the oxtail soup - five stars

Also, their Asian food were not bad either. They even had ramen!

For $50, I don't know if I should come back again...

Great place! Expect long waiting lines. good food. I just had a bad experience with the wait staff. The Asian lady that was waiting on us when we first sat down was amazing. Actually had a conversation with her about kids which was cool. When she left for the day we were left waiting for someone to take our plates and give us drink refills, nobody showed up for a good 45 minutes. Which was well beyond me. We were about to leave, but we opted to stay because we were waiting for someone to give us some water (water is very expensive at the hotel) so drinking some more to quench the las vegas heat was the goal. After about another 20 minutes I said fuck it and went to the wait staff's table and just grabbed a pitcher. The floor supervisor was giving us dirty looks because she saw the pitcher. What the heck am I supposed to do? Wait an hour just to get some water?

Otherwise the food was well seasoned, some were over seasoned. I probably would never go back. I would opt to go somewhere where it doesn't cost that much to eat semi good food.

we went there for the experience.
Large buffet.   People eat like pigs.  Really not worth the $54.00 unless you are a big eater. Mainly Asians eat there...and eat the night away.  You cannot imagine now much they eat.

Read the rave reviews and had to go.  The food was ok and only two hot items that rocked my boat were the chicken and waffles and the chorizo potatoes - best I ever had.  The rest of the food was old and crusty from sitting under the heating lamps.  The freshest piece of food was the watermelon and pineapple.  For this price, I expected much more.  Decor and ambiance is divine.  Excellent customer service and great dessert bar.
I enjoyed the variation of quality seafood and meat. I would recommend this place to anyone.

The wait was only 30 mins!!! woohoo! Tried this new beautifully decorated buffet after a long day and boy was it worth it! It was about $100 (with tip) for two people. It is a huge place with every food type you can imagine. I especially enjoyed the seafood section with the huge king crab legs, oysters, giant shrimps, and loved the lobster chowder! The carving stations was also great with a selection of ribeye, lamb chops,  and prime rib .You can tell they take care to ensure that each item is of quality. Now onto my favorite part, dessert! In my opinion, the desserts at wicked spoon at the cosmo were better, but don't get me wrong I still thought the ones here were good. Loved their creme brûlée and macarons. I would definitely come back to try a lot of the items that i couldn't fit in my belly this first time!  I probably wouldn't wait more than an hour but if I was here and the wait was reasonable Id stick around :)

I would agree this buffet is the best!!!! 40$/person for lunch and so much to eat. The sorbets at the dessert bar have really unique flavors, such as mango habanero! (My boyfriends fave) We lined up around 12:30-1 and the wait wasn't too long! I enjoyed my experience here :)

This place has decent food. This place is located inside of Caesar's Palace which is an impressive hotel but the food was a bit of a let down.  It was impressive to see such a wide variety of food but each individual dish was under average. The cold crab legs were over salted, the macarons had too much filling, the crepe stand only had  canned fruits as fillings and so much more. The Asian noodle soup station would also always be prepping the food I would want when I ordered it so in the end I didn't get any noodles expect the miso soup I shared with my brother.  I would not recommend coming again considering that they had under average food for such a high price.  

More reviews on the food:

The miso soup was salty

You couldn't taste the fish in the ceviche

The corn on the cob had too much pepper

I couldn't finish any of the desserts except the gelato, creme brûlée, and panna cotta.

In the seaweed salad there was slimy tuna, rice, and like 10 strand of seaweed

There wasn't a wide spread of sushi like other buffets
Food is amazing and endless. When I first walked in I thought it was pricey. Then I saw the food and the quality is unbeatable. Highly recommended

This IS the buffet to go to when in Vegas. Don't waste your time on other places because this place will give you quality food with abundance of choices.

That being said, this is the second year visiting this place. The first year was OUTSTANDING but this second year it was still up there but not the same. The quality is dropping a bit...

The mini burgers are my favorite. The salad bar is awesome....

I think my favorite thing this year was the chocolate filled peanut butter cookies. OMG!!! Don't tell anyone but I snuck an extra cookie with me.

My hunny can eat and we stayed here for almost 3 hours. He went straight for the cuts of meat while I took my time enjoying the different soups, variety of salads, different ethnic dishes and finally dessert.

I can't wait til next years visit to Vegas to see how the quality is after the third year!

I had high hopes with all the hype... That was my first mistake.  High expectations often puts you at risk for more disappointment than necessary... Ok enough of Ms. Obvious. The chicken n waffles photos I saw online before we went, we're NOT there anymore, at least not the same version when we went... Instead we got a waffle cone (yes, like an ice cream cone) with waffle fries and one tiny chicken wing.  The wing was synonymous to grocery deli status and the fries were like high school cafeteria.  The waffle cone itself tasted like a fortune cookie gone wrong.  

The dim sum was OK except the egg roll tasted like fried wrapper surrounding soft doughy wrapper inside... Albeit a few pieces of previously frozen veggies.  The wide Asian noodles tasted like they had sat out for a while... Ok, so we went around 8pm, but if they're going to lower the quality then they best lower the price.  Full price expects full service and quality.  Not even including tip, we paid roughly $60pp.  The noodles were worse than if Sizzler decided to make Asian noodles at 6am in preparation for dinner that night.

The dessert was just eh... Everything was attractive... Not Bellagio attractive, but appetizing looking enough... Flavor was NOT there either. How do you have molten chocolate cake with zero goo in the middle?  PS, the answer is, you don't.  The crepes were fine in themselves, except all the toppings were watered down and just made it gross.  How hard is it to make a decent Nutella banana crepe? My daughter made better ones when she was 10.

I could go on and on... Just coming out of Eat and Drink SF, I was looking forward to a sampling of gourmet bite size morsels and Bacchanal absolutely does not deliver.  That was my first meal on this particular trip to Vegas (we go about 4 times a year) so I have to now find another restaurant to take this bad taste out of my mouth...  :(
Crab legs hot and cold awesome! It was all good just like all the other nice buffets on the strip. Biggest problem was that things were too salty! Drink lots of water

We came around 4:00pm on a weekday (Thursday). Definitely worth the price we paid for the dinner.  At the time, there was a very small line (it gets busy once it hits 6:00pm), so we were seated right away.

Here are the highlights (in my opinion):

Wagyu slider - I recommend it! Wagyu (Japanese or not) is moderately expensive, and getting this was something I just had to get. It was pretty good, but some of them were a bit overcooked.

Fresh pineapples - I had a craving for pineapples and Bacchanal answered.  They had tons of fresh fruit, but I just stayed to sate my pineapple-craving. It was perfectly succulent, juicy, and delicious.

Crab legs - huge crab legs that are perfectly juicy. They only had the cold version (I heard some buffets have both hot and cold?) when I went here, but I was perfectly fine with that. They serve it plain, and have a small section at the end of the line where you can put whatever sauce you want to go with your crab legs. I just ate my plain.

Slow roasted prime rib - no buffet should go without a huge slab of prime rib on your plate. 

crepe - they have a crepe station for dessert. This was awesome, I had to visit this place twice.  Someone will make the crepe for you, piping hot, and put it on your plate. Then  in front of the crepe station, you can put whatever ingredients you want to make.  I usually put nutella (addicting stuff), whipped cream, and bananas.  Just do it, it's freakin' delicious.  Or if you want, there's strawberries, caramel, chocolate, etc.  OR! Go next door to the ice cream, get some ice cream, put it on your crepe and just go with that... either way, you can't go wrong!

watermelon mint sorbet - I think I have a new sorbet fave flavor. Goodbye raspberry, goodbye, strawberry... hello watermelon mint!  It's awesome - it's refreshing. 

peach iced green tea - new favorite beverage

brie - they had a station dedicated to cheese.  I just had a minor issue as to why the cheese station was nowhere near the bread station? I mean, they had some bread around the corner but nowhere near the actual bread station....It's weird, but whatever, they have brie. 

Ruth is probably one of the best waitress/servers I have ever encountered at a buffet or a sit-down restaurant, EVER!  If you ever meet her, you probably know why, if you haven't... well let me tell you. 

From the first moment we sat in, she was attentive and friendly, with a smile on her face.  She recommended the Peach iced green tea - and you should take her for her word on that non-alcoholic beverage, it's addicting if you love something not too sweet while having something refreshing. It's my new favorite drink!  She also came by frequently to do a light chat while making her rounds from table to table.  She would make a casual recommendation or would tell us her opinion on some of the food that she saw us getting.  

Overall, this place is one of my top favorite buffets of all time.

For $48 you get a brunch buffet.  You check in at the computer station and wait for the text message.  The wait today was supposedly one hour at noon but it was only a 20 minute wait for a group of 6.  What was worthy of filling up the tummy? Udon (add whatever you want that you can find ex. onions), prime rib, boiled crab legs, green tea brulee and bread pudding.  Don't get me wrong, everything was good quality! However, you enjoy the food more when you haven't wasted stomach space with other essentials.

My husband and I come to Vegas at least once a year. We heard so many great things about Bacchanal Buffet and this would be our 2nd time coming here. Our bill came out to $150 for the both of us (NOT WORTH IT). What even made things WORSE is the horrendous wait/line. We were in line for Brunch yesterday at around 2 pm and By the time we reached the Cashier it was almost 3:30 (brunch was over at 3)... So because Caesar's Palace  FAILS MISERABLY at having a better system in place for reservations and moving their buffet line... I give them 1 1/2 stars (there's no 1/2 star so I was forced to do 2) lol. 

Anyway's... Their food quality to me didn't justify the price. The Beef Ribs were tough as heck, even a caveman wouldn't have been able to eat it. Crab legs were really salty. My husband loved their Lamb chops so much he had 6 (he said that was the best thing about the buffet). Their dessert station was decent... The pistachio cupcakes was a hit and their crepe station not bad too. Don't be fooled by their pretty pictures.

Wow!  I decided to try them again two years later.....the same disappointing experience.  I have to smile sadly at those who think this is the BEST of Las Vegas...it clearly is NOT!!!!  If you have been to "all" Vegas buffets and still think this is the best, then fine....but I have been to better ones and have still not tried them all.  The first time no shrimp.  The second time crab legs that had hardly no crab meat in them.  I see other posts saying they have King crab legs...No they do not!  And caviar?  I never saw any.  I don't know what time of night these people are going.  I went both times during normal dinner hours.  I wasn't impressed and won't be returning.  The first time I brought relatives from NY.  The second time relatives from PA.  I'm done.  Moving on to the M, the Aria, The Wynn, etc.

we only found at Bacchanal buffet just three or four items better than Paris but the price was three times higher.    The server Mark  was very good and fetched some excellent green tea.  the bathroom design is horrible with two shower heads we are checking out today.  No blower dryer. Did not get replacements for stinky pillows as promised by the desk.  So     Next we go to Paris.

My wife and I spent a week at Caesar's Palace and eat at Bacchanal Buffet twice. First time was for breakfast then for dinner the following day. This was the best buffet I had ever been to hands down. Its a bit pricey but we were on vacation so why not.

Being vegetarian at a Vegas buffet isn't always the best. Bacchanal made it tolerable. Everything I tried was good, especially the pastas. But then again, there's lots of pastas & carbs.

The wait: barely any on a Saturday around 10.30am. It was starting to be nuts around 12.30. We stayed until they asked us to leave (2hr limit). 

Brunch- around $55 on that Sat. 

Service- no complaints. 

Here's pretty much what's available at the brunch-time buffet (I might have missed some things though) 
- vegetarian sushi roll: a few veggies, no avocado- average. 
- mashed potatoes: creamy and buttery, as expected. 
- Mac and cheese: equally creamy. Cheesy also. 
- Alfredo: sundries tomatoes & broccoli. Sauce was above average. Not gritty, smooth, great texture. 
- Pesto pasta: sun dried tomatoes & mushroom. There's a good bit of salt, maybe from the cheese in the sauce, but it was rich & worth a try. 
- Caprese salad in a cup: funnily enough, the tomatoes were good. Sweet, juicy, & almost crisp. 
- Fried tofu: this stuff was actually really good. Salted & crunchy, you can eat a bunch of them as a snack while hunting for more food. 
- Cross cut? Criss cross cut? Fries: too salty.
- Seaweed salad: standard. And salty as well.
- Scrambled eggs: pretty average.
- Fresh OJ: the best. The best!
- Fresh watermelon juice: not bad. 

They also have a miso soup. 
I wish I had info on the desserts, but I don't have that 2nd dessert stomach. Just a gigantic main meal one.

Best buffet I've been to in Vegas. Crazy variety of food options and the best arrangement and dining room. The dessert station is incredible. Price is not cheap but the quality and selection is second to none.

There are a few things that factor what makes a great buffet: high quality, high diversity, and decent cost. Let's see...

There are a couple things I would avoid, even though they seem great, like the pre-cut chilled crab legs and the meat carving station. I found the crab a bit flavorless, and the meat mealy.

But there are some gems here you definitely wouldn't find at other buffets. Great choices include the poke, truffle pizza, lamb osso buco, and roasted bone marrow. Of course, if you want crab legs, go with the fresh steamed version which are much superior, even if they're not pre-cut.

The desserts are delicious as well. A large variety of cookies, tarts, and ice cream, including ube ice cream! They also have Thai iced tea in the dessert area if you ask.

Yeah, the price is high, but you're in Vegas to splurge, not hold back. The large variety and mostly good quality are why this place has been the buffet to beat for so long.

If you ask me, and I know you're not, but I'm gonna tell ya anyway... Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas.  

Rarely would I say that a buffet in Vegas is worth the price of admission but this one is. With that being said, theres no need to go into their high "P2P" value.  They offer almost everything you could want and the quality definitely hits the mark.  I've been there for both dinner and breakfast and was not disappointed.  

Service is outstanding and Uber attentive.  Desert bar is huge and has a vast variety to satiate the most picky of pallets (like me.)

Get there early cause the line can be long but i assure you it's worth the wait.

Awesome buffet! So far my favorite in Vegas! Fresh and diverse quality good. Worst part is that it's pricey but that's normal being in Caesars palace on the strip! It's around $52 per person! Other than that, must go to! Starve all day before you head over there.

I am still here eating, it's been an hour and I am not leaving, also to make this story even better, I just saw there is another part to this buffet that I totally didn't know it was here, I am about 4 plates in, all fresh as I see them constantly bringing out the food, most of the time it's different but for sure it's fresh. I don't want to leave and so worth every penny. I didn't find it expensive at all. $40 a person for brunch. Take a look at my pics and you will see its worth it.

The Bacchanal buffet at Caesars Palace is the best buffet in Las Vegas. And it's really not even close. Make no mistake, this is an expensive buffet. However, it is well worth it as there is a tremendous selection of high-end foods. Standard fare is prepared extremely well, and a lot of more interesting and less traditional foods are also featured. It is a great place to try something new which could become a favorite. This is a can't miss if you are in Las Vegas. You'll pay a lot, but you will not be disappointed. This is a great place to eat on the day you are going home, as you will not need to eat again that day.

Went to this buffet last night for dinner, and ended up spending 2 hours there. There are 6 different kitchens running there: 
1. Seafood
2. American
3. Mexican 
4. Italian 
5. Asian (with both Chinese and Japanese offerings) 
6. Dessert

Every station had a lot of variety and made to order options. The dessert section had sugar free options, I grabbed one out of curiosity and it was actually quite good. The Prime Rib at the carving station was phenomenal. I don't think you can rate buffets the same way you write made to order restaurants, but I can honestly say that this is the best buffet that I have been too.

The Best buffet in Las Vegas hands down. My wife and I have tried all the big name buffets in Vegas like the Cosmopolitan, Wynn, Bellagio, Rio, etc, and we came to conclusion that Bachannal came on top. It is the most expensive but well worth the price. The selection is amazing and the taste is outstanding.  I could go in details describing every single food but I'll keep it to a minimum since I could go on forever. If you are in Vegas and have never eaten here, you have to at least try it once. In our case, there is no other place we would rather go if we're in Vegas again.

40 bucks for lunch 50 for dinner. Be prepared for a long line. Is it worth the high price and the wait? You bet your ass!! There are different stations for seafood Italian Mexican Chinese etc. Food quality is better than your average buffet. The dessert choices are awesome. Do yourself a favor and try this buffet if you are in Vegas. Just be ready to hit the swimming pools and gym because you will definitely gain some pounds!
my second review on this, and it is still 5 stars.  The quality is still very high, and plenty of options to choose from.  Keep it up Ceasar's,  you're doing a great job!!

By far the best buffet place in Vegas i have been to! It is on the more pricier side, but I think was definitely worth it if you eat alot! $15 unlimited mimosa was a plus!!!!! There was litterally everything for everyone, and the seafood variety was amazing!!!

If you plan to dine here, arrive 2 hours before you're hungry.  Their "check-in" system is a joke...  you check-in at a kiosk with a wait time of 45 minutes. You get a text that you're table is ready, check in with a hostess and are told it's another hour. Really?  Plenty of other options. Pass.

Um... AMAZING. MY FAVORITE BUFFET IN VEGAS!

Someone I was with had a "diamond" members pass, so we pretty much got to "cut" into the shorter line, and only wait 15 minutes to get seated. 

Im a small girl, and I like to get my moneys worth. I remember the first 5 times I have been here, I would try everything that looked good... and then I would get too full and was unsatisfied. After all the trials and errors, I have figured out a perfect set menu (for myself, my opinion) and have picked out only the "good" food in this large buffet. 

My recommendations aka Favorites here : 
1. go to the middle of the restaurant and there are giant pots, grab a plate and they give you  a large amount of hot freshly steamed crab legs that are cut in half so it is easy for you to eat. The butter is on the right side! Eat it while its still steaming! I eat like two whole plates first thing. 
2. The taco station! Made right in front of your face. (get like 3 -4 at a time. usually there is a bit of a line)
3. Freshly shuckkked oysters! This is the first thing in line of the buffet. They are sweet and amazing. I also eat a entire plate or two of these. 
4. I love the pho that they make you here. Also fresh and made to order. The soup is incredibly flavorful and rich.
5. Oreo Chocolate Moose Dessert! (I don't even like sweets but this, i can eat 5 of.) Then, Go to the crepe station and make a nutella crepe + strawberries and then go to the ice cream station and dump your ice cream on top of your warm crepe. (; 

Thats my set menu whenever I go to eat at bacchanal and in my opinion the best items there. 

OH! and in the mornings they have endless mimosas and endless bloody marys! YESSSS.

Not impressed at all!  Mostly lunch items at breakfast time. Most of the breakfast items were cold and not very well prepared. 

Bellagio's buffet is MUCH better!

I came here in 2011 and we had a discount for all buffets. This was one of the best buffets in the Las Vegas strip. We came back today and saw the price per person was $58 !!! That's outrageous.  So we gave up after having walked 5miles from mgm. But it is definitely worth spending money when you ome visit Las Vegas.

I got there at 6:30, so there wasn't a line to get in.  When we left around 8, the line was long. I would say it looked like people would have to wait an hour to get in.  Not sure if it was because we went early, but the oysters and sushi tasted like it was sitting there for a while.  So I don't recommend that.  The chicken and waffles is a must.  The meats look delicious, but tasted a bit dry and too dry for me.  The desserts look great and are showcased so.  The gelato is nothing to rave about but the crepes are good.  I think you can have dinner just trying one of each dessert!   Overall, for $55pp, it's not bad.  I think because we went early, the food didn't move as fast, so a lot was sitting around, but food should be consistent no matter when you go right?

The Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace is STILL the best buffet in Las Vegas.  And Alvaro Gomez is the best server at the buffet!  He's knowledgeable and considerate and takes the best care of his customers.

It was a nice environment to relax and have a brunch buffet! The set up is nice where the food is away from the dining area. There was sections in each part. One seafood, next is meats, then breakfast, then deli cuts, juices part then the sushi. Then in the other side is the dessert part! It had an gelato part, pastry part, and crepes. It was a very nice place to have a good eat. The service was nice.

If you can stomach the long wait the Bacchanal buffet is probably one of the best in Las Vegas!  They think their new ticketing system works well but to me and most other guests it's a complete clusterfuck!

While we were standing in line my friend E.L. made an interesting observation.... she said (and I paraphrase her..) in 3rd world countries people wait in line for clean water and vaccines that could save their lives,... in North America we wait in line to stuff our faces with food!!!  Wow EL. what a revelation!  I never expected you to have the depth to make a comment like that!!!  Haha!  

ok....  I could only stomach two average size plates.... 1 dinner plate and 1 dessert plate....  Maybe sitting there watching all these people gorging themselves took my appetite away...   I kind of remember this place being really good last time I came here...  this time not so much!  

I think it will be a while before I come back to the Bacchanal Buffet again!

First time visiting this buffet at lunch. The atmosphere was very soothing unlike other noisier buffets. The food was yummy. Unfortunately, there were no crab legs, steamed shrimp or lobster (as advertised on their website). However, our waitress was attentive, though she seemed a bit irritable and ready to leave. Some great food, and some mediocre food. Also, for some strange reason the food gets cold fast. So you Must hurry and eat. 

Top Foods:
Brisket
Short Ribs
clam Chowder
Crab claws.... If they were warm 
Gelato
Tacos

I love this buffet; the husband and I went twice just to cover the amount of food they serve. It's simply astronomical in terms of variety, quantity, and freshness.

We went for a Thursday morning-lunch meal, and also for Friday dinner. Make sure you walk around and strategize on what you are going to consume, because you will miss things if you don't, and end up going back again... or end up going back again because you love it.

Steak and eggs? Sure. Fresh smoked slab bacon, brisket, and ribs? Of course. Italian pasta dishes? Why not? Dim sum, sushi, sashimi salads? Bring it on. Stir fry, Mediterranean spreads, bread selection, sliders, sides, fried chicken, tamales, carne asada? king crab legs on dinner Fridays? YES PLEASE.

So there's no hours posted anywhere online on when they switch from breakfast to lunch and then dinner, so here they are:

Weekdays
11:00am lunch starts
3:00pm dinner starts

There's a humongous line you can beat if you go at odd hours... people have reported 1.5 hour wait times, we got in waiting a measly 40 minutes when we got there at 2:20pm, and about 20-25 mins when we got there at 10:40am.

Beats any other buffet on the strip, hands down.

I forgot the peking duck. And the lamb chops. Oh and the rib eye. And the pizza. Oh and the salad bar. Dessert too!!! cheesecake, brownie, and mousse lollipops, artfully crafted wedges of pecan and apple pie, cheesecake, choc chip cookies still hot in their own ramekins, chocolate creme brulee, and fresh crepes... cupcakes, chocolate covered strawberries, gelato section, AHH!!

No way can this buffet earn less than 5 star. My favorite place to eat when in Vegas, the option of food is awesome for a vegetarian. I like to hit this later morning into lunch so I have more options.  Make sure you check out Groupon to see if there is a deal, they do many times.  

Located in the back left of the casino when you walk into Cesar's palace, I t can be hard to find. There are several different stations of food. Dessert is in the middle all by itself, ranging from 15+different gelato, cookies, cakes and fresh desserts.  There is a seafood station with crab, shrimp etc etc. Mexican, American pub style food, carving station, Italian, Asian and a mix of Mediterranean.  The Asian station is my favorite with different ramen to make yourself and dim sum there are a ton of options. 

The only thing they need is to list out if the food is vegetarian, since this is Vegas and millions of people come here; I think it's a must. Put a "V" next to the food name, that would give this place 6 stars and save me the task of asking the chefs if it's veg friendly! Worth every dollar!

This place has anything and everything you could imagine on a buffet. Crab legs are already split saves a ton of time getting those into your belly. Breakfast is also stellar you can have traditional American piles of bacon and eggs or Italian style meatballs and frittatas or even seafood and sushi. They have unlimited mimosas and beer for a up-charge but dont forget to use you total rewards card to pay or earn points . If you come to Las Vegas don't miss this buffet its fit for a Emperor and Gladiators alike.

So, what's your opinion on buffets?  I grew up as an east coast boy, and my exposure comes with my family's outtings to Atlantic city during their "investments".  Me and my little sis will grab a $20 from my dad, then run out to the arcades on the boardwalk where I'll skeetball my way into a handful of plastic party favors (aka junk).  Inevitably this will buy my folks some free time on the tables.  Someone would inevitably build up enough credits with the casino to get everyone comped in for free.
