We'll come back from the arcade within a certain time and meet up at the buffet lines.  The buffets were fine for us in the sense that there are plenty of choices, but they were not exactly memorable, and there is usually a certain sense of gloominess at the table - like my dad being given the stinkeye by my mom for cleaning his clocks cleaned out in Blackjack, and now, well, there goes the grocery money.  I guess it's canned beans and spam for dinner for the next 2 weeks.

Well, deja fucking vu.  Thanks to those pointless outtings to Atlantic City I developed an immense distaste for gambling (but I love messing with the stock market), and as for the buffets, I still have a rather low opinion of them in general, considering them a manifestation of gilded mediocrity.  When I visit Vegas nowadays it's usually for work (trade show support), and I would rather be somewhere else (the Grand Canyon, or Lake Tahoe).  I am not here having much fun.  

Anyways, The Bacchanal buffet at Caesar's palace (oh, the irony of celebrating the life of a self-aggrandizing plunderer with dictatorial tendencies whose death caused the end of the Roman Republic) - was it worth almost $70/person (including tips, you cheapskates)?  In one short word?  No.  For most people here it means eating your body weight in oysters, snow crabs or shrimps in order to get your money's worth, and for some, it means comparing it to the seafood pricing at, say, CostCo and determining value from that.  Of course, this being Vegas, the house always have "vig" (advantage) over you - in this case, they are a casino with massive buying powers that would always beat your best attempts at pennypinching to a pulp.  For me, I look a bit beyond the value prop.  How was it as a restaurant, then?

First, the Asian offerings like noodles, dimsum and the rotisserie offering like char-siu...they were only so-so, like the takeouts at the local Cantonese seafood joint, and not really worth the carb load.  The sushi...were meh as well, the fish quality only being so-so, the same quality from your local Chinese "Japanese" joint, and not similar to a good Japanese place (I prefer the Omakase at Raku myself).  The Mexican offerings - were they good?  Eh, better than the gringo joints, but still not up to snuff compared to, say, Los Altos ranch market (the local Mexican supermarket with a built-in food court) in Phoenix.  The aquas frescas (jamaica and horchata) are okay.  The salads were forgettable, and as for the carving stations?  Eeeh, the roasts that I had looks great but lacks flavor - it's not salty enough, and the beef lacks a certain definition (not aged), similar to chewing meat bubble gum.  If you have been to Homestead/Strip House (NY), Ruth's Chris, or Lowry's Prime Rib, that's not the flavor you'll find here - think Ponderosa or Outback steakhouse.  Now, what about the seafood?  Eh, similar results to what you'll get if you microwave Costco snow crab legs at home with some rosemary, and then dipping it in clarified butter.  This isn't Joe's stone crab quality here, and as for the whelks, I had better poached in court bullion and served in aioli in Paris at some local brasserie. The desserts were surprisingly good (usually pre-made and mediocre at the past outings) - as far as the tarts and creme brulees are concerned.  

What's the verdict?  Well, if you want something good in Vegas, focus on one thing and splurge.  Want great Chinese?  Take a cab to Chinatown.  Want great Japanese?  Raku, also off-strip.  Great steak?  Lowry's or Ruth's Chris.  Seafood?  Look for a good boil or hit Joe's.  Want good value?  Stay off the strip and cab/drive to places outside.  As for this place?  It's passable, but just like everything Vegas, the house have the edge on you, and don't be surprised if you felt taken afterwards.

This is by far the best buffet in Vegas, hands down. 

The variety is amazing! There are food stations featuring cuisine from all over the world and, of course, the vegas standard: lots of seafood and dessert. 

The stations I remember: Mexican, Korean, Japanese, Chinese, Standard American, Southern American, Spanish, Vietnamese, Seafood, Dessert, etc.
Like, seriously, it was a LOT of food. 

ProTip: Go on a weekday, much cheaper!
Amazing buffet!! Has anything  you could ask for!! Very polite staff!! Definitely will return!

Defiantly one of the best tasting and most well rounded buffets on the strip. Wait was super long even though I went later at night (around 9) and it was a Monday. Even though it's a lot more expensive than many other buffets it's worth it if you're not in town for long.

simply Terrrrrible...
Probably the worst buffet ever. 

I'm writing this review for the poor crowd on the long line for this buffet. 
Wished I could shout at the loooooong line at the entrance when I walked out of the place "Never worth to wait for a couple of hours on line even if it was free." 

It was Christmas feast(Dec 24-25) and it showed special menus at the front. Lobster and so on.. And when I found the numbers of yelp reviews, this seemed the most popular in vegas. So I decided to have meal here for Christmas and waited for about 3 & 1/2 hours.

And... *sigh*..... it ended up I felt like I had collection of 1 star rated restaurants of all kinds of food in one place that is Bacchanal Buffet. 
So regretful......what an Expensive learning...
 
Lobster: First of all they didn't have the lobster in garlic & pepper as shown on the feast menu at the front. All they had was just lobsters boiled in hot water. And they smell/ taste weird when you really eat it in your mouth. Also there's long line again in this menu. But they give you only one piece per person so if you want more, you have to repeat waiting on lines for more lobsters..Well, no worth to repeat the waiting you will find out though... 
I almost came this buffet for this lobster but such a big disappointment. 
(PS. after writing this review, i found another yelper uploaded photo of AYCE whole lobster that I haven't seen or had at all. There were only boiled tails on 12/25 around 2pm.) 

Oyster and the Crab: looking like trash at the serving plates. And they taste no fresh at all like the look of them.  

Sushi collection: so limited kinds and very small amount on the serving plates. Only salmon and yellow tail sushi are the better menus in this section.   

Meat: tri tip, wagyu beef,etc: no flavor, no taste. Sausages are better options. 

Fried Chicken: one of the best menus in this buffet. Probably this and the mushroom soup are the only 2 menus I can say great. 

Lobster bisque: I didn't know lobster bisque could be bad until today. 

Cioppino: better than lobster bisque but I'm from bay area so it doesn't taste original to me. 

Mushroom soup: the best menu in this buffet. so funny that something really delicious from this $$$ buffet was mushroom soup only. 

Dessert: not many options on fruits. Cantaloupe, honeydew, pineapple that's all. And other sweet things..no delicious at all on all pies and cakes and whatevers.

Pizza and other italians: it's ok probably similar quality in Souplantation but less selections.
Chinese section: noodles: all soggy and been there so long. not tasty, dimsum: Do not make your belly fat with something not delicious at all
Mexican section: I lost my appetite so i didn't try the taco bar that they made by your order. It could be good.. 
Other small sampler dishes : probably better at costco samples 
If you come here for lobster, I recommend you to get a couple of packs (usually 6 tails in one pack) in costco and put them in the oven and crave. Much more delicious and enough amount. 

What a Crapsmas Buffet..

Just going to present facts - went to the "sign in" terminal to give phone # so I'd get a text when I could get in line. Declined the $25 per person charge to skip the wait because I saw, people who paid this still had to go wait in another line, but would just go in front of the general line. 2 1/2 hrs later went to check & was told to come back in 20 mins. 10 mins later, got the text so went to wait in line. 45 mins later, got to the register & paid $148 for 2 people. Waited another 15 mins to be seated. Waitress came by & took drink orders & we went to eat. Looked like quality items on the buffet but "hot" dishes were cold or luke warm. Crab cakes were dry & tasteless. Prawns dried out. Wagyu sliders were tasty. Other items had "off" tastes. Dessert flan didn't taste like custard, creme brulee was burnt. Crowded so didn't try anything else. The wait staff was very attentive & refilled drinks when needed.
Best Buffet I experienced in Vegas! You have to be open minded to trying new and gourmet foods very ethnic foods. Everything was cooked to perfection! It was very spendy but worth every Penny!

The updated buffet has a massive offering.  I have been to several buffets in Vegas and other casinos is this is the best so far.  The seafood station with pre-cracked crab legs was great.  Great selection of quality meats like lamb, ribs, fried chicken, etc.  The Asian station was good as well.  The vast offering doesn't negatively affect the quality.

Kinda disappointing!  Wag you beef was sort of like well done roast beef.  Didn't even eat the Alaskan crab legs because I wasn't interested.  Turkey was pretty good though.  Paella wasn't too flavorful.  Fruits and dessert pretty good.  Last time I was here was over 5 years ago - doesn't seem quite as good as b/4.

My husband always takes me here. This place never disappoints us. When the line is long.. My hubby and I love how they have an express lane. you can pay 25 additional each person to save an hour of our time. The Bill came out to be 200 for the both of us with tip and all. Worth every penny in my eyes

One of The only buffet with edible quality fresh oysters besides Wynn . I love the amount of variety at this buffet. Dinner is definitely wayyyy better than lunch I know lunch it's cheaper but I tried both and lunch is not even worth coming to . It has half of the stuff dinner has . I had the lunch buffet and did not care for it but when I returned for dinner I loved it!! Dinner had king and snow crab legs, oysters on the half shell, many types of seafood, everything from Mexican to Chinese and ooohhh the truffle gnocchi and truffle mushroom soup are to die for . Plus they have macarons!! It's still my favorite buffet for vegas as of to date ..(Jan 2017)

I've heard rave reviews about Bacchanal but I'm not entirely sure what all the hype is.  Granted, I was in Vegas on a super busy weekend (Labor Day) so prices were hiked up (to $65) and the wait was extraordinarily long (2 hours!).  One thing that was a nice touch was that they had people passing out free bottled water and popcorn (cinnamon sugar and white chocolate) while we waited.  We had a large group of 9 people and they said if we wanted to sit together, we'd have to wait ANOTHER hour so we said screw it and parted ways to sit at two separate tables.

The buffet ambiance itself its gorgeous and huge.  They have a decent enough variety like salad, cheeses, Asian, Mexican, seafood, and meats.  The waits weren't crazy long once we were inside and I made sure to get my share of meats and seafoods.  Notable favorites were: mac n cheese (SO creamy and cheesy that I wanted more but alas could not fill my stomach), cream of mushroom soup, oysters, ceviche.  I thought a lot of the meats were overly salty and couldn't eat too much, but they do offer a variety (from prime rib to brisket to ribs, oh my!).  They also have an entire dessert section in which I indulged on mochi ice cream (even Asian flavors like red bean and black sesame!), macarons, bread pudding, tiramisu, etc. Keep in mind that they do serve coffee or tea afterwards but espresso is an extra $5 (boo, since I'm already spending so much on food).

Everyone gorged on food, but then after we all left really uncomfortable and sick.  I'm not sure if it was the food we were eating or the amount of food, but that doesn't seem too normal (especially for the boys).  I think most of us didn't eat another real meal for at least 24 hours.  Overall, the food was fine but not necessarily worth the wait and the price.

Went to Bacchanal the day after going to the Wicked Spoon with my boyfriend. I thought the experience was just average and I don't think it lived up to the hype of it being apparently the #1 buffet in the US. Here's the lowdown:

FOOD:
Just Average Average Average!

Tried:
-brisket- pretty tender and cooked well, bbq sauce was just ok
-prime rib- ewww, I got a center cut and the carver cut me a really thick (about 1 inch) and big slice, It was mostly raw, I just nibbled on it and threw most of it away. My boyfriend loves rare steak and he couldn't even eat it. I felt embarrased for throwing out like almost a lb of prime rib. Slices need to be a lot thinner and portions not THAT HUGE. 
-scalloped potatoes- just average, I've had better, I thought the potatoes was a little undercooked
-salad bar- not impressive. Greek salad was good, but dissapointed they didn't have any more creative salad selections. A nice fruit or nut salad would be nice with some creative type of dressing. 
-burger slider- meat was cooked well, but bun was a little hard
-lasagna- subpar
-seabass- it was okay, I thought it needed more flavor
-sushi bar- tried the nigiri, the salmon and tuna seemed relatively fresh. Didn't have any of the other rolls because they were plain- california, spicy tuna roll etc. I was dissapointed they didn't have low sodium soy sauce. 
-sweet potato tater tots- seasoned well, above average, relatively crunchy
-tomato basil soup- typical cafe/restaurant quality soup
-mango chili lime sorbet and blood orange sorbet- pretty good
-mini tiramisu- subpar, the portions of ingredients are off and it didn't seem fresh
-mini strawberry lemon cupcake- not that good, icing didn't taste that great, I make better cupcakes at home
-juice bar- probably the best part, but obviously not worth the 32.99. I had the tropical juice and thought it was yummy and fresh but it could have been colder.

PRICE:
I think this buffet is overpriced especially for a weekday during 11-3. It was 32.99 for lunch on the weekday. It's almost 10 dollars more expensive than Wicked Spoon. For the quality of the food it's not worth the price. 

THE BOTTOM LINE:
Bacchanal has a better seafood selection, but I'm not into seafood anyways and it was just average anyways. I saw that a couple people raved about a CREPE station but it was not available when I went, so don't expect it to be available. I love crepes too. I feel cheated now.. My boyfriend and I will probably not be back to Bacchanal.

The night before - "Wear your tight dresses tonight because BUFFET TOMORROW!!"
The day of - "SO EXCITED FOR BUFFET!"
Four hours into it - "How are we going to fit into our dresses tonight...."

AMAZING. Seriously. Bacchanal Buffet is the best buffet I've ever had. 

If you go in during direct lunch/dinner hours, the wait can be gruesome. However, I'll let you in on some cooooool thangs!
Cool thing #1: They have a system where you can wait-list yourself and it will send you a text to let you know when you can be seated. You don't have to wait there! Go grab a Fat Tuesday and walk around (burn off some calories before you eat more heh). 
Cool thing #2: You can actually pay an extra $15 to get in right away, just ask the hostess to direct you to the "express line". 
Cool thing #3: If you go in during lunch hours, you can stay until dinner hour hits (at 3pm)! It's cheaper and you get the best of both worlds! This is the reason we stayed at the buffet for four hours...

They have a HUGE variety of food and there was not one thing I tried that I didn't like. Not only is their food good, but their dessert is also delicious!! Even though I was really full, I couldn't help loading up my plate with different desserts. I was actually quite impressed with their macarons, not too shabby for a place that doesn't specialize in macarons. 

If I haven't convinced you yet to try Bacchanal, I know the one thing that will!

BOTTOMLESS MIMOSAS.


(9/100 in 2014)

My personal highlights about Bacchanal:
- Amazing seafood options: crab legs (cold or boiled), jumbo shrimp, ceviche and my absolute favorite - UNLIMITED half shelled oysters!! My goal was to eat 50 to recoup my cost but alas, I set myself up for failure...I only had 20...but no stomachache so that's a winner in my book!
- The taco bar: NOT FOR TACOS! The best thing about the taco bar is that you can make your own FRESH NACHOS! None of the pre-made crappy nachos that has been under the heat lamp. Grab some chips, ask the chef for some freshly grilled meat (carne asada was my choice) and drizzle on toppings galore at their amazing condiments bar. Fresh guac and pico de gallo was allllllll over my tasty nachos. 

What I disliked about Bacchanal: 
- the price: $50+ for dinner, not including tax or tip (that puts you closer to $60+). There's a $15 price difference between lunch & dinner so definitely try to make the lunch-dinner transition if you can. I think dinner price starts around 3pm. Sucks that the price difference between weekday and weekend dinner is only a few bucks. 
- the extremely sad Japanese selection: ummm...pre-made sushi roll with mushy rice???? Not worth my stomach space. 

- Use your total rewards card for $1 off and you get points!
- No wait for Monday night dinner. We got there around 4pm and the place was pretty empty..no lines at any of the station. Around 6pm-ish, the lines started to form at the seafood area and the carving area.

Best buffet in Vegas!!! Why eat anywhere else when you can get everything you can think of here and its DELICIOUS!!! Incredible Chicken and waffles, mac and cheese, dim sum, meats of all kinds, amazing crepe bar, most delicious sausages and bacon ever and that's just on one end of the room!!!

I've been waiting for weeks to eat here. Even more than that, I've been waiting to mark my 5 stars and add Bacchanal to my list as the best buffet in Vegas. Unfortunately I didn't get to do any of those. There's not a lot I can say bad about this place. Overall, it was a good experience, but it wasn't the best there is. 

First of all, I parked in the garage and found it difficult to find once I was inside Caesars. There were no signs to the buffet until you're almost there. We asked four employees along the way. One person didn't have a clue. Once we got there, a long line awaited us. On a positive note, we only had to wait 25 minutes. We got there on a Monday at 10:00. I can't imagine what the wait is like on a weekend. The great thing about getting there after 10 is that they start changing the food line at 11. You get the end of breakfast and the beginning of lunch. Hmmm...I believe that is called brunch. Oh....there is a big price difference between breakfast and lunch. 

The facility is beautiful. It is large enough to walk between tables without disturbing others. Yelpers comment about how expensive it is, but I think it is well worth the money. The food was very good. I was stuffed when I left. For breakfast I had bacon (greasy and fatty), red velvet pancakes (just OK), sweet potato tots (scrumptious), biscuit (OK), scrambled eggs (runny), shrimp and grits (OK). I tasted my partner's french toast and it was very good. 

For lunch I had dim sum (all that I tried was very good), paella (good and an unusual dish for a buffet), BBQ spare ribs (smoky). I didn't bother waiting in line for the very small salad bar. I tasted my partner's very good fried chicken. There were a lot of food choices and the food was a little above average for a buffet. There were no signature dishes that would be unique to Bacchanal such as some of the dishes you will find at the Wicked Spoon. Actually, the way that the food was displayed and served makes you think that the designers spent a lot of time checking out the Wicked Spoon as they were designing this place. Unfortunately, they didn't bring over the chefs.

Lastly...the desserts. I only had the red velvet cake and carrot cake. They were both very good. I usually hate the nasty carrot cakes at buffets, but the bakery stepped up to the plate and hit a home run with the carrot cake. My friends had different desserts and said that they were all fabulous. The coffee was good. 

I don't like to do buffets because I tend to overeat. I can't imagine that I would ever go back to to this one unless I was with someone that insisted upon going there. I'd much rather go the the M or the Wicked Spoon.

Absolutely no taste to anything.
Went to this place because of all the reviews and was completely let down.
There is a huge variety of every dish you can imagine and all of them are between tasteless to just disgusting.
This is most definitely not the best Buffet in vegas or best anything anywhere.

Save not just your money, but your time! This was the cheesiest, messiest, tasteless place I've ever had the misfortune of visiting. Spending as much time as I do in this city I tend to avoid buffets all together for the obvious reasons (cold, tasteless, stale food) but there was so much talk about this place I thought I'd give it a try. 
If you come here and manage your expectations accordingly...

This is the best buffet to eat in Las Vegas for quality of food and taste.  The downside is the price per person and the long lines.  

We initially tried to eat at this place on Christmas Eve and was told we wait is many hours long. 

Finally, we made it inside on the day after Christmas.  The prices are definitely on the high side if you are value conscious but the food is top quality. There's a 2 hour limit inside per waitress. You get what you paid for food and quality. There are tons of seafood like crabs, snow crabs legs, ham, dessert and a whole lot more. During special occasions the place adds more special dishes.

NOT impressed. NOT worth the wait. NOT worth the price ($45)

After waiting for an hour and a half, we were very excited to try the food but ended up so disappointed :( 

1st trip around, everything tasted like it was left out for too long or over cooked. The chicken soup was good. 2nd trip around, everything was cold...but the lamb chop was good.

We got in at 8 pm, it's unacceptable that anything should be cold or taste like it's been left out for too long especially if it was busy... doesn't make any sense.

The desserts and service were decent; tonkatsu ramen was surprisingly good. I don't see myself coming back here anytime soon. Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan is better in my opinion.

We had Jeffrey as a waiter and he was beyond amazing. He was always checking in on us, making sure that we had everything we needed. He was a great conversationalist and also suggested the crepes at the dessert station which were DELICIOUS. The food was visually appealing and plated very nicely. I wish that I had eaten more because everything was amazing. Must go. Worth it.

I first heard about this from a friend when he showed me a pic of his wait ticket for 465 minutes on Christmas Day. With almost an 8-hour wait, it must be good, right?

YES, OMG YES.

First off, you'll need to understand that food at buffets are never going to as good as a restaurant where they serve you one dish at a time. If you have that expectation, crush it because that's unreasonable, honestly. Secondly, I'm a little biased towards buffets. I've gone to tons of buffets since I was a kid so I always have a soft spot for the whole experience of loading up plate after plate with ridiculous piles of food until I feel like dying.

So Bacchanal? Definitely some of the very best buffet food I've had thus far in my 26 years of life. There's a ton of variety so I had tons of fun trying a little bit of everything. There's the section of Chinese food (includes dim sum and BBQ items), Latin American food (roasted pork, ceviche, etc), Japanese food (sushi!), typical American fare (burgers, fries, etc), seafood (crab legs, of course!), Italian charcuterie and cheese, and a bunch more that I can't possibly remember. I honestly felt a little overwhelmed, but in a good way! There's so many choices, and the food is all pretty well cooked so there's something for everyone in your group (unless someone you bring hates food). Personally, I think the best part is getting to try a little bit of everything because why would you want to limit yourself to just 1 dish. Why not 5? 10? 20?! One of my favorites was the ceviche (there were 2 kinds! shrimp and fish). I went back a bunch for that because it's hard to deny 2 giant colorful bowls of fresh seafood sitting there waiting to be eaten atop some crispy tostadas. Sushi was good; no real commentary about that except that I ate a lot of it. The crab legs obviously are a huge hit here, and I thought they were well-prepared. There were two kinds that night--the plain boiled snow crab and the Dungeness crab prepared in a sauce. While I liked them, I couldn't eat too much because my stomach is unfortunately (or fortunately, depending on how you look at it) rather small and ran out of room. Also, if you're a sweets fan, leave A LOT of room for dessert because there's a whole giant bar dedicated to just desserts. You can get typical cakes, pastries, and pies, but also a pretty large selection of gelato and made-to-order crepes. Pretty siiiiick.

This buffet is definitely more pricey than most, but I found the value well worth it for the variety and quality of the food. I went for dinner when they were doing their holiday meal pricing, so it was $60-something + we got all-you-can-drink too ($15), so per person was probably about $90-95 (includes tip)? Our waiter was incredibly attentive and funny, so that definitely made for a great experience on top of the yummy food. Note on the AYCD--you can't switch around on the different drinks. You have 4 choices where you can switch back and forth between 2 drinks of their choice. Like for example, the wine choice was between red wine and white wine. If you pick that as your drink choice, you can't jump from say... wine to beer. Honestly, the drink deal is a great deal if you can stomach a lot of food AND liquid. Drinks were running $10-15 a piece at the bar, so having about 2 drinks at least lets you break even. When in Vegas, amirite?!

I've decided that the next time I'm going to Vegas, I will make another stop here. I have terrible gambling luck so if I have to spend a lot of money, might as well be on the buffet of my dreams

I gave this one star only because half is not an option...
I was here a year ago and recommended this buffet to all my friends....my how things have changed in a year.
We waited a half an hour for their new "speed seating" system to put us at the head of the line, then waited another hour to pay and be seated..
Once we were seated there were so many people that there were now lines for every area of the buffet, and the seafood area nearly 30 minutes! The crab legs are smaller, lines are longer, and the desserts are less plentiful and uncreative.
Street tacos were the highlight, but for $65 a person, I can go to chipotle and have comparable food with plenty of cash left in my wallet.
Very disappointed, we will stick with Wicked Spoon from now on... I recommend you all do the same!

My first thought about this place, naturally, was $70 for a Vegas buffet?  I wondered why, in a town of fantastic dining, from celebrity-run swanky Casino joints, to amazing ethnic strip-mall fare, I would pay so much to sit among the din and clatter of a buffet, shuffling along in line, plate in hand, craning to get a glimpse of the carving station over the shoulder of the slow-moving family in front of me.  I feared too many rejects, items that seemed promising but simply succumbed to the weight of time, and ended up soggy and heavy and bad.

But we had heard inklings that this place might be different, and when we tallied up our nearby options we realized outside the food court, any restaurant at Caesers would set us back $40-50 before tip, if not much more, so the price tag seems less onerous in comparison.  These are after all, Vegas dollars, which must be discounted like dog years, so that $70 here is really only $20 in "human dollars."

So in we plunged, plates in hand.

And from the very first bites, we knew that this was something different.  The duck? Crisp of skin and beyond succulent.  The baked scallops? Tiny plates of tuna ceviche? The mussels in coconut curry?  All perfect.  Beyond perfect actually.  As we kept sampling in amazement we realized every item we tried was an ideal representation of its form.  Green beans perfectly crisp and seasoned to perfection.  A crispy tiny wedge salad here; a perfect slice of fungi pizza with truffle oil there.

It seemed impossible.  How could pad thai for 500 people be not only delicious, but light and perfectly cooked, with none of the gloppiness that typically plagues pre-cooked noodles.  And then we started to notice that this was not industrially prepared food as in buffets of old.  Each station had its own crew of chef and cooks and expediters.  Each crew was assiduously tending their station so that food was all fresh and hot and perfectly rendered.

There may have been a miss or two -an overcooked whole pig did disappoint, and the steamed shrimp were simply that and nothing more.- for bite after bite, for nearly two hours, we were constantly exclaiming "try this!" and "Oh my god!!"  Luckily there were four of us, so we sampled even more than we would have.

And then the desserts!  Often the Achilles heel of a buffet, loaded with deceivingly pretty lumps of over sweetened lardy disappointments, here we could hardly resist, despite already being many plates into the experience.  Carmelly flan, perfect mini-creme brulees, a vast array of homemade gelatos.  I can hardly remember now the dizzyingly wide array of sweets that tempted us.  Jasmine rice pudding! Things I've never tried.

In the end, we realized that we had undoubtedly had more bites of never-tried, never-knew, never-tasted foods than at any meal we could recall.  We also realized sadly that the deliciousness had caused serious dining injury, and we would all be paying the price well into the next day.  A price however, that along with the one measured in dollars, we are very happy we paid.
Dinner on 10/25/2015.  Prime Rib was overdone and tough.  Much better last time I was here (2 years ago).  Rest of the buffet was just OK.

We arrived on 9/12 at about 4:45pm.  There was no line but I am sure there would be at a more normal time.  This buffet is over the top.  Where Wynn's, Bellagio stop this one goes to #11.  I am not exaggerating by much that the serving area is almost as big as the table area.  American, Mexican, Asian, Italian sections.  $45.00 for a buffet is a ton of money.  But let me make a case for the price to value.  If you want you eat all the crabs, shrimp, oysters, kyobi beef burger's you want.  If you don't want to eat seafood you can have lamb chops or prime rib carved to you specification.  Now I had two lamb chops and a slice of prime rib(not a huge slice just polite).  If I go to any high end steak house I have just spent $45 or more for either the lamb chops or the prime rib.  And these meats are high end quality.  Had a few shrimp, a couple of crab legs just to make sure I got my monies worth.  I did not have dessert but Mrs K said they where very good.  I am sure she did not get her $45.00 worth of food so there is the price problem.

This buffet is really a "must try", even with its crazy price tag and even crazier wait time (where you take, essentially, a "number in line" ticket with a return time plus additional hours of waiting in line).
The price is the highest I've come across at about $70/person (during holidays). 
The choices...oh my...where do I start! TONS of things to try and most are exquisitely pre-plated. I've tried every single item (not getting the samething twice and some only a single bite) and I was stuffed like a thanksgiving turkey.
The service was superb. Clearing plates and refills without us asking, whaaat?! But honestly, I wasn't expecting anything less.

Would I pay the hefty price and go through the agonizing wait? 

Hell freaking yes.

Bacchanal Buffet is like Disney World, and much like Disney World they should sell passes that are good for more that one day. I believe it would be impossible to try everything that your heart desires in one (or maybe even two) visits to this buffet. 
Buffet doesn't even seem like the right word to use to describe the smorgasbord  of perfectly crafted dishes.
The food is of fantastic quality and it seems as if everything is prepared with care. There wasn't a single item I chose that I didn't like. The salmon was perfectly cooked, the sushi was fresh and delightful the clam chowder and buttered dinner roll, amazing. We also had a basket of calamari, grilled asparagus, salmon croquets, delicious cheese board, fresh chips and salsa and the JUICES! fresh squeezed watermelon, orange, cucumber and carrot juice. I would go back for the juices alone. 
And as for the dessert bar, I don't even know what to say. The macarons, gelato ( blood orange and balsamic fig, heavenly) the key lime tart was delicious and I didn't even get to try half of the items I wanted before I was full to the brim. I also liked that I felt as if I was able to stick more closely to the healthier food that I eat on a daily basis even though I use a trip to the buffet as a "cheat meal".
I will definitely be returning to try out the Mediterranean and American sections. I would also like to check out breakfast as I'm sure that would be incredible as well.

If you like quality of the Wynn and Bellagio-type buffets, Bacchanal is in the same arena but dips into your wallet a bit deeper. The 4 of us for a Sat brunch came out to a little under $180 and that's WITH the player's cards. It's a weekend champagne brunch and that's where the additional costs come in when comparing it to Wynn and Bellagio but, there isn't even an option to opt out of the champagne if you don't care for it. I agree with past reviewers that the design of the new place is absolutely gorgeous, but that's not what people wait hours for and spend $$$ on. Most of the items were either too sweet or salty, and while it's always left to personal taste, I still rather have food that is spot on or that I can add to for personal preference. The highlights for me were the carving station (prime rib was super delicate, slow roasted brisket was smoky and the thick slabs of bacon were sweet and savory) and gelato. I enjoyed the abundance in variety and cuisines and while I didn't sample any, liked the cheese, meats and dressing station! The small plates (like Wicked Spoon) were enough to sample almost everything Bacchanal has to offer without going overboard and rolling yourself out of your seat. I wouldn't return unless someone else was footing the bill and even then, I'd ask if Wynn or Bellagio could be considered.

I'm going to be as objective as possible writing this review because I'm in the hospitality industry as well and I certainly know how overwhelming can be dealing with people everyday. If I could give this buffet a grade for effort it might be a different thing but let's see. First, 4 hours of total wait to be seated, 3 hours in virtual wait and 1 hour 15 mins approximately physically in line waiting to get a table (just 1 hour before the buffet closes) 3 different hostess with an awful attitude, in my time on line 4 different people complained about this so called "best buffet in vegas" service. The manager Mike explained it was no one's fault, that the system is flawed and they can't do anything about it and you're free to leave if you want... again, this is what we called the best buffet in town? Don't get me started on the food, as a culinary arts graduate, the food was mediocre I appreciate the work and effort of the people behind it, it's not your fault, it's the restaurant/hotel management fault and people that don't complain about this awful service. It's Caesars Palace right? It should be good! It's the best? No people, not everything that shines is gold. (Sorry for my english, not my native language)

One of the best buffets that I have been to. The buffet has every type of food imaginable...the wait wasn't long, because I went right when the brunch menu began being served. The entrees are amazingly done, they are served in a single dish (like a personal food item, not a big pan of whatever the food is.) The drinks are great (mimosas, bellinis, bloody marys), dessert is on point, and they have freshly jucied/squeezed juices (carrot, cucumber, watermelon).

All in all, it was a great experience.

Came there for lunch. Paid 35 dollars with tax (something you pay in other places for dinner), said would be like 50 for dinner (making it probably the most expensive buffet in Vegas). Given that, was greatly disappointed. Meat was tasteless. Could not find any salads. Come on, people, there are visitors from outside the U.S. that would like to have a proper starter, not to start biting on a steak the first thing. 

While reading reviews for other buffets like one in Cosmopolitan, where I went twice for dinner and liked a lot, I started to wonder if this is common disease of Las Vegas buffets: they try hard only for dinner, and serve previous day food for lunch?

This was one of the best Buffets I've ever had. They had unique doors such as Escargot and bone marrow, but I didn't try any of that. I had the crab, which was okay. But the squash ravioli was probably my favorite. They also had sushi, pazoli, homemade pizza, lamb, prime rib, mashed potatoes, salads, pastas, and a large verity of desserts. We came on Christmas so the wait was forever, and the line was long. You could tell they were doing their best though and they did what they could to accommodate us. Highly recommend coming here, but make sure you use the bathroom before you come in to the restaurant because there isn't one located inside of it.
unbelievable and gorgeous ambiance.  great food, custom omlets, no limit to the creativity here!  loved the dessert bars!

I've been here a few times and after having tried almost every food item they have to offer, including every ice cream flavor.. I'm sure the employees hate me by now. 

My favorite items: Japanese udon, the eggs benedict, the shu mai, the Chinese mini egg tart dessert, the cold shrimp, sausages, the lobster bisque, french fries, meatball in marinara sauce, the truffle mushroom pizza, meat lovers' pizza, fresh juices in bottles, sushi, sashimi, Japanese seaweed salad, al pastor tacos packed on with an all-you-can-eat toppings and condiment bar, Japanese rice pudding dessert, creme brûlée, thai tea float, crab legs, etc. 

I didn't get any of the fruit, cheese and nuts, churros, lamb, candies (reese's cups), snails, waffle and fried chicken, but they all looked amazing. Next time, Bacchanal. 

Only downside is the usual long wait and high price for dinner. I recommend going during lunch time when they're just about to open for a better pricing deal and a shorter time in line.

I was here on a Saturday for Brunch. I really don't see what people sees in this buffet. Food wise, nothing worth celebrating about. They do have more spacious table and seating compare to other buffet, which I guess was nice. But honestly, my main reason for coming here was the high expectation from all the raves from over 5000+ reviews. I mean if you think the buffet here was spectacular, I'm sorry, but you need to eat out more. Quite frankly, the selections was mediocre and the food was just average, heck some was kind of nasty tasting. I paid $50 a pop, which I felt cheated toward the end of my unsatisfying meal. In conclusion, if you have extra money that you don't know what to do with it and want to spend it on bland tasteless food, go here!

This is my favorite buffet place in Vegas! Dock them one star for very long lines during dinner. The seafood is very good. One of the best oysters I've had. The clams, scallops, crabs, and fish are all very fresh. Don't really care for the other stuff, but it a buffet they're also up to par. Lastly, the dessert station is one of the best. None of that cheap donuts and ice cream stuff. They even have very good gelato...

Very expensive but worth it when you come to Vegas. I am a big eater but I didn't get to try most of the food here. I ate mostly seafood, steak and desserts. I also paid an extra $15 for endless drinks. Our server was fast and efficient despite it being a weekend night. We gave Rosa a nice tip. They have the best king crab with drawn butter here.

First  visit  to  Las  Vegas ,  and  you can't  go to Las  Vegas  without  going  to a buffet at least  once. Although  the hotel that I  stayed had its  own  buffet ,  my sister  stated that  she likes the buffet at Ceasars  Palace because they have hot snow crab legs and not just cold like most buffets. 

The first thing that a got was the hot crab legs which were  delicious .  After that I got a little bit of a few things to see how I  would like each item--I believe in tasting  a small amount at first ,  that way if it is not appetizing,  not much would have been wasted.  This buffet  was $50+, and maybe for some you may get your money's  worth, but for  me, I was not crazy about most of the items that I tried. The only  thing that I  really enjoyed was the hot crab legs, and if I  had not gotten full on trying  items that was not all that, I would have gone back for seconds of crab legs. The only other items that I  enjoyed were the pizza, macaroni  and cheese, the hibiscus  drink was very delicious .  The highlight for me was the dessert! Oh, my, the assorted desserts  were just beautiful  and the taste was delightful. I hate that  I  was too full to really enjoy, but I  did taste quite a few. The bread pudding was so delicious .  My sister  said the chocolate  molten  cake was also delicious .  If I  had known the desserts  were so good, I  would have started  my meal  off with those first.

Afterwards ,  I  thought I  don't  need to ever do another buffet  in Vegas  again, but I  may try this one more time and just fill up on crab legs, hibiscus  drink, and definitely  try more of the desserts.

Really good. Most amazing buffet I've ever had. Not quite 5 stars because during seating and serving the staff seemed confused about who to seat next and what line was for which people. Overall though it's definitely worth checking out. Like after you haven't eaten for 3 days. Tacos, thai, italian, meat cheese and fruit, bbq, seafood, this mushroom soup was knocked off the chart though. Gotta try it.

Best buffet I've ever been to in Vegas. The food was great, they had a wide variety of choices and they were very quick on filling up the plates as they were emptying very fast. I went there on thanksgiving night so it was a bit pricey and busy, but even so the service was great. The hostesses were very comprehensive and understood that customers were hungry so they tried the best to clear the lines. Besides that, I would definitely recommend it. Service is great, food is great, and definitely worth the money.

So Chris and I arrived about 8pm-ish on a Saturday saw the line was crazy long, really we had no idea where it ended. So we left to go get a drink before standing in line, by the time we got back (20 mins later) it was under control and didn't seem to long. We chatted with some folks ahead of us from San Francisco so it made the hourish wait go by fast. When we finally got up to the front to pay one of the employees came and announced they were at full capacity and would stop letting people in at 10 and would pull food at 10:30. 
We were next in line and figured mehh we waited all this time and we can eat in an hour. Never again will I do that! We felt rushed the whole time, I barely got to eat with my husband because either I was eating and he was up in line or the other way around.
Now to the food. It's was OK, it wasn't worth the $102 we paid. When we came here in November they had KING crab and this time had crap snow crab. I was very disappointed! What I did like was the prime rib, oh boy was is cooked perfectly it was succulent and moist, and the lamb. I tried the Thai tea gelato and loved it, it tasted like the real thing. However, that's about it unfortunately. We loved it so much the first time and we were so sadly disappointed this time I doubt we'll ever be back.
Every single bite was delicious, the service was excellent as well. I dream of being here for Thanksgiving or Christmas some day.

The food was good, but definitely not worth the price. Went here for Christmas brunch. Walked right in at about 9:30 am.

No eggs with truffles. I had one slice of pizza, salami, cheese, beef with asparagus, frisee salad. The sushi had no fish -- just tamago and such. My boyfriend had roast beef and some scrambled eggs.

Cost -- $129.99 for two with iced tea, plus $20 tip. Won't do that again!

This was my favorite buffet in Vegas! The food is top notch not like any buffet in Vegas. We went for brunch and the selections were great. Although the Asia food was not good but there was so much to choose from that we didn't mind. In the dessert side you have to try the caramel salted ice cream!
Overrated and pricey.  It was just ok to our party of 20.  We all had better food for $60+ per person.
Solid buffet, variety of foods was as good as any, quality was variable but overall enjoyed!

Had lunch here on a Friday and in terms of buffet food, the food here was pretty darn good. 

Started out with a seafood plate of king crab legs, shrimp, and oysters. The crab was my favorite--the meat was sweet and delicious!

Then moved onto a charcuterie plate that was decent but nothing to write home about. 

Next got some congee at the asian food station. Grandma would have berated me (such cheap food! Waste of stomach space!), but it was so good. 

Then came the tacos--get the pork. 

Then a return to the king crab legs and some more shrimp cocktail.

Finally some truffle mushroom soup (so surprisingly delicious!) and this amazing parmesan cheesy cracker crisp thing...noms. 

Oh and I'm not really one for sweets but the green tea creme brulee was on point. 

Overall, lots of options for everyone. The boy got lots of the meats--wagyu beef sliders and prime rib cuts. Those were also pretty dece. Quality isnt as good as you can get at some restaurants but it's certainly the best quality I've ever had at a buffet.

After hearing all the hype I tried this buffet and was so disappointed. Was the food good? Yes, but not worth the exuberant price. I think the price was more for the presentation of the food then the quality. I love seafood, especially crab legs - I've had better. I don't like the split crab legs at all. They may be easier to get into, but it messes with the meat of the crab. Also found the crab to be overcooked. Been there once, and don't expect to go again.

Just got back from a lovely time in Vegas and I feel I really HAVE to review this buffet...  No, really.  My bitterness compels me, even several days after the fact.

A friend of mine who had tried this buffet on a previous trip just raved and raved about it and was eager to have the rest of our group try it, all the while hyping it up to be "the mother of all buffets!" and "so good you'll pass out!"  ...Yeahhhh, not so much.  I felt bad for disappointing him, but after spending $50 for a single meal, I have a right to be a tad critical.  So here's how it stacks up:

PROS

-Amazing food.  The ingredients seemed fresh and well assembled, and every dish I tried was incredibly flavorful....  Gourmet indeed!  (And the only reason this buffet gets three stars from me instead of one or two.)
-Varied selection of dishes/cultural representations
-Gorgeous atmosphere.  I loved the clean lines of polished glass and stainless steel at every turn.  And I appreciate the fact that each separate area has its own individual look and feel.
-STREET TACO STATION!  Someone, somewhere, heard my prayers on this.  I was so excited to try my carnitas tacos that I almost ran into some poor, unsuspecting lady in my frenzy to get back to my table.  However, by the time I was able to make it out of the crazy line for food, they were ice cold and the carnitas were hard.    More on that below...

CONS

-Price.  This mutha is EXPENSIVE.  I mean, seriously, what is that about?  I chose to try this the one time for the experience, but for what this buffet offers, it hardly seems worth it.  I could go to the Wynn buffet or, to a lesser degree, Wicked Spoon to get more for my money (if the goal was, as it usually is, stuffing my face with yummy foods!).  
-Service lagged.  Once my friend was able to flag down one of the servers to order our drinks, he was pretty good about seeing to our needs.  Initially, though, he was nowhere to be found.  We had just come from the Valley of Fire about 40 minutes outside of Vegas and were dying of thirst, but no one came to ask for our order for a good 10-15 minutes after being seated.  Plenty of servers passed us and our conspicuously empty table that evening, but no one bothered to stop.
-LINES!  CRAZY, UNFORGIVING, TORTUROUSLY LONG LINES!!!  As a few previous reviewers have noted, this place has an absolutely awful set up.  I can see that if they just moved a few of the stations around the dining area (perhaps on the other side of the dessert bar, for instance), it would help immensely with the pileup of angry/hungry patrons.  As it was, I waited a good hour on my feet, plate in hand, just for a chance to SEE what foods were offered!  And this is after waiting almost an hour and a half just to get in!!  The line hardly ever moved because the lady working the carving station moved at a glacial pace and honestly looked like she could cry from being overwhelmed with orders.  I would've avoided the meat altogether, really, but after waiting that long to get a shot at my different options, I knew I had to at least try some ribs and the brisket.  There would be NO going back, that's for sure!!  I hardly ever got a chance to eat with my friends because we all stood in the massive line of doom at varying times.  :(  Boo...
-Rude staff.  The situation in line was intense, folks, as I have mentioned, but there was intensity from the kitchen, too.  When I had finally made my way up to the carving station (hallelujah!), an older gentleman came right up in front of me and lifted his plate up, asking if the carving lady could put just the tiniest piece of chicken on it.  While I was in NO MOOD to allow someone to cut in front of me, even I felt this sweet old man deserved a better response than what he received...  One of the kitchen staff heard him and came forward, rudely yelling at him to get to the back of the line.  He scowled in the general direction of the rest of us, too.  I get that he may have been having a rough night with a bunch of unhappy patrons, but there was no need for that.  I'm a big girl, and I can speak for myself, thanks.
-Repeatedly out of foods.  I missed out on mac and cheese and green tea mochi balls, people!  And once they ran out, there was no replacing them.
-THEY LIMIT YOUR PORTIONS.  ...Think about this.  It's a buffet, for crying out loud!  For $50, I think I am entitled to pile my plate if I choose, but management came around and literally limited the quantity of meats per person.  Not cool.  Not cool at all!

There's definitely quality in the food they serve but for some reason it does not seem at par with Wicked Spoon nor the Wynn buffet. 

Came here for dinner a couple of months ago.  There was a long line at 8 pm on a Thursday but we were seated after a short wait.  There was enough variety and the seafood station made it worthwhile, but nothing stood out.  And I was disappointed with the dessert.  Only thing I liked was the chocolate creme brulee.

Service is outstanding however.  Something you would expect from Caesars.

Overall this is a very good buffet.  I like the individual portions of things and it is definitely above average.  The highlights was the beef brisket and the macaroni and cheese.  I found the prime rib to be cold and lacking in flavour.  If I was looking at it considering the price I would be so so about it but I was able to use my points.

New management saw my review. Took action. 
Not very often a restaurant wants to make a difference based on honest customer reviews.

Returned! 

Food has improved!

Highly recommended.

Its worth it just for the pizza!

Its okay but not worth the price. For instance, the beef is too dry, the seafood is gritty. The dessert section was the best part of the meal. Im sure you can find the same stuff with a better deal at another buffet.

Wow! The food was amazing. I kept my portions small so that I could try a lot of different things. Out of 4 plates, I had maybe 3 items I wasn't fond of, but overall very impressed with the quality, variety, freshness and flavor of the food. Especially enjoyed some of the unique dishes like lemon basil, ube, & black sesame gelatos. Thai basil beef, cold soba noodles, and pork baos were the best I'd ever had! Breakfast offerings like crepes, scrambled eggs with Boursin, and sausages were all very good as well. Excellent charcuterie! My companions were impressed with the seafood offerings. I did not partake. 
I love that they put out small-ish quantities and the staff is cooking so near that food is replenished quickly & is always fresh. 
When we arrived, the staff seemed irritated, like directing us where to get in line, and seating us was inconvenient for them. It was not busy when we arrived. There was not a line to get in. They sat us at the worst table, next to the door where bussing staff come & go. The table was the shabbiest looking one in the places, and it leaned and wobbled horribly. I found it odd because there were plenty of nicer tables large enough to accommodate our party of 6 available nearby. 
Our waitress literally rolled her eyes when I asked for coffee. She eventually warmed to us and even brought my mom a plate of desserts with a birthday message written in chocolate, and a candle to blow out (it was her 60th) and she was very sweet wishing us well when we left, but we had a rough start. Maybe parties of 6 tend to be rude, so they expected us to be. I don't know.

Came here for a weekend brunch.  We were
Really disappointed- very overpriced for the quality.  The crab legs were not impressive- some still frozen.  The only worthy thing was the dessert bar (check out the Ube icecream) and the crepe and omelette station.  Don't think we will he back, but will recommend to go closer to lunch time because we noticed they started to serve warm crab legs and better dishes

We finally get to try Bacchanal Buffet - thanks to coupon on Groupon!! Or else, I would never pay that much for a buffet.

The trick is to come before 5 PM so you don't have to stay in such a long line. 

They have so many selections! I vouch for the ramen and also the sushi. They're pretty good. I also tried the carving station. The prime rib is okay but they had something else (beef rib?) that was better. The prime rib was too raw at the time. The Asian station is also pretty decent. They have the juice pork belly and a bunch of dim sum selections. Their seafood station is also pretty good. I only tried the shrimp cocktails and oyster shooters.

Their dessert station is also so huge. They had a lot of macaroons and also gelato. I would definitely come back for the ramen :)

My favorite buffet in Las Vegas. We waited around 20 min until we get in, we arrived at 5:30pm.

Design: I love the layout of this place, it's large inside, some other buffets fill so many tables at once, which makes it difficult to move around. 
They have different food sections: Seafood, American, Italian, Mexican, Thai, Japanese, and Chinese.



Recommendations:

Chinese: I strongly recommend Roast Ducks, it's so bomb especially with their sweet sauce. The dim sums are the must have.

American: The prime rib always has a waiting line, but it was fast. Bone Marrow is a must, they run out so fast.

Seafood: The raw oyster taste so freshly. Cocktail shrimps are in good sizes. 

Dessert: Creme brûlée is a must, the crispy caramel on top plus creamy texture filling is heaven like. Ice cream station is also popular. Egg tart taste like the one I used to have in Asia.
(Make sure you leave some stomach space for dessert, don't stuff yourself out for main dishes only.)

I always recommend Bacchanal whenever people ask me which buffet is the best in town. Definitely would have another visit in the future.

Excellent buffet! Lots of options: American, Italian, Asian, Mexican foods. Seafood, salad bar, dessert bar, various beverage options. Everything I tried was delicious especially the lamb chops. I only gave it 4 stars because the wait is unbelievable. They require that you check-in with the hostess first, she gives you a ticket stating when you should come back (our ticket was for a 1 hour wait). When we arrived at our designated time slot, they made us wait in line for another hour! Shameful! Also, the price was $60 (July 2015). I could not eat $60 worth of food. Ladies, bring a sweater/cardigan. It's freezing in there! And to the fellas with a hefty appetite, you're allowed to stay at the buffet for two hours.

Antho and I visited here a bit back and had a lovely meal. There is no shortage of options available to whet your palate and tempt you, so it's easy to find your plate overfloweth... As a result, the poor bussers and wait staff have quite the task on their hands. Refills on our beverages were not the most expeditiously brought, but I think that's understandable given what they have to contend with.
Food is well maintained and fresh, though during peaks you may have to fight a small crowd to get to it. We loved the seafood selection and the dessert bar was pretty amazing, too. 
If you're nearby and have the funds and an indecisive crowd to feed, this is definitely a good option. If you're looking for a worthwhile buffet to visit in Vegas, still a good option. If you're looking to pinch your pennies or trying to budget you may want to look elsewhere.

Bacchanal is my must go-to buffet spot in Vegas! (with the other one being Wicked Spoon). Yummm love their lunch buffet with bottomless mimosa and unlimited fresh grapefruit juice! Downside is that there's always a huge line, but I guess, well it's Vegas lol.

It ain't a Vegas trip without a buffet. This buffet is probably the most well known one in the Vegas strip and conveniently located in Cesar palace. This past visit was my second one and I can gladly confirm that it was on point.

The line is usually a hour or two but I suppose a Wednesday visit only made it 15 mins wait at most. Cleverly lined up at 2:30pm and got in by 2:45pm paying for lunch price ($38 + tax ) while getting to experience dinner options as well. Price after 3pm is ($54 + tax ). 

The buffet is creatively displayed and well organized with much space for everyone to enjoy. I personally would love to point out some of my favorite food choices. When it comes to buffets... It's all about the seafood. Mussels, clams, salmon,  sole fish, seabass, raw oysters, clam chowder, lobster bisque and of course..the Alaskan king crab legs ( served at dinner only). There's also a fine selection of premium meat including brisket, ribs , steak etc... But those are usually very filling for me. Also there's bottles of delicious juices where mango is my personal favorite. I didn't really touch dessert, Asian food selection or any other food choices because of my focus on seafood but everything else was very well presented and I'm sure top tier.

Tip: king crab legs on King crab legs with butter. The legs are already half opened so it's very easy to just peel out the meat. Do prepare for small wait time for them though because of its high popularity. 

Overall, I would say this is the best buffet in Vegas.

Complete and utter disaster with the line we waited for two hours and they kicked us out of the line because the whole party wasn't present. The manager was extremely rude. She did not even apologize. We ended up not going at all. DONT GO HERE. NOT WORTH IT
I think this the second best buffet in Vegas after The Buffet at the Wynn. Their Asian selection was the highlight as well as lamb chops.
Very pricey but well worth it. Love the hot crab legs and the amazing pizza. There's a guy who makes great street tacos as well. Every clean and classy.

The space is contemporary, comfortable and the array of foods is worthy of a Roman orgy. 
Yes Vegas has buffet everywhere but there is a reason this one consistently gets high marks. 
True.. it is not cheap. But in my opinion it is a very good value.

We went for lunch where in my experience in a medium high end restaurant on the strip with a drink or a glass of wine you will pay at least 100 + per person plus tip. If you are going for dinner and move up to a tasting menus and you can get into noise bled territory making the Bacchanal a real deal. 

These are the latest price breakdowns.
Weekday Brunch $39.99*
Mon.-Fri. 7:30 AM - 3 PM
Weekend Brunch $49.99*
Sat.-Sun. 8 AM - 3 PM
Weekday Dinner $54.99*
Mon.-Thurs. 3 PM - 10 PM
Weekend Dinner $57.99*
Fri.-Sun. 3 PM - 10 PM
All You Can Drink: Draft Beer, House Wine, Mimosas $15
Buffet of Buffets® Upgrade Pricing: $25 Brunch, $35 Dinner

We were here for a week day brunch. If you like a drink or so I highly recommend you do the all you can drink option. That was our choice on our visit. We had a great wait person Vince who saw that our sparkling wine was never empty and our coffee always filled. 

My personal favorites were the seafood offerings including green lip mussels that happen to a favorite. Crackers are delivered by your wait staff so that you can handle any hard shells. But most were all very easy to tackle. A choice of sauces are available for dipping and mixing if you are like me and like to do some of your own creative culinary experiments that can really only be done at buffets. 

At the Bacchanal you can eat your way around the world and the states with choices from New Orleans gumbo and crawdads. Waffles and friend chicken, Pho, sushi, pot stickers some of the best Mexican tacos, really great choice of Italian dishes, and for those who love a a great steak or prime rib  excellent beef. .

If you live for dessert you will find a mind boggling display of overwhelming tasty options. 

A gentle reminder. Tip your wait staff. Just because it's a buffet these people do work hard. As I said our person Vince was top notch. 

Observed: Parties of 2, 3 or 4 did not have a hard time getting seated. Larger parties can run into a wait. It is difficult to put together a table of 8 or more at a buffet because tables do not all come up at the same time and there are no reservation.

Went for lunch around 1pm on a Monday. No crazy line! Walked right up to pay and be seated. Amazing menu! My top faves were the beef brisket, jasmine rice pudding and the mango habanero gelato. Decently priced for the quality and variety. I must go for dinner next time I'm in Vegas b/c the crab legs aren't served during the lunch buffet.

I like how they have warm crab legs! The food is usually good here but the rib eye is a hit and miss when it comes to flavor. Here at Bacchanal the Rib eye comes out after 6pm FYI. I've been here about 6 times now and there's no line usually until after 8pm!!! I recently visited Wicked Spoon here in Vegas.. I found that their food is different from most buffet you would come across. Bacchanal is still better because you get your monies worth! At Wicked Spoon the price goes from Lunch $23 to Dinner $41 but the only thing different is cold tiny crab legs, lamb that isn't the best and i can't remember much else that is different! lol So hurry up and come try Bacchanal!!!! But let me warn you ... you might need a wheel chair to be wheeled out haha.. cuz your legs will give out due to the weight of your belly!!!! :)

I liked their crab legs. I was second in a huge forming line. They are cracked, so no work has to be done. Sushi was very fresh. They have really cute bite sized desserts, so you can sample a lot of things. The dessert section is hidden away from everything else, so I think there is a good chance a lot of people forget about it. They have gellato in many different flavors like sour cherry. Very cute desserts. I don't know what kind of dessert I was eating. White chocolate with edible silver balls and soft center. Good what ever it was. I am very picky, and I found a lot of stuff I could eat. However for the price, I think I like the Bellagio better. Their is also a buffet on the stip with circular aquariums at the buffet with tropical desserts that are out of this world. Just can't remember the name of it :( I just remember you take an esculator down to get to the buffet. If you love Sushi Todai is a great fish and sushi buffet for reasonable prices. They have chicken and beef too!

Some unexpected choices that makes this buffet stand out.

Went to the buffet for a late lunch on the Buffet of Buffet pass.  We had to pay $20/person on top.

Some unexpected and noteworthy items:

--the extensive raw bar: lots of shrimps, mussels, oyster on the half-shell, oyster shooters and ceviche; fresh cucumber juice and tropical juices
--big Mexican food section with fresh juices: tamarind, mango and pineapple juices, horchata; good carnitas
--extensive Asian food section: good springrolls, reasonable barbecue pork, fresh sliced ginger
--extensive dessert section with lots of ice cream and sherbet choices: notables include toasted coconut, fig and balsamic, and baklava ice creams; blood orange sherbet and mango lime chili sherbet (all yummy!)
--Kobe sliders

The service was attentive--they re-filled our drinks and checked on us frequently.

Some not so hot items:

Asian foods: sushi (Costco caliber), fried wontons, tofu was probably not fresh
Carver station: prime rib and brisket (dry and tasteless)
Seafood: Mussel Meunier were gritty; lobster corn something or other was too salty
Dessert: crepe station where someone cooked the crepes but did not fill them.

Overall one of the better buffets.

My friends tell me this is the buffet to try when in Vegas so I had to try it. The wait was pretty long, around 1.5-2 hours long, though I hear that's the usual wait time? It was worth it though! Their selection of food is incredible! Their fresh crab legs were so popular. My favorite section: the desserts. They had a wide selection of cakes, gelato, and even mochi ice cream! I wish my stomach was big enough to try everything they had there!

I will never waste my time or money going here again. I bought the VIP option to avoid the line only to find out that after the first line to get to the registers there is an additional line to be seated. I waited in that additional line for an hour... That's right I paid extra to skip the line and ended up waiting in line for an hour to be seated. The food itself was just ok, it was often lukewarm or cold. The only thing that was notable was my waiter who was super nice and attentive. Personally I won't be back.

Be prepared to wait about 45 mins to 2+ hours during busy hours. The food is great!

Stars of the buffet:

Fresh Oysters
Shrimp
Prime Rib
Black Chicken Soup
Hot and Cold Crab Legs
Crepes made to order
Ice cream AND MOCHIIIIII

Great value and great food. You will not be disappointed in the selection and the customer service. There were so many options, I wish I could have posted more pictures. All of Bacchanal's staff was polite and welcoming. I definitely will be back here every time I visit Las Vegas.

Went here for New Year's Night Dinner, paid $156 for me & my husband. Waited in line for almost 1.5hr :( The food was amazing.. What I love the most is their bone marrow, omg it melts in ur mouth. Really worth-it & highly recommended.

One morning while laying in bed with my lovely fiancee, my tummy were making some weird noises. I look at it and says " what the hell you want now?" It says, "bro, you remember those commercial posters in the lift at cesar that you always seen on the way home from work?", "oh you mean the bacchanal poster?", "yeah, lets go check it out!"

So I wake my fiancee up and tell her, boy do I have a surprise for you. Half and hour later we are ready and on our way. Arrived at 10.50 am, walk right through the line, no waits, two please and sit our asses down. I dont know what I am expecting right now.

The server arrived to take our drink orders and off we went to the wonderland of buffet. We try the M buffet and M Resort and Casino who supposedly the best in Las Vegas, oh well, they bumped off to number 2 now. I am so glad that the best bufftet in Las Vegas belong to Cesars the center of Las Vegas Strip. 

Dim Sum, Sushi, Crepe Station, Fully squeezed fresh juices, mexican stand, omelet station, on and on it goes. Absolutely wonderful place. Attentive service and an absolute place to take your friends and relative when they are in town. 

I can honestly says that this buffet just messed up a lot of other restaurant in cesar palace. You should see the line when we are done with our lunch. Phew, glad I dont have to wait in that line.

Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Casino is my favorite buffet in Las Vegas. 

I first dined here a few years ago and then just recently. The food is even better! Expect at least an hour wait for dinner. 

Highlights:
-braised beef rib is my favorite item here. The meat is full of flavor and falls off the bone! 
-street tacos were great with all the fixings!
-king crab legs - super fresh
-Roast duck and roast pork
-kim chi fries rice! So good!
-hot link was tasty
-the dessert macaroons and Thai iced tea with a scoop of ice cream were great

I'd skip the sea bass appetizer -it was really tough. 

Can't wait til next time!!

Tried this place, for the first time this week, during lunch time just to find out what the hype was all about..

Some positives:
- Overall atmosphere & ambience was great.
- Food presentation was quite good, probably @ the same level if not better than Wicked Spoon
- Service was good
- Desserts section was decent
- Food variety was good

One big disappointment is the lack of sushi/nigiri/sashimi selections (I recall there were probably only 5-7 different types)......In comparison, I would say Vegas Buffet (in the L.A. area) is probably much better..

Other comment : Long queue for the raw seafood & meat sections

For the (lunch) price, I think one could get better deals elsewhere in Las Vegas, esp. if one craves for seafood

My friend and I were in Vegas for the Memorial Weekend.  We purchased Buffet of Buffets pass and in addition they charged an extra $25 for the Cesar's buffet.  Total we paid $105 per person.  I was told they charge $65/person for dinner because of holiday but regularly it's $50/person.  
Their cocktail shrimp and their crab legs were the best of all Vegas buffets that I've been to.  However, we only had one hour to eat and food was take away in 45 minutes because we only got seated at 10pm and they close at 11pm.  That was a horrible experience!  I think they should stop taking in people after 9pm.  You still have to wait in line for food after you get so it's totally a rip off if you get seated with less than 2 hours to eat.  
Besides the large cocktail shrimp and the good size crab legs, nothing exceptional about this place.  sushi section was very small and pathetic.  Total not worth the money you pay for.  My advice to to skip it.

Went here on a Tuesday evening and price was roughly $60 after taxes.  Many good samplings including Korean beef spare ribs, various sushi/nigiri, roast duck, and other asian cuisines.  Snow crab legs were rather small and the stand didn't have a lot of stock.  There was also an oyster bar but I did not try it.  Dessert is extensive with flan, panna cotta, ice cream, and other delicacies.

Definitely the best buffet I've had in Vegas. The selection is truly diverse and high in quality. They've got everything from dim sum to enchiladas. A taco station and a crepe station. 

When the crowds have eaten a selection up, Bacchanal replaces it with another completely different food. 

Always fresh, always changing.

When you go to Vegas, you want good food and a fun time. If you visit Bacchanal Buffet, you'll get both, IF you are lucky enough to have Julie as your waitress! We ordered bottomless mimosas and she kept our glasses full and our spirits high with her quick wit, laid back demeanor, and humor. The food is excellent and there is literally something for everyone, with every major cuisine represented. I'd have to say the little pots of shrimp and grits were my favorite!

The only downside is it will cost you a pretty penny, especially if you opt for the booze. It also didn't look like everyone enjoyed the same impeccable service that we got from Julie. But it's well worth it, considering it's not something you do every day!

One of my favorite Vegas buffets located in Caesar's Palace. Have gone twice for weekend dinners. It's on the pricier side, but totally worth it! I'll definitely be back again. 

They have a wide spread of ethnic foods that are blocked together, including Asian, South American, Italian, and American. There's a great selection of tasty foods. Their carving station has the typical things, but something unique is the Wagyu steak (might be for weekend dinner only?). For seafood, they of course have the endless crab legs, but the sushi options were pretty limited even for weekend dinner. 

The desserts section had a wide variety of things as well, including a gelato bar with a ton of flavors.

ALL YOU CAN EAT, PERFECTLY SLICED CRAB LEGS WITH BUTTER ON THE SIDE. I got my money's worth just in the seafood section alone. Worth every penny!! Best and biggest buffet I have ever been too, definitely a must!!

After seeing Bacchanal on several food documentaries and hearing how amazing it was from word of mouth, I felt let down with my overall dining experience. 

Pros:

Service: the waiters and waitress were super fast in refilling drinks and taking plates off your table. 

Dessert Bar: the only time where I felt this buffet lived up to its popularity was based on the dessert bar. There was a assortment of chocolates/truffles, cakes, cookies, gelato, shaved ice, and mochi ice cream. 

Cons:

Food: the selection at the seafood bar was weak, could of have more premium items. They had other items that you can find at any other buffets for half of the price. The overall taste was just okay, not what I expected from the overly hyped buffet. 

Price: it's about $50 per person during dinner and I personally thought I could have had a better tasting meal someplace else on the strip for the amount I paid.

The service provided by Maryam today was excellent. She was kind and surpassed our expectations from a server.  She brought our drinks before we would run out. We will definitely be back and hopefully we will be able to request her as our server again. The food was great, you must save room for dessert. Delicious!

Arrive at this Restaurant at their were busy during lunch time but got seated quick. A lot of Variety of food from all around the world, food was excellent quality. Staff was friendly. Price was little price but worth it for the food you get to choose from. Good amount of selection of dessert to end the meal. Also have many different beverage to choose from you can have. If you love to try different food that is made with attention and good quality of ingredients this is the place to go. I would come back here again to eat and recommend it.

I came here this past weekend after reading some great reviews for this place. My brother and his girlfriend were visiting Vegas from Hawaii, so I met them and took them here. We got there around 10:30 am, as breakfast was ending and lunch was starting. For the three of us it was around $63, not too bad.  

It definitely lived up to its hype! 

They had the standard breakfast fare like eggs, sausage, pancakes, and various juices. These were all pretty good. They also had some more interesting dishes. Of the breakfast foods, they had huevos rancheros, croque madames, corn beef pizza, steak and eggs red velvet pancakes, and chicken and waffles. Unfortunately most of the breakfast foods were not great, except the chicken was delicious.  

However, the lunch and Asian foods were really really good - I'm not talking Chinese buffet quality, but much much better. They had dim sum, and not just spring rolls, but soup dumplings (WOW!), sticky rice (good), and har gau (which I don't eat). The noodle station had amazingly flavored ramen. And the Peking duck was some of the best I've ever had.  

The charcuterie and salads rocked, especially the prosciutto. Who doesn't love prosciutto. The prime rib was also really good and a perfect medium rare for me.  And the sliders were definitely a winner too. 

The desserts were good but not spectacular, but I am rarely wowed by desserts anyway. The macaroons were especially delicous

So, just go. 
Don't waste any more time. Stop reading this. If you're in Vegas, go. GO!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

This hasn't ruined all buffets, but god damn it sure has set a standard.
My boyfriend and I went to celebrate my audition for Nevada Ballet Theater, so we went the next morning. Now this is eeeeeeeeeeeeeexpeeeeeeeeeeeeensiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiiive!!!!!!! Again, which is why we went for breakfast.

I was quite skeptical as to why it was so expensive, and when we first came in still didn't see why. Until, we found a WHOLE extra room of food. Variety variety variety. This place was everything  you'll ever want. Nicer quality food than most buffets I have ever been to. This is a buffet gastronomy experience and a HUGE ass dessert section with gelato. Super unique dishes, and desserts. 

Just go dammit, why are you still reading this?!?!?!??!?!?!

Really tasty but wasn't blown away...

So I have been dreaming of coming to this buffet for years but my friends and family never wanted to wait in the 2 hour line.

I was in Vegas on business by myself and a table for one was only a 30 min wait. I approached paid the $58.00 and waited with deep anticipation.

So the waitress explained to me that I was in for a treat and not to eat the bread because there is so much to try.

I started with a little of everything from the world of China, Italy, Mexican, Meats and seafood.

I was super impressed with the set up and variety of all the foods as well as the quality.
The only thing for me is this two be world renowned and so expensive I was expecting things I have never seen or tasted before.

I'm a certified (by my family) Crab leg queen!! I will devour the legs so quick you would think I had build in claws and butter and lemon in my veins.

So excited that they had Hot crab legs, I hate cold crab legs! They were sweet and good but for the price I would have preferred to not have them pre cut. Anytime you expose the crab meat to boiling water outside of the shell it will loose some of its flavor. If you are ever in Honolulu the Pacific Ocean hotel has THE BEST CRAB LEGS YOU WILL EVER HAVE! NOT PRE CUT JUST PURE MASSIVE SWEET GOODNESS!!! And not to mention that buffet is only $35.00.

I also loved the truffle and goad cheese pizza and the scallops Rockefeller.
