Much like the rest of the yelpers the dessert area seems so great but really the options aren't that diverse. No Key lime pie, no cobblers, no candied walnuts etc. I was your basic chocolate lovers dream, lava cake, carrot cake, cup cakes and crepes. I didn't finish any of my dessert it wasn't worth the calories.

My favorite part hands down about the whole buffet is the fresh Aqua Frescas in little personal glass bottles. Things like that make you feel like you are paying for something different.

Food was good but for the price and the normal wait time I wont be back..

It was about $63 per person when I went with my family. The cashier didn't tell my sister it was $20 per person for the unlimited mimosas so that was disappointing because it didn't also state that on the menu or paper they had on there! :( The food was really good. I love how they have alot of variety here and the fresh juice selection you can choose from. Their food was really good, well presented, and fancy looking. This buffet is really good for many food selection to choose from and really bug portion! My favorite was the green tea mint ice cream, roasted pork, fresh juice, and street taco. Amazing! Some food just needs a bit more flavor.

Worth a visit to say you've done a Vegas brunch and the selections are astounding! Plus you can get bottomless mimosas for $15. But, the food quality is not that great, is definitely a deal but not the best meal you will have so that's the three stars here. A fun experience though and we had friendly service.

I'm not a huge fan of buffets because the food is usually mediocre and I just can't eat plates and plates of stuff.  However, this was the best buffet that I have been to in a very long time.  We went for a late breakfast and it had a very wide variety of things, all freshly prepared and tasty.  We happened to be there on a weekday and it was nearly empty so that was nice.  They started switching things out for the lunch buffet while we were there so we should have waited a while because there were some other things that we would have tried, but we were all too full by then.  Service was great, too.

Out of all the buffets I have tried in Vegas (wicked spoon, rio carnival, bellagio), this surpasses all of them. Yes, it's a little pricey, and yes you have to wait in a long line, but in the end you get what you pay for and it's all worth it. 

Highlights: KING crab legs that they make warm for you (upon request), steak tacos that they freshly make for you, gelato, sushi rolls, buffalo chicken wings, fried chicken, ribs,.... too many to list. Everything was just freshly made and didn't taste like it was sitting under the heating lamp for hours.

If you're in the mood to splurge on a buffet in Vegas, then this is definitely your go to spot!
Fabulous selection and great staff!!! Especially loved the sushi selection, the sweet tater tots, & fresh crepes for dessert! YUMM! A little pricey but worth it.

Not worth it!!  We had the buffets of buffets pass. Gets you into quite a few different places for $50. We were told that there was a $10 up charge for this particular Buffett. When we got there we were charged $30 extra per person. What????  But we thought hey it's supposed to be awesome so let's do it. 

It was very sub par. The Buffett at the Rio is larger and has more variety. This one is mostly Asian food and seafood. It also took the waiter 20 mins to take our drink order. I will not return and I will be talking to someone about the outrageous up charge.

This place has fallen off from the quality buffet it used to be when it first opened.  The Kobe sliders were extra dry, the fried chicken was soggy, and the waffles were cement.  Low grade Prime rib, and no more fresh squeezed juices top off the list of disappointments on today's visit. Do not waste your money.

I be been here for lunch and dinner and the food is great. Not huge but still a very good selection with great present. They have a beautiful selection of desserts as well. Steamed crab legs are the best!! The food overall is a bit salty but still my favorite buffet on the strip so I have to give it 5 stars!!

Great variety and well worth the $50 dollars.
I would say it's on par with Wicken Spoon.  It actually might be better due to their fresh oyster bar and hot/cold king crab/snow crab selection.
I was impressed with their noodle section, serving both ramen and pho. 
Try to go therearound 3:30pm to avoid huge lines.
Also, ask for the tables in the back, noticed how spacious it was compared to the other dining area.  Enjoy!

I succumbed to the hype. It was an emotional roller coaster of excitement, waiting, hanger (being hangry), and satisfaction. The buffet has plethora of different cuisines like Italian, Asian, Spanish, seafood, American, and etc. 

The wait was unbearable but was it worth the wait? Eh. Food was excellent. Everything we tried was phenomenal and they catered to variety of palates. The service was very attentive and friendly. I would go again only if I made reservations in advance (which we didn't and waited two hours in line).

I totally love this place! Large variety of foods to pick, all of them from different cuisines. You deserve to wait for more than an hour of line. Anyone who stops by at Caesars Palace at night should stop by at this buffet.

It is out of expectation for all dishes with high price..and long line 
Yes, it has more international foods selection 
But it cost about $52.00 per
I spent 2 hours and can not tasted all....
The quality is poor .. It is not yummy at all..
The brisket and sausages are overcooked..

Even you can sitting in but has been with another long line for seafoods and prime rib line...
It is not worth it for that $ and spent time
 the long line ..
It was so disappointed !!!

My favorite thing here was the tacos. So good and they're made to order in a little revolving grill. Unfortunately the boyfriend being cheap said we had to eat as many crab legs as possible and that tacos would bot get us our money's worth. The food was great and in my opinion worth the price. We went early to avoid the long lines and waited 10-15 minutes to be seated which really wasn't that bad. Overall great selection and small portions ideal for trying as many things as possible. Only negative was when we got up to get Dessert, our table was cleared when we got back to our seats and after we had been sitting for a moment a host came and was about to seat people where we were still sitting. This is understandable given the size and the wait and was only a slight annoyance. I would come here again and recommend to a friend

Trying to do Vegas on a budget is no joke! I figured this buffet would suffice to fill our stomachs for the rest of the day but due to the quality, I pretty much left most of it on my plate. It's all about the hype from the outside. Don't be fooled by the enormous crab legs and seafood buffet. The lines are long, God knows how many people have touched what, and pretty much most of the food reeked of being over salted. I paid $100 for two, for the lunch buffet and thanked myself later for not going to dinner here instead. 
The table service is spotty. Trying to just get water is a feat unto itself. Also hide your forks, because the staff seems to just love to take them from you when you go back for seconds. Even the dessert bar, which was decent to some exstent, cheapened out. I saw bowls of smarties candies and other cheap brands all piled up. Really? Isn't this suppose to be a top-notch buffet. Sad to say this, but I've had better meals at Old Country buffet in the years past.

For such an expensive buffet at Caesars' Palace, this was a big disappointment... Had to wait in a long line since their crab legs and meat cutting area because it was only a single station... Room for improvement there. Food was typical but their fresh juices were good... It'll be a while before I return here... Prepare for that long line...

The selection of food is for sure amazing. Especially their Asian food and desserts are the best part of this place. The worst part of this place is the waiting line. It is the way too long a lot of times. Overall it's one of the best buffet in Vegas.

Ate a ton of crab legs, always good but they were kind of falling apart as if they were in water for too long (after being cut.)
Oysters were SUPER FRESH and lovely. 
Ceviche was delish

Brisket smelled amazing and smokey but it was chewy, I was looking fwd to it falling apart as it should. I got a gigantic piece of fat with little meat :(
Fried chicken good but a little dry / Sweet potato fries were good. 
Mashed potatoes were a buttery bomb - SO good.
Mac 'n Cheese a-okay.
Baked Beans, delish.
Sliders - ridiculously AMAZING

Asian food, just ok, not a lot of flavor and everything kind of tasted the same. 
The meats were tender though.
hot & sour was good and super spicy. 
Dim Sum kind of been sitting there for a bit - it was late.
Mango juice delish.

Deserts - Amazing. Loved the cheesecakes and mochi ice cream (green tea especially)

Bottom line, check was like $200 almost with a bottle of wine (not the best I've tasted but I didn't order it). Left very full but somewhat satisfied.

Abundant. Appetizing. Diverse. Dynamic. Mouth-watering. Beautiful Presentation of food that will leave you breathtaken by it! Hungry yet? 
It sure is a fantastic splendiferous gourmet international buffet with excellent food presentation and deliciousness that will blow your mind and unbelievably mouthwatering and a feast for the eyes, that is sinful to the point of bacchanalianism, (that is to go so driven, in drunken revelry, in excess, and wild). Bacchanal is openly decadent at $17 million extraordinarily modern 25,000 square feet venue which seats 600 with 9 open kitchens, more than 500 dishes daily by a team of master chefs in sleek contemporary atmosphere with sleek dinnerwares. Bacchanal in Caesars Palace which overlooks the world-famous Garden of the Gods pool oasis at Caesars Palace is contemporary excess to both mind, sight, and gastronomic senses! An extreme buffet!

 Here's my epicureanism picks from the buffet as evidenced in my photos...
From left - right, top line: tuna ahi poke (in round clay bowl), clams espresso (in mini-tin can), seafood ceviche (in square glass canister), oyster shooter (in a tall shooter glass), sweet potato tots (in mini frying rack), ice cold lemon water, iced tea.
On plate: carrot balls, grilled asparagus, spicy crab sushi, italian meatballs, chinese shumai, steamed lemon halibut, steamed salmon, roast duck, saffron arroz rojo, real mexican guacomole.... 
 And there were many more... 
Irresistible! these delectable desserts presented in cute-sy sized portions in which one would be mindful to their manners on how to eat such dainty presented desserts that resemble an art form!  Here's my favorites: pecan bar (with a stick of milk chocolate and a drop of dark chocolate as topping, as seen on an orange-colored square platter), key lime pie (with leaf-shaped chocolate as topping, as seen on a mint-colored square platter), chocolate creme brulee (in blue ramekin), fig and balsamic ice cream and watermelon and mint ice cream (both in white bowl), candied almonds: all yummmmy!! 
 
There were many more to have had but this brings to mind another, or a second or more visits. Why ever not? So should you. Expect a line or a wait to the venue. Or maybe shouldn't.; to leave a table for us who regularly loves partaking of the buffet every time we hunger bacchanalian style! Bacchanalian hungry yet?

The reason I'm giving this 4stars was only because we waited two hours to finally get seated. We went on a Saturday table for 2 around 3:30 registered put phone number so we could be notified via text when table was ready. Once we got the text we went to stand in line for about 45mins. Ok now the food is delicious there is so much food from all types Mexican Italian Chinese Mediterranean and more. I had about 3 plates of steamed crab and about two other plates of mix. The waitress came whenever my drinks were low and was on top of the plate pickup. My overall review of this place is if you've never been you must go and try it for yourself especially if you like Buffet style this is a prestige buffet. For my first time I loved it ate good feasted like a king.

I don't give a ton of 5 star reviews, but after a couple trips to this buffet, I gotta do it.  The cost is around $45, but the buffet is HUGE!  Not to mention that price includes UNLIMITED mimosas!  that is huge, because other buffets charge as much at $15-$20 per person for that upgrade.  We are talking crab legs, gourmet salads and cheeses, chicken and waffles, and almost anything else you could ask for!  My only gripe is that they didn't have fried shrimp either time I was there.  That is a favorite of mine, but it wasn't an issue.  The food is really great, I am not just saying that.  I used to think all the buffets taste the same and the Bacchanal buffet has changed my opinion and the game when it comes to buffets.  I love this buffet and I cannot wait to come back and go again!!!

First off, I'm a sucka for sweets. 

Bacchanal Buffet is as good as it gets (I have yet to try the buffet at the Bellagio). They have a huge variety! People often complain of the cost, but honestly, you're in Vegas... splurge! How often do you really cough up the money to eat at a nice buffet? We go to Vegas often enough and we still always splurge on a buffet or two (or three :p). The way to happiness will always be through your stomach! Bacchanal Buffet makes my stomach happy. The wait isn't too bad the day that we went, I believe it was for brunch. I read a lot of reviews beforehand so I was ready to face a parade of hangry starving people, nope. We even had the whole VIP thing where you check in and they give you a buzzer when your table is ready- just in case. Decent line that moved quickly. The staff were all professional, fast, and efficient. Whatever it is that your mouth desires, Bacchanal Buffet most likely serves it. Shoot, there were things I didn't even know my stomach needed until I saw it. Everything was scrumptious and looked appetizing. From the pastas, meats, SEAFOOD, soups... they all TASTED AMAAZZZIINGG. I was completely stuffed but this was MAN VS FOOD and I was not going to be beaten. 15lbs heavier I walked slowly (breathing heavily*) to the dessert station. Ohmysweetbabyjesus, the variety! I had to get assistance with carrying an extra plate so I could stay seated and sample each dessert that looked appealing (which was almost everything). The sweets were just perfect, I loved that nothing was too overwhelming. OH! The juice. That was some damn good fresh juice they had, YOU MUST TRY. Get fat, splurge. You don't do it often enough!

They deserve to be called the best buffet in vegas. Probably the only buffet that I consider to be worth the last penny! We came on a Saturday which is typically champagne brunch so a little pricey at $45/person. Nevertheless, my take is still way cheaper compared to going to a fancy steakhouse. The carving section had prime rib, beef brisket and hot links, and were all a hit. They also have a full-on mexican section, which I find unusual but the tacos and guac were spot on.  Great for kids because they have pizza, mac and cheese, and french fries, and they are not fast food quality. The desserts are phenomenal! Especially the caramel flan, green tea creme brulee and gelato. Since it's champagne brunch they serve champagne or mimosa but you could also get regular juices or soda. The servers are fast and friendly.  This buffet is quite a handul folks and there are too much postives about it.  The only negative I could think of is the big line and long wait (average 1 hour), but still not a deal breaker for me.

Best buffet in Vegas. Large range of selections. The milk bottle drink is very tasty. I really like the horchata and guava drink. The prime rib roasted perfectly at medium rare. Seafood - calms, mussel, king crab, snow crab leg, raw oyster, oyster shooter, and more. There's a noodle section where the chef cook the noodle when requested. The cheese and cure meat section offered pretty good selections. I am not a big dessert fan but their dessert selections was definitely a MUST TRY! I really like their lemon basil and mango habanero ice cream ! 

The wait time was 9 hrs long for thanksgiving. If you plan on eating here fir the holiday, please make sure you put your bane into their sign up system earlier on that day, like around 12pm... We ended up eating there the day after Thanksgiving and the estimate wait time was still 4 hrs. PLAN AHEAD!

3.5 but I'll go 3 because while I was full, for this price I could've eaten at Delmonico. I've never done the "Vegas buffet" thing and so I wanted to try it SOMEWHERE.

Price:
Lets be honest, its expensive. For 8 people they pre-charge 18% gratuity, which was $61. Total bill was over $400. Gratuity was not earned AT ALL.

"Service":
My drinks were never refilled. Dirty plates were ALWAYS left on the table. For $61 tip and you don't actually serve me or take my order, you better make sure I have unlimited iced tea. 

Food: 
It was a long wait just to get into the restaurant. Luckily you don't wait for food as long as stations are spaced out well. Dessert is the best station. Italian second best followed by American. Food was just mediocre generally. Another yelper said "a fest for the eyes but not for the stomach." I agree completely.

Shellfish:
I'm allergic to shellfish. There is shellfish available at almost every station and they are NOT really marked. For example, I couldn't eat anything at the chinese section because hidden throughout were tiny shrimp in almost everything. I believe you can ask the chefs to accommodate you but I didn't really want to deal with that. In terms of the seafood station: those in my party said the shrimp was rubbery. My sis in law actually spit hers into her napkin. However everyone loved the crab legs and probably ate their $40 worth in that. 

Ambiance:
I enjoyed the ambiance, table sizes and music.

I think it was a cool experience but I'd try another buffet or just go to a sit down place for the same price.
Amazing. The food was sooooo good. Went on Memorial Day weekend and pod extra ($25) to skip the line... Not sure if it's worth $90 but I'll definitely be back for $60!!

Still the bomb.  Been about 5 months since I've been here and was not disappointed. This time waited a really long time due to the sema car convention. 

Tried more asian flare this go around
The green beans were addict ing 
Porridge. Yes I said porridge yum with some thousand year old egg and spices. 
Didn't know they had this but sealed it for the wifey.  Boiled snow crab.  She loves crab but typically too salty at buffets. Well boiled was perfect i think she had 4 heaping plates. 
Potatoe something on the meat station. Wow
Even the clam bake which looked Derry but was tasty 

All and all worth the 50 bucks. 

Maybe because we had atleast 10 ice cream mochi as well.

My husband and I decided to check out Bacchanal Buffet during our first trip to Vegas. We had done our research and knew to arrive at that sweet spot between 2 and 3 to get the brunch price but the dinner food.

We had about a 45 minute or so wait to get seated. My first thought was where the heck to start because this buffet was insane. We walked around for a while just checking out options. Some of my favorites were the steamed crab legs, poke bowls, tacos, clam chowder soup (seems basic but it was so good), all the dumplings, and curry. I was so full by dessert time but did snag a chocolate covered strawberry, which was a perfect end. 

We definitely left feeling full and satisfied.

The best buffet in Vegas so far,  get the ticket at 5:00, just wait 10 min, you can get call to pay for dinner.
The food inside has variety choice and dish are just delicious, each portion is small that you don't need to worry that waste the extra food.
The crab leg was cut well, you can enjoy it easily, the oyster is fresh and sweet.
The dessert taste great, especially their Macaron, very chewy.
We will definitely come back if the rate still good next time.

In my eyes this place has to be the best buffet I've ever been too. The food was all very good, I mean everything!! The carving station served up a variety of meats which was cooked to perfection, the taco bar made some real street tacos, I mean I can go on and on about this place. When I'm here I feel like in feasting! Exactly how you should feel at a buffet. I definitely want to visit Vegas again just to come back here.

A good range of varieties, with so good presentations and welcoming staff. Overall worth the dollars and a must-try in Las Vegas.

Our personal favorite for brunch/dinner time are bone marrow, Pho soup, avocado toast, Asian pork belly & chashao. I'm not a big fan of their seafood. The crab legs, both raw and boiled are not very good quality, smelling very fishy. But their desserts are definitely the best! With so many choices and good executions, you should try all of their cute little desserts!

We've tried the Bacchanal Buffet and the food was bad considering the price. Food and desserts were both terrible, we felt that we wasted money.  There are better buffets in Vegas that are reasonably priced, such as The Buffet at the Wynn.  This was the first time at the Bacchanal and will be the last.

We chose/were directed here over Wicked Spoon and sampled plates from every station, with everything being fresh and available without much of a wait for weekday lunch. We found the lunch price worth it, but surprisingly couldn't see ourselves being buffet regulars if we visited more.

This place is definitely 5 stars if you ignore the wait and the price. I think this is one of the more expensive buffets I've been to, and it is not worth the price when you have to wait so long to pay for the buffet and then wait some more in line to get food. 

I've been to the buffet at two separate dinners on weekday evenings, first time the wait was about an hour, we paid the $15 fast pass. The second time the wait was half an hour, it was more manageable. 

Food was delicious, I love the seafood selections and most asian selections. I think it is one of the few buffets that does asian dishes right (except for sushi). They had very tasty congee, pork buns, lightly fried salt and pepper fish, and duck. 

The first time I went they had more adventurous ice cream flavors (savory), but I was very disappointed to see them disappear the second time I went. Crepe is always good, so I am happy.

Came on a Friday night around 5:30 pm and surprisingly, there was no wait. Was curious to know what the "best buffet" in Las Vegas was like and it was pretty good for a buffet. The main difference between this and a more standard buffet was the variety of food (500+dishes) offered, the presentation, and the atmosphere. There were tons of dishes to choose from such as shrimp, crab legs, ceviche, and crawfish. I love seafood so this was a big plus. There was also a carving station with turkey, prime rib, and brisket as well as lamb chops and pork belly on little plates. One of my favorites was the fried calamari presented in little fry baskets. The presentation of the salads was a nice touch. I also liked the desserts and thought the gelato bar was cool. There was Chinese (dim sum, jook), Mexican (taco bar), Italian (pastas) and Japanese (sushi) food, too.

I'd recommend going early to avoid the long lines which can be up to 1-2 hours long.

Ok, We already all know the food here is amazing, but has anyone mentioned the staff? 

Honestly, every time I go to a buffet in Vegas I feel like I am left on my own. Yes, I know that is the point, but where is my waiter half the time? Even then, I feel as if they are saying to themselves "Oh God, here is another round of people to stuff themselves". Bacchanal Buffet is different,  in so many ways. 

We came her after a very disappointing Saturday night delayed flight into Vegas for a Bachelorette party. We stayed up until 6am to make up for it.  We knew the wait would be long at Bacchanal, but just could not make it there until 12:30pm.

The hostess Erma told us to go get a time card from the machine. It printed out with a time to come back (kind of like a fast pass at Disneyland) for 3:15pm. We were so sad because the bottomless mimosa's on Sunday only go to 3:00pm and we had a whole itinerary planed for our soon to be bride. I went up to Erma to ask her if there was anything to be done. Seeing how we had a Bachelorette who's face was covered in crushed dreams, she asked to see my ticket.. and then allowed us to go in!! Erma you are the best :) 

The wait was a bit long to get to our table but once there our waiter Jeff and busser Vladamir took great care of us. Jeff was amazing. He kept our mimosa's full, and even played games with us to see who had had the most to drink. We loved his humor, attention to detail, and the fact that he never let us see the bottom of our mimosa glasses ;)

We also met the manager Wolf. We actually met him when trying to find Bacchanal inside Caesars. He kindly showed us the way and mentioned he worked there. Later in our brunch he came over to our table and asked us how everything was. Upon remembering us we began joking. We ended up having a nice little banter between our server Jeff, Wolf and our table. 

Jeff even brought an assortment of deserts from the buffet with a candle in it for our Bachelorette to blow out in a celebratory congratulations! 

The food here is amazing to say the least, but the staff behind it all is equally as satisfying. I know this review seems to have a lot of info about the staff, but they truly made our experience so fun! I want to thank you for making my friends Bachelorette brunch so memorable!!  

Seriously, ask for Erma, Jeff, Vladamir, and Wolf! They are amazing! 

Also.... get as many crabs legs as you can. They are super fresh!! :)

I typically hate buffets but all my cousins wanted to go to this one because it was the go-to brunch buffet in Vegas. After reading about this place on Yelp, we decided to try to get to the Buffet around 11 am so we could eat by noon. 

Since we had a group of six, we were brought over to a different line that was separated from the people with five or fewer people. From there we just had to wait to pay and then to be seated. For some reason, the hostess got nervous when we said we wanted to pay separately, but it seemed like we would be seated faster (we skipped a couple of groups in line) because my cousin put everything on her card, the buffett (with free mimosas and Champagne) came out to about $65 each.

We were seated in a booth - which was very nice because we couldn't really hear the others in the dining area and we were able to easily get in and out of our booth without disturbing anyone else. 

Now for the food:
I had about 5 mimosas and 4 plates of food.

I started off with a "breakfast" plate - which included red velvet cupcakes, chicken and waffle fries, hash browns, bacon, macaroni and cheese, squash, and a slider. 

My next plate was primarily from the Asain section - lo mein, spring rolls, chicken and other various noodles

My third plate included one taco, a iceburg blue cheese wedge salad (lunch items started appearing since we ate so long), more macaroni and cheese,  and more hashbrowns. 

For desserts I took a bunch of little things including - a pecan tart, creme brule, a strawberry eclair, strawberry short cake, gelato, and fudge.

I skipped over the seafood section and pizza section because I do not like seafood and....why eat pizza.

I was very impressed with how clean and tasty everything was and how quickly the plates were picked up. There was only one time I had to ask for additional champagne was towards the end of the meal.

Favorite and best buffet in Las Vegas!!! Love the steak and crabs!! I can just eat those 2 the entire day!!! Super worth your money trust me! And once you eat here! Other food in Vegas will taste so basic!!  Lots of amazing varieties! Super good food! Totally recommending!! I like it better than wicked spoon!

As a rule I loathe buffets. Our friends were in town and wanted to eat here. The price is high,the wait is long ( you get a pass that tells you when to come back, think Disneyland Fast Pass) and you feel like cattle waiting to get in. The place is very pretty but a little confusing to figure out where the different food stations are, and the plates are tucked away under the food areas. 
The food was very good,and many dishes were pre portioned into little plates/bowls. The wait for the seafood is very long,but people waited patiently in line. This is not your normal buffet, with people shoving in front and children running wild.
 The cod with miso was fabulous, and I loved the dim sum area,it's very tiny but very good. You can also get fresh Pho, ramen or udon soup,along with anything you could think of to add.
There is something for everyone here,from sushi to hot dogs,lamb to shrimp. The desserts are beautiful.macaroons to a dozen flavors of gelato and a made to order crêpe station.

The Bacchanal Buffet is the best buffet on the Vegas strip. The quality in food simply cannot be beat. Furthermore, they have a large selection to choose from, especially from the Asian cuisine. So, if you're looking for a buffet that has Asian food then this is your place. However, they do offer many other types of food. The only issue with this place is the horrible, horrible, HORRIBLE line.

Good buffet. Very cosmopolitan, with pretty authentic choices of various ethnic cuisines. Something for everyone here. Allow yourself a couple of hours for this one. Time to wait in line (we waited about 45 minutes), and also time to pace yourself at the dinner table. I'd go back, for sure, but I can only handle a buffet like this about once a year!
Large variety of average to slightly better than average foods for a steep price. Worth if your goal is to eat a few days worth of calories in a sitting.

It's a bit expensive compare to other Hotels. Especially when we went there for breakfast-brunch, it was about $90 for two. We paid $80 for buffet dinner for two at Wynn. Nevertheless, the food was delicious!  The cashier and our server was just okay. The gals working at the dessert bar were very friendly!
Yum!!!  Everything that I had was very good.  Went for dinner mid-week.  Love the mini portions.  Although a little pricey, I'm finding if you want good food you're gonna pay for it.

Gorgeous renovation of the old buffet that used to be here. Pricier than most in Las Vegas, but by far the nicest. There's so much to choose from and something for everyone. They even have sugar free options at the dessert bar which is great to include. Great service and very comfortable seating.

The 6 1/2 hour wait for the golden ticket into this place is a little intimidating, but go in and sign up at their kiosk  then head out on the strip for some fun and come back.  
I think that I ate like $25 worth of macaroons ( the green pistachio flavor is heaven), so that helped make up for the fact that some of the fun specialty items that I was looking forward to trying (watermelon salad and King crab legs etc.) but were not available. Some of the dishes were over the top awesome!  There was a creamy baked polenta with mushrooms and truffle oil that was to die for and the desert area is absolutely amazing!

This is the best looking and best laid-out buffet on the strip. The food was uniformly good. I gave only four stars because it is more expensive than all the other buffets, and I thought the Bellagio's food was slightly better.

Best buffet in Vegas! Their selection is huge! Their plating, food presentations are great. Food is excellent!!! I have a sweet tooth so I loved their dessert section. So many choices! The ambience is really nice. Worth every penny!

The wait was a bit long, so always go a bit earlier so that you won't be starving in line.

The food was delicious, pretty reasonably priced considering the amount of seafood was available (crab legs, oyster shooters, shrimp).

Definitely a fun experience, and something you must try while in Vegas!

Ok..so the food really deserves a 3.5 or 4 star for a buffet.
BUT.....bait and switch alert people.  BAIT AND SWITCH.

Ok...I came here about a month after opening for a Yelp Elite event.  It was free.  It was glorious.  Now it's chalk full of problems.
1) No Monta ramen.  For tourists, this is a local ramen joint that is very popular with the foodies.  They hired someone from there to help them with their ramen.  It was close to the real deal.  Last night?  Gone gone gone.  At the Yelp event, they even had the head buffet chef walking around bragging about how much trouble they were to for the ramen.  I believe him.  So what happened?  Good thing I didn't pay $50 for this buffet expecting this ramen.  Oh wait...$50 it was!
2) Whoever manages this buffet needs a demotion, stat.  At even the premium buffets in town you expect to wait for seafood.  Crab legs, etc.  Mostly the crab legs take a lot of work and it's a bottleneck.  Fine.  
At Bacchanal, they had combined the seafood and carving station lines into one, gigantic line.  GIGANTIC. Moved slower than molasses in the winter, too.  Not only did that make carving station only patrons wait a VERY LONG time for some meats that were ready to go, the long line obscured about 25% of the buffet's offerings.  And most of the "good stuff" if we're being honest.  Basically, if you wanted fried chicken, or any of the potatoes, any bread, a whole host of things - you had to squeeze your way in between the dirty looks of people who thought you might be cutting in line.  How's about separating the lines?  Oh wait...they DID end up separating.  After I complained to a manager and was told, I'm not kidding, "Just go ahead and walk up to the carving station and ask for what you need.  Just bypass the line."  Whatchu talkin' bout Willis?! Despite my misgivings,  I tried that assuming the people were all in line for seafood.  They weren't.  I almost got murdered by the people in line. 
Only my cat like reflexes saved me.  
Also, they had 1 chef at the carving station - all the while a huge line was continuing to build.  Here's a hint - have another person there carving while another person takes orders and serves it up?  The lady in front of me literally took, and I timed this, 3 minutes to get 3 different kinds of meat.  With like 30 people behind her and growing.  The line is long and the meat is not going to sit there more than a minute if you cut it early.  It's already rested - it's fine!  Good thing I didn't pay $50 for this buffet.  Oh wait...I did!
When I went before, they obviously had separate lines.  It took ME to get them to separate it despite the seriously angry patrons.  And no surprise things went much smoother afterwards.  Hey Caesars Palace - where's my paycheck? I managed your buffet for one night, Gary Loveman(CEO of Caesars).
3) No fresh fruit except for blackberries.  They used to have great chocolate covered strawberries.  We were told they had been out since 2 days ago.  Thank God I didn't pay something outrageous like $50 for this buffet only to have them run out of the most popular fruit in existence.  Oh wait...I did pay $50.  F$#k me!  Great I'll get some rasberries.  No?  No rasberries either?  Well...we are in the desert.  At least I didn't pay....
4) Dishes at the table took a good long while to be cleared.  Not the biggest deal in the world - but when your table is full it does get a big messy.
On the positives:
1) For our group, we paid $15 extra each to skip the line to get in.  Well worth it if you're willing to shell out the $15.  Looked like at least an hour wait if not more.  Wish other places would have that option.
2) The carving station meats were pretty good.  Sausage was spicy and delicious.  BBQ ribs were tender and flavorful.  And the ribeye was solid.  The brisket, however, was awful. Dry as a bone and really overcooked.
3) Desserts were nice.  I didn't eat much but the Kona Coffee mochi was very very good.  One of my friends had a crepe and she thought it was one of the best she's had.  So big thumbs up for the dessert stations.  Oh yeah..and no wait.  haha
4) Temperature was fine in the buffet.  Also, no fire, flood, nuclear explosion, etc.  Hmm....struggling to think of things to come up with in this section.  No terrorists!

In a nutshell, if you're already at Caesars and $50 isn't a ton of cash for you to spend then go for it.  It's perfectly fine.

If you're making a special trip to a buffet then I'd recommend Bellagio or Wynn over this one.  

Just disappointing to see them pull out all the stops initially to generate that good publicity.  Then just bend you over and stick it in rough like this.  It's brutal.  Really, I should give this kind of crap the 1 star treatment.  You know what?  I will.  Dropping to 1 star. 

Honestly pays.  Dishonesty shouldn't.  John H. OUT!!

Edit: Let me add one thing. Bleu cheese dressing constantly gets stuck in opening of hard plastic bottle. Can't squeeze it.  Thus, it's unusable. LOL?

Let me start off by saying how much I dislike buffets. My mom is a fan and I know Vegas has some of the best buffets around (this being one of them) so I said we should give it a try. 

First things first - Caesars, you are one of the most stunning casinos, but why must your signage be so terrible? We asked probably 7 people where this buffet was before we finally found it. It was worth the chaos though. I will warn you that there will be a line at dinner time. We didn't get there until about after 8 and it was a good 30 minutes. 

I can't say I have ever seen a buffet this large in my life. They really do have something for everyone. If you want seafood its there, bbq, italian, asian, mexican, you name it they had it. I don't eat a lot so it was a bit overwhelming and I definitely didn't eat $65 worth in food but I would do it again! One of my favorite things was the clam chowder and pork dumplings.

It may be very expensive ($40+ for dinner, I think?) but it's the best buffet I've tried. There's an endless amount of items and no matter how hungry I am I never really feel like I've gotten my money's worth. As with all buffets, some items are hit or miss. On less busy nights dishes sit out longer than others and become cold and hard.

The meatballs were great, the lamb was good, ribs had a rub with a rub made from a great blend of spices.The yellow curry chicken and barbequed Asian meats were delicious. The sushi, as at all buffets, should be avoided.

Desserts are always the main draw for me, and theirs doesn't disappoint. The chocolate lava cake actually had a liquid center. The Oreo mousse and pecan tart were excellent compared to typical buffet quality dishes. Gelato flavors are diverse. The strawberry cheesecake was my favorite out of the ones I've tried.

Again, it's expensive and if you're looking for a quality meal you'd be better off going to a regular restaurant. But, if you're looking for variety and just want to stuff your face silly, this is the buffet to go to.

Lines are always long, but they have a kiosk system where you can check in and they'll text you when it's time to come back. Although when you do line up, you still have to wait in line to pay and to be seated.

4.5 Stars
Nothing is worth 4 hours wait....what a chaotic experience!!! Why put yourself through the circus???

Visited on a Friday afternoon in the off-season at approximately 3pm, no wait and it's a better price before dinner at $39.99 + tax and tip (and honestly I ate so much I couldn't eat until the next morning so it was a good deal). 

There is SO MUCH variety here, it was actually possible to lose your table while you're wandering around and trying to take in all the various options. Favourite were the warm alaskan crab legs, truffle gnocchi pasta, the prime rib was pretty good, CURLY FRIES (I'm a sucker for carbs), and two of the ceviches in the ceviche station. 

There were so many stations that just when I thought there couldn't be more I discovered the chinese food section at the back with dim sum and others. I noticed that dessert had made to order crepes but I didn't get a chance to try them. Pretty sure there was also a made to order noodle/pasta section that I skipped over too. 

Service was attentive and we received our drinks almost immediately after being seated, but it was the off-season and also an off-dining time. 

Solid 3.5 stars for service and variety of food, but nothing outstanding that would draw me back here as I prefer restaurants to buffets.

The best buffet in Las Vegas. I came here every time when I stay in town, love the variety they offer, everything from seafood to soul food and on a top shelf quality. The ambiance is always great here. The staff is courteous and helpful. The dining area and food areas are always clean.

I absolutely love this place. Hands down currently the best buffet in Vegas.

I used to love the buffet at the Bellagio but their's seems to have gone downhill over the years. Bacchanal is where it's at! Everything is fresh and yummy. The dishes are sometimes not what you'd expect for a buffet but are very well prepared. And snow crabs. Lots of snow crabs.

Definitely go before you think you might be hungry!! There's almost always a long wait here. You go to the check-in systems to put your name on the waiting list. You provide your cell phone number and you are sent a text when you are ready to be added to the line. Yup, they call you to let you know when to get in line THEN you pay and then are waiting to be taken to your table. If possible, make reservations for larger parties ahead of time!

I wish I was back there again.

Hands down, one of the best buffet experiences I've had. 

I think I ate my body weight in crab legs. The line was always flowing, and there's a person standing right there behind the counter, constantly refilling so there's never a lack. He was my hero.

The Chinese food section was surprisingly tasty, although I merely tasted a few selections. I was focusing my night on seafood and meats, but I enjoyed most of everything I grabbed.

The only disappointments were the wait to get in - over an hour (yes, it was soooo long), the table next to us got way more drink service and attention than we did, and although the desserts are extremely pretty, nothing really stood out as having amazing flavor and as something I'd go back for a second time.

One of the best brunch buffets my husband and I have been to. We had a Groupon too!! #win 

We saw different types of individual foods/desserts, that no where else has. (See photos) Some were cute! Of course, I didn't have time to take photos of all, but I guarantee this is the place to go to for brunch next time you visit, not just because the food was cute, but of course it was delicious! It was nice that the waitress was helpful too. 

The buffet space is quite big, because when you turn a corner, there's some other type of food. I was getting lost. LOL

Servers are on point with cleaning up the tables, and very good service!

You just have to try this place for yourself. Enjoy :)

I think it is overated. My boyfriend tried to talk me out of it because with $120 we can get ourselves a full course of meal with wine at some nice restaurants, but I haven't been there and there are so many good reviews on Yelp so I have to try. I'm a big fan of seafood, but the seafood there are nothing special. I can get that at Tomi buffet  for half of the price (if you live in San Jose, Ca, you know what I'm talking about.) The sushi section is very limited and their side dishes such as pork belly are too salty and hard. The dissert section is good but not great. I viewed a lot of pictures on Yelp before eating at this restaurant. The pictures of the food looked so good but the reality is far from it. This is just my opinion but here are a few highlights:

unlimited soft drinks and tea included with meal purchase
Flan cake
Mango pudding
Shrimp cocktail
Crab legs (Asian cuisine section)

We had our second visit to this buffet on 1/24/2018.  I cannot compliment the staff there enough for going above and beyond with a situation we had with a dish that wasn't up to the quality of this restaurant.  The manager Raz was very apologetic and insistent on making it up to us.  Even after telling him we didn't want anything in return, just that they take the dish off the line and make a new batch, he went above and beyond and had one of the chefs bring out a giant plate of king crab (not normally served on the buffet) and came back to check on us a couple of times.  Our table attendants Martha and Mahyar also went above and beyond with making sure we were enjoying our visit.  When it came time for dessert, Mahyar insisted on having the dessert bar staff make us a special crepe just the way he loved them.  And he was right, it was amazing.

From my check list this one is on the top!!!! At least one time you have to go and if you are in a group even better because had 500 dishes so I'm pretty sure everyone will leave full and happy the price make sense because the amount of good food and desert justify the crab legs were really good. The mini doughnuts are fresh and tasty

I got the Groupon for Brunch which came with mimosa. I was excited about trying this buffet since I've hear it's one of the best. Overall, I think this buffet offered a lot of variety, but I didn't think it offered a lot of fresh foods although I came during lunch. The southern foods like mash potatoes, mac and cheese, eggs and hash browns were pretty good. I really enjoyed the crab too. Customer service was really good. I was definitely really satisfied after the meal.

One thing I didn't like was that before we went in, they asked to take a picture of us. And then someone comes by to sell the picture for $20. It kind of ruins the dining experience because why?? Thus, if you walk in and they ask to take a picture of you, just say no.

Wow this buffet had everything. Definitely on the bucket list for anyone. It is expensive if you've got a big family like mine. The bill was around $600 but we figured we weren't going to be back in a while so why the hell not. Well they certainly don't disappoint. Seafood and prime rib galore. They even took portraits while you waited in line which I thought was funny. Alright alright you got me. I did buy the pic lol. 

Anyways if you're in Vegas, you gotta try this place and cross it off your list!

Get stuffed!!!!
Go for dinner! There is everything and anything you can imagine!!! service is incredible, as well as quality of food! The Pho, Lamb, and King Crab legs are a hit!

Yes, it's pricey but totally worth the money. This has been the first Buffet that everything tasted great. I was floored by how tasty the sushi was (I had a plateful). I loved the Mexican Juices, I drank my Horchata so fast! The desserts were perfection (minus the red velvet whoopie pie: I don't know what happened here). It was 35$ for Lunch, but really really tasty. Can't wait to try them for Dinner.

I'll be honest:  I wasn't too thrilled about eating at a buffet during my Vegas vacation earlier this month.  I didn't want to eat anywhere that quite possibly had little kids sticking their fingers into the chocolate fountain (hello, Golden Corral).  But my husband really wanted to check it out, and he was paying, so what could I really do about it?

Turns out, this is a very nice, well thought out buffet.  Much better than any buffet I'd ever been to.  Granted, the price for lunch was almost $40 a person, so I wouldn't expect (or shouldn't expect) anything less than stellar.  But the variety was what made this buffet so awesome.  You have your standards, but there are also several international stations, like Japanese, Italian, Indian, etc.  I'm putting dim sum on the same plate as my polenta, mashed potatoes next to a bowl of chicken chile stew.  There's seafood, sushi, eggs benedict, with chicken and waffles and a large array of assorted desserts and gelatos.  It truly is an amazing buffet, in variety especially. There would be something here for everyone.

Food was very tasty.  Cleanliness was top notch.  Even the speed with which we went through the long line was pretty decent.  So despite my unwillingness to go to a buffet restaurant on my vacation, I'd have to say since I had to go, I'm glad it was this one.

Don't believe the hype. I think this place is overrated, overpriced, and not worth the money. Two people would roughly cost almost $80. The selection here is no where near wicked spoon. Go elsewhere like to the cosmopolitan. I would even rank some other buffets way better than this one off the strip.

For buffet fans, this is the world series. We got the buffet groupon. Well worth it. I had 7.5 plates. 
American, seafood, Japanese, mexican, Chinese, Italian, desserts, meat and cheese section, aged wagu beef. It had everything.
Comida muito boa, recepção boa. Só não recomendo adicionar bebida pois o atendimento é péssimo.

This buffet is really nice and really clean. I don't really understand the long line, for what I've tasted, it wasn't that special. 

The seating is really nice and classy, the food separated by type. There is a dessert bar, a juice section, a sushi section, and a cold seafood section. (I'm only laying out the important parts for ya ;] ). There are tender, juicy cut meats, and hot and cold crab legs. 

Overall, what I tasted was very average, the M's buffet is so much better :/ I really thought the dessert bar was going to be so great--it wasn't. The gelato is!! Too bad it's not homemade lol. My waitress only refilled my water once. It was just a weird experience after waiting so long..
This is by far my favorite buffet in Vegas the wait is long but worth it. Also the staff is friendly. Dinner is the busiest time so expect to wait up to 2hrs.

I REALLY want to give this place more stars, but I just can't. We first came here two years ago when my husband and I got married. We had a fairly large group and our kids enjoyed it mostly because of the spectacular desert bar. I thought it was "ok". It's impressive to look at, but the food was just so-so; mainly because the hot items were barely lukewarm. I also wasn't impressed by the prime rib which was difficult to cut. I decided to give it another try this March and had the same experience, except two years ago there was quite a wait to get in, and this time there was no wait. Maybe it's because we were there for lunch both times? Still, at $40 a person, I expect food that hasn't been sitting out so long. I also don't care for the fact that the staff act like they really hate their jobs. Unfortunately, that's pretty typical in Vegas, though.  It's a fun place to go once, but after two times I think I've had my fill.  If this were a $20 meal I would give it three or four stars, but the food and service just isn't worth $40.
I come here every year during Rugby 7's and I absolutely LOVE the Seafood! Well worth the price!

Love this buffet! I always bring my daughter and granddaughter. We love everything, but especially the lamb chops and cheeses and salads! My granddaughter loves the Asian selection and my daughter loves the Mexican spread!

MY FIRST LAS VEGAS BUFFET!!

Bacchanal Buffet is located in the Caesars Palace on the Vegas strip. It cost about $37 per person for lunch (11am-3pm).

Talk about a place that has everything. I'm not sure how much they change up the buffet here since this was my first time, but we came here for lunch and wow the spread was impressive.
 
The Grub. (from what I can remember)
- Chinese Dim Sum
- Chinese Jook
- Sushi
- Pasta
- Pizza
- Tacos
- Mac & Cheese
- Cheese station!
- Chicken and Waffles 
- Fresh Seafood (crab, oysters, etc)
- Omelets and Eggs Benedict (probably left overs from breakfast)
- Prime Rib, Ribs, Meat, Meat, Meat!

The Dessert.
WHAT A SELECTION OF DELISH GOODNESS! They had all the desserts you could think of. They even had a fresh crepe stations, made to order!

With$57.99 price + food, it is not exceptionally good, so then I only can give 2 stars. Compared to the buffets in LA, it is almost the same, but LA buffet price is lower. The only good thing to eat there is their fresh crab. The chairs that we sat on were not comfortable, so without a comfortable chair you can't really enjoy your meal.

What a waste of money.  We came here last year and the food was so much better!  And they had lots of different foods, the food was in cute little portion, it was so good and look amazing too! I've been looking forward to coming back to vegas for this buffet, but I am extremely disappointed. This year we come here with family of 5 for lunch spent $200 and the food wasn't good! Just like a regular buffet anywhere else. My husband ate about $5 worth of food.

It's awesome. About $38 for lunch and $60 for dinner. There is fresh food constantly being made. My husband took me here and now I'm in love with the variety of food. There is a 2hour max time limit that you can eat for dinner. I reached that max with a couple of friends chatting at dinner over the desserts and coffee...it's easy to do. There is a desert island (huge) and food from all over the world. Lovely.

This is by far the best buffet I've come to in Vegas and best buffet I've ever been to period! Awesome selection of items, I suggest sharing portions with someone to get the opportunity to sample as many of the numerous dishes they serve. My favorite is their lobster bisque. It's the best I've ever had. Sadly it appears to be seasonal because I've had it on two occasions in the winter and found it wasn't there in the spring. Perhaps they just continue to offer different entrees and this one had it's run. Nevertheless prepare to wait if you go during peak dinner time especially if you are in a group. I recommend going very early for their dinner time to avoid the lones. We've waited as long as an hour and a half to eat here during peak time so be prepared!
Great food! Great service! Vanessa was especially helpful and friendly to make our dining experience even better.

If you want a true Vegas dining experience, this is the place to go! They have everything you could imagine from seafood, meat, Asian, Italian, Mexican cuisine and so much more. Their desserts are beautifully created and taste even better. 

I strongly recommend getting the king crab legs. The beauty of it is that they save you the hassle of fighting with your food by cutting it for you to chow down and enjoy. They also have stone crabs, Dungeness crabs and more. Prepared to get messy. I recommend going on a empty stomach so you can really sample everything they have to offer.

I been here many many times. It's either a hit or miss. The food is either great or what the hell. 

Very wide selections on the food and our services wasn't bad. Was a little bit of a prick after we passed our two hour mark and he wanted his tips, but everything else was great.

Food was good. Definitely a must to come here for their crab legs.
Slightly on the pricier side.
However service was prompt
They have a lot of selections to choose from.
The ambience here is phenomenal as it takes you back to the roots.
Would definitely come back if there was more availability of their lunch menu into their dinner menu.
Staff was very pleasant to deal with and they even remembered us from last time which is great knowing you are being acknowledged

My Vegas buffet days are long past me but somehow I still ended up here for a bachelor party a few weeks ago.  After being appalled by the $60 price tag and feeling like I wasn't all that hungry to start with, I still did everything I could to muster up the strength to stuff every part of my stomach.  Impossible here.  There is so much freaking food from every part of the world and it's all good.  My favorite was the coconut ceviche.  Hands down, best Vegas buffet I've been to and made me want to relive my eat til I drop days.

As buffets go bacchanal would be hard to beat. The food was good and of course plentiful. I especially liked the cheese station. Deserts were good. 

The biggest downside is the eternal wait to get in.

You do not pay for what you get l. Extremely long lines to pay to wait longer to sit
 Long line for food and not a huge selection. It is a huge time investment. My server got me my drink after sitting for 20 minutes and 1 plate deep. Finished my tea and never got a refill. For 60$$$ there are better ways of spending your time and money.

Regardless of what the food will taste like. I paid $15 extra per person for a party of 3 to skip the line & currently waiting in a line. That's $45 that I'll never get back. 

Here's a tip, just wait in line next time & don't waste money on the expedited line charge. It will save you time compared to waiting, but was it worth $15 extra. Absolutely not.

I'll do a follow up review for food up next.

Just sat down. First off, customer service is excellent without a doubt. Keep in mind, I'm not paying the $30 price for this buffet, more like $45, so my expectations were already heightened. 

The food is good, along with the variety, but freshness was lacking. Their Seabass dish wasn't tender & really tasted old, but still tasted good, but not as fresh(as in cooked) as it could be. The best tasting thing was their truffled potatoes. Lots of desert options which also another plus!

The food is more like a $20 range buffet & not even close to the $45 that I paid. 

I came here because "USA Today" rated it as the best Buffet. Now I don't think I'll trust USA Today anymore

Great quality food and excellent care in preparation and presentation. I'm not a frequent buffet person, so this exception was well worth it. The crab legs were wonderful. We enjoyed a little taste of so many wonderful foods. Great fun & we enjoyed the bottomless mimosas too - keep them coming!

I honestly wasn't that impressed until I started eating. The dishes aren't anything out of the ordinary but the ingredients tasted so incredibly fresh. I definitely noticed the difference between this and other buffets. I had made to order pasta, it was a very good sized portion with delicious fresh roasted mushrooms and a very tasty sausage. Even simple things like mashed potatoes and steamed crab legs tasted very fresh. Nothing tasted previously frozen or processed. Some of the baked desserts were served warm, just heavenly...

There sure is a lot to like at Bacchanal.  The hot sweet potato puffs in individual baskets, lamb chops, smoked brisket, corn and lobster bisque, Kobe beef sliders, and shrimp with grits were among my favorites, not to mention the exceptional dessert selection that topped off  a (ahem) bacchanalian feast, straining the elastic waist on the pants I thoughtfully donned for the occasion.

There was so much more that I didn't get to try.  Who in their right mind could partake of all 500+ items and still live to write about it?  I'm not normally a huge eater, so this selection boggled my mind.  

I didn't like some of the things I tried, such as the Chile Verde, which I normally love; here it was too spicy, the pork was way too fatty, and the sauce tasted bitter.  There was a Mexican concoction that one of our friends was eating, but when I went to get some for myself, it had been replaced by something else.  Oh well, I think I managed to stuff my face pretty well without it.

I'm not crazy about the cold stainless steel ambience, which to me is completely devoid of charm.  I also was impatient with the long line at the seafood section, which was held up by the people waiting for their crab legs to be steamed.  By the time I realized I could cut the line to take the couple of shrimp I was waiting to get, I had already eaten too many of the sweet potato puffs from the basket I grabbed at the beginning of the line.

Our waiter was the most attentive and helpful of any buffet we've ever eaten at, as was the hostess, who explained the setup and told us about the "other" side of the buffet, which we easily could have missed, since we were seated near the desserts.

I can't say this is my favorite buffet in Vegas, but it definitely is worth the price of admission, especially if you have a big appetite.

Came here on Easter Sunday & cost factor was pretty high thus the 4 star rating ($151 for 2).  I guess it was for the special dinner.  Otherwise the food was great from crab legs to Asian foods.  The best part was the desserts.  I loved their cheesecake pops and gelato!  I would go again during a normal day.

Starting to go downhill.

2nd visit in May 2014, one of the hosts was really rude to us.  As was one of the cooks at the meat carving station.

3rd visit in June 2014 someone needs to regulate the lines.  and the food wasn't as good.  the meat was terrible.  brisket seasoning was subpar.  and the prime rib was really dry.

Pho, Tacos, Sliders, Crab Legs, Beef Chow Fun were all good.
Best buffet ever!!! We've lived in Vegas for 10 years and have made the rounds of buffets.  Although we've moves away for about 11 years now, this buffet is still topnotch in our books.

This place did not disappoint, I have to say one of the best buffets I've ever had and I'm not a big fan of buffets. Two types of king crab legs, cold and ones that are freshly boiled. Great selection of food from Italian, Asian, and desserts. Go there for brunch and get never ending Bloody Mary or mimosas. They also have an amazing juice bar with flavors ranging from mango, tamarind, hisbiscus, etc.

This is so much better than the buffet at the Wynn.

Extremely underwhelmed by the food. I was expecting better but the food was mediocre and some of the food wasn't warm, just room temperature. It was definitely a disappointment for me. It wasn't bad, just wasn't good. Had better buffets.

Food quality was inconsistent, slow service, long lines at seafood and carving station, and poor value for price paid.  Some things were great: lamb chops, street tacos, and seafood little plates.  The cooking staff behind the lines were just bothered at times.  The music at 3pm was a distracting clubby trance.  The whole experience did not live up to the hype.  It just seemed this buffet was trying too hard to be hip and cool, at the expense of providing a consistent quality product.

The M Resort, The Wynn, and The Cosmopolitan buffets are much better quality and value.

Look at the ratings for the Bacchanal Buffet and you will see why they are the best in the strip. There is so much to try that I never had the same thing twice.  Keep up the standards we will be back on our next trip.

The servers are very rude the long line ruins everything but honestly doesn't worth The time the food is OK but it does not work to wait 2 1/2 hours in line and then deal with employees that give have a  attitude The crab legs are OK but like I said it does not work 2 1/2 hour wait The Wynn buffet is better

oh em gee!! From now on I'm returning to this buffet every time I visit Vegas, and I don't like buffets! Steamed King crab, shrimp, the best gelato I've ever had! Sushi, Mexican food, dim sum, etc. Food was delicious! $60 for lunch, worth every penny. Thank you Bacchanal Buffet

Amazing selection of high quality foods. Four hour wait which was tough. Save yourself time by going to the kiosk 3-4 hrs before the actual time you want to eat there. Bill was $128 for two ppl at dinner which was rough. Worth the experience. Food is unparalleled but will likely get a similar dining experience de at the bellagio and wynn.

food is dry and old as i've come to expect from any buffet, so this may not apply to the average buffet goer. i'm also here on a tuesday evening. the only thing that might put this over other buffets that i've been to outside of vegas is the wider selection of food.

One of the best buffets in Vegas next to the Wicked Spoon. After having been to both, I think they are neck in neck. It's pretty pricey, but pretty worth it. We went here for both breakfast and lunch. I had some mini red velvet pancakes, eggs benedict, lobster egg benedict. There was also a taco bar and a juice bar with tons of auga fresca and horchata in small bottles. I had to try one of each flavor, but only managed going through the pineapple, guava, and cucumber. They also had pozole! The coffee they served was okay. Lots of yummy fruit like honeydew melon, cantalope, and watermelon. I had an orzo with scallops dish and a coconut curry mussels dish that I loved - probably my favorite savory dishes here. Sweet potato tots and mac n cheese were okay. The shrimp cocktail was meh. I liked the seafood ceviche, which had nice bits of scallop.  For dessert, I had a bunch of mousses and cakes. I had a coconut sago, which was my favorite dessert here. The panna cotta was not bad, a little too hard. In the end, I also had a small plate of assorted charcuterie meats and cheeses - good stuff like Cypress Grove Humboldt Fog and Cowgirl Sidekick.

Overhyped buffet with unimaginably long lines just to get in then to get food, then to find out that the food is just okay food, and service was lackluster. For $55/person for Saturday brunch, you really expect a lot better. You're better off taking your $55 somewhere else to get better food and not gorge.

The steamed crab legs in the back are way better than those that are already sliced open in the front. The pre-sliced legs are likely easier for dipping in butter but it was flavorless on its own-- likely lost to boiling/steaming. Just go a little farther back near the salad/Asian section and get much more impressive and tasty snow crab legs.

The carving station, seafood hot bar, and oysters were arguably the only worthwhile items in this buffet. Note that the wagyu beef is overcooked but tri-tips are delish. Load up on those and top off your Vegas-style excess with some powdered sugar crepe. You'll have completed the gorging portion of Vegas at the completion of your visit. Please prepare in advance to have someone roll you out after attempting to get your money's worth.

This buffet definitely live up to its hype! Everything that they serve was delicious! The staffs were mostly very friendly and helpful except for the guy that serve at the carving station, he was the opposite of friendly.

My friends and I came here on our last day in Vegas and decided to go around 2PM on Monday purely because we were tired and couldn't get out of bed until noon. Little did we know that we had hit the jackpot with our incredible timing! We waited for barely 10 minutes before we were seated and the selection of lunch buffet food was decent. However, at 3PM they started switching up all the food into the more expensive dinner items so we got super lucky and basically got to eat a bunch of different things all for the lunch pricing. 

I really liked the shrimp cocktail, lasagna and tortellini dishes in the Italian section and the made-to-order udon was good too. The prime rib and mashed potatoes with gravy was probably my winner of the night though! The Alaskan king crab was also delicious and we preferred the hot steamed ones instead of the frozen ones. Keep in mind that at lunch time, they only had Dungeness crab while the Snow crab + Alaskan King crab come out after 3PM.

For dessert, the hazelnut gelato was delicious paired with the Nutella crepe. There were some lacklustre dishes (e.g. the sushi & pizza) but still a good selection of yummy things to make me want to come back again. It was also super worth it to pay $43 (including tax) for lunch and get to eat both the lunch + dinner buffets!

Oh my can't rave enough it's the absolute best buffet in Las Vegas. Let's start with the staff our waitress was the nicest lady she went out of her way to bring different juices for us to try and they were fantastic. The cheeses were out of this world true gourmet. The crapes were custom made so save room you don't want to miss them. 
Steak, Prim rib chicken everything can't stop thinking how amazing the food was thinking I'll be back soon
Amazing food. Lots of  choices. A little bit of everything. I love it here. Favorite buffet of all time. Try it. You won't be disappointed.

This buffet was the one of two buffets I had on my must go to list while I visited Vegas (other being Wicked Spoon). We ended up going around 1pm which made the price for each person $35.99.  The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The waitress called me by name (since I paid) for the entire meal and even asked my friend her name.

There are seven different sections including seafood, sushi, breads, cheeses, tacos, meats and even fresh juices. They also have a separate bar for desserts including gelato. The food was delicious. The standout for me was the sweet potato tots. The desserts were so amazing and were my favorite part as I am a sugar lover. I would recommend this buffet, especially if you can make an earlier time so it will be the lowest cost. The price was the only downfall for me, besides the bathroom being up the entrance making you walk all the way out of the buffet to use it.

The very best buffet in LV. No question. worth extra money! 
Definitely will come back for lamb chop.

YES! I just may come back just for this buffet. The meat station was unbelievable. My favorite was the lamb chops & the pork belly with lentils. But the HOT crab legs were dream worthy. The Asian station had so much to offer I need to go back just to try everything there. I didn't have room for 3/4 of the what they had to offer but I made room for dessert. 
Price: $52 per person
Includes Mimosas & Whatever other beverage you would like
And it was all so worth it! I ate about $80 in crab legs alone. Worth every penny!

This is my favorite Buffet In Vegas !!! It is by far the Best in quality and selection. I'm always satisfied in so many ways, from the freshness of the seafood to the orgasmic decadent desserts !! I have been coming to this amazing place for years, customer service is the best. The waiter I met on my first experience still remembers me and greets me with the greatest energy and welcoming smile. Alvaro always has the most entertaining stories of his travels. Makes me enjoy my Buffet experience even more. Don't pass up the opportunity to try,  (in my opinion) the best meal in a Buffet style you'll ever experience !!! 

Laura Dietz

It was about $60/person after tax for dinner. So for that price, I don't think it was worth it.

Good things to eat:
-Brisket (if you get a good cut)
-prime rib
-lamb chop (again if you get a good cut)
-sushi
-tacos
-chocolate lava cake at desert station

Desert station looks amazing but it really sucks. Everything is really sweet and really blend.

I have been to way better buffet in Japan for $20. I would not go back to this place again.
I came here a couple times for lunch and dinner.  Didn't like the lunch buffet much but the dinner was good.  I would come back if the line is not too long.

Have been here twice, first time was during weekday lunch, price are reasonable and food has lots to choose from! Oysters, hot dishes, dimsum, ramen, pizza, pasta, guacamole, tons of dessert. It's under 25/person! Food taste in general very delicious, I was very satisfied! Second time came on a Sunday. It was their Sunday brunch, unlimited champaign and mimosa, I am not a big drinker and I could do without it. The food is still very good, and added the crab leg. Crab leg is very fresh and tasty compare to other buffets I have been to in vegas. It was 50/person

But I would prefer just to come during weekday.. I could do without the crab leg and mimosa.

We went as a party of 8 (which means they add on a tip so your server is not tempted to attend to your table as much as if they knew they had to earn it, however, she did an ok job).  We all thought the food was average and definitely not worth the amount paid!  Some of the meat was dry.  The brisket was good.  The lamb was so dry.  You can't even make your own salads, they are pre made in tiny little servings.  The desserts were good.  But, for the price I would say the food wan't that amazing and we wish we didn't go.

This buffet is best for an early pre-show dinner. Go at 5pm on a weeknight and you won't even have to wait on the line so many people have complained about. We walked right in. The wagu beef sliders and crab legs were my favorite. You can stick to a large quantity of a select few high end items for which you would have to pay much more elsewhere or try a range of things - they really have most of the major cuisines covered. For only $49pp, its still one of the best buffets on the Strip!

Went for the holiday menu on December 24th, tried checking in at 4pm to be met with a 253 minute wait just to get back in line. Decided to come back the next day Christmas morning 10am. MUCH better line but menu was not as advertised. Despite listing multiple lobster dishes, we only got one boiled lobster with no seasoning that was bland. Lobster bisque was good and there was lobster benedict which we didn't try. American wagyu beef was also disappointing. 

Generally this is my favorite buffet on the strip but their holiday menu was a let down.

The buffet has gotten pricy and the lines are always long. 

Overall quality is good and the variety is unbelievable.

Outstanding food from all around the world including beautiful, tasty deserts - it doesn't get much better than that for sure. If you come before 5pm you might just queue for a few minutes, later the queue gets super long. Price is on an evening around 60 Dollar per person which seems fair considering the quality and variety of food you get!

So many foods to select from! 

We tried so many items: duck, crab legs, bone marrow, various types of mussels and clams, oyster shots, shrimp, soup and fresh juices. Make sure you leave room for the deserts, especially the freshly made crepes to order!!

Be prepared for a sensory overload and be prepared to eat what you pay for!

Service was impeccable.
It is ok for what it is. I was just disappointed by all the hype. It was not worth the price of admission. They do serve some specialties that other buffets don't serve.

(Review based on 4.5 stars)

I tried this buffet for the first time with my husband last Thursday for dinner (cost most on Friday-Sunday and holidays), $50.99 per person (prior to tax and tip...total came out to $110.24 with tax, prior to tip for 2). We arrived around 5:45 pm and waited in a short line. 

After it was our turn to enter the buffet and be seated, the seating hostess showed gave us a brief tour of the food and selections (she had asked if it was our 1st visit). My initial thought of this place was that the selection is smaller than other buffets on the strip. I would say that this buffet is more so focused on quality over quantity. I was impressed with the Chinese section, as the food was quite authentic. I was definitely a fan of the roasted duck and dim sum offerings. The employees and chef in this section were quiet friendly as I spoke with them while I was browsing the area. 

I also enjoyed the Italian/ French section with the chicken confit and polenta. You can really taste the flavors in each bite. I liked that these fancy tasty items were served in small little serving dishes. 

I also enjoyed the lamb at the carving station and also the seafood section (which is what I am guessing they are known for... especially with the long line forming). Offerings that I enjoyed included stone crab (very few buffets offer this type of crab, which happens to be my husband's favorite type of crab), oysters and crab legs. There are also mussels, ceviche and pureed smoked salmon and such available as well. 

I thought the dessert section was nice, but again did not have as many choices as other buffets. But the taste and quality of the desserts were quite good and indulgent. I was sadly disappointed to only see one macaron (an interesting flavor of red bean, white bean with black sesame seeds) offered. There was also this pistachio flavored cake that looked like a macaron that tasted nice but still sad that it wasn't an actual macaron (I thought there would be plenty of macarons here because of the photos I saw on this yelp page and also was mentioned in previous yelper reviews). 

This buffet does offer things that other buffets may not necessarily offer that includes waygu sliders and truffle fries and street tacos. So I can see how this buffet is highly rated and also known as one of the best buffets on the strip. 

Service was friendly and attentive. Our server, Maria was wonderful. There was also another male server working near our area who also helped to remove our dirty dishes who was also friendly as well. 

Overall, this buffet definitely raises the bar for buffets in Sin City and would come back here again.

By the way, this buffet is located in Caesar's Palace towards one end of the hotel. Make sure to ask employees where it is and don't come here starving. When we arrived, it took us 20 minutes to figure out where this buffet was at after we parked in the self parking area. Wished there were more signs around the casino to better direct us.
Don't waste your money here.  We were there on Tuesday night paid 119 for two. I had better quality buffet in Vegas than wasting my appetite on this.

Absolutely love this buffett. Some items, i find hard to understand? Just like, why is this here? Dont get it etc...but everything else is super good. Yes we waited 45 min or so, then when we got in, it was pretty worth it. Go here. Is it better than the Wynn?  Like neck and neck.

I came here with 40 guests, without notice, on a Tuesday night hoping that they could accommodate us. I after talking with the hostess, she sent over the manager on duty, Micheal. After a few minutes, he had a section ready for us to all sit together, when we were ready. 

The food, selection was vast. More items than you can eat in a week of visits.

The servers were good at getting us our drinks, which was a full time job with my group.

All through the meal, Micheal was checking with me to see if there was anything that my group needed. Service how it should be.

40+ people together and no issues, is outstanding.

I will be bringing my group back next visit for sure.
I really wanted this to be a 5 star review, but unfortunately it's not what I was expecting. First and last time.

Still an amazing buffet and the selection......holy Batman is the selection ever huge! 
During Chinese New Year weekend I was amazed at how busy this buffet was. I don't think I've ever seen more people waiting in line during peak times! Also most food stations were well stocked up. There are other buffets I've been to where they just can't handle the mass volume of people. Not here. I avoided the seafood area because the lineups were too long however there seemed to be a never ending amount of crab legs , shrimp and crab claws. 

I ended up sticking with my Asian food.

Here is what I had: 

Crispy fried fish- nice seasoned flavour and still crispy and crunchy with some hot peppers and salt. 

Crispy pork- similar to the fish but a bit more spicy and well seasoned

Beef Pho- wow.....my friend is Vietnamese who takes me here and their pho on the buffet is amazing. Not too salty and the broth is amazingly rich

Braised eggplant with beans - perfectly cooked with beans in a rich sauce and not too salty
