Dim sum- a bit dry but decent nine the less. I wouldn't consider it fresh dim sum (probably frozen but not bad for a buffet)

Pad thai- not the most flavourful but a good amount of shrimp and sauce and freshness was decent

Assorted sushi- not my favourite. A bit flavourless so I didn't finish my portions. 

Creme brûlée- very nicely done and up to Montreal- Quebec standards

Strawberries- fresh and a nice way to finish off after 2 big plate fulls 

If you are a person who deeply appreciates good food come here. You won't be disappointed!

The oyster taste soooooo bad, like dead more than 4 days, their manager come and question me why I think oyster is bad, sounds like he think that I never ate oyster b4. Then I told him go try himself. Then he never come back. Really bad experience with them

dined for breakfast & lunch, fabulous. the selections are awesome! If you can't find what you want, no one can satisfy you!!!  Everything is top notch. Best part, locals can self park for free !!!!  I'll be back, also bringing friends & out of town guests !!!!

You cannot visit Vegas without coming here! It's worth every penny. When you arrive you have to sign in electronically. They will text you once you're up but don't get too excited lol! They said a 45 minute wait and when I received a text after 10 minutes I was excited. 
So when I received the text, it was basically to stand in line for the register. You pay and then you're standing in line to be seated. So it was about 45 minutes total. 
Once I was able to view the buffer omg!!! I mean what do they not have. I went to the dinner and it was about $55. 
Sadly I was still full from lunch so I only ate seafood but that was delicious! They have king crab legs! 
The dessert were also great to. I heard the breakfast is good as my friend tried earlier that day.

This review is from Thursday, December 14, 2017. The last 2 times I came here were Thursday nights. This time I came for Thursday brunch. The reason for the extra half point is because of the different variety of food compared to evenings. Examples are; fresh juices, lobster Benedict, great pastries, better, fresher and more variety of dim sum and sushi, much fresher oyster shooters (last time 1was more than enough, this time I had 6). This time I discovered Crab Cioppino and Singaporan Laksa, a spicy seafood noodle soup and smoked oysters. As always,  I loved the atmosphere, great service, all you can drink champagne and extraordinary quality and variety of food!!! I'll be back in June for a weekend brunch.

Had lunch buffet last week. It was a good meal but still disappointed compared to what I paid. Also disappointed that the variety of food is far less than what I expected, maybe because it was lunch, not dinner.

The Wicked Spoon vs. Bacchanal?

Bacchanal Buffet wins hands down!!

Their prime ribbbbbb... drooool

It was my birthday on September 22, 2014, we usually go to the M resort for the seafood buffet, this time we decided to go to the Bacchanal Buffet instead, what a great decision.  I would vote this the best buffet I have ever been to in Vegas.  The presentation of each station was overwhelming.  The food was delicious and the desserts would blow you away.  I would recommend that if anyone is looking for a great buffet, Bacchanal is the one.  Wanted to go back the next day the food was so great.  Staff wonderful.

Would leave minus stars but you can't~~have no idea how this buffet got rated #1 cause it is so far from that~~we went on Sunday the 23rd for Brunch which of course was upcharged from their regular price cause of the holiday~~the food was lukewarm not all that..no where near 500 items heck I doubt there were 100 items and they only had like 4 of each thing out~~the desserts where not great~~they don't even know how to make a crepe and the girl who was making them was complaining the entire time that she was too busy~~but the kicker was when the chef on the egg station dropped his spatula on the floor and picked it up and used it~~APALLED

This buffet was okay, but personally I think the Wicked Spoon was a lot better.  We used the new virtual line system and put our names in at 4:30pm.  We had a party of 11 and were told to come back at 5:51pm to enter the main queue to get in.  We got into that line and ended up waiting until roughly 6:45 to actually get seated.  It was pretty ridiculous.  I would recommend going a little earlier if possible because the VIP members were getting a high priority holding up the regular queue.  Once we were seated, we got up and ate.  

The first noticeable difference between the Bacchanal and the Wicked Spoon is that there is much more variety here than at the Wicket Spoon.  Although the quality of the food seemed significantly lower.  The food here wasn't very exciting, but they had a lot of the typical things you'd expect from different food ethnicities.   The food was just average, it wasn't as adventurous as the food you'd see at the Wicked Spoon buffet.

TL;DR
Pros:
-Virtual wait line might save you some time
-Large Variety of Food
-Seafood is pretty good

Cons:
-Seat time varies depending on the VIP members in line
-Despite the variety, none of it is particularly memorable

$50 for a Thursday night was far overpriced.  I've had better buffets for much less money. Bellagio for $35 is a better deal and better food.  The smoked meats at Bacchanal were the best part of the meal.  The brisket was the best I've ever had.  However, everything else was subpar.  The seafood wasn't that great and neither was the Asian food.  I won't be going back there for this price again.  If you manage to get a deal for about $25 then it would be worth visiting.
Oh, I forgot to mention that the service wasn't that great.  Most of the time I was dying of thirst because the waiter took so long each time to refill my glass. Also, I always had my dirty dishes still on the table each time I returned from getting more food.

Went in NY and it was extremely disappointing for the price. We had heard it was the BEST buffet in Vegas and had high expectations. It was mediocre. There was a lot of food but no food (if that makes sense). There was nothing that tasted phenomenal for the steep price. I recommend to stay off the strip and find local spot for a reasonable price and better quality than the buffet. Try Rollin Smoke Barbecue, AMAZING!! Tons of food for a good price and tasted amazing. If you really want to go to the buffet to say you went, go for it, but don't expect anything fantastic.

This is our favorite buffet in Vegas! It is not the cheapest by any stretch, but you also get what you pay for it. It's the only buffet I've ever been to where they take a souvenir photo for you and some people actually buy them! :) 
First off, the line can be kind of long. Word has gotten out that it's good. They offer you the option to "skip the line" for a certain amount of money. My opinion is you are already dropping a huge chunk of change on this, it isn't really worth the dough. When we went hte last time they quoted 60-80 minutes in line, and the line ultimately took about 20-30 minutes.
The food is great! All kinds of varieties and pretty much everything we eat is great! The crab legs come in two varieties - frozen and warmed. The first time I didn't realize they had the warmed though that's y preference. They come pre-cut so you don't have to waste time cracking crab legs. The shrimp are HUGE. The sushi isn't like deluxe, but for a buffet, it's pretty good. They have some great soups, the breads are surprisingly good, and many of the dishes come in individual containers so you aren't just scooping out of a bucket. And one of my favorite things to test, their lemonade, was awesome. 
Comparing it to the wicked spoon, the bacchanal has a much more significant variety, though the wicked spoon has some more "fancier" dishes. We'd prefer the bacchanal though...
Not too many buffets can offer an seemingly never ending selection of food while maintaining quality. Enough said.

I went during Christmas Eve. Lines were over 5 hours for the regular line and 1 hour for the express, but that'll cost you an extra $20 per person. I thought the seafood was better than others. Fresh shucked oysters cold crab legs (skinny though). The hot crab legs are pretty much the cold legs dropped into hot water, which overcooked them. The meat was a bit of a disappointment. I tried the spare rib, lamb chop, tomahawk steak , rib eye and prime rib. I have to say that the spare rib was smokey but didn't seem to be tender at all. All the other meat seemed to be lacking seasoning. I will have to come back again and give it one more shot. I haven't really had a great experience will buffets during Christmas. The crowds are ridiculous!!!!

Third time eating at this buffet mecca this past 4th of July weekend. This buffet embodies the word massive (in food selection, gluttony, and flavor) so if you are only going to eat at one buffet in Vegas, this is the one to try.

Wait: They recently installed a kiosk system, giving you a time when your table will be ready. If you choose to go this route (HIGHLY RECOMMENDED), it frees you up to go gamble, relax, or putting on loose fitting clothes. This new system erased my previous main gripe about this place - the lines.

Price: This is one of Vegas' most expensive buffets, so be prepared to pay $35/person for lunch and $45 for dinner ($50 on the weekends). For those doing the 24-hour Buffet of Buffets, it is a $15 charge per trip, per person to eat here. For best bang-for-your buck, aim for a 2 - 3 PM arrival, so you can catch some of the dinner foods at a lunch price. This place, as with most other Vegas buffets, will charge you extra on holidays and their corresponding weekends (Memorial, 4th of July, Labor, Thanksgiving, Christmas, and New Years are the ones I remember them mentioning).

Food Highlights:
You really can't go wrong with anything here. This is a rarity for buffets, which I have found to be largely "meh" with a few sprinkled good dishes. It WILL take multiple trips and many hours to explore their vast selection. Here are my favorites:
- The Seafood section, which includes selections such as snow and steamed crabs, fresh oysters, and various seafood concoctions are a must try, as are the many selections at the carving station. Quality is much higher than those at other buffets.
- The TACO STATION is delicious! I love Mexican food and these were taco truck at 3 AM good!
- Your Asian and American foods are definitely a cut above others in terms of quality. I did find some of the foods to be on the salty side, however.
- The fresh squeezed juices (I believe 5 different kinds) are unique to this buffet. We came on a Sunday, so we were also able to take advantage of mimosas at no extra charge.
- The desserts here are the best in Vegas, no comparison. Tiramisu, creme brulee, macarons, and mochi ice cream are some of the more gourmet desserts that make this the highlight station.

Overall:  This buffet's selection and quality is definitely a cut above the others that I have recently tried. The dessert station here itself is worth the price of admission and makes this place worth checking out. I'm not sure if it's worth the holiday pricing, but it is worth the regular prices or the $15 Buffet of Buffets add-on. If you only have the time, budget, or stomach space for one buffet, make it Bacchanal, the God of Buffets.

It's tough writing a review for this place. There were some things that were just okay, but some items that were very memorable!

My favorite parts are the carved meats station and the dessert block. Of course, various items (such as they're tator tots and oyster shooters) were also really really good. And their maracoons and chocolate mousse dome were awesome.

Other things just seemed way off, such as their egg rolls.

But overall, had enough to choose from and plenty that were enjoyable.

This was my first real las vegas buffet. It was amazing. So many selections american, seafood, asian, mexican etc. it is very expensive but so is everything in vegas. The one downside is if your group is 8 or more they charge the standard 18% but $71.00 for a buffet meal is a little much don't you think? A lot of the dishes come on little individual plates, bowls our even lil baskets for the fried foods. Better quality than a regular buffet for sure. Go early to avoid long lines snag make sure you have plenty of rom in your stomach to get your moneys worth.

One of the best buffets out there in Vegas! Price isn't too bad, $42 for lunch. I came here two weeks ago and the wait wasn't too long, a 40 minute wait for lunch. It was one of the better buffets I've had. The food was very good with a HUGE variety. Presentation of the food was nice and it tasted great. Plenty of fresh crab and oysters. You can even get it steamed hot if you like. Their tacos were excellent, wide variety of cheeses, caprese salad, watermelon and feta, and the beets salad were refreshing. Prime rib was good...sushi was fresh! They even had ramen! 

I loved their dessert section! It was phenomenal! I had to try a bite of everything! They even had French macaroons and mochi! The gelato bar was amazing and not to forget the homemade crepes. I had so much food, I was stuffed!

I really want to like this place, but it was extremely disappointing. Maybe it was overhyped. The food was just okay, nothing sets it apart from other buffets. 

Based on other reviews, I might give it another shot next time I'm in Vegas, but I'd rather go back to the seafood buffet at Rio before dining here again.

All I can say is wow!  Awesome tasting food.  There is a great selection of food so there is something for everyone.  I liked the seafood gumbo and had at least 2 or 3 cups.  There is also pizza, Chinese food and steak.  One can also find a large selection of beverages and desserts. The price for a meal was not cheap so it is recommended you pace yourself and scan everything before just plunging in and eating.  We stayed a few hours and kept eating so I think we got our money's worth.  This is supposedly one of the better buffet places at Las Vegas and one should try at least 1 buffet when in this city.
Overpriced and overcrowded. You can get the same quality of food at a more reasonable price at multiple places on the strip. The wow factor is in presentation only.

Thanksgiving at the Caesar's Buffet...OUTSTANDING.  Of all the buffets in Vegas, this one is the very best.  The selection is amazing and everything is cooked to perfection.  The seafood station is the best I have seen, the crab legs were amazing. There is definitely something for everyone.  It is pricey but with two teenage boys, we MORE than got our money's worth.  I think my one son had 5 slices of prime rib. LOL.  The other focused on shrimp and my daughter on crab.  Well worth the buyin!! I focused on the desserts...my bad!  So much to choose from I will definitely make it our Thanksgiving treat for years to come!

I went to this place on 09/30/12 and I must say this is my new favorite buffet in Vegas. It had the largest selection of good food I have ever seen at a buffet. Any buffet can have a large selection, even Rio's world buffet has a very large selection. What makes Bacchanal different is that the majority of what I ate was very good.

I liked pretty much everything I had there. I tried to have a bit of everything, but that wasnt really possible. I'll list some of the notable stuff I enjoyed:

- All the carved meats from the pork ribs to lamb chops
- The dim sum was just as good as what I eat at my local dim sum restaurant. I especially liked the shu mai and xiao long bao
- Beef lasagne was good
- Loved the soup flavor of the tonkotsu ramen 
- The carnitas was very good
- They would heat up the crab legs for you on request
- Enjoyed the sushi rolls and hand rolls

Now why did this place only get 2 stars? Because it had the WORST service I had ever seen! The wait in line was 3 hours. I dont mind if its cuz the restaurant is extremely popular and the wait was warranted due to lack of tables, but that was not the case. The buffet had maybe 1/5 of the staff they needed to keep things flowing. Even the hostess told me that it was because they could not clear tables fast enough. When I was eating, I noticed that the table next to me was never cleared, in fact I saw MANY tables that took forever to be cleared!

Our server was horrendous. We were at the restaurant for almost 2 hours and I think I saw our server 3 times. Fortunately we ordered 3 drinks per person to last us through the meal, but the plates were never cleared since the server never came. I dont think he was lazy or anything, he just simply had like a million tables to work on. Which in turn left us with empty cups and plates on our table at all times. Which in turn resulted in the 3 hour wait.

Another thing that bothered me was that the staff told me that if I wanted to pay an additional $15 per person in our party, we can use the VIP line for a shorter wait. 

I would love to come back, but they need to get their staff issues in order.

It's not worth the 60 dallors...maybe more about 40...
Anyways I was soooo excited for the oysters til my dad and sister had it and they said it tasted off. Didn't look that great but hey, its a buffet ...had to try it..
So that was disappointing to hear. 

They had Chinese,  Japanese, Salads, American,  Italian,  Mexican, a variety of meats, and of course the Seafood ..clams, crawfish, salmon, cocktail shrimp, oysters, stone crab claws and crab legs. 

Dessert was okay tooo. .nothing too special. Food isn't terrible just didn't have a wow factor in my book.

Line was very long it felt like I am checking out at Walmart super store and have 5 full shopping carts of merchandise to checkout, after 40 mins of waiting in line and waiting to be seated, the food was NOT GOOD $54.99 per person is a hugeeee rip off in entire continent of america, the pizza was sucked old and hard, fries was not fresh, the humus was tasted from expired can food, the spanish rice was cold lower quality than taco bell and it was a big disappointing, plz do not enter, this restaurant is wayyyyyyyyyyyyy overrated. I do not understand the hype, Do not go!!!! Stay away! It is a big rip off, the dine in is huge but food selection ain't, stale, cold, undercooked and simply just garbage, trash! I left after couple medium plates I had. It was bad bad bad, maybe it was good in the past with good reviews maybe the restaurant manager needs to be replaced or the chef there, something was ridiculously wrong, I unfinished my food and left there, That was my last stop before I left Vegas and it was a bad experience overall in this so called Buffet, this experience made stop going to buffets all together. This was a really bad food cross the line! Baddest and the worst garbage trash dumppyfood so far I remember in my entire life.

We arrived at 11 AM on a Saturday morning after a long flight across the country. We got to the payment desk at 11:15 AM. We got seated at our table by 11:30 AM. The options are incredible. There's a Mexican station, carved meat station, seafood station. And then halfway through my meal I stumbled across an entire second room of Italian food and Asian food. They have an unparalleled spread. Quality is very good. The prime rib was cooked to perfection, it was not a bloody mess on my plate. The brisket had wonderful marbling although some parts of it were a little dry. The congee was very nice. The egg tacos are also delicious. My wife loved the fried chicken. My son had double portions of the sticky rice. For dessert I tried the jasmine sticky rice which was fine. The bread pudding was very good. Damage was $50 for an adult and $25 for my eight-year-old son.

Wow...it's extensive, and the selections are great.  The quality and quantity are far better than most Vegas buffets.  At over $50, it's pricey, but nothing in comparison to what you'd pay at many high-end Vegas restaurants.  I'd highly recommend it!

It was terrible service. We were 6 people. Since we started eating, the empty plates were stacked. Our table waiter did not show up until stacked for 4 or 5 plates per person. I had been shaking my hand to call waiter. However he dis not show up. So, our drinks never refilled and my parents had to drinks water instead juices.

The array of items in the Bacchanal Buffet would have anyone overwhelmed but still, I have to say -- it's one of the best buffets in Vegas!! Having a not-so-great experience at another buffet the night before -- I can't even believe we decided to go to another the day after. We went during lunch on a Monday and the lines were not that long. We got seated pretty quickly with our big group and headed on over to check out the food.  You really have to be there yourself to actually see all the different varieties of food they have to offer... it's pretty amazing. I'll just write about my favorites. I absolutely LOVED the fresh squeezed juices in the cute little milk bottles!! I tried the cucumber and the carrot juice... YUM! The little noodle area was pretty impressive as well -- I had the tonkatsu ramen... the noodles were perfectly cooked and the broth was delicious! In the dessert area -- I was in heaven! They had cute little taro cupcakes which were not overly sweet and in their gelato area, they had green tea mint gelato and black sesame. My favorite dessert in the sweets area had to be the coconut tapioca pudding with tiny pieces of jackfruit -- I ate 3 of those little cups!! I'm really looking forward to my next trip to Vegas so I can come back and try out their weekend brunch!!

Came here for lunch on a weekend, got here at 11:45am, no line for a party of 10 and got seated immediately. First thing you do if you are a seasoned buffet eater is walk around the entire buffet and see what their offerings are before you decide on what to get.

Bacchanal's did not disappoint. They have an array of cuisines, plenty of seafood, hot foods, fresh juices, breakfast food, sushi, soups, salads, desserts and much more. Gluttony at its finest. I dive straight into the seafood and pile my plate high with snow crab legs, giant crab pincers and shrimp. They tasted fresh and delicious. I love how they cut the snow crab legs in half lengthwise so it took zero effort to eat the juicy sweet meat. Allows me to eat more at a faster rate. Prime rib was juicy but a little too salty for my taste. Maybe I shouldn't have dunked it in so much au jus. I grabbed a crab benedict which was really good and served in a tiny wok. So cute. Presentation matters, you eat with your eyes first did you know that?  Have I mentioned we also had bottomless mimosas? Those were gooooooooood. 

And the dessert choices were amazing. You have to try the jasmine rice pudding, it is so good. Sweet, warm, and fragrant little cup of pudding really lit me up! And not to mention the gelato bar! Shieeet! So good damn good. Those if you who know me know how much I love good ice cream! 

Do not try the Oyster shooters. Nastiest thing I've ever eaten. Clean and well kept high end buffet! Someone is always going around cleaning up the counters and spillage. Will definitely come back another time and try dinner!

We came here during the Labor Day weekend. Boy, the wait was LONG! We waited over 2 hours to get in. The food selection was great! There are a lot of choices and numerous stations. The seafood such as crab legs, oysters, crab claws, shrimp cocktails, and crawfish were fresh. We also tried their oxtail soup. It was pretty good. The dessert station was great as well. They have all kinds of cakes and pastries, gelato, mochi ice-cream, chocolate covered strawberries, as well as crepes. Overall, the food and services were great. It's the long wait that makes us rethink whether to come back again. That's the only reason for knocking off the one star from my review.
Amazing buffet.  The best in Las Vegas.  Don't miss the seafood expertly prepared.  Pretty pricey but well worth the $$$

Timed this to hit breakfast and lunch, clearly a good choice! Breakfast was incredible, so much to choose from. The biscuits and gravy was delicious,  great bacon options, fresh fruit, shrimp and grits, waffles, fried chicken, crepes, muffins, eggs - good lord looks like I ate alot. Oh wait, I did! 6 plates. Why? Because I was on vacation and wasn't eating until 7:30pm that night!
For the lunch portion, I had some sushi (could have been a better variety), miso soup, tried some new Asian dishes Id never had and loved!  Nothing I tried was gross and I the dessert was great too, cobbler. 
Did I mention the fresh orange juice and the service was great, never had to wait for a refill. 
This place is a dream and the best $25 spent :)

Wow. I love this place . Problem is it's just too much food to sample all at one sitting .  You'll get sick trying to try a little of everything , it would be so much better if I could come back for lunch and dinner And have smaller plates each time than trying to get my money's worth at one dining session . The seafood is great , crab legs and claws very tasty and meat carvings delicious . My favorite from the Mexican station are the juices , taco bar and elote (corn on the cob with spices ).  From the Asian station I liked the Peking duck and bbq pork. The charcuterie and Parmesan cheese is the bomb . They would get 5 stars if the price was lower and they included lobster , and the lines can be horrendous , so 4 stars it is.  It's the best Vegas buffet hands down .
One of the best buffets in Las Vegas. The Bellagio was my favorite before but this one is better. Snow crab and prime rib were both top quality.

This is the best buffet I've ever been to in my life. They have a huge selection and excellent service. In my opinion, it is pricey but it's worth every dime! The wait was long but also worth it. They had everything to eat that you could ever imagine and I tired it all! The quality was great. I will definitely come again.

It pains me to write an average review since I was tremendously excited to try Bacchanal for the first time but, at least for the brunch, it left me feeling meh.

I got there around 10am on a Friday for the weekday brunch, paid the $39.99, and it was smooth sailing to my table. Then it was time to scope out the offerings and see what I could fit into my empty stomach. 

I tried every station from the seafood station, to the meat station, to the Asian station, and even had room for some gelato. Rum raisin gelato to be exact. But nothing really wowed me like I thought it would. There were some disappointing dishes. The lobster benedict didn't have lobster meat incorporated, just a lobster sauce on top of the benedict. The meatballs were way too dense and heavy. The red velvet pancakes were very dry. 

The service was excellent though as they cleared my empty plates when I sought out to get more food. Overall, the food was average for brunch. Perhaps the impressive dishes are saved for the dinner service. I'm willing to give dinner a try the next time I'm in Vegas.

Not as many selections as I had expected.
The seafood was not very fresh as well.
Asian food is generally better than other stuff.
Steak is good.
Will try other places next time.
overall okay experienced, but maybe I set my standards too high for the price.

First let me preface this by saying after 3 nights in Vegas I went to the World Carnival at Rio, Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan, and then Bacchanal at Ceasar's. I started getting sick the day of Bacchanal, I'm guessing I drank a drop of that grimy pool water at Rehab the day before, because that night was about the time I started feeling the bug. 

Anyways on a 5 night binger in Vegas, I thought this was going to be my last meal that I could enjoy. I was not disappointed. I can really only review the things I had and the experience I had here. So we'll start with:

Plate #1
Leek dumpling, not too much dough and the soup was still warm, mmm fond memory. The fried dumpling wasn't as bad as frozen dumplings I guess that's all I can say about them, typical greasy deep fried potstickers, probably not worth the stomach room but if you're craving it, eat it, it will at least satisfy that. The hot and sour soup was a hit at the table, it definitely lives up to it's name, as being both spicy and sour, a little more spicy and sour than I'm used to, but at least it does the name justice. Also a bonus: had a station next to the soup to put extra things in, like chives! I love chives. Shrimp spring rolls in that peanut butter sauce, decent not the best but definitely satisfying for a buffet. 

Plate #2
Time for some BBQ. Got a piece of the prime rib, better than Wicked Spoon's, if anyone can relate to that, otherwise not better than anything you could make yourself, if you know how to make a roast and had the time, but it was juicy enough and rare enough in most places. Like most places however the slice was huge and couldn't finish it. Kielbasa, very tasty with some dijon mustard, nothing special though, how do you mess up kielbasa, really? Lamb shank, ok here we go. You look at it on your plate and you see the bone and the fat slab of meat on the end like a big 'ole meat lollipop and you are excited. You're thinking, I'm going to devour this, and it's going to taste great. At least that was what I thought until I had one bite and realized it was over cooked and not prepared in a matter that I would have prepared it and thought it was a waste of the meat. Let me tell you how I really feel, right? Sorry, I was just excited about it and I didn't like the seasoning and it tasted like it was boiled?? Also way overdone. Could have just been mine, and I would say that but it was everyones at the table. Oh well you can't win them all. Wagyu beef sliders! Tasty, get them. The meat definitely shines through in the little slider, cool presentation as well. The bread was buttery and light. Went to the fried baskets and got the "Chef's Special" which was fried pickles, I do love me some fried pickles, kosher spears in a delightfully light batter, bar food, beer food, comfort food. Yum. 

Plate #3
Sushi,
I got every piece of sushi they offer and poke! That being said, the plate wasn't full. Shrimp tempura roll, some rainbow roll, spicy tuna or salmon roll, then salmon and tuna nigiri, and poke! The sushi was sushi. That is it, nothing special here, pretty prototypical of any all you can eat sushi, whatever. Poke! You usually don't see it too often at buffets, although I see it more often now, It was good. The tuna was very fresh and spicy. Worth the stomach room if you like poke. 

Plate #4
At this point I'm feeling kinda full and that stomach bug is acting up, I know I have precious valuable time before I hit a wall or the bathroom. I go to the seafood, I think this is not going to bode well for later on in the night, for we have plans to see Kaskade at Tao. But I can't help myself when I see a sign for lobster rolls, I wait for a new batch. Looks like a little crostini with some sort of lobster schmear... Now I am from New England. No way you are going to tell me that that is a friggin' lobster roll. Whatever, I want one. I look at the rest of the seafood and think about Kaskade and back away slowly. The lobster roll, was, well not a lobster roll. I could taste the half slice of grape tomato that resides on top of the pink goop on top, not good. I go right to the desserts. I wish I could have a second stomach at this point. I already did a cursory glance before hand and saw mochi at the ice cream station, drool. I get a oreo chocolate dome cake, fig balsamic and thai tea ice cream with a strawberry mochi. Ok. I could eat a tub of that fig balsamic. The thai tea was also tremendous, better than Wicked Spoon, I just liked the sweetness/tea balance in it more. The oreo dome cake was magical as well. Also had a piece of a friends honey comb chocolate bar? Very interesting, I don't know how I didn't see that but it was good, poor honey bees.

Great buffet, get there early. There was a huge line at 6. We waited probably 20 minutes and paid the 20 dollars extra for the shorter line. Everything was prepared well, and of high quality. When I think of "Vegas buffet" this is the kind of stuff I think about.

HONESTLY, do not go here if you are on a diet!!! Dieter's worst nightmare. They have such a huge selection and I can see why the lines are so long. It was $65 a person which is expensive but once you go in and see endless buffet, it's worth it. For a buffet that makes food in large quantity, the quality wasn't as bad as I thought. I'm really glad we came to try it! They have so many different types of food from different parts of the world. Kudos to everyone who helps run it.
One of the top 2 buffets in vegas  (wicked spoon at the cosmo is my other pick). no complaints, great selection and quality

One of the best buffet I've been to! I love that they have so much food! They have everything from breakfast hot foods, to pastries to dessert. They have all sorts of different type of food! From Italian to Mexican to Asian! Also has fruit juice in glass station! I couldn't even go around to try everything because I got so full so early. They have a two hour limit which I think is more than enough. The brunch cost $33 per person using Groupon. It's as good as dinner but dinner I think you get seafood and other expansive dishes. Also, the cost for a child no matter the age is $20! I mean under 2 should be free but that's not the case here! Either way, it's great! They also have crepes station and gelato! I love it! Nice and clean place and if you want to beat the crowd, go early on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. Although it's pricy, it's a nice one a time experience. I couldn't eat much more to make up the moneys worth. All in all, food was incredible and so was the hype about this place!

People don't waste your money. This Buffett is not what you would expect from "The best Buffet in the USA". It started with waiting for 30 minutes in line. The waiter only asked once what we want to drink. After that no show. The plates were almost never removed from our table. A lot of the food was blend, dried out or was sitting way to long. I was missing the special twist in the food. There was nothing special about it. One hour after eating there I am feeling somewhat sick. Spending 55 bucks for that? Never ever again. Go to the Wicked Spoon instead. Way better choice with the twist. Overall super disappointed.
Addition: I am very sick after having eaten there. It was either the oyster or sushi. The entire night running fever, chills and very bad cramps. I will never ever go there again.

5+ stars for the food. 1 star for the 2+ hour long wait.  The time given to you on the ticket doesn't mean much.  It appears as long as you have a ticket you can stand in line.   The best crab legs at any buffet I have ever eaten.  Get the boiled crab legs at the station inside by the pizza and salad bar.  Tastes much better than the cold ones on ice (but the cold ones are pretty good too).  Sushi is above average but not great.  Prime rib (given medium rare unless you ask for well done) and lamb chops are great.  LInes at all food stations move fast (It's just the line to get in that takes forever).  Although $56/person for dinner (get the TR card), I think it is well worth it.  Fabulous dessert station so save some room.

Totally not worth the $70 per person for dinner !? Don't waist your time and money here ... it's a big lace mediocre food but seats are super dirty and if you want diet beverage your only option is Diet Pepsi for $70 a person please invest in a diet sprite !? Very loud and very dark as well .

Amazing amount of food. Everything was very good. I normally do not like buffets, I usually do not like the quality of the food. But I was pleasantly surprised by how good everything was. I would strongly recommend  for breakfast or lunch, I can not speak of dinner.

Came here for dinner on Sunday night. The food choices are many. So many I actually forgot what they had by the time I made one choice and went back for more. LOL. The raw oysters were not as fresh as I would have liked. It had a frozen seafood taste. The snow crabs were good but a bit salty. Butter made it all better! The tacos were good but I was so full that I wasn't able to enjoy it. I'm giving it 3 stars bc I feel I need to go back and give this place another try. It's funny that they have a sign requesting diners to limit their time to 2 hours. But I feel you need 3 just to have a rest period. Haha

Trust me. It's NOT worth the money. Holiday buffet is approx $60+ and the food is indeed so so. Crab legs are very salty, sushi only so so, and the Chinese dim sum was subpar. The only things I like are the gingsin chicken soup ms moji ice cream. Very disappointing. Instead, try the sterling buffet at Bally. Even though it's a bit more expensive, it includes unlimited champaign, orange juice, king crab legs, lobsters, filet mignon, etc. and service is great.

BEST  BUFFET I BEEN TO IN VEGAS! 

I came around 11:15 AM and it was $35 per person. I guess for dinner it's $50. They had lots of food and endless amounts of meat, steak, BBQ. One side had Asian food, another side had Mexican, another side had American, another had Seafood, and guess what?! They didnt forget about the Vegetarian population! Yes they had a Vegetarian section!!!! Most buffets dont have that! Their desserts section was on the opposite side of the buffet but the sweet confections were to die for! Macaroons, gelato, cookies, and much much more! They had crab but a worker told me it didnt come in until 3:00 PM, which was a big bummer but i resorted to a bucket of mussels lol. The ramen and pho were pretty good and the sushi was great! They even had Horchata (mexican rice and cinammon drink) as well as Tamarindo, Pineapple juice, and other drinks from Mexico. Their tacos were also mad on a flat grill like at the taquerias back home in California. 

Also, the workers were friendly and very attentive! They took care of me and my table of friends and made sure we were catered to! Now thats the 10 star service that i expected from this place!

Not to mention its located in the beautiful Caesar Palace Hotel and Casino! Lines may get pretty long which is a big bummer but the food is well worth the wait!! Not to mention, they also take a picture of you and your group before being escorted to your table!

If your a gelato or macaroon or seafood fan, this is the place to dine at in Vegas!!

One of the best las vegas buffet as far as I remember.
But one thing I definitely like about this buffet is that the food is made freshly. It wasn't sitting there for a long time and not premade. Everything is made right there..

They have steamed crab  legs as well as cold crab legs. Oysters.. which u have to wait in line for. There's a crap load of dessert options, but they look better than they taste and was a disappointment. Pho was legit considering it's a buffet and tacos were made to order and tasted authentic. 

Their more gourmet food prepared in individual stainless mini pots tasted amazing: truffles mushroom polenta, squash ravioli, and more I can't remember..

As far as service.. it's decent except that they seem less happy compared to other buffets i've been to.

Went there for the second time.  While they do have an amazing variety of food, nothing they served warranted a $65 per person charge.  You're paying for the Caesar's name and nothing else.  I've had better buffets and endless champagne for half the price.

Heard a lot about Ceasars buffet so I decided to try it. Came for brunch at 2:45 so that we can get some of the dinner items. The place was big and it did offer a wide selection of food. I think the food is mediocre and was not as good as I hoped. The desserts looked really pretty but it did not taste so good. The safest dessert is crepes anx ice cream.  The crepe itself was good but the fruit topping was not. This was the only buffet I went to in vegas so I could not compare it to any other buffets. But would definitely recommend coming for late lunch so yoi can get soke of the dinner items as dinner can be quite expensive

When this buffet opened in 2012, Hubby and I checked it out.  The price was slightly lower than it is now at $25 per person for breakfast with Total Rewards card.  Since then, we have returned twice for breakfast and once for dinner.  Breakfast has improved and I now find that I can't make enough room for everything I want to eat! 

Also, the breakfast meat carver is the most friendly and entertaining guy you'll meet at a buffet.  Say hello with a smile and he'll brighten your day.  Enjoy!
The food was good. Great selection and awesome deserts. However not worth planning your day around (i.e. 3.5 hours of wait plus eating time).

Where do I start - 

The first time I went with my family we got the 24 buffet that allows you to go to different buffets including this one. On the list it did not state that we would have to pay extra for this one. So it's $45 for the 24 hr then when we get to this one there was a sign that said it would be $15 more. We looked at the paper and they hand wrote in each that it was $15 more - HOW GHETTO IS THAT?!?!?

On top on the extra $15 if you wanted to get to the front of the long line IT'S ANOTHER $15!!!! 

So my bros girlfriend went to talk to the "manager" who was a complete ass and was trying to negotiate more $$$ out of us. Our whole party of probably 10 people ended up leaving.

Second try I went through the diamond line and found out it was close to $50 a person. I told myself might as well try it right?

In a nut shell ALL THE FOOD was SALTY. Everything was over cooked or rubbery. The servers who were cutting the meat in the front we too busy checking out girls to know there was a long line. I HAVE IT ON VIDEO TOO. The managers were too busy micro managing the servers at the tables to even notice this. The dessert organization was horrible. The plates were small. 

You are serious putting money down for them to make it look fancy as oppose to how the food taste. Like other reviews - it's not worth your time waiting in line and spending the $$$ 

People say you should at least you should try it once??? Go ahead if you want to feel like you got robbed. Ro, Harrahs, Flamingo, Paris buffets are waaaaaaaaaayyy better than this one!!!

IT'S NOT WORTH IT!!!!!!!
Buffet has so much to choose from. Loved the pizza, snow crab, the burger and fries and fried chicken. We had a wait 45 minutes for a table but was well worth it!

As you step into the entrance of the Baccanal Buffet, you are struck with sheer amasment. There is glass every-where. There are open tables, booths that are two sided with glass.  There is a buzz of people, look at this and look at this.The entire staff is extremely friendly. 
There is a seafood station--a carving station--bread and rolls--An Italian station with pizza-quich-meatballs- pasta- lasagna. There are assorted cheeses--salads and all the topping and more for the salads.There is a carving station with freah cooked chicken-smoked brisket-ribs. The Chinese station was large- hanging duck--char sui pork-kalui short ribs and much more. I am sure that I missed a lot as hte buffet is spread out and so that there is no grouping and long lines.
I found the dessert station, which was in the middle of the dining room. If one thinks that they are impressed with the buffet line, thenwait till you see the dessert station, it is nothing but sweet delights.
I tried the brisket-a rib-a couple of shrimp-a small sladwith some toppings-a small piece of quich-a meat ball with some marinara sauce ( thought the marinara could have more garlicly as I like garlic in marinara)-small amount of fried rice-a couple of crab legs.
One of the things that stands out is that the food is being cooked on the line so the customer can see what and how it is done.
I rated my exprience at the baccanal as A-1. You will not be disapointed, and the price is just right. 
Good job everyone. You make yourselfs proud.

It is a little pricey but for the amount of foods they offer it is what you pay for. They have, I think, 9 stations. Each is a different type of food, i.e. Mexican, Asian, American, etc. I tried almost all stations (1 item per station) and the food was good! I've been to other buffets where their is a wide selection but the taste of the food was below average. They even had a gelato station.. now that was impressive. I loved the food and the outlay of the place was very pretty. I understand it can get pretty busy, but I only got water once throughout the entire service which was disappointing. I was so thirsty but I waited until I went to the coke shop to get something to drink because our server just disappeared. When I saw her I asked for more water but she never came back so that is the main reason why I'm not giving it 5 stars.

This was my first Vegas buffet experience in many years, and I was not disappointed. We came on a Sunday around 12pm for brunch and there was only about a 5-10 minute wait. The cost was $45/person and included unlimited mimosas. Our server was really sweet and did a great job explaining where everything was located. I was overwhelmed with how many different food options there were, and I wanted to try everything if only my stomach space would allow it. I loved the meat and seafood sections the most. Steak, shrimp and crab are the three things I could probably eat everyday for the rest of my life, and they were plentiful at Bacchanal.  My favorite starch was the truffled scallop potatoes. I need to find myself the recipe because it was that good. In the dessert section, I tried the carrot cake which was good. The chocolate lava cake however was overcooked and burnt on the edges. You definitely can't go wrong with the gelato. I really liked the Nutella and strawberry balsamic flavors. The best part of dessert were the cupcakes. They had the perfect amount of sweetness and were super moist. Thanks Bacchanal for the food baby that appeared under my shirt. It was well worth it.

Yum yum yum!! Love this buffet. I personally loved it because of the amount of seafood they had. We were VIP customers so we had extra comps ;) but other than that really nice buffet, sanitary and delicious! Definitely recommend this place

Even if this place is buffet, the service has always been very good. The ladies on the floor are very attentive. When we go to Vegas, this is the only place we eat buffet at. Very good selection and top quality food and service.

Caesars Bacchanal Buffet is the top buffet on the strip. They have every type of food for all people. Seafood, American, BBQ, Sushi, Mexican. You name it they have it. And let's not forget all you can drink Champagne with collectable glass. If your on the strip it's a must on your vacation in Vegas.

I think it deserves the designation of best buffet in Las Vegas ( although of course I haven't been to all of them) it's large, food is good and for those who think it's expensive its VEGAS!  We had a salad and appetizer on the strip for the same price. 
Go during lunch if you want a better deal . It was 39 bucks .

Because of a Groupon deal, I was finally able to try out this buffet that everyone is always raging about. I've never been as overwhelmed by brunch before, but there were just so many options! The many varieties of Eggs Benedict were my favorites because of how different they were and how they all were presented so nicely. I also LOVED the crepe station. This is the place to indulge yourself.

This place was great!!! Juices galore, sausages by the feet, fried eggs with steak skirt....nothing bad on this menu expect maybe the dish with quail eggs (but I wasn't brave  enough to try). All of the food was fabulous!!! Will most definitely be back everytime we are in Vegas! Stop in and give it a try!!! I believe we only paid $56 for a weekday brunch for both of us. Just the desserts alone was with it!!!

Don't pass this one by!!!
The Bacchanal Buffet Is the best one I ever get!  Service is OK, too. I strongly recommend it to everyone, locals or visitors. I'll put it on my list for next trip to Vegas.

I'll say this is the #1 buffet in Las Vegas at least for now! The food is really tasty and fresh. They have more variety than any other buffet in Las Vegas. The interior design is just stunning! Really love it!!!

Due to a very high review on Yelp, my friend and I decided to come here for dinner. We tried almost everything. Seafood is not very good and food is salty to me. But, deserts are good. 
Price is $55 including tax on Friday (dinner)

Went to the restaurant last year and was thoroughly impressed. Came back again this year and was sadly disappointed. 

We had booked a reservation for 7:30 and had been advised to come in at 7 to be seated for 7:30 however after showing up at 6:55 which is pretty early by our standards, we were advised that we needed to wait in a 70 minute line just to pay to get in.  Wasn't unreasonable however because of the expectation that was set and what time we were actually seated wasn't a very pleasant experience.  

We came in to the restaurant at 8:20 which is about 2 hours before closing and an hour before last call. Unfortunately the quality of some of the foods seemed to have also reached the end of their shelf life.  Going to start with the good then the bad.  Tried a bit of everything. The pork belly on mashed potatoes was absolutely divine. I could have just eaten that for the entire evening and would not have regretted it. Also really enjoyed the king crab legs, the chef's special which was a shrimp risotto, truffle pizza (all their pasta and pizza were just perfect), and their dessert selection is basically the expectation side of an "expectation vs reality" meme.  Now for the bad. The meats available for the entirety of the evening were all dry. The butcher area also had staff that didn't seem at all interested in serving food to anyone. I was standing for a solid minute and wasn't acknowledged by anyone. This literally put a sour taste in my mouth. 

Two of us decided to get bottomless mimosas. I don't like to hit the bottom of my bottomless mimosas and our server made sure I never hit it either. Our server seemed to get the idea as soon as the first mimosa was finished in 35 seconds so he started giving us bigger glasses which we didn't realize was the equivalent to four mimosas each. We finished 3 of them. 


Overall between the lineup, dry meats, and the most expensive buffet we went to on the strip. Was not impressed of my second trip to Bachannal. Unsure if I would go back next year.

I had heard a lot of good things about Bacchanal, so my expectations were pretty high. We went on a Friday night around 7 and had to wait about an hour and a half to get a table. The line moved rather quickly, especially as I had good company with me. 

There are a bunch of different stations (Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Mexican, Meats, Seafood, and Dessert), but I only got from the Japanese, Italian, Meats, and Dessert, mostly because I figured that if I'm trying to make a $51 worth it, I shouldn't have Chinese or Mexican since I can get them for a lot cheaper elsewhere. 

Japanese: Average. The fish wasn't super fresh, and the quality wasn't very high, but it was tasty nonetheless. They had several different kinds of rolls and some poke.

Italian: Since I only had the bread and meatballs from this section, I can't say very much about the station as a whole, but the bread was delicious (there was a focaccia with bacon bits on top that was absolutely exemplary).

Meats: Lots of choices here. There was brisket, racks of lamb, prime rib, short rib, sausages, and other things. The lamb was overdone, and the short rib was extremely tough. However, the prime rib, sausage, and brisket were excellent. The only downsides to getting the food were the unfriendly meat carvers and the long line.

Dessert: LOVE. LOVE, LOVE, LOVE. If I could have, I would have feasted solely on the desserts. There's a bunch of different flavors of gelato, lots of cake, and chocolate dipped items like cheesecake, strawberries, etc. Everything from here was good, and it truly is a desserts lover's paradise.

Overall, I definitely recommend Bacchanal. Food was good for a buffet, service was very friendly, and atmosphere was nice.
Overrated! I don't mind spending $$$ on food but this place is not worth it. There's lots of choices but nothing to rave about. I enjoyed the seafood buffet at rio more.

It is a great big buffet. Quality is 4/5. It's $60/person and on weekends, it's a long line and holidays you can't even get in. This time we went on weekday evening and there was a short wait but there were a lot of available tables. But no matter, we're here for The Food--glorious glorious food!!  

They have a large Asian section with dimsum items-shumai, hawgow, egg roll, and jasmine rice, bbq pork, roast pork, roast duck; then they have ramen station, sushi galore, a Mexican section, a carved meat station, seafood section, Italian section, Did I miss anything?  And oh yes, desserts and fruits and salads including gelato. 

It really is a smorgasbord. No wonder people rate this as #1 buffet!!!

This is where I ate too much and hated myself after having reached the highest level of fullness that my stomach could handle. I've been here three times over the span of two years, and many things have changed since its opening.

There are now kiosks where patrons submit their name and cell phone number to be contacted when it's time to line up. In a way, this system is somewhat useless, especially on busy weekends. We still had to wait a half-hour to be seated. 

For buffet food, this is one of the best on The Strip. There are international offerings that aren't limited to egg rolls and pizza. The desserts are fantastic with cake pops, a crepe station, and assorted pastries. I noticed that they did eliminate certain items from their dinner selections -- I guess seaweed salad wasn't a hit. 

Currently it's $54 per person on the weekends. The price is average compared to other buffets on The Strip. You can save a buck by joining Caesars' Total Rewards program.

In my book, this still remains as being one of the best buffets in Vegas.

Being that I'm in the buffet business, I've been to quite a few buffets in my life time.  This is probably the best buffet I've ever been to (next time I'll try Bally's brunch).  I wish Yelp had half stars so I could give 4.5 but I went ahead and gave 5 since it was more of a 5 than 4.  They had a very wide selection and many of the items were served in small plates.  Even though it was a good experience I still would like to point out the negatives.  1) I grabbed 8 raw oysters.  The first one I ate was average but the second one was really bitter.  I spit it out and continued to the 3rd and 4th which had a mushy consistency that I also spit out.  I love raw oysters but I never eat them from a buffet but I was thinking since this is a little higher end I'll give it a try.  I believe they were going bad.  2)  the hot King crab legs were flavorless.  I only ate like 3 halves.  It didn't have any salt or that natural sweet crab flavor.  Maybe i should have tried the cold ones?  Oan...A casino in Seattle had very good snow crab legs.  3) I tried 2 soups and they were both really salty 4) the corn on the cob was not cooked long enough.  Other than that everything else I had was good.  But then I only had room to try about 20% of their items.  I'll have to try more next time.  And maybe they should hire me to watch over their buffet line lol

This is HANDS DOWN the best buffet we've ever been to! The food is DELICIOUS, very well presented & the variety is INCREDIBLE! Also-- a special shout out to our server MARK who made our meal EXTRA SPECIAL!!! He was extra attentive, kind, funny & made our time here PHENOMENAL!!

MAN BEWARE for dinner it was a 2 hour wait to get in!!!!!!!!!!!!!
obviously cause its new, i was fine to wait as i was stuffed from a late lunch. we lined up at 5 pm got seated a little after 7pm. i think it was like 40 a person? forgot. 

first off server attention needs improvement!! not enough servers i guess. we only got our plates cleared once and drinks refilled once and we didnt see a server for like an hour!! we had to play jenga with the plates!!!!!!!!!!!

but that didnt stop me from enjoying the food! seriously this is the best buffet in vegas right now. i ate almost everything except for the salad bar, mexican stuff.

asian section
sushi/spicy tuna/sashimi was soft, tasty n fresh
bowl of ramen chewy noodles with tasty broth add you own toppings.
the couple of dim sum items the shrimp n pork dumplings was prob better than a chinese restaurant 
crispy fried fish was good
ginseng soup was authentic better than my moms =X

seafood
oyster shooters was yum
now the crab legs man!!! i could eat these all night it really filled me up, they would offer to put em in boiling water to heat em up for you if you like, add in drawn butter = heaven!!
clam bake wasnt bad
couldnt get my hands on any oysters it kept disappearing when i went

meat
prime rib was juicy and wasn't tough
i really really like the lamb chops man!! sweet, savory, juicy, tender.... wouldnt expect this at a buffet

pastas
vodka penne? i think it was was tasty
calamari was crispy n seasoned well
didnt like the lasagna 
bread selection was great like the butter garlic rolls

dessert
my favorite part!
fresh hand dipped chocolate strawberries
hot made to order crepes very soft n tasty
really loved the hot choco chip cookie dish
creme brulee was ok wasnt what i expected kinda too soft not as creamy
gelatos was pretty standard had choice of dipped cones 
i think i liked every dessert except the cupcakes which i thought was kinda bland. oh and theres candy too =P

bacchanal can only improve through time or gradually suck as time passes we will see as this is still new...  hopefully after a while it wont be too long of a wait and services improves.. will be back! the food was soooo good FRESH! compared to other buffets despite the negatives its a 5 star! it dont get better than this!!

I have tried all the major buffers on the strip. My old favorite was wicket spoon, but now I think bacchanal is leading the industry without any doubt. That being said the price is also the most expensive other than the sterling brunch at Bally, however the price is getting close during holidays.

This time I came during Christmas Eve and let me tell you about the wait time first, I got there around 4pm, got the ticket which tells me to come back at 06:17pm, I can back around 6 and was told to go to the end of the line that was out side of the regular roped waiting area.  By the time I got sitter it was already 07:30pm and the only reason I got sitter at that time is because I was in a party of 2 who was able to skip around 20 people ahead of me.

Now let's talk about the food. They do have variety of selections:
The meat: lamb T-bone cooked to medium/medium well, very tender and perfectly seasoned. Prime meat cooked at different stages depends on your preference, very tender.

Seafood: soft shell crab very crispy and flavorful. Raw oyster is good size and fresh. King crab has chilled and cut in half or whole boiled, they are very fresh and has unlimited supply.

Asian section: the roast pork looks good but the skin was not crispy, disappointed. The sushi/sashimi does not look like very fresh also disappointed.

Dessert section: lots of choices including gelato and tai tea. Has fresh fruits too. 

Over all very satisfied, price is on the high side but quality is probably the best on the strip for now. Avoid peak times such as thanks giving and Christmas. The line is long even on regular time, plan ahead and go early to get the ticket so you can eat on time.

Now I know why everyone calls Bacchanal the best buffet in Vegas. Food is delicious 

Came on Tuesday afternoon, no wait at all!! 

Best time to go is around 2pm right before they change out for dinner items at 3pm 

You have to pay for parking at Caesars (~$12), I recommend walking from a casino that offers free parking.

Excellent buffet with a ridiculous amount of variety. Really liked their Asian section, which they did really well. I gorged on toast duck. I only with they had all the fixings for pecking duck; steamed bun, shredded scallions, and hoisin sauce. The meat section was okay. Seafood was a little disappointing since they didn't have king crab. Plenty of other variety to distract the momentary disappointment, though. I'll be back for more!

Well, we were looking for a place to eat before a show at Caesars and thought we'd try this place. Had a lot of time to kill so waiting in the long line was acceptable but not pleasant. I was struck by the high price of $53.99 per. I don't mind paying if I feel it has been worth the price. I think the only thing the one star would cover is the huge variety of food available. Better like fish because the entire restaurant reeked of fish. When I eat at a buffet, the first trip, I will get a small portion of a lot of items and then return on the good ones. Everything that I sampled on the first trip was not worth the trip back. The desserts were good but by then I was so angry at getting "ripped off" that it was hard to enjoy. 
      In short, for the money you pay, this is by far the worst buffet that we have ever experienced. After tax and tip (not workers fault), our bill was $136.73. Grrrrrr!

Delicious! So, trick is to come at the end of brekky and beginning of lunch. It does get crowded the closer you are to 11 am. Expect to wait unless you get vip. You can skip the sushi... I had it when it first came out and it didn't taste super fresh. Raw salmon was a bit chewy. Still tastes good. 

Crab was amazing. Ramen was amazing. Staff was very helpful and nice!

This is a great buffet with lots to choose from and the food actually tastes decent-good. 

I came with 3 other people around 230 pm on a thursday. It was not busy at all. We paid and were seated immediately. Since we came at this time, we were able to taste both the brunch menu, and dinner menu since dinner starts at around 3pm. 

At the time we came in, there's a seafood section with cold stone crab legs, cold snail, cold snow crab legs, cocktail tiger prawn, raw oysters, and some cajun styled crawfish and seafood. Hot crab legs are served at the italian section during dinner time. At dinnertime, there was also softshelled crab with corn puree which was good. Then there's also a meat section with sausages, turkey breast, beef, lamb and etc. I didn't really get much food from this section since I didn't want to get myself too full from the meats. I tried the wagyu beef without any sauce and and it tasted really bland. The buffet also had alot of soup, mexican food, Italian food, and Asian food. The selection of sushi was very small. They have a noodle bar with Singaporean laksa which was pretty good. They had galbi, charsiu, peking duck, dim sum. ALOT OF FOOD which I can't name. So much to choose from and my stomach couldn't fit everything I wanted to try which totally sucks. The dessert bar was amazing as well with make your own crepe.

How do you turn a 5 star place into 2 stars?  You get GREEDY!  I was here yesterday and they raised the price to $55 per dinner.  That's pretty expensive.

Service was very spotty and it looks like they downgraded the quality of the items in their buffet.  The Chinese spareribs are gone and so are many of my favorite items.  Just plain SAD SAD SAD.

First, they added a lot of salt to every entree.  Second, they increased the volume of the music in the buffet.  Finally, they jacked up the price and lowered the service level.

I get the point.  Now the buffet order has been restored on the strip.  Bellagio and Wynn are back on top.

What moron would blare music during dinner?  Is that a tactic to drive you out sooner?

The marinade on the ribs tasted horrible and was full of salt.  Crab legs were not that fresh but it didn't stop them from serving it.  The balsamic strawberry gelato is just plain wrong and disgusting.

Waited a long time to get a refill on my drinks.  This should be automatic.

This was a good buffet. It was a good buffet, not a great buffet like we heard, and certainly NOT the best buffet as some had reported. We chose this place because of the reviews and their own advertising. 

We enjoyed the food, but the ads and reviews made it sound like it would be incredibly delicious. Not the case. Yes, they have an extensive selection of food. Yes, there is lots of seafood, desserts, meats, etc. etc. etc. But I expected much higher quality, which is my fault for getting too excited. 

I do not regret going, but for $40-50 per person, there are other meals one can have which would be more satisfying. 

In the future, I will make sure to read the good AND the bad reviews to have as complete a picture as possible before deciding. 

Would I return? Yes, to try the brunch. The service was good. Everyone was friendly and nice.

If you only have time (or money) for one buffet, Bacchanal would be the place to go. They're pricey but not unreasonable considering the selection. I believe we paid $54.99+ for a Friday night dinner. Starting Dec 19 it's $62+ since it's holiday season menu.

Some of my favorites: 
Crab legs. Actually, almost all of their seafood items
Oreo chocolate mousse dessert
Pho!!! Who would've thought? Awesome Pho at a buffet?
Siu may and har gaow (dim sum items)
Made to order tacos had me pleasantly surprised. I thought this was on par with some of the best taco trucks.

Stay away from: 
Ramen. Broth is funky tasting
Sushi items. When we went it wasn't that fresh, and with so many other good options, it's not worth the stomach space
Macaron. Flavorless. It tastes like I'm straight up just eating sugar and nothing else. 

My friends and I are Platinum Total Rewards members so we only waited around 15 min, but I can see why many reviews docked stars for having to wait 1 - 2 hours. If you already know you're gonna be waiting a while, just bring a small snack so you don't get hangry in line! Better yet, if someone you know is a Diamond/ Seven Stars member, have them walk you in so you get into the buffet with minimal/ no wait time.

Ladies and gentleman...Here it is...The best buffet in Vegas. The Crab legs come out of a steaming pot. There is a huge variety of meat in the carving station.  The deserts are absolutely beautiful to look at and more importantly totally delicious.  I am totally impressed with the modern decor.  I would go back to this place in a heartbeat.  It is pricey but worth every penny.

Favorite buffet in Vegas without a doubt. The atmosphere is clean and modern yet comfortable. The food is fresh and always seasoned properly...which is pretty rare to see in buffets. Love the fresh seafood and the sushi beats most sushi joints in town! Highly recommend.

Once you get past the long lines, the Bacchanal offers a great selection of crab legs, crab claws, seafood, salad, sushi, carving stations, and hot foods. On my visit, the tonkatsu ramen stood out with a creamy, meaty broth and noodles cooked al dente. 

Although a huge spread, Id say everything else was just ok in taste and freshness

$200 for 2 people, we paid to skip the line and still had a long wait. The drinks didn't come out until we were finished eating our first plate. The food was mediocre and looked much better than it tasted. The staff was friendly, but unfortunately I did not get my monies worth.

The service sucked. We saw our waitress twice. Once after flagging her down after about 20 minutes of being seated, and another time towards the end of our meal to deal with our check. The busser ended up taking our drink orders, and bringing us our utensils.... the seafood was really mediocre, if not bad. The prime rib was pretty good with the horseradish, but the other meats were not good. The Asian station had unimpressive food. Nothing was worth writing home about. 

The one redeeming thing of this place was the chocolate mousse. Had about 3 of those, and I'm not even a dessert person.

Hope they come up with a better system for the servers to check on their tables more efficiently.
Best buffet in Vegas, hands down. Only downside is thats expensive and the wait is so long but totally worth it

By far the best buffet in Vegas. Lines can be intimidating but can go by quickly. Been here a couple times but most recently came here and  they didn't serve any fresh oysters. Amazing selection of food and dessert zone. The asian section of food is quite tasty and real cool to have a variety of made to order soup. It is expensive but if you can grub and love to stuff your face this is the place to come.

I came here once during the summer for EDC and just recently for Spring Break and nothings changed. The quality of the food is great, and they offer a wide variety of foods. I came during the transition between lunch and dinner (best of both worlds) and it was well worth it. 

Coming here is like going to food heaven! Comparing it to the world map, you have food from all around the world, like literally!  Although this place is on the pricey side, I think that its a great experience!

Not worth the price. Pictures show lobster and Kingcrabs, but no lobster by themselves & King crabs are $55 per pound after paying buffet price? Non sense. All Asian dishes were salty & blend. The only thing that's worth the price in this place is dessert. Their made to order crepes and gelato bar was good

How in the word could this place be rate at four stars. 

Went there today and let's see EVERYTHING was off temperature, the eggs were  cold and the food not very good.

This is still the best buffet on or off the strip! More options than you can even imagine and very fresh! All the employees are friendly and helpful. If you get here during peak times, expect a wait. But it will definitely be worth it once inside. 
If you want the best Vegas buffet, spend the extra money and eat here. You will not be disappointed!

Let me just say that their selection of food is out of control! Come here hungry because you would want to try everything here and I mean everything! I thoroughly enjoy their seafood; crab, mussels, oysters, shrimps, etc. and their desserts are quite sweet and tasty!

We went on a Thursday night. There was no line and it was mostly empty inside. My wife loved the crab legs and they had rock crab claws. The prime rib was very bland. They did have many things to eat but nothing special. They did have a very exotic Asian fruit like lychee which was the first I've seen. The dessert selection was ok. I don't think I will go back as I've have similar at Paris and Wynn.

The food was good overall. I noticed that many of the cooks plating dishes behind the counters didn't seem to take much pride in their plating, just throwing it on there. Still tasted great though.

One thing that really rubbed me the wrong way, though, is that I paid for a buffet that included KING crab. There was definitely one station that had a sign reading "Snow & King Crab", but after visiting that location 3 times over 2 hours, never once did I see a single piece of king crab. I even asked the employees behind the counter: one shrugged and seemed surprised that they were supposed to have king crab in there. The other one muttered something about it being mixed in, but again, I visited over and over again and there was not a single one to be found. Also, I asked another employee near the HOT crab station on the other side of the buffet, and when I asked him where the king crab was, he laughed at me and seemed surprised when I told him the buffet advertised king crab. KING crab, not snow crab.

Wow!! This buffet doesn't end! Every time I thought I was at the end I was pleasantly surprised by another turn! We had brunch on Sunday morning and I was very pleased with the assortment and variety of items to choose from. I loved the individual dishes and the cast iron skillets perfect size for tasting everything, so cool!! Presentation of the freshly squeezed juices were very fun. The staff was very attentive, much better than the usual buffet experience in town. Overall it was great way to spend the morning and we left very very full!!
Quality went down hill. Use to be the best when they first opened up and slowly the quality went down hill. I was there this weekend and ended up getting a food borne illness... really really bad!

I've been here a few times for brunch and have never been disappointed. There are so many options and the food is quality.  If you get unlimited mimosas, servers refill your drinks before you're done. I've tried wicked spoon but this place is so much better!

My husband and I normally go to the buffet at the MGM but this one was very delicious. The food was on point. Dessert was on point. The only thing not on point is the waiter. Took for ever to clear our table. We wanted to make the most of our bucks but our waiter couldn't keep up with us. We had a party of 5. This place is a must.

I'm not sure why people think this is the best buffet in Las Vegas.  It's definitely a good buffet, but not close to the best.  I'd rank the Wynn, Aria, and Bellagio buffets above this.

Cost-wise, this buffet is pricey.  At over $50/person, it's ridiculous, especially with the crazy lineups.  They have a nice kiosk feature which is great, but still, if you don't plan ahead, you're looking to wait 1-2 hours just to eat.

The worst part is, how the buffet is designed, it's always over capacity.  There's a lineup to get food, after you lineup to get in.  It's crazy.  People lineup to get the seafood items, which aren't very good.  The oysters are tasteless, the crab legs are small and salty, and they don't even have King Crab during the weekdays.

For better value, stick with Aria, Bellagio, or the Wynn!  You get much better bang for your buck.

Bacchanal is the best Vegas buffet on the strip HANDS DOWN!  Be prepared for the wait though... and the hefty price per person, of course.  We waited around 45 minutes on a Tuesday at 9PM.  They were at max capacity at one point too.. ON A TUES!  $50 per person for dinner.  

They have it all from seafood, american, pizza, mexican, asian, sushi, bomb-ass desserts, and more.

My favorites were:

-The oysters on half shell.  They were so good! WTF?! Buffet oysters can be this good?! They didn't have Tabasco which is a MUST for me with oysters but their cocktail sauce with lemon made up for it. 

-Steamed Crab legs.  Although other places steam the crab legs for you... It comes already steamed here - so you don't feel like you're bothering the workers.  

-Juices.  In the mexican food section, they serve fruit juices in little glass milk bottles.  I thought this was so interesting.  They have tamarind, hibiscus, strawberry, mango, and horchata.    

-Lamb & Beef Ribs were SO GOOD!  The texture and seasonings were ON POINT.  I was pretty disappointed with the prime rib though... Maybe it was an off-day?

-I am asian so I had to try one of their noodles w/ broth.  The guy recommended the Ramen broth so I got it with the udon noodles.   IT was SOOO good.  Reminded of a traditional Korean beef broth called sullungtang.   It is not miso based.

-Desserts: They had gelato, ice cream sandwhiches, cake pops, macarons, macaroons, freshly made crepes, and assorted cakes & cookies.  All were yummy.  

Other Vegas buffets usually have 3-4 really good dishes.. I felt that at Bacchanal, EVERYTHING was either pretty good or REALLY bomb!  Ugh.. I gained almost 5 lbs this Vegas trip and BACCHANAL is definitely to blame.  T.T

Well. Maybe I expected too much. Maybe I'm just not a buffet person anymore. 
I guess I was disappointed in the food mostly. The prime rib was just ok, the lamb was terrible and dry, I've had much better bone marrow. The pizza looked like microwave pizza and the Asian selection looked like a typical buffet. In all most of the food was just "ok". 
The high notes: so the seafood buffet was pretty awesome. Tons of crab claws split for you so you could eat more and crack less. The oysters were big and delicious. The salmon dish and shrimp and grits were not good. The jicama salad on the Mexican section was really good and we designed a pretty awesome meat and cheese platter from the Italian section. 
The desserts were AMAZING. I ate one of everything, literally. The creme brûlée was the best I've ever had, the gelato was so fun, made to order crepes, little creamy bites of deliciousness at every turn.  
In all for the VALUE ($169.00) for 2 including the all you can drink wine, beer, mimosa, sangria upcharge, I would say it's worth it. But next time I'll stick to the seafood section and desserts. If I go a next time.

Ah, another good 'ol Friday night in Vegas.  

The clinging smell of cigarette smoke as you stroll through the crowd of patrons trying their luck...

The incessant beeps and chimes of slots machines echoing near and far...

And of course the lovely parade of scantily-clad ladies on their way to the clubs.

Yes it was another glorious night in Sin City.  But amongst all the debaucheries I could've indulged in, I decided to partake in stuffing my face at Caesar's revamped ($17,000,000 that is) Bacchanal Buffet.

HANDS DOWN THE BEST BUFFET ON THE STRIP!!  We all know that Vegas is central to providing some of the best of the best restaurants in the world.  There is a tremendous amount of expectation and high standards to land an eatery on the strip, and Bacchanal did not disappoint.

The food was superb and deserves that distinction in every sense.  Normally you would think of a buffet as serving sub-par, dried-out food that has been sitting under the heat lamp for hours.  Not only that, they've been prodded and molested by the hands of god knows how many people.  But not this one. No no no.  This was the epitome of all buffets.  Everything was served amazingly fresh with the utmost quality.  And from over 500 choices to choose from, that's saying a lot.

I swear Caesars hired a chef from every corner of the world because the variety of food to choose from was unreal.  From dim-sum tapas to freshly steamed crab legs, there was something for everybody.  Cheesy I know.  And speaking of cheese, there also was a cheese bar...and yes you can "wine" all you want.

On top of the usual menu items like prime rib, soups, and salads, they also had various stations where you can request freshly-made entrees.  I confess I have a fetish for pork ramen, and when I came to find out they make it to order with the ingredients I choose, I actually came ;) figuratively that is. Ahem.

The highlight of everything, in my opinion, has to be the dessert bar.  Let's face it, we've all eaten at a buffet to the point of throwing up and yet still find room for dessert.  Now look in the mirror and say it with me, "I'm a fatty".  There are your usual pastries and puddings, but what was really astounding was their very own gelato and crepes bar.  I particularly fell in love with their cheesecake lollipops, especially the cookies and cream one.  Think of a cheesecake on a stick, encrusted with smooth white chocolate, topped with crispy dippin-dots style Oreo cookie crumbles. Good lord...

The buffet was also surprisingly clean.
