I went on the 5th day since it opened so I guess that isn't really saying much, but the service counters (referencing to the aforementioned molestation by many hands) were spotless!  Not one spill mark or greasy tongs; there were waiters on stand-by to clean these up as soon as they occur.  I guess in Caesar's Palace, cleanliness IS next to godliness. 

Service was beyond anything I have ever experienced.  The staff was super friendly and extremely attentive; not one damn detail overlooked.  Drinks were refilled in a flash, requests were greeted with a smile and followed-through with great attention.  We had an amazing waiter, whose name I forgot as I was too busy being a glutton.  He even went to the extent of grabbing bottles of different sauces because we didn't know where to find them.  When he said "I'm gonna be taking good care of you", he wasn't messing around.  I can honestly say that this was the best service I have ever gotten at any restaurant.  I tried to catch a glimpse of his name tag to honorably mention him but the man was so dedicated to providing excellent service that he never stood still.  Bless you, good sir.  You were the Alfred to my Batman.

Bacchanal is truly like no other buffet experience.  If you're on the strip and the borborygmus hits (hopefully only because of hunger), definitely check this place out.  This is THE buffet where you can truly dine like the gods.

-A Roman Feast it is!

This Buffet offers quanity and quality!
 You do need to wait in line to pay but well worth it.I gave this 4 stars because if you are coming to eat stone crab you won't find them. Yep! I was informed people were complaining they were to difficult to open? The rest of the buffet was good. My suggestons 
1. You need to come HUNGRY
2. If you want to take full advantage you want to give yourself time. You might wait in line to serve yourself from the food line.

The buffet is pretty good,  but not necessarily outstanding.  At $59 for Sunday brunch, I would expect higher quality food.  Definitely more than enough selection, but I think some of the items could have been better.  For instance, the sushi selection was sparce and very average.  The Chinese food included some traditional congee, but that was very poorly done - no taste whatsoever, and very lukewarm.   I would have also expected a bit more bang with the desserts.   Service was also below average.   Could not even grab the attention of our waitress to get refills of water.   The impression we got from the waitress was that we were an inconvenience to her - and we try to be very courteous.   Service gets 2.5 stars.  Food gets the 4 stars.

Decided to see if this was really the best buffet in LV, but I got disappointed. 

They had a lot of choices but quality-wise, I wasn't satisfied. The buffet was too pricey for the quality of food although the service was great! But never again am I going to spend $60 per person for this buffet. i've had better buffets in my life.

I'm a bit baffled at all the hype.   Yes, there is a relatively large spread of food (that being said, the layout of the buffet creates the appearance that there is more food than there really is), but there is a corresponding loss in quality.  I found almost every dish I tried quite average and lacking in flavor.  The food has a mass-produced and somewhat processed taste to it.  For example, the paella tasted like it was seasoned with store-bought taco seasoning and the "fresh" jamaica juice tasted like hawaiian punch.  I also thought that the spread lacked creativity - the selection was fairly standard and predictable.  I suspect this buffet gets such good reviews because of the sheer amount of meat (I will admit the seafood is very high quality).  I'm not vegetarian, but if you are, this is definitely not the buffet for you.

I did think that the pastas were tasty.  The desserts were by far the best part of the buffet.  By contrast, the Aria buffet is the best buffet I've had in Vegas, and does laps around Bacchanal in terms of flavor, freshness, and selection (although there might be less food overall at the Aria buffet, there's more variety of ethnic cuisines).

This buffet is an attraction in its own right! The variety is incredible, presentation is exceptional, service is excellent and the food is an all round winner. I would travel to vegas again just to visit this buffet without question!
The brisket is sublime. Head and shoulders above any buffet. Fresh, hot, and flavorful with lots of variety.

I love its all desserts! If I had 2 stomachs, I would eat all of them! Seafood paella and Italian food area were my second choice. I feel like oysters were not fresh for me. I had much better oysters before, so they were kind of disappointment. Overall, good price and a large variety of delightful food.

BEWARE!

My wife and I arrived in Las Vegas for a few days on Saturday.  What better way, we thought, than to start our trip with a meal at one of the best rated buffets in town.

We both had an assortment of buffet items so that we could collectively try as many offerings as possible.  One of the only items that we both had in common were the raw oysters.  She had three, I had fourteen.  It was a costly mistake.

Approximately two hours after our meal, I began to experience stomach pains and we decided to return to our hotel room.  Shortly upon returning to our room, what would be approximately nine hours of strong and very unpleasant diarrhea began to kick in.  Fortunately for my wife, she only experienced mild stomach pain and a little bit of vomiting.  

It was a long first night in Vegas, and not in the type of way that we had pictured it.  

There was lots of great food at the Bacchanal Buffet but my strong advice to anyone reading this is to avoid the oysters.

Ayant déjà fait l'expérience de plusieurs buffets lors de mon précédent séjour dans cette ville de folie, je ne m'imaginais pas la quitter cette année sans retenter l'expérience d'une orgie de nourriture !

C'est par hasard en lisant un dépliant que nous avons appris l'ouverture  un mois avant notre arrivée d'un nouveau buffet au Ceasars Palace (juste en face de notre hôtel donc), le descriptif vantant la cuisine raffinée et la décoration moderne avait finir de nous convaincre, cette année ce serait celui-ci !

Première impression : le descriptif ne mentait pas la décoration est moderne et assez classe, c'est très lumineux et agréable et le service est tout à fait en accord avec le lieu !

Une fois la note payée, c'est parti pour un festival de nourriture avec des associations dans l'assiette assez improbables... c'est ça de vouloir goûter un peu à tout ! 
Missions toutefois impossible tant l'offre est pantagruélique, pas moins de 9 stations proposant un éventail de toute les cuisines du monde.

Je ne vais pas vous décrire tout ce que nous avons goûté mais les oeufs brouillés étaient excellents (fait assez rare), les french toasts avec céréales très sympas, et le mini burger l'un des meilleurs de tout le séjour !!!
Même le café passe bien, et ça ce n'est vraiment pas courant !

Beaucoup de plats sont proposés sous la forme de petites portions individuelles, non seulement c'est assez agréable à l'oeil mais en plus ça évite d'avoir les yeux plus gros que les ventre en se servant et ça permet de goûter facilement à plus de choses

Bon après le salé et après avoir déjà goûté 4-5 desserts, je décide de me calmer un peu et de finir sur une note rafraîchissante, direction le bar à glaces !
Ce sera donc "figue balsamique" : original et bon, et surtout pour finir en apothéose "Mango chile lime" et alors là ça envoie du très lourd, tout est bien là piment y compris !!!

Petite astuce : comme dans de nombreux buffets à Las Vegas, si vous venez un peu avant la fin du breakfast, vous pourrez profiter de la fin du breakfast et du lunch en ne payant que le breakfast qui est moins cher (mais pas d'inquiétude tout le monde est au courant !)
The best buffet on the strip! Just a bit expensive. There were plenty to eat. I'm going back next year.
Lots of choices. Enjoyed the crepe made in front of me. The roasted tomatoes and roasted mushrooms were especially good. We came for breakfast and will be full until supper. We will be back.

Booked a room for my husbands birthday because we have always wanted to stay at the Cesar's hotel and were excited to try the buffet and besides it being WAY over priced ALL the food was cold or room temperature and all the seafood smelled so bad. I was honestly so shocked at how such an upscale hotel could have such a poor buffet. Would never come back

Ate here last night, waited about 20 minutes to get in on a Monday at around 7 pm. The food was blah, king crab legs had no meat, oysters were musky, not creamy and sweet. The prime rib was ok but they ran out for over 20 minutes, the guy keep saying "its coming". The gelato had only three flavors. The dessert table was pretty empty. The sushi bar did not have sashimi. It is not worth the $50.00 plus price.

We went to the buffet for breakfast. The selection of foods was amazing. 
Everything was fresh and tasty, and the food was kept up to high standard even though it is a buffet. 
The presentation was awesome and good service in all stations.
Although the price is pretty steep ($25/person), It is well worth it.
Consider going a bit later (The breakfast is serves from 7am to 11 am) and make it a brunch :) You will definitely wont want lunch after!

This is about a $50+ buffet. Food was good. Selection was great. Depending on your food allergies it is going to be a hit or miss but there were a lot of options. We went for breakfast and definitely ate a good portion. However I am not sure it was worth the $50 we paid. Service was OK but nothing fantastic.

Arrived at the Buffet for the weekend Brunch at 10:15 AM. There was no line at the entrance and we were seated immediately. Our arrival timing was perfect because we left at 12:15 PM the line was extremely long. The buffet area is expansive with a large seating area and the food stations well spaced. The food quality was good and a variety of items. 
The Posole was a welcome surprise as it is not available on most buffets. This one had a great flavor. The crawfish boil was way to much effort to remove a small amount of meat from the crawfish. The crab legs were very good but small. Requires you load up the plate.
Overall when the cost is factored in the Brunch Buffet is 3 stars. I don't foresee another trip anytime soon as I wasn't impressed.
Always good food, I go back whenever I'm in Vegas. Their pazole was fantastic, sushi was great, and I love the desserts!

Bacchanal is definitely one of the higher end buffet options in Vegas. We went during Easter weekend and it was a bit pricey that entire weekend at 59.99. 

There's always a line at Bacchanal but they do message you when it is your turn to come in. The buffet was divided into different section including asian, italian, seafood and dessert. I am sure I missed a few sections. 

They had quite a bit of exotic fancier foods such as bone marrow, elk burger and American Wagyu during the Easter special. 

There was also a taco and crepe station that was made to order. They also had a noodle bar that was custom made and included noodles options such as pho, wonton soup, laksa, ramen and few others as well. You definitely have to shell out the money and try it once!

so we decided to give the latest and greatest buffet on the LV strip a try.  After glamouring recommendations from friends about this joint, we stopped by.

at close to $50 per person, we decided to "upgrade" to the fatty pass (24 hour buffet pass) for ~63 per person.  That way our money is evenly distributed upon the gluttony that was about to ensue over the next 24 hours.  We timed our visit precisely at 9PM, so we can enjoy a second dinner the following night, like a true fatty would.

enough about the caveats and more about the buffet.  if you eat with your eyes first, like me, then your mouth was watering just walking by the buffet to the table.  the decor was eccentrically classy.  the layout was great, the food looked A-MAZE-ZING (hard Z on the third syllable).  kobe beef sliders were yummy.  shrimp cocktail were HUGE, you could sink your teeth into it!

I will definitely be back to this buffet with obesity on my mind and a vengeance on my appetite.

This is an updated review in light of my holiday experience.

Since my first time at Bacchanal, I've been here an additional four or so times, and it's always gotten better each time. More crab leg stations, "fresh-squeezed" or (SUGAR WATER? the horror!) juices in cute bottles, great ginseng soup, and never-ending food and desserts. FIVE STARS for the past.

FOUR STARS now during the Christmas holidays (and even last year during the Christmas holidays). Here are a few things to keep in mind (for people eating at Bacchanal and for Bacchanal's own improvement):

ITEMS THAT HAVE DISAPPEARED (AT LEAST DURING THE HOLIDAYS)
- GINSENG SOUP: Where did it go? How do you get rid of one of the staples at Bacchanal and replace it with ... sweet and sour soup?  That's blasphemy.  Unfortunately, Bacchanal seems to have done away with this soup. Even the waitstaff said that they haven't seen the soup for a couple of weeks.

- MACARONS and SOUFFLE:  How do you run out of dessert by 6:15 p.m.?  If you pay an arm and a leg to eat at Bacchanal, the last thing you should be doing as an all-you-can-eat buffet is run out of items halfway into dinner service. And the worst thing you can say to your customers is that you won't be making it at all anymore. I thought this was a buffet, and Caesar's Palace should be prepared for the holiday rush and demand.  

- LINE:  During the holidays, the line is horrendous and was quoted as a four-hour wait. TERRIBLE. They used to give out bottled water while you wait in line, but I don't see that kind of service happening anymore. If people are going to wait half their afternoon for dinner, it'd for Caesar's Palace to bring back some of their service to create an overall pleasant experience.

-------------

To be fair, this is still the best buffet in Vegas in terms of selection, quality, venue, overall experience and nomness.

I've been to Bacchanal twice now - once for dinner and once for breakfast/brunch/lunch with unlimited mimosas. Yes, you will wait in line whether VIP or minion, and, yes, once you are seated, you'll gaze around and notice empty tables, pound your tiny fists upon your own, and declare, "Well, what took so long?!" 

Just forget it. Let the food and lively service take over. Walk to the Asian-inspired corner and pop boas and sushi upon your plate - don't take too much, you'll want to try everything. Move on to the noodles and soups, cheeses and charcuterie, the carving station, omelets to order (if breakfast!), bite size pans of truffled potatoes au gratin. Do you want shrimp and seafood? Head to the front of the buffet - ceviche awaits, snow crab legs taunt, giant shrimp beg for lemon or sauce - only to be popped into awaiting mouths. There's mac n cheese to faint over, Italian dishes to feign over and enough good stuff to go around that no one's going to be fighting over anything.

Despite having been here twice, I have made the mistake of not visiting the dessert station - or, island. I'm not a huge sweets gal so that's why, but it does look lovely! 

Our server, Jules, on our last visit for breakfast/brunch was phenom. She kept the mimosas flowing and us laughing. Major props to her for working her tail off and keeping our plates off the table.

Definitely worth a visit - there's a Groupon for breakfast currently and if you get there around 10 a.m. for pancakes and other sweets, they'll start flipping to lunch at 10:30 - the best of both words, amiright?

Just Wow (once you get through the misearble long line that is).  So many decadent options ... definitely possible to eat your money's worth ... unless you're allergic to seafood (which I, happily, am not!).

There are different stations organized by cuisine.  I ended up trying most things from each (and obviously some things more than others).  Not to brag, but my buffet prowess, though having faded a bit with age, is still pretty impressive, so much so that the people at the next table asked me at one point how it was possible I could still keep eating.  

A few tips:  

~  DON'T start with the American station - that'll fill you up too quickly with all the fried, BBQ and starch (read: hot dog buns are NOT your friend).  Save tasting these for the end.  

~  Also try to go light on the dim sum and noodles at the Asian station and pastas/pizzas at Italian (though I'll admit I love Italian and the station was right next to our table, so I did break my own rule on that one - the truffled polenta and veal lasagne were delicious!!).  

~  The best bang for your buck is obviously the seafood stations - the crab legs, oysters, mussles and various ceviches are all super fresh and unlimited for your taking (and take I did!).  

~  The dessert station was a masterpiece of shapes, texture and colors, but only a couple of the options really stood out taste-wise.

Despite this being a buffet, the atmosphere was quite classy and the decor ultra sleek and modern.  I thought the price was very reasonable (I think it was only $90 for 2, plus tip), especially considering bottomless champagne and mimosas are included in the tab.

All in all, way better than the Bellagio buffet, which I enjoyed but is glaringly out-dated and out-classed compared to Bacchanal.  (I've yet to try Wicked Spoon)

This is by far my favorite buffet in Vegas.  They have the best choices and the quality of food is hands down the best.  

If you happen to come here before 3pm on a weekend, mimosas are included in the fee.  Def try to get here before the cutoff time to take advantage of the bubbly.  They offer all types of cuisines.  The buffet offers crab legs, succulent shrimp cocktail, prime rib, brisket, along with your typical carnivorous meats, Mexican food, Chinese, sushi and you can create your own pho/ramen too.  Their dessert selection is off the chain!!! So much too choose from so try to leave a bit of room for the sweets!  

If I had one complaint it would be the check in process.  I recently noticed this last visit they implemented a check in time for parties.. You walk to a screen and enter the number of people in your party and are given a print out that says the time you check back with the front hostess.  This can take up to two + hours. Once you get to this point, you get in line to pay.  This is where I feel like the employees did more chatting than working efficiently.  Our group was given two diff instructions from two diff ladies that conflicted each other's instructions, making it seem like they were both not on the same page regarding protocol.

Good food, lot of varieties, nice ambience, good service, drinks are included in the buffet, it's crowded this is the bad part I didn't like about this place !!! We had to wait 10mins in line to get lobster, this was a huge turn off, This is the reason why I am giving 3. If you have patience to wait in line after paying $47/person for the buffet it's a good place to eat it.

Great place to eat!  You must bring your appetite, there's so much variety. It has so ma y differ stations with multiple varieties of food.  It's pricey but well effort it if you are hungry and want some great tasting food. I couldn't tell you walkathons to eat...just try everything!

I decided to splurge for my sister and I yesterday, Sunday January 17th since I won some $$$ the night before. 
We got there around 9:30am-wait was nonexistent, which was a relief since I'd read there can be long waits w/o an express pass. We didn't order the unlimited beverage package(additional $15pp) since we aren't big drinkers). I did mention we were in Vegas to celebrate my sis' birthday and noted she wrote 'Birthday' on our table receipt. Our server was Alexandria, and she gave us awesome service! Beverages were brought out quickly and dirty plates whisked away in a timely manner...I commend her for the congenial 'service with a smile' even though she had five or six tables in her station and was kept pretty busy!

Now about the food...for the price($49.99 for weekend brunch served 8am-3pm. Note that it is an additional $10 more after 3pm), the exceptional quality of the food is well worth the price!!!!

Here are my standout faves with pics posted:
Lobster Benedict was heavenly-hollandaise sauce perfection perfection! Prime rib was sliced thin and bleeding rare just as I requested. The seasoned peppered crust was the best part! Ate my share of crab legs and mussels, but they weren't anything extraordinary to rave about. The inclusion makes the brunch a bit more easy to stomach price-wise.
Sis had sushi but wasn't impressed by taste or quality from the two pieces she sampled. She rated it average.
I did luv luv luv the congee(Chinese rice porridge), which needed the requisite shredded pork, chopped green onions and pickled radishes-yes, provided  on the side to add! 
Alexandria, our server, brought over a birthday dessert place for my sis, which was a nice touch. Overall, we'd definitely visit again. Lots of choices, great variety of dishes for meat eaters, vegetarians or picky eaters.
My suggestion is to sample a little of everything that appeals to you...food is freshly prepared so ENJOY.
Now I can say I've been to the Bacchanal at Caesars!!!

My all time-favorite buffet of LAS VEGAS. Bacchanal...yes bacch - ANAL...named formerly from the God of Wine and Festivities/Intoxication...BACCHUS!

Anywho...this buffet is a MUST GET for me. I WILL NOT LEAVE VEGAS WITHOUT DINING HERE! YEs its that GUUD! In fact...I would even be willing to skip out on a night of clubbing to dine here! Yep thats right...I would rather get a table at BACCHANAL vs. XS, MARQUEE, SURRENDER, etc...

Heres a lil 411 on this buffet. Caesars Palace placed $15 MILLION into this buffet. Let me say this again...they put $15 FREAKING MILLION! With over 25,000 square feet and over 500 items to choose from...yah this place is going to be guud. Lets go on an adventure inside...

What makes this place so guud? Here are my reasons and some things; errrr I mean many things that stand out to me:
-most buffets are either known for their quantity (but with high quantity comes low quality) or quality (with high quality...comes with low quantity). This place has the right balance of both but to an even greater extent. In my world and my eyes...BACCHANAL has the MOST QUANTITY WITH THE HIGHEST QUALITY!
-No joke...this buffet line is LONG!
-the orange juice here...next to the seafood section...this is seriously the best tasting orange juice that Ive ever had. If there was a GUINNESS BOOK WORLD RECORDS ON BEST TASTING ORANGE JUICE...this place would have to be it
-I usually judge a buffet by its prime rib, pasta, fried chicken, and pizza. Yes the prime rib is so tender and juicy. Yes the pasta is al dente to the correct italian taste w/o any liquidy runny pasta sauce. The fried chicken is crisp and juicy...just how its suppose to be. And the pizza...finally...crust with a crunch...and toppings that dont slide off as your about to bite into it. WIN!
-they have a noodle bar! Big plus for me...I love noodles...especially as a hangover meal. The selection they have are: PHO, UDON, RAMEN
-I love HOT AND SOUR SOUP...any buffet with this soup is a win! and this place has it! Obviously Im a huge noodle fan...my lil secret is to get noodles from the asian noodle bar...and add hot and sour soup to it. One of my favorite Taiwanese/Chinese soup and noodle dishes.
-the BBQ and MEAT section....drool for days that I could make a puddle. The BRISKET...errr maiii godd. So guud. They also have a variety of sausages...from turkey to spiced to artisan, etc... FAT SLABS OF BACON...yes thats right!! and others as well too
-a TACO BAR? cant be that great right? WRONG! with their homemade salsas and avocado sauce...the tacos are quite yummy to be honest.
-etc...

As you can see...and from the ratings and blogs from all over the net...BACCHANAL...is the number 1 buffet in Vegas...and definitely top 3 if not. It is a must go for everyone...and obviously me of course. 

Put this way...when I come to vegas...its not that Im excited to gamble...its not that Im excited to night club...its not that Im excited to day party (well sometimes I am)...IM EXCITED TO EAT AT BUFFETS...specifically this one!

VERY VERY WELL RECOMMENDED...this is a MUST GO!

UNTIL THEN!! ^-^

Had Christmas special dinner here. The line was crazy. We came over around noon and planned to get lunch. Ended up getting a ticket from machine to come back at 4:30pm. After we came back, we waited in line for another 1 hour until we were finally seated! You could pay 50 dollars per person to skip the line or be a member. The food was great though! Very fresh oysters, shrimps, crabs, sea snails, and lobster tail. Lobster pot pie was also delicious. The Peking duck was amazing. There's a large variety of desserts too but they were not as impressive as the food.

I am not usually a fan of buffets but this is by far the best buffet out there.  My girlfriend and I ate there again last Saturday for brunch.  I hear the line is usually one to two hours long.  Fortunately, I have a Platinum Total Rewards card so we only had to wait about five minutes.  They do offer an express line pass for $25 per person for those who do not have a player's card and don't want to wait in the main line.  The weekend brunch is $106 for two people.  They offer All-You-Can-Drink Miller Lite, Mimosa and Bloody Mary's.  They do have a two hour dining limit but I'm sure it's not enforced.  The variety and quality of food is amazing.  My favorite is the steamed crab legs (already split open) and the jumbo pealed shrimp.  The guy working the carving station absolutely LOVES his job and spreads the happy vibe to everyone he comes in contact with.  It is always nice to see him. 

The only complain I have is the music.  The music can be quite LOUD and obnoxious, especially if you are seated under a ceiling speaker.

It had all the regular buffet foods. Don't get me wrong most of it was good, I love a delicious buffet but I didn't feel like they had anything unique. My favorite part was the crepes. The crab was good, we asked for our crab to be warmed. They had a lot of Asian food. It was more of a lunch type brunch buffet. Overall, it was a good buffet. I don't know that we will go back because we found another buffet with comparable pricing that we liked better. These buffets aren't cheap but I'm happy to pay when it's a good quality buffet!

The staff was 50/50. Our server wasn't great. I had to constantly wave for more drink. The bus guy was great, he was quick and kind. I watched another server act inappropriately with a table of guys, nothing too bad but she was flirting the whole time and then gave each them cheek to cheek side hugs and whispered in one of their ears. It was uncomfortable. Our server saw it too and looked just as uncomfortable. But I guess it is Vegas so I guess I shouldn't complain.

Holy cow.

I'd heard about Vegas buffets before but had never eaten at one.  After having breakfast at Bacchanal buffet one morning during my most recent stay, I get it now.

Not only was I full until dinnertime, I also had the choice to eat pretty much anything my heart desired.  The wide range of foods went anywhere and everywhere from shrimp cocktail to chilequiles, beef chow fun to pizza.  Mind you, this was at 7am when they opened.  Don't ask me why I was up at 7, and yes, I had gone to bed from the night before.

I stayed pretty much within the realm of standard breakfast indulgence, eggs benedict, breakfast potatoes (I had my choice of at last four types,) bacon, a frittata type dish with Brussels sprouts and other veg, SLAB BACON.  Dude, they were carving SLAB BACON to order.  The slice I got was like a friggin' steak.  Graham and I had to share it.  They also had breakfast burritos, shrimp and grits, bagels...

In addition to stuffing myself (c'mon... this buffet was over $40 per person, did you think I wasn't going to make sure I didn't have to eat again until dinner?) with those items, I did get down on some shrimp cocktail, smoked trout, mussles, and a TON of great coffee.

Bacchanal buffet.  I'm not normally a buffet fan.  At all.  But you're a'ight in my book.

Uh. Just yes. Yes to everything about this place. Huge selection of food, And mostly everything was delicious. They have some very original desserts, namely the jasmine rice pudding. Who does that?!?!? So good!! A buffet is a buffet...you'll find the usuals: crab legs, carving station with meats, Asian section, etc. But there was nothing mediocre about any of it at Bacchanal. I loved every second of my life here. Take me back!

I was there on 10-30-18.  I took my mom there for early dinner.  But right when we got there, there sprung a leak through the roof by the carving station.  It made it dripping wet and towels and then chained off the area was very unappealing.  

They should of asked how the patrons are doing while this was happening.  But we got nothing from management with no apology for being so inconvenient.  The point being it was an expensive dinner with the leaking right where they serve the meat.  

I didn't like the oyster shooter either.  The wagyu meat was somewhat tough. The crab legs should be cut in half so we don't have to crack and use so much time doing it.  The stone crab claws was okay.  It was just a pain to get to the meat after cracking without small folk to pick at the meat.  

Maybe they should have 2-3 sushi chefs to make individual hand rolls.  If u do have that, sorry for not noticing.

Staff gets 5 stars for being so good to the patrons. 
Food gets 3.5 stars.

I'm sorry to say this Buffet has surpassed the Bellagio Buffet interms of food selection and ambiance, making it #1 on my list of top Vegas buffets. My aunt wanted to treat us for lunch and so she decided to take us to Bacchanal Buffet because she had a great experience with the range of food offerings. The modern design of the buffet makes this place relaxing along with the hip music. The last time I was here was when this buffet was the Lagos Buffet and I wasn't impressed at all and being in Caesar's Palace, you'd thought it would be on par with the Bellagio or Wynn Buffet. WRONG!

I went during lunch time on a Monday and there wasn't a line so we just went straight to the buffet. Just by looking at the new chic design of the buffet, I knew I wouldn't be disappointed, the first section on your left was the seafood and I just had to have the cocktail shrimp first as always but crab legs were only offered during dinner time.

 =/

The cocktail shrimp didn't disappoint, I tried the lobster melody or lobster chowder and that was very good and creamy. The meat station always had a long line but the wait was worth it and included;  hot links, fresh sliced bacon, wild turkey, beef brisket and your choice of sauce for the meat. On the far left side of the buffet was the Asian section, tucked away in the corner that included, Chinese, Vietnamese and sushi, the food was excellent and tasted like it came from a 5 star Asian restaurant. They also had a Mexican, Italian and dessert section. I must warn you not to skip the dessert section and save some room in your stomach for your sweet tooth. The dessert section was designed with glasses all around the top of the dessert island and glass in blue and yellow squares gives it a chic touch. I went to the crepe station where they make your crepe but you personalize it yourself with toppings and different flavors of sauce they leave out. The mini muffins were very sweet and so was the tangerine cake. 

The customer service was excellent and they always refilled my drinks and checked how everything was and the quality of the food. First time diners were given a tour by their host about the location of each station and what food was offered, I thought was very nice. Caesars really has stepped up on this buffet and sorry to say has outdone the Bellagio, Aria and Wynn Buffet.

My new list of Top Buffets in Vegas include:

1. Caesar's Palace - Bacchanal Buffet 

2. Bellagio - The Buffet

3. Aria - Buffet of Aria

4. Wynn - The Buffet

5. Planet Hollywood - Spice Market Buffet

This is probably the best buffet we had in vegas while we were there. We decided to go on a weekday so that there'll be less if a line which worked out quite nicely! Arrived at 10:45 and there were only a group of 8 people in front of us, hardly a line, AND because we got to the cash 5 minutes before 11AM we ended up paying the breakfast price for the lunch menu. They have a 2hr sitting rule where they expect you to finish eating within 2 hours, which is very do-able, but don't worry, they don't kick you out if you don't leave immediately after 2 hours. We stayed for about 2.5 hours and nobody said anything. 

Now for the food, compared to other buffets, this one probably has the most variety, and my parents definitely enjoyed the vast choices of Asian dishes which were pretty well made. The other thing they loved, the crab (and various other seafoods). Although to be honest, the crab at Bellagio was better, but this was still pretty awesome. For those of you who love comfort food there are delicious Mac and cheeses, mini burgers, fried chicken, wings etc which were also pretty fantastic, though if you have a bird stomach like me I wouldn't suggest those choices cause they'll fill you up real fast and you hadn't even gotten to the sushi table yet. 

There was a lot of food and I had to make 3 different rounds before I actually made my way through the entire selection (and that's not counting the dessert round). That said, it's very nice that they do make small portions, very delicately presented in tiny bowls/dishes/baskets, unless it's the one you portion yourself. Which I appreciated, so that I don't over indulge in any one item. 

There's also a juice bar with a variety of juices, some of them are just Snapple I'm pretty sure, but there were a few that were fresh juices (like fresh watermelon juice yum!) 

The dessert table is a bit smaller than the one at the wicked spoon, but it still offers a pretty good variety. 

The service was also pretty good, dishes were cleared very quickly and you never even see them taking them away! (So watch out of you're not done your dish yet!) 

The décor is also very contemporary and comfortable. Nothing to complain about. The bathrooms are outside of the actual eating area though so it was a little confusing at first trying to find it. 

All in all good food, good experience, just try to plan a way that you don't have to wait 2 hours to go in... weekdays, or go a little early and just have an early meal, you'll be holding your belly for the rest of the day anyway!

Ask for Maryam as your server!

I've had the pleasure of visiting the Bacchanal Buffet several times. The food has always been wonderful and the wait staff sometimes awesome and other-times just OK. This last time was so spectacular I feel I have to leave a review. The experience was so wonderful because we got Maryam as our server. She kept our drinks coming and gave us tips on foods to try that we had missed or were tucked away in the middle of the desert area. She went beyond what any other server has ever done for us at this buffet. I'm going to ask for her next time! 

Don't miss out on this buffet. The food is awesome and the deserts, oh my. I wish I could take them home.

Don't come for a holiday like July 4th. I looked forward to this place all year because I came last year and it was amazing. Rather disappointed at the overcooked meats, unclean oysters with a sea smell and lots of sand, and pretty much sad. I think they were just overcrowded and slacked off on quality food. This was one of my most expensive meals in Vegas and also one of the most disappointing ones.

Been here twice now, once for lunch and dinner. I'm pretty sure they have the same things for both so lunch would definitely be better worth your money.

I loved the crab station and you can take it back near the pastas to be steamed. The truffle potato was incredible and you could pick them up on little hot plates using small rubber plate holders. Sushi was also fairly impressive since I never expect Asian food to be anything worth having at a buffet.

The dessert station was what made me suppress all my thoughts of imploding. There's a crepe station where you can add on your favorite toppings, and all of the baked goods were delicious. My favorite had to be the crème brûlée. Top that off with some of the freshly whipped cream (from the crepe station) and..well I had like a million of those. 

Definitely a place to try at least once in Vegas if you're looking for a buffet.

We were a little leery to try a buffet especially with a mix of reviews. They offer a large variety of food and drinks that ate specialties around the world! 

Everything we ate was amazing!!! They didn't give us any directions as to how to go about getting beverages but after our waiter came by, we really liked him! 

HUGE dessert selection:)

I worked for Caesars for 7+ years and was on property when Lago was the only buffet....the comparison is just like night and day! The improvements are an A++! Food was phenomenal and this is now THE BuFFET in Las Vegas! Move over Wynn, Bellagio and Cosmo!!!  I've tried all of the competitors and for the price....bacchanal tops the list!  Seafoods were fresh and NOT salty! Dim Sum selections were so good and the duck and char siu were yummy!! They also have a tomahawk rib eye that was so juicy and tender!  There are your usuals like American, Mexican and Italian but I think the seafood and Asian dishes were my fave! For desserts there were just so many selections....the have mochi ice cream too! The best was their fresh made to order crepes....the fresh whipped cream and berries were just so tasty!! We went on a weekday at about 3 pm so there was a small line but we waited less than 5 minutes and were seated...our server was so attentive and refilled drinks constantly! She was even nice to being me decaf hot tea and lemons...just a very good meal! Bacchanal keep it up!!!
Good Food, but over priced. Not worth the extra expense.

This used to be my fav buffet. Not any more!!! We came for brunch on sat and as a diamond member we got to cut the line. No point it that, the lady up front doesn't know the members club works and let maybe 30 general public before us. Also breakfast items are limited and not vegetarian friendly

Throughout the Vegas trip we kept hearing about the..

"..#1 BUFFET IN VEGAS.."

..."#1 BUFFET IN THE NATION."


I just had to see if this #1 thing was the real deal. Each person was about $50...there was an extremely large line. If you wanted to go in faster you could pay more $$

[Location]
Inside Caesar's palace. Very large areas to sit inside. Fancy BUT COMFORTABLE CHAIRS. 

- - - Selections- - - 

Obviously you develop a plan. Seafood, expensive food, uncommon pricey food, high-end version favorites, and comfort foods.

[Asian section] (So much variety: Chinese- Dim Sum, Vietnamese-Pho, Indonesian, Thai, Indian, Japanese- sushi pretty good)= 4 out of 5

[Mexican section] Didn't try. Looked good

[American/Meats]- Hit or miss with some, Mac and cheese was light but creamy

[Pizza] SO GOOD. SAUCE IS LITTLE SWEET.

[Seafood] Heard crab legs were ok-good. I tried the salmon and that was delicious. Lobster corn chowder was nice but kinda salty.

[Veggies/Fruit] Pretty small, less veggies but more fruit (fresh)

[Dessert] Impressive: icecream, cookies, freshly made crepes

 ----------

Overall: Filled me up, seemed like some items were lacking in something, worth the trip and experience.

There's definitely an amazing selection of food at Bacchanal, sure to please the most discerning of diners in Vegas. I visited this much hyped buffet last weekend, but unfortunately was unable to really get my $60's worth since I started feeling unwell once we sat down at the table (thanks to the hard shots I took earlier in the afternoon - never consume alcohol on a near empty stomach!). Fortunately, Bacchanal has the likes of pho and this God-like Chinese chicken ginseng soup (which comes in little pots, too), and after a few of those, I started to feel a bit better. I grabbed a few plates of good stuff and scoured some of the desserts, but like said, I just feel I didn't eat up to anywhere near what I paid for.

The set up and design of the buffet is modern, but has the elegance that Vegas buffets are known for. 

The biggest downer for me aside from how my head was hurting was the service. Our waitress technically did do her job, but drinks came slow and she even served two guests in our party by slamming cups down when we asked for coffee. Not very professional (accidental or not), and we were given one carafe with a broken spout. Also, given that our party was billed a 15% gratuity fee since we had a large group (which might I add totaled to near $100), we expected service to be up to par. Not cool.

I'm disappointed due to personal reasons, but I know I will definitely be back again to redeem myself. And for sure no more pre-alcohol next time!

Overall, our experience was disappointing.  Dinner on Saturday, so of course the wait was long - to be expected.

However, I was shocked at the cost, $57.99 per person plus tax.  The meats were OK, but not a high quality.  Lots of shrimp and crab claws which were good, average Italian and Mexican.  

Deserts were good, lots of selection.

At $57.99 per person, there is no value.  For the same amount, a restaurant woudl have been a far better choice.

We went here for dinner around 530 PM with a group of 10 on a Sunday evening. Line wasn't bad at all but it definitely got busier after we were inside the buffet. Huge variety of options that will satisfy any palate - except probably not the best place for vegetarians. Definitely expensive, about $75 per person for dinner. The seafood is in the front and includes crab legs, oysters, shrimp, etc. The shrimp were huge and I was told the oysters tasted great. They also has freshly boiled crab legs at the back of the buffet near the Italian food. Those were a hit or miss - my first place tasted great but the second plate we got was too salty. They have a bunch of meat options including prime rib, wagyu, tri tip, bacon and brisket. The night we went the tri tip was really tough and the wagyu didn't have much flavor but the other cuts tasted great. Some dishes I really enjoyed were the mushroom and arugula pizza with truffle oil, the mashed potatoes and the French fries. Also loved all the dessert options and appreciated that they came in small portions for someone like me that just wants a taste of everything.

Overall a great buffet but really pricy. If you're only doing on buffet in Vegas and you're feeling like shelling out money, this is definitely a great place to go. Probably won't be back here for a while though due to price.

I am not going to go against the tide here. People love this buffet, I love this buffet, my family loves this buffet, all my friends that go to buffets love this buffet. 

We go just about every time we are in vegas and have time. Yes the lone is long but we usually pay the extra 25 a person to get express or if we are early I pop and audiobook on my phone and wait the line out.

Most recently the pork dumplings and the duck were just to die for. I went back for thirds. I had a crepe made with Nutella and cinnamon, topped with bananas and mixed fruit. I thought I had died and went to heaven.

Yes this is a buffet, but there is always a nice grouping of things here that are better than at most restaurants out there for even the same price. Believe me when I say the duck was out of this world. 

Thus is the number 1 dinner buffet in vegas. It is also the best dinner buffet west of the rockies. Nothing in Los Angeles compares.

The food is fantastic and everything one would expect it to be for this price-point (thus the second star in our rating). The process, however, is like gourmet dining at a McDonalds. This buffet is larger than Caesar's can manage. While the manager did quickly fix our many service complaints, it was clear that the system is so broken, the employees are not the problem here. Write this one off your list and blame the Vegas corporate system that brought you 6-5 blackjack and triple zero roulette for its irrevocable downfall. We won't be returning again.

B est buffet in Vegas
A ll you can eat
C harges you $65
C hoose from hundreds of dishes
H eavenly place
A mazed by the seafood selection
N eed a nap after getting food coma
A wesome service
L ove love love!

Dine at Bacchanal to feed not only your tummy, but also your eyes. The presentation of the dishes are really Instagram worthy! 

Eat until you can't. And then get dessert. There's always room for dessert. (And the dessert at Bacchanal is out of this world!)

We arrived at 2pm on a Sunday to be welcomed by a long line. According to our ticket, our wait time was anticipated to be 69 minutes. Fortunately, it was misguiding and we ended up being seated at 2:30pm. As champagne brunch was ending soon, we were allowed to double dip into dinner.

My favorites were the raw oyster bar, salami and cheese platters, and prime rib. I love it when my prime rib is done perfectly at medium rare. It was particularly juicy and tender with the right amount of fat. The Jonah crab legs were a slight disappointment. Since there was such a high demand for them, they couldn't supply them quick enough and some were still frozen. The udon came as a surprise. It is not what one would usually go for at a buffet but we decided to give it a try. The noodles were very absorbent of the broth which was very strong. 

Other than the entrees, the juice bar and dessert station were very pleasing. There was a wide selection of beverages, ranging from guava to horchata. The dessert station was so vast that by feasting there alone would have equaled to a whole day's worth of calories.

We went on Saturday for a late lunch.  It's pretty good; it's a buffet.  Like some others have posted... there is a great variety, but none of that matters if it doesn't really taste good.  The decor is nice and it's designed well, but other than that, it's a buffet.  I will say that it is probably the best on the strip.

If you are going to Vegas and really want to enjoy every bit of it and going to a great buffet then going to bacchanal is such an easy choice. Without a doubt I will be going back next time I go to Vegas. If anyone has any hesitation about going because you can probably go to a cheaper buffet in Vegas then I will say all the other ones don't pay attention to the small details that they have here. Can't say it enough I loved it and will be going again.

Came here for lunch with the wife. We tried A LOT of different foods and a lot of it was just OFF. Cioppino, menudo and pozole broth tasted like it was canned. NO BUENO. Prime rib was cold. Underwhelming experience to say the least...

STOP LOOKING FOR OTHER BUFFETS!
This is the buffet you wanna go if in Vegas. Trust me ive been to others and they have nothing on this buffet. The selection of food/drinks is excellent and the service is top notch. Also a really nice place. 
Better be very hungry if going there as you would like to try everything and there is so many different things to try.
Only negative side would be that the bathroom is not easily accessible as its not inside the buffet. Seriously that is the only bad thing.
Have an epic feast!
I think the best buffet I've had in Vegas so far. Spendy, but worth it.

While driving across the country we knew we would be driving through Las Vegas. Other than the hotels we were staying in, this was the only must see/ eat stop. We had a hard time finding the right parking lot. The attendants kept directing us to diffent lots.  At the 3rd one we just parked and walked through the casino. It was hard to find the restaurant too. Once we did, we waited in line. I have read some other reviews than mention a 3+ hr. wait. I am not sure if it was because we were there on a weekday or we just lucked out and only waited 20 min. 
The amount of food is a bit overwhelming. The buffet spans multiple rooms. The food was good. For the price paid I was expecting better than good. I tried so many things that I can't even think of them individually. I wish I would have eaten less of "food," and saved more room for desserts. In my book, they were superior to the food. The chocolate creme brule was balanced well. Not too sweet. The top stayed crunchy while sitting out. They have an amazing array of sorbets, in sophisticated flavors. The fig and balsamic vinegar sorbet was magic. I could eat it everyday.  The desserts were of a much higher caliber than the other items.
It would take multiple meals to truly taste everything. Unfortunately, at the price they charge, even if we had more time, the one meal will have to suffice.
In a word.......awesome!   Food was four star restaurant quality.  Service was fair.  Price was HIGHISH for a buffet.   Again it was good.

Really good. Great variety. A little overpriced.

We went for an early dinner, around 5 PM, so we didn't have to wait to get in. The selection is tremendous, for sure. The seafood is really good, my personal favorite being the crawfish. The shrimp, salmon, and tilapia were all worth getting again, too.

The rest of the food was good, some of it very good. The best thing my husband and I tried were the made to order mini tacos. We got a couple with beef, pico, and guacamole. Great flavor and good quality ingredients.

The desserts were really good. I loved the French macarons, as well as the tiramisu, cheesecake pops, and chocolate decadence pops. The mini cupcakes were really dry and disappointing. The red velvet cake was OK.

Overall, I would go back, but for an earlier meal because dinner was expensive. I would recommend trying this buffet at least once.

The desserts are the most delicious thing I had in Vegas . The meats are not as great. All the meats , I could still smell it after eating . 

The Asian foods are way too salty . The soups, fishes and even rice . 

Compare to other buffets , average .

Location: Caesars Palace

Tip: You have to check in at the Kiosk! Don't just stand at the end of the line. 

Also, don't be fooled by the ridiculous "estimated" wait time. I checked in at the kiosk at 3:30 pm and on the receipt it said: "estimated seating: 7:45 pm". I was in disbelief because all the yelp reviews I read said at most the wait time would be two hours and thirty minutes. I double checked with the tall asian manager with glasses and asked him several times about the wait time. I asked, "Is this a good estimate? The line is pretty short, and we don't have time to wait for four hours." He assured me the estimated time was pretty accurate so I should def consider paying the $20 express line option. I gave him the benefit of the doubt and paid the extra $20 for a grand total of $76!

I got a text notification about one hour and twenty minutes later letting me know that I was at the front of the line and I would need to come back to pay (if I hadn't already) . Basically I got hustled... Four hour wait my butt, I only had to wait an hour, no need to go to the express line! Shout out to the Asian manager with the spiky hair for hustling me! 

Food: Enormous selection of food! You start with Chinese food at the back of the line. Everything was excellent save for the shrimp "dumplings". If you're the type that looks for good asian food at a buffet, Bacchanal is perfect for you! They had the leanest pork belly I've ever had in my entire life. The shrimp shumai was also very good. The fried rice was also very tasty. 

There wasn't really a "Nice" selection of Japanese food. The California roll they made was very good though. 

NOODLE OPTION: FINALLY a buffet that offers UDON Noodle soup, PHO, AND RAMEN! I have never seen that before and I've always wondered how old I would have to be for someone to make a smart business move like that. Bravo Bacchanal. 

Italian option: Looked appetizing, but didn't have the patience to wait for that section of the line! 

Meat option: If it's bulking season for you, this is the buffet to be at. The BEST prime rib I've ever had in my entire life. No joke. The lamb was also amazing. They offer BBQ ribs, turkey, and a huge freaking bone with a chunk of meat.. (Not sure what type of meat it was, but let's say it was a buffalos leg. Jk.)

Soup selection: My wifey tried all of the soup selections and she loved every single one!

Juice: don't skip over the juice! They had a little section with glass juices and they tasted wonderful. I loved the pineapple ;) and mango option! Make sure you don't fill up your stomach with juices though.. (Another smart business idea)

Carne asada tacos at Bacchanal over King Taco. I'm not even kidding.

Fish: I can't remember every fish I tried off the top of my head, but the salmon was fresh and baked perfectly! 

Seafood: Sadly, they have this section at the start of the buffet line so you'll have to wait till you get to the front to dig in... I'm not a huge seafood fan, but my wifey does. Being the man of the year, I stacked a plate full of KING crab legs, oysters, mussels, AND JUMBO shrimp. You know a buffet is on another level when they offer jumbo shrimp. The oysters were fresh and simply amazing. My girl has very high expectations for seafood and Bacchanal exceeded those expectations. 

Desserts: My wifey loves her desserts and there were so many options to choose from... Cakes, macaroons, ice cream, ice cream cookie sandwiches, basically everything.. Basically, top selling items from well known dessert places all put together.

Everything at the Bacchanal was amazing. The only negative was the misleading information by the manager working that day. A little shady that he urged us (group of five) to pay the extra $20 to go through express on a Monday afternoon w/ barely any people in line... Five-Stars for everything else.

I absolutely love this place for breakfast.  I have never seen so many selections for breakfast.  I'm definitely coming here again when I'm out in Vegas.

Dinner:  its 108 for 2 people and I don't really think its all that.  Yes, they have crab and a seafood selection but I was disappointed.  I thought dinner was going to be better than breakfast.  For that amount of money you can get a nice meal at Mesa Grill located in Caesar Palace.

Had to wait a little to get in, which is to be expected with a buffet IF there weren't tables available.  BUT, there were lots of tables available. :(  We went for breakfast and the price is reasonable.  Lots of options for breakfast and pre-made plates are nicely presented.  My husband caught a lady customer touching the food with her bare hands.  We informed our waiter of this and he quickly went to tell the cooks in charge of that station.  We really appreciated that he shared our same concern.   The food was good, nothing spectacular, but maybe that's because we went for breakfast.  I'd go back, but probably for dinner.

The breakfast is a three star experience: imo not worth the price. The lunch appeared to be a better deal.

Going through what I had:

Lobster eggs Benedict. Disappointing, with very little lobster.
BBQ pork bun: solid enough, though very little pork in it.
Pasta: had a decent flavor, would eat more.
Steak and eggs: not good. Tasted like glorified lunch meat.
Huevos rancheros: ok, not spectacular.
Prime rib: more like not prime. Dry and lacking flavor.
Two different mussels: enjoyable.
Dungenese crab: good.

I ended up also getting a bit of sushi, American wagyu, and shrimp from the lunch menu, all of which was better than the breakfast items.

I also tried a number of desserts. The raspberry mousse was good, as was the cheesecake. The cookie was ok. The matcha item, the tiramisu, and a lemon item were all not good.

The service was very attentive and professional. Bonus points for that.

Verdict: skip the breakfast, go for the lunch.

I've been here twice now and just love it.  I stay off of free mount st and make it a habit to come here at least once while I'm on Vegas everytime.  The food is so good and the best service I've ever had at a buffet.  Tons of choices to pick from and desert is the best part of my night:)

Make sure to get here early if your gonna plan for dinner because the line does start getting a little long but it is well worth the wait

This is the buffet of all buffets. You will never find one close to this in the Vegas or anywhere is the US because 

1. They shuck the oysters in front of you.
2. They boil the king crab legroom in front of you.
3. They have tomahawk ribeyes. One of these will set you back $90 at a steak house.
4. Stone crab claws...that's crazy. They didn't have it when I went so I'm guessing it's only available on weekends.
5. You get to build your own crepe.
6. They have congee, pho, and ramen but don't eat the pho.  It is nasty. They need to hire the cook from Rio to make it.
7. There are many more stuff that you won't find in other buffets.

I took off 1 star for the long azz wait. If you come for dinner show up at lunch time. Bring a portable toilet, chair or sleeping bag...you will need it!  Or you can do what I do. Find a high roller and have them bring you in. The only bad part about it is you have to eat with them and hear all their bad beat stories...lol
Been there 3 times within a year.  Twice in October, once this month. Very expensive but still the best in Vegas.  Seafood is wonderful, selection is impressive, not a bad dish on the line.

All I gotta say is....Wow!

The crab legs are already cut open for you - You just pull the meat out and go - I've never seen this before.  They also make street tacos at the Mexican station - Hella good!  

The dessert bar was off the chain - The crepes are my personal favorites.  

Honestly - There's so much food available, you'll be overwhelmed...

Tips:

Be prepared to wait in line for a while.  Don't eat anything before coming here...You're going to want to be hella hungry so that you make every dollar of your meal count.  Place is not cheap, so be prepared to break the bank on this one...haha.

There's a reason they call this the number 1 buffet in Vegas...Come see 4 yourself...You won't be disappointed!

Thanks Groupon!  Haven't been back to the Bacchanal Buffet since a Yelp event several years ago.  4 stars!

Groupon, I love you.  Thank you for blessing us with your coupon that granted the wifey and I entrance to the sin of gluttony.  VIP breakfast M-F for two at $65?  Plus I had an extra coupon to lower that price 20%?  Sign me up baby!  Not only did we get to go to the shorter 'Fast Pass' line, we saved bucks on the meal too!  Get in by 10:30 AM - skim some breakfast, stay for lunch!  Yes we did!

The buffet is truly MASSIVE.  You wouldn't believe the kind of work and planning running a shindig like this takes.  I used to run the UNLV Dining Commons and that was work.  This must be WORK.  There's almost everything imaginable to eat, and things that you didn't even know you wanted to eat!  For breakfast, then lunch, wifey and I got the true breadth of what Bacchanal has to offer.  Expand your belt, it's time to GORGE!

I came hungry, and wanted to do this review right.  But damn, it's so hard to remember EVERYTHING we ate!  Luckily I took pics which I will happily include.  There was just so much I sampled.  I feel like between wifey and I we tried nearly every major item at each station!  Endless mimosas didn't help me either.  I started off slow - did you know for breakfast they offer individual carafes of fresh orange juice, carrot juice, and cucumber juice?

OK, back to the feast we sampled:

-Steak & Eggs
-Pork Belly
-Red Velvet Pancakes
-Croissant Sandwiches
-Fresh cut charcuterie
-Seafood Salad (with scallops!)
-Cheeseburger Sliders
-3 types of sausage (Mango & Jalapeno, Spicy, and Kielbasa)
-Slab Bacon (thick!)
-Po Boy Sliders
-Sushi
-Dumplings
-Ravioli
-Ramen (yes!)
-Carne Asada & Al Pastor Tacos
-Nutella Crepe
-Assorted dessers
-Assorted gelatos
-Shaved Ice!

We ate SO much!  Not because we wanted to, but because I wanted to maintain the integrity of my review.  Ok, we wanted to eat!  This being a buffet there is great variety, but of course quality is always hard to keep in check.  Most of the items we sampled were very good, I don't really have a complaint because a buffet like this is not often on my radar because of price.  My only gripe is that some of the things were either cold or old from sitting on the line too long.  The red velvet pancakes were chewy since they sat too long.  My steak & eggs were overdone from sitting under the heat lamp too long.  But these are minor complaints because it is a buffet.  Plus, just about everything else we had was darn tasty!  Quality standards are above buffets of lower caliber.  Many unique things you won't find at other buffets!  Like ramen!  And it was decent!  The street tacos were excellent because of the fresh hand made tortillas!  Exotic shaved ice to order with green tea, condensed milk, and azuki beans?  Come on!  

I do have a big complaint though with regards to service.  This is why I had to take this review down a notch.  We were basically ignored throughout our entire meal by our server!  After taking our initial drink order, he only came by ONCE to check on us and refill our drinks, after I had to flag him down!  And we were there over an hour!  Horrible, horrible inattentive service!  Our busboy did majority of the work clearing our plates!  This was bad enough we had to take to talking with the assistant manager, tables around us were all being served by this guy & we were promptly being straight up IGNORED.  Assistant manager assured us this was very unusual and would have a talk with our server.  We still tipped well of course, but I hope most of it went to our busboy!

If Groupon does this deal again, will I be back?  You can bet your Arnold Schwarzenegger lovin' @$$ I will!  Great deal for a great buffet!  Hopefully next time we get a server who might actually like us!

OINK OINK PIG PIG!

What did I not love?

Ok, just the line, but at any good place, there usually is a line. Get there early and pace yourself!

We were there for over 2 hours and I didn't even get to try 1/4 of what I wanted to eat. I can't wait to go back for brunch and for dinner again!

My highlights:
oyster shooters
freshly chucked oysters
snow crab
wagyu beef slider
blackened chicken soup
creme brûlée
fresh baked chocolate chip cookie soufflé
mochi
gelato
macaroons

I would not suggest getting the 24-hour buffet deal for this particular buffet. As advertised, "as low as $49.99," it is NOT $49.99 for this place. It is $69.99 plus an additional $25 per person for dinner and additional $15 for brunch. I wouldn't say it's worth it unless you plan on eating at least 4 meals in those 24 hours. BUT you gotta try it at least once!

You Can Desserts (5/5 NOMs)
It was sweetness overload with so much to try. I kept going back for more a few times. You got to save room for all the sweets.

All You Can Eat Asian and Mexican (5/5 NOMs)
That is some crazy amount food in there. Anything and everything from American to Asian and Mexican. You got to eat little bit of each dish so you can try everything. There is a lot to try! Love Asian section with super nomnom Shao Mai and Roasted Duck! I went for few more. Not a bif fan of their sushi. Tasted very buffet style dry and bland. Other then that I'm a fan! 

All You Can Meat (5/5 NOMs)
I was told this is the place to stop by during your Vegas trip. Welcome to the amazing meat world with all type of BBQs you can think of. Love the brisket, sausages, chicken and prime rib. Make sure to go during lunch so its cheaper. Dinner is crazy expensive!

Awesome ! The price for me was fine but for a few people in my group it was a little pricey. The way I see it you get what you pay for. Everything was fresh and delicious. The one thing I wasn't happy with was I had to get up and search for the waitress a few times for us. To get drinks, eating utensils, a nutcracker and straws.

This was one of two buffets I tried during my Vegas trip. I would rate this one better than the other, due to the variety and unique culinary options. Everything I tried was delicious! I didn't try the seafood because I'm originally from an area that has a great seafood buffet. I decided not to waste any useful space in my stomach. I'm sure it would've been tasty.

The atmosphere has a mature feel to it. The dimly lit dining room is perfect for places that have a large dining area. The buffet is organized perfectly too. The service was good. You really can't rate it very much because you don't have a lot of interaction with your server.

Every option on the buffet line was hot (or cold) and fresh. It seems that the chefs were constantly busy preparing dishes behind the line. If I had to wait for a certain made-to-order dish, the wait was relatively short. This was my first experience trying bone marrow, and I found it to be very good. I'm sure I can find a better one at a steakhouse, but I enjoyed it. I would say the dessert line was a little mediocre, but I didn't visit for the dessert.

I will definitely visit again during my next Vegas trip. The price is expensive. However, you are able to choice from a large selection of gourmet entrees. It's worth the money.
OMG!!! The food and customer service was awesome! Cannot believe I've spent so much time going to Rio all these years instead of trying out Bacchanal! Can't wait to go back!

Great buffet! Lots of seafood options including hot and cold king crab legs, shrimp, sea bass, salmon, and a lot of meats including prime rib, brisket, and so many other choices.  We paid $15 extra for unlimited alcohol (you can pick either wine, champagne, or beer). Waitress was fairly attentive and we were able to get a good amount of drinks included.  The buffet closes at 10pm so just be careful when you arrive!

The foods are delicious and there are so many choices. Each section has their own unique style of food. The only problem was the service. I asked for a cup of water to 4 different servers and it took FOREVER.

Rosemaria working in the front provided terrible customer service. Not did she look miserable the entire time, she gave our party (platinum members) attitude. We gave her our ticket and waited to be seated and she lost our ticket momentarily ... Making us wait even longer. While we waited about 6-7 parties seated in front of us. Terrible! The food is good otherwise.

The interior decoration is nice like most of the casino buffet, although it has the most selection of food in Vegas, the layout could be better, all the food are scatter in outer edge of the buffet with great distance, so half of the time, I can't even remember where to get my food.  I went during lunch time because that's the cheapest time to go, but it's still too expensive in my taste even after employee discount, which is only M~Thursday lunch only, exclude the holiday and holiday week, to me that's just not a good discount at all, and what happen to Macaroon? It turn out they will only serve macaroon during dinner from now on starting 3pm, I think that's a bit cheap, and that's pretty much what I look forward to the most when I came to this buffet, talked with the manager and he was kind enough to bring me some, but I will not come back because they move macaroon to dinner.  Food is tasty, love the cucumber juice and most of the meat course, but nothing really wow me, maybe it's because I don't feel it's worth the value I paid, after all, there's only so much food you can eat, however, I LOVE their service, our waitress Colleen is such a sweet heart.

Great Stuff.  Spicy Tuna Sushi rolls,  ceviche, crab legs, paella, pho,  , great steak cuts. all great!  Desert go for a crepe, key lime pie ,and carrot cake and a mochi mango ball. Service was nice, place is huge though, remember there are 2 sides to it.

Its gone down a bit. 

Won't come back.

Not recommended. Used to be stellar... now not so much.

Lost its swing

Our first trip to bacchanal after it's opening was a wow factor. We have dinned there  a number of times since it's opening.  Breakfast, lunch, and dinner, I  have done them all.  It  is  only 2nd to the Bally's sterling Sunday brunch at Bally's), The wow factor is still there.

This buffet is wonderful and full of so many different options. Our server, Carlos, was one of the kindest and most hospitable servers I have had in a long time. The brunch was amazing and I am leaving COMPLETELY stuffed and happy.

This is definitely a great buffet with a wide diversity of exquisitely prepared foods however there is one thing I can't get around that will give me great hesitancy to return again. I have eaten there three times and faced the same problem... great food but difficult to get to it. For one thing, it is popular and this means you have to show up maybe 60-90 minutes before you wish to eat and sign in at a kiosk to get a time to return. I showed up at 6:35 pm on a Wednesday and was given a return time of 8:11pm. I showed up at 8:10 and was put in a line of so called reservations and had to wait in line and got a table at 8:35pm. So effectively a 2 hr wait. It is kind of like Disney's fast pass only you don't return to go in a special line bypassing others..just a line that is shorter.
     The second problem is design. They need more stations for the food.  There is a dessert station, a crab station as well as an Asian food station but a great many of the main dishes have to be passed on your way to the carving stations which are at the end of a long buffet line ...so you have to walk along a buffet line passing several dishes that you do not want to get to the carving  station and at the same time blocking people who want one of those main  dishes and not the carving station. So if you want something in that line that is not the carving station, you have to wait in line along with others waiting to get to the carving station or you have to somehow break in line to get some of a chicken dish that has 15 people in front of it waiting to get to the end of the line to that carving station. I hope that makes sense. I found myself saying heck with the other dishes (that I wanted to try) rather than stand in line 10-15 minutes and I just concentrated on crab legs which were great but I did want to try other dishes. If I only want crab, then I'll probably return but otherwise probably not.

This is the buffet of buffets in Vegas. Me and 2 friends decided to check it out since we were staying at Caesars. We skipped breakfast and came during lunchtime. 

This place is basically the Epcot of buffets, a taste of every place in the world meshed into one restaurant. You have cuisines from Italy, China, Mexico, USA and etc. Its really hard to describe, you just have to see for yourself. And be sure to arrive famished.

Just a forewarning, this review is specifically for the breakfast buffet on a week day.

I did more research than I'd like to admit when I was trying to decide what buffet to go to in Vegas. My partner and I don't have a lot of money so we wanted to be 100% confident in our buffet choice. We didn't want to blow all our moolah on a so-so buffet. Bacchanal was on almost every top buffet list that I had read. There were a couple other buffets that shared this spot, but Bacchanal appeared to be the most frequent while also having a breakfast buffet that wasn't going to need me to take a loan out to pay for it. Now that we had our buffet choice, off we went!

Before we even got into the buffet we made a blunder. Apparently they split the entrance into the buffet into different lines. Each line was for a different type of guest (high roller and VIP status type of stuff). Well, we unknowingly walked down a VIP line to pay for the buffet. Fortunately for us the lady that was taking care of us at the desk informed us of what we had done, but told us she'd still take care of us even though it looked like we had skipped over a couple people. She was very kind about it and I appreciated that a lot.

We waited only a short amount of time to be seated. We were brought into a buffet that looked a lot more modern than I was expecting. I have to be honest and say it was the fanciest looking buffet that I've been in. Once I sat down my heart started racing. I needed to go get the food. I was starving and I saw the line of breakfast options. I immediately got up, ran past the dessert bar, and straight to the breakfast.

The presentation of all the food on the buffet line was nice. It wasn't messy, and for a lot of the options they had cute little pans/baskets that separated the food into individual portions. As for how many options there were...there were a ton. It was astounding to see all the options that were there. Chicken and waffles, chilaquiles, biscuits and gravy, French toast, churros, red velvet pancakes, and more. I was in a dream. The scary part is that my partner and I thought that the front area was the buffet and that was it. However in our exploration we discovered an entire other room where the buffet continued. It wasn't even repeat food of the first room. This second room contained all new stuff. It was mainly Asian breakfast items however (dim sum, noodles, congee) but there were some typical things like egg frittatas, croquet monsieur, and a charcuterie section. Bacchanal was paradise.

I'm obviously not going to go over everything that I ate (6 plates of mostly all unique food) but I'll go over some of my favorites and some items I was disappointed by. The French toast was delicious; it was fluffy and fresh. The mac and cheese was a surprise favorite of mine. It was creamy, cheesy, and the cheese was still in that awesome gooey state where it's still basically melted. The churros were simple but addicting (never had access to all you can eat churros before). The bacon was cooked perfectly with that in between of being overcooked and undercooked but leaning more on the cooked side. The sausage links were surprisingly delicious and very plump. They are probably 2 to 3 times the size of a normal breakfast sausage. Another surprise favorite of mine was the peppered beef in the Asian food section. The beef tasted delicious and was very tender.

As for what I was disappointed in there weren't a lot. I was not a fan of the biscuits and gravy. The gravy and biscuits were both on the cold side and the biscuits were a little dry. I just didn't enjoy eating them. The eggs benedict was a huge let down. The ingredients were poorly assembled on most of them with the ham and egg sitting half off the English muffin and the ham was thin and shriveled. It didn't have much flavor to it other than the egg yolk. The red velvet pancakes were not bad by any means, but they really just tasted like a regular pancake. I couldn't pick up on any unique flavor that I was expecting. That was really about all that I didn't like which is not a lot given how many choices there were.

They had so many dessert options, but the trick was that half of them had no labels and many of the ones that did were named things that I had never heard of. That didn't stop me from piling them all on my plate. They had a gelato section, reduced sugar sections, pastries, a small fudge section, a cake section, and with the cake section that's where a lot of the unique desserts were. They were little layered mousse and cream desserts that were in plastic containers. Hands down my favorite dessert was the jasmine tea rice pudding.

Overall the buffet was amazing. It has now set the bar for any other buffet that I go to as far as variety. While the food was great, it wasn't in a league of it's own taste-wise and I'll still be going to cheap buffets to save money. With that said, definitely try this buffet out. You won't regret it.

This is a delayed review from November 2012.

We had walked by at dinner time the night before and the line was ridiculously long. The thing about restaurants with long lines is that it usually means good food is being served. Unfortunately, we had reservations elsewhere and could only look through the windows with envy at the people getting plates full of cold and hot crab.

We went back the next day at around 9:15 am and got seated near the crepe station. Like many other Vegas buffets, there were plenty of types of foods to choose from Unfortunatelly one of the choices was not cold shrimp or crab (sigh). Okay fine, so I'll have to settle for a freshly made crepe that I get to dress, bowl of ramen with wonton added, sweet potato fries served in little pails, and tater tots served in wire baskets. We know there was more but it's been a couple of months. 

There was also fresh squeezed orange, watermelon and cucumber juices available from our server. The OJ was good but they ran out of the watermelon and cucumber didn't not sound particularly appealing to us though it's probably great when you're hot.

Oh, the service. Every employee on the dining room floor was friendly and accommodating. Our server made sure that she introduced us to her partner while she went on a break. Even though the line of new customers was beginning to back up, we never felt rushed. 

We stayed so long just nibbling, drinking coffee and chatting that we got a chance to try a few lunch items and see the lunch offerings before leaving at 11:30.  Oyster shooters for the win!

Lemons, how do you not have lemons for the seafood?! 

This place has gone WAAAAY down hill since we used to eat here 5 years ago. 

The line system makes no sense, they sat exactly 6 parties of 4 people ahead of us, who came after us  because we had only a party of two.

Food was not fresh, hot plates for cold seafood, meat was tough, fish was dry, service was so slow I had to buss my own table, management wouldn't calm down rowdy patrons who cussed across the halls. 

Waste of money and time.

The quality of food is great along with a good variety of different cuisine.  
The food is served in small bites and perfect portion for a buffet with no waste. I seem to think the variety is not your standard fare.  With options like lamb, legit made to order street tacos,  tamales were some items that really stood out.  

My usual favorite is the crab legs station.  It's not self serve,  but the line moves once they have the crab legs in order.  It's a messy process and the the tool crackers are necessary to shell out the meaty goodness. Luckily,  my husband and I are on the same boat.  No need to eat ladylike.  Hehe.. and we got wetnaps along the way.  

Hefty price tag even for a lunch occasion,  so it's definitely a nice treat. If you want to be savvy and save a few bucks, read about opening up a total rewards credit card and a free buffet comes along with this perk.

Was the wait long? Yes. Was it expensive? Yes. Was it worth the wait and the money? You betcha!

Great food. Lots of choices. Friendly service. Clean. What I'd expect from 'the best buffet in Vegas.'

I enjoyed the delicious little details like the cranberry quinoa salad, cheese display, peach green tea, and variety of sauces for the  Mexican cuisine. The miso and pho were on point.

We'll certainly come back!
