**first time visitors at the bacchanal buffet**

*During very busy times, in order to avoid fire hazardous long lines, they offer several kiosk to make reservations that print out a ticket that gives you a time to come back. The forum shops are conveniently nearby (and of course gambling) so theres a place to kill time walking around. I suggest that one person in your party to go there early before everyone else to make the reservations at the kiosk*

The Bacchanal buffet is the Godfather of all the buffets in vegas. They have pho, sushi, lamb, truffle potatoes, cold or warm crab, mussels, mochi, french macaroons, AND SO MUCH MORE! 

Service at buffets usually suck, but at the bacchanal our dishes were cleared out when we were finished and our drinks were never empty. We didn't have to wait forever for a server to come by for refills. We had not only one person helping us, we had two! They were both kind and very helpful. 

Holiday pricing is more expensive than their regular price. 

Christmas time pricing
$49.99 lunch time 11-3
$59.99 dinner time 3-close.

This is the place to go to stuff your face! Come here super hungry!

Hands down my favorite Buffet in Vegas! It's like I'm visiting 9 different restaurants! But the dessert station takes the cake... Literally. I always visit the Bacchanal Buffet when ever I'm in Vegas. No questions asked.

It could be pretty pricy because I paid around $55 for fixed holiday dinner price. But I think it is so worth it. I personally hate waiting to eat so I usually always go to the kiosk first like in the early morning and get my ticket to eat dinner later time. It's usually 4 hour wait when Vegas is busy.

But let me tell you, even after you get your ticket, you have to wait for the text message saying 'your table is almost ready and you can come pay first'. It almost sounds like you can get in right away and dine in right? Well, no. You have to wait another hour or more depending on the volume of people. It's so horrible. But that is why I go in and stay there and try every single food possible.

I have my few favorites from here. First would be their crab legs. I prefer to eat the warm ones from Italian section than the cold ones from the Seafood section. But then again, I saw them cooking and they literally take the cold ones and put them in the pot full of water and you get your crab legs later when it's warm enough to serve. I wish they can actually steam them on a steamer instead of 'boiling' them in the water becauae while its boiling, it loses all the flavor. But it was good enough for me to taste the crab so I liked it.

Secons favorite would be lamb chop or rack of lamb. I dont know if they have this regularly because last time I went, they didnt have any. But they had it on my most recent visit. They are so tender and juicy. I am definitely not a fan of lamb but this would probably be the only lamb I would eat. I dont know how many racks I had but I had so much.

My other favorite would be the udon noodles from the Asian section. I really like the broth here and a couple bean curds they put in. It's pretty strong in flavor, the bean curd, but its good as its moistened in the broth. It was an unusual find to like the noodles here.

Juices in the cute glass bottles are definitely a must try. I really like the two flavors the most. Pineapple and Horchata. These two were so good that I made my friends try it too. It's refreshing. Sometimes they would have none out, and you can ask the guy working inside the kitchen for the flavor you want. They will hand it to you if they have it.

Last but not least their pistachio souffle and pistachio macarons are great to try from the dessert section. For pistachio souffle, you have to order them because it is not out most of the time. They will tell you to come back in 10 minutes or so. It's pretty good. Do I need to say anything about macarons? Their green pistachio macarons are so good. Macarons from Le Village Buffet is horrible. You wont be disappointed. However, they might not have it depending on when you visit the buffet.

I still think Bacchanal buffet is far better than  The Buffet at Wynn. A small tip for you would be to go in around 2 PM before 3 PM to pay Lunch price and enjoy dinner menus. But you have to be lucky because you dont know how long it would take to get to the front of the line to pay for it.

I'll give you a little guided tour of the buffet..

Food: 4/5
Meat Station:
Hm...maybe they were off at the meat counter?  I gave their prime rib a try, and it was really dry and tough.  I had to literally cut away the edges to really enjoy the juicy portion of the meat (which was medium).  The meat station was certainly overwhelming.  All types of sausages, poultry, and red meat. I simply got full by glimpsing at the counter.  LOL... honestly, I am not a carnivore, but other patrons seemed to have enjoyed the meat station, since it always had a line.

Asian Stations (actually more like Chinese & Japanese):
The Chinese station was filled with dim sum (XLB, sticky rice, chow mein, fried rice, preserved duck egg and pork congee, cruellers (aka Chinese Donuts), blacken chicken ginseng soup (in claypots), cha siu (BBQ pork ribs), and a noodle station (Udon, wonton, & pho). Since I live in SGV and am Chinese, the dim sum didn't look very appetizing to me, but what WAS impressive was their blacken chicken ginseng soup. It tasted homemade and authentic (just like how mom makes it)!  Even my mom went and got seconds...so that says a lot.

Sushi Station:
Not many options, so if you're the type who goes directly to the sushi section in a buffet, you'll be disappointed.  They had salmon, shrimp, and tuna nigiri, a couple rolls, and Japanese seaweed. Yep, that's all folks.  Quality was good, but just not much to choose from.

What really bothered me was how some people had the nerve to pick off the fish from the nigiri, leaving just the ball of rice lying on the serving platter. It's not only classless, but it's a waste of food. The rice to fish proportion was good...seriously... the amount of rice was no more than a pinky size. So do yourself and the rest of us a favor (and maybe gather some good Karma), pick up your own "reject" rice balls and take it with you, please.  Ugh....people these days!

Italian/ European Station:
Pasta, pasta, and more pasta. The portion sizes were doable, since they serve them in individual baked plates. The lasagna looked good, but I didn't have any myself.  I'd probably fill up with just that, and with the price that we had paid, I decided to stick with the other food options.

Fine cheeses and deli meat was wonderful...quality was good, and the deli counter was barely keeping up with the demand....

Latin & Central America Station (least busiest station)
They had pasole (sp?), rice and beans, and ceviche. When dinner time came, the taco (freshly made upon ordering) station began serving al pastor, carne asada, and other meats you would usually have in a taco.

American Station:
Fried food in their own frying basket. Had their fried chicken, which was well seasoned and moist...the sweet potato fries had better days. It was bedding for the fried chicken, and it had gotten all soggy by the time I got to them. If it was crispier, the fries would have been perfect! They also served sliders, which I heard were good and juicy.  The mac & cheese was really popular, but again, I didn't have any myself. 

There was a TRUFFLED POTATO GRATIN dish which was my FAVORITE.  The serving size was small (appetizer-like), but it certainly was jam packed with great flavors...creamy, savory, and with a nice crusted/crispy top! Too bad I had this towards the end of my meal, otherwise I would have had more... SIGH....

Seafood Station
The had clam bake, lobster chowder (with bacon bits), seafood paella, jumbo shrimp cocktail, and raw oysters.  I only had their oysters, and boy, were they GOOD!  With a squeeze of lemon juice and pinch of grated fresh horseradish, I was in BIVALVE HEAVEN. The oysters go quick, so be sure to stand guard when the next batch gets loaded on the ice.  =)

Juice Station:
I had their orange juice, but they also served watermelon, cucumber, and carrot juice, too.  The juice tasted freshly squeezed, although I saw the workers pouring them from gallon sized containers... As long as it tastes freshly squeezed, it's good enough for me.

Dessert Station:
Hm...I was literally circling this station like a shark around its prey.  Actually I was waiting for their churros (filled with vanilla cream), I finally gave up and settled for their velvet miniature cake and raspberry mouse cup.  Both were very decadent, but perfectly sweetened.  The gelato  and crepe making station was busy, but I couldn't eat anymore...so I simply let my eyes feast on the options.

Service: 5/5
Great service, and attentive. The waitress and her helper would check up on us, and our plates were cleared on a regular basis.  I cannot understand how people who eat a lot (I mean, 10 plates for 2 people) actually have the nerve to leave $1 as a tip. REALLY PEOPLE? UGH... If you can afford to spend $37 on a meal, at least give a decent tip for the person clearing your table.

Final Verdict: 
I'd come here again if there's enough interest from the gang. But I'd rather spend that money on another extravagant Vegas buffet.

Been to this buffet before, but this time it was not as expected. 

Our reservation was for 8:50 and we sat down around 9:10 - not that bad. 

We sat at a table with a bunch of trash and food on the floor, it was not cleaned up. The food items were already running out - even a whole hour before they closed! The worst part is probably the fact that the dessert station ran out of food before the rest of the buffet. 

If you do decide to come, make sure it's early enough in the night to ensure food survives your visit!

Great food and taste very fresh. When around 10ish and stayed til 12ish, so I wish they started serving the more savory foods a tad earlier since it was pretty much all breakfast items until noon. I thought the buffet would stay generally the same since "Brunch" hours are from opening to 3pm. Our servers/busser was very courteous, quick to clear our plates, and quick to refill our glasses. Would recommend this buffet if you're looking for some fresh options.

Super overpriced and overrated, the food was not great, I would say it's even below average. We paid almost $200 and didn't have good experience at all. I'm giving 2 stars only because the lava cake and raspberry cake were just okay and grilled salmon was good enough and not over cooked

I think this my favorite for buffet in the Las Vegas Strip Coz they are have everything and Big line for foods Asian, Mexican, seafood and etc. but the price it's little expensive (but if's you see foods I think it's no at all). 
I'm been here 1 time almost every month if's I can. Just love it.

Quality went down on the food but the dessert was on point. Things seem to have been over cooked, under seasoned or over seasoned. The sushi selection was very limited and BBQ station wasnt very impressive. Meat was either over cooked or tasteless

Truly the buffet of buffets! Nothing can compare to the quality, variety, and taste of the food. I can honestly say it's the best buffet in Vegas. It is expensive, yes, but you get what you pay for. Go hungry and enjoy!
It's my favorite buffet now :) My top three. Belagio, Wynn, and now Caesars :) You won't regret paying for that price! it's worth it

Way over priced for the quality of food.  Good service but all the food was cold. I was really looking forward to eating here and I was very disappointed.  Mandalay bay is much better and less expensive. I don't know what all the las vegas reviewers are carrying on about this was no worth the money.

Don't waste your money! This buffet is so overrated. I asked my Uber driver who has lived in LV all his life & he recommended this. At 2:30 in the afternoon I was starved & it seemed a buffet was in order. I pay almost $50 which was shocking for lunch. I did get a decent sized slice of prime rib & some big ol shrimp but was it great? Meh. Got a biscuit for some carbs & it was so stale it crumbled apart when I tried to butter it. Desserts were mediocre. I really felt like I got ripped off!

I have been waiting to eat here for an extremely long time; it was during the week for dinner. I understand that the best time to go is during the weekend for dinner, so the food during the week was mediocre. The typical fried foods, Italian section, seafood, and carving station. Unfortunately, the hype of the restaurant didn't live up to the actual experience. There was an incident at the carving station that should have never happened. A guest went up to the carving station to return the meat they had just received and was unsatisfied  ( they brought it to their table and came back). The carver put it back on the carving board and served it to the next guest, yes, used meat. I was the lucky one to received this second- hand meat. Yay! This should have been thrown away, it was on someone else's plate. The manager had the audacity to offer a soda for the experience. Awesome. For the price of this buffet this should have never happened and the manager should have been more apologetic.

I wish I took some pictures but I absolutely love their brunch . No doubt I will bring my friends & family there when I go back to Vegas.

We had a large crew of about 18 which they accommodated smoothly (they got us a huge long table.) Some of us got brunch plus mimosas which was low 50s and some got just food for 38. Our server Maria was a goddess she made sure our glasses were never empty.

Let's get to the food. The assortment and variety of food is what made this amazing. They literally offer everything. Scrambled eggs, omelets, eggs Benedict, Breakfast meats - sausage, bacon, ham, hash. Fresh seafood of all variety. There was a cutting session with prime rib. A variety of bagels, bread and muffins with condiments. Then you hit the corner there is vegan and more healthier options (pass lol.) There was an Asia section where sushi, noodles, dumplings, meat dishes, fried rice were served. At this point I saw enough.

Literally food paradise. As a bit of a buffet enthusiast I can easily say this was the crown of buffets and a lot of my crew felt the same.

What a great experience at this buffet ! The meats ! Prime rib , ham , bacon , sausages . All so good! My favorite part of this buffet was the crab legs and wagyu beef! 
All delicious the options felt endless 

Desserts were great i mean who doesn't love a gelato bar! Donuts and candy bar ! Personally i Love creek brûlée so that what i got and it did not disappoint. 

 The wait was long but come on it's Vegas and this is the best rated buffet! Worth the wait !

Can't go wrong with Bacchanal.  There are so many options and it's all good... well, except for the ramen.  That was a rookie mistake on my part.  No go on the ramen.  Everything else is legit.  The wait is long just like any other vegas buffet.  After you get your ticket and wait, you have to get in line and wait.  Once you're done waiting in that line, it's time to pay and wait in line.  And it's all worth it.  Go.
I love love Bacchanal! Every station was delicious, service was great. The mushroom truffle pizza, bone marrow and desserts are my favorite here

I only waited about an hour to be seated. I took the ticket from the kiosk for a 2:17 arrival time, and was seated by 3:20pm.

There are two lines. One to pay, and then one to be seated. Both were excruciating, so I can't imagine waiting any longer than I did.

I went here with high expectations, and was disappointed. The hostess was wonderful, but the service was run-of-the-mill buffet. Waiters taking plates with your silverware on them, slow refills, and a lack of communication. Sure it was busy, but from the other reviews it seems it's always busy.

The food wasn't anything special. Lots of "fancier" food items, but nothing tasted amazing. You won't get any greasy or fried food here, but there is prime rib and crab legs. Very diverse menu. But the food just wasn't good to me. Everything was either spicy, chewy, or just strangely flavored. I guess I don't have the sophisticated palate to really enjoy the food here.

The atmosphere is like any other buffet; crowded, people pushing, loud, lines to get the higher quality food items. For the cost of two customers ($120) you'd expect a more classy environment. 

If you're in the Vegas area, it's worth a try. Most dinners are going to cost 100-120 dollars anyway, but if you're looking for a more delicious or classy establishment, go elsewhere.

Cost - 3/5
Atmosphere - 2/5
Food - 3/5 (quality of the food is good, don't like the tastes)
Overall - 3/5

Oh so disappointing! I had really high expectations for this place after watching numerous YouTube reviews of this place. Boy was I wrong! 

We came on a Monday evening. The decor was nice but the lighting was just too dark. I guess they're probably trying to go for the romantic sheik look but I don't think it went very well being I didn't feel any more emotional or romantic in the dim lighting. 

The prime rib looked very good. However, upon receiving a thin slice of the "rare" cut, I found it to be bland and tough. Major fail for a fancy buffet staple. 

The oysters we merely decent. 

The escargot is butter sauce was good but it only contained one . 

The pizza was outstanding. 

The pho was very bland and was not authentic in any way. 

The Mexican pozole was decent. 

The fresh made-to-order tacos were yummy. 

I tried numerous other dishes but in summation, for the price we paid, it was absolutely underwhelming. I would not pay $60+ for this buffet. The quality of meats and seafood was lower than expected. The prime rib at the Rio buffet tasted better than here. So sad having waited over a year to try this place only to be disappointed.

Food was good, our waiters were great, but the people preparing and serving the food were disgusting. The guy making the tacos threw the plates on the counter. The people serving the Chinese soup and ramen was rude and had a sh*t face the whole time. The woman making the crepes kept demanding everyone for their plates. What a great way to spend our Christmas Eve. They need to teach their employees about customer service. I would rather go somewhere else with the crazy wait times, price, and bad service.

I had such high expectations after the last visit to Bacchanal Buffet. After the hiking trip we stayed overnight at Las Vegas just so we could go to Bacchanal Buffet again, but, after all the excitement, the food didn't turn out as great as I remembered it to be, especially with the prices we paid and the time we waited.

Maybe it's because of the Chinese New Year, or maybe because it's the President Day weekend, prices were $49.99 with Total Rewards card, and there was a 2hr line at around 8pm. As we've experienced the much longer Thanksgiving hype, we were prepared to wait for it.

At the pay counter, they gave us small little silicon plate grabbers and said to use that because some of their plates tend to be hot, and I thought that was a very nice gesture.

After we were sat, we all went to the seafood counter right away, because it always has the longest line ever, and of course, I couldn't wait for those yummy oysters! After waiting patiently for my turn, I filled up a plate full of freshly shucked oysters as well as a few oyster shooters and went back to my table a happy gal.

The oyster shooters were still very good, but I couldn't help but notice the oysters were generally smaller than what I had the last time. And as I wolf down the delicacies (I was very hungry after a day's hiking and standing in line), I also got more of the broken off shells into my mouth. It's understandable I guess, with only one person shucking the oysters but so many people waiting on them, one cannot expect the staff to wipe the debris and broken shells off... 

As I ate a few more pieces, I found myself actually using the lemon wedges because the oysters had just gotten too fishy without the lemons. Uh Oh, that's not good! Oysters weren't fresh enough! But hey, it's 10pm right, it's been a whole day right, can't expect them to still be fresh at so late a time right. Except, I've had perfectly shucked fresh juicy oysters on my Thanksgiving trip at 10pm also! But I just love oysters, so who cares about how fresh the oysters were when I can have as many as I want right? Yeah... that's what I thought, until I bit into one that had gone bad! I've had oysters at other buffets, granted, they were the cheap big chunky version and didn't taste that great, but none I've had at a buffet had actually gone bad. I couldn't believe my luck when I had this happen at a supposedly top tier buffet. After that incident, my appetite for seafood just went whoosh.

With no more craving for seafood, I was left to explore the many other options offered at Bacchanal. So I walked around the place abit, noticed that they offered nigiri but no sashimi at the Japanese station, and was further put off. The plus side is the rice that came was the nigiri was smaller than at other buffets, but it still wasn't sashimi where you can have as many raw fish as you want, and I do feel bad leaving all the rice uneaten, so I ended up not getting any from the Japanese station.

The tater tots and sweet potato tots were still very good, though not as crispy as I wished. I guess they were left on the station for too long, and the kitchen definitely won't be making more as they were close to closing.

At the Chinese station I've noticed a small black-brownish pot, and the tag said "black chicken soup". Now that's something nice! As I tried to pick up the pot, it was still way too hot for my sensitive fingers, so I remembered the plate grabber I got at the counter, except the pot is too thick for the grabber to work! Urgh! With no utensils around to help me pick up the pot, I was forced to pick up the pot with my fingers. Sigh... the things we do for food... The a bit burned fingers were well worth the sacrifice, because the soup was just soooo tasty! I definitely recommend everyone to try out their black chicken soup! (Unless you are into heavy flavors, then you'll find the soup to be flavorless or too light.)

My second favorite of the night was the mochi. Sadly you can only get two at a time, but several trips back to try out all the flavors were worthwhile the time. The ice cream wasn't too sweet, so it can act as a good palette refresher as well. The rice was soft and almost creamy, unlike the usually sticky and chewy mochi you buy at the frozen section of a supermarket. Definitely try them out when you visit.


Overall... I'm disappointed with this time's visit. The food in general just wasn't as fresh nor tasty as the last time. For the price I pay and the time to wait in line, I don't think it's worth it to visit Bacchanal again.

WOW, I can't believe I ate for 3 hours, nonstop. I just HAD to try almost everything they had to offer. Damn that "get more bang for your buck" mentality!!!!! 

In my opinion, Studio B at the M hotel and Bellagio were my top buffets in vegas. Yes, even Wynn and Wicked Spoon at the cosmopolitan cannot compare. This buffet is definitely on par with Studio B and Bellagio. I'm going to list out how the top buffets rank in comparison to each other for each category and let you decide where you want to try for yourself. (1 = best)

Carving Station: 1. Studio B, 2. Bacchanal, 3. Bellagio
Seafood: 1. Bacchanal, 2. Studio B, 3. Bellagio
Asian: 1. Bacchanal, 2. Studio B, 3. Bellagio
BBQ: 1. Bellagio, 2. Bacchanal, 3. Studio B
Salad (who comes to this station anyway?): 1. Studio B, 2. Bacchanal, 3. Bellagio
Italian: 1. Bellagio, 2. Bacchanal, 3. Studio B
American: 1. Bellagio, 2. Bacchanal, 3. Studio B
Dessert: 1. Bacchanal, 2. Bellagio, 3. Studio B

As you can see, they all have their goods and not so goods. It just depends on what you're craving. I will say that Bellagio's buffet is smaller in size so they do not have as much variety, but you can count on their quality. Everything they put out will be good whereas quality decreases as Studio B and Bacchanal offer more quantity. Also, Studio B includes all you can drink beer and champagne whereas Bacchanal has fresh squeeze juices (orange, carrot, tropical, and watermelon)

Last tips, its $46/person for a holiday brunch, but it's $2 off/person if you're a total rewards member. Also, no lines before 11:30am for brunch! I hear their line goes round and round and round!

By the end of the 3rd hour, all foods taste the same. Trust me, I don't think you'd want to eat anymore. FYI, the restrooms are right outside of the buffet.

This is one of the most disappointing experiences I ever had in Vegas. Waited 3 hours for a meal that was mediocre- food were cold and uncreative, oysters were small and sad and didn't look fresh, wagyu beef was drier than the Nevada desert. Definitely not worth the wait nor the price. It is overhyped. Giving it 2 stars because the environment is nice.

Hands down the BEST buffet I've been to!! It is definitely worth the price. We arrived at 930 and lid $41 each for the brunch, which includes unlimited mimosas!! We stayed until 11 when lunch was being served and the great food just continued! Definitely recommend for this buffet to be a must when in Vegas. Also our server Jeff was funny, personable and super attentive to all of our needs! Great overall experience!

3.5 stars to be honest

I was here on 12/21/13 for dinner $54 pp

First off.. No buffet should be worth 2 hours wait. Everything was fine, the line went pretty fast at first until all of a sudden it just stopped. This wait has nothing to do with the stars.. my stars are solely based on the food & services.

I like the varieties that they have here from seafood to meat to desserts. Lets start with the seafood:

while they have a lot of choices, I was surprised they offered snow crab legs only. I thought they would give out Alaskan King Crab legs. The snow crab legs aren't the best. The crab meat had this grainy texture, wasn't sweet, nor was it meaty. The shrimps were big, but had a weird taste; not saying it wasn't fresh but it just had this after taste that I cannot describe. The steamed clams and mussels were bland, the presentation was cute (in a pail) but the taste was just lacking - add some garlic an wine please! The clams were small too, that I didn't mind, i can always get more, but that pail was just filled with shells and they could really have executed better with the flavors. 

Moving onto the meat, the fried chicken was dry. The truffle scalloped potatoes were tasty but is it only because of the truffle flavor that made it "tasty"? The risotto was just meh. Prime ribs and flank steak were just okay - a bit tough. 

i like their salami and prosciutto selections - all were tasty

the tacos section was pretty good for a buffet; i could have eaten more tacos but why would i fill up my stomach on tacos when i can eat other stuff and get real true authentic tacos in San Diego?

The noodle station was a nice addition, i thought their ramen and pho was pretty good - the flavors were definitely there, they could make the broth stronger but nonetheless it was acceptable.

I enjoyed their salad selection and their chinese dim sum station was surprisingly not bad for a buffet style. The japanese section was pretty sad. Those nigiri were thin cut -- not many choices, but the good thing about the nigiri was that they give less rice. 

i also like that Bacchanal have a variety of soups: from chowders to tom yum but their bowls are just SO big! i only wanted to try the soup, i don't need such big noodle bowls. I think Bacchanal need to invest in some smaller bowls; AND stock up on more little sauce plates, please! 

Their dessert bar was amazing though. Chocolate dipped strawberries, gelatos, mochi ice creams, french macarons, crepe station, and the list goes on. The dessert was just WOW. So many choices for one small stomach. I really like their dessert selection. 

$54 pp was just a bit over price for the food they were serving especially when the quality was not good at all. (yes i went during the holiday weekend; but still... $54 i better see some good fresh seafood) 

As much of a disappointment, I still enjoyed my meal. I am only telling you the truth of what I tasted and saw. I'll come back but if I had to pay $50+ for dinner again, i better expect better quality in food and more plates / bowls / sauce plates out and ready for guests -- cannot have slow turnaround!

Bad food. We couldn't find one entre we liked.  We actually accidentally slight "over ate" since we kept trying different things, even though only a small portion but it crept up to be more than we planned.

Bacchanal is amazing. It has easily 4 times the options of a normal buffet and the quality is unbeatable.  Then again, for a $55 buffet, it better be.  I wouldn't eat here often because of the cost, but for a date night, or when out for a special occasion seeing  concert at Caesar's, it is a nice upscale option for a fancy treat out.
This buffet has the best quality food and varieties in Las Vegas, on the other hand our server seemed to be a bit overwhelmed and stressed on getting stiffed by our foreign visitors.
Fruits and deserts are wonderful. Wait time is short and the price is fairly low. Downside is that not too many sea food choices.

Loved this buffet! As a local I visit many of the buffets in town, and this will definitely be a frequently visited place for me! The price is good for what they offer, it felt clean and the food was fresh... I didn't feel like I was eating food that had been sitting under a heat lamp... I would definitely recommend my family and friends to this buffet and will entertain out of state relatives here as well!! Three thumbs up and a 5 star from me :)

Eat all the seafood first! Start with the crab legs!!! Jumbo shrimp!!! Then proceed to the meat area! Prime Rib medium rare is a must! Then take advantage of assorted variety that they have to offer...Italian try their resoto & meat balls..head to the sushi bar & take advantage of their salmon rolls...

Save room for desert! Best desert I've ever sample hands down..they have exotic fruits and their gelato is so good!!!

Quick tip..if you come in around 1:45 to 2pm they start changing the menu for dinner which means you pay the lunch price but you get to sample and eat the dinner menu as well!

I paid $60.00 for a mediocre buffet experience. I don't understand how this place was rated #1 of the buffet world. All the dessert tasted store bought and the main course dishes were just OK. My favorite dish was the mash potatoes and prime rib. Do yourself a favor and don't get the tacos. Better yet, do yourself a favor and dont spend the money at all.

This is one of the best buffets on the strip or even in all of Vegas. It's costly so go after a couple of days of fasting. They have meat , crab , sushi, Mexican , BBQ and so much more. It's fresh it's well prepared and the service staff seem to be happy in the job. They also have a secret drink it's a peach iced tea that is absolutely amazing. All I can say is go!! Go enjoy , take your time and taste everything that they offer. Oh and try the tea , it's so thirst quenching. Be prepared for a wait in the line. I must say that it is worth the wait. Eat well.

My favorite buffet in Vegas! I have been here twice and both experiences have been great. I have tried many other buffets in Vegas but this one is by far my favorite.They have a wide selection of food and everything always tastes fresh. You can add bottomless mimosas as well. Only complaint I would have is the last time we were there the waitress was very busy so it took a while for our glasses to be refilled. Will definitely come again next time I visit Vegas!

Went there for breakfast with family.  Very similar to Wicked Spoon buffet at Cosmo.  Great selection of food...specially like the back section with the Asian food.  You can order your own noodles, they have dim sum, miso and congee.  Better to get discount somehow using rewards card or something...otherwise get ready to pay about $80 for a family of four for breakfast during the mid week.

This review is for customer service and not for the food. We were asked to take a token for the buffet with the wait time of 3hrs. When we showed up after 3 hrs with the token we were asked to wait in line again for couple of hours. Why do they even give you the token if that is the case. Why give wrong expectation to customer that they can have the Buffett when they come back at the time specified in token. They could've managed the holiday customers better given they charge more during the holidays.

57 a head  ...best be hongry if ur gonna hit this place up for dinner!!

The extravanganza known as Caesar's Palace proudly presents BACCHANAL the Buffet!!  ...price include the Hype!
This place is just huge, tho. like 4 gourmet buffets corraled into 1 area decorated by hella people, alot of lighting, glass displays and a rediculous amount of FOOD. 
Dining area is spacious and looks like an upscale metropolitan restaurant in some areas.  
 NOTE: there is a bathroom located right out front of this buffet BUT has     NO baby changing station accommodations so it is very inconvenient if you bring a lil one. FYI
 theres alot of food here to choose ..from crab legs to sushi to prime rib to mexican, breads, assorted gourmet cheeses, asian foods, barbeque, pizza, large dessert bar, assortment if juice drinks on ice, order drinks, PAID bottomless mimosas .....the SAME SHIT you find at all the other buffets but better tasting and slightly better quality dishes. it is what it is as a buffet located at Caesars Palace. arguably the best 'a tourist' ever had ....it IS great but did not amaze me for the amount of hype I read before coming here.

Really meet my expectations when it comes to food , you get a great variety of all kind of dishes , from great selection of meats, salads , seafood and of course dessert area . They have some creative dishes that blows your mind , the taste in every bite you take it really comes so good in flavors, only problem with this place is the price , is $64 on the weekend ( $74 with tax ) , but overall this place one of the best

I was debating whether if I should rate this place 3-stars or 4-stars, then I went with 4...  Here is the reason why.

I first went here about 4 months ago with my boyfriend. We came here around 3 after an hour long walk from Encore Beach Club (Never again, don't do that). There were no lines. We were seated right away, weirdly, because everyone was telling me how packed this place was. After being seated, we went to start our food journey!

I started from the right, which was the Asian food area. Their sushi is SO dry, I cannot eat their rolls or sushi. I gave up on the Asian section eventually. Next to it was the salads... then Italian.... they were both okay. Moving on to my next meal was the meat section. I decided to skip the Mexican section since I am not a fan, but it looked tasty. THE prime rib was good, at least my first time around. It was cooked medium rare, very soft, melted in my mouth. My third plate was the snow crabs! My favorite. You can ask them to get it steamed! It doesn't really take long. There were oysters... cocktail shrimps, etc. as well. WAS I BLOATED AND FULL by then. But I had to get desserts. You can't skip it. Honestly, I think their dessert section is better than everything else in the buffet. To gelatos to crepes, to cheesecake, it was so fancy and colorful.


I was eager to come back to this place..... so I did. Which was last weekend. I came around 1? Don't do that. The line was ridiculous. However, I was lucky enough to cut in front of everyone because my friend was like the player's card? (IDK) But EH. I was 100% sober this time and the food did NOT taste wonderful like last time I came around. Sushi again was dry. HOWEVER, the pho was really good. The soup was actually tasty, instead of just watered down. (Fitting to American taste) The prime rib was NOT tasty at all. It was overcooked, mashed potatoes were so watery. The snow crabs was just the only thing I just enjoyed. My belly was able to take in dessert again by the end, and I again thought dessert was overall the best section out of everything else.

I do not plan to return to this place. I rather go to Wicked Spoon next time.
After writing this review, I changed my rating from 4 stars to 3 stars.

Oh Bacchnal, how I wanted so deeply to love you, but alas my experience fell short. 
The Buffet & Dining area itself was beautiful, that alone was very impressive. you have all the options, just dream of a type of food and it's there!
The staff were all kind, helpful, and efficient. They clearly were pros at the buffet game and were used to all the questions and did not have any judgement if you were back for the third round of bacon! 
I tried so much food it seems like a blur. I do however remember a few items standing out...the Elk sliders were delicious, I found out I was a fan of Elk! That's a fun experience! The huge delicious chunks of bacon were awesome, they tasted great and were just really fun to have to walk around with a huge chunk of bacon on your plate! I was impressed at the different Salsa options you can try, there were at least 6 of not more! 
There are 100s of options for food at this buffet, you definitely will not go hungry. 
The quality of food just does not add up to the price you have to pay per person($55/person), it was an experience and it was a truly very beautifully decorated area, but when in Vegas, I think I would have to pass on this next time.

4.5 Stars! It's hard to say which buffet is better in Las Vegas because they all are amazing. This one is no different!

I've been here twice now, first time was during Christmas, second time was during New Years, so as you can imagine, the wait was a bit long. You get a reservation number from a machine in the front,  the machine will then text you when it's near your turn to get seated. Altogether I waited 2-3 hours.

So now onto the food! This buffet has a wide selection of seafood, Japanese food, Chinese food, different types of american steak and Mexican food. All the food are decent quality, but the ones that stuck out were the seafood and the steaks.

The seafood portion had not only cold crab legs but also hot ones which tasted pretty fresh. All the legs have plenty of meat on them. The steaks were all made from hi-grade quality beef, even Wagyu was an option! (Although it is American Wagyu not Japanese Wagyu)

The dessert corner wasn't too bad either, you can custom make your own crepe. There are so many different toppings and fillings you can use to make this crepe. 

Altogether everything tasted great, I have no complaints about the taste however their dumplings seem to be made too hastily. Every time I try to pick one up, it breaks, I'm Chinese so I should be good at picking up dumplings, but these dumplings weren't made too well. Overall a great buffet and I may even come back for a 3rd time.

Geeze, I thought I already made this review.  I guess I didnt. But I do remember first walking into this buffet.  You are at the beginning of entry with a first impression of modern art work and I was just fascinated by the modern chandeliers too.  We walked in about lunch time.  My parents were unaware after about 30 minutes that there was more to the buffet than to one area.  I have no complaints at all.  Everything was delicious.  The quality of food was just wonderful.  The workers were nice and I have to say it is worth coming in.  You wont regret it at all.  I really love the juices and the Choppino.  I cant help but think in my mind that I really loved everything that I ate.

I didn't know what to expect. I had heard lot's of talk about this buffet. I have been to what I considered the best and also the worst buffets. This buffet has risen to the best of my list. I line was long but not bad and it moved right along. The decor is beautiful. From the fresh flowers at the entrance to all the modern art inside. I doubt you can say there isn't something for you in this buffet. The carving bar has 5 meats. 9 different salsas. Salads are excellent. I don't eat Sushi but it looked very good. Fresh fish and seafood dishes. The desserts are to die for. Everything from cheesecake on a stick to 12 different kinds of ice cream. The service was excellent and I loved the techno/smooth jazz music playing. Of course this all comes with a price. I payed $36.00 on a Friday for lunch. But if you only eat at one pricey buffet in Vegas this should be the one. Wicked Spoon, Wynn and Bellagio have been my favorites but this one jumps to the top.

Here's how two people eat dinner at the Bacchanal Buffet for $55 in two easy steps:

Step 1: Sign up for a timeshare tour a day or two before you plan on going. Spend 3.5 hours looking at a property you have no interest in, keep saying no, get a $25 voucher for this buffet (plus tickets to Jabbawockeez!).

Step 2: Get in line between 2-2:30pm. Don't come too late! Pay the lunch price of $36.99+tax per person. Use voucher. Eat from the lunch buffet for a bit, then at 3pm, enjoy full access to all the extra stuff the dinner buffet has to offer (basically oysters and crab legs).

Total bill: $54.97

I know some "high rollers" can eat here for free and not have to wait in line; however, I am not one of those dudes and I probably won't be back to Vegas for at least another ten years, so this was a pretty good deal for a two normal people who are not Seven Diamonds/Platinum/Solid Gold Toilet Club members.

In terms of quality, this buffet is more than adequate. I've been to a multitude of buffets in my day, from Ponderosa to Westin champagne brunches, and I'd say this is in my top ten. It's comparable to good brunches in Asia, though it doesn't have as many luxury items like foie gras, caviar, steak/tuna tartar, or free booze, all of which I take full advantage of when I'm back in China. It also lacks the pomp and circumstance I'm used to in Asia, such as seven-foot pizzas, curry fountains, clowns, and paella that needs to be carried by two full grown men.

The sushi was much worse here than the buffets I've been to in Asia, but the Mexican food, WARM crab legs, and stone crab claws make up for it. The fried foods and desserts were also good here; it is American, after all. The ice cream actually ruled. Even the macarons were edible! I also enjoyed the aguas frescas, particularly the horchata and jamaica. The pozole and chicharrones were great too, although I don't have a lot of experience with Mexican food.

I eventually decided that if Mexican people are making the food, the Mexican food is good and if Asians are making the food, the Asian food is good. On a related note, the Peking Duck and dumplings here were gross and I'd never get them again for as long as I'm alive.

In addition, the oysters were not good at Bacchanal, which made me so sad. They had virtually no "liquor" and lots of shell shards cramping my style. After eating at Swan Oyster Depot in SF about a week ago, these oysters were noticeably less fresh and more worrisome. 

It's a buffet, I guess. 

Overall, it's a pretty good buffet. It's got good stuff and bad stuff, but the good news is you don't have to eat what you don't like. I spent the first hour of eating only shellfish and the second hour eating everything else. That should be your strategy, if you're smart.

I think if I had paid the full $80 for two lunches (or even more for dinner), I would have felt terribly ripped off. Good thing, I'm cheap AF.

I tried every single item they offered, I kid you not!  I'm seriously not impressed and think that the $44.99 price tag per person is too much!  

This buffet offers pretty much every cuisine you can think of, except Indian.  How cool would that be if they had a little naan station though?!?!  Anyway, there's nothing really out of the ordinary that they offer.  Every station had "American" staples that Americans enjoy most.  

Chinese: pecking duck, chow main, dim sum, fried rice.  Italian: pizza, pasta, meatballs, Japanese: miso soup, ramen, rolls, nigiri.  Stuff like that.  The standard fare any buffet pretty much offers.  I didn't see anything that stood out or made me feel like... "Damn, this ish was worth $50!

I go to buffets because of the variety.  I can't say I ever eat my money's worth, but I really did want to put forth the effort and try everything so I can be as fair as possible in my review.

The crab legs were a total fail as well.  It was too salty and overcooked.  I love indulging on crab legs during my visits to a buffet, but I couldn't even finish the plate they gave me.  *it is nice that they offer warm & cold though.

I'm actually a little disappointed cause the pictures posted gave me a lot of hope!  I really thought it was going to live up to all its hype.  They didn't offer some of the stuff pictured.  I went on a Sunday night if that makes a difference.

I thought their desserts were just ok.  I prefer the one at the Wynn for sure.  They offered a lot of different pastries, but they looked better than they tasted.  The gelato selection wasn't too great, but I did like the baklava flavor!  They also had mango chile, which reminded me of those Mexican candies!  Yum!  There was a crepe station as well.

I didn't experience the service you other yelpers are talking about.  My server took our drink orders and that's about it.  I was with a party if six and we were stacking plates ourselves pushing them to the side.  There was a girl who kept coming to clear them out.  She also replenished our drinks.  Our server started doing his job towards the end, when we were just about ready to finish up.  I paid for my group with CC and wanted to tip with cash after we finished.  I don't know if that made a difference, but i'm sure we probably would've received better service if I had tipped upfront.  Again, that shouldn't matter, but service was nonexistent for my group.

Overall, I probably won't come back.  The quality of the food was better than most buffets, but Wynn would still be my choice.  I think ambiance has a lot to do with it as well.  The decor at bacchanal was kind of bland.  It's modern and sleek, but lacked character.

overated 


food dont taste as good

customer service are less likely to be not friendly

Best Buffet in Las Vegas!!!  This is the best buffet in the valley!!!  I can not describe in words, all of the wonderful food, dessert, and drinks you will experience during your time here.  This is not a cheap buffet, so come prepared to pay and wait in line, but once you are in; your in for a good time.

Took my Grandma here for her birthday, and blew the Bellagio buffet out of the water! All of us had been to the Bellagio last year and even though we still love that buffet, we all agreed this one wins. Great spread, and cheaper by $8. Plus they got realky creative with their presentation

This is without a doubt the best buffet I have ever been to. The variety is unbelievable. They have just about anything you could want: traditional Chinese, dim sum, sushi, pizza, a meat station, made-to-order tacos, and seafood. If you are a seafood lover, you will be in absolute heaven -- snow crab, stone crab, mussels, oysters, lobster bisque, shrimp & grits, many more I'm forgetting...and sea snails!! I love seafood & am a pretty adventurous eater, so I was thrilled to be able to try a food that I have never eaten before! The dessert section was equally impressive and even included a gelato station. I absolutely could not make up my mind, so I got 6 different desserts and just had a little bit of each.

We went for a late brunch on a weekday (around 1:00), so the wait wasn't too bad. We got the all-you-can-drink package, which was worth it for us because we love wine with our meals -- even just lunch! The selection of drinks included in the package could've been better, but for the price, I'd say it was fair. (Cocktails are not included, just mimosas, sangria, the house white wine, & house red wine.) I would recommend avoiding the sangria, though. We tasted both the red & white sangrias, and both were pretty weak & not as flavorful as you'd expect from a sangria -- sort of tasted watered down. That really was the only negative at all, but since we had the drink package, it was no problem. We switched to wine & all was good!

I'm not a huge fan of buffets in general. I like variety, but don't feel like I'm able to eat enough to make it worth the price for all-you-can-eat, and the quality of most buffet food is usually pretty mediocre. But with the huge variety and impressive quality of the food here, I definitely felt like I got my money's worth, even though it is quite expensive. I can't wait to return the next time I'm in Vegas!
The food was amazing. What more could you want from a Buffett? They have it all. Shoutout to Rosa for her kindness and making my party feel special.

Best buffet in Vegas, hands down.

Yes, this means better than Bellagio, better than Wynn, and even ahead of Wicked Spoon (not by much). Well deserved 5 star establishment.

Highlights:

- Fresh oysters
- King crab legs: a stable at most high-end buffets so it's nothing special
- Street tacos: Better than Bellagio's (and they have Al Pastor)
- Sushi: Nigiri is decent, specialty rolls were tasty, made to order ramen and/or udon is the winner here.
- Carving station: chicken sausage, chorizo, hot links, Italian sausage, turkey, brisket, chicken, prime rib, and lamb chops by way kills all buffets on the strip
*I asked for a piece (3pcs b/c I'm fat) of RARE prime rib, it was available. Nice and bloody, unlike other medium-rare to medium prime ribs elsewhere.
- Dim Sum: Delicious. Good Shiu Mai, Ha Gow, tasty dumpling & a decent BBQ pork bun.

Extra points:

- Congee: Very flavorful definitely not your typical buffet food
- Seafood paella. Extremely underrated. Filled with shrimp, clams, mussels.
- Chinese BBQ pork & shrimp fried rice. A little dry but I still thought it was one of the better fried rice dishes around
- Pozole. Yeah I said Pozole; what!?!?!
- Tiramisu gelato, orgasmic. The thought of it makes me want to go back there right now.

Say what you want, this review is anything but fugazi. It's not possible to have tasted everything above in one setting.

I had 5 plates. You're Welcome.

Happy Yelping To All.

Being my first time in Las Vegas I wanted to try out this buffet. After hearing so many good things about this place, I had to try it out. 
I bought a groupon and went to have breakfast on May 2nd, it looked more like brunch. There was a couple of breakfast idems on the buffet, but mostly Chinese food, seafood, italian food, dried meats, cheese's, sushi ect.

I tried everything but the meat carving station, and dessert bar.

Things I liked out of all dishes was shrimp and grits, breakfast sausage links. Everything else was ok, or could have been better. 
The things I thought was really bad and needs major improvement is the sushi. Ive had lots better sushi comming from the grocery store, and the grocery store's sushi isin't even fresh. 
Some of the dried meats and cheeses was very salty and could not eat them.

We went here tonight on our last night in Vegas to celebrate our anniversary and for $112 I was absolutely pissed off at the food quality.  What we ate and what they had to offer was really quite disgusting.  The Asian food was gross. The salad bar was lackluster. The crab legs are tasteless and the butter machine wasn't even turned on so the butter was cold.  The Mexican food looked nasty and I tried some nachos and they were way too spicy.  The American food all tastes like burning wood and the mashed potatoes were lumps of nasty tastes! And afterwards well lets just say.....I stayed close to a bathroom the rest of the night.... Mild case of food poisoning!!!!

King of buffets, they say, and there is some truth to that. The sheer number of options makes you feel like you've stepped into a palace fit for kings. They have stations for Chinese, Italian, French, Greek/Middle Eastern, pizza, steak, seafood, dessert. 

I do wish it were possible to sort through Yelp reviews based on brunch vs. lunch vs. dinner though. We came for an early 8am brunch on a Sunday, and I was disappointed that some of the items mentioned in other reviews were not available - macarons, wagyu beef, for example.  I also wished there were more vegetable dishes -- not vegetarian-friendly dishes like a meatless pizza, but literally just things like a simple asparagus in olive oil, etc. When you're traveling, it's just so hard to get your vegetables in, and all the greasy, buttery stuff gets tiring. Plus, vegetables won't hurt the profit margin!

With so many options, not all up to par, you find yourself eating more or less 10 things anyway, so truly no amount of Groupon-age makes the brunch buffet worth your money. You'd only do it for fun, and maybe only once.
I really love the selections they have here. the meats and seafood section is great and i like how you can get hot/cold crab legs. One of my fav buffets here in vegas.

I have never been a fan of buffets but our group was set on coming here. Once I saw the price tag I was even more reluctant to go but went anyways because that's what you do when you get peer pressured into things. 

My husband and I got two buffets and two bottomless mimosas which was just under $60 a person, not including tip. The food was good, the lines were endless, the service was friendly but it's probably not something I would do again. To be fair I am not much of a buffet kind of gal because I will never eat the amount of food it would take to get my monies worth unfortunately. If you can put it down and enjoy an array of pretty decent food this might be a better option for you. 

Thankfully, we didn't have to wait long because we went to the secret line hidden behind the kiosks where a shorter line for bigger groups resides. With that said, clearly I would recommend going in a big group because you'll be seated earlier.

I was excited to finally check out Brunch at Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's. My friends and I thought we'd be safe from the lines if we came for a late brunch, and boy were we wrong- it was still an hour and a half wait when we got there at 1pm on a Sunday, although this was still during the busy Summer months (end of June). We went to the automatic kiosk machine and entered our information, so we could gamble and/or walk around until our table was ready. We ended up getting texted before the 1.5 hour mark, but you still have to stand in line to pay and be seated, which took about 10 minutes from when we got there. Adult Brunch on Sunday costs $43.99, but this includes bottomless mimosas (I don't think there is a way to waive the alcohol if you don't drink). 

-Seafood Plate (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=n-9x_33nc6kufoos1XDSHg#n-9x_33nc6kufoos1XDSHg): The chilled shrimp were amazing- super fresh and huge pieces. Crab legs were good, and you can ask them to steam it quickly if you don't mind waiting for a few minutes. The smaller crab legs were really difficult to eat even though they are partially cracked, but you can ask your server for a small mallet if needed. The gazpacho was only ok.
-Sushi & Asian Foods Plate (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=n-9x_33nc6kufoos1XDSHg#GmKIYZO_0rIIlQJozVPNIQ): The sushi isn't that great, but at least the fish is fresh. The pad thai, green curry, and Chinese style eggplant were good, and the dim sum solid for a buffet (I had the Taro Bun and Pork Dumpling). The donut in the back was REALLY good, so definitely get that fresh if you see them making it. Skip the smoked salmon, which was really salty. The cup of vegetables would have been better without the sauce.
-Desserts Plate 1 (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=n-9x_33nc6kufoos1XDSHg#SGztT_WtbOC8VC2M7P0MOA): From bottom L to R: Passion Fruit Cheesecake was ok but not great, the macaron like dessert wasn't good, and the Mango Pudding? was just ok. I liked the Pandan Cake, which was moist, and the Green Tea Crème Brulee was the best out of the 5.
-Desserts Plate 2 (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=c30_hSNhwaedDB7VAXdoHw#c30_hSNhwaedDB7VAXdoHw): The cupcakes were horrible, but the pineapple tofu cakepop was actually really good! The mango mousse cake and their other cakes were just so-so.

Service here was ok- our server was around at first, but there would be times we didn't see her for half an hour or more, and thus couldn't get our mimosa flutes re-filled. Other than that, Bacchanal is by far the best buffet that I've been to in Vegas (I've been to the Wynn, Cosmo, Bellagio) with the selection and quality of food. Definitely make sure you come early on the weekend if you want to avoid the wait.

Until recently I cannot even remember the last time I had gone to a Las Vegas buffet.  We chose Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace because at the time, it had great Yelp reviews and simply a reputation as being "the best" buffet in Vegas.  At over $60 per person, my expectations were pretty high. 

When we got to Bacchanal there was a huge line and we were told there would be a 3 hour wait!  I believe you may be able to put your name down  and walk around until your name is called.  However, there was no way I was going to hang out and wait at Caesar's for a few hours, especially when my family and I were starving.  I don't think I would wait 3 hours for any restaurant.  Turns out, we were able to get in right away since my mother-in-law is disabled and has problems standing.  Props for the manager for being so gracious about that. 

What surprised me most about Bacchanal was the atmosphere.  Because of it's reputation and price I was expecting something a bit more elegant.  A buffet though, is still a buffet, no matter how much you try to dress it up.  The large rooms with diners getting up and down and walking around to get food still reminded me of a school cafeteria.  

The food is divided into stations from several nationalities:  Asian, Mexican, Italian, plus "American" (prime rib, Kobe sliders, fried foods, etc.), a seafood station. And of course the required dessert station.  

My love of Asian food and Seafood prompted me to concentrate on the Asian station (sushi rolls, various Chinese dishes) and Seafood (crab legs, clams casino, crayfish).  Nothing was bad, but honestly, nothing stood out either.  Things I would not recommend:  the tacos (made with homemade tortillas) and the Kobe sliders (hard as a rock with no flavor).  There was a huge array of desserts. I sampled a few but I could not really point out anything that was truly scrumptious for me. I did not even really care for the gelato served.  

Perhaps compared to other Vegas buffets this is first in class. I would prefer. spending a comparable amount of money on a restaurant that specializes in one type of cuisine and does it well.  I would also feel more comfortable dining in a bit of a more intimate setting, instead of the large cavernous rooms at Bacchanal. 

.

As far as Vegas buffets go I'm inexperienced. To be honest though, I've been to other buffets near home and have had a far better selection of food options. Bacchanal is not bad as a whole since the decor is mesmerizing and the servers are phenomenal (I'm talking about you Adelaide). If you get to this place before noon you can skip the wait lines, and even better yet, if you have a party larger than 8 people you can get into an even more expedited line. 

The price per person is up there. It cost about $75 per person and an additional add on for the bottomless mimosas. I had a total of four dishes, making sure to efficiently pace myself through the 2 hour meal. My starter plate was the seafood since this was the most talked about on the Yelp reviews I read. Surprisingly, this was my first time having crab legs, so I was excited-needless to say. Unfortunately, the crab meat was not as savory as my fellow Yelp Elites had mentioned. Maybe it was the cook for the day... 

What I did like a lot were the juices, the salami selection, sushi dish, and the dessert especially. I highly recommend having the Nutella coffee ice cream since it combines two of my favorite flavors. Overall, a great buffet in terms of living the lavish Vegas lifestyle, but maybe not a place to drop dough on parties that aren't inclined to trying new foods or groups of children under 12 who will end up eating pizza and fries regardless of the options presented.

In between the 20 mins, I saw the server in that section handing 4 jars each to 3 customers that appear to know them. I'm Asian & since they were conversing in Chinese, I can tell the server was cutting slacks for them & let them have more soup, leaving other customers waiting & go back for nothing. 


The pros:

3) fresh seafood

Seriously, when you see the line, you will think it is so good that ppl are willing to wait for 3 hours or more to get in. Great and fresh selection of delicious foods, including non-oversalter meats and fish, and no sugar added desserts. Plenty of veggies.

First off I am not a buffet fan, but after all the hype about this place I've been wanting to go.  So my husband asked me where I wanted to go, I said, "Bacchanal."  He said, "A buffet? I can't take you there for your birthday!"  I said, "Yes, you can and you will give the birthday girl what she wants." So here we are on a Tuesday for lunch.  If a buffet is good at lunch, it has got to be great at dinner, right?

The line to get in was short at 11:30 am. We tipped up front, not sure if this was why we were seated by the window with a pool view, which was nice since it was a beautiful, spring day and my birthday. Love that the hostess seemed just as excited as us to eat here.  

We were seated and the waitress swapped the $10 unlimited mimosa for straight "champagne" for me, saying she won't tell the boss.   Nice, but it was cheap "champagne" and I probably should have paid more for a better quality glass listed on the menu. However, the "nice" wines by the glass are waaay overpriced since they are ordinary wines, but I guess they can overcharge.

First off the presentation of everything is exquisite.   My suggestion from learning lesson,  is survey the whole buffet before you start, otherwise, you can miss out on some atypical buffet items, which makes Bacchanal worth your while. There is a seafood station, carving station, Mexican, Italian, Asian, and American stations.  Oh and I almost forgot, they have a HUGE dessert station.  I saw one person just eat desserts. 

I liked how many items are already plated and diners can grab and keep moving along, which means you don't have to wait extra long behind those who don't  know how to use tongs or other basic serving utensil. 

Given my limited capacity, I chose items that I can't readily get or takes way to much effort to cook, and then I choose a few items I've never had before.  I picked up a few shrimp, which were prepared correctly, but I normally skip because I eat them often enough. However, I was hungry while waiting for oysters, which were being shucked, but they disappeared within seconds of reaching the service station.  Never got any oysters.  They also had seafood salads and oyster shooters too.  They were decent fillers, but were not chilled enough.  No crab legs, which was a bummer, but it was the lunch buffet which is priced at $32.99/pp.  Can't expect everything at that price. 

I hit the carving station which was impressive, especially for lunch. I chose the brisket, prime rib, slab bacon, and specially requested getting the cracklings off the ham.  They also had pork ribs, roast turkey, and a variety of sausages.  What is not to love about fatty, roasted meat?  All solid choices; meats all juicy, but my personal taste requires a bit more salt.  Prime rib was probably the best from any buffet...rare, med-rare and still warm.  Yay! The carver also asks you how you like your meat before carving it, which is nice.

Third round I cleaned up with some carnitas pork from the Mexican station.  Some interesting cheese and charcuterie I never had before as well as purple mustard, which tasted wonderful.  I also picked a few cheeses and a beautiful checkerboard feta and watermelon salad (my type of dessert).  Remember that shrimp I ate? Well, I am kicking myself because I had no room for roast duck from the Asian station or any sushi.   

Overall, I think the higher quality of food and detailed presentation is worth the higher price in comparison to other buffets.  I like not feeling like I am eating at a buffet, but I like eating a buffet. YKWIM? This is the only place I will eat a buffet a now.   

Don't miss out on good food, just because it is a buffet. This as an upscale buffet, better food than some restaurants.  The servers and the staff are all professional and nice, which makes it feel much more restaurant-like and less like a cafeteria.

Eh, felt really crowed and the route to get the food wasn't well arrange. Basically feels like you climb through all the customer's tables to get food.

They have really good meat, cheese, crab legs and pizza!(mushroom pizza!!).  The meat station: both ribs, brisket are very good!!
Cheese selection is amazing, goat cheese and mozzarella cheese both smooth and rich.

Soups taste like butter and sugar....I tried onion soup and butternut soup both tastes very sweet.
Dessert didn't stand out (Wynn buffet has way better quality dessert.) but they have good verity.
The speed of cycling the food wasn't fast enough. The clams only have the shells left for a while...and the oysters are sandy doesn't look fresh. ( I didn't even want to try, them look so dirty)

Lives up to it's reputation as the best buffet in town. Whether it is the setting, variety of food or quality. If you can afford the price, you won't be disappointed; especially with the seafood section. Make sure to try the mushroom truffle soup. It's to die for, and the calamari. For desert, the choices are endless but fresh made crepes should be a must. The setting is more like a fancy restaurant than a buffet with beautiful decor and nice music. It this is what it is anyway, with the quality of the food. Make sure you try it once even if it's above your budget. It's absolutely worth it.

After doing much research and hearing great reviews about this place, my husband and I decided to try it last night for dinner...what a huge mistake and waste of money.  All the food tasted like it had been made for quite a while...everything tasted lukewarm or cold.  The calamari was very stale as were the little baskets of nachos.  The pizza was so soggy, I couldn't even pick it up without it falling apart.  The lasagna was so cold inside it still had pieces of shredded cheese that had not melted inside of chewy lasagna noodles.  The cheeseburger sliders were raw on the inside and the bun was so hard, it was difficult to even bite into it.   Everything looked so beautiful and delicious, but nothing and I mean nothing tasted delicious.  I was even disappointed in the dessert bar.  Again, it all looked very appetizing but tasted terrible.  I've never had a meal where I couldn't finish chewing the food, but had to constantly keep spitting it out into my napkin.  My husband had to do the same as well.  $118 for 2 adults, ridiculous for this poor quality of food.  Do yourself a favor and skip this place.  There are way better restaurants on the strip.

Yummy. 

This place had a lot of variety of food to chose from which is always a plus. Only bad thing about this place is the never ending line. Lucky for us, our friend is a seven star so we got the crab legs delivered to our table but everywhere else, the line was so long. Maybe it was because I went there on a super busy weekend...then again when is it a not a busy weekend in Vegas. It is definitely worth a visit if your staying in Caesars but I would not wait in that long line to eat their food.
We sat for 3 hours lunching and still felt we didn't do justice! Great variety, great ambience, great service, great experience!

This buffet was fantastic! Never had anything like it! Food was cooked to perfection, and all staff was super nice. Must have in Vegas, for sure! The crab legs were so tender you could crack with your hands, sushi was delish,  and even the lamb and Mac n cheese was superb!

Okay the first time I tried this place, I wasn't impressed and I was kind of disappointed because I've heard so much hoop-la about this place.  The last time I went to Vegas I gave this place another shot and for whatever reason, it was sooo much better.  We waited for a little over an hour to be seated, but it was definitely worth the wait this time around.  They have a variety of food for your palate, from seafood, Asian, American-traditional, Italian and so on. The seafood station and dessert is probably my favorite. 

The King Crab is juicy, sweet and plenty of meat.  It's served either hot or cold. They also have raw oysters, crawfish, crab legs, and shrimps.  

The dessert station is great for those who have a sweet tooth.  They have crepes made to order, gelato, and etc.  

I always thought Wicked Spoon was the best buffet in Vegas, but now I understand why they say Bacchanal is the best.  I'm glad I gave this place another shot.  If you go during the holidays, then be prepare to pay extra from their regular price and wait in a long line.  It's about $60 per person during dinner.   There's a 2 hour limit, so eat your heart out.

An enormous buffet, but I was a bit disappointed, especially it was $70 per person without the drinks.
First, it was advertised to serve king crabs, it was actually snow crabs.
Secondly, the sushi selection was less than meh.
Lastly, the steak selection was also weak.

is good too i a super deserrt eatter so everything is ok

Hands down, this is still the BEST buffet in Vegas. I've tried the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan and the Buffet at Bellagio. Both are cheaper but you really do get what you pay for. Neither can compare to the variety of options that Bacchanal can offer.

Plus, THE DESSERTS! I'd come here just for them. They have an entire section just for desserts including a gelato bar and crêpe station. I also love that they offer fresh juices and smoothies too, and not just orange juice and apple juice. They have watermelon juice, cucumber basil juice, and an orange smoothie that tastes just like an orange creamsicle pop.

I love love love this buffet and I'll definitely come back next time I'm in Vegas.

The lines can be long but in my opinion the best buffet in las vegas. When I eat at buffets I usually find a few things I like but at Bacchanal every item is like a 5 star dining experience. The meat selection is incredible.

The best of the best! The food is excellent.  We eat here all the time.     I wish, I could live there.  

It's the best place on the planet.

I read many reviews about seafood buffets in Las Vegas.  After multiple negative reviews about the Circus Circus seafood buffet I chose to opt for the more expensive seafood buffet at Caesar's Palace. While the food was good and of quality it lacked the variety that I expected for a $100+ for two buffet.  I went on a Tuesday for lunch arriving around 2 in the afternoon.  No snow crab legs or raw oysters which I was looking forward to.  The all you can drink Mimosa's were nice as were the mussels and prime rib.  The crawfish were small and again, a lack of variety for the price.  The oyster shooters aka "bloody mary" oyster shooters were good.  The deserts were rather good and in small portions that provided a taste rather than over eating.  If you are looking for a "high quality" buffet try the Broadmoor  Sunday buffet Brunch in Colorado Springs.  Far better for the price and costs less.  For the "experience" this was a good buffet but I will not go back to it.  I could have had a decent seafood dinner at a restaurant for less money.

By far, this is one of the best upscale buffet in Las Vegas. Fresh steamed lobsters, cocktail shrimp that is so juicy and succulent, fresh oysters, and arrays of gourmet brunches that are just completely worth every single penny. The line was long during the holiday season but it moved up pretty quickly. Service is excellent, awesome decor and we all had an excellent time. 

I'll definitely return soon!

We had a group of 5 on a Friday night. The wait time was 120-minutes but my boss was extremely hungry and paid an extra $25 each to skip to the front of the line. Which means you get to wait in line with other people that paid to skip. It was quick about 10-minutes.

The service was excellent. Our waitress was friendly and attentive.

The seafood was delicious from the King Crab to the oysters. My only complaint would be that my Tri-tip was very cold and not edible.

I most likely would not go back due to the large crowds and I am not someone who can eat multiple plates of food. If you have friends that have a big appetite it is a good experience.
Good food. Good seafood.  Good desserts. Love the steamed crab legs.  Quality of food is better Than other Vegas buffets.

OK. I'm not sure where all these positive reviews came from as I decided to try this buffet BECAUSE of these reviews, but I need to post this review to help all the foodies out there.  AVOID AVOID.  If you are looking for interesting new food, complex flavors, spicy, or just plain solidly cooked food this is NOT THE PLACE.  It is 40 dollars for lunch  (50 for dinner) per person and its NOT worth it.  We tried a little bit of everything. The asian station was bland and the meat was chewy.  Dumplings were bland, noodles were bland, rice was tasteless, stir fry dishes were just brown sauce messes. 
Latin station was the best of all of the stations. Decent tacos but nothing that makes you run to them again and again. 
Seafood was just cooked, no seasoning and sauces were standard and bland.  
Chicken and waffles were decent, nothing to scream about. 
Sweets stations is all looks and no taste.  Even the cookies were bad.


After I ate here I had indigestion, stomach pain, and it lasted ALL DAY.  PLEASE DO NOT GO HERE.  There are so many other places in Caesars worth going to like Gordon Ramsay Pub, Wolfgang Spago, or Bobby's Mesa.  Save your health and stay away.

It was my third time in Vegas and I had yet to try one of their famous buffets. My friends and I decided on Bacchanal due to the rave reviews and it was the worst mistake ever. 

During Labor Day weekend, the buffet was a horrifying $70 per person for dinner - yes, $70! Now, the steep price would not have mattered had the food been tasty or edible. My friend found a sizable PIECE OF METAL in one of their Italian meatballs. The metal resembled an industrial staple of some sort and luckily my friend spat it out before swallowing. We were absolutely horrified and disgusted - all appetites were lost at that point.

Prior to the discovery, I sampled a number of dishes from their snow crab legs, crawfish, stone crabs, to their fried chicken, calamari, dimsum, and crab cakes. All failed to impress and were very disappointing. The snow crab legs were still frozen and small in size. The crawfish and shrimp was flavorful but way too salty. The dimsum lacked quality and seasoning. 

Bacchanal boasts a large variety of dishes and desserts but the overall quality, cleanliness, and preparation is an absolute disaster. I give props to the manager for reacting quickly when we informed her of the metal staple, however, simply comping his meal and offering us free drinks was not enough. I mean, we had just started our meal and all appetites were lost following the discovery.

For a group of five, it was over $300 down the drain due to a poor buffet that could have landed my friend in the hospital. Save your time and money and avoid this buffet!

Before Vegas hotels fancied up their buffets, I was not a fan of buffets at all. Granted now you're paying more for the trendy decor & creative individual mini fry baskets/ramekins/buckets, but the food quality has also improved. 

Par-for-the-course beautiful desserts, but only tiramisu & the caramel macaron stood out as worth the calories. The rest were just eye candy (literally.)

Everything else I tried was phenomenal: har gow, shrimp cocktail, warm king crab legs w/ buttah, black bean crab, mashed potatoes, sweet potato maple tots, lobster corn chowdah, mango juice. 

Wish I had more room to try: pozole & tacos. 

My group went wild for the carving station & charcuterie. 

$51/person. Not a long line at 4 pm on a Friday. 2 hour max at your table. Became a favorite of mine & the bf's after just one bite!

It's amazing and delicious here!
Best Gourmet Buffet in Vegas!
Tip:
6 or more people you pass the crazy line!
2 to 3 people check in on YELP you pass up the lounge and go straight to the front! 
Everyone must show your check in on your phone

Came here for a weekend brunch. I was honestly underwhelmed by the experience. We had a reservation so there was not a wait, but the food was only average. We also had to switch tables 30 minutes into our meal due to lack of cleanliness one table away. The servers seemed to only be concerned with whether I had prepaid their tips.. Yes, there is variety in the offerings of the buffet, but the quality is not present.

Absolutely worth the money.  The quality, service, selection.  This was a really great experience.  We had a reward for one buffet and we are so glad we chose Bacchanal Caesars brunch Buffett. Favorites were breakfast pizza, banana fosters donuts, shrimp and grits, scrambled eggs with Boursin cheese, basil cucumber juice, watermelon juice, desserts were all amazing.  I had a pink lemonade cupcake and it was perfect.  Seaweed salad was so good and fresh.  Charcuterie looked amazing but we didn't eat any.  The presentation and atmosphere were excellent.  I like that it wasn't self serve drinks.   Due to traveling with groups over the years I've eaten at several buffets (Plant Hollywood, Rio, Paris, Flamingo, Mirage, Bellagio) this one was the best in all aspects.

We've returned two years later, and I wasn't as WOWed. 

First of all, their texting waiting system? They don't tell you that it takes another hour PAST the waiting time printed on your ticket for you to be seated. My ticket time said "742pm", which was literally 5 hours later, but we figured it was still fine and gave us time to still get ready before going out. 

I get my text around 730 saying to head over to the podium. We get there, and are told to stand in the line just to pay. From the time we stood in line to the time we got seated, it was another extra hour. I feel like they should tell you this on the printed ticket, because it falsely makes you believe that you'll get in at a certain time. I was pretty annoyed by the time we sat.

The goods:
Crab legs- they have them hot and cold, and if you ask the guy behind the table, he'll hand pick some good legs for you
Nachos- love the nachos in the small saucer
Baked potato- like the small size with cheese, bacon, and sour cream
Mushroom truffle soup- pretty good flavor. One of the better soups I've had at a buffet
