This place wasn't bad by anymeans. I'm sure tourist of all over will absolutely love it here. But for a born n raised vegas foodie, it just didn't do it for me. But hey, neither did wicked spoon and it was voted best in vegas! Maybe buffets just aren't my forte :)

(Note that I'm rating 2 stars which I think is applicable for vegetarians or ppl who don't eat seafood and are going for the dinner buffet). 

This is my second time at Caesars and the first time for dinner. The first thing we noticed was that my girlfriend who is vegetarian didn't have many options at all - we've come to assume that Vegas buffers are good for vegetarians but this definitely was not the case. And even though I eat meat, I don't really eat seafood so a lot of the options were ruled out for me too. It seemed to us that most ppls meals revolves around seafood and that seemed to be the highlight of the buffet. 

Apart from the lack of food options, we were extremely disappointed with the service at the counters - there seemed to be no one around to help answer our questions, the dishes were mislabeled quite a few times, and the Choco lava cake that I got was mediocre at best. 

Nevertheless we had enough food to stuff ourselves with, and coupled with the bottomless mimosa package that we got, made up for some of the experience.

We arrived at 11:53 on Tuesday for brunch and were surprised to find no line at all. 2 families in front of us were handled by the cashiers and we stepped right up to a cashier in time to see the line rapidly building behind us. By the time we finished paying and were led to our seats the wait time looked like 20 minutes.

Caesar's palace still has free parking so it's wise to use it and avoid walking around in the oppressive afternoon heat.

The huge dessert selection, the excellent service with free unlimited soft drinks really puts the experience above any buffet I've ever enjoyed.

Is it worth it? Yes for lunch, but I would not pay for dinner at this or any place, but that's me.

I managed to taste about 75% of the offerings by eating a little of everything. I didn't waste my time with pizza or cold cuts but by the time we were all stuffed to the gills, they were setting out different food that I didn't have any space to try.

Upon visiting another buffet, I now realize that Bacchanal has ruined me for other buffets by setting the bar so much higher. I thought I was underwhelmed and that the establishment was over-promoted but now realize that this is the benchmark that all other buffets should be compared and because of this realization, I'm adding a star to my review.

Yes all the hype about the Bacchanal but I think it's about preference...it's my first time here with a bunch of my girlfriends. We went during lunch time which ranged at $45 if you want their unlimited drinks (only a few varieties) it's an additional $15. We waited for a good 20-25 min from cash register to seating which isn't bad at all seeing that there were a lot of ppl. If you have a big party they do allow separate checks!! Kudos! This is a pay first then eat buffet. The restaurant was clean elegant and updated with Decor. 

The menu was quite extensive and the buffet was large! the different food stations take you to different parts of the world. So I recommend pacing and eating small portions (pictures included). Asian,     Italian, Mexican, American, and Seafood are just about some of the region of foods.

Asian Food Chinese/Japanese/Southeast Asia (3/5): I literally took one piece of food/veggie from each food tray from the Chinese section. The mix veggies was good I liked it, dimsum: only had the hargaw-good especially with chili oil!! Mapo tofu was decent. Eggroll was mushy and decent. Korean japchae decent, Thai beef basil was decent but was not even that warm when I ate it...sushi was mediocre had better sushi at cheaper buffets. They are constantly doing different rolls bc the sushi area is small they can't fit all their types of sushi do it ranges from different time frames...the curry was quite good as well.

Asian Soup Station: 4/5 they had pho, udon, ramen, wonton. Pho broth 4/5 delicious prob one of my favs there lol noodles could've been better but they give you a fat thick cut of beef for the pho bomb! Udon 3.5 decent broth and noodles good shrimp temporary on the side. I wished I couldn't gotten a chance to try the other soups but I was too full! You may have to wait quite some time bc there was only one guy doing the Soup station and trying to roll sushi...so be patient.

Mexican 3/5: the only thing I ate there was the tacos which at times had a long line so I had already ate mostly everything else. Finally When I went there was no one in line, I ended up getting all three kinds of meat: Beef, Chicken, Al Pastro. They reheat the meat onto a rotating flat grill and cook the corn tortilla ontop so it takes a few min...Super sad like honestly I feel like the taco trucks versions were better---the flavor was mediocre. I didn't try the pazole but heard from the group it was good. The guacamole was good per my friend too. They only use one tortilla with a bunch of meat piled on top it would've been better if they doubled it. 

American Station: 4/5 only giving it more rating bc they had a lot of variety in this section. Prime rib was good but I believe the star of this show was the Wagyu Beef omg super delicious!! The roasted veggies were delicious...Mac and cheese was quite good not the best but decent. Fried chicken was too dry but the coating outside layer/skin was bomb. 

Seafood: 0/5 I'm a seafood fan so I'm super disappointed in the selection of seafood. Cold seafood consisted of Dungeness Crab, Stone Crab, Snow Crab, large shrimps and snails. The hot seafood stuff like mussels, Paella, etc...
What I was aiming for was lobster or king crab but there was none...

Didn't get to the Italian area/salad area was too full by that time 

The dessert station was amazing!!!! Their selection of ice cream is super adorable recommend the pistachio and the all white one forgot the name and it's NOT vanilla! Loved their fruits!! 

Our server was awesome! I loved their hot green tea brand! I think I had really high expectation from Vegas buffets so my expectation was a little to high for the lunch rush--maybe next time I'll try the dinner portion and re

It was a great experience, researching the many great buffets and attending many of them, bacchanal buffet was right up there with the best. The wait was a bit long but well worth it. The customer service was good but Esmeralda Juarez was a great help with bringing beverages to our table and having some good conversation with us. The food quality was well and a lot of it was made right in front of us which made a fun experience. To end the night with great dessert with everything in between freshly made crepes to boba drinks made with our choice of ice cream.

I LOVE this buffet in Vegas. Arrive early though because there can be a wait from 45 min to 2  hours !!! I really enjoyed the cheese and salami ! Especially their prime rib or steak ! This is definitely a go to place buffet when in Vegas !!!

Save up for this buffet, it's worth it. 
So good, so much to choose from. I had a large chunk of time and money dedicated to this with great expectations. I wasn't disappointed. 
I left full, and happy.

I came here after hearing the rumors that this is the "best buffet in Vegas." Let me preface my review with the fact that I am a pescatarian, a recession-era college graduate, who doesn't drink and I was underwhelmed with my experience here.

I checked out the tips on Yelp, which advised me to arrive early so that I could get a ticket before paying and being seated (thanks, Yelpers!). My boyfriend and I grabbed our tickets from one of the kiosks next to the hostess's podium, which is already pretty confusing as people were fumbling around, wondering how to get seated at the Holy Grail of Vegas buffets. Of course, we checked in at 1p so we would have enough time to embrace the brunch price tag (with the unlimited mimosas for my beau) and stay for the beginning of their dinner service. We were notified via text exactly 70 minutes after we got our ticket (as promised) that our seats will be held for 15 minutes. We made it in the nick of time and, luckily, there was no line to pay. We were asked to pose for souvenir pictures in front, which we were later solicited to purchase for $25 during our meal - just because we are eating here does not mean we want to spend $25 to commemorate our excessive spending on excessive eating! We were seated pretty quickly, as there were plenty of vacant tables around the restaurant.

The selection was tragically lackluster. There were the standard staples of most buffets (e.g. salad bar, pizza station, hamburger sliders, crab legs, sushi, pastries) with stations for meat-carving, meat and cheese, dim sum, udon/ramen, and southern comfort food (i.e. corn on the cob, tater tots, etc.). As a pescatarian who doesn't like shellfish, you could imagine how limited my options were. There were about 5 types of rolls to choose from [including pickled vegetables (seriously?!), imitation crab (come on!), spicy tuna], and then a few choices of nigiri (salmon, tuna, and shrimp). The dim sum selection was pitiful and I'm pretty sure the har gow had been frozen. My boyfriend loved the shumai.

We moseyed on over to the seafood station and grabbed some salmon and some sort of unmarked whitefish, both of which we decided not to finish after one bite. My boyfriend excitedly filled his plate with the selections from the meat-carving station only to find out that most of the lamb chop had been fat and it was underwhelming, despite the grand presentation.

Now onto the desserts -- they have a crepe station, which I was really excited about until I realized that they cook the crepes for you and then you slather on preserved berries, bananas, and cool whip to your liking - where's the nutella? Why didn't they put fresh fruit in them for me like a real creperie would have? Oh, right, I paid $50 to do it myself... I also tried their gelato, which was pretty delicious, but they were distributed in small servings (smaller than my fist), which, in retrospect, is probably wise since people are probably stuffed by the time they reach dessert. Their vanilla with fleur de sel and salted caramel flavors are delicious! They also have a create-your-own ice cream sandwich option with chocolate cookies or almond cookies, which was a pretty neat option.

Essentially, this buffet is not pescatarian/vegetarian-friendly. I ended up filling up on spicy tuna rolls and cocktail shrimp with dabbling in new, disappointing dishes in between before giving up and diving into the desserts. I am also disappointed that their brunch selection was more "-unch" than "br-," as they did not have many "traditional" breakfast options (other than dim sum and red velvet pancakes).

My favorites from this place were the juices they had in adorable individual carafes (guava, mango, cranberry, to name a few) and their ice cream, I guess. 
If you're looking for high prices, limited selection, and even less satisfying quality, this is the place to be! Nothing in this buffet seemed notable or worth coming back for. My boyfriend mainly liked his sliders that he topped with their guacamole, but seriously? I'm not going to pay $50 for sliders, juice, and gelato.

I'm glad we tried it so that we know what "the best buffet in Vegas" is really like, so we can go back to The Bellagio with $20 more in our pockets and Beef Wellington and sushi hand rolls in our stomachs!

Highly overrated..... Everything in this buffet looks gorgeous, I can't argue that at all. I have never seen such a huge selection of foods at a buffet in my entire life. Everything looked wonderful and unique.... but nothing tasted that way. Everything was bland, the fish was NOT fresh, and not one thing impressed me. The chili and little tacos were probably the best things we had..... We were really disappointed. Everything was cold or melted by the time we got it back to our table. This buffet would be absolutely amazing if all of the various foods they served that look so great, were actually good.... It's not worth the price nor the hype, and it's definitely not worth the extra $25 when doing the buffet of buffets.... I would never go back here.

Caesars Palace New Buffet. Trying to be like Wicked Spoon, eh.
Sorry Caesars, Wicked Spoon still wins in my book. 
Yeah you got the Seafood going on but other than that your average.

This is probably the best buffet I've been to. A little pricier than most buffet but it's worth the money. Avoid peek hour cause it's a wait. I came around 8pm. Made it in like 15 mins. They have Chinese, Italian, Mexican, seafood, American, seafood...overall im happy with our buffet. Definitely recommended

OK, it's time to get out your fanciest pair of fat-pants. We have ourselves a buffet here, folks. And not just any buffet--it's a Vegas-style buffet!

Back story: I was on a mission and meticulously planned out this meal. I came during the tail end of lunch so I could pay the lunch price but grub out on the dinner dishes. Yes, I'm so Asian. But 2:30pm was also the latest my stomach could last before the intense pangs of hunger kept me from functioning normally. I wanted to milk the most out of this buffet (I'm forking over nearly $40, yo!). I even went on an intense hike before my meal with only a Clif Bar to hold me over. I'm not joking when I say meticulous. 

Bacchanal is heralded as the best buffet in Sin City. Although I haven't visited any other buffets in LV, I won't really have any reason to if Bacchanal is the best...especially since the food here was simply average. There were a few highlights but even on a VERY empty stomach, I wasn't impressed. I'll give them credit though, the selection is extensive and quite diverse. However, nothing was so amazing that I would return. 

Like most things in Vegas, Bacchanal Buffet is a spectacle. From the chic venue to the paparazzi-esque photographers snapping a photo of you before you enter the buffet (because clearly you will look and feel like crap after the buffet), everything is over-the-top and grand. That's not bad but it can be exhausting. 

This buffet provides huge variety:
Seafood - raw oysters, mussels, shrimp, king crabs, clams, fish, seafood paella 
Meats - BBQ ribs, briskets, lamb chops, chicken, sausages
Asian stations - sushi rolls, nigiri, dim sum, Chinese stir fries, BBQ pork, noodle soups (own station with "fresh" won ton mein, udon, etc.)
Latin station - didn't check it out but there were plenty of chips, salsa, tacos, (did try the aguas fresca and they were super sweet)
Desserts - cookies, macarons, ice cream/sorbet, flan, churros, cakes, brownies, candies, chocolate-covered strawberries, ice cream mochi (black sesame and green tea), and made-to-order crepes
Miscellaneous - sliders, Parmesan fries, sweet potato tots, pizzas, pastas, chicken & waffles

Not to mention you have your standard salad and fruit stations. Sweet Jesus (or is it Caesar since this buffet is located in Caesars Palace?). It is so overwhelming. The only items that stood out were the lamb chops, unagi nigiri, green tea creme brulee, and churros. And these were enjoyed with an asterisk; the lamb chops were savory but 40% of it was purely fat. The unagi nigiri was surprisingly tasty but it had a huge roll of rice underneath. I liked the freshly made crepes (you choose the toppings and sauce) but that's just waaaaay too much, even to share. I was excited about the mochi ice cream but these were not handmade. I saw the staff unwrapping and dumping them out of plastic containers. Oh wait, I lied. I did enjoy the red bean ice cream!

At the end, your money does go a long way in terms of the food offered. Although, it's just a lot of mediocre food and not the highest quality. 

P.S. I overdid it with my meticulous planning and didn't account for the delayed fullness. I went for three rounds of dessert when I should have thrown in the towel after the first one. I literally have never been so stuffed in my life and I eat A TON. I was 88.6% sure I was going to throw up at my table. Thank God (Caesars?) I didn't. Be forewarned, buffets can turn you into greedy monsters. Don't overestimate your stomach capacity!
Definitely best buffet in the world. Wide variety of delicious food, great atmosphere, very clean and excellent customer service. I highly recommend this place!

I'm disappointed my boyfriend and I wasted our money at this buffet for dinner. It's mediocre at best and we had high hopes. This place needs some training on flavor and quality because everything is bland. The price is outrageous too.
The food was okay. Maybe im just bad at directions but the layout was little confusing at first. Price was little high.

I used to like this place. I came there 2 times, the first time everything so amazing but my second time it's quit disappointed, lamp smell bad, crab lag so small and they didn't refill their crabs, service so slow, I have to ask for my drink twice times and waited so long for taking my dish off. By the way I love dessert zone :)

We ate at The Bacchanal Buffet (Caesars Palace, Las Vegas) on March 17, 2015. We picked the restaurant because of the high ratings on the internet. We were disappointed at the variety of foods; we have seen much more food choices in other buffet restaurants. For a $52.99 dinner per person, we had expected better value for the money. Perhaps not all foods were prepared at around 4:45pm?

Also, we found the sushi (located in a different section) somewhat hard or dried as if they were made hours ago. 

Relatively speaking, the soups were good, the seafood were fresh. The desserts were delicious, with many to choose from. I give the desserts a 5-star, the rest a 3 because it's nothing so different from the other buffets we've sampled.

Arrived here at around 8pm, we checked-in and received a time of 10:21pm to check back.  We left and came back early at 10:00pm and finally were seated at 10:50pm and were told that the food would stop being served at 11:30pm.  The price ended-up being $173.20 for 2 people (more than usual since it is holiday prices).  So, bottom line, we had to rush through dinner for a very expensive meal.  Food was good but it still sucked to have been that rushed.  Side note:  The lobster was pretty dry, steamed crab was tasty.

It doesn't worth the wait. I gave this place two chances and it just didn't surprise me. If you are just looking for just being full and spent 1-2 hour waiting to get that feeling, you are in the right place. However, if you are expecting impressive buffet dishes, then don't go.

Honestly this place is overhyped.  Dinner prices have gone up to about $50 on the weekend.  It was worth about $30.  The wait was about 1.5 hours on a Saturday night at 8:30 PM...  We got in and then on my second trip they started shutting down the stations.  WTF!  No oysters worth eating (they put out leftover mini oysters...)  The crab legs were older and the chef "refreshed" them by dumping them in hot water and then serving them to us with all sorts of leftover pieces of crab meat hanging all over the crab legs.  HOW APPETIZING!  There is a lot of variety here that is for sure, but nothing really tastes amazing.  Wicked spoon is still the king of the Las Vegas strip buffets.    The prime rib was good and so was the mac and cheese.  I honestly don't remember much else.  Unless I get comped, I won't be coming back here.

This is prob the most delish buffet in the strips... the have cold snow crab leg and also steam crab leg.. and it's a lot of seafood other that the crab.. the foods were delish .. everytime we went here never disappointed .. they also have delish laksa and pho.. pizza .. Mexican food.. pork chop.. everything just so good .. service is hit and miss.. but whatever.. is buffet anyway..

Oh man. It use to be my favorite buffet when it first opened up. All I have to say is quality went down so low, all of there food taste like its at bottom of a deep sea trench. Biggest disappointment ever.

All the selection you want. The king crab (boiled hot ones) is not in the seafood section but in the italian section in the back. Great carving station selection but lines usually very long. Next time would like to try their Asian section and their oysters.

A lot of options but pricey for what you get. Oysters were really fishy and the crab legs were relatively tasteless. Soft drinks had no fizz, our waitress tried from various machines. The freshly made crepes were good but the chocolate dipped strawberries tasted like they were dipped in chocolate flavored wax instead of real chocolate. The sushi was ok but the rest of the meats were relatively bland. Just a step up from eating on a budget friendly cruise ship. If variety and quantity are what you crave you will like this buffet but if you want a tasty meal look elsewhere.

A really great buffet for 55 bucks +7 dollars if you want to cheap champagne that will give you a hangover I must say the only other buffet worth considering as far as I'm concerned in Vegas is Rio which is gone downhill Bellaggio which is still holding up their own and this buffet which I would really give foreign a half stars to

Hands down nothing better than a buffet right. We decided to stop in here for breakfast.

I was in awe when I walked in so many different food's to try. There was different types of sushi, fresh fruit, cheeses, meats, sauces, and eggs. It was like visiting every country without every leaving home. 

I of course tried sushi some I have never tried it was amazing. I chose some exotic cheese (as we call it stinky cheese) which was very delicious it was a nice change. 

There was so many foods and goodies I can't even remember everything I tired all I know is each bite was pure heavenly bliss.

I enjoyed my breakfast to the moon and back I left with a happy belly.... laugh I was so full I had take a nap... it was that good. 

If your up to an adventure I suggest trying this Bacchanal Buffet out.

Don't waste your time or money! We waited almost 2 hours for dinner on a Wednesday night. It wasn't even during the dinner rush. The food was hardly edible and certainly not worth $60 a person. The signs and pictures showed such delicious looking food and none of what was shown in the pictures was offered that night. I have no idea what kids eat there because everything has weird ingredients or sauces on them. Also, there is no description of the items next to them. Just the name. Thus, you take 5 things and realize they are all gross. Unless you want to eat a million helpings of fish, don't bother. Even the desserts were below average.

I don't get the high praise for Bacchanal because I walked away from it feeling pretty ripped off. The food was good but not exceptional and the service was absolutely terrible for the price point.  You practically have to tackle a server to get a refill on your mimosa or your coffee (which was burnt) and the buffet is set up so terribly that you end up spending an obnoxious amount of time waiting in line.  Definitely would not go back nor would I ever recommend anyone else to do so.  Only reason I am giving it 2 stars is because the desserts were good and I'm permitting a small allowance for the level of service because the service in Vegas generally sucks everywhere.

AAAMMMAAAZZINGGGG. I wish I had more than one stomach! They had lobster eggs Benedict and garlic mussels! So many choices. I had so many different flavor combinations on my plate. Not to mention the amazing desserts as well!!! Definitely recommend and so worth the $$$. Come hungry!!!
It sounds like we should have gone for breakfast instead! Dinner was mediocre at best. Quantity does not trump quality.

I had the joy of trying the Bacchanal Buffet for their weekday breakfast. I was blown away at how beautiful the space is. I love white, clean, and airy spaces.

We went relatively early and it was a weekday so we had no wait before we were promptly seated next to the crepe section. Great location!

I really enjoyed the fresh juice section drinking at least 3 glasses of their freshly made carrot juice. My boyfriend loved the watermelon juice. The perfect remedy to a night of debauchery :)

I really enjoyed the congee and dim sum section. The lotus wrapped sticky rice was divine. 

The mini red velvet pancakes were delicious too. The rotating pancake grill was a sight to behold. The savory dishes were really yummy. Every menu item came in a small dish so it was easy to try everything without wasting food. The steak and eggs were cooked perfectly! 

Presentation for all the dishes was top notch. I would love to come back for dinner or weekend brunch sometime.

Don't forget to leave room for dessert.

This was my first time at this buffet (I have gone to Wickedspoon plenty of times), and after eating here, I don't think I'll be going back there. My $60 (per person) went a long way! We had a group of 13, and checked in at about 2:45pm on a Saturday afternoon. The lady told us to pay in order for them to tell us how long the wait would be, and timing was everything. Apperantly 3 pm is the time they change from lunch to dinner, so we paid for the lunch, but got to eat the dinner food! I highly suggest that if you have a group of less than 5, to check in at least 1 hour early. Luckily, with our large group, we were able to be seated within 15 minutes or so. 
The buffet itself had plenty of options - a meat station, seafood station, Asian station, pasta station, and of course a dessert station! Everything was fresh and tasty! My only complaint is that we waited a bit long for our drinks and for someone to clear our tables when we done with plates. Other than that, this will be my go to buffet in Vegas.
Food and service was excellent. One of the better buffets in Vegas. Came during later part of lunch and was there through early dinner.

To be fair, we didn't actually eat here....but that was the problem. We got there and got a ticket to come back in 2.5hrs. Frustrating, but we walked around and came back 2.5hrs later.....just to wait in line for another 45min to pay. Then we were lead to ANOTHER line to get seated. This line was huge. We waiting in that line for 10minutes without moving one step, and decided to give up and go elsewhere. Thankfully we just made up a story that we had a show to get to and they gave us a refund. I should also note that from the seating line you could see inside the buffet and there were even lines for the food. This experience would have taken up our entire day.

We went for Easter Brunch and it was $49.99 a person. That's a little pricey! But we waited for 35 min line so we paid and then waited in another line for 15 min to be seated. 
The dining area is beautiful. The tables are a little close together, so eating was a little uncomfortable with your neighbor just over your shoulder.
The food is great. Fresh and hot!! Lots of selection and great flavors. Some of the food is packaged in cute little baskets but the portions were too big for a Buffett portion.
All in all, it was a great Buffett. Almost worth the $50 a person. It goes down to $32 on regular a Sunday Brunch. It is great for that price!!

I love this place! Seafood and Meat selection are the best. 
Price is comparable to most Vegas buffets.

I rarely eat lamb and I really loved it. 
Their mint jelly was perfect here.

Dessert bar is better at Wicked Spoon but the food here is really good.

One of my favorite buffets in Vegas.

First the wait was insane. You have to go to a kiosk to get a waiting ticket. It tells you what time you have to go back to wait in a looooong line to just pay. Then you have to get in another line for them to seat you. But once I got to my table it was on. I got the all you can drink alcohol along with my dinner and it so with it for $15. The waiter was super nice and kept giving us drink after drink. He was great! My favorite was the meat station. The bone marrow and mashed potatoes were so delicious. All the meats at the carving station were scrumptious. The fried chicken, YUM! Now for the seafood, they had a great selection. The oysters shooters were yummy. They offer all the seafood you could ask for. Loved all the oysters. The only complaint was the crab legs, they were good but they were served almost frozen. I didn't care for that too much. But everything else was so yummy. I would definitely come back.

Paid $60 per person for dinner around 5-6pm no wait at all. Your picture is taken before entering and then they try to sell it to you. I heard from a local that this was THE BEST buffet down the Vegas strip. It was good but I still like Wicked Spoon the best. They have Mexican , Italian , Asian food just to name a few. The pork rib was super dry and rubbery. The dessert had a lot to offer but I was disappointed in the macarons. The macarons weren't of any good flavor. They had sesame flavor for example which isn't flavorful to me. Their other desserts were good looking but at that point I was too full to sample some. The gelato ice cream was good and creamy and there was a variety to choose from.

The buffet here is like no other.  I usually don't care for buffets what so ever but the quality of food is off the chart.  The only downside is that it is a bit expensive and the line to get in is ridiculous.  We had to wait 2.5 hours just to get in.  Not fun when your hungry.  They have added a new check in system but it still sucks because I saw people skip the check in and get in line.  I've been here 5-8 different times and its the same every time.  Staff is slow and your going to have to wait a long time.  That being said.. I always go back because it is really good..

I was SO shocked at how diverse this buffet was.
It was on the pricey side (I forgot how much it was because I went in a group), but if you find yourself with some winnings from the tables or just want to splurge a bit go here!

They have things like shrimp n grits (I'm a fan of grits), lobster bisque, TONS of dessert, mac & cheese, fried chicken and waffles, soup dumplings (although there was no soup in them..so I don't know how accurate this was...), ramen, snow crab legs, prawns, etc.

The food was on the salty side though....Actually, it was very salty (reason for taking out a star).

Come into this with a real strategy on how to eat because I promise you, you will get full ASAP.

decided to check out the supposedly best buffet in vegas.

there is a strategy to buffet... there is only enough room in your stomach, so don't bother with any of the lower end stuff...

i had 2 servings of prime rib, one plate of dungeness crab, oyster, and shrimp cocktails..  and lastly one plate of snow crab legs..  

i wish i had not did the oyster, dungeness crab plate, should have done 2 plates of snow crab legs...  also had a slice of truffles pizza.  

probably should not had that 2nd helping of prime rib, instead i should have sample more desert...

the damage was $55 total for thurs night with tax

Not my best buffet experience in Vegas, but I don't regret trying it. My favorite part was the fresh, hot king crab legs.  Some cheaper buffets only have snow crab.  It's just not the same!  They had mochi for dessert, but only the flavors carried at trader joes.  The shrimp were gigantic.  I haven't tried Rio, but this is the best seafood buffet I've tried. Oh, and I got a huge slab of prime rib.  That chef knows what's up.

We went for the brunch and got a deal off groupon. This had been on my bucket list for so long but it's not worth the hype.  The location and atmosphere are exceptional.  Presentation and selection are great,,,,,but the taste of the food was just meh. Best thing I had was the pistachio gelato and shrimp n grits.  Everything looked so good we couldn't wait to dig in but was surprised that nothing really tasted as good as it looked, especially some of the desserts, they were just disgusting. I've had better tasting food at those simple breakfast houses. Sad to say I would never go back to this one even if their prices were dirt cheap. Hoping the one at the Bellagio is better which was recommended by our lyft driver.

An amazing buffet. Definitely one of the best on the strip (and I've been to almost all of them).  Though pricey, the price definitely matches the quality. I seriously must have eaten half of the 300 dishes they had to offer at dinner and liked every single thing I ate. If you like buffets, you should ask for the buffet of buffets which give u access to 5 other buffets on the strip for free for the next 24 hours and its only 15 dollars more. Do not pass this up. Oh yeah, plan on waiting in line for 40min to a couple hours. Even though this place seats 600, it's just that popular.

There is a reason that this is the most expensive buffet in Vegas. It is because it is twice the size of any other buffet in Vegas. I have always been a die-hard Bellagio buffet fan. However, I have to say that now I am a convert to the bacchanal buffet. We went for brunch, and I'm not even a fan of brunch, and I was blown away by the selection that they had. We didn't even know about the whole separate room in the back until we've been to the buffet at least two times. Do not make the same mistake we did! If you like breakfast food definitely go for brunch because there's an assortment of amazing things, but I would shell out the extra money for the dinner having seen the brunch and how awesome it was.

Bacchanal buffet is a relatively new buffet in Las Vegas located in Caesars Palace. It's definitely on the pricey side, about $58 per person.  The wait can be long if it's a busy day. If you're super hungry and want to eat right away, there's an extra $20 charge.  I wasn't lying when I said pricey!

This buffet is nicely decorated and they even offer taking your picture while waiting in line

Let's first start off with how HUGE this place is. In the back is the Asian foods, then there's salads, Mexican food, American food, and sea food. The seafood line gets long as they have crab legs and oysters. They also have steamed crab legs near the salad.  

Dessert area is good too!  I had the shaved ice and tried macaroons. The first time I was here, they had bomb pistachio macaroons. Recently, I got green macaroons thinking they were pistachio, but they were green tea!  Disappointing!  I guess they switch it up. Oh, the horchata is good!!

Buffets for me are kinda a waste of money because I can't eat a lot in one sitting. Bacchanal buffet is a good place to try out but it's a bit pricey for me to eat here often. Give it a try if you can. 

Ps, if you or someone in your party are a total rewards diamond or platinum member, you can bypass the line!

Minus 1 star for the rude worker!  He was directing people to go in the right line. My husband is a diamond member. We paid and proceeded to the diamond line to get seated. This RUDE worker rushed to us said wait wait go in this line (regular line).  He didn't even ask "excuse me, are you diamond."  It was just an assumption we were idiots and can't read the signs. He didn't even apologize. I tried to look for him later to get his name, but darn I didn't.

My wife and I ate here Sunday night 11/11/2018 both of us were unhappy with our food and experience. Their ingredients are quality I had American Wagyu beef roast that was slow cooked for 12 hours, it was dry and tasteless. The tri tip, brisket, and bacon were dried out and like lightly seasoned jerky. Pasta was ok, the crab legs were old and tasted like they had sugar added to them, and the pasta dishes were old. I spoke with the morning manager who couldn't help me. Then I emailed and got a reply from the assistant manager who said he'd tell the chef we weren't happy. We feel cheated and Caesar's won't offer us a partial refund since the food was so bad we both left hungry but threw away a few plates of food. They never should have taken our money if they couldn't provide fresh food on a Sunday night.  The tacos are good but not worth the $70. Our recommendation is to save your money try a different buffet.

This is one of the best buffets there is and I have tried lots the variety of food here is so many they have Japanese food Chinese food Vietnamese food Italian food Mexican food American food rib eye turkey , ribs,salads breads crab giant legs and a yummy variety of delicious dessert.... I recommend this place highly and will continue to come here.
This was well worth the price. So many options and nothing was bad. Unique presentations and flavors. Loved the sushi, and poke which is hard to like at a buffet.

It was a Saturday, around 1 pm, the line was extremely long, about 1 hour wait, the cashier informed us it was during brunch time, the price each person came out to be $44 something like that. 

I had high expectations since the reviews I read were all pretty promising, time to test out the food myself, nothing particular caught my attention, the dim sum section was nice but nothing too special. I suppose a lot of people go there for the slow crab legs which were all cracked open and made easier to eat, I am never a fan of these things, I did enjoy their jumbo shrimp.

The dessert bar was nice, but I didn't like how each dessert comes in small individual plate, it makes it hard to carry them back to the table, and I ended up looking like a fat kid going back and forth for dessert!

Overall it was okay, service wasn't that great, I like Bellagio's buffet better than this, cheaper too.

Rounding up from a 3.5 star review! 
I went for brunch on Saturday, and arrived just before 12p.  The line was not crazy, but when we left it was, so we hit the sweet spot, apparently.  The line moved quickly, and there was even loungy mood music playing, which helped pass the time. The cost was $45/person. 

This new buffet had beautiful ambiance, natural lighting, friendly staff (the guy at the meat carving station was super friendly!).  The tables were quickly bussed, and the layout was very big! It went on and on.  Mostly everything was clean and replenished often.  They even give you mini-potholders made of plastic to help you grip hot bowls and pans. 

Small rant:  I HATE those individual serving containers! From mini-pots/pans to baskets, to bowls!! UGH! They take up a lot of room on your plate, you can't really hold them in your other hand, and they are just frustrating in general! I'm at a buffet! Stop trying to restrict my servings! Or at least give me a cafeteria tray so I can put everything there. I was tempted a few times to dump the food out of the fancy-schmancy little dishes and just onto my plate, but I resisted the urge. 

Rant over.

Of course, on a buffet, food can be hit or miss.  I loved the steamed (chilled) shrimp, the seafood pasta, the mushroom risotto, the chicken marsella, and the ribs.  I also thought the ham and cheese croissants were great, and enjoyed the brisket as well.  I also really liked the freshly made crepe- a nice ending to a meal. The coconut shrimp was just ok- I didn't see any sauce for it, and the sweet potato tater tots were great!  I had a small bite of the sliders, and they were tasty too.

I tried some of the Asian offerings- the spicy fish was super spicy (lots of chili pepper), and the dumplings were fine.  I skipped the pizza and most of the pasta selections. There were also sushi offerings and a few Mexican items too.

On the negative side, the crab legs (which can be steamed upon request), were rather puny, and the mac&cheese was nothing great. Neither was the fried chicken in the chicken and waffle basket (not very seasoned).  I was pretty disappointed with the French toast too (bland).  The bread pudding seemed to be the only thing that wasn't refreshed- it looked old and picked over.

On balance, I still think the M buffet is tops around.  Next, I'd probably give the edge to Wicked Spoon, because their food is a bit more flavorful.

All in all, I'm glad I finally checked it out, but isn't going to be a must-do on my buffet list.

I don't see what people are talking about. 

There's another buffet that serves food by the spoonful, and its wicked that one would even mention them in the same category.

I liked the steamed crab legs and the fact that they offer real butter on the side was a plus. There was nothing else that really stood out. The sushi rolls were blah. Soups were salty. Mac and cheese lacked flavor. Baked chicken was undercooked and very pink inside.The oysters (Blue Point) were pathetic. What are they doing? Shucking them and putting the leanest ones out there? It looked that way compared to the Blue Point oysters that we enjoyed at another hotel. 

Also, the service was horrible. The excuse was that they were understaffed that day. We waited 15 minutes to get sodas, and never saw anyone offer a refill during our visit. Unacceptable. This is the world famous Caesar's Palace on the Las Vegas Strip. If they want to compete with some of the 5 star/diamond caliber places within walking (staggering) distance, they need to step it up.

 I might give them a second shot, but there is less than a 50% chance that I would even bother.
Great food! Especially the dim sum. The wait was a bit long but it was worth every minute (and penny)

Definitely not worth the price. We were excited to try the best buffet in Vegas, and wished we hadn't wasted the money on it. The vibe was stuffy and snooty. The food was sub par and dried out. The desserts were flavorless.

Hands down best buffet in Las Vegas! From there crab legs oysters shooters to there tacos!!! Let's not forgot those amazing desserts omg I a obsessed with there cupcakes and there chocolate cover strawberries!!! This is place is a must!!!
This is my favorite buffet in all of Las Vegas.  It is expensive, but the quality is as good as it gets for a buffett!

Bacchanal Buffet is an absolutely superior buffet!! EVERY single dish was incredibly delicious. I am not a fan of trying normal dishes at LV buffets just because I like to try things I normally wouldn't. However I did try the Mac and cheese and
It was delicious as well. I found it hilarious that something so simple could be made to have such a delicious taste. We  went with a party of eight therefore they automatically added the 18% tip.  I was not surprised being most restaurants do that nowadays. I am happy to say that every single person in our party agreed it was the best buffet in LV. It was such a nice experience. Everything about the restaurant is awesome. Additionally I enjoyed their decoration and the way the food is presented. I cannot say enough great things about this place definitely worth the price considering there are other buffets that cost nearly the same and are not close to being as good! Can't wait to be in Las Vegas again so that I can come to this buffet again!!

Best buffet no doubt in Vegas.  Worth every penny.  The wait might be dreadful but it's worth it.  Although it doesn't have as much selection as other buffets you might see but they really focus on quality.  Great foods all around.

Everything here is so delicious, but spending the money truly hurts. However, I will say that you do get your money's worth. Buffets tend to get sloppy with their food, but almost everything I had at Bachannal was truly delicious.

I love how the crab legs come presliced so you don't have to waste any time trying to get them open. They are BIG crab legs, too. Lots of meat to dunk into the little plastic cups of butter. Soooo delicious. My friend actually ate around 5-6 full plates of crab legs... he did not feel so great afterwards LOL.

The prime rib here was also very good. Flavorful and medium rare. The lamb was the only thing I didn't like, but I usually don't like lamb, anyways. I thought it was a bit dry and tough.

I also think the oysters here are passable. They are extremely small and flavorless, but they do have a variety of toppings/sauces to decorate your oysters with!

I'm embarrassed to say that I wasted my stomach on some nachos because they were the first thing I saw and they looked too delicious. It was worth it though- they were some great nachos :D I can't remember everything else I ate here, but it was good good good.

I have a crazy sweet tooth, so dessert was one of my favorite parts. They have a crepe station, so I had a nutella crepe that was absolutely delicious, along with two scoops of ice-cream and pretty much one of every dessert LOL.

Expensive restaurant but the food is so damn good. $84 for 2 for lunch. 

Recommend going around 2:30pm so you can pay lunch prices but stay for dinner which starts at 3PM!

Gluttony at its best! That's the best way to describe this feeding frenzy. You can pretty much eat anything from seafood, Mexican, Italian, American, and so on. This place is so big I would get a bit lost walking back to my seat. If your skeptical about buffets let me tell you this isn't a shitty Golden Corral, it's amazing,GO!

I've been here so many times before for brunch and I never fully enjoyed it to it's extent but that all changed when when I went for dinner this past Monday night!
Maybe it's because I've always been drunk or super hungover so I cant ever really stomach buffet food but I was sober this time and it was soooo gooooooood!!

My boyfriends a Diamond status for Total Rewards so we got to skip the entire line & got seated right away which was definitely a PLUS because the line here is always SUPER long.. like 2+ hours wait long.

In my opinion, buffets are ALWAYS better for dinner than brunch.  I don't want no scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage when I'm at a buffet... I want the GOOD STUFF. and thats exactly what I got when I went ;)

$108 for 2 people for dinner.
$80-$90 for 2 people for brunch on a weekend? that includes unlimited mimosas.
If you're a Total Rewards member, use those points for a free meal! (;

In the mood for some Chinese? Sushi? Pho? Prime rib? Mexican? Seafood? This place has it all! 

I consumed a lot of seafood here--salmon, tuna, & red snapper nigiri, sushi rolls, fresh oysters, crab legs, clams & mussels.  The quality of seafood is always a hit or a miss at buffets in my opinion, but the quality here was well worth the money.  
Oysters were very fresh with no fishy smell/taste, the crab legs had decent amount of meat to them & the nigiri was fresh as well.  

I also finally got to try the juices that come in cute little bottles.   I tried the Guava, Mango & Horchata. Mango was really good and I also liked the Horchata but I found it a bit too sweet for my taste.

Nothing much to complain about here except I would stay away from the hot & sour soup and the prime rib as I found both of them to be extremely salty and unsatisfying.

NOW FOR THE DESSERTS!
Loved:
+Chocolate covered strawberries--the chocolate one was sweet & salty.  
+CREME BRULEE--such perfection.
+Italian Cookie Gelato is probably the best flavor they offer.
+Macarons are soft and sweet. Was not a big fan of the flavors they offer but they were still good.  I mean, what other buffet offers macarons at their dessert bar?!

BASICALLY, if you're in Vegas, got time to kill & super starving. COME HERE.
Truly the best buffet in Vegas, hands down.

This place has everything. From seafood to sliders to pizza to sushi. And what's great about this place is everything taste so gooood.They even have Filipino adidas lol. They also have unique desserts that you should definitely try.

Hands down the best buffet I've been to in Vegas. 

This place seemed to have everything! The seafood bar and the dessert station definitely stood out. 

Make sure your come with an empty stomach because you'll need to be rolled out like a barrel when you're finished. 

Start off slow with non-carb items (seafood bar was my first stop for Oysters, Oyster Shooters, Shrimp, Crab). 

Make your way over to a few pieces of sushi, BBQ rib tips and some shrimp dumplings. Take a little break and contemplate some veggies - the Bacchanal Buffet has a good selection of veggies and salads. 

Once you're done with the light stuff, prepare for fried dishes (this is where your stomach will start to feel the pain). Load up on more dumplings, egg rolls, noodles, pizza or whatever else you fancy - just be sure to only fill yourself to 100% capacity. 

At this point you may want to chill at your table and let the food settle. Enjoy some drinks and check to see if anyone has commented on your previously shared photos. You'll feel as there's no way you're going back again, but this is just your stomach battling your mind, don't let it win!

Before checking out the dessert island (it's huge), you may want to do another round on the seafood bar. Oyster shooters will settle your stomach really nicely in preparation for dessert. Have a couple of those and curse the gods for not giving you a greater stomach capacity. Also, many use this time to take a potty break! You can go out of the buffet and come back in to do this - no questions asked. 

Now, for the grand finale you will show your friends the true power of mind over matter! Grab a fresh plate and wobble over to the crepe station. Don't be fooled by mini desserts and gelato in your path! Order a crepe of your preference - they will look like heaven on your plate. To complete the color spectrum, add a few strawberries or other assorted fruit on your plate. This will also make for a nice photo op. Struggle back to your table and unleash your inner photographer! Some may choose to order a cup of coffee to enjoy with their crepe - but to each his own. 

At this point you should be bursting at the seams but we're not quit done. Suck your gut in as much as possible so that you don't look like a hippo and walk slowly over to the mini desserts and gelato area. Grab as many as you like. I recommend the creme brulee, macaroons, pistachio gelato and chocolate mousse. With a second cup of coffee, painfully ingest as much as you can, and try to remember the flavors as the feeling of joy won't last too long now. 

When all is finished you will feel like the biggest pig in the world and will avoid eye contact with anyone you came with. Not to worry, a few hours of walking will wear off any feelings of shame. You'll even start walking normally without having to suck your gut in.

I personally think for the price you pay it just isn't worth it. We went for dinner and the price for 2 was over $100. The variety of food was great, a little bit of everything and for those who like seafood and meat they had plenty. However, the quality of the food just wasn't there. I basically filled up on pizza and guacamole. My husband tried the salmon and said it was dry.  Alot of tasteless food. The dessert section wasn't great either, a lot of weird flavors and again the quality wasn't good. Next time around we will go elsewhere. 
On a side note what's up with them wanting to take a picture of you before they seat you?! Why do we think this is an attraction or something? Seemed a bit strange and just another way to get more money out of you.

Best. Buffet. Ever. 
This was the most expensive buffet I've ever been to, but it was well worth it! They have many different cuisines to choose from and all of it was absolutely phenomenal!

This is currently our favorite Vegas buffet - it is pricy but you will get high-quality food and massive variety.  We've been here once before for dinner and they do change up the menu.  Our favorite items were:

Smoked Brisket: Burnt ends with juicy meat interlaced with small amounts of fat and smokiness permeating all throughout.

Lamb Chops: Seared well and tender, with a slight fruity aftertaste.

Street Tacos: Made to order - pastor, carne asada and chicken.  Served on single layer tortilla warmed both sides.

Chinese Gai Lan: These greens were surprisingly crispy and loaded with garlic flavor - surprising for a buffet!

Mexican Juices: Cool how they have this bank of milk bottles filled with classic Mexican drinks.  Horchata tasted like what we had in Cancun and had lots of cinnamon.  Tamarindo was tangy and perfect to soothe dry throats.

Pandan Coconut Jelly: By far our favorite dessert!  Dual layer jelly with a firm skin and soft coconut jelly underneath.

The biggest downside of this place is that you really need to be selective - possible to get a tummy ache from eating too much good stuff!  Maybe the key is portion control - get a tiny piece of everything!  Or come her after a marathon!
Long wait trying to get in on Thanksgiving Day. Food is okay but not overwhelming. Foie Gras was the best of the night.

This place was so good they had everything you can think of and crab and also the different stuff along with sushi so I highly recommend you go there it's pretty expensive but it's worth it if you go there an empty stomach

At the Bacchanal Buffet we consume delicious items such as: perfectly smoky black pepper edged bacon, miniature Monte Cristo sandwiches, amazingly moist and succulent beef brisket, lox (salmon) shaped like rose buds, mini cast iron skillets carrying eggs prepared over easy with skirt steak strips resting on top, flan, gelato bar with interesting flavors (ex. Baklava, sticky toffee).

The quality is very high which does warrant the high sticker price...if you can do some damage.

Wow the choices the fun. I really enjoyed my meal at the buffet. I have been trying to get to this buffet for two years and it was worth the wait. Great food and lots of it. I went for brunch with the family it was crowded but the line went quick. It was definitely worth the wait. My favorites were the seafood and the Meats as well as the dessert. Don't miss the gelato which is great. This would have gotten five stars but the service wasn't the best. It felt at times that I was annoying our waitress when I asked for a refill of soda or when I asked her to get my plate.  That was the worst part of my experience.

This has got to be the best buffet ever! I went for dinner a little before 5 on a Friday and there was no line! They have everything from crawfish, mussels, BBQ ribs & brisket, prime rib, cold & hot crab legs, pizza, sushi and great desserts. The sushi was not great, but the variety of foods, fresh seafood and hot carving center made up for it. I've ate at Bellagio's buffet and it has nothing on Bacchanal. I don't think it's worth $50 for dinner but it comes close. Can't wait to go back for their breakfast buffet.

We decided we wanted to celebrate our 8th anniversary and the well-known and most expensive buffet in Vegas. That is just how we roll!

We came in the Monday before Thanksgiving to beat the crowd. My theory is to stay away from expensive and usually well-known places on holidays because the quality might not be as good as it would on another weekend. So, it was the perfect time for us to try this place for the first time.

Pros:
oyster (I ate 3 dozens by myself!)
prime rib (nicely seasoned...still thinking about it. Must eat it hot or warm)
lamb chops (must eat warm or else it will taste gamey and chewy)
sausage (not sure what it was made of, but it was sweet, moist and delicious)
kabasa (sp?) (always yummy fatty sausage)
warm crab legs (in the Italian area...sweet and yummy goodness)
lobster chowder (just enough amount of creaminess)
oyster shooters (I just ate the oyster in the shot to avoid taking up precious space in my tummy)
horchata and all other frescas (DELICIOUS!)
dessert ( try everything!)


Cons:
Brisket (you can either get a fat on one end and lean meat on the other hand..it needs to be marbled. Therefore, it made it taste dry.)
skirt steak (well-done..I am a med-rare kinda gal)
Peach green tea (it was bland and not as sweet as I would like it)


I took a tour of the place: I

In the Asian area  few pieces of bbq pork and some eggplants. BBQ pork was pretty good but the eggplants were greasy. They were serving up pho, ramen, noodle soup, too. I didn't try any of it.

In the Mexican area, I had an order of carne asada..that was pretty good meat if you're in to a little fat and tendon going on.

Italian food looks like a bunch of pasta or bread...don't waste your stomach on that when you are at the buffet.

Salad area was small for a reason...and a good reason, too. =)

So was it worth $50? I told my friends that it is worth if you plan to hang out for 3 hours or more. If you have to be some where at a certain time, your standing in line to pay to get in or food will eat up all of your time. We were there for 4 hours and my husband had to drag me out ( plus it was already 10pm) so take your time and enjoy the food and the company.

We would definitely come back again!
Food was good, excellent crabs. Service was slow and waiter took too long to serve our drinks.

We went to Vegas with the Bacchanal buffet as our top priority and I wasn't disappointed! It was Thanksgiving weekend so we knew lines were going to be insane but I think we lucked out when we hoped in line at 10:45am and waited for only 30 minutes so definitely go early. Love love love the decor and food presentation. My plan of attack was to take my time and not load up so early but everything looked so delicious that I started double fisting plates of sliders and tiny baskets of fried chicken on the first trip! I'm a sucker for food served in cute miniature fryer baskets, which is why I also recommend Wicked Spoon as a quicker alternative (I don't think their line is as epic as Bacchanal, Bellagio, or Wynn).

Unfortunately overrated. We went on a Saturday evening in mid-December. We were in line for over an hour (got in line at 8 pm). Even with the Total Rewards member discount, dinner buffet came out to cost ~$50 per person =(

Lots of reviewers have compared it to the Wicked Spoon buffet, but I personally think Wicked Spoon has improved significantly since it first opened (and now I consider to be among the ranks of Wynn Buffet) and is better than Bacchanal Buffet.

Whenever I go to a buffet, I pretty much make myself try as many different foods in order to get the best overall feel of the quality. 

Although this buffet really offers a huge selection in terms of variety, the quality and taste was not impressive at all. Pretty decor and furniture, but food does not match up =(

Probably will not return unless a friend insisted on coming again.

(See photos for reference)

Corn on the cob: good, but nothing fancy

mashed potatoes: average

BBQ ribs: WAY oversmoked, can't even discern any meat taste due to all the smokiness; meat was also dry and tough

seaweed salad: decent, but I can get better seaweed salad at my local Costco

Italian meatball: Very good -- juicy, flavorful, and very well seasoned. AND huge!

xiao long bao: NO SOUP INSIDE AT ALL. tiny lump of flavorless meat wrapped in dried out hard peel. failed on all levels.

roasted duck: good for a buffet, but cannot compare to a Chinese restaurant of course.

Alaskan king crab legs: I got the legs cooked hot (although I feel they are just boiling legs that have been already cooked before but are now cold) -- there is a separate line formed for the hot legs, which moved slow and ultimately was not worth the 10 minute wait. The crab meat was tough, rubbery, dried out, and didn't taste very fresh.

(BEST crab legs are still at M buffet)

cooked shrimp (in-shell): DELICIOUS! perfectly seasoned, very tender and fresh! Watch out, these run out fast, so make sure you get some before you end up waiting for the next batch to be ready.

Spanish rice: decent

fruit: watermelon was terrible, pineapple was fresh and ripe, (chocolate-covered) strawberries were sweet and fresh

desserts: you bet I tried most of them that evening (8+ kinds) most are pretty good and on par with the desserts at Wicked Spoon, but nothing amazing or comparable to those at M buffet or Wynn buffet.

After studying many of the buffets Las Vegas has to offer, my family and I settled for Bacchanal! It's pricier than some of the other ones, but I thought it'd be worth it - perhaps my expectations were too high...  

We dropped in during the post-Christmas/before New Year's period, so there was a $10 increase on their normal meal price. :(
There was a good variety of different ethnic foods, but nothing wowed me - it was more of "oh, this is okay, I might get it again" and other times "what am I eating...?!?" - in a bad way...  

Some of the food I tried was:
+ AMERICAN (of course): cute mini red velvet pancakes - flat and grossly sweet, french toast -actually gross to where I wouldn't swallow another bite
+ MEXICAN/SPANISH: seafood paella - very eh, mini churros - tasted microwaved, customizable (though limited) taco station!
+ ITALIAN: few types of pizza (of course), pumpkin gnocchi - decent
+ CHINESE: typical dim sum offerings like pork dumplings, taro buns, shrimp/prawn dumplings, fried rice, stir-fried broccoli; none of them more than decent
+ JAPANESE: sashimi, soba, basic sushis 
+ DESSERT: if anything, I got full on the dessert...! the gelato was satisfactory, and I tried one of their customizable crepes with nutella. the MINI PECAN TARTS were honestly my favorite food in the entire buffet...  

One major pro - service was quite good! The bussers we met were quite friendly, and one of them actually stopped to chat with us for a bit. :) 

Would I come back? Definitely not. I was ridiculously disappointed by this buffet experience and wish I'd spent my money someplace else.

We went for breakfast at 9:30 on a Wednesday morning.  There was no line so we were seated quickly.  The price was just shy of $30.  There were lots of yummy options, eggs benedict, chicken fried steak. croque madame, breakfast pizza, red velvet pancakes, chicken and waffles the list goes on and on.  We were seated close to the buffet so we were able to grab a couple small plated items and put them on our table and go back for more.  That was nice cause they are so cute but take up a lot of room on your plate.  Most of the stuff we tried we split in hopes of not filling up after one round.  The food was good but not amazing..not even special really.  It was good for a buffet I guess?  I was really looking forward to the fresh juice I had seen pics of.  They only had tropical and by the time we left were completely out.  I am surprised they don't restock, especially at breakfast.  Service was lacking.  Plates were not cleared and drinks not refilled, which wouldn't have been such an issue if they would restock the damn juice.  It was not busy at all.  So we should have been able to get better service.  The dessert section was nothing special.  I hope they put out better desserts with lunch and dinner.  There was crepes, pastries, cookies and candy in jars and gelato.  That was it.  We got some gelato on a small cone on the way out.  I would try again if a friend wanted to go for lunch or dinner.  I'm over breakfast though.

Bacchanal, I wanted to love you - I really did. You were actually one of the places I was most looking forward to when visiting Vegas for the first time in my adult life after all the publicity you've been getting. However, I was a bit disappointed unfortunately.

Don't get my wrong, the food was good. I actually quite liked their macarons. However what was offered overall, just didn't seem very exceptional. When I think about the cost of admittance, I felt like I could have gotten better elsewhere. 

I just couldn't justify spending over $50, on overly salty food. 

But with that said, the next time I'm in the area, I'm willing to give you another try. Perhaps brunch? Bottomless mimosas!

This place BEATS all the buffets I've tried here in this sinful-gluttonous city of Las Vegas. Just freaking get your ass here and try their food. It's WORTH THE LONG HOUR + WAIT. Quality here is phenomenally amazing. Portions are just right for your meal. The food here is flavorful enough to tickle your taste buds. Great place to rage for hangover food after a night of drinking, double-fisting, and dancing. I'm definitely coming back here again and again every time I visit Vegas. 

Service is even excellent here. As for the decor, amazing! Their dessert buffet is to die for. From their succulent quality of their gelato to their scrumptious, thick and fatty caramelized flan. UGH. DROOL.
Love this place.. what a night out with all you can eat! Definitely be back to his place. Starting tonight!

What I Learned From My Bacchanal Buffet Experience

                                                              by Lori R


    1)  If you want the SUPER Bacchanal experience you must go after 3pm!  A lot of what I've heard described in reviews was NOT on the buffet that we went to on a Tuesday at lunchtime.

    That being said, we also paid half of what others pay at night.  We arrived around 10:45 a.m., so it was around $50 for both of us (before tip).

   2)  TIP!  Add gratuity to that bill when you pay it at the register.  They will MARK your receipt as a tipper.  Don't know if that gives you extra credit or what, but they sure make note of it.  And if that's not reason enough, these servers work hard keeping your drinks refilled and whisking away endless empty plates.  They also take salt and pepper shakers very seriously, as I heard a serious conversation that involved keeping track of whose were whose. (you have to ask for it, if you want them, by the way, they aren't on the table).

  3) PACE YOURSELF.  They were changing over from breakfast to lunch when we arrived, so they kept putting out new things.  Favorites for me were some Asian items...the eggplant, green beans, fried fish.  Also thought the sliders were excellent quality, onion rings very good.  There was an awesome truffled potato gratin, a tasty tater tot casserole...a very flavorful chicken habanero sausage (although there was nothing habanero hot about it).  From the Italian section, not a lot was calling out to me, but I did have a meatball which was good, although very big...a smaller one would have been even better.    Seafood was disappointing to me, as expectations were high based on the reviews I had read, but those were obviously for dinner.  I asked if it was too early for crab legs, and was told yes, not until after 3.  Steamed shrimp were good though.

   4) Dessert selection must be different this early in the day, also.  VERY GOOD though, but sadly, no macaroons!  I tried a passion fruit meringue tart and a chocolate creme brulee.  Both were pretty good.

   So, to sum up my personal Bacchanal experience, it was quite good, but being lunch-time buffet eaters,  we have preferred our lunch-time experiences at both  Wynn and Wicked Spoon.

I went to this buffet specifically to eat seafood.  Brunch is $55 I called before I went as asked two questions.  How long is the wait and if the seafood was hot.  I was told the wait was 20min and that seafood was cold but they could heat it up at the Italian area.  Got in line and the wait was over an hour.  That was fine I was already there and was just hoping the food would be good.  When we finally got in and got crabs we asked where we could have them heated up and were told they don't do it until 3pm.  This is not what they said over the phone and I was not going to pay $55 for burgers, pizza and tacos.

Price is a budget if you have a family but it's Worth it!!!
Weekday brunch 8am-3pm $40/person
Weekday dinner 3pm-10pm $55/person
Week-end brunch 7:30am-3pm $50/person
Week-end dinner 3pm-10pm $60/person
The only " discount " they offer is if you are a total reward platinum or a " high rank " gambler
The quality is served! You eat what you paid for :)
If you visit vegas for the first time do it! 
My favorite buffets are Bacchanal, Bellagio and M resort ones.

Long wait so avoid the rush hours of 12pm  for lunch and 6pm/7pm for dinner

If you like Sea Food, this buffet is THE PLACE to enjoy it (Not Rio anymore!)
Stone crab, king crab (they boiled it and serve it warm!), Sea snail, oyster, blue crab, shrimp, crawfish... 
Main around the world gastronomy is honored
Italy, France, Morocco, Asian, Arabia, Mexican, American and I am sorry if I missed someone.
My favorite was the " clam chowder " Amazingly tasteful in Le Creuset pot and THE rotisserie.
The meat is juicy and so tender! Beef, Turkey, sausage, lamb, chicken seriously everyone will be pleased!!!
Tacos lover, they prepare your taco the way you like!!
I tried the Pho Soup and the Ramen soup at the Asian station ... I think they should hire a Vietnamese Chef for that " station "
The broth was off and way too salty. 
Dessert? Gosh me who don't have a sweet tooth
I tried almost everything LOL
What I love to see is the great selection of fresh fruits!!!

Soft drinks are included in the price. You have to pay extra for wine/beer.

They were so busy Thursday night when we had dinner, our host took 30mns to served us our drinks then we had to ask 3 time before we got 1 refill
I was annoyed so I asked another host...

Maybe management should give less table to each host to avoid this... 
beside that we had a great great time

This is my third time here and I have to say: THIS IS THE BEST BUFFET ON THE STRIP!

I usually don't gorge myself in food, but Bacchanal serves the best types of food with the best quality. When it comes to buffets, I don't really expect much. I know the chefs are making food for the masses, so the quality would be okay at best. Bacchanal has impressed me time and time again. Every time I come to this buffet, it just gets better and better. I wanted to make sure that it wasn't the first two time I went, but it seems very consistent. 

TIP: I recommend that everyone goes in line and pays for their meal before 2:30 PM. You essentially pay for lunch pricing and get dinner food. (Win/Win if you ask me).

Food:
The food was really good for a buffet. The quality wasn't five-stars or three $'s but it was definitely up there. You pay for what you get and it is definitely worth it. I recommend the steamed snow/king crab! very delicious and you can have unlimited amounts! The prime rib and tri-tip were very juicy and loved how they cooked it (medium rare). It seems like the bone-marrow is their new addition and it is a must try! VERY FATTY AND VERY SAVORY! The desserts were pretty good too!

Service:
Our waiter was really nice and always made sure we had our drinks filled or accounted for. He even offered us tea at the end of our meal (which made my stomach feel 10x better). The only thing I didn't like him telling us we had to leave because of our 2 hour mark. I was okay with leaving but I felt like he didn't have to be that pushy.

5/5

Pros:
-Good quality food
-Variety of ethnic foods
-Cheap pricing for what you get
-Great service
-UNLIMITED SNOW CRAB! 

Cons:
-2 hour limit
-Long wait times

I had a lot to say about this place initially and most of it was not what you'd expect which ultimately led me to giving a very dis-appointing 2 Stars. I was shocked to hear back from a Lovely Guest Relations Manager by the name of Samantha B. who unexpectedly invited us back on a Partial comp to give them another chance and I accepted. She met us there promptly and welcomed us which went a step further in her desire to make a customer happy. She single handedly changed my mind about my first experience. The food was secondary to me after that but after having king crab legs and the Fathers Day assortment I can say that this truly is a must try if you're in Vegas. Finally I'd like to pay an extremely high compliment to our table server who was the best I've ever had. Courteous to no end and we never had to ask for a thing. I will visit again and see if I can sit in his section. I believe his name had "LUIS" in it somewhere. Thank you Samantha again for an awesome experience.

This buffet rocks!!! So many great options that all taste great. The surprise to me was how awesome their Pho was!! The broth for the Pho was phenomenal! It's still overwhelming thinking about all the great dishes I ate, but all I know is, it was ALL good. ALL GOOD! Still daydreaming about the food.

Vegas is known for its buffets, and if you are hungry, its hard to do better than Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace. The fact of the matter is, buffets either suck or are really good. This buffet is the later.

Let me frame this: after a long day of traveling and then working, we were hungry. We did some quick local research and Bacchanal came up over and over again as the spot to check out.

If you've ever been to a buffet before, you know what to expect from style and ambience. The dining room is spacious and the food is continually well stocked. There is a nice variety too. Aside from the usual meat, fish and dessert stations, there is massive Asian section, a tasty Italian area (with plenty of salted meats) and a small but interesting Mexcian area. I dealt enjoyed the dumplings, gnocchi, Mac and cheese and lamb chops. 

To close: hungry? Ok, really hungry? Good, want to try a lot of little dishes of a wide variety? Excellent! Go visit Bacchanal. And then go gamble and Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's!

The only food is average is the prime rib station.  Other stations are so bad especially Asian station.  Dim sums are  not flavorful and not authentic for the price.  Bowl of pho has  a lot of noodles with two thick slices of beef that are so chewy.  Expensive price for such mediocre foods.
Still probably the best buffet on the Strip. Be prepared for the wait. And as others have mentioned, don't miss out on the lamb chops!

Came here first thing when I landed to Vegas and im glad I had the experience. We got there around 6pm and has to wait in line for around 30 minutes. The weird part was we had to tip before we got seated.. 

atmosphere: not your typical buffet, it has a bit of class and its not too loud. 

Food: hmm, I don't know where to go with this one because I never expect too much from buffets. The crab legs were way way way too salty which I feel like they did on purpose is people don't eat too much of it. The oysters were delicious tho! so fresh! What they have as NY wagyu beef is definitely not wagyu... but their DESSERT section is AMAZING! must try the mochi ice cream! 

overall, I would visit again if I am ever in town but this time ill know what I should eat or what I shouldn't

It's over-hyped in my opinion. It's 70 bucks with tax and then more with tip. There's a pretty long line to get into the buffet and once you're in, there are even more lines to get your food. There's a lot of options of different styles of food and a large dessert table. I definitely did not feel like I was able to eat my money's worth of food and probably couldn't because I simply didn't like it enough to.

I don't eat a lot of good buffets so I gotta give this a 4/5. Pretty good quality Asian food (all I really tried was the duck and the red pork because that's all I wanted for the moment). There was only one set of sushi and a lot of sushi rolls, they were all pretty good in my opinion. I don't know what people were complaining about the sushi for. 

There's really good Asian food, some Mexican food, Italian food, and really good, boiled crab legs. The American meat (turkey, brisket, and others) were too smoky and dry, definitely could've used some work there. But otherwise, good stuff all around. 

The decor, environment, and seating is excellent and puts you in a good mood for the food. 

LOL, the people whining about how long the line is. What the hell do you expect, just wake up early before the opening and you get in easy. Otherwise, pay for the express  and just go in. If you're not willing to pay for the express line, I don't see how you afforded to come to Vegas in the first place.

The is the best buffet I've ever had. Best. The food quality here is top notch for a buffet. Sure, you can get Kobe beef somewhere that beats any steak at this buffet or better crab legs at a seafood restaurant, but the variety here just trumps everything. The highlights for me were the shrimp and grits, the thick sliced bacon, the American wagyu, and the nigiri. Oh, did I mention the dessert? They literally have cheesecake with the same quality as the ones I had in New York. Not to mention the sorbet, the chocolate mousse, the crepe, etc. This place is gluttony at its best. As a tip, try to catch the brunch right before they switch to dinner at 3pm so you can pay less and still get the dinner items.

The hordes of people at the entrance kind of scared me (crowds!), but I understand that they had just opened so it was to be expected. I went here as part of the Elite Grand Opening event (thank you Yelp & Caesars!).

Near the entrance is the seafood area. There were a number of hot prepared seafood-y items, like clams and mussels in a bucket, shrimp & grits, halibut / salmon, paella.. My friend asked one of the guys back there if any of them were gluten-free. I'm not sure if it was because he was busy / first week jitters, but he seemed inconvenienced. Anyways, he said the fish and mussels were safe. After the hot items, you got the cold seafood items. Piles of shrimp and crab legs. On my first pass, the shrimp looked a bit dried out and grey. After taking a look at it a second time, I saw that they had changed it out and the shrimp was much pinker and plump. The crab legs was what I was in line for. They can heat them up for you, and it does seem to taste better that way.

After seafood, I went to the salad and charcuterie area. I liked their variety of meats, but was a bit miffed to see Tillamook cheddar on there. I like Tillamook cheese, but it's something I can get at the grocery store. I will give them points for labeling the cheeses. The honey "station" was probably the best part though. They had fresh honeycomb, which people could take a chunk out, while the honey dripped down into pots with star anise, cinnamon in them so that it would infuse the honey.

Next up I went to their comfort food and meats area. Mac n cheese, scalloped taters.. Yum yum! I saw that they had prime rib there, but wanted to save room for dessert I opted for the lamb chops. They only give you one chop, so I asked for a couple more hehe. :) It was nicely medium-rare, and went very well with the scalloped taters.

There were a lot of things that I wanted to try, but I don't like to waste and I was getting kind of full by this point. So I went off to the dessert area. I didn't see any standalone fruit. I don't think I saw any in the salad area as well. You know, the freshly cut melons and oranges that seem standard in a buffet. Maybe I wasn't looking hard enough? *shrug* Anyways, they have a great selection of small treats. There was this passionfruit (I think) creme cake that was utterly divine. Light, smooth and not overly sweet. My friend got one of the custards, he said the attendant told him it was gluten free but when I tasted it, it seemed like there was a cake layer on the bottom. Either that, or it was gritty.

Our server at the table was very nice and helpful. She came by a couple times to check on our drinks. Other servers cleared our plates efficiently. They offered coffee as things were winding down, which was unexpected. I'm not sure if this is part of regular service or if it was because we were there for the event.

Overall, I would say this will give other buffets in town a run for the money. The assistant exec chef said that they are still in the learning process, so things may change.

As I walked out, I looked at some of the tables to see what they were eating. Maannn, they had PHO and RAMEN??
