Wow. This buffet is huge! We came for brunch around 0900 on a Saturday and it was pretty dead surprisingly. Around 1000 it became quite busy so I would recommend going before 10 if you want less people.

There was a huge selection of food... lobster eggs Benedict, croquet madam, scrambled eggs with Boursin cheese, and the hush puppies were my favourite. 

They had prime rib, king crab, pho, crepe station, made to order French toast, fresh juices etc. 

I was very impressed and full at the end of my meal(s). 

Definitely save this for a day you won't be in a bathing suit!

Come here and you'll feast like a king. After learning they put in $17 mil to renovate, I just had to see and taste EVERYTHING for myself. No doubt this is the best buffet in Vegas. They thought of all the little things to really cater to your taste buds. I was really impressed with what they had to offer. For starters, having Alaskan King Crab legs as opposed to snow crab or dungeness already makes a world of difference. Fresh squeezed juices, homemade sauces..the list is never ending. Even the nigiri (something I typically pass up at buffets) had sashimi pieces that just melts in your mouth. They use the best quality ingredients and each dish is crafted beautifully. Only thing missing is bone marrow (like Wicked Spoon) and oysters on half shell and this could very well be the perfect buffet.

If you arrive at this most overrated buffet at 6:30pm plan on filling your first plate of dinner at 8:30pm. Once finally in we were excited to eat the much hyped food. The prime rib was dry, the paella tasted like rice out of a bag from the supermarket and the oysters were questionable. For the $51.00 cover price the food definitely wasn't up to par, equally disappointing every single serving spoon I touched was filled with food and stickiness. If you're going to spend this kind of money for dinner there's hundreds of restaurants in Las Vegas and which you will have a much more enjoyable evening.
Not impressed at all. Super long lines and seafood was below average especially if you're used to California seafood. I'd say the Rio seafood buffet is better.

Everything was great except for their dessert. The lava cake was very over cooked and no chocolate lava flow because it was over cooked. And the cream brûlée was under cooked. AWESOME seafood and Asian food. The Mexican menudo was so good. Dinner is different from lunch.  They have 2 different kinds of crab (Alaskan king and rock), oyster half, shrimp, prime rib and lamb, sushi (at both), they have more different pressed juices at dinner. We did the buffet of buffet (you can go to 6 different buffet as many times as you want within 24 hours). For the seafood buffet at Rio and Caesars you pay an extra free. Rio did have lobster. Your welcome :)

One of the better buffets in Vegas, but overpriced and a bit overrated. We came in between lunch and dinner at around 3:30PM, so it might've been the timing. The meats were overcooked and dry, and some of the dishes didn't seem all that fresh. The selection was great, and seafood was nice. I've had friends telling me they've gotten sick after eating here.

Currently the best buffet in LV. I love how they give you the option of hot or cold crab legs (if hot-they are prepared for you right then and there). There is a wide selection of food ranging from ramen (the broth was actually quite good) to wagyu sliders (overcooked). I do appreciate that everything is portioned out for you so that food doesn't go to waste. 

Try coming at off hours to avoid waiting for hours. The first time I came to Bacchanal the wait time was 3-4 hours. Hell no. I came back the next day and only waited around 40 minutes.

I loved every minute of my 2 and half hour eating frenzy.  This place is beautiful with an awesome selection of various food stations that include Asian, American, Mexican, Seafood, breads, pizza, deli meats, desserts, and more.  Bottomless mimosas are served with brunch on Sunday's.

If there is any buffet in Las Vegas you need to try this is it!  Every time I went to get more food my last dirty plate had already been removed from the table by the time I got back.  Bacchanal has buffet food and service down to a Science and I would recommend them to even the most pickiest and finicky eater.  You must experience this buffet.  The music they played made me happy and I ate to the tunes.  I could have very well experienced my first foodgasm.

Really great selection service and price..
Some things did not get replenished often but some very tasty things.
Also mountains of crab and shrimp..
Next time crepe station..
For $60, you'd expect to at least have your glass refilled. Disappointing service. Food is ok. This is my second time, but I'm less than impressed. Probably last time too.

Wow, this was an amazing experience. As a diamond player, our host treated us to an unforgettable dinner at the bacchanal buffet. Some of us are Vegan and chef Eddie and chef Ricky were extremely cordial and brought us an amazing platter of various foods including veggie fried rice, amazing veggie sushi and other delights. For the rest of us, Chef eddie brought us an amazing platter of king crab legs. The rest of the buffet was delicous and we had a great experience. Hats off to the friendly chefs and the courteous wait staff. I can't wait to go back!

Bacchanal you have let me down! 

The one star is for downgrading food and the bad service from this head of the host guy.    

We have been here since March 2013 and the food has downgraded a major major level!!! There used to be Asian chicken soup, awesome soup station and tomahawk  ribeye to name a few of my favorites.  They stop serving any of the above and what's even better it's $60 pp for dinner!!

Now, the service; The look-like-manager, head of host STEVEN KUO is an a$$hole.  We were here with a party of 8 and wanted to put together 2 tables right next to each other where MR.KUO claims it's too small even though we say we don't mind.  He insist saying that you'd have to wait another 30 minutes if we would like a table together. If we had to split into 2 tables why do we have to pay 18% gratuity? WHY if we are sitting at two separate tables and have to pay 18% tip? MR manager STEVEN KUO please Fix your attitude and retake customer service 101!!!!!!!!!!!!

My mouth waters when I think about this place! Such a solid seafood selection and I LOVE oysters! So I spent all my time eating oysters and crab legs.

Came during a holiday, waited for an hour an a half or more, paid the holiday prices which are steep... But it is a Vegas buffet and definitely one of the more popular. (I would rather spend money on a buffet which is a for sure win than on gambling which... Well a gamble). Located in Caesars palace & almost indistinguishable except for the long lines. Ask for directions! 

The decor is really nice with glass walls and floating lights and this place is a lot bigger than it looks from the line. I would definitely suggest walking through all the buffets sections (there are corners and turns!) before committing. Remember where your table is too! I got confused, but luckily sat right next to the dessert bar which is in the center of the room. 

I love love love the small plates here, especially since I like taking a bite of something and then sharing with friends so I don't waste it. Seafood and meat section are superb! Everything else ranges from "ok I'm not getting that again but still good" to "I'm glad I got to try this! Om nom." 

Save room for dessert... Or dabble in the other sections and go all out for desserts! French macarons to gelato to melt in your mouth chocolate chip cookies. 

Want to gamble, but don't want to lose too much? Come spend your money at this buffet! Worth the wait and $$$.
I went here for my birthday and I damn near had to leave in a wheelchair after eating so much food. And they also provide a free glass champagne. Excellent service as well.

Not a fan of the service or the management. However the food is the best of the different buffets on the Strip. Just be mindful if you order all-you-can-drink, they will be slow to keep your glass topped up. Also, the music is HORRIBLE and too loud. However the ambiance is lovely and the food is terrific.

Finally I got to try Las Vegas #1 buffet and yes the food here beats all the other buffets combine. Bacchanal buffet is pretty pricey but if you have your total rewards card it will be only $53 for dinner. Still pricey but as a foodie I'm here to enjoy!!! After paying I was amaze from the food option available here.  Soda and coffee comes with the buffet so make sure you drink up $53 worth of soda and coffee!!  Service was amazing and they would constantly come and pick up our dirty plates.

The food-
Personally I thinking the best thing I had here was the seafood.The oysters here are shuck in front of your eyes and put on the buffet line constantly. The crab legs were so sweet and I really like how it's slice in half so it makes eating the legs a little bit easier. Another thing that I couldn't keep my hands off were the individual agua fresca bottles they had! I love the variation of foods from different parts of the world. When you come to this buffet you don't need to travel around the world to try great food! I'm such a huge dessert fan and this place didn't disappoint me at all. I'm a sweets kind of gal!! When I walked in I saw the huge selection of sweets that I make sure to keep enough room to try all of them! The Thai tea float and cakes were my favorite and I truly recommend you guys to try it out! Overall, this place is a must when you visit Vegas.

Hands down my favorite buffet on the strip!  It may be more expensive than others but the food is definitely worth the splurge!  The is a wide variety of food to choose from: seafood with both hot and cold crab legs, grill station, Mexican including street style tacos made to order, Italian and pizza, extensive Asian including dim sum and soup/noodle bar, Desert bar featuring not only crepes but gelato, Mochi, shave ice, and other unique offerings.  The selection changes slightly from visit to visit but you are sure to find something to fit whatever you are craving.  Come ready to try new things!
The servers are prompt at refills and clearing tables and food on the line is refreshed just as promptly.  
If you can only experience one buffet in Vegas I say this is the one!

If you like buffets this one is for you, IF you can afford it.

As far as me, I hate buffets, I don't even go near them anymore, the Bacchanal has a lot of food but nothing really stands out, The food is better than other buffets but it is still not good, it is a buffet, I enjoyed the Bottomless hot crab legs and that's it the rest was "meh to OK" I rather spend my $60 dollars in a memorable spot other than spending my time making a line to get something is not that good, so again don't get me wrong if YOU love buffets this is the one to go, if YOU love to feel stuffed and seconds away to feel like you are not going to be able to breath anymore, this is the place to go, if you love to get into a diabetic coma, this is the place to go, they have a looooooot of sweets, if you love good food, go somewhere esle.

But what do I know.

Two stars but I gave it 3 because I love crab legs.

OMG!  Went here for lunch on a Tuesday.  There was no wait at all when we went.  Of all the buffets we visited for lunch during our stay in LV (the buffets at Wynn, M Hotel, Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan, and Treasure Island) this one was the best!  There was seafood for lunch and a made-to-order crepes!  There was only one problem that I did have, and that was when they ran out of oysters.  However, since everything else was so great and the desserts were the best, I still think the buffet deserves 5 stars.  The service was so friendly, too.
Amazing desserts and great selection of seafood during lunch.  I would love to come back to try this place out for dinner.  Totally worth it!

My first run-in with Bacchanal was a 2.5 hour wait for an expensive Sunday brunch, which we ended up giving up on. Flash forward to a Tuesday evening. There was still a 45-minute wait and the price was $55 for dinner on a weeknight. Fortunately, we were given a ticket to bypass the wait time, but I was still surprised by the price compared to Wicked Spoon. But, I convinced myself that I had to try Bacchanal at least once before forming judgment. 

The "#1 rated buffet in Vegas" failed to live up to its hype on several fronts. Let's start with the good. You're basically paying the price tag for the amazing seafood and carving station options. The crab legs/claws were some of the best I've had at a buffet and I really went to town on the jumbo shrimp. They also had oysters on the half shell, which were mediocre. Several amuse-bouches included a good seafood ceviche, oyster shooter, and a salmon spread. Another winner was the scallops Rockefeller. I found the brioche crust to be perfect. For meats, the prime rib was bloody excellent, and I loved the rack of lamb. Head to the Mexican station to grab freshly-squeezed guava, pineapple, strawberry, or horchata juice served in a bottle on ice. 

Where does this buffet fail? Pretty much everything else. There were some pretty bad dishes including an extremely dry cod and awfully salty BBQ ribs. But, I really didn't like the offering of sushi, pizza, and desserts. If you're paying top dollar, should you really be serving pizza sitting under a heat lamp? How about something different like flatbread? The sushi was pretty much like any other buffet sushi - dried out rice with old-tasting fish. I liked the ice cream offerings, but all the other desserts and pastries tasted stale and dry. 

Forget the stupid ticketing system and heavy wait times. Forget the expensive price. Forget all the disappointing food. I'll take Wicked Spoon or a nice steak dinner any day.

Wanted to splurge and try the #1 rated buffet. I knew what to expect price-wise. Check in is automated, which is nice. I checked in at the kiosk around 805p and was texted to return about 835p, 15 minutes prior to my estimated seating time (~850p), so actual wait time in line was minimal and there's plenty to do/see at Caesars while you wait for your text. There's an option to upgrade to Express seating for an extra $55, if that's how you're living life.  Decor was nice.  The interior is a little dark so there's nice ambiance. Might be a little too dark for some, trying to maneuver between tables and such. THE FOOD: wonderfully done. Plenty of food choices.  My favorite: the candied bacon,  lol. Nothing I ate was bad, but there's another buffet on The Strip that was TOP NOTCH for flavor. I won't mention the name here, but it rhymes with a late-90s MTV show starring a cartoon teenage girl with blunt bangs, glasses, and sarcastic humor. I'll wait.....

 ..... you figure it out?! Mkay, let's carry on. 

Bacchanal was good, not mind-blowing. I can check this one off the list.  May return to try out the brunch buffet one day.  As for a higher end dinner buffet, I'll stick with Aria....oops, I mean "rhymes with Daria." Just unread that last little bit.
So much great food. I wish I had a bigger stomach but the food quality is excellent. The seafood were fresh as can be. This is one of the spot to hit while in Vegas.

Based on my friends' recommendations, Bacchanal was a required item on our itinerary for my most recent Vegas trip. I heard about the 1.5 hour amusement park-like lines, so we decided to come for a late lunch/early dinner.

BEST BUFFET in Vegas! Why the 4 stars instead of 5 you ask? The lunch selection was a bit cheaper, but the quality wasn't nearly as good as the dinner quality. Also the way the buffet is arranged is that the prime rib and the seafood sections are very close together, so the line is VERY LONG and and SLOW.

Tips:
1) $15 for express line
2) Dinner selection, which tastes wayyy better starts at 3:00pm.
3) Come early for quicker entry. If you're coming during peak times, you better not have anything else planned for the night because you'll spend the whole evening there standing in line and eating.

Cuisines: There are more, but it's too extensive for me to include everything.
Chinese (Peking duck-AMAZING, chow mein, soup, etc...), 
Japanese (some nigiri, rolls, ramen), 
Mexican (soups, 
Italian (pizza, pasta, etc...)
BBQ (ribs, brisket, sausages)
Steak (Prime Ribs
Seafood (oysters, crabs, mussels, shrimp cocktail, oyster shooters)
Fried foods: (chicken, tater tots, sweet potato tots, etc...)

Essentially, they something for EVERY taste and preference.

Desserts:
The dessert station is huge! It includes a bunch of pastries, cookies, chocolate-covered strawberries, unique sorbets, crepes, etc... There are so many I can't even remember a quarter of what was offered.

If you got to any one buffet in Vegas, I think this is the one.  They have an amazing of amount of unique foods to offer such as cooked to order street tacos, lobster corn chowder, lamb chops, etc.  This buffet is one of Vegas' premium Buffet (think Aria, Wicked Spoon, etc), and as such, commands a premium entry price.  The price was higher than normal the day we went because it was Labor Day Weekend.  The line in was over an hour and a half wait at 7:30pm on a Saturday.  We decided to pay the express fee to skip the line; even so, it was a half hour wait.  Not too bad.  

Most of everything offered here are in small portion size; it helps pace you.  Our favorites were the seafood selection and the dessert island.  We believe the food you get at Bacchanal is distinct from other buffets which is worth your time and money.

The Bacchanal is said to be the best buffet in Vegas...well, it definitely is! The selection is huge and the service is top notch. Bacchanal literally offers everything that you can think of and the quality of the food is great, nothing like typical buffet food. The ambience is a modern classic with clean lines and very neutral/calming tones. All and all an excellent dinning establishment and worth the money! Think of it as the "Rolls Royce" of buffets.

Buffets are never worth it to me, because I can't eat more than half a plate. (Then how are you so fat Dan? I have no clue). But I decided to bring my parents since they haven't been to Vegas in 20 years and you need to do a buffet, right? Anyways, this buffet is $60 and completely not worth it. First off, you have to wait in a 2-hr line, or you can enter your phone number and they'll text you when to return. Sounds great right? Nope. After you receive the text and return, you still have to wait another 45 min! Ok...
Now the food. Not great. I've had $20 buffets better than this place. I don't know who is giving this place high reviews, but the food is not great, at all. The meats suck; dry and chewy. The seafood sucks; oysters are dirty and huge, snow crabs are cold and limp, steamed crab is slightly better. Sushi is horrible and so limited, cannot even call it sushi. Asian food sucked. Everything basically sucked. 
The only decent section was the desserts. But cmon, $60 for horrible food and desserts? Plus the huge wait? Take a pass everyone, and go somewhere else.

Hubby and I have been coming to this buffet for some time. It gets pricey on holiday weekends, but you can get a Groupon for weekdays.  We like this buffet because they are wheelchair accessible and staff are attentive to your needs.  Every item is good tasting and fresh - very important when you are spending good money and when you have s large group and/ or kids. There is something for everyone.  Their seafood station is fantastic and they have booked crab legs as well. The have an Asian station with various fresh and tasty sushi and a Mexican- American station with pizza, Mexican dishes as well as a salad bar and meat carving station. Staff at the carving station are always pleasant and helpful and everything in the dessert station is yummy.

I definitely ate too much or ate too fast, because I was way too full when I left. My favorite is the shrimp cocktail, ramen and mochi ice cream. I did not get to fully experience the dessert station because I ate too much in the beginning. I got in at 2:30 and paid the lunch price and left at around 4:30, I got to experience some of the dinner menu and it was fancier than the lunch menu. They add a little something to each item for dinner.

I had the impression that this buffet place is huge, but it really isn't. There are about 6 different stations; 1. Cold/hot seafood, 2. Meat/soups, 3. Italian, 4. Mexican, 5. Japanese/Chinese, 6. Dessert. I think this list makes it seem like a lot, but when I was there it didn't seem like a lot when I was there. 

Overall, I ate a lot at the buffet, but I did not think it was super special after reading that this buffet is rated #1 on multiple accounts. Please save some room for the dessert! Or get dessert first. There as so much that I did not try at the dessert station because I was too full.

This was our last meal in Vegas before heading homes I had high hopes for this place after reading all the reviews but at the end of dinner I found myself disappointed. All of the items were just okay. Nothing stood out as amazing. The duck was super chewy and I found myself having to spit it out because I couldn't get through the meat. The prime rib was not tender at all and in the  saltier side and the line to get to the seafood was a bit much. I have to wait for 20 minutes to get some raw oysters?? Really? To top it off the oysters didn't taste that great. Maybe the east coast oysters have me spoiled but I did not like these oysters at all. The soup dumpling had no soup in it!! Most of the side dishes were good but whose going to eat plates and plates of sides. I did enjoy all of the desserts that I tried. However I don't think the meal was worth the price. I'd much rather go somewhere that is not a buffet and have meal be delicious than have mediocre all you can eat food.

I love this buffet!
Because this buffet is extremely popular and number one among other hotel's buffet, my boyfriend and i waited for more than 2 hours to get in and have seats.
When you first go to make reservation, there are 5 or 6 monitors to make reservation individually. You put your name and phone number in the reservation system and it will give you estimated time to come back and you can freely to go other places and come back at that time when you have messages! 
But don't be fooled! When you come back, you still have to get in line and wait there! Well it took me almost 30-45min. So it's not that fast or anything.
Be prepared to pay it with your cards! They don't prefer cash i guess. 

The interior design was really amazing and was clean!
The food was worth the money! I loved seafoods the best especially boiled crab legs.. The meat was good too but some were really dry like it had been out for too long time.. 
The sushi wasn't worth trying.. It was fresh compared to Wicked Spoon in Cosmopolitan but it wasn't as good as other premium sushi 
And they will automatically take 15% tip out of your card!

Hands down, the best buffet ever in Vegas! Went here twice on my last Vegas trip! It beats the one at the M resort! I can actually say for the first time that I've stayed in a buffet for the entire time limit they give you! My family and I took advantage of that 24-hour buffet pass which was like $50. We had access to about six or seven buffets, but this buffet and the rio buffet included a $15 upgraded everytime you dined there, but it was worth it! We figured getting that pass would be good because it would cover all our meals for the rest of our trip. I definitely recommend doing that because everywhere you go in vegas to get food will cost you about $20+ each time, so why not take advantage of that pass. Since you have access to the buffets you can pop in anytime for a quick bite, get a quick snack, or have a full on buffet experience again and again, lol! Your in vacation, so why not! 

We came here for lunch the first time around and for breakfast the second time around. We got to enjoy all of the breakfast items and all the lunch/dinner options. The food here is bomb!! So many choices! I love how they set it up in little plates and portions for you. Everything is so cute! I definitely enjoyed the breakfast menu and desserts the best! They also keep track on how long each dish has been out, which is something I truly appreciate! You will definitely find me here on every Vegas trip here on out! Wish I could give 10 stars!!!

Thursday buffet dinner time! Woot woot!! Worth the price! Bf and I went to go eat early because we didn't want to wait in the long line (previous yelpers complaints). There was no line and no wait! We went around 6pm. There are 9 different stations to eat from. I loved the seafood selections. They have cold and hot crab legs at different stations. Seafood, mexican (street tacos), soups, meats, sushi, chinese, american comfort food (chicken & waffles, mini burgers and mini hotdogs), meatballs, pasta, salad bar, fruit bar, and juice bar. The most impressing part was the dessert place. Oh my! I should have tackled dessert first before eating the main courses. They got everything from gelatos, cookies, mousse cakes, cake pops, creme brulee, green tea creme brulee, dipped  chocolate strawberry and suger free sections too. After we overeating we saw the line being super long. We are glad we went early.

Totally worth the expensive price. You can spend easily 2 hours there. Take your time. We by luck walked in at 2:30pm, paid the lunch price and got the dinner foods at 3pm, so crab legs etc. It was glorious! The sushi was amazing, salsa bar outstanding. Deserts could have been a bit better. Highly recommend it
Absolutely amazing!!! The best buffet I have ever been to! The sweet potatoe tater tots, and the blood orange gelato were my favorite! If your in Vegas this is a must!

I'm not a buffet girl. My ideas about buffets come from crappy Chinese buffets with food that looks like it's been drowning in grease for ages and getting food poisoning from Golden Corral. But when in Vegas - right? My boyfriend and I spent at least a solid two hours trying to figure out which buffet to go to and eventually settled on Bacchanal because it was the most famous and people talked about its consistent quality a lot. There is nothing more attractive in a buffet than consistency.

We came for lunch right when it opened and the wait was maybe 20-25 minutes, which wasn't bad at all. The amount of food was overwhelming once we got in. I remembered the biggest reason why I'm not always jumping at chances to go to buffets - limited stomach space and too many decisions to make. 

Standouts:

THE DESSERT BAR. I was on first name basis with the guy who scooped gelato by the time we left because I went back three times. Also the creme brulee. Also the Japanese matcha crepe cake. Good stuff.

Eat the sweet potater tots. You can thank me later.

The Asian food section is surprisingly pretty good! Their soup dumplings were aight, which surprised me. Worth some stomach room. 

The taco stand is good! I went when I was full but the meat was definitely very flavorful and well cooked. Also the juices are awesome in the Mexican section - tamarind is one of my favorites but I can never find it anywhere. 

Overall? I think it's worth the hype. Come by if you're looking to spend the rest of your day or night in a ridiculous food coma.
I felt like I was eating around the world. Very good food and good service during my experience. Thought it was a little pricey. Then again everything in Vegas is.
Outstanding Buffett. Deserts are amazing and everything and more you can think of. Good place for a group.
Loved it! Brisket, beef ribs, spicy sausage, mac n cheese was delicious and meat just fell off the bone. Dessert was beyond delicious. Cheesecake was light and perfect. Creme brûlée was perfect.

7/31/2018. 
Arrive: 1:45PM
Pay: 2:10PM
Seated: 2:45

Food: 4.5 star. Lamb, hot crab legs, tacos and desserts really stood out.

Service: 1 Star. Cashiers were talking with each other and ignoring customers. Our waitress looked like she was very tired and couldn't wait to go home. We were a group of three, but she only took away 1 or 2 plates each time she passed by, not to mention that she only passed by 3 times during 120 minutes. As a result, we had plates piling up on the table... 

Won't come back.

Excellent place.  Should've ate more king crab legs but now I know! Everything was pretty good. I like this spot and definitely coming back.  $50 is not too shabby to spend on this buffet and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a buffet that isn't price sensitive.  You wont be disappointed especially with all those king crab legs!!!

The buffet of all buffets!  My husband and I came here last weekend with 9 other people.  One member of our party had a platinum card which was the sole reason we were able to be seated.  The line was long and we were told originally that it would take over 2 hours to get in.  When we walked in I was in awe of the shear amount of food.  Table after table of food with the whole center of the room dedicated to dessert.  Oh my!  There was Chinese, Mexican, American, Italian cuisines, along with a whole seafood table, various salads, a whole row of cheeses, etc.  Literally a sight to be seen.  Food was definitely good and my personal favorite was the dessert bar.  Made to order crepe station-YES PLEASE!  They also have a wide selection of gelatos, however I was too stuffed to try one.  

My main issue with this place was the high price ($70/person for dinner, which does NOT include alcohol) and the lack of vegetarian options.  Soft drinks are included and if you are a platinum member then wine and champage are included (lucky for us that our friend was!)  My husband and I are both vegetarian and we could probably only eat about 1/3 of the options.  Despite this, I left absolutely stuffed and was actually a bit uncomfortable probably bc I carb loaded!   Service was also lacking and given the fact that we paid 18% gratuity at the beginning, it was a bit of a disappointment.  I had to hunt the waitress down repeatedly for my drink to be refilled, plates to be taken away, etc.  I ended up bussing the table myself at one point.  

If I was to go again, I would go for brunch as the prices are more reasonable and it's supposedly less busy.  Would I rate it the number 1 buffet in the US as they claim?  No probably not, however worth trying once.

So I'm a person whose main course is the crab legs and shrimp - so keeping that in mind,I love this buffet . Highlights : crab legs are cut in half and taste fresh , cocktail shrimp are huge and precut also taste fresh , bone marrow delicious, prime rib good for buffet style. Everything else I would give an average shout out . Oysters were not old but not super fresh either , ate maybe 3 and called it quits after . They have Dungeness crab claws which I thought looked great but tasted old - so don't waste your plate space ! The service is great , there was a lady server that was just on it ! She was clearing our plates like no other, and she did it without lurking behind us waiting to finish eating lol. I would come here again most definitely . Me and the mister payed an extra $35 each to skip the line ..honestly worth it . Was sitting and eating within 20 min.. rather in line for 2 hours.

Pretty good food! I always love the dessert section the most. I went during 4th of July and I loved the specials they had, as well as the cute little American decorated desserts for the holiday. 

Only reason why I took down one star is because the quality of the food has clearly gone down since the last time I went (last year) and the year before that.

Ate here soon after they opened. With two children, waiting over two hours was a pain. However, we soon found that by paying an extra bit of money, we could cut in line- and we did. Service was great, and the food was AMAZING.

Unlike other buffets, where some dishes are disgusting and simply discarded- we ate everything on our plates! We can't wait to go back!

Best buffet in Las Vegas, or the United States in general.

The varieties here are enough to make anyone with any taste bud love this place. I especially loved the seafood and Asian food section. They had everything from cold crab to hot crab, from sushi to all kinds of noodles to ginseng chicken soup, and so much more. The presentation of the foods were also fabulous. I loved how most of the servings were already placed in tiny saucers and pots, each juice came in its own jar, so you didn't have to wait for the server to bring you a new drink. Their dessert bar is also just so amazing. Anyone who has ever loved desserts would love their selections.

It's definitely worth your every penny despite how costly it is.

This is an absolute MUST if you go to Vegas and want good food!

Good food.  Slow to get in even when there's plenty of seating available.  Very Spotty service. Now that they raised prices (most expensive buffet on strip that I've gone to), I won't return.  Back to Bellagio which is now cheaper.

I heard this was the best seafood buffet in Las Vegas. It most definitely was not. We even called the manager to our table to ask "is this fish spoiled? Smell it!" The selections of seafood left a lot to be desired. E won't be going back again.

Oh my! I do not regret coming here! Without a doubt the best buffet in Vegas. I had the buffet of buffets deal and tried a few buffets. This one is the best! The food is top notch. my favorite were the hamburger sliders and the ambience is amazing! Thumbs up!

What a disappointment!!

We researched the best buffets on the Strip for weeks beforehand and decided to shell out $62 per person (including tax) for the Baccanal because it had rave reviews and looked really upscale.

We arrived at about 8:30 for dinner, waited in a ten minute line to pay, and another 30+ minutes to be seated. The seating area is a maze of tables and huge room dividers which make it a confusing experience to find your way back to your table from the buffet. The service was pretty bad as all of the servers seem overworked with too many busy tables to deal with. We only saw ours once during the entire evening.

We went primarily for their advertised lamb chops and BBQ racks of ribs, which are a real premium at buffets. When we arrived at the carvery, a none-too-nice chef/server said: "No more lamb! No more BBQ! You can have chicken." What was left were portions of a roast chicken, and some very standard prime rib. I can get this at my local small town buffet for a quarter of the price. This is really disappointing when paying so much and not getting what you've paid for.

There were about three types of salads to choose from, these were all good, but I don't really go to an expensive buffet for a salad.

The Chinese food outweighed the options in every other area in terms of quantity, but none of it was any better than Panda Express. They offered a glazed duck bits which were sweet but otherwise flavorless; more sinew and cartilage than anything. 

The Mexican area had a chef making street tacos to order which looked good, but we didn't try them. They had pre-prepped servings of a sort of nacho dish with quacamole which had been sitting there for a while and just made the tortilla chips soggy.

The single best item on the menu was a gorgonzola pizza slice I had.

The desserts were all those trendy little taster cups of overly fancy decorative chocolate; the best item there was a tiny cup of tiramisu.
Best buffet. This is definitely worth the money. The choice of food was the highest quality and something for everyone. Will definitely go again.

I am not a buffet person, thought I'd get that out of the way. In 2013 I tried the brunch @ Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan and my mind was changed dramatically. My friends said that Bacchanal was the best in Vegas. Since my mind was more open, I figure?...lets do it! First of all...don't come here hungry. We rolled up, put our name down and printed out a ticket that said when we should come back and that we'd receive a text to confirm that as well. With the terrible reception in the casino/shopping area, we received that text a lot later than expected. We were in line forever...waiting and waiting...that we missed the cutoff time for lunch. We were the transition time between lunch and dinner and unfortunately had to pay the DINNER price...and since it was the weekend before Christmas, we paid the HOLIDAY pricing which was about $62 with taxes. AHhhh....i better eat my ass off. But that's why I hate buffets, I'm not prepared to eat more than I actually am capable of.  We complained about the pricing, but they couldn't do anything about it.

Once you get through the paying line, you have to fall in OTHER lines. I'm over the lines and waiting by this point.

Finally... we're in, seated right next to the desserts. I left a note for the waiter that said "4 Waters please"....haha...sorry, I had to go eat something. We pigged out at the American/Carving Station area...picked up french fries, fresh juice, prime rib, ribs, brisket, mac n cheese...it was endless. AHh don't forget the pork belly. Most of this was absolutely delicious...ended up being worth the wait, KIND OF. I walked even further down the buffet, they have Chinese Food, Italian, Seafood, whoa. After that first plate, I was dying. 

When I landed dessert, I had an amazing fresh nutella crepe and some french macarons (people crowded like vultures once it was put out). So I just hate the pricing and the wait, but the food is actually good here. I don't suggest coming here in large groups, you'll just be waiting even longer, just saying.

Not worth the price of admission! The wait is terribly long! Over an hour just to pay $40 per person. There were no crab legs, lobster, or hot fish dishes. Minimal sushi choices and just about everything you could get at any other buffet for half the price! I will not be back here to eat mediocre food at an exquisite price tag!

I didn't get food here because the reception lady, which is MEAN! She asked me to get a ticket at the kisko machine, which indicate a time 3 hours later. She asked us to come back 3 hours later to wait in the loooong line!!! While we are watching from the far away, she let people without ticket into the line all the time!!!!

Came back for the 2nd time and I was not disappointed. You pay for the very best buffet at Vegas here! If I was stranded on a island and was only allowed to being one buffet with me this would be the place. They offer plates from around the world and there is something for everybody. All you can eat restaurant styled plates!

If you enter before 3pm for lunch price and stay until dinner would be good. 
They have raw oysters and love stone crabs.
Their Chinese dumplings suck so bad so I don't even get it. They have pho, ramen and these are ok.
Steaks are good but depend on what kind.
Lots of desserts but ice cream and crepes are only good.
I like their service so I would go there again but I only pick some nice dishes I only like.
This time I had Truffle soup and was great.
I was thinking about either 3 or 4 stars but since I would go there again, I decided to give them 4 stars but really 3.5 Stars.

My girlfriend suggested I give this place a try on my vacation.  I'm so glad she recommended this place.  It was right up my alley.  The food selection and quality was spot on.  They offered everything from seafood, to Mexican, to Chinese.  The desserts were delicious as well.  I went for lunch and returned for dinner.  It was well worth the price.

One of the best buffets in Vegas! Bottomless mimosas / Bloody Mary for $17 was a steep price but if you have the desire it can be worth your money. Lines can be pretty long at times but luckily they offer a line pass for $10 / $15 depending on the day you go. The food options were endless from food ranging from sushi to breakfast to steak and chicken. The bone marrow, king crab legs and mussels in a curry sauce and sliced meats are the best options for getting the most quality product. Service was eh but that makes sense considering how large the place was. Overall 100% a buffet I would go back to in the future.

This was the first Vegas buffet I've had and boy was it excellent! The staff made me feel welcome and the food was absolutely delicious! 

It is pricy, but well worth every penny!!

In particular, the pizza was ridiculously tasty! They also have amazing horchata! 
I also enjoyed the veggies. 

David, who slices the meat, was super helpful when I had questions. 

I highly recommend coming here!!

Woww what a delicious food... from their fish to their meats... Everything has such flavors and just melts in your mouth... omg what about their deserts... i would just go there for their deserts... crapes with fruits and chocolate... cheesecake... cookies... it was very good experience... I would recommend VIP/ express pass so you wont wait in line to get in

I wish I hadn't eaten here for lunch...it's too easy to try everything and stuff your face full until you can barely crawl out of the buffet. They have nearly every cuisine you can try and a whole island full of desserts, which was well done in taste and presentation.

I've had this place bookmarked for so many years now, and I'm glad I finally was able to try it. I went in for the dinner buffet. Sadly, I wasn't as impressed as I thought I would be. Maybe it was because I've (over)hyped myself up for trying this place. 

I'm a seafood lover so I was super excited for the crab, oyster, mussels, clams, crawfish (you get the picture). I actually really liked the clams and the crab; they were not salty at all! The crawfish, however, was so salty I was only able to eat a couple.... The oyster did not taste fresh at all. It tasted like it had been just thawed and it was super watered down. Maybe I'm spoiled by the freshness of the NorCal oysters, who knows, but even a dash of hot sauce wasn't going to save the oysters here.

I think my favorite part of the buffet was the dessert! You can't go wrong with freshly made crepes! But I don't think I'll be spending $$$ for dinner buffet again. 

I am going to give the place a try for brunch. Hopefully, it'll be better than the dinner buffet.

AAA+ for ambiance and presentation of food!!!  But once you come down from that visual overload and get down to eating, you will notice some discrepancies!  By this I mean, your eyes are sending signals to the brain of "Omgosh!  Must try!"  However, once you taste, your tongue and tummy may say, "What?"   I'm not saying it was really bad, just that the flavor wasn't always on point!   I will tell you that the pork belly, smoked salmon Vischaisse, red velvet bread pudding, and pot de creme with miso were INCREDLE!!!!

Also, enjoyed the fresh juicing carafes!

Reviewers have given this place high ratings due to the popularity. But is it worth the minimum one hour wait? If you're really hungry, yes. 

The variety is endless but quality is average. Nothing in particular amazed me. It's so crowded that the service is so poor. We had to wait for so long for drink refills. Almost like begging sometimes. 

I think the desserts is better than the food. 

The stone crabs is supposed to be the star item on the seafood table but it tasted like it was frozen & thawed, completely no sweetness to it, oysters were yuck. We did enjoy the brisket though.

This has got to be my favorite buffet in Las Vegas. They have over 500 items to choose from several culinary backgrounds such as American, Mexican, Asian, Japanese, Italian, BBQ and my favorite Seafood! The line for this buffet is very long, thanks to our high roller in our party, we got the expedited line. If you time it right, you can pay lunch price and get all the dinner entrees. We came around 230 pm so we still paid $38 for the lunch price, so by the time we were seated we got to try the end of lunch entrees and the new dinner entrees coming out. 

The King crab legs are served over ice and are sweet and tasty. Fresh Oysters on a half shell were delicious especially topped with the vinegar sauce. The cooked shrimp were humongous! Prime rib was excellent, cooked perfectly and well seasoned. The lamb chops had a really great flavor but over cooked for my taste. There are also many different varieties of desserts. My favorites were the green tea cream brûlée, carrot cake and lava cake. Definitely come hungry so you can try all the different yummy varieties of food.

Mega godt og mega stort. 

Lækker mad selvom det er i store mængder, deres dessert buffet er fabelagtig.

The best dinner buffet in Vegas I have ever been to. The variety is astounding. The combination of dishes is immeasurable. Once you get past the long line to get in - can take anywhere from an hour to two on busy days - it's utter bliss. Mexican, Italian, seafood, Japanese, Chinese, American, and sooooo much more! The desserts are sinfully good. Everything is top notch. It all tastes as good as if you would have ordered each item on its own at a 5-star restaurant. I left miserable...the good gluttonous kind. Food coma for days! $55 price tag and I definitely had much more than that to eat! Well done Caesars.

This buffet was pretty disappointing for me. We paid a $25 upgrade with our 24hr buffet pass and it was not worth it unless you are a big seafood fan. They offer a huge selection of seafood options but a lot of there cooked seafood items had bacon in them which I don't eat. They have the standard omelette bar, Chinese corner with sushi, noodles, make your own Pho with different broth choices to choose from and one chicken choice of sweet and sour chicken with a hot and scour soup which was a bit too tangy and a corn soup option. They also had some slices of different pizzas but the vegetarian options were sitting on the same tray as the bacon pizza which I don't eat religiously. I also noticed a fresh taco bar but also mainly pork options. I was surprised the chicken options were very limited here. They did offer roasted turkey, beef, and lamb though. The drinks are served at your table and the coffee was freshly brewed and delicious! The orange juice and fancy green tea was also quite refreshing. The staff here is very nice and welcoming. They also has some infused water and a hibiscus drink at the buffet station. 

We went for brunch around 10:30m and had to wait in line for 5mins buying the pass and and then 2mins to get seated to our table. When we were leaving around 11:30am we noticed the lines were a lot longer since people are getting in for lunch.

I would say the quality is definitely better then then other buffets but still not worth the upgrade fee and overpriced for the Bacchanal name.
Great service. fresh food and good wine. You need to come early to avoid waiting too long.

We avoided this place our first few days because buffet food is not usually something we enjoy. But we did enjoy it. I tried a tiny amount of a handful of things, but my dinner mainly consisted of salmon, sautéed mushrooms, and salad. All were delicious. My husband got roast and some ribs with a few sides and enjoyed it. He went back to get some warm crab legs and didn't care for them... I couldn't decide on a dessert, so we got a few of those too, and we both thought the little cannoli were the best. If we were going back it'd probably be the only thing I'd grab... Overall it was good and a good value for all the food we got to try. But that was the only problem, we overate, and walked around really uncomfortable for several hours. Lol.

I visited twice in two weeks. 

Once for a breakfast and the next trip to Vegas for Sunday Brunch. Out of all the buffets, this new buffet to me is a "foodie's buffet."  

Everything we tried tasted to be of excellent quality. The fresh cut bacon they were serving is flown in from a farm in Virginia.  Everything from the presentation to the food, bread, cheese, meats, and meat are a food lover's dream.

They have a variety of food to choose from to the left they have fresh squeezed juices, then they have the seafood -- king crab, oysters, then they have some wagyu beef sliders, croque madame, corned beef hash beautifully presented, a meat station, sweet potato fries, fresh bread section, pasta, pizza, sushi, and dimsum.

I also enjoyed their king crab for Sunday brunch and also their watermelon juice... oh and there unlimited champagne and/or mimosas.
It was just okay. More a checkbox visit. A bit overrated in my opinion. Lots of food but the quality was average, I have had better buffet.

Caesar's Palace is always keeping it fresh! This is the newest buffet and probably my favorite on the strip. Here are some highlights:

- Lines are insanely long! Some of our friends got there at 5pm and didn't get in till 8pm. It's a good opportunity to level up on your angry bird game or have a long and deep convo.  

- Warm crab legs!! Better than most buffets, and there's a line for the crab legs too.

- Ginseng with chicken soup?!! Wow, definitely appeals to the Asian crowd.

- Lamb chops were my fave. Tender and succulent.

- I like how they serve their food in big pots and pans instead of the traditional square pan in the water warmer. Good display of food.

- One of the most expensive buffet. Weekend holiday buffet (in December) was $50 per person.

--------
Overall, it's a great experience and definitely something worth trying. It's one of those been-there, done-that, ate-it one-time experience. The Studio B Buffet at the M Resort 20 minutes outside the strip is still my ultimate fave.

My favorite buffet in Vegas! I always come around 2 something and pay for lunch but by the time I'm seated and eating the dinner time items are already out (You're welcome). The prime rib & crab legs already make this buffet worth the price for me. Another favorite here are the tacos which they grill the meat of your choice in front of you. There's also a noodle soup corner and I always get the ramen, even though it is a little salty at times. The laksa soup is also really good as well.

The sushi section isn't as great as I would like it to be & sometimes the oysters aren't as fresh, but besides those two items I think everything else is pretty good. The dessert section is amazing. I usually get a crepe,which they also make fresh in front of you. They also have a large selection of ice creams and baked goods. I'm always craving their chocolate lava cake the next day. I know the price is steep and the wait is sometimes ridiculous, but this buffet is worth visiting at least once.

This was probably the most kick ass buffet with the most selection I have ever seen before. Me and two other friends went during 4th of July weekend when they had $40 brunch deal (normally $45) if you arrive before 9:30am. While this is a bit early, I highly recommend coming during brunch time because there won't be a line, there will be alot less people there, and it's almost half the price for full dinner and you still get premium items like snow crab and rock crab. 
The decor is very modern and pretty, I love the patterned glass inside the restaurant. The food selection is incredible, they have everything from king crab legs, scallops, shrimp, duck, pasta, steak, sausages, and gelato! They almost have orange juice, cucumber juice (pretty gross) and watermelon juice (fantastic!)
They also have a large dessert selection and just too much food to try them all. 
I don't think I would pay the dinner price to come eat here but the brunch deal is a steal!

Bacchanal Buffet has amazing food!!! the quality and selections are great. BUT my visit here was not that great, the line is over an hour and I think since they have so many customers they can expand easily... The staff are nice and friendly and I would definitely go back bc of the food but I would think twice bc of the line and wait!!!

After extensive research, we picked this buffet for our Vegas weekend. Some quick tips:

The line for dinner is insanely long. We made our way there around 5-530 and it was still a 1.5 hour wait. There is a line to check in and get a receipt for when to come back and wait in the second line to pay. Then there's the third line after you pay to be seated. If you have a large group or older family members who can't stand in line for almost 2 hours, send a tribute to wait in line for everyone. 

You have a 2 hour limit, which I didn't see advertised and also didn't see enforced, but be aware if you're planning an ultra-feast. The food is arranged by country with asian, italian, french, southern, and, finally, seafood. The crab legs are really what its all about- Grab a few plates of hot legs for the table (located near the southern food separate from the rest of the seafood!!) and find cold legs, oysters, mussels, and sea snails at the cold seafood bar towards the front. 

Absolutely save room for desert- the gelato bar is amazing, as is the selection of mini desserts, including tiny chocolate lava cakes and macarons.
THE BEST buffet, HANDS DOWN! We ate here twice while visiting Vegas. My girlfriend wants to go back just for this buffet.

For the highest rated buffet in Vegas, the lunch option was lack luster. Most of the seafood items like, crab legs and oysters were Mia.

It was large, and the food was pretty good.  The meatballs stood out as the best thing I had. In the end I would say not worth waiting in line for, as I have had other buffets in Vegas on par with this.
Love this Buffet!! Great variety of food, and its all top notch! Would recommend to any Chinese food lover cause you can have all your favorites while trying new things as well!!

Absolutely insane buffet - definitely one of the best in Vegas! It's more expensive than most but they have a bigger selection including a whole fresh seafood section. The dim sum was great; the pork dumplings were phenomenal. And the pho was SO good, some of the best broth I've ever had. Worth the wait!
This buffet is phenomenal. I have been to other "top rated" buffets and their selection is always hit or miss. However everything I got was delicious! I will be back!

Okay, have to admit this is the best buffet ever. COME EARLY to avoid the long lines or else you'll end up waiting quite a while especially on the weekends... The variety of food in this place is AMAZING. From seafood to a variety of ethnic food, and then ending the night with an IMPECCABLE dessert bar, this buffet has an endless selection. Although this is on the pricier end, it is definitely worth coming for. Also, the ambiance in this place cannot be more elegant and the cleanliness of this place is profound. The quality of their food definitely excels all standards. The best on the strip and highly recommend!!

This is the place you want to go for a great buffet. Almost every detail has been looked at and every weakness that other buffets have are the strengths of this place.  A little pricey for me but still worth every penny.

If quantity over quality excites you then you will probably enjoy your meal here. However, we waited over 30 minutes in line at 8am on a Monday.... just to pay to get in. Food was well presented, but not anything worth waiting in line for....

They have changed.   No longer do they have the tuna and salmon poke. That's a big disappointment.   They also got rid of some of the charcuterie and chichirones at the Mexican station. 

The duck and dumplings are very good so is the hot and sour soup.  Skip the pho sometimes it's good but too often the broth is bland.

Not worth the weekend price for brunch it is no different from the weekday lunch.

Not worth the hype at all.  We went here on Xmas eve and was literally in line for what felt like hours.  We decided to pay extra to skip the larger line only to find ourselves in a shorter line that took 45 minutes.  It seemed like those Diamond, Seven star members kept popping up in front of us!  Then more lines at every freakin' station!  Since we're patient people, I wouldn't have minded the lines if the food was worth it.  

Cocktail shrimp -- good, but could someone really mess this up?
Prime rib -- bleh... tasteless, dry, unappetizing (i was thinking thank gawd this is a buffet and I can politely leave the food on my plate without feeling bad about wasting money).
Lamb chops -- pretty good if you don't get a dry piece
Onion rings/fries -- good, but c'mon that's expected right?
Paella -- decent
Oysters -- not the freshest... wouldn't recommend for those with weak stomachs
Crab legs -- ok, standard
Desserts -- good selection... too bad I'm not a sweets person
...
... 
list goes on but nothing that really stood out.

Vegas has alot to offer and I'm definitely better off spending my moola in those other places!

Very disappointing and VERY overrated. For the amount of money we could have had a much better dinner in a nice regular restaurant. The food was not appetizing looking and did not taste good. The seafood area stank (and I love seafood). The Buffet at Wynn last night was ten times better. This was a huge waste of money!  Won't go back!
Love the Buffet at Caesars. It's a be pricey, but that's what Vegas has turned into!
One of the best buffets. It's pricy about $85 per person but the food quality is great and there is so many verities to choose from
Such a great buffet! Truly recommend! Our server, Mark, was awesome and went above and beyond! Thanks Bacchanal!

My favorite buffet of all-time!!!

Food:
Great selection, good quality. The menu changes from time to time, but to give you an idea, here's what I've had: pork chops, prime rib, crab (served steamed or cold), oysters, shrimp, dim sum, sushi, bone marrow, pho, congee, mac&cheese, fried rice, watermelon salad, macarons, gelato. If you are not looking for an unconventional menu with crazy unique dishes, Bacchanal will definitely do the job for you. It is what you would expect out of a buffet, and more.

Environment:
Lots of seating, lots of room. High ceilings, moderately dim lighting. Clean. Basically you will feel comfortable at your table and get to enjoy conversation with your group. Nothing to worry about here. You can have a nice date, get rowdy with friends, or spend time with family. One thing to note is that the restroom is located right outside the restaurant, but walking outside and coming back in is not really a hassle.

Verdict:
Vegas buffets I've tried: Aria, Wynn, Wicked Spoon, M
LA buffets I've tried: Vegas Seafood Buffet, Hilton buffet
Bacchanal is easily my favorite out of all of those. It has the best combination of selection and quality. Bacchanal is a must for anybody looking to enjoy a buffet on the Vegas strip.

Tip:
Come here before 3pm to get seated for lunch price and still get to enjoy the dinner menu! Dinner starts at 3pm. Bottomless mimosas used to be included with lunch but it looks like it doesn't anymore. With lunch it costs $15 extra and for dinner it costs $25 extra.

Really good but the wait is terrible.  We were in a shorter line because we are platinum members but the wait was still LONG.  We came for Christmas eve dinner so I know that it is a holiday but from what I hear the wait is long regardless of a holiday or not.  For the price you get a very big selection of delicious food.  I was sad to see that there was no lobster because they had lobsters on display in the front.  Other than those two things I have no complaints.
Excellent buffet! Food selections galore. Why didn't I give it 5 stars??  This buffet is very pricey as it is. But they raised it even higher because of the holiday. Not nice...

You know that feeling when you eat somewhere so good you JUST have to go home and tell everyone about it? Or when the price is so high but the food so amazing, you and your friends come in at 3pm for lunch price and eat for 4 hours until dinner just to get at those lamb chops (no shame...)? Or when you get 10 rounds of food and then 20 rounds of dessert? How about when you and your party just have to exclaim to each other how incredible the food is in between every other bite? 

Yep, this is it. I don't think I'll ever eat at another buffet as good as this again. It has come to a point where if I'm only in Vegas for 3 hours, I'd come here.. and here only.
Most decadent buffet I believe in Vegas the drinks are a must and yes you must keep drinking and eating don't stop until you can't walk

Definitely one of my favorite buffets in Vegas! Here and Wicked Spoon are my top picks. The selection is endless. Quality of food is good. Service is decent for being a buffet. 
Honestly, the wait is not that bad. We waited for a while when we went for dinner on a weekend. But you just leave your information and then they text you when your table is almost ready. The wait was less than what they told us it would be (they said 2 hours and I think we waited 1 hour). When we went for an early dinner on a weekday, we did not have to wait at all. 
I especially enjoyed the sushi, ramen, lamb chops, and dessert! 
Of course, the price is a bit much, but if you come hungry you'll get your money's worth! You definitely have to try here at least once!

Rated the Best buffet in Las Vegas and I certainly concur. Quality of food is superb and serving sizes perfect. Allows you to sample a greater variety of dishes. I especially love the poke, the variety of different noodle dishes, and raw tuna sushi. If you have any room after eating your main courses you have to try their dessert bar. Hugh calorie but so good. It a bit pricey but well worth every dollar.

This place is like an amusement park for foodies. 
It's expensive -- we went the day before Thanksgiving and paid $65 per person for the "brunch pricing" and then proceeded to eat so much food I thought I was going to throw up. 
The dessert bar was incredible, make sure to save room for all the individual treats. 

Some things to skip: the pizza, steak and egg, crab.
Things to grab: fried chicken, tiramisu, pork belly.
Best buffet I have been to.  Favorites were the brisket, ribs, spicy sausage, made to order tacos, hot crabs legs and butter, and oreo truffles.  Nice settings.  Great selection.

Wow this was a terrible buffet. Are good reviews coming from drunk people??? Many dishes were salty and disgusting including the polenta, scalloped potatoes, and mushroom soup. Decent items included the beet salad and sweet potato fries. The crab rangoon was ok and the vegetable egg roll wasn't bad. The spanish rice was meh. Macaroni and cheese was nothing special. The one good thing about this buffet is the crab legs. The snow crabs were awesome, especially when you get them from the hot food area. Don't eat them cold!  Sushi had too much rice, fish didn't taste fresh. The dessert was horrible. Crepes were floppy and didn't have a nice crunch to it like other creperies. Whoopie pies were dry and too sweet. The little cakes were bland and dry. The chocolate mousse was surprisingly not sweet enough. The tapioca had a bitter orange layer on top that tasted worse the more I ate it. Even the souffles which were recommended to us by our server came raw in the middle - I'm really sad we waited 10 minutes for them to cook. Obviously they didn't cook long enough. Overall, we overpaid yet again in vegas for mediocre to bad food.

The food we had at Bacchanal buffet (Caesars Palace) was truly and completely worth every penny. The bacchanal buffet is voted as the best buffet in Las Vegas. They offer......hold your breath.... more than 500 dishes to choose from. We were in a foodies wonderland. I remember having tasted almost everything. They also had an impressive spread of desserts. With so much to choose from, you will definitely leave the place happy and satisfied.

Definitely the best buffet in town. Well, it's actually the best buffet I've ever been to. Food was very good, great selection. The only reason I'm giving it a four is because it's still buffet food. Definitely worth the money.

I spent a breakfast/ brunch/ early afternoon at the Bacchanal Buffet with my dad and brother when I visited Las Vegas and it is a sight to behold. For $59.99 per person we gained access to an endless array of food and non-alcoholic beverages (the drink package was another $15)! There was seafood and sushi, Mediterranean style cuisine and I could even make myself a full English breakfast if I was so inclined. A better question to ask about this buffet is what food doesn't it serve? My table tried some stuffed olives, toast, a poached egg, bacon and sausage links, a full English breakfast, several pieces of sushi and some crab legs. Included in spread was also a decadent array of deserts and I tried a croissant, a chocolate chip cookie and a slice of cheese cake. If you are looking for a buffet, this is definitely worth trying. 

The dining room is huge and it took a little longer than I would have liked for our server to arrive to take our coffee and iced tea beverage orders so we could get to the buffet. They have several chilled drinks in the buffet but I would have liked a little quicker service with the other drinks including water. The wait staff was also very nice but, again, it took a while to get refills on the drinks and the plates cleared. 

Although there were a ton of food options, I found many of the flavors lacking. I suspect the Bacchanal Buffet makes a lot of the food bland to appeal to a wider audience but I wasn't impressed. Yes, there are a ton of options and you can eat enough food to last several days of your vacation but none of the food items I tried were all that delicious. My brother made a great observation that the whole experience (large dining area and bland food) reminded him of the dining halls at his university and I 100% agreed with him. Maybe we were just trying the wrong food but I didn't walk away from any dish thinking, "That was delicious!". Instead, I walked away full but unfulfilled. 

If you love the buffet experience, this will give it to you and then some. I don't regret trying this buffet but in general I would rather have a smaller portion of something tastier.

My wife and i went to check out this buffet for our anniversary as we heard it was the best in las vegas.

We were disappointed that it didn't live up to that hype. 

Here's a couple of things we felt about the food we did eat:

- Mapo Tofu : enjoy this very much, lots of taste and a good amount of spice

- Shrimp Shumai : was over cooked. the wrap of the shumai was really mushy

- Pork Shumai : good taste.

- Snow Crab legs : we definitely have had better. there was no real taste to the crab legs. Yes i know there is butter that we used to dip them in but there should have at least a slight taste without the butter. What i did like about the crab legs is that they were pre cut and easy to break.

- Dungeness Crab : taste better than the snow crab legs.

- Wagyu : a little too well done. 

- Prime Rib : good taste, cooked just enough.

- Sushi : we didnt really get to enjoy the sushi as the variety was very slim.

- Truffle / Mushroom Pizza : Definitely liked this.

Customer Service:

Our waitress was good about refilling our drinks before it ran out and swapping out our plates that we were putting our crab shells on.

Im not sure we will be coming back, nor recommending this buffet to family / friends.

There is another buffet that we have previously tried, and will remain unnamed, that we felt was far superior.

Hopefully the upper management will take this to heart as constructive criticism and work towards improvement.

Bacchanal -- IMHO -- rates a solid Meh (or three stars). Part of that may just be my problems with buffets. I don't enjoy overeating and hate to see food wasted -- which it is by the plateful here.

Does it represent good value for the money? If you're eating breakfast or lunch, the price is much more reasonable than dinner. And it seems to be pretty easy to get in at those times (zero wait for me at 11am on a weekday) so you save on the added cost of excessive waits that others have written about here.

Service on my visit was friendly and prompt. No complaints there.

Bacchanal is probably a good bet for the chronically undecided, those with fussy children, or those with enormous appetites.  Otherwise, I think you're better off spending a few moments thinking about what you'd like to eat and seeking that out at one of the multitude of places on the strip. You'll probably pay less and have an all around better experience.

Probably the best buffet in Vegas! Well organized express entries so you know when to return if you aren't VIP. So many items to choose from and different types of eats from all over the world. I used to think Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan was the best, since it was knew but they've come off from the pedestal a bit. I especially like their seafood section that offers crab claws, crab legs both cold and boiled as well as large shrimps not the itty bitty ones you find in most Vegas buffets nowadays. With all the options you need to plan accordingly to make room for dessert. Check out my pics and you'll drool...

This is the new leader is Vegas buffets!

There is a nice assortment of Japanese (sushi), chinese, mexican, seafood, etc.  The dessert assortment is also top notch with many flavors of gelato.

I have experienced most of the buffets in Vegas and these days have been going to Aria and Cosmopolitan but I enjoyed my meal here more than those 2 places.  In prior years I used to head over to the Bellagio, Mirage, Rio's (seafood), Paris, etc.

I will be back!

You will not regret paying the  money for eating here! From the excellent customer service to the mouthwatering delicious food, make plans to eat here! Definitely will be coming back for more but more than anything for the peach green tea! 

P.S. there is a two hour limit so pick and choose your meals wisely

09/23/2012

Its been a while ive been to Vegas..so i gotta try out whats new! 
I heard about this buffet, its a new renovation at the Ceaser's Palace. and i wanted to check it out. The layout was pretty cool and looks elegant. The line was long as usual like other types of buffets in Vegas. my Bf and I went here around 3:30 pm, hoping they still serve Lunch.. but no.... they start dinner pretty early (3pm). entrance for us two reached almost 70. but hey, worth it?

They have the usual crab legs and claws, sushi on one side, italian food on the other...but whats unique about this place, they make your food in front of you fuh fuh fuh FRESSSHHHH! They literally make RAMEN in front of you. just let them know what kind of ramen. they have the tonkotsu ramen,.. mmmm my fav. and for the crab legs...i mean.. the heaven section of the buffet.. you basically grab the crab legs and claws onto your plate and place it on top. the chefs will ask you, how you like your crabs cooked. steamed crab legs and claws are the bomb. They have other types of foods thats been readily made onto mini plates. You can just grab and go. they have them all presentable and all cute and what not.

now lets talk about sweeets! They have pretty nice dessert section. lots of varieties and in cute little dishes. they do gelato ice cream and OMG! they have crepes. they also make it in front of you. just let them know, what you want on it. 

I'd totally come back here...VEGAS ANYONE? haha

I'm not one of those negative people whose life sucks, so all I write are negative yelp reviews.

This place is definitely a novelty concept compared to the other Vegas buffets, however, this is not a buffet that will not stand the test of time.  

THE FOOD IS SALTY!!   Most foods taste amazing when you add excessive butter or salt.   

You have to try this place at least once so you don't feel left out.  However, it's definitely not worth the wait or the money.

I had heard so much about this new Ceasars Buffet and couldn't wait to try it.
My sister and friend were visiting so we decided to go there for lunch! Well missed the lunch cutoff at 3 so we had to pay dinner prices $50 pp!!  BUT BUT IT was so worth it.
I have been to many buffets in Vegas and while i rave about the M this Bacchanal has taken the ball and made a touchdown!! THE fresh cut up crab legs are awesome and they will steam them for you. I hadnt realized there was a WHOLE OTHER side!! WOW and i was getting full already. I cant even describe the decadent foods i saw and i tried really tried to taste it all . Sadly my stomach didnt agree with my brain lol i was too stuffed to try anything else. AND i missed the whole iltalian foods and some others. This is a definite try buffett when in Vegas IF you can afford the high prices for lunch and dinner. BUT its worth it to treat yourself at least once. YOLO

It was a bad experience to be asked to leave after two hours, I had a surgery in my stomach and I have to eat very little bites, the claim there is a signage every where, but there was not a single sign stating that I have to leave with in 2 hours

Good food and tons of it? Yep, sign me up! With top quality offerings such as chicken and waffles, sushi, house made BBQ, fresh made pasta and more, it is easy to see why Bacchanal has become a destination on it's own here in Vegas. You can still get your Vegas Buffet classics such as crab legs, pizza, sushi and more desserts than you can shake another new plate at.. but there are a lot of surprises here as well. I really enjoyed the single serving items. I found that these items really showcased what the staff here can offer at a Buffet. The blush ravioli and the chicken n waffles were my favorites and ranked up there with food Id expect to get at most any 5 star sit down affair.
Do yourself a favor and grab those pants with the elastic waist band, I know youve got them stashed in the closet, and come spend some time here and "explore" this culinary yellow brick road for yourself!

Went here to celebrate a 30th birthday with a large group. Two of us got sick shortly after eating and ended up throwing up everything we ate. There was another girl in the bathroom of the buffet throwing up as well. When I let them know what happened, they refused to refund us- instead suggesting that we sue if we were unhappy. Eating here ruined my whole night. I wouldn't recommend eating here to any of my friends or family.

We came here on a Saturday night at 6pm which was probably our first mistake. But we knew we would have to wait a while and were fine with that. We've waited for tables in the past for 1.5 hours so we are used to it. 

We checked into the electronic kiosks and were given a wait time of 60-75 mins. We thought that was reasonable as we could wait in a bar and they would text us when we had to return. BOY WERE WE WRONG. We were texted about 15 minutes later to report to the hostess. We returned to the restaurant only to find that we had to stand in a line that lasted TWO hours. We then got up to the hostess who told us we had about another 20 minute wait to be seated. We already committed so much time to this endeavor that we agreed and paid. We then proceeded to wait in said line for over an hour.  So after almost 3.5 hours we were finally able to eat.

After all that, the food is pretty good but not amazing. There's a huge selection of foods and an extraordinary variety. There's no denying that this buffet is great. However, In my opinion, no food is worth standing in line for 3.5 hours. We were mostly angry at the disparity in advertised wait time with actual wait time. ( and the wait would have been probably twice as long but half the people in front of us gave up on the wait and left for other restaurants.)

If you want to try this place out, do so at your own risk and don't plan anything else for later in the night because you will probably be waiting for longer than you think......

Cold decor, mostly uninspired offerings, high price, and THE WAIT even after the electronic pre-check-in. Best eats include: "street tacos" and the good guac that goes with it; sliders; and some desserts. Overall pretty underwhelming for what was a "best buffet in vegas" not too long ago.

tl;dr hot new buffet, ask for crab legs steamed

It seems like every year, there's a bigger and better buffet in town. This is the year of Bacchanal. Luckily, we arrived early enough on Saturday to avoid any sort of line. Almost two hours later, the line appeared to be a 45 minute wait. 

Brunch automatically includes mimosa, which I thought was strange. But since I paid for it, I suppose there's nothing wrong with drinking at 11am in the morning. This is Vegas afterall right?

Other buffets I've been to repeat their food items, either for lack of creativieness or to avoid congestion. As our host lead our party to our table, I noticed that nothing ever repeated. The food options stretched beyond what I could see. I continued to eyeball where along the buffet I should start until we were abruptly welcomed by the gentleman at the carving station. How nice I thought to myself until he started with the Ni Hao. That was just weird.

The wide array of food left me satisfied beyond stomach capacity. Instead of this being brunch, I treated it like a cheaper version of dinner. Though annoying at the time, the presentation (small amounts of food on dishes larger than they needed to be) helped me to avoid eating until barfing. Bathrooms are right outside the main entrance just in case.

Tip: Ask for your crab legs steamed!

COCKROACH! Saw this beast at the dessert bar between the watermelon and the pineapple platters next to the lady making the crepes. I saw it and walked back to make sure I saw it right before I reported it to one of the managers. She ran to tell a guy behind the counter. This isn't even connected to the kitchen directly! Be wary everybody...

Definitely not worth the price $55 or the wait time.

I thought for sure, it would exceed Wicked Spoon but it just didn't.  They do offer  more food, but you definitely feel like you are in a mess hall - everyone just waiting to get some grub.  It was a bit ridiculous, waiting to get seated which can easily take over 1 hour, and then once you are inside, you are waiting in a long assembly line to get some food on your plate.

Nothing stood out here at all, other than the jasmine chicken soup, which stayed piping hot.  Unfortunately, that was the only highlight for me.  Don't get me wrong, everything was good and there was plenty of variety, but I didn't feel like the price was justified.  I probably wouldn't choose to come here again.

I enjoyed this buffet, but definitely not worth the $60 I paid.

Pros:
-Rock Crab
-Japanese Soba
-Tacos to order
-Sea Snails
-Oysters
-Lamb
-Mochi Strawberries
-Marrow
-Lime Basil Ice Cream

Cons:
-Crab Legs overcooked
-Prime Rib is very average
-Where the hell is my Lobster?
-Why did you run out of Scallops? After 1 hour!
-Frog legs were underwhelming

Not very satisfied. Still don't know how this became the best buffet in Las Vegas.

Location: In Ceasars Palace off the strip! Won't be hard to find follow the signs or ask one of the staff!


Customer Service: Great customer service they are attentive and take away the plates very fast!


Decor: It's really appealing to the eyes! The way the whole setup of the buffet.


Presentation of Food: Very nice!!! Everything is presented beautifully that you would like to try everything! BTW I LOVED the mini milk jars that were filled with different traditional Mexican drinks (horchata, jicama, pineapple juice.", etc!!!!)
