How did the food taste?:AMAZING! I can't even begin to tell you! The food stayed warm, the seafood was fresh, and there is every station you can think of! The Chinese buffet is soooo good, next to the yummy fresh sushi, the Asian dishes such as pad Thai that was surprisingly good!!! As you move along they have traditional American dishes, and a stationJUST for steam king crab legs with yummmmmmy melted butter! They have a Spanish section with a huge grill just for tacos etc and as I mentioned the mini juice jars of traditional Mexican drinks yummmm! The meat section is ridiculous prime rib etc melts in your mouth so tender and juicy!!!! The seafood section has to be my favorite because there are raw oysters and crab legs! YUMMMMM!



Overall Experience: Ceasers really stepped their game up, mosdef the best buffet in Vegas right now.


Would I Come Back?:YESSSSS!

Best buffet I've been to in Vegas.All food was fresh and up to standards of a very nice restaurant. I even forgot at times I was in a buffet lol. 

Décor was nice and unique, not plain and boring like other buffets yes its more expensive than other buffets, but its well worth it!!!

Yummy even the clam chowder was awesome! fresh salads, juices, shrimp, ribs, ham, duck, pastas all look appetizing.

Enjoyable experience! will come back next time im in town :)
It's not inexpensive but you can find anything you want there. The quality of the food is excellent and they have the service part of it down to a science. Well done.
Quality buffet! Worth every penny. We went around 2-3pm and there was barely any wait!

The Bacchanal Buffet is hands down the best buffet in Vegas. It has a great variety of different foods that taste good. The carving station is always on point.

I find that they cater to their Asian clientele with authentic foods. I didn't see on my recent visit February 14, 2018, but two years ago, during the Lunar New Year, their Asian section was stocked full of delicious authentic Chinese food. What I really wish they had were the authentic Chinese soups, like fish maw soup and black chicken and ginseng...but they only had generic hot and sour soup. Pfft.

But, this review is really for Delmar the dude at the Taco station. Delmar was an amazing service member with a positive attitude. I really want management to read and I hope they do read this Yelp review. Get that man some training to be a team leader or some kind of supervisor. Because he deserves it. I spent the entire time talking to him while he was making me tacos. He was respectful, and just a really good dude. Other members at the buffet just go through the motions but this guy had so much confidence and a super positive vibe. So, please, please, please, give him a bonus or something. Delmar, if you're reading this, thanks for having a chat with me. I hope good things come your way.

In my opinion, this place doesn't live up to its reputation. I was expecting king crab for lunch, but it was snow crab. The selection is great and there's something for everyone. I especially enjoyed the sushi. The other dishes were mediocre and dessert was below average. Not worth the price tag. I really wanted to love this place. Also found a hair in one of my dishes. Very disappointed.

Have to do brunch here to fully enjoy! I've been here several times every time (but once) for brunch. For brunch they have unlimited mimosas and a better menus selection. The food is fantastic and have plenty of dishes to choose from. From pizza and sushi to crab and steak. Seriously huge selection, you will definitely find something even if you are a picky eater.

This is the buffet @ Caesar's Palace and definitely one of the more higher end.  Lots of variety and I really did enjoy it, but not as good as Bellagio IMO.  I did like the fact that they have a wider variety of options (more asian food for example) than Bellagio, but I have a preference for Bellagio.  However, you can't go wrong with Bacchanal either if Bellagio is not an option for whatever reason.  

Pluses:

Leek dumpings are fantastic
Char Siu Pork and Ribs delicious, though could use some more work to keep it moist
Wagyu Beef sliders tasty
Truffle Scalloped Potatoes yummy
Kung Pao Chicken solid
Beef w/Broccoli is tasty and they used chinese broccoli and not american
Meatloaf suprisingly savory
The four desserts I had kicked butt (Tiramisu, Lava Cake, Vanilla Creme Brule, and "Hot" chocolate chip cookie)

Cons
Har gow skin WAAY too dry and thick, awful
Lotus wrapped sticky rice was too dry and lacked flavor on the inside, bland without soy sauce
Waffle fries too salty
Risotto too salty

Etc
Orichetti cream pasta wasn't stand out, was decent
Meatballs were good
Osso Bucco was tasty, although a bit salty too

I wish I could eat like I was 10 years younger so I could chow down on the other cuisines.  I didn't have any seafood, mexican, pizza, or the lobster chowder which looked really good.  I'll have to come back though to try the other stuff.

I think it's a little overpriced at $55 (with tax).  Was worth $40-45 tops.  The Bellagio Buffet was $15 cheaper and because of that, I give the edge to Bellagio for overall value.  

One thing this has a plus over Bellagio is that there are more vegan options.  I saw eggplant w/tofu, salads, fruits, sweet potato tater tots, waffle fries, green beans, grilled carrots, hummus, some tomato salad looking dish.  Bellagio was far shorter in terms of being vegan friendly.

Awesome buffet! We had to wait around an hour to be seated for a party of 3, but it was worth the wait. Bottomless sangria, beer, wine or mimosas for $15 is a great deal! There's a great selection of all different kinds of food. Friendly staff and great service. I would love to go again!

I love this buffet. Expensive --yes, worth it---yes. Huge selection of food to choose from. Everything was fresh and hot. I love hot food, especially in a buffet. Huge dessert selection, I could not eat them all, so pictures will need to suffice. They had a street taco station, made to order as you wait. The tacos were filled to the brim with meat, I had the carne asada, and al pastor. Very flavorful and tasty and the condiment bar was awesome. Guacamole was some of the freshest and best tasting ones I've tried. Their selection of noodle soup included udon, ramen, and vietnamese pho. The pho was surprisingly very tasty and tasted authentic. Our sever was hit or miss, wasn't always available for our refills but there were juices out at the buffet that quench our thirst.  Went to 2 other buffets and this one is the best.

Came here on a Tuesday night. Wait was less than an hour and got in pretty fast. The food this time wasn't as good as my first experience. 

The crabs were so small, the prime rib was extremely salty, and the sashimi was just ok.

The good part was the cocktail shrimps, they were delicious. The dessert was also very good and our server was amazing. Other than that I hope this is just a one time blip and not something that I've noticed other buffets following the trend of bad quality.

Went on Easter and was excited to try this place after my cousin raved about it. I was shocked that it cost $60 per person for a buffet but I don't mind paying for good food. I was looking forward to eating the stone crab claws after seeing pictures of it posted on Yelp except there was none. Instead of king crab legs, they had snow crab legs that hardly had any meat. Tried other foods instead and everything just tasted ok, dessert wasn't great either, won't go back.

People who leave good reviews for this buffet must have no taste bud. First, priced was over $60 for Sunday dinner price. Seafood was standard crab legs, shrimps and oyster. The oyster looked disgusting. Not fresh at all. There is a huge line for the carving of their meats and it was not worth the wait at all. Everything I ate was salty. I put bbq sauce over the ribs and I can taste the salt still. Not worth finishing. Our first server went on lunch break and his replacement came to help us out one time and never showed up again. This is the second time trying this place not because I wanted to but someone lost their cell phone in our group at Omnia and everyone wanted to eat there. I tried warning them but they didn't listen. Only give them two stars because they have decent dessert. Go elsewhere and save your money. You can thank me later.

Seriously, as good as it gets.  OMG, the crab legs, the miso seabass, the prime rib, the green tea mochi ice cream, and on and on.  Every single calorie was worth it.  I've really tried to be discriminatory with my calories as I've gotten older but this place is by far the best buffet beating Wynn hands down.  The price of course reflects that as well as the wait in the long lines.  If the wait is unacceptable when you go, there are so many other great options for dining in Caesar's that it isn't a waste to park your car and try.  Go during off hours and the likelihood of success increases.  If nothing else, stop by Payard for their absolutely fantastic everything!
We were lucky to have skipped the lunch rush but the overall quality of the food and options provided didn't seem to be worth the price. Service here was awful.

From my check list this one is on the top!!!! At least one time you have to go and if you are in a group even better because had 500 dishes so I'm pretty sure everyone will leave full and happy the price make sense because the amount of good food and desert justify the crab legs were really good.

Hands down, the best buffet in LV IMO. 

We were a party of 5. We arrived at 5:30pm on Friday since we had to catch show at 8:00 and only waited about 15 mins. The space looks small from the entrance but it extends towards the back a long ways. Overall, the quality of the food stood out for me along with the  huge variety -- seafood, italian, asian, meats, etc... Did not disappoint! The space has a modern and hip decor. They had lounge music playing in the dining area. 

Don't over eat and leave room for dessert -- not to be missed. Wished I could of just kept eating. Definitely heading back here again.

Date of visit 12/23/13 (Monday)

As good as a buffet gets.

we got there at 10am (no line) .  by the time we left about 11:45am.  there was a decent line (but similar to other buffets).

they're fried foods were off.  fried chicken was a little dry.  french fries were sitting out too long and too potatoey.

sushi wasnt that good either but no worse than any other buffet.

but everything else was better than other buffets.

and I know you can't get your money's worth eating it, but the chinese food is legit.  way better than the wynn buffet.

for holiday champagne brunch they upped the price (even though it was a monday) so don't think we'd ever pay another $44.99 (total rewards price) for what we ate.  not worth the brunch items (even though there was prime rib and crab legs)

i saw everyones comments about bone-in ribeye.  i think i'd want to come back just to eat dinner.

This buffet is simply amazing! I've been here twice and have not been disappointed. They have so much high quality food to choose from. I suggest starting from the back and work your way towards the front. Make sure to try their crab legs & ask for them to be steamed. 

My little tip for going to for dinner without paying the dinner price is to go just a little bit before 3pm (when their lunch ends & dinner starts) and pay the lunch price. It might be a little early, but just don't eat a big lunch before you go. :) 

And don't skip the dessert! They've got a giant selection of dessert to choose from.
The best buffet ever. Only 49 bucks a person for so much delicious variety! I've spent more for generic crap at the Cheesecake Factory.

Buffet so good, it has kicked me out of my review slump.

I'm not exaggerating when I say I am a Huge Fan of buffets... From the extravagantly exquisite to the questionably edible. 

In my humble opinion as a buffet connoisseur and aficionado: Bacchanal is the best Buffet I have ever had!!
From the raw bar to the special main courses, from the carving station to the desserts, from the service to the cleanliness. A perfect 5 stars. I really wouldn't change a thing!

To be honest, I used to like this place. A year later it has lost its magic. Throngs of ravenous people that don't seem like they have been fed for a week, would elbow and body slam you as they swarm the seafood station. 

Asian people who are obvi not from the U.S. Will plow right into you and keep walking, not even blinking twice for spilling a plate of food on your shirt.

The food quality has been lowered, although the ravenous mass doesn't seem to pick up on that. Shelling out $60 for lunch, i expected Bacchanal to delight my taste buds. Sadly the only taste left in my mouth is that of the foul Casino air.

I am updating them from a 4 to 4.5 stars...and here's why..

I came here for dinner, and the servers really impressed me, hence the upgrade in stars.

Meat Station:
The guy (buff and tall black guy, sorry, I didn't catch his name) who was serving the meat was really friendly, and greeted all of his guests with a smile and booming voice of "Welcome to Bacchanal!"  And he was kind enough to look for a medium-rare lamb chop upon my request.  Excellent service and hospitality.

Seafood station:
Raw oyster bar section, the guy working behind the counter was making sure that people weren't cutting in line and getting their rightful turn when it came to picking up the oysters. It shows that the workers here care about quality and fair service.

Food worth a try for dinner
Grilled Scallops
Lamb chops (ask for medium-rare)
Mochi Ice Cream (Black Sesame, a must try!)
Fried Calamari (looked good, but too stuff to have any)

I'd say best buffet in LV, thanks to the servers!

I liked this buffet ....mostly. Some of the standouts were ribeye steak, Oysters, Crab & the super amazing infused honey.
A few things that need to be better...the shrimp had an off texture & flavor about it, almost like it had been soaked in a watery chemical to make it look bigger, prime rib was just meh, no real chocolate souffle here. Warmed Chocolate Fondant Cake is not Chocolate Souffle for those of you that do not know. They had a banana flavored souffle which was terrible. Please don't tease me and say your going to have Chocolate Souffle and then try to offer me banana as if that will cover my chocolate souffle craving. This could be a huge item that would draw a lot more people in for you guys if you did it right. Easy solution - get rid of the fondant cake and make sure you have chocolate souffle everyday instead. Maybe rotate in some other flavors in addition to the chocolate like grand marnier. 
Oh yeah the lasagna was a bit on the dry side due to overcooking or being under the heater. 
I'm going to check back with them in a few weeks to see if they have made any new changes.

We had breakfast and just about all the food looked a lot better than it tasted especially for the $$$. A little less quantity and a lot more quality would better justify the price and caloric intake. .
great buffet, a must go buffet place in Las Vegas. Have a great selection of dishes from seafood, steak to Asian dish.
Yummy the food here is better than at most buffets I've been to. The deserts are really good too. I'm definitely coming back to this buffet when I'm in Vegas.

Wow, I've had my fair share of buffets in Vegas and this one holds my medal as of yet. I certainly never eat my share of buffet prices, but the quality and choices got me. There are a few themed sections such as Japanese (with sushi and soups), Chinese, Mexican, American with carving station and mini burgers & hot dogs and seafood all on it's own. Not to mention, a whole dessert bar with mini macaroons & several ice cream choices!
I enjoyed the snow crab legs as they were meaty and sliced lengthwise for easy peeling. The sushi (salmon) was good to me. I did have the stone crab legs which were quite hard to eat as the meat was stuck to the shell. If I'm not mistaken, this can be an indication of overcooking. Sweet and sour soup was pretty yummy and I've had plenty in my lifetime. The mini burgers were quite "meaty" and chosen mostly for its appearance.
Drinks (non-alcoholic) were included within the price (I only mention this because some buffets do not include beverages).

Buffet ended at 10 pm on Thursday. We arrived at 9 pm and was still seated at regular price of $51+tax/person! The food discontinued serving at 10:30 pm and was plenty of time to eat. 

Service was sufficient and pretty good. 

I'm not quite sure what the other reviews experienced, but I'm going to attribute that to really high expectations.
Food was just ok...price was expensive...nothing too special about it...I like the buffet at Cosmopolitan alot more

To me a resident from Orange County, this buffet is ok. First thing, the oyster disappointed me big time. The customers came to buffet for seafood like me showed their disappointed too. The crab leg were okay. Food are plenty and good. The only thing on points is their dessert, crepe and ice cream. With the price $50, I do not recommend this place to SEAFOOD lovers. Come here if you like Chinese food or steaks and dessert.

Probably the best place I have ate on my vegas trip. Not only is the restaurant cool as can be looking, the service was pretty darn awesome. The food was fantastic, specially for a buffet. I left this place feeling like my belly was going to implode over the casino. It's just so darn good, and so much stuff. and I only went during lunch... I could only imagine how awesome the dinner selection is. 
The food was absolutely delicious, the atmosphere was awesome, server was awesome, overall, great great great experience.

I was so looking forward to eating some delicious crab claws and was highly disappointed. The meat was soggy and adhered to the interior cartilage. Was this due to them being frozen and refrozen, I have no idea.  I went up twice and it was not edible either time. Very pricey. Excellent service staff. I will not return.

This was definitely the place I was looking forward to eating the most in Vegas. While it was a great buffet, here's why it didn't meet the hype. Before I dive into that, two tips that might help you are 1) Download total rewards app and reserve your place online. They have a kiosk at the buffet but you can do it all online with the app. The only downside is that you have to create an account. 2) Go to the buffet around 2:00pm. Not only will you pay lunch prices ($40) compared to $60 for dinner, the buffet starts bringing out dinner food around 3:00pm so you'll be able to get some "better" food while paying a lower price. A bonus is that lines are relatively short then as well!!! Now the review...

Pros:
- A wide selection ( Seafood, Carving Station, Taco / Mexican,  Asian + Sushi + Ramen, Italian, and Dessert. 
- Unlimited crab legs - 3 different types- Dungeness, Jonah, and Alaskan. Pretty good! 
- Dim sim was solid 
- Ambience was good: comfortable & clean 
- Food was constantly getting refilled 
- Good selection of desserts: Gelato, Crepe Station, cake pops, strawberries dipped in chocolate, egg tarts, assortment of pastries and fruit, etc. 

Cons: 
- Service is slow: Expect to wait 20min before being asked for drinks 
- Juice bar not available for lunch/ dinner 
- Carving station meats were dry and lacked flavor. They have several cuts such as prime rib, wagyu station, smoked brisket, lamb chops, assortment of sausages, etc but after trying a little bit of each, none were great and some were inedible. 
- None of the food was memorable 
- Sushi lacked texture and flavor. Mostly consisted of Philadelphia / California rolls. Preferred grocery store sushi tbh. 

Overall I don't regret giving this buffet a shot but in my opinion, it did not live up to the hype. If your there for a variety of food this is the place for you but don't expect high restaurant quality food - especially if your a big fan of meats.

My favorite buffet in Vegas! Lines can be long but if you have a party of 6+, there may be a shorter wait for you! They have a variety of food that range from Asian, to seafood, to meats, to noodle soups, to desserts. All sorts of delicious and filling food. Service is usually on par, depending though. 

Come hungry and with stretchy pants!

For being the #1 rated buffet in Vegas we couldn't disagree more. Chosen for our trip as my moms birthday dinner 3 months ago, super excited to come try it out. Upon arriving we had to wait over two hours to get in which was expected, not a big deal. After finally getting to go in, we sat down with our first plate and everything was terrible. Dry, cold, soggy and lacking meat inside of the crab legs and crab claws, was barely enough to taste. To be honest if I could not give a star I would not. We came in having super high expectations and left with nothing but disappointment. I would not recommend wasting $64.99 a person to eat any of this.

My favorite buffet in Las Vegas. Sandra was amazing as a server. Jorge and someone else at the meat station made sure my prime rib was perfect. Ate lunch here yesterday. Came back because it can't be beat on the Quality of food as well as service. Elaine, who sat us, was so nice and made sure we had Sandra again today. What a gem. Environment does not make you feel like you're at a buffet. Grace at the register is fast, friendly, and remembered us Five stars plus.
P.S. We went back again on Friday and experienced all these wonderful people and food before we caught our flight. The Bacchanal trifecta.

First time at this buffet. Now this what a buffet should be. Classy yet cozy, elegant and inviting. Waiters and servers all professional and very well groomed.  I highly recommend it! The food was amazing and a variety that I could not taste it all.

Their average should be 5 stars! BEST BUFFET I've ever been to! And for around $50/person you can't beat it! Well worth the wait. You get to travel the world with food! Don't expect much from the drink service but that's not why you go- you go to eat phenomenal buffet food! Everything was so fresh and delicious- excellent quality of food. The dessert stand is amazing as well. The decor was modern and really nice. They really have a great thing going here! Saw the executive chefs walking around during dinner making sure everything was in order and talking to folks in the restaurant- do not waste your time at any other place on the strip- come straight here!

This Buffett is a fat man's delight!  

We dove head on into this after a round of golf in which we were super hungry!  

Selection is mind blowing!  Seriously something for everyone!

Fried food, salad bar, meat station, pizza, Italian, Mexican, Asian, Seafood.  It's a belly buster!

I focused on the Asian and seafood.  Started it off with some Pho (pretty damm good) in a smaller bowl!  

Next I had some Ahi poki!  Something I have been missing since visiting Hawaii.  

Then I moved to a few spring rolls, some pot-stickers, some asian veg with soe Shrimp and dim sum!  

The dessert area is to die for if you are a sweet tooth!  

Year's ago I went to the All world buffet @ the Rio.  This one tops the cake!

This buffet is the best tasting I have ever had! Everything is sooo delicious. The atmosphere is really classy. The  dinner price for adults is 55 per person and it's well worth it If u want great food! I won't be going to no other buffets in Vegas but this one! Also if u want your cold shrimp sauted they will cook and season it for you and it's amazing!

Come when they open or before !! On a friday i came when they opened and the wait was 10 minutes...saturday the wait was 3 hours...not worth rushing through a buffet that cost $50+ a head...of course there is always a line for the carving station and the snow crab legs (no king crab legs here). 

Balsamic Fig Ice Cream: what a wonderful and unique combination...I jumped at the chance to try this and think it was one of the best items there 

Aztec Chocolate Ice Cream: There a kick to this one...and while it's unique I would not get this again.  

Lamb (Carving Station): well seasoned and cooked to perfection...this is a must try 

Beef Brisket: This is fall of the bone tender. One of the most popular items at the carving station and worth the wait 

The food here is all around the world but I'd say the most popular were the seafood & carving station. Dont forget to try the variety of juices which is next to the variety of breads. On top of that they also have a meat & cheese section. 

Overall this buffet has a very good variety with some stand out dishes. I'd return when the wait is shorter
Best buffet I've ever been to. The quality of every food served there is beyond any expectations I had. It's a flawless menu.

Now this is a world class buffet! I'm a big buffet lover so we made a beeline for this after hearing the rave reviews. We went on a Friday afternoon for lunch, around 2PM I think, and we only had to wait in-line for maybe 10 minutes. The restaurant is absolutely gigantic, and they have the biggest selection of food at a Vegas buffet. All of the stations are in a row at one side of the buffet, and you could easly just walk through the entire thing at once, but I personally prefer working station by station. 

We startet at the Asian station, and they had a vast selection, and I have to say that everything I tried was absolutely delicious! Next was the Italian station which was a bit smaller, with a selection of pasta and pizza. Moving on to the Mexican station, where you have a selection of toppings/sides, and a person frying up the meat you want in a burrito wrap. Not to mention, as many as you want! Second to last was the American/BBQ station, which I think was the biggest one. There was a carving station with a selection of warm meats, and the brisket was just beyond yummy! You can also choose any type of potato your heart desires, and then there's the selection of small, random things, like delicious sliders and sweet corn. The last station (or first, depends on where you start) is the seafood station. We didn't get anything there, but the station was very inviting and it looked like they had tons of fresh picks for the seafood and shellfish lover. In the middle of the room you find a big dessert station that you can walk around completly. In all honesty, I was a bit dissapointed. I'm a big chocolate lover, and they only had a few chocolate picks. I actually had a little sugarfree sticky cake type thing, and I would have never known it was sugarfree. They also have tons of ice cream, and they'll make you a cone with the flavours you want.

Now, the staff. I think I would say that this is the least friendly staff we found at a strip establishment on this trip. They weren't rude or anything, but it seemed like most of them hated their jobs and didn't try to hide it. It's probably a pretty crappy place to work with all the guests that come through, but still. 

One thing I would recommend is that if you like a certain station, get smaller portions and then come back later in your meal. They change up the selection all the time, and when they're out of one dish they replace it with something else (atleast in the dessert and grill stations). It may seem obvious if you think of the fact that they serve about 500 dishes every day, but we didn't really think it through and saw lots of exciting dishes that we hadn't tried on the way out. 

The room is very airy and spacious, and there are glass walls out towards the pool and the garden.

All in all I think this may be my favorite Vegas buffet. I'm not sure it's the best tasting food (I think I'll have to go with the Wynn buffet on that one), but the sheer selection makes it incredible. Will definetly be coming back!

I recommend coming for lunch, and on a weekday. We walked past Saturday night, and the lines were insane. Everything is also cheaper on the weekdays, and I think we paid about 35 USD pp for lunch, and I think it's 10-15 USD more on the weekend.

I was really skeptical about this "Best buffet in Vegas," after all ... it's in Caesar's. I mean it's an older casino ... it's not shiny and cool and crafty like Wicked Spoon or City Center and it's too easy to get in and out of (ha!) so ... how can it be suddenly THE BEST BUFFET in Vegas?

I was extremely impressed by Bacchanal and I only came here during a week day. I don't know how they might pull out all the stops on a weekend. That would just be insane. 

I love that all buffets in Vegas now portion control, so I could have several plates of very small things and try just about everything I *loved* my tiny tiny breakfast burrito and miniature sized belgian waffle because it allowed me to try out other goodies in their dim sum and hot foods section as well as the insane spread of desserts.

The other thing I thought was amazing was that some things don't scale well. Like it's hard to make a tiny breakfast burrito and have it hold together but contain all of the flavors of one, or a delicious moist but perfectly crunchy on the outside belgian waffle in such a small package. They really have thoroughly thought through all of their foods and the variety is astonishing.

All of the staff are extremely friendly, although I don't get the little rubber thing that they give you ... and I forgot to carry it with me at almost all times. I love that they had coffee and tea at the table so you don't have to ask for it forty times, and CREPE BAR. MADE TO ORDER.

The end.

Disclaimer is that I didn't pay for this place, I may have felt differently if I paid whatever the obscene cost was to dine here or someone I cared about paid. Totally worth it otherwise lol
Amazing! Top notch quality food. So much better than Bellagio's buffet. King crab legs, shrimp cocktail, prime rib, lamb chops, sushi, dim sum... oh and delicious desserts!

Best buffet I have at Vegas so far over the week I spent here, most food are very good but the Asian area is just extremely bad for the amount you have to pay for this place. The crab legs were ok, it all depends on your luck because some will be extremely salty. The best food are the carved beef, and the desert.

This is definitely my all-time favorite buffet in Las Vegas. People should not leave Vegas without spending their precious savings here. I promise that investment is well worth the food you'll consume while at Bacchanal. 

With what seems like an endless array of delicious food, Bacchanal comes out on top simply because of the quality AND quantity it serves. (Those crab legs also play a large part, but hey) The prime rib, bison, pasta, salad, sushi, ribs, chicken and waffles, the list can just go on and on. It's never ending. Kind of puts other buffets to shame when most are trying hard to maximize profits with less-than-stellar products. 

But that line doe...it's long. Better play some slots or blackjack while you're at it...or be like us and go in a big group. For some reason they favor bigger tables and will escort you to another line. Instead of waiting for 2 hrs, we waited basically 20 minutes before having a table with a superb view of the fountains outside. Talk about service! 

Buffet itself is decorated splendidly, and it really makes you feel like you just spent $63.04 for the champagne brunch all well worth it. Attentive servers constantly bringing endless mimosas and drinks, while the seafood bar kept pumping out crab legs and oysters. Hey, there were even crawfishes and mussels too! 

Grab dessert and a built-to-order crepe station (that rivals Paris's buffet) and oh wait, there's guava juice, mango juice and horchata in mason jars? OH GIRLS YOU ARE IN FOR A TREAT! WIN WIN!

Bacchanal, come to me oh mighty buffet king!

First of all I want to praise the wait staff and manager I dealt with. Alvaro (waiter) and Fred (manager) did a wonderful job helping to make sure the dinner was more than satisfactory. I went this Christmas and I expected there to be a long wait but I didn't expect they would be out of some of their signature dishes like bone marrow. I also didn't expect to be in another line for lobster that took 30min for dry lobster tail. For a high end buffet it is designed very poorly and lacked many basics like roasted veggies. Not something I would do again.

Wow! As much as I loved Wicked Spoon, I have to admit this is by far my favorite buffet in Vegas! I was blown away at the variety of dishes they had. The spread was amazing. Bacchanal also compliments each genre of food well. For example, the seafood bar had raw oysters, ceviche, and shrimp cocktail; the bbq section had various grilled/bbq'd meats with a variety of sauces; there was a mexican section that had various types of hot sauces and salsas.

I was impressed by three sections in particular. One, their juices (yep, it's kind of weird) were extraordinary. Though they weren't chilled the point that I would like them, the freshly squeezed orange juice was to die for! I must have had at least 6 bottles of it myself. Two, the pastas were very good for a buffet. Would I pay $33 for a plate of it in a fine dining restaurant? No but I would have paid $20, so I still see the value in this station. Lastly, I oddly enjoyed their sushi station. They actually had nigiri sushi and sashimi and the quality of the fish wasn't bad! I enjoyed their creativity in the types of sushi as well.

What was nice about our visit is that we meant to arrive for brunch though we arrived late and ended up paying the lunch price. But since they do not close between meals, we enjoyed the best of both worlds. We ate so much it actually became our dinner as well.... I know, gluttony at its finest.

Like any other "must try" buffet, the wait was long (40 minutes+) and you have to check in using their computer kiosk to enter your cell phone number.  

They have a huge variety to choose from: crab, lamb. steak, noodle soup, taco station, nachos, sushi, pasta, etc ...  and tons of desserts.  

Don't get me wrong, it is beautiful, food presentation is very nice, and they offer lots to choose from with a sprinkle of "gourmet sounding/looking food," but for the price that we paid, I expected more. The good was good, but nothing to rave about.  For the price you pay, I would rather go to a nice sit down restaurant.  But hey, it's a buffet in Vegas, and I'm full.

I don't normally buffet, but when I do... Bacchanal is where it's at

I'm not a huge buffet person but this one is quality.  I've been to most of the popular ones in Vegas, but this is definitely my favorite.  Not only is quality there, I'm loving the beautiful presentation and excellent customer service.  Last time I came, was a Thursday around 5:30pm and we came right before the rush.  Me and two other people just walked right up to the counter to pay.  Once I turned around there were already about 30 people in line.  Suckers =)

For around $50 a person it's damn worth it.  I like the organization of the place.  It's divided into different stations.  There is an Asian, Italian, Mexican, Japanese, meats, seafood, and dessert station.  They literally had everything and the way the buffet is set up made it easy to go around.  Props to the chefs for everything being so well done and beautifully.  

They sat us by the impressive dessert bar.  It was literally a bar that wrapped all the way around.  I think I saw at least 3 people video record the desserts walking around it.  LOL.  Kids went crazy over it.  They had all types of cakes, cupcakes, macarons, chocolates, ice cream, chocolate covered goodies, pastries, creme burlee, and candies.  However, my favorite thing at Bacchanel was their seafood station.  Their raw oysters were to die for.  I also loved that the crab was pre-sliced for your ease and they had hot butter to dip.  I'm not huge on meats, but their meat station was very impressive.  They even had lamb chop!  A few of my other favorite items that are worth mentioning are their ravioli in the tin cup, their fishes, and their Asian soups.  I wish I could have been less full so I can try everything.

The inside is very large.  The tables and chairs are comfortable and it's easy to get around.  You get a view of the Caesar pool too so that isn't bad.  Overall, Bacchanel is the best buffet in Vegas.  You must go.

Came to LV for work and decided I wanted to have Bacchanal this time around. Table for 1! Was a tad awkward waiting in line alone, but buffet calls. I came to LV 2 weeks prior, but went to the Bellagio buffet. It was cheaper, but did not leave me satisfied. I have been to the Bacchanal plenty of times before (5x at least) and have never been too fond of it. Buffets never leave a good impression as I go believing every dish should be amazing. Fortunately this time, it lived up to the hype. I lost the rest of the food pics but at least got the dessert.
From memory, all the meat selection were great. Prime rib was awesome as well as all the crab legs. Their lamb was pretty good as well. It still has the lamb flavor, but if you actually aren't disturbed by it, its worth it. Their laksa soup noodle was delicious. If I got that broth outside at a restaurant, I'd be happy.

Special shout out to Bacchanal for having black sesame gelato. Wow, it was amazing. They had Ube also which was good too. Wish I saved stomach to try ALL of them, although my dessert plate might have been too much for a party of 1.

Everything this time tasted good if not great. Few items were meh, but it was probably due to being left out too long and dried up (sliders).

If there's one buffet I know everybody was raving about, it was the Bacchanal buffet located just inside Caesars. First, get your rewards card for discounts. Also, as soon as you go in, they'll ask to take your photo and will try to sell you the photo. 

They have a variety of cuisines in this buffet, but personally I thought it was okay. The seafood was absolutely delicious, however I thought they could have done better with the Asian cuisine as the food tasted a bit plain there. It also was not very accommodating for vegetarians, but then again I'm not sure if Vegas is really vegetarian friendly. The line ups may seem long, but it goes by really fast. 

No extra charges for drinks, and the staff there are extremely friendly.

Make sure you save room for the desserts tho! 

Personally, I was expecting more since everybody kept raving about it. I found it just as good as the Bellagio buffet.

In my opinion, the very best items at the buffet are the following: duck, waffle fries, sausage(not the jalapeño), burger shooters, miso soup self serve, crepes and lastly the sorbet. I appreciated the selection and the exotic foods, but some were mediocre. I am especially picky because I pride myself on eating excellent food on vacations, and with that said, I feel that most of the food could be better. The service was excellent; I enjoyed having the coffee pot at our table as well.

Bacchanal is fancy and overpriced and did not live up to they hype for me, however there are many nice dishes.  My favorites were spicy sausage, chicken enchiladas, meat and cheese platter, Mac and cheese, and seafood orzo. As for the downsides:  the plates were wet and smelled fishy, the fried rice was hard, the music was way too loud, and the hot dog buns were hard.  Some things were not as fresh as it could have been.  Anyway it's good to try this buffet once.

Very well organized, and just a good vibe overall.

I love buffets because I just like being able to try everything, and tossing it aside if I don't like it... It's terrible, I know. But in my opinion, buffet food really isn't THAT good. It's just nice to have unlimited of whatever you'd like to eat. It's nice because Bacchanal does a good job providing their customers with a wideeeeee range of food. Example for their "asian" food section, they serve sushi, dim sum, udon, pho, and a bit of others.

I pretty much tried everything and wasted a bunch of food.... butttt I'll just talk about the things that stood out to me...

I really enjoyed their hot Crab legs, they have the cold ones up front, but the hot ones are near the back. It's kind of hidden. There's just a guy standing there in front of 2 big pots and if you walk up to him, he'll pack a whole plate of crab legs for you. 

Their mini red velvet pancakes were soooo cute! They were garnished with some fresh berries, and they looked absolutely amazing. However sadly, they were not good at all...

I reallyyyy like their Guava Agua Frescas.. (the pink one, just in case). I probably drank around 5 of them....?? And they were providing complimentary mimosas (they're actually pretty strong!) which I would down half of and fill the glass with some guava juice to adjust it to my liking. I had about.... 5 of those too... .____. 

There little xiao long baos weren't that good at all. I would pass on those if I went again.

I didn't try their meat because the line was so long, but my friends who did... they didn't like it very much.

Everyone raves about how amazing their dessert bar is, and yeahhh it's cool. Has a crepe maker dude, gelato, fresh fruits, and a whole variety of little cakes and such. But I couldn't get myself to finish anything.... BUT I DID eat most of the flan I got. THAT was pretty darn good.

If you wanna do a buffet in Vegas, this is the place to do it. I've done the Wynn and Paris, and this is definitely the best (sorry Wynn). 

The worst part of this buffet is the wait. You put your name and number into an electronic ticker, then they give you a wait time (about 2 hours) and then you'll get a text 1 hour later to come back, and then you wait in line again for 1 hour to actually get in. Prices are steep but to be expected. Dinner was around 60+ including tip.

Some drinks are included! Mimosas and bloody marys, from what I can recall (we went on Sunday around 3pm). Bloody mary was good, and apparently there was a build your own bloody mary fixin's bar which I never found...

Things I loved: Dim sum (Har gow), duck, oysters, FRESH KING CRAB LEGS (it's in the hot food section near the italian food, don't get the ones in the cold seafood section), all the cheeses, al pastor street tacos, smoked brisket.

Things I would avoid: ceviche (not enough seafood in it), crawfish, mini burgers, crepes (gross and not enough filling), sangria bread pudding (REALLY GROSS).

Everything else falls in the "good but not great but not bad" category. 

The quality of food is the best in Vegas for a buffet. In terms of my waistline and time, I don't think I'll be returning too often unless I'm trying to gain 5 lbs for some reason.

Okay so I'm writing this sitting here in the buffet. That's how bad this is. Really disappointed with the food selection. Way too bland and so far the only thing that has been good was a Strawberry cupcake I just devoured. Not to mention I nearly had a heart attack when I had to pay $40 just for me! Way overpriced for the quality of food. Service was great which is why I gave it 2 stars rather than 1. Food = NO!

This place is not for the faint of heart.  It is gluttony paradise!  There's a ton of food prepared with expertise and care.  It is definitely well worth the price:  $52.99 per adult and 24.99 per child (dinner prices).  

Everything is great, but the crab legs rule them all.  I have eaten at many of the "high end" buffets and the one thing and I am constantly disappointed with are the crab legs, but not here.  Ironically, I did not get any pictures of these because I was too busy stuffing my face with the sweet, delectable meat of the crustacean persuasion.  It just tasted so fresh like it was just fished right out of the water and the butter was clear and dispensed out of what looks to be a stainless steel fancy water dispenser.  I just figured that was ingenious since I hate having to deal with ladeling hot melted butter into a small container typical in other buffets.  Not to mention, it just seems more hygienic since no one else can actually "touch" the butter.  

The Mexican cuisine was delicious.  The street tacos are amazingly delicious and the ramen was unexpectedly authentic tasting.  I was the most surprised by the ramen having tasted a fair share in my lifetime.

Overall, everything was amazing.  Well, almost everything.  The one thing I do think Bacchanal is weak on is the dessert department.  It was very standard:  nothing horrible, but nothing memorable either.  I do have to say that The Wicked Spoon over at the Cosmopolitan has the dessert thing down.  However, I think both places are equally good and well-rounded in terms of variety and quality of dishes.  I will definitely be returning to Bacchanal Buffet, but I will make sure to come really hungry to maximize my dollar.

Came here for the inflated holiday priced weekday dinner. Was the food worth 65 pp? No. Was it worth the Bacchanal experience, waiting over 2.5 hours to get seated? Yes. It's just a must when you go to Vegas.

Yes, 5 stars. Enter a buffet that gives you 5 cultures, American, Italian, Asian, Mexican, and coastal (sea food) galore! I have been to the Wynn (delicious, was my favorite) but this place tops them. The PRICE is the highest for that reason. Yet there will not be an item you choose that won't be exquisite in your mouth. Examples: (sushi, poke, Italian Gaspacho, t-bone lamb, fresh dumplings, king crab and pacific oysters till you drop). You Will be PLEASED.

+Oyster shooters and crab legs!!!
+Dessert is amazing.
+So much variety, there's definitely something for everyone

-Sugar-free desserts don't taste like anything
-They don't warn you when you have to wait for things to cook....like the crab legs. So you just wait until they're ready for you again :\

It's ~$30 for brunch during the weekdays and closer to $45 during weekends. $50 for dinner. BUT. If you stick around the seafood section, the amount of crab legs and oysters and oyster shooters you get makes the price TOTALLY worth it. 
The desserts are amazing. Definitely get a crepe and some of their mousse creations. The tiramisu is to die for! 
They even have dim sum as part of their buffet! Win!

This is one of the better buffets in Vegas.  The foods are better quality.   My favorite thing to eat here are the oysters and crab legs.  They have really fresh oysters and I like to dip it in the jabenero salsa from their salsa bar.  I also liked that they served their crab legs cold or hot.  Also if you are a meat eater, this buffet offers great selections lambs,  prime ribs and etc.  The only bad thing that I have to say is that if you are not a platinum reward members then the wait is really long.  Also be prepared to spend some money cause the price is pretty high for a Vegas buffet.
RIDICULOUSLY GOOD!! Everything there is off the charts good. Even foods that I normally don't like I tried and enjoyed. Definitely a place to stop by and try. The wait is a little long, but Worth it.

Super happy.  Selections are endless. Many vegetarian options too!   Almost $130 for two.  Come empty.  We skipped lunch that day and just had breakfast.  No waiting at 5pm.  But when we left an hour later a huge line had formed.

Sadly, the quality at Bacchanal has dwindled since it started. The biggest hit is supposed to be the fresh oysters, but they were nasty as hell when I went. 

However, the best seafood dish would be the hot crab legs! Don't even have to wait in a line AND you're given a FULL plate! Best thing in the whole buffet!

Also, the juices! No, I don't mean the juices offered by the waiters. I'm talking about the ones at the station: guava, pineapple, horchata (not a juice but w/e), etc. These are soooo good, and you definitely can't find these at other places.

The copious amounts of desserts are also not to be messed with. So many choices of gelato are available! They even added shaved ice (hawaiian ice style) to the mix as well with toppings such as red beans, popping boba, and mochi. 

Overall, the food and selection is great! But, the quality is not as good as when it first started.

Wow. What an amazing time with Lexie as our 
L hostess with the most us and our server Maria they gave us everything we ever need it, but at the same time made us feel welcome to a place that we would never forget five stars +10 every day

GREAT variety of MEDIOCRE foods. Service was great, but definitely not worth the price. I don't understand the hype about this place AT ALL. The raw oysters were not edible. I took a bite and had to spit it out right away. Definitely regret this place. I'd rather pay the same amount of money for one amazing meal than ever to come back.

One of my favorite buffets in Vegas! They never disappoint and I can get my fill of crab legs without judgement. They have a pretty good meat selection as well (briskets, ribs, prime rib, sausages, etc) I like the street tacos, and the chicken chile verde with some tortilla chips. They have a pretty legit Asian food selection too. Pho or ramen.. However, I went with my bf tonight and he said the meat in the pho tasted and smelled funny so beware. My favorite part of the buffet besides the seafood section are the desserts!! They have EVERYTHING. Chocolate covered strawberries, gelato, macaroons, cupcakes, cookies, fruit, cakes, and the best part... Make your own crepe station. Every time I'm in Vegas, I try to make a stop here.

OMG where do I even start. Gluttony is one of the 7 deadly sins, and I sure as hell planned on committing it in Sin City. It's times like these when I wish I was a cow, and had 4 stomachs. But alas, I do not but I sure ate like a cow. For a $45 dollar dinner, you'd be a fool to not eat like one! This is not a time to be faithful to your diet. This is a time to cheat cheat cheat because well, you paid for it. 

Located in the Caesars Palace, I was so excited to try this buffet out. I drove from LA to Vegas, and made sure not to eat breakfast or lunch before getting to Vegas. I suggest not eating for at least the whole day if you come for dinner because with all the food here, you'll want to be hungry. 

When I first saw the line, the first thing I wanted to do was RUN. I was so surprised it was long because I went on a Tuesday. It looked like a line from a theme park! I can't even imagine the lines on weekends.  I was in starvation mode and the line just made me so sad. But I decided to stay and it was worth it. The line went by surprisingly fast and before I knew it we were seated after about 20 minutes. 

This was the biggest best buffet I've ever been too.  Their food is divided into sections like Seafood, Mexican, Asian, Italian, and American.  I like how they serve the food in small portions so you can try a lot of different food.

My favorite thing there was the shrimp cocktail on steroids! They were the juiciest biggest shrimp cocktail I've ever seen. SO GOOD. There was a station with all types of meats that they cut for you but the line was so long so i didn't even bother.  I decided to get the tacos instead, and they were just as good as the tacos I get from LA trucks. The pasta that I tried like lasagna and rigatoni was amazing too. All the food was such good quality. They had cute little drinks in glass bottles near the Mexican station. I helped myself to unlimited horchata and mango juice.

After driving through 4 hours of endless desert to get from LA to Vegas, I was so relieved to see endless DESSERT! They have gelato and endless mochi, and a crepe station where you can make your own crepes.  On top of that they had cake pops, chocolate covered strawberries, and red velvet woopie pies, a million types of cake, and the best part was UNLIMITED MACARONS. Macarons are usually almost $2 each in other places, and here I could eat as many as I please. They were just as good as the ones at the restaurants too.

Me and my friends stayed a full 2 hours stuffing our faces, and I pretty much had to be rolled out of there.  Hands down the best buffet in Vegas.

Better, IMO, than The Wicked Spoon and The Buffet at the Wynn.

We did have to wait a long time, and the seating area isn't as large as the wicked spoon, but your selection was huge - especially for fish--and I honestly don't think I tried a bland, dry, old, not fresh item.

My favorite items follow in order:

1. The prime rib.
2. The mochi ice cream.
3. The lamb.
4. The crepe bar.
5. All the other desserts.
6. All of your breads.

I'll tell you why I think this place deserves two stars. Quality vs Quantity. Any buffet has a great selection of food, but not everything will be great because there is too much to focus on. But a little more effort from the chefs could've make this place worth going to. FYI $55 per person....

Main courses-
Dim sum-DRY DRY DRY 
Thai Curry Noodles-DRY 
Lamb-over cooked and DRY
Jook(Chinese soup)- Taste like water and paper 
Crawfish-cold and needed more season. Crawfish is suppose to be warm/hot *even the butter dip is cold and tasteless 

Dessert (this is so disappointing) 
Crepe station was the best part, can't go wrong.
Lemon meringue-good
Apricot tapioca flavorless, taste like your chewing styrofoam
Creme brûlée- vanilla bean? Don't think so, more like no flavor brûlée. How do you go wrong with custard? 
Soap Bar shaped cheesecake- haha this was cute because it's the shape of a soap bar. But no flavor either.

I would say all the desserts in the little cups are gross, they need to spend more time making them taste better. How can you go wrong with these simple desserts? Just add more sugar haha.


My overall experience was 5/10. Due to over pricing on below average food. And two stars for having seafood and having a big selection of food.

This is still my favorite buffet in Vegas for the quality and selection but I definitely noticed some areas where they can improve.  This is better than wicked spoon hands down if you're comparing.  The options for meat and seafood are overwhelming.  They have hot and cold snow crab legs.  King crab legs are not available to everyone, only diamond members and up. This was a little disappointing since there's a sign that says snow and king crab legs at the seafood station...a little misleading.  Also, the souffle oven was broken when we visited...which was one thing I was looking forward to.  However, this time around noticed the addition of american wagyu beef.  The meat was very tender and flavorful.  The bone marrow topped with short rib was really enjoyable as well.  The Asian offerings of duck and roast pork and dim sum were all done well.   There were other options like frog legs, lamp chops, soft shell crab that you definitely do not see anywhere else. The steamed crab legs were also delicious, although I wish these were split in half like the cold ones.  The cold ones were so cold...literally ice....not edible....eek... The hot butter couldn't even defrost them =(  The sweets station is another overwhelming station but full of good options.  I particularly enjoyed the creme brulee, matcha covered chocolate strawberries, and matcha cake.  If you want to let your friends have the full Vegas buffet experience, this is the place to go.   Pro tip: go at 2-2:30 on the weekend, pay brunch price and overlap into dinner (starts at 3 but full selection of dinner items is probably not ready until 4:00).  You will get to see an even bigger selection of options.  Even better if you go with a party of 6 or more....separate line for bigger parties.

GREAT restaurant. The bbq and seafood were amazing. Mexican was good. Chinese so so. But, definitely GREAT. Only reason I didn't give 5 stars was the price. $62.50 per person was a little steep. But no complaints.
blows Wynn buffet out the water..highly recommend everything here is fantastic buy get there early gets real crowded but we'll worth the wait

The food is definitely good here but I don't know if it's worth it for the long line up. There were a few stand out dishes but a lot of just alright dishes. My boyfriend got his money worth in eating the crab legs but I really enjoyed the fish dishes. The waiter was absolutely fabulous. He's a better waiter than waiters at restaurants that require more in terms of service. It's a buffet that you should try at least once if you're in Vegas.
Salty foods   overpriced buffet. Not worth it. I think ALL the foods are salty.. especially the meats and seafoods.. uggggggghhhhh!!!!!!!!!! We need a refund

If you are in Las Vegas, it is a must go place to eat!  They have lamb chops, pizza, Pasta, Chicken tenders w. fries, seafoods, curry, soups just to say a few!  My favorite of all "DESSERTS"!  
$59.00 per person is worth it.

We love this buffet, and we come here every time we are in Vegas. Huge variety of food and it is delicious. This resto went above and beyond to make the dishes authentic. Ceasar Palace brought chefs from the respective countries to cook authentic dishes. Make sure to save space for desserts because they were pretty good as well. 
The service is a hit and miss. Most of the time, it's great, but this around, it wasn't. The waitress kept forgetting  things, and we had to ask numerous times for the same thing.

I will give this a five star when it should be 4.5 but it's all good. Ever since I found out about this buffet, every time I go to Vegas I eat here once. It is probably one of the more expensive buffets on the strip, but you pay what you get. What you get is a whole lot, from Asian cuisines to Italian to southern to Mexican to seafood towers to desserts, you will find something in this buffet. Wait time is usually pretty long but they have machines where you can put in your number and they will text you when the table is ready.

So much food to choose from!  My favorite was their dimsum station and dessert.  We got there at 11ish and was in line for maybe 5mins and waited to be seated for another 5mins. However,  around noon,  the line got busier so better come earlier if you're on a tight schedule.  We paid $54ish and that doesn't include the drinks.  Place decor was so fancy and creative I felt like we we're fine dining.
I was underwhelmed and sad at this buffet. I love food and flavor and I did not find it here. I suggest you go to another restaurant.

They can get one star from me is because the staff otherwise I would give no star if I could for the food. I bought " buffet on buffet " on 2/1 super bowl night, and enjoy very nice buffet at Rio (carnival world buffet). I had very high expectations for Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars, because all the good commands left at yelp.
They are asking 25 dollars more for upgrade. That's just bad. Then shrimp cocktails all had very black tails and tasted squishy. I had to spit it out. Chinese food too salty. Then tried to eat something I would not normaly eat at buffet ... The cheese burger. All the burgers had dry cheese. They were so dry you can crack them like crackers. Finally the fruit none of them were cut right. Pineapple with skin. I would say DO NOT waste you time (always waitinglong line ) and money at this place. You would find Rio and Spicy Market have much better quality and tasty food.

This buffet was amazing! The food was great and fresh! It's definitely pricy so expect to pay over 100$ for two people. But you get what you pay for. They had every type of food and it was amazing! They also had a great dessert bar that had every dessert you could imagine! 
The only negative comment I have is that the line to enter the restaurant was HUGE. we waited over 25 minutes just to get inside after we initially paid. The staff seemed a little overwhelmed and kind of held us there in line. When we finally got a table, there were a bunch of empty clean tables around so I'm not so sure what the hold up was! But that's my only gripe. I would wait in line that long again to eat there cause it was so yummy!
Bacchanal buffet and wicked spoon are a must stop in Vegas! Delicious food with great presentation!!
Boo.... I was so excited to come here to eat again but I can tell Over time this place went downhill :( quality is no longer there.

There is not even one item on the buffet that is exceptional and I would go back for it.

One item I was searching in the Buffett was barbecued pulled pork. Which I never found. There wasnt even the old fashioned Ice cream on the Buffett, instead there were sorbet and gelato... 

Definitely not worth $60 or waiting 150mins... 

$50 burger at Ramsay's restaurant would have been more classy and pleasant...

This buffet has one of the most offerings I have ever seen in a buffet! They had 3 kinds of crab legs, crawfish, oysters, wagyu beef, ribeye steak, prime rib, ham, turkey, ribs, lamb, siu mai, har gow, roast duck, roast pork, char siu, and a whole bunch of other great stuff! Their food is exceptional and deserts are phenomenal. You get free beer and wine. The decor is fantastic for a buffet. It feels like you're dining in a fine restaurant. Prices kinda high, though, at almost $55 a head, but what the heck for this kind of experience! Great atmosphere, delicious food and they even take your picture which you can purchase for twenty big ones. What else could you ask for? Oh, by the way, the lines to get in are extremely long, so go early. Holiday season, the wait is darn near 5 to 6 hours, I kid you not.

Amazing buffet. It was my second time eating here yesterday and it did not disappoint. I went with friends in town for dinner so the price on a Sunday was a hefty $55 but it did not disappoint. First time I was here was back in November on a Saturday early noon and the line was about a 20 minute wait. Yesterday, Sunday around 4:30pm there was no wait in line at all, but there was a rush of people whe we concluded our meal. 

On my first trip to this buffet, I had one of the best cooked prime ribs I'd ever had. On my second trip here, I strayed away from that and instead focused more on the seafood.

Presentation was unlike anything I've seen before. They had tiny little cute buckets of wings or fried chicken pieces with fries. The lasagna was served on a tiny skillet with a decent amount of meat and the sauce, was UNBELIEVABLE. The chef's special was also served on a tiny cute little iron pan and it was a lightly breaded calamari.

On my first trip, I thought the shrimps were bigger and the king crab legs were small portions and were also very salty. But I realized this was only because it was busier back in November when I went as there was a 5min wait to get the king crabs. This second time around, there was alot less of a wait and I just realized the workers there can serve you warmed up king crab that is dipped in hot water. I got my king crab served this way this time around and they were far less salty and on point and of course, dipped it in the melted butter!! 

In the seafood section I also enjoyed the baked salmon, pan seared halibut, mussels, half shell oysters, corn lobster bisque, the large shrimp, and an amazing oyster shooter! 

Instead of prime rib, I thought I'd try the pork ribs and the lamb chops. The chops were amazing and very juicy! The pork ribs, on the other hand were not so much. 

I was hoping for standing chocolate ice cream but they had one that had cinnamon that I wasn't too big a fan of. 

Overall, this place is highly recommended by me if you have friends in town.

Ok buffet but unfortunately I do not think it is worth the price you pay.

I will go through this review station by station.

1) Asian Station: All of the food was decent enough and tasted like your run of the mill Chinese take out.  They did have strange pouchy things with meat in them that were ok.  Maybe I was there at a bad time, but the food tasted old.  My fiance liked it, but she is Asian.  Getting an Asian to like Asian food is like getting a dollar bill into a stripper's g-string (it isn't that hard).
2) Carving Station: Brisket was very very fatty and tough.  It seemed very rushed as though they didn't have time to cook it properly or to trim the fat.  The pulled pork sliders were very good though and actually the highlight of the entire buffet.  But, the brisket was a disappointment.  I walked up to the station and said "I want some brisket" and the guy gave me a rectangle of lard and fat.  I then said "no...not lard...brisket."  Yeah...it was that bad.
3) Pizza Station: The pizza was actually decent.  It was cooked in an actual pizza oven, and honestly I ate the pizza more than anything.  My fiance thumbed her nose at me thinking I was a peasant eating something so juvenile like pizza.  I needed to remind her that she did not have air conditioning until about 5 years ago....so I think our degree of class is about even at this point.
4) Seafood Station: I heard there were crabs here and I was looking all over for them at this station.  No crabs....it seems the crabs were served later.  Instead they had crawfish, which were horrific (I am cajun) and some oysters (which I am not crazy enough to try).  You want to try raw oysters at a buffet then be my guest, but I will not pay for your investment in 2-ply toilet paper.  
Then....suddenly....the crab legs are served!!!  People jumped on them like they had "hot and cold runnin blondes" in them.  I do not know what that saying means, but I hear rednecks say it when something seems good.  Anyway, I grabbed some crab legs.  They were cold.....like iced down cold.  Weird, but I like cold seafood...and they were already cracked open for you.  Pretty cool.  Holy crap these things were full of salt.  Tons of salt.  That is all you could taste from these crab legs was salt.  Certainly this was a mistake right?  They couldn't be this salty on purpose could they?

Big disappointment, but probably one of the better buffets on the strip....which is a sad state of affairs.  Go here if you want to experience a buffet and are starving....that is the only way you will make your money back.  Apparently I lost some class street cred.....thanks Bacchanal.

Can't express how amazing this dinner buffet was!  Spending the same amount at another restaurant would only get you 1 dish & a glass of wine.  Here it's all gourmet, & as much as you want of whatever you want!  Awesome cheese, great crab legs freshly steamed, beautiful & delicious desserts!

First attempt to come here was last Thanksgiving. 3 Hour wait, um no thank you. Finally able to hit up this place in July and I have to say, this place is top two along with the buffet at the M resort. When you have smoked BBQ at a buffet, you had me at hello. Typical new concept Vegas buffet with stations from around the world. The kicker is that the food is actually good and your a not wasting it by taking a bite and throwing away the rest. Granted the 1st time I came here i had the runs 4 hours later (I'm guessing it was the pastrami at greenfield deli NYNY casino). Was hoping it was a fluke so came back a month later and I was a ok. Bacchanal and Studio B buffet, you are the reason I waste my money on food and not gambling.

If I could give this buffet 0 stars, I would. After seeing the great reviews on yelp, we attended during Thanksgiving weekend and my husband and I waited on line for about 4.5 hours. Checked in with the kiosk and came back 2.5 hours later to the time printed on the receipt and still had to wait another 2 hours on the line. On top of that we paid $69 a person and it was RIDICULOUSLY overpriced. Good luck eating here if you don't eat a lot of seafood or meat in general because that's all they carry. Save your time and money and check out some other buffet that has more variety, better presentation and better tasting food for the amount of $$ you spend!!

4th of July weekend recap:
*Waited 1.5 hours on a Friday night to get seated.
*Paid 60 bucks. (usually 50 for dinner but they jacked up the price bc it was a holiday)
*Stuffed our faces in 45 minutes to make it in time for our 10pm Cirque show.

I'm not much of a buffet girl because I always end up stuffing my face to the point of gluttony to get my money's worth.  Plus my eyes are bigger than my stomach and the whole eat slowly and wait 15 minutes deal  goes out the window.   But when in Sin City, gotta hit up at least 1 buffet!

Yays:
* A variety of food to choose from from and the quality is better than most buffets One yelper mentioned there are 9 stations.  I saw people at the stations cooking nonstop so the food is fresh.
* They have macarons, cake pops, gelato and mochi!!!!! ( Tried it all except the cake pops and they were deelish)
* The sweet potato fries and fried chicken baskets
* The seafood (they'll even warm your crab legs for you), Italian and Asian stations
* Prime rib, kolbi sliders and kalbee ribs
* Our waitress was really nice and apologized for our wait.  She kept our water glasses filled and was really quick with clearing our table.  Maybe too quick. haha
* Crepe station
* Nice presentation and gourmet looking


Nays:
*The ramen/pho/udon station is exciting to see but the taste is meh.  Disappointed.
* Mexican station looked a bit unappealing for some reason so I passed right by it. But I liked how they offered dishes I don't usually see at buffets like pozole, tamales, street tacos, corn and sopes.  Maybe I'll try it next time.
*The long wait.  Def. avoid the prime dinner time of 6-8 if you don't want to wait.
* Jacking up the price during holidays- well I suppose this isn't their fault, gotta make up for the tons of customers to feed I guess...
Came here on vacation and the food amazing, huge selection and great seafood cant wait to comeback in town will eat here again.

Tried this place out after reading all the hype.  I'm underwhelmed.  So first of all, we're there for Easter weekend so for whatever reason they charged $60 a head.  Alright fine, I knew going in this was one of the expensive buffets but I could not tell if they had any specialty food that they don't normally serve.  

All of the Yelp reviews and pictures tell of food that is NOT guaranteed to be there.  So do not get your hopes up with what you read here.  It looked like the usual buffet slop... Seafood, American, Italian, Asian, salad, dessert.  I did not get a chance to try the asian food but I heard it was good.  The rest of the food was "meh".

Nice try but Wicked Spoon is still better.

I can't imagine finding a better buffet. We researched the best buffets in Vegas and this one came up, repeatedly. At over $50 a pop (for dinner), it seemed expensive for a buffet. However, it worth every dime. Amidst all of the glitz, glamor, and bullshit- this meal is actually money well spent in Las Vegas.

The only way to try a little bit of everything is to have a dinner partner that will share things on your plate with you. We tasted food from every international station and were very pleased with the flavors, variety, and overall quality of food. The trick is take several trips (we made 9 total each) and make small plates each time. On our 7th and 8th trips, before dessert, we took 2nd round trips to the items we really loved.

The highlights were: crab legs, the whole asian set, charcuterie, and the truffled potato gratin. And the waygu beef sliders were awesome. 

We received excellent service. Plates cleared each time we got up for another round, and our iced teas and water were filled constantly. 

We recommend going at 5pm to avoid lines. The seating system they have in place somehow makes is feel casual and not like a feeding frenzy, which is tricky but they seem to pull it off. 

The only thing we would've liked to see was salt and pepper on the table.

All and all- this place is worth the money and wait. If you don't pig the fuck out on the first and second round, you can actually enjoy all of the stations and not leave feeling sick.

TWO THUMBS UP. WORTH IT.

First impression: 
The line process, you have to get a ticket to go into the payment line, which could take time before getting into that line. Our wait was 20 mins. (Received a text to allow us to join the line), It's really not clear what is expected until you wait in line to speak to the person managing the line. 
After paying for your food, you take a picture (cost is $20, if you want to purchase) before being seated. Oh there is a 2 hour limit to eat and go.

Price per person: $55.99

Service:
Everyone was extremely nice! Loved the customer service!

Food:
The area was clean and the food was good. Since we were looking for Crab Legs specifically we hoped for all we could eat. Unfortunately, we were disappointed with the amount of crab legs received on our plate (literally 3 or 4 legs) and when we opened them a lot of the legs were empty. 
I know it's a buffet and you can keep going up but the inconvenience of the back and forth was annoying. Not to mention, there was a wait on the crab legs. You will see in my video the inventory was very slim.
The other food items were good but not worth the price.


Overall:
I wouldn't recommend this place since there are other buffets that can offer the same quality food selection. Hey it's Vegas buffets are everywhere. 

Unless you were like us and just wanted the experience GO FOR IT, but don't say I didn't warn you.

The best buffet you'll ever have in your life. Great people, great service and certainly great food. 
Everything is great about this place. You should not skip it if you're in town.

wow!!! best buffet in vegas so far. like how you enter your info for the ticket and come back to check in via sms, and wait wasn't to bad. said 2hrs,but luck was on our side i guess so we checked in about 30-40min. 

i was very pleased with the option of hot king crab legs. most buffets do cold, and it gets boring. oh, and their black pepper saute rock/dungeoness crabs are a must!!!!
oysters were fresh and sweet, cocktail shrimp plump and sweet. 

a must for vegas again on my calendar next year

This buffet reigns supreme. It used to be Wynn and bellagio but this buffet is a game changer. Fresh, quality ingredients. Diverse selections. Creative dishes. Gluttony at its best. I don't remember how many times I've been here but it seems like it's almost tradition every time I'm in vegas. I do like that they changed the waiting system. Instead of making you stand in a 2 hour line, they give you a ticket and tell you to come back around a certain time.  Is it cheap? Definitely not. But the food is completely worth every penny. The staff here is always very nice and accommodating. Impeccable cleanliness. Words can't describe how awesome this place is.

Went the week before Christmas.  The line was pretty short.

One of the better buffets in Las Vegas.  Very pricey.

My favorite items; Beef Brisket, Shrimp, Lobster Corn Chowder, and the whole dessert station.

Two words: SO good. Food was as aesthetically pleasing as it was delicious and the decor was beautiful. We went during the week for lunch (around 12pm) and there was no line. There was an insane variety of food to choose from; from seafood to soup to tacos to sushi to pizza to pho to dim sum to burgers .. And the dessert table.. Out of this world! All you can eat GELATO bar. Build your own crepes. Candy bar. Fruit, cheese cake, mini donuts, creme brulee.. Definitely worth the money and without a doubt would go again!

CRAB LEGS ALL DAY. Thee best buffet I have ever had in Vegas. When you first walk in, you instantly feel you're in luxury. Everything smells fresh and each dish is carefully thought out to accommodate the masses. They have a large selection. I would go to Vegas just for this buffet

This buffet was worth the money! It's a little pricey compared to other buffets in Vegas but you get your money's worth. Keep in mind there is only a two hour limit eating here so pacing yourself is the key to enjoying a bigger selection of the food they provide you.  Despite the time limit; the quality, flavor, and texture of each plate was delicious. You can tell they put a lot of thought and preparation into cooking or setting up every dish. One of my favorite parts of the meal were the juices. Each bottle of juice was inside these cute bottles and they tasted fresh. Another favorite part of the meal was having a taste of my fiance' s brisket and it was succulent! It was moist and the meat melted into your mouth. The service was fast and efficient also. Every time my fiance was done with his drink they would have a new one in front of him!  I would highly recommend this buffet.

I guess that we came at a really weird time because when we got here there wasn't too much to choose from. It might have been close to where their almost out of food but I believe we got there at 6PM so we couldn't have been late. Anyway as far as the food goes I was kind of disappointed. I've heard so many good reviews from this place and how wonderful the food is and either they had a recent staff change or just weren't feeing it at all because when I went the food was just okay. It wasn't spectacular. I mean paying almost $65 per person the food could've been better. It tasted more like a $25 buffet and even then the buffets that are at that price point do not disappoint. The service was okay, the lady serving us was always ready to help. If we needed water or beverages she was there to help us but it was pretty packed so some times we would have to wait for her but it wasn't an issue. Overall it was a big let down from what I've heard from the past. I always dreamt of coming to this place but I think I waited too long. I should've went when it opened not after a couple of years. To those who swear by this buffet I hope you'll let me know when is the best time to go here because I would love to actually experience Bacchanal the way way it was meant to be.

Maybe I was just expecting to be blown away because of the Yelp reviews, but I was genuinely disappointed when I finally got to go to Bacchanal. This was the one Vegas buffet I decided to splurge on during my latest Vegas trip, and I really wish I went elsewhere. The set-up is undeniably impressive with eeeeendless bars of fresh dishes from every food genre imaginable. Everything looked lovely and I was always excited to go back to my table and try things out. While there were a few dishes that I loved (and that combined with the great service resulted in my 3 stars), I unfortunately found myself finding more things that I didn't like :(

My favorites:
-The Mexican food! I don't usually go for Mexican at buffets, but every meat dish looked incredible - and they all were! My favorite here by far.
-The chicken fingers. I loved the presentation in the little baskets and the flavor was very rich and unique.
-Prime rib
-Glazed carrots. INCREDIBLE!
-Mac and cheese
-The ice cream/gelato bar!! I had baklava and coconut, and I wanted sooo many more!

My gross list:
-Roasted duck. I've never had duck before and I thought it was alright, but my boyfriend tried it and said it was awful (he's had it many times). Weird texture I guess?
-Sliders. Waaay too greasy!
-Sushi. I heard good things on here but I was disappointed in the quality and selection.
-Chili and cornbread
-Shrimp and grits
-Yogurt parfaits
-Red velvet cake. I'm a baker/red velvet lover and this was a disgrace to the dessert!!
-Italian dishes. Veeery plain

We were here on a Wednesday for lunch, and at $33.99 each the quality should have been 5x what it was. I'll only be back if the price drops (ha!) or I end up with a comp somehow :P

Y'all such a disappointment for a luxury buffet! I'm a Dallas native and the buffets for 30 bucks in Dallas are 10x better than this luxury buffet for $55 bucks per person. Not only did the food suck, the wait is terrible. My family of 3 arrived around 11am and got a ticket to come back at 1220pm to get in line.
