Now when I say line, please note that there are two lines  you must pass before you even get seated. The first line is waiting to get to the cashier and pay. After that, you wait in another line depending on the number of your party to get seated. The total wait time from when we first arrived till the time we got seated was about 2 and a half hours. Now when you wait that long and are almost starving to death you expect to have some godly food at the price we paid. The seafood and sushi section was a joke! All they had for sushi were either salmon nigiri or tuna nigiri which both looked like unfresh raw fish slapped on some crumbly rice. The seafood section only had shrimp cocktail and crab legs that were so skinny,  they were the size of fingers. While they had a lot of different types of American food such as fries, bacon, mini sliders, and Mac and cheese, everything was average at best. After having an epic failed brunch, you would expect to have at least good dessert. And I'm sorry to deliver that dessert sucks too. The only thing cool about it is that you can order a crepe to be made which tasted like dough and a squirt of nutella. The desserts were dry and not tasty whatsoever. Please steer clear from their "chocolate lava cake" as it is as dry as a desert with no chocolate flow in sight. Overall would not recommend it to anyone, not worth the wait or money.

Go to Wicked Spoon!  Your wallet and palate will thank you for it.  $47 for very mediocre food.  Kids over 8 were the same price and it was brunch.  Nothing was spectacular.  The ingredients were average and didn't seem very fresh.

Their website gave us the bait and switch.  It said $41.99 for weekend brunch and champagne was included.  They charged us $47 and champagne was an extra $10.   I can't believe people wait in long lines for this crap!

This buffet is the creme de la creme of gourmet buffets. Just the decor would make you want to enjoy the experience. The food is really good. The steak and eggs I enjoyed. And if you don't see anything that you were looking for just ask. The reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because the waiter was very impatient with my drink order when I asked him about the beverages menu. But when a high roller and his family asked for a bottle of wine he made sure he gave him all the time in the world. But overall I enjoyed the experience.

I heard so many great things about this Vegas buffet and guys, honestly, its the best buffet all across America (i might be exaggerating but I've been to a lot of buffets). 

There's such a grand variety of foods to fit anyone's taste buds. We went for brunch so there was a great amount of breakfast items such as eggs but there was also dim sum, which made me very happy! 

Needless to say I OD' on pressed juice, baked goods and dim sum.

Bacchanal Buffet vs. Wicked Spoon @ Cosmopolitan. 

If this was a Vegas fight than it would be a KO in round . The champ is Bacchanal. 

I had the opportunity to dine at both buffets and my personal opinion is that Bacchanal is designed with the utmost attention to detail in its looks and culinary offerings. The aroma of food was fantastic and awakening to my senses. I made sure I came here on an empty stomach with a mean appetite, and it was well worth it.  The Buffet has an extravagant selection of food to choose from, and everything is presented very well. The selections are quite creative as well in contrast to most standard run-of-the-mill buffets. 

For $55/person, it's not the cheapest (i.e. Wicked Spoon). Nevertheless, the premium price for dinner was definitely worth the money to enjoy this amazing dining experience especially if you're a fan of seafood.

This place was OK. The service could have been better. I hated the lines too. Not worth the hype. For better service go to Rio. They are friendlier and the food is pretty much the same because they are both owned by the same company.

This is my first review of less than 5 stars. It pains me to leave a review anything less than glowing but this experience needs to be shared in hopes to save someone some money or let know know what they may be getting. The wait wasn't terrible but the temperature of the food was. Nothing... and I mean nothing was still hot once seated at the table. Much less even warm! My salmon was actually cold. So cold I spit it out. I would let this slide and chalk it up to you get what you pay for... expect I left still hungry and paid $75.00 for cold food and terrible house wine. I expected so much more from a buffet named "one of the best in Las Vegas" I have had the Wicked Spoon in the past. My advice.. go there, it's about the same price maybe even cheaper but 5 times better of an experience. The funny thing is the Bacchanal even have hot pads for your fingers to carry plates as if they were hot! One buffet trip I did have one extremely hot item..only problem is that was my desert plate I had for cold food that melted.  Go figure. Save your money. The Bacchanal Buffet is a #BustDine

Stay away during holidays- cost is inflated to $79 pp - staff are stressed out with snappy comments and the wait is LONG - finally seated just under 3 hrs (including get your return time at the kiosk) and they have shoved the tables so close that there is minimal space between tables - just shows the greed of these casinos

Went here for dinner last night after reading all the great reviews - I totally do not understand the hype.  First we arrived at 5pm and checked in at the kiosk with an estimated 1 hr wait...no problem.  They actually called us back 45 minutes later (awesome), but that was to just stand in another line.  After standing in that line for almost another hour we decided to pay an additional $25 per person to jump to the front so we weren't late to our show.  Done - then had to wait another 15 minutes to be seated.  The above was annoying - but we were in, and excited to try out one of "Vegas's best buffets".  I was seriously let down at the overall quality of the food.  Selection was reasonable at best, I enjoyed the crab - but it went downhill from there.  The men thought the meat & prime rib were under seasoned with no flavor (and very fatty).  My husband tried to get street tacos from the Mexican station and wasn't even acknowledged.  The Italian & Asian stations in the back had food that looked like it had been sitting for quite some time and was nothing fancy (at prime dinner hour).  The desert selection was okay, but again, average.  Overall, it was over $300 for 4 of us and no one thought highly of the place or would return.  Save yourself the time & money (and calories) and go have a nice dinner elsewhere.  Regretting my choice.

Bacchanal Buffet has dethroned the Wicked Spoon Buffet as my favorite buffet in Vegas. I'd still go to Wicked Spoon when given the opportunity, but I'd say Bacchanal is superior in essentially every aspect.

More variety of foods, better selections, and better tasting food. 

With the popularity that Bacchanal has gained, they now have a ticketing system that works very similar to that of the Fast Pass at Disneyland. You get in line to input information into a call-back system. They print out a receipt and text you when your turn is up. This, I'm assuming, helps with their line so that people don't crowd the Bacchanal area. Also, if the wait is 2 hours long, you can go to the Forum shops, go blow some money on the tables, then come back.

After you get back, you get in line to pay, then get in line to be seated. With so many lines and checkpoints, I guess this added call-back system is necessary.

One thing that annoyed me was that we came here for the Champagne Brunch and were forced to pay the higher price, even though my wife and I don't drink. But alas, we fell victim to this.

They had a raw bar, meat carver, street tacos area, stews and soups, Italian, and an Asian section. Some highlights were the prime rib, the seasoned steamed shrimp [if you didn't want it cold], the wonderful cheese selection, the Kalbi, and the awesome and amazing sweet potato tater tot balls. Oh My Amazeballs - those were awesome.

Everything else was just us pigging out and eating in absolute gluttony and excess. 

What was very disappointing was the dessert bar. I've read review after review of how great the desserts were and how extensive their selection is. Sure, there is quite a variety and a great selection... but everything was underwhelming and quite a disappointment. The Bacchanal dessert bar is like Floyd Mayweather - rich and flashy, but surprisingly disappointing when you realize he can't even read a book. The flan was dense and thick when it looked beautiful and light. The black sesame gelato had no flavor. The cakes and cookies, while looking exquisite and beautiful, were .. again.. disappointing. 

So yeah.. for the price you pay, you certainly get a great variety and, as with the Wicked Spoon, or any other buffet, there are plenty of hits and misses. Bacchanal sure had its share of hits, but the dessert bar is a complete miss.

I had been to there Dinner buffet. Too many food items, but none of them deserve second serving. Desserts were better. Not worth the money, and the wait. I cannot remember of anything which I liked. I usually like everything. I give two starts only for the staff service.

Freshly cooked dishes. Unlike other buffets, every single menus were pretty good. Dessert menus were phenomenal. Friendly staff, reasonable price, and upscale dining area. I have no reason to not to come back here.

EXCELLENT buffet. 
A little expensive ($60+/pp), and yes, you will wait for at least 30 minutes to get seated, but amazing variety and VERY good food! 
Asian station, American comfort food station (w/amazing Mac & cheese, btw), Mexican station, seafood station, meat station, plus a great variety of juices and an exceptional dessert bar. Best flan I've ever had!
Totally worth the price, and the wait, especially if you like seafood.
We were lucky to get seated right away, usually there always seemed to be a long wait. The was good except their crab legs... it was WAAY TOO SALTY. Love their taco stand!

Came here with a couple of friends for dinner around 8pm. There was a bit of a wait about an hour or so, so we asked the receptionist if we could pay to skip the line and it was an option. It's a bit pricey but it's Vegas and it was worth it. Once seated they immediately placed our drink orders and we were free to seek our meals. There are lines inside but they don't take long, and different areas inside offer foods from different parts of the world. Mexican, American, Asian, and a great variety. The only disappointment was the dessert buffet, some of the offerings were just okay. I would definitely return on a future trip.

I wish this could be a review on how wonderful the food and service was. Sadly we did not get to experience any of that. When we arrived at 5:00 we were told to check in at the kiosk and get our time to come back to be seated. We do so and our call back time is 8:30, ok that sucks but with all the rave reviews we can tough it out. So we spend the next 3 hours wondering around the shops waiting for our turn. 8:00 we start heading back over we get back around 8:20 and to our surprise there is a line wrapped all the way around the bar out front. We find the hostess and ask what the line is for and where do we check in for our what we thought and were told was our 8:30 seating. We were told that we would need to get in the line and more than likely we would not be seated at all because they seat the last party at 11:00 and put all the food away at 11:30. Again confused I ask but we were told we have an 8:30 seating time. We were then informed that the call back time on the ticket was the time to come get in line and then wait in line for another 2-3 hours and after you wait all this time more than likely you will not be seated or get to eat but thanks for trying. Not ok. This system is so very flawed. If you have a limited number of seatings or time then don't continue to give out tickets. Also please train your staff to explain the kiosk system in a proper way, the time on your ticket is not your seating time it is your time to get in line and wait another 3ish hours.

This was not as good as I hoped it would be.  The line was long, very long, even at 9:30 in the evening, and because of that, I forked out the extra $15 to go into the express line.  The set up is huge and there are plenty of things to choose from.  

I was very happy to find some quality ahi tuna and could have ate just that and dessert.  In an effort to mix it up, I tried a little more than that and discovered that the only things I really enjoyed was the stuff that wasn't really cooked (the tuna, the crab legs and salads).  The ice cream mochi was delicious as were many of the other dessert offerings.  However, the main dishes, soups and sides all seemed to have a ton of salt and got to the point of just too much.  Even the soy sauce was way too salty, if that is even possible.

Of the buffetts we tried in Vegas, this was most definitely not my favorite but certainly the most painful to my wallet.
Your can tell they use good ingredients, but some of the food had been sitting out a bit too long and you could tell. The prime rib was excellent and the dessert bar was fantastic.

The worst experience ever very long wait the food isn't that good and the management is horrible they treat u like a criminal. From when I paid until I was seated took 45 minutes and you have to leave in 2 hours .
Server Alvaro was very friendly 
Management was terrible
Go dine at a fine restaurant cheaper and better quality food and you can take your time and enjoy your food

Aight yo check it: BRING SIX PEOPLE. WHY? You'll get seated faster. You're probably hungry if you going to a buffet, so you about to starve if you don't have 6 people.

Once you got your squad, some old lady gonna gonna bring you to another line. She's a nice lady though. Once she lets you in, you pay and guess what, ANOTHER LINE. But it's cool cause you get to see the nice entrance and the best part, the crab legs. 

Once you're inside, you got seafood, meat, mexican, Italian, and lastly Asian food. 

All is pretty good. My recommendations, the CORN, Rib eye is coo, and the lamb chop thing is good too. Nothing really stood out, especially if you paying for $60 almost. 

The best part was probably they desert. Ask for a Thai Tea shot looking thing. It's pretty good. Once you get it, everyone else gonna want one too. You probably want one right now. I don't blame you. 

Alright, long story short, four stars. Solid food. Choices are okay. If you starving and got some time to kill, go for it. Is it worth $60? Nah. If it was $40? I'll be back again. 

Service was great as well. Lines are whack. Food was coo. But desert was great. 

SCORE: 3.5 SwaggieStars. But Yelp shiesty so I rounded up to four so y'all Bacchanel (BOCK-CUH-NULL). 

Sorry, I got no pics. I was too hungry.
good good with many choices and varieties. I love the seafood with king crabs, spider crab and oyster. all the foods here are above average.

- Dark.  You can see the food you are eating.  For those who love to take pictures of their food for social media, the lighting is really bad for pictures.
- Expensive.  Yes, there is lot of seafood.  Is it worth the price?  I don't think so.  There are others buffet restaurants on the Vegas Strip that offer similar seafood selections with similar taste but at lower prices 
- Be prepared for long lines, just like all the other buffers in town.
- Cramped inside. Because of the popularity of this place, they try to fit as many tables in the space.  It feels like you are sharing a table with strangers and you could hear their conversation.
- The snow crabs and most food are on the salty side 
- Not that many choices for vegetarians

+ Lots of yummy desserts
+ Platinum and above Total Rewards members get their own express lines 

It's ok to go once just so that you can say you've been there.  Be prepared to leave feeling not satisfied with the food and service you get with respect to the price you pay.

We came again for their brunch buffet with bottomless mimosas. It was heavenly.

I especially loved the plentiful portion of warmed crab legs they gave me. And the pork buns were exquisite as always. 

The macaroni and cheese was rich and succulent. 

The desserts were to die for - so much to choose from and none of what I tried was against my tastebuds.

Great experience.

Hands down probably one of the better buffets I've had.  I thought Cosmo's buffet was good, but I think I've found myself another winner. 

The line wasn't too long when we arrived at 11:15am but it was pretty long when we left around 1pm.  The selection of the food is actually pretty overwhelming and I didn't even get a chance to hit up the seafood bar b/c I was too busy trying to get in on all the other areas. 

I think it was $45 for the brunch on a Sunday which includes endless mimosas.  That alone is $12 a glass so you're really getting your money's worth.   We had some Total Rewards points to redeem (they expire every six months) so that took our price down to $30-$32.  I must say the food is very well worth the $45 though.  I would definitely go back again.

I don't know much more to say other than it was an excellent experience and I would visit again!

Best of the Vegas buffets.  Far better than the peers in quality of the food, on par in service,  and a little pricier than the rest.   The meat section is the main attraction with the desserts.   The usual suspects as well as lamb chops. The macaroons and the general quality of all desserts are wonderful.   The temperature sensitive foods are okay, wagyu sliders would be great if they weren't over cooked and sitting for who knows how long.  Sushi isn't really edible as are most of the Asian section.   What they do well are great and setting is wonderful.   Will be back.

Not worth it!  For $60 per person, and paid extra $20 for the express line.  Even without the $20 up fee, it's still not worth it.  Mind you, there is a 2 hr time limit to dine.  That starts the minute you pay, and then there is an additional 15-30 min wait to actually get seated, and to get seafood or prime ribs, that another 30 mins wait.  The food is really just any other buffet quality,  the sushi bar is an embarrassment.  There is a bit of everything, like Pho (value, $6) and Ramen ($8) But this still does not justify the overprice and time wasted.  You want to come to Vegas feeling like you won something... This place def makes you feel like you've been swept at the poker table.  Better off to make reservations at Mastros for a real Bone in rib eye and lobster mash potatoes, you will feel much better.

Really good buffet! The $15.00 all you can drink wine is a plus. Excellent variety of food, and not your typical buffet quality either. The taco station was my favorite, and the ceviche was perfect. The service was also a highlight. Would definitely come back to this place.

Why, oh why, oh why did I have to be hungover as death when eating here?  I was literally squirming in my seat trying to keep my food going the right way (as in down, not back up).  I started with 2 soups, hot and sour and French onion, and crap-load of Sierra Mist.  The hot and sour was meh, the French onion was yummy, and the Sierra Mist was to die for.  I just wish I had felt better, because I know my perception was skewed due to the number of alcoholic beverages I had consumed the previous night.  Some things I probably would have loved were the antipasto meats and cheeses, and the tacos, but alas, I was forced to stick to soup and salad for the most part.  Boooooo.  Next time....I will wreck you.

Went here for lunch with a local who is a friend of ours.  She said dinner isn't much different.  We went for lunch.  Not at all impressed.  First, I am not a buffet fan anyway.  However, when it's Vegas.... I mean I have to do the best one.  The last time we came was 10 years ago and back then it was all about the Bellaggio. Now it's Bacchanal.  I had a little sushi, dim sum, crab claws, prime rib and brisket.  Had some soups and a variety of desserts.  Also had a taste of pho.  NONE of it was really notable.  For the $50 lunch price I expected more.

Absolutely not worth it.  In my opinion, the lunch price tag should be $35-40.  I would much rather go to a good high end restaurant and have a more enjoyable meal.

They really have improved the wait situation.  I always thought it was strange that a casino would be OK with patrons waiting an hour or more in line when they could just be given a time to check in, so they could do other things like say...maybe spend money in their casino or have drinks at the bar.  It is so much better.  You check in at a kiosk, and I believe it gave us an estimated time to check back.  So we did spend money in the casino while waiting, checked back and maybe waited another half hour (still not optimal but better than it was) to be seated.  Once seated though, there were so many choices.  These were my favorites on this visit:
1) Dim sum - shrimp dumplings, potstickers, crispy pork belly, Filipino lumpia, bbq pork, etc.
2) sushi, edamame
3) deviled eggs (different types)
4) steamed crab legs
5) made-to-order street tacos (THE BEST) - I think I kept going back for these.

Great food and lots of options ! I was treated very well, my waitress Socorro M was very sweet and very fast. The food here was delicious from sides, to the entrees, to the deserts! I would definitely come back for more. The seafood especially was very fresh. I will most definitely come back
One of the best buffets I've had. We were spoilt for choices!!!! The crab was excellent and the desserts were calling us back again and again!

I was pleased with the service from the team member Mahyar Rabbani that I had express my gratitude to my fellow yelpers. He was prompt in cleaning out the tables for us so we can bring new food. You could tell the guy takes pride in his work and I do see him going up the chain very soon. If only I had my business in Vegas would probably take him to work with me. As always the food and everything is fantastic and will always come back. I have to say it's always a plus to be a platinum member as you do go ahead of the wait.
This is suppose to be the best buffet of Vegas?  Really?  Prime rib was tough, crab leg was salty, terrible service.  Definitely not going back there again.  The worst was the 2 hours wait.

We've been to Vegas many times and finally decided to try this place. 

Hands down the best buffet I've had in Vegas! We were there for the Sunday Brunch. They have so much variety and the quality of food is amazing! It is worth every penny and definitely worth the wait. 

The line was long so we checked in and went shopping at the forum shops for about an hour. They then sent us text message for us to head back for a table. From then, it wa about a 10 mins wait. 
So, you're not wasting your time waiting. 

I've been to many many buffets and this one is even better than Cancun and Playa Del Carmen. Just to name a couple of places =)
Next time we will try the dinner.  

5stars for quality and variety!

Breakfast buffet is awesome!! The price is great compared to what you would have to pay for 1 order in a restaurant. They have a variety of chinese, mexican, american, italian etc. The selection is great and the buffet is very clean. I would recommend this place, i've been here twice already!

A very decent casino buffet. The food is generally good. It is spread out so it doesn't feel too crowded. The seating people are nice, Issac in particular.  It would be nice if they could change up the menu from time to time. They keep everything full until closing, then have to dump what has been out. It is a little hard to watch. I wish they would downside the platters for a time before closing.

Omggggg!!!! This place is amazing!!! The wait was about 30 min, but whatever! It's Vegas, everyone's out here trying to eat! The selection of food is just.... WOW! You definitely need a big appetite if you come here; you are gonna want to try everything! Totally worth the price you pay! I will be back on my next Las Vegas trip!
Extremely over rated. Avg buffet and way over priced. Waited in line for over 1 hour. Not worth the wait or the price.
When I die, if I get to heaven, this will be my breakfast everyday for eternity.  Pricey.  But you'll see what I mean when you get there

My absolute favorite buffet. It's pricey but worth it. The selection is spectacular with every tastebud satisfied. I love the crab legs and even the sushi is up to standard. Here's a great tip, get the crab legs sauteed by the chefs in black bean sauce. DELICIOUS. I come here every time I have family in town. The lines are long but they'll sometimes have deals on Groupon for brunch. Definitely worth a try if you love buffets.

My family and I came here as our last night after staying at Caesars Palace and staffs were all super friendly. The food was also phenomenal, especially the desserts. One of the servers, Francisco Busser, had attended to our every need without question. No matter how busy he was, he always made time to stop by our table to ask if we needed anything else. Francisco noticed every detail, for example, when we needed refills on drinks, needed to clear the plates from our table or just getting special foods from the kitchen, he was always on it! I honestly couldn't have asked for a better waiter for the night. 

Moving onto the food selection, must I say WOW! There are so many options to choose from. The food was also delicious. I honestly don't remember what I ate considering I ate a lot due to the abundant selection. I do know that the King Crab was the highlight for me. For the desserts, you must try the Tiramisu or Creme Brûlée if you're into it. If you're in Vegas for the weekend/or any day, be sure to stop by this buffet and come with an empty stomach because you won't regret it!
Lunch is mediocre here, so don't make my mistake. Go for dinner.

Omg. The food here is divine. I couldn't rave enough about it to be honest. Everything I got was fresh and delicious and I went up 3 times. However, the sushi and Italian food was tucked away and I actually missed it my first two rounds. Definitely keep an eye out for it. 

Prices are a little high but not a huge deal. We went a little later on a Monday during lunch to avoid the crowd.

Let start off saying that I am totally not a buffet person, but Bacchanal changed my mind.  This place is ridiculous, best buffet food EVER!  Sure it is expensive, but you are getting quality food.  Bacchanal was the only place we considered making a second visit to during our LV trip.

My husband and I ate there on December 30th and at first I was taken aback by the ticketing system because it said our wait time was 287 minutes. That is right 287 minutes, which is a little more than 4.5 hours. You input you mobile phone number and it  they will text you when it is time for you to come back to pay and get in line to eat.  Since we had time to waste we got us an appetizer from Cheesecake Factory and then went to the miracle mile shops to look around. At 4:30 they text us to get back in and pay, we got back their around 5 pm checked in, got in line and paid. We sat down to eat around 5:55. 
Now to the food, it was great.  They had, seafood, Asian food, Mexican food and pizza and dessert stations. I loved that they had a separate station with the hot crab legs, so I didn't have to wait. The desserts where delicious. I hate buffets but this one is one that I would be happy to go to again.

All you can eat King Crab legs
Oysters Jumbo Shrimp
crab claws Lamb chops !


Eating here is better than 


Boom Boom !!!!
had great vegan options. you just have to make sure to ask the servers to walk you through them. I was pleasantly surprised with the service, décor, and food!

Selection was over the top!!!! But that's all I could say super positive about it!!! Bakery selection was good
However, quality of food was questionable, I felt sick after.
Crab legs were to silty, seafood was ok, I have tried better. Meat has not been done well enough. The bottom line, for this price , you would expect better quality. I don't think it's the best buffet in Vegas!!! Surly not!!!
Hands down BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS!!! Our new tradition in Vegas? Here, for Sunday brunch!! Best selection, best quality!! Expensive but soooooo worth it!!

It's my first time in Vegas, so I've always wanted to try the famous buffets everyone raves about out here. We've heard nothing but great things about Bacchanal so our group decided to try it. 

It's located in Caesar's Palace, and we heard the lines get pretty long here, but lucky for us we definitely beat the rush. We decided to get a table for 8, which inclines that we all are charged gratuity up front (18%). The buffet dinner was $57.99 and after gratuity came around roughly ~$75 a person. 

We were seated right away and all ordered our drinks. Now on to the food. We dove into the seafood right away and went straight for the steamed snow crab legs (recommended), and continued to come back because these were to die for. The buffet had a wide range of food from, pastas, to various cuts of meat (prime rib, Tri tip, etc.), sausages, pizza, and Chinese food. They also had a taco bar which was delicious, and a seafood section full of oysters, salmon, and even seafood paella. 

Lucky for us, the chef brought out two special plates of food that wasn't offered in the buffet. One was cooked oysters with some kind of cheese topping with bell peppers. The other was an eggplant dish that I didn't get to try. I thought the oysters were decent but I was too fixated on the snow crabs to care.

Now onto my favorite part of the meal, desserts! They had a HUGE dessert bar which ranged from pastries, gelato's, and fruits. The ones that stood out to me were some made to order soufflé's, Thai tea float with boba, and the green tea white chocolate covered strawberries (omg). All a must try. 

Overall, the buffet was delicious, we definitely ate too fast for our own good, but I think we were able to try almost everything. Would definitely recommend this buffet! Enjoy!!

If you are in vegas, one of the things you have to do is go to a buffet. WHY? just because you can stuff your face with international delicious food! Why is it? that the buffet in my home town are so shitty. The only time I go to a buffet is when I go to VEGAS. Normally when I do go to a buffet, its filled with sub par ehhh food but here at bacchanal I can find many items that I love. Which is awesome because i can go for seconds and thirds without paying so much. My favorite item was the prime rib. I even love going to the line and getting the prime rib lol The guy that serves it, is super friendly and funny. He makes me feel at home so I feel at ease revisiting him over and over lol

The price isnt so bad either I only paid 36 and I felt like I got more than my money's worth here.

We wanted to eat a buffet in Vegas during our vacation. We decided on Bacchanal because it's currently voted the  #1 buffet in Vegas. 

We made sure we weren't starving when we went there because I've read from reviews that the wait was really long. We got to the buffet around 8:30pm, got in line to put our name down on the computer, which told you what time to come back to get into another line. I think that whole putting your name in the computer is a great idea because you can go and gamble or walk around and then comeback close to the time on your ticket and not have to stand there for an hours. They also give you and option to enter your no# so if the line moved a little faster, they will text you. Which they ended up texting us 15 mins later.

Once we got the txt, we then stood in line for about 30-40 minutes until we paid and got seated. The price of the buffet was $50 something (under $55) for adults and $25 for kids (dinner time).

Omg, this buffet had everything! Crab legs, oysters, scallops, prime rib, Italian food, noodle bar, dim sum station, gourmet pizzas, all kinds of cheese, everything!!! And everything we ate was delicious! The dessert area was amazing! So many delicious dessert. The service was A+! I see why it was voted the #1 buffet on Vegas. 

Kids: our boys loved it. We told them to try a little bit of everything and told them NO pizzas or burgers (that's usually what they fill up on at buffets). Although we did let them get a slice of their pizzas because it was amazingly delicious!

So, we went here for brunch New Year's Day.  We had heard a lot, and for $70 each, we had raised our expectations.   There was an hour wait to get to the line that did not look like it was moving, so we opted in to paying $25 each (on top of the $70 ea to "skip the line".  We went to the VIP area and stood in line for about 15min only to be told we were in the wrong line.  They insisted there was a sign that instructed where the express VIP should stand, and there wasn't.  Indeed, I brought them the sign they insisted said "express" and pointed out that it said "diamond" and that two of the signs said diamond.   I was foolish to expect an apology, or professional correction, or something.  So - we went to the back of the line (after four other parties got in front) and meanwhile we saw the same thing happen to another couple in another unmarked line!  We let them go first bc they had been standing there being ignored longer than any of us. 

Ok, it's NY day and they were busy and have incompetent ppl taking money.  No reason to that that spoil anything.  We the learn that the $50 convenience fee was paid to skip the hour wait to stand in line to pay.  Ok- so an hour later we are being seated.  Woot.  

We love food.  But, With the prices paid, I expected more.  We could have gone pretty much anywhere else and gotten the same quality.  You're paying for presentation here.  They had all kinds of things, great variety, but all of it mediocre. And much of it room temp or cold. Some strangely cooked. (A roasted gourd salad that was too raw to cut, mushy egg rolls).  And for brunch I love eggs, but they only had soggy scrambled for someone like me - lobster Benedict otherwise which is lost on me.  

The Rio buffet was so much better.  Wouldn't recommend this one for the price.

I've been to every buffet in town, so I do have buffet knowledge.  Bacchanal is 2nd best only to the evening Wynn Buffett, however these buffets differ from one another so they may both be #1 on my list.  The bacchanal is over the top and in a good way.  The other great thing is that I've only stood in line once and it didn't take very long.  Most buffets take forever to get through the line.  PS You can avoid the line at the Wynn Buffet by paying extra - super expensive but worth it.

The food is rich and everything is specially crafted.  Seafood is a plus.  Downer: The honey bar should actually have honey, not just a display.  

For vegi lovers, it really pleases.

The only downer are the tourists, racing to get to the food and pushing you out of the way to get to it as if it were going to run out, perhaps this is a cultural thing in highly populated countries.  The other downer is the mid west mullet tourists who must eat the food at the actual buffet (taste testing) disgusting ;(

Other than that I highly recommend this buffet over all others.  Something worth trying!  Oh, it's pricey  at $40 but worth it.  Take your time and enjoy it.

Brian and Chef Nicola were amazing! They took care of us from the moment we sat down. Everything was delicious, well cooked and seasoned! Our waitress Racquel was really good and attentive, she did a really good job!

I was so excited to finally have the chance to try out this place. The wait was about 5 minutes for a Friday around 11:00 for brunch. They offer seafood, Chinese food, sushi, pastas, pizzas, chicken and waffles which was to die for! The beef lasagna was a real winner for me- I kept taking a bite out of everything to not get overly stuffed at a buffet but could not stop myself from going back for a few more bites for the lasagna. 
The sausages, bacon, eggs, pancakes were all so good as well. 
I did not like the donuts/ they taste store bought and remind me of 7/11 donuts. 
Price was just right for all that food and coming just early enough made it even more worth while. 
I will be back next time!

Yumm........I have been to many buffets, and this one is definitely above all.  My wife and I had a disappointed buffet at Wynn,and decided to try out this one to compensate for the bad experience.  In comparison, it's really day and night.  Not only it has more selections, but even the same food tasted much better. As soon as you bite into the food, you can tell it was really made by a good chef indeed.  Most of the buffets would only have few items being great while rest of them are average.  Not in this one.  I would say 90% of the food is way above average.  They even have oyster, tonkushu ramen and mochi which I have never seen available in other buffet place.  Yes, it's expensive (had it been like $40 or so, it would be five stars), but it's really a great tasting experience that you should definitely try while you are in las vegas.

Nice food. However, it took a really long time for waiting the sites. I suggest you take a number around 3pm for the dinner, then go shopping for one hour. In this case, you can eat dinner at 4pm without any terrible line waiting in front of the restaurant.

Perhaps my favorite buffet since 2013.  It's got everything you need and surprisingly, their variety of asian food is quite delicious.  Every time I went it was for Sunday champagne buffet and they always had a nourishing soup available, whether it was ox tail, black chicken, ginseng chicken, or whatever, but it was soooo fulfilling after being hungover.  

Aside from that, the seafood station is pretty standard yet good quality.  There's never a shortage of shrimp and crab and as I recall, I've seen oysters served at a certain point in time - just goes to show how they really rotate different items in and you can never really have the same thing each time you go back.  

Overall, great variety, and good quality for the price.  I don't even need to go anywhere else knowing that I can count on Bacchanal to deliver a fine buffet meal with never ending champagne.  Also, they have the ticket system which eliminates the need to stand in line forever like the Wynn.  NO thanks.

Great buffet for seafood lovers! Oysters on the half shell and all you can eat crab that is already cracked is perfect! Wonderful imported cheese assortment, sushi selection is fresh and a good variety, brisket, ribs and prime rib selections.
For 2 people for dinner we spent $115 so it is pricey so be prepared to spend good money!

Great buffet, but long wait time. No salad bar, soup bowls were not easy accessible it's located after you have passed the soup area. You have to line up to get your food, unlike other buffets you grab and go and enjoy your food.  Crab legs were a little too salty.  Food selection is great, ambiance and decor is wonderful. Overall I give an average rating 3/5.

The wait might be a pain but this place is definitely worth it. Easily one of the best buffets I've been to on the strip. Huge selection of meat and seafood and everything tasted really fresh. I've been to most of the buffets on the strip and this one is easily my new favorite.
Our new favorite buffet.  Had king crab which was awesome and ended it with there home made crepes the best I ever had.  Will definitely be back.

Was starving after a 5 hour flight from New York City. So what better way to start off our Vegas trip then to dine at Bachannal Buffet. 

Came in at 12:30pm local time and the restaurant was fairly empty. Took about 5 minutes from the minute we paid to the time we were seated. The ambiance is pretty spectacular for a casual restaurant. Staff is very lively and welcoming. 

Now, the food selection itself is somewhat underwhelming. They advertise themselves as catering from all corners of the world. But their selection was pretty limited to justify that claim. They have your typical cuisines like Japanese and Italian covered. 
 
The food itself pretty average. Nothing really stood out but I have been told that there is a noticeable difference between their lunch and dinner service. 

What this restaurant does really well is the print attention the wait staff pays. Minimal wait time between finishing your plate and that plate being cleared from the table.

Food is as expected in a buffet. While there's plenty of variety the quality is not that great. I ate there only for their crab legs, and even that has about 25% that are somewhat stale and rubbery.

It's most definitely not worth the 2.5 hr wait time and $65 dinner price tag.

Do yourself a favor and frequent another restaurant. Their queue system is a mess from my past experience.

Meh... I don't know why I keep giving this buffet one more chance.   Dined here for the fourth time since they opened and the food still hasn't gotten any better.  Long lines, long waits, overpriced, and either super bland or super salty food (pretty sure they are trying to get you to drink more). Best thing here was the unique gelato flavors.  Definitely wouldn't come without using the Groupon deal.  I'd rather go to the Rio or Wicked Spoon for better quality and less money.

Worth the time lining up and the seafoods were fresh and tasty. I enjoyed having dinner there and the service was good. I think it's a must-try in Las Vegas and I will come again:) really lots of types of foods there, I wish if I could eat more and more.
It is the best buffet that I have ever had, however it is too pricey and the wait was long. I don't think I will come back to this because 125 for 2 people is simply too much!

What's a trip to Las Vegas without experiencing a buffet?  Hearing great things about the Caesar's Buffet, we decided to give it a try.  We arrived at 5 pm to beat the rush.  Most items, were well-stocked, however many were lukewarm.  As the restaurant became busier, food became hotter and fresher.

Overall food presentation was nice.  I enjoy the small plates, which helps me control my portions and try many different items.  They were especially slow to refill the oysters, which I found annoying.  I stopped by a couple of times and saw an empty tray.  I wish they had different seasoning options for the crab legs, not just the standard cocktail sauce and butter.  The mini sliders were tasty, and the black chicken soup hit the spot when it was served hot.  

Service was ok.  Our waitress was MIA at the beginning of the meal, but service improved through out the meal.

Overall a good experience and value at $40/person.

This was a pretty good buffet but I though the buffet at Aria was better.  If you wanted to skip the line, you can pay 20-25 dollar extra to just not wait in line and get a seat.  This place is big and there is constant large amount of people.
I went for breakfast after finding a groupon deal. The food was really good and I really liked the decor. They had a great selection!

OVER PRICED. (50$)

Food is good - ton of variety. Especially the dessert. It is all worth for a lesser price though. Try it once for a lifetime experience.

Went there because of the great reviews. They were false! $60 a head what a rip off! The service was horrible and rude! The Prime rib was tough and had little to no flavor! They claimed be serving wagu beef (beef Round) that was chewy and flavorless. I had a better steak at breakfast for $6.99! The cheesecake had a sour taste to it. I should of just had a hotdog from a street vendor!

Hand down the best buffet I ever been and ate at. And with all the wide variety of different foods and desserts. They had fresh oysters, shrimp  the list can go on but the crab  legs was off the hook. The whole experience was just amazing. If your looking for a great buffet here this is the place.

One of the most amazing buffets I have ever experienced.  It may seem pricey but it is worth it to splurge and enjoy once in a while.

Excellent selection of menu items.  Love the seafood selection as well as all the desserts. 

The decor is much nicer than typical buffets.  The staff was friendly and attentive.  Don't be shocked if there is a long wait to get in, especially on weekends and holidays.

Meh -- just OK. This buffet was hyped up to us by Caesars staff during our last visit in August 2012 before it opened, so my fiance and I figured we'd stop by during our December visit to give it a try.

Price was more expensive than other buffets on the strip. With a Total Rewards card, our bill was $48 per person for dinner on Friday night. 

It didn't feel like the food selection was much larger than the RIO buffet, but the selection was a bit better. If you're a seafood fan, which I am unfortunately not, there were quite a few choices. My fiance pigged out on the crab legs and said that that alone was worth the cost. I did like that they had a taco station where they grilled up some beef and had a wide variety of salsas and some seriously delicious guacamole. Besides that, nothing in the main food buffet stood out to me.

The dessert section was where I was actually impressed. The crepe station was a nice touch, wide selection of mochi, and some delicious macaroons. Yes, I did go up for seconds.

It was the service that really made this a 3 star (I'd give it 3.5 stars for just the food). One waiter was servicing a whole section and wasn't able to keep up with the seatings. It took 20 minutes (almost 1 dish) to get his attention then another 15 minutes to get water. The table next to us (and boy, some of the tables are close) tried to get an iced tea for almost 20 minutes before walking up to another waiter. The server didn't come back for water refills until the end of the meal and plates were piling up on all the tables around us. 

I probably would not make a return appearance at Bacchanal.

Amazing buffet and loads to choose from! They had cuisine from all over the world: China, Mexico, Italy, etc. I stuck close to the seafood section, which is usually my preferred meat. My most memorable dish was the clams (pictured: top, right above the shrimp) that laid in thin cream sauce (I'm guessing) with a kind of "salsa" consisting of tomato, corn, onion and fresh jalapeño for a spicy kick. Mmm. The dessert section was small in comparison to the vast selection of actual food. Though, by the time I finished eating my dinner, I barely had room for dessert. That's probably how most people feel  and hence the smaller selection of sweets. Lol. My crazy theory. I'm not a buffet person because I can never eat enough to make sense of how much it costs. This buffet is definitely tasty and worth the when-in-Vegas treat. YOLO

Came here for the dinner buffet to see what the hype was all about. Upon entering 6:00 pm there was a 2 minute or so wait after we had paid and we were seated in no time. Our waitress took our drink orders upon being seated and we were off to the buffet food line. 
   There is an Asian cuisine (includes various dumplings, pork buns, seafood and meat dishes, sushi, Chinese sauced crab halves, rice, and noodle dishes), Italian cuisine (pastas, breads, gnocchi in truffle sauce, meatballs), a Mexican station (make your own tacos, nachos, etc), a seafood station (crab legs, crab claws, various clam and mussel dishes in various sauces, etc) a salad station, soup station (truffle mushroom and New England clam chowder), carved meat station (rack of lamb, prime and short rib, etc), pizza, French fries, fried chicken, and a dessert station. There is also a selection of juices in the middle of the station (guava, mango, orange, etc) that are served in small capped glass bottles. 
     I had the crab legs and claws that were on ice, mussels in some type of green sauce, sushi and hand rolls, halved crab in Asian sauce, rack of lamb, truffle mushroom soup, gnocchi in truffle sauce, short rib (served in a small dish on a bed of mashed potatoes and gravy), shrimp and tofu in a white sauce, and a spicy raw fish salad. The crab legs were a little bit too salty for me and I was not able to find the hot steamed ones that I like better, the crab claws were average. The spicy raw fish salad (found next to the sushi in the Asian station) was fantastic: the kani and the hint of sesame seed oil was a great compliment to the freshness of the fish. The tuna and salmon on top of the sushi was relatively fresh (I didn't eat the rice so that I would have more room for other food), the combination of fish in the hand roll was delicious, but again I didn't eat the rice that was a part of the roll. The halved crab in Asian sauce was ok, I found the meat on the inside a little bit too over cooked, which I found to be true for the short rib as well. The truffle mushroom soup delicious the gnocchi in the truffle sauce were cooked perfectly and the sauce was a great compliment to the gnocchi. The mussels in green sauce were delicious along with the shrimp in white sauce. The rack of lamb was perfectly cooked and spiced well. 
   For dessert I had the Crete brûlée, the tiramisu, and the Italian cookie gelato as well as the snored gelato. The crime brûlée custard was good and not too sweet,  but the sugar top wasn't as crispy as I like and a bit soggy. The tiramisu in chocolate was good,  it when I bit into it 2 or so teaspoons of coffee liquid came out, so less of that would have been better. As for the gelato it was perfect and they do have a lot of different flavors to choose from. 
   Caesars buffet does have a lot more options than Aria, which I also tried, especially when it came to the gelato variety, but for a $20 difference ($40 at aria vs $60 at Caesars) I would go to Aria as I love my hot steamed crab legs more than I like the iced ones.

Love this buffet!!! Raw oysters, crab legs, lamb, ginseng soup...I could go on. This buffet is so delicious. The service is excellent and the decor is lovely. I want to go back to Vegas just for this buffet!

Love this buffet... Especially the Italian section with the single serving hot dishes like lasagna, chicken Parmesan.  Also loved the dessert bar with real Salotto and homemade crepes.  

Service was attentive playing and presented beautifully.  Good thing this place is not in my hometown!

Good buffet. Loved the crab legs, pho, prime rib and more. Go early because you will wait.  They have a ton of food and desserts. You can also sign in and come back at your designated time so you don't have to stand in line. It is a lot and more on the weekends. I think after 3 is when they have crab legs. Look for famous people. The night we went was an awesome night when we saw Pete Rose there.

Definitely Vegas' new fave Buffett!  They offered tons of food selection using top ingredients. The oyster is fresh and the rack of lamb was cooked to perfection! Chicken ginseng soup taste really authentic, just like mom's ^^.

AMAZING!!!! this and wicked spoon are the most amazing buffets in vegas. 

with fresh oysters, sushi, desserts, and anything else you can imagine you can't go wrong. 

Now the 49 dollar charge isn't too cheap but its worth it for Vegas. GO HUNGRY ;)

you wil not be disappointed, located in caesars palace, its in a great location
Good food. But no lobsters. enjoyed the place and the dining experience was superb. would be coming back to this place when we visit Vegas again.
Top notch food. We waited about 45 minutes for a party of three but it was well worth it.

I called ahead to make sure they were serving Alaska King crab and they said yes. 8 of us showed up at 3pm and we paid the 52.00 per person at the front I asked again to make sure they were serving King crab and they said "yes at 3pm".  No Alaska King crab in site! Only Snow crab! I complained to one of the managers and he apologized and said he'll personally bring it out.  20 minutes later he brings out a nice plate of Snow crab.  I was starving so I ate it.  Then i complained to another manager and she said that the King crab must have arrived late and she'll bring it out asap.  20 minutes later she brings out small King crab legs and they taste like they've been frozen from last season.   Lies lies and bad crab.

The food was pretty good, but the crab legs and shrimp were still frozen. Yuck. Not worth the prices they're charging! Save your money and hit a Golden Corral or such for buffets......it's much better, and the crab legs are steamed! We won't be returning. There are better restaurants off "The Strip".

Really bad service here , no one come to our table after with sit down for more than 30 minutes. Food was ok but not as good as I expected, only the meat selection was good. (Oyster was not fresh at all)
So good great variety and Groupon got a discount!  Went during lunch ryt b4 dinner and paid half price then dinner price. Got to try their lunch and dinner... Good stuff, loved their desserts too

Went to the buffet earlier last month for the first time ever. I've been to Vegas a few times before and typically loaded up on food at the cheaper establishments on the older part of the strip. Since i only eat once a day while in Vegas (buffets stuff me for the whole day) i decided i'd spice it up a little bit and go pricier to experience the better buffets Vegas had to offer. 

The price is on the higher end. I wasn't too impressed that the cashier up front knew very little english and was rude. thankfully it got better from there. 

first off, the meat station was excellent. the prime rib, sausages, chicken/turkey were excellent. This is a small detail, but the onion rings were in a little crate and it seemed like they took the time get them to taste better than any rings ive ever had. typically small side items like that aren't normally done very well. All the side dishes i tried like the mashed potatoes were excellent. The desert area was also superb. 

The only negatives were : the fried chicken was dry and the seafood selection wasnt as good as expected. 

The best part was the mexican food station. I couldnt believe they had pozole. The rice was good. The street tacos tasted better than most tacos i've had. The toppings had guac, which is definitely a nice touch. When in Vegas, im coming back here first. . . because those street tacos alone are worth the price.

Great buffet but since the first time I came here in 2012 the quality has gone down a lot. I have been to this buffet at least 6 times. They used to be so great in every aspect of their dishes but now that they have become so popular I think they have gotten very lazy. The sushi is not fresh, nor is the oysters. They do have a great selection of desserts, prime rib, seafood and more. For their Asian cuisine selection the quality is not that great. Their forte is definitely in the American food and desserts. They have an abundance of crab both cold and steamed which is great! I also like their fresh squeezed juice selection decorated within cute bottles. This is a great buffet to try out if it's your first time because of its variety but their quality of food is definitely not that great.

Excellent! Huge selection of foods to choose from. Loved the crepe section & the carving station. Each meat that we tried was cooked perfectly and so juicy. Everything was really fresh. The staff was very friendly and helpful!
Very bad oyster test so bad called the manager and the chef and that was my first bite they apologize but they didn't care about me don't go there at all $60 a person ripoff

Being locals we often don't mosey on over to the strip, but for this special occasion we couldn't have made a better decision! We went around 8:00 a.m. on a Friday and there wasn't that many people there, so that was an absolute plus. Our waitress was quick and quite the riot. 
As for the food, it was an excellent selection. Something to mention for those looking to have breakfast there, there is a lot more than just breakfast food. I had a whole plate of asian cuisine and pizza, along with red velvet pancakes & biscuits and gravy. Try the coffee as well, it was excellent. We would all definitely recommend, the price is worth it and the atmosphere can't be beat. It's a very clean restaurant and doesn't feel stuffy but is really nice. Would definitely go back again!

I not really an avid buffet-goer, but I really do recommend Bacchanal! While the wait can get horrendous...I felt that the food made up for it! The miniature individual buckets of seafood tickled my fancy, and it was all adorable and delicious. I felt that the dishes they had offered a little bit more complexity than other buffets. For instance, they had this really good shrimp over polenta,sitting in  a little plate of sauce. Normally at other buffets, you get shrimps in a dish, polenta off to the side, and the sauce nowhere to be found. I loved how they had everything together for me in a miniature slice of heaven. All in all I was pleased for the $40 i payed to get in. Also, you can't really go wrong with spicy chocolate gelato for dessert.

The Bacchanal seems to have the reputation of "THE Buffet" to experience in Vegas based on numerous other reviews and articles so needless to say I was pretty pumped to check this buffet out.  As you can tell from my rating, I was sadly disappointed.

One key factor that led to this rating was the sheer amount of other diners.  It made it impossible to get food from the buffet in particular in areas for key items like crab legs and also to get service.  Our server was trying to keep up with refilling drinks and clearing plates but she just had too many tables and it was impossible.  The other issue is that the quality of the food just isn't the best.  The Bacchanal presents itself as going after sheer quantity and while it does have some of the higher end options (again, crab) it doesn't measure up to other buffets on the strip that focus a bit more on taste and quality.

My wife and I went here for dinner at 3pm a week ago.  We did not have to wait too long to be seated.  The food was good but not anything worth $60/person.  Not sure I would recommend someone to spend that much since it wasn't that great.
Around 7pm I experienced a severe case of food poisoning from eating here.  This was my only meal of the day so I'm sure it was from Bacchanal. I had to call off from work the next day.  I filed a report with security and qas told that some from Risk Management would contact me but it's been a week and a half and nothing.  I've even called them and left several messages. 
Needless to say, I will not be dining here again and I will not recommend any of my family and friends to do so.  I will say that my wife enjoyed her meal and did not get sick, but she had to watch me giving it up from both ends.  
Thanks for nothing.

This place is pretty neat. DEFINITELY go at lunch time though. The pricing is a bit high for what you get in my experience(3 times). Lunch is best price per food selection. I found the hype to be a bit much with this place. They do have a few unique dishes you dont see at other places but they are seriously lacking in what I consider most important at a buffet.

Foods: 
They have virtually zero fruit. Only two small bowls of pineapple and watermelon hidden by the meats and then a few berries in the dessert section. The salad section is an absolute joke. It consists of 2 types of lettuce and about 4 types of toppings and a few dressings. This should be unacceptable to any normal human considering about 50-75% of our diet should be vegetables and fruits. I was extremely disappointed.

Service:
It took about 45 mins to get in which was sort of expected. Once we were inside however there were many many open tables so it didnt make sense. Next it took 11 mins before a server came to take our drink order. It was nearly another 10 mins before she returned with the beverages. We had 6 people at our table and we just ordered waters and iced teas. Now each person made 3-4 trips to the buffet and at any one time there were at least 5 dirty plates on our table. Our server litterally only clear the table twice but never got Everything. This is how our table looked much of the time. http://bit.ly/Y5TCXN

Overall the buffet is slightly over priced comparatively to most big name casino buffets. The food is tasty but seriously lacking in areas that are VERY important to a human diet. I say Skip it.

One of the most famous buffets in ze world! $40 before tip and tax for brunch. Was it the best buffet I've been to? Yes. Was it worth it? Not really. 

Basically there's a million options of generally decent quality food. You'd get much better price/performance at restaurants that specialize, but it was a fun experience.

Great items- chicken and waffles
Good- salmon poke with Yuzu rice, lychee Bellini, speculoos biscotti, flan, soba noodles
Okay- basically everything else

In particular- Don't get the dim sum as it is not very good and you could do much better at a legit place.
Probably the best buffet I've been to in a long time!  Pricey so make sure you get your money's worth!

Prob the best buffet I've ever been to.   Yes, it's $63 dollars a person but where are you gonna get high quality buffet food?  I didn't have 85% of the offerings cuz I'm not a big eater BUT I was left stuffed full of tasty Hot BUTTERED crab legs.  Dessert offerings were also wonderful. Staff is super!

Amazing buffet not your typical buffer offerings.  Had something for everyone. Or if you just wanted to sample a bunch of different cuisines. Dishes that stood out were the Kung Pow chicken it was spicy and so good. Also the beef brisket was smoked with the right amount of flavor.  Can't say I disliked anything and we tried almost everything.  Worth the $60 a person price tag. And I am frugal and don't say that often. Oh and the dessert buffet was so amazing!!!

Was so exited to come here for dinner, but after eating the food I must say it was overly hyped and not worth it! The food was either way too salty or over cooked, even the dessert was not that good. I won't be coming back here again.

Bacchanal is so good! The quality of the food is high and there are so many choices. I'm salivating just thinking about it. Everything I had was so good. Make sure to leave room for dessert. There are so many yummy choices!!

came here last time when i was in Vegas! it is around fifty something per person for lunch. seems expensive but the food are super good. there are seafoods, raw seafoods, meats, steaks, ramen,.... all kinds of food from different culture....
I love their dessert, they are super yummy

i am planning to come back to eat again next time i go to Vegas~~
minus one star for the long wait..

This place is amazing!! I managed to get through 3 food rounds & 1 massive dessert round & all I can think of is when can I return to Vegas & eat here again. We got here around 1130am on Sunday picked a good time because while we waited about 30min to get in, by the time we sat down the line was ridiculous. The only thing that could have made this buffer more enjoyable would be more breakfast selection. I know I got here at 1130 but that's a perfect time to still get stuff it just would have been nice to see more. 

Also the pretzel rolls are beyond to die for.

I've heard mixed reviews about this buffet, but we decided to venture here since most reviews pointed to the Bacchanal as being the 'best' in the strip. Honestly for the price that we paid, the food could've been better. The wait was long, but that was to be expected - you could pay $35 to jump the line, but we didn't want to add an extra $200 to our bill. So we waited a total of an hour and a half for dinner.

I was most impressed with the selection of chinese food (the duck was delicious), the mexican food, and also the dessert. The oysters in the seafood bar were great, the crab not so much. A bit on the salty side so my relatives had a difficult time eating the crab.  

I would definitely advise those to come here for the experience, it's an experience of it's own (Maybe come during lunch when it's cheaper). I will say that the presentation for all the foods were excellent. Albeit, most of the dishes looked better than they tasted - our plates were 'instagram' worthy due to the wonderful presentation! 

Definitely remember to try the green tea covered strawberries! They were coated with crunchy strawberry mini balls - simply DIVINE.

In my opinion, this place doesn't live up to its reputation. I was expecting king crab for lunch, but it was snow crab. The selection is great and there's something for everyone. I especially enjoyed the sushi. The other dishes were mediocre and dessert was below average. Not worth the price tag. I really wanted to love this place. Also found a hair in one of my dishes. Very disappointed. 

Update:
I received word from someone who works at the Caesars hotel. I was told to email this person to discuss matters further, which I did, and never got a response back. Changing my review to 1 star to reflect the poor customer service.

Service was good, but they closed off the food 30 minutes+ before they were scheduled to close at 11:00 (closed off the food at 10:20-10:30). The service was great though, but kinda bummed about how quickly they closed.... Food variety was okay for what we paid,  $110 for 2 people plus tip.

We went because of the all the amazing pictures posted on yelp for this buffet but it turn out to be a bit disappointing. They didn't have a lot of the stuff we saw on the pictures and some of the stuff we actually had didn't look as well executed as the ones shown in the pictures. it is also very expansive for the quality of the food they serve. Don't think the buffets on the strip are better than anywhere else. I actually think the buffet we had before at other states are better than this. probably wont return.

Crab legs, mussels, oysters, clams, shrimp, sushi, dim sum, middles, rice porridge, bbq, sliders, fries, sausages, cheeses, steak, ribs, tacos, macarons, pie, cake, gelato, etc. That's only scratching the surface of what this place had! And it was all delicious! Thinking about it makes me hungry right now! There's pretty much something for everyone here. The wait to get in was horrendous, but that's what happens when it's a buffet considered the best in town. If anything, it'll just make you hungrier when you get inside. Definite must try.

There's a ton of food to chose from its almost overwhelming!! There is definitely something for everyone. Lots a seafood for us seafood lovers. Go EARLY!!! Or u will be stuck in a long line up. We got there at 4:30 walked right in and were seated with no wait. U need lots of time to get through this buffet so bring those stretchy pants & get ur appetite on!! Good luck

After reading USA Today's review ( http://www.usatoday.com/experience/las-vegas/best-of-vegas/vegas-buffets-five-to-find/1991653/) that this was the best buffet in Vegas,  I decided to give it a shot.   The review deemed this place unique,  but I would not totally agree.   The venue is beautiful,  and not your typical "stuff your face fatty" environment.   It's nicely finished,  and gives you the feel like you are in a bubble.   That's really where the uniqueness ends.   
Service is par for any buffet, so don't expect anything better than the service you get at an Old Country Buffet.   The staff was friendly though,  but it would have been a huge WOW factor if they knew our names,  even a first name woukd have WOW'd me.   

The food selection is nothing all that special.   I really expecter a better quality and variety than what was there.   Don't get me wrong,  the glutny of US culture is well represented and the sorority girl types will have to pull the trigger a few times if they want to try everything that fancies them,  but it didn't meet my WOW expectation.   I expected more seafood, meats,  and non typical buffet foods.   When you dedicate 10% of you buffet to pizzas that are not all that great,  then you lose me. 

Suggestions:
1.)  You can really up the service here to get an edge.   
2.)  Go less typical pizza and be inventive.   Have some deep dish pizza,  goat cheese,  and other unique stuff.  
3.)  The Chinese food is insulting,  and is really just Chinese-American take out.   How about authentic Chinese food? 
4.)  Seafood was below par,  and Atlantic City's Borgota has you beat hands down.   Yes Atlantic City!  I hope I woke you up on this one.   How about some Lobster meat for $60?  

Compliments 
1.) Loved,  loved,  loved the brisket!   This is some of the best brisket meat a I have ever had!   It's easily in the top 5,  and probably top 2.  Can I get that recipe? 
2.)  Dessert bar was awesome... You can't go wrong with any selection.   Great unique style and different flavors (i.e.  Green tea creme brullette).   

In the end,  I don't see what makes this the best buffet in Vegas when compared to other buffets across the country I have been too.   If this is really the best,  then I probably won't try others (realize that I am writing this while eating breakfast at the Wicked Spoon Buffet).

I never knew there was an entire room with more buffet stations until my 3rd visit!  I guess they stick the more asian fare back there.  This place is too trendy right now so the wait is too long and $50 for weekend lunch was not worth it.  They didn't even have any oysters or lamb!  Prime rib was dry and overcooked.  There was nothing of value in this meal.

This is supposed to be the new benchmark in terms of buffets in Vegas.  The insane line to get in is artificially conjured by intentionally being inefficient with their table clean up and seating.  You'll see plenty of open tables during your 2-3 hours wait to sit down!  And hell that's genius on their part since they offer a cut in front of the line option for an additional 15 bucks!

The overall food quality is pretty good though i'll give them that but there is a crazy line to get all of the "good stuff" like crab legs and prime rib.  I mean i eventually  gave up and just ate the random stuff that didn't have a line.    I could have easily eaten 2-3x as much raw oysters and crabs legs if the line wasn't so insane.  Another genius move on their part to move these lines a long so slowly.

I mean if you are one of those people that love buffets then definitely check this place out but personally I think you are much better off at one of the many great restaurants in vegas.

I was apprehensive to go to a buffet because quality food did not come to mind. Bacchanal however is the exception. While it is pricey, it is SO worth it. The food is innovative, delicious, and high end... and there is a huge selection -- seafood, mexican, italian, sushi, etc. My only advice is to go super hungry so you can go up several times to get your moneys worth.

Wanted to give them a 5 but not all their food was great. The crab was meh, kinda watery. Ceviche was soggy. Not everything is great butttttttt what was delicious and what I highly recommend was:

- prime rib with mash potatoes and gravy [omg so divine]
- roast duck [soooooo juicy]
- oysters
- lemon basil gelato :D

I believe we paid 60$/ person even though it was dinner. #wurth. lol . some people said it is 75$. Idk what happened but I'm not complaining lol. 

Oh yeh the kitchen stops at 10/1030pm [i forgot which one] and that's when the food starts to clear, so get your fill before that haha. 

Sadly did not take too many pics cause the lighting was bad and ...cause we were busy stuffing out faces

The waiting system is the worse. The kiosk is very unclear about next steps and doesn't clearly differentiate between phones and tickets.

There are essentially 3 waits. One in which you get a time estimate and are expected to go back to the buffet when you are called. The 2nd wait is to pay and this is most frustrating part. 90% of the people who are filtered through to pay are folks that paid $25 to skip the line. Now I understand this is part of Vegas, paying for privilege, but wtf. If you're a regular guest, you feel like a 2nd class citizen here, more than any other buffet in Vegas I've been to.

This buffet is simply over the top exhaustive in its offerings. They claim over 500 items, and I don't doubt that. They have stations for Italian, including pizzas and pastas, sushi, Mexican, meats, charcuterie, desserts, seafood, soups, salads, and on and on it goes. 

The meat area included a huge roast of waygu beef, the first slice of which was tough and rubbery. The second, rare piece I had, was much better, but still not what you would expect from wagyu. The prime rib was better. They have bacon too, both sliced and slab, the slab more of a braised belly. Why they put so much on your plate of each thing left me scratching my head, and feeling guilty for throwing so much food away. Bone marrow came out after a while, and that was pretty darn good too. Sausages and other miscellaneous meats of all kinds were also to be had, but you can only do so much, and I did three hours.

The sushi bar area changes fast, so it's good to keep checking. Rolls and pokes are replaced with other rolls and new pokes in a matter of minutes.

The Mexican area includes made to order tacos, and was a popular spot.

The seafood for me was really mixed. The crab legs, the long ones, come out at three and are very sweet. I liked those, but the oysters, also out at three, were muddy in flavor and not at all cold. They were of the large variety better suited for grilling than serving raw.

You can't really go wrong here with pleasing everyone, as there is literally something for everyone, and then some. Pay the up-charge for unlimited beer and champagne, but know that the sparkling is of the three or four dollar variety. 

Servers are quick to take your unwanted plates away, and let you pace yourself, as you brace for yet another plate of food.  While I tend to be buffet-phobic, I will likely eat here again, just because it was so much fun.

I got there at 2:30. Waited in line and paid at 3:07. Because we paid at 3:07, we were charged dinner prices. Fail. 

With tax, dinner is $55. While the buffet is good, quality is never as good as a fine dining restaurant. 

I hate how they split the king crab legs open. All that lost flavor! But its warm. But it has almost no crab flavor. 

The ramen broth is really good. :) 

The lamb chops were also really tasty. Fatty deliciousness. It's also cooked medium-rare-ish. I loved that!  

The ribs - salty. 

The prime rib - overcooked. 

I forgot what else I had, but I tend to stay away from fillers at a buffet.
Great sea food option, nice decoration & good options for vegetarians. Desert & drinks were great. Obviously pricy, but worth it once in a while.

If you are a diamond status (my dad) you don't have to wait long so we were very lucky! (otherwise it would've been an hour for our party of 13. We got the back corner table which was semi enclosed and felt like we were dining in our own private room. Def. worth the price with all the seafood and desserts along with complimentary glass of wine (for member) and champagne and excellent server who kept removing our plates! (for more)
Very good variety, love the different fruit and vegetable juices

I got in right away since my party was already inside but they waited less than 20 min on a Friday night, maybe it was a slow weekend.  I went straight for steamed king crab legs.  I believe this is the only buffet that serves steamed king crab legs?  Let me tell you, I won't be eating refrigerated cold crab meat ever again in Vegas.  It's ridiculously delicious when warm and dip it in butter.  Too bad they only serve you one plate at a time!  After many plates of crab legs, got a plate of oysters.  They were pretty good, they could have done a better job cleaning/rinsing so they won't be so gritty.  To finish my meal, got a plate or two of prime rib with au jus, I thought it was little too salty for my taste but good none the less.  I didn't try every single thing they offered since I was too busy filling myself with crab meat.  I got my money's worth just from king crab legs.  Yum!

We went to Wynn as well, but not nearly as good as here. If I live in Las Vegas, I will be here every weekend. 

A great selection of food, especially for my Asian taste. My favorite dishes include ramen noodles, dark-chicken soup and a white fish probably sea bass. But almost all dishes are executed very well. Nothing I saw look generic and each dish can easily go to a restaurant and be served individually. Think about it. It is actually a very high bar for a buffet place. Comparatively, a lot of items from Wynn probably can only be served at buffet or lower end restaurant. The food item options are quite limited as well. I wish I went to Wynn first and then to Bacchanal. I probably would not be this disappointed.

My boyfriend and I were a little disappointed by the initial wait, but I think it was because we had been driving for a while and we were starving. We soon discovered that this buffet was entirely worth all of the waiting. Not only does the buffet have extensive food options, but the food quality itself is incredible. The crab legs were probably our favorite. I personally really enjoyed the nachos, dim sum and the shrimp cocktail. The dessert bar is also excellent! Some of the desserts look too gorgeous to even eat. I really appreciated the gelato bar. I definitely recommend going at least once, just for the experience. The price is pretty high which is our only deterrent in terms of coming back again.

Although the wait is long, you can buy a $15 line pass!!!! This place is amazing!!! Even if you chose to wait, guaranteed it's worth it. The decor is B-E-A-U-tiful!!! There are so many options, so make sure you save room to try everything. The food is also NOT buffet quality!! The presentation and taste is something you would find in a 5-star restaurant. I've lived in Vegas my entire life and been to every buffet, but this tops them all. All the employees give amazing service and treat each and every person like a VIP. I love it here and plan on coming back all the time!!!!

I visited vegas recently and gave this place another try just because my friends wanted.   The second time around was much better service even though it was a busy Friday evening.  

4 stars for much better service experience.  

3 stars for food experience

$51.99 for lunch on Christmas Eve. 

I normally dislike buffets but this one was probably the best one I've tried. There is just so much variety. I didn't even have enough stomach room to try everything. My family and I decided we would all get something different and take bites of each item just so we would have room to try everything... nope, that did not happen. We missed out a lot of pastries and other items. Also, we went crazy with the warm king crab legs... mmm... so good. 

We arrived at 10:55 and sat down at 11:35 which wasn't bad. Because of the holidays, we only had 2 hours to eat but whatever, I don't think obesity was on my Christmas wish list anyway. 

Would I come here again? No. Bacchanal is ridiculously expensive. It was worth to try it once considering it is a new buffet and was recommended by a few friends. If I had it twice, then I would agree with some reviewers--overrated.

Bacchanal is a major improvement over the previous Caesars Palace buffet.
