In a city where buffets can be found in nearly every casino Bacchanal is a solid contender for one of the better ones but not the best.  Boasting 9 "action stations" that feature seafood, dim sum, sushi, a carving station, freshly squeezed juices, and gelato its easily one of the largest buffets on the strip.  

Comparing Bacchanal to Bellagio, Wicked Spoon (Cosmopolitan), and the Wynn, all have components that are very similar (large cocktail shrimp, sushi, carving station with prime rib, gelato, fancy little pastries, blah blah blah).  And they all have speciality items (bone marrow at Wicked Spoon, rack of lamb & Kobe beef at Bellagio).  Unfortunately because we went on a Saturday during brunch the speciality items like stone crab, oysters on the half shell, and made to order souffles were nowhere to be found. Needless to say my husband and I were disappointed. 

For $45/person I expected a bit more seafood and perhaps better executed dishes.  I was often disappointed with beautifully plated dishes that failed to deliver. The fried chicken & waffles looked good but was way overcooked, dry and under seasoned.  The cute fried quail egg on corned beef hash looked good but was oily and bland.  Dim sum was so-so and the sushi average.  I did, however enjoy the black chicken & dried scallop soup and Aztec chocolate gelato (chocolate, cinnamon, & chile).  My husband liked the chicken fried steak with country gravy and the sweet potato tots. 

The restaurant has an open feel to it and I appreciated the attentive service we received.  Plates were cleared quickly and drinks refilled often. 

Overall I'd say the Bacchanal brunch is overpriced for what you get. Personally for the price I'd much rather go to Bellagio or Wicked Spoon. But since we always stay at Caesars, I'm willing to give it another chance.  Next time I'm going to try the dinner. It's a few bucks more but I'm hoping that there will be more of the speciality items.

Super good buffet! Went on a Tuesday afternoon and it wasn't that busy... We went while it was lunch into dinner and glad we went in between times. Lots of variety of food...also had a dessert area to as well! Pricing was okay for lunch time it is pricey.. would recommend to go in between time to get the best of lunch and dinner! Service was nice.. but did take a little slow to get plates and drinks. I would come back again when I come back to Vegas!

Hot damn.

I feel like I say this every time we try a new buffet in Vegas, but that really was the best buffet meal I've had yet.

We barely squeaked in (well, I sat and played slots while my bf bartered with the hostess and scored us the last "tickets") so send a friend!

They really did a good job revamping this buffet though. I remember going last year and it being a sad little affair. Now there's a ton more space, multiple food stations and plentiful offerings. Was impressed with the little aguas frescas bar (horchata, yum!), the legit noodle bar, charcuterie offerings, decent dim sum, bacony brussels sprouts, staple prime rib, even raw oysters! Yes I braved trying them and didn't get sick. Only downside is some of the food is dry (kobe sliders, lamb chops)...big letdown. Figure that's par for the course at a buffet anyway.

The desserts take the cake. Ha. They had a yuzu-infused red velvet whoopie pie, oreo mousse topped with a cute mini oreo, plain & matcha creme brulee with legit sugar crust, cookies/cakes galore. Grab something from the ice cream case full of gelato and sorbet on your way out if you have any room left.

Three words: DOUGHNUT GELATO SANDWICH 

I had two. :)  The doughnuts are equivalent to large doughnut holes, and the Mexican Vanilla Bean Salted gelato was the perfect creamy compliment.  The strawberry balsamic and lemon basil gelato were also delicious and refreshing.

Despite this, both my husband and I agreed that the Oreo mousse was the best thing in the entire buffet.

What sets this buffet apart from others in Vegas is its Asian section.  Sure, everyone has a salad bar, an Italian section, a meat carving station, and seafood.  Bacchanal has six or seven different dumplings, Korean-style ribs, pad thai, sushi, and more.

We arrived at 11:30 AM on a Saturday morning in December, and only had a ten-minute wait or so.  Price was ~$45.00, and includes champagne.

Christmas Day dinner here. Call eve and got the price for holiday ,$60 instead of $50.. Went to get in line at 3pm.. Surprise they say it was sold out.. So they won't let people wait in line at all.. And then to milk u more, they say u can pay for express lane then u can eat here tonight. At $20 more per person.. Gotta be joking to hear a buffet sold out n then to pay more then its not sold out.. For almost $100 person , I don't even want to try..
Bacchanal was good food it's just i don't think i would pay that much money for the food!!! $70 ?!?!?!?

Overhyped.

Only word that came to mind after dining here.

We lucked out and there was no line to get our name on the waiting list.  After that we waited two hours.  Gambled and drank for awhile and finally checked back two hours later.  We were brought in and seated in the back corner by the Asian foods.

I was expecting my mind to be blown.  My girlfriend and I had been waiting since July to eat at the Bacchanal, so maybe we were expecting too much?  Everything seemed... meh.

My cuts of meat were 80% fat.  Perhaps I just got unlucky with my cuts?

To be honest, I enjoyed the buffet at the Wynn over the Bacchanal.

Big plus for the Bacchanal was the dessert section.

I'd pass on the Bacchanal next time I'm in Vegas.

at first, i was really excited to eat here. being rated number 1 buffet and everything, i thought i would give it a try. waited about an hour, but for good food it would be totally worth it. for a saturday lunch came out to about $55. i think the little skillet thing holder they give you is adorable but the grease of them? not so much.

all the chefs and servers are very friendly.. though there were alot of awkward moments when i put something on my plate and one of the chefs goes, "chef so and so made that! isnt he good?" and theres a bit of an awkward pause because I havent tried the dish... i cant tell you its good but i dont know what to say...  but they are all very friendly.
on the staff, the only part that kinda got to me was drinks. our drinks was never refilled, nor did they come by and ask if we wanted more. it was prob because they were super busy? but i would like more than one cup of lemonade for my 50 dollar meal... 

as for the food. they all look very exquisite. i wanted to eat everything. and i tried. my friend and i would share dishes just so we could try most of them.  i was looking for a dish that would make me want to go back and get more but it didnt happen. our verdict was.. greasy. the food is good but not what i had expected for a number 1 rated buffet.
desserts looked delicious but i have had better. for the first time, the macaroons were sour.. jam? maybe I am used to the way LA makes it... (Milk, bottega louie, mochilato, etc) but these were the first that i did not like.. 

i eat at ayce places pretty often but i was bloated and had this nasty feeling afterwards... i think its because of the grease...
if you havent tried it, by all means you should and judge for yourself. this place clearly has good reviews from other people. but i personally would not go again.
Over an hour wait, but well worth it. They have all types of food from different parts of the world. Everyone seems to be on top of the crab and shrimp line though.
Look, it's a buffet, so there can't be too much to say about it. HOWEVER, the red velvet bread pudding was earth-shattering. Staff was great!

First off, this buffet is way overpriced.  For $65 a person before tax, you're better off eating something else that's cheaper.  The quality was just meh...there was so much food yet nothing really stood out.  Maybe I expect too much, but for 65 a person??  It's so not worth it.  Save your money.  I would only go here if I got it for free or had a huge discount.

This was my first time at the buffet and I was very disappointed. I'm a loyal Bellagio The Buffet customer, as I've been countless times there and I ALWAYS go every time I visit Vegas (2 or 3 times a year), so I will use it as comparison. The process for the line was fine. You take a number and come back after the designated time and wait in line to get in. I hated how we got taken to our seats. They took 5 tables and we followed each other like a herd of cows to get to our tables. The staff even asked us to follow closer as to not get lost. It really isn't hard to follow the person in front of you so I was already not in the mood. Shortly after we were seated, we ordered drinks. My family likes to order 2 drinks each as non alcoholic beverages are included. The waitress proceeded to say "you don't need to order it all right now. You can order as you go" but in such a tone that she didn't want to assist us. Anyways, then we proceed to eat. The food selection is nice. The only thing better than The Buffet was their seafood. They had raw oysters, crab claws, and sea snails. Aside from that, everything seemed average. As we are the seafood, you can imagine we had a lot of plates with empty shells. The waitress was nowhere to be seen for 20+ minutes. She walked past us and ignored the fact that our small table was completely full of plates that needed to be taken away. So we couldn't even get more food. She never came to refill our drinks. I could never even get her attention. At the end of the 2 hours of dining (which I only knew was a thing because it quickly showed up on the screen when we paid), she proceeded to tell us our 2 hours was up. The cashier never told us. The waitress never told us. And she pretty much kicked us out. I have NEVER received that treatment at the Bellagio. Bellagio kindly asks for 2 hour dining at the bottom of the receipt but have NEVER asked me to get out. I was especially unhappy because at the "2 hr" mark we were eating dessert and getting ready to leave. If she had taken away our plates faster, I would have left before the 2 hours. Plus, you cannot expect that first timers at your buffet know about the 2 hr dining limit when it passes the screen in 1 second. If I wasn't paying attention, I wouldn't have known at all. There was no sign anywhere either. All in all, VERY unhappy with the AWFUL SERVICE. Will not be going back. Highly do not recommend for 1st timers. The Buffet at the Bellagio is impeccable service and better food. I had high hopes for this buffet and it is ranked #1, but needless to say, I won't be going back.

If you are going to try a buffet in Vegas, THIS is the one! So much food, and good food. We stocked up on the Seafood- crab legs, shrimp, and mussels. The quality was surprising for a buffet. Although the price is steep, the quality (and quantity) of the food justifies it. Also, don't forget to save room for dessert- recommend the gelato and  macaroons! The ONLY buffet we will return to in Vegas.

Sooooooo good!  Pricey,  so get a total rewards card,  you'll save a few bucks. They have an Asian section, Spanish,  American, seafood and the dessert section is huge! You'll have to ask them to heat your crab legs because they are served disgustingly cold. The lines can get very long sometimes, I think I waited an hour once. But definitely worth it,  a must try buffet in Vegas!

I've tried just about all the top buffets in Vegas now that I recently was able to visit the Bacchanal.

My rating is based on this buffet compared to all other buffets in Vegas--and even buffets everywhere else I've tried.

I'm not going to mark stars down to compare a buffet to some fine dining Michelin star restaurant. I'm just reviewing this place as it is--a buffet, compared to other buffets.

The Bacchanal is as great as you've heard and/or seen. The decor is not as chic or extravagant like others (Wynn, Wicked Spoon), but it's still a nice clean space. 

We got in right before the end of breakfast. There is no stoppage in service like some buffets--most notable being Wicked Spoon. Some places shut down so you can't stay during the transition. No problem here. We got unlimited mimosas as well.

There are so many pictures already of the food from others. All I can say is it is a bit overwhelming. Everything looked and tasted pretty darn good for a buffet. The sushi actually tasted legit. The crab were all claws. They were Jonah Crab, and as mentioned all claws. The were always stocked and tasted great! The desserts were amazing. Including the gelato. I think Wicked Spoon may have a little better gelato, but its not that huge of a difference. Just like the food, I'm a bit overwhelmed on what to right about. There are so many reviews already so you have an idea what to expect.

The staff was great, but maybe we got extra attention because we had that Diamond member VIP status? 

Yes you will be paying a pretty penny, but you have a lot of high quality food to pick from. You should already know yourself and your eating habits. If you don't think you will make the most from a buffet, then don't eat at one. Vegas is filled with a lot of fine dining spots. But if you are a buffet lover, be prepared to have this place become the standard in which you compare most other buffets.

The only other "buffet" that is touted to be better than this is the "Sterling Brunch".  That is the only other I have yet to try, and one day I will, when I'm ready to shell out $100 for it.

Believe the hype. 

We waited in line for about half an hour....paid and got seated before too long. Then came the feasting that began at the Asian section and ended with the seafood section.  I can't remember it all, it was a blur from buffet line to table and back to line. Dear reader, please appreciate that my wife and her sister cannot stop talking, but for the duration of the meal they were too busy conversing with their plates to talk with each other. Silent it was, yet the waiter was afraid to put his hands near  our table, lest he get caught up in the carnage and devoured before anyone noticed. 

Yeah. It was like that. 

I was amused by the carving station. I was in line when they brought out a piece of pork loin, and watched it fall apart tenderly when it was paid on the carving table. An audible murmur went through the line like they were watching some kind of magic show. 

Now that you've had your fill...make your way over to the desert station! Deep dish chocolate chip cookies? How about apple cobbler?  How about watermelon mint ice cream on a hazelnut coated cone? 

Its pricey. There is a possibility you'll be made to wait a while. So what, its worth it to me.

A great buffet with many selections and a variety of foods.  Pricey, but you can eat as much as you want of costly food such as oysters, crab legs, etc.  Service is ok, our server seemed like she wasn't happy but I have a feeling that happens often working in Las Vegas and dealing with tourist all of the time.  Overall happy we went but I'm not sure I would go again.

This place is unbelievable. My family and I went here for a Sunday Brunch, and we were not disappointed. Quite honestly, if the other best buffets on the strip are even close to this, I would give a 5 star to all of them.

This place has everything. From seafood to delicious breakfast, from mimosas to cucumber juice. Seriously, there were things of cucumber juice. We tried the food from most of the stations, and we honestly were very happy with all of it. The most impressive was perhaps the dessert bar, and I greatly enjoyed the shrimp and crab. 

The most impressive thing was the mimosa refilling! I'm used to servers kind of forgetting about you at a buffet, or at least not being constantly present. Here they instantly topped off mimosas that were running low, and brought us new coffee within a minute of asking for it. It was incredible, and it did its job of getting us all pretty buzzed and chowing down on tons of food. 

The price is steep, but it is WELL worth it to experience at least once. It is truly something to be remembered, and all we could do is gawk at the outrageous amount of choices we had when some people are so much less fortunate. To think that places like this exist...well, it's just incredible. Truly a bacchanal!

Sadly I have to update my prior review of this place. I visited on October 2013 and I was so happy with my overall experience that I mistakenly made it a point to visit again on Feb 16, 2014.


          For starters this is currently the "#1 buffet" in Vegas and its advertised everywhere you go in Vegas thus making it extremely popular. I firmly believe that it started out as a wonderful buffet. However now it has gone down the drain with its horrible customer service.

          For instance as you approach the buffet you are assaulted with big crowds of people trying to figure out what to do. Moreover as you get a glimpse of what everyone is crowding around its a monitor that allows you to input your party information. It then prints out a ticket informing you of the wait time encouraging you to go the surrounding shops and or casino instead of waiting in line and you will receive a text message letting you know when your time is up. (for me it was a 2 hour and 30 minute wait) The idea of it all is great. However in practice it is extremely unpractical to believe that crowds of people visiting your establishment will figure out exactly what to do with those little monitors. Consequently making it a big confusion for a lot of the patrons visiting the establishment. Then finally when you see a human face Patrons flock to the person asking him/her what are the steps to sign in. The "hostess' rudely responds that you must use the monitor with no inclination to assist you in using it. Granted it is not rocket science here in the states similar monitors are now everywhere with "self checkout" being extremely popular. However I feel that she was incredibly inconsiderate to people asking for assistance. More importantly there are patrons that truly do not understand the concept of checking in  on a monitor. I can understand that she is probably assaulted with the same question over and over again and it might be incredibly overwhelming to repeatedly answer the same question.
 


         However  rudeness is never acceptable. Secondly and more importantly after patiently waiting for an over two hours I directed to my table. Ironically the restaurant is beautifully designed however there where empty tables everywhere with dirty dishes stacked on them. It seems as if they paid so much attention to detail however the dirty dishes throw away all that effort.  It definitely killed my appetite. After 15 minutes of waiting we still had no waitress no utensils no drinks. I quickly became infuriated at the fact that I had wasted TWO HOURS of my life waiting to enter this dirty restaurant with incredibly inconsiderate staff. I asked the "hostess" if our waitress/waiter would show up anytime soon with which she replied " she is making her rounds." I was FLABBERGASTED. I have no problem with waiting my turn however after paying $60 dollars a plate and waiting more than 2 hours to be seated I expect for them to have it more under control and at the very least have some kind of human empathy. I WILL ABSOLUTELY NEVER AGAIN VISIT THIS ESTABLISHEMENT AND DO NOT RECOMMEND ANY ONE TO SPEND A DOLLAR HERE. The food is ok but for the most part Rio offers the same food for a fraction of the wait time and better customer service. Mc Donald's workers have better training and service than the workers at this place.

For the price and the hype, it didn't impress me. 
Went for brunch, and was pleasantly surprised by my constant OJ refill haha. So +1.

Foods to stack up on: crab, oysters, and that dessert bar ;) 

Coming in 2nd: the filet mignon, sirloin, interesting juices (green, red, check the smoothies section).

Avoid? 
Probably the sushi. The mini poke plate is fine, but the sushi? Looked sad, dry, unwanted :( 
Maybe dim sum because it was the same old same old, but that's more a personal preference to reserve my stomach space for more important foods.

Bacchanal, you got me again! I thought maybe, just maybe I had an off day. Nope. This was a very busy evening, and after a two and a half hour wait, was uber disappointed. Our service did not exist. None. Nada. Zer-o. No refills. Barely took plates. Not call me crazy, but when you end up paying almost 70/person for a meal, you kiiiiiinda want someone to at least pretend you are there. So that was terrible. I had better service the last time I ate at Waffle House (ooooooh buuurrn) 

Now to the food. We kept telling our friends how huge the place was and the diversity. Well it was still huge and there was diversity, but it seemed like instead of having more dishes, they just put repeats out. So fries on a plate, then at the far end of the  area, in baskets. This was done with several dishes, and none were good. It was the crap like onion rings... Very very disappointing. The salad was great. The Asian buns were delicious and fresh, and as usual the breads, charcuterie are fabulous. Oh and the horseradish is knock your socks off, take your breath away (literally) amazing. But at the end of the day, I didn't find one thing at the buffet I could justify trying twice, other than those items aforementioned. 

Dessert was better than last time.  It seemed like there were more options. Creme brulee also seemed to taste better.

Bottom line. Not a great experience. We paid almost three hundred dollars and would have had a better experience at Green Valley Ranch. Oh well.

The first time I tried to go to Bacchanal Buffet in December, the wait was crazy.  The machines where you get your wait time said that I had to wait like 8 hours to get in line.  I was curious about the hype about this place, so we gave a second try this time when we were in Vegas.  

We were lucky this time to get there just in time before it started to get busy for their brunch on Sunday.  We got there right before 10am, so there was almost no line for us to be seated.  Once we were seated, we were greeted by the server and he was very attentive and refilled our drinks throughout.  Since it was Sunday brunch time, mimosa was part of the buffet price, so we definitely took advantage of that.

It has huge selections of foods and I liked them a lot.  They had breakfast foods, pasta, omelet station, noodle station, seafood station.. I can clearly see why this buffet was attracting so many crowds.  The only thing that I was disappointed was the sushi station.  Maybe it is because it was still earlier of the day, but they only had one plate of sushi roll plate while we dined.  At first they had a california roll but they changed it to a veggie roll but I did not see much of other options when it came to sushi /sashimi.  I am assuming it is because of the timing of the day that we dined and I didn't get to check the foods again when they started switching the foods later on.  However, regardless, we enjoyed almost everything we tried.  For dessert station, I was happy with the crepe station and the gelato station.  They had other cookies and cakes and other dessert options, but I was not too into them to try.  

Before I came to this buffet, Wicked spoon had been my favorite buffet in Vegas.  Foodwise, I think their foods were better, especially my last experience at Wicked spoon was less impressive.  However, Wicked spoon's dessert section still is more impressive as they have chocolate dipped strawberries and french macaroons which are one of my favorite dessert items.  However, regardless, I enjoyed my experience at Bacchanal buffet and I would definitely come back!

Food: 4 stars
Atmosphere: 4 stars
Service: 4 stars
Overall Experience: 4 stars

Overrated and mediocre would probably be the best way I could describe this buffet.  My husband and I were here this past weekend for "Easter dinner" in which they upped the prices to 70pp (normally 60).  Not sure if I already had high expectations but I was expected to be blown away at this price.  We were a bit disappointed.  The sushi variety basic and quality was subpar.  The dinner rolls were cold and hard.  The brisket was dry. The crab claws were bland.  There wasn't much king crab legs, which we were looking forward to.  They did have plenty of snow crab legs.  My husband did enjoy the bone marrow.  I liked the prime rib which was juicy and had good flavor.  The sauce on the scallops was amazing but sadly the scallops were over cooked.  I think the best thing I had was the shrimp cocktail which is not saying much.  I did also enjoy the dessert station although the macaroons were a bit hard.  We won't be back.

This buffet was a bit high priced, I mainly went for the seafood offering and the only crab legs I saw being served (hot and cold) were snow crab... at the price they were charging was hoping for a much better selection.. pretty much became an ordinary buffet, though I did get my fill of crab legs.

As a fan of Wicked Spoon, I thoroughly enjoyed my brunch at Bacchanal - but not enough to turn my back on my beloved.

My top items: Fried chicken with sweet potato fries (although the tater tots are better!), Korean BBQ, the endless crab legs and the deep fried cinnamon sugar donut. Most of the other items we tried such as the dim sum, breakfast standards, and the sliders were good but nothing worth mentioning. I was VERY sad that the pho and ramen stations weren't available for brunch, perhaps we came in too early around 11:30AM.

Don't forget to try the fresh squeezed juices! The horchata and cucumber juice were definitely our favorites. Champagne and mimosas are also complimentary, which make the $45 price well worth it.

The best buffet in Vegas in my 25 years visiting here. Asian Italian Mexican American seafood etc...you name it! Be ready to eat. You won't be disappointed. Food prepared to order as well. Fresh juices during breakfast or brunch.
Food was amazing. Great variety and quality. Service was stellar. Exceeded my expectations for a buffet experience.

I love Vegas for the awesome buffets.  Caesar's really delivers a feast.  My bf & I came here for brunch on Saturday.  We got the bottomless mimosas which barely ever made it to the bottom.  The food here was awesome.  There is really too much to talk about, but let me just say there was an endless supply of delectable eats to surpass anyone's expectations for a satisfying meal.  The desserts were top notch.  The Chinese food in the corner was yummy goodness.  You can have a bowl of ramen, udon or rice noodles with pork.  Gorge on shrimp dumplings as you please.  The Italian meatballs are soft, juicy and teaming with Italian spices.  I only allowed myself to sample the pesto pasta despite craving more.  The potato and chorizo Mexican dish was all about a nuance of flavors.  Pig out on all the shrimp cocktail, mussels and crab legs you want.  I like how they slice the crab legs in half here.  That means you don't have to do any cracking.  If you want a regular breakfast with scrambled eggs, bacon and sausage, they have that too.  

The staff is friendly here, and the ambiance here is the best ever for a buffet.  The glass dividers, fancy chandeliers and lighting scheme here do not give the impression of a buffet.  This is how it's done!

As a local, this is the only Vegas buffet I will go to. The price is very hefty but well worth it. The sushi bar and seafood area are my favorites but there is not one bad plate there. The fruit juices they have are amazing and fresh. I would recommend this buffet to anyone.

If you're in the mood for mountains of food, this is the place for you. Their selection of seafood was great, but nothing stood out taste wise. The best thing that I had by far was the sweet potato tater tots. The massive dessert bar with almost anything that you could imagine on it was fun to peruse. I had a gorgeous pecan tart that was pretty tasty. Made me with that my wife was there to enjoy it as well!

The greatest buffet out there!

Very nice selection of seafood. Crab legs absolutely delicious there. 

Yum, desserts! Very nice selection of case and little parts. Kudos on there sesame ice cream I found and whipped cream.

wow! this buffet was outstanding! the king crab legs are literally to dieeee for. the service was quick and did i say how good the crab legs were?? i plan on coming back here on my next trip to vegas!!

I am happy to say I've finally tried the famous Caesars palace buffet! And I was honestly impressed by the options they had available. I watched many YouTube videos in preparation of this exact moment in my life. We went in on a Saturday right before the dinner time price started. Can you say crab!!? Honestly I was first drawn to the cold snow crab legs and the rock crab they had on display at the front, but what I didn't figure out initially was that there was another room in the back! HA silly me! That's where they had the steamed crab legs! Not only did I get to enjoy some of the lunch food options they had available but when those dinner foods came out mmmmmmmmm. One of the differences that I saw was that they opened up the noodle bar at dinner time, there was a couple of more expensive food options and crab was still be served at both times I went. Here's the only reason I'm not giving this place 5 stars, THEY KICKED US OUT AFTER THE 2HOURS :( they absolutely stuck true to the limit. Which is fine, but I don't think they were respectful by it, but honestly when you're serving the kind of crowds they are I don't blame them. I will definitely go back!

This place gets two stars ONLY because the food was decent and the best thing were the desserts. 

ADVICE: Do not go if the line is really long. You'll wait on line about an hour just to pay to get in and then wait ANOTHER 20-30 minutes for the carving and seafood stations. This is true ESPECIALLY on holiday weekends. 

The above advice comes from first hand experience and in talking with the servers. I wish I knew this before hand but it was so hyped up that it was like a must see like the water show in front of the Bellagio! 

It was pure chaos in the dining room and I even saw a verbal confrontation when some people tried to cut in for seafood. The seafood line blended/meshed with the carving station, no one knew what was what and NO manager was on site to help. A simple roped off line would of even helped. The way this place is organized is just a mess simply put. Did I mention what a mess this place was? I think you get the message. 

Go when it's quiet and go somewhere else when this place is busy. Not worth the heartache (or heartburn).

The wait time is ridiculously long. We waited 1 hour. The food is great and the service from the waiters are top notch. The seafood section is amazing. fresh and tasty. The asian section is "ok", they need to add or replace a few in their menu. The rest is outstanding. Would I come back? Maybe. Until they fix the wait time, I would have to go around and search for "the spot".

Always one of my favorite buffet in Vegas when we visit!

Tons of food. Love all the deserts there. Love that they have fresh crepe made to order. Love the basil lemon ice cream

So much hype! I heard such great things about this expensive buffet so we had to try. The first visit was just ok. WAY too many people, extremely long lines and price was high. My friend however loved it so we tried again. Same experience in my opinion. They do have a large selection of food. Unfortunately I prefer quality over quantity and this simply did not deliver either time. Was forced to go a third time for a Christmas luncheon. Again, nothing to change my mind. I really tried to like it.

This is my favorite buffet in Vegas. If you're willing to splurge, this is the place to do it. Bacchanal is located inside caesars palace, and weekend dinner price is $60. They have such a big variety of food and everything is so good! The downside to bacchanal is that the wait time can be very long during rush hours. Other than that, I see myself coming back here whenever I'm in Vegas.
This is by far one of the best buffets I had while experiencing vegas! Food is presented nicely and the taste is out of this world. Would definitely go back on my next visit.
Best in Vegas ! buffet quality is way above the rest.clean, great spot

Love this place, every time I visit Vegas this is a must to eat at. Yes it is pricey but it well worth the money. There must be over 500 items of Food to choose from. It has to be in the Top 5 Best Buffet's in Vegas! You will not regret this spot

Great experience at this buffet, no lines too enter at all. My server Alvaro Gomez is one of the best servers I have had here in Las Vegas. The seafood station was absolutely amazing!!! Each station was amazing! Alvaro bought us steam crab legs and they were too die for! Absolutely the best buffet in town!

I went to this buffet on a tuesday night and the lineup was very long, it was 20 and 30 minute wait time. this buffet we were looking forward to it because it was said to have cost 17 million to build. and one of the highest recommended ones. so we had a lot of expectations coming in. 

The buffet costed us 65 per person after tax. when we walked in the buffet you noticed a lot of choices in terms of seafood, and many varieties of different cultures food. including a lot of asian style food, as well as western style foods. The type of seafood includes king crab leg, lobster, scallops, jumbo shrimp, and many varieties of sea fish that clearly tasted fresh.

the seafood choices came in various varieties of cooking, including some asian style crab and oysters. with bbq and raw depending on what you may like. 

the butter lobster and chinese stir fried crab, and cocktail shirmp are all a must try, as they are definitely high end restaurant quality. the seafood selection was simply amazing. 

the roasted beef and lamb was also good, and they also had a lot of speciality items such as beef wellington the British dish.  as well as a mexican section, with speciality non alcoholic drinks, as well the basic pop and juice.

The desert layout was very diverse, they had a macroon mountain and 6-7 cupcake flavours that were tasty and pretty. 

The service was top notch, it was very friendly and efficient. such as we asked for hot water, and they anticipate our needs by giving us teapots as well as tea sets, and a variety of honey to choose from. 

I would strongly recommend people to try this buffet on any vegas trip. as it is simply amazing.

The line is really long on weekends, but I totally recommend it if its your first time.  Buffet interior is really modern and spacious, and you can see a lot of the chefs cooking at each station.

What stood out for me was the lamb chops, prime rib, and oysters.  I do not know how they can get get such a perfectly cooked mass production of lamb chops.  Best part of the meal, hands down.  Lamb chops are pink the in the middle  Prime rib comes second, wow.  This however you can ask the chef how you want it cooked.  Third, the oysters.  There was 4 guys working literally the whole night cracking them open.  Some of the people at the restaurant were taking twenty at a time it seemed, which was kind of ridiculous, consider the time it was taking to open each one.  It seemed every time they put oysters out, it would need immediate replacement.

For the desert, I actually really liked the baked cookie, and their ice cream selection.  There was watermelon mint, baklava, sour cherry, some random flavors I had never had.  Great touch.

Whenever I'm in Vegas, I always make time for either a brunch or dinner here. I've also tried the wicked spoon and know that this is the better buffet spot in comparison. Try to come early if you're with a big group because the lines here are pretty outrageous at times. 

Their tacos and crab legs are absolutely amazing. Other items on their seafood bar such as oysters and clams aren't very fresh. They also have amazing asian duck and seasonal dishes that make for a different experience each time I come here!

Would I think of this place as great value tho? NOT really, its not for those that don't have a stomach. I was full within 3 dishes but they offer a great selection of food with GOOD quality as well.

From prime rib to seafood all you can eat on a higher scale.  It's really fit for a king or queen.  In the 90's, bellagio was known for buffets.  Mid 2006, Wynn was top notch.  And 2016, bacchanal at Cesar's, beats all competition.

Not sure how long the wait usually is, but dropped in here on a late Sunday evening, and the wait was minimal! What I like about this buffet is that it felt like a tapas-esque experience. Small plates, bountiful variety of flavors, and diverse cuisines to try. Nevertheless, it was an imperfect and ultimately, underwhelming experience. Most of the foods I tried weren't memorable and the flavors were on the bland side. This is ironic, but take all Yelp reviews of this buffet with a grain of salt: they'll hype this place up too much. There were two or three dishes I did truly love, but I think this buffet was worth it just for the opportunity to try foods I ever have before all in one place. Also, the guy who worked at the dessert station tried hitting on my friend by "creating" a special dessert for us, served with his phone number. Yeah, the dessert was just fruit with whipped cream and chocolate syrup spread on top...which I believe is an accurate metaphor for this dining experience: charming demeanor, but unoriginal on a closer glimpse.

So beware.  Super crazy getting in here for lunch or dinner during the holidays.  Maybe other times too but we tried for lunch and wait was 5 hours.  But if you come early (say before 10 am) you can get in at a reasonable time.  

Brunch buffet was a nice spread that included sparkling wine.   Omelettes, lots of shellfish, chicken dishes, potato, mini pancakes and waffles, sushi, and much much more.  Of course there are deserts and sweet rolls.  Main thing lacking was decent bread.  Found croissants and some other ones but no rolls anywhere.  

Good overall was pretty good and fresh.  Waitresses did a great job keeping the glasses and cups full and tables clear.  

Worth a try but not worth a long wait in my opinion.

I have to give this one a 3, just because I didn't feel the price was worth the buffet and line waiting experience (unless you're going for platters of oysters, crab legs and prime ribs then yea you'll break even quickly).   The oysters were also not the freshest but I reckon that's kind of expected with buffet bars.  However, they do have a wide selection of buffet items so there's probably something for everyone!  I might recommend trying the buffet around town (not in hotels) which are often less expensive and just as good :)
five stars for being what it is, one of the top buffets in vegas

This was a great buffet, no doubt at all.  However, for the cost-equivalent to some of the excellent steak houses on the strip, I would go that way next time.   We showed up at 430 and waited ended up getting seated about 6 on a Saturday.

I went to the Bacchanal Buffet this past Friday night. It was NG. I really do not think it is worth what I paid. My husband and I have heard how great the buffet was. We were excited about going to try it because they claim they are the best buffet in Vegas. We paid $116.73 for two. Alcohol is an additional charge. We had two glasses of white wine for $18 including the tip. The total bill was about $135 for two people.
I saw a dirty, disgusting spot on the chair when the host seated me. They switched the chair for me when I pointed out the problem to them. However, they simply swapped it with a chair from another table.

The food selection was low. There was an Asian section. Chinese dishes were typical cheap American Chinese food. Crab was soaked in a heavy soy sauce starch gravy.  There was a couple of dim sum. The fillings of those dishes were not fresh, skin was on the thick side. On top of that, they really did not taste that good. Japanese food included a few typical rolls and they were mediocre at best. My husband tried the pizza, he said it was all right. If you like cheese, you will not find any good ones here. The selection was poor, and they were old and cheap. I tried yellow cheddar, white cheddar and Brie, and that was pretty much all they had. 

Italian assuage was OK. Sea bass was terrible. They were cold and old. Crab legs has nothing special to mention. Dessert was just OK. I have had better ones somewhere else. I am disappointed about them. They said the buffet included soft drinks, but that does not include latte. I chose the coffee at the end of the meal. It was not that good at all. I believe it was cheap coffee. 

Overall, I believe they have cut corners. The ingredients are on the cheap side. Believe me, there is no such thing as dishes made to order on the spot. It turned out to be false talk that they have been putting in people's ear. I truly regret going there. I ended up eating some cheap (at a high price) food that I normally do not eat. My definition for this buffet is "cheap" ingredients + American cooking techniques + fancy name ( I am looking at you BACCHANAL) = TV dinner in Caesars Palace . I HATE IT. If you do not believe me, please go find out by yourself. 
if you need any advice where to eat in Vegas (and it probably won't cost as much as Bacchanal Buffet) you should try "Joe's Stone Crab" at Cesars, "Social House" for Japanese food in Crystal and "Sushi Roku" in Caesars (with a great strip view) is good to me, along with Mon Ami Gabi in Paris.

Great brunch buffet! So many choices, there's no way you'd leave hungry. Prime rib for breakfast - yes! The pastries were amazing, the mimosas were delicious, I'd highly recommend this place. We used a Groupon to go, but it's so good we would've paid full price anyway. The eloquent environment was a pleasure to the dining experience. The meat display was so unbelievable that even a vegetarian couldnt resist the appealing aroma. Two thumbs up

We have dined there twice this month...

Very good food and selections of entrees and side dishes.....however, the dessert section is not up to par with the buffet...no pies or cakes....just little macaroons. Would love to see a little variety

We had a brunch at here. All the Asian food was not good. And they don't have things like   hot sauce and ketchup on the table which is not very convenient. But the dessert island was very impressed. Over all ,it is still is a good place for a buffet experience.

They gave my husband a hard time about dress code.  Apparently the hostess did not like the tank he had on and refused to let him in citing that this was a "family restaurant".  To give you some context, it was a white tank with a girl wearing a bikini.  That's it...no foul language,  no nipples, nothing that would make it inappropriate and of all places especially Vegas.   But whatever,  he turned his tank inside out and she let him in.  What a witch.
So on to the food.  This was my second time trying a buffet in Vegas.  My first was at the Bellagio and it was amazing!   Since this one was so much expensive than the Bellagio one assumed it would be better.  But definitely not the case.  For the price the food was mediocre at best.  Yea they had oysters but some were definitely bad if you know what I mean.  Also the shrimp and snow crab did not look fresh. 
They're dessert bar is bigger than Bellagio but not better.  They have gelato here and the macaroons were good too. Everything else was bleh.

One of the best buffets on the strip and I've been to a few.

So many options from lunch til dinner. Be prepared to pay $50, but trust me it's worth it. For lunch/brunch they have unlimited mimosas of different flavors, they have full breakfast, to crab legs, to sushi to pizza etc etc. .. anything you could think of they probably have it. Dessert was also on point. 

They say you have a 2 hour limit, but there's no way for them to track it unless you literally spend like 5 hours in there. So, take lots of breaks, drink lots of mimosas and get your money's worth!!

DO NOT EAT THE OYSTERS... I was sick for over a day after eating the oysters here. How do I know? Well everyone in our group ate the same thing over the course of two days, the one thing that was different was the buffet. Sure, it could have been something else at the buffet, but everyone else in my group refused to eat the oysters except me. I gave it three stars because everything else was pretty good there, especially for a buffet. Was it worth the $65? I don't think so...

This buffet is not worth the price. The food is subpar at best. Crab legs aren't even whole. They cut them in half to make it look like a lot. The food was about as good as Golden Corral. No lie,  save your money and go to Searsucker across the hotel. Food is definitely worth the price. The other reviews are paid for posting.  Better yet, leave the hotel and take a cab to Fogo de Chao which is a for real 5 star quality meal. This buffet just has a bunch of junk.
Love this place! I enjoyed every single thing about this buffet except the wait. We did arrive a bit early during the day so the line wasn't too long yet. Yes, always save room for dessert!

I have been eating there for brunch and dinner for two days. I vote them the best buffet compare to wynn, bellagio, paris, and rio. The waiting line is not as long as I expected. Their dessert is the best. highly recommend.

Great selection on everything. It is $15 for all you can drink sangrias, beer, wine and mimosas. I tried mimosas and sangrias and they were great. Come before 3 pm so you can stay for dinner menu at lunch prices.

Horrible!  If you can not accommodate any more people you need to stop giving them inaccurate information.  Went to kiosk which said we will receive a text to come back with an approximate time.  Did not get!  Prior to that we asked since the wait was long if what time it was closed (11) and if we would still get to eat even if we don't get to the front by then (line super long).   She was like oh yea...you will be able to eat.  930 still no text even them approximate time was 9pm.  We went anyway and the new person was like well they take all the food away at 11pm.  Had I known all this I would have just found another place to take my family.  I think it's shameful that you don't just tell people straight that they may not get to eat.  I just can't believe we waited 3.5 hours for nothing.  It's a holiday (Thanksgiving)...I knew we would have to wait long but we waited but are not even going to be able to eat.  How is that fair?

Asked my friends which buffet to go to in Vegas and they all said Bacchanal in Caesars.  I normally love the buffet at Bellagio, but since EVERYONE told me to go here..I just had to try it.

And IT WAS AMAZING!!  Best presentation and quality for a buffet ever!  I wish I could go back and just live in this buffet.. It has everything you could want and more.  

Street tacos they make fresh on the spot (get the al pastor), hot crab legs already split for you with sides of drawn butter, and an insane dessert station!  Was surprised to see many varieties of mochi ice cream here, drool.

The only thing missing was the xiao liang bao that everyone talked about that I guess they didn't have this one day.

Still though, most amazing buffet ever.  Plus, there's a Britney Spears slot machine near the buffet, so I know I'll be back!

Really great buffet. Can't say if it's the best in Vegas but it's gotta be top 5. The selection of food and quality was really top notch stuff. That would explain its price per person, gotta pay for that kind of quality. I personally loved the carver station but no matter what you eat it's gonna be great!

Seriously the BEST in Las Vegas! My girlfriend and I came on over during EDC weekend and the food and selection (it was our first time here) was absolutely amazing! Variety is an A+++ and food quality is right up there too! Service was meh, but it was super busy while went there for a late lunch. I still dont care. I will always hype this place up for anyone wanting the best LV buffet!

Honestly, I'm pretty disappointed after hearing all the hype for the buffet. It seems to have just been my luck though, compared to my friends. The wait wasn't too bad, about 40 minutes that we were waiting inside the casino. They have a system where they can text you when you return to get into yet another lineup/wait.

I started on the seafood section of the buffet, which I loved. Crab legs everywhere, there was a lobster bisque, and shrimp and grits. Felt like I started off strong. While I was eating, my friends had arrived with a nice plate of meat, but the line was long so I waited for later.

Next I moved onto the back area of the buffet to the Asian section. This was decent, and there was even salmon and tuna poke that I was lucky enough to grab.

Remember how I said I waited for the meat for later? Turns out that was a mistake. By the time that I got to the meat, every single slice that I received was more well than medium. Some pieces felt like I was chewing for a solid minute to be able to make it digestible. Makes me sad, because my friends definitely came back earlier with the same cuts and had some red showing.

Tables weren't cleared at all for us until right near when we were getting ready to grab desserts, which meant that our table was getting a little full. Thankfully our table was only 3 of us so we had a spot to put things.

The desserts section looked top notch, and I wish I had more space to eat all of them as this point. This is also where the crêpe station was.

All in all, it didn't blow me away and I wouldn't go out of my way to come back.

We book this ahead of time. Yes they make you sign a contract with a group of over 15 if you want to make reservations. You don't get point for rewards or any discounts. I though it was going to be great as my daughter had said it was a great place. But I have to say it wasn't worth $65 a person for a party of 18 and you have to do the tip included  The food was ok on a Saturday brunch day with no mimosas (I though a brunch always or at least a nice one to offer mimosas. Yes it was my 50th birthday get together with family. I would just get them all the 24 hour Buffet deal next time so we get a chance to try them all and see witch one has better Customerservice and better food and mimosas included please. Wasn't impressed at all. It was nice but not worth it. The line wasn't long at all at 11am " Now I know and won't be back"

Best.
Buffet.
Ever.
.

Everything that I ate here was good. Even the small shao long bao's were good, and they are never good at buffets! Even the gyoza's were good and those are never good at any place other than a true asian joint. Even the pho was good and that's sometimes not even good at pho places.

The only thing that's wrong with Bacchanal? They serve Pepsi instead of Coke. Change that up and they will take over the world.

If you are a vegetarian there's not lot of options for you. The tomato soup tasted horrible, hot n sour soup was good. The chef don't speak English so they can't tell you more about the food at display, you have to go with your instinct about what to eat and what not to eat. Don't taste random things if you have food allergy, menu doesn't specify ingredients.

What a disappointment! My family planned to go the buffet while in town and ran across so many issues, we never actually made it in. The wait list electronic system allows you to "save a spot in line" and gives you a ticket to come back. Our ticket was for nearly four hours later. We (begrudgingly) came back a little earlier than our ticket and was told we can't pay or get in line until the exact time on our ticket (9:19 pm). Our ticket said return to pay - not wait in line for another HOUR before even getting in, and there was a line at the seating station as well. After nearly five hours of being drug around trying to get in, we left. Word to the wise, if you want to go to this buffet, expect to be waiting or if you're not patient and want to eat the same day - to go else where.

What a disappointment for 2018! 
I have always been a fan of Bacchanal Buffet, but not today, especially the first weekend of 2018!
The seafood was extremely bland, no favor, and way too salty.
My brother and I were looking forward to feast on the king crab legs, but came to find out that we would have to pay an extra $55/pd if we want to have king crabs. 
WTF????
The wait was not that bad, about 45 mins, since we got here at 5:30, before the dinner rush. However, for $60/pp, I'm no longer impressed.
I live in Vegas for more than 10 years and seen the ups and downs of buffets. I was hoping that Bacchanal would be different but sadly, their quality go down.
I doubt that I'll be back to this Buffett anytime soon.

I really wanted to like this buffet.  In comparison to the wicked spoon or the buffet at Wynn it just didn't measure up.  They had a lot of options, but I think they fell short on quality, at least for lunch.  The dessert options were also limited and with such great reviews from other yelpers I expected this to be the new go to buffet in Las Vegas.  Hopefully the quality has improved since I've last dined here and maybe I'll give it a second try.

I don't think any Vegas trip is complete without experiencing at least a Buffet restaurant...at least I can't remember any Vegas trip that I've taken where we didn't eat at one! Over the years we usually go to the Bellagio or Wynn buffet, but this time around, we heard interesting news about the Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars being the new "it" buffet and decided to give it a try (friends also agree that Bacchanal's new set-up is one of the best in Vegas).

We got there as early as we could for dinner and there was already a line forming - the wait wasn't ridiculously long (thank goodness) and they actually have a computerized interactive check-in system for when the line gets very long to help minimize wait time, so that's pretty cool!

They have a large variety of food options and the service was actually pretty good for a buffet! Their dessert station is easily the largest I have ever seen at any buffet - I literally went for at least 3 rounds before I was able to try everything I possibly could stuff myself with!

Everyone says this is the best buffet in vegas but I think it's one of the biggest and one of the sub par buffets. I may have missed it when they were putting out the 5 star stuff. I personally enjoyed the dessert bar here more than the food. The price was something I feel that for that amount of money that you're paying there should be something that stands out here besides offering crab legs which BTW weren't that great. I did enjoy the street tacos but again I felt like it was just mediocre. Honestly IMO I could do without eating here you're really not missing much compared to other buffets. Maybe I'll give it another shot and see if I can muster up at least a 4 star rating. As for now I wish I enjoyed eating here the first time but maybe next time.
One of the best buffets in Vegas! Clean, high quality, well prepared and nicely varied food. Love the place!

Still love the food but hate the long 3-part wait lines for Sunday dinner.  At 6pm, we registered at one of the buffet kiosks and got a paper slip telling us to return at 7:17pm to pay.  At 7:17pm, we stood in the cashier line for 50 minutes before reaching a cashier.  After paying, we stood in another line for 20 minutes before we were led to a table...total wait time was 2.5 hours.
The buffet gives you much variety of food to choose from thr only downside is the food could be warmer.

lol I thought you save a lot with the rewards card so I made everyone walk around to get one.  found out you only get $1 off. -___-" 

I really liked their prime rib and mashed potatoes.  I don't know the name but it was this one type of meat with the bone attached (probably rib meat?).  Also very good.

I also likes the ox tail soup.  they had a variety of desserts but I love flan and theirs was good.

The best buffet in Las Vegas! Find a coupon in one of the free tourist booklets for a discount. So many interesting options, I tried a lot of foods I never would've ordered on my own. Totally worth it!

I believe we paid about $60 for Saturday Brunch with bottomless mimosas. 

You walk over, enter your information into a kiosk and get a return time. In the past we would get a text to come back, but this time we just showed up at 2:00 for our 2:19 return time and it was chill.

2:00 pm was perfect because we were able to grab a couple breakfast items just before dinner items came out. Also, since it's an in between eating time, it was a lot less crowded during the second half of our meal. We left satisfied; there's a big selection of food (just look at everyone else's pictures) and bottomless mimosas? It was just about a $7 add-on to the base price.

I went exactly at 8:00AM on a Saturday morning to avoid the lines. My boyfriend had raved about this place, and I was REALLY looking forward to this since I love brunch and breakfast foods. I was pretty disappointed. The selection was definitely overwhelming which I appreciated. I was really excited for the crab claws, lobster eggs Benedict, and a Mexican-inspired dish with a tortilla, egg, and chorizo. The lobster claw, when I bit into it, was FROZEN. I literally bit into it, and water filled my mouth, and I almost gagged. The lobster eggs Benedict was lukewarm, even though I was one of the first people to grab one. And the chorizo disk was sub-par. 

I did however really enjoy the waffles. I must have eaten 5 of them, I enjoyed them so much. The sweet potato tots were also quite tasty. The rest of the breakfast fare was fine enough. I definitely do not think it was worth the high price tag, however.

after almost three hours wait time, we were seated. honestly 8/10 of the items we picked were really good. for 50$ you won't find any better buffet in Vegas. the service was ok. our waitress wasn't very attentive at all. but it's a buffet. I'm just glad that the food didn't suck after a long wait. I had high expectation for this place and it delivered.

Decided to try this place out since Wicked Spoon has always been the go-to spot.

Wrong decision but at least now I know. 

The decor is really nice. I like the comfy chairs. 

Service: hm..my water stayed empty til the end. 

Food: average for the price of $44 for brunch. No real stand-out dishes. The hargow was terrible. So fake. The sweet buns were good. I love bacon so the breakfast area with bacon was cool. Hashbrowns were tasty. Sushi was sushi, not bad. Mac n cheese shouldn't get messed up, but they did, not that flavorful. I think my fave dish was the au gratin potatoes, it tasted like there was truffle cheese. I don't know because there was no label. I was expecting more macarons too but no luck. Dessert was sub-par.

It was an experience... I'll stick to Wicked Spoon next time.

This buffet makes you feel like a herd of cows eating cheap garbage.

Food is made with speed and no care to taste or quality.   Yuck!

I'm a sucker for dessert & they have all my wants and needs from creme brûlée to crepes! Food is standard not anything out of the ordinary, honestly think it's a bit too over priced but it's a buffet so it evens out in the long run...but I'd suggest lunch over dinner better food I think.

I'm always amazed every time I come to Bacchanal Buffet. Everything is always great except the amount of time we had to wait this time to get soft drink refills. Food is always great, but service can be a little better.

I should ask for my money back, as the only thing that was great to eat was the pizza, which at $50 a head should be a little more than that.  Very disappointed.

My taxi driver to the hotel highly recommended this place. He was prasing how nice the decor was because they recently had a renovation and they've added many more selections to the menu.

We went relatively early.. around 6 on a Monday, there was no line and you pay the bill upfront. How convenient! There were Asian, Italian, Seafood, Salad, dessert...etc. In the Asian section, they had Chinese and a minimal selection of Sushi  I was disappointed to see there were not too many selections of sushi and they didnt have sashimi!!!! My favorite was the seafood station, the oysters were fresh and the crab legs were delish. I spent most of my time at the seafoods. Overall, it wasnt bad but wasnt anything you'd wow for either. I wish i stayed with my original plan and went to Wynn though.

Had a groupon here so I took my bff to come with me.  It was our first time coming here, and it was well worth it!  So much selections to pick from, we didn't get a chance to try everything out, but everything on our plate was delicious!

You come to Vegas for this kind of grotesque, unadulterated gluttony. Yes, you can stuff your maw at other buffets -- many of which cost less -- but this is the best one I've encountered. I've strapped on the feedbag at Wynn, Bellagio and many others, but the sheer variety and quality here is pretty breathtaking. Piles of fresh seafood, a slew of breakfast, lunch and dinner options for the unadventurous or curious diner, and enough fruits and desserts to make the greediest of eaters ponder a vomitorium. But wait! There's more! They don't just have Americanized versions of ethnic cuisines (though they offer good ones)... they have authentic Chinese dim sum, compelling Japanese broths and noodles, Italian meats and risotto. Don't be stingy - tip when you pay and you're likely to get insanely good service to top it all off like we did. I don't often repeat my dining spots in Vegas, but I'll probably walk in and roll myself out again next time I'm there.

We've been wanting to try this buffet for a while now and finally had a chance this past trip. 

Very well organized seating process and the selections were pretty good. 

LOTS of different types of seafood to choose from and each were prepared perfectly. 

Definitely will be back the next time we're in Vegas!

OMGOMGOMGOMGOMG.

If you come here, you come here for the PRIME RIB and LAMB; I don't care what else you eat, but you must take try those two (sorry vegetarians).  I could rave on and on about how much I loved the prime rib and lamb here.  Succulent pieces of meat, melt-in-your-mouth goodness.

Come with a small party or split a large party into groups so you bypass the 18% gratuity for a party over 8.  Come at 2pm, stay until it hits 3pm for dinner.  Pace yourself, don't load up on too much to drink, and go pound plate after plate into your stomach.

Wasn't a fan of the desserts, but they have mochi ice cream and macarons, which I haven't seen anywhere else--but they're not that great to be honest.

Seafood is on hit.  Freshest cocktail shrimp I've seen at any buffet.

But who am I kidding, prime rib and lamb.  That is all.

And the meat carver David is awesome.

Okay, I'm really done.

The best Buffett in Vegas. Every time I come here I overeat to the point of pain, discomfort and shame.

Thankfully, none of those are enough to keep me from continuing to indulge in felonious gastrointestinal abuse at Bachanal. 

Go get a good book..... Then spend the money, eat everything you see.... After your Conehead consumption of mass quantities you will know why you need the good book....

This buffet was on the next level! It's pricey as hell, but worth it. (Groupon might still have a special with VIP access) Vegas is the only place I trust for buffets, and this place is classy and clean. I stay away from places like Golden Corral or any Indian casino buffet. Don't want any ecoli, hepatitis, herpes, and who knows what else. But I digress.
Back to the review:
To start with, this is the first buffet that actually knows how to make a decent tonkatsu broth. That's worth mentioning!
Service is great...used plate pick ups and drink refills are like clockwork.
I don't wanna be redundant, so 'ditto' on all the great reviews on Bacchanal! Can't go wrong with this place.

Best buffet in Vegas. Ever.

We were able to get into the lunch buffet for the price of breakfast (heh), so of course we went!

What makes this buffet amazing is the extent of it- seafood galore, meat galore, dessert galore, everything galore! The seafood was fresh, the meats consisted of prime rib, beef brisket, pork belly, etc. They even had an Asian section which was complete with sushi, duck, congee, and dim sum. 

They even had some delicious Elotes which was delicious as well! It was soooo good. 

And don't even get me started on the dessert-they had everything from creme brûlée to tiramisu, to little cupcakes that you pipette the flavoring on top of the dessert, to mango tapioca dessert.

I was so stuffed of good food. Usually buffets have mediocre food  that you stuff yourself silly with, but this buffet had all great and amazing food. Oh, I can live in that buffet all day....

Best buffet I've ever had. Possibly even the best food. Such a hip place with a modern twist on the look and feel, the whole place looks like a home and garden magazine. They even have chandeliers made out of drinking glasses! The food is immaculent(word of the day)! And all of their selections from the street taco bar to asian fusion has a flavor that is so fantastic, it's unforgetable, indescribable. My favorite part was the selection of juices and other drinks like horchata by the asian cuisine and also the different choices of mini sliders. You won't regret coming here and neither would your stomach.

Bacchanal Buffet is by far the best buffet I have ever tried in Las Vegas and overall in my life! A few friends and I went for Sunday brunch/lunch, and the wait was only around 20-25 minutes. The quality of the food is superior, and I highly recommend going to this buffet. First off, the mimosas are bottomless. How can you go wrong with that? The food ranges from dim sum to pad thai to yellow chicken curry to clam chowder to steamed crab legs (that are already cracked open for you) to shrimp (that is already peeled) to dishes that are served on little hot plates. The variety is endless. In addition, the atmosphere of the buffet is classy, modern, and elegant. I was blown away by Bacchanal, and I would definitely go back again.. and again!

One of the best buffets I've ever been to. Such a diverse spread of food with a wonderful presentation. I learned about this place from Mike Cheng (YouTube channel: Strictly Dumpling) and his review was pretty on point. We went around 2:30pm and we were able to experience the brunch menu and dinner menu that started at 3:00pm. It was $70 for dinner and $60 for brunch, but that was for the Friday after Thanksgiving. It was very organized. You check in at a kiosk and get a return time. Once you get a text, you come back to line up to pay. It took a total of 25 minutes from the time we received the text to the time we sat down at the table. That's the quickest for any buffet around the Vegas area. If you're in town visiting, this is definitely worth a try. Everything we tried was amazing! Service was also fabulous! Great atmosphere and food all around. Would definitely come back!

My 1 star is strictly because of how sick I was for two days after eating here... I will reflect on all of the food that I tried and then also note what I ate that I know got me sick. 

First of all.. there are a lot of high quality dishes that Bacchanal offers. I do not think that they have anywhere near 500 items... Not sure how they got that number, maybe they counted every single section of sauce and the hot sauce bottles and each spoon for each individual sauce...

however what they don't have which was advertised when they first open was Snow Crab or Stone Crab Claws. Friday they only had KING CRAB and KING CRAB only... I am not sure if this is a 'Friday Saturday" only thing or if they have snow crab on other days but one thing that is readily apparent is that they do NOT have STONE CRAB anymore. 
(with Joe's Stone Crab in the Forum shops selling those things by the half dozen for as much as this buffets price I would have liked to see that they were included completely in this buffet as I think Stone Crab claws are extremely sweet and flavorful.) 

Also they raised their prices for Friday/Saturday dinner buffet to 39.95. the hour and a half long wait in line stunk too... 

I started with the Asian section.... the big surprise there was the soup dumpling. this little thing exploded in your mouth and was fantastic.. on from there the crispy beef was pretty good and so were the egg rolls surprisingly. 

When I got to the sushi, everything looked pretty fresh so I took 1 piece per roll and a few lone pieces of salmon and tuna on rice.. when I began to eat these however, the tuna tasted way too fishy and the salmon didn't smell right so I did not consume the pieces of fish. 

I moved on and unfortunately I skipped the ramen noodle section so I can't report how good that was. 

I took some of the sliced deli meats and drizzled some of the infused honey on top of them, this was great! 

The Italian meatball was good and so was the lasagna.

I liked the taco section, the meats they use were really good and it's nice to have the taco warmed up right in front of you.

The slider burger was fantastic, I could have eaten 5 of them for a regular meal and would have been very happy with them.

The best part of the buffet I think was that nice slice of tomahawk rib eye that the very entertaining meat cutter guy threw me.. so flavorful and tasty.

On to the seafood section... the shrimp were very good huge large shrimp that had great flavor and were just great... the lobster corn chowder was very good.

the shucked oysters and mussels were very fresh and sweet and had no bad smell to them whatsoever... 

The king crab legs that I got were very large however they were also very frozen, I literally bit into an ice cube of crab meat and that wasn't very pleasant.. I should have had them heat the crab legs up... so unless you like a crabcicle then please have them do that.

The desserts were awesome... no big surprise there..

Now here's where things went wrong...... I grabbed an oyster shooter... it was a small cup filled with an oyster on the bottom, some hot sauce and tomato juice.. after I shot it a few minutes later I immediately had a terrible sensation in my stomach that stayed there for 6 hours... at that point I was in so much pain I figured that I had to do the old apple cider vinegar trick to take care of food poisoning and 12 hours later I started to feel much better... so please be careful of those things... not sure if it was one of those off chance things and I got lucky but it had something to do with the sauce they used or the oyster or something however it was extremely painful and I'm glad it's over with.

Whoa! Seafood coma! We had a total of 9 people, although the the place was packed, we were able to get in pretty fast. They serve an abundant amount of seafood. I went straight for the fresh oysters! Ate almost 20 of them (maybe I shouldn't have)! They also serve a variety of cultural cuisines, which I think everyone should certainly come to get s taste of. The desserts are small and cute! Not only do they look good, they taste good. I would also like to comment on the meat...it's so juicy!!! Love it! Would come again :)

The nicest buffet I've eaten at. Just don't eat for at least 4 hours before you go as you're going to need the room in you stomach! The highlight was the Mexican corn, I forgot what they called it but OMG the flavour! The waitress was very hospitable and made the experience ever nicer. I have no idea how people could queue for over an hour to eat at a buffet though. We had a show to catch in 1.5 hours so paid the extra $15 to fast track our entry which was wise as we only just made it to the show. You need time to sit and digest between plates.

Super long lines must mean great prices and great food right???
Partially right. 

For around $70 per person after tax and tip (Memorial Day weekend dinner price), you'd expect this place to be as good as a $$$ steakhouse in beverly hills. Some dishes were really really really good (watermelon mint sorbet), and some dishes shouldn't be allowed in the buffet (sushi rolls). 

The goods:
- Crab legs, flan, prime rib, veges like green beans & corn, blackened chicken soup, scalloped potatoes, cocktail shrimp, salmon poke, bbq pork

The not so goods but still decent:
- Scallop, fried chicken, sushi, macarons, sausage, muscles, clams

Service: relatively quick for a crowded evening

I'd probably come back on a weekday and not a weekend, and honestly if I had to wait more than 60 minutes for any buffet, I'd probably bounce no matter how good the food is. BUT if you're willing to wait, or have a membership card that lets you skip the long wait, then by all means, weekend lunch or dinner at Bacchanal's won't disappoint.

Many complaints here are about the wait----we got in line around 2 something on Saturday during Thanksgiving weekend.  We had the "buffet of buffet pass," which was $50 (normally $45---I think the price was higher during the Holiday).  The wait was about 1 hour & we paid $15 per person upgrade for this buffet.

Here is what I tasted:
Sushi: had many choices, taste like REAL sushi from a legit sushi place, the shrimp tempura roll was my favorite

Potstickers:  really good

*some other thing that looked like a potsticker, but in a small metal container: not sure of the actual name (obviously), but I noticed people were taking these like crazy.  This was better than the potstickers.

Sweet & sour soup: really good, better tasting than the one I usually get from "Pinoy Pinay" Filipino restaurant

Prime Rib:  Picked this up at the carving station when I thought I was in line for the seafood (wrong line).  This was delish!

Crab legs: It's not like other buffets, where the waiter puts the legs out and the first person in line at that time takes all the good legs on two plates and leaves nothing for the rest.  You give them a clean plate (1 plate allowed per person) and they serve everyone the same amount of warm crab  legs.  These were the best I have tasted at any seafood buffet.  At one point, they ran out and said the wait was 20 minutes.  ummm this seems too long & shouldn't happen if you waited in line 3-4 hours outside like some people have said.  I only got one serving of this, because I started eating other things & was full by the time the crab legs were ready again.

Oysters: o.k. (not a big fan).  They ran out of this (or some other thing) while we were in line and there were only about 5 in the back & no thongs.  I got 2-3 with my hand, but the server got mad when he saw my husband getting them with his hands.  The server told my husband something about using the thongs & not your hands, & my husband said, "Oh, I'm sorry.  There weren't any thongs out here."  The server was a little rude and said to ask for the thongs next time.  Ummmm aren't they supposed to check for these things and make sure they are there?  Another thing: I noticed the servers get pissed when you are grabbing items as they are laying them out.  The person in front of me started to grab items as the server was replacing them, so I did the same thing when it was my turn.  I could tell the server was pissed and quickly took the thongs away, so that the next person wouldn't grab anything until he was done laying them out.  Maybe this is why there are missing thongs & people grab stuff with their hands!

Creme Brulee: one of the best I have tasted

Flan: my husband really liked this

Gelato: skip the baklava flavor, watermelon mint was awesome

I would go back again with my buffet of buffet pass, but wouldn't pay the regular price & wait in line 3-4 hours.  We were inside about 2 hours & I've heard others say that they stay inside about 4 hours.  Try going BEFORE the peak hours.
It's a little costly but it's good. They have a wide range of desserts. Their macaroons are really good. :) The food is good too. Would definitely go back.

First one here and impressed.  Waited an hour at least and paid $57 for dinner but well worth it. Los of food and great variety. Staff was sooooo friendly and helpful. 

Food tasted amazing as you would imagine. For sure try the Mac and cheese!!! But everything is good so no worries.

Seriously, no joke, super emperor leader of all buffets of the universe. I came here on a Thursday evening around 6pm, so there was only about a 10 minute wait. I am not sure what it is like on Fridays and Saturdays, but from what I have read, sounds like the wait could be up to three hours.  Its about $50 a person and totally worth it. First off there is like one section of the buffet where everything seemed to have truffles in it. Truffle potatoes, truffle fries, truffle sliders, truffle pasta, truffle stuffed truffles, so many things and it was so friggin good. A whole lot of fresh items too, from their sushi to their seafood area, everything will mesmerize your tastebuds. The Kobe beef sliders with truffles had to be the best item of the night. Although some of them were a bit dry, so try to grab them as soon as they come out. I managed to eat six plates of food here and left my stomach really uncomfortable but still managed to check out the desserts. Their french macarons were definitely worth the additional pain. If you come to Vegas, this is the spot you must check out.

This buffet is too darn big to write a detailed review. Is it expensive? Yes. But did you expect any less than $50 a person in Vegas anyway? Luckily, my boyfriend and I chose to go on a weekday, so there was no wait. It was basically like we had the buffet to ourselves which was awesome. 

We arrived at the perfect time. Breakfast was ending and lunch was starting. The seating area is fancy and they give you little rubber plate holders :) I love souvenirs. 

They break it down by sections, obviously. First was seafood/breakfast seafood (lobster benedict, etc.) then a bunch of different meats (steaks, sausages, etc.) then after that I just don't remember specifically. Like I said, this buffet is huge. 

I was disappointed at first. I was like, this is it? My boyfriend came back with a slider (my favorite food in the world) and I was like, "Where did you get that?" --He said, "You didn't turn the corner, did you?" No, no I did not. 

But when I did, there's cheeses, breads, italian food, asian food, FRESH SUSHI!!, and a DIY ramen station. OMG this place. 

I would definitely come back. The table service is amazing, my water was never empty. Plates were always cleared quickly. WIN. 

Bacchanal : 1 , Janelle: 0

I am a total foodie and love to try different kinds of food. This place is like heaven for foodies.It has everything from crabs to oysters to Chinese food to sushi and almost 50 kinds of desserts made by finest chefs fresh. I waited in line for almost an hour but its worth it. I was having brunch for almost more than 2 hrs. Plus they offer unlimited champagne for 7$ thats a steal. I want to take my foodie brother there :)
