I really love this place, probably one of my favorite buffets of all time. Even the Asian food was delicious and you never see that at buffets. Comparing this with wicked spoon, this was way better. Not even a comparison in quality. Must go to if you go to Vegas
The food was very good. We came around 10am when it was empty. The variety of food  was well developed. Definitely worth the price. Mimosas are the added benefit!

I remember the first time I came here a couple of years ago and it was definitely my favorite buffet. After going a few more times over the years, I think I've come to realize that it really just isn't worth the wait... They do have a nicer system in play now, where you can sign in on the tablet and they give you a ticket with an estimated time on when to come back. They'll then text you approximately 45 minutes before that time, in which you'd then go check-in and wait in line to pay. There time estimates are pretty on point, but it's still typically an hour wait (on a less crowded day). Waits can be up to 3 hours from what I've seen. Price is $57.99 for dinner on a weekend (about $65 after tax/tip).

There steamed crabs are SOO good. The crabs have a nice buttery flavor, so you could totally forego any sauces and just eat it by itself. The line is generally very long for fresh, out-of-the-pot steamed crabs. I think you are free to grab the ones that were steamed in bulk or opt for cold crabs instead.

They also have fresh tacos now! I think this is new. They warm up the corn tortillas and meat for you, so you've got some piping hot tacos--just like from a real taco truck. Don't forget to add you toppings! They also have an elote-like corn. Pretty good as well.

I'm a huge Asian food lover, so I'm always in that section. It's not the best, but it satisfies my cravings for all types of Asian foods. I love getting their noodle soups (Laksa and Udon are yummy!). I wish they had better sushi, but I know that's a tough one to perfect. 

The Italian section isn't that great. Pastas are meh and pizza is not good.

I don't think I ever get my moneys worth because my appetite sadly isn't made to withstand the options of a buffet. Nothing here was outstanding enough to make me feel like it's worth the money. I'd much rather get food from another restaurant (try Gordon Ramsay!).

5 full stars. Why?

So it was the second time there, and when we got to the line, it was shorter than the first time we went there. We waited for about an hour and a half the first time, but this time- only 45 minutes. And let me tell you, both times are so worth waiting for when it comes to this specific buffet.

The servers are super super nice to you, and the service is great. I love how they set up everything, how they managed to make it a bit fancy but casual at the same time. But, let's talk about the FOOD. Oh my gosh, if I had to pick a buffet for variety, it'd DEFINITELY be this buffet. They have different foods from many cultures around the world, such as Chinese, Japanese, and so much more. And of course, everything tastes delicious. 

Their dessert section was more than I could ever ask for. They have the sweets that all buffets have in common- cake, cookies, etc., BUT...wait for it... they have other foods like macarons, freshly made crepes which you can customize with different sauces, a Thai ice tea boba float, and gelato. 

The prices are a bit expensive. It's around 50 dollars for an adult, but it's half the price for children under 12 I believe. So I only payed for half the price, but I honestly ate at least a hundred dollars worth of food. But it's so worth it.

There's only one word to describe this buffet.

Heaven.

I think this is easily the best buffet in vegas. I have lived here for almost twenty years and I have been to almost every buffet, but this buffet offers the largest selection of high quality food. I highly recommend this if you are visiting Las Vegas. 
I went with a friend to this buffet and he had an express pass, which saved SOOO much time. The lines for dinner are extremely long if you don't have a pass. But really, this place is just gorgeous; the atmosphere and the food are unbeatable! The service was pretty good too.
I definitely recommend this buffet although it is quite the investment in one meal...

We had heard sooo many good things about this place we had to try it, especially since we were staying at Caesar's. My group I was with tend to sleep in a bit so by the time we got downstairs it was 2:45. WE got in line and we were seated before 3pm. No so bad.... Also if you present your Rewards card, you got a discount $1 a person for lunch which is something. But we got the end of lunch and the beginning of dinner so we got pretty lucky. 
They had just about everything you could possibly think of to eat and everything had such great quality. I started out by going straight to the seafood and I got crab legs, ribs and their' "southern food." Which I thought was really tasteful. My next course was a mixture of the asian cuisine in the back and also more seafood. I was so very satisfied with this buffet... out of all the others I could think of. I thought that their food was very unique and it was all good quality. Their dessert bar is very very well done, with different small desserts like flan, cakes and they also had cake pops, macaroons, mochi and mini cupcakes. I would definitely come here again!

Came here on a Saturday evening for their dinner buffet around 5PM. The line to get in was nearly nonexistent. We walked straight to the front of the counter and has $52 ripped from us. We came here for dinner because there was a lot of great reviews about this place but it was definitely not worth $52. Yes they had prime rib, rib eye, spare ribs, lamb chops etc., it was still not worth it when your meat either dried like jerky or it's drenched in oil fat. They advertise that they have an Asian kitchen and yes they very well do but the quality of the food was comparable to what can be found at Panda Express (no offense to people who like their Panda) but considering the price that I'm paying, I just expected so much more. I feel that the food was price would be more worth while if you go to the Bellagio buffet. By the end of the meal, I felt sick and wanted to vomit just looking at the food. I think the one good time about this place was their vanilla bean creme brûlée and their well presented dessert bar. I would definitely not come back to this place even if my meal was comp!

My parents decided to treat us to Bacchanal while we were home for thanksgiving which I immediately cringed.  I hadn't been to a buffet since I was 10 years old and at that time we frequented buffets and my memories of them were NOT good to say the least. I guess those days of gross Vegas buffets are in the past!  Bacchanal blew me away with the amazing variety of food and fantastic service!  Being a holiday weekend we expected the wait but everything was well worth it.  I forgot to take pictures of course because I was too busy stuffing my face!  Definitely going back on the next trip home!

after hearing all the hype about how good this new buffet was, i decided that i must try this place the next time i go to vegas... so i actually did try it when i was in vegas couple of days ago..

i waited for 3.5 hours just to get inside.. i didnt know they have express line where you have to pay an extra $20 until i was about 1 hour away from the front line.. i probably would have get that i had known earlier.. and since its holiday season, they jack up the price of the buffet to $50/person.. for $50/person, i expect a really good quality of foods and services. 

at the end of my 3.5hours of waiting, i finally inside and was able to feed my starving stomach.. i didnt really have lunch that day to save room for this buffet and it was 9.30pm by the time i got seated.. so i couldnt help myself being greedy and took more than what i could eat!! 

- their asian section - i like the spicy fried fish in the chinese section.. its perfectly fried with a hint of spiciness.. the sashimi in the japanese section was pretty good and fresh also.. i got quite alot of them but my favorite dish of this section was the ginseng chicken soup.. i wished they have a stronger ginseng flavor, but its still goo regardless.

- salad section was average.. i didnt really try any of their salad.. i mean i could have gone anywhere if i wanna eat salad.. but i did try the watermelon and cheese salad simply bcoz it was presented nicely.. nothing special about the taste.

- meat section - after all the wait i had to endure to get inside this place, i needed to wait another 30mins to get the meat.. im not a meat eater to begin with, but my bro is a meat eater.. so i got this for him.. he said that the lamb chop was his favorite and i also think that they did a really good job in cooking the lamb. the beef brisket was okay, the rib wasnt so good, and the steak was pretty dry.. they also have quite a good selections of the fried stuffs next to the meat counter. the sweet potato fries is a must try, its so good and sweet.. the rest was just so so..

- seafood section - this is my main reason of wanting to come here.. i wanted to try their seafood... i love their shrimp cocktail.. it was so juicy and fresh.. clams was pretty good too, the lobster bisque was average, and the crab legs was a disappointment. both the hot and cold crab legs didnt taste as good as i'd expect.. it had too much water inside and too salty.. the oyster and oyster shooter was also yummy and something u must get if u like oyster.. and they have some shrimp tomato cup too, which i didnt really like..

- dessert - one of the dessert buffets ive tried in vegas.. the quality, variety, and taste was just as good as it gets. their gelato and mochi ice cream was refreshing and has unique flavors. the cakes and tiramisu was delish.. the panna cotta and cake pop was also yummy.. but my favorite of the night was their creme brule.. love both the chocolate and vanilla one.. the crispiness of the sugar on top with all those egg and milky stuffs underneath.. im drooling again as im writing this..!! they also have the suger free creme brule if u want to cut some calories down!!

pretty good service.. out server kept refilling our drinks and kept on coming back to take the dirty plates away... even though i dont think i ate $50 worth of food, i still think it was a good experience and might come back for their brunch

This is the gold standard of buffets in Las Vegas. It has a huge selection of meats, food, desserts, Asian section, etc. I was pleasantly surprised how extensive the Asian section was even though it wasn't authentic or the best Asian food out there. The thing is that they have a passable quality with the amount of food choices that they are churning out.

I was able to enjoy myself with a wide variety of foods and even pho was available, which is very rare for a buffet. I also had the shrimp dumplings, which are usually only seen in dim sum places. They had smoked salmon and shrimp cocktail. They had a carving station. I remembered getting a plate and as we walked to the end of the first line, we realized another room with more food. This was the moment that I realized that this place was huge!

I really enjoyed myself here and wished I could come back to try their food. If they were to somehow mix more eclectic foods like the Wicked Spoon, this could be one of the best places to eat for hours on end.

They have variety of food selections! The seafood, especially the crab legs, is very fresh! You can even taste the sweetness of the crab meat. The brisket is really good too, it is cooked perfectly. I also love their pot stickers! I cant stop eating their pot stickers because it is as good as pot stickers served by chinese or taiwanese restaurants. Their desserts are to die for!

However, be ready for the super long line! Yep, super long! It is located in Caesar's Palace. You can check in on the computer then they will text you once your table is almost ready. Once you receive the text, you can go back and stand on the line. So you can walk around while you wait. 

Overall, it is worth it!
I love coming here with family, it has so many options and the food is always great, the dessert section is to die for! A little bit on the busy side but most definitely recommend the wait.
I love the wide selection food they had going on there. I ate there twice while in Vegas. Would highly recommend it.
Lots of options and very good quality. Definitely one of the best buffets that I have been to in Vegas. A must to try especially if you have a sweet tooth!

so disappointed came with family party of 8. place so crowded that u cant even line up for some areas where they r serving shrimp and crab leg,most of the food shown in their website are not even there! we dont mind paying $55plus per person as long as the food we came for to eat are there! not coming back ever! overprice and over rated not worth a dime
It's like international food likely food court. If you expect seafood verity, you'll be disappointed.

Excellent food selection! Everything from sushi to tacos. There were some weird things I didn't like as much but it's a buffet so I just went and good food I did like. Dessert is a must. I strongly recommend anything they serve cheesecake wise!

This buffet was very disappointing!  We were told this was the best buffet in town - NOT!!  It is nothing like the billboard advertising at the airport.

We were a party of 5 on Sunday evening at 6:00pm, although the wait was short, the lines to get the food was ridiculously long. I'lll give it 1star for the big spread, food was not great, it looks like most people went there for the crab legs. Service was non-existent, it took a minimum of 20-30 mins. to order water, etc.  tables were not cleared promptly, after 20-25 mins. we just piled our dirty plates onto the next table.  Needless to say, we will not be back!

If you want quality and service...go somewhere cheaper, at least, if you are not pleased with the food, you are not out $62.50 each.

In order to enter, it was disorganized. Workers did not explain which lines to stand in and caused additional delay to get in. Disappointed and not impressed. Over priced and not worth it. Sushi was limited and not tasty. Meats were okay. Dessert was okay due to large selection, but still not as tasty as I had hoped. Music inside was cool. Not worth the wait and price. I recommend another buffet in Las Vegas.

Things I did not like- the seafood, the Mexican ceviche had no flavor whatsoever and some of the Asian food was to salty. The dessert bar needs jellow, everything else is great. Beautiful buffet to go for special occasions. Limit 2 hr for eating and if you go in bigger groups they take u in sooner.

NOT the SAME ANYMORE  

Used to be my regular must-go buffet whenever I'm in Vegas but was really disappointed by today's lunch.

No more raw oysters, Alaskan crab legs where so salty, lobster bisque  also super salty, no sashimi, very limited sushi  selection, pineapplewas sour, even the melons  were over ripe and spongy 

Well at least the Pepsi was the one unwavering constant

I had been hearing rave reviews for Bacchanal for quite some time and knew I needed to give it a try. I usually avoid buffets simply because it's not really my preferred style of dining; I like being served, I like well thought out plates and inspiring flavor combinations, I believe that if you try to do many things quality will suffer- keep it simple. But this year for Thanksgiving, I had to go into work and it just made sense to do it Vegas style instead.

The line was insane! I'm not sure what it's usually like, but it was Disneyland status for this holiday. Fortunately for my party of three, I don't think anyone was aware of the express line, and for $20 more a person, we cut our wait time down by at least 1.5 hours. Easy. So was it worth the extra $20? Heck yes!

First off, the place is massive! I don't even know how they manage to keep everything organized there. Our server/busser was kind, attentive, and brought us plenty of champagne (complimentary during brunch). The champagne served here was slightly sweet, which was disappointing for me, but also a safe guard since I did have to be at work in several hours.

As for the food- they have everything you could want, really. Everything is displayed in an appealing manner, and they weren't out of any single item while I was there.
I started with the charcuterie which was fantastic, although it was all salamis and a mortadella. Cheeses were next with a raspberry crown (like a raspberry croissant) and the pastry was excellent. They weren't offering any soft cheeses, since I suppose they're probably harder to hold on a buffet line.
The cold seafood station had a good selection from ceviche (delicious) to crab gazpacho (skip it) to mussels (good) and shrimp cocktail (odd texture, but tasty still). They do offer crab legs on the buffet line which are cold. If you're looking for hot crab legs, they have them at the Italian station.
The crab legs were the only thing I ate from the Italian station (too many filling carbs) and they were pre-split, which did make them easier to eat, but it also affected the flavor since they were boiled after they were already split. Just a mention: they're a mix of snow and king, with no option between the two. You get what you get, and there's definitely more snow than king.
The Asian section had congee, steamed buns and dumplings (the shrimp har gow were delicate and delicious), pho, sushi, stir fries and noodles.
The carving station had some really charismatic people working the line that I thoroughly enjoyed serving up prime rib, sausages, smoked brisket and- of course- turkey! Everything was delicious, although they could offer some creamed horseradish rather than just the fresh horseradish at the cold seafood station.

By far the most amazing part of this buffet are their desserts. I'm not really a dessert person, but I couldn't stop myself. I tried, well, I think everything. DO NOT MISS: The passion fruit tarts! The gelato- I had the Fleur de Sel vanilla and Brown Ale Caramel. The two on their own? AMAZING! But together... epic!

If you're a buffet person, Bacchanal is reputed to be the best on the strip, most likely because it's the newest, and it is an impressive spread. But for $70 p/p? I'd rather have a meal with service.

Wow, this restaurant is worth every cent my family and I paid. Everything is so delicious. The food is plentiful and very high quality. It was better than I expected. So many options to satisfy your taste buds with every option being delicious. I highly recommend eating here. Next time I visit the strip I will be back.

Plenty of variety, everything was just "ok"

Jack of all trades, master of none.  I've had better buffet sushi here in detroit buffet's 

Lot's of stuff I've never seen before.  I went at 2:30 on a Wednesday and did not have to wait at all.

31.99 BEFORE tip and all i drank was water.

If this is the best buffet on the strip the other's must be totally awful.  I thought Vegas buffet actually had "AMAZING FOOD"??  It's just total over indulgence.

Way to expensive for mediocre food.  for half that I can eat at the Grand Lux cafe inside the Venetian and have EXCELLENT food.

Not impressed.

First of all, pricing was weird. I'm a guy and I was with my friend who is a girl. We went in to the buffet just past 3 on a Friday, so basically dinner prices just started. Both of us are total rewards member, but she got charged 49.99 pre-tax and tip and I got charged 54.99. What?

Secondly, the seafood was not that great even though that's supposedly what set Bacchanal apart from other Vegas buffet places.

Thirdly, quality of other sections are not worth the price. The dim sum were not very authentic. A lot of the items taste like they've simply been placed under the heat lamp for way too long. This applies to most hot food section actually. The meat at the meat station were either too hard to eat (like dry and hard) or too salty. Dessert station, not impressed either. All the desserts look better than it tastes. Also, com'on, best buffet in VEGAS? I've seen better dessert selection elsewhere, not to mention it's Vegas.

Things I liked: the taco station, the order-to-make ramen was good but small portion. Order peach iced tea at the beginning of your meal with your server. Best thing ever. You can also get coffee if you need that extra boost to help you through the day.

Service was overall satisfactory. A decent experience as like "now I know what all the hype is about", but prob won't come back unless my friends really want to go in the future.

Tip: if you can, try come right before 3, say like 2:30-2:45, this way you can pay for lunch price and enjoy dinner food starting at 3. We wanted to do that, but strip traffic threw us off schedule.

Hands down the BEST buffet in Las Vegas. It does live up to its hype. I suggest if you're in town go to THIS buffet. I mean visiting Las Vegas, it is all about eating at buffets! The dessert section as always was my favorite!! They have all kinds of flavors of mochi ice creams and so far I have not seen any buffets serve mochi ice creams. The interior and the decor is beautiful and the seating from what I remember was very spacious, unlike other buffets besides the Studio-B buffet, the tables are so close to one another you will be able to hear strangers that are next to you chew on their foods. (annoying!) and of course the quality of the food is great. I think this is the biggest buffet I have ever been to.
Not worth my $60!!! Mostly seafood and other foods are just basic. For sushi, you only have 3 basic rolls to chose at. Service is too slow too and it's too dark for us.
I don't eat enough to make the $$ worth it but I can't complain about anything I ate.
the food taste common I can eat the same thing elsewhere, the same taste, and the price is cheaper.

Omg. This place was yummy. It was expensive but really good. It's a must try for first timers. Would I visit again probably not. Only because it was $165 for the two of us with unlimited drinks and to be honest we only ate like two plates each. Well more like one and half lol. The food selection was great. Make sure you visit the tucked away section. The cold seafood wasn't my favorite. It was super salty. Stick to the hot food. I never made it to the desert table. Lol.

This buffet definitely lives up to its hype. If you have the time it is worth the wait, or if you have the cash it is worth paying to jump to the front of the line. Really, if the line is less than half way to the back of their waiting area, it's probably worth waiting rather than paying extra, but I suppose that depends on your means. 

There's definitely an extra edge for the seafood lover, but the creative mixture of dishes offers something for everyone's pallet. The presentation is excellent with individual platings for most dishes. 

They are not the first thing that you will see or hear about, but the freshly squeezed juices must be tried.

 The lunch and dinner options future fresh oysters on the half shell along with muscles and a variety of other fresh sea foods. The sushi is of decent quality, along with a good variety of other unique Asian dishes. The cheese spread is only so-so given the exceptional nature of the remainder of the buffet. 

The dessert bar is excellent, with particular highlights on the crepes and gelato. The self serve candy station adds a fun touch.

Good place to eat buffet. Everything I tried was flavorful. I wish they had lobsters on their menu. Brisket was delicious and I even got to try poki ! Yum! One star off because waiter took forever to refill out drinks.

If you are in Vegas and want to try buffets, make sure you stop here! Amazing and scrumptious. The biscuits and gravy are worth 5 stars alone. A bit pricey (around $48) but the food is so good you want to keep eating and eating! They have everything you can possibly want for brunch. Italian, Chinese, Mexican, Seafood, etc...We ate so much food we really didn't have room for dessert but they all looked amazing! Next time we are in Vegas we are definitely coming here

This review is for my visit on July 28.  Although I found the Bacchanal quite expensive ($35 additional supplement per visit) compared with the other buffets on the 24-hour pass, the food was good and the service, in particular by Michael, was outstanding.  I came in late at 9:30 pm and Michael took fantastic care of me as well as the table next to mine, with conscientious thoughtfulness and consideration.  The service was 5-star but the food was 4-star for the price.

Having dinner 1st at the Wicked Spoon, my expectation fell short. With a more options as far as entree's I felt they were not as tasty as the Wicked Spoon. I expected better for being a pricier place but quantity cannot replace quality. Don't get me wrong they are good but think twice about shelling out more clamps when I've experience a better quality place with less money,

Karen and Vanessa are the best !!! 
After losing way to much money in the casino, they can put a smile on your face!!!
Best buffet on the strip !!
Thanks to both of you for making us laugh...
Annette was our server and she was awesome.

All time favorite buffet with quality and everything!! The line in the weekend may get ridiculously long. I usually go for the weekend bottomless champagne brunch around 2:30pm, seated and situated by 3pm, and eat until the beginning of the dinner.  I've been here few times, but I dont come here everytime I visit Vegas. It's good to pig out once in a long while. Each visit, there is something special that they are serving. 
Here is certain items I fancy:

Fresh fruits - FIGS! Hawaiian papaya

Desserts - Passionfruit, green tea, guava, panna cotta, macarons, and variety of gelato (thai ice tea!) Love the variety of Euro -Asian inspired desserts. I would pass on the cupcakes... Crepes was quite average.

Mexican grill - sweet plaintains with churros, beignets!!

Seafood - Chilean sea bass, fresh shucked oysters, and shrimp cocktail. I didnt care for the stone crab claw and it was still thawing...

Juice bar - Fresh juices served in glass bottle with a limited supply.  I've seen horchata, hibiscus, and watermelon. 

Meat - I only go for the prime rib medium rare.. Good job on the meat! (I still prefer the ones from Wicked Spoon bc it comes with the bone in)

Good selection of cheese and variety of fancy salad. 

Asian selection - I usually try the Pho or the Udon which is quite decent. It's not the best but it's comfort food! Being Asian, I dont really eat Asian food from buffet.. I would only eat noodles. 

It's always a pleasant to dine here and I highly advise to selectively chose what you want to eat. There's no way to sample everything in one seating!!
Too many options to try everything:) good quality good overall. Felt the July 4th weekend menu was a little overpriced. But would recommend.

This buffet has an extremely large selection of food for all tastes. The quality of the offerings was pretty high. I would say the only downsides is that the place can get super packed and waits can be extremely long. Don't even think of waiting in this long line with youngsters unless they are the patient type. Price is right up there with the rest of Vegas, but I felt that the quality of the dishes makes it worth it. A lot of guests seem to gravitate to the crab legs, I personally focused on some of the other seafood offerings as well as BBQ, Asian cuisine, and Italian sections. Service is a bit slow when it's packed so bare that in mind when you chug your drink down. Overall a classy buffet that is sure to please even those put off by buffets in general.

Having compared this against the Bellagio's buffet, I accept that the highest price is due to the far more luxurious food choices. By this, I mean that what you have to choose from, is equivalent to having the best main meals from every favourite restaurant you ever been to, on buffet. Whether or not you can fit it in is another question!  

So I highly recommend this buffet if you only have time to eat at one, but whatever time you choose to eat I would plan to expect 45 minutes to 1 hour of waiting before you eat so your don't die of hanger.

The brunch food was amazing. The waiter was the bomb.com. Carlos kept our drinks topped off. And as we were about to leave came in with the freshly squeezed orange juice and fresh champagne. The best brunch on the strip!

Date and time of visit: Friday, 02/10/2017, 5-6:30pm

Wait time: 5 mins wait, practically no line. Upon leaving at 6:30pm there wasn't a significant amount of people waiting to get in. 

Price: $57.99! ouch.

Food: After having been to Bacchanal at least 5x during the course of when it first opened until today's visit, I would have to say the overall food quality vs value of price has worsened progressively. While the selection remains diverse and abundant, there has been a definite decline in the quality of the food and the overall morale of the staff.

For example, if the quality of the prime rib was a 4* level when the buffet first opened a few years ago, it is now a 2.5-3*. The staff appeared to be a bit less service orientated and friendly despite not having a full house. There just wasn't the joy and genuine happiness that I enjoyed when the buffet first opened.  During the grand opening months, I distinctly remember a particular gregarious tall African American individual who had absolutely impeccable customer service skills at the carving station. He would keep customers in line engaged, entertained, and welcomed. He precisely cut each type of protein to the customer's wishes and did it so with a beaming smile. He even greeted international guests in their native tongue. I noted to myself that he probably wouldn't be there long since any manager would have noticed his skill set and promoted him on. I was happy (for him), but also, sad that he was not there tonight.

The highlight of the Bacchanal buffet is the Stone Crab claws which remained consistently small to medium sized claws -- you may be able to get your money's worth if you fill up on a couple of plates of these.

There was also some cold and steamed "king" crab legs already halved. However, they were very emaciated and did not have much meat.  I would recommend the steamed ones since the cold ones were very salty.

They did have fresh raw scallops which were creamy and oysters (I did not try).

Differences between Brunch and Dinner that I could tell:
- Brunch does not have "king" crab legs, raw scallops, oysters.
- Brunch does have Stone Crab Claws.

The desert station was very good and had a wide variety of sweets. The highlight for me was the crepe station. There was also Thai tea with Boba and a small scoop of vanilla that was a nice touch. Another new item that I have not seen before was Matcha green tea dipped strawberries in addition to milk chocolate dipped strawberries. Fruit selection was decent but nothing too exotic.

The rest of the stations were pretty unremarkable so I will leave it to others to review.

Service: Server was nice and attentive for the first 15 mins only and then we never really saw her again until the end when she asked us if we wanted coffee.

Overall: 3/5 stars mostly due to high cost and because I know they could do better because they have done a lot better when they first opened a few years ago. I don't think it is worth the dinner price.

"Would I Come Back Again?" Rating: Maybe... but only for Brunch as the Brunch and Dinner differences were negligible and not worth the increase in cost.

Similar places to try: Aria Buffet breakfast/lunch actually was surprisingly good. They had both Stone Crab Claws and Steamed Crab Legs for 1/2 to 1/3 of the price that Bacchanal is charging.

best buffet on the strip. hands down.

i'm a big fan of the wynn buffet and the wicked spoon buffet (in its glory days. its still not bad yall! dont @ me with that wicked spoon hate). so when the bacchanal buffet came on the scene a few years ago i had to go try it. 

not much to say except that i love the food and i love the dessert. definitely sat there and just gorged out for hours. 

PROTIP: wear something with a stretchy waistband.

PROTIP: dont eat during the day before coming here. trust me. you'll wanna save room in your stomach for this buffet

PROTIP: come during the latter lunch hours. pay lunch price. eat lunch food. stay until they put out dinner. eat dinner food. dont eat for the next week.

Now I know why people come to Vegas for the buffets. It was definitely worth the money coming here at 2:30 and playing for the brunch place ($45) vs the dinner price ($65). The crab legs come out at 3:00 so you get to eat all the dinner items for the brunch price!

There's a variety of cuisines, ranging from Chinese to Mexican to seafood and more. You can make your own pho bowl or tacos even. I skipped all of those, trying to save my stomach for the good stuff. It was nice being to try new food items that I normally wouldn't eat. The sushi selection was pretty sad, it didn't taste fresh. Also I was hoping for a bigger selection of seafood, but I guess the crab legs makes up for it. The crab legs line always seem long but it's worth waiting in line for a bit. I was also excited for the bone marrow but it tasted nothing like how it should have tasted. 

The dessert section was amazing. So many wonderful little treats. My favorite was the creme brûlée. Overall I was impressed by the variety of cuisines but not so much the quality. I still would recommended this to anybody who haven't ate a Vegas buffet before, but to go during the weekday brunch, right before the dinner time. At that price, it's definitely worth it. Other than that time, not so much.

Siu mai: too much shrimp
Prime rib & tri tip: chewy not tender
Wagyu: ok
Octopus: chewy
Lamb non-French style: ok
Bone marrow: ok, needed something to dip into it
Guac: Good!
Pork sausage non-spicy: delish
Calif roll: good
Lamb chop: good and tender

$80/person comes out to $160 for two, whoa!

This is one of the better buffets in Vegas.  The assortment of food choices is excellent and the quality is right up there as well.  You should give this place a try if in Vegas but be prepared for a long line in the late morning or early afternoon.  The one issue I had was an 18% gratuity automatically added on parties of 8 or more.  Someone would need to explain why this makes sense for their employees given the recent IRS changes that treats this amount as wages rather than tips when automatically added to the bill.

I live in Vegas and visit Bacchanal Buffet at least once a month. It is definitely the best Buffet in town; from the wagyu beef sliders to the red velvet pancakes to the au gratin with truffle oil to the dessert bar! Well worth the price, great food, good service, nice atmosphere.
Will be coming here every time I go to Vegas. It is very expensive, but not one single food item disappointed, I don't know how this place could get any less than 5 stars!

Food was excellent which is not something I thought I'd ever say about a buffet style restaurant. Everything was fresh, cooked to perfection and well presented. Food was at perfect temperature versus some of the other buffets where it's sitting for a long time under a heat lamp. Servers were very attentive.
Went on Thanksgiving. Thought it was overrated for the price. We went for the Alaskan King Crab, there there wasn't any. Not sure I'll ever go back.

I was not prepared for this place the first time. It is not like other buffets! We've been to almost all of them in Vegas but this place is HUGE! Their offerings are extensive!

We started with Mimosas and I felt wicked. It was so good and breakfast started with a warm fuzz, not quite a buzz! They have a juice bar and everything from there on only gets better!

I'm pretty sure there are corners that I didn't even get to see , let alone know what delicious fare was hidden there.

I always go straight for the seafood when going to buffets but I didn't linger or get more than a bite of any one morsel. Still, there was more I didn't reach than what I was able to consume.

We're giving it another go and this time I'm starting from the back. We will start with the Mimosas again, however. And this time I'm wearing sneakers!

Heard a lot of good things about this place, so we decided on this buffet for our Vegas trip.  We didn't realize how long the wait would be.  We first had to check in at a kiosk, where it gave us a check-in time for two hours later.  We came back two hours later, checked in with the host, then got in a long line to pay.  After paying, we would have to get in another line to wait for a table.  We had a show to go to, and didn't have time to wait too long, so we got out of line and skipped the buffet.

We came back the next day early, prepared for a long wait.  We checked in the kiosk which gave us a two hour wait, came back to check in with the host, and waited in the lines. So in total, it was a three hour wait to finally get to eat at the buffet.

We were excited to eat, especially with all the seafood.  At first, I thought the buffet seemed kind of small; I had expected it to be larger.  Then I walked around a corner and realized there was another whole section I had missed the first time around.  I got even more excited.  Although, I still had expected the buffet to still be larger, everything was good.  The food was good quality, and almost every time I went back up again, there was something new they put out.  I ate a lot, actually, I ate too much.  But we all enjoyed ourselves.

Wow. That is all I can say. Wow.

My family and I recently spent our Thanksgiving in Las Vegas since my cousins turned 21.. Of course, you have to celebrate in Las Vegas, for us Hawaii people it only makes sense at least.

My other cousin told us that we have to eat at Bacchanal while we're here so we've decided to save this place for the day before we leave as our one last hurrah. Part of me wishes we came here first but the other part is glad we came here last. 

We got here around 430 pm on a weekday after being told that it shouldn't be too crowded and we'll beat the dinner rush. I'm so glad we came at that time because as we were dining, it slowly started to become more and more packed. We had a party of 9 so tip was already included to our bill so in total we payed about $50 each. Not too bad if you ask me, given the amount of food my family annihilated.

The food... Oh goodness the food. The food there was so awesome that I can't even figure out where to begin for my review.. That's exactly how I felt when I was trying to figure out what dishes to start with! There was:
sushi:
Salmon Nigiri
Maguro Nigiri,
Hamachi Nigiri,
California Rolls,
Specialty Rolls,

dim sum:
Char Siu bao
pork hash and other rolls

mexican food, japanese food and korean food like kal bi, they even had a noodle station where you could make pho, ramen, saimin or udon. the pho was not bad.. after adding hoisin sauce it tasted a lot better. 

They have oysters, clams, jambalaya, and these cute chef specials where the food is served in these adorable little plates and pots. They even give you these silicon finger grips to grab the hot plates.. My mom and bestie, for some odd reason didn't feel like they needed those grips.. Oh how wrong they were.. I was standing there just watching them and then I hear, "Ow! Yeah, maybe we do need those grips"... If only they remembered that if they listened then they wouldn't have to learn the hard way...tsk tsk tsk..

You have to see the meat section... There's an area where one guy is cutting all of these meats.. They have prime rib, ribs either beef or pork, brisket, chicken, lamb and sausages.. If I had a drool emoticon then I'd add about 10 of them.  They have a taco station and all of these assorted mexican foods, I'm not too familiar with mexican food but my mom and aunty attacked that section! 

The desserts... I saw on a previous picture on Yelp that there was a macaroon section.. so here I am with the thought that I'd get some macaroons... Unfortunately I was wrong.. I'm  sure they change up the selections every once in a while but that time I went... was just not my time.. but they did have a crepe station, yerm.. Petite tarts and cake pops, bread pudding, gelato bar and cookies and lava cakes. 

They even had a juice section.. You could get guava, pineapple, and these other juices and they are served in these cute little milk bottles. Of course, the guava and pineapple juice tasted like nothing compared to what's at home but hey, I knew what to expect. 

Service was excellent! Su was our main server and she was just the best! We told her that two of our cousins were celebrating a birthday and she was so sweet and came out with a dessert plate for them and had the other staff members come and sing happy birthday to them. 

I know that the next time I come back to LV, I'm going to try this buffet for their brunch and lunch and come back for dinner.. all on different days of course... or not?? dun dun dunnnnnnn!!!

Great buffet place. It's on the expensive side but I feel that it's worth it. It has so much different kind of foods. from Italian, mexican, japanese, chinese, american, and lastly seafood. The crab legs are worn not cold. Lamb chops are so delicious and tender. Do try their Ramen it's surprisingly. Then there's desserts so much assortment that I can't even eat all of it.

AMAZING!! Hands down the best Buffett I have ever been to. So much options to choose from you really have to your time in each area. Not only is there a great option with food but drinks as well. 

I gave it a 4star because of the set up. It can be a but confusing if you have never been here before but other then that from the quality, options, and service it was well worth it. Not once did we have to call a server everything was brought to you before you could even ask. Drinks where refilled halfway through. 

I do suggest you plan your time you will be in line for atleast over a hour. Don't try everything at once cause you don't enjoy it. You have to really go section by section and every option they had especially the desert area was well worth trying. I don't eat Mexican food but those fresh tacos where great! 

We will be back for more!!
Great Buffet and I am not always a fan of buttets. It is a little pricey but well worth it. They had 4 kinds of crab legs all very delicious. And the dessert bar was fantastic.

this is one of the most expensive buffets I've been to but for the reviews I figured it was worth it. honestly, I was a bit underwhelmed. if you are big into Asian food, then come here it was outstanding. the desserts were great as well. the warm crab legs also good. everything else was just okay

Best buffet in Vegas. $163 for three of us on a weekend lunch, without an optional $7 mimosa. Good service, I enjoyed almost everything I chose from the buffet. We could not have purchased and prepared the variety of food we tasted for $175 with tip! I highly recommend this restaurant, take a walk along the entire buffet before you take anything so you dont load up in one area.

This is probably one of the better buffets in Las Vegas, and it is pretty good food, but no longer a good value.

There is reasonable variety -- particularly strong Italian food, and some decent Asian food, plus Mexican and seafood.  Unfortunately, there is never any king crab, and snow crab only on weekends or some dinners.  Breakfast is a particularly poor value.

Waiting lines are really long unless you have TR diamond or seven stars, or a pass.  (I'm a diamond so it only takes 1-3 minutes to be seated).

Staff are great -- friendly, and good about keeping drinks refilled.

I went here for my birthday and had an amazing time. Even though I couldnt get to everything, all the food I was able to eat was absolutely delicious. And they have SO much dessert. I was in heaven. The only thing that may be a problem for many people is the price, but I think its really worth it. I will definitely be going again for my next birthday.

This was hands down our favorite place to eat in all of Vegas. We visited this buffet on Saturday, Feb. 6 around 2ish. The wait was 75 minutes and at first we weren't interested in waiting that long but we decided to suck it up and walk around Caesars.  So glad we did. 
The wait went faster than expected and we ended up paying $50 each.   The food was AMAZING!!!!   Fresh, organic, and every dish cooked to perfection.   Definitely no complaints and I enjoyed the atmosphere very much.  Not huge buffet person but it reminded me of the Blue Duck at the Park Hyatt in DC.   Upscale but not to pretentious with 4 star quality.  You won't be disappointed.

I heard this place is one of the best buffets in Las Vegas. I had high expectations. It's very pricey. If you're there Mon-Fri don't buy dinner buffet price. The lunch price is $32.99 and dinner is $45.99. The cut off for lunch time is 3pm. The lunch and dinner menu items are really not that different. 

Tip: 
If you're curious to try the buffet and want to save money, then go for weekday lunch hours and save $13 bucks. Try to be there before 3pm to buy your tickets. Otherwise, you would have to wait in line and can hit the 3pm mark. After you buy your tickets you are given a time when you can be seated. it's a process, so be prepared. 

Food: (2 .5 star) 
- Taco
Was not great. The black guy was making tacos, surprisingly, and didn't know how to make it. I told him that I wanted a vegetarian taco, he then puts a big spoonful queso fresco cheese in my small taco. That's not how you make tacos. Have a skilled Latino guy at the taco station. 
- Meat Carving Station
Why do they have to have a 2 big bulk of meats, beef and pork, on the same slicing board. Cross contamination for people who don't eat pork. 
- Desserts
I am a dessert person and these desserts were...meah. Made with low quality ingredients. The chocolates were melted from the light heat source. 

I rate this place 2 1/2 star. The food was okay. Nothing special. I'd rather eat at Wicked Spoon buffet, better food and reasonably priced.

Probably the best buffet in Las Vegas. Can't speak specifically as I've yet to try the Sterling buffet. But among Le Village, Spice Market, and Bellagio buffet, this one is a clear winner. No questions asked. The freshest seafood and a wide selection of desserts.

Best buffet on the strip, hands down. It had such a huge selection of meats, seafood and dessert that I was stuffed even after only sampling a small selection of each. Prime rib was really juicy, lamb had a decent crust, but the wagyu was a little on the dry side. Pork ribs were some of the best I've had in a long time - well seasoned and fall off the bone. I'd go back if that's the only thing they had. Nearly all the deserts I had were also really well made, but particular standouts included the carrot cake, berry cobbler, and the pineapple upside down cake. 

Definitely come here for any trip to Vegas, but make sure you leave room for dessert!
This place is amazing! We had to wait 1hour to eat but it was soo worth it. Fresh! Great presentation! Delicious! Oh and look to spend about $180/3 people (15% tip included)

Let me start off by saying I'm not really a buffet person. However, this buffet was EVERYTHING. We found a Groupon for this amazing deal that included 2 mimosas per person with unlimited coffee, tea, and other beverages. The buffet itself expands over two rooms! Anything you could possibly want at brunch/ breakfast including things you'd never thought of are on this buffet. It was clean and items are kept full. So many choices you're bound to make 3 or 4 trips! Don't skip the dessert bar either - fresh fruit, croissants, pastries, and more! They even had an area dedicated to Asian cuisine that included sushi! You want chicken and waffles?  Shrimp and grits?  Lobster eggs Benedict?  Prime Rib?  Fruits de mer?  Red velvet pancakes? 

I could go on and on, but really, just go! And check Groupon before buying tickets!

I ate for at least 90 minutes straight at this buffet. The offering spans global food choices, and everything uniquely American (copious portions, and southern-style dishes). This is a once-in-a-lifetime meal, so prepare and push yourself to keep eating. U-S-A! U-S-A! U-S-A!

Used to be good
Dinner was my choice and I was disappointed
Service was not really present, other than removing plates off the table with no words spoken 
Food quality was at local cheap buffet (dried surface of cheese, deli meats, steaks, sausage, and half cut crab legs with dried crab meats.)
The food quality is not something that I would expect at a strip's main hotel buffet and at the price of $57.99/person

A fat man's paradise, skinny people too I guess.  Was so so so so so good, I wish they had napping stations where you could come back later and eat more so you can actually make it through MOST of the 500 items, go just before breakfast ends so you can get some of the breakfast food and then lunch for the same price ;).  If you only eat one buffet in Vegas, make it this one.

$49.99 lunch buffet during the weekend. $57.99 for weekend dinner. Wait times during 2pm weekend lunch: 30-40 minutes. 

Prime rib: hell yeah. Other great selection of beef, brisket, etc. 

Dessert deletion: huge.

Taco bar had a cool rotation late to make lots of tacos faster.

Asian food section surprisingly large. Oysters on half shell looked dried out and dangerous to eat. 

Snow crab and king crab legs mixed together... Disappointing. Guess they have to save somewhere, so it seems fair to punish those who don't know better. They serve it cold. Around the corner near the pizza, they serve it hot: yum yum. 

Selection of food was plentiful. Everything was surprisingly delicious even for a Vegas buffet.

As is the story with buffets, some things were great and others were not. One thing that definitely sticks out from other buffets, was their definite attempt to raise the bar and offer more upscale dishes. A highlight for me was the mushrooms with polenta. I've never had anything like that and found it to be very good. I also enjoyed the sushi. I was disappointed they didn't offer a little soy sauce dish and only had the packets of soy sauce available. That put a damper on how I, and I think most people, prefer to eat their sushi when using soy sauce. Two home-style dishes I surprisingly really enjoyed were the mac n' cheese and the green beans. Those were very well done. I absolutely loved the warm chocolate lava cake. Had I been smart, I would have made sure to get some vanilla gelato to go with it, but my plate was already stacked with desserts. The lava cake was amazing, but other desserts I tried didn't particularly blow me away.

Some negatives:
Most dishes were not well labeled. I am a pescetarian and only eat seafood, no land animals. For example, the pad thai was only labeled as "Pad Thai" and I saw shrimp in it so I excitedly put it on my plate. Once back at my table, and upon further inspection, I saw that it had chicken in it too :( No pad thai for me. I feel bad that the food was wasted and it could have been avoided if the sign was more specific as to the contents.
A huge draw of this buffet seems to be the carving station and I felt like they put meat in a lot of the dishes that didn't necessarily need meat. I felt excluded from a lot of selections of the buffet.
They did not have crab legs! My boyfriend and I were SO sad. We both love them and had really been looking forward to them. I thought crab legs were standard at all upscale buffets these days. Guess not. They had the claws, but those are totally not the same.
One piece of cooked fish I did try was very dry. I took maybe two bites. What a waste.

I feel as if the food quality tastes better during the lunch portion compared to the dinner; however, I still love coming here!! I recommend going early for dinner just so the food is extra fresh. There are a wide variety of options and my favorite part is always the dessert station!

Whenever I'm in Vegas, this is a conversation. 

The buffet is pretty damn good. So many stations, seating is great, odd music choice, and the food is a good quality for a buffet. 

Most of my items were good if not at least interesting to have on a buffet line. Staff was a tad oblivious and spilled a tray of food on me. They focused on clean up instead of handing me a rag or something to clean my pants. But that's not ownerships fault, it's just panicky staff. 

Typically long wait and quite pricey. But...... It's worth it if you want to deal with both.

I don't really know how to rate this place. Most of what we had was decent. The standout item for me was surprisingly the brisket. I wouldn't have expected brisket to be so good at a Vegas buffet. Granted, I haven't had much legit brisket in places like Texas...but from what I could tell this was pretty good. On the other hand, I guess I come more from the philosophy of doing one or two things well rather than tons of thing sort of mediocre to good ish.  Am I glad I went? Sure, it was an entertaining experience. Is it cool getting brisket, crab legs, macarons, and fried chicken at the same meal? Absolutely. Would I go back next time I am in Vegas? Eh probably not.  I will gladly spend the 60 something on a good seafood or sushi restaurant instead of trying to eat as much crab as possible to make myself feel better about the price. I guess the point is that I enjoyed the experience but I don't think it was worth the price of admission. I would give a 3.5 if I could.

The most famous buffet in Las Vegas, the Bacchanal buffet at Caesars Palace is delicious and filling, but pretty darn expensive. This Vegas trip, we came with the intention of eating at a buffet. A majority of the group wanted to try Bacchanal. Our large group of 16 came for dinner and we were sent to the large parties line. The front desk was patient and compromised, they allowed us to pay individually instead of splitting the check three way. 

The food itself met our expectations, especially their seafood. In addition, they have every popular food from different cultures you would expect. I loved their drinks selection. They had refreshing bottled juices such as mango, guava, and horchata. 

Plate #1: I went for the seafood first, salmon, calms, crab legs, shrimp, and mussels. Salmon and calms were great! Their mussel pieces were big as well, yum! 

Plate #2: Oysters were not as amazing. It didn't taste as fresh. 

Plate #3: Decided to try some of their Asian selections. Not bad. They had dim sum, orange chicken, BBQ pork, sushi, chow mein, pretty much all the Asian delights! 

Plate #4: Pasta and Pizza! The pasta was good, pizza was alright.

Plate #5: Ravioli and Brisket. At this point, I was stuffed already. Liked the ravioli. Didn't have too much of the brisket because I was too full, but from what I tried, it was good. 

Plate #6: Dessert plate. Gelato and strawberries, great end to a meal! They also offered a Thai Tea Boba Float, mixed with some coconut gelato. Macaroons were just average though. 

The dining area was nice and accommodating. Our party was in a private dining area in the corner, they just needed to bring a few extra chairs to fit us. It was a good dining experience and if you have the money, go for it. However, would I go back? Probably not. The food was delicious, but not enough of a deal breaker and way too expensive!

Chinese Station #7: Dim sum anyone? BBQ pork buns, shu mai, shrimp dumplings, pork dumplings (eat only the inside...the bottom part was uncooked...please change the foil tart for these dumplings because it all fell apart), black chicken soup (BEWARE! IT'S HOT!), BBQ spare ribs, chow mein, rice (Omg! Huge!), and other selections...Wasn't a big fan.

Dessert Station #8: Save the best for last! Wow! Just thinking about the decadent sweets makes my eye budge and my mouth salivate! Creating your own crepes was my favorite (personal chef) create your own masterpiece with fresh fruits and not that heavy syrup fruits. Ew! Mine was made extra crispy with blueberries, strawberries, raspberries, almonds, banana slices, nutella and to top it off powdered sugar! Nom nom! The selection here is by far the best! Cookies, cake pops (chocolate and cheesecake), brownie pops, creme brulee (ate about four of them...only get the regular one not the chocolate...it was not good), fruit tarts (delicious!), sugar free desserts (for all you diabetics), cupcakes, pies, create your own pazooki, ice cream, gelato (rare selection and very creative, but prefer the strawberry cheesecake), candy jars (mmm...sour apple rings), and many many more! But wished that they made cotton candy...Sugar high! =]

Service here is what I love the most! They treat everyone with the utmost respect and cater to you. You are like treated like you own the place, which I believe lives up to the Caesar's Palace title. Left a hefty tip, hope our servers enjoy! 

What I most regret is not trying their breakfast and lunch, so I will DEFINITELY be coming back! I would recommend coming to this buffet, you won't regret it!

The food is not so uniformly bad that it warrants a single star. In consideration to the price and the expectation it sets, it most certainly does. 

Saltiness seems to be the overriding factor in all the dishes, so much so that you can hardly taste the quality of what you're eating. In fact, I don't think any individual item would taste better than at a $20 buffet if the comparison was made between the same dish. If you had the appetite of three people and the desire for mediocre food across a spectrum, then maybe it would be worth it?

That is excepting the sushi section which is among the saddest I've seen. Something you should probably steer clear of.
Best buffet in the world !! The long wait was well worth it. Love the variety, very clean big open space desert was wonderful must go when in vegas .
One of the best buffets in Vegas. If you don't want to wait in line, you can buy an express pass to bypass wait.

On our last day in Vegas, my friend suggested that we go to Bacchanal's in Caesar's Palace. Bacchanal's is probably one of the more popular buffets on the Strip, so I was really looking forward to stuffing my face with delicious food for a couple hours.

We arrived around 3:00-3:30 p.m. and they were setting up for dinner. The wait time was ridiculously long (almost two hours) so we decided to put our names down and do a bit of shopping at the Forum Shops (I highly suggest doing this so that you're not getting too hangry). We came back just before 5:00 p.m. and the line was much shorter and we were seated and eating by 5:30 p.m. They give you 2 hours to eat but I'm sure if you stay longer, they wouldn't notice ;)

The buffet cost us $65/person so I had huge expectations on the food quality and selection. I can't say that there was anything that really stood out to me, as far as the selection goes, but the food quality was definitely 5 STARS. I wasn't really wow'd by anything that I tried but I will say that the seafood was extremely fresh - I loved the shrimp cocktail and crab legs. Just to give you an idea of the types of food, we had: pulled pork, beef sliders, tacos (made to order), nachos, meatballs, mac & cheese, mashed potatoes, fried rice, sushi rolls, prime rib, marinated shrimp, shrimp cocktail, grilled salmon, and crab legs.

I'm not much of a buffet person so perhaps Bacchanal's was wasted on me but for the price, I was just expecting a bit more. However, the seafood and dessert are worth the trip if you haven't tried Bacchanal's yet! Maybe I should go back for breakfast or lunch on my next trip but for now, 3 STARS.

I have been here 5 times before and loved it . The time before last I felt the quality and cooking was a little off but thought I came on a bad day. My wife and myself went again yesterday and had a repeat experience. Food was not hot at many stations the salads didn't have that artsy style they had before and the ceviche was sour with no real flavor, clams and chorizo  tasted liked over done clams with a can of corn chowder dumped on them . The BBQ server was very rude and when I went to get my meat and then again when I realized the BBQ sauce was not out and I had to ask for some he told me to get in line. My overall experience this time was very poor . I don't think I will be back because for the $160 I paid for 2 people ($30 bucks to skip line) I could go to Wicked Spoon and get better service too.

Second time here and I think it is safe to say it is average. For the price you pay I would expect something more, but maybe I'm just picky. 

We got here before the line got really long. Waited about an hour. 

They had a meat, seafood, Mexican, Asian, and dessert section. I really enjoyed the lamb rack they had it was amazing. There was a place where you could get tacos made. From the seafood I really enjoyed the crawfish, clams & oysters. Idk what they marinated the clams in but it was delicious! The desserts they had a variety of gelato, and they make crepes too. They had a forbidden rice dessert which was supposed to be Asian but I don't know I think they just added whatever into it and it didn't taste right. 

Service was okay nothing spectacular. My boyfriend's soda never got refilled... 
Overall I would come back but I don't think it's all that great.

Luckily we came on a comp, because $125 would have been horrible to spend on this "buffet."  If you can get a line pass, do it.  The wait to get in is far from worth it.  The employees from the cashier to the picture taker to the hostess, not to mention the manager, all need a class in customer service (or at least a smiling class.)  It's a service industry people!

After finally being seated, we proceeded to the food.  Like many other buffets, there is quite a selection.  We tried a little of most that was there, and it all was meh.  Funny as it might sound, the tater tots and pizza was the tastiest, and proper temp.  Much of the food was warm to somewhat cool.  That in itself is not very appetizing.  Some of the "exotic" choices was ok...we have had better at the Wicked Spoon in Cosmo.  The service is to be desired.  If you are not a Diamond Level diner, you can expect to wait until they are all taken cared of.

Definitely not worth the price.  Would not go back or recommend.

My boyfriend recently took my friends and I here for my birthday dinner and it was a great experience and definitely worth the price!

As we were a group of about 10 people, we didn't have to wait in the general line and got seated in about 20 minutes. This buffet definitely offers a wide variety of food that's all high quality!

They are known mostly for their crab legs and I can see why. The crab legs were extremely fresh and I liked how they were already cracked open making it a lot easier to eat. 

Aside from seafood, they have steak (the lamb steak was a personal favorite of mine), a taco stand, pizza stand and an asian food section. Not to mention all kinds of deserts ranging from fruit to crepes and chocolate.

This place was rated best buffet in Las Vegas and i understand why. Literally everything to eat from seafood to pizza to prime rib! If you are hungry from a long day at the pool and can eat a lot, head over to the bacchanal! I loved it!

Amazing.
New restaurant plus it looks very classy as well!

The food is just magnificent! Though their are many buffets at Las Vegas this was one of the best I have ever been in! They have food from Chinese, Mexican, Italian, Japanese, Seafood and etc. 

The line up LOOKS very long but as you line up you will notice how quickly the line up actually is. Plus if you have a lot of people you can go to a "vip" line where you do not have to wait as long.

Like many other buffet at Las Vegas the price is around $40 for adults and $20 for kids, it is all worth it! The food, the atmosphere, the variety, the appearance is just beautiful and astonishing! 

Highlights(Food):
Calamari, Dimsum, Crab legs, Other seafood, the meat section(steak, lamb, chops ribs...etc.), ice cream, Mochi, Macarons, The salad bar, fresh Oysters and Gelato

TIP: *Do not waste money to but a drink when they ask you. If u go get food you will notice they already serve fresh juice in a nice cup (don't waste money)
       * If you have 8 or more people you would need to pay 18% tax. If you do not mind you can split up your family and ask to be near each other

Most important thing;
For you who loves sweets and pastry. They do have Ice cream Mochi here and they also serve Macarons!

Overall, I am a big fan! 5 stars!

Best in Vegas!   Honestly, I'm not a buffet guy....but good golly!  I don't need to go into detail. It's a buffet.   But, you get the absolute best of anything for which you are in the mood.   I went to the buffet at Aria the following night. It's an awesome place; but by comparison......it seemed like golden coral.    Bacchanal is tops.    period

Lucked out the day we came because there was no wait! I've been waiting to try this place out ever since the day I booked my flight to Vegas. Definitely didn't leave disappointed but rather stuffed to the max ahahah

Service - very friendly and welcoming. Our server cleared our plates and refilled our drinks without us even having to ask. 

Food - wow, just wow. I had to strategically plan through how I was going to get through this buffet. I was not gonna leave until I got to try everything for a whooping $60. I worked my way slowly from the back to the front. They offer a variety of things: Asian food (dim sum, noodles, sushi, meat entrees, etc), Italian food (pizza, pasta, etc), American food (burger sliders, mac n cheese, fries, fried chicken, etc), Mexican food (tacos, chips, etc), meats (prime rib, lamb chop, bbq pork ribs, etc), seafood (crab legs, shrimp, oysters, etc), soups (ramen, pho, etc), juice bar (orange, cucumber, pineapple, etc), and a decked out dessert area (gelato, cookies, cakes, fruits, etc)! I was literally in heaven for those two hours I was there. Highlights of my meal would be the salmon and tuna nigiri, truffle mushroom pizza, prime rib, steamed king crab legs, and the smores and nutella coffee gelato. 

If I ever come back to Vegas, I know where I'm going to eat first.

Las Vegas has many different buffets and I was really excited to try Bacchanal. However, I can see why it's reputation has been on the downward spiral lately. 

For one, our hostess had a poor attitude. We had a party of five and she stuck us in the middle section of a very small area where it was difficult for us to maneuver in and out of our chairs. Our neighbors bumped into us on multiple occasions getting in and out of their seats. Not their fault necessarily but I wasn't happy. After about 20 minutes, I got tired of playing human Tetris through the crowd of others around us and asked the hostess for another table. My request was met with her being snotty and pretending to check our table receipt to make sure we paid for everyone. I find it really ironic that once she saw how small our seated table was, she still had the nerve to question us. Why not accept you put a large party in a table meant for 3-4 people? Vashna, I think that's her name, should get a clue and personality adjustment.

Now on to the food, which I will admit saved the evening for me. The servers and culinary folks working the stations were accommodating. Shout out to the man working the taco bar! Best items IMO; mussels, paella, shrimp and cocktail sauce, lasagna. I would skip the fried chicken and waffles and other things that look like they could have been kept out for a bit. Biggest disappointment was the lack of fresh squeezed juice bottles! Although the people working the counters said we could special order, that wasn't the case.

Final verdict? If you have your heart set on a buffet experience, there are plenty of other options around the strip.

The best Buffet ever, every dish tasted great as if you are trying it at an authentic restaurant of the origin. You can try many dishes at the same time, wonderful tasting experience. Waiting line was good. Highly recommended from a guy who loves food.

Our party had 6 people and they have a separate line for bigger parties so we were seated probably within 20 minutes of us getting there. We went for dinner and there were so many different varieties of food to choose from. There were some that were hit or miss but overall, it was good compared to other buffets in Vegas. If you are a small party, expect to wait around an hr if you go around four ish but if you go any later, probably more so be ready to wait.

Probably the most expensive buffet I've ever been to. I just wanted to get that out of the way. However, it was also probably the best buffet I've been to. The food was excellent and tasted fresh. There was a lot of variety from Asian to Italian, to whatever else there was. High quality food for sure, but only if you're willing to shell out the big bucks.

Hands down the best Buffet I've had in Vegas. It might be the best buffet I've ever tried in general. Everything was extremely fresh as expected being that it's in Caesar's Palace. EVERYTHING was good and tasty. Nothing was dull or lacking flavor. They had seafood, breakfast, Mexican, Asian, Italian American all of it. Most buffets have all of these as well, but it's how they're served. Every item is higher restaurant quality and super eye appealing. 

I usually don't hype up buffets but there's no hype. It's all legit. The dessert area is to die for. Be sure to try the lobster eggs benedict! The made to order taco area as well! You can't go wrong. If I didn't get so full, I would've tried every item! I'll definitely be coming here every time I'm in Vegas!

First time in Vegas, lunch buffet was around 60 due to Memorial Day special pricing. Came here with my mother, mother-in-law and wife as an end of the month celebration of Mother's Day. 

The consensus among all of us is that the food was too salty. It got to the point where we had to dip our food in water in order to eat the food or just could not take another bite for fear of another salt shock. 

This buffet definitely does not live up to the hype.

The decor and ambiance is upscale however overall the buffet was mediocre. 

The selection is mostly carbs. I went on Sunday for brunch. At $50 per person after tax, this buffet was not worth it for those who don't drink. One perk that I did like is that the king crab legs were cut in half. 

I had high expectations based off the numerous reviews and 4 star rating. No point in getting a Total Rewards card, you'll save a whopping $1.

Huge amount of food selection, certainly above the average of other Vegas buffet. The desserts were awesome, the service was excellent. 

Be ware that you have to wait 40 mins to get a seat, or you can pay $35 to get in the express line. 

But if you ever had a chance travel to Asia countries and have any top rated buffet, you will give only 3 stars for this.

Okay you pay a lot for this buffet but you get high end meat cuts and basically every possible you can think of. I went here for brunch and had breakfast from filet minon and eggs to premium cut prime rib and fresh fish. Definitely worth the money and your time while in Vegas.

When people ask for the craziest, most amazing, most fun thing I did in Vegas...I talk about the Bacchanal Buffet. 

WAIT....HEAR ME OUT. This was seriously amazing. Why doesn't every person in Vegas eat here all the time? I would. My friend and I split a full EIGHT PLATES of food, and then rolled home and hated ourselves, but it was so good. Some people are put off by paying 58 dollars for a buffet, but you have to understand that you are getting a ridiculously large selection and HIGHEST QUALITY choices. Call me crazy, but I think 58 dollars is actually under-priced! 

We started out with a pitcher of red sangria which was the perfect blend of sweet/tasty and strong. We both got very buzzed and giggly after drinking/chugging it. The food choices are just seemingly endless to the point that it's almost over-whelming and you can never try EVERYTHING. Food is separated into different sections which was really awesome. An Asian station, Italian, meats (prime rib, lamb, sausage, etc), seafood, soups, salads. Here is what I tried:

Chilled Alaskan Crab Legs (ALREADY CRACKED AND SLICED! HOLLERRRRRRRR!)
Freshest Oysters EVER
Mussels
Clams
Truffle Scalloped Potatoes...heaven on earth
Truffle Mushroom Soup
Cheese and Meats (brie, asiago, etc.)
Sweet Potatoes with Bacon (THE BEST)
Potato Salad
Shrimp Cocktail
Lobster Claws
Mac and Cheese (the CREAMIEST EVER) 
A million other dishes I am forgetting...

I can't even believe that this is a buffet. It's the so much the place to see and be seen that there are professional photographers who take your photo before you journey inside. If celebrities all hung out at a super cool buffet...this would be the one. Worth every single cent. It was so good, I could not stop eating! COME HERE!

This has to be the worst place in the world. My friends and I were looking forward to a casino "buffet" but this was just the worst experience. 
Everything had something to do with pork
Carving station smelled horrible and didn't look sanitary 
I love lamb chops, after taking a bite in one it tasted more like pork and smelled bad 
Tacos had no flavor in them 
Dessert bar was so so better then the food for sure
We had to fill our self with desserts 
Also the waiter and waitresses don't care about you at all.  It took me 15 min first to look for our waitress cause I wanted coffee, no where to be found I had to ask another server luckily he was nice. 
Overall I would not recommend this place unless you LOVE pork or seafood bad smell and bad service 
Also worst part is for $60 per person service sucks also. If I were to go to any steak house and paid this amount even the manager would come see how you are.

What's not to love? We usually don't do buffets as many lack quality of food. This place did not disappoint! Every dish was unique and flavorful. Unlimited mimosas were a plus! Will def visit on our next trip!

The 3* and a half rate is given by comparing  with other buffet restaurant.
There are many kinds of food from all round  the world. Seafood from the raw bar is fresh and they have something like stew fish.
However, one thing need to mention is that the sushi from the Japanese bar is extremely stale and the soup from the Chinese bar tastes sour and weird.
They have plenty of desserts and the tastes are decent.
Overall this buffet is better than most of buffets in Vegas.
Good but falling down as time passes. Quality is there but nothing mind blowing. The desert is still pretty bomb. Vegas buffet been on the downfall, too many good restaurants

I'm not really a buffet person.  I'd rather get a smaller portion of high quality food than a glut of so-so food.  But I had heard good things about the Bacchanal buffet so I figured I'd better give it a try.

Well the place certainly didn't disappoint.  We decided to go for lunch, (about $40) because the dinner price is outrageous, (about $60).  There is a HUGE selection of food at this buffet, (American, Italian, Mexican, Asian).  I tried the crab eggs benedict, (not so great), tacos, brisket, roast turkey and pizza.  The gentleman working the carving station was hella funny.  He even spoke Tagalog to my Filipino mother in law.  Very cool.  They also serve fresh juice which is very good.  It might have even been cold pressed.  I sprang for the unlimited mimosas which were good also.

The dessert bar is pretty crazy as well.  I tried one of the made to order crepes.  They have a decent selection of gelatos along with just about every kind of cookie or cake you could want.

The problem with going to a buffet is that the price is generally so high that you have to absolutely stuff yourself to feel like you've gotten your money's worth.  But I guess that's kind of the point.  Not really my thing though.  I guess everyone should try the Bacchanal at least once.  The food quality is a step above most buffet's I've been to and the offerings are incredibly varied.  The food isn't amazing but it's pretty darn good.  The service was very good too.  The waiter and all of the staff serving food that I talked to were very friendly.

Not super impressed. I was invited by the GM to dine. I figured that meant it would either be comped or at least discounted. In stead, we were given a reservation for the VIP which is not really anything special. It was an unpleasant misunderstanding that we didn't find out until paying at the register.

The food was mediocre. Better than other buffets but still mediocre. Sushi selection is small like something from a grocery store. Pizza is dried up. Etc. Although other items are more than what I expected, for the price, I don't really see the big deal. For that price, I could get one really good entree. With some very rude servers, I think going here once is enough. 

The only thing that my girlfriend and I liked were the prepackaged macaroons that aren't even made in the restaurant.

Overall, it's good. There is a lot of food. Some of it is very basic. The best part is the Chineese. For example the meatballs are the same as you would find at a family restaurant or a diner.  Nothing special. I did not like the replenish process where the food being removed was dumped on top of the fresh supply.  As far as fresh, I also did not like seeing the crawfish all prepared and sitting around for a long time with the plastic wrap on top. The same goes for the pizzas, with them all prepared waiting to be put in the over. Eh, not good. Did anyone teach these people that the shelf life time out of the fridge is 20 minutes? The two workers by the Italian area just standing around, meanwhile the pasta is cold. My choice is the Wicked Spoon, try it, it is great and none of theses issues exsit. My point is, I expected more from this place and none of this should be allowed at the rate that is being charged. At a price north of $50, that's a lot of Bucchanals.

We usually do 1 buffet per trip to Vegas. This was the best buffet I've ever been to in Vegas - and we didn't even go for dinner. We had brunch with the family here and we were blown away by the variety of food. They seriously have something for everyone. The wait wasn't too bad and our service was fantastic. I've been to buffets at Paris, Wynn, Flamingo and they all pale in comparison to the Bacchanal. I hear the dinner is out of this world so I'll make it a point to try that the next time we visit.

Long lines. Tasteless snow crab legs and
raw oysters. Rock crab claws a big disappointment   Lots of shell fragments in oysters. Meats just OK. Deserts good. 
Not worth $55 per person.

I've visited many buffets here in Las Vegas. This one was surprisingly pretty good. The selection of food is well varied. The quality of the food is also well balanced. The only reason I'm giving this 4 stars Instead of 5 stars is based mainly of the price.  I paid $55 for dinner. I feel that it's a bit over priced based of what you get in return . A fair price would be $39.99 regardless of the time in the day. Overall it was a good dining experience. Just come here before dinner, the price is too high after 3pm.
I enjoyed the fresh food and variable options but i have to take one star away because of the price. ;)
