I had been reading all the good and bad reviews on here and decided to go ahead and take a shot and eat here.  I went to Las Vegas about 6 years ago with a friend and only ate at the Bellagio Buffet.  I came back to Vegas with my mom this time and we wanted to try and eat at some of the many different buffets that Vegas has to offer.  Well we decided to try this one as our last stop on our trip.  So we got in line at about 2:45 pm and got the lunch price of 35.99$ instead of the dinner price of 50:99$.  Dinner starts at 3 pm so we got to experience both lunch and dinner for the cheaper price and I am sure glad we did.  I wouldn't recommend paying 50$ for this buffet.  I am the type of person who loves going out to eat and I also like eating a ton of variety too.  The service was awesome, so nothing wrong with that.  I took a little tour around and looked at all the food before I put anything on my plate.  I wanted to try a lot of different items so I thought well it is a buffet so why not.  Probably the only thing I liked was the mashed potatoes and the california roll sushi.  The crab legs were frozen still, but when you got a piece that wasn't they were very sweet, just didn't want to get plate after plate and only getting about a few pieces that weren't frozen.  I did get them to steam them for me and when they did that the crab legs had NO flavor at all.  So I don't recommend crab legs as one of their main point getters from people.  I am not a fan of much else in the seafood department unless its fried shrimp.  I went to the asian station and ate a few pieces of sushi and thought that the Bellagio had them beat.  Mostly all the food was kind of bland.  I would not want to go back and try it on another night but if you are in Las Vegas and really want to go to a buffet then why not go and try for yourselves!!  Only you can really judge the food not just by reading a review, we can only suggest to you some pointers!!  The desserts were really bad too.  No flavor at all.  I enjoyed the Bellagio Buffet much better.  Even the buffet at the Wynn is better.

This buffet offers a huge variety of food including crab legs, endless meat sections, made to order tacos, Chinese food, cheese platters, and a large dessert section. Unfortunately it is very pricey and we had to wait in line for more than 30 minutes. They do have an option to skip the line but that is also an additional charge. I also wish our waitress was more attentive; we had a difficult time locating her to order beverages and then she forgot one beverage three times. Other than that I will be back to try Brunch.

I'm giving this place 2 stars because it is way overrated and not worth the $110 I paid yesterday for 2 people. It may be that it's over hyped and my expectations were too high but still the price is not at par for this. The food quality was a hair above regular buffet quality for some items but I think overall very comparable to say the Paris buffet when it comes to what is offered. 

On that note for the "500 or 600" different foods...Lie!!! They offer many different types of breads, pizzas, and things like corn dogs if this is what they mean by "500" I guess. (Which I'm sorry that is not what I went there for.)  As for decor and stuff, very plain, nothing compared to say the Wynn. 

Overall, I think most of these reviews come from people from out of town or something that don't have higher standards and are just amazed by "the lights." For everyone else that would rather enjoy their overall experience... take your time (the line sucked) and money (priced too high for what it is) to the local nice restaurant and actually walk out not regretting your decision.

I'm not a big fan of buffets, but this is definitely my first choice for a buffet...I've been here twice, and highly enjoyed both visits! 

They have a great selection and top quality food! Everything I tasted was great, and I love variety so I find myself getting a bite of many different items and try to place them nicely into little sections of my plate, I can be semi OCD at times. 

I really liked the Asian food all the way in the back, it's a pretty large section with chinese food and sushi. I also had a slice of pizza that I loved. There is also a street tacos section, where they heat the meat and tortillas for you, delish! There was a brazilian bbq section but the line was fairly long for that so I didn't bother but I did get to try pieces of the meat from my BF's plate, and it was good. You can't miss the seafood section, loved the crabs and clams! And the dessert selection is amazing, loved it all. They also had a variety of gelato  They also have little glasses of juices and drinks, and you can pour one into a paper cup, and bring it out after your mail. 

Brunch was about $50, and included bottomless mimosas!

This was my goal when I went to Vegas. 

I looked up all the buffets ,and this was just the best one out there.  
We got in line around 1:40 pm on a Saturday, and paid by 2:58 !!! saving 3 dollars lol because 3  - 10 pm is dinner, so the price increases from 41.99 - 44.99. 

It took another 20 minutes after we paid to be seated. 

I was shocked that they had SO MUCH SEATING, there are empty tables everywhere, so I'm guessing they understaff in order to profit ( which most places do ).  When we were walking to our table, I saw many tables that had not been cleared of plates, but were just waiting to be filled. 

Unlimited drinks ( fruit juices ( they have fresh squeezed watermelon juice, carrot juice, etc, but unfortunately, when we tried to order them they ran out :( , coffee, soft drinks, tea w/ real honey !!! imported from France !!!! , ) 
The coffee was hot, but I wish they used a darker roast, because there wasn't that much flavor.

alcoholic drinks are extra. 

Seafood = oysters ( I had about 35 of these, I wish they were bigger, they were soo small compared to the picture shown in the advertisements)  The oysters flesh was kinda washed apart, like they had been washed too much.  So the flesh of the oysters became flaky. 
            crab legs =   I had a small piece of crab from my friends place, it was a little salty but not that bad, I like how you can choose to steam the legs.  I don't eat crab / try not to, because they are becoming endangered. 
            Mussels & clam & paella = all yummy esp the little bits of ham in the mussel soup 
            Cocktail shrimp = the shrimp were bigger than most shrimp cocktail i've eaten, not as big as tiger shrimp though . 
             
Meat = prime rib juicy and tender 
             lamb chop = could have been more tender, and they had a whole bucket of them sitting on the serving station, so I'm not sure how long they were cooked before they were served. 
             slider = soo tender and i loved the mayonnaise spread the had on the buns 

Mexican = fresh tortillas & guac & the mexican style sweet corn w/ butter & cheese & chili  the mexican pollo soup ( i'm not sure what it was called ) it was red and oily on top was very yummy and savory. 

Japanese  = They had tuna poke salad !!!  & the fish was very fresh ! 
               sadly no sashimi, but the sushi was all very fresh. 
                also have your choice of miso soup ( make your own ) 

Chinese = typical chinese food, they had xiao long bao and lo mai gei !!! 
               xiao long bao is the soup dumpling, and lo mai gei is the glutinous rice with meat inside.   sweet & sour soup was good too !

Italian =  they had 6 different kinds of dried meats to choose from 
                (Prosciutto, Pancetta, Dried Beef, Salami, and a few other kinds ) 
                these were all delicious, and tasted very good with the cheeses & fresh fruit they offered. 

Fruit  / Salad = I didn't have any salad because I didn't want to waste space in my stomach, but the honey dew was so sweet !!! Too bad they ran out after everyone else figured out how delicious it was.  The watermelon wasn't that sweet. 

Cheese = I tried the white cheddar, and blue cheese, and my friend said the parmesan was yummy even though she doesn't usually like cheese.  I tried the blue cheese on accident, and spat it out because I hate blue cheese. But if you liked blue cheese, you would like there blue cheese. 

Dessert = I don't save dessert for last, I feel like if you do that then you will run out of room in your stomach.  I prefer to intersperse my dessert within my meals at buffet, that way you can try everything. 
             Creme bruleee = they have chocolate & regular creme brulee here, I tried the chocolate one and it was pretty good. 
          TIramisu = so good and light !!!! unhh i really liked it. 
          Chocolate dipped strawberry =good 
           Chocolate & cheesecake pop = so decadent and rich and creamy. the white chocolate cheesecake pop was SO GOOD. I would buy these separately if they offered them. 
           Flan = i finished all of it so good. 
           White / pink fluffy marshmallow = mmm so light ! home made too i think ! I even felt cute eating it ! 
           Mini red velvet cupcake = so cute loved the decoration ! and cheesecake frosting was delicious. 
          Syringe dessert = i enjoyed injecting my dessert with red jam like filling, too bad they are probably not reusable. 


Gelato = only tried the sorbet, blood orange, tangerine, and watermelon mint all sooo refreshing light and fruity. 

Crepes = so good !!!! ate a whole bunch of the fresh fruits that they offered as well !!! 


We ended up staying at the buffet for 2 hours, I wish I stayed for longer, and walked some laps around the buffet so I could have eaten more. 

P.S.Cannot believe I wrote so much, I commend anyone whom actually read all of this shit.

A lot of waiting and waiting. We had the dinner menu. The food was okay but  the desserts were awesome. I would go back for the variety of desserts. Came to Vegas and went to a buffet. That's checked off the list!

Food heaven. Those are the only 2 words that come to mind. Seriously. Can they have any more selections?!
We came here on a Monday morning right before noon thinking we would beat the lunch rush but we were wrong. There was already a line that was moving pretty slow so patience is key. Groups of 3 or more have to stand in a separate line which seemed to be moving SO much quicker than the line for a party of 2. Bummer!

Nonetheless, this buffet is ah-mazing and I'm looking forward to coming back in the near future and stuffing my face. It's organized by type of food which was very helpful. They had Asian in one section (sushi, rice, egg roll, duck etc.) followed by salad, then cheese (goat, swiss etc.) then Italian (pasta, meatballs, gnocchi etc.) and the list goes on. They had it all. Hispanic food, seafood, American food, everything! A ton of meat too! Ribs, chicken, sausage, the whole nine yards. There were also made to order stations such as pasta, tacos and crepes.

My favorite would have to be the duck because it was so moist and flavorful. The sweet potato tots were good too. I think I rambled too much so I'll stop now. Anyways, try this place! You won't regret it.

(I want to give this place a 3 and 1/2 stars)
Everyone raved about this place when people found out that I was going to Vegas. The dinner buffet is about $50 and way to expensive for person on a budget. Though they had like hundreds and hundreds of food options, I thought that the food would have tasted enchanting. I do admit that it was good but I didn't think it was as great as everyone told me. Servers were very nice and diligent!
We had to order our drinks and the servers will bring it out to your table. But how do you run out of lemonade? So as replacement, I got a lemon iced tea (and my dumbass didn't realize it was unseewetend so I had to pour a lot of sugar in the ice tea which I over estimated on taste).
After my trip back home, I find out that more people likes the brunch menu than the dinner menu. I freaking wanted the breakfast menu but my friends didn't want it even though it was on Groupon for about $35!! 
I wanna come back to try the brunch and to give this place another chance.

This place was quite disappointing as I've read many over hyped reviews about this buffet. Yes they have a wide variety of seafood but the line ups for the seafood section were insanely long (and not worth the wait) as almost everything if not all seafood tasted like they were from frozen. I was surprised to see that they had soft shell crab though but for the price of this buffet I would not recommend to go just for the softshell crab lol if you are looking for a buffet with good quality, do check out the WICKED SPOON AT THE COSMO!! Unfortunately I only tried this buffet on my last day in Vegas but otherwise would have went again. Yes. That's how good it was.

Other than the world best peach tea/sweet tea, there is nothing else better than that. Most of the iconic dishes are gone like the tomahawk steak and  Green applewood smoked wagyu. Service is perfect, food is bomb however, there is not as much as I expected.
I love the desserts..and their seafood. I'm usually not a seafood fan, but this is pretty good! Especially the crepes~

Absolutely phenomenal! Far better than Bellagio's The Buffet. I made the mistake to go there in December. I regret not trying Bacchanal sooner! 

We visit on a Saturday afternoon (2:30-3pm). We had a larger party (7) and were seated fairly quickly. Just make sure all parties are there otherwise you will not be seated. I do agree with others that if you arrive any time during evening dinner time, do expect to wait at least 1-2hrs+. 

The buffet has a lot of variety. I really enjoyed the seafood, Italian, American and dessert stations! I do appreciate that they make gluteness desserts. I loved their cake pops, macrons and fruits. The mango habanero ice cream was somewhat interesting. Maybe they were trying to do a fusion of mangonadas? Lol

But next time I visit Vegas and I am having a big appetite I will definitely visit Ceasars buffet! 

Ps: Btw, Michael and the busser (lady..I forgot her name) were on point with there customer service! Def won me over! :)

Variety selections of food: seafood, steak, asian dim sum, sushi,...I love the way they cook crawfish even though It's frozen, hopefully they will have fresh one in the summer. There are crab legs, warm and cold.

We had the 24 hour buffet pass and paid the extra $25 for the brunch upgrade. This was by far the best buffet we have dined at during this trip. The food selection was fantastic. There were small individual portion sized servings for many of the items. There was a good selection of seafood to choose from such as mussels, and chilled crab legs. The meat caving station included beef brisket, beef wagyu, pork belly and ham. There was a made to order taco station. My favourite was the dessert selection. There was shaved ice and a huge selection of ice cream to choose from. 

Service was great too. Our server and bus boy were quick to refill drinks and clear plates. They were very efficient despite the large crowds.

Overall, I think the price was reasonable for the experience and food options. Yes, it is one of the more expensive dining experiences, but worth trying at least once.

第一次去，沒有傳說中那麼神奇。
first time there, worse than my expectation.

作為一個老吃客，我姑且給他兩顆星作為鼓勵和安慰。
as a picky customer, i barely leave 2 stars......

排隊給我留下的印象最深
waiting time period impressed me.

裡面地方很大，從自己桌子出發，去拿一盤東西，再走回來已經佔用了他們所限定時間兩小時裡的相當一部分時間。
the place is big. it takes a little bit extra time to grab the food. time limit is 2hours.

河粉一塌糊塗，跟周圍的亞洲款菜式一樣，只能滿足於這輩子沒吃過河粉的人。
pho is horrible, as well as other asian cuisine, the only person will like it is the person have never had pho.

有帝王蟹(是橘黃的而不是最好的那種紅的） 過了下午六點後才拿出來，跟雪蟹混在一起，跟其他所有菜一樣，拿起來不太容易！因為，放的太靠內，距離太遠。
there is king crab clusters (but ,they are brown king crabs instead of the best red king crabs) mixed with snow crabs. not easy to reach them,just like other food. 

羊排一般，太熟，沒有水分，而且不夠熱
lamb t bone,over cooked or well done, not juicy, not warm enough.

沒有帶子和石頭蟹鉗
no sea scallop and noah crab claws .


如果你真希望嘗試滿足海鮮自助餐，建議試一下位於加州傑克遜的農場自助餐，禮拜五至禮拜一，全天35塊一個人，龍蝦，帝王蟹應有盡有！

If you really like to try a better sea food buffet , recommend you try rancheria buffet in jackson,CA.Fri-Sun. whole day.
$34.99/person . they have chilled and warm king crab legs in separated tray , lobsters , raw oysters are also available.

People have claimed Bacchanal as the best buffet in Vegas, but I don't really think so. They have great selection, but they lack in taste in a lot of areas. I don't mind coming here because it isn't bad, and because of the huge variety, I can usually find a handful of things I like. The price is on the high side and I'll never eat my money's worth here for sure. They don't really have discounts here either unless you do the Buffet of Buffets 24hr deal, which I have done on occasion and pay an additional $20 for the Bacchanal add-on. Line is long at night, but they have a tablet for you to leave your phone number and they will text you when you are up.
I came here this past April for the early bird weekday brunch special ($30 before 9am), but I think the promotion might be over now.
Although I didn't really need to use it this last time, I have a Diamond players card. I pay a heavy premium for this membership....and thus I can skip the buffet line at all Caesar's entertainment hotels if I want to.
I didn't see any prime rib for the brunch, and was pretty disappointed with that. I just went around picking up whatever looked good. 
I'm not even Chinese, but stay away from the Chinese food. At least not the chow fun or fried rice. Honestly I can make better chow fun and friend rice at home and it turns out pretty bad when I do.....so yeah that says a lot about their food.
Dessert selection is quite nice, but I didn't see the cakepops I really like the last time I came. Maybe it's a dinner thing only. I did leave with some gelato though.
So this early bird brunch special wasn't that great, but for my overall visits, I still give them a 4 star.
I haven't been to every single buffet on the strip, but my order goes something like the following based on taste/price/variety:
1) Rio Seafood buffet (I think they just combined the 2 buffets now, but have 2 different price options, not MGM) Unlimited New Zealand lobster tail at dinner.
2) Wicked Spoon (Cosmo, not MGM)
3) Bellagio
4) Bacchanal (Caesar's Palace, not MGM)
5) Le Village (Paris, not MGM)
6) Aria
7) The Mirage
8) Planet Hollywood (Not MGM)
9) Mandalay Bay
10) Harrah's
11) The Excalibur
12) MGM (From here on down, it's not worth your money to go)
13) Luxor 
14) Monte Carlo (The only place I didn't feel full when I left)

I've also been to the buffet at "M", but you would need to drive to get there or take a cab/uber. That one is ranked up there with Bellagio. I'm just going to list that in all of my reviews for each buffet.
Pretty good buffet, lots of choices, and a good sized carving station. My personal favorite Vegas buffet. The line can get long sometimes, but a little planning can alleviate that.

We were so excited to try this popular Buffet here in the Cesar's Palace!! The Bacchanal Buffet is very popular for its meats, seafood, and desserts! I watched a popular YouTuber Mike Chen and his visits here and I couldn't wait! 

Now, it gets extremely crowded.... I mean really crowded... and since we went on 4th of July weekend, it was even more crowded! 

My tip is to the lunch buffet.... still the same good food, but little less crowded and the cost is less. We tried to attend the lunch crowds but didn't make it! 

Also, since it was only 2 of us, the wait for even longer because if you have groups of 6 plus, you get to get in earlier because those large group tables move faster than parties of 2.... so we were lucky because a family of 4 asked us to join them so it made a group of 6 and we got to enter the line asap.... and they allow you to split the bill two ways (in case you wanna split)!

You wanna get your money worth so avoid foods you can get anywhere and attack the good stuff.... but never overload your plate.... take samples of what you wanna eat!

I attacked the crab! King crab legs and Dungeness crab!! The crab was pretty good.... sweet and tender and you get butter with it!! 

Also, I attacked the prime rib, pork belly, mashed potatoes, Truffle mushroom soup (must try), mushroom truffle pizza, and BONE MARROW!!! (Bone marrow is a must try!) 

Dessert area is awesome! They have a crepe station, gelato, cakes, fruit tarts, chocolate covered stuff, etc! 

The food overall was good, but I was expecting it to be awesome..... also, the family who we dined with, who has been to this buffet several times said last year was better..... so would I try it again, yeah.... but for $70 a head, you gotta get your money's worth! 

Good, but I expected awesome!

The Bacchanal Buffet truly is "the best buffet in Vegas" if you enjoy eating seafood. If you are not a seafood lover, this isn't the place for you as there are other buffets of equal quality that are less expensive.
I asked if there was a military discount and was told that I'm not special just because my friends died overseas. That sums up this experience
Esmeralda Juarez is the best. I love Bacchanal  so many wonderful options! We love coming here when we're in Vegas!

Disappointing food, with even more disappointing service. 

I had heard amazing things about the wagyu steak and buffet at Bacchanal, but during my dining experience last Christmas, not only the wagyu but all steak slices were fairly bland and/or overcooked. Wagyu should be cooked in away to accentuate the natural taste of high quality beef used, so the fact that this tasted like any typical piece of steak was so disappointing. My family also tried a lot of the seafood (i.e., raw oysters and lobster legs), but had stomach problems after our dinner which speaks volumes about the seafood's cleanliness. From the food itself, the buffet was definitely not worth the price point.

Now for the service: My cousin was a diamond member which had its own line. Since we were a larger party of ~15, my cousin emailed the buffet days in advance and received explicit permission to include our full party in the Diamond line. However, when we actually reached the front of this Diamond line, the line staff pulled us out of the line and to the side "for violating their party cap rules", then proceeding to ignore us for the next 15 minutes. My cousin tried to grab these staffs' attention and explain about the email but they not only refused to acknowledge this email, but kept rudely brushing her off as if she was a nuisance instead of a valued customer. They even ignored her requests to talk with the appropriate manager, forcing her to basically catch any other line staff she could to re-explain the same thing multiple times before we found someone rational and reasonable. Even after the negotiation, we still had to wait an hour even though we reached the front of the line far before any of these issues began. 

This whole experience left a sour taste to what was supposed to be a happy family reunion. Had we known that a party of 15 would need to be in the general line, we would have accounted for this in our timing instead of 15 people basically waiting and starving for almost 2 hours at 7:30 pm. Definitely would not come back or recommend, as the staff don't care about their customers.
Had a great time at the Bacchanal Buffet. Only wish is that they didn't pressure you to leave after 2 hours.
Came for brunch and had a great selection including a wide variety of fresh seafood. Was super quiet before 9:00am

Phenomenal buffet.   I wanted a way to commend Delmer for making our experience amazing.  

The food is by far the best in Vegas.  A bit pricey but worth every penny

This buffet is the flagship buffet for the Caesars hotel and casino chain.  The servers are friendly, including the individuals handling the food. There was a meat carver it was extremely kind and friendly on the day we went. Not only does the food look wonderful, it is delicious. This specially true of the desserts, which I find rather bland and unimpressive other buffets in the Caesars hotel and casino chain, even Paris.  The atmosphere of the restaurant is modern.  If you're wondering what the little Blue and purple rubber pieces are in dishes above the stations, they are for hot plates, such a small plates that you carry back to the table.  I would like to see the crab split like it is at Paris. That would be my one improvement for this exceptional buffet.

This buffet was a huge disappointment. I cannot believe we paid $65 each to eat here. The Indian Gaming Casinos in San Diego County have far better buffets for half the price. Buffets with larger crab legs, lobster, rack of lamb, steak, I could go on. The crab legs at Bacchanal we're the biggest disappointment. I've never seen such small crab legs! One carving station with a long line of people waiting to be served.  My drink was never refilled. The restaurant was dirty. The carpet was filthy, the wall our table was against had old food hardened and splashed all over it. It was filthy. The upholstery on the chairs was dirty, worn and had tears on the seat. The arms of my chair were sticky and had dried food stuck to them. How do they get away with charging that kind of money for that? Certainly doesn't seem to meet the standards of Caesar's Palace.

Best buffet in my life! Forget the amount of money you will pay to get in here, it is totally worth it!! They literally have it all. What you really need to go here is an extra stomach , I tried to get from every section and didnt even get to half! The place is nice and fancy and the workers were all friendly. The dessert section is also big and they have gelato! I actually forced myself to have dessert because there was no way I was leaving without having any!
Incredible variety.  The spare ribs, brisket and hot steamed crab legs were delicious, the rest was ok.  Its a buffet, hard specialize any one item there's sooooo much to choose from.

Everything was so nice ...the food was absolutely amazing so many varieties and so tasty. 
Definitely if  you are in the area you should try its worth it

Service was excellent. From the dessert station to the taco station, every attendant I encountered greeted me and asked how I was doing. Instead of, you know, throwing slop on a plate and yelling NEXT. In a place as massive as the Bacchanal, I felt like more than a number, and found that very impressive. 

We came for dinner and brunch and enjoyed both visits thoroughly. The quality has definitely improved from my visit about a year ago. One little thing was that the salt and pepper shakers I came across during brunch could've used a little wipe down. Would be good practice to have every table's shakers wiped down between guests, for sure, as the ones we had were kind of yucky. 

Bacchanal still is the place to visit if you only want to eat at just one buffet during your trip. And if you go twice like I did, they have so many items that you could probably go all week without any repeats!! Bring those stretchy pants and get to bidness!

Top of the line food. Lots of amazing choices. Food is put at a very high standard here! High end Buffet. 
The price is a little hefty but worth it! Best buffet in town hands down!

Bella n Tony

Put your name down early - we had an hour wait to get in line, and another 20 min wait once we got there. I liked the drinks service but for the price expected wine and beer - it's twice as expensive as Harrahs buffet and while it was tasty, it wasn't worth THAT kinda mark up. 

I loved the lamb though and the fingerling potatoes.   But wasn't sold on the mouthfuls of fat I got in my Asian beef dish or the stale bread. 

Again if I liked crab and shrimp etc it woulda been fine but I'm more a red meat and carbs Gal and I wasn't overwowed like the rest of these folk.  Not worth the wait to me.

Don't mind the line... it's VEGAS! 

Honestly, I ONLY come here when i'm craving for some crab legs haha

Other than that there are SOO MANY things you could try! I dont think anyone could eat every single dish they have! 

The newest dish I tried was their bone marrow....OMG! I LOVE IT!!! (Not salty at all!!!!!) 

But of course, they continue to change things up here and there :)

Went here after not going for about 2 years. I was really excited but left under whelmed. The service was great but was lacking in the food department. Tried to avoid the raw seafood due to the previous reviews of them getting sick. Had some crab legs though, which were not as long as they usually are. Went during brunch and they didn't have much choices to choose from. They say they are number 1 but I think they are not in that spot anymore. They had a panda creme brûlée which was one good thing.
Best buffet in town, and I've been to all of em. Pricey, but worth the selection. Often a wait, but not terribly long.

Can I say jaw dropping, salivating mouth and let me stuff my face with endless delightful, good looking and grand variety of feastful food!?!  

YES and most definitely YES!

While my girlfriends and I were walking to the table that the hostess was directing us to, I was looking left and right on what the whole buffet place had to offer!  While at it, pre-determining on what to get! 

My eyes were on the savory selections of meat and seafood haven side!  I loved the prime rib, lamb chops, garlic string beans, king's crab legs (were a bit on the salty side), shrimp and oxtail broth with topped green onions served up on the side!  Those were to name some of the highlighted favorites that night!  Don't get the creamy mussels and clams!  A few had a bit of crunch sand to it and I felt like my tooth chipped a little from the grinding of it!  Their oysters didn't look fresh, so I didn't get that.  I dislike the grogginess down the throat when swallowing raw oysters that are not freshly shelled!

I did leave space for macarons!  My all time favorite dessert!  They had ice cream, creme brûlée and more!

If you are unlike me with carnivor-ing, seafood-ing, then I would suggest the salad bar, dim sum, sushi, tacos and/or pasta bar!

I would say one of the best buffet (costed $65, it better be) quality restaurants - especially in Vegas!  I also do like the machines that take your reservations so you won't have to wait.  It didn't give us a concise estimate wait time because it over estimated from 90 minutes to an actual 20 minute wait time frame.  A margin difference, I would say. 

I would surely be back for more nom-ing, nonetheless!
This is the best buffet I have eaten at in LV. The food, in general, isn't that tasty given the price. The selection is the best in LV but just falls short of being worth the price.

Best buffet in Vegas, hands down! There was a variety of food choices and they were all delicious (or at least the ones I had!). My friends and I went around 10:30am and we were seated right away. Because we arrived around brunch time, we were lucky enough to have a bit of their breakfast and lunch options  Will definitely come back during my next Vegas getaway!

Best yet! And I've been to all of them!  Seafood, perfect!  Deserts, wonderful. Overall selection is absolutely impressive and makes my "favorite" list.  Considering how many buffets and how many years I've been jotting opinions on yelp over Vegas buffets, that's a high vote. Ceasars has finally made the list.

The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because of the long wait times.  This place is most definitely worth the wait! Be sure to cruise and take a look at EVERYTHING before piling up your plate. The biggest and best selection of just about anything u could imagine.

Save your money. This was very disappointing.

Maybe we fell for the hype or maybe we had expectations that were too high. The pictures of this buffet are way out of date. All of the photos taken more than a year ago no longer match what you get there anymore. 

We went for dinner through the VIP line. The wait would have been 45-60 minutes otherwise. I'm glad we did or we would have been even more disappointed. 

The crab isn't prepared properly and they just boil the crap out of it so it tastes of water and nothing else. It's not well cut so you spend a lot of time just picking at it. And the worst of all, you have to line up to give your plate to someone behind the counter to receive a few crab legs they fish out of a vat of boiling water. It makes no sense.. the hot crab legs are on the other side of the buffet from the rest of the seafood. The process is very slow and the line is easily 15 minutes just to get a small plate of tiny crab pieces. 

The "wagyu" beef was over cooked and stringy. The prime rib was mediocre, but the guy was generous with the slices. 

Everything else was just "meh". The service was the slowest I've seen at any Vegas buffet (and we've been to pretty much all of them over the years). We got our beverages just as we were done eating and we had to stack plates just to keep some room on the table.

Given all the hype and positives things we heard... we expected better. We left 150$ lighter, covered in boiled crab water and unsatisfied. I've had better at half a dozen other buffets for much less money.

Best buffet in the world? Nah.

I do like them but they are very pricey with that huge price tag (30% more than the next priciest Vegas buffet?). 

Unusual delights we found are beef briskets (well done! best of the buffets), jumbo shrimp (as you cant find bigger elsewhere), lamb chop, disappointed with $68 pp and you still have to pay extra for the lobster, for that price you can get all lobster dinner for two in average restaurants, and yes stone crab, but after paying $3 for 2 claws in Publix Florida it is difficult to be impressed (and Publix tastes better because it is freshly cooked). Ethnic food are aplenty, all less than authentic, Chinese/Japanese similar in quality to Bellagio but they do have spicy crab (and I enjoyed the porridge which is one of the best), Mexican dishes there are quite a few and yes probably Bacchanal has the best Mexican dishes for a buffet (ya happy?). Family is very fond of the great pastry and little cute utensils they have for things. 

Service is so so, it is Xmas and I dont see any smile on the waitress' face, so we paid someone else the tips, and they are not up to speed with cleanup and refreshments.

Dont forget to go there and put your reservation in (yes you cant reserve on the phone) and wait the next 2-3 hours, they might call you in 45 minutes, but you never know.
One thing i hate was the wait. The wait is long if you have a lot in your party. If its just 2 of you then the wait is better. But the experience and selection is so worth it!!

If you are going to splurge on a buffet in Vegas, this is the one!

We came for dinner on a Friday night and it was $130 for two adults. You really do get what you pay for here though, especially in the seafood department. They have crab legs, oysters, crawfish, and shrimp to choose from. Other pricier items were prime rib and brisket. 

There is a wide variety of foods to choose from: Asian, Italian, Mexican, and tons of sea food choices. Their Asian food selections offered some traditional Chinese American fare such as chow mien and fried rice, but some more authentic foods were the delicious dim sum choices. 

We also tried many of the meat choices: sausages, prime rib, bbq ribs, brisket...all delicious and cooked to perfection. 

There's also a very decadent dessert island to try! I call it an island because it's just that! It's on the opposite side of the buffet with tons of sweets ranging from crepes made to order to macarons. 

We left this buffet disgustedly full and miserable, just how we had plan. LOL!

Bacchanal Buffet has won best buffet and been much talked about since it's 2012 debut. Please know that the long lines do not at all effect my rating because I do not wait in any line here and wouldn't for something like this let alone pay extra for a "line pass" to skip ahead some. If you are from Vegas like myself, you aren't the type to do that sort of thing and usually know people who can help you avoid such nonsense or have players card perks. The screen said there was a 103 minute wait when we arrived for dinner, so I was very happy that we were escorted right by it and taken to the platinum dining area with no wait. Our drink order was taken right away and our server was great about checking on us. I ordered coffee and he never let my cup go empty and he also was quick to clean up dirty plates. I'd go to one area and get a plate and then pass by that same area later and see something completely different. They are constantly putting out freshly made food, so don't forget to keep your eye out when passing by an area you've already been to.

I liked that they had pizza with thin and thick crust. I thought the pizza had great flavor and some of the best buffet pizza I've had. Some of the pasta dishes were hit and miss, but the lasagna was very good and the guy who makes the pasta custom to order is awesome. I had some linguine and he added garlic and white wine to the sauce per my request and it ended up tasting really good. The salad area had a good variety of things to offer and the veggies were fresh. They have an area with a variety a meats, cheeses and breads along with nuts, roasted peppers and olives that is definitely worth making a stop at. There was a small line for tacos and with good reason. After you get your tacos don't forget to check out the salsas, cheese, sour cream, guac, etc. and also get some of the beans and rice. I didn't care so much for the al pastor taco however the carne asada taco was very good. The guac I added to the tacos tasted fresh and delicious. When I passed back by the taco area, I noticed some nachos getting put out and grabbed some. The nachos came in a small tin pail and had beans, cheese, salsa, sour cream and guac with tortilla chips. I loved these so much that I went back for seconds! Get the nachos! The much talked about sliders here weren't that great, or at least on the night that I tried them. I liked the thick slice of cheese on the burger and the bun was good, but the burger itself was overcooked and dry. I was excited to try the prime rib and it was tender, but seriously lacked flavor which was disappointing. I thought the mashed potatoes were very good and the mac and cheese was good also. The sausages tasted great and while the ribs were big, they weren't big with flavor sadly. One thing I really liked was the fried chicken and onion rings. My hubby came back with a plate of fried rice, steamed dumplings and pepper steak that looked so good I had to go make myself a plate. The pepper steak was a big hit between us both and he went back for seconds. The crepes were ok, I didn't care for how crispy my crepes were. The desserts here are amazing and they have a good selection to choose from, so make room!  The buffet itself isn't the biggest in town, but they make up for that with what is offered. The price for the dinner buffet is more than reasonable considering the types of quality dishes offered.

"I'm usually not the Buffet type, "BUT"...... I'll make an exception for this one!" If I come to a buffet and have to wait 2 hours to get a table, "It had better be great!" Lol. "You better believe that this buffet was worth it!" 
Allow me skip the part where I waited 2 hours to get in. It was a weekend, during dinner hours, at Caesars Palace, and on the famous Las Vegas Strip. So, Yes..."I understand that part "VERY" well when it comes to dining!" However, "I was there to dine!"  Upon entering the buffet, I notice the setup....."GREAT!" That's not what got my attention though. What got my undivided attention was the food displays. "Fresh, well presented foods!" I'm in food heaven? Fresh juices in individual glass bottles, oysters served on the half shell, displayed on a bed of ice for you to choose, desserts fit for royalty? "Maybe!" This is how a buffet "Should" be. Oh, and did I mention the fresh crab legs that are cooked right in front of you then pulled from the steamy pot then onto your plate????  "I'm sold there!"

I am absolutely dumbfounded by how disappointing this buffet was. Where do the great reviews come from? My dad and I decided to stray from our trusty Mirage buffet and it was a mistake (if you're reading this- save your money and go to Cravings buffet at the Mirage.) This was the first time I have ever left a buffet unsatisfied. First of all, the prices are absolutely asinine. You can enjoy much better buffet options and save yourself roughly $20+ per person. We came on a Tuesday at 4 pm strategically to beat the dinner rush. To our surprise, the line was huge, but we figured it would go by fast. We unknowingly ended up waiting over an hour in line. We should have absolutely gotten out of line and ate elsewhere. After this obnoxious wait and a pretty penny for dinner, we expected this buffet to blow our minds. Instead, we did not have drinks until halfway through our meals when we had to flag a server assistant down for a simple glass of water, and our actual server came over for the first time while I was eating my dessert. Absolutely unreal. At that point, just don't bother coming over at all. The food was not good. Seriously, I read rave reviews about it - what am I missing here? We left with empty pockets and extremely disappointed in putting so much money towards a beyond subpar meal.

Well this is one of the best Buffet in Las Vegas i guess. The price is a little expensive but definitely worth for whatever inside. This restaurant is huge and im guaranteed with there is always a line outside to wait to get in. The food is great for a buffet , plus there seafood fresh overall. Also different countries food is pretty good too. This place im highly recommend.

We've been to several buffets in Vegas and this one takes the cake. Food is amazing, desserts were by far the best of any of the others. Best part was our server Mark! Made sure our visit was super fun and memorable. We'll definitely be back!
For how much this place costs, there are better buffets around. The variety is limited.

Look out, this place is the king of noms. When a buffet has a two hour time limit for people I would take that as a good sign. This place has everything you could want, LITERALLY. When you walk in you start with the seafood, yes seafood at 8am. They have crab legs, shrimp, mussels, shrimp and grits, calamari etc. This is followed by "breakfast" but really, who has time for boring "breakfast"??? They have varying types of carbs like waffle fries, tater tots, chicken and waffles and wedge styles. Here you'll find eggs, bacon, huuuuge sausage and a crepe station. I believe in here was also the fresh juice bar with things like fresh cucumber and watermelon juice. Now we move onto red velvet pancakes, regular pancakes with strawberries, mini banana donuts, churros, chilaquiles, steak with an over easy egg. Hug the corner and you are greeted by the salsa station with around 6 different, homemade salsas and sour cream. After this there was mushroom ravioli, 4 types of pizza and mini croque-monsieurs. NEXT comes the made-to-order omelet station, this was standard but delicious. The chef can work on 4 omelets at time because WHO WANTS TO WAIT IN LINE WHEN THERE IS ALL THE FOOD. Now comes the charcuterie area with various cheeses and thinly sliced meats. Now we come up on to the Asian cuisine, there were fresh noodles being cooked and fresh miso soup, steak fried rice, noodles, SUSHI, dumplings, egg rolls, pot stickers, spring rolls, bagels and cream cheese randomly, a make your own pho station and then we come to the end where they had a salad bar (ew).

I know, I couldn't believe it either. But I'M NOT EVEN DONE.

In the middle of the restaurant there is an island with sweets galore; fudge, gelato, cookies, cakes, pies! It was so decadent and I loved having gelato for breakfast!

I do also believe they add different items to the menu as the day goes on since they are open from 8-3. I think I saw sliders in a picture so I'd take that as a yassss.

This place does get packed, we got there around 9:40am one day and there were 40 people in line already, so get here early!
I've been here many times and still the Best buffet in vegas. They have different food items to choose. And the food bar is clean and presentable to the guest. Love there food and desserts.

This was one of the worst restaurant experiences of my life... the food was absolutely horrific. Not a single person in my party enjoyed any of the food. Most food on the buffet was cold or stale.
The service was poor- no drink refills, plate removal, etc... Avoid this restaurant at all costs.

Long line on a Saturday night. Finally got in and they told me they ran out of oysters! Very upsetting because we still had to pay full price $64.99. And then later I saw a VIP table get oysters. Food was good and good variety. Crab legs were juicy and meaty. Not worth the price since they put away the oysters at 8pm on a busy Saturday night.

This was really good, and I would maybe go again if I ever come back to Vegas. I thought the selection was outstanding, although the desserts were a bit too fancy for me so I had trouble finding anything that I liked other than gelato. 

Good: prime rib and atomic horseradish, St. Louis ribs, cheesy mashed potatoes, glazed carrots. (I went back for a second serving of all of those)

Ok: service. Our waitress unfortunately went on break as soon as we arrived and the gentleman that covered her tables had trouble remembering to refill my milk.

Not so good: lava cake was extra dense and dry with almost no melted chocolate.

I'm giving this review 3 stars because there actually is some good food here, but unfortunately, as they say, you take the good with the bad. 

I went as they were shifting into dinner mode. 1st impression was good. I was seated quickly (although it was late afternoon before the dinner rush and on a Wednesday. I'm also a Diamond member which has its own line). Server took our drink order fairly quickly, and I had no problems with service. 

I opted primarily for vegetable options, even though I am not a vegetarian. Cutting to the chase, the problems seemed to come from the seafood and a brussel sprouts dish(which was clearly ad by both smell AND taste). I quickly spit that out and set it aside. The crab legs, well, you get what you pay for folks. Don't expect high-quality snow crab legs at a buffet, at least not here. The cold crab legs were dry. The "freshly boiled" crab legs were better, but clearly not top quality. I'm guessing this is what caused our GI irritation). Fortunately, no stomach pain or nausea, but the rumblings "down there" (sorry to be so graphic), were clearly related to something not very fresh. 

My advice, go early when it's cheaper, and steer clear of the expensive seafood dishes read: crab, even though that's what you want to go for because you think you're getting good value. There's no good value about being on the toilet for an hour or two after your dinner.

The atmosphere, the service and the variety of food is great. Several things we tried were cold and didn't taste fresh. The lobster and the prime rib were both overcooked. 

Overall, the service and the atmosphere doesn't add enough value to justify the over priced food. Fewer hot, fresh, well prepared food items would at least make up for the astronomically priced subpar choices we had today.

We haven't been to Vegas in probably 10 years but one thing I always remember is the buffet's we'd go to. This year we decided to do a family trip to Vegas for our Thanksgiving holiday and my brother mentioned that the Bacchanal buffet is supposedly the best in Las Vegas and since we're staying at Cesar's it was a great time to check out the hype. We came down for dinner at around 4 PM and waited a good hour in line which was fine because the buffet did not disappoint. It is a bit pricey I guess but if you were to go out with 4 for dinner it would probably end up costing around the same if you were to go to a restaurant. The atmosphere is really nice for being a buffet; definitely is not a home town buffet vibe haha. Now to the important stuff-the food. Let me tell you, Cesar does not play around. After getting seated, my brother and I made our way to get our first plates. What we thought was the end of the buffet actually continued around the corner!! There is A LOT of food. So many options that I was actually overwhelmed! What I really liked though is that there are lot of mini dishes that are created and set out rather than it all being serve yourself style. It really created a bougie dining experience. I did not eat anything that I did not like-honest as that. Just make sure to leave some room for their beautifully crafted desserts! All of the waiters and chefs behind the counter were very nice as well. Definitely would recommend coming here-you won't regret it. I've attached some photos but they don't do it justice!

They always say: "don't eat the sushi at a buffet" 

I was very skeptical going to this place because generally I'm anti-buffet. I find that buffet food is usually just a large quantity of bad quality food but, Bacchanal changed my mind! 

The selection here was unbelievable, and the quality was really good! Not 5 star amazing but really really good. 

If you're a seafood lover, they have a very large selection of crab, lobster, oysters, muscles and so on. 
The American and BBQ selection was also noteworthy!

Last but not least was DESSERT! Oh man, if you have a sweet tooth this place is for you! Desserts on desserts on desserts! 

If you're going to try a Vegas buffet, I'd definitely recommend Bacchanal!
Seafood is very fresh, and a lot of choices, cooked by different way, different style, spicy, steam and wine source. One of the best buffets we had, really worth to try!

Best food I've ever eaten in my life.  We went at lunch time.  Lines seemed long at dinner.  Our server was a "newbie"--ONLY working there for 21 years. That speaks volumes about a place.  She was fantastic.  Awesome experience!

This place has so much variety! We went around 930 am and that was perfect. We started with a variety of breakfast and ended with lunch! They even had dim sum, gelato, Italian, sushi, Mexican and traditional American breakfast! Would highly recommend going. Staff is also so nice!

Great buffet only if you eat seafood.  The large crab claws and crab legs are the freshest and the sweetest.  The king jumbo shrimps are to die for. Eat five of those, and I guarantee your stomach will be full hehe. The clam chowder, really hidden from view because they have so much selection of pretty food, is actually really delicious and packed with huge chunks of clams. Sometimes they have tiny scallops on the shell. Those are little bites of crispy and creamy goodness.  I also always gravitate towards their selection of cheeses and thin slices of cured meats.  Very tasty and so not good for your arteries hehe. I really only focus eating on the seafood because no other buffet can compare or come close to offering that kind of seafood. I've been here at least 4 times.  And every single time had been enjoyable for me and my tummy. 

I suggest eating early for dinner (around 4pm) to avoid the crowd and wait time. And to go on mon-thurs, it's cheaper than Fri sat and sun.

I'm lived in Las Vegas for 37 years and this is hands down the best buffet ever!!!  Each section is like a gourmet restaurant...  They have freshly shucked oysters, crab legs, colossal shrimp, lamb, prime rib, duck, sushi and much more.  The attention to detail is awesome.  We come here for birthdays because everyone gets what they want and don't get me started on their deserts!!!  They have a desert crepe station!!! And everything else (ice cream too!).  I've been to many buffets but this is my favorite.  It's pricey but worth every penny!!!

The food is high quality in general. But I didn't see king crab leg as shown in some of the photos in Yelp. Instead, they put snow crab legs. Don't get me wrong, the food there in general is still in high quality than many buffet restaurants. However, the fact that they're charging premium price made me expect more from them. This place is a little overpriced.

2nd time eating here and ooohhh, this place will never disappoint you.

I went here on a Saturday night for a birthday dinner with my cousin. We arrived around 6 pm and waited 2 hours in line. Worth the wait tho because once you get seated, you are hungry as hell and you will get your money's worth. They offer different types of food. My favorite one will be the dim sum station and seafood station. I had 3 plates of the King crab legs, they have two option; they have steamed and cold king crab legs. I tried both and it put me to heaven. I can say I got my money's worth off of that. 

I didn't get to try all the food here but I can say that this is the best buffet I've ever had in my life (based on the stuff I tried lol)

I can't imagine why anyone would recommend this place. The lines to get in are long  and the food is awful.  There are so many great places to eat in Vegas do waste your $65 here.  We took  a group out for a Birthday dinner and paid $530 for 7 people what a waste of money.  The only reason I gave this place two stars is because the street taco station was delicious. Most of the food was cold or tepid. The meats were either way too salty or no seasoning at all, add the fact that they were cold and it makes for a really disappointing experience. Lobster bisque tasted like a salty cheese sauce. The bread was placed under a hot lamp which made the rolls hard and crusty. They may have had butter, which would have helped soften the bread, but the buffet was so disorganized I couldn't find the butter.  What a waste of money.

Best buffet in Vegas! I have a gluten allergy and Samuel Acevedo, the chef goes out of his way to make us gluten free food. Gluten free French toast and fried rice are amazing. Thank you for your help and great service Samuel!

Oh Bacchanal. You were one of the main reasons that I came to Vegas, and everyone hyped you up (ahem Strictly Dumpling). I was so pumped to go because of the immense selection, and I love to eat seafood. Our group of 6 got to the line at around 6pm on Saturday, and the large group line was already winding far outside of the ropes. They were truly busy, but there were also a lot of groups that had fewer than 6 people who just stood in line without reading the signs that stated there was a separate line for small parties. Also the kiosks were not in use yet even though I thought they should be since the lines were already getting out of control. We waited about an hour or so in the line to pay and then at least an hour and a half in the line to get into the buffet. I thought the lines were kinda ridiculous and I don't understand why they can't text you whenever they're ready for you but they do a good job of controlling the number of people actually eating so that you don't have to wait in long lines for the food.

I headed straight to the seafood and got everything in that section along with miscellaneous Asian meats and noodles, pizza, etc. I mean, you gotta try it all to get the value. I was disappointed from the first bite. The fish was so dry - I can make better salmon at home. The crab legs were weirdly salty, chilled large shrimp had no flavor, and the lobster claws were tough. The clam bake and crawfish were good but again, they were the only things that weren't overcooked or old or not flavored. Oysters were really fishy smelling, and one guy in our group got sick from them.

Meats, vegetables, and noodles were across the board bland except for the duck. Tacos were ok but I've had better from a taco truck. The dessert area was large and looked promising but the ube gelato barely tasted like gelato, and half the desserts were skippable.

Talking to the rest of my party who had previously been to Bacchanal, it sounds like the quality has really gone downhill every time they go. I get that they can't execute every item amazingly because of the wide selection but I was hoping that at least 75% of the food wouldn't disappoint me. For the line and the price, I wouldn't go back.
Not bad.. Really clean. Great desserts. Liked it over most buffets in Vegas.

This was a good buffet but I think a bit overrated. It's expensive.
Desserts and American food are done well.
When it comes to the other cuisines I felt they missed the mark (sushi, soup dumplings), I didn't try the Mexican food.
Service was a bit slow for such a "fancy" buffet, long time to get plates cleared or have water filled.
I would come back with buffet first timers but probably not again for myself.
Delicious and very clean! Best buffet I've ever been to in the states. A bit pricey but it's worth it. Staff is friendly enough.

I've been trying to eat at Bachanal for 4 years and the 3 times that I had tried to eat here, the wait was over 2 hours long each time. We came the day before at 11:15 and were told it would be a few hours so we got up early the next morning to try again. We arrived at 10:30 and got right thru this time. Get the Groupon as it will save you a few dollars for the buffets. Yes you will still have to pay a service fee and tip afterwards, but still it should save you some money. 

The food is different everyday from what I understand. This like any buffet is going to have some things that are great and others that you are going to take one bite of and be finished. 

A couple of the things that I enjoyed were: Mac and cheese(they had 2 different ones and one was great and the other was meh), Chinese dumplings, sushi, sweet and sour chicken, fried okra, sausage, chocolate lava cake,and rotisserie chicken. 

A few things I didn't care for: the biscuit was hard as a rock, the Thai beef was cold, the tri tip was tough on the outside, and the chocolate chip cookie weren't anything special.

They've got a lot of seafood and all sorts of options options for anyone. The waitress saw me stuggling to crack crab legs and brought me some crackers. I really liked the deserts of only I hadn't eaten so much already tho. I did also notice that several of the food items that you will see in the pictures weren't on the buffet at the time we went that I had sort of expected to see.

Is it worth a 2 hour wait? Absolutely not, but it was the best buffet I've had in Vegas out of the 5 or so that I've been to so far. By the time we left about 12:30, the wait line was very long of course.

Went here on a Friday night for dinner. This is my 4th time here and I was a pretty disappointed. When the bacchanal first opened up, I was very impressed with their large selection of foods. But this last time the selection was a lot smaller than then the previous times and the quality of food was not that great. The meat was over cooked and dry, and there were a lot more "filler" foods (I.e. fried rice, mashed potatoes, etc.) than previous years. The bacchanal is not what it used to be.

So dissappointing a few friend and i went on a thursday night and paid the $45 per person and we ended up hating the majority of the food... we all tasted alot of food the shrimp and grits... gross iam from the south i make shrimp and grits I grew up on shrimp and grits they tasted like they had enchilada sauce in them...the chicken in the basket with the fries were dry the sushi tasted like gas station sushi... the duck was dry...the butter they had for the crab iam pretty sure was the butter at the movies that they put on popcorn... I was generous with giving the 3 stars because the things that were good were good like the crab legs... the meat carving station was great... the beef ribs in the asain staion was amazing...the lobster pasta was good and the desserts were not bad...the chile lime ice cream was good tasted like  tamarindo which i like... if you want any drinks other then water,tea and fountain drinks be prepared to pay more and also be prepared to leave a tip on top of what u paid per person too... Wont ever go again and if anyone that works there is reading this email me and i wouldnt mind giving some advice on making the shrimp and grit, not a chef but i know mine taste better!

We had high expectations for this buffet having read the great reviews on Yelp. One star is given to the overall poor experience and low quality of food. A few of the disappoints include: crab legs were way toooooooo salty, the oysters weren't fresh, meat tasted bland, desserts were mediocre. The only section that was a little decent was the Asian section, although the soup tasted awful. $70+ per person is ridiculously priced given that the quality of food and service just lack of delicacy. We will unfortunately never consider returning to this place on our future trips.

Absolute bummer for the price ($64.99+tax). Most of the food was cold and the place was over crowded. Horrible wait time and the most disgusting part was there were small flies all over. Just overly hyped and not worth the time or the money. Would never go back or recommend this place to anyone.
Great selection, but the food itself was completely average.  Nothing special at all.  For the price charged, some of it should have been much more impressive.

Ended up getting terrible food poisoning which led to a hospital visit. Reported to the buffet and they initially responded but after a week of calling we have been ghosted. They said they would refund our food but still haven't received that back.

Stay away if you dont want to ruin your vacation with food poisoning.

Not really worth the wait...we waited in line over an hour. The hostesses had a really crappy attitude. The beef short ribs and bone marrow were great. The prime rib and Wagyu were just ok. I wanted it to be exceptional but it wasn't ‍ seafood was fishy too

The best casino buffet in Las Vegas. The dishes are seasoned as the best restaurants would prepare them. The meats, fish, and poultry are cooked to keep them moist and tender, not overdone like other buffets. Asian dishes are prepared like you would find in the better restaurants (where else do they serve a whole roast pig?). Snow crab was available as chilled and warm just out of the pot. Small plate appetizers like duck confit were excellent as were the array of desserts. Go early because lines get long (kiosks available for waiting list).

Best buffet in Vegas hands down. Enough said. 

But seriously the best. Come hungry and try a little bit of everything or you'll be stuffed.

Cashier Vanessa had a bad attitude in service and
Charging fee without explanations and notice ! She said" I am asking you questions?!" What a nice restaurant with this kind service

One of my favorite buffets at Vegas. Groups 6+ need to wait in a separate line and are charged 18% tip, which comes out to $75 per person for a weekend dinner. I think it's worth every penny.

We waited about an hour, which was  a lot more than what we would've waited if we were in a group of 6. The wait time for larger groups seems to go by faster than for smaller groups. 

The prime rib is perfect, the brisket is perfect--and those alone at any other restaurant and you're looking at a $50+ meal. The warm crab legs, the fresh sushi, yum. Warm crab legs are deep inside the restaurant. Oh and ramen is amazing too. Better than any ramen I had back in LA. The oysters looked a little weak so I stayed away from those. 

The dessert bar isn't very unique, but it did have the essentials. I especially loved the thai tea float with boba. 

They don't have mac and cheese! And no lobster. Don't be fooled by the display of lobster at the front of the restaurant. It's funny that despite the hundreds of offerings, I still managed to notice what they were missing.

Finished my meal with some jasmine green tea and honey. Alcoholic drinks are not included but the peach green tea was the favorite of the table.

Can't wait to be back.

Delicious! We came here for dinner and there was such a wide array of high quality food. The crab legs and lamb were personal favorites along with the variety of petit desserts. I loved it so much that I came back for brunch and that did not disappoint!

Let's start by saying, it's an expensive buffet. So make sure you come with an empty stomach. Make your money worth it. Lol.

Their craving station has a variety of cooked meats from prime ribs to brisket... Also they have a good variety of seafood. Oyster shooters, half shell raw oyster, king crabs and more. It was definitely a plus for when they have steam and cold crabs. 

Everything was good. You can't really expect a delicious meal at a buffet. Can you?  
Overall they have a wide range of food selections. 
The food was warm and fresh. Friendly staff. Clean. 

Dessert bar : whoa... I felt like I was in heavy when I first saw their dessert bar. You can see my photos. 


I haven't tried other buffets in Vegas so I really can't say if this is the best. But if I was to compare Bacchanal and Aria buffets, I say Bacchanal has my vote.

This buffet is WAY overrated 
Came in first for a dinner to find out the wait was 2.5 hours long. So we tried again the next day for brunch, the wait was still over 2 hours. We paid $55 on top of the regular buffet for a total of $115/ person for an express lane.. SO NOT WORTH IT! The food selections were mediocre. Quality and taste is so so. What's the hype?!? We spent the same amount for a nice dinner at Cipriani and the food was on point for Italian. Think twice before you get in those ridiculous long lines... trust me!

BE AWARE OF THE 5 HOUR WAIT.

The 4 of us went on a Thursday evening. We were told to put our name down at the kiosk machine, which we did at 4:17pm and were instructed to come back at 6:29pm. Kiosk machine was broken and never dispensed ticket. Came back then and were told we couldn't get in line until we show them the text message, which we recieved at 6:43pm (2.5 hours later). Finally got in line and were told to wait another 2.5 hours to pay and get seated. ARE YOU SERIOUS? You can't be upfront about the 5 hour wait? I would have went to Wicked Spoon if I knew. 

In addition. The staff seemed annoyed to answer even one question. Understaffed much? 

Anyways, thanks Bucchanal for the horrible customer service and for wasting our precious time.

We finally showed up at a good time with hardly any line.  The day was Sunday, December 17 at about 5:15 pm.  We haven't been for about 4 years because of the line.  

The downside of no lines means that some of the less popular items sit and get cold.  Of course the popular items like the crab is still fresh because of the heaping plates sitting on most of the tables.  

I usually eat a few crab legs but I lean more towards their Asian choices.  Their sushi is good and rolled nice and tight.  They have Japanese Oshinko pickles.  I can't even get that at most Japanese restaurants.  Their dim sum choices are delicious.  They are usually hot and in the traditional steam baskets.  As for the American choices, the fried chicken and pizza are pretty good too. 

Save room for dessert because not only is their dessert pretty, it's all delicious.  Well.. maybe except for their cookies.  They were hard and cold.  The donuts on the other hand were fresh and yummy.  The macarons and the macaroons were all delicious.  I also had a white chocolate mousse that was outstanding.  
 
Prices are high and if you don't fill up on crab, you can definitely can not feel like you're getting your money's worth.  My husband doesn't eat any crab or shrimp.  He mostly eats the carne asada Tacos.  Those are some expensive tacos.  

Our seating for 2 were very close to our neighbors on both sides.  Definitely can feel like a pig with people sitting so close.  Well, I guess we are all in the same pig boat.

I am livid about our experience here tonight. It was the ONE place my son wanted to go in Las Vegas. We called before getting an Uber and the operator told us it was currently a 30 min wait. We hopped in an Uber and $20 later we were at Caesars. There is a very meek woman at the entrance to the line. I asked how long the wait was and she said 45 minutes but you have to check in here first - pointing to a digital kiosk. I entered my info in the kiosk and the stated wait time was 37 minutes. Great. We killed time walking around and came back at the specified time. The last opens the rope to the line. We were alarmed at how many people were there and asked how much longer the wait would be. Another 45-60 minutes. We have show tickets so we had to leave. And now another $20 Uber ride to get back where we need to be. Without dinner. 
I get that the place is popular and there is a line. Which is why I called ahead. HORRIBLE service and crowd management.

Was in Vegas for a couple of days with the homies and when in Vegas, you gotta hit up a buffet! Why not choose one of the best in town! Everything about this buffet was nice. The staff were very attentive and friendly. We came right when dinner started on a Saturday and luckily the wait wasn't too long. The price was $70 for dinner which sounds expensive but for the food you get, it was just right. Also if you yelp check in, you get a complimentary alcoholic beverage. It was either a house wine, beer, or cocktail. 

There is so many different foods to choose from it would be impossible to list them all. But they had different meats, seafood, and desserts. I enjoyed the snow crab legs which were steamed, the bone marrow, and the freshly shucked oysters! There were other foods I ate which all tasted good, but those were my favs. 

If you're in Vegas, there's no excuse not to try The Bacchanal buffet. Even if you don't eat much, you gotta try it! Definitely will be back again the next time I'm in Vegas!

BELIEVE ALL THE HYPE! 

well in my opinion you prob should! my bf and i were there looking at the line and i was this close to not waiting but my bf said we should just stay. we went on a saturday during their brunch hour. although it was a bit pricey...but hey it IS called a VACATION plus you are in vegas..youre gonna overpay anyways but hey you gotta splurge all that moneyyy honeyyyy!!

we stayed in line for 40mins - which wasnt so bad because the line was moving time to time. i was looking at the lights by the lines and i was getting worried that all those glasses would fall during a earthquake haha. the service was nice, the chef at the meat station was pretty cool and he welcomed my bf and i as we were walking to our tables. 

omg the food was AMAZINGGGGGGG! the stations were crazy amanzingly delicious! they have horchata, street corns, all kinds of meats, the asian station was pretty good and i was rollin' out like i was going to give birth to a cow. i was walking out of the place wanting so badly to go back to the hotel to lay down!

worth the hype? yes! expensive? yes!  
long lines? yes! should you stay?! HELL YEA!!!!

The Bacchanal was my favorite out of the 3 buffets I tried it Vegas. They had the most options and most of what I tried I liked. The sushi was fantastic and the dessert options were the best! Perfect macarons and delectable Vietnamese "coffee".

So this is the first buffet I went to in Las Vegas. My wife and I are not normally buffet people but I read quite a few things about it and so we went. We thought it was going to be $40 each but it turned out that dinner was $70 each. To be honest now that I know what I know, it was totally worth it. The environment is very clean and modern. The service was very nice. All of the services were the food was were very well clean and organized. The selection was unbelievable. The best things that I enjoyed were; the hot crab, Definitely the oyster bar, the truffles egg, the duck and the pork belly were also extremely good. I had a tremendous amount of food and didn't feel disturbed or have any kind of upset stomach. It was actually really good quality food and I definitely ate my fill. Having visited another Las Vegas buffet the next day I can really say that this was heads and tails above anything else I've seen. I recommend it if you don't want to go out for expensive fine dining meal. If you can eat a lot of food, and well prepared buffet food this is a great place to go. I recommend definitely having the hot crab station over the cold crab. I think my favorite was the oyster bar though. Unlimited large oysters that were very fresh and very well shucked. A good place to eat. To be honest Las Vegas is extremely expensive no matter what and this was a good deal for the money if you like eating a lot of food.

The only reason I enjoy going to Las Vegas is because of the food, and of course this means buffets.  The Bacchanal Buffet is said to be the "best buffet in Vegas" and it better be if they're going to charge $65+ per person. I'm going to go into a lot of detail about the entire experience because there is more than food to this review.

Starting with the set-up of the restaurant, it is split up into different sections. Next to the entrance, there are the crab legs and shrimp cocktail, basically all the seafood. Next, is the American food, mashed potatoes as well as mac & cheese: comfort food galore. They have a Mexican section w/ horchata and pozole. Moving to the back of the buffet is the Italian section, and finally the Asian one with sushi, miso soup, etc. My favorite section is the dessert section, they have a crepe maker and this is my favorite part of the entire buffet. The first and last thing I get whenever I come here is a nutella crepe with homemade whipped creme, MY FAVORITE.

The food is exceptional. All the bowls that the food are served in are placed over heaters, so the hot food stays hot and fresh. I love the dessert section, gelato, chocolate covered strawberries, I could stay here all day. If you're feeling fancy and hungry, try this place and you will definitely be coming back for more.

I'll preface this by saying that I'm not a buffet fan, although I've been to my share. I think this is a typical case of tons of quantity, and lesser quality. It's not bad...it's just void. I didn't think it was worthy of all the accolades it received. And be forewarned, the seafood options that are mentioned are not available at all mealtimes. I went for breakfast, and there was no king crab in sight- just Jonah crab, which is second-tier in comparison, and difficult to eat. Mine were still frozen.

There are multiple cuisines represented, and a nice looking charcuterie display. Like most buffets, it had a lot of carb "filler" foods. The salad bar sort of reminded me of a Sizzler. 

I agree with other reviewers who said the dessert display is the most expansive and impressive. Everything I sampled, looked and tasted good. The servers were older ladies who seemed exhausted. I felt bad for them. 

For the price, I'd rather go to my local buffet, where you get both king crab for breakfast AND unlimited mimosas. In Vegas, I'll stick to sit-down restaurants.

Expensive ($60) but delicious. Lots of variety and well kept. Staff isnt the nicest, especially the hostess, but the servers and cooks were much nicer. The only thing I didn't enjoy was the 90 minute wait and the oysters were unfortunately disappointing.

Way overpriced. I don't see the hype. Yeah it was good but was it $60 good? Not at all. I left feeling like I wasted my money and I could have gone out to dinner for myself at least 4 times somewhere else spending the same money. Our server didn't pick up our plates or refill our drinks and a different server had to do it for him. They really should rethink the pricing although I know they won't. Very crowded. Some of the food was good but I just expected a lot more considering how excited I was to eat there. I will not be going back.

This is probably one of the most hyped up places in Vegas. Here is why.

1. No reservations accepted
2. Average wait time is atleast 1 hour, probably more than two hours during peak times. 
3. The buffet is extraordinarily expensive (ranging from 50-80$ depending on the time/day of the week, season etc). 
4. Seafood (yeah, I hear you, Asians) has a separate queue in the buffet (took us 30 minutes in the seafood station to get to some crab legs). 
5. Food at best is mediocre. 

Bottom line - Go to the buffet if you want some pretty instagram moments but the food won't please you. And your pockets won't thank you. 

My advice - several other less hyped buffets in town which are cheaper with less wait times and better food!

=====================================

EDIT TO THE ORIGINAL 

I was contacted by Bacchanal. Turns out there is a "VIP experience" for 98$ - No wait and available through opentable. Or you got to be a VIP to get in (whatever club/gem status equivalent they use to define that). 

So.... pay double or be a big fish for the hotel. ‍ Else wait 2 hours and still pay twice as any other buffet in the city. 


And they did claim to be the best buffet in America. I have attached the picture  of the messages and leave the verdict to my readers.

My husband and I selected the Bacchanal Buffet during our inaugural trip to Las Vegas based on the great reviews. There was a relatively short wait for a table and our server was very attentive. I was amazed by the sheer variety of foods available. When I thought I had reached the end of the line I would turn a corner and there was a whole new section. I tried a little bit of most everything and nothing really stood out to me as delicious or particularly memorable. I didn't eat anything that was bad, but I didn't enjoy my meal. I feel like I had a completely different experience than what I read in the reviews that prompted me to come in the first place.

Excellent environment, friendly service, greatmenu choices and really decent food and at affordable prices. Will be back." "What a lovely restaurant, good food and service and atmosphere, definitely hope to go back.  YUMMY!!!"

We had read good things about Bacchanal Buffet which is known as one of the finest buffet spots in Las Vegas, so we decided to give it a try. 

But first, finding this restaurant was quite a challenge. Located inside the Ceasar's Palace casino, passed the Forum shops and precisely across from Rao's restaurant. We arrived at 5 p.m. on a weekend and already the place was swarming with people. They have two lines: one to pay and the other to enter the dining area. It was chaotic. 

The restaurant itself is spacious and quite extravagant, it rings fancy big time. As for the food, they have different stations representing different regions (Mexican, Italian, American, Japanese, etc) and those excluding the dessert station that's definitely worth checking out.  I must say that they did a good job in displaying each station, it was quite eye-catching. 

With over 500 choices, I didn't have the belly capacity to try them all lol, but some highlight for me is the Alaskan King crab and prime ribs (who can say no to those?). I also had some sushi and Chinese cuisine, which I thought was underwhelming. The burgers/sandwiches and pizza was just decent. The dessert station, however, was quite special, they have shaved ice, gelato and crepes... Love this! 

The price is ridiculously high for a buffet, on our visit, dinner cost $65 per person.

The service, on the other hand was very efficient, they are prompt in filling up our drinks and clearing up our plate.
