Since this is one of the most busiest buffet in town, come early for a friendlier queue. Overall, glad to have sampled a terrific amount of variety in great quality. But I feel like it might just be a one time thing for me.

A great variety of food, only some are great. Bone marrow, prime rib, boiled crab legs, fried sweet potato ball are the ones I recommend. The Japanese section is neither fresh nor flavorful. The Chinese dim sum section is ok, but not worth the $55 price tag. Other things are just very average and you can pretty much eat them anywhere. I think it's a little over priced even though you have many choices. I recommend people to come and try it for once and be done with it. If you love cold seafood, then maybe you will enjoy more but for me I don't like eating cold food for dinner so I only ate the boiled crab legs for seafood.

I had breakfast at the bacchanal buffet this morning and had a wonderful experience, the food service was excellent, so many choices! It was my first time here and as vegas local i know phenomenal service when I see it , our drink server was absolutely great very patient, polite and with a beautiful smile was happy to give us yummy recommendations! thanks Sandra from Brazil (if I'm correct) and Caesars Palace for hosting a spectacular buffet!!
Breakfast selection was amazing I loved everything! Especially the Mexican food! The fresh squeezed orange juice was awesome and I loved that there was birria

We came for breakfast.  Completely missed the board that forewarned us of the pricing. For two was nearly 100 bucks.  No one can eat that many eggs or pancakes, seriously.  The food was really good.  The orange juice is fresh squeezed.  The bacon was cooked nicely and the sausage had a nice flavor.  I liked how many of the offerings had their own little dish.  The eggs Benedict, I thought was wonderful even cold (not cold by their choice, but rather that was the last item I tasted on my plate).  The Menudo is not "Authentic" but the flavor is pretty yummy.  If you don't know the true meat ingredients Menudo then you will be happy with the hunks of pork roast.  They had mini pancakes topped with fresh berries as well as red velvet mini pancakes that looked decadent.  They offered a nice array of Asian cuisine that I would expect served at dinner as well as sushi offerings.  They had a fresh omelette station as well that had your standard offerings.  We attended the Buffett during the week.  Food was ve good, again pricey for breakfast, but then again everything in this Resort is pricey. I now understand why Caesar is draped in gold.

9/27/2019.  Dinner leaves a lot to be desired. For the price of $65 per plate they should have a lot of things right.  Unfortunately,  there was a lot of wrongs.  The crayfish was so over cooked it was quickly transferred to the trash plate.  The prime rib was tough and had no flavor.  The Tri Tip had a good flavor but was tough and difficult to chew.  The rotisserie chicken had a flavor that was just weird, kind of earthy, but not cumin or cinnamon flavoring.  The crab legs, were sweet and would have been a home run if they hadn't been over cooked.  
The Mac n cheese the pasta could have stood a few more minutes in cooking as it was just before al dente. 
The mashed potatoes, I'm not real sure if they were made with real potato's but interesting with hatch chili's and cheese.  The had a twice baked stuffed baked potato with bbq tritip, not bad but the bbq was super sweet to the taste.  They offered a lot of seafood that I wouldn't venture to eat.  Sea snail, clams, shrimp, whole prawns.  
There was pizza, and a taco bar serving Carnitas. Menudo, nachos.  An offering of sushi along with run of the mill Asian fare.  
Spend the money for breakfast,  but I can't figure out why to spend the money for dinner.  ‍

There's something about Las Vegas that brings out everyone's inner glutton. Look no further than the Bacchanal at Caesar's to satisfy your desires. At $49.99 for brunch and $59.99 for dinner the price tag is hefty, but find solace in the fact that there are enough dishes to make your head spin. With its reputation as one of the best buffets in Vegas (one it lives up to), a small wait is unavoidable. But even with a large party of twelve, I ended up getting seated mid-Saturday afternoon in about 30 minutes. 

As a firm believer of value eating at all-you-can-eat restaurants, I would suggest pacing yourself, which is easier said than done, and staying away from most of the Asian dishes and carbs. Instead, gorge yourself with succulent, perfectly medium rare prime rib (they also have wagyu beef!), fresh oysters and shrimp, and of course the coveted steamed crab legs. In addition to these buffet classics, Bacchanal churns out more dishes as the day transitions from breakfast time to lunchtime to dinner. Keep a look-out for dishes like baked bone marrow, T-bone of lamb, and even soft shell crab. 

If you haven't KO'd into a food coma or had the meat sweats at this point, there is still a crepe bar and a fully loaded dessert section with fresh fruits and assorted pastries. Oh, and they also have an ice cream section with neat flavors like lemon basil. Finish off by questioning how you managed to eat your own body weight, and waddle happily out the door.

The first time I tried Bacchanal was when they were newly opened and it was actually a first for me to wait in line for more than 2 hours just to eat at a buffet. The people in our large group were pretty much irritated with each other and you just pray that this better be worth the time and the additional cost (we had the buffet of buffets pass and back then it was an additional $10 for Bacchanal). If you ask the people in our group, they will probably tell you it's not worth it (they ran out of the big plates so we just had to cram our food in those little dessert plates, they also ran out of utensils, they were closing in less than an hour, buffet line was long, food ran out, our group needed to be in 3 separate tables in different corners of the restaurant, etc). But I have been back twice since that fateful evening and yes, Bacchanal redeemed itself and I'd have to say it is worth it. A solid 4 stars for me. Just be mindful of the time you are going or expect that you will be waiting in line for a long time. 

With that said, they have so many different kinds of food. Their selection is so massive- seafood, chinese, thai, mexican, italian, etc! Some of their dishes are also pre-plated on small dishes. Great idea to prevent people from getting more than they can handle. Speaking of handle, they also provide you with these little finger protectors (lol I don't know what the hell they are called) to prevent you from burning yourself when picking up hot dishes. Thanks for thinking about our well-being. Oh! They also have juice bottles in the buffet line that you just gotta try! They have different flavors- strawberry, mango, etc. Overall, quality of food is top-notch and delicious. Their dessert station is awesome as well plus, it looks so pretty! Lastly, service is always exceptional. One of the best in Vegas for me!

My friends and I were making a trip to Vegas from the bay area. When it comes to buffets over here, we only have mediocre places like hometown buffet or asian buffets such as Tomi, which used to be Todai. Bleh. After asking my friends for a recommendation of where to eat, many suggest Bacchanal and I am SO glad that my group and I settled for Bacchanal. The food is outstanding and everything is high quality. It is a bit pricy. For a week day dinner, it was $55 including tax, but I still think my meal was worth it taking that most of the things I ate was seafood. :) There was seriously so much variety and different kinds of foods. There was also a meat area where they served sausages and meatballs and I could definitely tell that it was high quality and fresh. 
The first thing I want to do when I get back to Vegas is go to Bacchanal. o:)

I love this buffet. The best in Vegas you can have everything you want. The only problem it's the line during the brunch and the price. 
The best moment it's the night for diner.
This buffet was amazing! So much food & so many options. I was stuffed when I left. If you're in Las Vegas go to this buffet!!

With the Groupon, the breakfast buffet was an amazing deal!  Everything was delicious and decadent and the service was phenomenal. Our server, Sandra, was always helpful and very sweet. I would definitely come back.

Crab 
::drool:: 
Lobster claws 
::drool::  

This is definitely the best buffet for price and location!  If you check in on Yelp you get a free alcoholic beverage.  Sometimes has a long wait so plan accordingly!

Best Buffet as of date! What are you doing reading this? You should be on your way there.. beating the lines!

Long Version:

If you are here to gobble down crab legs, what are you doing here? You can get those at Todai for cheaper! Crab legs come out of a box, defrosted and served. Bacchanal had no influence on the taste.

You're here because you are trying the quality of their prepared foods. Prime rib? Melts in your mouth! Potatoes au Gratin? Buttery and flavorful! Fish and Chips? One of the best I had!

Best part? They offer every selection in tapa sized portions. Gone are the days where you would be stuffed because you got one pizza slice too many, or that one dish was just a little too big. Now, they are portioned small so you can eat more of a selection!

Definitely try this place! You won't be disappointed!

There's never enough stomach space to try everything here and it's a shame because it's ALL delicious. Highlights are the crab legs (not a seafood fan myself, but my brother helped himself to several plates), carne asada street tacos, ramen, wide selection of freshly pressed juices, mac and cheese, and the amazing sweet potato TOTS! Don't even get me started on the dessert selection because I could eat their creme brûlée, lava cake, and chocolate covered strawberries all day. Bacchanal's does periodically swap out items from their menu and they serve specialty items during holiday weekends as well. 

The wait is always horribly long (it was a 2.5 hour wait the day before New Year's Eve) but the food is always delicious and the service is excellent.

Their first names are Mehdi, Martha and Leonard, but their last names are WOW!!!

By far, the absolute best buffet experience, best high quality food and dessert options and hands down, the best service team not only in Vegas, but anywhere! Mind you, the lines are long, but worth the wait!

The Manager, Mehdi had the place running like a well oiled machine! As it was extremely crowded due to the holiday, he managed to juggle the logistics and operation with a smile! When he found out it was my birthday, and despite it being Christmas Eve, he sent Champagne as a courtesy for an extra special touch to our celebration! The great service didn't stop there though... 

Our server, Martha was wonderful! Very attentive and delightful. She saw we loved the steamed crab legs and had a large portion brought to our table to enjoy!!! Wow, just wow!

After feasting on what may be the very best meal we've ever had in Vegas, it was time for dessert. To our surprise, yet another above and beyond moment. At the dessert station, Leonard heard it was my birthday and decorated a cake plate, with a candle ready for us to seal this exceptional experience just right!

Be sure you don't let this opportunity pass you by when you're in Vegas. Don't be turned off by any long lines because it is worth the wait. Suffice it to say, this will be a dinner experience to remember! SPEC-TACULAR! You're welcome

Two thumbs up and a snap.

You will pay for it but you will be extremely happy.

Drinks were always full. 

Buffet selection was phenomenal 

Quality was out of this world

If you are hungry and need to drop some of those winnings off, go here. You will not be disappointed at all.

We searched yelp and the internet and decided this was the place and it was. Will be back

Definitely one of the better buffets. I recommend the seafood as well as the marrow. There's a station for most cuisine.

The pho/soup station definitely stands out. Tastes delicious for a non pho place.
So good! Lorri was our waitress and did an awesome job. The food was delicious and I officially will not need to eat for a week. Buffet success.

Definitely the best buffet in Vegas and probably the world. Love that they have a ton of smaller dishes that you can just grab versus serving out of a huge pot. Great juice bar and meat section. A definite must. The trick is to go early to avoid long lines because it can get pretty long. But it's worth it.

Oh Bacchanal, how you've spoiled me.

Bacchanal seems to be the new hype around town, evident from the LONG wait line for Thanksgiving weekend. After arriving at Bacchanal at around 5pm during the Thanksgiving weekend, we were informed the wait time would be around 3 hours. If you were willing to dish out another $20 for the express line, you'd still be looking at 1hr wait time. And since it's the holiday season, prices had gone up to reflect the holiday spirit.

No matter, we were prepared to wait. I mean, I get to eat my fill of fresh oysters, I would be willing to wait for that!

So...after a turtle-slow moving line and well over three hours later, we found ourselves finally at the pay counter. In the meantime, we were entertained by the other onlookers or passer-by scoffing at all those dumb people willing to wait for so long just to get into a buffet...or maybe we were entertaining them? Who cares?

The seafood station is right by the entrance, all those shelves in transparent container sure kept me giddy for bit, not to mention watching those crab legs and oysters being shucked. So as soon as we got our table, I went to the seafood station.

Food was definitely fresh, since you can see them being prepared right in front of you. In fact, there were such a long line at the seafood station, and since most people were there for the crab legs, the service guy just ended up serving crab legs right out the pot! Hot, steaming crab legs, how can you not love it? The downside was since oysters were being shucked fresh, there wasn't enough to go around. I just grabbed half a dozen before I got a guilt trip and had to leave so there would be enough for the people waiting behind me. But no matter, I visited the station numerous times to get more~

The fried goodies, like french fries, tater tots, came in individual serving sized frying basket, which I thought was very considerate and cute. The french fries were still crunchy after I've left them on the table for over an hour.

Sadly I didn't have enough stomach to sample the other stations, though I don't regret that at all. Next time when I'm back in Vegas, I'll still drop by Bacchanal to get my seafood fix!

Best buffet I've had on the strip. They have an electronic system that allows you to reserve a spot without having to endlessly wait in line. Smart.

For $55/person, it's not the cheapest but it sure is the greatest. Sooo much variety that it takes a minute to soak it all in. Their seafood is incredibly fresh so don't waste stomach space - go straight for the seafood station if you're a 1 plate wonder like me. It's worth it.

The food and service was great, but the lines are long and horrendous. With I've 100 people in line it was three cashiers and the third cashier was directly traffic. You guys must come up with a better solution to relieve the stressful lines. You'll receive a beer and or a glass of wine if you check-In and show it to the waiter.
The picture should say it all this place is expensive but very much worth the price!!!!

Came to the Bacchanal Buffet for Sunday brunch around 11:00am, or so. Beware: the line CAN get long, so make sure to plan accordingly. There is also a "time limit" of two hours to dine at the Bacchanal Buffet. Lines everywhere. (BTW: they have a $15 all you care to drink option that may be added on top of the buffet price that I passed up because I just wanted oranges juice and water.)

Favorite things: mini churros, French fries, bacon (all the bacon), Denver? Colorado? egg mix with bell pepper and cheese, and gelato ice cream. I was so full that I couldn't try the eggs Benedict like I was wishing. Other food I did have on my plate but didn't like as much: crab legs and shrimp cocktail. There was also a line to get these items but really the legs and shrimp were a bit too frozen-esque for my liking. 

I think there is something for everyone!

I just wish it wasn't so expensive....... hmm.

Vegas is a mecca of food... and this buffet alone boost that they have other 500 items for you to gorge on! I don't know if there really is 500 items and I don't plan to count them anytime soon... but this buffet does have a HUGE selection! And seriously, like everything I tried was good!

I've been here several times and it's hard to say if this buffet is better than Wicked Spoon. I think they are pretty much head to head and I guess it would come down to personal preference as to which place has more foods you like to eat. I've been to both buffets several times and even I can't decide which I like better! As far as the Studio B buffet at the M hotel that is also raved about, I think that buffet is nowhere to compare to Bacchanal or Wicked Spoon. I've tried Studio B buffet - I didn't like it much... 

Anyways, this buffet feels very open, airy, and the lighting is good. When you enter, cold seafoods are to your right, followed by American food, hot meats, Mexican food... follow the corner and you will hit the Italian, salads, and Asian food sections. You can order and customize tacos, pasta, and Asian noodles. They even have honeycombs here! The desserts here are also very good and I always take a gelato cone to-go!

As far as prices, this buffet is the MOST expensive of them all!! Dinner is a staggering $51 and lunch is $32. If you have a total rewards card, it will take $1 off the price and give you some tier credits as well. I've never experienced a line here, but from what I read, the line can be horrendous... maybe I've just always gone at the perfect time! During breakfast/lunch, they have fresh squeezed juices which taste amazingly fresh! The only difference I've noticed between lunch and dinner were the cold seafood... since I'm not a fan of cold seafood, it's not worth paying an extra $20 to me. If I wanted to gorge on purely seafood, I would just go to the Village Seafood Buffet at Rio which is $45 because they have HOT seafood, including all the lobster tails you can stomach. Service here is good and they clean your tables fairly quickly. 

NOTE: This buffet is NOT included in the Buffet of Buffet passes. Breakfast is extra $15, Lunch is extra $20, and Dinner is extra $25. I've done the buffet of buffet pass before and I don't think it's worth it to use it here and pay the surcharge. Just use the buffet of buffet passes to it's full value at the other buffets and come here to eat another day. 

I think this buffet is definitely worth the try! I've gotten many people to fall in love with this buffet after trying it. I think by a small margin, I would say that this buffet wins when it comes to the Bacchanal vs Wicked Spoon buffet. It's like saying one got an A++ and the other an A+. Both are spectacular buffets. Wicked Spoon is however the original master of this new way of buffet - high end foods in small portions. If price is more important, than go with Wicked Spoon, dinner there is about $40.  I think that I would say that Bacchanal wins barely because they have a larger selection and a slightly more upscale feeling. They also have candy in candy jars! I can't wait to come back here and eat again!

I've been to Bacchanal Buffet too many times to count as a child, unfortunately I don't think the quality is worth the time, effort, and money. 

I came for brunch last year and we made a reservation since there was Enough people. Unfortunately I couldn't find anything that was worth the money besides unlimited juice. There simply wasn't anything to justify their cost besides the fact that it's a buffet at Caesar's Palace.

Dinner this past weekend was a disappointment as well. When it came down to which buffet on the strip, we came here because there were seafood options. Sadly their oyster wasn't fresh. There was a hint of creaminess such from personal experience, suggests diarrhea down the road. 

Sushi options we minimal to non existent with a couple of basic fusion rolls and nigiri where there's too much rice. American Kobe steak tasted like which is weird brisket since the two completely different types of meat. 

Waiting list is ...stupid lol
You put your party size, name, and number down. You wait till a text is received to return. But once you return, the wait is another hour..so what's the point? Might as well cut people off at 7 so they can go enjoy their meal elsewhere.
This was ok buffet not the greatest not the worst. I didn't like their sea food clams were not good. Very pricey! For that price not impressed.

I want to say I was impressed but truly I expected more. I enjoyed the variety of food it was a good selection. I dealt with the staff very little but the few interactions weren't really welcoming or kind. I had several different food items I enjoyed a couple but most were OK at best. I am never a huge fan of buffets because they have an overwhelming feeling to them. I kind of had a hard time navigating this buffet as well I thought some of the placement of items was off. All in all I had good food, fresh pressed oranges juice, chilaquiles, a good omelette, some good Chinese options, and tried some other items as well.
Great food! Fun times. Went here with a few coworkers visiting from out of town. The line was very long but moved very fast didn't even have to wait long.

A wide variety of foods to choose from. I had the crab legs, shrimp cocktail, sushi and a variety of Japanese pickles that I love. I tried the Pho. There was so much to choose from. I'm sure anyone could find something to eat here. If you love seafood than the $60 you pay will be well worth it.

Here in Vegas for 1 month and went to eat at the buffet twice. Best to come just before 3 pm when the line up isn't too long to get in and you save $15 per person off the supper price. They let you stay up to 2 hours, which allows you try out some of the lunch items before they start bringing out the supper items. Everything I tried was well prepared and of high quality.  There is also something for every food preference you can imagine. I like taking shall bits of as many different things as possible.
Ramona is the best server in Vegas! We had a great time and ate too much but can't wait to come back!  The mimosas are great too!

Probably the best buffet in memory. It might be better than the one I had at the Bellagio.

The presentation is way beyond what one would normally expect at a buffet. Seemingly meticulously presented shot glasses of soup and gazpacho, little cups and cones of desserts, pleasingly plated netted baskets of waffle fries and fried chicken, the individual portions of lobster bisque and Cajun steamed crawfish, and the single serve bottles of freshly squeezed orange juice (nothing like it!).

And it goes beyond mere presentation. They taste as good as they looked, maybe even better at times. The shot glass of ceviche is probably one of the best I've had, if not *the* best. The desserts were fantastic; I'd highly recommend the sugar-free cheesecake and the sugar-free creme brulee. The understated flavours of these two desserts were outright home-runs, touch downs, three-pointers, sixer, goal, or whatever sports-related superlative you might want to use to describe it.

The day's chef's special dish of, what I guess, Halibut with shavings of coconut was indeed special! The dim sums were good, and the sushi, passable. I guess no matter what you try, it's just not possible for left-out-in-the-open sushi to compare with made-to-order sushi. But keeping that in mind, the sushi didn't disappoint much.

It's funny how the spread is spread out around the corner. When you take a few steps to "that faraway table", you realise there's more just around the corner. And this repeated about three times for me. It was like going down a rabbit-hole --- albeit a very pleasant one. :-)

At $38 (inclusive of tax), it's more than bang-for-the-buck.

Amazing good food located at Caesars palace on the strip. I would be 5 star but it is just to expensive. The lines are way long, I got my diamond card now which helps a lot but I have had to wait 45 minutes before getting it. 

I wish I could pay less and not get seafood like the Rio offers. Many people get 3 huge plates of crab legs and make the cost go up for everyone, just seems terrible because I will not eat here nearly as often as I would if it was $10 less for people that didn't want the seafood. 

They don't give discounts to locals or diamond card holders which is so bad. I really hope they take a look at fixing this like the recently fixed the Rio and offer good discounts for locals. 

It would be a easy 5 star if they just did something to make it better for locals and make the seafood separate add on. 

Will hopefully update later for the better but can only give them 4 star at the moment.

A pricey but excellent buffet.  Quite possibly the best Ive ever had.  Excellent were the fish, the prime rib, the pot roast.  Crab legs were OK but smaller and salty.  Cocktail shrimp was good.  Desserts were top notch.  Service and decor were excellent.

I read that Bacchanal was named number 1 best buffet in Vegas so I decided to give it a try. 

PROS:
The crab legs were good. I liked that they were cut in half so it was easy to eat. 
The prime rub was very good, long line. 
Lobster bisque
Truffle cream soup 
Gelato 
Dessert 

CONS:
The stone crab claws were not my favorite. A bit too mealy...
No oysters either for brunch, other than the oyster shots. 
Sushi, very mediocre... 
Service was slow and inattentive... Probably because we were seated behind a pillar but that still made it frustrating because I saw other tables next to us getting served. 

Overall, good buffet but I would go elsewhere as I love seafood and I felt their offerings were limited.
So much improvement since the first time I went. This is the best buffet in Vegas. It has a little of everything you could want. All high quality food,variety of desserts, and clean.

Ok this is by far the best buffet I've ever been to! I'm not a huge fan of buffets but the Bacchanal is outstanding. Worth every penny as all the food is small portions and tastes made to order. Ridiculous amount of options. It also feels like your in a restaurant rather than at a buffet. The seafood was so fresh and the meat was cooked perfectly, not to mention so many delicious deserts all in small bite portions so you can try them all. Seriously this a must while in Vegas!!!

I was a little disappointed that the second time around was pretty much all the same food for dinner. It was even $50 per person on a Wednesday night. I went during brunch my first time for only $35. Same seafood, same EVERYTHANG. Well everything was still good, I love the oyster bar. 

The service was great. My sister mentioned she forgot butter for her crab legs and all of a sudden a server walks by and handed her a cup of butter because he overheard us...talk about great service................

This buffet is excellent! I came for lunch on a Saturday around 12:30PM and only waited about 20 minutes before we were seated. The decor inside is gorgeous! We were curious why everyone had mimosas on their tables and we found out it's included in the $45 price you pay for lunch!

The setup is very similar to Wicked Spoon but bigger and better! I love the king crab legs and the meat station. They also have Asian, Mexican, and a HUGE dessert station! They offer udon, pho, and ramen at the Asian station and fresh made tacos at the Mexican station. Great gelato and cookies at the dessert station.

Only downside is the waitresses are a little slow to refill your drinks, there doesn't seem to be enough workers to go around.

Too many different foods to describe but everything was excellent!

This buffet was recommended to me by many so o had to check it out. We put our name in and it was a two hour wait. Came back after two hours and than you check in with the hostess and wait in line for another hour. I was so hungry I had to have a snack before going in. Overall the food and desserts were amazing, $60 total for a Monday night dinner buffet with drinks included (non-alcoholic). They stop making food at 10pm but you are still able to get whatever they have left and eat as much as you can! Tons of seafood and meat!

We came to splurge on a buffet brunch and the variety was endless. There was breakfast and lunch food items to pick from and the dessert bar was heaven! Wait time was surprisingly short, we came on a Sunday around noon.

If you like to wait 3-4 hours for some mediocre buffet food, then Bacchanal Buffet is for you! My girlfriend and I came to this buffet through many recommendations from friends as well as family. We were so excited to grub out on some yummy buffet food, but I'll tell you this, it is pricey and overhyped. 

This was our first time eating at this buffet located inside the Caesar's Palace. There was already a long line of people just waiting for their chance to get into this "remarkable" buffet as people have said. So the first thing you do when you get to the front, you have to sign your name into a machine and it'll print out a piece of paper of when you can actually go wait in line. You heard that right, you have to sign up to wait in line! Hilarious! After a 30-40 minute wait, you're in for a better treat, you then have to wait in the actual line so you can be seated at a table. This will take about 2-4 hours. For my girlfriend and I, it took us about 3 hours but if you count the 30-40 minute wait to actually get into the line, then you're looking at 4 hours in total. The price for the buffet was $65 each so in total it was around $135. Pretty pricey for a buffet, but we were told it was worth it so why not! 

We were finally seated at our table. We were so hungry, we had to get two plates each and stuff them with food. When we went to the different areas, some actually had ran out of food and were still in the process of making more because of the over capacity of people inside the buffet. Which was really odd to me because you're starving yourself for 3-4 hours, then you actually go inside and they've run out of food?! Wow. On top of that, to get fresh seafood, such as; oysters, sea-snails, crab legs, and other dishes that were made from fresh seafood was a 20 minute wait. 

They had a good selection of meat. They had prime rib, wagyu, applewood bacon, and some steaks, butte could only try the prime rib because we were told that the chef was still in the process of making it! Oh my goodness, terrible news to tell that to hungry people. 

Bacchanal Buffet has a huge selection of foods, fresh seafood, different types of meats, dim sum, Italian, Mexican, and also a dessert bar with gelato ice cream as well. They even had fancy bone marrow appetizers! Just because this place has nice pictures on Yelp and good reviews, don't let that fool you into going to this place. It was a good experience to try it, but would I go for a 2nd time? Absolutely not. Their food was rushed, flavor was a 3/10, just to be nice. I'm not a famous food critic, but trust me on this one, don't let the hype cloud your judgement on this place. Instead go somewhere that you don't have to wait more than an hour to eat. Whatever happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas. This buffet should definitely stay in Vegas.

What a buffet!  The food was soooooo delicious and the desserts....THE DESSERTS!!!  I won't need to elaborate on the food except...you should try it!  But, I did take away 1 star because of the following:

1. Of course the "best buffet in L.V." has about a 2 hour wait on Sunday evening at 6:30pm...still it was worth it.

2. We came in a group of 6 + 1 baby.  When we got to the cashiers, we told her that we had that many in our party and she told us that they only have seats for groups of 5 or less.  What?!  I don't believe it!  So we said we'd split if that was the only case.  When we got to the end of the line for seating, we saw TWO groups of more than 7 people (who were in line WAY behind us) go in together!  When I asked the host why we were told they didn't have tables for 6 or more, she told me we asked to split up!  And that if we really wanted to, we could've pretty much begged the cashier to put us together, but our wait would be much longer.  WHAT?!  The family BEHIND us didn't have a "much longer" wait than us.  

Usually, with service like that, I'd take at least 2 or 3 stars off...but it was good food, AND the waiters who walk around were SO nice!!!!  Yes, each person is about $51 during weekend dinner time, but this is a top buffet...I think it's actually CHEAP for what you'll get!

Went here with my family. Thought the food tasted great until a couple hours later I realized  I had dood poisoning. I called to complain. They sent me to security- took a complaint and hung up. Nothing else. Seriously- I am trying to enjoy a vacation and wind sick as can be and they just say give your info to security. 

Ruined my night and rest of my vacation!

I give this 5 stars if comparing it against other buffets. This was my second time here and it does not disappoint. The selection is plentiful and everything I put on my plate was well prepared and taste good. Like I started with this a 5/5 buffet. If I had to compare it against all other restaurants it would probably come in at 3.5 stars.

My God, avoid the oysters!

First, my wife and I stood in line for an hour JUST to PAY! But, a word to the wise...when you get past paying, the line for seating parties of +2 moves faster than parties of 2. So, we made friends with the people behind us who we had spent an hour with and were seated fairly quickly.

I'm fairly certain that the draw of this place is the crazy amount of options. They have everything! But, it's hard to do anything well when there's so much to do. All of it was mediocre at best.

Now, I had 3 Pacific oysters which my wife said was risky, given that we were in the desert. Um, let's just say that 4 hours after we left,  my $60 meal was sewer bound. DON'T DO IT!

This place is overrated. $60 in the slot machines is a better bet!

I came to Las Vegas and everyone said "You have to go Ceasars buffet it's the best in town".  Overpriced hype.  The food was mediocre.  The meats were dry or rare.  Grocery store quality sushi and Asian fare.  I was expecting knock your socks off for $118 for two.  Would not recommend it to anyone going to Vegas.   I would recommend skip it.

By far the best brunch buffet in Vegas!  The food choices are endless and the staff is so friendly and attentive! We will be back in our next visit to Vegas! Jennifer was our server and she goes over and beyond to make our dining experience 5 stars! It's nice to see a server with a smile on her face and one who looks like she enjoys her job here!

Dined in on 6/13/19. 2-3 days later, when I returned to Los Angeles, from Las Vegas, I contacted Bacchanal. Initially called to dispute a parking charge, along with informing management of my poor dining experience. I was informed they (did not write down name) would investigate the issue and contact me back. 2 weeks later, with no follow up avail. Called once again and requested to speak with a manager. This time, I took the name down (ROSE). I explained to Rose, my two issues during my dining experience.1. My server (Female)Was inattentive, disregarding and disrespectful. The issue started when I asked for "wet naps". She gave me a dirty look as if I had already asked and she had already provided (she didn't). She then looked at the table next to me and said to herself "Oh!" Because she gave the table next to me wet naps and not me. After asking for additional napkins, I didn't want to ask for anything anymore. Towards the end of my meal another party sat down next to us. They were very particular in what they needed (asked for items one at a time - Arnold Palmer, no ice. Cup of item. More napkins. Wet naps. Etc.) from the server. The server's response were "yes sir, yes ma'am, of course, right away..etc. I then asked for a refill on my Arnold Palmer (first refill and at the end of my meal), no response and had to ask for a second time. 2. Chef (Male at Crab Legs - Cold Bar)I asked the chef for additional crab legs. His response was "no crab legs for you." Was this because I had my 5th serving? Was this a joke? Whatever it was, it wasn't funny, especially what happened next. As I was going through the ice to dig out some crab legs, the gentleman (sat on the 3rd table to my right in a red shirt) behind shouted out, "do you guys have anymore crab legs???" The chef said, "yes of course, I'm just adding more ice first."
I just lost my appetite. How am I being TREATED completely differently completed to the patrons sitting to the table next to me and the one sitting 3 tables to my right?? I informed Rose, it could be due to discrimination. But, whatever it was, it was completely obvious and unnecessary. My mother and I didn't complete our meal and decided to leave, because if we stayed longer, we would have to pay for the parking (which we ended up paying anyways, because we were there for an hour and 3 minutes. 3 minutes over the allowed time to park for free). Rose apologized for the experience. She asked me what I thought the best service recovery resolution would be. I informed Rose, if I lived in Las Vegas, I would love to be asked to be invited back and to be taken care of. Rose said that's what she normally does for her guest, but because I didn't live in Las Vegas, there was nothing she could offer me. I informed her what about crediting me back the amount. Rose said she would love to and CERTAINLY would, but I waited too long to call for the request. I informed her, I did call once before, but no one called me back. Rose then said, "to be honest, a week is already too long for the request." I informed her again, at the beginning of the call, I said I called 2-3 after the day I dined with them. Rose then started getting irritated and informed me for the last time, she just doesn't have the power to look up the information, since she didn't have the physically card with her. I was willing to read out the credit card number, but she said she would not be able to do so. 
I then called my credit card dispute department and explained the situation. The credit card agent called, introduced themselves and asked for Rose. But the restaurant said, "we don't have a Rose that works here." I then asked the credit card agent to be on a recorded 3 way line with the merchant and myself. We were able to speak with Rose. I let her know, the credit card agent is on the call with us (they had already informed them we were on a recorded line) and that the credit company can open the transaction and refund the charged amount. Rose said she had no idea why this was happening. I reminded her what she had said. Since she wasn't able to open the check to refund me the amount, I asked the credit card company to help us. Rose then said she said no such thing. I continued to remind her. She then went off on me and said, "I would have taken off half the check, but since you're being such a %@%$^, you're getting nothing." And then Rose hung up.

They have different prices for different days. They have a lot of options. We went on a Sunday during brunch so the had breakfast, seafood, Asian food, and classic american food. It is also important to note that it cost around 65 dollars per person on Sundays. Make sure that you check the line signs when you go. Me, my friend, and my younger brother accidentally stood in the line for groups of 5 or more accidentally for 20 minutes. We finally got in 45 minutes later in the correct line. The dim sum was one of my favorites. I would have to say that the best part of the buffet was the dessert. The creme brulee, mosse's, crepe's and many more are delicious! They want to limit each group to a maximum of 2 hours but we only ate there for 1 hour and 20 minutes. Overall, it is definitely a once in a life time experience.

I have lived in Vegas my entire life and this definitely has to be the best buffet I have ever had. So many fresh tasty options to choose from. 

My husband and I came here around 3:30 pm hoping to beat the crowds. It was still pretty busy, but not as bad as it was starting to get when we left around 5 pm. 

We pretty much tried almost every meat option they had. We enjoyed lamb, prime rib, brisket, tri-tip, American wagyu, very thick cut bacon, meatball, barbecued pork ribs, halibut, salmon, some Mexican braised beef (can't remember name), king crab legs, and one Bloody Mary oyster shooter for myself. 

It took quite a while to get through the line to get crab. The crab was good but not as big as I would have liked. The other meats and fish were all very good, not the best, but still very good. We were disappointed to see there was no lobster, nor stone crab claws like we saw on previous yelp pics. 

We hit the desserts and everything was great. My favorites were the turtle cheesecake, creme brûlée, and the pecan bar. They had some no sugar added options that were decent too. 

Service was good. Im glad we finally got to try the infamous Bacchanal buffet. But I honestly don't think I would return especially since, as a local, I hate going to the strip. I also don't want to stuff my face and eat myself sick every time which is hard not to do at a great buffet.
Hard not to find something here that is excellent...service is great...found they had trouble on serving temperatures....but the variety more than made up for that short coming

My girlfriends were leaving Vegas a day earlier than the rest of us. What did they choose as their last meal? Bacchanal! We came by on Friday, July 10th around 1:30pm. The line wasn't bad at all and we got to the front within 5-10 minutes.

The lunch buffet is $39.99 with a 2 hour limit. Though I don't think they really enforce that as we were there until almost 5:30pm. The girls took part in the $22 all you care to drink mimosas, while the guys did the beer version. You also get to keep the glass as a souvenir. With the mimosas you can control the amount of juice, so if you just want sparkling wine, they will give it to you sans OJ.

We all hit the seafood first and loaded up on shrimp, oyster shooters, ceviches, crawfish, clams, mussels and crab claws. I actually started feeling full after we hit the seafood station, but I continued with the gluttony and hit the American food section. Grabbed some meat from the carving station, soups, salads, side dishes, etc. Now I'm hitting a food wall, but I decided to barge through it by hitting the Asian section. Loaded up on dim dum, roast pork, duck, etc. I skipped the sushi as it was mostly rolls. One of my friends got the ramen which looked delish, but I skipped it as I was trying to make room for the oysters and crab legs that just came out. So yes, I ventured back to the seafood section. Clarified butter and crab legs? Yes please!

I know there were many more plates than what I mentioned and took pix of, but I was too busy eating and thinking about what to eat next to remember to take pictures of everything. Though all the dessert I consumed was photographed. I just made myself a little dessert platter and got some gelato. I loved the matcha covered strawberry. The brulee and flan were also pretty good. Of the gelato flavors, I really only liked the black sesame. The raspberry hibiscus was too sweet and the green tea tasted like soap.

$62 for four hours of eating and drinking. All I can say is I've never felt that full in my life! I really wish I could have had even more, but there was no way I could stomach anything else. Even I got to a point where I could drink anymore. I'm not really a buffet person in general since I hate feeling super full, but one of the better places to do it is at Bacchanal.

We came for breakfast.  Completely missed the board that forewarned us of the pricing. For two was nearly 100 bucks.  No one can eat that many eggs or pancakes, seriously.  The food was really good.  The orange juice is fresh squeezed.  The bacon was cooked nicely and the sausage had a nice flavor.  I liked how many of the offerings had their own little dish.  The eggs Benedict, I thought was wonderful even cold (not cold by their choice, but rather that was the last item I tasted on my plate).  The Menudo is not "Authentic" but the flavor is pretty yummy.  If you don't know the true meat ingredients Menudo then you will be happy with the hunks of pork roast.  They had mini pancakes topped with fresh berries as well as red velvet mini pancakes that looked decadent.  They offered a nice array of Asian cuisine that I would expect served at dinner as well as sushi offerings.  They had a fresh omelette station as well that had your standard offerings.  We attended the Buffett during the week.  Food was very good, again pricey for breakfast, but then again everything in this Resort is pricey. I now understand why Caesar is draped in gold.

Best buffet in LV I have been to so far. The buffet is huge....don't miss the dessert buffet in the middle. Almost everything I had was delicious, truffled bechamel with poach egg was the best....the dim sum was wack as hell....there's better dim sum at those cheap dim sum places than what Bacchanal offered. That's my only issue with this place....other than that I absolutely will come back for brunch....it was a quick $40 but I know I got my money's worth out of this place....not to rag on other high end buffet....this is the best so far.

My boyfriend and I came here and decided that we'd try every and anything that we normally can't get access to regularly. There were a lot of options
 but the best part was the dessert section!

Best buffet we have ever been to. Stopped by on our way back to CA for brunch. The crab is frozen and terrible quality, but the shrimp was amazing. Everything else I ate was phenomenal. The dessert bar is outstanding.

Get here early to avoid the long lines! Hubs & I got in line around 4:30PM on Saturday & barely a line ;)

I'll just talk highlights since there's so many reviews already:

* SEAFOOD: Clams, crab legs, oysters & scallops. That's what you need to fill your plate with stat! Also grab little sauce containers to get your condiments. Be sure to go all the way to the end to grab the coconut ceviche shooter, it's the bomb!
* DIM SUM: I really didn't think the dim sum would be good, but I was wrong. So fresh & done right!
* AVOCADO TOAST: Soft toasty bread topped with plenty of avocado & assorted toppings. Didn't feel heavy at all. 
* DESSERTS: Tiramisu cup, chocolate covered strawberry (not the green one), pandan/ube/coconut cup & strawberry lychee gelato were the stars. Hubs liked the flan as well. 
* DRINK: Get the peach tea, so light & refreshing. Definitely better than the regular iced tea. 

Hubs & I really enjoyed our time here & stayed the whole 2 hours allotted to us. Probably the best buffet we've dined at to date! We'll definitely be back the next time we're in Vegas :)

Used to LOVE Caesar's Palace, but  it has become a little bland and boring over the years. They want to be modern and posh and thus are erasing all that was endearing like the talking fountains, the Omnimax, The Magical Empire or Caesar & Cleopatra walking around :(  WHY, oh WHY??? 


Despite the buffet's Roman name the decor is not reminiscent of old Rome.  What a pity! 
The food is fancy, but a little underwhelming for the rather enormous price.  All in all it was a good experience just not the one I had hoped for. Certainly nothing out of this world. I think I might go next door next time and see if the Mirage Buffet is still as delicious as it used to be, but I have little hope.

Great food great service. I think ever one who goes to Vegas and can afford it, should go to this buffet. I think their sea food is amazing, their fries at bomb, and their Mexican and Asia food is great but I don't suggest that you eat the Mexican rice because personally as a Mexican, I didn't like it.

This is my all-time favorite buffet in Vegas!

Although I feel like this visit wasn't as great as the last times, I still love this place!

They're getting better and more organized with their line system. Before you would wait, and wait, and wait in a long line to get in. Nowadays they have a ticket machine-- input your party info, how many, what type of occasion, your name, and your phone number. Then they give you your estimated wait time by printing out your ticket and they'll also be able to text you when you can go up to the front!

As to many buffets, Bacchanal has varieties of food to choose from! They're definitely more of the quality! Seafood, like steamed crabs, oysters, different fish dishes ; Meats, like prime rib, beef ribs, baby back ribs, sausages, smoked turkey, lamp chops ; Soups, clam chowder, mushroom truffle soup, chef's special ; Breads ; Mexican ; Asian, like pho, dim sums, fried rice, roasted duck ; Italian, like pizzas, meatballs, pastas ; Fresh Salad Bar ; Cheese and Dried Meats.. And I must not forget their desert bar! Make your own crepes, carrot cake, pandan tiramisu, chocolate cakes, macaroons, pies, AND their ice cream/sorbet section!
 
My favorites are the Wagyu Beef Sliders with their Truffle Potatoes!

Well worth the price! And a must try!

This is my fourth time eating here and once again, I was not blown away or impressed with anything here. 

My friends and I came for dinner a few nights ago and while the ambience was nice and the dining room was pretty, the food left a lot to be desired.

The pasta dishes (including the macaroni and cheese) were undercooked and hard. There wasn't much flavor either. 

The pizza was also very disappointing and tasted cheap like the Chuck E Cheese type stuff you get at theme parks. 

The "gelato" which tasted more like bland ice cream wasn't impressive either. 

This is one of the most expensive buffets in Vegas and you expect it to have very good quality. That was not the case and I suggest you save a few dollars and go to the Bellagio Buffet instead which has better tasting food.

I keep hoping that each time I come to Bacchanal I will have a better experience but honestly that just has never been the case. I only give three stars because there is a huge selection with many options but I value quality over quantity.
Been here several times and it seems like the quality is going down every time.  They have very limited cold press juice.  They use to have a full bar of it.  The chill seafood is a overly salty.

Great selection of food and friendly service. 

Be prepared to wait for the soup line ( averaging 30 minutes to 1 hour wait) 

Good is fresh but a bit salty so it'll fill you up pretty quickly. 

Selection of food range from American to Asian.
Super hard to eat!  The food is not fresh!  The waiter has a bad attitude!好难吃！超难吃！东西不新鲜！再也不来吃了！大家千万不要来吃！！！

THIS IS THE BEST BUFFET THAT HAS EVER EXISTED. They have large slices of delicious prime rib that was so tender, wagyu roast that has a delightful meat flavor, and a brisket that just falls apart. They have bone marrow with a little fog jam that just adds so much umami to the meats. They have unlimited king crab legs and you can pile on a deliciousness of buttery goodness. They have an Italian section with soups and pasta, the sausage ravioli was my favorite. An entire Asian section with pho, Thai curry, roast pork, bao, and then a wide assortment of sushi but the unagi is a can't miss! 

A seafood group that has a nice assortment of shrimp and mussels and how could you forget a taco stand that make fresh tacos right in front of you!

There's also a dessert island (which I barely had space for) but the crepes and bite size banana crepe pie were worth!

Let's start the year off with Gluttony!!!!

Well, not full gluttony, but a review of Gluttony.  So the Bacchanal Buffet has been touted as being the best buffet on the Las Vegas Strip.  That's a pretty tall order considering the amount of competition they have.  I mean, Las Vegas is synonymous to the word Buffet... or was it the other way around?  Either way, that statement is a HUGE statement.  

My verdict?  Over-hyped!!! Why?  I was told it's a mind blowing amazing buffet that has huge amounts of variety and great quality.  When I got in, I was presented with a decent variety with decent quality.  I think people see all the stations sprawled out about the walls and think that it's a ton of different variety.  In all reality, I think it's the same (okay maybe a little more) as the other major buffets, but just against the wall.  So when people say it's a huge variety, this was a disappointment.  

Quality was another thing that was said to be amaze-balls.  Was it great?  No!  The wifey and the in-laws all said it too, "It's good for a buffet".  If somewhere is going to be the BEST of the best, you can't add that "for a buffet" at the end of the statement, that's just cheating!   That's just not right!!!  The seafood station was okay, they had oysters, shrimp, crab legs, the usual fare.  Just nothing stood out.  The shrimp were slimy and the crab claws were poorly cut and had very little meatiness.  

In all reality, based on Quality and Variety, I'd probably give it a 4 star.  I mean, it is good.  Not amazing, but it is good.  Why 3 stars?  I had to wait 2.5 hours for this.  TWO AND A HALF HOURS!!!!  We went in at 4 o'clock thinking we'd beat the rush, nope!  After standing there for that long, after having asshats of people cut in front of us (who gave me dirty looks when i wouldn't move out of their way to cut), it was just not worth it!   The only saving grace for the line was that they had some computer kiosks that the wifey and I figured out how to get to the windows prompt.  Because it's vegas and everyone's watching, i put it almost back to normal.  Everyone behind us thought they were geniouses because they pulled up ms paint and had fun playing with it.  Your welcome. 

To add insult to injury of 2.5 hours of my life wasted in line, the price was insane.  We paid ~$60 pp NOT including tip.  They called it "Holiday pricing".  We called it a rip off since they didn't even have alaskan king crab legs (which i actually didn't mind.  I prefer snow crab).  

I read a lot of reviews with all the things they had before, and honestly, I think they did what all other buffets did.  Start of with great quality and decent prices. Once you get your name out there, jack up the prices and then let the quality slowly degrade.  That way no one knows the wiser.  Me?  I'll stick to Wynn.

TL:DR - Over-hyped.

I love the food choices and taste 
The 4 hours  wait was super long I wish there was a way
To check-in online n receiving texts before coming.
FYI you only have to 2 hours to eat. After 4 hours of waiting and paying  $75.76  I Felt some type of way when  my waiter told me you have two hours to eat starting now.

Here's a tip! Go about half an hour before the dinner times start, then you pay less, but still get to eat off the dinner menu - this buffet definitely gets pricey and long lines form!

Great variety of foods: meats, seafood, tacos, pho, sushi, pizza, crab legs, DESSERTS!

They do a great job at keeping food at all the stations, I went up for about 4-5 plates and had something new each time. Water, ice tea, coffee are all included in your pricing. 

Eat the mini lava cake !!!!!!!

I came here around 1pm to enjoy the brunch buffet. I have read so many reviews about this place and the buffet. My first thought was, "Am I really going to eat 50 dollars worth of food?" 

I occasionally like to dibble and dab in a buffet here or there. I said YOLO and went to see the hype! There was rope around to indicate they may have long lines for this buffet so I was happy that there was not a line. We just walked right up to the cashier to pay. After you pay, you are given a receipt to stand in another line for the hostess ...BUT wait! A camerawoman comes out to take your photo before you are seated! I'm serious. I was kind of baffled about that since I have never been to a buffet where they want to take your photo and you have the option of purchasing the photo as a souvenir. On a cruise ship, they may do that in the dining room, but a buffet..I dunno. It was interesting. 

After we were seated you can order water, tea, fountain drinks. They have Mountain Dew..score! 

Food: different varieties (seafood, Italian pastas, Asian dishes, tacos, American food, meats, desserts, fruits). Score ! There were many workers on the other side of the buffet keeping the food warm and refilling items as they got low.

The Poke Salad was the highlight of the meal. Amazing flavor! The mee goreng was delicious! The sushi was good, but it was not easy locating the soy sauce since somebody mixed up the sauces so I ended up with chili oil and soy sauce mixed lol! The dim sum was decent. I was not a fan of the Chicken Satay or Peking duck. Fresh shrimp was delicious. The dessert bar is large with endless options. I loved the mango habanero ice cream. Sweet then had a kick. Hard to choose something good. Their red velvet brownie and the Tiramisu were so yummy! Score!

Overall: the food was pretty decent. I agree with the other reviews that some items were lacking and some items really stood out. This buffet deserves a solid 4 stars. The servers were really nice and accommodating.

It's good, our second time here and a bit disappointing in taste of food. Love the presentation and numerous choices. 

Prime rib good, esp the Chinese ribs. Check out the prime rib block hubs got, sheez. Sushi good, desserts and other items average. I didn't hit some of the stations as they are pretty generic, just stuck to what I really like. 

Not as awesome as the first time, but I think it's because it WAS The first time, and it was beautiful. Price was $20 more for Presidents' Day (so $80/person). Not worth it, but we know now that one and done is enough, for the experience. It's just fun to choose your own. Our wait was about 45 min on a Saturday around 4:30...not bad.

We beat the dinner rush, and came at around 530pm on a weekday.  No line!  You pay first, then they bring you to your table.  The buffet itself is pretty extensive; there's just about any type of food you can think of, from different regions.  There was an asian section, complete with sushi, miso soup, etc, seafood, different types of meats, different types of soups... all that jazz.  
Of course my favorite part of the buffet (as usual) was the dessert section.  It was separate from the general buffet, in it's own section in the center of the restaurant.  Fabulous looking (and tasting) desserts that you can go right up and grab!  And, my favorite gelato section, of course.  Wouldn't I be saving a lot of money if there were just Gelato buffets I can go to and indulge.  (Are there any?  I know not where I'm from :() 
One star off because woah.  It is pretty pricey.  Have an empty stomach and a big appetite to really get your money's worth.  Overall good experience.

1st time visitor in this buffet. Some of the foods were exelent (ribs, tuna sashimi, deepfried shrimps from chinese kitchen) most were solid good and some dissapointements like salmon and oysters. All in all as an experience it was worth the money and most food were good or exelent.

This was our first time here. We tried the Rio buffet and that was major disappointment. Plus it reeked of cigarette casino smell.  

This place is amazing. Seafood was fresh and in abundance. No waiting. No cigarette smell!!!

Patty our server was also amazing. She attended to us and was very nice and always smiling. 

The cost was around $65 a person for 4 adults. 

I highly recommend this buffet. Ask for Patty and that will complete the experience to a high level.
If you ain't stalking the steamed crab legs. You ain't doin it right. Steak is good too!

Bacchanal Buffet is the ultimate buffet of all buffets.  It has been on my list of places to visit.  I wanted to eat here for dinner when I was in Vegas several months ago for my birthday, but the wait was over 2 hours.  And we had a show to catch, so ended up eating somewhere else at the time.

This time around, we came here during brunch-lunch hour.  The wait wasn't too bad at that time-like 20 minutes?  There's 2 lines: one line is for paying to get into the buffet, the second line is to get a table.  We were debating getting the Groupon, where you get the VIP breakfast experience for two, but decided not to get it.

They have so many different varieties of food.  I tried a little bit of everything: dim sum, prime rib, roasted duck, clams, sushi, creme brulee, flan, etc.  My favorite was the prime rib and there was this speciality dish of pork belly on top of squash and another similar one with short rib on top of mashed potatoes.  They also have fresh fruit juices-my favorite was the guava juice.  Their dessert selection was so good also! So many varieties!  

Overall, its a great place to eat.  I would come back to eat here again, but during dinnertime.

Food is almost similar to most Las Vegas buffet. Only seafood I went but is average taste. The price is not worth it since similar other buffet are cheaper. Most importantly, there's a 2-hour limit in the buffet which they won't tell you so keep that in mind. In addition, they ran out of popular item fast and majority there's a long line going it and a long line inside for popular food. You spend a lot of your time waiting in line.

Best way to enjoy the Bacchanal buffet is for breakfast which they do wonderfully, it was a Monday after weekend, no line and not overpriced like dinner. This is the what best way to get the best selection, there breakfast is amazing. I am also a big fan of dim sum and while Beijing noodle number nine is right next-door, this buffet selection is also very good. Loved being able to put century-old eggs in the congee I was eating.

On the western side five different types of salami all very expensive. Amazing gelatos like the raspberry hibiscus and also the Mojito. New favorite buffet on the strip:))

If you're in Vegas, chances are you'll probably hit up one of the many buffet options. Bacchanal buffet is definitely one of the most popular (not to mention expensive) options around. 

I visited with a large group during peak lunch time around 1pm and the line was longggg. Luckily, one of my friend's dad's was a seven star member and we were able to be seated in 20 minutes. I would definitely recommend visiting during off hours to avoid the long lines. 

Once we were seated, service was prompt and quick. During our first round of food, we could tell the buffet had a variety of options that can please everyone. The most notable selections were the made to order taco grill, king crab, and dessert bar. Sadly, the meat selections were disappointing. I tried the American wagyu and prime rib but both were dry and tasteless. The brisket however was tender and juicy. The king crab tasted fresh and had nice chunks of meat on each piece. 

The best part of the buffet was definitely the dessert bar. Each dessert is beautifully made and looked almost too pretty to eat. Keyword almost. Out of the full plate of desserts I got, my favorites were the creme brulee, chocolate cake, and gelato. Definitely do not skip out on the gelato!! I tried the pistachio and mango flavors and both were delicious. Light, creamy, and very flavorful. 

Overall, Bacchanal buffet is definitely an experience to try at least once. Although the meat selection was a let down, the desserts definitely made up for it.

We love the buffet at Caesar's Palace! My fiancé and I always are amazed at the spread of seafood and the crab legs are to die for! Plus, there's a good dinner Groupon during the week for it if you want to save some bucks!

In my opinion, Bacchanal Buffet is over rated. Let me tell you why. 1. We waited in line for almost an hour. By the time we were seated I was so hungry that when I finally started eating I was full in the first few bites. However, I didn't pay $60 not to try as much as I could, so challenge accepted! 2. There were tons of options!! The most I've ever seen at a buffet. But the food was mediocre. I rather have paid $60 per person for a nice dinner than an okay buffet. 3. For my seafood lovers - not many varieties of shrimp. The small crab legs on ice were unseasoned and bland (it was nice that they were split so cracking wasn't required). I give the seafood one star. 4. I think the best thing I had was made to order tacos making it the most expensive tacos ever. In summary, I was really looking forward to dining here but left feeling extremely disappointed and that I'd wasted money. There's my two cents! Bon appetit!

I've heard so much about this buffet over the years, everyone hyped it as one of the best buffets in town so when I got the opportunity to snag a Groupon while a friend was in town, I did it. 

My experiencing was underwhelming. The quality of the food was great, however I found that I didn't finish most of the things I tried. I've been to many buffets in Vegas and this one felt small. There were many things out to try, however it seemed like there were many "variations" on the same thing, like shrimp next to a differently prepared shrimp. Eggs, next to eggs different stuff in it. It felt limited considering the cost, the cost seems to be on quality ingredients, which is outstanding but I would have preferred more variety. 

I would discourage anyone from paying full price but I'm not disappointed that I paid $35 for the experience. The dining was clean, our server was incredibly friendly and the bathroom was close (silly, but as a parent I've been to many places where my daughter says "I have to go to the bathroom." And we're wandering aimlessly around the casino looking for a restroom) you don't even have to go into the casino to access it.

Although, the food was delicious and to use the word plentiful would be an understatement. The service was terrible. We, as a table may not have existed. We never got drinks served to us, our plates kept piling up and no one was there to take them away. We had asked one woman to help us and she said she be right back and never came. We have some other woman she helped us but never came back. It's unfortunate, because aside from the bad service the place is excellent. There are so many different stations of all kinds of different food. You have Japanese cousine, you have Italian, seafood, Mexican, and a huge dessert station. Definitely go hungry. I wasn't that hungry when I went and I ended up over eating because my eyes were bigger than my stomach. Like Las Vegas restaurants, the environment was awesome. I'm not sure if they make reservations but I know there was a long line. My fiancé and his family had gotten there half hour before me to wait in line. On a busy Friday or Saturday night you could be waiting for over an hour so definitely try to make a reservation or go early to avoid becoming Hangry.

Believe the hype! This place is awesome. I've been to many buffets and I can now say that this is one of my favorite places. Unfortunately, this place is a little more pricey. Bacchanal replaced their old buffet at Caesar's palace, which is a good thing because their old buffet was horrible.  For a party of 2 on a Friday night, we waited 20 minutes to pay for our meal and 15 minutes to get seated. Not too bad, at all! I was expecting longer wait times.  When you pay, you have the option to tip in advance....I don't recommend this. I tipped during payment, but I wish I had waited until the end because our server wasn't great. 

The food: there's too much to talk about so I'll just going to highlight a few things. The sliders are amazing! Just be careful because their plates are hot. The patty just melts in your mouth. I would also recommend their prime rib and sweet potato tots. My favorite of the night had to be there king crab legs. They offer both iced and hot, oddly they are at two different stations. I prefer the boiled crab legs. When I approached the station, I had a big grin on my face as the server lifted the lid and grabbed a bunch of steaming deliciousness for me. By the end of the night, I had about 3 plates full of just the crab legs. You'll also find fresh squeezed fruit juice, such as guava, pineapple, cantaloupe, etc. Although these sound good, I wasn't a big fan...they were tasteless to me. The dessert station is on the side and they have a bunch of great things. They had freshly made crepes, gelato, pastries, cakes, etc. Before arrive to Bacchanal, I browsed and found a things I wanted to try and I was a little disappointed that I didn't find some of those items...mainly the watermelon and feta cheese salad and their deep fried chicken wings. 

The service here was below par, which is something I didn't expect coming from a place that charged us $50 for dinner. First, at the meat station, I asked for some baby back ribs. The server grabbed two, but as he was transferring ribs to my plate, he accidentally hits the light lamp that was above the meat. I was thinking he'd get me a new piece of rib, but he proceeds to give me the same one which was contaminated with dust. Also, he looked as if he hated his job. Second, our server dropped by to get our drink orders. Period. That was all we saw of her the entire night. Other servers were there to take away our old plates, but no one filled up our drinks. 

I am giving this place 4 stars because I really enjoyed the food and the atmosphere. They could have gotten 5 stars if their service was better. Most people will come to Vegas and have the Buffet Buffet, but I'd recommend this as  a place to try. You will not be disappointed.

OMG I think I died and went to heaven! This was a memorable trip and it was all thanks to Bacchanal! There's is an insane variety of food here. I started from allllllll the way in the back and made my way toward the front! So much food to try, so little stomach space I can provide. If you can, definitely try a little bit of everything, but the money is in the seafood! Crab, oysters, crawfish etc! The prime rib was juicy as can be! There is also an amazing amount of desserts too!

This is the best Buffet in Las Vegas with very good food and deserts.
They also have international food too.  Service is the best where they serve you drink and take your plates most often.  The seafood is perfect for those who loves Lobster Claws and cocktail shrimps.  My kids love their desert with variety of nice decorated cupcake and macaroon.

Went there for my birthday and it was fantastic!!!!! Great food and service! Met the executive chef and she made my day by personally bringing me a dessert plate and even took a moment to take a picture with me for my birthday and it literally made my day!!!!

Great diversity of items. Super nice atmosphere.  Prices are higher but you have the high side of choices.  Food taste good. I'm not a buffet fan but had the items I choose at fine dine restaurants.  Desert bar was nice. Great selection also.

We were really looking forward to trying this buffet based on all the reviews. It did not live up to the hype. There was no king crab, no lamb chops. Snow crabs were okay but kind of strange very thin shells and with small amount of meat. We went early to avoid the crowds. Pho broth was flavorless. Short rib was tough. There is a huge selection. Service was not great had to ask for refills on our drinks. The desert section was impressive looking but only a few items were worth their calories.

Even at breakfast/lunch this buffet is amazing. But as you can see from the reviews this place is good and worth the visit. We were lucky and came on a weekday so it wasn't busy at all. Weekends can be a bit of a nightmare. Plan ahead if you're coming weekends or go during an off peak time. Worth the price tag and the wait. The variety is just so good.

This place was amazing! I'm from New Orleans, so I'm a food critic! They had everything and anything you could imagine. We ate here for brunch and I couldn't make it have way through the buffet with so many selections! Everything was so fresh and the place is so busy the food is prepared and served fresh! The omelette Chef was very friendly and so was the staff! I would love to come here again with a big group! Caesar's Buffet Rocks!

It is expensive (especially during the holidays), but it's worth your money especially if it's your first time! It was my first time here and I came here with high expectations since I'm paying $60 for brunch. I was overwhelmed by the variety of food they offered. My friend and I stayed there for 2 hours eating nonstop.  There was unlimited American wagyu beef and prime rib and it was amazing! We got there around 10:30am so we were able to get the breakfast and lunch food when they were changing the menu/food. We were obsessed about the lemon and basil sorbet. It was soooooo good. I wish they had fish when we were there, but I can't complain that we had unlimited wagyu beef and prime rib! I wish I had two stomachs because there were other things I wanted to try. It was a great experience and we left very satisfied. We ended up walking off the pounds of food we inhaled for the rest of the day.

I'll have to admit...I'm cheap, maybe because it's being Chinese and I rather spend my money at the tables or what but I'll admit. I'm that person that bought the buffet pass. Yes I spent $44.99 on a one day pass to Harrahs amusement of buffet. 

I really didn't know Caesars had a buffet, but whatever. So my friends and I waited in line for about 50 minutes to get in. We had our 24 hour pass there and as soon as we got up to the line...

"Oh you need to pay an extra $16.99 on top of your pass to enter here."

"What? Your kidding right? Nowhere it says that I have to pay more money."

"Sorry."

So essentally I got screwed on this deal. I wasn't going forget it. I already wasted 50 mins already in line so we all paid. 

So we got our table all the way in the back and waited for our server. We waited a good 10 minutes until he realized, "whoa...I have people!"

So they do have everything. What it really is another copy of Rio's Carnival Buffet except it's more fancy! 

The food was not bad. For the extra $17 I put in it better be decent. The meat was moist and the veggies were not bad at all. Didn't like the buffalo chicken wings, tasted like somebody dropped a bucket of vineger in there and just decided to serve it. 

Apparently service lacks, maybe when Caesar died, he decided to take all the nice servants back with him.

I think the Rio is still hands down better in the Harrah's family of amusement foods, but Caesars Palace does come a close 2nd.
I just went today for my birthday and I have to say everything was really good. The only thing is I was sad the bone marrow wasn't available at brunch.

Keep a lookout on Groupon for special prices.  This place is known for the seafood section. Service here is great and quality of food plates and variety of different foods.  One of my favorite buffets to come visit when in Vegas.  Be prepared to wait in line though, get's really crowded, but the lines move pretty quickly.  Don't get overwhelmed with the amount of food stations and food plates, you can do it.

For a city known for its buffets - I was mostly disappointed in the food in Vegas- until I came here. By far the BEST buffet I went to in Las Vegas. It seemed never ending with so many Options ..and the food was continuously rotated and kept fresh. (Seriously would find a new dish out that wasn't out the previous with each trip) ((btw. I almost never make multiple trips in a buffet as is.. so that's something right there) There were a couple dishes that were eh for me.. the  carved bacon was really fatty and the shrimp and grits was lacking. But overall the food was so good. They had an amazing carving station with 5 options (brisket was mmmmmm) and since I went for brunch, they had a really nice balance of breakfast and lunch options. Their dessert station was awesome and had me eating even though I was long past stuffed. The mimosas were a bit eh. Mostly juice.. but let's be honest- you aren't coming to this buffet for the mimosas anyway. Also really like that even though it was a very large space it wasn't too loud and very comfortable. If you only eat at one buffet in Vegas I suggest this be the one.
This is the best buffet I have been to. Lots of selection of freshly cooked foods, great variety. Dessert section was delish! I hope to come back soon :)

Oh where to start.  I checked in our group and it asked if we were celebrating anything special. We were celebrating 3 birthdays, so I marked that.  The wait time to get seated, we were told, was 17-22 minutes.  We were instructed to come back when the system texted my phone and wait "a few minutes" for our table to get ready.  When we came back we had to wait in an enormous line to pay and then an obnoxiously long line to get seated.  After 45 minutes waiting to get seated (total wait time of one hour and 23 minutes now), we were finally able to sit down.  This was extremely nerve racking because we had show tickets and were seriously worried we would not make the show.  While we were in line they repeatedly pulled people from behind us in line to get seated.  Once seated our server came over and took our drink order.  She came back with our drinks and was never seen again.  We pretipped $40 and I wish we hadn't left that.  
Now to the food: the crab legs were great.  Sushi was exceptional.  Mashed potatoes were phenomenal.  Macaroni and cheese was good.  Lamb was tasty.  Good choices for desserts.  However, there is such a thing as having too much.  There were so many choices that I almost felt cheated out of my money because there's no way someone my size could get their money's worth.  Which, by the way, is an astronomical amount.  $56 a person just to wait for almost an hour and a half for a table that we spent 30 minutes at?  No thank you.  
Overall: food is great.  Service is terrible.  And you're lucky if you ever get seated.  Will not return ever again.  Save your time and go to the Wynn for a fabulous buffet.

Still wish someone from Bacchanal had reached out to me about our horrible experience. I would be willing to give it another try. However waiting 2 hours for a table when you're quoted 45 minutes and then having a rude server is not something I desire. As a restaurant industry employee in still upset by this experience.

I was pretty disappointed in the whole experience, we've been to all higher end buffets over the years and this one was always too expensive in my eyes and pricewise above everyone else. The hype of course also let's you think this is the best of the best, which sets expectations very high. 

We finally decided to buckle down and try this one, even though I think $65 (not including taxes and tip) is way too much for any buffet, period.
