I was hoping though for the high end food and experince I expect in this price range and was not impressed at all. This compares to any lower priced buffets of $40 and under and others even surpass this one. The fact that that 50% of stations consist of cheap chinese take-out and mexican everything... WHAT? I can get all of that for less than half the cost in cheaper buffets and their options didn't look or taste refined and special either. The meats were chewy and didn't taste of high quality, my husband tried 3 different meats and didn't like any of it. I personally liked the lamb, but nothing stood out as being worth coming back again and again. 

The only thing that was good about the buffet were the limited seafood options and their dessert corner, which I agree was better than most. The macaroons were actually pretty good and some of the cakes really impressed me for being buffet dessert. 

The service was also pretty subpar, which I was surprised about as well, plus wait times are very long. Overall, I don't think this is worth the price they charge and I don't think we will be back.

We enjoyed our dinner at the Bacchanal. The freshly cooked crab legs were a hit (so tasty and not the usual frozen, overcooked tasting crap... I meant crab, that are available at most buffets).

There are so many selections available at this buffet. It should please most people if they aren't trying to eat their money's worth.

The desserts were pretty awesome. Colourful and overall, just appealing. My belly grew an inch after this meal.

Visited in Jan 2019. I literally only ate once that day. I got the 2hr buffet pass with mimosas. I ate for 2 hrs straight. There are like 3 different areas of food.  They do not disappoint with Breakfast, dinner, or dessert. Something for all taste buds. $40-60 depending on time of day and day of week. 

TIP: Go with a full appetite. Groupon has weekday deals.
Great variety and quality. Around 65$ for dinner. This is inside of caesars palace. Good variety of seafood.

Its like eating at EPCOT, food from around the world and although the selection was good, the food wasnt off the charts great - when lunch is $170 including tax + tip - it ought to be off-the-charts-good.

Noted 5-star items: mash potatoes, prime rib, creme brulee, mango mousse  and sushimi.

The staff was attentive: clearing plates and bringing drinks etc.

No snow crabs at lunch.

Time and money are definitely worth it here. Me and my bfs wait time was about a good 266 minutes and it's about 54 dollars each person excluding the tax. 


They have almost everything you can think of here. There's the seafood section, Italian, American, Mexican, Asian and dessert. I'm a small girl but I made sure I devoured the whole buffet making it worth 54 dollars. 

I can't even describe how good or what kind of foods they had. You just have to try it. 
And the only thing I can describe are the  desserts. Omg there were macaroons, cheesecake, mochi, gelato. Everything, I was in heaven. 

Someday when I'm back in Vegas I'll devour the this buffet again. Also they take a picture of you before you eat as a souvenir. Which was also pretty cool. Memories of how I gained 10 pounds that night.

I've always enjoyed this buffet. They have gone down in recent visits, no more lamb chops, just lamb itself, the crab legs are not the king crab legs from the past. All things I could live with, as there were lots of options. 

However, price, I would spend mid $35 for lunch, and price keeps going up. This last week, its now $44 for WEEKDAY LUNCH. I'm sorry that's crazy. Even Fogo du Ciao with all it's amazing meats, including lamb chops and full menu of great cuts of meat is $39. 

I probably would have come to it this time around, if the price was $39 which was listed on the website 2 weeks ago, it's up AGAIN. $40 is the ceiling, no lunch buffet is worth more. Absolutely not. 

PASS. This is just excessive greed.
Good place. I will be here again went I come back to las vegas. It the good buffet place for family

Wow! What a spread! There is no way you can try everything on the menu. It spans from sea food to mexican to asian to a range of desserts (I couldn't go past the crepes) to what not! The first thing that I tried was a small plate - Mexican style eggs I am sure most of you must have guessed which dish I am referring to. It was classic! Would love to go back
The crab legs were the best we've ever had!   Everything was good.    Went at 4:00 on a Tuesday.   No crowds!
All I can say is WOW. The food was delicious and the service was excellent. I would recommend this buffet to anyone that asked me on the street. I will most definitely be back!

There is nothing about this Buffet that's worth $47 for lunch. Food was cold, and wasn't stocked well. Tons of Chinese food options. But you can find those for $20 and a more desirable buffet elsewhere. Not impressed and wish I would have looked first!! Service was good. Food options weren't much.

Amazon food selections. Ton of seafood and and meat selection such as lamp, Waygu beef... I tried 5 other buffets at different resorts nothing compared to the Bacchanal Buffet. Make sure you plan to show up early. I was there at 3:30pm didn't get seated till 4:40 but it was well worth it.

Favorite buffet in Vegas. Ice cream, crepes, king crab... Need you ask for more? Love the stations that are culturally sensitive, LOVE the soups. Just wow. I get this every time I'm in town. Week days are cheaper but about $44 on the weekend.

Way Overpriced and Way Overrated!

$55.12 per person on a Sunday!
Yeah.. it's a big buffet, but so not worth it unless you are a BIG meat and/or seafood eater!! Then MAYBE.. if you are really really hungry.

I don't eat much seafood so I didn't even go to that area.
The crappy fried food was good and served in individual baskets.
The fresh made street tacos were average. 

The dessert station was horrible!!
Didn't like any of the desserts.
They sure look good but that's about it.
Worst dessert buffet ever!!

Service was horrible................. S L O W on everything!!
I would pass on this buffet!!

We bought the 24 hour buffet pass and decided to pay the surcharge and come try this place out because of all the great reviews. It's located in the Caesar toward the back, right by one of the pool entrances.  Boy were we right in that decision!!! This place is the BOMB! We got here late in breakfast and they transitioned to lunch and I couldn't believe they still could bring more different dishes out after looking at the spread when we got there.  They have everything imaginable including fresh squeezed juices including cucumber juice, carrot, tropical, watermelon, orange, food from every area of the world and seafood galore and a dessert bar to die for that included about 20 flavors of gelato. I think we stayed over 2 hours just relaxing, talking, eating and digesting. We had originally planned on going across the street to one of the other buffets just for the included mimosas to get that morning buzz started but we were so full when we left we had no need or room for fuzzy bubbles! we were high on the fabulous quality food that this place puts out.  Highly recommend coming here for a minimum of one meal while in town or more if you are staying nearby!

The buffet was absolutely amazing. I wish I hadn't eaten for a week prior so I could've enjoyed more things! I shared/took little bites of everything and there were still more items I couldn't try. The king crab legs are the best buffet crab legs I've ever had. We enjoyed a delicious dinner with a part of 20 to celebrate a friend's 50th birthday! Definitely call ahead to prepay and reserve a table if you have a big group. The line can sometimes be hours long! Bon Appetit!

There's so much hype around this buffet. So, my friends and I went to try it out for dinner. It's expensive at about $70 per person. Granted, they had a lot of variety. But, not all their items were good or freshly prepared. I have to say that I'm not a huge seafood fan, and I didn't take advantage of their crab legs. So, you may want to try these out if you come here. 

For their meat section, the item I enjoyed the most was definitely their prime rib. While it wasn't the best prime rib I've tasted, it was above average here. It was cooked medium rare to medium, and it was nice and beefy. However, their wagyu beef was overcooked and quite dry. The spicy sausage was freaking awesome, and had quite a kick. Their bone marrow and brisket mashed potatoes were nothing special. I did try their lamb chops with quinoa, and this was pretty good. The lamb wasn't overcooked and had a nice flavor to it. It complemented the quinoa nicely. Aside from the meat, I liked that there were grilled veggies available to break up the heaviness of it all. 

I went to their Italian food section and grabbed their mushroom ravioli. Sooo good! It had a beautiful mushroom pate filling and a nice texture to its ravioli shell. I went back to grab more of their ravioli, prime rib, and spicy sausage. 

I did try a couple of their seafood items. Their halibut was overcooked and bland, and their lobster bisque wasn't a wow in terms of flavor. Not pictured here was their clam chowder, which was surprisingly good. It was on the watery side, though. 

Last, but not least, with the little room I had left, I got some dessert. I really liked their coffee mousse and mint chocolate gelato. Both had fantastic flavor. The coffee mouse was particularly a standout. It tasted like Vietnamese coffee in mousse form. Their banana pudding was not too shabby. It was dense, though. The best banana pudding I've had would still be at Terry Blacks in Austin. 

Overall, it's pretty pricey for the quality that you get. I would say to take advantage of eating the prime rib and crab legs to really get the most out of the buffet. Have an empty stomach before you come here, and have a second stomach ready for their desserts. Enjoy.

I went here almost 5 years ago when it first opened. It was a really good experience and I love the options you get. The food is really good. I came back last month and again, the food was amazing. However, after 3 hours, I experienced the worst food poisoning of my life. Not just me, but also my brother and sister. Looking at other reviews, it seems to be an ongoing issue at this place and that is very concerning. It's such a disappointing because I do enjoy going here, just don't want to pay for the aftermath.

As a local, this is my favorite buffet in town- whenever i have guests, highly recommend to go place- different kinds of deserts for kids- modern design environments, warm-welcoming staff. I loved the bottomless mimosa tho-

Come early! There's always a line in this buffet because this is truly the best buffet in las vegas. I've tried a bunch and they weren't even on the same level as Bacchanal. So many food choices and amazing desserts!

Don't even get me started with desserts. Thai tea float. Not many people know that they have thai tea float and it is literally the best thing that they could make in terms of milk tea/sugary drinks. 

10/10
literally the best buffet that i have ever had. the lamb chops were so freaking amazing!!!!!!

I decided to come to Vegas for a short trip with my father and splurge a little by eating at a nice buffet while in town.  We were super excited to eat here after reading some of the reviews and looking at pictures.  We went around 5pm on a Monday night, no reservations.  We had to wait in line a little but not bad, maybe 10-15 mins.  Between the both of us we tried various items, all were good but I don't think it was worth the price.  The prime rib was dry and the lamb was really tough.  I've never had wagyu beed until this buffet but I thought it was good.  It was juicy and tasteful.  We decided to go for the hot crab legs that were in the Italian section.  They were nice and hot and had a good taste, however we weren't able to find the crackers so we just had to use our muscles to crack them open.  I tried the Jonas crab (again cracking with my hands) and I thought they were just okay.  The dessert bar was my favorite! The gelato was really good and you were able to pick your flavors and could go back to get as much as you wanted.  All in all the buffet is good, our waitress was friendly and we left with a full belly but I definitely don't think it's worth the price.  In my opinion, the buffet a Bellagio is actually better.  I'm happy we tried it just to get a bit of the Vegas experience.

Okay.. This was pretty pricey.. Just about 60 bucks! Howeverrrrr... We thought.. What the hell.. It's Vegas... And it sure was worth it!!!! They had American food (including soul food), Mexican, Asian, pre cracked crab legs, oysters... Everything! Lol. I only wish my stomach was bigger!

After hearing so many rave reviews about how great this buffet was, my group had to give it a try and it surely did not disappoint. The Bacchanal houses one of the best selections when it comes to buffets in Las Vegas.

Coming here for dinner, you definitely get both quality and quantity food here. Highlights were the taco stand, seafood area, and carving station. My personal favorites were the truffle mushroom pizza and crawfish! Amazing. 

Lines are expected to be long, but we arrived on a Sunday at around 3 and waited no longer than 20 minutes for a party of 6 to be seated. 

Overall, my experience was amazing and every craving was satisfied. When in Vegas, come eat here!

Amazing buffet! Normally when I think of buffets, I think of cheaper, lower-quality food. This buffet proved me wrong with its vast selection of cuisines and food options. The most impressive section is the seafood section - the crab legs were so fresh and delicious that I kept going back for more! For those willing to pay a little extra, they offer a VIP Seafood Tower, but given the quantity of seafood already at the regular stations, you definitely don't need to pay the extra money. The tacos and meats were delicious as well. Of course, some of the food options are hit-or-miss, but given the sheer size of the buffet, there's always going to be something good for everyone! The waits are usually long, but if you go for a weekday lunch, you'll get seated pretty quickly.

This buffet is located in Caesars Palace hotel, which is a lovely hotel with beautiful artwork that truly immerses you in the world of Roman history. Definitely walk through the hotel before your meal or on your way out!

The wait wasn't too bad on a Friday evening. The food was great. I got caught up in the cold seafood section and didn't realize what I really wanted were the crab legs next to the pizzas. So good! Save room for dessert. Skip the cupcake though.

I'd say probably the best buffet in Vegas as of the time I'm posting my review. Been to Bacchanal's a few time and it is good. You'll spend a pretty penny for a buffet dinner ($56-60) but it's worth it. 

Amenities are new, there's a lot of space, the buffet selections are plentiful and the service is good. Be mindful that Bacc's does get super busy and the wait times to just be seated might be a long time. 

Food: they have tons of meat and tons of seafood. Mind you, no lobster. Two kinds of crabs, FRESH raw oysters, Asian inspired, Italian, Mexican, etc. I love their desserts, good tasty and pretty fresh as well. 

I always feel like crap after a buffet because it's 2-hours of pure food coma bliss. Love it!

I purchased the Buffet of Buffet package and went to use my package for the morning fare. When I arrived they informed me that I had to pay a brunch fee even though I arrived at during the morning fare time.  Their website site states they have 3 dining  time: morning fare, brunch, and dinner.  On the documents they give you, it says there's an up charge for brunch and dinner. 

The manager on staff proceeds to tell me that we have to pay because they put crab legs out on the buffet this morning. And I explain I here at 9 in the morning for morning fare not the 11am brunch as sited on the website and the form they attached to the receipt. Then she explains we consider our buffet premium, we only do brunch and dinner. But the websites says differently. 

Completely unacceptable! You can't advertise one thing then try to charge people something separate. Poor service! 

Just gonna say co

My girls took me here for brunch during my bachelorette weekend. This place has a wide selection (apparently 500 different food items). There was a line for their meat carving station but it's worth the wait. Even though I try to keep in my mind that buffet food is never going to be the absolute best, Bacchanal is actually pretty damn good. 

The interior of the buffet was designed with various textures of wood, metal and glass. It is so modern and clean that it didn't really look like it belonged in Ceasar's Palace but that it would rather fit better in one of the newer casinos like Aria or Cosmo. But it still works out well since the buffet is located in a little area, tucked away to the side of the building. In my opinion, the dining ambiance here is better than any of the other buffets (Bellagio, Wicked Spoon, Wynn etc..) I've been to in Vegas. 

It's a bit pricey ($42 per person for brunch on the weekend) but I think we drank enough bottomless mimosas to make up for it.

This was my second visit to Bacchanal! The first was 25 year ago, then it was amazing and mesmerizing. It was my first BIG VEGAS Dining experience. I remember that long walk back to that corner and those steps that are now gone, boy that was a fun night! I ate so well and drank wine, service was so good and kind, I felt special, and have always loved Caesars Palace since!

Today I had lunch at the new Bacchanal, I have had it on my short list for some time and although dinner wasn't in the cards this trip lunch today worked out just fine.

Lets start with me breaking the cardinal rule of no pasta, but I couldn't help myself because I had some BBQ in front of me. both were missteps. The BBQ sauce was off and the meat was too smoky. It was tender and generous, and the mac was grainy and overcooked but still an awesome effort from any buffet. 

The salad bar had been devastated and almost all of the veggies gone and not replenished but I had some arugula, field greens and Maytag Bleu Cheese from the next station, and red wine vinegar, it was stellar.
 
Other stand out Items included Chinese BBQ pork, California Roll, although the F&B manager would be proud of the amount of rice used (lots). I enjoyed the Shrimp and crab but not the lobster corn chowder from the seafood station. The Deserts are very cool and all bases are covered. The Peanut butter and chocolate pop was my favorite, but the Oreo mousse was also delish!
 
I had 6 small plates including desert all were good or better, service was efficient and friendly, what more can you ask for. As far as value it was fine, I knew the price and never felt cheated.

Will I return, you bet, only for dinner! and we shall have wine and celebrate the abundance of food before us!!! I actually cant wait.

Stopped in for brunch time buffet with the family on the last day of our vacation in Las Vegas. It's inside the Caesar's Palace Casino so it looks really nice with amazing decorations. The buffet has a variety of different foods and are made really well. My favorite was the Mexican section because they did a really great job with traditional dishes that were there. The buffet is not cheap as I would have paid $84 for me and my wife if it weren't for the Tix4Tonight dining card.

I highly recommend this buffet as it tops any other buffet I've been to in Las Vegas so far.

5 Stars - especially considering we're talking about a buffet and I can't rave enough about that wonderful slab bacon! 

----------

When you're in Vegas, you can't not stop by one of their lavish buffets. Voted Best Vegas Buffet since it's opening in 2012, Bacchanal Buffet in Caesars Palace is a showstopper indeed. So after a wonderful morning at the pool, we decided to stop by for a late afternoon lunch. It's $57 for dinner and $37 for lunch, though a dollar gets knocked off with your Total Rewards card. If you're in a drinking mood, bottomless mimosas are available for $22. Beware the lines at certain hours, though if you purchase the Caviar and Champagne package for $150+, immediate seating is yours!

There's plenty of house-baked bread, stellar cheeses, and fresh Jonah crab claws (lobster and king crab for dinner service!). The sushi rice was a bit mushy, but the fish was undeniably fresh, especially for a buffet. 

I appreciated that the large majority of dishes were either served to order or were portioned for individual servings, which elevated the experience. Chicken and waffle fries cone in a waffle cone? Don't mind if I do. Creamy sharp cheddar mac and cheese, sweet potato gnocchi, crispy sweet potato tots, and moist meatballs were also on offer.

You know I posted up right by the butcher though. The slab bacon? Amazingly juicy and unctuous. I must have gotten an entire pig's worth. While the mammoth beef rib was unfortunately dry, the prime rib was juicy and tender. The char siu pork was on point and the Chef's special of pork belly on parsnip mash? Sign me up!

The GF was in heaven with the dessert bar. Plenty of sweets including cream puffs, flavored marshmallows, creme brulee, macarons, and a bevy of gelato and ice cream. I went with the straciatella gelato - delicious. 

So if you're in Vegas and are aching for a well-executed and somewhat elevated buffet experience, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend the Bacchanal Buffet. I know I'll be making at least one trip every time I'm back!

This is hands downnn the best & most worth-it buffet in vegas. EASILY. The don't have try to stuff you with carbs and other filler foods. 

They have oysters, crab legs x3!!! THREE stations for crab (hot and cold) 

They also have good dim sum surprisingly, korean bbq ribs (bomb), tuffle & mushroom pizza, crazy stuff you'll never see at any of the other buffets. 

BUT, of course the wait around 7 pm on a Saturday was an hour long and it cost $140 for two people LOL 

So def eat lots to get your money's worth!!

This is definitely the best buffet in town! They have such a large selection and everything is so fresh. I think we went around 3 or 4 pm so it was $60 a person and totally worth it. My favorite was the hot crab legs and there's also hot melted butter straight from a spout. I think my hubby's favorite was the pork belly.

Read a lot about Bacchanal and was excited to get brunch here. It was a great value for big eaters, a group which seems to include many visitors to Las Vegas.

Just walking to the end of the buffet stations is a workout in and of itself. I was satisfied with everything I sampled. The standout was, without a doubt, the Wagyu Steamship. Just watching that thing get sliced brought a smile to my face, and it was some of the most tender meat I've ever tasted.

If you are one of those crazy crab leg people, though I don't know what really makes you tick, you may be disappointed.

Like any other buffet, you go mainly for the quantity and not quality (but if it's great quality that's a huge win). The decor is really nice and they have a large seating area. Not too bad of a wait (10am on a Sunday, during non-touristy season though). So many great food choices to make your head spin. We came in as the breakfast choices were switching out to lunch so we got lucky to check out all the options. I loved the presentation of the food (kudos to that) but I can't say I was impressed with the flavor of any one food item. Everything was just ok...sure it wasn't cheap but I pretty much expect that and you do also get to eat all the crab legs and shrimp you want (I skipped it but it's a deal if you're coming to load up on that). The one item that defintely stood out to me was the lime basil sorbet - that was amazing. Our server was very sweet and kept checking on us. I wouldn't come back and spend that much for average tasting food but if you're curious to check it out, you definitely should (for me it's more like, been there, glad I did it, but don't need to do it again).

There are a thousand reviews already for the Cesar's Buffett. What can you say, but amazing!
If you have house money don't look anywhere else. If you don't, it's expensive. Ultimately, it's Las Vegas and you gotta go big or go home. This Buffett is crazy. It goes on and on and on. Most people go for the seafood, but even the pizza looks great! Save room for desert or you'll regret it as you force it down.

I've heard so much good stuffs about this place. I definitely can say this place has more outstanding higher quality dishes. I was little disappointed by the desserts here though. I loved their little sides like truffle egg benedict, mac n cheese and more. But I honestly didn't like any of those desserts there.

The food was good. We purchased the 24 hour wrist band. We paid an extra $30 per person to eat here. Later we ate at the Paris buffet. It was just as good, but there was not an additional up charge. Lines were in comparison to a lines at an amusement park.

Everything was good. "Best buffet in Vegas" is well earned. There only complaint I have is the raw oysters had too much sand and shell pieces. Some had so much sand that I had to spit it back out. If it wasn't for that, those raw oysters would've been the best I've ever had. So juicy and flavorful.
Really good buffet. Excellent service. I'd honestly say it's the best buffet in Vegas

The Wicked Spoon was my favorite but now it's Bacchanal! 

My husband, along with our two daughters dined here for lunch on my youngest daughter's Sweet 16 on May 19th. 

The wait was a little long...about 20 minutes and I was getting agitated that whenever the Elite folks walked up, they were seated ahead of us. But in the end, it was definitely worth the wait.

Everything was fresh. There was so much to choose from which made it really difficult to decide what to eat. I made sure I chewed slowly and sampled small portions of just about everything. Everyone at my table was stuffed but I was still nibbling on yumminess I shall never forget. 

It is pricey though, so we'll save this spot for very special occasions. $177 and change is nothing to play with so bring your fat wallet, be ready to tip your very capable waiter or waitress and get your grub on!

I really need to get that Diamond Elite status card. Can someone hook me up!

Visited Bacchanal Buffet July 2nd 2019.  Heard so many good things about it including fro Youtuber "Simply Dumpling".  The conclusion is this place is way overrated.  I paid $54.99/person.  Went with my daughter and sister-in-law.  All 3 of us felt there is nothing special about the buffer. Overpriced for the standard of quality.  Does not have King crab, only snow crab is available.  Service is slow and replenish is slow.  Dessert selection is limited and his average.  The only highlight was a the crepes.  As for entrees, beef is over cooked and very chewy.  Raw oysters are fresh. The best dish is the Bone Marrow - that's the only high light at the venue. Waiting line is long.  

Conclusion - this place is no better than any other Casino Buffet.  Overrated and pricey.  You can definitely enjoy a better dinner elsewhere that specializes in serving steaks.

I came here for sooooo many times, but two days ago I brought my fiance who came from outside of the country to visit me; I took him to Las Vegas! I told him that Caesar's buffet is the best! so I took him but two days ago, the service was the worst that I had ever have in my life. My fiance didnt enjoy the meal at all.

We came in and the usual, ask if anything to drink, we ordered. After our first round of the plate and my fiance finished his drink, we were waiting if someone would help us to take the plates, but none and already our second round of our plate already. We were waiting probably like 20 minutes for customer service. There is one waitress that saw us but just felt like didnt want to help us out. This pissed us off.

So, I had to go to the hostess to tell that we dont have anyone to serve us out. Now, they called the person to help us out. We ordered and it just put the drink and turned right away without a smile. WTF?! 

The worst thing is that I asked for the coffee and the half and half was dirty! That really became double pissed to us. We had to call manager! and the manager seems like didnt really care. 

Is not what I said but I was looking at the reviews, this buffet seems to discriminate Asian a LOT!!! so if you are Asian, just be careful. and I just waste my money over this "best" restaurant.

Got in right before brunch started today, so we got the breakfast price. Waiting in the 1-2 person line less than 5 minutes. Seated in the furthest corner near the Asian station. Also got a free mimosa for checking in on Yelp. 

They had a variety of things, but nothing that really appealed to me. Brunch had more lunch/dinner type items, severly lacking on breakfast items. Everything I picked was either cold or had this odd sweet flavor that didn't work. Turkey breast, mac and cheese, a piece of bacon, mash potatoes, and a roll. Cold, bland, and didn't eat much. 

Went back up for a berry yogurt with granola. Only thing I enjoyed.

I don't get how this is considered the best buffet on the strip. I'm staying at the Excalibur and actually enjoyed their buffet better. 

Not worth the hype. Overpriced as well.

Rather disappointed...I had heard great things about the Buffet and was so excited to try it! We waited in line for about 30 min and it wasn't even that long of a line. There were no king crab legs or oysters which was basically the whole reason I wanted to go--major bummer.... the prime rib was very bland and extremely undercooked in the middle (and that's coming from someone who likes it rare). The lamb was super gamey and the shrimp was a bit fishy. I thought the best thing I had was the pizza and a couple of the desserts. The staff was super nice and the service was good but that was the about the only positive thing about our experience. Spend your money elsewhere in my opinion. You can get a way better dinner in Vegas for two for $140.

We was expecting more from this buffet since it has 4 stars review. Was told they will serve king crap and get some when we pay but we were disappointed because we did not get any king crabs. Aside from that, the snow crabs were bland and tasteless. The Italian ice cream was full of artificial ingredients ( not natural fruit flavors). Moreover, we got a mango tapioca with  mongo toppings which tasted sour ( we believe it's gone bad), And the miso soup, was so salty and tasted weird. The mini green cake was mushy. Overall, it's not worth the money you paid for a high end buffet.

Honestly, not sure what all the fuss is about. Wife and I tried it and we were certainly wowed by the selections - and we were very careful to pace ourselves and try probably close to 100 different things - but very little stood out. It was a giant cavalcade of "meh".

Quite honestly, the best thing there was the desert selections; those were excellent, but of the hundreds of different dinner selections, I honestly couldn't pick one thing that stood out and made me go "wow".

I recommend you save your money and get a nice dinner elsewhere, not like there's any other great spots in Vegas.

The food was very good, but the highlight of our visit was our server, Julie.  She was SO helpful in picking out items that we would enjoy, and we most certainly did.  She was friendly, clearly enjoyed her job, and my coffee stayed full.  Go see her and eat yourself sick like we did.

Tons of choices, so many food, so spacious, one of the best buffet place in Vegas and also a must try place if you want to do a buffet, they have all kinds of food, and very high quality, excellent service, highly recommend
Awesome food with nice service! I will definitely visit again. Strongly recommend! Variety of menu from salads to seafood. Their drink menu is really good.

So they say u can kiosk, so I did at 3:30 pm. It said see hostess at podium at 4:58..Sounds like ur gping to get in...NOT..I reported to podium, and they redirected me to another podium..Then they said u got to wait in line, whuch was 45 min..Then why do they have a kiosk?..Oh u can by pass for an additional 35 a person on top of the 70 for dinner...Is it really worth 105 dollars a person for a buffet that probably has the same food as every other buffet...The Managet ciuldnt give me an answer to the reason of a Kiosk when u have to wait anyway...I would consider Bacchanal an epic failure, unless of course one is going just to say they ate there.

What I liked:
-Large selection of different types of cuisines- something for everyone
-LOVED all the seafood...especially the crawfish, king crab legs and oysters! They also had a great selection of other seafood dishes like ceviches and cod fish
-Great dessert selection...macarons!!! Loved the unique gelato flavours...small twists on classic flavours such as green tea mint...also loved the dipped strawberries...loved the green dip with pink beads...tasted like Pocky

What I didnt like:
-HUGE line up (thankfully we bypassed the line by being with a Seven Stars member)
-Wait staff a little slow
-Loved that they had Singaporean style crab but the crab meat itself didnt taste too fresh/good

One watery, bland oyster literally sent me to the ER. The person I was with did not eat any, so it's safe to assume that is the culprit. I love seafood, but tragically could not identify a bad oyster until it was too late and I was vomiting and dry-heaving over 20 times before and during my overnight stay at the hospital, where I was also immobilized by repeated and sharp stomach contractions. If you are considering eating here, I would say to heed the warnings of the other reviews, which actually consistently comment on the sorry state of the oysters.

As for the other food, the selections are diverse, but the quality is underwhelming. The sushi was sad, misshapen, and drained of color. The meat tended to be plain and dry. Even the braised pork, a dish where there is typically a nice strip of fat along the meat, lacked flavor and tenderness. The only great thing besides the novelty of seeing such a variety of dishes was the desserts.

Overall, I feel the buffet was worth it years ago before they jacked the price way up, all while letting the quality slide. If you're going to pay a ludicrous ~$70 per person, you shouldn't do it for mediocre food and poorly maintained seafood. Food poisoning happens, but for it to send a person to the hospital is a bit concerning. I personally think you'd be much better off eating at one of the literal hundreds of other exciting places nearby, rather than being gouged for disappointment and a vacation cut short by illness.

Don't listen to the hype for this buffet. It's clearly not the same anymore.

+1 star for killer desserts, but minus the rest for murderous seafood.

Went on a Saturday around 2:30 and paid the weekend brunch price. Stood in line for about 20 minutes before we were seated.
The good:
Street tacos, posole, crab claws, Some of the Chinese food 
Just ok: steamed crab (most didn't have much meat), corn, desserts, salads. 
Not worth it: all the meats - dry, bland and over cooked. 

Probably our last visit. Definitely not as good as it was a few years ago. Skip it.

My son, daughter, and myself went to the buffet for dinner on June 3rd. It was such a disappointment. The selection was amazing. Too bad EVERYTHING we ate was ice cold( including the clam chowder) . Cold soup is very bad.. Definitely not worth the price. My son lives in Las Vegas I highly doubt he'll be bringing any future visitor.

Known as one of the best buffets in Vegas, it definitely lived up to it. When you think of buffets, you think of quantity over quality, but this place had both. It is super crowded and may take some time to get in, but it is worth it in my opinion. The staff are very professional and take care of you even through the night. The cooks at the line will make delicious food right in front of you. 

When I got to the counter to grab my dinner, I was overwhelmed because I did not know where to start. So I went to one end and walked down the aisle. I filled two plates and only got half way! There is so much selection! One positive surprise I had was Asian food. It was done really well. Some highlights were the honey walnut shrimp and roast duck! If you like seafood, they have plenty of crab options. There will be a section that does boiled crab. That was not my favorite. I think they boiled it in salt water so it was too salty because crab meat is already salty from the sea. The best crab is at the end of the line on ice. 

If you like dessert, this place is for you! They have such a great selection of desserts. My favorite was the gelato and mango cake. Wow it was so good! Definitely will be coming back!

What a great buffet to come and enjoy a big feast! I walked here with my husband from the Venetian which took about 15-20 minutes and luckily for us we got there around 6pm and was seated right away. 

The dinner buffet included with  tax is about 75 dollars per person and it's all you can eat. They serve high quality food that look and taste amazing. Our waiter was sweet and always refilled our drink without having to be asked and continued to take away our plates once we were done. 

All their foods were categorized in cultural foods which began with Asian foods, Italian, Mexican, American, meats, Cajun style foods, raw seafood, and dessert. My husband and I decided to try basically everything in that order by making more than 6 trips in our visit.  

Never have we ate so much food in one sitting but I'm glad we were  able to try a ton of different options here at this buffet because I figured when will we ever have a big feast. Our top favorite foods were the bbq ribs, tacos, Jamablaya, lamb Greek style burger, Asian style shrimp, Caesar salad, and many more. 

The dessert section was heavenly and I couldn't decide what I wanted to try first. My top favorites was the banana cream pudding, chocolate lava cake, the Nutella crepe. My husband loved the Nutella crepe which they make fresh in front of you and add any kind of topping of your choice. I'm glad we stopped by here for dinner because it was worth the walk, the money, and time!

We're done with this buffet. Something about it has changed. Plus it has gotten LESS vegetarian. Believe it or not they no longer even offer a leafy salad only section!  Luckily we booked a 2 nite deal at Ceasers  that included a $75 food credit.  So we won't be back.
Excellent buffet. Excellent service. Fairly reasonably priced. My only complaint is If they can get lobster on a more regular basis, this place would be completely awesome!

Came here for my 21st birthday while I was in Vegas. It can be pricey, but let me tell you it was WORTH IT!!! We came for dinner, but we had an early dinner. Around 4:30 or 5:00pm I think we came, right when they just opened for their dinner time. There wasn't really a line when we got there, considering they just opened for dinner. Upon entering after we paid, there was a gentleman to take our photo for us. Which later on, he came around to our table while we were eating and offered us to buy the photo for $20.

The food was AMAZING. Soooo many choices!!! All different types of food from different countries. Seafood was probably my all time favourite here, especially the king crab legs!!! I believe they even had wagyu steak. They also have a selection of different types of sushi/sashimi. The amount of choices for food here is ENDLESS! Their dessert table was to die for as well. Soo many different types of desserts, you can even make your own crepe! Different cupcakes, macarons & ice cream flavours.

With that being said... Being in Vegas, coming to Caesar's Palace to Bacchanal Buffet is a MUST!!!
Worst experience ever.  service was terrible. The lobster was raw.  Steak was burnt.  I had party of 13, family from around the world.  Embarrassed

Unreal!!! Excellent quality food as far as you can see...Crab,oyster,shrimp,prime rib, ham, turkey,sushi blah, blah -it never ends and it's all wonderful. The room is so beautiful and the servers are good. However $17 for a small glass of wine was ridiculous.
Great food. Worth the hour wait. Definitely something to splurge on and not do every day with prices being $55 a piece at dinner time for adults. But a great experience!!

This was a very good Buffet. I live in Las Vegas and I've tried many this one truly is at the top the amount of shellfish and seafood available is crazy. The service was very good and their dessert bar is unbelievable I was too full to eat dessert but ended up coming back with seven different things and pay them all

Such an amazing assortment of foods. My husband and I had just started Keto and were worried there wouldn't be a ton of selection. Much to our dismay we had TONS of things to choose from. We went during breakfast time and can't wait to go back and try it for lunch. We left happy and full!
The best buffet in Las Vegas the food is so fresh the seafood is so so good in Emma she explains everything we recommended
Food here NEVER disappoints. Our server was an angel and she was very attentive. We make it a point to come every singe time we're in town

I must say, this time around was way better than the first time I came in April 2013. Its $50/person on a weekday dinner.  Thank goodness we didn't have to wait in line too long!

MY FAVORITES:
-the raw oysters: juicy and flavorful! I expected them to taste plain but they had their distinct oyster taste. The bad part about it is that they always run out, so you have to wait until they shuck more oysters and there's always a line.
-snow crab legs: always good and taste even better with the hot butter. Most people miss the butter because they didn't know it is in what appears to be a glass beverage jug. A girl even asked me, "What is that?" Clearly, it is hot, melted butter!
-clams, mussels, scallops: the clams were cooked in a really creamy sauce and it was delicious. The mussels were simmered in white wine and tomatoes, but the meat was a bit small. The scallops were still in their shells with spinach, sauce, and bread crumbs (reminded me of an Oyster Rockefeller).
-fresh juices: near the Mexican station they have jars full of different juices. The guava and Jamaican tea were good! 
-desserts:  the mango gelato was my favorite! The lava cake was moist too.

They have a very long buffet- seafood, American, soups, Mexican, Italian, Greek, Japanese, Thai, Chinese, desserts. The prime rib was dry and the soups were okay. I'm a soup fan but the chicken noodle soup and the tomato bisque were mediocre. They have a ramen, pho, and udon station too! Three different noodles, three different broths. The ramen noodles were too undercooked and had that flour taste. The pho was better but the broth was super salty. My BF said the sushi was good though. I was amazed at the Chinese station because they had porridge with lots of condiments and ginseng soup! The desserts were so-so. I took a bite of everything and just left it. 

Overall, it was okay. I didn't think it was worth $50/person. The only station worth eating here is the seafood station. Our neighboring tables expected the food to taste better too! One table even asked to speak to the manager and head chef to complain about quality and taste...

I usually stay clear of Asian buffet stations, since most places serve Panda Express style garbage. But to my surprise, Bacchanal's dishes are as real as they can get. No Orange Chicken or Chop Suey here. Instead, you'll find a great selection of dim sum, fresh sashimi, and even made-to-order noodles. Never in a million years, did I think I'd be enjoying congee and pho out in the middle of the desert. 

Buffets are a dime a dozen in Vegas, but what sets Bacchanal apart is the attention to detail they place on every dish. Nothing is prepared half assed.

agree with everyone else regarding their tips: go on a weekday at 2:30pm or so to get dinner food for brunch prices, stay away from the seafood on ice and get the steamed/boiled crab in the back when it comes out (I only found this out after I was at 95% capacity sadface).

Still, for around $45 with taxes per person, Bacchanal buffet lives up to the price tag, especially considering some of the things they are serving: mussels, oysters, shrimp, sushi/nigiris, a wide range of rich and decadent soups, juices, a crepe bar, etc. For even a little asian girl like me, the sizes of the dishes to sample weren't too large and I feel like I was able to try (not finish!) some from almost every station. 

Definitely come on a weekday for less wait times and avoid convention season if you can (unless you're going to LV for that specifically lol), and bring at least one person with you, so you waste less food! Not sure if its good or bad that they don't charge you extra for not finishing your plate.

This place is seriously AMAZING. I've never tried a buffet in Vegas because I just don't like buffet style eating. Well, I do, but I just have no self control so I never go :P I really, REALLY wanted to try unlimited crab legs so I begged my boyfie for a few weeks straight to come here and he FINALLY caved over the weekend #winning. We came around 1:30pm on Saturday and the line was RIDICULOUS. Fortunately, we were able to go through a special line so our wait was less than 5 mins. 

The variety of food here is just AMAZING. They have EVERYTHING. I'm not going to lie, I only had crab legs, pho soup, and creme brûlée, but I really did want to try everything else. It's ok though because I definitely ate my monies worth in crab legs (seriously like 7 plates worth between the 2 of us)... they have chilled crabs in the seafood section, but also serve steamed crab legs in the Italian section. I'd recommend trying both because they were both so delicious. Oysters didn't come out until after 3 or 4 (yes, we were there for that long LOL).

It's a bit pricy, but for the quality of food you get it's TOTALLY worth it. I came wait to be back in Vegas to eat this again :)

I love this buffet
I was very fortunate that there was a deal on Groupon. It got us two VIP passes, free mimosas, and saved us some $$
A great amount of options when it comes to meal choices 
Their dessert options are endless as well  (see photo)
They have gelato and someone making crepes in the spot. I would definitely come back again!!!

Bacchanal Buffet is the craziest buffet I've ever been to, the food selection is HUGE, however the quality of the food is either a hit or miss--some things are amazing and others are not-so-great. Just an overview of the food options available starting from the entrance (subject to changes, obviously): raw seafood (crab legs, shrimp, mussels), some random cooked seafood dishes (cod, crab cake benedicts, etc), breads and carbs, salad, meats (tri-trip, sirloin, ham, ribs, etc), pizzas (these are actually really good, esp the truffle mushroom one), Asian dishes (noodles, fried rice, eggplant with spicy pork), sushi, other Asian dishes (dim sum, spring rolls, etc), and of course, the desserts (all kinds of cakes, ice cream bar, crepe bar, macarons, vegan desserts, Asian cookies and desserts). There are definitely a lot more options than what I just listed; the list was just what I could remember on the top of my head. 

My favorites/must try items: crab legs (don't forget the butter--it's in that little spinny machine right next to all the raw seafood with the tiny metal cups), meats especially the tri-trip and sirloin, pizza, Asian noodles and the meat dishes (e.g. char siu), ice cream from the ice cream bar ON TOP of the crepe :D

My friends (5 tiny Asian girls with a large appetite, yep) and I literally sat here for 4 hours (there's a 2 hour maximum time limit but no one really cared about us) and ate 7 rounds of food. WIN!

Pricey, yes! But I think it's worth the price. If you want the ultimate Vegas buffet experience, you have to try Bachchanal. They have cuisines from all over the world. Some dishes I'd never expect to see at a buffet. Chicken ginseng soup, bone marrow, and fresh raw scallops still in the shell are some examples and the list goes on. I like to describe it as "fine dining but in buffet form."

Awww yes how time flies, this place holds some good memories it was the summer of 2015 when I tried this buffet.  It was the final stop to one of our many grand adventurous road trips and after leaving this location we lost our friends in Las Vegas, so we had our little very own HangOver part one moment...wolf pack disbanded, BUT reunited and good times.

Alright enough reminiscing and onto what's important the review.

Okay, so me and my friends did get this deal in Vegas that I cant really how much it was or what it was called, but it allowed us entry to many of the buffets in Vegas.  The only thing is I believe it did not include the Bacchanal Buffet, so we had to pay separately.  First thing about this place is that it has a very nice design to it and the inside of the buffet is very spacious as well.  Waiting here though can be a little bit of a drag because the lines can be long.  So if you're looking to want to try this place out either plan ahead of time or be prepared to wait a couple of minutes to be seated.

Next, this place is designates its food and desert very well so you won't have trouble if its food or desert that you're after.  Most foods just have a lot of choices and it makes you think wow, but this place takes that wow to the next level.  This is no Home Town Buffet... (sorry)...its quality.  They've got Asian, seafood, steak, ham, pizza, hamburger, Spanish....honestly I don't think I could name everything, but they've GOT CHOICES!! And desert...yo they make crepes in front of your face.  Cupcakes, cookies, a lot of flavors of ice creams man this place...gets you FULL.

I would come here again, but the only thing is the line can be long and even that price is kinda up there, but because of the choices and the quality it makes for a very satisfying buffet experience.

Awesome variety!! Would come back. Located in Caesar's palace and food overall is good. Don't make the mistake of overeating as you'll regret it and your tummy will hate you for it. Just because it's all you can eat, don't over do it. The only reason I didn't gave it 5 stars is due to the long wait. They need to come up with a better system to get people seated. Waited for about 2 hours on a weekend.

This buffet has a wide variety of food to select from. From Italian to Asian to Seafood to BBQ. I'd like to point out that this buffet has a wide variety of seafood. I loved how sweet the snow crab legs were and the Italian food was delicious I almost forgot I was eating at a buffet. The birria in the Mexican food section was to die for. The dessert also has a large variety to choose from and the people working the dessert area were extremely friendly and helpful as was everyone else working the buffet line but the ones working at the dessert bar stood out to me with their hospitality. Now as I mentioned the good unfortunately here comes the bad. First, our waitress was not very approachable she wasn't friendly nor was she attentive. She did not act with a sense of urgency! Secondly, the seafood in the cioppino were over cooked and sadly under seasoned and lastly the lamb chops were over cooked and burnt on the edges. Overall this buffet I would say is definitely above average but I don't think it's all the hype it seems to be. I hope this review is helpful to both the customer and the buffet staff.

I was looking forward to this for the longest time. The food was definitely a big disappointment nothing I hoped it would be. Definitely overhyped didn't enjoy anything at all but just the dessert. Went on a Monday food was very dry and tasted rubber. Ice cream and service was great but not enough where I will come back again.

Came here this past Saturday around 1pm for lunch (we arrived at around the time they're finishing lunch and preparing to transition to dinner food). 

When you go to any Vegas buffet, you're mostly paying for the variety of food. Bacchanal's food was pretty decent all around (I wouldn't say it was like THE BEST FOOD I'VE EVER TASTED, because it's hard to be good at everything), however, the food was a solid 4 star, and the variety is what you're paying the big bucks for. 

My highlights that I thought were very tasty and I would recommend filling your stomach with (avoid anything you get at a better restaurant - as an Asian person from the Bay Area I didn't touch the dim sum/ Chinese food at all):
- prime rib
- tomato bisque
- lobster bisque (very tasty!)
- truffle and mushroom pizza
- salmon and tuna poke (so good)
- oyster shooters (weird, but pretty good actually)
- mac n cheese
- lobster eggs benedict
- key lime pie dessert
- creme brulee
- lemon basil ice cream

There's a very hefty dessert station that has shave ice, lots of different ice cream, cakes, etc.

Things that were just okay and I wish I didn't get because it wasted stomach space:
- wagyu meat (I was really excited for this when I saw it because it's typically very expensive, but it wasn't good at all and very dry)
- the elk sliders (kind of dry, didn't taste like anything special)

I would recommend trying things that are typically very expensive and that you usually don't get access to. It's a pricey buffet, $59 with tax for lunch, and $65+ for dinner (volume wise, I feel like it was more than I would want to pay for, but it was my first time and it was worth experiencing once). If you're just going for a large meal and you want to capitalize on volume, I would say any buffet in Vegas or Reno would cut it. come here for the special stuff. I tipped after eating at the table, but I know a lot of other people don't.

Another con is that if you pay for parking it's like $20 for 1-4 hours you're eating. Lunch seems less crowded, we didn't have to wait super long to be seated and it wasn't packed. They kept the food pretty stocked and I never had to wait super long to get one particular thing. They kept our waters filled the whole time, I have no complaints about service. I wish that I had a very large stomach and could keep eating haha. 

Overall, worth a one time trip, and the best way to capitalize is to try a bunch of different things (going with friends is ideal, because then you can all try each others' dishes). Peep pics for some food aesthetics. The food is beautifully plated sometimes and it's pretty fun.
I came here with my family during Christmas time. It was so crowded and the price is kind of expensive compared to other buffets in the area. Foods are just fine, nothing special.

Probably my favorite buffet to go to in Las Vegas which is also located in one of my favorite casinos/hotels in the strip. I'm almost attracted to all their food items presented at buffet. From their crab legs/claws, oysters, shumai, prime rib, sushi, sashimi, scrambled eggs, to their pad thai noodles I'm loving everything about the place and got love for the foods I've never tried yet lol. It's a little bit pricey so if you go, make sure to come hungry and to take your time to enjoy the foods.
I came for the crab and the oysters and Now im full of seafood and can die a happy man
WOW amazing food. We loved everything. Very creative food and presentation. The Chefs were very friendly and helpful.

So delicious...I don't even know where to begin. I had to take glance and just admire the presentation and the selection. The food was so yummy from king crab to korean bbq ribs. We did pay a little more than usual due to Memorial Day but definitely worth the wait. I think it was about an hour from the moment we got in line to the time we got seated. I even had this seafood soup with crawfish, muscles, and clams there was so much flavor packed in this soup and was in individual tin mini pot (see pic). The service was great too. This goes to the waitress that cleared, got endless refills on our drinks, and just kept on checking on us to see if we need anything else. To all the preps at stations even saying hello as they prep the made to order tacos and made to order crepes. I had this peach ice tea that was so simple but was such a good pairing with all the food. The desserts were such a nice treat.. from mini lava cake to mini matcha chocolate cones. I ended my meal with an amazing coconut and ube gelato. So much to write about. Yes...I would go back again. I would recommend this buffett and pay the $$$ again. My only simi unpleasant experience I would say was the guy taking pics in line. He just didn't have a friendly appearance he didn't even smile or greet you and this is while you're in line at any point can decide not to pay for this expensive buffet and how does he chose who to take a photo of, I mean profiling can be a little demeaning but once you are in all is good.

Wow. Hands down the best buffet I've ever been to and it definitely lived up to the hype. We went for dinner on a weekday. The only downside is the wait--we waited for a little over an hour. Nonetheless, the food was extremely satisfying! Our waitress Ruth was always attentive and wonderful. The variety of the food here was unmatched and you will leave feeling like you got a culinary taste of different parts of the world. The seafood--oh my! Exceeded our expectations. And the desserts were unique and tasty. COME HERE! Worth the price and the wait.
Great food it was very tasty different but to get a seat took an hour when we walked in we saw lots of empty tables their es no need for such slow service but over all the food was ok
Very good.. our waiter mark was more then fantastic. For the price the buffet is endless and every item is good.. I know cuz I tire everything they had today.  would def go again.

This place was highly recommended by my friends when traveling to Vegas. They fo have a great selection of foods, especially for the meats. My favorite is the Spanish section in which they have a lobster soup that is very creamy and in butter taste. They meats are okay to me, they have beef brisket, roast beef, and back etc, the great one is the lamb chop that is near the meat section too, it is seasoned and cooked in perfectly done. Came on a Thursday night, there are some kiosks in the front when there are too many people waiting. The kiosks were closed when I got there since the lines were longer, but still less people as compared to weekend. Waited for about 45 mins from lining to be seated. 2 people are around $110 plus tax. Overall, I would say this place is so far so good to me, but it would be great if they can add more selection of sashimi and seafood.

I'm not really a buffet person but I heard so much about Bacchanal Buffet and decided to try it.

I guess the worst part of any Las Vegas buffet is the uncomfortable and crowded seating and here it was extreme. Tables are really close together and it just made dining here unpleasant.

Of course there are many selections and I didn't try everything but what I did try I didn't like. There was one exception however and that was the selection of shrimp dumplings. These were fine, especially by buffet standards.

Desserts all looked nice but what I had was consistent with the below average or awfulness of everything else I had.

They advertised on their website that only Thanksgiving Day and the Friday and weekend after it would be holiday pricing. However the Wednesday before Thanksgiving they charged a holiday price. Yes they post the new holiday price on one sign not visible to every customer who enters the line to protect their behinds but they know people will still go because even though they made effort to go there based on original price online and might not have if they saw.the holiday price online, they want to enjoy their vacation and they $20-$30 difference is acceptable to them to avoid going through the trouble of going somewhere else. I feel this practice is still false advertising because many people travel from out of state and the website should be accurate.

The food itself was restaurant quality for many of the items with the exception of the the sushi and the deserts I had(gelato and cupcakes) which were supar. Based on the amount the typical person would end up eating I feel if you were to order the good items separately at restaurants the price would be approx the same. With the holiday pricing I think ordering a la carte would be cheaper. The point of a buffet though  is selection, convenience and peace of mind of a flat rate. Many people i think would spend more money than buffet price if they ordered the same amount of food a la carte so i think it is worth it for most people. Just be wary of misleading advertising practices the week of holidays.

Busy brunch time. Food is good. The brisket is so crispy. Asian food so so. Various deserts.

这家的肉食很不错，人多的时候要排队等拿，有好多种烤肉和香肠供选择：）

甜品也很多，巧克力慕斯浓郁极了

Of course, this is Vegas and I needed to get to a buffet to get my fill of great foods. Fortunately, I was staying at a best friends and we decided to do a search of buffets of Vegas.  Bacchanal Buffet seemed to interest us even though i was not used to paying over ~$21.95/person. Hahaha.. We decided to get there by dinner time and see what it was all about. Guess what! This place TOPS all the buffets i've been to in Vegas. Great Customer Service from when we first got greeted at the front to the very-friendly waitress Maria who checked on us to ensure that we were doing OK throughout our dinner. Got to meet a couple of chefs that were walking on the floor as well speaking with with customers. That's what customer service is about, servicing customers to their needs.

Food - 5 stars (btw, i'm not a picky eater)
I started to walk from the the beginning and kept walking and walking towards the end. Could not believe the food varieties they were serving. It was unbelievable! For me to try most of it, I had to get small portions from the different areas (Asian, Italian, American, etc...) I  could not get an ounce of negativity from what I ate that evening. Foods were cooked to perfection. Even the prime-rib/lamb chops was superb! Seafood... OMG! The fresh oysters! Large shrimps! The dungeness crab legs! The desert area was unreal! So much selections and all looked good. The Chef that evening had told us that we also could order a chocolate souffle from the baker and it'll be in ready in 6 minutes! I can go on and on here..but I may have character limitations.

Overall experience was such an amazing one that i'd recommend this place to anyone that loves the higher standard of food quality.

The PRICE IS RIGHT for the quality of the foods served at the Bacchanal. Well done!

I'll definitely be back here on my next trip to Vegas.

On a side note, thank you Maria for taking care of us!

(Coffee was on point as well)

PLEASE DO NOT GO HERE. $116 waste of money. Go to Wicked Spoon or Wynn or literally any other buffet in town and you will enjoy yourself a lot more. 

I love a good buffet and for my girlfriends birthday dinner I was so excited to take her to the best, bacchanal. But we were amazingly underwhelmed. Heed these bad reviews, we aren't lying. The food was terrible, the lines were worse. When my waiter came around and asked how our meal was, I said it was terrible and when I glanced over my shoulder to him, I saw he had already moved on and wasn't listening at all. I emailed Caesars and told them my entire story and 3 days later received a copy/paste impersonal response that said "thanks for making us aware of that issue".

CAESAR'S DOESNT CARE IF YOU COME OR NOT. They are too big too care as evidenced by the absurd $116 price tag and the 2000+ reviews. I care a lot more about you enjoying your meal than they do. They messed up my girl's bday dinner and didn't even care. Jerks.

3.5 stars in my book

If you starved yourself all day long because you knew this was on the agenda, prepare to show up and wait a good hour+. We happened to show up during the Blue Plate Special Senior Citizen Hour and only had to wait about 20 minutes. By the time we left, the line was wrapped around the corner and down the hall. 

$54/person isn't too bad at all. We had reservations at CUT but after my less than stellar performance with the dice in my hand, we had to rethink the situation to save a few shekels. Such is life in Vegas. 

Make sure you packed your bottle of Patience because it's a real bleep show at times. See, tourists feel compelled to get their moneys worth. Ya know that over the top camera with the telephoto lens? Cost a pretty penny I'm sure, but it doesn't belong at a buffet. However, these folks clearly disagree because at least 4 times, as I was attempting to get my grub on, these camera carrying peeps were in full blown photo shoot mode. I get it, the buffet looks good. Relax slugger. Honestly? What do you do with those photos once you get them developed in your dark room? 

Food: Overall 4 star food experience indeed. Alaskan crab legs were the best I've ever tried, the prime rib was a quality slab of beef, despite the fatty piece I received. Wide selection of just better than supermarket sushi, which I didn't have the guts to try. Very nice selection of Asian options. My faves include: crispy duck, Korean BBQ spareribs. Dim sum options didn't look all that great, but the dumplings tasted pretty darn good. 

Dessert: Beyond incredible selection and every single item I tried was delicious! Fresh gelato was excellent. They even had tiny waffle bowls dipped in chocolate, which were hidden on top of the counter. 

In closing, I would say that this dining experience was pretty good. I will say that all the chefs were working very hard and doing their best to provide food quickly and that's a huge plus in my book. I'd definitely visit them again, but if I have better luck at the craps table, I am headed to CUT instead.

I don't mind paying $50 for a 5 star buffet but this wasn't what I expected. 

First of all I found someone else's used straw on the chair they seated me at. They did not acknowledge it and I refused to touch it when my hostess should have checked the table entirely. I ordered a ginger ale and they obviously ran out of syrup from the machine or the bar so it only tasted of club soda. I put the napkin on my lap and I saw a spot of DIRT, yes dirt on my napkin and I was about to wipe it onto my mouth. 

The soup dumplings were sitting in their container for so long the gyoza soaked up what was left of the soup. I really hated the small trays that held one small item of food that was too hot to carry and too big to put on your plate for the rest of the food. The oysters on a half shell weren't their freshest. They can at least put some flavoring in it I.e. green onions, hot sauce, or salsa. The shells were not rinsed well enough. 

I wanted to complain to the manager and explain the fact that their quality control needs to be at their best because of the price that we paid for but I don't want to go back even if they offered a discount on my next visit.

I can not fathom Bacchanal is not #1 because of the poor service and forgettable bites. However I do back up the fact that their desserts are amazing. 

I feel that paid a large amount of money to google for advertising because the experience was not great. I think we're going back to Wicked Spoon.

If you're in Vegas and have a huge appetite, come to this buffet! It is definitely one of the biggest (and most expensive) ones on the Strip. We came for the weekday dinner at around 5pm because we had a show afterwards. It was $55 pp. A bit on the pricier side, but worth it, especially if you're into seafood. Surprisingly, there was no line at all, so that was great. 
      The first thing you see when you walk in is the seafood station. They had fresh oysters, shrimp, sea snails, crab claws, and crab legs. To go along with them, there were different sauces, such as cocktail sauce, clarified butter, and horseradish. There were oyster shooters, mussel dishes (don't remember what they were called), and clam chowder, too. Oysters tasted a bit funky imo, so I only had one. The shrimp and crab legs were delicious. Oyster shooter was very good, as well. I didn't have the guts to try the escargot (sea snails), though! 
      The buffet also had a carving station with wagyu beef, tri-tip, slab bacon, brisket, pork ribs, and sausages. I tried the wagyu, brisket, and ribs. All were very good and tender. They had au jus and barbecue dispensers, and both were great. There was bone marrow, too! It was delicious. Next to the meat was a spinning wheel where they were making little made to order tacos. I tried an al pastor taco with pineapple, pico de gallo, and cotija, and it was delicious! 
      I wasn't as focused on the rest of the stations (besides dessert of course), but they had an Asian section with dim sum, sushi, soup, and more meat. Sushi and dim sum were good, but not great. They also had different pizzas that looked good, but I didn't try any. I try to focus on foods that I don't eat at home. There were also a few salads, and they looked pretty good. 
       Moving on to dessert! Their dessert station is in the middle of the dining area, and it is huge! I think they have more dessert than the Wynn and the Wicked Spoon. They have many different types of interesting gelato and sorbets, such as lemon basil and ube. They also had regular flavors. I was so excited to see a crepe station! 
       We decided to try plain vanilla to go with chocolate lava cake (which is really just chocolate cake), lemon basil sorbet, a raspberry beignet, a pink lemonade cupcake, a crepe with a berry syrup, a Chinese egg tart, blueberry cobbler, chocolate pistachio mousse cake, chocolate toffee cookie, macarons, and the chocolate peanut butter mousse (nsa). I know, I know, it's a lot, but my whole family split everything! Honetly, everything we tried was fantastic! The chocolate cake was dense, but paired perfectly with the gelato. The pink lemonade cupcake surprised me by how good it was. It had no artificial taste like I expected. My favorites out of all the dessert had to be the crepe, the gelato, and the chocolate cake! 
        This buffet will now be one of our go to's in Vegas. They have some of the best desserts, seafood, and meats. Sorry for the long review and no pictures!! I was to busy enjoying everything!

Very bad food. Nothing to eat. And the king crab only serves seven star cusWe have to wait for five hours to eat the garbage!!! 
Why I waste my time here... The worth Christmas ever.

Everything about this buffet screams the best money can buy. It's been years since I visited this place and I still remember how good it was. Thankfully nothing has changed, it's still the same amazing 60 dollars buffet it has always been. The tacos and Spanish rice were my two personal favorites, followed by the chocolate chip cookies. I will be back to chow down on some dinner soon enough. I highly recommend this place for all your buffet needs.

My daughter and son in law took me here for my birthday, at first I was mad because the line was extremely long but it well worth the wait. The 
Food was great and fresh. Great service clean and the best part of it was me finding $700 in the bathroom.
Whenever I go there is always a long line but the food options are crazy

This is the KING of buffets!! 25,000-square-foot buffet extravaganza.

It is SO worth it to eat here. =) Lines can get long here so get here early.

So many varieties of different foods here that its unbeatable & unbelievable.

9  live stations (chefs cook it live): seafood, Asian, Mexican, Italian and dessert, that present hundreds of daily items.

My faves:

Shrimp jumbo cocktails so fresh & delicious 11pts

Sea bass so buttery & flavorful 11pts

Snow crab legs - be sure to ask them to steam them if u like them warm.

Oyster shooters so delicious 11 pts

Seafood & Chinese station was great.

Italian & meat station was ok.

Creme brulee was very yummy & not too sweet 9pts

Mochi ice cream was yummy 8 pts

Gelato station was so delicious w/ so many delicious flavors to choose from (you can sample each one of the flavors if you like. =) 10 pts

Dark Chocolate dipped strawberries were huge but  not sweet. =( 7pts

Deserts looked very pretty & there was a huge variety but the flavors were off.

Wicked Spoon's desserts are better.

Service is great here. =)

FYI, if you sign up for their rewards card you will get a discount for this buffet with that card here. 

Open daily.

Breakfast (Monday - Friday, 7 a.m. - 11 a.m.): $25.99
Brunch (Saturday - Sunday, 8 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $40.99
Lunch (Monday - Friday, 11 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $32.99
Dinner (Daily, 3 p.m. - 10 p.m.): $45.99 on weekdays, $50.99 on weekends

A few standouts to me was the assortment of sushi and poke. Surprisingly, very tasty and fresh for buffet standards.

Also, in the seafood arena, the Jonah Crab Claws stood out. It tasted fresh. That means it hasn't been frozen for a period of time like the Dungeness crab available.

The desert section was surprisingly good as well. 

My partner and I have been wanting to dine here for a while. It was on our 3rd try that we were successively seated!!
 
1st attempt - we arrived at 8:30pm for dinner but the waiting line was so long that they no longer admitted any more guests
2nd attempt - we arrived at 5:50pm for dinner. Waited for 1hr. Paid for dinner. Then waited to be seated. All of a sudden there was a power outage in which they said they would have it back on. We waited till 8pm then gave up. They offered us to cut the wait line the next time we visited.
3rd attempt - we had lunch at 11am and was successfully seated in almost immediately due to our long wait the night prior. 

Tip: Dinners are pricey, I suggest going in for a late lunch that rolls over into dinner. 
Also, it's great for dodging the hour long waiting line that's bound to happen for dinner even on a weekday!! We had waited for 1hr + on a Thursday evening at 6pm. 

Costs: Dinner ($55 pp), Lunch ($45 pp)
O yea!!! Been here before and am back! Food and service is great! Clean, positive place, the food is a good place for foodies to enjoy!
Biggest buffet I've seen and eaten so far. So very many varieties and styles of food! It's a great experience.
Food is great!!! I love our server Jennifer, She is very attentive which is good if you have 2 kids with you!!!

It has been awhile since I have gone to any "high end" buffets but Bacchanal definitely checks the blocks to be up among the best. The diversity of food is astounding as I had Mexican, Japanese, Chinese, and a multitude of American options plus a wide array of desserts. Most importantly, nearly all of the items I tried were adequate to above average.

This place made me wish I had a bigger stomach. Everything was amazing. You can get a free beer if you check in, but who wants beer to take up precious space in your stomach with all the food options? I would definitely visit Vegas if not just to come here.

This is my favorite Las Vegas buffet. I love the variation of foods. The line wait is a little long but it is worth the wait. The service is very good and I really would recommend to my family and friends.

Plus: you get to people watch and see the frenzy that is Asian people collecting buffet food in extraordinarily planned fashion. (You. Crab leg line. Me. Meat line. Transfer plates. More. More.)
Minus: overrated.

It was my first time in Vegas, and I just had to try the infamous Las Vegas buffet. This is the newer one out of the bunch, and judging by photos and reviews, it looked like we were in for a luxurious feast. Not your normal buffet!

The line was long and sweeping, and took approximately an hour to get to the front where you pay first. Memorial Day weekend we ended up paying brunch prices, not lunch, which was approximately $50. Okay, well, I heard about the steak...and the starters..and the seafood...has to be worth it! *If you tack on $20, you can go in the express line.

Upon entry, it looked gorgeous. The tall chairs and round tables were groups felt very cozy and intimate. Plenty of seating to go around. However, once I started lining up for the meat/other-unhealthy-yums line, I knew that my experience would begin to deteriorate. I waited 30 minutes before I even got one item on my empty plate. The buffet here operates by lines; you can't really cut in to just grab a certain dish, unless you are daring enough to brave the snarls of hungry line waiters. There were assorted Mexican rice dishes, then some salads, soups, bread rolls and cold pastas (which no one ventured into cause it curved inwards and people didn't want to lose their spot in line) before hitting the Memorial Day sliders. The sliders and small items were placed on cute colored square dishes, which take up much real estate on your plate. I saw a man plop those items on his white plate (genius!) before he got reprimanded by the chef for not taking the square plate with him. But let's be real--you have to wait so long to just get an item....people are not going to be going back in line because your plate sizes don't make sense.

Onto the food:

PROTEIN: Cuts of meat included rib eye (best protein here), lamb shank (salty), brisket (salty), chicken (didn't try) and a fatty bacon slice. The waffle fries were in cute mini fryer baskets, but unfortunately were overly salty. 
PASTA: baked lasagna cube. Nasty, dry, heavy....nyuck.
SALAD: So-so. Again with the square plates!
SUSHI: too much rice. If you pick off the salmon off the nigiri, you can get some good sashimi bites, though.
UDON/RAMEN SOUP: Actually pretty decent. The broth was yummy and not too salty! Cooked fresh per order, and the line went super fast for this.
DESSERT: crepes were one of the highlights of Bachannal desserts. It's DIY except for the fresh crepe. The lava cake was good, but overly heavy and dense. fresh, no yucky icicle ridden gelato here. They only give you 1 mini scoop which again, takes up valuable plate real estate if you get more than 1 flavor.
SEAFOOD: Shrimp was wonderful. crab legs were good, but mine were cold. You'll have to wait for the fresh steamed one and work at it. No oysters until dinner service...sad.
SIDES: only liked the fresh vegetables, which was probably cooked in butter. The mac and cheese was dense. Salty fries. 
DRINKS: peach green tea for the win.

Service was good--the people clearing plates were very, very fast and efficient. However, drinks were very slow. It's too overpriced and too limited in good items that you can get at subpar restaurants. You might as well take the $50 and go to a nice steakhouse. "Las Vegas buffets"--nothing to see here at Bachannal, folks. Move on.

Come hungry!!! We waited in line for this buffet for quite a while but it proved to be DEEEEELICIOUS! The selection, the variety,
Quality, I can't say enough! It wasn't cheap but we all left happy!

Came here for Thanksgiving lunch and we only had to wait forty minutes. The restaurant texted us when a table became available. I mainly filled up on two plates of crab legs as they were the most expensive, and then had some prime rib, sliders, ginger congee, goat cheese, manchego, mocetta bresaola, triple creme brie, mortadella, and felino.
