Since it was Thanksgiving they had turkey and mashed potatoes but I steered clear as I wanted to try rarer foods.

For dessert I had orange beer shandy, lemon basil, and strawberry balsamic sherbet.

All the food was incredibly delicious and there was plenty of wait staff to fill your water or the bottomless mimosas. I didn't really drink the mimosas as I concentrated on the juices- strawberries, cucumber, mango, and guava.

I think this place has passed up Wicked Spoon for me as the go to buffet in Vegas. they have way more options, and almost everything is actually pretty good. tons of asian food, seafood and meat. a little light on the italian food, which is a bummer, and the pizza isnt good, but there is so much stuff to try it won't matter. I mean they have bone marrow, Ive never seen that at a buffet. I also really appreciate how they break up the line here by party size, moves a lot quicker if you are only two people.

Don't waste your money and definitely don't waste your time of 3-5 hour wait, gone are the tomahawk steaks and the king crab legs, now it's an additional $55.00 on top of the $78.00 for the buffet, if you want king crab. The prime rib was very tough, which leads me to believe it's not cooked correctly or it's not prime and why at this price are you limited to one plate of snow crab at a time when my wife and I have such trouble walking. The Bellagio, Makino's and Hot and Juicy a much better way to go.

Best buffet i've ever been too....great food, fun atmosphere, long lines to get in (meh...) but well worth the wait.  the restaurant is spacious but if this had seating for 100 more people they could cut the wait lines a lot faster, but then there would be lines at the food...so who konws...$70 for dinner on the weekend, but if you want quality food, this is the place.

First timer (not VIP) and it was an excellent time. Five stars all to Adrian who was serving the steamed crab (4/13/19 8:15pm). He he funny, polite and very patient even with some impatient people. He helped organize that whole area into a crazy efficient machine, serving, cooking, assisting, refilling, helping lost diners, everything. All with some jokes and a smile. Great experience. Thanks!

My boyfriend is Vegan and he was so worried about going here because he was worried he would find nothing to eat but he was pleased to find that there was a lot! Also! We asked the host if they would be able to show us some options and a server and chef came over to us and completely made our night at the buffet amazing! Thank you Daniel and thank you Mark! The chef brought over about 3 different full size dishes for my boyfriend which included vegan rice, vegan full size pizza, vegan and I think something else! We really enjoyed ourselves and will definitely be going back! The Caesar hotel really give you a homely feeling and they all seem to care about their guests.

We stopped in on a whim and are glad we did. This place is top notch. We went in for dinner and was so good we went back the following day. It has a great selection ranging from seafood to asian, carving stations, and great dessert selection, including to order crepes. It is well kept very clean and the staff is constantly checking the lines to make sure things are full and hot. Items covered properly with proper serving utensils. Staff works well together when busy. Javier was exceptionally friendly and had great customer service skills. Highly recommended!

Came for brunch on Sunday and the wait was roughly 45mins. You have to stand in a line to pay, then stand in another line to get seated. 

The food was just as good as I remembered. They serve prime rib and crab legs ( warm and cold) for brunch? There's a dessert area, ramen/udon station. They had acai and smoothie shots for brunch too! 

Over all, nice experience if you have time to kill. Still one of my favorite buffers in Vegas.

Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace is the absolute best buffet, in Las Vegas, and arguably the entire world!

If you are going to splurge this is the place to do so; and to be fair, splurge is probably the wrong word, what you are paying for here is quality. Everything at the Bacchanal is top tier, the elegant decor and furniture, the service always fantastic (shoutout to Mark), the food always fresh, the international options are always changing, always delicious. Specialty stations such as: made to order tacos, warm crab legs out of this world good.

In my opinion, you truly get your monies worth here, I've been here for breakfast, brunch and dinner (all on separate trips of course) all memorable, its competitively priced when ranked against the other eateries in town; truly an experience not to be overlooked if you are in town.

Oh, man I wish they've told me about this place long time ago! All this time in Vegas, and we just now tried it. Best food, and our server, Romulus was so attentive and professional. Next time we'll stop here first.

Ive been to alot of buffett in town and was super excited for this BUT was disappointed. YES- there is a huge variety of stuff. YES- everything was pretty good. YES- half of my food was cold. YES you did read that right. Things like the elk sliders that were under heat lamps that were cold to the touch . I did like the ramen and taco station those were fun. The carving station was huge but was the 1 thing i didn't try. Id still go again however i honestly prefer the M seafood buffet to this buffet and there is less selection but i feel quality is higher.

I am in the huge minority with negative reviews so if I were going to Vegas and I saw my review I'd be like "Psssshhh, there are another 2500 positive reviews...so this person had a bad experience, whatevs that won't be me!" Read on dear reader.

So to start, there was no line. We went at 5:30pm on a Thursday and just zipped right in. In fact, this was our first night/restaurant in Vegas and I was so excited to try this place out! The food was really good! The standout was definitely the lambchop and brisket. Yummmmm....

Our waitress did not inform us what beverages came with the meal (we didn't ask) but I see on yelp that beer and wine are included with the price? And we did not get our picture taken when we entered. Big deal. Not the reason for the one star.

The reason I'm giving Bacchanal one star is because by midnight I had come down with the rowdiest case of food poisoning I've ever had in my life. Yes, food poisoning, it's true!! For 2 days now I haven't been able to consume anything but water and crackers and been confined to my hotel room. I'm so sad. This was my anniversary trip with my hubs which I had been planning for months which has now been ruined. My conclusion is it was either the crab legs or the seafood that put me in this state because my husband is fine, but he didn't eat anything that came from the ocean. 

So, go to this buffet because I know you will, I'd be surprised if my review stopped you but think twice about eating anything that was living underwater. Also, I'm curious, did anyone else out there who ate at this buffet on 11/20/2014 for dinner get violently ill? Just wondering if it was just me...

Such a delicious buffet!!! The best of the best! Everything tasted as if you specifically ordered it and not just a dish at a buffet to fill you. I was shocked they had menudo! And it was as delicious as authentic Mexican restaurants! All the foods that were plated in their mini plates were my favorites! And dessert was just amazing! Specially the macaroons that just melted in the mouth! My hubby Said he's willing to drive 4 hrs from our home to just come and eat here and go back home. LOL

Where do I start? We flew in from California and haven't ate all day! It was already 4pm by the time we got to our suite. I was starving and this was the number one buffet I wanted to try. I had read many great things upon coming to try this buffet. Although it like $52 it was SO worth it. The food was just outstanding. The selection was pretty big. I have tried another buffets in Vegas in the past and to me this place topped them all. I will definitely come back!

What a disappointment! It was a waste of time, effort, and money eating here!

We signed in at the kiosk at 6:30pm, and we got a ticket with a 150 minutes (2.5 hours) wait-time. We finally were seated at 9:15pm. 

The food was the most disappointing part of this dining experience! The only thing that tasted good was the oysters at the front-end seafood station . That was because the raw oysters didn't require any cooking. The holiday special soft-shell crab tasted awful. The snow crabs (served in different stations) were so salty that eating only a couple pieces had burned our mouths (not just the tongue). Someone in our dining party described that as salty as a TABLE spoon of salt in bringing solution. The saltiness didn't stop there. Almost every food station had something that were exceedingly salty. 

The food at the Asian station wasn't cooked properly. Over cooking, soggy rice, and improper seasoning were just a few problems to be mentioned here. 

Roasting meat station had a few good dishes. The roasted prime rib was excellent, and we were so grateful that it wasn't salty. However, the holiday special char-grilled lamb T-bone failed at proper seasoning and grilling technique; thus, wasting the high quality meat. 

The salty food was so damaging that we had to drink a lot of soda, juice, and lemonade to cleanse our palettes. The sweetness and sourness of the drinks helps to cover the salty & burned sensation in the mouths temporarily so we could tasted other food. However, our taste buds were saturated by these flavors, and it prevented us to taste the desserts properly at the end!

We paid $70 per person holiday price. I think this meal should be valued at $25 based on the quality of the dishes even without the salty component in this dining experience. Don't get me wrong, they have good quality ingredients, they just butchered them by not cooking or preparing them well!

In summary:
1. All the food that didn't require their in-house cooking or processing tasted good. 
2. Avoid the crabs especially the cut-in-half crab legs. They were all soaked in very salty brine solution. 
3. All the soups tasted salty. 
4. Sign in at the kiosks earlier during the holiday season. The waiting time is long. You can do something else while waiting. The buffet staff will text you if you can be seated earlier.

I decided to splurge for my sister and I yesterday, Sunday January 17th since I won some $$$ the night before. 
We got there around 9:30am-wait was nonexistent, which was a relief since I'd read there can be long waits w/o an express pass. We didn't order the unlimited beverage package(additional $15pp) since we aren't big drinkers. I did mention we were in Vegas to celebrate my sis' birthday and noted she wrote 'Birthday' on our table receipt. Our server was Alexandria, and she gave us awesome service! Beverages were brought out quickly and dirty plates whisked away in a timely manner...I commend her for the congenial 'service with a smile' even though she had five or six tables in her station and was kept pretty busy!

Now about the food...for the price($49.99 for weekend brunch served 8am-3pm. Note that it is an additional $10 more after 3pm). The exceptional quality of the food is well worth the price!!!!

Here are my standout faves with pics posted:
Lobster Benedict was heavenly-hollandaise sauce perfection perfection! Prime rib was sliced thin and bleeding rare just as I requested. The seasoned peppered crust was the best part! Ate my share of crab legs and mussels, but they weren't anything extraordinary to rave about. The inclusion makes the brunch a bit more easy to stomach pricewise.
Sis had sushi but wasn't impressed by taste or quality from the two pieces she sampled. She rated it average.
I did luv luv luv the congee(Chinese rice porridge), which needed the requisite dry shredded pork, chopped green onions and pickled radishes-and yes, it was provided  on the side to add! 
Alexandria, our server, brought over a birthday dessert plate for my sis, which was a super nice touch. Overall, we'd definitely visit again. Lots of choices, great variety of dishes for meat eaters, vegetarians or picky eaters.
My suggestion is to sample a little of everything that appeals to you...all the food is freshly prepared.
Now I can say I've been to the Bacchanal at Caesars!!!

I went here on a Saturday night waited about an hour and a half to get in, just to be disappointed by the food. My top items at this buffet were the tacos made on the spinning wheel, macroni and cheese, peach green tea, and the lamb t bone. The rest of the buffet was pretty under qualify for a $60 buffet a person... Went to the Rio buffet at a fraction of the price it was better overall.

Very high price. Wait for 5 hours in Christmas day night. No king crabs as declared before as they are only provided with the 7 star customers.
The beef are really raw and plastic and they are  hard to chew. Other seafood has too much salt and the water provide service was really bad...
Will not come here for the second time.
Definitely a waste of time.

I hyped this place up soooooooooooo much to my husband, and when we finally got to dine here, well, not much of it was memorable.

We splurged on the lobster and champagne split combo that included line passes, and that definitely was delicious. Everything else at the Bacchanal was not worth writing home about.

Gone are the many different types of mochi. The place is just one GIANT buffet with food that pretty much tastes the same no matter which cooking station you visit. 

For the price and the wait, I highly doubt I'd ever be back. There are better options in Vegas to explore.

For ~$60, I expected more from this place. I waited a whole freakin year to come back to vegas to hit this joint up only for it to come short. 

While the wait system was convenient and the service, friendly,  the food itself was nothing special. There were only a couple of items that were good, really. 

For about the same price, I recommend doing the 24hr pass offered by Paris and its affiliate casinos. Paris' buffet is  way better and you get a whole day to stuff yo face in between those crab legs just like you did to that random when you got..crabs. Aaahhh the circle of life.

This is a first class buffet! If you are a foodie, have a refined palate, and enjoy high quality food then this is the buffet for you. If you love fine dining you will love the seafood and meats, and amazing international foods. Every meat is perfectly cooked and can get a nice med-rare high quality prime rib at carving station. Even if you don't eat a lot this is your best choice since they have multiple small plates with amazing culinary treats- salmon deviled eggs, miniature Caesar salads, oysters shooters, 4 types of crab, poke, lobster Mac n cheese, bone marrow, and many others. Paella and Chinese food is quite delicious too. They have much more than you can sample. Including CPK quality pizza for kids, pastas, and tacos if you don't care to get your money's worth with the fancy foods. Desserts and gelato are amazing and extensive, including a crepe station. You will not be disappointed-- look for a groupon for a true bargain.
Hands down his best buffet in my opinion! Lots of choices and the food is fresh and delicious! The dessert bar is outstanding. Would definitely recommend and will be back on our next Vegas trip!

This our third time here and while the Bacchanal Buffet was never amazing it has clearly gone downhill.  We got here at 0930am on a Sunday and there was no line whatsoever. That's not a good sign for a Las Vegas strip property on St Patrick's day, but we had a LivingSocial deal and don't get to the strip very often.  While the Buffett got a little busier while we were there, it never drew the crowd one would expect for a holiday weekend in Las Vegas. 

The buffet has a lot of items that are individually presented in a tasting style, such as shrimp and grits in a single serve skillet, but every time we have been here the food is cold.  There is the typical mix of foods, including seafood, American, Mexican and Asian dishes.

There was more of a focus on presentation in the past, with carefully crafted individual servings, but the buffet is changing to a more traditional approach of mass quantities of food. Despite this, the food is still served cold and lacking in flavor, which is a huge disappointment.  I will say that their pastries were excellent, however they are likely purchased from an outside bakery.  If not, Caesars employs some outstanding pastry chefs. 

Service was lackluster today, and during prior visits was the only real highlight. While our plates were cleared relatively quickly by a busser, drinks were not refilled without asking and our waitress was often missing.  

I can honestly say that the Bacchanal Buffet isn't worth full price, it's not even worth the frequent coupons that are sold on LivingSocial and I'll spend my money elsewhere in the future.

Food was excellent quality for the most part. The only disappointment was the sausage had a funny taste. 
Our server, Sandra Williams, was helpful and quick and enhanced our Bacchanal experience. 
Definitely worth it for the price.

Came here to eat with 4 people at 3ish on a Saturday. Was surprised to see such a long line, broken up by guest count: 1-2, 3-4, 5 or more. We asked the lady who was watching the lines some information as to pricing, how long the wait was, etc. , but she said it was her first day and she didn't know much. 

We waited for about 20 mins before paying up, and then waited in a separate line to be seated. Waited about another 20 minutes before we were taken in. 

Pricing:
Weekends after 3pm: $65 for each adult 

Highlights:
Brisket
Pulled pork 
Cold cocktail shrimp 
Cold crab legs
Warm crab legs ***is located in the Italian section and is absolutely delicious. Highlight of the whole meal 
Mac and cheese (with bacon) 
Truffle mushroom soup 

They have your typical Asian section with dim sum and other dishes, Italian, seafood, Mexican, etc. , but crab legs is where it's at! We will be back.

What the heck happened to this place?This was one of the best buffets in town period. This last visit not so much. 

The food was subpar,the quality really dropped. The choices were few and far between. They didn't restock or put anything new out when something was out. Some of the food was cold and stale and not hot and fresh.

We both got sick shortly after eating there. Are they not cooking the food right? A lot of money spent just to get sick. We use to leave satisfied and thought money well spent, not this last time.

Our server barely refilled our drinks so we had waive other servers down just to get a refill.

We use to recommend this place to friends and family but now I don't see us recommending this place again.

I don't see us coming back anytime soon. I almost think we would of been better off going to the Rio or some other place in town.

A great experience, the sheer amount of food from so many places around the globe is both amazing and overwhelming. Our waiters were very kind and attentive. The only thing is that a lot of the good options don't come with a whole lot of flavor, but I imagine this is willingly sacrificed in favor of offering so many options.

Bacchanal Buffet has selections from all over the world: Italian food, American food, Chinese/Japanese food, etc. Don't be scared off by all of the meat talks about this buffet- I'm not a big meat person, and I felt that I still ate a lot of vegetarian options that the buffet had to offer. The selection is endless, from crab legs to ramen to bone marrow- you can definitely find something that tailors to your taste buds here. I was extremely impressed with the dessert selection as they had made-to-order crepes, matcha cake, and mochi ice cream. The restaurant ambiance was nice, and our server was very attentive.

Cons in my opinion: I was a little disappointed with some of the items I've tried such as the ramen and miso soup because the taste was a little off. In addition, I think that this buffet is a little overrated for the price. According to the web, weekday dinner is $55 and weekend dinner is $60 per person. I did however enjoy my first experience dining at the buffet and eating the variety of foods they offered.
Uninspiring average offerings for 20 bucks more than the competition.  I think this place is run by Fredo because it is a disappointment.
The food did not fill my epectations as a five star buffet. Was it worth the price? Probably not. In fact most of the foods from their kiosks were either bland or dry.

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS! My family and I are extreme foodies when we go to Vegas on vacation and we have tried pretty much every single buffet. This one beats the Bellagio, the Wynn and the Wicked Spoon.  Everything is hot and the hospitality of the servers is incredible. The passion they have is exuded in the food they create. Wish I could just live there lol

Excellent, especially if you are looking for different choices.  Mushroom ravioli with escargot, lobster bisque, oyster on the half shell, and other delicacies you just do not find at other buffets.  Delicious.

Used a Groupon with no issues.  No line at 4:00pm or when we left a couple of hours later.

services was good, not excellent. However, food SUCKS- not fresh, cold, dried up.   oyster not fresh, crab not fresh either (snow crab mixed with king crab- seriously? ), lamb was overcooked and dried up...really Caesar entertainment (cutting too much cost?). 

services and food NOT match the great name of Caesar. 

disappointed. would NOT recommend. Not worth the overpriced ticket anymore.

uber driver recommended another buffet. shouldve listened.

This is our number one buffet but never again in new years eve lol the wait was ridiculous we check in at 12 and we were told to go back at 2 and got seated at 3pm , all the good buffets had a long wait so we decided to get coffee at starbucks and walk the forums to kill time and went back to the line.

Our waiter was AMAZING i checked the receipt and his name was Ricardo  lol he was on top of our mimosas and making conversation even thou he was so busy , taking all our plates away .

Sad we didnt make it for brunch :(

But we are going back again soon !!

Right after our plane landed in Las Vegas from Sacramento, my boyfriend and I came here to eat. 

The service was good, but I would expect it to be for $50+ per person!!! I was appalled at the price, but we were hungry and it took us about 20 minutes of walking to find the buffet in what seems to to be biggest casino/hotel on the strip. 

The ambiance is nice, and very clean. There are plenty of tables for small and large groups. 

The food was good. I think some items could have been better, but it's a buffet so I'm not expecting every single dish to be the best I've ever had. There is so much variety here and soooo many dishes to try out. My favorite was probably the Italian station. The pastas and meatballs were good. 

Only complaint is that the desserts were not good. I probably tried about 2/3 of what was on the station (not the crepes, cus the line was too long), and many were left uneaten after one bite. The creme brulee was probably the best one I had. 

If you're looking for a lot of variety and lot of choices, this is a great buffet.
Motherfriggin food poisoned!!! You unsanitary, filthy, lazy ass Lima beans!!!!!!!!!!!

This place ruined our night! Took a number: 1.5 hour wait. Not to get in though.. to actually get a table there's another line which we were told was another 1.5-2 hours. That would put us past closing time of the buffet. The hostess just shrugged her shoulders and was no help. In the end: 3.5 hour wait and no table. What a ridiculous establishment! Now it's too late to get a table anywhere else.

The Bacchanal Buffet is by far the best buffet I have ever been to. I was part of a large party and the servers were not only accommodating but efficient in their service. Romulus was very kind and gave us good site seeing tips. 

Food: 
There is so much food to choose from; Mexican, American, Asian, and a wide selection of desserts! 

The seafood was amazing. I haven't been more obsessed with crab legs than I have here. I had to wait after eating that first to make room for more food. They also had snails which I thought was interesting but a lot of people seemed to enjoy them.

I also tried the el pastor and carne tacos at the taco station and they were very authentic. They also had chicken but I didn't get a chance to taste them.

The sushi was fresh and the perfect temperature! The spicy tuna was my favorite. They also had dumplings and other types of Asian dishes.

Lastly, you absolutely cannot miss out on the carving station! They had slabs of bacon!!! I spent most of my time there. 

Overall, I am definitely coming back to this buffet every time I'm in Vegas.
Best buffet in Vegas by far. Amazing seafood and like 5 times more desserts than other buffets. Only downside is waiting in line almost an hour to get in.

Lovely experience. Paid $68 for all you can eat buffet at brunch/breakfast time. Truly enjoyed the crab legs (both hot and cold), the assortment of seafood and the special "check in on Yelp and get 1free drink." It was the perfect wrap up brunch for our bachelorette weekend! Our server, Sandra, was amazing!!! Would definitely come back for dinner.
Still in line can't wait to eat.  My mothers first time she can't wait.  Wait is a little long for a Monday and forgot my coupon but all good.  Hope the food is good because of the wait.

Beware- Expect long lines! 

Saturday at 6pm

Didn't make it into the buffet due to the overwhelming line. We were given a hold time of 34 minutes just to be let into the entrance line. The entrance line wait time was an additional 1 hour. We decided to leave. Not work the wait.

The buffet was alright. I came here for lunch and had to wait a long time to get in. Now, i am not opposed to waiting for a great place for food, so i wasn't mad. 
Once we got in, i was neither impressed nor disappointed. Their meats were great. Prime rib and American Kobe? yes please. They cooked them pretty dang well too.
They had a few dim sum options and sushi options as well. Then they have your traditional American, Italian, other Asian, and seafood. Overall, it was a decent experience and I am glad I can say I have been to the buffet at Caesar's Palace. However, would i ever pay $40 per person for this place? probably not.

Don't do what my friends and I did and come right at dinner time.  Coming at 7 on a Saturday night meant waiting for about 1:5 hours till we sat down.  

The wait staff was very fast and we got drinks served quickly and the plates were cleared promptly.  The OJ here was really good and tasted fresh and not like Tropicana or Florida's Natural.  For costing $17M dollars the placed looked nice.

The 30 day dry aged Tomahawk rib-eye was the best thing they had imo.  It was cooked perfectly every time, the crust on it was great and was juicy.  But it took me going up there 6 times to get 2 servings of it.

The quality at sushi station was not good at all and I had better sushi at Famima today.  Their fried chicken, the mussels, the clam bake, the halibut,salmon and mexican food were all overcooked and dry.  

There were many other things which I was disappointed with but that Rib eye is still in my mind.

I have only been to two buffets in Vegas, but this by far is my favorite.  It had the most variety and the highest quality of any buffet that I have ever seen.  

You could spent the day here, visiting country after country - actually you get a two hour maximum because there is always a line of people waiting to get in.  However, after two hours in this place you will be stuffed.  

A couple of my notable favorites were in the Chinese/Japanese section.  They had amazing dumplings, dim sum, etc.  They also had a great juice bar with several different kinds of fresh squeezed juice.  But most importantly perhaps was the dessert section.  There were several trips made to try all the different varieties of bite size sweets.  

I could go on and on about this place.  It is pricier, but the best food that I have ever had and I think if I came back to Vegas, though I would want to try something new - I would be tempted to go back for a sure win.

My family and I went for the holiday dinner. It was roughly 70 bucks a person, which is pretty up there compared to other buffets. With that being said, my family and I expected a somewhat great experience. Sadly it was not, the line was 4 hours. However, the staffs will only tell you the wait is max 2 hours. They don't mention that you have to wait in line for 2 hours to pay first then wait another 2 hours to get in. I told one of the staffs that they have to inform their customers better and the first thing she said was "we have a table for you, so do you want it or not?" I don't think I have to say much about their customer service after that. 

Now about the food. Omg, I honestly was beyond disappointed. There are a lot of food options; however, most of the food are either too salty or have no flavor profle at all. Crab legs were extremely salty and yes you will have to wait in line for at least 20 minutes to get like 5 crab legs. Oh did I also mention you only have 2 hours to eat? Yes, you only have 2 hours to eat plus waiting in line for different food. So if you do go here, prepare to suffer mentally before eating and while eating. It will be one of a kind experience, in the worst way possible. Highly recommend trying other places like Rio buffet.

We all remember $54.04.
That's how much it costs to eat here WITH a discount card from the hotel.

I bet it might've been a different experience had we not come on a holiday weekend. However, we did. Read on if you're also considering coming here for New Years' weekend.
If not, then see others' 5-star reviews.

We all felt like cattle being herded along through the food lines. People had no manners. Where did these people come from? Had they never seen a buffet before? Had they starved themselves for days? My party hails from SoCal where buffets are abundant and food is in abundance. Every couple minutes, I would hear people telling others to "don't cut!" or "is he cutting?" Seriously people, calm down!

The experience of being yelled at by others stands out more than the food. Oh, and the fact that my cousin waited 20 minutes before she could get a lemonade and our table was a mess since we had a tiny table for 5-people. Half of our party was too lazy to get much food though since the lines were so discouraging.

Good eats
Pistachio macaroons
Prime rib was alright

Dislike
No one was a fan of the oyster shooters (how sad!)

Other foods I recall are the crab legs which all go for, tamales, sashimi, crepes, ceviche, miso soup, carnitas,

Ehhh, I'd rather forget this dining experience! However, my brother and cousin regularly frequent this buffet so maaaybe I need to give it a chance on a non-holiday. Bacchanal, you disappointed me with the clientele and the slow (poor) waitstaff.

First thing we hit up when we got to Vegas. It's definitely a good buffet place with lots of variety when it comes to different cultural foods. Asian, American, Mexican, Indian... they have something from each culture which is pretty nice. 
My husband liked all the meat of course. And I loved the desserts. The thing you gotta remember is that when you go to buffets, just don't expect the best tasting/quality of food you've ever tasted. Expect decent and then if they surpass that, even better!
Try their peach iced tea by the way... its' refreshing!
Ok, onto the foods... they have small servings of each dish which is good so you get to taste the variety of stuff they have. Don't go for the sushi as it's definitely not up to par with good sushi. But everything else is pretty good. The meat that they slice up for you is pretty good.. wait til they get to the middle part of the meat though, as it does tend to be dry near the end. They do have roasted duck in the asian section but it goes fast, so try to get it it as soon as it comes out.
Overall, pretty great buffet. Expensive... but what isn't in Vegas? =P

This buffet is huge!! Everything I tried was ok, but nothing really knocked my socks off and it's really expensive. $300 for 4 of us! If you're a big eater this is probably the best buffet you can get on the strip, but we're not so it's kinda a waste of money for us.

#1 Buffet in Las Vegas for a good reason! Good service with interesting varieties of delicious food. My friend and I spent a good 2 hours of eating to find one surprise after another. I want to come back for more because apparently I missed some items to try. Eating at a nice buffet in Vegas is the good life!

Overall, everything was appetizing, fresh, and delicious. There were some highlights and few, minor twilight. I didn't get to try everything I wanted but I still enjoyed my meal. My best tip for first timers is to get a brief tour from the waiting staff/host to know where everything is (someone mentioned alligator meat, I gotta come back to try!).

Highlights: 
The fresh oysters, shrimp n' grits, lamb chop, sweet potato tater tots. The oysters were so rich and delicious, the lamb chop was marinated and cooked to perfection, the sweet potato tater tots were some sweet, delicious surprise because it was glazed with either honey or maple syrup. My favorite desserts were green tea mochi icecream, pistachio souffle, macaron, and thai tea gelato (YEAH THAI TEA)! I enjoyed drinking horchata and mango juice that were offered by the mexican selections. 

Tip on souffle: 
After you order the souffle, best thing to do is set an alarm on your phone for 10 minutes. (It's all about getting it out at the right time for delicious souffle) You want to get the proper timing and best result for the souffle. The people working on your souffle won't forget your face in 10 minutes so just be sure to remember to pick it up and add icing! Pistachio was delicious!!~

Twilights: 
The few things I didn't like or did not find special were the chef special fish and prime rib. I thought the chef special fish was not so special, it was very bland to me. And the prime rib was overcooked and did not melt in my mouth (I definitely prefer Wynn's prime rib more).

You're most likely going to have a good time eating since you're paying $50+. Another tip about these kind of buffet is eat very few stuff that you eat often (to me, Chinese/Asian food), much more of what you hardly eat (like oysters, lamb chop), and try 1 or 2 dish that can be new to you (like alligator meat).

Long story short.....
You are basically paying for the all you can eat seafood part. And that.....was delicious. So why only 3 stars?

For $60+ per person, I would prefer meat that doesn't have gristle and as dry as a bone. Mashed potatoes were cold, and the mac and cheese wasn't the best. If you want an "upper class" buffet in Vegas, I guess you'll be happy here. (Stick to the seafood).

Otherwise, I'd rather use that money to lose in the casino, as opposed to a meal that, despite the plethora of options, actually had me dissatisfied...and somewhat hungry (and I'm skinny). Probably won't be returning any time soon

Bacchanal Buffet was recommended by family and friends so we decided to go there after an all morning and afternoon pool day. The heat outside and the tiring pool day got us really hungry so we made this a priority. 

Tips: We came here and got seated around 2:15 PM and paid the Brunch price of $39.99. The buffet transitions into Dinner selection ($54.99) at 3 PM, so we got to experience dinner at a lesser price.

Food: B
-The food was not bad nor great. The selections are in good variety considering its price. The best sections were the meats and taco section where I kept coming back for more
-I enjoyed the Dessert the bar the most since I have a sweet tooth yet very picky with desserts. The ice cream selections included more than 10 flavors and included a variety of selections.

Service: A
- Our server was very nice and polite. She refilled our drinks even before it was finished. Our server also ensured that our plates were already out by the time we came back with our new plates.
-Note: You pay the price at the counter but does not include the tip for the servers. Don't forget to tip your server before you leave =)

I'm giving a four star because the food was alright but overall the service was excellent.

My party (10) and I arrived at around 5:30 pm on a Sunday. The wait time for 1-5 people was pretty long, about 65-90 min, but because we had more than 5, we went in a separate line where our group would be charged an automatic gratuity. We only waited for about 20-30 min and a dinner buffet for one person including tax & gratuity was ~$75. 

I've been to Wicked Spoon before and I have to say, I enjoyed Bacchanal a lot more! The food variety is greater, the quality of most of the food is great, and our server was so sweet!

If you like king crab legs, this place is a must! There are cold ones and hot ones. The hot ones are on a different side, and you don't need to bring them any to heat up. They already have it boiling in pots. The tacos are freshly made in front of you and the quality of the meat is delicious! I also recommend the prime rib! :) 

I wish they had salmon sashimi/sushi, but all they had were rolls. They did have a sashimi salad on the side though, which was really good. As for dessert, the crepe and green tea cake was so yummy!! 

And as always, never get too much of one thing because it may not taste as good as it looks... 
I highly recommend this buffet if you're in Vegas. It is pricey, but I don't mind paying the price because depending on what you eat, it's worth it.

One of the best buffet dinners I had out in Las Vegas although the food was great the wait to get in was incredibly long it took me around two hours to get in but that's because the food was way much better than the other buffets out there. They stop service at 10 so if u want to good id suggest going around 6:30-7:30. My bro and I went around 6:30 and didn't get in till 8:30. We originally went the day before and we thought that 8:30 was a good idea because we thought since it was closer to the closing time there would've been fewer people however the wait was only longer and if we waited till the time we were able to go in the place would've been closed by then so I suggest you going in to expect to wait at least an hour thirty- two hours. Also if u wanted to skip the line it's an extra 55 dollars per person so you'd have to pay the original bill which is 55 dollars and another additional 55 to skip the line and tax.

Hands down, one of the best buffets in Vegas. The only downside is the long wait. If you're hungry, be prepared for a long wait peak long hours.

LOCATION: Inside Cesar's Palace. 

WAIT: As mentioned, always a long wait. My group of 8 waited for about 30 minutes to get seated but we came right around 6:30pm before the huge dinner rush. 

PRICE/ADMISSION: I came here for a Friday evening so the pricing was already weekend pricing. It was pretty pricey for each person for weekend dinner it was about $65 a person before tip and tax. 

BUFFET: Pretty large restaurant, meant for huge and small parties. We got a table right beside the seafood, so we were really lucky. 

BUFFET ENTREES: There were just SO much variety. It took me at least 5 minutes to just breeze through each station and I was just mindblown by the selection. There was all sorts of various entrees and dishes so much that I had to take a little of each item just so I could a bit of each.

I definitely recommend getting the prime rib, that was my favorite along with their wagyu. The bone marrow was okay only because I could barely scrape off any marrow. I wish I had room to try more of their other foods, I barely made it past all of the Chinese food. They were good, but I was sad to skip the tacos only because I wanted to make extra room for all of their steak cuts to make it my money's worth. I also really enjoyed the seafood here. The lobster claws are my favorite, you crack the claws open and a thick layer of the meat comes out. The snow crab legs were good too, but a bit salty. Add some lemon to balance it out.

BUFFET DESSERTS: I am such a dessert girl.  I knew I couldn't skip the dessert and I am so happy I didn't. My friend and I decided to share our items, we got a bit of everything. We love the coconut sorbet, it was the best. My favorite cake was the tres leches. It's so moist and yummy! Most of the desserts were really good, but those two were the true winner.

CONCLUSION: A new favorite of mine in Vegas. Definitely on the steeper side, but still worth trying out at least once in your life. The seafood is so fresh and delicious, the prime rib is so nice and juicy. I'm still dreaming of it as I'm typing this! I would probably come back here on a weekday if I can, just to avoid an even longer wait.

Enter this pantagruelic paradise, where all lust for food is satiated: from appetizers to desserts, passing through wild meat and tasty seafood, there is hardly anything left out that comes to your mind! Highest quality food for a buffet you can find, service was neat and accommodating, the price is reasonable (almost 60$ for dinner), everything was very well organized! The only thing I regret is that I can't dine there every night!

Wow!

Best buffet I have ever had the "button popping" pleasure of experiencing! Living in Vegas, land of the buffet, I have certainly seen my share of buffets. 

My biggest regret here is that I ran out of stomach for all the tasty items that were available! They have over 500 options for you at any given point in time! I tried to keep the portions small, so I could taste as many different things as possible, but after 3 plates,an awesome dish of Rigatoni, and some deserts, I had to throw in the towel.

Everybody seemed to be mobbing the Seafood and Meat stations, so I started out with some Asian and Italian. The peppered beef was so tender and juicy and the orange chicken so full of flavor! Chicken skewers were second only to a friends Mom who makes  it homemade. That being said, they were great! The Peking Duck was pretty tasty as well! 

They had these sliders there that were rdeiculously good, and much meatier than I first thought! I wanted more of those, but had to try as many different things as I could. A must for my next trip here(which will happen soon!) You could tell presentation is a high priority  for the buffet as well, making it feel more like an experience and not just like "just another buffet".

During one of my trips to stock up on more food, I was at the Italian "station" and commented to my friend that the little deep dish rigatonis looked good, but it appeared as though it may have been there for a few minutes. Just as quickly as the last word slipped out of my mouth I see a hand pull that dish back and a second later a fresh staeming one slid right back in its place! lol Oh hell yea! Now THAT is service aimed at guest satisfaction!

The deserts were incredible as well! I hate to sound redundant, but this place is truly impressive. They had a selection of unique and exotic ice cream flavors, including Strawberry cheesecake. I enjoyed Watermelon Mint, and it was mighty tasty! 

Table service was great as well, Whenever I got up and left the table for another trip to the buffet, I always returned to a clean table with dirty plates gone and drinks refilled! There was a little issue where my drink was ordered twice and forgotten, but considering everything else, and how packed the place was, I can certainly be understanding.

All in all, a great experience and when I have friends and family in town(which is quite frequently) I will use that as an excuse to come back here and try all those things I didn't have room for on this occasion.

5 stars and a double rainbow all the way!

Our 5th visit this year alone. Bacchanal is a def must every time we visit Vegas. Dinner was amazing once again. We especially loved the mushroom pizza, poke bowl, and gnocchi. Staff is always very welcoming and the stations are impeccably clean. P.S. Please bring back the fig and prosciutto pizza!

This is by far the best buffet I've ever seen. They had EVERYTHING! Located in Caesar's Palace, it is the most popular spot to eat. It's a little pricey but it's worth it. I recommend getting there early because the lines are usually pretty long. While I was there I indulged in the crab legs (a couple plates worth), prime rib, brisket, mashed potatoes and Mac and cheese. They have something for everyone. Tacos, Asian cuisine, sea food, raw seafood bar, Italian, pizzas, meats and a dessert section that will rival any bakery. If you're in Vegas and have a huge appetite, this is the place for you!

8 trips to Vegas, and I finally make it to Bacchanal, and it was just about everything I hoped for. The price is steep, with lunch prices comparable to other well regarded Vegas buffets' dinner prices ($34.99 + tax/tip for lunch), but even so I would come back here every time and not think twice.  As per usual, I came about 15 minutes before the dinner switch over (no line on a weekday afternoon), and got to try the best of both worlds at lunch pricing.  

Highlights:  The brisket, goodness, was the best brisket I have ever had.  I have yet to visit Austin, so I reserve the right to retract this, but it was the perfect combination of tenderness, smoke and seasoning.  Pad thai was also really delicious, and incredibly spicy, which I like.  Other fantastic offerings include wagyu beef sliders, peking duck, sweet potato and truffle tater tots, and rack of lamb.  In fact, a combination of all of the above would probably make my last meal if I face the electric chair.  The desserts were quite varied, from made-to-order ice cream sandwiches, cake pops, green tea creme brulee, crepes, shaved ice and every cake-y dessert imaginable, although I'm not sure anything was super memorable.

All in all, absolutely the best buffet I've tried in Vegas.  For comparison, I went to Bellagio's weekend dinner the following afternoon and it didn't hold a candle.  I make the cross-country flight to Vegas almost annually, and the chance to relive Bacchanal is one of the few things that entice me to keep the streak going.

The worst buffet I have ever ate in Vegas. The line wait for crab is crazy long. It spend me almost one hour to get crab legs. The food in here is just normal but the dinner is insanely expensive. Totally not recommended

Mama didn't raise no fool.

When you go to a buffet, you eat the expensive stuff first. Translation, sprint for the seafood and don't you dare eat a leaf of salad or eye a piece of bread. Love the king crab legs that are already sliced open for you, what does this mean for the eater? You aren't wasting your time cracking the shells (peasants) these shells are just open and the meat is laying there saying, "come and get it, big boy"... or something like that. Tip: Cold crab legs in front and warmer ones near the back of the buffet in the italian/asian area. Yes, there is another area, the first time here I completely missed it.

Another favorite is... gasp, pho. Say what? Pho at an American buffet? It works and it's great for those hangovers. Other excellent noodle broth options are tonkatsu ramen and udon.

Dessert: made to order crepes and the most succulent amazing chocolate covered strawberries.

I love you bacchanal, 637.

honestly i really can't tell the difference between buffets in vegas, but what i can tell you is that bacchanal is definitely worth the $ especially for the detail-oriented displays and the food is simply just top notch!

what i will come back for:
1)  efficiency / wait:  i love the check in and leave phone number thing, so smart, because why waste customers' time standing in line when the casino can maximize their profit and let customers shop, gamble, and continue to spend money!  because you can't possibly be spending money waiting in line!
2)  food:  duh.  honestly, all the food i love were ones that you can find at other buffet, but were just executed on point.  like mushroom pizza WITH truffle oil and the crepe station was to die for.  lol!  i think the seafood station could've been better with smaller / fresher oysters and bigger crab legs.  oysters were too big, crab legs were too skinny.
3)  ambiance:  very upscale.  we were first placed in the back of the dining area but was later switched to a table near the entrance and it was much better.  i love the modern decor and the dessert bar... DIE.

the price is super steep, but you really do get what you paid for.  i think $49.95 would be reasonable, but $57.82 (tax & tip incl.) was a bit difficult for me to hand my credit card over...  but nonetheless, i ate plenty of crab legs to justify the spending.
This is a wonderful buffet I strongly recommend if you visit Las Vegas to definitely come here for breakfast lunch or dinner it is well worth it.
Probably the best buffet on the strip. I just wish the price wasn't that high. $70 for a dinner buffet, but yea they probably got the best food. Can't deny it

4.5 stars!  BAM...my 200th review. Gotta give it to Bacchanal. 
What's a Bacchanal?  A drunken or riotous celebration. I can see this happening in my tummy!  Being the ever so hyped up Vegas buffet that has trumped Wicked Spoon, I had to try it for myself. For $50 and a wait of about 45 minutes (Saturday), was it worth the wait?  Yes - 80% and No-20%

QUICK TIP: 
--For an additional $15 you can get a "front of the line pass!" Hilarious how many people justified paying the extra fee.  "We are wasting our precious gambling time standing here,"  "awww that's nothing, lets do it,"  "time is limited in Vegas."  

******THE GIST*******
Your eyes will be on CLOUD 9 and your mouth will be salivating.  Your head will be going TOPSY TURVY deciding where to go. I recommend scoping out the place 1st.  See what you got coming at you and do a mental game plan in your head.  The food selection is HUGE. 

Although you may be thinking it's all about the quantity, this buffet has QUALITY as well.  Fresh seafood and meats. Crisp & colorful produce! The aroma of all the food is outstanding.  

MUST HAVES: 
--warm snow crab legs
--artisan cheeses and cured meat
--soufflés, gelatos and macarons.  

FUN DISHES:
--custom made tacos
--Asian noodle soups:  pho, udon, ramen....OOOOhhhh Laaa Laa.  
--chicken wings

***In all honesty try to taste a little bit of everything.  Buffet is sectioned off by cultural regions & theme:  Asian, Hispanic, Seafood, Desserts, Pastas.  A plethora of salsas.  It's pretty darn awesome. 

CON:  Price is a bit steep.  Realistically, it's hard to get your money's worth b/c you just can't stuff that much down.  Everything was good, but nothing stood out.  Except the desserts.  Our waiter was nice, but bit on the snail pace.   

***The BIG TIP: Go towards the end of lunch. This way you can enjoy both the lunch and dinner menu at the lunch rate.  I gotta try that next time. 

Bon Appetit.  Don't blame me if you can't button up your pants afterwards.

Been coming to Bacchanal at least twice a year since they opened and the food/service does not disappoint.
This post is specifically as to the tacos...Yes, tacos...(when I first saw tacos, I thought to myself I didn't pay $60 for tacos...I've been hooked from the first bite)
A couple of years ago the corn wheels that were served in the taco section were revamped to the american/bbq section...Simply not the same.
Today, 3-18-19, I mentioned that I missed the corn wheels to STEVE O. as he was making the ohh so delicious tacos al Pastor with pineapple...He made and personally brought the corn wheels to our table...Gracias STEVE O.
This place has bad food my friend got food poisoning and spent half the day being sick. Definitely do not reccomend this buffet

I love the place and food, however seafood selection is limited in weekdays, hopefully they should a variety of seafood to choose from.

Ferdie

The first time I would've given it 5 stars, but after visiting for the 5th time or so, I prob wouldn't go back. It's just ok. They also recently raised their prices. They have a pretty large selection, but I would say everything is mediocre taste wise.

It seems like with each visit to Bacchanal Buffet, my love for it dies a little.

My last visit in 2014 was not the best experience, but I still remembered the times when they first opened, and still hoped to catch a glimpse of that wonderful and delicious memory again.

So this Christmas 2018, on 12/27/2018, I decided to give Bacchanal Buffet a try again.

Long story short, we paid $120 per person ($75 for Buffet of Buffet and $45 for upgrade), we had: spoiled oysters full of sand, gravel, and broken shells, crab claws from the hot crab station at the Italian station (yes, we were given a plate full of claws), dry and chewy beef brisket, not so flavorful prime rib, great salad, and great gelato and dessert.

We cut our dinner short because half way through our meal we started feeling unwell.

We returned to our hotel room, and the rest of our night was a battle of the restroom with diarrhea and puking for the two of us.

Apparently we lucked out by coming to the buffet on a Friday morning at 9 a.m. There were so many empty tables I knew they expected many more people. When we left we saw the lines. However, the food IS awesome and there is so much. I don't know if anyone has ever left hungry... Not too much if you don't eat dairy, but we made it work.

Sweet sparkly baby Jesus is this place good. 
We made use of our Groupon deal for Sunday brunch, with a well worth it VIP line access and 2 free mimosas (which we upgraded to all you can drink). 
The food choices are not only extensive, but creative and well prepared. Standouts include the American wagyu beef, the cilantro lime oyster shooter, the roast turkey, and the lobster bisque. 
Service was attentive but not intrusive. When we expressed "I hope we're done in 2 hours (there's a 2 hour time limit), our server said-"don't worry about that. You're in my section and there's no time limit here". I won't report their name so they don't get in trouble :)
We made multiple rounds (after starving ourselves for a day and half in anticipation), and few things went uneaten on our plates. We positively gorged ourselves and loved every minute of it. 
Strangely enough, the desserts were rather "meh" for me. The only real standout was the lemon basil sorbet. I could eat that til I puke. Oh-and the sushi. The sushi offerings were lousy, actually. I skipped them. 
So in closing, by all means visit this buffet-but only with an empty belly. 
I'm so glad we went, and I'm sure we will eventually return-but with all the dining options on the strip not sure when that will be. The Wicked Spoon and Sterling Brunch deserve a shot too :)

This is the best buffet I have ever been to.  We went to breakfast (but intended it to be brunch) in order to avoid the crowds.  Be prepared to eat and eat and then eat some more.  There is an unbelievable amount of food and selections.  The only complaint is trying to figure out where everything is located.  If you want a certain kind of fruit you may have to find it somewhere you weren't expecting.  They seem to have it all, it's just spread in nooks.  Lots of small portions beyond your wildest dreams for breakfast.  I had fresh squeezed orange juice in my champagne.  I had red velvet waffles.  I had crème brulee.  I had churros.  I had eggs benedict.  I had skillet potatoes.  I had chocolate fudge cake.  I couldn't make it to the gelato...And all the food was wonderful, good quality, and freshly prepared.  I was impressed and stuffed.

The BEST Buffet in Las Vegas...BAR NONE!

The first time I was in Vegas, it was exactly about a year ago, Wifey decided to purchase the 24 hour All You Can Eat option, which included Bacchanal and several other places. Never again will we do that. Of course after eating here first, the rest of the buffet places were nothing compared to Bacchanal. 

The first time we where here, the line was so long I almost wanted to quit and go to another place. I was starvin' like Marvin. I'm so glad we stuck it out even though it was over an hour before we eventually made it inside. It was totally worth the wait.

I remember tasting the boiled King Crab Legs dipped in melted butter and I was blown away. Cold King Crab Legs is good, but boiled King Crab Legs is another level of flavor. The sweetness of the meat really comes out and the melted butter just gets absorbed into each nook and cranny when it's boiled. It also makes it easier to go down so you can pig out like a Sumo wrestler. 

I also had a taste of the Lamb Chops, and it was one of the best I've ever had. However, when we went last year, they only had a few Lamb Chops left as it was close to closing time. I also had one too many plates and felt like I was going to burst. 

So on our subsequent visits, we learned our lesson and strategized on how to attack this place. We picked what we liked and didn't eat too much carbs and fried food; the type of food that would quickly fill you up. So less is more, in theory. However, it's easier said than done. Actually applying it is so difficult with so many good options they offer. It's a cornucopia of everything that we should have in moderation. But that's not how a buffet works. 

The last time we were here, which was last week, I made sure to get the Lamb Chops first and I got that out of the way. (I got eight) We got a few more of our favorites to share and definitely a lot of seafood. We didn't leave too stuffed, but got more than enough to please our inner pigs inside us. 

You will definitely need to hit the gym or go for a long walk after eating here.

"As good as it gets?"  Dang tootin'!

Remember your ABC's? (No, not your ABC's from pre-school; I'm talking about the "ABC's" of the "Las Vegas prestiges" as far as the buffets are concerned - Aria; Bellagio; Cosmopolitan).  

You all know that the holidays can be a real pain in the tail as far as traveling is concerned:  Traffic on the freeway, even traffic off the freeway.  But that didn't stop me from getting what I wanted when I went to Vegas for the second time after I turned 21 five years ago.  Now, onto the "good stuff":

I heard (and read) from a lot of the media that the Bacchanal Buffet is supposed to be one of the top buffets in Las Vegas with fantastic food for the price.  And you know what?  They were right.  The lines were long (even for the Seven Diamond members), but the food?  No word to describe it.

Did you know that there was actually a LINE just for the crab legs?  Yeah, it was THAT good!!  Still don't believe me?  Try to grab about 6-7 crab legs on your plate with a lemon wedge and get back to me.  As far as the other types of "cuisines" went for this establishment, the Chinese ginger soup was hot enough to help soothe my throat, and the desserts?  TO DIE FOR!!!  

As for the others (food-wise)?  Well, you gotta try them first before you say anything. :)

This is my second time at this buffet. The initial line was 20 minutes long, the second line 10 minutes?, and the final line is 2-3 minutes? When we were finally seated, we were placed in the back by the Asian food. I love Asian food, so it wasn't a big deal. You are given a cloth napkin with two forks and a butter knife. The bathroom is towards the front, so make sure you use it before eating. Sometime it can be a long line.

Dishes I would recommend: I absolutely enjoyed the eggplant dish and recommend it for anyone who loves eggplant. The pork belly were also good. Get the fried pork belly instead of the stir fry one. The duck was delicious. The oyster tasted good with the lemon juice. There's even a pho option, which I didn't get to try. The other people who went with me did try and they said it was good.

Services: This place is very busy, hence the long wait line. During my visit, the waitress was kept busy and was more in the area towards the middle where more tables were visible. My table was hidden by the column, though within the view of the wait station. When I got my tea refilled, no new tea bag was given to me. It took a while before the plates were cleared from the table. Other staff were friendly and told me to take me time enjoying the food.

Busy food lines: The line is long where the lobster legs were given out. Be careful of the area in front of the staff handing out the lobster legs since it tends to wet and slippery. I almost slipped.

The prime rib line can also be long, too. Luckily for me, it was quick trip. I got the prime rib and Wagyu steak; they tasted delicious!

Food that didn't work for me:  I wasn't a fan of the salads I grabbed. (See pictures). The tuna poke bowl lacked flavor. I should have added a little soy sauce to it. The Mac and cheese dish was not good. I only took a small portion and most of the macaroni were dried up. There were 2-3 that were soft. I didn't like the clam dish. It tasted dry.

Overall, for a steep price, they have an amazing selections to choose from. I'm not impress by their overall services. If I can, I would give them an over 3.5 star.

All for the price of a little under $50:

- Seafood station. Spent most of my time here because, well, why wouldn't you?

- American station. Great tater tots and sliders.

- Asian station. Not terrible, but nothing exciting. They do have kalbi (Korean short ribs), which is appreciated.

- Italian station. Great pastas, decent pizzas!

Wish they had more salad options as my stomach was not too happy the day that I went, but yes, I would go back. I'd go back in a heartbeat.

Came here at 10am on Sunday with a large group and probably only had to wait ~30 minutes to be seated. By 1pm, the lines were similar to the lines I see in front Disneyland. Bacchanal is touted as the best buffet in Vegas and after watching a YouTube video of head chef Leticia Nunez's daily routine to keep Bacchanal running, I was excited.

Pros: 
-Seafood: Large variety of crab and shellfish with some coming pre-cracked. We made it just in time for a fresh batch of crab legs to come out. Perfectly salted, steamed, and displayed. Absolutely amazing. Oysters and clams tasted fresh. I prefer their plain shellfish instead of the other fru-fru seafood dishes other buffets put out. We ate so much crab that our waiter was shocked when he came to clear the table. 
-Meats: Love a good medium-rare prime rib and felt like a savage with my plate stacked high with slices. Smart to have the gravy/au jus come out of a dispenser instead of spooned from a communal bowl. 
-Sweet potato tater tots are so good. Crispy, sweet, and addicting
-Fresh crepes made in front of you at the dessert station. You get to choose from a variety of toppings. My favorite part of the desserts. Also enjoyed their gelato.
-Asian food: My friend, who's from the San Gabriel Valley, took one bite of their xiao long baos and said it tasted like home. That's how good it was. I was so impressed by the taste of their dim sum. The XLBs aren't very soupy, but the meat filling was spot on.

Cons:
-Tri-tip and wagyu beef very dry compared to the prime rib and brisket.
-Our waiter was very gracious, but with how packed that restaurant was, it did take some time for the dishes to be taken away.
-Creme brulee: It needs more burnt sugar. The bottom has the right consistency. But the best part of creme brulee is making the initial first crack through the caramel topping. Their topping is too lightly dusted.
-Dessert: Did not like their mousse desserts or baked/bread-type desserts. The pineapple upside down cake was okay. Rose cupcake did not taste like rose. The desserts that have a mousse texture (like the Thai tea and Ube cone) tasted sugar-free/not made from real milk.

Overall: What wins me over about Bacchanal is the attention to detail they have to the dining experience. Each "main" has accompanying sides and condiments (I ate my weight in guac). Beautiful presentation and uniqueness without sacrificing taste. Would definitely come back here for a group buffet.

I don't really know what I can add to the reviews except that they are indeed warranted. You can't go to Vegas without going to a buffet. It's just which one? Next time I go I will purchase the buffet of buffets which offers multiple visits over a 24 visit with an upcharge if you want to visit this buffet, but if executed well totally worth it.

We went during the middle of the week so we managed to escape any long lines. But they are organized for easy flow. The parking lot at caesars is a FAR trek to this buffet, and to offer a complaint paying $12 for parking on top of the prices was unreasonable to me. But I don't appreciate Vegas new wave of charging for parking anyway, for such a rich city it's just tacky.

Off my soapbox I go to the food. There was no crab while we were there which was my only food related negative. There's sooooo many options that you're not sure where to start. The food is quality, fun and good. I enjoyed the flavor. Our server gave us two drinks and a water to start, which made me happy bc I drink a lot while eating.

Don't leave without having dessert, it's a treat for sure. I loved the ice cream, I went back for more! And the lemon bars yummmmm.... see you next time!
What a great place to eat. So much variety available and such freshness on all of the food

Oh the choices!!!  This was definitely the best buffet I have ever been to.  I said down, took my time and did my best to try a taste from every station. Unfortunately, I did not succeed... but I got pretty close!  If I have to say something negative, the only thing I could say is that some of the food wasn't really hot or even warm for that matter but it was still tasty.  If ever I am back in town, I'm definitely dining here again!

Very Good not great anymore.   for it being the 2nd most expensive buffet in town for breakfast-brunch next to the sterling, both run by the same company, the sushi and asian selections were very lacking which used to be one of their strengths.  the carving station was truly exceptional, the beverage choices were also very well done but the sweets section also needs more help being out there literally on an island, it is not as special as it was a few years ago

As far as buffets go - this one was delicious. I got here at 10:30 and experienced breakfast and lunch. I really liked the multi-ethnic choices from American to Latino to Asian. All the choices were very well seasoned and prepared. You'll find everything you expect (seafood, steaks, etc). I thought the dessert choices were the weakness of this buffet - but they were still very yummy. Service was great and I found everyone friendly and enjoyable. Would revisit and recommend.

I have been here twice now the first time was dinner and the wait was 1 1/2 hours when we got in they had a great selection but as it got to 10 they stopped bringing out rib eye steak and the king crab legs weren't there also.  I would say the lamb chops were great and the sliders were awesome also.  The king crab legs are good if you can get them. The oyster shooters and on the half shell were good also they were from the east coast.  I like the dessert choices.  The service has a lot of improving to do but you can't expect much for it being a buffet.  

The second time we went was lunch time and there was no king crab legs, lamb cops or rib eye steak.  So or the price of 29.00 it wasn't worth it unless you stayed into dinner time then they brought out the king crab legs the lamb chops and the rib eye steak.

If I go again it would only be for dinner.

Today I invited 3 friends to join us for dinner. I goggled this Buffet and found several sites that gave it very good reviews but clearly stated the price started out at 35.99 and adults Sunday thru Thursday was 45.99$. This is false and misleading. Once the 5 of us were there I payed the actual price of 65.99 and as I left I asked to show the manager. When he finally showed up I showed him the articles and  he claimed it's not their problem. Didn't care.

Came here at 10:50 and was able to pay the breakfast price just before lunch prices started. WIN! 

There's a reason why there's so many 5 star reviews, THEY HAVE EVERYTHING. I was so overwhelmed, and I desperately tried to only take bites of everything to save room but I still couldn't try it all. This buffet is a definite must if you're on the strip!

Bacchanal Buffet ranks the number 1 buffet in Las Vegas, but it ranks number 1 buffet I've ever had in my life!

Cover photo prices are wrong, mon-fri lunch is $35.99.  But good food!  LOTS of seafood, prime rib, tri trip, sushi, pasta, pizza, salad bar, chinese, viet, and japanese.

When you eat at Buffets, it usually goes like this:

"Hey that's good!"
"Eh, that was ok" 
"Gross"
"Not bad!"
Alright...."

But at Bacchannal, everything was "pretty good!" I really liked the consistency.  The sea bass, seafood paella, ramen, truffle scallop potatoes, and king crab were my favorite.  I've never had a craving for any food when I go to Vegas.. (earl of sandwich is alright...) but I'm going to have a craving to go to bacchanal and try ALL the delicious food! :)
My second favorite Vegas buffet after Wynn's buffet. Bacchanal has lots of options, won't disappoint.

Came here on a Saturday morning around 11 am with some friends. The food was honestly so bomb. But I docked stars because of the service. Service is always hit or miss here. Unfortunately it was a miss during our visit. Our waiter was no where to be seen almost our entire meal. It took maybe 20 min (we were already on round 2) just to order some  mimosas and some waters. Luckily there are fresh juices around the buffet or else we would have been parched. Secondly, we literally had to bus our own table because our server was no where to be found to take our dirty plates. When he came by to bring our drinks, he saw our dirty plates and didn't bother taking them. We literally bussed our own table and walked our dirty plates to the dirty plate trays. We ate 4-5 rounds of food and our server was no where around to take our dirty plates away. Imagine paying top dollar at the best buffet in Vegas, only to have you clean your own table... 
I wanna love you Bacchanal, but you gotta work on that service.

Food is hit and miss, some Seafoods where good however, others not. Had so-so small crab claws, crab legs and the prawns, I think where tasteless, mussels w/sauce where good, the hot boiled crab legs where good, peeled shrimp was good. The Asian food was good, the cold cuts / cheese good. The prime rib was good, desserts good. However paying $140 for 2   people recently 9/23/19 is ridiculously expensive, last time was there in 2016, I paid $45 for each person and that was w/24 hour (Ceasers buffet pass included). Now not the pass  ($69  Ceasers pass) excludes the Bacchanal buffet? Honestly overall I will skip it in future, it ain't worth the money.
If you want Seafood buffet go to the (Silverton hotel casino) for $35 bucks and it's good w/ lobster tails. Advised by a Uber local born driver? Hope this helps, I'm a seafood lover and know seafood how it tastes but I ain't paying that kind money! For that kind of money I'll go to a Hi-End restaurant!

Review #125 - 2017

After hearing some pretty good things about this buffet, I was quite excited to hear when my cousin told me that he was planning to have his 50th birthday dinner here.

He's a Diamond card holder, whatever that means...but all I knew was I didn't have to wait in line when I showed up because he already made reservation for a party of 20+ in the back of the restaurant.

The place is huge so they have a very wide selection, ranging from seafood to prime rib to Japanese to Italian.  The only downside is that when there's too many selections and they're all just ok, it gets kind of disappointing.  I always believed in quality over quantity.

Honestly, nothing actually stood out to me.  I'm always one to take lots of pictures of food, but I took one look and said, "I don't see anything that I'd actually come back for."  The only item that was even worth going back for seconds was the prime rib and the guy serving it was really stingy.  He cut such a small portion for each person that even the old man ahead of me asked him why he gave him such a small piece.

For $49.99 a person, I'd say skip it!  I wish we'd gone to the Bellagio buffet instead.

A buffet that's considered this popular should learn customer service 101. Bucchanal decided to close off the entire buffet from open to 1PM on a Sunday so they can suck up to their high rollers but they didn't think about the consequences. The communication was lacking so we were all told different things by different reps. First there was no communication whatsoever on the closure of the buffet until we get there and get turned away. Upon getting turned away we were told to come back at 1 and that those with VIP passes won't have to worry about lining up. 

Well guess what? If you close off a buffet on a popular day for 6+ hours and tell everyone to come back at 1 and not to worry about the lines, then the whole world shows up at exactly 1.  Not only did the massive crowds become an issue, we all received incorrect/conflicting information on where/how to line up. People were told to step out of "line" to go into another line that ended up being incorrect. The "lines" formed were a massive blob of people who end up cutting in front of one another because we were all told different things. There were people who lined up for a long time and ended up having to line up again because they were in the wrong line. 

I ended up calling Dirk the buffet supervisor and he did not seem to care. In his words, "you can always come back another day." He did not sound apologetic and just wanted to get me off the phone. For those of us who have been waiting around since 8am it would have been a 6+ hour wait. Would I want to come back again after waiting this long? Also many of us had purchased a VIP fast pass which ended up being useless because we had to wait another hour anyway. Isn't that the same as the normal line if you were to get there earlier? Oh wait, we couldn't do that because Bucchanal wanted to close unannounced....

This is poor experience, and if Caesar cares about customer service at all, I would like someone (even Dirk) to respond to this post.

Tonight I want all of you tonight
Give me everything tonight
For all we know we might not get tomorrow
Let's do it tonight at...BACCHANAL BUFFET! - Pitbull (give me everything)

It's been a long time coming but I finally got to try this place! I'm not a big fan of waiting in line for buffets and Bacchanal (part of Caesars entertainment group) is the only buffet in Vegas that I can't get a front of the line pass for (we had a falling out on my part about four years ago lol) The day finally arrived and it was already confusing lining up here. You take a ticket and you can come back when they text you, but the line that you come back to looks like the same line that you would wait in line for even if you didn't take a ticket? Sigh I was so confused LOL

Foods that I was looking forward to:
1. prime rib - it was alright but couldn't find horse radish sauce and also was the only meat at the carving station that I was interested in
2. sweet potato tater tots - oh oh oh haha the only buffet that I know of that has these tasty treats
3. warm crab legs - they serve it to you and will give you as much as you want, we had a lot of these!
4. dessert - the cake selection was a little disappointing and the macarons were really too sweet

Foods that I hoped to like but didn't:
1. taco bar - cool concept with a chef making it in front of you but the meats were salty
2. fried rice - so sad if you mess this up, thus i was so sad
3. dim sum - they do not have an asian chef back there, I'm convinced!

Foods that surprised me:
1. fresh juices - I wanted fresh watermelon juice but it wasn't in season; there were like 6 to choose from and I tried like 3 of them and all good, including mango and strawberry
2. ramen and udon - you feel almost silly to fill up on noodles at a buffet but these had great texture
3. congee - add in the egg and it was flavorful

I think this is a buffet that's still worth trying if you've never been here before. The food selection is diverse (I think I expected more) although you would probably only go back for seconds for a select few. I was disappointed that dessert wasn't up to par with Wicked Spoon or the Wynn. Even if the ladies are disappointed with any buffet, at least they'll leave happy if the dessert is yummy...
This place is phenomenal! Soup, asian, meat station..they have it all and no short cuts taken here. The food is prepared using fresh ingredients and there is so much to choose from! Worth the $$$.

Best buffet in Las Vegas NO DOUBT!!! Talk about great quality food at a great price. If you come here and have Diamond or better status with their Total Rewards program, you get this nice little black card which entitles you to different drinks, food and get to bypass the 2-3 hour wait line. YES of course we were Diamond status lol. 

First they have horchata which is great and refreshing. If you're Diamond you get unlimited Mimosas so you can get pretty tipsy early on. 

The main entrees are amazing. Crab, Chinese, pizza, Italian, seafood and 6 different types of meats. Tritip, top sirloin, primerib, wagyu beef, chicken and couple kinds of sausages. They also have a Ramen and Pho station if you feel like Soup. 

CRAB!!!! On the main line there's snow crab legs and blue crab. BUT....again if you're Diamond and above and have the little black card on your table....waitress brings out Dungeness Crab legs to you and OMG is it good. There was 3 of us and it's enough to feed 6, but of course we had seconds. We made sure there was no carbs when we ate hahaha!

Also the dessert station if off the hook. They have gelato and sorbet and different kinds of mini cakes, candy, donuts and other stuff. 

Hope to come back to Vegas in a couple years and bring the rest of the family to come check this place out. GET SOME!!!!!

A must try Vegas buffet when you stop by the city! The rave here is REAL guys!!!

Prices here can get expensive, especially on weekends but it really is a buffet you must try once in your lifetime. Good buffets with great quality food are hard to come by!! The line to wait will get long, only dandy thing is that you can leave your name, phone number, and number of people at table down and they will call you when your table is ready (usually the wait is 2 hours) BUT you can pay $15 to cut the line and go inside.

I was really hungry by the time I came so I just paid the extra $15 and headed inside the eat. First thing, the place is so nicely decorated! Second, free unlimited mimosas!??? WHAT!??? 

Okay, back to the food. SO many varieties! Steamed crabs!?? Mussels?? Oysters??? Egg tarts, flan, and so so so much more. I was already full looking at all of the food. To feel like I got my money's worth I mainly ate seafood so sorry guys I don't know what the meat quality was like but it looked good! The crab legs was AMAZING. Get it steamed!!!
