The mussels were like heaven in my mouth and oysters were bommmb too. The desert area was also my favorite as they provided so much and you can request for some item fresh like the egg tarts!

I really like this place but don't think I can afford to come back here anytime. It was a great experience and I got to say I enjoyed a high end buffet. 

I recommend:
- Oysters
- Flan
- Egg tart
- Mussels (the ones with two shells)
- Shrimp (HUGEEE)
- Crab legs (steamed)

3+ hours wait on Saturday night, worth it? I rather spent less money, less time to wait, scarify little bit less variety of selections, and spend the nice and enjoyable evening with my family in other buffet. 

We arrived at 5:45pm, and got our ticket for 1 hour 20 minutes wait. We walked and shopped around inside the hotel, and returned to be told to line up for another 1 hour wait for the payment & table. 

We ended up spent 2 hours 15minutes to get our table after 1 hour 20 minutes. Total 3 hours 35 minutes wait, and over $250 for our family. 

We enjoyed the snow crab, fresh oyster, shrimp, prime rib, bone marrow, seafood paella, a few sushi, a few Chinese dumpling, and dessert. However, we are dead tired after the wait, and we lost some of our appetite. Kids were sleeping in the couch after they finished their only bowl of undon (kids are half price, and the bowl is probably $35 worth it).

I should have reread the latest reviews before coming back here. Seems they have really disappointed quite a few patrons within the past month--ourselves included. 

Let me start by saying, "this USED to be my absolute favorite buffet". We had been coming back for the last 7 years, and alas, dinner last night was the LAST time we will ever return. I swore by this buffet! You guys had the BEST presentation, used to have unique and tasty options, used to have fresh food, fast service, and a friendly staff. I'd say it was an off-night, but this off-ness seemed pretty consistent in the past 23 days. Yep, I went through reviews this morning and was surprised to read so many bad ones...

Also, We arrived around 8:30, yes, towards the latter end of a typical dinner service...but pretty early for Vegas times. We were told the wait would be 15-20 minutes--it was closer to 45 as we watched them seat multiple parties of 3-4 (who arrived way after us) get seated first. You can see how frustrating this would be to any guest who has already paid, tipped, and been patiently waiting...

Brian, what happened? I truly hope you read these reviews and change your restaurant for the better. I feel cheated out of my money and my time.
The best buffet in Vegas. Many options and very clean. Really good service. Yes, it's expensive but well worth it. If you want the ultimate buffet you must go to Bacchanal.

After a day of outdoor activities, we happened to walk by this place.  We werent dressed for  anything fancy so we decided to come here. It was a little pricey but it was a weekend during dinner time and we were starving.  Based on that, this is my favorite seafood buffet. The had american italian , asian, dessert, lines that went on forever.  It was a workout o get from end to the other
This is what I had. A lot of crab, Sashimi(didnt eat the rice) prime rib, shrimp, calamari, ribs, oysters, scallops. I didnt not touch any bread, rice, mac n cheese, pasta. Blah! Forget that give me the good stuff!! I saw someone getting rice porridge. I said to myself" WHAT A NOOB" why pay all that money for water and rice. I definitely left happy.  when you walk in you see a display case of caviar, I  was looking for the caviar line, but then the waiter said itw as a couple of hundred of dollars.  What?!?!? No free caviar, then why are there cans of caviar the second you look at this place!! 
One definitely eats really well when you have a good day of working out. I must of had plates and plates of crab shells. It was a graveyard for crabs on my table. lol! there were two types, one that was hot an boiled and the cold one. I thought the crab that was in the pot was a bit salty, so I just ate the cold one. The sashimi was just ok.  Didnt eat a lot of it. Prime rib as above average.  Oysters and scallops- cant go wrong!!! I just need someone to pay for my next meal there.... hmmmmmmmmmmmmm!

This buffet is awesome. Lots a variety and reasonable prices   Have lots of deserts    The waitress Kathy was so nice and friendly. even they the place was super busy yesterday they still had so many choices no food running out

Went here on Saturday 8/11/2018 for a birthday Lunch. We arrived at around 2:15pm, logged into the kiosk & was advised the wait was about 30 minutes. We walked around about 12 minuets & was texted to come back. We were surprised we were in, seated in about 20 minutes. Thumbs up!! This place was delish!!! Everything I had was hot, flavorful & very good. I have no complaints at all. I took a spoonful of everything I wanted to try & it was all good. The desserts I tried was a crepe with bananas foster, mango monchi, & strawberry gelato. I will be coming back & I think it's worth the money.

We had an enjoyable experience here at Bacchanal. My husband was happy to find a good variety of cheese on the counter which included local and international selections. There were numerous seafood available on the counter which were fresh and nicely presented. The Mexican food station was also exciting. I saw the "posole" and I was happy. Both the American and Asian food station did not fail to impress us. Those prime rib and korean bbq ribs were irresistable.  Did I mention that the dessert station was mouth watering? Those lollipops were cute and lovely on the outside and tasty on my mouth. I also enjoyed those gelato and the toppings they have available. Tiramisu! What? Where? Yes on the dessert station next to many other yummy sweets.

The bright, modern and spacious decor of this place provided an enjoyable dining experience to us. I cant speak enough how much better this place is compared to the Wicked Spoon. Lucky for us that we came here on a Thursday thus we did not have to wait. The price was not cheap but definitely well worth it.

Pretty sure the seafood here is what gave me food poisoning, but that's Vegas baby. However, overall this place is overrated. I've eaten at plenty of other buffets in Las Vegas, and I thought that the food at this one would blow me away because of the price you pay to eat here. The quality of the food was really only a little better than the $25 buffets I'd eat at in Vegas. 

I'll be saving my money and eating at my usual spots next time. 

I will say that my favorite food here was the meatballs, very tasty.

I have tried The Buffet at The Wynn, Wicked Spoon and this is definitely the best one.  Similar price to the other two but you do get more selections.

Lots of seafood selections with fresh oyster, cold and warm crab legs, crab claws and many more.  They also offer small plate dishes like sea bass and salmon.

Chinese section offers really good choices, way better than what's offered at The Wynn and Wicked Spoon.  Really loved the black bean crabs, lots of meat in the crabs!  They have dim sum as well as congee.

Loved their selection of juices in glass jars, I tried their carrot juice and I can say it's pretty real juice.

Let me tell you this, every section of this buffer offers more and better selections than those at The Wynn and Wicked Spoon.  

You gotta try this at least once if you're in Vegas.  The selection is so huge that I can't possibly go through everything here in this review.

Those CRABS were super delicious. There's a large selection of other foods that were really good. I do wished the BBQ and prime ribs were more tender than I would like. Lots of dessert options to choose from with the perfect portion that I was able to try a lot of them. 

I would definitely recommend this buffet to go if you're hungry only if you are fine with the wait. It's a little pricey, but totally worth it if you have a empty stomach.

I was very impressed the first time I tried this buffet despite the long wait on a Saturday night. I loved the Oysters, juice bar, and variety.

However on my second time here, I had lunch on a Friday afternoon, I was mildly disappointed. Dinner is much better than lunch. Lunch was still over an hour's wait at noon. Instead of waiting, I opted to pay $25 extra per person for their express line, which isn't really an express line. It depends on how big your party is and availability at the time. If the food were good, I wouldn't care about the slight wait or price over charge. But it wasn't nearly as good.

The salmon sushi wasn't super fresh. I know you aren't suppose to expect that but when you get better ones at a buffet that is half the price, you would be a little unhappy.

There are no Oysters or crab legs for lunch. The stone crabs were ok according to my husband. The desserts were ok. The fruits were not sweet.

The only thing I really enjoyed were the red potato salad, Tri-Tip, and prime rib.

Went on 1/29/19 around 11:45am no line the price was reasonable once you see the food they have. Got seated quickly and drinks were taken right after. 
Buffet food was great. First plate was breakfast Colorado eggs, breast sausage and spicy sausage with a piece of prime rib. And a bowl pozole. Everything was prep and had a good taste. Second plate was pizza, prime rib, steak and egg and fried chicken with a piece of waffle. The pizza was decent, steak and egg was good a bit dry on the steak, the fried chicken was ok generic chicken. There was no syrup near by but can't complain. The pozole was so good and being Hispanic I'm really picky but went back for seconds. I saw the sign for menudo but couldn't find it. Overall the buffet is worth the price. Staff is friendly and the wait staff makes sure to check on you
Sorry..I know this place is great but it's too damn expensive.  Strictly meant to snag the one time tourists.

By far the best buffet in Vegas!! A must stop, with a TON of variety.
Located in Cesar's palace hotel.

To start off, the wait time wasn't too bad. Lines are extremely long but they move quickly. You pay up front and its all you can eat. It was about $50ish dollars per person. Also, there is a photographer while you wait in line, and the picture is $20 a pop for 1 large and 2 small included in a small paper frame folding thing.

There is everything here! Seafood, asian food, soups, meats, drinks, and the finest desserts. 
They have crab legs, sushi,mashed potatoes, creamy soups, even dim sum omg. What don't they have really? Come here hungry, and try everything. 

The desserts are what really make this buffet stand out. They have neatly crafted carrot cupcakes, macarons (which are expensive!), and melt-in-your-mouth cakepops,etc!

Think of this buffet like a high school cafeteria. It will be long lines for all the rows of food on display. You grab a plate, and you get in line, pick and choose. Everything is neatly labeled to know what it is. 

The staff is attentive and friendly.

I take one star off because there is no menu for regular drinks so you just have to guess what you want, or ask the waiter at the top of their head. Also, this place is a maze and its easy to get lost and confused to find your table. It doesn't help that its dimly lit and everything looks identical left and right. Other than that, this place is the best buffet I've been to. Not just in Vegas but in anywhere!! Gogogo.

This restaurant was one of the experience that made my Las Vegas trip beyond awesome! The seafood is super fresh and the foods are amazing. You will be able to taste food from different cuisines with high quality. Oh let's not forget about a variety of desserts that one could possible get in the entire planet. This is the BEST and MUST buffet to go to in Vegas. The line is long but don't be discourage! It totally worth the wait and the money. I would come back to this buffet every time I visit Las Vegas again and again!

This is HANDS DOWN the best buffet in Vegas, better yet, the world! They have soooo much to choose from, literally ANYTHING you can think of. My lady and I went here a couple months ago and we were blown away. My favorite thing about this buffet - HUGE king crab legs, hot or cold. The best part about their crab legs is they cut them in half so you literally just pull the meat right out and drench in lemon butter, no time wasted making a mess trying to crack them open! Their dessert selection is incredible!! My favorites were their macarons and the fresh made gelato. 

This is the most expensive buffet I've ever been to, I believe it was $60/person. BUT, it is soooo worth it!! Money well spent if you ask me.

Whether you're a Vegas local or a tourist here for the weekend, you MUST go here if you're looking for the best buffet possible!

How much would you pay for a popular & busy buffet with hundreds of quality choices?

   A: $54
   B: $74
   C: $94
   D: Anything ... just let me in the freakin' buffet already

Be prepared to pay any of those prices at Bacchanal Buffet cause this is the current "It" buffet in Vegas. Caesar's Palace can pretty much charge whatever they want. The line is KuRAAAYzeee. We tried to go for dinner Monday before Christmas and the line was 3 1/2 hours long. That's over 200 minutes. We read on Yelp about an "Express" option for $20 extra, but it wasn't available that night. We left.

So, we came back on Christmas Eve for a late lunch. The set-up was different and line much shorter ... because it was a 25-minute line to put your name in for a time slot 3 1/2 - 4 hours later. The registration part is cool if you can wait. I can't. Luckily, the "$20 Express" option was available at that time. Whew! Seriously, I would of paid anything to skip the wait. So, after paying $74 for lunch per person, we headed to ... the next line. It took another 25 minutes to get seated with express. 

      This better be one hell of a buffet!

            It was.

Bacchanal Buffet really is a great buffet. It is, of course, overpriced and hardly worth the wait, but if you want quality and choices like this in Vegas you have to either pay for it or have the patience of a very bored saint to stand in line. When you do finally get into Bacchanal, go nuts on the seafood and meats so at least you feel like you're making it worth your money/time.

The price is fair a higher quality of grub, lots of choices 
To pick from. The only problem is after tasting all the goodies your belly blows up and you have to walk i

Buffet was really good

If you come around 10:15 you get breakfast and they are putting out lunch

One of the top buffets in Vegas everything is always fresh and delicious

Despite this being rated as the top buffet in Vegas, we couldn't help but feel that it's overrated and overpriced. We got the early bird dinner Groupon and even with the express passes still ended up waiting over 30 minutes to get a seat. We also had to ask several times for our waitress just to get some water. The food was mediocre and the oysters left much to be desired. Most patrons were eating plates piled high with crabs and going back for more, but even the crabs we're just ok. The best part was the dessert area, but it wasn't worth the cost of admission. Would definitely try a different place in the future if looking for a buffet.

Wow !! Fantastic experience. Second time visited and very happy with the service by waitress Sandra's & her attentiveness to keep us happy. Will recommend to all my friends and family and everyone seeking to get spoilt in Vegas!!

This was my first Vegas buffet experience and it did not disappoint. There are a wide variety of selections from sushi to prime rib. My partner loves Asian cuisine so we were pleasantly surprised of their selections which included dim sum, ramen and mini poke poke bowls to name a few. Definitely save a little room for dessert. There are a plethora of mini desserts as well as a crepe bar and gelato station to satisfy your sweet tooth. Everything was delicious! I only wish that I had brought my second stomach so that I could enjoy it even more.

This buffet has significantly gone down hill since I visited 4 years ago. The quality of the food has significantly gone down. They used to serve rack of lamb but no longer. Much of the food was cool to Luke warm. Save your money and goto one of the many nice restaurants around the strip. I won't be back. Especially considering I had to wait over an hour for the privilege of eating their low quality offerings on a Thursday night.

I give this buffet 4.5, but rounding up since I can't give half stars. The flavors were amazing here. Even something as simple as scrambled eggs was absolutely delicious. We loved the variety of carved meats and the desserts were very tasty. I would continue to go here based on the flavors and food quality alone. My only complaint was that some of the items were cold. We were there pretty early into breakfast/brunch, so I would expect things to still be warm. If they could discover a more effective way to keep the food warm, this buffet would be perfection!

It looks nice located in Ceasars Palace which is a nice hotel/casino. The buffet apparently is also very popular. So popular that even though you get told that it will only be a ten minute wait you will wait closer to 40 mins just too ser the podium at the front of the line. 

The problem lies in the fact that there are three other "exclusive"  lines that you can only get access to if you gamble a lot so you will get skipped a lot by the VIP's which there will be a LOT. A LOT. 

Getting a refund was also not fun becase there is only one guy Fred who has to swipe his card like six times to issue a refund and that had to happen for both me and my friend, and fred keeps getting pulled away from doing the refund to do something else. Really (Kevin Hart voice ) annoying and time consuming it took almost as much time to get the refund as we had stood in line.  

So good luck. Dont go when your hungry. Make sure you Cell is fully charger and maybe pack a snack you will be there a while.

Lastly its already a lil pricy 54.99 for dinner but apperantly there is a price hike of 20 bucks that happens on holidays that is not advertised or told to you till your paying.  Also the normally included beer and wine that comes with the buffet will now cost you 27.99 with tax its about 100 plus to get in and thats before the line.

But its supposed to be good and thats what the food hunt is supposed to be about. Happy Hunting.

Enjoy.

This is definitely one of my favorite buffets on the Las Vegas strip. The buffet is in Cesar's so the atmosphere alone is amazing. To be a buffet I didn't find the establishment obnoxiously loud or anything. When you first pay they give you a 2 hour limit so I HIGHLY suggest making sure you take your time and get a bit of everything. My best friend and I went at around 11 and we surely did not leave until 1 and tried every section. There is a large Asian food section with everything from fried rice to dumplings and the rice was phenomenal. They even had smoothies and a ton of delectable desserts. We decided to try a bit of everything and while some things exceeded our expectations others fell short. The dessert table, however, did not disappoint in even the slightest way! If you are going you much have the bread pudding and vanilla ice cream, it is truly to DIE for. Also their banana fosters was amazing, I'm so glad they even had it as a topping for ice cream or even crepes if you wish. This buffet is a bit pricey but well worth it and they also had an amazing seafood section with shrimp, lobster, and crab legs. If you're looking for an amazing buffet go to Caesars Palace and try this place out, you will not be disappointed.

I read the reviews, I heard yummy things about Bacchanal but Oh My Gooood Greatness!!! We ate delicious, non run of the meal food until we darn near passed out!  

We were in Vegas for my bday and hubby and daughter took me here for dinner. We waited in line for aprox 30 mins but it was fun passing small talk time in line with other patrons. Next thing we know, we were greeted and seated and left to our own self destruction.

So much yumminess in one huge place! I tried not to eat the "common" foods, you know, fried shrimp, chicken, casseroles OH NO!!!! Instead I went in on the Oysters, Pho, King crab, and delectable desserts.  Daughter purchased the drink package for which we enjoyed bottomless wine and champagne.  Yes, Yes, YES!!! 

So what are you waiting for, Go ahead and eat for yourself. You wont regret it.

While this is not the biggest buffet I have seen, this Las Vegas buffet does not disappoint due to all the food actually being pretty dang awesome! 
I wanted to give this place 5 stars, but the service just wasn't up to par. My water glass was completely empty twice. 
Everything that others have said is true - carving station serves juicy meat cut right in front of you (prime rib!). The shrimp were huge and took at least 2 bites to finish. Their crab legs are cut in half and make it that much easier to enjoy the food. There's a meat & cheese pairing section. The bite size chicken marsala was full of flavor. Desserts are off the chain and they serve Mochi balls (a favorite of mine). 
Some tips:
Lunch cost $82 for 2 people (that's including tax). $15 per person for unlimited house wine, beer and/or mimosa. 
You do wait in line and also wait to be sat at a table. We waited about 30 minutes total. 
There is a 2 hour limit.
We came for Sunday brunch. Pretty decent food, and not a bad wait either. Lots of selection as well.

This buffet was awesome!!! I recommend going during the week though, especially if it's a holiday weekend. You'll be more susceptible to finding a coupon to combat the cost of M thru F prices asI went over Labor Day weekend this past Saturday. The wait was 2 hours!!!
We like to eat over here but last time we eat there is no snow crab leg thats why where kinda upset but over all is good

Paying an arm and a leg for a buffet one would expect nothing less than excellence from the quality of food to the service.  Although it's quite odd that there's actually a time limit to how long you can actually stay and eat...there's a cornucopia of food from various cultures to appease even the picky eaters.  Crab legs are always seemingly high in demand no matter where you go.  It's quite remarkable the never ending vast array of foods they serve.  Don't spend too much time wandering trying to figure out what to eat because you only have 2 hours to go on a guilt free gluttonous binge.  Bring sweat pants.

Of all the buffets in Vegas that I've tried, Bacchanal has got to be my absolute favorite. Come before dinner on the weekends (3pm) because I don't think paying more than $50 for a buffet in Vegas is worth it. Plus, the dinner menu might change, but you'll still be paying the lunch price. Now THAT is worth it in my opinion.

Dine at Bacchanal on a day that you don't plan on doing anything productive, mostly because all you're going to want to do is take a nap immediately afterwards. There usually is a 2 hour limit per table, but I've never had a problem staying longer and they don't really enforce this rule. 

Bottomless mimosas is available for around $15 and if you're nice to the server, more than likely they'll keep your cup filled to the brim everytime they come around. Fair warning though, you really won't be doing much eating if you and your friends are pounding down glass after glass, so proceed with caution!

My favorite station has to be the seafood station. I'm sure their menu changes from time to time, however they always seem to have oysters and crab legs on hand. Oysters are pretty good, although not the best, but that's typical for buffets. The crab legs are flavorful and sweet and paired perfectly with a touch of lemon and some cocktail sauce. They also have butter on deck, so that's a huge plus for me. Oyster Shooters and their Glazed Salmon were one of my favorite items!

Carving station has prime rib and it's cooked exactly the way I like it! Bone Marrow is also a favorite of mine although I don't think it's served all the time. Lamb is occassionally available and you must get it if you see it!

They have a charcuterie table with salami and cheese on occasion but I try not to fill up on those things. Mexican/Latin cuisine is available with Paella, Tamales and even Agua Frescas. 

The Dessert Bar has such a huge variety it's insane. Just when you think you're full, you take a stroll next to the dessert and immediately your stomach makes room for it. They have Panna Cotta, Gelato, Macarons, Flan, Tiramisu, Cakes, Cookies, you name it, the possibilities are pretty much endless. And if you're feeling it, they even have candy on hand as well. 

Things to probably avoid is the Chinese Food and Sushi, I don't recommend either of these. Neither of them look that appetizing or fresh and who goes to a Vegas Buffet to eat Chinese Food?

Overall, Bacchanal just keeps me coming back every single time, I absolutely love it here. The only thing that I have to complain about is the wait time so just plan accordingly if you do want to come here before they serve dinner.

Best buffet in town for a reason- it's the best. Most buffets have a few great options, a few solid options, and a few filler options. Not the case at Bacchanal. Everything is stellar here. 

Price is high because quality is too. Best bet is to go late for weekday breakfast. 10:15 or 10:30 is a good time to get breakfast pricing (and their bfast options are amazing!), but still be able to stick around a bit for some of the lunch dishes if you pace yourself.

Massive selection, from charcuterie and pizza to sushi and some of the best dim sum, fresh-squeezed bottled juices,  shrimp and Jonah crab claws, multiple types of Benedicts, and a whole host of Mexican and Chinese options. The dessert stand will blow your mind, too.

This was my favorite buffet and best buffet experience in Las Vegas during my last visit. It is indeed a lavish spread. 

My recommendation is to get the buffet of buffets pass / deal and then upgrade for $25 to have the Bacchanal for dinner at least once. 

First, the selection of foods is truly extravagant. On my last trip some of the more decadent dishes offered include - jonah crab claws, duck, pork belly, lamb, and bone marrow. 

*If you take the time to peruse the entire buffet before starting you can create a balanced experience and not miss out on unusual treats that you might not have expected.* 

This buffet has 9 different sections - including a massive selection of small plate desserts. There are always many unusual gelato flavors.

Second, the service on my visit was excellent. My waitress brought me extra water, crab cracking tool, extra paper napkins and an extra cloth napkin without being asked (she saw my first course was a heaping plate of crab claws, crab legs, and shrimp) and anticipated my needs! (That is some old school, quality service.) She was friendly without being obtrusive. I did not have to ask for a drink refill - not even once. She brought extra drinks and napkins a second time while I was serving myself a second plate. 

Third, the presentation of dishes is artful and carefully done here. Many of the menu items are served on their own individual plates and are garnished and creatively plated.

I am sure there are little tweaks and improvements with the food that can make the experience slightly better at times - but it seems like it is always an experience.

*What really cliched my 5 star rating was the excellent service. 

Highly Recommended.
Great food and desert. The pricing for kids should be less. My 5 year old ate a slice of cheese pizza and 2 ice creams for $32.00.  The line is a bit long too.

Expensive for a buffet but worth every penny,  love it Asian dumplings, crab legs, the man making crepes amazing,  exotic food you want to try but don't order Incase you don't like it,  shrimp, roast, and on and on the dessert can't imagine, gelato can't say enough save up and give it a try.

Food was great, 1.5 hour wait, paid $20 per person to only wait 1/2 hour in line in staed. Line to geat food was also long, buddy waited almost an hour to get carb legs and prime rib. Price i cant complain as our meal was comp due to a cockroach decided to join us for brunch. Moved us to another table, gave us front of the line passes for each of us (good for only 1 person). Manager brought our buddy a plate full of crab legs. He also over herd the manager talking to another saying that it wasnt the first time this has happened. If it wasnt for the roach id say its worth the $70.25 we paid initially. but after the roach i dont know. 1 roach means there are millions more hiding.

The one star is primarily because of the cost, which is far to high for what you actually get. The dessert spread and the pre-plated buffet items were very tasty but most of the food was cold and essentially unremarkable.  For some reason there were what appeared to be two bone chips in my baked stuffed potato, thought I broke my tooth when I bit down on them.

The service was also low marks from me. When we returned from getting our food there were drinks we hadn't ordered on our table so we let the waitress know and instead of just taking the drinks away and getting us water she proceeded to accuse us and two nearby couples of switching tables...which we had not. I've worked in service jobs my whole life and this was just weird.

If you win big and have a bunch of money to throw away, sure this could work.  The ambiance and decor are lovely, but they are not worth the wait time and price. We've had better for far more reasonable expense.

For $58 this was a COMPLETE RIP-OFF. What happened?! I had high hopes for this place
As I have heard great things. What a disappointment! EVERYTHING we ate you can tell was previously frozen. Crab was to frozen and watery, shrimp cocktail was mushy, crab claws were so hard you couldn't crack them, ramen was so SALTY, sushi was froze salmon and the rice..omg it was so gross like someone put water in the sushi rice instead of rice vinegar,Fried
Chicken was way over cooked like they hadn't cleaned the oil, then... The dim sum. You can tell those were super old the wrappers were falling off. 

The ONLY thing I liked was the warm crab (which is hidden behind a glass?!) and the creme brûlée. So much to choose from and yet everything I tried and everything my group of 6 tried WAS TERRIBLE! Omg and they serve wagu, and what a waste it was over cooked. I can go on and on at how amazingly disappointed I was and I was super exited to go here. PLEASE save your money and go to Wicked Spoon!

DIAMOND & SEVEN STARS No longer get KING CRAB served to their table. Not sure when they made that change but I was just there 4/4/19 during the dinner hours and 2 different staff members told me they no longer bring it to the table. 
Is this true? Could someone confirm this? 
·They still offer snow crab in the Italian section as they have been. 

I have a question for you guys: is the water here suppose to taste funny, like watered down white wine or Champaign? 
Every time (3x) they refilled my water... It taste and smelt like there was alcohol residue. I brought it to the staffs attention, he smelt it and agreed it smelt like alcohol. I found it weird that he didn't apologize for it. He just said, "must have been from the leftover...* Sniffs again & walks away to grab me another glass of water" .  
I'm staring at him like... Leftover WHAT?! 
Leftover from a slosh bucket? The next glass still smelt like alcohol, but not as strong as the first one. 

Look, I always and only come to Bacchanal because it was my favorite buffet in Vegas. I'm not tryna bash them but I feel they need to revamp and step it up. I came here 3 times this year already --mind you that I don't live here in vegas; I have to fly here. 

I feel bad for being so negative towards my (former?) favorite buffet, but the staff should ask you if you're done with your plate before removing it. We were using the plate for our snow crab trash and he just took away the plate in mid course. Now I have to walk over and grab another plate cause I have no where to place the eaten crab legs. The plate he took away wasn't even at the edge of the table... It was sitting directly in front of me and I was in the middle of eating. If I didn't have food in my mouth I would have stopped him or said something. --I was over it after THAT because this happened the last time I was here (Feb 2019) but I'm not explaining that story.  I don't see why they can't ask, "can I take anything out of your way / done with this one?" 

I would usually rate Bacchanal as a solid 4 but today's experience was a 3. 

Ok. I'm done.

I had some issues with this buffet about a year ago. My main point was that the food was not hot, or even warm. The manager reached out to me and offered a bogo to give them a second chance. We arrived just after seven and it was pretty busy. Our server was friendly and did her job. The food was fantastic!!  Everything I had was delicious and hot!  I'm so glad that I came back. We went to several buffets over the course of our trip and this was, by far, the best buffet in Las Vegas!!

My bf and I spent Thanksgiving '18 in Vegas because my family was out of town. We decided to go to Bacchanal for Thanksgiving lunch because he's never been and I loved it the last time I was there (back in 2015.)

Is it just me or have the quality declined? Maybe we went on a off day? Because everything we had was just so-so. The prime ribs were flavorless, chewy and many of the dishes were lukewarm. We really looked forward to gorging on chilled crab legs, but because they were super salty, we only ate one leg each. We tried the hot crab legs and they were also salty, but not as bad. 

The best things I ate was from the dessert table. This tiramisu coffee cup thing, creme brulee, gelato, and brownies were all very delicious. 

But come on, we paid almost $70 per person for holiday lunch pricing and waited three hours to eat. The desserts shouldn't be the best part of the meal. ;( I want to go back and give it one more chance, but I'm apprehensive. I will update my review if i do!

Pricey buffet but soooo worth it! The food was amazing everything was great! crab legs alll day!!! i would definitely come back the next time i'm in vegas!! We came on a Sunday, the wait was about 45 minutes long. No complaints at all!

I remember this buffet being better before, but the last time we went for my bachelor party, it was a huge let down, don't get me wrong it's massive and you can try to sample a little bit of everything.  However, most of the items just weren't good.  The only good items was the crab legs, the oxtail, and the desserts.  Beyond that most of the items was just awful.  The price point is really high too.

Our first time in Las Vegas and of course we want to try a buffet. We love to eat and Las Vegas is known for buffets. We did our research and we choose the Bacchanal based on other people's review and suggestions. Our expectations were very HIGH specially coming from Winstar World Casino's buffet to Sin City. We paid $70.00 per person and we included a $15.00 tip for our waiter. The total of the bill $155.00. For the price we expected something so amazing that would kick every buffet we previously attended off the map. Unfortunately, that didn't happen and we are bummed out to find out the food isn't that great. The variety of food wasn't much and the taste was not glamorous like we expected. I am not saying the food was bad but at such a high price it left a lot to be desired. One major disappointment was the iced seafood. If you like iced seafood then perhaps you may be willing to give this place a higher rating. We prefer our seafood hot or would just rather not have it at all. Maybe next time we will try another buffet but we will most likely not return here. 
At last I must add the our waiter was amazing. He cleared our table and refilled our drinks. He was on top of it.

I've had lunch here a few times and recently breakfast.  Every time I came out of this place full and satisfied!

Recently we tried the breakfast buffet when Sugar Factory let us down with their poor service.  Fortunately, we came around 830AM and there were no lines to wait in!

The food selection for breakfast was amazing.   The first section hosted an assortment of seafood type items including a variety of salmon, bagels, cream cheese, capers, etc.  along with clams/mussels/oysters.

 But the best part of the first section:  Crab Egg Benedict!  Huge pieces of blue crab, on top of perfectly poached egg, a sweet sauce, over what I think was a croissant. 

There were also shrimp and grits, and lobster on a biscuit in a spicier sauce.

The buffet offered the typical breakfast foods as well as mini-red velvet pancakes, chicken and waffles, and more.

Also, if it is your first time to this buffet, don't forget that around the corner of the buffet area is a whole other section with even more food!   It was my co-worker's first time there and they were already happy with the first half of the buffet.  When I told them there was another room of food they were wow'd!  

The 2nd area had assortments of cheeses, proscuitto, omelette station, salad bar, fruit bar, and then a whole chinese food section with soups, noodles, and dim sum!

Top it all off with their desert section: they have crepes ready to order, so much variety in deserts, and unique flavors of ice cream.  This trip I tried a coconut ice cream w/ real coconut shavings inside, and buttercream caramel.  Both amazing!  

5/5 would definitely go again and again and again!

It was my first time trying Bacchanal Buffet and I definitely had a great dining experience. I got there around 530-6 ish and there was already a long line. However the line moved really fast and we got in within 40 minutes. This place is definitely huge, it took me a while to finish walking around and figure what I want.

I started with the cold seafood section. King crab, oyster, shrimp and scallop. The crab was delicious, paired with butter they provided. They definitely have great amount of seafood selection. This section also had the longest line out of other food section. I had so much food so I cant really specify what I had. I also had they BBQ rib, surprisingly it was not as dry as buffet food rib. I also like their noodle soup section (of course...Asian) I had the udon soup. The soup was pretty good and the udon was definitely with the right softness. I was surprised that they had dim sum style snacks like dumplings. In their Italian section, there are different selections of pizza and pasta.

Now its my favorite part-dessert section!
They had crepe section where dessert chef make crepe for you. I had nutella crepe and I love it. It was still warm since they just made it for you.They have varieties of cakes, cookies which take me a long time to fit everything into one plate. I would definitely come back here if I am starving in Vegas next time!

It's been a while since I last went to Bacchanal Buffet.  The prices are a head-scratcher now since they only have 2 price options for brunch and dinner.  It's pretty messed up in my opinion but from a business sense I could understand why they're doing it since a lot of people usually came early for breakfast before and stuck around long enough for the lunch items, saving them money in the process.

Paying $40 for brunch seems almost ridiculous to me considering that just a while ago, dinner at the Wynn Buffet was $35.  At that price point, I really would rather just get a simple breakfast meal at Mon Ami Gabi or Bouchon.  Plus, I can't stuff myself silly as I used to when I was younger, so I really can't do buffets anymore.  Case in point, with this visit I only did 3 plates and called it a day.  But I definitely made sure that I got my money's worth.

First off, I made sure that I had plenty of cold pressed juices.  I think I had 4 bottles of their Hibiscus Berry Juice.  It was so refreshing and lightly sweetened.

On to the food plates.

1st Plate -- http://bit.ly/2kxIuTP
Bloody Mary Oyster Shooter, Veal Osso Bucco, Rolled Sole, Coconut Ceviche Shooter
The best thing on this plate was their veal osso bucco and it was amazing!  If I wasn't going to try anything else at Bacchanal, I probably would've had more of this.  The marrow was dangerously good and the braised veal was so tender.

2nd Plate -- http://bit.ly/2kxtdSO
Pickled Greens, Spicy Thai Beef, Poke Salad
I think with my second plate, I made a huge a mistake and had a huge amount of poke salad.  That immediately filled me up.

Because I was already reaching complete fullness after just two plates, I went straight to dessert.  And my dessert plate was loaded!!

3rd Plate -- http://bit.ly/2kxtq8t
Sugar Free Mango Pudding, Limoncello Sorbet, Ginger Gelato, Bonet, Exotic Fruit Sago, Green Tea & Sesame Seed Opera Cake
I'm not much of sweets person, but honestly, this was the best overall plate of food I had from the whole buffet.  Everything was good, but my faves were definitely the Limocello Sorbet and the Exotic Fruit Sago.  Both were very sweet and refreshing!

All in all, Bacchanal is still my buffet of choice on the Strip, just slightly edging by Wicked Spoon.  It's a still a great dining experience when you're with a group and the food selection is still great and extensive, but it's not one buffet that I'd rush back to visit again and again simply because it's become way too expensive.

During my stay in Vegas for the Labor Day weekend, how can I not hit up a few buffets. One of the buffet I went to was Bacchanal Buffet located inside Caesar's Palace. Once my friends and I got pass the 3 step waiting n paying process we were able to indulge in some very yummy foods! The first station I went to was the meat station. WOW they had all kinds of meats prime rib, sausages, brisket, etc. I was only interested in the prime rib. The handful of pieces I had were perfect. I splashed on some horseradish cream and I was in heaven. The next station I went to was the Asian food station -of course! I was surprised they had chow fun and some of my favorite dim sum selections. I was not too impressed with the Italian station and I don't really care for crab legs. The last station I went to was the dessert area. WOW everything was so delish. My two favorite items were the apple pie and the thai ice tea  ice cream. I repeated those items at least 4 times in addition to all the other foods I have already ate. Vegas would not be Vegas without buffets, and I am glad Bacchanal rasied the buffet standard pretty high.

We use to come here whenever we came to Vegas and were always pleased. This time it was absolutely no different than any other buffet just over priced. The staff at the carving station are so rude they must've forgotten that we are paying customers. My father asked for a center cut of prime rib and for it to be cooked to medium well. The man told him if he wanted medium well to eat the brisket. My father obviously said no I want the prime rib but would like it cooked more. The man had an attitude the whole time and said it would take 10 minutes. He then threw it on the grill and was about to burn it   father asked for it and he gave him a slab of straight beef fat. Dogs wouldn't even eat it, trust me. Then we spoke with the manager to express our concerns and he said I will talk with him, but in no way did he ask what he could do to make it better. The food this time round is absolutely awful. Truthfully, it would've been better to eat in n out. I also saw that everyone said the dessert is the best, but no. My molten lava cake wasn't even molten. Cheesecake tasted like rubber.

When i checked into my Vegas hotel, I was told by the woman at the reception desk that this is the best dinner buffet in Vegas--she was right! Although, if you're planning to check it out I would highly recommend either getting there early or making a reservation because you'll likely wait. We went at 7pm on a Saturday and would've waited an hour in line, but my boyfriend has diamond status at Caesar's so we got to wait in a much shorter diamond status line. 

The food was phenomenal, I seriously couldn't zip my romper all the way after eating so there's that. My highlights: bacon, brisket, lobster claws, crab legs, Nutella crepe from the dessert bar, lobster bisque, and duck breast. 

My advice: get in line early or expect a decent wait. Pay $15 for unlimited wine add-on, it's worth it!

Raises the standard for Vegas buffets. We were big fans of the Wynn and Bellagio buffets and visited Bacchannal and Wicked Spoon on our most recent trip. 

What really impressed us was the service we had. We had a gentleman by the name of Miguel and he was absolutely outstanding and similar to service at more traditional "fancy"  sit down restaurants.  We did not have to ask for things he just made it "happen" so to speak like he was reading our minds.

Some highlights included:  Crab Won tons, prime rib and the scalloped potatoes.

Comparison vs Wicked Spoon

Pros: Has a wider variety of food. The number of food stations here is absolutely amazing. They even had a Taquero and Horchata which was funny for this California Hispanic boy. 

About the Same: The quality of food. They both had cracked snow crab legs which are always popular. The both had some different options but for the most part everything was "good" to "very good". The dessert options were both about the same as well. 

Negatives: Long Lines, and it's a little more expensive than the other buffets but given the service and variety I think it's reasonable.

Also the Horchata was not cold enough and the Churros at the dessert bar were not kept "warm " enough .

Buffets are always over-rated. Whenever my BF drags me to a Vegas buffet, the Wynn buffet is better. 

This one has decent variety but food is not as fresh & flavor component was lacking. Oysters are not fresh. Wynn oysters are! That's what I was looking forward to when he dragged me.  Everything else was just ok. Prob great if you are w/ a big group & no one can agree on food. BF said it was good but he also thought Wynn buffet was better. Then, Wicked Spoon at Cosmo is 2nd place.

All & all I love Cesar's. Just not this. If you get fresh oysters, call me.

I've tried Wicked Spoon, The Buffet at Aria, and now Bacchanal Buffet, and I gotta say that Bacchanal is by far the best.  There are a ton of different cuisines to choose from - Chinese (dim sum, lo mein, fried rice, chicken and broccoli), Japanese (sushi, miso soup, ramen), American (mashed potatoes, assorted meats, truffled mac&cheese), Mexican (tacos, nachos), seafood (shrimp, king crab legs), all sorts of salads, juices, pizzas, and desserts.  

I was in a group of about 10-20 people, and the service was still pretty good.  By the time we were done, we wanted to explode from all the food we had just eaten.  Luckily since we were at Caesar's, it meant we can walk around and shop afterwards to walk off all the calories we had just consumed :)  It's OK though because it was definitely worth it.

Pretty good. Probably the best buffet on the strip I'd say. Is it worth the price? I'll leave that for you to give it a try. Seafood selections were pretty good but the meat qualities I felt were just ok. The brisket  was good, the American wagyu was tough and not tender, the prime rib was a bit tough and tasted like a steak. 

Stayed away from the Chinese food and pizza area. Did not want to carb up those items. The cold tiger prawns were really good. Crab legs were not bad. The crab claws had a lot of meat. Taco bar was nice to have you. Make sure you save room for dessert. The Vietnamese coffee was really good.

After hearing so many positive things about the Bacchanal buffet, I finally got to try it. I've never been to a buffet at Vegas because there are also lots of great restaurants around. I went with a large party of 9 on a weekend for dinner. After taxes it came out to ~$70 before tip. There is a separate line if you have a bigger party. We went around 4PM to beat the lines and got seated pretty immediately, maybe a 15 min wait. 

The king crab legs: I've been told I need to eat enough of these to make the price worth it. However, after I got through half my first plate of trying to crack them and get the meat out, I was over it. It was good, but not the highlight of my bacchanal experience. 
Fresh oysters: these were good! Super fresh and delicious. 
Prime rib: meh, mine was pretty dry so I didn't finish it. 
Bone marrow: this was really good! Loved the little toppings on it, I went for a second round
The pasta was really good too. Desserts.. maybe my favorite. They have a huge selection of different ice cream flavors, you can get a boba thai tea float (yum), and a bunch of other little things. 
I tried a piece of almost everything, like the nigiri, dim sum items, etc, and thought they were all decent. 

I wouldn't say anything tasted bad, but it just wasn't a striking experience as people made it to be. I think maybe it would be more worth it during lunch hours, so it's cheaper. There are supposed to be great brunch food options as well, so maybe I'll give it one more try for lunch.

Came here for lunch based on the reviews online. It did not disappoint. I mainly ate the beef and seafood station options. There's a ton of food. My waiter wasn't as attentive as I'd liked. I needed another set of silverware after the seafood portion but had to wait a good 10 mins. The dessert area was great with tons of options. Get here early or the dinner line does become large. Overall glad I tried it as an opportunity, but would not return again.
I love coming to Bacchanal every time I come to Las Vegas. This place offers so many different delicious options.

Still good. They have the best Dim Sum/Sushi selection out of any buffet I've seen in Las Vegas. 4-5 different dim sums/dumplings/steamed buns and 4-5 types of Nigiri Sushi as well as ramen.

Lots of other options as well like soups, fresh juices (yum!), and plenty of Meats & Seafood. The Meats section has a good amount of variety - I would say the Lambchops were the best. Prime rib was just okay. In the Seafood section, the Crab Legs were larger than normal but they still had ice in them.

Overall, the selection here is fantastic and enormous, however, I do think Wicked Spoon is a better value/less wait though overall. Bacchanal will have a crazy, long wait on weekends...Yes, I do like their computer system that prints out a receipt with a return estimated time. However, once you return during that time frame, you'll have to wait an additional 20-30 minutes.
Aesthetically pleasing, service was horrible, food lacking in taste and quality. This is not the same buffet as it opened. Has gone down a lot in last year or so. highest priced buffet in town too.

One of the most professional buffets I have ever attended by far will be going for lunch or dinner next time ..  the Deserts are more than colorful and constantly being brought out fresh you can taste the different from other buffets I have gone robin the past .. fresh colorful, decorative and most important a taste that last long after you have finished leaving you wanting for more.. who ever is cooking in the back is a true chef.  
Robert was the server who told us about the station and nothing short of what he said was there was there  if not more.  They even made the crepes fresh upon request shocked at what an amazing buffet and staff they have here so friendly and very quick to pick up after you and get your drink filled without you even asking ....

Wow! Just wow. This is the best buffet at which I have eaten. I am not normally a fan of buffet foods as they are low quality and prepared too quickly. This place, however, is like several complete restaurants all in one place. From Italian to Japanese to Mexican and of course American comfort foods and many, many desserts, this place has it all. I was especially impressed with Asian desserts like matcha cake and egg tarts. I have eaten here twice and could go many more times but sadly with this high quality all-you-can-eat comes a higher price. However, its perfect for special occassion.

Highlights: one of the better buffets in Vegas, LOTS of crab legs, good variety of selection

They offer a Groupon deal for 2 people valid Mon-Thurs from 3-5PM for $110 (not including the $9 tax they charge you at the register).

The interior of the buffet is modern and nicely decorated to created an upscale ambience. My group was a party of 7 and we waited about an hour to be seated on a Tuesday afternoon. 

There is a good variety of cuisines that include Asian, Italian, American and Seafood. I tried the bone marrow that everyone was raving about but I wasn't a huge fan of it. They do not skimp on crab legs and always give me a full heeping plate of it. 

I know I enjoy the food when my stomach is so full that it hurts haha. But even though I had no room for dessert, I couldn't pass on their sweets section.

This is our second time in this buffet and I have to say I am not as impressed as I was the first time. 
I understand I have to wait and I am ok with that and I love the system that you have. 

Got to the table got drinks right away but been sitting and eating for about an hour now and no one even stopped or asked if I want a refill. 

The table next to me, the people left about 45 minuets ago and no one came to clean the table and have it ready for the next couple ( is this the reason for the wait times ? And then you are charging $20 per person if they don't want to wait ? ) 

Food was great and I will sure to come back for the food but the service at the table is a joke and that is the reason for my 3 stars. 

Come in enjoy the food but ask from the get go an extra drink and be here 1/2 an hour to an hour early to get in at the time you want because while it took me about 8 min to write this review they still didn't clean the table next to me or picked up the empty plates from our table since we got here.
Great food. Worth the hour wait. Definitely something to splurge on and not do every day with prices being $55 a piece at dinner time for adults. But a great experience

It's a buffet, not everything is going to be extraordinary. It depends what you plan on eating and if you're going to take advantage of the $15 aycd if it will be worth eating here. For me it was. I checked in and got a free beer. Hubby took advantage of the all you can drink. As far as variety, if you're in the mood for something they should have it. A lot of different cuisines, much more than I've seen than at other buffets and hey present their food well. 

The items that I loaded up on was the crab, brisket, wagyu, and bone marrow. Those were really good and stood out from the rest of the items I chose. Oh, and the lobster bisque was good too. The rest of the food I had was just ok and not worth eating for my $. They had an awesome dessert island and most of what I had was very good, light, and not too sweet. The only things I didn't care for too much was the donut and coffee creme brûlée. 

Overall above average buffet I'd try once at

Honestly, it's just ok.
Maybe it was the staff being rude, the food being left out too long or the general lack of give a damn by the staff in general that lead to my dining experience here being really lackluster.
It didn't really live up to the hype and image that you would expect from Caesar's Palace.
In all reality, the buffets at other hotels were all in all a better experience.
The only thing this place really has going for it, is that it's ridiculously large. But with that also comes the fact that the staff will lose track of how long food has been out. Which I can say is what really killed this place for me. 
Most of the food I ate tasted like it had been out on display for at least a few hours and in many cases flat out cold.
The "Wagyu" beef for example was dry, bland and frankly felt and tasted like a dry sponge. 
So all in all, not really impressed.
The only thing impressive about this place is the display at the entrance. Other than that, it's meh.

The best buffet we went to in Vegas by far.  I was impressed walking in to be seated.  Counters filled with every type of food you could imagine.  Cold and hot. Ready made and custom made to order.  Service was spot on.  My water was never empty and the table was never left with used plates.  Such a great start!  We had the great timing to be there during change from breakfast to lunch so we got to try a lot of variety.  The usual breakfast fare was included bacon, eggs, sausage, etc as well as made to order omelets, eggs benedict, croce madam, acia bowls, fresh exotic fruits ( dragon fruit, mango, etc), smoothies, fresh squeezed juice (orange, cucumber, watermelon, hibiscus).  Not to mention a full Mexican area, Italian, and Asian.  Made to order ramen and other noodle dishes.  Dim sum. Sushi. A carving station. Crab legs. Shrimp. You want it they have it there somewhere.  And the desserts....oh my goodness.  Creme burlee. Gelato. Made to order crepes. And many many more.

I still cannot believe what I experienced. This buffet was simply amazing! We arrived about 11:10am and we were so lucky there wasn't a line! It was also a Tuesday, but literally an hour and half after we left, good luck getting inside. 

They have many options to choose from, pretty affordable for the options they provided, the quality of food was great and they have awesome customer service. 

Will definitely come back next time in Vegas

There are SOOO many reviews for this place already and with a 4ish stars average? That should already be a sign that this place is pretty good compared to other Vegas buffets.

My quick take on this buffet:

1. Great meat, seafood, and dessert selection. Meats of all sorts? YES. Crab legs? Shrimp? Yes and yes! Gelato? YEP. Gelato man who was friendly? NO.

2. No salad bar? I wasn't particularly happy with the salad selection.  There are only a few pre-made salads.

3. Service was great! The man who was covering our area was attentive and super friendly.

Worth my $60ish? Yes!  

PS--Do expect a wait.

So far I want to give this - 5 stars. They r totally misleading with their wait time. You go to a kios to get a return time slip for when you go into line. But they don't tell you that the line to go in is another 2 hrs.  Gonna be a 4 hr wait that is misleading because you expect the return time to be when you get in. Poor dealing of their wait time. Let's see if the food changes this review. 

Update after eating: food is alright, nothing out of the ordinary compared with other Vegas buffets. Not worth the wait and is over hyped.  I'm guessing they don't tell you about the additional 2 hr wait cuz you won't stay. Kitchen closes at 11 but they stop refilling food around 10:30 but still let people in. SMH

I'm a sucker for dessert & they have all my wants and needs from creme brûlée to crepes! Food is standard not anything out of the ordinary, honestly think it's a bit too over priced but it's a buffet so it evens out in the long run...but I'd suggest lunch over dinner better food I think :)

This has got to be one of the best buffets at the strip. Sterling brunch? Skip that and come to this instead. For the same value you surely get more out of here. The variety of food they have here is amazing.

First off their valet service was amazing even though we did not stay in their hotel. We just wanted to eat there without the hassle of carrying all of our luggage 

Yessssss-pros
1. Amazing variety as mentioned. Chinese to Spanish to Italian to seafood
2. Dessert. Omg really. Cakes. Mousse, icecream. You need a separate stomach. The flavors were exotic. Ube icecream. Thai cake. Yuzu coconut tarts. Yesss
3. Friendly servers
4.paid for a head of time prior to eating so you won't need to find your server and look for the bill at the end

Nooooo-cons
1. Long line. We were at the register for 15 minutes even though we were in a vip line and another 10 at the seat g line. If you are on regular line you should be prepared to spend some time there
2. They enforce a 2 hour limit subtly... Not sure if it's actually enforced

I will Def come back to here for brunch next time!!

I honestly don't know why people think this is the best buffet in Vegas.  We got the coupons from travelzoo and it's totally BS.  The coupon stated it's 45% off but in fact is only 5% because you are only allowed to eat breakfast here.  Plus you will have to pay tax on full amount.  

Anyways, we got here at 8:30 am and most of the foods look like they are from yesterday.   The fried rice is super dry (under the heating lamp for too long).  Besides the eggs, nothing looks fresh at all.   
Even the pastries are dried out.  

Not really impressed with any specific dishes here.

Been here every time I'm in Vegas and will continue to come back. The selection and taste of the food is amazing.

They used to have Chocolate Lava Cakes where there was chocolate in the middle. PLEASE BRING IT BACK!!! Right now there is no filling :( 

Pro-tip: mix it with the scoop of vanilla ice cream.
What you paid for is definitely what you get! Lots of love on this buffet! Everything is a little pieces of heaven.. the food is awesomely delicious! You can't go wrong!

Very Good.  The food was great, no lines when we went at any of the stations (a little at the carving station).  Met the manager Wolfe, great guy, wife had picture taken with him (will post when I can).  Definitely worth the money.  Everyone was friendly and helpful.

This buffet has the worst setup to get seated! You first wait in a line to put your phone number into a kiosk. Once you wait about 50 minutes, you get a text to come back. When you think you are a shoe in, you wait in another awful line to pay. When you think you're close to paying, think again! You have to wait until they feel ready to let you pay. Once you pay, you wait in another long line to be seated. I haven't even been seated yet, and I'm over it.

Update: After the god awful wait, the food somewhat made up for it. If the line setup was better, this place would be 5 stars for sure!

Many of you may know this as one of the best buffets in Vegas. They have a huge assortment, be prepared to eat! Meats are good and they have some specialties like bone marrow and lamb chops for dinner. Everything was great.

The food was fresh and so much variety! Loved the dessert bar a lot! 
It was packed but still the service was great! 
Definitely will recommend ppl to go here.. It's the best buffet in town for sure! The best part they have a lot of variety for vegetarians and also some dessert options for the diabetic ppl! :)

Based on the good reviews, my group ate at the Caesars buffet last night. We were all disappointed the the limited number of choices and the quality of the food considering the premium price. But, to be fair, a couple of items stood out positively including the large prawns and the American Waygu beef. The made to order crepe made for an excellent desert. One special note was that we had excellent service with respect to drink refills and prompt clearing of dishes.

Well, I paid for the buffet later. I don't recall the last time I had a case of diarrhea. Well, by the time I got back to the room, I had a bad case of it. Was it the raw oysters or something else? Now, you know why they received a single star.

Definitely a must try buffet when you go to Las Vegas. It's expensive and the lines are long if you don't get there early enough. It's worth it though, the ingredients are significantly better than what other buffets are using.

Being a rewards member my husband and I only waited for about 30mins during peak dinner hours. The hostesses were efficient and pleasant. Drinks and cleaning services were prompt. Good variety of food. The raw seafoods were fresh. The only thing I dislike was the staff manning the soup noodle stand - he was VERY rude and impatient.

Bacchanal has stepped up their game.   We haven't visited in 2 years as the food started to get too routine.   We recently went back and found additional assortment added to their dessert table and seafood.  Best of all Manivone S., our server was very attentive and we received the best service.  The best buffet in Vegas and we have tried them all...worth the price for the variety and quality.  There is a reason why there is a wait.   We are Platinum Caesars Reviews members so we only waited about 10 minutes to be seated on a weekday.
Amazing presentation, food is diverse and tasty, plus the hotel is great. One of my faves in Vegas. If you don't like the food... you can drown the taste in 15 dollar unlimited mimosas. Worth the $$

Hands down BEST BUFFET I'VE EVER BEEN TO! I say this with enthusiasm as I've paid a lot of money, especially in Vegas, to eat at these crazy buffets. Most items offered taste like cafeteria food and there are only 1-2 good things to eat while everything else is almost flavorless. This is not the case with Bacchanal Buffet. Every single piece of food we got was delicious. Every. Single. Piece. My children, toddlers, ate so much, I couldn't believe my eyes. It made me question my own home cooking, because they don't ever eat at home like they did here. We tried food in the American, Asian, Mexican, Italian, and dessert sections. My babes loved the pizza, mac and cheese, chicken, vegetables, meatballs, pasta, and chicken parmesan. They had a bit of each and liked what they got. I loved the breakfast buffet; it had individual plates of chicken and waffles, eggs, 3 different breakfast meats, and plenty of fruits. My husband enjoyed the seafood selections, including shrimp, crab, lobster, and salmon. For dessert, they have a station in the center of the space surrounded by small cakes and pastries. There is a crepe station where you can make-to-order a fresh crepe! I got the Nutella with Banana Foster filling and shared with the family. It was delicious. They also have a gelato station with more than 10 flavors, we liked the strawberry and mango flavors. 

This was our best meal in Vegas and worth every penny. If you're a 7Star or Diamond Member with Caesar's Rewards, you have your own line to enter. When we arrived during lunch time, the line was almost an hour long. We walked right up through the empty Diamond line and were seated almost immediately. Great treatment from the hosts and waitstaff as well. I highly recommend this buffet be the one you visit when you're here!
Best buffet in Vegas. Enormous variety of food.  Prime rib is always my go to. Crab legs hot and cold.  Wide variety of salads.  Plenty of seafood.  Worth the money.

Coming here again definitely is another level of experience. I felt like I missed a lot of good stuff during my prior visit here.

I particularly liked the Asian section which is partly hidden. That delicious pork belly definitely melts in your mouth. I had to keeping back for more. 

The husband got his crab legs and prawns worth. He said that one can tell that they're fresher than the other buffets in town.

Food is soo good there!! Prime rib, crab legs, lobster. Only bad thing about the lobster is that it's cold. There's no hot lobster. However all the other food makes up for it. I'm never disappointed when I go there. Always full and satisfied

Oh. My. Lord. This was the best buffet I've ever been to. We went for breakfast, which covered about 300 feet of counter space and food from every continent. I ran out of room in my belly long before I ran out of great food to try. Also, and this was a bit surprising, the drinks were amazing. Juices of all kinds and coffee were all great. They have an unlimited drink menu, but we didn't try it.

This buffet is the best! I've had 4 buffets in Vegas and this one is the best. I've had treasure islands, Mandalay Bay's, Bellagio and now Cesar's palace.  We paid 39.99 for brunch which is how much you are gonna pay for a buffet on the strip. They had so much food to select from it is crazy!! They had fresh squeezed juices, sushi, seafood, Chinese food. One of the best things about this buffet was the fresh fruit. The watermelon was so fresh and crispy I think we had 3 plates of it. The shrimp was also very good too! The only thing about this buffet that was weird was I could not find salad dressing for all the salad they had but it was okay cause I put shrimp on that thing and ate it. If you are in Vegas you have to come to this Buffett. This is my #1 and I will be back at my next visit!!

My cousin took me here for my birthday & when I say this ish was amazing, you must believe me. I have this thing with germs and they saved the day! Most of the items were in individual containers. Yaaaaaas! Shrimp & grits, seafood galore, Asian, southern, (you can get the seafood heated up just asked the person behind the seafood bar). Shhhhhhh. I ate so much good food I can't even remember what I ate. The chocolate melting cake at the end with strawberries was life!!! This place is amazing. Guess I'll have to take my cousin here for groundhogs day. *insert eye rolls*! They often have this on Groupon for $35.  The only thing that bothered me was I tipped on my receipt and the servers said they don't get those tips. Well I spoke to a manager and got that worked out. Get there and grub you won't be disappointed!
Best buffet ever it is pricey but it's worth it. At least for us. Their tacos and posole are great. We are not too far from Las Vegas so we visit this place a lot.

Some fantastically original offerings...some standard Ponderosa/OCB offerings...mainly mouthwatering, and more less worth the $53 check and 45 minute wait. The seafood station was undeniably a lock for the top spot. Boasting an excellent sea bass dish, and only the most meaty and largely abundant crab legs. BBQ, Chinese, Mexican, Sushi, Vegetarian, Charcuterie...the buffet stations went on and on. Not to mention a ridiculous dessert station worthy of the highest praise. Without a doubt the preeminent buffet we've taken in while devouring Vegas; but I'd have to say that we'll be trying others before a return. The long wait, to go along with a steep bill, left me wanting to venture out in search of other decorated competition. I definitely recommend Bacchanal for buffet goers in search of the acclaimed "best buffet in Vegas"...but does it end there?

We went on 9/29/2019. For 2 adults the price was $119.05. Before you pay, or after you pay, a photographer is there taking your picture as a souvenir, of course you would have to pay for it. They print out the photos and find you to show your picture and see if you would like to purchase it. I thought it was a little strange.

It was about 2pm when we were there. We were really disappointed. Most of the menu items were dry or tasteless. Tri tip steak was tough with no flavor, pho lacked flavor and authenticity, pad thai was plain, the italian philly cheesesteak was also dry with no flavor, lobster mac and cheese was dry and didn't see nor taste any cheese. 

Now on to the good stuff, the mushroom ravioli was great, the prime rib was tender, and most of the desserts were just ok, however the mango sorbet was so good! It didnt taste like it was mango flavored, it tasted as if it was made of fresh mangos. I did have some crab claws which were decent tasting. 

I was disappointed that for all that money, I didn't get the chance to try some lechon or bone marrow. Also that most of the items were dry and flavorless. 

Our waiter, I forgot his name, he was so nice! I must say, the service was great. 

If I were ever gave this place a chance again, it would have to be closer to dinner time even though the wait would be long. I am sure dinner time the menu items would probably be much better.
One of the best buffet in las vegas strip. Im so sad they didnt have oysters. The beef brisket is the bomb

I don't usually like to do buffets because, of course, I have to overeat to get my money's worth, and I never eat enough to actually get my money's worth, so it always ends tragically. I also haven't eaten at any buffet that I could give full stars.. until now. I had maybe 3 plates of food, consisting of what I thought looked good: beef brisket (mini plate with what we thought was grits, BOMB), another brisket from the carving station, sweet potato tator tots, roasted rainbow carrots, chilean sea bass, xiao long bao, curry mussels, clams, and the elote corn. I mentioned only items that I liked. Favorite item was probably the chilean sea bass since that's harder to come by nowadays. There were a few other things I tried that I will pass next time: kobe sliders, mac n cheese, feta & watermelon salad, and ceviche. There was so much more food that I could never possibly sample, including a massive dessert selection. I loved the oreo mousse cake (and the gummi bears!!!!).

We went for lunch on a friday around 11:45, and only had to wait about 30 mins. You can dress up if you want, but definitely can wear tee and shorts (or other fat pants). Service was great. Our lady was very attentive in removing our plates and making sure we had enough water and other beverages. Also, you can take a hot coffee to go!!! They will give you a huge cup with no lid, but you can take it out!

I went to the Bacchanal buffet last Tuesday for dinner, because I have read lots of positive reviews on Yelp. I don't know what those people have to rave about. There was a lot of variety but flavor was lacking. It was past 5 pm and should have been dinner time. However, every item was ice cold and dry. For more than $ 50 a person, it was highly unsatisfactory. The day after we went to the Wicked spoon and the food was warm and tasting great! I will not return to the Bacchanal.

Perfect for the best of the best I ever had.  This is the 2nd time for this place.  Even better and better than the first time.  The bad thing is waiting too long to being seat.   There were plenty of table for 2 empty,but they took us wait for 45 mins to seat us at the table.  This is the reason for only 4 stars.
Having lunch with my besties! The seafood looks delicious. Decor is modern and eclectic and the music is cool!

Nothing special that you should pay 65$ nor wait in line 1.5 hours for. Yes they offer fresh seafood and other decent food but what vegas buffet does not? The cold crab legs were super salty, oysters wetter terrible tasting,  meat selection was good but tastes average,  asian selection was diverse but taste was nothing spectacular although I have to admit the pho was tasty for a non specialized buffet. The one memorable item was the mojito nonalcohol shot- cantaloupe with pineapple like mint juice ..I must have had 12!

Excellent buffet experience; the best I have had in a Vegas so far. The dining room is beautiful and there is a lot of attention to detail in the decor and how the food is presented. The food was incredible and made you wish you had three stomachs to fit everything in! The crab was sweet and delicate, not salty or briny at all. My favorite item was the bone marrow; the other hits of the evening were the osso bucco and the truffle mushroom pizza. Service was friendly and attentive. Sue took care of us and really treated us well. We will be back!
The best buffet across the nation. Huge selection of food and deserts. The best picks here are the halibut, brisket, salt&pepper prawns, pizza, and ramen.

This place is seriously the KING of ALL buffets. None come close to this place as this place as nearly every kind of food that you can imagine. From the fresh, to the savory, to the hearty and lastly, to the lovers of the sweet. This is all complimented by an excellent looking restaurant. Sure the lines are long and its pricey but considering what is given, it's worth the price and definitely worth a visit, if you haven't been there yet. Gotta go atleast once.

Dined here on a Monday at 8 p.m. It took an hour to get to the cashier, and on top of that the cashier told me I was not allowed in because of my attire (I wore a romper with a plunge neck line) come on man it was 115 degrees outside! Let me eat! So i spoke to the manager and she said I was ok. 

Them waited another 25 minutes to get a table and was told we only have 30 minutes to eat. 

The line for the seafood was horrible and unorganized. People were coming in and out of the line trying to get food and would cut the line not knowing everyone has been standing in line to get some crappy snow crab legs. 


Snow crab legs are cut in half and sitting in an iced bath water which made the meat soggy and tasteless. Stone crab claws were hard and the meat stuck to the shell. All the other foods is whatever. 

Waste of time and money. Never returning.
Had an amazing experience here at the bachanal and our server Esmeralda Juarez was excellent! The food was really good, especially the prime rib and brisket!

What can you say about a buffet the size of Bacchanal. Remarkable selection at every station. The downside, it's not cheap but every visit I walk out of there satisfied. Tip, make sure you are hungry when you go. If you have a sweet tooth the dessert station will put a huge smile on your face.

Let me preface this by saying that I am not a huge fan of buffets. Therefore 3 is quite a high rating for me.

Bacchanal buffet is the place to be if you are really hungry. There is so much food here and the space is so large that I got lost trying to find my table. Twice. It's also really crowded, so I felt like I kept having to maneuver in order to get around people or to get in line for food. 

But in terms of having the most food and variety I have seen in a buffet, I'd say Bacchanal is definitely up there in terms of a buffet. There was a chinese station, a japanese station, a noodle station, congee, a charcuterie station, cheese station (YES!), pizza station, meat station ( with brisket! ), sides for the meat station, seafood station ( those king crab legs were all the rage...)

I tried prime rib, brisket, both of which were not overly salted nor dry, but needed au jus to really bring the flavors together. 

It really wasn't bad at all, but I really just don't pull my weight at buffets, so it's always super expensive in my opinion. But, to be fair, I never waste any of the food.

19Oct19 - Food looked great. Before we paid we asked two different cashiers, and one spoke to the manager; 
KING CRAB IS NO LONGER ON THE MENU. 
We were so looking forward to king crab. (Had some last night at Water Grill - the best crab I have ever had - but one leg was just a start). 
Hope someday they go back to unlimited. But management said king crab is not even available as an add on.

Food was fabulous, great atmosphere, and our server, Julie, was the actual best 

Come hungry. You're going to be here a while. It's best to go early in the morning, it gets very busy after 10am

This is about my 5th time going here for the past half decade and I am not quite sure what the he'll happened to the quality of food here? A good amount of food is dry and the rest are just bland. It appears that Bacchanal lost its spark and just went with cost cutting procedures so that they can maximize their profit.  For anyone reading this, please suggest a much more better buffet for me please.
Amazing Staff and food!!!! A bit pricey but delicious and worth it !!! Not sure what else to say other than it's a must when in Vegas !!! endless food and delicious!!!
