The best Buffet I have had in my life! Even though it is also the most expensive, it is worth it. It is an enjoyable dining experience.  The buffet, which offers small plates for entree options,  includes varied dishes,  including lamb t-bone, bone marrow,  multiple types of crab, seafood paella,  and lobster bisque,  just to name a few. 

Everyone should splurge and dine at Bachannal at least once as part of their Las Vegas culinary experience.

How this buffet has better ratings than the buffers at the Wynn or Bellagio is beyond me! We were very disappointed in everything about this experience. Here is a list of issues:

1) the wait is longer than what they advertise at the beginning of the line. They estimated approximately 25 min if wait time, but that was how long it took to pay.  Then we had to wait another 20 minutes to be seated. 

2) the hostess asked my wife and I to stand in 3 different places when we finally got to the front of the line. It was almost comical as each spot we were told to stand were less than 5 feet apart. 

3) the decor is way too busy. Not an inviting look. It's also way too crowded! There is no easy way to navigate between tables. We had to keep dodging bussers and guests in the tight and and winding pathways. 

4) the carpet is dirty and full of spots. 

5) the food itself is good, but NOT better than Bellagio or Wynn. 

6) the buffet line itself is way too hard to navigate. No real flow to it. People are coming from both directions... it's a mess. You can't even see the entire buffet. You have to just keep following it. Many of the selections aren't even labeled.

7) the dessert bar is a joke. No cheesecake (only sugar free). Not many selections. Poor labeling of selections here too. 

8) the crab legs are much harder to get too than at Bellagio or Wynn. 

9) ambiance is lacking... I was not impressed with Caesar's hotel  

We have been going to the Wynn and Bellagio buffets for years, but thought we would try something else because of the high Yelp reviews. This is the first time Yelp has failed me! Bacchanal is NOT better than Wynn or Bellagio.

Loved this buffet! This will be a must go to everytime I go to Vegas now! They have everything you can think of at this buffet, crab legs, prime rib, sushi, all the deserts you can think of and so much more. Staff was friendly & always made sure our drinks were filled & plates were taken away once done. It is very spendy but I definitely think it was worth the price.
The wait was long but once inside it is quite easy to become overwhelmed by the choices. If you are a foodie and open to trying new things this is the place for you!
The food was great but what made our experience even better was Lorri queen. She was amazing, she has the best customer service and made us feel so welcome.

Flag Ship of Buffets; setting the standard of what a buffet should be.  Very expense but worth every penny. Long wait time unless your diamond member but every second worth the wait. Negative reviews doesn't justify the fantastic food and service. Super fan if I can afford this at a regular. The hype is real and reviews from Yelp to YouTube are spot on.

The family visited on 5 July 2019 at 1630. We waited for a table for about 30 minutes and limited to a two hour period due to the holiday weekend. In total with tip total bill was $225.00. Two adults and one child under 10 years old.

Highly recommend a visit!

What a great buffet with a amazing assortment of choices! Definitely the best buffet in Vegas. I love seafood and they had so many options not just your standard fair! My husband is more of a meat and potatoes guy and he was overwhelmed by the choices. Overall amazing experience.
Simply the best buffet that I've ever attended. Wait time is less than half of whatever time the staff quotes you. We were told 90 minute wait and were seated in less than 45 minutes.
Vegas and their impressive buffets. So many options, so select wisely and take small portions so you can try it all!

This was the best meal I had in Vegas. There was so much variety, and everything was very good quality. I tried the seafood, tacos, sushi, American options, and desserts! Loved it all. I did not try the meat station, but it looked and smelled delicious!
The quality of food was not up to expectation. Buffet was definitely not worth the wait, effort, and money. Memorial weekend price was 69.99, and the best dish there was a fried shrimp taco.......

Bacchanal Buffet in the Caesar's Palace Hotel and Casino is slated as the number one buffet in Vegas and the one that all others live up to. I guess to be able to appreciate what that means, you'd have to take a step back and think about what you value in a buffet. Don't think you can game the system and get "your money's worth." While most buffet's advertise themselves as "all you can eat" that's not really what you're paying for. What you want is good food, good variety, and a fair price. Sure there's the added bonus of eating however much of food that fills you up but honestly you're never going to get there. 

Bacchanal starts to get busy around 12:30pm. Although the line goes fairly quickly, they do attract a ton of people and a lot of those people take up the entire 2 hours that they are given to eat their food. Most people will shed light on their seafood. I'd say that's only ok because the real stars here are the meats, tacos, sushi and dessert. Sure you can laugh and say these are the filler foods but why stuff yourself with mediocre seafood when you can gorge on other amazing eats?

They have a fantastic array of desserts with pastries, fruits and gelato. The black sesame and POG flavors are the best but they also have pistachio which was quite popular. Like I said their tacos are pretty awesome and their cut meats are good too (wagyu and prime). The au jus could use some salt but once that's corrected, they're all pretty tasty. In the seafood section they have snow crab legs, stone crab, Dungeness crab and large cocktail shrimp. Nothing to write home about for the seafood honestly.

If you're looking for a buffet, then this is the place to go. It's $54.99 a person. They only take reservations if you choose the VIP package which is $98 a person. Otherwise you should wait in line. Once you pay, the clock starts ticking towards your limit of 2 hours but most people are done way before then. Keep in mind that it is a buffet and unlikely to serve fancy foods like you'd expect with a tasting menu (if you want that just go to Partage).

Holy Moley, Any AYCE buffet is so opposite of me but after hearing my Yelp buds rave about Bacchanal Buffet, its time I dine here. 

We arrive 4:30 on Saturday night. Since I'm a Caesars Platinum member, our line moves very fast. I turn around to the general line and its starting to build up. If you have a show to see and want to come here, plan to come here at least 3 hours before your show. Now that we have the pleasantries out of the way, lets Bacchanal!

This is a serious buffet, so it will take some expert planning. The carved meat section? Sure, they have prime rib. But they also have American Waygu beef as well as Tri-tip carvings. Top of the line carving meats!

Onto the fish section, crab legs, jumbo shrimp and raw oysters await your plate. It's any fish you wish at the Bacchanal Buffet!

I make my first plate, forget the salads, I dive into a cut of Waygu Beef and a slice of tri tip along with the creamiest mashed potatoes I ever had. I poured the Au Jus all over those meats. My wife comes back with tacos. Tacos?! There's a guy spinning a wheel and making tacos. Gimme the Au Jus thankyouverymuch. 

I started to stray at the Asian section. From the smoked duck to the various dumplings, this is my downfall. I load my new plate high with the yummy offerings, soooo good!

Now, I'm pretty packed. The dessert section looks crazy. They have a crepe section?? How can you pass up a warm crepe? I loaded mine with nutella and topped with with freshly made whipped cream and nuts. 

Was it worth the money, AYCE quality foods in a very clean setting? It was good, if I'm back to Vegas with my sons, we'll get our Bacchanal Buffet on.

Cheers!

We went on Wednesday evening at like 6:30pm and the wait was only 20 min from when we got in line to when we went inside. They told us it would be an hour wait but went faster so that's great. Now the food was amazing, a lot of variety, delicious, and very clean.

This buffet slightly misses expectations.   I had seen the ridiculous line for dinner and decided to go to brunch instead.   I had my heart set on crab legs, but I guess they dint serve them mid morning?  I was there until 1pm and never saw them come out.  Plenty of other tasty foods, and I think LUNCH  there is better than the breakfast.   Service was a bit slow, and pumped me for a tip which was rude.   Waited top long for refills despite the restaurant not being super busy. 

Desserts were excellent.

Next time will go elsewhere.

This is my third time coming to this buffet...in two months. That just goes to show how good this place is. The food is always good and on point; from breakfast to dinner I am always satisfied when I eat at this buffet. The pros: the beef ribs, sausage, breakfast items where the gravy is thicc, and the tacos. The cons: some of the desserts looks better than they taste and one of mine had a piece of aluminum wrapping in it. That's still not a deal breaker for me but if I would've eaten that who know what might've happened to me. This place is pretty big and always busy except for the mornings around 8-9 am and it is a good atmosphere with people laughing while having a good time. Lines can and will be ridiculous if you get here late; you can also buy a line pass the skip everyone and it might be worth it if you're really hungry. Despite the aluminum in my dessert I give this place a solid five stars. It is well worth trying.

Overpriced for sure. The food was very good and the service too, however; not worth the price. My biggest disappointment was that they did not have ceased salad I mean it's the Ceaser Palace that's the least that they could have. If the price was less I would go back because the food was good but that will never happen so I think that was my one and only experience at this buffet.

The buffet was good, I tried it based on recommendations I had received. Honestly, I didn't like they didn't have espresso coffee to offer not even as an extra cost. The food was good, the service was whatever. They had these red velvet waffles that I was dying to try and when I finally got around to them they were gone, I asked how long until the next batch and I was told that they were not refilling them and to try something else. I was annoyed that they don't replenish the dishes.

The food was amazing. Everything was fresh. My favorite was the shrimp and grits as well as the mussels. Our server was good. She had a lot of tables but she made sure she checked on us often. Well worth the wait. I will return again when I visit Vegas.

146 $ for two adults and one child . We were not impressed,oh well with the price we were and the amount of salt in everything to. Cold crab legs were not eatable, to salty . Oysters looked at me and said Warnings, we may kill you ! They were almost dry. Tuna poka was  made two nights before we came , same with sushi . We don't mind to pay for a good food, but this place is not the case

I don't have option to give 1/2 star else would have given. This buffet is running only because of fame and location and may be because of fake reviews. I feel like waisting money. Food is horrible, bad service, none of the food has taste. Seafood bar looks huge but have bad quality and most of them are empty and crappy quality. Stakes have very limited choice including Mexican and Japanese food are horrible in quality. I personally like "The buffet at wynn", way better quality and service along with a huge variety. If today all yelp comments are reset today none will give more than 1star to this place.

Sometimes timing is everything.  When we were in Vegas last year, I had just missed the opening and this year I just missed the one year anniversary celebration, and the Yelp event to boot.  But I finally got to try the famed buffet that everyone else is raving about.  One thing that worked in our favor was that we were staying at Caesar's on this trip and so after checking in and dropping our bags off in the room, we immediately turned around and headed straight downstairs to the buffet.  We were anticipating a huge line but to our surprise we walked right in at around 515pm.  I realize that this is not typical because the line to get in was super long by the time we were finished.  You can purchase a voucher that is akin to using a toll road in LA to avoid the wait, but you'll have to decide whether the extra $15 is worth your time.  Using our Caesar's Total Rewards card for a slight discount, Bacchanal's price on a Fri night was still a whopping $50 per person...

Boasting  of a menu of over 500 items, the $17 million  buffet pushes the envelope for LV buffet dining rivaling Wicked Spoon for current dominance.  They recently had their 1 millionth customer this last LDW and promptly gifted her a two day stay at Caesars w/spa treatment at QUA and unlimited buffet during the stay!  Doing the math, that works out to a mind boggling 3000 to 3500 people per day on the average.  Just another reason why they were voted the #1 buffet in Vegas by USA Today...

Split into 7 or so separate food themed areas, I was particularly impressed by the Asian section.  Everything is good, but nothing is the best you've ever had quality.  Still, the selection is dizzying,  and there are items that you don't always see at a buffet.  The rice porridge section was surprisingly ok and had all the fixings as well.  I read that they offered tonkotsu pork ramen at some point but they didn't have any that evening...
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=T1MSMPa-rJ4GoKkwTclsWg#T1MSMPa-rJ4GoKkwTclsWg
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=T1MSMPa-rJ4GoKkwTclsWg#bvP0vUR6sWwT49KY_qdk-g

The carving station is a must try at any buffet, but my jaw dropped a couple of inches when I saw the long bone tomahawk ribeyes waiting to be plundered http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=T1MSMPa-rJ4GoKkwTclsWg#qYw8pfJcXqVMccWZ9G46gw.  It's too bad I was in such a state of shock seeing about a dozen of them lying there otherwise I wish I had the balls to ask for a whole one, bone and all after all what can they say:  no?  As it was I was very pleased with the the outer ribeye cap that they had sliced off of one of them for me as it is the best part of the cut imho...
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=T1MSMPa-rJ4GoKkwTclsWg#M22z-WrpCtwH6p8Ce12LUQ

The dessert section was actually not as big as some buffets but still had a nice sampling of items.  I was drawn to the mochi ice cream but like I said before they're not the best that I've ever had (Mikawaya in Jtown, LA...)
http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=T1MSMPa-rJ4GoKkwTclsWg#KDUuYNSlPAX989mnJ_cDgg

The service was very attentive down to the small details like replacing silverware and refilling our beverages when they were half empty.  I never even saw them actually doing the work because they silently did all their magic each time I got up and helped myself to another plate...

After about a dozen trips back and forth between my seat and the buffet line (it seemed ridiculous to over stuff and pile on your plate at an AYCE) we finally threw in the proverbial white towel and vowed to ourselves that we would be back during another trip to try more...

Easily one of the two or three best LV buffets in most peoples minds, the missus actually said that she preferred the Wicked Spoon over Bacchanal, whereas I was the opposite and gave this place the slight nod.  It doesn't really matter as both are terrific, you'll just have to try both of them...

I have a true love / hate relationship with this buffet. On the one hand, the quality, quantity, and variety is still very much on point. I consider this the best buffet on the strip. On the other hand, due to its ever growing popularity, there is almost ALWAYS a long wait and the price seems to keep increasing. 

After once being horrified by a 240 min wait time (we ended up eating elsewhere because that's completely absurd!) I had a bad impression of the buffet. However, during my last two visits to Vegas, I ate there both times and the wait wasn't nearly as long. On one visit, we went during off peak hours on a Thursday and only waited 5 min (SCORE!). On another visit, it was during peak dinner time on a Friday night and the wait was about 45 min. There is also a 2 hr eating time limit which I'm still not certain if it's strictly enforced. I generally am so full after about an 1.5 hrs that the rule wouldn't really bother me (even if it IS enforced). 

I very much appreciate the Asian (especially Chinese) food selections and find that they do it better than most. I like the Chinese herbal soups and porridge with authentic toppings to go with it. 

The raw bar is so abundant and delicious - yum yum yum!! I definitely got my crab legs and oysters fix here. I also LOVE the variety of desserts - there's SOOO many to choose from and they have fun stations such as mini Thai Tea boba floats and freshly made crepes. They also had tasty drinks in dispensers including horchata and watermelon aqua frescas. They do have a nice carving station if that's your thing but I'm not a huge fan of all the meats. I rather save room for more crab legs! 

The environment (while loud at times) is pretty spacious and the decor is aesthetically pleasing. The presentation of all the food is very nice and the endless choices can definitely leave you feeling a bit overwhelmed. I suggest taking a quick look around to see what's available that day before you load up your plate and definitely don't take too much of any one item. Be adventurous - try different things! 

I think overrall this buffet is worth the price because it's AYCE and truly one of the best on the strip (in my opinion). If you have the patience and willing to splurge, it's definitely worth a visit. Make sure you come hungry and ready to get your grub on!

The best buffet on the Strip, hands down, and I've eat a lot of Las Vegas buffets. So many terrific options from breakfast to sushi to comfort food to Mediterranean and it's all top notch! This past weekend, I made it through two rounds of brunch, trying the poached egg dish, spicy teriyaki tofu, kale and green apple pizza, and bananas foster French toast. They also have an island of desserts that features brownies, cheesecakes, cookies and ice cream. I usually roll out of here, barely able to move. The only reason I even dare take off a star is because the cashiers are absolutely the rudest people I've ever met in my life. Not the servers, the cashiers. This past weekend, the cashier chastised my husband and I for walking up to the register before she called us. Then she proceeded to make snarky comments about how we should've waited until she beckoned. Don't most people who show up at a restaurant approach the host staff? There's no signage saying otherwise, so it's strange that we would be criticized for this. Ultimately, the food was so incredible, it made me forget what a pest the front of house was.

The crab legs were great.  My husband also had the lobster claws and said they were wonderful as well. The Creme Brûlée's did not disappoint and the coffee was the perfect finishing touch. Michael was our server and was awesome!
Such a good variety and moderately tasty, but a lot of the food was cold and the desserts lacked flavor.

Been here a few times. Delicious. Consistent. Huge selection. Every station is so good and nicely done.
Extremely clean and sanitary. I'm cautious about buffets. 

Probably the best buffet in town. If you're not sure about which buffet to go to in Vegas, this is the one. Trust me.
Probably the most pricey, but it's worth it.

Breakfast, lunch & dinner are different menus and different prices. It's in the Caesars, so you know it stays busy. Good thing is, now you can get a number and they text you when it's almost your time.

Great service too. So go!!

Prepare to come hungry and leave happy! I highly recommend coming early since the average wait is around 1-2 hours. Luckily, we only waited for about an hour. This buffet is spacious and has LOTS of selections.

I enjoyed their Asian selection. Black chicken stew? It reminds me of my mom's homecooked soup. There's dim sum options, soups, and vegetables as usual. I actually was surprised with the flavoring of the black chicken stew. It's not exactly on point, but it's good enough!

As for the entrees, there's crab legs!! I think we got about 2-3 plates of those. Not only that, but some of the food dishes are served in small portions, which is helpful in preventing you from "overeating." What I mean by that is that you leave more room in your stomach for the other dishes. The sweet potato tater tots were delicious! In addition to the prime rib and the truffle potato gratin!

Some other memorable choices that I've tried was the lobster clam chowder and caprese salad and the artisan sausage. There's seriously lots of things to eat here! Another favorite of mine was the lasagna!!

Now onto the desserts, they have mochi ice cream! Vanilla, Kona Coffee, and Chocolate. I was a bit disappointed there was no mango or green tea, but -shrugs- the dessert was still good. They had French macaroons as well as ice cream! The mango lime sorbet was my favorite along with the creme brulee.

My stomach had the time of its life here. One thing about this place though is the expensive price. With the food selections - there were a variety and there were some hit and miss dishes. However, looking back on it, I would probably say that this is a one-time thing. I enjoyed the food and the experience here, but won't return until my wallet gets fatter.

On a whim, the fiance and I went to try it out. Going on a Sunday during brunch hours, expect to wait in line for half an hr to an hr. Price wise, get ready to break the bank. Expect to pay over $100 bucks for two ppl. Or take the option of doing the VIP for an additional  $98 per person. The catch, you do not have to wait too long in line and will get a seafood tower with your package.So come hungry. Place is extremely huge, and believe me it is one of the buffets that can feed everybody and then some. 

Going into the buffet, they do have a high end selection of Asian food, Mexican food, Southern food, seafood, and minimal on the Italian food (just pizzas and one selection of pasta). Taste of everything was better than your average buffet in Vegas. Try out the bone marrow, the meatballs, pozole, and all the Asian food. These were the type of foods that will have you coming back. I also had the rotesseri chicken (a little dry on some parts).

As for the dessert section, ohhhh boy. You will feel like a little kid in the candy shop. They do have the basic fruits, crepes, gelato, little cakes, cookies. The best part is being able to get such sorts of gummy bears, sour candy, and chocolates like, M&Ms, Butterfingers, and many more.

Only part that was disappointing on our experience was the fruit was not fresh and having cold food. Probably will try during the week. 

Overall, a place you do have to try and say that I have been here.

I'm mixed.


Good food BUT

horrible service and a very cramped space.

I consider it mediocre. 

But that being said, the food was pretty good. 

But at 60 a person the setting and service should rival the food, for a buffet.

I'll stick with the Wynn's buffet.

Bacchanal, is this best you have to offer?!?!

It is but a prime example of what to expect from a buffet. Even more so in Vegas where it is especially over inflated,    considerably overrated, underwhelming, and rather sad.

From the overly mashed mashed potatoes, which ended up being incredibly  gummy in consistency, to the overly sweet ramen and bland pho, to the over cooked and teeth shattering steaks and seafoods, and the not so properly chilled oysters, it was just disappointing. 

Service was attentive during the times they so infrequently visited our table. 

The beverages were all watered down. Not all of them were so terrible though. The soda water was quite pleasant, what my wife and I agree to be the best Bacchanal has to offer. 

We quickly moved to the desserts as our appetites were diminishing at an astonishing rate. Desserts are what I typically consider the saving grace for all buffets. Unfortunately Bacchanal is an exception to this. Many of their desserts were texturally off. Let's not mention their tastes. Some of the malt balls which were meant to add some textural contrast were stale and/or soggy. We did enjoy the Vietnamese coffee pudding and their black sesame gelato and their chocolate covered strawberries though. 

Sooo unless you want to saturate yourself with soda water, Vietnamese coffee dessert, black sesame gelato, and dessert strawberries, please do yourself a favor and steer clear of this place.
Hands down the best buffet in Vegas. The options are amazing and the selections are enormous. Shrimp and grits, truffle pizza, lobster Benedict, bread Mac and cheese, are some of the must tries.

We enjoy this buffet so much. My wife and I have been coming to Las Vegas every July for the past 4 years and the Bacchanal never disappoints.

Our server, Esmeralda, was absolutely great. Very attentive and friendly.  If you can, try to sit in her section.  She'll make the Buffett an even more pleasant experience. 

The food quality is excellent and they have a wide variety to choose from. They have:

Chinese: dim sum, duck, rice, noodles, soups
Japanese: Sushi, Sashimi, noodle soups
Italian: pastas and pizzas
Mexican: Tacos, soups such as pozole and 7 mares. 
Seafood: crab legs, shrimp, mussels, oysters
Meats: Wagyu beef, prime rib, tri tip, brisket, sausages, bacon, and my personal favorite, lamb. This year they served lamb t bones. In past years they had lamb chops. 

That's just what I remember. I don't have more details about the Italian food because I usually stay away from fillers like bread, pasta, noodles and rice. I'm Mexican so I don't really eat from the Mexican section. 

If you're looking for a good buffet in Vegas, you should definitely try the Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace.

The best buffet in Vegas. You can skip the hella long line if diamond/platinum member. Bone marrow, truffle mushroom soup, roasted pork belly, and desert are my favorite items. I would always come back if I travel to Vegas again. This is my 3rd time dine-in here.

Excellent food, service and value. 

Our go to buffet whenever we are in Vegas.

Their seafood was very fresh ! Extensive selection of dishes and dessert.
Lives up to the hype.  Loved the red velvet pancakes, crepes, and unlimited crab legs.  Also loved the fresh assortment of juices, especially watermelon.  Overall, definitely recommend.

This place is fucking amazing! Oh my GAWD! I just love this buffet so much, and it's for sure worth the money! I have been here each time I come to Vegas and it never disappoints. This last time we went for dinner opted for VIP and let's just say I'll NEVER go back to standing in line if I can help it. Unlimited Champagne and crab legs sounds like an amazing start of a night. Or end depending on how much you throw back. LOL. I had about 10 glasses of champagne and was feeling L O V E L Y the servers were EXTREMELY attentive, at one point I was even drinking two champagnes at a time. (Don't judge!) The food from start to finish is amazing! I can't wait to go back to Vegas in June.

We had been going to Belagio buffet for years. This time around read Bacchanal has a higher review and decided to give it a chance. 
As far as service is concerned, it was starting promising. As we were standing in line, the manager learned we had a service dog with us, asked all the right questions (allowed by law), gave us the table by the far wall to keep away from foot traffic. 
Things in this department went south in a hurry as I asked for a bawl of water for my dog. We have 101 F outside as an FYI.
The waiter said they are not allowed. Hoping same manager can be helpful to override this rather absurd rule ( first time in years have we been denied water for a dog), but as she stopped by our table, there was no negotiation whatsoever. Manager just rattled the narrative of the rule and that they even don't have disposable containers of any sort (not true- see photo, they serve drinks in plastic cups). When there is a will, there is a way.  But it was another NO. Period. End of conversation.
Of course I managed this my way, by washing this cup and filling w water from my glass.

I wanted to order a beer to go along with a meat dish. Waited for server to surface until I was done with it, ready for desert.

Crab legs and claws most people come for to LV buffets for were tiny, rubbery and oversalted. 

Interior is nothing to write home about- noisy, forgettable, no table clothes (not even paper).
Sorry to admit, but the $52.95 pp we paid  to join the eating party, was a complete waste of money and time. 

My suspicion is the reason they get favorable reviews is because , if you book your seat through this Yelp app , you get a free alcoholic beverage with paid buffet admission.

Well, gamble at your own risk, but we are going to Bellagio if hungry for buffet.
Jennifer is fantastic! Everything looks and tastes amazing. The line was short so we could quickly stuff our faces with all the delicious scents that made us drift in

Fantastic Server Esmeralda!!! 
Excited to eat everything, there is so much food. 
Crab legs are phenomenal

I've had this buffet three times now - so I can say for certain that my rating on this place accurately reflects how I really think about it.  I'm unable to give halves so 4 stars will have to do (if I was able to give halves, I'd give it a 3.5).

From first having it years ago, to most recently 2 months ago, I still feel like Bacchanal Buffet is so incredibly underwhelming especially when it's reached legendary status in the world of Vegas Buffets.  Sure, they do have a huge and wide selection of all different types of foods, but I feel every single one is just "meh" *Shoulder shrugs*.  The price has risen from $50 when I first had it to $75 most recently.  The food is just "alright", however the service, ambience and decor is definitely up there.  (When it comes to Vegas buffets, I've had one that beats Bacchanal out of the park: Wynn).  Although I've remained unimpressed by Bacchanal, I do believe that it's worth visiting just for the experience and the "I've Been There" factor.
Loved this buffet and the selection from all the buffets i have tried in Vegas.  Go early, line gets packed ljke all others.

False advertisement alert! There is no Alaskan crab legs ever included with the buffet.  Doesn't matter what is advertised and even written on the food line sign.  I have even been here twice! It's dishonest that the line cook even says it's in there and when I said I don't see any that's when they sent me to the hostess.  Where the hostess told me "you have to pay 25 to 50 per pound of Alaskan King Crab legs."  Go somewhere else that's cheaper with better quality and does not rip off the consumer like this place!
Una excelente opción para comer rico variado y para todos los gustos, los dumplings dejan algo que desear no son tan ricos el cangrejo u camarones lo mejor, ah y no dejes de probar los postres
my favorite buffet so far, buffet is all about the quality of food, most them are pretty fresh. I would love to recommand all my buddies 100%%

While planning out my trip to Las Vegas, the thing I wanted to do the most was eat at Bacchanal Buffet. I have heard so many great things about this place, and I'm so happy I dined here. Despite the hefty price, I throughly enjoyed my meal. The only thing I didn't like was that we were seated next to a very large party that stood around even after they finished their meal disturbing everyone else eating around them. 

Pros:
- A HUGE selection of food to choose from ~ They have everything from crab legs, to sushi, to tacos, and pizza
- Everything tasted amazing 
- Great service

Cons:
- Very long wait ~ We waited in line for about 1 hour 
- Very expensive 
- Hard to find ~ Caesars Palace is a huge hotel/casino. I wish there were more signs directing which way to go

Overall:
- When in Vegas, going to a buffet is a must and if you had to choose just one, I would definitely choose Bacchanal Buffet
The Best buffet in Las Vegas. Lots of selections, great atmosphere, superb service. Make sure you have a big appetite when you eat here

Terrrrrrible ... 140$ ridiculous wait time and the worst dinner I've had in Vegas yet ... meat station was extremely dry.  Sushi looked old ... and the "lobster claws" tasted like water, ZERO flavor ... I've never in my life have thrown away lobster before ... macaroni and cheese was defiantly undercooked and all the "chilled" seafood was still frozen  

Save your money go to station casinos for 12$ buffet

Omg. The dessert buffet. The lemon bars, chocolate covered strawberries, Nutella filled beignets, and the egg custard tart were deliscious. I feel i got my money's worth on dessert alone!!!!!!!!!! Best dessert buffet ever. 

Sorry no review on food lol. Got here at 6pm, wait was like 20 minutes. 

Negatives: mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese were not so good. 

Positives: cheeses, spare ribs, crab legs. Osso bucco

Honestly not worth the wait, the food was okay and it was cold idk if it because we ate around 8pm but yeah super cold. They only part of the buffet that was actually pretty good was the Mexican food and the desert buffet. You would also think because they have you wait 2-3 hours to seat you that they would have more servers but I only saw one server serving. Poor girl looked like a chicken with her head cut off. 
Well at least I can say I ate here but will I return I don't think so.
Long wait, uncomfortable seating, cold food, and flat soda. Disappointed. Would not return.
First time in vegas n i really loved this place, expensive if you ask me, but definetely good place to eat all u can

I think we have been here twice during our trip.

They have a ton of variety Chinese/Asian, Mexican, bbq, seafood, Hawaiin, Vietnamese, pho, American, Italian etc. just name it!! I don't think they had Mediterranean the day we went, we couldn't find it. It was a Saturday. 

Personal favorite: taco stand (al pastor is great)
Dessert selection is amazing (ice cream , donuts, mousses, cakes, pudding, muffins, gelatos etc) 

If you come here early (15 mins when the buffet starts then you can easily get in fast before the items are running out. Otherwise there is a huge line to kill)

The BEST BUFFET, I have ever been to. They have the largest selection of food here its unbelievable. I would come here for dinner and skip lunch just to fit more food in. The seafood here was delicious, they offered cold and hot versions. They had clams, oysters, mussels, crab legs, jumbo shrimp etc. The prime rib was the consistency of butter, the best I have ever had. The lamb chops were also to die for. I enjoyed the asian soup dumplings and sushi and nigiri. The lasagna was delicious, as was the lobster and corn bisque and wagu beef sliders. The dessert selection was huge, they had gelato, sorbet, mochi, crepes, cupcakes, tiramisu, macarons, and so much more. I was informed that they make special desserts as well. I was delighted to have a banana soufflé...Ok this was no joke the best thing I have ever eaten in my entire life. I had two. I would actually just go here for these even. Really an incredible experience. The wet napkins they have are actually warmed, wet towels individually wrapped. I would make it a point to come to this buffet. Amazing selection, incredible quality, more pricey but worth every penny.

This was my first casino buffet experience so I want to first say that I am not an expert on this matter. 


As a self proclaimed foodie, I definitely had built up a lot of excitement around the buffet experienced. Before our Vegas trip, I did my research to find the BEST buffet. 

We arrived at 1 on a Friday afternoon and waited about 20 minutes to get in. The space was really pretty and well organized. 

We tried food at all the stations and my favorite was definitely the ready to eat/shelled shrimp. We did not think the crab was very good. I enjoyed that they had a lot of seafood offered. I also really liked some of the Italian food. There was a huge selection of desserts, my favorite being the mini creme brûlée. 

I think next time we are in Vegas, I would try a slightly more affordable buffet but I am still glad we visited this one.

Lots of choices, our favorite buffet in Las Vegas. They have food choices from all over the world so you will most likely find something you will like. I would go back but I would want to be very hungry for the price.

Rereading my review and I think my stars didn't really match my words. I would return here without complaint. It is not a cheap buffet by any means but it was good food. I would recommend the place easily.

I have attended the buffet at Caesar's in the past for breakfast and lunch. It was always delicious. My downfall is that my stomach feels full really quickly so I skipped many of the offerings. However, this past trip, after watching the amazing video showing the care that chef, Leticia Nunez, takes each and every day, I decided to try the dinner buffet and follow her lead of only taking a spoonful of each dish to make sure it garners her approval. So I took only a taste of each dish--sometimes directly on my plate; other times in the small black cups provided. What a wonderful experience! I took my time between choices and ended up feeling like I had visited a world of tastes without feeling stuffed. Starting with the truffle mushroom soup could have been my downfall--it was so delicious I was tempted to taste more. But I kept on the mission of only tasting. The rosemary peppers in lemon oil were amazing, as were the batter fried green beans with aioli dip--such a light batter and superb taste. (I would love to know the recipe and process.) Prime rib--perfect. "Grandmother's Meatballs"--delicious. Shumai and all of the Asian-inspired dishes, delicious. Lovely to have cheese and nuts which tend to be my finale to a meal. Though I didn't indulge in the Mexican dishes, except for the shredded port (delicious), I noticed that everyone around me loved them and enjoyed the one-on-one creations with the cook. Since I'm from Maine and am surrounded by seafood, I didn't try anything in that theme so I can't comment, although the shrimp bayou chowder was amazing, as were the other Southern themed dishes. Desserts--I am not a "sweets" person but do love creme brulee (great) and found a new favorite--the Vietnamese Coffee.
All in all, I ended up tasting more than 20 offerings and thank you Chef Nunez. You are an amazing chef, organizer, leader, and inspiration!
Muy bueno el lugar de la Vegas buena comida muy amables todos el establecimiento muy limpio todo elegante

Pretty disappointed in the food quality and service. 

Went during Labor Day weekend and was super excited to try the food. A lot of the food that we tried was salty and did not hold up the expectations. 


Plus, while eating couple of us on our table(as well as another table) got splashed with some sauce. It was literally all over my hair, clothes, and even chair. Honestly lost my appetite. Spoke to the manager who didn't seem to care and asked if I wanted a complimentary mimosa..... wth.

Not worth the wait or money. Wouldn't go again. I suppose if you have loyalty status the wait isn't as long. But we didn't and waited 90 minutes to be seated. Once we ate, the food was good, but not great.

Demasiado alto el precio fueron $141 por 2 personas y la comida es muy simple como cualquier bufet de precio más bajo. La carne estaba simple, la comida faltaba sal o más sabor.q Tenia muy buenas expectativas pero salí muy decepcionada, y mi cerveza tenía un mosquito.

What's a better wedding gift than the gift of a never ending buffet at Caesar's Palace?
Nothing. Absolutely nothing. 
We got there at about 3:10 pm and waited no more than 10 minutes. 
The hosts were so friendly and pleasant. 
When seated our server came over and introduced herself and explained how the buffet worked and what her favorite foods were. 
After that we were off in a mad dash to the crab legs and meats!
The aromas in the room were intoxicating. 
I practically floated through that buffet. 
The food was delicious and beautifully displayed. 
I never once felt like I was trash at a regular buffet. I actually felt like high class trash at a fancy pinky up buffet. 
After dinner we hit up the never ending dessert table which I must have fainted twice because I walked outta this buffet happy, confused, and in a haze. 
The food was amazing just like the experience and the service. 
If you're in Vegas, this is a must. 
If you're not in Vegas just watch videos on the buffet on YouTube.

Nothing to rave about. Yes they had a LOT of options - Asian, Hispanic, seafood, comfort food, Italian, desserts. Did not feel like anything I tried was actually that good, would not have been happy with the individual items if it was not a buffet. Rice in the sashimi was hard as well as the Mac and cheese noodles. Crab claws served not legs. Would spend the same price at another restaurant for better quality food that is still filling. Friendly front desk service and free mimosa with Yelp check-in, but probably won't go back now that I've gone once.

Not a bad buffet.  We got to try them for breakfast/brunch.  We really wanted to try them for dinner, but didn't get the chance to do that.  The buffet for this time came with shrimps and mussels.  They don't do the crab legs or oysters this early. They also had their steak bar going on with prime rib, and steak tips, ham, and different kinds of sausages.  They had a really good dessert bar.  It was pretty much average breakfast items.  The layout was very nice.  I liked that the food didn't have too much sodium going on.  I think the flavor was just right.  For 2 people's breakfast, our ticket was about $86 and the buffet includes our drinks (non alcoholic).  If you want to do unlimited alcoholic beverages, it is an extra $15.  I think that for forty something dollars per person, it was a little too overpriced for what they had to offer, especially for breakfast.  I travel to casinos often, and buffets like this are usually $20-30 the most for breakfast.

This was by far the BEST buffet and worth the $130 for two adults! We went to the Sunday brunch around 1pm and we did have to wait in line about 20-30 minutes but it was WORTH IT! Wynn has NOTHING on Bacchanal! 
With that being said, the only reason I cannot give them 5 stars is because...we purposely went between 9a-3:30pm because that was brunch hours. With that being said, there was only 4 breakfast items (sausage, bacon, hash browns, and over easy eggs) that's it! No muffins, pancakes, waffles- NOTHING. It was mainly lunch and dinner. My Husband whom picked the time and place was very disappointed as he was expecting more breakfast items and BRUNCH. I on the other hand, was in heaven- i like lunch and dinner. 
I do think that was VERY disappointing and deceiving. If you are looking for BREAKFAST, unless they served more breakfast items before 1pm I would skip this location.

Although my husband and I didn't travel to Vegas to gamble (we traveled to Vegas to drive out to California), we couldn't pass up the opportunity to try a Vegas buffet. The Bacchanal didn't disappoint!

We luckily arrived to no line but not even 10 minutes later the waiting line to get in was huge! The buffet is very large and extends from the front of the restaurant to the back. I am sure all Vegas buffets have great service but the waitstaff was very attentive. Everyone was friendly and we had someone checking in on us every 10 minutes or so (maybe less.) 

The king crab legs were not self serve but the portions given for each plate were substantial. The crab meat was very sweet so I was happy (it's always a gamble at a buffet!) The variety of food was extensive: Mexican, Italian, Asian, American, Indian and much more. The quality of everything I ate was delicious; I don't believe there was anything I tried that I didn't like. My favorites were the variety of dumpling and Chinese buns, and all of the shellfish of course!

We spent about 2.5 hours here, I tried to tackle as much as I could before  desperately wishing I had on sweatpants. I read a lot of reviews before committing to the Bacchanal (because there are a million Vegas buffets) but I definitely recommend this one!

Selection is HUGE! I enjoyed eating to my heart's content. Is everything perfect, no, but for such a wide range of options, I feel it delivers quite well. I felt a tried quite a bit of so many things that were average to above. If you really want something made really well, go to a place that specializes in that item. If you want a place that is going to give everyone a nice variety/selection of choices this is it.

Hands-down the absolute best place for a breakfast buffet on the strip. Not only is the food absolutely delicious there are so many varieties that I don't think it is possible to try everyone in one sitting. This is our third time this week. Special thanks to our server Romilus who was fantastic.

Wait time: 2:30+ on a Friday. While we waited we got hungrier & hungrier. (I thought perhaps it's why everyone rates it so high, becuz after this long anything is going to taste good) Arrived about 6pm. The food was not the greatest. The wait, the price, or the food, plus they don't validate parking is just not worth coming back. (You'd think after dropping almost $650, they'd at least cover your parking). Overrated, don't bother!

Was the food good?

Sure.

Was it worth the wait?

Eh.

Would I return?

No.

Don't get me wrong - the food was okay, the desserts were better, and overall the company really saved the meal experience for me. However, the only word that really comes to mind with Bacchanal is "overrated". If time is a commodity for you during your trip to Vegas, I'd recommend finding somewhere else to eat.
I was shocked at the prices for a brunch.  I thought only a few items were really good.  The other items were mediocre
Horrid breakfast food selections if you're an average American. Can't recommend, will never return!

Waited a little under an hour for our group of 13 on a Saturday at around 2:30 pm to pay lunch prices for dinner menu (saved $5 pp). No reservations available unless you book VIP package. I was pretty impressed by the selection of food available. Most of the food looked good but just tasted average. Service was pretty good as well. Check in on yelp for a free wine, champagne, or beer. Go for the steamed snow crab legs at the Italian station and dip it in the hot butter sauce. I liked the steamed version more than the chilled. The garlic spicy shrimp at the Chinese station was delicious too. The dessert station was huge! I liked the made to order crepe with Nutella and mango gelato.

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS.

Sunday Brunch includes bottomless mimosas and food is AMAZING. Endless crab legs that are already pre-sliced for you so you don't have to work to get at the meat. The selection here is also SO GREAT. Chinese food, sushi, pho (vietnamese), freshly sliced selection of meats and seafood galore. I love coming here even though the wait is usually long (~1-1.5 hours if you don't come early). We had a party of 6 which waits in a separate line (groups of 6+) and the wait was approximately 30 minutes.

Make sure you leave room for dessert because you won't want to miss out! The freshly made crepes are my favorite and you get to choose the sauces they put on top along with the fruit and sweet toppings to add on.

Mediocre.  For the price, there's barely any seafood besides crabs legs.  Everything looks average and does not reflect the premium buffet it is known to be.  For 65.00 a person, I'll rather spend it at a regular sit down restaurant than mass produced buffet food.

This place is always on those "Top Vegas Buffets" list and out of all the rest, this one is definitely the best. The food is always fresh and restocked (is that how it's referred as?). There's not an 'endless' selection of dishes like some other buffets because they focus on making their selected dishes great. They have a big seafood selection so it's a shame I don't like fish or oysters. However the crab legs and shrimp are delicious. It can get busy so try to avoid normal lunch and dinner hours. We got there at 2:30p and there wasn't a wait.

I came here on a Monday afternoon and we were fortunate to have been seated immediately; I feel like it's also a fantastic value on the weekdays, with a brunch base price of $40. 

The fun part is obviously going through the buffet for the first time, trying to fill your plate as full as possible. There are Asian, Latin, Breakfast, seafood, Italian, and health-conscious sections to name a few, and I opted to try a little bit of each. I would definitely recommend the made-to-order tacos; there's a nice selection of toppings as well so you can customize however you wish. I was also pleasantly surprised to see that they had Horchata! Unfortunately, I may have gotten too filled up on that. 

If there was one thing that I was slightly disappointed by, it was the carved meat selection that they had. I felt that the meat I had was pretty dry and I decided to not finish it. 

The dessert selection here is extremely impressive, with a wide array of different flavors and nations represented. I loved the Creme Brulee and Tres Leches cake. I also enjoyed the Tiramisu and the Chinese Egg Tart (which I wished had been a bit warmer, but meh, not a huge issue). 

Overall, I had a great experience at Bacchanal and I can definitely see why so many people praise it as the best buffet in Vegas. The selection is fantastic, the food is tasty, and the price is right; I would definitely recommend Bacchanal to anyone who wants to eat their way around Vegas!
Loved this buffet! So good and the wait was really quick, we went just before dinner buffet and had the better pricing.

The wait/process to get in is a 1 - horrible, awful wait times. Took us 3 hours on a Monday afternoon from 3-6pm to get in. A cramped wait line for the last 2 hours, and then wait in line for most buffet items. Flat out not worth it, even if the food was amazing (which only a couple of items are). 
The food is very hit-and-miss. The snow crab legs and shrimp and stone crab claws are phenomenal. The beef, sausage, pizza, ribs, and every American items are incredibly awful - as in spit-it-out bad. As was the fried rice, dim sum. 
To end on an up note, there is a dessert square we almost missed with made-to-order crepes. And the waiter was nice - but over-worked. 
Not coming back.
So many varieties & a super duper long wait. gave me the worst diarrhea of my life never again

Pricy and overrated. The stone crab claws were not good the snow crab legs were super salty. There was a good variety but most things were forgettable. The best dish there was the pho. Desserts were typical buffet standard.
If this is your first time in Vegas, this restaurant is a MUST. Add it to your to-do list! Expensive, yes, worth it? Every time.

Best Buffet I went to. It had a really nice variety and a general good quality to the food. It's hard to pick out the best foods at a buffet, but I loved the truffle mushroom pizza. And they had lots of cute desserts, including I've ice cream. How fun!

Came here with a Groupon for an early "dinner" (more like late lunch since it's 3-5pm only). You have to pay tax when entering so our Groupon was $110 and then an extra $9.

The "VIP" line is not really faster. There are 2 lines - one to pay and one to wait to sit. You can VIP through the pay line but we still waited 30mins to sit, and it wasn't even a peak time. 

Now the food - yes, there are steamed and chilled crab legs. The legs are pretty awesome but don't expect King Crab - there's none of that. Sushi was a lot better than other buffets and then they have all your standard buffet fare: BBQ, prime rib, pasta, pizza, etc. The seafood was a standout (skip the oysters though) as well as their varied Asian section which included childhood favorites of mine like stuffed lotus leaf, fried shishito peppers and an array of dim sum!

Now for the Groupon deal - this is worth it for the seafood alone, but at normal price, I'm not sure that I'd come back. After being wowed by the unusual offerings at The Wicked Spoon (and for a way lower price $28 for brunch) this was expected but not stellar. 

My husband however disagreed as he loved it so we compromised on 4/5 stars.

Expensive? Yes. $50pp. Worth it? HECK YES!  

Seriously folks, this buffet will RUIN you for all other buffets. The other buffet we ate at, (Bellagio) was a joke compared to this one. This one is just in a class by itself.  If you only can afford to go to one buffet in Vegas, make it this one. My boyfriend and I are tight-wads when it comes to money, and we grimaced when they swiped our cards for this meal, but you honestly get your money's worth here. 

If you love Chinese or Japanese food, this is the place for you. If you're a seafood or meat lover, this is the place for you. Every dessert IMAGINABLE.

The only station that was not on par with everything other cuisine was the Mexican station. They only had a single type of taco (no vegetarian option - no bueno) and nachos.

Note: the price DOES INCLUDE sodas, teas, etc.

If you're planning your trip to Vegas and you're there from Friday through Monday, don't go on a Friday or Saturday if you can avoid it only because the line to get in will be long. We went on a Monday night and 'only' had to wait 15-20 mins (and we got there early around 6).

I put very high expectations because of all the recommendations and videos I had seen prior to coming here. Also add in the fact that My family decided for our family Vegas trip, this would be the only buffet we would eat because it was so expensive, so my overall experience would fairly warrant a 3/5. First the food is really really good, I love shrimp but I have to argue that this buffet has probably the best shrimp that I've ever had in my life. Other notable dishes were the lobster Mac n cheese, clam chowder, and prime rib. The setup for the food is rather convenient because it's basically this really long line that goes only one way and has each section split into different cultural areas like most other buffets, starts from Chinese to Japanese/sushi to deli to Mexican to American. Also idk how they make their peach tea, but it taste incredibly fresh and unlike anything that I've ever drank. 

 So there are a few downsides unfortunately and I say this with all the respect that this establishment deserves. First the seats feel really old and uncomfortable, like they were the leftovers seats of the actual hotel rooms. Second, the food selection wasn't very large imo (Chinese section had very basic entrees you could get from Panda Express, only 3 choices for sushi which were in some form of California rolls, taco setup is supposed to mimic street tacos trucks but it doesn't work too well because it seems still like a very basic constructed method of cooking on what seems to be a giant circular hibachi grill) and there wasn't as many things that seemed actually appetizing, however the foods that I did want were phenomenal. Third, our server we saw literally only 3 times, there didn't seem to be a huge wait staff which doesn't make sense for such a high end buffet. Fourth has mainly to do with me, I have moderate anxiety when being around large crowds and just being in the lines to get food made me feel really rushed in carefully looking at what I wanted, I just felt like 80 percent of the time I was diving in and picking out whatever I could remember because of like 10 people watching me get some food.

I will not be coming back here because it just seems like a $25 buffet priced for 3x the price. However If someone asks me about the food here I will rave about the very specific items that I really did like.

After hearing the big hype about the Bacchanal we decided to try it.  $60 per person is really expensive compared  to other buffets on the strip but since this was supposed to be the best we had high expectations.  Friendly staff at the register which was expected as they are happy to take your money.  But as soon as we got in that was a different story.  We were meet by one of the hostesses that had a bad attitude which she passed us over to another hostess that seated us and her attitude was equally bad. They made us feel like we're are bothering them for being here. Our sever was friendly and brought us our drinks. After that we never saw him again. We Had to ask other severs for drinks, napkins, straws and she was extremely stressed out and didn't have time to wait on us. She kept saying out loud "I can't do everything myself". With the exception of poor service  and hostesses with attitude, the food was excellent.

Really fun experience! The buffet is huge, fancy, and very dimly lit (so it feels even more fancy). Me and my boyfriend got the brunch Groupon which comes out to about $80 for two. Pretty steep pricing but hey, how often are you in Vegas? 

Parking in the nearby garage is $12 for 1-4 hours (a real scam, thanks a lot caesars palace). Zero line when we came at 10 am on a Monday but by noon the line was insanely long. However, the Groupon comes with a front of the line pass so even if we came later it should have been fine.

Little service, you have to flag down servers to get drinks and our plates were cleared maybe twice in 2.5 hours.

From 10-12 it was almost solely brunch foods but after noon they brought out the crab legs, wagyu beef, fish tacos, etc! Really great to have so much variety included in brunch pricing. I don't actually like crab legs but I appreciate having the option for brunch! The foods that stood out to me were the tri-tip, mini breakfast croissants, gelato bar, custom omelettes and crepes, mini cakes, and lobster bisque. 

Most of the stuff was very high quality and yummy and there was everything from pasta to ceviche to clam chowder to tonkotsu ramen. Before they started bringing out more lunch stuff at noon there were definitely too many egg dishes (eggs Benedict, egg tacos, omelette, steak and eggs, etc) but at least they were all solid. I think I must have eaten at least 6-7 poached or scrambled eggs while I was here.

Things to avoid: The tuna nigiri was absolutely the worst thing I've ever eaten I almost threw up. Yes it may be my fault for getting sushi at a buffet but don't make the same mistake as me!! Pizza if it looks like it's been sitting out for awhile. Or really anything that looks like it's been sitting out for awhile. Prime rib was very tough and tasteless, and the second round I got was very rare and tasteless. Dim sum was really really bad.

Would really recommend this buffet if you have the chance to go! A few dishes really suck but the vast majority are tasty! So many foods, it's like window shopping for your stomach.
I like it a lot. The food was very please and could satisfy all pallets. The only thumbs down I would give is the two hour time limit.

The wait time is way out of the ying to the yang!!! (3hrs) They have a good variety of foods but it was coldyou'd think they'd have warmers or something but it was not even warm. Had to line up for crab, staff took awhile to serve us drinks, dessert choices are probably the only thing that made up for the time we stayed in line. 
Tried it and won't be back.

Best buffet in LV hands down! 
So many dishes to choose from and the quality is really good. When you have bone marrow on the menu you know the standard is high! Everything is super clean. Since we were diamond members of Caesars we only stood in line for about 5 minutes. Which was also a great perk! Will be back if we come back to Vegas!

5 stars again. Must try. Best buffet in Vegas. 

$15 all you can drink alcohol. Try to save room in your stomach and just drink wine or champagne. 

Check in on yelp for 1 free alcoholic drink!  Bonus!

Came around 4. No lines. 

Crab - can get it steamed in the Italian station. They have it cooking already over there. 

Different selections from the first time we came here but no complaints. Just don't expect everything you see in the pictures. Food is still great for a buffet. 

Planned it out better this time. Went for the meats first. Seafood second and third. Everything else when I started getting full. 

Service was excellent. Both times was good. I think this time might have been better. Cleared our tables quickly and kept our drinks full. Brought wet towels and crab crackers.

this place deserves 5 stars! yesterday I got to eat 2 slices of pizza 1 bowl of ramen and 2 bowls of Mac and cheese. but for staff they were very nice and also I am glad that I choose to dine here. :D

Bacchanal is probably one of my favorite buffets in Las Vegas and we alway stop by when we visit. They got an assortment of shelled seafood and tons of meat. Their dessert variety are decent. 

This visit was super busy for them. If you have a large party, you get to stand in a special standing waiting line. It took us about 45 minutes of waiting before we got to our table. It appeared they might have been short on the wait staff as well, because we only had our drinks filled once and we had to track down the waitress, who seemed irritated that we did. We also had to track her down to remove all the dirty plates that were stacking up on our table. Our visit to this restaurant is usually a very good one, but this time, due to the poor wait service that will leave a lasting impression, I had to one star this visit. The food still gets a five star.

Heard all about Caesars buffet and thought we'd give it a try for the first time and upgraded our buffet of buffet passes.  Wife and I made a beeline straight for the seafood and crab legs.  Steamed crab legs too!

A little over an hour later and at risk of having to be carted off like award-winning oversized pumpkins, it's easy to see why this place gets rave reviews.  Friendly staff, fresh and often replenished food.  And did I mention the crab legs?  They also have gelato and an overall amazing dessert area.

The food is great.  Is it worth $75 including tip?  For once in a lifetime yes.  Did I eat enough food to surpass the $75 bill?  Of course I did.  I ate 2 platters of shrimp, had prime rib, their bbq pork ribs and plenty of desserts.  The best dish I ate was the bbq pork ribs, it was a dry rub, moist and juicy.  The prime rib was phenomenal.  There is so much to choose from.  Why a 4 star instead of a 5?  Bc I'm not totally convinced that this was the best $75 I spent on food.  Vegas is full of places with great food.  There is so much to choose from here and yes majority of everything taste good.  The pizza on the other hand was very subpar, if there was one dish to discontinue there it would be their pizza.  Pizza Hut taste better.  Their Mac and cheese was great.  My wife's favorite dish was their corn on the Cobb.  I had many trips to the dessert island.  The best dessert was their chocolate ice cream and Oreo cupcake.  Their ube filled mini cone was great too.  Service is great as usual.

To start the occasion the cashier by the name of alma h was a total B. We tried to pay first and get a table for 4 people there was only 2 of us there and she said we couldn't purchase the buffet first until the whole party was there.  I tried again to purchase the buffet first stating that I'm paying for this not a comp once again she said i couldn't until the rest of the party arrived fine we waited and when i could see the rest of my group i went to pay and she tried to run the same spiel about the group having to all be there i stopped her and told her to stop with i can't ring you up spiel because the rest of my group is right there she tried again to tell me again i can't i told her to stop they are right there talk about a major B.  I don't know what was going on today they ran out of plates the food was empty on a lot of spots.  I haven't been here in about a year major disappointment to past experiences never had a problem with purchasing the buffet before my whole group was there which was more than a couple of times and never seen the shortage of plates or food items.  For a friday night I've seen better from here.  Once again very disappointing.

Oooooh my.. words cannot describe the love I have for Bacchanal Buffet. 

Upon walking into the buffet I felt like I was transported into a modern, chic version of food heaven. I honestly could not look around without my mouth watering from the vast choices and options I had in front of me.

-Feeling like seafood? You can indulge yourself in the mountain of crab legs they offer. (Be sure you give the shrimp some love too!)

-Not feeling crabby? Their carving station offers a variety of perfectly cooked meats from prime rib to brisket. 

-Maybe you're looking to travel around the world? If that's the case, Bacchanal offers Mexican, Asian, and Italian food that will definitely keep you coming back for more.

-Maybe you're looking to satisfy your sweet tooth.. Well don't worry, the dessert option is plentiful and just as delicious as everything else this place has to offer. I mean, any place that has chocolate covered strawberries automatically earns an extra star from me. 

If all of this wasn't enough to convince you, I first went to Bacchanal for dinner and came back the next day for lunch. That's how good it was.

Best buffet in Vegas! They have a little bit of everything Asian(Chinese Japanese and Vietnamese) Italian and American of course. By far they have the largest selection. There quality is always spot on. The staff is well trained as usual for Caesars Entertainment. Just to let you know depending on the season and time the lines can get long and I mean longgggggggg! So if your planning to go there get there at least 2 hours early.

made my way back to Bacchanal but for brunch this time and i was just as impressed with this experience as i was with my dinner one! brunch starts at 7am on saturday and sunday but there was no way that our group was going to make it at that time haha. our group of 8 showed up closer to 11am on a saturday morning and there was NO LINE! 

price is $41 for brunch and that includes unlimited mimosas :) note that if you are with a party of 8, then they will charge 18% gratuity so make sure to mention your group size when you are purchasing your meal. we didnt know this so after we had paid separately without gratuity included, we all had to go back to the cashier and get gratuity added to our total - was a bit confusing but no biggie.

we got seated right away and off to the food! there were a lot of breakfast-y items at 11am but as time progressed, we did notice food items being changed out so it was kind of cool that every time you looked at the food, you could find something different to try. seafood options included crab legs, shrimp cocktail and mussels. the carving station had a ton of options too like prime rib, beef brisket (my fave), ham, sausage, and more that i can't even remember. and omg i loved all the asian food that i tried! the har gow, congee, fried rice, chow mein, ramen - it was all legit! also loved the tacos that are made fresh for you. i stumbled upon this toward the end of the meal i had to make room for these and im glad i did cuz they were delicious! oh and desserts too - fresh churros, souflees, lava cake, ice cream, and gelato. perfect way to end the meal. we were told there was a 2 hour time limit for the table and we definitely used the entire time to eat and drink the morning away :)
Not to expensive at 69 dollars a head worth it. everything was amazing good +sushi was AAA

I do not like buffets but I had to try this one since it is considered one of the best in Vegas. Everything that I sampled here was really good. The street tacos are made to order, the chicken was crispy and seasoned well, the crab legs were huuuge and even the desserts were delicious, I will definitely be back!

I wish I could give this place 6-stars. I even changed my last meal on earth in my profile to Bacchanal Buffet- it was that good.

Weekends are WAY more expensive because of brunch. We had a little mishap when we called and asked for prices and were given the wrong information. When we told the cashier that- she said that we should have called the buffet and not the hotel. WTF- you work there, right?

Anyways- it was off-season in Vegas, so we only waited about 10-minutes before being seated. Because it was brunch, mimosas were complimentary and we were going to get our money's worth. We 

I seriously could list out all the food that I ate, but that would be a super, super long review. If you want to know- you can see the photos I posted while here. Everything was scrumptious!

A couple of standouts:
- Beef brisket: It was smokey, tender and came in a big slab on your plate. You could break apart the meat with your fork with little effort. This one of my favorite things.

- Eggs Benedict with skirt steak: A small individual portion served in a cast iron skillet. The egg yolk was calling my name from across the restaurant. I ate two without any effort, but had to contain myself before going back for a third. They also have this same dish with fried chicken instead. I wanted beef. The meat is tender and has that nice grilled flavor. Break the egg and it's like a slop of heaven soaking into your bottom piece of English muffin.

Quail egg flatbread: This came lathered with small little over-medium eggs and bacon. The outer crust was crispy and you heard that crunch when you broke it apart or took a bite. It definitely had that wood-brick oven taste, though, I'm not sure how it was cooked. 

I am just going to say that you HAVE to eat here at least once. Like a tourist destination, you should make it a PRIORITY. Screw the bodies exhibit, screw the Grand Canyon- you need to go to Caesar's Palace for their Bacchanal Buffet. It's seriously worth it.

Great buffet, worth the extra money. Tons of good food choices here and very fresh food. Special shout out to the chefs on the grill area including Steven who was helpful and friendly to patrons. Service was good from all staff and dining area was clean. Save extra room for desserts as there are tons and good quality as well. Will be back.

I call BS on this. All you lying bastards out there, yall owe me money! Ya heard???

OMG lol. My experience fell super flat. Here goes:

At about $60 per person on a weekday dinner, I am cheated, slighted, betrayed, lied to, lied upon, lied under, lied sideways, you understand? I tried a bunch of food, but here are the main high lights. 

Let's start with some good stuff:
- Brisket = DELISH. Nice bark on the outside, by far one of the best briskets Ive had, juicy, tender, and very tasty. 5 stars.
- Bacon =  OKAY, OKAY. Smokey, got a bit of chew, but definitely enjoyable. 4.5 stars
- Lobster Bisque = MHMM MHMM. Not picking up on the lobster taste too much, but I like the velvety, creamy consistency. 4 stars
- Crab legs = Since this goes out the door super fast, they remain moist and fresh and tasty. 4 stars.
- Desserts = Hit or miss. 3 stars.
- Orange juice = FRESH. 5 stars.

And that's where it ends.

Here's the list of the HOW DARE YOUs.
- American wagyu = Bland, tasteless, and CHEWY. 2 stars.
- Beef Ribs = Tasty, but TOUGH. The edible part is like 2%. 2 stars.
- Stone Crab Claws = Impressive to look at, but OVERCOOKED. Pass. 1 star.
-  Clam Chowder = More like Butter Chowder. 1 star.
- Pizza = tried two different ones, both very soggy. Tasty though. 2 stars.
- Steak Burger = Please go ahead and grind this into an actual burger, because that steak was disappointing. 1 star.
- Mashed potatoes = almost warm. Overly engineered, but okay. 2 stars.
- Dim sum items = ew. 1 star.

And oh, did I mention the long long looooong wait to get in? It was give or take an hour or so just standing there, and if youre in a much bigger crowd, prepare thy self!

All in all, I feel completely duped. Service was fast and friendly so not a complete disaster, but I mean, I 95% came for the food, and they did not deliver on the items I was excited about. Food temperatures were off (hot food werent hot, cold items were lukwarm), the seasoning were like a juvenile delinquent in senior high school - not present at all, and the all in all quality just didnt meet expectations especially with all the hype they surround themselves with.

So in short? Food is only good on photo - it's all for the Gram, fam. That's all it is.

I dined at Bacchanal last week for dinner one evening and breakfast a different day.  The food overall was very good and service was good.  The variety at breakfast wasn't as large as dinner, but the food tasted much fresher.   The meat carving section was good but some of the meats were not as flavorful as others. The Wagu Beef was not very flavorful and tri-tip was over cooked.  The remaining meat dishes and seafood was amazing.
Definitely over hyped for sure. Food is honestly just ok. There are a lot of options which is great, but for the two hour wait and the HEFTY price point it definitely is not worth it.

Delicious. Get the hibiscus tea and peach tea if you like something sweet to drink. It's a good. Shrimp tacos are good, brisket potatoes, and carne asada. Seriously the brisket potatoes are great. Cheaper than the buffet at the Wynn and not over crowded. Plenty of space between the tables and very clean. Friendly staff. Thank you Vegas!! Desserts are same as Wynn delicious and plentiful.
This buffet is over-priced. I don't think it's worth the price at all. The food is pretty good and they have a lot of variety but I feel like it's unorganized and pretty regular for $70.

Whoaaaa maybe better than Wicked Spoon buffet at the Cosmo!  My party of 8 were very lucky to get a spot for dinner.  They were sold out for dinner on Saturday night and we were on standby.  Only waited 15 minutes!  I think the lady felt sorry because I looked like a sad, starving puppy so she let us in, but split our group in two, which is fine with me!  They have great selections.  Fresh sushi and crab legs!  My favorite was the dessert bar! OMG the ice cream was mad good!! There is always a line here so come early!!

Ceasars Bacchanal buffet lives up to all the hype!  I think it's probably among the tops as far as buffets goes in Las Vegas, the price is too, but certainly well worth the price.  The buffet is about discovering the semi hidden room off to the end of the buffet line, it houses the area where they have boiled alaskan crab legs, the sushi bar, the asian cuisine area, they have melon soup and it also has the salad fixings in the same area. The asian area has dim sum like steamed pork buns, har gow, siu mai, some version of XLB also, but they have gems like roast duck and barbecued pork and the standby fried rice, chow mein and the unusual sweet potato noodles, like glass noodles but thicker. If you are a seafood lover, this is the place for you, they offer mud crabs, dungness crabs, alaskan crab legs, fresh, very fresh shucked oysters and sea snails.
The cooked meat section has turkey breast, boring, and american wagyu beef and slab bacon, real yum!
I can't do this place justice in a indescribable buffet.
I haven't rven gotten to the dessert area yet, but I leave that up to you to experience, it's well worth it!

We were in Vegas around New Year's, which explains the long wait. We weren't able to eat here, but their wait lines were so unprofessional. We had to print a ticket indicating the time we should come back. It said we only needed to wait around thirty minutes. After thirty minutes we came back and they said that that was the time to come back and start waiting in LINE! We asked them how long we would have to wait in line for, and they told us it would be about two hours until it was our turn. If we do come back, maybe we'll give it another shot and eat again. Other than that, we wasted uber money to get there so we just ate at tacos and the food court, which were really good!

Went to today for an early dinner. All I can say this place was all HYPE. I've been to other buffets that have left a good impression on me. 

The brisket, was dry and tasted like pot roast. Oh the taco bar was decent, in Asian food section wasn't that good at all fried rice tasted  old and the char sui was dry. 

I really did enjoy the crape bar, which was worth the wait. Ended up finding some sopes near the taco bar, Which was quite good. 

You can find alot of food here but it's a hit or miss. 

I suggest to looking at other places, my favorite  places have been in the Cosmo.

Lesson learned - go EARLY. The lines anytime after 11am are ri-fucking-diculous. They have this convoluted system where you queue up in a line that looks legit but is really just a line to receive your wait time - which is anywhere from 1-3 hours. Soooo dumb. The place is enormous and yet they stagger entry. 

Once inside the food offerings are diverse and very good. You will be full ALL DAY. Service is friendly too. Not super fast, but good enough. Price is worth it but go early and leisurely spread out your meal to 2 hours like we did.

Before i even start dont forget its a BUFFET... For BUFFET food it was SALMMIN!!! We arrived around 6/7 and the wait wasnt that bad. We walked around first since there was so many sections and do whatever we wanted. We returned to the table ordered drinks then it was a non stop feast! LOL... 
1. Seafood- chilled shrimp, raw oysters, sea snails, cold crab legs, etc. 
2. Seafood paella, Mexican food, tacos to order tacos and topping bar. which includes tortilla chips, rice, beans, and etc 
3. Next station was the meat station where they had slabs of meat that chefs would cut off for you. They had wagyu steak, brisket, pork, and turkey. I was very surprised that the brisket was really good! The bone marrow was ok, they added some crunchy stuff on top and some pomegranate seeds. The sliders were good and the lobster mac & cheese could have been a little cheesier a little watery for my taste. 
4. Near the Asian station go here for HOT crab legs, across the way they had Chinese food different dim sums, inside steam baskets as well as roasted duck, roasted pork, fried rice, etc Then come the small sushi bar with Salmon nigiri, spicy tuna rolls, etc not too much on sushi selection. 
5. Then desserts: Different cupcakes, macarons, rice krispy treats, 31 ice cream flavors (just kidding), creme brulee, and cut fruit. 
So YES overall for around $60 + not bad of a deal for ALL the food you can eat and the choices... Well worth it! Just crab legs alone is $100 per person on a good day!
