No wait when We arrived. Food was amazing along with the desserts. The staff was on point. They get a 4 because of the seafood selection. The crab legs we not in clusters and only half full. Not what I expected for the price. And I paid full price for an 11 year old.

See food... Usually I see food and then I eat it! But this time I'm talking about seafood. To be fair you're going to need to read my review all the way through to understand why I'm giving them 3 stars. 

I am a breakfast fanatic and wanted to come for breakfast, unfortunately they only had breakfast brunch until 3 o'clock. (This is the average time in vegas that buffets serve breakfast). When in Vegas it's sometimes hard to get anywhere by then. I rushed my friends out of the room and we  to got to Caesars at 1:45 PM. Unfortunately I didn't realize that the wait could be hours long, I should've read the other reviews. They wouldn't be able to seat us till after 3 which means I was not going to get my breakfast buffet. Prices also go up after 3. 

We ended up getting seated at 3:15 which means the buffet has turned into dinner now. Even though the food was good and had a lot of seafood, my preference buffets with more choices. My friends who enjoy seafood loved this buffet so if you enjoy crab legs, crawfish, and other seafood you will probably enjoy this buffet. I ended up eating pizza, some Chinese food, and a few of their desserts but nothing really blew me away. They had someone preparing crepes and tacos, which was nice. The food is good but I prefer more selection at my buffets especially because I'm a picky eater who doesn't eat pork, red meat, or seafood. I would be willing to come back and try their breakfast brunch. 

Lastly this buffet is not cheap, be ready to roll out the dough. I paid about $60 and my friends added unlimited mimosas for about $70! At least they were drunk enough to forget how much they spent.

Great place to eat very clean and good service and excellent taste if the food excites you just wait to get at the dessert time .. omg it is really a place to go back again... hospitality is usual at Vegas but at this place they go above and beyond.. definitely I will recommend to my friends to pay a visor next time they are in town... me for sure see you next time Bacchanal Buffet

Being an out-of-town'er, Las Vegas buffet seems to be a once every few years affair. Before this recent trip, Wicked Spoon of Cosmopolitan was the "it" buffet. And before that it was Wynn's, and Bellagio's, and so forth. My wife though has been telling me that Bacchanal at Caesar's was pretty good. Of course, it is my duty and I must oblige. We fell in line that moved briskly at about 5pm, just beating the dinner crowd.   

The spread was pretty good. We ate at Wicked Spoon later on our trip and Bacchanal has more selections. Big plus on the lamb; coupled with mint jelly, mmm delicioso! I tried my kinds pizza and man, that some serious pie as well! Bacchanal has some good selection of dessert but tops it off with a Thai Tea Boba Float. On a side note, I'm still surprised some people are still perplexed as to what Thai Tea and Boba are. Its been a while since I have visited the other buffets in Las Vegas but right now, Bacchanal of Caesars seems to be one of the top buffets in the city.
Irma was our server! She was so great.. over all there is great variety off food and we loved it. We will definitely be coming back soon.
Great service from Lexi! She really managed the line well and we didn't have to wait that long!

Ok first of all this 5 star system really irks me sometimes, because in all honesty I would give this place a 4.5. It is by far one of the best buffets I have tried in Vegas (next to the Wynn Buffet) but not the best food ever! However, I am leaning more towards the 5.

Their selection is AMAZING. Things that were really delicious are listed below:
- Lamp chops. Okay first of all, I am not really into lamb but their lamb chops did not taste game-y at all. AMAZING.
- Buffalo wings. Ok seriously delicious, in a perfectly portioned 2 pieces in a mini bucket (ADORBS)
- Pretty much any potato thing you could think of, all were SO GOOD: mashed potatoes, sweet potato fries (came with fried chicken), potato skins, potato wedges.. and probably more
- Fried chicken. 
- Oysters. I'm not a big oyster fan but these were GOOD and very very fresh!
- Seaweed salad 
- Korean short ribs
- DESSERT!!!! Almost every dessert I tried was good, which is embarassing because I tried alot. This deserves its own list below

Desserts:
- Tiramisu (reminds me of that of Portos in Glendale. So good!!)
- Cheescake pops (not too overwhelming like many other cake pops I have tried)
- Creme Brulee (I'm a chocolate person, and these were pretty damn good)
- Crepe bar (I just about screamed when I saw this. lol Pretty good I was too full to eat the entire thing)
- Mini chocolate cupcake (very good)
The dessert bar was my favorite part n_n

Things I found mediocre:
- Prime rib. I have come to the conclusion that if you want good prime rib, cook it yourself or go to a prime rib joint. 
- The asian selections (minus that which was mentioned above)
- Crab legs are better at the Wynn


All in all, I would say Bacchanal and the Wynn are my favorite Vegas buffets. Wicked Spoon is right below. I guess it depends on what you're looking for. 

The line for Bacchanal was insane, on a 4 pm Saturday afternoon... It's nice because you can pay $20 extra for an express pass to skip the line. Don't come at dinner time (6 ish) because when we left the line probably had a few hundred people.

Ahhhhh, Bacchanal Buffet!  I was going back and forth between a 3 or a 4 but I ended up with the latter because there were some items that left a memorable impact on me.

The Good:

Lamb chops - Absolutely delicious!  Well-seasoned thick cuts of perfectly cooked lamb chops.  Totally caught me by surprise how tasty they were.  I had one, then another, then another, then it dawned on me - I had to eat something else!  I may have to go through my archives and post a few more photos... or maybe I'll just keep them to myself. =)

Lamb chops - In case you missed what I wrote above.

King crab legs - Meaty, juicy, and sweet.  Served chilled or hot.

Prime rib - For a buffet, the quality was way above than I expected.

Other seafood items - Raw oysters, crawfish, stone crab legs, shrimps, and then some...  These were not the kind that you'll see at a typical Chinese buffet restaurant.

Dessert station - Impressive!  This is a buffet in itself with a lot of choices for your sweet tooth.  Did I mention they have plenty of gelati and you can have them in your donut sandwich?

Timing - If you can time it perfectly near the cut-off point, you can pay for lunch and stay for dinner.  That would mean a very early dinner / late lunch though.

Entire spread - Huuuuuuuge!

The Bad:

Price - $50~ per adult.  This could have pulled down my rating because we are a family of 4 and our youngest, 13 years of age, already qualifies as a paying adult.  I was thinking $200~ could have been better spent somewhere else.

Wait time - Register and get a ticket with a specified time to come back or get a text message.  The lady behind the counter told my wife that if she upgraded her Total Rewards card to platinum, we can hit the queue right away.  We still had to wait about an hour even after upgrading because of the long line of customers waiting to get in. 

Missing items - For the $$$, the steaks and lobsters should be on the menu.

Sushi - It's not even worth the rant...

Overall, it was a pleasant experience despite the long wait and the hefty price tag.  I guess that's expected since this is one of the most popular buffets in Las Vegas.
Pretty expensive, but damn that food good. I had a breakfast plate, a seafood plate, a meat plate AND a dessert plate!

4 stars - from a Buffet's perspective not for Fine dining - had to get that out first.

Recently went to Vegas and wanted to grub at one Buffet. My friend and I picked Bacchanal considering it was the "New" buffet to be at.

Location/Restaurant:
a little hard to find, we walked 10 mins into CP until we finally hit it. At least it was a good walk just to let things settle once we got done. 
Restaurant wise, it was very nice, but the floor plan is really bad, we didnt see the other half of the restaurant until we got our second plate by then we were full!!!

Food:
Has everything you would want in a buffet. The three feature food stations are Steak/American Seafood, and desserts. They are the first stations you see when you walk in. Like i said, they had Italian, Chinese, Japanese etc... but it was on the other side of the restaurant. We actually didn't see it until later when we were already full!! disappointed :(
Regardless, the food was great. Primerib, ribeye, lamb, sausages, everything you would want was there at your fingertip!
Desserts were great as well, lots of choices, even candies (which is always a plus). They even had mochi ice cream. quite refreshing.

Value:
Pricey but i'd say worth it. It's Vegas! You have to do one buffet. It may as well be the best they got :)
We wanted to do the buffet of buffets but we were so glad we didnt do it. It would have costs us over 2 bills and we wouldnt have enjoyed it. 

Minus
a little pricey compared to other buffet. but well worth it.
layout of the restaurant isn't the best, remember to checkout the other food stations!

Would I go Again?
For sure!

Came in at 2pm. No wait, no hassle. Brunch items were good. Got to try the dinner items as well. By 3pm, the dinner items started coming out. Dessert was awesome. Crab legs and Bone marrow were on point. I wish I had more room in my tummy. Definitely satisfied with the food.

Tried this place for the first time this past weekend. Came here for Sunday Brunch with my family. There were about 13 of us (8 adults, 3 kids, and 2 toddlers) 

There is a 18% Gratuity Charge for parties over 8. That's like an additional $75 bucks for us getting our own food, just to be seated together. Seriously?! We decided we didn't want to pay that ridiculous amount for minimal service. Which I'm glad we didn't. The waitress rarely came by to our area. So they spilt us all apart. One group of 4 adults, 1 kid, and 2 toddlers. Then 2 adults and 2 kids. Then finally 2 adults. They wouldn't sit the 4 adults and 2 kids together. Seriously?! That's just bullshit. When the lady in the front obviously told us we can do 4 adults on each table. Then her dumbass changed her mind. Ugh so annoyed.

Food was only ok, but not worth $48. Some stuff are overly salted. Others are just plain. Only 2 things I actually liked there was giant shrimps and the crepes. 

For the price you pay, you would think they would be a lot larger. Nope. I think they're actually smaller than most of the other buffets. 

Would I come back here? Nope. Not even if you paid me to. Bad first impression.

I've heard a lot about this buffet and when I went; it was barely 4 pm on a weekday and there was already a long line. The service was really nice; the person making the tacos, for example, had a smile on her face the whole time :D
As for the food, I thought the meats were tender but nothing wowing. My favorite would be the ribs in Mexican and Meats sections. 
The pork buns/dumplings in the Asian section was very soft and had well proportioned filling. 
I was a disappointed at the sushi section, for there was only two choices of sushi in which both had crab fillings. Some of the oysters in the seafood section was not as fresh as it could be.
For the desserts, I liked the rice pudding and mango mousse the most. They also had a good variety of gelato where you could make boba floats and donut ice cream sandwiches. However, nothing was super special.

Really pricey (about $70 for dinner on a saturday), but the food is pretty good.

-SEAFOOD - amazing! raw oysters, mussels, shrimp, crab legs, ceviche, oyster shooters - all delicious! there was also this salmon dish that practically melted in your mouth.
-SUSHI - pretty good. the salmon and tuna nigiri were really fresh.
-MEAT - the lamb was amazing and tender. beef was good, but nothing special
-DESSERT - HUGE selection. the green tea creme brulee was amazing.

Wow ... from the atmosphere to the food...lets say it did not disappoint me. Everything tasted like at least a 4 star restaurants quality. I like that the juice were not concentrated. Prime rib was pretty good for a buffet. I was suprised to see that they had pho and ramen....which were both shockingly good. I mean theres not much else to say everything tasted good; I duno if its because we went to the MGM buffet the night before...which was a horrific experience. The ONLY thing is that getting inside might take u around 1 to 2 hours but it is worth it guys. Good job to the management team they did a really good job with this hope they will keep this up. Def will be back i dont care if I gotta wait 3 hours.

Went on 3/25/2019... at 1030am ... it's been a few days so I'm not as sharp on my review but I'll stick to things that made an impression ... good or bad ... went during brkft ... pros were good on waiting services from paying the cashier/hosts to sitting down. The curry, fried chicken, and pho (for a buffet) was good or better than expected. Mini donut was good.

Cons ... brisket or beef was not good, I expected more flavor ... didnt see the pork soup dumplings the 3 separate times I went up. I guess the YouTube reviews from the previous years hyped me up n i did not see some items I thought was going to be there. Limited items ... I did not see the separate glass juice (maybe it's a dinner only thing) ... no red velvet pancakes. 

Claiming n hyped as the best buffet in the world or Vegas it was disappointing ... even if it was bc I tried the breakfast session ... maybe if I ever show up in Vegas n want to wait in line for 30 min plus ... I mite try the dinner

Did not live up to the hype at all. Everything was just average, and a couple things were below. There's equal level buffets for less money. But if you must go, be prepared for wait if you go during peak hours.

I don't have to say much about the Bacchanal, as it is the most popular buffet in Vegas. I thought I'd try it out for myself and splurge on my trip Nov 2018. So worth it!! I think my favorite thing is the seating. Lots of buffets are super crammed together and seating isn't comfortable. The Bacchanal is spacious, and have different theming between the different dining areas. It's definitely a place of art! The food is amazing, fresh, and flavorful. The Mac and cheese is to die for! Julie was our server and she was generous with our mimosa refills and clearing out our table as we finished plates. She is truly a gem! Always smiling and was super friendly. Hoping to make another visit real soon! If you're reading reviews, thinking about going, I promise you won't regret it!

Expensive buffet. We went on Mother's Day weekend. The price is $69.99 for dinner if I'm not mistaken. 

We got a $100 dine credit - the only reason I'm willing to try. Sometimes bringing a small Asian lady to a buffet is not exactly worth it... I'm debating whether I should give 4 star or 3 star, and decided to give 4 star because we got the $100 off, but will I come back? Probably not. 

We immediately hit the seafood. The oyster, cocktail shrimps, and steamed crab legs are totally my favorite. They have some selection of soups - which were too salty for my taste. 

The butcher table served ribs, brisket, American wagyu, ham, etc. The sides were pretty good the corn on the cob and the Mac n cheese was the most memorable. 

Then there's the Mexican food area with tacos, ceviche and horchata. Which I didn't even bother trying because I was already 3/4 full. 

The Chinese food section was ... not so great. It's located all the way in the back - and by the time we reach there I'm pretty much done. The dim sum area were not so great. Dim sum items were dry and not looking fresh. The only one I tried were the honey walnut shrimp and it definitely hits the spot. 

The dessert section is to die for. Definitely leave some space for the desserts. 

Now I'm too full... can't write anymore. Try it once... maybe it's for you - but as for me, Las Vegas strip is such a culinary adventure. I feel like I need to try them one by one - instead of trying to stuff myself in this buffet. 

Lastly, there's a limit of 2 hrs inside the buffet. Pace yourself well.

When we got there at around 8:30pm (peak time), the line was super long and we were told the wait till be about an 1 -1.5 hrs and we had to physically stay in line (some review said you could put your name on the list and then wander around). So we decided to walk around first and then came back around 9:30pm and only waited around 10-15 minutes. 

Food was delicious. Nice selection.

The reason why I'm giving this 3 stars is that we were still there at 10:30pm (closing time). And what happens at 10:30pm? The piles and piles of good go straight to the bin! Piles of perfectly good food trashed! It was painful to watch. Let employees take some home or donate it to homeless shelters. Pathetic!

This was the worst part of Vegas. We wasted our time waiting 1 1/5 waiting for the time that said in the ticket after that 2 hrs in line to get to the cashier. After we noticed that we have to make another line to get in OMG we spend 3 1/5 for NOTHING. we end up living WORST SERVICE EVER! This was our 3 time coming no more.

Honestly, Bacchanal Buffet is hands down the best buffet i have ever been to. Expect a huge selection of food and definitely make sure to still be hungry for the desserts. 

Pros
- Food selection is easily the best and really delicious 
- Service is pretty good especially with amount of people.
- Express pass is genius and suggested when not on a holiday

Cons
- Prices are a bit too high 
- Wait can be ridiculous. Anywhere from 1 hour- 3 hours on average on weekends/holidays. Weekdays are much better. 

Other than that, Bacchanal truly deserves the title of best buffet on the west coast and I can't wait to come back here.

This buffet is simply over the top exhaustive in its offerings. They claim over 500 items, and I don't doubt that. They have stations for Italian, including pizzas and pastas, sushi, Mexican, meats, charcuterie, desserts, seafood, soups, salads, and on and on it goes. 

The meat area included a huge roast of waygu beef, the first slice of which was tough and rubbery. The second, rare piece I had, was much better, but still not what you would expect from wagyu. The prime rib was better. They have bacon too, both sliced and slab, the slab more of a braised belly. Why they put so much on your plate of each thing left me scratching my head, and feeling guilty for throwing so much food away. Bone marrow came out after a while, and that was pretty darn good too. Sausages and other miscellaneous meats of all kinds were also to be had, but you can only do so much, and I did three hours.

The sushi bar area changes fast, so it's good to keep checking. Rolls and pokes are replaced with other rolls and new pokes in a matter of minutes.

The Mexican area includes made to order tacos, and was a popular spot.

The seafood for me was really mixed. The crab legs, the long ones, come out at three and are very sweet. I liked those, but the oysters, also out at three, were muddy in flavor and not at all cold. They were of the large variety better suited for grilling than serving raw.

You can't really go wrong here with pleasing everyone, as there is literally something for everyone, and then some. Pay the up-charge for unlimited beer and champagne, but know that the sparkling is of the three or four dollar variety.

We may have come on an off day, but I really wasn't impressed the second time around.  My husband and I had come for our babymoon on a Sunday afternoon and everything was great-- moist meats, an array of wonderful single serving bottled Aguas frescas, tasty fresh sushi/poki and desserts that amazed.

Second time around I came for breakfast and though the selection was just as wide, the execution wasn't great.  My roast beef was dry, the sushi tasted less than fresh, lo mein was bland.... it says something about the food when your favorite selection in the entire buffet was the hot and sour soup.  

Desserts and bottled Aguas frescas were still great though, especially the jasmine rice pudding and the sandia! Gotta figure out how to make that pudding!!

All in all, great selection of a not quite delicious array of foods this time around.  But perhaps timing is key.

Pros
Large selection
Individually bottled Aguas frescas (pina, guava, sandia, and cucumber were offered during breakfast) were delish! 

Cons
Nothing stood out
Pricey (esp at dinner) even at vegas standards

This buffet serves an enormous variety of food from all over the globe. The Asian section served some obvious favorites, as well as some things that are less common of a find (stuffed lotus leaves for example) so I'd highly recommend stopping here and trying a bit of everything. They have a pretty extensive seafood section with a decent variety to choose from - would absolutely recommend to stop at this station to really get your monies worth. They also offer typical American food as well as Mexican and Italian food, which were all very tasty. Their dessert bar is also phenomenal and they offer a lot of high quality sweets to satisfy any sweet tooth. 

The price of this place was a bit exorbitant and not what you'd expect of a buffet but of a higher end restaurant. They definitely offer a ton of food but I'd question whether the price was really worth it. I was expecting lobster tails and filet mignons to be present but there weren't any. As I mentioned, stop at the seafood station if you're into that to get your monies worth, otherwise you're paying almost $100 per person just for some basic items you can find almost anywhere. Place also is huge but is always packed and there was always a long line when we went by the area. They do separate the line into groups of 3 or more and just 1 or 2 people so it is well organized in that sense and seems to make it go a little quicker.

Came here last year when in Vegas and had purchased a Groupon. This is my absolute favorite buffet in Vegas (I've been to about 5-6 now.) They have a great selection of food. The sushi is amazing, but they seriously have the best dessert selection of all the buffets.

****REVIEW #100 for ME!****

Decided to review Bacchanal Buffet because it's a well known spot in Vegas and considered one of best buffets out there. Was here with some buddies for a bachelor party. I had been here before but never for dinner buffet. It was a busy Saturday so there was a bit of a line around 8pm. 

Price for dinner buffet including gratuity for our party was $74! It's a hefty price tag. Depends on who you ask if they feel it's overpriced or not. But it's Vegas go big or go home!! 

Personally, I think based on the selection of seafood, meats, BBQs and dessert they serve it relatively appropriate and customers flow in constantly. I think to really made the dinner buffet worth it you gotta go with the seafood and BBQ and meats item which seem to be what separates Bacchanal from other buffets. Must try items were the crab legs, the bone marrow, the BBQ ribs and the WAGYU beef! Lines get really long for the meats sections and it's understandable. 

My overall favorites here were the bone marrows and the BBQ ribs. So much flavor and tastes so bomb! The bone marrow was so tasty had to go back multiple times! The BBQ were so tender they come off so easily off the bone. Overall, I wouldn't be quick to say it's my favorite buffet in Vegas. It  definitely has all the characteristics for it to be at least top 5 Vegas buffet in my opinion. Thank you, Bacchanal! :P
Soccorro and Rogel provided great service during our first visit here. 10/10 would recommend !

The ticket at check in show the estimated time to get back in line misleads a lot of patrons. That time meaned to get in the line to pay for buffet. Average waiting time after you get back at the time showed on your check in ticket is 1:15hours to get to the table. 

The service is super slow due to lack employee. Too few of servers for a large amount of tables in the his/her section. The bussers works non stop to clean up and set up but it is impossible to keep the pace up and faster. I don't understand why the manager decided to assign servers section like this, the waiting line is crazy ass long. You basically wait 98 minutes to get to the line. Then 45mins to pay for ticket. And another 45mins to get the table. 

You better just get Orange juice because you can refill by yourself; otherwise, you will need to wait another 15mins to get your drink. Don't blam rhe servers and bussers tho. They work non stop but the large quantity of patrons really makes them left behind. I actually feel bad for them because I think nobody will leave good/ decent tips after waiting too long to be seated, paying too much, and not getting attention while dining. 

The food selection and quality is mediorce. Nothing special or stand out. I have been to other smaller casinos in my hometown and other state and this one is over priced, over rated. Not worth the money and time waiting. 

Oh, btw the food is easily to get cold after you leave the station. 

I would not recommend anyone to here tho.

We read so much about this buffet before heading to Vegas, and we were a tad disappointed. There were several types of food, including the following:

Seafood- smoked clams were amazing, and the shrimp was average.

American- great honey glazed ham and delicious prime rib.

Mexican- the salsa bar was disappointing. Banana foster's doughnut and red velvet pancakes were just ok.

Italian- omelette was good but nothing above average. Spaghetti, meatballs, and pizza were all equally average.

Asian- sushi was great as were the bbq pork dumplings and pork curry. Spring rolls were just ok

Desserts- banana and Nutella crepe was very good, as was the gelato. The other items were meh.

Overall, lots of choices but really excellent food was hit or miss. Alcoholic drinks were also extra on top of the $40+ per person.

Incredible. The best buffet---I mean gourmet buffet. The enormous choices are incredible. My dad worked at Caesars since the first day it opened in 1966, and STILL delivers to the high standards of Caesars Palace tradition. Everything was delicious. Beautiful decor, and for the craziness of a buffet, it is so orderly, great service, every time you get up to get a different dish, when you get back to your table, dirty dishes are gone snd table cleaned with new silverware, cloth napkin, and not a crumb or soiled glass on your table. Definitely an A++++

VEGAN @ BACCHANAL???
     Yes- if Steven Lee is there! In July 2018 we visited Vegas to attend a friends wedding and Bacchanal is where they were having their after wedding meal. Not being able to find a vid on YouTube showcasing veggie choices there and knowing the high price we were going to pay, I contacted them by email.  I basically stated that sometimes it's intimidating/embarrassing to ask about non-dairy/non-meat choices in person and could they notify me at least one entrée that we could safely choose.  I never did receive a response. 

       When we arrived we found there is no salad bar at this buffet. Therefore we found ourselves in the position of having to ask the waitstaff. The waiter sent over Steven Lee, who basically told us there were no vegan choices readily available, however he would take care of us. Mr. Lee brought us so many vegan entrées to our table we couldn't possibly finish them all. Every single one of them were amazing! Kudos to all the chefs there.  We had everything from an amazing sushi to a flavorful Italian pasta.  And even pizza! 

      Now let's talk about this pizza... I was grabbing some olives which is semi near to the pizza station when I overheard one of the pizza chefs complaining about us.  Now that were over a month away I can actually laugh about this, however at the time it was quite embarrassing and belittling.  This guy was so angry about having to make us a vegan pizza.  He loudly stated how ridiculous this was and how he can handle "vegetarians but not vegans".  Hey pizza dude first of all-you never know who's listening to your rant, secondly if you can make a veggie pizza-making a vegan pizza is actually one LESS step for you... You just don't add the cheese my friend.  And thirdly, the pizza you, or one of your co-workers, made us was incredible! Thank You! 

      Mr. Lee was so incredibly kind, professional and attentive that the other guests in our party stated "maybe we should become vegan".  Mr. Lee definitely made sure that we got more than our moneys worth and all I can hope is that Caesars is a company that recognizes incredible staff such as Mr. Lee. As he deserves recognition from  his employer for stellar customer service.  We wish to express a tremendous amount of gratitude and appreciation toward all the chef's and Mr. Lee for making this a spectacular experience!
This restaurant gave me and my parents the worst diarrhea after last night eating their seafood. Horrible.

Amazing buffet. Awesome selection. We tried so so hard to eat everything and couldn't. This was our first dinner out on our honeymoon and it was perfect! Our waitress was awesome and funny and we enjoyed her. It was lavish, and totally gluttonous, and exactly what you're looking for in a buffet. The dessert bar was amazing, I recommend the little matcha cup!
Great food and experience. A must in Las Vegas.....Best buffet ever with a variety of options. Tou can't go wrong at this establishment.
Everything on my plate was good ,the drink was good ,the service was amazing . It's a little pricey but worth every penny.

The reservation system is great. They text you 15 minutes prior to availability and you wait in another line to pay but honestly very organized.  We went for Christmas brunch and I put my name down at 10 am, we were seated by 1045.  By 1230 there was a 7 hour wait. OUCH.  Go early.  Favorites was the crab and seafood and the sliced meats.  Soups were great.  Bad thing is the place is so big that hot food is barely warm by the time you sit down to eat it.  Service was amazing!  Like I said well organized.

Terrible, first you wait in line for 1+ hours, then you get to wait in line for the food. The buffet has a lot to offer but be weary of the seafood, I ate lots of crab, oysters and sushi and ended up with food poisoning, throwing up all night. And the fact that I spent $400 for my family of 5.... never again!

Buffets are buffets...WRONG!  When it comes to buffets there 's nothing like the Bacchanal Buffet located in Caesar's Palace.  It's definitely one Epic Fest!

So much food to choose from...and the variety is overwhelming.  Foods from all regions.  Huge and fresh Seafood section, meats of every variety you can imagine including Wagu beef, Mexican with cook to order full taco bar, huge fruit bar, great Italian section, huge Asian cuisine section, and the best part...the Desserts!  Enormous dessert section in the middle of the restaurant with every imaginable dessert you can  think of.  Even Boba drinks!  The service is excellent and super attentive .

Pictures doesn't do this buffet justice.  You have to come here to experience this gastronomy.  The variety and food quality here makes this buffet far above other buffets.  

 Hands down...Caesar's has it all and does it right with their Bacchanal Buffet!
At Caesar Palace.  Week day is good value, after 3pm , king crab legs r available. There are large choices.

Returned here for the second time after a wonderful experience the first.  Hyped it up for the parents and brought them here

Experience was horrible.  For a party of 8, 80 dollars in gratuity was paid.  Plates were not cleared.  The server seemed annoyed when asked for basic things. Would not come back.

I heard a lot of good things about this buffet before going, and man it really is amazing!!! The Asian portion was definitely my favorite selection of food. They have a wide selection, salads, Mexican, Asian, meats, pastas, and seafood. I do wish they had more hot seafood selections but everything I had was absolutely delicious! Don't get me started on the dessert! Must try!! Worth the price

Hands down the best buffet I've been to. The reason why I gave 4 stars instead of 5 was we waited 1 hour to get in and there wasn't that many people in front of us, the line moved extremely slow. We waited a while once we were sat for our server to come get our drink order other than that the food was AMAZING! They had delicious hot crab legs I probably ate about 3 lbs!! They were so good. Most of the food was on little plates and in single serve portions which was mush better than most buffets which everything is in one big pot that everyone gets from. $64 a person for dinner was a bit pricy but the food was definitely top notch

Extensive buffet at $55 for dinner per person on a Tuesday.  We arrived at three and we had to wait 5 minutes the place was packed.  We started with roasted duck, pork belly, Filipino grilled pork on a skewer, and char su.  Everything was good, the duck skin was a little fatty but still good.  My major complaint is and only reason for the point deduction was the lack of drinking options, juices, sodas, etc in the buffet.  Next course we had was fresh shucked oysters, sliced cold snow crab, cocktail shrimp, and grilled river shrimp.  The oysters and crab were not my favorite, but good.  They had two kinds of ceviche a Mexican station that makes fresh tacos, an Italian station that will make fresh pastas, and meat carving station with prime rib, Waugh steak, and tri tip steak.  Everything was good the Buffett has more to offer than what, I could even attempt to try.  We did save room for dessert, freshly made gelato, great cakes, pastries, everything is presented in a really good way and taste great.

Food: 5 stars
Waiter:  5 stars
Hostess:  1 star

I can easily see how Bacchanal holds its reputation for being one of the top buffetsin Vegas.  I was impressed with the selection as well as the details put forth to the food.  Our waiter, Jose, was funny and engaging.  It was clear to see he enjoyed interacting with his customers.  However, the hostess was RUDE.  We were a party of 5, and the cashier escorted us to the appropriate wait line.  When the hostess came, she proceeded to seat the party behind us.  At this point, I informed her my party was there first.  First she chastised me for not standing at the head of the line, for I was to the left of the pole but still in front of the party behind me.  Then, she asked to see my ticket and subsequently pointed me to follow the person who was seating 2 other parties. Never once did she apologize for her attitude or mistake.  After the other parties were assigned to their tables, the seating hostess was quickly leaving.  She was unaware my group was following her.  My dissatisfaction was the way the hostess treated me and her lack of communication with the person who was leading people to their tables.  In this hospitality industry, this hostess definitely dropped the ball. Besides the cashier, this hostess was essentially the first contact a customer has with the establishment.  Instead of treating me like a customer, I was merely a number.  This was a poor representation of the business.
The food and service here was amazing! Incredible service! Great selection, absolutely the best buffet in Las Vegas I'm from New Orleans and every trip I make sure to come to Bacchanal!

The 3* and a half rate is given by comparing  with other buffet restaurant.
There are many kinds of food from all round the world. Seafood from the raw bar is fresh and they have something like stew fish.
However, one thing need to mention is that the sushi from the Japanese bar is extremely stale and the soup from the Chinese bar tastes sour and weird.
They have plenty of desserts and they are decent.
Overall this buffet is better than most of buffets in Vegas.

What in the world?! Hello to this what appears to be an endless indulgence of food! 

There was a little wait to get our grub on, but it was well worth it. 

So, they have this deal where you can spend $22 more for unlimited alcoholic libations but we stuck with water. . This certainly is no time for drinking! We needed all the room we could spare so we can try the WHOLE buffet.

There was everything under the sun to chose from. Everything was fresh, clean & tasty. I loved how the crab legs were already split in half so it was a lot easier to eat. There was a sea bass dish that I had (3 times) which was quite possibly one of the best bites of food I've ever eaten. Seriously, it definitely blew my mind. 

Thanks Bacchanal, I loved my visit!

Waste of time. 
Came here at 4 pm and didn't mind waiting for at least 1 hour...
There was a 357 minutes wait. No need to calculate. That's like 6 hours of waiting haha 
So we grabbed the slip and went to eat something little somewhere else until our 357 minutes were up 

45 minutes later, as we were about to bite a not so juicy burger, the system texted us that our table is ready! WTF man...

We called and they said we can still come at 9:30 so whatever 

Then went there at 9:30 a HUGE line with all the ppl who were waiting with the same situation as ours lol 
I asked the lady working there and she said the line will take 45 minutes and in 45 min everyone will get into the buffet 
BUT at 10:00 they close the buffet and at 10:30 they take the food away!! 


So you tell me we wait from 9:30 till 45 minute later and get in MAYBE at 10:15 and by that time have only 15 minutes to grab food?! 

Ummmm no...
Waste of time 

Manage your buffet better 
Stay open later
Or don't take people beyond limit and tell them they'll be able to come in n wait for hours when they can't even get in.

Came to visit the buffet with my family. As soon as we stood up to get our food, our Seven Stars sign was picked up by Denise and the busser got rid of our entire table. I told Denise we were still sitting, she didn't apologize. She shrugged her shoulders and told our server what happened. The least she could've done was be apologetic towards us who are paying customers, rather than not speaking ONE word to us when YOU were the one who decided our table was finished. The management gets too excited once the table is clear to bring in new guests but do not bother to care for customer service. Our server and busser were the ones who apologized. 

Later that night, I saw Denise making faces and gossiping about her coworkers. Pointing in our direction. Please own up to your faults and apologize to your customers for your mistake. 

Other than that, the food was good. Just very displeased with the customer service from DENISE. Put on a smile, be communicative. We see that you're unhappy and can hear your gossip. Save that for after your shift. Denise-- that is NOT how you treat your Seven Star guests!

2 times of visiting and both I got sick.

Pros:

Desserts are good. 
Food tastes good.

Cons:

I got sick from it even tho I ate proper amount of food. 
Too much waiting. 

Im not going here anymore again :(

Wonderful buffet and great service! We got there around 10am and stayed until a little after noon and was able to enjoy both breakfast and lunch. 

Everything was plated nicely and was constantly fresh. Very impressed with the quality of food on this magnitude. 

We bought a Groupon with a "VIP" pass and it was worth every penny.
sooo much food!  our server esmeralda juarez is the best!!!! she was so kind and gave us excellent service.  highly recommend!!!!

Both of my disappointments during my latest trip to Las Vegas were with Caesars Palace.  The first was lack of customer service by the hotel staff and the second was with Bacchanal Buffet.

My wife had done her due diligence regarding Bacchanal ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=bzYtcCHsdE4WrFvoFxCXgw ) coming here before we arrived at Caesars and the reviews indicated it was about a 2 to 2 1/2 hour wait for this buffet so about 1:30 pm the day after Thanksgiving we went to get our ticket with the return time printed on it.  The reviews don't take into account holidays cause the ticket printed out a wait time of 234 minutes (3 hours, 54 minutes) and we were looking at another 1 1/2 hour wait once we were in line.  We had tickets for Mat Franco at 7:00 pm, I did a quick calculation and realized we were screwed!  Bacchanal Buffet does have a way to circumvent both queues and it will only cost you (sarcasm) an additional $25.00 per person.  Since there wasn't a plan B, once again we felt trapped by Caesars and begrudgingly paid the extra money to cut the line.  The total cost for two people ... $175.10 ... with $3.00 per person discount through Total Rewards.

It took us about another 20 minutes to be seated, our server came over within a few minutes and took our drink orders (a Mimosa for me and a Bloody Mary for the better half).  Both drinks were substandard and Laina said her drink tasted like a can of V-8 sans alcohol.

The buffet itself is extremely large and includes Mexican, Italian and Asian cuisines, but the seafood section seems the most popular.  My lovely wife saw several diners walking around with plates piled high with crustaceans:

( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=ZF6BB097jqEmXYpJXovzOQ )

( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=pML-RoDrE1Qw9u-Bop7roA )

I sampled the shrimp (twice) and it was fresh and of good size, but they were no better than the shrimp I have eaten at other buffets.

The Peking Duck (http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=SGnzFIpaDrJ4MB2_WB39IA  ) in the Asian section was pretty good and the plum sauce complimented the duck well, but it would have been nice if they had deboned the duck, some of the small pieces could cause someone to choke.  Laina had some of the ramen and what was the word she used ... ah ... disgusting!  She had one sip and never touched it again.  

As other reviews have pointed out, one of the shocking strengths of this buffet is the pizza ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=dK1z7jJJW-rHZu7Xa3jTXw ) in the Italian section.  It had an excellent sauce and there was a good amount of pepperoni on each slice.  The Italian section also produced one of the worst lamb chops I have ever sampled.  These chops were tough and fatty ... two words that should never be used to describe lamb!  Each us tried a chop and neither of us came close to finishing it.  I thought the pears and walnuts ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=T2c9PchyncstrmuEJmj0rA ) side was a little overcooked, but the flavor would have went well with the chops had they had been edible.  The pumpkin gnoochi ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=vPEtBfMmIvDdz-JWtmsK8A ) was good, but didn't really have a "wow" factor.

The Mexican section also was really strong with their freshly made tortillas ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=-SGS6A4FkFgoPOrdezHbYQ ) and choice of carne asada, al pastor and el pollo for your tacos.  The salsa and condiment section ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=rHAxXwRiddShZ5mWbyXA4Q ) was extensive with plenty of fresh choices to finish off your tacos.

Another item on the more disappointing side was the prime rib.  The gentleman carving the prime rib had more personality than the slices of meat he was serving up.  The roast was cooked to proper temperature, but one bite and we could tell the quality of meat and seasoning was lacking.

Rohlinism:  Your server should never be spicier than the food he / she is serving!

The dessert selection was also extensive and there were a few hits here between the crepes section ( http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=IxPCXOf-wN25UU3PjqyH-w ) and the chocolate lava cake (the better half had at least two cakes).  Most of the rest of the dessert section seemed to be the standard buffet fare.  The crepe section was lacking chocolate sauce, which was disappointing to the better half.

Service was actually on the poorer side even for a buffet and there was long pauses between glasses being refilled, although plates were removed in a timely manner.

I wouldn't recommend going to this buffet during the holidays and it is probably not even worth the wait time during a normal week.  I have no intention of returning in the future!
Great varieties of food. Average waiting time is about 1 hour for lunch time. Like the other reviews said to take your time to eat cause it could be overwhelming.

WORST EXPERIENCE EVER!!! Very disorganise and cashier not very nice. We signed up in the kiosk and was given a time to come back in line ( approx 2 hours). By the time we got the text, we fell in line and waited about 90 minutes till we got to the cashier. After we paid, we waited in line for another hour or so. Too late to change our minds since we already wasted about 3.5 hours in line. Cashier not very nice which did not  help the situation.  If we have known about the wait ( we asked the staff on how long the wait was, each one gave us different times), it could have been better. NEVER AGAIN!

New favorite buffet! Extremely pricey but so worth it. If I needed to I would sell a kidney to dine here. The black truffle mushroom pizza was a winner, it just melts in your mouth and flavors explode like fireworks. Su is adorable and she made us feel welcomed, always checking up on us. We got lost trying to find our table at first. There will always be someone taking dishes away. Love the bloody Mary oyster shooters. They have such a large variety of food. I'll definitely be returning when visiting Vegas again. 

Their meat and cheese selection is spectacular. Along with their red sangria. Best part is you can ask your drinks Togo!

The King of Buffets on the Strip for sure! This buffet is the biggest, the most crowded, the longest wait, and has the most expansive food selection. 

This is Bacchanal's dinner buffet review. Tiered pricing for Mon~Thurs of $55 and Fri~Sun of $58 +tax. 

Anyways the food is... WOW! I read in an article that is has over 500 dishes. No wonder they charge the prices they do! That's an enormous amount of food that will appease even the pickiest eater. 

There is an excessive amount of food and it can get confusing to which station to peruse as you need to pick carefully and quickly since each station has their own respective long lines. They had Wagyu beef sliders, crab legs, exotic Asian soup like ginseng chicken soup and mushroom truffled soup etc. 

They also must have the biggest selection of seafood. They had scallops, prawn, crab, mussels, crab legs, shrimp, and more! 

Both times I waited over 1.5 hours :(
Next time I would go on a weekday if possible to avoid the horrendous wait or just go to Bellagio Buffet which isn't as hyped as Bacchanal but food is delicious!

We went to Las Vegas in April 2019 for a birthday trip with friends and realy enjoyed this buffet. One of the things we really liked was that they had an Asian section with all types of Chinese food i.e. Honey Walnut Shrimp, Eggrolls, Stir fried rice which was really cool as it had a lot of options. Besides that the buffet had a lot of other tasty options and in general had more options than the Wynn buffet that we went to the day before. Lastly the service was amazing. Our server was Sandra Williams and she was very nice and attentive to our family during our visit. The restaurant itself has nice decor as well. Looking forward to our next visit to Las Vegas so we can hit this buffet up again!

Went there on a weekday morning around 11am. There's no reservation available but we didn't wait for too long to be seated (about 20min). There are many dishes ranging for a variety of cuisine. Seafood is very fresh and I like the beef brisket too! I had a lot of desserts as well: cream brûlée, Vietnamese coffee mousse, cheesecake, raspberry cone and mango sorbet... The time limit is 2 hours for brunch and drinks need to be ordered from the server. I feel like there are so many customers inside and would appreciate more space between tables.

Came in with high expectations. Was told "Best buffet in Las Vegas. Can't go wrong with Cesar's Palace buffet". Meh.  There are some good things, but the bad made me wish I chose something else.

There are some good things I liked.   The carved meat was tasty. The bacon was my favorite.  Few dishes with rice were dry. I figure that's an expectation of buffets so I avoid those unless it's sushi or steamed rice from rice cooker.  Rotisserie chicken and grilled veggies were good. I loved the cheesy mashed potatoes. Scrambled eggs was good. 

====
The Bad:
====
The Asian portion was bad. Not food poisoning bad, but just tasted bad. The beef broccoli was too salty. The sui mai has very little flavor. XLB was not good. The noodles were oily mess. Having lived in Asian populated areas, this buffet doesn't compare.  Taste your food!

Some items weren't refilled quick enough.  I wanted some smoked salmon. Unfortunately when I got there it was out. Ok, I'll wait 15 mins and retry. Oops all gone. Try again after walk-in whole Buffet. Nope. 

The deserts were ok, but the fruit was just bad. Did anybody taste it?  The watermelon was not sweet. The cantaloupe and honeydew were dry.   If they tasted the fruit they'd realize how bad it was.

The service from my original server was just non-existent.  I had to ask another lady that was helping bus for a cup of water, utensils and napkins.  I usually tip between 10-20% at a buffet depending on how well my dishes are taken and whether my refills are handled on time. This time I was so disappointed I didn't want to tip. My wife was just as mad as me. This part is what made me realize this buffet and it's not worth it to return.
Food is delicious, service is awesome, diverse in food choices! We are local and go often and would recommend it to anyone that asks what to eat in vegas! Definitely worth it!!

We visited Bacchanal for lunch on a weekday and found only a 10 minute wait in line before we were led to our table by a confused "tour guide" of a hostess along with several other parties.  The hostess got our table wrong and had to retrieve a new receipt to place on our table.  She was having trouble communicating with the hostess stand on her headset.  While she was gone a server scolded us for not having a receipt and accused us of sitting at a table to which we weren't assigned.  Honestly, I think she scolded us because we are Asian.  She spoke to us slowly and like children, as if she expected my Korean American husband to speak back with a heavy FOB accent.  We complained to the manager about the mistreatment and lack of professionalism and the manager was disinterested in what we had to say and blandly offered to bring over a glass of champagne.  Champagne?  The experience wasn't worth celebrating.  

Once we settled down and sat at the table for several minutes deciding if we wanted to stay, we thought getting a refund would cause more hassle so we decided to just hit the buffet and try to put the terrible service behind us.  The buffet was long and large and plentiful.  Stick with the main buffet area and don't bother going to the side room which is stocked with high carb cheaper fair like Chinese food, bread, pasta and salad.  The main area has about six types of juice rotating at once as well as variations of maybe ten types of meats as well as fish and stone crab claws.  The dessert bar was pretty and plentiful.  There were crepes on command and unique gelato flavors.

While the buffet was pretty huge and we left with full stomachs, I don't know that we need to return.  There are just too many ostentatious buffets in Vegas and certainly we can find one that balances food, flair and good service.

Cesar's has tons of food options but it was more hype than substance. While there was your usual Vegas buffet staples like crab legs and beautiful desserts the items were not any better than take out I could've had back in Florida. The service was ok, nothing spectacular. On a more positive note I was happy they had several vegetarian, and even a few vegan options for my wife. Pro tips- use a Groupon if you have two or more people going - and don't get the sangria it tastes like pure sugar, we switched ours out for a few beers.

Great atmosphere 
Great variety 
Everything was really good 
Nothing was "spectacular"

If you LOVE food, this is the place to be.  Vegas is known for a variety of things including gambling, shows and food.  The Bacchanal has a little bit of everything for foodies far and wide!  I first visited this buffet years ago back in my college days.  A group of friends and I were in town for spring break and thought it would be fun to splurge on a meal before heading back to school.  This was a whole new experience to say the least.  

The location has moved from what I recall.  Used to be just outside of the sports book, but now is a bit further back (or forward depending on how you look at the casino).  Various sections include seafood, meat, hispanic, italian and asian.  Can't forget the all important dessert section since it's one of the first you see when you arrive.  

I'lll try to recall as many of the details as possible since my phone died just as we entered and couldn't take photos of the sections of delectable treats.  At the seafood station, there were chilled crab legs, shrimp, lobster claws, ceviche, baked clams, steamed muscles and other wonderful creations. I don't know how many pounds of seafood we ate, but must have been a few platefuls.  The meat section had prime rib, ribs, sausages, turkey, lamb chops and others.  There's also good 'ol american sliders if you're feeling like going basic.  I know there was more, but my eyes were locked in on the prime rib.  Italian had pasta, pizza and steamed crab legs.  I skipped the latin section simply because I ran out of room.  The sushi near the back was simply wonderful and I believe the oysters were located near this section as well.  You could order your favorite asian noodle dish along with a wide variety of dumplings and other asian dishes.  I also made sure to get a couple mini salads to balance all the gluttony.  I actually didn't dive into the desserts since I literally couldn't move for a while after finishing my last plate.  But some of the desserts that came back with others included creme brulee, pistachio cake, fruit tartes, red velvet cup cakes and gelato.  

We sat and enjoyed family for a while before heading out.  The one drawback I encountered was that they overcharged me for our group.  I had three adults and two children.  I'm bummed that they charged my 13 year old daughter the adult (holiday price even more) price since she eats like a bird.  They also charged my 9 year old the same adult price when it should have been the children's price.  The cashier had said it had been a long day, but yikes!  While there are quite a few delectable treats here, I can't agree with that mistake!  Yes, I should have checked my receipt before leaving the cashier, but thought I explained the ages of my children well enough not to have to especially after she confirmed the ages.

Over all a great dining experience.  Be sure to wear the stretchy pants and leave plenty of time before and after you plan on eating.  The lines can be daunting prior to entering and you'll need to muster up energy after gorging yourself.  In the future I'll try to avoid a holiday weekend to avoid the price increase and cashier lag.

Keep on Yelp'n!

Easily the best buffet I've ever been to. 
Great selection, tons of fresh food and its SO FREAKING GOURMET.

This place re-defines the entire image of the "american buffet". Just look at the pictures


Buffets i have been to in order from best to worst:

Bacchanal - Ceasars
Wicked Spoon - Cosmopolitan
World Carnival - Rio
Spice market - Planet Hollywood, 
The Bellagio
Paris Le Village - Paris
Paradise Garden Buffet - Flamingo
More Buffet - Luxor

In my opinion, it's a great quality buffet! $55 for dinner, but I ate my money's worth and everything I chose was delicious!

Can't remember every item, but here are the one I really liked:

Lots of fresh king crab legs that already cracked for you. All you need to do is pluck out the meat. I ate hella.

Prime rib was juicy red. Satisfies the carnivore in me. 

Lobster macaroni- big chunks of lobster!!

Fresh oysters- yum! They're putting them out though- it's on purpose. Dress pretty, as all ladies should try in Vegas, and the cook might hand you some freshly chucked ones!

The sweet potato fries- omg soo good! I usually don't care for these type of fries, but these are coated with roasted sesame seeds and ginger honey (I believe) and it takes it to another level!

Yum mochi, macarons, and an array of unique flavors of ice cream for dessert! You can also ask them to make you fresh crepe and strawberry dipped chocolate!

Presentation on the foods are lovely. Ambience is modern, clean and very pretty. It's next to the pools, and the windows give off a beautiful natural lighting.

Tips: Dinner is at 3PM. Come at least 45 minutes before (waiting in line took us 30 min) that time so you can pay the lunch fee instead of dinner fee. We were late because we hung out too long at MGM pool. Got there before 3, but the line of course took longer than we hoped.

Avoid the carbs! Don't drink too much liquids. Eat the SEAFOOD and prime rib!!!

I've gone here for both brunch and dinner. Hands down the best dinner buffet in Vegas ... dollar for dollar. I went on a Friday night dinner more recently and was worth the wait. The variety of seafood (shell fish) and specifically the crab, was impressive. Their selection of Sushi was good as well. They also had bone marrow the night I was there. Their desert options were good, between gelato and various pastries you'll be satisfied.

I've been here several years ago, but this review is for my visit this past week. Lined up on a weekday at 2pm and there was barely anyone (yes!). Got a table quickly. Limit is 2 hours and we were able to stay past 3pm when they switch from lunch to dinner menu (lunch price is cheaper of course). 
In general, food was alright. The seafood section was the best (crab legs, shrimp, and seafood paella were awesome). The meat section where they give you slices was okay - the best one was the brisket, but the tri-tip and steak weren't that great. The Asian food section needs work at least. There isn't a good variety of sushi, and the BBQ pork (char siu) could be better. However, the other dimsum and Asian food were not bad. The dessert options were the best part! I tried as many as I could without exploding my stomach. I really liked the matcha green tea cake and pandan creme brûlée. The sakura mocha ice cream was good. The ube gelato tasted like ube but didn't really have the consistency of gelato.
Service was good, they cleaned up as soon as we were done with our plates. 
I think this place is worth going too, but don't expect much from the Asian food section!

My wife and I decide to give another try on Friday when they have their prime rib 
 Special,  all their prime rib that they had was medium well to welcome, ask for medium rear sorry we don't have it, don't get full by the reviews this is one of the worst buffet in Vegas

One of the best buffets that Vegas has to offer. It is included within the Buffet of Buffet's Total Rewards deal... although dinner service comes with an upcharge. Rightfully so! They offer multicultural options, from American, to Asian, and Latin American/Mexican. 

Ambience: Just gorgeous. Colored, glassy, vibrant. Modern, updated seating. There are no bad seats. 

Make your own taco station. 
Bite sized amuse-bouche-like plates with pork belly, or braised short rib. I'm sure there's another term for it, since it's mor than just a bite-size. But a mini portion. blah. whatev.
Juice bar! fresh individually bottled options, like watermelon, carrot, cucumber, and orange.
Raw/Cold bar. The shrimp is HUGE! who cares about the crawfish. The shrimp you don't even have to work for. 
Dessert bar also widely impressive. Gelato options. Cupcakes. Cake pops. Endless. Simply endless. 

This is the kind of spot I just wanna be super gluttonous, and sit it out so I could have one meal to another. They offer crab legs only for dinner service. Warning: they are pre-cut in half. Vegas is the mecca for buffets, in my mind, and this is my current gold standard (I still have yet to try Wicked, so that may change on a return trip.)

Be warned. There can easily be a line. So try and go during an odd hour. Late lunch is preferable, since they start putting out them crab legs at 3. Otherwise, get in line for dinner and be prepared to wait for a bit.

After a recent bad experience I gave this place another try but today was upsetting and ridiculous. Even though the majority of the food was fine, I will not be returning because my boyfriend literally got sick from the raw seafood. 

Long story short, my boyfriend and I came here for dinner and after a couple hours, he began feeling nauseous and starting vomiting and having diarrhea. The food at the buffet was all we had today so we can't figure out what else it could be. The only thing he had that I didn't was the oysters because I was a little skeptical of raw seafood.

The worst part was when I called to speak to management to check on the quality of the seafood they're serving, the operator said the manager refused to talk to me and wanted me to file a security report. Basically they care more about incident reports than customer care. Unbelievable.

This buffet is a winner!  I'm pretty sure that when I left my body was made up of about  10% Crab
 and 5% Shrimp!  

Besides the great seafood, I was impressed with the assortments of meats and Asian Foods.  The bacon was excellent!  And yes, the was a well stocked salad, fruit and dessert bar for those of you who waste your money filling up on these foods!

Drawbacks,  $55 is a steep price of a Sunday Buffet (but worth it), parking is not free and the lines to get in are really long.  Expect 30-60 minutes before you get a table.  I was surprised that once you were seated, there really wasn't much of a wait for any of the foods, except the made to order stuff.

I could honestly say this is the best buffet on the strip! The variety and the quality of the food deserves a five star in my book. My fiancé is pretty hard to impress when it comes to food but he loved everything he tried. For two it was about 80 bucks around breakfast/lunch time with a two hour seating limitation which is way enough time to try everything!!

This buffet is always delicious..... I really dont have any other way to say it. Fresh seafood, amazing cuts of beef, GREAT asian food, It was almost like they had a different personal chef for each region. If you are in Vegas I would suggest going early... The line may be long but it is more then worth it.

Long ago, in a land known as Norrath, I was a level 60 half-elf assassin. Meanwhile, in the non-online world that is known as real life, I was a fat teenager.

While I may have slayed the titan of a teen that I used to be, his soul lives on in my now chiseled body. Every once in a while, I let the elven assassin take over my body, and most recently, he did so at the Bacchanal Buffet.

You ever been to Disneyworld's Epcot Center with all the countries? That's the buffet.

- Mexicoland. Tacos, pozole, salsas, guacamole
- Chinapan (Chinese and Japanese food are next to one another). Dim sum, stir fried dishes, hot and sour soup, sushi
- Poseidonstan (not at Epcot). Crabs, shrimp, fish, more crabs, more shrimp
- Italia. Pizza, pasta, charcuterie
- 'Merica. Prime rib, barbecue, Freedom

And then, off the boonies, lies Carblandia. Cheesecake, gelato, chocolate, caramel, sundaes, cupcakes, cake pops, tarts, and fruit.

I, or should I say the elf, ate until it was impossible to consume another bite. I was literally in pain from the amount of food I consumed. I received a status message "You are too encumbered to move!"

Yeah. I'm aware. And it's okay. Cause it's Vegas.

Best buffet in Vegas!!! Went for lunch which was great because I avoided the crowds. Made a bee line for the all you can eat crab legs and the jumbo fresh shrimp. I did nibble on a couple of other things such as: shrimp and grits, fish sliders, waygu beef, prime rib, lobster bisque, mash potatoes to name a few. Ultimately you will not be disappointed. Something for everyone. Different stations such as Chinese, Italian and so forth. Do yourself a favor skip breakfast and hit the buffet for lunch.

This is the best buffet in Las Vegas. The food is delicious and fresh.Dessert was great, many choices.The best part of my visit though, was my server Su, she was amazing..When I go back I want her as my server..She's awesome!

Ok, going to this buffet is not for the faint of heart. You show up and you get a ticket telling you to come back an hour later to wait in line. An hour later, you come back and you wait in line. After half an hour, you officially get put in the official line. Then you wait another hour. Then you drop something like 80 bucks and you wait in another line for a table. Then you sit down. And then you feast. This buffet had everything and the quality of the food is amazing cuz this ain't your momma's hometown buffet. They got prime rib, bone marrow, oysters, King crab, shrimp, Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Italian... pretty much the entire world worth of cuisine. And they have a Thai tea float which was pretty sick. The lead up to the buffet was an ordeal, but it was so hashtag worth it.

Bacchanal has an impressive (almost overwhelming) selection of food, but compared to other buffets in the area, I didn't find it worth it of the high price tag.  

Although it's great to have such a large range of choices for food, there were so many options that by the time I had gone through and tried everything that I wanted to, nothing stood out to me as being so great that I had to go back for more.  I gravitated towards the seafood, because it's one of the more valuable items in a buffet in my opinion, and while it was good, it did feel weird to be eating seafood in the middle of the desert (but maybe that's just me).

The dining room is clean and elegantly decorated, and service was pretty attentive for how large and bustling the restaurant is.  Overall, I'd only recommend Bacchanal if it's for a special occasion or you're with a group that really wants to be wowed by an extravagant, Vegas dinner.  I think that you're not gaining that more quality with the sheer quantity of food and high price.  There are better buffets out there that serve better food that are much more reasonable in price.

The Bacchanal Buffet. I don't know where to start. Everything here is beyond amazing. Starting from the food and ending with the customer service. The manager, Brian Murzyn is one of the most nicest people I've ever seen. We talked a lot and turns out we have a lot in common. Then there's the great hostess, Nicolette. She's very nice and helped us with any problem, she always came around asking if everything is ok, making sure that we don't have any trouble. The food here is amazing sorting with different varieties. There's Italian, American, Chinese, seafood, and the best of all desserts.
The crepes here are the best. And one of the best crepe workers here is Deimar. His crepes are the best and it is 100% recommended for you to come here and try it.

The customer service here is the best and you don't have to wait for your waiter or waitress to come around asking for your drink! You also get seated almost instantly, not too close to others. My family and I are recommending this buffet 10/10, not only for the food but also because of the customer service and the buffets manager, Brian Murzyn.

Honestly..so extremely underwhelming..

I was in a group of 7, and we got to go to a shorter line for groups of 5 or more (which was pretty nice). I believe it was about $55 per person, and we waited a good 45 minutes till we got seated.

There was a camera lady there, and because it was my sister's bachelorette..we just said F it and took some pictures. It was really awkward, and...just..yeah.

Anyway, the moment we sat down, the lady who sat us mentioned that in 30 minutes..the entire food options were going to change so we should hold off for a bit.

We thought, "How awesome of her to tell us!" So we just got some small plates of the things they had and were eating small portions here and there. (It was 2:30)

The entire look of the buffet was completely different from what I expected. I was just expecting it to look..nicer.

I started off with Wagyu (chewy..flavorless), prime rib (dry af), mashed potatoes (pretty good..but luke warm), lobster mac and cheese (literally cold..) and I think that's all I had to begin with.

They had a guy making tacos so I got all 3 (asada, chicken, and pork) with toppings on the side. These were good.

A LOTTTTT of options are seafood, so for a non-seafood lover like myself..I found my options pretty small.

I was surprised that they had someone making ramen, which wasn't bad to my surprise..but literally all the other options are things you'd find at any other buffet. Their pork dumplings were like mushy and flavorless as well.

I got their chicken and waffles and idk if there was supposed to be syrup anywhere? But there wasn't, so...it was just a dry waffle and a piece of chicken.

I will say, I did LOVE how they had chicharron just chillin and ready to eat.

ANDDDDD hardly anything changed at 3. -_- Waited for no reason lol

The dessert bar was so sad. There was hardly anything on display. Lots of named items that weren't there.

It was just sad :( and I definitely did not get my money's worth at that buffet. I enjoy Souplantation way more than Bacchanal.

Last minute they put out bone marrow which I went to go snag, and out of the entire bone...about 5% was edible..so yeah, that was cool..

It's a no for me.

Meh. we went on a weeknight it was really crowded we were in line for almost two hours and the layout of the buffet is just so ridiculous. With the layout you end up spending more time walking from end to end than eating. The lamb dish was so good though it made it three stars instead of two.

The complaint : Quality of some of the meats where to tough to eat. And friend chicken wasn't good. Also the deserts were way to similar to each other. As in it was all sweet without flavor mixes.

The service was great. I went when it was dead so it was fully staffed working very well.

Overall I liked it. I ate until I couldn't walk. My favorite items were the shrimp and egg rolls.

Recommended as part of your visit to Vegas

Where have the good times gone.  There was a day when this buffet was impeccable.  The variety and the culinary disciplines were unmatched. The freshness and quality melted in your mouth. And from that they received a branding to the buffet that was a must go.  Unfortunately much of the quality has slipped, the cuts of meats are not as good nor is the cooking.  Fish has less of a variety and not as fresh or cooked as well. 
The entire buffet industry has fallen sadly. Which makes this one of the better ones. But 70 dollars a person! I don't recommend it.  It's like a cattle call and they treat people like a number. Nothing special here.

Not what I expected.  I enjoyed this buffet several years ago before the remodel.  We waited for over two hours to get our party of ten seated.  If you are a seafood lover, than you will love this place.  For everyone else, it is mediocre at best.  Not a lot of options, no salad bar or Mongolian grill.  Very little fruit or vegetables.  The Mexican area was a joke. The dessert area was decent,  the Bananas Foster was the one thing that I really enjoyed.  I have no idea why others talk this place up, definitely NOT worth the $65 per person entrance fee. One person in our party got their $65 worth of crab legs and has been driving the porcelain bus for that past 45 minutes.  Others in our party said the Wynn buffet was much better, so I will try that one next time.  My wife wants to add that she liked the pineapple juice!
The Best buffet in Las Vegas. Lots of selections, great atmosphere, superb service. Make sure you have a big appetite when you eat her
Our server Socorro made our experience a 5 star experience at Bacchanal! She was super sweet and attentive.   Great smile! Thank you Socorro!!!!

The buffet is ok- I think if this it top tier for buffets then maybe all buffets are just mediocre. It's a lot of quantity so you get to try a lot which is fun but the quality is not really there. We came at 2pm on a Friday and the line was extremely fast but a lot of stuff had been sitting a while. Maybe go when it's busier if you want stuff to be fresher? I thought the steamed crab legs were the best part of the buffet. The desserts were good though- definitely grab a creme brûlée and Nutella beignet!
This place is worth every cent! We were floored by the selection of food on the buffet. I encourage anyone to go!!

Great variety, mediocre quality. What really disappointed us was the quality of the prime rib. It was dry and tough. Even dipping it in au jus couldn't make it taste better. After a couple bites I couldn't finish it. And the oysters gave my husband an upset stomach. And we've eaten raw oysters before, but these ones didn't taste right. 

On a brighter note, loved the dessert options.

Good food and a wide variety. But it can get very busy. If my husband didn't have card status to get in the expedited like I don't know it would be worth it. Because even with that you still have to wait (around dinner time). I don't eat seafood but they do have crab which people seemed to enjoy. The prime rib was good.
It was good a little bit pricey for Saturday night the problem eggs and crab claws were amazing lots of things to choose from. And a beautiful desert part of the service was good and we did like it

This buffet is inside Caesar's Palace it has a very nice ambience and the chairs were super comfy. The food was just ok. There was a lot of selection so I did go to different areas, but still just ok. I had the prime rib and it was over cooked for my liking. There were two areas that you could get crab legs from, the front were chilled legs, and the back area by the pasta were hot crab legs. I tried both, and both were bland. 
Now the dessert area, off the chain!! All the cakes were moist and flavorful. Our server Jo was awesome!! She was very attentive and super friendly. 
Would I go back again? No.

This buffet was one of the better ones that we went to in Vegas, although it was the most expensive.  We decided to go just before dinner so we could try some of the brunch items and dinner items.  I think the best way to describe the options are rich.  There are a lot of options, and many of them were very flavorful, but I really enjoyed their seafood and Asian cuisine.  I also enjoyed multiple trips to the dessert area because they were changing them out throughout the meal, so I got to try a lot of different things.

I've had better food in a hospital. 

This place used to be solid but they are serving frozen crab legs and incredibly fatty meats. Not impressed at all. Will not return.

While there's a big "selection" it's all sub par. I can think of several buffets on the strip that are better than this one.

Yes they have a HUGE selection of foods. Was not very impressed at all. I was very happy that I didn't pay full price.. Food was tasteless and meats dry. The dessert was pretty good liked that they had many different options including gelato.

My 100th review!!

Bacchus: The Roman God of Feasts
Bacchanal: A Feast Worthy of Gods

If I could give this place more than 5 stars, I really would. I love the open and modern decor of this buffet and how easy it is to get around. It's seriously one of the biggest buffets around. There's a huge variety of foods including seafood, meats, cheeses, salads, etc. I think some of my favorite dishes here are the dim sum (mostly the hargow), steak and eggs, broccoli casserole...you know, to be honest I really can't list all of them. There's just so much to choose from! There's even an Asian soup station! You can order unlimited amounts of pho, ramen, or udon!  Crazy, I know!

I absolutely love the breakfast here. They have so much to choose from. This last time I visited they had some new dishes out compared to what they usually have. Not sure if it's permanent changes but I'm not complaining! 

Warning! This buffet is more expensive than others and on weekends it's almost a ridiculous price. But hey, you get what you pay for. Even so, you have to at least try it once! You won't be disappointed. I've tried other buffets and they don't compare. This has become a regular stop every time I'm in Vegas and I always leave fully satisfied. 

I have to say we truly ate like
kings. Definitely a feast worthy of gods.

I just had the buffet. HORRIBLE See the display case with crab and oysters? There were none available on the buffet. Hot dishes were cold, the meats were overcooked and under seasoned, The buffet at Caesars is not as good as the those at Bellagio and Rio, which are 1/3 the price. Definitely, the worst buffet on the strip.

I read quite a few reviews on this buffet. I was really excited because I'm a huge fan of crab legs. So last night July 4th 2019 we dropped a $150 to eat at the  
BACCHANAL BUFFET at Cesar's Palace in Las Vegas and it was NOT WORTH IT! All of the food was very bland and the crab legs were tiny and salty. So disappointed. I cannot recommend eating here. There are much better choices in Vegas pass on this one.

Bacchanal is the epitome of Las Vegas buffets. Brunch during the weekdays is $44.99 per person, and $59.99 on the weekends so it does carry a pretty hefty price tag. I suggest coming at "off times" to avoid the rush since wait times can reach 1.5+ hours. Out of the three times I've been to Bacchanal, I've only come during brunch hours (11AM-3PM). We usually come around 1:30PM to let the brunch rush end, and found that there was a very short (5-10 min) or no wait to pay and get seated. 

FOOD: there is a LARGE selection of foods. It ranges from Asian selections with made-to-order noodle bowls, to made-to-order street tacos, and a seafood section consisting of crab legs, shrimp, clams, and more. If you're one to want to try everything, BE PREPARED because there is literally a lot of options! They also have a carving station with a WIDE variety of meats, including beef brisket, roast beef, bacon slab, and American wagyu (my personal favorite). I feel like they tweak their menu from time to time, so I can't really point out a favorite entree other than the options at the carving station. My favorite thing about the whole buffet has to be the central dessert table! The dessert selection varied between my visits and some of my favorites were the macarons, matcha custard, and banana cream pie.
