SERVICE: since this buffet is normally full of people, the servers can become very busy. Most of the time, it took a while to get a water refill or for plates to be cleared from the tables. It will take a little bit of patience but they eventually make their stops at your table if you have any requests or need plates cleared.

The point: COME WITH AN EMPTY STOMACH! It would definitely help make your $45-$60 worth while. I would definitely recommend this to any foodie enthusiast/buffet lover that visits Vegas, but it's not a necessity.

I love this buffet!!! I make it a point to visit every time I go to Vegas. I've brought multiple friends here and my husband and they all return with someone else raving about the service and food. I always attend breakfast or what use to be brunch so I can't review the dinner menu, but the seafood, crab legs, shrimp, red velvet waffles, meat selection, is amazing. There is every type of cuisine you could imagine, food for everyone!  I must say the unlimited mimosas are always worth the extra charge. Most recently our server Romulus was very attentive, I had crab claws on my plate and without me asking he brought over the claw crackers (my kind of guy).  I will always continue to visit, anyone who is a foody or if with someone who is very particular about what they eat should definitely choose this place, it will not disappoint!!!

Um okay so...... the food wasn't bad, like there was a lot of selections but some of it was not good either. 

So my boyfriend and i actually went around to all the stands and gathered up as much food as we could to try everything (one spoon of this and that, one sample, etc) and split it. 

I only liked the mushroom truffle pizza, the chicken and waffles, mashed potatoes, cremebrule and cheesecake. Also loved the churros with the sauce! Probably my favorite  thing And i actually hate churros so it was shocking to me that I loved it so much! The Asian  chicken was super chewy, couldn't eat it. I think it was sweet and sour or orange? Can't remember. The potato wedges with crumbles of cheese was horrific, neither of us could eat it! The cheese tasted expired or something!! 

 It was kind of unfortunate that we tried close to everything because we got so full from trying everything that we couldn't eat more of the items we liked.. pretty sad about that. That being said, the desserts were the best part for sure!!Idk if I'd go back, i hear this buffet is one of the best on the strip so i wouldn't even bother trying out others at this point. 

Another note: our waitress was kind of rude. I was casually asking what happens to left over food (I'm from Los Angeles and homeless population is insane, way worse than Vegas so it's too bad that buffers can't ship all the food there but that's life ya know) anyway, i literally was just making conversation and said "what do they do
With the left over food? " and she got really defensive and was listing health violations and sounded super mad.... we just sat there feeling weird after that . Never once did i say you HAVE TO GIVE to homeless!!! NEVER SAID THAT. Was just asking because places like Panera bread have to donate food like left overs so i just thought it would be interesting to ask about a place that produces so much food. But she went into great detail and had so much frustration about how y'all can't give away food and how you are forced to throw it away bc this and this and acted like we just insulted her business and as if she owned the place and that we had no right to be curious...... like ok i was just asking a question .. chill. Could have just said "we have to throw away because of health regulations" and gone on about ur day! No need to get defensive ! Geez just spent nearly 90 dollars to have that type of service . Smh .

I honestly feel like it was quantity over quality here. Maybe we arrived too late (8:30pm), but both my friend and I felt the food was dry. Everything was dry, it wasn't just one item, so we suspect it might be dry cause it was kept warm, and we came later in the night. We loved the dessert table though! I've got a sweet tooth and loved nearly all of the desserts!

Edit: for typo
A lot of waiting and waiting. The food was okay but  the desserts were awesome. I would go back for the variety of desserts. Came to Vegas and went to a buffet. That's checked off the list!

Waited in a long line at 7:30pm for one hour on a Sunday night to get in the table. Food was really salty, that night I had to drink 2 liter of water but still felt so dry in my throat.  I think they did it in purpose so that you couldn't eat much!! Not worth $75 at all for these kind of salty food! I didn't even touch the meat section. One of the crab leg tasted bad, probably was left out for too long. Also the cold soba was sour, I think it also went bad for being left outside too long.  The last 2 times I went to this buffet the quality had gone down, not the same as it was 2-3 years ago! I will not come back to this buffet again.

ANCIENT ROMANS & BUFFET

Las Vegas is known for their buffets but it is the Ancient Romans who mastered the concept. The buffet concept is synonymous with the Ancient Romans and it's fitting that the best buffet in Vegas is inside Caesars Palace. The reason why I love Bacchanal Buffet is taking the Ancient Romans concept of buffet into a modern approach. Sure there are no exotic dishes like flamingos that were served during Ancient Rome in this buffet, but the variety and quality of food remains the same. This is coming from someone that despises buffets in general. The last time I ate at a buffet in Vegas was a little more than two years ago at Wicked Spoon. I had a terrible experience there. The waiting line for Saturday brunch at Wicked Spoon was two hours long. Then my friend and me rushed to eat for 45 minutes because the brunch menu would be over. The experience at Bacchanal Buffet was much better than Wicked Spoon.

Last Thursday night I paid for my friend's birthday. We came here around 5:30PM. Surprisingly there wasn't a long line. That was because we didn't go to the buffet on a Friday night our weekend. Knowing that there is an abundance of items at Bacchanal Buffet I took a strategic approach. Instead of placing lots of items in the plate I took 3 items at a time. This allowed me to get more plates than I normally get. At most buffets after three plates I'm stuffed. But getting three items at a time I was able to eat nine plates of food. I knew I wasn't going to eat all the 500 dishes. I had to place a priority of items. No standard items that I would normally get - fried chicken, pizza, pasta, tacos, Chinese food, etc. I was sticking to dishes that are rare in buffets in general.

There were certain sections that stood out. The meat section included brisket, prime rib, and lamb chops. I couldn't think of any other buffets that have lamb chops. Having beef brisket rather than the typical roast beef is one feature that makes Bacchanal Buffet stand out from others. The seafood section was exceptional also. On the seafood section you can see shuckers take out the top half of the oyster. I love how the raw oysters are smaller than the raw oysters at typical buffets because the smaller oysters are sweeter. In addition I love how there are not only two types of cooked crab legs (cold and hot), but also how the crab legs are opened for you. How many times when you go to a buffet that you have to work to crack open the crab legs that leave your hands messy? The one section that surprised me the most is the dessert section, which is bigger than the buffets in the suburbs. There are varieties that I don't see at a normal buffer. While most buffets have ice cream at Bacchanal Buffet there is gelato. In addition there is crème brûlée at Bacchanal Buffet. Can you think of a normal buffet that has crème brûlée for dessert?  

The fact that I didn't try every dish makes me want to go back to Bacchanal Buffet in the future to try certain dishes I didn't have last time. For example if I go back to Bacchanal Buffet I would like to go for breakfast/ brunch so I can try the red velvet pancakes.

I'm not necessary keen on a decor of a restaurant but inside Bacchanal Buffet the minimalist decor makes the setting feel more like a high end restaurant than a buffet eatery. This makes you enjoy eating because you're more relaxed. After eating nine plates of food I was stuffed but not bloated. That is the standard how all buffets should be like with the number of dishes that are provided. Right now for me Bacchanal Buffet met that standard and I can't look at buffets in the same manner as I did before.

Tons of options. Different cuisines. Husband was happy with all the seafood options. Long lines but that is to be expected in Las Vegas. They had a cool option to put your name in a kiosk and you come back at your designated time.
terrible. people paying to get in front of the line, holding us back when we have waited for hours.

Wow! LOVED eating here. So many options, most i had never seen at buffets. They even have french toast made as you order. The service was fast,  but we did come early in the morning. Worth the price we paid, and will definitely  come back for dinner.

This place is crowded.. I have been to almost all the big buffets in Vegas and I can assure you that this buffet offers the most variety of food. I am saying variety!!!!! Basically each dish they have are different from one another. I dont have a better way of explaining this, but I feel that you will get what I am saying as soon as you compare this place with other buffets. 

The food are pretty good too. Even the buffet in Bellagio was just soso. I was impressed that their "inventory turn-over rate" is pretty high. i.e. you will always get fresh cooked food and HOT... 

I think its worth the price... but try to come early and skip the queuing time

I was super excited to experience the Bacchanal because of all the amazing reviews and super yummy looking pictures. It is probably one of the best buffets I have been to, but I do think it's overhyped. It's way to pricy for what you end up eating, and I wasn't totally overwhelmed with the quality- the oysters we actually some of the worst I have ever had in my life. The Asian area was awesome though! Best udon soup I have ever had! I was also impressed with the crab legs. I don't think I will ever come back here but it was a good one time experience.

We came here around 11:00 a.m. on MLK day. Thank God we did too, because just a few minutes after we were seated, the line got extremely long. 

I can't comment on the price since my lunch was paid for, but I believe it was around $45/person. As soon as we were checked in, the hostess seated us and we were able to order our drinks & go on ahead to the buffet lines.

The food was.... well, buffet food. There was a seafood section, starch station, breakfast station, taco station, Asian station, American station, and a carving station. A LOT of variety. I'm not too much of a savory person so it did not interest me too much. My family, however, enjoyed the different types of food--especially the prime rib. One thing I'd like to comment on are the crab legs. The king crab legs and oysters (the good stuff) are tucked away at the very end of the food line. My whole family missed it entirely, and only saw it as we walked out. Because of this, I don't feel like we ate our money's worth. If you're going to a buffet for the crab legs, make sure you keep this in mind. 

Ok, now for the good stuff--DESSERT!! As soon as you walk in, you'll see the dessert section in the middle of the room. There were so many options, and all of them were good! One dessert that really stuck out to me was the Pandan Crème Brulee. It was so delicious! I still think about it 'til this day :P 

Service was great. Shout out to Fidencio, who was so polite. He has the best customer service! He always cleared out plates on time and made sure our drinks were filled.

All in all, I would come here if you're in the mood for a hefty meal. Make sure you wear something stretchy and clear your afternoon-- you'll probably end up wanting to sleep afterwards.

Located towards the back of the hotel by the pool.  Caesars is a complete maze so if you get lost, definitely ask the staff.  
Came here on a Friday at about 11:45 and there was a fairly long line halfway snaked back into the casino.   As a single diner, it took me about 30 minutes to finally pay and then get in line to get in.   Once seated, i asked the staff the lay of the land.   There are multiple options in the buffet that include Asian, Italian, Latin,  American (comfort, bbq, seafood).   

Service was decent.  Once I came back with my first plate, my waiter asked for my drink order and I got my glass of water promptly but it was never filled the entire time I was there.  They did clear my plates though.   

On to the food,  so many options with limited real estate in my belly.   I had to choose wisely.   I picked a little from here and there and everything was great.   Highlights were the truffled egg, Deviled egg, different selctions of meat(brisket, tri tip, wagyu, prime rib), shrimp, crab legs and various desserts.  


The meat works best with the side of bbq sauce(at the beginning of the meat line) or horseraddish(you can find in the seafood section), or A1 they had a bottle hidden behind the counter.   Crab legs were pre-cut and easy to crack into.   

Desserts had all sorts if different styles from different cultures.  They were small enough to sample, but easy enough to take too many.   

Overall, a great buffet, however, the best bet is to try to come here on a weekday lunch when it's $40.

Being from Louisiana I was impressed they offered boiled snow crabs although they could use some creole seasoning or Louisiana crab boil... also remove COLD crawfish and shrimp. Boil those as well!!!! Overall the other food was good. Loved the steak tacos!!!! Will be back next time!!!!!

This was on my bucket list for places to eat and I finally got to try it!! It was $75 per person when we went, but they had a lot more on their menu. They had a large variety of seafood, meats, salads etc...and their dessert section was heaven! Besides it being a bit pricey, I would definitely say it was well worth it!! If you think about it, the variety you get, is the same as if you would've ordered one entree at any other Vegas restaurant. I'll be back next time I am in Vegas! Our server Jeff was awesome as well!!

Bacchanal is second to none!

This is the best Buffet in Vegas hands down, and we've been to them all. The restaurant is set up perfectly and all of the food is cooked to perfection! 

Every time you go up to get another plate of food you discover you have a new favorite item. Weather it be the succulent brisket, fresh shrimps, dumplings, tacos or the prime rib that melts in your mouth. Don't even get me started with the desert. 

If it wasn't for the union worker staff that the restaurant is required to have I would be pushing for 6 stars! The management team is amazing and is doing phenomenal job given what they have to work with. 

Bacchanal is a must eat at when in Vegas. Be prepared to unbuckle the belt because you won't want to stop eating!

Brought my dad here on our Vegas vacation for his birthday dinner. Although it was very expensive it didn't matter. It came highly recommended by a friend and plus you only turn 70 once. Such a huge selection. It was almost overwhelming at times. In a good way. Only because your eyes want to try it all but your stomach won't let you. Hahahaha. Although I wasn't a fan of the chicken for the tacos I still give it 5 stars. The chicken had cinnamon and I hate cinnamon. Not their fault. Prime rib was a little bland as well. But overall the selection was outstanding. And Maria who was our server was very nice and even set up a dessert plate for his birthday! Made my dad feel very special.

This buffet is ok but I wouldn't rave about it 

The lobster claws look good but they were dry and lacked seasoning. Maybe I was supposed to dip it in the butter to make it more moist ... I don't know. The snow crab was also the same. 

Oysters on the half shell were ok but whoever shucked mine didn't do a good job because there were bits of shell in the meat. 

The prime rib wasn't sliced thin ... it was a chunk of meat about 2 inches thick and it was square-shaped.  The suckling pig was fair but they didn't serve the crackling skin. 

The deserts were pretty good especially the little cones. 

I wouldn't recommend this buffet when you consider the price.

I also tried the buffet at the M's and that I would recommend going to instead of here.

The buffet was superb when they first opened but as time went on they have lost their flare.  There was a nice quantity of food but it was all bland and tasteless.  Left with a bad taste in my mouth so to speak.

Caesars is supposed to be a five-star establishment but they never could get the buffet right.  The buffet prior to Bacchanal was terrible and it seems Bacchanal is heading down the same road.
Very good food. This buffet and Wynn's are my favorite in Vegas. The quality of this buffet passes all.
My favorite buffet in Vegas! I've gone to other ones and none compare to the Bacchanal Buffet. I make sure to come here every time I go to Vegas.

At first I was skeptical, $70 a person for dinner? Sounded way too pricey.

With a big group of people, this was perfect. The variety, service, unique foods, all made it worth while. Highlights included lamb, bone marrow, shrimp tostadas, giant crab legs already perfectly sliced open (how'd they do that??) And the desserts... 

Also, our server, Socorro, gave us the best service, way better than most restaurants which makes it exceptional for a buffet. You typically dont expect good service at buffets. 

Conclusion: if you're worried about the price and would rather get your monies worth somewhere else, you would probably end up spending close to the same amount. So forget the calories, come indulge!

For forty bucks a person before 11o clock, you can enjoy a pretty good buffet. Majority of the food is decent but nothing to write home about. American and any western section is pretty authentic. The Asian section maybe a little wacky and not what you're used to if you know what you are eating. If you're a seafood fan, the cocktail shrimp is amazing good/fresh. I was looking for crabs but of course there was no snow crab legs for $40 in Vegas. There are however, stone crabs but they're tasteless and noth worth your time to pick at. The crab soup is great though as with most soup. The desert section is a proper way to end your buffet visit since everything was super delicious. Creme brulea is my fav.

What happened to this place? SO different from 2012. 
Just not the same place it used to be! 
Presentation is still beautiful but that's about it. Nothing exceptional except the decor and the layout. 
Waited in line and paid $70 to eat salty, frozen and chewy crab legs... Oyster had shell bits. Sushi corner was lackluster at best. Prime rib was chewy, brisket was oily, lamb was overcooked, sausages were dry. There was nothing appetizing. Their noodle station was mediocre as well. Tonkotsu was smelly-they need to put more herbs to get rid of the smell! Pho was bland and Laksa needed more spice. Dimsum was overcooked-the sides popped and it was unappealing. 

Dessert tasted like any other buffet deserts, 
you really can't tell what you're eating, it all taste bland. 
Just try the Creme Brûlée you'll know what I'm talking about. 

Went with party of four. With the same money we could've had a better meal in Vegas.

Ken L. and I came here the weekend after Thanksgiving on a Sunday night. I wanted to see what all the hype was about since I've heard stories of 4-5 hour waits. Insane! Luckily, we didn't have to wait as long. We got there around 6:00 p.m. and the line grew quickly after we got in line. There is a line to pay and then another line to get seated. 

It's a pretty epic buffet with so many different stations. I'm not a big buffet eater and wasn't quite sure how to tackle this and still get my money's worth. I haven't tried many other buffets in Vegas but everyone I've spoken to has confirmed that this is the pretty much the best (for now at least). 

I decided to first tackle the seafood area first and work my way down. The seafood was very fresh. I think I ate almost a dozen of the raw oysters. I loved their taco station and had stake and pork ones made for me on the spot. There were also bottles of horchata, mango, hibiscus, and agua frescas near this station. There was pretty much a station for everything, bread, cheeses, soups, dim sum, sushi, Chinese food, etc. 

I'm a big fan of their dessert station. Don't forget to get a freshly made crepe topped with your favorite fruit and other toppings. They had a good variety of sorbet and gelato flavors. They even had bakhlava flavored gelato! I couldn't help but try a taste of everything here... from their macarons, creme brule, flan, etc. Everything was carefully decorated and too pretty to eat. 

While the wait was longer than I would have liked, the quality of the food for the price you pay wasn't too bad. I don't think my stomach could handle multiple buffets during a single Vegas trip but if I had to choose a buffet to come back to, I'd probably pick this place.

We stop by on Sunday 7/28/2019 for dinner. The woman at the cashier is hostile to a family with young children. She insists in telling us, a family of four and a 2 years old, has to wait in a party of 5+ line after we tell her we can sit on a table for 4 persons. That is fine for us to wait for the 5+ party line: but when we are about to pay, she tells us at loud voice we would wait for at least 2 hours to get a table for 5. It is around 6:00 PM. We leave with no hesitation. It is an unpleasant evening to go for dinner buffet ai Ceasars in Las Vegas.

Wow! I don't know how I haven't written a review for this place... Bacchanal takes the gold for LV buffets without a doubt and this is my 2nd time here - they continue to hit the mark and serve delicious food!

Imagine every type of cuisine that you may find all around the world.  They have stations for seafood, meat carving, chinese, japanese, mexican, italian, american, french, etc.  You have to be strategic on what items you need to try as there are so many options that you can get overwhelmed with what's out there.  Luckily, the make some of the items small plates so you can just taste it.

When I went this past time, I saw a lot of new items I never knew they had like Bone Marrow, Poke, Duck, and Paella! All 100% spot on! 

The dessert bar is also something to save room for and savor.  They have all sorts of pastries, cookies, and my very favorite Crepe station and ice cream bar!

Keep in mind when you come here, you're going to be waiting in long queues even with the ticketing system.  I came for the Christmas holiday and they charge $70/person versus $60.
This is my favorite place in Las Vegas you can't beat it it's the absolute bestThe ambience and the food is exceptional and the service of the lovely people are wonderful here

Definitely worth the money if you have a good appetite! They have an assortment of different cuisines to choose from so if you're not feeling a certain one you can just move right onto the next. Little tip: take a small bit of everything, that way you can try it all before getting full. Service was quick and we got seated right away. Esmeralda took care of us well. It's a yes from me.

Oh what a ... show. 

Before you go, know that: This will be a stressful experience. You will wait. You will encounter humans behaving on a less-than-civilized level (this is a BUFFET afterall). You will stuff your face well beyond gluttony. You will see the worst and best of humanity. But just keep this in mind: This is not real life, this is a one-time experience. 

The food is good, you can eat yourself around the world, but save room for the endless crab legs. 

I'm glad I went, but I'm even more glad it's over :)

Referred to as a "crown jewel" by its new executive chef and purporting a "feast for the Gods" a visit to Caesars' Bacchanal Buffet comes with certain self-appointed expectations and although prices have crept upward since the sprawling space opened to the public I can only say that my $47.50 Saturday Brunch, complete with bottomless champagne, was worth every cent.  Grand in both scope and spectacle with ornate glass, open floorplans, and plush seating complimented by a staff of over twelve-dozen overseeing preparation, service, and customer needs my arrival at Bacchanal shortly preceded its 8am opening and greeted first by a cheerful cashier, then by assistant manager Stephanie, my experience commenced; the subsequent three hours adrift in 70+ of the buffet's offerings and a sea of smiles emanating from each employee and nearly every patron.  Divided into several sections with many offering cooked-to-order options including crepes and omelets it was Asian that my meal began and with fresh steamer baskets just opened the dim sum excelled - a small quibble in the thick-skinned har gow more than compensated by bao, duck and pork as good as that at Jasmine plus full-service congee complete with century egg, not to mention Sin City's best Egg Custard Tart later discovered at the dessert island.  Moving next to things more "American," one is well advised to monitor for items fresh from the kitchen as both the crunchy waffles and well seasoned chicken proved superlative while later tastes of waffle fries and tots fell flat - a fresh buttermilk biscuit, hot seafood preparations, and sliced meats including smoky beef ribs with caramelized crunch all showing far better.  At times a touch liberal in salt with Kung Pao Chicken and Risotto suffering the most, Bacchanal again shines in selections of shellfish, cheese, and charcuterie but with much eating to do and such things widely available elsewhere it was thoroughly in my sweet tooth that I indulged and although I passed up a few cookies plus a duo of sorbet suffice it to say that I nearly ran the gamut; cakes, doughnuts, pies, tarts, and more all justifying the calories with the aforementioned egg custard, pecan pie, cream puff, carrot cake, and citrus 'tiramisu' all warranting special mention along with the lovely pastry team who jovially tended to baking, saucing, arranging, and making crepes at a pace seldom to lull.

Slightly more expensive than Wicked Spoon but making up the difference in complimentary champagne there are things to love about both of Las Vegas' premier all-you-can-eat experiences yet aside from a more expansive gelato case and my predilection to The Cosmopolitan's soundtrack I'd be hard-pressed to ever recommend it over Bacchanal.  Obviously limited by the constraints intrinsic to feeding anywhere from 2500 to 4500 persons in a given day yet defying the odds through a combination of remarkable customer service and striking attention to detail I'm happy to say that Bacchanal lives up to the liberally applied superlatives and although "Gods" may require something slightly more refined I'm almost positive they won't find it in such a format for less than $50, especially on Las Vegas Boulevard.
The best buffet I've ever had! I've been to many buffets and honestly I'm not a big buffet person. But Bacchanal is definitely worth the dining experience!

Came here for my boy Joe for his birthday. This place is known for being the best buffet in Vegas and it definitely lives up to the hype. Food is fresh and delicious and the staff is especially attentive and accommodating. A special shout out to Esmeralda for making Joe's first time here a real treat. Our plates were promptly cleaned and our waters were always filled and we even had champagne to celebrate the birthday. I always consider coming to this buffet compared to all the other ones

Another spot that's awesome pretty awesome
Got there and it was a breeze to pay 
Gosh what a great selection of everything

The food is good, but I feel that the price is just too crazy.  When I went there was a crazy long line that took FOREVER!  For the price I also expected that the seafood selection would have been a lot better. I was excited for the Ramen station  but it was nothing crazy or special about it. Disappointing..

Best buffet I've been to so far, hands down.  Get there early if possible to avoid the lines but the different choices of food was really overwhelming from Seafood to Chinese and everything in between!!

All the food is so good and there is so much variety. They have seafood, Mexican, Chinese, prime rib, lamb, crab legs, and anything else you can think of. They also have a great dessert bar. The restaurant is clean and staff was very friendly.

This was probably the best buffet I have ever had. In my entire. Life. Of course, it was probably also the most expensive buffet I have ever had in my entire life, but that sounds about right.

Came here after my friend kept raving about it.  This is part of the Harrah's chain and therefore part of the buffet pass, but try to go when it's NOT a long weekend, as you have to pay a premium.  The pass was about $100 per head (buffet pass, weekend upgrade, long weekend upgrade, $25 premium for Buccanal).

The lineup was faster than expected.  Even though the entire queuing area was completely full, we got through in about 50 minutes.

Seriously, if you ever wanted allyoucaneat fine dining, this is it.  Right here.  Alaska king crab?  Lamb chops?  Steak?  Oysters?  The food here tasted much better than many restaurants (fine dining) back home, and if you factor in the volume, the pricing is actually quite decent.

There was so much variety here that I couldn't even cover the entire buffet.

The overall experience was life-changing.  I only tried 3 buffets with my pass (Le Village in Paris, and Spice Market in Planet Hollywood were the other 2), and this one blows the other 2 out of the water.

Not sure about the other buffets out there (Vegas has so many), but if you were to only go to 1, you definitely will not be disappointed with this one.

Yes.  I found the one buffet I would be willing to break my diet for over and over again.  As was described to me, this buffet is an experience.

Seafood Bar: Fresh oysters, crab legs, shrimp, fish, and seafood dishes galore.  Topped with many different sauces for my dipping delight.

Ramen Station:  Thank goodness for the tiny bowls these are served in.  Let me have room for all the rest of the food.  Although this was delicious already.

Asian Area: Is the porridge I see?  And I can put fried garlic, green onions, and ... omg, do my eyes deceive me, or is that a century egg?!?!?  YES! Porridge with century egg, my FAVORITE.

Mexican station:  They had a taco station.  It looked so good, but my stomach was already filling up with all the goodies.  However, I DID stop to take a horchata, which was SO delicious, I want all my horchata drinks to taste like that please!

DESSERTS!!  DESSERTS!! DESSERTS!!  Pandan Tiramisu.  Have you ever tried it?  You should.  Here at Bacchanal!  And, what I thought was a green tea or pistachio macaron ended up being a pandan macaron!  Yes! All the flavors!  White chocolate covered strawberry topped with strawberry crunchy balls.  Can you say delicious?  And some other goodies like an shaved ice station, creme brulee, cake pops ... is your mouth just drooling right now!?!?!

We arrive there around 5:30, and surprisingly we came RIGHT BEFORE the line started.  We didn't have to wait at all.  LUCKY US!  Yes, it's $50+, but this buffet is WELL WORTH THE PRICE.  Make sure your stomach is ready for a feast worthy of kings!

We went to this new buffet for the first time on a Thurs night in Feb '13.... Having read all the hype and reviews both good and ba we were braced for whatever we might find. The first thing we did was purchase the Buffet of Buffet passes for $49.99 plus a $25.00 upcharge then agreed to eat our next 4 meals buffet style..thus each meal costing $18.75... for us a savings of about $60.00 each.  This took the sting out of this $50.00 buffet particulary! 

First off the wait on this Thurs night was only about 40 minutes in a line that moved quickly.  Once in, the restauraunt is beautiful and surprisingly calm for how many are dining there. We were very graciously greeted and introduced to the buffet. The decor and music were fantastic. 

All food stations were well stocked and looking good. Given the high cost of the meal I focused on King Crab, Jumbo Shrimp, Ribeye and Brisket. All were fantastic though the Ribeye was tough IMO. The green peach ice tea is beyond delicious.. Desserts were breathtaking and fun to sample several...the maccaroons were awesome!

Service was basically pretty good though dishes could have been cleared alittle quicker.

I do have to mention the cook who I asked about where to find the watermelon/feta salads I was so looking forward to...she apologised and said they would not be available that night then immediately offered to make one special for me...I was stunned! They are not that easy to make, and I told her that wasn't necessary...she kindly insisted...I was SO IMPRESSED ! That really blew me away..She is pictured in the photos I have submitted...

We go to Vegas frequently and would recommend the all should try this terrific buffet!

If this restaurant and Nobu are signs of the kind of quality the Caesar's properties are stepping up to that would be fantastic because overall their properties are starting to age and need this kind of major infusion to keep us coming back...we were impressed!

This buffet has a lot of offerings which is the best part. Their dessert options are great about 20+ different desserts. The tacos were very good also. Steamed crab legs were delicious and fresh. prime rib was lacking in flavor. oysters and seafood were good. chinese food and sushi area is just okay. price is very high around 60 a person for dinner. the waiters are excellent! my plates were always taken when i left my table. overall everything is kinda just okay, nothing standing out BUT the offering and selection is the biggest positive.

Currently the best and largest buffet in Vegas.  A shellfish lover's dream.  Unless you have status with caesars total rewards, be prepared to wait or to purchase a line pass (when available).  Fortunately you don't have to physically wait in a line as they use an electronic waitlist system to text you (look for the kiosks to sign in).
I thought it might be a fabulous restaurant, but it's food just so-so for me, the snow crab was too salty, and the food is not too much variety. The dessert and Japanese food are good.

Not worth the money. People rave about the great seafood but I would rather stuff myself on a single serving of Gordon Ramsay Fish & Chips. Also, the unlimited beer selection includes Coors Light (barf) or Blue Moon (filling) which is not worth $15 unlimited. You must be very hungry with low standards to go here. We visited on a Monday at 6:30 and waited more than an hour.
Lots of choices and everything was well prepared, fresh and delicious.  The shrimp and prime rib were on the breakfast menu!

Here's a healthy eating tip that I'm sure you've heard:  eat slow because it takes time for your brain to know that your belly is full, therefore if you eat slow, you will feel full before you overeat.

If I'm at a buffet, I would tell this tip to gtfo!  I am there to eat my money's worth!

What disappointed me at Bacchanal is that after you've waited in line to get in,  you don't expect to have to wait some more, but unfortunately there are long lines for seafood, carved meat, tacos and gelato.

This resulted in me eating a little bit at a time, food getting cold while waiting, dreading going in line to get more food... My hunger went away but I didn't quite feel like I enjoyed my meal or ate as much as I could have.

Moreover, because there are lines at the popular stations, people are standing in front of all the food, and it's just troublesome to look around and ask people to move so you can look and grab food.  It also means that a lot of the dishes stay under the heat lamp for a while because people can't easily see them, and the plates get burning hot.

OK, now as for the food: I really enjoyed the tacos.  Not worth $50, but they were good! I only tried the steak, but they also have al pastor and chicken.  Since you have to wait in line for these, I suggest getting many!

There were so many meats!  I usually only get red meat (cuz it's worth more, ya knooow) so I got prime rib, rib eye, brisket, ribs and lamb chops.  The prime rib and rib eye were too rare for my taste and kind of bland. I should've gotten the more cooked pieces, but I was not gonna wait in line again...
The brisket and ribs were super smokey... dislike.
The lamb chops were my favorite meat.  Soft, flavorful, fatty! 

There were many seafood dishes (fish, clam bake, mussels, lobster chowder), fresh oysters, cold and hot king crab, shrimp cocktail.  The hot king crab was worth the wait! So meaty, and the legs are already cut in half so it's easy to eat.  At that station, I also enjoyed the ceviche and gazpacho soup.

I had to rush through dessert because everyone was already done eating... but I still tried as many as possible!  I loved the creme brulee and the chocolate creme brulee.  The tiramisu was yummy!  Macarons were the perfect texture, I had bites of the blueberry, orange, and pistachio flavors.  Not a fan of orange flavor but the other two were good.  I ate so many desserts I can't remember what else, but they were all so delicious.  That was probably my favorite station hahaha
I didn't get to try the crepes!

Overall, my expectations were too high but this is still a good buffet... so many choices and so many things I didn't get to try.  but the inside wait is ridiculous and ruins everything -__-  the timing, the temperature, less time to sit at the table and actually eat -___-   losing one star there.
better grab lots of the popular food and serve it family style at your table.

Outside wait was around 40 mins.  We got there at 2:30pm, but later on for dinner time, the outside line was packed like crazyyyy.

Brunch ends at 3pm and includes unlimited mimosas.  Come right before that time and get dinner food for the same price! $42 vs $50 for dinner.  Bring your players card and get $1 off.  I don't know if I would go back though, it is expensive... but worth trying if you come at the right time.

Rounding it off to a 4.5. 4 for the taste and quality of food, 4 for the buffet selection, and 5 for Mark's warm and attentive service. 
We were in Vegas for Labor Day weekend and this came up as a must-try experience so we went for it. After reading up about the ridiculously long lines, we strategically went during brunch time at around 11AM so we can try both the breakfast and lunch items. We were able to get in right away and was seated and welcomed by Mark. We immediately got drinks: Peach Bellini for me, Strawberry Pineapple Bellini for the hubby. Oh and coffee. 
We went around first scouting everything and carefully choosing what to have and to try to get our money's worth. Was able to try various rounds of plates to be able to get a taste of everything, portioning was the key obviously. What stood out for me were shrimp and pork dimsum, chicken & waffle combo which came in a mini iron basket and was really cute, and for dessert, hazelnut beignets which I would have missed noticing because its at the farther end. The Prime Rib and Wagyu was just alright and the Ube, Coffee, and Vanilla gelato was kind of lacking. I was also given a fresh pot of coffee while having dessert.
We had another glass of champagne each and we decided to then explore Caesar Palace, not wanting any food anymore for another 12 hours. Recommended for the experience. I just wish the food selection were more and better. Oh and no crab legs during brunch. If you want that specifically, go for dinner.
This was amazing food! Beautiful displayed food and desserts!  Loved all the choices and the food was hot!

We eat at this buffet every time we are in Vegas. Food is fantastic. So much to choose from. Fresh. The only downside is the ridiculous price. I hate paying close to $70pp but if you get there before 3pm, you get the lunch price. Ofcourse that is still pricey but pace yourself and get your money's worth. The wait can be horrendous too. We got there at 2pm and didn't reach the desk to pay til almost 3p.

Food was awesome clean good food a gourmet buffet worth every penny 30 to 45 min line but still worth it wait till you try the 16 hr smoked brisket and the prime rib wow not to mention the seafood from oysters on the half shell to prawns in ther own skin crab legs claws giving it 5 stars on the food about 31/2 on service  the food is what it's all anout
Overpriced! Got nothing much there! Price same as Ruth's chris but food is nothing comparable

Honestly, I think we could have had a better experience at Old Country Buffet. They couldn't even get their Thanksgiving dishes right. We most enjoyed the unlimited crab legs and pastries (especially). I had hopes of enjoying all sorts of cuisines, but I couldn't bring myself to get seconds of most things. Spent 1.5 hours in line and $100 for two. Wasn't worth it.

Bachannal Buffet...come to poppa!!!

I can not over emphasize how amazing this buffet is!!! 

After watching (either food network or travel channel) a show on the greatest buffets & seeing this one topped the charts- I said "I am there"! 

And here I am...enjoying the abundance of delicious food. This buffet really pays attention to detail. From the fancy stations decorations to all the individual tasting plates. This is not your typical "stand in line, one at a time" buffet. The buffet goes from room to room & each room is a different culinary region. From the Asian room , to Italian, to Mexican & seafood ....of course you can't forget to visit the dessert room.  Make sure to check everything out before you dig in. There is so much!! The best I like- a lot of dishes are served in small individual dishes.  There is an up charge for wine & beer. 

Service was great. Kept pouring the drinks & cleaning the plates. 

Yes, a tad expensive - but WELL WORTH IT!!

The buffet here for brunch was okay. I was a bit disappointed because everything looked appetizing but taste was a bit lacking. For the price we paid I thought it would be much better. I grabbed some crab legs, shrimp cocktail (my fave from here so far), some of the prime rib and wagyu beef, and some sushi and dim sum. The crab legs were okay but texture didn't seem fresh. I liked the prime rib and wagyu beef the best. The shrimp dumplings seemed a bit dry and the sushi as well. Best part was dessert for me! :) I loved their gelato.

So many options. Great food.  Our server, Raquel, was so sweet. We opted to get the drinks pass as well and she kept our mimosa flutes topped off   Cold seafood options were first rate. Soo many delicious desserts.

Tried out Bacchanal to experience the good reviews I've heard so far. So, lets get down the business. I came in here last Sunday to try it out and here is my quick review.

1. Good customer service 
2. Busy at dinner. At 5pm, line was long and slow moving.
3. Lots of shellfish seafood selection
4. Variety of dishes
5. Lots of meat
6. Desserts, dissappointed. Hurt the rating. Not many selections. There's a crepe service. Not dissappointed. 
7. Price for dinner: Good
8. I'll return again for sure.

Main suggetions: if you like buffet, this is a must try. But arrive here famish and be hungry, like have not eaten for 2-3 days hungry. And if you like crabs, this is the place to be. Enjoy and bon appetit!!
Excellent food & excellent customer service! Best Vegas buffet by far! Great for any day or night! Definitely a 5 star!
The best buffet place in Vegas. It's worth the price. Almost every single item was great. Recommend to anyone who wanna try buffet in vegas.

I loved this place and always make sure to stop by Bacchanal whenever i'm in Vegas. however, this trip was drastically different. the food is no longer as delicious as i remembered, there were fewer options, and seafood did not seem fresh. worst of all, i got food poisoning the day after dining there.

Terrific. No other word for it. For the money, it cannot be beaten. Don't hesitate to pay $59 per person. It's legitimately worth it. They have absolutely anything that you could possibly want. Wagyu? Lamb t-bone? Snow crab? Tri-tips? Oysters? Kimchi? Tacos? Lobster? Crepes? You name it, they have it.

Honestly, the only thing keeping this place from receiving a fifth star is the fact that some or the food items have been sitting under a heat lamp, and you can tell. That part was a little bit disappointing, but to be expected from a buffet as huge as this one.

Definitely worth trying, since it is known to be the best buffet in the world. It is definitely the best I've ever been to.

Had brunch here last week with my group of friends in vegas celebrating a birthday.  We purchased the Groupon for 88 per couple. 

In my opinion the Groupon was worth it because you get to bypass the LONG  amusement park line! 

The food and service overall was great.  Our waitress was super nice and friendly.  Very attentive.  The food selection for brunch was good.  Our only disappointment  was the crab legs!! They don't serve it until 3pm and there was no way we can eat ourselves from 12 noon to 3. 

This buffet is definitely one of the better ones.  We'd definitely do this again but come later so we get the crab legs!

Food is very mediocre for the price. Desserts taste like they are from Costco. Nowhere near as good as the Wynn Buffet yet more expensive. Bachannal seems to value quantity over quality which is very disappointing considering that they're the most expensive buffet on the strip. Service was also very poor - the waiter didn't refill my drink and left plates of food on my table. Completely unacceptable.

Decided to go based on the reviews but our expierence we extremely disappointing. 

The buffet is extensive and the variety of types of food is amazing. The dessert were visually pleasing and our server was very attentive even though it was a buffet.

This was my first Vegas buffet expierence and I generally don't eat at buffets. So to begin with its a bit overwhelming and I wasn't sure where to begin but decided to start on the Asian end and to move forward. 

Unfortunately the Asian food was not very good, it was dried out and not hot. They had pork belly in two places, it was inedible, like shoe leather.

The salad, cheese, and charcuterie were good. Actually problem the best items they had. The made to order pasta station and made to order tacos were both very good. The tacos were one of my favorite items. They only other item that was good and memorable in a positive way was the posole.

The various meats they has was way too salty. I spent the day drinking a ton of water. There were multiple items I felt were on the salty side.

On to desserts, they were so pretty and artistic looking but the flavors weren't there.  It was just average. I was hoping to be wowed but they were underwhelming .

Really disappointed and if I had to stand in line or pay the amount many people did, I would be very upset rather than disappointed.

Did not find this place all that for brunch, maybe better for dinner.
Service was good but food was just okay. They have a large selection and all different types of food but nothing stood out.
For the money I'd just go to a regular restaurant, there are plenty of choices at Cesar's. 
I guess ones got to try it for themselves. 
OJ was good! Lol
Better if the buffets in Vegas that I have been to, while others have failed this has came through, haven't tried the dinner yet but I am very eager

This is definitely the best buffet on the strip! The choices are out of control. They have every type of cuisine you can imagine. From every single Asian dish imaginable (and they are all delicious) Tio Mexican food and so many seafood selections. Will definitely be back soon!
So big. So friendly. So pretty. Great time. Defitnely a must visit. Romos (or Romulus as it is on his name tag) was a great, attentive, and friendly waiter
Pretty good. Nice spread. Lots of good seafood, my kids were in heaven. Don't know if this is all the time, but if you check into yelp you can get a free wine, champagne or beer.

We stopped into Bacchanal after a weekend at the Life Is Beautiful festival and it was the best decision. I'm giving it a 4 star only because it is a little pricey being 90$ per person for the buffet. Very good food and quite a few vegetarian/vegan options that were yummy although I did expect a little more. I personally did not eat 90$ worth of food but for the quality I do understand. We were there on a Monday afternoon around 1pm and the wait was not very long maybe 10-15 minutes before we were taken to a table. It was busy but not overly crowded and the staff are friendly. Bottomless mimosas are 15$ and I don't remember them ever stopping so I'm sorry to say I can't confirm the cap on that. Overall the experience was nice, only 4 stars because it was a little pricey for me and I would love to see just a few more dairy free options in the buffet. Great food if you're looking for a buffet with a wide variety of foods.

Went to dinner at the Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace. This is supposed to be the best buffet in Las Vegas and one of the best in America. Where they are supposed to differentiate themselves is on having many items that are plated and well-presented vs. just items where people dish out spoons for themselves. Unfortunately, they underdeliver and provide a disappointing experience.

First issue here is the extremely long lines (queues) for the buffet. While they do have a system where you can go to a kiosk and get a ticket and then return to wait in line later, they really should take reservations so you can plan specific times in advance. Once you do get through the line, you pay. This is odd because you have no way to tip based on the actual service since the tip needs to be filled in on the receipt when you are paying upfront. Additionally, they are improperly asking people to provide ID with signed credit cards. With regard to the food items:
- Airline chicken was very good, and came plated with a mushroom risotto.
- BBQ Chinese Pork was mediocre, and was quite dry.
- Plated wedge salad was excellent, so much so that I ended up getting a second one.
- Crab legs, both hot and chilled, are good and they are pre-split so you don't need to deal with cracking.
- Sushi was okay, but definitely not the best to be had in Las Vegas.
- Fried chicken & waffle was a total joke. The waffle was a hard waffle cone, like what you would serve ice cream in. The chicken itself also was not that good.
- Salad bar section was somewhat limited in choices. They did not have peppers, for example.
- Italian meatballs were excellent and very flavorful.
- Chilled seafood choices were good with oysters, Jonah crab claws, and shrimp.
- Brisket from the carving station was excellent. This rivaled what you get in Texas.
- Deserts were generally good. Miniature pecan pie and apple pie was great. Tiramisu and gelato also excellent. They have over 15 flavors of gelato / sorbet.

Some of the seating at Bacchanal Buffet is also oddly positioned and has different parties/tables awkwardly close to each other. Service to bring beverages / refill was not very quick. Often we would go several minutes with empty glasses before being asked about refills or seeing someone to ask for more. One other issue is the desert area did not have chilled plates, and as a result some of the deserts with chocolate would start melting as soon as they were put plates that were hot. Additionally, for $55 there was no included alcoholic beverage at all. Other buffets will include a beer or glass of wine. The split of typical buffet fare vs. plated items was also 90% - 10%, and I was expecting to see more plated items. Also, some items were obviously mislabeled or lacking labels on the buffet.

Overall, the Bacchanal Buffet is not worth going to for dinner. The quality and execution is just not there for the price. This might be worthwhile at $25, but not at $55. You're better better off at the Bellagio, Wynn, or Aria buffets.

If you're in Las Vegas, you must check out this buffet. It's the B-O-M-B. Pricey, but worth it. It's over $50 bucks per person during dinner. Arrive early or grab a reservation ticket in advance to avoid the long wait. 

Like any other Asian, I love crab legs at a buffet. It's the best way to get my money's worth. Having said that, I hate how most Vegas buffets slice the crab legs down the middle. It actually makes it harder to get the meat for us crab enthuiast. At least they warm the legs up in boiling water prior to serving, which can be requested at the Italian section. Jumbo chilled shrimp? Yes!

This place even serves pho, which is actually not too bad for a buffet. It's not OMG amazing, but it's excusable. Try it out yourself and you'll know what I mean.

You'll hate yourself if you're seated next to the dessert section. It's that good. They have unlimited mochi ice cream. Yes, unlimited. No joke. Not as many flavors as last time, but I'm not complaining. I was content with the green tea and vanilla options.

Check this place out. I recommend it. Although I was not as excited coming here my second time, the buffet is still hands down a great eat.

When a highly anticipated movie comes out, everyone raves about it. Then my expectations are set high only to be let down when I actually go see the film. That is the case w Bacchanal. 

I was surprised by the 45 min from line to table when arriving at 12:30, since others claimed they waited over 2 hours. The cashier said everyone arrives around 1, wait in line and try to time it by staying for the dinner dishes starting at 3. It easily becomes a 2 hour wait before being seated. For me, it's just not worth the time wasted unless I'm sitting next to Bourdain.

The seating area is huge and cleverly partitioned by modern dividers made of wooden blocks or colored glass. The food stations were definitely not what I expected. Their claim of 500 items made me picture an endless line of different cuisines. Instead, there were a few average size stations. 

The layout is not well thought out. The Asian station is placed around a corner past the end of the Mexican station. Unless people are told, it may be easy to miss the entire area. The lines for the crab legs and oysters get long quickly and cuts right into the front of the carving station, which has its own line. The dessert station, its own island in the middle of the buffet is the exception. It's visible from all sides, easy to navigate and displays some tempting sweets ( macarons, ice cream mochi & exotic flavor gelato are some items that stood out ) 

The flavor of the dishes vary...
Tacos were good. But the steak tacos were too salty and oily.
Fried chicken in a basket was dry. Sweet pot fried underneath glistened w grease. 
Buffalo wings lacked that "kick". 
Tater tots were indeed crunchy and good as many had mentioned. 
Prime rib: bloody, tender and tasty. 
Brisket was also good but get the slice w the bark and some fat for flavor. 
Black chicken soup: fragrant, soothing and good. 
Ramen: not too bad, but don't expect a real nice bowl of perfectly cooked noodles w ingredients. They just threw in 1 piece of BBQ pork. I threw it back out. 
Steamed crab legs: good but need to ask for them.
Fresh OJ, watermelon juice and mango nectar in a small glass jar. Great! Stops at 3 so load up. 
Macarons, of course good
Mochi: same stuff in stores but they had Kona Coffee, which is harder to find in LA and not cheap. 
Corn beef hash w a tiny egg: very cute dish, almost a one biter but had no corn beef, just a tiny egg over potatoes. 
French sandwich w a tiny egg: also tiny and cute, but I pulled out something that looks like a hair, so skipped it. 

Though we were told it's regular menu, we were charged holiday prices. Using the Rewards card knocked off 2 bucks so it was $45 each. Not worth it imo. But for first timers wanting to fill the curiosity, try it during regular prices, at about $28 if I recall correctly (?)

Bacchanal is not a place I'm anxious to return to, but may give it another shot some time in the future.

It was $50.80 for Sunday Brunch... 

Food.. Um... okay...  The first prime rib I had was super delicious.. then i went for my 2nd one and then it was too salty.. guess it's not consistent...  The Chicken.. it was okay.. pollo loco taste better.  Fried chicken quarter/leg with sweet potatoes.. um... KFC taste better and Boiling crab sweet potatoes taste better.  Miso soup.. too salty... pesto pasta.. okay..  king crab leg.. alright.. kinda skinny but maybe because its not the season..  cocktail shrimp.. was nice and big and fresh.. 

Dessert... disappointed... too sweet.. they put out like 10 types to cookies.. it didnt even look delicious... :( I can't believe they didn't have cream puffs.. I know ppl say macaroons are good.. well... Definetely didnt show up on brunch menu :(  Vanilla ice cream.. too sweet... chocolate and peanut butter cookie.. too dried. tons of pastry.. 

The price I paid... I think I rather go Wynn's buffet... and My friend says she rather go to Cosmo buffet or Wynn's..

All three agree we wont be back here... 

I know dinner menu might be slightly different.. but.. im guessing the fried chicken, fried wings will still be on the menu.. advertise for 500 food items.. they have to have some dumb food items.. I didn't even bother to try some of the food.. cuz its not worth it and didnt look like you will drool over something.. 

One word.. OVERRATED...  

Maybe dinner was better.. but I don't know if I want to come back here..

This buffet advertises as the best buffet in Las Vegas. Not so. Very pricey, For the cost, it seems they are more interested in quantity rather that quality. Some items are just not edible. Overall very dissatisfied with quality of the food, poor preparation.  Will not return.
This isn't a bad buffet, and I would go again.  Definitely worth the money for a buffet and better than most that surround the area.  Great selection and cleaner food than most.

Dessert is excellent but other is salty
Icecream cake is good 
Seafood very salty 
Beef pork poor
Chicken is best

Local here! A few years ago I went to the buffet knowing it was the best buffet in town. At $50 price tag at the time, it was the best! Now with a $75 price tag I'm not so sure. Most the food were delicious but not better than when it was. Also 4 of the people that I came with became very sick and we were the only people to eat the oysters. I honestly don't know if I'll go here again.

Best new buffet in Vegas!  We showed up on a non-holiday sunday right before 2pm and there was only a handful of people ahead of us.  Cost was $45 for lunch time and I made sure I got my money's worth.  Buffet has a really nice modern design and big. Just when you thought the counter ended, there was more food around the corner.  Food is da bomb! I would consider it a much more "fancier" version of Studio B Buffet at the M Casino.  Quality meats that are so flavorful and tender and a great variety of food too.  I pigged out until I felt like I was going to explode (oh, the gluttony). Some memorable dishes: tacos from the taco lady, rack of lamb with meat sooo tender, King and Snow Crab legs already cut in half, sweet potato tater tots drizzled with brown sugar (reminded me of a dessert my grandmother used to make), dumplings, pork buns, spring rolls, oyster shooters, lobster chowder, corn dogs, sushi, pork chops, brisket, prime rib, sausages, chicken and "waffles", and way more... For dessert they had macarons, mochi ice cream, gelato, chocolate creme brulee, strawberry cheesecake pop, and way more. So much food! I will definitely be saving up that extra cash to come here again.

I will not give this place -1 star because of the small plastic spoons for dessert.

7 million dollar buffet? Caesars I salute you.

Bacchanal separates themselves with various mini containers of food. For example mini steak and eggs in a mini skillet. These little treasures are not only tasty but all wrap up in a little portion so you don't over eat.

Highlights:
Shrimp and grits
Crab
Prime Rib
Shrimp
Gelato- Thai Tea, Fig Balsamic, and Brown Ale.

Do yourself a favor and go early around 9am. No wait, when I left(4 hours later) the line was crazy.

I recommend avoiding weekends. They charge significantly more for the exam same buffet. They say Friday's buffet had an expanded weekend menu, but my brother said it was the exact same the last 4 times he went on a weekday.

Delicious food though and a fun experience.

Oyster was awesome! We went on a Wednesday night around 5:30pm so there was no wait for us. After 6pm was busy. 

We got seated right away and the sever was very friendly. There is a lot of choices from seafood (oyster, crab leg, clams), rib, sausages, Mexico food (seafood soup, chips, dips), Italian (pasta, salad), Japanese (salmon, sushi), and Chinese (veggie dumplings, pork buns...). Desert is the best! Egg tart and ube gelato

In previous years, it wasn't a Vegas trip unless you went to 1 or 2 buffets.  However, times have changed.  The days of going to your Circus Circus, or Stardust buffet, are over.  The abundance of not only good, but superb restaurants, is overwhelming.  The last few years, I strayed away from buffets and started going to these restaurants.  However, buffets are making a strong come back.  With your Wynn, Bellagio, Wicked Spoon, and of course, Bacchanal leading the charge. 
 
We came on Christmas weekend.  This meant there was a special holiday brunch/dinner menu.  Holiday pricing was $59.99 for brunch and $69.99 for dinner.  We came at brunch.  First, seating can be a little confusing if you're going with a group of 6 or more.  There is basically another line closer to the buffet room behind the regular cashier.  When you get there, you wait in a shorter line.  But, you don't pay there.  Basically, someone gets out of the line to go the cashier, and then goes back to wait again.  The wait, thankfully, wasn't too long.  I would have to say about 15 minutes total.  Not bad considering I've heard of wait times of 1-2 hours.
 
Now, for the food.  I can't believe I'm going to say this, but there was way too much food!  The selection is enormous and the plating was gorgeous.  You have your seafood station with different crab legs and cocktail shrimp to name a few.  There were also Mexican, Italian, and Chinese stations.  Not to mention salad, juice, and bread stations.  Some of the unique items were veal osso bucco, gnocchi, truffled potatoes, Chilaquiles, pork belly, and many different fruit juices.  Since this was brunch, of course they had  your omelet station, but I stayed away from that because I could get that at other places.  I also stayed away from the Chinese station, because I knew I couldn't try everything and I wanted to get the more unique dishes.  What stood out for me was the veal, the different salads, and churros and cronuts.  Now, those churros and cronuts weren't even in the dessert section.  The dessert section is a whole other story.  And a similar story.  The selection is quite extensive, but not only that, the desserts were absolutely scrumptious! 
 
Aside from the food, the service was phenomenal!  Jeff was the best by not only refilling our drinks, but he entertained the kids, just by being a great guy!
 
Because of the price, and my infrequent visits to Vegas now, I don't know if I'll be back any time soon.  Not to mention, I want to give the Wynn buffet another chance since they changed their menu up.  But, with than being said, I can't wait to cross Wynn off my list, so I can come back here again!

There are close to 9,000 reviews, so I don't think I can add anything too different than what has already been said.

 Came on a Friday at 2:15pm and there was a long line already.  We had a party of 3 adults and 2 children, so when we asked the worker what we do, she showed us a line for parties of 5 or more to skip the line and go straight to the register to pay.  She kinda had an attitude and said "how come no one ever reads the sign?"  Kinda pissed me off as that line was roped off, so how would we know where to go.  

Anyway, we paid $235 (including tip and tax) for 3 adults, 1 child, and 1 child under 4 who eats for free.  We had to wait in another line, but got seated after about a 5 minute wait.

The buffet was actually pretty good. I think they have too much stuff, there was some things I didn't even get to try because I was already full.  Nothing I ate was horrible, but the prime rib was a little dry.  My sister and brother in law enjoyed their seafood and I thought the sushi and Asian food were especially tasty.  You should pace yourself as you might fill yourself up on some foods and won't have the appetite to try others.

I wouldn't pay $60 bucks for a buffet back home, but when you're in Vegas, you have to try it.  I would recommend you try it if you have not done so before, but i probably won't be back.
Back again. Solid 4-4 1/2 stars. Definitely the best buffet in Vegas hands down.

This buffet was awesome!!! I recommend going during the week though, especially if it's a holiday weekend. You'll be more susceptible to finding a coupon to combat the cost of M thru F prices as well. I went over Labor Day weekend this past Saturday. The wait was 2 hours!!!
Jennifer made sure I had all I can eat.  This is the best place to go right before the pool so you will look your best. ;)

The place is definitely over hyped. The food was good, decoration were good,the vibe was good but the service is terrible! They know they're getting their money that's why they don't care. Overall the experience was adequate. This wasn't what I was expecting from a fine establishment like this in Vegas especially in Caesar's palace...

Came here for a second time this past weekend and I'm still blown away! 

I love the food here. Most of the stuff Is perfectly cooked, packed with flavor, and delicious!

I've been here a few times now and had amazing experiences and also not so good ones.  Surprisingly, we went for lunch and had a better experience than dinner.  The items were quite similar and you're paying a little less.  Lines are also not has horrendous during the day.  

Tip:  Get a travelzoo voucher if it's available.  You get a huge discount and a VIP pass.  Makes your visit that much better.  

Speaking of VIP passes, I can't believe how crazy the lines get where some people feel as though they need to cough up extra to get through the line faster.  I believe I've waited 2 hours before so be prepared.  

As far as the food, Bacchanal is the best buffet as far as desserts.  They do offer many meat choices including wagyu.  Seafood is a little more extensive than other buffets with fancier items and a nice ambiance.  

Service was pretty basic as the other buffets on the strip.  They'll get to you eventually for your drink orders.  Lunch is prob the best way to go, in my opinion.
Loved this! Got a custom made gluten free pasta due to celiac! It was awesome as the first time! My new favorite place!

I can't wait till I'm bacc for more.

Just thinking bacc to the meal I had at Bacchanal Buffet makes me hungry and as such I think it's important that I give the buffet the right feedbacc to convey the emotions and culinary pleasures that BB offers.

I've gone to a decent number of buffets in my short time on this fascinating planet and I can say with great certainty that Bacchanal Buffet has been the best in terms of food quality- by far. It is a bit pricey, but totally worth. SO WORTH.

The variety of food offered ranges from delicate salad croutons to finely prepared steak to skillfully crafted asian cuisine to dessert chocolate blocks... basically this place offers a TON of different options to suit almost every customer imaginable.

Sweet tooth? No problem, head to the endless dessert bar and cop 37 (or more) blocks of cube-shaped chocolate or perhaps a tiramisu cup of joy.

Don't have a sweet tooth? Not a problem either. Head to the normal-food section and indulge in the carbohydrate and protein filled selections that populate themselves on the buffet stations that politely and anxiously wait for you.

Bottomless mimosas for just a few bucks more and you're truly prepared for liftoff.

I'll be bacc.

Location: Inside Caesar's Palace in the back of the Casino, was a bit hard to find had to ask around. 

Decor: Beautiful! Everything was so nicely placed and eye catching. Very clean, the only thing i didn't like was that not everything there was labelled. The Charcuterie board we had to guess what the meats and cheese's were. The cold pressed drinks we had no idea what was in them. They need more labels. Including the desserts stating what is in them.

Food & Drinks: The food was mediocre at best. I would say the best thing there was the desserts & seafood. The Chinese and Japanese food is a big pass. The Charcuterie board was also very bad, the cheese was ROCK HARD. You can barely bite into it. I did like their soups, should definitely try their lobster bisque and truffle soup. Very strong flavors amazing! Their oyster shooter's come with decent sized oysters too. The desserts my favourite was the Vietnamese Coffee cream. Would say for how much this place costs, its not worth it. Do not get the drinks, absolutely terrible. Both the pressed drinks and the lemonade... and peach green tea was so bad. 

Service & Cost: Service is quick, our tables were always cleared by the time we came back. Bill was quick, she also came by to check on us to see if everything was okay. For cost i would definitely not say its worth it. We paid $47 for lunch which comes out to around almost $60 Canadian. It was nice to try it out since it was supposed to be the #1 buffet in Vegas, but i will not be returning.

For a buffet, its probably one of the better ones I've been to in a while. However, if this is the best buffet in Vegas I'd be terrified to go to any other buffet on the strip or Fremont Street. 

The Good: 
- The line to get in to the restaurant moves quickly. I believe I waited about 20 minutes in what looked like an incredibly long line. 
- The variety is great. From steakhouse favorites to Asian to Latin American and Southern fare nearly everything is covered
- Things that were supposed to be cold were cold, and vice-versa. 
- The buffet areas and the dining room was clean 

The Bad: 
- Service in the dining room was awful. I was finished with my salad plate and up getting my main entrees before I ever got a drink. 
- The oysters are horrible. They're giant and have a pungent milky center that oozes in your mouth. I almost gag just thinking about them (and I like oysters)
- The food was average even though there was a good variety. There was really no difference in this and any other decent buffet other than more choices. There also weren't any choices that were "decadent" or "awe-inspiring". 

In all, it was an okay experience. In my mind, a mediocre sit-down restaurant is still better than a "good" buffet.

Update review:
I decided to come back this weekend. The seafood section was the best section, all fresh, my favorite was the big shrimp and snails. Mexican and Chinese sections were also great. Desserts are excellent with so many choices.  I still think some of the food were salty, especially the ramen soup. I drank lots lots of water afterwards. However they provided excellent customer service, nice atmosphere! 

*********
Waited in a long line at 7:30pm for one hour on a Sunday night to get in the table. Food was really salty, that night I had to drink 2 liter of water but still felt so dry in my throat.  I think they did it in purpose so that you couldn't eat much!! Not worth $75 at all for these kind of salty food! I didn't even touch the meat section. One of the crab leg tasted bad, probably was left out for too long. Also the cold soba was sour, I think it also went bad for being outside too long.  The last 2 times I went to this buffet the quality had gone down, not the same as it was 2-3 years ago! I will not come back to this buffet again.

What's the point in having a text-message based wait system if there is an additional half hour wait after you receive the text message? After posting this review, staff contacted me just to say that is how their waiting system is supposed to work. These are obtuse people.

My party was moved to a different table after being seated, then the waitress took half an hour to get around to cleaning a spill after saying she would go grab a towel.

This place is badly managed.

I first heard of this place through the food travel channel so I needed to visit when in Las Vegas! 
Then asking the concierge at our hotel they named Bacchanal and other to got to for all you can eat buffet but this was the number one spot, the place to eat so we went! 
First reservations are hard to get and trying get there without reservations you normally have to wait longer or just go later at night. Our reservation ended up being at 8:30 so we arrive a little early. When we arrived there was a big crowd, it was like as if you were heading to a theme park. The system at arrival was not so people friendly. First there was a system that the restaurant has that they expected you to already know what to do. When getting there you me suppose to go to these computer screens to get your reservation ticket which no one informed people who were arriving so everyone just followed the crowd into a roped area. This roped are also did not make sense because it was too thigh to fit the groups that were coming in. Once in line a staff member would ask for your ticket that you never got from the computer, this had one person from our group go back to the computer to get it and it was just not us it was majority of the people waiting in line. Once you get to the hosts table you get separated into different line based on how much people are in your group so if you have more than two people you are left waiting even more to get a table. 
Once inside I was excited. However I think it was the time we had was towards the end of the night because we didn't start eating until after 9:00pm with waiting to get seated. The pictures that I posted are the fresher of the batch of food that was presented. 
Everyone was there for the seafood especially the crabs. But the line was long because people were picking out what they wanted. The sections I enjoyed the seafood, fresh made pasta, and steam dim sum. 
I was disappointed in the most of the  selection I thought there would be creative ideas or new flavors created for this menu being such a higher end buffet and the price that you pay for $$. Instead I felt it was average quality of food.

**UPDATE**

The food was amazing the manager Brian who reached out to me and let me know that the food has changed did a wonderful job after manager of the establishment. I would definitely be back and the macaroni and cheese with the jalapenos in it was superior. Here are some of the pictures I took of the food that I ate.Bacchanal Buffet was really delicious.

Santiago, our server was nice. Steamed crab station is actually​ boiled. Separate area from cold crab. When I visited, they split the crab legs lengthwise and it was a bad idea because a ton of sandy, shell bits were everywhere.

The line to get in was so long. 

Ate here as part of the 24 hr buffet pass. We paid extra $ to go to this buffet. You have to get the total rewards card for each person for the discount.

2016 Yelp 100 Review Challenge 88/100

I've been meaning to try this buffet for a while now (but the price tag was a turn off for a local Las Vegan like me who's been to almost all the buffets in Vegas) BUT relatives from Hawai'i and Rhode Island were in town and they mentioned that this was THE buffet they wanted to go to. Coincidentally, this was THE buffet that popped into my head when they said they only had time for one buffet. For a few of them, it was their first time in Vegas...and when you're in Vegas you gotta go with the best, the #1 buffet in Vegas, right?!

With a group of 9 and being islanders...yes, that can make things complicated. Some of us are always on that "Hawai'ian time" haha. Fortunately, we were all seated immediately when our whole party arrived. 

The most memorable options from Bacchanal: 

- My fave was the Thai Curry mussels. I LOVE Thai curry and I LOVE mussels. I went back for more. 
- Along with that, the most memorable were the Pork Belly with yams (surprisingly, it worked well together) 
- pork street tacos - freshly grilled, there's usually a line but worth the wait. 
- chocolate cake pop, steamed crab legs, flavorful clams. 
- ohhhhhh and the cheese station. I LOVE CHEESE. I enjoyed their selection. I went back for more. I love cheese. 

The juice station was a nice touch. I loved it! I haven't seen that in any other buffet. Sorry, no photo. I tried the tamarind and horchata. They were delicious. I love the fact that it's displayed in bottles, so after you pile your plate you can stop here on your way back and pick up a bottle without worrying about spilling. 

Being a buffet pro, I strategically saved dessert for last. I didn't want to get too full too fast. 

Tip: No carbs, save dessert for last, don't drink too much liquids, eat your seafood (crab legs ;-) ) first. Check out your options first before you start piling your plate. 

Our beverage server was ON POINT. He had the best customer service skills that I've seen in any buffet or food service establishment. I'm sorry, I don't remember his name. He checked up on us every few minutes, he was kind, enthusiastic, full of energy. His work ethic was a 20 on scale of 1 to 10. 

 The dessert station is the best I've seen so far in all Vegas buffets. They have a made to order crepe station!!! I was too full to try the crepes but my cousins got to try it and they enjoyed it. The most popular items that night were the cake pops and macaroons. Those were awesome. Those were restocked every 30 mins. Luckily on my last trip back to the dessert station the macaroon tray was filled. Yes! I finally get to try it. 

I've went to many buffets here and this is the one I'd recommend! One of the few must try buffets if you only have time for one during your trip!

The line was super long.  First have to check in at kiosk to come back at the time assigned.  Another wait to pay at cashier and another wait to get the table.  Doesn't matter you stay in the hotel, they don't care.  So why we have to care to come back again.  Better stay another hotel where they care their guests.
Quality of food is not all that great. Soggy, cold. Price is way higher than what they're actually worth.

4th time and still the best buffet I've had in Vegas. 
The only downside is that the lines can sometimes take 1hour+

+Try to come with a group of 5 to get past the regular lines or make some friends and go together to be in the party line.

+Desserts are awesome. Try a bit of everything
+prime rib is great, the horseradish is super strong and delicious
+so much variety of food and it's all good so eat a little bit of everything
