$55 buffet?  Yes.  Worth it?  Yes. 

By far the best buffet I have had in my life, the quality of all the food here was well above what I had imagined it would be.  The beef brisket they had here was worth $55 dollars alone.  And for the price you get a glass of wine or beer.  

They have something for everyone, if you a bit hesitant to try it because of the price, just do it, it is worth it.

This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas. It is so expensive but they have everything you could ever want. The food is delicious and I love how there are several made to order areas where you can request things like tacos and slices of meat. There is a time limit here if two hours. There are also several lines to wait in to get in. The larger your party the longer the wait. If you go for breakfast or lunch it's much less expensive than dinner I honestly just love the variety of foods you can get here. There is so much to see and this is truly the biggest feast around!

I am a huge fan of this place! Everything tasted amazing. Quick tip, the steamed crab legs aren't located in the seafood section but can be found by the pasta/pizza area. I highly recommend saving room for dessert and complete your meal with some exotic gelato flavors or a create your own crepe :)
The food here is amazing! Hands down the best buffet I ever been to in my life!! So many options and they all taste amazing!! I will definitely be back!!

How this place has 4 stars is beyond me. The food is average at best, and the service is subpar to say the least. I guess you can't really expect gourmet from a buffet. But when you pay extra to be a VIP, you would expect, well, VIP service. Save yourself and time, money and trouble and visit your favorite fast food spot

I'm baffled why this buffet has good reviews. 2 stars is quite generous rating in my opinion.

When compared with other buffets is the MOST EXPENSIVE, however ever disappointing. I would leave hungry if not for desserts! Not worth $90 for 2 people for lunch. Everything is VERY SALTY, I mean by a lot.

Seafood - very old and limited (don't be fooled by the photos!)
Fish - nothing available 
Vegetable - nothing eatable unless deep fried
Crepes - undercooked

Quality: 2/10
Variety: 4/10
Service: 7/10
Atmosphere: 7/10


Buffets that are better:
1. Wynn
2. Belagio
3. Paris
and probably few other


Conclusion:
Will not be coming back 100%

If you're looking for the best of the best, look no further, Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's is THE best buffet in the world! Bacchanal sets the bar and standards high and there's no competition against the other Vegas buffets (I've been to most of them- Wicked Spoon, Wynn's The Buffet, M Buffet, Carnival World Buffet, Bellagio). This place is foodie paradise for food and buffet lovers. 

Expect long lines especially on the weekends around lunch time so you won't get too hangry. There's lines separated by party size (groups of one to two, three to five, and more than six) and by status (gold/general admission, platinum, or Seven Diamond). I went here on a Saturday at 12:30PM and didn't get seated until 1:30. You first check in at the entrance to get your time ticket then they will text you to come back to get in line. An hour wait wasn't terrible when you can kill time gambling at the casino or shop at the Forum Shops.

Price for weekend brunch is $50 as of August 2017 plus you can bottomless alcohol (pick one- champagne, mimosas, beer) for $15 which is a good deal! Last time I went here was in August 2015 and weekday brunch was $30 (weekday brunch is now $40) so the prices definitely went up since then. Don't be surprised by the price because they have over 500 food items that are high quality and unique items to eat at a buffet that cost $50 if you order a meal at a restaurant. You are definitely getting your money's worth at this buffet!

There's different stations- Seafood, Carving Station, Mexican, Breakfast, Italian, Salad, and Asian and of course desserts! Where else can you get all you can eat crab legs, dungeness crabs, stone crabs, Manila clams, lobster eggs benedict, lobster bisque, crawfish boil, American wagyu beef, prime rib, sushi, salmon and tuna poke and 490+ items that I didn't list?! The desserts is amazing and decadent where there are delicious desserts like creme brulee, gelato (flavors like mango banana, green tea ginger, and roasted coffee), rice pudding, panna cotta, dulce de leche, and even a crepe station! 

The only negative was that service was a bit slow but I felt bad for our server because it was super busy on a Saturday at lunch time. He was walking around and serving multiple large parties of 6 or more so he was MIA for a little bit but we did get our waters and our bottomless drinks filled so I at least appreciate his hard efforts.

Eat like a queen (or king) at Bacchanal Buffet, it's so worth the price and experience!

Let's call this place for what it really is, honestly a little overhyped.  Yes, the oysters are all you can eat, but I can hardly bring myself to call those dry morsels "oysters".  I tried to taste as many different items as I could, but went HAM on the oysters and crab legs, a trait instilled in me by my frugal Asian heritage.

Although I am very salty about the oysters, the crab legs were, well, crab legs.  I like to get a small cup of melted butter and amass a huge collection of crab meat, then mix the concoction and gorge on my delectable creation.

Other great contenders were the Potatoes with truffle shavings, and lobster soup.  The desserts were also plentiful and tasty, but dear lord in heaven what the hell are those things they call Macaroons?

Tasteless, dry and god awful, these macaroons left a salty taste in my mouth much like Napoleon felt after the Battle of Waterloo.

I regret not trying out the warm crab legs that were only available upon request at the Italian station.  Also, the sushi sucked, if I'm paying upwards of $60 for this buffet, I think I can damn request some decent sushi.

All things considered, Bacchanal Buffet IS very impressive, but in my opinion, overhyped for the price they charge.  Aside from some few unique dishes, the overall experience does not live up to the expectations that I feel were set by other respectable reviews.

That being said, if you have a little extra money to spend or profit a lot from your blackjack winnings in Vegas, do try the Bacchanal Buffet at least once in your life!  I do not think I will be returning anytime soon, for I am just a poor boy and nobody loves me. (He's just a poor boy from a poor family).

Recommended by a friend, who researched everuthing for us onthe Vegas trip. This brunch buffet IS by far, the BEST!   We were sticker shocked, as the meal is allmost 50$ per person, plus tip, & there is a parking fee from Ceasars Hotell of an additional 18$

There is EVERYTHING you can imagine on it.  Far to much to even try to explain.

The service and the food was the best our group had.  However, I do not recommend taking children.

If you only want to stuff yourself once during your trip to Vegas, Bacchanal Buffet is the place to go. A wide range of selections from Asian to Italian to Mexican to seafood to carved meat. It's got something for everyone. Not to mention a nice spread of desserts.  

My favorites were as follows:
1) Steamed crab legs: it's probably the only station where you may see a line but it moves fast. The guy who served it was super nice and generous if you asked for a bit more. And the best part is that the legs were half cracked already so it was much easier to get the meat out.

2) Roast duck leg and sautéed vegetables. Those were in the back section so make sure you don't miss it. There were also dim sum stations.

3) Seafood: snails and cocktail shrimps were good. Raw oysters were huge but there was sand in some. There were also cooked seafood such as salmon, trout, seafood paella, etc.

4) Desserts: tried coconut sorbet, green tea and ube ice cream. So good. Make sure you save room for desserts. Lots of flavors to choose from.

5) Drinks: Guava juice and home made horchata were awesome. I must have a few cups of those. Got a big pot of coffee all to myself. Soda and juice was included. 

PS: we got there around 2:30pm to pay for the lunch prices and dinner started at 3pm. Saved $10 pp. Line is much shorter too (waited about 15 mins). There was no one waiting around 4:15pm so that's another good time to go. 

Service was attentive. Good quality of food. You won't be disappointed.

OMG! SO GOOD!!!! SO FREAKING GOOD!!!! Well worth the hour long wait for a Monday lunch! Seriously, the moment I was in, I had no idea where to go first! SO MUCH GOOD FOOD!!!! Fresh shrimp, prime rib, sushi, Italian, Chinese, Mexican, EVERYTHING! I don't think I have ever eaten so much food at one time! I really recommend wearing stretchy pants- you'll be so stuff that you'll really appreciate more belly space :P

My favorite part of the buffet was, by far, the dessert station- there were loads of ice creams, tiramisu, strawberry shortcake, MULTIPLE kinds of creme brulee, and even A CREPE-MAKING STATION! Ah, it was foodie heaven!!! I cannot wait to go back the next time I'm in Vegas!!!

Our large family of 13 had an amazing time eating here, and it was amazing! Shoutout to the Ice cream man today, Deimar, for being so wonderful and kind. By far the nicest employee I have ever met! Highly recommend.

This place was good if you don't mind dropping some cash. On a Wednesday night it took about 20 minutes to get in and get going. All the food was above average for a high end buffet. The roast pork belly and dim sum was very good. I was lucky to get some hot snow crab legs and they were excellent, one of the cooks hooked me up so I tipped him 10 bucks. Otherwise I would have to wait about 20 minutes to get it. The meats were awesome, the desserts were awesome, the ramen was very good, the only thing that was pretty sad was the sushi, it was not good.

Was expecting better flavors at this price. I have had a better experience at the M Buffett for less money. The lines were long at the seafood and the mimosas took long to get to the table. Overpriced and overcrowded

Everyone kept telling me how good this place is so we decided to try it.  One word describes the buffet - Awesome!!!  Food was fresh and delicious. It was a great mix of seafood, assorted meats, Italian and Asian. I am sure I missed a lot of it.  The seafood was terrific - - A good assortment of steamed crab legs, lobster, shrimp and more.  Wagyu beef was off the charts.  I left some room for dessert and I really  wish I had space to try everything else.  Great experience.

Great buffet but pricey. There were many high end options available such as bone marrow or steaks and lobster. However, it definitely is pricey compared to other buffets on the strip. The buffets at Aria and Cosmo may be a better deal and food is also good at those. Overall, good for a first time Vegas buffet experience.

We went for lunch and were disappointing with the selection based on what I had seen online for dinner. I know it was cheaper, but it felt as though it was a half effort at lunch time. Overall the quality of the food was way above average buffets, but some dishes were much better than others. The sliders, cheese selection, tiny plated salads/vegetables, and tacos were stand out items at the buffet. The sushi was decent too as well as the meat station. There was a lot missing from the seafood section at lunch time so if you are a seafood fan do NOT go for lunch.

The desserts were nicely displayed, but it was a mixed bag in terms of flavor. The strawberry cheesecake pops were amazing and the green tea creme brulee was creative, but the red velvet whoopie pie was flavorless. 

Although I enjoyed the lack of a crowd during lunch time at Bacchanal, your money may be better spent at dinner, when I assume they put in more effort.

Wow I never thought I would have the patience to stand in line and wait for this Buffett. I came here for lunch/brunch on a Friday. It was about 11AM. There was a line but I saw it move quickly so I jumped right in. We were in the line for a good 15 - 20 minutes before we were allowed to get seated. During lunch, it was $40 per plate. I thought it was worth it. I tried a little bit of everything from every section. This Buffett had an Asian, Italian, seafood, roast bar, Mexican, soup bar, and dessert bar. Everything was served in small portions/plates so you wouldn't over indulge. I was a huge fan of their truffle soup, prime rib, roasted vegetables, and salad selections. I had their fried chicken but I didn't think it was anything out of the ordinary. I really suggest you hit the roast bar.

ROACH crawled onto our table. Manager was nice but Wonder how many other roaches lurking around....

Ate at this buffet because it was highly recommended by my brother. We came here for annual business conference so our meals were paid for by company.

Still my favorite buffet!

unfortunately they have cut down their gelato selection to a quarter of what it used to be.  an improvement is the electronic waiting system where it texts you when you should come back and get in the line, very convenient! 

Favorites included:
- shrimp and cheesy grits
- selection of salsas
- fresh pineapple and watermelon juice
- cheesy tots
- SUPER DELICIOUS CHICKEN and waffles
- corn bread
- ceviche
- fresh donuts with banana and syrup
- basil and sundried tomato pasta
- SEAFOOD RISOTTO (or was it a paella?) 
- lobster benedict
- BISCUITS
- nutella gelato

Don't waste your time: 
- red velvet pancakes (dry and tasteless)
- salty green beans

Definitely master the technique of having a eating partner so that you can split the small plates (they add up and make you full if you eat all of it alone) so you guys can try more foods.   honestly I did not have room for more, otherwise I would have expanded into the congee and dim sum section.

Get the groupon because that is worth the price, Do not pay full price up front because that is to much for a buffet no matter how good it is. Overall we came for breakfast and did the groupon for two people $88 is a steal, but they charge you some tax when you get there about $7 i believe. Breakfast has a lot of options, never thought I would be eating clams and shrimp early morning but I was. everything is fresh and good and never disappoints, you will leave full and satisfied. I sadly have never had the chance to come here for lunch or dinner, this was my second time coming for breakfast and have left feeling happy and full majority of the day. Money well spent, lots of buffets out in vegas. I would not wait 2 hours for this though because no body should wait that long to eat, so much things to do in vegas honestly then wait for a buffet.

The best buffet in Las Vegas!! You won't regret it. Plenty of options and quality of food is excellent. 5 star buffet for sure. It is a little pricey but it's worth it, there's so much food, it's overwhelming. Wait times are a little long. Very clean and organized. Staff is friendly and helpful.

IMO THE buffet to go to in Vegas if you want to treat yourself. At almost $70 for dinner it starts losing the buffet value proposition. Food however is very good with a large and diverse selection using high quality (and often high priced) ingredients. Nicely laid out and decorated as well. If you're not doing Vegas on a budget I say give it a go.

One of the best buffets hands down! My friends and I had a Groupon here for brunch and it came with mimosas and at a cheaper price with VIP passes! They also have dinner option if you're interested!

The food: oh my it is so good! They have so many options from Asian, Italian, meats, seafood, and more! They definitely have different types of food for everyone. I got to try different foods that I've never tried before. Usually I don't try new food but here I'm willing to! They have different unique foods you normally don't see! The dessert section is AMAZING!! The gelato bar is soo freaking good! Definitely try it.

The service: we had really good service all around! The waiters were very attentive and always refilled our drinks and took our plates away. My group of 4 ordered lots of drinks but she was able to give us everything we wanted! 

Definitely check this place out if you're visiting Las Vegas!

Buffetus Maximus! 
This is a great buffet! They had a great selection of different foods, all prepared deliciously! We came here for breakfast after an all-night gambling binge. The shrimp and salmon were a welcome sight for our sore eyes. They had snow crab too, which was delicious. 
The food went on, and on, and on. In fact, I didn't even realize I had missed about a quarter of the food by the time I was nearly full. There's more around the corner that I didn't realize was there. 
All the food was fresh, and meticulously prepared. Each dish was delicious, and there was nothing that tasted badly. 
I really enjoyed the eggs Benedict. They had two varieties, including a curry flavored version that was exotic as it was yummy. 
The thing I didn't care for was the fact that we had to have the hostess seat us as some particular table, even though 95% of the seats were free. Also, we couldn't get our own drinks, we had to have the waitress come and bring us coffee and juice. Most of the time, she was nowhere to be found. Fortunately, she saw our beady red eyes and knew to bring us a carafe of coffee. 
The place was incredibly clean. Every time I made a mess at the buffet (which was often), I was impressed to see that it was cleaned up by the time I went back for more. 
The music was weird, an Enya-like mix of strange music. I did enjoy the view of the Temple Pool at Caesar's. The decor at the buffet was rather unassuming. Not much to look at.
The buffet wasn't as good as the one at the Bellagio, but was much better than the one at the Mirage.  
I never found the vomitorium.

Not worth it! Long wait, rude receptionist, old dry food, and watered down wine and sauces. I don't get how it can be so bad, and have such an ego. Wait staff was excellent, too bad food was not. Very disappointing.
Julie was the best!  Would come back the food was perfect love the eggs and bacon and waffles
Be a yes person. Come here for brunch. Maricela our waitress was fantastic!! Will be back :)

I'm here again found out they don't serve ribeye anymore major disappointment and the lamb chops not quite good also.  The oysters seem to take awhile to be brought out.  Hot crab legs over by the Italian side and the cocktail shrimp are still good.  The sliders are still awesome.  The desserts are good also.
oh yes! If you want to go to an amazing BUFFET!... This is where you go to. It has everything under the roof! Asian, Mexican, Seafood, Delicious Desserts! etc.

November, 27, 2018

We went for dinner tonight.. no king crab legs (I couldn't find them past half hour, until I almost to leave.. 2 of us just tried 4 pieces of it, we are not big fan of it) , Peking duck, big snails as in September dinner buffet.. but its USD $10 less than in September.

We paid USD $54 + $8 tips per person. Not much line up.. waited less than 15 minutes..

I didn't eat much.. I tried...

Waygu beef... 1st slice was too cooked, chewy and hard to cut... 2 and piece was medium rare.. way better...

Prime rib... way better than waygu beef... more juicy

Beef morrow bone.... too fat.. too much herbs on top

Fresh oysters... pretty fresh

Snails... a lot of sand inside

T bone lamb... extremely dried and over cooked

Ribs ... taste too much curry on it

Some dessert..

Some juice and red wine as well..

There's a lot of selections... but not worth for the price we paid for...

This is the worst experience at Bacchanal. I got food poisoning from the seafood I ate there. Oysters is the killer! Don't trust their seafood! I was been sent to the hospital by ambulance. Spent a night at the hospital and no one from the buffet come and visit me or solve any problems the next day. I have been waiting for a whole week now. Their risk management is the worst too. I called at least 6times to get in touch with them. Now I am looking for lawyers to help me. No Bacchanal buffet again! I got two reports from iwaspoisoned.com, both of them happened on August 10-11th 2019.

Excellent food, everything was perfectly cooked, and carefully made to perfection. Each and every item I ate was superb and can't wait to go back for more.  The only negative thing was the long line getting in but what do you expect when coming in on a Friday? :-)

Always my go-to buffet when I'm in town.
500 or more dishes to choose, you can always find something that you like.

Wow!!! Amazing. This buffet has been ranked #1 for so long and I admit, I was skeptical. What makes the Bacchanal at Caesar's top rated? First, the staff is attentive, they are constantly putting out food and cleaning the area around the dishes. Do you know yucky buffets can get? Not here. The staff at the Bacchanal kept the food areas spotless. No food spills or errant pieces of broccoli in the rice. Perfect. 
There are various lines to get to the counter to pay and the lines do move pretty fast. I can only imagine what these lines look like during peak tourist season. It wasn't as bad in February. About a 10-15 minute wait for dinner. Price is about ~$65 and if you want to add bottomless mimosas or wine or a Bloody Mary to the dinner, it's an extra $15 (So. Worth. It). 
Our waitress, Sue? Just lovely. She made sure we always had our Mimosas and water. Word to the wise: this buffet is massive. You need a strategy because it can feel quite overwhelming. I started out with the made to order Tacos (shout out to the handsome guy on the grill Friday night). Lots of sea food. Most people were drawn to the king crab legs. There were two stations of this alone. I can't even describe all the food havens. Whatever you wanted, you could probably find here. 
The dessert station had at least a dozen flavors of gelato including Ube. Come hungry. I had an amazing time. Remember to tip the servers.

Believed to be one of the best buffets in Vegas, and I would have to agree with that! 

My friends and I decided to come here for lunch on Monday, and when we approached the entrance, there were hella people. When we checked how long the wait was, the check in thing said it would be 6 hours...Our flight was in 4 hours, so there's no way we were going to wait.

However, they do let you cut in line for a fee of $26. That's like the price of two meals! Time is money, money is time tho! Luckily, we had a big party and we ended up going to the "big party" line and waited only 20 minutes. 

Of course, selection is impressive and generally everything is decent or beyond. Worth spending the $50 to enjoy! Its comparable to Wicked Spoon, but there's less desserts here. No chocolate covered strawberries, but there are fresh squeezed juices.

This by far has been the best buffet we've had in Vegas.  It is on the pricier side but the food is delicious.  The selection of seafood is mind blowing. Crab, shrimp, crawfish, clams and oysters. There is a huge selection of meet at the carving station to choose from as well as the traditional sides.  There is a large selection of Asian food as well.  Whether you have a craving for fried rice, dim sum or ramen they have it covered.  They also had a station to make tacos per your request with tortilla soup and posole. Our waitress was friendly. The reason that a star was deducted is that table booth we were sat at was filthy on the seats.  That aside i don't think anyone will be disappointed in the food selection and the quality of the food.

This buffet is probably the best on the Las Vegas strip. The prices are really high for a buffet, but the restaurant is nice and there are seemingly endless options. There are multiple sections for each food type-asian (sushi, stir fry), Italian (pastas, pizzas), deli food (fresh meats and cheeses), American (beans and mashed potatoes), seafood (crab legs, clams), salad bar, and healthy options (smoothies and hummus).  The drink options for us were juices, hot teas and coffee, sparkling water with berry infusion, and horchata. The dessert bar was by far my favorite spot. Located on the other side of the restaurant, it has mini treats, a crepe bar, and a gelato bar. They have full-sized cupcakes, mini donuts, caramel corn, cake slices, custards, and so much more. The service was amazing!! Our server was great. He checked in on us often and brought our drinks quickly. Overall, I love this buffet. The only thing is it is expensive. If you are willing to splurge, I think it's worth it once in a while.

I came here with my husband for lunch, and we came in with high hopes because one of the Youtubers I watch is in love with this buffet (Mikey Chen if ya'll were wondering). Maybe he came for dinner because the lunch spread was not impressive to either of us. The quality of the food is just like what you would find at any other place. Not much stood out to us. Even though there was a variety of foods, we couldn't really name a dish that stood out to us. The foods tasted just ok and not worth what we paid (I think around $50 per person). Honestly, the best thing about the buffet is the dessert. The gelato was outstanding and I just kept coming back for it. Maybe we would have to try again for dinner, but for first impressions, we wouldn't want to come back for lunch.

Had breakfast here on Sunday, the best buffet in Vegas so far. I sampled far more food then I should have, but everything that I ate could be something that I would be willing to eat as a main course in a meal. Worth the experience!!!!

I just WISH my stomach was larger so I could eat more. Almost every single dish was so good, I wanted to keep eating. It is pricey, so this is one of those special treats to share with a special person. The food selection was broad and extensive. It takes a few trips just to get around to the end of it all. Then you'll need at least two plates for dessert. I love this place!

Best buffet in America period! 
Ate here twice and was so good. Wish they have this in Maryland I'd be there everyday!

We came for lunch and stayed for dinner.

Hands down, Bacchanal beats every other buffet in town in terms of service and sheer number of offerings. There's so much to choose from, it's impossible to eat everything. Believe me, we tried. You name it, Bacchanal has it. Seafood, Italian, Mexican, carving station, Chinese, Japanese, charcuterie, etc. 

As soon as it hits 3:00pm, they switch over to dinner, the crab legs come out, and everyone goes crazy. Watch out, because people will start throwing elbows! They do steamed crab legs, along with chilled ones. The king crab is mixed in with the snow crab, so you kind of have to just pile a bunch on your plate and hope for the best. Boyfriend plowed thru two plates of crab for every one I had. The oysters and shrimp were also incredibly fresh. 

We spent roughly two hours here and ate so much we weren't hungry until the next day. The lines can get long, but I think it's worth it. The dessert section was also impressive. Overall, service and food quality were great. I totally get why this is rated the best buffet in Vegas.
Place is still good but not like it use to be . I will still come occasionally as I'm a diamond player but it's good to try other places on the strip .
This Buffet was everything we had seen on YouTube. Definitely the best buffet on the strip. Worth its price. Loved the variety and selection will return. The wait is not bad either.

Wife wanted sushi and raves about this place so checked it out. Business is in a sketchy area but once inside I found the staff was friendly and attentive. Food arrived in a reasonable time even with business levels being extremely busy on my visit. I tried several items on the minute and was more than satisfied with all my choices. There was a large selection to choose from. Pretty sure they would offer something to satisfy everyone. Price was reasonable I would eat there again.
This was the second time I ate here. The first experience was a wonderful experience. This time, the waiter was inattentive to custom

Best buffet I've ever been to ..... my husband and I ate there to celebrate our birthday the wait was about an hour or so not bad for a Friday night! Food was excellent almost overwhelming being I only have one stomach and can't eat everything. But I got small amounts of most of the menu just to taste and what I had was delicious!!! Ambiance was romantic..... my husband and I will definitely come back well worth the wait and cost... absolutely love this place

Dined at The Bacchanal at Caesars for our anniversary. Thank you God for keeping us together and growing our family over the years. Have to ask for forgiveness too because temptation surrounded me and there was a lot of waste after my "take one bite of everything approach." We arrived early anticipating a long wait for this buffet on a holiday weekend. Enjoyed small talk with the fella in front of us who displayed his foodie knowledge by engaging us in a discussion of American vs. Japanese kobe beef and his insight on the "Jiro Dreams of Sushi" documentary. He built his food knowledge credibility with us as the line inched forward.  This guy asked us if we've been here before. We said no, and he then stated emphatically that this was the #1 buffet in the country. COUNTRY people. Wow, alrighty then. He told us not to waste time on filling up on bread and I responded that I don't do salads either at big buffets like this. Way too much good looking food that I can't resist piling on my plate.  You know how you leave a blackjack table or slot by saying "good luck" to your neighbor you've been sitting by, that's how I felt when we parted ways with this guy. Boy was he right on. The Bachannal is the  Best. Buffet. Ever.  It should be on your buffet bucket list! Come here hungry and look around first because there's too much to try! Presentation alone was tops! So many cute containers and individual serving dishes. If only I brought a big tote bag for some souvenirs, hahaha! They have the usual buffet food but some nice surprises: aguas frescas in mini carafes,  big pieces of chicharrones to munch on with your carnitas, machaca, and pozole, tonkatsu ramen, wagyu sliders, lobster rolls, deep fried pickles, surprisingly good Chinese dishes and dim sum along with the overwhelming carving and seafood section. Every animal on the farm is pretty much represented. For dessert you'll find black sesame and kona coffee MOCHI (and other flavors) in the gelato display with some really good macarons worthy of Chef Payard himself. Eric waited for this weekend to come and in the city of Lost Wages it was a big winner! We give it a our stamp of approval!

This is the BEST buffet to go to in Vegas. It is very pricey but I think it's worth every penny. If I'm going to spend money in Vegas, I would rather have it be on delicious food than on gambling. I've tried other buffets that are lower priced or that people have compared it to online, but this one is still my absolute favorite one. I've never had a bad experience and I always stuff myself mad.

If you try this place, be aware that there are very long lines and the wait times can be pressing. I am used to this, so I know what I'm getting myself into but if you aren't aware, this might sour things for you. My favorite times to go are during brunch or linner. By that, I mean it's best to go when they change out their menu so that you can try either both breakfast and lunch, or lunch and dinner. Some might wonder who stays that long for buffet but this is the city of sin and gluttony and this buffet go hand and hand. 

They have many different kind of stations that you can go to to try different food. A lot of buffets just offer American food but this buffet has more selections. There's a big seafood section that has king crab legs, shrimp, crabs, and many more! Next to that, they have the meat section which has everything from Canadian ham to brisket. Chicken, roast beef, ribs, etc. You name it! There are burger sliders and French fries. There's a station where someone can make you street style tacos. There is horchata and fresh fruit juices. I've even had nopales before. There are all kinds of pastas, salads, breads. There's an Asian food section which has had pho, ramen, sushi, pork buns, dumplings, taro desserts and more! Honestly the selection is impressive. Oh and there's a dessert station with macaroons, ice cream, cakes, gelato, etc! The food changes but the stuff I listed above are things I have all tried here. I've never been disappointed. Please show up on an empty stomach and be aware that you will have a food coma afterwards.

This was worth the $200 and 2 hour wait in line. One of my best culinary experiences. Thank you for genuinely depicting essentially every corner of the earth through culinary goodness. You can literally see, smell, and taste the culture through all of the offerings.

The management is confused to say the least.

We stayed at both the NOBU and Planet Hollywood this time for the new year (decent rooms, but the fireworks are underwhelming). Wanted to show my girlfriend the buffets experience in Vegas so I bought 2 tickets to the 24 Hour Buffet of Buffets for Dec 30 along with the room order, went to Bacchanal on Dec 30 and after 2 hours in line, we were told the passes cannot be redeemed and was shown an internal letter to employees to not "sell" buffet of buffets on Dec 30 after 3 pm.

Well, the piece of paper in my hand says "customer paid for one or more" buffet of buffets, so I called over a manager.

Manager requested to see email confirmation (glad internet works in Vegas), and upon seeing the confirmation manager pointed out to the cancellation clause at the bottom: "Management reserves all rights including the right to cancel or amend this offer at any time." Then told us that he'd make a one-time exception for us. Well, thank you sir!

Then somehow the computers won't accept the redemption code, so manager tried to fix this by putting the charges on the room instead and comping it, so that we don't get double charged from the original room order. So technically we were "comped" the 2nd charge of the passes, then charged 2 upgrade fees. Great, we lost some time but at least it's fair and we get to eat on Dec 30.

2nd day, went in line again in the afternoon. After 2 hours in line we were told that NO UPGRADE ALLOWED on New Year's Eve. Excuse me? This is not what the giant poster before the line says. After the considering the disappointment experience and quality of the food from day 1 we simply walked away. 

It was interesting in a sadistic way, and the food is definitely not worth the wait anymore in 2019 even on a non-holiday. Many better options elsewhere.

Back from the trip, I'm seeing 2 charges of about $260 for the buffet visit for 2, not counting the original payment back before the trip. Time to waste more time on getting this resolved.

Would stay away from Caesars Entertainment for personal or business trips from now on.

This place came to me highly rated from a Vegas local, and although I can put away a large amount of food, I wanted to limit myself to only one buffet this trip to Vegas. I balked at the price of Bacchanal since it's about 20% more expensive than other buffets on the strip. However, after eating there a few days ago, I would only give it a 3.5. The food was good, but was it $50 good? That is debatable.

With the cost, I aimed for the meat cuts. My cut of American Wagyu was sadly a little too over-cooked (well-done) for my liking. My first cut of prime rib was delicious (medium to medium rare), but for my second helping, it was too rare for my liking, to borderline raw given how difficult it was to cut. I ended up not finishing the second helping to reduce my risk of gastroenteritis. I also got the beef brisket which reliably good, but needed BBQ sauce and salt. I actually liberally salted all my meats. 

I also got the seafood dishes here. Mussels and crab legs were delicious and on point. I didn't get the other seafood but there was lots of shrimp. Sushi and poke was in the Asian food section and better than the grocery store, but nothing amazing.

There was also a ton of Chinese food, including soup dumplings. I decided not to get any since I'm really picky about Chinese food, and also know I can make my own food or ask my mom to make the food I like.

There was also an impressive selection in the Italian section including some fancy looking pizza that I decided to pass on to get more meat and seafood. I did get some cheeses, nuts, and cured meat though.

I was quite pleased with the dessert bar, in particular, the gelato. There were many options and I got the sesame gelato and the lemon basil sorbet. I have to say the lemon basil sorbet was an excellent way to finish my meal. I also got egg tarts (really flaky!), creme brulee, a freshly made crepe, and a macaron. I would pass on the macaron. The crepe was fair (I think it probably depends on who is making it), and pretty big, so this is one that is probably better to split so you don't get full too fast. 

As for drinks, alcoholic beverages are extra, so I just had water and horchata. Service is good. They also limit you to 2 hours, but not sure how strict they are on that. I was only there for about 1.5 hours. 

Overall, I think this place is good but I'm just not sure if it's worth the price, because I can only eat so much.

My favorite buffet when I come to Vegas. So many options and everything is cooked well. The brunch option on Sunday is my preferred time. It's pricy, so come really, really hungry to get your moneys worth but enjoy getting to try such a wide variety of foods.

Tips: If you're a platinum card holder your wait time is very short. If you're a diamond or 7 star there is no wait time really. 
Best time to get there is 2 pm. They add the dinner items at 3 pm so you get brunch items and dinner too. 
If you're doing all you can drink for 15 dollars extra, ask to be seated in the area that are being serviced by Jeffrey or Santiago, these gentlemen will not let your glass be empty and will take care of whatever you need. 
They absolutely rock! 
When you're ready for dessert see Mr. Delmar at the crepe station in dessert area, he's whipping out fresh delicious crepes in literally about 2 minutes! Mr. Delmar is awesome! 
Check into your Yelp and get that free champagne! 
 
We went to the buffet around 2:30 on Friday, we wanted to be extra hungry so we could sample as many dishes as we could. For 2 lunch buffets and my bottomless mimosas or all I could drink beer it came up to $130 for two of us. The wait for us to be seated was less than 10 minutes. We had a platinum players card. We were sat right in front of the meat station! I waited for about 10 minutes and the person that's suppose to take my drink order didn't show up. I'm used to Reno, Nv. Peppermill service where the drink person is at my table within 5 minutes of me being sat down by the host. I was disappointed because when you order bottomless mimosas you want those coming in as quickly as possible to enjoy your meal. Not only that but as I start to take in food, any liquid would be nice! When I came back 7 min later a waitress came to see what we wanted to drink and I explained to her the importance of having a drink with my meal to which her response was, "I waited for you and you weren't here. You left". Didn't take her name down and it doesn't matter anyway because not even 5 min after than convo took place, there was a shift change and I got Mr. Jeffrey as my waiter! Score!!! I can't even say enough wonderful things about Mr. Jeffrey. He's got an amazing personality and he's one of those long time employees who just loves his job. I told him about my experience with the previous person and he promised me he would not my glass of champagne run empty. Promise was kept. This man is full of energy and good vibes! 

The Bacchanal Buffet has everything your little heart desires plus a bit more. I had heard about this buffet and always wanted to come here. It definitely lives up to the hype.I was just happy and content to have Wagyu beef, whole roasted pig and fried bananas at Mexican/Cuban station , made to order hot miso and noodle soups at Asian food station, lobster claws and escargot at seafood station, freshly made crepes at dessert station. They have many many more items, I'm just listing the food I was surprised to find here. 

I loved this place so much that I went back on Sunday. We asked to be seated in Jeffrey's section because we wanted everything to go without flaw. Unfortunately it was his day off but the host agreed that Mr. Jeffrey is one of a kind employee and hard to substitute but that she had another wonderful person working there that day and she'd seat us in his section. We got seated with Mr. Santiago who was amazing too! Another knowledgeable, quick, polite, and hard working staff member. I was very happy with my over all experience here and I will continue to be back due to these 3 empoyees.

The place is amazing and the line is very very long. We waited for 40+ mins at 1:20pm, considering this is not the lunch hour. We loved the food and the long wait made us hungrier.

We will go this summer again.

Best buffet in Las Vegas? If I was going to pay $51.99 for dinner, then it better be!

We checked in at a kiosk when we arrived. At the kiosk, you enter the number of people in your party and a phone number. It tells you the estimated time it'll take to get a table and you'll receive a text informing you when to return rather than staying in line the whole time. After some hassle I'd rather not get into, we finally got seated. The interior was decorated nicely and is divided into three dining rooms- glass, wood, and steel. 

All of us headed to the seafood section first. It had shrimp, oysters, and most importantly snow crab legs. I loved how they were cut down the middle lengthwise. It made it easy to pick the meat out. If not, I wouldn't have bothered eating crab- too much work. They have heated snow crab in the Italian section as well.

There were a variety of stations besides seafood including: Chinese, Japanese, American, Italian, Mexican, meat carving, charcuterie and cheese, etc.  A few of those stations were located in the back room. There is a whole separate section devoted to desserts too. The desserts were hit or miss. I loved the green tea crème brulee, while I didn't like the texture of the overly sweet macarons. There are made-to order crepes too. 

I didn't try everything I wanted to. I should've mapped out a better strategy. In the end, I felt like I could've eaten much more than I did. I was full, but not $51.99 full.

Came here for brunch on a Sunday morning. No lines or wait time around 9 am. Definitely does get packed after 10 though. They have kiosks so you can put your name on the wait list and they'll text you when it's your turn which is nice. 

The staff was very professional and friendly and visited frequently. The ambiance and decor was aesthetically pleasant because it wasn't glaringly bright and very relaxing.

My favorite part of the buffet were the fresh juices. There was orange, watermelon, and cucumber basil. They also had more drinks from the drink menu and brunch came with two free alcoholic drinks which most people chose champagne or mimosas.

Because it was brunch, there were a lot of breakfast items like yogurts, smoothies, pastries, eggs, bacon and sausages, pancakes, and waffles. (I definitely have to go back to try their lunch/dinner menu.) The other deviation from breakfast were some pastas, Mexican dishes, pizzas, a small selection of dumplings and Asian cuisine like sushi rolls and and noodles. And a very tiny salad bar.

Their gelato was decent but I wasn't too sure about their pudding. 

Overall, a decent buffet but it's definitely not something you should go out of your way for when Vegas has so much other great food. Unless you only want to eat buffets...

My friends and I come to the Bacchanal every time we're in Vegas. It's something you have to experience once while in you're in town! They have literally everything you can think of. The reason for 4/5 is because of the sea food. Sea food is my NUMBER ONE favorite type of food. It's just not the best sea food I've ever had. But what can you expect from somewhere that's busting out 20 pounds of crab legs an hour. The price is pretty high (around 70ish) but honestly worth it. My good friend is vegan and never has a hard time finding something to eat there. You can also check out Groupon and find some 2 for 1 deals or something like that. The pasta dishes are honestly my favorite next to the desserts!!! The lemon basil sorbet is literally to DIE for. Like I want it served at my wedding. Lol.

Still my favorite buffet in Vegas!  

-Hot snow crab legs
-Freshly opened oysters
-rock crab claws

Repeat.

-Ribs
-Prime Rib

Repeat.

I already miss it.

FINALLY, Caesars is getting its act together! It has always been my #1 favorite hotel in Vegas, but the truth was it was getting pretty dumpy...and basically coasting on its legendary name. Thankfully, hotel brass is now on a mission to make Caesars a 5-star resort, which includes revamping customer service, renovating rooms, and replacing the SAD, nasty-ass old buffet with this fabulous masterpiece!

The name hearkens back to Caesars' old Bacchanal restaurant, the legendary scene of many a debauched meal partaken by fat plutocrats reclined on pillows, Wine Goddesses pouring the finest booze down their gullets. This being 2012, they toned down the excess just a TAD...so no more pillows, and no more Wine Goddesses...but in every other respect, this place is a true bacchanal! All that's missing is a vomitorium -- for now, you'll have to make do with discreetly puking into the potted plants.

You'll most definitely want to puke when visiting this buffet -- there's SO MUCH EXCELLENT FOOD, there's no way you can try everything without doing so. The chefs behind the Bacchanal visited every single buffet in Vegas (EVERY SINGLE ONE...even the crappy Arizona Charlie's ones, LOL) to suss out the competition...and then they proceeded to design a buffet that kicks every other buffet in town's ass -- hands down!! Even the vaunted M Resort Buffet!!! 

First off, beer and wine are included with dinner -- and whatever wine they pour is pretty damn good, so drink up! The selection of food is GREAT -- a fantastic sushi/sashimi spread, dim sum, tons of Asian salads and oddities. Plenty of glistening roasted animals hanging on hooks, waiting to be sliced up and gobbled down by salivating patrons. Fantastic salad bar, with fancy hi-class accouterments. FABULOUS charcuterie, with stinky cheeses and a variety of cured meats and dried fruits. Artisanal honey straight from a proudly displayed honeycomb -- with different spices, like star anise and vanilla bean, added to the various jars (the honey pairs GREAT with the Stilton bleu cheese). Hand-made tortillas at the Mexican station...individual baked lasagnas and zitis at the Italian station...a GINORMOUS seafood selection with every sort of shellfish imaginable, and a fine spread of greasy, lard-assed "comfort food" for the Amurricans in the house. My only complaint is that their middle Eastern selection is limited to hummus, tabbouleh, couscous and dolmades...and there is no Indian selection. But seriously, I couldn't fit any more anyway, so I forgive them! Oh, and the desserts are fabulous and WAY more varied than at other buffets -- it was like Willy Wonka's Chocolate Factory! I'd never tried a REAL marshmallow before...and I'm here to tell you, THEY ARE DELICIOUS! 

The decor is clean and modern, with lots of classy food-as-art design flourishes. The background music is modern and the perfect tempo for eating -- fast enough to keep you pushing on through your miserable fullness, yet mellow enough to allow for a relaxed feeling.

There is a large private dining room in the back, perfect for wedding receptions or private high-roller parties -- in fact, the room includes an 80" TV and will soon feature a karaoke system for those krazy hi-rolling Asian parties! I can't *WAIT* to get invited to (or crash) one of THOSE!!!

Ugh, I can't write about this anymore because I am still reeling from my visit, and just threw up a little in my mouth. But take it from me -- this is a GREAT buffet!!! Its fabulous vibe of excess and decadence fit in perfectly with the whole Roman Empire shtick at Caesars...so if you really want to experience the glory and bounty of America, head here at once. You won't regret it!

This buffet is worth a try when visiting Vegas. It can be more than an hour wait though, so be prepared to go and put your name in, leave to pass the time until they contact you, and then go back to stand in line for nearly an hour to pay and be seated. But like I said, to try this buffet at least once is worth it.

There are so many options including: seafood (hot and cold), Mexican, American, pizza and Italian, Asian, and probably more that I cant remember. The desserts are enough to fill a dinner plate themselves. Some items I really enjoyed: steamed pork buns, pizza, pasta, a pho bar, shrimp Lo mein, brisket, sweet potato tots, Mac and cheese, nachos, red velvet brownies, and creme brûlée. 

The service was kind! And be kind to your waiter/waitress and any other workers you see there, they seemed tired and under-appreciated.

Hmm, overall I rate this buffet as the 3rd best on the Strip.  First being Bellagio, Cosmo second, and Wynn 4th.

Me and my buddies arrived at about 8pm and were in line for an hour.  We even paid the extra $15 for their express line.  So damage was $65 each.

It is a good buffet because it has 7 different stations with each station catering to different palates.  These stood out for me.  You could get the crab warmed up.  A rep is there ready to take your empty plate and quickly cover it with warmed crab legs.  I think it was snow crab and not king crab although I like both.  I really liked their roast duck in the Asian station.  It wasn't dry as my friends had feared.  The best item at the buffet was clearly the steak--very flavorful!  Better than the 6 month dry aged steak I had at Carnevino the following night.

I liked this buffet, but all things considered and with the extensive wait time and better buffets on the Strip, I probably won't schedule another visit here.  Would only come here if it were a consensus within my group....

Excellent buffet, extremely high quality meats & overall selection. Went on a Friday night, had bone marrow that was incredible. Wagyu beef was amazing, lamb t-bone, bacon slab--over 500 items on buffet! The only complaint was very limited selection of sushi, and what was there was not good at all. Otherwise, very enjoyable experience. It's pricey, but arguably the best buffet in Vegas.

Make a reservation for VIP treatment through Open Table and skip the lines! This buffet is great. The food is fresh. Our server, Patty, was so helpful and attentive. We were greeted with bottomless mimosas and a seafood tower. Yum!!!

IF HEAVEN WAS A RESTAURANT, IT WOULD BE THIS BUFFET. 

As someone who absolutely detests going to buffets, this is easily one of the best restaurants I've ever been to and definitely in my favorite fine dining establishments.

I visited the buffet around the Christmas holidays / new year holidays so to say that I had an insane waiting experience is an understatement but Lord help me, the wait was absolutely worth it. Some tips for anyone is visiting here for the first time, during peak hours they segregate the queue into 3(?) groups by the size of your party. With a party of 13 people, we were definitely one of the larger parties and were split from the rest. 

Let's start with the genre of food: everything. You might be skeptical because of the price point, but where normal buffets tend to add easy to prep dishes for convenience, The Bacchanal generously prepares every single dish with both quality and patience to ensure that whatever you put on your plate is the best this place has to offer. The buffet is divided into different areas of the world and awesome cuisine of that region: oysters from the United States, Fish tacoes for Mexico, Lobster from Maine, sushi from Japan, carbonara from Italy, the list can go on and on. To write each single dish would be absolutely insane, but my favorites were hands down the oysters, sushi and fish tacoes. 

Their food and quality were only out done by their exceptional wait staff. Not only were they the salt of the earth, but they were quick to clear our plates, take our orders and answer any questions while attending to the much busy holiday packed tables that i'm sure they had.

If you want one of the best dining experiences ever, please come here.

This place is AMAZING if you love: seafood, beef, pork, and desserts. If you like vegetarian or chicken, then it is NOT worth the $65 price per person. If you're a vegetarian then you will have salad and roasted veggies. If you like poultry only then you'll have tacos and maybe one more dish. That's about it. Dessert section is awesome. A lot of beef, pork, and seafood options!

Would have been 5 stars except for the two screaming kids sitting next to us  whose parents did nothing to control.  The food selection and quality was outstanding as was the service. A bit pricey but excellent non the less.
Soccoro M was our server and she is great! Not only was the food awesome, the service was amazing and we didn't have to wait for anything.  Only downfall was not enough room to eat everything

Came the day after thanksgiving for Brunch. Place was packed but still enjoyed the whole experience! That's what it is, an experience! The price is high but see this place as a Las Vegas "attraction". You wont eat for another 24 hours after haha. 

Pace yourselves, stay the whole 2 hours like my fam did. Strategize! All this may sound insane for a buffet, but again, this ain't just an "expensive" buffet. Its a fancy-ish , "GLAMOROUS" food extravaganza.

Bacchanalia, a festival of merriment and libations, a riotous tribute to Bacchus, the god of wine and ecstasy. Intoxicated revelry, drunken orgies...the Romans had it good.

Contemporary visitors to Caesar's Palace aren't so lucky. They must queue up before indulging at the Bacchanal Buffet by checking in at the self-service kiosks. A piece of parchment with a wait time will be dispensed. 

At 3 in the afternoon on a Sunday, our wait was CLVI minutes. That's fancy for 156 minutes, which is, in other words, 2 hours and 36 minutes. Within an hour and a half, however, they delivered a message that our turn was up, at which point we were allowed 15 minutes to come claim our spot.

The price for dinner was LVIII dollars and some change. You're better off not deciphering that. For those who put in the effort to understand it, you'll probably want to know, was it worth it?

If you just want to load up on typical buffet foods like crab legs and prime rib, you can be satisfied somewhere else and pay less. The draw of Bacchanal is their dishes, prepared with the attention you may find at a fine-dining restaurant.

Many of their selections come tapas-style, on a tiny plate or miniature pan that you take with you to your table. They even provide silicon finger tabs so you don't burn yourself as you grab. The seabass on wasabi mashed potatoes was outstanding as well as the shrimp on grits. 

As for seafood, crab legs were available hot or cold and cross-sectioned for easy extraction. Raw oysters were offered but only half-shucked, and they weren't that meaty. 

Dessert items were hit or miss, but the chocolate-filled beignets were exceptional, and the chocolate macarons were on par with the ones from a nice bakery.

Although the price and wait time may make the gods gasp in dismay and tumble out of Mt. Olympus, the quality preparations would satisfy the pickiest of the pantheon. The god of wine continues to inspire cult-ish gatherings, this time in the name of refined gluttony.

This place is really fun.We used groupon and got a free champagne.Any non alcoholic drink is included.Variety of food plus and my number one favorite food,king crab legs.Dessert were amazing as well.
I had a great experience here.

Buffets are a Las Vegas staple so I had to see what the hype was all about. My group and I decided on Bacchanal because it seemed to be a good deal for dinner and we've heard good things about if from friends. 

In our group of 6, we were able to find a Groupon for ~$50 for dinner with a free drink. We went around 4:30pm on a Tuesday and only had to wait for about 5 minutes to be seated. However, when I went up for my second round, a little after 5, I saw that the line had increased by a lot. 

Our waitress was very engaging and always made sure that we were doing well. 

There was a variety of food, which made it difficult for my indecisive self and limited stomach space. I chose to stay away from Asian food as I knew that it would not compare to the traditional foods that I've grown up with. 

Foods that stood out to me:
- KING GRAB LEGS (chef piles it onto your plate & really gets your $ worth)
- scallops 
- truffle pizza 
- tri-tip
- white chocolate covered strawberries
- gelato 

Foods that were a little disappointing:
- lamb t-bone (dry)
- green tomato sliders
- majority of the meat section 
- oysters 
- stone crab claws (grainy texture)

My 1st visit on 4/26/19.

I thought the food at Bacchanal was mediocre for the most part. But over-rated and over-priced. ($65 per person just for dinner is really overdoing it IMO)

Came with my immediate family (5 people). We had to follow another group of people in order for the server to show us our table. (which was nearby)

The buffet line goes in a zigzag. It starts with the Asian food (mostly Chinese with a few Korean staples such as Jap Chae and Beef Short Ribs) and ends at the King Crab/Lobster area. (near the register area where you pay). There is a separate counter for Desserts & Gelato which is away from the main buffet.

Although there is a lot of food not everything tastes exceptional. I'll rank it down from Tasty to mediocre to not tasty. Tasty: Salmon with Green Sauce, Pozole, Pho, Fried Green Tomato Sliders, Paella. Mediocre: Pizzas, Mac n Cheese, Tonkotsu Ramen. Not Tasty: Crab Legs, Beef Sliders

There were more types of food I've tried too but don't remember what it's called.

I'm probably not likely to return again at least not at that price point. I'll try another buffet.

Yes the seafood is good here but realistically for the price you're paying, it's just an ok buffet. We had a rude server that didn't even bother looking at us. I went here because people say it's a good buffet but honestly the service just killed the mood. I looked around and my table wasn't the only receiving this crappy service from our server. 

Thankfully the nice manager was super sweet and helped us. That was the only great part.

I had to take a second and thank my server Milka. Servers aren't usually the stars in places like this so I wanted to make sure I took time to shout her out. She was the sweetest most attentive server I've had in a long time. If you're lucky enough to be sat in her section you will see what I'm talking about. My dinning experience was perfect because of her! Thanks Milka for making my birthday even better! 

PS: Cesar I sure hope y'all take care of these servers! They are the unsung heroes of this establishment.

PSS: I believe Milka can read the customer mind. She knew I wanted a cup of coffee after my meal before I could ask. Honestly that is a gift that has been lost since the 60s. Y'all I can't keep saying great things about her.

We had the buffet on 9/17/19 for lunch. Weekday price for 24 hour buffet is $59.99 and Bacchanal has a $25 upcharge. Food is good but not sure it's worth the price. They do have a wide selection of foods from desserts to meats... if u haven't tried it probably worth going to form your own opinion. However, if you're not buffet trained recommend going to a good restaurant not necessarily buffet and better deal. I've been to this buffet probably three times in the past 2 years and this last time somehow there wasn't a wow factor. Don't recommend the 24 hour buffet, the restaurant selections are lot less than past and quality has dropped. Foodie out

My husband and I went there for thanks giving dinner. The wait was around 3,5 hours long but as soon we where seated  we got treated with the best and delicious foods from all over the world and the dessert variety was insane! 
Definitely would recommend it. But come early to stand in line

This is probably the number one voted buffet on the Las Vegas strip. It's pricey but excellent. It's $65 per person. There's tons of seafood, American food, also Chinese food. You have chilled shrimp and crab legs. They also have steamed snow crab legs that's already split and ready for you to enjoy. 
The ice cream is real fruit sorbet which is my favorite! I had the banana mango sorbet. We need an ice cream shop like this in Michigan. The wait time to get in wasn't too bad, we were only in line for about 5 minutes and once you get to the front to pay, there's someone there to take your picture. The camera man will find you while you're eating and hand you your photo for you to view and then if you really like it, it's only $25.  If you're going to go to a buffet and spend around $35, which is about the average price for a buffet on the strip, then I suggest to come here for an additional $30 and get a whole lot more and having an excellent variety of food.

The seafood was disappointing.  Other meat items were alright. Dessert was really good. Service was ok. There was no line when we arrived around 10:30am. I don't think it is worth $60 per person to be honest.

Food was great and like the service they provided. 
But waiting was too long. Only reason I waited almost 3 hours to eat at this place is for sea food buffet my wife wanted. 

FYI
Caesars Palace Casino valet parking is now $7 or you need to be some sort of member with 7 stars or diamonds to get anything free. Oh, yes!! there is advantage of being 7 stars or diamonds for not waiting on the line at the buffet as well.

Gary W. Loveman
Caesars Investor Relations
One Caesars Palace Drive
Las Vegas, NV 89109

RE: Bacchanal--11/10/12


Dear Gary--

My son turned 21 on November 9th so we traveled to Vegas and had a very nice experience for the weekend.  On Friday night, we were quite entertained at Pure.  That place is phenomenal--great music, great venue and tremendous energy.  For his birthday, Pure was the real deal.

On Saturday morning, we researched and found that the Bacchanal was the best rated buffet in Vegas so we decided to try and recover from the night before with a good meal.  Your buffet was exceptional in every way.  We particularly liked the Bacchanal Benedict--a very nice twist.  Our server Lilly was also tremendous.  Our group never wanted for service, the mimosas were filled very quickly and the experience overall was a home run.  We liked it so much, we considered returning for dinner and inquired about the Buffet of Buffet's.  Lilly explained the program to us and we were ready to sign up.  On the way out, we grabbed great cookies with the fudge layer.

At the desk on the way out, we presented our ticket to do the upgrade to BOB.  The hostess said it didn't work that way.  We said, all we want to do is give you money and buy dinner for tonight.  She got the supervisor over who sadly was a troll.  We explained that we liked the buffet and wanted to return.  The supervisor told us that this was not possible and we could not buy the BOB in no uncertain terms.  So much so, that we were quite offended.  Clearly, we weren't looking for a deal, we were looking for resolution--that was not possible and we left.

I stopped at what looked like a management area and talked to a lady who took my number and said somebody from management would call me.  She said I would be better going to the registration area and speaking to a manager.  So I ambled over there-yes, I was pretty frustrated.  So I talked to Joel who was helping direct people to check in.  He told me that only the ICU manager was working and that Marcus the Food/Beverage General Manager who recently was some other manager would be the person to speak with.  I left my number for Marcus and asked for a call.

So in essence, I requested a call from two different people about the treatment at the Baccanal with my guests and son.  You have a good thing going at your establishment at Caesors.  We travel to Vegas 1-2 times a year and enjoy the get away from our home in Tucson.  You are only as good as your weakest link.  I'm not sure what's more disappointing, the supervisor at the Bacchanal or the fact that no member of management followed up on my concerns.  Remember one thing; I tried to give you more of my money--not sure I'll try next time.

Sincerely,
This is the best buffet in Las Vegas . Worth the price !!! & Excellent service our waiter Nancy and Omar were so nice to my family and I.

One of the better buffet in vegas (and all the buffets are pretty legit!) and wouldn't mind coming back. I did not have a huge line to worry about and got in with 10 mins from arriving as I was on the early dinner plan (around 4:45pm). Definitely recommended trying to come early to beat the rush, when I left the line was backed up for days. 

During my 2 hour stay there, they switched up the food offerings over time but was unable to keep up with all the delicious being presented... Keeping the options fresh.

The seafood options were the bomb and have many sauces to choose from ( i just went with the hot butter, cuz you can't go wrong with hot butter). The soup options were ok, but pairing them with the parmesan crips was money!! The meat, such as the prime ribs and wagyu were pretty chewing and I was unable to finish those. 

Getting carb items in a buffet usually isn't the best plan, but their mac & cheese and mashed potato were on point that I didn't feel guilty for getting 2nds on those items. 

Their backroom had asian food, which was aite and definitely was satisfied by it. Also, there are cheese and crackers in the back, which did not look too appetizing, had to make a hard pass on those. They did have this watermelon juice which was on another level, I probably had 4-5 cups worth myself. 
 
Overall, the buffet is so large and the options are so many that it is hard to not be satisfied with something.

One of my top buffets in Vegas! 

I've heard so many good reviews about this buffet and I was finally able to give this place a try. I went in on a Friday morning for breakfast around 8-830 and there was no wait and was not busy at all. I also purchased this buffet through Groupon that had a deal of 2 for $88 and two mimosas were included in this deal. I think it's worth it especially because of the mimosas.

They have a great selection of food and you're even able to order some food off the grill. They had a variety of different foods such as Mexican food, oriental food, and American food. My favorite dish was probably the chicken and waffles. The portion looks small but it's definitely filling and the chicken is super crunchy! 

If you're looking for a good buffet to visit, this is one buffet you need to try. Great selection and lots of seating.

First time here but it really wasn't great...if M Buffet's crab leg quality was more consistently good, then I'd rather go to M buffet. Prob on par with Bellagio in the fact that choices are vast but quality is lacking....especially for the price!  $60 is not bad but I'd rather go to Sterling buffet for $85/person
Restaurant environment is ok. But the food definitely don't worth 65 bucks. Maybe $35~ won't come again.

By recommendation, I ate here on Friday 11/15/19 after first going to the Rio and finding out that they no longer have a seafood buffet. After waiting in line for an hour and having my heart set on crab legs, I was extremely disappointed with quality and flavor of the crab legs especially for a buffet that cost almost $70 per person. Some crab legs were mushy (overcooked) and others just tasted poorly. I have contacted management and was told that they don't issue refunds and the best they could do is offer half off a future buffet if I would submit my complaint via email. I have not received a reply and have tried leaving a voicemail, but have not heard anything back and have already returned home from my vacation. Based on other reviews, it seems to be their policy that refunds are never issued and it is the standard to offer half off the buffet. If I don't hear anything, I will consider disputing the credit card charge since they have not reached out to handle my complaint.

This buffet is now on my "been there, done that" list in Vegas. It's pricey, the selection and quality make up for it, but for that price I would want to try something else next time. And you really need to be a big eater to feel you get your money worth.

Buffets are all the same, right?  Well not this one.  It's concept is similar to that other one that serves everything in individual plates and bowls, but this one doesn't go that far.  Only certain items are individual servings.

First, standing in the line, we're it and it's 6:55 am, no one is here but us, we are eying the crab legs, piled high, and right next too it a huge pile of shrimp.  Our mouth's are watering before we even get a chance to taste anything.

We're given a brief walk through, then taken to our table.  I take advantage of the complimentary mimosa and we're up and loading our plates with the most wonderful delights.  Each station, the staff are friendly and acknowledge us when we approach.  The displays are both full of color, smell and arranged to attract.

I made so many trips back and forth, I must have worked off most of the calories, right?  This is one of the best buffets in town. Worth the extra bucks and definitely worth a revisit.

I loveeeeeeeeeeeeeeeee this place, of all buffets in Vegas (Yes that was my goal in going to Vegas every time....to find the best buffet haha). Best is if you have dinner here, but it gets very busy and it is pricier (about 50pp) but that's comparable with other hotel buffets. They have kiosks up front for you to schedule your reservation, kind of like a obtaining a fast pass at Disneyland LOL. You return with your party at the provided time on your ticket, get in the line for ticketholders and pay up front, then you are seated. The buffet includes a variety of different foods including dim sum and real Chinese food like roasted ducketc, and Mexican food, American food...There is a lot of seafood to be had. If you go to the far right side of the buffet there is a spot where you stand in line and they will give you a plate of steamed snow crab legs (yes endless snow crab legs) with melted butter on the side YUMMMMM. There is a center area that has all the desserts including freshly prepared for you crepes, gelato or ice cream, macaroons, cookies, usually chocolate covered strawberries (they did not have them on this go around). Everything is delish, This is a must try, and for me a must return! =)

Food was ok. Unfortunately the service is we're it's lacking. We paid for the unlimited drinks, which we only received 2 because our waiter was hard to find. Our plates kept stacking up but he would not come and clear them out. We ended up having to flag another waiter to come help us out instead. We spent good money and sadly, we didn't even get to enjoy ourselves. What a shame. We left a tip but that's because we are good people.

My partner and I will not be returning and spending our money in this buffet.

Every person that patronizes this institution should be required to enroll in DARE after  the meal. Except unlike 6th grade, it's not about drug abuse this time. It's Diners Against Rage-ful Eating. 

I went with a few girlfriends to celebrate a pal's pregnancy and although only one of the five of us was with child going into Bacchanal, somehow all five of us left pregnant, the last four of us with food babies. How did this happen!?

Well. I'll tell you what happened. Caesars went and renovated their buffet and pulled themselves up from zero to hero with their multi-million dollar remodel. Suddenly they are boasting 500 items - 500 items OF QUALITY, I should add. There are stations for salad, carving, seafood (you can request for your crab legs to be steamed!), Asian, Italian, American, etc. Be smart and strategize - take a mini tour of what's available so you can mentally prep your stomach accordingly. People, it's all about the pacing. 

The service is impeccable and each employee tries to make conversation with as many guests they are in contact with, so you don't feel like you're just having prime rib slapped on your plate from the cafeteria lady. 

The price tag can initially give you some sticker shock but remember: with this buffet, you're paying for both quality and quantity, not one or the other. Happy noshing!

This is an amazing buffet.  The stations are fully staffed and constantly replenished.  There is not a long wait inside for the higher-end foods.  There were about 6 or 7 different styles of food from Latin based, Asian and southern.  The brisk was outstanding and any choice on non-alcoholic drinks from fruit juice to Arnold Palmer included.  The desert options ranged from small pieces of delightful pies to handmade ice cream.  We ate for the entire 2 hour limit that we were there.     

I am one that will 9/10 times say no I will not go to a buffet.  I do not like little hands touching near my food.  This buffet is setup where a lot of things to grab are individual.  

If you are a diamond rewards member from Total Rewards, it is the best way to go.  There is no wait in line and you get great seating and service.  

Can't wait to go next time!

My partner was so excited to try this place out!!!!!! 
However, i had low expeciations to start with and now even lower after eating here.

He was so hyped up that he bought the VIP package; so we can move pass the first line and get a complementary champagne [THAT WE NEVER GOT!!].

Food and Presentation - Basic AF; nothing jumped out. The placement of ethnic/oriental food category didn't make since.
 
Chinese Food - Very small selection located way in the back corner of the buffet. I mean, I'd place it their too when Panda Express is better quality and the better option. 
Mexican - Pretty much the only decent thing to eat here compared to the rest, in my opinion. They give you enough sause option to help make make things taste better.
Japanese - Your basic California Sushi Roll selection.
Italian - I'm not a fan of sour tomato sause. Can't taste anything but sour tamato.
Meatssss - Looking back at it now; Where is the BBQ pit? Where is the smoke room? How are they able to pump these out so quick? Oh the magic of liquid smoke, steam and a quick char in the broiler. Look at the crust line on all the meat selection its thinner then Donlad Trumps lies.

Service
Slow, rude and racist.
They like to pair up same races in the same room.
White people with whites/Black with blacks/Asian with asain
Unless an area gets too packed then there is spill overs.

Ambiance
Dimm down the lights all you want, Bacchanal. 
But i can still see that your just a mediocre cafeteria.

My partner left very sad and this bothered him, on our stay in LV; The whole damn time... 
And i still can shut him up, and its getting irritating.

Places i'd compare this pace with.
Only because your better off saving money for the same quality, better and faster waiter service, PLUS they are super nice their.

THE MIRAGE

I'm impressed by the manager's follow up. I was sick for a week after visiting here but the manager had asked me questions to improve their restaurant. I will update my review again next time I visit Bacchanal
I dont know what happened but I got very sick after visiting this buffet on May 28, 2019. I'm not sure if this was incidental but it was very unpleasant. Food was good though.

We got here around 1p on a Thursday. We got a Groupon for 2 lunch buffets, with 2 mimosas/beers and VIP passes. Well first of all when you get there you can fall into one of two lines to get to the cashier. I can't remember how they were marked but it wasn't clear to us that we needed to go to the express line since we had the VIP pass. So about 10minutes of waiting we get to the cashier and ask about the VIP pass and she said "it let's you get into the express line. But you're here. Sorry." Well damn. At least we only had to wait 10 minutes to find that out.

Then you fall into another line based on how big your party is. We waited about 20 minutes.

The options are endless. Seafood, American, Italian, Asian, huge dessert section with gelato. There were some misses but overall the food was really good!

One thing that bugged me was that our waiter said our only alcoholic beverage option for our Groupon was a mimosa (not beer) when it clearly said mimosas or draft beers. Oh well!

We've tried many of the buffets in Las Vegas and we enjoy this one the best.  They have a variety of Japanese, Chinese, Mexican, Seafood, traditional fare along with fresh squeezed juices and a yummy dessert island.  The food is good but the lines to get in are loooonnnngggg!  If you like buffets, this is a great one to try!

We didn't even made it to the buffet. I called several days in advance to "make a reservation" for Sunday brunch for august 25th. The lady on the phone said there were  no reservations required for sunday brunch,she just "just show up" , this is after I told her the DATE we were planning to go. We walk a half a mile under 90 some degree weather on sunday, we are so excited to try it out since our favorite brunch, the Sterling brunch, was sold out, (and we knew because they had the courtesy to tell me over the phone). We get to the Bacchalan buffet only for them to turn us away because they were having private event and no one else was allowed to come in. Just WOW! I told the woman who was turning people away "I called to make reservations for TODAY and they never mentioned that you guys were having a private event" do you want to know her response? "I'm sorry"  wow, the nerve! Like if saying sorry will give us a better impression on this place. Seems like the service in vegas really lacks manners and consideration for guests, such as La Salsa restaurant inside planet hollywood, where they'll send a over glorified hostess to kick patrons out without reason. If it wasn't because the Sterling brunch was having also a private event, we'd go there.. Sterling brunch is A LOT MUCH BETTER.

Best buffet I ever had. So much different food I doubt you can try everything there. I eat all the seafood and eat first. And if you still can eat (which I highly doubt it) you can try other stuff. And there is a million type of desert too!

I want to start with the Great Service we were provided by our server Sandra Williams.  Thank You. 

The service upon check- in a whole different story. 

We were in line to pay and had Vicki helping us.  We have 3 people in our party with Standing limitations and All 3 of us have handicap IDs from DMV validating that.  Vicky got very short with my Mother in-law and said "I know my job mama".
