Way to familiar with the "mama" because she was visibly irritated.   

The food was pretty Good - although for $65 + $15 for 2 types of beer and 2 types of wine( Red & White) $80 way way too much to sit in these filthy chairs. 


Sad to say we will not come back.
No lines! Glad we came early after the gift wrap up! This time I tried more Asian food and seafood... Also enjoyed the mimosas

DECEIVING, but in a good way? We had a party of 5 and when we asked for the wait time while paying, they told us it would be about 2 hours... When we got to the line, for parties larger than 4, we only waited around 20 minutes and got in. I think they do this so some impatient customers would pay an extra $50-ish to cut the lines and get in faster. 
For the price of $70 per adult, the food was not worth it. 
Boiled King Crab Legs (2/5): The crab legs were REALLY salty. It was really hard to eat more than 3 legs, let alone an entire plate.
Chilled Crab Legs (4/5): The chilled crab legs were a little better than the boiled. 
Carving Station: The carving station was really good where you get to pick prime rib, brisket, pork belly, and tri-tip. The only concern with the carving station is that when you ask for medium-rare or medium, they sometimes give you cuts that are overcooked and it is really hard to eat all of it. 
Dessert Bar: The lines for the gelato were super long. It took around 10 minutes of waiting just to get gelato, but the gelato was really good and they give you as many flavours as you want. All of the other desserts were really good, especially the creme brulee and chocolate lava cake. 
All of the other food items were pretty good but nothing that is really unique or so good that it warrants a price point of $70. I think they cut some corners so people do not eat a lot (ie. salty seafood / tough cuts of meat). Would I come again and pay $70 for food that is average? Probably not. Would it be worth it if you have never been to Bacchanal Buffet?? Yes.

Came here for brunch on a weekday. $40/person. We had a good time. The seating area is very comfortable. We were given a 4 person table. The menu was very expansive. We were most impressed by their freshly squeezed juices (available before 11am). We had 6 bottles.... Haha. Other highlights - craving station, omelette station, charcuterie, over 10 flavors of gelato, etc. Surprisingly the Asian section was decent. They also have cereal, yogurt, fresh fruit, salads (not that good), pastas, etc. 

We were very happy to spend our money on brunch and thought it was worth it.

The infamous Bacchanal Buffet has been featured on many YouTuber's blogs. Variety is fantastic here! Variety includes cuisines of Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Italian, Seafood, and etc. It also seems to me that they are aim to use high quality and premium ingredients for their food. Drinks like soda, coffee, tea, and fresh fruit juices are included in your buffet fare. Pineapple, grapefruit, orange, and apple juices were all great! 

Crab Legs are the most highly sought after item here! They are served during dinner hours starting at 3:00 pm. When I was there, they were serving them at the Italian station. A long line was form but the it moves quick and the crab legs turnover is fast too! Carving station is also another favorite of mine - prime ribs and briskets were good. I did love the side dishes such as their Mac N' Cheese and Cioppino. Snails and stone crabs were pretty good and I would skip the gigantic oysters, they weren't good. Dessert station was an island of its own. All the cakes, puddings, gelato, Taiwanese shaved ice, and made-in-front-of-you hot, fresh crepes. This was another meal for me as well! I was so full at the end of my meal and I lost count how many full plates of food I had. It is definitely a place where your eyes are doing all the eating! 

Yes, it is pricey but I would say it is worth the try! Tip: My hubby and I came to Vegas the week after Labor Day. We walked in around 2:30 pm to pay the weekday brunch price and we got to enjoy both brunch and dinner foods when they turnover at 3:00 pm. :)

This buffet went on for ever!! We watched a bunch of review videos on buffets and this one was recommended by a friend. $60 a person for dinner is expensive I never fell like I eat $60 worth of food. I need a 3 day pass to try everything!! Clam chowder was my favorite! Brisket was not what I am used to, was a bit mushy. I got a plate full of steam crab legs and real sushi! I would totally go back!

This buffet is insane! We had a party of 6 and 2 of the people are Diamond players at Caesar's so we were able to get right in on a Thursday at 6pm. We were each given a glass of champagne, which was very nice. 
The buffet itself is pretty large. Starting at the beginning of the buffet is an Asian section with different steamed dumplings, rice, soups, and other specialties. There is sushi and they offer assorted rolls. I didn't like the fact that they didn't tell you what the rolls were. Sign just said "assorted" and it looked to be about 4 different ones. There was a salad area, cheese and honey area, pizza and Italian section. The line for crab legs was always so long and disorganized that I never actually got any. 
The next room has a Mexican area, beef section and more soups and American items. They do have at the other end some crab claws and escargot and there was never a line for those. The food we all had was amazing!!
Whatever you do, save room for dessert! The dessert island is a must have. Gelato, cookies, little pastries of all types.

I tried every single items they had to offer.  It did not live up to the expectation.  Crab claws ? meh.  Little shrimps? meh.  Steaks ? Need more seasoning and kind of dry for one of the cuts I got.  
Best items: tacos, ceviche, coffee chocolate dessert, and the chocolate brownie cake thing next to the pineapple upside down cake.  Not worth the 50 bucks.  We also paid extra for the unlimited mimosas, that might be worth it if you drink a lot since the drinks are pretty pricey in vegas.

Lots and lots to eat, so many choices. Cuisine from many parts of the world.
They can improve their vegetarian options though.

It took a very long wait, but I knew that it will be worth it... Guess what... It wasn't. The food was very mediocre and was honestly "meh". But, their desserts very in good portions and was very magnificent.
One of the best buffet I would eat at when visiting Vegas time after time. Opt in for the all you can drink as well and you're set in one sitting.

#1 buffet in Vegas? I guess I'll have to try it out. Say what? The wait is 2.5 hours long?!?!? Alright, fine. Since I'm already here... wait what? No? 2.5 hours just to get into the line?!?!? Omg, that's ridiculous. So it's a 3+ hr wait and $50+ per person? Dang. Ok, you know what? I give up. Just take my money, take it!

Anyways, the point is be prepared to wait and dish out money even if it's during the holiday season (down time for Vegas standard).

The selection here is excellent, worthy of its high ratings. The food look fresh and taste fresh. The stations are divided by ethnicity and high level categories so it's easy to zone in on what you want. Below are some of the highlights from each station. Overall, there are more health-conscious options (instead of just deep frying everything like other low-tier buffets) and the creative twists on some of the food are a breath of fresh air.

Asian: dim sums, miso ramen/pho, decent sushi selection
Italian: custom pizza, salad
Mexican: fresh tacos
American: carving station w/ large selections
Seafood: jumbo shrimp, crabs fresh from the pot
Dessert: sugar free options, crepe, green tea mocha ice cream, thai tea creme brule, red velvet pudding

Btw, is this Chinatown b/c I seriously can't find any non-Asians here... ... ... nope, still nothing. Oh wait, I found a white guy!!! ... with a group of Asians. Jokes aside, while I was standing in line, I literally felt like I was in Chinatown or in China.

I would like to start be saying $70.00 a person isn't worth coming to this buffet. I attended March of 2019 on a Friday and the menu was standard. I.E. Ribs, over cooked roast, taco's. The first plate of food I got was just under warm, and I would expect hot. My dining area had a crab crawl under the table on the floor. I was highly disappointed in the menu and the clean table tops with dirty floors. In a good note the food was good but I was expecting more of gourmet food. Buffett bar presentation was done very well.
The waiter service was A1. I didn't have a dirty plate on my table for longer 3 min literally. All the staff had an welcoming smile and was ready to help or serve you. The high light of the meal was the crab legs. I not a desert guy but they liked good.  All and all not worth the $70 a head, but the food was better than average. Just my opinion

Food was good, service was HORRIBLE! We made the MISTAKE of paying for VIP service. Service was shotty, at best. Server took FOREVER to bring us our drinks and when he finally did come to our table, it was 1 drink at a time. They limit you to 2hrs, even though it's not disclosed on the website. We waited 50 minutes for our (small) seafood tower. We paid for TWO VIP lunches and got ONE tower to share. Will NEVER pay for VIP again. Aside from express check-in, there was no other perk. DONT WASTE YOUR MONEY ON VIP!!!!!!

Best buffet?  Yes.  Take your buffet experience to the next level with Bacchanal.  I've been to numerous LV buffets and Bacchanal tops all of them.  The lines do get long so come early or during the down times.  

My group got in at 5 pm with no wait and then we were set free to devour anything and everything we wanted.  There's so much to choose from.  When you think the buffet ends, keep going because there's more around the corner.  In front of the buffet counter is the seafood.  You will find the crab legs there.  They only have it out at certain times so check before you visit especially if that is what you want.  I preferred the warm crab legs that was further down the buffet line.  Less salty than the cold legs.  The wagyu beef is another attraction.  I thought it was okay as it was on the chewy side.  I liked the prime rib more.  The awesome thing about Bacchanal Buffet is that I am certain you will find something that you love.  The options are endless.  The dessert bar was extensive as well.  If you're a sweets person, this spot won't disappoint.  

There is a two hour limit.  I'm not sure how strict they are but our group didn't get close to the two hours.  Everyone found the options they liked and indulged.  You'll need coffee, a long walk, and/or a nap after this buffet.

This buffet had nice portions and what seems like high quality food. The lines are really long and the lighting is extremely dim. I enjoyed the pre-cut crab legs. The servers were attentive and quick to get us the drinks we wanted. It was great to get a free glass of champagne with a Yelp check-in. 

Overall, for the price of the buffet, I would go for special occasions.

DISAPPOINTED!!! We are the guests at the Ceasar Palace and we were recommended to check out the buffet because we love seafood. We were very disappointed after tasting the oysters.  The oysters were very gritty, salty with an old flavor texture that was so bad that we had to spit them out!
We spoke to Brian, the general manager, a person you want to avoid speaking with. He seemed unbothered with our very first experience at their restaurant. He didn't offer for any compensations nor try to suggest another option for our enjoyment, even though we spent $178+ on the buffet... we only went there for the seafood.  He clients service was NOT there. We then asked for the assistant manager later on who is named Andre and he said they're doing a investigation on it as we were speaking and they were actively in the process of switching vendors because of complaints in the past and the very recent seafood poisoning incident that has happened at this restaurant. One of the chef's happened to walk by while we were speaking to Andre and he even admitted that the oysters do come in bad batches. 
Andre heard our complaints and felt compelled to take $59 off the bill. I appreciated that but Really? Since we paid that much, so I decided to sit back and have a glass of wine before I try something else. The seafood soups i"ve tried is so salty as if someone dumped the whole canister of salt in the soups.  We ended up paying $119 for bad oysters and still walking out HINGRY so we ate elsewhere.  We're just more so extremely disappointed with the oysters and could get food poison by it if we swallow the oysters.  Glad we didn't!!!

This place is a must stop in Las Vegas! Truly an amazing atmosphere, nearly every food you can think of, and fresh! The staff was super efficient. while we did wait, we got in quicker than anticipated. This was definitely our best meal by far in Vegas! If you haven't gone here you need to AT LEAST once!!! You won't regret it!
I don't know what the hell they are doing in their kitchen but I know it's not good.

I've been coming to Caesars since I was a young man and was spending high dollar to enjoy amazing meals and meet hot chicks at the Bacchanal Room.  They got rid of that restaurant and now several years later they bring it back but now it's a buffet... but not just any old run of the mill average Vegas buffet.  

This is the buffet where you spend a little more but get a lot for your money.  Not just average food with fake sushi or small crab legs.  This is high end, great food and amazing drinks with spectacular service. 

If you have the money and want to try it then do... If you don't have the money I suggest you splurge and you won't be disappointed.  

I've now been here 3 different times and it's just getting better and better.  

I might even try the desserts on my next trip.

We took 6 family members to what I considered the very best Buffett or food on strip but was let down.  We finally got through the line and the host was not friendly and very short. I had been many times and loved it.  It's pricey but was always worth it.  My one guest asked for shrimp hot or a dish that had hot shrimp and was rudely told we have what you see.  I understood bad days but this was her bday and was very upset by the tone. I had dry sushi and was very surprised that they were taking their time to get fresh shrimp and other seafood replenished.    The carver station meat was dry and carver was very stingy with portions.  When asked for more I was surprised to get a hesitation and look.  



Sad to say as a local I won't be back. I will not spend money here again. Sad because I tell everyone I cross that this was the greatest place ever.   I guess it was just a bad day.
Speechless!! It was amazing . The food the service. The entire place it's wonderful! I rate a little bit of everything . Left the place stuffed n very happy
Great Buffett. Amazing sea food and desserts. The crab hot or cold all you can eat was worth it. I highly recommend this place.

It was really good. The key is to get there at 10 am when it opens. The small plates were delicious as most of the egg dishes were absolutely fantastic. The Monte Cristo sandwiches were really good along with the mini burgers and the lobster eggs benedict. The warm lobster crab legs were also delicious. The desert selections were really good especially the chocolate mousse dish. While it is a bit pricey for example a party of 8 that includes for children was around $350, I think it was worth it and we won't go there all the time but it's definitely an experience. You definitely need to pace yourself and not finish all the food, but have a taste of all the selections that you want to have. You do have a two-hour limit. My only main critique is that they didn't bus the plates fast enough.
Amazing quality and service!! Won't be disappointed with the hot seafood and rosiotto!!

Great selection of different cuisines from carved turkey to Asian dumplings. I would recommend asking for seating closer to the buffet tables. One change I would make to improve the experience would be for the plates to be positioned under a heat lamp to keep food warmer for a longer period of time. The buffet was so large that I noticed my food would be room temperature to almost cold by the time I sat down to eat.

I don't think I ate $60+ worth of food, but that's not good old Caesar's problem, that's my own dang fault! Totally disappointed that I had to tap out early before I could taste everything they offered, which is a lot. The higher value delicacies - seafood and meat- are farther from the dining area, and we started gorging on whatever delicious appetizers we found near to us. The whole experience was a lot of fun though, and we enjoyed the fun, grazing, and people watching for two hours! Staff was quick and friendly to help clear plates and serve beverages.
Best buffet in Vegas! A little pricey so make sure you get your money worth. The warm crab legs are one of my favorite parts, everything seems really fresh and restocked. Love it

My fiancé and I went for the brunch buffet, everything we tasted was delicious!!! We went around 9:45am on a Saturday and it wasn't over crowded! Everything was hot and fresh, waiter was very nice (gotta love when you don't have to ask for refills)! We will definitely be going back soon!!!

Great food, but was expecting more selections for a Caesar's Buffet. The crab legs were mouth watering amazing with lots of meaty legs and claws! The service however I feel could have been a lot better for a luxury buffet. It looked like they were understaffed for front of house workers. FUN FACT : the bathrooms near the buffet only has like 4 stalls so there is always a line,  I suggest you go before you get there lol. But I liked it overall, would come back for the crab legs, lamb, sweet potato maple tots and Nutella crepes. Wish I took more pictures

High quality buffet. 
The thing about it is for $55 you're really better off going to an upscale restaurant and getting something cooked fresh to order. That is unless you insist on a lot of variety or you can eat a lot!!!
The prime rib was excellent as was the sushi and shrimp. Dessert selection was impressive and delicious

It's significantly worse than everyone describes. The food was not fresh, even though the number of people there was quite significant (they should have a better turnover rate). The asian food was absolutely inedible. It's actually quite an insult to asian food in general. The meat was either overcooked or just horrible, although the tri-tip was fine. They also desperately need to figure out how to cook crab. Honestly I'm not sure what was going through my mind when I decided to eat crab in the middle of a desert, but I paid the ridiculous price, waited the ridiculous time in line at 3pm, and have nobody but myself to blame.

One word: HYPE.  We were so excited to try the "best buffet in Vegas," based on some articles and advertisements. We even paid an extra $25 per person to supposedly skip the line, only to be dumped at another line and wait 30 minutes. Granted, we went on a Saturday night but geesh! For $25 on top of the $60 we expected to be seated in 10 minutes at the most. 

Now about the food. The entry selection was pretty typical of Vegas buffets...don't expect anything out of the ordinary. The only thing new to us was the wagyu beef. I was also pleasantly surprised to see pozole, chile verde, and suckling pig, but altogether the flavors are lacking...all across the board. There were about 4 types of sushi rolls offered...nothing out of the ordinary. Oysters were fresh. Honestly I have been to better buffets in the area, and even better Asian buffets here in SoCal. For the money I paid I was seriously expecting more. 

The service,however, deserves mentioning. They were very quick to clear the tables and refill our drinks. Even though they were very busy, they were open to a quick chat and very approachable. 

Needless to say..would we ever come back? No. I wanted to love this place, but it just didn't cut it for me.
I like crab legs and when I go to a Buffett in Vegas I usually get 3-4 plates of them, and right now these are the best in town. The deserts and other items are awesome as well.
Im sorry to give one star I wish I could just write my review. we stood in line for twenty minutes and the line barely moved so we decided to leave.

As I type this, I am still in the recovery phase of one of the most glorious food comas in recent memory. I will persevere though, because I must spread the word about this buffet to the people of Yelp. Go here. It's worth it. You're hungry, you've been walking around all day, you're cranky, maybe you've lost a little money (not me, I always win) and you're wondering if you'll "get your money's worth" at a $120 (for two after tax and tip) all you can eat buffet. Just go. Your circumstances will immediately get better once you lay your eyes on the plethora of tasty food available. You'll fill your plate with Szechuan Chinese, country style barbecue, cheesy pizza, and sushi. You'll be so excited to see pork belly, king crab legs, and build your own pasta on round 2 that you didn't even spot the pastor and carne asada street taco station. No fear, there is always round 3.  After all that, with a big smile on your face, you will discover the dessert section. Tiramisu, macaroons, gelato, cookies, cupcakes and many many other colorful and tasty confections will take your worries away and give you the energy you need to continue on your Vegas journey. Or make you want to fall asleep.....but it will all be worth it.

Overall I was pretty happy with most of the selections offered here!  I left full and satisfied.

I love buffets that have salmon sashimi (in this case nigiri).  I ate many many many.  The oysters were not that good though, disappointingly.  Oh yes, if they have the lava cake...eat multiple of those.  SO good.

The ticket system is pretty convenient.  Instead of waiting in line you get a ticket to come back at a certain time.  It's a win win because you'll won't have to wait, but you'll probably go spend money in their casino gambling or drinking in the meantime.

Unless you like seafood, don't waste your time. We waited 3 hours and spent $120 (the prices went up in the new year). Food was mediocre, I've spent less money on better food other places in Vegas. But I do not like seafood.

A little bit of everything with high quality! They say it's the best buffet in America. Everything I tried had great texture and great taste so I agree with what they say.

$39.99 for weekday 7:30-11:00am 11:00am-3:00pm $45.99 then the price gets higher for dinner

Everything was the bomb. Except the half hour wait in line. They had snow crab and King grab already sliced in half, huge cocktail prawns, several ramen soups made to order right there in line! Sweet potato tater tots! Peking duck! Gourmet Cheeses and salami(s), fresh mango, guava, pineapple juice! Horchata! Several kinds of Smoked sausages, big ass flinstones beef ribs, pork ribs, clams, oysters, Crawdads, fresh calamari, hella salads, beef roasts, Mexican food, American Chinese food, dim sum, sushi, fried chicken, and much, much more. I'm just naming the stuff that caught my eye.
Amazing Buffett, good variety of food. Definitely a Buffett that you don't want to eat breakfast for so you can try as many things as possible. Very friendly staff and just an amazing Buffett!

I think coming here is more for the experience rather than coming for the actual food.  Having said that the experience was basically going to a mediocre buffet.  Food was nothing unique, nothing upscale, quality was pretty poor.  So relative to the price, one of the worse experiences.  Seafood - raw or chilled, taco station - why would I eat this here?, cuts of meat - been drying up all day and not edible, noodle station - pennies to make, sushi - little variety, dim sum - poor quality.  The top items here are the beef ribs, and the duck.  Overall just not impressed with the quality.

Woah. Just Woah. This place has basically every kind of (good) food you could expect to see at any buffet in vegas - from upscale breakfast classics like steak and eggs, to chicken and waffles (fried chicken in a waffle cone), an extensive selection of seafood (raw bar and salads), an asian, sushi, italian, and latin american sections, and an extremely decadent selection of desserts. They even have fresh pressed juices! Come with your stretchy pants and a big appetite. 

If you have a food allergy/intolerance just tell your server and the chef will take you around telling you exactly what you can and can't have. So helpful!! I found I had more gluten-free options (like pancakes, pizza, pasta, etc. if you wanted any of those) at the Bellagio buffet but this one was amazing too. 

Favorite dishes: steak and eggs, pork belly, street tacos, thick-cut bacon, and woah the desserts. Homemade marshmallows, sorbet, tapioca pudding, and gluten-free cake pops! 

It's a bit pricey, even for vegas, so prepare for that!

My daughter and I went to Bacchanal on a Saturday evening for dinner. As locals, it's one of our favorite buffets on the Strip. It did not disappoint. First of all, our waitress, Su, was absolutely amazing! The only waitress at any buffet we've been to, to give us clean linen napkins and silverware when we needed them, but did not ask. She was on top of everything... from refilling drinks, to providing paper (and linen) napkins, and clearing plates. Plus she was very friendly so a shout-out goes to Su!

The food: It was very good. One thing I did not know but thoroughly appreciated was that when I went to the meat station the prime rib was a touch too rare for me (which is often the case at many of the buffets). The chef asked me if I'd like it cooked a bit more, and promptly did just that! I've never been asked before, and the meat was delicious. With a nice sear from the grill, too. Lots of choices, as usual, plus the chilled and split crab legs which are now on weekends only. Steamed are available during the week (at night) but not split. The mussels in fennel sauce were a have to go back and get more. And desserts, which are my fave part of a Bacchanal experience were fab. I do miss some of the items which they have since replaced since visiting previously (like the chocolate bark; crème caramel; and for my daughter, the mochi), but overall one can't complain when it comes to desserts. 

We will definitely be back!
High class food but definitely not coming back again... came for my first buffet in Vegas, maybe I expected too much... although lots of selection, the quality of the food is not that great...

Super disappointed. Me and my friend watched some exciting introduction videos of Bacchanal buffet on YouTube before going and were ready to be impressed. But instead we decided never going back. 

I've NEVER seen worse customer services than this buffet. The staff's attitude was just "eye-opening". So I found hair in my plate and our waiter simply told us "This is normal. There are many ways chef's hair can get into food." with a don't-act-like-this-is-a-big-deal face. When the manager finally came after 30 min wait, she's like "we can only refund one of you and that person has to stop eating if she wants a refund." Wow. And no apology the whole time. 

Also, food selection were not as much as we expected or shown in the intro videos (maybe they secretly changed the menu?). And the food quality was disappointing (e.g. meat was quite dry). 

There's a reason this buffet is going downhill (it's cheap and arrogant). We will see if it's still around next time we visit Vegas.

The buffet itself deserves 5 stars. I subtracted 1 for having to stand in line for an hour to be seated. There prolly wasn't a way to get around the long line, simply because its a very popular buffet inside of Ceasar Palace hotel but it definitely took away from the experience. Anywho, it is an amazing buffet with a variety of quality food: prime rib, crab legs (chilled and boiled), shrimp, sushi, dim-sum, frog legs and the list goes on and on. I was overwhelmed with joy. U will not be disappointed. The staff were friendly/helpful. I was able to check-in thru Yelp to receive a free alcoholic beverage. Yes! I will be visiting again.

The most grand and probably the best buffet on Vegas strip (not counting the Sterling brunch at Bally's).
Expect some wait because they're about the most popular buffet on Vegas strip.
My younger days, I did enjoy the variety and endless quantity option but yup, I think this would be my last visit to this buffet. I'd rather spend a peaceful time at a more relaxed atmosphere - next dinner will be at the Joe's steakhouse at Caesar's:-) This is a buffet so do  not expect everything to be seasoned and cooked to perfection.  Not everything here is delicious. 
Don't get me wrong, I give them props for having different choices with better quality and service buffet spread than the other Vegas hotel buffets.
However, I feel like the food has been sorta declining in taste and quality than when they first opened.
If you are young and have fast metabolism - go for it!
Stand outs for me this time were the sea snails, lamb chop, & as always their desserts! (My hubs gorged on snow crab legs - I liked the hot steamed ones)
The service has always been good on my visits.
So the fun thing about the buffet is that you can eat and enjoy variety of offerings at one place. 
Bacchanal does offer all the food you can eat!
Go there and eat like the Greek Gods~ 
Enjoy the grandest Vegas buffet there is!

This is my second time visiting Vegas and I decided to visit the Bacchanal again, despite coming a few months ago. The buffet never disappoints... it was so good that we decided to come twice this trip! The price is on the more expensive side compared to other buffets, but you get what you pay for. As a fair warning, their prices are more expensive around the holidays. On non-holidays, lunch is usually around $40 on weekdays, but today it was $55 as part of their holiday brunch. 

As far as food, there are a variety of choices, my favorite being the duck, crab legs, tomato bisque, bone marrow, beef brisket, and so much more! Make sure you come hungry because you'll likely spend around 2 hours trying the different foods. Desserts are a must as well.. I loved the macarons, pandan creme brûlée, and even their simple gelato/ice cream are a must try. 

This experience is like no other buffet experience on the strip. If you're visiting the city, this is one buffet you won't want to miss.

Oh man, if you only stop at one buffet in Las Vegas, make it this one! I had heard great things about this buffet, but visiting it is another thing entirely.
The seating area is very open and spacious. You get to also enjoy the view of Caesar's pool, a very lovely sight. Service was alright. I think our waitress did disappear on a long break at one point, but we weren't really needing too many drinks, so it wasn't a huge issue for us. Especially since they just leave a pot of coffee for you at the table. 
The food selection is phenomenal. There is just SO MUCH good stuff to choose from, it was almost overwhelming (in the best way possible). Not only is there quantity, but QUALITY. Everything looked so good and it all WAS good! Definitely not the case for every buffet I've been to, or the majority for that matter. 
We went for breakfast at around 9:30am. This is a great time and there was no line! We had the Buffet of Buffets pass so our surcharge was only $15. A fabulous deal for this buffet. Then we hung around until lunch time and while we were basically stuffed, we did get to see what they put out for lunch which also looked amazing. 

Get the chocolate lava cake. It's amazing.

Got the Groupon and so worth it. Even without the Groupon. Best breakfast buffet in town. Recommend the steak and eggs skillet, Mexican soups (calorie and pozole), pork belly, prime rib, and chicken and waffles. Desserts are phenomenal. Gelato bar is amazing. Can't say enough good things. Come hungry and pace yourself. You have 2 hours to enjoy it.

No crab legs (as advertised) which was one of the main reasons we chose to go! There are plenty of choices, but very few truly tasty ones. The entire Asian section was cold/dried out. Italian section was also dried out, though the pizza was hot. The employee near the soups and cheeses REFUSED to give me the stuffed grape leaves even AFTER 11am (lunch service starts) and just stood there clasping her gloved hands staring off. My husband reached through and grabbed four of them just to spite her. Sadly, it wasn't worth the drama. Very bland. The roasted chicken was great and the lemon basil sorbet was stellar - seriously, I ate TWO scoops. Otherwise...meh.

Too expensive for mediocre food with so so service. Servers doesn't smile and didn't look happy to be working there.  Seafood was not fresh and tasted over cooked and salty.
Sad.
2 hour wait on a Monday night @ 6p. Prime rib and snow crab legs were the ones I focused on. Other items sat around if it wasn't popular and tasted old and dry . Not worth the wait.

This is without a doubt the best buffet I've ever been to. The wait was really long. Over an hour wait but it was Easter Sunday. The food was great and had a very large selection.  Being a foodie I had to try a little bit of everything (impossible here) and there wasn't anything I didn't like.
Lots of variety. Really good/fresh food. Good value. Slab bacon, brisket, etc. Tons of good stuff.

I wish I would've listened to my fellow yelp friends when I read their reviews.  This place is overhyped, overpriced & overrated.  Absolutely nothing blew me away, and that includes the seafood too.  The crab meat inside all the crab legs looked as though they came from severely malnourished crabs because they were limp, stringy and scrawny looking.  Everything I tried was mediocre and underwhelming.  I didn't try any of the meats, but my partner described them as disgusting and had really bad indigestion & acid reflux the entire day after our meal.  He couldn't even walk by the meat station after eating the meats because the smell made him nauseous.  We tried almost every single dessert & nothing blew us away, everything was too sweet and unbalanced.  I should've expected this from a buffet, but I expected more since this place is supposedly the best buffet in vegas.

One of the biggest food disappointments of my life. After hearing about this place for years, I finally got a chance to try it, and my expectations were sky high. I think they might have been too high, because Bacchanal just seems like a slightly better than average casino buffet.
First thing, you'll be waiting. Expect to wait 45 minutes on a weekday night, and probably a lot longer for a weekend. I only mention this because I didn't think the restaurant was worth that extended wait time.
If you've been to a high end buffet in Asia, you'll remember how they walk you through the buffet, getting you all hyped about the food. Well, they do that here too, but as the hostess took us around, I had a sinking feeling. Like, that's it? Where was the king crab I heard so much about? The lobster? The crawfish? All we saw were lobster and brown crab claws, cut up into pitiful looking chunks. They didn't taste great either, not fresh tasting at all.
What stood out? There was a fresh taco stand, I enjoyed that. The halibut was one of the better dishes of the night. And the desserts were plentiful and excellent. But the meat station wasn't as good as expected. You could choose from cuts like tritip, or wagyu, but it was all dry and tasteless. Even with the aus jus, I could barely get through one piece, let alone all 5 or 6 cuts.
Another thing, the food all had fancy names, like truffle pizza, or truffle and mushroom soup, but in the end the pizza was just average and the soup tasted like it came from a can. That's how everything was, it looked and sounded good, but the taste was saddening. 
At nearly $60 USD, you'll be expecting a lot too, and I'm sure it's great for all the guests that want to eat and gamble or play slots, but it simply isn't worth going out of your way for.
One of our favorite buffets anywhere. We keep coming back for more. Love the desert bar!

This buffet is a must try spot for foodies visiting Las Vegas! This is probably the most famous buffet on the strip and the wait time is pretty worth it. 

Bacchanal is well known for its food diversity. There are so many different types of cuisines to choose from and there are a lot of chefs that will serve you. My favorite areas were the noodle bar and the dessert section. A lot of diners will come here for the seafood area and for the huge king crab legs. In my opinion, the crab legs were super salty so I avoided them after I realized they were too intense for my taste. 

While there were a lot of delicious dishes here, I think that some areas fell short. For instance, the Chinese dim sum section was a bit disappointing - I wish there were fresher items there. Bacchanal is definitely a "quantity then quality" buffet so don't be surprised if not all of the cuisines are treated with equal care. 

My only tip for Bacchanal is to come with a huge group. The restaurant has two separate lines: one for groups over a certain number (I believe it was 15 people?) and one for regular groups. When my giant group got there, we saw that the regular line was packed with people and the "big groups" line only had two groups in line. We got put in the big group line. We ended up getting seated before many others in the regular groups line.
However, my experience was also during EDC weekend so I'm not sure if the Bacchanal typically sorts groups that way or if my group got insanely lucky.

I dislike buffets.  Low quality food that has been sitting there for hours is just not my type of culinary experience.  Having said that, I have about eaten in all of the casino buffets.  When I come with friends or family, it seems we always end up in one of these places.  Being a non-fan of Caesar, I figured that I would unlikely come to this place.  However, my father had free buffet here, so reluctantly, we headed over here.  Hidden in the back of the casino, you will find this place with a snake line to accommodate large crowds.  Being a Diamond Total Rewards member, we walked right up to the front and got in quickly.  So quick entrance and free meant that my expectations should be exceeded.  And yes indeed it was.  The buffet, like most Vegas buffet was humongous.  But to my shock, the quality of the food appeared to be good.  Appearance was true.  Sushi selection was limited, but they had nigiri so that made me happy.  The prime rib was tender and delicious.  It matched the quality of high end steak places.  The seafood rocked.  How many buffets have raw oysters?  And they were high end raw oysters.  Crab legs and large peeled shrimp added more to my amazement of the high quality food that could be found here.  In fact the food choices were humongous.  I doubt that you could find some you didn't like.  If I had to pay the $50 price tag, I probably wouldn't come back since I wouldn't get my moneys worth.  But if I get a complimentary buffet or even a good discount, this is the buffet I would chose.  So far, for me, the best buffet in Vegas.
Great selection of multicultural food.   Desserts were so amazing.   Loved the Mexican food especially.

Buffet of buffet. Endless choices of gourmet goodies. Waited about 20minutes in line. My visit was during one of those 3 day weekends so it was given.

Very well organized and clean. I tried eating as many dishes I could and even wore stretchy yoga pants. I would definitely return to do some damage.
Over price, went here twice, first time was just okay, second was not good at all, the oysters are not fresh, good selections, but still not worth the money

I'm not a buffet person. For me, it's a huge waste of money because I can only eat so much. But I was willing to try Bacchanal just because I haven't had the chance to dine at a buffet in Vegas. It was this or Wicked Spoon. Since I won some cash on the slot machines, I figured why not just go to Bacchanal and spend my winnings there since it was deemed the most popular/best buffet. 

We paid $38.99/person (lunch price) and got in line at 2:25 (45 minutes before dinner time). Dinner started at 3pm. The wait was about 15-20 minutes so by the time we got seated, it was about 2:45. We were able to experience both lunch and dinner for lunch price. Smart huh? I recommend doing that to get the most out of your money and to save you $25-30/person. But I cannot guarantee you will have as short of a wait because we went on a Thursday. I assume it'd be busier Fri-Sun.

Started off at the seafood section which is right by the entrance. I think the crab legs attract all the visitors. I grabbed plates and plates of their steamed mussels. They were soaked in some sort of green sauce, but they tasted AMAAAAZING! I also tried some pork belly over mashed potatoes, miso sea bass, sole - all served in these little tiny pots/pans which made them very presentable. I stayed away from the pizza, sushi, noodles, soup, and Chinese food. The dim sum they served were just shrimp dumplings (ha gow), pork buns, siu mai, etc. They had a variety of sushi as well (not too many selections though). They had a juice bar where you could choose from mango, guava, pineapple, and tamarind. The juices were served in cute little bottles.

3pm - aka dinner time - AKA CRAB LEGS!! Once they brought those out, a line was constantly forming, but it went by pretty quickly. Even though some people grabbed a lot, the crab was being restocked constantly which was great. They had a butter dispenser right by the crab legs, but I chose not to get some. The crab tasted fantastic and fresh just by itself anyways. What I loved the most about these crab legs was the fact that they were already cracked open for you. This was a big deal to me because I suck at cracking crab. I hate doing it and just having it like this just saved me a whole lot of trouble. The crab meat just peeled right off - the easiness of my crab eating experience allowed me to fill my tummy with tons and tons of crab!!!!! The crab and mussels were the best part. Totes worth the money.

The other section of the buffet with the Asian food, sushi, and pizza didn't change much for dinner (or perhaps we didn't stay too long to see it all change). We were only there for about an hour and a half? There was a two hour limit which was more than enough time to fill us up. The dessert section was in the middle. It had a couple of fruit options - melon, watermelon, pineapple, and honeydew. They had tons of dessert options from cheesecake, fudge squares, gelato, boba floats, cakes, cupcakes, etc - you name it. Didn't really try a lot here because I'm not a huge fan of dessert, heh.

Definitely worth it for the price we paid. To experience both lunch and dinner for $25-30 less was great. Lots of variety too! The only problem I had with the place was that they took forever to clean our table. We had tons of finished plates and when we came back with new plates of food, there wasn't any space to put them.. 

Other than that, my tummy was very satisfied! :)

Wow. We had to line up before we could get in line and I can see why.  First, they actually serve your drinks and give you refills.  Many buffets no longer do this in Vegas.  My partner and I waited a little bit over an hour on a Tuesday evening at 6pm.  We later learned  this was the worst time to go.    

Loved/ Stand outs: 
- The prime rib and wagyu steaks.  They were thick and juicy!

-The black sesame gelato ! They know their Asian crowd and I was blown away by the flavor!  What a treat !!  

Disliked:
The seafood line. They need to speed this up a bit. 
The sea snails were on the tough side. 
The oysters could've been colder.  Wished they offered more sauces.  
Egg tarts didn't taste authentic.

We came here on a Thursday night. 
1) Ambient - It is very crowded. But everything was decorated beautifully.
2) Service - We saw our server 5 times during our entire meal service of 2 hours. We got a bigger table and was able to put away used plates around our table.
3) Food: There is a huge selection but quantity does not equal to quality. The food are ok, nothing fantastic. The Asian food are not tasty. The roast duck is no authentic at all. This is not how Chinese makes roast duck. My husband say it's American Chinese food. I think Panda Express makes better Asian food. Also, they ran out of king crabs legs at 6pm of the dinner buffet, which is ridiculous for a buffet that ends at 10pm. The mushroom soup is the best item that I had at the buffet.
Given the price that we paid for dinner, I would say it was slightly disappointing.

I love this buffet. Not because it's good or anything but it's the buffet that pretty much has turned me off of buffets forever. Literally the biggest waste of money ever. Let's start with the line..wtf is that?! There were plenty of tables around. For $120 for two people, I seriously expected more. I think there are more higher quality items at the freakin Golden Corral. Don't get me wrong, the spread is obviously impressive. But the taste of everything was horrible. 

Start with the asian section. The Chinese food is just stale, the dim sum has been overly steamed, the sushi rice is stale. The Italian section..man, awful. Mexican section was okay. Mainly because lots of things were DIY. The "wagyu" was offensive..that the cow died for that garbage to be served that way. The lobster bisque had a layer of film on top, the shrimp is mushy, and the bone Marrow is dry.. 

To top it off, my server, Martha refused to acknowledge my existence. Her only job was pretty much to refill drinks and I almost felt like she deliberately ignored me because she never refilled my drink until I had to wave her down. 

Thank for bacchanal for teaching me a lesson. Never allow y'all to rob me blind again

I can tell this buffet in vegas is one of the best buffets, you have a lot of choices of foods and desert.
Usually the quality of food in the buffets are not in high quality but this place has good quality.
The only thing you need to consider is wait time in line specially when you wanna go to this place on holidays or weekends.
Totally happy with food and service.

Food coma...must stay awake...must write review...

I've been waiting to try Bachannal and tonight, a few friends and I finally went after shopping.  At 5:30pm there was already a long line.  Since I don't gamble, I don't have a rewards card so we had to stand in line for 30 minutes which allowed us to chat while waiting.  I paid $54.04 per person and I think it was worth the money.

As soon as you get in, you're greeted by seafood: crab legs, oysters, clams, mussels, shrimps, etc.  Since I'm allergic to that stuff, I didn't bother trying it (one allergic reaction per week is my quota). Then you pass through the American station (sliders, ribs, BBQ, rib eye, sausage, onion rings, prime rib, tater tots, corn on the cob, truffle potatoes, sweet potato fries, etc), Mexican station (salsa, tortilla, etc) and dessert station (macarons, gelato, cakes, cupcakes, tarts, fruits, cake pops, creme brûlée, bread pudding, crepes, etc) in the middle. The charcuterie (mortadella, coppa, salami, prosciutto, mocecta and air-dried sausages),  and cheese stations plus Italian (pizza, ziti, stromboli, etc) and Asian (sushi, pho, ramen; salty and spicy fish, bao, shumai, hargao, dumplings and other Chinese dishes) stations are in the back.

I was so excited about the pho and ramen.  I ordered a bowl of pho and I asked the two chefs "where's the noodles?" and they kept pointing at it and I was like "all I see is broth?" so I gave them back my bowl and shamelessly asked for more - much better.  If I were on a diet, I wouldn't be at a buffet.  Also, try the salty and spicy fish.

Let's talk about desserts...they have mini vanilla cupcakes, mini chocolate cupcakes and mini red velvet cupcakes (with extra tart cream cheese frosting), chocolate brownie tart (skip the tart and just eat the chocolate brownie on top), cake pops and tiramisu were nothing to write home about.  The chocolate and passion fruit dessert was not good.  I give them A for effort on the macarons.  They're not fantastic.  In fact, the pistachio, orange and rose all tasted so artificial and only the vanilla and chocolate macarons were good.  They're hard to make though.  The desserts I did enjoy were chocolate creme brûlée, fig & balsamic gelato, baklava gelato and Aztec chocolate gelato.

Now the best buffets in Vegas in my opinion include: Wynn, Bellagio, Wicked Spoon at The Cosmopolitan and Studio B at M (my favorite).  For having pho, ramen, unusual gelati, macarons, charcuterie, salty and spicy fish (YUM!!!), crepes and juicy sliders - Bacchanal deserves 5 stars.  The quality of fish they use for their sushi isn't as fresh as Studio B's.  Just imagine this, if Wicked Spoon (single serving plating) and Studio B (delicious variety) had a buffet baby...Bacchanal would've been it.

Went to this expensive buffet to see what the hype was all about and I was disappointed! Prime Rib was horrible! For $60+ I was expecting some delicious steak and/or juicy full of flavor Prime Rib and what I got was a tough piece of meat where I was adding salt !! The other stations were okay but not for $60 bucks! This will be my "one and done" won't be back!

I've been to most of the Vegas hotel buffets and this one is the best one, which means a long wait if you eat here during peak times. This is also the most expensive one too, located in Caesars. 

We came here for crab legs. These things were huge and delicious. I didn't need any butter. The line moved quickly, less than a minute. 

I also tried some bbq meats (just ok), sushi (decent variety), seaweed salad (awesome), and some other stuff that all tasted better than what is offered at other buffets. 

The desserts are pretty decent. I was impressed with the creme brûlée, just don't get one that's dark brown cuz that's too burnt. The mini cheesecakes and chocolate parfaits were also a hit.  

Service was top notch all around.

In short , one of the best buffet I had in my life . 
I was skeptical of the long line and the price . But after having the meal , I think it was absolutely worth every penny of it !

This is a probable!!! The most popular restaurant in Vegas!! but it really leaves a lot to be desired !!!  We waited in line for more than 1 hour to be assigned a table! We were really excited! ... wow!  more than an hour !! ... we said to each other "this has to be worth gold" ..... and that moment just arrived .... passing between the buffet bars !!  seafood!  Mexican food!  Italian food!  Chinese Food!  Japanese food!  Dessert that in sight, you didn't want to eat them !!  Look so beautiful, so craving!  ..... we walked in a hurry to get to our table !!  We left our things and ran to the buffet bars to start savoring those delicacies !!!  REALITY ... DRY FOOD, ... WITHOUT FLAVOR .. totally THE OTHERWISE !!  $ 200 THROW TO THE GARBAGE !!!

Excellent quality overall
Ribs a little dry
Other than ghat, steak prime rib, crab claws, crab legs were wonderful
Great sides 
Great desserts

Only negative- hostess or server took our receipts from table while we were getting first course, which I needed   Didn't notice until after we left
Bacchanal has seen better days.  Quality is way down in my opinion.  I had better buffets on my last cruise ship.  Quantity over quality for sure.  Especially for the $$$ you pay.

Best food best best service
best Francesico thank you so much, it was the best Crablegs

This is probably the best buffet I have been to. It is probably one of most expensive too, weekend dinner price listed at $65, $15 for unlimited alcohol?  There is a huge variety of food and a lot of their food choices were good. There were a few items I did not like. I did not care for the poke/sushi. The carving station was good. Surprisingly, the ramen was pretty good too. 
The best part of this dinner was the King crab legs (the ones with spikes). It was brought to our table by the server and I didn't see it on every table. I'm guessing it was a special only available to vip card holders. The Buffett offered snow crab legs. The server didn't explain so I'm not sure, but the King crab legs were very good. It was all precracked too!

Went here for the first time. Had heard so much about this buffet over the years and it being in the top 2 or 3 in Vegas. I have to say I was seriously underwhelmed. The food was ok at best. The prime rib was over cooked and could only be served as medium or medium well. Not how a prime rib should be. The brisket was mostly fat. The waygu beef had no flavor. The pizza was basic. The Asian food was nothing special. I enjoyed the chilled shrimp but it's pretty hard to mess that up. The dessert area was one bright spot as there were a number of items to choose from that were a bit unique and very good. Overall, this buffet was not worth $65 per person. 

In comparison to the Aria buffet, I would choose that over this one. The Aria buffet is almost as large, cheaper at $54 a person and the food was way better. I won't waste my time coming back to this buffet again.

Best buffet of all the major strip resorts! Every item is carefully prepared and showcased. A bit pricey and disappointed there's no lobster from the selection. All in all, 5 stars well earned. Prime rib is elegantly juicy and street tacos are awesome. The Vietnamese Pho is not quite authentic but satisfied my craving. It's what to be expected.

When in Vegas, you got to go to a buffet (or so I've been told). Since my friend's been to Vegas several times already, I trusted his judgement and decided to go to Bacchanal for their buffet. Let's just say there were no regrets afterwards- it's kind of difficult to not find something you like when there's a plethora of options. So, where do we start?

First, it's important to note that unlike most buffets (at least the ones in NYC), they don't care if you don't eat everything on your plate. Not saying that you should leave a copious amount of food on your plate intentionally because that's just wrong, but by chance if you picked up something you're not a huge fan of you won't get "penalized" for it for lack of better terms. At a buffet, especially one as large as this one, I think that's really important so you don't feel obliged to eat something you didn't know you were going to like. At the same time, I would like to think it also let's diners know to not take a platter full of something they've never tried before because they could literally go back if they want more.

In regards to what I tried, I think a better question would be what didn't I try. Yes, some things fell flat (boba tea with no milk and lukewarm? Come again?) but they accomplished what I always thought would be the hardest things to do at a buffet which is- A. keep the food consistently fresh and B. extremely great and cordial service that wouldn't give you the side eye if you couldn't finish something and may even ask you why you didn't like it instead (9/10 times I'm guessing the answer would be "because I'm too full" anyways).

Though my taste palette was left pretty confused after an hour here, I can say that in the midst of everything there were a couple things that really stood out for me. 1. That brisket. I think I had opted for the Kobe Steak initially but after trying my friend's brisket I can easily say that was some of the best brisket I've had. 2. The corn fritters. I know what you're thinking, corn fritters, really? Maybe because it was the first thing I ate and I like virtually anything deep fried but I liked them. 3. The desserts- all of them! All jokes aside, you can't go wrong with any of the gelatos and the mini key lime tart was surprisingly really good too as it actually had a legitimate amount of filling. All in all, if you're going to do a buffet in Vegas, you can't go wrong with this one.

Went with a group of 5. The wait time was about an hour, which I completely understand. There is a variety of food that ranges from American to Seafood to Asian. However, I felt that for the price, the food was somewhat bland. Especially the dessert, which I was super sad about since that's always the favorite part for me. Would I eat there again....maybe.

Positively the best smorgasbord I've at any point had. The nourishment is somewhat lower than eatery quality so truly, it's a chill thing to check the old pail list, yet on the off chance that you need a genuine dinner you ought to go to a particular area that serves that kind of sustenance. I will say their Tennessee Pork Ribs and their "Road Style" tacos merit striving without a doubt. An extraordinary one night buffet that you will recall!

The CRAB LEGS and PRIME RIB, perfection. If you are not a seafood or steak lover there are always other options but for the amount you're paying I'm hoping you are. To be honest I was expecting a lot more food selection and very different dishes. Either way everything I got taste so fresh that it made up for it. Their calm chowder is a must and it has ruined all other calm chowders for me! I didn't know how delicious and tasty clam chowder was suppose to taste. Make sure you taste a little bit of everything. Their lechon and crispy duck, delicious. I've never had crab legs with so much meat at a buffet before. They have them pre cracked for you so it's very easy to open. And don't forget your clarified butter and lemons for your crab legs. The aguas frecas from the Mexican section are a must try. Very refreshing after eating so much rich food. Now for the Dessert table, it was a little under whelming. Not so much variation to choose from. Very simple and nothing special. The only good thing was the creme burlee.

Best buffet I've ever been to. The workers are constantly rotating items to keep them fresh and warm. The crab legs are endless as is the options you have to choose from. The dessert section here is as big as most hometown buffets themselves. I didn't have a bad item. They were all amazing.
I think is just the famous that it has been done of it, the food is not that good and is not worth it yo make the line and spend your money

Mmmmm Bacchanal, the consistently voted best buffet in Vegas... why you gotta do me wrong and not let me give you 5 stars?! We ate five plates of snow crab legs (wish we got more) and it was crab heaven. I'm breaking the climax for y'all and saying I can't give Bacchanal 5 stars because the meat station had overcooked meat during my visit. I was reaaally sad because that automatically knocks off a majority of what some people come here for, including me (I'm a half meat, half seafood with bits of everything else kind of girl). I asked for what was the rarest item of anything on the carvery and what the butcher showed me looked medium well, which was the prime rib. Gross. I hope I came on an off day. If you serve me rare to medium rare meat any time I come in the future, I'm giving you that extra meat star.

Aside from the meat problem, everything else is pretty great, but maybe not fantastic. Bacchanal excels in variety, as I thought there was something for everyone here. There's a salad section, various composed salads, and vegetarian dishes floating here and there. In order of what you see first coming from the entrance, here is some of what they were serving:

- Seafood (raw bar such as oysters, shrimp, snow crab legs, sea snails, river prawns, composed plates and hot items, soups)
- American/staple (fries, beans, Creole food, carvery meats, corn, bone marrow, rotisserie, potatoes, bread and grains)
- Mexican and Spanish (salsa bar, pozole, tortilla chips, chicharron, composed and made to order tacos, beans, plantains, horchata and other beverages, ceviches)
- Italian (composed plates, pastas, meatballs, steamed snow crab legs YESSS, breads and pizza)
- Salads and antipasto (various composed and tossed salads, charcuterie with several cheese types and dry cured meats, dried fruit and nuts)
- Asian (Thai noodles, curry, Filipino skewers, sushi, poke, Chinese soups, meats, and other dishes, dim sum)
- Dessert (kid desserts, cookies, cupcakes, fruits, gelato, donut wall, tons of mini desserts that I can't possibly name but desire to eat)

I loved how organized everything was. I did feel like the Asian section got shoved in a corner and thus, the quality of everything there also needed more attention. For example, they had Korean short ribs that were over sauced and too chewy, Filipino skewers that were too dry, and poke that was bland.

Highlight for me was definitely the steamed snow crab legs from the Italian section. That's gold. I saw a couple of tables with people who ONLY ate crab legs! Some of the items had a little too much flavor, salt, or sugar (cioppino), and some items did not (poke). I liked the variety of cold and hot seafood. The bone marrow is also a must get. The Italian pastas were al dente and had delicious sauces and flavor.

The dessert section is also luxurious, and I wish I had enough space to eat one of everything. They have basic desserts like cookies, jello, and whipped cream for people who like that, and miniatures of loads of different dessert types! I had a cheesecake bite that tasted more like bread pudding than cheesecake, but everything else were nice little samples of dessert. The lemon basil sorbet is the obvious superior frozen dessert choice.

Our server was very friendly, but maybe not available at all times. The Groupon deal is really useful here, as you basically pay the same price for a regular meal, but you skip the first line and get an extra drink. We got champagne and a mimosa, which were so smooth! We waited about 20 minutes in the second line on a Thursday at 3:30pm (first line is to wait and pay, second line is to be seated). The lines looked way too long when we got out, so good luck getting through that at normal hours...

Worth the money if you plan on eating a lot. Great variety of food. The quality wasn't anything amazing but definitely good for a buffet. Don't come if you can't eat a lot, spend $60 on a gourmet meal. Overall a pleasant experience

Sorry but this is over rated in my opinion. Compared to other Buffetts it's probably better but for $80 I wouldn't do it again. 

Food: So they have a good amount of options here and the quality was decent but it was not amazing. Some stuff was not good at all. Mostly the food was mediocre. 

Service/decor: It's a buffet so not much service here. The drinks take forever to come out so if you're thinking to do alcohol and think you're going to get a lot I wouldn't count on it

If you are reading this review that means currently, right now, sitting at almost 8000 reviews, my chances of you reading my review are somehow better than me winning any money in Vegas and I not only hate you, but hate my luck. Also this buffet is pretty good. 

Being at Caesars Palace means you have to eat like Caesar himself and boy does this buffet mean business when delivering the goods. If you are looking for your typical fried chicken and spaghetti types of food then you will not find that here. Every dish is more so gourmet and more often then not will impress even the most skeptical buffet haters. 

I could spend the next two hours naming off a million things that they have, but the end result is that if you are looking for an upscale buffet then look no further than the Bacchanal because it has a plethora of items that you wouldn't find on most restaurant menus.

At around $70 give or take the weekend, it isn't the best in value unless you can take down a good number of plates before you go. Of course that rule applies to pretty much any buffet.

This place is so good and worth the wait!

Went by myself in May for brunch and waited an hour for one person. It was beyond good and I walked out way too stuffed with so many good options to choose from!

I recently went again on a trip to Vegas with my girlfriend and we decided to go but for dinner!

We showed up around 5 and the line was incredibly long! We were given the option to put our name in and come back at 7 so we did! It gave us a chance to walk around Caesars and we ended up having a few drinks at the Mirage too. 

Finally, when we got back at 7 we still had to wait another hour but once we were in it was so worth it!

The food is amazing and totally worth it. Plus it's Vegas so it's not like there's nothing to entertain you when you're waiting! I can't wait to come back!

Admittedly this was my first and only experience with the upscale buffet options that are littered around Vegas, but I was both pleased and disappointed in ways I hadn't expected. Since there are so many aspects to this buffet, I'm just going to go over what I was happy with and what I would pass on if I were to go again.

First off, the good stuff. The crab legs were great. I opted for the cold to avoid the larger, slower line that was held up for the hot legs. I also found this gave me more opportunity to be picky about which legs I wanted, versus having to take a huge pile of them to keep the line moving. The crab legs were also great, as were the oyster & shrimp cocktail shooters. It was all fresh and the pre-cracked shells were done well, making meat extraction easy.

Also good were the (extremely) buttery mashed potatoes and the prime rib. The quality of the cuts seemed to vary a lot from what I could tell - mine was pretty mediocre, overcooked and really fatty, but someone else I was with had a beautiful, all pink, rare cut that was as close to a perfect cut as I've ever seen. It may be worth scoping out where they in the cut of meat before hopping in that line. I'd also start off with a healthy addition of pepper and salt to the meats as they seemed under-seasoned.

On the other hand, the jumbo shrimp and oysters (located by the Asian food, not the rest of the seafood) were probably some of the most bland pieces I've ever tasted. Shrimp needed a lot of sauce to make each bite worth it, and the oysters tasted like they were boiled - no saltiness, no flavor, just watery and gooey. 

While I was excited about the huge bowl of bone marrow, it was really hard to eat more than a little since I realized it was impossible to find any pieces of bread to spread it on to dilute the richness. I briefly considered the corn bread muffins, french fries, or slices of pizza to do the trick, but at that point I had already had so much rich food I just passed. It definitely needed a fair share of salt added as well.

So with the entrees being 50-50 as far as good/bad, I was optimistic that the deserts would be more reliable, and they were! I somehow managed to fill another whole plate with bites that were all great, such as the pumpkin creme brulee, thai iced tea with boba, sesame seed gelator, green tea and sesame seed (cake?) bite, guava shooter, green tea chocolate coated strawberry, etc. etc.

Knowing now what some of the best dishes were, I think I'd only feel compelled to return if I was really going to be dedicated to eating a purely seafood dinner with a large desert finish. However, it was a neat experience, if not overwhelming, with all of the options available. I avoided most foods I could regularly have anywhere else, but I am sure the sliders, fried chicken, pizza, etc. are all delicious. They're just not on my radar for a pricey buffet!

This is probably my favorite buffet in Vegas and I've been to most of the more well known ones including Wynn's buffet, Wicked Spoon, and Bacchanal, all of which are pretty good. None of these buffets are stellar if you consider a meal you might have gotten outside of a buffet where your one item is specially cooked for you for the the same price or less. At around $60 for your experience here at Bacchanal, the real value comes in variety like most buffets, but also in the quality you get. Receiving a prime rib slice from a buffet is a huge miss for me most of the time. Usually the meat is overly cooked or just plain dry, but here, the prime rib slice was actually medium rare just how i like it and had all the extras that you can get on the side, namely horseradish, cream, and au ju. The wait can get long, so definitely get here early.

It's not bad, but it's not great. I don't usually do buffets but this one was a treat. 

First you somewhat check in to receive a text to approach the line, that way you're not waiting in line for more than one hour when you could go grab an appetizer or drink while you wait. 

Once your called, you wait in an actual line that takes about an additional 10-15 minutes to get in. At this point, I could've eaten a cow! 

Once we got in, our hostess and servers were really nice and cute Hispanic ladies. 

We started out with the Asian food which was good...I was craving sushi which they had, pad Thai, Kung pao chicken and noodles. It was surprisingly good but not great. 

American sliders and roasted meats were out of this world...I only say that because I recently came back from being vegan for 3 years. The Seafood was a bit disappointing and wish I would've went to Milo's to have their grilled octopus. 

Dessert selection is quite beautiful however it seemed more cookies than anything else. But lucky me, creme brûlée was on the menu. 

I myself had 4 entree plates with generous portions and not mountain high status. Here's a tip to keep the food down, drink either hot tea or water while you eat. It keeps your metabolism going and digests the food a bit quicker. Cold drinks solidify your foods making you full quicker. Take that tip if you want to get your money's worth. 

Enjoy!

The food here is amazing!

The only problem is that if you aren't a platinum or up total rewards member, the wait can be dreadful.

However:
Food - Delicious, Huge variety. I usually start off with the hot crab legs (a cook hands you it fresh from the pot) and then work into all the amazing meats. The asian food is actually top-notch as well! Don't forget about the taco station. They make it fresh and hot customed to you! (I get the al pastor and carne asada mixed in one taco) 

Service - Amazing, We usually tip in advance, AND afterwards. It shows that you've tipped on the receipt when your seated so the waitress knows.

Dessert - They have their own dessert section in the middle filled with fresh fruits, and amazing exotic desserts -- macarons, build your own crepes, and a gelato bar! I usually ask for an extra crispy crepe with light nutella then I bring it over to the gelator bar and top it off with a scoop of gelato, add a mochi to the side, a macaron, and topped with fresh fruits.

If you go during brunch hours, bottomless mimosas! Man we get messed up here. Drinking and eating, life couldn't get any better. Always stop by at this buffet during my Las Vegas trip.

Located at Cesars Palace on the Las Vegas strip. I was staying at the Wynn so I just walked over. It was a 15 minute walk each way so not too bad. Just head straight in and past the slot machines towards the back, you can't miss it. We went to the breakfast buffet at 9AM on Sunday with a two hour limit so we got part of the lunch buffet.  There was no wait to be seated but as we left at 11AM there was quite the line.  Typical buffet with a large variety of above average food. I enjoyed coffee and a mimosa plus you get a free glass of champagne if you check in on yelp! I had a little bit of breakfast food and small variety of meats.  The meats were delicious and not over done plus the service was quick and attentive. Plus they have my favorite crab legs! Yes!! And they cut them in half making it so easy to enjoy!  I'd come back here for sure, come with an empty stomach lots of great food here.

Been here couple of times and this place always makes me full. Last time we went the prices was $50 per person but don't like that bother you. I really recommend that you go in with an empty stomach to get your money worth. They have the different types of food from many places. I wish I took pictures but maybe next time. During the main times such as lunch and dinner could get busy. So I highly suggest to go in between those times so you're not on line for quite a while. I like to start off the Asian side and work my way back to the front where the bbq and other meats are at. If you want to get warm crab legs go to the Italian side. And don't forget about dessert. Crepes or gelato will always have space in my tummy. Attached to Cesar casino so parking you may have to pay. Customer service is alright. Never had a complaint about them yet.

I would travel the two thousand miles to Vegas just for this buffet.

Okay, maybe that's exaggerating. But seriously, this food is fantastic. This buffet is very expensive and can get busy, but the food is worth it. Many finer restaurants charge $80 for a single a la carte steak, but at this buffet, you can eat as much steak as you want! The lamb here was absolutely fantastic, possibly the best tasting dish I've ever had. I definitely recommend eating here if you're in Vegas.
Waited an hour and a half to get in, paid $140 for two and the food was bland... it would have been $30 more just to have house alcohol.

Such an amazing buffet!! My girls and i were in hog heaven. There is so many different types of food: Asian, Mexican, American... Oysters and fancy meats and cheeses. The desserts were gorgeous and at no other buffet that I've been to do they hand scoop gelato and serve it to you :-P

Came on Sunday at 11:15 AM.  Seating system sucks.  Had a sign stating 5 or more  people get in this line and see cashier.  Waited in the other line with 4 people and an infant. (My bad I guess.  Should have counted the baby.) Parties of 5 or more paid more quickly however, were put into a line to be seated.  So we waited in the regular line then got put at the back of the line of the 5+ behind 5 groups that all technically got there after us.  We finally get to the front of the line and they start seating parties of 7 and 8 behind us.  They did this 4 different times while we were at the front of the line.  Then we were sat at a four top anyway.... The food is plated to look fancy but I swear I have had equal quality food at Golden Corral buffet (at a better price than $60 per person.) Long lines for the meat station and subpar food at best.  The bathroom was discussing as well.  6 stalls for a line of people and 2 of them were unusable because they were so dirty.  Ugh!  This place was rated #1 brunch buffet in Vegas... Very disappointed..
1 and a half hour wait and $115.00 later and it was so worth it, the selection of food was fantastic and it tasted twice as good as it looked!!! would love to go back again and again!

Omg this place is amazing. I was crying inside when I became stuffed and couldn't try more dishes. The hot crab legs and drawn butter was a nice touch. I have eaten at the wynn, cosmo and rio buffet. The bacchanal buffet definitely wins in this category. There is always a line so be prepared and wear pants with extra room.

Above average Vegas buffet. The price is on par with other buffets at big hotels in the strip. But the selection here and the quality of the food is mostly  good. 

Our party was 13 people at about 3pm on a Saturday 
The wait was about 45 mins. After you pay, they have you stand in a separate line for big parties to wait to be seated. 

Snow Crab Legs were tasty. They're served cold and steamed. I thought the cold was better than the steamed ... not the prevailing opinion. The liquid butter dispenser is near the station for steamed crab legs. No more King crab legs though. Apparently they stopped serving them like 8 months ago. The Lobster Claws' meat was a little overdone/over-steamed. Kinda tough. The cocktail shrimp was perfect. Chilled not frozen. The Brisket was very very good ... succulent and tender, great flavor. The Risotto with Escargot was ok. I wish it was saltier or more buttery or garlicy. The Oysters were not bad. Pretty standard oysters. 

Duck bone marrow ... nope! The marrow was too loose. Just had the texture of fat. The Poke cup was light and flavored well. The Drunken Noodles were pretty good but were way way spicy. The Thai Basil Fried rice was pretty good too and worth a try. The Asian Crab was pretty good! But it was just so much work for not enough meat. The sauce makes it messy too. The Guacamole lacked enough lime flavor, but at least it's made with real avocado so all is good. The Spanish rice and beans were terrific. The Mexican corn was wonderful. 

Gelato was tasty. Strawberry flavor was pretty good. So was the mango. The olive lemon was way too olivey for me. Overpowering. The banana cream pie was not good. Tasted like banana puree out of a can and was lacking the airiness and whipped texture that it should have had. 

Check in on Yelp and get a complimentary champagne, beer, or wine. There's a small men's and women's restroom by the entrance. They are very busy though, so if you're looking for privacy after a big buffet meal, look elsewhere. It's not too crowded in the restaurant despite the line to be seated being really long. 

Would probably come back for the crab legs alone.

Food was delicious.  Great variety of different cuisine.  But i thought it was way over priced.  We went the day before Thanksgiving trying to avoid the long lines and the high price but they charged us a 'pre Holiday Price of I believe was $69.  It also took us an hour in line for us to be seated.

There is a new "Fast Pass" like system for busy days. On weekends and holidays, you need to first "check in" at. Kiosk to receive a return wait time for the entire party to wait for a table. They text the lead persons phone when a table will be ready. This allows your party To go to the forum shops or gamble while you wait instead of wait in line. One bad thing is on super busy days  expect to get a pass time only to return 2+ hours later. Try to call to see wait time if anything. 

The food is still good and the service is also still very attentive! Kudos for maintaining food and service quality!

Pretty good as far as buffets go, but a bit disappointing for the price (i.e. it's not sufficiently different from a $40 buffet to be worth going to).

Where you enter there is a raw bar with oysters and clams as well as (cooked) shrimp and crab; they're of comparable quality to an appetizer ordered in a typical seafood restaurant. Then there is a carvery offering prime rib, brisket, wagyu round, and bacon, which you can expect a short line for. All the meats were good except the round, which was undercooked and barely chewable. The longest line is for the freshly boiled crab legs in the Italian section; you might wait 10 minutes for your crab legs, but rest assured the wait is worth it.

The Chinese section can be hit-or-miss; the stir-fried vegetables were surprisingly good, but many of the meats/seafood were not fresh. The dessert section had a lot of variety and were beautifully laid out, offering traditional favorites like tiramisu, cheesecake, mousse, and creme brulee as well as some of their own creations.

Hmmm.. Not sure what the hype is about. This place is overpriced and nothing to show for. I wanted to try this place because of the reviews, but honestly I am glad the dinner was company expense, or else, I probably would have been upset to have spent $65, personally.
