Literally, I only liked 2 items from that place. The fried elotes bites and the mango tapioca dessert. Everything else was something I could have experienced at a place like golden corral, furr's, or whatever $10 buffet restaurant people go to. I feel like the restaurant have so many different types of cuisine available, they just make it quickly without thinking of the quality and taste of the food. Also, I don't really like the idea they had some elk meat to compensate for the cost of the buffet, when the elk meat is suppppperrrrr dry and no flavor. Only thing that was worth some cost of the buffet is the king crab legs, if this wasn't available it would have been, even more of a waste of money and calories.

Because they deleted my first review, I have lowered the starts to just one. (I will copy and paste this one in a word document so I can continue to post it as often as I have to until they stop removing it)

After coming to Las Vegas for numerous years and having the pleasure of being able to eat at numerous places I finally tried the famous buffet at Caesars Palace and I cannot tell you what a disappointment it was. Understanding that buffets are hit and miss I normally steer clear but the popularity of this one was too much of a draw - save your time and more importantly your money.

The food was mediocre at best, the tables and floors were strewn with dirty dishes and debris on the floor and the servers we stretched to thin to actually service the tables.

Huge disappointment.

If you are looking for a buffet to visit in Vegas this is the place to go!

It has a ton of selection to choose from. There is a nice seafood selection and cut crab legs so it's easy to peel. The carving station offered tons of selection of meats we had prime rib, brisket, and even wagyu need to choose from!

If you wanted the hot snow crab legs you have to go to the Italian section (odd yes) but you can get the hot snow crab legs to choose from

The Asian section has a nice selection dim sum to choose from and there is poke bowls and scallops that were quite delicious as well!

There was an amazing selection of desserts also so pace yourself to get yourself to the desserts! There are a ton of gelato flavors to choose from and definitely did not disappoint!

Service was on point always prompt!

Overall had a great time there and it was a great buffet to choose while in vegas!

I came here in a group of 6 people around 11am on a Monday morning - almost no wait and the service was great! 

In terms of food here, I was not really impressed. As someone who doesn't eat red meat, the value for the buffets in Vegas lies in the seafood. However, the seafood served at this time was just shrimp and crab claws (which were stringy and very hard to crack). A lot of the dishes were cold/bland (I'm talking about you, Pad Thai). I did enjoy the smoked salmon and stuffed sweet potatoes however! 

Dessert wise, this place blew away my expectations. The gelato was creamy and delicious (and tasted a lot more authentic than I was expecting). Also notably yummy was the little Vietnamese coffee cup. Had a blast at the crepe station as well! 

Overall, I had a much better experience at Wicked spoon eating crab legs (easier to crack and more worth the price) for a lot less $$. I left Bacchanal satisfied and glad I came, but probably wouldn't go back.

I have tried almost every buffet on the strip.

Decided to take the hit and paid $50 for dinner.

Bacchanal is definitely the best on the strip.  They have everything and their Asian food is actually very good!  Jumbo shrimp, king crab, tiny lobster, sushi that is not full of rice, noodle soup that actually tastes very good, very delicious dessert, etc.

They even take a picture of you before you enter like it's an attraction.

BUT I can't recommend it at $50.  The value is just not there.  You will be just as happy at the Wicked Spoon or the Wynn buffet or the Bellagio buffet for 20%+ less.

You'll be busy trying to get your moneys worth.  The people around me were done eating, but it seemed like they were waiting to digest so they can fit in more.  The receipt states to "please limit your stay to 2 hours"

The restroom is to the right of the exit and yes, you can re-enter after you unload.

Your friends will be excited to go, but won't talk about how good it was.  They'll just talk about how they went to this $50 experience.  Ask them which food item specifically was better than other buffets?

If you are visiting Vegas, I highly recommend this buffet! Heck, if you live in Vegas you should try this buffet. It's one of the best buffets I've ever been to. 

First, let's start with the pricing. It's $64.99 per person during dinner and $54.99 during lunch. There is a known trick if you want to pay lunch prices and still eat their dinner. Since dinner starts at 3pm, I would recommend getting in line at 1:30-2pm since the wait can be quite long. And voila! You'll pay the lunch price and still get to try their dinner. The first time I came it was just my hubby and I, the wait was about two hours. The second time I came with a group of five the wait was only 20ish minutes. They have a separate waiting area for groups of five or more. I'm not sure why this is, maybe to get the lines moving faster? 

THE FOOD... delicious. I am a big crab lover but I HATE opening them. Here, they already had it sliced open so my lazy self was able to eat it without much effort. I recommend the hot crab legs more than the cold ones because the hot crab legs were less salty. However, you do have to use the crab opener to open these ones. The oysters were yummy and their seafood paella was superb. They had a wide selection of soups such as ramen and pho. My husband, who is a big pho lover, said the pho was pretty good. They have almost everything you can imagine: dumplings, poke, pasta, menudo, tacos, fried chicken, prime rib, short rib, pizza. Their dessert bar is a diabetes persons dream! My favorite was the creme brûlée and macaroons. Also, there was a lady making crepes.

The only reason for a four star rather than a five is the ridiculously long lines to enter, the line for seafood, the line for crepes. Literally, a line for almost everything. But if you are patient, it's definitely worth the wait.

Bachannal used to be my go-to Las Vegas buffet joint, but not anymore...

Waited 3 hours on a holiday weekend dinner to finally sit down & eat. Devoured the prime rib & snow crabs to get my money's worth. The pistachio gelato & Nutella crepes were delicious. Other than that, nothing else caught my eye. Some of their holiday menu items were MIA (i.e lamb, salmon). Beware of their oysters- not as fresh as it looks. It had a cake-like texture to it.

I would never pay $75/per person with tax included ever again.

I have to give it up for BB, it is the best buffet I have had in Las Vegas.

The computer kiosk to sign in was down, so we just stood on line for about 20 minutes after paying and were seated.....table of 5, $60.00 per person.

The Asian section features food from Japan, China, and sort of a mix from there, the Italian section has pastas made to order, plenty of antipasti to choose from as well.

There is a hot seafood section and a cold seafood section.  I mixed the mussels, baked cod and clams with chorizo together and it was pretty danged tasty.

The little bits of pork belly were a resounding success and our cholesterol levels must have peaked that night.  The carving station had a long line, my friends said the beef was excellent.

A  double Captain and Coke in a tall glass is $30.00, so watch the drinking.....soft drinks are included in the cost.

The dessert station was truly awesome....I had a couple opera cakes and about 6 macarons.  Considering that most of the joints around Las Vegas are charging about two bucks each for macarons, dessert alone represented a fair deal.

I don't do a lot of buffets anymore because when I'm done, all I want to do is sleep, but for an annual trip to Las Vegas, you probably won't find a better buffet.

Good food. Each section is dedicated to its own type of good. Mexican, italian, sushi, etc... Service was decent. Took a little bit to get drinks. Crab legs were OK. They didn't have the butter marked and it took a little bit to find because it wasn't adjacent to the crab legs like you would expect. 

They ask you to limit your stay two-hours. That may seem like a long period, but it does go pretty fast, but it's long enough to get plenty of food. 

I probably wouldn't recommend paying the extra for the unlimited drinks though. You'll be more focused on eating than drinking.

My Goodness Gracious!!!! This buffet puts an end to all buffets! If you love buffets and don't mind serving yourself you ALMOST NEED to come here. If you're not a fan of self service well it really doesn't matter, you'll still love the place. 

It's tucked in the old and cluster-phobic Cesar's palace hotel. However, this buffet is High class on its own. I was not shocked to see a crazy line up on a Tuesday night at around 17:00! It was packed. However, there's a wonderful trick to cut the line called "the express no wait line" for 25$ extra per person you get to cut the line ;). The place is so organized! 

The food: beyond belief! It was Fresh!!! High end quality! A whole seafood raw bar with shrimps, lobster, crabs, clams, mussels & OYSTERS!!! They had an insane amount of food and they kept stocking new and better food every 5-10 minutes or less if it was running out.

Service was phenomenal! I was so impressed and so happy to have been able to check this place out. It is a matter of fact the best buffet in The USA!! :p

Easily the best I've had here in Vegas!! The pastry chef was amazing and send me a special for my birthday ! The food was absolutely amazing and the selection was so large I literally didn't make it to all the stations! I'm coming back every time I'm in town !!

We came here for lunch and I was kinda hoping for the best because of all the wonderful reviews I read, but I thought it was just OK. I've honestly been to better buffets for less the cost. Maybe the selection of food wasn't that great because it was lunch and not dinner... or maybe I'm just being too picky.

BTW, I was impressed with their dessert selection! Everything from crepes to macarons to chocolate covered strawberries... yum!!!
Love this place breakfast is amazing. Sea food is fresh and personal is super friendly

I'm not typically one for a buffet but holy seafood. I ate my heart out and took advantage of the raw bar of shrimp, crab legs, oysters, and other great seafood. Worth the money. The only downfall is seriously long lines- I think they can do a better job at facilitating the lines.

A solid buffet. Tons of options, and many different cuisines and everything tastes great. One downside is that if you are a vegetarian, then there's no need to spend this much amount of money to come here - you're going to have at least 4-5 options. I've tried both the dinner and the brunch, and although I'm personally a brunch guy, I did think the dinner was just over the top good, as compared to the brunch. Especially if you're a seafood eater, this is the place to be.

The buffet is slightly better than others but it doesn't take away from the fact they they offer low quality food items. Their only saving grace is the dessert selection which were surprisingly decent for a buffet.

The service is a typical buffet service, meaning next to none. The wait time isn't horrible if you come odd hours or else you'll be herded like cattles.

Save yourself some money and go get better food elsewhere that's not a buffet.

Bacchanal is the buffet to eat, drink, and be merry as you gorge yourself with delicious food from an array of cuisine. Brunch and dinner here are both good, each having certain highlights. 

Dinner: Raw oysters freshly shucked, plates of steamed crab legs, ceviche 

Brunch: Bottomless champagne/mimosas (extra $15 a person)

Both: Prime rib, wagyu beef sliders (melt in your mouth), exotic gelato flavors, really good dessert overall. 

Tips: there is a bathroom inside which is likely to have shorter lines, some items are featured on signs that you have to ask for (i.e. thai tea float), and you can make your own mimosas/bellinis by asking for champagne, drinking a bit, and then using other juice flavors like pineapple/mango/peach!

$62+/person after tax for this crap is definitely a waste of time. We arrived circa 1945 & waited to get paged to get in line then another hour to pay & get seated.  We finally get to grab food around 2100.  Selection is definitely of wide variety.  Dishes & desserts look decadent. But flavors? Wrong & inconsistent.  First batch of clam chowder...best I've ever had, 2nd bowl from a different batch was missing clams & tasted sour.  Steaks overcooked & cold.  I'm sure there was more the be had if only I was given more time & opportunity.  Service was the worst - only saw her when I have had to stop the manager who happens to be walking by.  To make the experience even more horrific?  They started cleaning up & took food away while there were still plenty of people. No consideration how much money people paid for this trashy experience.  We were basically given less than 2 hours to "enjoy" this buffet they describe as "premium". Don't waste your money, enjoy a peaceful dinner at a steak house where you don't have to fight for food, lines, tables & service.

We were staying at Caesars Palace so we thought that we would go to the Bacchanal Buffet for breakfast. The signage promised all kinds of high end dishes so I was looking forward to a gourmet breakfast and wasn't too nervous about the $40 each price tag... what a mistake! They had NONE of the tantalizing high end dishes anywhere! It was just your 'run-of-the-mill' buffet that was worth only about $7 each. If I could have rated zero stars I would have! Save your money and go somewhere good! You have been warned!

Bacchanal Buffet is always a favorite during any of my Vegas excursions. Super pricey- depending on the time of day the price can range between $40 and $60, however the selection of food is insane!

This place has everything from crab legs and oysters, tacos, Chinese fried rice, sushi rolls, pizza, açaí bowls, etc. Meal portion aside, there is also an extravagant desert selection as well.

The food itself is great for buffet food- wouldn't necessarily call it gourmet, but definitely worth the price- it's hard to leave and not be stuffed because there is TOO MUCH FOOD! 

The line to wait can get kind of crazy, but star card owners can skip the line. I would advise to not come here during prime lunch hours!

If I can give this place a big fat zero I would! First off Rosa at the front was so busy fixing her hands that my family and I wanted her to explain the buffet of buffet that she did such a piss poor job of doing it.  I almost had to explain to my niece and I stopped myself and told her "why the hell am I going your job for you".  Then the food OMG it was such a let down.  The variety is so dismal it was not even worth the price.  The taste is a hit or miss. Bottom line is the price and hype is not worth a dime!! Spend your money somewhere else.

Fresh and clean buffett. This place was one of the restaurants I wanter to visit when I was in Vegas. Normally my wife and I are not buffet fans but we heard so many good things from others so we tried it. They have a great waiting and seating order that helps makes things run smooth. The front area staff was amazing. 

My only negative was that it was hard trying to get someone to refill our drinks. 

The food was fresh and they had great variety.  I ate mostly the seafood and meat station. The staff there were all friendly. Their crab legs where amazing. The meat was fresh and cooked just right. The deserts where so good. They had so many choices which was a bonus for my wife. She likes to try many things and their portion sizes where just perfect for her. Def a place ill come back to in the future.

Over priced! Over rated! Over hyped! UNDER SEASONED!

Under seasoned?  Every dish I tried at Bacchanal was extremely bland.  The seafood tasted over boiled.  The Asian dishes were over cooked and mushy.  The desserts were extremely artificial.  For what Bacchanal charges per head for dinner, they really should have better food.  I was so disappointed with our experience here, I lost my appetite immediately after round 1 of food stuffing.

The service was questionable.  Since wifey and I paid for an upgrade in our Buffet of Buffets voucher, we paid tip in advanced.  Never did anyone stop by our table to offer refills on soda, which was warm btw!  It took flagging down the staff to clear our table of plates as well!  

Such a poor experience. I'm happy for everyone who got good food and great service, I unfortunately was not in that crowd. Womp womp.

Buffet was outstanding! The chicken and waffles was mouthwatering and the steak and eggs was to die for. There wasn't anything our group of 4 had that wasn't absolutely wonderful. Lily kept the mimosas flowing and was an absolute delight, anticipating our every need. Incredible service and food all around. 5 out of 5! Ask for Lily, she's the best!

Do not understand how this was voted #1. They up sell you to unlimited wine and beer but they fail to mention it's only house wine let alone the fact it took 20 minuets to get first glass of house wine and 20 minuets for the second at which point I was done eating poor service. Some of the crab legs were still frozen hard to eat that.  Went to the Asian section for Pho and they did not have any noodles,  the chef said hold on and went into fridge opened 3 packs quickly ran them under warm water threw them in a bowl with three small pieces of beef and then poured broth on it are you kidding me. Stay away plenty of better places for less than the $70 they soak you for.

I normally hate buffets because it's really germ fest! However the price of this buffet did the job for me! I will say this is one of the best buffets in Vegas. What place do you know has sliced crab legs? Only in Vegas! The price was moderate and I would gladly pay it again because this is not your Golden Corral. You are seated and you have a server that makes sure your table is clean after each plate. There was a 2 hour time limit and I wish I had enough room to use all of it. My eyes were definitely bigger than my stomach because I didn't eat close to half of what they offered. Can't wait to go back!

The worst service I ever had in my life. The waitress never take away our finish plate. Even the drink I need to ask from the front desk.The most funniest part is when the waitress pass me drink just walk right away. Overall, the food is good but the customer service just threw me off the appetite.

One word: Over-hyped.

I've been to various buffets throughout Las Vegas and had high expectations based on reviews.
The wait was about an hour typical for a buffet in Vegas. Food was average at best, many similar stations at other buffets. The dessert station was probably the best station there. Would recommend only if you never ate at a buffet in Las Vegas before but other than that save your money and eat else where like at the RiO.

It is over rated and over priced.  It must have been a holiday weekend.  We paid about $85 per person and tax and tip came out to be $550 for party of 5 including kids.  I don't believe there was kids price.  Their Asian food was very dry and had no taste. I would had the same quality food for $15 in my town. I give 1 star for the Asian section. 3 star for American. 5 star for the dessert.  Overall, 2 star.

This place used be the best when first opened. Not anymore. Be aware many pictures in this posting are not serving anymore! 
Paid $79 for special but all I can see special is long long line to get in. It's a beautiful place but paying  $400 for a family dinner is not worth it.

There is king crabs, meat, pizza, and Chinese food. No salad bar, no sushi bar, no pasta bar, no fruit bar!!   Dessert used to be the best ahain, when first opened but now this place is nothing more than others.

Not worth for 4 hour wait plus $60~80!

Really enjoyed the buffet hear. I don't think their set up is efficient to handle the all the people that flock in. But big crowds mean they are doing something right. The brisket was so darn good. I wanted to keep coming back for more. Jonah crabs and snow crabs were good as well. The pork was way too salty for me. And the crawfish was okay. I has better. Enjoyed this place for the experience. But I prefer the buffet at the Rio.

I am surprised how people are obsessed about Bacchanal buffet. It's not even worth it in my opinion. I paid $140 plus tax for dinner, expecting good food and good service. However, most of the dishes tastes even worse than $30 buffet. Seriously!!! Not worth to try and get in line!!! Not recommended for sure.

The food was great and the people working there were wonderful.
My mother in law is very old - Miss Perez and Taylor - the general manager and the manager were very helpful. I can not wait to go back.

The wait was long, nothing too crazy especially for Vegas. I had mostly meats, and deserts. The 16 hour smoked brisket was great, but I found most of the other meats to be lacking in flavor. All the stations were clean and had a neat appearance. The sweets were all great. Typical options, and presented well. Over all I have to say one of the best places I have eaten in vegas. 4 stars.
Amazing food- loved the sushi! The dessert table is also great. Lots of variety. Our waitress Esmeraldo was the best! She was the best mixture of friendly, professional and helpful.

Finally broke my Bacchanal Buffet virginity, and I'm sad to say that this place has been over hyped.. Or maybe I just had too high of a standard for this place because of everyone's reviews about it. 

My family and I went during dinner - around 3pm, so there was almost no wait time. Walking in, I thought this place was quite impressive. The decoration was beautiful. I've never seen a buffet decorated like this! 

We got seated, told the waiter our drink order, and left to get food. 

--- 1st serving: 

- Lo Mein noodles: Pretty yummy. Just the way I love my Asian noodles to taste like! Noodles weren't dry and it was pretty flavorful. 
- Salmon Nigiri: Can I just say.. YUM?! The salmon was nice and buttery. It tasted so good and fresh! But can I just say that the rice tasted TOO vinegary for my liking.
- Kalbi ribs: Ehhh... Taste was yummy and very bbq-y BUT the meat was rubbery :( that killed it for me.
- Edamame: Pretty good; wish it had a little bit more flavor to it though.
- Penne alla vodka: HOLY YUM. I wish I got more of this, but I wanted to try bits and pieces of everything before I got insanely full. 

--- 2nd serving:

- Oysters & crab legs: Mmm, my favorite seafood ever. So good! Though I wish the crab legs were a bit more meaty though. The ones at the Carnival buffet at Rio had more meat and were a bit more flavorful than the ones here.
- Beer-battered shrimp: Not my favorite.. And I LOVE BEER. I was expecting these to taste like heaven but the shrimps were too overcooked so the meat stuck to the shell. I don't know about you, but I want to eat ALL of my shrimp meat.
- Cocktail shrimp: I prefer the ones at the Carnival buffet better. Sure the shrimps here were ginormous but the flavor was not.
- Corn on the cob: BEST CORN OF THE COB. HANDS DOWN. 

As for the dessert, THIS WAS MY FAVORITE PART! It was like every single item I got was a little part of heaven going into my mouth. So good! 

--- Service: I thought the service was poor :( They took forever to get the plates off of our table. Not to mention they also failed to refill our drinks. I don't know if I'm spoiled or what, but I like it when my server is pro-active. They see an empty glass, they refill it. Simple as that right? I don't have to sit in my chair for an extra 5-10 minutes just looking around and waiting for ANY server to pass by just so I can get a refill of my peach iced tea. I understand that they get busy, but don't neglect your guests in the process of that for 20 almost 30 minutes sometimes! 

Anyway, I would go back.. If I won the lottery. This place is WAY TOO overpriced. $200 for 4 people for Saturday dinner. Yeah. OVERPRICED. When I could go to Carnival buffet for HALF of that price AND eat amazing quality foodies!
So many varieties of delicious food.A bit pricy $145 for two but worth every penny.Lines can get really hectic at times.

This is by far my favorite buffet in Las Vegas.
I've eaten here twice now and I must say that each time was well worth the $$$ and the full stomach. My friends and I decided to try it the first time because it had just opened and we wanted to see if it lived up to the Vegas Buffet standards; it did. Over a year and a half later, I dragged my entire family to eat att this buffet because of the positive experience I had the first time.

It's around $65 for weekend dinner buffet (that price included tax and 18% gratuity for my 8+ party), but they have such a vast variety of the food and wonderful presentation for each of the dishes that the price doesn't stop me from wanting to go back even as I'm writing this review.

They have several different types of food stations (going right to left from what I can remember) chinese, dim sum, sushi, made to order ramen, pho, udon, salad bar, cheese bar, pasta, pizza, mexican, the mexican fruit juices (i loved), soup, bread, meat - lamb, prime rib, fried chicken, etc., mashed potatoes, macaroni and cheese, fresh seafood, and dessert in the center of the restaurant. It's awesome. 

They also gave each of us at the table a complimentary glass of wine which was nice.

Loved both of my dining experiences here and I will definitely be back!

MY BUFFET RESUME: The Wynn, Wicked Spoon, Bellagio, the M, the Rio

And now...the Bacchanal!

THE HIGHLIGHTS: What you really go here for are the oysters and the crab legs. Crab legs are meaty, and you have the choice of either having them cold or steamed depending on your preference. The oysters are the best I've had from any buffet in Vegas. They have a large supply of the smaller sweeter oysters that are not briney.  Why in your right mind would you eat giant raw oysters is beyond me! The cocktail shrimp...wow! They are massive and perfectly cooked! Slightly sweet with that perfect bouncy consistency without it being hard and rubbery. Obviously I spent most of my time eating seafood, but other memorable things were the Posole, Mushroom Risotto, and what I believe was Raspberry Panna Cotta.

BE SMART, PAY LESS: Like any seasoned Vegas buffet-goer. Come here right at the end of lunch, pay lunch price, eat dinner food. If you are coming here for a weekend trip try to squeeze this in on a Friday. The lines are short and won't be swarming with people who just woke up from a long night of raging and are grumpy and hungry. 

There is a line to pay, then a line to wait to get in. Dinner starts at 3pm so as long as you pay before then, you are good to go. I came here on the Friday of Labor Day weekend and we arrived around 2:40, paid within minutes (around $32 plus tax per person), and were in by a little after 3. Extremely pleased! 

THE LET DOWN: I was extremely disappointed in the meats! There was a wide variety such as different types of ribs and prime rib and sausages but there was SO much of it sitting out it didn't look appetizing or fresh. My first piece of prime rib was way too salty and well done so I went back and asked for a rarer piece to give it another chance. Nope, still no go. I also tried a KC style rib...extremely dry. Wynn and Bellagio, although not as fancy in presentation anymore compared to Bacchanal and Wicked spoon, still win in the meats department. Less variety there but better quality. 

FANCY SHMANCY AMBIENCE: Ambience is beautiful. Take time to take it all in while you are taking a digestion-break, you paid for it! Half of the space is based on glass elements with actual drinking glasses/vases used as the lighting fixtures and the back half is all based with wood elements as the walls, ceilings, etc. 

DIVERSE CUISINE: Seafood section (mussels, crab legs, oysters, seafood paella, lobster rolls), "American" cuisine (sliders, fried chicken, mac n cheese), Mexican cuisine (tacos made in front of you, delicious posole), Italian (variety of pastas, chicken marsala, meatballs), Asian (duck, kbbq, made to order udon and ramen, dim sum) and much more!

CONCLUSION: $32 well spent! Not sure if i'd pay the dinner price of $50+ for it though. SO COME EARLY! GRUB ON MY FRIENDS :)

I'm not really a Vegas Strip kinda guy. I'm also not really a buffet kinda guy. But I figured if I'm going to be here, I have to try one of the famous buffets, right?

And guess what? It wasn't terrible! In fact, it was pretty darn good. 

PROS:
-It's beautiful! Everything is absolutely gorgeous.
-The people cooking the food are all delightful and super helpful.
-The food itself really is delicious. There is something for everyone--from a big carnivorous meat station, to everything Asian, to Mexican street tacos. I didn't have a single item that was subpar. 
-They are very gluten-free friendly! In a city where I was hard-pressed to find gf goodies, Bacchanal gets it right. Especially at the desserts! (Just ask.)

 CONS:
-It's expensive. There's no way on earth I'm ever going to eat enough to even remotely cover the cost.
-I didn't think the service staff was very attentive. I definitely needed refills more often than they cared to stop by. And you tip when you pay--before eating... so they knew I had tipped well. Not really sure what the problem was.

I don't think this is something I'd do on every trip to LV, but I absolutely think it's worth doing the first time!

Wow this buffet was amazing and well worth every penny from the great food to the outstanding customer service. All kinds of cultural foods freshly made on the spot, including a whole dessert bar. Now that I have tried out this buffet I will be coming here every time I visit Vegas.
Friendly front desk and very clean environment! Jennifer is an amazing server! We will come back every Vegas trip
Back two weeks later for dinner only to be more impressed. Though expensive, absolutely everything is amazing. Best buffet in Vegas.

So disappointed with this buffet.  It supposedly had all these "greatest buffet" reviews and titles, but it was just so mediocre we felt we wasted $56/pp.   The wait to get a table at 4:45 was 45 minutes long, and they kept letting VIP members through immediately so our wait in line was even longer.   Once seated, no one came by to take our drink orders (not even water on the table) until we got up and flagged somebody down.  If you're there for just the crab legs and oysters (which we weren't) maybe it's worth it, otherwise don't waste your money!!  Also, the line for the BBQ was so long it wasn't worth getting back into.

A must go when visiting Vegas. It's a pricy meal but worth it. The experience is exciting and the food is actually good (compared to buffet food elsewhere). I would also recommend getting the champagne bundle!

I finally did it! I went to Baccanal! We went on a Saturday afternoon, 3pm actually right as they were changing over to dinner. There was almost no line at all and we were pretty much seated right away. When we were coming out at 5pm there wasn't much line yet either, so for a Saturday I would say timing key to avoiding long wait times and lines. Between 3pm and 5pm seemed like a great slow time to go. I didnt like how they seated us tho. We paid and then we're told to stand in another line with some other people who had also already paid( about 3 tables worth of people I think) they said " follow the line" so we did all through the seating area, at one point for whatever reason the line stopped moving and I was stuck in between 2 tables it was quite awkward I felt like my butt was in people's faces and that I was invading their space. For as much money as it cost ($140.00 for 2 people PLUS tip) I don't think being seated party by party is too much to ask, where the hostess asks you how you are doing and it's like welcoming and stuff. This didn't feel warm or welcoming, I didn't like it. Now the food. The food was good, for sure the highest quality of buffet food I have had. Everything tasted good and not cheap if that makes sense. no canned peaches in this buffet. They have some crazy stuff, like escargot ( snails, cold and in the shell), raw oysters and oyster shooters, plenty of shrimp cocktail, cold crab legs and steamed crab legs, they have fancy meats and a lamb steak thing, they has a station to get fresh made tacos, they had sushi and lots of asian food, and lots of little cute already plated small things. And what I will also say is they have actual good desserts. Desserts at buffets drive me crazy because they always look so good but taste like garbage! Even at Bellagio. But at Baccanal they were actually great and there is soooo much. So I give them that. It was quality and it wasn't bad but it still feels overpriced to me. But most things on the strip are overpriced so it makes sense. I am glad I finally got to experience eating here, it was a bucket list moment for sure. But I wish I had been more wowed. I wish they had more fancy little plated things. And I don't really eat meat, like steak and stuff but if you're a meat person you can for sure get your money's worth.  They even have bone marrow. Fancy weird shit. I ate about a million crab legs and some fancy deviled eggs lol and tried a bunch of stuff. I almost feel like I should leave 4 stars but I'm going to give it 3 because it IS so expensive and for that price I would want better service and for the food to like blow my mind and it didn't. I got crab legs so I'm happy. You can go to Texas De Brazil for 50 bucks and the service is AMAZING and you really get the 5 star treatment and it's all you can eat, has a buffet and is bomb .com.  I'm just saying.

**Please Read**
I've been recommending this place to my family that always come to visit. After Friday nights dinner, I'm just so shocked on how much it went downhill. 
First off,the lines were not as crazy as it used to be. After telling my family that there may be a 2 hr. wait time, it was only 5 mins. That should have been a red flag, even after reading negative reviews. 
There were a lot of dishes that was still authentic and good, but we came for the crabs. It's was horrible. For the ridiculous high price, we should have gone to a sit down dinner. The quality was another factor. They were thin and not at all tasty. They were the same  ones you get at the cheap Chinese Crazy buffet which you pay around $12. 
We had to flag down the waiter to clear our table and get refills. We even cleared it ourselves by putting it on trays. 
I've been to many buffets and now this one, is on the bottom of my go to list.
Another factor, and I pointed it out to the waiter, a table full of Alaskan King crab legs all wasted. He said they were only for the VIP's. They should have a special area for them and not be up front where people are looking at it. **So, Bacchanal will not recommended**

Las Vegas is known for their buffets, and this is one where you get great value!
***
Locals  
Almost no locals would come here. Overpriced for a normal meal, but if you're willing to wait long lines, great for a celebration. 
***
Travelers 
There are many buffets in Las Vegas, but this is one of the more famous ones. They are situated in Caesar's Palace, and there are very few signs on how to get here, but ask around and you'll see a crowd of people and you're there! They have kiosks that give you times on when to line up, wait based on size of party, pay, then enter and eat up!
***
My Recommendation 
You can get crab legs, oysters, clams, bone marrow, and food from many different cuisines. Like most buffets, you should always prioritize the big ticket items. Go for the gold! Coming on the weekdays, you can get a cheaper price and avoid the crowds.

IG: @foodisseur

Nothing less than amazing!

This buffet is located within the Caesars palace. My girlfriend and I came around 8pm on a weekday and the regular entrance line was moving pretty quickly albeit it was rather lengthy. Thankfully I used the Caesars diamond line and my wait was short. Once in, the stewardess took us through the restaurant and showed us where the different food stations were. There was fish up front, crab legs in the back, meats in the middle, pasta and other treats, then sushi and Indian towards the back.

Now, to the best part, the food!! Wow, it was like every single plate that I tasted was better than the last. I started off with taking little bits of chorizo and parmesan bread to start my dinner off light. Then I went for the Mac and cheese (wow!), the sliders (omg), and the ribs and sweet potatoe tots. I later tried the prime beef and I wasnt a fan, I don't know much about meat cuts so it was just a matter of trying something else. Towards the end of my night I discovered an Indian dish with chicken, I forget the name. Wow, it was more than delicious. The texture of the chicken was simply amazing. Two things you can't miss out on: the corn and the cheesy mashed potatoes - both blew me away.

Every dish here was beyond delicious and the quality was top notch. It's amazing that a weekday entrance is only $55 per person. To top it off, the sheer amount of desserts was phenomenal. I will be back after I try other nice buffets!

It has got be the best Buffett ever.  You will never be able to taste everything they have to offer.  The wait was kind of long.  We came on a Friday and we waited about an hour or more.   The servers are extremely nice!  Plates do not pile up on your table. Servers are on there job.   It is very much worth the price!

AMAZING!!!

I must return because I haven't even tried half of what they offered here. This weekday dinner is a great deal at $55pp

The food was good not great compared to the local casino buffet where we live that is half the price. The hostess' were rude. The bus boy was great, did an amazing job keeping our table clean! The desserts were good minis in many flavors perfect way to finish the meal.

My wife and I heard about the Bacchanal Buffet on the travel channel. I was skeptical that my experience would not live up to the expectations. I was absolutely blown away by the selection and quality of the food. The experience exceeded my expectations.

I was so pleasantly surprised. I've never been to a buffet like this one. The food is sectioned off by theme- seafood, meats, comfort food, Mexican, Italian, Asianc vegetarian and desserts. The quality was superb, and well worth the price. My favorite dishes were the Thai food, ramen, crab claws and tarot (ube) ice cream. You even get a free alcoholic drink if you check in on Yelp.

Very pricey for the selection of food but very clean. Presentation is really good. The major problem is seating. When they sit you down they try to sit you down in a tight spot. I feel like I'm boxed in and have no way out or unable to have a somewhat private conversation with my fiancé. Gives you a feeling of anxiety and the person next to you watching you eat. Other than that it's  very nice and great service.

This is one of the things my husband and I were so excited for on our Vegas trip. We went and waited in line, which was expected and no problem. We thought it would be worth the wait, and the price. It wasn't. The food was OK... just Ok. The dessert was absolutely terrible, and If you want more than crab and prime rib you will be extremely disappointed. Over priced, dried out meat, and not a very friendly staff. I'm so shocked by all of the great reviews.

On our last day in Vegas, we decided to have our final lunch here and oh boy we made the BEST DECISION ever.

The food and its quality is simply outstanding! From the hot plated breakfast to the mouth watering gelato desserts. The pork buns and dimsums were a family favorite. The roast beef etc were hot! Everything was phenomenal. 

Staff were very attentive too. Nice and courteous. 

These are the reasons this is the BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS. 

When we come back in Vegas, expect us to be back!!!

Worth every penny. I'm embarrassed that I ate all that I did. The only thing that was missing was lobster tails (and I probably just missed them). They had everything you could think of. This was by far the best Vegas buffet experience I've had. Not only did they have a vast spread but everything was prepared well. The dessert bar was so massive, it could have been its own restaurant. The only reason I didn't give it 5 stars is because it was so pricey to add alcohol.

Hmmm, come here early, look for Groupon deals if possible, and if not, just come!

There is such a large array of food here:  from country potatoes to hash browns, a soup bar, pastry bar, a fresh omelette making station to dim sum... yeah, it's a place to be.

We especially loved the tofu soup and shrimp/grits pan.  Mmmmm.  Ladies and gentlemen, please be sure to work up an appetite before coming here.  It is worth the money.

This is by far one of the worst buffet that I have ever been. The only reason i gave 2 stars because the crab legs were good. That's the only good thing. Waited approximately 1 hr 40 mins and paid 50 bucks then it must be good. WRONG. This is just some BS hyped thing. Oysters were super bad, ate 1 ewww (maybe just bad luck) ate 2 more and done. Crawfish, the entire plate all black when i opened them. Im not done, then i tried the shrimp (look like tiger head shrimp, very big) right next to the oyster, opened it up and the shrimp meat crumpled like powder. I mean seriously??? Zero quality control??? Im here for the seafood. Then hoping desserts can cheer me up, nope....although ice cream was good.  Next day went to the M buffet paid less, almost no wait in line and everything was much much better (except the crab legs).  I wouldn't recommend this buffet. Huge disappointment and total waste of time. This was a Friday night btw.

Oh where do I begin? 

This was an amazing dining experience. I specify dining - because the checking in and waiting was a nightmare! (Check Groupon and the Caesar's website for info on getting "VIP" to have a reservation time & no wait, we didn't) by the time we sat to eat, it was about 45 minutes after we had first arrived. I guess for one of the most popular buffets in Vegas this isn't too bad ? 

They had EVERYTHING! The only wait I really saw was for the carved meat, but they were moving quickly. The crab legs were dished out quick as well, no line there. The appetizer themed food stole the show for me. Fried green beans were out of this world! The mini wedge salad was refreshing and crisp. The ribs ? Melt in your mouth. 

Take your time here and enjoy all that the buffet has to offer and make multiple trips!

Definitely my favorite buffet in vegas! Love that they have so much variety that you can choose from. From seafood, American, Italian, Mexican, Asian, and get forget the dessert. 

Everything here is just so good! I always try to make sure I get to try a little bit of everything. From this past weeks visit to the buffet, I really enjoyed the crab legs, taco station. The elotes which I have never seen there, the Brussel sprouts and the dessert. 

Would definitely recommend this buffet and will be back soon!

Being a tourist in Las Vegas, I looked up the best buffet and this was rated #1. This buffet did not disappoint. There was so much food!! It was well worth the money. I got the buffet with unlimited beer and wine package which was $75. The only negative is that when it says a 2 hour limit, they abide by that. The waiter that we had stopped coming to our table to clear our plates and refill our drinks once the 2 hour mark hit.

Yummy! Pricey buffet but the wide range of food, and quality makes it worth it! There can be a crazy long line so go and sign your group in on the tablet or if you're a large group, go straight into the large group line.

Some of my favorite items on the menu are ones I've never seen before in a buffet include bone marrow and sea snail (although I didn't eat that). The venue itself is beautiful as well and is in the heart of the resort.

If you're in Las Vegas for any amount of time, you're going to hit a buffet. This one is roughly double in price of the average buffet in Las Vegas, but it's way more than doubly worth it. 

Most buffets will have a variety of food from multiple cultures, but how many of them do this well? The Bacchanal buffet has a little something for everyone and it's all done really well. Their attention to detail is evident in most of the dishes they serve. From the sushi bar to the carving station, everything is neat, attractively displayed, and always delicious. I've gone with some picky friends, some not so picky friends, and my buddy who is a strict vegan. Not once have I had a bad experience.

A buffet in a Vegas is something you should experience, and this is the place to do so. On a typical weekend trip to Vegas, how many buffets can you actually eat anyway? For me, one good dinner buffet usually suffices and this is the one!

Although the food was amazing and there was a wide variety of choices, out service was horrible. I was very surprised at how bad it was considering the high price

We recently went back to the buffet and had a much better experience this time. We had great service, the food was great, and the desserts were to die for!

The food here is good, but this buffet costs about $15 more than others in town.  The service is HORRIBLE.  Our waitress hardly checked on us and we were there for 20 minutes before she even got our drink order.  I feel that for the cost, the other buffets are a better deal, but don't get me wrong.  The food is good.

Very Vegas, you get into a long line to first pay and then get placed into one of four lines so that you can wait some more and watch the "VIPs" swiftly get a table as you continue to wait. Once seated, I found the food to be ok, not great and not really worth to $60 per person cost. One piece of advice, walk around and see the large selection of food first so you don't load up in one area and fill up with no room to try more things....as I did. Overall, it was good but not spectacular.
Every time we come to Vegas we have to stop at this buffet. It has anything you could possibly want.... AMAZING!

Paid for lunch, stayed for an early dinner. Ate on a weekday so the buffet only ran me about $45 and it was definitely worth it. I didn't have to wait in any long lines, food was fresh and appetizing, and the servers were very attentive. 

There is everything from the popular seafood, elk sliders, bone marrow, tacos, asian food and more. There was never a time when i walked up to a station that was empty.

So my family and I went today to the buffet, we were a party of 8. After we paid we still waited a good while to get a table. One of the waiters told us we were going to get a round table, we ended up sitting at a table that they had combined with other tables. We did get mad because that's not the table they told us we were going to get, and we waited even longer to get that particular table. In the end we got the table they initially told us we were getting, but the staff (for whatever reason) looked upset, as if they were the ones standing for a long period of time for a table. Anyways, approximately an hour and a half later this random lady comes over our table and tells us our time is up and made us leave. My family and I have been going to the buffet since 2011. To us the Bacchanal is a must go, we always look forward to going there. We go to Vegas about 3 times a year and stay for at least 5 days, on every trip we go to the Bacchanal at least 3 times. It is a shame that the petty manager couldn't manage her middle school attitude and ended up kick us out. This is the third time we had gone to the Bacchanal in the past 6 days we stayed in Vegas. Shame on the staff for being so unprofessional. 
A tip for future customers: don't get on the mangers bad side otherwise you will be kicked out after an hour!

There's been a lot of talk about the Bacchanal Buffet. I've heard it from friends, seen Yelp reviews, read stories about it on foodie websites, but never experienced it myself. I figured it was time, so I took myself here on a Sunday morning at 9 AM to partake of the brunch offering.

The steep price of $54 hit me in the face after I sailed through a non-existent line (come early, you will avoid the hung-over tourists). But I willingly paid my bill with hope still in my heart that it would be worth it. Please, please be worth it.

I was seated at a small table, perfect for my one person party and told I could begin, and my waitress would be back to get my drink order. 

The place does have a large, selection, I'm not going to say it doesn't - it does. They also do a mix of small personal plates, with normal buffet offerings you spoon onto your plate, which by the way can make things kind of weird, especially since the plates aren't all that big.

First I went for the seafood - crab claws, crab legs, raw shrimp, a lobster Benedict (personal small portion). This is where things get weird, I wanted the lobster Benedict, and I would have happily just grabbed the tiny dish and made my way, but it was too damn hot, and the little plastic grabby things they offer DO NOT WORK very well. So I had to cram the tiny square plate onto my normal sized plate which was already full of raw seafood.

A listing of what I (can remember) I had and impressions:

Raw Crab/Shrimp - great, can't really complain there.

Lobster Benedict - Also good, creamy, and plenty of lobster

Red Velvet Pancakes - Terrible, dry, and not enough syrup. Stacked three high and yet who wants to eat the other two even drier pancakes under the first one?

Mini Donuts w/ Bananas Foster - Very skimpy on the bananas foster, also the donuts were dry, just like the pancakes. 

Chilaquelas - Much better dish, very good, I should have gotten two. Good flavor pairings. 

Machacha - I'm not even sure what this was, but it was again, FREAKIN DRY. It looked good, then you dig in and.... ddrrryyy.

Scrambled eggs, hash-browns, and mushrooms - All very good, and did not come as tiny plated versions, I dug them out of a large heaps like a regular 
'ol buffet style. The mushrooms to note were one of my favorites of the whole buffet. 

Chicken/Waffle/Fry THING - So, so cute, but such a disappointment. It comes in an ice cream waffle cone, and I was like, I'm not eating this. Okay the little chicken wing that was in there was OK. I would have rather just had a bunch of those chicken wings, but I guess it would look kind of weird for me to dig them out of all the waffle cones eh?

Mixed fruit parfait - Heavenly! Yes, I thoroughly enjoyed a yogurt cup with mixed fruit. 

Porky Belly w/ mashed taters - Very good, salty, fatty. Everything pork belly should be.

Of note, but I did not partake of: the meat carving station looked amazing, but I had no hankering for meats during my visit. An omelet making station, I did not want to partake because I thought it would fill me up too much and I wouldn't have room for other food. A bar for making lox - looked good, did not try. A decent Asian section of food. A small salad bar. Quite a few decent looking pizzas. 

Oddly disappointing: 

Meager sushi selection - they had out spam musubi and one other roll. Maybe they have the better selections outside of brunch.

Desserts - Totally comparable to smaller, less expensive buffets, with the exception of the make your own crepe and gelato bar.

But also pleasing - service was great, especially for a buffet. My server really took care of me, which I really appreciated. Whenever I got up and came back my dirty plate was gone and my water was refilled. She also kept me stocked on decaf coffee and creamer. 

Would I go back? With soooo many buffets in Vegas I doubt I will, unless someone wants to pay for me and I wouldn't do brunch again.

Our first time at the Bacchanal buffet , the place was very nice well decorated very clean large variety of food and cuisine, large selection of desert . How ever the quality of the meat was not good , frozen farm rase seafood from China most likely , the service was very poor , the ladies at the cashier and host was not nice and unprofessional 
And that the reason why I am giving  this place 3 stars. 
I do recommend this place if you care about quantity .
Romulus at Bacchanal Buffet was great. Happy go lucky. He was very helpful. He was fast at bringing our drink orders. All the staff working on sept 27 and 28 , 2019 were great. Thanks. From navinder

I like to think of myself as a buffet aficionado.  This is one of the best buffets in all of Vegas.  It's pricey, but you CAN make your money back on your first plate just based on all the amazing items.

Some highlights on the Saturday Brunch Buffet menu ($55 a person)
- King Crab legs already cut
- Prime Rib
- Slow roasted pork belly
- Red Velvet Pancakes
- Fresh Ramen noodle soup
- Sushi
- Fresh Donuts Gelato Sandwiches
- Crepes made to order
- Unlimited Mimosas
- Fresh Fruit Juice
- Giant Shrimp

And its not the cheap stuff..this is REALLY high quality ingredients and well cooked food.  

Save yourself an expensive dinner and just eat their brunch and load up for the day.  The food quality can beat most of the restaurants around the country.

I've lived in Vegas for 18yrs and have been to MANY restaurants and buffets(from $ to $$$$) so I'm familiar with what this city has to offer. This buffet although good is NOT WORTH THE PRICE. Most reviews are from tourists not locals so they don't know better. If your a tourist please read reviews FROM LOCALS. Just because a buffet is huge doesn't mean it's automatically a five star. This buffet should be no more than $40.  I still think the Wynn, Aria, Bellagio and MResort are the best but ONLY on weekends. Go to the ONLY five star  Asian restaurant in North America inside Wynn. Money well spent.

Fantastic! My kids and I tagged along with my husband, who was in town for a work conference. We came just before the dinner menu/pricing as suggested by other reviews. There was a wait, maybe half an hour, but they were nice enough to get our party in by 2:58! We were there eating until after 6:00. The selection is high end (wagyu, prime rib, tri tip, hot crab legs, taco station were our favorites to name a few). This will be our go-to buffet when in town from now on.
The quality and variety of food does not come close to the price of the buffet. It might have been good in the past, but wasn't very good on recent visit.

The best buffet around. I came here on two separate occasions and was never disappointed. There's a variety of food to choose from, drinks are provided in a timely fashion. Though my fiancé doesn't do buffets but he will attend this one with no hesitation. 

The quality of food is great. The atmosphere is relaxing and welcoming. Pricing is 55-60 dollars a person, definitely worth attending for the first time. 

Great place to try especially if you are a tourist.
The food is great, however,  the tongs are very very hard to use. The bad tongs have ruined the soup dumplings...

So horrible! Food selections were better 5 years ago, but now it is just filled with your generic stuff. The oysters were so disgusting that I couldn't finish them. Would never be returning here again.
Great buffet with lots of choices. The steamed crab legs were so good and I will be back for those alone. Long lines, but with the wait. When we want a buffet this is where we dine.

After 4 days in Vegas filled with hours of research, I finally decided that Bacchanal buffet out of all the other buffets in Vegas was it. Bacchanal would be the destination for my last supper before I headed back home. It was going to be an epic one filled with glutton and happiness. However, I left feeling seriously underwhelmed and honestly just annoyed. We waited for 50 minutes to pay $57 pp for the dinner buffet. After that, we waited another 40 to be seated. After being seated  I had to wait another 15 minutes in line for the carving station that promised prime rib. Once I got to the front of the line I found out they were out of prime rib. I settled for sausage that I could buy at my local grocery store, chewy spare ribs, and overlooked lamb chops. After about 4 plates, my boyfriend and I decided to go look at the dessert station. We were gone for about 4 minutes and when we came back, our table had been bussed and resat. They do have a 2 hour max but we had only been there for an hour. Areas where clean plates should have been were constantly empty for very long periods of time. Anyone with eyes could see they were seriously understaffed; some tables in the dining area were left unbussed for 30 minutes. The dessert station gave this otherwise a 2 star buffet 3 stars. I really regret choosing Bacchanal.
This is one of the best buffets in Las Vegas. Everything is fresh and flavorful. It is on the pricier side but it is worth going there once in s while.

I have no shame in saying this.. not worth the Christmas weekend price. Either the regular chefs weren't working on 12/23 or the food quality control isn't up to par anymore. 

We had watched a video a few days before and it showed how the quality and the chefs make sure the food is prepared correctly and they prided themselves on every aspect of the meal. Didn't hold true for our experience. We probably won't ever end up coming back to this place.  Not worth the price and it wasn't all that great.

One thing to mention is, the desserts were actually good. That was the only thing on point. Everything else was subpar.

Today we went with group of 17 people! The waiter treated us like shit and thought one of us was getting free drinks and not paying for it. He was wrong, 7 of us paid for it instead of 6 people. He was incredibly rude! We spent more than 1300 dollars and we are gonna cheat people out of 15 bucks? It would have been good if people would take a minute and think! No one is going to cheat you for the bottom shelf glass of wine, dude! The food was average. It took them one and a half hour to sit us. They let smaller parties to go ahead of us. We were cool with splitting up and getting two tables. No one listened or tried to communicate with us! The worst crap I have ever seen

Its poor customer service we asking about the buffet of buffet how that 
works first this lady's name is Rosa she didn't exactly explain how its work she asked  my aunt  to explain to us but the way this do it it's a very rude manner. The food  not too good   fruits (watermelon it's not fresh) I'm not empress with food and expensive too..

Great buffet only equated or surpassed by the top strip buffets. Expensive, but this IS Vegas, and it's worth the experience. Great crab legs, oysters, shrimp, steak and superbly crafted desserts. Ok service, and they watch that 2 hour time limit!

This is the most expensive buffet I have eaten at in long time. The biggest question I had was 'is it going to be worth it?' And for me, the answer is "no". You find the same items of the same quality at other nice buffets for 20$ cheaper. 

I don't have any complaints about it in general besides the price. I'm even willing to pay extra amount if there was some thing unique offered. Lobster tails, nice beef besides prime rib, game hens, sushi made to order, etc. or even if there were drinks included in the price like the M resort used to do.

Ate here today for the first time, but I soon regretted it. Needless to say I spend the rest of the day in my hotel room, due to a bad case of food posioning. I suspect it was the different types of shellfish. Likely the oysters or lobster claws.

One observation I made was some people cutting in line and piling their plates full of stuff (specifically the seafood). One particular person I witnessed cut the seafood line to fill one plate full of oyster shooters and another overloaded plate of lobster claws. She didnt stop until one of the food servers saw her and grabbed the tongs out of her hands. I really wish they did something more about this, because it ruined the experience for me. Id glady pay even more to avoid that kind of nonsense. I also hope and pray that the person enjoyed their loot, along with an even more severe case of diarrhea. Projectile vomiting would be the icing on the cake.

Anyhow, regarding the food, it was good overall, but my opinion of it has dropped significantly since I got sick. It ruined my first day of vacation here in Las Vegas and I hope I get well soon so I can enjoy the rest of my trip.

Hands down, my FAVORITE buffet place in Vegas!

Unlimited steamed crab legs, yes please!

Instead of listing every single item I ate, just know their buffet will exceed your expectations of a "normal" buffet, after all, it is Vegas!

I recommend going early like 5pm, if you want Bacchanal for dinner because anytime after that, it will be a wait. Not the "let me get a slurpee from 7/11" wait, it's the "let me buy random junk I don't need on black Friday" wait.

CRAB LEGS AND LOBSTER CLAWS says it all. These are served during dinner and totally worth the price. They have a large selection of other foods: Asian (sushi, pho, rice, miso soup, etc), Mexican (tacos made to order, ceviche, etc.), BBQ, prime rib (this was only okay - they cut the slices way too thick and it wasn't as tender as I would have liked). Lots of dessert options with small portions so you can try them all 

Definitely recommend to go if you're hungry and ok to wait. It's a little pricey, but totally worth it if you can eat. They also have an option to add-on their alcohol package.
Amazing selection and service! I loved the crepe station and the fresh squeezed juices! As well as 150 more things on the buffet! An experience you must try!
Italian section looked old and hurt though the Mexican section and desserts made up for it. For the price to see old chicken parm and old lasagna as the only Italian items worthwhile was a letdown.

This buffet is an eating experience. Plan to be there early- there will be a line. They had multiple stations and several types of cuisine. Their ceviche and poke were incredible. You can try new foods (sea snails or frog legs, for example). They have most foods in tasting portions, which was great so you could try. Some foods were just meh. Their roasted root veggies, for example were very undercooked. Their dessert bar was a let-down. They had probably a hundred to try, but they all were fairly bland (exception- creme brûlée). I would skip the desserts and try new food.

WOW. Hands down one of the best buffets on the strip! I tried a few buffets (Bellagio and wicked spoon) and the Bacchanal had to be my favorite. I love the cleanliness of the buffet and the wide variety of cuisine they had to offer! I watched a video of the executive chef on YouTube and how she reads the yelp reviews, and the amount of critic and her eye for detail made the experience great! The one down fall that I did find quite confusing was during their rush, it made it quite confusing where to line up at. There were a handful of lines, but we asked the people of ahead where to go it was smooth sailing! DONT HOLD OFF ON THE CREME BRÛLÉE. YOURE ON VACATION; JUST DO IT!

Super impressed with Bacchanal Buffet. It is pricey but worth the variety.

I came here with my bf who generally doesn't eat much, but I was impressed with how much he could put down at Bacchanal. Some highlights (although everything was so good)-

Made to order tacos- I got the al pastor tacos and my bf got the steak. Mine was mixed with pineapple per request and I think it was slightly better than the steak one. Both are worthwhile and you can order one or two of each type. Didn't bother with the chicken but am sure it's good.

Bone marrow- very rich and flavorful like standard bone marrow, but I think the bone marrow here is tastier than Wicked Spoon because it's more pure meat? Like Wicked Spoon's bone marrow is served with a fig jam if I can recall correctly, which I think kinda took away from the bone marrow.

Chili mashed potatoes- these kinda reminded me of Popeyes mashed potatoes but with the gravy mixed in. I loved it.

Prime rib- I'm not usually a fan of prime rib because it's usually wetter than other cuts (WET not MOIST but maybe I've only ever had bad prime rib) but this was so good that I went to get my own after having a bite of my bfs.

Our server was also super nice, attentive and charismatic. He was on his way out since it was the end of his shift, but he brought us over some tiramisu which, as far as we knew, was no longer available at the dessert buffet since we were there pretty late.

Despite what I said about Wicked Spoon's bone marrow, I still think Wicked Spoon is slightly better. It's worth going to both Bacchanal and Wicked Spoon to see for yourself though.
I just have to say this was the best buffet I've ever been to. Food was amazing. The waiter I had was amazing and funny. I will be coming back for more when I'm on Vegas again.

TLDR: expensive (but you're in Vegas...sooo), impressive selection, some majors hits and minor misses, long wait, worth the experience.

Definitely try: tacos al pastor, crab legs (at the back station - they're freshest and not pre-cut), thai tea float, ube gelato, bone marrow, wagyu steak.

The reviews don't lie. 
Expensive? Yes but it's a fancy Vegas buffet. What do you expect?
Long lines? Yes but not as bad if your group is smaller than 5 and you get there early. We arrived around 4pm, had a group of 4, and waited only about 30 minutes.

The selection was beyond my wildest imagination. It was like being in Willy Wonka's Chocolate Factory. With the huge selection, of course, some dishes are totally awesome and other dishes are just meh. If you're a fan of crab legs, definitely go to the station in the back (near the Italian food). They cook the crab legs right in front of you and hand it to you on a steaming plate. They also don't pre-cut the crab legs which is great. 

I'd also totally recommend the tacos al pastor. The tacos are made to order and are delish! And don't miss the large salsa bar around the corner! The other dishes I had were all pretty good! Nothing out of this world but definitely tasty. The best part, though? THE DESSERTS! I am a total sweat tooth so I was in heaven. Everything was so good and they give small enough portions that you can pretty much try everything you want. My personal favorites were the thai tea float, ube and matcha gelatos, the creme brulee and the ube cone. 

What you're paying for here is the experience. Yes, the food is good but it's really about having the exciting huge selection and being able to try so many different dishes. The atmosphere feels expensive and the food makes it worth it. There will definitely be some meh food but it's a buffet. If you're a real food snob you'll probably be happier somewhere else. As long as you know what you're getting yourself into, you'll enjoy the experience.

Went for holiday dinner.  Paid $79 per person.  Needed to take a ticket from a machine which will tell you what time you'll get to start waiting in line.   130 minutes was the initial wait time,  plus an additional 60 minutes of waiting in line. I've been waiting years to try this place, so didn't mind the additional 3 hours.  What a disappointment.  Food was on par with several other buffets on the strip.  The selection is good, but the taste, is not worth the price.  The desserts are the only saving grace.  I would add another star if the line were short and/or the price were cheaper.  All in all, overrated.

&& I fell for this place :3

Even though they just opened 3 weeks ago, I think they're doing very good in terms of quality, cleanliness and service. BUT THAT LINE WAS HORRIBLE! I don't know if I could or would ever wait 2+ hours for a buffet... so thank goodness a lady came around and told us we could pay $15 extra for the express line. Considering how hungry and excited I was, I thought $15 extra was worth it if I can cut down at least 2 hours of wait time. She said it would take 5 minutes if we go through the express line but the cashiers obviously didn't get the memo and refused to call us up until the people in front of us got frustrated. 

Once all of that was over it was time for the FOOD!! MY FAVORITE PART :3 I absolutely loveeeeeeeeeeeeeeee the lamb chops (best thing there in my opinion). They also have king crab legs and snow crab legs (you can ask them for the steamed ones, taste so much better). The sliders are yummy if you add a bit of salt. The lobster corn chowder was very flavorful and hit the spot. Not sure if they had 500 items there but they sure had enough to make me go 7 rounds... don't judge me, I'm a fatass! OH! They also have some legit fresh honey next to the bread and cheese area. Make sure you walk around the entire place first so you know what you're up against. I never ever want to leave their dessert section...soooooooooooo amazing!! The biggest selection I've ever seen! They have everything from mini cupcakes, gelato, macarons, BANANA souffle!, creme brulee, MAKE YOUR OWN CREPES (my fav because they have fresh fruits and nutella!!!). 

I took off 1 star because:
-They were very unorganized with the line and the seating in general even though there were tables open
-Some of the dishes were kinda cold
-The busboys cleaned out our table while we were getting desserts ):

If you're not a diamond or 7-star member, you'd probably want to dish out another $15 so that you can use that time to actually eat something instead of wait in line. WORTH IT!!

The food was very high quality and fresh.  The desert table was amazing.  So many unique things to choose from.  Vietnamese coffee dessert and the mango dessert was my favorite.  Salmon was cooked to perfection.

My first Vegas buffet experience and I was completely spoiled. It is definitely expensive but SO WORTH THE MONEY! Do not eat anything leading up to the buffet because you will want to stuff yourself with all the food there. 

They have tacos, ramen, pho, crab legs, prime rib, lamb, and so much more! The ramen broth was delicious and came with big pieces of pork. The tacos were pretty decent. The clams were so tiny and delicious. They have several dim sum buns including taro buns and shrimp shumai! 

Their drinks are amazing too. Get the sweet tea! We were confused because whenever I drink sweet tea, it's dark brown while this one was clearish. It was sweet with a hint of peach and at my table of four girls, we must have ordered 10 glasses between all of us. 

Lastly, their dessert bar. I could write poetry to it I was so in love. They make crepes, have dozens of sweets (creme brûlée, Chinese custard tarts, tiramisu cups, puffs and pastries galore!). They also have gelato and the strawberry balsamic paired surprisingly well with the Nutella coffee. 

It's steep for $62.72 on a Sunday night but they don't kick you out and we stayed definitely more than half an hour after closing. I definitely have to come back on my next trip to Vegas!

Stayed in Caesar Palace, so tried this buffet, it was okay, liked the bone marrow which is awesome, waited on a long line for the crab legs (thought it was king crab legs as I saw some ppl had on their desk but it turned out snow crab legs, was told the king crab legs charge extra), not much choices for sashimi, a little disappointed, not bad just to have a try. but probably not visit again since there are so many other good options in Vegas

As others described, there is a ton of delicious and specially prepared foods. There's something for everyone. My only complaint is that I couldn't eat more food because I was so full, and I left dessert for last! The crab legs were tasty and the portions were large. Everything looked high quality. I would go there again and skip any other Buffet. It gets busy so go early.
Simply amazing food! The variety of food and the precision of presentation and quality of taste is just amazing! My family and I will return as we love this place! A MUST when in Vegas!!!!
Absolutely an amazing experience! A little on the pricey side but totally worth it. Great experience and will definitely come back for seconds!

Food was top notch for a buffet.  Some restaurants don't prepare food nearly this quality.  Servers and chefs were really friendly and helpful.   I suggest everything but the seafood as it's not as good.  Asian, BBQ and Italian items were the best parts.  Desserts were many and all were great.

First time coming to Vegas and Bacchanal buffet was on my list to visit since there was so much raves on it. Came here at 4pm and my group was expecting a two hour wait since that's what everyone claim to be. Luckily someone helped us and realized bigger groups have advantages and gets seats faster. Us being a party of 8 waited an hour and a half so not bad. We were starving and Caesar's palace was huge!!! Took us a while to find the buffet too LOL. You pay first then you get seated. It was about 63$ including tips for every person in our group considering it's AYCE. There were lots of options but nothing really stood out to me. Food was decent but wasn't great :/ I tried the king crab, prime rib, American wagyu,Hawaiian poke, raw oysters (not fresh), siu mai, Caesar salad,mash potato, and lastly fries! For dessert I got black sesame gelato, chocolate brownies and some fresh fruits (kind of sad they didn't have any berries) only got watermelon, honey dew, and bananas. Glad I tried this place out since it's my first time at Vegas but wouldn't return. 

P.s if you're ubering tell your uber driver to drop you off at the backdoor and not main entrance. Less crowded!

i give this place full stars because thw food and service hits the spot at all times when i come visit. 
they have so many variety of food with a chef to each certain ethnic food that makes the food. most dishes are fresh and tastes good and they use good quality food or ingredients mixed in the dishes. 

lets start  with the seafood bar. they have oysters to shrimps to crab to mussels and crawfish to lobster chowder. there seafood are the best quality for a buffet but its doable and taste great. 

next they have a american / soul food which have plenty of fried to grits to steam food with a chef cutting up ham prime rib and sausages too. 

next they have a bread station with tons of different breads for your meal. next to it they have a juice bar where they have freshly juiced drinks for you enjoy such as grapefeuit. apple. cucumber. tropical. orange. and etc. these juice are so worth the money. imagine going out on strip to buy a bottle of juice  for 5 bucks. 

also the chinese station they have ginseng soup and porridge too like wow those two items are soo good. and ok dim sum for a buffet not bad and not  good but ok and edible. 

for the sushi i dont like that because its too americanized and doesnt look appealing. 

they also have a cheese bar with variety of cheeses too and a salami bar too with different cut out salami too. 

they also have a fresh salad bar to go to your healthy selections  if you wanna balance your meal. 

also a dessert  bar with  20 flavor gelatos from green tea mint to pumpkin spice to black seasme and the original flavors such as choc vanilla and strawberry. and fresh made crepes too like wow thats the best dessert serve there. 

best lunch buffet money spent for 35 bucks leaving satisfy. totally will be back again!

My friends and I recently came here again since Samantha, the owner, offered a great discount since I was not very satisfied with the Asian food section. I noticed the variety was better during the lunch set. The seafood and comfort food were still very good. The desserts were excellent as usual (black sesame gelato and turtle cheesecake are perfect). Thanks Samantha for having us. Would recommend others to come here.

My love took me here for Valentines! The line was long but it moved up pretty fast ! Would I do it again OF COURSE Waugh beef, their omakase non-cooked food was amazing  everything was absolutely perfect !

Went on Labor Day 2019, the day before I went to buffet at Wynn to compare. Wynn was $60, Caesars $65. Desserts improved greatly from my last visit, as did sauces for meats. Brisket and other meats made it worth it for me, along with desserts. Beat out Wynn, for sure. However, I still find the sushi and pizza sections to be very poor quality, visually and taste. We also went to a AYCE sushi spot in Vegas that weekend, and this is what I'm comparing it to. Yes I know I shouldn't expect a buffet to be best at sushi, but it's best at its meats and desserts, both of which I also love. I say if they can't make it great, remove it. Also, a waste of food are servers who don't speak or ask if someone is done with a plate and just take it. This happened a few times to our party of 8 and we had to get up and get more food. Also, workers at food stations should listen to customers at an AYCE buffet. If I say "can I have more ice cream?" It means, more than a child's scoop. Still the best buffet in Vegas IMO and I've eaten at most all from Harrahs, to Mirage and those off the strip.

I was reading the reviews on this place and thought wow #1 in Vegas we HAVE to go. I waited 2hrs in line to get in, I was STARVING! Thought to myself maybe that's why all the reviews are awesome because everyone is starving? After being seated it took the waitress 45 minutes to bring us drinks. They brought us water but not enough for our entire party. We had to keep asking for utensils  and and refills. The atmosphere was classier than most and they were extremely creative with their recipes, however most items aren't labeled and you have no idea what's in the items so accidentally ate goat cheese that which disgusts me. Aside from creative recipes their food was mediocre at best. It's a great place to eat if you love sea food but definitely not if you have sea food allergies. I gave the place an extra star because the crepe lady is SO NICE and she does her job perfectly!

One of my fellow yelper recommended me this place, and based on the reviews from other yelpers, I've decided this place. This place is pretty good and looks like a 5 stars buffet, but I have qualifications.

The wait time for the buffet during dinner on the weekend were so pathetic. 1+ hours wait for the line and then another 1+ hour for the buffet. I've never ever waited that long for a buffet in my entire life. I shouldn't have done that for sure.

As soon I got to the cashier section and pay for the buffet which is like $55.99 for dinner, I got in line for the buffet. Then finally, I got a seat so I could try to enjoy some food. Oh and if your wondering how long you can enjoy eating for, there's an 2 hours limit.

Food: The actual dinner is very yummy. Really love their prime ribs, mac and cheese, lobster ravioli, and other stuff that was good. Great selection of foodies. Their dessert weren't as good at all. I had the red velvet cupcake and an pumpkin pie gelato. I didn't actually care for either of the dessert.

Overall: very high price, not so good desserts, and long wait time really made me give it a 4 stars and have no plans on coming back here when it's not worth my time and money.
