The only good thing about this buffet is the selection.  Not much else.  The arrangement is horrendous--you have navigate between tables to get to the food counter.  The food counter in the asian section soup area is so low you can't see what food is down there unless you're under 5ft tall.  The prime rib was horrible -- low quality meat.  The crab section was a joke -- a ratio of 1 king crab to 10 snow crab is not acceptable given the price.  They tried to hide this fact by mixing the two together.   The cocktail shrimp was acceptable and so was the grilled scallops w/ mayo(my favorite).  the dessert section had a lot to choose from but they sucked -- tiramasu, cheesecake, creme broulee, mango tapioca.  The Wynn buffet had better food but this one had better selection.  For $60 you would expect better.  I'd rather spend $30 at Jackson Rancheria Casino and get AYCE Lobster and flavorful prime rib.

We went to eat there today 4/17/19 @ 3:45pm for $44.99 and there were no wait. We got seated within 5 min. The food is okay to good. I wouldn't say the food knocked my shoes off, just another buffet for me. I won't be coming back.

Crabs were okay - there were dungeonous amd snow crab legs. No king crabs.

Seafood - just ok. The seafood paella taste loke rice and shrimp. The saffron seasoning was unnoticeable. Halibut was alright. The texture was great, not overcooked. However, it lacked seasoning. Coctail shrimp was good but it's hard to mess up with that.

Asian - you're better off ordering take out. The prok belly was really good, that was qhat stood out to me.

Crepe was okay. It was thin enough but the ingredients were all articifial so it's not my cup of tea. Although i love nutella. I suggest you ask for a small portion or they will make you the standard size. 

I don't get the hype. Service was great. Wait staff, chef, pastry chef, they were all super nice.

Wish I could give this 0 stars. Went to the buffet at 7pm on a Tuesday. Expected to wait in line for a bit but we waited for over an hour just to pay. We were only three parties from the front of the line and didn't move for over 30 minutes because they kept taking parties of two and parties of ten that were in line behind us. We ended up leaving after they took a total of 15 groups before us. We would have waited at least 30 more minutes to get a table and then would have only been able to eat for 30 minutes.  Absolutely ruined our last night in Vegas since we were trying to save the best for last. Sadly we never got to try it.

I had the pleasure of trying the famous, Bacchanal Buffet a few days ago, when some friends of mine invited me to celebrate their huge poker tournament win ;) 

As many past reviewers have stated, the food here is delicious - more than 5 star worthy but I stand at a solid 4 stars, stay tuned why... but let's talk foods first since I'm still dreaming of all the yum yum they serve at this buffet.

I was shocked that on a Wednesday night around 8pm there was still a large crowd waiting to get in and eat. This just confirmed to me that this buffet really is legit. 

After waiting a few minutes we were seated perfectly next to the buffet, so we didn't need to walk far, score! Maria was our server, who was super friendly and attentive. Thanks for the great customer service, Maria! 

So back to the foods... in my opinion this buffet is clearly known for their seafood selection. One island/section alone was dedicated to crab, oysters, muscles, scallops and sooooo much more! Can we please talk 'bout how beautiful the presentation is?! So in awe! Next to the seafood we have alllll the delicious carved meat! My favorite was the prime rib and then the American Wagyy Beef. But before the prime rib, my absolute favvvvvvvvv was the big bone marrow pieces with bread crumbles plus a few pomegranate sprinkles! Holy cow these were delish! I can eat those all day. The following section is "Mexican" where they make fresh street tacos, yup! 
Don't forget to turn the corner cuz they have an additional area with Italian food + Asian food. The Asian food serves up ramen, pho, udon, sushi and MORE! Let's just say the variety here is great and the food actually tastes amazing! 

Here's where the 5th star basically disappears for me, because we were one of the last tables to leave we unfortunately were exposed to how they clean up everything. Get ready, so they throw everything away in one clean sweep. Meaning they WASTE so much food, it's not even funny! My heart broke a little seeing how much food just got thrown away, like that!!! I feel like they should have a better system on what to do with extra food instead of waste it...

Would I still return to Bacchanal Buffet? Yes, because the food is good - it's so good I hate to waste it!

I've been to a lot of the buffets from Henderson to Vegas and this one is for sure my top favorite. A great variety, lots of foods that not most buffets have, the quality of the food is top notch, and the flavor is delicious. On top of all that, having a major sweet tooth, this buffet has THE BEST dessert section of all time! Sooooo many options and fresh crepes that are so yummy. This buffet is worth your money. 

Went Olympia weekend and though busy, the wait was not too bad. Our waitress, Soccorro, was also very helpful and attentive. Great service! I'm not one to go to the buffet often because #fitlife , but whenever someone wants to go, Bacchanal is the first place I think of. 10/10

The hubs and I FINALLY had a chance to eat at Bacchanal. We were told so many wondrous stories about the food - how there is a seemingly never-ending offering of different cuisines that make you wish for a bottomless stomach.

The service was fantastic - everyone was so welcoming, friendly, and attentive. Given that this is a buffet, it's more common place for people to just walk around cleaning tables and picking up dirty plates here and there. At Bacchanal, there always seemed to be someone close by at all times.

The food was good, but I can't honestly say that it was AMAZING. The seafood section was decent, but a lot of the crab legs had dried out. The carving section had the longest line - and for good reason! Every piece of meat I tried was moist and flavorful. The Italian section had steamed crab legs served warm, and this was the saving grace for the hubs. He claimed that if we were to come back, he would just eat the crab legs. 

My favorite? Their desert section: so many selections of cakes, cupcakes, brownies, ice creams, crepes... 

B-E-A-UTIFUL.

The service was fine.... Actually our waitress was superb, however the food was not.  

We went for breakfast, and made the best Western Continental breakfast look like a five star restaurant.

Everything we had was cold.  Everything!  And even though it was breakfast I tried dishes from fried rice to eggs. 

The eggs in the eggs Benedict were raw.  The pastries were dry, the Chinese food tasted ok but was cold. The bacon was rubbery.

For 40 dollars a person, I expected much better.

There's no doubt that Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas, but it is nowhere near my top ten when it comes to buffet ranking.  Took us 90 minutes to get in, but oh well, expected of the top buffets in Vegas.

It was really the seafood drew us to Bacchanal, thus it was only natural that we hit it first.  Given their fame, voluminous advertisements, and reviews, I started my journey with high expectations, but boy was I wrong...  The snow crabs were over salted, dry, and empty.  The oysters were covered with broken shells and stacked on top of one another.  On the other hand, shrimp and stone crab claws were fresh, meaty, and lightly seasoned with salt.

As for the carving station, I got really excited when I saw that giant slab of what they call "American wagyu".  Do NOT be fooled by this!  Just a regular piece of beef wrongfully crowned with the title of wagyu.  Lacked that signature wagyu marbling and was tough as hell.

Then came the dessert lineup...  Options ranged from Asian pastries like egg tarts, ube ice cream, and almond custards to classics like lava cakes and creme brûlée.  Extensive selection? Yes, but a big no no for quality.  Egg tarts had soggy shells, ube tasted artificial, and creme brûlée had that unnatural taste and texture as if corn starch was used to solidify the dessert.

Was it worth waiting for?  Not for me personally.  If it's your first time in Vegas, I'd certainly recommend visiting either the Wicked Spoon or Bacchanal.  But if you're already a seasoned buffet goer that has experienced buffets like Colony or Edge in Singapore or even CafeToo in Hong Kong, Bacchanal certain pales in comparison to them (both in terms of price and options).

Best buffet experience in Las Vegas. Outstanding food and service. While the wait in line to get in is very long, it's worth the wait. Also a bit pricey compared to other top buffets. Overall a great one time experience.

Waited for an hour in line before paying and getting a table 

Mediocre depressing food 

The roast beef was dry as a rubber door stop
Sushi was ok 
 
Classic over rated Buffet
We've come several times but today too many people. The wait was around 45 min. The food was not good. No salads. The meat super dry and fatty. For the price it could have been way better

The price was super high for the overall experience.
First off, there was a child screaming for 40 minutes and no one came over to do anything about it so we had to ask to switch tables just so we weren't too stressed out to eat our food. A manager should have spoken to the couple before everyone around them was complaining.
Second, there wasn't a lot of options for the seafood area... I was super disappointed. Aside from the amazing hot crab legs, there wasn't much to choose from and nothing stood out. 
Third, the tacos I had barely had any flavor to the meat... nothing I couldn't get at a food truck on the side of the road. I expected better from a place so highly rated.
The only reason I am rating this place as highly as I am is because the Asian food was really great, the dessert station was to die for, and the server was really on top of making sure our drink were always full.

I've heard great things about this buffet and finally after three attempts to get a table. My family and I landed a dinner for 4 on Sunday, 9/2/2018 at 9:12PM. The buffet is about $70/person which our bill came out to a little over $320 not including gratuity.

The only thing that did not disappoint was the snow crab legs and the macarons. Everything was your typical buffet style food. The hand carved beef was so dry that the au jus and gravy couldn't save it. the sliders (beef and a thin slice of white cheese was so dry), the "pulled pork sliders" were a waste of stomach space. The bun was really hard. Felt like it was sitting there for the whole day. The rest of the food was not worth mentioning. 

Most of the desserts were mediocre. Not worth the price that we paid. 

The 7up tasted like club soda...which was odd. 

To be honest, save your $70 and find another buffet.

There was not a long wait time, we were seated right away.  After that it just went downhill!!! We where charged $60 per person which is fine but at least we were expecting a better service the food was just ok and they dont have any vanilla ice cream.  I wanted steam crab legs thats what I went for, but they were not available for the price that we pay I was expecting at least steam nice hot crab legs. Not going back.

It's 5 stars for Ohio buffet standards ( we don't have good one) but 3 for Las Vegas. Went there for lunch. It was good especially if you love seafood.

It has a lot of asian dishes and soups. Prime rib, brisket, ham, and other meat choice. But for some reason prime rib wasn't tender and cake was too sweet.
The buffet is very big.

Overrated. If you want to go, go for the lunch. Dinner is too expensive and will be even more overrated. Got to this buffet with my buddy even before checking into our hotel because we were really excited to try out this famous buffet in Vegas. We waited about 30-40min before sitting. The food was too salty for our taste. They do have HUGE HUGE selection of food, though. Some were good, but overall, they are underwhelming.

Not going to write too much because i wasnt really satisfied with this buffet.

I expected a little more food, i mean they had the seafood part down but the other food was just ok. 

I went crazy for their raw oysters but that was pretty much it. 

Their dessert bar was really good, they had fresh made crepes and cake pops. Really good dessert. But i wouldnt ever go here again. 

Such a disappointment. I expected a bit more especially since a lot of people were telling me to try this place.
The best buffet on the strip. All the food was fresh and there were so many options, my loved this place and would eat here again when we come to town. A bit pricey but totally worth it.

We went at 4:30pm and there was no line. Party of 8. Always a nice buffet. Lots of items. But no one item really stood out. The seafood was average, meats and desserts. But for a buffet it's one of the better ones, but for me is there really a good buffet? Especially in Las Vegas where there are so many?  But for our party any venue would have been great because it was our group that made the food taste good. See my photos

What a let down. I was so excited to head back to this buffet. I've only been there once before years ago. I didnt get to enjoy it that time due to the massive hangover I had. This time, had a clear head, and was full of hunger. The brisket was the best item. It was fucking delicious. The prime rib was great. The American Waygu, terrible and dry. Pizza was stale. Pad thai was stale. Taco station chef was awesome, too bad the ingredients suck. The pastor and asada were stale. Meatballs, you guessed it, stale. Sushi, stale. I don't know if I caught this buffet on an off day or what, it was Friday at 6pm. But yeah, super dissapointing. Especially when you're paying 60 bucks per person. I wish I had done the Wynn buffet instead.
First time here and food was delicious! Our service from Esmeralda Juarez was awesome!

TL;DR: Worth one try, but not more than one.

The Bacchanal Buffet is often cited as the best buffet there is in Las Vegas, and based on my experience, I would have to agree with the general consensus. Unfortunately, though, the buffet is definitely one of those things where the experience doesn't necessarily live up to expectations. After trying the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan (which was not great, I've also reviewed them), I had high hopes for Bacchanal.

Regarding the stories about long waits and lines, I can only speak from my own experience. I went to the Bacchanal Buffet for Thursday dinner and arrived at 4:00 pm. There was a short wait to pay for entrance, and an equally short wait to be seated, totaling to around maybe 15 minutes. While I was eating (be aware of the 2 hour time limit), I noticed that the line outside began to grow longer, but there were many empty tables inside the restaurant. While I don't know what it is like on the weekends, the reason the line becomes so long by 6 is not simply because the buffet is super popular, but because the buffet is constantly short-staffed and wants to keep its lines long by only using half of the restaurant's tables. 

As for the food itself, the variety is definitely there. Overall, the food quality is fairly high, but because of the breadth of the food that is offered, there are missteps in execution across the board. Overall, the buffet goes for quantity over quality, and if that's what you prefer, then this is perfect for you. The Asian section offers a decent variety of dim sum options and some supermarket sushi. While it was better than what I expected, if you are really looking to eat Chinese food, you'd be better off at a Chinese restaurant. The salad station is boring, and the cheese and meat selection is relatively meager for a buffet of this price. Bacchanal's strong point is definitely its meat carving station and its seafood. The variety of meats offered is great, including slab bacon the day I went. The seafood is good, including shucked oysters and a variety of cooked fish. The crab legs are not bad either. The taco station is a nice place to get food that is actually piping hot. One stickler is their fried chicken, though, which is probably among the worst I've ever tried.

Desert is interesting, and the variety of cakes and mini-deserts offered is enough to satisfy a sweet tooth. I am personally not a fan of gelato, which seems to be all the rage these days, and would much rather prefer creamier custard-based ice creams. The gelato at Bacchanal is passable, and the fact that they offered no chocolate options other than sugar-free chocolate disappointed me. I wouldn't say any desert was especially delicious, and the cookies and cupcakes were not nearly as good as what I regularly whip up at home. 

Overall, the Bacchanal is a testament to the quantity over quality business model, and is an epitome of the hyper-commercialized and overly-wasteful Las Vegas culture. It is an experience to be had, but it also isn't somewhere I would personally make a return visit to. If you do happen to have the $60 bucks to drop on this buffet, it is worth a try for the curious, but for many who value quality of execution, it may disappoint. If you want a high quality meal at a similar price, I would recommend trying out some of the fancier sit-down options such as the steakhouses found at many of the other Las Vegas hotels.

We came at 3:30 and we had missed the lunch buffet which ends at 3 pm. When we arrived, there wasn't that infamous line that Bacchanal is known for. We didn't have to use the kiosk as there was no line to get in. After paying $55 each, we were whisked away to have our picture taken. Hmm, I guess for some it may be a memento that they dined at one of Vegas' great buffets. 

I had high hopes of eating at this grandiose of a buffet. I'm sorry but our experience was just mediocre. There was no lobster tail, instead they offered steam snow crab legs. Bummer! I had some of the crab legs, basically the same crab legs I would find at any other buffet. I tried the lobster chowder, bland and cold. Hubby had a couple of slices of prime rib, just ok. The ribs were nothing to write home about. The lettuce wedge was bland as well. As a matter of fact, most of the food was quite bland and either cold or old?! The fried rice at the Chinese food section was dried out and looked unappetizing. After having so many misses with my food, I found that they had Tonkotsu ramen! Ugh! The noodles were mushy and overcooked. Matter of fact, nothing stood out in my memory as spectacular. It was just another buffet. 

After being there for an hour, I noticed that there were some people who really enjoyed this buffet. There was a group of about eight people and three of them were asleep in their chairs while others were getting endless plates of food. We could see that they got their money's worth because there was a mess of plates on their table. Seriously, if you are gonna take a nap, isn't it time to call it quits?? Go back to the hotel if you're gonna sleep, people! 

Anyway, Bacchanal failed to impress me, it was more quantity than quality. I had high hopes, but the food was just mediocre. I would have rather eaten at a fine dining establishment at that price. To me, it was a lackluster experience, but so glad I got it off my bookmark!

I loved Bacchanal when I first came here in 2012 but the last visit, the food was just ok.

Service was TERRIBLE. It was not busy at all but they had only like 3 servers in the entire buffet. We had plates at our table for the entire meal. We got no drink refills for anything except water. When we wanted coffee at the end, I had to wave down someone and tell her that we have not had a server come here the entire time. 

I came here for weekday brunch $39.99 at 2:30 pm so that I could also get the dinner food which starts at 3 pm. Dinner transition does not happen at 3. They were in the weeds and it was still mostly brunch food once we left. So you could end up paying the dinner price after 3 but be eating the brunch stuff.

Ton of soup stations. Taco area is pretty cool, but you cannot make your money back on carne asada. Sushi section sucks. They have cold crab legs for lunch, steamed for dinner. The meats are basically the same for lunch and dinner, but they add lamb and beef ribs. Beef Ribs were awesome. I loved those. Bone Marrow was really good also but it needed to come with some bread or cracker. The Wagyu Steak and Prime Rib were both flavorless and not tender.

Dessert bar looks fancy but its pretty mediocre. Nothing made me want to take a second bite except for the gelato. 

I honestly think I would have enjoyed the Rio World Buffet over eating here. Very disappointing!

My first review on Yelp goes to Bacchanal, because they are just that awesome all around in what they do contributing to the buffet scene in Vegas. :D

First off, the prices. Yes it is expensive for a buffet, especially if you come here for dinner ($50.99, $30 upgrade if you choose to do Buffet of Buffets), but you are not going to regret spending that amount of money once you see the vast diversity of food they have to offer. 

Second, the food. Nowhere else on the Strip can you find the vast quantity and quality of food that Bacchanal has to offer. I've been to many other buffets on the Strip, and none comes close to the titan of buffets that is Bacchanal. Some of the highlights: 

-The seafood selection alone is worth the price of admission. From the fresh oysters on the shell, juicy king crab legs, succulent chilled jumbo shrimps (get it with their horseradish sauce!), and even oyster shooters, it was something truly to behold and enjoy. 
-The meat selection is pure heaven. The big ones: their brisket:  perfectly smoked, seasoned just right, and quite literally melts in your mouth. The prime rib was juicy and tender, and with the au jus, nothing comes closer in terms of buffet quality prime rib. 
-Dessert: my goodness I didn't even know such desserts could exist under one buffet roof. The made to order crepes, selection of sorbet and gelato flavors, crème brulee, cheesecake pops, berry cobbler, and UNLIMITED MACARONS will certainly make your experience at Bacchanal a sweeeeeet one that you won't forget. 
-Some other buffet standouts worth trying: wagyu beef sliders, lobster bisque, oxtail soup, lamb racks, sweet potato tater tots, and the fresh fruit drinks in glass bottles by the meat station. 

Overall, if I were to have a last meal, it would definitely be at Bacchanal. I have no regrets putting down that much money for what I got, and will be coming back for as long as I come back to Vegas. Bacchanal, you have my heart and appetite for life. :)

This is probably the best buffet in the Las Vegas strip. There are some off-strip buffets for a cheaper price, but I would definitely recommend Bacchanal if you are staying on the strip. The food is very decent, and there are a lot of choices. Beware of the lines because they can get very long during lunch and dinner times on weekends.

I just had the buffet. HORRIBLE See the display case with crab and oysters? There were none available on the buffet. Hot dishes were cold, the meats were overcooked and under seasoned, The buffet at Caesars is not as good as the those at Bellagio and Rio, which are 1/3 the price.

In response to the above review, Caesars contacted me and offered me a two-for-one buffet. Oh my God! Why would I pay for another horrible buffet?

The staff were friendly, good atmosphere and it was clean. The food was good but I'm thinking that we may have gone at the wrong time because the selection wasn't worth the price, not at all. I left feeling cheated, especially for a Restraunt in Vegas.

Incredibly disappointing. I was so excited to eat here. The food quality was poor and flavor lacking. Basically an overpriced buffet. Would not recommend at all. I finally decided to stop eating, as it wasn't worth the calories. If you're remotely food educated, skip it and save your money for something better.

Definitely the best buffet in all of Las Vegas. Since the first time my friends and I have gone we always make it a point to go back at least once a trip. 

One thing to keep in mind crab legs are not available until after 3pm on weekdays. And that there are two stations for crab legs (cold up front and hot in the back).

I used the VIP offer on Yelp for VIP line but we only got half VIP line privileges.  On this occasion it allowed us to skip the first "main line" and didn't work for the seating line according to management.  (I've used this thing before and were treated VIP all the way, maybe it depends on whose working)

On the end of my recent long winding road trip, one of the things I looked forward to the most was to visit and check out Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas. I've been to Vegas and have heard of Vegas' famous grand buffet many times but never had the time or chance to visit until very recently.

My travel companion and I decided to stop by Bacchanal on our stop in Vegas for Friday lunch and I was glad I eventually got to try it. There's a huge selection of food...pretty much almost from every continent of the world to try. I had a hard time selecting what to eat given I hadn't been having such heavy meals for such a long time. Despite all the great, quality selection of food (though Asian food aren't as authentic...as expected), my favorite selection/part of the buffet had got to be the green tea and ube ice cream. It was so great that I ended up eating 3-4 scoops of that (on top of 2.5 huge plates of other things from the buffet line!).

For close to $50pp (incl taxes but excl tips) for lunch on Friday, I thought the price point wasn't so bad. We were in Vegas after all! Now that I had tried it..and although I'm generally not a big fan of buffet, I had to say I was glad I tried it..but probably won't be dying to come back any time soon. I ate way too much that it was so painful walking around the strip/in the casino post my buffet feast. I think to keep my eating habit sane, I could take the money and eat for less money and with a better portion size..and maybe get slightly better taste, too.

If you had never been to Bacchanal though..i recommend trying it for the experience. You are in Vegas after all!

This buffet has been on the top of my Vegas list forever and I finally got the chance to so during my last visit. It was quite underwhelming, especially for the price. The service was sub par and nothing too memorable. The crab legs were very good though. Everything else was mediocre. The Asian buffer was the least impressive.  Most dishes are less than comparable to your local sub par Chinese take out. The seafood area was very slick. I was there for about an hour, and no one seemed to come by to clean it up. I did see a few people slip around in that area as well. Wouldn't come back and wouldn't recommend. There's plenty of other buffets in Vegas.

The good, the bad, and the tasty!
The good:
Almost everything to be honest! Usually when you goto a buffet there are hit or miss items. You always get the same/similar things like prime rib, mash taters, salad, etc. and sometimes you eat it all or you leave some because it wasn't sooooo awesome. Well let me tell you I ate every portion I brought back to my table! Mind you because of their serving style and my desire to leave room for dessert I didn't have any heaping portions. 
The bad:
Our service was horrible. Our table was covered in dishes and we only received one refill on drinks. And my husband will drink my drink if his isn't refilled!  So I was irritated AND thirsty :| 
The tasty:
Okay fresh squeezed OJ? Hell to the yes Yuuuum ramen was awesome, steamed king crab legs were cooked perfectly, and my favorite item out of everything was a carne asada taco on their home made flour tortillas!!! Holy hell I could have eaten those by themselves for dinner!!! 
Their desserts were to die for as well :) I had a fresh made Nutella crepe with lots of berries and baklava gelato! Their macarons were not as good a manons buuuut those are hard to beat! I hope the price goes back down because I can't afford $46 a person :(

I came here for dinner on the night of Christmas Eve. It was an EXTREMELY long wait for dinner. I arrived at 2 pm, and I got a ticket which said to come back at 5 pm. I joined the lineup at 5 pm and I was originally with a group of four people, but there were so many people lining up that the workers were only letting parties of two pay first. We decided to split up as they said the wait time for three to five people would be a lot longer. When we paid, we had to line up again for a table. So it's 6:40 pm, and we finally have a table but we're split up.  

Food: I tried the prime rib and american wagyu, which were cooked medium rare. I found that it lacked flavour but it was juicy. I also tried the lobster and king crab which were too salty for my liking. The macarons, chocolate green tea cake, and gelato were probably my favourites of the night. There was no juice bar. However, there was hibiscus juice and hachata which were enjoyable. 

Value: Since it was holiday pricing, we paid around $90 USD per person. The food was decent, but I don't think it's worth spending the amount of money and time that I did to try it out. I probably won't return after this experience, as long line ups are not fun.

So I did two buffets while in Vegas and was thrilled with both experiences: Wicked Spoon for brunch, and Bacchanal for dinner.

Bacchanal definitely lives up to its reputation, it's a wonderland of food. We can very close to closing, which while cutting down considerably on the line to get in and the line for food, I wouldn't recommend doing quite as close to the wire as we did. The lines are long. They have to shuck those oysters by hand, ya know?

The seafood alone is worth the visit. Raw oysters, crab legs, cocktail shrimp, escargot, and help yourself horseradish for the cocktail sauce. 

But the meat is also impressive, with bone marrow, ribs, sausage, steak, slab bacon....all the meats. 

They also have paella, stews, soups, vegetables, fruit, pasta, chicken and waffles, sushi, dessert. 

I wish I could be more specific about that laundry list I just typed out, but it was late and I ate myself into a food fog. Go, deal with the lines, have patience, order a drink, you'll be fine.

My favorite buffet in vegas, pricy  but worth it
always love to sample all the deserts

My favorite buffet in Vegas (The Wynn and Bellagio ones are close but not quite there). Granted it's very expensive, even with my totalrewards perks, but it's worth it. I always manage to devour at least 12 plates before I head to the tables/room. Steaks were not bad for Vegas buffet standards, definitely love the sweets, dim sum was a nice touch, and the prime rib was very juicy. I just wish they'd put out food faster and find a way to lessen the lines but overall, just excellent.

This is the first review I have ever done, I have had bad dining experiences before but never inclined to write a review due to giving the place the benafit of the doubt. I'd like to also add I have eaten here in the past and it was not bad so we decided to give it another shot. But this WAS by far the worst dinning experience I have ever had in Vegas. I don't know where to even start. The food: I tried a variety of meat, wagu, prime rib, beef ribs and ALL were sub par. All meat was super dry and tough. All the salads we chose tasted as if the have been on the shelf for 2 days. It tasted all like out dated baby food. Then for the "famous" crab legs... What a joke. They hardly had any meat on them. You could eat 50 plates worth and never even get full. I also tried a udon soup.. Microwave noodles are better. No joke. The sushi was as good as pre packed grocery store sushi (you'll know what I mean if you ever had real sushi) This is just my experience with that I tried, not even all the things my wife tried. After a very very very disappointing meal we were both optimistic about the fantastic looking dessert. Let me sum it up quick, the mini donuts were STILL FROZEN when we bit into them. The crepes were a joke and the guy making them wasn't very friendly either as they had some what of a confusing system and he did not seem to care to help. The one good dessert was the crème Brule. This is an absolute rip off for 140$ for 2 people. Honestly I'm disgusted with the quality of ALL the food for the price. If you enjoy a good a good meal do not waste your time or money. Trust me I do not mind spending a few extra dollars on food as long as it's not microwaved crap. I am beyond disgusted. Plus I totally understand that a buffet isn't going to have the BEST of everything, but the point of a buffet is to have a huge variety but STILL have good quality to it. I am writing this at the table and me and my wife are still hungry and going else where. How sad, we left a world renowned und buffet hungry. Comical actually.

To top it all off, as we were walking out a gentlemen pasted out and hit his head on the ground and had a seizure. I am trained in emergency response and first aid as I frequently train at work in these fields. It was literally right in front of me so my instincts kicked in and helped the man. Me and another fellow were with the injured fellow until the EMT's arrived (10 min) . I even stayed to make sure he was ok and until they took him away. During this scene the manager and staff had no idea what to do and just stood there dumb founded. I was absolutely not looking for any recognition, but they never even thanked me or the other gentlemen. They were actually rude about the situation as if it was a burden to their day.  Their behaviour and deminor to the situation was a million times worse than the food. WORST EXPERIENCE EVER.

I was excited to go here since it seems to have one of the higher buffet ratings, but it kinda made me want to punch a hole in my derby hat. 

It was on the expensive end of the gorging spectrum, yet didn't seem to offer anything more high end or well made than supposedly lesser buffets. 

They served me beef so raw I thought was practical joke. I thought Ashton Kutcher was gonna jump out and declare I've been Beef'd

Bonus points for having something as unusual as snails, but the reality is they were bland and chewy. A little garlic butter maybe?

The Mac and cheese almost tasted like it was made with whole wheat noodles. Many side dishes were perplexing and unpleasant. This caliber of buffet should have that feeling of having an experienced chef behind the wheel, not some mental patient trying to make dishes out of whatever random ingredients they could find in the back of fridge.

I've had better experiences at Wynn, Wicked Spoon, Sterling brunch, and even several California buffets (Pechanga, Valley View, Pala).

I tried the all you can drink deal too but neglected to read the fine print that it's a limited selection of toilet wine and piss beer. I mean, I had 8 drinks because I could....but it was pretty cheap stuff.

The decor and presentation of food was excellent. Great desserts too. But overall seemed a poor value.

It's my first time trying this place. The machines to sign up was pretty much all having issues. The only way to bypass the issue is if you put down some event, such as a birthday or anniversary on it. 

The food was mediocre and their truffle items was overpowered with all truffle. Their hot boiled crab legs came out smoking, but was really luke warm.

I don't think I would come back here again anytime soon.

Best buffet in the world. The best you can get!!! It's truly the best. The seafood is the freshest. The steak and lamb awesome. For seafood, get the escargot and king crab. The lamb chop and prime rib is spectacular. I come here once every year while I'm in Vegas. Down to every single cuisine it is awesome. Try everything. Everything is good here. From Italian, American, Chinese, Japanese, etc. Everything here won't disappoint and you will truly love this place almost as much as me
Although the food was amazing and there was a wide variety of choices, our service was horrible. I was very surprised at how bad it was especially for the high price that the buffet costs.
Great Buffet and all you cab eat! Very nicely setting and great environment for Family to eat.
Long waiting line but worth it. Hopefully food is as good as I been told from my three sons.

This was my second time here. Last time was during a holiday weekend and the buffet cost me $75 for dinner. This time, we got a Groupon deal (2 breakfast pass for $71 + tax) so I was happy to give the buffet a second chance for a more reasonable price. 

A day later, we also tried the buffet at Wynn which is supposed to be the runner up to Bacchanal and so I could see how they were different.

Bacchanal definitely have a lot more to offer than other buffets at the strip. There are endless options and it makes it hard to try it all (a good thing!). There's seafood options, such as shrimp, crayfish, lobster benedict, there is a meat station, sushi, dumplings, egg rolls, cheese and charcuterie, açaí bowls and smoothies, italian food, juices etc. I can go on. I get that there's something attractive and exciting about having all these options, but when it comes down to it, I think of the expression "quality over quantity". When I think back, there's nothing I'm really craving to try again. Nothing stood out, nothing was special or so flavorful that I would want to go back for it. 

Last time here, I remember that I found the dessert table to be the highlight of my visit. This time, it was really lacking. Maybe it was smaller because of breakfast time, but it was mostly just cookies, chocolate and pastries like donuts and danishes. Last time, they had creme brûlée, made-to-order soufflé, mousse and a lot of other things. Because of this, I would probably recommend to go during lunch or dinner instead. The best thing of the whole buffet was the crepe station where they make you crepes to order. 

It came out to be $40 with tax + tip. I would give it 4 stars if the dessert station had been like it was last time, but it was pretty empty so if I come back it will definitely be during lunch or dinner even if I have to pay a little bit more than for breakfast. If you're looking for lots of food options and just want variety, pick Bacchanal. If you want smaller food selection but a better dessert table, go to Wynn.

My husband and I recently celebrated our 25th wedding anniversary. Our plans were to go home to HI to celebrate with family, but we had some issues with our home that required us to take a staycation instead.  And since we couldn't leave the 9th Island, my husband wanted to splurge a little as we have been waiting for a special occasion to feast at Bacchanal. We've heard so many good things about it and we were excited.

That day, we had to pick out the new flooring and carpet for our home, and the rest of the day we spent at the MGM pool. We couldn't waste a perfect mid-80 degree day. And maybe with the stress of our home and spending all day at the pool, that I didn't think Bacchanal was all that special.  And then I went a few weeks ago for my girlfriends bachelorette party that I still wasn't impressed with this overpriced Las Vegas strip buffet.

I mean, yah, I liked that they had cold crab legs, fresh oysters, steamed crabs in another area, oso bucco, elk sliders, and so forth, but I guess with all the hype that I've heard, I expected more for $56 dinner on a weeknight and $65 for the same dishes for a weekend dinner. Not sure what justifies the high prices when the foods are similar at Wicked Spoon, Bellagio's buffet, Wynn's buffet or the Palms AYCE.

Although the servers were friendly, the restaurant is large, the service is slight bit slower and the pepsi is flat.

I understand wanting the experience, so go for it and I hope you won't be as disappointed as I was.

Great service, slow service, good food, great ambiance, high prices, flat carbonated drinks sets my good experience at 3-stars .

Well my last review for the buffet was not outstanding and we were offered to go back as their guest.  We accepted and we chose to attend the Sunday Brunch.  It was a Great choice!! The shrimp cocktail was fabulous as was the thick and tasty cocktail sauce.  Not like the watery one we had at dinner.  It was spiced right as well.  The choices were many. I sampled the crab claws  the avocado toast and the maceroni and all had my taste buds in a frenzy trying to decide which was best.   They each were so good ...I think it was a choice between best best and best.   Then I tried the prime rib and was skeptical since last time it was dry and it very tasty.  Well at brunch it was juicy and mouth watering and when I took my first taste it melted in my mouth.  The champagne was bubbly and crisp and was the perfect a compliment to my food.  I also had unsweetened tea which didn't have the Bitter taste that most seem to have. I ended with pecan pie.. excellent... Vietnamese coffee...also excellent...and bananas foster...good but better if they served it hot.  All in all I give it 4 stars as price is high for most.  However we'd go again but would look for a Groupon. Enjoy

We waited over 2 hours to get in to eat. They have  a wide variety  available on their buffet. We both became profusely sick after eating here tonight. I wish I could say it was worth the $150+ we spent. It was one of the worst  experiences we have had in Las Vegas.

It's a good buffet but definitely not exceptional. Price is $65 plus tax per person.  We went on Saturday night  10/19. Arrived at 5pm'ish. The wait was about 30 min.  

It's a meat seafood lover haven, but completely lacking a salad bar for vegetarians or for people who wants to eat healthier.   A wide variety of dessert.  Again nothing stood out as outstanding.

My girlfriend and i had heard many great stories of this buffet so we opted it be our only buffet stop during our first trip to Vegas. 

We were very disappointed with our visit. 

We waiting roughly and hour and fifteen minutes just to get inside, this seems reasonable HOWEVER we were  only 10-12 people back from the front. Get to the cashier, $165 for two adults. Again reasonable for 2 all access good meals, HOWEVER. Not good meals, and I'll touch on this in a moment.

We finally get in and get seated, it takes right around 20 minutes for the waitress to come to the table to take our drink order. 

The food, honestly, best part was the deserts! Everyone raves about the crab legs...obviously hadn't had even decent legs. They appear to be pre-notching the legs so that the boiling water gets inside to cook them faster. This in turn seemed to make the aggressively salty and thin.

Only positive other than the deserts was the cut to portion meats section. 

We made 4 separate trips to the buffet, none of our plates were taken from the table until our last trip which led to us sitting and waiting our table (for 2) had space for a trip back. 

My suggestions would be to find a spot down on Fremont St. to visit a buffet. Lower expense / Better food.

Hype, Hype and more Hype is all this place is. It's insanely expensive. Buffet lines to get seated are even more ridiculous. I paid an extra 30 per person to bypass the line so when it was all said & done I spent $325 for 3 of us. I can't say that after all of that I didn't have high expectations but looking back even with NO expectations this would have been a terrible let down. Lines, Noise, Price and make this place a cant win no matter what. I'd like to tell you something about the food so I'll just say that the variety of food is not for majority so most of you will end up eating what your familiar with and those things are not really a big deal. I'm not being ignorant so I won't give this one star because it isn't but 2 Stars is fair when you factor in all of the above information

BEST buffet! They have quality food over quantity! I highly recommend all the seafood and I love that there's variety of food. We all have that mentality of "getting our money's worth" by trying to eat all the seafood (oysters, musscles, king crab leg, etc) but save room for the other things they offer! 

The dessert section- there's soooooo many to choice from! It breaks my heart to see them throw absolutely everything away... So try a bite of everything if it's towards the end of the day...

The design and overall feel of the place is amazing, but the food.. I'm not so sure. My boyfriend and I decided to try this buffet out because we did the TotalRewards 24 hr buffet deal (the deal allows you to go to the 5 buffets listed within 24 hours). When we got to the register, we paid $70 total/ $35 per person WITH the deal, and proceeded to wait approximately 40 mins until we were seated. This kind of ticked me off, because even though they have separate lines for diamond (which I assume are premium members or something) , parties of 6+, and a regular line. They kept sitting everyone else even if they got to the buffet after us. It was frustrating for because we hadn't eaten anything yet.

By the time we sat down, I immediately went to get food. I was pretty surprised they had so much to give, but I realized EVERYTHING I had was too salty, or sat out too long so it became cold/dry. After my second plate, I started to feel sick and ended up throwing up the entire night back in my hotel room.

I wish I had a great experience like everyone else that left great reviews, but maybe next time.

I've anticipated in trying this buffet since it first opened, but never got around to planning a vegas trip. Finally got to try this buffet in August '13 and Oct '13!

My goal is pretty much to eat at every buffet offered in vegas and so far I've tried almost all of them! In my comparison to The Buffet at Wynn, Wicked Spoon, Aria, Bellagio, M Studio Buffet, I would say Bacchanal didn't exceed my expectations :( The Wynn still ranks best for me.

Both times that I've tried Bacchanal was during the time between brunch and dinner so I got to try food from both menus. Surprisingly the food doesn't change much... Both months had the same food for both brunch & dinner. TIP: Make sure you come in between so probably around 2/2:30 so you can get both brunch and dinner but pay only brunch price! Plus the wait isn't as long and goes by fast. Both times I only waited about 30 mins and make sure you get your TR card so you can get a discount it comes out to be about $40 with UNLIMITED MIMOSAS ETC

Anyway the foods that really stood out for me were the sweet potato tater tots in the little baskets they were soooo good! The meat section always had a long line, the standout meats were the lamb chops & ribs. They had all sorts of variety of sausages as well from chicken to turkey. The prime rib was good perfect medium rare. I found out the reason for the long line at the meat station is 'cause there's only one worker manning the station. In other buffets they sort of divide up the meat sections so there isn't always one long line of carnivores waiting in line starving.

In the back is the asian/pizza section. The asian section here is HUGE compared to other buffets. Surprisingly the asian food served here is REALLY good. I like the crispy spicy fish thing (forgot what it was called) and the eggplants. My friends had a bunch of the sushi and said it was good quality. They give you these cute plastic fish soysauce holders also. The dim sum section was good especially the shu mai. The DIY pho broth and tonkatsu broth flavor were on point as well. Same with the roast duck & BBQ PORK!!! So yeah if you have a super asian family, bring them to bacchanal

The pizza here is ok, the Wynn is still better. The dough just isn't crisp enough

CRAB LEGS!! They boil them fresh for you so you get hot crab legs to dip in butter. What most ppl overlook is their delicious clam chowder here!! It's sooo good and creamy with their pretzel/sourdough bread. The breads look like its on display, but you actually can eat them I think that's why most ppl overlook the clam chowder area. They also have baked clams & mussels in little portioned buckets, but those were just ok

The Mexican food station is bomb as well, they've got made to order al pastor, chicken, etc tacos. I love the pulled pork as well it's always nice and tender

Omelette - I like it here 'cause they use the nonstick spray to "grease" the pan instead of ladling a ton of oil onto the pan.

DESSERTS - They've got MOCHI, gelato, and DIY crepes. The dessert section isn't as great as the wynn or wicked spoon. However, they have these delicious chocolate cookies w/ peanut butter filling inside sooooooo good!!

Overall this buffet is HUGE! I pretty much ate everything there, but still something was missing at this buffet, not sure what.

It was ok IMO. I read great reviews on here and was really excited to try this place but I was underwhelmed. I tried a number of different dishes and thought the best parts of the buffet were the cooked salmon in the seafood bar, the wagyu beef, French fries and the desserts. The shrimp was ok but the crab legs were disappointing. At the time I went there were only skinny crab legs and they were really salty. I found other dishes were too salty too IMO including the shrimp dumplings. The Lomein was ok but the duck wings in the Asian food section had no taste really. The pork ribs were decent but the mashed potatoes were far too creamy - not enough potatoes. The elk burger was good. The highlight of the buffet really was the dessert section but the desserts were quick to go and staff didn't put more out fast enough so I didn't unfortunately get to try all the ones I wanted to. 

I would not pay 39 a person again for this buffet and I did not think it was worth the thirty minute wait. Of course buffets are supposed to be the thing you do when in Vegas so this was for the experience only. I would have rather visited a good restaurant. 

A couple of other things to point out - the line for 1-2 parties was far slower than larger parties so that was annoying. Also our waitress thought we were done 3/4 of the way through our meal likely because we had desserts then. So when we got back to our table all of our dishes and drinks etc were gone. The next waitress apologized but still. 

The food gets 2.5 stars. The service gets 3. I don't know how others gave this place more than two stars for food based on my experience and next time I check a new place out I will be sure to check the negative reviews more carefully!

I heard this was the best buffet in Vegas, so I went. It was worth...

PRO TIP - get the groupon!! The lunch had a long line, but with VIP, I skipped the line and got into the buffet instantly. 

I tried everything, legit everything. The only section I do not recommend is the chinese/asian section, it tasted like regular chinese restaurant quality.

This is definitely the best buffet in Vegas.  The lines can be long to get it, but it is so worth it.   This has been our go to when in town for CES, and look forward to it when hanging out with a large group after a long day of being at a conference.  I love the variety and quality of options they serve.  It's so much fun to try everything, and it's actually good.  The issue is that I like a bite of everything so I can't have more than a small taste before I go on to the next option.

The food that was supposed to be hot was cold. For the buffet to be so large the selection of food was meh. We went for breakfast which they call brunch because they offer breakfast and lunch. The place is sprawling but the hostess didn't tell us there was an additional place for deserts which we saw as we were leaving. The cost was almost double what we paid for at the Wynn the previous day, whose buffet quality and selection was phenomenal! This place might be best for dinner but definitely not for brunch.

Overhyped and overpriced.

$70 for dry, overcooked food.  Soup dumplings were terrible, didn't even have any soup in it.  All the fish dishes were bland.  Duck was overcooked, so overcooked it tasted like overcooked chicken.  Bone marrow was undercooked and cold.  Fried green tomatoes tasted like they were left out for days, breading was so hard and tough to chew, same for the bacon inside of it.  Creme brulee was too sweet.  Prime rib was so dry and way overcooked.  "Wagyu" beef was even worse, how do you get Wagyu beef so dry??  Stone crab claws were dry and brittle.  Snow crab claws that were cut open were the worst I've ever had, ridiculously salty and overcooked, all the meat was sticking to the shell.

I gave 2 stars because there were some good things.  Walnut shrimp, ravioli, mushroom soup, mac and cheese, spicy sausage, kielbasa, tamales, cocktail shrimp, remoulade sauce, hot king crab legs were a little salty but definitely not as bad as cold ones.

I've been to better buffets that cost less than half this price.  Don't waste your money.
Amazing offerings. Slow wait for diamond members. Slow staff. Food highlights: dungeoness crab, lobster claws, cioppino, truffle pizza, sushi, dim-sum, deviled eggs, waygu beef, and much much more!!!

Wow.. wow.. wow...I give 5 stars for food variety & taste and 3 for service.. yielding a 4! Best Buffet in Vegas I have been too hands down. And let me tell you I have been to Vegas a many many times.

The cost is actually reasonable compared to restaurant sit down dinners or lunches. At $70 you get everything your taste buds desire. The seating and location are not bad either.


When I was first seated, I waited and waited for the server to come by. I purchased the endless wine and champagne option for an additional $15. After about 5 minutes, I went and got my first plate. Eating and still no waiter. Finally I flagged someone passing by, and they said we will call your waiter. 

I went and got plate number two. And after being there 20 mins I got service, which is horrible. I saw a red jacket employee and asked her if she was a manager and she said yes. So I complained, and she immediately turned things around. She said "I don't know why they are slow, we aren't even at full capacity". So problem solved and wine was flowing to my table :)

Moving on to the good stuff:-

Seafood AMAZING, the Lamb, AMAZING.. Dessert OMG...my photos tell the rest! I'll be back!

Enjoy! And Viva Las Vegas!!!
We have been waiting for 3 hours in different lines. First to put your name down, then to pay and then to get a seat. It's been awful.

Not really great.  Seafood was NOT fresh. Shrimp had bad texture like it was in the fridge for weeks. Meat just broke apart on my fork. Osyter not fresh.  Only thing that was good where desert (ice cream was good) and the bone marrow. For the price I have to give it a one star.  Otherwise it would get a 2.5 stars for the food if price was the same at other local buffet I pay like 31.99 in Seattle.  Any Buffet in Seattle should overdo this one.

This buffet is truly an experience. I am a vegas local so don't frequent buffets much but was able to experience the bacchanal and it was amazing. It's kind of overwhelming at first because of how much food they have, but after picking the things you want to try, the quality of the food is almost unbelievable! Definitely a buffet to try if you're not a local, and even if you are a local, this buffet doesn't compare to all the rest in town.
Great place. Love the seafood option. Great display. Best time to come is before 5pm to avoid long wait.

I've been here twice and this is probably my favorite Vegas buffet (Move over Wicked Spoon!!). Both times I came for lunch around 11am to avoid the long lines. Both times we got seated immediately and on our way out the line was probably an hour long! The variety they offer includes: Seafood, American, Pastas, Cheeses and Cured Meats, Mexican, Japanese, Chinese, and much more. 

My favorite items here are the Brisket and Prime Rib (both are cooked super tender and juicy), and Mussels and Oysters (fresh!), and their drinks (specially the Horchata). However, the star of the buffet is their dessert section! Tons of options for your sweet tooth from Creme Brulee, Gelato, Sorbets, Egg Tarts, Tiramisu, Crepe Station, and much much more!

I even saw Metta World Peace here my last time! It is pricey, but worth it!

Over priced at $75. Same food as the last ten years. Service is uninspiring, slow and at times nowhere to be seen. 
Stay away, that's my advice. 
The house wine is $9/glass and worth about $5/bottle. 
If you get anything hot, eat it fast; the temperature inside the place is "freezing", so the hot crab legs become slow quickly. 
Other than the above, the buffet is a pleasant experience.
There are so many choices at this buffet. Spacious and upscale venue. What I love the most is the dessert area. Food is freshly prepared, top quality and delicious. Highly recommend it!!

We were very disappointed with our dining experience. We had checked the reviews and understood there was king crab legs. There was not and we were told they never have then. The snow crab was ok but not the same. The rest of the buffet was OK. But definitely not worth the price. We also purchased the 24 hour pass which cost $227 for 2 of us including taxes and the up charge for using Bacchanal is $35 each is included also. We will not return here anytime soon.
I'm not a fan of buffets but this one pleasantly surprised me! Bone marrow was on point!

We went there around 5 pm on Tuesday, so there was no line at all, which was great!! 

The food: seafood was great overall. Steamed crab legs, oysters, shrimp, Poke, grilled fish. 

I had a high hopes for Prime Rib, but this was somewhat disappointing. I guess this is not Lawry's. 

Pasta and noodles were very good, and desserts were amazing! 

I know it's more expensive compare to other buffets in Vegas, but I think it's still worth the price to try at least once!

With all of the places to go on Valentines Day in Las Vegas, my wife and I decided to engorge ourselves at the Bacchanal Buffet 8-)

We went through the VIP line and had no wait. We ordered some waters and juice and began our trek through the maze of foods from all around the world. Near the entrance there were quite a few interesting items I had to try: frog legs 4/5, bone marrow 2/5, fried octopus 4/5, oysters 3/5 very big, a couple plates full of crab legs (get a cracker as they are not easy to peel) 5/5 and plenty of shrimp 4/5. Next we ventured to Asia to try some sushi 4/5, fried shrimp and rice, bao buns and dumplings. Then off to Europe for some pasta and meatballs 4/5, pizza and polish sausage 5/5. After about four plates of food we decided we better head to the desserts before we ran out of room.

For dessert we stayed in Europe and had crepes made fresh with a variety of toppings and some macaroons. On the crepe I topped mine with fried bananas, candied almonds and a caramel sauce. It's a must to top it off with powdered sugar and whipped cream ;-) 5/5

We tried almost all of the dessert items between us including donuts, cream brûlée, cheesecake, chocolate dipped strawberries, cookies, flan, sticky buns, gelato and they also had an assortment of candy bars and candy. 

We asked for wheel barrows when leaving but they were fresh out. Thank you Bacchanal Buffet for a World tour.

We decided to walk around the strip after our meal to work off some of the calories we in-took. Not sure how long we would have had to walk to work them all off but at least it was a very pleasant evening with the one I Love.

Alright guys- this was crazy expensive $125 for two people (no alcohol) plus $10 to park. But hey, it's Vegas Baby!! Most people come here to spend money- so here we are. Huge oysters, king crab legs, large shrimp, ceviche all were delicious. Lots of meat choices: prime rib, angus, ribeye, Kobe, roasted turkey, pork ribs- I didn't try them all, but those I did try were good. They offered sushi, sashimi, dim sum, pho and many other traditional Asian choices. They offered salads and cheeses and cold meats. They had a Mexican area with posole, Spanish rice, carnitas... so many choices. The dessert section had so many things to choose from, everything was yummmo! Honestly this was one of the best buffets I've ever been to. There are tons of choices, like all buffets, but the quality of food was top notch.

I don't get how this place is popular. I went for the first time (pretty sure it will be my last time as well) on a Thursday night around 5:30pm and waited over two hours to get a table. The cashiers looks like I owe them a million bucks and obviously don't want to work there. After the initial around of drinks, the waitress never came back to refill any of our cups and just disappeared. I am not sure was it because I didn't tip at the cashier before getting a table but I am not use to tipping before actually receiving the services and was glad I didn't in this case. Food selections were big and displayed nicely but non of them taste good. From my understanding, there were suppose have king crabs but they were no where to be seen. At the seafood section, only shrimps and oysters were served. They also had a sign saying the steam crabs were at the Italian section but they were small crab legs and were 100% not king crabs. Overall, the place looks fancy and good for photos but that's it.

Five stars because of our waitress, Josephine, W., would be 4 stars without her. She was right on with cleaning up and getting our next glasses of wine. Didn't even have to ask her for our next drinks. Even checked on us whether we're driving or not before bringing out our next drinks. 
I've been to other Vegas buffets before and this buffet is good but not great. The food selection is good but not great compared to other Vegas buffets.
Amazing food and Service!!!frog legs is great all food was Outstanding!!!Atmosphere is wonderful an my waitress!!!
其实还好，没有评价说的那么好 毕竟他只是一家buffet 餐厅！首先值得点赞的是他的品种很多，你可以在一家餐厅吃到所有你想吃的！当然口味和品质可能没有那么的好，作为buffet 我给75分！服务是很好的，酒水是额外付费的！价格相对于国内是真的便宜！国内hyatta一个人rmb400 so......这家餐厅总体给80！

The king of buffets in Las Vegas, at least according to this yelper. This is a must try, it is a bit pricey but the sheer selection and top grade ingredients make it well worth the price. You will have so many entrees, sides, and desserts to try that you won't be able to sample them all... but if you are a foodie like me you will attempt the feat to sample as much of the food as possible.

Best buffet i have ever been to!!! Soooo many options i had to go twice!  Customer service was awesome! Very knowledgeable team. Teresa(who shares my name and even spells it correctly lol) had great suggestions on what to try and even got my very picky son to try the lamb! Btw he loved it!!
Love this buffet. Come here every time we are in Vegas. Especially love the seafood selection and desserts.

Great place loved the seafood and service 
Great prime rib  and food and drinks we went there as a family is on the expensive side yet worth jtmgreat

Not top knotch! I have no idea what the fuss is all about. Why people wait 2 plus hours in line for cheap crab legs and food sitting out for hours. Pretty dissapointed with our experience paying dinner price and being served shitty snow crab legs not even the same kind of crab displayed in the case in the entrance. Some of my food was obviously old or had been exposed to the open air food troff. Who wants to go sit around a bunch of people slopping down wet food like pigs.

Not worth it never going back

There were 5 of us.  We were so forward looking to this buffet.  paid extra to get the seafood tower brought right to our table.  Seafood was sub par.  No taste to the 2 types of crab.  No taste to the lobster.  snails like rubber.  Oyster that they served were the ones you usually BBQ.  Low grade.  We also tried there meats.  Ribs way over seasoned.  Prime ribs not much flavor.  The group did like the deserts.  I would never go again if it was free.  Way overrated.

I recall my last business trip to Nevada, I searched for a quality buffet to attend and a friend who drives taxi suggested this as the finest in Las Vegas.   Boy was he right!  The cleanliness of the area was impeccable even though the line of people was tremendous.  I thanked the woman who was taking such good care to keep the food serving area clean and neat.  To me the serving area being kept clean and strictly organized is vital to my enjoying my visit.  Whoever manages the employees at Bacchanal, thank you for teaching your employees to care for and nurture their buffet line.  I applaud their efforts!  I cannot wait to return!

Not worth the hype
Three stars for service and for the variety of food. However the quality was mostly lacking in flavor.

Bacchanal Buffet, the highly touted buffet in Las Vegas I coveted. Family and friends have indulged. It was my turn =)

No wait time! Wednesday at 6pm. YES!!

I was seated immediately and my drink order placed. It was time to indulge. 

I scoped out each station, taking mental notes of what looked good. 
I decided on the seafood station for my first plate. 
My second plate was from the carving station (BBQ & Prime Rib this evening)
My third plate was from the cheese & cured meat station. 
Last but not the least, Dessert. 

My food rating of each dish:
GREAT DISHES
*Lamb Chops - tender, perfectly cooked medium rare, yum!! Get the mint jelly too. 
*Shrimp Cocktail - Big pieces of shrimp. Not over cooked like most shrimp cocktails, perfect. 
*Goat cheese with fig - wow, wow, WOW!
*Mushroom & Truffle Soup - this was decadent, creamy with that earthy richness, Yum!!

GOOD DISHES
*Oyster Shooter - the oyster was just okay, but the liquid it came in was delicious. Cucumber juice?
*Brisket - I asked for the fatty part, yum!  Melds in you mouth goodness. I didn't see any BBQ sauce though. 
*Polenta - the only thing I got from the Italian station. 
*Wagyu Slider - delicious. It would have been better with mayo. (Which I found after I ate it)
*Mango Pudding - the coconut jelly made this dish good!!
*Coconut Calamansi Dacqoise - I don't know what a "Dacqoise" is, but it was like a macaron to me. Lol. 
*Beignet - great with coffee, just too sweet. 

OKAY DISHES
*Raw Oyster - it would have been better if it was sucked better. The oyster was still attached to the shell and a lot of shell bits in the oyster itself. 
*Prime Rib - the medium rare parts were good, other parts were very chewy. 
*Creme Brûlée - not too sweet, yum. 
*Goat cheese with basil - good flavor!!

BAD DISHES
*BBQ Pork Spare Ribs - too salty & not tender. 
*Jonah Crab Claws - even though they were pre cracked, it was still hard to eat. The crab meat was stuck to the shell. Over cooked. 
*Mint Gelato - first gelato I asked for was pistachio, I got "Mint" instead. Since I ask for 3 other flavors, by the time I got to my table, the mint had started to melt and ruined the other 3. Oh, I don't like mint ice cream / gelato. 

Info: The plates are HOT. Super hot. Be careful. If you want cold plates, get them from the salad station. 

Service was good. 

Suggestions: it was hard to get some of the dishes. For example the soups. The clearance between the pot and the shelves on top of it was too low. It was hard not to spill the soup because the ladle was hitting the shelving. 

The flow of some of the food station was also a bit off for me.

I didn't get anything from the Chinese & Mexican stations, I was too full. Lol. 

The food here was good, I definitely indulged, okay, over indulged. Lol. 

Solid 4 Stars. 
Try it for yourself and decide.

It was amazingly large. The food was beautifully prepared. The largest selection of food I've ever seen at a buffet. Every thing was very tasty. 
However,that being said. The wait to even get in was long and we went at an off time. About 2:45 pm. And our table was so far away from the food,by the time we made it to the table some of the food was cold. So try and plan on a long wait to get in. And ask for a table closer to the hot food. Also the price is big. 140 for two people.

It was amazingly large. The food was beautifully prepared. The largest selection of food I've ever seen at a buffet. Every thing was very tasty. 
However,that being said. The wait to even get in was long and we went at an off time. About 2:45 pm. And our table was so far away from the food,by the time we made it to the table some of the food was cold. So try and plan on a long wait to get in. And ask for a table closer to the hot food.

Worst waiting experience me and my family have ever had. We had to wait an hour just to check in with the hostess, and then our hostess had the worst attitude toward my family, which pissed me off IMMENSELY. Not to mention she checked in people out of order for some odd reason, sending my family to the back of the line and making our wait even longer. Then the hostess proceeded to ignore my mom and respond in a stuck-up tone when all she did was ask the hostess a question. Worst customer service possible, we couldn't even get to the food, we lost our appetite from the start. We would rate this lower, but 1 Star is the lowest you can go.
I recommend the VIP service if available, totally worth it for $40 more to skip the huge line! You also get a seafood tower!

The buffet had plenty of options for different palatea.  The downfall for us was that the majority of the seafood was cold.  There was a station doing hot crab legs, but the lobster claws and everything else was cold.  Ice cold. It was an experience, and I liked how some of the food was already plated and you could just grab and go.  We went on a Friday at 330 and there was no line.  We won't return.

Food and service (from Romulus) this morning was fabulous. 

I've been to the buffet many times and this is why I love coming back. Weekend buffet is def better. Crab claws, lots of fresh seafood and huge variety. 

The team is very attentive. Especially for a Vegas buffet. Especially over places like the Cosmopolitan. I came straight from the airport and despite not staying at Caesar's, they checked my bag while I ate and hit the tables. 

There's a reason bacchanal is voted #1 every year. I'll see you next time for sure!
So many to choose from. It's fun to mix and match. The desert was so good. Highlights: desert, tri-tip, and oyster shooters.

I haven't been to Bacchanal buffet in 7 years due to increased High prices. This time I purchased a deal on travel zoo deal $35.99 for breakfast on M-Th 7am-11am. We arrived at 10am and went to express line and shown our voucher to cashier. The hostess gave us a table near the Asian side. I head first to Asian to eat sui Mai (tasty) and congee (watery) then to Italian side for their pizza area which they make the best something light for breakfast and wait for lunch. 

The servers were transitioning the breakfast to lunch. 
The meats area was busy with prime rib, brisket, fried chicken w/waffle, sausages, Mexican food  w/various tacos -shrimp, chicken which was tasty. The seafood area was small claws, shrimp, snails. The dessert area had no macaroons just small cupcakes, gelato, etc. My stomach was stuffed after 2 plates. I think the quality declined since I ate there 7 years ago.

Went there with high hopes due to recommendations despite high cost. Solely going for king crab but what a BIG disappointment!! Firstly, cocktail shrimps are are SOGGY! Then king crab...You don't get to grab as much as you want. Have to give server your plate and you'll get 1 king crab with plate full of SNOW crab. And my king crab is covered with sheet of ICE! Cracked it open, it was like eating ice popsicle!!! Sorry, NEVER AGAIN!!
P.S. Me & one of my friends both had upset stomach that night which I believed was the oysters we ate there because other people in our group who hadn't had oysters were just fine.

Overpriced, but the brisket was really good.  The desserts were not that great.  Overall this buffet had a large variety of food.  The sushi was worse then fast food sushi...the seafood had a nice spread and tasty.

Let me do you a favor and save you any argument on your next venture to the Strip of what the best buffet in Vegas is. It's here.

Yes, for breakfast it is a little pricier than the Rio or pretty much the other options. But it is 1000% worth it. They have everything here. You've got the American breakfast basics...and the Mexican breakfast basics...and the low-carb basics. There's Asian fare (including donuts I haven't had since in China). There's an entire section of charcuterie and cheese (it's phenomenal cheese). They have pressed juice. They have mini everything. They have sugar free and sugar OD desserts. There's a ton of places to sit. It's divine.

When my boyfriend and I went, we went about 30-45 minutes before they switched to lunch. So, we got to try the breakfast AND the lunch options. I would have eaten more (there were these awesome looking sliders and soups) but while the mind was willing, the body was not strong enough.

I feel this will be my only buffet in Vegas from here on out. My only regret of coming here is not having a big enough stomach to cram in everything I want to consume.

Came here for dinner years ago, then recently came for breakfast/brunch on a weekday and I have to say the breakfast was the best! We ended up getting there near the end of breakfast and beginning of brunch. So many delicious breakfast foods by the time it was my 3rd round, they were changing some of the foods and I was getting intense fomo so I had to go around a couple more times before I was satisfied.

Very disappointed for the price. I had looked up the Bacchanal buffet and was so excited to try it. This was the only buffet we were hitting this trip and given it's rated one of if not, the best buffet in the world I had high expectations. However, what I was greeted with was a buffet focused more on the variety over quality. And the variety wasn't great. There was no lobster, no king crab, no Dungeness, only snow crab. The rib eye was tough and tasted more like roast beef, the salmon was super dry, we went back after a brand new fresh salmon was brought out thinking it was dry from sitting there but the freshly brought out salmon was also dry. You couldn't even taste the lobster in the lobster bisque. The only oysters they had were in a bloody mary mix that was so incredibly strong you couldn't taste the fresh oyster. I even tried to take the oyster out and eat it alone but it sitting in the bloody mary mix made it impossible to taste anything else. There was pizza that was super dry but aside from the mac and cheese there wasn't even any pasta despite containers of dry pasta displayed all over. 

My friend had the bone marrow and said that was good, the sushi was pretty good and while disappointed to see only snow crab, that was good, but I don't really know how you mess that up. The mac and cheese was super creamy but was pretty bland, the shrimp was obviously just plainly boiled and tasted the same as I could buy from our local grocery store. 

The positive, was the dessert. The dessert options were plentiful and delicious. My only criticism there was the cheesecake was sugar-free and tasted like a no-bake cheesecake which disappointed me. 

Overall, the buffet here at the Casino in Oregon is 10 times better than the Bacchanal and half the price. I'm so disappointed that we didn't try the Wicked Spoon instead. I don't recommend coming here. Perhaps my expectations were too high after all the build-up but it is DEFINITELY nowhere near as good as other lower class, cheaper, buffets I had in Vegas. The one at Excalibur is better. I wouldn't come here again and wouldn't recommend it to anyone. I've in fact told my friends and family not to come here. 

Save yourself some money, ignore the hype and go elsewhere. I would say it was an off day but I overheard other people stating that it was just as good as every time they come. If that is the case, they are wasting a lot of money. I had really high hopes, it's unfortunate to walk away so disappointed.
Pretty good. A bit pricey, but best value on the strip. Tip to avoid the line: You should definitely go for lunch to skip the wait (relatively) and a bit cheaper as well

$70+/person is not worth it for this buffet. The reason why we came here is its closer to the Bellagio fountain (and I really want to see and experience it firsthand). So instead of going to Wynn for the buffet, we went here instead. My husband and I have been to a considerable amount of buffet, and so far this place is not at all impressive. The meat is cooked dry, their Japanese selection is limited, and no King Crab. I would think for the price we're paying there should be King Crab. Their buffet should be priced at $30, IMHO.

When 13 of your friends travel to Vegas for a weekend of debauchery for your birthday, you want them to experience the best of the best. Out of all the itineraries that we had, I was most excited for brunch at Bacchanal (my favorite buffet on the strip) as our last hurrah to end the weekend before we fly our separate ways back home. 

We were all prepared to spend $60+ for brunch on a Sunday at around 1pm, but unfortunately my birthday fell on Easter Sunday this year. I was told that they usually up the prices for holidays, so I called them ahead of time on the number listed on their website to ask ahead how much it would be. I spoke to a gentleman and he said it is $60. Kewl, we make our trek to Caesars palace from our hotel. 

When we got there, the woman that was in charge of the line told us that it's $80. She pointed to a sign/poster that stated "Easter Feast $79.99" But clearly above it, it says April 21st, brunch until 3pm is $59.99" (picture attached). She still insisted that it's $80. Now, if anyone knows me, I'm pretty easy going and have never asked to 'speak to a manager' in my life. I've been waiting to eat this meal for months but I did not appreciate the bait and switch. So she called the manager Brian, and a gentleman showed up. He was polite and accommodating. I explained to him what's going on, and why the poster is confusing, and I even called ahead of time, if I had known, we would've gone somewhere else. He asked what number I called, I showed him my call log. He then said that he will honor the $60 and asked how many was in my group. He seemed a bit overwhelmed when I said 13, but he somehow made it work and escorted us to a nice large semi private area for my group. I really appreciated that! However, as he escorted us to the register to pay first, the ladies at the register were openly talking crap to each other about the accommodation he did for us "The poster clearly says is $80, idk why this is, etc etc etc" *cue eye roll here*

Food was as delicious as I remembered it. The pasta was amazing, tonkotsu broth for the ramen was more flavorful that I expected, sushi was fresher than the usual buffet sushi. My friends enjoyed their meat selection and seafood, and the tacos were good. I didn't care for the poke. Dessert was great. Gelato and Thai tea boba yassss. Hilda took care of our table and she was great. So big shout out to Brian and Hilda!

I was super excited to go here!
Was very disappointed!
This was our first stop once we got into town..
Most of the dishes we tried were barely Luke warm,
The meatballs were actually cold!
