Asked for French toast to be made, they told me to come back in 4 minutes, which I did but it was never made.
Never ended up getting that-
Best thing we had were the deserts!
Not worth the price

This place has somehow gotten better since the last time I was here a couple years ago and it was amazing! For the first time ever out of all the buffets I've visited, I can truly say that each item here is of top quality. So fresh and perfectly made by the chefs that each tasted like a $$$$$$ dish I would've ordered at an expensive restaurant.

First of all don't come here without the Groupon. It lets you go through the VIP line and the price per person is cheaper than the regular price and you get some free alcohol with it.

We came here around 2 (must pay by 2 PM if you use a Groupon) and we enjoyed every minute of our time here. The carving station is the BEST and had the hands down best brisket and prime rib I have ever had. The brisket was like butter, literally. So tender I didn't even know what tender was until then. The prime rib was encrusted with some coffee beans and was extraordinary and unique in flavor. If you're lucky you can try some of the beef ribs carved off the prime rib which was juicy and delicious. 

My absolute favorite from this section was the elk burger sliders. Yes, ELK!!! IT TASTED LIKE HEAVEN!! Basically tasted like a high end beef slider with the perfect caramelized onions and some kind of fancy melted cheese. I've ever had this kind of cheese before so I don't know what it is, but it was so creamy!!

The sushi here was amazing too which is a surprise to see at a buffet. All their food was amazing quality and made fresh by actual chefs that you see behind the glass. For the first time ever, I was so full by all their different items that I forgot to eat my favorite street tacos al pastor from the rotating taco grill!

The desserts were amazing and super fancy with the cool flavors of gelato like black sesame and Hawaiian guava passion fruit mango. They have giant chocolate covered strawberries along with the best crepes I have ever had from the made to order crepe station.

The best part of this was the super fresh raw oysters and the steamed king crabs. My gosh, we were in food heaven. No trip to Vegas is complete without coming here. They are truly the iconic Vegas buffet experience you'd dream of here.
This is literally the best biggest in Vegas, dare I say the country! It's unreal. I don't even know how to properly review this place, it's just that good. You have to experience it for yourself.

Came here for dinner during the labor day weekend. Food is excellent ( king crab, waygu beef, bone marrow...ect). Come early, the line getting in is long like as if you're waiting for an amusement ride.

I honestly don't understand the hype, maybe we were there on a bad day.    We were there Wednesday afternoon, roughly $50 each and the wait was under 10 minutes.   Right after we paid, there was a guy taking a photo of us, which I knew they would try to sell it later.   We didn't buy the photos, can't quite remember what they asked for, but it was some ridiculous price.    And the photo was an up close shots, with no significant background, looked like it could have been taken anywhere.
Now about the food, let's just say it was baddd.   The seafood was smelly, we couldn't eat it.   The "fishy" smell was so strong, our hands stunk, you couldn't even wash off the smell.   They had a variety of bread, all were dry and stiff.  Even in the Asian food section the bread sticks "Dau Chao Quay" were hard and crunchy.  Not soft and crispy the way they should be, but dry and rock hard.   Sweet and sour soup tasted badly, sushi didn't look appetizing...    
Prime rib wasn't too bad and desserts were good.    But overall it was a huge disappointment, maybe because of the hype and high expectations.    For us, it was our first time and likely our last.
This is my favorite buffet in Las Vegas - has everything thing you can imagine and always fresh and delicious

Reason for Visit: First time coming to Vegas and was told this is a must go for anyone who eats. 

Menu: Like most first comers, I was extremely surprised and shocked that there are those who wait 3 hours to get in. (Pro tip: get their Groupon online for free VIP line so you only have to wait ~half hour ish to get in). I of course am thinking that the people who line up 3 hours for this are all out of their minds and are probably in retirement. 

When I got in the buffet and got seated,  I knew these people were in fact geniuses and were simply waiting at heaven's gate to head into the promised land. 

This buffet has essentially every food known to mankind. They got your Chinese, Viet, Mexican, Japanese, Western, Jamaican, etc. Unfortunately, since I am in significant debt and also went to the casino before hand, I was in no mood to try the less costly items. 

I essentially had a few things only, their wagyu, crab legs (cold and cooked), oysters, bone marrow, shrimps, fresh watermelon juice and desserts. 

Their wagyu was extremely tender and juicy. This was extremely flavorful, highly recommended. Their cold crab legs didn't have much flavor to them, but that is to be expected. Their cooked crab legs (at Italian station) were much better, definitely recommend everyone to try their cooked ones as well. Oysters and shrimps were fresh. Bone marrow was so tasty and just melts in your mouth. Their fresh watermelon juice was so refreshing especially after the salty fatty foods, I must had drank a jug of it by the time I left. 

Their desserts station was bigger than my room. Their gelato bar is a must go visit. 

Service: My waitress replaced my dishes fast as I was eating extremely fast at beginning due to their 2 hour seating limit. She was very friendly and professional. I suspect she is used to serving foodies such as myself.

Atmosphere: Extremely well renovated, seats were very comfortable. Whole place was extremely clean. Foods all were labeled and were constantly being refilled non stop. 

Overall: Price tag for a meal of a king is ~$80/person. This was definitely the highlight meal of my trip. Highly recommended.   

Pro tip #2: check in on Yelp for free champagne
Best buffet! food is incredible and the service is even better especially at the crepe station.

Obviously, when you go to Vegas it's about overindulgence; so, we clearly planned to overeat while in Vegas (now that I'm home, a fast, diet, starvation, etc. is calling me)! We decided to stop at the moderately priced (clearly being sarcastic) Bacchanal. 

We went on Friday around 5ish, the line was not bad at all.  In fact, the only reason there was a (slow moving) line was because there were only two cashiers. Well, we got through the the line, dropped $125 for my hubby and I and we were seated.  Our pleasant and attentive server approached us immediately and got our drink orders. 

First impression: At first glance the buffet appeared to have a lot of options of various types.

After loading up our first (second, third, you get it...) plate, the options in each category were minimal and the food itself was at times, lacking flavor and just meh.  

The steamed snow crab legs were so good! So, so, so good! The pizza was also quite good. My husband really enjoyed the pork belly over polenta and the pork ribs. Everything else was honestly JUST okay. 

We would certainly pick another (possibly cheaper) buffet option next time. For the money we spent, I wasn't impressed.

I've been to Vegas many times and this is easily my favourite buffet and I make a point to go each time I'm in town. It's on the pricey side but well worth it. So many items to choose from all great quality , you don't feel like you're eating "buffet food". It is very beautiful inside and huge ! (Still there's always a long line though!) They have various sections of food based on type ex Asian , Italian , meat station , seafood station etc the meat and seafood sections are amazing they do not disappoint and neither does the rest of the buffet.  Save some room though if you can because They have a huge dessert section with every item that will still be drool worthy even after having eaten multiple plates of food ! (I assume this because you're going to want to try everything , self control has no place here lol). staff is also always friendly and professional and really a well oiled machine , they don't miss a beat and everything is always clean and the food is always fresh. A must try buffet in Vegas !

I had high expectation for this buffet due to good reviews on Yelp and Youtube. My hubby and I have tried Buffet of the buffets  a few months ago and we did not get a chance to dine here at Bacchanal until recently.. 
When we came here Saturday night and it was pretty crowded.. We had a great service from a very a nice lady.. But with regards to the food selections, I think there were only a few that stood out (prime rib, tri-trip,lobster claws, tacos, and ceviche). Honestly, I think the Paris, Carnival and M buffets are better because the set up are spacious unlike in Bacchanal where it's cramped and there is no wiggle room going from one section to another.We are glad to try this place but there are better options available elsewhere.

Still my favorite buffet in Vegas, even though I don't think it's as good now as it used to be a few years ago.

Crab legs for days!!!! And their Asian food section is actually quite good. My fave for some reason is the porridge! Perfect for that hang over morning after.
Another favorite of mine is the juice bar! Think pineapple, tamarind, carrot, etc.

Try to go at off times and non-weekend if you can, because the line can get pretty long (1hr+ wait). But they do have an option where you pay $25/person to skip the line...worth? well that depends on your schedule and how hungry you are :]

My bestie and her BF were in town and wanted to head on over here as they've heard nothing but good about it. I never really seek out buffets, but when tourist come I will oblige and indulge.

Just a note that a few of the pictures show a price list when it first opened and it is NOT accurate. The profile picture is a outdated price list. 

This is the cost (currently) as follows:

Breakfast (Mon - Fri, 7 a.m. - 11 a.m.): $25.99
Brunch (Sat - Sun, 8 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $40.99
Lunch (Mon - Fri, 11 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $32.99
Dinner (3 p.m. - 10 p.m.): $45.99 on weekdays, $50.99 on weekends

One thing about this place is that it is sleek and modern and was very well designed and the music selection contemporary downtempo type stuff. Of course we came for the food and the buffet was nicely spread out and nothing was looking old and dried out. We came around 4ish on a monday so it wasn't busy and had no line. That sometimes is a cause for concern that they wouldn't rotate out the lunch out fast enough, but everything was fresh by that time. I wouldn't want to wait hours in a line to eat either and would probably greatly change my opinion of this place. I rarely think anything is worth standing around 1-2 hours so I will go before rush times. 

I got a little bit from various savory stations among several rounds and nothing was bad. Even at some other higher end buffets I've had some misses I did not eat which did not occur here. Most ranged from good to very good with only two OK items (fried chicken could be juicier but had good breading, ceviche a little too lime and not enough salt). I was most surprised that the oysters were sweet and not strongly briny, mussels and snow crab were good. The meat station was solid - the veal steamship was juicy and fall apart tender, the lamb chops were perfectly cooked and good quality and the skirt steak was really tender which I'm normally not a fan of as it can be stringy. The baked salmon was surprisingly not overcooked and was perfect, The handmade dim sum were rather nice as I went back for seconds on their pork and leek dumpling. 

Dessert wise they were also strong. I really enjoyed the panna cotta with berry, the creme brulee was great texture (though the top could have been torched more), their warm pizookie type cookie was awesome with a scoop of ice cream and fresh whipped cream. They had french macarons, which is my favorite, and theirs was surprisingly decent! I loved the orange with chocolate creme macaron out of the 5 flavors they had and overdid it with inhaling these. 

Service was great. He was on top of drinks, but was also friendly and engaging conversation. 

My bestie really enjoyed the variety and definitely thought it was worth it and gives it a 4 while she giggles about my funny hobby. Her BF is a bit of a picky eater and doesn't eat some of the higher ticket items like the seafood bar to have made it worth the high pricetag of what he got, though he thought it was good. 

I can see why this buffet gets rave reviews. It is quantity that is serving up some quality too. I don't know if it's "good value" enough for me to return on my own, but I'm sure I'll be back at some point with tourist friends.

I honestly didn't even know that buffets were a big deal in Vegas, but when I found out they were, I knew that I needed to go to the best one. After a good deal of research, we landed on Bacchanal, and it was pretty fabulous.

Our setting: Wednesday, arrived right at 11am. There was literally no line. We elected to come in right at the breakfast/lunch changeover time, paying the lunch price, because we were more in it for the lunch foods. However, a decent amount of breakfast stuff was still out.

Our strategy was to walk the whole line to check out the offerings, and I'm glad we did because it helped me prioritize my choices. We stayed for a full two hours which was really the perfect amount of time. My absolute favorite things that I ate were custom-made ramen with mushrooms and pork belly, chicken and waffles, tri-tip steak with mashed potatoes, creme brulee, and gelato. I also ate a mini burger, mac and cheese, chilaquiles, a mixed berry smoothie, avocado toast with lump crab, and many desserts (chocolate ganache, lava cake, passionfruit panna cotta). It was all delicious. It was also all pre-portioned, which made it easy to have small servings and not overeat. I honestly didn't feel over-stuff by the time we left. There were so many dishes that I didn't try and really something for everyone's taste: several preparations of fish and shellfish, fancy pizzas, a whole charcuterie section, 5 other custom-made Asian broth dishes, tacos, soups, sushi, a custom-made crepe station, etc. The experience was certainly worth the price (particularly in Vegas, where many restaurants are pretty pricey to begin with).

We had very pleasant customer service from the cashier, the chefs, and our waitress. Make sure to bring some cash to tip the waitstaff!
Good selections of seafood, extremely busy so it's not easy to walk around and review all the items easily. Tentative staff was amazing. Not really worth the price

So this is more like 3 1/2 stars.  We went to Bacchanal this past Sunday for Dinner.  The tomahawk steak was on point...it was downhill from there which is a true bummer for me as I was looking forward to eating here for 14 months.  Snow crab legs instead of king, and I agree with other reviewers that their flavor was gone due to being pre-cracked.  I tried this and that but it became apparent that the quality was just not there.  It was more like cafeteria food which is brutal I know, but for $50?? I expected much more.  Another issue was that there were several items that i was looking for were missing.  The biggest issue for me in this area was the mochi ice cream.  I looked all around the huge dessert island and could not find it.  I asked a cook behind the counter and she said "oh it's over here" pointing to the gelato area so I walked back over there thinking I just missed them.  She caught me before I got there and said "I'm sorry, there's no mochi today"; I'm guessing someone  intercepted her and set her straight.  This brought my anger level up to boiling but I had to keep my cool as I didn't want to ruin it for my wife.  I then saw the Chef De Cuisine and asked him when the mochi was coming out.  He acted surprised that it was not out and stated he would bring a a plate of mochi to my table.  10 minutes later he came toward my table with four different kinds of mochi: orange, green tea, vanilla and mocha.  He apologized for taking so long but stated that he had to go to a different restaurant to secure them.  THAT was huge to me and garnered them another star.  In closing, I think this proves that quantity does not necessarily save the day.  I'd prefer half the dishes and twice the quality compared to what Bacchanal offers.  After this dinner the wife and I decided that we're going to swear off buffets (again).  On the plus side the room is beautifully designed and decorated.  The shrimp and grits were really good, the rolls in the Asian area were actually really good.  The busser in our area was clearing plates from our table like his life depended on it.  He was maybe the best busser I've ever seen in action and was a complete opposite to the reviews I've read in the past year.

We tried to come here on a Monday and were met with an hour wait just to get in the line to the buffet that was an estimated hour longer. We decided against it and came back on a Friday instead. I would keep in mind that more people try to go Monday-Thursday because of the cheaper price - reserve if you can or arrive a couple hours before you're hungry! Once we came on Friday, the line was only a half hour and COMPLETELY worth it. So many seafood options and the best dessert table I've ever seen, we stayed for over an hour! While it may seem a bit pricy, there were so many options for all and it was the best buffet experience I've had.

Buffet was great my family and I will be going there every time we go .. Line moves very fast and great prices all the servers are more than friendly constantly checking up on us even when they are not assigned to our table... thank you so much for the great experience and can't wait to come again.  So many choices and not enough time will be going for lunch and dinner this week ..
The crab legs were the best part of the seafood portions unbelievable .  Have attended many buffets none like this and the snails were amazing also .

There even was a carving station with huge slabs of bacon( to die for )...  the best part was the Asian station hand rolled sushi, sashimi, dumplings, shu Mai can't ask for a better time here at Cesar's palace .... 

ask for Julie or Gwen when you are there they are amazing and never stop making sure you and your family are more than satisfied .. 
thank again

The Bacchanal Buffet.  Don't make me do it anymore Mommy!  It is always a great idea, like making plans with a coworker for some weekend event.  Until you do it...

The Bacchanal aka the Caligula Buffet is to the hundreds of people embracing the overall excess is a true Vegas experience.

Beautifully set in Caesar's Palace, there are stations for whatever your heart desires from seafood to dim sum, tacos to Italian, donuts to gelato.  Dear lord, just make it stop!

The food is the star in its own right, wonderfully prepared my an army of chefs and likely 10 times more backroom staff that keeps the food plentiful and beautiful.  The flavors unlike the majority of the offerings in this town are prepared like each item is served from an al a carte menu.

Nothing is dry and dead.  The only unfair part is that your senses are overwhelmed by the shear size and smells of the food!

Do I go left to the fresh shrimp cocktail or right to the hand sliced charcuterie board??   Are the giant shrimp in the spicy Chinese sauce next of the ever so tender brisket.

I hear rumors there is a salad bar but honestly I didn't see it.  I broke no bread, I didn't scoop soup and delve into the deli.  I stayed true to the things I loved the most.

When I was done, my 60 year old body gave me the 'WTF were you thinking?' Sort of feeling!  And alas it was correct.  You need to be ready for something like this.   A dozen crab claws sounds awesome in theory. 

But go, experience if.  Get a Groupon and save some cash but if you can afford it, try it.  It will not disappoint.

Definitely worth the wait. Everything is so good!! They raised the price though for their champagne brunch. Paid around $50.

I love how they also have hot crab legs. The roast beef was good and they also have salmon sashimi! LOTS of options to choose from and some interesting ones as well like their Thai Tea Boba Float. It's a must whenever I'm in Vegas!

I went to the breakfast buffet on my birthday with my bf! As locals we have been to many buffets, but this hands down is the best one in town. From the fresh watermelon, cucumber and organe juices in cute little glass bottles to the amazing cheese bar I was beyond impressed. Everything I ate was delicious. Chicken and waffles in a cute mesh basket, quiche, amazing kale smoothies, so many interesting choices. I like how there was sushi in the morning which was quality. I love how there was healthy and fresh options as well. There are so many options for so many different tastebuds. We got champagne to celebrate. We will be returning!

Really not worth the price. Maybe it once was, but it definitely is not anymore. The food is very bland and the service was slow. The desserts look good but don't taste special at all.
We got the Mac and cheese for giggles and we found that the macaroni wasn't even cooked all the way through. The meat is chewy and the best dish there was the Honey Walnut Shrimp. You might as well just go to Panda Express. 
I really can't believe it was almost $60 per person for dinner. 
We didn't finish anything we got (sorry, wasteful, but did not want to waste stomach space).

The Bacchanal Buffet at Caesar's Palace is one of the highest rated buffets in Vegas. For our last meal in Vegas (that wasn't a pre-airport Shake Shack trip), we decided to have brunch here. You put your name on the waitlist using one of the touchscreen machines. It'll spit out a ticket for you and an estimated time frame to return to the hostess to get on the real line. We put our names into the machines and were quoted a 45 minute wait. 10 minutes later we were called back via text, which was pretty cool. 

The real line took about maybe 15-20 minutes, which wasn't long compared to the wait time we had at the Wicked Spoon on the first day of our trip. I have to say the selection of food here is a lot larger than say, the Buffet at the Bellagio or Wicked Spoon. There are a lot more options. In particular, I liked how the crab legs were pretty much already cracked open so it didn't take a lot of work from us. 

The desserts here were pretty sad, however, which is something I've noticed in a lot of buffets. The ice cream section was a nice touch, but the regular desserts were pretty meh. 

Service was not as attentive as the other buffets we went to, but I guess that's what happens at such a large buffet. 

All in all, if you're looking for a larger selection, this one might be for you. If you ask me which buffet was the best, I'd probably go with the Wicked Spoon.

I was very excited to try this buffet. I figured with it being so expensive everything must be great. We went for lunch on a Friday and there was virtually no line. Once we got in the place was beautiful and the server was great. She was super quick and helpful. I'll give a quick rundown on the food I tried. Waygu sliders were awesome. They pretty much melted in our mouths. They had a truffle potato cake type thing. It was amazing... highlight of the place for me. The brisket was extremely fatty and dry. Chicken marsala was fatty and nothing special. Lasagna and meatballs were very good. The sausage was very spicy but good. The fried chicken and sweet potato fries were excellent. The dessert station was very good. I'd say it was overpriced but pretty good overall. I'm glad we went but think it's an overpriced and overhyped buffet.

Welcome to the most expensive buffet ever, at $88USD per person, you will walk in fully determined to eat your money's' worth and leave hating yourself as you dread the food coma that follows immediately after. Selection for food was extensive, from dim sum to ramen to barbecue and tacos, there's choices for everyone! Worth a try if you're a seafood lover, it's literally crab leg galore. TIP* There is a man in the middle of the line up near the asian station with a big pot, get your crab legs here. He boils the crab legs in a salted pot, brings out so much more flavor- add a squeeze of lemon, so good.

Some other favorites of mine were the watermelon salad,  the pork belly served on top of grits, clam chowder and the highlight... THE DESSERT STATION! Egg tarts are a must, the cake pops, slivers of different cakes and tarts. Aside from that - beef brisket was really dry, sausages were way too oily, some of the bread rolls were stale and bites of roasted pork and duck skin were either perfectly crispy and fresh while others tasted like they were sitting under the lamp for way too long.  Wouldn't say this was worth the money and i certainly wouldn't come back on my next visit, but I'd suggest to come once to get that full Vegas buffet experience.
Good stuff and relatively good value compared the other area options.  Solid food from all regions around the world.  Asian, Italian, seafood, Wyagu beef. Lots of good options.

I had a really great time eating here. I went slightly before brunch as to be able to get to sample the breakfast as well as brunch options. There were plenty of items to choose from and they serve seafood all day. The food options that I tried were good. The only down for me was that the dessert wasn't that tasty. All in all I'm glad I stopped here during my stay in Vegas.

This place wasn't worth the price. They decorate their food to look visually appealing, but the food has disgusting seasoning and taste to it. It's no wonder they didn't know what to name their buffet restaurant. Don't be fooled by the beautiful decorations in the buffet setting and ambiance just because it's located in Cesar's palace, it doesn't prove anything. They have to change their menu for me to ever come back here again. The drunken noodles was spicy hot, one bite will burn the epigastric lining of your stomach. The mushroom bisque with hard bread was odd. I walked around and didn't see anything appetizing. I attempted to eat and like something, at least one entree, but could not find one favorite. Disappointing.
Had a high expectation about the seafood but they were not fresh, especially the oysters.

Excellent service.  Came at 2pm on a weekday so got to try both brunch and dinner.  

5 star food
Brisket 

Dessert 

Hatch chile mash potatoes 

Ricotta garlic crouton.

Food was good but we ended up not eating very much because our table was covered with plates and the servers refused to clear the table, or refill beverages. We waited 3 hours to sit down and paid over 200 dollars for a family of four. The food is good but it is not worth the price or the wait.

Wow speechless is the word that describes this amazing buffet. I have never ate at a buffet this great. Pricey? very but worth it? Very......they have a big selection of everything you want and everything is fresh and very tasteful. I can't wait to come back to eat here again. Eating here 3 times during my 4 day stay wasn't enough. Brunch and Dinner amazing!

Cold tasteless food.  FROZEN crab claws. Frozen as in an ice cube  For $44 you would think something would be edible. I alerted the manager about the crab and she confirmed that they were frozen but she forgot to bring any when they were thawed.    The only thing she had to offer was an applology

The price is well worth it! They have everything here and its not your typical Buffet.
Oysters on the half shell?!! I mean come on! 
Everything is so fresh and good! I absolutely would recommend this place!
Everything is so clean and the staff is friendly.
I ate crab legs until I could no longer crab! 
Tacos also made on the spot.
One of the best spots to eat at when in Vegas. It's probably the best buffet and at a reasonable price. The variety of food is Amazing.

Pro Tip: Go to the Italian section to get hot crab legs.

I really want to give this place 5 stars, but I just can't do it.  The reason I can't do it is because this buffet is not what it once was.  The items that i loved most are no longer served.  Those would be the king crab legs, lamb chops, and the blue fin tuna.  All you get now are snow crab legs and the low grade color added tuna that isn't that appealing.  

On to the good stuff.  What I do like are the snow crab legs, bloody mary oyster shooters (this was so good), osso bucco, prime rib, beef ribs, dim sum, noodle bar (pho, udon, ramen, and a few others), and made to order street tacos.  I think the highlight of the buffet is their dessert section.  You've got everything including freshly made crepes.  Call me crazy, but the best item in the ENTIRE buffet are the gummy bears.  This isn't your ordinary gummy bears my friend.  Oh no no no.  I'm not sure where they get them from, but these gummy bears are the best you'll ever have in your life!!  I ate a huge bowl of them.  They are that good.

For the quality of food you get and the price you pay, I'd say the value isn't quite there anymore.  It used to be the best buffet and the best value.  But like all great buffets, they always go downhill after the first year or two.  Nonetheless, this is still one of my favorite buffets in town.

The buffet is too over hyped. Waited 1 hour in line (after making reservations on a weeknight) but from the looks of it they put you in one line to just pay and then another to get you seated and after finally getting seated waited another 10 min for drinks. The food was ok nothing me and my husband went and got a second round of. The dessert bar however is amazing, and we both ended up just filling up on dessert! Did it for the "experience" and would not do it again.
Great place I love it has everything you need and more I always bring my wifey she loves it too the line is a little long so be prepared to wait a little

One of the best highlights of my trip! This is a pricy buffet (~$90 USD) pp but it is also a very popular buffet! Expect 2-3hr wait times even on a weeknight. My party was informed and bought groupons online to skip the long line (still had to wait 30 mins). 

The food selection was phenomenal. AYCE waygu, prime rib, oysters, crab legs, shrimps, lamb chops and a full out dessert station with a gelato bar! All the food was top notch quality and service was also on point. 

Not sure what more I can ask for :) will def be back next time!

I had a really good experience at the buffet with my dad every thing was really good especially the service from our waiter Mark! He made sure we got everything we needed and always made sure we were good. Good service is so important and I feel I really got that from him! Definitely a good place to go with friends and family.

Apparently this buffet is ranked at the top and most popular right now. So we waited in line for about 1.5 hours. There is a check in system however the person who runs the line can decide to turn the system on or not. When we were there it was turned off so if you wanted to eat you had to stay in line. 

It was $69/person for the 4th of July weekend. It sounds like they can raise the price in any given "holiday" as they pleases. Memorial weekend it was $79 when I called. Regular price is $59. 

We ate so much we had a tough time walking out. They have tacos which was amazing!!! 4 types of soups, bone marrow which was really tasty, an entire desert area with fresh to order crepes, of course seafood area. The warm crab legs were good but the cold ones were small and I was not impressive with the size. 

We waited so long in line yet there were plenty of open sitting inside. I supposed it's nice so everyone has space to eat etc. 

Customer service was ok- they looked exhausted. The front line people. The chiefs and cooks were amazing! They were all so nice!

Expensive buffet, supposed to be one of the best in Vegas. Long line (2+ hours). Definitely lots of food and the best variety I've seen in Vegas.

The food was decent, but nothing stands out. There were a lot of choices, but be careful what you grab. 

I don't usually goto buffets to eat rice or potatoes or bread. Their more expensive selections (oysters, seafood, carving stations) needed to be restocked more often. There's usually a horde of people waiting for fresh oysters to pick over, and the line is often not worth it.

I preferred wicked spoon for putting more care into their food and having less food but more "restaurant" quality dishes.
I like the place because of the crab legs but the other food are cold so I give them a 3 star

Ehhh it's really 3 stars for me overall. Sorry. 

TRUST ME I wanted to love it especially after all the HYPE of it being the best buffet right now in Vegas. Better than Wicked Spoon and The M??? Hmmm idk. 

The other half and I went on a Saturday night for dinner (priced at $49.99 each) 
HOLY GUACAMOLE!! Maybe our expectations were set too high because of all the rave reviews and thinking that for $50 a person, this better be worth it. IT'S NOT!

** Side note ** 
There is an EXPRESS LINE to beat the wait for $15 extra!!!  
(my advice, DON'T WASTE YOUR MONEY!) The wait was not that bad.. it was long, but it was moving at a steady pace. 

The ambiance and decor of Bacchanal is definitely worth the millions of dollars spent. I dig the seating areas and fancy lighting. Maybe its just me, but I NOTICED each ethnic food station (Japanese, Mexican, etc) are actual Chefs from that ethnic background. Kudos! No offense. There's places that have Mexicans cooking Asian food and call it "authentic."

Food quality was okay. Majority of the food selections I grabbed were room temperature to cold. My ramen soup was bland. I want my food "hot off the press,"  you know HOT/STEAMY/SIZZLY.  The Snow crab legs were not juicy enough, possibly because the chef steamed and boiled the juice out of it! So dry! Even the rib eye at the meat station were cooked too dry. We tried to get a side of Au Jus sauce, but the sauce was also bland. Sigh. 

We got our money's worth by taking the rib eye bone home!! Since we could not enjoy it, we thought our dog would sure love it. Why waste it?! Hahah (see picture). Yeah like that!!! 

On to the dessert station, LOVE LOVE LOVE that they offer the greatest dessert fad, Macaroons, and everyone's favorite Japanese ice cream MOCHI. 

I suggest trying Bacchanal for the 1st time to say you've eaten here (especially for tourists), but to come back repeatedly? then that's up to you. 

I still think M buffet, Bellagio, and Wicked is better hands down!

Some of the best buffet food and food in general. Starting in the Asian section, the roasted duck was tender, juicy, and the skin had a good amount of crispness to it, much better than most Chinese restaurants. So was the pork belly and char sui slices. The dim sum was ok, but again as good of not better than actual Chinese restaurants. The honey walnut shrimp was very good too, although the coating was more crunchy not not like a regular Chinese place. It seemed like the same coating as the chicken wings, which were just ok. The egg roll was good, better than most other places. The pizzas were pretty good, especially the mushroom one, very flavorful. Crab legs were salty but the meat was good, not mushy. The prime rib was more tender than the wagyu, although the wagyu was juicier. Brisket was decent, tender and fatty goodness. The lamb t bone was a bit dry as were the mashed potatoes. Bone marrow was just ok. Cioppino was not good. The other mussels/shellfish were pretty good, meat tender and not dried out like you would expect from a buffet. The fried chicken was probably the best thing there. At first glance I had my doubts that it would just be dried out. It was super juicy and tender, and the skin was crispy and crunchy, not hard. I went back for seconds of the fried chicken and the duck. Paella was ok but pretty strong with the saffron. I smelled it coming out the other end the next day. The oysters were fresh, not much flavor, but for a buffet I'm not complaining. I didn't have room for desert but they all looked very good. The fruit was fresh and fragrant. You could tell they were juicy and sweet. Others in my group liked the fruit the most and the gelato. The staff were very nice, friendly, efficient, refilled drinks and clears plates promptly.
Hands down best buffet I've ever had. So much delicious food. Could not try everything in one day. Cant wait to come back soon . Thanks to Maria Becerra for great 5 star service.

This place was worth the wait! This buffet is pretty big and the food did not disappoint. The seafood station was stocked with so many options: crab legs, shrimp, lobster claws, seared ahi tuna, seafood stew, lobster mac and cheese- just to name a few. That along with the sushi/ asian soups/ asian station were my favorites. There was also an Italian station, that also offered steamed crab legs. For brunch on a Sunday it was $65 a person, with the option of bottomless mimosas for $15 or so I believe. I've been to plenty of Vegas buffets and this one is definitely top 2!

Voted best buffet in Vegas 5 years in a row.  We arrived around 5:00 with a party of 5 and wait about 10 minutes.  Food was great quality for a buffet but it was still buffet food. There wasn't anything I ate that I said, wow that's awesome. If you want to eat a lot and want a variety then it's worth the $55 but if you're after quality then take your money to one of the many other top rated restaurants.

The food is absolutely amazing, great selection, the only negative I would say is the line to get in, depending on the time of day will also determine how long you're going to wait. Dinner lines are long, lunch lines are shorter, but the selection is amazing and the food is delicious.

OK. This will sound snobby but this is supposed to be an honest review.... if you live in a large metropolitan area like LA NY or Sf the food will disappoint- first of all the line is horrendous- we waited nearly 2 hours... then had a 2 star meal. The bottom line is when you have a buffet of this size, quality tanks. It's big and beautiful with a mind boggling array of dishes. Then you actually eat it. I've had better sushi at a grocery store, Thai noodles were average and biggest disappointment was the quality and preparation of the the red meat. Sides were good. The only saving grace was the crab and shrimp. And so was the duck confit over polenta and short ribs. The desserts alas beautiful but average.
Too much hype... horrible food, if you like to waste your $ then come to try it out. Over price for a decent buffet.  Totally regretted .

Perhaps I have myself to blame since I came on Christmas Eve - the wait time was atrocious and we skipped breakfast because we wanted to pig out for brunch - but after salivating for 3 hours and finally gorging on everything I could get my hands on, I didn't think that the buffet lived-up to it's name.

Pros
-Assortment of Mexican juices and beverages
-Thick slabs of bacon
-Giant shrimp with cocktail sauce
-Taco station

Cons
-Oysters (I actually spat mine out :/)
-Luke warm butter (I like mine hot)
-Most of the other items at the stations  

True, there were some memorable items and they offered a wide variety of items, but at $53 a person (+ tip), I'd rather splurge at a nice seafood and steakhouse - just saying!

the wait was approx 65 minutes on a saturday 5pm weeknight.  I was expecting to see king crab legs, but they were now a 70.00 upgrade. the food was good but not the best, as expected. the oysters were frozen, the shrimp were not firm, and tasteless.  the gelato was top notch I feel it was better a few years ago,

Came at 4:50 PM on a Saturday and NO WAIT!! Decided to skip lunch and have an early dinner to have enough stomach space to try as many dishes as possible, but also to avoid waiting in line... and it worked! There were a few families who came around the same time as us but multiple registers were open. We were seated right away and everything ran smoothly! So glad for that.

Good buffet! there was a long line when we got there but the wait was not long at all. There were a variety of foods (like all bufffets) and they did not lack the quality. I was so stuffed on my first plate. My favorite was the asian section. They had everything from sushi to crab legs. Also the dessert section was phenomenal. They had a person making crepes and hand scooping ice cream. All the desserts looked too cute to eat as well.

I've been here maybe about 3-4 times and this past Monday when I was there for my birthday, it just wasn't the same. I felt kind of bad for raving about it so much to my boyfriend and my friend's boyfriend. Everything seemed like it was left out for too long, most of the food was very dry and didn't taste fresh at all including the desserts, its upsetting to pay $45/person for lunch to get mediocre food, especially coming from this establishment. I remembered it being a lot better, maybe it was an off day, but most likely I will not be back here for a long time. It's just not worth $45 to me when there are plenty of other buffets in Vegas. Besides the mediocre food, the service was awesome!! They were on it, we had a party of 6 and they did such a great job clearing out the table for us every few minutes. Thank you Michael for the awesome service! I appreciate you and your hard work this past Monday.

Had an enjoyable experience with my visit.
The food, service, its clean, and foods are moved and offered a lot of variety. Seafoods GALORE! 
Tried bone marrow just because 1. Not likely to order it 2. It tends to be pricey - was great!
It's a good place comfy chairs n no pressure like they pushing you out. It's worth the indulgence. 
Best of all the French macaroons heavenly!!!!

We went there on a Monday night pretty long line it took about 25minutes to get in . They give you little Nasty rubber things to hold the plate with in case it is too hot. 
I thought okay it must be really really good.
Don't get me wrong it is good but for $55 .....nah. Not for me. 
Perhaps $35
Overrated

Update: look at my profile, this is literally the only negative review I have posted in my many years using yelp. I don't believe in berating owners of company's; however, I had to write about Bacchanal because of how bad I feel this location has treated me. I speak perfect English having been born in the states. Yet I feel they think they can treat me differently because of my race. The hotel reached out to me in order to "make things right" they offered me several comps had they been fulfilled it would have been great. I let the hotel know I was coming to Las Vegas again and ready to take advantage of the comps. Nothing crazy just a bogo and line pass. I was met by deafening Silence. Definitely disappointed. But this is what Vegas is known for special treatment for a certain few higher level members and the rest are just unimportant temporary nuisances.

If I go to any buffet on the Strip, Bacchanal at Caesar's Palace is the one.

Yes, there is always a line, but you can bypass the line if you order their VIP package on their website. The VIP reservation comes with a dedicated reservation time so you don't have to wait in line. For dinner, it's only $98pp and comes with a seafood tower on ice (so you don't have to wait in line for the seafood, either) and comes with small lobsters which you can't get from the normal buffet. Keep in mind this also gives you access to the rest of the buffet as well (though if you eat all the seafood, you won't have room for anything else!). I prefer my seafood warmed instead of on ice, and their crab legs were a bit salty for my taste. 

I really really liked their prime rib. They also had a lobster mac and cheese, as well as mashed potatoes that were really good. They have a wide selection  of foods, everything you could want in Asian, Mexican, Italian, and American foods. Their made-to-order tacos were delicious as well. They also have a section where you can create your own meat and cheese charcuterie plate! The section had nuts and dried fruits, which was fun! The pistachio and pecans were my favorite, because they were roasted, unsweetened, and unsalted.

Overall, I still think it's one of the best buffets on the strip if you want to eat at a buffet.. but.. is any buffet worth $70-100? Questionable.
This is my first visit to Vegas, and I am very glad that we dined in this buffet. So many to choose from and I went to the seafood section 3 times!! I love this!
Now my favorite Vegas buffet after some others have went downhill. Great tasty selections that is high quality. Not getting a full 5 star review since it is only my favorite by default.

Oh My Smorgy Heaven! There is soooo much fooooood here! All of it, every single bit was perfection! I was happily ashamed and disgusted with myself after eating myself silly. There really is something here for everyone. I am trying to think of a diet that couldn't be humored at Bacchanal and I'm not coming up with any.

So it is expensive and you have to make a reservation at the kiosky thing. The day that I went, my party didn't think to call ahead and we were so sad to be told it was at least two hours wait...unless we paid an extra $20. I will admit, we paid it. It was worth it to get in right away and not mess up our whole day waiting around or skipping an epic-sized meal. 

I will be back, oh yes. I will be back.

I've heard good and bad things about this buffet, so I thought to try it out myself. My wife and I bought their Groupon which was valid for early dinner (before 4 if I recall correctly) which gave us VIP access, but wasn't necessary since the time we went was slow. The general line went way quicker than VIP and the employees looked reluctant to even help us. Once we got through the first line, we then had to queue again and there was a line for 1-2 guest and 3+ guest. The 1-2 guest like was ridiculously long and surprisingly the 3+ guest like went very quick. There was a variety of food options, from seafood, to meats, tacos, sushi, dim sum, vegetables, etc. I thought the food was pretty good for buffet. I really enjoyed the dessert station, which had chocolate covered strawberries, hand scooped ice cream, cheesecake and fruit. I recommend this buffet if it's 3+ guests, or a special day and have a few extra dollars to spend.
Definitely the best buffet on the strip and our waitress, Esmeralda, made our buffet experience the best and highly recommend her!

I was pretty excited for this buffet and went specifically because I was craving some crab legs. Was so disappointed when all the crabs were FROZEN! Now I understand they must keep it on ice to keep it fresh but seriously at least defrost it before serving to people who are paying good money for this highly rated buffet! I literally bit into a piece where it was icy and so much water just coming out of! Other than that, there was a great selection for sure, LOTS of different ethnicity food! enjoyed the prime rib, homemade mash and my husband enjoyed the thick cut bacon on the carving and the Benedict. I enjoyed the variety and the fact their always bringing out new stuff to try. The only downfall was the frozen crab legs just because you pay more then the average for a buffet on the strip for it. Service was pretty consistent.

This place is everything people rave about. We made sure to make a stop before leaving. The buffet can get pricey like any other buffet options but this place is worth it.
The options are from dim sum, breakfast omeltes, smoothies, a whole dessert section with cakes, pies, cookies, ice cream. A chinese food section, american, mexican with posole that was bomb. Oysters, crab legs, soups and fruit bar.

Never disappoints and the service is great. Our waiter was pleasant, attentive, and provided us with great service.
Great Buffet and I don't like Buffets. Lots of fresh, good tasting food. Elegant set up. A little pricey but worth it. In a city where Buffets are everywhere this is well worth going too.
Absolutely best buffet in Vegas. Our server Socorro is sweer too. Line was really long but worth it

Good buffet, but over priced at $70 a person for dinner on weekends.   I can go to a fine dining restaurant in Las Vegas for almost the same price for a 3 course meal.

Best dishes were the brisket, raw oysters, and pork ribs.

This is our go to buffet when we are in Vegas. You can't go wrong. The dessert bar is insane and my favorite are the crepes that are made to order. Julie took care of our parents last night and was so great we came back today and asked for her by name. We were not disappointed! Wonderful food and service.

I prefer the dinner buffet over the breakfast because there's more options. There was a wide range of food from Asian, Mexican, American, Italian, and Seafood. If you're getting snow crab legs, there's two selections of it. Don't get the ones from the seafood selection. Go between the Mexican and Asian food where you can get freshly boiled snow crab legs with butter. Here are a couple of my favorites from each selection...

Asian: The sushi that I tried was good. The dim sum/dumplings were okay. The Filipino pork skewers were one of my favorites. The galbi and pork belly were good.

Mexican: You could never go wrong with tacos and elote! There's three different meats - Carne Asada, Al Pastor, and Chicken. There's a taco bar after you get your tacos so you can add toppings you want - guacamole, sour cream, hot sauce, cheese, etc.

Italian: I didn't try that much from this selection. Except for the beef ravioli which was really good.

American: I had the prime rib, Mac & cheese, and some grilled veggies which were all good.

Desserts: The creme brûlée was good! The ube gelato tasted like they used real ube to make it. I forgot what they were called, I think it was mini cones but they were sooo good!! I tried the pink strawberry and ube cones. My favorite was the pink one.

We were told that it was an hour wait but it was more like 30 minutes. If you check into yelp, you can get a free drink. There's also a Groupon coupon it costs the same but comes with 2 free drinks and a time limit. If you're staying at Caesar's for 2 nights or more, you can get two complimentary breakfast buffets at Bacchanal. If you're running tight on time, you can pay extra for the express pass.
This was our first time trying this Buffett and it didn't fail the food was amazing!!
it has wide variety but I was looking forward to bone marrow. unfortunately they didn't have it.

Priced pretty high but the food is delicious and has a wide variety of goodness! 

I took my employees here as a thank you lunch and the service was great and everyone really seemed to enjoy it! 

Only reason I didn't give them a 5 STAR rating is because I don't think the price matched the quality. If they maybe did special days and adjusted their prices just a tad I'd definitely would have given a 5th STAR. Vegas has to many delicious cuisines for amazing prices! It's not hard to find delectable cuisine for great prices!

Really good buffet. I would say the best but I have noticed a slight lowering of standards since they opened.  Very slight but it is there. Had dinner there tonight. Really nice selection. They did lose a little ground against the rush. Buffet looked picked thru at times and the desert section was almost barren but like I said it was during a rush. One sour spot was in service. I had a very hard time getting refills. My server was very attentive to the bigger table but essentially ignored me as I was eating alone. Not a major complaint but it was a significant issue for me because I really like the buffet. Spoke with a manager who said he would address it.

The King of Buffets in Las Vegas!

Even if you don't like everything, you're sure to find at least a dozen plates that'll please you. This buffet is serious about flavour and presentation. 

Service was amazing!! Although expect a 20-30 min wait to get into the buffet. 
From the front desk to behind the food stations, it's apparent all of the staff received proper training in hospitality. 

At $39.99 person for the weekday brunch, you can't go wrong! Think about the truffle in the mushroom pizza, the king crab legs and the made-to-perfection prime rib. The cost for 1 plate of the aforementioned would cost you approximately the same amount. But here, its unlimited, and you can have anything or everything you want. 

A "must-try" if you happen to be in VEGAS!!

食物还可以，但吃饭要排很久的队。而且歧视中国人，吃饭还要出示护照。
不是很好找，在凯撒一楼赌场的里面。
牛排还可以，但是螃蟹腿、海鲜等食物一般，没有想象中的好。
没有醋等调料，吃起来可能会腻。
饮料需要找服务员单独要。
总体来说就餐体验和环境都不是很好。

Heard so many great reviews so we decided to splurge and give it a try. The wait can be long and on the Sunday we went for dinner, it was 30-45 min for two. But if you're a Caesars reward platinum or higher you can get express entry.
Place is fairly large, lots of food options. We took a walk around just to see what they had to offer before we got any food. Since we went on a Sunday night it was $65/ person. For that price I expected much better quality food. Don't get me wrong, some items were delicious, and there were some items you don't normally get at a buffet like bone marrow,  a whole roast pig to pick at, etc. But we were somewhat underwhelmed at the overall taste and quality. Several of the items we got were dry, though it did have flavor. Some items were just plain tasting or not as good as we expected it should be. The dessert section did have a lot to offer, but again nothing spectacular as we expected. 
Service was very good, all the staff was extremely helpful and polite.

Well...originally when it opened it was $48, than $52 and now it's $62 per person! Is it worth it? Well it has crab legs, crab claws (although it was somewhat cracked it's still very difficult to open it to get the meat out). It has a array of meats and different options than your traditional vegas buffets. So if you're already in Vegas, why not splurge on a good meal you'll probably leave it at the tables anyway! Happy eating!

Sorry to break the bad news to everyone but the  Bacchanal Buffet is NOT worth it. I love buffets and was extremely excited to finally try this one but I left very disappointed. 

THE BAD
__________________________

Food: For an expensive buffet with a long wait time I expected delicious food and a large selection. They do offer a very extensive selection of food  but I expect both the quantity and most importantly the QUALITY of the food as well. The food is mediocre at best. Nothing stood out to me and even though I got small amounts of everything I didn't find myself wanting to finish everything on my plate let alone go back for seconds. I think the issue is that they offer too many different types of food. Their effort gets divided into too many directions and they lose out on the quality of each dish. They also try to make their food appealing to so many different types of people that they make everything generic and "safe" to cater to a larger audience.

Asian Food Section: Forget about the Asian food here, it's not worth your time. If you've had actual Dim Sum before this is not comparable at all. The Mapo Tofu was meh. The Thai dishes were not well made either. The Drunken Noodles and Pad Thai lacked flavor and were not spicy at all. Thai food needs a kick to it! 

Sushi: The Sushi section was small. They offer 2-3 different rolls plus a salmon sashimi, and a tuna sashimi. None of them looked that appetizing or fresh so I passed on those. I did however try the poke salad and I wasn't that impressed. 

Soup/Salad/: This part of the buffet was okay. Very limited salad section and all pre made. The soups were a hit or miss. The tomato basil soup I got was cold. 

There were a lot of other specialty items offered, most of which do not stand out in my memory. 

The price: For $60 I did not think it was worth it. I would rather spend that money on a nice steak or seafood dinner. 

THE GOOD
____________________________

Meat Carving: All of the meat offered was fantastic. I got the prime rib, wagyu, and tri-tip. All were delicious and cooked perfectly! 

Seafood: I loaded up on crab to try and get my money's worth and really enjoyed it. They also cut the crab legs in half so the meat is exposed and you don't have to work for your food. They also offer shrimp cocktail and lobster claws which are very good. I loved the seafood section! 

Dessert: They offer a whole gelato section with tons of flavors and a crepe station! Needless to say I got both. I had them make my crepe with Nutella and topped it with strawberries, so good! There are also a lot of other small desserts in this section which were very tasty. 

Bottomless mimosas: If you're in the mood for drinking this is definitely worth it for $15. The servers come around often to refill so your glass is never empty. 

Although there are a few redeeming factors of this buffet, overall I still do not think it is worth it for the price. You are better off going somewhere else.

We used a groupon for this last Friday afternoon's Brunch. It was $88 for 2, including 2 mimosas each. It also included VIP line skipping but there was no line so that wasn't relevant.

And then we turned around and went again for Dinner the next night! This time we used the OpenTable "#LikeACaesar" reservation deal. This one was $98/person but it included VIP line-skipping and All-You-Can-Drink. It also comes with the legendary seafood tower. 

About the Crab:
Crab shipments are seasonal. When they run low on the king crab, they're going to start holding it back for the VIPs and the high rollers. 

There were no snow crabs or king crabs during the brunch. There were rock crab claws but they weren't worth the trouble. Very little taste and very freezer burned. But the good news is that there was Dungeness crab! Again, this is a seasonal issue. The Dungeness was the only crab that didn't taste like it had sat in the freezer for a year. Since this is D crab season, they were probably harvested recently.

There WERE, however, king crab on our seafood tower and we enjoyed them, even tho they were a little freezer-burned and still frozen in places. There was no steaming of crab legs to be found. Frowny face emoji.

I completely understand the outrage of some of the reviewers that see snow crab legs and oysters clearly on display at the entrance but not available to eat. They stand in line for a LONG TIME and stare at those crab legs, telling themselves that it's worth the wait. And then, "none for you!" I could hear grumbling from some of the other diners during the brunch.

About the Seafood Tower
We got 2 halves of a small, freezer-burned lobster, 6 king crab legs, 4 green mussels, 4 oysters, some sea snails, and a handful of medium prawns. The oysters were clearly frozen. Thawed out oysters are fairly unpleasant. I'm very suspicious about where they source their oysters from... The prawns were in good shape. And green mussels freeze pretty well so we particularly enjoyed them.

About the Asian Section
Nice selection of dim sum. Not the very best you can get, but better than the Trader Joe's frozen section. The sushi rice was sticky and unseasoned like grocery store sushi. But the fish was tasty so I was peeling them off the rice and eating them as sashimi.

During the dinner they brought out char siu and roast duck.  They were both fantastic! The rest of the dishes were standard Asian-American fare, but done well.

About the Dessert Section
We found that most of the desserts were your standard "look great but taste lame" buffet desserts. It seemed like they used non-dairy "creme" in most of the items. We agreed that besides the gelato, the only one that actually tasted like what it was supposed to taste like was the key lime tarts. Imagine creme brulee being made from cool whip. And tiramisu made out of cool whip. And so on...

About "The Rest"
The rest of the buffet were standard stuff and nothing really stood out. We did like the bone marrow. There was pasta, pizza, tacos, prime rib, all done well but nothing stood out as amazing.

I'm really not getting why everyone thinks the Bacchanal is some sort of amazing thing. It's a very good buffet. For a buffet. But it's still the same old buffet food, although many dishes were better than you might expect. And I was actually expecting something larger. I'm pretty sure I've eaten at buffets of this size. There were actually very few bread choices, salad choices, and fruit choices in favor of comfort foods like meat, chow mein, and pizza.

I'm glad I went and I had a great time, but I doubt I'll be back because there's always other new things to try.

Nor impressed. Pricey for the food served. Did not even include an omelet for brunch. Service was so-so. I asked for water refill from a server but had to wait and had to request from a server assigned to our table.

I had high expectations prior to coming here and honestly, it was disappointing! If not for the dessert, I would say there's a lot of better options for buffet other this place. Food just fell short when it comes to the taste department lol I didn't even try their crab legs, just didn't look appealing ugh! I wouldn't recommend this place to friends when visiting Vegas.
The best buffet you will ever visit! It wasn't voted best buffet in America for no reason!

Fasted and looked forward to the hype of the Bacchanal Buffet! We had a Groupon for the weekend brunch that included alcoholic drinks and to be in the VIP line - no wait! There were several seafood items and more traditional items during this time. Items that stuck out were:

Some seafood
Soups
Sushi 
Desserts
Dim Sum 

Looked forward to the bottled fresh juices but sadly they stop putting them out at 11 am - Boo!  

The Buffet selections are crazy plenty but it is overrated for the price. Is this a must try? No but it's an experience!

Best buffet in town, period!!  Almost pricey but lunch is reasonable so do that if you can't afford it.  Enjoy the fresh everything!   Be prepared to wait at dinner in line too.  But they do it conveniently so it's not just a line.

In my opinion, if there is only one buffet you gonna try in Vegas, this is it.  selections and quality are excellent.  

Frankly, I am surprised by how comfortable the environment is here.  People seem to hang out for a long time.

One draw back is that the wait can be Disney long.  We went in a Monday afternoon at 3pm.  The wait was at least 30 min.  Cannot imagine what the line would be like at prime meal time or on weekends.

The lining system is interesting.  You use a kiosk to put your cell number and get a ticket that shows your wait time.  You will be texted when it is close to your turn.  Then you will stay in line, pay the cashier and be seated.

Since the wait can be long, go to the kiosk and grab a ticket early is important.

Every item in the buffet is of supreme quality and unique taste. They have Asian, American,Italian and Mexican cuisines. They have a good range of seafood and meats. 
Desserts are really good 
Pricey but worth it.

Their seafood is definitely top notch. They have different types of crab legs, (and crab) and oysters. Their different cuts of meats are awesome too like prime rib and lamb. I think their most underrated dish is the chicken ginseng soup, not only is it expensive if you eat it alone, it's actually really calming and tasty to a certain extent! If the review was based on food alone, 5 stars. But the issue resides in other areas. I have been here for dinner 3-4 times. Their price is reasonable especially for the taste of the food.  But the wait time easily even on a non busy day is 2-3 hours. I mean what am I supposed to do for that wait time? Just gamble my savings away? And then the parking is kind of old so it takes a little longer to walk to the restaurant. The restaurant itself has nice decor,  that all goes away when there is no wiggle room in the whole area; I felt like a dude in an elevator. If this review was just food, 5 stars. But I have to take points away for the wait time, the inconvenient parking, the lack of moving space and sloppy customer service.

There's almost 10k reviews on this buffet so I really don't need to go into much detail. There are two sections to this buffet, service has been amazing every time I have been, the food is delicious, and it is expensive! Dinner is $60 per person with tax. 

The only thing I wish is they would decrease the seafood section and add a bigger salad bar. They only offer about 3 pre-made salads. Other than that I love this place. The coffee gelato is delicious.
Best buffet ever!!! Yes it is expensive but if you're eating steak, prime rib, wagyu, and endless seafood it's definitely worth it. Always gotta hit up this spot when in Vegas.
If your going to splurge this is the place to go, worth spending here! I tried a sample of almost everything on the menu delicious. Desert was the icing on the cake.
Was an okay buffet place. Prices are fair for in Vegas. Food is common a the quality of "buffet". Lines are long and huge, recommended to go early, dont wait till you're too hungry.

Just same good buffet. Price is high but the quality of everything even the pizza is good.

The only thing I would knock them is their prime rib could be a little better. It may be the butche serving it but I think it could be cut with a little more care. 

Diamond members get a few extra perks as well!

My current go to when in Vegas.

Desserts are the best I've had at any buffet and is unrivaled. End the meal on a high note.

This is my all time favorite buffet in Las Vegas, amazing prices and great food. There is a lot to choose from, including Chinese, BBQ, seafood and Italian food. There are hot and cold prepared snow crab as well as variety of meats including brisket, prime rib, wagyu and bacon. OMG they have bone marrow, bone marrow!!! So yummy! There are so many varieties of dessert including a crepe station, gelato station as well as chocolate dipped strawberries. There is also a soup selection including congee and pho. There are so many varieties of food. Come here prepared to eat!! Make sure to take advantage of their fresh squeezed juices in the AM as well as their mimosas. All dishes were prepared accordingly and did not appear to be sitting out in the cold. Their buffet station was kept clean and lines were organized. The servers were friendly and took our empty plates away quickly. Very friendly. 

This is by far my favorite buffet in Vegas and I have tried many.
Awesome! No other way to put it!! The buffet has everything. Be prepared to wait but food is worth it!

Not worth the insane price tag...
The buffet is huge, but it really wasn't anything special. We went for brunch and there were barely any breakfast foods. It also seemed like as soon as we were full they brought out completely new dishes that we would've liked to try before being full. The gelato was good. Very few gluten free options.

This review is for their Sunday brunch. Was really looking forward to a great indulgent meal after all the hype I've read and the videos I watched. Well, if you like shrimp more than anything in the world and there is a meteor about to destroy  earth in a week, I would suggest you gather all your savings,  rent a Jet  and go to this buffet. The  amount of shrimp is ridiculous! barbecued, Asian style, Italian style, in bulk with cocktail sauce, I'll stop before I turn into Bubba Gump -I think you get the idea.  I've enjoyed many brunch buffets but I have never been to one that had such a poor choice of egg dishes and no smoked salmon!!!! I don't mind paying $65.00 but at least have a decent selection of more than a few dishes!!!! Take your money to a place that doesn't live off what it used to be!

This place is amazing.  I used Yelp's vip promo to avoid the long wait in line.  I don't know if this prompted special treatment since they knew I was going to review the food, but they sent a delicious appetizer of lobster, shrimp, and caviar to my table.  I'd never had caviar before so I was very impressed.  This was my third visit during my short 4 day stay in Vegas.  The food was superb.  I'd even went to the breakfast buffet earlier that morning and tried their freshly squeezed oj and was blown away.  A must for anyone visiting Vegas.

I have came here several times and so far it has never disappointed me. This is one of the best place to have buffet on the Strip right now. Many options for food - good food, not the crappy ones you usually see at cheaper buffet restaurant.
My wife work for the casino so we got 20% off the bills as well. Recommend to come here before 6pm or you would have to wait in line for a long time. 
Highly recommend this place to everyone.

Came here to eat with 10 other girls around 2:30pm-3pm on a Saturday, which was a good time to come since it was AFTER the lunch rush. We only waited in line for about 10 minutes =). It was about $53 per person with tax and an 18% gratuity charge since we had such a large group. 

This is an awesome new buffet and the architectural construction, decor, furnishings, and interior design is stunning. The beautifully bright, modernized atmosphere greatly enhanced my dining experience here with friends! You'll enjoy the simple, yet artistic displays of food. Every section with categories and subsets of certain types of food are so well organized! There's a seafood section, a tacos taqueria section, a cheese section, salad section, soup and bread section, dessert section, a meat section (prime rib, baby back ribs, & etc.), an Italian food section, a Spanish food section, an American food section, and an Asian foods section with Vietnamese, Chinese, Indian, Japanese, and Korean dishes. I tried some of the dim sum and was really impressed with their xiao long baos (Shanghai juicy pork soup dumplings) and Shumais (These Cantonese style steamed dumplings). To conclude, you'll love the WIDE varieties of different types of cuisine that Bacchanal Buffet has to offer! 

I ate mostly seafood because I'm a HUGE seafood fan. Shrimp and grits, poached salmon, king crab legs, mussels, shrimp cocktail, oysters, oyster shooters, clam bake, sashimi/sushi, you name it, I had it, and I LOVED it. I also tried the prime rib and baby back ribs which I loved as well. Pretty much everything I ate was desirably delicious.

Service was excellent which made our experience here even more worthwhile. Our waitress kept making rounds to our table to pick up used plates, cups, and she consistently refilled our drinks! We had a table of 11 rather demanding, but sweet girls, and our waitress worked it LIKE A BOSS.

I've been to plenty of buffets in Vegas and as of now, Bacchanal ranks the highest above all others in my book.
Best buffet in Vegas hands down!  I always go here because of their high quality food! Place is pricey but they offer a variety of food. Highly recommend it.

After seeing all the great reviews and, I was really looking forward to eat at Bacchanal buffet.  the line was long, it took us about 1.5hrs to be seated.  For the price point of this place, I was expecting raw oysters, choice of fresh seafood, freshly made hot items but what I found was old stale food, sad looking sushi and NO raw oyster w/ limited choices for seafood.   Desserts were average.

I absolutely love love this buffet! Best buffet in Vegas considering how much food there is in the restaurant, phenomenal!! Always hot & fresh & to mention the dessert bar is amazing!! They even have macarons, to die for!!!! Delicious each and every time! Yes it's expensive but I feel you get what you pay for!! I love this buffet!!
Awful experience at Bacchanal buffet after paying $75+ $45 upcharge for Labor Day dinner. Lines as long as 30 people waiting for crab legs and ice cream. Total scam...

Yes the concept is like Wicked Spoon, but the food here is actually good and so much nicer. Came on a Saturday, so it was Champagne Brunch 41.99...Yes it's pricey, but hey it's AYCE! Everything I had was really good. Even the prime rib was super delicious. They have a noodle station with pho, ramen, udon and all the broths that match it. I just can't stop eating. Staff is nice and the place is really clean. Also the crab legs are cut in half for you already so u don't need to make a mess and get your hands too dirty. LOVE IT!
It's ok the quality has gone down since they opened and they table they gave me to sit at was all dirty on the floor around it.  Better off at the Wicked Spoon or Wynn
Delighted.  Love the snail.  Oyster needs to keep cold not just cool.  Great service.

I've been to lots of buffets in Vegas, but this is the best. I loved the big assortment of tiny plates of food- the shrimp & cheese grits, the Greek dolmathes, and the shrimp-and-avocado taco were my favs. Very fresh, with quality ingredients. The surprise star of the buffet (at least to me!) is the meats-and-cheese section. Excellent quality Italian deli meats, an assortment of yummy cheese, and spreads like marmalade and chunky mustard were fun to make combinations with on a lavosh or crostini. The fresh watermelon juice was also a favorite. I quite enjoyed the unique Asian-influenced desserts, especially the pretty little raspberry jelly in a flower shape. There's a 2 hour limit, but honestly I could probably spend all day trying new things...the items are rotated out quickly, so if you see something you like, get it before it's gone! Dine like a Caesar! Go to the Bacchanal!

Buffet is one of the better ones in LV. There was a long line during my visit on a weekday but it seems to go pretty fast. Their paying and waiting in line system seems pretty efficient. The lighting is a bit on the dim side but is overlooked with the great service. Waitress checked on us every 15 minutes. The variety and quality of food is definitely 4 star. I was all over the seafood and prime rib. My son gave his stamp of approval on the pizzas and his favorite dessert bar. Sprinkles and toppings on your gelato? OF COURSE! They won me over with their creme brûlée's

The food here is absolutely amazing and worth the price. The only problem you may have is overeating. Pace yourself. Prepare to wait in a long line or purchase VIP pass. My personal advice is to ask for Ruth, she's the best server, very observant and happy to assist. Tiramisu is delicious, my mother ate 2 and she normally doesn't care for it. There is something for everyone, and make sure you walk all the way around before you commit, because there is a lot to choose from. Enjoy!!!

Came here on a Thursday evening for dinner a few months ago. There was  NO LINE which was a super plus. The food was definitely good quality, but I just wasn't that impressed. I actually enjoyed the lunch buffet at Wicked Spoon better and it was half the price. I expected to find a variety of things I wouldn't see at other buffets seeing as this is the largest but to me the selection wasn't particularly wowing. For the record I don't eat seafood so that portion of the buffet was lost on me and it seems to be what everyone raves about. 

Customer service wise our waiter was fantastic. Didn't rush us, made great conversation, was ultra attentive and it really helped make the experience. I'm glad I got to try this place once and was even happier I didn't even have to wait in line for it, but I don't think I'll ever come back unless someone else is paying. And even than I'll probably try to convince them to go to Wicked Spoon.

The wait can get ridiculously long but luckily my cousin who's a 7stars was able to get us in with out the wait. I love it also came with a complimentary red or champagne for 7 stars. 

I love their seafood selections. They have cold and hot alaska king crab legs, sea snails, any seafood really. I highly recommend the Japanese scallop dish. OMG so good. They of course have American, vegan, Italian, Japanese, and Chinese food.

The also have great customer service.

After reading all the awesome reviews on Yelp, I was really excited about trying this buffet. It was quite a let-down. For $38.99 weekday brunch, I felt like I was at a Golden Corral/Hometown Buffet meets Asian buffet. Yes, everything is really fresh and clean and delicious--hence the three stars--but nothing wow'd me.  When I checked back on the Yelp photos, none of the really pretty buffet pictures were actually there, so, they might have been posted by the staff/photographers.

I didn't even need the two-hour limit...the king crab legs were not prepped for consuming without crackers, the lobster Benedict just okay, the lobster bisque crazy salty, where was the soufflé?  I had a good crepe, fresh fruit, and creme brûlée.  Service was excellent.
Great service and seated at the promised time. Everything was fresh and delicious!! Best buffet in Vegas hands down. The crab legs were excellent and there were so many choices.

Well I did it... I waited an hour and a half and spent $50+ to eat tacos....yep. That was the only warm food here. Everything else I got was cold by the time I got to the table (which wasn't too far off) however the Pepsi (which should be cold) was somehow warm??!!

The food is okay. Pretty bland, but most of the stuff pictured isn't actually there. Kinda sad. They had a variety of dishes but they all fell under the same bland category. Do yourself a favor and ask to look at the food before waiting in line and paying a ridiculous amount. It's underwhelming.

Are you planning a trip to Vegas and trying to find what epic places to indulge your tastebuds in?

WELL, crikey, THIS IS GONNA BE THE ONLY JACKPOT YOU'RE GONNA HIT! 

Bacchanal -- simply, it's a MUST for everyone to try at least ONCE in their life. 

I could write a 1,000 word essay breaking everything down but lemme just tell you the biggest WOW's for me here:

ASIAN - can you believe they have xiao long bao (soup dumplings)?! gotta be a good sign that chefs are speaking chinese to each other. 
MEXICAN - oH laWd I love me their salsa collection and their fresh taco factory.
SEAFOOD - one word - OYSTERS. crab legs are sOo last summer. 
THE FRESH JUICES IN THE LITTLE GLASS BOTTLES - so cute and so yum.
DESSERT - every time I come here there is always something new and intriguing. The biggest shocker for me was when they had FRESH JAPANESE SHAVED ICE - as in, shaved ice with red beans, green tea syrup, condensed milk, and mochi. WHAT! what. WHAAT!!! Can I marry whoever is in charge of the dessert menu puhlease.
CHARCUTERIE - adds a nice elegant touch but lezzbereal...aint nobody wasting belly room for dat! SKIP.
GROUPON - be on the lookout for their weekday breakfast groupon deal! $69 for unlimited mimosas + breakfast for two, only valid M-F. 


PRO TIP: 3PM is happy time because that's when they bring out the OYSTERS!! slurpslslruprslurp. spill melted butter on the floor so people slip and you beat them to the front of the seafood line!! 

i'm kidding, please don't.

In summary...Bacchanal is...is the perfect manifestation of America - it offers Diversity and Fatness. It is the land of opportunity...to wear sweatpants, hair tied, chillin with no makeup on and just PIG OUT. TRY IT!!
