This Buffett has a variety of foods from across the culinary globe. So much food to choose from. I try to get a little bit everything. The service is great. I really enjoy their cakes, cookies, and ice cream. Great dim sum and very good seafood such and crab and shrimp. Must plan a next visit.

A lot of people say that this is the best buffet in Vegas, or at least on the strip.  I can see why.  Honestly, it was probably the best buffet I've ever been to, but it is not without it's flaws.

PROS:
* Amazing food, hands down.  What we tried was great.  What we didn't try, we wanted to try.  There's just too many options to try everything (around 600 choices, if I heard correctly!).
* Great service from the waiter.  Ramos took great care of us.  He was always stopping by to make sure our drinks were filled and we were taken care of.  
* Lovely decor.  It's modern, but clean looking inside.  I like the use of highball glasses for the 'chandeliers.' 
* Groupon specials.  We saved over 50% by using a Groupon deal.  Definitely the way to go if you're unsure about the price or trying it out.

CONS:
* The cashier shorted me $20, and I didn't realize it until later.  Count your change.  Lesson learned.  That's on me, as much as it's on her.
* The staff behind the food is no better than any other buffet.  Rude at worst, but lacking communication skills at best.  Try telling the chef that the metal ladle sitting under the heat lamp is way too hot to touch.  No comprehension at all (or understanding of basic thermodynamics).
* The regular price (without the Groupon) is pretty steep, though it was a pretty good buffet in fairness.  Not sure it's THAT good, but still... you get what you pay for I suppose.
* It's not very easily accessible, as you have to pass through the entire casino just to get there (if you parked in the garage).  Maybe it's a tad closer if you're staying at Caesar's?  Regardless, it wasn't easy to find.

I will say that it pretty much set the standard for food quality, variety, and freshness.  I really can't complain about any of the items we ate, nor the drinks we consumed.  Again, Ramos took amazing care of us, too, so not all the service was bad.  It was mostly good, overall.  But, there were enough red flags to warrant some mixed feelings overall.

Still, all that being said, I think I would do this again (with the Groupon).  It really was an experience.  Brunch on Saturday was a great time to go, too, because the place was pretty darn quiet, thankfully.  I was worried about the long lines and need for VIP passes.  Unnecessary when we went.

Worth the hype?  Maybe.  Definitely worth trying, and probably worth trying again.

Basic food with little flavor or uniqueness. The sushi station was very very disappointing. They had little left when I got there (7:30pm) and for my second trip... even less. They do not make more on demand. Once what they have prepared is gone, it is gone. Rib eye was only thing that was good. Pizza was gross. Pasta was gross. Fish station was Ok but nothing special. I could not believe they had mac and cheese  that was box like mac and cheese. Really? Salad station was disappointing.  If I did go with a friend and hang out for a couple hours and eat and chat, I would have been angry. But everything in vegas is expensive... so I just looked at it like an 'entertainment' item versus good food. I expect far more for the price. But that is vegas isn't it? Wolfgang Puck's restaurant couldn't even make a proper pizza. Food for the mass that just consume. Not food for the foodie that likes to savor flavors. If you are hoping to find good flavors here, go somewhere else. Unless, you want to stuff your face only with steak.

We've been back 2 times since my last review.

This time is was for Caesars 50th Anniversary! We were hesitant to buy a groupon coupon for the buffet, but since they were running a special with tax included it was $60.00 for brunch with bottomless mimosas. The coupon itself makes it seem like your only getting one each but the up-charge (included in the coupon ) at the buffet is for bottomless mimosas.

This included front of the line service but we're already VIP cardholders so that didn't make a difference. They had a scanner all ready for the coupon and it was a snap to check in. Again you will be charged tax at the register which is noted on the Groupon page. I think it was $7 or $9 dollars cant remember which one.

We were seated within 3 mins. Just a side note for people complaining about the long lines.
This is touted as the best buffet in all of Las Vegas so yes there will be long lines.

We always start at the very end or beginning depending on how you look at it at the Asian section. We love the food. My favorite is the ribs and potstickers! Every section seems to have something for somebody and the crepes are my wife's favorite dessert!

I had the beef brisket at the food carving station and the American style ribs are always on point. I could only do 2 plates this time around but i made sure they counted. We tried the cream of corn for the first time and that was really good.

Our waitress, I think her name was Ramona was amazing as well, very quick and very pleasant.

We will be back in Sept!

Let me just start by saying there are two ladies in the front working to seat guests that need to take a refresher course on customer service (older ethnic woman with brown hair and an older white woman with white hair).

The woman with the brown hair instructed us to follow "her", that word is extremely vague when there are multiple people walking around as well as other customers. My husband followed the older white woman who was our hostess and she got very snappy and said "get in back of her" which was a customer... we were extremely confused because most places wouldn't instruct you to follow another customer.. we did and the first group was dropped off and then us.. 

We were sat at almost the furthest spot away from the food, when my husband mentioned we told the hostess that he was disabled and we needed a place closer to the food she seemed extremely irritated and rude. We felt very uncomfortable because she looked him up and down almost questioning where his disability was ( he has plates in his spine from being a veteran) It was so unwelcoming and it hurt his feelings.

We felt extremely unwelcome and we hadn't even sat down. The food was great and our server was amazing! The only upside to our dining experience

Very good restaurant 
Specially Socorro is very kind and beautiful sever
I want to visit here again ~

I usually come here for Sunday brunch, which i think is pretty fantastic. I come earlier to avoid waiting in line. Food and service are pretty good, plus you can eat crab legs for breakfast w fresh juices. (We usually find a Groupon or coupon somewhere to get a cheaper brunch at an earlier arrival time.) 
The dinner buffet is actually pretty similar to the Sunday brunch. Less egg and waffle/pancake style items but the same main stuff is around (seafood, Mexican section, Italian section, meats, salads, Asian section, noodle and soup bar, and desserts). 
Personally, I found the dinner to be a little underwhelming. Probably still one of the better buffets in Vegas (compared to the Wynn, Bellagio, cosmo, etc.). 
Check in on yelp for a free alcoholic beverage. Score! 
Also, being VIP, Diamond, etc. is clutch as you get to skip the lines.
Great food and service. Amazing  beef! And Sea food. Price is not bad for the quality.
We tried many different buffets while in Vegas and hands down this was the best one: extensive options for appetizers, entrees, and dessert! The crab legs were a crowd pleaser.

This buffet has a long line to get in and the food is really not worth the wait. It is average at best and very expensive.

There are so many nicer places to eat in Las Vegas. This buffet is very over-rated.

Hey so yah it's my sexond time around. Yah it's good...but not $75. Check groupon for a deal they have during the week (which is what I should've done). Thumbs up for the free mimosa with they yelp check-in. Prepare for a wait, if you're with  small group. Make friend with others in line....make a bigger group and get seated faster!!

Not as good as I was hoping due to all of the hype and mystery around it. Most things tasted bland and nothing really stood out. The saving grace was maybe the dessert island in the middle. But for the hour wait that we had to endure just getting through the door, it was definitely not worth the money.

We purchased the buffet online and the price also included the EXPRESS LINE service.  We were very disappointed to find out that the Express service only got us through the first line faster to purchase/show our paid voucher.  It does not get you ahead of the second line that is waiting to be seated (this line was extremely long)
So I would not waste you're money on the Express service.  
Also while we were scrolling the desert station our table was completely cleared and reset for the next person.  Quite frustrating!
But high remarks for the food.

Great place to go if you're not too hungover from the night before ;) 

I really loved it here! They section the food: seafood, asian, American, desserts, meat, and Mexican! The longest line will be seafood of course! Be prepared to dive in raw oysters, clams, seafood paella, crab benedicts, muscles, cold crab, warm melted butter, cocktail shrimp, and more!!!! If that doesn't make your mouth drool enough, they have a wide variety of meat-- prime rib, lamb, ribs, and about 5 different types of sausages! The Mexican side has tacos but I was way to full from the seafood and meat to eat anything else.

The asian side is in a separate room. 
There is a lot of sushi rolls and nigiri but the raw fish is not very fresh.. It wasn't as buttery and I hoped they would be. The hot and sour soup was wayyyy to thick. Actually, all the soups in general were NOT hot enough. I love my soup HOT and they only offered warm soup.. 

The service was great! They always refilled drinks and NEVER let plates pile up on tables. I feel like every time I left to get more food, I always came back with a clear table! :) 

There is unlimited drinks and even mimosas if you come during brunch! 

The only desert I had room for at the end was a scoop of mango ice cream and it kinda tastes like perfume...

All and all, I highly recommend this buffet! It's the most pricey though! You can find seafood buffets for $35-45 on the strip.

My friend and I were those tourists who were looking to experience a luxury buffet. We couldn't get our hangover selves out of bed on Sunday for the Sterling Brunch so we decided that we would try out the Bacchanal Buffet on a Monday. Do yourself a favor and buy the groupon! You save about $5 per person and anything helps right?!? You'll have to pay tax and tip, but still a good deal. 

Firstly, don't go the long way to get to the buffet like we did. After you enter Caesar's Palace entrance, go through the Casino and follow the signs. 

We showed up around 10:45am and didn't have to wait! Our server took our drink order right away and it was champagne for me. At first when I walked around, I was not impressed. It was alot of breakfast food: sausage, eggs, bacon, eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, etc. 

I love me some lox, but I came for the king crab and seafood. I figured I would start with the meat station that was serving American wagyu, prime rib, turkey, etc. Prime rib and wagyu were yummy! As I was finishing up my plate of meats, what do you know, they bring out the king crab, snow crab, shrimp, and crab claws. All of this is well worth the price of the buffet. You can't get this quality and quantity for cheaper. 

But awesomeness doesn't end there. Our server was amazing! Our glasses were always full of champagne. He was super attentive and gave me new silverware and cloth napkins cuz you know I'm a messy eater haha. This and the amazing pandan creme brulee took my rating from a 4 to a 5. 

Go for the brunch/lunch time or dinner (I heard it is alot busier during this time, but there are even more seafood options). Don't go too early or you'll fill up on breakfast food and not have room for the seafood which seems like they bring out around 11ish. Skip the dim sum, sushi, pizza if you are an avid seafood lover so you so don't fill up. But who am I to tell you how to live your life! I did sneak in all of those things too haha. Of course get some champagne because why not?

Such an amazing buffet! 

The seafood was the best part of the buffet. The crab legs were so good. Sushi was amazing, we loved the tuna rolls. Make sure you come on an empty stomach so you can get a taste of everything. 

All you can drink add on for $15!
Super good food .. shrimp & crab legs ! You do need to crack them yourself (the Wynn you don't lol)
What a way to start a quality Sunday brunch Buffett. Awesome choices. Beat the line.  Start early.

My friend and I decided to go here on a whim and ended up not only feeling like ballers (that price tag is quite hefty...) but also full of the best buffet food I have EVER had the pleasure of eating.

Let's begin with decor. The place was decorated in a very modern fashion, down to the glass cases of king crab, the comfortable chairs and extra-soft napkins, and even the lounge music! I was surprised the wait was so short as well (20 minutes for a 7:30pm dinner). Then again, it was the Monday after Thanksgiving so people were probably still full of turkey. 

Looking from the outside, I thought the buffet was going to be fairly small but it turned out to be a massive freaking labyrinth. I was shocked when I walked in. From what I remember, there was an Asian food station, salad, Italian, Mexican, American, MEAT, and SEAFOOD. Dessert is in its own private island in the center of the buffet. 

Here's a quick summary/review of what I ate:

-* Lamb chop: AWESOME. My first time having lamb. Perfect and not too cooked or chewy at all.
- Brisket: Oh. My. Goshh. I can't even. It was as good as my favorite slow-cooked brisket my mom stews at home (and she's the best chef I know).
- Prime Rib: Pretty good, but I've had better.
- Sweet Potato Fries: Yummy and sweet but by the time I had been through the lines and got to eat it, it was cold ):
- Mac and Cheese: Why would I get mac n cheese at a 45-dollar buffet? I was craving it, okay! It was nothing extraordinary though.
- *String Beans: Tell me...How in the world could string beans taste so good?! I still can't get over it.
- Lobster Corn Chowder: A little too sweet for me and I couldn't find any pieces of lobster meat in the tiny tray.
- Pretzel Roll: Cold and too tough. The ONLY thing that I legitimately did not like.
- *King Crab Legs: Pre-opened, juicy, delicious, sweet, just hnnnng. Dipped in butter, of course. You can get it hot and fresh from the boiler if you give the server your plate.
- Oyster Shooters: Yummy!
- Raw Oyster: Small but fresh.
- Shrimp Cocktail: The shrimp are larger than normal buffet shrimp. I appreciate that.
-* Creme Brulee: Awesome. The creamy part wasn't too sweet and the sugary top was crisp as should be.
- Macaroons: This was my first time having macaroons so I don't know if it was supposed to be so sweet, but I definitely felt a tooth-ache after a few bites.
- *Cupcake: Strawberry Lemon cream...Perfectly smooth, light, and not too sweet. Loved it!

*Favorites

I tried a lot of little desserts but most were similar and I'm not much of a dessert person in the first place. I also tried a lot more food but the ones I listed were most memorable. Also, I basically skipped all the Asian food because I felt like they weren't worth it for the buffet when I could eat something else.

Rated four stars instead of 5 because of the price and how long I had to wait in line to get food. If they only served the best half of their dishes and got rid of the duds while lowering the price a bit, I would definitely rate this place a five.

Sorry if my review is a bit incoherent. To be honest, the best description I could give you of Bacchanal is the following: SKHLKDHJFLAH HNNG.

That is all. I will probably come back here for my birthday in a few months.

I waited in line for 1hr and 40 min for weekend brunch at 11:30am.  Since they have a seperate line pass $15, the wait to pay for a cashier got longer.  This new line made waiting in line longer because 3 cashiers would help line pass/silver members and only one cashier for the regular line.  Otherwise I enjoy the food-Asian, carving, Italtian, desserts, American food.  The staff refill my drinks without asking. It's also perfect for big groups since they have tables for large groups of 6-10 people.  No blue stone crab, just shrimp, oysters, and crab legs. 


Cons:
 -They also charge $15 for a line pass.  -Need a price info posted on a wall
-Didn't know the omelett station is at the desert station before I was too full to eat
-Need to post the buffet  prices info on the wall

Pros:
-Love carne asada tacos, duck, asian food
-red velvet pancakes are delish
-sweet potatoes tots were delish
-variety of juices are tasty too
-macaroons are good
-pizzas are tasty

Everything was top notch quality and the selection was huge. I am a picky eater and I made the decision to try everything  even if I didn't think I would like it. 

Every single item was absolutely delicious and it was relatively easy to feel like I got my money's worth even with the all you care to drink package added.
Mehhhh. Just super overpriced. I'd have given 4 stars if it was $40. Nothing made me want to go back for seconds.

When people say that Las Vegas is the Mecca of buffets - this is no joke. I experienced this for the first time at the Caesar's palace-Bacchanal Buffet. The stereotype definition of buffets are about stuffing your face at a low cost all you can eat station-loading up on carb rich fast food items- like pizza, burgers and nuggets. Come to Bacchanal and you'll learn the art of true sampling.

We went early to avoid the line up my friends warned me about. Went around 10 Am and there was no lineup -120$ for two people entry-very worth it! We were greeted warmly by Elaine, the employee of the month, she walked us through each of the stations and how everything works before seating us close to the omlette station. Super glad to have met her! My eyes glowed I'm awe of the presentation. Seafood stations with tiger shrimp, snow crabs; meat station with sliced filet mignon, turkey or chicken; an Asian station that includes sushi, dim sum and Chinese food; cheese display, that's only to name a few! Oh and can't forget the dessert bar that had chefs to custom make crepes, equipped with a candy station, gelato station and assorted cakes and pastries. 

My favourites: deviled eggs, chicken & waffles, Mexican open faced egg on a tortilla, boursin scrambled eggs, the dim sum, lemon basil gelato and the freshly made watermelon juice.

Purely heaven. It makes sense that I wasn't able to sample every dish becauase it keeps changing.. And as we exited around noon, the line up for bacchanals was huge.. So make sure to go super early to sample their brunch menu - a true delight to complete your appetite!

I went for brunch. The Wagu beef was good. Salmon sushi was salty but The California rolls were good. I enjoyed the fresh beet salad, Cesar salad and lettuce wedge. The lobster Benedict was different and on a fresh artichoke heart. I was not impressed with desserts The hot lava cake did not have chocolate inside. The creme brûlée's was good and my favorite of their desserts. If you check in with yelp they give a free glass of champagne.

Stay away. I can't believe how bad the food and the service was. To add to this, they charged us $45 per person + tax! I left they're saying to myself "never again". I remember walking into a buffet at Caesar's about 20 years ago. I don't recall the name of it back then. But I remember how bad the food was. I guess some things never change. They just charge you more now. Do yourself a favor. Find a Pollo Loco and you'll be much better off ordering off of the $1 menu.

Decided to come here because I couldn't land a reservation at the sterling brunch and I am a total rewards member so why not just come here. First off most of these pics are a LIE I can tell the website promo photos from actual tourist ones. Wanna know why? Cause 90% of what's pictured was never there!!!!! No lobster, no king crab, no lamb, no carving station, no hot butter for the stingy little crab legs they DID have... ugh a mess. The yogurt parfait and gelato station were actually real.... yogurt looked old waffle station was a mess. I did actually enjoy my green juice though. Over all this was a cheaper alternative but does not hold a candle to the sterling brunch what so ever. I feel paying almost $70 per person with beverages if my memory serves me correctly, was a bit much for a BUFFET (not brunch) that was honestly worth less than $20. I WISH I got at least half of what's pictured on yelp, but unfortunately I feel swindled to be honest.

HANDS DOWN THE BEST BUFFET 
We went for dinner which was $54.99 on the weekday. The line was long as expected.
We were able to get inside at 8pm which was 2 hours before closing. 
They had a seafood section, meat section, Chinese food selection, salad section, tacos made to order, soup(ramen,pho,miso), dim sum section, Italian section, dessert/fruit section, and so much more!
My favorites were:
1. American Waygu Beef
2. Lamb 
3. Snow crab legs(they split it in half for you and there's melted butter to dip with too)
4. Oysters 
5. Roasted pork belly 
6. Beef ribs 

Honestly, everything here was good. It was well seasoned and did not taste like cheap buffet food. I think it is worth the money. 
However, I did not enjoy their steamed snow crabs legs. It was really salty! They also have bone marrow, but it was too much for me.
Thumbs up! Lots of variety! Definitely coming back! The atmosphere is awesome :) I love the decor, vegetarian friendly, great staff!
饥饿营销..明明里面很多空位还告诉我们要排队1个半小时到2个小时，大厅很暗淡，黑灯瞎火的，食物一般吧，就蟹比较新鲜好吃。性价比不太高，有点失望。they told us to wait 1.5h while we just waited for 20min.when we walked in there were lots of empty table available.

Insane collective of different types of food from around the world, the service was really good (they will give you a new soda, when the server sees it is empty). The homemade Italian ice cream was really tasty too. The only thing that didn't live up to the price (80 USD) was the selection of meat, expected a larger variety of high quality meat, which you wouldn't normally eat..

Skip the line when you have 7 Star, Diamond or Platinum Status with Caesars Rewards. Otherwise you'll be in a long line waiting. We were seated immediately. There is a huge variety of food. I'm mostly into Seafood they have crab legs on the far right side that a served hot. There are several chefs on hand to make you certain things and at the end dessert is so good all the things you can think of.
This place was great and worth the money.  You will have to wait for about 45 minutes but be patient, you will be satisfied.

This is the most spectacular buffet I have been to, well worth the $35 I paid for brunch. As a big fan of Mexican food, I was impressed with the Mexican food station. There were freshly-made corn tortillas, and the carnitas were top-notch. All the accompaniments were well-prepared. There were many salsas to choose from, all of which were excellent.

The other stations looked excellent too but I only sampled a small number of things. The dim sum was good, the sushi was just so-so, with paltry helpings of fish in rolls; no nigiri. There was a charcuterie display that had delicious sliced salami and so forth. There were a selection of fresh juices, probably 8 or 10 different ones, but they weren't labeled. I just picked a red one and it turned out to be watermelon, which was delicious. I later learned that I should have just asked what they all were, because when I got to the dessert island, there were a bunch of unlabeled tiny plated desserts. They all looked delicious, but I wanted to know what they were. I asked the nice young lady behind the counter and she very graciously told me the name of each item I pointed out. After I pointed out and asked about 3 or 4 I realized she was going to be patient enough to tell me what they all were, so I asked to her to name them all. She seemed honestly pleased to take the time to explain every one to me. She also offered me a tiny souffle that was just coming out of the oven. A different young lady who made me a crepe was also really friendly and helpful. A chef walked by while she was making my crepe and asked her to wipe off the top of the counter when she had a chance. She smiled and nodded, and said "yes, chef". 

The space itself was absolutely gorgeous; one of the finest dining rooms I have ever had the pleasure to dine in. We dined in the wood section and there lots of nice subtle details that added up to make the expense obvious. My only complaints have to do with things that were not the food:

(1) It was slightly difficult to navigate from the table back to the buffet areas. At one point I found myself squeezing between the chair occupied by an obvious buffet-lover and a wooden partition. I'm not sure how that happened but more obvious aisleways in the dining area would have helped.

(2) There just weren't enough labels for the food. Once I figured out I could ask and the staff would be gracious enough to explain everything, it was fine, but I'm sure there were lots of things I would have loved to sample if I had just known what they were.

(3) The only bathroom was outside the entrance and woefully undersized for a buffet that seats hundreds of people. After tiring of waiting for a stall, I went in search of another bathroom elsewhere in Caesar's Palace. I found a nearly empty one near the main lobby that was three times the size of the one near the buffet, but it was a long hike there and back.

Girls trip! 
Been a few visits and think its time I let you all know... this buffet never disappoints. 

The line can be long at times but moves fast. It pays to have status so you can move ahead the general line. 

Food - wide variety, fresh and yum. One of my favs was the shrimp and grits and duck. Dessert bar has something for everyone too.


Eat up!

overrated and underwhelming. often seen as the "best buffet in vegas", I have to wonder the quality of the other buffets... At like $60 for a meal, you're better off trying other restaurants; especially if you're craving something specific.

The Good: brisket was juicy and fat! (take it from a southern boy like me). Some of the seafood was also delicious like the salmon.

The Bad: Not all of the seafood quality was great... let's just say some of my friends had a bad time a few hours later. The dimsum could've used sum more flavor.. being cantonese (and actually the gentlemen behind the counter were speaking cantonese), I was surprised at how bland the dimsum was... stay away from it.

The Ugly: If you're like me and you look for the sushi at AYCE buffets... just don't bother looking. You actually might miss the section cause it's so small(not that you'd really gain much from eating it.)

For starters, I am generally not a big fan of buffets, but since that is one of the things vegas is known for I decided to try quite a few of them (over time of course). With that being said, this is by far one of the best buffets out there. They have a huge selection, ranging from pizza and sushi to a street taco section and all of it tastes amazing. Since I goto vegas multiple times a year I go to this place every single time and even introduce my travel companions to show them how great this buffet truly is. Even there dessert selection is gigantic and filled with an abundance of high quality decadent treats.
Clearly the best buffet in Vegas. Service is awesome, and all food is delicious. Price is well worth it.
Beet buffet in Vegas!  I recommend going on Friday if you can to avoid the lines.  And always load up on crab legs!

GREAT FOOD! Lines could be very long but the wait is worth it! This buffet is price about $70 a person but it is Las Vegas right? Definitely worth my money, prime rib and crab legs was delicious! Their dessert section with even better! They have ube gelato, which was really delicious! Our server was really nice and attentive! Check in for a free champagne!!
Good place for buffet with family. Check in this place if you stay Caesar's place Las Vegas hotel and casino

TLDR; great food for a buffet. Lines can get long

To start off I'm not really a huge fan of buffets because the idea of stuffing yourself until you physically can't eat anymore in order to make your money's worth is..kinda ridiculous to me. I've never walked out of a buffet feeling healthy/energetic/ready to go for a run. It's more like sleepy, tired with a hint of regret and disgust. 

Anyways, the line can be a little confusing. First off there's a line to *purchase* the tickets. BUT in that line if you're a group of 5 or more, they let you go through a shorter line that only deals with big groups. Second BUT is that all members of the group needs to physically be there in line in order for them to let you through. This is probably because they don't want you to cheat and have one person in the group wait in the line to get in the restaurant itself. Which brings me to the next point...
After you purchase your tickets, you need to stand in line to *get in* to the buffet. There's separate lines for 1-2 ppl, 3-4 ppl and 5+ ppl. They'll call your name and you'll be escorted to a seat. 

Now to the food - I'm never amazed at the quality of buffet foods because it's usually always about quantity over quality. However I was impressed at the type of food that they offered. Bone marrow, escargot, brisket, gelato to name a few. They categorize the foods to different cuisines so once you figure out where everything is it's convenient. I also liked how there's a few BYO sections (tacos, crepes, noodles) and there was a ride range of desserts to choose from. 
I do think the desserts were overall not that great in terms of taste though. Presentation was there but they all tasted a bit off. Either bread was too dry or cream was too bland and sweet. Also, the music. The only songs I listened to during my whole 2 hours there were pop songs from 10 years ago. Justin Bieber before he hit puberty, Katy Perry with her Teenage Dream and Pitbull. Not the best music to listen to at a high class buffet? 

Overall I still enjoyed the food more than I thought I would. But I'd still rather go to somewhere else for the same wait time and price.

The food quality here was beyond my expectation. There were numerous dishes from different cultures to choose from: Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, traditional American, French, and Vietnamese, etc. I loved how they present their buffet and the food was delicious. Not to mention they had great selection of high quality seafood from oysters to snow crab. Their meet selection was also very diverse and tasty. Also, they only serve snow crab for dinner so if you love snow crab you should go after 3pm. Their decoration and service were also outstanding. The staff was helpful, especially Ms Shu who was our server. She consistently followed up with us for drinks to make sure we were happy. This place is for sure the best buffet in Vegas. I'd definitely come back again. A must try!
La comida riqisima EMMA  nos atendio exlente al llegar a la linea nos dio buena informacion la berdad qe es wl mejor buffet

It was very busy when we came in but we got seated right away. Lots of choices! The sushi is fresh / legit. I'm iffy about sushi. Coming from Hawaii, I'm used to sushi being a certain way. It did not disappoint. I was also craving char siu pork and haven't had any red and juicy like the ones back home. Got some here and omg drool. Cute pastries. Friendly server. Vast variety. I could barely finish my food

If you check in, you get a complimentary drink.
Best buffet!  Ramona was an excellent waitress!  Highly recommended!

One of the best buffet ever we had. Definitely we will come back here when we go back to las vegas. :)) how I wish I can eat and taste all the food. The price is kinda expensive and line is long but its all worth it. :))

Best buffet in Las Vegas! Yes, it's a huge statement to make but unless another one opens, I'll stick to what I said! Bacchanal Buffet is pricier compared to other buffets but it is worth it. There are a lot of options to choose from and a lot of different cuisines. My favorite thing to get here are the crab legs! I came in for lunch on a weekday and came too early for the unlimited oysters that they would be serving at 3 pm. Bacchanal Buffet is much much better than the Buffet at the Wynn. I walked around the Wynn Buffet not knowing what to eat, but at Bacchanal, there are so many good dishes to choose! In my opinion, Bacchanal Buffet is more comparable to Wicked Spoon, but still better. Make sure you leave some room for dessert. They have a crepe station where they can make crepes however you like! 

Tip: Looking to cleanse your palette? Try the Lemon Basil sorbet ice cream. Sour, but definitely works!

Let me break it down for you~

-If you're going to spend money on a buffet, I really think Bacchanal is where it's at.

-If you're impatient (like me) you can go sign up beforehand on their digital kiosks and then hang around until you get a text.

-They give you souvenir plate holder things to protect your baby fingers from getting burned.

-The dessert bar OOOMGGGGGGG I could pay just to eat multiple rounds of their desserts.

-There's also fresh juices in ~*exotic*~ flavors like Hibiscus haha.

TL;DR: this review is hella short just read it and GO TO BACCHANAL~
Number 1 ranked Buffett in Vegas for a reason. Seafood here is on point. All options are on point. The dessert bar was fantastic. It's probably the best buffet I've ever been to.

This is still the best buffett taste and food wise...
I do wish they would bring back the Lamb chops... they were the best in the world.... 5stars out of 5...!!!

I was in Vegas by myself and thought I would try this out. It seems to be rated highest of all buffets. I am not eating meat, except fish but there was plenty to eat. Sushi, dim sum, shrimp tacos, veggies, etc. There is no salad bar but there were salad samplers. The dessert station was pretty extensive. It's a large place but I do like Aria's buffet too. At $54.95 per person it isn't cheap but I felt I had good food and walked away without feeling sick.
Went here for brunch to avoid the queue. A variety of food selection. A go-to buffet in Vegas.

Excellent food, everything was perfectly cooked and served, and carefully made to perfection. Every item I ate was great and can't wait to go back for more.  The only negative thing was the long line getting in but what do you expect when coming in on a Friday and to a nice place?

Maybe we came on a bad day but the food definitely looks a lot better than it tastes. Only reason this place didn't get a 1/5 is because they have so much variety so I'm sure out of the 100 or so dishes on offer you'll find one or two you like and 90 you really don't. 

What was really off putting about this place was there were about 10 flies crawling all over all the fruit! Absolutely gross and it explains the food poisoning I got. 

Again, I must stress the food looks A LOT better than it tastes. So if your goal is just to make your friends jealous with photos of nice food then sure come eat here. If not, there's definitely better places you could go.

How dare this place still operate?! They don't just rip off precious guests' money from slot machines but also from this awful buffet place. Not as many selections as I had thought, and most importantly the crabs! Yes - they offered a lot of Jonah's stone crabs, as well as Alaskan king and snow king crab legs BUT THEY HAD NO TASTE. Expensive seafood but cooked incorrectly. What a waste of money and crab resources. Pissing me off. Also, with the amount of time we waited and amount of money we paid, you would think they would help us crack open the stone crabs, BUT NOPE. with a 2 hour eating limit, it took us 15 mins to crack open 1 stone crab so we didn't even go back there second there. This place is too hyped up, my disappoint also hyped up

Best buffet in LV in my opinion. Of course long wait on line is not fun,  but it was worth it.  Absolutely loved it!
Great choice of seafood, meets, Asian cuisines, desserts were really good too.
Delicious, just saw the feature video of the chef. Just wondering if there's any plans to stop wasting so much plastic during the tastings by switching to metal spoons that are washed everyday?
Good food and extensive variety. Great customer service by Steve O the chef. Thank you!
This buffet is hands down the best buffet in Caesars and maybe even all of Vegas! Our server was Jennifer and she is excellent, amazing service!!

Overall the buffet was good, but for the price I prefer Aria's buffet. Long line even with my Platinum players card to get in. The selection was ok but for the price I expected better. The sushi was good, the lobster mac and cheese was undercooked and if you found pieces of lobster in there you won the jackpot lol. Disappointed they didnt have flan as a dessert option however the strawberries and cream was excellent.

We had a poor dining experience particularly due to the service with our waiter. Seemed to be racist throughout our dining experience. Otherwise, the ambiance would have been great if our waiter wasn't so terrible. It really is a very nice room.

Food was pretty decent, but not particularly a wow factor. Asian noodles were on the wrong side of mediocre, BBQ sauce was terrible for their meat selections. American food was again mediocre, Italian food a little better than average. Meat carving station was solid, but then again it's hard to mess that up. Dessert was pretty impressive though for the wife, but I'm a dude, I'm there for food.

Definitely overrated compared to some of the other vegas buffets. We're locals and have tried many of the buffets. A lot of our friends from out of town have really enjoyed their dining experience there, but from my perspective, perhaps explore your other options.

After watching and reading reviews of the Bacchanal Buffet, I decided this would be a must go to buffet while in Vegas. Indeed, most reviewers said it was one of the best or the best, buffet in Vegas. Sadly, it was one of the worst buffet's I have been to. I arrived on a Friday at 2pm. It took an 45 minutes to get seated. The good is that I only was charged for the lunch price and was able to see the lunch leftovers and get the fresh dinner food. Looking forward to the buffet, I had not eaten all day, and I was starved. My first trip out I loaded up on a plate of cold jonah crab, and wagu beef. It was terrible. The crab had been frozen to long and was icy and deteriorating. Worse, the crab was not cut and they only provided a cracker.  I had to chase down someone else's table waiter as I did not see mine for the first 20 minutes just to get a cracker. I was told that they did not have any shellers for the crab legs.  I saw people coming out with fresh plates of crab legs that were steamed and decided to give that a try. The steamed crab was ok, but a lot went to waste because the "best buffet" did not cut the crab or have shellers for the crab legs. In between my crabby plates, I did try the wagu, medium rare. To say the least, it should almost be a crime what they did to the wagu. It was dry and un-flavorful (not like other wagu I have eaten in the past. I did go back again and try and get a better piece of wagu, but it was the same thing. However, I saw fresh lamb t-bones being put out and grabbed a couple. It was tolerable, after all I was still starving, but way to dry. Thankfully, I the table waiter decided to show up and get us something to drink. It took him about 10 minutes to get back with our drinks of coffee and lemonade. A lot of their food did not look that good that was out. For instance, I usually load up on cheeses and deli meats like prosciutto. However, the meager selection of such looked extremely dry and hard. The sushi was as good or bad as what you get at a normal Chinese buffet, nothing special. The desserts were also not very good compared to other buffets like the Peppermill. I usually get an ice cream cone to go and the "best buffet" did not even have cones for the ice cream. I left full, but not over full, like I usually leave a buffet. Most of the food out was just not worth going back for seconds. I like crab and would have gone back for more, but without shellers, it just was not worth it. The waiter that I saw one more time in my 2-hour stay said they normally cut the crab in half so you don't need shellers. Perhaps it was a bad day for the Bacchanal Buffet. I would not go there again even if it was a cheap Buffet. Based on my experience, I would encourage others to try one of the other buffets on the strip and not waste your time, calories, or money on the Bacchanal Buffet. I should also mention that It might be good to stay around a toilet about an hour after you leave.

So delicious!!!! This place is amazing. Will be going back. Be sure to go on a weekday due to the long wait times. I went on a Friday around 4 and ended up waiting for about 30 minutes which is better than the time I ended up leaving because it was 8pm on a weekend and the wait was over an hour and a half.

If I could give this a bajillion stars I would.  We decided to eat here on a weekday morning for breakfast since it's cheaper, and went around the time they switch to lunch so we could try those foods too (there is a 2 hr max limit).  Using my Yelp app I was able to get a coupon for free VIP access so we were able to skip a very long line (at least 20 people ahead of us) and be seated immediately.  I think because we had this VIP status our hostess gave us a detailed tour of the buffet.  Our waitress once we were seated was very attentive.  And most of all, the food was SOOOOO GOOOOOD.  I especially enjoyed the create your own crepe bar - I definitely went up for seconds.  I also hit up the omlette bar and got an egg white bar which was very tasty.  The desserts were out of this world too and included numerous flavors of gelato.  This place definitely is expensive but it's definitely well worth the money!
The best buffet I have ever been to. Food and service was excellent. Never have had a server as good as Romulus.

The Bacchanal Buffet is the best buffet on the strip. It has the widest range of food, the best tasting and a great layout. One of the first things I would like to praise them on is having hot crab. A lot of buffets only sever cold crab and it's fine and all but to me hot crab taste better. I have been to close to all buffets on the strip and the the Bacchanal has the best quality around. I can't say everything was perfect but about 95% of the food there was great or better. The line can be long but I feel it's worth the wait. Whenever I'm in Vegas this will be my go to buffet.

I don't understand the hype. Most of the food here was just ok. The items that stood out the most to me were the truffle poached egg, pho, and chocolate dipped strawberries. Don't even bother with the "wagyu" or brisket, both were tasteless. I saw 2 tables around of loading on the salt on the meat. That says a lot, especially when these are fattier cuts of meat and should have a ton a natural flavors. I don't think I got my money's worth at all. They only way I'd be back is if the prices went down.
The quality food is not as great as before.... i used to love this place when im in Vegas.. but i guess this will be my last time here..
Great Service and food !! Esmeralda our sever was excellent. Always eat at Bacchanal when staying at Caesars.

Pretty good value for $65, lots of quality meats but mediocre seafood. No king crab and very little lobster. Immense selection of food though with everything overall decent quality. Great service. 

I went on a Friday night at 930 and there was zero line up.

My rating: 3 Stars / My wife's rating: 3 Stars / My dad's rating: 3 stars / My mom's rating: 5 stars - so I decided to give them 4 stars. Yes, they're expensive. Yes, they have many selections in terms of different kinds of foods. Yes, their service is great. Food quality is the biggest point here. According to my mom, the quality on their food is great and that she would definitely return to this place, especially for their sea food. On the other hand, my dad, my wife and I had different opinions. Their sea foods weren't that great, and other food selections were mediocre. They may be good enough for $30/person buffet in my opinion, but they definitely weren't worth the price that we paid for. Unless it's my mom's birthday, we won't returning to this place.
outstanding selection of high quality tt tasty dishes fresh and many prepared right in front of you. pricey so go for the protein. you can eat carbs at home.

We heard lots of mixed reviews about this buffet. My wife and I were in Vegas for a trade show and decided to use our Diamond Caesars rewards $100 voucher here for brunch. It covered the price for both of plus unlimited spirits. Food always tastes better when it's free! 

Overall we were very impressed. The buffet food area is huge. It starts near the entrance and wraps all the way to the back. There's lots of custom options like omelets and crepes. We love crepes! Deserts bar is awesome too. Plenty of choices for the picky palette. They even have gelato rather than just a soft serve machine.
Best buffet I've ever been to... unlimited mimosas need I say more?? No, but I will! Make your own cheese and cold cut plate!! What the?! Definitely worth the price and wait. Period.

The name of the game here is excess, folks. I mean, it is called the BACCHANAL BUFFET. If you don't hate yourself at the end of the meal, you didn't do the place justice. 

My motto is "come for lunch; stay for dinner," and that is exactly what my group and I did, for three hours on a friday afternoon. 

Bacchanal highlights: 
*My bro and his wife loved the burger sliders. They said it was the best thing they had there.
*I really enjoyed the congee. It was freaking amazing!
*Macaroons were a-freaking-mazing!
*Charcuterie was great. Wonderful selection of meats, cheeses, dried fruits & nuts. They could add some more bread and cracker type things. 

Bacchanal MISSES: 
OYSTERS were disappointing. They were sandy & icky. Come on now, Caesar's. 
CRAB was also disappointing. They had them pre-cut & sliced down the middle, and sitting in big pots of what seems like just plain water. Crab came out really bland-tasting.
SERVICE was hit or miss. The lady we had at first was rarely there. When it was time for her shift to end, she came over, opened the check presenter (i ordered wine and paid at the table) to, i assume, see if i included her tip, and when she saw that there was no tip in there, said, "I'm off in ten minutes," and handed it back to me. After I put her tip in there, she disappeared! I had to hail a random person to ask if I could get plates cleared. 

Tip: Am glad I came for lunch instead of dinner that friday. for an extra 20 bucks, dinner came with crab, buckets of mussels & clams, and not much more that couldn't be missed. Go for lunch and save yourself some $$ for the tables!

***oh, and they also had mochi, but i saw the person refilling them & they came out of boxes (mikawaya brand)!

Overall the variety is good. A bit overpriced but I guess it's not too crazy considering it's in Las Vegas. A bit disappointed on the seafood choices. I was expecting more seafood and more fresh options with this price.

Good buffet they have a great seafood selection. Price is $59.99 for the weekend. They have a good selection of food, be prepared to wait a little while if you're a group of 5 or more. Staff friendly.

This review is mostly from a vegetarian point of view and a very tired vegetarian who keeps hoping for more options! I was really excited to check this place out! I was a bit disappointed with the lack of flavorful options for vegetarians (focus on word "flavorful" as there were multiple options but not many of them hit the spot)! I started out strong with some fried green beans and was really looking forward to other dishes; however, the macaroni and cheese had an interesting meaty flavor, not my favorite flavor. Breadsticks and marinara were delicious and the cheese pizza didn't disappoint, but I would really like to see something that is not just pizza and breadsticks and salad as vegetarian options! Coming towards Asian food, fried rice didn't look all that appealing and pad Thai was alright, nothing out of the world. The only winner for me in the Asian food area was the miso soup! It was perfectly salty and full of simple delicious favors! I wish there were some vegetarian ramen or dim sums. Mexican food was also limited for vegetarians. Chips and salsa and guac were alright! The dessert section was great! Loved everything I tried and was pleasantly surprised by the variety and freshness of it all! This was a once in a while kind of experience, probably may skip it next time to try other buffet or may be regular restaurants in Vegas!
AMAZING food, A LOT of cuisines with TONS of food. Unless you're a whale, you won't be able to try everything

Great selection of food, from Asian to Latin American and southern food. Although, the food was good, $60 is a little steep for a buffet but I get it (prices are inflated because it's on the strip). A large group of us went for my boyfriend's birthday to celebrate. The payment process was fast and we were sat quickly. For such an upscale price a few things were lacking. #1 our waitresses attitude. We wish she was more welcoming, she had a very cold personality and a sour look on her face. #2 the furniture. The tables and chairs seemed to be old and not grand enough. The buffet itself was so grand and up-scale looking, then you go to sit at your table and the cloth chairs are wobbly and visibly dirty. Some solid furniture to match the buffet would be cool.

Probably the best buffet I have ever been to. I came during dinner time and there was a Yelp check-in offer for a glass of free champagne, so make sure to check if that is available. My server was awesome and ended up giving me a couple of free refills of the champagne so that was definitely a nice touch. The food itself was pretty high quality. Don't expect fine-dining level of finesse, but for a buffet, the food is as good as it gets. There were dishes with truffle, foie gras, and other expensive ingredients. In addition, they had bone marrow, which was delightful. Although the buffet can run you over $80 per person if you include tax and tip, overall I would say it is worth it. Seriously, you're in Vegas, live it up a little!

I'm kinda disappointed with bacchanal... they were missing some key items when i went couple of weeks ago... they didn't have king crab legs,waygu beef or rack of lamb. I understand that it was EDC weekend and there were more people than there were food. But if they're gonna charge the same $51, they should have those items!! 

I was also disappointed with some of their dessert items.. like their mini cupcakes! WTF? they were so dry! 

I definitely need to go again on a non-crazy weekend because i'm pretty sure they can do sooo much better!

This is hands down the best buffet in Vegas!

My boyfriend and I came here on a Monday for brunch, and we waited for about an hour. Was it worth the wait? Heck yes!

The amount of options they had was huuge! They had seafood, multiple types of meats, Italian cuisine, American, sushi, Chinese, Mexican, and a few Indian options. Everything was so good and so fresh. 

The dessert section was mouth-watering.

The service was very good. The servers kept checking on us, taking our empty plates, and refilling our drinks.

Compared to other buffets I tried (Wynn and the Wicked Spoon), this one stands out with the food quality and quantity. The dinner buffet at Wynn had half the amount of food that Bacchanal had for brunch.

I like the way they will text you when it's your turn to wait in line to pay. Overall the food is better than Wynn's buffet. The King and Dungeness crab was too salty. I got the King crab warmed up in salt bath. 
I wished they would steam it instead, so it's not as salty. 
I'm not sure if it worth the long wait and expense.

I came here with a group of 8 and was seating down shortly. One of my friend is a diamond member. Usually it is quite a wait. There is all types of food here from prime rib to tacos, crab legs to sushi. Take your time eating because there is a lot of choices.

I've been here twice and the soup station always a fail for me. Of course their beef selection are the best compared to others that I've been to. But in my second visit the au jus and gravy are not well stocked. My server was also not smiling could be already tired. Still my favourite buffet in Vegas but hoping next time the soup station will be better because it's not cheap for $65/person.

I finally experienced "WOW" We went for my boo's birthday here and it was unforgettable experience. The decor is 5 star, the customer service is 5 star, the food is 5 full stars!! This restaurant is Cesaer's extension sort of. It's elegant, classy and I would say it's a fine dinning experience. Come hungry but don't attack only crab legs and claws, try at least Italian, 16-hour roasted beef, LOBSTER BISQUE omg the one in tiny metal pot with cute little crawl fish soaked  YUMMMM It is the best experience I had in a buffet! Oh desserts... Japanese souffle cups with tiny decorative edible flower, pistachio ice cream scoop, berry souffle cone, hot crepes....mmm I want to go back already! Do yourself a favor and go there on empty stomach and have fun!

Maybe I drove my expectations too high. But I found this buffet as ordinary. There was seafood but the sea snails were bland and the crab legs were of medium size. I was looking forward to some sumptuous lamb, but the chops were overdone and were a huge disappointment. The brisket and tri tip were acceptable but the stars of the carving station were the Prime Rib and Wagyu beef. And the Paella was good. Japanese fare was ordinary and Chinese options were a joke. My wife and I were relieved that we didn't opt for the Bacchanal VIP option (or the all day buffet) since the seafood tower is built with what can be had at the buffet. Perhaps that option is better for heavy drinkers

I had very high hopes as it being the best buffet but didn't quite have that experience.  My motto is normally "ya get what you paid for" but this was definitely not the case.   At $154 for one child and two adults...nope.  if anything the curiosity killed this cat.  I still prefer M Buffet with the crab legs and more of a variety of seafood options AND unlimited beer/wine.  Best part was probably the comfortable seating and the carving station.   Layout though seems like you are in one line after the other line and more lines.   And as a newby, ya had to watch people so you'd know what to do.   I would've never known where to find The steam crab legs if i didn't see people in line for that.   The wait was ridiculous.  Got there at 5:30 didn't get in till almost 7 and left at 9.  If you are curious, and willing to spend that much $$$ and wait in line, by all means try it.
Amazing buffet with a giant assortment of various types of food. Hot and cold crab legs and a big variety of meats to eat/select from!

Amazing!!! We loved this place . It was 119 for 2 adults for dinner on a Thursday.There was no charge for our two children. There was something for all of us to enjoy. It wasn't overly busy and the staff was very nice. All the food tasted amazing definitely worth the money. The brisket potato skins were our favorite. We will definitely be visiting again on our next trip.

I came to Bacchanal on a whim for lunch with a few co-workers and I was surprised to see so few vegetable dishes. There were plenty of meat dishes and noodles but not a lot of roasted vegetables for those who aren't into meat and carbs. As for desserts, I thought the items offered were very typical with nothing that stood out or made me go "wow, I must consume that!" 


I left disappointed and wanting for more.

Here and wicked Spoon are the 2 best buffets in las vegas!!

Wow....what a great experience....the best thing ever was the crab legs in hot soup....service was outstanding....the place was sooooooooooooo clean too!!!

The people eating were all nice and well kept and this was a high end restaurant -- where you can eat all you want...

It was probably the best 2 hour dinner I have had in years....

I will go back, next time im in Vegas....

Summary: you pay for the variety, not the taste (except desserts, which were amazing)

Lot of variety (cuisines and preparations), but average taste. 
Good service.
Expensive (but at par with other options).

If I could give this place 10 stars, I would.  So many people will recommend the Wicked Spoon or a different buffet, but the Bacchanal stands TALL above the rest.  It is the only buffet you need to try in Vegas.  It is the highest quality with over 500 dishes - this is the cream of the crop.

We went for the brunch buffet (beverages included in price), and were able to use our $100 celebration dinner voucher from Caesars Rewards.  Walking in, you are immersed in total opulence from floor to ceiling.  Amazing towers of fresh seafood on ice including stone crab claws, mussels, colossal shrimp, and more!

 The highlight for me among the sea of food options was the noodle soup bar - Tonkotsu Ramen and Pho were both excellent and authentic.  They had a very substantial Asian section with dim sum, stir fries, congee, Thai noodles, and sushi.  There's also an Italian/Mediterranean station, salad station, southern down home cooking, a street taco station with a plancha, and an immense line of brunch foods that included chicken and waffles, and steak and eggs.

Pace yourself, for the desserts are amazingly crafted.  Every gelato flavor you could imagine (think green tea, ube, coconut), and even a Hawaiian/Asian dessert section!  Such a lovely assortment of food here - wish we had more stomach room to graze a little more!

This is a no brainer if we come to visit again - now go on and treat yo self!

Amazing buffet for $60 per person. After eating the Wynn buffet we were very disappointed and were not planning to eat another buffet. To my surprise, the bacchanal buffet had very fresh dishes. They even offer steamed crab legs as the Wynn buffet does not. Everything tasted fresh. As a non beef/pork eater, only thing I didn't enjoy is the taco station where the employee uses the same tongs for all the meats. The salmon, steamed crab legs, shrimp, turkey and pizza were great. The desert area had sooo many items! They had matcha dessert, chocolate covered strawberries, cakes, tiramisu (FAV!!) gelato, and Vietnamese coffee dessert. Everything was so good! Will definitely be back next time!

I ate here on 8/20/19 and it was the best buffet I have eaten at in Las Vegas. Its a little pricey, but if you can eat a whole lot of crab go here. It also had a little sushi too. I will go here when I return to Vegas.

I went here solely based on yelp reviews, wow clearly i have different tastes than most, while it was all good food and lots of variety you people must not eat much meat, there is no way my wife and i ate $75-80 worth of veggies, maybe i was there on vegan night or something? (Okay I'm joking). But seriously some COOKED seafood would have been awesome. Up here near canada we cook our fish before we eat it and it tastes good that way too. Yep i don't mind sushi, but seriously.. Dessert bar was awesome and over the top maybe? All in all i left with a bad taste in my mouth (pun intended) and had to wash it down with another $9 margarita from a street vendor.

I enjoy Caesar's Palace from the shows, the forum shops, the gambling.. but most of all, Bacchanal buffet. I've tried buffets on and off of the strip, and Bacchanal is one of the few that keeps me coming back. I enjoy that they have kiosks that give you an estimated time and take down your number so that if there's a long wait, you can go shop and come back once you get a text message that it's time to wait in the line. Depending on the season is how busy it is, but there's usually at least a 20 min wait. The lunch and dinner pricing are a little different but not too far off from each other. Your meal comes with bottomless soda/mimosas/bloody mary's, etc. They used to serve Harry and Sons tea but they got rid of it and now serve lipton, which is my only complaint.

The buffet itself has a variety of foods: seafood, Asian food, Mexican, breakfast foods, and good old American. But the best part? The dessert bar. I can go on and on about the buffet, from the mini cheeseburger slider with a toasted bun to the noodle bar that holds ramen, pho, and udon with a section to customize your own veggies and spices. They have some Asian desserts including egg tart, Thai tea boba bombs (boba, a scoop of Thai tea ice cream, and coconut milk), and my all time favorite--their strawberry cheesecake pops. I literally eat 5 of them.

The service is fast and friendly and they don't rush you while you enjoy your meal. Bathrooms are nearby and I love the ambiance of the buffet. I love coming in groups or even just one other person. My mouth is drooling as I write this review and I can't wait to go back!

This place is not what you think it is . The food quilting is very low and the place smell like sea food . The price is very high for what they are offering . I am not going to come back. Aria buffet is much better than this place .

The wait is insane... We got there around 830pm and it was still a very long wait (as expected).

The food was meh... for how much it costs, how long we waited, and the anticipation built up... it was all just meh.

Last time I was here was in 2013, and all these years I kept telling everyone how delicious everything was. This week was absolutely opposite. My friend and I went there for dinner. We expected a long line so a 70 min wait in line wasn't a surprise. But the lady at the register was absolutely rude. She was so unbelievably rude that even after paying I wanted to just walk out. My friend tried to ask her something and instead she raised her voice and slapped the receipt on the counter. Wow. No hi, no bye, no eye contact instead talked to everyone as if she was irritated with everyone. After I mentioned how rude she was acting, she tried to smile at the next person. 

Now let's go over the food. The selection was impressive; however, the taste wasn't. The Thai fried rice tasted very good, but it was so dry and hard. The pad Thai and drunken noodle had no flavor. Very bland. 

The ravioli didn't taste good at all. The pasta was so thick that it tasted worse than frozen ones. The meatballs were delicious. Boneless chicken wings were so overcooked that it became very very dry. Tasted worse than a fast food chicken. The halibut was so way overcooked that it turned rubbery and hard. Couldn't even finish the bite. Found a giant fish bone too. Overall all the seafood except for scallops tasted very bland and dry. Some shrimp were ice cold. 

My bowl of poke tasted really good, but the next batch of poke was bland, no flavor. The sushi looked as if a new cook made these. The cut was extremely uneven and just didn't look appetizing. 

Desserts didn't disappoint us. Highly recommend the desserts. 

Overall NOT a good experience. Absolutely not worth $59. If the price is going to remain so steep then raise the standards.

Just average. 

I was here for Sunday holiday brunch. I came at 8 am, right at opening. There was no wait. Cost: $55 plus tax, so about $60.

The king crab legs were too salty. No stone crab or oyster. The shrimp and seafood salad were good. The "lobster" eggs Benedict was sad...it had a few shreds of lobster on it. The biscuit in the eggs Benedict was fluffy, though.

The Asian station didn't have raw fish for sushi. It was disappointing. A number of the dishes were already dried from sitting out for too long. The dimsum was solid.

I liked the fresh fruits and vegetables. They were fresh. The egg tart was also fantastic.

I did not think this was worth $60. Just my opinion.

Gr8 buffet, the seafood line is a bit much but I don't dig on seafood do it worked out great.  This buffet is in Caesers Palace.  I highly recommend giving this a go on Sunday after the madness.  They have a huge variety of eats.  I tried my best to eat items that weren't filling with hopes I can try lots. I started with a cheese/fruit plate topped with things like beef broccoli, ribs, egg roll.  Also tried the taco bar and it was def worth it.  Had 3 slices of meat with Mac n cheese and mashed potatoes.  Then dessert.  I highly recommend getting drunk before hand and do not get the mimosas.  I had like 6 and barely felt a buzz.  I'd rather save belly room for more tasty bites.  :D

Ever since staying at CP one year during our annual sisters trip, Bacchanal has been my go to buffet. I usually venture out and try different buffets when in Vegas, but since that first time at Bacchanal I was hooked! Since then, I've probably dined here about 5x. Bacchanal has never let me down until my most recent visit on 3/25/19. I'm not quite sure if it's because it was a Monday, but they did not offer a wide selection of seafood as I'm used too. They didn't have crawfish, oysters on a shell, clams, or king crab. They did however have snow crab, snails, shrimp, mussels, and dungenous crab. They also use to split open the crab legs in halves so it was easier to eat, but they quit doing that for some reason. I still appreciate Bachannal for having a variety of different cuisines. They have an American, Asian, Mexican, Italian, and Chinese section. They also have a carving station, dessert section and sushi bar. I'm a seafood junkie, so I'm mostly disappointed in their lack of seafood choices on this particular night. I guess all good things must come to an end! Back to the buffet drawing board! Thank you- NEXT! (Lol!)

Pro Tip:
Find you a Diamond Rewards player, otherwise expect to stand in a long a** line to gain entrance!

Love this place! I always go here when in Vegas. 
Not everything is super amazing but it's the best buffet you can go to. Try it out!!

I don't normally pay $60 to eat at a buffet, but when I do, it's because I'm in Vegas.  

After all, where else would you have to spend that that much on a buffet?  And while I'd typically prefer to spend that kind of money on a more "traditional" meal, things are a little different when you're in the City of Sin/Gluttony.  So, if I'm going to do some damage at a buffet, I might as well do it right!

Like so many of the better (and pricier) buffets in Vegas, Bacchanal does a great job of combining both quality (for a buffet) and variety in their offerings.  Seriously, there's PLENTY to choose from - seafood (crab legs, raw oysters, mussels, shrimp, etc.), sushi, salad, pizza, pastas, made-to-order tacos, carvery station (lamb, prime rib, sausages, pork loin, etc.), Asian dishes, fruits, desserts (chocolate covered strawberries!), and more.  

-- PLATE #1 - Prime Rib, Sausage, lamb, Onion Rings
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=p2b3VrXJwMZiRd0JwLCdJA#mrb056oZjB9C2jzPM-2sYQ)
The guy gave me a cut matching the wellness I wanted, but also with lot of tendons.  Still, the meat was tender and well-seasoned.  The lamb was great as well (perhaps a tad salty) and the sausage was fine, though nothing special.

-- PLATE #2 - Raw Oysters, Fresh Snow Crab Legs, Salmon Sashimi, Tempura Roll
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=p2b3VrXJwMZiRd0JwLCdJA#IK9Vz3U6qMf6W1-Yi22rNA)
For the most part, Bacchanal's seafood is fresh.  The oysters were plump and meaty (though not as sweet as smaller varieties) and the crab was terrific (too bad no king crab...).  Also, while the tempura roll was rather "meh", the salmon sashimi was pretty good.

-- PLATE #3 - Carne Asada Taco, Carnitas Taco, and Chips with Salsa and Guacamole
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=p2b3VrXJwMZiRd0JwLCdJA#ITbZBYTJhTZ8GClrU4nLHg)
I had hopes for the tacos since they were cooked to order, but they were just okay.  The taste was fine, but both the carne asada and carnitas were dry and tough.  Not surprising given how small the meat was cut though.

-- PLATE #4 - Lobster Chowder and Kobe Beef Slider
(http://www.yelp.com/biz_photos/bacchanal-buffet-las-vegas-7?select=p2b3VrXJwMZiRd0JwLCdJA#J0kJKgJhIn2HdzgdVPaWOQ)
The chowder was a little salty, but the consistency was spot on.  Impressive for a buffet, though I wish there was more lobster.  The sliders though were easily the worst thing I had.  Sitting under the warmers grossly overcooked the beef.

To deal with the steady crowd that flows in every night, Bacchanal has a pretty good system set-up.  Instead of the usual snaking lines, they have kiosks where you can enter your name, party size, and cell phone number.  After the machine prints out your ticket, you're free to leave until they text you to let you know you're next.  Otherwise, you can pay an extra $15 per person for the "express" option.

While the "express" option is nice, it's also a gamble.  The kiosk quoted a 45-55 minute wait for the two of us, which seemed high since it was quiet on a Thursday night at 8pm.  Still, we declined since we weren't that hungry anyways.  No more than about 5-10 minutes later though, we got a text telling us we were up.  Risky, to say the least.

Although I can't say for myself, I've heard from friends that Wicked Spoon has fallen off a bit as of late.  Between that and how the vast majority of what we had was pretty solid (save for the sliders, but much better overall than Bellagio), Bacchanal just might be my new favorite buffet in Vegas.  Even if it might be by default.

Fun fact: It costed $17 million to open this restaurant.

Bacchanal Buffet (formerly known as Café Roma, Palatium Buffet, Café Lago, Café Lago Buffet and Lago Buffet) is located inside of Caesars. The buffet consists of multiple show kitchens and over hundreds of daily dishes. Roughly 15 daily chef's specials are added to the menu and they change depending on products, season and the chef's desires. Bacchanal completely reinvented the traditional buffet in 2012 - with modern food presentations and an upscale setting.

Fill your plates to the top with prime rib, chilled crab legs and oysters or truffle deviled eggs, red velvet pancakes and made to order dessert crepes.

Buffet tips:
- Ask your cashier about unlimited mimosas and all-you-care-to-drink upgrades
- Freshly squeezed specialty juices are available before 11 AM (watermelon, cucumber, carrot, etc.)
- Avoid long lines. Pay a little extra for our express pass.
- Crab legs are served after 3 PM on weekdays and all day on weekends.

Voted as the Best Buffet for five years in a row, the crowd has caught on. Make sure to make a reservation and skip the wait.

Extra ordinarily expensive. After waiting in line for extended time we were hit w $160 for two. I was too shocked and not thinking properly or would have declined and left at that time. NOT what was priced like the LV literature.  Seafood stringy  only thing I found tasty was a stuffed crispy sweet potato appetizer. TOTALLY NOT WORYH THE PRICE! NCB

Slightly overpriced, I payed $69/person plus tip. Felt that was a little high for a buffet, especially considering that the Wicked Spoon at the Cosmopolitan hotel where I stayed had a similar buffet for $30-40/person. Nevertheless the number of food plates available was high, it was like 2-3 rooms of food. Food was good quality and they had a decent desert selection. If your at or near the caesars hotel and are looking specifically for a buffet and don't mind the price tag, this is your spot. Be ready for a long wait! The lines are long!

Every one was like this  is the best buffet In vegas.... eh
.. wasted money there. The food was ok.... sucks. Is pretty expensive for the food they had... mind you this was the weekend too.  their desserts was way better then their ok food. Line was long but this was not worth the wait... wish I had just gone some where else

overall a good buffet！ but does it worth 60 dollar one person in dinner？ i doubt that, also we were told they only offer two hours for this price in a not busy afternoon time. (Dinner start at 3:00 pm)

This is the most elaborate and creative buffet, that I have ever seen! I am not a buffet person, but have been hearing nothing but positive things. So we take the chance and did it pay off. When we walked in I could not believe all the choices of food. It seemed to be endless!!!! I loved the little basket of tater-tots, it was perfect for my 1 year old!!! I had some rid eye, mouth watering! The sliders were great, not dry at all which seems to happen a lot! Fresh hot pizza I think it was 4 or 5 different kinds! You can see all the Chef's and cooks preparing the food in front of you!! They also had a cheese and meat section, what a great idea!! The dessert station WOW!!! I had never seen so many dessert, in one place!! My favorite was the mixed berry cobbler and the girl behind the counter, ( who was so friendly and polite) suggested brown butter caramel ice cream! Also fresh hot cookies too! They have thought of everything for this new buffet!!! We will be back!!!

I'm pretty heart broken to give Bacchanal 3 stars because it has been my all-time favorite buffet in Vegas since it first opened back in 2012. My first time was a few months after their opening and I have been going back countless times every time I visit Vegas. I've been to Vegas too many times lol.

My visit to Bacchanal last Monday wasn't as great as it used to be. It had become a mediocre Vegas buffet to me after going for countless years now. What use to taste so amazing here is now just okay and like any other buffet :(. Either something changed with my food palette or the quality of their food is declining. I really do think they are losing their flame, but that's just me.

Not sure when I'll be back again to see if I get a better experience but for now I want to take a break from Bacchanal for as long as I can so I can leave room to try other new Vegas buffets.

I was honestly expecting more more more. It was good, and it's nice that people don't lurk around pressuring you to finish what you grab and make you pay extra if you don't like most other buffets in Vegas.

Amazing sea food (crabs, lobsters, clams, jumbo shrimps). A real Paradise for Seafood Lovers! 
Also a huge variety of American and Asian cuisine! Probably the best Buffet in Vegas I've done so far! Highly recommended.
Our server Esmeralda was great and lovely! She was very prompt and took care of us really well. I'm hoping we have her again very soon!
Great selection of seafood and meat. Lunchtime buffet ~$50/person and dinner time buffet ~$70/person. The only buffet I'll get in Vegas!
We enjoyed the presentation of all the buffet items & loved everything, especially the crab & desserts.

Its pricy and yet delicious at the same time. With that being said always a line. The wait time avg from 1hr to 3 hr.

Tip: You can have your concierge make reservation, pay an additional fee to move up in the queue, or having diamond / 7 star status to move up queue.

Beware, overhyped!! Customer service here is sub-par. When you pay around $60 per person you would expect to at least get refills of your drinks without having to ask every time. The food is honestly not worth it either for the price. I would consider checking out another one if you are reading this. I will not be back nor refer friends or family to here.

Where to even start? The 50 minute wait for a party of four? Expected (even pleasantly surprised - we thought it would be 90 minutes at least). The absolutely incredible feat of producing such a massive scale of good quality food? Well, it's Vegas. The diversity in the featured cuisines? That definitely caught me off guard. I hadn't read much about Bacchanal before my friends insisted that we go. Since I almost never eat at buffets, the only impression I had was of something like Old Country or Golden Corral (*cringes*). But Bacchanal changes the game. Seeing the rows of dishes inspired by American, Italian, Chinese, and Japanese cuisines made me SO unbelievably happy. Also, that doesn't even include the incredible seafood row as well as the entire DESSERT island. Plus, my friends and I got the mimosa pass as well, so endless bubblies were part of the experience too!! 

Must-try dishes (hopefully they keep these in the buffet!):
1. Shrimp ceviche (seafood section) - so fucking good; the sauce is super savory and tangy 
2. Custard buns (Chinese dim sum section) - these were my favorite growing up, and they were so warm and fluffy and the custard was perfectly sweet (but not too sweet!)
3. Sushi hand rolls (Japanese section) - these cute little hand rolls were yummy and adorably packaged...also the rest of the sushi was amazing as well
4. Sticky rice in lotus leaf (Chinese dim sum section) - another favorite of mine; the rice was perfectly savory and sticky and the meat in the middle was delicious
5. Guava something (dessert section) - not sure what it was called but it was sort of like a panna cotta and probably my favorite dessert; just delicately sweet, slightly tangy from the guava
6. Jasmine rice pudding (dessert section) - warm rice pudding with a drizzle of honey at the bottom; I loved it because it was perfectly sweet and satisfying

Strategies to succeed at Bacchanal without exploding your gut:
1. If you're trying to taste as much as possible, only take a bite or two of each item...and then pass it over to your friend for her to try (vice versa)! I made the mistake of inhaling one of the custard buns in the beginning because that 50 min wait time had me STARVING. Rookie mistake. That custard bun actually filled me up quite a bit, and drinking all of those carbonated-af mimosas didn't help.
2. Wear sweatpants or anything with a stretchy elastic waistband. Two of my friends wore jeans and had to unbutton their pants midway through the meal haha. 
3. Take a nice loooooong walk around the Strip afterwards. Or go on a leisurely hike or something. You'll feel so much better.

So yeah, this was a pretty life-changing meal. I don't think I could do this more than once in a year. By the end of the meal, we all hated ourselves a little (but it was WORTH it). I definitely recommend Bacchanal, the feast for the gods.

Where do I even begin? My boyfriend and I came here for Christmas dinner around 3:30pm to be welcomed by rude hostesses that seemed to hate their jobs. We were confused about what we were supposed to do but finally we figured it out no thanks to them. Then we waited almost 3 hours to wait in another line! Finally, we paid and managed to get seated. Perusing around was complicated since we never visited before but I noticed everyone else coming in got a run down which didn't seem fair.
