We also felt rushed given that we only had a 2 hour time limit and the waiters were circling us like hawks to leave towards the end. The food was okay but not worth the $80 per person price tag. But this is why I'm giving it a 1 star. FOOD POISONING! My boyfriend and I both had gastrointestinal issues the next day, most likely from the crab legs. Very disappointed on how a "high quality" buffet doesn't take food safety seriously! I will never return and I will tell my family/friends to stay away!

A little pricey ($59.99), but very good food and amazing variety. I really like how they serve most food...in small portions on individual plates. The amount of food wasted in buffets really bothers me, but I think the small plate service helps alleviates that.

Quite honestly, I don't think this place is worth the hype. Overall, however, I'm starting to realize that buffets will never be a good buy. When you go into a buffet your focus is too loose. I myself went in like a tiger. Every sense of humanity disappeared as I transformed into a voracious muncher. I downed a glass of milk, two glasses of orange juice, two sets of mini buttermilk pancakes, a slice of pepperoni pizza, miso soup, part of a smoothie, many pieces of shrimp, watermelon, cookies, and then nothing. 

If you've read my Seafood Buffet review you'll know where this path leads. It doesn't end very well. Well, if you want to do buffets right, you have to be very patient. Don't go in like a ferocious beast that's been unleashed. You need to get micro portions of everything. Take small bites, breathe, and calmly digest your food. When you go up to get food, also take your time. This rushed feeling of trying to get everything down as fast as possible isn't going to reap solid results. 

I'd say that anyone should try a Las Vegas Buffet at least once. Out of all the ones that exist, this is probably one of the better choices. I'm not so sure I'd go for dinner though - way too expensive.

We came here on a Monday night to celebrate my wife's birthday.   We arrived at 6:30 and waited about 45 minutes.   It was nice considering that I have waited at other buffets for 3 hours.  Dinner on a Monday night was $44.99.  The cashier gave us their "Total Reward" discount, even though I did not have my card.   Dinner for the child was a mere $25.   This is one of the better buffets that I have been to.  Unfortunately, I do not have enough money and stomach space to eat at the top rated buffets more often to be able to say that it is the best buffet.  

The food was very good.  We had way too much crab legs, mussels, shrimp and other shellfish.  It was a good thing that I brought my cholesterol medication so that I could eat more.  I tried my crab legs hot, but, by the time I started eating them, it was lukewarm.  Not a big difference between hot and cold.  The carving station was okay.  Well done meats are not edible.  When I went back for something less cooked, it was perfection.  The lamb was a hit and miss.  I had a piece that was full of salt, and a couple other pieces that were perfectly seasoned.  There were many things that I did not have an opportunity to try.

The Asian woman working in the dessert station deserves her own paragraph.  The daughter and I asked her if they had a candle since it was my wife's birthday.  She told me that she did, but, told me to wait a minute.  She went to the other side of her workstation, and starting doing something with wax paper.  I thought to myself, "Why did I ask?  This girl just ignored me.  I'll never get my candle".   A few minutes later, she gives me a dish.   She wrote in chocolate on the dish "Happy Birthday!" and she also handed me a candle.  But, that wasn't all!  She then took a flan, and put it on the dish that she had prepared for me.  She then took the candle back from me and placed it on the flan.   Like a helpless person, I then asked if she had matches to light my candle.   She had something better!  She grabbed her torch and lit the candle for me.  I could not thank her enough.  She was the best employee there that I encountered.

Service was okay.  They cleared our plates frequently during the beginning of our meal.  But, toward the end of our meal, they stopped coming.  Our waitress did keep my cup filled.  

Overall, this is a very good buffet.   Good food with lots of selections with some outstanding employees.   I'll be back!  Hopefully, someone can treat us next time!

We went with a group of 8.  The wait was about 45 minutes.  Once we got in and seated, we started our worldly food adventure.  They have an Asian area with 20 or so different dishes to choose from.  Everything from dumplings to ramen to szechuan shrimp.  An italian area where they have fresh pizza and some pastas for you to choose from.  Fresh cheeses and salads as well.  Latin area that had barbacoa, and freshly made street tacos in perfectly portioned sizes.  Crab legs, hot and cold.  An American area with several different meats cut on demand, and classic staples like mashed potatoes and mac and chees.  Their dessert station is the size of some of the small Las vegas buffets.  They have made to order crepes and hand scooped gelato.

Everything I had was good. The street tacos were so good because they were made fresh right in front of you.   The Asian dumplings were great and were always refilled.   I never saw an empty serving dish on the buffet line which is always a good thing.   The staff behind the buffet were always helpful.   Our table service was good but at times slow to pull empty plates off the table.  Our drinks were always full, which is a major plus in my book.

All in all, I would recommend this place highly.  If you dig seafood go for dinner and spend the extra money.  If you are like me, and don't care for seafood, the lunch price is not too pricey.
This tastes like a $20 dollar a person buffet, food is edible, not worth to even come to this place. Long wait lines and overpriced
The food is great, servers and staff are very friendly. The environment is slightly below par compared to other casino buffets but still a great place to eat. Patty was a great server, very friendly.

Scrutinized for having went in the Platinum line but did not have my new card updated to the current color because it happened recently. Would have thought they check through your card but apparently not. Lady told me to look at a Diamond member waiting for me because of my negligence. Bad experience makes me not want to come back.

No picture taken of how much of a pig I am at Buffets. LOL! But I will say that it was pretty damn good. I'll compare it to the other high end buffet, Wicked Spoon. I like how the Wicked Spoon was set up more. It was a more intimate buffet place. This place was more friendly with some crazy maze line at the front offering first dibs to people that get their rewards card. The food was spectacular. Seafood, meats were so damn tasty. Try it once and only once on a trip!

My Family's Favorite Buffet and the best buffet in Las Vegas. If you are going to splurge a little on a buffet, might as well go to Bacchanal Buffet, the selection of food and quality,  is great, so worth it.

After so much hype about this buffet, i was expecting more selection. We came here for brunch on a weekday, the food were delicious. However for the price and hype i was expecting more selections.  Servers were on top of providing beverages and keeping our table tidy.
This place is so mediocre for the price point. Yes I went to town on the crab legs but the sushi was borderline gross and the rest of the food while okay was not worth the steep price.
This was an awesome experience. Insanely good food. Nice servers. A little pricey for the upcharge to be at this place, but still good. Esmeralda was the best server :D

My favorite thing about Bacchanal Buffet is that you can really get over it.. Most people who eat at Buffets say they eat the best. But if you go here, it's the best for me. 
    All the food is separated in areas and really good, my favorite I have to say is the meat. The main entrees are basically start at the enterance to the very back, walking down it isn't far but looking at it is.
    The Dessert is in the middle and the workers are very nice, I had a allergy on a food and asked if they had anything that doesn't have it cooked in. (At the Desserts Area) And somebody kindly told me. (Viewed example of many others). And also my 2nd time coming. 
    The Food is good and overall great. If you have never been you should go, it's a very well cared for place.

This buffet had good food, but the wait to get in was an hour standing in a line like at Disney. Can you say miserable? It was more expensive than the mirage without the variety, but the food was excellent. If you can get past the wait and the price you'll enjoy the food.

I wish I could surgically add another stomach (and liver) to my body so that I could feast on every single item at Bacchanal TWICE. BUT! Since that isn't possible, I did the next best thing. I went TWO days in a row with my gf. It was sort of asinine to drop that much money on food, but to us it was worth every penny. 

The quality of everything I had was on point. Even the Asian section of the buffet was good! At other buffets, it's stale and/or dry, tastes different, and is usually only limited to Panda Express type of dishes. However, I suggest staying away from the noodle station though. There wasn't any flavor in my broth. I had to make up for the lack of flavor with limes and sriracha.

Their carving station was the best I've ever had. All the meats were fresh and juicy; unlike other places where they dry out and get crusty. Normally I'm really skeptical about prime rib because it's either too rare or too dry. After my first run, I ended up coming back for more prime rib or brisket. It had just the right amount of seasoning and the best part was that it wasn't so rare to the point where it was still kicking on my plate.

And of course, every Asian's favorite part of a buffet: the crab legs. I'm guilty as charged, but I don't bring back heaping piles of it though. :p The legs aren't soaked in salt. It's lightly salted and you even have the option of boiling them, depending on your preference.

Unfortunately I can't say much for the dessert section because I end up trying to conquer the rest of the buffet. I've had a few bites though and it's just as good as everything else.

SHUT UP AND TAKE MY MONEY :D

Arrived past 10:00 am on Saturday 12/29/18. There was nobody in line and we got seated right away. The spread was not as we expected, the Asian section was rather limited and disappointing. The meats in the carving station were not impressive, lacks flavor and a bit red to our liking, they also have crab legs cracked in the middle for your convenience but it tasted like it had been frozen and thawed a number of times as the crab meat did not taste fresh, but we liked the bacon slab. The desert station had a huge selection and we enjoyed the pandan creme brulee' and the Ube Ice Cream. They have freshly squeezed orange juice and also Hibiscus but none of the meals they prepared stood out for me or my family which was a bit odd because we are not hard to please when it comes to food, we eat everything and we love trying out buffets. However. my entire family shared the same sentiment regarding this buffet, it was not worth the $60/person price tag we paid for just to partake at this holiday meal. We have always wanted to try out their buffet but after we did, it was anticlimactic and sorry to say - we'll not come back anymore. Our experience with Wicked Spoon was so much better and the spread was bigger and better than that of Bacchanal. The service was good but the food was not worth the price. It's a known fact that Vegas Hotels always have a holiday buffet spread - if during this time we were not impressed with what they served what more if it were their regular buffet?

We were looking forward to the VIP experience at Bacchanal and it was fun.  We sat near the buffet serving area and it is a fantastic people watching place to sit. We paced ourselves and really didn't overeat. Watching others do that is a hoot. It is so great to see that lots of people follow the "rules" of buffet dinning by not overloading their plates or carrying two and three plates. For those who have never eaten at a buffet, you CAN come back for a clean plate and start again. I only saw one person (a guy, of course) eating as they were going along...where did they come from? Anyway, everything was good to excellent. The seafood tower was pleasant, the prime rib and brisket were excellent, the best thing for me was the fried green tomatoes (fantastic), charcuterie items and the variety of Japanese pickles and sushi made it a tasters delight. The VIP package is a good deal and people were stopping by our table and ASKING what made us VIPs. That was a hoot!

Great food. What is not good is the line to get special foods cooked is single file and connects to the line to get regular food. So when you are getting regular food, you are clogged up waiting for the people to get their special food cooked.
Wow! My new favorite buffet in Vegas. Will be coming back and bringing family and friends.
Everything was great until I chose an upside down pineapple cake with a giant hair IN it and under it! So gross. Not worth the 54 per person.

Our second time to this buffet and unfortunately we were not impressed. We were expecting things to be just as great as our first time but things have changed. Food was mediocre, the selection was alot smaller, and overall quality of food just wasn't worth the $$ spent. Alot of the stuff we tried was dry or flavorless. Tasted like it was sitting out for a while or just stale food. Chicken and Waffles was missing syrup, which would have been ok of the waffle or chicken wasn't so dry. Chinese food tasted about the same as your local Panda Express. BBQ section was okay..bbq chicken was also a little dry. Taco station was cool, get fresh tacos made however you like BUT that too was nothing spectacular you can pay alot less and get better tasting tacos at Original Lindo off strip. I think this time Bachannal truly felt like your typical buffet where you're paying for the selection of foods rather than the quality.

I don't  know why this place has 4 stars.  I waited for almost 2 hours for a party of four with the anticipations of some really yummy food.  Boy was that a big let down.  I think its just a normal buffet, nothing too special to charge $65.  What a waste of a meal and time.
This is the best buffet in Vegas. Huge selection of food and great ambience!!  Our server Elsmerda was really sweet and gave us good options on drinks.
Over priced crabs was very small no oysters the meat was dry. Don't spend your money  there

Bahk-uh-null or BACK-ANAL?  If it wasn't for my friends saying the former, I'm sure I'd pronounce it as BACK-ANAL Buffet.

We got there around 1pm with a part of 5.  The wait was a little more than an hour, not as long as I thought.  During busy times they'll have a kiosk where you input the number of your party (which includes an estimate time wait).  They ask for your name and number, and they will text you when your table is ready.  Also, you will be given a ticket regarding the information you just inputted.  The texting idea is great because my friends and me were able to roam around for a bit as oppose to waiting in line.

At 2pm we got our text and headed over.  You check in with the hostess and pay immediately.  Everyone can pay together or separately.  At 2pm it was still the Brunch time and our total ended up being around $48.  The cashiers will give you this little rubber things to prevent you from getting burned when picking your food, but it isn't necessary unless you are sensitive to heat.  They had us wait in another line before seating us where someone asked to take a photo of us.  I later found out, they will try to sell you the picture.  Like really, it's not a theme park so no thanks.

Eventually another hostess led us to our table.  Because it was our first time, she had the opportunity to tell us where everything was.  As you enter, everything is on the left in the following order: Seafood, American, Mexican, Italian, and Asian food.  The dessert is in the middle-right of the area.  This place was surprisingly not as big as I thought.  When we sat down we immediately ordered mimosas.  Unforutnately, the mimosas were lacking.  As others have mentioned, it did seem like those concentrated orange juice you find in the freezer aisle of grocery stores.  If you let your mimosa sit, you can the concentrated orange juice and champagne separate.  Geez, for $48 you'd think they would use fresh orange juice.

Finally, it was time to dig in.  I decided to work my way from right to left.  To keep thing short here were some of the highlights for me of each area:

Asian Food - Chinese food was good (but please, I can get that for cheaper and just as good in Chinatown).  Sushi and the other noodle dishes were on point.

Italian Food - You can tell the ingredients like pepperoni were bigger and tasted more high end.  Here you also got your steamed crab legs.  If you give them an empty plate of it, they will fill the whole plate with crab legs so brace yourself.  The steam crab legs are worth getting here as oppose to the frozen crab legs in the Seafood section.

Mexican Food - The tacos were freaking amazing, and they make it for you right there.  On the adjacent part of the mexican section, they have fresh Horchata, Guava Juice, Mango Juice, and Tamarind Juice.  All come in this cute milk jug shape container.  Try all of them!  They were definitely made fresh and sweet.

American Food - Meat, meat, and more meat.  I gave them an empty plate and asked for some Brisket and Prime Rib.  They literally filled my whole plate with it.  I felt like I needed to balance all that meat so I got a small corn on the cob.  Both the Brisket and Prime Rib were flavorful, meaty, and juicy.  It did not taste as good cold, but there was so much I couldn't finish it while it was still hot.

Seafood - Muscles, oysters, clams, crab legs, and shrimps galore! All were great, but they kept running out of hot sauce.  People kept taking them otheir tables and not returning them back. Grrrr.  The hot butter is on the corner in the beginning of the line, so don't forget! 

Dessert - I think the dessert area purposely serve small portions because you will be full by the time you get there.  There is someone making fresh crepes for you.  Grab one, pour some strawberries, drizzle some nutella, and add a bit of powder sugar and you got yourself a tasty treat.  Creme brulee was nice and sweet, while they had an assortment of chocolate covered strawberries.  My favorite one was the white chocolate covered strawberries with strawberry coated rice treats.  Lastly, they had ice cream where you can also make cute little ice cream sandwiches with them.  The person scooping your ice cream will ask if you want 1 or 2 scoops.  My friend and I concluded, no matter what combination you say (for example Mango sherbert and Chocolate), she is still bound to say "oh that's a good/popular combination." Haha.

Overall, I along with my stomach were satisfied.  I would suggest going there around 1pm to get seated around 2pm.  At 3pm, they beging circulating and changing their menu for dinner.  For example, I had the crab eggs benedict during the Brunch hour.  But as soon as 3pm hit, they were no longer serving those items.  If you want to experience everything that would be the best time to go.

Just remember to pronounce this place correctly.
The best buffet in Vegas. The wait in line was moderate and the staff was friendly. I have tried other buffers in town but we always come back to the Bacchanal. Great food and great times.

I literally ate to the point where I got sick! I ate so much food and got sick, so we ended up leaving Vegas early (lol! Sometimes I disgust myself!)

But besides that this place is great. Really does live up to the hype and I honestly think it's totally worth the price. 

Seafood was fresh and delicious. Loved the jumbo shrimp cocktail & crab claws! 
When I went for lunch there was a taco station! Unlimited tacos = my dream come true. Their carne asada tacos are so good. Taste almost as good as street tacos.
Loved their noodle station. I ordered an udon and it was so fresh & tasty. Only downside is I found a hair in my soup :( management was so friendly and offered us free alcoholic beverages to compensate for the hair. 
The protein station was amazing! The prime rib was a bit dry but my friend loved his brisket. It was salty fatty and sooo juicy. 

I would definitely recommend this buffet over all the other buffets in Vegas. I'm a fatass and literally tried all the buffets. This one is pricier but the food is amazing. Totally worth it.

Bacchanal is hands down the most outstanding buffet on the Vegas strip. In fact, it was the highlight of my recent Vegas trip.

At Bacchanal, you will find the following stations: Mexican, Italian, Chinese/Vietnamese, Japanese, American/carvery, seafood, pizza, deli and dessert. I like Bacchanal because the food is fresh, made-to-order right in front of your eyes. Most of the dishes are prepared in small plates, so you won't feel like you ate too much. The trend of using small plates at buffets is thoughtful since it reduces the amount of potentially unfinished food. 

If you are a fan of boiled Alaska king crab legs, mussel, oyster shooters, or ceviche, then you belong here. Imagine yourself walking up to the seafood section, handing over your plate, and walking back to your table with a plate stacked with crab legs - unlimited amount of times. Note that Bacchanal is one of the few Vegas buffets that still carries crab legs (probably due to budget cuts).

The Chinese section at Vegas buffets is typically avoided by Asians, but probably not here. I found the congee and juicy char siu to be very delicious at Bacchanal and worthy of sampling. In fact, the char siu was very popular, so be sure to grab a few pieces. Basic nigiri (tuna and salmon) was available in small quantities. The fish was fresh. Don't expect thick cuts or sauces - just fish and rice. There was also a black chicken soup at the Asian station that I recommend if you are looking for a very light hearty Chinese soup. 

Skip the Mexican station. Why eat oily tacos and quesadillas when you can save room in your stomach for the seafood and the tender prime rib or brisket at the carvery? Go get your money's worth!

Pace yourself and save room for the fancy desserts. Or feel free to eat desserts first. The dessert selection is phenomenal. You will find an island full of cakes, tarts, flan, cupcakes, all prepared with extraordinary culinary sophistication. The desserts at Bacchanal are far superior to the other Vegas-strip buffets, in terms of variety, creativity, and quality.


Notes:
1. The menu on the cover image is outdated. Weekend dinner (Fri-Sat-Sun) is now $50.99 ($55 including tax) and weekday dinner (M-Th) is $44.99. 
2. Be prepared for a long wait. Don't come if you are an impatient person. Sunday dinner at 8pm sounded like a time when most people left Vegas already, but at that hour, I was still met with a 60 minute wait. There was still a line at 9:30pm. 
3. Once you get into the buffet, you may have to wait in line again for food. The longest line was for the boiled crab legs (~20 minute wait). The second longest line was the carvery (~10 minute wait). Fortunately, you won't encounter lines for anything other than the meat and seafood.
4. Pace yourself. Save room for the desserts. Wear loose clothing before coming.
5. Soft drinks are complimentary. Alcoholic beverages are not included in the buffet cost.
6. Purchase the Buffet of Buffets 24 hour pass ($49.99) if you intend to try other buffets after Bacchanal.
7. I ate at the Wynn Buffet the next day, and without a doubt, Bacchanal was 5x more impressive than the Wynn.

My daughter and I ate here as part of a recent vacation in Vegas. We paid full price as I didn't have any deals or coupons and, to be honest, full price is pretty high.  However, it was completely worth it. The variety of food was astounding and the quality was higher than anything I've ever experienced at a buffet. The meat counter alone was probably worth the price!
Have eaten at many nice places over the years and the buffet at Caesars is good over all it's not worth what they charge for it

80 dollars pre tax. Waited for about 4hrs. When I get in, a lot of food are running out. Some food are not kept warm after cooked. I would come back if it's not that crazy price and that long waiting time.
Been here a dozen or so times and it's top tier. The food quality is excellent across the board. It's pricey compared to other buffets but well worth it!

I promise you will never go to a buffet with so many options. From pizza to sushi and amazing desserts. It is very pricey but if you are lucky you can get a groupon, you definitely will be impressed. If you only eat at one buffet in Vegas make it Bacchanal.

So far, THE BEST buffet I've been to in Vegas. Their menu selection is ridonkulous. Service is excellent. This place is worth every penny, and definitely worth it to come early to avoid lines. My dad loved this buffet, and he is probably one of the toughest people on the planet to please with a meal. Just read all the glowing reviews and you'll see the common thread, no need for me to repeat what everybody else is saying. :)

One of kind buffet i recommend everyone try it you would love it  it's clean fast and fresh customer service was absolutely fantastic 
Next visit will be here again with my family 
Thank you

My experience here was amazing. I went for the brunch around 2:30 pm and they transitioned to dinner at 3:00 pm. I ordered the bottomless mimosas which are not included but definitely worth it. This is the best buffet I have ever been to and it is on another level. They have cuisines from all over the world. Their cutting board has an excellent selection from wagyu to prime rib and brisket. If you're into seafood, they have oysters (which were huge but not that tasty), shrimp and crab legs. Their dessert table was also really good. The price is the only reason I am knocking 1 star since it was pretty high.

Forgive me Lord for I have sinned. 

I came into Bacchanal buffet knowing I was going to commit sin, Gluttony. I placed myself in a position where I knew I wouldn't be able to resist and of all places, Sin City. I needed to say a thousand Hail Marys for the amount of food I consumed. I must though confess; sinning never tasted so good.
 
Bacchanal Buffet is located at Caesers Palace. This fancy and upscale buffet made a name for itself by being voted as " Best buffet in Vegas " Who could resist the temptation after hearing they've been named the best? Not me!

Being Diamond status for Total rewards ( Yelp elite status is much cooler ) allowed me to bypass the long line. I've heard of atrocious two hour wait times. Luckily, with the new self check in ticketing system, you input your cell no. and get a text response when the table is ready.

Talk about a feast! The food was never ending. Just a few highlights of what to expect at Bacchanal buffet: 

Menu:
* Seafood *
Crab. shrimp. oysters. mussels. smoked salmon. ceviche 

* Carving station *
Prime rib. lamb chops sausage. pork tenderloin. beef brisket

* Sushi *
Spicy tuna. shrimp rolls. California roll. eel roll. sashimi

* Chinese *
Chop suey. chow mein. fried rice. Mongolian beef. shrimp with mixed vegetables. kung pao. BBQ pork

* Mexican *
Street tacos. enchiladas. elotes. Mexican juices

Lobster clam chowder. ramen. pho. Ox tail

Also included in the buffet line were sandwiches, soups, salads, cured meats and cheese, desserts and much much more.

Service:
Great and friendly service with a smile. Whether I needed a refill or more napkins, it was already provided before I could even ask. The great service was consistent. 

Tip: 
Breakfast Mon-Fri $25.99
Brunch Sat-Sun $40.99
Lunch Mon-Fri $32.99
Dinner $45.99 weekdays & 
$50.99 weekends

Overall experience:
Bacchanal buffet was everything I expected it to be, exceptionally delicious with a phenomenal selection of food. I would definitely come again!  Happy eats!

Went for the hype and it almost lived to it, except for some of the items in the Asian section. The dimsum is dry, and the sushi is okay. Ice cream and smoothies selection isn't that great. Except that everything else was wonderful. Went on Monday morning around 10am and I didn't had to stand in the line.

If you're in Vegas you are going to try a buffet. We decided to visit what is genuinely one of the top 2 buffets in Vegas. The Bacchanal Buffet has had a lot of exposure on television and most of the marketing is positive. 

We visited around 1pm and the line as expected on a weekend was a little long. It took us 30 minutes to get seated. 

Once inside the deco is clean, light, modern and fresh. Clearly they put emphasis on maintaining high cleaning standards in this restaurant especially considering the amount of people that are served daily. The clean plate locations are placed in corner slots at the end of each serving area. Look close it's a little hard to find. 

The selection of food is enormous. The start of the line catered to Asian cuisine. Dim Sum (Har Gow/ Siu Mai) pork buns, fried rice and various Chinese options (Beef And vegetable). Then you have your carvery and comfort foods with mashed potatoes, Mac and cheese etc..  followed by a Mexican bar with custome made street tacos. Next is the BBQ options with sausages and chicken options. The main focus is the seafood area with shrimp in all forms, crab, Alaskan Crab Legs and various sides. 

The dessert bar was amazing every type of option you can imagine including a gelato bar. 

Our server was terrific and very attentive. The reason for the "3" rating is that while the food looked great, and had good flavor...the majority of items we had were like warm at best. Some dishes (especially the Asian food) were downright cold. Apparently the warming plates were not functional. This was really disappointing. 

Overall a good selection, clean eating area, good service, average food due to it not being warmed properly.

Outstanding service and offerings. Best buffet hands down for the price. Arrive early to avoid the lines however if you plan on going during the weekend for dinner expect over 1 1/2 hours without a reservation. Worth the wait!

WAGU BEEF on their buffet daily along with a great selection of sea food line up. Oysters, clams, crab legs and seafood paella. 
Eggs done numerous ways as well as prime rib, pork belly, bacon and lots of sausages.
WAGU BEEF!! 
To many food selections to mention so experience your self , take your time and GO HUNGRY!!
This place is pricey, but worth the food and experience, great place to make some memories with family or friends, laid back, but definitely 5 star buffet

Forget the shows. Forget the hoes. Vegas is known for legendary buffets. Caesar's palace arguably has the best buffet in town. Prime rib at 8am? No problem. Absolutely delicious, high-quality food at a reasonable price. The baked mac n cheese. The seafood. Oh, God, the seafood. I never eat mussels. But here I was at 8am, eating mussels, mac n cheese, and a salad. And it all went exceptionally well together. The service was also the best I had ever experienced at a large buffet.

Whoa! Game changer!!! When people talk about buffets in Vegas, this is what they're aiming for! There are tons of buffets al over the place, but Bacchanal will change your life! I'm not a buffet connoisseur, but after eating here, I don't really need to go anywhere else! They literally have everything! Asian, American, Mexican, Italian, non-stop crab legs and seafood as far as your eyes can see, and a dessert section that will make you pop! Everything was delicious, and the one thing I didn't like I couldn't even remember! The good always outweighs the bad. They have hot crab legs as you walk into the Italian/Asian section, and cold crab legs in the front if that's your thing (bleh). 
We went pretty early 5:30-6p and there was a line, but it moved fairly quickly. I think the wait really depends on how many people are in your party. After paying you are lined up according to the amount of people in your party. You're going to pay a good amount for dinner but I definitely think it's worth every penny! It's not outrageous by any means, you, yourself just have to make sure you remember to make it worth your while! We sure did!!

Delicious. Not overwhelming and a wonderful selection of quality seafood, meats and food items.  Come hungry. Get your dollars worth because this place is not cheap.  Nothing about it is cheap. HOWEVER, its worth what you pay for (about $75.00 a person).  I am not normally a buffet lover but this is pretty luxe.  The food is good but not extraordinary.  Nothing that I say is memorable, except of course the crab legs and shrimp.  Nonetheless, it's good and food somewhat the same as everywhere else, EXCEPT better quality.

 The crab legs are only served for dinner if you go for brunch it's an extra cost. The oyster selection is minimal and the taste is muh! 

If your a carnivore like me this is your buffet!!

She started to give us attitude  from the beginning.... long story short, we were a party of 8, but we decided to divide our group into two, and the hostess, purposely, sat one to the north pole and the other to the south pole even though  there were plenty  of tables right beside of each end. There are literally hundreds of buffets in Vegas. However, Bacchanal is by far the most talked-about and critically-acclaimed of the lot. All the hype surrounding this place had me salivating for weeks before my trip, and I couldn't wait to get in. Luckily, our group of 12 or so didn't have to wait too much longer after arriving; we showed up on a Sunday at about 2:00, and were seated within a half hour. Bacchanal's got a huge range of food -- obviously, I can't detail every single dish here, but I can say that I was very pleased with the variety. As far as quality, it was pretty solid for the most part, if not completely amazing. I've categorized some of the dishes below:

Freakin' Delicious:
- Hamachi Kama (broiled yellowtail collar): Probably the only thing I can say was fantastic -- I literally ate four of these.

Great, Would Go Back For Seconds:
- Sweet Potato Tater Tots: these were awesome, perfectly crispy and not too sweet nor salty
- Mac and Cheese: dangerously cheesy and topped with panko
- Mushroom risotto: super fine grains, very creamy
- Hazelnut gelato: best of the desserts
- Penne pasta: forgot the exact sauce, but really liked it
- Sausage: ate a couple pieces in line, lol

Decent, was Worth a Try:
- Tacos: 3 meats offered - carne asada (beef), al pastor (pork), pollo (chicken)
- Wedge Caesar salad: tasty, topped with anchovy
- Shrimp/Crab: pretty fresh
- Slab Bacon: a little fatty, but that's a given
- Mini Waffle with Maple Syrup: nice and crispy

Disappointing, was Expecting More
- Brisket: looked amazing, but was pretty bland
- Prime Rib: also pretty bland, a little dry
- Pan-Seared Salmon: weird green sauce and aftertaste

Complete Waste of Calories:
- American Wagyu Beef: dry, super bland, overcooked... was really excited for this one
- Lamb T-Bone: extremely dry, needed salt
- Poke: really weird aftertaste, didn't seem very fresh
- Cheesecake Bite: dry and not creamy

OVERALL: Not too shabby, especially for a buffet. Great variety, but price perhaps a little steep for the quality of some of the food.

There are some reasons that this place is worth my 2 stars. 

The BEST thing they have here is their desserts. They are amazing and i respect the chief cook for this dessert bar. 

But here is what made it the worst: 

1. Oysters aren't dead but almost there. I eat oyster everywhere i go but never thought such a place can have those bad oysters. Their smell is really strong. 

2. Sushi bar is the second worst. In many buffet restaurants, their sushi bar usually have around 20 different rolls and here they have 4. Not even that good rolls. 

3. Frozen crawfish, frozen shrimps. Frozen crawfish can be understandable because it is off the season but did not expect that for the shrimps. 

4. Did not have any kingcrab or lobster at all. When i asked, the waiter said they dont have it in menu anymore and it is used to be extra $110 for kingcrab and $100 more for lobster which is ridiculous because i never have to pay extra for food at buffet restaurant. 

5. Everytime I came to the seafood bar then there was barely anything left, maybe i came too late lol but i came around 4 times tho. Or maybe their food is so good or maybe somebody didn't refill them at all. 

6.To be honest, the same chinese buffet can cost $20 or $30 to have steamed lobster and snowcrab while i bought VIP ticket here for $179 but did not even see the line when i came. 

I came here for brunch once and did not like it but wanted to try one more time at dinner to see if they are better but just the same foods.

Overall, this place is overrated and overpriced. I did not recommend this restaurant to anyone and not coming back either.

I visited the Bacchanal Buffet around 7pm on a Wednesday with a party of 4. We probably had to wait in line for a half hour, but you are able to bring drinks from other hotel bars into the line so that made it more pleasant. After you pay, they split you into lines based on the size of your party, and we were lucky that night that they're weren't many other parties of 3 to 4 people. There were lots of parties of 2 so keep the wait in mind. 

This was the most extravagant buffet I've been to. There were designated sections for every corner of the world with a wide variety of offerings under each section. There are lots of opportunities for customization - the highlight for the table was custom ramen/pho and make your own tacos. The dessert section was extremely large - make sure to not eat too much food before in order to plan for dessert!

The only negative I can really mention is that sometimes the servers can be slow in picking up finished plates. Our table got a bit crowded at times because of this. Otherwise really positive experience and would recommend the Bacchanal Buffet while in Vegas!

10/10 would recommend. There's plentiful options for foods varying from bone marrow to frog legs. Our server was the nicest lady who gave us extra things like crab shears when we didn't ask. Love her! Line was long but the wait was only 30 min!

Went for Saturday Brunch, got there right before 11am and the line was quick. Buffet was impressive with mexican, italian, chinese, sushi, seafood, etc. I could have used an omelette station and a couple more breakfast items though. Highlights for me were the amazing service from our waiter, brisket, sushi, fried chicken/waffle, seafood and desserts. Low lights would be burned meat on the made to order tacos, cheap champagne for drinking package and lack of breakfast options. 

Overall an amazing brunch buffet, go check it out yourself!
Large variety of food! I fell in love with the dessert!! Made to order Crepes! Sooo good!
Best buffet ever. Just prepare yourself to go to bed afterwards as you won't be able to do anything else with a full tummy. Best dining experience ever!!!

How have I never been to this buffet before?! Over the last 30 years, I have been to just about every buffet in Vegas. I tried this one out for the first time and I was blown away! Everything my wife and I ate was cooked perfectly. Unlike other buffets nothing was dried out or cold instead of hot. The quality of the food is every bit as good as a full service restaurant! My compliments to the chef- easily the best buffet in Las Vegas!

What a great buffet, SO much food for the price. The cracked crab was amazing. I would say the Chinese food and the Italian food was not the best, but the Mexican food, Sea Food, beef, and desserts were all above the rest. 

We had two servers who were over the top kind, truly had servants hearts. Leissia and Maryam were SO nice and kind, smiles all around and really paid attention to our needs in such a gracious manner. It was so refreshing to be around people who clearly like their job. Thank you for making it a great experience!

Just came back from this buffet spending $350 for 5 people. Quality was decent but not worth $70 per head. Deco 4 stars. Variety 4.5 starts. Service 4.5 starts. Quality 3.5 starts. Tastes 4.
I know things are expensive here in Vegas strip but to me this buffet worth $40 at the most.

omg.. this buffet was amazing.. everything was soo good .. i tried everything i think.. and they have a variety of food that you don't know where to start... gigantic shrimp... the best ceviche.. dessert station omg.. i was in heaven.. drinks were so good.. champagne out of this world....i love it.. definitely i'm going back next time  that im in town...you've to try it. 
. won't regret it

As far as fancy buffets go, this is a grand place.  Price was pretty expensive, and my friend treated me for my BD.  The char siu was a standout, and the meats were dry & overcooked.  Rarely do these fancy buffet places have a bad piece of prime rib.  This buffet, I couldn't finish the slice.  Also the bone marrow, was not bone marron.  it was a rib.  for this fancy place, they should know what it is.  Sorry!

the desserts were terrific.  although i'm mostly on the keto diet, I did break for this meal.  I had the macarons, cookies and the thai ice tea w/ice cream.  very excellent!  

overall the best things here:  shrimp; dessert.

Honestly the worst buffet I've ever been to. I can't express how disappointing this buffet was. Literally every meat I tried was severely overcooked. The ribs were so burnt I couldn't even take the meat off the bone without a ton of force. Some of the items I've seen on YouTube reviews weren't out when I went. Vegetable options were sparse. Even the desserts were subpar. The gelato tasted like discount brand soft serve. The only OK items were the crepes (1 of 2 were ok) and the steamed crab legs (although no tools to crack them open made it very time consuming). 

I would NEVER consider eating here again and would recommend others to look elsewhere for a buffet. I would give this zero stars if I could.

Although I loved the hotel Ashe stay, I wasn't too happy about the buffet that I barely ate one plate for $72. 
No lobster or crab as expected. Then my friend had plastic wrap in her soup. Spending over $72 each times 4 of us, I'd expect a little someone better than a free beer.

Bacchanal used to be our go-to buffet for special occasions. We pretty much stopped after they started charging for parking (out of principle), but got invited and went. I couldn't believe what a nose dive the food quality has taken over the past year or so. There was not a single dish I had where I said "I need to get me some more of that".
Generally, the food was severely lacking in flavor. Pad Thai, Chow Fun, Ravioli were all extremely bland. The cocktail shrimp were overcooked and just barely edible, the river prawns were completely hammered and inedible. The crab legs were incredibly salty, as if all the salt they had went into the crab legs, so there was no salt left for any of the other dishes.
Both the mushroom flatbread and the pear / fig jam flatbread had some incredibly astringent on it that completely took over and completely ruined the dish. The Mac&Cheese tasted like wallpaper paste, the New England Clam Chowder tasted as if you mixed a cup of heavy cream with half a cup or funny mashed potatoes, and oddly sweet. No seasoning, no clams. Pathetic.
Fast forward to the desserts. The bread pudding was completely dried out, the blueberry cobbler was 80% plain cake, and every other dessert had this annoying buttercream with no flavor all over it, worst of all the "Tiramisu", with but a crumb of ladyfingers on the bottom, and the rest of the cup filled up with cream. 
$55 for a midweek dinner ? I don't think so. Bellagio and Wynn buffets have better food at lower prices.

Went for brunch on Monday around 9:30AM. There was no wait and there were not many people there at that time. The cost after tax was about $42. This does not include gratuity. My waitress was very friendly, and there seemed to be a lot of buss people helping to clear empty plates. The amount of food is insane. I had shrimp, prime rib, green beans, bacon, and eggs Benedict. And that was just my first plate. Everything was hot, well seasoned, and delicious. There is a two hour time limit, but I never felt rushed at all. My favorite dishes were the shrimp and grits and the eggs Benedict. There was also a station where inlets were being made.
The decor was very nice and warm and extremely clean. I would recommend this buffet to anyone who likes a big breakfast!
The wait was worth it! Great food and yummy desserts  I will definitely come back and bring my other children
Food is average.  Lots of selection.  Place is just ok.  Waitress was attentive.  But a lot of selection.  Desert is good.  I like their ube sorbet.

Great buffet! So much choice at rhe brunch buffet, everything i could thing of was part of the buffet. I eat until I was sick! The only thing are the dessert, they taste like they are not self made. But besides that it is great!!!

Finally!! Got to try this place. Definitely the best buffet I've ever been to. I'd say you get your money's worth in the quality of food served. Some of my favorites were fried egg and skirt steak
Raw oysters 
Lobster chowder 
Tropical juice
Mango chili gelato
Caprese salad
I couldn't keep up with the amount of food that they were bringing out.
Oh and go during the end of breakfast hour you pay the cheapest and you still get the lunch items.

Excellent!!! Been here like 4 times and every time we come here, their food and the ambiance is perfect, disregard the long wait specially when you are coming in for dinner, because you will receive the best customers service and fresh, awesome food in all of their selections. Will definitely come back and will eat more lol!

This is one of the best ultimate brunch buffets' I have ever had the pleasure of dining. The buffet is extremely clean and tidy as it should be for the cost to eat here. It's in no way shape or form a trough-like buffet, not at all. It was a delightful experience; the food selections were prepared well and the items on the buffet were endless. The only thing missing were fluffy pancakes and an omelet station. 

They had an incredible seafood station, all kinds of rich savory stews, poached eggs benedict options, scrambled eggs, chicken and waffles, shrimp and grits, country ham, all types of bacon and smoke sausage links, brisket, and almost every other meat for breakfast, lunch and dinner. The fruit and dessert bar was beautiful and enormous. I had menudo for the first time, and it was so satisfying. The food was sumptuous; the service was adequate. It was money well spent.

By far the best buffet on the strip! I have waited in this line more time than I would like to admit to eat here. Food quality is great and the ability to eat whatever you want is amazing! Hit it right at the end of breakfast and stay for lunch too :)

Again food section was very good. It's a shame it's pushed to the back. Very hit and miss with everything else. Delmar making the crapes was very respectful and helpful. He help us by telling us the information about the buffet and the easier way of doing things. If only more employees were like Delmar!
Good variety, but I feel the quality was lacking. The deserts were probably the best part of the buffet.

I'm not a buffet person but my fiance was jonesing for a big food display. The wait was still long at 845pm and we joined 4 others so we could get in faster...shout-out to them for including 2 strangers for the greater good! The best thing I had was the beef brisket, and they ran out!!!! The mussels were perfect too. Any of the vegetable dishes I recommend skipping. I love roasted beets and root veggies, not these though. Brussel sprouts and quinoa, awful.  All the standard things ( pizza, sushi, tacos) were below average. Most of the meat was overcooked. The staff was really nice despite a huge amount of cleanup and traffic they endure. I'm a dessert lover. I loved only ONE of all the many pretty choices on the separate dessert buffet, the lemon basil gelato. The others at my table didn't eat their desserts either. Glad I went. Not going back.

Overall a good Buffet choice for the price range. The service is poor which is typical for buffets. Slow and minimum service and basic table cleaning. Also there is very little chance to enhance or substitute what they have. 

They have a good variety of foods. The crab legs are definitely the main reason why people come but the line can be long. The beef options were mid tier and in many cases dry from sitting under the lamp. 

The dessert selection is over the top and another defining piece of the buffet. I would come again if I had a large group with me that had differing tastes. Otherwise, I'd steak to a restaurant that's good at something rather than being ok at many foods.

Amazing. 

My wife thinks that Bacchanal is slightly less impressive than the buffet at Belaggio but I disagree. 

The seafood was great. I'm a shrimp fan and I was not disappointed. I liked the world cuisine options. 

The wait times can be longer but it's worth it.

The buffet place to go when you are in SIN BITY!! I would go here pretty often during my pre-21 days because I wasn't old enough to do 21-year-old Vegas things yet. So, Bacchanal Buffet holds a good place in my heart! The wait for large parties is usually pretty long, and for a party of about 4 people or less that'll take about an hour or so.

Getting on to the food - there are just endless options for anyone to choose from. From my experience, everything is pretty fresh and nothing seems like its been left out sitting in the warmer. You got your selection of Asian, American, Seafood, and many many more. I like to start off with the hot food, so I head to the meat cut section and pick the different cuts of meat that I want to devour. You can't forget about the HOT crab legs. It is key that you get the hot crab legs because I think those taste a lot better than the cold, but its personal preference haha. You can't forget about dessert, which is conveniently located towards the middle of the buffet selection. So many little dessert options to choose from and they can even build custom crepes for you.

Everyone knows that this place is one of the top buffets in Vegas. So, if you're not hung over from going out, make sure you come eat at this spot.

The only reason I am giving this buffet 4 stars is because I am vegetarian and there aren't that many vegetarian options here. Other than that, this place is amazing! It is so big and they have so many varieties. The most vegetarian options were at the Italian station, and there were barely any vegetarian options at the Chinese/thai stations. I ended up going on Monday, and am glad I did because paying the full weekend price would not have been worth it for the number of options I had.
Nice layout, great food and selection.  Eat a heavy breakfast, skip lunch so that you have early dinner around 4pm to avoid long lines later.

The buffet was very good! You have too many options to chose from, I really enjoy the buffet with my family! I will recommend it to anyone.... the only thing is that is very crowded at dinner time that is why I put 4 stars

Wow! So my uncle had recommended I go here when I traveled to Vegas this past September and I'm so glad I did! This buffet tops any other buffet I've been to period. So many choices and all reflecting culinary excellence and tasty. It is pricey but for a reason so I say try it out and go.
Definitely the best buffet in Las Vegas! Amazing diversity of food options and very good quality. It's usually really crowded on holidays.
Great variety of food! Luxury restaurant excellent for all times! Italian, desserts, chinese, sea food and drinks

It seems like Bacchanal is always battling for first place buffet in Vegas. I've been to several of the contenders, and there is honestly no comparison. The quality and quantity of Bacchanal goes unmatched by every other Vegas buffet. 

I don't even know where to start. The seafood. Oh god the seafood. So. Much. Seafood. Hot, cold, crab, shrimp, sushi. Yes, even the sushi. Quite literally the best sushi I've ever had. No, not the best buffet sushi, the absolute BEST sushi. 

I was already in a food coma from my salad and seafood, but I managed to force down some prime rib, which was also excellent. 

When I was finally ready to thrown in my towel, someone told me the best part was the dessert buffet section. Holy shit. I didn't even see that area. I don't have much of a sweet tooth, but I gave it a shot to give a full review (oh the things I do for Yelp). I didn't even know I liked macaroons. Get the macaroons. Repeat: get macaroons. 

So in summary, yes it's $50. Yes you will wait a while (maybe more than an hour) to get in. It is worth it. Wait in line. Pay your money. Indulge in the best buffet of your life.

I was very excited to come here as I heard it's one of the best buffets in Vegas. We stopped in on a Tuesday around 7 and we had to wait in line for about 30 min. At $54/person, this buffet is on the steep side, but hey, it's Vegas! I have to say the decor is overall a little dated. Once we were seated, we decided to survey the buffet to see all that was offered. The pros: they offer a lot of high end food items, including bone morrow, crab, lobster, and prime rib. It was nice to be able to try foods I've never had before in a small quantity. Another pro is that the service was great. It seemed like all of the wait staff worked together. Some cons: the food was warm.. at best. Also, while they had a lot of different items, this buffet wasn't any larger than any other buffet I've been too. Overall, I'm glad I had the chance to experience one of the "best buffets in Vegas" but I think I'm going to try somewhere else next time.

The Bacchanal Buffet has wonderful food and incredible service. Not only did they assist my family and I with a complication and gave us a deal, they also assisted us in finding out check out times. Mr. Brian Murzyn was so nice to us in helping us through anything we had trouble with and I really appreciate it!On top of all of this, the food is incredible, one of the best things I have tasted. This buffet is truly one of the best and is one hundred percent recommended by my family and I.

We chose this place buffet based on them advertising they had great vegan options as well. Well that w.d a bad joke on us.   Their vegan options were minimal, and only had two vegan dessert options. A mango pudding and vegan cookies.  It's ridiculous that we get charged the same as those that stuff themselves with expensive meats, and various fish, sushi and other non vegan  gourmet dishes.   Which is really not fair considering we don't eat expensive  or sushi.  If you say you cater to vegans  then you should really make an effort to provide more of a selection. A total waste of money.

Lines were long at 9pm on a Thursday night, but it moved quickly. 

SERVICE: Friendly all around. Somehow with the crowd that this place handles, all the employees have a smile on their face.

FOOD:  The options of food that you get here are outstanding, there's literally something for everyone. I wish I had enough room in my stomach to try everything! The meat/butcher station had great quality meats. The prime rib was delicious. I wish there were better sushi options the day I went, but the sushi I had was pretty good. The dessert table looks so beautiful, but honestly I was disappointed with half the desserts I tried (matcha cake, chocolate "lava" cake, and cheesecake). The matcha cake was flavorless. The chocolate "lava" cake cannot be called a lava cake as there is no hot fudge oozing out of it. The cheesecake was too dense for my preference. So I had to knock down a star for that.
Amazing selection of exceptionally good dishes. The best buffet in Vegas. I was reluctant to go because quality by far outweighs quantity, but in this case you get both-- in spades!

I've been to the many casinos buffets while in Vegas.  This one was particularly good. Not only because it's the upgraded one due to the immense amount of sea food offered but because the food was delicious.  If you get the 24hr pass note that you have to pay the additional 35.00 dollars at every revisit.  Even after you've already paid the pass sum to get in. Which essentially means for 4 people you pay around 400.00 for 24hrs. Then when you come back its about 120.00 for lunch and 120.00 for dinner. Get place to spend you comps if you have them.

1 hour wait, ok. 65 dollar per person, fine. Mediocre food, Get out of here. Not worth my time money or empty belly sorry. Nothing was great most things where just ok or leaning torwards good. But will not go again.

I have been to this buffet before, and the food is very good, but getting into it takes forever and a day. I purchased the VIP pass this time around to try to get in a bit faster, and it took longer than if I had just gotten the normal pass. The lines were not clearly labeled, so I had to switch lines twice, and once I was in the VIP line, it did not move for 30+ minutes. I recommend the buffet because it has great food, but you should expect to wait 1-2 hours even if you purchase a pass that is supposed to expedite the line.

Delicious options and my favorite Buffett I've been to on the strip so far. My only reason for not giving 5 stars is the temperature on some of the food. I went for lunch at noon on a Monday and it was $49 before tip!! It's pricey but if you're at an elite level with Caesars you do earn points on the purchase. Will definitely be back.

On our last day in Vegas, we decided to have our final lunch here and oh boy we made the BEST DECISION ever.

The food and its quality is simply outstanding! From the hot plated breakfast to the mouth watering gelato desserts. The pork buns and dimsums were a family favorite. The roast beef etc were hot! Everything was phenomenal. 

Staff were very attentive too. Nice and courteous. 

These are the reasons this is the BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS. 

When we come back in Vegas, expect us to be back!!!

Buffet's are not really my thing, but this one almost changes my overall opinion. First, expect a very high price. Second, expect to be sincerely overwhelmed - though I understand this isn't even one of the biggest buffet's in town. 

We were there for brunch on a Sunday, right when they were switching over to lunch. There is a crazy number of stations, make sure you ask for the layout so you don't miss anything. They have seafood, meat, salads, various options like Italian and Mexican, sides, desserts, a lot of everything. I made two rounds focusing on vegetarian options, clearly if one is a vegetarian this might not be the best place for the money but at least the options are plentiful.

The wait staff were very nice, it's super clean, and the tables aren't too on top of each other (they kind of are, but I've seen worse). But for the price, I have to say no to a second time.

My hopes were high for this popular buffet, but we were quickly disappointed. We came for brunch on a Saturday so it was very busy. Upon arriving you have to put your name in the kiosk where it prints you a ticket with your wait time. You get the ticket and it says it will text you when to come back. Ten minutes later we got a text and got in line. We waited 50 minutes in line. 

We purchased the unlimited beer and wine package. Once seated we asked for drinks and explored the food. Our server never came with the beer. He kept saying he would be back and by then we were full and left wondering where the unlimited was. We asked to cancel and he said it would take two weeks for a refund.

I wish they had pasta options for brunch but didn't find any. The breakfast was terrible. The eggs were watery, donuts hard as a rock, along with other breads being hard. A lot of food just wasn't tasting good. I did enjoy the pizza and gnnoci and that was about it. Desserts were way too sweet for my liking. 

For me the hype was too out there. Wait times, price, and food do not live up.

This used to be the best buffet for me and I have recommended this buffet to everyone I know and not know! 

I came here twice in one month thinking maybe that time I came in which was in mid January was an off day. But why would the "best buffet" have an off day, ok let's go again and this time with a group so in case it was me going crazy. 

Well that wasn't the case, this buffet has gone down, first of all the corralling of people and groups of to the sides and I get it they feed the masses and people come in large groups, fine. The other that really is annoying is that no one tells you that if your a diamond member and above you have to ask for king crab legs from your server or you don't get it at all. 

Your server doesn't even tell you, I found this out through yelp and we've been diamond members for 5 years! Anyway the crab legs weren't good anyway, small and bland. The Asian food section was a mess! The signs were not exactly what they say and the dim sum area looked so stale and dry. The sushi and soup selection was also not appealing so we all passed that. 

The Italian well it left a lot to be desired, the meat selection mehhh. I was hoping for more spectacular meat selections, not run of the mill meat I can get at any buffet. Wynn buffet has great meat selections as well as bone marrow. This just looks like a ton of meat just thrown around. 

Now for the seafood selections, everything from the shrimp cocktail to the Jonah crab claws was so bland? I mean the oysters tasted like nothing? Just slimy nothing it was the weirdest thing! No sweet ocean taste, just rubbery shrimp, tasteless crab claws and oysters. The stews and mussels over cooked because they just sat there. 

The best part of this buffet was the Mexican and dessert area. I'm so super sad because this was the best buffet, for the price and quality it's so disappointing.

I'm just going to give this place five dang stars!.  Couldn't ask for a better bday dinner. It gets a little crowded but the food is worth bumping into a few people.  The choices are abundant for whatever you want.  Get the line pass, well worth it. Second year for bday dinner and.ill be making this an annual tradition.
One of the best buffet in Las Vegas with lots of options including those who are vegan/vegetarian. Love their gelato!!

I can only give one star because I didn't end up eating here.  After waiting in a long long to pay, I went to another long line to be seated.  I was meeting friends for a show and simply ran out of time waiting (I still had to go back to my hotel to change and met up). 
What I found irritating was they have 3 waiting lines based on different elite statuses.  We all paid the same price for the buffet and there should be one line!  They refunded my money and I won't be back.  Too bad I really enjoyed this buffet last time I was in town.
First time coming here and oh man walked out with a food coma. They had a lot everything, sushi, seafood, Mexican, American, Chinese, and a lot more. Fresh deserts getting made right in front of you.

Although it is a little pricey the food and variety is insane. This is definitely the best buffet you will get in vegas. The crab legs and bone marrow are out of this world! The desserts are very taste and rich. The environment is also very clean and lively!

We visited on one of the busiest days of the year - Thanksgiving! We anticipated a wait and after 1.5 hours, we were seated and it's worth mentioning that the staff were very organized and kind while handling the mayhem that ensued on this busy day. 

Once seated, we began to explore the buffet stations and we're pleasantly surprised with such diversity of food offerings. They had selections of Japanese, Italian, American and Spanish dishes. And the presentation and attention to detaol with every offering was excellent! They had all of the holiday fixings and an overwhelmingly amazing dessert table. The staff were incredibly friendly attentive and helpful. We look forward to returning next year!
This place has made me stop loving buffets.  Quality sucked.  Oysters were large but putrid.  Asian section was ok.  Dessert section was the best of all the sections.

Overrated. For a buffet that has raving reviews and being this expensive, it was really REALLY disappointing. Bone marrow and steamed crab legs were burnt. Almost everything else tasted like it sat out for too long. Dessert was okay but all buffets have the same quality these days. Why would I wait for something so sub par?

This is probably one of the most diverse and cleanest buffets on Earth.  Everything was excellent.  Asian, seafood, carving stations, etc...this place had it all, and all was too notch.  The dessert buffet is even amazing!

The sea snail was gross! The desserts were an after thought. The service was just ok. Beat part was salmon dish, poke and the mushroom truffle soup. The other soups like the lobster bisque was overly salty. For almost $60 a head. I would rather eat at wicked spoon the bread pudding alone at wicked spoon taste a lot better than the bread pudding at the Bacchanal. I will maybe return in a year to see if they improved. So disappointed was hoping for an amazing foodie experience.

Excellent service great vast selection but with mimosas almost 100 dollars breakfast.
Cheese ohhh a few to choose from .
Stone crap....ok. Just ok...lol
I had a few lol
t

We came here for brunch on a Sunday while in Vegas. I mistakingly thought this was in the Belagio but it's in Caesars. We arrived when they first opened. They get busy very fast. There is a huge selection. The staff is friendly. Our drink server was very accommodating. I loved the breakfast options although it's a Vegas buffet so the options extended beyond breakfast food. The omelet station was my favorite, and my boyfriend went back for seconds. The mimosas were delicious.  This is a very pricey buffet, but everything pretty much is getting to that point in Vegas on the strip.

Everytime I come to Las Vegas I have to go to this great buffet! The better way come @3:00pm that you don't need to wait so long.The stone carb and steamed king crab legs are so good.  The service people are also very nice. Great time for me and my girlfriend !

My group of about 15 came in around 8 PM and was quoted an hour and a half wait. We thought  that it wasn't not too bad, so we opted to wait in line. Once we get close enough to pay, this bigger gentleman comes and tells us that we will get in by 10, and that we'd only have 55 minutes to eat. Seriously? It is currently 9 PM, and they decide to tell us that now? That's absolutely ridiculous. The lady at the very beginning should've told us that we would only have 55 minutes to eat, not tell us after we wait a complete hour. The gentleman was giving us extreme attitude too. This is terrible management and something needs to be changed about this restaurant. What a joke.

Booofay is a hit or miss, for me!  So far, i only love one spot (buffet at the Aria). But Bacchanal is not bad either, Saturday was about $48 pp. There's a whole lot of choices and presentations are top notched. Great variety of cuisines. The lines (at 12pm) wasn't deadly but it was 45min to get seated so, grab a drink at the bar situated right outside the buffet. 4star is for our awesome male server, endless champagne pour and cleaned our plates everytime we got up. The place is huge so grab two or three plates at a time =) Crab legs were a bit too salty, only complained (still i had four plates by myself)

Hands down, the best buffet on the strip! We have been here 4 times and it never disappoints. The staff is excellent and friendly, the food is impeccable and the dessert island is amazing. I can go on and on! Highly recommend!

I would rather spend my money elsewhere, as this is the most highly priced buffet in Vegas. Wicked Spoon, and the buffet at the Wynn, provide better food options for better prices. It was still quite an experience though, and I might give it a third attempt, lest it change my mind?

Sooo disappointed! I used to love this place and after visiting 3yrs later again last night I'm never coming back! Not to mention my 1yr old and husband for really sick and my daughter was crying/ screaming of stomach pain all night! Such a horrible experience! $70 a person with pathetic food! I was so looking forward for the lamb chops and they were dry and disgusting, the meat station meat lacked flavor, the seafood was scrawny and scarce, and the only other food station was an Asian with probably the only good thing being the salmon poke and the "pizza station". This was a joke! Seriously save your selves the money and go somewhere else.

Oh gosh this is such a great buffet to really chow down on an amazing variety of food. There is a huge variety of food... Chinese, Japanese, Italian, American, etc. I was a bit disappointed that the Filipino section is gone since I wanted to try the sinigang, but everything else made up for it. Must tries are the mint fudge, the gelato!!!, the wagyu beef, the mini crab at the Chinese section, and the snow crab legs with butter. Sooooo yummy. It's not the best tasting food (some of it is mediocre at best), but the variety is worth the price and you can tell that the staff really cares about your experience here. Within minutes of a counter being dirty, it's being wiped down. The hot snow crab server and steak slicing servers are very attentive. My waiters were so on point and fast with refilling drinks and taking away plates. What a great restaurant. 

I watched a video of Chef Leticia on Eater that made me put this on my itinerary, and I'm so glad I did. She evidently does a wonderful job running Bacchanal :)

I came to celebrate my birthday at Vegas specifically so that I could eat at the Bacchanal Buffet and it didn't disappoint!

Located in Caesar's palace, the Bacchanal buffet is located to the right hand side if you are coming from self parking.  

You pay for your meal before you are seated.  If you check in on Yelp, you get a complimentary beer or wine.

What I loved about the buffet was first the customer service and then the variety of foods available.

Pros:
-staff are great.  They helped celebrate my birthday by putting together a little dessert plate with items that weren't even on display for the general public at that time.  How cool is that?!?!?  They were also very attentive and got us new plates and utensils when we went up for seconds/desserts
-the variety of food is great!  The options wind all around the restaurant. 
-In the morning they have fresh pressed juice

Cons:
-none.

Tips:
-look on Groupon for any deals and save yourself some money

After eating there I had diarrhea and the worst kind.  Pretty sure it was the oysters.  No one else dared to have them.  I am pretty sure many other had the issue but were lucky enough to be near the bathroom.  I was not as lucky.  Horrible stomach flu.  We left about two hours after starting and walk to the Venetian to visit other friends.  From there I walked back the the  Mandalay to get car to pick up the family.  I guess it was getting late got the car from valet to pick up the kids at   the Venetian on the way all hell broke loses.  I will spare the details.  If they cant manage to keep food stored properly they should not serve food.

You will pay more for admission to the baccanal than it takes to fill up your car's tank. You will wait an hour to get in line and then another half an hour when in line waiting to be seated. It is worth it!

All I can say is that I ate my weight in steamed crab legs and then got up and asked for more! Best crab on the strip; the rest of the food was awesome, too. The only part I didn't enjoy so much was dessert, but I'm not sure if that's because I was feeling pretty miserable after eating too much or if the sweets were legitimately not as good as everything else.  

I tried everything except most of the sides- I was a woman on a mission and had no room for fillers, aka, veggies. I don't remember it being very vegetarian friendly, either. I mean, there are vegetarian options, but nothing nearly as appealing as everything else. 

If you're like me and seek out buffets for the crab, this is your place. I ate at 2 other buffets offering crab legs in the same week and nothing compared to the baccanal!

I hate buffets, but I had heard so many good things about Bacchanal I said I'll give it a whirl for breakfast ($28/each).  We had:

Freshly squeezed juices like carrot and cucumber
Smoked salmon & cold shrimp
Steak & egg
Biscuits and gravy, sausage and cheesy tots
Fried chicken and waffles
Sorbets:  Thai tea; fig & balsamic; mango chile lime; and blood orange

There were also your basic fare of eggs, bacon, hash browns, waffles, and an extensive array of desserts.

The juices were excellent and full of flavor.  I had four:  5 Stars.  In addition, the salmon and shrimp were fresher compared most buffets:  4 Stars.  Unfortunately, the hot dishes disappointed.  They were not warm.  In addition, the biscuits were not that moist, the sausage in the gravy was not crumbled well, and there wasn't enough pepper:  2 Stars.

On the other hand, the sorbets were really good and flavorful, with the mango chile lime being my favorite.  You could really taste the chile:  5+++'Stars for the latter flavor.  The woman who served me was from Puerto Rico, and we struck up a conversation in Spanish which was cool.

The remainder of the service was spotty.  Although there were many open tables, it took a while to be seated.  The group in front of me thought the same.  Additionally, we had to ask for water, and our glasses were not refilled.  Lastly, we told one server that we were going to the restroom.  However, when we returned, someone had cleared our table:  2 Stars.

I would come back here for breakfast.  However, I would not come back for dinner ($55), and wait an hour or more.  There are far better things to do in Vegas, than wait in a buffet line.
Great Buffett. Long line in get in. But my favorite part was the mini jelly jars . So cute!
Thank you bacchanal buffet for making delicious food . After a week of being at Vegas I visited many buffets and none came close to having the flavor your plates do .

This place is a little overrated considering the price and super long wait! Don't get me wrong, the food is good and you've got a whole variety of cuisines to choose from but it's no better than the options you can get from other buffets on the strip.

When it comes to a buffet like this, you'd expect some awesome seafood but the quality just didn't hit the spot.  The crab legs were either super salty and dry or just flat out bland.  The oysters didn't seem to be very fresh either.  They didn't wash them too well after shucking the shell and seems like that had died hours prior to being laid out.  They did have a decent nigiri selection, with the fish being fresher than what you'd typically get at a buffet.

The only two things I really enjoyed here was the huge dessert selection (presentation was great as well).  Everything from the creme brûlée to the macarons were on point.  They even had mochi (matcha green tea was the bomb).  The fresh juices were also quite refreshing and comes in a cool glass bottle with a cap on top.  

Overall, if you want to wait for well over an hour to get in and see what the hype is all about, give it a shot for yourself.  Other than that, do know there are other places up to par for much less of a wait and much cheaper too!

Came here for a buffet lunch with a few friends. Had great expectations since there was such a huge hype. It is located in the casino of Caeser's Palace. Food turned out to be great, but not amazing. There is a huge variety, but because there is such a big variety, they are not able to excel at everything. I find that many foods were hit or miss. They tried really hard to cater to every culture. 

It was quite cool to see a noodle bar which is not very common at many buffets. There was pho, ramen, wonton noodles, etc. You can choose your own style of noodle and toppings and the chef there would make it for you on the spot. They also have a separate area for desserts which had a wide variety, ranging from macarons, cakes, pastries, ice cream, fruite, etc. Would come back and try dinner next time.

Bacchanal Buffet was absolutely straight fire! Hands down the best buffet in Vegas. Don't be discourage by the wait time especially during brunch! It is highly recommend. I destroyed the all you can eat lobster claws, and the wagyu beef. We also got pretty tipsy off of the bottomless mimosas.

PRO TIP: check groupon for discounts on the buffet .

Visited here with a friend to begin our New Years celebration. I had high expectations as I heard this is the best buffet in the country.

To start, we got into line at 2:30pm. We waited for almost 2 hours and were inside by 4pm. By the time we were entering the buffet, we saw the line size almost doubled, and I'd say those who got in line at 4pm would have a 2.5-3hr wait. 

Inside, the decor was nice, and the seating was laid out well. The buffet itself had many options to choose from, everything from crispy pork belly to snail to crabs to tacos.

Some of the Foods I tried:

Crab legs: 5/5. 2-3 minute wait in line, legs were cooked on the spot. They're also cut halfway near the joints to make it easier to break the shell.

Raw oyster: 5/5. You need to shuck them, they were pretty decent

Crispy pork belly: 5/5: crispy on the outside, melt-in-your-mouth on the inside. Very good for a buffet

Pork belly buns: 4/5: buns were squishy and delicious. Pork belly had good flavor and was very tender

Elk sandwich: 2/5: wanted to try elk for the first time, however it's not for me. Meat was gamy and cold. Would not recommend 

Snail: 4/5: first time trying snail, had the texture of oyster, was pretty easy to eat

Prime rib slices of meat: 5/5: meat is cut for you on the spot. This meat was very tender and had amazing flavor. Better than the steak I had at Gordon Ramsay steak 

Dessert: 5/5: massive selection of samplers. My stomach was at capacity at this point so I didn't get to try everything

Overall: 4/5: after 2 hours of eating some amazing food, I feel this buffet was worth the price and wait

Love the food here. You can find a lot traditional food from different countries. You won't be disappoint here. They also service fresh juice in the brunch. I was there during the holiday weekend, price a little higher than usual, but worth it. If you like seafood, they also service crabs crawfish and shrimp in the brunch.

I've seen the food from here all over Snapchat and Instagram and thought, darn. It looks mighty delicious. It was only right to have this dining experience as part of my first ever Vegas trip.

Went around 11 AM and it wasn't crowded, no wait and lots of empty tables. 

Why make this review long when there are thousands of reviews already on what types of food are served?
