Anything I had was either dry, cold, or tasted like they been sitting around for a long time. 

Freshly squeezed juices were good. Ice cream was good. 

People. Please read the signs of what you're getting. I heard a lot of customers complaining the yellow cubes they had stacked onto their plates weren't pineapples. Yea, the little placard says YELLOW WATERMELON. It doesn't even look like pineapples...?

Servers were amazing though, always clearing the plates and asking how things were. 

Left at 12:40PM and the place was packed! I zig zagged my way out since people were holding plates laden with food but not paying attention to where they were walking. There were so many people waiting to be seated, it was crazy!

Left Bacchanal confused.

Overall i thought that this buffet was one of the best buffets that i have ever been to. They had many different variety of meats such as lamb and primb rib (which were cooked really well). I am usually very picky with slider but the one at this buffet was amazing. The ramen was decent and so were the crab legs. This buffet had a giant variety of many different types of food and they all hit a good level of satisfaction. Not a big fan of buffets but this one is an exception for me.

Very good quality buffet. It was pricier than others on the strip but you get what you pay for. Large variety and selection of food and everything I got tasted delicious. If you are a seafood lover than you should definitely try this buffet out. I would go back anytime.

This is hands down the best buffet in Las Vegas. If you're ever visiting in town or even a local, you have to at least try this place once. It's definitely not the cheapest in town but well worth the money. The food is high quality and the choices are great, even a little overwhelming at first. Be ready for a little bit of a wait standing in line at the entrance. A wait is expected since let's not forget that it is located in one of the busiest casinos on the strip. The service is great and I never had to flag down a waiter for anything. As a tip, use the colosseum parking instead of the mall parking. Well worth it, you won't regret it.

Everything was phenomenal. I could not find a single thing that I did not like. The biscuit and gravy with the ham and hashbrowns was the best part. I give all my respect and admiration for everyone working in the kitchen

Food is just ok. Staff is not very friendly. Only food I really enjoyed was the shrimp campechana and a lime pasta next to it. Those two had an amazing flavor. For the price... for sure I will not be returning.

Bacchanal was not this mediocre a few years ago. I remember my first experience at Bacchanal and I was so blown away by the crazy variety of dishes from different cuisines. The buffet still features a million dishes, but none of them were well done. The entrance line was ridiculously long. Even though my boyfriend and I had platinum status, we still waited for a good 30 minutes in line to enter. The regular line was so long it probably had an average wait time of 2-3 hours. They now have an "express" option where you pay $30 extra (I think) and you get to skip most of the line. I don't think it's worth it. 

Everyone was all over the seafood of course, but none of the items were impressive or fresh. We got some oysters, snail, and crab...and we opted to not finish them because none of the items tasted fresh. The dim sum items were super dry and just not well made in general. None of the Asian cuisine dishes were appetizing. My boyfriend got some ribs and steak as well, but they were way overcooked and dry. 

The dessert bar used to be my favorite, but now everything was so mediocre and tasteless. We tried the flan, creme brulee, and gelato...and we were not impressed by anything from the dessert bar.

Fantastic Buffet with some unique offerings with great flavors and top notch quality on most dishes.  Notable mentions include: American wage beef, slow cooked pork soup (forgot name - delicious), Mexican chocolate, churros with special sauce, berry infused mineral water, fresh watermelon & cucumber juice, tuna & salmon poke, big fat crab legs, jumbo shrimp (really big & meaty), fantastic dessert selections, such as red bean ruby buns, Vietnamese boba coffee with vanilla gelato, shaved ice with all the fixings, all kinds of exotic flavored gelato.  The  only reason for a 3-stars instead of 5-stars rating, is deal to their less than acceptable service.  The hostesses and waiters seem to work hard but lack personality.  I am paying for reasonable fare, yet it feels like I having to beg for their service.  The worst part is where we were reminded repeatedly of a two hour limit for the sitting.  Very UNWELCOMING!!!

This is one of the reasons why my wife and I came to Las Vegas was to eat at this buffet. Everything has changed since our last time here. The last time we were here they had great selection of fresh seafood. They had huge king crab legs. This time we went they told me they no longer offer king crab any more. They instead give you cheap crab legs that you can eat at any cheap $19.99 bedder. The crab was frozen. They have also stop offer a variety of meat that they use to. They use to offer rack of lamb and other variety of meats that they no longer offer. I had some wagyu need but it was horrible. Like eating a piece of card board. Very dry. Prime rib was ok. It just looks like this buffet has stop caring about there customers. It seems management made decisions to offer cheap quality of choices in order to make more money. Trying to cheat the customer. I was so disappointed in this buffet. This use to be the best buffet in Las Vegas and now it's become one of the worse. I really hope management reviews all these bad reviews and make changes and offers the selection that they use to. Customers are educated and see the bad changes that you have made. Please offer your customers more value.

When arriving and even with vip status you have to wait for over a hour to even pay and get back into another line and wait even longer it is disheartening. The food was ok but between the stupid concept they have for corralling customers and the wait line design plus the extremely rude and unhelpful staff at the check in if I hadn't already pre paid to eat here then I would have gone to wicked spoon which was a hundred times better. If you are planning on purchasing a Groupon for the restaurant don't bother. They penalize you for it and make you wait for full paying customers to go first. Screw this restaurant and everyone one associated with it. Please learn from my mistake and go elsewhere!!!!

Best buffet I've ever been too. Especially impressed with the carving station. One of the best things I had was green Beans fried with a dipping sauce that tasted like wasabi. Desserts were great-presented mostly in smaller portions so you can try a lot of different things. Loved the Boursin macaroni and cheese and the dim sum. Nice attentive servers. Price is high -but it's renowned so we gave it a try. Long waits-probably waited  over 2 hrs to get in
Excellent food. Everything is served in small portion! Great presentation of buffet!!!

Daughter bought a groupon deal and headed out there for breakfast. The selection is pretty limited but it is breakfast and people are either hung over to realize what they are eating or they are still passed out. Food is fresh and tasty. The service is so-so. Our server was not into the "customer experience" and when my daughter asked for non-dairy creamer (I do not consume dairy), she brushed her off as, "we do not have any". Worthy note: orange juice is really FRESH!!!

To be honest, I thought this place was overrated. I tried one of each dish and didn't find one particular thing that really shocked me. Don't get me wrong, there's a wide array of dishes. There's tacos, seafood, sushi, Chinese. You name it, and it's probably there. 

I paid during brunch and stayed until dinner. I was in a party of two and the wait for food was about 20 minutes. I paid around $60 for my whole meal. The dining area is extremely large. It is kind of a pain if you're seated towards the back and if the foods in the front. There are no duplicate dishes so if you want something you'll have to know where it is. 

For me, this was just a one time, tourist thing. Three stars for the wide variety of food but I don't think I'd ever pay this much for a buffet ever again.

Visited for the first time last month, and I am definitely planning on coming here next time we're in Vegas. My niece texted me last week, telling me how much she craved the food from here, so I'm not the only one wanting to go back. Worth every penny. We got there shortly before 11 am and we paid for breakfast, but also enjoyed lunch. Sooooo yummy.
Food and service were good. Lots of variety although I miss bot having a salad bar. All in all it was a good experience but definitely over priced

Truly a great experience! Food, desert and service. What more can one expect. Worth every penny. If I have to Express a complaint, would have to be the wait to get in... 2hours..., but well managed when you get in.

I fail to understand all the hype about this buffet.  There was nothing extraordinary about this place that justifies the astronomical cost.  A buffet is a buffet is a buffet.  The variety of food was noteworthy, but c'mon.  Pizza and breadsticks on the buffet line? I can get that at Olive Garden or Pizza Hut.  The variety of desserts was also noteworthy, but again, nothing extraordinary. Service was average. I would've expected more attentive service, even for a buffet, considering the cost of it.

If I wanted something this rude, tacky, and expensive I'd spend Christmas with my dad's ex-wife.
Waited through a rather short, but painfully slow line during off-hours on a weekday.  When I got to the front, an irritable, unhelpful woman rejected my discount card, but couldn't be bothered to articulate why.  She tried to sell me 2 tickets for $120 with no explanation of drinks, obscene pleasures, or anything else to explain the exorbitance.  Ahead of me, I could see yet more inexplicably slow lines.  (It's a buffet, not a rock concert!) So I left.

FYI, no buffet with stupidly long lines can be considered fine dining under any circumstances and no endangered shellfish on ice or oversized plaster busts could make these people worth tolerating.
Excellent service, short wait, friendly staff. Also huge variety of food to choose from!

I had high expectations for this buffet after reading the high reviews on yelp. I tried their lunch and dinner buffet and was not completely blown away although there are a few items that stood out.  

We purchased the buffet of buffets 24 hour pass and I found out that each time you enter Bacchanal there is an up charge of $15 for breakfast $25 for lunch & $30 for dinner. To me, the major difference between lunch and dinner is that dinner serves Alaskan crab legs and fresh oysters compared to lunch, but they carry the same items during both times.

My only favorite here are the street tacos that you can have made to order which are fresh and tasty.  Also, in the seafood section you can have them cook shrimp your way. So cold cocktail shrimp can be cooked with butter and garlic on the spot.  The lava cake and egg tarts were my favorite in the dessert section. I was disappointed with some of the miniature cake slices and cupcakes as they did not taste fresh to me. Some were rather stiff in texture. 

Customer service at the cashier was bad both times we entered.  Lady first time was not informative about how we use our 24 hour pass and did not smile or look hospitable.  In the restaurant and hospital management business I think being friendly towards your customers is rule number one.  Second time around we gave our total rewards card to the lady (which had our 24 hour bob purchase on there) and she charged us full price for lunch at first without listening to my comment that we were there for the buffet of buffets 24 hour deal.  

Mind you there was no line and not busy the time she rang us up.  Focus is key when paying...for the person ringing up the meal purchases. 

Please Caesars Palace, improve on the customer service.  People travel worldwide to enjoy world class food, entertainment, and service.  That's my 2 cents on Bacchanal.


I don't know if I would purchase the buffet of buffets for this anymore.

Waiting in line for 3 hours for a buffet is nuts. We can all agree on that right? But when you're waiting in line for something called "the best buffet ever" it kind of makes you question whether or not you should stay in line... my family and I stayed. For 3 hours. In line. 

After you pay, there's 2 separate lines for groups of 4 or less and groups of 5 or more. After we got through the 3 hours of waiting in line to pay, we finally made it to the line for a table. It didn't take long after that. Soon enough we got seated near the way inside and it was time to dig in.

The atmosphere? I like it. Yes. Glass walls. Lovely decor. Wonderful staff service. And pretty much people everywhere. 

The food? It's definitely decent and some were above decent. The sushi area was good since they had fresh salmon and tuna for you to eat. And near that area is a worker cooking udon, ramen, and pho for you. Definitely should check that out. You should also check out their bottles of juice and horchata. Not super special, but definitely a cute idea from the normal "Can I have water? Coke?" Only problem? You have to line up for the seafood. I know it's seafood (oysters, crab legs...) but when you're lining up where the meat products are then it's kind of nuts. People are repeatedly waiting for the workers to dump more oysters out and you can even see them working on opening the oysters and everything. Patience is the key at buffets. 

The dessert bar was also cool. Cupcakes, cakes, crepes, ice cream, mochi ice cream, all were interesting to try but probably not more than once. And a bummer? There was no beautiful plate of macarons when I went. I was looking forward to it and it just didn't make an appearance so I was bummed out about that. 

Overall, this place IS probably one of the best buffets I been to. I ate till I was bloated and could no longer walk. But the 3 hour wait leaves your feet aching and extremely hungry. Oh, and the receipt also says to keep your eating to a maximum of 2 hours. But you know people will sit longer than that so that might be why I was waiting so long.
Food was AMAZING drinks were not! The waitress was very rude and old. I saw many old women serving customers, it is better to give them jobs with better accommodations, like a cashier!

Highly recommend! We were not sure whether the high price would be worth it or not, but it definitely was! We went in with a plan, we tried to only eat a bite of everything at first and then come back for our favorites. Our plan went out he door immediately when we saw the selection! There's so much high-quality food here!!! They had every type of food you could imagine and the quality of it all was unmatched! Three different types of crab!! We waited in line about an hour, which is actually pretty good but we went around 4pm on a Tuesday so we were expecting a shorter wait. Doesn't really matter though because it's worth the wait!! This is a must in Vegas.

We were all excited going to the buffet being that all you can eat king crab.So we was told over the phone.So we waited at least 3 hours.We figured was worth the wait.As we finally went in we was told a additional 50 bucks more for the king crab and was not all you can eat.So was a very disappointed evening for my son in law and daughter during there visit.
We spent $50 per person,  the food was unimpressive at this price.  Service was sub par.  Had to ask for refills. For all of us it was $400 and they would not validate parking.

Elfenish the lady taking in customers for the lines was very rude & not helpful. I got here at 9 & stated we have a party of 5 & would like to eat here she went on to say that "umm we close at 10 and there might be a 45 min wait line so probably no" so as I'm standing waiting to see what else we can eat, 3 different groups ranging from 3-5 people in each group are able to get in line. As I'm watching this I become frustrated because she did not let us in yet she did the other people. So I approached her  & asked her "why did you let those 3 different groups of people in yet you denied us entry to make line", she stated "oooh I thought you didn't want to eat here". Now I'm just more frustrated. Customer service gets 0. I ended up leaving with my party of 5.

We were looking for a seafood buffet and after walking through, decided this was our place! The food was amazing! When we went to get steamed crab legs, they didn't just give you a few, they piled them on the plate! Definitely got our moneys worth! The biggest complaint I have is the waiter we had. He came by to take our drink order and cleared our table once after. We did not see him for an hour and he NEVER came back to our table. Literally the only reason we saw him again was in passing when he had another table sat. No refills of drinks were brought to us, we had to ask another waitress to bring us hot tea. It was very frustrating! So great food, but terrible service!

I've been coming to this buffet for several years. It's very clean and the quality of the food is very good. But on my most recent trip I started to question the value and variety. I think I'll try a different buffet next time I go, I've read that the Wynn is great. This most recent trip was good but not enough variety for me to get something new every time I went up. I don't eat meat or most fried foods so I don't get everything that others may love from the carving section. I love that they have the pre-split crab legs and shrimp cocktail. Their desserts were also good but I wanted more chocolate options and they didn't have tons. I recall waiting a long time for water and I remember that happened before too. Overall it's good and def a place to try once. But for me I'm going to try a diff buffet when I go again in the fall just so that I can have more of a comparison.
Food Was Tasty for a buffet, great customer service and plenty of space. Pretty nice inside and comfortable environment.

The food here is so good that I thought I was actually going to die from overeating. When I was on my third plate of seafood and rice, it occured to me that maybe this whole thing was a test, some kind of study on what happens when humans are able to taste The Food Of The Gods. The answer is that we lose all common sense, and stuff ourselves to the point of bursting. 

Anyway! I loved this buffet and I know people are talking about a long wait to get in, but when I went I picked up a VIP pass ($100, reserved through OpenTable) which is only about $30 more than the usual cost of the buffet and I was seated in about fifteen minutes. Of course, you can save that extra cash and just wait in line, but I recommend the VIP service for sure (they also bring out a seafood tower for VIPs which includes lobster and lobster is NOT on the regular buffet lineup, it's only available in the VIP package).

It is a great buffet but $45 for lunch really come on. They didn't tell us either that the king crab legs don't start until 3 pm for the same price that kind of was a bummer to find out after we paid but what are you going to do it's Vegas.
This is the best buffet in Vegas little pricey but good quality food, so we're hight recommented, go weekend is the best

Not worth the wait. We did go on a busy day, Friday night. We waited 2 1/2 hours before we were seated. Maybe be best to go during the weekdays. Once we were finally seated, the person attending our table took about 40 min to bring us water. But stated there was 2 tables ahead if us and she would not be able to help us right away. After seeing reviews we were expecting the food to be outstanding from the best Buffett on the strip. But the food was just Ok. We were starving after a wait of 2 1/2 hours and the food was just Ok. After an hour of being seated we finally had to ask the waitress for some drinks. We were able to get some sodas. Were didn't even get time to get our free beer or wine after checking in on Yelp. Next time I'm going back to the Buffet in the Rio. Way better service.

Having had this buffet on my bucket list for at least a year, I had high hopes and expectations for Bacchanal. I was expecting perfection and of course that doesn't exist. I give Bacchanal a 3-star rating. 

The buffet really starts in my opinion at 3pm, when they bring out the crab legs. It's the only thing that was on every one of my plates. Before then they have stone crab claws, but their shells are beastly and even though they saw them half way open the second half isn't always easy or possible to break open. 

My favorite items were the lamb chops, the crab legs, any of the dim sum, the oyster shooters, the creme brûlée and interestingly enough the horchata. I did a lot of research before going and I saw that some of their presentation and offerings had changed since they redid the buffet. 

For example I was a little bummed out when I didn't see any honeycomb or shrimp and grits. I also didn't see any king crab legs however I imagine those are reserved for weekends or holidays. I would advise against the BBQ ribs (tough and burnt with no BBQ sauce), the asian duck (greasy and extremely tough),  and the gelato (way too soft). The bone marrow was both greasy and burnt. 

I totally loved that the servers have such a small area to cover so they are really attentive. Ours was very kind and when we started getting close to the two hour mark she said we could take all the time we would like. 

As for the wait, we got there at 2:15pm (highly recommended as you pay lunch price but get dinner offerings). It took us probably 25 minutes from entering the like to getting our table. After you pay you still have to wait to get a table. Small parties get in much faster than large. And what you pay for is a two hour buffet. 

Some tips I have are to go during the work week, just before dinner starts, to not carb overload early on like my wife did, and to hydrate along the way. It's a lot of sodium you take in! Be sure to get moving after you leave. There are lots of things to see and walking off the calories will get you back to your normal self quickly.

Finally got the chance to do a buffet in Vegas!  Talk about a huge variety of different cuisines!  We arrived early so there was no wait, and we came during the breakfast and lunch transitioning time, so we had best of both worlds!

There were snow crab, king crabs and dungeness crabs clusters for breakfast! Heck yeah!  Overall there food are mediocre, but there's a little something for everyone!

Bring a stomach or two, to get your moneys worth of food!
as of right now.. it's the best buffet in vegas. they have charcuterie!

Ahhhhhh someone please take me back!!! And I apologize in advance because I know this review is going to be very long...but it is a HUGE buffet so don't blame me, blame Bacchanal :) 

If you are short on time just know..this buffet is WORTH VISITING. I was pretty skeptical by all the great reviews and the yelper's never lie..now for the people who would like to know what there is to have at this buffet: keep reading! 

Ok, I swear I'm not all over it because I'm asian but I can say i was genuinely impressed with the selection of asian food they had. The dim sum, multiple different soups varying from rice porridge, miso soup, hot and sour, won ton soup, ramen, and a curry type soup. Not only was the selection huge but the quality was great. I was really excited when I saw the korean bbq but it was a little tendon-y for my taste...
Highlights: seaweed salad, roast duck, rice porridge, and all the dim sum items.

Large assortment of deli meats that I didn't get to try because I was stuffing my face with other things. Same thing apples to the italian/pizza station. I did try some of the meatballs and the tortellini. They were both tasty but neither "wow-ed" me. 

Next to the mexican station were probably 20-25 different types of salsa, yummmmyyyyy

Ok, the meat station...they probably need more than one guy working this station but I was one of the lucky gal's that tasted the brisket...man is that brisket the best brisket and meat and fat I have EVER tasted. Not that anyone has to convince me to go back to Bacchanal, but I would go back for the brisket period. I also had the ham but the ham was nothing compared to the brisket. On my next visit I hope to see chicken breast instead of whole chicken where you pick your pieces. I just try to avoid bones when possible...

The next station was carbo-junk food galore. Little baskets of sweet potato tater tots (please don't get me started), regular tator tots, fried chicken and french fries, don't remember the rest because I was too busy with the sweet potato tater tots. 

This is also really random...but the grilled asparagus was delicious. I am a fighter when someone serves me asparagus but I willingly got up for a second serving of asparagus here.

Unfortunately, the seafood station is another one that seems understaffed. I didn't try much of the seafood besides the crab because there were SO MANY PEOPLE! But, the crab was much too salty for my taste.

Before I end my praise of how great Bacchanal Buffet, PLEASE visit the crepe station and have one for me. In my visit, I ate 3, and its not because the crepes were small, unfortunately. I literally could not stop myself. There is an assortment of fresh blueberries, blackberries, raspberries, and nutella, caramel, chocolate, freshly whipped whipped cream, etc. This crepe station alone is what sets Bacchanal aside from the others. 

However, there were a lot of things I was flat out not impressed with: 
1. The pathetic fruit selection. Not only was the selection pathetic but the presentation was not up to par with the other things in the buffet. Simple things like the pineapple...they didn't even remove the rind. My school dining hall serves the pineapple with rind. An upscale buffet where people are paying $45+tax and tip for dinner shouldn't have to do more work with the simple PINEAPPLE. Ok, enough with that. Onto the next thing
2. The Mexican station...I thought this station could use some improvement. First of all, the shredded beef or whatever meat they served definitely has way too many chunks of fat in it. That is all. The tamales, tasty but not enough meat. 
3. I understand that everyone is adapting to the "small plates" trend but I am not a fan..some of the items like the curly fries or other fried items I wanted to try ONE of but since they were pre-portioned, I couldn't! Sometimes the buffets end up wasting more through this method. Thats more of a suggestion than a complaint but whatever.
4. This place didn't have macaroons on my visit. But there are pictures on Yelp saying that they have macaroons. They either need to have macaroons everyday or not at all. (angry emoji)
5. Lastly, they need a bathroom inside the actual buffet. The bathroom is right outside where you pay but its inconvenient having to share a bathroom with everyone in the casino/hotel along with the buffet customers.

Of course, no buffet is perfect so I'm afraid I have to give it a solid four stars. I hope to see continuous improvements on my next visit! (and hopefully not another price increase)

PS. I didn't think the servers were as slow as people made them out to be. Within 2 minutes we had our initial greet with our server to take our drinks. By the time I brought back my first plate, the drinks were there. Just an FYI!

Probably one of the most popular buffets in Vegas and the world. Prices range from $55 - $70 depending on when you go and if you go on a weekend. For a Sunday brunch, we paid $55+tax & tips and it came out to be around $70. The lines are definitely not as crazy as it was years ago when my family came here.

The selection of food is huge, ranging from Asian food, to American food, to Seafood, etc. Because we came at brunch time, there were a lot of breakfast menu things on there such a crepes, sausages, eggs, fries, dim sum. The food is honestly whatevers, definitely not worth the price that you pay for because no matter how much you eat, there's just no way to eat your moneys' worth. 

I'd say the best part of Bacchanal is always the desserts. They have a wide variety of desserts, ranging from crepes, gelato bar, creme brulees, macaron, cakes, etc. Definitely the highlight of the buffet! I definitely ate wayyy more dessert than the actual food because it didn't really appeal to me as much. I think a couple of years ago when I went to Bacchanal, it was definitely the peak of their time because I remember they had more selection and the quality was definitely better.

The buffet here is okay but not worth the high price compared the other buffets I have had with a similar selection. I would definitely recommend getting the Groupon to make it worth it. We came here on a 2 for $88 Groupon that includes VIP service. It comes with two mimosas and skip the line passes. The caveat is you have to get there before 10:30am. The regular brunch Buffett is about $60 and it is not worth it.

There is a good selection of food ranging from  asian to seafood. They don't have many vegan options but certain vegetarians would be good here. A wide selection of desserts but not much of a salad bar. People enjoy their selection of crab legs and other seafood. I liked the made to order crepes and gelato. 

The asian selections included sushi, dumplings, and noodles etc... this was a nice treat but I would not come here without a Groupon.

7 years ago I went to the newly redone Caesar's buffet and lost my mind at how extravagant the selections were they were they had so many offerings mini plates just perfect so u could try a bit of everything
Finally I was in Vegas last week and made it to the buffet again at 745 pm the lines were unbelievable I checked into the kiosk at qued up in line at 830 I had tickets for 10 pm  the line was moving so slow they had a $55 upcharge to go to the front of the line I talked to the hostess and said that was a little steep she came back and offered me a 20$ discount to go to front of line so I accepted it and paid $95 to go to front 
I waited another thirty minutes in front of line and got sat at 910
The seafood selections were excellent but I never made it past the second station with prime rib which was delicious I got sick and couldn't eat anymore not from the food from the standing and waiting  I suffer from a cardiac condition that excessive standing drops my blood pressure 
So I went to restroom it was 940  so I was going to try dessert after anticipating the fresh berries and real whipped  cream I had 7 years ago I find berry compote and non dairy whipped topping I find it embarrassing for such an elegant buffet to offer cheap imitation cream
I went to red rock the next day paid $15 for buffet and found real whipped cream next to the jello
Don't get me wrong the buffet at Caesar's was very good but the wait times are excessive and quality is still good but offerings were definitely less than what I remember 7 years ago

Heard a lot of good things about this Caesar's Palace gem and decided to give it a go.  I came at 10:45am with my family on a Sunday.  We had to wait like 15-20 minutes, which was a lot less than I had expected.  There's a line further in dedicated to groups with parties 6 or more.  Our party of 7 was the third group in that line.  I felt bad for the snake like line that we bypassed.  If ever that's the case, I'd totally ask another group in line if they'd want to join groups. Whatever gets you in faster right? :D

Since we went on Dec. 28, it was holiday pricing.  It costed $47 vs. the usual $42.  Service was awesome!  My mimosa glass was never empty for too long and our waitress was really sweet.  She didn't even complain when I wanted a different drink each time.  Their hot chocolate is amazing by the way and it comes with whipped cream (:

The food was amazing!  They had a huge variety and the presentation of everything was immaculate!  Totally worth your money!  I actually enjoyed the cha siu ramen and pho.  Some buffets make asian soups too salty, but they made it alright here.  Here are a few of the things I had tried (don't judge how big of a fatty I am haha): Mussels, Crab Legs, Oysters, Shrimp Cocktail, Breakfast Burrito, Mac n Cheese, Red Velvet Pancakes, and Chicken & Waffles with Sweet Potato Fries, etc. Seafood was fresh and I loved almost everything I tried.  Dessert was awesome with the made to order crepe station and the gelato station.  I appreciate the scoops of the gelato are small, so that you can try a bunch of them haha.  I can rave on and on and I really enjoyed my experience. Definitely stop by if you're in the area (:

We went here tonight for my husband's birthday, as he's been wanting to go for awhile. The service was definitely impeccable with our beverages and clearing the table. We went around 5PM and probably waited 20+mins in line, which wasn't too terrible. (It cost $211 for 3 of us.); in my opinion...not worth it and I really have no need to return.  There are a ton of options to choose from, and most of what I had was "good".  Nothing was mouth-watering or exceptional. Just "decent". Some of the food was lukewarm or just plain cold. When I consider spending that much...I know we could have a much more extravagant meal for the same price.

Extremely expensive for what you get. You find crab legs and a very extensive buffet but the service lacks completely. To provide you an idea, after you spend around $100, you need to pay to have a latte. The waiter did forget what we were drinking and served another rounds of mimosa and champagne completely wrong. Who was drinking champagne find for themselves a mimosa and viceversa. If they take away your silverware, you will need to ask again and wait long time before you get another clean silverware. Often time your plates were not removed in a timely manner and you had to stack your plate to be able to eat. Overall experience is just average. If you pay top price compared to the rest of the other buffet on the strip, you need to offer a top experience which we definitely did not receive.
Don't bother checking in to get your free glass of wine. No WiFi or data available once your inside so you won't be able to get it since you can't click redeem. False promises.

Attempted to visit this restaurant during dinner hours 7pm and had to return the next day- I was in a party of 7, arrived around 4pm. Their was no wait, we were seated and helped ourselves. The food their is amazing! So many different food group to taste from. Wish i could've tried many more of the varieties offered. The seafood section is where I spent most of my time.

We try to visit this buffet a few times a year, but I"m not sure we will be back after our last visit. We have had some great visits and a few okay/bad experiences in the past, but this one was really bad. There are always long wait times and that is understandable, but what was messaged as a 45 minute wait turned into more like 1.5 hours. That alone wouldn't have deterred us, but it was followed up with some very poor service (I'm guessing our server went to lunch or left for the day because she never returned) and we had to spend far too much time trying to track someone down to clear our plates. We finally tracked someone down to get a drink refill, but they took our order and never returned either. We were surprised at how rude and dismissive a few of the staff actually were. The food didn't seem to be as good as usual either and we were there at peak weekend time. Would be hard to justify coming back again just because of so many other restaurants/buffets on the strip. Which is really unfortunate.

This buffet was amazing everything was delicious, service was excellent.  This is like no buffet I've ever been too before sort of should be in another category.  All foods were fresh, the right temperatures, and plentiful.  Well worth the price!
lovely buffet but overpriced.  Need to offer a better selection of breakfast cocktails,

This is the only buffet that I have been going to in Vegas for the past 3 years and honestly it's always just as good as I have remembered year after year. Bacchanal Buffet is really the best buffet in Vegas and it definitely satisfies that Vegas Buffet craving every time.   

I love the fact that they have food from all over the wold. From what I recall, there's a seafood, BBQ/Meat, Mexican, Italian, and different type of Asian sections. The variety of option are endless and you probably won't leave being able to try them all because you will be too full. I had the seafood to the pizza and they are all really good! This buffet is proved that it is not quality over quantity but both! 

The dessert table is also to die for! They have a huge dessert station that offers really good types of desserts! (Ex: Crepes, gelato, chocolate covered strawberries, macaroons, cheesecake pop cakes, cookies, creme brûlée, and many more!) I found myself grabbing a whole plate full of desserts and even finishing it all because it was so delicious! 

The customer service here is also awesome. Our server was constantly checking up on us and grabbing our finished plates often. Our soda/water was also refilled often. 

If you're in Vegas, this is the buffet to try!

Great restaurant/buffet with multiple options of food.  The one drawback is the wait so I suggest you go before you are starving for food, otherwise you'll be miserable waiting.  But once you are in, it is food heaven!

My absolute favorite buffet! My children and I ate here while on our trip to Vegas and were all blown away by the quality of the food! Our favorite was the enormous selection of fresh seafood. My son said eating here made the trip to Vegas worth it in itself.

Amazing variety of food, desserts, drinks and so much more! Definitely recommend this place for your buffet craving.  If your into seafood, they have an amazing variety to choose from & everything is absolutely delicious.

Hands down the best buffet experience I've ever had! 
I would definitely recommend to anyone visiting Vegas. We came around 2:00PM on a Thursday so there was no line. We walked right in and paid the brunch price but was able to enjoy the dinner options as well at 3:00PM. 
That's when the crowd began to make its way to the steamed crab legs! We also paid an additional $15 each for unlimited wine,sangria and beer. So worth it!
The best buffet we have ever had! Great selection and quality! Love the crab legs for lunch! So worth the money! Highly recommend.
Honestly: meh. With all the hype and the hefty price point, I was expecting everything to taste amazing. Obviously that wasn't the case.

Wasn't too impress the last time we went last month but we did go again to a Sunday Bunch. At 2 pm, the place is still packed. Varieties of food being served and quality is great. Special thanks to Samantha whose customer service is top notch.

It had pretty large selection of food choices but seafood was pretty disappointed. Need some improvement for that price. Desert was good. Steak and other meats were pretty good. vip buffet seems way better! Oh well

Was so excited to try out THE most popular and raved out buffet in Vegas. Located right in the Caesars palace. Went around 12 ish so you can say line was long. I hear it's around 1-2 hour wait line but luckily this time around it was 40 min. But my gf's and I were hungry so we paid an extra $15 on top of the $40 lunch fee for the express lane and waited only about 5-10 min. 

The inside is real nice, spacious and clean. Mimosas's are free and lots of other refreshing beverages at the stations. There was about 4 or 5 stations of Asian, Mexican, Breakfast, Seafood, and Italian. The asian station had good dumplings, and the pho hit the spot since we were hungover. For the meat area the habenero sausage link was so juicy and had a nice kick. The meat tacos were real good! highly recommend it!. Of course the food always changes so sad some of the food I saw on the pictures were not at the buffet :( 

The dessert station was centered right in the middle. The desserts were sadly just okay. I got practically one of each and most were just okay while 2 or 3 were tasty. The gelato was a miss for me. The crepes however were pretty good and made right when you order. 

I think I just had such high expectations from all the reviews I expected everything to be top notch. Overall I would come again. Still pretty good and would like to try dinner and breakfast. I must say I ate so much I felt I had to be wheel chaired out! Be ware you will leave satisfied and in my case sick haha but worth it :)

My friend really wanted to try Bacchanal since its the newest buffet place in Vegas, so we came here around 6:30 on a Thursday night. I have to say after eating Wicked Spoon at Cosmo, Wynn buffet and Aria's buffet..and all other buffets that I had in vegas in the past, Bacchanal is definitely OVERRATED. I talked to some people who live in Vegas  on our way back from Bacchanal, and they all said it's just okay, and they all agree that its a toss up between Aria's and Cosmo's buffet as the best buffet in town. So let me describe to you why this place is..just...okay.

1. the food selection was not as good as Wicked Spoon in terms of Asian food. I liked seeing the sushi chef making fresh sashimi and sushi at the sushi bar at Wicked Spoon, and the seafood definitely looked more fresh there than the ones I saw at Bacchanal. The only good Asian dish I had was the chicken soup, it was a little bitter because there's tiny pieces of ginseng, so that's the only thing I liked at the Asian selection.

2. Also, I didn't see anything unique about Bacchanal, and the selection for dessert was really standard...I was expecting the macarons to be good since I saw a lot of pictures of Macarons on yelp. But the taste of those macarons were not what I expected. 

Overall, I have to say I rather spend 50 bucks at Wicked spoon for dinner and 40 bucks at Aria's buffet for brunch... ( you get 2 complimentary buffet if you stay at Aria for two or more nights...) and Bacchanal is just one of those restaurants you probably want to go since it has been hyped up so much by friends and yelp reviews...but honestly in my opinion, I would pick Wicked spoon as my vegas buffet destination.

Love the decor and food selections! Dessert station is impressive.
Got seated immediately when we came at 5:45pm on a weekday.

Likes
Sushi/salmon sashimi (they don't usually serve sashimi but you can make a special request to the chef at that station), chilled or boiled king crab legs, stone crab, shrimp, clams

Used to like
Oysters. Sadly not as fresh as when I last ate here in Nov 2015. The server said that they now order pre-shucked oysters, which obviously are not as fresh, in order to save money :(

My fave desserts are the chocolate ganache mini cakes/brownies. The warm melted chocolate inside reminds me of lava cake! Also liked the huge chocolate covered strawberries

Our waiter was attentive. We stayed for 4 hours even though there's a 2-hour limit without anyone saying anything. My brother even got a special birthday dessert plate!
One of the best buffet I've been, very delicious and great service, I'd totally recommend this place, but I'd much rather go to the cosmopolitan buffet!

Fantastic food!!! Haven't had such good tasting food at a buffet before. The seafood selection is awesome... from split snow crab legs, lobster claws to prawns. The boiled shrimp is what I filled myself up with. The paella and even the Agua Fresca were great. The dessert were a little disappointing.

I was told this was like THE buffet in Vegas? I fail to see how. Sure, it's pretty inside, and there are a ton of options, but everything was legitimately bad. And that's not because I expect too much of a buffet. Literally every other buffet I've had in Vegas was better than this over all. That includes the random lower-tier "budget" buffets that'll be less than half the cost. 

Tough, flavorless meat, odd-tasting Asian options, weird bar-food section, terrible desserts. Also, who the hell does sweet potato tater tots? Perverts, that's who. The only decent thing was the Mexican food section, but who pays to eat Mexican food at a buffet? 

INCREDIBLY slow service. We waited fifteen minutes to have our drink order taken, and eventually just gave up and went to grab food. 

Also, trying to sell us pictures of ourselves as we enter the buffet? Really? That's beyond tacky.

Okay, where do I even start. Idk my friends and I are just obsessed with bacchanal. Obsessed. It's the best buffet in the world. Let's go station by station of our favorites.

1. Seafood: There are Crab legs that are cut in half and prepared for you so you can eat instead of working to open up the crab. Unlimited shrimp cocktails - I could probably eat the price's worth in shrimp cocktails. The second time we went the shrimp was not as cold as we wanted which was a little sad and disappointing. You can also get a plate of the boiled crab to eat it hot - make sure you get it with butter. Yum butter and crab legs yummmm

2. Meat: get the prime rib. It is so tender and juicy and again, would be $40 itself. I guess depending on the day you can ask the guy what he recommends to get the best cut for the day. SO GOOD.

3. Sushi: not the best best best sashimi quality but it's a buffet and for a buffet, pretty good nigiri. There's usually an assortment of salmon tuna and hamachi or albacore. 

4. Chinese: dim sum!! The sesame balls are petty filled with red bean and not full of air like some sesame balls are. The shumai and shrimp hagow are great. And the pork buns are fresh hot and deliciousss.

5. The pho here is surprisingly pretty good with clean broth. Get it to help you digest and settle your stomach so you can keep eating more. Cause it's bacchanal. Eat more.

6. Desserts: Thai tea boba with vanilla ice cream - ask for it at the ice cream station. The crepes are bombbbb. Just get as much dessert as your body will allow you.

Other tips: go with at least 6 people, go before 3 to pay lunch prices and get dinner. We didn't wait in any line on Saturday at 2:30 with 6 people. WE LOVE BACCHANAL.

This place was excellent! We stopped by on our last day of vacation around 1pm and we only had to wait about 45 minutes for a table. Our server was really helpful and our plates were always removed before we returned to our table. The stations were clean and the food tasted fresh. What really blew us away was the quality and presentation of each dish and the variety! My husband said the Caesar salad was the best ever. We especially enjoyed the chicken and waffles and fresh watermelon juice, Mmm! Be sure to leave a little room for the over the top dessert bar.  Try the chocolate covered strawberries, you won't be sorry. We look forward to returning.

My Dream Buffet, but we had to put up with a nightmare of a line to get there :( 

Almost 3 hours in line tonight, waiting to be seated.  On top of that the family was forced in to a Man vs Food timed food challenge to make our curtain for Cirque.  The staff was absolutely overwhelmed with the masses of people.  At 2.5 hours, I elected to talk to the manager; he was apologetic, and promised to check to see how much longer it would be...he never came back and left us to starve yet again.  Yes the food is wonderful, but I urge you to be strategic you make the plunge  

Pro Tip 1: Between 2-3 PM is the shortest wait time on the weekend.
Pro Tip 2: The snow crab gets scooped up quick, if you see it grab some. There is a seafood steaming station in the second room that has a fresh supply everytime.
Pro Tip 3: Take a walk about around the buffet before you dig in...everything here is top notch and could stand as menu items at the finest restaurants.  It's easy to get starstruck by all the goodies in room 1.  The Chinese walnut shrimp hidden in room 2 is in the top 3 I've ever had!!

Although the food was glorious, the experience was trumped by the poor management of the lines.  I definitely will be back though and will update.

Ummm go on a day where it's cheaper.  It's basically an all you can eat surf and turf with Asian, Italian and  Mexican dishes.  Yelp check- in gets you a complimentary glass of wine, champagne or beer.    Assumed it was a glass for each in your party, buts it's not.  Mediocre flavor.  Had much better for far less.  Sadly I can only rave about their blue cheese and the Asian baked fish (wasn't labled).  Don't think I would be coming back as trying it once was enough.  Very disappointing could have tried something else that was on our list of restaurants to try from.
What a selection!  Everything you can imagine!  Pricey but amazing!  Desserts to die for, clam chowder was exquisite
Went 4 vday, it was very good but many of the dishes werent hot but that's 2 be expected

We had a great experience for a brunch buffet. We arrived early, so no wait, a great table, and an attentive server. We were impressed by the food options too, especially the shrimp and grits, lobster eggs benedict, steak, and blueberry danish. With the amount of food and the variety available, this buffet definitely lives up to its namesake.

Brought a Groupon and was very happy with it. The amount of food that was on the menu for breakfast and brunch was mind blowing! I love sweets and was a bit disappointed with their dry and mostly coffee cake sections. The gelato was tasty and trying different flavors was cool. Our waitress was on top of things and we never sat at a table with an empty plate for long. Their green peach sweet tea is amazing! 
I would go back for brunch or even dinner because of this experience. We went around 10am and it was slow. Towards the end of our visit around noon it was starting to get busy. We didn't need to eat lunch and really had a light dinner after this hardy meal.

One of the best Buffets in town hands down. There's typically not a long wait when you come here. Standard buffet pricing for Vegas. I've been here about 4 times in total and each time I have to say that i'm impressed with the consistent quality and awesome service here. 

Give yourself a great window to browse before you start pilling the plate one. Trust me your eyes will deceive you and make you think that you can eat everything here but you can't and will regret it later lol. I always start off by taking a stroll and seeing what's on the menu. You can't go wrong with the meat cuts here. Really great stuff. One of my favorite parts has to be dessert. There's so many options and I like how the portions are considered small so you can grab a few options for dessert. 

I will be coming back here next time I'm here in Vegas. Great food, great service and decent pricing.

This place is AMAZING ! I went here on Friday night with my boyfriend around 9pm they didn't have a line at all. The girl told us food will serve until they close which was 11PM on a Friday night we said okay lets do this. 

We paid for this buffet along with the 24 hours buffet we had the total reward card so it was a bit cheaper. Total for two on Friday with the 24 hour buffet ( paid $30 extra each for this buffet ) came up to $205 and something cent.

We were seated had the server took down our drinks. We rush like animals to get food cause they were closing soon. I was surprise they had EVERYTHING still refilled !! 

Prime rib, steak ,
Lamb chop...... Oyster were fresh! Fresh juicy crab legs!! And Kobe beef burger ! What!!!!?? Delish! Also don't forget to check out the dessert place if it's your birthday tell them and they will make you a plate of their choice and write happy bday on it which is nice. When it hit 11pm all the food is put away EXCEPT dessert so yum yum. ( we went clubbing after this ... Yup not a good idea lol )
Denise is the best! She was very friendly and informative. One of the many great faces of Caesars :) definitely would come back to eat here because of her!

The buffet is amazing...the quality of food is top notch.  I am not a regular at buffets, but have experienced a couple others...no comparison.  Save room for desserts!  Grab a "made to order crepe" somewhere before the end of your meal.  What an experience!  up!

This worst buffet I have been to if I can give them 0 stars I would,the food was the worst! Ribs were burned and over cooked, hard and chewy  as the lamb was too, and crab had no flavor to it and not much variety to choose from.  Don't waste your $70.00 on this badly cooked food you will be very disappointed as I was, so sad they did not have lobster either. Very disappointed with Cesar's palace.

Luckily my friends bought the Groupon deal, it's the same price as paying in person but you do get one free drink and you get to enter through the express line. The wait is normally is 2 hours, we only waited for half an hour because we got it through Groupon.

There was a lot of food selection but everything was mediocre, nothing really stand out and a lot of the seafood I had didn't taste very fresh. There was also a huge selection of dessert which was a plus. 

Our waitress was extremely attentive and made sure to clear our plates and refill our waters despite how busy she was.

A variety of dishes. Lots of dessert to pick from. Pace yourself, each dish is good. My best friend and I, it took us about 3 hours to try at least all that was served. So far this is one of the best buffets I've tried. I'd definitely come back to.

I want to preface this review. I ate at the Bacchanal Buffet quite some time ago and had a horrible experience. Upon learning what happened, one of the managers reached out to me and offered a BOGO for dinner with a VIP pass. The BOGO dinner is what I am reviewing. 

Food: I give the buffet a 5/5 for quality of the food. There was quite a selection, most of which was fantastic. (The crab legs were way too salty). The steak I had was perfectly cooked. The desserts were plentiful and diverse, with something for everyone. There was only one thing that was mislabeled in the entire buffet. A supposedly coconut cream dessert was actually lemon. It was still delicious, but when your expecting coconut and get lemon it's a bit of a shocker. 

Ambience: This place was crowded, boy howdy!! It was very difficult to get to the food at times, but we managed. You need to be quick and snag something when there's an opening because a typical line doesn't exist. (Most buffers in Las Vegas are like this).  The tables are nicely spaced apart, so you don't feel crowded once away from the buffet line. 4/5

Service: Our waiter (I couldn't quite catch his name. It was similar to Eduardo, but I didn't get the exact spelling), was amazing! He made fantastic drink recommendations and was prompt with refills. He had one in front of me right as I took the last sip. He truly made the experience enjoyable. 5/5

Things to know: 

If we weren't set up with a VIP pass, the wait would have been close to an hour. Go early if you can. 

There are so many choices, you won't be able to eat them all. 

There is a sign requesting people limit their dining experience to no more than 2 hours. I think 2 hours is an excessive amount of time to eat (we were in and out in 30 -40 mins), but as a courtesy to the people waiting to get in, don't dilly dally. 

Try and be as laid back as possible. Despite all of the people clamoring around the food, you will get a chance to get some. Not one dish was "out of stock" at any point. 

This buffet is the best way to sample 5-star quality food without the 5-star price. The $54.99 (weekday dinner price) is reasonable considering everything you can choose from. 

Bottom line: For me, it's worth the occasional splurge.

I will never love another buffet again!! I came here with my friends for Labor Day Weekend Sunday Brunch and for about $60/person that also included unlimited mimosas, champagne and bloody marys. My friend had the mimosa and our waitress made sure that her glass was full the whole time. I love bloody marys!! It was missing celery and bacon, but no worries. I got bacon from the buffet and threw it in!! Perfection!! 

Asian breakfast, American breakfast, European breakfast, seafood and desserts!!! We definitely got out money's worth. I started off eating what felt like a trip to dim sum. Then cute little plates such as mini red velvet pancakes, steak and eggs, and lobster cake benedict... Then I had crab legs dipped in hot butter. Yummm!! 

I was so full!! I ALMOST didn't have room for dessert. The dessert bar was amazing. I definitely will make it my first stop next time. They had fruits, crepes, gelato, mini muffins, danish, croissants, egg tarts, tiramisu, chocolate bark, creme brulee, and all of the other happy happy things one would imagine in dessert-heaven. 

I definitely would recommend Bacchanal Buffet for earlier meals in the day because I would have just rolled over and crashed if we ate this for dinner. There is no way I can get pretty and hit up a night club feeling like this much of a fatty!!

If you're looking to spend a little more, for a LOT more, this is the place to go! The buffet is amazing to say the least. There's something for everyone. Highly recommend. Only downside is there's usually a wait, so if you've got some time- it's worth the wait!

I was very excited to try this extravagant and hyped up feast. But in the wise words of Public Enemy "dont believe the hype." This was a disappointing feast to say the least. A friend and I went and luckily were spared a 2 hour line and instead only waited 15 min. The staff was friendly and as we were being walked to our table the hostess showed us where everything was and gave us her recommendations. 

The selection of food is good with some unique features such as a taco stand (one of the few really good things there) and a noodle stand where they will make you ramen or pho dishes (which are just meh). Most of the food is typical buffet food which is expected to be just ok because its in fact just a buffet, but at $55 I expect a level of quality higher than the norm. I went to the carver part of the buffet and saw a good selections of meats like prime rib, roast, duck, and rack of lamb. I decided to try the lamb and regretted that decision  immediately.  It was completely inedible and that is not a word I use lightly. The meat had a taste similar to burnt rubber with a similar consistency. The dessert section was really good with a wide selection of gelato various pastries including macaroons and cheese cake pops. 

I may of just fell victim to the hype of this place and had a bitter taste in my mouth because of its failure to live up to it or the inedible food that they served,  whatever the reason I could not justify giving it above 2 stars.

I dragged my boyfriend out of bed early Saturday morning to walk 2 miles to eat here. Online review listed this place as voted "best buffet in US" but other diners have mentioned the line gets long and I wanted to beat the line. Also, I wanted to walk the 2 miles to get my appetite ready for the buffet. You can't go to a buffet without being ready to eat! Since we got there around at 9AM on a Saturday, we were seated immediately. You can't dream up places like this. 

Price: The price per person is about $50 and additional $12 if you want alcohol with your breakfast. Since it's brunch, I kind of expected some types of alcohol to go with the meal i.e. mimosa or bloody mary. 

Food: The food was delicious and plentiful. The first room starts with the seafood, which has both cold crab legs, cocktail shrimp, ceviche, and poke, as well as hot items like lobster bisque.  Then it continues to the American breakfast filled with smoked bacon, sausages (chicken, pork, etc), roast beef, grits, and many more. Some of the meats are behind the glass counter and has to be served to you by the chef working behind the counter. The service line then snakes to another room where you can get custom crepes, quiches, pizza, smoked meats and cheeses. At the end of the line are the Asian items like shumai, shrimp buns, stir fry noodles and rice, and congee with appropriate add-on items like the thousand year old egg and diced green onions. Lastly, there's a desert bar in the middle of the first room lined with fresh baked croissant, chocolate croissant, fruit, fruit cups, and almost any other kind of desert you may ever want at 9AM.

Drinks: Since we didn't want to appear to be alcoholic and be drunk by 10AM, we didn't get any of the alcoholic brunch items. The coffee was smooth with a good flavor. 

Décor: It has a very modern vibe in its decoration and furniture. They played EDM type of music and very loudly for morning. Maybe the music wouldn't be so jarring if the room is fuller with more conversation noise. But that early, it's feels like breakfast but sounds like the club. 

Conclusion: I gladly paid the high price because I figured it's a once in a long while experience. The quality of the food makes the price almost seem reasonable but it's definitely something to do only a couple of times in your life.

Wide variety but overall disappointed. Saw a cockroach crawling over the counter and put a plastic cup over it because I had no idea what to do. I didn't want to squash it all over the counter... A server pointed out that this senorita (me) had caught a cockroach with a cup to a gentleman behind the counter. I left and he came with a rag and covered the bug and proceeded to drag the rag across the countertop. I think he was trying to hide the fact there was a cockroach under the cup. I was amused

Everyone that I have met tells me that they love this buffet; I didn't have the same experience.  However, if you are a picky eater, you should go to Bacchanal, there are tons and tons and tons of choices, but I, personally, didn't love anything.  

We went for brunch, which is very costly, and felt more like lunch than brunch.  The breakfast options were limited, which was a bummer, especially when the options weren't anything special. Instead, there was a bit of eggs, a bit of sausage, a hash brown, and chicken and waffle. Yet, nothing was special, nothing had any extra flare.  These breakfast options could have been found at any breakfast buffet in any town.  

There are tons of great lunch options. Mexican, Greek, Asian, American and tons of meat. If you're a vegetarian, there are also tons of veggie options...and a salad or two.  Again, I didn't really find anything that I would want to grab again if I went back.  The coolest part was the make-your-own taco bar, I didn't partake, but that's an awesome part.

The desserts were also plentiful. Fresh fruit, ice cream, sorbet, gelato, and every type of other thing you could want..cake, pie, brownie, doughnut, etc.  Again, nothing all that great, but enough to try tons and not feel bad.

Overall, for the price, I really expected a wow factor...I guess the wow is the size..not the food.

Where do I start! The variety alone is worth the cost! It's about 60$ USD per person. There's a seafood station that serves up shellfish on ice, individual portions of grilled fish and some other hot fish dishes. Then there's a carving station that has crispy bacon, American wagyu beef, lamb, sausage and individual plates of beef bone marrow (so good!). Then comes the section divided by ethnicity: Mexican, Italian, Chinese, Japanese. All had delicious options. My personal favourite was the endless steamed crab legs with clarified butter! The best part was the dessert station. Again, so many options! There's a section for sugar free desserts which I thought was nice and actually tasted really good. They had minis of almost everything. Some of my personal favourites were: pineapple upside down cake, lava cake, cheesecake, tiramisu and ofcourse the fresh crepe and gelato station.
The line up to get looks intimidating but moves fairly quickly and the services is really good. Friendly staff and table gets cleared pretty frequently (you go through a lot of plates). I've been twice and I will definitely go back!

2 star for neatness, decor, and jar honey for the tea. I came to the buffet expecting a be "wowed" due to so many good reviews on here and from family and friends. However, the experience did not live up to the hype and price paid. My boyfriend and I are truly disappointed. Lots of cultural/ethnic food choices but most of the food was old, cold, and soggy. The best thing I ate was a taco. If you are going here expecting a variety of sushi rolls or nigiri, do NOT go here.  Will not be returning when we come back to Vegas.

Garbage and service has gone down to an Applebee's type of venue! Waited 10 minutes before and were never acknowledged. Went to manager and she seemed uninterested in really assisting. Noticed they didn't check me in from opentable and was told we don't check people in and we just use their service. For $100 buffet?!?! I've gotten better service on food trucks, don't waste your money!!!

I had the full splurge for the VIP option, after pouring over reviews for Vegas buffets. I really wanted to give this place at least 4 stars, but a tremendous amount of items tasted as though they were sitting out too long. Their Italian food area really is worth avoiding completely as their Stromboli tasted as though it was spoiled. Their fish selections were dry from being under a heat lamp too long, but could have been great if they were made in smaller batches. Their Wagyu beef could have easily been regular Angus prime for as forget-able as it was. I did appreciate Josephine (Jo) as she was highly attentive and the dessert items were great, but truly lacking for the price point of almost $100 a person for the VIP experience.

Crab legs is only on weekdays dinner and weekend lunch/dinner: subject to change during holidays. Now-a-day, buffet in Vegas is not that good anymore. Crab legs here is tasteless now. They have cold/warm ones. The warm-up (locating towards the Asian foods) snow crab is a tad better, but still not that great considering the $ we paid. My 1st choice: Clam chowder/crab bisque/tuna poki/matcha gelato and green tea mousse. 2nd would be: oyster shooters/scallops Japanese mayonnaise/shrimp cocktail/ube (purple) gelato and creme brulee. Overall, bacchanal buffet has more ethnic foods variety then other buffet in Vegas.
There's a 1 hour wait and the food is great. There are about 15 different vegetarian dishes and I love most of them.

Holy gluttony yelp crusaders!!! Seafood on ice: crab legs, shrimp, oysters, a taste of sushi  but nothing exciting as far as that's concerned: spicy tuna, shrimp and California rolls. Chinese food, Pho, steamed clams, a touch of pasta, tacos made on demand. Carving station with Waygu beef, brisket, tri tip, prime rib, roasted turkey, fried chicken and fries served individually in little baskets. The most memorable things for me were the fancy deviled eggs and individual wedge salads. It was a good buffet Nd I barely made it to dessert. Think you could get more variety at other buffets. 119 bucks for 2 people. Tips: gravy & bbq spouts spit out hot sauce. They recommend a tip so good to write it in when you pay if using a card otherwise will need a new ticket or will have to go back to ATM. Also if you gamble you can get discounts with a players card.

I've been here about 4 times now and I feel like the quality is not as good as before. Part of my group were able to get nigiri but by the time I went to that section there was no more. I waited a few minutes and even went by a second and third time but still no nigiri. Also, sometimes the carving station is not so good. My cut of the tri tip was super tasty but the others in my group said theirs was dry. 

I would definitely still go back but I need to try wicked spoon!

I came here for lunch. There is definitely a wide variety of food, such as Japanese, American, Italian, etc. I felt that a lot of the food was way too salty. All the Asian soups were way too salty. I enjoyed the tempura shrimp udon noodle bowl, but again the soup was very salty. One of my favorites was the mushroom arugula pizza! The tomato bisque was pretty good. Some of the more unique items like the lobster egg Benedict dish, lacked flavor. The mini orange smoothie was also way too sweet. There aren't a lot of vegetable choices if you are vegetarian. Even the potatoes had bacon I believe. The Caesar salad lacked flavor and the rest of the salad options didn't look great. There were plenty of meat options though , from sliders to fried chicken to several different types of meat you can have cut in front of you. My husband enjoyed the brisket. I found the tri tip to be just ok. The best part of the meal was dessert! I really enjoyed the mini key lime pie and this sugared cube of strawberry rhubarb. For the price and quality of food, I would not come back.

In the food industry, service is everything. It looks like the Bacchanal Buffet at Caesars Palace fails to understand even this.

This is a review purely based on their reservation system. 

I've been a longtime patron of Caesars. Not necessarily a high roller, but I burn hundreds if not thousands here. I've been to the buffet many times. Fantastic food.

What's most important to me is that a business upholds whatever promise it claims to deliver. I thought the Bacchanal was truly unique among Las Vegas buffets for this as it allowed patrons to put their name on a virtual queue in advance in order to save unnecessary wait time. I'm glad that in this modern society, we have a business actually willing to skirt the very much unnecessary psychological trap of more people waiting = good restaurant (though I admit this is a very effective trap).

That's in theory. In reality, what Caesars Entertainment did was say "oh cool, but we have a lot of people here today, go to the end of the line."

This is not okay. If you make a guarantee, no matter how difficult it is to do so, you have to follow through or at least offer some message of consolation. Rendering the virtual queue useless just because your physical queue is too long is not how this works. 

Extremely disappointed. I'm taking my business elsewhere. The strip is long.

TIP: I prefer Wicked Spoon or Bellagio, good eats and don't go back on their word.

TLDR; if you want cold and hot crab legs on end, get them here! No oysters though. 

For about $70 pp, before tip, there's a huge variety of foods to try. Most everything is on the "innovative" side but not worth more than a few bites. Skip over any of the veggies and go for the UDON + short rib ravioli. Dessert bar is pretty sick as they have tons of desserts infused with asian flavors.

Update: my friends and I got the bad case of the runs from something here- be careful what you eat!

Ok ok dont forget its  BUFFET first off... For BUFFET food it was SALMMIN!!! We arrived around 6/7 and the wait wasnt that bad. We walked around first since there was so many sections and do whatever we wanted. We returned to the table ordered drinks then it was a non stop feast! LOL... 
1. Seafood- chilled shrimp, raw oysters, sea snails, cold crab legs, etc. 
2. Seafood paella, Mexican food, tacos to order tacos and topping bar. which includes tortilla chips, rice, beans, and etc 
3. Next station was the meat station where they had slabs of meat that chefs would cut off for you. They had wagyu steak, brisket, pork, and turkey. I was very surprised that the brisket was really good! The bone marrow was ok, they added some crunchy stuff on top and some pomegranate seeds. The sliders were good and the lobster mac & cheese could have been a little cheesier a little watery for my taste. 
4. Near the Asian station go here for HOT crab legs, across the way they had Chinese food different dim sums, inside steam baskets as well as roasted duck, roasted pork, fried rice, etc Then come the small sushi bar with Salmon nigiri, spicy tuna rolls, etc not too much on sushi selection. 
5. Then desserts: Different cupcakes, macarons, rice krispy treats, 31 ice cream flavors "just kidding", creme brulee, and cut fruit. 
So YES overall for around $60 plus not bad of a deal for ALL the food you can eat and the choices... Well worth it! Just crab legs alone is $100 per person on a good day!

ラスベガスに行ったらバッフェに！
少しお値段高めですが、こちらは種類の多さ、美味しさ、どれも良かったです！

わたし達が行った日は待ち時間も五分程で案内され、スタッフの方々の対応も丁寧でした！

どの料理も目を引くような盛り付け方や、彩りがよく、みているだけでもワクワクします。

私は、野菜料理ばかり食べましたが、シーフードも美味しかったと家族が言っていました。

また食べに行きたいと思えるバッフェでした！

Visited on the Monday after new years @10:45am. No wait for the line. Paid for breakfast at $67 for 2 people, even tho lunch starts in 15 minutes, score!

Honestly to say, I stayed for a little over 2 hours and the food between breakfast & lunch did not change much. Only the omelettes and toasts got taken out and replaced with sliders.

Foods of what I can recall:

SEAFOOD section: Jonah crab claws, roasted mussels, shrimp, mini shrimp cups (no oysters or crab legs *sadface*)
*crab claws and shrimp was the standout!

COMFORT FOOD section: mac n cheese, bread, bacon, omelettes, sliders, fries and fried chicken
*Bacon wass awesomeeeee! Sliders are salty.

DRINK section: watermelon, orange, carrot, cucumber juice
* Watermelon juice is love! 

MEAT CARVING STATION: Tri tip, assortment of sausages, prime rib
*meat was yummy, not very warm & not great enough to get 2nds

ITALIAN section: Variety of pastas and huge meatballs

CHEESE section: lots of different block of cheeses

STEW section: 3 different variety of stews

SLICED MEAT section: Ham, salami, etc. The thin slices that goes great with wine

JAPANESE section: minimal sashimi and rolls
*Sashimi is not melt in your mouth good, but it's above average for a buffet

SOUP section: chef makes you udon soup, pho, etc.

CHINESE section: peking duck, dim sum, buns, congee, hot & sour soup, turnip cake
*chinese donut was bomb! Don't get the dim sum stuff, quality is decent but not exceptional like regular dim sum places.

DESSERT section: gelato, cake pops, macarons, crepes, cakes
* Out of this world! felt like I was in a candy shop 


Overall the only standout to me was the huge variety of desserts available and some seafood and bacon. Majority of the food was too typical for buffet (i.e. comfort food section), over salted, or wasn't flavorful enough. Sad that I don't get the fancier stuff like dinner (I want oysters and crab legs dangit!) but I guess that's what the price difference and 2 hour wait is for.

A-ok in my book. But not my favorite buffet in Las Vegas.

The food here is not well prepared or fresh.  This is a tourist trap.  They are charging a high price since this buffet is part of famous hotel in vegas, otherwise they would not get much business for the good or service that they provide.

This is the best buffet available in Vegas IMHO. I thought I'd written a review but just noticed I hadn't. The quality of food is great, and I love that their snow crabs are already pre-cut for ease when eating. There's none of that hardcore cracking and digging to find meat, plus crab bits flying into your face, hair, and clothes. Cuz that's super hot. 

The line was a bit crazy, as we went on a three day weekend, and they jack up the price a bit for special holidays so keep in mind to check your price on those national holidays.

The fried food section wasn't as good as I had anticipated. Love the cool metal wire baskets, but the presentation was superior to the taste. The desserts were alright. Here is where I have to give it to wicked spoon--they shine more on desserts. 

Ambiance is gorgeous, and it's definitely a must-try on the strip. Service is great, and not too shabby for a date or a stuffing fest with large groups.

The food and service was not what I expected. Waiting time was extremely long and there was a waiter dropped the dishes purposely in front of us. Overall, it's not worth it to pay 70 dollars have a normal dinner in weekends night.

Probably the best buffet on the strip. 
Not too much of a seafood options for lunch. No crab legs etc. But there are other great options. 
Right now they are offering a free drink if you check in on yelp, but you have to show your phone to the waitress and she has to activate the offer. The fun part is that she came back and asked me to show her a 5 star review, which was a little too much ... 
the deserts are very beautiful, but many of them tasted similar...
Still the best buffet on the strip...

If this is what heaven is like then I'm going to be good for the rest of my life (minus the whole lesbian thing hahaha) so that I can get in!! This buffet had EVERYTHING, it gave me life and I did not have to eat again until literally the next day. It was hot and fresh with bottomless mimosas and every type of food you could want. Carved meats, asian station, tacos, italian, cheese and breads, gelato, tiramisu, creme brulee, lobster and crab...Jesus H. Christ...we went for brunch on a Sat, checked in and then left to play some slots to kill time. showed back up at our ticketed time and were seated in less than 10 minutes. The servers were nice, clearing plates fast and filling our glasses. It's definitely not cheap but if you like high quality food in a gorgeous space then this is the place for you. I plan on visiting this place every time i'm in Vegas

maybe because I had expected more.

maybe because I had heard they served tomahawk steaks
but then they didn't.

maybe because Bacchanal fell victim to my cognitive dissonance
of a quality selection versus a variety of quantity.

Whatever the reason maybe
I was not impressed.

That's to say it wasn't good,
Bacchanal is a very good buffet.

The layout of the seating is
quite comfortable
and cozy when
considering the size of the place.

The steamed king crab legs were hella tasty

Lamb chops were also superb.

And overall, the quality of the food

And if you are planning on having

for less.

And there the rub.

Where are these place you may ask?

Check out my Vegas list on Yelp
(which I'm continually compiling and updating
as we speak)
or look for upcoming link
to my blog eatery.

Last time we came here the oysters were horrible I only come to bacchanal just for their oysters. Mentioned to the manager he had chef brought a plate from the back personally by chef himself. Kind gesture but oysters was so bad I didn't eat any of it. I didn't spend almost $300 for four to get bad oysters. Been here at least nearly every time we go to vegas

We had the opportunity to visit this buffet on Mother's Day weekend. I can say our experience here was a good one I indulged with the steamed crab legs. The Mac n Cheese was very tasty and the deserts were decorated with detail. Not bad with how they tasted but they looked tastier than what they actually looked. They had a good variety of dishes to pick from. It was on the high side for a buffet at $65 each but since it had good reviews It was on our must try on our bucket list.. Any plate at a mid to upscale restaurant will run you $$35 to $60+. Some dishes aren't for everyone as in many Buffets the upside is the choice and variety. My Girlfriend is a bit picky with food and didn't find a lot of the plates appetizing and for that reason I gave it 4 stars..
