URGENT!!!!!! A guy was harassed by the manger because a dumb hostess accused him of not sitting at the table and he was a fraud.  He was Chinese.  Minorities are not treated well here.  I expect a response to this post. So think twice before you go here. Firstly, horrible system and service.  Since these poorly prepared people do not take a reservation, we have to wait in long lines when the lines don't move. They are disorganized.   At this rate I would rather cook the food myself.  Also it looks like this restraunt will go out of business soon if they keep this up.  Will never come here again and I advise u all the same.
A lot to choose from, but not much flavor. Overpriced. Sorry this was my buffet choice in Vegas.

Went at 11am, there was so much variety and we got a little bit of the breakfast and lunch menu. The asian selection was pretty good, the latin selection was awesome. Came too early for crab legs but overall pretty fulfilling experience.

I use these reviews so I wanted to share our experience. The food was cold and no where worth $110 for 2 people. I'm sorry we made the hike and paid the price to come here. It was cold and just did not taste what I expected based on previous reviews. Skip it.

So basically waited in line for 1.5 hours watching groups of 5-12 people passing up the line just because they are large groups and they get called up to pay and get in the SECOND hour long line to be seated.
The people are nice who work here but come on.
A single person waiting for 3 hours to eat is uncalled for when parties of 5+ get to eat in 45 mins or less.
No VIP no nothing.
Sorry but you just lost my current and future patronage.

The place: 9/10 The line for our dinner wasn't that bad, about a 10-15 minute wait on a Thursday night. It's pretty dimly lit towards the night time in some areas of the space. All of the food is neatly sectioned region to region. 

The food: 9/10 The dessert section was probably my favorite section! Everything looked and tasted AMAZING. I didn't give this part a 10/10 just because the crab legs were what I was the most excited about but when I got there, the pieces were already cut. It makes everything easier but the portion of the legs were much smaller and less satisfying. None the less, the shrimp was also a star for me, they were HUMONGOUS! 

Price: 10/10 $60 per person! Not too bad for Vegas prices!! 

Definitely would say this is on the "more affordable" side of Las Vegas luxury buffets so its a must try!

Utterly fantastic!  Tip 1) wear low or no heels only... even with a high tier pass to skip the first line, everyone has to stand on that hard floor for awhile in the 2nd line.  Just don't put your precious feet through that.  2). Eat smart.  If you don't LOVE something that's offered, skip it.  You can't possibly try Everything so save your stomach room for what you truly love to eat.  3) everything is wonderful and it's all you can eat, so don't hold back.  I tasted literally 60% of the offered desserts.  I filled 3 heaping plates of dessert.  Most memorable:  lemon tart, lava cake, lemon basil sorbet, chocolate gelato, bread pudding, raspberry cobbler, donut... actually everything, except the cupcakes.  They were so so.  4) get in line for the carved meats.  Don't let it deter you from getting out-of-this-world prime rib, mashed potatoes and fried chicken 5) The poke' here is excellent and so is the salmon sushi.  6) the cheeses are hard to find, so scout those out- worth the hunt 7) sweet potato tater tots are a thing.  At least at Bacchanel,  and you won't be able to stop eating them once you start 8) take pictures of your food.  You will remember this meal Forever.  I promise

AMAZING!!
One of the best buffets I have been to in Vegas, I've been to many.
The food is amazing, the flavors are on point. The variety is so much and it's simply amazing. 
I was surprised to see a ramen and udon station at the buffets which was some new. There was honestly everything you want to eat.
The desserts were a different story OMG! Where do I even start???? The flavors burst in the mouth, the mango and lime dessert are simply (I have no words)
Try it, you won't regret it!

We did the VIP experience, made a reservation through Open Table. HIGHLY HIGHLY HIGHLY SUGGEST RESERVATIONS. Otherwise you WILL wait In A 2-3 hour line and even then Possibly NOT get in.

This is one of the highest rated buffets in Las Vegas, it did not disappoint. 
The VIP service comes with a seafood tower and all you can drink. I was expecting something like some shrimp and cocktail sauce....but this was EXTRA. Here is what it included

4 - lobsters
Dozens  - king crab
Dozen - another crab not sure what it was
Dozens - oysters 
Dozens - sea snails
A MOUND of shrimp
Lots of cocktail sauce, horseradish and butter.
FREAKING BOMB.

I'd love to go back and try their breakfast this was for dinner. We had gone up and grabbed a few things from the Buffett and they were all really good. But the tower MADE IT. I had grabbed a few oysters, crawfish, cooked salmon, 2 crab legs, salad and some Mac and cheese. They were super yummy but the crab legs were definitely not as fresh as the ones in the tower. They pump the seafood out real quick but these just tasted a lot better on the tower. 

The dessert. Ermygerd. Favorite was the blueberry cobbler and the chocolate lava cake....but I literally tried everything. So so good. 

TOTALLY TRY IT!

I haven't been to every buffet in Vegas but, this is one is awesome!  We went for breakfast which they refer to as "brunch".  There are so many things to choose from. You can have breakfast or lunch or both!
Yes, this one is very pricey but worth it!  Go hungry!  You won't be sorry!
Not worth the wait!!! No consideration for infant. They let  everyone pass us in line. Food is basically aria with more selection only.

I love this buffet, and have been several times. I was a little disappointed that scallops were not an option on my last trip, and I found the ribs to be over seasoned but apart from that the food was fantastic. I was there 11/03/2015 for dinner.

My two stars comes from the fact that there was a roach on the dessert table.  We were seated right next to it, and as I was eating I watched it make it's way from the top of the table where the food was down the tiled sideboard and onto the floor towards my table. I pointed it out to my husband and he stomped on it.

I would have mentioned it to the waiter, as my appetite completely left, but he only ever came back once to grab our plates while my husband was grabbing another plate of food (the roach didn't bug him) and I was in the bathroom. 

Sadly, this one time favorite is now no longer an option. The price they expect should assure a bug free meal, but that was not the case.

What can I say about this buffet that hasn't been said already which would drown in the sea of all the other reviews?

Known for the notorious wait time and prices, Bacchanal Buffet definitely meets that expectation with the predicted 1 hour wait which isn't too bad since you can drink in line and the price is about $70 for dinner.

The interesting thing about this buffet is that there are some items that are just plain terrible (The wagyu was chewy and bad). On the other hand, the short rib ravioli, the big juicy ribs, the prime rib and the seafood can be pretty awesome. You really need to scope out the good items to make it worth your money. The funny thing is that my friends and I agreed that the Chinese food is pretty good although it would be considered cheap.

Dessert wise, there are a lot of options and it is kind of away from the rest of the food so don't miss it! My recommendation is definitely don't get the egg tart here. It should be killed with fire.

This was our last buffet for our stay in Vegas.  Why not go big?  My sister heard about the Bacchanal and said we should meet here.  When I went to the kiosk (why does everyone in a party have to go to the kiosk together? So crowded!) it only allowed to check-in 4 guests.  So I asked this woman standing near the kiosks what do I do...

She: How many do you have?
Me: 6
She: Are they all here?
Me: No
She: When they are all here, come back and see me.

I will have to agree, it looks crazy chaotic in the 1-4 guest lines.  There's also a line for Caesar's palace club members, and what also may be a high roller line.  When we were all present I went back to the friendly woman, who turned to another woman at the 5+ line.

She: The wait is about 3 hours, are you okay with that?
Me: Sure, I've never been here.

My mom was like "three hours?" But I'm like, we're already here so why not?  After waiting about 5 minutes, a cashier came to the line and said it would be about 2 hours, "Is that ok?"  Look, we already shaved off 1 hour!  As I'm paying, we started talking about waiting tables and people complaining and we laughed.  

She: You'll have to be present since you're the one paying.  I say 2 hours as a guesstimate, it could be less.
Me: No worries.  I totally understand

So we go and wait in this other line with two families ahead of us.  30 minutes later, a woman called my name and told us to follow her.  We shaved off another 1 1/2 hours.  They gave us a nice round table in the back near the cold crab legs and Asian foods.  Our server who took care of us was great!

My favorites: roast duck, brisket, shrimp, tri-tip, gelato

I also liked their pizza and fried chicken.  Didn't have enough room for the sliders or spicy sausage.  I also tried the mini pecan pie and chocolate pie which were great!  I didn't care for the Chinese egg custard tart, it was good, but not like the ones in Chinatown.

Overall, a very fun and delicious experience!  I feel sorry for all the others who weren't happy.  It's the waiting that makes them hangry and then they have to write about it.  Here's a suggestion: GO WITH A GROUP OF 5 OR MORE!  Your wait time is practically nothing!  Although, when we left, even that line was long.  3-4 pm is an ideal time for groups!

Sure the price might be steep for some, but to be with my family, eating some really tasty food, is priceless!  Especially during the holidays! I would definitely come back, but only with a group of 5 or more.

Happy New Year Bacchanal!

Food is really bad - quality of meat is very disappointing 
Oyster can be better 
Crab is salty, other selections are below average 

Service is okay 

Don't know why this buffet got 4 stars

Food doesn't justify the price

Overall very disappointing 

Will not go back

Came here for lunch around 1 on a Friday. There was no line and no wait to get a table. I saw a lot of reviews saying ppl waited two hours so I would say if you don't have an exact time and day you have to go then just leave if there's a long line and come back later. You pay first, came out to $100 including tax and tip for two people so around $40/person base price. I think the lunch is completely fine, they had plenty of seafood and Dungeness crab legs and rock crab claws that were delicious. I guess for dinner they bring out oysters and king crab? I'm not sure. Our server was very friendly but I think she was a little overworked so she wasn't able to come around that much to refill our waters. Our busser was working super hard though and I never came back to a dirty plate on the table. 

Overall I would say there wasn't any dish that was mindblowing but there wasn't a single bad dish either. This is a really solid buffet choice if you want something of everything all in one place. If you have picky eaters too this could be a good choice since there is so much variety. There's an asian food section, which was quite good, pizza, appetizers, carving station, sushi, fried chicken/southern food, seafood, desserts, and some brunch items and more probably that I'm forgetting. The pho was actually quite good and they boil the noodles fresh for you. You have a choice of several types of noodles soups as well.  The sushi was pretty good but I didn't want to fill up on rice. The poke was also quite good. All the meats from the carving station were pretty good. 

I tried to focus more on seafood so I didn't fill up. Both crab types were quite good. The prawns were also quite good. The desserts were average but I think their bread pudding was really good. 

Overall I had a good experience here. It's probably one of the best buffets I've been to in terms of quality and selection but don't expect any one dish to blow your mind. 

I know this place and Wicked Spoon are often called the best buffets so in comparison I would say Bacchanal is better. It is about $10 more expensive but you get twice as much selection it feels like and everything is worth a try. Whereas at Wicked Spoon I just felt very limited in what I wanted to eat. Also overall the quality of the food at Bacchanal was better in my opinion. If I had to choose between one or the other I would choose Bacchanal.

Let's start off 2019 with a BIG BUFFET BANG!!  Unfortunately I have to give this big boy buffet a bit of a downgrade.

Mom was visiting from Maui and wanted to eat a 'fancy' buffet - of course it meant Bacchanal Buffet was one of the fanciest ones we knew!  We ended up having a bit of a big family get together!  Like 10 of us ended up going for Sunday Brunch!  Eating party to commence!

Dude, what happened to the Bacchanal - the buffet to end all buffets?  Maybe it was me, but wow some things were a bit off this time around to the buffet at Caesar's.  Then again I haven't been back here in over a year maybe.  Lineup at the front was off.  Service was off.  Heck, even the food was a bit off!  OUCH!!  If we seriously are paying like near $60 a head after tax & tip for their Sunday Brunch - I kinda wanna be impressed!

We waited in line for longer than I expected, even though on Sunday the line really wasn't that long.  Being that we were a large party the 18% or so gratuity was automatically added to our bill.  However - no clue why they tried to sit our party on separate tables that weren't even really close to each other!  We saw one of those long tables with the privacy glass all around it by the dessert area like wide open - and it sat 10-12 people.  Why not give our family some privacy, eh Caesar's?  We ended up on a large round table that sat 10 of us - rather uncomfortably.  Close quarters!

Bacchanal Buffet needs to do better at both their seafood line & carved meats line.  Such a cluster**ck!!  You seriously have to wait it either line for 10 minutes or more to get some food!  Plus, if you want to just get in there to get other items off the line - it's such an inconvenience.  People think you're cutting the line when all you want is a slider, or some paella!  I had to wave through folks to even get me some horseradish sauce.  Kinda silly!

Look - I know it's a massive operation to run Bacchanal on a daily basis, but this time the food for me was just kinda MEH.  I mean, I think the quality on some of the items took a bit of a dive here.  The dim sum in the Chinese section seemed to have been sitting for way too long (and I'm not normally picky on dim sum) so they were dry, and some of the rolls in the sushi section were easily falling apart.  The Mexican and Italian sections seemed to be lackluster and partially empty during our entire meal there.

Thankfully the seafood like the crab legs were in constant supply, as well as the various cuts of meats.  I had a few crabs legs and they were tasty, and the meats were tender and flavorful as well.  Only problem again was the long, disorganized lines.

Also, the cured meats & cheeses section was on par - probably one of the most priciest sections of the buffet!  I believe I also had at least 3 Black Truffle Deviled Eggs - delicious!  But I don't come here to indulge on appetizers, gimme the mains!  And this visit the mains just didn't stack up!  I just wasn't impressed.

The desserts section was a sweet lover's dream - still full of all kinds of fun, creative treats.  Crepes are always a good choice, as well as the addition of ube gelato!  That was tasty!

Another big issue we had was the lack of service!  We already paid a hefty gratuity beforehand, and at least some decent service should have been supplied.  Our server took forever to get our drink order done, then hardly came by to check on us and get us refills!  We went short on beverages and napkins multiple times during our meal.  I mean, I know we weren't status VIP but come on now...you gonna just ignore us for the big sharks?  That was a huge thumbs down.

Overall it was just average this time around at Bacchanal Buffet.  I really wanted to impress my Mom for her 1st visit here but it was just frustrating.  The uncomfortable table seating, the average food, and the lackluster service really put a damper on things.  And believe me, the value just isn't there - it's expensive for all those shortcomings!  Get a grip Bacchanal Buffet, your locals should be near the top of your list!  We're the ones that suggest the buffets!

The rules of Vegas-cations:
1. Never go on a holiday wkd
2. Never go to buffets on Sundays (especially new ones! Best to come here on a weekday, even Friday afternoon)
3. Know your limit! Or don't but don't get your Friends kicked out of the club with you and have to ride in a cab with your grossness

Yes! New fave. 8gajillion times better than wicked spoon. Worth the price! First of all atmosphere is amazing, and presentation is squeal-inducingly cute. Fresh juices in cute carafes, dim sum in mini steamers, tater tots in mini fry baskets. I die. Yes everything here is amazing, taste everything, photo and insta it all. 

They give Togo cups for your after dinner coffee. Fresh baked bread, donuts, muffins, a taco man, salsa bar, cheese bar, cold cut assortment. The one downside is that all of the adorable individual portions make it hard to put a lot on your plate. Or maybe that's another plus cuz you gotta walk around more and work it out to eat! Seafood was decent (fresh at least) and meats are tender and flavorful. The Asian food is the weakest. My guess is because good ole Asian food is better when a little dirty. Hehe. 

Desserts look like they've been food styled.... And they're decent with the exception of those noted below under must trys. Creme brûlée is a little watery but really great flavor. Bread pudding a little too dry. Same goes for cupcake (mad buttercream is blah). Panna cotta has too much preserve-y stuff on top. Caramel pudding too dense. 

But here are the must try's- watermelon fresh squeezed juice, broccoli cheese casserole, tacos, tropical mango cake, chocolate mousse with passion fruit.

Yummilicious factor = A

When you're half-sober and you're preparing for a long night out in Vegas and you know you're going to be starving later... you stuff your purse with parmesan truffle fries. SORRY! Not my finest hour.

I love Bacchanal, I love the variety and the quality of each food. I love how the foods are sectioned off, from seafood to meats, to fries, to desserts, pizza, Asian foods, and more. 

Bacchanal has a large wait time for a large price. Luckily, that wait time and price is well worth it (if you remember, parmesan truffle fries). Save your stomach and wear stretchy pants because you WILL feel disgusting afterwards.

After two failed attempts to make it to bacchanal for dinner my next attempt was for their weekend brunch. Show up by 11am for lunch like we did and there definitely is a long line already, but if you have a group of six or more, tell the lady by the kiosks and you'll get moved to a way shorter line! Win! The wait was maybe 15-20 minutes and only two other parties were ahead of us. 

Okay guys the variety here is insane. Especially for brunch, since you get all the typical breakfast foods (pancakes, eggs, bacon, sausage, French toast) but you also get all the lunch offerings as well! There's dim sum, noodles, fried rice, a congee station (porridge), sushi, nigiri, hand rolls, laksa, seafood pasta, pizza, muffins, crab legs galore, and all different types of meat for the carnivores out there.   I've seen other reviews mention a comparison to hometown buffet and I could not disagree more. This buffet is one of the cleanest and most organized I have ever seen. And they have charcuterie stations with as much cheese and dried meats as you could want! Add the bottomless mimosas for $7 and you're all set!

Make sure you save room for the desserts though, specifically the Thai tea boba shot with coconut ice cream. I'm in love. This is the perfect way to end your meal, or in my case, to cleanse the palette before going back for thirds..or was it fourths.. For future reference, you have to order this at the ice cream section of the desserts! Otherwise you'll end up just circling the dessert bar over and over to find it. But it was worth the wait! 

For $50pp for weekend brunch, it seems a little steep but you guys won't be disappointed. They don't compromise quality for the variety of the food and it really pays off!

This was my first time having a dinner buffet here at Bacchanal (I wasn't too impressed with the lunch last time). I totally can say 100% that the dinner is so much more worth it! The price difference is minimal but the food selection was better, at least in my opinion. Brunch/ lunch buffet on the weekends were $49.99 excluding taxes and fee but dinner is an additional $10, at $59.99 excluding taxes and fee. 

And I also highly suggest getting the all-you-can-drink package for $15 - it was so worth it!!! As you already know, purchasing alcohol there are pricey so $15 was an amazing choice. The package includes bottomless mimosas, house red and white wine as well as draft beer. And I bet you would want some wine or mimosas to go with all those meats and seafood available at the buffet.

The variety of food available here are wonderful. At the most right of the buffet line up are the wide selection of Asian food. There are some dimsum items (shumai, hargao, charsiu buns). These were okay, they aren't great but they aren't bad. There are other Asian dishes like Thai Panang curry, Indian curry, stir fry as well. Then you progress to the Japanese food section which includes things like sushi rolls, miso soup and seaweed salad. I do not recommend the rolls however. There are also a selection of made to order noodle dishes such as Pho and ramen as well. 

The salads here are great! Every single type of salad I've tried tasted fresh and had good flavor. And the fruits are very fresh as well. 

Then there is the meat buffet that include steaks, ribs, BBQ, fajitas, tacos and bone marrow! Pretty good stuff but sometimes the meat are too dried out. You have to understand they have to cook large amount of food to provide for all of us in the buffet and all those people lining up hours to get in. But the food is always warm. 

The highlight though, is definitely the seafood. I sort of wish they also have sashimi (a girl can dream right?). But unlimited (chilled) CRAB LEGS and oysters! This is what most people come here for. The cocktail shrimps are great too (juicy, sweet and big) and also big juicy sea snails. There are also things like seafood paella, grilled salmon on mashed potatoes, escargot in garlic sauce (love that garlicky flavor) and oysters shooters (the sauce was a little too overpowering). 

The desserts, however, are subpar. Great selection, but mostly wayyyyyyyyyyyyyyy too sweet. The creme brulee and chocolate covered strawberries are probably that only thing I'd recommend. There are gelatos which were decent. But the rest wasn't great. 

Overall, I think the food was great. Obviously you don't come here for 5 star quality tasting food, you come for the quantity. But overall the food tasted pretty good. Certain dishes are better than other but you can tell they are carefully crafted. Definitely worth the price, and I'd still say this is the best buffet in Vegas for their superior quality. 

TIP1: Be sure to be there much earlier than when you plan on eating. You're going to have to go enter your party size and get a ticket. The ticket will tells you what time to come back (we got an hour and a half wait time). KEEP THE TICKET! Once you come back, show the ticket to the host in front of the line. You line up (which could then also add about extra half an hour depending on the day and time) before you are seated.

TIP2: To be honest, the two hour limit FLIES BY! Sometimes you have to wait in line to get certain dishes you want. Don't stuff yourself by eating super fast, but pace yourself so you can get to try everything.

TIP3: Wait for the next batch when you see them low on certain type of dishes. Because you'll get much fresher and better tasting food than getting the food at the bottom of the serving bowls/ plates. For example, you'll be able to get those juicy, big crab legs and enormous oysters if you wait for the next batch. I promise, it's much more worth it. 

TIP4: As mentioned, their desserts arent the best. So maybe save that extra room for the crab legs and booze?

Check out my pictures on here and IG @dreammieeee

I can't tell you how long I have been waiting to go here. I heard the hype when it opened and I kept saying "I need to make it over to Bacchanal"....and then 2 years passed lol

I came here last week for an impromptu lunch and it was heavenly. If you have the opportunity to obtain a Diamond Total Rewards card (either as a player or via Founder's Card, like me) utilize it. You get your own separate line at the entrance, which consisted of zero people when I went. No wait. It also gets you UNLIMITED MIMOSAS. Yes. That certainly made our lunch far more enjoyable. 

We enjoyed too many delicious bites. Some of my favorites were:

guacamole
sweet potato fries
pho
rice and black beans
stone crab claws
stracciatella gelato
pumpkin cheesecake
nutella crepe (made to order)

Lunch for 2 costed us $63 + we left cash tip on the table. The waitress was so kind and kept our mimosas filled. Do it. Come here on a weekday for lunch and have fun :)

I think this place is overrated and way too expensive for what you can actually eat. This was my second time coming while in Vegas the first time was better than the second the one thing that's kinda worth it is the ribs tri tip and oysters my sister loved the jambalaya

We went to other buffet place but it was disappointed since the food was not fresh. so we decided to come to satisfy our Vegas buffet experience lol. Fresh seafood! And a lot of food and dessert selections! Already recommended to a friend who has Vegas trip coming up.

Highly recommend the Bacchanal Buffet for a delicious brunch. I came back for another try and this time I had so many favorite dishes. the hash brown ham and biscuit was so good I had to get it twice. Another one of my favorite dishes was steak and eggs. They also had a variety of potato which enjoyed. Everything was warm and fresh. Our servers were very friendly like always and they were able to accommodate us with the baby stroller. They kept our table clean the whole time. As a whole the place is kept tip top clean even the floors looked shiny. Brunch and dinner are two whole different experiences. But both equally good. Although did enjoy this time brunch a bit more. The place was full and yet they still kept the food coming and everything neat and organized. The desserts area is like a rainbow. A wide variety of colors from fruit tarts to donuts, macaroons and even an interesting dessert I had for the first time called Vietnamese coffee, elegantly decorated with a gold chocolate coffee bean. To end this wonderful and flavorful experience I got an Oreo cupcake. Best oreo cupcake Ive tried. The frosting was delicious not too sweet just the right amount of sweetness to end my meal. I see myself coming to brunch here more often. Oh and I recommend you give the horchata a try it's very yummy something about it it's so refreshing and different than any other horchata Ive tried. Which explains why you see them refilling it constantly. I'm very pleased with this buffet and I must try for those that come visit.

This was our second time, and we are were even more impressed this time! There were so many selections and all of them looked amazing. Our server Socorro M was so sweet and took great care of us! 10/10 recommend!
Lot of choice, different styles, good service, even need to wait for a long time. Deserts look pretty and yummy

The Best of the Best.  The Lord of the Rings.  You are not going to find a better buffet in Vegas. You wont find a better buffet anywhere in the world! The Bacchanal Buffet is it, seriously one of the best eating experiences I've ever had.  I cant think of a better buffet that I have been too, or any meal better than this.  This buffet is located in Ceaser's palace.  We checked in on a Friday night and headed straight for the buffet.  The line and wait wasn't too bad, we wanted for about 30 minutes.  It was 55 per person and for two people it came out to 120.00.  Pretty expensive, but the amount of seafood I ate, it was well worth it.  1st of all the buffet is pretty big and long.  I would encourage you to take a long before you grab a place.  There's different sections, such as Chinese, Sushi, Italian, American, etc.  The most impressive was the seafood section.  They had fresh oysters, split open crab legs, stone crab claws, shrimp, ceviche, etc.

The quality of the food was excellent.  Every tastes great and you can tell the amount of effort that put into their food.  We ate at the Belligio buffet the next day, and it didn't even come close to this buffet.  The service was top notch, I highly recommend going to this buffet if you go to Vegas.

We have been here four times in the last few years. On the busy weekends there will be a hour and a half wait to pay and get seated. During the week like today (Monday) it was 45 mins. It costs $54/person. The all you can drink wine is $15/person. You can pay extra to cut the line ($25/person) or if you have a Total Rewards card of Diamond or Seven you will have a shorter line. Food various from Indian, Mexican, Texan, sea food, sushi, and lots lots more including the colorful dessert bar. See my pictures.

This buffet has gone so far downhill.
I use to come to this buffet quite often in the past. It's been awhile since I been to this buffet but I decided to come back and try it out again since I was in town.
I came here at 3pm only to see a line for ages.they said I was not able to line up and had to sign in at the kiosk to get a time card on when I'm are able to come back and get in line. My wait time said 3 hours Jesus but I was hungry and really was looking forward to this buffet so I decided to wait it out. After wandering around for 3 hours I was able to get in line only to wait another 1 hour and 10 minutes just to get to the payment station. Dinner price was 70 dollars a person my lord. I remember it being cheaper when I came here when it first opened. But oh well I paid because I really wanted to eat here. Then after paying I had to get in another line in which I waited 40 more minutes before I was able to be seated. So all in all I waited 4 hours and 50 minutes to be able to be seated. Oh well I really wanted to eat here so I didn't want to let the time thing get in my way. 
After being seated I was off to get some of the yummy food. I noticed a lot of the foods that they had before were no longer being served like the fresh fruit juices which were my favorite. As you know with any buffet you always have to start with the meats or seafood first as they are the most expensive of the foods and you had to get your money's worth. I went and got the prime rib, American waygu, beef brisket, tri-tip all medium rare and some bone marrow. When I brought it back to my table the American wagyu was leaking so much blood that it covered my whole plate. I swear that wagyu came back to life and started moo'ing. Not only that but it lacked any flavor and didn't have any seasoning to it. The prime rib was super dry and bland, the beef brisket was dry but had a bit of flavor to it. The only good meat was the tri-tip which tasted really nice. Overall the meat station didn't appease me. At this point I'm dying from thirst as my waitress never came to me. So then I decided to get a plate of seafood now. I got escargot, oysters, Jonah crab claws and snow crabs. I saw that they had king crabs too but I couldn't find them. I asked about it and was told the king crabs were an additional charge in order to get them. You would think paying 70 dollars a person for a buffet would get you all the crabs in the world. But oh well I didn't let that bother me. The escargot was very bland and lacked any flavor at all and it also had a bunch of sand in it as well. Definitely not cleaned well. The oysters were ok nothing too special about them. The Jonah crab claws were the tastiest but it took awhile to break the claws open. But that's ok as they were tasty. The snow crabs on the other hand was soo salty I could barely eat them. Not only that but they were the skinniest snow crab legs I had ever seen. Where do they even manage to find these. Overall seafood was lackluster besides the Jonah claws. So far my experience with the food was mediocre as the majority of the meat and seafood were bad. But oh well I was still hungry. Now onto my third plate. Meanwhile my waitress finally comes to me and offers me a drink. That took ages for her to come. To be honest I didn't see any food worth really getting outside of meats and seafood. I stayed away from the tacos and fried rice and noodles because if you are paying 70 dollars for a buffet and you choose those as a food to eat then you need to be slapped or you have a pallet of a rock. So the next best thing was the Chinese dim sum which they had quite a variety to choose from and also some sushi in which they only had 4 kinds. Overall they were pretty average nothing too spectacular about them. They tasted and felt like the sushi and dim sum you can get at any local Chinese buffet. Then all of a sudden mid meal my waitress comes and says my 2 hour limit is up when I clearly had 30 minutes left. I know this because I set a timer down when I got seated as I know about there 2 hour limit policy. I was furious. I said I still had time left and that the buffet was closing soon so it shouldn't matter anyways. They had plenty of open seats available so why did I have to be  told to leave. The waitress didn't care and wanted me out. That just left me in disgust. I didn't even finish my dim sum and sushi and just got up and left. Didn't even bother to tip the crude waitress who barely even did anything for me. I use to come to this buffet quite often in the past but not anymore. I'm never coming back to this dump. It has fallen so far down the hole. The food was bad and service was terrible.
I suggest you all do the same. Food is lackluster and way overpriced. Bellagio or Wynn buffet is way better. Hell if you want to splurge on a buffet then wait till Sunday and go to the sterling brunch at Bally's. At least there you can be sure of them having great tasting food.
The Best Selection of what you need, great taste, Fresh seafood, good pizza, nice Asian foods nice interior, Dinner starting from 3.30pm. I do love Key Lime Tart and Crepe.

After wanting to try the infamous Bacchanal buffet, I was finally able to give it a go yesterday on a Monday afternoon. Given that it was EDC weekend, the hungry patrons came in large masses and wait time for the early bird dinner boom was quite the spectacle. 

Weekday dinner is approx $55/person. There is a Groupon deal that includes "vip express entrance" and a free drink, but that line was so saturated that It was probably the same wait as the regular line. Please note that there are limited number of upgrades costing $55 to bypass the line. 

Now onto the food:
Overall Bacchanal had a good selection and variety of grub to chose from ranging from a made to order taco station, "Asian soup station", carving station, and of course the crab legs that everyone rave about. 

I would say that I was satisfied with the meal but nothing stood out to me as exceptional. To be honest, I was quite disappointment in many of the dishes that I tried. 

Here are some of the not so good selections that I tried: 
-prime rib: tasteless and tough. Not tender and super chewy. Skip 
-braised salmon in some sort of red sauce by the seafood section: sooo dry. Why? 
-wonton soup and veggie dumplings in the steamer section: literally tasted like paste and play dough. Skip. 
-only boring sushi rolls. No nigiri available. 

The good?:
-fresh oysters were fresh and delightful 
-crab legs were fresh and very sweet 
-most of the roasted veggies and sautéed Veggies were on point and flavorful. 
-surprisingly the selection of Chinese roasted pork, roast duck, and pork belly were all made well and approved by this ABC. 
-selection of gelato and sorbets were amazing. Go for that lemon basil sorbet. 
-per the fiancé, the seafood cioppino was spicy and bustling win flavor. Good amount of seafood too. 
-the grilled hamachi Kama was probably best dish for me. So simple, yet made so well. The fish was soft and flaky and seasoned simply with salt. 

So will I return and spend the higher price for Bacchanal? No, probably not. The option for crab legs does not justified the price for me when everything else was sub par. I feel like
I couldn't gotten the same quality of food elsewhere for a buffet on the strip that cost $30-40. 

Hopefully they didn't "downgrade" their  food quality  knowing that their patrons are the post edc crowd.

My husband would say 5, my shellfish allergy says 4!  Great is you are a seafood lover!  Great selections, high price!  Yelp check in gave us a free champagne or glass of wine.  Delmar in the dessert area made a custom bananas foster!  Service is great!  Come hungry and ready to stand in line for a while at normal meal times.  Definitely need to do once during your Vegas trips!

Literally unbelievable! Everything I put on my plate was fantastic. The price was steep on the weekend but it was absolutely worth it! The crab legs were steamed perfectly, the braised short rib was to die for and everything else was just as amazing! Worth the wait and worth the price!
The best buffet in Vegas. Show up at opening for a empty and peaceful buffet with the whole spread of 500 items for yourself!
The best buffet I've ever eaten at! If you go right at lunch and right before dinner hours you can pay for the lunch price but eat for dinner.

This is seriously the best buffet I've ever had in Las Vegas. We went there to have a breakfast buffet and were amazed by the quality of the foods and their varieties. The freshly squeezed juices were great choice for health concern. The Mexican, Japanese and Chinese food hit me in the right spot. The poke was fresh, and even the plain congee mixed with assortment of bean curds and pickles was unbelievably delicious! The desserts and pastries were top notch.
Let's talk about the customer service. From my observation and interaction with our friendly and helpful wait staff, it was a pleasant experience throughout our meal. Our wait staff  cleaned up our plates promptly. She was patient, professional and communicative. 
We had such a great time dinning at Bachannal and were all satisfied!

Top of the line, no-doubt, easily, the best, and the most awesome-est buffet I've ever been too. I've been to enough buffets around to know that I can definitely settle down here for awhile.

The diversity of food goes a long way here. They have everything. Literally everything. I probably had like three slices of the prime rib before I realized that there's like the whole other half of food selections located in the back room. Dim sum, Italian, Chinese, American, you name it! It's all there. 

The presentation of these foods are very unique and attracting. Like for example the fries and wings come in their own little fryers - or even the ravioli and the fried calamaris come in their own little plates.

Does not end there because no matter what, there's also room for dessert. Desserts here are, what my cousin argues, "the best thing here". I didn't have much of a sweet tooth at the time but I would say that some may even agree. There's the white chocolate thing, the cream cheesecake cake pop, ice cream, tiramisu, and the list goes on. Grab me a spoon. 

Pricing is definitely big on this one. For a Saturday night, the total is over $65 a person. That's almost enough for the all-day buffet bracelet. Both have its ups and downs but it's best to try the best of both worlds. 

Coming back next time I'm in Vegas!

This is easily the best buffet in town. Check deal sites (Groupon or Living Social) for brunch deals. It is $39.99 for brunch, but you can find them online for cheaper.

Tip: save room for dessert!!

I love buffets. I love yelp. I love reading user reviews to help me make dining decisions, but my experience with Bacchanal Buffet was not nearly as positive as the experience of others 

Meat/Seafood: 
The crab almost had this "stale" like texture, watery and somewhat tasteless but strangely salty. The glazed ham? was intensively salty and was inedible. The prime rib was okay - nothing special. Everything else was literally just OK.  (Oh, and the sushi was pretty bad too) 

Others: 
Nothing that really caught our attention to where we went for seconds. 

Dessert:
The lady serving the Gelato must have been having a mid-life crisis. Super rude. The cakes and other sweets, although appeared enticing, lacked the quality to satisfy our already damaged tastebuds from the salty meats and seafood. 

Verdict:
I would suggest going to Joe's Seafood Prime Steak & Stone Crab instead.  Better quality for your money.

For the price of $70 this deserves a 2 star. Wait was ridiculously long. Did an online line for 3 hours and then waited in line to be seated over an hour. The quality of food was not to par. There was a lot of seafood options but coming from Pacific Northwest not great quality. Server also weren't friendly and they took too long to clean table up during the course of our meal.

I was SUPERRRRR full after this buffet! My favorite and most unique reason why I like this place is because if their tonkatsu ramen and pho. Most buffet places don't serve this but Bacchanal did and it wasn't bad. My second favorite is their desserts!! Their apple pie, fresh made crepe (though I wish they had fresh fruit as toppings instead), and mochi ice cream!!! Their salmon sushi was also good and sliced the way I like it, not too thick. The warm crab legs were also a favorite, because it didn't have the fishy sea smell/taste to it and it was flavored just perfectly so I could eat a plate-ful. The oysters were pretty fresh as well. Service was great and oh yeah, the peach green tea was definitely huge factor of my fullness too. Had two glasses of it because it was so delicious. Definitely will be back, maybe next time lunch to see what other dishes they serve. Also, their food seemed super authentic which is a plus because each cuisine, the chefs are from that culture, which makes it even more authentic!

This is an OK buffet, but definitely not worth the money ($70 + tax), nor the wait time. We arrived at 3:30PM and picked up the ticket to wait in the queue, after 70 minutes we were notified that we could check in. Then there's another line to check in and pay which we stood in for 20 minutes. Then yet another line to wait in to be seated which took 10 more minutes.

The food was OK just like any other $30 buffet. The only special thing not usually found in other buffer was bone marrow. Everything else was common. Also, they didn't replenish popular food often enough. For fresh oysters, I checked 5 times, and for 3 times it was out of stock.

It'd be a 4-star review if it were $40. But for $70 + tax + potentially tips it definitely overpriced.
One of the most amazing buffets in Vegas, amazing desserts, great variety and good customer service.
Always. Never a doubt. One of the best buffet. Every time come to Vegas I have to dine here.

Rude service management that was robotic and longer than humanly possible lines! This place has no room to brag! Don't get caught up in the hype because that is all this place is.food was 3.5 out of 5 cold and bland! Not what I expected.

I love this buffet. Of all the buffets I have been to in Vegas, this is by far the best one. I love the selection because of its diversity. Definitely go for the oysters, crab, mushroom truffle pizza, and pasta.

We went for brunch on a recent Sunday.  The line was only about 20 minutes (arrived around 11am), surprisingly enough.

The food was mostly hit with a few misses (the crab legs, for one - super dry).  Semi-DIY crepes were fun and delicious.  They were constantly out of the red velvet pancakes so I didn't get to try them.

My only complaint is that at $46, the price is STEEP especially given that you have no choice between champagne or no champagne.  Other buffets are $10+ less if you don't spring for the alcohol, and I wasn't drinking that weekend, so I was stuck having to pay for unlimited mimosas that I couldn't drink.  Boo on that.

I am writing this review as I take my fifth break from this buffet. My tummy is about to explode as I have been eating since noon. It is a little before 2pm and we are staying until the dinner transition at 3 when they finally serve the macarons for dinner. Here is my story. 

It is Monday and there was practically no wait whatsoever. We planned on going to the buffet after all that clubbing and pool activities and this was pretty much out highlight/thing we looked forward to the most. I forgot that it is also cheaper on Mondays so yay we win. Lunch is around 35 after tax and if you come after 3pm, then you pay around 10 bucks more. The best thing to do is come around 1:30 to 2 so you pay for lunch but then you are there for the dinner goodies. Asian cheap thinking right there. If it is weekends, the wait in line can be close to an hour and is more expensive so be prepared. 

They have a range of food from Chinese, Japanese, Mexican, Italian, seafood and hella meat. They will have the typical food you expect at buffets but I noticed there are not as many of those prepared dishes with multiple ingredients if that makes sense. These are the things I got and I really recommend

Orange juice- fresh with pulp and no sour taste! Some of the best OJ I have had
Omelet- comes with everything you can imagine like sausage, ham, mushrooms spinach
Congee- tastes so good and has preserved egg! Chinese donut tooo
Ramen- comes with pork and even tonkatsu flavor
Pulled pork- in the Mexico section. So flavorful
Guacamole- next to Mexico. So fresh and there are chunks of guac! 
Salmon- it's seared and I only got it cuz it's an expensive item
Tacos- they heat it fresh and are so the flavor

Lava cake and hot baked cookie combo- they come in two separate containers but cut a hole in that and mix that fresh cookie in. It is mind blowing. 
Fudge filled chocolate chip cookie- nuff said
Peanut butter filled dark chocolate chip cookie- my most favorite thing cuz I'm a Cookie Monster and I love PB. Nuff said
Gelato- so many flavors but I got caramel and strawberry cheesecake
Macarons- available for dinner starting at 3

Overall, buffets are good no matter what. It's also cheaper on weekdays for lunch so that coo. I was trying to do the lunch dinner transition for the Wynn buffet but they close down in between. I feel like there are not as many dishes at this place than The Buffet or Wicked Spoon. I like Wicked Spoon better cuz I feel like they have more savory plates and more desserts. I just remember their yogurt with blueberries in the chocolate cup was divine. I'm still sitting here and waiting for my tummy to chillax until my flight leaves. I knew if I didn't write this now, I would forget the entrees and I would be eating more shiz instead of resting. Good luck. 

**TIPS**
1) Weekday lunch is 11am to 3pm for $35 or so. Dinner starts 3pm and after for maybe ten bucks more. 
2) Peanut butter filled chocolate chip cookie is heaven. I love you. 
3) Wear the loose clothes that is a two sizes bigger than usual. It will be filled. 
4) Enjoy!

Been thinking and planning to celebrate my birthday this year here. It happened. I had high expectations for this buffet given it was the most expensive buffet I have been to here in Las Vegas. 

Upon arriving we were asked how many are to be seated and the staff member was clear and polite and led us to the designated line. There were already several long lines all waiting to be seated. We waited for about 30-45 mins.

The interior was impressive, it was elegant but IMO the lighting inside was just really dim, i guess it was part of the effect or ambience but to where we were seated it was just really dim. It does not feel so right not being able to see clearly what u are eating. 

We started to get our food coz we were so hungry and my disappointment started at that very moment. It was a weekend, president's day weekend and I was really looking forward to eat lobsters! Dinner weekend.. DINNER WEEKEND. Unfortunately there was none 

The choices were not that much to my dismay. I expected for more or even if there were few it could have been of really good quality and really delicious but none really stood out or made me go back and have another.

I guess Bacchanal buffet is more geared for the tourists and not the locals. 

The whole experience was just 3 stars. Their offerings were not something to be raved about but were not that bad either. I won't recommend it to a friend.
This is the most extensive and well thought out buffet I've ever been to. This is a must when you go to Vegas. The food is well prepared and worth the price. Will def return!!!

shit sucks now, been going since opening... this thanksgiving, it was a mess. the oysters had sand and were bitter/warm. the fucking guy cutting steak gave me all fat 2 times. the crabs were too salty, almost inedible. I am seven stars and this was pure bullshit.

I went to this buffet during their dinner prices and it is definitely a run for your money, but it's worth every penny. There is an array of options from all kinds of cuisines so you are bound to find something you love. I personally love tapas style dining and they curated a bunch of mini dishes so you can get a taste of everything. The crab leg line can get crowded so plan your visit to get those before it's too packed. Overall, it was an extremely fun dining experience, lovely ambience, and serves all your food needs. It's great for big or small groups as well!

I would say a good time to go is a little after 10:30 a.m.  The line only took about 15 minutes.  Upon my first perusal, I really wasn't overly impressed with the selection of food items.  

I'm not the biggest fan of breakfast food so I skipped over many of those items.  They had several Chinese items including some dim sum.  They also had a small sushi section, a Mexican section with a taco bar, an Italian section with some pizza and pasta, etc.  The long line was for the meats including prime rib, tri-tip, ham, turkey, sausage, etc.  I had a slice of prime rib which was huge and too rare for me although the ends were good and tasty.  The tri-tip was also good and I liked the bone marrow. The garlic mashed potatoes were yummy and, of course, went well with the meat.  There was also seafood like shrimp, crab legs, mussels, etc.

As for the dessert section, they had a wide, colorful, and inviting selection of pastries, sweets, cakes, mini desserts, gelato, sorbet, candy, etc.  They even had a line for crepes.  The flan was good.  The mini chocolate pecan pie and fudge lava cake were just okay.  I tried the pumpkin gelato and the mango banana sorbet which were pretty good even though I was stuffed.

I'm glad I was able to try Bacchanal.  I rank it about the same as Wicked Spoon.
This is one of my favorite buffet I've ever been to great food and dessert. I would recommend everyone to go here if you are hungry and in the area.

Are you kidding me??????? $62.99 for a buffet!!!!! Enough said....
The buffet was wonderful, but not worth $69.99 a person.  Raising rates for Memorial day is shameful!! There are a lot of active and retired military families in Las Vegas.  Seems a bit harsh Caesar's

The food here is not well prepared or fresh.  This is a tourist trap.  They are charging a high price since this buffet is part of a famous hotel in vegas, otherwise they would not get much business for the good or service that they provide.

Make sure you come prepared to stand in line here at the Bachannal Buffet. Being one of the more popular buffet's on The Strip, this line can get outright outrageous I heard.  We were lucky this time,  waiting less than 45 minutes, after hearing stories of people waiting 1-2 hours. BTW, you can opt to pay an extra fifteen bucks to enter via the "Preferred" line. Nope, I'll wait. After paying for two, which by-the-way set me back a cool $102 bucks, we were escorted to our seats and invited to start anytime we wished. Ah, my dining companion and I decided we would make a "dry run" through the entire buffet to prepare ourselves for the journey ahead of us. After familiarizing ourselves with the setup, we proceeded to get our food. For me, the first stop was the Asian section. Being savvy enough to discipline oneself to realize that there is one big huge buffet ahead and not to fill up on starch here can be difficult here.  There was a nice layout of sushi and other Oriental delicacies. As I made my way around the buffet, I couldn't help but notice the standard items found in most buffets. People were piling their plates with crab legs, which btw were probably snow crab, really skinny. I think I took maybe two small legs. I made my way to the prime rib, which is kinda how I judge a good buffet. I asked for a medium rare piece, but was a little disappointed in it's being dry. There were other meats, but they looked equally dry also. The oysters are good, though, very fresh. They have a nice display of fish in the display case which made for a great photo op!  The Mexican section was pretty good, but I think the star of this buffet had to be the dessert section. Macarons, cakes, pies, cake pops, even mochi ice cream! A dessert lover's paradise! All in all, I have to give this buffet a three star rating because I felt it was a bit overrated and because the meat section wasn't what I expected. The service was fair, although I noticed towards the end of our meal it got slow and our drinks went un-refilled... Would I go back? Probably not, I did want to try the brunch one day though. I think for the money, there are other better choices in Vegas.

I got in line at 2:25pm and I was seated at my table at 4:25pm on Sunday. Was really hoping I could get in before 3pm for the lunch prices but definitely didn't make it in! It was $75 for dinner so I made sure to load up on their snow crabs! Holy cow (holy crabs?) their crabs are sooooo delicious. I really think that's the only reason people come here! They have a seafood section, pasta section, taco station, dim sum, pho, and premium quality meat. No salad bar but that's probably because the chefs want to hand craft the mini salads for you!

Their dessert section also has ube, black sesame, and matcha gelato. I also got the POG (passion fruit, orange, guava) gelato. On top of that, I also got a crepe from the crepe station! I'm pretty sure I gained several pounds because I ate and I ate nonstop for 1.5 hours.

I visited this place when I went to Vegas. All I can say, is that I was not disappointed at all! The line moved fast, and customer service was also great. I read some reviews before coming here, and I am so glad I came. My family and I enjoyed all the different foods they had to offer. But of course my favorite was their Snow Crab Legs. Next time your in town stop by and try this place out. Ask for Vince he will be sure to assist you in everything you need. Nothing better than great food and great service.
Lives up to the hype.  Loved the red velvet pancakes, crepes, and unlimited crab legs.  Also loved the fresh assortment of juices, especially watermelon.  Overall, definitely recommend.
Food was delicious and service was amazing - we had Esmeralda Juarez. Highly recommend having her as a server.
Came for lunch a few years ago and thought the food was mediocre but dinner was a entirely different story. Food was fantastic and exceptional service from our waitress Esmeralda. Highly recommend!
This is my favorite Buffet restaurant, and they also will give you free champagne and mimosa when you check in.

For being the "#1 buffet in Las Vegas" I came in here with a little higher expectations than I would for most. To be honest, I'm not a buffet person in genera but Las Vegas is suppose to be the holy trinity of buffets. So, you have to give it a chance at least once right? Maybe not... 
   The wait is obviously out of their control so I'm not taking stars away for that. But oh my gosh... when you're crammed into a Disney Land line with what seems like hundreds of other people. It gets uncomfortably hot. I had to go outside and get fresh air because everyone was so close together we started to sweat. 
   Food wise, we went with the chilled seafood and shrimp. Shrimp was great but the crab was still semi frozen. We moved on to the beef, wagyu and tri-tip. The wagyu was tragically overcooked, while the tri-tip was medium rare but bland. It seemed like everything was just unexciting. 
   The desserts were an entirely different story. So many options and everything was delicious. I don't think dessert makes up for $65 a person. So, there's probably better/cheaper places to eat.

Been wanting to try this buffet spot for awhile. The price was slightly steep but I thought, why not! I went on a Saturday @2pm and the wait was really long, prob 45 min/1hr. I was expecting more choices but I was disappointed especially for the price. Some dishes were kinda stale not sure if it had been sitting out for awhile. Their dessert options were amazing!! Overall the staff was friendly, it was a clean buffet, but I wasn't impressed with the food options and price. That's just MY personal opinion. I'm more of a fan of Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan prices are awesome and food is DELICIOUS.

If I were to define disappointment in a few words, I would say Bacchanal Buffet. And trust me, I tried so hard to justify paying $70 for a buffet. I tried the seafood, the meats, and all the desserts; and the best thing I tried was the pho. That's right, out of everything, the pho, which costs about $10 anywhere else,was the best thing.  And for those who are wondering, the most expensive items (the lobster and the steak) tasted old and flavorless. I know this place claims to be the BEST BUFFET in Vegas-maybe at one point it was-but it certainly is  not anymore. Old YouTube videos( Mikey Chen) of this place will just show that they  definitely cut down in quality and don't have the same selection as they used to. Do yourself a favor and go to other, much cheaper buffets in Vegas.

Snow crabs, sea food, Italian, Chinese, Indian, etc, you can probably find whatever you've a craving of in the moment. The downside is probably the price, as it's the most expensive buffet I've been - it costs about 100$ CAD for an hour and half of buffet (hey! You're in Vegas! You can spend this money for the belly instead of losing it at the casinos... )

If you like to WAIT then this is a place to go for dinner on the weekend.  I understand this is a popular seafood buffet but you shouldn't have to suffer TRIPLE waits.  Firstly, we have to WAIT about 1 hours 15 mins to get to the pay counter.  Secondly, we have to go into 1-2 person line and WAIT for another 20-30 mins.  Eventhough it's quick here, but the total time to get a table is almost 2 hours.  Thirdly is their excuses for not having the food ready is to WAIT for 10 mins before the food is brought out.  They shouldn't charge $70 (tax included) per person and treat us like this.  For me, the experience is very very BAD and I don't plan to return in the future.
Best buffet i been to yet. Name the food and they got it. Its pricey but well worth it. Staff was friendly. You can taste fresh.Next time in Vegas might even stay at Ceasers just for that buffet.

I'm not a big fan of buffets, that being said, this buffet was incredible. They seemed to have an endless supply of seafood and all the fixings. The diverse menu is a sure cure for all your cravings.
Be prepared for long wait lines cause the secret is out. When in Vegas put this on your to-do list.

Solid selections Options.  The line took over an hour but I'd suggest arriving early to avoid the madness.  The service is good in that they cleared the plates and were prompt with requests.  The Mexican station was not well kept and the condiment area looked messy and unappetizing.  The dessert selection was exceptional compared to most buffets.  I wish there were more Italian options.  It is one of the most expensive buffets right now and expected the quality to match the tag but I was a bit disappointed.  I still think the Wynn is preferable with cleaner presentations with smaller portions that are constantly refreshed. Free glass of wine with yelp check in.

Excellent buffet! Everything was well prepared and the servers were very attentive. The spare ribs were super tender and melted in your mouth. I loved the seafood, particularly the crab legs and shrimp.
Great buffet. Can't ask for really anything more. The price is pretty steep, but if you enjoy a quality buffet it is worth it.

It's worth the price. 

For a buffet the food was good. Compared to a sit down restaurant at the best place you've ever eaten I'm sure you'd lower the rating. I didn't base this on the best ever. I rated this compared to other buffets. 

5 stars for the price
4 stars for the food quality
5 stars for the selection 

There is a 2 hour time limit. I'd assume to keep the lines down?  We came at 4 on a Tuesday, and it was still busy. You can spend $15 for all you can drink beer/wine. I didn't get this because I wanted to be full of food. $25 for kid dinner. 

For the price it's a great deal. A lot of variety of different kinds of quality food. It's cheaper than a sit down quality food without the huge variety. 

Service was good. They kept the tables clear of plates. Drinks were full. 

Food was above average. Some items were really good. Some were average. 

Selection of meats was amazing. It all tasted good. Carving station is a must try. Pork belly was a little more crispier than expected. Prime rib and tri tip was very good. Added au jus. 

Seafood has a mix of cold and warm seafood. You can get steamed crab legs as well as cold. Clams were flavorful. Seafood all was good. 

Sushi was good. We had to have 2 helpings even though you can get this anywhere for a decent price. 

Chinese selection was a mix. Good - duck, bbq pork, shu Mai, rice was good. Soups were so-so. All the noodle dishes were disappointing.  They weren't soft and a bit crunchy. This seemed to be a theme. 

Mashed potatoes were good. 

Didn't particularly love any of the pasta dishes. Mac and cheese and the chicken Parmesan weren't very good. It probably sat out to long which lead to the crunchy pasta. We might've liked the Mac n cheese when it was fresh. 

We might've missed a few pictures of our plates. We were excited to try everything and eat.

Usually don't eat this much food in one sitting but my son-in-law recommended the Bacchanal buffet to us. He was right on! The seafood selection was great and the food went on forever! Desserts came to late after we were stuffed so we didn't give them a true test!

We heard so much about this place and everywhere we go people recommended it to be the best rated buffets in Las Vegas. Well if this is the best buffet in town then I'm afraid to even try any others. The price with taxes is 70 person. Let's start off with their seafood. Snowcrabs looked like they are malnourished and their meat is very mushy, lobster claws and tiger shrimps oh dear they were just plain cold and miserable. I honestly couldn't even finish one claw. The wagyu beef along with all of their beef selections wywas chewy and no flavors. Their sushi looks worse than Kroger sushi and all they got was salmon and tuna nigiri and spicy tuna and salmon roll. The one thing that really pisses me off is that these people have the nerves to serve dumplings that I feel like came from frozen section at Costco. Food here is worst than golden corral in my opinion. The only tolerable food they have was the soup section pho. My boyfriend and I decided to fill ourselves up with pho and left. I mean if you want to spend 140 for 2 bowls of pho by all means go to the bacchanal otherwise stay away. This place is way too overrated and overhyped. As we left the buffet we see people lined out the door and honestly felt sorry for them.

We went to this buffet about 2 weeks ago. It is super expensive, but the food is amazing. It is a buffet and yet all the food taste very fresh and there is a huge variety. It was even more expensive than usual when we went due to the holiday. $70 per person was crazy! Overall great selection, variety, just not so great price :) Which is why we have only been twice in 7 years lol
One of our Vegas favorites! Best buffet on the strip. A little pricey but you can find deals online if you search for them.

One of the best buffets I've ever eaten at. If you love quality, show stopping food you must make time to put it down here at Bacchanal Buffet! 

Top notch service!

The Bacchanal Buffet was no doubt one of the most expansive and elaborate buffers I've ever been to. Though buffet's are never my favorite, this one is definitely next level. So after an um... eventful night in Vegas, we ventured out from our rooms, shielded by our sunglasses, and headed to the buffet. We started with champagne and coffee, because, well... Vegas. Then we attacked all of the hangover food on the buffet. Everything we tried we loved. 

My only critique would be on the approach to seating. We waited for what seemed like forever as we looked out at an almost empty dining room. The older ladies that were seating everyone seemed to be very overwhelmed. When we were finally seated, they bearded together about 4 groups of people and we played follow the leader to each of our tables. ‍ Wow.

It doesn't help anything that we went here during the Christmas holiday. 

But, since we never tried this place, we figure why not since we were staying at Cesar's palace. The wait was about 30 minutes to an hour wait (being Christmas and all) that's with being a diamond member. 

Food selection was definitely worth the wait. They had almost everything and top meats you can choose from. 

For the price you pay ($70/person-holiday) it was worth the wait. Now, I just have to try t when they're serving breakfast.

I went to this buffet on 2-14-2016 though it was a holiday, (Valentines Day) I doubt that was the reason for the 2 HOUR Wait time. It was my last day in Las Vegas and I wanted to eat at a nice Buffet before leaving. Bacchanal Buffet was one of the higher reviewed Buffets so I tried it. (I did not realize this would take up the majority of my day)  The Kiosk in the front of the Buffet prints out a ticket and tells you to return in 30-45 minutes to meet the hostess and pay in advance for the Buffet, what you don't realize is that upon returning to meet with the hostess you still have to wait in line another 1.5 hours and based on what some employees have told me that is considered a short wait. After we were seated I felt the décor and the ambience were very nice, the servers very attentive but for the most part every dish that I tried was only slightly warm and not hot as most people would prefer. This was an immediate turn off. for 49.95 I expect my food to be hot. On the positive side they have huge Crab legs that are already split down the middle so they are easy to eat, The have a variety of "small plates" that were very tasty, I'm not sure who is frying the chicken (Chicken and Waffle fries small plate) But it was crunchy, juicy, moist and well prepared (It takes a lot to impress me with chicken since my mother makes great chicken LOL 

I would say, it is not worth the long wait in line, If you can find a time to go when you can walk right in and you have 49.95 to spare then go for it, it's an experience and the food is pretty good just not hot. 

P.S. You have a 2 hour time limit in which you can dine at the Buffet so eat quickly and don't take to long to let your food settle in between selections. (No one came over to rush us or anything but I did read that information on the bottom of the receipt.)
Excelente comida,muy fresca y bien elaborada,platos especiales que no se encuentran en muchos lugares,la atención del equipo de trabajo espectacular,100% recomendado.

For my first experience, Bacchanal was amazing! So much to choose from and the quality was excellent. I especially enjoyed their prime rib and mint gelato. Bacchanal is so massive that you really need to pace yourself to enjoy everything they have to offer. Can't wait to go back!

Don't believe the hype...

We've all seen the youtube videos proclaiming that the Bacchanal is the best Buffet in Vegas. At a whopping $70 a person for dinner (without lobster) it was a big letdown. 
That being said, the Bacchanal is the definitive quantity AND quality buffet in Las Vegas. But the overall experience for dinner was far from extraordinary, and at times downright boring. At this price range I want an incredible experience, exotic and rare cuisine, and dishes that I'll remember for years. All I got was insane quantity with some sea snails.

The one highlight of this dinner buffet was their phenomenal carving station (which apparently is also available for brunch). Of course the seafood was very popular too, as someone else in line said "Crazy Rich Asians"  were eating their body weight twice over with Opilio Crab legs. All of the other stations had a few interesting food choices, and some of the presentations were indeed impressive, but again nothing that screamed opulence, or should I really say, SEVENTY dollars worth. An argument could be made that the sheer number of "gourmet" options justifies the high price. But to take advantage of all that they offer you, you would need to be a competitive food eater even if you're just sampling.

What was awesome here:
- The truffle mushroom pizza was sooo good
- They had very hot horseradish  (atomic)
- They did have halibut
- Wagyu beef
- Perfect prime rib
- Tri tip and brisket
- The dessert bar was one of the best on the strip and very photogenic. 

What was really disappointing:
- It's not serve-your-own drinks. Beverage options were very limited compared to other places that offer a beverage bar.
- Food depth in some stations were also a little frustrating. Sushi and salads were pretty thin. No build-your-own salad bar. 
- Taco bar. Basic street tacos are indeed tasty, but is this their idea of a cooking station at a $70 buffet??
- Labels missing or wrong.
- Don't even get me started that the cashier gave me the stink eye when I DIDN'T tip her for taking my $140.. Note this TIP doesn't get you off the hook for tipping the women that serves your drinks or gathers your empty dishes. 

Tips 
- If you're traveling to Vegas and you're into buffets, check out "All you can Vegas" on youtube.. They're informative "average Joe" reviews of buffets. 
- Go before 5pm for dinner. No line. At 6pm very long line. 
- Based on videos and reviews, the brunch is more approachable. Dinner is just paying for sea snails. 
- Although very limited at times, check out the Groupon deals for the Bacchanal

This place is worth it for the dessert buffet alone. Really. I had like five million crepe brûlée's in one visit. And that's not including the main courses I had. But the dessert buffet is where's it at. 

By far the best buffet experience I've had in Vegas. The price tag may hurt a bit, but once you're in you should be happy with your dining choices. 

5 stars kid!

The food is really good, my favorite was the taco station it's really similar to mexican food but i think they have to make better desserts, i always wait for dessert it's my favorite part!so when i went to the dessert station i was a bit disappointed they only had a few cookies and ice cream, they should add more quality food(cheesecake,pecan pie,bread pudding,apple crumble etc)
My second times here and probably  the last. The food quality was not worth  the price. Save your money ,go somewhere else.

The food is good for a buffet. Staff INSIDE was nice. However, the stomach problems and nausea afterwards is not so fun. The wait was 3+hrs, then the price for one adult was $65+tax for dinner. Only for us to get sick after. Not great, time consuming. The lines were a total disaster, crazy amount of people and loads of disorganization. Would never go again. Don't bother going, not worth your time or money.

Just to put it out there; I HATE buffets. I prefer quality over quantity. However at this place, I got both! I came in around lunch time and to my surprise...they had poke and all types of sushi in the Japanese section! They had EXTENSIVE choices, all of which I have never experienced at a buffet before. Everything was amazing, but here are some highlights; meat & cheese board selection (shoutout to all my Keto friends out there, this ones for you!), CHURROS, poke, FRESH sashimi, a soup/noodle section (they had pho, ramen, udon), and the seafood section! In general, I suggest getting a small portion of everything you want, then coming back for the ones you loved!

The buffet itself was clean and well kept. Our server was quick and prompt with her service. 
Ugh, as I'm writing this review, I want to go back so badly! I've been to many buffets growing up, but this tops them all!

we payed for 7 people and waited for 2 hours in queue, got skipped by 2 group of 8 people because the people who organizes the booking said that they dont have a table that would fit 7 yet they manage to get 8 people fit on a table, I find it odd that there's a table that would fit exactly 7 people, and then we had to find out after 2 hours of wait they placed us on a 8 seater table. The lady who talked to us about the matter was rude and manager wasn't able to resolve the matter as well. The manager was belittling us. Food was good but the customer service and management was horrendous. Avoid this place during peak hours speccialy on weekend. Not $75 per person worthy for the service and wait we had experienced.

Dined at this buffet due to all the hype we heard! Our biggest mistake! We dined here on Easter so it was $70/pp which is outrageous for the service and quality of the food they serve. I'm assuming it was a bad weekend to try this buffet out but I wouldn't give them another chance! 

First off, the selection they advertised was FALSE! Our main reason we wanted to try this buffet was for the seafood. They said unlimited king crab, which was not true. They had a mixture of snow crab and king crab in a pot.. ridiculous! It was a 80 to 20 ratio. We paid for king crab but we got mainly snow crab. Asked for them hot, but it was still cold. They advertised lobster bisque but only had tomato bisque. They also advertised tomahawk ribeye and filet mignon.. they didn't have either!!! Oysters were gross, lacked flavor. Jonas crab were DRY! And actually smelled rotten. Sushi rolls consisted mainly of rice... ugh. If we're paying that much per person, you better expect some fresh fish or sashimi.. negative!! The butcher cutting the meats was spitting in the food as he was talking. As if that didn't turn you away yet, check out service. 

Service was HORRRRRRIBLE. We didn't know where our server was the whole night. And when we did find him, he was arguing with another server about what table was his and what wasn't... RIGHT NEXT TO US. How awkward it was for us to hear that. We had to ask for everything -- napkins (which we were given a stack of cocktail napkins), silverware, nut cracker, refills. So inattentive. Probably because he was worried about his table that ordered a bottle of wine instead. 

I would not ever recommend this buffet to anyone. My review will get lost in the thousands of reviews but I sure hope I get one of yalls attention and do yourself a favor and not go here. Don't want to have to say "I told you so!"

Hypertension Buffet, heeey! 

The last time I came to this buffet, everything was ridiculously salty.  Everything was so enticing as you walk down the aisle of food. I grabbed crab, bone marrow, tacos, and dim sum.  The meat on top of the bone marrow was incredibly dry, it tasted like it's been sitting out for too long. I grabbed a whole plate of crab and couldn't get myself to eat it because of how salty it was.  The only thing that was enjoyable was the oysters because all they had to do was shuck them.  They even got rid of the juice bar, which was something I always looked forward to as well. 

For the desserts, everything is enticing. I grabbed a whole plate of dessert, but nothing really stood out.  My favorite was the Thai Tea Float that you ask from the gelato guy.  The gelato is also very good & you get to try exotic flavors.  

For $50, I definitely expect more.  The past couple of times I've gone have been underwhelming.  Everyone at the table complained of how salty and inedible the food was.

This place is my "go to" place every time I visit Vegas. I've tried multiple buffet restaurants but none of them satisfied my palate as much as Bacchanal. Why? even though the wait is long? The food are all fresh especially the seafood. It's a hit or miss on oysters but most of the times I like it. My boyfriend didn't like it as much so that means everyone has different preference. Don't starve yourself before going or you will not be able to eat as much. Try having a big breakfast or brunch for dinner at Bacchanal. I wish I knew a way to not having to wait for more than 1 1/2 hours without paying extra..:( If anyone has an idea, please message me!

But all in all, please do check it out.
Good food, it could be a little tastier with more refined selections. The NFC is this week, so I don't know if this menu was catered to the weeks crowd. More basic items then I was expecting.

Visited this place to try . It's pricey $50+ pp . It's started out as a waiting game for a long line of customer outside since it was lunch time. But it moved pretty fast, even the line for 5 and up group was not too bad. But I only had 2 in my party . The buffet was enormous from seafood to prime cut meats , the one I was surprised was the scallops in the sushi section. I can say I almost tried everything including the desserts , it all tasted good , since it is the main part of the dining experience!
This is the best place I've ever been, too much food I couldn't try everything. Definitely worth the money. Very nice staff as well

I visited on a Wednesday night, under $60 per person. The environment was so nice and the ambiance made me feel like I wasn't at a buffet. 

There was sooo many different types of delicious food to sample. My favorite must been the dessert island. The maccorns was heaven and the ice cream. Mmmmm
