The only thing I was really looking forward to was the seafood. Snow crab legs were tooooo salty and I didn't even get to try any king crabs bc they barely had any there. The raw oysters was weird too. All that seafood definitely wasn't fresh and tasted funky. All the other food was really good though. You will get your money's worth for sure.
Very nice buffet. Very expensive cuts of meats and fresh seafood makes this buffet worth it. I went during brunch and I'll come here again no doubt

Pretty great buffet but with a lot of hits and misses. Some really great hits were the small tuna poke influenced bowl, short rib ravioli and the brisket. The dimsum was fine, as were most items at the asian station. Dessert bar was great. My issues came with the service (server never came by without calling for her and even then refused to bring drinks like soda) and the raw seafood bar. The quality of the seafood was horrendous and I really don't understand why people go back for more. For the dinner price of $60 per person, I definitely expect higher quality seafood!

Delicious food. I can say everything I've tasted here is very tasty and full of flavor. Cooked to perfection. With so many options of food from all types of cuisine. Don't forget The dessert section!  It's  by far everyone's favorite. Definitely worth every penny!

WOW!  Everything you could want from a buffet and I went during lunch and it was unbelievable.  Chinese, Japanese, Italian, Indian,American, Mexican and more.  The carving station,at lunch, had seven different meat choices. The selection and flavor was outstanding.  Desert? Oh ya!  An endless offering of an confectioners wildest dream. All you can drink mimosas, wine beer program for $15 plus a free drink with a Yelp check in.  Yes it's expensive but you have to experience this restaurant if your in Vegas!

Great buffet, regardless of the price. This is in my opinion the best buffet in Las Vegas and I have frequented Vegas and buffets since 1973. The food, the staff and the atmosphere were all excellent. I plan to return in the next few weeks for another meal.


The seafood both hot and cold, the meat, the salads and the various cuisines were all well presented and delicious. The dessert section is amazing. Delmar, the crepemaster is a professional and a really nice guy. Be sure to ask him about his favorite crepe. My family really enjoyed meeting him and wish to thank him for his caring service. Thanks Delmar. The Bacchanal Buffet is not to be missed when in Las Vegas. It is the epitome of buffets.

This buffet is so huge and well known.  I have been a fan for a long time but this last trip, I think all the flavor just fell short for me.  Nothing stood out beside their lemon basil gelato.  Other than that for the price that it is, I would rather go to the Studio B buffet at the M resort.

The single most thing I'm currently passionate about in life is to make great restaurant experiences in a way that those restaurants make great money and to unlock this virtuous cycle and replicate it for all , who have the ability to make great food and the will to feed patrons . 

In my first yelp review (because I think my view point is slightly more biased and not useful for yelp readers) It gives me immense pleasure to commend the job Chef Leticia Nunez and the team carries out each day in and day out at the Bacchanal. What is phenomenal about the entire process is the operational excellence achieved. 

Whilst the buffet may start at 7:30 in the morning , things start coming together pre dawn at 4. Even cooler is the fact that one of my earliest learnings working as Commis 1 was to have the food perfectly set up at 0th minute of the buffet  and make sure the selection is always perfect till the end in regards to the display, taste, quality , warmth etc of the food as well as the service,  which really highlighted the complexity. 

Over ~500 different items on the menu everyday here, To keep them consistently available for the guest is just a genuine feet. 

For any of this cool logistics to matter, what really mattered was What a frickin meal it was! 

Amazing lobster, roast and sweet potato dishes. 

The only thing I would change jn the Establishment  is the restaurant design which I did not think was much like the contemporary restaurant experience that BOH was ready to deliver. The stations were confusing and the food was very cramped on the line. Feel like it was slightly an effort to make the food look abundant which was a slight turn off. There could also be more sunlight in the room given food would tend to look better and give a break from the casino. Adding a big booth to drop your plates(as just an option would be good) - makes easy for quick tastings.

The menu can also be improved in the protein composition - there seemed to be very few chicken dishes as well as a complete lack of any complex chicken dishes, slightly similar with shrimp both of which seem to be more "basic" proteins. Perhaps not ideal for large and diverse crowds.

Personally I think a buffet should not really have a "star" dish but perhaps having a more interactive experience around a set of dishes could make that more engaging. The way to perhaps do it would be perhaps a dumpling wrapping machine that is a station by itself , where there is a selection daily roasting dumplings being wrapped and steamed.

Well well well, I was a big fan of Vegas buffet and I probably visited all the major buffet (Bellagio, Paris, Wynn, Caesar's palace and much more) for breakfast, lunch and dinner but it's been three years since I had a chance to come back to Vegas so I decided to give it a try to Caesars palace for lunch. 

I got there slightly before 11 so I felt somewhat lucky to pay the breakfast price (still above $40) but hey you get what you pay for! 

Well, that concept is no longer true anymore with Vegas hotel buffet anymore. With resort fee going up and parking, Vegas isn't the place I used to enjoy. They take more and give less and less and this buffet proved that to me in a sad way. I eat a lot at so many places travel a lot. So my idea of what's reasonable and what's good for certain locations are more and more refined. And while charging so much more for these buffet, you can get so much better experience and quality of food at restaurant! Guy Savoy upstairs, while pretty pricy, can provide that experience. Or if you can travel, go to AYCE places and they are cheaper (less than $30) AND you can get much better food. While the selection was pretty amazing (give a few stars for that), and surprised about the watermelon juice; there was nothing really there that I want to go back and get again because they taste all so average. Using the clam or mussels or crab or shrimp, they can do so much better to give better experience but except, they gave us typical cafeteria food quality.  Nothing fancy taste. What happened Vegas? Greed and getting better at collecting money but I'm so not impressed. Sorry if you are a big fan here. I don't mean to offend but besides the selection of choices, nothing much was that high quality food.  Didn't work for me.

Btw, servers service seems pretty good still though. So that's always a good thing. Not just my server but all the other servers had Big nice smiles and no bad attitude at this Buffet. If you are first timers in Vegas, you'll have to try at least once.  There aren't many places in the world (except where I had several Hotel breakfast in Hokkaido Japan) that they have this many variety of food. So if you are into variety, yes yes!!  If you are into quality, I'd say, hmmmmmm. I have to think second again. But that's a sad thing about being a big foodie. Become picky in quality, but I still recommend you try if never done and see yourself. Not a Hometown buffet or Golden Coral for sure.

I'm a huge fan of the buffet at Wynn so was nervous to try Bacchanal while staying at Caesar's. I'm vegan and of course all restaurants at the Wynn have dedicated vegan menus. Perusing the buffet as soon as I entered Bacchanal I didn't see many options so requested to speak to the chef. She was very kind and walked me through the whole buffet and laid out what I could and could not eat (I also have several allergies). They ended up making me several custom items and basically asked me what I wanted to eat. 

I got: a veggie pizza (no cheese), sushi, and fried rice. The chef came by my table a couple times to make sure everything was ok and to ask if I wanted anymore food. The pizza and sushi were good and the fried rice was so-so. I can't speak as to whether my experience is dependent on who was working that day but, overall, vegans or those with dietary restrictions need not fear - you'll get your money's worth.

Hands down the best buffet I've been to in a very long time.  I can't believe it doesn't have 5 stars. I only went for lunch which was just under $40. Dinner was just under $60. Breakfast was $30. 
You enter via velvet rope lines and pay for the buffet before you are seated. 
I liked the decor here too. Had more of a restaurant feel than a buffet feel. 
The food was delicious and plentiful. Fresh seafood, a few breakfast options, soup, meats including brisket, sausages, sushi, pasta, salad bar, dim sum, etc. Every section of food was themed. Chinese, Japanese, Italian, etc. I could have filled up in just one of those sections. I tried to sample a little bit of everything but there were just too many options to pick from. All of the food I tried was delicious. 
Lastly the dessert section. Huge. Crepes, macrons, ice cream, cakes, etc. 
Best buffet I've been to in a very long time if not ever.

Bacchanal Buffet is one of the best buffets I've ever eaten at. This buffet has amazing food sorting with different varieties. My personal favorite is the breakfast waffles. The customer service here is amazing. You get seated almost instantly from my experience and you get served immediately with the drink of your choice. The service here is amazing. The manager helped us out with a problem we had and he immediately fixed it not giving us any trouble. He also helped us out with the Caesars Palace check out time as we had passed it. 

As my parents went to check us out, the manager said he'll keep an eye on us and he kept us busy, asking us questions and not making us bored. I'm at the buffet writing this right now and I can't stop eating because the food is incredible. Customer Service is amazing, and so is the food here. This buffet is 10/10 recommended by my family and I, and we had the most amazing time here with no trouble! Definitely a memory that will last! Whoever reads this, you should really come here because you for sure won't regret it.

Pros : 

The food - Seafood, Italian, Chinese, American (bbq), the desserts. They also of a variety of drinks you can choose from. I haven't gotten a chance to try all of them. And of course everything here is absolutely yummy!

Customer Service - 100%

Seating - The seating is not too close to other people so you have space to push your chair out and leave. This is just one of the best things here because any other restaurant I go to, I have to ask other people eating there to push theirs in.

Cons :

NOTHING!
Very disappointed. Went there for Bone marrow. NO bone marrow. Better go to wicked spoon they have bone marrow and much cheaper.

Wait time is horrible and after the almost 2 hour wait they never brought out lobster claws that were empty they entire 40 minutes I was there waiting for them. Rest of the food is ok but sooooo not worth the wait

This is such a great buffet. It seems to go on forever and has endless options. I never eat enough to make going to buffets worthwhile, but I love the variety so I go anyway. They had this truffle gnocchi that was out of this world, and the crab legs were amazing (I heard). The fruit and dessert bar was fabulous, everything was fresh, and the cooks are more than happy to make a vegetarian option of the eggs benedict (WIN!!!).

I am almost glad I am not a local, otherwise I would probably be here all the time. 

Yay for buffet!

I had never been to the Bacchanal Buffet before and after a rave review and recommendation from a foodie friend of mine I decided to give it a try. My group and I showed up around 4 pm on Friday. The line went by fairly quickly. I believe it ended up being a 30 minute wait until we were seated in the restaurant. At first glance, it definitely looks like there is a ton of food options and lots of variety available. I had high hopes for this buffet but unfortunately I left pretty disappointed. The price point is too high, especially if there are vegetarians in your group. Their was barely any vegetarian food options available and a lot of the food felt so heavy and greasy. Most of our group left the buffet feeling "meh". We had one person who loved the buffet and another who actually ended up getting sick from the food. Honestly there are so many other restaurant choices in Vegas that this one was just a miss and not worth it.

Food was good to great overall, can get busy. A must try (best) was brisket, trip tip, cured bacon and crab legs. (Good ok) desserts and seafood area. (Maybe good) Asian, Mexican and american. (Need attention) coffee, hot sour soup, Chinese rice was cold broken buns. Overall very clean and servers were very friendly.

We literally drove from LA to come eat here. All you can drink for $15. Endless crab legs. The dessert bar featuring a lovely human making fresh crepes. Sushi. Soup. Large slabs of meat cut with you desired internal temp in mind. This is a go-to. Sorry. A MUST anytime while in Vegas.

The best buffet I have ever eaten from. It just keeps going and going and going.

Brunch was the choice today - it's served like from 10am until 2pm. We bought a Groupon for $88 and it includes two mimosas per person and brunch and VIP passes (which doesn't mean anything to them apparently).

This buffet has everything - from fresh LOX and BAGELS to an entire Asian section with Dim Sum and all the fixings. It's truly amazing!

Fresh made-to-order:  French Toast, Eggs, Crepes, and Waffle stations are scattered around.

Steamed seafood section. Eggs Lobster Benedict and Shrimp and Grits - just too good to pass up!  Heavenly actually!

The carved meat section was astounding - ham, Tri-tip, sausage, and roast beef to rotisserie chicken and smoked turkey.

You can also get chicken and waffles and there are tons of soups from Egg Drop to Tomato Bisque to Lobster Bisque to Cream of Mushroom. Amazing!

There is a Vietnamese area where you can get fresh Pho and all the toppings to go along with it.

The desserts are also amazing - the Tiramisu and Creme Brûlée were perfect. There is also a Vietnamese Coffee mousse which is rich and tastes just like a Vietnamese coffee drink - even has a golden coffee bean on top.  

I am sure you won't be disappointed and there is definitely something for everyone here. Just take super small portions so you can try as much as possible!

Compared to other Vegas buffets, this has to be the best one. Lots of choices and very good quality food. Desserts were a little bit weak but okay. They even gave us a free glass of champagne for checking in on Yelp. The only problem I had was that the lines were super long to get in. Looked like there were plenty of tables available but they couldn't keep up with clearing them as people leave. We waited about 45 minutes to get in.
Wonderful buffet, it was SO good and so big. Loved every bit of it, highly recommend coming here for sure.

Bacchanal Buffet is arguably the quintessential Las Vegas buffet. 

It's always on my "Need to hit up this place" list whenever I go to Vegas. Their offerings are comprehensive: Everything from fresh seafood to Italian to Mexican to Chinese. But I have come to find that with buffets, you definitely sacrifice quality for quantity.

The menu is always rotating but having come here months - even years apart - there are some pretty consistent items on the menu, or at least pretty consistent flavor profiles. The seafood is always tasty. The Mexican offerings can be weak at times with insanely dry meats (e.g. barbacoa). The meats (e.g. prime rib) are always a win. The Chinese food is always my favorite here because they really nail the Chinese-American sweet and sour tastes. The Italian selection can be hit or miss. The pizza is weak, and I would not waste stomach real estate on it. But the pastas are always perfect.

The desserts are by far the weakest items on the menu. I have a theory that the desserts at all the buffets are basically from the same distributor because they all tend to look the same. Even the cakes all look the same (and have that same plastic wrapping). In so much, that when I considered reviewing other buffets in Vegas, I couldn't help but come back to, "Man, all the desserts taste the same. I wonder if they all come from the same place."

Service can suck depending when you are here. I have only been here during lunch, so I cannot comment on breakfast/brunch or dinner. But I have been here when it's crowded (noon time) and when it's pretty-okay like after 3 PM. When it's busy, it's hard to even get a water. I'd recommend they just set up a soda fountain and free up the waiters.

Well, what do we have here? Another slam dunk, a home run, a touch down, a perfect ten, a hole in one, ya dig?

It turns out all the things my coworker was describing to me about this buffet were true. It is, without question, the greatest buffet I have ever had the pleasure of sampling (so far). Just a caveat upfront: this place ain't cheap, so be prepared to open up your wallet and spend some mula. But trust me...it's worth every single last penny you own. I'd sell my last pair of JNCOs just to eat at this place if I had to!

Not gonna lie; probably my favorite thing about the breakfast buffet in particular is the bottomless Mimosas for the all time nominal fee of $15. I mean, the waitress literally walks around with a pitcher of sweet, magical Mimosa juice to constantly refill your glass until you get so tipsy, you forget what day it is. My wife was so f*cked up afterwards that I had to practically hand carry her back to our hotel room. It was hysterical!

But the food...oh lawd! It's to DIE for! This is the epitome of a buffet done right. And I can only describe this buffet in one word: HUUUUGE! Obviously, there are way too many items here to list off. But my personal favorites were the cheesy scrambled eggs, shrimp and grits, and home-fried potatoes. Nothing was short of delicious. And the presentation on the line is top notch.

Upon the wife's request, we'll return one more time before leaving this beautiful city to try the dungenes crab legs. Yes! They actually have dungenes crab legs, y'all! Between that, and the bottomless supply of Mimosas, I gotta give Bacchanal Buffet 5 drunk-as-a-skunk wives who can barely walk straight out of 5.

I really wanted to try this and love it. But have to say that for the money I expected alittle better.  The crab legs were wonderful and the service was excellent.  But honestly several of the dishes We got were not great.  The deserts were all pretty and a couple were excellent we just got a bunch and all shared.  I liked the gellato the best. All in all it was a good meal but just not worth the price.
Was there for my B'day (Feb) for Dinner on Friday Night. I was highly disappointed because the food didnt taste good nor fresh. I dont know why?!

Ohhhhh LAWDY! BUFFETS! I am usually hit or miss with buffets, Im not super into gourmet foods so its like meh with me! 

There are many different selections from this buffet and it's also in 2 different room if you weren't sitting in the back you would probably never noticed that there is a back area of the buffet as well. I followed 2 of the other people who are on our table and it brought me to the macaroni and cheese, prime rib, lamb chops, ribs, and chicken tenders with tater tots station. the way some of the food is served are in little metal  look basket things like fry baskets but they're really cute the only thing is you can only grab 1 or 2 at a time without having a full plate. the first place I got included lamb chops, which I have never tried, so I was really excited. I also got some chicken tenders with French fries and tater tots and a side of macaroni and cheese. I thought down to my plate of goodies and took a bite, the first thing I took a bite out of with macaroni and cheese and left me a little sad and needed seasoning for sure. It was pretty bland in my opinion. the second thing I tried with lamb chops, now I have never had lamb chops before so this is definitely a new experience for me and I was very pleased. the lamb chops to cook perfect in my opinion they were so so so succulent and tender and they were exquisitely seasoned very very very delicious! next I tried the chicken tenders tater tots and French fries. They were all seasoned soo deliciously it what a breath of fresh air. The chicken was also very succulent under which is also very nice because that shows that they were not some of those frozen chicken tenders that other places serve! 

there was so many different things to try out I didn't really know what to pick. I definitely do not like seafood I do like shrimp but only need the coconut type which they did not have here. Although a lot of the things did look appetizing I just didn't try them mainly because I do not like seafood or the way it smells. here they had some crab legs which everybody was going for that shrimp mussels and other types of others seafood that I really wasn't sure what they were I did try though the grits with shrimp and it was okay. 

Next to me my way to the back area where they were serving dim sum and ramen, pho, and different types of meats and cheeses as well as Italian foods. here I got some ramen, which had pork belly in it, as well as some cheeses. next I want to Mexican food area where they had carne asada as well as homemade tortillas and big pieces of Mexican corn. I also really like the way they just played the different types ugh salsas although the jars should have had a bigger openings so that way it wouldn't be so difficult to maneuver the spoon to get a spoonful of salsa or guacamole. 
between a Mexican food and the American type food thank you have an array of different breads that you can choose from I did try some of the roles which word very delicious and they also had cheese bread and regular pieces of white bread as well as other types.

Once I got seated I did try out the different types of foods that God I did like the Ramen it was very delicious and wonderful! I also tried the mini burger sliders, these were so delicious and cooked perfectly! I bit into my big piece of corn and was very happy and pleased, I taste just like the kind you would get in Mexico with butter and cheese on it, very delicious! 

Next I ventured off to the desert area where they had a humongous array of different desserts you can do some gelato  bananas foster to different types of cupcakes as well as chocolate dipped cones most and other types of yummies! opted for the tiramisu as well as a souffle and a chocolate dipped cone which was super delish!  

overall the buffet was very tasty and delicious I don't know if I would pay 40 dollars for dinner since I do not eat seafood and  really wasn't too too much that I would chose to eat, plus I'm really bad at some types of buffets because I'm so simple. I like normal things and here is a little bit of a wicked spoon slash Bellagio type. Overall all I will go back and try it again, once pay day comes!! Hahaha plus I wanna try breakfast!

THE best Vegas buffet. Yes the prices are crazy high. More than $50 per person. And the wait times can be an hour. I definitely recommend checking in to the wait list earlier then shopping around then returning later. There's not much of a waiting area outside of the buffet.
Once you are finally seated, you don't have to order drinks as the buffet includes juices like watermelon, mango and pineapple. 
The assortment of food ranges in so many different cultures. At the furthest end is Asian food, which includes dimsum buns, congee, sushi and so much more. Then, there is a pizza bar, sliced meat bar, and on and on. In the front, there is both heated and cold seafood items. 
I wish there were nicer quality crab legs though. They also have breakfast items if you go at brunch time.
Please note the times you dine have different prices because they include different foods. So just know what you pay is what you get.
Lastly, the dessert bar is HUGE. They have a plethora of different kinds of desserts, including a gelato station.
Definitely my favorite buffet in Vegas of all time! The price and waiting time are worth it because you will be stuffed and leave satisfied.

My friends says, "Let's go check out one of the newest and coolest buffets that just started!!"
I replied, "OK, sure, let's go!!"
So here goes another road trip to sin city. One thing is for sure when you keep quoting the same thing over and over, it really gets old. "What happens in Vegas, stays in Vegas." Totally true but gets really old.

I'm sure this is the new hip and happening spot. Great idea to think like Disneyland and start a "Fast Pass" program. Then up-sale just to offer patrons to pay an additional amount to bypass the wait to get in. If you wait for the time designated on your "Fast Pass", it would be $60 each. You want to get in right now, pay us $80 each and we can seat you right now. Never ending mimosas in two flavors and AYCE buffet, you would think this is paradise. You would swear up and down this is the best thing in Vegas because your friends says so and all the reviews says so. Here's what they didn't tell you.

"When you're ready, you can all go grab a plate to start." What the server really meant was, get off your ass from this table so I can come back with your drinks while you grab a hot plate you cannot really hold in your hand while waiting in this long ass line just to see what they have for food. Yes, everyone and their mothers wants the oysters, shrimp, cracked crab legs, and all the other seafood options. One of my friends waited for the seafood who I did not see for a while but did grab me an oyster to try. You don't want to know if I tell you I didn't think it was that fresh to begin with. A few of us decided to head towards the back where there's another line and not quite as long. Chinese food, Mexican food, desserts, and everything else. It looks pretty good but I really wish we went somewhere else for my $80. I'm just gonna have to stop at the roulette or craps table to make up the difference. We tipped our server accordingly because they did come around often enough to fill our drinks and clear our plates. Another over-hyped place you can add to your list. I'm just going to remove my bookmark now. As they say in Vegas when you place a money bet, "Good Luck!"

Had a wide selection of food , But everything I grabbed was cold . The wait was beyond long and not worth the $70 a person price. Was a nice experience but wouldn't say it was the best buffet they didn't even have pasta.

3.5 stars

Maybe my expectations were too high? I've heard great reviews of Bacchanal so my excitement level was off the roof when we came this past Saturday evening. Arrived at 5:00pm and the wait was already 1.5 hours for a party of 5! We called earlier in the day to see if there was a separate line for Total Reward - Platinum cards but the lady advised us there wasn't. We asked the hostess one more time just to make sure and sure enough, there IS a quicker line for Platinum card holders which cut our wait time to about 10 minutes. Woo Hoo!

The only thing that's a bang for your buck is the stone crab & king crab legs! Better eat a lot to get your moneys worth. The biggest downfall for the buffet was the amount of sodium in most of the dishes... even the king crab legs from the mass amount of salt they boiled with the crab. We drank so much water during and after our visit. Ribs were really dry and the pho broth had almost no flavor.

Huge variety of asian food (including pho, ramen, udon), charcuterie, taco station (which ran out of pastor by dinner time), sushi, etc. Huge dessert section filled with macrons, made to order crepes, chocolate covered strawberries, cupcakes, flan, tiramisu, carrot cake, etc. If you want variety, this buffet has the largest selection I've seen at a buffet, but it doesn't justify the $52 dinner price.

Our service throughout the entire stay was great, thanks to Rosa. Be sure to order your drinks (i.e. soda, tea) with your server, otherwise there are some selections of juice prepped in bottles by the taco station.
Socorro M was awesome! Great service and very attentive. Oh yea and the food is freaking amazing!!

Good quality buffet, the dinner option is the best. However aftermath of a heavy buffet is not very pleasant for those who don't over eat on a regular basis. So remember that - if you're spending $55 for a meal don't schedule visiting any show after that, you will surely need to use the restroom multiple times - of course this doesn't apply to those who are 300 lbs.

Wow! What an amazing place! Everything was "wow" from the entrance. Jennifer, our server,  was happy and kind! She accepted this Yelp offer knowing what it was and encouraged me to start this review. Good thing that the men in the family started off to get the food while I had time to write this review! There's no excuse in this place to not find what you want. The price is worth the surprise! Thanks, Yelp for the free champagne with this brunch!

There are two lines that you will go through before you're able to indulge Bacchanal's delicious food. The first line was just for purchasing your buffet pass. The second line is to seat you at your table. We waited about hour and half in total from purchasing our pass to being seated. 

If you're not super hungry, it's worth the wait. By the time your seated, you'll be hungry. Bacchanal's staff from the cashier to our waiter were very friendly even while it was super busy. 

Regarding the Bacchanal's food... The selection is endless. Seafood selections like Cioppino, freshly boiled snow crab legs, cold lobsters crawls. There also have a wide selections of Japanese, Filipino, Chinese, Thai, Mexican food. 

Also, the dessert selection was endless and also delicious. Overall, the food was amazing. Check out my pics at Bacchanal...

Hands down best buffet!! 

We were a party of 6 so we had stand in a separate line. Heard the best time to go was around 9, when their about to close because it starts to slow down. Sooo not the case! Line was still crazy long. But we got in time and still got the full experience!! Everything was great!!

This buffet is best in vegas but it's also one of the most expensive and the wait is really long! You can put your name down for the waitlist and go gamble or shop in the meantime. I guess that's the best part about the wait. The quality and variety make it worth a try if you've never had it.

It's ideal for those who want to try a lot of different foods. The made-to-order ramen and udon is awesome. The dessert station is also fantastic and I'm not even a big sweet person!

Bacchanal is or was once known to be one of the "best" buffets in Vegas but I have to say it is not what it once used to be.

The variety is there but the dishes are lacking in creativity and I saw more take out style Chinese, pizza, lasagna, salad, and Mexican food more than anything. Nothing against those food options but for the price I was expecting more upscale gourmet style dishes with creativity rather than basic dishes I could find back at home.

 The crab legs and oysters were fresh and plentiful! Make sure you load your plates full to get your money's worth here. I agree with some Yelpers who mentioned the food is a tad bit under seasoned. I do understand that because this is a buffet that the dishes can't be salted to everyone's liking but each dish I had was on the bland side. I think for the dinner price Bacchanal can do MUCH MUCH better. It is clear that they are now cutting corners and the quality vs. price per person has decreased. (Wicked Spoon has it down when it comes to this plus its cheaper!)

Service was shaky, our waitress could've checked on us more than twice for the two hours we were there. The desserts bar is the best out of all the buffets in Vegas! Other than that I definitely think it has now become over priced and I am super sad about that.

I have to say this buffet was a complete disappointment. If your looking for quantity, this is the place for you. The quality of the food was horrible. The lamb t-bone was so over cooked it was inedible. The turkey was very dry. The prime rib was also over cooked. The only decent meat selection was crab legs. The Caesar salad was just ok, and the sushi did not seem that fresh. The only thing we enjoyed was the crab legs and dessert bar. It was extremely over priced. There are so many other great restaurants in the area for the same price. Save your money.

Sadly I'll have to give this a 2 star just because I didn't have the best 1st time experience here. My BF and I were seated in a corner and next to where people wait to be seated so it was such an awkward place to seat at just because hungry and some what angry customers look and watch you eat while they wait to be seated. That's not the bad part of the experience, the food was great but they were not the best. The only food that I really enjoyed here is their arugula pizza, shrimp dim sum, chicken and mushroom (Found in the Chinese food section), and their bottomless mimosas. The worst part for me is that I also had stomach pain from eating seafood salad from here...Is it worth $60+ per person for brunch (HELL NO). So much for the best buffet in town, I only enjoyed 3-4 items from out of how many selections lol.. I still think wicked spoon is better (cheaper and their brunch menu is more tastier). Am I ever coming back here? Who knows.. Maybe if I'm forced by friends but if it was my choice probably not.

**Update**

I received a very formal apology from what appears to be the business owner, which I'm not sure I believe. She stated that she can put me in touch with the Risk Management group (sending your sick customers in the direction of lawyers is laughable) AND she would like me to take her up on a buy 1 get 1 free and VIP line upgrade!! What part of my review, where I mention food poisoning and puking my guts out alerts anyone in their right mind that I'm walking through those doors again. WTF is wrong with people?? 

Motherfriggin food poisoned!!! You unsanitary, filthy, lazy ass Lima beans!!!!!!!!!!!

We had enjoyed this budget in the past and it's the highest rated on my Yelp search so we dined again. 

Simply put, without going over all the items I actually enjoyed, I was stricken with a food born illness and I'm friggin pissed! Sick as a dying dog I was cursing them all through the middle of the night as I tossed up every last bite at our hotel. 

If they were, legit and all, Brian, the GM, would read this and call with an apology, refund and drop the cleaning crew at my hotel a couple c notes!! I'm still piping mad today and this is the kind of unsanitary activity that kills people!

I rarely give a place 2 stars.

I'm not sure if I just came on a wrong day but this place definitely not worth the $60+ per person for dinner. Just go to wicked spoon which is almost half the price and 3 times better.

The sushi was just a mountain of rice with the thinnest slice of sashimi. So thin I didn't even think it was possible to cut a piece of sashimi so thin. Also the crab legs just tastes like I was eating sour seat salt. Everything else was just so so.

Overpriced, overrated and not worth the wait or the price, Bacchanal offers a wide array of bland, mediocre food that has somehow spent far too long sitting in the heat lamps despite the immense traction it receives. 

On the plus side, the dessert is very good. Perhaps I came at an off day, but this buffet has not left me much reason to make a return visit.

AMAZING! Until last night I told everyone I met that The Wicked Spoon at The Cosmopolitan was the best buffet in town. But no longer. The Bacchanal at Caesars is the new KING of Vegas Buffets. The selection is crazy, everything is fresh and the cooks are knowledgable and friendly. Have the pasta cook make you pesto chicken bow tie pasta....so good! For me, at a buffet, dessert is the deciding factor and this dessert selection is spectacular. Crepes, soufle, creme brulee, gelato (both regular as well as interesting flavors such as watermelon/mint and chocolate aztec), bananas foster, cakes, cookies etc. 

Finally, the price. Compared to other Vegas buffets it is awesome. During the week with your palyers club card is was $28.99 per person. You can't beat that in Vegas.

My only suggestion to Caesars is to train their staff better on the pricing specifics of the buffet. We asked 4 employees (concierge, Player Club and at the Buffet itself) about the prices and if there was a discount for having a players card and everyone gave us a different answer or simply stated 'I don't know" and all 4 were incorrect.

Other than that, the place is beautiful and food is amazing. I HIGHLY recommend it!
My first trip to Vegas and had great experience plus very bad experience but this buffet was out of the world. Very well organized and lot of options. Will definitely be back for more
A must go to when visiting Las Vegas. The food selection, the experience is absolutely worth the price. BTW - I checked in on Yelp and got a free drink. Enjoy!

This is truly the superior buffet in Las Vegas. I've tried so many buffets hear and nothing compares to bacchanal! There's a nice variety of foods and desserts and you can really taste the quality in their food. If you're debating on whether or not to splurge on this place I say go for it!

ラスベガスで一番美味しいと言われている
バフェです。ランチで行ってきました。
種類が本当に豊富で驚きました。ジャンルも中華、イタリアン、メキシカン、和食など
どの国の人も満足出来ると思います。
デザート類も種類が多かったのですが、
アイスが冷蔵庫の匂い？が移っていて変な味がしたこと、冷たいデザートを盛りたいのに熱いお皿しかなかったことが残念でした。(デザートは以前行った、Ariaの中のバフェの方が良かったです)
少し値段は高いですが、どこのバフェに行くか迷っているなら行ってみてもいいかもしれません。ピーク時は2、3時間待つこともあるようですが、こちらはチケットを発券し
その時間に戻ってくれば良いので長い行列に並ばず、他のことをして待っていられます。
その点はいいと思います。(ラスベガスでこのシステムがあるのは、このバフェだけのようです)

Quality Food! I've ate at most of the buffets on the strip (as well as off the strip) and I would have to say they serve quality food. From their Asian section (Japanese/Chinese) to Italian (Pizza, meatballs) to Mexican (Street tacos) to American food (Prime rib, etc), I would have to say all of the food that I've tried taste great. They have a wide variety to choose from and they execute on most, if not all their dishes. I was surprised at some of their foods, like the street tacos taste up to par with a taco place off the strip. The roast duck taste exactly like something you find at a Chinese restaurant. They serve tuna or salmon nigiri's that are pretty good. The best thing about this place is all these foods are all in one spot! My only criticism, hence the not five star rating was the seasoning on the prime rib or wagyu beef at the carving station. There was pretty much no seasoning on it. Usually the skin or bark of the meat has a lot of flavoring but there was no taste to it. There is salt and pepper on the table, but after trying it. It left me not wanting to finish it. Still craving a flavorful prime rib as we speak. A lot of desserts to choose from as well. Gelato/ice cream, molten cake, etc. A new item I tried was the Mochi ice cream. I honestly think it was too defrosted, so the texture of the mochi was off putting. Overall, my wife and I enjoyed our dinner. Ambiance of the restaurant is always nice (It's in the Cesar's so I wouldnt expect any less). Depending on the time you go, there may be a line, so the earlier you get here the better. As far as price, it is a little pricey, but again for dinner you do get seafood (crab legs, shrimps) and prime rib and like I mentioned in my review- the food is quality.
This is one of the famous buffet in Las Vegas. On weekdays brunch time, it's $44.99 per person. Lots of choices. You can stay 2 hours to enjoy and check in on Yelp to get a free wine.

We came here in the switch from breakfast to lunch so we got to sample a little bit of both worlds.  I wish there were more breakfast items, because I'm more of a breakfast person than a lunch person.  

All in all, its a pretty good buffet but nothing I selected was memorable unless you count potatoes.  I felt like it was just an array of average food.  I think it must've been an off day.

The Bacchanal Buffet was a great experience with my wife and family. We were all in vegas this past weekend and wanted to eat here to celebrate my sister's birthday. I was running late to meet up with my parents and sister and husband. So they waited in line first. They told me that you had to grab a ticket to reserve a time to come back since there was a long wait or you could pay $20 plus the dinner price (around $53) just to not wait the 2 hours and wait in line. So they were waiting in line around 6:15PM on a Saturday. My wife, her parents and I finally met up with my family in front of the buffet. I saw that they had a separate line for the total rewards members; a seven stars, diamond and platinum line and a regular line to wait. This was the first time I got to use my diamond players card to my advantage. There wasn't anyone in the diamond line so I walked right up. The worker called me and we basically just had to pay and walked right into the buffet. No waiting at all! This was the best use of my diamond card and started off the Bacchanal Buffet experience on a good note!

We were seated right at the front. I believe they seat the higher card holder members in their own area. So there was 8 of us and they gave us a nice 8 person table with a great location next to the seafood kitchen at the front of the buffet. The worker told us all the different kitchens and locations. The buffet is huge! You walk to the back of the buffet and turn the corner and they have 2 other kitchen areas to eat at. 

The asian kitchen had some really good food. They had duck and dim sum and ramen/udon/pho. They also had sushi there and steamed crabs that were really fresh. I got the steamed crabs and the worker was really nice. The steamed crabs are brought out in pots so if they run out they have to make more and you just have to wait or come back for the next batch. They have an american and italian section. The wagyu beef sliders were so good! A definite must try! The meat kitchen had so much good food. They had lamb chops, ribs, prime rib, and other goodness. They had little bottles of juice. The horchata was delicious! The seafood kitchen had oysters, cold crab legs and shrimp and some fish. There was so much food to choose from. I would definitely come back to try out more food as there was way too much good food to choose from. The dessert area had really good desserts as well. They had shave ice with different flavors and topping to put on it. The popping pearls were surprisingly delicious!

The buffet is decorated really nicely. They have lots of glass decorations everywhere and like a glass wall in the front. The buffet is really open and feels really big. The food selection is great and gives you a lot of choices to cater to different tastes. This is probably my #1 buffet now in vegas. The buffet is pretty pricey though with dinner around $53 a person. But this experience was definitely worth it and the food was excellent!

If you eat here with someone who is a platinum, diamond or seven stars member, make sure to use the benefits and cut the line!
Really really Poor management, they are only letting two parties in each time and party over 2 need to wait for an extra hour. This is really unfair.

Went here with high expectations....especially with all of the bragging n boasting and the $65 per person price tag. After all, it's Caesars Palace honey chile....There was about a 30 minute wait on Friday night. The place is beautiful, definitely not your typically decorated buffet joint.  Bacchanal actually has ambiance and a lot of fru fru.....for two people we paid $131 including a $10 pre-tip that I gave at the register BEFORE being seated. I wanted to make sure that we got some attention. Buffets are predominantly self-serve, but I do like my drinks and napkins brought to me with a smile. And my beverages re-filled like johnny on the spot. Anywho....the wait was finally over. As we were lead to our table, there were plenty of ooohs and aahs as we passed by the various stations and spreads because we were about to get down up in here! Sadly, the food was a bit disappointing. Overall the quality of the food was outstanding (for a buffet). But some of it was just tasteless. However, this is the Ballers' Buffet so when you are on vacation in Vegas, ya gotta do it!  If you've never had exotic cuisine to hit your palate, you will find some interesting things to sample here. The presentation is eye popping. And I watched the "Chefs" make the sushi rolls fresh in house.....However this is not the best spot for vegans...you will be stuck eating guess what??? A salad or noodles and rice from the Asian station.  Vegetarians and Pescatarians you are GOOD! I just so happen to eat Tuna and Salmon on occasion...so I found a few things here. The salmon was very fresh and of high quality. The "Chefs" even made me some without the heavy sauces. Now, I read about the fresh juices in other reviews BUT the ones on the Buffet are not the fresh ones to enjoy. After having the Tamarind juice on the buffet, I inquired. NOTE: It's always good to talk to the people handling the food because most of the time they know EVERYTHING you need to stay away from. ALL of the juices on the buffet are a concentrate from a plastic jug with water added....yuck! Loaded with enough sugar to send you into a diabetic coma. There is a "hidden stash" of actual fresh squeezed juices, that you have to REQUEST. However; there is nothing indicating that you must ask. I immediately guzzled two fresh cucumber juices to calm my system down from the shock of the other crap. To wrap this all up in a pretty little bow, my Partner is a meat-eater and was not impressed. I have a palate for good food and overall, I was not impressed. We were not impressed with the value. It was not worth the price. A whole lot of pomp and circumstance, failure on the execution. Service was good. It is definitely a spot for people who have never had better food, and want to ball out of control while on vacation. If your usual intake is McDonald's, Hamburger Helper and/or Olive Garden, then you will be impressed and delightfully satisfied. If you enjoy really good food.....then this is hit or miss.

Very weak during lunch. Vegas has too many better options. I wanted to try it cause it's so hyped up right now.. not worth the 2 hour wait on a Sunday. Food was terrible, most of it. Oyster quality sucked. Prime rib was over cooked and salty. Sushi fish was okay, but the rice made it nasty. The steamed crab legs were good, and the yellow curry. Then I enjoyed the green tea and horchata. The dessert section was very weak. Overall this place is pretty small... and I was very disappointed.

Not worth the hype and I probably won't be back.

First of all, I'm not a big buffet person, so I may be biased, but I had high expectations of Bacchanal after all the rave reviews, and was quite disappointed. 

We got there early for dinner on a Friday, and it was not packed at all. The decor and everything was quite nice, well presented. I didn't really care for our chairs that were like big sofa chairs with arm rests, making it hard to get in and out.

The food was just so-so, nothing that really stood out. The meat was either overcooked, or fish was just not tasty, crab was mushy, oysters were dry. I actually thought the pizza at Bellagio buffet was way better, and the only thing I really liked here were the soup dumplings, various cheeses, the nachos, and desserts. Clearly, not worth $60+! I would have to say the macarons and iced thai boba were clear favorites from the desserts.

Overall, I would rather have one nice meal, than so-so foods at this price.

Wow! This isn't just a nice place to dine. It's  an attraction. Talk about "all you can eat." No one could eat this much.

You'll want to, though. There are cuisine's from 'round the world, each better than the last.

Think you'll try just a little sample of each? Fat chance--whatever you try, you'll want more. Then a little more. Then...get it?

Don't make plans after your meal here. You won't be able to move.

The bacchanal buffet at ceasers palace is pretty good. Whenever we visit Vegas, if we plan for a buffet, it is invariably at Bellagio. This time we decided to try something different. The Bacchanal buffet is slightly higher priced, but the range of food items are more. The sections are neatly separated based on geography. The stations are clean, well maintained and regularly stocked. The staff was friendly and attentive. I really liked the food here. The only negative - the deserts were not that good. They tasted bitter; like they were made with some chemical or had artificial sweeteners and similar stuff.

The Bacchanal was highly rated by friends and all internet search reviews. We decided to come for breakfast/brunch around 10am. The line wasn't long, we paid and was quickly seated. 

Once walking in, we couldn't get over how beautiful the buffet is as well as the variety of stations. They had everything you could possibly think of; bacon, eggs and hash, seafood, Mexican, Italian, omelette station, charcuterie, asian, wagyu and prime rib, they even had crawfish! Everything was amazing, we came at a perfect time because we were able to eat breakfast/brunch and got some lunch items as well. 

The dessert station is in the middle of the buffet and has a good variety of items. Everything was delicious. I'm so glad we changed our minds and tried this place out.

I was rather excited to visit this buffet after the big redesign several years ago.  Previously - the Caesars buffet was something that didn't really pique my interest.  Even though I've stayed on the property several times, I've always found myself dining elsewhere when it comes to the buffet.  This time around I decided to give it a try based on the all the buzz about the refit.

I'm glad to say the buffet lived up to expectations ... for the most part.  

This place now reminds me of Wicked Spoon and the buffet at Aria.  It's much more modern and features lots of small exotic dishes along with the usual copious servings of seafood, meat, Asian stuff etc. that you'd expect from a traditional Vegas buffet.  Even the little taco station was a nice touch.

As for the food itself, the quality was pretty decent.  The crab legs were great and it was nice to see them freshly steamed and served hot on your plate.  The meat section was intense, with lots of options to choose from.  Unfortunately I was only a fan of the prime rib as the other meats I tried (pork spare ribs, brisket, lamb etc.) were all on the dry side.  The sushi was also so-so, and relatively dry.  However, the other seafood offerings (cold and hot) were pretty excellent and the dessert section was definitely worth saving room for.

The ambiance was nice, though I wish the smaller tables weren't so close to each other.  However it didn't detract from my overall experience.

Personally I still think this buffet ranks among the top 3 in Vegas (alongside the Wynn and Wicked Spoon @ the Cosmopolitan).  However if I had to pick the best, I'd still go with the Wynn simply because even though their selection is inferior, the quality per dish is just a bit better.  Nonetheless, I think Caesars made huge strides here and I would still definitely come back on my next visit to LV.

Tried this place in September a few days after the grand opening. Three words:

Oysters. Oysters. Oysters!

If I can count each oyster as a dollar-- I definitely got my money's worth from eating here!

I've been to the Cesar's buffet back when it was on the Buffet of Buffet deal a while ago. Now that they remodeled it, it certainly is a treat. The food stations are very well organized and have a lot of offerings from American, Seafood, Asian (Chinese/Japanese), Mexican, Sliced Meats anc cheeses, Soups, Salads, and basically everything else. I like how everything was presented modernly (similar to the Wicked Spoon). The only thing I couldn't dig was the huge ass dinner line that stretched for at least a mile and three quarters. Similar to waiting for your favorite ride at Disney land, it definitely built up my expectations (and my hunger) as my friends and I were waiting in it.

More recently, my dad was telling me how the Bellagio buffet was around $25 back in the day and how he thought that was expensive... My oh my how things have changed...

I may be the only person on Earth to think this, but crab legs are overrated. Seriously, everyone I ever see at a buffet piles plates high with these things, and it just takes up space and uses a ton of energy for such a small payoff. Call me crazy! 

But if you are like every other buffet attendee, there are plenty of crab legs for you to hoard, along with other popular buffet fare like prime rib, sushi, and creme  brulee. They also have some more original offerings, but to be honest after spending more than an hour there I couldn't really remember anything I had eaten. I think that's why I'm not a huge buffet person to begin with! 

The ambiance is luxurious, conducive to large groups, and the waiters are very attentive about drinks and cleaning up your dirty dishes. There are several spread out stations including Asian, Italian, meats of all kinds, and of course the precious seafood. Funny enough, one of the favorites of my group was the pho broth. Who knew?? I think the desserts were really underwhelming and next time I'd just stick with a little gelato and call it a day.

If you love going to buffets and stuffing your face, you'll definitely enjoy Bacchanal. But if you're anything like me you might want to consider if you'd rather spend that $60 on a delicious regular meal or maybe at the slots!

Food wasn't as good as I thought it would be, maybe we went on a off day and it was during lunch time but again that's still no excuse, especially with the amount you pay(40-50$ per person)...it wasn't worth it.

The food was very good and there is a huge selection. For the price you pay, this would be expected. Unfortunately, towards the end of our meal, my wife and I were asked to leave as we were told there is a two hour limit. Feeling apologetic, we did so. As we left I checked our receipt and saw that from the time we had paid, there was still 15 minutes left until it would be two hours. From some details I remembered as we left, it seemed like they had kicked us out to prepare a section for a large party that was coming.

Simply amazing! It's too bad they only allow 2 hours per visit to eat. We went in on a Wednesday for brunch and there was no wait at all. Their weekday brunches are a lot cheaper than the weekends. We were shown to our table immediately and left to explore the restaurant. You can easily spend an hour just walking around and checking out all the different sections. It is like a world buffet with different types of food. 

The day we went in they had a seafood section with crab legs, clams, fish, etc. They had an Italian food section with pastas, pizzas, some traditional Italian dishes and appetizers. There was a Chinese food section with different types of chicken entrees, fried rice, chow mein, egg rolls, etc. There was a breakfast section with your typical brunch fare like eggs, hash browns, meats, chicken waffles, sausages, etc. There was an american bbq section with grilled and smoked meats that was very good too. They had a dessert section with lots of fresh cookies, cakes, ice cream, pastries, donuts, fresh fruit, tarts, puddings, etc. 

Everything we tried was very good! I was surprised thinking the variety and food options would be about the best thing about Bacchanal and thats what you would be paying for. I was so wrong, not only are there tons of food options but the food actually tasted good and not like your typical cafeteria style buffet food. I can talk about each and everything we ate but I'll probably run out of room in this review. The only thing I can say for sure is next time im in Vegas I will be returning for brunch or maybe even dinner. They have so much food for brunch I can only imagine what all they would have for Dinner on a weekend. Their staff is friendly and happy to answer any questions you may have. Our table was checked on frequently and drinks were refilled on time.  I highly recommend Bacchanal.

Awesome buffet! Huge and so much to choose from! Why not 5 stars? The PRICE Holy hell it's expensive! We came for my mom's bday (about 8 of us) and had to pay gratuity in advanced (totally ok with that) but it was $85 per person!!! Soooo insane! I just can't pay that Everytime lol that's like one hotel room at the linq haha but it it's delicious! 

I would recommend everyone try it once in their life. It's bomb everything tastes fresh and the desert selection is insane! Just be prepared to wait hrs to get in or upgrade to platinum status. Either way, you're spending money lol

This buffet was amazing! The price was alright considering it's on the strip & inside a casino, we paid around $60 per person. It had a lot of selection and the steamed crab legs were my favorite. The dessert was amazing-a lot of little bite sized options which included sugar free and vegan options as well. 

The only thing that needs to be fixed is the monitoring of patrons-we were eating when we noticed the table in front of us had left for the day. Then, a group of about 6 women had come in and sat down. The server immediately noticed and came over, calling a manager. These women had snuck in! I guess it's easy to do since the bathrooms are outside the restaurant. 

Overall, I'd definitely be back. I loved the food choice and selection. It was a nice atmosphere. Good for a special occasion!

We stopped here about 3:45pm on a Wednesday. My husband found rave reviews on his Korean website that he uses. He said the line would be long and we'd have to wait but there was no line when we got there. The cashier was nice. Took our $200+ and seated us. We didn't know where to go so we kinda just walked around aimlessly to each station. In the cold side with the cold crab legs there was a sign stating there were steamed crab legs in the Italian section. But there was no one to ask where the Italian station. I finally realized it was by the pizza and you actually had to request the crab legs from the cook behind the counter. They were both, cold or hot, overly salted and it was hard to swallow without trying to take a sip of water which we didn't have because no one came to our table for at least the first 20 minutes. During the meal it got busier and i noticed there were different levels of customers: members and non members. We were obviously non members, because members got the grand tour of the buffet by the cashiers. Members also got their drinks right away and their empty dishes cleared so they didn't look like fatties. Our "server" waited until we left to clear our plates and we actually wanted something else to drink but literally it wasn't until Joe or whoever took over and said our server went on break that we actually got refills on our water and ordered drinks. By that time we were pretty much done. The food selection was no more than a glorified Golden Corral. There was no lobster and the sushi rolls were all gluten free=no thanks. The dessert section was good however each piece was essentially the same batter but just decorated differently. The meat section was probably the best. Obviously if you're paying over $100/person you're going to eat the most expensive things on the buffet and not get suckered into eating things like rice and noodles which cost them mere cents to make. The oysters were good but they weren't cleaned as we were eating sand with them. Overall I would say it was ok but definitely not worth the money and if you're not a member you won't get the customer service. I say save your money and go to Golden Corral where you could eat there 10x.

*correction, I think the buffet was only $50/person but we got charged twice?

I came to this buffet last year with my husband and one of my best friends. We ate a lot of crab and I remember it tasting quite delicious! So we came this year however along with another one of my best friends and my best friend's sister. 
This buffet is rather pricey and honestly it is not worth it unless you fill up on the crab. The oysters were horrible. My husband loves oysters and he could not stand it. There was a little mini scallop salad from the Asian section which was okay, but definitely did not deserve the money we spent to eat "good." I never trust buffet sushi anyway, but the sushi really did not look good. The prime rib was overcooked and the mussels were literally swimming in butter that had absolutely no remarkable flavors. I tried a few things like the caprese salad, the mini burgers, the mini nachos, the gyoza, vegetable and spring rolls. Honestly the only thing I really enjoyed was the crab, the stir fry noodles, and pistachio gelato and if that was all I was able to enjoy while eating at this buffet, I would rather spend my money somewhere else. I will not be returning. $55 for what??
I would give 1 star but I am giving 3 stars because the person taking care of us was very quick in removing empty plates and refilled our drinks promptly.

Hmmmm don't know where to start! The food was good and it has a huge selection of so many different types of food! I got a Groupon for 2 for a Mon-Thursday deal so it's the same price as regular but it included 2 drinks. We each ordered a mimosa and a champagne. I like Groupon! Friday is considered weekend so it's $10 more expensive per person. 
There was no line when we came around 4:30 on a Thursday. We got seated/ordered drinks and didn't want to start getting our food until 4:45ish. 
I don't eat much so this was for experience not so much for the food. 
The crab legs I looked forward to but left with disappointment. It was not juicy nor sweet like a good crab meat should taste. The steaks were good, surprisingly I didn't like the wagyu steak as much, it was soft but not much flavor. 
The sweets table was awesome though! I ate so much macarons hahaha 
Would I want to come again? Nah. One time is good. But of course I wouldn't mind coming again if friends are going :)

If I can give 0 star I would. Not worth the $$$ to eat here especially with bad service. Save your money and eat somewhere else. You can eat 2-3 other buffet better than this place. And I wouldnt call it the best buffet just cuz theres alot of food choices; I prefer quality over quantity.

I've been to this tourist hotspot a few times now. Every single time I'm struck by how much food there is to choose from. The logic goes something like this: "Maybe if I have one bite of everything, I can try it all." That said, I'm not really a fan of buffets -  generally speaking, but after this one was recommended to me, as the best, when I first moved to Las Vegas, I return again and again. Come with a very large appetite. Don't be hungover. Pace yourself and leave lots of space for dessert. I kid you not, the third time I went, I ate dessert first, just like a twelve year old. Other times, I've not had much space in my stomach or energy to eat  the sweet stuff.

I gave it 4 stars because of a few things, lack of bbq sauce at rib station, and often running out of desserts. I don't mind paying $50-60 IF* no food runs out and there is sauce for ribs!! Maybe I'm being picky, but common if the tasteless crab leg station never runs out of butter, then why can't ribs have endless sauce? And how are they going to run out of cookies and mochi? Its Caesars!! Taste is great and I'm being picky for my $50-60 range, yes.

This place has good food and particularly the hot snow crabs. They had lobster claws which were flavorless, and though they had on display rock crab claws they weren't included on dinner buffet but after I inquired with the personnel they did go in the kitchen to get us some. That was very accommodating of them to do so. The short ribs with polenta, might of been grits, was tasty. They also had crawfish items boiled and included in some soup items which I didn't try because being from Louisiana I knew they would be like what I'm use to eating. All the deserts where good and especially the French macaroons and creme brulles.
Save your appetite to eat this buffet. Great choices. Our server Gregory was very polite and very efficient. Save enough space to eat dessert.

You won't be disappointed with this buffet. It's different from most buffet. They have some interesting dish. 

Service: The staff was friendly and nice. 

Food: I love that they have crab legs, raw oysters and snow crab legs. They have a small selection of sushi though. They have tonkatsu ramen, udon, pho and dimsum. I didn't try these because I didn't want to be full from them. They also have ceviche, tacos, Italian dishes and lamb. Desserts included macaroons, gelato, crepes and a bunch more. Wasn't disappointed at all.

I enjoy food but my taste runs a bit all over the map from a hole in the wall to 5 star.  The buffet delivers all my wants and needs in one place and it's a buffet.  While the crowds can get heavy on the weekend it's still kinda of worth it and much better than Wicked Spoon. 
Juice bar, chicken and waffles, pho, dim sum, sliders, stone crab , desserts and more.

This is the greatest brunch buffet in Vegas! They literally have any type of food your heart desires and bottomless mimosas for $60! You can sit there for hours and eat amazing food and drink! Our server Julie was the best! She was so friendly and provides service! Request to sit in her section and you will have a fabulous time!

Well, one of the larger buffets in the Sin city and the Country indeed.
to no surprise, it is one of the largest multi-cuisine buffets we ever had.
From American, Italian, Mexican to Chinese, Thai and other international cuisines, its got plenty of items to chose. I guess if they can add Tikka masala and Naans that will great.
We walked in on a Monday and to our surprise there was a decent line and wait time about 20 mins. Tip- Its only about $40 for Lunch on weekdays. You wanna go around first to see where you wanna start.
Start slowly into the large meals. There are pizzas, Fruits, Noodles, Rice, Sandwiches, Meat roasts, chillis, Juices, Soups, Sea food and more. There is a separate section for Desserts and keep some room for sure.
I guess I had about 50-60 varieties including Deserts. People spend about 60-90 minutes at Lunch. Plan for yourself to get there early for Lunch.
This high rated Buffet in Las Vegas is worth a try unless you have been here before.

Bacchanal Buffet..what can i say? It isnt #1 for no reason! 
Ive been here a few times, mostly when friends are visiting.
This buffet is the only buffet id go to, the food is really good quality and theres sooo many options. But i mostly come for crab legs! Thats where you get your moneys worth.
The wait is usually about an hour, you go to the kiosk and it tells you when to come back. So dont come hungry already lol because you will get worse while waiting.

Great buffet selection! The steamed crab is a must!! Also, not everyone knows but they also have a thai tea float with boba at the dessert section! Definitely the best buffet in Vegas and is worth the price compared to other buffets in Vegas! This place is definitely expensive, but worth it every time I come!

Bacchanal Buffet is a must when visiting Las Vegas! They have a vast selection to choose from and everything is up to par. Usually Buffets will offer a wide variety of food that has your basic seafood, prime rib, salad station, and desserts and all the food is just okay. This is not the case with Bacchanal. I haven't had anything that I don't like. It's located at Caesar's Palace which is a beautiful place to look and visit.

My Vegas trips wouldn't be complete without dinner at the Bacchanal Buffet. Let me tell you this place is special. Prices range in the $58-$62, which isn't bad considering the offerings. Unlimited alcoholic beverages are a $15 upcharge. I don't drink however it's nice to know. 

Once you pay, you are escorted to a table where you can immediately eat. It seems overwhelming at first, as the buffet spans the length of the wall. From entrance to the rear. At the "beginning" there's the asian cuisine, salads etc. Plus fare from other continents. I'm a meat and seafood kind of guy and they don't disappoint. 

For dinner only patrons, you get hot crab legs, drawn butter with lemon and old bay. I can knock back three plates of those. There's also tiger prawn shrimp cocktail, escargot, cold crab legs, different types of seafood stews with mussels and clams, Mexican station with fresh made tacos, meat station with Wagyu Beef, Brisket, a selection of sausages, charcuterie with cheese and accouterments, and so much more. 

And then there's the desserts. Good night nurse. Mini Crème Brûlée, Gelatos, Mini Chocolate Bundt's, Strawberry Lemonade Muffins, Macaroons, Mini Cheesecakes, Sugar Free Options, mini bread puddings and tiramisu and so much more.

Parking is simple, I pull into the valet at the forums shops and its about a 5 minute walk through the casino from there. There's a two hour limit as noted on the receipt however I've never seen it enforced. Depending on the day and time, you can expect to wait in line however I never waited more than 45 minutes.  

I highly recommend this be you're "Go To" Dinner Experience!
Exquisite, gourmet food in small doses so you can taste everything.... The creating preparation that the chefs put into each and every item shows! A must!
Really delicious and so much food and desserts to choose from.  High priced but worth to try

You will get the most bang for your buck here during dinner. The variety and quality at Bacchanal are phenomenal, and pricing isn't more expensive than other hotel dinner buffets on The Strip. 

I loved the meat and seafood selections. The dessert selection is also lovely, with great twists on classical desserts. I wish I had more stomach capacity to sample everything! I thought the drink selection that was included, was much larger than at other buffets as well. My friends and I were there for about 2 hours, and food coma hit us pretty darn hard.

Service is typical of other hotel buffets on The Strip. If you can only choose one buffet for your stay in Vegas, I urge you to choose Bacchanal. Trust me, your stomach will thank you!

If you come to Vegas and believe the saying "What happens in Vegas stays in Vegas" then you've obliviously haven't tried this buffet. You are guaranteed to gain weight from this buffet at the Caesars Palace.  

One downside was the wait time prior to actually entering the buffet. They do conveniently let you check in first before having to wait in line again to pay then get seated. The first check in prints out a receipt than tells you to come back in a few mins depending on how busy it is. It's convenient because you can walk around the forums or test your luck on the machines so you're not standing in line the whole time. I went during CES week so there was a long wait everywhere in Las Vegas. In total the wait was over an hour to enter. 

The amount of food that's offered gives the customer a wide variety of foods to try. The only downside of the foods I tried were the crab legs. They were frozen and that took away from the taste of the crab legs. They do offer steamed crab legs which is the better option in my opinion. 
Finally for the desserts. The amount of dessert alone is impressive. They offered a wide variety of treats from gelato, mochi, fresh crapes, cake pops, etc. 

Something to try if you're looking to fork out some cash and experience something different. 
Just be warned, the weight from the amount of food will probably not stay in Vegas.

Wow this buffet is huge! Much bigger than Wynn but some of flavor qualities took a hit. Abundance is what matters at this one. There is something for everyone and it was a very short wait time. The seafood options are plentiful, there's raw bar, snow crab legs and stone crab claws, mussels in sauce were good but not like PEI mussels. don't understand why they keep the hot steamed crab claws on the opposite side of buffet away from rest of seafood. We tried a little of it all even though our stomachs regretted it later. The mushroom goat cheese pizza, truffle devil eggs, cheese selection and Italian station were stand outs. There are unique and standard dishes, a variety of international cuisines, many fresh carved meats and seafood. Their desserts were great and way too much selection after a huge meal. Some of us can't help but try it all! The cross station was the best, order a Nutella crepe with the banana foster sauce on top, so good. The creme brûlée was one of best I've had. Cute Easter cupcakes, unique variety. Truly a fun experience if you want to eat a lot. Almost $200 for unlimited mimosas or beer for two people and tip, for Saturday brunch. For us it was worth it, but I ddI find some dishes that could use some better flavors or preparation. But mostly everything was fresh and tasty. A nice reason to come to ceasers and check out the property and casino.

Maybe I am getting too old for buffets, but if this is the best buffet in Vegas then I am never going to another buffet. 
Yes the variety here is impressive but the overall quality is low. I wasn't very satisfied or happy after the meal. 

- the oysters were large but mediocre 
- the crab legs were all overly salty
- the "American wagyu" is a worse cut than something you could buy at Safeway 
- the asian section is awful
- the dessert section is all overly sweet 

Perhaps I'm a spoiled tech brat, but this buffet serves about the same quality if not lower than the cafeteria at my company. Why not get lunch at google sometime rather than pay $70-80 for a meal here and feel guilty and fat after? 

As for the service - servers were so nice but my water was empty after the first cup. No teas or coffees were refilled. 

I would pay $30-40 for this meal
But definitely never again at is current price point. You can get much better for the same and eat the same amount elsewhere. And definitely better and cheaper 10-15 min off strip! 

Vegas does not consist of only one overpriced street.

Wow, what a great selection. My favorite thing was how items were labeled vegan/gluten free/etc. I ate about six plates of food and almost died haha.

The good: a lot of variety, LOVED the crab legs, some items were really top notch. Things did seem to be pretty fresh with a good amount of item replenishment. Our server was friendly and knowledgeable.

The bad: a lot of items didn't have enough flavor, or they had good flavor but were exceptionally salty. 

This is great to do once or perhaps if you come to Vegas infrequently. Definitely a high quality buffet but I wish that the flavor on things was overall better.

We have been standing in line for 2 hours.  We are in the line for parties of 5 and up.  They have seated the other lines for smaller parties until they were down to nothing and here we still are after 2 hours... dying in line.  They have forgotten about this line and now it's wrapping around toward the pool entrance.  People are starting to sprawl out on the floor from exhaustion.  Kids are crying.  This is what we pay $70 per person for.  We have a show to attend at 9:30.  Never did I imagine that coming to a buffet at 5:30 would put us in jeopardy of missing a 9:30 show.  We asked if it would be faster if we split our party up (2 adults and 3 kids) and the lady said we may have to go to the end of the first line to do that.  Whaaaaat?!  This is 100% absurd.  If you come in a party of 5+ you will get neglected... So probably best to split your family up, as they prioritize tiny parties.  Or just don't come here.  It's not worth the wait.  I don't even care about the money.  This is painful.

I use to eat in almost all Las Vegas buffets,except Bacchanal,so I decided to fix this in my recent visit to LV.We were party of 3 people,line was huge and slow,but after 1 hour in line,we finally paid $200,tips not included.
I thought for that money it gonna be best buffet experience in my life,at least I expected large variety of food,freshness and service.
But,unfortunately,not in this case...Interior was dark and ugly,dirty smelly carpet with pieces of food and napkins everywhere,dirty and very old tables and chairs.Food was not fresh,bland and ugly looking.This is my worst experience in Las Vegas,I would not recommend anyone to eat there.
In my opinion the best,clean and delicious buffet in LV is in Cosmopolitan hotel,"Wicked Spoon".
review #9000: the hype is real. one of, if not the best, buffet in vegas hands down. it's on pricey end of the spectrum but the food is worth it!

I really believe they pay users to jack up their rating system. I would never suggest you spend $70 a person to eat at this place. The food quality was terrible and not worth the money at all. Long line for people excited to try this place based on these reviews and it's not worth it. Meats were dry, crab legs had a foul odor to them, none of the food tasted of quality. Only decent item was the tacos. Desserts were bad as well. I was super disappointed and felt like I wasted my cash at that place. Save your time and money...trust me! I usually post pix but food was not worth the memory on my phone

BEST BUFFET IN VEGAS. Possibly my best dining experience in Vegas. If you are planning a trip, make sure you put this on your list of places to eat. They have food from all different regions and it is all fresh and delicious. They lay out is awesome too, just when you think you've hit up all the stations there's another corner to turn and BOOM there's more amazing food to taste. The service was on point as well, my waiter made sure my champagne glass was full at all times. Wish I could remember his name because he most definitely deserves a shout out for being an excellent server.  Also, lets not forget this is located in Caesar's palace so the ambiance is top of the line and everything is easy on the eyes. Prices aren't steep either, check this place out for sure!!

This pLace is not tickLe my fancy.
From aLL the hype that you hear, this being a higher end Vegas buffet..... I honestLy expected MORE.

Food was just okay and the Long, unorganized Lines made for a not so enjoyabLe visit.

BacchanaL's onLy saving grace is it's dessert area. 
[One added star]
Not onLy does the sweets have its own designated isLand, the seLection is out of this worLd. Whether you're craving for some creamy geLato, a piping hot crepe, or even a few sugar-free options- I guarantee you wiLL find  something that wiLL hit the spot.

With aLL the buffets being offered here, I don't think I wouLd make a return here. Meh.
