When I go to Vegas, one of the favorite things I like to do is eating at a buffet.  My family and friends think I'm not a "buffet person" because I don't eat much but I still go because I enjoy the different selections of food!  From what I read, this is one of the popular buffets in Vegas. 

::Food::
The buffet seemed endless, so many things to choose from.  Some of the foods are served on small plates or on large pans where you can serve yourself.  We went for brunch so they were still serving breakfast.  Based on my memory, they were serving the following: Red Velvet Pancakes, pancakes, French Toasts, Fried chicken & waffles, sausages, prime rib, lamb chops, brisket, pork belly, Mac n Cheese, Churros, pizza, pasta station (choose your pasta and they cook it for you), dumplings, fried rice, duck, egg rolls, oysters, salmon, crab legs, sushi, and more!!  

 ::Dessert::
For my favorite part, they had a variety of things: gelato, cookies, cupcakes, lava cake, cake pops, tiramisu, crème brulee, candies, and cake slices, etc.  I was surprised to see they had Ube (Filipino Dessert) but it didn't taste like Ube.  Unfortunately, none of the desserts "wow'd"me.  

:: Highlight::
We ate a lot of Crab Legs!!  It tasted so good with lemon and warm butter. 

:: Customer Service::
Friendly but slow.  It took a while to get drinks. We had to ask someone else to help us.

::Tips::
-To avoid standing in long lines, check in at the kiosk.  Just enter your name and mobile number and when it's time to eat, you will receive a text.  I'm a fan of this idea! 
-For prices,  check their website. 

::M's Notes::
Located inside Cezar Palace Hotel

Delicious Food. Unique Experience. Avoid Weekends.

I recommend avoiding weekends. They charge significantly more for the exact same buffet. They say Friday's buffet had an expanded weekend menu, but my brother said it was the exact same the last 4 times he went on a weekday.

Delicious food though and a fun experience.

I went this weekend and it was pretty good! They had a huge selection of seafood which I love!! The dessert was pretty good! It was $55 person so try to come on an empty stomach so you can eat what you paid for! The servers were very nice and sweet and checked up on us. 
It was my first time with my group of girls and so the hostess showed us around the restaurant on where every food is. They have a ramen area!! It was okay but that was pretty cool lol.

Of all the buffets I've eaten at, Bacchanal Buffet is the best I've ever had. 

Now keep in mind this place is very pricey, but the quality of the food make it worthwhile. Even going through the atrocious wait is worth it just to eat here.

There are plenty of meats to go around, not the mention the seafood. It's not just a small selection, it's a huge selection of options. My girlfriend is a crab killer and all she does is pile up a plate of crab legs and shrimp. The other staple items like mashed potatoes, green beans, fried chicken, etc are all perfect. Especially the mashed potatoes. They are buttery and creamy. Even the pizza and sushi is decent. Rare for a buffet to ever give effort on pizza and sushi. 

Desert section also has a lot of variety too. I'm not a huge dessert guy, but they do offer a lot of choices. 

One has to do the prep work before you come here. Make sure you know what you're paying, be aware and mentally prepare for the long wait, make sure you're hungry, and make sure you eat till you want to puke. Best buffet in Vegas.

I would've given this place 2.5 stars for their crappy service, excessively long and unorganized wait time, decent food selection and quality, but... once my son got FOOD POISONING, my stars immediately dropped to zero. 

My toddler, who only ate the rotisserie chicken, pasta, and candied yams, spent the entire next morning and day vomiting!  My poooor poooor son.

The quality of food here is poor! I think so many people just eat the crab legs that most everything else gets neglected and left out for long periods of time. 

The line, which we waited in for two hours, was ridiculous, not because it was super long, but because there was NO transparency or organization. You wait in a line for an hour, then after you pay, you wait in another line based on your party number. Unless your party is 1-2, you may not be seated for another extended length of time. I watched a bunch of people pass us up because we were a party of 3, and not 2!

By the time we were seated (8:40pm), we had a little over an hour to eat. Our server came by ONCE and argued with us about the free drink Yelp check-in. After dropping the drink off finally, she never came back. No water, no drinks, nothing except to grab our plates as she quickly walked by. I had to go to a different server to get my son and I our drink orders. And when we ran out, that was that. No refills. 

My recommendation, go to Wicked Spoon in the Cosmo instead. Way better service, line is short, no food poisoning, decent food selection.
Lots of seafood choices! Can't pass this up when you're in Vegas.  The lines are long so come early to get your seats.

With such a high rating, we came here with high expectations. However even though there was a great selection of all types of cuisines from Asian, Italian, Mexican, breakfast items, seafood and desserts, but nothing just tasted that great. Quality is still much more important to me than quantity. Their prices are not cheap either at $39.99 per person for a weekday lunch without taxes.

Let me get this out of the way - I hate buffets.  I truly, truly hate buffets and the whole concept.  At the time I visited Bacchanal I was starving and my husband is a lover of buffets so there's a little bit of a conflict.  I was originally very weary of the price but we came on a day that was NOT the weekend so the prices were much MUCH cheaper.  We were seated quickly and the service was friendly.  There is a variety of foods (as it should be) and the food is changed frequently for the most part.  There were a few experiences where the food was cold but for the most part I enjoyed my experience.  This experience however, hasn't changed my mind about buffets in general, but if you are like me and can't stand buffets - this may be the one...and only one you may enjoy.

Let's end the debate for best buffet in Vegas because Bacchanal has got to be the winner, hands down!!! They have cuisines from all around the world--American, Italian, Mexican (a made to order taco bar!), Chinese, Japanese, Vietnamese and a made to order noodle soup section too. Not to mention they have an extensive seafood section!! And once you're done with main courses, there's a HUGE island of desserts.

Everything is fresh and high quality; it seems like they really try to cater to every culture's tastes. In addition, the service has always been good. 

My insider tip would be to come mid afternoon. My group was in late around 2-3. We paid lunch prices, but ended up being there when they transitioned to their dinner menu, so we were able to try options from both menus!

Only the desert table was good. Sushi station had two kinds of roll and two sashimi - very disappointing!!!Seafood was either cold and too heavy on the cream. And there are lines for every station. I was looking forward to this place, but was very disappointed. Not worth the money.

A nice end to our weekend getaway. Food was great, loved the variety. My eyes were hungrier then my stomach could handle. My personal favorite was that the shrimp were peeled and deveined! I had a plate of just shrimp, so good!!

Whoa! Food was aweeeesome!! I'm only bummed causer I got full too quick. But hands down best Buffett I've ever been too. The dessert section was so awesome! 

Only negative: the waiter was kind of rude. Like he was just going through the motions of having to be at work. He was kind of snippy and took a long time to get our drinks to our table. 

But overall food and atmosphere was pretty good.  It was expensive a.f though be prepared to spend at least 120 for two people.

You know how buffets even in vegas seem to be just average to good food at best? This was worlds above anything else in quality and taste. The brie was perfection. We went at the end up brunch when lunch foods were coming out. The breakfast dishes were tasty especially the broccoli quiche. Make sure you leave room for dessert.  You much try the creme brulee it is to die for.

Vegas is expensive. A Sandwich, soup and drink at a Starbucks will cost you $35. Might as well pay $45 for a huge buffet! Lots of different foods - Sushi, pad Thai, noodles, taco bar, seafood, soups, pastas, pizza, carving station, and desserts. Definitely worth the extra few $$

My new favorite buffet! Definitely better than Wicked Spoon but it is more expensive and you may have to wait awhile in line. Luckily, I went around 5p on a Sunday and waited no longer than 30 minutes. 

The food options are very diverse and you'll be sure to find something you like. I was surprised that they offered ramen and pho, and the ramen was decent! Definitely worth a try it you like ramen like I do. The prime rib was probably my favorite of the meat options and of course their crab legs + butter is a heavenly combination. It's nice that their crab legs are already split in half so you can focus on eating haha. The sushi was okay, not their best items imo. But the dessert is reallly good if you still have room! Gelato, tiramisu, even mochi ice cream to name a few items. 

Don't forget to check in on yelp for free beer or wine!!!!

This is easily the best buffet I've ever been to. I don't want to rant on and on about the hundreds of dishes here. You can check out a short video of the buffet at https://youtu.be/7q1A8BXm4qQ and my photo of the things I ate. I had done my homework before going here so I knew exactly what was good and what I wanted to get so I didn't waste anything on the average/so-so dishes. 

Pro Tip: Explore the entire buffet before taking anything. Plan out what you want to eat so that you don't get carried away and load yourself up with carbs and miss the good stuff. The seafood section and the meat section are the biggest bang for your buck.

Pro Tip: Their lunch buffet is for ~$43 after taxes while the dinner buffet is ~$65. A good hack is to go at around 2:30pm and start off with the things they have for lunch and they switch to the dinner menu so you get some of the fancy stuff for the price of lunch.

4 stars seems right.

1) The food is awesome. The best buffet in Vegas (better than Bellagio/Wynn).

2) Service - the waiters were fine, just the lamb chops came out 45 minutes late (after dinner opened) and I was continually told just a couple more minutes. Have to hold off filling up on other delicacies if you are anxiously awaiting something. My only "constructive criticism" would be to have the entrees ready when you open for dinner (or shortly afterwards). 

3) Yes the wait is long, but their queueing system helps mitigate that, and they do call you on the time of your ticket.
This is my favorite buffet when I visit Las Vegas. Wagyu steak is so so good! Make sure you leave some room for desserts.
Amazing service from Javier our waiter! Food selection is great and remember to check in on yelp for a free drink.

Absolutely amazing selection and quality. I over ate. I loved it. I'll definitely eat here again. Might want to have some herbal encouragement to make sure I eat as much as I paid. The check in for a free glass of champagne was worth it. The employees here are very sweet and helpful!

Overrated.  Huge set of options but everything was mediocre.  Prime rib was way overcooked.  American wagyu was too tough.  Asian food area was really mediocre.  Seafood was unimpressive and seemed low quality.  The bellagio Buffett is more expensive but worth the extra cost.
Food was ok but got food poisoning and ruined my trip. I would be very weary of the seafood.

What could I say that hasn't been said already about this buffet.  Exclusively my favorite and we don't eat at any buffet in Vegas because of the quality at Bacchanal.  They always have the best selection and if you go away hungry here it's because your picky!

Now a staple destination for when I get into Vegas if I have the scratch to treat myself. The breakfast buffet is awesome and you can get endless mimosas. The dinner is even better with beef, duck, crabs, oysters, shrimp, etc but also so much more and an amazing dessert buffet where they'll make you fresh crepes. All you can drink special for mothers day was also great. Service is impeccable. The line can get a bit nuts. Try to come an off peak time and take your time tucking in to get your money's worth!
The variety of food is good, but the taste is disappointing. This is the second time I tried this. Even worse than last time.

Food was good
Variety is there
Lots to choose from
Food are kept clean and organized 
Expect a long weight to be seated
High rollers get priority 
Along with Cesar credit card holders that are platinum

One of the most incompetent setups I've ever experienced for their Thanksgiving brunch.  

They created an 'Express Lane' in which you could be "seated faster" if you paid an extra $25.  I went for that.  Got in line around 2:45pm.  The line only slightly moved over the next 15 minutes because people were getting out of line out of frustration.  

At 3pm we were told it would be about 20 minutes.  35 minutes after that we were told it would be another 10-15 minutes.  I was only second in line during this entire process.

Then somebody came around at about 3:40pm to say they weren't accepting express lane tickets.  People started complaining (obviously -- we'd been standing in line for close to an hour at this point) so they allowed us to remain in the express lane (that didn't move).

For another half an hour the "EXPRESS" line didn't move as the regular line moved past.

At 4:25pm they took my money ($118 -- they still charged me an express fee) and sent me to another line.  

Around 4:40pm I still stand in line waiting to be seated after spending $118 on lunch.  

Hey, Caesar!  F U!  Your hotel is past it's prime and I won't be back.  Oh, and ditch the 'Express Lane' you incompetent twats because you F'ing bozos don't know how to execute it!  I mean, honestly guys, that was BAD BUSINESS.
Jennifer is a great server.  Wonderful personality.  Great way to start off my morning.  Food was good too.

Our family agreed that there was a big variety of
dishes which were prepared well
We also had a party of 7 and we were put in
a separate line and recognized as a large party for 
seating purposes
A negative was we didn't not have enough napkins and place settings when asking a waitress she did not get them for us rather she said your waitress 
should be with you shortly 
Once the waitress arrived we received what we
needed, but I do believe it would not have hurt
for the first waitress to help with our request

This buffet is overpriced. I have paid the same or maybe more to taste a way better buffet (at the Cosmo) and a slightly better one (at the Wynn). I really don't mind paying if it lives up to the quality, but everything here is a gimmick.

For starters service is ridiculously terrible. You know most places train their employees to move out of the way for guests when they're walking by, here you have to move for them? As if we should be lucky to taste tacos being served up by someone who probably just got released from a rehabilitation home or omelette's from a "chef" that messes one up, doesn't apologize and just cycles through another 5 minutes to give you it. 

It's a large buffet. They have a lot of sections to chose from. I did sample sizes of I'd say 75% of the food and nothing stood out. Really..NOTHING. Things were either decent or a disappointment. I was sad, I usually use table time to talk about how great or good certain things are, I was silent. I had to check my location and make sure I wasn't inside of like the Southpoint Hotel or something of that level.

Avoid this buffet. I don't see what's so great about it? If you want a specific thing I suggest to just find a restaurant that specializes in that in Vegas. If you want brunch find a romantic little spot that will give you a quality experience. And if you really want to go to a buffet, there's a great one at the Cosmopolitan. Even though this buffet is a little pricey, it's ironically cheap.

This Vegas buffet has most of the bases covered. The meat station has tri-tip, prime rib and more. They have Chinese/Asian, Mexican and American cuisine. Plenty of choices.

I think, however, that it's overpriced. The problems with buffets are that some foods may be dry, overdone or cold. Not all items are always available. I saw marrow sign, but no marrow. The wait could also be a bit long for seating.

On the good side, the Asian station offered tasty duck and short ribs. There was plenty of cold shrimp, and hot and cold crab. The dessert station was excellent. I will crave a coconut/yuzu custard after having it.

If you drink alcohol, the $15 add on would bump this up to four, because then you're really getting a better value.

Get the f***ing express pass if you really want to eat here. We didn't know about the express and nobody here has told us about it, so we waited 5 hour :) and the pass only $15.
Food is okay

I WILL NEVER COME BACK. ROSE NISON the manager is the worst manager I have seen. I would not give any star with their customer service. I was here on my Last day in Vegas tried to go to their brunch buffet. Price was ridiculously expensive and their service was not acceptable. I would avoid this place and go somewhere else with better service.

Bacchanal is really like a dream. My friends came here for lunch during our visit to Vegas because we heard Bacchanal was the best of the best. I don't know if it met all my expectations, but it was certainly a good bang for our buck. First of all, I want to give a huge shout-out to the staff - the woman taking our drink orders, clearing our plates, and checking in on us was so warm and friendly that it instantly made me feel at home.

Onto the food: when it comes to Bacchanal, it certainly has a large selection of food. There are sections for French, Mexican, Chinese, and Japanese cuisine, as well as good old-fashioned American comfort food. However, I don't necessarily know if I felt like the quality was all there - there were some dishes I had that were a little soggy and didn't have much flavor. Of course, this is understandable considering Bacchanal is a massive buffet, but considering we were paying quite a bit to eat here, I would have liked a higher standard for preparing food.

So would I come back to Bacchanal? Yes - it's one of those peak Vegas experiences that I feel like everyone should experience. Is it the best buffet in Vegas? To be frank, probably not. 

Tip: check in on Yelp for a free glass of champagne!

Great choice of seafood for buffet. Long line to get in on Sunday night. Our party had a "Caesar Diamond" card access, so it was NO line. 5 of us had a $316 check. 
Crab legs, bone marrow, clams, dim sum, desert section: matcha, ice cream choice, yum yum yum... portion control is hard to leash.

This is my second time coming here and it still hasn't disappointed. Javier actually waited our table this time and consistently coming back and forth to make sure our table was clear, but also making sure we had refreshments. Everyone needs a Javier in their life! 

Also, if you check in on Yelp, you get a free wine, champagne or beer!
First time at the buffet. Ask for esmerelda. She's the best. Buffet is huge has everything you could want

Very expensive especially on holidays, but the food selection is unbeatable. Asian food, Mexican food, Italian, seafood, and a huge dessert buffet including a make your own crepe station. This place is guaranteed to make you uncomfortably full!

The place has a ton of selections but the layout is so outdated. If you are not paying attention you will miss a whole section of food.

Beware Groupon pretends to sell a deal for $36 for lunch. Normal price is $40.
They are shysters as its only good for early morning. But you will never know this until you get the bad news upon entering the buffet as it's buried in the fine print way below. 

Lines are long but once in. Good service.

I prefer the mirage and or Wynn buffets.

If you don't want to be stuck in a 2 hour wait line, I recommend reserving online on Open table. Easy and quick! Be prepared to have room for unlimited drinks, and ALL the food they have to offer. Customer service by our waitress was always quick and accommodating. If you pay the extra for the seafood tower the only 'extra' you get is lobster. You'll be more than satisfied with paying regular dining price!

I have a diamond card from my mom and the general manager Dirk (white man with blonde hair and in a grey suit - Sept 2, 2018)wouldn't let me use it. I used it earlier in May, and he said that isn't the policy. I had to pay $55 extra than the normal price just to get in. He was unreasonable. Do not recommend, esp being treated unfairly.
Food is really good with a huge variety. A little pricey but the wait staff takes good care of you!

When in Vegas, you've got to do a buffet! Typically we aren't buffet people, we prefer nice restaurants but Vegas does them so well! We had a reason to celebrate so chose Bacchanal. We had already tried the Wicked Spoon before and so we wanted a different experience. First up; be prepared to wait in a line and arrive at least an hour earlier than you would like to be eating. We arrived around 7.30 on a Friday night (May 19) and waited about 10 mins to check in at the kiosk: we then received. a receipt saying the wait time was 127 minutes, yes 2 hours. But less than 10 mins later we got a text to come back to the host. We waited about 15 mins in a line to pay for our buffet tickets and eventually we were seated at 8, which we were very happy with. The restaurant is huge and the selection offers something for everyone. We ordered our drinks and started selecting our food. Of course we didn't try everything and I believe the dishes change often, but I don't think there was anything we didn't like. Sushi was very good, enjoyed the little individual cups/dishes with salads eg. Beet salad, Caprese. Also enjoyed little baskets of fried calamari, antipasto; Ceviche, seafood salad. We skipped the pasta and pizza, they had a nice little tostada cooking plate where they make them individually to order, the carnitas was delicious. As was the carvery prime rib, mashed potato, vegetables. I love paella and had some of that too, and it was good but not the best I've ever had. The steamed fish in the Asian section was delicious. there was an abundance of crab legs, shrimp etc but we didn't have those. We enjoyed our meal with a bottle of La Marca Prosecco - very reasonable we thought at $25 a bottle. Opted not to go for the $15 "drink as much as you wish" option as I got to try the red and white and wasn't too excited about them. We don't tend to drink much anyway and would rather pay the extra for what we really like. Now, dessert. Oh my, these were amazing! So don't go stuff yourself with food and not leave room for these gorgeous morsels! Beautifully presented, colorful and just the right size to try a little bit of everything that appeals to you. Gelato selection (sea salt caramel mmm) chocolate covered strawberries, yummy little cheesecake "pops" so pretty, cookies and macaroons (which we didn't try), little vertical glass cups of some strawberry deliciousness, little carrot cakes, made to order crepes (which we didn't have) and the favorite for both of us were the little tiramisu's served in their own chocolate cups which can you eat as well. It's among the best tiramisu we've ever had. All in all, we had a fabulous, fun evening, enjoyed lots of great food (without gorging ourselves) and a nice bottle of bubbly. Exactly what we wanted. No it's not cheap - about $60pp plus tax, tip, drinks etc... but there is a lot of food, something for everyone, beautifully presented and very good quality. Remember it's a buffet. We never expect them to be as impressive as our favorite restaurants - but Bacchanal (which means feast for the Gods) delivers an impressive array of quality, tasty; beautifully presented dishes that foodies will appreciate. If you're willing to pay for the quality and experience as we were, you won't be disappointed. If you like buffets with a lot of food for a good price and don't necessarily like or have an appreciation for trying new and different foods, or see the value in pretty presentation, you may be happier with some of the other more generic buffets - there is no shortage of them in Vegas! It always amuses us to see people PayIng so much money for an upscale buffet then loading up on mac n cheese and pizza, but each to their own. But if you're after an experience with a fine assortment of cuisines and quality food, beautiful presentation, and you don't mind the cost, we highly recommend Bacchanal. Couple of final points, the drinks and table clearing service was a bit slow for a restaurant of this caliber but maybe they were short staffed. No biggie. Prepare to allow waiting time upon arrival, take your time and don't rush! It's an experience, the roulette tables can wait. It's a lovely hotel and plenty to see and do within Caesar's Palace and Bellagio foundations next door, and everything else around. You're in the heart of The Strip after all. Have a fantastic time!

We decided to come back again even though our July 4th experience was terrible last year. This weekend they had the President's Day special featuring specific items on their menu, including bone marrow for $69.99 per person, excluding gratuity.

I mentioned the bone marrow above, but there wasn't any at all when I went to grab some with my SO. One of the cooks said it would take 15 mins for more. We waited and checked again. We asked him again. He said another 10 minutes. Then we watched him and he took off the sign that said "Bone Marrow." Another hour passed and guess what? No bone marrow as advertised on the menu, and no bone marrow as stated by the employee in the kitchen. Not cool.

As for other dishes that we could actually find, the food was okay.

The oysters were more clean this time, but there were still hints of sand and strong ocean taste. The crab legs are delicious as usual.

The prime rib was definitely on point this time around. It was cooked perfectly medium rare with a nice chunk of fat surrounding the prime rib.

There were plenty of other options, including Chinese barbecue, Mexican food, Italian dishes like pizza and pasta, and American barbecue.

The dessert area is also fulfilling. Options range from gelato to cheesecake to crepes made on the spot. I love my crepe made with nutella and powdered sugar.

Overall, this was a better experience than when we ate here back in July. However, it was definitely not worth $69.99 per person so I will not be returning here with my SO.

We finally braved the Bacchanal Sunday Brunch Buffet ($50) and must have hit it just right because we only waited a half hour to be seated.  The check-in kiosks were not even in use because the line was not long enough.

The buffet is pretty massive, but instead of being stuffed with the filler foods of most buffets, it was chock full of quality items like pre-split crab legs, jumbo shrimp, fresh squeezed juices, noodle soups & crapes made to order, a carving station with 9 meats, and on and on...  It tried to get a little bit from each section to sample, but got full so fast just on the seafood station!

It is definitely a must try at least once.

Bottom line: This now wins as the best buffet in Vegas! In terms of quality, flavor and variety, it's better than Bellagio or Wicked spoon. 

We had:

1) Raw oysters (Kept going back for more. Not a single bad or slightly less fresh one)
2) Dim sum (Pretty good as far as buffet dim sum is concerned. Not the freshest since they sit under the broilers, but not overlooked and mushy either)
3) Seafood bar (Offers freshly steamed or iced snow crab legs, which is nice, rock crab legs, shrimp and more. The hot drawn butter dispenser is a lot of fun to play with!)
4) Meat & carving station (Skip the ribs, but the roast beef and selection of sausages are all great)
5) Italian station (Macaroni was bland, but the fusilli was really good and the mushroom pizza was to die for)
6) Hot seafood (The curried mussels and clams in cream sauce were both good! The dynamite scallops were okay)
7) PEKING DUCK (perfectly spiced, fatty, juicy--favorite part of the buffet!)

There was just too much to try everything! Need to go back and try the pho/ramen station. Didn't even get to the desserts! The only drawback is the wait. Put your name in 2 hours before you plan on eating and then hit the Forum Shops because the line is inescapable. They stopped taking names about 2 hours before closing time, so don't delay thinking the crowds will be less if you go later.

Pricey but definitely worth it! Great selections and amazing quality, especially the dessert section; felt like I was eating nectar of the Gods. Recommend the Groupon deal which allows you to jump in the express line and save you some time and money.

I personally think this is the best buffet on the strip. The only downside is the line, so be prepared to wait an hour or two. Or if you can get into the VIP or have Seven Stars, you can skip the line. So this is the famous buffet inside Caesar's Palace. As of March 27, 2017, self parking is free. 

I've been here for brunch and dinner.  Both have been amazing and nothing short of what I wanted. During brunch, you can pay an additional $15 for bottomless mimosas. Dinner food comes out at 3 pm. My fave here? The Bloody Mary oyster shooters. I may have had one or two too many. 

Servers are very attentive and everyone is courteous.  There's a Groupon for the brunch, so make sure to check that out for a good deal.
Wonderful brunch choices.  Lily was our server and she was 5 stars!  Would definitely recommend worth the money!

Overpriced.   Food stations left unattended for unusually long periods of time with empty spaces.    Food signage was wrong it missing.  Quality seemed less than.  Chinese area was pretty weak and Italian food station was sloppy and lacking.   Felt like a cafeteria.

The carving station area was top notch.  The brisket was outstanding.   So was the toast beef and bacon slab.   

Seafood station had subpar seafood and most of it was previously frozen.  Crab claw meat was crumbly.    Just not feeling the vibe.   Checking register ladies seemed disinterested and preoccupied with other things. 

Lack of seafood selections. 

Dessert area was excellent in all regards.

Not sure what is going on here, this used to be the best buffet in Vegas.
Best place ever!everyone has to try this one! Crab legs and most polite service around!

No time to fool around here. Eat, eat, eat! I have no shame to call this buffet place one of my favorite restaurants in the world. I go here not for variety but solely for juicy crab legs. We have been to other buffet places in Vegas but there's no one like Bacchanal to me. By far, this place offer the best quality of seafoods. Their crab legs are always fresh and bouncy. Lots of flavors! Ah! The sinful oysters! 

I don't know why but somehow we had the better crab legs on weekend dinners. This might be just coincidental but that has been my experience. 

If you go between 2:14pm to 2:45pm, you might end up paying lunch price for dinner! Unintentional but we lucked out half of visits.

Ridiculous.

Never in my life have I seen a bigger buffet then Bacchanal.  And it was also the highest quality buffet I've seen as well.

Initial impression was poor.  A cattle call waiting line (confusing on where to enter and unnecessary in the morning as there was no line for breakfast).  Once you get past that it was great.  Atmosphere was top notch.

Vast variety of pretty much anything (breakfast).  I was impressed they had healthier items like chia seed pudding and a smoothie, but the smoothie was more like a juice and in a minuscule cup. More healthy items would be great and would entice me back.   Otherwise probably not as these all you can eat buffets are dangerous.  

But for a special occasion, this place is great and a total experience.

For the price and variety, I really don't think you can beat Bacchanal. After visiting, I understand why it's one of the top-rated buffets in Vegas. It rivals (and maybe beats) my OG favorite buffet at Paris. 

FOOD: I was in Vegas to do the Rock n Roll Half Marathon, so we came for breakfast to have a nice carby meal before running the race later in the day. The breakfast spread was honestly incredible, and even though they were only serving "breakfast" at that point, they had plenty of non-breakfast options, including fried rice, ramen, pizza, mashed potatoes, and lobster mac n cheese, just to name a few. The breakfast items themselves were honestly top notch - they had huge variety of items that were all pretty upscale in their presentation and style, which I really appreciated. A majority of the dishes presented were not your standard pancakes/waffles/eggs! I also loved that they had a little pastry/muffin/donut section as well full of delicious baked goods, as well as a small fruit stand. My one regret was not trying the sushi and/or seafood options, as they had shrimp, crab, and other seafood items at the breakfast buffet, but I wasn't willing to risk it for the race. I'll be back though! Highlights of the breakfast buffet included lobster mac & cheese and the dulce de leche french toast. I'm still thinking about that! In case you came to the buffet to eat healthy, I appreciated that they had smoothies, pressed juice, and acai bowls as an option. But honestly, come here to chow down and get your $$ worth!

AMBIANCE: Since we came for breakfast on a Sunday morning, there was no wait and the restaurant was mostly empty. The restaurant itself is absolutely huge and beautiful! The service was friendly and very prompt which we appreciated as well. 

I know I'll be coming back to Bacchanal on my next trip to Vegas!

Everything high end you could ever think of eating. We had a platter of King crab legs brought to our table. Everything that swims in water was just about everything they served there, crab, ahi etc...The highlight was they had Wagyu! They had Elk sliders, crawdads, snails and everything under the sun. All the meats you could think of.

The price was $55pp, you should make reservations, the place is packed. The entire room within the Bacchanal was wall to wall food. You need to start in the back wall on the left side and work your way to the front. I only made 1/4 of the wall and sat down. The other side of the room on that wall is where the desserts are. Everything was international. Desserts from every country it seemed like. When you have a lot of people with you it's good, because everyone gets something different and then when just made our own little buffet at our table, try a taste of this and that.
The crab legs was the best, I sat and enjoyed them for a good hour with hot butter.

It was my sons 30th BD so the Chef made him a dairy free dessert. That was very special for my son for the Chef to make it and bring it out to him.

Expect to be there a good 2 - 2.5 hours, well at least we were.

There is so much food that its ridiculous, you can't try it all. That means I have to go back, yyyeeesss!!

I wanted to try out this buffet because of its high reviews. We came on Christmas Eve lunch so the line was extremely long and hectic. Holiday lunch was priced at 79.99 per person so I expected quite a lot from the food provided. However, when it was finally our turn to sit down (around 2 hrs of waiting) and I checked out the food, I was seriously disappointed. They had the basics, but nothing worth the price. The crab leg was not that fresh, oysters were small and frozen, lamb was extremely hard. Not to mention they have a 2 hr limit, but almost every station had a line!!! So you have to wait outside to come in, then once inside, you also have to wait in line for food. I understand that maybe it was the time period we arrived that the buffet was this crowded, however if the food was good it would've justified everything. But sadly, the food was really disappointing and I have no idea why it was priced at 79.99. No one was satisfied from our party of five and all were confused at the hype and price of this place. Would not recommend

I would say that this is an incredible buffet. It also comes with a pretty incredible price. It is touted as the best buffet in the world. I wouldn't even say it's the best buffet in Vegas. The meat I had was overcooked. The variety is impressive but the quality of some of the items could be better. The desserts were along the same line as some were excellent and some could be better. The crêpe making is pretty tasty.I was also not impressed with our waiter who simply needed to fill our drinks and clear our plates. Neither of these happened very promptly. If you have money to splurge on a expensive buffet, You will enjoy it here. 
Is it the best buffet in Vegas, I don't think so. There are at least two that I would

I've been here a few times already and frankly I just don't think it's worth the money.  All of the meat was dry and flavorless, the smaller dishes like mini waffles, egg, bisques, etc. bordered on inedible. Most of the desserts I tasted where meh. A few highlights: the crab legs were great (although the crabs did most f the work there, they were not seasoned), the soup station with Pho', Udon, and Ramen, and the chocolate strawberries. But all in all nothing that was worth the price of admission. 

I beg all of the resorts (if any of them are looking at the collective reviews for all hotel buffets) to rethink the product they are offering in a unique way. It's becoming boring. Uninspiring. Tasteless. 

Bring in a new chef from overseas and let them introduce some different flavors. 

Something needs to change.

Awesome buffet. Ive been to a few buffets in Vegas in the past but my god.....this one takes the spot for first place. Its a little bit on the pricier side but its for a reason. The food is just amazing. Tried so many things that were just so scrumptious and delicious to my pallet. Had 7 different cuts if meat...SEVEN!!! All cooked exceptionally well. Best flavor had to go to the brisket. Falls apart in your mouth. Had the Tacos as well from their taco station. Amazing!! Asada, Al Pastor, and Chicken. I mean c'mon. For my last serving I had to try the desserts. Tried the pistachio gelato, tiramisu, creme brulee, lava cake, macaroons, and while browsing one of there dessert chefs asked me if I wanted to try something special and naturally I said yes. He made me a vanilla bean gelato sunday with a brownie, fresh made whipped cream, and an amazing fresh berries sauce over the whole thing. This man deserves the employee of the month award. It was mouth watering and it didn't disappoint. He knew what he was doing. Just made our experience so much better. I definitely recommend this buffet to anyone looking for the awesome experience. Loved it.

I have no idea how you rate it more than one star. It should be zero. The food was really bad Oysters are uneatable, fish was hard. Prime rib was not prime or even choice. The desert....... well I didn't like anything. Watermelon was good.

Simply the BEST buffet in LV, period.

I am spoiled, like a child with unlimited mutual fund, after eating at this establishment.  The quality is top notch and i mean top notch!  While other buffets hide their subpar quality with salt seasonings, this place present what food should be:  high quality with acute singular service.  The $50 for dinner @ first is hard to swallow but trust me its worth every single penny as you will forget it with your first bite.  Expect line during weekends thus, come early and simply the #1 buffet in LV.  Don't forget to tip your server!!

I am not going to reiterate what has been said 1000's of times, but I will give an honest overview of this buffet. First, if you never had a buffet in Vegas, I would say that this one should be the one you go to. They literally have everything you would want, service is good, presentation is excellent, and quality is very good. Cost? I opted to just go for dinner and though the price was fair. Apparently there's a brunch for 2 special on Groupon, and I would probably give that a shot as people say it's cheap. But we wanted dinner, so dinner it was!

Everything we tried in this buffet (and we tried most things) was good. We honestly did not try any foods that didn't agree with us. Be prepared to see people getting huge plates of the crab legs. I'm not really sure why, other than they are expensive. I took the approach of having a little bit of everything on the buffet and thought that the variety was much better than trying to get my $ worth by eating the most expensive foods. 

We went around 5:30 on a Sunday and there was no line. I mean we literally walked right in. So, I have no idea of the wait times. When we left there was a line, but it didn't seem terrible.

Again, I can't see how you can find a better buffet.

Just skip it, not worth the money or the wait, 2 hour wait or pay $45 a person to skip the line, bringing the cost to $115 per person. Everything is out, takes forever to get a refill,  crab legs are only thing worth waiting for, ok over all but definitely not worth the hype.

I was going to give it 3 stars because I love the dessert station. The variety is immense and every bite is a culinary experience.   One boo boo was the bananas foster was cold.  It's supposed to be warm.
The overall buffet was a big disappointment. I expected much better quality. The crab legs were a good size but they were tasteless.  The prime rib was dry.  Plus my worst disappointment was that I specifically asked if there were king crab legs on buffet and was told yes..when I inquired they wanted an additional $55 for 2 lbs.   Can you imagine!!!  I've had tastier buffets for less than 1/2 the price.

$70+/person is not worth it for this buffet. The reason why we came here is its closer to the Bellagio fountain (and I really want to see and experience it firsthand). So instead of going to Wynn for the buffet, we went here instead. My husband and I have been to a considerable amount of buffet, and so far this place is not at all impressive. The meat is cooked dry, their Japanese selection is limited, and no King Crab. I would think for the price we're paying there should be King Crab. Their buffet should be priced at $30, IMHO.

UPDATE 2/25/19: So, we gave this place another try. But instead of dinner, we went for brunch. I didn't expect much since I had an unsatisfactory experience the first time. However, that changed! Their breakfast menu is way better and FRESHLY served. They serve Singapore noodle with a hint of curry that reminds me of my favorite Chinese restaurant in Portland, OR. They have a variety of breakfast viand using poached eggs, and I love poached eggs! Truffled egg cocotte and egg sardou. Those are now my favorites. Also, on their gelato menu they have Ube Gelato, which is similar to a famous Filipino ice cream brand, Selecta. I think I had two servings. I'd go back for more but I'm stuffed. I should have just went for the ice cream in the first place.  The service is exemplary, even on our first visit I never once encounter a rude hostess/waitress. They always check in on us. I would recommend brunch in Caesar's first before going for dinner. Their brunch costs $40/person.
This is the best.  The food selection, tastes and variety are second to none. When visitors come in, I take them here. Everyone is happy.

The best buffet in Vegas.  Great evening out, alone as the rest of the crew were still traveling.  My favorites: Lamb T-bones with mint, Prime Rib, Tri Tip and the BBQ ribs.  I also enjoyed sampling the wide variety of foods from different places.  Could have gone anywhere.  I chose this place as I only had one open night in Vegas.
This place is a must if you're in vegas! The good selection was awesome and so was the staff. It may seem pricey but once you see the offering I'm sure you'll agree it's well worth it!

Went here on Fourth of July expecting an awesome Vegas Buffet, and it was extremely DISAPPOINTING!! The service was good but the food taste, quality and selection was no better than a hometown buffet.  For 60 dollars, made it even worse.  They had terrible Asian food like steam buns which were from frozen I'm guessing, Mexican food was awful. And seafood selection of shrimp cocktails and cheap mussel salad and smoke salmon. The carving station: bacon slab, ham and sausage was either too salty or not enough.
It's a must in Vegas!  Worth the price tag food is fresh and the staff will make sure you get what you need !

Such a disappointment today at the Bachannal.  I have been coming here for about 6 years and wont be back after today. First we came here yesterday about 245pm and there was a 3 hour wait so we decided to come back today.  Line wasnt that bad and we were a party of 5 so we got to pass the normal line and go to a separate line. So last year the price during the week was 39.99 and we always got a 5 dollar discount using our total rewards card. Not today it was 44.99 and no discount. We got seated and got our drink order in. Food was ok but the items I always come here for were not here today when the dinner came out. The cooks were always rude when asked if there was steam crab they were rude and said ya in 2 mins. So i wanted oysters but they said none today. Few mins later i seen them defrosting in water and put on the seafood tower for the high rollers I guess. Also no calimari. No more meatballs. Limited salads . No fresh squeezed juice like usually. Prime rib was way over cooked. Only one round of refills and no one came back after that. So they charge more and get rid of some food. Wont be back I would rather go to earl of sandwich

Second time here.  Good food and desert selection. 
Went there Monday around 1pm and there is no line.

Just check it out. You won't regret it!!

We only had one day in Las Vegas and we were itching to eat at a buffet. There are so many choices, but we narrowed it down to Bacchanal vs Wicked Spoon. We watched many Youtube videos and read many reviews comparing the two and in the end, Bacchanal won our heart and we waited in the dreadful 2 hour line to experience what many calls the best buffet in Vegas! 

It definitely lives up to its name! The selection is amazing! Every item is made so intricately and everything had was spectacular!! I wish I had a bigger appetite to eat even more. 

Definitely leave room for dessert! There is a large selection of gelato, sweets and a crepe station!! 

Ugh this place is just out of this world. Would wait in a million lines to come back again!

Dec.13 is my Birthday . My dear husband and son took me  there  to celebrate . All food style  are excellent . My favorite crab legs . Best Hongkong Chinese dishes ,  The service and staff are great and thoughtful . They provide quick service for drink delivery and used plates  removal. Very nice professional customer service . When the staff know my special day. Ms. Socorro Lopes made special birthday cake with candle. Thank you Bacchanal Buffet to offer me a nice pleasant birthday  experience !

Great food, great service! Only downside is my group wasn't aware that online reservations warranted VIP price. Wasn't a big problem though.

Brisket was great! Melt in your mouth great!

Wagyu beef and oysters weren't great but everything else was superb!

Went to the buffet with my family and must say will only be going here moving forward ... 

Taco station was amazing carne aside , chicken, and al pastor tacos to order never seen this wide of a selection before .  
Carving station has more than you can ask for chicken , brisket and beef ribs all in the right places .
This buffet is a must see and must go to don't pass it up 
Great prices and ask for Romulus great looking servers and great food ...

The best darn Buffet I've ever dined for brunch or dinner. Both times I ate here were amazing! Everything from the crab legs, prawn, fresh juices, veggie frittatas, and lamb t-bone was delicious. I'm not a huge fan of buffets because normally they are not good especially the overpriced and underwhelming one in Vegas but not this one. It's everything you could want and more. When I go back in a couple of months I'll eat here again. It's that good. It's expensive, but hey it's Vegas and if you come here now and expect to fly by on the cheap and have an amazing blow your mind time you won't and you could just stay home for that.

The icing on the cake and what was really kind nice to see was that the Executive Chef of the Buffet was there both time I was there walking the outside of the buffet making sure that the the food was displayed properly was the correct temp and looking the dishes over for imperfections. She even told some of the cooks behind the buffet to take things off the buffet while I was there it was great to see that because it shows that while they may not be perfect they catch their mistakes spot doesn't impact the quality of the experience for guests at the buffet.

I can't wait to get here again for brunch.

Many delicacies and flavor combinations. It's a culinary masterpiece. Seafood and sushi bar was great. The gelato selection was impressive and delicious. Really a great buffet to sample all the variety and not just load up on slabs of meat as is the norm at a buffet style dining experience.
Every food item at this Buffett tasted great! Loved that they serve hot crab! Everyone has to try it when I'm Vegas!

One of the best buffet I ever been..Delicious and exotic foods.try the desserts. .they are out of this world.

Great service as well.

What a disappointment.  Paid $65.00 per person. Expected excellent quality and service.....what a joke. Definitely cheap buffet food. The crab legs were cheap Chinese buffet quality, the rest of the buffet were not much better. Service:  what service?  Each waiter is assigned so many tables they are unable to service. Ordered our drinks upon arrival.  It took our waiter at least 15 minutes to bring us the drinks . Poor waiter. I know it's not his fault but still the restaurant should had never assigned so many tables to him to where he can't service.  We will never ever go back again. Too expensive for the cheap quality buffet food and lack of service.

Best buffet in Vegas! Not sure it's worth the price for a weekend dinner anymore.
David the butcher knows he's meats, so trust his recommendation, and say hi, he is super friendly.
Chocolate bark with Whipped cream for dessert is a great way of finishing a meal.

3.5 stars.  
Normally, I don't do buffets but my friend had a diamond card and people were raving great things about this place, so decided to give it a try.  We got seated just/ after 10 minutes wait.  
Their desserts  were phenomenal.  I love the creme brûlée and gelato.  Try the Baklava flavor..  So yummy.  Their ramen was amazing.  I would recommend getting the broth with a lot of chasu pork (minus noodles to save room in your tummy).   The mini burgers (both wagyu and turkey) were something you must try.  
The crabs were a little salty for my taste.  The dim sum was mediocre...
The station were poorly designed as we had to wait over 20 minutes just to get crab legs or prime ribs.  
$55 per person including tip for a lunch on Sat.  Not bad!
Overall, one of the better buffets I have been to in vegas.

This place was soooo goood!  We came here for brunch and left with our pants tighter haha. They have a variety of items from different cultural cuisines. Fresh seafood, different sausages, meats, and so many things that I wanted to try, but couldn't because I got so full. If you come here for brunch, it costs less than dinner, but it is still great quality. Brunch goes until 3pm. Service is great, and you will not be disappointed. Enjoy! Check out my pics ;)

This is by far the best buffet I've had on the strip! It is pricy but you are paying the quality  of food. There are so many different things to try and 9 different stations of different types of food! I like that some of the food is pre-portioned out and is small enough so you can taste but able to get other food items as well. Since I don't need a lot of food but I like to sample a ton of things so the pre-portion is great! I love the sweet potato tator tots-sooo good! Their lobster corn chowder is also to die for! That is my favorite thing there. They also have tiny burgers that are quite good. 

The best part though is of course dessert! I think between my whole family and I we tried a little of each dessert. I love that they have cake pops! They were so good. I can't pin point one favorite dessert because they are just all so good. I asked for mochi but they only have that at dinner so I guess I will have to go to dinner next time ;) 

If you are a buffet lover you have to try this place out!

Really good service, when you ask for a drink they come with it literally 30 sec after you ask for it.
Alot of different food from different cusines
So if you are on vacation in Vegas and want to Treat yourself, i'll sugest you go to this place

OMG!!!  This was not overhyped!  The hubby and I loved this buffet. It was worth the tedious triple wait (which we knew to plan for thanks to Yelp). You get a ticket that tells you the time you may go wait in line. That line takes 30-45 min. Then you must wait to be seated. The whole ordeal takes approximately 4 hours including eating time. It's definitely worth doing at least once. We plan on eating here each time in Vegas. 

The crab is fantastic. I ate crab 4 different ways. The king crab claws were yummy, but the dungeoness crab was even sweeter and tastier. I ate 2 heaping plates worth. I heard the tacos were fantastic, but I chose not to partake. The dim sum area had fabulous hargao. The gelato was fantastic, authentic. The shrimp was amazing!  My hubby literally ate 50+ shrimp. 

We payed around 2:30 and were able to eat dinner options at the lunch price. It's hard to time for this because the wait times are unpredictable. If you can, go for this eat time. 

Bottom Line: Worth the $!
Good food but little pricey. I love their oysters and crab. Really fresh. However the wait Line is too long. It almost took us 2 hours to get in

We have heard for many years how good the buffet at Caesar's Palace is. We never got a chance before the other night to finally break down and try it. Well, the past reviews were correct. Best buffet in town!!!

Favorite buffet in Vegas! Came here during the week due to less crowd and it being cheaper. We were seated right away. The selection of food is great. From Asian, Mexican, and seafood. My favorite were the Asian dishes. From sushi to noodles. I would suggest to start with protein first since you will get full very fast with the carbs. Plus, you don't want to miss out on the desert buffet! Delicious, comes with all sorts of deserts, gelato, candy, pastries. Will def. come back here.
Super recomendado todos muy amables desde la entrada . Todo buenísimos. Nuestra primera visita y asta el momento estamos encantados

4 stars for *buffet* food, 3 for food in general. 

Came here for the first time last year and I had a stomachache so didn't eat too much so decided to give it a real first try today and left disappointed again. 

Sea bass - chewy/overcooked 
Oysters - was looking forward to these but they tasted blah. Took a bite into one and took it right back out. It honestly feels like they froze these bad boys up and then took them out to defrost. 
Sushi - wasn't expecting too much quality here but the fish tasted old, it made Costco sushi sound appealing 
Prime rib - dry and bland
Congee - tasted like watered mush. Adding soy sauce did not help. 
Ramen - flavorless broth. Instant noodles taste better than this 

Only things I liked:
Exotic mushroom pizza
Green Tea mint gelato 
Mashed potatoes
Their Chinese food section (and I don't even care too much for Chinese food) 

When all else fails, at least you have the dessert to look forward to right? And I had high hopes of turning my experience around by ending on a good note with the sweets. The dessert section was also disappointing. Is it just me or the selection here has narrowed down since this place opened? Got the banana Nutella crepe (3/5), green tea mint gelato (5/5 can't really mess that up) and the creme brûlée (4/5 Wynn's is better). 

PROS:
- Very diverse selection of cuisine. Mexican, Japanese, Chinese, American, etc. 
- No complaints about the wait because we were a party of 6 which 6+ get their own line so I believe we only waited 15 mins
- Very modern and chic. I'll give them that. Adorned with glass walls, modern wooden tables and semi-dim lighting, this place makes for a great dining experience regardless of the quality of the food. 

Forgetting cost, I still prefer the Wynn Buffet over Bacchanal. Now taking into account the $10 difference.... I don't think I'll be coming back to Bacchanal. 

The Wynn is definitely the winner here. Before splurging on Bacchanal, see for yourself. Or rather... Taste for yourself!

People have told me this is the buffet to go to if you're in Vegas, and they are right. Every time I been to Vegas I was make it a goal to try different buffets to see what is good. In comparison to aria that I went to yesterday, this is a whole different level. The dessert display alone showed that they are superior. The whole section filled with sweets (donuts, cupcakes, crepes, ice cream, etc). My favorite was the small little cone that looks like ice cream. They were just the right size and bite. The ice cream Selection was also amazing as they have flavors that you don't typically see at other buffets, like Ube, black sesame and lemon basil.

Food wise, it's a little above standard. The selection is good and there are things that was definitely delicious while others missed the mark. My favorite: chicharones and sea snails. You don't see these items anywhere else in other buffet places. I also like this egg custard thing for breakfast that I couldn't describe. The brisket was super tender and flavourful. Some of the so - so items: dim sum selection, sausages. The sushi area was very small so that was a little surprising for me. They also have various parfait and fruit cups. I definitely like that they have selection from all over the world. A plus is that you get complimentary beverages and service is great.

Overall, the price is high but you do get what you paid for so it is worth it in my opinion. One of the better buffets I've been to in Vegas for sure

All I can say is it was worth wait!!! The crab legs were juicy and sweet! The mussels were so flavorful. Tri-tip so good! No oysters until 3pm but there was enough great food to satisfy my pallet. Save room for all of the great desserts...and not the ones that look good but aren't lol. Gelato was great okay!!!

While the variety of offerings was excellent, I was very disappointed in the quality of most of the buffet items.

It might have been a slow lunch, but many items looked and tasted dried out as it they were sitting out awhile. This was especially true in the asian dim sum section. While placed in bamboo steamers, there was no steaming on the line to keep items at peak presentation.

I was also looking forward to the brisket but that was also lacking. The slices I received were tender but really dry and eventually unsatisfactory. 

The saving grace was the service. Everyone on staff was amazing, from the entry cashier, the hostess, and especially our waiter. Never waited for a refill or for a plate to be cleared.

With all the dining options available just on the strip,  I'm going to pass on Bacchinal for near future.
Amazing food and service. Would recommend coming herre with family and friends. Nice setting and mood

First time trying this buffet.  Was not disappointed!  The food, ambiance and service was top notch.  I was worried when I first arrived.  I heard the wait time can be long.  Got there at 1700hrs.  No line!  They do have a 2 hr eating time limit.  It is clearly listed on your receipt.  We were there for over 2 hours.  My favorite food when I visited was the veal, prime rib, Chinese roasted duck and the bread pudding.

I came here on a Saturday morning about two weeks ago before 10 am (we had a groupon to use) and there was NO wait what-so-ever! The cashiers were extremely kind and we were seated right away. I was here on a family trip and had to change my one year old and realized there was NO changing table in the restroom right outside of the buffet. The bathroom attendant was an older Latina women with a MAJOR attitude. I asked her where the nearest changing table would be and she laughed and said "this is Vegas, why would you bring a baby to Vegas?"....SO I WENT RIGHT AHEAD AND CHANGED MY BABY ON THE SINK. She looked at me with a shocked expression and asked if I was really going to change her there and I responded with "You bet your ass I am" ...well she didn't like that too much and started to complain to her coworker in Spanish but little did she know, I'm Mexican. I knew every word she was saying and made a comment to my mom in Spanish in a rather loud voice that I was going to let the staff at the front know about my experience.

I didn't and i regret not having spoken up however our experience past the bathroom situation was so lovely that I really couldn't let it take the shine away from this buffet. 

THE CHOICES ARE ENDLESS. There is pizza and sushi and jumbo shrimp so big that it's literally a mouthful. Crab legs, and tacos and all sorts of deliciousness. I am literally spoiled and now no other buffet even comes close. The selection was amazing our waiter was attentive. I do believe it's worth every penny.

By the way, changing tables are located in the bathrooms in the middle of the casino by the slot machines, go figure.

This is by far the best buffet I ve been to. It is expensive but totally worth it!  We went for Sunday brunch and it was phenomenal.  There was breakfast section, seafood, large Asian food section including pho, Singaporean noodles, sushi etc  the buffet was huge!!! I starved myself the night before and was ready to eat (and trust me I can eat a lot) but I only made my way through half of the buffet.  Oh did I forget to mention the dessert section? You gotta try the pastries and gelato ice cream.  They were soooo good!

Come hungry... 

I'm not a buffet person, and I definitely can't eat as much as the cost. But I will say this is one of the best buffets I have been to in Vegas. We go during brunch and they still have plenty of the lunch / dinner options available. The crepe station was sooo good and I love the fresh pressed watermelon juice!! Check out travelzoo and snag a discounted rate!! Also the staff is pretty amazing, they work hard and it shows.

I went down 18:40, almost wait 10 mins more in line.
Kinda lots people in there already.
Be sure in early :)

Bacchanal is definitely my favorite of the buffet options in Vegas.  The options vary and and the food is delicious.  The price is definitely on the higher end, but in this instance you get what you pay for.
Amazing buffet with unmatched selection!   Can't wait to go back again. The line is worth it.

I had been to Bacchanal once for lunch and I thought it was just a tad above average for being one of the most touted buffets in Las Vegas.

We went this weekend for dinner (which I thought would be way better than lunch) and I must say my opinion hasn't changed much. I hate reading that it's the "Best Buffet in Vegas" because it's not!

[Buffet]

Bacchanal does offer a decent variety of choices but I think the Rio Buffet [include the seafood section ], the Wynn and Bellagio  buffets are much better.

The meat section which had lamb, tri tip, prime rib, kielbasa and polish sausage were pretty tasty except the lamb which was not cooked correctly.

The chilled jumbo prawns were excellent but the quality of snow crab was pretty weak.  King crab legs only available for the Diamond members and above.  Oysters were good.

The rice was dried out, Sushi was lacking in everyway.  Variety of sashimi almost non existent.  Clam chowder looked watered down.

Your typical pizza and Mexican choices looked ok.

Dessert was average with cookies, cakes, gelato, etc....

[Service]

I do like that they have a kiosk at the buffet entrance were you can enter your phone number and then you get a text saying you can get in line when your group is called. This allows you to walk around and gamble, drink or shop instead of wasting hours in line. 

Don't get me wrong you still have to wait in line for a period of time before you are seated.

You do have the option of paying $35 more per person to have expedited seating.

The waitress we had could have been better but she was average service-wise.

[Price]

The price for one person on Saturday night is about $60 a person. If you eat several plates it's worth it.

It's $15 more for unlimited drinks. 

I personally think this buffet is way overrated!

The best buffet in Vegas if not anywhere! This is a feast of variety and there's really something for everyone. When you arrive, take a moment to take it all in, take your time and try as much as you can! You won't be disappointed. 

Not only is the food incredible but your service will match your experience. It actually feels more like a restaurant than a buffet.

(Don't forget to save room for dessert!)

I've had this buffet twice now and it's still great. I recommend going for brunch because it cheaper and you still get all the good stuff, just not the crab legs! 

The unlimited beverage package is great because we had mimosas coming the entire time we were there. 

The food is hot and fresh. I loved the fried chicken, the meat station, the Chinese food (my favorite part), everything is delicious. I haven't had one bad thing on this buffet. I also have never experienced the super long wait times, in fact, I've never waited. I just make sure to get there in the morning around 9-9:30am and I can walk right up and be seated. 

If you're gonna do a buffet in Vegas, do this one.
The food here is super good!! I love the crab legs and the baked potatoes with stuffings. 50$ all u can eat ;)

This place has its ups and downs. Overall good experience.

Thankfully it's located right by the entrance of the Caesars palace because my feet were dying.

Went around 10:30am and did not have to wait in line. Paid the $85ish for my girlfriend and I. Perfect time to go because breakfast is ending and lunch is starting. Got a little bit of both. 

For breakfast food, they had your basic eggs, bacon, sausage, steak & eggs. Steak was chewy and not seasoned. Everything else was bomb. Also got the chicken and waffles and it was AMAZING. Waffles were fluffy and chicken was juicy. Perfectly cooked. Literally my favorite dish here. Honestly wish I would've gotten more but I wanted to try everything.

For lunch food, we tried about everything. And I mean everything! Out of all the food we tried, I liked about 52.3% of it. For the price, I should've at least liked 90%. Quality was good for some but not for others. 

Desserts were bomb! Especially the Creme brûlée. Best dessert. Macaroons as well.

I highly recommend coming here but it was a one time thing for me. Food was good and service was okay. I expected more but it was a nice experience.

Well damn, I've been to a ton of buffets in my time on this earth, but this one takes the whole cake. Great service, thanks Geovany, amazing food and a really great selection of food! Def hit this spot up if you're ever in town. Try their amazing Wagyu and Prime Rib station, it's fuego AF.

B - BEST BUFFET in Vegas; BELIEVE the Hype

A - AMAZING AYCE Assortment of everything from breakfast to order to really tasty dinner options including Southern cuisine. 

C - CHINESE Food section is at the very end of the second room with Hot and Sour soup, appetizers galore from egg rolls to chicken skewers, 6 different meat dishes, vegetarian options - Veggie Stir fry which was really good, dim sum, siapao and shumai. COOL CHARCUTERIE section with really good cuts and choices. I grew up on Long Island and lived across from a deli  that had the best cuts ever. Yummy memories reignited. 

C - CAESARS PALACE! Yup, that is where you will find the Bacchanal Buffet. Fitting as this buffet is fit for a king and an emperor. Please keep in mind that if you are staying at a different hotel/resort and drive and park at Caesar's in the Self Park, it is $12 from 61 to 240 minutes. Where else can you find CROQUE Madame and fried CHICKEN and waffles in the same beautiful meal.


H - HEALTHY options in every section. Yogurt, bean salads, fresh cut and very juicy fruit, jumbo tiger prawns,
smoked salmon, seaweed salad, lean cuts of cooked and bbq meats, asparagus, string beans, mixed veggies,cucumber salad.

A - AWESOME staff - Kumudu was my first point of contact and welcomed me & registered me. Very kind and personable. Hats off to Nathalee, the amazing hostess who walked me to my table and the absolutely fantastic Ramona who kept my coffee cup filled and refilled with hot java and cleared my mess. Racquel was the sweet lady very appropriately in the sweet section who served me my gelato. Curtis was the fun gentleman who made my superb omelette and engaged everyone with love and kindness. 

N - NOODLES - the Singapore noodles with Shrimp were out of this world. They also had Pad Thai.

A - ABUNDANCE of ATTRACTIVE Food - my guesstimate is over 500 different items from bagels and cream cheese to banana foster donuts to pizza to ten different fruit and vegetable juices to sushi to prime rib to jumbo tiger prawns to smoked salmon to fifty different dessert preparations. The unlimited crab legs are served after 3:00 pm. 

L - Loved It! Loved It!! Loved It!!






B - BRING your appetite. Please do walk the entire display that stretches to a second room in the back with breakfast, pizza, cold cuts, juices, Japanese and Chinese foods and a separate section altogether for desserts, cookies, fruit, crepes made to order, assorted cakes, danishes, and pastries and twenty plus flavors of gorgeous gelato. 

U - UNLIMITED refills on soft drinks and coffee. The coffee is strong and really good. Extra charge for wine and beer. Unlimited trips to all food areas. 

F - FIND a cool deal on Groupon for $35 pp  for this from 7:30 am to 10:00 am- have to be seated prior to 10:00 am. The second option is $75 for two people and gives you till 2:00 pm. Both get you in quick via the VIP line. Both expire in 70 days or so on September 30th, 2018.

F - FOODIE heaven . 

E - EXCELLENT quality; EXQUISITE items. EGGS made to order. 

T - TIP well after you TRAVEL on this Tasty  Tantalizing Tour from US via France and Greece to Singapore, China and Japan. Ramona worked really hard and was on top of things. She brought me fresh cups and fresh coffee over the two hours I was here. My table was cleared and clean in a jiffy.

Awesome!

Read all the good reviews about this buffet and decided to give it a try. I recommend coming 30 mins prior to when you'd like to be seated. Upon arrival you will see a kiosk asking you how many are in your party and some other questions. It will print out a ticket for your party. When we visited, there was quite a line before entering. You will pay prior to entering, the dinner buffet price was about $58/person. It's definitely pricey, but since this was our first time here, we decided why not. The buffet had a lot to offer. The crab legs, prime rib, beef brisket, and the dessert section were some of my faves. Our server Marvin was the sweetest. He was attentive, friendly, and really made our experience here all the more enjoyable.

Overall, we had a lovely dinner here and the company can't be beat :D

Definitely was not impressed with the brunch buffet today. Most of the food was cold, not as many selections as I thought there would be. No salad bar, no mashed potatoes, no lobster. For $100 for 2 people I should've spent my money at a restaurant and got some good, hot food.

EXTREMELY RUDE STAFF, TERRIBLE PLACE. TOTAL SCAM. 

We bought Groupon "VIP" passes for 6 of us and came and found that there was a huge line. Went to the front desk/registrar and asked how long the wait will be and was told 1.5 hours. 

Fine, we got in line, and 1.5 hr later we got to the registrar again. Only to be told that for a party of 6 there will be an EXTRA 2 HOURS.

When we said that they could've let us know BEFORE we got to the first line, two people behind the front desk just shrugged their shoulders, grinned and said "it's the holiday." 

In short, this place is a TOTAL SCAM and I'm sure you can feel my rage through the screen. AVOID at all cost.

I can't lie, I get to skip the line since my family has a diamond membership. But I've gone and had to wait before so I still think it's one of the better buffets and is worth the wait. I am a little sad because I do think the quality has gone down a little, or maybe I just wasn't feeling all the options. It's still one of my favorites and you can tell it's got the goods since I see hella Asians in line. Y'all know they love seafood and know a good deal when they see one. 

The variety here is insane. I rarely get to try everything but having all these options is what makes this place great. It is hands down my favorite buffet in Las Vegas. If you want seafood (oysters and crabs!), bone marrow, creative desserts (Thai tea custard, ube ice cream and red bean cakes!!) and endless options (still haven't made it to the taco bar! Gahhh) you have to come here.

Over an hour wait. 3x the cost of other buffets. Totally worth it. Best Buffet Ever. Great Quality and variety.

Dim Sum/Chinese, Mexican, mac n cheese, lamb, lobster, crab legs, oysters, shrimp, bone marrow, sushi, poke, cheesecake, gelato, donuts, creme brûlée...are some of my favorites...

Give it a try.
Food variety was insane. Food quality was average. The raw seafood bar was to die for! Probably makes the trip worth it if you are into that sort of thing!

Bacchanal continues to never fail us. Delicious and quality food as always. We went for the brunch menu and every item was superb. The seafood selection did not disappoint. Highly recommend visiting this place.
Out of all the buffets I have gone to in Vegas, THIS WAS THE BEST!!! Breakfast was amazing, so much variety and flavor! Will be coming back!

We came here for the seafood since Rio no longer has their seafood buffet. So glad we did! It's ~$50 ... which I thought was pretty good for unlimited king crab legs and everything else that you get. The seafood did not disappoint. Started with the snow crab legs, then I discovered the king crab! The king crab are put out on ice by the staff and you can request to have yours steamed. Great selection of seafood, sushi, and carved meats. Side options were somewhat limited but they were done well. The roasted/grilled vegetables were my favorite. Desserts topped off the meal, great selection complete with gelato. I would definitely come back here for my seafood fix next time I'm in Vegas. Completely worth it!

I've always wanted to try out this buffet and I finally got to do it this past weekend. It met my expectations, as this was supposed to be the best buffet in Vegas. I have yet to try all of them but it definitely met my expectations. The steamed crab legs were amazing, although the size of the legs were a bit small, still steamed to perfection. They even have a made to order taco station which I really loved! They have a diverse selection of food to choose from and also portion the food well so you have room to try one of everything!! Their dessert selection was also very large!! Definitely a must try for buffets in Vegas!

My friends and I went here for dinner over the weekend. Baccanal's buffet selection had a great variety of food selection to Asian to Mexican, seafood to meats and desserts. The dim sum selection was actually pretty good quality for a buffet. The scallop sashimi tasted fresh, and had good flavor.

If you're fan of seafood, the steamed crab legs were my favorite. There's a variety of other seafood as well such as mussels, shrimp, and prawns with the option to be heated in the boiler.  The carne asada tacos at the taco station packed a lot of flavor with other choices being chicken and al pastor.

Make sure to save room for dessert! They have a lot of bite sized desserts like mini creme brûlée, and a make your own crepe station and a gelato station.

Overall Baccanl is my favorite Vegas buffet with many delicious options.

Overrated and expensive. Not worth the time (45 minute wait) and money spent. Food was flavorless and generic across the board. Nothing unique about the selection of food, you could get this at most buffets especially in Vegas. Desserts were a disappointment, gelato was just OK. Oysters were the only thing that saved it from being a 1 star review. I would not go here again and would not recommend it.
Long lines and a little pricey. On the plus side huge selection of food quality is diffently on the better side than most other buffets we have been to   Desserts were really good

Vegas is no doubt the place for buffets and they ain't playing! When you search online for the top buffets in Vegas, Bacchanal Buffet is always on the top 5 in any given year. It cost $17 million to build, opened its doors in Sept. 2012 and has many chefs from different cultures!
 
This is my 3rd visit at Bacchanal going into Memorial Day weekend. Since I'm a local, no shocker here where prices for buffets around town do increase on major holiday events and Bacchanal is no exception! They have special menu added for the holiday such as king crab legs, suckling pig and squid ink pasta! The lamb chops I thought it was just "okay". Texas De Brazil and Shish Kabob House lamb chops rock!

The dessert station was not all that bad. I think it was above average without the "wow factor". I'm just happy with the live crepe station where you are responsible to create/pour your own toppings! Love love fresh crepes! The large strawberries were fresh and dipped in green tea and white chocolate. The sweet potato fries was one of the best I've had! It was piping hot so I made sure I took some. 

The Mexican station where all the fresh juice you can consume such as horchata, guava and strawberry drinks! Oh my! They were all refreshing! It's a VERY overwhelming place to eat. So, make sure you have a strategy prior to your arrival to break even what you paid for. I'm overwhelmed writing this review because there's too many positive things that I failed to mention. I over stuffed myself with the crab legs and left no room for the meat galore! LOL! 

Bottom line, it is not fair for me to say that Bacchanal is the best buffet in Vegas. There are awesome buffets around town that offers different specialty menu AND do have some "wow factor"! There is no way you can find the best of everything under one buffet roof because it's impossible to offer ALL. However, I can see why this place always makes the cut for the top buffets in Vegas.
