The wide range of international cuisine to the most finicky eater. It sure has something for everyone!

The best buffet in Las Vegas. Love this place with all my heart. There's a separate line for big parties more than 8 people!! I came here for my 21st birthday and no disappointments in the food at all! You know the buffet is poppin' when there's restrooms inside. 

There's a 2 hour limit and they will kick you out if your party exceeds!  like the idea for the crab legs station because it makes it more orderly. The oysters go by really fast FYI!

For $65 pp, this was disappointing.  The flavors were ordinary.  The selection of seafood, including Dungeness crabs were the highlight of this buffet.  We were seated at the very back where the air conditioning was blasting.  Once we sat down our food was cold.  Do not accept a table at the very back.  I will not come back.

I stopped going to buffets in Las Vegas for a long time as I felt there were plenty of local places that served amazing food at better prices. Well, Bacchanal has changed my mind on that. Pricier than a lot of other buffets, the offerings they had were quite amazing. I enjoyed all of the stations from tacos, the carving station, the seafood, and the desserts. I do have to say, the weakest link of the buffet was the Asian fare. It seemed like it was just lacking compared to the other offerings. We showed up just around 10 and the wait wasn't too long for our party of 3. If I have to go to a buffet on the strip, this would be the place.
The selection was second to none. The wait staff was attentive, but not overbearing. And dessert was phenomenal!
really unique dishes compared to other buffets. I liked the wagyu steak and the Lobster mac n cheese. Worth the price premium if you're willing to try it!

First time in Vegas and I learned that by buffets are all the rage. 

After asking many locals the recommendations I settled on the buffet at Caesars Palace. I also saw this one on The Profit so I figured it had to be good. 

There was a short line but it moved quickly. Dinner for two was a nice $140, but there were a lot of options, good options.

My favorite was the Asian section and the sushi and the dessert. If you are confused about which buffet to choose since there are so many options I definitely would recommend this one.

I was lucky enough to snag a groupon for the buffet to take family since it was rated #1 of the best buffets in Las Vegas, but what a huge let down it was.  Although there was a variety of options with crab pinchers (the best part) and something new like bone marrow, the quality of the food here wasn't great and almost tasted mass produced, including the desserts. I do have to say that the one thing I did enjoy was the spanish rice.

Also, The workers here looked like death was looming over them. So if you come here, tip well. They'll do a service for you.

Overall, no go. I won't be coming back or recommending this place to anyone...ever.

TUUUURRRRIBLE - Save your money!  

They can't even shuck oysters properly.  The oysters are fresh, but the two people shucking them didn't know what they were doing, a lot of shell crumbs were left on the oysters, so make sure you don't just shoot it down like you would at an oyster bar.

The wagyu beef and prime rib were super dry and tough, even though they were medium rare looking, not juicy and tender like they should, had to pour a ton of Au Jus sauce on them.

The dessert station is nicely laid out and colorful, but the gelato lady was rude and literally threw every cup on the glass top, if she hates her job so much, she should do something else.  

The crepe chef is a funny dude, he can chat you up a storm, but when it comes to really making crepes, he had no clue what he was doing.  I had to teach him each step on how to make a real crepe.

The sushi tasted as if they were left out for hours, dry and chewy instead of moist.  Their so-called Tom-Yum soup so bland, felt like they took it out of a can and added ten times the water.  

A couple of decent items were the crab legs, which you can get the ice-chilled Dungeness or the hot King crab legs.  The bone marrow was nice, accented with an onion sauce on top.  But just a couple of items for that price, save your money!

I came here knowing that it was one of the best buffets in Vegas. In the end, I would have to give it 3 stars.  It didn't live up to the hype that I was hoping for.  I came here around 2:15 on Saturday to hopefully line up and get in line to save a few bucks for the lunch price.  Well, as I went to the kiosk to type my info in, it was only up to a party of 5 and we were a party of 6.  Deep down, that was a blessing because we ended up skipping the long line because we were a party larger than 5.  We went straight to paying and got the lunch price!  Then we got sent to another line that wasn't as long, aka the big party line.  We waited in line for about 30 minutes, which wasn't bad since we wanted to digest our lunch anyways.  As we walked in, we were seated right away and started heading to check out what there was.  In the back beginning, it was more Asian food, which didn't look very appealing.  It was dimsum, some Chinese stirfry and sushi.  It moved on to other types of food and a taco bar.  Of course the best places were the crab lines and the meat lines.  That was where you'd get your money's worth!  The crab was okay for me, the meats were quite tough for me.  Didn't really taste as what I'm used to.  The dessert was average at best, I've had better desserts at other casino buffets.  

All in all, just an average buffet place with a high price tag.

Esmeralda Juanez provided exceptional service. she was attentive, knowledgeable, and consistent in providing the best service one could receive. her service matched the beautiful food and ambiance of the restaurant. honestly probably the best service I've received so far while here in vegas.
Makes Bellagio buffet look like golden corral . Plan and simple. Has a lot to choose from only ate half the items spent 2 full hours there

I was very surprised when we showed up around 11 for brunch and there was no line. We paid around $60 per person and were seated immediately. I walked around looking at the food which looked good for the most part. I filled up a plate and sat down to enjoy my Father's Day brunch. Unfortunately I was disappointed that the food was not hot. For the price we paid I expected much more. Not being a seafood fan I decided the buffet is definitely not worth the high price. Service was good but I just couldn't get past the room temperature food.

Best place ever !!!!

The staff is amazingly attentive and polite.  The food.. man what can you say besides they have everything and everting is great quality!!
Love the food! A must try when visiting Caesars palace!! Wonderful options and great drinks

No longer deserves its fabulous reputation.  The quality of everything from the seafood to desserts has dropped since our prior two visits in years past when we rated it 5 star.  The Wynn is top notch and others are as good or better for less money.  And definitely not worth the wait.

No where does it say that you MUST have a reservation. NO WALK UPS.  Not even a line if you are willing to wait because you don't have a reservation.  Totally felt like the bad Disneyland Fast Passes where they tell you when to eat and no choice.  Go somewhere else if you don't have reservation.  UPDATE: at 6:30 I got the reservation ticket that said estimated wait time was 260 minutes which was came to 11:29pm.. Left and went to another Buffet .. Got in .. Then at 8:36pm received a text to come stand in line and there may be more of a wait. too late and they weren't even close in their estimate.  Bad system. Needs to be re-thought out by a sober person. LOL

Don't bother. Food was mediocre at best. Treated like cattle upon seating. Not worth the money. Go the the M or GVR, the food is slightly better and much less expensive. Bacchanal was a huge disappointment. As a local, I won't recommend and I won't t be back.

My daughter saved her money to treat me for a birthday Bacchanal breakfast buffet. It would be our first time and we were looking forward to experiencing one of the top-rated buffets in Vegas. We wanted to verify how much they were charging at the time, so we could have budgeted for it correctly. We called the casino twice; first time was before we left for vacation from Tucson. The second time was when we arrived in Vegas the afternoon before we planned to attend the Bacchanal. Both times they told us "around $40". The next morning we went to the buffet (after paying for parking), waited in line for a bit, just to be surprised that they were charging over $60 for a holiday brunch. The gal at the counter pointed out that although it was July 2nd, they were offering a premium holiday brunch. I spoke with the restaurant manager Raz P. to explain that we were told $40 on the phone. Without an ounce of compassion, he told us to come back July 5th for that price. I had enough money to cover the difference that my daughter had saved up to buy breakfast. But we felt $60 was way too much for us to pay for breakfast. We walked out and in a couple of hours, we attended a lunch buffet at A.Y.C.E @ Palms Casino. Palms was a wonderful buffet offering great food choices and outstanding service. We vow never to give our business to the Bacchanal.

This place is shiit!!! The worst buffet ever! 500 dishes my ass, ketchup is consider one of the 500 dishes... i guess! They posted with lobsters crabs claws but when i saw nothing but dry pork roasted, steak is so bad! Its definitely not waygu. WHO EVER WANT TO COME HERE TRY, PLEASE GO SOMEWHERE SAVE UR MONEY!!
Meh! There is nothing on this breakfast buffet that warrants an additional $15/pp on your 24 hr buffet pass at Caesars Palace.

I wasn't planning on having a Vegas buffet, ended up going to this one, and regretted it. So much money for not a great meal. Lots of variety at lunch, but the options are a little disappointing. I walked the whole length of the buffet a few times too. I tried at least 15 different items of mains/sides and another 10 of dessert, and didn't find many that were delicious. Only the brisket, pork shoulder (at Mexican cuisine station), and meatballs in marinara were good. Everything else like avocado deviled egg (hard boiled egg with avocado purée on top, not a real deviled egg), ramen (poorly cooked noodles), clam chowder, beet salad, quinoa apple salad, wagyu (so chewy), prime rib, etc were not worth the stomach space. I won't list all the failed desserts that I only took one bite out of, but the fresh crepe and ice cream were good. That's about it... Also, fruit was not chilled and refreshing like I'd hoped. 

I wish there were more pasta options and some sushi options that weren't raw--like unagi sushi or California rolls without raw fish on top would have been great! 

Note to self: no more Vegas buffets when I'm here.

In a nutshell, DO IT!  I've been to plenty of buffets in Vegas and I was really surprised with the great quality and the vast variety of food of the Bacchanal Buffet.  Make sure you recon the buffet areas first and prioritize the locations that have the food that you want.  Don't forget to hit the high value targets (seafood, sashimi, crab legs, steak, prime rib, desserts, etc.).  I was surprised that when I went back for seconds, the kitchen had swapped some of the menu items for other great looking food, so it was hard to keep track of all the different stations that I wanted to go to.  My group ate heartily and we all agreed this is one of the best buffets to go to while in Vegas.  We didn't even have to battle the other patrons for the monster Alaskan crab legs or for the other expensive seafood items.  Even with a graduated price scale that correlates to time of day and day of the week, the most expensive time slot (weekend dinners) is well worth the price and experience.

After waiting 45 minutes and getting no closer to the start of the line, we decided to pay extra to get in earlier. 

While their variety is great, being told (suggested, by a sign) that I can only stay for 2 hours to feed my fat face, was a little annoying.  Then being told, by the cooks, who are sitting there in front of me, WHILE SHUCKING THE OYSTERS that were making my mouth water, that I could not get them for another 3 hours just annoyed the shit out of me.

All in all, the food was good. Great even - Specially taken into account that this is all a buffet...

 Time restrictions just bothered me... $50ish per person, and getting oyster teased left me unhappy... All I wanted was some oysters to fill out the rest of my meal...

Sad Panda

I came here with my girlfriends on a Monday during lunch time and only waited about 10 minutes in line before making it to the register to pay. $45 each which is a steal compared to the $65 price tag on a weekend for dinner. We were seated immediately and then I rushed off to explore the giant buffet. 

There are a variety of styles of food here, including Japanese, dim sum, pizza, poke, Chinese, seafood, Mexican, meat options such as brisket, ham, and American waygu. The quality and presentation of food was unlike an ordinary buffet. Since we did come burping brunch/lunch time, they had small dishes like steak an eggs, which was served on a cute, personal sized skillet.

I was impressed by the Caesar salad, black truffle and mushroom pizza, and the brisket. The brisket was so tender that I could take my fork to it and the meat would flake apart. It melted in my mouth. 

The dessert area was a dream. Ice cream, crepes, macarons, Creme brûlée, coconut mango mousse, Oreo cupcake, tiramisu, the list goes on. Everything I tried was amazing. 

Now I know why Bacchanal is notoriously one of the best buffets in the area. Can't wait to come back.

I was here on Saturday, July 20th for dinner. I used to come at least once a month. The price has gone up (to be expected). However, I will not be returning mainly due to one of the workers. I was getting some ramen soup (they have a soup station where they will make you ramen, udon, etc.), the Asian man working there was beyond rude. I told him I just wanted the noodles and the soup and he raised his voice to me and basically started yelling at me, telling me NO. He was very unprofessional, he never smiled at anyone, he never said hello, never acknowledged you were there except to yell at me. Just sat there behind the counter with a VERY angry look on his face. He made me feel very uncomfortable and not welcomed. He had to get another worker to help me. I told my husband who then wanted to confront him. I asked my husband not to because trust me, it would NOT have been a pretty scene. My resolve is to not go back to this buffet again. I will not spend my money anywhere to not feel welcomed.

We had an amazing experience back on July 4 this year to celebrate my birthday. The food was amazing and since we were celebrating we decided to get the drink package. Valerie was great helping us check in and Julie was an amazing server. She even brought over a cupcake with a candle and sang me Happy Birthday. It was definitely worth the price, and all of the seafood, beef and dessert were so yummy! I hope we can celebrate a special occasion there again!!

Hmmm... Bacchanal...food great server (1 star) not so much...towards the end of our Buffet meal, the server asked whether anyone wants coffee a mix of no and no response.... he said if you change your mind let me know.  He came back asked the group anything else?  I said yes 2 coffees... Jerk Jeff says - I asked you all if you wanted coffee you said no.  Judy's response - yes, you did but stated if we change our minds, you could get us coffee.  We have changed our minds and would like 2 coffees. He delivered the coffees but did not return to the table until 20 minutes later. He walked all around our table but did not stop. Finally, Jackass Jeff (promoted from Jerk to Jackass) stopped by and asked if we wanted refills. I said no but I want a coffee. He said oh. I said I am joking I do not want coffee because of your attitude.  He said what - I explained to Jackass Jeff the story. He said I did not say anything rude.  You did and now you are being argumentative. Jeff the thing to remember - I am the customer where is my service. He continues to defend himself. I said you need to step away. Jackass Jeff continues to yap away.  Jeff you need to close your mouth (using my hand for emphasis) and go away please.  Jackass Jeff walked away.  He has a primary service, at a Buffet, request drink orders and deliver the drinks in a courteous manner. Epic fail!

I must say, Bacchanal buffet is one of the higher quality restaurants I have eaten at. If you haven't had it, I suggest for you to give it a try. Although the price is in the higher side, you must experience it. 

Over the past years, I have had Bacchanal 3 times, and let's say it's time for me to stop going. Prices have risen up to $75 per person, and although the food is high quality than most buffets, $75 is not worth spending if you had tried this place a couple times already. The question is, did I feel like I ate $75 worth of food? I would say no. 

They have a great dessert section, but things get over repetitive and there was nothing I found worth getting over and over. They also need to stop seasoning the boiling water with so much salt for the crabs legs. They were overly salty, I couldn't eat anymore. 

Overall, try this place if you haven't! It's worth experiencing. Also, order the PEACH GREEN TEA, it was amazingggg. I can drink around 3 glasses of those!

I ate here 3 years ago and I gave them 5 stars, but much has changed...

Went for Easter holiday dinner (2017),  $75 a person. The meats were all burnt and over cooked, there were no wagyu sliders as advertised,  I had to ask for then and a chef opened a drawer, pulled out a pan with a couple dozen of them,  took off the ceran wrap and placed one in a small plate and gave it to me. Clearly they aren't that fresh and ontop of all that,  it was severely undercooked and cold. Even our waiter told us we should not eat it. Dessert selection was subpar, Wynns buffet has more desserts. 

Overall it seems the buffet scene is dead in Vegas, quality is down everywhere,  your better off spending your money on one nice fancy dish!

First of all, I feel like contacting USA Today who rated this the "best buffet" in Las Vegas and ask them "says who?".  This was by far the WORST buffet I"ve been to anywhere on the planet.  That said, my friend who is a Las Vegas local and almost choked on the tough-as-a-boot prime rib grabbed the manager (who was courteous) to tell him how bad the food was.   What I find interesting is that I saw another couple talking to the manager saying "the food was unedible" and pointing at full plates saying they wanted a refund.

So let's go through the "burn list" on Bacchanal Buffet:
1) Dim sum was cold and mushy
2) Salmon sushi was rubbery and tough
3) I got two slices of prime rib that were 80% fat and my friend got a lean cut that needed a chain saw to cut
4) The battered thick fries were cold
5) I got the tacos they create in the Mexican section and the chicken were  OK but the carne asada (beef) were pure gristle and stringy (I needed a good flossing after trying to eat)
6) The mac and cheese tasted like fake cheese and seemed to be spicy?
7) The loaded mashed potatoes were bland and barely warm (see a trend with a lot of the food being cold?)
8) The molten lava cake wasn't molten!  There was no liquid inside, just a weird tasting chocolate that my chocoholic Vegas friend took one bite of.
9) The plates for the cold seafood, e.g. the shrimp, oysters, were HOT
10) The iced tea was cloudy and tasted like instant
11) The champagne we got as part of the groupon was SWEET -- I guess Boones Farm makes sparkling wine?
12) The pizza was a notch below Dominos
13) The pork belly was cold
14) The fresh fruit like cantaloupe and watermelon still had the rind on them (are you supposed to eat with your hands?)

And last but not least my friend got us some cheese, bread and olives and I took one of the olives that seemed to be pitted and a pit fragment was still in the olive and it lodged between a tooth and crown and I almost cracked a tooth!

Maybe I'm too picky, but I do like Grand Slam breakfasts at Denny's and Cracker Barrel so I can't be that much of a food snob.  For the price of this buffet I found the quality of the food lacking and the accolades as "best buffet in Las Vegas" to be completely false.

We arrived at the buffet around 7 and signed in at the kiosk which said to come back in an hour. We were able to walk around and do whatever we wanted in that time, then return to stand in line. After the time on the kiosk ticket you are able to stand in the actual line which takes another hour. 
After paying at the register you stand in another line that varies by party size (1-2; 3-4; or larger) and then get seated. The main food is lines up on the left side with different foods grouped by type. 

First was Seafood- chilled raw oysters, shrimp, sea snails, crab legs, and similar items. I started here and had roughly 6 of the oysters. There was also several sauces like cocktail, spicy aioli, and horseradish along with lemon wedges. 

Next were a few seafood gumbos, paella, and clam chowder. Another station had Mexican food, complete with made-to-order tacos and a topping bar. Also beans, rice, tortilla chips, and similar things to that. The taco meat was a little under-salted, but the choice of toppings were great 

Another station was meat where they had slabs of meat that chefs would cut off for you. There was bacon, wagyu, pork, and turkey. All of the meats were overcooked, dry, and tough. I was disappointed especially with the wagyu as it seemed they ruined such a nice and expensive meat. Near here I believe was more American foods such as sliders, bone marrow, and more. The bone marrow was very watery but they were smart to add something crunchy on top and some pomegranate seeds. The sliders looked really good but were always gone the 2-3 times I walked by. 

There was also a Spanish/Italian section with different cured meats and cheeses as well as pasta salads and regular pastas. There is also a salad section which was minimal - 3 main salads (caesar was a little over dressed) and some toppings like basil, nuts, and lime wedges to add. The cured meats were really delicious, and the cheeses were just okay. Some of the pastas were portioned out and plated beautifully but this took up a lot of room on the plate. 

Finally there was an Asian section that mostly consisted of Chinese and Chinese-American food. There were different dim sum options inside steam baskets as well as roasted duck and roasted pork. I also saw fried rice. There wasn't much Korean food, I saw kimchi and maybe chapchae. There were probably 4 types of Japanese hand rolls but nothing special about those. The roasted duck along with several sauces to add were great but nothing else here particularly stood out. 

In the center was an area for dessert. There were different flavors of cupcakes, mini macarons, rice krispy treats, a dozen or so ice cream flavors, mini creme brulee (which I suspect are store bought as I've seen similar ones at Costco and other buffets from different states) and cut up fruit. The cupcake I had was tasty and beautiful- the frosting was coated with some kind of fine edible sprinkle. 

Overall- I think for a $60 per person buffet in Las Vegas my expectations were met and slightly exceeded. Compared to other LV $60 buffets this definitely stands above those. The website said the wait was an hour but at peak times I'd expect at least 2 hours (we went on a Wednesday, maybe linger for Fri-Sun). There was some really tasty dishes and some that really fell short. I wouldn't reurn on my next trip as there are so many buffetd and food places to try, but I don't regret my visit either.

My favorite or the best buffet while in Vegas that I've had by far. This place does not disappoint. Depending on the hour, of course, it gets busy and the lines are long. Plenty of options available, eap seafood.

I can at least say I have had the experience of dining at Bacchanal but if honestly asked if I'd return, I would pass. I noticed many people here go straight for the crab 
(trust me, you're not getting huge crab legs) but in my opinion, the dessert bar is the highlight of this restaurant. I will say they have many options from a small Italian section, small section for Mexican food, sushi, seafood, and various meats but to be honest, it's overpriced. After paying, prior to entering the restaurant, your picture is taken, special right... only for them to come to your table and tell you the photo is $20.  So I just paid over $100 for two people and you're trying to sell me a $20 photo, coupled with the fact that I don't at least get one or two glasses of champagne included in that $100. This restaurant is highly rated and has many good reviews but  I do not believe the price point supports the food. I had a couple of small salads, sushi, tasted the lobster bisque which was okay and tried a tamale at the Mexican station but the salsa was way too spicy, after being told it was mild. Various meats but again, the desserts were the most pleasing part of my experience. Various flavors of gelato, cookies, crème brûlée, freshly made crepes but pass on the chocolate cupcakes, they are dry. Overall, I was disappointed because I had been looking forward to coming to this restaurant and left feeling as if my money could've been better spent at a different restaurant. Please do not misunderstand me, it's not that I have a problem with paying for a "high end buffet" but I expected better. This is Vegas and we all know there are no shortage of four star restaurants. Our server wasn't very engaging and appeared more agitated by the table next to us that had apparently been there way too long, the restaurant wants you to observe a two hour limit while dining. Again, I had the experience and that's where I'll leave it.

Service is good. The only reason why they get 5 stars is because they require that for the free glass of champagne beer. The server actually clicked on the 5 stars.There are a lot of food options. Most of the food doesn't have any flavor. Looks great but no flavor. Way too over priced for what is offered. All the meat they roast has no seasoning. Very bland. The lobster claws and crabbed legs are served cold, straight out of the fridge. The steamed crab legs are over cooked. Rubber! The dessert bar is good. Don't fill up on lunch or dinner. Showed up late enough to catch dinner. Not worth the money!

This place is what i will now imagine when I hear anything along the lines of "... The world on a silver platter". You name it, they got it. There was so much food available it should be illegal. Be forewarned: you're gonna wait a bit and spend a whoooole lot but if you're a "here for a good time not a long time" this place is for you! I never thought I'd see the day I turn down crab legs but alas there is a first time for everything. I got a literal taste of the world. The food was pretty good (honestly not worth the cost but I'm a here for a good time not a long time kinda gal ) and the staff was awesome. If you go here DO NOT EAT ANYTHING for like 18 hours before so you can really appreciate the amount of food available. Also, try something new! And for the love of all things holy don't get rice on your first walk around-- it takes up valuable international space that could have been replaced by lamb (rookie mistake‍)

Editing this review.... they give you free drinks if you post a review before going in. So I went in giving a 5 star review. Got seated, for my free drink and went to get food. Wow. Lines like 30 minutes long just to get food which isn't a issue but the buffet gives you only a 2 hour time limit inside. They need to make a better process for lines for food. Then it's literally 90% seafood and 10% beef/pork/chicken. Don't expect to come here to eat some gourmet meat how they advertise it to people. Dessert was above average and that's all I ate in order to get full cause the meat was fatty nothing lean and I hate seafood.

Best buffet in Vegas no more to say! 
There are plenty of options and this place caters to everyone's needs. 
The crab legs are a highlight and they have two options cold or hot.

I don't know why it has high rating. Went there yesterday and the foods were nothing special, and I have to say WORSE STEAK. It is too pricey for the quality, feel like nothing deserve to eat with the price of 75$/person including taxes. Everything is not hot (except the overcooked steak, crab leg, and dimsum). Moreover, wainting for more than 2hrs and then when I got inside, many tables were clean and there were many empty tables. SO, the first time gonna be the last time, I will never come back and very disappointed.

This is my 2nd review! My first was for dinner, this review is for brunch. 

My family and I went to brunch on a Saturday afternoon at about 1130 and we got lucky the line was suuuuper short. We tried going to dinner a month ago but the line was wrapped around the entire massive room!!!! So we tried standing in the fast pass line to pay extra to be seated quicker....IT DIDN'T MOVE! 

We got sat down and started grubbing! My favorite item and definitely a stand out we're the maple glazed sweet potato tater tots!!! I would add these to my last meal if I were on death row! Other stand outs were the Kobe beef sliders, create your own omelette, watermelon mint sorbet, and the fresh juices on the buffet!! I drank like 3 of those juices plus my mimosas :) truthfully I don't like breakfast, at all, I like cereal. So the fact there were plenty of lunch items made me happy! The prime rib was melt in your mouth and the king crab was meaty! 

Bacchanal is STILL my favorite buffet and I can't wait to go back :)

By far the best buffet in Vegas. They have such a huge selection and everything was cooked well. The sweets counter is amazing, the mini creme brûlées were my favorite. Plus all you can eat crab legs. This place did not disappoint.

When I left the Bacchanal Buffet after eating there for brunch I left with a full belly of very tastey items. I was nervous about there being a limited selection of food going during lunch instead of dinner but there is still plenty of offerings during the brunch service. There is plenty of seafood options that came out later in the brunch service around noon. Before noon it was primarily crab legs and other standard seafood item. The meat offered was various so you have plenty of options to pick from. The dessert buffet is great because of the portions are the perfect size. You can get a taste of everything there if you have enough room.

My family made a surprise visit to Las Vegas We decided to go to Bacchanal Buffet. What a great decision! Our server was Gwen, she was amazing, she got our drink orders perfect, even with all the crazy changes my family made, our drinks stayed full and she made sure to check on us to make sure we had everything we needed. Sooo much food, we had to pace ourselves, carving station was delicious , ribs, brisket and prime rib even wagyu! Seafood selection is great,yummy crab legs definitely my favorite, and my husband dined on snails which he said were great. Made to order taco station, and Asian dumplings (I had 2 plates so worth it!) Definitely save some room for dessert, handmade crepes!!!  If you haven't been you have got to experience it, you won't be disappointed. Looking forward to going back soon!

TIPS:
To save a few $15 each, arrive 30 minutes before lunch turns over to dinner. Pay lunch price and take your time sampling those items. Then enjoy the dinner items at less than full dinner fare.  

If you buy a Goupon coupon, check the restrictions carefully. They usually are for weekdays and off-peak times only. My sister got burned on this. 

REVIEW:
If you are a regular buffet goer and you regularly enjoy places like, say, Golden Corral, Hometown Buffet, etc. then you'll likely love this pace. If you are a foodie looking for 5-star food experience, you'll likely be disappointed. However, if you have realistic expectations for what ultimately is an above average but nonetheless still a just a buffet dining experience, then the Bacchanal is likely going to please you. They have a pretty decent variety of food options - some very good, some disappointing in overall quality and taste. 

The crab legs are thin and probably frozen at some point because they are stringy rather than meaty. The sushi was heavy on rice and light on fish. Not a problem if you eat the fish and leave the rice. The lamb was excellent, as were most of the Asian dishes located way in the back corner.  I tried a lot of small bites since I love variety in most things in life. I'd say 33% was excellent, 33% was OK, and 33% was not great. Based on price and wait time in line, I'd like to see 70% or higher hitting the excellent mark. Still, not bad for a buffet, which based on the business model must either cut a lot of corners on quality or charge a small fortune if everything was excellent.

Went to eat around 630 for dinner and was told an hour and a half wait. We really wanted to eat here so decided to stand in line. It took maybe 45 mins. All I can say is WOW!!! Anything you could want was there. But the desserts..  A-M-A-Z-I-N-G!! All little bites except for the handmade gelato. Yes, you heard me right HANDMADE. My favorite out of the 7 desserts I tried was the lemon basil gelato. OMG! So light and refreshing and clean. Yummm!
If you ever try this buffet, bring a wad of cash and a wheelbarrow to haul yourself out of there! :)

"Pace yourself" let's those words stay with you at this WORLD CLASS buffet.  There are over 100 different choices of high quality, varietal, delicious tapas and more.   I'm a guy that can appreciate quality and value.  I went straight for the shrimp and lobster.  I followed up with some chicken and waffles and mashed potatoes.  The dessert options were too much for me to handle at the end but I would count my waffle as dessert and I guarantee you this waffle is fresh and if you ask they will give you two waffles without the chicken.   This is the only buffet I'll do from now on.  Don't forget to checkin and you get some free champagne.  I took advantage of that and gave the drink to my buddy (don't tell him I didn't pay for it)

Bacchanal Buffet is still not a bad buffet. I came to this buffet started from 2012 at the time when they first open. They are "THE BEST" at the time. Everything is top quality at the time. They are expensive, but they are good. I have no problem pay for the best buffet in Las Vegas. I ate here at least once a year. 2-3 times a year at the first few years. But I found out both of the foods qualities and the services getting lower each times when I am here. They still has the bigger selections of the food. They still very busy. But they are not stand out anymore. Also the price is keep going higher. I think they are still busy just because they still have one of the biggest name of all the buffets in Vegas! They are way over price based on the foods qualities they are offer and the services they have provided now!

Starts from the foods, the seafood station is still okay, but the mixed crab legs has more than 95% of the snow crab legs, a very few pieces of king crab legs you can finds in the mix now!  Roast lamb chops is replaced by the roast lamb meats now! The Chinese foods station is below the average compared to the other Vegas buffets. It is very bad! Too much oil and all the foods in the Chinese station looks and testes like the worst supper market's Chinese foods! The Chinese soups was the Chinese herbs soup use the small individual bowls years ago, it is replaced with the big pots with the egg flower soup and the vegetables soup etc.! Also, Bacchanal Buffet has very little choices of the leafy vegetables at any of the food stations included the salads station!

The services in Bacchanal Buffet is also very base and on the slow side! I don't know how many tables our waitress have to cover. I saw her all the time, but she was running around try to take care all the other tables in the section. She don't look around, she only take care one or two tables at the time. You will not getting her attentions if you needed anything before she come to your table! Our table is at the edge of her section. We don't see her very often! She does her job when she came to our table. But you can tell she is overloaded!

For the price of Bacchanal Buffet. We have many choice of restaurants or buffets in Las Vegas for less money and better services. I will not come back to Bacchanal Buffet in the near future. I might come back and check them out again when I see they have the better review!

The selection here is pretty decent. Their sushi station was sparse and lackadaisical. The cooked seafood station along with the carving stations were very well stocked. 

Slightly annoyed that there were bean sprout roots-- dirt and all in my ceviche. The server didn't even apologize. And my table was sticky and gross.

I have to say I gave up on Vegas buffet.  This used to be the last hopeful good quality low quantity buffet.  But for over $150 for 2 people.. Thr quality control went down hill.  Food was OK but most definitely disappointing
The best buffet in Vegas! Definitely best time to hit is between breakfast and lunch to get both selections. Do not go to a Vegas buffet without going to this one!

I believe when Dante wrote Circle 3 (Gluttony) of his Inferno, he had this place in mind. There's enough food here at any given moment to feed a village three times over.  And at roughly $60 or so per person, it's a surprisingly good deal.

That said, the quality isn't that great. They were frequently out of the popular Alaskan crab legs, the cakes were pretty dry (as were some of the meats) and other dishes were either over-seasoned or under-seasoned. If you really need to get your food on and have $60+ burning a hole in your pocket, come here to make your IG followers jealous. Otherwise, there are plenty of other restaurants serving better, fresher food that hasn't been getting stale/cold/bland with time.

Love love love this buffet. The environment is pretty, food looks fresh and they have lots of great selections. Me and my husband had a great time. We will definitely be back next time we come in Vegas!
First time to the Bacchanal Buffet and the food was good.  I had a gang of crab legs that reminded me of the east coast. All soft drinks are complementary and it a good price.

I could not be more disappointed in this place. 
I'm not a huge buffet person, but the food variety was not there and the taste of it all was mediocre... and for the price! There were lots of extra heavy types of options, no oysters the Sunday brunch time we went and the crab legs were so salty and off-flavor, they were hard to eat. Overall, I like how it's clean and the food has good turnover, but there was nothing at the dessert table that was good. 

Thankfully, we came during the breakfast/lunch transition, because breakfast foods were nothing special or more than what you couldn't gotten at your hotel room. 

Note: I'm working off the Ritz Carton, Half Moon Bay Navi's Sunday Brunch Buffet as the standard.
The seafood at this place tasted really fishy and bland the beef that i had was under seasoned and was very tough, the sushi was dry and sloppy.
Awesome selection!!! So much to choose from. Come hungry. Dessert bar was fabulous!!!

When you're in Vegas you got to go to at least one buffet and my friends and I decided to go to Bacchanal inside Caesar's (also didn't hurt it was next to the Mirage where we were staying).

We got there on a Saturday around 6:30PM (which is prime time) but the line moved quickly and didn't take us very long to get a seat. 

In true Asian fashion, you skip most of the carbs (their mac and cheese was amazing that my friends and I couldn't say no to) and go for the carving station and the seafood station. One of my favorite things about Vegas buffets is that you don't need to crack the crab and that its already cut in half which makes it easy. I do love snow crab better but for quantity the king crab legs are where its at. I will say the king crab was a bit salty but just eat it with some veggies and you're good to go. I also got prime rib and waygu steak (both were a medium rare) which was perfect for me. We ended with dessert and shared a bit of everything with the table. They have a crepe station, shaved ice station and even had ice cream (they also had flavors like ube and BLACK SESAME!!!) yes!!

Our server was super nice and always had our drinks refilled by the time we got back to the table.

If you're reading this review and are seriously considering eating here, I recommend training your stomach to prepare. You will literally eat the biggest meal of your life.

Was in Vegas and was treated to the Bacchanal Buffet. At 5 PM on a Wednesday, the line was around 20 minutes. It's also around $60 a person for dinner, but they have coupons available! I walked in and was in awe. The buffet is so spacious and so beautifully decorated. They have piles upon piles of food. Their seafood section is the most famous, with rows of mussels, clams, shrimp, and snow crab legs. Everyone walked away with plates full of snow crab legs. I was really happy that Bacchanal cuts their snow crab legs in half so it's so easy to eat. They literally boil hundreds of pounds of these crabs per day and you can get them freshly boiled or chilled. The line for the popular foods became long but nothing more than a few minutes. I also have sampled their ribs and their oh-so-juicy flank steaks. 

Their sushi section was a bit small and didn't seem attended to as much as the other sections, but it had a selection of rolls. They also have an Asian section, American section, pasta, etc. After a few more rounds of crab legs and shrimp, I was ready to tackle dessert.

Their dessert section has the largest selection of sweets I have ever seen. They have cake pops, an entire bowl of macarons, a huge array of cakes, pies, tarts, fruits, and an entire gelato selection. I sampled the passionfruit and lychee gelatos, which were so delightful. I would recommend saving 30% of your stomach for desserts. 

I absolutely loved my experience and would definitely come back if it weren't so darn expensive!

Was pretty disappointed.  Sushi was meh and had more rice than fish. They hardly had any rolls.  Cooked food was meh, soups were salty, freshly sliced beef were over cooked,  chicken and waffles had over cooked dry inedible chicken. Most meat dishes were over cooked and dry actually. Pizza did not look freshly made.  They had little soba bowls that were already half dipped in sauce so it was half dry and half soggy.  Disappointed they didn't have any oysters.  Really, there weren't any highlights EXCEPT for their dessert selections.  They had many dessert choices like cakes, creme brule and many ice cream flavors.  But really this place was over priced for the quality of cook food they served.

It wasn't really my favorite buffet but people who like crab legs and other seafood items seemed to really enjoy it. Honestly, I only came because the family wanted to go and I like dessert. 

We had a Groupon but even after getting past the first line you still have to wait a while to be seated. Luckily there were no lines for good except the crab leg line. The buffet was kept pretty clean and tidy for the most part. 

Nothing really looked appealing but the food was decent. I think I liked the fresh tacos the best and the egg rolls were pretty yummy. My husband enjoyed a massive plate of king crab legs, bone marrow, meats and all that goodness. I thought it was cool that they had fruit smoothies, I've never seen that at a buffet before. There's really something for everyone but don't expect anything to blow your mind. 

The desserts were so good I just wish I had saved more room. I absolutely fell in love with the coconut gelato. It was the only thing I got seconds of. The Ube cone was another tasty one. They also had shaved ice, crispy treats, chocolate strawberries, crepes and so much more. The Oreo cupcake was amazing but I could only take two bites because I was so stuffed and might have puked if I had more. If I could do it all again, I'd skip the food and go straight for the desserts.

As always, the bacchanal buffet was delicious.

Server: Esmeralda - was absolutely amazing and attentive!! 

Types of foods: carving station, Chinese, Japanese,  Mexican, Italian, desserts. 

Will definitely come back :) 

Parking: Self park with your players card (platinum or higher)
This is a great place. Our server Socorro M was awesome. Would highly recommended. If your are in Vegas this is a must do!!

Was just here last week and I love the crab legs, that's all I come here every year for the last 5 years when I'm in town with friend or family. Great variety but service was just bad this time, sucks because I've been coming here for years and this time the service was a disappointment. Will still come back just hope we get a better server.

A bit disappointed in all the hype of this premium Buffet. We were on our extended Thanksgiving vacay to Vegas, and heard this was the place to go for Seafood. They did not have Lobster tail, no Oysters, and the River Prawns were cold and mushy. The deserts however, were phenomenal, I could easily give 5 Stars if they took care of my missing items I thought they would have. Also doesn't fit the bill for 69.99 pp cost. I could value it more like 39.99 for what I was getting. I was there on a Sunday, dont know if that was why the seafood options were limited... Service was Excellent though, us why I gave it 3 instead 1 star.

We came for the dinner buffet on 6/11/19. WOW! It was amazing. They had the biggest selection of food I've ever experienced at a buffet. I definitely plan to visit again because I wasn't able to try everything. The crab legs were really delicious just a bit salty. Other than that, no complaints!
Expensive, but a high quality  and variety of food and food styles. My only regret was not having a larger stomach

Had some serious troubles checking in for the buffet. Ten parties went through the regular line before any status person checked in. The excuse: I'm the only person working status lines. Then pull a person from regular queue to check in status. Saw the server twice. Manager no where to be found! Waste of money for a buffet where people don't care!

The Food
Most said that Bacchanal Buffet was one of the best buffet in Las Vegas. My friends also wanted to try it out, so it was a good chance for me to visit. First up I got the Salmon Poke, it was well flavored but doesn't taste very fresh. I also got dim sum, but they were dry and not fresh. The beef station had a variety of beef  to try including Wagyu, Prime Rib, Brisket, and Bacon. The Wagyu and Prime Rib is by default cooked well done, and you need to ask for more rare slices. The Brisket tasted good, but the others were mediocre. The second round I got their Meatballs, Japchae, Curry Chicken, and charcuterie. I also got bowl of Menudo Soup. These dishes were alright, but the Menudo Soup was pretty good.  Next we got King Crab Legs, which was good, and make the meal worthwhile. Last but not last, they have a good variety of dessert to try, and most of them are pretty interesting and well done.

The Miscellaneous
Bacchanal Buffet itself is within the Caesars Palace Hotel & Casino. The inside is very big and well maintained, with a long stretch of buffet stations. There's a good variety of food selections to choose from. The organization of the stations is also intuitive and easy to figure out. It is definitely more choices than you know what to eat. The services was good, there were never a shortage of food, and the buffet line is well cleaned. The staff was sincere, our waiter was very attentive and fulfilled our many requests. Though the chef at the meat carving station seem to be a bit irritate toward the customers. Based on the reviews about Bacchanal Buffet, I guess I had high expectations. But it was more of an slightly upscale buffet with a more expensive price tag. Though it is still worth visiting at least once with their huge selection of food.

First time staying at Caesar's & have eaten the buffet 2 days in a row as more expensive but so much quicker than waiting to eat any other breakfast restaurant. There is quite a selection but so much more lunch/dinner type foods than breakfast. But.... Gabriela helped me this morning having fresh made French toast with bananas foster topping... yum! She was very sweet & helpful.. thank you :)
Fantasic buffet. A little expensive, but delicious

I give this place a 3.5 stars. So the buffet is about $60-$65 for dinner on the weekend. I went on the a Friday night. I think the food is good and the flavors are on point, but for the price I was thinking there be more seafood option. Sure they do have shrimp and some clams and crab, but no lobster or more seafood option. I feel the seafood option is kind of lacking for the price. But it was a good experience,  I'm not sure if I'll come back because of the variety in seafood wasn't what I expect. If you dont care about seafood and more of just the meat options then it good. The Craving station was good and had a lot of options and the desserts were good. The service was good and it was a very nice clean buffet, but might be overhype.
Best buffet in town!!! Highly recommend! Place is always busy but great food and definitely worth the wait.

I never fail to go this place when I go to Vegas.
This is the best buffet ever!
ベガスに行くと毎回行きます。種類も豊富で、１つ１つの料理のクオリティも高いです。
価格は少し高めですが、満足度が高いです！

ビュッフェスタイルのレストラン、夜に20～30分ほど並んでの入店です。

店内は非常に広く、その広さを活かして様々な料理が用意されています。
寿司や蕎麦などの和食、中華料理、ゆでた蟹、お肉料理にフルーツやジェラート、ケーキのデザートなどなど。

どれも安定して美味しいですが、飛びぬけてうまい！というほどでは無く、量も沢山食べられない人間からすると、お値段に比べてう～ん・・な感想になってしまいます。
アルコールは別料金なので、飲む人は更に・・な感じでした。

中には、ひたすら蟹を食べて蟹の殻タワーを作ってる人もいたので、大好物をひたすら食べるのはありかもしれません（笑）

We went on a Wednesday at 10am and it was $88 for two ppl including tax. As soon as we sat down, we showed our waitress the yelp "free mimosa/champagne" check in perk. The waitress told both my husband and me that we had to write a 5 star review on yelp before we could get the drink.... what?? Well we wanted the drinks so here's what I typed even before I got to drink water: "Lots of different options and quick service. We came here from a different hotel because of the great reviews. Make sure to check the times you go because prices can differ." 
The waitress actually came back to read my review on my phone before putting my mimosa on the table. Is this legal? I thought you weren't supposed to bribe for reviews on Yelp.... well here's my actual review. 

There's A LOT of variety. Everything from Chinese dim sum, fake sushi, pseudo Thai, Tex mex, standard American breakfast items to desserts. My husband and I walked from one end to the other and made a game plan to how we would try a bite of everything. I was disappointed. The food was mediocre... the dim sums were the frozen kind from asian markets and any ethnic food was very Americanized. The desserts get half a star more because they did have a gelato stand which is hard to screw up. The concept of mini donuts and mini pancakes were adorable and makes it easy to try a little of everything. However, the pancakes were crunchy on one side (maybe it was stale?) and a lot of the cute fruit flavored sweets were artificial flavoring instead of the actual fruits. 

For $44, I did get a bang for my buck, but it did feel like I ate calories to not waste money instead of actually enjoying the food. If you've had continental breakfast at any hotel, expect that level of food. The variety was great but everything was standard at best. 

It is now 12:30pm and I'm not full from the food I ate because it just wasn't worth gorging. Hence the standard average 3 star review.

I looked up this place months before my Vegas trip and was looking forward. It did not disappoint. Every item I got was so delicious. It's a bit pricey but totally worth it with all the seafood you can get. Definitely recommend.

Pros:
- Good quality for buffet food
- Lot of variety
- Lot's of seating

Cons:
- Huge line
- A little pricy

I came here for dinner and had to wait for a little over two hours. Theres a line where you can pay a little extra and get seated a little faster. After you pay there are separate lines, but the workers didn't do a good job of separating the two lines and it got very complicated. If I knew I was going to have to wait for two hours I wouldn't have waited, but it was too late. They had a taco station (my favorite) and a lot of meat and seafood. There was also a back room that I didn't know about where they had Italian and some Asian food. The good thing about this place is that there's a lot variety. They also have a lot of desserts. If I didn't have to wait such a long time I definitely would have enjoyed it more.

Bloody prime rib, Rubbery tri-tip steak, and $55 extra charge for king crab legs. 

We called at 12:30pm to find out how long the wait is for lunch. They told us 25 minutes. When we got there at 1pm, they said about 2 hours. 

We waited for 2 hours and right when we got to the register, it just turned 3:05pm and they charged us for dinner price $70.

Right when we were the second group to go up to the register, hostess named Sara was apparently slowing down people in getting in because it was about to change to dinner. Then she let parties of 3 behind us to go first who paid lunch price, which is the only reason we paid extra. And each person  in that group was paying separately taking even more time.

If you come as a couple, be prepared to be treated the worst.

We used to come here since they opened few years a ago, and I can say the quality of food and service has gone down real bad. The good ratings for this buffet is mostly from when they first opened. Do NOT be fooled by 4 stars. It is not like that anymore.

Never coming back here and wasting my precious time and money. Try different buffet for cheaper price. It's not worth it here.

Bacchanal is pricey, but it is sooo worth it! During our Vegas trip, we had dinner at this buffet and at the Wicked Spoon buffet inside the Cosmopolitan. In my opinion, Bacchanal is a million times better! They have a longer buffet setup, the food is better, and they offer a lot of things that Wicked Spoon doesn't. They took our picture right before the host took us to be seated and they try to sell it to you later at your table, which felt very touristy and kind of weird.. But we bought the picture and now we have something to remember this meal forever I guess! Hahaha :) The hostess explained all the sections of the buffet as she walked us to our table. Our server was also really sweet and met us at our table seconds after we were seated. 

This restaurant is beautiful and huge! The buffet setup seemed to go on forever! The seafood section included chilled and steamed crab legs, crawfish, shrimp, oysters, scallops, mussels, clams, salmon and even a seafood paella. It was all good! Some of the meat they offer includes prime rib, brisket, and lamb chops, which were delicious and tender! Even the lasagna and meatballs were great! Desserts were hit and miss. Try the creme brulee though, it's amazing! I don't know about brunch, but for dinner this place is definitely worth your money, offering both quantity and quality! Best buffet I've ever been to!
This place is amazing but expensive you are not getting for hours unless your a diamond or higher.

Definitely the best buffet I have ever been to, and I've been to quite a few. At your typical buffet there is always a great variety, but the quality of the individual food is just ok. Not here. It seems as though almost every station could be served at it's own individual restaurant and be considered amazing. I now see why the wait can be up to 3+ hours. Located inside Cesar's Palace, if you walk in towards the front entrance, just walk straight back and you should see signs. You wait in line with your party, and then there will usually be another long wait to be seated. However, you may get lucky. Going in at 4pm on a Saturday, we were seated with a party of 5 within 10 minutes. Tip: water and soda is included, beers/wine is extra.
The first station you see as you come in is the seafood station. There are delicious oysters with all the fixins, shrimp, and 2 types of crabs.
Probably the most popular station was the carving/bbq station! Beef ribs, American wagyu steak, short rib, bone marrow, brisket, and thick cut bacon. Sides like corn, fries, beef sliders, mac n cheese, and green tomato sliders.
There were so many different stations that go all the way to the back, make sure you don't miss them! There is Chinese/dim sum, japanese (poke, sushi, etc), Italian (pizza, pasta), steamed crab legs, curry, Mexican food, and more!
And we cannot forget the dessert bar! Along with the little cakes, cheesecakes, and treats, there is an awesome gelato bar with a good selection, and a crepe station! The crepes are made fresh an have a lot of options to stuff them with like chocolate, caramel, nutella, powdered sugar, strawberries, rasberries, and top with whipped cream!

Service was just ok, but let's be honest, who goes to a buffet for service. Food was amazing, and definitely worth the price tag. Just make sure you come hungry!
That was one of the best food experiences I've had in my entire life. All my favorite food items were there in a spectacular fashion.

Thank you  Francisco! You are a greatest waiter that I had never have. This is the first time I bought my parents go to Las Vegas. The trip is for my parent's 38th anniversary. Also, My uncle invited us to have dinner with him at this buffet. He had the tablet for us. When I sit down , Francisco came in and ask us what you want to drink. In my mind I am just ok with old people service us bc I knew they are always a little slow and forgot  when I ask something. However, I was wrong, he is so quick and fast. He is working hard for us Bc we had two little two children. They didn't have cooperate. But Fancisico always smiled. Also, my dad feel so special when he got attention. I will be back here and ask for you when I am back to Las Vegas. Moreover, I want to thank the Caesar have opportunity for people, who have age, workings in service industry. You change my opinion." Never judge people in their look ".

Good food but too pricey for the service offered. The chair I sat on had a tear on it and you'd think if I'm paying 160 bucks for dinner for 2, there would be at least an undamaged chair. The line was also ridiculous. Had to stand for 45 minutes. For the price they charge I expected a waiting area, some seats, a buzzer or a number to be called upon when the food is ready. Not standing in a line for so long.
Esmerelda was awesome! We had a great time! We spent a few hours there and she was attentive and always there when we needed her! 10 out of 10

A feast for the gods. 

$50 weekend champagne brunch. 2 hour wait. Doesn't matter. Amazing.

Yes this place is more expensive than most of the other buffets and I have waited longer here than any other buffet but it is worth it. First off, you can put your name on the list and they will text you when your seat is ready. SO just gamble for two hours until they text you.

I start with three-four plates at once. I hit up the Asian section, there are dumplings, fried rice, some chinese dishes and a few Thai dishes. Next up is the salad and charcuterie section. Pile up my plate with salad and cheeses and meats. Move over to the latin american section. Grabbed some chili verde and some kind of stewed pork dish. You can also make your own tacos here. Next up is the meat section. Prime rib, sausages, ribs, and chiken. There is also mac and cheese, bbq baked beans, and mashed potatoes. Finally there is the seafood section. Lobster benedict, fish slider, seafood paella, oyster shooters, ceviche, jumbo shrimp cocktail, oysters and crab legs. Don't forget the melted butter. 

I am breathing heavily just thinking about it all. 

Back at the table you get unlimited mimosas and bloody marys. For dessert there is a lot to choose from as well but I stuck with some gelato, crepes, cookies and brownies.

You have to try this!

Went with a couple of my friends to eat here for the first time. We we're very impressed with the service from the wait staff. We really loved how attentive they we're, it made the experience even better. Every expectations we had from this buffet was met. We really enjoyed trying the different varieties of food from other countries. My boyfriend really liked that they had a crepe station for dessert.

Absolutely amazing selection, quality and taste. Went during the week around 730pm and wished I had gone earlier as there were Groupon deals if you go before 5pm.  I had terrific Asian food, seafood and beef.  The made to order crepes at the dessert station were yummy!

It's like a internal buffet in one! Steamed bun with duck skin! Yumm.. I love the option and it's clean! One of my favorite buffet on the trip! 

Must try!

Wow.

I got to visit this buffet during one of my work related lunches, and I... I just didn't know.  I JUST DIDN'T KNOW!

Buffets are a dime a dozen here in Vegas.  Some of great.  Delicious, in fact.  And some are like eating the dollar "value" aisle from the grocery store.  Bacchanal Buffet is incredible.  In fact, I'll go on record in saying that it's the best buffet that I've had here in Vegas.

The food choices are more diverse and plentiful.  They had some surprisingly exotic foods to sample here.  Not too many buffets here serve quail eggs, for one.  But the more standard beef, chicken, seafood fare was all excellently prepared, and stylishly done.

The buffet itself has a nice, modern, low-key vibe to it.  Everything is very clean and minimalistic in style, but it's very nice in presentation.  The staff was very accommodating, and quick to meet any need.

And then the desserts.  Holy cow.  It's like strolling into the "previews" section of Willy Wonka's factory.  I'm not a huge dessert enthusiast per se, but everything is presented is such an eye tantalizing way that I had to sample a few of these exotic treats.  Being full, they proved to be my undoing, and I had to call "Full", but man, was it a wonderful, yet brief, journey.

Is Bacchanal Buffet worth the hype?  Yes.  It's a bit pricey, but "you get what you pay for", and what you get can be greater than what you expected.

Well worth a meal here.  It's delicious.

For the price they charge the rib section should have way better bbq sauce selections seafood should have shrimp ceviche and not only tasteless crab legs. Sushi can also use a lot of work, looks and tastes like super market selection. But what gets me is that no buffet, including this one has a dessert section that has enough of the most common flavors of ice cream/gelato/cookies, CHOCOLATE. No one wants green tea gelato, what's that taste like? Leaves??? I was there opening weekend and have gone multiple times a year, always hoping for some improvements but have been noticing the opposite. The Mexican street tacos are amazing, but not $45-$55 worth. Can get those for $5. Pizza is also worse than dominoes.

Simplemente espectacular y la atención muy buena,en especial Raquel,siempre preocupada d las necesidades d los comensales.

Aplausos !!

This would be a 5 star review if not for the RUDE woman working in the entrance of the Buffet. Samantha is her name, was on her tag. Almost seems like she was showing off in front of her peers. What a scab on great place to come and enjoy your vacation. When you pay THIS much for a buffet, you do not expect rude people working there. The other employees were in word, wonderful.
Muy buen servicio y todo la comida esta muy buena  sw les recomiendo mucha  variedad  de comida y de poatres. Los drink  estan buenos
Jennifer was our server this morning and was attentive, fast and friendly! The food was excellent, lots of selections. The desserts were my favorite!

Sadly bacchanal seems to be too successful. Went on 4/17/19. There is now a kiosk to get a time to stand in line. You return at the appointed time and you get to stand in line. At the end of this line you stand in line again until there is a table clear. The food was still amazing and the guy at the meat cutting station was very personable. Now the bad. I waited 18 minutes to get a drink. I finally flagged down what I thought was a manager and she found my server. My drink was plopped in front of me. If you have ever told a teenager to bring you something that was the attitude I received for the remainder of my visit. Finally another waiter began bringing refills despite my being in a different section. He was a rockstar. I notified the manager on my way out and left a significant tip for the waiter that helped me. The manager told me I should have notified him earlier ( I thought the hostess with the headset was a manager) and promised if it happened again he would wait on me himself. Realistically I come to Vegas twice a year so my business is not going to make or break them and clearly they aren't lacking in business. Truly a disappointment from one of my favorite stops

We had very high expectations for this meal based on eating here last year. Ironically, we at the wicked spoon the next day. The wicked spoon was hands down 100x better. The options at the bacchanal buffet were twice as many, but the food at the wicked spoon was clearly prepared better and focused more on creating better quality vs. quantity. My favorite was waiting 10-15 minutes to get a half plate of crab and the employee who was limiting everyone's intake of crab. Glad I spent $65 to be limited. I would highly recommend the wicked spoon buffet over this one.

They have a check in,but still 3 hours wait.Its good buffet but no-one needs the swollen ankles from standing in line or drunk surroundings for the trouble.Your better off watching youtube videos and buying your own shit!

One of my favorite buffets ever. I've been here a lot, since we always bring people who are visiting us to this buffet at Caesars. I have to say that every visit to Bacchanal can be different, depending on which meal you're eating and which events are going on.  

If you go for breakfast/lunch, you can expect a good mix of food but you may not see some of more expensive entrees and desserts until later. Of course for dinner, you wont get all the breakfast stuff and you're paying more. Also, they do have specials for holidays, and usually do charge you extra on those days. Weekends will also cost you more, and you will have a longer wait during peak meal hours. You can also add on a beer/wine package to your dinner if you'd like.

My favorites at this buffet are: Prime rib, street tacos (made to order), fresh juices (at brunch), gelato, noodle soup station (ramen, laksa, pho, etc), lamb, Portuguese egg tarts, and any of the pastas.  The great thing about Bacchanal is that everything is portioned in small plates, so you can try everything you want to and explore new cuisines.  The service has been great, and they'll get you your drinks and clear your plates pretty quickly. It has something for everyone, so you don't need to worry about picky eaters!

This restaurant had the best food I have ever tasted in my entire life I wished that I was 50 pounds fatter so that I could continue to stuff my face with the greatness that the restaurant serves. Even my wife approves of this comment.

Amazing food and presentation. I want to come back again. Our server, Santiago went above and beyond. He was very prompt and answered all our questions. I only gave 4 stars because of a woman behind the dessert counter who was not very pleasant.

Choices of food are so awesome from quality to taste it's a winner! It's so worth it!!! Very friendly servers and I got my free red wine!!! There's always room for this beautiful desserts! Thank you so much! We definitely coming back on our next Vegas trip!

It was incredible, just incredible. I love my buffets (Vegas and other places), and this was the First place I'd seen small plates of gourmet tapas, amazing flavors put together on small plates. Of course there were some items that weren't great, but luckily I could just not finish them. It is a hefty price tag, go for a late lunch. It was a 'holiday weekend', lunch was $55(?) & Dinner would have been around $70(?). Would have been VERY hard to swallow a $70/pp price tag. They are very strict on the time cut-off, if our party of 5 hadn't paid together, the last 3pp would have had to pay the dinner price. So, I reiterate, this is NOT to be missed, but go for a late lunch. Also, there are usually Groupons (weekday) or for us, we checked into Yelp & got a free champagne.

Visited this buffet for breakfast/lunch on October 3rd.  The ladies at the resisters checking my group in were helpful and kind.  The rest of the staff were just as kind and checked up on us regularly. 

The food is absolutely amazing and we would come here again and again.  The selection was suitable for friends whom had dietary preferences and restrictions - vegetarian and allergies to certain ingredients. 

We paid the up charge to include this with the buffet of buffets pass. The group decides from now on to omit the pass and simply pay a similar amount to visit here once or twice on our next trip.
Great spread. Good noise level!! Yummy all around. Server was a little slow with my champagne but that's okay it gave me more time to enjoy the world wide cuisine.
Wow this place is the place to go to for the ultimate buffet experience! There are so many food and dessert choices. I really like the taco station

I came. I saw. I kicked myself for spending $25 on this dreck.

Break out your map and compass. Freshen up on the orienteering skills you learned at summer camp. You're going to need all of that to find the buffet at Caesar's Palace.

We all know that casinos don't have direct lines between any two places. But Caesars raises the bar to a whole new level. I swear to Jesus, their maps are wrong. Even after I successfully found Bacchanal one time, it took literally 15 minutes to find it when a friend insisted on going there for dinner (we bailed out after seeing the line).

I sampled all of the high-end buffets during my latest trip and Bacchanal was easily the least impressive. (BTW-The breakfast on a Tuesday morning for Total Rewards members was $25--NOT $16.99 as shown in the first pic on their Yelp page).

Bacchanal has several kinds of scrambled eggs--Mexican, Italian, plain Jane. And all of them were cold and congealed. There were just as many forms of bacon--regular bacon, slab bacon cut to order, pepper bacon. Again, all were just a smidge above room temperature.

The easy-to-miss omelet station was a big swing-and-a-miss. Who likes an undercooked omelet that's runny in the middle? 

The Asian section was barely passable. No spoon in the steamed rice cooker, so I used a nearby soup spoon to dish mine out.

Someone in the buffet department needs to be fed to the lions...cold, of course.

I cant believe I havent written a review for this place yet.  We stay at Ceasers every time we come to Vegas because my 5 year old loves it.  We come twice a year.   We deal with the crowds and the wait just to come to this waaay over priced buffet.  But I'm a crab leg and seafood girl so I take advantage of that.  Lines on the inside can be redundant.  I'm so over lines by the time you get inside I miss half the food but there is so much that you won't leave hungry.  I love the pho, the sliced meat selections, and mashed potatoes.  Plan on taking your time.  Desserts are good but by the time you get there, your so full, blah.  My little old lady momma takes some to go lol.  Makes for good snacks especially for a 5 year old.  Service is basic.  They get drinks, clear plates but thats it.  I don't expect anything more.  The food shines here but I just wish the hot dishes were actually hot.  Everything is lukewarm at best.   Must try at least once.

A bit pricey, but a lot of options and reasonably high quality at that.

We stopped by with a Groupon, which was sort of helpful, although coming at the time we did (4 PM on a weekday), it wasn't particularly busy and still took us a bit of time to get seated. The variety is quite good with various cuisines represented, and portions all not too big so that you can try them all. The service is reasonably quick to whisk away your unnecessary plates, and it's a fairly large space--a good place to have an all-you-can-eat meal.

I still give this place five stars even though I came out of it hating myself for allowing myself to gorge. I swore I would not touch food for 10 days (ate breakfast the next morning...) and having to recline at a 45 degree angle after eating because sitting upright would be too painful.

But was it worth it? My God Yes. If you go to Vegas, you have to do it right. Eating like there's no tomorrow is one of them. The food here is TOP NOTCH quality for buffet food (except the sushi -- skip that). The desserts were heavenly, and I loved that the seafood was already cracked open for you -- at least the king crab legs are. If you like meat, you will be stoked by the meat section where you can get ribs and succulent cuts of anything imaginable. They also have an Asian, Cheese, Udon, Sushi, Mexican, and seafood section (obviously).

Yes, the wait is extremely long. You'll have to line up for 2-3 hours for lunch alone, but I think the experience was top notch. Yes, it's very pricey ($50 a person) but imagine dining out an ordering all of these things separately! It'd be much more than that, so I definitely think the entire experience was worth it -- both the money and time. The quality is unparalleled and you'll think it's worth it, especially if you're a sweet tooth like me!

It takes an hour to go into the buffet(it was tuesday!) There is no computer waiting system. It has a lot of sea food stations. I loved foods and interior, especially the ceiling of the buffet, but it needs to have some digital waiting system.

This is the best buffet in Vegas, or anywhere I've ever been for that matter. Yes, it is pricy. But it has the most selection by far. Tons of exquisite desserts, the Viennese drinking chocolate is exceptional, gelatos, creme brûlée, cakes, chocolate covered strawberries, all so well done, none "throw aways" like at some other buffets. The carving station had like 7 different choices when I went, exceptional seafood, Asian station had tons, Italian. My favorite is the little touches that aren't at other buffets: the tacos station where u select your meats from a man and he warms them up with extras for you on a grill, the smoothies, the micro-sculpted fruit cup, never saw anything like that before. I've been 3 times, all 3 perfect. I've taken my family, they all said best meal ever. Period. We went for lunch & for dinner, and both equally exceptional.
The buffet has every type of food you could want--from seafood to tacos to sushi to roast beef. There were also so many desserts to choose. Come hungry because there is so much to try.

Everything was delicious. We were so busy eating we didn't really take advantage of the "all you can drink" upgrade even though we paid for it. The line took about 30 minutes but it was definitely worth the wait. Definitely recommend going there at least once during any trip to Vegas.

We wanted to love it but it was really painful.
I highly recommend DO NOT GO THERE.There are much better options like wicked spoon. here is why

1) We were expecting huge lines, we got a ticket for reservation which suggested to come back in 1.5 hrs. And we learnt that after 1.5 hrs u actually get to stand in line and it took 2 hrs to get table total of 3.5 hrs waiting. Worst thing is you MUST have to STAND in line for 2 hrs. Only way to avoid that is 65$ express fee per person. It was ridiculous when we are already paying 75$ per person. Few of my friends were fainting almost and had to call someone to have them seat. It was just painful for everyone in our friends and family.

2) Really bad number of selection for vegetarian. It was hardly 10% of total items

3) There is no labelling for Vegetarian so you always have to ask someone. And employees were cluless as when I ask 'Is this Vegetarian?' few told yes others said no. I was like what if I am allergic service was totally pathetic.

Food quality was definitely good but these three points ruined our experience. When our friends went to wicked spoon it was opposite. Host actually got all veg food in plates from buffet and just gave it on table for them and also lines were not painful like this

Came here based on a recommendation made on Yelp.  This is a new buffet at Caesar's Palace and looks like they spent a pretty penny creating this place.

I waited about 25 mins in line and noticed there were a lot of young 20-something asian kids.    To me that was a good sign as my fellow yellow brothas and sistas and I have similar food tastes (haha generally speaking).

I sampled the goods before I committed to anything and surprisingly a lot of the food I ate was pretty good.

The woodfired pizzas were actually surprisingly good (I mean who the freak eats pizza at a AYCE buffet?).  I also sampled the prime rib which was cooked well and to my liking.

Even the fried chicken was pretty good.

The dessert bar is amazing here... you can eat everything from gelato, to cheesecake and they even have freakin jelly bellies!!!

My fellow asians and I were hoarding the crab legs as well... 

This buffet costs about 49 for lunch and is more expensive than your typical AYCE LV buffet but the quality level is definitely a notch higher than most.

My only gripe is the crab legs weren't as good as other buffets... just my 2 cents.

Well I had the pleasure of sampling two Las Vegas buffets, Aria and Bacchanal. Well let me say this; Bacchanal is worth its price tab based on the varied items it has. It has maybe five times or more as Aria. And all the similar items I sampled tasted better except for the pork belly. Arias pork belly was the bomb. I can still taste the happy feeling in my mouth. Bacchanal provided me the thinks I liked. Everything I had was great (brisket, some type of mac and cheese, mashed potatoes, some type of fried rice, they had more than one type, bacon, sausage, pizza). I was completely full after just two plates with one cup of coffee and OJ. There was so many other things I wanted to try but had no room. I now clearly see the argument for Bacchanal vying for the number one spot. Oh the desserts though were meh.

My family and I were super excited to get into this buffet and even endured the long line to get in and pay that steep price.... and was honesty really disappointed. The staff was very nice and helpful but the food was just not up to what I expected, especially for it to be rated as the #1 in LV. Not a tremendous amount of variety and what was there was just not good..
