This is probably the best buffet in Vegas right now, in my opinion.  It is also the most expensive buffet!!  At around $59.00 a person on average (the prices change) it is much pricier than most.  But why is it so good?
Awesomeness:
- Beautiful Buffet Display
- Taste is much better than most other buffets in Vegas.
- Custom Omelet, Gourmet Pizza, Fresh Gelato, Chinese Porridge
There is a lot of vegetarian options which is nice.  Not that many gluten free and vegan options unfortunately.  
This is in Caesars Palace.
I went here literally one time and I went during the day, it was AMAZING the buffet is great for only 50 a person where it's SO MUCH food I would go again

another buffet in vegas?
who'da thunk it!?

we first dined here at a yelp event and liked it enough to go again and pay full boat to try out some of the stuff we couldn't fit in our bellies the first time around.
it was my friend's b'day, visiting from l.a., loves buffets so this was the obvious choice.

we went early, 5pm, to avoid the long lines.
we used our player's cards to receive a small discount...$2 if i remember correctly.
there was a very short line and we were seated within minutes.

what i like about bacchanal is the way all of the food is set up and displayed.
they've definitely taken some ideas from wicked spoon with some items served in individually portioned dishes.
i really appreciate that since i'm quite phobic about other people's germs (opg, if you will.)

i was also pleasantly surprised with the level of service at each station.
at most buffets in town, the chefs/cooks manning the food stations don't speak, aren't helpful and typically keep to themselves.
that was not the case here.
there was a friendly greeting at each station with hands prepared to help out in every way possible.
for example, i'm perfectly capable of serving my own bowl of soup but the gentleman in the soup station was kind enough to spoon one up for me.
it was like that the whole night.
nice touch.

as for the food, it was good...not amazing.
i want to say it's due to the fact that i'm a non-meat eater.
the rest of my party, especially those eating meat, was loving the tomahawk steak, lamb and other selections from the carving station.
the seafood was decent.
it's tough to have a perfectly cooked piece of fish when it's been sitting in a large serving dish under a heat lamp so i was disappointed with that.
the cold seafood was decent but also underwhelming.

the desserts were the highlight for me.
made to order souffles, macarons and a delightful assorment of pastries.
love it!

i would most certainly return when guests are in town and are craving a buffet.
show up early to avoid the crowds, sign up for a player's card for a little discount and you're good to go.
This is the best bacchanal buffet restaurant in Las Vegas and thank you the best service

Fantastic buffet with restaurant-quality food. Large variety of food (Asian, Italian, Mexican cuisine sections and a huge array of seafood, along with a dessert bar) and efficient, friendly service. Nothing was oversalted, which was a nice change of pace for buffets. Highly recommend the in-house gelato!

The early bird special is worth the saved money - the Groupon is the same price with one free drink per person, with about an extra $10 off with Groupon Select.

I love buffets. It gives me an opportunity to try a variety of dishes at once. It's like a carnival for my tummy ! And this Bacchanal buffet is the biggest of all I ever tried. I had my share of very high expectations on this and dreaming about it. I was constantly worried about being in Line for more than an hour to get seated. 

Waiting and getting in ***/5 : They have virtual line kiosks but they are not working when we went on a Saturday. We went during breakfast to pre-book a table for dinner which they do not offer ! That is uncomfortable. I would suggest going between 3 pm-4.30 pm for dinner.

Space and service *****/5 : all problems stop right before you enter inside the restaurant. Their service is impeccable. Water and soda refills were quick and taking away used plates too. 

Food : ****/5 : I loved most of their dishes and their selection is Hugeeeeeee. Few dishes stood out for me.
1. Bone marrow with crackers 
2. Hot snow crab legs 
3. Duck roast and pork belly
4. Fried Frog legs
5. Dimsums
6. Creeme brûlée samplers

I wish I had more appetite to try everything on their menu. Great food and service except for wait times to get in.

So I heard this place was the place to go!! So We was in Vegas for my wife 40th bday , we decided to try this buffet out for ourselves. Talk about HELLA people..... The line was so long it was redonkuless! Good thing my little cousin Andrew was smart enough to pay in advance so you can skip the line and wait in the , WAIT TO BE SEATED LINE. It didn't take too long to be seated at that point. The interior was pretty nice for a buffet, which it should be since it's in Vegas. Waiter was quick to take our drink orders which was a plus. You had a smorgasbord of food to choose from! You got Chinese food to Italian to American etc, you name it. I'll list a few dishes that I would totally recommend you to try , if you go to BACCHANAL. 

Corn On The Cob- this is a must must must try!!! It was so buttery and delicious! It reminds me of ELOTE . For those who didn't know what elote means, you are missing out!!! It's basically corn on the cob Mexican style. With butter , mayo, and paprika, cheese. Anyways, you just gotta try it lol 

ROASTED PORK - This was really good. It was flavorful and the crunchiness was amazing. I'm a protein guy so this hit the spot. 

Pork Belly - who doesn't love pork belly?! This was an awesome dish. It's was like a party in your mouth . A taste of heaven , is how I would put it.

Iceberg Lettuce - I'm a sucker ,when it comes to iceberg lettuce. Something about that crunch. I actually like ranch in mine but I don't mind blue cheese. 

Beef Ribs - This was one of my favorites. Sprinkle a little bit of salt on it , then taste the magic. I had to go back for thirds in these bad boys. 

Dessert , TINY CREAM FILLED DONUTS -  I'm not a huge deal guy, but when I find singing that's delicious I really Indulge a lot of it ha ha. These little suckers are out of this world good. 

Over all it was an awesome experience at Bacchanal. Would I come back again??.... Maybe. I'm the type that likes to try new things as much as possible. There was so much food,  i really didn't know what to eat. It's prob impossible to try everything they had. I try to take pictures of all the food as I possibly can to give you an idea of what it looked like tho.

Look out for a woman named SARA, she will check you in express if you're white at no charge! We got an express ticket to get in faster for a $35 extra charge. But no she'll ignore the line and help out her white customers. Wonder if we looked too poor for her to at least say "I'll be with you in a second. Then getting in, our waiter gave us one round of drinks, and never table tapped, or refilled our drinks. His only job was to get drinks and check in on customers, but the runner was doing more work than him. Sucks that a restaurant with good food, is ruined by a lack of hospitality from front of house.

I was so excited to try out Bacchanal for the first time...I was a bit disappointed with my experience.  My mouth was watering after reading these amazing reviews, and once I coerced my friends into going, I left painfully full of mediocre food.

We went at the end of brunch on a Saturday, so paid a little less than $50 for unlimited mimosas.  That was a plus...I definitely got $50 worth of champagne.

The seating and the buffet stations were set up nicely in different food types.  I made a bee line for the seafood station, which was probably my favorite aside from the desserts.  They had huge jumbo shrimp, crab legs and oysters.  I would recommend getting the crab legs warm and don't forget the butter!  I enjoyed the miso glazed sea bass and the lobster corn chowder.

Next, I had to try the carving station.  I tried the prime rib and pork belly...all super salty and dry.  Very disappointed.  Mac and cheese was ok.

I would stay away from the sushi...sushi rice was not good and it is just filler anyway.  The dim sum station was decent.  Nothing else really stood out to me.

The dessert station is located in the middle of the restaurant and is filled with delicious gelato, chocolate dipped strawberries (huuugge!), mini-cakes, macarons and other delightful sweets.  

Personally, I would rather go to Wicked Spoon for brunch since they have bloody marys and an awesome dessert section as well!

Be careful! Food poisoning! Unfortunately, I need to change my review due to getting food poisoning and the quality of the food having gone down drastically.

On our last visit 3/5/18 for late lunch I got food poisoning about 5 hours after leaving. It was awful and unexpected, yet in hindsight the food temperature as well as appearance of many items indicates it was most definitely due to the buffet. Further, it was my only meal that day. Lastly, we have been here before so this is a reminder to myself and others to be very careful and trust your instincts when looking at the selections. 

Even before getting sick the entire party agreed that the food quality, selection, choices, and service has gone down. The meat selections while visually appetizing were under seasoned and under temperature, the Asian food was awful with many items being lukewarm, the dessert selections were just fine but lacking oomph...

Eat at your own risk. Sure this can happen anywhere but a place like this is responsible for ensuring each item as well as staff are abiding by proper food preparation and serving guidelines. We have tried contacting management but were unable to get a hold of anyone over the weekend.

Got VIP and still had to wait on line. Lots of choices but not for the picky eater. Everything was very fofo. Great for my husband who could eat unlimited crab legs. And lots of desserts. My favorite part.

I am finally getting to redo this review. A few weeks back, my friends and I went out to dinner at Bacchanal. 
My experience was awesome, so I feel it is only right to update my review. Staff was on point, our server was on point and the food was hot! I did not find my self complaining at all which is a bit rare. 
Not sure how consistent this place is but for that one night, I really enjoyed my dinner.

Here is a major key: knowing when to come to a buffet to indulge in all of their yummy offerings. The last time I was here I came during brunch hours and it wasn't too bad, but last night I came here during a weekend dinner omg, what a feast. The taco station was fantastic, the roasted duck and dim sum tasted great. I was a bit sad that they didn't serve sashimi so I ate three more roasted duck drumstick lol. I ate so much of the savory food items, I didn't leave any room for dessert. Boo, foodie fail by me! Although I did not eat any dessert, what I had throughout the evening was great!

This buffet was definitely worth the wait and hype. We came here on a Tuesday, after Labor Day weekend. It was still pretty busy. We arrived at the check in podium at 1:39 and used the kiosk to get a ticket. Ticket told us to come back at 2:27. About a 40 min wait, and we hopped back into line to pay. Then we waited about another 30 min to pay, and I was ecstatic because we got charged the lunch price for dinner. Great tips by other fellow yelpers. It doesn't hurt to save some money, and the cashier didn't mind because she was a ninja getting these customers in by 3:00pm. Then we waited another 20 min to get seated. 

After the long wait, we decided to sit down first to rest our feet. But before long, my eyes started to wonder and my stomach grew. There were so many stations, that I didn't see the Chinese section hidden in the back. Their dim sum was amazing. No knock offs, with even the soy sauce and chili to go with it. They had a noodle bar where you could get ramen, pho, or udon. The udon was delicious and I would have gotten another bowl if I didn't eat so much. They have steam crab in the Italian section, and the man before the counter is very generous. He serves you it. I prefer cold crab usually, but it was really salty, so the steamed crab was a better choice. They had roasted pig, and it was perfection. I could grab crispy skin without feeling guilty that I needed to save the rest for other patrons. The dessert section had so much variety but I only had room for creme brûlée. 

The service was fantastic. Other than the wait, I would definitely be back again! I'm hungry just writing this review!

Came for my 21st birthday...left feeling sick and annoyed.

Our night started off amazing, with great food and service but as the night progressed, we barely saw our server and had to ask other servers for drink refills, crab crackers, and other things.

Our entire table of oyster lovers spit out the oysters because they were clearly rotten, and we told our server but neither she nor a manager cared to ask if we were okay.  

After the incident, we waited for about 45 minutes for our server, even made eye contact with someone who seemed to be a manager but she ignored us and went to stand in a corner the entire night. We finally got to ask our server if we can get a candle and she actually sang to me too, which was sweet.

All in all, we were pleased at the beginning but the night ended poorly and although this place will always be iconic, my birthday dinner and first experience here was ruined.

Came here on Easter weekend cause a friend and her family was in town. Totally forgot that buffets jack up the price on holiday weekends. Spent a total of $148 for my bf and I ($74/person)

Was it worth it? Nope!

Food - Some were good and some were not. Their Asian food was not bad. Sui Mai dishes tasted better than other restaurants I've been too. Their Brie and truffle oil pizza was good but obviously not as great at Sammy's Woodfired Pizza. It would probably taste the same if the crust was thin like theirs. Their seafood section wasn't interesting to me at all. Everything is on ice, miso halibut was super sweet and the lobster chowder was beyond salty. Sushi section, the nigiri weren't bad at all. Desserts are awesome. I love me some rich chocolate!

Drinks - by the bread station they have a bunch of mini milk bottle type w a variety of juices. Love love love the guava!

All in all, it was good but nothing to boast about. Would I come back? Definitely not. The price is outrageous.

This place is soooo good too! If you're very hungry and not in the mood to wait you can go here and still get quality food but quickly and with so many options! I am a local but I still like to treat myself and go here and "play" tourist without wasting my day when I still have a lot to do and am not in the mood to actually have a long, sit down meal. I don't usually love buffets because I question the cleanliness and freshness of food but here they are so on top of sanitary guidelines and food standards. I've never had one thing that doesn't taste great and I feel good afterwards too! The seafood is my go-to item that I like. Thanks for the awesome experience. I will definitely be back again sometime soon.

Our group of 6 were there for dinner on Friday. Being Diamond member, we didn't have to wait long.  The food, unfortunately, was not up to par (it has been up & down the couple years).  The jumbo cold shrimp were not "jumbo", the famous crab legs were not the same (and of inferior quality).  They also eliminated some of the items we liked.  There were plenty of food to pick from, but for $65 per person, the quality of the buffet has definitely gone downhill slowly.  It has come to a point that we wondered if it was worth the price.

I think I'm officially done with Las Vegas buffets.  We were beyond disappointed with the food at Bacchanal.  Waiting in line for this buffet took most of our day since it was Christmas.  The cost is atrocious for the quality of food.  It seems like they were simply keeping up with the crowds and hurriedly providing the food.  Cleanliness was an issue for us.  Anytime you have a buffet, you have to constantly clean the area since so many people are dishing up food.  $160.00 for 2 people, I think not.

This was an amazing choice for brunch I was definitely not disappointed. I usually stay away from buffets but this one will get my Monet every time I am in Vegas. The staff were amazing my mimosas were great and the food well that's a league of its own. If you are in Vegas or visiting I definitely recommend that you visit this great restaurant.

The dish was well prepared and the food was delicious. I like the crab leg especially those cut in half one which make me so easy to eat but whole leg is more juicy. Pizza is so nice crispy and  full tasted cheese and mushrooms. The dessert is wonderful which must try. The only disappointment was the queue too long nearly 1.5 hours to wait. Tip is go there earlier or later of the meal time.

3 best strip buffets are Bacchanal, Wynn, Wicked Spoon, plus a honorable mention The buffet at Aria (because I get bogo deals). 

Bacchanal can justify the higher price $40 for lunch and $55 for dinner because they invested over $100 million usd into this buffet worthy to seat Caesar himself. 

Some of the stand out items I personally recommend: steamed king crab legs (back room), 12 hour smoked brisket, bone marrow, beef ribs and short ribs, dim sum, sushi sashimi, and made to order tacos al pastor. 

There's over 500 items to make the pickiest eater happy. The dessert selection does not match the variety at Wicked Spoon, but the quality was top notch. To finish your meal be sure to get tiramisu, creme brûlée, and Thai tea mousse.

I came yesterday for salmon . I was craving it . I went to the sea food station four times . Each time I was told it would be ready in ten minutes . It never came . I left without tasting it .  I am so so so sad . When you spend $250 dollars for a family of five for dinner you expect everything to be available . I watched a YouTube video of chef Leticia and her high standards , and that is what brought us to try it . I am sure she too would be disappointed. I really wanted some salmon

Expensive buffet for nothing. Power went out when we started eating and we had already paid. All cooks said they weren't sure when electricity would come back, in the mean time we ate what was left. Not the workers fault, but for 120 dollars me and my girlfriend expected more. Food became cold, grills stopped working, and me and my girlfriend were left feeling like we had to leave. I wanted to be mad but seeing that there were so many on the same boat, I didn't wanna be entitled and complain.... yet here I am on Yelp.. fuck man I want hot crab legs...

Ate dinner here last night after hearing all the awesome reviews about it, let me start off by saying they food was great, nice selection of different varieties of food. However I personally think $55 per a person is a-bit steep for this buffet, unless your going to go all crazy on there seafood section I wouldn't bother. There dessert bar was amazing. Four stars because everything was great except for the price.

So many options it can be a little too intimidating. I found a few things I liked but there honestly wasn't a lot of flavor in the foods. It's so expensive and we had to wait about 25 min to enter. Service was great but I would probably check out another buffet. People rave about this one but it wasn't for me.

Came here for dinner during the labor day weekend. Food is excellent ( king crab, waygu beef, bone marrow...ect). Come early, the line getting in is long like as if you're waiting for an amusement ride.

By far the best buffet in Vegas - trust me, it's worth the line up. 

With over 500 dishes to choose from and 15 chef specials that change daily, dishes are prepared in an open kitchen concept for customers to see. From the Italian section to Mexican, Chinese, Seafood or Japanese section, you won't get to try out everything in one dinner, so choose your dishes wisely!

My favourite station at the Bacchanal is the carving station. I have yet to visit a buffet that offers this much variety in quality cut meat - which includes rack of lamb, beef flank, prime rib...etc. The lamb is AMAZING - I would come back and pay $50.00 again just to have the lamb rack. 

The dessert station is also worth coming back for. Why? They have mochi ice cream, with flavours that include black sesame (my favourite) , strawberry and chocolate. Candy pops looked really cute, but I saved my stomach to have some macarons that were out on display. Crepes are also made in front of you to your preferences, sugarless/fat-free cakes are also offered as well as tiny tiramisu shots and bread pudding. 

I'm not too big a fan of seafood, so I didn't even bother visiting the seafood station. From what I can see, there are tons of seafood varieties for seafood lovers out there!

I'll definitely be back! With your TotalRewards card (free to register), you can save $1 on your dinner. I know it's only a dollar, but hey.. that dollar can be the token to big casino winnings!

Amazing quality of well cooked dishes!!  Seafood,  Burger sliders,  Chicken & Waffle pre-made combos, perfect fresh cut french fries, pizza, beautiful dessert pastries. ...... Highly recommend this buffet....pricey, but worthy.
They have Oxtail Soup and Shave Ice, what more could you ask for?

Highly Overrated, I went to the Bacchanal Buffet expecting the best and got mediocre at best. As my party arrived it took about an hour to get seated and I was still optimistic about the food, I surveyed the buffet to see what's in store and there wasn't very much. The Asian cuisine section was very basic, the seafood section was just shrimp and crab legs and the protein section was the usual meats like pork, ham, lamb which was tougher than some of the fights held in Vegas. I didn't see any rotisserie chicken, or tasted anything that was seasoned well. The desert section has cupcakes, ice cream, some cheesecake, and other selections of desserts. I was highly disappointed, especially after spending $70.00 on this basic food stop. I will not be returning unless they step their game up significantly. If you want basic food at an inflated price this is the place. If you want good food and more of a selection, go somewhere else.
Service was top notch! Lorri took really great care of us and made sure we were all very happy! 5 starts for service!

Oh so painful to write bad reviews... but I think I need to do it for future diners.

I've been to Bacchanal buffet 4 times. The first time it was great- I mean it's known to be one of the best buffets in Vegas of all places! We thought the selection was good and there was a nice variety. 

The second time we thought it was a bit off or maybe we weren't hungry enough... 

The third time, hm we weren't impressed at all. 

Finally the fourth time - mind you these trips were over a 2 year span... we were so disappointed and barely ate half a plate of food combined. Even though my husband and I didn't want to go back after the 3rd unimpressive trip, our friends have never been to the buffet so we took a chance and returned. A group of 4 of us went and we each brought over about 3 plates of food each in total (not very full plates) but we were painfully trying to work our way though each bite. We actually all hate wasting food so every time we went for a plate we took very little bit of each item we wanted to try but we could not finish any of them. So after each disappointment we thought maybe we need to try something else and therefore ended up going up for more even though we couldn't finish our other plates. 

EVERYTHING I mean EVERYTHING was so salty or dry. I mean.... goodness man we dine out a lot and I'm not one of those people that eats a salad with olive oil and lemon. I do like my food well seasoned but this was a whole different story. Way, way too salty. Even the boiled seafood was salty! And my friend had 1 "fresh" oyster that was clearly not fresh at all. Not expecting the best but expected the oysters to be acceptable.. but it wasn't. I think I drank $20 worth of juice mixed with club soda to wash down the salt there. Like come on... I know buffets make their food salty so people can't eat 20 plates of food, but when charging so much they should know better not to go so overboard with it. The 4 of us could have spent about $10 more each and went for fine dining. 

No longer worth the money... and talk about the wait. The time and meal we wasted was a true disappointment. This last trip almost made my husband and I never want to return to ANY Vegas buffet. We wanted to try Sterling brunch buffet but now we're afraid that might suck too :(

Incredible buffet. We were awed by every experience at this buffet. They have so many options for food and it all feels/tastes like high quality fresh food. The staff were all incredible pleasant and easy to communicate with. This is definitely a Vegas experience you shouldn't miss.

Amazing food... amazing experience.... servers are great .. go straight for the meat first. Thanksgiving buffet was a little bit of a wait but completely worth it. Food delicious. What more can i say ? Fabulous

Definitely the top buffet on the strip. I've tried Aria and Wynn, among others and this is the one I recall the most. Good stations, clean, solid desserts.

The attention to detail with the finger mitts is unusual and very helpful.

(Visited 2 years ago)

Total disappointment! The steak, lamb chop, bone marrow, ham were terribly made and hard to chew. The seafood station served two kinds of crab legs, crayfish, and while I was waiting they added a kind of shellfish. There were also some other cooked seafood dishes but I didn't try. The waiting line for boiling seafood station was forever long. It took me 45 minutes to get to the station and had the staff (cold face with no communication at all) boiled the seafood (I put on a plate) to serve warm. Or you can just take them and leave without boiling them. Shame on the management to charge such high price on Christmas Day but poorly presented the food and made people wait a long time in line for seafood. They did add another line later while we were there (around 1pm) by the asian food corner, but that station only served crab legs and did not allow you to pick (staff randomly grabbed a few legs, boiled them and then put them on your plate). After they added that line, the waiting time for getting crab legs dropped a little bit.

We used VIP reservation via opentable ($98 per person including the buffet cost) and didn't have to wait in line for hours and that is the only plus we felt worth the price. That became nightmare for other people if they were walk-ins. The VIP reservation came with a seafood tower with lobster tail, crab legs, shrimp, raw oysters. The lobster tail was not fresh at all although other items were okay. The crab legs came with the VIP seafood tower were much less salty and fresh than the ones served to the public. Shame on the management again! You had to pay for freshness!? Other customers would not know the crab legs were less fresh and much more salty if they didn't have the VIP seafood tower. 

The only one good thing I can say about is the service was okay. VIP reservation came with unlimited alcohol drinks and the waiter checked us frequently to refill our drinks. 

We will not go back to this buffet again and do not recommend to others!

Came here to eat with 4 people at 3ish on a Saturday. Was surprised to see such a long line, broken up by guest count: 1-2, 3-4, 5 or more. We asked the lady who was watching the lines some information as to pricing, how long the wait was, etc. , but she said it was her first day and she didn't know much. 

We waited for about 20 mins before paying up, and then waited in a separate line to be seated. Waited about another 20 minutes before we were taken in. 

Pricing:
Weekends after 3pm: $65 for each adult 

Highlights:
Brisket
Pulled pork 
Cold cocktail shrimp 
Cold crab legs
Warm crab legs ***is located in the Italian section and is absolutely delicious. Highlight of the whole meal 
Mac and cheese (with bacon) 
Truffle mushroom soup 

They have your typical Asian section with dim sum and other dishes, Italian, seafood, Mexican, etc. , but crab legs is where it's at! We will be back.
很多种类的选择，有海鲜，甜点，和各国的美食，就是现在价格变贵了，周日54美元一位，价格还是不便宜的！味道还是不错的，可惜一个人肚子有限吃不了那么多好吃的！

Well this place is a disaster and I recommend you avoid it at all cost   We will start with the food   The prime rib was suppose to be warm and is ice cold. The sushi looks like it has sat out in the Vegas sun and I didn't even try it. It just looked nasty and old. Other meats were tough and hard to chew. Now for the worst part.  The service. The staff was obviously angry. It took 23 minutes to get a beverage. I actually just look at my watch as we sat down and then when we got service   When they would walk by and we put our hand up to get their attention they ignored us   We actually had to get a manager to get our drinks.  Now if they are understaffed for the price they charged they could hire more people    And just one more nail in the coffin here. This was my birthday dinner my better half bought for me and has spent the last 2 hours apologizing to me for the poor service

5 stars? ABSOLUTELY. Holy fine dining buffet! I have been here twice. There is a couple different ways to get in....if you are a platinum member you can access the buffet through an express line, otherwise, be here early or LINES AND WAIT TIMES OF 1+ HOURS. Fortunately, we typically do Vegas trips as a family so express line it is. Also, be prepared for the PRICE:: $45-$65 depending on if it's brunch or dinner, per person. You can also purchase exclusive packages that include all you can drink alcohol which ranges an additional $15-$35 depending on the type of package and whether it's brunch or dinner. OKAY LETS HIT THE IMPORTANT NOTES. THE FOOD!!!!! I want to let you all know something personal before I start this review, the first time I came here I was extremely sick and was suffering from horrible stomach problems that had me in and out of the hospital and I want you to know....I drove ALL THE WAY TO VEGAS TO MEET MY FAMILY SPECIFICALLY FOR THIS BUFFET.  I know, insane, but if you are a hardcore foodie, nothing stops you! My biggest critique of this restaurant is literally WHY IS IT SO FAR AWAY FROM ME?! I would recommend this to people who want to try a variety of foods that are from around the world. It's a "tasting bar" buffet. Not sure if that's a legit thing or if I made it up in my head but either way, IT IS! And it's not the run of the mill buffet where a bunch of frozen crap is put out. IT IS ALL MADE FROM SCRATCH MY PEOPLE. That's why the price is high and it's a BEAUTIFUL restaurant. I am a HUGE seafood fan, particularly catering to crab, their king crab is ALL YOU CAN EAT and I swear it's lowered from the heavens, they also offer snow crab, mussels, scallops, shrimp etc and it has an ENTIRE area, plus the best drawn butter I've ever tasted in my life! They offer a full serviced meat area where you can have steak, prime rib, filet mignon.....They have Italian food, southern favorites, China/Japanese area that include an array of buns and foods, they have A CHEESE BAR  where you can taste TONS of cheeses, they have AN ENTIRE BAR AREA DEDICATED TO DESERTS and serve everything from cheesecake to macaroons, creme brûlée......my favorite thing that I tried that was complete out of my comfort zone.....COLD HONEYDEW MELON SOUP. HOLY CRAP!!!! It was so delicious and had a hint of mint. Sweet lord and the sushi....don't even get me started because remember I LOVE SEAFOOD! Do yourself a favor, when you go to Vegas, go here, pretend the price doesn't exist and just go. You'll never want to go to another buffet in your life. Five stars. FIVE STARS! I don't ever give 5 stars unless a place deserves it and sweet Jesus, these chefs and this restaurant does! Also, I haven't been here in almost a year and I feel as equally strong about it. I think they deserve a good review!

I've been to so many different buffets in Vegas and other cities . Bacchanal is probably on my top 3 lists . The wait was long , but when seated I felt very comfortable and not been overwhelmed by others. Our waiter was very attentive and made us feel very special. Overall, if in Vegas , make sure try this buffet specially If you are in the mood of having some good crab legs!
Still my favorite buffet in Las Vegas. To me its amazing how Ceasers stays relevant and up-to-date as a place to explore and food to indulge in.

59.9$ per person,a regular price
I don't think it's deserved 
Oyster is big,but not so fresh,also with conch

I'm giving this buffet a 4 star for the brunch... 44.99 can't beat that.. the crab claws were great but cold.. they had a variety of breakfast and lunch item including menudo and pozole.. Raquel provided the best service, I'll definitely return in the future.

Co-worker: How did you spend your Thanksgiving Day?  

Me: I went to the Las Vegas and tried Bacchanal Buffet for the first time... 

If you are a table of 5 or less you pull a ticket from the kiosk machine and stand in line after they text you. If you have a table of 6 or more, you stand in another line and get seated after the next big party leaves. I had a table of 6, so we stood in the other line. The line wrapped along the wall and turned the corner. We stood in line for 3 hours! They had a guy come by take photos then try to sell it to you (no thanks). 

After we got close to getting in, they ask you to prepay and stand another 30 mins until our table was ready. Once we were seated the inside, the place was spacious, with dim lighting, wood accents, and over all a relaxed feeling. I was thinking it was going to feel packed, but it wasn't packed at all. Our server was nice, courteous, and funny.  He made some jokes and made the us feel at home.   

I had the best time trying out all the different types of food. Too much in fact that I didn't get to try everything :(  They had a Seafood Station one for hot and another one for cold, Carving Station, American Station, Asian Station, Cured meats and cheese station, Latin station, soups and salads, and Desserts. 

For the Seafood Station I had the hot crab legs. Crab legs are put in a big pot of boiling water. I had asked for some. When the lady put the legs on my plate, I said, "this is way too many" and she smiled back. They were sweet and perfect and hot!

From the Latin station I loved the horchata and the aguas freasca are amazing. They were perfect. 

I am such a sucker for sweets and that this is where I kind of lost it. I asked them to make a chocolate soufflé it was wonderful! It takes a bit of time for them to make it, so make sure to ask for it while you are trying out something else. 
 
This was one the best Thanksgiving. Hanging out with my family, not having to wash dishes or clean, and the best part was getting back to our hotel and passing out. 

Would I go back again?  Sure, why not......

FOODIE ALERT! YOU MUST EAT HERE BEFORE YOU DIE! 

Never have I fallen in love with such an amazing buffet! I am forever in Caesar Palaces debt for blessing such a wonderful place. 

Thursday lunch price is $30-35 and weekend Fri-Sun $45. unlimited mimosas for additional $10. Holiday weekends prices go up. 

During dinner at 3pm they start to serve LAMB! I must have had a whole lamb to myself because I am a huge rack of lamb fan. Amazing. Everything from oysters, king crab legs (served hot or cold), and desserts are to die for.
Awesome food, alot of selection! Really like the Asian food selection. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Check in gets you a free drink

We got there at 6 pm and put our name one of the kiosks and it gave us a time to come back, which was two hi later. When we came back at 8:92 pm, we wait in line for almost 2 hours to pay and another 20 minutes for our table. We ate around 10 pm and needless to say we were starving. They close at 11 pm so we did not get the two hours to enjoy our food. This was our first and last time eating here. The good was not great for $65 per person.

Me and my wife went on a Saturday night around 6:30pm, we waited in line for 2 hours.  The system that they implement isn't really working for all the multiple lines they have.  Also for $70 per person, the dinner buffet really isn't worth it.  The crab legs was too salty and tasted off.  The prime rib and brisket was too dry with no flavor or seasoning at all.  The lobster bisque is disgusting! This place is all HYPE, and don't believe in it.  Would rather save that $70 and try to go to the Sterling Brunch at Balleys.

Had to see why everyone recommends coming here.

There is a bit of a wait, maybe 1 to 2 hour wait depending on how many are in your party. Saw that the 1-2 person wait was longer than the 3 - 3 party.

Food selection is great - you have asian, sliced meat, seafood (snow crab) - its out cold, but you can get them nice and warm towards the back, asian, desserts (yes they have matcha green tea) and etc. Would definitely come again.

A buffet would not normally be my first choice, but if I had a bunch of people visiting and they wanted a buffet, I would take them to the Bellagio. It has a wide array of delicious food and it is dependable. I have tried almost every Buffet on the Strip and this is the best one for high quality choices. They have something everyone would truly enjoy.

Wait? did i go to the same place as everyone else? or maybe it was a bad day.
The reviews and fellow friends had gotten me very excited for the buffet and waiting in line I just could not wait! but unfortunately I was very very disappointed. 
Many of the meats were dry and unflavored. They did not even offer a steak! The most expensive thing they offer is probably the king crab at dinner time and they are served cold.
My tactic was to get a little bit of everything and go back to the things I loved and I did not find anything that I really wanted more of! I'm normally really easy to please and for the price I should of left happy and stuffed! But I left not even full but disgusted of eating anymore of the mediocre food. 
The most enjoyable thing about my meal was probably meeting the couple who sat next to me and talking about how much we all and other people we met in line were displeased with the food. 
Service was definitely lacking. I definitely didn't eat quickly but I'd have empty plates sitting on my table for a long time and getting a server for a refill was difficult because she barely came by. 
If there was anything that was good about bacchanal buffet was that there was much more variety compared to the Bellagio buffet which I went to the next day. But whats the point of variety if it all so bland and mediocre.
If I can suggest anything to you is to go to the Bellagio. It's cheaper and better tasting just less variety but hey, that's why you pay about $15 less.  Service was also much better. I'll be writing a review about how much I enjoyed the Bellagio more!

The only reason I'm giving this buffet 3 stars is because of the large variety of food options offered. However, the quality of those options in relation to the price left much to be desired. Even the desserts weren't very impressive. 

If you're looking for a quality meal you'd be better off going to an upscale restaurant even if it costs more. If you don't want to spend that much, chose a more moderately priced option and get the same quality meal for a whole lot less money.

The Food is Absolutely Amazing! The Service is Outstanding! So much food to pick from with all kinds of Different items to pick from. Everyone will Love this place! We will definitely be coming back again! The Atmosphere is Beautiful!

So happy we found this place on yelp. We watched videos, looked at pictures and just drooled over the food. When we came we was so amazed by the food selection. The seafood, the prime rib,the beef bone & everything was delicious. The wait wasn't that bad when we came but noticed as it got later the lines was getting long. This is definitely a place we will come back in the future. 

Located in Caesar's palace.
Best buffet...
My favorite buffet I have ever been to, it was worth the price ! Children are 1/2 off. Food was delicious, and desserts were AMAZING !!!
The oyster on half shell.crab claws good. Lobster bisque excellent. Chinese menu was good. Would diffidently return again

This is probably one of the top 3 buffets in the city. I used to go to the M Resort for the snow crab legs, but almost all the buffets here in Vegas are cutting the legs in half and they end up being crazy dry and they just aren't fun to eat anymore. After M started cutting them, I stopped going there. That's when I found the Caesars buffet. 

Now the lines can be rather long, with wait times from 30 mins to 3 or 4 hours. You basically get a ticket that tells you what time you can return and wait in the line. For military and veterans, I recommend you go to the players club, Caesars offers military veterans platinum level for the players card. This allows you to get into a really short line at the buffet and free parking. 

The food here is great, marrow bones, good poke, a street taco station, and very authentic Chinese food. Even the pizza is good enough that I got a second slice, and I never waste space on that stuff at buffets! The seafood is what stands out here. Dungeness crab legs, snow crab legs, stone crab claws. The oysters are hit or miss, as are the north Atlantic sea snails. The shrimp is always good, but I gotta say, the snow crab legs have gotten soooooo small, I don't know if it's because they are out of season now, or if they are just going with cheaper suppliers. About a year ago, they were so big and juicy I wouldn't get anything else. Now they are a bit disapointing.

Make sure you save room for dessert. This place has an amazing dessert station. Over 10 kinda of gelatos and sorbets. Chinese egg tarts to rival any dim sum place. If you are in the mood for a good buffet, this place will not let you down.

I'm obsessed with Vegas buffets, and I've tried quite a few...so I will say, this place is NOTHING SPECIAL!!! Even though wicked spoon has gone down in quality it's still better than this place. I read they spent $17 million dollars building this buffet; well the reality is, it looks big and expensive but you can can get better quality at the Cheesecake Factory.
First off- All the meats were dry!!! From the salmon to the lamb chops to brisket. The only things I found good was the pizza. 
Sadly the sweet potato tots were soggy because they were in paper cones and the moisture from their steam, sitting in this cone made them soggy. The crab legs were empty. The jalepeno sausage tasted like a regular hot dog and the carrot puree which held the pork belly was digusting, and the pork belly was of course, dry...
Who pays $55 dollars a person for dry meat?
Secondly, the dessert bar was a joke. I have a raging sweet tooth, so I literally brought 1 of everything to my table to sample and I didn't like anything, wait, that's a lie...I had a table spoon of whipped cream because it was the only good thing.
Service...I won't even go into, but let's just say I was there 2 hours and I never got a refill on my drink.
Never going back unless it's free

Great selection of different foods! It went on and on. But sand in my seaweed salad --not so good. Foods didn't seem to be to temps which always makes me nervous! Overall though, it's a great experience and should be checked out.

If you don't leave here seriously stuffed, you're doing something wrong. We arrived around 5:00 and got there at the perfect time because when we left, there was a huge wait to get in. There are SO many options, from seafood to bbq pulled pork and ribs, oriental, Italian, and wow the desserts are to die for. There are two rooms of food and we couldn't even try it all because we were full after barely getting through the first! 

Some favorites were the all you can eat crab & lobster claws, the carved meats (turkey, brisket, prime rib, etc.), the homemade crepes (the guy literally poured the batter in front of us, wow these were delicious) and the sushi bar area. The dessert area was massive and we tried everything from banana creme pie to upside down pineapple cake, all of which was mouthwatering & delicious. They also have a taco bar and the chefs make the tacos for you with allllll the toppings; we didn't try this but the line was long to get it and it looked great. 

Price for two for dinner was $145ish but if you're wondering if it was worth it, yes most definitely. Hands down one of the best, if not the best, buffets we have had. Can we go back tonight!?!

I had bought the 24-hour buffet pass and I read that this buffet was the place to come for deserts. 

Time was running out, we had already eaten at another buffet because I was craving their won ton soup, but I still wanted to go to this buffet because we hadn't tried it yet. 

This was the last one that we were able to go to before our 24-hours was up. When we arrived, there wasn't too many people in line. We were seated at a booth within five minutes. 

I'd say that this is a little on the fancier side of buffets...not crazy fancy, but a little nicer than some of them. 

When we got there, I was focused on the desserts...even though the other food looked amazing. I got some desserts, which I do have to agree with other Yelpers...if you have the 24HP, then come here for that! But compared to other buffets, this one is much smaller. I probably wouldn't recommend coming here just to go to a buffet. 

Aside from that, our expectations of good desserts were met from this buffet.

What a disappointment!
The positive Yelp reviews, long lines, and pricey entrance fee make me wonder what I'm missing?
The only items worth visiting a second time would be the King crab legs and some of their desserts.  
The crab legs were cut in half, which in my opinion ruins it completely, and served either frozen or boiled.  The boiled option made the crab meat so watered down and flavorless.  
 
The meat section just consisted of cheap brisket and sausages.  Although the guy cutting up the meat was hilarious.  The rest of the food doesn't even deserve to be mentioned.  Fortunately, the line and wait wasn't that long so we were able to get in and get out.  

This was probably the first time leaving a buffet without a food coma.
Ended up having to get something else after :(

This buffet is simply awesome. The food selection is so big that you don't know to where to start. The buffet has everything that you can think of. The deserts are so good in the end and they even have numerous different ice cream to choose from. The bad is that the line can be very long when you arrive unless you are fortunate to have vip status and bypass the line.

I've had my fill of buffets in Las Vegas and I always swear that I can only go to Bacchanal and be satisfied and feel like I got my money's worth. Bacchanal's seafood section is by far one of the best in the Las Vegas Strip. 

Raw oysters (though previously frozen-I believe) is much better than Wicked Spoon's half baked oysters (yuck), and their cold and hot crab legs are succulent, rightly salted, and abundant. They also had sea snails! My biggest regret was not bringing Thai seafood sauce. 

There is no one in line trying to take food away from you or eyeing that piece of crab leg or other seafood. 

Their muscles were also to die for. 

Overall I believe the seafood here at Bacchanal was enough to convince me to always come back to this buffet vs others. 

My drinks were always filled and my server was very prompt with getting our drink order. 

The meat section were also really good. I enjoyed the American Wagyu roast a lot, and they had Aus Jous on the side that you can put some on. 

Like almost all buffets I would recommend staying away from anything on the Asian side. They need to hire a classically trained Asian chef, because their walnut-shrimp was one of the most disgusting shrimp I've ever had. The shrimp was too thickly floured and it had only one flavor - salt. Next time i'll pass this section entirely, plus it's quite a far walk if you're seated near the front. 

If you're a platinum rewards member you can skip the long line and get in express VIP line to the left.

Buffet is overpriced and less quality food compared to some others. Diversity of food origins is great here but the options are slim in each category.  Try the wicked spoon for a lower price, better food and service.

If you are looking for a buffet with many choices of food, Bacchanal Buffet is the place to try.  So far this is the best buffet I have been to in Las Vegas.  Wherever they place you, there is always a station of food near you.  They have two types of crab (hot or cold), they will cook street tacos on a big stove, chicken and waffles, a bunch of asian food, all kinds of meats and seafood, different juices, a good selection of desserts (yes macarons are there), and many more items.  If I was to name all the foods available the list will go on and on.  The food selection is just insane.  The service is good as they clear plates away often from your table.  

When I see a pot full of food that I like I would grab a bunch.  If you are like me, it will get you full and then you can't try other foods.  What I like about this place is the presentation for some of the items.  They line up small dishes of the item and it's like a sample size.  The decor is nice and very pleasant.  

This buffet is really popular so obviously the line can get really long.  The price for dinner buffet is between $50-$60.  The method on obtaining a table is not painful.  First you check into the buffet using one of their machines by placing some information like name, party size, and phone number.  Why the phone number?  Because they will text you or call you when your table is ready.  So during that time when you are waiting for them to call or text you, you can gamble or have a drink to kill some time.  

Tip:  My friend and I played video poker/blackjack at the small bar near the entrance of Bacchanal Buffet and the bartender comped a drink since we played on the machine.  It's only 25 cents to play each hand of blackjack/poker.
There is many food selections. The food is vood for a buffet. Just a little pricey, especially for families.

Was out in Vegas on business, and I've been to a few buffets out there, actually went to Bellagio's this time out.  Let me tell you, Bellagio's buffet was good, but this is on another level.

Went for lunch, during the week, was about $45 or so, don't remember exactly, but it was worth every penny.  They have pretty much everything you can imagine, setup in stations.  Do yourself a favor, bring your appetite and scout it out before diving in to make sure you are able to try everything you want to, otherwise you will get full way too quickly.

This was the best buffet, I've ever seen in Vegas, maybe anywhere, everything was on point, tasty, and I'd definitely go back.  Easily worth the price tag.

I will never return back due to the fact that me and my family of 12 were treated very wrong due to our race.
Fernanda was the lady that took our payment, she was very rude and automatically thought we were paying with a credit card. I told her that it was not going to be credit she smirked and said cash then whispered and laughed with her coworker.
Loved the food. But I thought this place opened at 7:30 (YouTube). If a place opens at 8:00, they've already lost half their clientele to other restaurants.

Manager Samantha Bennett is amazing.  She went out of her way to welcome my Dad and I.  My father is a local and we dont get to the strip too often.  We bought the groupon for 2 for brunch on Sunday.  It was amazing and Samantha made sure we got King Crab.  Please recognize her management.  She is the reason we will be back!
expensive yes but it will blow your mind with the selection of food,service,and taste

Unfortunately our experience at the buffet was ruined at the end... living  many years in vegas we finally decided to have a birthday dinner at the caesar's buffet. As expected the wait was rather long (1hr since we were a large party of 5) which was okay. When we finally got in we ate our dinner and everything was delicious. Towards the end were about to get our desserts and we saw the hostess and our server talking right next to our table, then the server came to our table grabbed our receipt, looked at it and set it back down. As curiosity i took a glance at it as well just to see that being a large group we have a 2 hr limit. I got upset because clearly in the receipt it shows what time we paid not the time we got seated.  keep in mind we were waiting an hour in line to be seated. At that point we didn't get more refills or our plates picked up... we got the hint and decided to leave. We had a bad taste in our mouths and wanted to talk to the manager. When we spoke with the manager he stated that in our receipt we should have been stamped what time we were actually going in because starting then we have our 2 hrs. His only solution was that he was going to talk to the server as she should not being doing that. I highly doubt he did. but working in the food/beverage dept in one of the casinos as well lets just say there are things that shouldn't be done in front of the client. We know that having customers is very important and our objective is that the customer has an exceptional experience for the obvious goal for them to come hack. In this case.. we won't be going back.

If you are in Vegas and you want to do at least one buffet then make sure it's at the Bacchanal at Ceasar's! 

This place is amazing! Service is excellent and the food is delicious!  My husband and I came here at 10:30am on a Sunday for brunch and we were seated within 5 mins! I opted for the unlimited mimosas for an extra $7 and boy did my waiter keep it flowing!  For the two of us it totaled $115 not including tip. Expensive? Yes but worth it? Hell ya!  


They had plenty of choices, when we first arrived they had their breakfast items out in full blast, egg benedicts, red velvet pancakes, different types of meats were just a few of the items they had, as the hour went on I believe by 11:30am they started to put out the lunch items and I had to find a way to make room for that . 

The dessert choices are even more amazing! Mini molten cakes, fudge, creme bruelle (sp?) were what I tried and they had different types of gelato a like s'mores and strawberry balsamic . 


I was going to do a video of the buffet but my stomach said no feed me lol!
Came for breakfast, stayed for lunch. The quality of the dishes were better this time around. Disappointed that they took away the mochi though. :(

THE BIGGEST AND BEST SHRIMP EVER! 

Wow, what an experience this was! I've heard from just about anyone and everyone that this is the place to go and try. I did a Groupon for 120.00 and we were set.

The WAIT: The VIP passes are pretty useless, because you're going to wait regardless. We had two passes, and maybe just skipped 3 people BUT went into another line where you're waited to be seated, and that takes literally forever. But, it is what it is. 

FOOD/DINNER: The food is really good, but i guess i was a LITTLE disappointed because i was expecting a bigger bang for our buck. Yes, there are so many choices and I guess it's more so the amount VS what they're serving.

HOWEVER, they had this jalapeño shrimp that I would 100% come back for. After that dish, i was honestly sold. 120.00 for the rest? Totally not worth it. The seafood was the most disappointing. I was expecting cut crab, thick prime rib, juicy slices of steak with bomb king crab, and for it to be great and fresh......... but that dream quickly died and fast LOL. 
They only had snow crab that you can literally get from most buffets here for a lot cheaper. The prime rib was decent, and the tri tip was amazing. But it missed that wow factor that I was really hoping to get while I was here. They did have street tacos, but AGAIN no huge wow factor. I can get street tacos in East Los Angeles for 5.00. 

DESSERT: THE MACAROONS are delicious! But again, dessert fell  VERY short. The cupcakes were VERY dry and crumbly so we didn't eat it.Everything tasted very Costco like, but older. Which I love Costco, don't get me wrong, that is my store! but who the hell wants to pay 120.00 for old Costco desserts? I'm almost certain that's where the macaroons are from. I did try and nibble on just about every dessert there was, and it could've all been way WAY better. The worst was the donuts. I'd forsure skip the donuts and cakes when coming here.

Service: Great service, the Mexican ladies really move their ass nonstop. I know there is a two hour limit, so they try to get you going as quickly as possible. We only stood for an hour, and didn't feel satisfied one bit. I had a much better dinner at different places for WAY cheaper. 

PRICE: 120.00 w/2 alcohol drinks included. Was it worth it? No. I wouldn't pay full price, or go out of my way to come back again. The only thing worth coming for was the chubby shrimp.

It's a good pain.  Really, it is.

Where to start on this monstrous buffet?  I ate so much food the pain lasted hours (my fault... gluttony is part of the Vegas experience, right?).  

Let's make this simple.

The great:
- the sausage selection (brats to spicy sausage)
- the prime rib
- the sesame balls
- the custard buns
- the creamed corn
- the KC BBQ sauce
- the mint fudge (soooo good)
- the macaroons (start with these)
- the chocolate covered strawberries
- the overall selection (if you can't find something you like, you don't like food)

The good:
- the macaroni and cheese
- the truffle gnocchi
- the sushi
- the sweet potatoes
- the crab legs
- the lasagna
- the bread pudding
- the creme brûlée
- the banana pudding

The Meh:
- the braised beef
- the sea bass
- the green beans
- the cookies
- the carrot cake
- the key lime pie
- the salted caramel cupcake
- the service.   (Nice but slow)

The bad:
- the Taro cake (yuck!)
- the pumpkin cheesecake pop
- the fact that I discovered the crepe station AFTER I was slipping into a food coma.   Curse you stomach limitations!! *shaking fist in the air*

Yes... I really did eat all of this.   I hit the wall and suffered, but the pain (and the price of the buffet was worth it).  When I come back (and I will on the next trip) I will tackle more of the Asian and Italian selections.

I can see why this Buffett won awards over the Bellagio Buffet.  It raised the bar on buffet quality and selection.

They say this is the best buffet right now in Vegas. We tried it for breakfast while staying at Ceasars. Everything was super clean and so many food stations. Don't order oj just get the fresh version from the buffet. Their salsas and attention to details was appreciated. Prime rib was yummmm. They have both breakfast & lunch items at breakfast time.  We love the Wicked Spoon Buffet at Cosmo  but this is a great option!  Diamond whales get a special sign on their table but everyone gets great service.

Their food selection is extensive, well prepared and tasty. As such, it is understandable that their price is not cheap. The only possible downside of coming here is if you have a weak will power, you will probably have a near-death experience trying to eat as much as you can.
This buffet is amazing! I must admit it's expensive at $60 per person. The food here is sooo good. If your in Las Vegas this is a must!!! Initially there is a long waiting

Exceptional food delicious and great for families of small or large groups.

There brunch and bottomless mimosas is awesome.
Well worth every dollar here .

Good food, and service. Good verity of food. Only downside was the price-$54 per person for adults for dinner time. Have all you can crab legs on the buffet ( only place on the strip where you can get them- June 2019). Had many different cuisines on the bar.

I would have to say that Bacchanal is the best buffet that I have experienced in Las Vegas. The buffet is located in the Cesars Palace Hotel on the first floor. Directions to it is pretty straight forward and not hidden which is great. 

The food itself is great. They offer warm and cold grab legs if that tickles your fancy, most places only offer cold and will heat it up if you request it. The variety of food that they carry is a lot. They have multiple selections of seafood, multiple selection of meat which includes Wagyu beef and brisket. The brisket was on point and was good. The prime rib was almost as good as Lawrys. They also have Italian, Japanese Sushi, and Chinese food.

The Sushi was okay, I personally wouldn't get it again. The duck was really flavorful and the skin was crispy. This is better than most Asian bbq places. 

The service here is excellent. They come check up on you often and clear your plates really quick. 

The only downfall is that there is a really long wait and it's one of the most expensive buffets. There is a wait to pay and then there is a wait to get a table. It took me over an hour on a Wednesday night which I think is pretty crazy. You're talking 60 dollars plus for this buffet, but you get what you pay for in this case. 

I highly recommend coming to this buffet over all of the other ones.

Wow, this is the buffet of all buffets!
I must admit that I'm not really a fan of buffets (even though I've been to many, which were all in casinos) but I was in Ceasar's and a friend insisted we go. 
We arrived for brunch and the price for 5 of us was a bit over $220ish. Yikes, right! But once I got in and saw what they had to offer I totally get it.
The options were top notch as well as the presentation. There were truly so many options that what I listed is merely a smidge of their offerings so I'll list the fancier selects that I remember...
Lobster bisque, shrimp & grits, chicken & waffles, eggs benedict crepes, truffle pizza, salmon deviled eggs, made to order street-style tacos, made to order dessert crepes, avocado toast, acai bowls. Again, this is just what I remember and is far from what they have to offer on top of the usual suspects you see at buffets.
So it goes without saying that THIS buffet is worth trying.

Horrible horrible food, no king crab, only small tiny snob crab. The prime rib was over cooked. Nothing worth 60 bucks. Lots of cheap Chinese and Mexican food we could've had in Golden Corral or hometown buffet that's 20 bucks. King crab cost extra!  That's just crazy when belligio and Wynn both buffets have king crab, never going back!

Didn't realize this was supposedly one of the better buffets in Vegas until I got back to Houston. I'm kind of said I didn't get to fully experience this buffet because we finally got into the buffet with a little less than 45 minutes to eat before we had to leave to catch our flight. If I had known this buffet was so popular, we would've definitely came out earlier. We got there around 2, didn't get seated til 330ish and then got to eat for about 30-45 minutes before our flight at 5pm. The buffet had crab legs that were pretty juicy. My favorite item before walking out was the turtle cheesecake dessert to eat on the road. My mistake for not grabbing more. Lunch and dinner prices do vary depending on what days you're there. 

I would definitely return just to fully experience the whole buffet without being rushed next time.

Heard this was the #1 buffet in vegas  so we checked it out. On a monday bout 4 pm.   First  its about 55 dollars a person,   and it was packed but only about a 20 min wait.  The place is huge, and there is so much food,  Its almost too much.   But everything was great, great carving stations, and fresh seafood.  And the dessert section is amazing,  if u go remember they charge 12 bucks   to park for 4 hrs in the parking garage.  But several casinos are charging for parking now.   This place has a top noch buffet.  But its pricy and busy.

To be honest, I thought this place was overrated. I tried one of each dish and didn't find one particular thing that really shocked me. Don't get me wrong, there's a wide array of dishes. There's tacos, seafood, sushi, Chinese. You name it, and it's probably there. 

I paid during brunch and stayed until dinner. I was in a party of two and the wait for food was about 20 minutes. I paid around $60 for my whole meal. The dining area is extremely large. It is kind of a pain if you're seated towards the back and if the foods in the front. There are no duplicate dishes so if you want something you'll have to know where it is. 

For me, this was just a one time thing. I don't think I'd ever pay this much for a buffet ever again.

Yummy!! Omg all the food is good and our server Michael is wonderful :).   They had seafood, brisket that was slow cooked, pork, duck, pork, prime rib, Japanese food, sushi, Italian food, etc...plus some amazing desserts that you could not go wrong with and moshi, yum yum yum ;) enjoy for the great price some of the most delicious food.  Be prepared to wait in line a bit.  It was a Saturday night and we waited about 45 min to 1 hour in line but we got some wine at the bar out side to enjoy while we waited and that made the wait go smoothly LOL.

Hands down the best buffet food I've ever had.  Started off with about 15 jumbo cocktail shrimp that where fresher than anything I've had recently.  The carving stations where heavenly they had pork belly which is something I've never had before.  Fresh squeezed juices including guava hibiscus.  Service was super Attentive the whole time.  It really is hard to decide what to have next.  Lastly there was the gelato sorbet bar which was truly heavenly.   I feel it lived up to the hype.  If there is a better buffet in Vegas I'd love to know.

SUCH BEAUTIFUL DECOR! 

Honestly for a buffet... I would have to say this place makes you feel like you are dining in a nice modern restaraunt. I would have to say this is one of the BEST buffets in Vegas... although it may be pricey... & the wait during the weekend dinner time is RIDICULOUS... there is at least a kiosk where you sign in & they text you when you are close to the front of the line. 

Staff is really friendly & help you w/ everything that you may need & keep your drinks constantly full! 

One AWESOME thing about this place was the OYSTERS!!! But I must say over time... the QUALITY of the oyster went down... they used to shuck them fresh but now you could tell they are being schucked & held in the refrigerator until they place them out... =\ SUPER DISAPPOINTING but also noticed this downgrade of quality started to occur when they brought out STONE CRABS. I would much prefer fresh oysters over COLD stone crabs especially when they already offer king crab legs cold & HOT which I LOVE HOT LEGS!! 

I also love the FRESH tacos they make to order w/ refreshing AGUA FRESCAS that they offer. They also have NOODLE SOUPS like pho & udon which is awesome to have refreshing hot broth to wash all the food down. 

DESSERTS are AWESOME here as I LOVE the flan & the chocolate covered strawberries plus the mochi ice creams & crepe! 

DINNER on a weekend is about $60 & if you wanna pass the line then you could pay $20 / person which is not worth it IMHO... the prices are cheaper during the weekday & if you time it right, you could pay lunch price & roll into dinner items =] 

One other awesome thing is that they give you a little wet towelette that smells like citrus to wipe your hands after all the crab legs you eat.

Worst service never ever had with any kind of buffet @ Vegas .... once again worst worst service .. u have to wait to get a ticket and wait to pay and wait for table and more wait for food .. somehow this rate 4 star but the service is just BAD . Got to be other buffet better then this

I use To eat here weekly as I worked In a different area of CP. My husband brought me as a treat today and wow it's changed for the worse.
Service as always is amazing, but the food is not. 9:30 am so no excuse for the food being out too long. The cut up fruit is dried out and flavorless. The crepes taste like they've added some sort of a gum to it so it actually is stretchy and gummy to chew. The toppings are all canned generic gross tasting. Pastries bland. The biscuits and gravy was amazing however, but when I went Back the biscuits were out. 
I timed It standing there 15 min. Literally. I asked 3 people if there were more coming. One On French toast duty looked at me and shook his head. The next one pointed to another guy. The other guy looked up and ignored. I stayed Waiting along with 3 other people, and no acknowledgement or biscuits 
Again service was amazing 
Cost would be worth it if the food didn't suck.
Worst buffet I've been to living here 11 years

All good things must come to an end...even the Bacchanal Buffet.

They have decreased the variety of options greatly. Only one type of Jasmine tea now, less options for the congee, less mochi, etc.

Service is lacking. I'm lucky if I can get a refill or my table cleared. 

Gotta still give three stars though for 1) the sheer amount of dishes, 2) atmosphere, and 3) THE TACOS! Yes, tacos!

Literally drove to Las Vegas from LA with a few friends for food. We came here on a Saturday night, and holy crap there was a long long line. We went here for dinner, and ended up signing in the line through their kiosk. It let's you reserve a spot in line essentially, and tells you when to come back to line up to pay. The wait was roughly 2 hours. I knew this place would be pretty expensive (around 65-70ish dollars), but I've always wanted to try this place. They have such a variety of food from seafood to American, Japanese, Italian, etc. It's nice to see a variety of cultural food to try. The number one food item they had for me was the cooked beef bone marrow, Omg soo good. The dessert section was the highlight for me, since I have a huuuuge sweet tooth. They have macaroons  small cakes, Crepes, gillato, chocolate, creme Brule, etc.. I literally tried everything. Overall it was a one time experience for me, and I would be bankrupt if I came here regularly.

Decided to come here for my last day in Vegas even I said I will not come back again... I decided to try their breakfast or brunch after check out. I definitely will come back again. We came around 10ish, no waiting... we are here for breakfast and they starting to serve lunch. They have beef, crawfish, and mussels for breakfast. A lot of selections which some of the food served in dinner as well.

Been a long 5 years since we came here. The long lines in the past scared us all away.

We came just when breakfast was ending and brunch being served. Lots and lots of food selections that mostly tasted very delicious. 

We worked our way to almost every section and enjoyed it all. Service was a bit slow on clearing plates and refilling drinks.

One item they no longer prepare is the seafood paella. And I loved paella with a passion. :-)

For sure will be back when we have a big appetite.

I came here on 9/23/18, and purchased a Groupon for the brunch buffet and thought I would give it another try. Since my last visit it has improved a little. The quility of food was better than last time, but the price is still way too high even with a Groupon for what is offered. For the price you pay they should offer caviar and escargot ( fish eggs / snail delicacy) for this price. Or offer a 24 hour entry like all the other Ceasars Entertainment group Buffets without paying extra in upgrades. With a one time entry at this price, its a total rip off. About the staff, the service is great. Just the price was most of the problem. Would return if the price goes down.

With 1,000 items of food, who would not love this place!  We have diamond card so the wait wasn't long (just two mins ^_^). But if you don't have the card, don't worry, it's worth waiting! :)) For the price vs quality of food and service, it was really worth it! Besides the variety of food, there are lots of drinks to choose from. If you're in Vegas, you should come try!

Not only the biggest variety of choices, but the food had good quality. The crab legs weren't the best I've tasted (nothing beats home boiled) so with that I was a little disappointed. The Asian section of orange chicken was tasty. I went for brunch, maybe dinner is a better choice. The service was prompt and the facility was well kept. I still think it is over priced, but...it's the strip. Dessert also had so many choices from pistachio, chocolate, black bean, sesame, strawberry, mint and more gelato flavors that are all a hit. Banana foster and ganache were also a great addition to the palate. I would go here again and it would be my top buffet choice at this time.

WOW. The wait was definitely worth it. We waited around an hour to be seated and I will admit there were times I wanted to leave to find a quick bite to eat. (I was so hungry)On our way to our table we got a quick look at everything they served and I already was planning where I would fill up my plate first. I am so glad we decided to wait to eat here! A day later and I already want to go back and eat there again.

The crab legs are hidden treasures. Find them next to the man behind 4-5 what looks to be steel pots. He'll also comment on how beautiful your fiancée is while you stand at the corner battling an Asian grandma on who gets to use the spoon first to dig into the last of the Pad Thai. 

The line for the wait is grueling so play Mario Kart or Wood block till you get permanent "Text Neck"

Food was good. Got one scoop or piece of each thing and still got full half way through each category of cultural foods. 

$120 for two************

Good luck.

People need to be realistic.  This is a buffet that serves 1000's at a time.  If they're expecting the beef to taste like the beef at Capital Grille or the fish to taste like the fish @ Michael Mina, than they're unrealistic idiots.

That said, this is the most extraordinary, creative, and quite simply overwhelming buffet Las Vegas has ever built.  The choices are immense.  For example, the mex station has homemade tortilla chips......with 15 salsas to choose from. 10 types of cookies.  15 gelato flavors.  8 italian premium cold cuts.  etc etc. 

The airy design and space is great as is the furniture.  If you want to know what a buffet restaurant can look like when $17 million is spent, this is it.

The prices are totally reasonable.  Whatever you pay, the quality is above average, and you will be full for 12 hours and soft drink included.  People give up $100 bills left and right playing roulette, than bitch about paying $25 for lunch.

Hats off to Gary Selesner for making this happen on such a grand scope.
Absolutely 5 stars for you guys its perfect for my family they are all so happy the food is not too pricey perfect for my family bonding.

I've heard that this is the #1 buffet at Vegas right now. Well I'm not surprised! It's pricey but fresh. There's a large variety which you can pick and choose from. I enjoyed the pho and sushi there. The seafood was great too! I especially enjoyed the crawfish because it was spicy ! 

The service was a little slow. Waitresses seemed a bit grumpy. Wait is also long, but surprisingly we only waited 40 min for lunch. Make sure your party is all there or else they won't let you in....

Very classy low key buffet with excellent selections of food from carving station, omelets made to order, desserts, seafood, noodles including pho, congee and some dim sum.  

There are fresh pressed fruit juices like watermelon, kale smoothies, gelato and a multitude of condiments for your dining pleasure.

As soon as hubs and my daughter left to begin the buffet, I started hurrying to take out party hats, birthday blowers and candles.  Our server was my cahoots buddy and went to tell the dessert staff so they made the cutest plate of desserts so I could insert her birthday candles.  It was so fun.

Now on to the happiest place on earth... just short of 4 hour drive at least from Yelp directions from Caesar'sPalace.  Speaking about Yelp you can get free champagne, beer or wine with your Yelp check in.  Win win situation  

I like it here, dining among pretty glass partitions, no loud talking or kids running around so adults can dine like adults in a relaxed venue for your 2 hour suggested time allotment.  Not always an option to dine without kiddies but if you can, this is a nice place to come.

Just a amazing experience!!

All the food is wonderful and the the service is amazing!

No wait on a Sunday! Boom 
Love it!

Been to the Bacchanal for lunch and dinner. Probably has the largest selection of items from various ethnic regions of any buffet. Overall food quality was good, but only a few items really stood out. Highly recommend the tempura green beans, brisket, lamb, bone marrow, made to order tacos, and crab. Something to note for dinner is that crab will be served in (2) separate areas, the freshly steamed crab will be back near the Italian cuisine area. Additionally, despite the beautiful aesthetics, my friend and I weren't too impressed with the desserts as a lot of the options were too sweet for our liking.

Best buffet in vegas! Do your research though. I have seen a lot of people  head over to the cold crab legs when there is a place where you can get hot steamed crab legs!! They also have a place where it's already cracked and open for you. Clearly, this is the buffet for you if you like crabs. But honestly, their meat, honey sweet potato tots, dessert options (thai tea boba float what?!?) were all amazing. Don't go anywhere else. This is where it's at!!

Food: 3.5/5
Service: 3.5/5
Ambiance: 3.5/5
Overall: A definitely high end buffet with some decent food but beware, it's costly and a long wait! I think one should try it once but I'm not sure i would wait for it again.

The extended review...

Buffet: There were a lot of good things to choose from and I think most people would go for the crab which is pre cracked.  The meat options were decent with prime rib amongst other roasted meats.  

The best part was the dessert bar I'd say.  I think this made my day and of course my phone didn't take a picture of my plate.  Boo!

Service: Standard buffet service with bussing.  Servers were friendly and nice.

Ambiance: Good seating but again be prepared to wait.  You have to get a ticket for a future time just to stand in line for another 30-60 minutes to get seated.  YES YOU HAVE TO STAND IN LINE!

I never thought much of buffets but this one had amazing food and beautiful presentation. Slightly pricey, about $50 for lunch but that's average for a good buffet in Vegas. Great service too. I highly recommend if your looking for a great meal.

Tried this place out on my trip to Vegas last week and I wasn't disappointed at all. We had VIP so we  only had to wait like 10 min to be seated once we where seated we ordered our drinks and after they arrived we all Took off like horses at the race track to see what food there was I didn't know where to start there was so much to chose from Asian food, Mexican food, American food and sea food.
