The thing I did like the most out of the the stuff I ate was the Brisket, the grits with shrimp, jambalaya and the tacos which where cook right there on the spot. The deserts where so good but I was so full from all the food I ate that I just took few bites out of the different desserts I got. Look at pictures and see all the desserts. Also there's a menu posted on front of what they're serving. I recommend this place to anyone visiting Vegas and I will be here on my next trip.
Awesome food, awesome service. We were waited on by Esmeralda Juarez and she was fantastic, fast, friendly and helpful. We will be back!

The Bacchanal Buffet is the best buffet on the strip. It has the widest range of food, the best tasting and a great layout. One of the first things I would like to praise them on is having hot crab. A lot of buffets only sever cold crab and it's fine and all but to me hot crab taste better. I have been to close to all buffets on the strip and the the Bacchanal has the best quality around. I can't say everything was perfect but about 95% of the food there was great or better. The line can be long but I feel it's worth the wait. Whenever I'm in Vegas this will be my go to buffet.

Do I need to really put anything down here? You cannot find a better buffet. You get what you pay for in this place. If I could design a portion of heaven, Bacchanal would be there in all its perfection. 
Go in with a game plan and strategy. And please, for the love of all that is holy, don't act like a noobe.  The idea is to take small portions one or two bites at the most when trying something new. There are so many wonderful choices, you must do your best to experience it all.

This is the best and seems like the largest buffet in Vegas. I love Caesar's Palace already and love that this buffet is located here. This is great after a long day of gambling and shopping. 

This is pretty pricey per person but for the HUGE variety of food, I think it's worth it. The buffet line seems like it goes on forever and I am sure everyone will find something here.

I don't have any favorites but found all the dishes flavorful and tasty. I enjoyed a variety of desserts as well (and I'm not a dessert person)!

I recommend coming at odd hours like 4-5pm and getting a head start before the crowds. Otherwise you can be waiting awhile, especially if you have a larger group.
Great selection... price is worth it totally. No need to stand in line I love their pager system. Top shelf spirits wine sake.... definitely a one stop shop for a high end outing

Adrian Acosta 
Excellent buffet
Amazing prepared meals to order. Will be back again!
A lot of Options. Great servers. Long wait some times. Peach tea is my favorite. Texas

5 hours wait, average food, expensive price, huge disappointment.
It's a tourist trap, stay away!!!

VERY VERY DELICIOUS BUFFET! Bacchanal has turned the term "Vegas buffet" into a whole new level! 

I'm not sure what else is there to say besides what has already been said in the reviews below me. 

PRICES: On weekday (we went on a Monday, I believe) for two people came out to be $69 and tax is already added with that price.

I paced myself. I had to get my moneys worth. But I especially saved room for dessert. Man...the selections there are endless. It felt like I was at a candy store or something. And the gelato....they had some "not your everyday flavoring" like thai tea. Yum!!!! 

Not only was the food fresh but the presentation was something new and different. They tried (and succeeded) to make things fancy like having fresh juice in a cute glass jar. Their dim sum came in these cute little dim sum holders (see pics attached.) Aah...I'm a sucker for stuff like this. 

So come and give Bacchanal a try. They won't disappoint you.

I've only been to a few of the buffets on the Strip, and I have to say Bacchanal Buffet has some incredible variety. After doing some gambling at Caesar's, we came in a large group for a later dinner. We saw a long line to enter the restaurant, but for some reason, since we had a large group, we were whisked into the restaurant immediately. Don't know what we did, but I'll take it.

The buffet spread is pretty darn long, ranging from seafood, to Mexican, to Italian, to Asian, to other new American specialties, so just remember to breathe and stuff your face silly. Tip: Go for the meats and seafood, don't fill up too much on carbs (except for dessert), and go for stuff you wouldn't typically get the chance to eat as often. I really enjoyed the gnocchi, the crab legs (duh), as well as the smoked ribs. Not too shabby. Desserts were plentiful too, and it was hard to choose, so we just got a little bit of everything.

Service was very quick in getting drink refills and such. We didn't get alcohol, so getting soft drink refills was much faster. Price came out to about $75 a person, which included gratuity and tax. Definitely more expensive, but again, we did eat ourselves silly.

If you're going up for straight up quantity and variety, then Bacchanal is a great choice. Would included it in my top tier of Bellagio buffet brunch, as well as Wicked Spoon in the Cosmopolitan.

Bacchanal you have my heart. 

Our party of 8 was so fortunate to be seated right next to the seafood section. I'm personally a fan of crab claws over legs and man were the crab claws to die. So fresh, soft, and lightly sweet tasting. AH-mazing. I'm salivating just thinking about them. Obviously, I went back for several plates of claws before I even started to explore the rest of the buffet.

The layout of the buffet was clearly presented, however it can get a little congested in various rooms at times (aka the Asian section).

They have an Asian noodle bar, which is on point. You have a selection of pho, udon, ramen, and Malaysian laksa, which I thought was pretty cool. I opted for the udon and it had great flavor! The Chinese dim sum however was lack luster. Pretty on the outside, no flavor on the inside.

My absolute favorite was the red velvet brownie. So unique, I've never had a red velvet brownie before! Chewy and the perfect amount of sweetness. Their dessert presentation is so beautiful.

Bacchanal is a must try.
This place is incredible! So many varieties of seafood and different cultures represented. Both my husband and my favorite part was our incredibly sweet, kind and helpful server, Su.

Completely overrated. Wicked spoon is better for sure. ONE GUY is preparing, refilling, steaming and serving the crab legs. The line was insanity. For 70$ a person, you shouldn't be waiting in a line for crab legs. The desserts were extremely underwhelming. When we got to the front of the line, paid, went to another line to be seated, the hostess takes our receipts. Then seats us, comes back later to tell us she couldn't find our receipts?!?!?! My husbands like, you took it?! Then she came back a while later and said we still didn't find it but the manager said it's ok?! Seriously, come up with a better system of taking everyone's receipts in a pile isn't working. I would never recommend this buffet to anyone. Overpriced, too hard to get crab legs and staff obviously has some issues...
Everything time I go to Vegas, I never miss the chance at this buffet! Love love love!  Best of the best in Vegas!
Best buffet in Vegas! Been to many buffets in Vegas and I go specifically for the seafood. It was all fresh and also had beautiful deserts that looked too pretty to eat
Awesome buffet , phenomenal food and quality is high like there seafood and lots of menu
Expensive, almost $60 a person with tax.  All food barely warm.  It might make more sense for a lunch or dinner.  This buffet has everything.

John-Doe P.  You said exactly right (they are loosing steam)
"Its gone down a bit. 

Won't come back.

Not recommended. Used to be stellar... now not so much.

Lost its swing"


Ceasars can do better for the price you pay.

Amazing, delicious, unreal, incredible, fantastic and on and on and on with the positive adjectives. 
Worth every penny. We paid the extra $25 to beat the line as we were pressed for time and it was a 90 minute wait around 8pm on a Thursday. $25 extra on top of $51.99 per person is pretty damn ridiculous and I wouldn't pay the extra again. I'll just plan better next time around. We also added $22 all you can drink champagne/wine/beer which was totally worth it. Tue wait staff were superb at keeping us topped all the time. 
I ate my face off of crab, shrimp, prime rib, mashed and scalloped potatoes, pho soup, almond green beans, oysters, mac n cheese, sushi, wedge salad, and too many desserts for me to care to admit. It was all super tasty and fresh and not reminiscent of a nasty old trough buffet in the least. 
I'll for certain return any time I'm in Vegas. 
Top tip* hot crab legs in the Italian section. Soooo much better than the cold.

First Off there are lot of Fake Pictures and Videos of Bacchanal Buffet seafood.  It should be called SEE food.  It does not exist any more or is not part of the buffet.

PLEASE DO NOT BELIEVE OLD YOUTUBE VIDEOS AND REVIEWS AS WELL AS PHOTOS.

I ponied up $75 per person for 4 persons  to have a King Crab/Lobster buffet with my family.  All they had was Alaskan snow crab boiled in water Yuks, even my wife who can put up with tasteless food and hates to waste  could not stomach and threw it away.

Rest of the food was OK but not worth $75 per person as we do not eat meat I felt I lost MOSTOF my money, the lobster bisque was tasty but i think $ 75 is too much for lobster bisque and dessert was good.
Great experience! Chef Jose is very nice, I am vegan and he made sure that I had plenty of options to eat. I definitely recommend this buffet.

Best buffet I've ever had.. esp in Vegas.  Worth the $$ go HUNGRY.  All you can drink is only $15 so worth it to get the Cabernet.. it's strong!  All kinds of fish.. lobster/stone crab/king crab and hot queen crab legs.  Mexican station they make tacos to order.. italian station.. and the meat station was the best.  Wagyu beef, beef brisket, ribs, prime rib.. all amazing.  Dessert station was something to see.  Was there 2 hours-- highly recommend and great service also.. gorgeous view of the pool too.

We've been going to the Baccanal Buffet every year on our anniversary since we moved to Las Vegas five years ago.  The first year it was knock-your-socks-off good with lots a variety and very high quality.  We've been back since with mixed results.  Sometimes we've sworn off it and then decided to give it another try.  This is the last swear off, I swear!  Some of the food was extremely good, especially the prime rib, and some, specifically the Asian section, was middling.  Based on food this time, it's not exactly stricken from the list, but put in the "maybe" category for future luxury buffet dining.  The real problem was this:  I pointed out to the dessert bar chef that what they had signed as "Fresh whipped cream" was really Cool Whip.  I think most people could make this distinction.  He suggested that I contact the floor manager and ask for a courtesy card so I could make this complaint in writing.  He said that really made a difference.  I contacted the floor manager, and rather than give me a card to fill out, she said she would correct the problem and took the sign down immediately.  I went back a few minutes later and she had put the same sign back up.  I asked her a second time if I could have a courtesy card, and she said the chef said it was real whipped cream, and that I could speak to the chef, because, "They're not allowed to lie," and that I should taste it again; i.e., she would not give me a courtesy card to make a complaint, and she decided to spin a whopper to deflect me from the whole enterprise.  Not feeling like going through some endless folderol of "Wait, I'll get him for you," or, "She'll be right back,"  I decided to beat a retreat and post this review, where I'm sure at least some actual people, not Caesars Palace bureaucrats, will see it.  If you want to spend $40 to $55 a person for food that has become, at best, hit or miss, with ingredients that are anybody's guess, then I recommend Baccanal Buffet.  If not, try somewhere else.  The Wynn buffet has been particularly good lately, and remodeled Treasure Island has way better food for way less money.

When this buffet reopened under its current iteration, it was a consistent 5 stars. Time has not been kind. There are high points still remaining, but some decreases in quality of preparation and in taste. At our most recent visit, there were no oysters on the half shell and the peel and eat shrimp were bland. The lamb chop was tough. Some of the Chinese items were very good and the sushi surpassed my expectations for a buffet.

Beautiful space and a well done buffet! The nature of a buffet is that not everything can be done perfectly, with that said Bacchanal does many of their dishes very well. It's a great chance to try some new things as well as have some familiar favorites. The meat and Italian section were my favorites, and the sushi was surprisingly good. The dessert section was awesome and most things we tried were good! Best thing we had was somewhat random, but the Nashville hot chicken- so good!

Was confused about tipping at the start of our meal before we had experienced our service, but maybe that's the norm at buffets. We didn't tip on our card (tipped with cash at the end of our meal) and I feel that because of that our service was lackluster (had to flag down our waiter when we wanted anything). otherwise the experience was great!

Went around 3:30 and didn't have to wait and wasn't too crowded! Also enjoyed the free champagne by checking in on yelp!
disappointing, I expected better. Paid at 9:11 and got a table at 9:45. Food was cold and really didn't worth price or wait!!! The Crepes was uncooked!!

Felt like we were at Sizzlers!! Food was mediocre. Seafood department was missing oysters and stone crab claws. Instead they had rubbery snails and some cold mushy river prawns. Some of the flat breads were out too long and super hard. 

The place has definitely gone downhill over the past few years. The restaurant and waiter service isn't up to par with "the best buffet" look. They need new uniforms and cleaning bins or something. I swear one guy had his shirt open with a beater underneath while clearing tables. 

Come on Caesar's Palace, you guys needs to step the game back up and pay attention to the details.

This place is amazing , the food is really really good we visit 3 different buffets and This one is the best , plus our server Socorro M was really friendly and helpful. 
I recommend this place !!

There's entirely way too many options for me here. As mentioned in a previous post, I can't do buffet's because I never seem to get my money's worth. But OMG, this place has got to be the best buffet experience I've ever had. It's definitely not on the cheap side. But you can understand why when you walk in and see what they have to offer. Plus it's Vegas! I payed about $42 to dine for 2 hours. I believe for an additional $15 you get bottomless Mimosas and Bloody Mary's. Otherwise you can just opt for their variety of juices (cranberry, apple, pineapple etc.) and soda's (coke, sprite etc.) they have, which is included in your price. My favorite station was probably the dessert area. There were so many options to choose from. And the presentation was absolutely beautiful. Also, the bussers were really really friendly too. We got there around 11:30am which I believe was the best time to arrive for lunch, because about 15 minutes later, there was a long line outside. I would absolutely do this again but next time, I'll have to hold off on eating the day before so that I can actually have that eat all you can experience LOL.

Bacchanal Buffet was amazing! Bacchanal had many variety of food ranging from Asian cuisines to seafood. I loved the all you can eat seafood. I had so much lobster tails and crab legs that I couldn't stop going to wait in line. 

The service was really good too. Our waitress made sure we got what we need and came to check up throughout our stay. The meats had a good variety, but my group liked a few. Some of the meats were a bit more dry than the others while I enjoyed the ones that just melts in your mouth. Going to the dessert table, you'll love the decor and the colorful sweetness. I had to double fist two plates in order to bring back to my table. 

All in all, Bacchanal Buffet is one of my favorite buffet in Las Vegas. It's definitely worth to try it if anyone stays in Vegas!

This place is absolutely our favorite buffet in Las Vegas, hands down. Breakfast, brunch and dinner. Unlimited seafood, brisket, desserts, the list goes on. The variation and quality of food can't be matched in Vegas. While it is more expensive than others, it is 100% worth it. In this instance you will get what you pay for. Treat yourself! Don't leave Vegas disappointed with the other buffet experiences.

Very 1st time going.  We celebrated Mother's Day!  I like the quality of the food.  I'm a seafood lover.  I really enjoyed the raw oysters.  The sizes were incredible.  The crab legs were delicious as well as the tiger prawns.  I like the different cuisine options.  The dessert was delicious. We will definitely be returning and recommending to family/friends when they come to visit!

We did a lot of comparison with all the buffets in Vegas. This buffet is the BEST out of all buffets in there! Totally worth it.
The place itself is huge, a lot of seating area although it gets pack during peak hours and the line can be 30 mins wait. The food selection is amazing! Specially their seafood section. You have your Asian food, Mexican food, meat section, salad bar and my favorite- dessert station! They have a crepe maker and I love how they have all the amazing pastries. We go to Vegas at least 3 times a year, and we are going here as a tradition

First off I'm not a buffet guy, let alone a Las Vegas Buffet guy. I leave buffets to guys named "Bubba" from Southern States that can do serious damage consuming large amounts of food. I did my research on-line, asked around a bit - Bacchanal Buffet was always mentioned at the top. Matter of fact, the "NY Post" ranks Caesars Palace Bacchanal #1 in the Country. It's was on November 2nd for my Birthday November 2nd. Arrived early at or around 4:45 or so on a Saturday. I snacked all day after I worked out at AnyTime Fitness on Desert Inn. I was ready to go, ready to do damage at America's Elite buffet. After a 45 minute wait in line (didn't have Yelp app on my iPhone 11 Pro at the time, could have gotten a free libation for checking in) i paid $70.00 to get in & left an $11.00 gratuity. It was sooo worth it - everything from Kobe beef, to crab legs to  Lobster - the food was gourmet level. As for the dessert bar...cmon you know the deal haha fantastisch Also keep in mind Caesars is a high-end casino; they can get away with charging for parking. Watch out Yelpers - Bacchanal will ruin you haha I look forward to my next visit

It was nice. After all the hype about how great it is- kind of a let down. Good buffet, nothing overly exciting. Highlight was the Dessert selection. Overall the food was good.  Some dishes were a bit on the cold side. The crab legs were cut down so much ( sliced lengthwise) it wasn't really worth the effort to pick them up. Ethnic selection was good, food was otasty. Overall, nice. Would I really want to spend $60.- on it again? No. I've had better.
Great food! Nice atmosphere! Good service. Deeliiiicioussssss desserts. No complaints. Will definitely comeback the next time I come to Vegas.

very wide array of food, definitely worth every penny!
must try when you're in vegas. especially liked the prime rib and the tuna poke

Las Vegas being Sin City i guess it's a great place to indulge in gluttony. When they made up the seven deadly sins they should have partnered gluttony exclusively with Bacchanal Buffet. I've been to Vegas MANY times but only discovered Bacchanal during my last visit. This was by far the best and most expensive (please note: upcharge if you've got the buffet hopper 24 hour pass) buffet i've ever been to. The smorgasboard went on what seemed forever. There were tons and tons of choices to pick from and food from all around the world. They had a raw bar and dessert bar which were both equally fantastic (separately of course...) Something for everyone here.

Can't wait for my next trip so i can stop in again.
Always great options and a little something for everyone. No complaints. I love the brisket! The giant bacon I could do without.

Best buffet I have ever been to and worth every dime. They have literally everything you can think of whether it's made to order tacos and Mexican, American, seafood, meat carving station, ramen made to order, extremely authentic Chinese (dim sum), sushi etc. and all of it is VERY high quality. The dessert bar is awesome, everything is portioned out and relatively small you can max out (lol). Also have a gelato/sorbet bar and crepe station. Best experience ever and will 100% be back!

The Bacchanal Buffet is a huge buffet with anything and everything you could want which spans two full rooms not including the desert bar. We were there on 11/13/2019 one thing you need to be aware of is the price. Buffets in Vegas are pretty consistent with a buffet price $25.00-$30.00 give or take a couple dollars. This brunch buffet was $44.00. Don't get me wrong this is an extensive buffet with quality food. This isn't some garbage buffet. Just be aware so there is not a sticker shock for you like the people in front of me. I'll go back there again. But before that, I'll try some other ones on the strip. I did not think the service was all that great to be honest. It was blatantly obvious the server wanted us to leave as she simply did not come to the table toward the end of the meal. She wanted us to leave due to the fact she wanted the table I'm not dumb I know how it works.

step 1: go to kiosk, ignore the ppl in the other line, you dont need to worry about that yet

step 2: input number of party, get print out slip, input telephonic numeros

step 3: wait for text to recall back to aforementioned line

step 4: get in line

step 5: pay, tip on card if you wish to leave tip right then and there instead of cash

step 6: before you get into the next line, a guy will take a picture of you

step 7: wait in line, give them your receipt

step 8: the hostess will take you to your table

step9: PROFIT

must gets:
-prime rib
-wagyu sliders
-their variety of drinks (not soft drinks) like horchata, strawberry juice, guava
-gelato selections
-dimsum (although not the best, probably the best vegas has to offer if you have the cravings)

brilliant table service, amazing hospitality, food selection wide and varied
50bucks for buffet, discount if you got your total rewards card i think

Bacchanal is one of the top buffets in Vegas, and you can tell because there is always a ridiculous wait, but you can circumvent that a little bit that by going at lunchtime rather than the more expensive dinner (you'll still wait though, so don't get too excited). You can see sooo many beleaguered partiers struggling to recover and families just stuffing their faces, it caters to pretty much every type of Vegas trip. This is the buffet my family always used to go to when I was a kid during our frequent Vegas trips, and it's a buffet I still want to eat at as an adult. The food selection is ridiculously expansive -- you can order pretty much anything you might want, and in true hedonistic Vegas fashion, it's probably here. Do note that this is a pricier buffet, but you do get what you pay for and I think the food quality is comparable to Wicked Spoon if you need a reference.

They have crab legs! Skip the cold bar (they're already cut and are so dry and stringy) and get the steamed ones at the Italian station, they're MUCH better. Other stand-out dishes from the last time I went include a duck confit risotto, bone marrow, prime rib, and all the desserts.

Our server Ramona was amazing. She was fun and entertaining when we came in during the brunch hours. Our food was definitely up to the standards that Bacchanal holds up high compared to most buffets. The service in a whole could have been a little faster but I think it was just the lack of help Ramona got that took too much time to get things in and out of the table. We felt bad that she had to take care of multiple somewhat large parties at the same time but she did an amazing job and we loved her for that. Hope to come back and see her again.

The "Flies on s@#t" effect is totally evident here, being that this is the newer, born-again buffet in town and USA Today has recently given the following rankings of the top buffets in Las Vegas:

1) Bacchanal Buffet, Caesar's Palace

2) Buffet at Bellagio, Bellagio

3) Buffet at Wynn, Wynn

4) Studio B Buffet, M Casino

5) Wicked Spoon Buffet, The Cosmopolitan

The decor looks pretty cool, kinda like the Wicked Spoon had a three-way with Studio B and The Container Store, and VOILA!!! 

We arrived between Lunch/Dinner and I checked out the whole set-up and snapped photos of almost every possible selection offered that evening before grubbin'...Here's a little rundown of MY perspective of things...

SEAFOOD-Pretty familiar set-up like other spots in town...Cocktail Shrimp, Green Mussels, Oysters, SWEET King Crab like Bellagio and Wynn, Snow Crab, and no Stone Crab.
Hot and cold seafood preparations as well.Gazpacho, Seafood salad, and Oyster Shooter were pretty bland, calamari was rubbery, Passed on the Oysters-Looked old, and sunken in instead of plump and fresh. Lobster Corn Chowder and Shrimp and Grits were okay.

AMERICAN/CARVING STATIONS-good comfort foods...perfect mini sliders, mini baskets of fried goodness-wings, fish and chips,chicken tenders, fried chicken, potato skins, onion rings, etc. Carving station had a similar set-up as well, your usual sides and meats...Prime Rib, Sausage, Turkey, Ribs, Brisket, Steamship Round, etc. Tomahawk Steaks and Lamb Chops were a cool addition. Lamb was one of my faves, Tomahawk slices were unfortunately full of fat and gristle.


MEXICAN/ITALIAN STATIONS-again, your familiar selections(Pizza, Pasta, Tacos, Pozole, etc.not really anything to set them apart from the rest, I snapped photos, but decided not to fill up on items from these stations.

INFUSED HONEY/CHEESE/CHARCUTERIE/ARTISINAL BREADS-Already a winning combo of tasty cheeses,charcuterie, and breads, do not pass up the infused honey which ties everything else in very nicely.

SALADS/ASIAN STATION-The Watermelon and Feta Salad was good, and the Tonkotsu Ramen was pretty good for being at a buffet . I was curious about the Ginseng Chicken, which was slightly bitter and medicinal...first and last time trying this one! Passed up the rest of the store looking sushi, stir-frys, and salads...again, familiar stuff like all the other buffets, nothing to set themselves apart, no wow factor, nada....

DESSERTS-Lots of eye candy with the spread here...Favorites were the Baklava Ice Cream, and the simplicity of a warm crepe made to order. Sorbets were more like an icy granita and lacked the smooth texture a sorbet should have, the Blackberry Panna Cotta glass was way more gelatinous than Jello. Of course, your standard cakes, pies, tarts, cupcakes, etc....99% of buffet goers would easily snatch up French Macarons, and I'm part of that 1% that could easily decline with no regrets.

Overall, 3.5 Stars.... Cool, sleek, modern spacious look that seems to have taken up the majority of the 17 million dollar investment, I was expecting the food to be on a more elevated level, outshining the competition on the strip, but that wasn't the case here. I honestly have had better first impressions at Studio B, Wynn, and Wicked Spoon, when those buffets first opened. 500 globally inspired dishes doesn't mean better....Sometimes less is more.

Will The Bacchanal Buffet be able to hold on to the top spot? Only time will tell....ALOHA!!!

Excellent,  Excellent,  and Excellent !
A great variety of foods.  Creative dishes,
gourmet shrimp tacos, pistachio creme brulee are a must have.  Service was amazing with a special "thank you" to
Romulus for making this dining experience 
outstanding !

Read good things, but my experience was terrible. 
Went for dinner. Food looked good. However, the quality was awful. Price for 2, not including tip, over $140. Meat was over cooked and tough as leather... I mean really dried out leather. 
Seafood was terrible. The lobster claws were pure rubber, I couldn't get a bite off. I tried a number of them and all were terrible quality. The shrimp looked unappealing. The crab claws were just shells. 
Very disappointed after being excited about the buffet, waiting in the long line, paying a lot and only thing I could eat was gelato.

Maybe it was a bad day there. I don't plan to do buffets anytime soon.
If I could give this 6 stars I would .. everything was so good. From the pizza to the steamed crab legs .The only downfall is that the wait is pretty long.. we waited about 45 minutes to get seated.
Great buffet, wonderful food and service. Lots of choices. Looks fresh and well maintained. Server was very friendly. Great!

This is the fanciest, upscale AYCE buffet I have ever been to. Went here with a party of 6 for my cousin's birthday dinner and it is definitely worth it just for the experience (maybe for special occasions or first-timers). 

I wish I had the stomach and appetite to try everything in this buffet!! Omg.. this place is huge! I definitely felt overwhelmed lol. However, the crab legs were a hit! I kept going back n forth toward the crab legs station. Their meat selection was good, too. Very flavorful and food was well seasoned and cooked to the right temp. Definitely not your average buffet. The price speaks for itself ;). AND their dessert section was F A T! I wish all buffets had a wide and good selection of food and dessert. Very diverse! 

Also, my party and I would like to personally thank our servers, Soccoro and Rogel for the best service!!! Very accommodating and super helpful and friendly. Love the atmosphere, service, and FOOD!

I visited Bacchanal today after my co-worker recommended this buffet. This place is worth the price, the food today was excellent. I loved the fact that you can try food from different places but there are so many choices it is hard to decide what you want to try! The food had great taste and I was not disappointed with anything that I tried. The service was also very good. If you want to eat great food I recommend this place, the price is worth it for the quality of the food.
Such a nice buffet. SO many choices and the food is displayed nicely, not in giant chafing dishes. Our server Ramulus was fantastic too!

This place is the best buffet by far, Jennifer is awesome !!!highly recommend 
I love this buffet!! 
Definitely coming back again tomorrow

Update...
After a long phone call to voice my concerns they refunded me the cost of my brunch. Way to go Ceasers!


Talk about a LET DOWN!

Of all the things that I did in Las Vegas, this was for sure the biggest, and really the only disappointment. It's truly a shame because I was so so so looking forward to this experience.

The Wait-  OK, so there is a wait to get inside. This is understandable so I paid the extra $15 to get in with only about 15 min. wait instead of over an hour. This however, is just the FIRST of many waits to be dealt with. 

Basically, they have the buffet set up very strategically so that each station has the best stuff at the end of the line,(meats, crab, duck, etc...) so hopefully(to them) you use up the real estate on your plate with cheaper more filling stuff first like bread and pastas. I had to wait anywhere from 20-30 min EACH TIME I wanted a new plate of food!!! I couldn't believe it. Anything that you get towards the beginning of the line is ice cold by the time you actually get to eat it.  There is something seriously wrong when it takes you three or four times as long to GET the food as it does to EAT the food.

Just to drive home how long it took to get a plate of food (and how bad the service was) they actually RESEATED MY TABLE when I was in line! Are you kidding me? That shows how pathetically long it takes just to get some food here. Basically you have two hours to eat, but good luck getting more than 3 or 4 plates in that time, its just not gonna happen.


Service-  Basically non-existant. I had to flag someone down every time I needed something, and had to ask 3 times just for some salt and pepper. When they finally brought the S&P, of course I was done with the plate that I wanted it for and then when I came back with another plate is when they reseated the table, so I never actually got to use any on my food. Then they left me standing in the middle of the dinning room like an idiot with my plate of food while they figured out what to do. It was pretty embarrassing actually and obviously the food continued to get colder and colder as I waited for them to simply find me a place to eat. Finally they sat me at a four top in the middle of the dinning room and I was able to eat my piece of thin, cold, over-cooked prime rib.

So, the waits were numerous and unreasonably long, and the service was equal to about a Denny's. But how was the food?...... There was none of the stuff that I was looking forward to. No stone crab claws, no half-lobster, no caviar, no ribeye steak. There was ABSOLUTELY NOTHING that stood out from either a quality, taste or creativity standpoint. The snow crab was very watery, as was the shrimp. The lamb chops and prime rib were over-done and cold by the time i got to eat them, and they said they don't put the rib eye out until 6:30... really? But you charge full price the entire time. 

I was so let down that I just left, and before writing this review, just to give them a fair shot at redemption I called to try to speak with someone at the buffet. The first call went to a machine that did not take messages, the second call just kept ringing and ringing, finally the third time I got someone in "total care" or something, who when I told her about my experience asked me if I talked to the manager when I was there. Look, I grew up in this business including high-end, low-end and buffets: If you reseat my damn table when I am at the buffet line, YOU have the manager come over and apologize. Don't make me work harder after you screw up. Besides, I never saw a manager when I was there, only  "servers" and a few ladies that walked around with their ipads trying to jockey the table/seating situation. I certainly didn't see anyone concerned with people's experience.

The bottom line is that the price is reasonable for the buffet, but with so many other places to eat in vegas, there was not a single thing that would ever make me want to go back and wait... to wait... and wait...  to eat bland, run-of-the-mill buffet food.

Headed here on a Sunday just right before peak hours which was 2:30pm. The wait itself was about 35-40 minutes which I'm guessing is a little under the average. Honestly, once you get past the wait you're treated to one of the top notch buffets in the city. Everything is plated and displayed so enticing you can't help but want to try everything. From meats and tacos to pho and pad Thai, there is something for everyone here. And yes the food was delicious. Would definitely come back again and I highly recommend trying it out if given the chance. Stop worrying about the price! Life is short so treat yourself!
Excellent Everything!!!!! Best buffet in Vegas. Stone crab and a great atmosphere make this place special.

This was my first buffet in Vegas. At first I thought it was good but not that special. But after going to other buffets, I think Bacchanal is the best. I would come back. 

I came during dinner and the place was huge. There was so many food to pick from. Even the desserts had a lot of options and were good.

Service was great.
Dessert was awesome.
The lunch selection was good.
The only downfall was that some of the food was cold...we paid a lot of money to eat here ...expected the food to be a little bit better.

Overall, it was a decent  experience .

Finally made a point to try this buffet since our group decided to eat here for a late lunch. We paid $60 for lunch, but they were in the process of switching over to the dinner menu. I personally think it's not worth it. For someone who doesn't eat shellfish, it's a bit hard to get your money's worth. I had some sushi pieces, which was very limited since the other selection had shellfish. I also got tacos (I can get that for $1). Everything else didn't look quite as appetizing, but I did try the meat selection. They had a 16-day brisket, wagyu, and prime rib. All were okay, but I felt like it was I had more raw parts than cooked that maybe I just broke even. Not really a fan of meat from buffets either. I tried the salmon, but it was also just okay. I think my favorite was the candied potato balls in little silver pots. It was very interesting and presentable. I did enjoy their dessert menu. I probably grabbed everything with chocolate in it. The chocolate covered cones with ube inside is my favorite dessert. The  Death by Chocolate cake was also pretty good. It was very rich. I also enjoyed the Vietnamese Coffee mouse and their macarons. I wasn't a fan of the Tiramisu since it was mostly cream and the lava cake was a let down. It was over cooked. I think the most surprising part was their Thai tea float. I really liked the vanilla ice cream they used and the Thai tea is pretty good. 

For a group of 19, I think we waited for almost an hour, or at least it felt like an hour. We were in line before 2:00, but it took so long that I didn't pay until passed 2:30 and we still had to wait for a table. However, our server Francisco, was amazing. He definitely catered to our table and we truly enjoyed his service. Another "been there, done that" experience in Vegas.
Came here with a group of friends. Great brunch  buffet! One of the best I've ever had. So many options to choose from.

The food is outstanding. Very high quality, fresh and a big selection. My only complaint is the service. The waitress is attentive at first, but as the evening went on the waitress came by less and less.  I also dont understand why empty tables are not bussed soon after people leave. The table next to me sat dirty for 15 minutes. This make no sense when you have 30 people in line waiting to be seated.

This was only my 2nd ~luxury~ buffet experience in Vegas and it was pretty underwhelming. I'd give it 3.7 stars if possible. It's a smorgasbord and like other premium buffets, they offer different types of cuisines including Asian, Latin American and Italian. Not sure how often they rotate the dishes, but the standouts for me were the Osso Bucco, Singaporean laksa (my first time trying so I have no basis of comparison) and maybe the bone marrow? Some of the dishes were exciting in theory but either the flavors were off or just weren't executed properly. I get that all of the food is mass-produced, and that's expected, but it just makes me sad that they have the ingredients and the resources to make it good but they just don't deliver. Especially if you're paying upwards of $50 per head. Try to go on their slowest days which is Mondays-Thursdays. They offer brunch and dinner deals on Groupon so be sure to check those out.
Great food selection! Esmeralda is the best!

Maybe I went on an off day but after waiting 45 minutes in line I had really high expectations. This wasn't that great. The crab legs were super tiny so don't plan on filling up on that. And I also upgraded with the open bar. The white wine was very bitter. Servers were quick to take away our dirty plates so that's why they even got the 3 stars. Variety of foods were good just very bland in flavors.
Awesome food!!! I love the atmosphere and the food variety! A must go when experiencing Vegas!

Here's my thoughts before the food coma sets in... a long wait time (slightly more than 1 hour) was a detractor and unfortunately the beginning of my experience. There was some mild confusion getting seated. Once seated, I checked in and got a mimosa (normally $15 all-you-can-drink, but 1 free with a Yelp check-in). The Chinese buffet was typical. The dumplings weren't fresh or the most flavorful, though the roast duck made up for it. The bone marrow was spoken of highly in another review - I enjoyed it but can't say it was amazing. The beef selection was impressive. That's the reason I rate Bacchanal a 4 - primarily for its impressive selection.

Dessert thoughts - the cheesecake was so-so, but the hazelnut beignets were delicious and the creme and pistachio brûlée's were amazing!
Delicious! So many choices and all's so good ... steak cuts are great, crab legs were nicely done and sushi was very good. Best buffet in town

This is, without a doubt, still the best buffet in Las Vegas. The quality of the food is stellar, with the exception of the breads which are pretty lackluster. But hey, you're not going to a buffet for bread, you're going for the proteins, and this place delivers. The crab, the shrimp, and the Wagyu prime rib were the stand outs for me on this visit. It's worth the wait, trust me.

This buffet is pretty exceptional, unfortunately you can wait up to an hour on arriving. The overall experience was great, the service we received was exceptional but we were stuck sitting next to the main entrance into the kitchen taking the gloss off of the experience somewhat. This said if you have waited that long you take what you are given and enjoy the many, many food options available to you.
Come hungry great food Make sure you go during the week on the weekends pretty crowded one hour wait the price for two was 140 but the food was great I'm sure during the week it's cheaper

This is my second time coming here and it still hasn't disappointed. Javier actually waited our table this time and consistently came back and forth to make sure our table was clear, but also making sure we had refreshments. Everyone needs a Javier in their life! 

Also, if you check in on Yelp, you get a free wine, champagne or
Over all Caesar Palace has best Buffett in the Vegas strip. Seafood is fresh especially hot king crabs legs. Other dishes are make to restaurant quality.

It's ok nothing to bragged about. $69 for dinner lots of choices. The foods ok service staffs too busy we have to ask for refill and ask for out table to be clean. They are working for tips but don't have customer service skill not attentive. We put some cash on the table for tip, once they saw the tip money on the table, the wait staffs stand close by. Circle around our area but still we have to ask for refill. The cash grabbed their attention. Just before we finished we didn't feel like the server do anything. We decided NO TIP... 
welcome to Vegas trick.. they showed good high quality foods... what you getting are different...no king crab were served just small Alaskan crabs and people wait inline for that junk. If you have money to waste go for the experience once. No return...3 stars for many varieties of foods.
NO RETURN........

best buffett in vegas by miles. yes it's not inexpensive. but imo - this is what a buffett is meant to be. everything is fresh and started with obviously quality ingredients. care was taken each step of the way. and the food is flavorful. tons of options done at a high level. well with the price and the wait in line if there is one.

Extremely over hyped. I was so disappointed. This was all very cheap food. Its no better than $10 buffet. I really thought it would live up to all the hype but it didn't. Anyone who thought this was a 4+ star buffet hasn't been to a good one, like Wicked Spoon. Save yourself the grief and spend your money on a quality place.

Food is good but not extra for the price.
$59.99 for regular weekend lunch, $98.00 for VIP weekend lunch as of Nov 2019.
If you're not planning on getting drunk with champagne I don't suggest the VIP option. The seafood shower that they provide, you can get it as well from the regular buffet. And don't mistake the VIP "VIP" coz you need to get your own food from the buffet just like the regular. A very long buffet with lots of option, international decent food. They've got everything

Maybe I came here on an off day, but it was terrible.
I went here for a lunch meeting and was really excited to try it out, the food was mediocre at best. The sushi was terrible, salad was mediocre, and the seafood looked inedible. 
The good things were the meat carving station and deserts, but you can get that at almost any other buffet.

Came for brunch Thanksgiving weekend. Got in around 11 am and there was just a 10 Minute line. When we were leaving there was a very long line, so keep that in mind.

I enjoyed Bacchanal more than the Bellagio buffet. More variety and better quality. Also, the restaurant itself seemed more modern and new. 

Very good selection of foods - seafood, comfort, Asian, Italian etc. and dessert. 

The carving board had prime rib, wagyu beef, ham etc. The roast beef was quite good. Bone marrow next door was VERY rich. Probably could have eaten all of it if i wasn't at a buffet. 

Sushi options were pretty limited. Very basic rolls with multiple types of nigiri. The rice was quite sweet. Liked the lobster bisque. 

Good selection of desserts ranging from gelato, to creme brûlée, to cheesecake. The mousse was good! Lemon merengue too.

ok, so you've probably heard people say that Bacchanals is the best buffet in Vegas.. and after having tried about 10 different places, and Bacchanal at least a bakers dozen, I'd say its the best.

Pricey? Yes

Worth the price? that depends.

What do i like best? the Crabs legs - mind you not the cold stuff, but the steamed king crabs legs -  its the only reason i really go.
BUT, now this may change my whole opinion on the Buffet - so usually the serve whole crab legs/claws, but my last visit the basically took the crabs legs in their cold section and boiled them.. this was a HUGE DISAPPOINTMENT. If my next experience is the same I will stop going as its not worth it. So guys and gals, before you line up for an hour, best to take a look.. if the crabs legs are not whole legs, don't waste your time and head over to the Wicked Spoon at Cosmo. 

Other noteworthy dishes: 

The meat section can be pretty good, but play it by ear.. if it looks good then get some otherwise give it a miss, the meats sometimes end up well done an then not so great.

Over in the asian section they have some great big meaty shrimp. definitely try the Sesame Balls -  they are probably my favorite desert item at the buffet... simple but awesome.

hmm.. dessert section, good variety, better than most other buffets. The Jury is still out for me when it comes to desserts (I would have said its the best if they still served the ice cream mochi's - boy were they good).

Also, when it comes to timing -  best go after 3.30pm -  thats when some of the better items such as the steamed crabs legs come out, and the shrimp mentioned above. Yes it costs an extra 10 bucks or so but its worth it.

Skip the buffet if its before 3.30pm -  just my opinion..


apologies for the longer than usual review.
We always come to ceasers buffet when in Vegas. The food is always great and it gives you a mass variety of food from all cultures. Our server ismerelda was also great. A must try.

Bacchanal is a high-end buffet inside Caesars. It follows the standard Vegas buffet format - a long line to get inside, a very large range of stations, and the challenge of finding your table again once you've filled your plate.

We arrived early - 6pm on a Friday (because we had a show), and only had to wait about 1/2 hour to be seated. 

We've tried a few of the high end places over the years. This one is among the better ones, but it didn't stand out as amazing. The best parts for me were the Asian sections. The most disappointing were the roasted meats - where the lamb chops were overdone, for example. There were some frustrating omissions - there was a great supply of high quality peking duck, but no pancakes. The dessert selection was especially good, though I was pretty full by then.

Service was well organised and helpful. 

Definitely a good choice for a pricey buffet, though not so great that we'll be rushing to visit again next time we're in town.

Pretty disappointed. This was talked about as the number one buffet in Vegas. This Buffet is not close to Bellagio Buffet. Sushi? Garbage. Did not even taste fresh. Sashimi? LOL in a little tiny plastic cup. Why? Stone Crab? Told that was not available for dinner guests only breakfast. What? Lobster? Where? King Crab? No big deal. Most have same. Snow Crab? Same thing. Big deal. Cioppino Soup? The Chef forgot how to make it evidently. Nothing in it. Broth and a few pieces of Stone Crab. Comical. The Waygu beef? Big deal. Nothing special. All the misc. Fixings of breads, veggies, etc. were over extravagantly put together for the eye and most were not even bothering with picking them. And at the end the deserts. We were quite amused but it capped off disappointed with a bunch of little deserts that looked like they belonged at the local street buffet. Why no sliced cheese cakes? No sliced pieces of pie? No sliced cakes? In the end for $120 for two people this is beyond over-priced. Save the money and head next door to the Ballagio Buffet. It slams this place. Very disappointed.
這是我第一次到這個餐廳吃飯，因為它在Yelp的評分很高，所以我想去試試，果然是一家好餐廳，雖然菜色不多，但是每樣都很精緻，蝦-新鮮，又鮮甜，墨西哥菜，也做得很到位，就連炸雞那塊waffle 都是我吃過最好吃的.Gelato 又濃又純，甜點裡面最好的是巧克力lava cake, 我站在旁邊介紹給其他的客人，深怕別人錯過，那就太可惜了！強烈推薦大家去試試看！

I have heard the words "Best buffet in Las Vegas". I try to avoid using this phrase, but Bacchanal Buffet. You had me at hello! :) THE BEST BUFFET in LAS VEGAS!! No Diggity No Doubt!

Yes, this place is expensive. The most expensive buffet I have ever been too including Brazilian BBQ. Yes, I am cheap at times, but this place is so worth it. I don't mind if other people think it's too expensive, give it a bad rating, and don't want to come here. Good for the rest of us because then we won't have to wait as long the next time we go. Hater are gonna hate. 

New Reservation System!
Type in your party size, name, and phone number in to the kiosk to receive a reminder text when your table is ready. Wow! Thank you so much! I hated my first wait here. It was only 1 hour which is on the low end compared to other people I've talk to. Now I can lose my money in the casino or watch the Seahawks kill the 49ers and go to the Superbowl while I wait. Too soon?

VALUE
This depends on the person. Some people can eat! I saw a dude hold 3 plates at once. The majority of patrons are really skinny and I don't know where they fit their food, but if they can do it. You can do it! Forget about your diet. Think of this buffet as your Thanksgiving meal in Las Vegas any time of year. I wish it was a little less, but I am sure most people lose more in gambling than the cost of this buffet. I choose food over slots any day.

PRICE
The price is around $55 person with tax for dinner on a weekend with a Total Rewards card. The price is less for weekdays and lunch time, but I don't know if there are any items not included in lunch. So, I usually get dinner. There is a $20 option per person to skip the line. I have heard this is a rip off. I have never used it but if I had the cash. Why not? If you have a lot of money and your time is more valuable do it. I do value my time not just in Vegas but I can't pay the extra bucks for now I will just wait the 2 hours. 

Breakfast (Monday - Friday, 7 a.m. - 11 a.m.): $25.99
Brunch (Saturday - Sunday, 8 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $40.99
Lunch (Monday - Friday, 11 a.m. - 3 p.m.): $32.99
Dinner (Daily, 3 p.m. - 10 p.m.): $45.99 on weekdays, $50.99 on weekends

FOOD
I try not use the words "to die for" or "Aaamazinnng!!" But this buffet makes me weak in the knees. I rather eat here than gamble, shop or do anything Vegas has to offer. In fact, Saturday night I was planning the evening and chose this buffet over watching Boyz II Men. I know I will sound lame but I love the Asian food section and bbq section! I know am not eating the most expensive food, but I will eat what I like. I am not a garbage disposal. From the BBQ station get both the pork and beef ribs they are smoked to perfection. Also, I love the Asian noodles, roast duck, bbq pork, and ox tail soup. I never have room for dimsum but it looks good. I don't usually get dessert or crab legs because that's too common in every buffet. I always go with oysters or if I have room the steamed crab legs. 
 
I highly recommend this buffet to anyone. I read this buffet took $7 Million to create. So $50 bucks sound like a decent price to live large.

Note to self. Stay at Caesars Palace already! I have wanted to stay here since way before I was 21 and before the modern Vegas strip was nothing but a dirty road and water spraying mist on your face along the sidewalk. Well Caesar you have given me a reason to live like a roman emperor.
Love it here!! Great choices and great atmosphere will be returning! Beautiful all around, each dish selection smells and tastes absolutely phenomenal

Not our first time here and it's still the top buffet in Vegas. Overall, tons of choices and the quality was top-notch. I especially like the noodle bar, nothing like a bowl of pho after some greasy prime rib and brisket. They used to have Laksa, but it wasn't there this past thanksgiving. Great dessert bar and great gelato selection. Arrive early, or else you'll be in line for a while....

No lines at 8:30am on a monday morning.  The breakfast price is $24.99.  I love this place.  Variety of cusines-American, Italitan, Chinese, Japanese, Mexican.  I had ham, slab of bacon, smoked brisket was moist and delicious.  The chinese food-rice porridge, noodles, dim sum, chinese doughnut was yummy.  Also their red velvet pancakes was moist not dry.  No complaints here.  I had no room for dessert which I was bummed about.  Next time.  In addition, they state 2 hours limit on the receipt which is nice to know.

We had gone here with our friend and recommended it as it being one of the best buffets. After a hour and a half in a confusing line and kind of rude cashiers, we made it in. The waiting staff was very nice and always had water and soda for us. As far as the food goes, it was a hit or miss. Some food was very good and hot while others were barely warm and did not have a lot of flavor. All in all it was a good experience but not one I'd wait hours in line for again.

One of the best buffet I've been to. There's some hit and miss, but that comes with any buffet. You can eat as much or little as you want, but what's the purpose of going to a buffet!? 

There was a great selection of different types of seafood as well as cuisines. Feast your way in crab legs, bone marrow, and green tea/white chocolate strawberries. Well, at least that's what I did!
Don't go unless you're diamond or seven stars. You will wait minimum of hour to get seated. We went at 4:30 in the afternoon and waited hour to get seated. Terrible service

The food is not good as I remember. Quality went down but prices go up. Even our server is slow and doesn't look too happy. The fried rice was hard, bread hard, sushi looks old, meat was salty, etc. I ended up taking one bite of each food I grab. I'm just really disappointed because it used to be the best buffet in LV but not it's not anymore.

I have been hearing rave reviews of the Bacchanal Buffet since they opened up. Now my Wife and I aren't big buffet people. If I'm in Vegas there are 100s of choices of good restaurants, so a buffet is usually the last place I want to go, especially since the new trend seems to be these mega style expensive buffets. 

So we get into Vegas on Saturday morning and decide to go over the Caesars(we were staying at the Palazzo) and try it out. It was around 11:30 and the line wasn't too bad, only took about 10 minutes to pay and get seated, the total was $125 for 3, my Wife, 10 year old son and myself.

We get seated and hit up the buffet. Visually the place is very nice and the food presentation is great, the issue and this is a huge issue, is that the food is just at best o.k.. 

Everything was lukewarm to almost cool. Didn't matter what station or what item. Eggs ,bacon,macaroni, grits,waffles,brisket,meatballs all cold. If it had any warmth to it, it was dried out as the fried chicken was.

Another issue was that lots of the items were just way too salty, and this is a trend I'm noticing at a lot of places now. People are confusing well seasoned to lots of salt. The only really solid items were the preprepared stuff like cold cuts, cheeses. Lots of other tables seemed to be enjoying the crab legs and shrimp, I didn't have any so I can't vouch for them

The highlight was the desert station, which seemed to be the most popular, they had a everything from gelato to pastries and gummi bears.

Now based on all the rave reviews I am seeing here on yelp, I either went on an off day or a very slow day and maybe this is the reason thing were cold and salty as they weren't being switched out as much as they should be.

I have no issue with buffets as a matter of fact if this were a $15 buffet it would have rocked and I would be much more forgiving, but at $50+ per person, it better be good, and it wasn't, like I said earlier there are 100's of choices of good places to eat in Vegas within 1 miles of this buffet at the same price point. Next time I'm in Vegas I'tt try one of those other places.

After seeing the long lines and hearing everyone call the Bacchanal one of the best buffets in Vegas, I thought that braving the 3 hour wait and $70/person price tag would be worth it. 

However, the whole day after I ate at the Bacchanal (which was the only thing I ate that day), I experienced projectile vomiting and heavy diarrhea. Boy that was definitely NOT worth all the trouble for the food.

The carved meet was very average; the prime rib was heavily under seasoned and the American wagyu was extremely tough! The steamed foods that they had were also badly prepared with wrappings that were tough and overly chewy. The only good things in my opinion were the roast pork, kielbasa, and desserts. 

I cannot ever recommend this buffet to anyone. To be completely honest, with the $70 that you're spending here, you are better off going to a steakhouse or a fancier restaurant.

Paid 48.00 for lunch here with tip and I was very underwhelmed.. all the meat I tried was not piping hot. Thai rice cold. I like my food hot and was disappointed with how Luke warm or cold. I tried the cookies very hard not warm. Gelato was very good . This buffet is overrated this was my second visit and last.

It's been one WHOLE year. ONE WHOLE YEAR. Who does that to the world's greatest buffet ever?

I didn't have to wait this time, it was cheaper than I remembered, and the food just got even BETTER. I craved the comforts of home aka Asian cuisine and when I finally got my bowl of pho, I was expecting something bland like last time. Instead, I slurped and sipped some legit and tasty noodles! It's like they listened to me!

If you want to recreate a bowl of pho like you'd get from home, here's how:

a) Get the pho from the chef (obv).
b) There are garnishes immediately to the left after getting your bowl
c) Go over to the congee station and get green onions!
d) Go to the taco station and look for wedges of lime!
e) AVOID THEIR WATERED DOWN SRIRACHA!

Also, you can kind of make carne asada fries. Just ask to get carne asada cooked on the grill, get their criss cut fries, get the mac 'n' cheese cheese, sour cream, and green onions.

You're welcome!

I heard all the buzz about this place for the top 10 buffets in Las Vegas so we decided to try it out.  This buffet has a variety of foods to seafood, Spanish, Asian, and American food. It has a great variety of desserts. 

I have been to other buffets in Las Vegas and I have not seen American Wagu or good portion of bone marrow.  In my opinion, it is worth it.
This is a great Buffett that offers a wide array of food items. It is a bit pricey but well worth it, if you can build up your appetite for this place.

I always stop by this buffet when I visit Vegas. You can expect the wait to be very long, so I try to get there between 4-5pm just to line up (which is about a 30m wait, and that's considered really fast). Truthfully, I was a little disappointed as they've changed out their crab legs from recent years. They no longer serve cold, full crab legs. If you want that, you'll either have to get boiled ones or settle for smaller half-opened legs. Everything else was delicious!!!! I ate so much here even when I was full. This is a must try even if just once!!

Okay--yes. I'm so glad we chose this buffet on our girls trip to Vegas. We were pretty decided on going to Bellagio but upon arrival literally everyone told us to go to Bacchanal. And for good reason, with a meat and seafood selection like this for $55pp on a Monday night in Vegas, you can't go wrong!

My only qualm is our group arrived at 5:30 thinking it would be easy enough to miss the dinner rush. Nope. We had to get a ticket that gave us a time to go back at 7:30. We came a few minutes early and the hostess said nope, come back at 7:30 on the dot. Only to wait in 2 more lines! We were finally seated at 8:40, which is sad because the restaurant closes at 10, so by the end of our meal there were definitely things we couldn't get a second portion of because they ran out like oysters and steak.

However, the food was super impressive for buffet food and we 100% got our money's worth. I had so much steak and seafood. It came with so many sauces and varieties of food, I never got bored. Barely anything was NOT good. Even the dessert section was delicious. The gelato was my favorite!

If I'm ever in Vegas again, I'll recommend this buffet, but I definitely want to try other ones. I also recommend doing VIP for $40 more so you don't have to wait as long as I did. And if you like alcohol the VIP is worth it!

A million stars. This place is the most elegant and life changing buffet i have seen or been to. I couldn't believe the options. It's like a cross between a club and a buffet. It would be a book if I labeled all the great things. The only bad thing about this place is that I had to leave. You are in Vegas. Spoil yourself and hit this buffet like a champ. Go hungry and pace yourself. I consider myself a great eater, but this challenge took me out. If you made it this far to Vegas don't stop at prices. This is about $60 pp but you were probably dumping that on a machine or on black or red. This isn't a gamble!!!! You win every time.

Great food and atmosphere:) I love the food here. Will return. 

Best selection of food out of all Vegas
Amazing food and service. Romulus is the homie! I took a little from everywhere and saved room for dessert
This is an exceptional buffet. The food was amazing!!!! So much variety. I was worth every penny.i can't wait to do it again.

This was the game changer for me. I'm 5'3 and I can never justify eating at a buffet. I can't eat enough to make it worth it, but this is where I throw caution to the wind! 

Dinner time is when they serve snow crabs two ways: cold and steamed. I recommend the steamed. The snow crabs are served morning to lunch, FYI if that's your thing. 

The dessert section is an island of dreams. Something for everyone.

If you get Romulus as your server, you will have an extra wonderful experience.

This buffet is fantastic!  It's better than Wicked Spoon, Wynn, and Aria.  The decor was great becacuse you could sit in 3 sections-metal, glass, wood.  I sat in the metal area with arm chairs and the chair was so comfortable.  I had a great time waiting in line for 2 hours to eat the dinner buffet.  It was fun chatting with people in front and back of me.  Show your Total rewards card and you will get $3.00 off.  Great deal!  I paid $36.99 for dinner buffet.

There were 7 sections-Asian w/dim sum, duck, pho bar, Italitan-pizza, meatballs, pasta, garlic knot bread, Mexican-salsas, homemade tortillas, carne asada, tamales, American-prime rib, chicken, sausages, fried chicken w/fries in basket, fish w/fries, salmon, Seafood-crab legs, shrimp, oysters, Japanese-Udon, sushi, rice, Desserts-gelato, macaroonscookies in a cup, cakes, mini cupcakes, Deli-cheese and slices of deli meat.  

Highlights-dim sum, duck, pizza, carne asada, prime rib, crab legs, desserts.  The staff was great especially behind the dessert bar and servers who refill my drinks.  I will definitely go back again.  I can't wait.

Dined here on Thursday 4/4/13 with 5 friends. I will say that you can definitely eat your money's worth so that's not the issue. We all spent an additional $15 for "express pass" otherwise we would not have been able to dine at all (Total: $65.93+TIP). The "normal" line was long, REALLY long. I don't think the $15 "express pass" was worth it though because it didn't seem like we were a priority to the staff. Then they tried to squeeze 6 grown men into a table made for 4 people. We essentially used mob-rule against the lady seating us to takeover a larger table. Our waiter was great, he was 5 star. The cashiers, host/hostess, etc were 2 star. The food was 3-4 star. I am not a huge seafood person so I didn't try the crab legs but did look them over, meh. I tried various things, liked the sushi the most. They had little cheeseburgers, sort of like gourmet sliders - although only in appearance - they were DRY and way too salty. Could only eat one. Prime rib was good. Dessert offerings were good, especially the crepes. Surprisingly few offerings to pare with the crepe however. Can't say that I would wait in line for this buffet again.

For the amount of money we paid I'd have loved to go to a sit down restaurant and be served quality over quantity 
Big lines for crab legs or meats , just a mess.
Deserts were okay
Oh and I mention the wait to enter , that was a nightmare as well.

I honestly was so excited to eat here, mainly because it's been years since I've last eaten at a Vegas buffet.  I'm talking like at least a good 4 years.  Every time I go to Vegas, I never got the chance to eat at a buffet because we're usually going clubbing and buffets and clubbing, do not mix.  

I had heard for years that Bacchanal was the best Vegas buffet so I was super excited to eat here.  I researched how to get your money's worth at buffets by watching Youtube videos and Googling "How to get your money's worth at a buffet".  

If you're curious on how to get your money's worth at a buffet, it's basically:

-Don't eat carbs
-Don't eat cheap stuff
-Go for the meats, seafood and expensive items
-Pace yourself
-Don't fill up on drinks
-Do a lap around the buffet before you start loading up a plate

So after eating here and following the above advice, I can safely say, I don't want to do a Vegas buffet again for a very, very long time.  Bacchanal was great, not going to lie, although I do think it was a bit overpriced.  It was close to $60 including tax.  

They have a ton of variety of foods, from all different kinds of meats to some seafood dishes to a taco bar to a charcuterie area, sushi dishes and noodles. They have a lot more but I'm just trying to drive home the fact that there's a ton of variety.  The food itself is good.  I definitely enjoyed myself, albeit a little too much, hence the reason why I don't want to go to a buffet again for a long, long time.

I liked it was more than I did the Wynn buffet (but the Wynn Buffet was insanely pretty) but I also like Studio B buffet but only because it's substantially less expensive but the quality of the food doesn't compare to Bacchanal. 

If you love variety and you can pack meat and seafood down like no tomorrow, you'll love this place. I love variety and I enjoyed myself a little too much here and left in pain from overeating and was pretty much full till the next day.

I would recommend it, but just be warned that it's not cheap and you'll probably have to wait. However, the food is good, there's a ton of variety and they're constantly restocking. Their desserts are lacking though, with the exception of the gelato.  Their desserts look super pretty but they don't really taste all that good, or at least, they didn't to me.

Been to Vegas 5 times this year, and since the first trip this year we tried going but always forgot. So our desire for it grew. This past weekend, we finally went on Saturday, the 21st. 

First off the line to pay, was about 40 minutes alone, and the seating wait time was about 20 minutes, so an hour to actually get in. The price was 65 dollars, which I mean its Vegas so its not thay bad for a buffet.

Options were decent, but was expecting a bigger buffet.  They had seafood, American, Mexican, Italian, Japanese and Chinese food, and i think some greek, not really fully sure. 

The food was exceptional, but nothing that I could really say was beyond amazing. I had a few plates to get my money's worth. It was typical food for the types they had, nothing out of the ordinary. 

The desserts were probably the best. I had a crepe, and was really good with the berry toppings they had, but I overpoured, still good. They had this mango puree with mango bits on it that was probably my favorite thing from the whole experience. Also the cheesecake was good, and the Nutella donut was alright. 


Overall we got our moneys worth, but wasn't the best buffet ever. I did get a free beer though, with the Yelp check- in, so that was a plus. 

Probably won't come back, and go to the buffet at Rio.

Heard this buffet was one of the top ten in Vegas. Knew this place was pricey but didn't realize it was $60 so I was quickly taken back by that. We definitely went at the wrong time because it was a zoo and the line was so long it felt like I was waiting for a ride at Disneyland. We went around 7pm on a Saturday. The line was about an hour or more long and hella stuffy and hot. You have to pay before you enter and at first glance I didn't even realize the entire back session of food. 

They have everything you could possibly think of from Asian, mexican, American, Italian, seafood, etc and let's not forget the enormous dessert bar with everything from crepes, pastries, gelato, pudding and much more. Omg FOOD COMA! The longest line belonged to the seafood because I swear people were rushing like those crab legs were going outta style. If you are looking for quality, I would pass and eat at another restaurant. It may cost you a little more, but you will get significantly better quality. I cringe to think this is considered the best buffet - I think the younger kid in me would have loved this place, but definitely not the adult in me now.

Highlights:
   * Crab: The crab was decent, it was really nice that you have the option of getting your crab warm or cold - they were also very good about keeping the crab fully stocked
   * Bone marrow: This was cooked and flavored well, I especially appreciated that they cut the bone in half to make the marrow really easy to access
   * Lamb chop: This wasn't great, but decent compared to everything else
   * General ambiance was nice, especially for a buffet. It wasn't too loud, and you didn't seem to have a lot of rude, pushy people

Lowlights (where to start):
   * Prime rib: worst I've ever tasted. I'm pretty sure it wasn't even prime rib or a Prime grade cut. It was tough and lacked flavor. I can't believe they would serve this garbage at their carving station
   * Sushi: it tasted stale and limp, definitely nothing like what we have at home; rice was a bit hard
   * Dim sum: Texture and taste weren't great; at least it wasn't too oily or salty
   * Mexican food: Flavors and meat just didn't work for me, definitely nothing like what we can get from food trucks or restaurants in the SF Bay Area
   * Duck: Overcooked, nothing special about the flavor
   * Noodles: Tasted very generic, nothing special about the flavor
   * Shrimp cocktail: Tough to screw this up
   * Oysters: Disappointed they didn't have any - I don't think they were out, I think they just weren't serving any (or maybe they were out)
   * Fried chicken basket: I saw tons of these pictures, VERY disappointed they didn't have this the night we went

I could keep going, but you get the point. Mediocre quality, HUGE quantity. You decide if this is what gets you excited.

Evidenced by the mere 18 updated reviews I've written before this one, it's safe to say I don't do these often.  And even then, several of those updates weren't even real "updates", as they weren't really to note any changes in my experiences or rating.  So, suffice to say, when I do take the time to write these, there's a pretty compelling reason why.  It just sucks that the reason why is because my favorite buffet on The Strip isn't nearly as good as it used to be.  Ugh...so sad.

Admittedly, my review was after my first trip here, which was loaded with excitement and anticipation.  Still, from their use of kiosks to manage the lines/crowds during peak hours, to their terrific selection, to their delicious food, I was truly impressed with Bacchanal.  However, across the three visits I've made since then, it feels like each has been progressively less satisfying.  Perhaps not to the extent where I'd swear off coming back, but definitely to the point where I debate if they're worth the money.

On the plus side, Bacchanal's range of options is still pretty dope, as it includes, but isn't limited to, a noodle bar, a taco bar, tons of seafood (stone crab claws, oysters, mussels, snow crab legs, shrimp), a range of carvery meats (prime rib, pork tenderloin, ribs), pizzas, sushi, salads, fruits, hot entrees (bone marrow, gumbo, ribs), dim sum, and an awesome dessert bar.  What's more, it looks like they added lobster claws to their usual slate, along with clam chowder and lobster bisque, though it's possible that they were somewhat seasonal/holiday driven.

That being said, it feels like the quality and taste of some of their food is really starting to slip.  In particular, the slice of American wagyu I got wasn't all that tender, the prime rib was badly in need of more seasoning, the lobster bisque was ridiculously salty, and the selection of sushi was kind of sparse (just salmon nigiri and a handful of cooked rolls).  Also, while it was never actually good, their "Chinese roast pork" is a sad take on the real thing, as the skin is far more soggy/mealy than crisp.  Gross.

Sadly, despite how some of their food is trending in the wrong direction, they pale in comparison to the service.  Granted, you never expect it to be great at a buffet, but this last trip was awful.  The folks we've had before have been friendly, accommodating, and very helpful.  Most importantly, they would come by fairly often.  This last time though, our server checked none of those boxes.  I would've chalked it up to him being slammed on a holiday weekend, but not when I see him socializing with folks.  No, I guess I can't get a new spoon, these plates bussed, or a refill on my Diet Coke.

Considering how dinner on weekends goes for about $65 a person before tax/tip (or even more, if you pay to jump part of the line), it's no small decision to come here for dinner (as opposed to going elsewhere and/or paying less for dinner).  They're still better than paying almost the same for Bellagio's buffet, but I think I'd rather pay the $20 Uber/Lyft ride to head to Studio B in Henderson for a buffet that offers almost as much, tastes just as good (if not better), and costs roughly two thirds the price.

Sorry, Bacchanal.  I've loved you, and will probably be back at least one more time to see if things get any better, but you sure are making it hard for my friends and I to keep you in our Vegas rotation.
