- the seared Tuna Nicouise salad is overwhelming with pickled red pepper
- consider adding soy free and dairy free products for coffee such as almond milk and oat milk
Overwhelming and yet underwhelming all at the same time. It is an experience but the quality is still limited by the buffet constraints.

This place is insane!!!! I can't believe I've never been before. So much good food, not enough stomach! 

Found this gem on Groupon for $85 for two people with two mirmosas! We made three trips to the buffet to make sure we try everything. Our fourth trip was to the dessert island and I was only able to eat half a tart. Lol. Breakfast was great and the seafood... mmmmm. The crab legs are on ice, but if you ask, they will steam them for you!

 We had to pay for tax ($7) when we arrived and we left a tip on the receipt when we paid with card. During our meal, we asked our server if he gets that money and to our surprise he had zero recollection of it. We went to the front and got that all sorted out to make sure he got that money. That was kind of sketchy just wondering how many times that has happened in the past, and where that money would go? This was the only reason I'm not rating it 5 stars.

We love this buffet and have them at least once a year.

We see the prices have went up a bit since the last time we had them and they also changed the wait system since the last time we were in. You now get texted to tell you when you can get in line to be seated. We waited less then an hour and were seated right away.

The food was amazing as usual,lots to choose from,but our waiter could of been more attentive with our drinks,keep the Pepsi coming.

At first I was hesitant about this buffet because 1. it's a buffet and 2. because it's rather expensive. However I was horribly wrong. The food was freaking amazing. I went for brunch and buffet was extensive. Steak and eggs was delicious, best ravioli of my life, delicious sushi, actual fruit, which seems to be rare for buffets. My husband asked for some crab legs to be steamed and they gave him a heaping plate. The buffet was so long I almost missed the dessert buffet, which included gelato, sorbet, fudge and the most delicious mousse fruit tart. It'll cost you a pretty penny but it's so worth it.
this place is so overrated, prime rib was cold, over cooked fish, chinese dish and sushi was so so. dessert was good. NOT worth $55 and the long lines. just my opinion

This was my favorite Vegas buffet, It might still be.  When the buffet opened it looked somewhat similar to the advertising truck that goes up and down the strip enticing guests to come. They went down down down hill. It's still better then most.
Great food. Amazing. However, the long wait destroyed my appetite. The first time I came here, the wait was 4 hours. This time, the wait was 2 hours. Never coming back.

This is by far the best buffet in Vegas. However, the wait is ridiculous so that's why I'm only giving four stars (plus the not so attentive waitress). They got pretty much everything in their buffet: oysters, sushi, fresh crepes, crab legs/claws, sliders, prime rib and much more! We ended up paying $25 more per person to skip the line. We were here during Labor Day weekend tho.
If you want to wait multiple hours for horrible food, this is the place for you. Would NOT recommend!

This buffet is awesome! We went to 3 buffets in 2 days... Yes you heard me, 3. Gluttony to the max. From the three Bacchanal is the best buffet. I've also been to other buffets in Vegas prior to this binge eating, and Bacchanal is still the best. 

It's the best because they have a variety of seafood for dinner from stone crab claws, crab legs (cold and hot), mussels, oysters, jumbo shrimps and all kind of meats from prime rib, steak to ribs. Yes ribs! They also have all the fillers you can ask for: sushi, pho, pizza, pasta, ramen, salads, dim sum, cured meats... I could go on and on but this by far was the most food offerings I encountered from all the buffets in Vegas! 

The dessert area was also great, they had everything! I'm in love with this buffet. I would come back here. Lots of options. 

We came on a Monday night so there wasn't a line, but I read reviews that you could wait up to hours!! That would turn me off. Come on an off day and you don't have to wait! 

This is considered fatso heaven, if I die of obesity it's because of stuffing my fatass here. Beware fatties, as this will satisfy all cravings!
Nice selection and the dinner line moved fast. Food was pretty good and abundant but many selections were salty.

Nice selection. Tried many things...I think my favorite was the Hatch Chile Mashed potatoes, and the New Orleans Shrimp and Grits. Grits were cooked right, nice and creamy! I tasted a Lemon Basil sorbet for my dessert...it was !!!
Yummo. So bomb dot com. Love this place yum yum yummmmmm Yas yum. Would go to seafood buffet every day Yas
Esmeralda was an amazing host to us she was very helpful and was always making sure  everything was okay, and the food was amazing.

Las Vegas, one of the most food-centric places- - possesses one of the top buffets, The Bacchanal Buffet at the Opulent Caesars Palace!

In an elegant and modern setting and offering a wide selection of artfully crafted cuisines from all around the world. 

With precise techniques and top ingredients to elevate American, Italian and French classics paired with traditional Asian and Mexican fares, this place is the perfect specimen to enliven and satisfy every picky eaters and foodies alike! 

With the massive amount of food that's mass produced, one might expect low quality with mediocre results. However, the food here was surprisingly good and the flavors were on point! 

An endless amount of offerings and too many to mention. I mean the carving station alone has six different cuts of meat, seafood was abundance, luxurious offerings like lobster bisque and bone marrows, delicacies such as escargots and sashimis and so much more were readily available for you to consume to your heart's content! 

The best part is....their dessert lineup is stunning! From made to order crepes, mousses, tarts and cakes to creme brûlée and chocolate covered strawberries with toffee crumbles. 

Tip: Get there by 3 and pay the lunch price for a dinner menu. 

Definitely worth the trip!

AHHHHHHmazing!!!

Background: I've been here three times in the past 6 months, the last two times were from my most recent trip. All three visits were with Total Rewards Seven Stars or Diamond tier guests, so I've never paid for my meal or have experienced any sort of wait. Also, these guests receive better treatment than the average Joe (better seats closer to the buffet, special perks), so a normal guest experience might be different, although the food experience should be the same.

My first visit was truly overwhelming. Our party of six were seated in plush, covered booths near the dessert station, and we were on a mission to get the most out of the meal: seafood, seafood, seafood, meat plate, one plate of whatever you want, and dessert. We ate a ton of crab legs and shrimp, plenty of meat, but I truly didn't get to enjoy everything else.

The last two visits weren't quite as overwhelming because you get used to how large and extensive the buffet is (and it is incredibly large), and the navigation is easier. In the last two visits I tried a bit of everything worth trying and that I had room for, and here are some of my favored highlights:

-Snow crab legs: two options - freshly steamed (literally straight out of the boiling pot onto your plate), and chilled + pre-cut. 
-Chinese selection: some of the best quality, authentic Peking (roast) duck and crispy roast pork. 
-Tuna and salmon poke: some of the only carbs I allowed myself to eat (pictured). These tiny plates were bursting with flavor, freshness, spice and texture. 
-Shrimp, mussels, oysters, stone crab claws, specialty seafood dishes: these were ALL GOOD. Great size and quality of each item, especially at a buffet. The stations were always full, so eat your heart out. One of my favorites was the fried soft shell crab on a bed of puree and fresh shaved corn (pictured).
-Meat station: the line was popping to get to this - it's a carnivore's dream with tons of hearty meats. I tried the prime rib here and it was delicious! 
-Mac and cheese w/ Hatch chiles: this was some of the best mac and cheese I have ever had. The cheese is strong but not overpowering, and the hatch chiles added a great contrast to the flavor. 
-Pizza: in full disclosure, I am not even a pizza fan, but I tried one slice and it was cooked perfectly with a thin, crispy crust, high-quality cheese and excellent flavor. If this weren't such a carb-heavy item I would have eaten more!
-Dessert: Kudos to the dessert/pastry chefs here. I tried almost every single dessert offered and all the desserts were made with such detail and extreme care. They were bursting with unique flavors and not hiding behind the mask of being overly sweet. My favorites were the cheesecake (phenomenal!!!) and panna cotta topped with tropical fruit (amazing!!).

PRO TIP: Diamond tier level get your choice of champagne or king crab legs for the table. Choose the crab legs, obviously (pictured).

I've read over some of the negative reviews of this place, and even as a fairly critical reviewer I struggle with understanding the logic of rating Bacchanal poorly. For a $60 AYCE, you're paying a pretty standard price for supreme quality where every item is expertly prepared with great flavor, detail, and creativity. There was not a single item here I did not enjoy, and I have tried many of them! Well done to the incredible team of chefs who create amazing experiences here; will be back time and time again!
Food is good average. The meat was a disappointment except for the brisket. I felt it was better than Aria Buffett.

Too many dishes available to even try them all! All kinds of cuisine, and all you can eat! Quality is good. Truly a world class buffet! If you're a big eater and like variety, it's worth it. Everything's expensive on the strip anyway! If you have some snow crab legs, oysters, sushi, pork belly, duck, Peruvian and creole food, you pretty much got your $ worth! 
Wait can be long tho.
I'd check this place out again! 2 hour maximum eating limit, but you probably won't last the whole two hours anyway!
Don't skip the dessert bar! Was really good! I like the pistachio creme brûlée!

One of the things my friends wanted to do when they were visiting Las Vegas was to eat at Bacchanal Buffet, and considering I've been wanting to eat at this buffet, I readily agreed. We found a Groupon for the buffet that suited our needs and off we went.

Bacchanal Buffet is located in Caesars hotel and we didn't wait long in line before we led to our table. After ordering my drink, I went to sample food at every station. Maybe it was hype, but I thought the buffet was going to be a lot bigger in size than it actually was. 

I liked most of what I tried, especially the Mexican and dessert stations. There are ube desserts! The tacos were amazing. The Asian station left me disappointed though, especially with Chinatown nearby providing better tasting Asian dishes for a lot less. To be fair, I don't think I've tried any buffet in Vegas that had a decent Asian station.

I wish I had a bigger stomach so I could have continued eating that day, but I guess that just means I have to come back another time since I did like Bacchanal Buffet.
Fresh,eye catching,fact is people eat with thier eyes,taste and smell are over the top,this is one place i would return to every time i walked past! Amazing !
The most amazing buffet. There are so many choices. Save room for dessert. The service was great as well. Everyone in my party raved about it. We will definitely be back on our next visit.

I  have eaten here for the breakfast and lunch  before and was satisfied. Tried dinner a few days ago and what a disappointment. Prime rib was tough and tasteless. At 8 pm they ran out of carne asada. Some of the food was warm, not hot. Desserts were ordinary.  Have had a better experience at Golden Corral.  Paid $75 including tax and tip. Waited 1 hour and 10 minutes in line to pay and get seated.  My waiter was very attentive.

Where do I even start with this buffet.... 
First, let's talk about wait time. There are multiple lines when you arrive just to pay for your buffet. Most of the lines are based on status, so there's a general admission line and lines for Platinum/Express, Diamond, and Seven Stars status members. They are all about status at Caesar's hotels. We are fortunate to be Diamond, so we only waited maybe 20 minutes at 6:30pm on a Monday to pay for our buffet. We then waited another 20 in the next line to wait for a table. I can only imagine how long someone in the GA line waits during peak lunch/dinner times. I would assume hours. So if you don't have a higher Caesars rewards status, I would recommend not eating during peak hours. 

Once we got in, the service was better than other buffets we had visited. Our server arrived within a couple minutes, took our drink order, and set us free to explore the buffet. He regularly cleared our plates and offered us after dinner coffee. He was a gem! 

There's so much food, you have to prioritize what you want to eat most. I started with the American and cold seafood section. I made my way over to the steamed crab legs where I waited for maybe 10 minutes to be served, but it was completely worth the wait. I was shocked at how much the server piled onto my plate but I was up for the challenge. It was delicious. They have a hot butter station for dipping as well. 

I selected random eats from the American/meats, Italian, Asian, Mexican, cold and hot seafood sections. Then to top it off, every single dessert I tried was delicious, especially the molten chocolate lava cake and pineapple upside down cake. Warm, gooey, and rich.

For the price that we paid, $19 per person because we had a Groupon deal, I thought it was pretty worth it! Especially since we got a free mimosa with our meal. Even though the deal was for two people per table, the staff was able to accommodate us and allowed all 6 of us to sit together with no problems. We came here at around 9am and I am glad we did. There was virtually no wait to get in and just 30 minutes later we saw that the line had extended past the waiting area. There is seafood, meat station, four types of eggs benedict, salsa, guac, tater tots, waffles, crepes, chicken and fries, ramen, dimsum, salad bar, cold cuts, a large dessert bar area, and more. There is definitely something there for all types of taste palettes. You will most definitely leave very full, just remember to pace yourself so you get your money's worth!
Esmeralda was really helpful during the whole process and took her time to explain everything to us! She was great

In thanksgiving day I stayed in line for three hours. I went in at 9:00 and many people are still waiting in line. In yelp it said their was sashimis and Hawaiian foods but there wasn't any. It only had leftovers foods and not fresh sushi.The management won't refill foods and they kept letting customer in. One star for the waiter still patiently to serve.
I love love love this buffet! Best in town! Every time I come to Vegas I have to eat here!

I feel like they opened up a water park in my mouth. It's like BOOM! From nowhere, a cascading river of saliva and a waterfall of drool!

There was a very short wait time on the Sunday dinner service ($65 pp) we went to. We paid, got seated, and ate x1000! Every bite I had was pretty dreamy and delicious and I definitely walked out of there happy. Did I eat my money's worth? Definitely not. The House *always* wins when it comes to buffets but hey, we were told we that we had to experience Bacchanal Buffet once. And so we did. Not bad.

They have a huge variety of options from crab legs to wagyu beef, dim sum to pizza, gelato to sushi, bone marrow to roasted duck, and sooo much more! Even the pickiest of eaters can find something to eat here. And if they can't find anything, just get new friends. Picky eaters are the worst.

But for me, I'm just not a fan of AYCEs and buffets. I rather just have a nice dinner somewhere else and not feel like I'm bursting out of my clothes like The Incredible Hulk by the time I'm done with my meal.

Very nice place. Good for big group. We have like 20 people for our company. Got there around 11 and get sit within 15 mins. Food is good and have many varieties. I would recommend for any groups visit Las Vegas looking for good breakfast and lunch.

It's our 3rd time coming to Las Vegas and this is the longest line I've waited but the waiting time isn't that long but I feel like it's going to worth it. The staff is super nice and friendly and they love helping us if we have any questions. The place is nice and warm since it's winter right now. There's a couple of lines to make it faster so that's a plus.

Too long to wait to be seated. More than two hours. ..,..,..............
If I knew we have to wait for that long I would go somewhere else

Not worth the money. $75/person. Man, I could have more delicious food at other restaurants, for cheaper price (for instance, Paris - across the street, 3 course dinner for $50!-very good food, great service)

Here are the highlights:

- As expected from other reviews, the spread had a good variety and the seating area was quite spacious. 

- However, the flavor of the food was nothing out of this world. But it was a good option to get to try a lot of different types of food but the food was okay in my opinion. 

- I was initially attracted to this place because it had a large number of reviews and popped up high in my yelp search list. But it's important to note that they have an offer of a free drink for each person who checks in on yelp so it's bound to be on the top of your search list. 

- What made it completely worth it was the dessert  spread. I think I may have tried more than 3/4 of the items and loved them all. 

- It was a bit odd for me that they ask for the tip upfront when you pre pay for the buffet, so this is even before you are sitting down and have met your server!

I went to the Wicked Spoon at Cosmopolitan and loved it before this one and so Bacchanal was disappointing. While there were a lot of offerings, they weren't as refined or special as elsewhere despite the price being higher. Some of the prepared dishes were bland, there was a lack of fresh salads and veggie/fruit based items, crab legs tasted off, and overall there was a lack of gluten free items (with inconsistent labels on food). I was disappointed. I also thought there would be more stations with chefs preparing made to order items (like shellfish) and had read that they offered gluten free breakfast items like French toast but they did not. My boyfriend said that the Asian selections were disappointing and bland too. It just seems like the sheer volume they pump out has negatively impacted the food quality. It's also so crowded and servers are stretched thin. Overall it just doesn't seem worth the price.

I am one disappointed buffet-loving foodie. :-|

We finally had a chance to try out Bacchanal while we were in Vegas for the Olympia this year. We had a group of 6 for dinner here about 90 min before they were closing.

Let me just cut to the chase on why I don't ever plan on Bacchanal-ing again:
1. The wait for this place is somewhat confusing. You walk up to this lady that gives you a ticket and she tells you, "15 min for your group." So we're thinking, "Wow! Only 15 min to get seated? Awesome!" WRONG-O! It's about 15 min to get in a line to then pay and get in the longer line to get seated. Boo! Don't tease us like that lady!

2. They seated us wayyyyy in the back, like literally having to trek it out to even get to the food. There were plenty of tables closer to the buffet area that needed to be cleaned off. Seemed like they were understaffed.

3. Food. Blah! Yep, I said it. Everything seemed too salty and not much effort put into cooking it. Only thing I really enjoyed were the snow crab legs and their sweet potato tater tots (which were probably frozen to begin with).

4. Pricey. Yes, it's a Vegas buffet, I know. But the quality of the food is not up to par to have it priced "Vegas style".

Here's one plus that actually solidifies why my review is staying the way it is:
Our waiter was hilarious. He had jokes up the culo. We also were really upfront with him and told him the food wasn't all that. So..he also let us in on a little tidbit. Apparently, the old food court at Caesar's that closed down had chefs over there that held seniority. So those crappy food court chefs quite possibly booted out the stellar chefs that first started out here at Bacchanal and that is why the food is crapola today.

My live review in my YouTube vlog here during that weekend: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DhN4ggfu52w&list=UU5YaBtOxOYqeFEEQ_aW6JiA

Found this place the show the profit great place if you like true variety cultural buffets good everything is not over greasy/fatty or over cooked/under cooked they're complimentary house wine u get for checking in with yelp is delish will return in the future kid friendly they provide high chairs
For my first Vegas experience this buffet was great, expensive lol but great.  Way better than the Bellagio Buffet which was a total waste of money

I was so super excited to eat here based on everyone's reviews and what friends have told me.

We put a reservation through Open Table because it was for the day after Thanksgiving and we had no idea how long the wait would be.

Open Table promises a VIP table with a seafood tower. Didn't really care about the tower ... but here's where this place fell short with me.

Once we got there we went up to the girl at the podium in front and asked her where we would need to stand since we have reservations through Open Table. She slammed her hands on the podium and said (and I quote) " Okay so let me tell you about Open Table. I know is says there will be a Seafood Tower but we won't be offering it since the seafood is already on the buffet line. There is also no unlimited beverage service as it's stated" and then gave me a seriously cocky look. 
Like shit, I know it's the day after Thanksgiving and you're slammed here but have some effing better customer service girl.

So anyway, she told us to go stand in the express line on the left -_-  ... we were helped instantly, paid for our buffet and led to our seats. 

Now, I don't exactly know where in this place that there's supposed to be VIP seating ... from what everyone's told me before my trip .. they have tables with VIP markers on them, yada yada ... we got seated right next to the desserts.
So we paid $98 per person for VIP but got none of what was offered .. go figure right 

But we seriously picked the wrong day to go. When I mentioned earlier that it was slammed ... I meant it. Never ever go the day AFTER Thanksgiving. 

The place was packed .. and people are assholes in means of pushing you aside when your mid transferring food to your plate ... people did that to me more than once in line. 

I will however say that the copious amounts of food choices were overwhelming. What I did pick was awesome.

The food was beyond belief, the service from the beginning however was subpar. 

I would come back again to try the rest of the food. But I think I'll skip paying $98 per person the next time.

I came back to this buffet because after I wrote my first review, the manager kindly messaged me and apologized that I didn't have a great first experience. She was so sweet and great and even offered us a deal if we come back and give them a second chance, so we did. I came with my husband and two others. It was the two others' first time visiting this buffet. I will definitely say, we all had an amazing experience here. 
We came for dinner this time since my first time here was for brunch. Our server, Maryam, is the sweetest woman ever! She took care of us so well. She kept coming back to check up on us so much, she refilled our drinks so fast and she was very funny too, throwing a couple of jokes here and there. She made us feel so welcomed and comfortable to eat there. 
Now, onto the food, I will say I was extremely impressed with the food selection this time. Ranging from their Asian food to meats to seafoods, I ate a bit of everything. I usually never eat more than 4 plates at a buffet...on this trip, I had 7 PLATES! That's a record for me. All the food tasted so fresh and I kept going back for thirds on certain foods, like the bone marrow and seafood. Everyone in my party enjoyed the food as well. The dessert was excellent too! We all got the made to order crepes, and I will say that these crepes surpass to crepes at The Wynn Buffet. 
Overall, I am so happy the manager invited me back to give the Bacchanal another chance. I'm sure we will be back again for the excellent service and the great quality and variety of food here!

First time coming to this. Made reservations on opentable.com which is highly recommended since this place can get pack easily. We came to check it out early to see how the whole check in process works seeing there are a few different signs but not one specific for open table. We were assisted by a gentleman who was confirm the diamond line was opentable reservations and confirm what type of reservation this was specific to. For basically a $100 person you get a dedicated time window, seafood tower, unlimited drinks which includes some alcohol choices, and of course the Buffet. He inquire if we like to be seated earlier since there was availability. The Buffet itself has a massive selection of seafood, desserts, freshly cut meat (tri tip American wyagu prime rib and one another) pizzas, dim sum, sushi, salads, individual servings of fried chicken, pasta, roasted lamb, and it goes on and on so please wander and explore with a game plan! The service was ok as we were greeted but it appear we had to flag down our server or someone numerous times for numerous things. There was also some type of residue in my friend cup and we show to the server who did come back with a replacement drink. The seafood tower this comes with is massive! Chill Crab legs lobster mussels oysters sea snails crab claws! This can easily feed 4 people! Will be back and may just do the regular Buffet but overall a neat first time experience!

The BACCHANAL buffet is in my opinion the best buffet in Las Vegas! I think the variety and quality is tops in the world of AYCE buffet options.

I enjoy the steamed crab legs, jumbo shrimp cocktail, and the seafood station just to name a few of my favorites.

I noticed on this last visit that they are no longer slicing the crab legs in half so you will have to start crackin! :/

The ambiance and decor is romantic, cozy and inviting so you can get really comfortable.

The service and staff is super nice and keep up on those many drink refills!

The selection and variety can't be beat, they really have a lot to offer in many food categories.

The dessert station is great as well with options of gelato, made to order crepes, chocolate covered strawberries and stuffed mini donuts mmmm yum.

I don't visit often as we save this buffet as a treat for special occasions!

We went to Bacchanal on Easter Sunday as it was my brothers birthday. The ambiance was amazing. But more than that was our amazing server Esmerelda that heard it was my brothers birthday and brought a surplus of desserts and added a candle to help us sing "Happy Birthday" to him. She was so sweet and kind. We had the best time! And the food was amazing! We will definitely be coming back when we come to Vegas. Thank you Esmerelda!

Came him from LA! Thanksgiving Week. We decided to eat here, after waiting for over an hour to be seated, We a family of 4 we're do disappointed . The meat was tough, the Seafood wasn't fresh, not to mentioned We had a rude server!!! We spend all this money to get in for nothing, not to mention I ended up in the hospital with food poisoning. Only time I would go back is if the Owner calls me!!!
Every time we visit Las Vegas we go to this buffet. This buffet is the biggest and best buffet in LV
Best buffet ever! Irma was great, served us better than any other place here in Vegas!!

Hollllllyyyy moleyyyy! 

This buffet was one for the books. Iv never seen a buffet so huge. The Asian section was easily my fav! the hot crab legs had a long wait but totally worth it!! The only let down was the meat station, while there were so many great options... they were bland all of them. Hopefully it was just that day!
The selection is amazing and all the food is excellently prepared! Esmeralda the server had great service as well. Would definitely come back another time

One of the best buffets I've had in Vegas. My only visit was unfortunately marred by a choking incident (I'm fine now). The food was terrific with so many choices, the wait was a thing (long), but worth it. I can't wait to go back!

I got a chance to go to the Bacchanal Buffett just this last Tuesday at Caesars Palace. Wow, what a yummy place, it's always packed here. I got a voucher Travelzoo deal and paid about $39 to get in, Tipped my server about $7 (but you don't need to tip). . There are ton of food to choose from and I tried mostly the Japanese Sushis, Chinese Dim sum, American steak, pizza, meat section. Service was great too whether you are solo, 2 or in a group. Good attentive service, good staff and a good place to eat. I had about 3 plates and several small dessert plates, I was basically done eating for the rest of the day. lol, Give this place a try at Caesars when you're in Vegas. 4.5 Stars all the way. Love it. Love it and Love it. -- Wish I can go back and eat there again now. Haha
